Every prime power and natural zero remains. The denominator is log Nb,
not an approximation by log D. All required finite derivatives of V_D
are bounded on the fixed annulus, uniformly in its positive m range.

## G199. Complete prime-band product estimate

For first powers split the exact band into dyads P<=Np<2P. Set E=D/P.
Before choosing a row,prime or color, separate the common profile V_D(yz)
on a fixed ambient compact box by PR9 B3.3. The normalization is exact:
P^(-1/2)E^(-1/2)=D^(-1/2). A separated term is M(R)Q times one new
prime slot at P and a plain factor at E. Apply its same-bin plain bound
FIRST, then enlarge only the remaining positive MI norm. This gives

    ||M Q * first-power dyad||^2
      <<H_J U^(1+epsilon)D^beta P^(-beta).             (2)

The prime coefficient can be fixed as log Np/log U, extracting the bounded
scalar log U/log D. Scale derivatives therefore do not change arithmetic
coefficients. The new slot has the SAME orientation phi, not another
moving character absorbed into a coefficient. All original slots remain.

With lambda=log_U(P)<=4eta+small and G137's first reserve>.01017,

    1-r-2(v+lambda) >=217/100000-small,
    3-2r-8(v+lambda)>=39417/50000-small.               (3)

Both margins hold throughout the whole window, including v=0; shortening
the inverse improves them. The enlarged fixed slot system and finite orders
are chosen before witnesses.

All support collisions are paid. Split the new pool outside the union of
old pools and into its intersections with each old pool i. For p=q in
an intersection, remove the old slot and extract its prime. The old scale
P_i is comparable to P, and ideal counting gives coefficient mass
sum_p(P_i Np)^(-1/2)(D/Np)^(beta/2)<<D^(beta/2)P^(-beta/2).
The remaining slots satisfy MI. The phase phi(p)^2 is a contraction,
including its zero, and the inverse is not declared coprime to p.

For p!=q independently color the prime IDEALS of that finite old pool:

    1_(p!=q)=4 E_color[1_(p in E0)1_(q in E1)].        (4)

Each colored pair has disjoint row-independent supports, so MI applies.
Minkowski under the NORMALIZED probability measure costs4, not the number
of colorings. Distinct ideals of equal norm must receive distinct labels;
coloring only norms would be false. Original pools are disjoint, so this
exhausts all new/old coincidences at a fixed count of cases.

For j>=2, apply the shortened plain bound before taking the extracted-prime
absolute sum. Its dyadic mass is P^(1-j(1+beta)/2)<=P^(-beta). The complete
j sum is geometric and gives squared saving A^(-2beta), better than (2).
All natural zeros, higher powers and collisions remain inside that bound.
Summing dyads costs only the prescribed small loss. Therefore

    ||M S^[theta] Q||^2_Omega
      <<H_J U^(1+epsilon)D^beta A^(-beta).            (5)

This complete product estimate is independent of the previous removals.

## Complete height and profile implementation

Factor the original witness twist BEFORE separating the common profile:
(yz)^(sigma+i gamma)=y^(sigma+i gamma)z^(sigma+i gamma).
Separate the remaining height-free kernel W_0(yz)log D/log(Dyz). Its
arbitrarily high fixed derivative constants do not grow like |gamma|^N.
The two Fourier coordinates shift the new slot and plain heights separately;
all original slot heights stay independent.

Within a fixed fraction of the old height buffer, use the same shortened
plain upper bound at gamma+tau without reselecting the bin or zero.
For the entire complementary Fourier range, the internal floor
T_ht>=U^kappa and E<=CD<=U^C imply, for a sufficiently large fixed J1,

    E^(1/2) <=C E^(beta/2)(1+|tau|)^J1.

Use absolute ideal counting on that range, and integrate the resulting
polynomial against the SAME height-free Fourier kernel. B3.3 gives its
finite weighted L1 norm. No Fourier or arithmetic tail is omitted and no
shifted lower spike is assumed. Fix the MI/Sobolev height degree and losses,
then a sufficiently small internal kappa; the extra kernel derivatives do
not enlarge that already fixed MI height degree. Choose final external
height degree afterward. Tensor Sobolev controls rowwise parameters only
in the positive upper majorant, not a derivative dominance signal.

Subunit nonempty scales are bounded dilations and smaller scales are empty.
Fixed punctures use complete smooth-power restoration. The source detector's
own contour tails retain their raw-count-before-decay order. No new
growing-conductor or high-height theorem is claimed.

## G200. Complete weighted removal and the fourth paid class

For a fixed extracted ideal L,E=D/NL, the literal multiplier is theta(Lc).
Its exact plain expansion is

    S_(theta,L)(E)=ell_B(L)/log D S(E;V_D)
      +(1/log D)sum_(p,j>=1)log Np phi(p^j)(Np)^(-j/2)
                                      S(E/(Np)^j;V_D). (6)

When p|L the first term counts its existing valuations and the second counts
every additional valuation of c. Nonempty support gives NL<=CD. The complete
first-power absolute mass is Y^((1-beta)/2), and higher powers are smaller:

    |S_(theta,L)(D/NL)|
      <<H_J U^epsilon(D/NL)^(beta/2)Y^((1-beta)/2).     (7)

This uniform bound on actual plain blocks is not an arbitrary coefficient
multiplier theorem. Insert it before [restricted research revision]'s complete q,k,lcm convolution,
including every shared divisor and all inverse smooth-power restorations.
The old gcd/square pieces gain exactly one squared cost Y^(1-beta).
For G=Y=U^(4eta),H=U^(2eta), their weighted savings are(8beta-4)eta;
(5) saves2beta eta. Since beta>2/3 with reserved buffer, the latter is smaller.
The complete old weighted core therefore saves2beta eta, with its exact
signed intersection subtraction paid by triangle.

More sharply, [restricted research revision]'s coupled cut F(a,b)=N(gcd(a,b))Ns2(b)^2 has exact blocks
M^(q)(R/Nq)S(D/Nlcm(q,k^2)) and FULL positive mass T^(-beta/2)U^epsilon.
It satisfies the author's conditional interface exactly. Thus

    ||C_T^[theta]Q||^2
      <<H_J U^(1+epsilon)D^beta
                [A^(-beta)+T^(-beta)Y^(1-beta)]
      <<H_J U^(1+beta*m-2beta*eta+epsilon),            (8)

at T=Y=U^(4eta). This is the complete weighted core, not a signed subset.
Keep [restricted research revision]'s three paid classes FIRST. On their complement |C_T|>|MS|/2.
Define the new actual class there by |C_T^[theta]|>=|C_T|/2. Dividing (8)
by the original SAME-beta plain spike pays original inverse moment

    sum_newclass w_u |M(R)Q|^2
      <<H_J U^(1-2delta*eta+epsilon).                 (9)

The preloss saving is at least(34/25)eta, reserve(9/25)eta above eta.
Q is never divided out. Every remaining row retains the exact signal

    |C_T^[1-theta]|>|MS|/4,
    1-theta(b)=log N(b_outside_band)/log Nb,            (10)
    N(abP/rad(abP))<T NP=U^(4eta)NP.

Band prime squares are absent from this core since p^2|b,Np>=A implies
F>=A^2=T. They were nonetheless fully paid in the preceding expansions.
The large-prime plain sector with squarefree coprime inverse has F=1 and
theta=0, so it survives. This is a coefficient example, not an actual
high-zero row or a lower bound for a signed norm.

The complete coarse norm from C_T^[1-theta]=C_T-C_T^[theta] is still
H_J U^(1+beta*m+epsilon). After the original plain division it is U^(1+epsilon).
The full signed outside-band estimate and whole-row cover remain OPEN.
No norm/class monotonicity follows from0<=theta<=1 or tuple inclusion.

All physical roots, projectors, positive children, original slots, labels,
low/high and fixed-inducing branches, shortage/empty cases, Euler shifts,
residues and common-Delta return retain their old prices. A signed projector
need not preserve a dominance class; paired restricted gains average under

statement:
## 2. D04: exact reconstruction, complete quantifiers and zero return

Write f(n)=mu(rad(n/3^v3(n))). Fix tau>0 and one ordinary character chi
modulo q, with its actual zero extension on nonunits. Define

    F_chi(x)=sum_(n>=1) f(n)chi(n)g_tau(log(n/x)).

For finite P of unramified primes>=5, let V_P have the SAME coefficients
but vanish on integers divisible by any p in P. Define a_P(r)=f(r)chi(r)
on all P-smooth integers, zero otherwise. The unique decomposition of n
into its FULL smooth part r and rough part v gives the coefficient
identity a_P*f_P=(n -> f(n)chi(n)) and hence

    F_chi(x)=sum_(r P-smooth) a_P(r)V_P(x/r).       (A1)

At every deleted p, a_P(p^j)=-chi(p)^j for ALL j>=1. The local series
is (1-2chi(p)z)/(1-chi(p)z), not1-chi(p)z. The precise positive price is

    W_P(u)=sum |a_P(r)|r^-u=product_(p in P)(1-p^-u)^-1.

Prime2 and exceptional3 remain in V_P; natural zeros at q are retained.
For any fixed P and a weight u>1, the positive Gaussian integer field
is bounded by C_u t^u on all t>0: at infinity its size is O(t), and at
zero it has faster-than-power decay. Summing this bound with W_P(u)
proves absolute, locally uniform convergence of A1 before any open
moment hypothesis. Thus no rearrangement hides a source assumption.

Fix1/2<gamma<1,0<sigma<gamma,0<delta<1,A>0 with

    A(1-sigma)<1,
    q_head=sigma+delta(1-sigma)<gamma.              (A2)

For each large dyadic parent X, freeze
P_X={5<=p<=(log X)^A:p does not divide q}. OPEN-D04 asks for every
epsilon>0, with a constant uniform in X and EVERY REAL U,

    ||V_(P_X)||_[U,2U],dx/x <= C_epsilon U^(gamma+epsilon),
                   X^delta<=U<=X.                (A3)

The parent prime set stays fixed during every dilation. Replacing it by
P_U, or bounding only primes/one rough depth/a submask, changes A3.

Since sigma<1, summing p^-sigma over all integers up to(log X)^A gives
log W_(P_X)(sigma)=O((log X)^(A(1-sigma)))=o(log X). No PNT is needed.
Split A1 at r=X^(1-delta). For shorter r, the exact shell U=X/r is in
A3. Minkowski gives X^(gamma+epsilon')W_(P_X)(sigma), and a smaller
epsilon' absorbs the subpower price.

For larger r, t=x/r<=2X^delta. The positive Gaussian integer field is
O(t) when t>=1 and O_sigma(t^sigma) when0<t<1. Therefore uniformly on
this head it is O(X^(delta(1-sigma))t^sigma). Summing EVERY smooth r
in the head bounds its pointwise, hence shell-L2, contribution by

    X^q_head W_(P_X)(sigma)=X^(q_head+o(1)).        (A4)

The strict gap in A2 pays it. The norm triangle pays the head square
and both cross terms of a subsequent energy expansion. No inheritance
of a masked moment, projector commutation or deletion of positive energy
is used. This proves the conditional full F_chi gamma moment. The head
price is sufficient, not a universal optimum or impossibility boundary.

### 2.1 Independent Mellin check

For Re s>1, Fubini and the exact local factors give

    M(F_chi)(s)=exp(tau*s^2/2) H_chi(s)/L(s,chi),
    H_(chi,p)=(1-2chi(p)p^-s)/(1-chi(p)p^-s)^2, p!=3,
    H_(chi,3)=(1-chi(3)3^-s)^-2.                   (A5)

Factors at p|q are1. For unramified p>=5 the first-order term cancels;
the product converges absolutely locally in Re s>1/2. Its numerator
zero lines are Re s=log_p2<1/2, denominators' zero lines are Re s=0.
The exceptional p2 numerator has zero line Re s=1, and p3 has no
numerator. Thus H_chi is holomorphic and nonzero in1/2<Re s<1.
Complex character phases do not alter those real parts.

The full moment implies that the defining Mellin integral is holomorphic
in Re s>gamma: on each large dyadic shell use Cauchy--Schwarz with an
epsilon smaller than the distance to that line; all fixed derivatives
are summable there. The left Gaussian tail handles x tending to zero.
Multiplying A5 by L and analytically continuing, a zero rho with
gamma<Re rho<1 contradicts the nonzero right side. The independently
accepted right boundary covers Re s>=1; principal pole handling is
meromorphic. No claim that the p2 numerator is nonzero on Re s=1 is
needed. Every height is covered by analytic continuation, not a grid.

This is a conditional result for EACH fixed chi separately. Zeta-only
A3 is not a bound for all chi. No growing conductor, new angular scope,
Hecke family or SP/H addback is imported.

### 2.2 The reverse implication is valid and fixes the strength claim

The inverse local series is

    (1-chi(p)z)/(1-2chi(p)z)
       =1+sum_(j>=1)2^(j-1)chi(p)^j z^j.

For fixed u>log_5(2), the inverse coefficients b_P have mass

    B_P(u)=product_(p in P)(1-p^-u)/(1-2p^-u).      (A6)

The sign and every prime power matter. For fixed u<1, its logarithm
is O_u((log X)^(A(1-u))). The coefficient identity and absolutely
convergent field identity are V_P=sum_r b_P(r)F_chi(./r).

Assume the original fixed F_chi moment with exponent gamma and every
epsilon. Its real-shell bound follows from at most two dyadic shells;
its Gaussian left tail extends the bound to all positive shell scales.
Choose0<epsilon'<epsilon small enough that u=gamma+epsilon'<1.
Since gamma>1/2>log_5(2) and gamma>sigma, A6 is finite and subpower.
Minkowski gives

    ||V_(P_X)||_[U,2U] <= C U^(gamma+epsilon') B_(P_X)(u)
                       = U^(gamma+epsilon') X^o(1).

For U>=X^delta the last factor is absorbed into U^(epsilon-epsilon'),
uniformly in X,U. This is exactly A3. Together with A1--A4 it proves
the first critic's additional interpretation: **under A2, OPEN-D04 and
the original complete fixed-character gamma moment are equivalent at
the every-epsilon exponent level.** The idea pays a range obligation
and changes the organization; it does not weaken the required arithmetic
exponent. This equivalence is credited to the first Sol critic, not
retrospectively to the generator or to this final validation.

| gamma | Conditional c | (A,sigma,delta) | q_head | gamma-q_head | A(1-sigma) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
|2187/2500|313/2500|(6,17/20,1/10)|173/200|49/5000|9/10|
|5/6|1/6|(5,41/50,1/20)|829/1000|13/3000|9/10|
|3/4|1/4|(3,7/10,1/10)|73/100|1/50|9/10|

All prices and strict gaps are correct. The first hypothetical gain over
c4 is13/200000=.000065; it is not achieved. The stated sufficient
ceiling A<1/(1-gamma) follows by choosing sigma just below gamma and
then delta small. The zeta baseline beta=.8749 only reproduces its own
exponent through A6; at A=6 its log-price power is.7506<1. It does not
prove gamma=.8748.

D35.1 already gives fixed/moving prime normalization, frozen-parent
dilation, positive reconstruction prices and complete zero return. Its
mu inverse is finite squarefree and its underlying detector differs.
W36 smooth-state organization and current G28/G29/[private research revision] S1--S5 retain
credit. The useful continuation here is the literal f3*chi all-power
source and explicit paid head, not a new rough-detector architecture.
No literature priority is claimed.

## 7. Protected audit W40-12: exact conditional drift and projection cost

The author parked12 as U-FILTRATION duplication. Its high-reach intent
is retained, but an actual prime model must replace a convenient
independent law. This audit provides the following exact laboratory and
uncut source identities; no source-saving martingale bound follows.

On the explicit four labels n=1,p,q,pq, with p,q distinct primes other
than3, keep w_ab=g_tau(a log p+b log q-log x), a,b in{0,1}. The original
f3 signs are+,-,-,+. One exact Gaussian calculation gives

    w00 w11/(w10 w01)=exp[-log p log q/tau]<1.      (R40.7)

Thus the two presence bits are not independent under these weights.
Writing Z=sum w, alpha=P(A=1), beta=P(B=1), c=P(A=B=1),
Cov(A,B)=c-alpha beta=(w00 w11-w10 w01)/Z^2<0, and

    E[B-beta | A]=(c-alpha beta)/(alpha(1-alpha))
                              *(A-alpha).         (R40.8)

This is the exact drift lost by unconditionally centering B and then
treating it as a martingale increment after revealing A.

There is an exact rational instance with native Gaussian weights:
p=2,q=5,x=sqrt10,tau=(log5)/2. By symmetry and R40.7 the four weights
are proportional to(1,2,2,1). Consequently alpha=beta=1/2,
c=1/6, Cov=-1/12, correlation rho=-1/3, and normalized f3 mean=-1/3.
An independent pair with those same one-bit marginals would give parity
mean0. This is a four-label conditional diagnostic, not the infinite
Gaussian source or a claimed uniformly likely conditioning event.

The two conditional-expectation projections E_A,E_B fix constants.
On centered functions they are rank-one projections onto the unit
vectors X=(A-alpha)/sqrt(alpha(1-alpha)) and
Y=(B-beta)/sqrt(beta(1-beta)), with inner product rho. In the basis
X,(Y-rho X)/sqrt(1-rho^2), their 2x2 matrices are

    P=[[1,0],[0,0]],
    Q=[[rho^2,rho sqrt(1-rho^2)],
       [rho sqrt(1-rho^2),1-rho^2]].

Thus ||[E_A,E_B]||=|rho|sqrt(1-rho^2), equal to2sqrt2/9 in the
rational example. The correct increment Y-rho X is orthogonal to X;
the naive increment Y has the nonzero conditional drift rho X. These
identities are derived within the actual finite weighted L2 space, not
by assuming projections commute.

The complete positive integer-Gaussian measure has a separate exact
source formula. Let Z_(q,a)(x) sum g_tau(log(n/x)) over ALL positive
integers n congruent to a modulo q; Z(x) is its unrestricted sum.
For distinct primes p,q and an integer shift h, let r_h be the unique
CRT residue satisfying n=0 mod p, n=-h mod q. Then

    P(A)=Z(x/p)/Z(x),
    P(B)=Z_(q,-h)(x)/Z(x),
    P(A B)=Z_(pq,r_h)(x)/Z(x),                      (R40.9)

where A=1_(p|n), B=1_(q|n+h). Formula R40.8 applies with these actual
probabilities. It retains the shift, all positive integers and every
endpoint. In the unshifted case joint mass is Z(x/(pq))/Z(x).
No factorization of these Gaussian progression sums has been asserted.
Fixed-modulus sum-integral estimates explain approximate independent
densities at large x, but rare conditioning and growing prime information
can amplify their errors; they do not pay a full arithmetic filtration.

Finally, any genuine Doob martingale for the complete bounded observable
sigma(n)=f3(n) under this positive measure has initial value
M0=E sigma=F(x)/Z(x). With all prime-presence information its terminal
value is sigma; on this countable space convergence follows by bounded
conditional expectation. Orthogonality gives

    sum E|Delta M|^2=1-|F(x)/Z(x)|^2.              (R40.10)

This identity does not make its unknown initial mean small. The physical
factor Z(x) is of order x and must be restored. This is the recorded
W07 seed05/U-FILTRATION obstruction, not a new universal impossibility.
The quantitative projection example is a useful exact first test; a
new result needs the actual predictable drift/conditional correlations
and zero-sensitive readout uniformly paid. W38's different three-prime
positive-covariance example also remains valid; this four-state negative
covariance is not a sign law for all marginals.

## Transport and common-unit centering of an inherited graph bound

Put S=N+L+(NL)^(2/3). The original raw target is
G K S sqrt(Omega1 Omega2) P_orig, where Omega_i=sum|u_i(P)|^2/q_P
and P_orig contains the actual profiles, coefficients and scalar gains.
The outside physical factor is N^(-1)G^(-2), applied once.

The previously accepted JSR19 bound for graphs with both degrees<=B is

    |C_E| <= Z^epsilon G^(2+103/359) B K^(231/359)
                         N^(103/359) S sqrt(Omega1 Omega2) P_orig.

The graph may be frozen with each original short pair, but must be
independent of live rows and marks. This raw graph bound is inherited
credit. Its full signed projector expansion retains both roots, all
D,D' cross terms and the lcm Schur bound.

Move only the smooth row factor from R/sqrt(K) to(R+P+P')/sqrt(K);
every sharp support stays on the original variables. Its global smooth
extension has difference bounded by C sqrt(L/K)||grad rho||. Counting
O(G^2) short pairs, O(NB) edges and O(K) rows, and paying both rooted
mark sums by L sqrt(Omega1 Omega2), gives

    |C_E^tr-C_E| <= C G^2 K N B L sqrt(L/K)
                            sqrt(Omega1 Omega2) P_orig.

No sharp indicator is differentiated and no signed-submask monotonicity
is assumed. This coarse estimate is enough for the stated sparse graphs.

The actual common-unit Jacobi numerator has two square-root Jacobi
factors and denominator

    product_(p|pi*pi') [q_p^2-3q_p+3-1_(p|T)].

Both local convolution signs cancel. The ratio is O(N^-3), including
exceptional totals. The absent local factor begins as an unrestricted
constant; unit insertion is justified by the actual small-mark support.
Counting all mark off-diagonals and graph edges yields

    |M_E^(J,tr)| <= C G^2 K B L/N^2 sqrt(Omega1 Omega2) P_orig.

The sharp row remains R=T-P-P'. The original injection
Q>C_orig(K+L) makes the transported smooth factor constant on each
occupied residue-total fibre. No additional Fourier or unit normalization
appears. The centered form is C_E^tr-M_E^(J,tr).

All three terms are paid by the original target when, with a fixed buffer,

    B <= K^(128/359) N^(-103/359) G^(-462/359),
    G B L sqrt(L/K)<=1, G B L/N^3<=1.

At B=floor(Z^.055) their relative pressure exponents are approximately
-.00103535,-.1055331,-2.288709. All corners of the wider rational
box .8355<=k<=.8356,.1708<=ell<=.1709,nu=k+.003 retain strict savings.
This is an adapter for the inherited pressure block, not a new endpoint
solution. Multiplication by N^-1 G^-2 gives the complete physical bound
Z^epsilon K S/(NG) sqrt(Omega1 Omega2) P_orig.

Both original preprojection corrections vanish on this prime packet by
support. They are not removed from composite or other branches. Both
ordered heights are integrated against their actual product separation
densities, whose weighted L1 moments pay the radial/gradient powers.
Complete source tails are bounded before transport; both mixed tails
and the double tail are paid. The transported object retains the original
discarded tail or its exact correction. Unbounded heights are not hidden
in epsilon and a shifted tail is not given its old argument by assertion.

Actual primary-generator displacement graphs of squared radius Y have
degree O(Y+1), so Y of order Z^.055 supplies admissible strict-far

statement:
## 2. Development02: bounded-coefficient summatory norms are not an algebra

For a finitely supported real sequence a, let A(x)=sum_(n<=x)a(n) and

    ||a||_[sigma]=sup_(x>=1) x^(-sigma)|A(x)|, 0<sigma<1.

**W43.1.** There is no constant C_sigma such that

    ||a*b||_[sigma] <= C_sigma ||a||_[sigma] ||b||_[sigma]

for all finite real a,b, even if |a(n)|,|b(n)|<=1 and both input norms are at most1. Thus a uniform Banach-algebra argument based only on the buffered Mertens exponent and bounded coefficients cannot justify the seed's reciprocal iteration.

Proof. Fix N>=2. Set A(d)=(-1)^(d+1)/2 for1<=d<=N and A(d)=0 for d=0 or d>=N+1; a(d)=A(d)-A(d-1). Then a is supported on1,...,N+1, its endpoint magnitudes are1/2 and its other magnitudes are1. In particular |a|<=1 and ||a||_[sigma]<=1/2.

Choose a large integer H with

    H>=4(N+1)^2,
    H^(1-sigma)>=16(N+1)^(2-sigma),
    t_d=floor(H/d), 1<=d<=N+1.

These t_d are distinct. Prescribe B(t_d)=sign(a(d))*t_d^sigma. On the real interval[0,2H], define B by linear interpolation through those points, B(0)=B(2H)=0, and set B=0 outside. The signed interpolation lies between the concave envelopes +/-t^sigma: its absolute value is bounded by the interpolation of the endpoint absolute values, which is at most t^sigma. Therefore |B(t)|<=t^sigma.

For consecutive d,d+1, the spacing is at least H/(4d^2), while the change in B is at most2(H/d)^sigma. Thus each inner slope has absolute value at most

    8 H^(sigma-1) d^(2-sigma) <=1/2.

The two outer slopes have absolute value at most1. Let b(n)=B(n)-B(n-1). It is finitely supported, |b(n)|<=1 and ||b||_[sigma]<=1. Dirichlet convolution and summation now give the exact positive alignment

    sum_(n<=H)(a*b)(n)
      =sum_(d<=N+1)a(d)B(floor(H/d))
      =sum_(d<=N+1)|a(d)|t_d^sigma.

Since t_d>=H/(2d), the last expression divided by H^sigma is at least

    2^(-sigma) sum_(d=2)^N d^(-sigma)
      >>_sigma N^(1-sigma).

This diverges with N, proving W43.1. The proof works with rounded-down peaks floor(t_d^sigma) as well, losing only an absolute factor for sufficiently large H. Rounded peaks permit entirely rational finite certificates when sigma=7/8, by computing the integer eighth root of t_d^7.

With H chosen of order N^((2-sigma)/(1-sigma)), this family has a convolution value of order at least H^(1/(2-sigma)). Since 1/(2-sigma)>sigma, even the input exponent is not preserved by this uniform norm argument. This is a family of finite sequences with uniform input constants; it is not a claimed asymptotic lower bound for one fixed infinite sequence, and neither sequence is claimed to be mu. At sigma=.874864 the comparison exponent is the exact62500/70321, not a QRH exponent.

**What this changes.** A signed reciprocal construction cannot invoke submultiplicativity merely because both inputs have partial sums O(x^sigma). It must estimate the actual convolution or use a genuinely stronger norm with its inclusion and complete zero return proved. Weighted coefficient l1 is a true algebra on its convergence half-plane, but moving from the signed norm into it pays the omitted absolute values and does not supply a new strip. This sharpens the generic bounded-coefficient failure; it does not refute source-specific Mobius convolution estimates.

Functional signature: finite bounded arithmetic sequences; interpolate opposite partial-sum peaks at hyperbolic sampling points; exact positive alignment under convolution; first unpaid input is a source-specific stronger convolution norm; quantitative output is an unbounded norm ratio, not a zero-free gain. Ancestry: W26's finite-Euler H-infinity obstruction and W35's absolute renewal failure concern different norms and coefficients. No literature novelty is asserted for the general nonalgebra fact.
title: 2. Development02: bounded-coefficient summatory norms are not an algebra

## 5. Uniform two-prime PNT, its diagonal and exact density

For retained r<=R put y=x/r. Thus

    X^(1-delta)<=y<=2X,  z>=X^rho_0,
    y/z^2>=X^(1-delta-2rho_1).

The last exponent is positive. Define the unordered prime kernel

    P_z(y)=sum_(z<p<q) g(log(pq/y)).

First replace it by half the ordered p,q sum. The exact subtracted
p=q diagonal, after summing all retained cores, has absolute size at
most

    (1/2)sum_(p>z) sum_(r>=1) g(log(rp^2/x))
      <= C_tau x sum_(p>z)p^(-2)
      <= C_tau X/z.                                ([restricted research revision])

Here the complete Gaussian lattice bound `sum_r g(log(r/u))<=C_tau u`
holds for all u>0, as proved in [private research revision] renewal F17. Thus the diagonal
is paid even at small scales and with all valuations in r.

For completeness, the following Stieltjes estimate justifies both
prime replacements with their sharp lower endpoint. Put

    H_1(s)=exp(s)g(s)+integral_s^infinity exp(v)|g'(v)|dv.

For fixed p>z, ([restricted research revision]), integration by parts on `(z,infinity)`, and
`log v>=rho_0 L` give

    |sum_(q>z)g(log(pq/y))
       -integral_z^infinity g(log(pv/y))dv/log v|
       <= C_N (y/p)L^(-N)H_1(log(pz/y)).              ([restricted research revision])

The boundary is `-[pi(z)-li(z)]g(log(pz/y))`; it is bounded by the
first term in H_1 and includes the case in which z is itself prime.
The endpoint at infinity is zero. H_1 is bounded on the negative axis
and rapidly decreasing on the positive axis. Bounding primes by
integers therefore gives

    sum_(p>z) p^(-1)H_1(log(pz/y))
         <= C[1+log_+(y/z^2)]<=C L.                 ([restricted research revision])

This follows by the harmonic sum up to y/z and an exponentially
decaying majorant above it. The analogous replacement of the outer
prime sum in the already continuous inner integral is bounded, after
Fubini, by

    C_N y L^(-N) integral_z^infinity
               H_1(log(vz/y))dv/[v log v]
       <= C_N y L^(1-N).

The last inequality uses the same harmonic integral and rapidly
decaying tail as ([restricted research revision]), and `1/log v<=1` for sufficiently large X.
Thus the two-prime error is at most `C_N y L^(1-N)`. Summing the
retained cores absolutely at this already priced PNT step costs only
`sum_(r<=R)1/r=O(L)`. With N=8 the TOTAL error is `O(X/L^6)`.
Both prime errors, their actual lower endpoints, and their interaction
are included; there is no use of independent prime signs.

The continuous ordered-pair integral can be evaluated exactly. Put
`t=log z=rho L`, `A=log y+w`. With `s=log u`, `log v=A-s`, the
Jacobian is `du dv=y exp(w) ds dw`. Its interior integral is

    (1/2)integral_t^(A-t) ds/[s(A-s)]
         =phi_t(A):=A^(-1)log((A-t)/t),  A>2t,       ([restricted research revision])

and zero when A<=2t. Consequently, after ([restricted research revision]), ([restricted research revision])--([restricted research revision]),

    R_z(x)=x integral_R exp(w)g(w)
             sum_(r<=R) f(r)/r phi_t(log x+w-log r)dw
          +O(X^(1-kappa)L+X/z+X/L^6)+O_A(X^(-A)).   ([restricted research revision])

This formula keeps the literal ordered-pair normalization and its
removed p=q diagonal. It is a derived source estimate, not a change
of the Gaussian kernel or an identification with the earlier SP source.

## Reciprocal Hankel determinant: a complete conditional return

The [source](upstream/report.md) and
[independent proof](upstream-review/report.md) supply the arithmetic and
nonvanishing missing from W36's parked abstract adjugate construction.
For an ordinary character chi, put F=1/L(s,chi) and

    D_delta(s)=det[F(s+(i+j)delta)]_(0<=i,j<=2),
    1/5 <= delta <= 1/4.

Cauchy--Binet gives the literal ordered triples a<b<c and their squared
Vandermonde weight. Every surviving coalesced coefficient is
chi(n)*lambda(n)*W_delta(n), with W_delta(n)>=0. Individual factors must
be squarefree; shared primes and squareful outputs remain. Prime-power
outputs vanish, but the actual (1,p0,p) short-factor channel proves that
the absolute coefficient series still diverges for every sigma<=1.
This is an actual obstruction to absolute treatment, not a lower bound
for the complete signed field.

Expansion at the unshifted entry is D=C_delta*F+E_delta, retaining all
three complementary products. For each hypothetical zero rho, the
cofactor is a nonzero analytic function of delta: the least unramified
prime dominates as real delta tends to infinity, with the entire tail
bounded. Its zeros in the fixed interval have measure zero. A bound for
the averaged Gaussian energy on every dyadic scale gives holomorphic
Mellin transforms for almost every fixed delta by Tonelli and dyadic
Cauchy--Schwarz. Intersecting those full-measure sets with the cofactor
nonvanishing sets for the countably many zeros selects one fixed delta
for the entire half-plane. No height cutoff or uniform lower cofactor
bound is needed.

At a multiple zero, C_delta(rho) multiplies the **leading Laurent
coefficient**, so the pole order is preserved. Lower Laurent coefficients
may involve derivatives of C. The principal pole of L is a zero of F and
creates no missing residue. This wording refinement controls any loose
reference to a pole's coefficient in the frozen source.

The complete median-factor tail b>floor(X^.315) is O(X^.874), uniformly
in delta and the character, by V_delta^2<=a^(-4delta)b^(-2delta).
The two product tails outside
[X exp(-2 sqrt(log X)), 2X exp(2 sqrt(log X))] are X^(-1+o(1)).
All their overlaps and mixed scalar terms are paid by the joint norm
triangle inequality. The resulting exact finite D20 signed moment at
X^(1.74898+epsilon) would give gamma=.87449 and c=.12551 for every
ordinary character for which the full hypothesis is proved. Its diagonal
is X^(1+o(1)); its complete signed off-diagonal is OPEN. A zeta-only
estimate gives only a zeta conclusion. No Eisenstein Hecke extension is
asserted by this ordinary-character argument.

The separate delta=2 cofactor is quantitatively invertible in the weighted
dilation algebra: its normalized remainder norm is less than19/20,
and the inverse norm is less than20. The exact rational certificate,
finite-support cutoff and entire small-scale tail are supplied. This
shows that the large-shift determinant is a stable filter of the original
Mobius field. It does not estimate the small-shift averaged target.
Even-modulus characters require the explicitly labeled one-atom repair
only for this auxiliary anchor; D20 keeps all original natural zeros.

The independent finite Leibniz/Vandermonde audit includes a nonreal
character modulo5 and natural zero coefficients. It and the rational
inverse certificate passed. The controller independently checked the
all-scale parameter selection, median/product exponents, inverse
direction and complete error return against both manuscripts; no new
formal-kernel verification is claimed.

## 4. Nearby expanded products, with arbitrary further masks

Expand the two original finite sums in \(\Xi(de;x)\) and
\(\Xi(fh;x)\). For \(0\le P\le X\), the total absolute contribution
of

\[
|\ell de-mfh|\le P,\qquad 1\le\ell,m\le J,
\tag{SP20}
\]

is

\[
\ll_\epsilon X^{1+\epsilon}(P+1).
\tag{SP21}
\]

The bound holds after any additional bounded tuple mask, in particular
after excluding \(A(K)\).

**Proof.** Put \(n=\ell de\), \(n'=mfh\). Support gives
\(n,n'\le Z=2JT_u\ll XL^8\). The numbers of representations are
at most \(d_3(n)\) and \(d_3(n')\). Each individual profile factor
is bounded and the cutoffs have modulus at most one. Thus the absolute
contribution, including integration, is bounded by a constant times

\[
\sum_{\substack{n,n'\le Z\\|n-n'|\le P}}d_3(n)d_3(n')
\ll(P+1)\sum_{n\le Z+P}d_3(n)^2
\ll(P+1)(Z+P)\log^8(2Z+2P).
\tag{SP22}
\]

The first inequality is Cauchy--Schwarz for each difference. The second
uses \(d_3(n)^2\le d_9(n)\) and the elementary mean bound for \(d_9\),
the precise positive majorant already proved in
[AD3](../review-cycle-20.md#exact-coalescence-of-all-product-coincidences).
This proves (SP21) without extending either short third-factor range.
\(\square\)

**Exact coincidences are already absent.** For nonzero Möbius terms the
four factors are squarefree, and prime by prime

\[
(de,fh)\le(d,f)(d,h)(e,f)(e,h)<R^4.
\tag{SP23}
\]

Indeed, if a prime occurs \(a\) times in \((d,e)\) and \(b\) times
in \((f,h)\), with \(a,b\in\{0,1,2\}\), its exponent on the left
is \(\min(a,b)\le ab\), the exponent on the right. If
\(\ell de=mfh\), put \(g=(de,fh)\). The relatively prime factors
\(de/g\), \(fh/g\) force \(de/g\mid m\), so

\[
g\ge de/J>T_l/J\gg X/L^{10}.
\tag{SP24}
\]

This contradicts \(g<R^4=X^{1/175}\) for sufficiently large \(X\).
Thus (SP21) adds a sector of nonzero product differences to the existing
reduction; its center is already empty under the cross-gcd cuts.

Initially Re(s)>1, the actual Dirichlet series is

    C(s)=sum_n c(n)n^(-s)=m_r(s)/L(s,chi),
    m_r(s)=1-chi(r)r^(1-s).                          (R7)

The coefficients are bounded by 1+r, so all initial integrals, series and one s derivative converge absolutely. The accepted G149 exponential test therefore gives

    Q(z)=-d/ds [m_r(s)/(sL(s,chi))], s=a+z.         (R8)

Its growth adapter applies to this source without a new arithmetic hypothesis beyond the stated full Gamma[c] norm bound. For intervals I_i,I_j of length one, opposite translations preserve t+u and put their rectangle in the square with upper endpoint (i+j)/2+1. If K_a(L)<=C exp(2eta L), multiplying by the heavier weight sigma>a gives a block cost `C exp(2eta) exp[-(sigma-a-eta)(i+j)]`. Summing all i,j is finite for sigma>a+eta. This includes arbitrarily unbalanced rectangles. It uses no positivity or self-adjointness of the source: for complex chi the bilinear form is turned into the usual operator norm by conjugating a test input, not chi.

Consequently the every-epsilon/all-L growth bound with eta=gamma-a+epsilon gives holomorphy of Q in Re(s)>gamma, taking epsilon below the desired horizontal margin before summing. Constants may depend on the fixed character, r, real weight and loss.

Because |chi(r)|=1, every zero of m_r lies exactly on Re(s)=1. At a zero rho of L with gamma<Re(rho)<1, m_r(rho) is nonzero and rho is nonzero. If the L zero has multiplicity j, the quantity inside the derivative in (R8) has a genuine order-j pole and its derivative has an order-(j+1) pole with nonzero leading coefficient. Meromorphic identity continuation contradicts Q's holomorphy. No cancellation is supplied by differentiation.

This proves the claimed strip exclusion only below Re(s)=1 directly from this single multiplier. statement:
## G212. Fixed-family binding and complete row/column lifts

Let K=Q(omega), q_a=N(a), with the original primary convention, fixed
excluded set S containing the primes above6 and fixed conductors, and the
original finite ray dictionary. Every character power, including a
cancelled phase, retains its zero at a nonunit. Write
psi_u(b)=chi_b(u) and phi_u=nu psi_u^(+/-1), with nu fixed; nu need not
have order dividing6. All coefficients below are independent of the row
being summed. A moving but fixed puncture is a zero column coefficient,
not a new fixed character datum.

The external input is de Faveri, *Optimal large sieve for fixed order
characters*, [arXiv2610.04045v1, Theorem1.1 and Sections2.3–2.5](https://arxiv.org/html/2610.04045v1).
It is the operator bound for sixth-power-free S-coprime ideal rows AND
columns, with arbitrary column coefficients:

    sum_(q_a<=A)^(6) |sum_(q_b<=B)^(6) lambda_b chi_a(b)|^2
      << (AB)^epsilon T6(A,B) sum_b |lambda_b|^2,
    T6(A,B)=A+B+A^(5/6)B^(1/3)+A^(1/3)B^(5/6).       (1)

The constants depend on the fixed construction data. This manuscript
already cited that theorem in Appendix S.1; its reuse is not a new
discovery of the external result. Its analytic proof and external
definition/import/admission remain named inputs, not newly verified here.

Here is the actual family binding. In the class-number-one Eisenstein
field choose the source's representative generators m_E to be global
primary generators. In its decomposition a=(x)E g^6, x=1 modulo the fixed
ray modulus, take a primary generator g0 of the fractional ideal g.
Then x m_E g0^6 and the primary a0 generate the same ideal and are both1
modulo3. Their quotient is a unit congruent to1 modulo3 and hence equals1.
Thus the source's symbol equals (a0/b)_6 on coprime ideals; its prescribed
zero extension also agrees. Other permissible generator conventions split
into finitely many S-unit classes modulo sixth powers, giving fixed column
twists. Split element units and S-valuations modulo6, then count their
S-supported sixth powers with a logarithmic loss. Absorb nu into the
column coefficients. For the opposite orientation conjugate the WHOLE
inner sum. Reverse residue-symbol orientation, when used, retains the
original finite modulo36 reciprocity sectors. No row-column coefficient
array or moving-conductor character license is inferred.

For a product of J fixed normalized polynomials of lengths X_j, put
B=product X_j. Exact ordered convolution, including all collisions, has

    F_u=sum_b lambda_b psi_u(b),  q_b<<B,
    |lambda_b| << B^(-1/2) d_J(b).                    (2)

Signs, phases, independent heights, original slot coefficients and the
fixed nu remain in lambda. Disjoint slot pools do not imply a slot is
coprime to a plain factor. Write b=d h^6 uniquely with d sixth-power-free,
allowing (d,h)>1. Then

    psi_u(d h^6)=psi_u(d) 1_((u,h)=1),
    sum_d |lambda_(d h^6)|^2 << B^epsilon q_h^(-6).

For each fixed h apply (1) and remove the h restriction only from its
positive outer norm. Hilbert Minkowski sums q_h^(-3), a convergent ideal
series. This gives T6(U,B) on sixth-power-free rows. For ALL rows write
u=a e^6, with all units and S-parts as above. The extra factor
1_((b,e)=1) is a fixed column mask for each e. Applying (1) at U/q_e^6
and summing every e yields

    sum_(0<q_u<<U) |F_u|^2 << (UB)^epsilon Tall(U,B),
    Tall(U,B)=U+B U^(1/6)+U^(5/6)B^(1/3)
                         +U^(1/3)B^(5/6).           (3)

The term B U^(1/6) counts the sixth-power repetitions; they are not a
finite dictionary. No principal or fixed-inducing row is discarded.
The normalized short gate is B<=U^(1/2). In particular S(U^m)^2 Q has
B=U^(2m+v), and two independent plains have B=U^(n1+n2+v). The failed
proposal m+v<=1/2 for a fourth moment lost a factor of2. The correct
2m+v<=1/2 and inverse r+v<=1/2 were already in equation (S.4) of Appendix S.1.

Now take the literal PR9 B3.6 canonical energy, writing X=Z^N,
U=Z^M, F=Z^V:

    E=F^(-1) sum_(q_f~F)^(sf) w(f)
       sum_(0<q_k<<U)
       |X^(-1/2) sum_n^(sf) a0(n)nu(n)rho(n)
           chi_n(k)chi_n(f)^4 d_I(n) W(q_n/X)|^2.    (4)

Here a0=bar(alpha)gamma_2 has modulus1 on good squarefree indices;
w is nonnegative divisor-bounded; rho is the fixed puncture; d_I is
the original product-form mark from fixed disjoint slot pools. Pools,
coefficients and punctures are independent of the live f,k. A fixed
polynomial-size puncture can move between instances. The coefficient
mass for each fixed f is Z^epsilon, uniformly in its natural holes;
F^(-1) cancels the count of f. Thus (3) gives exponent

    Eall(M,N)=max(M,N+M/6,5M/6+N/3,M/3+5N/6)
       = M                    for 0<=N<=M/2,
         5M/6+N/3             for M/2<=N<=M,
         N+M/6                for N>=M.              (5)

This bound alone remains valid for column coefficients depending on the
fixed f, provided the coefficient mass is uniformly controlled. That
extra freedom is NOT available in the label-average argument below.

The full completed theta source has index A=c b^3, c squarefree, and
coefficient

    a0(c)nu(c) bar(alpha(b))^3 nu(b)^3
      chi_A(f)^4 rho(A)d_I(A)V(q_A/X)/(sqrt(q_c)q_b). (6)

Its character is psi_k(A), with all common c,b primes permitted. Each
A has at most one such representation. Writing A=d h^6 gives
d=c b0^3, b=b0 h^2, with c,b0 squarefree and possibly overlapping.
The exponents of d are0,1,3,4. At fixed h the squared coefficient mass
is at most

    X^epsilon q_h^(-4)
       sum_(b0 sf) q_b0^(-2) sum_(q_c<<X/q_h^6) q_c^(-1)
      << X^epsilon q_h^(-4).                        (7)

All whole-index marks, phases and f/puncture/row holes stay in (6).
Minkowski now sums q_h^(-2), again convergent. Both T6 and Tall therefore
apply to the COMPLETE theta source with X as column length. This is not
a restriction to its b=1 or coprime c,b part.

The profile contract is annular support or rapid decay at both endpoints,
with prescribed finite derivative orders. Original common product
profiles use the Fourier measure fixed on the whole ambient box before
the live labels, as in PR9 B3.3. Minkowski and dyadic decomposition sum
these tails; subunit scales are treated at the original profile. Tensor
Sobolev restores the independent heights and the bounded profile/scale
suprema at a fixed polynomial cost H_J. Derivative orders and Fourier
decay precede the final large-scale threshold. This argument does not
grant a new small-x decay bound for an arbitrary sharply reflected
profile. Genuine detector tails keep their own prior payment.

When f=1 and rho=1, the old unmarked completed bound B2.43 may be
combined with (5). The resulting exponent is M, then5M/6+N/3, then
2M-N, thenM on the consecutive intervals
[0,M/2],[M/2,7M/8],[7M/8,M],[M,infinity). Its maximum is9M/8.
For the old marked S.5 scope, z<=M/2, take the minimum with
M+max(0,(N+2z-2M)/4,M+2z-N); e.g. N=.7M,z=.04M improves
1.38M to16M/15. These old-theorem comparisons are not extended to
new labels or punctures without their own proof.

B_p(j)=\begin{cases}

\]
PC2 gives the middle value exactly on its forced valuation. PC3 has divisibility-coefficient mass

## G123. Complete relative mass and full-hole Poisson

For the actual valuation differences modulo6 of l,l', let q1,q2,q3 be
the radicals with residues {1,5},{2,4},{3}. Define

    Q_i=Nq_i, Q=Q1 Q2 Q3, H=Q1 Q2^2 Q3^3.

The complete residue vector e specifies the relative phase. Good-prime
nonzero residues have conductor that prime; fixed ray factors cannot
cancel a conductor outside S. The zero vector is the entire same
sixth-power class, including unequal roots.

For one choice of actual difference signs write

    l=g a x^6, l'=g b y^6, (a,b)=1, Nab>=H,

using the actual gcd g. Multiples of6, including differences with zero
residue, enter x,y. There are at most2^omega(q1q2q3) sign choices; no
coprimality between g and ab is imposed. Allowing all x,y only overcounts.
Put A=Na(Nx)^6,B'=Nb(Ny)^6. The lower supports imply
Ng>=M=max(1,L0/A,L0/B'). Since 1-2sigma<0,

    (AB')^(-sigma) sum_(Ng>=M)(Ng)^(-2sigma)
      << L0^(1-2sigma)(AB')^(-1/2)
       = L0^(1-2sigma)(Nab)^(-1/2)(Nx)^(-3)(Ny)^(-3).

This also holds when L0/sqrt(AB')<1. Both root sums converge. The slot
factor U^((2sigma-1)v) in (1) cancels the v in L0 exactly, proving

    sum_(l/l' in e) |partial b_l partial' b_l'|
       << H_J U^[-(2sigma-1)t+epsilon] H^(-1/2).       (6)

This independent weighted-gcd proof covers all unequal dyads and roots.
The author's separate convergent-dyad proof agrees. Projecting onto large
individual cores only contracts the positive majorant in (6).

There are at most Q^(1+epsilon) vectors in a Q1,Q2,Q3 dyad. Their total
mass is consequently bounded by U^[-(2sigma-1)t+epsilon] * (Q1/Q3)^(1/2)H_J.
Global order6 need not mean Q1>1: a local order3 and a local order2 at
different primes already give order6. Those easier mixed cases are paid.

The actual row factor is

    psi_u(l) conjugate(psi_u(l'))=xi_e(u)1_((u,E_(l,l'))=1).

E retains every shared/trivial-relative prime hole, including exponents0
and6, and the fixed omissions. Its norm is polynomial after termination.
The fixed nu stays in b_l. For e!=0, literal PR9 B3.5 has prefactor
V/sqrt(Q), a normalized Gauss sum, and dual argument V Nh/Q. The dual
zero vanishes. Schwartz decay and lattice counting give
a sum_(h!=0)|F Phi(a Nh)|<<1, a=V/Q, so the primitive sum is
O(min(V,sqrt(Q))). Below the first nonzero-row scale the compact original
sum vanishes, which pays the small-V case. Fixed ray characters and finite
S-valuations retain their phases, conductor factors and holes.

Now impose sixth-freeness exactly by sum_(b^6|u)mu(b), and expand the
complete hole using d|rad E. All resulting phases are retained until
absolute values. The full bound is

    sum_(d|rad E) sum_b min(U/((Nb)^6 Nd),sqrt(Q))
      << U^(1/6)Q^(5/12) product_(p|E)(1+(Np)^(-1/6)).

Split at Nb=(U/(Nd sqrt(Q)))^(1/6). Linear ideal counting and the sixth
power tail pay both parts; if the split is below1, the whole tail is
O(U/Nd), which is smaller than the displayed bound. The hole product
is O_epsilon((NE)^epsilon), hence a requested U^epsilon. Combining with
the trivial row count proves the complete masked kernel estimate

    |K_e(l,l';U)| << H_J U^epsilon min(U,U^(1/6)Q^(5/12)).        (7)

Removing the original fixed finite exceptional free rows costs O_fixed(1),
absorbed in (7). Retaining them is also allowed. All units are retained.
This is not a theorem for arbitrary amplitude subsets or growing
exclusion dictionaries. The optional raw-row analogue covers only a
fixed finite list of excluded sixth-power-core families; its O(U^(1/6))
deletion cost fits (7). It does not license all moving physical selectors.

Multiplying (6) and (7), a complete relative-conductor dyad costs

    H_J U^[-(2sigma-1)t+epsilon]
      min(U(Q1/Q3)^(1/2),
          U^(1/6)Q1^(11/12)Q2^(5/12)Q3^(-1/12)).     (8)

For Q<=V, H>=Q and the ideal count give a total cost
U^[1/6-(2sigma-1)t+epsilon]V^(11/12)H_J. There are only logarithmically
many polynomially supported triples. The same-class contribution uses
the full class square, or (6) with H=1 and the trivial row bound:
U^[1-(2sigma-1)t+epsilon]H_J. It includes every ca^6,cb^6 pair.

# W58 independent review



## Verdict and calibration

The author's principal conditional arguments survive review. Retain the character-preserving minimum harmonic rank, the complete future-partner displacement return and its actual neutral-prime failure, the integrated Mertens Hankel return with the balanced-block growth adapter, and the explicit finite-height two-delay price. These supply exact contracts and scoped failures. They supply no new arithmetic cancellation estimate or endpoint. In particular the Hodge spectral gap is cheaply manufactured while its harmonic rank carries the original difficulty; the Hankel bound remains an unproved complete signed estimate.

The pre-outcome audits are **protected W58-22** and **uniform W58-08**. Audit22 gives an exact native-packet mixed-boundary identity, exposes the unsigned price, and leaves the actual inter-scale map unconstructed. Audit08 constructs a genuine two-variable squarefree lift with the correct diagonal, proves a principal-character branch obstruction for this lift, and gives a squared-lift repair whose holomorphy is equivalent to the original zero-exclusion problem. Neither audit justifies rejecting its entire seed family.

Current accepted calibration remains c11=312864909/2500000000=.1251459636, theta11=.8748540364. A first improved complete field exponent must be strictly below .8748540364, or a squared-energy exponent below 1.7497080728. The author's illustrative gamma=.87485 would conditionally give c=.12515, a gain .0000040364; that arithmetic premise is not proved. No new ordinary-to-Eisenstein, growing-conductor, angular or native H transfer is accepted. Existing F0/analytic ancestry, positive-slot uniformity and external binding/admission obligations remain open.

## Evidence, timing and selection integrity

Frozen author report: 29,331 bytes, SHA256 `35fc8c41f86cdb30b90b8631fca04759fd44144d1002102e5f35331cc99d8f12`. Author manifest SHA256 `91bedcf4f7a1f19be8e081eb7a2059b55a55066610b43d648b9432af49a7bc19`; original seeds SHA256 `55d8cbb0811f4874fbea51ba185d0a0d9c25ebff71b229477f43fbbe066997a1`. All eighteen bound files and the manifest were read as complete bytes and hashed. JSON was parsed and scripts inspected, not executed. `source-receipt.json` records exact pins. The report, partial-work, sampling code/receipts, calculation code/receipt, source manifest, late addendum and worklog received substantive readback. Hashing a historical source is not claimed as reading it.

The author hard deadline was 16:15. It reports a final ancestry/checkpoint update ending 16:15:36, freeze at 16:15:48, and release/absence at 16:16:03. This is **36 seconds late**, not an on-time stop. The critic retains its independent 16:45 deadline. The author sentinel was independently absent at intake. The critic's already acquired exact claim from seed preparation was retained; it was not duplicated or replaced.

Blind preparation froze at 15:44:45, before author outcomes. Its five files plus freeze total 11,931 bytes. Prep freeze SHA256 `29db07348ae16b9598f19989c9e0f8cc5fbdfdd641c9ec98a7b835a5780696e5`; pool SHA256 `c1aacce8446568927a91ee9b5986c35d0f30fb428a33695e2b82ad2e9ee5196c`; order SHA256 `74c64186aef2598b97a12a6da4e65615fbb49e128bbc6ef181cc776bc44a2a27`. One uniform integer below 30! generated the full permutation by factoradic decoding; the original rank, entropy receipt, inverse verification and every original seed ID remain frozen. The priority starts 22,28,05,24,08; the permutation starts 08,17,21,15,10. The final rule excludes the author's six and, for the uniform choice, the protected card. Thus 22 and 08 are forced without any new draw. The final handoff exposed outcomes before `audit-selection.json` was written; the choices nevertheless come mechanically from the earlier immutable orders. This chronology is explicit.

The author used three deliberate slots 26/19/25 and **three actual independent uniform stages**. There were no duplicate exclusions. Original literal p<.10 and p<.01 counts are 27 and 15. After the appropriate previous selections, the complete all-group pools have sizes 24,11,25. Stored zero-based indices 13,7,10 select 17,27,11. Independent `check.py` reconstructs each exact predicate using rational thresholds, compares every entire eligible card in original order, verifies predecessor source/plan hashes, pool-before-entropy timestamps and the exact 256-bit rejection mapping. All pass. None of the low-p cards was removed merely for belonging to another group. No redraw was made. Subjective p denotes generation likelihood, not success probability.

## 1. Character-preserving Hodge rank and displacement: accept at stated scope

For a fixed modulus q, take the vector space on squarefree q-units n<=X, with parity Gamma(n)=mu(n) and diagonal character action W_chi(n)=chi(n). Then Str(W_chi)=M_chi(X), with n=1 present, squareful zeros removed exactly and ramified zeros retained by the q-unit restriction. Requiring an odd differential d with d^2=0 to commute with **every** character modulo q forces its matrix into residue blocks. Character separation on the reduced residue group proves this; a condition for only one character would be weaker and would not give the same blocks.

Write E_a and O_a for positive and negative counts in residue a, and I_a=E_a-O_a. Finite Hodge decomposition into im(d), im(d*) and ker(Delta) cancels equal positive/negative paired dimensions. Consequently

    dim ker(Delta) >= R_q(X) := sum_a |I_a(X)|.

Matching min(E_a,O_a) opposite signs within each residue attains equality. Choosing unit arrows makes each matched Laplacian block the identity, so its nonzero spectral gap is exactly one. A gap without a bound on R_q has no force. The exact finite comparison q=5,X=80 gives I=(0,-3,-4,1), hence minimum rank eight. A fourteen-state rank from a particular differential is not a universal minimum.

Character orthogonality gives

    max_chi |M_chi(X)| <= R_q(X) <= sum_chi |M_chi(X)|
                                      <= phi(q) max_chi |M_chi(X)|.

This is already part of **[private research revision] G135's character/residue/rank-matching equivalence**. The author's late correction credits it correctly. Do not credit a new weaker arithmetic target just because the target has been written as a harmonic rank.

For a fixed neutral prime r, the explicit pairing m<->rm with r not dividing m gives an exact construction. To preserve all characters at once take r=1 mod q; for a single character chi(r)=1 suffices. If chi(r) is not one, the residual multiplier 1-chi(r) is present and may not be dropped. The boundary consists of the appropriate r-free squarefree bases in (X/r,X]. With

    d_q = (1/zeta(2)) product_(p|q) p/(p+1),
    sum_(n<=x,(n,q)=1) mu(n)^2 = d_q x + O_q(sqrt(x)),

obtained from the square-divisor expansion, its harmonic rank is

    d_q (r-1)/(r+1) X + O_(q,r)(sqrt(X)).

This is a linear rank failure for the named construction, not a lower bound for every changed differential. The complex-character signs in the exact finite check and the natural zeros survive.

The global pairing repair is also valid. In each reduced residue class there are infinitely many negative squarefree integers (primes), and infinitely many positive ones (a fixed prime r=1 mod q times different primes in that class). The external input needed for this existence argument is the infinitude of primes in each reduced progression, verified in [NIST DLMF 27.11.9](https://dlmf.nist.gov/27.11.E9). No prime-counting error term is being imported. Increasing-rank pairing is one definite choice; mere existence gives no displacement estimate.

For one fixed global same-residue pairing of all positive and negative q-unit squarefree integers, orient (u,v) by mu(u)=1,mu(v)=-1, and set a=min(u,v),b=max(u,v). Define the **complete** minimum-shell cost

    D_q(X) = sum_(X<=a<2X) (b-a),       X=1,2,4,... .

Every future partner enters, even if b is far larger than 2X. The sum in one shell is finite. If for a common 0<gamma<1 and every epsilon>0,

    D_q(X) <<_(q,epsilon) X^(1+gamma+epsilon)

for all sufficiently large dyadic X and every fixed q, then all ordinary L(s,chi) have no zeros in Re(s)>gamma. Initially Re(s)>1 permits complete absolute regrouping:

    1/L(s,chi) = sum_pairs chi(u)(u^(-s)-v^(-s)).

For sigma=Re(s)>0, the fundamental theorem of calculus yields

    |u^(-s)-v^(-s)| <= |s| (b-a) a^(-sigma-1).

On a compact subset of Re(s)>gamma choose epsilon below its horizontal margin. The dyadic bound is summable uniformly, so the paired series is holomorphic and equals the reciprocal on the initial overlap. The identity L F=1 continues meromorphically. It forbids an L zero and allows a zero of F at the principal pole. All fixed finite heights are covered, without any asserted height-uniform reciprocal growth. Imprimitive L and its finite factors remain the original function. This is a complete conditional return.

For monotone pairing, the number of crossing intervals at a cut is exactly R_q(t), and Tonelli gives total clipped interval length in [A,B] equal to integral_A^B R_q(t)dt. That clipped integral is **not** D_q(A): future portions and intervals entering from earlier shells must be priced. The author's distinction is correct. Under the already known G135 summatory/rank bounds with gamma>1/2, positive and negative endpoint counts give endpoints comparable to k and pair displacement O(k^(gamma+epsilon)); thus the complete D bound follows. The new representation has not bypassed that arithmetic difficulty.

The simplest global neutral-prime pairing has an actual source obstruction:

    D_q(X) = (r-1) sum_(X<=m<2X,(m,qr)=1) mu(m)^2 m
           = (3/2)(r-1)d_(qr) X^2 + O_(q,r)(X^(3/2)).

Partial summation of the same squarefree count proves it; half-open endpoint changes O(X) fit the error. Its positive main coefficient rules out gamma<1 for this rule's positive-cost certificate. It does not rule out other same-residue pairings, signed displacement estimates, or the Möbius target itself. Retain this useful actual-source failure and the explicit complete future-partner Mellin bill. Credit the broader matching mechanism to G135/W55, W01 signed transport and [private research revision] priced coupling.

## 2. Integrated logarithmic Hankel criterion: accept the full conditional bridge

For a fixed ordinary character set M(x)=sum_(n<=x) mu(n)chi(n), with M(x)=0 below one. For 0<a<1 put h_a(v)=exp(-av)M(exp(v)) for v>=0. The full truncated Hankel operator on L2(0,L) has kernel h_a(t+u). No positive diagonal replacement or omission of off-diagonal rectangles is allowed. For complex chi use the bilinear form B(f,g)=integral h_a(t+u)f(t)g(u)dtdu; its norm is the same as the usual sesquilinear operator norm by conjugating one test input. The arithmetic chi is not conjugated or doubled.

If K_a(L)=||Gamma_(a,L)|| is bounded uniformly in L, the forms extend by density to a bounded bilinear form on L2(0,infinity). For Re(z)>0, E_z(t)=exp(-zt) is a holomorphic L2 vector with squared norm 1/(2Re(z)). Hence Q(z)=B(E_z,E_z) is holomorphic and |Q(z)|<=K/(2Re(z)). Initially s=a+z with Re(s)>1 permits Fubini and differentiation:

    Q(z) = integral_0^infinity v M(exp(v)) exp(-sv) dv
         = -d/ds [1/(s L(s,chi))].

A zero of L at rho with Re(rho)>a creates a pole of this derivative; rho is nonzero since a>0. The holomorphic Q cannot have it. The principal pole instead makes 1/L vanish, so creates no false obstruction. The identity theorem for meromorphic functions supplies every finite height. A countable a-sequence decreasing to a common gamma is sufficient for a complete gamma return; uniform constants in a or in growing q are not asserted.

The pole-mode test is correct: for a single kernel R exp(lambda(t+u)), the singular value is |R| integral_0^L exp(2Re(lambda)t)dt. A critical mode Re(lambda)=0 grows linearly; an unstable mode grows exponentially. This identifies a model obstruction, not a license to split an infinite arithmetic spectrum or discard selected modes without paying their complete complement.

The exact Hilbert-Schmidt square is

    integral_0^(2L) w_L(v) exp(-2av) |M(exp(v))|^2 dv,
    w_L(v)=v (v<=L), and 2L-v (L<=v<=2L).

This positive estimate would recover the familiar full logarithmic energy difficulty. The function h(v)=exp(iv^2) provides a legitimate **nonarithmetic** separation: its truncated operator norm is at most sqrt(pi) by extension, Fourier transform at frequency 2t and Plancherel, whereas its Hilbert-Schmidt norm is L. Thus operator and HS targets need not agree as functional bounds. This does not construct arithmetic cancellation for mu(n)chi(n).

The strongest potentially missing step, rectangular blocks away from the diagonal, is paid. For I_j=[j,j+1), the I_i by I_j block is unitarily transported by opposite translations of its two coordinates to the square on [(i+j)/2,(i+j)/2+1). Those translations preserve t+u. Therefore its norm is at most K_a((i+j)/2+1). At a heavier weight sigma>a, the two multipliers cost at most exp(-(sigma-a)(i+j)). If

    K_a(L) <= C exp(2 eta L),       eta>=0,

then the complete sum of block norms is at most

    C exp(2 eta) [1-exp(-(sigma-a-eta))]^(-2)

whenever sigma>a+eta. This includes every off-diagonal rectangle and proves boundedness of the heavier-weight infinite Hankel form. Thus the all-L/every-epsilon hypothesis

    K_a(L) <<_(chi,epsilon) exp(2(gamma-a+epsilon)L),
    0<a<=gamma<1,

returns all ordinary-character zero exclusion Re(s)>gamma. Given sigma>gamma, take epsilon<sigma-gamma before summation. The baseline |M(x)|<=x gives only exponent 2(1-a), so supplies no improvement. At a=1/2, a first c11 gain needs K growth exponent strictly below .7497080728; the 1/6 and 1/4 targets would be 2/3 and 1/2. None is proved here.

The partial-work distribution identity also survives: extending h by zero to v<0 gives (partial_v+a)h_a=sum_n mu(n)chi(n)n^(-a) delta_(log n), including the atom n=1. For compactly supported smooth f,g in (0,infinity), pairing with f*g gives a B(f,g)-B(f',g); the convolution derivative identity has no f(0) endpoint. This produces an H1 by L2 test bound from the accepted Hankel bound, not an unproved converse or a transfer to native H.

Retain the integrated kernel and balanced-block adapter as a useful source-specific interface. General Hankel/observability, old W29 source dictionaries, W50 energy, W54 complete prediction and the existing reciprocal-return library remain substantial ancestry. The claim is not a new general Hankel method or an achieved arithmetic bound.

## 3. Delay bank and the other first tests

For the complete fixed Gaussian field U_chi with Mellin transform exp(tau s^2/2)/L(s,chi), the physical dilation D_lambda U(x)=U(x)-lambda^beta U(x/lambda) has multiplier 1-lambda^(beta-s). The Gaussian left tail and the original complete source remain required. Complete every-epsilon shell L2 bounds of exponent gamma on both channels lambda=2,3 yield holomorphic channel transforms in Re(s)>gamma.

The only common zero of these two multipliers is s=beta: their real parts force Re(s)=beta, and a nonzero common height would imply a nontrivial equality of powers of two and three. Both vanish simply at beta. Thus channel bounds exclude all L zeros in the target half-plane except possibly a **simple real zero at beta**; a multiple zero would still produce poles. The exception must be independently excluded or supplied with another paid channel. Choosing beta in an independently justified zero-free region is sufficient, subject to the accepted source-relative premise. Local division away from beta needs no height-uniform positive floor. This is chiefly G47/G109 and existing detector-bank ancestry.

Conversely simultaneous recurrence gives inf_(t>=T) of any fixed positive weighted sum of the two squared multipliers equal to zero. This is an all-height failure of a uniform floor, not of local division. The explicit finite-height replacement in the author report is valid. With kappa=log(2)log(3)/(2pi) and 0<t0<=|t|<=T,

    max(|m2(beta+it)|,|m3(beta+it)|)
      >= min(2t0 log(3)/pi,
             4 exp(-kappa T)/((log(2)+log(3))sqrt(3))).

Choose nearest integers k,l to t log(2)/(2pi),t log(3)/(2pi). If both vanish the larger phase error is at least t0 log(3). Otherwise distinct integers 3^k and 2^l give |k log(3)-l log(2)|>=exp(-kappa T)/sqrt(3); combining the two phase errors and 2|sin(e/2)|>=2|e|/pi proves the formula. ## 5. Uniform audit W58-08: genuine lift, principal branch obstruction, exact repair

The original seed leaves its two-variable source unspecified. Here is one explicit source satisfying its divisor/cofactor requirement. Fix an ordinary character chi with its natural zeros. For Re(s),Re(t)>1 define

    F_chi(s,t)=sum_(m,n>=1) c(m,n)m^(-s)n^(-t),
    c(m,n)=mu(mn)chi(mn) 2^(-omega(mn))
           (zero if mn is not squarefree).

The prime two is present unless ramified, and c(1,1)=1. Unique allocation of each squarefree prime to m or n gives

    F_chi(s,t)=product_p [1-chi(p)(p^(-s)+p^(-t))/2],
    F_chi(s,s)=1/L(s,chi).

More strongly, on every finite hard product cutoff mn<=X, summing the complete diagonal coefficient of k gives mu(k)chi(k), because a squarefree k has 2^omega(k) divisor allocations. This is an exact source identity, not a decoupled random model. The absolute convergence cone of this series is exactly Re(s)>1 and Re(t)>1: sufficiency follows from the prime sum; the single-prime terms on either coordinate axis force the two respective prime series. Removing finitely many ramified primes does not alter this obstruction at exponent one. Merely introducing a second variable has not enlarged the absolute domain.

There is a useful exact analytic factorization. Write x=chi(p)p^(-s),y=chi(p)p^(-t), and define on D={Re(s)>1/2,Re(t)>1/2}

    log G(s,t)=sum_p [log(1-(x+y)/2)
                     -(1/2)log(1-x)-(1/2)log(1-y)].

Each logarithm is defined by its power series, since |x|,|y|<1. The linear terms cancel. The quadratic term is (x-y)^2/8, and the remainder is bounded uniformly on each compact subset of D by a constant times |x|^2+|y|^2. The prime sum therefore converges normally. Hence G is holomorphic and nowhere zero on D, with G(s,s)=1. On the initial absolute domain,

    F_chi(s,t)^2 L(s,chi)L(t,chi)=G(s,t)^2.                 (A08.1)

For a **principal** character modulo any fixed q, fix a real t0>1. Its L(s,chi) has a simple pole at s=1. If this F had a holomorphic extension to a neighbourhood of (1,t0), equation(A08.1) would give

    F_chi(s,t0)^2=G(s,t0)^2/[L(s,chi)L(t0,chi)],

whose right side has a zero of order one at s=1. The square of a holomorphic function has even vanishing order. This is impossible. Thus this concrete normalized squarefree lift cannot be holomorphic on a whole product half-plane Re(s),Re(t)>gamma for any 1/2<gamma<1, **even if ordinary zero exclusion were available**. On the diagonal the two reciprocal factors coincide and the order becomes two; the original diagonal 1/L is perfectly consistent. A one-variable principal correction cannot be silently omitted in the two-variable construction.

This is an actual source-specific failure of this lift's uncorrected product-domain promise. It does not rule out a sloping tube avoiding (1,t0), a different lift, or a correctly pole-normalized mechanism with its own diagonal return.

A clean repair is to use B=F^2, retaining its actual two-variable convolution coefficients

    b(m,n)=sum_(d|m,e|n) c(d,e)c(m/d,n/e).

They are not the original c coefficients. The meromorphic continuation is explicit:

    B(s,t)=G(s,t)^2/[L(s,chi)L(t,chi)],
    B(s,s)=1/L(s,chi)^2.

For each fixed 1/2<gamma<1, holomorphy of B on the product half-plane is **equivalent** to zero exclusion of L on Re(s)>gamma. In the forward direction fix any safe real t0>1; nonvanishing G prevents cancellation of an L zero in s. In the reverse direction, 1/L is holomorphic on the zero-free half-plane, with a removable zero at the principal pole; multiplication by the holomorphic G gives B. This equivalence claims no growth bound, contour shift, or coefficient cancellation from holomorphy alone. It is a fully paid return, not a new estimate.

### A.1 Finite signed inverse and exact collar

For t>=1,y>=1, define R(t,y)=sum_(n<=t,P^-(n)>y)a(n), with P^-(1)=infinity. Unique least-prime factorization of each nonzero squarefree term gives

    R(t,y)=1-sum_(y<p<=t) chi(p) R(t/p,p).                  (R1)

The strict next-prime threshold removes repeated primes, and ramified prime edges have zero weight. R(t,y)=1 when t<=y. For any approximate state F on the finite descendant set, put

    Delta(t,y)=F(t,y)-1+sum_(y<p<=t)chi(p)F(t/p,p).

Then E=F-R satisfies (I+T)E=Delta. T is nilpotent on that finite graph: along a path primes strictly increase and their product is at most the root x. Expanding the finite inverse yields

    E(x,1)=sum_(d<=x)mu(d)chi(d)Delta(x/d,P^+(d)), P^+(1)=1.  (R2)

Each squarefree product corresponds to exactly one increasing path; all its partial products are admissible. This establishes signs, endpoints, n=1 and every natural zero. It is a signed sum across all depths.

For fixed r>=1 the collar t<=y^r is descendant-closed. Exact values there force Delta=0; conversely zero collar defects and terminal induction force exact values. At r>1 those exact values include shorter products and are not identically1.

On the distinct real-coordinate states (x/d,P^+(d)), the sup-norm to scalar norm for arbitrary independently bounded complex defects outside this collar is EXACTLY

    N_(r,q)(x)=#{d<=x: mu(d)!=0,(d,q)=1,d P^+(d)^r<x}.      (R3)

Triangle inequality proves the upper bound. Assigning the conjugate unit phase of mu(d)chi(d) at each counted state attains it, and finite back substitution realizes those defects by an F. The assignment may depend on x; it is not a single actual arithmetic approximation with that error, nor a lower bound for M_chi. Distinct real t coordinates are crucial.

## 3. A complete column bound

From (UC5), with endpoint exponents greater than one,
\[
|S_z^-(u)|\ll (1+|\Im z|)^C u\qquad(u>0).
\]
Thus every divisor in (UC7) satisfies
\[
q_r\left|S_z^-\!\left(\frac{X_0}{q_\ell q_r}\right)\right|
\ll (1+|\Im z|)^C\frac{X_0}{q_\ell}.
\tag{UC8}
\]
Taking absolute values only after the exact openings gives
\[
|T_e(z)|
\ll (1+|\Im z|)^C\tau(e)X_0
       \sum_\ell q_\ell|S_z^+(Y_e/q_\ell)|.
\tag{UC9}
\]
For each fixed `A>2`, ideal counting and (UC5) give
\[
\sum_\ell q_\ell|S_z^+(Y/q_\ell)|
\ll_A(1+|\Im z|)^{C_A}
\begin{cases}
Y^2,&Y\ge1,\\
Y^A,&0<Y<1.
\end{cases}
\tag{UC10}
\]
For `Y>=1`, split at `q_ell=Y`: a norm dyad `q_ell ~ L` costs
`L^2 min((Y/L)^A,(Y/L)^(-A))`, and both geometric tails sum to `Y^2`.
For `Y<1`, the convergent upper bound is
`Y^A sum_ell q_ell^(1-A)`.

Consequently, for every prescribed `N>0`,
\[
\boxed{
|T_e(z)|
\ll_{N,\epsilon}
(1+|\Im z|)^C
Dq_e^{-2/3+\epsilon}E_N(q_e/D),
\quad E_N(u)=\min(1,u^{-N}).
}
\tag{UC11}
\]
For `q_e>D`, choose the endpoint exponent in (UC10) as `A=3N+2`.
This includes the complete unbounded profile tail. The bound is uniform
on the fixed positive strip used for the row contour shift.

## 3. Complete return and its exact quantifiers

Suppose for each fixed ordinary chi and every epsilon>0, on all large
dyadic shells,

    integral_X^(2X)|V_b(x)| dx/x <<_(chi,epsilon) X^(gamma+epsilon). (R4)

The fixed b and fixed gamma are common to the intended family; the
constant and onset may depend on chi and epsilon. Weighted absolute
integrability for every sigma>gamma is equivalent to (R4): one direction
is dyadic summation, and the reverse bounds one shell by its weight.
The L2 hypothesis with exponent 2gamma+epsilon implies (R4) by shell
Cauchy--Schwarz. No pointwise estimate or uniform conductor constant is
deduced in this step.

Under t=1/x, the small-t Mellin integral is holomorphic on Re s>gamma.
On each compact sub-half-plane choose epsilon strictly smaller than its
distance to the boundary; powers of log x needed for s derivatives are
absorbed by that fixed margin. For t>=1,

    |F(t^b+it)|<=exp(-t^b)/(1-exp(-t^b))

pays the full complementary tail. Hence H is holomorphic there.

For b=3/2 and gamma>1/2, (R3) directly makes 1/L holomorphic on
Re s>gamma. Its numerator Gamma(s)exp(-i*pi*s/2) has no zero or pole
there. Multiplication by L, first away from its principal pole, excludes
every L zero in that half-plane. At s=1 a principal L has its usual pole
and the reciprocal has a zero; this is retained, not called a zero of L.
Natural imprimitive Euler factors are part of L from the beginning;
their zeros on Re s=0 have not been removed from the source.

For a general fixed b>1 and 0<gamma<1 choose FINITE K such that
1-delta K<gamma. Start with the Euler-product zero-free domain Re s>1.
If 1/L is already holomorphic on Re s>alpha, all k>=1 shifted terms
in (R2) are holomorphic on Re s>max(gamma,alpha-delta). Solving (R2)
for 1/L, with the nonvanishing A_0, extends it to that half-plane.
Finitely many repetitions reach Re s>gamma. Strict inequalities at strip
edges cause no gap, because each extension is to an open half-plane.
The SAME H and fixed source occur throughout. Higher shifted reciprocals
are not silently placed in the error where they could have poles.

This is a proved conditional return, not an estimate for (R4). No reverse
equivalence to an ordinary Mertens bound has been shown. At b=3/2 the
conditional energy targets remain 1.7497 for gamma=.87485, 5/3 for
gamma=5/6, and 3/2 for gamma=3/4, each with every epsilon. Any first
gain must use gamma<.8748540364. The boundary gamma in the input is
allowed because the conclusion is the OPEN half-plane sigma>gamma.

Merely increasing the positive prefix cutoff at fixed t charges(1-delta)lambda and eventually loses the existing envelope. Changing t without addressing the far source only moves the balance point; it does not improve the zero-free constant.

There is an exact scalar test for why the new simultaneous information is needed. With no slots and

    ell=5/(5-2delta), r_-=2ell/3, m_-=ell/3,
    r_+=ell, m_+=0,

all three marginal density exponents coincide:

    1-delta r_-=1-2delta m_-
       =1/6+(5/6-delta)r_+=rho.                       (F22)

These scales obey the new cutoff separation and lie inside the surviving coarse box. This does not construct an actual zero or a saturated arithmetic row, and it proves no lower bound for the true mixed norm. It does prove that retaining just the three stated marginal inequalities cannot yield a strict saving: their scalar feasible data still contain the old equality. The report's useful change is the rigorous reduction to the actual compatible mixed source where a new arithmetic estimate must act.

The cutoff change in F1 pays the original v<=.05 prefix and the far complement outside F3; it does not supply OPEN-SEP. For the original fixed t=4/3, the same proof gives F18--F19 at v<=1/25 using the already certified prefix gap. We do not use that narrower version to claim coverage of the larger slot window. The shorter truncation is explicit and its entire new prefix cost is paid in F13.

No direct OPEN-H return follows. Its target unit must remain with weight at least one and its total exponent must be negative. All positive counting exponents here are insufficient for that purpose. At a principal target the separate pole-annihilating kernel remains[s-1+Nn/Y]exp(-Nn/Y), with signal1-rho for rho!=1; a possible nonprincipal zero at1 keeps the unmodified signal-1. Nothing here identifies a new external root-LFunction definition. Near gains,1/6 and1/4 remain stronger conditional targets requiring their own full negative-power source estimate and complete scope.

statement:
### Two discrete dilations

If for every \(\epsilon>0\) and all sufficiently large integers \(N\),
\[
\sum_{b\in\{2,3\}}\sum_{N\le n<2N}|\Delta_bM(n)|^2
\ll N^{2a+1+\epsilon},\qquad 0<a<1, \tag{T10.1}
\]
then \(\zeta\) is zero-free in \(\Re s>a\).

On a unit interval, \(|M(bx)-M(b\lfloor x\rfloor)|\le b\), while \(M(x)=M(\lfloor x\rfloor)\). Thus (T10.1) gives the continuous dyadic \(L^2(dx/x)\) estimate with an affordable \(O(1)\) error on a shell. The shell argument of T09 yields holomorphy of
\[
\int_0^\infty\Delta_bM(x)x^{-s}\frac{dx}{x}
=\frac{b^s-b^\alpha}{s\zeta(s)}. \tag{T10.2}
\]
Both multipliers can vanish only at
\[
s=\alpha+\frac{2\pi i m}{\log2}
 =\alpha+\frac{2\pi i n}{\log3}.
\]
The irrationality of \(\log2/\log3\) forces \(m=n=0\). The remaining real point \(\alpha\) is not a zeta zero: the alternating eta series is positive on \(0<s<1\), and \(1-2^{1-s}<0\). Thus at least one multiplier retains every prospective nontrivial zero. Their inverses need not be uniformly bounded in height.

The exact consistency identity is
\[
\Delta_2M(3x)-3^\alpha\Delta_2M(x)
=\Delta_3M(2x)-2^\alpha\Delta_3M(x).
\]
It gives no contraction or decay without a new arithmetic estimate.
title: Two discrete dilations
