statement:
## Development A: remove the local numerator through a signed future state

Signature: object = complete f3*chi Gaussian and complete mu*chi Gaussian; transformation = exact J Dirichlet convolution plus future-scale inverse of N2; cancellation = signed telescoping with a vanishing large-scale boundary; first unpaid estimate = complete signed M or F moment below theta6; proved return = equal every-epsilon exponents for 1/2<gamma<1, and M's numerator-free zero exclusion. T2--4 contribute, with the future-state mechanism the high-ceiling development.

For sigma>0 define

    ||V||_sigma=sup_(T>0) T^-sigma ||V||_L2([T,2T],dx/x).

Let S_p V(x)=V(x/p), a_p=2chi(p), D_p=I-a_p S_p. For an unramified p and sigma below alpha_p=log2/log p, define

    E_p^- Y(x)=-sum_(j>=1) a_p^-j Y(p^j x).

Minkowski on EACH exact shifted real shell proves

    ||E_p^- Y||_sigma <= ||Y||_sigma/(2p^-sigma-1),
                      0<sigma<alpha_p.              (A1)

The series is convergent in local L2. D_p E_p^-=E_p^- D_p=I on this normed space by index cancellation; the latter equality on a source only known at another exponent requires its boundary. The exact finite formula is

    -sum_(j=1)^J a_p^-j D_p V(p^j x)
       = V(x)-a_p^-J V(p^J x).                        (A2)

The current accepted fixed-character baseline provides a buffered exponent beta with theta6<beta<1 for M and F. The standard fixed Gaussian shift is justified by polynomial reciprocal-L growth on a strictly buffered line, or by the fixed-character Mobius summatory input used in the source library. This is baseline evidence, not a new estimate. With p=2, a_p^-J M(p^J x) tends to zero in every fixed local shell since its norm is O_x(2^(-(1-beta)J)). If2 is ramified, D2=I and no inverse series is taken. Thus E2^- D2 M=M as an actual complete-field identity before assuming an improvement.

The T1 Dirichlet identity gives exactly

    F=J_chi * (D2 M),  D2 M=J_chi^-1 * F,             (A3)

where * denotes sum_r j(r)chi(r)V(x/r), with J_chi already including chi in its coefficients if that convention is used. Never twist twice. For either convention, absolute weighted mass at every sigma>1/2 pays every dilation and the Gaussian small-scale tail. This is the same literal K/H ancestry as G28, stated relative to M rather than A.

If F has the all-large-dyadic every-epsilon exponent gamma in (1/2,1), choose gamma<sigma<1 with sigma-gamma as small as needed. Complete small-scale F norms are finite because of its Gaussian tail. A3 and A1 give M at exponent sigma. Conversely M's complete gamma bound gives D2 M by the finite dilation cost 1+2*2^-sigma, then F by J's finite mass. Letting positive buffers shrink proves exact equality of every-epsilon exponent classes. Constants may blow up as sigma approaches1; no endpoint sigma=1 assertion.

The Mellin transform of M is exp(tau s^2/2)/L(s,chi), first on Re(s)>1. A complete shell exponent gamma makes its Mellin integral holomorphic in Re(s)>gamma, with the Gaussian left tail paid and dyadic Cauchy--Schwarz. Multiplying by L shows the nonvanishing exponential cannot coexist with ANY zero there. A principal pole at1 is not a zero and merely gives the reciprocal's zero. This bridge includes multiple zeros and all fixed heights; ramified factors stay literal. No numerator zero or signed tail is dropped.

At target gamma=5/6 or3/4, A1's prime2 costs are respectively 1/(2^(1/6)-1) and1/(2^(1/4)-1), approximately8.17 and5.29. At theta6 the cost is about11; it is fixed, not a power loss. Thus the coarsest sufficient high-ceiling input is simply the complete signed M Gaussian moment at5/6 or3/4. This is not easier by theorem; it is a concrete change of object with a fully paid return. It can combine representations only after their actual coefficient maps are respected.

An explicit second object is f2(n)=mu(rad(n/2^v2(n))). Its complete field F2 obeys D2 F2=D3 F. Both F2 and F have the accepted buffered beta<1 bound: their ratios to mu have only polynomial-growth finite-prime factors and quadratic-start odd-prime corrections absolutely summable at beta>theta6. A2 therefore proves

    F2=E2^- D3 F                                  (A4)

for unramified2; if2 is ramified the equality reduces to F2=D3 F. For sigma>a3, the causal inverse

    E3^+ Y=sum_(j>=0) (2chi(3))^j Y(x/3^j),
    ||E3^+||_sigma <=1/(1-2*3^-sigma)               (A5)

is exact on Gaussian-tailed sources. Consequently F=E3^+ D2 F2, with the trivial identity if3 is ramified. F2 and F have equivalent every-epsilon exponents in a3<gamma<1. F2's numerator N3 has zeros at a3 only, so its direct zero exclusion above any such gamma is complete. A4 uses future scales rather than an impossible absolute causal inverse at2. It is not valid as a finite moving-window replacement without paying those future tails.

Strongest objection: the future-scale inverse could covertly assume the very improvement being proved, or retain a homogeneous state. A2 explicitly isolates the state; the accepted beta<1 proves it vanishes for M and F2 before the new hypothesis. Without that boundary, x^(1+it0) with a_p p^(-1-it0)=1 is invisible to D2. Such a state is excluded here by the actual baseline, not by topology. At the critical line sigma=1 the inverse diverges, consistently. For3 a baseline beta>a3 does NOT remove the analogous future boundary at a3; that route is not used.

statement:
## 4. The actual row character, contour, and complementary core sum

Initially take a single row Mellin line `Re z=rho>1`, with
\[
\widetilde R(z)=\int_0^\infty R(v)v^{z-1}\,dv.
\]
The six unit multiples annihilate the row sum unless
`vartheta_e|_{mu_6}=1`. For every surviving core,
\[
\sum_{k\ne0}\overline{\vartheta_e(k)}q_k^{-z}
=6L_{\mathbb K}(z,\overline{\vartheta_e}).
\tag{UC12}
\]
This is the **full** Hecke function, with the fixed-prime row Euler
factors retained. The unit-neutrality and primitive-conductor statement
is supplied by [review [private research revision], section 1](../review-cycle-9.md).
Because `e>1` is squarefree, its primitive good conductor `e` is
nontrivial. Hence there is no principal pole at one.

The exact row Mellin identity is
\[
\mathfrak Q_{1,*}
=\frac6{2\pi i}\int_{(\rho)}
\widetilde R(z)K^z
\sum_{\substack{e>1,\ {\rm sf}\\
                 \vartheta_e|_{\mu_6}=1}}
\overline{\beta(e)}
L_{\mathbb K}(z,\overline{\vartheta_e})T_e(z)\,dz.
\tag{UC13}
\]
The initial exchanges, including the coprimality expansion, are
absolute by the original profile tails and `rho>1`.

Fix `0<delta<1` and shift only this row line to `Re z=delta`.
No principal pole at one is crossed. The contour stays to the right
of zero, so it crosses no small-argument Mellin pole of `R` either.
The ordinary functional equation in review [private research revision], section 1, and
three-lines give
\[
|L_{\mathbb K}(\delta+it,\overline{\vartheta_e})|
\ll_{\delta,\epsilon}
q_e^{(1-\delta)/2+\epsilon}(1+|t|)^A.
\tag{UC14}
\]
One may derive this by absolute convergence on `Re z=1+nu`, the
functional equation on `Re z=-nu`, and interpolation. The resulting
`O(nu)` conductor loss is allocated inside `epsilon`. The gamma
quotient has polynomial fixed-strip height growth, with its order
independent of the moving conductor. This is ordinary convexity,
not an invocation of the stronger I-HECKE package.

Equation (UC11), with arbitrarily large `N`, makes the core series
normally convergent on the compact strip used in the shift and pays
every polynomial conductor bound there. The rapid vertical decay of
`R_tilde` on fixed positive lines absorbs all polynomial heights in
(UC11) and (UC14). Horizontal contour integrals vanish accordingly.

Using `|beta(e)|=1` and ideal counting gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
|\mathfrak Q_{1,*}|
&\ll K^\delta D
 \sum_e q_e^{-2/3+(1-\delta)/2+\epsilon}
                   E_N(q_e/D)\\
&\ll K^\delta D^{11/6-\delta/2+\epsilon}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{UC15}
\]
The reverse orientation has the same proof after exchanging the
profiles and angular factors. This proves (UC1). For fixed
`1<=K<=D^B0`, choose `delta>0` sufficiently small in terms of the final
loss and `B0`, allocate the preliminary losses, and obtain (UC2).

A concrete fixed-contour check is useful: at `delta=1/4` and
`K<=D^.87653`,
\[
|\mathfrak Q_{1,*}|+|\mathfrak Q_{*,1}|
\ll D^{1.927465833333\ldots+\epsilon}.
\tag{UC16}
\]
Thus affordability already follows with a fixed positive contour and
a strict power margin, without invoking an endpoint-looking notation.
title: 4. The actual row character, contour, and complementary core sum

### B3. Exact remaining conditional-bias target and return

Use covariance with respect to mu_x and set

    C_P(x)=Cov_mu_x(a_P,r_P)
           =E_mu_x[a_P r_P]-E_mu_x[a_P]E_mu_x[r_P].

Then literally

    F(x)=Z(x) C_P(x)+F_P(x)E_mu_x[r_P].                    (B4)

Because |E r_P|<=1, B3 pays the second term to every power. Since Z(x) is comparable to X on the shell, for any fixed gamma>.5 the current complete moment target is equivalent to

    integral_X^(2X)|C_(P_X)(x)|^2 dx/x
                      <<_epsilon X^(2gamma-2+epsilon).     (B5)

This equivalence is uniform for every chosen family P_X satisfying B3, including a fixed P={2}. It is not a new estimate. At gamma=.874864 it asks an L2 covariance amplitude X^(-.125136+epsilon); the1/6 and1/4 goals ask X^(-1/6+epsilon) and X^(-1/4+epsilon). Every complement has been kept in r_P. The fixed original field F, rather than the moving F_P, enters the existing zero-exclusion transform. Thus no moving-detector analyticity is silently asserted. This normalized covariance exponent is a different proof quantity from G14's .24973/.24898 moment exponents and H's .004 deficit; their numerical savings cannot be added.

In syndrome form, if m_P(s;x)=E_mu_x[r_P|occupancy=s], then

    C_P(x)=sum_s P_mu_x(s)(a_P(s)-E_mu_x[a_P])m_P(s;x).      (B6)

All conditional means, including rare patterns, remain. B2's unconditional product law does not bound B6: the tail phase may correlate with parity after conditioning. Even perfect independence among exposed bits is not independence from r_P. This pinpoints a precise source-exact missing estimate rather than treating high entropy, a small partial parity, or a large number of exposed primes as a gain. No new c follows from B1–6.

For each fixed ordinary chi, replace r_P(n) by chi(n)r_P(n), including its zeros, and define the complex bilinear covariance by the explicit expression E[a_P r]-E[a_P]E[r]. Since |r|<=1, B3–6 and their full norm equivalence still hold verbatim for F_chi, while A13 supplies its own zero return. No independence from the character or change to the positive law is assumed. This extension does not treat ideal norms as integers or claim an Eisenstein transfer.

statement:
### 2. Squarefree sums and the two weaker cancellation bounds

The inherited smooth Poisson estimate, obtained by opening \(\mu^2(k)=\sum_{a^2\mid k}\mu(a)\), is
\[
 \sum_{k\ {\rm sf},(k,M)=1}\psi(k)W(q_k/K)
 \ll(KRq_M)^\epsilon\min(K,K^{1/2}R^{1/4}).
\]
Indeed an ordinary smooth character sum of length \(U\) is \(O(\min(U,\sqrt R))\); split the \(a\)-sum at \(q_a=\sqrt K R^{-1/4}\). Finite coprimality masks are kept during the opening and cost a subpower. For a forced squarefree divisor \(F\), substitution \(g=Fk\) therefore gives
\[
 \sum_{\substack{g\ {\rm sf},\,F\mid g\\(g,M)=1}}
 \frac{\psi(g)}{q_g}W(q_g/G)
 \ll(GRq_Mq_F)^\epsilon G^{-1/2}q_F^{-1/2}R^{1/4}. \tag{T07.4}
\]
Incompatible forced divisors give zero.

For the Hecke improvement fix \(b_0<b<1\), put \(\sigma=b/2\), and keep this choice fixed before varying scales. The inherited buffered bounds and the primitive functional equation give by three lines
\[
 |L(s,\psi)|\ll R^{(b-\Re s)/2+\epsilon}T^A,
 \qquad1-b\le\Re s\le b.
\]
Here \(\sigma\ge1-b\), since \(b>2/3\). The exact series is
\[
 \sum_{\substack{g\ {\rm sf},\,F\mid g\\(g,M)=1}}\psi(g)q_g^{-s}
 =\psi(F)q_F^{-s}\frac{L^S(s,\psi)}{L^S(2s,\psi^2)}
 \prod_{p\mid FM,\,p\notin S}(1+\psi(p)q_p^{-s})^{-1}. \tag{T07.5}
\]
Ramified factors retain value zero. The good part of \(\psi^2\) is nonprincipal; its reciprocal is bounded on \(2\sigma=b>b_0\). Finite factors are nonzero for \(\Re s>0\) and cost \((q_Fq_M)^\epsilon\). Moving the Mellin line gives
\[
 \sum_{\substack{g\ {\rm sf},\,F\mid g\\(g,M)=1}}
 \frac{\psi(g)}{q_g}W(q_g/G)
 \ll(GRq_Mq_F)^\epsilon G^{\sigma-1}q_F^{-\sigma}R^{\sigma/2}T^A.
 \tag{T07.6}
\]
This has the same form as (T07.4), with \(\sigma=1/2\) in the Poisson case.

For bounded marks, assign each marked prime first to \(g\), then to its residual core, then to its cube label. This is a disjoint assignment even when cores and cubes share primes. Forced assignments give divisibility in \(g,u,v,n,n'\); priority exclusions stay inside \(M\). After applying (T07.4) or (T07.6), ideal counting gives
\[
 \sum_{A\mid u}q_u^{-1/2+\sigma/2}E(q_u/H)
 \ll H^{(1+\sigma)/2}q_A^{-1},
\]
and the cube exponents become \(1+3(1+\sigma)/2>1\). Every distinct marked prime pays at least \(q_p^{-\sigma}\). A slot marked once therefore costs at most \(P^{1-\sigma+\epsilon}\); a slot marked on both sides costs at most \(P^{2(1-\sigma)+\epsilon}\), including its equal-prime diagonal. The completed core/cube sums have bound
\[
 G^{-2}Z^{1+\sigma}(L_DL_E)^{(3-\sigma)/2}(q_dq_e)^{\sigma/2}Z^\epsilon.
 \tag{T07.7}
\]
This proves the two weaker cancellation rows after the outer/embedding accounting in §4 below. The actual profiles used in the \(g\)-sum are the annular gcd weight times the two original \(V\)-factors. Their derivatives on \(q_g\asymp G\) have the envelope factors \(E(Gq_uq_n^3/N_D)E(Gq_vq_{n'}^3/N_E)\). Divisor losses involving arbitrarily large columns are absorbed into these envelopes, so no compact truncation of the log-Gaussian is assumed.

## 2. Exact curved-source Mellin extraction

Write a(n)=mu(n)chi(n), so |a(n)|<=1, with zeros at nonunits retained.
For Re s>0 and integer n>=1 put

       I_n(s)=integral_0^infty exp(-nt^b-int)t^(s-1) dt.

Fix an angle 0<vartheta<pi/(2b). Substitution v=nt gives

       I_n(s)=n^(-s) J_s(n^(1-b)),
       J_s(e)=integral_0^infty exp(-iv-e v^b)v^(s-1)dv.

Use the principal powers in the sector -vartheta<=arg v<=0. Rotating
to the ray arg v=-vartheta is legitimate: at infinity cos(b arg v)>0
makes exp(-e v^b) decay, and exp(-iv) has modulus exp(-r sin(-arg v));
the small circle tends to zero for Re s>0. For a fixed positive e the
large arc vanishes. On the rotated ray Re(e v^b)>=0.

Taylor's integral remainder therefore gives, for every integer K>=1,

       I_n(s)=sum_(k=0)^(K-1) A_b,k(s)n^(-s-(b-1)k)+R_n,K(s),
       A_b,k(s)=(-1)^k Gamma(s+bk)exp(-i*pi*(s+bk)/2)/k!,
       |R_n,K(s)|<=C_(b,K,C) n^(-Re(s)-(b-1)K)             (2.1)

uniformly on each compact C in Re s>0. Indeed
|exp(-z)-sum_(k<K)(-z)^k/k!|<=|z|^K/K! for Re z>=0;
the remaining ray integral is bounded by

       exp(vartheta Im s) Gamma(Re s+bK)
       /[K! (sin vartheta)^(Re s+bK)].

The coefficient integral is the Gamma integral rotated to -pi/2; it
converges there because Re(s+bk)>0. The remainder is holomorphic in
Re s>0. Consequently

       R_chi,K(s)=sum_n a(n)R_n,K(s)

converges normally and is holomorphic in
Re s>max(0,1-(b-1)K). This is an ABSOLUTE remainder estimate. No old
Mertens bound, zero-density theorem or Gaussian restoration is used.

Initially for Re s>b, absolute Fubini is valid because
integral_0^infty exp(-nt^b)t^(sigma-1)dt
=Gamma(sigma/b)n^(-sigma/b)/b. Thus

       H_chi(s):=integral_0^infty F_chi(t^b+it)t^(s-1)dt
        =sum_(k<K) A_b,k(s)/L(s+(b-1)k,chi)+R_chi,K(s).  (2.2)

Every denominator on this initial half-plane is its actual ordinary
Dirichlet L-function. There is no change of character, mask or conductor.
Equation (2.2) subsequently has its usual meromorphic continuation.

In the concrete selected case b=3/2, K=1 already yields

       H_chi(s)=Gamma(s)exp(-i*pi*s/2)/L(s,chi)+R_chi,1(s),
       R_chi,1 holomorphic for Re s>1/2.                (2.3)

The numerator has no zero in Re s>0. Unlike a fixed finite scale
difference, the new detector has no missing height on that half-plane.
No size bound uniform in all imaginary parts is asserted: local uniform
holomorphy suffices to exclude each zero at its actual finite height.

## 1. Surviving result: a complete actual coprime rough block is large

The completed result below is stronger than the initial low-gcd plan:
it concerns gcd EXACTLY ONE. It supplies a counterexample to a concrete
dispersion lemma on the ACTUAL coefficient source, not a general-input
operator bound and not a lower bound for the full f3 energy.

Fix tau>0. Let g(u)=(2pi tau)^(-1/2)exp(-u^2/(2tau)), and retain

    f(n)=mu(rad(n/3^v3(n))),
    K_X(m,n)=integral_X^(2X)g(log(m/x))g(log(n/x))dx/x.

Choose a FIXED kappa with kappa^2>=2exp(3tau), and set z=kappa sqrt(X),
L=log X. Let A_R(n)=1_(omega_z(n)>=2), A_T=1-A_R. The original fields
R,T,F have coefficients f A_R,f A_T,f, respectively, so F=T+R exactly.
Threshold masks are frozen throughout x in the CLOSED shell [X,2X].
No moving kappa or tau assertion is used.

For bounded real source coefficients u(n),v(n), write

    C_1(u,v)=sum_((m,n)=1)u(m)v(n)K_X(m,n).             (A1)

Subscripts R,T,F indicate the foregoing literal coefficient families.
This coprime scalar is NOT asserted to be a positive semidefinite form.
Its diagonal contains only m=n=1. R(1)'s coefficient is zero; hence
C_1(R,R), C_1(T,R) and C_1(F,R) contain no true diagonal at all.

Define the positive, full two-prime fields

    V(x)=sum_(z<p<q)g(log(pq/x)),
    U(x)=sum_(r>=2)sum_(z<p<q)g(log(rpq/x)).           (A2)

Every core valuation is included in U. The core r=1 is isolated only
inside the following complete bounds; the theorem does not replace
the original source by that favorable family.

**Theorem A (actual coprime obstruction).** For all sufficiently large X,

    C_1(R,R) >= (1/3)||V||^2 - C_(tau,kappa)X^(3/2),
    C_1(R,R) <= (16/9)||V||^2,
    ||V||^2 asymp_(tau,kappa) X^2/L^4.               (A3)

Thus this ENTIRE signed rough-mask coprime scalar is positive and
comparable to X^2/L^4. Its coefficients are the actual f3 signs.
The lower bound does not require Mertens, a full-field estimate, or
independence of primes. The only analytic input is the accepted fixed-
order PNT used for the independently reviewed critical source theorem.

For an explicit long-shift statement, put

    W_X=log2+sqrt(24tau L),
    I_X=[X exp(-W_X),X exp(W_X)],
    H_X=X/L^6.

Let C_1^H use additionally m,n in I_X, m!=n and |m-n|>H_X. Then

    C_1^H(R,R) >>_(tau,kappa) X^2/L^4.              (A4)

Every integer in this restricted source has exactly two distinct
rough primes, each to the first power. The FOUR rough primes in
every retained pair are all distinct. All residual core valuations,
all coprime cores, all long shifts and both orders are still present.

Using only the already accepted fixed buffered exponent beta, the
opposing interaction is also forced in this same hard region:

    C_1^H(T,R)=-C_1^H(R,R)
                    +O_(beta,tau,kappa)(X^(1+beta)+X^2/L^6),
    C_1^H(T,R) <= -c_(tau,kappa) X^2/L^4             (A5)

for some fixed c_(tau,kappa)>0 and all sufficiently large X.
The reverse ordered scalar C_1^H(R,T) equals C_1^H(T,R) by symmetry
and remains in every full reconstruction.

This refutes the proposed separate-piece estimate

    |C_1^H(R,R)|+|C_1^H(T,R)| << X^(2gamma+epsilon)

for every fixed gamma<1, by choosing 0<epsilon<2-2gamma. Even the
one-sided upper bound on C_1^H(R,R) is false at those exponents.
Thus the proposed assertion quantified over EVERY epsilon>0 fails.
It does NOT refute the
complete signed target G31/G34: the two displayed pieces must cancel
with their actual complementary pieces before any positivity step.

statement:
## 4. D2 — phase-balanced prime blocks and a paid complement

This development concerns a fixed NONPRINCIPAL ordinary character. It cannot by itself meet the all-character objective. Let all unramified primes be partitioned into disjoint finite blocks B and an unmatched set U, with finitely many exceptional primes freely moved to U. Assume fixed m,C and common exponents eta>0,delta_U<1 such that

    |B|<=m, r_B=min B,
    max B-r_B <= C r_B^(1-eta),
    sum_(p in B)chi(p)=0 exactly,
    #{p in U:p<=x} <= C x^delta_U for all x>=2.          (PB)

The constants and m may depend on chi; the desired exponent must be common across the characters being covered. Mere short gaps between some primes or approximate phase balance are not PB. It must account for EVERY unramified prime.

**Proposition.** PB implies that L(s,chi) has no zero in

    Re(s)>gamma_B=max(1/2,1-eta,delta_U).                 (9)

Proof. For s in a fixed compact set with sigma>=sigma0>gamma_B, differentiate u^-s along the positive real axis. Exact phase balance gives

    S_B(s)=sum_(p in B)chi(p)p^-s
          =sum_(p in B)chi(p)(p^-s-r_B^-s),
    |S_B(s)| <= m C |s| r_B^(-sigma0-eta).               (10)

Distinct blocks have distinct integer anchors, so their total is absolutely summable when sigma0+eta>1. Also

    sum_p sum_(j>=2) |chi(p)^j p^(-js)|/j
        <= C_sigma0 sum_(n>=2)n^(-2sigma0)<infinity.      (11)

Partial summation of the COMPLETE unmatched counting bound gives absolute convergence of sum_(p in U)p^-s for sigma0>delta_U. Therefore the full series

    sum_B sum_(p in B)log(1-chi(p)p^-s)
      +sum_(p in U)log(1-chi(p)p^-s)                    (12)

converges locally uniformly on Re(s)>gamma_B. Its exponential is nonzero there and agrees with1/L(s,chi) on Re(s)>1. Since nonprincipal L is holomorphic on this domain, multiplying and applying the identity theorem excludes every zero. No reordering of a conditionally convergent series is asserted before(10)-(12); initial agreement uses absolute convergence on Re(s)>1.

For partial products using complete blocks with r_B<=Y and unmatched primes<=Y, the whole omitted logarithm on a fixed compact has the deliberately coarse bound

    O_K(Y^(1-sigma0-eta)+Y^(1-2sigma0)+Y^(delta_U-sigma0)). (13)

Denominators sigma0+eta-1,2sigma0-1 and sigma0-delta_U are positive fixed constants. The three terms price block singleton mass, higher prime powers, and every unmatched prime respectively. Selecting by anchor can include a few primes above Y; it is the defined complete-block cutoff, and(13) already covers its actual complement. Agreement with the natural product is established in the absolute-convergence half-plane, not by dropping boundary blocks.

For a real character, opposite-sign pairs are the m=2 case. For complex characters, two-prime opposition may be impossible, so PB uses exact zero-sum root-of-unity blocks of bounded size. No existence theorem for these blocks is supplied.

**First-gain calibration.** To beat c10 through(9) one needs eta>.12514596 and delta_U<.87485404. The example eta=.1252,delta_U=.8748 would return the same conditional c=.1252 for every covered nonprincipal character. A restricted matching with unmatched counting exponent1 pays no gain, even if its matched sector is perfect. The principal character has no phase-balanced block at all: chi(p)=1 at every unramified prime. Its unmatched set then has exponent1 and its known pole contradicts any purported globally nonvanishing reciprocal continuation through1. The continuous vacuum in D1 is an actual separate repair, not an automatic extension of PB.

**Comparison and next arithmetic action.** W33 already separates the summable higher powers from the singleton; G76 already gives an actual prime-toggle matching for a different completed source. PB instead specifies matching of ordinary prime phases in the Euler logarithm, charges diameter and ALL unmatched primes, and proves its direct natural-L return. It is a candidate arithmetic transport estimate, not a claimed new prime distribution theorem. The next useful test is an actual-character construction proving PB with these common exponents, or a continuous-vacuum analogue for principal chi with its discrepancy paid. A finite matched list, numerical prime gaps, or pair-only formula cannot certify either infinite statement.

statement:
## UR6. The finite scalar, every interaction, and exact exponent return

For the exact finite tuple set, the coefficient is `chi(n)lambda(n)w_delta,X(n)` with real nonnegative w. Expanding its Hilbert norm gives D20 exactly:

    Q(X)=sum_(n,m in [A_X,B_X])
       chi(n)conjugate(chi(m))lambda(nm) K_X(n,m)
                                 integral_I w_delta,X(n)w_delta,X(m) ddelta.

No source pair, ordered mixed term or repeated product representation is omitted. The entire scalar is real and nonnegative because it is a squared norm; individual summands need not be positive or even real. For complex characters, conjugation on the second output is indispensable. Averaging the individual energies in delta is the definition of this norm, so no cross-delta term belongs to it.

Completing the square in the product of the two g1 factors gives

    K_X(n,m)=g_2(log(n/m))
       *integral_0^(log 2) g_(1/2)(u-log(sqrt(nm)/X))du.

Both the exponent and normalization agree: the product prefactor is `1/(2 pi)`, as is that of g2 times g_(1/2). The parameter integral is exactly the signed sum of the 1296 permutation-pair terms obtained from two squared Vandermondes. For each resulting integer r it uses `(r^(-1/5)-r^(-1/4))/log r`, with continuous value `1/20` at r=1. This is a finite identity, not a positive-sieve replacement for the signed moment.

Now assume the full D20 estimate `Q(X)<<_(chi,epsilon) X^(1.74898+epsilon)` for every epsilon>0 and all sufficiently large dyadic X. Put

    gamma=87449/100000=.87449,
    q=437/500=.874,
    gamma-q=49/100000=.00049.

Taking square roots and using UR5 gives

    ||H|| <= O(X^(gamma+epsilon/2))+O(X^q)+X^(-1+o(1)).

Thus `||H||^2<<X^(2gamma+epsilon)` for every epsilon>0. One may directly use `(u+v+w)^2<=3(u^2+v^2+w^2)`. If expanded instead, the largest target-tail cross term has exponent `gamma+q+epsilon/2=1.74849+epsilon/2`, and the median square has exponent `2q=1.748`; both lie below `2gamma+epsilon=1.74898+epsilon`. All cross terms with the product-tail norm are much smaller. Mixed terms between the three discarded sectors are also included in UR5's norm triangle inequality and its square. Every mixed contribution is paid below the claimed target exponent.

UR4 then excludes all zeros of the specified ordinary L-function in

    Re s>.87449,

so `c=1-gamma=.12551` follows CONDITIONALLY. For the family conclusion the same D20 hypothesis is required separately for every ordinary character. A zeta-only D20 theorem yields only the zeta conclusion.

The optional inherited-calibration computation D21 also checks. If the full H norm has exponent `beta=.8749` and R=H-Z has exponent q=.874, then

    | ||H||^2-||Z||^2 | <=2||H||||R||+||R||^2
                      <<X^(1.7489+epsilon)+X^(1.748+epsilon).

Its largest exponent is below 1.74898 by `1/12500=.00008`; choose the arbitrary calibration buffer correspondingly small when a strict comparison is wanted. This includes both ordered mixed terms and the error square. The direct norm implication does not need this smaller calibration margin.

The E_delta field is also correctly priced in D12--D13: each of its three products has every shift at least delta, giving `|e_delta(n)|<=4d_3(n)n^(-delta)`, hence a uniform weighted absolute norm at `4/5+epsilon` and a Gaussian field `O(x^(4/5+epsilon))`. E is already included in H's actual coefficients and in D20; it is not silently removed in the moment target. The cofactor absolute coefficient norm at beta>3/5 likewise follows from beta+2delta>1. These facts validate the optional baseline calibration but supply no new signed estimate.

The diagonal is `X^(1+o(1))`: w<=d3, `d3(n)^2<=d9(n)`, `K_X(n,n)<=constant`, and `B_X=X^(1+o(1))` give this by `sum_(n<=t)d9(n)<=t(1+log t)^8`. The coefficient inequality can be seen prime by prime: any pair of weak three-part compositions of k is the row/column margin pair of a nonnegative 3 by 3 integer matrix of total k. Choose one such matrix deterministically; different margin pairs give different matrices. Counting matrices gives `binom(k+2,2)^2<=binom(k+8,8)`, and multiplicativity finishes. Therefore the true remaining estimate concerns the complete signed off-diagonal, not an omitted diagonal or analytic tail.

## 2. The merged integer-state norm has exponent1 for every fixed collar

THEOREM A. Fix an integer r>=1 and a fixed principal ordinary character
chi0 modulo q. For G92's complete integer-state norm,

    lim_(N->infinity) log B_(r,chi0)(N)/log N =1.          (3)

More precisely, fix u>2 with omega'(u)!=0 and put

    P=N^(1/(u+r+1)),  kappa_r=(1-2^(-r))/r.

Then, as N runs through all sufficiently large positive integers,

    sum_(P<p<=2P) sum_(m>p^r) C_(N,chi0)(m,p)
       ~ -(q/phi(q))*omega'(u)*kappa_r
                    *N*P^(-r)/(log P)^3.                (4)

Consequently B_(r,chi0)(N) is at least a positive constant times
N^((u+1)/(u+r+1))/(log N)^3. This is a lower bound for the actual merged
coefficient norm; no unmerged count is substituted.

Proof. For fixed p, all integers m>p^r form a consecutive half-line. Its
disjoint intervals (N/[p(m+1)],N/(pm)] cover exactly

    (0,U_p],  U_p=N/(p*(p^r+1)).

Therefore their COMPLETE signed sum is

    sum_(m>p^r) C_(N,chi0)(m,p)=-W_q(U_p,p-).             (5)

For p in (P,2P], p is unramified for sufficiently large N,
U_p=(N/p^(r+1))*(1+O(p^(-r))), and

    log U_p/log p = u+O_(u,r)(1/log P).

The same small compact neighborhood of u works for EVERY prime in the
band. Formula(2), K=1, now gives uniformly

    W_q(U_p,p-)=(q/phi(q))*(omega'(u)+o(1))
                         *N/(p^(r+1)*(log P)^2).

All these block sums have one sign. Ordinary PNT and partial summation give

    sum_(P<p<=2P) p^(-r-1)
           ~ kappa_r P^(-r)/log P.

Together these prove (4). In particular the boundary m=p^r is not included;
using p^r instead of p^r+1 in (5) would be an incorrect exact identity.

For every arbitrarily large U there is u>U, away from integers, with
omega'(u)!=0. Otherwise omega would be constant on a tail. The equation
u*omega'(u)=omega(u-1)-omega(u) propagates that constant backwards one
unit at a time to (1,2), contradicting omega(u)=1/u. Continuity of omega'
at the selected u gives the required fixed-sign compact neighborhood.
Thus the exponents (u+1)/(u+r+1) in (4) approach1. The elementary upper
bound B<=N follows by expanding each merged coefficient, counting each
squarefree d exactly once, and using |chi0(d)|<=1. This proves (3).

This proves an issue explicitly left OPEN in G92 A5. The previously known
real-state exponent1 does not prove (3); equation(5) and the nonzero
friable main term do. The old example of complete cancellation in a single
integer fibre remains true and is compatible with (3).

An especially structured worst-case residual already witnesses (4): set
Delta(m,p) equal to one common sign for p in (P,2P] and m>p^r, and zero
elsewhere. It is bounded, constant across quotient states, and has no
path-depth tag. Finite triangular back substitution constructs a
floor-invariant F with precisely this residual and the exact collar.
This is NOT an assertion that a particular natural approximation has that
residual, and NOT a lower bound for M_chi.

   a power over its trivial exponent 3/2 but does not improve c11.

Initially for Re s>b, absolute Fubini is valid because
integral_0^infty exp(-nt^b)t^(sigma-1)dt
=Gamma(sigma/b)n^(-sigma/b)/b. Thus

       H_chi(s):=integral_0^infty F_chi(t^b+it)t^(s-1)dt
        =sum_(k<K) A_b,k(s)/L(s+(b-1)k,chi)+R_chi,K(s).  (2.2)

Every denominator on this initial half-plane is its actual ordinary
Dirichlet L-function. There is no change of character, mask or conductor.
Equation (2.2) subsequently has its usual meromorphic continuation.

In the concrete selected case b=3/2, K=1 already yields

       H_chi(s)=Gamma(s)exp(-i*pi*s/2)/L(s,chi)+R_chi,1(s),
       R_chi,1 holomorphic for Re s>1/2.                (2.3)

The numerator has no zero in Re s>0. Unlike a fixed finite scale
difference, the new detector has no missing height on that half-plane.
No size bound uniform in all imaginary parts is asserted: local uniform
holomorphy suffices to exclude each zero at its actual finite height.

## 3. Complete endpoint contract and target arithmetic

For b=3/2 suppose that, for every epsilon>0 and all sufficiently large
dyadic X,

       E_chi(X)=integral_X^(2X)|V_(3/2),chi(x)|^2 dx/x
                 <<_(chi,epsilon) X^(2gamma+epsilon),   (3.1)

where 1/2<gamma<1 is common to every fixed ordinary character required
by the family theorem. Constants and onsets may depend on chi and epsilon.
This is the COMPLETE source on every point of the physical shell, not a
sample grid, a truncated n sum, or a selection of additive major arcs.

For sigma>gamma, choose epsilon<2(sigma-gamma). Cauchy--Schwarz on
dyadic x shells proves convergence and locally uniform holomorphy of
integral_0^1 F_chi(t^(3/2)+it)t^(s-1)dt. At t>=1 the bound
|F_chi(t^(3/2)+it)|<=exp(-t^(3/2))/(1-exp(-t^(3/2))) pays the entire
upper tail. Thus H_chi is holomorphic on Re s>gamma. By (2.3), so is
1/L(s,chi), hence L has no zero there. More explicitly the continued
identity L(s,chi)[H_chi(s)-R_chi,1(s)]=Gamma(s)exp(-i*pi*s/2)
precludes a zero. For a principal character its pole at s=1 becomes a
zero of the reciprocal; the usual pole exception is retained.

Imprimitive L-functions are the inducing primitive L times their finite
Euler factors. We have used the exact original coefficients and L, so
all such factors are included; their zeros lie on Re s=0 and do not
create an unmentioned exception here. This is an ordinary-character
statement only. It neither resolves the project's external definition
bindings nor widens to Hecke characters or conductor-uniform bounds.

The weakest sufficient energy exponent for a first gain is any exponent
strictly smaller than 2theta11=1.7497080728 in the every-epsilon sense.
Concrete complete conditional targets are:

       gamma=.87485 -> c=.12515, E << X^(1.7497+epsilon);
       gamma=5/6    -> c=1/6,    E << X^(5/3+epsilon);
       gamma=3/4    -> c=1/4,    E << X^(3/2+epsilon).

Section 7 below proves that the actual diagonal has size X^(3/2),
but this is not a bound for E: signed off-diagonal terms remain.
Equality at gamma
in (3.1) is admissible because the return is on the open half-plane
sigma>gamma with an epsilon chosen AFTER sigma. No strict-reserve
vanishing is labeled an impossibility theorem.

More weakly, the return itself only needs

       integral_X^(2X)|V_(3/2),chi(x)| dx/x
                        <<_(chi,epsilon) X^(gamma+epsilon)           (3.2)

on every large dyadic shell. Equivalently, it needs
integral_1^infinity |V(x)|x^(-sigma)dx/x finite for every sigma>gamma.
Shell Cauchy--Schwarz makes (3.1) sufficient for (3.2); (3.2) is not
silently upgraded to an L2 estimate. This weighted absolute Mellin
condition is the weakest complete bound used in this proof. A first
gain requires gamma<theta11; the displayed energy targets are a more
structured sufficient way to reach it. No pointwise bound is required.

## 4. Actual coarse arithmetic theorem, including the infinite tail

Unconditionally, for every fixed ordinary character and every epsilon>0,

       V_(3/2),chi(x) <<_(chi,epsilon) x^(5/4+epsilon).  (4.1)

Here is a complete elementary proof. Put N=x^(3/2),
T=N(log x)^2 and U=V=floor(sqrt x); all assertions are for sufficiently
large real x. First use the exact finite identity

       mu=mu_<=U+mu_<=V-mu_<=U*mu_<=V*1
                         +mu_>U*mu_>V*1,

The identity follows on writing mu_>U=mu-mu_<=U and using mu*1=delta.
It holds at every integer, including n=1 and both short cutoffs; no
squareful coefficient or prime power is silently removed. This is the
all-integer extension of the standard Vaughan decomposition. The two
short sums contribute O(U+V). At each real x the integers U,V are fixed
before the auxiliary prefix Y or partial summation is used. No moving
cutoff is differentiated.

For fixed modulus r, finite additive Fourier inversion writes
chi(n)=sum_(ell=0)^(r-1)c_ell exp(2*pi*i*ell*n/r). Coefficients c_ell
are fixed and sum |c_ell|<=r is enough. This preserves the exact zeros
of chi before the triangle inequality; no nonunit is reclassified.
It suffices to bound each phase beta=ell/r-1/(2*pi*x).

We need two elementary geometric-sum estimates. Uniformly for fixed r
and ell, real x large, 1<=Y<=T and M,H>=1,

 sum_(d<=x) min(Y/d,1/(2||beta d||))
                 <<_r x log(2x)+Y/x,                  (4.2)
 sum_(h<=H) min(M,1/(2||beta h||))
                 <<_r (H/x+1)(M+x log(2x)).            (4.3)

A vanishing denominator means the first argument of min is used.
For (4.3), split h into blocks of length at most x and into its r
residue classes. Within each resulting progression the real phase moves
monotonically by r/(2*pi*x) per step and over a total interval shorter
than 1/(2*pi). It encounters at most one integer. Apart from at most
two nearest points, the inverse distances have a harmonic-series bound
O_r(x log(2x)); the nearest points cost O(M). Summing the fixed r
classes and O(H/x+1) blocks proves (4.3), without a Diophantine
approximation, an integer-x assumption, or an omitted resonant point.

For (4.2), a residue class with ell*d=0 mod r has distance
d/(2*pi*x) for 1<=d<=x, and contributes O(x log(2x)). Otherwise its
fractional initial phase j/r has j>=1. If a zero is crossed, it is
at d=2*pi*x*j/r, at least 2*pi*x/r. In a sufficiently small fixed
neighborhood of that crossing d is at least c_r*x, so the closest
points cost O_r(Y/x); all remaining points again have a harmonic
inverse-distance bound O_r(x log(2x)). Away from any crossing the
distance is bounded below by a fixed r-dependent constant, or is
covered by the same harmonic estimate. The possible distance to the
integer 1 is bounded below by 1/r on these nonzero classes. This
proves (4.2), including exact resonance at a noninteger-selected x.

Type I has coefficient
c_d=sum_(ab=d,a<=U,b<=V)mu(a)mu(b), supported on d<=UV<=x.
The bound |c_d|<=tau(d)<<_epsilon d^epsilon and the geometric bound
for sum_(k<=Y/d) exp(2*pi*i*beta*d*k), followed by (4.2), give
O_(r,epsilon)(x^(1+epsilon)). Polylogarithms and a harmless change
of epsilon absorb Y/x<=x^(1/2)(log x)^2.

For Type II group the large factor m>U and d=ck with c>V. The exact
second coefficient is b_d=sum_(c|d,c>V)mu(c); in particular |b_d|<=tau(d).
Both m,d>U and both are <=Y/U. Partition them into dyadic intervals
(M,2M], (L,2L]. A box with a nonempty hyperbolic cutoff md<=Y has
ML<=Y, and M,L<<Y/U. All endpoint rounding is included in constants.
In one box the sum is

       B=sum_m mu(m) sum_d b_d e(beta md)1_(md<=Y),
       e(v)=exp(2*pi*i*v).

Cauchy in m leaves the COMPLETE Gram expression

       |B|^2 <= C M sum_(d1,d2) b_d1 conjugate(b_d2)
                     sum_(m in I(d1,d2)) e(beta m(d1-d2)),             (4.4)

where I(d1,d2) is the intersection of (M,2M] with
m<=Y/max(d1,d2). The right side before further bounding is a
nonnegative square sum. This retains the physical cutoff, every
off-diagonal term, and its complex phase. Each I is a single interval;
thus its geometric sum is bounded by min(CM,1/(2||beta(d1-d2)||)).
The diagonal and (4.3), now taking absolute values of the signed
off-diagonal coefficients, yield

       |B|^2 <<_epsilon T^epsilon
          [M^2 L+ML (L/x+1)(M+x log(2x))]
        <<_epsilon T^epsilon (Y^2/U+Y^2/x+Y*x) log(2x).

Since U is comparable to sqrt x and Y<=x^(3/2)(log x)^2, this is
O_epsilon(x^(5/2+epsilon)). The O(log^2 x) boxes, the two short
sums, Type I, and the finitely many character Fourier shifts prove

       sup_(0<=Y<=T)|sum_(n<=Y)mu(n)chi(n)exp(-in/x)|
                       <<_(chi,epsilon) x^(5/4+epsilon).             (4.5)

Partial summation with exp(-n/N) costs at most this supremum. The
entire omitted tail, before using any cancellation, is at most

       sum_(n>T) exp(-n/N) << N exp(-(log x)^2),

which is O_A(x^(-A)) for every fixed A. Hence (4.1) follows for the
original INFINITE source, for EVERY sufficiently large real x. This
also gives the unconditional complete energy E_chi(X)<<X^(5/2+epsilon).
It is a nontrivial arithmetic saving of 1/4 in the pointwise exponent
relative to the trivial damping-length exponent 3/2. It is too weak
to exclude any new zero in the critical strip through Section 3.

The exact cost preventing a first gain in this coarse proof is visible:
the term Y*x in the squared Type II bound, and also the longest-factor
diagonal term Y^2/U, both cost x^(5/2) at the chosen parameters.
Changing a scalar reserve does not remove either term. For a general
damping length Y=x^b, the same absolute spacing step pays Y*x and
therefore a pointwise certificate exponent at least (b+1)/2>1.
This is an obstruction to THAT INEQUALITY CERTIFICATE, not a lower
bound for the actual source or an impossibility theorem for a better
signed estimate. The surviving target is arithmetic cancellation in
the complete (4.4), or a different factorization that does not pay the
short additive-difference correlations individually.

There is a SECOND unpaid branch: the present Type I bound has exponent
1, also above every target gamma in Section 3. Improving only Type II
to exponent gamma would therefore NOT complete a gain. The exact
ledger is: short terms exponent 1/2 (paid for gamma>1/2), Type I
exponent 1 (unpaid), Type II exponent 5/4 (unpaid), and the full
damping tail O_A(x^(-A)) (paid). A sufficient modular repair would
bound BOTH full smoothed Type I and Type II shell L1 norms by
X^(gamma+epsilon), with the actual cutoff/character terms retained.
A direct bound for their signed combination is also eligible and is
weaker than separately bounding both. Neither repair is proved here.

## 5. The growing-conductor branch exposed by rational frequencies

There is a substantive limitation beyond a diagonal heuristic. Let P
be prime with P not dividing the fixed modulus of chi and let (a,P)=1.
For Re s>1, direct finite character orthogonality gives the EXACT identity

 D_(a/P),chi(s):=sum_n mu(n)chi(n)e(an/P)n^(-s)
   = (1/(P-1)) sum_(psi mod P) psi(a) tau(conjugate(psi))
                                  /L(s,chi*psi)
      -chi(P)P^(-s)/L(s,chi*psi0).                    (5.1)

Here tau(conjugate(psi))=sum_(u=1)^(P-1)conjugate(psi(u))e(u/P),
psi0 is the principal character mod P, and products mean the ordinary
character on the common modulus with natural zeros. The first term
is precisely the P-unit part. For the omitted multiples n=Pm,
mu(Pm)=-mu(m)1_(P not dividing m); their phase is 1. This gives
the second term, including the zero at P^2, and proves (5.1).
Since tau(psi0)=-1, the psi0 coefficient can equivalently be written

       [-1/(P-1)-chi(P)P^(-s)]/L(s,chi*psi0),
       L(s,chi*psi0)=(1-chi(P)P^(-s))L(s,chi).

The curve includes x=P/(2*pi), where its additive phase is e(-n/P),
so a=-1 and the damping length is (P/(2*pi))^(3/2). Thus the proposed
complete source hypothesis encounters genuine growing-modulus twisted
L-functions. Bounds with constants depending arbitrarily on each fixed
character do NOT supply uniform control of this branch. No separately
reviewed low-conductor joint-density claim is imported here. Individual
uniform twist bounds plus absolute Gauss-sum summation can lose up to
square-root P; collective signed control, or a direct source proof,
would have to avoid that loss. Formula (5.1) is not used to claim that
such a loss is necessary for the actual signed sum.

This explains why the attractive diagonal exponent 3/2 in the source
energy is only a target. Neither fixed-conductor zero exclusion nor
discarding the nonprincipal twists proves it. Conversely, these
auxiliary twists do not change the scope of the completed return:
Section 3 itself excludes zeros of each original fixed L(s,chi), with
all heights and its principal pole exception paid.

## 6. General curved scaling, retained for a different future estimate

For any FIXED b>1 and 0<gamma<1, the complete every-epsilon shell bound
for V_b with exponent 2gamma implies zero exclusion on Re s>gamma.
Choose a finite K with 1-(b-1)K<gamma. Equation (2.2) then has a
holomorphic remainder throughout that half-plane. Start with the known
zero-free half-plane Re s>1 and descend in strips of width b-1. In
each next strip all k>=1 shifted reciprocals in (2.2) are already
holomorphic. Since A_b,0(s)=Gamma(s)exp(-i*pi*s/2) has no zero for
Re s>0, the unshifted reciprocal is holomorphic there too. Finitely
many steps reach Re s>gamma; equivalently continue to any compact
sub-half-plane Re s>=gamma+delta and then let delta>0 vary. The
argument retains every shifted reciprocal rather than declaring it
an error on a region where it may have poles.

Here b, K and the source itself are fixed before x tends to infinity.
There is no claim for b depending on x or for constants uniform as
b decreases to 1. Taking b<3/2 might reduce the raw diagonal price,
but the same coarse absolute Type II term x^(b+1) still gives no
subunit pointwise exponent. Thus this generalization does not evade
the identified arithmetic cost by parameter tuning.

## 7. Actual diagonal and a sharp obstruction to termwise absolute pricing

For every fixed q, the squarefree unit count satisfies

       Q_q(Y)=sum_(n<=Y)mu(n)^2 1_((n,q)=1)
             =d_q Y+O_q(sqrt Y),
       d_q=(1/zeta(2)) product_(p|q)(1+1/p)^(-1)>0.       (7.1)

This follows elementarily from mu(n)^2=sum_(d^2|n)mu(d): restrict
(d,q)=1, count the remaining integers coprime to q with error O_q(1),
and bound the d>sqrt Y tail of the absolutely convergent sum d^(-2).
Partial summation gives

 sum_n |a(n)|^2 exp(-2n/x^b)=d_q x^b/2+O_q(x^(b/2)).

The full source energy is the absolutely convergent double series

       E_b,chi(X)=sum_(n,m) a(n)conjugate(a(m)) K_X(n,m),
       K_X(n,m)=integral_1^2
         exp(-(n+m)/(X^b*u^b)) exp(-i(n-m)/(X*u)) du/u.   (7.2)

Absolute Fubini is licensed by the damping and |a|<=1. Its actual
diagonal contribution is therefore

       d_q(2^b-1)X^b/(2b)+O_q(X^(b/2)).                 (7.3)

For b=3/2 this is the target scale of the conditional quarter energy,
with every character-zero loss included in d_q. It is NOT a lower
bound for E: off-diagonal terms can cancel a diagonal contribution.

There is nevertheless an unconditional lower bound for the TERMWISE
ABSOLUTE off-diagonal price, using the actual coefficients, not an
arbitrary sequence. For every fixed b>1 and ordinary chi,

       sum_(n!=m)|a(n)a(m)K_X(n,m)| >>_(q,b) X^(b+1).   (7.4)

To prove it, set N=X^b and partition the integer interval [N,2N] into
consecutive bins of length at most H=floor(X/4). By (7.1), the total
number A of squarefree units there is d_q N+O_q(sqrt N+1). If there
are B=O(N/H+1) bins and A_j such integers in bin j, Cauchy gives
sum_j A_j^2>=A^2/B >>_q NH. Subtract the A diagonal pairs; since
H tends to infinity, there are still >>_q NH ordered distinct pairs.
For each, |n-m|<=X/4 and n+m<=4X^b, whence

       Re K_X(n,m)>=exp(-4)cos(1/4)log 2>0.

At squarefree units |a(n)a(m)|=1. Summing only these pairs proves
(7.4), with the full remaining infinite sum nonnegative after absolute
values. No assertion about the signs of mu(n)mu(m) is made.

At b=3/2 this price is at least X^(5/2), matching the exponent of the
coarse energy certificate. Thus any proof that prices the actual
near-diagonal pairs separately by absolute value cannot reach even
the first-gain energy exponent below 1.7497080728. This is stronger
than identifying a diagonal heuristic and narrower than excluding
signed dispersion: it explicitly leaves collective cancellation among
these actual squarefree pairs eligible. Natural character zeros do
not evade the obstruction for ANY fixed ordinary character.

The pointwise estimate (4.1) still uses the actual mu convolution law;
(7.4) concerns a different, absolute Gram price and is not claimed
to prove sharpness of the true source magnitude. In particular this
pass is not solely a new norm counterexample: it supplies the paid
moving-source return and an actual arithmetic power saving, then
identifies exactly why its coarse method stops short.

## 8. Result, limitations, source evidence and next action

The unconditional results are the exact pole-preserving curved-source
return, the actual source estimate (4.1), the exact full rational
frequency decomposition (5.1), and the actual-coefficient bounds
(7.3)--(7.4). The complete improved energy/L1 bounds in Section 3
are conditional arithmetic targets, NOT proved estimates. No c increase
is claimed; c11 and all its existing obligations remain unchanged.

The next useful task is narrowly identifiable: improve the signed Type II
Gram expression before (4.4)'s off-diagonal absolute values AND the full
Type I contribution, or control their exact signed recombination,
uniformly on the real physical shell. Retain the two short terms,
all character Fourier shifts and the exponentially damped tail. A bound
only on one dyadic box or one prime denominator is insufficient. The
method would require a genuinely stronger aggregate estimate, not a
renaming of the source norm or an unsupported diagonal calculation.

The proved pointwise exponent 5/4 exceeds theta11 by .3751459636.
Its energy exponent 5/2 exceeds the first-gain threshold by .7502919272;
the quarter target requires a full power of X improvement in that
energy certificate. These gaps are arithmetic tasks, not available
reserves. No equivalence of the curved-source hypothesis to an ordinary
Mertens bound has been proved or assumed. Its moving rational-frequency
branches in Section 5 must be faced by any attempted import.

This pass did try a deliberately coarse rigorous estimate; it did not
stop after proposing (3.1). It succeeds as a restricted arithmetic
theorem, but its power saving is measured against length x^(3/2), not
against the observation scale x. That distinction is exactly why it
does not beat the incumbent, 1/6 or 1/4.

Primary outside sources consulted in this pass:

- Bourgain, Sarnak, Ziegler, *Disjointness of Mobius from horocycle flows*,
  original author PDF, Theorem 2 pp.2--7. Fixed small parameter, sufficiently
  large cutoff; the criterion is not a uniform power-saving assertion.
  https://publications.ias.edu/sites/default/files/disjointness%20b-s-z%20oct.pdf
- Green and Tao, *Quadratic uniformity of the Mobius function*, original
  published PDF (Ann. Inst. Fourier 58 (2008)), Lemma 4.1, pp.1876--1877
  (PDF pages 15--16), checked from the primary source. The source assumes
  integer U,V,N with UV<=N and works on N<n<=2N. Our all-integer identity
  explicitly restores both short terms, so it does not apply that
  dyadic statement outside its hypotheses. The finite identity above
  is independently derived from mu*1=delta.
  https://aif.centre-mersenne.org/item/10.5802/aif.2401.pdf

No external theorem supplies (3.1). The elementary identities and contour
estimates used here are proved in the report. This work does not retire
any of the retained 29 families/109 children, near gains, or 1/6 and 1/4.

### Evidence limits and bounded completion

The companion check.py/checks.json checks the all-integer Vaughan
identity through 512, including a complex mod-5 character with its
natural zeros; it also checks (5.1) coefficientwise in the exact
cyclotomic ring for P=5, a=-1, chi mod 3 through 512. Fractions bind
the current calibration and the three conditional target budgets.
Those checks succeeded once; they do not prove any asymptotic bound,
contour shift, zero exclusion or exponent. The written proofs above
carry those statements. No unchanged successful helper was replayed.

checks.json records SHA256 pins for the inspected local source ancestry
and identifies exact primary-web pages. The web PDFs were inspected
through the web tool; no original binary download/hash is falsely
claimed. The related round24 C5 is an antecedent idea, not an imported
proved bound. Original theorem credits remain with their authors.

The same task suffered two stream interruptions (a6b8f29e-e72f-44b4-a931-
a5401db6329d, then [private operational identifier omitted]); root reconciled
the intact claim and saved artifacts. The original 12:00 author and
12:30 reviewer deadlines were retained. Current mathematical work is
complete; only full readback, frozen manifest, exact own-claim release,
absence verification and the single authorized review handoff remain.

## 8. Original fields, corrections, profiles and complete tails

Both preprojection corrections vanish on this exact prime sector by divisibility and support. Equality `pi*g=pi'*g'` would force pi into the opposite shorter source or into pi', impossible. Equality `P*pi*g^3=P'*pi'*g'^3` would force pi into P', pi' or g', also impossible at the stated original endpoints. Their intersection is empty. This does not remove the corrections from any composite or other source branch.

The theorem keeps all ordered g,g', including the exceptional short-row mode, shared short factors and opposite orientations. It uses G^2 in the raw conductor argument and both absolute adapter terms. There is no unexplained coherent G saving. Each graph may be frozen with the short pair, but is independent of live R,P,P'. The original two arrays remain independent; reversing an edge is not automatically complex conjugation for unequal arrays or an arbitrary complex core.

After the common profile separation, each side has its own original norm heights, component coefficients, source and short profiles, and scalar kernel gain. The row factor in a mixed pair has the actual height difference. The raw radial estimate charges `(3+|t-t'|)^(2delta+epsilon)` and variation; the new transport charges a gradient. On a fixed compact annulus away from zero, differentiating `rho_0(q_x) q_x^(i tau)` gives a fixed polynomial in the original height vectors, with no K power after the stated rescaling. Each cost is bounded by a fixed product polynomial in the two heights.

M B2.21--22 gives one common Fourier separation per side and weighted L1 bounds of every fixed required order for its actual density. Choose the differentiability order above those finitely many powers before integrating against the **product** of the two original densities. This preserves both scalar kernel gains and every component cross term. No row-dependent density, equal-height restriction or zero-height specialization is introduced. The new graph error uses only one derivative and so fits this existing order mechanism. No assertion that all heights are Z^epsilon is needed.

All sharp row/source/short/mark cutoffs stay on their original variables and at their original endpoints. The raw row theorem explicitly handles the full sharp interval and its two boundary strips. The new mean-value calculation does not differentiate its indicator. The sharp graph, including a strict far mask and floor boundary, is likewise never differentiated. No sharp-JD adapter or changed polynomial column profile is invoked; RHR's ancillary JD qualification is therefore respected.

For complete source and root tails, first apply M B2.23 and B2.37 to the original discarded series, before separation or transport. The discarded kernel argument exceeds `Z^(tau_ref/2)`, while all original source/root, row, tuple and branch counts have a fixed polynomial majorant `Z^Btail` chosen independently of the Schwartz order. An order exceeding `1+2(Btail+A)/tau_ref` makes the full linear tail `O(Z^(-A))` times the original seminorm. To bound the two mixed retained/discarded terms and the double tail, multiply by a fixed absolute polynomial bound for the complete opposite side and increase A once. The graph mask has modulus at most one; fixed bounded weights only change the constant, so the same absolute proof applies.

Centering also preserves this control. On a finite common-unit fibre, conditional counting expectation is an L1 contraction and its complement costs at most two. Thus the mean/fluctuation split introduces no conductor-sized tail factor. As in the source, transport is defined on the same retained components while keeping the original discarded tail unchanged, or retaining its exact paid correction. A shifted discarded profile is not simply assigned its former kernel argument. This is the precise source-return convention needed here.

The result covers the same-scale degree-one prime packet and any other literal blocks satisfying all displayed hypotheses and gates. It does not sum an independently widened range, estimate arbitrary unequal-block interactions, replace prime/composite or composite/composite Type II coefficients, or pay the other cusp/root systems. Fixed bad-place, inert and exceptional branches outside the stated packet remain obligations of full H. The report says so explicitly and does not delete them by analogy.

## 3. The retained Bc term in the actual paired ledger

Use c_s,d_s for genuine first-support widths, distinct from the zero-free constant. Put m=min(c_s,d_s), T=(c_s-d_s)_+, so c_s=m+T. LA.4 asks for

    sum_lambda N_C,lambda <= Z^[p+A-c_s+R+E+Bc+small],
    Bc=(3c_s-5d_s-R)_+/6,

and the side-exchanged target for D. The first outside factor and joint Cauchy then give

    M+p-(c_s+d_s)/2+R/2+(Bc+Bd)/2 <= M.

There is no new label count after these bounds. Retaining Bc in their relative excess does not alter that already proved target balance.

For either signed first-side orientation, the literal row and enclosing width are

    w=u0 e F_c G_c V_id h',
    W=M-R-T+Lc-6a, Lc<=5(R-R0), R<=m.                 (R1)

The original actual enclosing radius is used, and only its favorable -omega is discarded in this upper row bound. The child width remains M'=M-T-6a-omega-g2+t2 with its own exact padding; it is not confused with W. Both active residues 1+t_p and 1-t_p modulo six retain canceled-residue holes. No equality of their F_c is assumed.

Put rho=1-10delta/[3(5-2delta)] and k=rho+delta-1. For delta in [.68,.70], 19/54<=rho<=103/273<2/5, in particular 4rho-1>0 and 5rho-1>0. LA.13 is the final paired normalized excess inside the joint C norm:

    M(rho-1)+delta A+a(5-6rho)+E1+E2+small,
    E1=(1-rho)T-delta c_s-(1+rho)R-E-Bc+rho Lc+R0,
    E2=g2-t2-(1+delta)b2.                              (R2)

Substitution in R1 gives

    E1 <= -(delta-4rho+1)m-kT-E-Bc.                   (R3)

For c_s>=d_s, Bc=(3T-2m-R)_+/6>=(T-m)_+/2 since R<=m. For c_s<d_s, T=0 and the same bound is trivial. Set a_s=delta-4rho+1 and

    h_s=(a_s+k)/2=delta-(3/2)rho.

The claimed strengthening is now an elementary two-case inequality:

    a_s m+kT+(T-m)_+/2-h_s(m+T)
      = (2-5rho)(m-T)/2,           T<=m;
      = (5rho-1)(T-m)/2,           T>=m.              (R4)

Both are nonnegative. Hence **E1<=-h_s c_s**, with -E and any extra Bc still favorable. This is a uniform relaxation of actual valuations; equality in the relaxed variables is not claimed attainable by genuine prime valuations. E2<=-delta b2-t2 remains unchanged.

Retain the full signed second projector B3.65, its two extraction scalars and unrestricted quotients. Its label is outside the row reconstruction and its dyadic count is paid once by B3.69. The remaining shortening of the two plain factors independently contributes -delta rbar, where rbar is the average of their clipped nonnegative reductions. The surviving slot widths satisfy

    zbar=(z1+z2)/2 >= z-c_s-b2-rbar-small.             (R5)

This is the original incidence inequality for the actual two extracted columns; it counts multiplicities. The missing first radical is frozen before summation, and all remaining labels reconstruct divisor-many from the actual signed row. Natural canceled holes are not arbitrary row-dependent slot coefficients. The common Fourier majorant precedes labels. These are exactly the accepted [restricted research revision] transport gates, unchanged by R4.

Use only the accepted weighted gain eta_old=2k. Let s=c_s+b2+rbar. Because h_s<delta, the support/plain terms save at least h_s s. If s>=z, that gives h_s z and uses no weighted-width hypothesis. If s<z, R1 gives W>=M-c_s-6a>M-z-6a. Under M-6a>22z, each z_j<=z<W/21, so the old raw weighted estimate applies to both factors in their common paired normalization. The combined saving is at least

    h_s s+2k(z-s)-small >= min(h_s,2k)z-small.        (R6)

Thus g_old(delta)=min(h_s,2k) is the valid gain. No additional square root or second use of extraction scalars is allowed or needed. A nonempty negative nominal window is treated at its bounded supported scale in the old branch; the weighted case has strictly positive W. All-slot-exhaustion and clipped-width-zero cases are covered.

At q=17/25,

    g_old(q)=h_s(q)=g0=519/4550,
    2k(q)-h_s(q)=1/1950>0.

Furthermore h_s'=1+25/(5-2delta)^2>0, whereas 2k'=2-100/[3(5-2delta)^2]>=-139/243. The minimum need not be differentiable at its corner. Nevertheless each constituent obeys the same one-sided slope bound, so

    g_old(delta)>=g0-(139/243)(delta-q)               (R7)

on the full interval. This is the correct corner argument. It does not replace g_old everywhere by the larger constant g0.

# [private research revision]: complete square-source estimates and an enlarged factorization range

Accept G176-G178 from the frozen [author](square-source/report.md),
[independent review](square-source-review/report.md) and the reviewer's
[collision proof](square-source-review/support.md). This completes the
headroom pass begun at20:46:55.898UTC on12October2026. Its useful addition
is a complete estimate for a changed arithmetic source, with all square-row
collisions and complementary terms paid. The remaining signed core is open.
The accepted source-relative c11=312864909/2500000000=.1251459636 does not change.

Root reconstructed both proofs, including the independent strengthening,
read the complete helpers and receipts, and checked14 byte-preserved files,
nine inherited source bindings and two current-source pins. The latter refer
to the preceding revision93c3d864ae1a890b3fb98f69178b76a0a440de3a. The
[retention manifest](retention-manifest.json) distinguishes these integrity
checks from the mathematical arguments. No helper was rerun. Both owners
stopped and normally released their own claims; no claim bytes were copied.

F0/analytic ancestry, original positive-slot uniformity and exact external
root-definition/import/admission remain open. No formalization, new proof
packet, record admission, growing-conductor estimate or Hecke extension is
claimed. Original29-family/109-child history and subsequent results survive.

## G176. A compensated Liouville source with all square collisions paid

Fix an ordinary character chi modulo q, with natural zero extension, and a
fixed prime p not dividing q. All convolutions below are Dirichlet convolutions.
Let a(n)=lambda(n)chi(n), h(n)=chi(n), and s(r^2)=chi(r)^2, with s zero off
squares. The prime-power identity gives a*h=s. Set

    q1=delta_1-p chi(p)delta_p,
    q2=delta_1-p chi(p)^2 delta_(p^2), v=q1*q2,
    b=v*h, g=a*s, c=v*g=a*a*b.

Complete multiplicativity a(d)a(e)=a(de) includes shared primes and natural
zeros. There is no corresponding unrestricted identity for mu. The exact
Dirichlet series on Re z>1 is

    D_c(z)=P_p(z)J_p(z)L(2z,chi^2)^2/L(z,chi),
    P_p(z)=1-chi(p)p^(1-z), J_p(z)=1-chi(p)^2p^(1-2z).

In particular the p^2 coefficient of q2 is -p chi(p)^2, not -p^2 chi(p)^2.
The ordinary and root sequences

    b(n)=chi(n)[1-p1_(p|n)-p1_(p^2|n)+p^2 1_(p^3|n)],
    beta(r)=chi(r)^2(1-p1_(p|r))

have zero means and periods p^3q and pq. The source v*s retains the two
physical root rows d r^2 and p d r^2 with weights1 and -p chi(p).
This combines W49's exact square convolutions with [restricted research revision]/[restricted research revision] compensation;
the complete new cross-row estimate below is the substantive addition.

Use f_x(n)=exp(-n/x^(3/2)-i(n/x)^6), real x in[X,2X], and dx/x norms.
For fixed alpha0<1, every1<=A<=pX^alpha0 and every frozen root prefix R,
including infinity, satisfy

    ||sum_(r<=R) beta(r) f_x(A r^2)||_2
        <<_(p,q,alpha0) 1+X^(3/8)A^(-1/4).                 (1)

For completeness, choose R0=c0(X/A)^(6/11), with c0 small and fixed.
Each nonzero periodic Fourier frequency stays separated from integers
through this low prefix, including the last discrete increment. Discrete
first-derivative summation and Abel summation of the actual damping pay
every low prefix by O(1). Above R0 the complete positive shell kernel is

    exp(-cA(r^2+s^2)/X^(3/2))
          min(1,[(X/A)^6/|r^12-s^12|]^2).

Its diagonal costs X^(3/4)A^(-1/2). Summing both off-diagonal orientations
costs (X/A)^6 R0^(-10)=(X/A)^(6/11), no larger than that diagonal.
The norm triangle inequality pays the low/high interaction and all aliases.

Now take arbitrary frozen |u_d|<=1 and arbitrary frozen row-prefix endpoints
R_de. Retain both e labels and form the complete source

    Q_D(x)=sum_(d<=D) u_d sum_(e=1,p) q1(e)
                           sum_(r<=R_de) beta(r) f_x(e d r^2),
    1<=D<=X^alpha0.

The strengthened bound is

    ||Q_D||_2^2 << D^2+X^(6/11)D^(16/11)+X^(3/4)D^(1/2)
                    +min(X^(3/5)D^(7/5),X^(15/16)D^(1/2)).  (2)

All constants depend only on the stated fixed data. There is no hidden
logarithmic or divisor-epsilon loss in(2). It bounds the full merged source.

Here is the decisive collision argument. Write
W_D(n)=#{d<=D:n/d is an integer square}. The exact count is

    sum_(n<=Y)W_D(n)^2
      =sum_(a squarefree,a<=D) sum_(u,v<=sqrt(D/a))
                         floor(sqrt(Y/a)/lcm(u,v))
      << sqrt(YD).                                        (3)

Indeed d1=a u^2,d2=a v^2 can collide only when their squarefree kernels
agree. After floor(t)<=t, the remaining absolute series is bounded by
2sqrt(YD) sum_(u,v) gcd(u,v)/(uv max(u,v)). Substitution u=g h,v=g k
reduces convergence to sum_g g^(-2) sum_k H_k/k^2<infinity. Thus every
coincident square divisor and repeated multiplier is paid.

Remove the exact low prefix from each row. Its total norm is O(D). The
merged remaining coefficient z_X(n) obeys

    |z_X(n)|<=C_p W_(pD)(n),
    n>N0=c0^2 p^(-1/11)X^(12/11)D^(-1/11).

Positive coefficient domination survives every original prefix mask.
It is not domination of a signed norm by a selected signed subset.
On a comparable block n,m~N put H_N=X^6/N^5. W24's complete local
multiplicity count gives one positive kernel bound

    exp(-cN/X^(3/2))[H_N D+sqrt(ND)min(N^(1/3),D)].

The independent collision estimate(3), integer row sum O(1+H_N) and
2|z_n z_m|<=|z_n|^2+|z_m|^2 give another bound for that SAME block,
exp(-cN/X^(3/2))sqrt(ND)(1+H_N). Their minimum is at most a fixed
multiple of

    exp(-cN/X^(3/2))
      [H_N D+sqrt(ND)(1+min(N^(1/3),D,H_N))].              (4)

Summing H_N D from N0 yields X^(6/11)D^(16/11); actual infinite damping
pays the isolated diagonal by X^(3/4)D^(1/2). The remaining expression
grows then decreases geometrically. Its meeting scale is
N=X^(6/5)D^(-1/5) if D<=X^(3/8), otherwise N=X^(9/8), giving the two
alternatives in(2). For far pairs the full kernel and both cumulative
masses give X^12 D N^(-11); summing from N0 gives O(D^2). Both
orientations and low/high interactions remain included.

## G177. Complete adaptive core and conditional all-height return

Fix3/4<=gamma<1. Let

    L=X^gamma, M=X^((6-2gamma)/4), Q=p^3q,
    eta=1/(6000Q), B(n)=min(L,eta X^6/n^5),
    U(n)=B(n)^tau, V(n)=B(n)^(1-tau).

Choose tau before real x, in the closed corridor

    max(gamma tau,gamma(1-tau)) <= (11gamma-3)/8.          (5)

The identity c=a*a*b gives exactly c=Q_U+Q_V-S_tau+R_tau, where

    Q_U(n)=sum_(de=n,d<=U(n))a(d)(v*s)(e),
    S_tau(n)=sum_(de l=n,d<=U(n),e<=V(n))a(d)a(e)b(l),
    R_tau(n)=sum_(de l=n,d>U(n),e>V(n))a(d)a(e)b(l).

Define C_p,chi(x)=sum_n c(n)f_x(n) and the full finite core
T_tau,X(x)=sum_(L<n<=M)R_tau(n)f_x(n). Then

    ||C_p,chi-T_tau,X||_j <<_(fixed data,epsilon) X^(gamma+epsilon),
    j=1,2, for every epsilon>0, uniformly in(5).           (6)

To see the improvement, the norm exponents of(2) at D=X^alpha are
alpha,(3+8alpha)/11,3/8+alpha/4 and
min(3/10+7alpha/10,15/32+alpha/4). All are at most gamma under(5),
so both complete short sources cost O(X^gamma), including endpoint equality.
The root cuts remain prefixes because B(edr^2) decreases in r. The
small-double source is O(X^gamma) by the zero-mean period of b and the
original fixed derivative-gap cut. The coefficient bound
|R_tau(n)|<=(p+1)^2d_3(n) pays n<=L and the complete n>M tail, whose
squared bound is X^(3/2+epsilon)+X^6M^(-4+epsilon). Norm inequalities
pay all complementary interactions. No signed submask bound is imported.

The actual merged residual is

    R_tau(n)=sum_(m l=n) a(m)D_(U(n),V(n))(m)b(l),
    D_(U,V)(m)=#{ordered(d,e):de=m,d>U,e>V}.

Complete multiplicativity retains one sign times an ordered divisor count;
it does not prove cancellation. Near n~X the cofactor l<n/X^gamma is
short, but every cofactor and all of the interval through M remain in T.

The remaining hypothesis OPEN-LC is the full L1 bound

    integral_X^(2X)|T_tau_X,X(x)| dx/x << X^(gamma+epsilon) (7)

for every epsilon>0 and all sufficiently large dyadic X, for each fixed
ordinary character and each of a fixed covering pair of unramified primes,
at one common gamma chosen before the character and candidate zero.
Tau_X may vary with the shell and epsilon, before x;(6) is uniform.
The complete C and T norm hypotheses are equivalent by(6). Their
equivalence to zero exclusion is not asserted. A full L2 bound suffices
but does not follow from the L1 statement.

Under(7), H_p(z)=integral_0^infinity C_p,chi(1/t)t^(z-1)dt is holomorphic
on Re z>gamma, by shell summation and the damping at x near zero.
[restricted research revision]'s clockwise contour rotation, first on Re z>3/2, gives

    H_p(z)=A0(z)P_p(z)J_p(z)L(2z,chi^2)^2/L(z,chi)+E_p(z),
    A0(z)=Gamma(z/6)exp(-i pi z/12)/6,                    (8)

with E_p normally holomorphic on Re z>1/2: each coefficient integral
has remainder O_K(n^(-Re z-1/2)), locally with derivatives. A0 and
J_p L(2z,chi^2)^2 are nonzero in Re z>1/2. The zeros of P_p lie on
Re z=1. Two distinct primes have no common nonzero-height zero there,
since character values are roots of unity and log p1/log p2 is irrational.
For nonprincipal chi choose p1 with chi(p1)!=1 to cover height zero;
for principal chi the pole at1 is the permitted exception. This proves
the conditional exclusion of every finite-height zero in Re z>gamma.
Imprimitive factors, natural zeros and fixed-character dependencies stay.

| Conditional c | gamma | M exponent | alpha cap | allowed tau |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| .1252 | 2187/2500 | 5313/5000 | 16557/20000 | [313/5832,5519/5832] |
| 1/6 | 5/6 | 13/12 | 37/48 | [3/40,37/40] |
| 1/4 | 3/4 | 9/8 | 21/32 | [1/8,7/8] |

The reviewer's improvement is below gamma=17/21; it leaves the nearer
and1/6 rows unchanged. At1/4 the author's range[1/3,2/3] expands to
[1/8,7/8]. None of these rows proves(7). The near target would improve
c11 by135091/2500000000 if that missing full estimate were established.

## G178. Actual variance, complete logarithmic test and higher-ceiling scope

The actual coefficient g has the exact variance identity

    |g(n)|^2=1_((n,q)=1) sum_(d^2|n)d_2(d^2),
    sum_(n<=Y)|g(n)|^2=C_chi Y+O_q(sqrt(Y)log^2(2Y)),
    C_chi=(phi(q)/q)sum_((d,q)=1)d_2(d^2)/d^2>0.

At each prime power the identity is sum_(j<=floor(nu/2))(2j+1)
=(floor(nu/2)+1)^2. Counting coprime integers and d_2(d^2)<=d_3(d)
pays the errors and the convergent constant. The finite v convolution
retains all its cross terms under Cauchy-Schwarz and gives
sum_(n<=Y)|c(n)|^2<<_(p,q)Y. It does not assert an exact c asymptotic.

Consequently, for M>=X the full actual source tail satisfies

    ||sum_(n>M)c(n)f_x(n)||_2^2 << X^(3/2)+X^6 M^(-4).   (9)

The integer off-diagonal row sum is O(X^6/n^5). Both orientations,
the actual damped diagonal and all far pairs are included. At M=X,
the complete coarse bound is ||C||_2<<X, which fails the first-gain target.

The exact expansion g(n)=sum_(r^2m=n)d_2(r)chi(r)^2 mu(m)chi(m)
transfers the fixed-degree logarithmic input from
[Green-Tao, Theorem1.1, pp542-543](https://annals.math.princeton.edu/wp-content/uploads/annals-v175-n2-p03-p.pdf).
Use the fixed torus/filtration, finite character expansion and a fixed
logarithmic cutoff in r; pay the entire remaining square tail absolutely.
No GRH power remark or growing complexity is imported. Abel summation
of the actual damping and M=X(log X)^B in(9) then give, for each fixed D,

    ||C||_2^2 << X^(3/2)+X^2(log X)^(-D),
    ||C||_1 << X^(3/4)+X(log X)^(-D).                     (10)

The constants may be ineffective. Every fixed D still falls short of a
power X^(gamma+epsilon), gamma<1. Equation(6) transfers the logarithmic
bound to the complete core. This is a complete arithmetic test with a
recorded failure, not an inferred power improvement. Standard Liouville
Euler ancestry is also noted in
[Humphries, arXiv v2, pp1-2](https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/1569441/1/Humphries_the_distribution_of_weighted_sums_of_the_liouville.pdf);
his RH/LI/moment distribution hypotheses are not used.

For fixed k>2,b>1, the same single-square argument gives high cost
X^(b/2)A^(-1/2)+(X/A)^(k/(2k-1)). If b>=2k/(2k-1), the first term
dominates. Even the weaker Minkowski short-source corridor
alpha<=(4gamma-b)/3 is nonempty for every fixed gamma>1/2, by choosing
fixed1<b<=2gamma and sufficiently large fixed k. The complete return
retains all K shifts D_c(z+(b-1)j), with1-(b-1)K<gamma. Finite strip
descent makes every positive shift holomorphic before solving the
unshifted reciprocal with the covering primes. This is conditional
architectural reach only; no endpoint gamma=1/2 or variable-parameter
estimate is asserted.

The independent finite run checked56 exact collision identities, three
masked-row examples and five rational target rows; the author recorded
7680 frozen-cut identities. Those checks support algebra and bookkeeping.
The asymptotic proofs are(1)-(10) and the full retained arguments.
The next useful work is signed cancellation in the actual ordered-divisor
core, exploiting the enlarged asymmetric range, or a new upstream source
with a complete return. Merely improving an already affordable tail would
not close OPEN-LC.
