statement:
# [private research revision] discovery-first headroom pass: nonlinear-phase source compression



## Current worklog and calibration

The accepted written baseline is c11=312864909/2500000000=.1251459636,
theta11=.8748540364. Its F0, positive-slot and original external-binding
obligations remain open. This report neither discharges them nor widens
the fixed ordinary-character scope. All 29 families and 109 original
children remain available; nothing here retires them.

Read: current recombination policy; current index entries; the complete
[private research revision] G125-G127 curved-source integration. The previous author's frozen
[private research revision] output and its reviewer are complete, not this pass's work.
Completed this pass: discovery comparison; nonlinear Mellin return; exact
energy compression; actual tail asymptotic; imported polynomial cancellation
and its full-source logarithmic consequence; complete L1/L2 conditional
targets; exact exponent check. Remaining: independent review and, for any
numeric gain, the explicitly OPEN signed core estimate. No c gain is claimed.

## Discovery comparison before selection

1. **Coherent nonprincipal Gauss bank / short-arc averaging.** Reuse G126's
   exact whole-shell bank, including its paid principal Gauss and P-divisible
   branches. The useful target is energy <1.7497080728. Averaging over all
   characters is not the coherent bank, and the available generic source
   energy still has the old 2.5 price. A new signed short-arc estimate
   is needed. This is credible but too close to the previous linear source
   without a genuinely new arithmetic input.

2. **Quadratic-character family moments.** An outside primary result of
   Peng Gao and Liangyi Zhao, *Mean squares of quadratic twists of the
   Mobius function*, arXiv:2212.09241v2 (23 December 2022), Theorem 1.1,
   explicitly assumes GRH. It averages real quadratic characters with
   compact smooth profiles. It supplies neither a fixed complex-character
   coherent bank nor an unconditional moment. Its Poisson arithmetic is a
   possible long-term ingredient; importing its headline asymptotic now
   would be circular. Source inspected at https://arxiv.org/pdf/2212.09241 .

3. **Exact Vaughan cancellation before Type I/II pricing.** The all-integer
   convolution in G125 retains short terms and both long factors. For the
   principal character modulo one, the geometric Type I factor
   1/(exp(dz)-1) has a leading harmonic-divisor component at small dz;
   taking that component's absolute value costs exponent 1. A signed
   cancellation with Type II is possible, but neither a formal convolution
   identity nor the old 5/4 bound establishes it. No separate term may be
   deleted as a harmless major-arc contribution.

4. **Selected upstream change: a fixed superlinear phase.** Replace
   exp(-i n/x) by exp(-i(n/x)^k), with fixed integer k>2, retaining damping
   exp(-n/x^b), fixed b>1. The leading Mellin multiplier is expected to be
   Gamma(s/k)exp(-i*pi*s/(2k))/k, which has no zeros on Re(s)>0. Frequency
   gaps n^k-m^k grow strongly with n. This can pay a long physical tail by
   absolute integration while preserving a full zero detector. It is not a
   parameter change to Gao's local window or to the old linear Gauss bank.
   The live question is whether the remaining transition core admits an
   actual arithmetic power bound; a source transformation alone is no gain.

The fourth mechanism is selected for substantive development. Its plausible
reach includes 1/6 and 1/4 if the complete signed core is controlled. A
separate generic tail theorem would still be useful only if its bounds,
cross terms and exact residual source are stated, rather than advertised
as a new Mertens theorem.

A focused neglected-component check also read W14 seed 24 and its recorded
failure: no usable nonlinear phase retaining the actual Mobius factors had
then been derived. The construction here supplies curvature in a NEW
ordinary integer source. It does not claim a solution of that packet's
native sextic/prime-factor covariance or transfer any ideal-family scope.

## 1. The replacement source and complete Mellin return

Fix an ordinary complex Dirichlet character chi modulo a positive integer q.
Set a_n=mu(n)chi(n), preserving its values zero at every squareful integer
and every nonunit. Fix b=3/2 and k=6 once and for all, and define for every
real x>0

    W_chi(x) = sum_(n>=1) a_n exp(-n/x^b) exp(-i(n/x)^k).

The series is absolutely convergent at each x. There is no growing
conductor, inducing-character replacement, prime projector, averaged
character family or erased principal branch in this definition.

More generally fix b>1 and an integer k>2. For Re(s)>0 put

    I_n(s) = integral_0^infinity exp(-nt^b-i(nt)^k) t^(s-1) dt.

After v=nt, rotate the v-ray to argument -alpha, where
0<alpha<min(pi/(2b),pi/(2k)). The principal branch is used for powers.
On the connecting large arc the damping has real part at least a positive
constant times n^(1-b)R^b; the oscillatory factor has modulus at most one.
The small arc vanishes for Re(s)>0. Thus the rotation is legitimate for
each n. On the rotated ray, exp(-iv^k) decays as exp(-sin(k alpha)|v|^k).
Taylor's integral remainder, applied to z=n^(1-b)v^b with Re(z)>=0, gives
for each fixed integer K>=1

    I_n(s) = sum_(0<=j<K) A_j(s)n^(-s-(b-1)j) + R_(n,K)(s),
    A_j(s) = (-1)^j Gamma((s+bj)/k)exp(-i*pi*(s+bj)/(2k))/(k j!).

In particular, on any compact subset of Re(s)>0,

    |R_(n,K)(s)| <= n^(-Re(s)-(b-1)K) e^(alpha Im(s))
       * Gamma((Re(s)+bK)/k)
       / (k K! sin(k alpha)^((Re(s)+bK)/k)).                 (1)

The coefficients follow by substituting u=iv^k on the rotated ray and
rotating the resulting decaying Gamma contour to the positive real axis.
No conditionally convergent Taylor integral on the original ray is used.
The remainder is holomorphic and its series with coefficients a_n is
normally convergent for Re(s)>max(0,1-(b-1)K).

For Re(s)>b, absolute Fubini is licensed by

    integral_0^infinity sum_n exp(-nt^b)t^(Re(s)-1)dt
      = Gamma(Re(s)/b) zeta(Re(s)/b)/b < infinity.

With H_chi(s)=integral_0^infinity W_chi(1/t)t^(s-1)dt this proves

    H_chi(s) = sum_(j<K) A_j(s)/L(s+(b-1)j,chi) + R_chi,K(s). (2)

For the selected b=3/2, k=6, K=1 this becomes

    H_chi(s) = Gamma(s/6)exp(-i*pi*s/12)/(6 L(s,chi))
                 + R_chi,1(s),                              (3)

with R_chi,1 holomorphic on Re(s)>1/2. The multiplier has no zero on the
positive half-plane. All Euler holes remain in the original L(s,chi).

**Complete conditional return.** Suppose gamma>1/2 is fixed and for every
epsilon>0 and every sufficiently large dyadic X,

    E_chi(X):=integral_X^(2X)|W_chi(x)|^2 dx/x
        <<_(chi,epsilon) X^(2gamma+epsilon).                 (4)

Cauchy-Schwarz on every shell and summation of the resulting geometric
series make H_chi holomorphic on Re(s)>gamma. The t>=1 complement is
bounded absolutely by 1/(exp(t^b)-1), uniformly on compact s-sets. Equation
(3), initially on Re(s)>3/2, therefore continues 1/L holomorphically to
Re(s)>gamma. The ordinary meromorphic L-function has no zero there.
Its principal pole at s=1 is retained: its reciprocal is a zero, not an
obstruction to this argument. This proof is local on arbitrary compact
height ranges, so it excludes every finite-height zero; it assumes no
height-uniform source bound or growing-conductor theorem. For a common
gamma for all fixed characters, the constants and onsets may depend on
chi and epsilon, while the exponent is fixed before either is chosen.

This is an analytic implication, not a proof of (4), and not a claim of
equivalence to a sharper Mertens estimate. It uses standard analytic
continuation of the actual ordinary Dirichlet L-function; binding that
object to the project's imported root definition remains a separate
admission obligation. No Hecke or moving-family scope is inferred.

In fact the weaker shell L1 premise
integral_X^(2X)|W_chi(x)|dx/x <<_(chi,epsilon) X^(gamma+epsilon)
already suffices by the same Mellin argument. The squared norm is a
convenient stronger premise, not a required hypothesis of zero exclusion.

## 2. Exact full-energy compression, including every cross term

For this section only, coefficients may be any fixed complex sequence with
|a_n|<=1. Define N=X^b, X>=2. Expansion of the absolutely convergent square
gives the exact kernel

    K_X(n,m)=integral_1^2 exp(-(n+m)/(N u^b))
                       exp(-i(n^k-m^k)/(X^k u^k)) du/u.

For n!=m, put v=u^(-k). Integration by parts gives

    |K_X(n,m)| <= C_(b,k) min(1,X^k/|n^k-m^k|).              (5)

Indeed the amplitude on the fixed interval [2^(-k),1] is
exp(-A v^(b/k))/(kv), A=(n+m)/N. Its two endpoint values and the integral
of its derivative have a bound depending only on k. In fact this positive
amplitude is decreasing in v, so endpoint sum plus total variation equals
twice its value at 2^(-k), at most 2^(k+1)/k. The trivial integral bound is
log 2. Thus (5) is uniform in n,m,X and pays
the changing damping exactly, rather than freezing its profile.

For a real M>=2 let W_<=M be the same source with the SHARP, shell-fixed
cutoff n<=M, and define E_<=M by its whole-shell squared norm. Let

    D_>M(X)=sum_(n>M)|a_n|^2 K_X(n,n).

Every off-diagonal term not already in E_<=M has max(n,m)>M. Since for
integers n>m>=1,

    n^k-m^k >= n^(k-1)(n-m),

absolute summation of all these terms yields

    |E_chi(X)-E_<=M(X)-D_>M(X)|
      <= C_(b,k) X^k sum_(n>M) n^(1-k) sum_(h=1)^(n-1) 1/h
      <= C'_(b,k) X^k M^(2-k) log(2M).                     (6)

This pays the complete core/tail cross energy as well as the tail's
off-diagonal energy. In particular, it does NOT identify a diagonal with
a lower bound without first proving the error estimate. There is no
finite physical truncation and no discarded future tail. Taking limits
from finite sums is licensed by the damping and the summable majorant
in (6), since k>2. Also D_>M<=C_b X^b. Therefore

    E_chi(X) <= E_<=M(X)+C_b X^b
                       +C_(b,k)X^k M^(2-k)log(2M).          (7)

The same equation bounds E_<=M above by E_chi plus the error, because
D_>M>=0. Thus this is stronger than a norm triangle estimate and has no
unpriced cross term.

For k=6,b=3/2 and M=X^r the only paid exponents are

    diagonal 3/2; cross/tail off-diagonal 6-4r.             (8)

The earlier linear phase has no such summable n^(1-k) tail. This is the
substantive change of source geometry. Taking M=X in (7), E_<=M<=M^2 log2
gives the unconditional generic bound E_chi(X)<<X^2 log X+X^(3/2).
It already improves the old linear generic exponent 5/2, but does not
reach the first-gain threshold 1.7497080728.

## 3. An actual arithmetic far-tail theorem and a genuine energy floor

Return now to the literal coefficients mu(n)chi(n). The elementary
squarefree-unit count is

    sum_(n<=y)|a_n|^2 = d_q y + O_q(sqrt(y)),
    d_q=1/zeta(2) * product_(p|q) p/(p+1) >0.              (9)

To verify its scope, insert mu(n)^2=sum_(d^2|n)mu(d), retain (d,q)=1,
and count k<=y/d^2 with (k,q)=1 as (phi(q)/q)y/d^2+O_q(1).
The total error and the omitted Euler-product tail are O_q(sqrt(y)).
Partial summation in (9), uniformly for 1<=u<=2, gives

    D_all(X) = C_(q,b) X^b+O_q(X^(b/2)),
    C_(q,b)=d_q(2^b-1)/(2b)>0.

Since the removed n<=M diagonal is O(M), (6) proves

    E_chi(X)=E_<=M(X)+C_(q,b)X^b
               +O_(q,b,k)(M+X^(b/2)+X^k M^(2-k)log(2M)). (10)

In particular choose b=3/2,k=6,M=X^(19/16). Then

    E_chi(X)=E_<=M(X)+C_(q,3/2)X^(3/2)
                              +O_q(X^(5/4)log X).         (11)

The tail alone has the same main term and error, by (6) restricted to
n,m>M. This is an unconditional asymptotic for an actual signed source
sector, for every fixed ordinary chi, with natural zeros retained.
It also proves E_chi(X)>=(C_(q,3/2)+o(1))X^(3/2), since the core energy
is nonnegative. Unlike the earlier linear-source diagonal, this is a
proved lower bound on the WHOLE nonlinear energy; the full cross price
has become lower order. Consequently an every-epsilon L2 estimate with
gamma<3/4 is impossible for THIS b=3/2 source. Gamma=3/4 remains allowed,
as do the near and 1/6 targets. This is not an impossibility theorem for
L1 estimates, other b, other sources or zero exclusion itself.

## 4. A proved arithmetic estimate: polynomial Mobius cancellation plus (6)

The additional outside primary input is Green--Tao, *The Mobius function is
strongly orthogonal to nilsequences*, Annals 175 (2012), 541--566,
Theorem 1.1, pp.542--543:
https://annals.math.princeton.edu/wp-content/uploads/annals-v175-n2-p03-p.pdf .
For fixed rational nilmanifold data and degree, bounded Lipschitz real F,
it bounds the normalized Mobius correlation by every fixed negative power
of log N, uniformly in the polynomial sequence. Constants are ineffective.
We use only the circle R/Z, its standard rational basis, the degree-six
abelian filtration, and the two fixed functions cos(2pi t), sin(2pi t).
Thus for every fixed A>0 and all real polynomial coefficients,

    |sum_(n<=Y) mu(n) exp(2pi i P(n))|
                   <<_A Y(log(2Y))^(-A), deg P<=6.         (12)

This is an imported theorem, not a new proof of polynomial orthogonality.
Its statement is uniform in P; no equidistribution premise is being added.
Its logarithmic decay must not be changed into a power of Y. The theorem's
remark about power decay under GRH is not used.

The following deduction is specific to the present source. Write the
literal periodic chi as its finite additive Fourier expansion, including
its zero values. It is a sum over ell=0,...,q-1 of constants times
exp(2pi i ell n/q); the coefficients have total absolute value at most q.
Apply (12) to

    P(n)=ell n/q - n^6/(2pi x^6).

This gives uniformity for every real x>0. For prefixes Y<=M, split at
sqrt(M): the small ones cost sqrt(M), and for the others log Y is
comparable to log M. Hence all partial sums through M are
O_(q,A)(M(log M)^(-A)). The weight exp(-n/x^b) has endpoint plus total
variation at most two. Abel summation therefore gives

    |W_<=M(x)| <<_(q,A) M(log M)^(-A), uniformly in x>0.    (13)

Use M=X(log X)^B in (7). For every fixed D>0, choose
B=(D+2)/4 and A=B+(D+2)/2 BEFORE taking X large. We obtain the actual
unconditional source estimate

    E_chi(X) <<_(q,D) X^(3/2) + X^2(log X)^(-D).           (14)

Indeed the core term has log exponent 2B-2A=-D-2 and the complete
cross/tail error has log exponent 1-4B=-D-1. The diagonal contributes
X^(3/2). This is not a growing-order nilsequence argument: degree six,
q, D, A and B are fixed before X. Constants may be ineffective. No
claim is made that (14) follows uniformly when D grows with X.

This is a real arithmetic improvement of the nonlinear generic estimate,
and, as a whole-shell estimate, improves the old linear exponent 5/2 to
2 with arbitrary fixed logarithmic savings. It still misses the required
power 1.7497080728. Substituting D=D(X), declaring log saving to be a
positive power, or importing the GRH-only quadratic-family asymptotic
would be invalid. Neither the completed source geometry nor (14) raises c.

## 5. Weakest complete core targets at the useful endpoints

For the L2 route fix any 0<c<=1/4, put

    gamma=1-c, r=1+c/2, M=X^r,
    T_(chi,c,X)(x)=sum_(X^gamma<n<=X^r) mu(n)chi(n)
                                exp(-n/x^(3/2)-i(n/x)^6).

Both cutoffs are fixed from the original shell X, BEFORE x varies over
[X,2X]. The lower complement has squared norm at most (log2)X^(2gamma).
Equation (6) pays every term involving n>M by
O(X^(2gamma)log X), and the diagonal X^(3/2) is within budget because
gamma>=3/4. Consequently the SINGLE estimate

    for every epsilon>0, every sufficiently large dyadic X,
    integral_X^(2X)|T_(chi,c,X)(x)|^2 dx/x
                       <<_(chi,c,epsilon) X^(2-2c+epsilon) (CORE_c)

is sufficient for zero exclusion Re(s)>1-c, including the full
complement, physical damping, sharp cutoffs, natural zeros, principal
pole, imprimitive Euler factors and every finite height. A common c must
be fixed for all ordinary chi before the character-dependent constants
and onsets. This is a finite-band version of THIS detector input, not a
conductor-family average or a claim about an easier Mertens problem.

More precisely, for these fixed c the whole energy bound (4) and CORE_c
are equivalent at the every-epsilon level. In the forward direction use
(7), the lower complement and the norm triangle inequality. In the
reverse direction (6) and D_>M>=0 give E_<=M<=E+O(X^(2gamma)log X),
then subtract the already paid lower complement. No tail diagonal is
discarded on the reverse implication. This equivalence is useful because
(6) is a proved, nontrivial complement estimate; it supplies no saving
inside CORE_c.

| conditional c | gamma | upper core exponent r | complete energy target |
|---|---|---|---|
| 313/2500=.1252 | 2187/2500=.8748 | 5313/5000=1.0626 | 2187/1250=1.7496 |
| 1/6 | 5/6 | 13/12 | 5/3 |
| 1/4 | 3/4 | 9/8 | 3/2 |

The near target would exceed c11 by exactly 135091/2500000000.
These are CONDITIONAL implications only. The known estimate (14) has
power exponent 2 and does not meet any row. A deliberately coarse bound
already established here therefore FAILS the first-gain test by a power
gap 2* c11=.2502919272, before even asking for a positive improvement.

**Weaker complete target.** The minimum norm premise developed here is
actually L1, not L2. Applying the proof of (6) only to n,m>M gives

    integral_X^(2X)|W_>M(x)|^2 dx/x
                  << X^(3/2)+X^(2gamma)log X.

Thus its whole-shell L1 norm is O(X^gamma sqrt(log X)) for the targets
above. Together with the absolute lower-cutoff cost, this proves that

    integral_X^(2X)|T_(chi,c,X)(x)| dx/x
                         <<_(chi,c,epsilon) X^(1-c+epsilon) (CORE1_c)

is itself a COMPLETE sufficient input, and is equivalent, at every-epsilon
level, to the whole W shell L1 input. Both directions use only the triangle
inequality and the already proved complement estimates. CORE_c implies
CORE1_c, but the converse is neither assumed nor asserted. For the near
target CORE1 requires exponent .8748; the 1/6 and 1/4 targets require 5/6
and 3/4. From (14) we do obtain the actual arithmetic bound

    integral_X^(2X)|W_chi(x)|dx/x
                          <<_(q,D) X^(3/4)+X(log X)^(-D)

for every fixed D, after replacing D in (14) by 2D. This still fails the
first-gain power threshold by c11=.1251459636. No pointwise estimate or
energy floor is being substituted for the weaker L1 target.

There is no claim that this source is the only possible detector or that
its CORE target is necessary for zero exclusion itself. The old linear
Gauss-bank identity cannot simply be transplanted: its Fourier weights
and paid principal branch belong to exp(-i n/x), not to exp(-i(n/x)^6).
The new proof instead starts from the literal coefficients and constructs
its own Mellin bridge. No old Type I/II, Gao local-moment descendant,
joint-label estimate or high-conductor bound is invoked beyond scope.

## 6. Strongest objection and the arithmetic development still missing

The main objection is that higher frequency gaps could merely move the
old hard cancellation into n around X. That objection survives, in an
exact and useful form. Near n~X the phase exp(-i(n/x)^6) varies on the
scale X, not on a much shorter scale. Neither (5) nor an ordinary absolute
Gram estimate gives a power saving there. Polynomial Mobius orthogonality
does give the actual estimate (14), but its fixed logarithmic saving is
not enough.

For clarity, the GENERIC power exponent 2 is sharp for bounded arrays;
this is not a lower bound for Mobius. Given a shell X, set a_n=1 for
1<=n<=floor(X/2) and zero otherwise. On every x in [X,2X] all phases have
argument in [-1/64,0] and the damping is >=exp(-X/(2X^(3/2))). The real
part of W is bounded below by a positive constant times X, so E>>X^2.
The array depends on X and does not satisfy the global Mobius prime law.
Thus the generic argument alone cannot reach CORE_c. Equation (14), in
contrast, uses the actual Mobius function through a primary arithmetic
theorem and is genuinely stronger than that generic bound.

A precise remaining development target is CORE1 at .8748; the stronger
signed core energy bound X^(1.7496+epsilon) would also suffice.
The available estimate has only fixed logarithmic savings. All n<=X^.8748 and all
n>X^1.0626 have now been paid. Alternatively, one may prove a strong
enough signed cancellation in the explicit finite Gram sum for that
middle interval; its kernel is K_X(n,m), with coefficients
mu(n)mu(m)chi(n)overline(chi(m)). Any proposed treatment by residue
classes, nilsequence factorization or Vaughan decomposition must retain
the joint cross terms of the whole interval. The slow transition near
n~X is the first place to attack; a further treatment of very long
frequencies would repeat an already paid component.

## 7. Decision-ready disposition and evidence limits

**Proved here as ordinary analytic mathematics:** the fixed sixth-power
source retains the original reciprocal-L pole detector; (6) pays every
tail/core cross term; (11) proves an actual signed tail asymptotic and a
whole-energy lower bound; (14) combines the proved kernel estimate with
the explicitly imported Green--Tao theorem to give the full-source bound
X^(3/2)+X^2(log X)^(-D) for every fixed D>0. The finite arithmetic
receipt checks exact budgets only. The analytic proofs are Sections 1--4.

**Conditional, not proved arithmetic:** CORE1_(313/2500), or the stronger
CORE energy at exponent 1.7496, would give c=.1252. The analogous complete
1/6 and 1/4 returns remain available. This does not establish any of these
core estimates. The present complete coarse estimate misses a power, not
merely an endpoint constant. The accepted written c11 is unchanged.

**Rejected or deferred:** a coherent Gauss bank still needs signed
cancellation; averaging unrelated character families does not supply it.
The inspected quadratic-character family asymptotic is GRH-conditional.
Vaughan recombination remains possible but its signed Type I/II cancellation
was not proved. No generic bounded-array obstruction is asserted for actual
Mobius coefficients. The source-specific L2 floor below 3/4 is exact only
for the selected b=3/2 source and does not reject the 1/4 boundary or an L1
route. No numerical sampling stands in for a whole-rectangle/source proof.

This pass makes no use of formal proof assistants or kernel execution.
Its analytic claims await the separately reserved independent review. It
retains the project's upstream attribution and does not promote the PR9/Gao
analytic ancestry, positive-slot uniformity or external root-L-function
binding from open obligations to completed facts.

The support `checks.json` pins the exact local canonical sources by SHA256:

* [private research revision] integration, 11777 bytes:
  `12c96f06ad27ea044aec2a73889a6954cddb3cc1c19abe432fdf7def52bc3fe0`.
* Recombination policy, 14205 bytes:
  `2ab05a89464c9820b3a2bee591599091ef3ac5d82c79f8f52d19e03371f3a57d`.
* W14 generation packet, 33500 bytes (only seed/disposition section read):

`primary-source-evidence.json` gives exact published/versioned URLs and

statement:
## 1. Discovery and selection

Five materially different mechanisms were considered before selection.

1. Prime-dilation bilinear disjointness, inspired by the finite
   Bourgain--Sarnak--Ziegler criterion. Its square-root bilinear architecture
   could be powerful, but ordinary Mellin profiles have large correlations
   at nearby prime dilations. Its published fixed-parameter o(N) statement
   cannot be substituted for a power bound. Retain signed correlations;
   not selected for another general norm obstruction.
2. Full-cutoff fugacity root deflation (accepted G106) followed by a
   logarithmic potential along a complex path. The complete complementary
   branch and every other root are still present. No new bound for the
   actual endpoint Q_N(-1) was found; not selected.
3. Prime-block contraction with a von Mangoldt rather than prime-counting
   weight. Mean-zero profiles remove the prime main integral exactly, but
   the prime-power descendants and signed cofactor sum remain. A direct
   absolute cofactor bound loses the inherited saving. This is distinct
   from a useful completed estimate and is not promoted.
4. Additive-phase randomization or a rational Fourier bank. Its diagonal
   mean square is inexpensive, while evaluation at the original phase
   carries an observation cost. This remains eligible with actual signed
   cross-channel control; generic Parseval is insufficient.
5. SELECTED: separate the damping length and additive wavelength. For a
   fixed b>1 examine the actual, infinite source

       F_chi(z)=sum_(n>=1) mu(n)chi(n) exp(-nz), Re z>0,
       V_b,chi(x)=F_chi(x^(-b)+i/x), x>0.

   The damping length is x^b and wavelength is of order x. An ordinary
   square-root estimate at length x^b would suggest exponent b/2; b=3/2
   therefore has plausible conditional reach c=1/4. The essential missing
   bridge is that this MOVING profile must still see every L-function
   zero. Sections 2--3 prove that bridge with an absolutely convergent
   remainder. Section 4 actually attempts an elementary bilinear estimate
   for the complete source, obtaining exponent 5/4 at b=3/2. This saves
   a power over its trivial exponent 3/2 but does not improve c11.

This rotates away from fixed renewal profiles G112--G113, the previous
periodic-dilation source, and the separately owned joint-density lane.
The closest older library idea is round24 C5, angular Mellin contours;
it had no paid moving-source return. The present calculation uses the
literal mu chi coefficients, not a continuous coefficient countermodel.
No literature-priority claim is made for contour rotation or Vaughan's
identity.

statement:
## 2. Affine Green energy controls the actual fixed profile

This proves the portfolio's previously missing one-way affine-variance to
fixed-profile Möbius norm comparison. It is a norm inequality with explicit
tails, not an inverse Mellin or generic finite-Sobolev assertion.

Put
\[
\mathcal V(t)=\inf_{A,B}\int_t^{2t}|M(v)-A-Bv|^2\,dv,
\qquad R_j=2^{j/2}\quad(j\in\mathbb Z).
\]
There are fixed positive \(C,c\), for example \(c=1/4\) after adjusting
\(C\), such that
\[
\boxed{E_\phi(X)\le C\sum_{j\in\mathbb Z}
e^{-c(R_j+R_j^{-1})}
\int_{R_jX}^{2R_jX}\frac{\mathcal V(t)}t\,\frac{dt}{t}.} \tag{AD5}
\]

Choose a smooth nonnegative bump \(\eta\), positive on \((1,2)\)
and flat at its endpoints. With
\[
H(u)=\sum_j\eta(u/R_j),\qquad
\chi_j(u)=\eta(u/R_j)/H(u),
\]
the half-dyadic overlap ensures \(H>0\), \(\sum_j\chi_j=1\) and
\(|\chi_j^{(r)}|\le C_rR_j^{-r}\) on \([R_j,2R_j]\).
Use the specific function
\[
q(u)=-u e^{-u-u^{-1}},\qquad q''=-\phi',\qquad
k_j=(\chi_jq)''.
\]
Compact-support integration by parts gives, separately for each piece,
\[
\int k_j=\int u k_j=0. \tag{AD6}
\]
Stieltjes integration and the partition now give the exact identity
\[
S_\phi(x)=\int_0^\infty M(xu)q''(u)\,du
 =\sum_j\int M(xu)k_j(u)\,du.
\]
In each term subtract the best affine fit on \([R_jx,2R_jx]\).
AD6 removes it exactly; fits on adjacent intervals need not coincide.
Direct differentiation gives
\[
\sqrt{R_j}\|k_j\|_2
\le C(1+R_j+R_j^{-1})^2 e^{-R_j-(2R_j)^{-1}}
\le C e^{-(R_j+R_j^{-1})/4}.
\]
Thus Cauchy, followed by weighted Cauchy in \(j\), bounds
\(|S_\phi(x)|^2\) by a constant times
\(\sum_j e^{-(R_j+R_j^{-1})/4}\mathcal V(R_jx)/(R_jx)\).
Integrating proves AD5. Absolute convergence already follows from
\(|M(v)|\le v\); no arithmetic cancellation estimate was assumed.

The quantity on the right is an explicit signed arithmetic Green form.
For \(0<r,s<1\), define
\[
G(r,s)=\min(r,s)-rs-3r(1-r)s(1-s).
\]
Project the step functions off \(1,u\) in \(L^2([0,1])\). Their
centered covariance is \(\min(r,s)-rs\), and the additional linear
projection subtracts \(3r(1-r)s(1-s)\). Consequently
\[
\boxed{\mathcal V(t)/t=
\sum_{t<m,n<2t}\mu(m)\mu(n)
G(m/t-1,n/t-1).} \tag{AD7}
\]
Endpoint steps are constants or vanish almost everywhere and hence make
no contribution. AD5 has not taken absolute values inside this Green form.

Both infinite scale tails are paid. Since \(\mathcal V(t)/t\ll t^2\),
for every \(A>0\) the scales outside
\[
(C_A\log X)^{-1}\le R_j\le C_A\log X
\]
contribute \(O_A(X^{-A})\) to AD5 for sufficiently large fixed \(C_A\).
Only \(O_A(\log\log X)\) overlapping scales remain.

### Exact discrete-to-continuous bridge

Let
\[
\mathcal D_N=\min_{A,B}\sum_{k=N}^{2N-1}|M(k)-A-Bk|^2
\]
and let \(B_N\) be its least-squares slope. For \(N\ge2\),
\[
\boxed{\mathcal V(N)=\mathcal D_N+
\frac{N^2-1}{12N}|B_N|^2,\qquad |B_N|\le1.} \tag{AD8}
\]
The centered discrete time variance is \(N(N^2-1)/12\); continuous
time adds \(N/12\), while covariance with the step function \(M\)
does not change. The least-squares formulas prove the equality. The
slope is a convex average of increments \(\mu(N+i)\): its unnormalized
weights are \(i(N-i)/2\), whose sum is \(N(N^2-1)/12\).

For \(N\le t<N+1\), the intervals \([N,2N]\) and
\([N+1,2N+2]\) have overlap of length comparable to \(N\), for large
\(N\). The two best affine fits differ on that overlap by at most their
two residual norms. Norm equivalence for affine functions on intervals of
comparable length then proves
\[
\mathcal V(t)\ll\mathcal V(N)+\mathcal V(N+1). \tag{AD9}
\]
The finitely many small \(N\) are included in a fixed constant.
An every-integer estimate \(\mathcal D_N\ll N^{2a+1+\epsilon}\),
\(a>0\), therefore implies \(E_\phi(X)\ll X^{2a+\epsilon}\)
through AD5, AD8 and AD9. T09.2 transfers this to the frozen finite
balanced form with superpolynomial error. A hypothetical Mellin mode
\(M(t)=t^s/s\) still gives exactly \(S_\phi(x)=\Phi(s)x^s\);
equal resonances were not discarded.

The comparison is proved; the required arithmetic variance saving remains
open. It removes a genuine norm-comparison prerequisite without asserting
a new zero-free constant.

statement:
## 7. Exact scalar, diagonal and two-height interface

For a frozen original pair mask B_X(m,n), let c_i(n)=f(n)A_i(n),
and, on Re(s_1)=Re(s_2)=sigma>1, define

    D_ij,B(s_1,s_2)=sum_(m,n>=1)
                  B_X(m,n)c_i(m)c_j(n)m^-s_1 n^-s_2.

For |B_X|<=1 it is absolutely bounded by zeta(sigma)^2. Gaussian
Mellin inversion gives the exact bilinear scalar

    (1/(2pi)^2) integral_(R^2)
      exp(tau(s_1^2+s_2^2)/2) D_ij,B(s_1,s_2)
      [integral_X^(2X) x^(s_1+s_2) dx/x] dt_1 dt_2,
    s_j=sigma+i t_j.                                     (R30)

This is a real-coefficient bilinear representation, so it correctly
uses s_1+s_2 without an inserted conjugate. Changing t_1 to -t_1
produces the equivalent conjugated first-height convention. It
does not factor D_ij,B when B_X couples the integers. Gaussian
decay exp(-tau(t_1^2+t_2^2)/2) pays both independent height tails
and justifies the initial exchanges. No equality t_1=t_2 is imposed.

The threshold, divisor condition, shift condition and window are
original-X masks. They are not altered during Mellin inversion,
reindexed to X/g masks, or differentiated as a contour parameter.
The original complete TT,TR,RT,RR sum, the true diagonal and the
outer accepted full-source convolution must all be restored before
an improvement can enter the mismatch estimate. R30 supplies no
primewise-independent or RN/pair02 substitute through the kernel.

The actual obstruction therefore narrows the unpaid route: an

statement:
## 1. The replacement source and complete Mellin return

Fix an ordinary complex Dirichlet character chi modulo a positive integer q.
Set a_n=mu(n)chi(n), preserving its values zero at every squareful integer
and every nonunit. Fix b=3/2 and k=6 once and for all, and define for every
real x>0

    W_chi(x) = sum_(n>=1) a_n exp(-n/x^b) exp(-i(n/x)^k).

The series is absolutely convergent at each x. There is no growing
conductor, inducing-character replacement, prime projector, averaged
character family or erased principal branch in this definition.

More generally fix b>1 and an integer k>2. For Re(s)>0 put

    I_n(s) = integral_0^infinity exp(-nt^b-i(nt)^k) t^(s-1) dt.

After v=nt, rotate the v-ray to argument -alpha, where
0<alpha<min(pi/(2b),pi/(2k)). The principal branch is used for powers.
On the connecting large arc the damping has real part at least a positive
constant times n^(1-b)R^b; the oscillatory factor has modulus at most one.
The small arc vanishes for Re(s)>0. Thus the rotation is legitimate for
each n. On the rotated ray, exp(-iv^k) decays as exp(-sin(k alpha)|v|^k).
Taylor's integral remainder, applied to z=n^(1-b)v^b with Re(z)>=0, gives
for each fixed integer K>=1

    I_n(s) = sum_(0<=j<K) A_j(s)n^(-s-(b-1)j) + R_(n,K)(s),
    A_j(s) = (-1)^j Gamma((s+bj)/k)exp(-i*pi*(s+bj)/(2k))/(k j!).

In particular, on any compact subset of Re(s)>0,

    |R_(n,K)(s)| <= n^(-Re(s)-(b-1)K) e^(alpha Im(s))
       * Gamma((Re(s)+bK)/k)
       / (k K! sin(k alpha)^((Re(s)+bK)/k)).                 (1)

The coefficients follow by substituting u=iv^k on the rotated ray and
rotating the resulting decaying Gamma contour to the positive real axis.
No conditionally convergent Taylor integral on the original ray is used.
The remainder is holomorphic and its series with coefficients a_n is
normally convergent for Re(s)>max(0,1-(b-1)K).

For Re(s)>b, absolute Fubini is licensed by

    integral_0^infinity sum_n exp(-nt^b)t^(Re(s)-1)dt
      = Gamma(Re(s)/b) zeta(Re(s)/b)/b < infinity.

With H_chi(s)=integral_0^infinity W_chi(1/t)t^(s-1)dt this proves

    H_chi(s) = sum_(j<K) A_j(s)/L(s+(b-1)j,chi) + R_chi,K(s). (2)

For the selected b=3/2, k=6, K=1 this becomes

    H_chi(s) = Gamma(s/6)exp(-i*pi*s/12)/(6 L(s,chi))
                 + R_chi,1(s),                              (3)

with R_chi,1 holomorphic on Re(s)>1/2. The multiplier has no zero on the
positive half-plane. All Euler holes remain in the original L(s,chi).

**Complete conditional return.** Suppose gamma>1/2 is fixed and for every
epsilon>0 and every sufficiently large dyadic X,

    E_chi(X):=integral_X^(2X)|W_chi(x)|^2 dx/x
        <<_(chi,epsilon) X^(2gamma+epsilon).                 (4)

Cauchy-Schwarz on every shell and summation of the resulting geometric
series make H_chi holomorphic on Re(s)>gamma. The t>=1 complement is
bounded absolutely by 1/(exp(t^b)-1), uniformly on compact s-sets. Equation
(3), initially on Re(s)>3/2, therefore continues 1/L holomorphically to
Re(s)>gamma. The ordinary meromorphic L-function has no zero there.
Its principal pole at s=1 is retained: its reciprocal is a zero, not an
obstruction to this argument. This proof is local on arbitrary compact
height ranges, so it excludes every finite-height zero; it assumes no
height-uniform source bound or growing-conductor theorem. For a common
gamma for all fixed characters, the constants and onsets may depend on
chi and epsilon, while the exponent is fixed before either is chosen.

This is an analytic implication, not a proof of (4), and not a claim of
equivalence to a sharper Mertens estimate. It uses standard analytic
continuation of the actual ordinary Dirichlet L-function; binding that
object to the project's imported root definition remains a separate
admission obligation. No Hecke or moving-family scope is inferred.

In fact the weaker shell L1 premise
integral_X^(2X)|W_chi(x)|dx/x <<_(chi,epsilon) X^(gamma+epsilon)
already suffices by the same Mellin argument. The squared norm is a
convenient stronger premise, not a required hypothesis of zero exclusion.

## 4. Decisive pressure test and the remaining original-prime term

SF11 is stronger than D6 as an interface, but its leading arithmetic
certificate has NOT improved. At the frozen hard dyad write

    k=.835507578307735986...,
    nu=k+.003, gamma=.001,
    ell=.170813789153867993...,
    K=Z^k, N=Z^nu, G=Z^gamma, L=Z^ell,
    S(N,L) comparable to N.

Every factor split DE=N satisfies

    S(E,LD) >= (NL)^(2/3),
    S(D,LE) >= (NL)^(2/3).                           (SF12)

The balanced split E=LD, hence D=sqrt(N/L), E=sqrt(NL), attains this
order because NL>=1. The best balanced certificate SF11, divided by
the required raw G K S(N,L), therefore still has size

    G (NL)^(2/3) = Z^(.673880911641069319333...).     (SF13)

The separate near-band term with old exponent .221813789153867993...
has disappeared; it was not the leading obstruction. Compared with
the incumbent's .004 deficit, the remaining surplus is
.669880911641069319333.... The cycle's new interval argument has
therefore not paid an original prime interaction at the required scale.
SF12--13 are lower bounds on this positive CERTIFICATE, not lower
bounds on the original covariance.

Even replacing the cubic sieve by its hypothetical two-linear-term
version would leave

    min(E+LD,D+LE) >= 2 sqrt(NL),
    target-relative scale at least G sqrt(NL),
    exponent .5056606837308019895....               (SF14)

Thus neither free removal of the entire near band nor removing only
the mixed cubic term repairs this fixed-row argument. A proposed new
row average that replaces K in SF11 by K Z^(-sigma) would need
sigma>=.673880911641069319333... just to pay this balanced packet.
Even a hypothetical K^(1/2) row cost would leave a positive certificate
deficit .256127122487201326333... . These are diagnostic requirements
for THIS ordering of inequalities, not universal necessities for H.

### 4.1 Signed I/II return through the interval tree

Let F_I and F_II denote the two exact normalized linear terms of
[private research revision] B1--2, with all their original n,R,P,g factors. Restriction to
any tree interval J is multiplication by 1_(q_n in J), hence commutes
with the pointwise identity:

    (F_I+F_II)_J = F_(all-prime),J.                  (SF15)

The strict far covariance is consequently the exact sum of its four
ordered (I,I),(I,II),(II,I),(II,II) tree expressions. On every eligible
semiprime above both cutoffs the interval coefficient is still 1,-1
on the two linear pieces, giving 1,-1,-1,1 in the ordered covariance
whenever the original pair is in that rectangle. Thus the two ordered
mixed terms remain necessary. They cancel BEFORE the prime projection,
not as a post hoc cancellation between positive bounds.

On an original prime n, the coefficient in F_I is one and that in
F_II is zero. It stays in the unit factor cell D=1,E~N at every tree
level. In this cell

    T(1,N;L)=min{S(N,L),S(1,NL)} comparable to N,

so SF11 gives K G^2 N^2, of target-relative size G N, with exponent
.839507578307735986.... This is weaker than the existing joint
quadratic/cubic bound and is not promoted. Combining all signed
allocations FIRST restores the original prime source at original
length N; applying the established joint sieve to it restores
G(K+NG)S(N,L), still with deficit .004. No shortened unit source is
created by SF15.

This is the decisive obstruction to this attempted route. The exact
product-interval adapter fixes an analytic masking loss, but the
first positive fixed-row estimate still discards the covariance that
the unit prime source needs. The signed small-gcd complement remains
the original-prime form minus the already paid common-core composite
counterterm. No new equality identifies that counterterm with primes.

The next useful target is therefore an estimate on SF15's JOINT
original-row interval vectors before the fixed-R cubic Cauchy step,
or a signed Type-I/Type-II estimate in that same joint norm. A theorem
with the square-function scope of SF2 would now return the full sharp
far mask by SF8 at logarithmic cost. Proving such a row estimate is
still the arithmetic work; SF2/SF11 do not assume it.

statement:
## G165. Incidence kernels and all acyclic face matchings

On the q-unit squarefree states at most N, define natural edge observations

\[
(\nabla_\chi f)(n,p)=f(pn)+\chi(p)f(n),\qquad pn\le N.
\]

Writing f(n)=a(n)g(n) gauges this to ordinary differences, up to a unit
phase per edge. The graph is connected by deleting primes down to1, hence

\[
\ker\nabla_\chi=\operatorname{span}\{a\}.                \tag{95.5}
\]

The source one wants to estimate is the exact unobserved direction.
Unitary Fourier conjugation transports this kernel rather than removing
it. In a length-N additive transform with the original zeros retained,
the zero-frequency component is Mχ(N)/√N. For the quartic character
modulo5 at N=7, the actual coefficients on1,2,3,6,7 are
1,−i,i,1,−i: every internal flux vanishes but Mχ(7)=2−i.
Adding outgoing zero-extension observations incurs the positive boundary
cost ∑|w_p|²C_p(N). This edge-observation cost is distinguished from the
coherent operator E; they are not interchangeable quadratic forms.

For any elementary face matching, pair a lower n with upper pn. The exact
source sum decomposes into

\[
M_\chi(N)=\sum_{n\text{ critical}}a(n)
 +\sum_{(n,pn)\text{ matched}}a(n)(1-\chi(p)).            \tag{95.6}
\]

In particular, the least unramified prime ℓ gives an acyclic matching
n↔ℓn for ℓ-free n≤N/ℓ. Reversing matched edges cannot create a cycle:
after an upward ℓ edge, any permitted downward non-ℓ edge still contains ℓ.
The surviving critical count is C_ℓ(N).

More generally every acyclic elementary face matching with m pairs
satisfies m≤rank D for the unit-weight exterior differential. Select
matched upper rows and lower columns of D. An off-diagonal incidence
u_i←l_j gives the oriented alternating path u_i→l_j→u_j. Acyclicity
orders these paths, making the selected minor triangular with nonzero
diagonal. Therefore

\[
\#\text{critical}=\dim V_N-2m
 \ge\dim V_N-2\operatorname{rank}D
 =\dim H(D)=C_\ell(N)\asymp_q N.                       \tag{95.7}
\]

No such matching gives a power-saving **unweighted absolute** critical
count. This does not lower-bound the signed critical sum, nor all weighted
homotopies. Any elimination using gradient paths must retain their full
coefficients and the norm of the scalar evaluation map. In the modulo5
example, pairs1↔2 and3↔6 leave critical contribution −i and matched bulk2;
discarding the latter changes the answer.

The independent S18 audit leaves broader absorbing-boundary/scattering
operators open; S12 leaves signed dual certificates open. They require
additional observations that see (95.5) and a paid return to μχ. The
positive-count obstruction is not a rejection of those broader proposals.
title: G165. Incidence kernels and all acyclic face matchings

statement:
## A12. A prime Fredholm determinant and the regularization trap

**PROVED identity and method-specific obstruction.** Source: BA D9. On the Hilbert space indexed by rational primes let \(T_s=\operatorname{diag}(p^{-s})\).
For \(\Re s>1\),
\[
 \det(I-T_s)=\prod_p(1-p^{-s})=1/\zeta(s).
\]
For \(\Re s>1/2\), \(T_s\) is Hilbert–Schmidt and
\[
 D_2(s)=\det{}_2(I-T_s)
 =\exp\!\left(-\sum_{m\ge2}\frac1m\sum_pp^{-ms}\right)
\]
is holomorphic and nonzero, by locally absolute convergence. But initially
\[
 1/\zeta(s)=D_2(s)e^{-P(s)},\qquad P(s)=\sum_pp^{-s}.
\]
The compensating factor carries the unresolved continuation and possible poles. Regularization has removed the difficult arithmetic contribution from the determinant, not proved it harmless. A bounded similarity preserves trace-class membership, so it cannot repair the original divergent trace norm. A useful changed operator needs a new verified determinant identity with its compensator controlled.
title: A12. A prime Fredholm determinant and the regularization trap

statement:
## 3. The actual physical family and the selected slots

### 3.1 Coefficients, conjugation and eligibility

The fixed base for the numerator moment is fixedSourcePrincipal S, not the primitive target \(\eta\) occurring in the reciprocal denominator. The target affects fixed data such as S; the moving numerator is the sextic row character.

This is an exact source identification:

- PR9 PhysicalMomentInput.lean lines 23–34 identify physicalSlotCoefficient as the inverse fixed-base ideal coefficient times the common conjugate annular weight.
- At \(\Re z_i=17/50\), the annular real power is \(1-\Re z_i=33/50\), and its height is \(-\Im z_i\).
- source_physical_slot_conj, lines 100–112, identifies the normalized physical slot for fixedSourcePrincipal with the conjugate of the original canonical prime amplitude. The proof retains the actual prime pool and all ramified zeros.
- reflected_pair_norm_eq, lines 116–140, conjugates the *entire product* of the two reflected plain factors and all selected slots. It does not conjugate selected factors in isolation or replace a zero extension by an unrestricted character.

Thus, after choosing the two plain profiles appropriately, the local proposition's positive orientation is the exact physical orientation. There is no new arbitrary slot coefficient or independently selected row mask.

PR9 Physical-SourceState.lean defines weighted_sourceFixedIdeal as the source modulus intersected with (72), then uses internalQ with the actual anchor. Its fixed-gate lemmas retain nonzero/proper and containment conditions. weighted_source_keep_iff identifies initialKeep with the negation of the literal fixed-inducing predicate for physical FreeRow values. weighted_source_exceptional_norm, lines 48–60, gives a fixed bound on the norm of every exceptional sixth-power-free row.

For a fixed target these exceptional free rows disappear from every growing retained dyad \(q_u\ge Z^{d_0}\), \(d_0=1/200\), after a target-dependent threshold. They are not simply discarded from the original probe: the finite small-row treatment below includes them. The physical parent has zero *moving* width; absorbing its fixed modulus into an arbitrarily small width padding is paid in the requested loss after fixing the target.

### 3.2 Genuine selection and zero supply

For one amplitude class, let \(w_i=\ell_i/d>0\),
\(L=\sum_iw_i=\ell/d\), and \(0\le g_i\le\delta/2\).
Error slots have \(g_i=0\), but their widths remain in L. Set
\[
 q=\frac{\sum_iw_i g_i}{L}=\delta p,\qquad 0\le p\le1/2.
\]
When \(\delta=0\), q is zero and one may take p=0.

The generic zero_error_whole_slots theorem requires only
\(0\le z_A\le L\), the width mesh bound, these gain bounds, and zero error gains. It returns one subset I of positive-gain main slots, fixed for the amplitude class, with
\[
 z_I=\sum_{i\in I}w_i\le z_A,\qquad
 \sum_{i\in I}w_i g_i\ge qz_A-\frac{\delta}{2}{\rm mesh}.
\]
With the class's actual slot lower bounds this gives
\[
 \left|\prod_{i\in I}Q_i\right|^2
 \ge U^{\,2qz_A-\delta\,{\rm mesh}-o(1)}.       \tag{E1}
\]

This theorem has no positive-main-supply lower bound. If positive gains are exhausted, their total is qL, which is at least qz_A. The gain is therefore measured at the target capacity, even if the selected physical width is much smaller. Error factors or zero-gain main factors must not be reinserted in this lower-bounded product. Their actual amplitudes could vanish.

The source wrapper highData_weighted_selection has a \(d\ge1/2\) premise, but the generic theorem just inspected does not. The endpoint correctly uses the generic theorem on lower rows. For \(d<1/2\),
\[
 L>2\ell>1/3,\qquad
 z_{\rm old}\le1/(6\kappa)\le5/21<1/3.
\]
For other old rows the original supply inequality
\(\min(d,2y-d)\le y<4\ell\le6\kappa\ell\) suffices. The detector needs \(L>4/21\), checked at the largest retained d. The new local capacity is much smaller and satisfies the separately checked \(z_A<L\).

All actual original slot widths are positive. Consequently \(z_I=0\) means \(I=\varnothing\). If the generic nonnegative-width selection theorem is used elsewhere, that equivalence should not be silently generalized to zero-width slots.

A common-profile slot system can also be made explicit without arbitrary prime subsets: choose finitely many distinct positive \(\ell_i\), with sum \(\ell\) and maximum below \(d_0\) times the common mesh. For example normalize distinct numbers \(1+i/(2r)\), \(1\le i\le r\), to total \(\ell\), taking r sufficiently large. The minimum width is then positive and common to all targets. Fixed annuli at scales \(Z^{\ell_i}\) become disjoint at a single sufficiently large Z because the exponents are distinct. ## R7. Protected20: an exact Schur reduction must retain the completion

This is my independent development of the forced protected seed, not an author result. Apply it to the ACTUAL T in R6 after freezing packet, height pair and any proposed scale partition of its input coordinates. Write T=[T_R,T_E], v=(u,z), and let Pi be the orthogonal projection onto ran T_E in the output space. No assumption that that range is easy, small or character-neutral is made. Orthogonality gives the exact source identity

    ||Tv||^2 = ||(I-Pi)T_R u||^2
               +||Pi T_R u+T_E z||^2.                 (A20.1)

The first Gram matrix is the generalized Schur complement

    S=T_R*(I-Pi)T_R
     =A-B D^dagger B*,
    A=T_R*T_R, B=T_R*T_E, D=T_E*T_E.                   (A20.2)

To justify the singular case without a hidden inverse: ker D=ker T_E and B annihilates that kernel. Thus ran B* is contained in ran D, and T_E D^dagger T_E*=Pi. The identities follow from the finite singular-value decomposition; no arbitrary range condition is assumed away. S is positive semidefinite. In a true energy Gram matrix the fill-in satisfies0<=B D^dagger B*<=A; it cannot be treated as a free negative contribution making the full energy negative.

For a priced resolvent alternative put D_lambda=D+lambda I, lambda>0, and S_lambda=A-B D_lambda^-1 B*. Then exactly

    v*Gv = u*S_lambda u
       +(z+D_lambda^-1 B*u)*D_lambda(z+D_lambda^-1 B*u)
       -lambda||z||^2,       G=T*T.                   (A20.3)

G+diag(0,lambda I) is positive semidefinite, hence S_lambda>=0. Expansion verifies every cross term and the final subtraction. The inverse costs at most1/lambda, or the sharper actual spectral distance, only if that inverse representation is used; the projection formula itself has norm1 and does not inherently require an inverse blowup. Conversely, replacing the full completion by a small Schur term would be a false upper bound. The three-column algebra diagnostic

    E={second,third}, epsilon!=0

The canonical energy PR9 B3.6 permits a0(n) times the fixed ray character, common puncture and original product marks. It explicitly permits no further arithmetic coefficient on n. A second transform needs the full finite correlation/reconstruction calculation, not a formal interchange of two ordinary character Poisson formulas.

and derivative profiles have a fixed finite union cost. Tensor Sobolev

## 2. Literal source audit

Fix an ordinary Dirichlet character chi modulo q, with chi(n)=0 on nonunits, and p not dividing q. Set a(n)=lambda(n)chi(n), h=chi, s(r^2)=chi(r)^2 and s=0 elsewhere. Complete multiplicativity, including its zeros, gives a*h=s. Put

    q1=delta1-p chi(p)delta_p,
    q2=delta1-p chi(p)^2 delta_(p^2), v=q1*q2,
    b0=v*h, c=v*a*s=a*a*b0.

In particular q2 has coefficient -p, not -p^2, times chi(p)^2. Expanding v gives coefficients 1,-p chi(p),-p chi(p)^2,p^2 chi(p)^3 at 1,p,p^2,p^3. Thus

    b0(l)=chi(l)[1-p1_(p|l)-p1_(p^2|l)+p^2 1_(p^3|l)].       (R1)

Its period is Q=p^3q and |b0|<=(p+1)^2. Each divisibility-restricted character has zero period mean for nonprincipal chi. For a principal chi the mean is proportional to 1-p/p-p/p^2+p^2/p^3=0. Hence b0 has zero mean for every fixed ordinary character, including imprimitive characters. The analogous root coefficient beta(r)=chi(r)^2(1-p1_(p|r)) has period pq and zero mean. No shared-prime or squareful contribution is removed.

On Re z>1 the exact series is

    D_c(z)=P_p(z)J_p(z)L(2z,chi^2)^2/L(z,chi),
    P_p=1-chi(p)p^(1-z), J_p=1-chi(p)^2p^(1-2z).             (R2)

All subsequent physical sums use f_x(n)=exp(-n/x^(3/2)-i(n/x)^6), real x in[X,2X], with measure dx/x. Changing x to x/p does not reproduce f_x(pn); neither the author nor this review makes that substitution.

## 5. Original Schwartz weight, all tails and fixed-datum uniformity

Apply NP16 to the ball \(q_u\le H_G\) and to dyadic balls containing the shells \(2^jH_G<q_u\le2^{j+1}H_G\), as long as their radii are at most \(D^2\). Bound a final partial shell ending at \(D^2\) by NP16 at radius \(D^2\). The bound
\(\Phi(t)\ll_{\Phi,N}(1+t)^{-N}\), with a fixed sufficiently large N, makes both shell series converge. Choose the intermediate loss \(\eta\) sufficiently small in terms of the final \(\epsilon\); since these radii are at most \(D^2\), all losses and logarithms are absorbed in \(D^\epsilon\).

For the remaining infinite tail \(q_u>D^2\), use the actual coefficient bound
\[
|M_u(D;W)|^2\ll_I D\|W\|_\infty^2.
\]
Ideal counting proves this uniformly in u, since the column annulus has \(O_I(D)\) ideals and every coefficient has modulus at most one. Two-dimensional lattice counting on a shell of radius R gives \(O(R)\) element rows. Its weighted contribution is at most
\[
C_{\Phi,N,I}D\,R(R/H_G)^{-N}\|W\|_\infty^2 .
\]
Summing shells beyond \(D^2\), and using \(H_G\le D^{101/100}\), bounds this by
\[
O_{\Phi,N,I}\!\left(D^{\,3-(99/100)N}\|W\|_\infty^2\right).
\tag{NP17}
\]
For example \(N=6\) gives \(D^{-147/50}\), which is negligible against NP1. Thus no UM estimate is used outside its fixed polynomial range, and no Schwartz tail is discarded without a bound.

This proves NP1. The compact Fourier support included in Guo's datum is not needed for this deduction. Only finitely many fixed Schwartz seminorms of \(\Phi\) enter. The original W varies over all \(C_c^\infty(I)\) with one finite seminorm on the right. The finite order is chosen using the requested loss, then fixed before any D, H, core, sixth root or deletion divisor varies.

The zero row is absent from NP3. If the full GS5 family including zero is wanted, GS21 gives \(M_0(D)=D^{-1/2}W(1/D)\) under the unit-ideal convention. Its contribution is \(O_\Phi(D^{-1}\|W\|_\infty^2)\) and is absorbed in NP1. The unit ideal is counted once as a column; the six element units remain distinct rows.

## 6. Independent diagnostic: the first cell often collapses completely

This sharpened description follows from the same finite Bernoulli representation and does not assume Mertens cancellation.

For any EVEN chi, choose r=2 and let m_chi=q^(-1)sum_(j mod q)chi(j), with chi(0)=0 for q>1 and chi(0)=1 for q=1. On 0<=x<=1/q,

    Phi(x)=2L(2,chi)-2pi^2 m_chi x+2pi^2 chi(0)x^2.      (R10)

To prove this, expand B_2(x+a/q). Its x^2 coefficient is sum c_a=chi(0). For the linear coefficient, c_(q-a)=c_a and B_1(a/q) changes sign under a->q-a, so all nonzero indices pair off; the remaining a=0 term is -c_0/2=-m_chi/2. The constant is Phi(0)=2L(2,chi). Endpoint continuity gives the closed interval.

For every even NONPRINCIPAL character, both m_chi and chi(0) vanish. Hence Phi is exactly constant on the first cell, and for 0<=x<=1/(qN),

    R_N(x)=2L(2,chi) T_N +2cos(2pi x)-2.                 (R11)

The error term is O(N^(-2)). Consequently

    abs(sqrt(E_arc(N))-sqrt(h)*abs(2L(2,chi)T_N))
       << h^(5/2).                                     (R12)

This is the triangle inequality for the constant field and the explicit cosine error, with h=1/(qN). It shows directly that for this entire class the short-arc condition is a single weighted-tail bound, with a negligible deterministic remainder at every target c<1/2. The more elaborate localized Gram has not produced a separate known cancellation mechanism.

For odd chi and r=3, the first cell is

    Phi(x)=2L(3,chi)-4pi^2 L(1,chi)x^2.                  (R13)

Here chi is nonprincipal, so the cubic coefficient vanishes. The first derivative at 0 is zero by absolute convergence and parity. The second derivative at 0 is -8pi^2 L(1,chi). This last differentiation is legitimate: the finite additive Fourier expansion has no zero-frequency component, and the 1/k Fourier series is uniformly convergent near 0, away from its shifted jumps. Equivalently differentiate the finite Bernoulli expression. Only convergence of the nonprincipal L(1,chi) series is needed for this identity, not its nonvanishing. Thus the odd-character local field is determined by two finite weighted sums and the cosine target. This is a diagnostic reduction, not a proof of the required bounds on those sums.

Independent exact rational checks confirm the shapes for q=2 principal, q=5 real even, and q=3,4 odd after factoring their fixed Fourier constants. For example sum_(a=1)^4 chi_5(a)B_2(x+a/5)=4/25 exactly; B_3(x+1/3)-B_3(x+2/3)=2/27-x^2. These finite identities support the normalizations, while (R10)-(R13) are proved for all characters in their stated classes.

For a finite set P containing2 and not3, put

    Q=product_(p in P)p,
    a_P(n)=product_(p in P)(1-2*1_(p|n)),
    r_P(n)=f(n)a_P(n), so f=a_P*r_P pointwise.               (B1)

The last product is pointwise, NOT Dirichlet convolution. The bounded sequence a_P is Q-periodic. Its exact mean is product_(p in P)(1-2/p)=0. Let h_tau(t)=g_tau(log t) for t>0, extended by0 for t<=0. For any Q-periodic |a|<=1 of mean zero, finite Fourier expansion and Poisson summation give, for every integer m>=2,

    |sum_(n>=1)a(n)g_tau(log(n/x))|
      <=2 zeta(m)(Q/(2pi))^m x^(1-m)||h_tau^(m)||_1.         (B2)

    ||h_tau^(m)||_1<=K_tau 4^m m! exp(tau(m-1)^2/2).

    F_P(x):=sum_n a_P(n)g_tau(log(n/x))
       =O_(A,delta,tau)(X^-A) for every fixed A>0.           (B3)

Indeed the logarithm of the bound is at most -delta^2(log X)^2/(2tau)+O_(delta,tau)(log X loglog X). The estimate is uniform in the actual prime list and includes all positive prime powers. Fix b=3/2,k=12,gamma=5/6 and shell-frozen

    L=X^(5/6), U=V=X^(5/12), G=X^(1/6), M=X^(31/30).

With a_U=a1_(n<=U), the exact identity is

    c=Q_U+Q_V-S+R,
    Q_U=a_U*(v*s), Q_V=a_V*(v*s),
    S=a_U*a_V*b0, R=(a-a_U)*(a-a_V)*b0.

G191 pays the WHOLE S: its row coefficients are bounded by d2(m), supported
m<=UV=L. No output or gcd mask is inserted into G191.

The complete general-phase square-short proof in [restricted research revision], reconstructed in the
review, gives for every frozen root prefix R0, including infinity,

    ||sum_(r<=R0) beta(r) f_x(A0 r^2)||_(1,2)
                           << 1+X^(b/4)A0^(-1/4)

when beta is fixed bounded mean-zero periodic, A0 lies in a fixed sublinear
power range, and b>=2k/(2k-1). Its low derivative cutoff is
c0(X/A0)^(k/(2k-1)); the full high squared norm costs
X^(b/2)A0^(-1/2)+(X/A0)^(k/(2k-1)). Both orientations, diagonal, every root
and cross terms are paid. The original physical rows A0=d and pd, with their
literal weights, give

    ||Q_D||_(1,2)<<D+X^(3/8)D^(3/4).

At D=X^(5/12) the exponents are5/12 and11/16, both below5/6. No false scaling
f_x(pn)=f_(x/p)(n) or signed-subset norm comparison is used.

Every R tuple has de>L, so n<=L is empty. Its coefficients obey a complete
divisor bound. [restricted research revision]'s full infinite high-tail theorem gives

    ||sum_(n>M)R(n)f_x(n)||_2^2
                   << X^(3/2+epsilon)+X^12 M^(-10+epsilon)
                   << X^(5/3+epsilon).

The original proof retains all integer gaps and damping; it needs no M<X^b
assumption. G182 allows the literal mask d>U,e>V,L<del<=M and pays gcd(d,e)>G
by X^epsilon[X/G+X^(3/4)/sqrt(G)]=X^epsilon[X^(5/6)+X^(2/3)]. There is no
additional coprimality restriction involving l.

For C_p(x)=sum_n c(n)f_x(n), define the complete finite core

    T_p(x)=sum_(L<del<=M,d>U,e>V,gcd(d,e)<=G)a(d)a(e)b0(l)f_x(del).

Norm triangle for these WHOLE sources proves, for every epsilon>0,

    ||C_p-T_p||_1+||C_p-T_p||_2 << X^(5/6+epsilon).          (192.1)

All cross terms and complements are paid. The remaining cofactor satisfies
l<M/L=X^(1/5), compared with1/4 for degree6 at the same target. These are

The fixed detector retains its complete Mellin return:

    D_c(z)=P_p(z)J_p(z)L(2z,chi^2)^2/L(z,chi),
    P_p=1-chi(p)p^(1-z), J_p=1-chi(p)^2p^(1-2z),
    H_p(z)=Gamma(z/12)e^(-i*pi*z/24)D_c(z)/12+E_p(z).

Rotate the individual integral to a fixed clockwise ray with angle less than
pi/24. The unchanged damping b=3/2 leaves an n^(-1/2) remainder after one
Taylor term, normally holomorphic for Re z>1/2 after the full coefficient sum.
All local derivatives are controlled. No finite shift is omitted here.
The multiplier and J_p L(2z,chi^2)^2 are nonzero above1/2. A fixed pair of
unramified primes covers every P_p zero except the stated principal pole
exception; for nonprincipal chi choose one p with chi(p)!=1 to cover height0.

Thus a COMPLETE core L1 bound X^(5/6+epsilon), for every epsilon and every
large dyadic shell, every fixed ordinary chi and its covering prime pair,
would exclude ordinary zeros above5/6. The fixed full C_p is recovered from

## 2. Primary prime input and order of quantifiers

I inspected Johnston–Yang, *Some explicit estimates for the error term in the prime number theorem*, [arXiv:2204.01980v2, Corollary 1.3, PDF page 2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2204.01980v2). Its version stamp is 20 April 2022; the printed date is 21 April. It states
\[
 |\pi(v)-\operatorname{li}(v)|
 \le9.59\,v(\log v)^{.515}e^{-.8274\sqrt{\log v}}
 \quad(v\ge2).
\]
Consequently \(R(v)=\pi(v)-\operatorname{li}(v)
=O_N(v/\log^N v)\) for each **fixed** \(N\). This is sufficient here. No short-interval relative PNT and no prime theorem with an order growing with \(X\) is assumed.

Partial summation gives
\[
 \sum_{p\le z}\frac{\log p}{p}\ll\log z,\qquad
 p_z\asymp t^{-1},\qquad h_z:=\prod_{p\le z}(1+p^{-1})\asymp t.
                                                               \tag{RNR3}
\]
In fact \(p_z=(c_M/t)\{1+O_N(t^{-N})\}\) for every fixed \(N\).
To see the latter rate, write the partial-summation formula for
\(\sum_{p\le z}p^{-1}\). The limiting constant in its \(R\)-part exists,
and its tail is bounded by
\(|R(z)|/z+\int_z^\infty|R(v)|v^{-2}\,dv\).
Using a stronger fixed PNT order gives \(O_N(t^{-N})\).
The terms of degree at least two in \(\log(1-p^{-1})\) have tail \(O(z^{-1})\).
This establishes the rate without a growing-order PNT. Also
\(h_zp_z=\prod_{p\le z}(1-p^{-2})\) stays between positive constants.

The source's quantifiers are legitimate: fix the profile, analytic bidisc, requested logarithmic error orders and any fixed band ratio first. Then choose a common sufficiently large \(X\). Only the finite-Euler/Taylor degree grows afterward.
