# [private research revision]: multiplicative calibration and the complete window-energy return

The [frozen source](headroom-source/report.md) and
[independent reconstruction](headroom-source-review/report.md) prove two
useful results. **Neither proves a larger zero-free constant.** The written
incumbent remains c6=125139/1000000, theta6=.874861, with its existing
source-relative acceptance and external dependency/admission obligations.

## G71. A calibrated multiplicative countermodel

Fix q, tau>0, finitely many prescribed unit prime values away from q,
and 1/2<beta<theta6. There exists one ordinary multiplicative sequence a
with a(1)=1 and |a(n)|=mu(n)^2 1_(n,q)=1 such that:

- Every fixed ordinary-character twist has partial sums
  O_epsilon(x^(beta+epsilon)). An additional real height costs 1+|t|.
- Every fixed nondegenerate pair of positive integer affine forms has
  vanishing conjugated and unconjugated Cesaro correlation, also with
  fixed character weights. For each fixed H, its unweighted average
  window square tends to H times the squarefree/coprime density.
- Its complete Gaussian field has a nonzero leading power:

      F_a(x)=exp(tau beta^2/2) H(beta) x^beta+O_sigma(x^sigma),
      1/2<sigma<beta, H(beta)!=0.

This combines multiplicativity, quantitative summatory calibration and
fixed-form cancellation. W27 already had a **real** multiplicative
finite-prefix countermodel; [private research revision] had a calibrated nonmultiplicative
model. The present added package allows complex phases and is not a
strengthening in real-valuedness. No literature-priority claim is made.

The construction starts with squarefree Steinhaus multiplicative values
and replaces the prime value by1 independently with probability
p^(beta-1). The replacement primes have summable reciprocal mass and
summable p^(-b) mass for every b>beta. The exact local quotient has
coefficients bounded by2, so its weighted convolution norm is finite.
Orthogonal dyadic maximal estimates give the original x^(1/2+epsilon)
calibration; convolution yields the asserted x^(beta+epsilon) calibration.

Centering the prime values gives a holomorphic prime series on Re(s)>1/2.
The complete series factors as zeta(s+1-beta)H(s), with H nonvanishing
there and at most exponential height growth on fixed strips. The full
Gaussian contour crosses the simple beta pole; its height decay pays
every horizontal and vertical tail. Finite prescriptions and ramified
deletions preserve this pole.

For each finite prime modification, affine conjugated monomials are
indexed by a rational ratio, with bounded multiplicity from the nonzero
affine determinant. Unconjugated monomials are indexed by a product,
with at most two roots for each fixed local divisor pair. Their second
moments are O_F(N); square-subsequence Borel--Cantelli and bounded gaps
give Cesaro cancellation. Summable reciprocal mass transfers this from
finite modifications to the infinite replacement set.

The order of quantifiers matters: fix the finite prescriptions first,
then intersect over countable finite sets, affine forms and ordinary
characters, and select one outcome. There is no uncountable-intersection
shortcut. The critic's finite-component decomposition also proves uniform
finite-phase control when that stronger wording is wanted. No growing
conductor constant or uniform growing-H rate is supplied.

The sequence lacks the actual global prime law a(p)=-chi(p) of mu(n)chi(n)
and its prescribed convolution inverse. Thus G71 rejects deductions from
the listed coarse properties alone; it does not reject actual arithmetic
arguments exploiting those missing laws. Feasible individual finite
valuation masks preserve the pole. A signed combination may remove it,
but a complete reconstruction restores it.

## G72. A complete quantitative short-window return

For any |a(n)|<=1, extended by zero to n<=0, define

    B_H(k)=sum_(j=0)^(H-1) a(k-j),
    w_X(k)=exp(-log(k/X)^2/(4tau)),
    E_a(X,H)=(1/H) sum_(k>=1) |B_H(k)|^2 w_X(k).

Every endpoint and both tails are included. Put ell=log2 and

    K_tau=exp(ell^2/(3tau))
          [exp(tau/3+4ell/3)/sqrt(3pi tau)+1/(pi tau)].

For X>=1 and integer H>=1,

    sup_(X<=x<=2X)|F_a(x)|
       <=sqrt(K_tau (X/H+1) E_a(X,H))+2H g_tau(0).

Partition the positive integers in each of the H possible block offsets.
Replacing each Gaussian by its value at the right endpoint costs at most
H times its total variation, namely2H g_tau(0). Weighted Cauchy, the exact
Gaussian square completion and a unimodal lattice sum bound give the
displayed factor. Averaging the H offsets pays precisely the normalization
1/H; no extra H is hidden.

The exact signed lag expression is

    E_a=(1/H) sum_(|h|<H) sum_(n>=max(1,1-h))
       a(n) conjugate(a(n+h))
       sum_(j=max(0,h))^(min(H-1,H-1+h)) w_X(n+j).

The weight moves with n,j. It is not replaced by a triangular constant,
and no off-diagonal term is removed by positivity.

For H=floor(X^theta),0<theta<1, the OPEN hypothesis

    E_(mu chi)(X,H) <<_(epsilon,chi,tau) X^(e+epsilon)

for every epsilon, each fixed ordinary character, and all sufficiently
large dyadic X returns the complete fixed Gaussian exponent

    gamma=max(theta,(1-theta+e)/2).

The O(H) replacement error is included in gamma. Both Gaussian tails and
the nonvanishing Mellin factor exp(tau s^2/2) then return ordinary
Dirichlet zero exclusion on Re(s)>gamma. This is a fixed detector; growing
H changes an estimate of it. Principal s=1 is its usual reciprocal zero,
with the external explicit exclusion retained. No Hecke or root-definition
identification is inferred.

The first-gain conditions are theta<.874861 and e<.749722+theta.
At theta=.26, e=1.00898 would give c=.12551; its first-gain boundary is
1.009722. Further conditional examples are:

| theta | Assumed e | Returned gamma | Conditional c |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| .26 | 1 | .87 | .13 |
| 1/3 | 1 | 5/6 | 1/6 |
| 1/2 | 1 | 3/4 | 1/4 |
| 3/5 | 11/10 | 3/4 | 1/4 |

The generic absolute estimate has e=1+theta. Its gap to first gain is
exactly2c6=.250278, independent of theta. Qualitative o(XH) alone supplies
no fixed power saving. These quantities normalize through the proved
return; they are not new numerical progress on the arithmetic input.

## Why G71 rules out the coarse-data shortcut

Applying G72 to G71 with theta<beta gives, on every large scale,

    E_a(X,floor(X^theta)) >> X^(2beta-1+theta).

At theta=.26,beta=.8747, this is exponent1.0094. The sequence also obeys
the weaker calibration exponent.8748<theta6 and every fixed-H averaged
limit, yet it violates the proposed energy target1.00898 by.00042.
For every proposed gamma<theta6, a beta between max(gamma,1/2) and theta6
provides the analogous countermodel. The obstruction needs a strict
exponent gap and does not settle equality or the actual Mobius sequence.

The next useful input must distinguish actual arithmetic from this model:
the exact global prime law, its convolution identity, or quantitative
control of all growing lags with the displayed full weights. This is a
material narrowing of the live short-window attack, not a generic survey.

## Evidence and continuity

The author and independent reviewer each supplied complete analytic
proofs, full readbacks and frozen hashes. Root read both arguments and
accepted the exact scopes above. Eleven frozen files are preserved here
byte for byte; the helper checks verify finite indexing and arithmetic,
not the analytic theorems. The original29-family/109-child portfolio,
all existing stronger restricted results and the full-H .004 deficit remain.

The primary screens of [Tao's logarithmic two-point result](https://arxiv.org/abs/1509.05422)
and [short-interval higher uniformity](https://annals.math.princeton.edu/2023/197-2/p03)
are motivation only. Their qualitative conclusions are not premises of
G71/G72 and are not promoted to a power-saving input. Source dates and
authors are retained in the frozen report.

The original battery-interrupted author/reviewer deadlines and authorized

## G77. Full contour gluing includes the horizontal and residue terms

For fixed U, M(s)=exp(tau s^2/2)/L(s,chi). Start at b>1, choose a in
(1/2,1) avoiding zero real parts and a finite height T avoiding boundary
zeros. No zero-free interior is assumed. The rectangle identity is

    U=V_(a,T)+H_top-minus-bottom+Z_residues+R_(b,T).

A zero rho of multiplicity m contributes x^rho times a polynomial in
log x of degree m-1 with nonzero leading coefficient
m exp(tau rho^2/2)/L^(m)(rho). The principal pole at 1 instead gives a
zero of 1/L. The F numerator has no zeros in this open strip.
The complete right-tail shell norm is

    ||R_(b,T)|| <= C X^b T^(-1) exp(-tau T^2/2).

Choose a boundary-admissible T_X within one unit above
sqrt(2(b-gamma+delta)log X/tau). The error is
O(X^(gamma-delta)/sqrt(log X)); the truncated ORIGINAL b-line band
is thus exponent-equivalent to U. Moving to a requires the full prices

    C X^a integral_(-T)^T exp(-tau t^2/2)|1/L(a+it)|dt,
    C X^b exp(-tau T^2/2) integral_a^b
                      (|1/L(sigma+iT)|+|1/L(sigma-iT)|)d sigma,

and all residues. No proximity-to-zero bound is assumed away.
A fixed finite nonempty residue packet whose maximal real part is
sigma*>gamma has shell norm >=c X^sigma* (log X)^d for all large X,
by positive definiteness of the fixed distinct-frequency Gram matrix.
This is conditional on such zeros existing. Its constant is not uniform
in growing T, zero count or separation, and it supplies no lower bound
for the growing packet. Complete contour gluing remains an open
arithmetic estimate, not automatic flux cancellation.

## 6. High bins: all signs, holes, valuations and labels paid

The complete genuine integer row is w=u0 e F_c G_c Vh'!=0. At an active first common prime of net exponent t, the two coefficients have residues 1+t and 1-t modulo six. Residue zero remains a coprimality hole. Keep u0; reflected rows are -w. Whole-character conjugation reflects the whole character and height, never just its fixed factor.

Let R0 be canceled active radical width and L_c=log_Z NF_c. The exact signed identity gives L_c<=5(R-R0). The enlarged ACTUAL radius gives

\[
 \log_Z Nw\le W+O(\eta),\quad
 W=M-R-(c-d)_++L_c-6a.
\]

Only the first projector s divides the genuine second common parts, hence G_c and w. The second projector t comes from the artificial separated extension and need not divide w. Its exact label count is paid with both extraction scalars in B3.67–69.

First common primes missing from w have radical width <=p-R-E+R0. At fixed w and that radical, arbitrary first/second valuations, first projectors and bounded slot assignments are divisor-many by SR's support Rankin bound. This covers arbitrary valuations, not just residues 0,...,5. The missing radical costs Z^(p-R-E+R0) once.

The actual natural unmasked representative has conductor <=K Nw, K fixed. Polynomial holes are paid through FM, not absorbed in K. Zero bins stay inside the ACTUAL parent translate of the Q_*-character group; the finite union over translates only makes constants simultaneous. Literal eligibility and nonprincipality transport through the same fixed Q_*. Sixth-power removal creates further holes; the raw-row lift converges since rho(delta)>=2/7>1/6.

For high bins delta in [7/10,3/4], the unchanged density

\[
 \rho(\delta)=1-\frac{10\delta}{3(5-2\delta)}
\]

therefore gives the JOINT count Z^(rho W+p-R-E+R0+eta)(1+T_h)^J. Negative nominal W is either an empty supported range or within O(eta) of zero, handled by bounded-window payment. No nonempty population is bounded by less than one.

The original second-projector allocation and paired pointwise plain/slot estimate give normalized exponent delta(A-c-b2)+eta; clipped reductions are nonpositive. Relative to the JOINT target p+A-c+R+E+B_c, the total excess is exactly

\[
 M(\rho-1)+\delta A+a(5-6\rho)
 +(1-\rho)(c-d)_+-\delta c-(1+\rho)R-E-B_c
 +\rho L_c+R_0+g_2-t_2-(1+\delta)b_2+O(\eta).     \tag{H}
\]

The middle terms are <=(4rho-1-delta)p-E-B_c, with 4rho-1-delta<=-79/270. Use c=min(c,d)+(c-d)_+, min(c,d)>=p>=R, rho+delta>1, 5rho>1 and L_c<=5(R-R0). The last terms are <=-delta*b2-t2 since g2<=b2. Thus all first labels, missing radicals, canceled factors, arbitrary valuations and second-projector costs remain paid; there is no subsequent Z^p or Z^s0 factor.

For A0=1121/1250 and a0=1/160, the negative of the first line is >=M H(delta), where

\[
 H(\delta)=1-\rho(\delta)-A_0\delta-a_0(5-6\rho(\delta)).
\]

Because 5-6rho=6(1-rho)-1,

\[
 H'(\delta)=\frac{50(1-6a_0)}{3(5-2\delta)^2}-A_0
 \ge1657177/4860000>0.
\]

Hence on the WHOLE high-bin interval,

\[
 H(\delta)\ge H(7/10)=3149/1350000>0.
\]

Even total high-bin errors M/10000 leave 1507M/675000>M/500. Bins straddling .7 go to the low branch using .7+O(e); density is applied only above its supported lower endpoint. The partition has no gap.

## 4. Common profile before labels; actual HB and slot payment

The coupled profile is separated on the ambient box of the ORIGINAL inverse and individual slot normalized norms on both sides, together with q_a/A and q_ell/H on fixed dyads. Its kernel is

    K(C*y_ell/[y_a^6 product(y_original_columns)]),
    C=UH/(A^6 N0^2).                                  (R11)

PR9 B3.3 fixes the Fourier measure on that entire box before choosing a,f,ell or a slot tuple. C depends only on nominal scales. Euler derivatives are uniformly bounded in C>0 by Schwartz seminorms. Only afterward substitute d1=f1 x and the other extracted forms. Their extracted imaginary powers have modulus one. The original real inverse roots enter the profile once. Sharp arithmetic masks and the first-dual cutoff stay outside the smooth separation.

The two original heights stay on their own inverse profiles. Products of their fixed polynomial seminorm bounds can be absorbed in a larger H_J. This is finite-order bookkeeping under the existing source contract; it does not close the independently open positive-slot uniformity ancestry.

The primary unconditional cubic-sieve statement is [Dunn-Radziwill, Theorem 9.1 and (1.11)](https://arxiv.org/html/2109.07463v3): both the outer and inner variables are squarefree primary Eisenstein elements, and the inner coefficient is an arbitrary sequence independent of the outer variable. Its bound has size D+E+(DE)^(2/3), times (DE)^epsilon and the inner squared coefficient mass. The upper bound is unconditional. The paper's GRH-dependent optimality lower bounds are not used. Cubic reciprocity and conjugation give the orientation chi_y(x)^4. No squarefree restriction on the separate first-dual frequency ell is needed here, because ell is a fixed coefficient parameter in each HB application.

Set S(D,E)=D+E+(DE)^(2/3). For bounded separated coefficients, Cauchy in x and HB give

    |(DE)^(-1/2) sum_(x,y sf) alpha_x beta_y chi_y(x)^4|^2
       <= H_J (DE)^epsilon S(D,E).                    (R12)

Indeed the two coefficient squared masses cost O(D), O(E); central normalization cancels their product. Fixed punctures are zero coefficients or restrictions of the positive outer sum. Their conductor sizes do not enter the HB constant. This is why an arbitrary large ell causes no hidden gcd or conductor loss.

On a given allocation put D1'=D1/q_f1, D2'=D2/q_f2, P'=P0/q_fP. The normalized complete residual column is

    B_f(ell)=(P')^(-1/2) sum_(original surviving P) b_P
                   [normalized two-inverse bilinear sum at D1',D2']. (R13)

Each bracket satisfies (R12). Ideal counting and the retained bounded slot coefficients give sum_P |b_P|<<H_J(P')^(1+epsilon). Thus pointwise triangle, followed by squaring, yields

    |B_f(ell)|^2 << H_J U^epsilon P' S(D1',D2')
                  << H_J U^epsilon P0 S(D1,D2).        (R14)

Assigned slot coefficients are already outside with modulus at most their original fixed profile bound. The discrepancy between P' and the product of the surviving nominal slot lengths is bounded by the original annular constants; it is kept in the profile. Natural holes at ell, f and a remain contractions throughout. The conjugate-side estimate has its own shortened lengths and follows separately. Its product with the left side is bounded by their geometric mean, without identifying their profiles.

This is an admissible HB argument after actual tuple conditioning. The forbidden B3.6 canonical merged-coefficient estimate is not needed at any step of (R12)-(R14).

## 9. Exact remaining target and quantitative return

Let Rmix be the real ordered off-diagonal contribution from R12/R16 with

    n!=n', Q>U^(9/5), Q1/Q3>U^(8/5),
    Q2Q3^2<C U^(2/5+2v), Q3<=C U^(2v),                        (R22)

and with the actual coefficients c(n),c(n') separately restricted by their original tuple gcd cutoff. The final two conditions are automatic support from R20--R21; imposing them does not change the remainder. Retain every canceled-prime hole, fixed phase, original slot allocation and both independent heights. On the tensor Sobolev norm, sum the actual derivative coefficient products over its fixed finite derivative list and integrate with its fixed positive parameter measure.

The open estimate is a one-sided bound

    Rmix <= H_J U^[T-xi+epsilon], xi>0,                         (R23)

uniformly for the prescribed data and profiles. It does not assert nonnegativity or bound every pair absolutely. R18--R19 plus R23 would control the entire small-gcd positive norm. R11 and R1 would then give OPEN-MIX with a margin less than `min(xi,1/200)`. Evaluating on both actual inverse witnesses yields the original weighted separated-row count; no slot denominator is used. Combining with G147's paid complement gives a density margin less than `min(xi,1/200,1/2000)`, after separately allocating the witness, height and buffer losses. For example choose half this minimum and choose all auxiliary losses before the final threshold. This implication is for the specified free natural source.

A numerical endpoint would still require the complete raw/positive-child and physical return, including both signed coprimality projectors, all original family reconstruction and root/slot holes, fixed-inducing and exceptional rows, physical radii and amplifier charges, clipped rectangles, every shortening/Euler shift, principal cases, and the actual-supremum/common-Delta contradiction. No such new transfer is proved here. The original descendant/fallback budgets remain unchanged, and c11 remains the endpoint input.

The strongest limiting example for this method is an admissible coefficient pattern, not a high-zero realization. With no slots, squarefree n gives

    c(n)=(D1D2)^(-1/2)mu(n)nu(n)
             sum_(d|n)W1(Nd/D1)W2(N(n/d)/D2).                  (R24)

The independent twists stay on their respective divisors. This extra divisor-profile weight is not the canonical coefficient permitted by B3.6. Coprime squarefree n,n' can have `Q1` of order `N0^2`, `Q2=Q3=1`, and within-column gcd one. They satisfy every new support restriction and remain in R22. The available absolute envelope `U N0` is much too large; that is an upper-bound obstruction to these positive estimates, not a lower bound for the actual signed norm. A common zero does not make the two witnesses probabilistically independent.

The next mathematical action is therefore to estimate R23 using the actual Mobius/divisor-profile coefficient, or derive an identity that changes it while paying every complement. R20 identifies short repeated-prime factors that can be kept outside such an attack. A further clean Poisson transform or repeated optimization of paid cutoffs alone leaves the squarefree signed obstacle intact.

## 1. Literal source and statement

Write U=Z^W and use the original Eisenstein ideals, primary/unit convention,
excluded set S and finite natural character dictionary. One whole orientation
is fixed, phi_u(n)=nu(n)psi_u(n)^(+/-1), with its actual zeros. The fixed nu
need not have order six. Put R=U^r, D=U^m and

    M_u(R)=R^(-1/2) sum_a mu(a)phi_u(a)W_I(Na/R),
    S_u(D)=D^(-1/2) sum_b phi_u(b)W_P(Nb/D),
    B_u=M_u(R)S_u(D).

The profiles include the original common real power and common witness height.
The original slot product Q_u retains its independent heights, all canonical
pools, every individual coefficient, root/puncture hole and natural zero.
Its total normalized width is v. No pool or profile is changed here.

Fix the physical bin delta in[.68,.70], v in[0,.05], 0<eta<=.001 and the
G137 cutoff t=t_*(delta,v)-eta BEFORE witnesses. After their original
construction, partition by label, internal bin and dyads, and retain the
parts with |r-r_*(t)|<=2eta. The dyads are common within each ensuing norm;
the original moment thresholds are uniform before that partition. G137's certificate
supplies r>1/2, 0<m<=1/2 up to its small allocated tolerances, and

    r+2v <= 1-c_1,       2r+8v <= 3-c_2,                 (1)

with fixed positive reserves (the first exceeds .01017 before fine losses).
We reuse these gates, not another optimization or scalar certificate. The
following estimate in fact holds in any fixed length box satisfying(1).

Omega contains only the original NONPRINCIPAL supported-witness rows. Principal,
artificial and fixed-inducing exceptions are not reclassified into it.
Partition the original rows by their actual internal buffered zero bin and
fixed witness label/dyads. Call one part Omega and its lower squared grade beta.
Here beta>=delta-small, beta<=3/4; the internal maximum can exceed the physical
bin. At the selected common real part/height the literal B0.15/B0.18 bounds give

    |S_u(D)|^2 >= D^beta U^(-epsilon_det),
    |S_u(E)|^2 <= E^beta U^(epsilon_det) H_J,
          0<E<=C D, u in Omega.                         (2)

The second bound uses the direct (unreflected) line in B0.15, so it is valid
even when a small endpoint tolerance makes m slightly exceed1/2. Every E
below is an ACTUAL shortened scale with the SAME character, real power, height
and plain profile. Bounded nonempty subunit E are comparable to a fixed positive
constant and satisfy(2) with a fixed multiplier; smaller E have empty support.
The source buffer/derivative losses may be chosen arbitrarily small BEFORE U.
They will be absorbed in the displayed final epsilon. We never put beta in
place of delta in a physical slot upper price.

Throughout H_J means a finite polynomial (1+T)^J in all retained heights;
the separate symbol H below denotes a square-divisor threshold, not that height.
For a nonnegative original radial weight (or its paid U^epsilon majorant),
write ||F||_Omega^2=sum_(u in Omega) w_u |F_u|^2. Enlarging this set is allowed
only AFTER a pointwise use of(2), inside a positive original MI norm. No
zero-conditioned Poisson formula is asserted. The literal PR9 B0.4/B3.31 gives

    ||M_u(E) Q_u||_(all original rows)^2
          << H_J U^(1+epsilon),        0<E<=C R,          (3)

uniformly over the shortened scales and the required rowwise witness parameters.
Section5 below pays its profile, mask, height and small-scale interfaces.

For ideals b define the integral ideal

    s_2(b)=prod_p p^floor(v_p(b)/2).

Let G,H>=1 be fixed functions of U, chosen before witnesses. Split the literal
ordered (a,b) coefficient sum of B disjointly into

    B_g:       N(a,b)>=G;
    B_s:       N(a,b)<G and N s_2(b)>=H;
    B_c:       N(a,b)<G and N s_2(b)<H.                   (4)

Thus B=B_g+B_s+B_c exactly, with equality placed on the first two sides as
written. These are signed source polynomials, not positive projections.

**Restricted arithmetic theorem.** For fixed positive g,h and G=U^g,H=U^h,
within all the preceding source hypotheses,

    ||B_g Q||_Omega^2 << H_J U^(1+beta*m-beta*g+epsilon),
    ||B_s Q||_Omega^2 << H_J U^(1+beta*m-2beta*h+epsilon).
                                                               (5)

The common buffer grade is used before weakening to physical delta. Define
the disjoint actual row classes

    Omega_g={u in Omega: |B_g(u)|>=|B(u)|/4},
    Omega_s={u in Omega\Omega_g: |B_s(u)|>=|B(u)|/4},
    Omega_c=Omega\(Omega_g union Omega_s).

Then(2),(5) prove bounds for the ORIGINAL inverse moment, not a substituted
coefficient family:

 sum_(Omega_g) w_u |M_u(R)Q_u|^2 << H_J U^(1-delta*g+epsilon),
 sum_(Omega_s) w_u |M_u(R)Q_u|^2 << H_J U^(1-2delta*h+epsilon).
                                                               (6)

On the entire complement,

    |B_c(u)|>|B(u)|/2, u in Omega_c.                     (7)

In particular choose g=4eta,h=2eta. Both proper classes save at least
(68/25)eta before freely chosen losses, hence imply the requested saving eta
there with substantial reserve. This is a genuine source-relative arithmetic
estimate on defined actual rows. It does NOT prove that all rows lie in their
union, or supply J_eta^all on Omega_c. No actual high-zero row or nonempty
dominance class is constructed. Empty common support is allowed, including

The following records the accepted W39 proof. [private research revision] strengthens its density
range in Section12; the historical kappa restriction is no longer the current
input requirement.

The [W39 local-set return]([private research revision]/local-valley-integration.md) gives an
alternative exact input for the COMPLETE fixed Gaussian. For every
epsilon>0 suppose every sufficiently large integer j has E_j subset
[j,j+1] with

    |E_j|>=c_epsilon j^-kappa,
    ess sup_(E_j)|F(y)|<=C_epsilon exp((gamma+epsilon)j),
    0<=kappa<1/2.                                      (G43)

For a fixed ordinary character,0<gamma<1, this implies the full
pointwise exponent gamma and zero exclusion Re(s)>gamma. For each fixed
finite-order trivial-infinity Eisenstein Hecke character, the separately
proved ideal-lattice count gives the same return for gamma>.5. Constants
may depend on the fixed member, ray modulus and omitted primes; no angular
or growing-conductor statement follows. Each family needs its own G43.

give h=gamma+2kappa(b-gamma). Mellin continuation excludes zeros before

growth. A finite iteration gives h_m=gamma+(2kappa)^m(B-gamma); fixed

every fixed half-plane Re(s)>=b>.5. The same proof gives the zeta

    .5<gamma<.874865, with a fixed kappa<.5.             (G44)

Its full square-moment equivalence uses Mellin continuation and dyadic
Cauchy--Schwarz, not an arbitrary L2-to-sup estimate. Missing intervals,
density-one information, isolated finite samples and favorable signed
subfamilies do not satisfy G43. The arithmetic small-value estimate is

### 1. The coupled character survives all mixed embeddings

For two branches write
\[
 D=G_*d,\quad E=G_*e,\quad(d,e)=1,
 \quad m'=[D,E]^2r,
 \quad c=gu,\quad c'=gv,
\]
where \(g,u,v\) are pairwise coprime squarefree cores and \(u\ne v\). The original rows are \(e^2r,d^2r\). The cubic Gauss cocycle and row characters give, respectively,
\[
 \gamma_2(gu)\overline{\gamma_2(gv)}
 =\gamma_2(u)\overline{\gamma_2(v)}\vartheta_g(v)\overline{\vartheta_g(u)},
\]
\[
 \chi_g(e^2r)\overline{\chi_g(d^2r)}
 =\vartheta_g(e)\overline{\vartheta_g(d)}.
\]
The angular and multiplicative core phases cancel, and the remaining quadratic-refinement phase is a fixed-ray factor by M B1.4. Consequently the moving character in \(g\) is exactly
\[
 \psi(g)=\vartheta_g(ve)\overline{\vartheta_g(ud)}, \tag{T07.2}
\]
times one of finitely many characters supported on the original fixed set. Natural zeros impose
\[
 (g,ruvde)=1,\qquad(u,e)=(v,d)=1. \tag{T07.3}
\]
These conditions imply \((ve,ud)=1\). Every good prime exponent in either product is one or two. Hence the good conductor is \(\operatorname{rad}(uvde)\), with norm \(R\ll q_uq_vq_dq_e\). Its character is nonprincipal unless all four labels are units, which would give the excluded equality \(c=c'\). A fixed-place twist cannot cancel a nontrivial good conductor. This argument is performed before row Poisson or outer-column Cauchy; the outer fields are independent of \(g\) after the finite ray split.

## R9. Exponents, independent check and what remains open

The finite projection error has norm exponent q=2/5; its square has exponent 4/5. Product tails have exponent -1+o(1). Under a target norm at gamma, both ordered target/error terms have exponent gamma+q, as follows either from the full expansion or the Hilbert triangle inequality:

| gamma | Conditional c | Target energy | Each target/error cross | Error square |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 5/6 | 1/6 | 5/3 | 37/30 | 4/5 |
| 3/4 | 1/4 | 3/2 | 23/20 | 4/5 |
| 1/2 | 1/2 | 1 | 9/10 | 4/5 |

Each listed cost is strictly below its target energy. With only the unconditional O(X) source norm, the cross cost is 7/5. That proves the unconditional fully-shifted comparison for the first two rows; it cannot prove the third. The same source and fixed parameters support all three CONDITIONAL returns. No row is an achieved c, and the last row is not an RH or GRH proof.

The independent helper in this review directory multiplies the three squared differences directly, without the author's 36-permutation enumeration. It verifies the complete 19-term polynomial, all five coefficient patterns, the 12/24 absolute signed multiplicities, the cofactor free-label polynomial and the entire bivariate identity R7.1 coefficientwise, rather than at selected numerical values. A small exact Gaussian-integer check then tests actual product coefficients through 144 for zeta, an order-four character modulo 5, and the principal character modulo 30. It checks every unramified prime up to 13, including nonleast primes, complex phases, squareful outputs and natural character zeros; every p^2 coefficient and median-complement coefficient agrees with R3.1 and R4.5. These cases address distinct algebraic failure modes, not statistical cancellation.

The same helper checks the rational sinc density, normalization, tail coefficient 64 and all displayed exponent comparisons. It binds the exact author/source bytes. Its single execution passed. The receipt is independent-receipt.json, 3910 bytes, SHA256 01e080efcf0b8808728a060c97fdca6f6d6ab586b23c75af85b81a21fdab4513. Source helper inspection and this finite check support the algebra only. They do not establish Fourier support by sampling, infinite tails, all-character uniformity, a zero-free region or either open moment. R2--R8 provide the analytic proof of the stated reductions.

The remaining prerequisite is precisely R8.1, or the stronger equivalent square-moment pair R7.5, with its complete signs and all-scale quantifiers. It is not supplied by prime-power annihilation, the positive Fourier kernel, the now-paid 24 shifted terms, a finite theta window or the old determinant inverse. The free-factor channel retains the original correlations. A substantive next mechanism must estimate those signed correlations or provide a new source/readout that pays them while preserving all-height zero information.

# W40 independent review: exact budgets and their arithmetic limits

**ACCEPT the author's three developed results and the scoped failures in
all six selected tests. No material repair of their main arguments is
needed.** The sharp disk budget has a complete conditional zero return,
but its bare zeta hypothesis is false. The literal f3 positivity cost and
the length-dependent projector-cycle obstruction are valid. Neither is
a full-moment or native-H estimate. No larger c is proved.

This review adds a proved extension of the boundary obstruction: **even

the all-height budget**. It also executes the two pre-outcome audits:

noncommuting prime projections; uniform W40-22 gives a complete finite
phase-transport certificate with unmatched mass and angular error paid.

## 1. Immutable intake, sampling and audit chronology

## 2. W40-20: the Poisson budget and complete conditional return

Let h be holomorphic beyond the closed unit disk, h(0)=1, and
u(theta)=Re h(e^(i theta)). With dm=dtheta/(2pi), define
B=integral(-u)_+ dm. Mean value gives integral u_+=1+B and integral
u_-=B. For |z|=rho, the Poisson kernel ranges between
k=(1-rho)/(1+rho) and k^-1. Therefore

    Re h(z) >= k(1+B)-B/k.                          (R40.1)

The right side is nonnegative exactly when B<=b(rho), where
b(r)=(1-r)^2/(4r). Since b is strictly decreasing on (0,1),

    B<=b(r) implies Re h(z)>0 for every |z|<r.      (R40.2)

The non-strict budget is sufficient for the OPEN disk. On the target
circle equality only assures nonnegativity. The signed representation
by (e^(i theta)+z)/(e^(i theta)-z) follows directly from Fourier
coefficients of Re h and h(0)=1; no positive measure or logarithm of h
has been assumed.

Sharpness is correctly qualified. The two-atom signed Herglotz function
(1+B)(1+z)/(1-z)-B(1-z)/(1+z) vanishes at-r_B, with
B=b(r_B), and has boundary poles. Replacing z by tz, t<1, and choosing
r_B=tr gives a function analytic past the circle with its zero at-r.
As t tends to1, the positive and negative Poisson kernels concentrate at
opposite points, so the negative mass tends to b(r). For any larger
proposed budget choose r'<r with b(r') still below that budget, then
approximate at r'. Its zero lies inside the target disk. This proves
sharpness of the uniform budget even in the smooth-boundary class;
it does not claim attainment there at a boundary pole.

For a fixed ordinary or fixed finite-order trivial-infinity Eisenstein
character, take P=L for a nonprincipal member and P=(s-1)L for a
principal member, including the removable value at1. The fixed lattice
argument and periodic character sums give the respective counting errors
O_f(sqrt x+1) and O_q(1). Abel summation makes P holomorphic on Re s>1/2,
with nonzero regularized principal value at1. The Euler product is
nonzero on Re s>1. This package was independently reconstructed in W39
and is now explicitly accepted in [private research revision]; no small-set hypothesis is
being imported here. Fixed ray modulus and all deleted Euler factors
remain. Moving conductors or nontrivial infinite type are outside scope.

With R=7/5, h_t(z)=P(2+it+Rz)/P(2+it) is analytic beyond the unit disk,
whose left edge is .6>.5. For .6<gamma<1 set r=(2-gamma)/R. A zero
beta+it with gamma<beta<=1 gives a zero of h_t inside |z|<r; the Euler
product covers beta>1. Hence the all-real-height B(h_t)<=b(r) hypothesis
does imply the stated fixed-member zero-free half-plane. Each family
member needs that hypothesis separately. This is a complete local-disk
return, not a mean-height or finite-height assertion.

The target budgets check exactly: c=.125136 gives r=70321/87500 and
B<=295118041/24612350000; c=1/6 gives1/120; c=1/4 gives9/2800.
The first numerical difference from c4 is only a CONDITIONAL .000001.
No such all-height budget has been proved.

A finite Euler product E_t(s) preserves zeros on this disk because each
1-chi(p)N(p)^(-s) is nonzero for Re s>0, with trivial factor1 at natural
zeros. It is legitimate to choose a different finite product at each t
for this local theorem. Its existence with the required budget is an
additional arithmetic condition. The theorem does not silently assert a
single fixed Mellin transform for those varying products.

The constructive finite-height certificate is also valid. A negative-part
map is1-Lipschitz; integrating distance from each left grid endpoint gives
angle error pi M_theta/N. A height net with nearest distance delta/2 adds
M_t delta/2. Quotient differentiation yields exactly the author's
R sup|Q'|/m and sup|Q'|/m+sup|Q|sup_anchor|Q'|/m^2 bounds. An interval
certificate pays value errors as well and covers only its stated heights.
The packet performed no such L-function numerical certificate.

## 3. The actual zeta failure and an independent stronger obstruction

### 3.1 Primary input and the author's bare normalization

I independently opened Johan Andersson's [arXiv:1010.0386](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1010.0386),
Theorem2 on PDF page2. It gives positive-lower-density vertical zeta
approximation to each continuous target on a compact empty-interior set
in .5<Re s<1 with connected complement, for each fixed positive error.
Only this stated theorem is imported. The visible v1 stamp is3 October2010;
the PDF title date is30 October2018. No literature-priority inference or
PDF-byte hash is manufactured from these dates or the web extraction.

Take I=[pi-delta,pi+delta], delta=1/40, s(theta)=2+R e^(i theta).
This simple compact arc has connected complement and lies in
[.6,.6+R delta^2/2] inside the universality strip. For each fixed M>=32,
the primary theorem supplies arbitrarily large t for which
zeta(s(theta)+it)=-M+e(theta), |e|<1 on the whole arc.

Absolute convergence at2 gives w=1/zeta(2+it), |w-1|<3/4, so
Re w>1/4 and |w|<7/4. For t>=40,
k=(s(theta)+it-1)/(1+it) has |k-1|<=R/40;
|w(k-1)|<1/16 and |wk|<2. Therefore

    Re[w k (-M+e)] < -M/4+M/16+2 <= -M/8.

The normalized negative mass is at least M/(320pi). Letting M vary
proves sup_t B(h_t)=infinity for P=(s-1)zeta. For each fixed budget,
bad heights have positive lower density after discarding t<40. There is
no quantitative relationship between M and the first such height here.
This disproves the bare sufficient budget without producing, assuming
or excluding any off-line zero. The anchor phase and pole-removing factor
were both paid; neither was replaced by1.

### 3.2 Critic theorem R40-E: every fixed finite Euler universe fails

The author's bare calculation explicitly leaves finite Euler products
untested. The following additional argument closes **all subsets of a
fixed finite prime set simultaneously**, including height-adaptive choices.
It still leaves genuinely unbounded prime universes or other multipliers
open. This strengthening belongs to this independent review.

Fix a finite set S of rational primes. For A subset S define
E_A(s)=product_(p in A)(1-p^-s), and

    h_(t,A)(z)=[(1+it+Rz)zeta(2+it+Rz)E_A(2+it+Rz)]
                       /[(1+it)zeta(2+it)E_A(2+it)].

Then

    sup_(t>=40) min_(A subset S) B(h_(t,A))=infinity. (R40.3)

Use the same fixed arc I. Put a_p=p^(-3/5) and define finite constants

    m=(1-R/40)/4 * product_S(1-a_p)/product_S(1+p^-2)>0,
    Q=7(1+R/40)/4 * product_S(1+a_p)/product_S(1-p^-2),
    D=R/(40-R)+R sum_S (log p)a_p/(1-a_p).

Let

    q_(t,A)(theta)=k_t(theta) w_t E_A(s(theta)+it)/E_A(2+it).

For every t>=40 and every A subset S, product triangle inequalities
give m<=|q|<=Q. The local factors never vanish on this arc. Differentiating
their logarithms along theta gives

    |d/dtheta arg q| <= D.                          (R40.4)

Indeed k'/k has modulus at most R/(40-R), each Euler term contributes
at most R(log p)a_p/(1-a_p), and both anchor factors are constant in
theta. An argument branch exists on the interval I; no global analytic
logarithm or zero-free half-plane is assumed.

Choose one integer N>D+80pi, fixed once S is fixed. On the arc prescribe
the continuous, nonvanishing target

    f_M(s)=M[-(s-2)/R]^N
          =M exp(iN(theta-pi)).

The same primary theorem gives a positive-lower-density set of t>=40
where |zeta(s+it)-f_M(s)|<1 uniformly. These heights are common to all
A; the target does not depend on A or the unknown anchor phase.
For each such pair (t,A), the phase
phi(theta)=N(theta-pi)+arg q_(t,A)(theta) is strictly increasing, with
N-D<=phi'<=N+D. Its total range has length greater than4pi. Consequently
it contains some complete phase interval [2pi/3+2kpi,4pi/3+2kpi].
The corresponding theta interval has length at least2pi/[3(N+D)].
On that interval cos phi<=-1/2. If M>=4Q/m, the actual boundary satisfies

    Re h_(t,A)(e^(i theta)) <= -Mm/2+Q <= -Mm/4.

Integration on that interval therefore gives, for EVERY A subset S,

    B(h_(t,A)) >= Mm/[12(N+D)].                    (R40.5)

The interval can depend on A; its length and lower bound do not. No
intersection of independently selected good-height sets is needed.
Since M is arbitrary, R40.3 follows, with positive lower density of
simultaneously bad heights for each fixed proposed budget. The proof
uses only the inspected universality theorem and the displayed bounds.

Thus a fixed finite Euler product, or switching among subsets of a
bounded prime universe, cannot repair this positivity route for zeta.
The constants m,Q,D depend on S; when S grows without bound with t,
this argument provides no uniform m or D and proves no such rejection.
It also does not reject all zero-preserving analytic normalizations,
or establish a corresponding universality theorem for the Hecke family.
The all-family proposal already needs zeta, so this zeta obstruction
is a necessary test of any proposed fixed-universe repair.

This is distinct from W24C's negative-prime-frequency test for a
constant-corrected logarithmic derivative on Re s>1. It is also distinct
from SC25's exact alternatives for a fractional-linear pole transform.
Their scoped failures and genuine escapes remain correct. The new
statement concerns the particular normalized holomorphic source above.

## 4. W40-15: the exact positivity price for literal f3

The coefficient is f(n)=mu(rad(n/3^v3(n))), with value-1 at every
positive power of p!=3 and+1 at powers of3. It has no coefficient zeros.
Use the complete normalized Gaussian g_tau and sums F(x) and Z(x).
The accepted actual Euler convolution from [private research revision] gives
F(x)=O(x^beta) at beta=.8749<1; this is an independently paid Mertens
transfer, not an inversion of a presumed Gaussian norm bound.

## 5. W40-25: phase has metric content, with a cycle-length cost

    4sin^2(theta/2)<=m sum||u_j-u_(j-1)||^2

and count k<=y/d^2 with (k,q)=1 as (phi(q)/q)y/d^2+O_q(1).
The total error and the omitted Euler-product tail are O_q(sqrt(y)).
Partial summation in (9), uniformly for 1<=u<=2, gives

    D_all(X) = C_(q,b) X^b+O_q(X^(b/2)),
    C_(q,b)=d_q(2^b-1)/(2b)>0.

Since the removed n<=M diagonal is O(M), (6) proves

    E_chi(X)=E_<=M(X)+C_(q,b)X^b
               +O_(q,b,k)(M+X^(b/2)+X^k M^(2-k)log(2M)). (10)

In particular choose b=3/2,k=6,M=X^(19/16). Then

    E_chi(X)=E_<=M(X)+C_(q,3/2)X^(3/2)
                              +O_q(X^(5/4)log X).         (11)

The tail alone has the same main term and error, by (6) restricted to
n,m>M. This is an unconditional asymptotic for an actual signed source
sector, for every fixed ordinary chi, with natural zeros retained.
It also proves E_chi(X)>=(C_(q,3/2)+o(1))X^(3/2), since the core energy
is nonnegative. Unlike the earlier linear-source diagonal, this is a
proved lower bound on the WHOLE nonlinear energy; the full cross price
has become lower order. Consequently an every-epsilon L2 estimate with
gamma<3/4 is impossible for THIS b=3/2 source. Gamma=3/4 remains allowed,
as do the near and 1/6 targets. This is not an impossibility theorem for
L1 estimates, other b, other sources or zero exclusion itself.

statement:
### 4.1 The inherited exact source, with all endpoints

Fix an ordinary complex Dirichlet character chi modulo q. Let P^-(1)=infinity and P^+(1)=1. On integer states m>=1 and lower prime threshold p, define

    R(m,p)=sum_(n<=m,P^-(n)>p)mu(n)chi(n).

At the root the threshold is1. Least-prime factorization gives exactly

    R(m,p)=1-sum_(p<ell<=m, ell prime)chi(ell)R(floor(m/ell),ell).

All subsequent primes are strictly larger; repeated primes cannot enter. Let F be a floor-invariant approximation on the needed states and define its defect

    Delta(m,p)=F(m,p)-1
                +sum_(p<ell<=m)chi(ell)F(floor(m/ell),ell).     (W7)

For a fixed integer r>=1 suppose F equals R on the exact collar m<=p^r. That collar is descendant-closed: a child has m'=floor(m/ell)<=m and ell>p, so m'<=ell^r. Thus Delta=0 throughout the collar. In particular for r=1 the collar value is1; for r>1 it generally is not1.

G92's finite triangular inverse and integer merging give

    F(N,1)-M_chi(N)
       =Delta(N,1)+sum_(p prime,m>p^r) C_N(m,p)Delta(m,p),

    C_N(m,p)=-chi(p)
       sum_(N/[p(m+1)]<u<=N/(pm),P^+(u)<p)mu(u)chi(u).          (W8)

Every sign, zero and half-open endpoint in W8 matters. Its derivation is finite: expand E=Delta-sum chi(ell)E(child), obtaining one path for every squarefree d; write d=pu with p=P^+(d), then group by m=floor(N/d). The root term d=1 is retained separately. Grouping happens before absolute values. This is the existing G92 identity, not W52 credit.

statement:
## 6. An exact reciprocal-phase return, with a paid truncation

This is an alternative expression for the same remaining arithmetic, not an estimate for it. Freeze the product cap de<=8X before averaging on [e^{-1}X,2eX], with delta<=1/8. Every nonzero physical summand in DP26 lies under that cap. Extending its factor sum to this cap adds only zeros before Poisson summation. Define the Fourier transform with the convention hat f(xi)=integral f(u) exp(-2*pi*i*xi*u)du. Alternating Poisson then gives exactly

\[
 F_{A,\delta_X}(x)
 =-x\!\sum_{d,e>Y\atop de\le8X}\frac{\mu(d)\mu(e)}{de}
       \sum_{\nu\in\mathbb Z\atop\nu\ {\rm odd}}
       \widehat V_{\delta_X}\!\left(\frac{\nu x}{2de}\right)
       +O_R(X^{-R}).
 \tag{DP28}
\]

The outer sum is finite; the inner sum is absolutely convergent for each original pair. No unbounded factor range or absent zero-frequency term has been restored. For any fixed tau>0, its frequency sum may be restricted to

\[
 |\nu|\le X^\tau\max\!\left(1,\frac{de}{X\delta_X}\right)
 \ll X^{\eta+\tau},
 \tag{DP29}
\]

with an O_R(X^{-R}) error after all pairs are summed. To prove this, write s=de/(X*delta_X). DP23 bounds the tail, including x/(de), by C_B delta_X^{-1} X^{-tau(B-1)}; for s<1 an additional factor s^{B-1} is at most one. There are O(X log(2X)) ordered positive pairs with de<=8X. Thus the entire error is at most C_B X^{1+eta-tau(B-1)}log(2X), and a fixed sufficiently large B proves the assertion. No physical or spectral tail is silently discarded.

The phase itself is explicit:

\[
 \widehat V_\delta(\xi)
 =\int_{-1}^1 k(v)e^{\delta v}
                   \exp(-2\pi i\xi e^{\delta v})\,dv.
 \tag{DP30}
\]

Consequently the remaining sum has reciprocal bilinear phases nu*x*exp(delta*v)/(2de), actual mu(d)mu(e), and odd nu. Negative frequencies supply the complex conjugates of the positive ones. An estimate for unrelated arbitrary coefficients, independent d/e copies or a fixed restoration length is not a bound for this expression. DP28--30 expose a concrete candidate for a signed bilinear mean; they do not provide that mean or improve c.
title: 6. An exact reciprocal-phase return, with a paid truncation

 \frac{\|u_\nu\|^2}{\|u\|^2}
 =\frac{1-Q^{-2}}{1-Q^{-2-2\Re\nu}},\qquad
 (1-Q^{-\nu}x_p)P_s(u_\nu)=(1-x_p)P_s(u).
 \tag{A07.7}
\]
The cross-multiplied identity includes zero base periods and is first justified in absolute convergence or on finite prime products with the inherited continuation. Formally weighting the entire cube label by \(q_B^{-\nu}\) changes the fixed completion to
\(L^S(3s-1+\nu,\xi_{\rm ang})D_h(s)\).

### D1.1 One-sided local criterion

**Proposition.** Fix1/2<a<1. Suppose that for every compact K contained in Re(s)>a, every epsilon>0, and all sufficiently large integer k,

    integral_K log^+|Q_(2^k)(s)| dA(s)
           <= C_(chi,K,epsilon) 2^(k epsilon).           (LP_a)

Here dA is ordinary planar area and log^+u=max(0,log u). It suffices to assume this on a countable exhaustion by closed rectangles with interior in the half-plane. Then L(s,chi) has no zero in Re(s)>a. If the same a works for each fixed ordinary chi, this gives a common c=1-a, with character-dependent constants and onset. LP_a is OPEN at every proposed a<theta10.

**Proof, including the missing continuation.** Write h_k=H_(2^k). The positive part of the harmonic function Re(h_k) is subharmonic. The area mean inequality on a disk of fixed radius r gives

    (Re h_k(z))_+ <= (pi r^2)^-1
                    integral_(|w-z|<=r) (Re h_k(w))_+ dA(w).

Thus LP_a gives a local upper bound Re h_k=O_(K,epsilon)(2^(k epsilon)). At a fixed real b>1 the exact series in(1) makes h_k(b) bounded, including its imaginary part. The Borel-Caratheodory disk inequality

    sup_(|z-c|<=R/2)|f(z)|
       <=3|f(c)|+2 sup_(|z-c|<=R) Re f(z)

and a finite overlapping-disk chain from b yield

    sup_K |h_k| <= C_(K,epsilon) 2^(k epsilon)             (4)

for every compact K in the connected half-plane. A harmless absolute constant can be added on the right of the disk inequality when the displayed supremum is negative; alternatively use its maximum with0. All chain geometry is fixed before k grows. This step shows why an uncontrolled imaginary additive constant cannot enter: the actual logarithm is anchored at b.

Let f_k=h_(k+1)-h_k. On every compact subset of Re(s)>1, the omitted prime interval and the continuous integral give

    |f_k(s)| <= C_b 2^(-k(b-1)) when Re(s)>=b>1.          (5)

The integer majorant sum_(n>2^k)n^-b suffices; no prime theorem is used. Meanwhile(4) gives local O(2^(k epsilon)) growth for every epsilon>0. These two facts imply exponential decay of f_k on EVERY fixed compact in Re(s)>a. For completeness: start with a disk in Re(s)>1 where(5) has exponent -d<0. A chain of disks with radii r,2r,4r inside the half-plane propagates decay by Hadamard's three-circle inequality. An inner bound2^(-kd_j) and outer bound2^(k epsilon) give a middle bound2^(-k(d_j-epsilon)/2). For a chain of N disks choose epsilon<d/2^(N+1); then every resulting d_j remains positive. Finite covers handle an arbitrary compact. Constants depend on the compact and do not depend on k.

Hence sum_k f_k converges locally uniformly, and h_k has a holomorphic limit H on Re(s)>a. Q=exp(H) is holomorphic and nonzero. On Re(s)>1 it has the required initial value; the identity theorem extends(3) throughout Re(s)>a. Its right side never vanishes, so a zero of L at any fixed height is impossible, with every multiplicity covered. At1 the principal pole has already been canceled by its explicit factor. This proves the proposition.

**What is weaker and what is not.** LP_a allows any fixed logarithmic power in the positive pressure and even arbitrary subpower growth of the finite cutoff. It asks neither for a uniform O(1) finite-volume bound nor a lower pressure bound. The analytic anchor and rapidly converging dyadic increments force actual local convergence. It is nevertheless a complete all-dyadic-cutoff arithmetic hypothesis, not finite evidence, a density-of-good-volumes hypothesis, or a claim that independence proves cancellation. A finite isolated zero is visible to this return, unlike T24's bulk statistic.

## 3. D04: complete independent reconstruction

### 3.1 Actual coefficients, powers, masks and absolute convergence

Fix tau>0 and one ordinary chi modulo q, with natural chi(n)=0 on nonunits. Define f(n)=mu(rad(n/3^v3(n))) and F_chi(x)=sum f(n)chi(n)g_tau(log(n/x)). For P subset of primes>=5 not dividing q, write n=rv with r its complete P-smooth part. This is a unique decomposition, including repeated prime powers, n=1 and nonunit v. Therefore f(n)chi(n)=a_P(r)f(v)chi(v), and the coefficient convolution a_P*f_P equals the sequence n -> f(n)chi(n). The exact field identity is

    F_chi(x)=sum_(r P-smooth) a_P(r)V_P(x/r).

At p in P, a_P(p^j)=-chi(p)^j for EVERY j>=1. Its local series is (1-2chi(p)z)/(1-chi(p)z); replacing it with1-chi(p)z would change the actual source. Since chi(p) has modulus1 on P, sum |a_P(r)|r^-sigma equals product(1-p^-sigma)^-1 exactly. Prime3 is never removed; prime2 remains in the source; q-divisor terms keep their literal zero extension. There is no squarefree surrogate, free gcd restriction or altered character scope.

Absolute field rearrangement can be proved without assuming OPEN-D04: choose a weight s0>1, use the bounded t^-s0 positive Gaussian integer field on all t>0, and sum |a_P(r)|r^-s0. This handles even t=x/r tending to0 and gives local uniform convergence. For a fixed parent X, P is finite. Infinite powers do not require a finite compact-support argument. The later norm decomposition splits that very same exact identity.

### 3.2 All scales and the paid head

Assume1/2<gamma<1, 0<sigma<gamma, A>0, A(1-sigma)<1, 0<delta<1 and q_head=sigma+delta(1-sigma)<gamma. Freeze P_X={5<=p<=(log X)^A:p not dividing q}. OPEN-D04 is the complete signed L2 norm of V_(P_X,chi) on EVERY REAL shell[U,2U], X^delta<=U<=X, with constants uniform in X,U and every epsilon. Its cutoff remains P_X, including at U=X/r. An own-scale P_U estimate, prime-only source or selected rough depth does not satisfy this premise.

For fixed sigma<1, summing over all integers gives log W_(P_X)(sigma)<=C_sigma(log X)^(A(1-sigma))=o(log X). This elementary bound needs neither PNT nor probabilistic independence. At r<=X^(1-delta), exact U=X/r lies in the declared interval, including equality. Minkowski gives X^(gamma+epsilon')W_(P_X)(sigma). Choose epsilon'<epsilon and absorb the subpower cost.

For r>X^(1-delta), t=x/r<=2X^delta. Independently, S_tau(t)=sum g_tau(log(n/t)) is O_tau(t) for t>=1, by its integral and bounded variation, and O_(tau,sigma)(t^sigma) for0<t<1, by the Gaussian left tail. Consequently S_tau(t)<=C X^(delta(1-sigma))t^sigma throughout this head. Coefficient moduli<=1 then give its pointwise and shell-L2 norm at most

    X^(sigma+delta(1-sigma))W_(P_X)(sigma)=X^(q_head+o(1)).

This pays every omitted smooth r, the bounded/small t range, all character zeros and the entire head square and mixed terms after expansion. No submask energy heredity is invoked. The strict margin q_head<gamma closes the triangle proof. Gamma-epsilon conventions in norm versus square moment are harmless because all epsilon allowances are quantified. The coarse price is sufficient; equality of this price with gamma is not a general impossibility theorem.

**Verdict:** ACCEPT the conditional theorem D04.1--D04.6 with its complete quantifiers. OPEN-D04 itself is unpaid.

### 3.3 Character-specific transform and all-height zero return

For Re s>1, exact Euler/Fubini gives Mellin(F_chi)(s)=exp(tau*s^2/2)H_chi(s)/L(s,chi). At p!=3,

    H_(chi,p)=(1-2chi(p)p^-s)/(1-chi(p)p^-s)^2;
    H_(chi,3)=(1-chi(3)3^-s)^-2.

At every p|q the factor is1, including2 or3 when ramified. At unramified p>=5, the degree-one term cancels, so the product converges absolutely locally for sigma>1/2. Numerator zero lines are sigma=log_p2<1/2; denominators have possible zero lines sigma=0. At2 the numerator zero line is sigma=1, which must remain exceptional;3 has no numerator. Thus H_chi is holomorphic/nonzero for1/2<sigma<1. Complex characters alter phases, not these real parts.

The fixed field has a Gaussian left tail. Dyadic Cauchy--Schwarz with an epsilon smaller than the compact strip distance makes its Mellin integral holomorphic on sigma>gamma, with every fixed derivative. Multiplying by L and continuing the exact identity gives a contradiction at each L-zero with gamma<Re rho<1, because exp(tau*rho^2/2)H_chi(rho)!=0. The usual independently known right boundary handles sigma>=1; principal pole treatment is meromorphic and not a falsely excluded zero. There is no height cutoff or requirement of a nonvanishing p2 numerator at sigma=1. This is a separate fixed-chi implication: zeta-only OPEN-D04 does not imply the needed field estimate for every chi. No growing-conductor, angular or new Eisenstein transfer is proved.

**Verdict:** ACCEPT D04.7 as an ordinary fixed-character conditional zero return. The exact f3 transform is a changed source relative to matched-Max's mu detector, not a harmless renaming. Its character zeros, p2/p3 factors and conditional c=1-gamma are all retained.

### 3.4 Inverse and actual arithmetic strength

Inverting the local series gives b_P(p^j)=2^(j-1)chi(p)^j, j>=1. Its absolute weighted mass is product(1-p^-u)/(1-2p^-u), finite at each fixed u>log_5(2); for fixed u<1 its logarithm is O_u((log X)^(A(1-u))). For finite P containing2, excluding3, define Q=product P and e_P(n)=product_(p in P)(-1)^(1_(p|n)). These are f3's exact local all-valuation signs on P.     Q^-1 sum_(n mod Q)e_P(n)e_P(n+h)
       =product_(p in P)[1 if p|h, else 1-4/p].

## Compact worklog and discovery decisions

The objective is a genuinely different upstream source, retaining an honest full return. The accepted G83-G85 growing-order completion, Gaussian moment and its all-real-scale Mertens equivalence are inputs, not discoveries of this pass. In particular the old Q/Core estimate is not advertised as easier than Mertens. The full 29-family/109-child library remains retained.

Six mechanisms were considered before selecting one for detailed calculation:

1. A character-adapted Davenport/Bernoulli dilation source. Exact multiplicative inversion gives a two-frequency target, while the complete-period Gram can be evaluated through gcds. Potential reach is every gamma>1/2 if a sufficiently strong shrinking-arc estimate can be proved. Selected: it actually uses the global law mu*1=delta, unlike the earlier complex countermodel.
2. Prime-color expansion of the accepted growing moment. The uncapped local multiplicities are binomial, but a left-line Euler product does not follow from finite local calculations; G69 mass escape and the now-proved Q equivalence remain. Not duplicated.
3. Replicate a fixed character by inducing it to larger moduli and apply a large sieve. The copies are not independent primitive characters; their repeated direction carries the corresponding large eigenvalue. Removing the extra Euler factors also has a physical complement. No source bridge was found; not used.
4. A pole-normalized fractional reciprocal with fractional convolution. The library already contains W22-A/C and W21; an unnormalized fractional reciprocal creates a principal branch singularity at 1. There is no new contribution from renaming that route.
5. Quantitative almost-periodic repetition of a hypothetical zero. The naive box prescribing many independent prime phases has exponentially small volume, while the available approximation-tail control in that attempted construction is polynomial. No paid quantitative recurrence-to-zero-density bridge was obtained. This is a rejected unproved construction, not a theorem ruling out a better recurrence argument.
6. Renewal/Nyman positive floor kernels and a changed observation space. F08 and the Round25 floor/renewal pilots already retain the positive-cover and boundary-observation costs. The selected dilation calculation tests a different, explicit arithmetic Hilbert-space source rather than treating a finite Nyman fit as closure.

Weber, *Convergence of series of dilated functions and spectral norms of GCD matrices*, Acta Arithmetica 168.3 (2015), DOI 10.4064/aa168-3-2, arXiv:1407.5403v2. statement:
## 8. Uniform audit06: sparse scales, an obstruction and a paid repair

This card asks whether sparse observed scales plus deterministic interpolation can control the complete physical field. The distinction is between fixed geometric samples and a sufficient growing, explicitly located set of observations in EVERY dyadic interval.

### 8.1 One fixed bounded-coefficient Gaussian field defeats fixed geometric samples

Fix L>0, 1/2<beta<1, omega=pi/L and the original tau. Define the SINGLE real sequence

    a(n)=n^(beta-1) sin(omega log n - tau*beta*omega).

It satisfies |a(n)|<=1. For its complete original Gaussian field,

    F_a(x)=exp(tau*(beta^2-omega^2)/2) x^beta sin(omega log x)
                                      +O_(beta,omega,tau)(x^(beta-1)).   (A06.1)

Proof: replace the sum by the integral of

    phi_x(t)=t^(beta-1) sin(omega log t-tau*beta*omega) g(log(t/x)).

With t=x exp(v), the integral is the imaginary part of

    exp(-i*tau*beta*omega) x^(beta+i*omega)
                            exp(tau*(beta+i*omega)^2/2),

which is the displayed main term. The function is flat at zero and decays at infinity. Differentiating and making the same substitution gives integral |phi_x'(t)|dt=O(x^(beta-1)); all remaining v-dependent factors are a fixed exponential times a Gaussian and polynomial/trigonometric factors. Comparing phi_x(n) with its integral over [n-1,n] bounds the complete sum-integral error by that derivative integral. Both tails are included.

At x_j=exp(jL) the main term vanishes, so these samples are only O(x_j^(beta-1)). At the intervening half-period they have size comparable to x^beta, and the L2 energy on each logarithmic interval of length L has exponent beta with a fixed positive constant. Thus very small values on this fixed geometric grid do not imply a full-field improved exponent, even for a single fixed bounded sequence and exactly the original Gaussian.

One may take beta<theta6 to fit a buffered baseline. This is not mu*chi, integer coefficients or a multiplicative construction. W43 seed12 already contains the log-periodic invisibility mechanism; W38/[private research revision] contains different and stronger coefficient-class observation failures. The present calculation supplies an explicit bounded-coefficient fixed-Gaussian realization and does not erase those results or claim a new general countermodel family.

### 8.2 A sufficient all-shell Chebyshev observation contract

For arbitrary |a(n)|<=1, put mathcalF(y)=F_a(exp y) on the real line and extend it by the series sum_n a(n)g(log n-y). This Gaussian series is entire by local uniform convergence. The unimodal integral comparison gives, for real u,v,

    |mathcalF(u+i*v)|
       <=exp(v^2/(2*tau)) [exp(u+tau/2)+2g(0)].

For real y in [log X,log(2X)], X>=1, Cauchy's formula on a circle of radius A>0 therefore implies, with C_tau=2exp(tau/2)+2g(0),

    |mathcalF^(r)(y)|/r! <= C_tau X exp(A+A^2/(2*tau)) A^(-r).   (A06.2)

This prices the complex-strip growth and the derivative factorial explicitly. Let L0=log 2 and use the r Chebyshev nodes

    y_j=log X+(L0/2)[1+cos((2j-1)*pi/(2r))], j=1,...,r.

The monic node product has interval supremum 2(L0/4)^r. The sum of absolute cardinal polynomials is at most r^2: |T_r'|<=r^2 on [-1,1], |T_r'(t_j)|>=r at its zeros, and the difference quotient for T_r at t_j is bounded by r^2. Hence each cardinal polynomial has magnitude at most r. The divided-difference integral formula, obtained by repeated fundamental theorem of calculus, bounds the complex-valued interpolation remainder by sup |mathcalF^(r)|/r! times the node product. No false complex-valued one-point mean-value theorem is used. Consequently

    sup_(log X<=y<=log(2X)) |mathcalF(y)|
      <=r^2 max_j |mathcalF(y_j)|
          +2 C_tau X exp(A+A^2/(2*tau)) (L0/(4A))^r.          (A06.3)

For fixed 0<gamma<1 and delta>0, set

    r(X)=ceil((2*(1-gamma)+delta) log X/loglog X),
    A=sqrt(tau*r).

The logarithm of the remainder is

    log X-(r/2)log r+O_tau(r+sqrt(r))
       =(gamma-delta/2+o(1))log X.

Since r^2=X^o(1), the hypothesis

    for every epsilon>0, every sufficiently large dyadic X:
    max_(1<=j<=r(X)) |mathcalF(y_j)| <<_epsilon X^(gamma+epsilon)  (A06.OPEN)

implies the complete exponent gamma, pointwise and in dyadic L2. For actual a(n)=mu(n)chi(n), the same nonvanishing-numerator Mellin argument in Section4 gives the all-height zero return. This needs a common exponent for each fixed ordinary chi; no growing-conductor or ideal transfer is supplied.

The estimates are explicit enough to allow this r(X), unlike substituting a growing r into the fixed-order W48.1 theorem. Every shell and all prescribed nodes are required. No fixed number of samples, missing-shell condition, subsequence or computational observation establishes (A06.OPEN). The arithmetic node estimate is unproved, and no optimal sample count is claimed. Credit W39 G43/G45 and the prior observation/interpolation portfolio; the increment is a precise discrete sufficient contract for the actual Gaussian, not a new interpolation principle or a c gain.

## R3. Two exact presentations and the height-bin convention

For every nonunit ideal n,

    sum_(d|n)mu(d)=0,
    A_R(n)=-sum_(dm=n)mu(d)[1-V(Nd/R)].                (R2)

The unit is excluded in R2. No squarefree hypothesis or coprimality is needed. Complete multiplicativity of phi, including its zero values, gives both convolution presentations. Thus on any one nonunit product annulus with common weight W_X,

    T_X,u(s)=sum_(d,m)mu(d)phi_u(d)phi_u(m)(Ndm)^(-s)
                                      V(Nd/R)W_X(Ndm),
            =-sum_(d,m)mu(d)phi_u(d)phi_u(m)(Ndm)^(-s)
                                  [1-V(Nd/R)]W_X(Ndm). (R3)

Initially W_X contains 1-H, the exponential and the terminal cutoff. The sign is exact. The inverse coefficient remains mu(d)phi_u(d) in each presentation; no factor involving a live cofactor is inserted into a one-variable arithmetic coefficient. Fixed shared primes are handled by natural zeros, not by restricting to (d,m)=1.

Outside |P_R,u(rho_u)|>=1/4, the completed identity gives |F_R,u(rho_u)|>=1/2 for large U. A fixed dyadic partition in the original product n has O(log U) annuli, so some X=U^ell has |T_X,u(rho_u)|>=U^(-tau), for any prescribed small tau after the threshold. Initially t+lambda-o(1)<=ell<=B+1+o(1). This selection is a union over fixed annuli; it is not a moving arithmetic cutoff inserted into a source moment.

Separate d and m into fixed dyads D=U^r and M=U^m. On a nonempty product block, DM/X is between fixed constants, hence r+m=ell+O(1/log U). Mellin/Fourier inversion of the common product profile W_X(DM yz) produces powers y^(i omega)z^(i omega) with ONE common Fourier coordinate. The inverse-only profile is the dyadic bump times V(Dy/R), or times 1-V(Dy/R). All Euler derivatives of these profiles are bounded uniformly in their positive dilation parameters. The common measure is fixed on the ambient profile box before live rows, labels or real/height choices. Its total mass and rapidly decreasing tails are paid under B3.3.

The two representations can select different dyads and different Fourier coordinates omega_- and omega_+. Their actual character phi_u and actual zero real part sigma_u are the same. Within each pair its inverse and plain factors have the same height gamma_u-omega_±; the two pairs need not have equal heights. On extracting the central normalization,

    |M_±(U^r_±)S_±(U^m_±)|^2
          >=U^[(2sigma_u-1)ell-O(tau)],
    r_-<=t+o(1), r_+>=t-o(1),
    r_-+m_-=r_++m_++o(1)=ell+o(1).                    (R4)

When the stipulated buffered bin already covers both retained Fourier coordinates, write its exponent as delta_b=delta. B0.15, valid for every required bounded length, gives

    |M(U^r)|^2<=U^(delta_b r+small),
    |S(U^m)|^2<=U^[delta_b min(m,1-m)+small].           (R5)

The initial product lengths can be as large as B+1. They cannot be silently assumed <=1/2 before R5 is used. Comparing R4 with R5 first forces m_±<=1/2+small, since delta_b is bounded below. Then division by the other factor's pointwise bound yields saturation of each individual factor. All sufficiently large annuli ell>t+1/2+small are impossible in the original representation, rather than being discarded without a price.

For application to a physical high bin at a smaller initial height, use the retained [restricted research revision] internal buffered construction. Its actual exponent delta_b may exceed .70; it is not substituted into E_K or the physical slot price. Choose the internal attaining zero before either extraction. It has delta_b>=delta-O(buffer); the independently accepted zero-free bound keeps its real part in a compact subset of (1/2,1). Apply R4--R5 with delta_b, obtain m_±<=1/2+small, and only then weaken the four individual witness lower bounds to

    |M_±|^2>=U^(delta r_±-small),
    |S_±|^2>=U^(delta m_±-small).                     (R6)

Thus the two witnesses still use one actual zero, but that zero may be the internal-bin attaining zero rather than a previously selected physical-bin zero. Prefix evaluation below is valid at it because its real part is at least a-O(buffer). The enlarged integration rectangle and this O(buffer) change cost an arbitrarily small power. No upper assumption delta_b<=.70 is needed for saturation. This explicit convention avoids an unsupported extension of the physical height buffer and preserves the physical upper bound |Q_u|^2<<U^(delta v+small).

All finite profile and Sobolev derivative orders are set before the small internal height exponent. Take the common completion B large enough for the strip powers, all finite required tails and R6's later exponential removal. Those strip bounds can be chosen uniformly on the fixed real/length ranges without a live zero or buffer. The raw completion fixes a bounded maximum product length; the bin buffers can then be made sufficiently small for that range. Fourier tail powers follow their raw costs. Allocate a fixed part of the enlarged height box to each Fourier coordinate, and choose the final small height exponent after the returned finite seminorm orders, as in B3.3 and [restricted research revision]. For heights beyond that power range, the absolute row/slot count is absorbed in a larger fixed polynomial H_J. The final scale threshold precedes the live height. This is a finite source bookkeeping extension, not an unproved uniform estimate over arbitrary profiles or conductors.

For a small supplied height, inflate only the internal witness height box to at least U^(tau_-), with the two retained Fourier coordinates inside its buffered enlargement. The factor U^(tau_- J) from its fixed Sobolev height degree is allocated to the small loss. The source chooses the rapid Fourier decay order after the raw tail power and then tau_-, tau_+ compatibly with that loss. Original slot heights and their physical-bin exponent do not change. ## 7. Exact weighted extracted blocks, including all shared powers

Fix an extracted ideal L from the G198 expansion, let E=D/NL and define

    S_(omega,L)(E)=E^(-1/2)sum_c phi_u(c)W_P(Nc/E)omega(Lc).

For an ordered pair p,q in J put d=pq and h=d/(d,L). Primewise valuation
arithmetic gives d|Lc if and only if h|c. Consequently the EXACT formula is

    S_(omega,L)(E)=1/(log D)^2 sum_(p,q in J)
       (log Np)(log Nq) phi_u(h)(Nh)^(-1/2)
                                  S(E/Nh;V_D,2).    (15)

There is no division by a character value. If p=q, h is respectively
p^2,p or1 according as v_p(L) is0,1 or at least2. If p!=q, h contains
exactly the primes not already dividing L. The case L containing only one
power of p is therefore retained, rather than incorrectly treating p^2
as already extracted. The denominator is exact because
log(NL Nc)=log(D(Nc/E)). All remaining c valuations are still present.

Set s=(1+beta)/2 and

    I_L=sum_(p in J,p|L)log Np/log D,
    V_L=sum_(p in J,p not|L)(log Np/log D)(Np)^(-s).

The support of L in a nonempty original block has NL<=C D, so
I_L<=1+O(1/log D). Ideal counting and beta<1 give
V_L<<U^epsilon A^((1-beta)/2). For p!=q the absolute coefficient mass
after(4) is at most (I_L+V_L)^2. For the diagonal, p|L terms are bounded
by I_L^2 even when h=p; p not|L terms cost at most
U^epsilon sum_(p in J)(Np)^(-1-beta)<<U^epsilon Z^(-beta).
Thus uniformly in every extracted L,

    |S_(omega,L)(D/NL)|
       << H_J U^epsilon (D/NL)^(beta/2) A^(1-beta).  (16)

This is a bound on the literal extracted plain block. It is not an
operator norm for multiplying arbitrary signed coefficients by omega.
Its SQUARED loss is A^(2(1-beta))=Y^(1-beta), once.

Insert(16) inside the full G198 divisor expansion BEFORE taking its
absolute convolution. Its q0,k,L=lcm(q0,k^2) coefficients, all shared
prime valuations, and the complete q0-smooth inverse restoration are
unchanged. The uniform factor in(16) is independent of those labels.
Therefore the already proved absolute block mass T^(-beta/2) gives

    ||B_T^[omega] Q||_Omega^2
       << H_J U^(1+epsilon) D^beta T^(-beta)Y^(1-beta). (17)

No independence between L and p,q or between q0 and k is assumed.
In particular p or q can occur simultaneously in L, in the inverse
puncture and in a remaining plain cofactor. Formula(15), the old full
restoration and the literal character zeros pay those situations.

Now C_T^[omega]=B^[omega]-B_T^[omega] exactly. From(14),(17),

    ||C_T^[omega] Q||^2
       << H_J U^(1+epsilon)D^beta
                     [Z^(-2beta)+T^(-beta)Y^(1-beta)]. (18)

The squared savings at T=Y=Z^4 are 2beta eta and(8beta-4)eta.
Their difference is(6beta-4)eta>0 throughout the internal range after
choosing the buffer below its fixed reserve. At beta=17/25 they are
34eta/25 and36eta/25. Both exceed the requested eta, and(18) proves(2).
The complete removed-source price is why the paired extraction is useful;
it is not merely a new choice of scalar band endpoints.

### 4.3 Small and large shifts, including clipped zero capacity

The weight in (E2) pays \(U^{-\delta t/2}\). For small shifts,
\[
 \frac{\delta t}{2}+\frac q2[z_A(t)-z_A(0)]
 =t(\delta/2-q/C)\ge0,
\]
since \(q\le\delta/2\) and \(C>1\). Hence all these shifts preserve the nominal no-shift saving.

For \(t\ge t_0=10^{-3}\), put \(b=2y/d-1\) and
\[
 z_o(t)=\max(0,(b-2t)/(9/2)),\qquad
 S_b(t)=t/2-\{b/C-z_o(t)\}/4.
\]
The old capacity \(6\kappa\le9/2\) is no smaller than this comparison capacity. On the positive branch,
\[
 \frac1C-\frac29=\frac2{20241},\qquad
 S_b(t)=\frac{7t}{18}-\frac b{40482}.
\]
For the present geometry \(0<b\le9/50\) and \(b>2t_0\), so directly
\[
 S_b(t_0)\ge\frac7{18000}-\frac9{2024100}
 >\frac3{10000}.
\]
This is a simpler independent proof of the source's shift-reserve comparison. S is continuous at \(t=b/2\), with slope \(7/18\) before clipping and \(1/2\) afterward. Since \(b/C-z_o(t)\ge0\),
\[
 \frac{\delta t}{2}+\frac{qz_o(t)}2-\frac{q\,b/C}2
 \ge\delta S_b(t)\ge0.                         \tag{E3}
\]
This includes \(\delta=q=0\), and all shifts after old capacity becomes zero.

At zero capacity the two reflected lengths may sum to more than one. The source really does provide the needed unrestricted estimate:

- Energy-Bands.lean defines ZeroAt with only individual bounded-scale conditions \(X_i\le U^L\), not an affine sum condition.
- CertifiedZero.finite_pair_zeroAt permits each \(X_i\le U^2\) and returns \(U^{1+\delta_{\rm pad}+\epsilon}\). Here \(\delta_{\rm pad}\) is *fixed-character width padding*, not the detector zero-bin \(\delta\). The certified physical wrapper takes \(\delta_{\rm pad}=D.t/4\), absorbs it into the small requested loss, and returns \(U^{1+D.t}\), retaining independent Fourier heights.
- OriginalFourth.certified_original_numerator_fourth accepts precisely
\[
 2(m+\xi)+6\kappa\sum_{i\in I}w_i\le1
 \quad\hbox{or}\quad I=\varnothing,\qquad m+\xi\le2.
\]

Because \(h_0\ll Y\), every nominal reflected length is at most \(1+o(1)\), so all retained padded scales are below the cap 2. The physical row lower bound required in these wrappers holds in the growing dyads; fixed dyadic factors are paid by the reserved padding and threshold. There is no positive-part length penalty to add at empty selection. The weaker all-free-row unmarked estimate allowing exceptional rows is not the MP0 used in this endpoint.

Capacity decrements change either gain by at most \(q\nu/2\le3\nu/16\). Scale padding has a similarly bounded affine cost. These common errors can fit a prescribed fraction of the positive endpoint reserve; they do not change (E3)'s limiting exponent comparison.

## Coefficients, sectors and uniform tails

For p not dividing 3r, the local series of f_r is (1-2z)/(1-z).
Dividing by the Möbius factor 1-z gives
1-sum_(j>=2)(j-1)z^j. For p dividing 3r the quotient is
(1-z)^(-2). Thus the exact all-power convolution in S4 has finite absolute
beta norm for beta>1/2, bounded by C_(beta,delta)r^delta. This pays prime
2 and prime 3 without introducing a reciprocal factor 1-2*2^(-s).
Its constants are not uniform as beta approaches the accepted boundary.

For m=ga,n=gb and (a,b)=1, the two factors f(g) square to one.
After inserting sum_(q|a,b)mu(q), the next two f_g(q) factors also
square to one. The remaining whole field is exactly f_(gq), so the
signed coefficient of E_r(X/r) is sum_(g|r,g>=D)mu(r/g).
This proves S9 without assigning positivity to a correlation sector.
The Gaussian majorant makes the complete rearrangement absolute.

For r<=X the convolution estimate and the convergent sums in g and q
give X^(2beta+epsilon)D^(1-2beta). For r>X use the bound independent of
r, |F_r(y)|<=C_A y^A for y<=2. When D>X the ratio of the resulting
tail to the advertised bound is

    X^(delta-epsilon)(X/D)^(2A-2beta-delta) <= 1

after choosing delta<=epsilon and 2A-2beta>delta. When D<=X the same
tail is O(X^(1+delta)) and is absorbed at the worst endpoint D=X.
This independently closes the report's all-real-D quantifier.

The diagonal is the literal sum_(n>=D)K_X(n,n), since f(n)^2=1.
Subtracting it proves the off-diagonal statement. The complementary
sector retains all ordered pairs; writing b=a+h gives f_g(a(a+h))
only because (a,h)=1. The factor two and both Gaussian heights remain.
For gamma>1/2, the strict threshold
(2beta-2gamma)/(2beta-1) in S13 pays the large-gcd error and the

## 4. Simultaneous use: what has been paid and what remains

For one fixed eta, the old P_eta and the new M_eta,2 are related by a bounded invertible coefficient operator above 2/3. Their marginal exponent thresholds are therefore the same in that range. This does not forbid using them simultaneously: their arithmetic representations, usable partial estimates and cross terms may differ. It does rule out obtaining an exponent increase solely from the existence of two equivalent normalizations.

There are two legitimate directions for future combined work:

- Prove a complete bound for W_P in (3.5), or the distinct What_P in D26.4, using a source estimate for its actual coefficients. Equations (3.6), (3.12) and (3.7) pay the transfer and every cross term.
- Construct a fixed signal-preserving linear combination of actual fields and prove its signed joint moment. T01/T16 specify the signal constraint and the energy/mismatch cost. A source-aware combination may help; separately optimized shell weights, positive Gram diagonals or a covariance sign guess do not prove it.

The strongest objection to D02 was the possibility that nonvanishing H hides an unbounded inverse on growth norms. Equations (2.4)--(2.9) answer it with actual coefficients and reveal the 2/3 absolute threshold. The strongest objection to D26 was the omitted small-prime or higher-interaction cost. E is included in (3.5); all missing-prime interactions are included in (3.4); retained primes keep all powers; all shell cross terms are included in (3.7).
