statement:
## 4. An actual signed block with absolute mass of order X squared

Take \(W=2\). Choose odd squarefree, pairwise-coprime base variables

\[
D,E\in[\sqrt X,1.1\sqrt X],\qquad
f,h\in[3\sqrt X,3.1\sqrt X].
\tag{PO29}
\]

Retain the bases satisfying the orbital cofactor exclusions in
(PO11). For each such base quadruple, the following four terms all
belong to the new sector, with the right third factor \(m=1\):

| \(d\) | \(e\) | \(\ell\) | Relative Möbius sign |
|---|---|---|---|
| \(D\) | \(E\) | \(4\) | \(+1\) |
| \(2D\) | \(E\) | \(2\) | \(-1\) |
| \(D\) | \(2E\) | \(2\) | \(-1\) |
| \(2D\) | \(2E\) | \(1\) | \(+1\) |

Their common completed product is \(n=4DE\); all four product
cutoffs equal one for sufficiently large \(X\). Their individual
lower endpoints hold, and \(1,2,4\le J\). Also

\[
n\le4.84X,\quad n'\ge9X,\quad
\frac{n}{x}\in[2,4.84],\quad
\frac{n'}x\in[4.5,9.61].
\tag{PO30}
\]

Both profile values are negative and bounded away from zero on these
compact intervals, because the positive zero of \(1-t+t^{-1}\)
is \((1+\sqrt5)/2<2\). Thus each of the four integrated absolute
weights is bounded below by a positive constant. The gap condition
holds since \(|n-n'|\ge4.16X>P_{\rm gap}\), and
\(1-\sigma_2(n)\sigma_2(n')=1\).

There are \(\gg X^2\) base quadruples before the cofactor exclusion.
For completeness, this positive density can be proved by imposing
the desired divisibility patterns modulo finitely many prime squares.
The local density for an odd prime is
\((1-1/p)^4(1+4/p)=1+O(p^{-2})\): at most one variable has
valuation one, and all others valuation zero. The factor at two is
\(1/16\). The infinite product is positive. For primes above a
fixed cutoff, the excluded square divisors and shared prime divisors
have total upper bound
\(O(N^4\sum_{p>P}p^{-2}+N^{7/2}+N^3\log N)\), where
\(N=\sqrt X\). The first term is made arbitrarily small by choosing
the fixed cutoff, and the other terms are \(o(N^4)\). Finite Chinese
remainder counting then gives the asserted density in the four
fixed-ratio intervals.

For a fixed edge, a fixed \(a,b\mid2\), and fixed \(r,s\le J\),
the excluded relation \(|raD_i-sbD_j|\le\Delta\) leaves at most
\(O(\Delta+1)\) choices for the second variable after the first is
fixed. The two free remaining variables give an overall excluded
count

\[
O\bigl(J^2X^{3/2}(\Delta+1)\bigr)
=O(X^{1.874}L^{12})=o(X^2).
\tag{PO31}
\]

All gcd conditions in (PO11) hold for these base quadruples, since
their base gcds are one. Hence this is a block of absolute mass
\(\asymp X^2\) canceled exactly, quadruple by quadruple, by

\[
1-1-1+1=0.
\tag{PO32}
\]

This cancellation explains the distinction from the positive model
in SP30--SP34, which satisfies certain prefix and divisor-mask bounds
but does not preserve these Möbius convolution identities.

It also gives a sharp obstruction to a stronger claim. Restricting
the *actual* four factors to the fully pairwise-coprime stratum
removes the last row, because \((2D,2E)=2\). The other three rows
remain, and their relative signed coefficient is \(1-1-1=-1\).
Thus this cancellation crosses permitted internal-gcd strata; it
does not prove cancellation on the fully pairwise-coprime stratum
alone. Likewise, a base internal gcd in \([H/2,H)\) can cause the
original cutoff to remove the last allocation. This is the reason
for the exact orbital preparation below.
title: 4. An actual signed block with absolute mass of order X squared

statement:
## 2. Exact coefficient folding and all 2-adic resonances

For odd m, the only nonzero local values are
A(m)=mu(m), A(2m)=-3mu(m), A(4m)=2mu(m). All higher
2-adic valuations give zero, as do odd square factors.
This proves DP8 directly from DP1. Its Dirichlet series
multiplier is 1-2*2^(-s), giving DP9. Replacing N by 2n
in the second part of DP1 proves DP10 before any estimate.

The profile has logarithmic mass one:
integral V_delta(u)du/u=1. Its ordinary mass is M(delta).
Thus the ordinary integral of
V_delta(u)-2V_delta(2u) is exactly zero. There is no
additional inverse-width normalization of the vanishing
moment; the original bump still has amplitude delta^(-1).
The two lobes have the fixed logarithmic separation log 2.

Both entries of a nonzero Gram satisfy N/x,M/x in
[e^(-delta),e^delta]. This proves all support statements
DP14, with the stated absolute product-gap constant for
bounded delta. Expansion of the finite sum proves DP15
and DP16, including their cross coefficients -2,-2,4.

The exact identity at one completed index is

\[
 A(N)^2=\mu(N)^2+
       4\,1_{2\mid N}\mu(N/2)^2
       -4\,1_{2\mid N}\mu(N)\mu(N/2).
 \tag{DPR4}
\]

This explicitly accounts for the resonances N=n=2m and
N=2n=m in the original two-lobe representation. For even
m, mu(2m)mu(m)=0; for odd m it equals -mu(m)^2.
The usual squarefree density is 1/zeta(2), and the odd
squarefree density is 2/(3zeta(2)), each with error
O(sqrt z) by its elementary square-divisor expansion.
The three terms of DPR4 therefore contribute respectively

\[
 \frac{z}{\zeta(2)},\qquad
 \frac{2z}{\zeta(2)},\qquad
 \frac{4z}{3\zeta(2)}
 \quad\text{up to }O(\sqrt z).
 \tag{DPR5}
\]

Their sum is 13z/(3zeta(2)), independently confirming DP18.
Equivalently the local weights 1,9,4 at valuations 0,1,2
give (2/(3zeta(2)))(1+9/2+4/4).
Omitting the exact-ratio cross terms would give the wrong
constant 3/zeta(2). There are no unlisted higher 2-adic
resonances after the exact folding in DPR4.

Put S_A(z)=sum_(N<=z) A(N)^2 and C_A=13/(3zeta(2)).
Tonelli and u=N/x give the diagonal as

\[
 \int_0^\infty V_\delta(u)^2
       \{S_A(2Xu)-S_A(Xu)\}\frac{du}{u}
 =C_A X\int V_\delta(u)^2du
    +O\left(\sqrt X\int V_\delta(u)^2\frac{du}{u}\right).
 \tag{DPR6}
\]

Any endpoint atoms affect a measure-zero set of u. The omitted
factor sqrt(u) in the error is bounded on the fixed compact
support e^(-delta0)<=u<=e^delta0. Finally
integral V_delta^2 du=delta^(-1)integral k(v)^2 e^(delta v)dv
and integral V_delta^2 du/u=delta^(-1)||k||_2^2.
This proves DP19 uniformly even when delta X is small;
partial summation through derivatives of the narrow profile
is unnecessary. The error/main ratio is O(X^(-1/2)),
independent of delta. The diagonal remains a part of a
signed expansion, not a lower bound for its whole energy.

For a=.87449 its power is 1+eta and the strict diagonal
budget is eta<2a-1=.74898. The comparison with a separately
paid normalized first-derivative bump, whose diagonal power
is 1+3eta, is exactly the claimed factor-three interval
of allowed eta. This comparison provides no off-diagonal
cancellation estimate.

statement:
## 4. Uniform moving masks, the mixed term, and long shifts

The following use of Mertens is inherited, not independent new full-field
cancellation. Throughout this report beta is FIXED in (.874872,1),
using the accepted c2 zero-free conclusion and its buffered mu-Mertens
consequence M(t)=O_beta(t^beta). The previously accepted beta=.8749 also
suffices. No boundary-line assertion M(t)=O(t^.874872), no uniform
constant as beta decreases to the boundary, and no c3 input is used.
This dependency is the precise one in [private research revision] S3--S7, with the updated
accepted c2 boundary identified in [private research revision] independent review R0.
Theorem A's positive coprime RR lower bound uses none of this input;
the small FR comparison and resulting negative TR assertion DO use it.

For each positive integer d define

    f_d(n)=product_(p|n, p not dividing 3d)(-1),
    F_d(y)=sum_n f_d(n)g(log(n/y)).

The exact source identity f(dn)=f(d)f_d(n) includes all valuations.
Here are the local factors of h_d such that f_d=h_d*mu, with w=p^-s:

    H_(d,p)(w)=(1-w)^-2,                    p|3d;
    H_(d,p)(w)=(1-2w)/(1-w)^2,              p not |3d.

The second factor is 1-sum_(j>=2)(j-1)w^j. Therefore

    B_d(beta):=sum_a |h_d(a)|a^-beta
       = product_(p|3d)(1-p^-beta)^-2
         product_(p not |3d)[1+p^(-2beta)/(1-p^-beta)^2]
       <=C_beta product_(p|d)(1-p^-beta)^-2
       <=C_(beta,delta)d^delta                         (A16)

for every fixed delta>0. The infinite second product converges at
2beta>1. For the final inequality, each sufficiently large prime factor
is <=p^delta; finitely many small primes contribute a fixed constant.
Prime 3 is always in the first product. Prime 2 uses its displayed
applicable factor; no factor 1-2*2^-s is inverted. Constants depend on
beta,delta, never on d. Convolution and full Abel summation give

    |sum_(n<=t)f_d(n)|<=C_beta B_d t^beta,
    |F_d(y)|<=C_(beta,tau)B_d y^beta,       ALL y>0.   (A17)

For y<1 the cumulative sum is initially zero; both endpoints at zero
and infinity vanish under the Gaussian. The remaining integral is
y^beta integral exp(beta v)|g'(v)|dv. Thus (A17) includes d>X,
without an unpriced small-scale tail or a constant depending on X/d.

For ANY mask A_X(n) with 0<=A_X(n)<=1, allowed to vary arbitrarily with
X, put

    G_(d,A)(y)=sum_n f_d(n)A_X(dn)g(log(n/y)).

The only assertion about this masked field is the positive estimate
|G_(d,A)(y)|<=C_tau y. Inserting coprimality and f(dn)'s exact identity
before bounding either factor proves

    C_1(F,f A_X)
       =sum_(d>=1)mu(d) integral_X^(2X)
                  F_d(x/d)G_(d,A)(x/d)dx/x
       =O_(beta,tau)(X^(1+beta)).                   (A18)

Indeed (A16)--(A17) and the positive bound make the absolute sum at
most C X^(1+beta)sum_d B_d/d^(1+beta)<infinity; choose delta<beta.
Before using cancellation, Fubini already follows from the positive
majorant sum_d [sum_n g(log(dn/x))]^2<=C x^2 sum_d d^-2.
Thus every d, every repeated prime, and the exact moving mask A_X(dn)
are retained. No uniform estimate for a signed submask has been used.
This handles the specific R mask, and is uniform even for masks having
discontinuous moving thresholds. It is a scalar with one full factor,
not a theorem for TWO arbitrarily masked factors.

For comparison, the same exact identity with A_X=1 gives

    C_1(F,F)=sum_d mu(d) integral F_d(x/d)^2dx/x
             =O_(beta,tau)(X^(2beta)),               (A19)

by choosing delta<(2beta-1)/2 in sum_d B_d^2/d^(2beta). This is only
the accepted baseline. Its sole coprime diagonal K_X(1,1) is a
superpower Gaussian tail. Neither (A18) nor (A19) improves full energy.

The identity F=T+R now gives EXACTLY

    C_1(T,R)=C_1(F,R)-C_1(R,R),
    C_1(R,T)=C_1(T,R).                               (A20)

We next remove short shifts by direct positive counting. For every
integer h>=1, the bound sup g<infinity and (A11) give

    sum_a K_Y(a,a+h)<=C_tau Y,        ALL Y>0.

Consequently every bounded-coefficient scalar loses at most
C_tau X H when restricted to |m-n|>H, apart from a diagonal if it
was present. For the RR,TR,RT,FR scalars the coprime diagonal is
identically absent. Removing integers outside I_X costs (A12).
For general H>=1 let C_1^H denote these two simultaneous restrictions.
Then

    C_1^H(R,R)=C_1(R,R)+O(XH+X^-4),
    C_1^H(F,R)=O(X^(1+beta)+XH+X^-4),
    C_1^H(T,R)=-C_1^H(R,R)
                       +O(X^(1+beta)+XH+X^-4).      (A21)

The restriction is applied to the original integer pair, identically
in all identities. Therefore exact reconstruction remains valid after
restriction; no cross interaction is lost. At H=X/L^6, XH=X^2/L^6,
and both errors in the last line are o(X^2/L^4) because beta<1 is
fixed. This proves A4--A5. The eventual negative inequality in A5
means C_1^H(T,R)<=-c_(tau,kappa)X^2/L^4 for some c>0.

There is also a complete four-piece statement at these exact masks:

    C_1^H(F,F)=C_1^H(T,T)+C_1^H(T,R)
                         +C_1^H(R,T)+C_1^H(R,R),
    C_1^H(T,T)=C_1^H(R,R)
                   +O(X^(1+beta)+XH+X^-4).          (A22)

For the second line use (A19), noting its diagonal K_X(1,1) is removed
and negligible, and (A21). Thus the actual large opposite terms, in
this non-PSD coprime scalar, cancel across ALL FOUR pieces. We do not
replace these identities by a leading Gram, take their absolute values
as a surrogate for full energy, or infer a full-energy lower bound.

The literal primitive-shift form of the RR assertion is

    C_1^H(R,R)=2 sum_(h>H)sum_((a,h)=1)
      f_3(a(a+h)) A_R(a)A_R(a+h)
      1_(a in I_X)1_(a+h in I_X) K_X(a,a+h).          (A23)

Here f_1=f_3, and coprimality (a,a+h)=1 makes
f_3(a)f_3(a+h)=f_3(a(a+h)). For TR the corresponding bracket is
A_T(a)A_R(a+h)+A_T(a+h)A_R(a), without an extra factor 2.
Both orders remain. This places the obstruction on the actual g=1
slice of G34, including all h>H, all cores and all four distinct rough
primes. It is not the previously paid small-radical prime-two ray.

                  sum_a h(a) M_eta,2(exp(-5/3)x/Na),
    M_eta,2(x)=C_S^-1 exp(-25/36)
                  sum_a j(a) P_eta(exp(5/3)x/Na).          (2.8)

The real shift, width 2, scalar and original ideal coefficients are all necessary. These are absolutely convergent field identities, first checked on an absolute Mellin line and then by unique inversion. Polynomial coefficient growth follows already from any fixed absolute line, so the Gaussian also supplies direct locally uniform convergence. Composing the two series is justified on that line and by the same positive majorants.

For real-shell norm

    ||F||_[X,2X]=(integral_X^(2X)|F(x)|^2 dx/x)^(1/2),
    ||F||_sigma=sup_(X>0) X^-sigma ||F||_[X,2X],

Minkowski gives the paid estimates

    ||P_eta||_sigma <= C_S exp(25/36-5sigma/3) A_sigma ||M_eta,2||_sigma,
    ||M_eta,2||_sigma <= C_S^-1 exp(-25/36+5sigma/3) B_sigma ||P_eta||_sigma. (2.9)

Every x/Na shell has its own scale. No moving arithmetic cutoff is kept at an incorrect parent scale. Gaussian left tails pay bounded/small shells; at most two adjacent dyadic shells cover a real shell. Thus the complete all-dyad moments for P_eta and M_eta,2 are equivalent at every exponent gamma>2/3, also with the usual every-positive-epsilon quantifier. At gamma=2/3 the every-epsilon version follows by using (2.9) at sigma=gamma+epsilon; no exact-power endpoint norm is asserted.

A bound for M_eta,2 with exponent gamma makes its Mellin integral holomorphic on Re s>gamma by dyadic Cauchy--Schwarz, including derivatives on smaller half-planes. Its Gaussian left tail pays zero. The multiplier never vanishes, so every zero of the same L_K^S in that region is excluded; its possible pole at 1 is allowed. This supplies the complete conditional zero return, independently of an unproved covariance claim. To recover a common boundary for the original entire fixed-family scope, the proposed moment hypothesis must hold for **each** fixed target with the same gamma and every positive epsilon; constants, exclusions and large-X thresholds may depend on the target. A result for one eta alone excludes zeros only for that target.

## G136. Paid coupling repair and complete resonant feedback

The independent protected audit separates ordinary coupling conservation
from the actual divisor map. A coupling with additive marginal a(n) and
multiplicative marginal `(a*chi)(n)=delta_(n=1)` would have total masses
M(N) and1, so ordinarily cannot exist. A repair must carry M(N)-1.

For feasible equal-mass marginals r,c and allowed finite edges E, the
minimum full total variation is exactly

    inf_(BZ=(r,c)) sum_E|Z_ij|
      =sup_(|u_i+v_j|<=1) Re[sum conj(u_i)r_i+sum conj(v_j)c_j].

This is finite-dimensional quotient-norm duality: the compact image of
the unit ball has a supporting functional giving the constraint above.
For real coefficients it is a linear program; for complex character
coefficients it is a modulus/SOCP problem. Singleton additive cells force
full TV `sum|a(n)|=kappa_q N+O_q(sqrt N)`. This is not a bound on every
possible defect. Two equal arrays have zero difference at any common M,
so a small marginal-preserving difference alone supplies no cancellation.

The literal repair instead uses triangular divisor matrices

    C_(n,d)=chi(n/d)1_(d|n),
    A_(n,d)=mu(n/d)chi(n/d)1_(d|n), AC=CA=I.

For a candidate vector v and `e=Cv-e_1`, exact inversion gives `v-a=Ae`.
Grouping n=kd, for every integer interval (L,U] one obtains

    sum_(L<n<=U)v_n-[M(U)-M(L)]
      =sum_(k<=U)e_k[M(floor(U/k))-M(floor(L/k))].        (4)

Thus small candidate readout AND a bound on the entire signed response
return the desired M bound. Unrestricted weighted error TV has scalar
operator norm `max_k |M(floor(N/k))|/w_k`, attained by a single aligned
error; k=1 already contains M(N). Actual compatible defects can evade
that ambient worst case only through a proved restriction. This is a
source-exact application of the existing inverse/adjoint principle.

The independent uniform audit preserves the original native H tensor,
both projectors, masks, signed short core, CRT phase, angular factors
and1/Q normalization from [[restricted research revision]](../[private research revision]/h-joint-integration.md) and
[G89](../[private research revision]/wild48-integration.md). Splitting its source into a unit
mode v and its orthogonal complement retains BOTH scalar readout and
innovation. A small innovation cannot discard the scalar.

If an exact compatible scale map is actually constructed with block
coefficients a_j,b_j,c_j,D_j, then

    alpha_(j+1)=a_j alpha_j+b_j eta_j,
    eta_(j+1)=c_j alpha_j+D_j eta_j,
    alpha_(j+1)=a_j alpha_j+b_j D_(j-1)...D_0 eta_0
       +sum_(k<j)b_j D_(j-1)...D_(k+1)c_k alpha_k.        (5)

Every empty product is the identity; actual forcing needs its complete
Duhamel terms. For the diagnostic `T=[[1,e],[e,0]]`, D=0 while
`alpha_(j+1)=alpha_j+e^2 alpha_(j-1)` has a root above1. Changing the
feedback sign changes the conclusion. This is a scoped objection to
innovation-only reasoning, not a native arithmetic lower bound. The
actual scale map, conditioning and complete signed feedback remain OPEN.

# Candidate: the actual f3 complement in a square-root threshold window

Controller candidate for independent review, 11 October2026. This is a
distinct continuation of the fixed-power rho<1/2 calculation. No admission
or new zero-free constant is claimed. Sources are the exact f3 coefficient,
Gaussian lattice/tail estimates and fixed-order PNT already used in
[restricted mathematical source] the proposed proof below uses no
Mertens cancellation or complete-field bound.

Fix tau>0, g(u)=(2pi tau)^(-1/2)exp(-u²/(2tau)), and
f(n)=mu(rad(n/3^v3(n))). Let omega_z count DISTINCT primes greater than z,
retaining all valuations. For X<=x<=2X, define the original full complement

    R_z(x)=sum_(omega_z(n)>=2) f(n)g(log(n/x)),
    T_z(x)=sum_(omega_z(n)<=1) f(n)g(log(n/x)).

Set L=logX and fix kappa>=1. The threshold here is z=kappa sqrt(X),
not X^rho with fixed rho<1/2. Define the absolutely convergent functions

    J_tau(v)=integral_v^infinity e^u(u-v)g(u)du,
    Phi_tau(q)=sum_(r>=1) f(r)/r * J_tau(log(rq)), q>0.

Proposed complete asymptotic, uniformly on the closed x shell:

    R_(kappa sqrt(X))(x)
      = 2x/L² * Phi_tau(kappa² X/x) + O_(tau,kappa)(X/L³).       (CT1)

For kappa²>=2exp(3tau),

    Phi_tau(kappa² X/x) >= (3/4)J_tau(log(kappa² X/x))>0.        (CT2)

Consequently R is positive and has size comparable to X/L² on the full
shell, with fixed tau,kappa constants. This is different from the negative
X/L³ complement for any fixed1/3<rho<1/2. That earlier asymptotic is not
uniform as rho tends to1/2 on the scale1/logX.

## Exact source and every omitted coefficient

Fix delta=1/100. Terms with |log(n/x)|>=delta L/2 have absolute Gaussian
tail O_A(X^-A), for every fixed A, after increasing X. The same holds with
any fixed divisor multiplicity: d3(n)<=C_epsilon n^epsilon and the Gaussian
lattice bound at a slightly wider variance pay the complete tail. Constants
depend on the requested fixed A,delta,tau. This is an actual bound, not a
finite truncation of the source definition.

In the retained central range, n<=2X^(1+delta/2)<z³ eventually. Every n
having two distinct prime divisors above z therefore has exactly two such
primes, each with valuation one. It has a unique form n=rpq with z<p<q.
Moreover r<=2X^(delta/2)/kappa²<z, so neither rough prime divides r and
f(rpq)=f(r). The omitted three-prime and repeated-rough-power cases all
lie in the paid Gaussian tail. This proves, after paying that tail,

    R_z(x)=sum_(r<=X^delta) f(r)
                 sum_(z<p<q) g(log(rpq/x)) + O_A(X^-A),       (CT3)

where the extended terms outside the central range have at most d3(n)
representations and are included in the same tail estimate. Every omitted
r>X^delta forces n>kappa²X^(1+delta), so its entire completion also has
the same divisor-weighted Gaussian bound. These statements apply to the
completed prime sum as well as the original coefficient field.

Replace p<q by half the ordered p,q sum, subtracting the actual p=q
diagonal. Its absolute size is O_tau(X^(1/2+delta/2)): ignoring primality
and the lower cutoff, the Gaussian lattice estimate after the substitution
u=2log(p/sqrt(x/r)) gives sum_p g(log(rp²/x))<=C_tau sqrt(x/r).
Summing r<=X^delta proves this bound. It is o(X/L³). No coefficient for
p² is falsely identified with the two-distinct-prime source.

## Two ordinary PNT substitutions with sharp endpoints

Restrict p,q to [z,B_X], B_X=X^(1/2+2delta); the portions excluded from
the central product range again have the full Gaussian/divisor tail.
Use the accepted fixed-order PNT pi(v)=li(v)+O_N(v/log^N v), with N=10
fixed before X. Throughout this rectangle logp,logq are comparable to L.

For fixed r,q, Stieltjes integration by parts replaces the p sum by
integral dp/logp with error bounded by

    C_tau,N * x/(r q L^N).                                    (CT4)

To verify CT4, the error measure's primitive is O(p/L^N). Multiplying
the weight derivative and integrating gives
integral p|d[g(log(rpq/x))]| <= C_tau x/(rq), since
integral e^u|g'(u)|du is finite. Endpoint terms obey the same bound from
sup_u e^u g(u)<infinity. A sharp central cutoff, if retained during this
step, has two atoms bounded identically. A prime exactly at z is excluded
according to p>z; its endpoint atom is included in this estimate.

Summing CT4 over the actual q primes and r<=X^delta uses only the integer
harmonic majorants sum_(q<=B_X)1/q=O(L), sum_(r<=X^delta)1/r=O(L).
The first total error is O(X/L^(N-2)). For the second PNT replacement,
apply the same integration-by-parts estimate inside the existing positive
p integral; bound dp/logp by dp and integrate1/p over the finite
rectangle. This again gives O(X/L^(N-2)). Coefficient signs are preserved
in the main term; absolute values are used only for these error bounds.

The resulting integral has factor1/2 from unordered primes. Extend its
limits to p,q>z and its core to all r>=1. The positive integrals with
divisor multiplicity and log denominators bounded by a constant have
Gaussian tails of the same arbitrary negative-power size. Thus

    R_z(x)=(1/2)sum_r f(r)
       integral_(p,q>z) g(log(rpq/x)) dp dq/(logp logq)
       + O_tau,kappa(X/L^4),                                 (CT5)

where the displayed error also absorbs the square-prime diagonal and
all Gaussian tails. No signed Mertens assertion was used to complete r.

## Density expansion and the full critical-window profile

Write s=x/X in[1,2], p=sqrt(X)v and q=sqrt(X)w. Since kappa>=1,
v,w>=kappa and logv,logw>=0. For a=L/2 and b,c>=0,

    |1/((a+b)(a+c)) - 1/a²| <= (b+c)/a³.

The density is therefore4/L²+O((logv+logw)/L³). Its absolute integrated
error is O(X/L³), because

    sum_r integral_(v,w>=kappa)
       (1+logv+logw)g(log(rvw/s)) dv dw

is bounded uniformly in s in[1,2]. For an explicit convergence argument,
set y=vw; the inner integral becomes
integral_(kappa²)^infinity (1+logy)log(y/kappa²)g(log(ry/s))dy.
Put u=log(ry/s). Its lower limit is log(rkappa²/s); the Gaussian then
bounds this by C_(tau,kappa,B) r^(-B) for every fixed B, uniformly in s.
This prices the complete core and all logarithmic density moments by
absolute convergence, rather than by an invalid unsigned reciprocal
moment completion.

The leading double integral, without the extra logarithmic weight, is

    integral_(v,w>=kappa) g(log(rvw/s))dv dw
      = integral_(kappa²)^infinity log(y/kappa²)g(log(ry/s))dy
      = (s/r) J_tau(log(rkappa²/s)).                            (CT6)

Combining factor1/2, Jacobian X and density4/L² gives exactly CT1.
All constants are uniform for x in[X,2X]. No uniformity in moving kappa
or in tau is asserted.

## A rigorous positive part of the critical-window profile

Completing the Gaussian square gives

    J_tau(v)=exp(tau/2) integral_0^infinity
                   t g_tau(t+v-tau)dt.

If v>=3tau and h>=0, its pointwise integrand comparison gives

    J_tau(v+h)/J_tau(v)
       <= exp(-(v-tau)h/tau-h²/(2tau)) <= exp(-2h).              (CT7)

For q>=exp(3tau), the r=1 term is J_tau(logq)>0 and the absolute total
of all r>=2 terms is at most

    J_tau(logq) sum_(r>=2) r^-3 <= (1/4)J_tau(logq),

using1/8+integral_2^infinity t^-3 dt=1/4. Since f(1)=1 and |f(r)|=1,
CT2 follows. On the compact q interval[kappa²/2,kappa²], this lower
bound is a fixed positive constant. Thus CT1 is eventually positive
uniformly over the entire shell, even if its constant is small.

## Exact band consequences and limitations

For any fixed rho_plus>1/2, every coefficient of R_(X^rho_plus) has
n>X^(2rho_plus), so its full Gaussian field is O_A(X^-A) for every fixed A.
For fixed admissible kappa, X^rho_plus>kappa sqrt(X) eventually. Exact
coefficient subtraction, without using F or any full-field bound, gives

    T_(X^rho_plus)-T_(kappa sqrt(X))
      =R_(kappa sqrt(X))-R_(X^rho_plus)
      =2x/L² Phi_tau(kappa²X/x)+O(X/L³)>0.                      (CT8)

This is a complete actual positive band of order X/L² derived using only
ordinary PNT and absolutely convergent core estimates. It is not a
pointwise-prime-jump sign assertion. It also differs from the negative
fixed-power-late-to-terminal band, which crosses this critical range.

Only if one separately uses the accepted full-field bound F=O(X^beta),
beta<1, does T_(kappa sqrt(X))=F-R acquire a negative leading term from
CT1. That prefix conclusion uses the accepted baseline; CT1 and CT8 do
not. Neither conclusion improves the full-field exponent or c. No
arbitrary mask, low-gcd subfamily, Hecke twist, or inherited convolution
transfer is claimed. The uncapped Gaussian and every prime power remain
in the source through the paid tails above.

STOP candidate writing after full readback and hash. Independent reviewer
must particularly challenge CT3 tail multiplicity, the second Stieltjes
substitution, complete integral extension and the claimed uniform shell
error before accepting CT1/CT8.

## 1. Character-preserving Hodge rank and displacement: accept at stated scope

For a fixed modulus q, take the vector space on squarefree q-units n<=X, with parity Gamma(n)=mu(n) and diagonal character action W_chi(n)=chi(n). Then Str(W_chi)=M_chi(X), with n=1 present, squareful zeros removed exactly and ramified zeros retained by the q-unit restriction. Requiring an odd differential d with d^2=0 to commute with **every** character modulo q forces its matrix into residue blocks. Character separation on the reduced residue group proves this; a condition for only one character would be weaker and would not give the same blocks.

Write E_a and O_a for positive and negative counts in residue a, and I_a=E_a-O_a. Finite Hodge decomposition into im(d), im(d*) and ker(Delta) cancels equal positive/negative paired dimensions. Consequently

    dim ker(Delta) >= R_q(X) := sum_a |I_a(X)|.

Matching min(E_a,O_a) opposite signs within each residue attains equality. Choosing unit arrows makes each matched Laplacian block the identity, so its nonzero spectral gap is exactly one. A gap without a bound on R_q has no force. The exact finite comparison q=5,X=80 gives I=(0,-3,-4,1), hence minimum rank eight. A fourteen-state rank from a particular differential is not a universal minimum.

Character orthogonality gives

    max_chi |M_chi(X)| <= R_q(X) <= sum_chi |M_chi(X)|
                                      <= phi(q) max_chi |M_chi(X)|.

This is already part of **[private research revision] G135's character/residue/rank-matching equivalence**. The author's late correction credits it correctly. Do not credit a new weaker arithmetic target just because the target has been written as a harmonic rank.

For a fixed neutral prime r, the explicit pairing m<->rm with r not dividing m gives an exact construction. To preserve all characters at once take r=1 mod q; for a single character chi(r)=1 suffices. If chi(r) is not one, the residual multiplier 1-chi(r) is present and may not be dropped. The boundary consists of the appropriate r-free squarefree bases in (X/r,X]. With

    d_q = (1/zeta(2)) product_(p|q) p/(p+1),
    sum_(n<=x,(n,q)=1) mu(n)^2 = d_q x + O_q(sqrt(x)),

obtained from the square-divisor expansion, its harmonic rank is

    d_q (r-1)/(r+1) X + O_(q,r)(sqrt(X)).

This is a linear rank failure for the named construction, not a lower bound for every changed differential. The complex-character signs in the exact finite check and the natural zeros survive.

The global pairing repair is also valid. In each reduced residue class there are infinitely many negative squarefree integers (primes), and infinitely many positive ones (a fixed prime r=1 mod q times different primes in that class). The external input needed for this existence argument is the infinitude of primes in each reduced progression, verified in [NIST DLMF 27.11.9](https://dlmf.nist.gov/27.11.E9). No prime-counting error term is being imported. Increasing-rank pairing is one definite choice; mere existence gives no displacement estimate.

For one fixed global same-residue pairing of all positive and negative q-unit squarefree integers, orient (u,v) by mu(u)=1,mu(v)=-1, and set a=min(u,v),b=max(u,v). Define the **complete** minimum-shell cost

    D_q(X) = sum_(X<=a<2X) (b-a),       X=1,2,4,... .

Every future partner enters, even if b is far larger than 2X. The sum in one shell is finite. If for a common 0<gamma<1 and every epsilon>0,

    D_q(X) <<_(q,epsilon) X^(1+gamma+epsilon)

for all sufficiently large dyadic X and every fixed q, then all ordinary L(s,chi) have no zeros in Re(s)>gamma. Initially Re(s)>1 permits complete absolute regrouping:

    1/L(s,chi) = sum_pairs chi(u)(u^(-s)-v^(-s)).

For sigma=Re(s)>0, the fundamental theorem of calculus yields

    |u^(-s)-v^(-s)| <= |s| (b-a) a^(-sigma-1).

On a compact subset of Re(s)>gamma choose epsilon below its horizontal margin. The dyadic bound is summable uniformly, so the paired series is holomorphic and equals the reciprocal on the initial overlap. The identity L F=1 continues meromorphically. It forbids an L zero and allows a zero of F at the principal pole. All fixed finite heights are covered, without any asserted height-uniform reciprocal growth. Imprimitive L and its finite factors remain the original function. This is a complete conditional return.

For monotone pairing, the number of crossing intervals at a cut is exactly R_q(t), and Tonelli gives total clipped interval length in [A,B] equal to integral_A^B R_q(t)dt. That clipped integral is **not** D_q(A): future portions and intervals entering from earlier shells must be priced. The author's distinction is correct. Under the already known G135 summatory/rank bounds with gamma>1/2, positive and negative endpoint counts give endpoints comparable to k and pair displacement O(k^(gamma+epsilon)); thus the complete D bound follows. The new representation has not bypassed that arithmetic difficulty.

The simplest global neutral-prime pairing has an actual source obstruction:

    D_q(X) = (r-1) sum_(X<=m<2X,(m,qr)=1) mu(m)^2 m
           = (3/2)(r-1)d_(qr) X^2 + O_(q,r)(X^(3/2)).

Partial summation of the same squarefree count proves it; half-open endpoint changes O(X) fit the error. Its positive main coefficient rules out gamma<1 for this rule's positive-cost certificate. It does not rule out other same-residue pairings, signed displacement estimates, or the Möbius target itself. Retain this useful actual-source failure and the explicit complete future-partner Mellin bill. Credit the broader matching mechanism to G135/W55, W01 signed transport and [private research revision] priced coupling.

    i(d)=floor((log d-L/2)/H),
    I_i={d in N:Y<d<=Dmax, i(d)=i},
    J_X=floor((log B_X-L)/H).                            (G11)

Left bin edges are included and right edges excluded; Dmax is the
stated real cap. If i+j<-2 then de<X exp(-H), so G9 pays that entire
discarded source. If i+j>J_X, or d>Dmax or e>Dmax, then de>B_X;
G10 pays it. Therefore

    R_rect(x)=sum_(i+j=-2,...,J_X)
                 sum_(d in I_i,e in I_j)mu(d)mu(e)S_tau(x/(de))
    ||G_tau-R_rect||_(L2([X,2X],dx/x))
       <= X^(q_0+o(1)),
    q_0=max(1-kappa^2/(2tau),1-C^2/(2tau)).               (G12)

This argument bounds the actual discarded original labels. It does not
replace a coupled mask by independent rectangles without paying the
difference. Each retained bin factor is an ordinary Möbius interval;
there is no smooth-part state filter.

Take **C=kappa**. Then J_X=1 for all sufficiently large X. Precisely
the four permitted sums **i+j=-2,-1,0,1** remain, with at most
(.01/kappa)sqrt L+O_kappa(1) nonempty bins and O(sqrt L) ordered
components. This has different asymptotic count from SP's loglog X
times a very large fixed state count; it is not claimed to be uniformly
smaller in cardinality. Its arithmetic factors are simpler.

de*ell>B_X at another paid cost. In the resulting finite coefficients

                     i+j in {-2,-1,0,1})mu(d)mu(e)b(ell),
                  1<=n<=B_X,                            (G13)

one has |c_rect,X(n)|<=d_3(n) and

### A1. Source and finite arithmetic calculation

Freeze one original same-scale long-prime pair pi,pi' of distinct degree-one rational norms p,r. The actual field is Eisenstein, with the original primary, ray, unit, bad-place and angular conventions. Source: [restricted research revision] h-joint/report.md Section2, JN4-JN9 interface; its hash is in exact-receipt.json. The exact finite group is

    G=(O/(pi*pi')) x (O/pi) x (O/pi'), |G|=(pr)^2.

Its unitary Fourier normalization is1/(pr). The complete signed short sum, both mark projectors, all sharp supports, profiles and independent heights are folded into W before any norm. The kernel is

    K(h,s,s')=b0 chi_pi(h)^3 chi_pi'(h)^3
                    chi_pi(s)^2 chi_pi'(s')^4.                  (A1)

Here b0 retains b(pi)conj(b(pi')) and the exact fixed CRT phase. It is never set to1 in a native estimate. If b0=0 the following multiplier is zero; otherwise all singular values below are multiplied by|b0|. The factors vanish at their original nonunits. In the two degree-one fields, the cube of either primitive sextic character is the quadratic character. Thus the row factor is exactly

    m(h)=ell_p(h_p)ell_r(h_r), ell_p(0)=ell_r(0)=0,
    Q=pr, phi=(p-1)(r-1).

No ordinary Mobius coefficient is substituted into this H source.

Let S_t f(h)=f(h+t), with t nonzero modulo both primes, and M_m be diagonal multiplication by m on the complete row space. Then

    D_t=M_m S_t-S_t M_m
       =diag(m(h)-m(h+t)) S_t.                               (A2)

This is a specified row-FREQUENCY translation test, not an assertion about the displacement rank of the folded physical mark matrix.

For any odd prime p and a!=0,

    sum_x ell_p(x)ell_p(x+a)=-1.                              (A3)

Proof without an imported character-sum estimate: scaling reduces to a=1. Count z^2=y(y+1). The change to u=2y+1-2z, v=2y+1+2z is a bijection with uv=1, which has p-1 solutions. The same count is p+sum_y ell_p(y(y+1)). This proves(A3), including the zero sites.

CRT therefore gives sum_h m(h)m(h+t)=1. Both entries are nonzero at B=(p-2)(r-2) sites. Both are zero at exactly two sites; exactly one is zero at2(p+r-3) sites. The numbers with opposite and equal nonzero signs are(B-1)/2 and(B+1)/2. Consequently D_t has singular spectrum

    2, multiplicity n2=(Q-2p-2r+3)/2;
    1, multiplicity n1=2(p+r-3);
    0, on every remaining coordinate.                       (A4)

In particular

    rank D_t=(Q+2p+2r-9)/2,
    ||D_t||_HS^2=2(Q-p-r)=2(phi-1), ||D_t||=2.                (A5)

The admissible primes have p,r>=7, so the displayed norm2 occurs. For a shift nonzero only at p, the multiplicities are n2=(p-1)(r-1)/2 and n1=2(r-1), with correlation -(r-1); the symmetric case is analogous. These one-prime shifts also have a bulk defect.

On the full group G, the commutator of M_K with a row-only shift has(A4) replicated exactly phi times, since there are phi nonzero mark pairs and every nonzero mark factor has modulus1. All other mark coordinates contribute zero. Thus

    rank = phi(n1+n2),
    HS squared =2|b0|^2 phi(phi-1).                           (A6)

Fourier conjugation with the native1/Q normalization preserves these quantities; there is no extra1/Q factor to claim afterward. For p=7,r=13, the row rank is61 and row HS squared142. After factoring out|b0|, the full-carrier singular multiplicities are2448 at1 and1944 at2, with3889 zeros. This is an exact finite coefficient evaluation, not an evaluated full H packet.

# Partial [private research revision] source development: the complementary cofactor after row Poisson



## 1. Stop, useful result and limits

The assigned deadline was 2026-10-12T13:15:00Z. The last two recorded host clock outputs were 12:29:18.4224139Z and 14:32:51.5312727Z; the latter established that the deadline had passed. Development stopped when that result was read. This record does not infer a cause for the elapsed time or silently extend the deadline. Only preservation, full readback, hashing and exact claim release follow.

Two elementary identities survive this incomplete lane. The complete Mobius coefficient has an exact complementary-divisor presentation with a short cofactor when the product is close to the truncation. On squarefree columns, the first row Poisson transform moves its Mobius weight onto that cofactor through the literal PR9 Gauss identity. This identifies an actual restricted coefficient family that may be estimated using the old inverse input; it does not establish that estimate. It also shows exactly why the canonical Gauss-column theorem cannot simply be applied to the complete transformed coefficient.

No complete signed bound for R22, no fully certified paid prefix, no two-variable Poisson saving, and no larger c are claimed. In particular, the exploratory rational endpoint values below are not a whole-interval certificate or proof of the proposed source estimate. The useful surviving task is to prove and license the short-product prefix estimate, while retaining the full far-product norm and its cross terms. The original entire residual remains the accepted open input until that is done.

## 2. Exact inherited source and residual

The entire frozen [restricted research revision] review was read: `[restricted provenance path] research revision]-drafts/completed-crossclass-review/report.md`, 31738 bytes, SHA256 `7ba3b2182c1feba3d1cc999983bcd445ac79df1b800e6078d52022d3dc24bc6f`. Its independent weighted-gcd argument R12--R14 pays unequal roots and unequal column scales; it cannot be replaced by a same-dyad count. Its R22 is the present target.

Fix one natural finite source dictionary, one whole orientation and the original finite prime-slot list. Ideal columns use primary generators; element rows retain units. All residue symbols retain their natural zeros, including at exponents zero and six. Let

    R=U^t, t=4/3, Y=U^B,
    A_R(n)=sum_(d|n) mu(d)V(Nd/R),
    V(x)=1 for 0<=x<=1, V(x)=0 for x>=2.

The actual completed detector is

    D_R,u(s)=sum_(Nn>R) A_R(n)nu(n)psi_u(n)
                         (Nn)^(-s)exp(-Nn/Y).

Its fixed natural nonprincipal zero signal, genuine terminal tail and height restrictions are precisely the retained [restricted research revision]/[restricted research revision] contracts. They are not re-proved here. Original slots are

    Q_u=U^(-v/2) sum_P alpha(P)psi_u(P), 0<=v<=1/20,

with one prime from each original disjoint pool, all actual ray/profile factors and independent heights. Merge equal l=nP, including signs, before projecting to sixth-free ideal cores l=c a^6. The actual coefficient b_l includes the whole divisor sum A_R(n), every scalar and every zero.

The inherited full positive smooth norm is chosen before pair expansion. After its genuine terminal tail is paid, its residual consists of real ordered cross-class terms with

    Nc,Nc'>U^(6/5), Q>U^(6/5), Q1/Q3>U^(1/2).       (S1)

Here q1,q2,q3 are the relative valuation radicals for residues +/-1, +/-2 and3 modulo6; Q_i=Nq_i and Q=Q1Q2Q3. All original derivative inner products remain in the residual. An arbitrary zero-bin indicator is not a permissible Poisson weight. A pairwise signed projection is not dominated by a positive norm merely by removing terms.

The accepted current comparison is

    h=5-2delta, rho=1-10delta/(3h), k=rho+delta-1,
    D_K=15K-10-6Kdelta,
    a_K=delta(5-6delta)^2/(3h D_K),
    b_K=2delta(5-6delta)(K-1)/D_K,
    E_K=rho+delta v-min(3kv,a_K+b_K v),               (S2)

for delta in[17/25,7/10]. K is fixed from the accepted preceding-family input; there is no c11 feedback recalibration.

## 3. An exact complementary-divisor identity

For every nonunit ideal n, the full ideal Mobius convolution is zero. Subtract it from the cutoff convolution to obtain

    A_R(n)=-sum_(d|n) mu(d)[1-V(Nd/R)]
          =-sum_(m|n) mu(n/m)[1-V(Nn/(Nm R))].       (S3)

This identity is valid for arbitrary valuations, not only squarefree n. Its nonzero summands have Nd>R, or equivalently Nm<Nn/R. Equality Nd=R contributes zero. If a common bounded smooth cutoff restricts Nn to at most C L, the cofactor is therefore shorter than C L/R. This is an actual support statement, with the endpoint constant retained. It is not obtained by taking absolute values of separate original inverse dyads.

Multiplying S3 by the actual multiplicative character gives

    phi_u(n)A_R(n)
      =-sum_(dm=n) mu(d)phi_u(d)phi_u(m)[1-V(Nd/R)]. (S4)

This holds with zero extensions even when d and m share primes. A frozen hole dividing n forces a zero on at least one factor; it must not be dropped. No coprimality between d and m is imposed. The original slots may meet either factor; their natural zeros remain those of the complete product. No slot pool has changed.

For a smooth prefix cutoff H(Nn/L) and the genuine exponential weight, S4 gives the exact finite expression

    D_prefix,u(s)
      =-sum_m phi_u(m)(Nm)^(-s)
          sum_d mu(d)phi_u(d)(Nd)^(-s)[1-V(Nd/R)]
              H(Nd Nm/L)exp(-Nd Nm/Y).               (S5)

Only Nm<C L/R contributes. The original product cutoff and terminal cutoff are retained inside the coupled smooth profile. Thus the moving m changes an evaluation point of that profile; it is not a license to insert arbitrary coefficients into the inverse moment. A legitimate later proof must separate the coupled profile on its fixed ambient box before choosing a live row or m, using PR9 B3.3. The outside scalar phi_u(m) is a contraction, including at nonunits.

This representation uses a long inverse factor d>R and a short unweighted cofactor m. It is a new presentation of the existing coefficient, not an additional zero detector. It needs no positivity or presumed independence of the two witnesses. It remains valid at the target unit and under whole conjugation.

As a limited exact observation, if every proper divisor of n has norm at most R, then

    A_R(n)=mu(n)[V(Nn/R)-1].                         (S6)

Indeed every proper divisor has cutoff value one, and their Mobius sum is -mu(n). This includes appropriate first product annuli determined by the least allowed prime norm. This record does not assume an unverified numerical value for that least norm, nor a uniformly populated prime annulus. Positive prime-pair terms at the unit are therefore not evidence against possible cancellation by the entire first-annulus inverse coefficient.

## 4. What the first row Poisson actually does

This section concerns the concrete no-slot, coprime squarefree pair l,l' in S1. It records the exact coefficient change, rather than claiming an estimate for every pair of the full source.

Write a0(n)=conjugate(alpha(n))*gamma_2(n) as in PR9 B3.1. On good squarefree n, finite Parseval and PR9 B1.10 imply

    gamma_1(n)=mu(n)G(n)*conjugate(a0(n)).            (S7)

The source's G is the fixed ray function, distinct from the two-variable Gauss sum. To check S7, use gamma_1(n)gamma_2(n)=mu(n)alpha(n)G(n), and |gamma_2(n)|=1. Thus the transformed complete column contains

    A_R(n)gamma_1(n)
      =G(n)conjugate(a0(n))*mu(n)A_R(n).             (S8)

Since n is squarefree, mu(n)mu(d)=mu(n/d) for d|n, so

    mu(n)A_R(n)=sum_(m|n) mu(m)V(Nn/(Nm R))
              =-sum_(m|n) mu(m)[1-V(Nn/(Nm R))].    (S9)

The last identity uses n!=1. The cofactor m in its final expression satisfies Nm<Nn/R. Equations S8--S9 move the signed Mobius weight from the original inverse divisor to this complementary cofactor. They preserve the entire signed divisor sum. Applying them independently on both sides of the ordered square retains both cofactors; neither was averaged away.

For orientation, the literal clean row kernel before this coefficient substitution is obtained from PR9 B3.5/B3.52. With q=ll', a compact radial Phi and all six element units, the unrestricted sixth-free row kernel is

    U/sqrt(Nl Nl') * sum_b mu(b)/(Nb)^6 1_((b,ll')=1)
       * R(l,l') sum_h Gcal(l,h) conjugate(Gcal(l',-h))
                      F Phi(U Nh/((Nb)^6 Nl Nl')).  (S10)

The b sum is the exact sixth-free projector: retain its finite original range Nb<=(C_Phi U)^(1/6). Nonprincipal zero frequency vanishes. For squarefree l, Gcal(l,h)=gamma_1(l)*conjugate(chi_l(h)); in particular all frequencies sharing a conductor prime are zero. The -h and R(l,l') in S10 are retained; they cannot be replaced by unsigned absolute Gauss factors. Formula S10 is stated for the clean pair with no additional row ray restriction. Fixed ray restrictions require their complete finite expansion, including their b^6 phase. Natural fixed holes require the full d|rad(E) projector and its scale U/((Nb)^6 Nd). Removing the eligible finite fixed-inducing free rows means subtracting their actual finite kernel sum. These operations are exactly the retained [restricted research revision] contract; they are not implicit deletions from S10.

The prefactor is U/sqrt(Nl Nl'), not U/(Nl Nl'). It is the residue-class Poisson factor U/(Nl Nl') multiplied by the two unnormalized Gauss factors. Thus, for Nl,Nl' comparable to L, the dual scale is L^2/U. In the present first high-conductor range L=U^(4/3), that scale is U^(5/3). Merely retaining a high relative conductor therefore does not shorten the first frequency below the column scale.

S10 is an exact transform for this pair class. Its application to the full residual still requires the complete common-support allocation, all valuations, both physical coprimality projectors where relevant, slots, unequal roots/dyads and every outside scalar. That complete transformation was not finished before the stop.

## 5. A precise obstruction to the proposed shortcut

The canonical energy PR9 B3.6 permits a0(n) times the fixed ray character, common puncture and original product marks. It explicitly permits no further arithmetic coefficient on n. The factor mu(n)A_R(n) in S8 is an additional coefficient. It is neither a harmless unit-modulus phase nor an original prime mark. In S9 it is a signed sum over cofactors with an n-dependent norm threshold. The fact that it is divisor bounded does not satisfy B3.6.

Freezing the complementary m can produce a legitimate route for a short product prefix, provided every resulting common puncture, fourth-power label from B1.11, profile measure and m count is paid. It cannot justify direct application to the unsplit full coefficient. Similarly, after the first row Poisson, Gcal(dm,h) as a function of the remaining m has moving modulus dm; it is not a fixed-modulus ordinary character to which B3.5 can simply be applied again in m. A second transform needs the full finite correlation/reconstruction calculation, not a formal interchange of two ordinary character Poisson formulas.

This is an interface obstruction, not a theorem that no stronger transformation exists. The source's B1.14--18 correlation and B3.52--70 machinery may supply such a calculation after the actual coefficient family is reconstructed. This lane did not finish that reconstruction. Nothing here proves a lower bound for the signed norm, or infers oscillation from high conductor alone.

At a target unit the sextic phases on coprime columns agree. S3--S9 continue to hold there; they show that retaining the merged signs is essential, not that the total is positive. A target unit cannot be removed from an OPEN-H norm. The fixed finite exclusions permitted for density do not transfer to a direct target theorem.

## 6. Unverified short-prefix estimate: retained working calculation

The following is a concrete next calculation, not a theorem of this packet. It was not completed or independently checked on the whole required parameter rectangle before the deadline observation.

Let L=U^(t+lambda), and take the prefix in S5. Formally applying the retained free-row unmarked inverse envelope to the inner long divisor, after a valid common-profile separation, suggests

    exponent J_prefix=1/6+(5/6-delta)t+(1-delta)lambda. (S11)

The reason for the last term is worth retaining. For a cofactor dyad Nm~U^y with 0<=y<=lambda+o(1), the inverse length lies between t and t+lambda-y. The inverse squared norm has exponent 1/6+(5/6-delta)(t+lambda-y). The Hilbert triangle over m contributes (1-delta)y, leaving its largest combined value at y=lambda. This gives S11. Logarithmic dyads, derivatives and endpoint constants must still be assigned their losses. This uses the old free inverse amplification, not an unproved cancellation between m values.

Keeping actual prime slots inside that norm instead suggests the additional marked cost5v/3 in the r>=t range. That price is much larger than the desired gain at ordinary physical slot widths. It does not close the requested whole weighted norm. Alternatively, on an actual high-bin subset where the original pointwise slot price is |Q_u|^2<=H_J U^(delta v+epsilon), one could first bound the positive exceptional set |D_prefix,u(rho_u)|>=1/4 by the unmarked prefix norm and only then use that pointwise price. This would add delta v to S11. It is a different density argument; it is not permission to place a high-bin indicator into S10 or to assert a bound for the clean R22 norm.

For this latter proposed route, the tentative available gap at lambda=0 is

    rho-[1/6+(5/6-delta)*4/3]-min(3kv,a_K+b_K v).    (S12)

A small exploratory standard-library Fraction calculation, whose input used the displayed exact K and formulas, produced these endpoint decimal renderings:

| delta | v | S12 |
|---|---|---|
| .68 | 0 | .006178266178266179 |
| .68 | .03 | .0014744733932108979 |
| .68 | .04 | .0003556311697146849 |
| .68 | .05 | -.000763211053781528 |
| .70 | 0 | .007407407407407408 |
| .70 | .03 | .0032856302141035386 |
| .70 | .04 | .0022700967107301775 |
| .70 | .05 | .0012545632073568162 |

These values reject the naive claim that this displayed sufficient ledger is strictly favorable over all v<=.05. They do not prove a full prefix estimate even for v<=.04. No whole-interval polynomial certificate, fixed buffer distribution, scalar supremum recovery or complete source uniformity audit was finished. The optional prefix widths discussed during development were not adopted as established parameters. No exact numerical receipt is invented after the fact.

This calculation is useful because it isolates a specific actual coefficient source and makes its failure at the largest slot width visible. The strongest required next proof is the source-legal version of S11, including the fixed-profile inverse scale supremum and independent heights, followed by a whole-interval certificate at any proposed range. It must explicitly separate the clean weighted norm route from the high-bin pointwise slot route.

## 7. Complete complementary budget and unchanged open input

No complementary term is declared paid by the unverified calculation. The existing accepted [restricted research revision] payments are retained exactly:

* Low merged core Nc<=U^(6/5) is removed by the pointwise radical identity A_R(n)=0 when N(rad n)<=R and the ensuing positive Hilbert triangle. This pays low/high crosses, not just low-low pairs.
* The full same-sixth-power class includes every pair ca^6,cb^6 and has exponent1-4delta/3.
* The disjoint off-class union Q<=U^(6/5), then Q1/Q3<=U^(1/2) on its complement, has respective exponents19/15-4delta/3 and5/4-4delta/3. R12--R14 pay all unequal roots and unequal dyads.
* The complete sixth-free projector, pair-dependent natural holes and finite free fixed-inducing exclusions are paid by the inherited kernel min(U,U^(1/6)Q^(5/12)), with divisor losses allocated before the threshold.

Their source-relative current-envelope gaps are those of the frozen independent review, including its buffered reserve49477/6825000 after spending xi=1/100. This packet neither recomputes those certificates nor spends them on the new conjectural prefix.

If a prefix bound is later proved, define D_far=D_R-D_prefix with the same smooth cutoff. Split the actual positive polynomial norm before expanding pairs. The Hilbert inequality

    ||D_R Q|| <= ||D_prefix Q||+||D_far Q||            (S13)

pays all prefix/far crosses once both complete positive norms are paid. It does not bound a chosen signed prefix/far sector separately. For the proposed high-bin variant, use |D_R(rho)|>=1/2 to split rows into |D_prefix(rho)|>=1/4 or |D_far(rho)|>=1/4; the first set would be treated by its separate positive unmarked norm and the original bin slot bound. Only the second set would invoke a far weighted norm. The partition is for this positive counting implication, never for Poisson on a bin-selected signed kernel.

The far polynomial retains original slots, all valuations, both orientations, natural zeros, all columns above its smooth lower transition and the genuine terminal tail. Its radical cancellation still uses R; only its lower column-size support changes. There is presently no bound here for its high-core/high-Q1 residual. The full S1/R22 estimate therefore remains open without any deleted slice.

All original physical low/high/zero/extracted/fixed-inducing branches, both signed projectors, clipped rectangle pairs, shared label counts, physical6a/9a charges, physical K_phys^(5/6), shortening and no-slot complements, weighted Euler shifts including zero capacity, all-height recovery, principal pole and common-Delta supremum feedback keep their accepted c11 contracts. No centered exceptional M/24 reserve is used. A source prefix estimate alone would not be a numerical endpoint proof.

For OPEN-H near/1/6/1/4, every target unit and required fixed row must remain and the total exponent must be negative. S11 at the present parameters is positive. Consequently none of those conditional direct-return targets advances in this packet. Principal pole annihilation and the possible nonprincipal zero at1 retain their separate existing kernels and signals.

## 8. Evidence and credit

The full [restricted research revision] independent review and the relevant exact local primary slices were inspected. The source receipt binds the pinned PR9 paper, the external RM-A/RM10 note, the prior author/reviewer packets and the accepted density integration. A broad initial rg result was truncated; it was navigation only, not claimed as complete source evidence. ### Local masks and exact coherent incidence

At \(p\mid AA'\), write \(\alpha_p=v_p(a)\), \(\beta_p=v_p(b)\), \(d_p=v_p(A)-v_p(A')\pmod6\). AA14 forces \(\alpha_p,\beta_p\le1\) because the column character requires a unit row. The local row character exponent is \(d_p-\alpha_p+\beta_p\). Under (A01.1) it is zero and the factor is a unit scalar times \(1_{p\nmid m}\).

Since \(A=cn^3,A'=c'n'^3\), the difference between the two squarefree incidence differences lies in \([-2,2]\). It cannot cancel an odd multiple of three. Therefore, at those primes,
\[
\alpha_p-\beta_p=v_p(c)-v_p(c'),\qquad
v_p(n)-v_p(n')\equiv0\pmod2.
\]
Outside \(AA'\), the coherent condition is \(\alpha_p-\beta_p\equiv0\pmod6\), with the additional support restrictions below.

Consequently all surviving pairs admit the exact good-ideal parametrization
\[
c=gu,\ c'=gv,\quad
a=d_0ur_1^6,\ b=d_0vr_2^6,\quad
n=hs^2,\ n'=ht^2.
\]
Here \(g,u,v\) are pairwise coprime squarefree; \(h\) is squarefree; \((r_1,r_2)=1\); \((r_1r_2,AA')=1\); \((d_0,uv)=1\); and \(v_p(d_0)\le1\) at \(p\mid AA'\). Core/cube overlaps among \(g,u,v,h,s,t\) otherwise remain. In particular, \(r_i\) may share primes with \(d_0\) outside \(AA'\).

At a good prime outside \(AA'\), let \(E_j=1_{p^j\mid m}\), \(E_0=1\). Lifting a normalized local Gauss sum gives, for \(j\ge1\),
\[
G_j(m)=q^{j/2-1}1_{p^{j-1}\mid m}
\sum_{x\bmod p}^{*}\chi_p(x)^j
\psi_p(-mx/p^{j-1}).
\]
If \(6\nmid j\),
\[
|G_j(m)|^2=q^{j-1}(E_{j-1}-E_j).
\]
If \(6\mid j\),
\[
G_j(m)=q^{j/2-1}(qE_j-E_{j-1}),\quad
|G_j(m)|^2=q^{j-2}\{(q^2-2q)E_j+E_{j-1}\}.
\]
These explicitly retain principal-on-units spikes.

For unequal coherent valuations \(\alpha>\beta\), positive \(\beta\not\equiv0\pmod6\) gives disjoint supports. If \(\beta=0\), the principal formula for \(G_\alpha\) applies; if \(6\mid\beta>0\), \(G_\beta\) is constant on \(G_\alpha\)'s support. Every surviving local product is a linear combination of divisibility masks with coefficient \(\ell^1\) norm at most \(2q^{(\alpha+\beta)/2}\). CRT therefore writes the full good kernel as
\[
K_S(m)\sum_e b_e1_{e\mid m},\qquad
\sum_e|b_e|
\ll_\epsilon(q_aq_b)^{1/2}
(q_aq_bq_Aq_{A'})^\epsilon. \tag{A01.3}
\]
Here \(K_S\) belongs to the original fixed finite periodic family; no moving prime is placed in \(S\). If \(a,b\) are squarefree, the factor \((q_aq_b)^{1/2}\) is unnecessary.

# [private research revision]: a nonlinear detector with a completely paid far tail

Accept G140–G142 as written ordinary-character results at the scopes
below. The [author](nonlinear-source/report.md),
[independent review](nonlinear-source-review/report.md) and
[retention manifest](retention-manifest.json) retain eleven original
artifacts and two immutable local mathematical sources. No new c is
proved: c11=.1251459636, theta11=.8748540364 remain current. Inherited
F0/analytic ancestry, original positive-slot uniformity and external
definition/import/admission remain OPEN. This source has its own ordinary
Dirichlet-character return; no Hecke or conductor-uniform scope is inferred.
No formalization, kernel work, new packet or public-record claim is made.

The discovery pass compared a coherent Gauss bank, quadratic-family
moments, signed Vaughan recombination and this upstream phase replacement.
The first and third still need new signed estimates; the inspected
quadratic-family asymptotic assumes GRH and is not imported. W14's unused
nonlinear-phase idea motivated a new integer source, not a claim that its
native sextic covariance problem has been solved.

## G140. The actual source and its nonvanishing Mellin return

Fix an ordinary complex character chi modulo q, retain
a_n=mu(n)chi(n) with every squareful/nonunit zero, and choose fixed b>1
and integer k>2. Define for every real x>0

    W_(b,k),chi(x)=sum_(n>=1) a_n exp(-n/x^b-i(n/x)^k).

The sum converges absolutely and locally uniformly. The selected source
has b=3/2, k=6. The phase uses n^k but the damping uses n; neither may
be substituted for the other in the Mellin calculation.

For Re s>0 let I_n(s)=integral_0^infinity exp(-nt^b-i(nt)^k)t^(s-1)dt.
After v=nt, rotate clockwise by fixed
0<alpha<min(pi/(2b),pi/(2k)), with principal power branches. The large
arc is killed, for each n, by exp(-n^(1-b)R^b cos(b alpha)); the other
exponential has modulus at most1 throughout the sector. The small arc
vanishes for Re s>0. On the rotated ray exp(-iv^k) has modulus
exp(-|v|^k sin(k alpha)). Taylor's integral remainder for Re z>=0 gives
|exp(-z)-sum_(j<K)(-z)^j/j!|<=|z|^K/K!. Consequently

    I_n(s)=sum_(j<K) A_j(s)n^(-s-(b-1)j)+R_(n,K)(s),
    A_j(s)=(-1)^j Gamma((s+bj)/k)
                  exp(-i*pi*(s+bj)/(2k))/(k j!),
    |R_(n,K)(s)| <= n^(-sigma-(b-1)K) exp(alpha Im s)
       Gamma((sigma+bK)/k)
       /[k K! sin(k alpha)^((sigma+bK)/k)].

The coefficient follows by a decaying gamma-ray rotation. Local
domination, including each fixed logarithmic derivative, proves remainder
holomorphy. Its series with a_n is normally convergent on
sigma>max(0,1-(b-1)K). Initial Fubini is used only for sigma>b, where
the absolute sum of integrals equals Gamma(sigma/b)zeta(sigma/b)/b.
Thus, for H(s)=integral_0^infinity W(1/t)t^(s-1)dt,

    H(s)=sum_(j<K) A_j(s)/L(s+(b-1)j,chi)+R_chi,K(s).

For b=3/2,k=6,K=1 this is

    H(s)=Gamma(s/6)exp(-i*pi*s/12)/(6L(s,chi))+R_chi,1(s),

with R holomorphic on Re s>1/2 and nonzero leading multiplier on Re s>0.
The complete every-epsilon shell L1 bound

    integral_X^(2X)|W(x)|dx/x <<_(chi,epsilon) X^(gamma+epsilon)

for one fixed gamma>1/2 makes H holomorphic on Re s>gamma. Choose
epsilon below the compact real-part margin; shell summation also pays
all fixed derivatives. At x tending to zero the bound
1/(exp(x^(-b))-1) pays every Mellin power. Continuation of the displayed
identity excludes every zero of the actual L in that half-plane. The
principal pole produces a reciprocal zero and is retained; imprimitive
Euler factors remain in L. Arbitrary compact height ranges suffice for
all finite heights. For all characters, gamma is common, while constants
and onsets may depend on the fixed character. L2 at exponent2gamma is a
stronger sufficient premise; equivalence with zero exclusion is not claimed.

## G141. Every tail and cross term, including an actual arithmetic floor

For arbitrary |a_n|<=1, set N=X^b and write the complete energy kernel

    E(X)=sum_(n,m>=1) a_n conjugate(a_m) K_X(n,m),
    K_X(n,m)=integral_1^2 exp(-(n+m)/(N u^b))
                  exp(-i(n^k-m^k)/(X^k u^k))du/u.

Conjugate symmetry retains both ordered cross terms. With v=u^(-k),
the positive amplitude is exp(-A v^(b/k))/(kv), A=(n+m)/N. It decreases
on[2^-k,1]; endpoints plus total variation are at most2^(k+1)/k.
Integration by parts, with the damping differentiated, proves

    |K_X(n,m)| <<_(b,k) min(1,X^k/|n^k-m^k|), n!=m.

For n>m, n^k-m^k>=n^(k-1)(n-m). All pairs outside the core n,m<=M
have max(n,m)>M, so both orientations sum absolutely to
O(X^k M^(2-k)log(2M)), for every shell-fixed real M>=2. Hence exactly

    E(X)=E_<=M(X)+D_>M(X)+O_(b,k)(X^k M^(2-k)log(2M)),
    D_>M=sum_(n>M)|a_n|^2 K_X(n,n)>=0,  D_>M<<_b X^b.

This includes the full core/tail strip, distant tail, real-cutoff
endpoints and both ordered crosses. Damping and the summable majorant
justify limits from finite squares. The same formula without E_<=M
holds for the tail's own energy. Only after this identity can positivity
of the remaining core or diagonal be used in a lower or reverse bound.

For the actual coefficients, elementary squared-divisor counting gives

    sum_(n<=y)|a_n|^2=d_q y+O_q(sqrt y),
    d_q=zeta(2)^(-1) product_(p|q)p/(p+1)>0.

It counts the nonunit exclusions exactly and applies to every fixed
principal, nonprincipal or imprimitive character. With
C_(q,b)=d_q(2^b-1)/(2b), partial summation yields D_all=C_(q,b)X^b+O_q(X^(b/2)).
For b=3/2,k=6,M=X^(19/16), the complete identity becomes

    E(X)=E_<=M(X)+C_(q,3/2)X^(3/2)+O_q(X^(5/4)log X).

Thus E(X)>=(C_(q,3/2)+o(1))X^(3/2). An every-epsilon L2 exponent
2gamma<3/2 is impossible for THIS source. The gamma=3/4 boundary,
weaker L1 bounds and different b remain eligible.

The review improves the actual tail by keeping its cutoff correction:

    Q_(q,b)(X,M)=(d_q X^b/2) integral_1^2
                         u^(b-1)exp(-2M/(X^b u^b))du,
    D_>M=Q_(q,b)(X,M)+O_(q,b)(X^(b/2)).

Stieltjes integration on(M,infinity) includes the boundary error
sqrt(M)exp(-lambda M) and the integral of lambda sqrt(t)exp(-lambda t),
both O(lambda^-1/2), uniformly in M. Therefore at M=X^(4/3), b=3/2,k=6,

    E(X)=E_<=M(X)+Q_(q,3/2)(X,M)+O_q(X^(3/4)),
    E_>M(X)=Q_(q,3/2)(X,M)+O_q(X^(3/4)).

The cross exponent2/3 has room to absorb its logarithm. Replacing Q
prematurely by C X^(3/2) would lose a correction of order X^(4/3).

There is also a log-free UPPER norm bound on the original sharp shell.
Let h(t)=0 for t<=0, h(t)=10t^3-15t^4+6t^5 for0<t<1 and h(t)=1 for
t>=1. Then phi(u)=h(2u-1)h((4-u)/2) is nonnegative C^2, supported
on[1/2,4] and equal1 on[1,2]. Majorize the COMPLETE squared tail by
its phi-weighted integral. Its transformed amplitude and first derivative
vanish at endpoints, and its L1/second-derivative L1 norms are uniform
in A>=0, since A-polynomials are multiplied by exp(-cA). Two integrations
by parts give |K_phi(n,m)|<< (1+|n^k-m^k|/X^k)^-2. With
delta_n=X^k/n^(k-1), sum_(h>=1)min(1,(delta_n/h)^2)<<delta_n.
Thus, with all coefficients and the original sharp shell still present,

    ||W_>M||_2^2 <<_(b,k) X^b+X^k M^(2-k).

This proves E(X)<<X^2+X^b generically by taking M=X. It removes the
logarithm from an upper norm, not from the earlier sharp signed identity.
The bounded array a_n=1 for n<=floor(X/2), zero otherwise, gives E>>X^2
at b=3/2,k=6. This shell-dependent array is a generic obstruction,
not a lower bound for actual Möbius coefficients.

## G142. Actual logarithmic improvement and the remaining complete core

Use Green–Tao's [published Theorem1.1, pp.542–543](https://annals.math.princeton.edu/wp-content/uploads/annals-v175-n2-p03-p.pdf):
fixed-degree polynomial nilsequences have every fixed logarithmic Möbius
saving, uniform in the polynomial coefficients, with ineffective constants.
A fixed torus with the degree-k abelian filtration and fixed sine/cosine
functions gives sum_(n<=Y)mu(n)e(P(n))<<_A Y(log(2Y))^-A. A dummy torus
coordinate is available to satisfy the stated dimension convention.
The GRH power-decay remark is unused. The separately inspected
[Gao–Zhao v2 Theorem1.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2212.09241v2) assumes GRH
and is not an unconditional input.

Expand the actual periodic chi in its finite additive Fourier series,
retaining zeros and coefficient absolute sum<=q. Apply the polynomial
bound to ell n/q-n^k/(2*pi*x^k). Splitting prefix lengths at sqrt M
and Abel summing the decreasing damping proves
|W_<=M(x)|<<_(q,A) M(log M)^-A, uniformly in real x. For k=6,b=3/2,
take M=X(log X)^B, B=(D+2)/4, A=B+(D+2)/2. The core log exponent
is -D-2, the complete off-diagonal log exponent -D-1, so

    E(X)<<_(q,D) X^(3/2)+X^2(log X)^-D,
    ||W||_1<<_(q,D) X^(3/4)+X(log X)^-D

for every fixed D>0. This is actual arithmetic progress for this new
source. It still misses the first-gain energy threshold1.7497080728
by .2502919272 in power; logarithmic strength cannot grow with X.

For 0<c<=1/4 put gamma=1-c and r=1+c/2. Freeze L=X^gamma,M=X^r
before x varies over[X,2X]. The prefix n<=L costs O(X^gamma), while
G141 gives ||W_>M||_2^2<<X^(3/2)+X^(6-4r)<<X^(2gamma).
Both complementary L1 and L2 norms are therefore O(X^gamma). The
SINGLE complete core target is

    integral_X^(2X)|sum_(X^gamma<n<=X^r) mu(n)chi(n)
              exp(-n/x^(3/2)-i(n/x)^6)|dx/x
                   <<_(chi,c,epsilon) X^(gamma+epsilon).  (CORE1)

By the norm triangle inequality in both directions this is equivalent
to the full source L1 input. The same holds for L2, which is sufficient
but stronger. The complements also permit exact big-O equivalence.
No omitted cross is hidden: the full tail function was first bounded
in L2, and only then used in the L1 triangle inequality.

| Conditional c | gamma | Upper cutoff exponent r | L2 target |
|---|---|---|---|
| .1252 | .8748 | 1.0626 | 1.7496 |
| 1/6 | 5/6 | 13/12 | 5/3 |
| 1/4 | 3/4 | 9/8 | 3/2 |

Every row is OPEN. The first would exceed c11 by135091/2500000000.

The review also proves a fixed-parameter larger conditional architecture.
For ANY fixed 1/2<gamma<1 choose 1<b<=2gamma, integer k>2 with
r=(k-2gamma)/(k-2)<b, and integer K with 1-(b-1)K<gamma. Low prefix
and complete tail still cost O(X^gamma); CORE1 on X^gamma<n<=X^r
is sufficient. Use ALL the shifts in G140. Starting with 1/L holomorphic
on Re s>1, solve for the unshifted reciprocal on
Re s>max(gamma,a-(b-1)) whenever it is known on Re s>a. Each j>=1
term is already holomorphic. A finite number of steps reaches gamma;
the nonzero A0, principal pole and actual Euler holes are paid throughout.

For example gamma=3/5, b=11/10, k=12, K=5 gives r=27/25, remainder
boundary1/2 and tail energy exponents11/10,6/5. It is a fully paid
conditional c=2/5 architecture, with its actual CORE1 still OPEN.
It conveys no greater likelihood of success than the near target.
All parameters are fixed before X. There is no theorem at gamma=1/2
or uniformity as gamma approaches it.

## What changes the next attack

The long tail is now paid, including its actual diagonal and every cross.
The first decisive target is CORE1 at gamma=.8748 over the ENTIRE real
shell. Near n~X the phase changes by only O(1/X) per integer step;
fixed higher degree changes constants, not that power. Generic curvature
or another improvement to the far tail cannot supply the missing signed
bound. A source-exact Type I/II, restricted correlation, detector coupling
or upstream replacement remains eligible, with every return paid.

Root read both complete reports/helpers and both primary theorem
statements. Exact rational checks concern budgets, source pins and cutoff
endpoints only; no unchanged helper was rerun. Primary theorem text was
available on the web; no downloaded PDF binary hash is claimed. All29
families/109 children, later ideas, nearer gains,1/6 and1/4 are retained.

## Decision

Accept the author's three surviving components with their stated scopes: the exact squarefree character inverse and conditional Mertens-energy return; the completely masked Walsh representation and paid Gaussian complements; and the normalization/defect bill for a unitary dilation. None proves an arithmetic saving. The signed local transfer has no singular-value advantage over its absolute gate; indefinite conserved flux does not control its expanding null vector; a Cayley transform retains its inverse observation cost. These are limited obstructions, not impossibility theorems for complete signed sources.

The Gaussian Walsh result is a principal/zeta source result. It is not an all-character extension of that detector. The twisted matrix is complex symmetric in general, not Hermitian. The inverse-entry estimate remains the original arithmetic estimate in different coordinates. Current c11=312864909/2500000000=.1251459636, theta11=.8748540364, is unchanged, with its inherited F0, positive-slot and external-admission obligations open.

The independent addition gives a cofactor formula and weighted residual certificate, plus an N/log N absolute prime obstruction to its simplest truncation. Constructing a better complete certificate remains open; neither a zero-free gain nor literature priority is claimed.

Two corrections concern evidence labels rather than the identities: the author's cited parity-syndrome discussion is in the closing discussion of G174, immediately before G175; and its complex-character helper uses the conjugate convention to its displayed matrix. The latter tests the conjugate character from the same family, but is not literally the displayed chi-labelled identity. Our independent check uses the displayed convention.

## 6. Optimum within the elementary interpolation family

For every fixed \(1/6<\rho\le1\), the two row bounds give
\[
|\operatorname{row}(h)|
\ll R^{(1-\rho)/2}h^\rho,
\]
with the corresponding discrepancy statement for \(R=1\). Sections 2-4 supply the same weighted mass with \(q_k^{-\rho}\). The exact fixed-\((D,E,\mathfrak r)\) cost is
\[
Z^\epsilon\frac{|\omega_D\omega_E|Q^{\rho-1}}
{Yq_{[D,E]}^{2\rho}R^{\rho/2}}.
\]
Harmonic ideal counting, again using \(D=gd,E=ge\), gives
\[
\sum_{D,E}\frac{|\omega_D\omega_E|}{q_{[D,E]}^{2\rho}}
\ll_\epsilon Z^\epsilon L^{\max(2-4\rho,0)}.
\]
At \(\rho=1/2\) the endpoint logarithms are absorbed in \(Z^\epsilon\). Thus the whole family is
\[
\boxed{
\sum_{R\le T}|C_{\lambda\mu}-Z_{\lambda\mu}|
\ll_{\epsilon,C,\rho}
Z^\epsilon Q^{\rho-1}Y^{-1}
L^{\max(2-4\rho,0)}T^{1-\rho/2}.
} \tag{FR19}
\]

Writing \(M=x+y\), its affordable scale exponent is
\[
\tau(\rho)=
\frac{(1-\rho)M-\max(2-4\rho,0)\ell+(y-x)/6}
{1-\rho/2}. \tag{FR20}
\]
For \(1/6<\rho<1/2\), the derivative has the sign of
\[
-\frac M2+3\ell+\frac{y-x}{12}
=-\frac{7M}{12}+\frac y6+3\ell,
\]
which is strictly positive at the saved geometry. For \(1/2<\rho\le1\), it has the sign of
\[
-\frac M2+\frac{y-x}{12}<0.
\]
Therefore \(\rho=1/2\) maximizes this elementary interpolation family at the saved geometry and gives exactly FR2. This optimality statement is limited to FR19; it is not a barrier for other covariance estimates.
title: 6. Optimum within the elementary interpolation family

## 3. Gaps and the critical-density exponent ledger

For the gap extension, suppose around each large j there is a set in
[j/2,3j/2] whose intersection with every contained interval of length a_j
has measure at least d_j a_j. Require a_j>=1, 0<d_j<=1 and

    (a_j+1)log(C/d_j)=o(sqrt(j)).                          (R10)

The observation constant for the chosen epsilon must be uniform in j.
Since C>1 is fixed, R10 forces a_j=o(sqrt(j)), so the central interval is
eventually much longer than 4a_j. Any interval of length 2a_j either contains
an a_j interval in the central range or has at least a_j length outside it.
Adding the full exterior therefore produces thickness (d_j/2,2a_j).
The logarithm of the sampling factor is
O((a_j sqrt(j)+1)log(C/d_j))=o(j). R6--R8 and their paid exterior bounds
are unchanged. This proves A12 with its local, every-center geometry.
A density-one list of globally good intervals is not enough.

At critical density, assume
log(1/delta_k)<=(D+o(1))sqrt(k), D>=0 fixed, at source exponent gamma_src<b,
with arbitrarily small positive allowances. Replace I_j by the integer-ended
interval j+/-j^(7/8)+O(1), and use T_j=t sqrt(j), t>0 fixed. Then

    log Lambda_j=132Dt j+o(j),
    sigma_j=tau+O(j^-1/2),
    log e_j<=-tau t^2 j/2+o(j),
    log(exterior bound)<=-j^(5/4)/2+o(j^(5/4)).           (R11)

The narrowed range has k/j=1+o(1), so taking the worst density within it
does not introduce a factor sqrt(3/2). The real localization loss is still
O(sqrt(j)). After all amplification and undoing exp(-bu), the output is

    max{gamma_src+132Dt, b-tau t^2/2+132Dt},              (R12)

with arbitrarily small final positive buffers. Choosing
t=sqrt(2(b-gamma_src)/tau) makes the two terms equal and proves A17.
This is a sufficient choice, not a claim that the expression has been
globally optimized in t or that 132 is optimal.

For bounded integer coefficients, or ideal coefficients with O(X) absolute
count, any fixed b>1 is allowed. If

    gamma_src+132D sqrt(2(1-gamma_src)/tau)<gamma4,
    gamma4=.874865,                                      (R13)

continuity first permits a fixed b>1 close enough to one, then fixed source
and output allowances. This validates A18. Neither b-1 nor the allowances
move with j. The fixed tau in R13 is the same kernel width as in the
arithmetic hypothesis. Section 8 improves this sufficient critical target
for a calibrated actual Gaussian source, as a separate reviewer corollary.
title: 3. Gaps and the critical-density exponent ledger

statement:
## 6. Uniform audit S22: exact indefinite metric and the positive readout

Take the specified three-state laboratory with
J=diag(1,1,-1), q(v)=v*Jv. The nonzero vectors v=(1,0,1) and
w=(1,0,-1) both have q=0. Projection of v onto the first coordinate
has q=1, and onto the third has q=-1. For the readout l(v)=v1-v3,
|l(w)|^2=4 despite q(w)=0. Scaling w makes this readout arbitrarily
large with unchanged zero signed energy. Thus an upper bound for an
indefinite quadratic form does not by itself bound a positive witness,
and an ordinary orthogonal projection need not preserve its sign.
This is a finite countertest, not a claim that the native H Gram is
indefinite.

An asterisk on a vector or matrix denotes conjugate transpose in the
formulas below.

The exact escape is a source-range condition. Write v=(u,Ku), with
u in C^2 and K:C^2->C. If ||K||=kappa<1, then

    q(v)=u*(I-K*K)u >=(1-kappa^2)||u||^2,
    ||v||^2 <=[(1+kappa^2)/(1-kappa^2)] q(v).       (A14)

The constant is sharp at a top singular vector of K. For K=(kappa,0),
u=(1,0) attains it exactly. At kappa=3/5 the ratio is17/8. It blows
up as the physical range approaches an isotropic direction; kappa=1
has a nonzero null vector and kappa>1 has a negative direction.

The readout may cost less than the whole vector norm. For
l(v)=a*u+b*Ku, define d=a+K*b as a column and D=I-K*K>0. Cauchy--Schwarz
in the D metric gives the EXACT best constant

    |l(v)|^2 <= C_l q(v),
    C_l=d*D^-1 d.                                 (A15)

Equality holds at u=D^-1 d, unless d=0, when the readout vanishes.
This follows by writing d*u=(D^-1/2 d)*(D^1/2 u). Thus a near-null
direction is not automatically fatal if the actual readout annihilates
it with a controlled coefficient. Such alignment needs proof from the
original source, not an abstract signature.

For K=(kappa,0), reading the first coordinate costs1/(1-kappa^2),
the second costs1, and the aligned readout v1-kappa*v3 costs
1-kappa^2. The laboratory therefore supplies both the generic
conditioning obstruction and a genuine readout-sensitive escape.

To identify the actual Gaussian source, any finite set of its original
integer labels has the POSITIVE Gram

    G_mn=integral_[X,2X] g_tau(log(m/x))g_tau(log(n/x)) dx/x,
    ||F_N||^2=c*G c, c_n=f(n)chi(n).                (A16)

Both independent labels, all chosen signs and the natural zeros remain.
G is positive because it is a Gram of the actual functions. Absorbing
the source coefficients into a diagonal D_c gives D_c*G D_c>=0.
A signed expansion or a Krein realization may represent this same
quantity, but cannot replace A16 by an unrelated difference of positive
sector norms and call it the physical energy. In particular, a mere
signature count or small signed trace is insufficient.

If a proposed exact realization maps the arithmetic coefficient vector
into a graph range as above, it must prove the uniform bound on K and
the actual readout A15, then restore all excluded source terms. The
factor in A14 or A15 must be paid in the exponent budget; near-null
conditioning can consume it. No such graph condition or alignment is
established for native H, the full f3 correlations or a completed
infinite-label source in this audit. Conversely, the three-state
counterexample does not rule out a source-specific realization that
does prove them.

Ancestry is the indefinite storage/observer and U-VARIATIONAL readout
obstruction. The fresh bounded audit supplies an exact three-state
counterexample, sharp positive-range price and optimal scalar readout
constant. It gives no arithmetic energy reduction or new c.
title: 6. Uniform audit S22: exact indefinite metric and the positive readout
