## 3. D2 / S27: the collective dual transform retains the whole mask

This protected high-ceiling mechanism remains an exact open target after a decisive failure of the cheap version. Use the actual principal Gaussian coprime source, not a changed Liouville source. Fix tau>0, Y=floor(X^.495), and B_X=2X exp(C sqrt(log X)), with fixed C>0. Index a Boolean cube by ALL primes 5<=p<=B_X. Let d(u)=product p^(u_p) and write

    K(u,v)=(-1)^(|u|+|v|)1_(u&v=0),
    W_x(u,v)=1_(d(u)>Y,d(v)>Y,d(u)d(v)<=B_X)
       *sum_(1<=l<=B_X/(d(u)d(v))) (-1)^(l+1)
                   g_tau(log(d(u)d(v)l/x)).

The finite scalar Z_X(x)=sum_(u,v)K(u,v)W_x(u,v) is precisely the output-truncated G25 source. The prime2,3 exclusion, both strict cuts, repeated-factor zeros, ordered copies, alternating cofactor, exact product cap and every boundary are retained. Impossible cube states have W=0; the full cube is an algebraic ambient space, not an asserted efficient algorithm.

For k cube sites use the UNNORMALIZED Walsh transform in both variables:

    hat F(a,b)=sum_(u,v)(-1)^(a.u+b.v)F(u,v).

Finite character orthogonality proves the exact collective identity

    Z_X(x)=2^(-2k)sum_(a,b)hat K(a,b)hat W_x(a,b).         (4)

No conjugation is required because the Walsh matrix is real and the original contraction is bilinear; the identity remains valid for complex W. Locally H T H=[[-1,1],[1,3]], H=[[1,1],[1,-1]]. Hence hat K is the tensor product of this FULL local matrix. Changing basis has made the three-entry coprimality gate into four nonzero entries. The signs survive; there is no sparse-dual saving from the gate alone. Any sparse support must be proved for the complete transformed arithmetic W, whose product cutoff couples the sites.

The bridge has explicit complements. The original d3 output-tail majorant gives, uniformly for x in[X,2X],

    |P_Y(x)-Z_X(x)| <= X^(1-C^2/(2tau)+o(1)).            (5)

This bounds the actual omitted labels de*l>B_X, not an independently chosen mask. Choose C so that the exponent in(5) is strictly below a fixed gamma>1/2. G27 separately pays P_Y-F6 at X^(.495+delta), with delta small enough. G28's two fixed Euler convolution inverses have absolute weighted sums finite for every fixed sigma>1/2; they transfer all-shell F6 and G_tau norms in both directions. Their separate prime2,3 factors and each shell's frozen Y remain mandatory. Thus a full all-shell L2 bound of the signed RIGHT SIDE OF(4) by X^(gamma+epsilon) would return the original Gaussian G3 and zeta zero exclusion in Re(s)>gamma. It gives no ordinary-character or Hecke result without an additional source-specific extension. The new transform is not assigned an independent Mellin transform as X changes.

The remaining arithmetic hypothesis is the complete signed sum in(4), including both copies when squaring. Replacing it by the sum of absolute terms, estimating only a favorable dual block, or interpreting cube sites as independent arithmetic variables does not establish that hypothesis. The number of cube sites is enormous; the expression is not a computational saving by itself.

A useful retained boundary condition is therefore: supply a family of dual coefficients or compressed states and prove BOTH its whole signed output estimate and the entire omitted signed field norm below gamma. This is a concrete mechanism change with a paid projection back, but no such arithmetic family has been found here. G68 already owns a different biased-Walsh degree truncation with paid CRT error; G121 owns cutoff rectangle rank. Neither licenses deletion of modes in(4). G175 already contains the parity-syndrome blindness example, so that example is not recounted as a new result.

## 4. Radical cancellation and complete low-core payment

For n!=1 and N(rad n)<=R, every contributing squarefree d divides rad n and has Nd<=R. Therefore V(Nd/R)=1, and

    A_R(n)=sum_(d|rad n) mu(d)=0.                     (R5)

This is exact at the endpoint N(rad n)=R. It does not require n to be squarefree or Nn<=R. Inactive nonsquarefree divisors have mu=0. A single separated divisor dyad would not retain this identity. Natural omissions cause no problem: if phi_u(n) is nonzero, all its divisors have the same permitted prime support; if it is zero, the fully multiplicative convolution is zero already.

If b_l is nonzero, some retained summand in R2 has A_R(n)!=0. Since rad n divides rad l,

    N(rad l)>R.                                      (R6)

Write l=c a^6 with c sixth-power-free as an ideal. Then rad l=rad(ca), so N(rad l)<=Nc Na. Thus every contributing small-core column obeys Na>R/Nc. This is a substantially stronger restriction than the size-only Na>(R/Nc)^(1/6).

For C0=U^lambda<R, form the exact merged-column projection F_lo with Nc<=C0. Apply R3 and natural zeros only as contractions. For every individual row, every required derivative, and the entire real rectangle,

    |partial F_lo,u(s)|
      << H_J U^((sigma-1/2)v+epsilon)
           sum_(Nc<=C0) (Nc)^(-sigma)
              sum_(Na>R/Nc) (Na)^(-6sigma)
      << H_J U^((sigma-1/2)v+epsilon)
                      R^(1-6sigma) C0^(5sigma).      (R7)

The first ideal tail is O(A^(1-6sigma)) for A>=1 by the source's linear ideal count and partial summation. Its exponent is safely convergent on the fixed real interval. After substitution, the remaining c sum is bounded by sum_(Nc<=C0)(Nc)^(5sigma-1), which is O(C0^(5sigma)). Extending c to all ideals only enlarges the upper bound. All sixth-power roots, late column scales, unit cores, shared slot primes and exceptional rows are included.

There are O(U) element rows in the fixed ball. Integrating R7 and its derivative versions yields

    N(F_lo) << H_J U^[1+2t(1-6sigma)+10sigma lambda
                              +(2sigma-1)v+epsilon]. (R8)

At t=4/3, lambda=6/5, its derivative with respect to sigma is -4+2v<0. At the nominal edge sigma=(1+delta)/2 the exponent is

    L_lo=5/3-2delta+delta v.                           (R9)

A downward buffer h0 raises it by (4-2v)h0<=4h0. For F_hi=F-F_lo, the Hilbert norm satisfies

    N(F)^(1/2)<=N(F_hi)^(1/2)+N(F_lo)^(1/2).          (R10)

Squaring gives a fixed factor two, which has no power cost. This pays every low/high cross term, regardless of sign. It never divides by Q_u or assumes an amplitude lower bound. This is the decisive response to the concern that a paid low-low sector might leave unpaid crosses. The same pointwise projection is valid on a target unit row; a direct-return application still has to pay its different exponent.

## G230. Paid ambient realizations and two independent audits

If A=alpha P U Q with U unitary and P,Q contractions, alpha>=||A|| follows
by submultiplicativity. For C=A/alpha a contraction, the Halmos block
[[C,(I-CC*)^(1/2)],[(I-C*C)^(1/2),-C*]] is unitary; the defect intertwining
identity proves it directly. It realizes the optimum alpha=||A||. For
selfadjoint C its square is I, whereas C^2=I-(I-C^2); repeated use must
retain the returning defect or intermediate physical projections. A
source-specific approximation remains possible, with the full scalar
residual bounded by delta||u||2||v||2 when its operator error is delta.

The signed local gate T is a diagonal sign gauge of [[1,1],[1,0]], so their
singular values agree. The indefinite J=[[-2,-1],[-1,2]] satisfies T^TJT=-J,
yet v=(phi,-1), phi=(1+sqrt5)/2, is J-null and Tv=phi v. Conserved flux
does not bound that positive observation. For a selfadjoint K, the Cayley
unitary V=(K-iI)(K+iI)^-1 has (I-V)^-1=(I-iK)/2 and inverse norm
sqrt(1+||K||^2)/2. No selfadjoint claim is licensed for complex A_chi.

The protected S28 audit diagonalizes the disjointness gate orthogonally.
For K_0 sites its eigenvalues are (-1)^j phi^(K_0-2j), with binomial
multiplicity, and squared Frobenius norm3^K_0. Writing the FULL physical
boundary in that basis preserves its Frobenius norm; the generic contraction
bill is3^(K_0/2)||W||F. A product-only weight counts each ordered prime
allocation and produces mu(n)chi(n)2^omega(n), not the original Mertens
coefficient. A single n-divisor cube has omega(n)=O(log n/loglog n);
that does not bound the global prime set of every n<=X.

The uniform S09 audit uses the connected prime-adjoining graph on S_N.
For (Bf)_(n,pn)=f(pn)+chi(p)f(n), write f(n)=a(n)g(n), a(n)=mu(n)chi(n).
Then ker B=span(a). In ANY complete identity w=lambda e1+B^T t, pairing
with a forces lambda=sum_n w_n a(n). A rooted prime-deletion tree constructs

    inf_(lambda,t)(|lambda|+||w-lambda e1-B^Tt||1)=|sum_n w_n a(n)|.
                                                               (230.1)

The upper equality chooses the exact signed target as lambda; the lower is

# [private research revision] controller candidate: rough-depth renewal for the actual f3 field

Unreviewed candidate, 11 October 2026. This rotates the accepted [private research revision] signed-core/PNT method into the [private research revision] fixed f3 Gaussian source. It is not an SP mask transfer and is not a bound for the full field.

Fix tau>0 and B>0, put z=(log X)^B, and let omega_z(n) count DISTINCT primes p>z dividing n. Define the literal field

    T_z(x)=sum_(omega_z(n)<=1) f3(n) g_tau(log(n/x)),
    f3(n)=mu(rad(n/3^v3(n))),  X<=x<=2X.

All prime powers and the complete Gaussian are retained. Conjectured/proposed asymptotic to prove independently:

    T_z(x) = 3 log(2) exp(tau/2) P(z) x/(log x)^2 * (1+o(1)),
    P(z)=product_(5<=p<=z) (p-2)/(p-1) ~ constant/log z >0.

Reason for a different logarithmic order from SP: the entire z-smooth reciprocal f3 mass is ZERO, exactly due to p=2. Set

    H_z(s) = (1-3^(-s))^(-1)
             *product_(p<=z,p!=3) (1-2p^(-s))/(1-p^(-s)).

This finite Euler expression is represented by its absolutely convergent smooth-number series at Re s>0. At s=1,

    H_z(1)=0,
    H_z'(1)=3 log(2) P(z),
    sum_(r z-smooth) f3(r)log(r)/r = -3 log(2)P(z).

The literal one-large-prime part is -sum_r f3(r) sum_(p>z) g_tau(log(rp/x)). Higher powers of the unique large prime p^k, k>=2, and the fully smooth field must be paid separately; they are not absent.

Under PNT partial summation, the k=1 term is

    -x sum_r f3(r)/r integral_R e^u g_tau(u)/(log x + u - log r) du,

up to the paid lower cut p>z, tails, and prime error. Expansion at log x: the 1/log x term cancels via H_z(1)=0. The next term is -x exp(tau/2) times the signed log-r moment divided by (log x)^2, giving the displayed POSITIVE constant. The u moment also multiplies H_z(1) and cancels.

Proposed cheap rigorous route: cut smooth cores at R=exp((log X)^(1/4)) and Gaussian u at abs(u)<(log X)^(1/4). With s=1-1/log z, a positive smooth Euler product is O(log z), and Rankin gives reciprocal tail exp(-log R/log z) times a power of log z. The fully smooth field should be O(X exp(-c log X/log z)) up to polynomial logarithms. For p^k, k>=2, split r<=R (prime-power count at most X^(1/2+o(1))) and the smooth-core tail with a positive divisor majorant. The prime error can use the fixed-order Johnston–Yang PNT already accepted in [restricted mathematical source] §2, with order selected sufficiently large before X grows. It needs no unproved short-interval PNT.

An absolute second-order Taylor remainder after the exact zero and signed first moment should be O(x (log z)^3/(log x)^3); relative to main x/((log x)^2 log z) this is O((log z)^4/log x)=o(1) for fixed B. If correct, doubling log z changes P(z) by factor 1/2, so the signed band T_(z^2)-T_z has leading coefficient -1/2 of T_z (with both thresholds polylogarithmic). It gives an actual opposite-sign band in f3 and full leading cross-Gram for fixed finite thresholds. statement:
## 1. Kernel construction and exact scale transfer

Let U_j be independent uniforms on [-2^{-j},2^{-j}] for j>=1. Their sum converges absolutely, since the sum of their maximal absolute values is one. Let k be its density. The following elementary proof supplies all the properties used below; no random-coefficient arithmetic assumption enters.

The characteristic function is the normally convergent product of sinc factors. For every fixed integer B, its first B factors and the bound one on the remainder give

\[
 |\widehat k(t)|\le C_B(1+|t|)^{-B}.
 \tag{DP2}
\]

Fourier inversion, also after multiplication by every fixed power of t, gives a C-infinity density. It is even, nonnegative, supported in [-1,1], with integral one. Its bilateral Laplace transform is

\[
 M(s)=\int k(v)e^{sv}\,dv
 =\prod_{j\ge1}\frac{\sinh(2^{-j}s)}{2^{-j}s}.
 \tag{DP3}
\]

Each apparent singularity at s=0 is removable. Uniform convergence on compact sets follows from the O(4^{-j}|s|^2) deviations from one. Each factor has zeros only on the imaginary axis; off that axis the convergent product has no zero. Thus M(s) is entire and nonzero for Re s>0.

Write k_delta(v)=delta^{-1}k(v/delta), V_delta(u)=k_delta(log u), and let h_J be the convolution of the first J uniform densities. With delta=2^{-J}, the remaining sum has distribution delta times the original sum. Therefore

\[
 k=h_J*k_\delta,\qquad h_J\ge0,\quad\int h_J=1,
 \quad\operatorname{supp}h_J\subset[-1,1].
 \tag{DP4}
\]

For any fixed coefficient sequence B(n) of polynomial growth, all detector sums below are finite at each x. Define

\[
 F_{B,\delta}(x)=\sum_{n\ge1}B(n)V_\delta(n/x).
\]

Substitution of DP4 and finite summation give the exact identity

\[
 F_{B,1}(x)=\int h_J(t)F_{B,\delta}(xe^t)\,dt.
 \tag{DP5}
\]

Jensen followed by the change of variable y=xe^t yields

\[
 \int_X^{2X}|F_{B,1}(x)|^2\frac{dx}{x}
 \le\int_{e^{-1}X}^{2eX}|F_{B,\delta}(y)|^2\frac{dy}{y}.
 \tag{DP6}
\]

No derivative of B, a cutoff or a profile is taken. The width on the right is frozen throughout the enlarged shell. In particular put

\[
 J_X=\lfloor\eta\log_2X\rfloor,\qquad
 \delta_X=2^{-J_X},\qquad X^{-\eta}\le\delta_X<2X^{-\eta}.
 \tag{DP7}
\]

Only sufficiently large X is used, so J_X>=1. This constructs one fixed master detector from a family of moving profiles without pretending that a shell-dependent definition has a global Mellin multiplier.

Its fixed CRT phase and angular factors remain. Its nonzero set U is
(h,pi*pi')=1,s!=0 mod pi,s'!=0 mod pi'. The complete signed short sum
is folded into W before taking any norm. The physical row support has
O(K) elements; each mark support has O(L), with original injection gates.

For bounded integral lifts define a2(h) from odd good-prime valuations
and a3(s) from good-prime valuations nonzero modulo3. The order-two and
order-three subgroups of Z/6 intersect only at zero. Thus shared good
primes cannot cancel the quadratic row factor, and the exact good finite
primitive conductors are

    f1=lcm(a2(h),a3(s)), f2=lcm(a2(h),a3(s')).

Canceled conductor factors still retain their natural imprimitive zeros.
Fixed bad and angular data are separate; this identity does not give a
finite-order theorem for the full moving angular kernel.

The bounded row lifts with q_a2(h)<=D number O(sqrt(QD)): write
(h)=a_S a b^2, with finitely many bad-prime parity choices a_S and
good squarefree q_a<=D, then use ideal counting and partial summation.
All squares and arbitrary bad-prime powers are included. This is an
ideal count, not a count of squarefree rational norms.

Any selector, even one depending on transformed marks and coefficients,
which retains points with min(q_f1,q_f2)<=D lies inside that row-only
set. Enlarge its positive squared mass first, then apply row Cauchy
and both mark Plancherel identities. This proves

    ||1_U 1_(min(q_f1,q_f2)<=D) W_hat||_2^2
       <= C K sqrt(D)/N ||W||_2^2.

The original separate row injections and mark Cauchy give eligible mass
at least[1-C(1+L)/N]||W||_2^2. If W is nonzero, the corresponding
eligible fraction is bounded by the displayed ratio. If W=0 no nonzero
fraction is claimed. The adaptive selector itself need not commute with
Fourier transformation: only the containing row set does.

At the inherited pressure block N/K=Z^.003, a fixed captured fraction
requires D at least a constant times Z^.006. The product-conductor
version requires q_f1 q_f2 budget at least a constant times Z^.012.
D=Z^.004 or product budget Z^.008 captures O(Z^(-.001)) of eligible
squared mass. These are necessary norm-approximation thresholds, not
sufficiency at equality or lower bounds for H. The numerical .004
conductor example is unrelated to the .004 physical deficit.

The statement is for the unprojected tensor and bounded lifts. The
accepted kernel-invariant orbit projection can discard tensor norm while
preserving its signed pairing. Unbounded alternative lifts or a new basis
also require their own paid support and moving weights. These escapes
remain open; the obstruction does not rule out signed cancellation.

statement:
## 5. Paying the curved sectors and keeping every original tail

For (PH4)'s first bound, a conductor dyad \(T<R\le2T\) is paid when
\[
K\ge \frac{T^{9/4}}{QY}.
\]
The resulting factor is
\(Q^{-1/2}T^{3/4}K^{-1/3}\le Q^{-1/6}Y^{1/3}=P_a^{1/6}\).
For its second bound the condition is
\(K\ge(T^3/P_a)^{1/5}\).
If either lower bound is below one, use \(K=1\); this only improves the estimate. These are precisely the two parts of (PH5), up to fixed dyadic constants.

Similarly (PH7) pays the sector
\[
\boxed{
\mathfrak p_{\mathrm{coh}}=1,\qquad
1<R\le\max\!\left\{(QY)^{4/9}F^{2/3},\ P_a^{1/3}F^2\right\}.
}
\tag{PH16}
\]
The required lower bounds for \(F\) are respectively
\(T^{3/2}/(QY)^{2/3}\) and \(T^{1/2}P_a^{-1/6}\).

All these sectors have polynomial \(R\)-range: (PH3) gives \(F\ll Y^2\), so their displayed inequalities themselves bound \(R\) by a fixed power of the original scales. There are \(O(\log Z)\) conductor dyads. We do not sum the estimates over infinitely many unrestricted conductor dyads. Their logarithmic number is absorbed by choosing smaller losses in (PH8) and (PH14). Overlaps are disjointized by bounded row-independent masks. No positive-semidefinite assertion about a conductor or gcd mask is used.

The infinite completed columns have not been truncated. Each actual mark kernel satisfies the inherited bound
\[
|K_D(A)|\ll_\eta q_A^\eta E(q_A/N_D),\qquad N_D=ZL_D,
\tag{PH17}
\]
with one common two-sided rapid envelope and no separate marked-tuple length factor. The weighted masses (PH8) and (PH14) sum both envelopes before removing their dependence. Small powers of arbitrarily large columns are absorbed into them. The restriction on \(F\) depends only on the finite outer columns and embeddings; it never changes a profile or adds a completed tail.

For definiteness, the underlying field is absolutely defined before these sharper row bounds: the original completed coefficients obey
\[
\sum_{c,n}\frac{q_{cn^3}^\eta}{\sqrt{q_c}q_n}
E(q_cq_n^3/N_D)
\ll N_D^{1/2+\eta}\sum_nq_n^{-5/2}<\infty.
\tag{PH18}
\]
The outer labels and physical rows lie in fixed annuli. Finite completed truncations therefore converge to the original field; the positive estimates above pass to the limit. The unit ideal, shared core/cube primes, all natural zero extensions, signed roots and signed marks stay in the definition.

The joint row profile is always
\(W_0(q_r/(Hx_a))\overline{W_0(q_r/(Hx_b))}\).
Substitution \(r=kz\) changes its scale to \(H/q_k\), exactly as in FR. All annular parameters lie in fixed compact sets. If the original inverse representation is kept in Mellin form, the same finite profile seminorms grow polynomially in its real heights and are integrated against the original rapid densities. No moving-set Poisson constant, moving cutoff derivative, or unpriced height supremum is introduced.

statement:
## B. A parity-adapted Jordan source with its complete ordinary-character return

Fix an ordinary Dirichlet character chi modulo q, including its presented-modulus zeros. Write chi(-1)=(-1)^a, a in {0,1}, and choose once an integer r>=2 with r congruent to a modulo 2 (r=2 for even characters, r=3 for odd characters suffice). Define

    J_r(n)=sum_(d|n)mu(d)(n/d)^r
          =n^r product_(p|n)(1-p^(-r)),
    F_(chi,r)(X)=sum_(n>=1)chi(n)J_r(n) exp(-n/X).       (B1)

J_r counts primitive r-tuples modulo n: inclusion-exclusion over common prime divisors proves the formula. It is positive; chi J_r still has character zeros, while squareful coefficients such as J_2(4)=12 are intentionally present. The changed object does not pretend to have the original coefficient support. Absolute multiplication of Dirichlet series on Re(s)>r+1 gives

    sum_n chi(n)J_r(n)n^(-s)=L(s-r,chi)/L(s,chi).        (B2)

For principal chi let m_q=phi(q)/q, otherwise m_q=0, and put

    A_(chi,r)=m_q r!/L(r+1,chi),
    E_(chi,r)(X)=F_(chi,r)(X)-A_(chi,r)X^(r+1).          (B3)

In (B3), A=0 for nonprincipal chi. It is the entire principal main term, including all removed Euler factors, rather than the primitive-modulus residue.

### Exact periodic kernel and paid tails

Let

    H_chi(t)=sum_(n>=1)chi(n)e^(-nt)
            =[sum_(v=1)^q chi(v)e^(-vt)]/[1-e^(-qt)],
    f_(chi,r)(t)=(-d/dt)^r H_chi(t),
    g_(chi,r)(t)=f_(chi,r)(t)-m_q r! t^(-r-1).          (B4)

All these formulas hold for t>0, also for q=1. Convolution and the absolutely convergent reciprocal at r+1 yield the COMPLETE identity

    E_(chi,r)(X)=sum_(d>=1)mu(d)chi(d)g_(chi,r)(d/X).   (B5)

No cutoff was exchanged with a conditionally convergent series. Before subtracting the pole term, double sums converge absolutely for each X; after subtraction, the reciprocal sum is absolutely convergent since r+1>1.

The rational formula for H has only its possible simple pole m_q/t at zero. Its regular derivative in (B4) is analytic there. Reflection of residues v<->q-v gives H(-t)=-chi(-1)H(t), apart from the constant exception H_1(-t)=-1-H_1(t). The r>=2 derivative removes that exception. Since r has the parity of chi, f_r and its pole term are odd. Therefore

    g(t)=O_(chi,r)(t), g'(t)=O_(chi,r)(1)  as t down to 0.

At infinity, f_r and its derivative are O_(chi,r)(e^(-t)). Thus principal g(t)=-m_q r!t^(-r-1)+O(e^(-t)), with the differentiated tail retained; nonprincipal g decays exponentially. In particular

    |g(t)| <= C_(chi,r) min(t,t^(-r-1)),               (B6)
    |E(X)| <= C'_(chi,r) X  for X>=1.                 (B7)

The bound (B7) is unconditional but has exponent 1. For any target 0<gamma<1 and real cuts D=X^alpha, Y=X^beta, alpha<1<beta, (B5)-(B6) pay

    sum_(d<=D)|mu(d)chi(d)g(d/X)| = O(X^(2alpha-1)),
    sum_(d>Y)|mu(d)chi(d)g(d/X)| = O(X^(r+1-r beta)).  (B8)

Endpoints are d<=D and d>Y. All real X are covered. Thus alpha=(1+gamma)/2 and beta=1+(1-gamma)/r pay both pieces at exponent gamma. The middle source D<d<=Y remains a full signed arithmetic obligation. For a nonprincipal chi, the upper cutoff can instead be C X log X and its full tail made any prescribed negative power by choosing fixed C large enough. Constants may depend on the fixed character.

### No lost zeros in the numerator

Primitive L-functions have no zeros in Re(z)<0 except their real trivial zeros at the negative integers of the corresponding parity. The imprimitive completion is the primitive function times the exact finite factors 1-chi*(p)p^(-z). These factors have zeros only on Re(z)=0. Consequently our parity choice gives

    L(s-r,chi) != 0  whenever 0<Re(s)<=1.              (B9)

Indeed -r<Re(s-r)<=1-r lies strictly between consecutive trivial zeros, and is negative. Gamma(s) also has no zero or pole there. The functional equation and finite-factor formulas used here are the standard [DLMF 25.15.4-8](https://dlmf.nist.gov/25.15). This statement handles all heights and all presented moduli; no uniformity in growing q is used.

Suppose for every epsilon>0 and all large real X that

    E_(chi,r)(X)=O_(chi,epsilon)(X^(gamma+epsilon))      (B10)

at one common gamma<gamma11 for every fixed ordinary chi, with r chosen as above. Then L(s,chi) has no zeros with Re(s)>gamma, with the principal pole at 1 retained.

Here is the full Mellin justification. Initially on Re(s)>r+1,

    Mellin(F)(s)=Gamma(s)L(s-r,chi)/L(s,chi).

Split at X=1, subtract A X^(r+1) only in the large-X integral and add A/(s-r-1). By (B7) the resulting expression continues to Re(s)>1 except the indicated main-term pole. On 1<Re(s)<r+1 it equals the ordinary full integral of E. At X down to zero, F decays faster than every power and E=-A X^(r+1)+that remainder. Hypothesis (B10) therefore makes

    H(s)=integral_0^infinity E(X)X^(-s) dX/X

holomorphic on gamma<Re(s)<r+1, locally uniformly with every fixed derivative. Choose epsilon below each compact set's distance to gamma. Continuation of the product identity gives

    L(s,chi)H(s)=Gamma(s)L(s-r,chi).                   (B11)

By (B9), a zero in gamma<Re(s)<=1 contradicts (B11). The Euler product excludes Re(s)>1. At the principal pole, H has the compensating zero; it is not discarded as a bad point. This proof does not require assuming a bare zero-free strip already supplies a sharp Mertens bound. It proves a replacement detector's own sufficient return.

For gamma=.8748 the conditional target c=.1252 would exceed c11 by .0000540364. The basic r=2 principal cuts are alpha=.9374 and beta=1.0626. For gamma=5/6 they are 11/12 and 13/12; for gamma=3/4 they are 7/8 and 9/8. These are paid complementary regions, not successful estimates of their middle sum.

### An actual-source linear absolute price

Let Q_q(u)=sum_(n<=u,(n,q)=1)mu(n)^2. Elementary square-divisor inclusion-exclusion gives

    Q_q(u)=kappa_q u+O_q(sqrt(u)),
    kappa_q=(phi(q)/q) product_(p not|q)(1-p^(-2))>0.

Apply Stieltjes summation to the COMPLETE price in (B5). Because |g| is absolutely continuous, |(|g|)'|<=|g'| almost everywhere, and integral_0^infinity sqrt(t)|g'(t)|dt is finite by the two tails,

    sum_n |mu(n)chi(n)g(n/X)|
      =kappa_q X integral_0^infinity |g(t)|dt+O_(chi,r)(sqrt X). (B12)

The integral is strictly positive. For principal chi the nonzero algebraic far tail proves this; for nonprincipal chi the nonzero e^(-t) leading term proves it. This is an unconditional asymptotic for the actual arithmetic absolute price, not a generic coefficient toy. Thus triangle inequality on the full primitive-source residual cannot produce any fixed gamma<1. The changed positive coefficients and the paid outer ranges do not eliminate the signed middle problem.

## 6. Different attempted mechanism: finite-prime conditioning

After the hard-region test, a distinct affordable attempt is to expose
the local sign at prime 2 and exploit its almost perfectly balanced
positive Gaussian occupation. The source itself prevents marginal
balancing from supplying the needed joint signed cancellation.
This section identifies the precise missing conditional covariance;
it does not claim a new obstruction to every possible conditioning
argument, and the general dilation equivalence was already in N28.

Set psi=f_6; it ignores both primes 2 and 3. For every n,

    psi(2n)=psi(n),
    chi_2(n)=1-2*1_(2|n),
    f(n)=chi_2(n)psi(n)
        =psi(n)-2*1_(2|n)psi(n/2).                  (A31)

No squarefree restriction or conditional independence is used.
Define the full actual field P(x)=sum_n psi(n)g(log(n/x)) and the
positive lattice Z(x)=sum_n g(log(n/x)). Exact reindexing yields

    F(x)=P(x)-2P(x/2),
    D(x):=sum_n chi_2(n)g(log(n/x))=Z(x)-2Z(x/2).  (A32)

In fact D is smaller than every fixed inverse power. To see this,
the function q(u)=g(log u), u>0, extended by zero for u<=0, is
Schwartz on R: all derivatives vanish to infinite order at zero and
decay faster than any power at infinity. Poisson summation therefore
gives, for every fixed N and x>=1,

    Z(x)=exp(tau/2)x+O_(N,tau)(x^-N),
    D(x)=O_(N,tau)(x^-N).                            (A33)

The n=0 term is zero and the integral of q is exp(tau/2). Thus this
attempt starts with a rigorously balanced marginal on the actual
ALL-INTEGER positive Gaussian law, rather than an invented model.

Normalize that law as nu_x(n)=g(log(n/x))/Z(x). Its two sign variables
chi_2,psi have expectations D/Z and P/Z, whereas their product has
expectation F/Z. For ANY two +/-1 variables the total L1 difference
between their joint distribution and the product of its marginals is
the absolute covariance (each of the four cells differs by +/-cov/4).
Consequently the EXACT missing joint-control quantity here is

    ||Law_(nu_x)(chi_2,psi)
                  -Law(chi_2) tensor Law(psi)||_1
          = |F(x)/Z(x)-D(x)P(x)/Z(x)^2|.             (A34)

The second term is superpower small by |P|<=Z and (A33). Upgrading
joint independence to a new power is therefore equivalent to the
unpaid signed full field itself. Perfect marginal balance does not
bound it. The actual even conditional numerator is P(x/2), and the
odd numerator P(x)-P(x/2); the prime-two branch returns the same
remaining source at half scale. Both values 0 and 1 of the occupation
indicator, every prime-two valuation, and prime 3 remain present.

There is an explicit quantitative return for finite conditioning
depth, rather than an unpriced claim that iteration solves the issue.
The actual source estimate (A17) with d=6 gives P(y)=O_beta(y^beta).
Iterating (A32) FORWARD in scale gives the exact finite identity

    P(x)=-sum_(j=1)^J 2^-j F(2^j x)+2^-J P(2^J x),
    |2^-J P(2^J x)|<=C_beta x^beta 2^(-(1-beta)J). (A35)

Thus P(x)=-sum_(j>=1)2^-j F(2^j x), absolutely under the inherited
beta<1 bound. For complete Gaussian shell L2 bounds, and any fixed
gamma<1, a hypothesized bound ||F||_[Y,2Y]<=C Y^gamma on all large
dyadic Y would imply

    ||P||_[X,2X]<= C X^gamma/(2^(1-gamma)-1).         (A36)

Conversely a corresponding bound for P yields one for F with constant
factor 1+2^(1-gamma), using (A32). The infinite remainder in this norm
passage is paid by the actual baseline beta; no new bound for P has
been assumed. Summing the known beta estimates in (A35) gives only
the known beta estimate, so finite-prime conditioning has not created
a contraction in exponent.

To place the final term of (A35) strictly below X^gamma, take

    J > [(beta-gamma)/(1-beta)] log_2 X,
    2^J X > X^((1-gamma)/(1-beta))                   (A37)

with a fixed strict coefficient margin; these describe the sufficient
depth and its larger future scale, not a needed lower bound on a
physical error. For beta=.874873 the scale exponent thresholds are
125129/125127=1.000015983760499... at gamma=.874871,
500000/375381=1.331980041611056... at gamma=5/6, and
250000/125127=1.997970062416584... at gamma=3/4.
The helper checks these exact rational values. This is
an UPPER-BUDGET limitation of this iteration, not an energy lower
bound. Unknown cancellation inside the sum in (A35) could improve it;
estimating the entire sum by its signed value is essentially the
unpaid source problem again.

W38 R38.5 concerns the normalized SQUAREFREE occupation law of its
own arithmetic packet. Its proved coordinate laws do not assert joint
independence of chi_2 and this all-integer remaining multiplicative
sign, and they supply no uniform transfer to A_R(dn), coprime pairs,
or the two-height signed detector. Even (A33)'s stronger actual
marginal balance does not pay (A34). A viable reopening condition is
a quantitative estimate on the actual conditional covariance in
(A34), or on a genuinely new regrouping of (A35) with all future-scale
cross terms, below the incumbent power. Simply exposing more small
primes and discarding the corresponding remaining joint signs is not
such an estimate.

### D02.4 An explicit ordinary-Dirichlet return, with a paid width change

Here is a concrete bridge to the rational Gaussian architecture, rather than an identification of different coefficient lists. Fix an ordinary Dirichlet character chi with its actual zero extension, set psi=chi*chi_-3, and let eta(a)=chi(Na). Euler factors give

    L_K(s,eta)=L(s,chi)L(s,psi).                          (2.10)

At a split rational prime the two ideal factors equal the two same-sign Dirichlet factors; at an inert prime the product is (1-chi(p)^2 p^-2s)^-1; at 3 only the chi factor survives. Zeros at primes dividing the presented modulus persist on both sides. This proves the identity without an inferred primitive reduction.

First restore the fixed excluded ideal primes in M_eta,2 by the finite polynomial product_(p in S)(1-eta(p)Np^-s). Its inverse is the corresponding finite product of geometric series, absolutely summable at every positive weight. Thus the restoration has fixed cost and leaves the exponent unchanged. Call the resulting complete field M_eta,2^full.

Fix any delta>0 and put B(s)=1-2^(1-s). Define the **actual periodic** sequence and fixed field

    d_psi(n)=psi(n)-2*1_(2|n) psi(n/2),
    K_psi,delta(y)=sum_(n>=1) d_psi(n) g_delta(log(n/y)).

If psi has period q, d_psi has period 2q and total sum zero over that period, including when psi is principal. Poisson summation of the zero-extended Schwartz function g_delta(log t) on each residue class gives K_psi,delta(y)=O_A(y^-A) for every fixed A as y tends to infinity; the zero Fourier mode vanishes. Its left tail is Gaussian. Equivalently, m integrations by parts bound it by C_(m,q,delta)y^(1-m), with m fixed after A. Consequently

    I_(gamma,psi,delta)=integral_0^infinity |K_psi,delta(y)| y^-gamma dy/y <infinity (2.11)

for every fixed real gamma. The Mellin transform of K is exp(delta*s^2/2)B(s)L(s,psi), first on Re s>1; pole cancellation at s=1 is literal, not asserted away.

The multiplicative integral convolution therefore satisfies

    integral_0^infinity M_eta,2^full(x/y) K_psi,delta(y) dy/y
       = sum_n [mu(n)chi(n)-2*1_(2|n)mu(n/2)chi(n/2)]
                    g_(2+delta)(log(n/x)) =: G_chi,2+delta(x).             (2.12)

This numerator is B(s), not 1-2chi(2)2^-s; the second coefficient is written explicitly to avoid that error. It reduces exactly to current G1 when chi=1, at the permitted fixed width 2+delta. Minkowski and (2.11) give

    ||G_chi,2+delta||_gamma <= I_(gamma,psi,delta) ||M_eta,2^full||_gamma.   (2.13)

All convolution tails and shell dilations are paid. The new width is fixed before X. No inverse heat operation or estimate at width 1 is inferred. Since B has no zero in 0<Re s<1, this is a full conditional ordinary-Dirichlet zero return. The ideal result already covers each fixed finite-order trivial-infinity Hecke target. It does not create a growing-conductor assertion.

This comparison shows a legitimate way easier **complete** estimates from the old principal signal could help the new detector. It says nothing that permits transplanting PR15 local moments to G13, F3 or the short-divisor H form without their missing arithmetic source adapters.

## 5. Local planes, original atlas and all branches

Set q=17/25, Ka=34/21, alpha=1/400000. Let l_j=.034+(j-1)/100000, b_j=l_j+1/100000, j=1,...,600. For each fixed ORIGINAL slot cell choose

    g_j=B-1+(9/2-Lambda)b_j,
    a_j/M=Ka g_j+alpha,
    A_j/M=B-(Lambda-1)l_j.                          (V10)

No amplifier is chosen from live plain scales, profiles, heights, post-extraction widths or a zero bin. This same j is kept through all four scale-recovery profiles. There are finitely many fixed choices, so a maximum of their permitted thresholds preserves quantifier order. Fine slot meshes are chosen below their common positive amplifier and error bounds before the eventual slot list.

For the linear routes define C=5-6rho(q), D=q+C Ka, B0=(1-rho(q)+C Ka)/D=14200/14361. Put B=B0-3/500000 and Lambda=(q+(9/2)C Ka-eta(q))/D. This yields

| Route | B | Lambda |
|---|---:|---:|
| old density | 7099956917/7180500000 | 57614/14361 |
| linear marked plain | 7099956917/7180500000 | 11107910/2771673 |
| nonlinear marked plain | 3124981043/3159500000 | 25362/6319 |

At q all 600 high reserves are equal by exact cancellation of the cell slope. The low reserve is 7/30000000 in every cell and route. The principal changed margins are:

For the nonlinear route, a_delta'>=-15a_q: the positive terms in its logarithmic derivative may be discarded and -12/(5-6delta)>=-15. Also b_delta'>=b'_low, where

Because 0<1-6a_j<1 and z/M<=1/25, subtracting 15a_q and adding b'_low/25 is a valid uniform derivative lower bound. It is positive as recorded. Thus q controls the whole [.68,.70] interval. For every cell the independent calculation keeps the actual correlated A_j,a_j,g_j, particularly in 1-A_j-9a_j. For the highest route the other minima are:

|---|---:|
| valuation-one extracted error a/4-g/6 | 94689089/70772800000 |

The two other receipts retain the corresponding positive values. The actual main ball remains K0+(d-c)_++6a+omega. ## G225. Actual positive cofactor-hole prices, including after integration

Use the full G218 Gaussian over integers or Eisenstein integral ideals,
q_a=a or Na, with fixed eta,tau,S. Put c_a=mu_R(a)eta(a)1_((a,S)=1).
Let S+ add ALL natural-zero primes of the PRESENTED character, including
imprimitive modulus primes. On each entire shell[X,2X], choose arbitrary
nonnegative theta_Q with sum1 on radicals coprime to S, q_Q<=X^A,
fixed A>0. The choices may depend on X and the actual arithmetic source,
but are frozen in x. Define

    p(a)=sum_Q theta_Q 1_((a,Q)=1),
    K_X(a,b)=int_X^(2X)g(log(q_a/x))g(log(q_b/x))dx/x,
    A_theta=sum_(a,b)|Re(c_a conjugate(c_b))|K_X(a,b)p(rad(ab)),
    B_theta=sum_(a,b)|Re(c_a conjugate(c_b))|K_X(a,b)p(a)p(b).
                                                               (225.1)

The first is the average absolute-real Gram price of each hole field;
the second is that price for their averaged field. Both include diagonal
and both off-diagonal orientations. They are not the signed energies.

Uniformly over this entire family,

    X^2/log(2X)^2 << A_theta, B_theta << X^2.                (225.2)

Constants/onsets depend on R,S,eta,tau,A, not theta or Q. The lower bound
survives diagonal removal. This is a corollary of the G218 count and
G221 real-rank bound with a useful logarithmic refinement.

For Q*=rad(S+ Q), D(Q*)=prod_(p|Q*)(1+q_p^-1)^-1 satisfies

    D(Q*)^-1=sum_(d|Q*)q_d^-1
       <=sum_(q_d<=q_Q*)q_d^-1 << log(2q_Q*) << log(2X).

Partial summation of the elementary A_R(T)<<T proves this without PNT.
Subtract the uniform G218 squarefree counts at2X and X. The errors
are O(sqrt X log(2X)S_1/2(Q*)) over ideals and O(sqrt X d(Q*)) over
integers. The elementary small/large-prime split gives each factor sum
<<_delta q_Q*^delta; take delta=1/(4A). Thus errors are
O(X^(3/4)log(2X)), smaller than the main X/log(2X). No Q<=X
restriction is needed. Since g has a positive minimum on[-log2,log2],

    W_Q(x)=sum_a |c_a|1_((a,Q)=1)g(log(q_a/x))
       >>X/log(2X), every x in[X,2X],                     (225.3)

while the complete Gaussian majorant gives W_Q(x)<<x. No character
zero is replaced by a unit phase.

Regard xi_a=c_a/|c_a| as a unit vector in R^2 on its nonzero support.
With positive weights w_a, let M=sum_a w_a xi_a xi_a^T and W=sum_a w_a.
Then

    sum_(a,b)w_a w_b |xi_a dot xi_b|
      >=trace(M^2)>=W^2/2.                               (225.4)

The first step uses |t|>=t^2 on[-1,1]; the second uses two nonnegative
eigenvalues. All ACTUAL Mobius signs and character phases remain.
Apply it first to w_a=|c_a|1_((a,Q)=1)g, average theta and integrate.
Apply it separately to w_a=|c_a|p(a)g, whose mass is sum theta_Q W_Q.
These prove both lower bounds without comparing their kernels. For real
eta the constant1/2 can be1. Truncation, nonnegative convergence and the
Gaussian O(x) majorant justify every infinite sum and the O(X^2) upper bound.

The diagonals are sum_a |c_a|^2 K_X(a,a)p(a) and the same with p(a)^2.
Both are O(X), since0<=p<=1 and the squared Gaussian is a constant times
a narrower Gaussian. Subtracting them preserves(225.2) for large X.
The covariance kernels are not ordered entrywise: theta_1=theta_lm=1/2
gives joint/product1/2,1/4 at a=l,b=m, whereas theta_l=theta_m=1/2
gives0,1/4, for two distinct good primes and sufficiently large X.

For each pair the phase is independent of x and K_X is positive, so
int |Re(c_a conjugate(c_b))|g_a g_b dx/x
=|Re(c_a conjugate(c_b))K_X(a,b)| exactly. Hence taking pairwise real
absolute values AFTER integration gives the same scalar Gaussian price.
This identity does not discard cancellation in a collective signed sum,
extend to oscillatory joint-label kernels, or certify an arbitrary theta
as a zero detector. The latter needs its own complete fixed-source return.
G222's principal deletion-channel Holder floor and G127's different
curved-source obstruction retain their distinct priority and scope.

## 8. Paid sectors and literal f3 depth cancellation

The [actual f3 sector proof]([private research revision]/gaussian-signed/report.md) and
[independent reconstruction]([private research revision]/gaussian-controller-review.md)
now pay a common-factor sector of G31 directly. For each r define
f_r(n)=product_(p|n,p not dividing3r)(-1), retaining every prime power,
and let E_r(Y) be its whole Gaussian squared norm on [Y,2Y]. For any
fixed buffered Mertens exponent beta>1-c3 and every epsilon>0,

    T_>=D(X)=sum_(gcd(m,n)>=D)f3(m)f3(n)K_X(m,n)
      =sum_r [sum_(g|r,g>=D)mu(r/g)]E_r(X/r),
    |T_>=D(X)| << X^(2beta+epsilon)D^(1-2beta).          (G33)

This holds for all real D>=1, including D>X. Its diagonal is the
literal sum_(n>=D)K_X(n,n), paid separately. Hence G31 is equivalent
to its complete low-gcd off-diagonal estimate when
theta>(2beta-2gamma)/(2beta-1) and D=X^theta. The exact remainder is

    Q_<D=2 sum_(1<=g<D) sum_(h>=1) sum_((a,h)=1)
                       f_g(a(a+h))K_(X/g)(a,a+h).       (G34)

Both orders, every shift and all prime powers remain. The high-prime
switch comparison S17–S23 in that report also pays
X^(2beta)P^(1-3beta+epsilon), but the resulting signed energy sum
still contains E_1(X) itself. It supplies no bootstrap. Its low-radical
prime-two ray cancellation is real, but that region already has a
smaller positive cost than the current targets.

The [literal f3 renewal theorem]([private research revision]/f3-renewal/report.md), with
[controller reconstruction]([private research revision]/f3-renewal-controller-review.md),
directly handles a different signed partition. Set

    T_z(x)=sum_(#{p>z:p|n}<=1) f3(n)g_tau(log(n/x)),
    P(z)=product_(5<=p<=z)(p-2)/(p-1), t=log z, L=log X.

Uniformly on X<=x<=2X and 4<=t<=L/(1000log L),

    T_z(x)=3log2 P(z)e^(tau/2) x/(log x)^2
                                  *[1+O_tau(t/L)].    (G35)

The full proof gives its second term and prices all smooth cores,
prime powers, Gaussian tails, fixed-order PNT errors and growing
Taylor constants. Its leading reciprocal smooth mass vanishes at
prime2; the first derivative is positive. This is a direct proof on
the actual f3 coefficients, not an inherited masked convolution bound.
If t tends to infinity and both t,2t remain in range, the literal
added band T_(z^2)-T_z is (-1/2+o(1))T_z. All finite cross-Gram
entries are retained. The uncapped source has an infinite dominated
terminal telescoping identity, not an exact finite cutoff.

For the actual full field F and complement R_z=F-T_z, put
a=||T_z||, b=||R_z|| and rho=Re<T_z,R_z>/(ab). Then exactly

    ||F||^2=(a-b)^2+2ab(1+rho).                        (G36)

The accepted baseline already forces the large prefix and its entire
complement to nearly cancel. A proposed gamma improvement requires
BOTH |a-b|<<X^(gamma+epsilon) and
1+rho<<X^(2gamma-2+epsilon)t^2L^4. A leading asymptotic Gram does not
resolve either quantity at that precision. G35 and its negative bands
give no new full-field power estimate by themselves.

## R4. Protected author S29: exact state, expensive output and full anchored inverse

On squarefree q-units, sorted prime creation satisfies

    T_sigma e_n=sum_(p>P+(n),p not dividing q)chi(p)p^-sigma e_(np),
    ||T_sigma^j||^2 <= S_sigma^j/j!,
    S_sigma=sum_(p not dividing q)p^-2sigma < infinity, sigma>1/2.

The disjoint descendant claim is correct: deleting exactly j largest primes uniquely recovers a parent. Each column's squared mass is bounded by an elementary symmetric sum, hence by S_sigma^j/j!. The operator-norm Neumann series converges and gives v(n)=mu(n)chi(n)n^-sigma. This is the existing B22/G145 construction, not a new stability theorem. Its finite output Lambda_N v=M_chi(N) has

    ||Lambda_N||^2 ~ kappa_q N^(2sigma+1)/(2sigma+1).

The exponent sigma+1/2 exceeds one. Congruence by diag(n^sigma) transports any banded global terminal majorant to precisely the physical certificate considered in R2-R3; no norm factor has been silently lost. The original suspension/dynamical-determinant proposal is not constructed here. The supplied explicit alternative is a source state and a graph observation criterion.

For the connected finite graph of every squarefree q-unit n<=N, join n to np when np is another vertex. With arbitrary positive edge weights, its real Laplacian L has kernel constants. Put U=diag(a_n). Then

    L_a=U L U*,
    x*L_a x=sum_edges w_(n,p)|x_(np)+chi(p)x_n|^2,
    L_a a=0.

The plus sign follows from a_np=-chi(p)a_n; it is not a freely imposed character relation. Connectivity follows by deleting prime divisors. Squareful/nonunit vertices are absent because their original source is zero, not because their equations were inverted.

For lambda,eta>0 let H=lambda L_a+eta e_1e_1*. This is positive definite and a*Ha=eta. Define f=U*ell=conjugate(a), R=S minus {1}, and E=f_R*(L_RR)^(-1)f_R>=0. Then exactly

    ell*H^(-1)ell = |M_chi(N)|^2/eta+E/lambda,
    H>=ell ell* iff |M_chi(N)|^2/eta+E/lambda<=1.      (R4.1)

To verify the conjugations, conjugate H by U and solve (lambda L+eta e_1e_1*)x=f. Summing coordinates gives x_1=(sum f)/eta. Write x=x_1 ell+y, y_1=0. The remaining equations are lambda L_RR y_R=f_R. Pairing with f gives (R4.1); sum f=conjugate(M), which is why the harmonic term is |M|^2. All signed off-diagonal Green terms are in E.

For M!=0, lambda>E and eta>=|M|^2/(1-E/lambda) are necessary and sufficient. For M=0, lambda>=E suffices for any eta>0, including equality. For lambda<E no eta works. N=1 has E=0. The author's edge cases are correct.

This is an exact finite control identity and useful source-specific accounting, extending the earlier harmonic-mode warning. It does not supply a smaller arithmetic premise: increasing lambda can suppress E/lambda but cannot remove |M|^2/eta. A graph gap controls a complementary term, not the harmonic amplitude. A proved source-restricted observer or another signed nonlocal construction remains eligible; arbitrary positive gap arguments are not thereby upgraded to such a proof.

## G121. Exact threshold rank and the complete signed rectangle return

At integer N partition ALL unramified primes<=N into disjoint L,R.
List squarefree L-products u_i<=N and R-products v_j<=N increasingly,
including1. Put T_ij=1_(u_i v_j<=N), alpha_i=mu(u_i)chi(u_i) and
beta_j=mu(v_j)chi(v_j). Unique factorization gives

    M_chi(N)=alpha^T T beta.                              (80.2)

Ramified sites are zero rows/columns, not inverted factors. All retained
phases have modulus1; diagonal multiplication preserves matrix rank and
singular values while the final scalar may still cancel.

Let t_i be the row's prefix length, and0<h_1<...<h_d its distinct positive
values, h_0=0. The exact decomposition is

    T=sum_(ell=1)^d 1_(t_i>=h_ell) 1_(h_(ell-1)<j<=h_ell).

Choosing one row of each length h_i and columns h_j gives the triangular
submatrix L_d=(1_(j<=i)), determinant1. Thus rank T=d. Each length is
a function of floor(N/u_i), giving d<=2 floor(sqrt N). This is an
O(sqrt N) representation, not a polylogarithmic rank or cancellation bound.

L_d^(-1)=I minus a truncated shift has operator norm<=2. Restrict any
rank-r approximation T_r, r<d, to this submatrix and use an orthonormal
basis of its kernel, dimension at least d-r. Every vector has error norm
at least1/2. Hence ||T-T_r||_F^2>=(d-r)/4 and ||T-T_r||_op>=1/2.
Restriction is a contraction for either norm; the same result holds for
the character-weighted tensor. No rank-growth assumption is needed.

If R_N,C_N are the row and column counts, the COMPLETE scalar error is
alpha^T(T-T_r)beta, bounded above by sqrt(R_N C_N)||T-T_r||_op, or
the same factor times the Frobenius norm. Leakage outside uv<=N is part
of this error. The matrix lower bounds are not lower bounds on its signed
scalar contraction. A norm budget tending to zero forces r>=d; no claim
that every prime partition has such a budget or large rank is made.

Contracting the exact decomposition gives

    M_chi(N)=sum_ell [sum_(i:t_i>=h_ell)alpha_i]
                       [sum_(h_(ell-1)<j<=h_ell)beta_j].

Every prime restriction and endpoint is explicit. A selection of rectangles
must bound both its full signed contribution and the entire omitted signed
sum by N^(gamma+epsilon), for all large N/every epsilon/every fixed chi
and common gamma<theta11. Moving partitions need uniform bounds in their
actual choice. Then s integral_1^infinity M_chi(x)x^(-s-1)dx continues
1/L to Re s>gamma, giving ordinary all-height zero exclusion. This uses
the full source, not analytic continuation of the moving tensors.

statement:
## 1. The fixed-compact arithmetic input

Write W(x,y)=sum_(n<=x,P+(n)<=y)mu(n), and let omega be the standard
Buchstab function: omega(u)=0 for u<1, omega(u)=1/u for 1<=u<=2,
and (u*omega(u))'=omega(u-1) for u>2. For every FIXED integer K>=1 and
compact interval I contained in (K+1,infinity), the cited Theorems2--3 imply

    W(x,y)=x sum_(j=1)^K a_j omega^(j)(u)/(log y)^(j+1)
               + O_(I,K)(x/(log y)^(K+2)),                 (1)
    u=log x/log y in I, y->infinity,
    sum_(j>=1) a_j z^j = 1/((1+z)*zeta(1+z)).

This is the entire external friable estimate used here. The coefficient
a1=1 follows from the simple pole of zeta at1. To check applicability:
choose fixed epsilon in (0,1/3) in the source's domain
exp((log x)^(2/3+epsilon))<=y<=x. Fixed u in I satisfies that domain for
large y. I lies above all the exceptional integers1,...,K+1, and hence
satisfies its D_K(log y) condition. The source's additional error is
O(Psi(x,y)/L_epsilon(y)); Psi<=x and L_epsilon grows faster than every
fixed power of log y. The constants are uniform on I, but NOT asserted
uniform when K or I grows with x. No zero-free strip stronger than the
classical input of this published theorem is being imported.

The strict prime cutoff in G92 is handled by y=p-1, exactly, not by
discarding multiples of p. Replacing log(p-1) by log p in a fixed-compact
expansion changes the expression by O_(I,K)(x/(p*(log p)^2)), absorbed in
the remainder in (1).

For any fixed modulus q, let W_q(x,p-)=sum_(n<=x,P+(n)<p,(n,q)=1)mu(n).
Once p exceeds every prime factor of q, the same expansion is

    W_q(x,p-)=x sum_(j=1)^K b_(j,q) omega^(j)(u)/(log p)^(j+1)
                  +O_(I,K,q)(x/(log p)^(K+2)),             (2)
    sum_(j>=1)b_(j,q)z^j = A_q(1+z)/((1+z)*zeta(1+z)),
    A_q(s)=product_(ell|q)(1-ell^(-s))^(-1),
    b_(1,q)=A_q(1)=q/phi(q), u=log x/log p.

Proof of this finite-modulus extension: exactly
W_q(x,p-)=sum_(d:q-smooth)W(x/d,p-), with W(t,p-)=0 for t<1.
The local factor at a prime dividing q cancels by convolution; repeated
powers in d are necessary. Truncate d at D=(log p)^B. For fixed q and
any 0<eta<1, sum_(q-smooth d>D)1/d <=D^(-eta) A_q(1-eta), so the discarded
part is O_q(x D^(-eta)). Choose B to absorb the desired fixed logarithmic
error. On d<=D, log d/log p tends uniformly to0; apply (1) on a slightly
larger fixed compact, and Taylor-expand each omega derivative. The convergent
moments sum_(q-smooth d)(log d)^l/d identify the coefficients with the
Taylor product in (2). The Taylor remainders are paid by the next convergent
fixed logarithmic moment; the required derivatives are bounded on the
chosen compact neighborhood. Thus (2) preserves natural zeros at all primes dividing q.
It is a PRINCIPAL-character statement. No corresponding main term for a
nonprincipal character is asserted.

### D33.1 Actual local signs and their complete-period law

For finite P containing 2 and excluding 3, let

    Q=product_(p in P)p,
    e_P(n)=product_(p in P)(-1)^(1_(p|n)),
    W_P(x)=sum_(n>=1)e_P(n)g_tau(log(n/x)).

These are f3's ACTUAL local signs at the listed primes: every positive p-adic valuation gives -1. The function e_P is Q-periodic, including n=0 in a complete period. Chinese remainder factorization gives exactly

    Q^-1 sum_(n mod Q)e_P(n)=product_(p in P)(1-2/p)=0,
    Q^-1 sum_(n mod Q)e_P(n)e_P(n+h)
       =product_(p in P) c_p(h),
    c_p(h)=1 if p|h; c_p(h)=1-4/p otherwise.            (D33.1)

For p not dividing h exactly the two distinct residues n=0,-h contribute -1 and the other p-2 contribute +1; for p|h both signs are equal at each residue. This proves the formula with no heuristic independence of actual integers outside the completed period. The p=2 factor is -1 for odd h and +1 for even h. The natural p=3 exemption is literal. Both prime powers and h=0 are included.

For P={2,5,7}, all 70 shifts were checked exactly with rational arithmetic. This is an arithmetic periodic identity, not a bound for f3(n)f3(n+h): multiplying the true rough-prime factors before averaging changes the measure and destroys the completed-period factorization.

The marginal-only optimization has a complementary decisive test. Keep every small-prime divisibility pattern fixed, but permit a free hidden rough sign r(n) in {+1,-1}. Choosing r(n)=e_P(n) makes e_P(n)r(n)=1 while preserving ALL observed patterns. For a positive Gaussian Gram this attains the magnitude-only maximum; sum_n g_tau(log(n/x))=x exp(tau/2)+O_tau(1) has norm of order X. Those constraints cannot certify gamma<1. This assignment is NOT the actual arithmetic rough sign and need not obey its prime-deletion relations. Controlling that dependence is the missing arithmetic input. ### Two delay channels: local division versus a finite-height floor

For the complete fixed Gaussian field with Mellin transform
exp(tau s squared/2)/L(s,chi), physical dilation
D_lambda U(x)=U(x)-lambda^beta U(x/lambda) has multiplier
m_lambda(s)=1-lambda^(beta-s). Complete every-epsilon shell L2 bounds
of exponent gamma on lambda=2,3 give holomorphic channel transforms to
Re(s)>gamma, retaining the complete source and Gaussian left tail.

The multipliers have just one common zero, s=beta, simple for each.
Consequently these bounds exclude zeros in the target half-plane except
possibly a simple real zero at beta. A multiple zero still leaves a pole.
Independently excluding beta or adding another paid channel closes that
exception. Local division away from beta needs no global positive floor.
This retains the [principal Gaussian return](../[private research revision]/principal-gaussian-integration.md)
and [G109 bank analysis, including its G47 exception](../[private research revision]/sol04-integration.md).

Simultaneous recurrence prevents any all-height positive floor for a fixed
positive weighted sum of the squared multipliers. A finite-height replacement
is available. With kappa=log(2)log(3)/(2pi), 0<t0<=|t|<=T,

    max(|m_2(beta+it)|,|m_3(beta+it)|)
      >= min(2t0 log(3)/pi,
             4exp(-kappa T)/((log(2)+log(3))sqrt(3))).

For t>0 choose nearest nonnegative integers k,l to t log(2)/(2pi),
t log(3)/(2pi). If both vanish, the larger phase error is at least
t0 log(3). Otherwise 3^k and2^l are distinct integers, so the logarithmic
gap is at least exp(-kappa T)/sqrt(3). Combining the two phase errors and
2|sin(e/2)|>=2|e|/pi for |e|<=pi proves the bound; symmetry covers t<0.
The exponential price is deliberately coarse and yields no arithmetic
channel bound or uniform limit as T increases.

The retained weighted-degree and hidden-tail examples are narrowly scoped:
exp(i sin(t)) with weight A(1+epsilon cos(t)) has weighted crossing total
2A epsilon despite degree zero; exp(rho v)1_(v>=A) has Laplace transform
exp(-(s-rho)A)/(s-rho). Neither is a counterexample for actual native H or
an all-scale Möbius invariant. They identify unpaid weighted amplitude
and tail-continuation assumptions only.

statement:
## 3. B/S24: a complete residue-class rank-matching criterion

Fix q. For each reduced residue a mod q, list in increasing order

    u_(a,k): integers n==a mod q with mu(n)=+1,
    v_(a,k): integers n==a mod q with mu(n)=-1.

Zero Mobius values and nonunits are omitted from the lists, but their zero extensions are retained in every arithmetic sum. For fixed1/2<gamma<1 the following three statements are equivalent, with constants allowed to depend on q and gamma:

1. For every ordinary character chi mod q, M_chi(x)=O(x^gamma).
2. For every reduced residue a, M_(q,a)(x)=sum_(n<=x,n==a(q))mu(n)=O(x^gamma).
3. Both lists are infinite and their monotone rank matching satisfies |u_(a,k)-v_(a,k)|=O(k^gamma) for every a and all k.       (B1)

The equivalence also holds with the usual every-positive-epsilon loss. Thus a proof of the displacement bound with gamma<theta11 for every fixed q would imply the requested ordinary-character zero exclusion, while the q=1 case includes zeta. This is a direct summatory criterion; it makes no assertion that a short finite matching proves an asymptotic bound.

Proof of1<->2. The exact finite character Fourier identities are

    M_chi=sum_(a reduced)chi(a)M_(q,a),
    M_(q,a)=(1/phi(q))sum_(chi mod q)conj(chi(a))M_chi.

They retain principal, imprimitive and complex characters. This direction requires all characters of one fixed q, not one chosen nonreal character alone.

For2->3, the squarefree count in a reduced residue obeys the elementary formula

    Q_(q,a)(x)=d_q x+O_q(sqrt x),
    d_q=[q*zeta(2)]^(-1) product_(p|q)(1-p^-2)^(-1)>0.   (B2)

Indeed use mu(n)^2=sum_(d^2|n)mu(d). Since a is a unit, only(d,q)=1 contributes; each progression m==a*d^(-2) mod q has count x/(q d^2)+O(1). Summing at mostsqrt x errors and completing the absolutely convergent d^-2 tail proves (B2). Therefore the positive and negative counting functions equal d_q x/2+O_q(x^gamma). Inverting these monotone counting functions gives

    u_(a,k)=2k/d_q+O_q(k^gamma),
    v_(a,k)=2k/d_q+O_q(k^gamma),

and both sequences are infinite. This establishes3 with every endpoint accounted for.

For3->2, pair every u_(a,k) with v_(a,k). At cutoff x the difference of counts is exactly the signed number of pairs crossing x. A crossing pair has k<=x because its lower endpoint is an increasing positive-integer sequence. Its length is at mostC_q x^gamma, so its lower endpoint lies in(x-C_q x^gamma,x]. Distinct pairs have distinct lower endpoints. There are at mostC_q x^gamma+1 integers in this interval, proving2. No infinite series is rearranged: the two counts at each x are finite.

An exact check on the forward reasoning: if u_k<v_k within one residue, then

    Q(v_k)-Q(u_k)=M(v_k)+M(u_k),                         (B3)

because P(u_k)=k and N(v_k)=k. Both terms on the right are nonnegative. The reversed orientation has the corresponding negative signs. Thus the geometric gap is paid by the actual signed discrepancy plus the O(sqrt x) squarefree-density remainder. It is not controlled by density alone.

For a finite cutoff N, the algorithm pairs ranks only through min(P_a(N),N_a(N)); its unpaired count is exactly |M_(q,a)(N)|. Dropping those end ranks would delete precisely the arithmetic quantity needing control. Within two finite equal-sized ordered lists, monotone matching minimizes the largest edge length: uncrossing two reversed pairs cannot increase the larger distance. This elementary fact does not give a new bound on the resulting arithmetic distance.

Contact and novelty: G65 already derives monotone matching costs from an inherited summatory exponent for a Gaussian feature metric, with full ghost mass. W22 already prices ordinary-Mobius transport and its total-mass debt; G76/G94 explain why prime-toggle matchings leave a linear unsigned boundary. B supplies a clean two-sided l-infinity criterion simultaneously for all ordinary characters of a fixed q, with a self-contained squarefree-progression proof. It does not improve the previous cost or claim a new matching theorem in the literature. The next mathematical input is an actual uniform power saving for these rank displacements, or a different globally coherent pairing with a proved comparable crossing bound.
title: 3. B/S24: a complete residue-class rank-matching criterion

statement:
### Exact coalescence of all product coincidences

Define
\[
A_Y(q)=\sum_{\substack{de=q\\d,e>Y}}\mu(d)\mu(e),\qquad
\beta_X(n)=\sum_{\substack{\ell\mid n\\\ell\le J}}
w_X(n/\ell)A_Y(n/\ell).
\]
Then \(\mathcal B_X(x)=\sum_n\beta_X(n)\phi(n/x)\) exactly.
The coefficient \(A_Y(q)\) vanishes unless \(q\) is cube-free. Otherwise
write uniquely \(q=g^2k\), where \(g,k\) are coprime squarefree integers.
Every nonzero factorization is \(d=ga,e=gb\), \(ab=k\). Consequently
\[
\boxed{A_Y(g^2k)=\mu(k)
\sum_{a\mid k}1_{\{Y/g<a<gk/Y\}}.} \tag{AD1}
\]
This is an exact shared-prime formula, not a replacement by coprimality.
The repeated prime signs cancel, while their square factors remain.

Retain T09's full kernel
\[
K_X(m,n)=\int_X^{2X}\phi(m/x)\phi(n/x)\,\frac{dx}{x}.
\]
With \(A=m+n\), \(B=m^{-1}+n^{-1}\), put
\(I_\nu=\int_X^{2X}x^{\nu-1}e^{-A/x-Bx}\,dx\). Direct multiplication
of the two actual profiles gives
\[
K_X(m,n)=mnI_{-2}-AI_{-1}
 +(1-m/n-n/m)I_0+BI_1+(mn)^{-1}I_2. \tag{AD2}
\]
The endpoints are unchanged. In particular, the kernel has no short-shift
support. Products and shifts of order \(X\) remain.

The complete energy is exactly
\[
E_B(X)=\sum_n\beta_X(n)^2K_X(n,n)
 +2\sum_{h\ge1}\sum_n\beta_X(n)\beta_X(n+h)K_X(n,n+h).
\]
Since \(|\beta_X(n)|\le d_3(n)\), \(d_3(n)^2\le d_9(n)\), and the
profile decays exponentially at both ends, divisor counting and partial
summation prove
\[
\boxed{\sum_n\beta_X(n)^2K_X(n,n)
\ll X(\log(2X))^8.} \tag{AD3}
\]
For completeness, the local inequality used here is
\(\binom{j+2}{2}^2\le\binom{j+8}{8}\). It holds at \(j=0\);
the ratio of successive right/left quotients is
\((j+9)(j+1)/(j+3)^2\ge1\). Multiplicativity proves the divisor
inequality. The estimate pays all coincidences \(\ell de=mf g\),
including distinct factorizations, rather than only identical triples.
title: Exact coalescence of all product coincidences

## 2. Local proof and the delicate transfers

Set A=n1+n2+z, a=M/2000, sigma=3a and
g=(n1+n2+(9/2)z-M)_+. The geometry gives g<=M/12500 and
A<=44753M/50000. The amplifier cost is paid by fixed margins.

After both source transformations, low-zero rows have buffered parameter
at most7/10. Only now, within the resulting positive child energy, remove
enough slots to fit the old capacity. Their lost squared-norm exponent
is paid by the7/10 zero bound. Enlarge the already restricted positive
sum and apply the old moment; use the unrestricted zero-slot theorem
if the selected set becomes empty. Actual transformed widths may be
negative and are treated before clipping, using the appropriate monotone
bound. The resulting reserve is4M/225000.

For high-zero rows, the complete signed integer row is

    w=u0 e F G V h'.                                      (L2)

The two coefficient residues are1+t and1-t modulo6, and residue zero
means a coprimality hole, not the constant character1. Both transforms,
whole-character conjugation and the fixed unit factor are retained.
The first projector divides the second common parts and w. The second
projector need not divide w; its full label/scalar cost is paid instead.

Reciprocity phases, unit phases and allowed relative characters belong
to one fixed finite ray group. Keep distinct parent translates separate
for eligibility and zero maxima. The natural row constructor, rather
than an unconstrained abstract representative, gives conductor<=K Nw
with fixed K. Common Euler holes are paid separately and never absorbed
into a falsely fixed conductor.

The unmarked density, derived from the accepted empty-slot moment,
inverse moment and actual supported witness, has exponent

    rho(delta)=1-10delta/[3(5-2delta)],  .7<=delta<=.75.

Its threshold is chosen before all heights. Joint reconstruction counts
the actual row and first labels together, including missing radical and

W=M-R-(c-d)_++L_c-6a and L_c<=5(R-R0). This is a joint count, not a
density statement multiplied by an unpriced label multiplicity.
The complete high-row branch has a fixed negative margin below-M/100.

The exact main radius is K0+(d-c)_++6a+omega. The successive transform
error reserves are13M/120000,193M/120000 and119M/60000. The exceptional
maximum is A-M; its exact first expression contains-4a, while-5a is only

The common mesh follows from uniform numerical reserves over the compact

## 2. Both moving coprimality masks, exactly

For M (2.14)--(2.15), write `N1=c B^3`, `N2=e E^3`. The coefficient is
\[
\beta(c)\overline{\beta(e)}
\vartheta_c(k)\overline{\vartheta_e(k)}
\xi(B)\overline{\xi(E)}q_Bq_E.
\]
M (2.8) explicitly excludes an extra cube/row nonunit mask.
Total-column coprimality is exactly
\[
(c,e)=(c,E)=(e,B)=(B,E)=1.
\tag{DC5}
\]
There is no condition `(c,B)=1` or `(e,E)=1`.

Put `X_c=(D/q_c)^(1/3)` and `Y_e=(D/q_e)^(1/3)`. For the original
common column profile `W0`, define
\[
\begin{aligned}
S_z^-(X)&=\sum_b\xi(b)q_b(q_b/X)^{3z}
  \overline{W_0((q_b/X)^3)},\\
S_z^+(X)&=\sum_b\overline{\xi(b)}q_b(q_b/X)^{3z}
  W_0((q_b/X)^3).
\end{aligned}
\]
The original profile and its required Euler derivatives decrease
rapidly at both endpoints. Uniformly on every fixed compact interval
of `Re z`, the fixed angular argument gives
\[
|S_z^\pm(X)|
\ll_A(1+|\Im z|)^{C_A}\min(X^A,X^{-A}).
\tag{DC6}
\]
See [CS8](../[private research revision]-continuation/cubic-sectors.md) and
[T01](../[private research revision]/[restricted mathematical source]).
The auxiliary column Mellin functions are the fixed entire
`L^S(w-1,xi)` and `L^S(w-1,bar xi)`. Their shifts are residue-free;
the profile transform's vertical translation costs only a polynomial
in `Im z`. No moving deleted angular function is used in (DC6).

Open `(B,E)=1`, write `B=ell b`, `E=ell f`, and then open the two
remaining masks `(b,e)=1`, `(f,c)=1`. The exact column expression is
\[
\begin{aligned}
T_{c,e}(z)=\sum_{(\ell,ce)=1}\mu(\ell)q_\ell^2
&\left[\sum_{r\mid e}\mu(r)\xi(r)q_r
S_z^-\!\left(\frac{X_c}{q_\ell q_r}\right)\right]\\
{}\times&\left[\sum_{s\mid c}\mu(s)\overline{\xi(s)}q_s
S_z^+\!\left(\frac{Y_e}{q_\ell q_s}\right)\right].
\end{aligned}
\tag{DC7}
\]
The `ell` angular factors cancel. Both factors in (DC7) have the
**same complex `z`**. They are not replaced by an absolute square.
The residual cubes may overlap their own squarefree cores.

statement:
## A13. Jacobi identities and the quadratic/triple construction

For odd squarefree \(n\), unit \(v\bmod n\), and every frequency \(t\), including nonunits, put
\[
J_n(t;v)=\sum_{x\bmod n}\chi_n(x(v-x))e_n(tx).
\]
Substitute \(x=vy\) and apply QD (1), then scale the unit Kloosterman variable:
\[
J_n(t;v)
=\chi_n(-1)e_n(tv/2)S(1,t^2v^2/16;n)
=\chi_n(-1)e_n(tv/2)S(v^2,t^2/16;n).
\]
Nonunit \(v\) is outside this rescaling identity. The two visible squared parameters do not form two unconstrained dense intervals, and generic squareful moduli are excluded.

For a nontrivial cubic character \(\theta\) over a good residue field of size \(Q\), extended by zero, define
\[
J_\theta(t)=\sum_x\theta(x)\overline{\theta(1-x)}\psi(tx).
\]
The map \(v=x/(1-x)\) is a bijection from \(x\ne1\) to \(v\ne-1\). Thus
\[
J_\theta(t)=\sum_{v\ne-1}\theta(v)
\psi\!\left(\frac{tv}{1+v}\right),\quad
J_\theta(0)=-1,\quad
\sum_t|J_\theta(t)|^2=Q(Q-2).
\]
The zero value follows from the complete character sum and \(\theta(-1)=1\); Parseval gives the energy since exactly \(Q-2\) original coefficients have modulus one. Products of the good squarefree zero modes encode Möbius, but replacing one mode by all Fourier modes incurs the displayed large positive energy.

The proposed quadratic-twisted triple identity is algebraically consistent:
\[
\psi_u(cB^3)=\psi_u(c)\psi_u(B)
\]
for a quadratic \(\psi_u\), including its zeros. If an actual triple source realizes that total-index twist with the correct normalizations, its absolute-chamber Mellin series would be
\[
J_r(s)\frac{L^S(3s-3/2,\xi_{\rm ang}\psi_u)}
{L^S(s,\psi_u)}.
\]
No complete twisted source/current construction or conductor-uniform restriction estimate is supplied. Cubic rows evaluated on squares do not create quadratic characters. [BB R14; QD; [restricted research revision] Z13–Z18.]

Gemini's claimed prime-square identity is false: its proposed right side simplifies to \(S(1,4p^2;n)\), not \(\chi_n(p^2)\). At \(n=5,p=2\), it equals \((3-\sqrt5)/2\), whereas \(\chi_5(4)=1\). To check the value exactly, the Kloosterman sum is \(2+e_5(2)+e_5(3)=2+2\cos(4\pi/5)=(3-\sqrt5)/2\).
title: A13. Jacobi identities and the quadratic/triple construction

statement:
### 3.1 Rare replacements and all fixed-character calibration

Let epsilon_p be independent Steinhaus variables, and independently let I_p be Bernoulli with mean p^(beta-1). Initially set v_p = 1 if I_p = 1 and v_p = epsilon_p otherwise. Set

    a(n) = mu(n)^2 product_{p|n} v_p,

then delete primes dividing q and impose the finite prescribed values. The resulting function is multiplicative, a(1)=1, and

    |a(n)| = mu(n)^2 1_{(n,q)=1}.

It is not completely multiplicative. These are the actual natural zero conditions, not a squarefree replacement inside a completely multiplicative claim.

Write P = {p : I_p = 1}. For every b > beta,

    E sum_{p in P} p^(-b) = sum_p p^(-(b+1-beta)) < infinity.

A nonnegative random variable with finite expectation is finite almost surely. Intersect over rational b > beta; comparison then supplies every real b > beta. In particular, the reciprocal sum over P is finite. Choosing rational beta < b < 1 also gives

    # {p in P : p <= x} <= x^b sum_{p in P} p^(-b) = O_b(x^b).

For the unmodified source a0(n) = mu(n)^2 product epsilon_p, distinct squarefree integers give distinct Steinhaus monomials and hence are orthogonal in L2. Non-squarefree terms vanish. Multiplication by any fixed ordinary character psi preserves this orthogonality and does not increase the diagonal variances. The deterministic n=1 term is also orthogonal to all other monomials.

The dyadic maximal inequality used by the author needs no independence between the integer-indexed coefficients. Every initial segment of [1,2^k] is a disjoint union of at most k+1 standard dyadic blocks. Cauchy bounds its squared sum by (k+1) times the sum of squared sums over those blocks; enlarging to every block on every level has expected value at most (k+1)2^k. Therefore

    E max_{m <= 2^k} |sum_{n <= m} a0(n) psi(n)|^2
        <= (k+1)^2 2^k.

Markov at 2^(k(1/2+eta)) produces a summable series in k for every eta > 0. Borel--Cantelli and interpolation between dyadic endpoints prove

    sum_{n <= x} a0(n) psi(n) = O_{eta,psi}(x^(1/2+eta)).

Ordinary characters are countable: there are finitely many for each positive modulus. Intersect over all of them and rational eta > 0. Smaller rational eta recover every requested real accuracy exponent. No conductor-uniform constant is obtained or required.

The local quotient at a changed prime, with z = p^(-s), is exactly

    (1+v z)/(1+epsilon z)
      = 1 + sum_{j>=1} (v-epsilon)(-epsilon)^(j-1) z^j.

Its nonconstant coefficients have modulus at most 2. It defines a multiplicative convolution coefficient d with a = a0*d and, for b > beta,

    sum_n |d(n)| n^(-b)
      <= C_{b,F} product_{p in P} (1 + 2 p^(-b)/(1-p^(-b))) < infinity.

Finite deletions and prescribed changes multiply this by finitely many convergent factors for b > 0. Since an ordinary character is completely multiplicative, including its zero values,

    a psi = (a0 psi) * (d psi).

Choose 1/2+eta < b. Applying the preceding bound to x/m >= 1 and enlarging its exponent to b gives an upper bound C x^b sum_m |d(m)|m^(-b). For any epsilon > 0, choose b in (beta,beta+epsilon). Thus every fixed twist satisfies O_{epsilon,psi}(x^(beta+epsilon)). This supplies, in particular, any weaker summatory calibration exponent strictly between beta and b6. Abel summation also gives the claimed O((1+|t|)x^(beta+epsilon)) for the additional n^(it) twist, and fixed logarithmic derivatives cost another arbitrarily small power. This does not assert uniformity for a growing family of characters.
title: 3.1 Rare replacements and all fixed-character calibration

statement:
## 5. The unpartitioned hard target and exact return costs

For the full, unpartitioned coefficient, the accepted G33/S10 signed
high-gcd estimate and its true diagonal subtraction give, for D>=1,

    Q_off=Q_<D+O_epsilon(X^(2beta+epsilon)D^(1-2beta)).       (R21)

This estimate is not transferred to rough or arbitrary signed
submasks. The true high-gcd diagonal fits its size: if D<=X, its
O(X) total is at most X^(2beta)D^(1-2beta); if D>X, a Gaussian
weighted tail bound supplies the same inequality. Thus the separately
paid diagonal in the cited source does not leave a large-D gap.

Write m=ga, n=g(a+h), where g=gcd(m,n), h>=1 and (a,h)=1.
Using R13 and coprimality, the exact full off-diagonal identity is

    Q_<D=2 sum_(1<=g<D)sum_(h>=1)sum_((a,h)=1)
                          f_g(a(a+h))K_(X/g)(a,a+h).       (R22)

The kernel rescales exactly, with no extra factor g. For any ordered
threshold piece (i,j), its summand has the bracket

    A_i(ga)A_j(g(a+h))+A_i(g(a+h))A_j(ga).                 (R23)

The masks and I_X are evaluated on the ORIGINAL integers. Their
threshold is kappa sqrt(X), not kappa sqrt(X/g). For i=j, R23 is
twice the product. The full partition sums all ordered (i,j), so
TR and RT both occur even though the symmetric scalars are equal.
Summing all four brackets gives the factor two in R22.

For every g, remove primitive h<=H using R11 at Y=X/g. This costs

    C XH sum_(g<D)1/g <= C XH log(2D).                     (R24)

The original window costs O(X^-4) once in the whole scalar: the
original pair has a unique gcd, so there is no duplicate tail cost
to sum over g. Define Q_hard by R22 with h>H and both original
integers in I_X. Then

    Q_off=Q_hard+O_epsilon(X^(2beta+epsilon)D^(1-2beta)
                            +XH log(2D)+X^-4).            (R25)

To return to ||F||^2 add the true full diagonal
Delta(X)=sum_n K_X(n,n)=O_tau(X) exactly once. Delta is unrelated
to the p=q completion diagonal R4.

For D=X^theta, H=X^alpha, gamma>1/2 and the strict inequalities

    theta>(2beta-2gamma)/(2beta-1),  theta>=0,
    0<=alpha<2gamma-1,                                    (R26)

the complementary errors lie below X^(2gamma), after taking
epsilon smaller than the fixed margins. In the author's improvement
targets gamma<beta, so R26 automatically forces theta>0. The
one-sided bound Q_hard<=C_epsilon X^(2gamma+epsilon), for every
epsilon>0 on all sufficiently large dyadic shells, is equivalent
to the unpaid full f3 Gaussian target with those parameters. It is
an upper bound on the complete signed scalar; no absolute or
separate-piece estimate is silently substituted.

For the three displayed targets, the accepted G30 reconciliation
cost O_epsilon(X^(1.3749+epsilon)) is below X^(2gamma). The full
G25--G31 interface already pays the outer prime-power convolution,
finite caps, local product diagonals and both independent heights.
The present obstruction supplies no improved estimate for that
interface. A successful new full scalar estimate would still have
to enter it with its exact signs and scale.

I checked the author's c2-only budgets as exact rational arithmetic:

| gamma | theta | alpha | high-gcd exponent | margin below 2gamma | short-shift margin |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| .874871 | .000006 | .749740 | 1.749741501524 | .000000498476 | .000002 |
| 5/6 | .111 | .66 | 1.666524194 | 213709/1500000000 | 1/150 |
| 3/4 | .334 | .49 | 1.499330836 | 167291/250000000 | 1/100 |

These are budgets for returning a hypothetical bound, not a proof of
the hard scalar bound. The first line remains a historical c2 target;
it cannot be promoted as a gain over c4. The other displayed targets
remain open. All uses of beta have a fixed buffer, never equality
at a zero-free boundary.

statement:
## R42.4. Ordinary characters: the convolution and width change are paid

Let chi be an ordinary Dirichlet character with its presented-modulus zeros, psi=chi*chi_-3 and eta(a)=chi(Na). The Euler identity

    L_K(s,eta)=L(s,chi)L(s,psi)                         (R42.7)

is valid with those zeros: split primes give two chi factors, inert primes give (1-chi(p)^2 p^-2s)^-1, and the ramified prime3 gives only the chi factor. Primes excluded by chi's modulus vanish on both sides. This establishes the norm-pullback subfamily; it does not say every ideal character is such a pullback.

Restoring the extra finite set S multiplies 1/L_K^S by product_S(1-eta(p)Np^-s). Its inverse is a finite geometric convolution with finite positive-weight coefficient norm. The restored field U^full therefore costs a fixed constant at every positive exponent. For fixed delta>0 define

    d_psi(n)=psi(n)-2*1_(2|n)psi(n/2),
    K_delta(y)=sum_n d_psi(n)g_delta(log(n/y)),
    B(s)=1-2^(1-s).

If psi has period q then d_psi has period2q and mean zero: the first sum over2q is twice the sum overq, exactly canceled by the even term. This includes principal psi. Extend f(t)=g_delta(log t) by zero for t<=0; f is Schwartz, including at0. Poisson summation on each residue class gives a zero k=0 mode. For every integer m>1 the remaining Fourier series is bounded by C_(m,q,delta)y^(1-m) for y>=1, because |hat f(xi)|<=C_m(1+|xi|)^-m. The left tail is Gaussian by direct absolute summation. Hence

    integral_0^infinity |K_delta(y)|y^-sigma dy/y<infinity (R42.8)

for every fixed real sigma. No unproved reciprocal bound or inverse smoothing is hidden here.

On an absolute Mellin line, K_delta has transform exp(delta s^2/2)B(s)L(s,psi). Both fields are absolutely Mellin integrable there; Fubini and unique inversion give

    integral U^full_eta,2(x/y)K_delta(y)dy/y
     = sum_n [mu(n)chi(n)-2*1_(2|n)mu(n/2)chi(n/2)]
                       g_(2+delta)(log(n/x)).           (R42.9)

All coefficient zeros and the actual second term survive. The numerator is B(s), **not** 1-2chi(2)2^-s. Weighted Minkowski with R42.8 proves the same exponent at fixed width2+delta. This is a forward transfer from the appropriate ideal target to the ordinary detector; it is not a converse from one ordinary character to all Hecke characters, and it supplies no width1 estimate. B has no zero in 0<Re s<1, so the ordinary zero-return there is complete at all heights; the already known right boundary/Euler half-plane handles Re s>=1.
title: R42.4. Ordinary characters: the convolution and width change are paid
