## R8. A further parameter-robustness consequence

The review gives a small additional source corollary: the same R16 and the same residual box hold for every fixed t in [11/10,33/25], chosen before rows and witnesses, with lambda=1/2500. This is a useful range statement, not a new density saving.

Indeed J_t increases with t because q>0, so the endpoint certificate at 33/25 pays every smaller such t. The marginal A,C do not depend on t. Throughout this interval A<.94<11/10<=t<=33/25<C, which is exactly what the two presentation constraints need in R5. The gap C-(t+lambda) is smallest at t=33/25, so R13 and all cutoff-removal costs remain valid. The prefix proof uses inverse dyads of exponent at least t-o(1)>1, and the completed identity permits every such fixed t. All resulting residual lengths and marginal moment bounds are unchanged. Constants can be selected for the chosen fixed t; no live row is allowed to choose a new truncation.

This shows that the useful residual predicate does not depend on a delicate numerical optimization of t=1.32. It also explains why merely moving the cutoff farther inside this interval does not solve the remaining simultaneous estimate.

statement:
## 6. Identity readout, finite phase limits, and residues

Put A=chi2(p)Q, z=Q^-s and u=Q^(it). For radial integral inputs the actual normalized coefficient functional is

    J_s(phi)=sum_(k>=0) B_k z^k phi(pi^k).

It is absolutely convergent for bounded phi on O and Re(s)>1/2. Negative valuations are invisible to the two source slots by (W). The squarefree input gives J_s(1_O-1_pi²O)=1-z. Its Fourier-fixed exterior completion

    (1+Q^-2)1_O-1_pi²O-Q^-2 1_pi^-2O

has the same readout. Thus the existing exterior repair is genuinely exact at the coefficient level.

For a finite phase input

    a_(u,2J)=sum_(j=0)^(J-1) u^j(1_pi^(2j)O-1_pi^(2j+2)O),
    E(a)=a+Fourier(a)-(integral a)1_O,

every E(a_(u,2J)) is Schwartz, Fourier-fixed, and has value and integral zero. Fourier involution holds on these even radial functions; its value at zero is integral a, and integral Fourier(a)=a(0)=0. On O the Fourier term is constant integral a, hence E(a)|O=a. Consequently

    J_s(E a_(u,2J))=(1-z)sum_(j=0)^(J-1)(Au z²)^j.          (P_J)

These vectors converge in local L2 to E(a_u), where a_u(pi^k)=u^floor(k/2). For Re(s)>1/2 the displayed coefficient sums converge to

    J_s(E a_u)=(1-z)/(1-Au z²).                              (P)

The meromorphic continuation has poles at chi2(p)u Q^(1-2s0)=1, all on Re(s0)=1/2, with residues

    (1-Q^-s0)/(2 log Q).

They are nonzero, with absolute value between (1-Q^-1/2)/(2log Q) and (1+Q^-1/2)/(2log Q). At u=1 the Hilbert limit is 1_O, although every finite E(a_(1,2J)) has value zero at the origin. The point-value functional is not L2-continuous. This is an explicit reason that finite-stage boundary conditions and selected Hilbert-tensor convergence do not prove approximation-uniform limiting boundary cancellation. For u!=1, a_u has no specified pointwise limit at zero; assigning a point value to an L2 representative cannot fix that problem.

This counterexample concerns the defined arithmetic Mellin readout, not the still-undefined H-divisor germ. It neither proves that the latter survives nor that it vanishes. Its poles at 1/2 also do not prohibit a bound at .874864. The precise demand is a continuous or uniformly controlled actual germ map on the selected approximation space.

For u!=v, subtracting (P) gives

    (1-z)A z²(u-v)/((1-Au z²)(1-Av z²)).

The phase direction is nonzero, and its derivative at t=0 is i log(Q)(1-z)A z²/(1-Az²)². Distinct u have disjoint pole sets, so a finite linear combination with s-independent coefficients cannot cancel all their poles unless all coefficients vanish. In particular it cannot retain the constant coefficient 1 and become 1-z. Positive continuous scalar averaging achieves that only with Haar measure on the phase circle: all positive Fourier moments must vanish, their negative counterparts are conjugate, and Fourier uniqueness applies. Averaging Nth roots leaves (1-z)/(1-(Az²)^N). These claims concern local scalar recombination. They do not invalidate a retained phase vector with moving auxiliary numerator or prove finite rank impossible for a different relative map.

statement:
## 6. The joint plane and its precise strict-ledger limitation

Let S=(n1+n2)/M and t=z/M. When the actual old-capacity defect `g/M=S+(9/2)t-1` is positive, eliminating the amplifier at the low-reserve boundary `a/M=(7/3)(g/M)` turns the high reserve at delta=.7 into

`35/54-(7/10)(S+t)-(182/27)(S+(9/2)t-1)`.

Multiplying by 270 gives exactly

**`1995-2009S-8379t`**.

Thus the underlying necessary joint condition for these two strictly positive reserves is `2009S+8379t<1995`, in the positive-defect regime. This is not intrinsically a constant-capacity inequality. It is an actual geometric constraint, not a mixture of incompatible extrema.

For the cap S<=2N and capacity S+Ct<=1, write b=1-2N. Suppose the crossing t*=b/C lies inside the useful slot window. At that crossing, S=2N and g/M=(9/2-C)t*>0 for C<9/2. The strict plane is equivalent to

`C > 8379b/(2009b-14)`,

provided 2009b-14>0. For N=4223/10000 this gives

```
Ccrit=930069/212999=4.366541626955995...,
rcrit=56853/425998,
tcrit=212999/5985000=.0355888053467...,
(a/M)crit=6317/570000.
```

The point n1=n2=NM is literally permitted and tcrit lies between .034 and .04. At equality both low and high reserves vanish; increasing a makes high negative, decreasing it makes low negative. This obstructs simultaneous **fixed strictly positive reserves at that point**, not an epsilon-loss theorem or an epsilon-dependent construction. Equality is unproved by this argument, not declared mathematically impossible.

For completeness this crossing is the maximum of the eliminated plane over the relevant capped-capacity polygon: before the crossing S<=2N makes `2009S+8379t` increase in t; afterward S<=1-Ct gives slope `8379-2009C<0` for these C. In the region g<=0 the low deletion cost is absent, and the original high term at zero amplifier is already positive. Thus the crossing identifies the genuine strict-ledger bottleneck, subject to the stated geometry, rather than just one arbitrary test point.

This boundary is not used as a theorem. The explicit C=546/125 has

`C-Ccrit=38829/26624875>0`,

and the continuous joint-plane margin at its own crossing is `12943/130000>0`. Its actual fixed k=.309 and thirty ceiling cells are paid in Sections 3-5, including rounding and every terminal branch. The equality idealization does not replace any finite check.

At the tighter safe plain edge the old short-slot fallback permits a lower cutoff strictly below

`(1-2N)/(9/2)=259/7500=.034533333...`.

The retained .034 edge therefore leaves reserve .0024. This is a limit of that fallback envelope, not an impossibility result. No attempt to optimize to either strict boundary is part of this candidate.

### 4. Outer fields, branch summation, and endpoint allocation

The common row Cauchy inequality, after the character transform, is
\[
 \sum_r|\xi(e^2r)\xi(d^2r)\mathcal A_{D,t}(e^2r)\mathcal A_{E,t'}(d^2r)|
 \ll Z^\epsilon\sqrt{Q_DQ_E/(Y_DY_E)}\sqrt{\mathcal F_D\mathcal F_E},
\]
where \(\mathcal F_D=1+P_a^{1/6}+q_DP_a^2/Y\). It follows by injectivity of the two row maps and (T06.7). The physical normalizations multiply this by exactly
\[
 q_D^{-3/2}q_E^{-3/2}(Q_DQ_E)^{-1/2}
 \sqrt{Q_DQ_E/(Y_DY_E)}=1/(Yq_Dq_E).
\]
Use \(L_DL_E=L^2/(P_JP_{J'})\), \(q_dq_e\le q_Dq_E\asymp P_JP_{J'}\), and \(\sqrt{\mathcal F_D\mathcal F_E}\ll\mathcal F_A\). In (T07.12) the remaining embedded-slot factor is
\((P_JP_{J'})^{-(1+2\sigma)/2}\); in (T07.7) it is \((P_JP_{J'})^{-(3-2\sigma)/2}\). Both are bounded by one. Summing \(|\omega_D|/q_D\) and \(|\omega_E|/q_E\) proves the three cancellation rows of the theorem. Absolute counting instead uses harmonic \(g\)-mass and two \(u^{-1/2}\)-counts, giving \(ZL/G\).

For the strongest Hecke estimate \(\sigma=b/2\), the ratio between the numerator at \(b>b_0\) and its displayed limit is \((ZL^3)^{(b-b_0)/2}\). If \(L\le Z^\Lambda\), choose a fixed positive \(b-b_0\) small enough in terms of the final \(\epsilon\), then allocate the remaining losses, and only then vary \(Z\). The weaker Hecke row uses the ratio \((Z/L)^{(b-b_0)/2}\), also harmless. This proves the endpoint-looking arbitrary-loss statements. ∎

# [private research revision]: exact divisor recovery and its unavoidable unsigned price

Accept G143-G145 at the scopes below, following complete root reads of
the [author](wild57/report.md), [erasure development](wild57/erasure.md),
[topology development](wild57/topology.md), [independent review](wild57-review/report.md),
both finite helpers and the precise B22/G117 ancestry. The
[retention manifest](retention-manifest.json) binds26 original files,
eight immutable mathematical sources and three frozen assignment sources.
The actual host-local claim snapshot is excluded; its manifest hash remains.

The useful new constraint is source-specific: even on the actual Mobius
coefficients, the complete absolute price of the divisor-recovery formula
has limsup exponent1. A successful estimate must retain cross-row signs.
The exact regular-residue counterexample and the distinction between two
commutator realizations likewise redirect their specific proposed attacks.
No arithmetic power saving, larger c or formalization is supplied.
Current c11=312864909/2500000000=.1251459636 and theta11=.8748540364
remain unchanged, with F0/analytic ancestry, positive-slot uniformity and
external definition/import/admission OPEN. All29families109children and
the near,1/6,1/4 targets are preserved.

## G143. Divisor-erasure recovery with literal coprimality and two prices

Fix an ordinary complex Dirichlet character chi modulo q. For integer N
and 1<=Y<=N/2 let S be the squarefree q-units through N, E={n in S:n<=Y},
H=S minus E, and a_n=mu(n)chi(n). The other integers retain their actual
squareful/nonunit zeros. The full convolution a*chi=delta_1 gives

    sum_(d in H,d|m) chi(m/d)a_d=b_m,
    b_m=-sum_(d in E,d|m)mu(d)chi(d)chi(m/d),  m in H.

H is convex inside every divisor interval between two of its elements.
Consequently the triangular matrix Z_(m,d)=chi(m/d)1_(d|m) has inverse
mu(m/d)chi(m/d)1_(d|m). Its matrix product reduces to
chi(m/d)sum_(e|m/d)mu(e); no general principal-submatrix inversion is used.
Summing the inverse columns gives the unique scalar dual

    lambda_m=sum_(k<=N/m,(k,m)=1)mu(k)chi(k),
    M_chi(N)=M_chi(Y)+sum_(m in H)lambda_m b_m.          (88.1)

This final contraction is bilinear, with no conjugate. The moving
coprimality is forced by squarefreeness of the multiple mk. At
Y=floor(sqrt N) every dual has short argument, but the entire m range
through N and every exposed divisor in b_m remain.

For independent row errors bounded by1, the exact scalar norm is
K_(N,Y)=sum_H|lambda_m|. Triangle gives the upper bound; errors
conj(lambda_m)/|lambda_m| attain it. Every m in S with m>N/2 has
lambda_m=1. The elementary square-divisor count

    Q_q(x)=#S_x=kappa_q x+O_q(sqrt x),
    kappa_q=(phi(q)/q) product_(p not dividing q)(1-p^-2)>0

therefore gives kappa_q N/2-O_q(sqrt N)<=K_(N,Y)<=N(1+log N).
Adding all convolution rows through N, including squareful rows and
known zeros, does not remove this terminal price: the column of an
unknown m>N/2 occurs only in its own row, with coefficient1. Every exact
linear certificate must assign1 to that row. Weighted independent errors
w_m have exact price sum_H|lambda_m|w_m, including all terminal weights.
This result concerns that linear error formulation, not multiplicative
perturbations of the source or nonlinear arithmetic constraints.

There is a separate actual-source result. Put P_N=sum_H|lambda_m b_m|
and permit any cutoff sequence1<=Y_N<=N/2. Each unramified prime
N/2<p<=N has lambda_p=1 and b_p=-chi(p). Thus P_N dominates the number
of those primes, while

    P_N<=N sum_(m<=N)tau(m)/m<=N(1+log N)^2.

If P_N=O(N^alpha) for some alpha<1 at all large N, dyadic intervals
N=2^j would make sum_p1/p converge. Euler's elementary finite-product
argument forbids that: bounded product_(p<=T)(1-1/p)^-1 would dominate
the divergent partial harmonic sums. Removing finitely many ramified
primes changes nothing. Hence

    limsup_(N->infinity) log P_N/log N=1                (88.2)

for every such cutoff sequence, with log0=-infinity. This is neither a
pointwise linear lower bound nor a lower bound on the signed sum(88.1).
It rules out the full absolute-payment strategy on the actual source.

The particular moving prime omissions can be paid without a fictitious
growing-conductor theorem. For any m and T,

    sum_(k<=T,(k,m)=1)mu(k)chi(k)
      =sum_(r<=T, p|r implies p|m)chi(r)M_chi(T/r).     (88.3)

Every power of a prime dividing m is included in r. If the fixed-character
bound |M_chi(t)|<=Ct^alpha is available,0<alpha<1, its price is

    CT^alpha product_(p|m)(1-p^-alpha)^-1
      <=CT^alpha exp(O_alpha((log(2N))^(1-alpha)))

uniformly for m<=N. Split at log(2N), bound the small primes by all
integers and the number of large prime divisors by log N/log2. This is
N^o(1), but summing absolute prices still cannot beat(88.2).

The surviving OPEN-E9 target is the complete signed sum in(88.1), with
Y=floor(sqrt N), bounded by N^(gamma+epsilon) for every epsilon>0, every
fixed ordinary chi and all large N, with one common1/2<gamma<theta11.
The exposed sector costs at most sqrt N. Thus this target is exponent-
equivalent to the full M bound; it is not claimed to be a weaker premise.
Targets gamma=.8748,5/6,3/4 all have room for that exposed sector.
Any model must bound its own complete contraction and the full signed
model residual, with terminal rows, coprimality and phases retained.

A proved full M bound defines
F_chi(s)=s integral_1^infinity M_chi(x)x^(-s-1)dx holomorphically on
Re s>gamma, locally uniformly with every fixed derivative. Initially
Re s>1 it is1/L(s,chi). Periodic partial sums continue nonprincipal L
to Re s>0; the elementary zeta integral gives the principal simple pole.
Continuation of LF=1 excludes all zeros at every height in Re s>gamma.
At the principal pole F has the appropriate zero; omitted imprimitive
Euler factors have zeros only on Re s=0. This return is conditional on
the complete all-scale fixed-character estimate, which is OPEN.

## G144. A regular-residue cover cannot repair the weighted Euler trace

The augmented squarefree q-unit cutoff complex has a basis e_S for
product n(S)<=X, including the empty face, graded by|S|. Oriented
deletion d and D_chi e_S=chi(n(S))e_S give Str(D_chi)=M_chi(X), but

    [D_chi,d]e_S=sum_(p in S)orientation(p,S)
                       chi(n(S)/p)(1-chi(p))e_(S minus p).

Distinct deletions have distinct target faces. A local deletion commuting
with D_chi must vanish whenever chi(p)!=1; assigning a phase does not
remove this defect. The proposed regular-register cover uses(S,g),
g in (Z/qZ)^*, and deletes p by(S,g)->(S minus p,gp). The conserved
coordinate h=g n(S) conjugates it exactly to d tensor I. Its character
Fourier sector is D_chi^-1 d D_chi with one basis vector per face.
Its Euler index is the principal M_chi0(X), independently of chi.
For q=3,X=5, the allowed faces1,2,5 have index-1, while actual M_chi=3.
The commuting insertion chi(h) has trace0 on the full regular register
for nonprincipal chi. Anchoring g=1 restores the signal but loses the
chain condition. This is an explicit counterexample to this cover/readout,
not to different chain groups or nonlocal signed interactions.

The existing cone/prime-toggle repair remains useful with its full defect.
Let ell be the least prime not dividing q. Faces without ell and product
<=X/ell, together with their ell cones, form a contractible subcomplex.
Every boundary face of a critical ell-free face in(X/ell,X] lies there.
Let h insert ell on the eligible faces and define P e_S=e_S-hd e_S on
critical faces, P=0 on the cone. Then P^2=P,dP=Pd=0,dh+hd=I-P, and

    Str(D_chi)=Str(D_chi P)+Str([D_chi,d]h)
      =B(X)+(1-chi(ell))A(X/ell),
    A(Y)=sum_(n<=Y,ell not dividing n)mu(n)chi(n),
    B(X)=A(X)-A(X/ell).

P is not just the diagonal critical-face indicator; its hd correction
is necessary. Full telescoping gives

    M_chi(X)=B(X)+(1-chi(ell))sum_(j>=1)B(X/ell^j).

At positive exponent alpha its cost is
1+|1-chi(ell)|/(ell^alpha-1), after a finite head. Conversely
A(X)=sum_(j>=0)chi(ell)^j M_chi(X/ell^j), so B has the same full
exponent as M. No character-weighted arithmetic gain is supplied.

The unsigned critical rank is
kappa_(q ell)(1-1/ell)X+O_q(sqrt X), equal to2X/pi^2+O(sqrt X)
for q=1. The long exact relative-homology sequence gives
b(K_X,K_Y)>=b(K_X)-b(K_Y) for total reduced Betti dimension. Along
any finite increasing filtration the sum of these unsigned relative
masses is at least final mass minus initial mass. An initial o(X) mass
therefore leaves a linear complete price, even for a changing filtration.
Signed interactions across annuli are outside that obstruction.

This section credits W27/G74/G76 and W53-W56 cone, character and
reconstruction ancestry. Its new test is the precise regular-cover
failure, with the full valid repair retained rather than relabeled new.

## G145. Full-word and sorted-creation commutators have different returns

In the full free-word lift, all k! orders of an integer's distinct primes
have the same phase. Abelianization maps each word to that integer.
Adjacent-transposition differences span its zero-sum kernel: the
permutation graph is connected, and a spanning tree has k!-1 independent
differences. The hard product cutoff retains entire fibers, so integer
evaluation annihilates every such within-fiber commutator. For positive
word weights w_v, beta_n=sum_(v in fiber n)1/w_v, the least squared lift
norm is sum_n|a_n|^2/beta_n and evaluator norm squared is sum_n beta_n.
Their product is at least(#S)^2. This is the existing G117 price;
cross-integer correlations remain eligible.

The existing B22 sorted-prime space has a different, nonzero commutator.
For fixed sigma>1/2 define on increasing unramified prime words

    A_p e_n=chi(p)p^-sigma e_(np) if p>P+(n), else0,
    T=sum_(p not dividing q)A_p,  P+(1)=1.

Different parents have disjoint r-step descendants, so
||T^r||^2<=S_sigma^r/r!, S_sigma=sum_(p not dividing q)p^-2sigma<infinity.
Hence the norm-convergent Neumann inverse gives
v_sigma=(I+T)^-1 e_1, with coordinate mu(n)chi(n)n^-sigma.
For p<r, A_p A_r=0. Thus, with[A,B]=AB-BA,

    C=sum_(p<r)[A_r,A_p]=T^2.

The infinite sum is defined through finite prime cutoffs: their C_P=T_P^2
converges in norm since ||T-T_P||^2<=sum_(p>P)p^-2sigma. Compression
to n<=N preserves the same identity because intermediate products never
exceed the final product. With Lambda_(N,sigma)u=sum_(n<=N)n^sigma u_n,

    M_chi(N)=1-sum_(p<=N)chi(p)+Lambda_(N,sigma)(C v_sigma). (88.4)

The final term is exactly the contribution with at least two prime
factors. It must cancel the prime term; a small norm of C alone does
not do so. Only an estimate for the complete scalar(88.4) gives the
all-scale M return. The source/operator construction is credited to B22;
the complete commutator/source accounting is the present adaptation.

Fixed fractional logarithmic regularity cannot pay the arithmetic gap.
For ||u||_s^2=sum_n(1+log n)^(2s)|u_n|^2 and fixed real s, v_sigma
belongs to every such space, while partial summation against Q_q gives

    ||Lambda_(N,sigma)||_(s,dual)^2
      ~kappa_q N^(2sigma+1)/((2sigma+1)(log N)^(2s)).

Its limiting power is still sigma+1/2>1. More generally every positive
diagonal weight w_(n,N), even chosen separately for each N, obeys

    sqrt(sum_(n in S)w_(n,N)|v_sigma(n)|^2)
      sqrt(sum_(n in S)n^(2sigma)/w_(n,N))>=#S.

This is a price for a product of norms, not a signed M lower bound.
Non-diagonal correlations and source-specific boundary estimates remain
open, with their complete return to be proved.

## Sampling, other failures and evidence limits

All30 original cards remain. Author choices23/14 preceded the literal
uniform p<.10 and p<.01 draws from pools23 and13, selecting13 and26.
Card20 was a deliberate wildcard: the required third uniform remaining-
pool draw is absent. Preserve the deficiency, actual tests and immutable
entropy; no reroll or retroactive third-stage claim. Independent protected30
and uniform28 came from frozen blind orders. The final audit-selection
receipt followed exposure to the opening abstract; the blind orders had
already forced both IDs, so no discretionary reselection occurred.

The remaining first tests retain actual scope: invertible congruence
preserves principal inertia, while a complex Hermitian dilation has zero
signature and loses the trace. The high-prime polymer clique has
Z=1-r t at principal activity, with a zero at1/r, blocking that naive
absolute cluster expansion. Its exact largest-prime resummation retains
both the smooth sector and the entire signed prime contraction; G81
already owns that renewal mechanism. Neither result excludes broader
signed constructions. Twenty-two cards remain untested after the two
independent audits; ancestry alone is not a test.

Independent rational-complex checks cover54 erasure,6 topology and4
ordered-creation cases, including complex imprimitive characters and
natural zeros. Both original draws were replayed without new entropy.
Root read both helpers and the complete reports; unchanged checks were
not rerun. These finite receipts establish indexing only. The infinite
claims above use their written proofs; OPEN-E9 and(88.4)'s signed power
estimate are still the arithmetic work to do. No new packet or public
record claim accompanies this cycle.

### Complete core and all-height return

For b=3/2,k=6 and gamma>=3/4, set L=X^gamma and freeze
U=V=floor(sqrt(eta_0) X^(u/2)). For sufficiently large X these exceed
one. Define the full balanced core

    T_(p,chi,X)(x)=sum_(d>U,e>V,L<del<=M)
       mu(d)mu(e)chi(del)(1-p 1_(p|l))f_x(del).

Its low prefix costs O(X^(gamma+epsilon)) by the divisor bound; its
full tail, S and short terms are already paid. Consequently

    ||C_p-T_(p,chi,X)||_j << X^(gamma+epsilon), j=1,2.       (91.4)

Every-epsilon whole-shell bounds for T and C_p are equivalent separately
in L1 and L2. L2 is sufficient for L1; the converse is not inferred.

The G140 Mellin calculation applies to the bounded changed coefficients.
After v=nt and rotation by a fixed admissible angle alpha, it gives

    integral_0^infinity C_p(1/t)t^(s-1)dt
       =A_0(s)P_p(s)/L(s,chi)+E_p(s),
    A_0(s)=Gamma(s/6) exp(-i pi s/12)/6,
    P_p(s)=1-chi(p)p^(1-s),                              (91.5)

where E_p is holomorphic for Re s>1/2 and A_0 has no zero for Re s>0.
Initially the identity holds in an absolutely convergent right half-plane.
The rotated remainder is locally uniform at EVERY fixed height; constants
can depend on height and chi. At x down to zero,
|C_p(x)|<=(p+1)/(exp(x^(-b))-1). The hypothesized every-epsilon L1 shell
bound therefore makes the left side holomorphic on Re s>gamma.

Choose two distinct fixed unramified primes p1,p2. For a nonprincipal
character choose p1 with chi(p1)!=1: a unit with nontrivial character
value has a prime factor with nontrivial value. Each P_p zero has Re s=1.
A common zero 1+it with t!=0 would make both t log(p_j)/(2pi) nonzero
rationals, contradicting irrationality of log(p1)/log(p2). At t=0 the
chosen nonprincipal p1 prevents a common zero. For a principal character
the possible common point is its allowed L pole, not an ordinary zero.
Thus bounds for both fixed compensated cores exclude ALL ordinary zeros
with Re s>gamma. No line-one nonvanishing theorem is hidden in the return.
Actual imprimitive Euler holes stay present; their zeros lie on Re s=0.

More generally, for each fixed gamma>1/2 choose k large enough that u>0,
1<b<=2gamma, and fixed K with 1-(b-1)K<gamma. Retain ALL shifts
A_j(s)P_p(s+(b-1)j)/L(s+(b-1)j) in G140's K-term expansion.
Starting above Re s=1, finite-strip descent of width b-1 gives the same
return. No growing k,K, uniform limit gamma down to 1/2, or endpoint
theorem is claimed. This extends the previous conditional architecture;
its required arithmetic power premise remains open.

## 9. Far-graph examples, strongest objections and residual target

For actual primary generators, the geometric graph `q_(pi'-pi-z0)<=Y`, intersected with the literal original windows and strict norm-far screen, has both degrees O(Y+1): a translated Eisenstein disk of radius sqrt(Y) has that many lattice points. This uses no primes-in-short-regions theorem. Taking Y of order Z^.055 fits the buffered gate. At z0=0, the algebraic possible norm gap is at most `O(sqrt(NY)+Y)`, which can exceed the old Z^.05 band. The author makes no claim that the possible endpoints are populated. The finite cyclic bipartite example has the stated six edges, degree two, primary generators and norm gaps; it illustrates support only, not an asymptotic original-ray prime supply or the analytic H estimate.

The most consequential possible failures were checked as follows:

| Objection | Resolution or exact limit |
|---|---|
| Mark-adaptive projection fails to commute with Fourier transform | Enlarge the selected positive mass to E_D first; only E_D is passed through mark Plancherel. |
| Shared-prime valuations cancel the row conductor | Order-two and order-three subgroups have trivial intersection; the exact lcm formula includes all shared factors. |
| Squares or fixed bad primes invalidate frequency counting | Unique ideal parity factorization includes all squares and finitely many bad parity classes. |
| Natural-zero Fourier frequencies hold the missing mass | Separate original injections and mark Cauchy prove the explicit eligibility bracket. |
| A small tensor-norm fraction proves covariance saving | False; the report keeps the norm/pairing distinction, the orbit escape and the unhelpful [restricted research revision].13 price. |
| The arbitrary graph inherits the old norm-gap transport lemma | It does not; [restricted research revision].6 uses a new explicit absolute count with both mark counts and G^2. |
| The sharp row interval is shifted or differentiated | It remains on R; only its smooth factor moves. The raw sharp interval estimate is invoked in its stated scope. |
| Jacobi centering loses a factor Q or one mark sum | Exact common-unit count gives Q^(-3/2); all NB edges, G^2 pairs, K rows and L mark mass are then charged. |
| One payment gate is silently used outside its domain | The returned statement keeps all three gates and the actual endpoint/no-alias conditions. |
| All heights or discarded branches are hidden in epsilon | Original product densities pay fixed height powers; absolute whole-series tail estimates pay all mixed tails; other branches remain open. |

A degree-B cover of a complete bipartite prime graph on m,m' vertices needs at least `max(m,m')/B` layers, since one vertex must receive all its opposite neighbours. Absolute summation of the linear-in-B bound recovers the full degree cost. This is a limitation of that covering procedure, not a lower bound for the signed covariance. It gives no reason to declare the remaining far interaction paid.

The actual residual is the exact signed far complement after subtracting the chosen graph, with its original moving prime-pair Fourier weights, complete short core, projectors, roots, heights and components, plus the other H branches. A useful next estimate would control that aggregate or a correctly priced kernel-invariant orbit recombination. Repeating a low-conductor norm truncation or a positive graph cover does not supply it.

statement:
# [private research revision]: high relative conductor with a large forced row divisor

10 October 2026 UTC. Independent mathematical reviewer: c20_continuum.
Reviewed source SHA-256: 8a867c69b9d8677681a5efef240b9cffa71f098bb89b3079a32e1987620e2c62.
Review/confirmation SHA-256: ab6e32048a23cc42ec91e6f1d3bc65749e735000623dcb89cf87c73b52858b26.
Canonical changes are metadata and repository-link relocation only; the
accepted formulas and their input scopes are preserved. No increase in c
is claimed.

**Status: independently accepted relative to the stated physical inputs.** This is one bounded continuation of the accepted physical covariance estimates. It pays a complementary sector above the FR cutoff, including all original source powers and mixed embeddings. It does not close the small-true-gcd covariance or improve the accepted zero-free constant.

The full covariance estimate remains open on PH31–PH32. The accepted new sectors and the dominated active-conductor comparison have distinct scopes.

## 1. Inputs and result

The precise inputs are:

- **I-PC:** [PC1-PC5 and PC11](../[private research revision]-continuation/physical-covariance.md), including the actual normalized Gauss kernels, primitive relative character, natural zero extensions, mixed embedding map, and absolute complete-zero estimate.
- **I-FR:** [FR3-FR19](../[private research revision]/physical-forced-rows.md), especially the weighted fixed-radical mass for every fixed divisor exponent strictly greater than \(1/6\). The particular mass statement used is restated in (PH8); it is an accepted input, not silently strengthened.
- **I-HC:** [HC7-HC18](../[private research revision]/physical-radical-mass.md), used to prove the restricted exponent-zero mass in Section 4.
- **I-SEXTIC:** the actual fields, original marks, original profiles and polynomial scale ranges in [T06-T07](../[private research revision]/[restricted mathematical source]#t06-the-complete-same-core-sextic-square-function).
- For the separate active-conductor comparison only, the exact single-source reduction and coefficient count in [XM13-XM30](../[private research revision]/mixed-linear-transfer.md#4-exact-reduction-of-every-source-power).

Ordinary smooth character Poisson is sufficient. No new I-HECKE, I-ZETA, Dedekind nonvanishing, or higher moment estimate is assumed. The stronger inherited I-HECKE input is still needed if one separately invokes T07's strongest large-true-gcd tail.

Keep the exact parameters
\[
Q=q_{b_*}XY,\qquad P_a=Y^2/Q,\qquad Y_D=Y/q_D,
\qquad D=Gd,\quad E=Ge,\quad(d,e)=1,
\qquad H=Q/q_{[D,E]}^2.
\tag{PH1}
\]
The fixed factor \(q_{b_*}\) is retained. Here \(H\) is PC's common row volume, not the hybrid hypothesis \(\mathcal H\). Write \(A=cn^3,A'=c'n'^3\), with squarefree cores, and let \(a,b\) be the original outer columns. The relative radical and its norm remain
\[
\mathfrak r=\prod_{v_p(A)-v_p(A')-v_p(a)+v_p(b)\not\equiv0\ (6)}p,
\qquad R=q_{\mathfrak r}.
\tag{PH2}
\]

Define \(d(a)=a/\operatorname{rad}(a)\), and define the **forced row ideal** and its norm by
\[
\mathfrak f_{a,b;D,E}=
\left[
\frac{d(a)}{(d(a),e^2)},
\frac{d(b)}{(d(b),d^2)}
\right],\qquad F=q_{\mathfrak f_{a,b;D,E}}.
\tag{PH3}
\]
All ideals here are good; fixed-place factors stay in the original fixed family. The definition includes forcing at coherent primes as well as conductor primes.

The first new estimate is, for polynomial \(T,K\ge1\),
\[
\boxed{
\sum_{\substack{1<R\le T\\F\ge K}}|C_{\lambda\mu}|
\ll_\epsilon \frac{Z^\epsilon}{Y}
\min\!\left\{
\frac{T^{3/4}}{\sqrt Q\,K^{1/3}},
\frac{T^{1/2}}{K^{5/6}}
\right\}.
}
\tag{PH4}
\]
This is the absolute atom-pair sum, with every original mark and every pair of embeddings. An arbitrary bounded row-independent pair mask may be inserted, including small true core gcd or gcd one. For \(R>1\), the actual complete zero is zero.

Consequently the full physical sector
\[
\boxed{
1<R\le \max\!\left\{(QYF)^{4/9},\ P_a^{1/3}F^{5/3}\right\}
}
\tag{PH5}
\]
costs at most \(Z^\epsilon Y^{-1}P_a^{1/6}\). When \(F=1\), the first boundary is exactly FR's cutoff. The gain above that cutoff requires an actual large forced divisor; it is not a larger unconditional cutoff in \(R\).

There is a stronger restricted sector. Let
\[
\mathfrak p_{\mathrm{coh}}=
\prod_{\substack{p\notin S,\ p\nmid\mathfrak r\\
 (v_p(a)>0,\ 6\mid v_p(a))\ \mathrm{or}\quad
 (v_p(b)>0,\ 6\mid v_p(b))}}p.
\tag{PH6}
\]
If \(\mathfrak p_{\mathrm{coh}}=1\), principal positive outer powers are allowed at conductor primes, but not at coherent good primes. In this sector,
\[
\boxed{
\sum_{\substack{1<R\le T,\ F\ge K\\\mathfrak p_{\mathrm{coh}}=1}}
|C_{\lambda\mu}|
\ll_\epsilon\frac{Z^\epsilon}{Y}
\min\!\left\{
\frac{T^{3/4}}{\sqrt Q\,K^{1/2}},
\frac{T^{1/2}}{K}
\right\}.
}
\tag{PH7}
\]
In particular, this includes every locally nonprincipal outer pair but is a strictly broader local condition. Its affordable boundary is given in Section 5.

## 2. Exact local forcing, including the embedding exceptions

At a good prime put
\(\alpha=v_p(a),\ \beta=v_p(b),\ s=v_p(e),\ t=v_p(d)\).
The embeddings are squarefree, so \(s,t\in\{0,1\}\) and \(st=0\). The exponent in (PH3) is
\[
\kappa_p=\max\{0,\alpha-1-2s,\beta-1-2t\}.
\]
For every atom pair whose good local kernel is not identically zero, every nonzero row satisfies \(v_p(r)\ge\kappa_p\). Moreover PC4 can be formed so that every one of its divisor ideals \(k\) is divisible by \(\mathfrak f\).

Here is the complete local verification, before taking absolute values.

1. If \(p\mid AA'\), the original column zero extensions force \(r\) to be a unit and require \((A,e)=(A',d)=1\). The surviving outer exponents are
   \(\alpha\in\{0,1+2s\},\ \beta\in\{0,1+2t\}\).
   Thus \(\kappa_p=0\). A surviving embedded exponent three has **no** forced \(p\)-divisibility in the common row. This remains true when a column character is principal on units.
2. Outside \(AA'\), a positive nonprincipal outer exponent \(j\not\equiv0\pmod6\) forces the exact valuation \(j-1-2s\ge0\) on the first side, or \(j-1-2t\ge0\) on the second. A negative prescribed valuation makes that local kernel zero. If both sides are nonprincipal, their prescribed valuations must agree. If only one is nonprincipal, its prescribed valuation must lie in the support of the other side. For a surviving pair the resulting valuation is at least \(\kappa_p\).
3. A positive principal exponent \(j\equiv0\pmod6\) has the exact normalized kernel
   \[
   q^{j/2}1_{p^{j-2s}\mid r}
   -q^{j/2-1}1_{p^{j-1-2s}\mid r}.
   \]
   Its smallest supported valuation is \(j-1-2s\). Products of principal kernels combine divisors by their maximum. Consequently every term remains divisible by \(p^{\kappa_p}\). The lower divisor never receives the larger coefficient.
4. At a relative-conductor prime, some nonprincipal unit character remains. Outside \(AA'\), two principal-only outer factors cannot produce such a prime. If both outer factors are nonprincipal, the equality of their forced valuations gives \(\alpha-\beta=2(s-t)\). Away from an embedding this makes the prime coherent; at an unequal embedding it can leave exponent \(\pm2\pmod6\). This is the additional embedding-only active case. Its forced valuation is still exactly the one above.

At coherent primes an exact unit condition is expanded as a difference of two divisibility masks. Their exponents are \(\kappa_p\) and \(\kappa_p+1\), or larger. At conductor primes the primitive character supplies the unit condition and the forced valuation stays inside \(k\). CRT phases are units and are retained in PC4's coefficients. None of these operations can introduce a divisor exponent below \(\kappa_p\).

In particular,
\[
\mathfrak f\mid k\quad\hbox{for every term of PC4},\qquad
F\le q_aq_b\ll Y_DY_E\le Y^2.
\]
The original common row profile is supported in a fixed positive annulus \(q_r\asymp H\). Therefore a nonzero physical row also requires \(F\ll H\). These support assertions concern \(R>1\) covariances; an empty row sum is not being identified with a vanished coherent continuous zero.

## 3. Retaining the forced divisor in FR's weighted mass

For fixed \(D,E,\mathfrak r\), let \(\mathscr M_{\mathfrak r}^{(\sigma)}\) denote the sum over the actual atoms of
\[
\frac{|K_D(cn^3)K_E(c'n'^3)|}
{\sqrt{q_cq_{c'}}q_nq_{n'}}
\left|W_1(x_a)W_1(x_b)(x_ax_b)^{-1/2}\right|
\sum_k|b_{\lambda\mu,k}|q_k^{-\sigma}.
\]
Here \(x_a=q_a/Y_D,x_b=q_b/Y_E\), the \(b\)'s are PC4's **normalized** Gauss-product coefficients, and the finite ray indices and bounded original unit factors are included. The source factor \((Y_DY_E)^{-1}\) and the physical embedding factors are not included in this definition. Bounds for the original joint row profile use its uniform fixed seminorms.

The exact accepted I-FR input is
\[
\mathscr M_{\mathfrak r}^{(\sigma)}
\ll_{\epsilon,\sigma}Z^\epsilon\sqrt{Y_DY_E}\,R^{-1/2+\epsilon},
\qquad 1/6<\sigma\le1.
\tag{PH8}
\]
It permits arbitrary positive restrictions on the atom labels. FR13 pays the coherent principal powers using their exact two-term kernels. FR14 keeps the condition \(\ell_p\ne0\) when regularizing conductor-prime exponent sums. Its local \(q_p^{-1/2}\) gain would be false if principal-only vectors were inserted into that conductor sum. The present proof preserves that condition.

Let \(\sigma\le\rho\le1\), with \(\sigma>1/6\). For \(R>1\), the two actual row estimates give
\[
|\operatorname{row}(H/q_k)|
\ll R^{(1-\rho)/2}(H/q_k)^\rho.
\tag{PH9}
\]
On \(F\ge K\), Section 2 gives, term by term,
\[
q_k^{-\rho}\le K^{\sigma-\rho}q_k^{-\sigma}.
\tag{PH10}
\]
This is the new step. It retains the exact large and small Ramanujan coefficients inside (PH8). It does not replace both by the larger coefficient at the smallest forced divisor.

Multiplying (PH8)-(PH10), then restoring both source normalizers and PC9's physical factor, gives the fixed-\((D,E,\mathfrak r)\) estimate
\[
\begin{split}
\sum_{F\ge K}|C_{\lambda\mu}|
&\ll Z^\epsilon
\frac{|\omega_D\omega_E|}{Q\sqrt{q_Dq_E}}
\frac{H^\rho}{\sqrt{Y_DY_E}}
R^{-\rho/2}K^{\sigma-\rho}\\
&=Z^\epsilon
\frac{|\omega_D\omega_E|Q^{\rho-1}}
{Yq_{[D,E]}^{2\rho}}
R^{-\rho/2}K^{\sigma-\rho}.
\end{split}
\tag{PH11}
\]
There is no extra row Jacobian: the discrete common row is \(m'=[D,E]^2r\), the profiles have volume \(H\), and the physical factor is exactly \((Q\sqrt{q_Dq_E})^{-1}\).

Ideal counting and the original bounded slot weights give
\[
\sum_{D,E}\frac{|\omega_D\omega_E|}{q_{[D,E]}^{2\rho}}
\ll Z^\epsilon L^{\max(2-4\rho,0)},\qquad
\sum_{q_{\mathfrak r}\le T}R^{-\rho/2+\epsilon}
\ll T^{1-\rho/2+\epsilon}.
\tag{PH12}
\]
For the first estimate write \(D=gd,E=ge\), drop restrictions only in the resulting positive sum, and sum \(g,d,e\) harmonically. Below \(\rho=1/2\), the two inner sums cost \((L/q_g)^{2-4\rho}\), and the remaining \(g\)-sum has exponent \(-2+2\rho<-1\). At and above \(1/2\), only logarithms or convergent sums remain. This includes shared embedded primes and all slot subsets.

Thus the complete family is
\[
\boxed{
\sum_{\substack{1<R\le T\\F\ge K}}|C_{\lambda\mu}|
\ll \frac{Z^\epsilon}{Y}
Q^{\rho-1}L^{\max(2-4\rho,0)}
T^{1-\rho/2}K^{\sigma-\rho},
\quad 1/6<\sigma\le\rho\le1.
}
\tag{PH13}
\]
Take \(\sigma=1/6+\delta\), with a fixed positive buffer chosen sufficiently small for the final epsilon. Since every nonempty restriction has \(K\ll Y^2\), the extra \(K^\delta\) is absorbed in \(Z^\epsilon\). At \(\rho=1/2\) and \(1\), (PH13) gives exactly (PH4). No Euler series is evaluated at \(\sigma=1/6\).

## 4. Removing the principal-root loss on its exact exceptional complement

If \(\mathfrak p_{\mathrm{coh}}=1\), then
\[
\mathscr M_{\mathfrak r}^{(0)}
\ll_\epsilon Z^\epsilon\sqrt{Y_DY_E}\,R^{-1/2+\epsilon}.
\tag{PH14}
\]
This statement is more precise than requiring all outer powers to be locally nonprincipal. Here is its proof from I-HC, retaining principal exponents at conductor primes.

Away from \(\mathfrak r\), use the original PC6/HC7 parametrization. The absence of a positive principal outer valuation there forces the residual sixth roots and the principal part of \(d_0\) to be trivial. A common nonprincipal exponent cannot differ by a nonzero multiple of six on the other side: equal forced valuations require equality in an unembedded pair, and require a difference of two at an unequal embedding. The latter is incompatible with coherence. The column/embedding exception three remains the original \(x^3,y^3\) factor; it is not discarded.

Consequently HC9 has \(f=r_1=r_2=1\). Its \(d_\circ\) sum has the actual nonprincipal weight \(q_{\operatorname{rad}(d_\circ)}^{-1}\). Insert \(q_{d_\circ}^{-\eta}\), use the convergent Euler product, and pay the compensating power with the polynomial outer annuli. The \(x,y\) exponents remain \(3/2>1\), and the other square-root labels retain exponent two. The common-core harmonic sum is taken against both original rapid envelopes, uniformly in their two scales. This proves coherent mass \(Z^\epsilon\sqrt{UV}\).

At a conductor prime principal outer exponents are still allowed. Regularize the outer sums by \(q^{-\eta(\alpha+\beta)}\). With HC4's exact Gauss size, the principal sum is
\(P_p=(1-q^{-6\eta})^{-1}\), the positive nonprincipal sum is \(N_p\ll_\eta q^{-1/2}\), and the completed-column mass is \(D_p=1+O(q^{-1/2})\). The condition \(\ell_p\ne0\) gives the bound
\[
((P_p+N_p)^2-P_p^2)D_p+P_p^2(D_p-1)
\ll_\eta q^{-1/2}.
\tag{PH15}
\]
The principal-only, zero-column vectors are excluded by the actual conductor condition. Thus the same fixed-radical product gives (PH14). Its finite local constants have subpower product; the compensating source powers are polynomial, and completed powers are absorbed into the original envelopes.

Apply (PH10) with \(\sigma=0\) to this restricted mass. The argument through (PH13) now works for every \(0\le\rho\le1\), with the factor \(K^{-\rho}\). The two choices \(\rho=1/2,1\) prove (PH7).

## 5. Paying the curved sectors and keeping every original tail

For (PH4)'s first bound, a conductor dyad \(T<R\le2T\) is paid when
\[
K\ge \frac{T^{9/4}}{QY}.
\]
The resulting factor is
\(Q^{-1/2}T^{3/4}K^{-1/3}\le Q^{-1/6}Y^{1/3}=P_a^{1/6}\).
For its second bound the condition is
\(K\ge(T^3/P_a)^{1/5}\).
If either lower bound is below one, use \(K=1\); this only improves the estimate. These are precisely the two parts of (PH5), up to fixed dyadic constants.

Similarly (PH7) pays the sector
\[
\boxed{
\mathfrak p_{\mathrm{coh}}=1,\qquad
1<R\le\max\!\left\{(QY)^{4/9}F^{2/3},\ P_a^{1/3}F^2\right\}.
}
\tag{PH16}
\]
The required lower bounds for \(F\) are respectively
\(T^{3/2}/(QY)^{2/3}\) and \(T^{1/2}P_a^{-1/6}\).

All these sectors have polynomial \(R\)-range: (PH3) gives \(F\ll Y^2\), so their displayed inequalities themselves bound \(R\) by a fixed power of the original scales. There are \(O(\log Z)\) conductor dyads. We do not sum the estimates over infinitely many unrestricted conductor dyads. Their logarithmic number is absorbed by choosing smaller losses in (PH8) and (PH14). Overlaps are disjointized by bounded row-independent masks. No positive-semidefinite assertion about a conductor or gcd mask is used.

The infinite completed columns have not been truncated. Each actual mark kernel satisfies the inherited bound
\[
|K_D(A)|\ll_\eta q_A^\eta E(q_A/N_D),\qquad N_D=ZL_D,
\tag{PH17}
\]
with one common two-sided rapid envelope and no separate marked-tuple length factor. The weighted masses (PH8) and (PH14) sum both envelopes before removing their dependence. Small powers of arbitrarily large columns are absorbed into them. The restriction on \(F\) depends only on the finite outer columns and embeddings; it never changes a profile or adds a completed tail.

For definiteness, the underlying field is absolutely defined before these sharper row bounds: the original completed coefficients obey
\[
\sum_{c,n}\frac{q_{cn^3}^\eta}{\sqrt{q_c}q_n}
E(q_cq_n^3/N_D)
\ll N_D^{1/2+\eta}\sum_nq_n^{-5/2}<\infty.
\tag{PH18}
\]
The outer labels and physical rows lie in fixed annuli. Finite completed truncations therefore converge to the original field; the positive estimates above pass to the limit. The unit ideal, shared core/cube primes, all natural zero extensions, signed roots and signed marks stay in the definition.

The joint row profile is always
\(W_0(q_r/(Hx_a))\overline{W_0(q_r/(Hx_b))}\).
Substitution \(r=kz\) changes its scale to \(H/q_k\), exactly as in FR. All annular parameters lie in fixed compact sets. If the original inverse representation is kept in Mellin form, the same finite profile seminorms grow polynomially in its real heights and are integrated against the original rapid densities. No moving-set Poisson constant, moving cutoff derivative, or unpriced height supremum is introduced.

## 6. Size and limitations of the new sector

Write \(Q=q_{b_*}Z^M\), \(M=x+y\), \(Y=Z^y\), \(L=Z^\ell\). For a forced-divisor dyad \(F\asymp Z^f\), (PH5) gives the two scale-exponent boundaries
\[
\tau_{1/2}(f)=\frac49(M+y+f),\qquad
\tau_1(f)=\frac{y-x+5f}{3}.
\tag{PH19}
\]
Fixed \(q_{b_*}\) factors remain in (PH5), rather than being folded into these scale exponents. The two branches switch when
\[
f=\frac{6M-(y-x)}{11}
=0.447838197664883655\ldots
\tag{PH20}
\]
at the [saved geometry](../sextic-geometry.md#2-geometry-and-the-binding-numerator).
For \(\mathfrak p_{\mathrm{coh}}=1\), the boundaries are
\(\frac49(M+y)+\frac23f\) and \((y-x)/3+2f\); their switch is at
\(f=(6M-(y-x))/12=0.410518347859476684\ldots\).

Within the interpolation family (PH13), the affordable exponent is
\[
\tau(\rho,f)=
\frac{(1-\rho)M-\max(2-4\rho,0)\ell
 +(y-x)/6+(\rho-1/6)f}{1-\rho/2}.
\tag{PH21}
\]
Below \(\rho=1/2\), its derivative has the positive saved-geometry sign from FR20 plus \(11f/12\ge0\). Above \(1/2\), its derivative has the constant sign of
\(-M/2+(y-x)/12+11f/12\).
Thus \(\rho=1/2\) or \(1\) is optimal within this family. The restricted family replaces \(\rho-1/6\) by \(\rho\), and has the same endpoint conclusion with derivative contribution \(f\). This optimality is only for the explicitly proved family.

A concrete local/scale configuration lies strictly beyond FR. In the unembedded branch take pairwise disjoint source factors
\[
a=p^2t,\qquad b=q^2s,
\qquad q_p\asymp q_q\asymp Z^{13/100},\qquad
q_t,q_s\asymp Z^{y-26/100},
\tag{PH22}
\]
with \(t,s\) squarefree, and choose completed labels
\(A=u^6\), \(A'=p_0v^6\), where \(p_0\) is a fixed good prime disjoint from these factors. Their squarefree cores are \(1,p_0\), so their true gcd is one. Keep source factors coprime to \(uvp_0\). The exact row support has \(F=q_pq_q\asymp Z^{0.26}\), and
\[
\log_Z R=2y-0.26+o(1)
=0.662332873840431694\ldots+o(1).
\tag{PH23}
\]
The old FR exponent is \(0.576299562323534148\ldots\); the first new boundary is \(0.691855117879089704\ldots\), with strict margin \(0.029522244038658010\ldots\). These are nonzero local kernels: the source-square primes force valuations one; all sixth-power column primes impose unit masks, and the remaining source primes carry their actual primitive characters.

This configuration is compatible with the actual marked columns. For \(D=E=1\), the complementary mark product has size \(L\). Put its original distinct primes into \(u\) and \(v\), and retain the actual marked weights. The remaining sixth-root scale has exponent
\((1-5\ell)/6=0.0243218423717766725\ldots>0\).
Thus the mark requirement does not force an empty completed scale. The example is a compatibility and local-support witness for labels in the original nonzero windows, not an assertion of a signed covariance lower bound or a new prime-counting theorem.

The necessary physical support \(F\ll H\) bounds how far a particular branch can reach. In the unembedded branch the largest possible boundary from the second full-sector condition has exponent
\((y-x+5M)/3=1.421454395690458546\ldots\).
For the restricted sector it is \((y-x)/3+2M=1.699956921793037208\ldots\).
These are upper envelopes of a conditional sector, not claims that every conductor up to those sizes is paid.

## 7. What individual active-conductor sorting actually proves

For one original atom define
\[
\mathfrak h(a,A)=\prod_{v_p(A)-v_p(a)\not\equiv0\ (6)}p,
\qquad h_1=q_{\mathfrak h(a,A)},\quad
h_2=q_{\mathfrak h(b,A')}.
\tag{PH24}
\]
For every surviving pair \(\mathfrak r\mid[\mathfrak h(a,A),\mathfrak h(b,A')]\), in particular \(R\le h_1h_2\). The calibration \(\xi\) cancels in a covariance. Its nonprincipal linear completion cannot simply be applied to the paired row, and the XM linear functional is not a norm estimate.

There is nevertheless a rigorous way to factor positive pre-completion coefficient masses. Fix \(1/6<\beta\le1\), \(\gamma\ge0\), and a polynomial cap \(1\le B\le Z^C\). Let \(\mathscr A_D(\beta,\gamma;B)\) be the absolute sum of actual single-atom coefficients with \(h_{\rm act}\le B\), weighted by
\(h_{\rm act}^{\gamma}\sum_k|b_k|q_k^{-\beta}\), including its source normalization but not its physical branch normalization. Then the exact XM coefficient count gives
\[
\mathscr A_D(\beta,\gamma;B)
\ll Z^\epsilon Y_D^{-1/2}B^{\gamma+1/2}.
\tag{PH25}
\]
For clarity, this is a coefficient lemma derived from XM, not an inference from the value of its linear row sum. Write \(a=tu\), with \(t\) squarefree and \(u\) squareful, and let \(U=q_u\), \(R_u=q_{\prod_{p\mid u,\,6\nmid v_p(u)}p}\). Original zeros force \((u,A)=1\). On a core/cube dyad \(C N^3\asymp T\), its three positive factors are:

- the exact source-amplitude weight \(\sqrt{Y_D}U^{1/2-\beta}R_u^{\beta-1/2}\);
- the source/core count \(\sqrt{Y_D C B/(UR_u)}\), obtained from the actual gcd condition \(q_tq_cR_u/q_{(t,c)}^2\le B\);
- the total cube coefficient \(C^{-1/2}\), along with source normalization \(Y_D^{-3/2}\) and the bound \(h_{\rm act}^{\gamma}\le B^\gamma\).

Their product is
\[
Y_D^{-1/2}B^{\gamma+1/2}U^{-\beta}R_u^{\beta-1}.
\]
Its squareful-source Euler product converges for \(\beta>1/6\), with the exact principal weights \(q_p^{-6j\beta}\). The original completed envelopes sum the dyads and both tails as in XM27-XM30. This proves (PH25) for all actual source powers.

Now expand two single-atom kernels, retaining their exact divisors \(k_1,k_2\). After the common-row embeddings their divisors are
\(k_1'=k_1/(k_1,e^2)\), \(k_2'=k_2/(k_2,d^2)\).
Every surviving paired divisor is at least their lcm; coherent unit-mask expansion can add a prime but cannot lower it. Therefore
\[
q_{[k_1',k_2']}^{-\rho}
\le(q_{k_1'}q_{k_2'})^{-\rho/2}
\le(q_dq_e)^\rho(q_{k_1}q_{k_2})^{-\rho/2}.
\tag{PH26}
\]
If exact valuations conflict, the term is zero before this bound. At common active primes the additional unit-mask expansions cost only the usual divisor factor; all resulting phases retain modulus one. No independent row mask is inserted.

For \(R>1\), completion costs at most
\(R^{(1-\rho)/2}H^\rho\le(h_1h_2)^{(1-\rho)/2}H^\rho\).
Use (PH25) with \(\beta=\rho/2>1/6\) and \(\gamma=(1-\rho)/2\), then restore the exact physical factor. Since
\(H^\rho(q_dq_e)^\rho=Q^\rho/(q_Dq_E)^\rho\), the result for caps \(h_1\le B_D,h_2\le B_E\) is
\[
\boxed{
\sum_{\substack{R>1\\h_1\le B_D,\ h_2\le B_E}}|C_{\lambda\mu}|
\ll\frac{Z^\epsilon Q^{\rho-1}}Y
\sum_{D,E}\frac{|\omega_D\omega_E|}
{(q_Dq_E)^\rho}(B_DB_E)^{1-\rho/2},
\quad 1/3<\rho\le1.
}
\tag{PH27}
\]
The sum is understood with the corresponding polynomial cap in each branch. Constants may depend on the fixed polynomial range, \(\rho\), and epsilon, as in the original XM estimate. It permits extra bounded pair masks. It is an actual covariance-intersection estimate, not positivity of a localized form.

For uniform left/right caps \(B_1,B_2\), writing \(B=B_1B_2\), this becomes
\[
\sum_{R>1,\ h_i\le B_i}|C_{\lambda\mu}|
\ll\frac{Z^\epsilon}{Y}
Q^{\rho-1}L^{2-2\rho}B^{1-\rho/2}.
\tag{PH28}
\]
This particular factorization yields no new sector: \(R\le B\), and FR19 on that larger sector has the same \(Q,B\) powers but the smaller embedding factor \(L^{\max(2-4\rho,0)}\). Thus FR dominates (PH28) for every allowed \(\rho\).

Quantitatively, at the saved geometry the largest affordable product-cap exponent from (PH28) is its buffered \(\rho\downarrow1/3\) limit,
\[
\log_Z B\le
\frac45(M-2\ell)+\frac15(y-x)
=0.412469059106539142\ldots.
\tag{PH29}
\]
It is smaller than the FR exponent by \(0.163830503216995006\ldots\). The derivative of the affordable exponent has the sign of
\(-(M-2\ell)/2+(y-x)/12<0\), so another choice inside this family does not repair the loss. The limiting source series is not evaluated at \(\beta=1/6\); choose a positive buffer and absorb its polynomial cost as before.

A low/high cross term with no finite cap on the second side requires an additional bound on its actual coefficient mass or its actual Hilbert norm. T06 pays the sum of same-core norms, not the norm after summing all high-conductor cores. Substituting that unknown norm into Cauchy would restate part of the open covariance. A useful improvement would have to retain arithmetic coupling discarded in (PH26), or prove cancellation between the actual paired columns. The numerical loss above diagnoses this concrete factorization, not all possible active-conductor methods.

## 8. Exact residual and review targets

Let \(\mathcal E\) be the union of (PH5) and (PH16), always with \(R>1\). Combining their absolute estimates with the paid coherent discrepancy and PC11 gives, for the original small-true-gcd covariance,
\[
\boxed{
\mathcal C_<
=\mathcal C_{<,\,(\lambda,\mu)\notin\mathcal E,\ R>1}
+O_\epsilon\!\left(Z^\epsilon Y^{-1}P_a^{1/6}\right).
}
\tag{PH30}
\]
More explicitly the surviving nonzero-relative-conductor pairs satisfy both
\[
R^{9/4}>QYF,\qquad R^3>P_aF^5,
\tag{PH31}
\]
and, if \(\mathfrak p_{\mathrm{coh}}=1\), also
\[
R^{3/2}>(QY)^{2/3}F,\qquad R>P_a^{1/3}F^2.
\tag{PH32}
\]
The remaining arithmetic obligation is to bound this **actual signed** residual by \(Z^\epsilon Y^{-1}P_a^{1/6}\), retaining all original phases, marks, embeddings, profiles and heights. No estimate for it is asserted here.

In particular, all squarefree outer pairs have \(F=1\) and \(\mathfrak p_{\mathrm{coh}}=1\). Their high-\(R\) portion remains. In the unembedded main completed range one may take \(n=n'=1\), disjoint squarefree marked cores \(c,c'\asymp ZL\), and squarefree source columns \(a,b\asymp Y\) coprime to them. Then the true core gcd is one and
\[
R\asymp Y^2(ZL)^2,\qquad F=1.
\tag{PH33}
\]
These are surviving configurations of the actual coefficient support. They identify the remaining problem without replacing the field by arbitrary vectors. The exponent-three embedding exception can likewise leave \(F=1\), so an outer-power cutoff alone would misclassify that residual.

Independent review should focus on: the all-prime divisor identity (PH3) and the exponent-three exception; use of the accepted weighted mass at a strictly buffered exponent; the restricted exponent-zero mass (PH14), where principal powers at conductor primes are retained; exact physical normalization in (PH11); conductor-dyad summation under the curved restrictions; and the individual-mass versus linear-functional distinction in (PH25)-(PH28). Artifact checks establish only persistence and internal consistency, not mathematical acceptance.

A supplemental finite support check used \(q=7\), outer exponents \(0\le\alpha,\beta\le18\), the three embedding pairs \((s,t)=(0,0),(1,0),(0,1)\), and column exponents from zero through seven, with the original column zeros imposed. All 577 surviving configurations had minimum row valuation exactly \(\kappa_p\); all 460 with nonzero relative exponent had one exact row valuation. The 28 surviving column/embedding exponent-three configurations had \(\kappa_p=0\). The check uses the exact local valuation formulas and supplies a consistency check, not a substitute for Section 2's argument.

# Independent Astra validation of post52 Sol batch02



**Decision:** accept D04's explicit four-diagonal collar error and D48's complete signed-block transfer, conditionally on their still-open complete moments. Accept D02's normalization failure and exact repair, which recovers the original energy. Independently accept the Sol critic's additive finite-difference loss of reciprocal poles and its restricted post-character Fourier visibility bound. No c gain, full-H estimate, Eisenstein transfer or growing-conductor uniformity follows. Current written c5=.125136 and its separate pending kernel replay remain unchanged.

## Intake and sampling

Author report25367bytes SHA256fea2a5f642bbc33c12e8ba3a0f88c2fbbb69365fca5503a2a63ce3f6df6ef775; author manifestc543e65031c0add34e1de5c86f9f048cfb6839d8a29b2125e7ac625b41b1f759. Both reports were read in full after the authorized first-stage handoff. All17 author and11 Sol manifest files were independently completely read/hash-verified. Neither author's nor Sol's helper was executed in its directory.

All60 seeds remain. Literal Decimal pools include ALL eligible unreserved groups. Reservations are S04,S08,S02,S46,S18. Replaying the saved sequential seed213002587430500757690352512393298758067 gives pool sizes47/46/22/21/51, indices0/23/9/3/39 and selections S06/S37/S48/S41/S49. Sol's separate49-card pool, seed144058667576375153821187610876778501730 and index40 reproduce uniform S52 after protected S29 and the author10 are removed. Those audits are evidence reviewed here; they are not this critic's independent random sample.

Our ALL60 priority/permutation froze01:15:07 before selections/outcomes were known. Pool SHA2560f9d761d0e1c04f627d5c27888d39946da5224c5c7a4f8bf1f994f054a6f7b97; order SHA2567787a7b1e500779b12c560dd924294ed7aa7a5c6c8af06ad0ef12f9ed958ddd7. The retained29-family/109-child record and current index inform attribution. Specific comparisons include G11--G31, W41's numerator, JN1--JN27, [private research revision] H, [private research revision] grouping and W43's frozen projection. None supplies a new arithmetic input here.

## D04: complete collars and derivative costs

Use exactly tau=1,kappa=C=D=2,a=3/4,Y=floor(X^.495), the accepted G11 intervals intersected with Y<d<=Dmax, and all ordered i+j=-2,-1,0,1. The complete alternating ell source is represented by eta(s)=(1-2^(1-s))zeta(s) after its already justified Mellin continuation; an absolutely divergent ell series is not interchanged at a<1. Source G20 already pays the product/TypeI/height complements. Smoothing these intervals is a new mask with an explicit difference.

For each actual upper scale D_i, D_i=X^[.495,.505]+subpower and D_iD_j=X^(1+o(1)) on the retained pairs. An interior taper differs only on the full two endpoint collars, with O(D_iX^-delta+1) integer labels. Short clipped bins may be entirely collar. All endpoint atoms remain, and0<delta<.495 absorbs the +1. Its kth logarithmic derivative costs O_k(X^(k delta)).

Let Delta_i=U_i-V_i. At beta=.8749, ordinary Mertens and Abel summation at both endpoints give |U_i(a+it)|<< (1+|t|)D_i^(beta-a). Trivial collar counting gives |Delta_i|<<X^(-delta+o(1))D_i^(1-a), without short-interval Mobius cancellation. The exact identity is

    U_iU_j-V_iV_j=Delta_i U_j+U_i Delta_j-Delta_i Delta_j.

Mellin Plancherel applies to the complete difference on[-T,T], T=2sqrt(log X). The Gaussian and |eta(a+it)|<=|a+it|/a integrate all height polynomials; the shell weight costs(2X)^a. Each single-collar term has exponent at most.505+.495 beta-delta, while the double collar has exponent1-2delta. Summing the O(sqrt(log X)) ordered components yields

    ||G-Zpsi_X||_[X,2X] << X^(q+epsilon)+X^(-1+epsilon),
    q=max(.505+.495 beta-delta,1-2delta).             (AS2-1)

Every changed product and its mixed square is paid at the field-norm level. At delta=.064, q=.8740755, so gamma=.87449 leaves margin.0004145; gamma=.8748 leaves.0007245. Delta=.106 gives q=.8320755<5/6, and delta=.19 gives q=.7480755<3/4. The independent rational checks reproduce all four strict budgets.

For q<gamma, full all-dyadic every-epsilon norm exponent gamma for Zpsi is equivalent to the original fixed G exponent. Restore fixed G before its Mellin zero return; do not transform the moving cutoff family as one fixed series. The author's norms use X^(gamma+epsilon); squared norms use X^(2gamma+epsilon). One sentence in the Sol review calls the latter a bound for the norm. That is a notation error to correct in integration, not a different or weaker theorem.

No smooth complete moment is estimated. Any future integration by parts still pays X^(k delta), including the .064 per derivative in the displayed near target. Constants are for fixed parameters. This zeta/alternating source proves no new ordinary-character or ideal analogue. The explicit collar budget adds a source-specific interface to earlier sharp/smooth and thin-annulus work; it does not import those different masks or solve their arithmetic.

## D48: the block sum mode remains the hard source

For v_s(u)=g_tau(s-u),0<=u<=log2, the pivot after eliminating v_s from v_(s+epsilon) is

    epsilon^2 [||v_s'||^2-|<v_s,v_s'>|^2/||v_s||^2]+O(epsilon^3).

The bracket equals ||v_s||^2 Var_(v_s^2)(u)/tau^2. It is positive and has a positive minimum on the compact physical s interval. With epsilon=log(1+1/n), n in[X,2X], the pivot is comparable to n^-2. The larger eigenvalue is comparable to1, so condition number is comparable to n^2. This is a genuine native Gaussian conditioning statement; it is not a lower bound for the actual f3 energy in that direction, or for H.

For any fixed |a(n)|<=1, define b_B(j)=sum_((j-1)B<n<=jB)a(n), and V_B(x)=sum_j b_B(j)g_tau(log(jB/x)). Put k_x(t)=g_tau(log(t/x)). Its variation on(0,infinity) is2g_tau(0). On a block, each segment[n,jB] is contained in it, and at most B such segments cover any point. Hence

    |F_a(x)-V_B(x)| <= B integral_0^infinity |k_x'(t)|dt
                     =2B g_tau(0).                  (AS2-2)

This includes the first block, both infinite tails, every valuation and every signed coefficient. At0 the Gaussian is flat with limit0. No coefficient deletion or positive-submask monotonicity is used. For B_X=floor(X^theta) frozen for the entire shell and0<=theta<gamma, the complete norm exponent gamma for V_(B_X) is equivalent to that for fixed F_a. All interblock cross terms remain. This coordinate reduction does not reduce amplitudes: |b_B| can equal B.

For literal f3, f3(2j)=(1-2*1_(2 not dividing j))f3(j), so the displayed b_2 is correct for all powers of2. Multiplication by fixed chi preserves all ramified zeros. The independent checks verify this identity through j=600 and exact signed block masses for a quartic mod5 character, including its zeros. These finite facts do not certify an infinite moment.

For FIXED B and e_B(n)=Bceil(n/B),

    E_B(s)=sum_n a(n)[n^-s-e_B(n)^-s]

is holomorphic on Re s>0. The derivative integral bounds the summand by |s|B n^(-Re s-1); compact-set s derivatives add only summable log powers. On Re s>1, D_B=D_a-E_B by absolute rearrangement. Thus subtracting E_B preserves every pole of D_a in Re s>0, including order and principal part.

For a=f3 chi the literal Euler numerator is

    W_chi(s)=(1-2chi(2)2^-s)
      /[(1-chi(2)2^-s)^2(1-chi(3)3^-s)^2]
      *product_(p>=5)(1-2chi(p)p^-s)/(1-chi(p)p^-s)^2.

All ramified local factors are1. The infinite factors and inverses converge normally for Re s>1/2; their nonconstant terms begin at p^-2s. Prime>=5 numerator zeros lie left of1/2, denominator zeros on Re s=0, and the possible prime2 numerator zeros on Re s=1. Therefore W_chi is nonzero in1/2<Re s<1. The identity

    L(s,chi)D_B(s)=W_chi(s)-L(s,chi)E_B(s)            (AS2-3)

excludes a hypothetical L zero in that strip once a complete fixed-B moment continues D_B holomorphically there. Gaussian Mellin left tails are paid from the actual fixed coefficient source; the uniform bound(AS2-2) alone is not substituted for that left-tail proof. For moving B_X first use(AS2-2) to restore F_a and only then continue its fixed transform. Constants concern each fixed ordinary chi, with the usual principal-pole/right-edge qualifications. No growing-conductor or Eisenstein claim follows.

Accept the all-block specialization and fixed-B return, with W03/SBG/log-transport ancestry. The signed sum mode remains OPEN-F3; its budget is not added to D04's.

## D02 and the seven other first tests

For the actual finite Gaussian Gram M at distinct positive integer labels, M is positive definite: dividing a vanishing finite Gaussian combination by its common Gaussian leaves a sum of distinct real exponentials, whose derivative Vandermonde is nonsingular. This also covers complex source coefficients. Near singularity is compatible with exact positive definiteness.

The determinant lemma gives det(M+lambda cc*)/det M=1+lambda c*M^-1c. The desired energy is c*Mc. With v=Mc the corrected ratio is exactly1+lambda c*Mc. The repaired rank-one determinant and the shell Fredholm rank-one version encode the same original energy, not a weaker arithmetic input. Approximate Mc is subject to inverse-Gram amplification. The actual Gaussian tail or G13/G20 source error must be paid before a finite ratio returns to the fixed detector. D48's small pivot explains a possible primal/dual ratio of order X^4 in an innovation direction; it does not assert that literal f3 occupies that direction.

S08's matrix[[1,-1],[-1,1]] with c=(1,1) refutes monotonicity under deleting negative cross terms, at generic matrix scope. S06's irrational log2/log3 blocks the stated one-common-exponential polynomial substitution; multivariable resultants need their own diagonal restriction and height/error costs. S18 has not made arbitrary complex n^-s algebraic, and no denominator/conjugate height bound is supplied. These are failed bridges, not global impossibility theorems.

S46's unit-coefficient convolution recurrence forces mu. For general ordinary chi the recurrence contains chi(r) and yields mu(n)chi(n); matrix enlargement with the same scalar inverse cannot change it. A different nonlinear readout remains untested. S37 and S49 unitary gauges preserve norms, and zero-extended character values cannot be replaced by unit phases. A genuine cocycle also needs its loop products to match. S41's exact commutator is [C_Y,D_p]e_n=-1_(Y/p<n<=Y)e_(pn); the given p=2,Y=2 vector has quadratic form-1 despite trace0. Actual masked-boundary defects remain unpaid. These seven tests are independent of the three main developments and retain their narrow failure scopes.

**Changed additive branch near S29.** With a(n)=mu(n)chi(n), zero for n<=0, let c(n)=sum_(j=0)^r(-1)^j binom(r,j)a(n-jh), fixed h,r>=1. Exact reindexing gives F_c(x)=sum_m a(m)sum_j(-1)^j binom(r,j)H((m+jh)/x), H(t)=g_tau(log t), extended flat at t<=0. H is Schwartz. The finite-difference integral and the elementary W^(1,1) sampling bound yield

    |F_c(x)|<=h^r[x^(1-r)||H^(r)||_1+x^-r||H^(r+1)||_1], x>=1.

All terminal terms and original squareful/ramified zeros are included before differencing. The complete moment is O(X^(2-2r)) without arithmetic cancellation. Its Dirichlet series, however, converges normally in Re s>1-r because the rth difference of n^-s is O_compact(n^-Re(s)-r). In the exact expansion beyond N>rh, only 1/L(s+k,chi), k>=r, occurs, with its finite-prefix subtraction; all reciprocal arguments are then in Re>1. Thus original critical poles disappear. Writing C=N/L forces N to vanish at those zeros. The cheap field has lost the necessary signal. This is a valid actual-coefficient countertest on the changed additive branch, not a test of the original multiplicative/log-scale S29 and not a refutation of the paid multiplicative filters in G51--52.

**S52 visibility.** The actual JN transform is unitary with factor1/Q on a group of sizeQ^2, Q=qq'. Full physical source W includes the entire short d-sum, both mark arrays, sharp masks, both projectors and natural zeros. Support counts are O(K),O(L),O(L), with the original injection conditions.     kappa <= C_orig[K(q+q'-1)/Q+L/q+L/q'].

There is no assumption that these losses are independent. At N=K Z^.003 this tends to0, so for W nonzero the visible fraction captured in J fixed row frequencies is at most C KJ/[Q(1-kappa)]. S31 needs finite patches for the actual complete field and a uniform infinite return. The following is a source interface; no interval solver was run.

Fix a computable positive tau, for example tau=1, and a(n)=f3(n)chi(n) for one fixed ordinary chi, including natural zeros. Let ell=log2. For X>=1 the logarithmic derivative obeys

    |d/dy F_a(e^y)| <= 2K_tau X, log X<=y<=log(2X),
    K_tau=exp(tau)/sqrt(tau)+2/tau.                  (AS2-4)

Proof: for H(t)=|g_tau'(log t)|, its L1 norm is at most exp(tau)/sqrt(tau) by Gaussian Cauchy--Schwarz, and its variation is at most integral|g_tau''(u)|du<=2/tau. The unit-mesh sum bound gives sum_n H(n/x)<=x||H||_1+Var(H)<=K_tau x for x>=1. This bounds the derivative termwise by |a|<=1. For a positive integer N, y_l=log X+l ell/N,0<=l<N, replace a finite field F_R on each grid cell by its left endpoint value. The L2 error on the WHOLE shell is at most

All signs stay inside each sample; this is a source-value interpolation error, not independent random samples. To truncate, take R=ceil(2X exp(Csqrt(log X))). For Csqrt(log X)>tau, decreasing-tail integration gives the explicit uniform bound

    |F_a-F_R| <= T_X,
    T_X=2X exp(tau/2) * tau/(Csqrt(log X)-tau)
                    *g_tau(Csqrt(log X)-tau).       (AS2-6)

Since R is an integer, the sum beyond R is bounded by that integral. T_X=X^(1-C^2/(2tau)+o(1)); every low integer remains in F_R, and the full upper tail is paid. Suppose rigorous finite evaluations enclose F_R(e^y_l) in disks centered at z_l with radii rho_l. Then the actual certificate is

      sqrt[(ell/N) sum_l (|z_l|+rho_l)^2]
        +2K_tau ell^(3/2) X/N+sqrt(ell) T_X.          (AS2-7)

Proof is the piecewise-constant norm, pointwise enclosure, and two norm triangles. Every n,m interaction survives inside |sum_(n<=R)a(n)g_tau(...)|^2 before the finite enclosure. No unsigned surrogate is substituted. Choose N>=X^(1-gamma+eta), eta>0 fixed, C with1-C^2/(2tau)<gamma-eta, and sufficiently precise enclosures. The N power is the cost of THIS Lipschitz scheme, not a lower bound on every analytic interpolation scheme: W43 already supplies a different polylogarithmic analytic projection.

The first unpaid input is the finite signed sample energy for ALL sufficiently large dyadics, with one uniform C_epsilon for each epsilon. There is a precise generic obstruction to inferring infinity from finitely many bounded-source patches. For any fixed N0 let a(n)=1_(n>N0). On every fixed compact x range its Gaussian field tends uniformly to0 as N0 tends to infinity, while for each fixed N0 and x tending to infinity it equals exp(tau/2)x+O_tau(N0+1). The latter follows by the same sum-versus-integral variation bound. ## Own uniform audit S26: literal involution and the surviving source parity

Test the fixed involution T(h,s,s')=(-h,-s,-s') on the actual JN9 finite group for distinct good degree-one prime norms q,q', Q=qq'. Keep the entire W=sum_d W_d from JN6/10, both physical coprimality projectors, both mark arrays, sharp masks, source/ray zeros, two heights and CRT phase.     K(h,s,s')=chi_pi(h)^3 chi_pi'(h)^3
                        chi_pi(s)^2 chi_pi'(s')^4.

Natural zero support is T-invariant: h is a unit at both primes, s and s' are nonzero. Since chi(-1)=+-1 for a sextic character,

    K(Tz)=epsilon_(pi,pi') K(z),
    epsilon=chi_pi(-1)^5 chi_pi'(-1)^7
            =chi_pi(-1)chi_pi'(-1)
            =(-1)^[(q-1)/6+(q'-1)/6].               (AS2-8)

This is not uniformly -1. Norm pairs13/19 give -1;19/31 give+1, both admissible distinct split rational norms. An independent exact residue-exponent check exhausts61,009 and346,921 triples respectively, including every zero. These finite checks verify the kernel identity, not an asymptotic H bound or a choice of actual source arrays.

Let R_epsilon f(z)=(f(z)+epsilon f(Tz))/2. On the full finite group it is an orthogonal parity projection, and exact change of variables gives

    sum_z K(z) What(z)=sum_z K(z) R_epsilon What(z)
                     =sum_z K(z) Fourier(R_epsilon W)(z). (AS2-9)

The physical reflection acts simultaneously on(R,P,P'); the plus/minus signs in JN7 still give Fourier(TW)(z)=What(Tz). There is no additional Q, root or density factor. All fixed pair weights b(pi)conj(b(pi')), CRT zeta, C0 factors and ordered pair exclusions sit outside this equality unchanged. Reflection of the actual ZERO-EXTENDED coefficient function is essential: a primary-generator/ray mask need not be invariant, and arbitrary original mark arrays need not be even or odd.

For epsilon=-1 only the odd part contributes, so even W suffices for exact cancellation. For epsilon=+1 only the even part contributes, so odd W suffices. Other signed cancellations are not excluded. Neither symmetry follows from conductor/projector supports: coefficient phases, short-core weights, mark arrays and ray factors can break parity. Thus the exact pairwise positive bound is at most(q-1)(q'-1)||R_epsilon W||_2, since ||K||_2=(q-1)(q'-1). This projection may reduce norm, but its mere contractivity supplies no scale power and its positive prime-pair sum can be much too expensive. To return a full result one must estimate the complete signed sum of(AS2-9) with the original pair weights, exact Jacobi subtraction and any original transport error, at raw target Z^epsilon G K S(N,L)sqrt(Omega1 Omega2)P_orig; only afterward apply N^(-1)G^(-2). All other H branches and original tails remain obligations. A fixed prime-pair parity identity is not the needed H theorem.

 .41M\le n_1,n_2\le.44M,\qquad .03M\le z\le.04M,
 \qquad n_1+n_2+\frac{111}{25}z\le M,

the same actual natural moment satisfies

 \sum_{k\ {\rm eligible}}
 |S_{k,1}(Z^{n_1})S_{k,2}(Z^{n_2})Q_{k,I}|^2
 \ll Z^{M+\epsilon}\mathcal H_J.                 \tag{L44}

\[

 7/1250<a<6881/975000.

### The physical improvement

PH keeps the common forced ideal inside the divisor interpolation instead
of estimating every pair by F=1. For a dyadic block with relative conductor
R at most T and forced norm F at least V, it proves

\[
\sum |\mathcal C|
\ll \frac{Z^\epsilon}{Y}
\min\left\{\frac{T^{3/4}}{\sqrt Q\,V^{1/3}},
                 \frac{T^{1/2}}{V^{5/6}}\right\}.
\]

The common ideal is
\([d(a)/(d(a),e^2),d(b)/(d(b),d^2)]\), where
\(D=Gd,E=Ge,(d,e)=1\), and \(d(a)=a/\operatorname{rad}(a)\).
Thus relative conductor, individual active conductor, forced norm and
true gcd remain different parameters. The exact prime-mark-supported
example in PH reaches relative exponent .66233287384 beyond FR's
.57629956232 cutoff. It demonstrates additional supported paid sectors,
not a lower bound for covariance. The F=1 complement is still substantial.

### What the short-row and cubic estimates remove

NP uses sixth-power reconstruction with its exact all-power deletion
inverse. A finite fixed-prime restoration identity keeps the original
Guo exclusion set unchanged; the maximal-scale lemma handles every
Schwartz tail without a hidden common-column-scale assumption. For
\(H_G\ge D\) its bound already has the desired order. For
\(H_G=D^{1-\delta}\), \(0<\delta\le.01\), it gives
\(D^{1-\delta/6+\epsilon}\), leaving the factor \(D^{5\delta/6}\).

NP19 identifies its invariant term. Guo's \(47/375\) stays conditional.

SR uses the exact fixed-class character identity
\(\overline{\chi_c(n^2)}=\rho_d(c)\chi_c(n)\), with every natural

the quadratic class d is fixed. At \(K=D^{.87653}\), \(\gamma=1/4\)
and \(\delta=.02\), it pays cube labels through \(D^{.03449}\).
Applying separate fixed-twist UM bounds to a moving diagonal would
still lose H; even uniform constants would not fix that quantifier
error. SR18 is the exact joint moment still needed.

### Why two attractive shortcuts fail

SF's witness uses \(n=Wp q\), \(n'=Wr s\), with the four primes in
separated admissible boxes. Coalescing **all** allocations gives
coefficient 4, not cancellation, while the profile product is positive.
The prior PO local prime-square cancellations are retained. What remains
must exploit signs between different completed products; another local
absolute-value estimate cannot supply the exponent 1.74898.

SC proves that sending the Möbius removal cutoff to infinity moves the
selected main rather than disposing of it. Its auxiliary B2.29 prime
packet gives an explicit obstruction to a uniform coefficient-only
small-core estimate in the original short-divisor corridor. Those
auxiliary coefficients are not the physical infinity coefficient.
For the actual source, SC14 instead retains the full
\(\overline{\alpha(p)}\gamma_2(p)\nu(p)\) Gauss phase. Bounding that
first moment with its marks and deletions, or proving cancellation with
other dual cores, is a substantive remaining step.

The leading three routes remain physical covariance, all-branch H and
frozen-dyad Möbius energy. The precise surviving tasks are:

## 4. D3 / protected wildcard X28: interpolation does not remove residual debt

Suppose an admissible polynomial p also satisfies p(z_j)F(z_j)=F0 at finitely many nodes, with multiplicity allowed. Include z=0 once, since p0=1 already enforces that node. Nodes used as safe data must correspond to known nonzero L values, for example Re(s_j)>1. Let

    B(z)=product_j (z-z_j)/(1-conjugate(z_j)z).

The complete residual e=pF-F0 is divisible by B, and e/B belongs to H2 with the same norm: for finitely many zeros this follows by analytic division and the unit boundary modulus of B. At a hypothetical zero w of F not among the safe nodes,

    ||e||^2 >= |F0|^2(1-|w|^2)/|B(w)|^2.             (15)

The reproduction-kernel bound for H2 proves this directly. When B=z, it is (10). When the first m Taylor conditions are exactly fitted, B=z^m and the floor is |F0|^2(1-|w|^2)|w|^(-2m). Extra exact sample matches do not themselves make the full error smaller; they can force a larger invisible complement. This is compatible with the old invariant-subspace correction: no artificial additional norm cost is charged for dividing an error already known to lie in BH2. Equation (15) is the resulting point-evaluation bound for the divided error, not a claim that inner division expands its norm.

The exact example F=1-z/r and the Taylor inverse p_N=sum_(j=0)^N(z/r)^j gives

    e(z)=-(z/r)^(N+1), ||e||^2=r^(-2N-2).             (16)

It fits every Taylor condition through degree N at the safe origin, while its full residual grows if the source has an interior zero r<1. At r=1/2, N=4 it is 1024. The complete complement, not interpolation precision at the sampled nodes, detects the obstruction. For a fixed high zero, (11) and |w|^(-2m) show a fixed-anchor scale m of order T^2/(beta-gamma) for order-one exponential amplification. This is consistent with N29's older moving-anchor analysis; it is not a new all-height estimate.

The live escape is a signed arithmetic estimate for the full residual in (13), possibly using a nontrivial safe-node geometry and the exact divided residual. Conditioning, source formation and the complete tail must be included. No such estimate is proved.
