### Frozen-dyad balanced finite form

Set, for large \(X\),
\[
L=\log X,\quad Y=\lfloor\sqrt X/L^2\rfloor,\quad
T_l=X/L^4,\quad T_u=XL^2,\quad J=\lceil8L^6\rceil.
\]
Use [restricted research revision]'s fixed smooth cutoffs \(\rho,\chi\), and define on \(x\in[X,2X]\)
\[
\mathcal B_X(x)=
\sum_{d,e>Y}\mu(d)\mu(e)
\rho(de/T_l)\chi(de/T_u)
\sum_{\ell\le J}\phi(\ell de/x).
\]
For every \(A>0\) and fixed Euler derivative order \(r\),
\[
(x\partial_x)^r\{S_\phi(x)-\mathcal B_X(x)\}
=O_{A,r}(X^{-A}). \tag{T09.2}
\]
This is a bounded extension of [restricted research revision] V7–V8, not a new cancellation estimate.

To prove it, apply the exact Möbius convolution identity with the same arithmetic cutoff \(Y\) throughout the dyad. The short Möbius term is exponentially small. In the Type-I term \(de/x\le L^{-4}\); lower removed Type-II products have \(de/x\le2L^{-4}\). [restricted research revision] V6's complete Poisson cancellation bounds these by \(e^{-cL^2}\) before truncating the \(\ell\)-sum. The infinite upper product tail has \(de/x\ge L^2/2\) and is likewise superpolynomially small after divisor counting. On the retained support \(Jde/x\ge4L^2\), so truncating \(\ell>J\) costs the same. There are \(O(XL^3)\) retained pairs, all with
\[
\sqrt X/L^2<d,e<2\sqrt X L^4.
\]
Every arithmetic cutoff is fixed on the dyad; differentiating only changes the smooth profile. The same endpoint estimates hold for each fixed Euler derivative. Replacing \(S_\phi\) by \(\mathcal B_X\) in (T09.1) changes energy by \(O_A(X^{-A})\) after reserving a larger preliminary \(A\).

At \(a=.87449\), the target squared-energy exponent is \(1.74898\). The gain over the inherited baseline squared-energy bound is \(0.000793294079928262\ldots\). The energy estimate remains open; averaging does not erase a hypothetical \(x^\rho\) mode.

## 1. The complete arithmetic average

Let R be the positive integers or the nonzero integral ideals of
K=Q(omega). Write q_a=a or Na, respectively. Fix tau>0, a finite prime set S,
and one ordinary Dirichlet character eta, or one finite-order,
trivial-infinity Hecke character. Retain the original zero extension.

    U=U_1,  g_tau(v)=(2*pi*tau)^(-1/2) exp(-v^2/(2*tau)).       (R1)

Q denotes a finite radical outside S. All sums in this review are COMPLETE
Gaussian sums. Fix the label sets

    Eset={e: q_e<=E, (e,S)=1},

for T>=1,

    A_Q(T)=kappa T h(Q)+O(sqrt(T) S_1/2(Q))                  [K],
    A_Q^sf(T)=kappa T D(Q)/zeta_K(2)
                     +O(sqrt(T) log(2T) S_1/2(Q))          [K],
    A_Q(T)=T h(Q)+O(d(Q)),
    A_Q^sf(T)=T D(Q)/zeta(2)+O(sqrt(T) d(Q))                [Z]. (R3)

There is no Q<=T restriction. In the squarefree main term the factors
h(Q) prod_(p|Q)(1-q_p^-2)^(-1) are exactly D(Q).

Consequently the two avoidance probabilities for a fixed a have main terms

    A(a)=prod_(p|a,p notin S) q_p/(q_p+1),
    B(a)=prod_(p|a,p notin S) (q_p-1)/q_p.

Their product is w(a)=prod_(p|a,p notin S)(q_p-1)/(q_p+1).
The errors after division by the EXACT sample counts are, respectively,
F^-1/2 log(2F) S_1/2(rad a), E^-1/2 S_1/2(rad a) over K;
F^-1/2 d(rad a), E^-1 d(rad a) over Z. Since all probabilities and
main terms lie in[0,1], the product error is bounded by the sum of the
two errors. No additional mixed error or independence of prime events is
assumed; independence here is simply the Cartesian choice of f and e.

With the ONE fixed field

    W(x)=sum_a mu_R(a)eta(a)1_((a,S)=1)w(a)g_tau(log(q_a/x)),

the full comparison is

    |P_FE(x)-W(x)| << x log(2F)(F^-1/2+E^-1/2)              [K],
    |P_FE(x)-W(x)| << x(1+log(2+x))(F^-1/2+E^-1)           [Z]. (R4)

These bounds include both infinite source ends and hold uniformly for x>0
when the label counts have reached their fixed-S asymptotic range. Indeed
sum_(q_a<=T) S_1/2(rad a)<<T and sum_(n<=T)d(rad n)<<T log(2T).
Gaussian integration gives the stated whole-source bounds; at x<1 the
left tail is smaller than every fixed power of x. The complete sources
also satisfy |U_Q(x)|<<x uniformly in Q by the absolute coefficient count.

Minor clarification1: the author's(A2) should explicitly say T>=1 or replace
log(2T) by log(2+T). No use in the report requires a logarithm of negative
sign at tiny T. The underlying A1 remains valid at T<1.

## 2. Exact Euler multiplier, inverse, and all-height return

For Re(s)>1, absolute Fubini gives

    Mellin W(s)=exp(tau*s^2/2) H_eta(s)/L^S(s,eta),
    H_eta(s)=prod_(p notin S)
       (1-w_p eta(p)q_p^-s)/(1-eta(p)q_p^-s).                (R5)

Write z=eta(p)q_p^-s, delta_p=2/(q_p+1), w_p=1-delta_p.
The two local expansions are exactly

    H_p=1+delta_p sum_(j>=1)z^j,
    H_p^-1=1-delta_p sum_(j>=1)w_p^(j-1)z^j.               (R6)

For each sigma>0 their nonconstant absolute coefficient mass is
O_sigma(q_p^(-1-sigma)) apart from finitely many primes. Both Dirichlet
coefficient series are therefore in l1_sigma. Both local factors are
nonzero; normal convergence makes H and H^-1 holomorphic on Re(s)>0.
Factors with eta(p)=0 are simply1.

Coefficient convolution gives the full Gaussian identities W=h*U and
U=h_inv*W, where convolution means sum_d h(d)U(x/q_d). Absolute l1_1
convergence justifies formation. For either p=1 or2, the all-shell norm

    ||V||_(sigma,p)=sup_(X>0) X^-sigma ||V||_(Lp([X,2X],dx/x))

satisfies the corresponding operator bound sum_d|h(d)|q_d^-sigma, in
BOTH directions. Thus U and W have exactly the same every-epsilon shell
exponent for every gamma>0. This is a paid representation, not a gain.

Freeze F_X=X^v,E_X=X^r for the ENTIRE dyadic shell[X,2X], with v,r fixed
before X. If, for every epsilon>0 and every sufficiently large shell,

    ||P_(F_X,E_X)||_1 <<_(eta,epsilon) X^(gamma+epsilon),    (R7)

and gamma in(0,1), the error(R4) is paid when

    min(v/2,r/2)>=1-gamma [K],
    min(v/2,r)>=1-gamma   [Z].                            (R8)

Equality is allowed with the every-epsilon convention; exact endpoint
constants without epsilon are not claimed. First apply(R4) to obtain the
fixed W bound. Then its Mellin integral is holomorphic in Re(s)>gamma,
including each fixed derivative. Multiplication by L^S continues(R5),
and the nonzero right side excludes every zero there. The possible
principal pole at1 is not treated as a zero. Finite Euler deletions have
no zeros in Re(s)>0. Every finite height is included; no moving-height
theorem or final height ceiling has been imported.

For ordinary characters, gamma is common across all positive moduli and
all characters, including imprimitive characters; constants and thresholds
may depend on the fixed member. For K the conclusion covers precisely
the stated finite-order trivial-infinity family. The K estimate alone is
not an ordinary-character theorem. Source-independent return here means
independence of the unfinished PR15 source premise; it still needs the
usual continued L-function and, crucially, the unproved estimate(R7).

Minor clarification2: if a character is presented imprimitive modulo a
larger modulus, its natural zero primes include ALL modulus primes, not
only primes of its primitive conductor. Retain those zeros. In the
positive-array argument below, either include them in S or use the fixed
set S+=S union{p:eta(p)=0}; this makes the asserted unit modulus exact.
This finite correction changes no exponent or counting conclusion.

## 3. The genuine sextic bank and its recovery factor

Use the [restricted research revision] global primary generators and exact zero-extended symbol
psi_k(a)=chi_a(k). Their multiplicativity eliminates an untracked unit
in the representative of f^2 e^6. On every good ideal, including common
prime factors,

    chi_a(f)^4 chi_a(f^2 e^6)=1_((a,fe)=1).              (R9)

On coprime pairs the exponent is divisible by6; otherwise at least one
positive exponent preserves the symbol's zero. Treating a cancelled
character as the everywhere-one character would be wrong.

For X=Z^N,F=Z^V,E=Z^R define the genuinely new column family

    T_fk(x)=X^-1/2 sum_a mu_K(a)eta(a)1_((a,S)=1)
                  chi_a(k)chi_a(f)^4 g_tau(log(q_a/x)).    (R10)

The non-character column coefficient is independent of live f,k. On
each Gaussian annulus it has the normalized bounded l2 mass required by
the generic sieves. It is NOT the canonical Gauss coefficient a0, the
old physical numerator, or G115's completed Mobius divisor sum. The
ordinary source has not thereby acquired a native sextic identity.

At k=f^2e^6, T_fk=X^-1/2 U_rad(fe). For each fixed f the map e to k
is injective by ideal valuations, and q_k<=4F^2E^6. The exact selected
pair count is N_F N_E; possible repetitions across different f remain
distinct entries of the joint bank. With M=2V+6R and

    B_FE(X)=(N_F N_E)^(-1) sum_(f,e) ||U_rad(fe)||_2^2,
    J(X)=F^-1 sum_f sum_(q_k<=4Z^M) ||T_fk||_2^2,

positive enlargement gives

    B_FE(X) <= C_S X E^-1 J(X).                          (R11)

This is the actual recovery factor. There is no Urow^-1 divisor, no
additional division by F after F^-1 already normalized the f count,
and no discarded inducing/principal rows. Jensen and shell Cauchy give
||P_FE||_1<=sqrt(log2) sqrt(B_FE), so a complete B bound of exponent
2gamma suffices for(R7).

The Gaussian is handled by a complete annular decomposition: the j-th
profile and each prescribed derivative have polynomial-in-j times
exp(-c j^2) norms, while sieve prices grow at most exponentially in|j|.
Minkowski sums all annuli. Alternatively a C sqrt(log Z) annular cutoff
has arbitrarily small power tails by the absolute source bound. No tail,
short source or extra height/profile dependence is left out.

Conditional on the two named sieve inputs, [restricted research revision] applies to this fixed
coefficient class, and gives J<<Z^(Emix+epsilon), where

    Emix(M,N,V)=sup_(0<=t<=M) [(M-t)/6+min(C(t,N),t+L)],
    C(t,N)=max(t,N,5t/6+N/3,t/3+5N/6),
    L=max(0,N-V,(2N-V)/3).                              (R12)

Both estimates inside the minimum see the SAME complete positive norm
and the same fixed hole on each repetition layer. The cubic average
does not permit f-dependent coefficients. In particular substituting
k=f^2 BEFORE applying a free f-average cancels the character phase;
it does not leave an independent cubic family. A source-specific bound
on that correlated diagonal would be new arithmetic, not [restricted research revision] again.

Since C(V,N)>=N and V+L>=N, the member t=V gives

    N+Emix(2V+6R,N,V)-R >= 2N+V/6.                     (R13)

This obstructs THIS certificate below gamma=1 even before(R8). The two
author examples convert correctly to gamma97/96 and169/168. These are
upper-bound prices, not lower bounds on the actual Mobius norm.

## 4. Exact scope of the coefficient-blind obstruction

Replace mu_K(a) in(R10) by the ONE fixed sequence
b(a)=mu_K(a)^2 conjugate(eta(a)) on good ideals. On the additional fixed
natural-zero complement, b(a)eta(a)=mu_K(a)^2. It is bounded, supported
on squarefree ideals, independent of f,k,X, and satisfies the same
normalized column mass as the original mu_K coefficients.

For every fixed A and every epsilon>0, elementary prime products give
S_1/2(Q)<<_epsilon q_Q^epsilon and D(Q)>>_epsilon q_Q^-epsilon.
Applying(R3) to S+Q shows uniformly for q_Q<=X^A that

    #{a squarefree: X<q_a<=2X,(a,S+Q)=1} >> X^(1-epsilon). (R14)

Choose the auxiliary product epsilon small enough that the square-root
error is below this main term. The Gaussian is bounded below by a
positive tau-dependent constant on q_a,x in[X,2X]. Every positive
masked field therefore has size X^(1-o(1)) throughout the shell, so

    B_FE(X)>=X^(2-o(1)),
    J(X)>=Z^(N+R-o(1)).                                (R15)

The same example makes the signed-average output positive and of order
X^(1-o(1)); it does not merely obstruct squaring. Thus arbitrary-column
information cannot prove the necessary recovered power below X^2.
An improved generic operator bound could remove the EXCESS V/6 in(R13)
and would still leave the arithmetic saving2cN unpaid. Neither(R14) nor
(R15) lower-bounds the actual mu_K source, canonical Gauss coefficients,
or a coherent signed observation with additional arithmetic hypotheses.

## 5. Reviewer extension: omit e and keep the true squarefree label

The author's setup allows a fixed e=1, but did not develop this cheaper
boundary. Define it explicitly, rather than applying the two-sided
limit weight with E=1:

    P_F^sf(x)=N_F^-1 sum_f U_f(x),
    W_A(x)=sum_a mu_R(a)eta(a)1_((a,S)=1) A(a)g_tau(log(q_a/x)).

Here A_p=q_p/(q_p+1). Squarefree counting alone proves

    |P_F^sf-W_A| << x F^-1/2 log(2F)                 [K],
    |P_F^sf-W_A| << x F^-1/2(1+log(2+x))            [Z]. (R16)

The new multiplier is prod(1-A_p z)/(1-z), with
delta_p=1/(q_p+1); both it and its inverse are in every l1_sigma,
sigma>0. Hence the complete all-character return and exponent
equivalence with U remain. F=X^v, v>=2(1-gamma), pays(R16).

Its genuine principal rows are k=f^2, M=2V, with exact signal recovery
B_F^sf<=C X J, and the same zero-preserving identity(R9). No unit,
conductor, label or tail convention changes. This removes an unnecessary
long e^6 range while preserving a genuine f-labelled source.

More generally, for fixed N,V, subtracting the REAL recovery exponent
from(R12) gives exactly

    Emix(2V+6R,N,V)-R
      =sup_(0<=t<=2V+6R) [(2V-t)/6+min(C(t,N),t+L)].     (R17)

The integrand is independent of R. Extra repetitions only enlarge its
domain. Thus the recovered generic price is nondecreasing in R>=0;
the best price within this squarefree-label branch occurs at e=1.
This is a statement about the given upper envelope, not actual norm
monotonicity or equality of the different fixed detector weights.

Set N=1 and v=V/N. Direct evaluation of [restricted research revision]'s full envelope gives

    Emix(2v,1,v)=1+v/6              (0<=v<=1/3),
                  5/6+2v/3         (1/3<=v<=1/2),
                  1/3+5v/3         (1/2<=v<=1),
                  2v              (v>=1).               (R18)

All pieces are increasing, so at target c=1-gamma the cheapest allowed
squarefree-label choice is v=2c, in the every-epsilon sense. For c<=1/6
the best recovered energy price is **2+c/3**, compared with the needed
**2-2c**. Their gap is **7c/3**, sharper and cheaper than retaining both
cofactors. For1/6<=c<=1/4 that price is11/6+4c/3 and the gap is
10c/3-1/6. The endpoints agree. These are exact certificate deficits.

| Target c | Required energy exponent | Cheapest f-only certificate | Unpaid gap |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| .12 |1.76|2.04|.28|
| conditional .1251459636 |1.7497080728|2.0417153212|.2920072484|
|1/6|5/3|37/18|7/18|
|1/4|3/2|13/6|2/3|

The unlabelled one-sided e average has weight1-1/q and a different
normalization. At these targets its best named all-row prices are
worse (prices.json records them), so it does not rescue the construction.
The author already correctly identified that variant; the f-only
calculation and monotonicity(R17) are reviewer additions.

## 6. Reviewer extension: exact polynomial-hole and Gram transfers

For each fixed finite radical Q, the complete field satisfies

    U_Q(x)=sum_(d Q-smooth) eta(d) U(x/q_d),
    U(x)=sum_(d|Q) mu(d)eta(d) U_Q(x/q_d).                (R19)

These follow coefficientwise from the finite Euler factors and are
absolutely convergent Gaussian identities. For every sigma,delta>0,

    prod_(p|Q)(1-q_p^-sigma)^(-1) <<_(sigma,delta) q_Q^delta.

Thus if the ONE original U has every-epsilon shell Lp exponent gamma>0,
p=1 or2, all its polynomial-sized holes q_Q<=X^A have the same shell
exponent, uniformly with an arbitrarily small extra loss. Small shifted
scales are included through the Gaussian left tail. Q is frozen during
each convolution; no moving family is falsely identified across scales.

It follows that, whenever(R8), or the appropriate one-sided error gate,
is paid, the complete averaged POSITIVE cofactor energy bound
B_FE<<X^(2gamma+epsilon) is equivalent to U's complete shell-L2 exponent
gamma. The reverse direction is Jensen, fixed-source approximation and
the fixed inverse(R6). This equivalence does not identify the L1 and L2
hypotheses. It identifies where the same unresolved arithmetic survives.

There is also an exact full limiting Gram for the f-only average.
Let K_X(a,b)=integral_X^(2X) g_tau(log(q_a/x))g_tau(log(q_b/x)) dx/x
and p_F(d)=N_F^-1 #{f in Fset:(f,d)=1}. The finite positive energy is

    B_F^sf=sum_(a,b) mu(a)mu(b)eta(a)bar(eta(b))
                           K_X(a,b) p_F(rad(ab)).        (R20)

All a,b are S-coprime. The averaged FIELD squared instead uses
p_F(a)p_F(b); confusing these loses label covariance. In the fixed
limit, p_F(rad(ab))->A(rad(ab)), and

    A(rad(ab))=A(a)A(b) sum_(d|gcd(a,b)) q_d^-1

on the actual squarefree a,b support.

Consequently its full limiting energy is

    sum_(d squarefree,(d,S)=1) q_d^-1
       ||sum_(d|a) mu(a)eta(a)A(a)g_tau(log(q_a/x))||_2^2. (R21)

The d=1 term is ||W_A||_2^2; all other terms are the positive label
variance. Absolute Gaussian majorants justify the complete identities.
They do not bound that variance or its signed inner arithmetic.

Replacing(R20) by(R21) at a GROWING shell costs
O(X^2 F^-1/2 log(2F)) over K, or
O(X^2 F^-1/2(1+log(2+X))^2) over Z. To pay this ENERGY approximation
at exponent2-2c requires v>=4c, not the v>=2c needed for the FIELD
return(R16). This is a concrete guard against an apparently free limit
replacement. The exact finite kernel(R20) avoids that extra approximation.

## 7. Retention and next decisive work

Retain the author's complete average, counting proof, zero-free fixed
multiplier, exact principal channels, generic-envelope failure and fixed
positive counterexample, together with the frozen ten-route slate. No
undeveloped route is newly declared impossible. Retain(R16)-(R21) as
reviewer developments with their precise error/conditional-input scope.

The cheapest next arithmetic contract in this construction is the exact
f-only signed field average with F=X^(2c), frozen across the shell, or
the complete finite signed Gram(R20) at its requested power. A proposal
must use the actual mu_R prime signs and retain natural zeros. The field
average may exploit coherent cancellation across labels; the stronger
positive-bank route must retain its entire label covariance. Testing only
column mass,
an independent f,k sieve, or a limiting covariance without its error
cannot meet that contract. The fixed positive sequence above is a cheap
decisive rejection test for any proposed coefficient-uniform shortcut.

There is no new numerical endpoint, no external admission, no completed
PR15 estimate, no repair of the distinct PR26 high-row bridge, and no
change to the canonical R_U,hard+R_N,hard problem. The complete source
return is useful precisely because it states the missing arithmetic
without silently importing those premises.

### D33.2 Quantitative Gaussian cancellation for a growing model

Put h_tau(t)=g_tau(log t) for t>0, extended by zero for t<=0. It is Schwartz and flat at zero; every fixed derivative has a finite L1 norm (current G7 supplies an explicit bound). Expand the periodic sequence by discrete Fourier transform,

    e_P(n)=sum_(k=1,...,Q-1) b_k exp(2pi i k n/Q),
    |b_k|<=1.

There is no k=0 term because of (D33.1). Poisson summation and m>=2 integrations by parts show

    |W_P(x)|
      <= C_(tau,m) x sum_(k=1,...,Q-1) sum_(j in Z)
                              |x(j-k/Q)|^-m
      <= C'_(tau,m) x^(1-m) Q^m.                      (D33.2)

The reindexing r=Qj-k runs over nonzero integers not divisible by Q; their absolute m-series is at most 2zeta(m). The constant is independent of Q,P,x. No arbitrary ell-dependent mask is inserted into G9; this is direct Poisson on the stated periodic coefficient sequence.

Choose fixed 0<a<1 and the explicitly growing sieve

    z_X=a log X/loglog X,
    P_X={p prime:p<=z_X,p!=3}.

For sufficiently large X it includes 2. The elementary bound Q<=floor(z_X)!<=z_X^z_X gives Q<=X^(a+o(1)), without PNT. Uniformly on the CLOSED shell [X,2X],

    |W_(P_X)(x)| <= X^(1-m(1-a)+o(1)).                (D33.3)

Given any A0>0, choose one fixed m>(1+A0)/(1-a). Then W_(P_X)=O(X^-A0), after using a strict margin to absorb the o(1). This finite-prime model therefore passes every candidate Gaussian moment exponent, including gamma=3/4. That favorable result proves nothing about the full f3 field.

# W51: hard-cutoff fugacity deflation and the surviving prime boundary

**No increase in c is proved.** The accepted input remains c8=.12514261, theta8=.87485739, in the pinned source-relative framework. This batch freezes 30 seeds, tests exactly six, and develops two bounded mathematical outputs. The principal output is a full-cutoff fugacity root theorem and an exact two-branch arithmetic criterion with a complete ordinary-character zero-exclusion return. Its new arithmetic estimate is open. The second output records exact Schur/chain/cascade boundary identities and a scoped absolute-price obstruction; it does not lower-bound the signed Mertens sum.

All arguments below are ordinary written mathematics; no formalization or proof-assistant work was performed. Only the assigned ignored tree was written. No provider, child, canonical, tracker, or Git mutation was undertaken. Claims of novelty are limited to the passages searched in this project's record, never the literature.

## Frozen generation and sampling

The compact problem and immutable recipe hashes matched the assignment. Before reading detailed history, all 30 seeds were fully read back and frozen in `seeds.json` (28,856 bytes), SHA256 `49e5b066613303f6f2da07e71add4b09bef20233c6f3ebb0d547c59e356aca4c`. The root-only seed event preceded detailed-history intake. The six groups follow the recipe: two free groups, two p<.10 groups, and two p<.01 groups. Literal p is subjective typicality, not success probability.

Reserved strongest: S03, S16. Reserved high-headroom: S23. Uniform draws used every numerically eligible unreserved candidate across all groups, in increasing ID order. Each complete pool was written, read, and hashed in a completed tool call before the corresponding draw. The frozen SHA256 rejection sampler used the recipe seed `332214911731599467436410963675643056672`; counters 0,1,2 each accepted on the first block. No rerolls or recipe sampler reruns occurred.

| Remaining literal p<.01 | `pool-2.json`, SHA256 `81f303b31b57289dfe27521cbe6c30967f806796fa7627bfa57f0c151105e984` | 11 | 1 | 0 | S09 |
| All remaining | `pool-3.json`, SHA256 `169a22051ec1c8ccba00c22ba9073f27654f6f2c9292ab32f59caf064f27a211` | 25 | 2 | 0 | S01 |

The exact receipt digests and counter material are in `draw-1.json` through `draw-3.json`. The selected set is **S03, S16, S23, S18, S09, S01**. No candidate was substituted after deduplication or failure.

## History contacts and what is actually different

Post-freeze intake used `[restricted mathematical source]`, `[restricted mathematical source]`, `[restricted mathematical source]`, and the exact relevant sources listed in `sources.json`.

- S03 overlaps W35 R35.28 and G32's finite inverse/readout debt; G69 already proves zero feedback for its particular causal three-block split. The present arbitrary interleaved divisor partition is different from that causal split, but the block identity is classical algebra. Its nonzero-return example prevents an overbroad inference from G69.
- S16 and S18 overlap W31's innovation inverse, G47/G52, G70, and G73's finite future-plus-Euler reconstruction. They are not new bridges. A literal ordinary-mu sharp-cutoff check is retained, with no claimed cancellation gain.
- S01 overlaps the original fixed-order completion and G83-G85's substantially stronger growing-order completion and moment return. The simple residual cascade is not credited as a replacement for those results.
- S09 overlaps the divisor-incidence, exterior, and boundary ancestry recorded in W27/W31/W35. Coefficientwise chain cancellation is not cross-integer cancellation.
- S23's broad fugacity idea overlaps W07/W09/W22, W30's continued-power obstruction, W31 T21/T28's small hard-cap/face zeros, and W34's cluster obstruction. The developed statement here concerns the **complete ordinary squarefree polynomial at every sufficiently large cutoff**, locates its unique nearest zero with an explicit error, and gives a character-adaptive two-branch return. That precise full-cutoff statement and deflation criterion were not located in the searched passages. The critic should check the full index before assigning any new record credit.

No external specialist theorem is borrowed: the polynomial lemma uses elementary complex analysis, the block statements use finite algebra, and the needed lower prime count is proved below from a binomial coefficient.

## Six decisive tests

| Seed | Test and outcome | Disposition |
|---|---|---|
| S03 | Compute the exact Schur complement and the actual source injection. Prefix elimination has zero feedback but an unpaid injection. An interleaved partition has nonzero feedback: on integers 1..6, retain {1,6}; the (1,6) Schur entry is -1, not 1. Every prime endpoint still has its original inverse coefficient. | Develop D2 as exact interface and limited obstruction; generic inverse stability is old and insufficient. |
| S16 | Finite telescoping gives the proposed sign and denominator exactly. An inherited subunit Mertens bound removes the future boundary; no new exponent follows from the identity. | Valid duplicate, not a survivor estimate. |
| S23 | The actual N=6 polynomial is 1+3z+z^2, already a recorded obstruction. At large N, the full polynomial has a simple root near -1/P_N, not merely a selected face root. Isolating it yields D1's exact criterion; a bounded deflated factor is insufficient in the principal case. | Main developed upstream survivor, with an open arithmetic input. |
| S18 | The mixed filter is M(x)-2M(x/2)-3M(x/3)+6M(x/6). Commutation holds for every function. Its infinite inverse has only fixed constant loss under the same anchor. | Valid duplicate/equivalence; compatibility creates no magnitude estimate. |
| S09 | Ordered factorization counts are (1,2) at 6, (1,4,3) at 12, and (1,6,6) at 30; alternating sums give 1,0,-1. A prime has only one nontrivial chain. | Retain D2's boundary observation; no new cancellation theorem. |
| S01 | The exact cascade is verified including ramified and squareful zeros. At U=5, r_U(12)=1 although mu(12)=0; b_U*r_U restores 0 there. Every prime p>U occurs only in the first residual layer. | Retain D2's scoped obstruction; do not discard filled squareful intermediate terms. |

`checks.py` completed 12 exact Schur partition checks through N=48 for the principal character and characters modulo 3,4,5 (the latter genuinely complex); 64 full coefficient cascade checks through N=120; all chain coefficients through 120; 2,400 exact rational finite telescoping checks; and 300 mixed-filter checks. The 21 fugacity rows include principal characters modulo 1,6,30 and cutoffs through 200,000. Bracket signs are exact rational tests; decimal root locations are diagnostics only. The proofs, not those finite ranges, establish the statements below.

## D1. A complete-cutoff root theorem and a paid two-branch return

Fix an ordinary Dirichlet character chi modulo q, with its actual zeros on nonunits. For every integer N>=1 define

    C_k(N,chi)=sum_(n<=N; mu(n)^2=1; omega(n)=k) chi(n),
    Z_N(z,chi)=sum_k C_k(N,chi) z^k,
    A_N=C_1(N,chi)=sum_(p<=N)chi(p),
    R_N(z)=sum_(k>=2)C_k(N,chi)z^k,
    B_N=#{n<=N: mu(n)^2=1, (n,q)=1, omega(n)>=2}.

Thus C_0=1, sum_(k>=2)|C_k|<=B_N<=N, and exactly

    Z_N(-1,chi)=M_chi(N)=sum_(n<=N)mu(n)chi(n).          (D1.1)

These are hard-cutoff polynomials. They are not finite Euler products: an Euler product over p<=N also includes products exceeding N. No such extra products have been inserted.

### D1a. Explicit isolated-root lemma

Let Z(z)=1+A z+R(z), with R(z)=sum_(k>=2)c_k z^k a polynomial, sum|c_k|<=B, |A|>=8, and lambda=B/|A|^2<=1/8. Then Z has exactly one zero, counted with multiplicity, in |z|<2/|A|. This zero alpha is simple and satisfies

    |A alpha+1|<=2lambda,
    (1-2lambda)/|A| <= |alpha| <= (1+2lambda)/|A|.      (D1.2)

If B=0 this is immediate from alpha=-1/A. Otherwise, on |z|=2/|A|,

    |1+Az|>=1,    |R(z)|<=B|z|^2<=4lambda<=1/2.

Rouche's theorem gives exactly one zero in the disk. On the circle centered at -1/A with radius 2lambda/|A|, the linear part has modulus 2lambda, whereas

    |R(z)| <= lambda(1+2lambda)^2 <=25lambda/16 <2lambda.

The smaller disk therefore contains that same unique simple zero. Both estimates use |z|<1, justified by |A|>=8. This proves D1.2. In particular alpha is the unique nearest zero to the origin; all remaining zeros have modulus at least 2/|A|.

Define the exact polynomial

    Q(z)=Z(z)/(1-z/alpha),    Q(0)=1.

The factorization is exact, not a truncated series division. Reverse triangle inequalities and D1.2 give

    |A|/2 <= |1+1/alpha| <= 2|A|,
    (|A|/2)|Q(-1)| <= |Z(-1)| <= 2|A||Q(-1)|.         (D1.3)

For example the lower bound follows from |1/alpha|-1>=(4/5)|A|-1>=|A|/2. The upper bound follows from 1+(4/3)|A|<=2|A|.

For real A>0 and real coefficients, the unique zero is real by conjugation. D1.2 then makes it negative. This applies to all principal characters. Complex characters require no positivity for the isolated-root lemma, but their root need not lie on the negative real axis.

### D1b. Every large principal cutoff has a collapsing root

For the principal character modulo fixed q, put P_N=pi(N)-#{p<=N:p|q}. Here A_N=P_N and the C_k are nonnegative integers. For every sufficiently large N, P_N>=8 and B_N/P_N^2<=1/8, so D1a applies to the **whole** polynomial.

The requisite prime lower bound needs no PNT input. For m>=1,

    binom(2m,m)>=4^m/(2m+1).

Each p-adic valuation of that binomial is at most floor(log(2m)/log p), since each term floor(2m/p^j)-2floor(m/p^j) is 0 or 1. Consequently

    binom(2m,m) <= (2m)^pi(2m),
    pi(2m) >= [2m log 2-log(2m+1)]/log(2m).

Taking m=floor(N/2) and removing the fixed finite set dividing q gives P_N >>_q N/log N. Hence lambda_N<=N/P_N^2=O_q((log N)^2/N), and

    alpha_N=-P_N^(-1)[1+O_q((log N)^2/N)],
    |alpha_N|=O_q(log N/N),
    |1+1/alpha_N|=P_N[1+O(lambda_N+1/P_N)].            (D1.4)

This strengthens the old finite face examples in one precise direction: no fixed-radius zero-free disk about z=0 survives for the complete principal hard-cutoff polynomials. The Taylor series of the branch of log Z_N based at 0 has radius exactly |alpha_N|, because alpha_N is the unique nearest zero and is simple. A straight real interpolation from 0 to -1 crosses a zero for every sufficiently large N.

**Scope:** this does not prohibit an N-dependent complex path avoiding the root, a signed contour representation, analytic continuation with explicit factors removed, or a different smoothed polynomial. A zero of Z_N is not a zero of L(s,chi). The result supplies no lower bound on |M_chi(N)|.

Deflating the root does not by itself supply a power saving. For principal chi, D1.3 and P_N=N^(1+o(1)) show that, for each fixed gamma and every epsilon>0,

    M_chi(N)=O_(q,epsilon)(N^(gamma+epsilon))
      iff Q_N(-1)=O_(q,epsilon)(N^(gamma-1+epsilon)).   (D1.5)

The elementary bounds P_N>>N/log N and P_N<=N suffice for this every-epsilon equivalence. Thus a bounded Q_N(-1) only gives a near-linear bound. A near gain requires the deflated endpoint to decay faster than N^(-.12514261), in the every-epsilon sense; targets c=1/6 and 1/4 require N^(-1/6+epsilon) and N^(-1/4+epsilon), respectively. This is the precise remaining cancellation, not a proved estimate.

Some principal diagnostics:

| N | P_N, q=1 | B_N | -P_N alpha_N | M(N) | Q_N(-1), approximate |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 100 | 25 | 35 | 1.05283245 | 1 | -.04396480 |
| 1,000 | 168 | 439 | 1.01038783 | 2 | -.01210121 |
| 10,000 | 1,229 | 4,853 | 1.00172633 | -23 | .01876200 |
| 100,000 | 9,592 | 51,201 | 1.00025349 | -48 | .00500596 |
| 200,000 | 17,984 | 103,596 | 1.00013961 | -1 | .000055616 |

The oscillating finite Q values are not an exponent fit or asymptotic evidence. Every exact integer coefficient used is retained in `checks.json`.

### D1c. Full ordinary-character return, with the complementary branch paid

The lack of a large prime coefficient for a nonprincipal character is not silently ignored. At each N, declare the root branch precisely when

    |A_N|>=8 and |A_N|^2>=8B_N.                       (D1.6)

Use D1a to define Q_N only on that branch. On its complement,

    |A_N| <= max(8,sqrt(8B_N)) <= 8+sqrt(8N),
    M_chi(N)=1-A_N+R_N(-1).                            (D1.7)

Thus the unit and prime sector together cost O(sqrt N) on the complementary branch. This is an actual paid sector; it does not estimate its remaining composite sum.

Fix 1/2<gamma<1. The following two requirements, for every epsilon>0 and every sufficiently large N in the indicated branch, are equivalent to the full all-N Mertens exponent gamma for that fixed character:

    non-root branch: |R_N(-1)| <<_(chi,epsilon) N^(gamma+epsilon),
    root branch:    |A_N Q_N(-1)| <<_(chi,epsilon) N^(gamma+epsilon). (OPEN-FD)

Proof: D1.7 pays the O(sqrt N) complement; D1.3 pays the root branch with an absolute factor at most 2. Conversely subtract 1-A_N on the non-root branch, and use the lower bound in D1.3 on the root branch. All branch switches are allowed; no density-one, subsequence, or averaged cutoff hypothesis replaces every N. Finitely many small N are absorbed into the fixed-character constant. Natural squareful and ramified zeros remain in the coefficients throughout.

The polynomial construction is explicit: enumerate the literal coefficient sums, calculate A_N and B_N, select the branch by D1.6, and on the root branch isolate the unique root in the certified disk and divide by its exact linear factor. This is a constructive mathematical representation, not an efficient sublinear evaluation algorithm. The root isolation error is already specified by D1.2. Numerical approximations to Q would require their own certified endpoint error before use in OPEN-FD.

If OPEN-FD holds with one common gamma for **every fixed ordinary character**, it yields the requested zero exclusion. Indeed Abel summation gives a holomorphic function

    F_chi(s)=s integral_1^infinity M_chi(x)x^(-s-1)dx, Re(s)>gamma,

where M_chi(x)=M_chi(floor x). Choose each internal epsilon below the distance of a compact set to Re(s)=gamma; logarithmic derivatives are dominated there. On Re(s)>1, F_chi=1/L(s,chi), so L(s,chi)F_chi(s)=1 continues to the connected half-plane with the principal pole removed. A zero of L there is impossible. The principal pole at 1 is retained as the standard exception. This argument covers all heights and imprimitive characters with their actual zeros; it does not create growing-conductor uniformity or a Hecke-family extension.

The complete quantitative returns are:

| Common OPEN-FD exponent | Conditional c | Paid non-root prime sector |
|---|---:|---|
| gamma=.8748 | .1252, exceeding c8 by .00005739 | O(N^.5), exponent slack .3748 |
| gamma=5/6 | 1/6 | O(N^.5), exponent slack 1/3 |
| gamma=3/4 | 1/4 | O(N^.5), exponent slack 1/4 |

The difficult principal root branch requires decay of Q_N(-1), so these are **complete conditional budgets**, not achieved gains. OPEN-FD is intentionally equivalent to the original Mertens exponent. It changes the arithmetic object and isolates an easy branch; it does not weaken the required global cancellation merely by renaming it.

### D1d. A second root scale is forced by any Mertens power saving

For a fixed principal character, suppose the Mertens bound at exponent 1-c holds for every positive epsilon, with fixed c>0. Then D1.5 forces a different zero of Z_N to approach the parity point -1. More precisely, for every eta>0, all sufficiently large N have a zero zeta_N other than alpha_N satisfying

    |zeta_N+1| <= 2(log N)^(-c+eta).                   (D1.8)

It is enough to consider 0<eta<c. Let d=deg Q_N. A squarefree integer with D distinct primes is at least (D+1)!, because its j-th prime is at least j+1. The elementary integral bound for log((D+1)!) therefore gives

    deg Z_N <= (1+o(1))log N/loglog N.

If Q_N(-1)=0, take zeta_N=-1. Otherwise factor the entire polynomial, including every zero and its multiplicity:

    |Q_N(-1)|=product_(j=1)^d |1+1/zeta_j|.

The case d=0 is excluded at every sufficiently large N by Q_N(-1)=O(N^(-c+epsilon)). At least one factor is no larger than |Q_N(-1)|^(1/d). The every-epsilon bound and the upper bound for d make this factor at most (log N)^(-c+eta) eventually; first choose the internal epsilon sufficiently small. If delta=|1+1/zeta_j|<1/2, then |zeta_j+1|<=delta/(1-delta)<=2delta. This proves D1.8. It is a necessary consequence, not a sufficient criterion for a power saving: the other factors in the product remain unpaid.

Thus a complete principal hard-cutoff polynomial has a root near 0 unconditionally, and under any supplied subunit Mertens calibration it also has a root approaching -1 at a quantified logarithmic rate. The latter is distinct from alpha_N for large N. A proposed new c improves a necessary localization rate, but localization of one zero alone cannot establish that c. The full logarithmic product of all deflated factors is the relevant signed-arithmetic obligation.

**Strongest objection and next action.** The normalized root factor may encode the same hard cancellation less transparently. That objection survives. A useful next calculation would control the full deflated logarithmic product using actual root motion and arithmetic coefficients. Merely avoiding alpha_N along a complex path, bounding Q_N, or locating one zero near -1 does not meet D1.5. The immediate identity Q_(N+1)(-1)=[M_chi(N)+mu(N+1)chi(N+1)]/[1+1/alpha_(N+1)] is circular as an estimate and receives no credit. The non-root branch's full composite sum also needs an independent estimate before the full character statement can improve.

## D2. Divisor elimination changes the coordinates, not the prime endpoint

Fix N and an ordinary character chi. On indices 1..N in increasing order, set

    C(m,n)=chi(n/m)1_(m|n),
    A(m,n)=mu(n/m)chi(n/m)1_(m|n).

Every intermediate divisor stays within the cap, so CA=AC=I. Let R be any retained index set containing 1 and E its complement, each in increasing order. The E block is unit upper triangular. Define

    S=C_RR-C_RE C_EE^(-1) C_ER,
    v=1_R-C_RE C_EE^(-1)1_E.

Solving Cx=1 by block elimination proves exactly

    S^(-1)=A_RR,
    M_chi(N)=e_1^T S^(-1)v.                            (D2.1)

No full matrix norm substitutes for this source and readout. If R is a prefix, C_ER=0 and S=C_RR, but v still contains the entire deleted source injection. If R is interleaved, the Schur return need not vanish even though divisibility is acyclic. For chi=1, N=6, R={1,6}, one obtains

    S=[[1,-1],[0,1]],    v=[-2,1]^T,
    e_1^T S^(-1)v=-1=M(6).                             (D2.2)

The off-diagonal return is 2, from paths 1->2->6 and 1->3->6; direct C(1,6)=1. This is not a contradiction to G69's zero feedback: that result has a different, chronologically separated partition. Acyclicity forbids returning to the same vertex; it does not forbid a path from one retained vertex through deleted vertices to a later retained vertex.

For any prime p<=N retained in R, there is no intermediate divisor strictly between 1 and p. Thus

    S(1,p)=chi(p),    S^(-1)(1,p)=-chi(p).              (D2.3)

If p is deleted instead, its endpoint contribution moves into the source injection. More formally, replace 1 by an arbitrary endpoint vector w before elimination. The coefficient of w_p in the final root output is always A(1,p)=-chi(p). This is invariant under every exact elimination partition containing 1.

This fact can also be read directly from the finite chain expansion. Let T=C-I; T^k=0 for 2^k>N. Then

    C^(-1)=sum_(k>=0)(-T)^k.                           (D2.4)

For n/m=r the (m,n) entry of T^k is chi(r) times the number of ordered k-factor factorizations of r into factors >=2. Complete multiplicativity includes chi(r)=0 on ramified integers; it is never replaced by a unit phase there. At r=6,12,30 the counts are respectively (1,2), (1,4,3), (1,6,6), reproducing mu(r)=1,0,-1. At a prime p only k=1 survives. The cancellation over internal chains restores each individual mu coefficient; it supplies no cancellation between distinct final integers.

The residual cascade has the same boundary. With a=mu chi, b_U=a1_(n<=U), and r_U=delta-b_U*chi, convolution gives

    a=b_U+a*r_U,
    a=sum_(j=0)^(k-1)b_U*r_U^(*j)+a*r_U^(*k).          (D2.5)

Here r_U(n)=0 for n<=U, so r_U^(*k) starts at (U+1)^k. The identity is exact for every k, including all shared factors. For p>U prime,

    r_U(p)=-chi(p),    (b_U*r_U)(p)=-chi(p),
    (r_U^(*j))(p)=0 for j>=2.                          (D2.6)

For k>=2 the prime endpoint therefore stays entirely in the j=1 layer. Increasing k cannot move it to the terminal remainder. On squareful integers intermediate zeros need not hold: at U=5, chi=1, r_U(12)=1, while (b_U*r_U)(12)=0. Deleting the filled squareful intermediate term would break D2.5.

For principal chi modulo fixed q, an absolute certificate that itemizes the unramified prime endpoints before merging them with composite endpoints pays at least

    #{p<=N:p does not divide q},

or at least #{U<p<=N:p does not divide q} for the cascade's first residual layer. If U<=N^u with fixed u<1, the binomial lower bound above and pi(U)<=U make the latter >>_q,u N/log N. Such a certificate cannot prove any exponent gamma<1. Weighted variants must price their actual endpoint weights; no unweighted lower bound is silently transported to a Gaussian or native H form.

**Scope and usefulness.** This is a lower bound on a specified absolute price, not on |M_chi(N)|, a signed field norm, or a Schur residual after arbitrary signed endpoint merging. It leaves source-sensitive Schur estimates, cross-endpoint cancellation, different readouts, and changed detectors eligible. The broad prime-checksum and readout obstruction is already in W35; D2 assembles the exact arbitrary-partition and cascade statements and corrects the potential overgeneralization of zero feedback. It should receive modest interface/guardrail credit at most.

**Next action.** Any further divisor-matrix attack should name the retained set R, exact v, and the signed functional e_1^T S^(-1)v before asking for a norm. A potentially useful estimate must couple prime endpoints to composite endpoints prior to absolute values, or exploit a separately proved cancellation of chi over primes. The present calculation supplies neither.

## Duplicated scale returns retained without arithmetic credit

For b>1 and M(x)=sum_(n<=x)a(n), put F_b(x)=M(x)-bM(x/b). Exactly, for every integer J>=1,

    M(x)=b^(-J)M(b^J x)-sum_(j=1)^J b^(-j)F_b(b^j x). (T16)

If an inherited calibration M(x)=O(x^beta), beta<1, is available, the boundary tends to zero. For F_b(x)=O(x^gamma), gamma<1, the future sum costs precisely at most 1/(b^(1-gamma)-1), with no exponent loss. A bare claim of a zero-free strip is not used here as an unexplained pointwise Mertens estimate: the calibration is the separately stated input used by current-proof G24 and the G70/G73 source returns.

For H=(I-2D_2)(I-3D_3)M, the full mixed expression is

    H(x)=M(x)-2M(x/2)-3M(x/3)+6M(x/6).

Its ordinary principal coefficients at n=1,2,3,6 are 1,-3,-4,12, not the original mu signs. The two anchored future inversions multiply their fixed costs. Commutation is true for every function and therefore cannot imply new arithmetic cancellation. For a power x^rho the multiplier is (1-2^(1-rho))(1-3^(1-rho)); inside Re rho<1 neither factor vanishes. These facts match the recorded filter architecture. No numerical incommensurability or phase independence is being assumed.

constants are paid; smoothing alone leaves exponent1. The result is a

audits retain the full divisor response and scalar feedback; neither

statement:
## 1. Recovery on the squarefree unit set

Fix an ordinary chi modulo q, real X>=2, N=floor X, and 1<=Y<N. Let

    S={n<=N:mu(n)^2=1,(n,q)=1},
    E={n in S:n<=Y}, H=S minus E, a_n=mu(n)chi(n).

Values outside S are their actual zeros. The exact convolution a*chi=delta_1 gives, for each m in H,

    sum_(d in H,d|m) chi(m/d)a_d=b_m,
    b_m=-sum_(d in E,d|m) a_d chi(m/d).                (E1)

Write Z_(m,d)=chi(m/d)1_(d|m), m,d in H. Increasing numerical order makes Z triangular with diagonal1. Every interval d|k|m inside two endpoints of H lies in H: k>=d>Y, k<=m<=N, and k is a squarefree q-unit. Therefore its inverse is exactly

    (Z^-1)_(m,d)=mu(m/d)chi(m/d)1_(d|m).               (E2)

Proof: in the matrix product, the phase factors multiply to chi(m/d), while sum_(e|m/d)mu(e) is1 for m=d and0 otherwise. No entrywise absolute estimate or random model is used.

The unique row dual for the summatory functional on H is

    lambda_m=sum_(k<=N/m,(k,m)=1)mu(k)chi(k).           (E3)

Here squareful/ramified k vanish by their natural coefficients. This follows by summing column m of Z^-1: all squarefree q-unit multiples are m*k with (k,m)=1. Thus

    M_chi(N)=M_chi(Y)+sum_(m in H)lambda_m b_m.         (E4)

The products in E4 are bilinear, without a complex conjugate. All right endpoints use <=; H uses the strict lower cutoff >Y. This is an exact identity for every finite N and fixed character.

For Y=floor(sqrt N), every lambda uses only k<=sqrt N+O(1), but has the genuine moving coprimality (k,m)=1. These cannot be replaced by one unconditioned short M sum. The b_m retain every exposed divisor, and the sum covers ALL of H, including m near N.

## 7. Protected independent audit W49-29

The seed proposes a two-component conserved-total/residue-boundary evolution. It does not specify a unique state map. I therefore test a concrete natural realization on the actual Mobius source and distinguish its failure from all conceivable two-component encodings.

For an integer Q and fixed ordinary chi define

    M_Q(x)=sum_(n<=x,(n,Q)=1)mu(n)chi(n),  M_Q(x)=0 for x<1.

For a prime q not dividing Q, partitioning squarefree integers by divisibility by q gives

    M_Q(x)=M_(Qq)(x)-chi(q)M_(Qq)(x/q).                 (R14)

This includes character zeros and strict sharp endpoints. There is no higher q power in mu. A natural two-coordinate state at a fixed prime p is

    V_Q^p(x)=(M_Q(x),M_Q(x/p)).

The q update of this pair requires FOUR values of M_(Qq), at x,x/q,x/p,x/(pq). The total/residue identity alone supplies no closure into its two coordinates.

There is an actual-source counterexample, not merely an arbitrary-vector dimension argument. For principal chi, p=2, Q=2, q=3:

    x           V_2^2(x)         V_6^2(x)
    14          (-4,-2)          (-3,-1)
    17          (-4,-2)          (-4,-1).

These are exact sums of mu. Thus the new pair is not a function of the old pair ALONE, even on these genuine arithmetic states. In particular a universal fixed two-by-two update does not exist for this realization. This does not refute an x-dependent rule with additional arithmetic information, an encoding of the entire scale history into a coordinate, or an approximate source-specific closure with a paid error. The finite example is not an asymptotic energy lower bound.

There is a complete, useful repair, with its price exposed. Iterating (R14) toward smaller x yields the finite causal inverse

    M_(Qq)(x)=sum_(j>=0)chi(q)^j M_Q(x/q^j).             (R15)

Only j with x/q^j>=1 contribute. In the weighted supremum norm

    ||F||_sigma=sup_(x>=1)x^(-sigma)|F(x)|, sigma>0,

its cost is at most (1-|chi(q)|q^(-sigma))^(-1); the forward cost is at most1+|chi(q)|q^(-sigma). Both are1 at a ramified q. For a fixed prime block this is exponent equivalence, with all signs and natural zeros preserved.

For a moving block containing all unramified primes up to Y, the generic positive inverse price is the PRODUCT of these factors. If0<sigma<1, its logarithm is bounded below by a constant times Y^(1-sigma)/log Y, using the ordinary prime supply in [Y/2,Y]. At Y=X^delta this positive certificate is superpolynomial in X. That is a limitation of this absolute certificate, not a lower bound for actual signed arithmetic, and not a refutation of a new compatible-source estimate.

An improved two-coordinate proposal must now specify its actual additional state or error and bound the COMPLETE iterated residual at every scale and fixed character. A conserved mass identity does not perform that work. The useful result of this audit is the exact off-grid obstruction and the paid multiscale replacement (R15). G28/G52/RCC3 already supply paid causal inverses, G81 retains scale history, and RN/G69 retain terminal/past input. This audit is a source-specific diagnosis and repair, not a new inverse family or c gain. Its original protected choice and all priority candidates remain unchanged.

## 3. Weighted coherent coefficient mass

Use HC7's full coherent parametrization:
\[
c=gu,\quad c'=gv,\quad n=hys_0^2,\quad n'=hxt_0^2,
\quad a=d_0ux^3r_1^6,\quad b=d_0vy^3r_2^6,
\]
where \(x\mid e\), \(y\mid d\), \((r_1,r_2)=1\), and every inherited support restriction is retained. The symbols \(s_0,t_0\) here are square-root labels, distinct from the local embedding exponents above.

Split \(d_0=d_\circ f^6\) canonically as in HC7-HC8. Before counting \(f,r_1,r_2\), PC7 and HC9 give the remaining factor
\[
\frac{\sqrt{UV}}
{q_{\operatorname{rad}(d_\circ)}(q_xq_y)^{3/2}}.
\]
The weighted local formulas make the sixth-power sums convergent. Away from embedding rebates they acquire
\((q_fq_{r_1}q_{r_2})^{-3}\).
Overlap between \(f\) and a residual root is allowed: their exponents add to the maximum outer exponent. The residual roots remain coprime as in HC7. At an embedding prime a rebate occurs only when the larger outer exponent is on the shifted side; its local sum is still uniformly bounded.

Outside the completed columns, coherent nonprincipal positive outer exponents must be equal and unshifted. Their exact-valuation kernel gives the existing \(1/\operatorname{rad}(d_\circ)\) factor. Ignoring its additional negative divisor weight is harmless, and HC18's Rankin argument makes the total \(d_\circ\)-sum \(Z^\epsilon\).

At completed-column primes natural zeros force a unit row. The allowed positive outer exponents remain one or the embedded exception three, so no principal multiple of six survives there. Unit-mask expansion costs only divisor losses. The \(x,y\) sums retain exponent \(3/2\); the \(h,s_0,t_0\) sums retain exponent two.

Sum the common-core variable \(g\) against both original rapid envelopes exactly as in PC8/HC12. The bound is uniform in their two scales. Actual marks remain inside \(K_D,K_E\), with T06's divisor envelope and no extra slot count. Small powers of arbitrarily large completed columns are absorbed into the original two-sided rapid envelopes.

Thus, denoting by the superscript the divisor weight imposed on the actual Gauss coefficient mass,
\[
\boxed{
\mathscr M_{\rm coh}^{(1/2)}(U,V)
\ll_\epsilon Z^\epsilon\sqrt{UV}.
} \tag{FR13}
\]
The same conclusion holds with weight \(q_k^{-\rho}\) for every fixed \(1/6<\rho\le1\).

statement:
## 2. Exact full signed gcd sector, before any positivity step

For real D>=1 define the including-diagonal signed scalar

    T_>=D(X)=sum_{gcd(m,n)>=D} f(m)f(n)K_X(m,n).        (S8)

Write m=ga,n=gb with (a,b)=1 and insert
1_{(a,b)=1}=sum_{q|a,b}mu(q). Equation S2 gives the exact identity

    T_>=D(X)=sum_{g>=D}sum_{q>=1}mu(q) E_{gq}(X/(gq))
            =sum_{r>=1} A_D(r)E_r(X/r),
    A_D(r)=sum_{g|r,g>=D}mu(r/g).                       (S9)

Each square contains the WHOLE f_{gq} field, not a selected positive
subfamily of the original f correlation. Its sign in S9 is mu(q).
The crucial cancellation f_g(q)^2=1 is performed on the actual
coefficients before estimating the squares. The integer condition
g>=D is literal, equivalent to g>=ceil(D).

Absolute rearrangement is legitimate before the signed cancellation.
For fixed x in [X,2X], a positive majorant is

    sum_{r>=1}d(r)[sum_{u>=1}g(log(ru/x))]^2<infinity.

The inner sum is O_tau(x/r) when r<=2X and is O_(A,tau)((x/r)^A)
for r>2X. Therefore the majorant is locally integrable, including all
q,g and all prime powers. This justifies Fubini and S9 with no finite
cap, no tail assumed away and no infinite-series continuation.

**Theorem S-GCD.** For every epsilon>0, uniformly for X>=2 and ALL
real D>=1,

    |T_>=D(X)| <= C_(beta,tau,epsilon)
                        X^(2beta+epsilon)D^(1-2beta).  (S10)

Proof: first take the r=gq<=X part of the absolute majorant in S9.
By S4--S6, B_r^2<=C_epsilon X^epsilon, so this part is bounded by

    C X^(2beta+epsilon)
        sum_{g>=D}g^(-2beta)sum_{q>=1}q^(-2beta)
     <= C X^(2beta+epsilon)D^(1-2beta).

If D>X that first part is empty. For r>X use S7 and |A_D(r)|<=d(r).
With R=max(X,D), any A>beta+1, and a sufficiently small delta>0,
the remainder is at most

    C X^(2A) sum_{r>=R} d(r)r^(-2A)
      <= C_delta X^(2A)R^(1-2A+delta).

When D<=X this is O(X^(1+delta)), absorbed by the proposed bound
because D^(1-2beta)>=X^(1-2beta). When D>X, division by
X^(2beta+epsilon)D^(1-2beta) leaves at most X^(delta-epsilon),
provided delta<=epsilon and 2A-2beta>delta. This proves S10 uniformly,
even for D larger than every prescribed power of X.

### 2.1 The true diagonal and the complete complement

The diagonal retained by S8 is precisely

    Delta_>=D(X)=sum_{n>=D}K_X(n,n)>=0.                 (S11)

It satisfies the same S10 bound without the epsilon: for D<=X use
Delta_all=O_tau(X); for D>X use the Gaussian bound
K_X(n,n)<=C_A(X/n)^(2A) and sum it, choosing A>beta. Thus the actual
off-diagonal sector

    Q_>=D(X)=sum_{m!=n;gcd(m,n)>=D}f(m)f(n)K_X(m,n)

also satisfies S10 after subtracting S11. No sign is assigned to
Q_>=D, T_>=D or their complements.

Let Q_<D use the exact complementary conditions m!=n, gcd(m,n)<D.
Then, for every fixed theta>0,

    Q_off(X)=Q_<X^theta(X)
       +O_epsilon(X^(2beta-(2beta-1)theta+epsilon)).    (S12)

All ordered cross terms between the original integers remain in
exactly one of these two scalar sectors. There is no field partition
whose mixed terms have been omitted.

For a desired gamma>1/2, choose

    theta > (2beta-2gamma)/(2beta-1).                   (S13)

Then OPEN-F3 is equivalent to the ONE-SIDED estimate
Q_<X^theta(X)<=C_epsilon X^(2gamma+epsilon), for every epsilon>0
and all sufficiently large dyadic X. Necessity and sufficiency both
follow from S12 and its absolute error, allowing a smaller epsilon in
the fixed strict margin. Current-proof G25--G31 then supplies the
already proved complete zero-exclusion return c=1-gamma. No new c is
proved here because this remaining signed estimate is OPEN.

The inherited beta=.8749, gamma=.87449, theta=.0011 gives exponent
1.74897522, matching the numerical exponent of W36 but for this
DIFFERENT actual f3 sector. Using beta=.87489=theta_G+.0000034 gives
1.748955242, below 1.74898 by .000024758. In the limit beta down to
theta_G (a limiting threshold, not a boundary-line bound), S13 is:

| Desired gamma | Strict lower threshold for theta |
| --- | --- |
| .87449 | 661/624811 = .001057919914982... |
| 5/6 | 623299/5623299 = .110842229801403... |
| 3/4 | 624433/1874433 = .333131672351052... |

For any chosen theta strictly beyond the displayed limiting value,
choose a fixed sufficiently small eta>0 first, then epsilon. Neither
eta nor beta varies with X.

### 2.2 Both height variables

S9 is derived in the physical variable, so no height interaction is
ever deleted. For an explicit height readout, on any fixed a>1 put

    D_r(s)=sum_n f_r(n)n^(-s),
    B_r(t)=exp(tau(a+it)^2/2)D_r(a+it),
    J_a(v)=integral_0^log2 exp((2a+iv)u)du.

Absolute Mellin inversion gives

    E_r(Y)=Y^(2a)/(2pi)^2 integral_R integral_R
      B_r(t)conj(B_r(t'))Y^(i(t-t'))J_a(t-t') dt dt'.   (S14)

One may keep a>1 here; no shifted-contour statement is needed for the
sector theorem. S9 therefore contains every r, both independent t,t',
and the same local-window kernel J_a. Replacing the double integral by
t=t', or dropping signed mu(q), is not part of the proof.

statement:
## T05. Physical cube-row Type I restriction — PROVED RELATIVE TO ORIGINAL PROFILE

**Provenance:** SA Part II, (C1)–([restricted research revision]), with ([restricted research revision])–([restricted research revision]) for cutoff obstructions; inherited CP (14)–(25) and M's coefficient definitions. This genuinely resolves the restricted-Type-I gap explicitly left at CP (20). It is not a restriction of a bound for the whole signed form.

### Exact row projection and mask coefficient

Restore the original `k=0` row, use one common **total-column** Poisson period, and retain nonzero physical frequencies whose good valuations are multiples of three. Denote this linear operation by `P_cub`. Its fixed unit/bad-prime cube-residual states are `sigma_*`. The original row and transformed zero frequency are different; transformed zero is excluded here.

For a column `cB³` with `c` squarefree, the original internal Type I coefficient is
\[
\mathcal J[I]_k(cB^3)=q_B\xi(B)\overline{\mathfrak G(c)}\vartheta_c(k)
\sum_{t\mid B}q_t^{-1/2}\overline{\xi(t)}I_Y(ct^3)1_{(t,k)=1}.
\]
Write
\[
\mathcal A_Y(c,B)=\sum_{t\mid B}q_t^{-1/2}\overline{\xi(t)}I_Y(ct^3)
\prod_{p\mid t,\,p\nmid c}(1-Q_p^{-1}).
\tag{T05.1}
\]
The density applies only outside the core. At a prime in `c`, the primitive row character already imposes its nonunit zero.

For coprime total columns `cB³,eE³`, retain precisely
\[
(c,e)=(c,E)=(e,B)=(B,E)=1.
\]
Let `M0=ce`, and `R0=rad(BE)` with the primes of `M0` removed. The reduced common period is `M0R0`. A frequency `h` on that period represents physical frequency
\[
u=(B^3E^3/R_0)h.
\]
At primes of `M0`, the transform is zero unless `h` is a unit. At primes of `R0`, the cube condition forces `v_p(h)=1 mod 3`. At other good primes it forces `v_p(h)=0 mod 3`. Consequently surviving reduced frequencies are exactly
\[
h=\sigma_*R_0z^3,\qquad(z,M_0)=1.
\]
For an outside-prime mask `r`, CP (23)'s Fourier factor is then
\[
\sum_{s\mid r}\mu(s)q_{R_0/s}1_{R_0/s\mid h}
=q_{R_0}\prod_{p\mid r}(1-Q_p^{-1}).
\]
The two masks are disjoint by total-column coprimality and split into (T05.1). The factor `q_R0` cancels the Poisson denominator, and the primitive phase becomes the fixed ray phase `chi_sigma_*(c) conjugate(chi_sigma_*(e))`, with the restriction `(ce,z)=1` retained. Thus the exact projected form is
\[
\begin{aligned}
P_{\rm cub}\mathfrak Q[I,I]
={K\over D^2}\sum_{\sigma_*}\sum_{(B,E)=1}
&\xi(B)\overline{\xi(E)}q_B^4q_E^4
\sum_{z\ne0}\Phi\!\left({Kq_B^3q_E^3q_{\sigma_*}q_z^3\over D^2}\right)\\
\times\sum_{\substack{c,e\ {\rm sf},\,(c,e)=1\\(c,EzS)=(e,BzS)=1}}
&\chi_{\sigma_*}(c)\overline{\chi_{\sigma_*}(e)}\sqrt{q_cq_e}
\mathcal A_Y(c,B)\overline{\mathcal A_Y(e,E)}
\overline{W_0(q_cq_B^3/D)}W_0(q_eq_E^3/D).
\end{aligned}
\tag{T05.2}
\]
For `M0=1`, the transform is only a periodic mask; the same Fourier identity holds directly and includes pure-cube columns.

The restored original row causes no remainder ambiguity: its completed coefficient is zero unless `c=1`, and then `C_0(B³)=q_B xi(B)` while `J[I]_0(B³)=-q_B xi(B)`. At `k=0` only internal `t=1` survives and `I_Y(1)=-1`. Hence C–C and I–I have identical original-zero terms.

### Fixed-ray squarefree selector estimate

For one of these fixed characters `chi`, squarefree `R`, and a moving deleted set `M1`, define
\[
U_\chi(X;M_1,R)=\sum_{c\ {\rm sf},\,(c,M_1)=1,\,R\mid c}
\chi(c)\sqrt{q_c}W_0(q_c/X).
\]
If `R` meets the deletion set or the character conductor, this is zero. Otherwise, for every fixed `sigma>1/2`,
\[
|U_\chi(X;M_1,R)|
\ll(q_{M_1}q_R)^\epsilon q_R^{-\sigma}X^{\sigma+1/2}.
\tag{T05.3}
\]
Indeed `sqrt(q_c)W0(q_c/X)=sqrt(X)W(q_c/X)`. Its squarefree forced-divisor Dirichlet series is
\[
\chi(R)q_R^{-s}{L^S(s,\chi)\over L^S(2s,\chi^2)}
\prod_{p\mid M_1R}(1+\chi(p)Q_p^{-s})^{-1},
\]
with repeated primes counted once and conductor/excluded primes omitted. The denominator reciprocal converges absolutely for `Re s>1/2`; a principal numerator pole at one is canceled by the original root `W-hat(1)=0`. Moving local factors cost a subpower by the same elementary argument as T01. Shift Mellin to `Re s=sigma`; fixed-character height growth is absorbed by rapid Mellin decay. This proves (T05.3), including small `X`. No new zero-free input is used here.

**Profile qualification:** this is the original root-preserving profile, its conjugate, and permitted Euler derivatives retaining that root. An arbitrary multiplicative norm twist moves the root and is not covered by this argument without a corrected residue calculation. Do not advertise T05 for such a family merely because another theorem uses Mellin twists.

### Complete summation

The exact identity
\[
\prod_{p\mid t,\,p\nmid c}(1-Q_p^{-1})
=\sum_{a\mid\operatorname{rad}t}
\left(\prod_{p\mid a}Q_p^{-1}\prod_{p\mid\operatorname{rad}t/a}(1-Q_p^{-1})\right)1_{a\mid c}
\]
has nonnegative coefficients summing to one. Also
\[
I_Y(ct^3)=-\sum_{q_d,q_e\le Y,\,de\mid ct^3}\mu(d)\mu(e).
\]
If a prime divides `(d,e)` outside `t`, its term is impossible because `c` is squarefree. Otherwise divisibility by `de` is exactly one squarefree selector on `c`, formed from primes of `de` outside `t`. Combining the two identities expresses `A_Y(c,B)` as a finite sum of squarefree selectors with absolute coefficient mass
\[
\ll Y^2\sum_{t\mid B}q_t^{-1/2}\ll_\epsilon Y^2q_B^\epsilon.
\]
The selector norms have a fixed polynomial bound in `q_BY`, sufficient for their subpower local costs.

Insert the exact coprime projector `sum_{ell|c,e}mu(ell)` into (T05.2). Apply (T05.3) with forced divisor `[ell,selector]`, whose norm is at least `q_ell`. Choose fixed `1/2<sigma0<5/6<sigma1`, and put
\[
f(X)=\begin{cases}X^{\sigma_0+1/2},&X\ge1,\\X^{\sigma_1+1/2},&X<1.\end{cases}
\]
The two column sums cost at most `Y² q_ell^{-sigma0} f(D/q_B³)` and its `E` counterpart, up to subpowers. Choose those losses below `2sigma0-1`; the `ell` sum converges. The one joint row profile obeys, by ideal counting and Schwartz decay,
\[
\sum_{z\ne0}q_z^\epsilon|\Phi(Uq_{\sigma_*}q_z^3)|
\ll U^{-1/3-O(\epsilon)}.
\]
The fixed-prime cube powers also sum, and fixed unit states give constants. After this row sum the bound becomes
\[
(DKY)^\epsilon Y^4{K^{2/3}\over D^{4/3}}
\left(\sum_Bq_B^3 f(D/q_B^3)\right)^2.
\]
For `q_B<=D^(1/3)`, the summand is `D^(sigma0+1/2) q_B^(3/2-3sigma0)`; this exponent of `q_B` is greater than `-1`, and ideal counting gives total `D^(4/3)`. The tail with `sigma1>5/6` gives the same bound by a convergent sum. Therefore
\[
\boxed{|P_{\rm cub}\mathfrak Q[I,I]|\ll_\epsilon
(DKY)^\epsilon D^{4/3}K^{2/3}Y^4.}
\tag{T05.4}
\]
All originally infinite cube-label sums have now been justified by these positive majorants, after exact row/mask identities were established.

At `K<=D^(1753/2000)` and `Y=D^(1/100)`, the exponent is `5873/3000`, with margin `127/3000` below two. Bilinearity thus gives
\[
P_{\rm cub}(2\Re\mathfrak Q[I,R]+\mathfrak Q[R,R])
=P_{\rm cub}\mathfrak Q[C,C]+O_\epsilon(D^{5873/3000+\epsilon}).
\]
The available principal C–C bound remains `D^(5/3-2c0+epsilon)K^(2/3+epsilon)`, by CP (18). At this geometry it has exponent `2.000773294079928262...`. T05 is an upper-budget comparison, not a lower bound showing that C–C actually attains that size. The nonprincipal generic sieve still has the much larger `D²K^(1/3)` loss.

## 6. Size and limitations of the new sector

Write \(Q=q_{b_*}Z^M\), \(M=x+y\), \(Y=Z^y\), \(L=Z^\ell\). For a forced-divisor dyad \(F\asymp Z^f\), (PH5) gives the two scale-exponent boundaries
\[
\tau_{1/2}(f)=\frac49(M+y+f),\qquad
\tau_1(f)=\frac{y-x+5f}{3}.
\tag{PH19}
\]
Fixed \(q_{b_*}\) factors remain in (PH5), rather than being folded into these scale exponents. The two branches switch when
\[
f=\frac{6M-(y-x)}{11}
=0.447838197664883655\ldots
\tag{PH20}
\]
at the [saved geometry](../sextic-geometry.md#2-geometry-and-the-binding-numerator).
For \(\mathfrak p_{\mathrm{coh}}=1\), the boundaries are
\(\frac49(M+y)+\frac23f\) and \((y-x)/3+2f\); their switch is at
\(f=(6M-(y-x))/12=0.410518347859476684\ldots\).

Within the interpolation family (PH13), the affordable exponent is
\[
\tau(\rho,f)=
\frac{(1-\rho)M-\max(2-4\rho,0)\ell
 +(y-x)/6+(\rho-1/6)f}{1-\rho/2}.
\tag{PH21}
\]
Below \(\rho=1/2\), its derivative has the positive saved-geometry sign from FR20 plus \(11f/12\ge0\). Above \(1/2\), its derivative has the constant sign of
\(-M/2+(y-x)/12+11f/12\).
Thus \(\rho=1/2\) or \(1\) is optimal within this family. The restricted family replaces \(\rho-1/6\) by \(\rho\), and has the same endpoint conclusion with derivative contribution \(f\). This optimality is only for the explicitly proved family.

A concrete local/scale configuration lies strictly beyond FR. In the unembedded branch take pairwise disjoint source factors
\[
a=p^2t,\qquad b=q^2s,
\qquad q_p\asymp q_q\asymp Z^{13/100},\qquad
q_t,q_s\asymp Z^{y-26/100},
\tag{PH22}
\]
with \(t,s\) squarefree, and choose completed labels
\(A=u^6\), \(A'=p_0v^6\), where \(p_0\) is a fixed good prime disjoint from these factors. Their squarefree cores are \(1,p_0\), so their true gcd is one. Keep source factors coprime to \(uvp_0\). The exact row support has \(F=q_pq_q\asymp Z^{0.26}\), and
\[
\log_Z R=2y-0.26+o(1)
=0.662332873840431694\ldots+o(1).
\tag{PH23}
\]
The old FR exponent is \(0.576299562323534148\ldots\); the first new boundary is \(0.691855117879089704\ldots\), with strict margin \(0.029522244038658010\ldots\). These are nonzero local kernels: the source-square primes force valuations one; all sixth-power column primes impose unit masks, and the remaining source primes carry their actual primitive characters.

This configuration is compatible with the actual marked columns. For \(D=E=1\), the complementary mark product has size \(L\). Put its original distinct primes into \(u\) and \(v\), and retain the actual marked weights. The remaining sixth-root scale has exponent
\((1-5\ell)/6=0.0243218423717766725\ldots>0\).
Thus the mark requirement does not force an empty completed scale. The example is a compatibility and local-support witness for labels in the original nonzero windows, not an assertion of a signed covariance lower bound or a new prime-counting theorem.

The necessary physical support \(F\ll H\) bounds how far a particular branch can reach. In the unembedded branch the largest possible boundary from the second full-sector condition has exponent
\((y-x+5M)/3=1.421454395690458546\ldots\).
For the restricted sector it is \((y-x)/3+2M=1.699956921793037208\ldots\).
These are upper envelopes of a conditional sector, not claims that every conductor up to those sizes is paid.

### Fixed ordinary characters and the nonvanishing numerator

For a fixed ordinary character chi, including zeros at ramified primes,
complete multiplicativity gives

    chi b=(chi a)*(chi f), chi f=(chi d)*(chi b).

All products with chi on the right are coefficientwise before Dirichlet
convolution. Their absolute weighted norms do not increase. In particular
the exact equivalence extends separately to each fixed character, not
uniformly in a growing conductor. On the unit-index subspace the operator
is D_chi T^(q) D_chi; this is left and right unitary multiplication, **not**
unitary conjugation. Singular values are preserved, while self-adjointness
need not be. If2 is unramified, the core is optimal rank2; if2 is ramified,
the stated all-positive core is optimal rank1. It is not then claimed to
be optimal rank2. Prime3 is rank1 when present, absent when ramified.
Extending by zero returns exactly the missing rows/columns and coefficients.

Direct local multiplication, not an analogy to zeta, gives

    sum_n chi(n)f(n)n^(-s)=W_chi(s)/L(s,chi), Re s>1,
    W_chi(s)=(1-2chi(2)2^-s)
       /[(1-chi(2)2^-s)^2(1-chi(3)3^-s)^2]
       *product_(p>=5)(1-2chi(p)p^-s)/(1-chi(p)p^-s)^2. (R41-A9)

A ramified factor equals1. Each generic factor differs from1 by
-z^2/(1-z)^2, z=chi(p)p^-s. On Re s>=rho>.5 the generic product and its
inverse converge normally and are uniformly bounded: 2p^-rho<1 for p>=5
and the local deviations are summable. Denominators have no zeros for
Re s>0. The retained prime-two numerator has zeros only on Re s=1.
Thus W_chi is holomorphic and nonzero in .5<Re s<1.

The Mellin transform initially is exp(tau s^2/2)W_chi/L. An all-scale
Gaussian norm exponent gamma>.5 continues the transform holomorphically
to Re s>gamma, including every fixed height, by shell Cauchy–Schwarz;
logarithmic derivatives are paid by a small positive exponent buffer and
the Gaussian left tail. Multiply by the continued L-function before
evaluating at a possible zero. The identity theorem gives a nonzero right
side at every point gamma<Re s<1, contradicting any such zero. The known
right-edge result finishes the half-plane assertion; the principal pole
at1 is retained. There is no assumed all-height reciprocal bound hiding
in this direction of the argument. A hypothesis must be proved for each
fixed chi to earn that character's conclusion. No such new bound is proved.

**Ancestry:** W29's trace-class product tensor and Sobolev readout already
separate compactness from arithmetic evaluation; its odd local block has
lower-right0 and its prime-two block is different. AM18–21 already separate
finite divisor-inverse conditioning from actual readout. G28–32 and the
reviewed Sol D04 supply existing weighted-reconstruction interfaces.
W41's admitted delta is the explicit all-prime-power f3 optimal core and
its two weighted inverse kernels; the abstract spectral facts and Mellin
return are not new broad mechanisms.
