### 3.2 Critic theorem R40-E: every fixed finite Euler universe fails

The author's bare calculation explicitly leaves finite Euler products
untested. The following additional argument closes **all subsets of a
fixed finite prime set simultaneously**, including height-adaptive choices.
It still leaves genuinely unbounded prime universes or other multipliers
open. This strengthening belongs to this independent review.

Fix a finite set S of rational primes. For A subset S define
E_A(s)=product_(p in A)(1-p^-s), and

    h_(t,A)(z)=[(1+it+Rz)zeta(2+it+Rz)E_A(2+it+Rz)]
                       /[(1+it)zeta(2+it)E_A(2+it)].

Then

    sup_(t>=40) min_(A subset S) B(h_(t,A))=infinity. (R40.3)

Use the same fixed arc I. Put a_p=p^(-3/5) and define finite constants

    m=(1-R/40)/4 * product_S(1-a_p)/product_S(1+p^-2)>0,
    Q=7(1+R/40)/4 * product_S(1+a_p)/product_S(1-p^-2),
    D=R/(40-R)+R sum_S (log p)a_p/(1-a_p).

Let

    q_(t,A)(theta)=k_t(theta) w_t E_A(s(theta)+it)/E_A(2+it).

For every t>=40 and every A subset S, product triangle inequalities
give m<=|q|<=Q. The local factors never vanish on this arc. Differentiating
their logarithms along theta gives

    |d/dtheta arg q| <= D.                          (R40.4)

Indeed k'/k has modulus at most R/(40-R), each Euler term contributes
at most R(log p)a_p/(1-a_p), and both anchor factors are constant in
theta. An argument branch exists on the interval I; no global analytic
logarithm or zero-free half-plane is assumed.

Choose one integer N>D+80pi, fixed once S is fixed. On the arc prescribe
the continuous, nonvanishing target

    f_M(s)=M[-(s-2)/R]^N
          =M exp(iN(theta-pi)).

The same primary theorem gives a positive-lower-density set of t>=40
where |zeta(s+it)-f_M(s)|<1 uniformly. These heights are common to all
A; the target does not depend on A or the unknown anchor phase.
For each such pair (t,A), the phase
phi(theta)=N(theta-pi)+arg q_(t,A)(theta) is strictly increasing, with
N-D<=phi'<=N+D. Its total range has length greater than4pi. Consequently
it contains some complete phase interval [2pi/3+2kpi,4pi/3+2kpi].
The corresponding theta interval has length at least2pi/[3(N+D)].
On that interval cos phi<=-1/2. If M>=4Q/m, the actual boundary satisfies

    Re h_(t,A)(e^(i theta)) <= -Mm/2+Q <= -Mm/4.

Integration on that interval therefore gives, for EVERY A subset S,

    B(h_(t,A)) >= Mm/[12(N+D)].                    (R40.5)

The interval can depend on A; its length and lower bound do not. No
intersection of independently selected good-height sets is needed.
Since M is arbitrary, R40.3 follows, with positive lower density of
simultaneously bad heights for each fixed proposed budget. The proof
uses only the inspected universality theorem and the displayed bounds.

Thus a fixed finite Euler product, or switching among subsets of a
bounded prime universe, cannot repair this positivity route for zeta.
The constants m,Q,D depend on S; when S grows without bound with t,
this argument provides no uniform m or D and proves no such rejection.
It also does not reject all zero-preserving analytic normalizations,
or establish a corresponding universality theorem for the Hecke family.
The all-family proposal already needs zeta, so this zeta obstruction
is a necessary test of any proposed fixed-universe repair.

This is distinct from W24C's negative-prime-frequency test for a

## 1. Counts, collisions and literal tuples

Put r_G(n)=#{r>G:r^2 divides n}. The exact identities and estimates are

    sum_(n<=Y) r_G(n) <= 2Y/G,
    sum_(n<=Y) r_G(n)^2
      =sum_(r,s>G) floor(Y/lcm(r,s)^2) <=16Y/G.           (S2)

For the second inequality write r=gu,s=gv,(u,v)=1. Both root inequalities say g>G/min(u,v), and lcm(r,s)=guv. Since sum_(g>t)g^-2<=2/t for every t>0, removing coprimality in a positive sum gives at most

    (2Y/G) sum_(u,v>=1) min(u,v)/(u^2 v^2) <16Y/G.

The double series is bounded by 2 sum_u u^-1 sum_(v>=u)v^-2 <=4 zeta(2)<8. Infinite positive majorants are justified by convergence; the exact floor sum is finite. This retains equal roots, all collisions and real G's strict endpoint.

For an interval I in [cN,CN], with length h>=0, reverse the count n=r^2 l. There are at most CN/G^2 possible positive integers l. For each l the permitted real r interval has length at most C_(c,C) h/(sqrt(N)sqrt(l)). Length plus one, summed over l, yields

    sum_(n in I) r_G(n) <<_(c,C) h/G + N/G^2.            (S3)

This proof works for ALL G>=1, not only G>N^(1/3). If CN/G^2<1 the count is zero. Otherwise the N/G^2 term pays each isolated endpoint, including a singleton interval or h<1. The author's stronger minimum with N^(1/3) is valid, but is unnecessary for (S1).

Every actual ordered tuple has a unique exact r=gcd(d,e), d=ru,e=rv and (u,v)=1. At this r the number of remaining factorizations of n/r^2 is at most d3(n/r^2)<=d3(n). Consequently, for every fixed eta>0,

    |v_G(n)| <<_(eta,B0) n^eta r_G(n),
    sum_(n<=Y)|v_G(n)| << Y^(1+eta)/G,
    sum_(n<=Y)|v_G(n)|^2 << Y^(1+2eta)/G.                (S4)

The mask is preserved before this positive coefficient majorization. Coprimality is only dropped in an upper bound. No assertion about the norm of a signed subset is used.

### 3.2 Literal coefficients and zero return

Write z_p=chi(p)p^(-s), with chi(p)=0 at ramified primes. f3 has value-1 at every positive p-power for p!=3 and+1 at every 3-power. Therefore

    D_chi(s)=sum f3(n)chi(n)n^(-s)=N_chi(s)H_chi(s)/L(s,chi),
    N_chi=1-2z_2,
    H_2=(1-z_2)^(-2), H_3=(1-z_3)^(-2),
    H_p=(1-2z_p)/(1-z_p)^2, p>=5.                           (Q6)

This checks all powers, including2 and3, rather than substituting a squarefree or completely multiplicative surrogate. Both H and its inverse have absolutely summable coefficients at each fixed weight sigma>1/2: large-prime local corrections start at z_p^2 and 2/sqrt5<1. Their finite small-prime factors have no pole or zero in that half-plane. If2 is unramified the zeros of N have real part1; if it is ramified N=1. Thus N H is nonzero for1/2<Re(s)<1 at every finite height.

On Re(s)>1 absolute Gaussian Fubini gives

    integral_R F_chi(u)e^(-su)du=exp(tau s^2/2)D_chi(s).    (Q7)

The original left Gaussian tail pays this integral and every fixed s-derivative on compacta as u->-infinity. An all-interval bound at gamma pays the right tail locally uniformly for Re(s)>gamma. The principal pole at1 is outside that open strip and cannot be silently divided through; the inherited known right edge is separate. Each fixed ordinary character needs its own arithmetic bound. Integer CRT below gives neither an ideal theorem nor a growing-conductor estimate. F_a(x)=sum_n a(n)g_tau(log(n/x)), with the normalized log Gaussian.
Fix A>0, L=log X and C=sqrt(2tau(A+2)). Cover the entire log interval
[-C sqrt(L),log2+C sqrt(L)] by unit bins, rounding outward at the ends.
On each bin use counting-measure orthogonal projection onto polynomials
of degree<m in log(n/X), where

    m=ceil(2(A+2)L/log L).

If a bin has fewer thanm points, take its full value space. This defines
a fixed projection P_X for the entire shell. Both infinite tails and all
within-bin Taylor residuals are paid, and uniformly on x in[X,2X],

    F_a(x)=sum_n (P_X a)(n)g_tau(log(n/x))+O_A(X^-A).

The rank is O(L^(3/2)/log L). The proof uses the center-uniform error
2(2pi tau)^(-1/2)(e/(tau m))^(m/2); Gaussian tails supply the stated
truncation. This makes the projection source-exact, but its small rank
does not estimate the projected arithmetic coordinates.

The complete readout Gram c* K_X c is equivalent to the original shell
moment up to the paid errors. The positive coordinate energy
E_X=||P_X a||_2^2 is a stronger sufficient input:

## 3. Short rational cofactor relations are affordable

For \(ij\in\{13,14,23,24\}\), define

\[
A_{ij}(K)=\{\exists\ 1\le r,s\le J:
 |r d_i-s d_j|\le K\},\qquad
A(K)=\bigcup_{ij}A_{ij}(K).
\tag{SP12}
\]

**Proposition.** Uniformly for \(0\le K\le Y/2\),

\[
|Q[1_{A(K)}]|
\ll_{b,\epsilon}
X^{b+1/2+\epsilon}(K+1)
+X^{1+\epsilon}(K+1)^2.
\tag{SP13}
\]

The proof is uniform in the two original gcd thresholds. In particular,
it also holds on the fully pairwise-coprime stratum by setting both
thresholds to \(2\).

**Proof for one edge.** Freeze squarefree \(d,f\), retaining
\((d,f)<R\). Put \(D=\operatorname{rad}(df)\) and, for \(r\mid D\),

\[
F(r)=1_{(r,d)<H}1_{(r,f)<R},\qquad
G(r)=1_{(r,f)<H}1_{(r,d)<R},\qquad a_g=1_{g<R}.
\tag{SP14}
\]

These encode exactly the five remaining original gcd restrictions.
Apply (SP9) with
\(W(e,h)=\Xi(de;x)\overline{\Xi(fh;x)}\). On every nonempty dyadic
rectangle, the support gives \(EV\ll X^2L^4/(df)\), and
\(\mathcal S(W)\ll L^{12}\). As \(D\ll XL^8\), the divisor-mask
loss is absorbed into \(X^\epsilon\). Summing the
\(O((1+\log L)^2)\) rectangles yields

\[
\left|\sum_{e,h}\text{the complete remaining summand}\right|
\ll_{b,\epsilon}X^{2b+\epsilon}(df)^{-b},
\tag{SP15}
\]

uniformly in \(d,f,x\), with the sharp endpoints kept.

If \(|rd-sf|\le K\), \(1\le r,s\le J\), and \(K\le Y/2\), then
\(sf\ge rd/2\), hence \(f\ge d/(2J)\). For fixed \(d,r,s\), there
are at most \(2K+1\) possible integers \(f\). Taking absolute values
only after the two-variable cancellation therefore gives

\[
\begin{split}
\sum_{\substack{d,f>Y\\A_{13}(K)}}(df)^{-b}
&\ll J^{2+b}(K+1)\sum_{d>Y}d^{-2b}\\
&\ll_b J^{2+b}(K+1)Y^{1-2b}.
\end{split}
\tag{SP16}
\]

Combining (SP15)--(SP16), and integrating over an interval of
\(dx/x\)-length \(\log2\), proves

\[
|Q[1_{A_{13}(K)}]|
\ll X^{b+1/2+\epsilon}(K+1).
\tag{SP17}
\]

The same argument applies to each cross edge.

**Signed union.** Let \(k\) count the four events holding at a tuple.
The pointwise identity has error bounded by

\[
\left|1_{\{k\ge1\}}-k\right|\le {k\choose2}.
\tag{SP18}
\]

Any two distinct cross edges form a two-edge forest on four vertices.
For fixed multipliers, choose the two root variables freely; each other
variable then lies in an interval of length at most \(2K\). Taking the
positive union bound over at most \(J^4\) multiplier choices shows that
each pairwise intersection contains at most

\[
O(J^4U_{\max}^2(K+1)^2)
=O(XL^{32}(K+1)^2)
\tag{SP19}
\]

tuples. Bound the coefficients by one and the weight by \(O(L^{12})\)
only for this overlap error. Equations (SP17)--(SP19) prove (SP13).
No positivity of a signed localized covariance is asserted. \(\square\)

statement:
### 3.1 A binary checksum does not automatically preserve a complex character

For a finite unramified prime set P and subset S, write w(S)=(-1)^|S| chi(product S). For a fixed nonempty toggle C,

    w(S symmetric_difference C)/w(S)
      =(-1)^|C| product_(p in C)chi(p)
                    product_(p in S intersect C)chi(p)^(-2).       (C1)

Therefore w(S xor C)=-w(S) for EVERY S if and only if

    chi(p)^2=1 for every p in C,
    (-1)^|C| product_(p in C)chi(p)=-1.                            (C2)

Necessity follows by comparing S empty with each singleton in C; sufficiency is substitution. The hypothesis product_C chi(p)=1 alone is insufficient for an odd toggle when nonreal phases occur.

Actual counterexample: take the primitive quartic character mod5 with chi(2)=i, chi(3)=-i, chi(11)=1 and C={2,3,11}. The empty subset pairs1 with66 with opposite coefficients. But {2} pairs2 with33, whose actual coefficients are BOTH -i. All four integers are squarefree5-units. The exact script checks all eight states. The restricted edge6<->11 is valid; a code must track the state as well as its syndrome.

For a binary matrix A and principal chi, if the parity vector1 lies in the row space of A, parity is constant on every syndrome class and there is no within-class sign cancellation. If it does not, the full uncut cube has balanced parity in every class: translate by an odd element of ker A. The multiplicative cutoff need not respect that translation. This is elementary code duality, not a new theorem about arithmetic cancellation. C1-C2 identify the extra phase failure for the actual complex coefficients.

## G166. Prime removal with exact correction and all-shell return

For a fixed finite prime block B, let e_B be μχ on squarefree divisors of
P_B, r_B be χ on all B-smooth integers, including prime powers, and
a_B(n)=a(n)1_{(n,P_B)=1}. With Dirichlet convolution,

\[
e_B*r_B=\delta_1,\quad a=e_B*a_B,\quad a_B=r_B*a,
\quad A_B(s)=\frac1{L(s,\chi)E_B(s)},
\quad E_B(s)=\prod_{p\in B}(1-\chi(p)p^{-s}).            \tag{95.8}
\]

For overlapping blocks, A_A A_B=A_{A∪B}A_{A∩B}. This is an exact
overlap identity; a determinant invariant under a common meromorphic
multiplier cannot exclude that multiplier's poles by itself. It preserves
the earlier overlap/renewal ancestry in [G79–G81](../[private research revision]/wild47-integration.md),
G92, G108 and [G135](../[private research revision]/wild55-integration.md).

For the field norm sup_{T>0} T^−γ||F||_{L²([T,2T],dt/t)}, Minkowski gives
the absolute forward/reverse coefficient costs

\[
\prod_{p\in B}(1+p^{-\gamma}),\qquad
\prod_{p\in B}(1-p^{-\gamma})^{-1}.                    \tag{95.9}
\]

Every shifted shell and small tail is included. These are valid coarse
bounds, not claimed sharp operator norms on a restricted arithmetic
source. A same-shell bound alone does not supply (95.9).

For smoothing kernels exp(−n/x) and exp(−(n/x)^2), the Mellin factors are,
respectively, Γ(s)/(L(s,χ)E_B(s)) and Γ(s/2)/(2L(s,χ)E_B(s)). Their gamma
factors are nonzero on Re(s)>0. A complete large-shell bound of exponent
γ, for every ε>0 and the required fixed characters, yields the usual
all-height reciprocal-L continuation by Cauchy–Schwarz and Mellin
integration, retaining small x. The principal pole is allowed. Choosing
a different block at each x does not provide one fixed Mellin transform;
the transition costs cannot be dropped. This is a conditional return,
not an estimate for the smoothed arithmetic field.

There is also a sharp-cutoff identity with an explicit small-argument
correction. If min B>√N, then for every real1≤x≤N,

\[
M_\chi(x)=M_{B,\chi}(x)
 -\sum_{p\in B,\ p\le x}\chi(p)M_\chi(x/p).            \tag{95.10}
\]

The correction uses the **original** Mχ, and includes Mχ(1)=1 at x=p.
Two removed primes cannot occur in an integer at most N. For
B⊂(N^α,N^b], 1/2<α<b<1, and an available bound
|Mχ(t)|≤C t^β on t≤N^{1−α}, where0≤β<1, elementary summation gives

\[
\left|\sum_{p\in B,p\le x}\chi(p)M_\chi(x/p)\right|
 \le C\left(1+\frac1{1-\beta}\right)
 N^{\beta+b(1-\beta)}.                                \tag{95.11}
\]

No prime number theorem is required. As b decreases to1/2, this absolute
method approaches exponent (1+β)/2. Using the current β=0.8748540364
would leave exponent greater than0.9374270182, which is inadequate.
To beat the current γ, reach5/6, or reach3/4 by this limiting budget,
one would need respectively β<0.7497080728, β<2/3, or β<1/2, as well as
the independent estimate for M_B and a strict admissible b. These are
unpaid prerequisites. An inadequate upper bound is not a lower bound
for the signed correction.

When used as detectors, the full norm is ||U_B−C_B||², including its cross
term. Chaining prime removal with another detector, or controlling both
simultaneously, remains valid only after paying (95.8)–(95.11) or a
stronger proved signed transfer. Thus the user's mixed chained/simultaneous
strategy remains open in its full scope.

## 5. A complete averaged zero-exclusion theorem

Fix tau>0 once, independently of X, and set

    g_tau(v)=(2*pi*tau)^(-1/2) exp(-v^2/(2tau)),
    H_chi,delta(x)=sum_n h_chi,delta(n)g_tau(log(n/x)).    (D9)

The series, and each fixed x-derivative, converge locally uniformly. The uniform d_3 majorant gives a Gaussian left tail as x tends to zero. Absolute Mellin Fubini on Re s>1 yields

    integral_0^infinity H_chi,delta(x)x^(-s) dx/x
          =exp(tau*s^2/2)D_chi,delta(s).                 (D10)

**Theorem D3.** Fix 4/5<gamma<1. Suppose for an ordinary chi, every epsilon>0 and all sufficiently large dyadic X,

    integral_I integral_X^(2X) |H_chi,delta(x)|^2 dx/x ddelta
                  <<_(chi,epsilon,tau) X^(2gamma+epsilon). (D11)

Then L(s,chi) has no zero in Re s>gamma. Its principal pole at one is not asserted to be a zero. If D11 holds for every ordinary chi at the same gamma, this gives the common zero-free constant c=1-gamma, with constants permitted to depend on chi.

Proof, including the exceptional parameter issue: choose a rational sigma_0>gamma and epsilon<2(sigma_0-gamma). Summing the weighted dyadic inequalities in D11 gives

    integral_I integral_1^infinity
       |H_chi,delta(x)|^2 x^(-2sigma_0) dx/x ddelta <infinity.

Tonelli implies that for almost every fixed delta this weighted square integral is finite. Cauchy--Schwarz then makes its Mellin integral holomorphic on Re s>sigma_0; logarithmic derivatives follow on compact sub-half-planes. Intersect over a countable sequence sigma_0 decreasing to gamma. The common Gaussian left tail completes holomorphy on Re s>gamma for almost every fixed delta in I.

For each hypothetical zero rho in that half-plane, D8 shows that the bad set {delta in I:C_delta(rho)=0} has measure zero. The zeros of a nonzero meromorphic L-function form a countable set. Remove the union of these bad sets, and the null set from the preceding Fubini step. At any remaining delta, all shifted entries in D7 are holomorphic throughout Re s>gamma (because gamma+1/5>1), and the cofactor is nonzero at every hypothetical zero there. A zero of multiplicity m would therefore give a pole of order m in D_delta, contradicting D10 and the holomorphic Mellin integral. The exponential multiplier never vanishes.

There is no finite-height cutoff in this proof, no selection of delta depending on X, no assertion that an average bound holds pointwise for every delta, and no missing residue from the principal pole: 1/L is holomorphic there. A fixed full-measure set of parameters is used after the all-scale summation. Countably many ordinary characters can also be intersected if desired; this does not require a conductor-uniform norm constant.

This uses a SMALLER paid small-prime sector than A=7 and therefore a LARGER hard remainder; it is a tradeoff, not an automatic improvement of the same H_F estimate. No candidate F meeting(C7) is supplied. The terminal-only F still has a large defect; F=R has zero defect but leaves F(N,1)=M_chi(N), a circular root estimate.

The final bridge is complete. If M_chi(x)<<x^(gamma+epsilon) for every epsilon and all large real x, then s integral_1^infinity M_chi(x)x^(-s-1)dx is holomorphic on Re s>gamma: on each compact set choose epsilon with room for all logarithmic derivatives. It equals1/L(s,chi) on Re s>1 by a*chi=delta. Meromorphic continuation of L times this function=1 excludes all zeros in the half-plane. The principal pole at1 gives a reciprocal zero; it is not an excluded L-zero. Floor extension covers real x; every finite height is present, and all imprimitive zeros remain. There is no Hecke or growing-conductor transfer.

## 3. The other author tests: precise certificate limits

### Free words and orthogonal integer fibers (27)

For squarefree q-unit n with k prime factors, all k! ordered words carry the SAME mu(n)chi(n). Summation P e_w=e_n has norm sqrt(k!) on that fiber; the minimum-norm right inverse sends e_n to their average, of squared norm1/k!. The empty word uses0!=1. Therefore the complete generic Cauchy price is

    (sum_n1/omega(n)!)^(1/2)(sum_n omega(n)!)^(1/2)>=#S.

The more general statement is correct: for an orthogonal sum H=direct_sum H_n and <u_n,v_n>=1, U=sum a_nu_n,V=sum v_n satisfy <U,V>=M, and

    ||U||||V||>=sum_n||u_n||||v_n||>=#S,

because |a_n|=1 on S. This is a lower bound on the PRODUCT OF NORMS used by that certificate, not on the scalar M. The density #S=kappa_q N+O_q(sqrt N), kappa_q=(phi(q)/q)product_(p not dividing q)(1-p^-2)>0, follows by the square-divisor identity and the full d^-2 tail.

Pair02 BR3-BR9 already constructs an increasing-word inverse with one word per integer, analytic bounded operator at Re s>1/2 and an unbounded generic reciprocal readout in the desired strip. Its B30/B07 already price collision restoration. W52's arbitrary internal fiber geometry is a valid general formulation of that obstruction, with modest record credit. It does not reject cross-integer correlations, a source-specific scalar estimate or a changed exact observable.

### All fixed finite preconditioners on the full sup space (02)

For B_gamma with norm sup_(x>=1)x^-gamma|f(x)| and f=0 below1, the locally finite dilation operator T_c has extended norm sum_n|c(n)|n^-gamma. To attain each finite prefix on unrestricted functions, set x=K and align f(K/n) with conjugate(c(n)); the arguments are distinct.

For FLOOR-INVARIANT functions, take a different integer X>K(K+1). Adjacent quotients X/n,X/(n+1), n<=K, differ by more than1. Monotonicity then makes each floor(X/n) a singleton quotient fiber among ALL n'<=X, not merely among n'<=K. Assign on that interval the value floor(X/n)^gamma times the aligning phase, and zero elsewhere. Its norm is<=1. As X tends to infinity the attained prefix tends to sum_(n<=K)|c(n)|n^-gamma. This proves the all-scale lower bound but does NOT identify a fixed-X merged matrix norm with an unmerged price. The finite exact witnesses independently verify this distinction.

For fixed finite b supported at most B, r=delta-b*chi. If b(1)=0, r(1)=1 gives norm>=1. Otherwise at every unramified prime p>B, r(p)=-b(1)chi(p); its weighted absolute tail diverges for0<gamma<=1. The elementary proof of sum_p1/p=infinity is valid: a convergent prime sum would bound the Euler products, while their expansions dominate arbitrarily long harmonic sums. Finite ramified exclusions change nothing.

The hypothetical contraction would have a legitimate return: T_chi M=1, hence M=T_b1+T_rM. A Banach solution U exists when ||T_r||<1, and b(1)!=0. On[1,2) the equation forces U=1; induction on integer intervals using x/n<x for n>=2 identifies U with the actual M, without assuming M belonged to B_gamma initially. Thus it is the full-norm premise that fails. Infinite/preconditioned arithmetic subspaces, moving families with paid tails, and cancellation-sensitive norms remain eligible. Pair01 MH8 rejects an unmodified polynomial-in-zeta absolute Newton norm; W52's EVERY finitely supported b extension is narrower in norm but broader in finite preconditioner choice. Neither is a universal inverse impossibility.

### Other selected screens (14,30,22)

Card14 supplies no actual chain complex, determinant line, two native factorizations or transition map. Treat its result as a failed STRUCTURE screen for that raw proposal, not a proof that no such H construction exists. The JN source retains b(pi)conj(b(pi')), CRT phase, cubic row characters, both marked arrays, both full projectors, rooted normalization and distinct-norm deletion. The bare geometric name supplies none of these. No synthetic matrix is credited as a native H counterexample.

For30, independent discs |z_j|<=1 have exact dual sup|sum c_jz_j|=sum|c_j|. But the N=20196,p=17,m=18 arithmetic fiber merges u=65,66: principal coefficient0, real mod4 coefficient-1 and quartic mod5 coefficient i, with their actual zero masks. The free-leaf price cannot be imported into this signed quotient. The N=30 complete depth-two tree has seven principal prime pairs; its first true leaf is0 and other six1, giving1-10+6=-3. It is a valid finite screen and G92 restatement, not a new lower bound or rejection of all SDP methods.

For22, on squarefree q-units, chi(p)chi(ell)=chi(ell)chi(p). The unit gauge chi(n) trivializes that ordinary cocycle, while the cutoff and alternating parity remain. Ramified directions have zero weight and are not inverted. Native JN has additional phases/projectors; this scalar square calculation does not flatten them. A coupled geometric construction is untested.

## 4. Protected audit25: a finite-prefix convex relaxation admits hidden poles

The high-reach card proposes separating zero-compatible coefficient data using finite convolution equations and a known tail envelope. A useful audit must name that body. If ALL equations a*chi=delta are imposed at ALL integers, the sequence is already uniquely mu chi; no free convex tail remains. If only finitely many equations are imposed, the following explicit completion identifies what that relaxation cannot certify.

Fix the PRINCIPAL character chi0 modulo any fixed q. Put w_q(n)=mu(n)^2 1_((n,q)=1), and let the first K coefficients be exactly a(n)=mu(n)chi0(n). For every n<=K, the finite equations

    sum_(d|n)b(d)chi0(n/d)=delta_(n,1)                         (C8)

force this prefix recursively, because chi0(1)=1. Conversely any tail beyond K leaves every equation(C8) unchanged. Preserve also ALL squareful and ramified zeros, real coefficients and the pointwise convex bound |b(n)|<=1.

Let1/2<gamma<sigma<beta<1. Suppose C>0 is consistent with the known prefix's summatory envelope, in particular |M_chi0(K)|<=C K^beta. Choose an integer T>=K with |M_chi0(K)|<=C T^beta/2. Choose

    0<lambda<=min(1, (C sigma/2) T^(beta-sigma)).

For any fixed nonzero real t, define the complete sequence

    b(n)=a(n)                              for n<=K,
    b(n)=0                                 for K<n<=T,
    b(n)=lambda w_q(n)n^(sigma-1)cos(t log n) for n>T.          (C9)

All claimed finite equations and global zero masks are exact. The coefficient bound holds because sigma<1 and lambda<=1. For K<=x<=T the sum is M_chi0(K), which obeys Cx^beta. For x>=T,

    |sum_(n<=x)b(n)|
      <=|M_chi0(K)|+lambda sum_(n<=x)n^(sigma-1)
      <= Cx^beta/2+(lambda/sigma)x^sigma<=Cx^beta.             ([restricted research revision])

The middle bound follows from the decreasing-function integral: sum_(n<=x)n^(sigma-1)<=x^sigma/sigma for0<sigma<1. Thus even a LITERAL old power envelope with a fixed consistent constant C survives, not merely a newly chosen big-O constant. The delay T can be arbitrarily large and t arbitrarily high.

Nevertheless its Dirichlet series has actual poles at sigma+it and sigma-it. This can be proved from the same elementary density used in W4, without a prime-distribution input. Write

    Q_q(x)=sum_(n<=x)w_q(n)=kappa_q x+O_q(sqrt x).

Initially Re z>1,

    D_q(z)=sum_n w_q(n)n^-z
          =kappa_q z/(z-1)+z integral_1^infinity
                                  (Q_q(x)-kappa_q x)x^(-z-1)dx.

The error integral is holomorphic for Re z>1/2, including its compact-set derivatives. D_q has one simple pole there, at z=1, with residue kappa_q>0. From(C9), initially Re s>sigma,

    B(s)=sum_(n<=K)a(n)n^-s
       +(lambda/2)[D_q(s+1-sigma-it)+D_q(s+1-sigma+it)
                  -sum_(n<=T)w_q(n)n^(sigma-1-s)
                         (n^(it)+n^(-it))].                 ([restricted research revision])

The finite terms are entire. Since t!=0, the other shifted D_q is regular at each of the two poles, so each residue is lambda kappa_q/2, nonzero. This gives meromorphic continuation at least to Re s>sigma-1/2. It is an exact analytic construction, not a numerical fit or an asserted L-zero. If t=0 is preferred, the single pole at sigma has residue lambda kappa_q.

**What this proves:** the convex relaxation consisting of the true finite prefix equations, all squarefree/nonunit masks, |b(n)|<=1 and the old summatory envelope contains pole-bearing completions beyond any proposed gamma<beta. A functional valid solely for that body cannot certify holomorphy of every compatible inverse candidate to the better line. Arbitrarily high t also defeats a conclusion that finitely many controlled heights cover all heights without a tail theorem.

**What it does not prove:** b is NOT the actual Mobius sequence and does not satisfy full convolution or global multiplicativity. For an unramified prime p>T, the full convolution residual is1+b(p), which is nonzero because |b(p)|<1. The actual L-function is fixed; these synthetic poles are not its zeros. Imposing the complete arithmetic equations, additional true tail correlations, or a stronger analytic constraint could exclude these completions. The audit does not rule out finite certificates that prove those additional facts by an independent theorem. It rejects only the asserted sufficiency of the specified relaxation.

This preserves the card's potential: identify an actual arithmetic constraint that removes(C9) and has a quantitatively paid all-height return. MH8's unpriced analytic tail, the standing finite-observation/readout cautions and W51's all-height source discipline are close ancestry. The explicit real, zero-masked, arbitrarily delayed completion with fixed-envelope control is the audit's concrete evidence; it is not a new general impossibility principle or a new literature claim.

## 5. Uniform audit09: exact parity-layer flux and its unreduced absolute price

This seed tries to couple adjacent squarefree parity layers with factorial weights. The exact source can be derived before testing any Poisson analogy. For every fixed ordinary complex chi, define

    B_k(X)=sum_(n<=X,omega(n)=k)mu(n)chi(n),
    B_j^(p)(Y)=sum_(m<=Y,omega(m)=j,p does not divide m)mu(m)chi(m).

Squareful terms vanish automatically. Every squarefree n with k>=1 prime factors has exactly k representations n=pm with p not dividing m. Each obeys a(pm)=-chi(p)a(m). Hence

    k B_k(X)=-sum_(p<=X)chi(p)B_(k-1)^(p)(X/p).              ([restricted research revision])

Natural zeros remain in both factors; no division by chi occurs. Prime powers cannot be inserted as new squarefree directions. All degrees0<=k<=D_X, where D_X is the actual maximal squarefree degree below X, are retained. Sum([restricted research revision])/k to obtain the complete root flux

    M_chi(X)=1-sum_(p<=X)chi(p)
       sum_(m<=X/p,p does not divide m)
                     mu(m)chi(m)/(omega(m)+1).               ([restricted research revision])

This is an exact deletion-edge normalization, not a new arithmetic estimate. Equivalently, with the full p-free cofactor polynomial

    G_(p,X)(t)=sum_(m<=X/p,p does not divide m)
                            mu(m)chi(m)t^omega(m),

one has

    M_chi(X)=1-sum_(p<=X)chi(p) integral_0^1 G_(p,X)(t)dt.    ([restricted research revision])

Every coefficient, the strict p-free restriction, hard product cap, degree and endpoint is present. There is no independent-prime replacement and no restriction to central degrees. These are finite polynomials, so the integral is literal; no logarithm through a fugacity zero is taken.

The full coefficientwise absolute price of([restricted research revision]) is EXACTLY

    sum_(p,m:pm<=X,p not dividing m)
              |chi(p)mu(m)chi(m)|/(omega(m)+1)
       = #{2<=n<=X:mu(n)!=0,(n,q)=1}.                        ([restricted research revision])

For each nonzero n the k parent edges each have weight1/k. This proves the equality without asymptotics. By W4 it is kappa_q X+O_q(sqrt X)-1. Thus the natural degree normalization removes ordering multiplicity but leaves the entire exponent-one positive mass. It does not make the actual signed sum large. Cancellations between different n or correlated p-free responses are precisely what a useful method must exploit.

Factorial rescaling cannot by itself change this conclusion. Replacing a layer by B_k/k! requires the compensating readout k! to recover M; one must estimate the resulting correlated arithmetic scalar, not declare the normalized coefficients to be a smaller source. The k=1 prime layer is itself unchanged by1!, and central-layer concentration does not settle its compensation by composites. Pair02 word/readout results, W52 W1-W4 and prior factorial-flux constructions are the exact broader ancestry;([restricted research revision])-([restricted research revision]) specialize the full ordinary sharp cutoff and its zero masks.

There is a complete useful approximation interface. For any proposed cofactor polynomials or integrable functions Gtilde_(p,X), put

    Atilde(X)=1-sum_(p<=X)chi(p) integral_0^1 Gtilde_(p,X)(t)dt,
    E(X)=-sum_(p<=X)chi(p) integral_0^1
                                   [G_(p,X)-Gtilde_(p,X)](t)dt.

Then M_chi(X)=Atilde(X)+E(X). Bounds for BOTH complete signed contractions at X^(gamma+epsilon), for every fixed chi and every epsilon/all sufficiently large X with common gamma, yield the Mellin return of section2. If the cofactor approximation depends on X, this formula returns to the fixed source BEFORE continuation. An absolute error bound might suffice but must pay([restricted research revision]) when it treats all edges independently. A favorable variance, central-layer fit, or a small error at each selected prime without its summed price does not prove the required statement.

A related exact log-weight check exposes another easy omission. For the ordinary source,

    a(n)log n=-sum_(p^j|n,j>=1)chi(p)^j log p a(n/p^j).

This follows by comparing the coefficient of each formal log p, including n divisible by p^2: the j=1 and j=2 terms can cancel to restore mu(p^2)=0. Summing and applying Abel summation gives

    M_chi(X)log X=integral_1^X M_chi(t)dt/t
       -sum_(p^j<=X)chi(p)^j log p M_chi(X/p^j).              ([restricted research revision])

The prime-power terms are essential in this different convolution representation, even though the original a has squarefree support. Discarding them is not the same identity as([restricted research revision]), which explicitly excludes p in its cofactor. No spectral contraction or cancellation bound is inferred from([restricted research revision]).

The audit preserves the high-reach idea of estimating an actual signed edge flux. What fails is the specific claim that adjacent-layer bookkeeping, factorial normalization, or independent absolute edge control already supplies a power saving. A complete arithmetic estimate for([restricted research revision])'s signed cofactor responses remains open.

## 6. Every card remains in the record

The author tested01/02/27/14/30/22 and developed27/02/01. The two independent critic audits are25/09. The other22 cards remain untested, not disproved by analogy. Near gains,1/6 and1/4 remain eligible; the full original portfolio is retained.



## 7. Exact evidence, calibration and next mathematical action

The independent check.py ran ONCE and passed. Its12 merged cases include q=1, complex q=5 and imprimitive q=20, N=2048 at r=1/2/3 and N=20196 at r=1. Every coefficient was independently reconstructed from the half-open smooth interval, not only grouped from paths. It checks actual collar values, singleton status, full root/short/small/hard equality, strict hard support, exact integer-power versions of(C3), and nonzero hard contributions. Y=3 is a finite partition test, not the eventual logarithmic cutoff or a quantitative arithmetic claim.

Six floor-quotient witnesses test singleton isolation for the ALL-scale supremum argument. Nine parity-flux cases verify all layers, complex/ramified zeros, the exact rational edge price and complete prime-power logarithmic coefficients. Four exact finite convolution prefixes support audit25; its analytic pole construction is proved in section4 rather than inferred from finite checks. # [private research revision]: plain-L2 Hankel source, complete complement and a signed obstruction

Root accepts G158–G160 after complete independent author/reviewer intake.
The accepted written constant remains
`c11=312864909/2500000000=.1251459636`. The new result removes a
derivative-norm prerequisite and identifies the exact remaining estimate;
it does not prove that estimate or increase c. The licensed density
`K=28114053/6250000` retains its preceding-c10 ancestry. Inherited analytic,
positive-slot-uniformity and external-admission obligations remain open.

Evidence: [author](hankel-source/report.md), [independent development and
review](hankel-source-review/report.md), [author exact receipt](hankel-source/exact-checks.json),
[reviewer exact receipt](hankel-source-review/receipt.json),
[input pins](hankel-source-review/input-receipt.json), and
[retention manifest](retention-manifest.json). Frozen source statements are
interpreted with the qualifications below. The changed arithmetic identity
already occurs in [DP21–24](../[private research revision]/dilation-pole-killing.md); the earlier
Sobolev formulation is [W29 R29E1–7](../creative/round29-review.md).
The full-rectangle exponential-test return is [G149](../[private research revision]/wild58-integration.md).
These are reused components, not newly claimed identities or priority.

## G158. Actual Type I removal on plain L2, including every character

Fix a Dirichlet character chi modulo q, extended by zero at nonunits;
principal, complex and imprimitive characters are included. Put
`alpha(n)=mu(n)chi(n)`, `alpha0=alpha 1_(n<=Y)`, `alpha1=alpha-alpha0`,
with integer Y>=1. Since `alpha*chi=delta_1`, literal Dirichlet convolution gives

    alpha = 2 alpha0 - alpha0*alpha0*chi + alpha1*alpha1*chi.

The pairs in these products are ordered and can share primes. Separate
pieces need not vanish on squareful integers; only their sum restores the
original coefficient. Neither squareful coefficients nor n=1 can be deleted.

For an arithmetic sequence z, write `Z(x)=sum_(n<=x) z(n)` and let
`Gamma[z]_(a,L)` be the operator on plain `L2(0,L)` with kernel
`exp(-a(t+u)) Z(exp(t+u))`, where `0<a<1`, `X=exp(2L)`.
Complex bilinear tests conjugate the test function, not the arithmetic
character. All operator norms below refer to this precise source.

Here is the prerequisite removal. If `B(y)=sum_(ell<=y)b(ell)` is zero
below 1 and bounded in modulus by Cb, then
`h(v)=exp(-av)B(exp(v))1_(v>=0)` has `L1` norm at most `Cb/a`. For each k,

    exp(-a(t+u)) B(exp(t+u)/k) = k^(-a) h(t+u-log k).

Zero extension, reflection, convolution, translation and restriction give
an operator norm at most `Cb k^(-a)/a`. This uses the complete partial sum
B before taking its modulus. No input derivatives or endpoint traces enter.
The same estimate holds for arbitrary rectangular restrictions.
An atom z(n) similarly costs at most `|z(n)| n^(-a)/a`.
With `A_Y=sum_(d<=Y)|alpha(d)|d^(-a) <<_a Y^(1-a)`, a nonprincipal
character has `Cb<=q`, and therefore

    | ||Gamma[alpha]|| - ||Gamma[alpha1*alpha1*chi]|| |
       <= (2 A_Y + q A_Y^2)/a <<_(a,q) Y^(2(1-a)).

This conclusion is not asserted for the principal character unchanged.
Indeed at Y=1 its removed piece is `2 delta_1-chi`; its partial sum is
`-(phi(q)/q)x+O_q(1)`. Its operator norm is
`(phi(q)/q)(exp(2(1-a)L)-1)/(2(1-a))+O_(a,q)(1)`.
This is the removed operator's size, not a lower bound for the full sum.

For a repair valid for every fixed character, choose a fixed prime r not
dividing q and set

    kappa = delta_1 - r chi(r) delta_r,
    c = kappa*alpha,                 b = kappa*chi.

Thus `c(n)=mu(n)chi(n)-r chi(r)1_(r|n)mu(n/r)chi(n/r)`; it is a
different coefficient sequence, including its possible squareful terms.
The sequence b is periodic of period qr with mean zero. Writing
`C_chi(y)=1_(chi principal)(phi(q)/q)y+E_chi(y)`, with `|E_chi(y)|<=q`,
shows `B(y)=C_chi(y)-r chi(r)C_chi(y/r)` is bounded by `q(1+r)`.
The linear terms cancel for the principal character, for which chi(r)=1.
Consequently the exact identity and norm comparison are

    c = 2 kappa*alpha0 - alpha0*alpha0*b + alpha1*alpha1*b,
    T_Y = Gamma[alpha1*alpha1*b],
    | ||Gamma[c]|| - ||T_Y|| |
      <= [2(1+r^(1-a)) A_Y + q(1+r) A_Y^2]/a.

The actual remaining partial sum is
`sum_(d,e>Y; de<=x) alpha(d)alpha(e) B(x/(de))`.
After expanding B it retains the joint cap `de ell<=x`, not merely
the individual bounds `d,e<=X/(Y+1)`, `ell<=X/(Y+1)^2`.

For completeness, the source return is literal. Initially in Re s>1,
`sum c(n)n^(-s)=m_r(s)/L(s,chi)`, where
`m_r(s)=1-chi(r)r^(1-s)`. G149's exponential test gives
`-d/ds[m_r(s)/(s L(s,chi))]`. A diagonal-box bound
`||Gamma[c]_(a,L)|| << exp(2 eta L)` controls every unit rectangle:
opposite translations preserve t+u and put rectangles i,j in a balanced
box of upper endpoint `(i+j)/2+1`. At a heavier weight sigma>a+eta,
their costs are bounded by a constant times
`exp(-(sigma-a-eta)(i+j))`, a summable double series.
Hence bounds `||Gamma[c]|| <<_(chi,epsilon) X^(gamma-a+epsilon)` for
every epsilon>0 and all L make that differentiated transform holomorphic
in Re s>gamma. Any zero rho of L with `gamma<Re rho<1` creates an
uncancelled pole: m_r has zeros only on Re s=1, rho is nonzero, and
differentiation raises the pole order. This single-repaired-source return
**retains the previously accepted safe-region premise Re s>=1**;
it does not silently prove that premise or rule out numerator cancellation
on that line. The principal pole at 1 is not an L-zero. Imprimitive factors
remain literal. No height-uniform lower bound on m_r is needed or claimed.
The unrepaired nonprincipal version uses G149 without this numerator.

## G159. All arithmetic and frequency complements are accounted for

Split the actual d,e sum disjointly into d=e, d!=e with gcd(d,e)>R,
and d!=e with gcd(d,e)<=R. The last class includes equality at R.
The first has partial sum at most `Cb sqrt(x)` in modulus, so its norm
is at most `Cb D_a(X)`, where

    D_a(X) = integral_0^L exp(2(1/2-a)t) dt.

It is O(X^(1/2-a)) for a<1/2, equals L for a=1/2, and is O(1) for
a>1/2. This estimate does not treat chi(d)^2 as positive.
For the second class, write d=gu,e=gv and discard coprimality only in
the positive counting bound. The count is at most
`x(1+log x) sum_(g>R)g^(-2) << x(1+log x)/R`.
Restoring the complete B before taking absolute values gives norm
`O_(a,q,r)(X^(1-a)(1+log X)/R)`.

For the third class define its exact coefficient

    C_Y,R(n) = sum_(de ell=n; d,e>Y; d!=e; gcd(d,e)<=R)
                   alpha(d)alpha(e)b(ell),
    S(x) = sum_(n<=x) C_Y,R(n).

The observed kernel is `k(v)=exp(-av)S(exp(v))1_(0<=v<=log X)`.
With Fourier convention `hat k(tau)=integral k(v)exp(-i tau v)dv`
and `s=a+i tau`, direct integration of each atom gives

    hat k(tau) = [F_Y,X(s) - X^(-s) S(X)]/s,
    F_Y,X(s) = sum_(n<=X) C_Y,R(n)n^(-s).

Both the complete hyperbolic cap and the sharp endpoint term are essential.
An atom at n=X cancels in this expression, consistent with a corner of
measure zero. Nonintegral X uses its literal summation cap.
The estimates
`sum_(n<=X)|C_Y,R(n)|n^(-a) << X^(1-a)(1+log X)^2` and
`|S(X)| << Cb X(1+log X)` yield
`|hat k(tau)| << X^(1-a)(1+log X)^2/(1+|tau|)`.

Split the entire full-line multiplier at `|tau|<=Omega` and its complement,
then reflect, extend and compress to L2(0,L). This defines Tlo and Thi,
with exact `Tlo+Thi` equal to the third arithmetic class and

    ||Thi|| <<_(a,q,r) X^(1-a)(1+log X)^2/Omega.

The low-pass kernel need not be causal; the full-line multiplier definition
makes the compression legitimate. A uniform full-symbol bound is sufficient
for the compressed norm, but is not necessary or equivalent to it.
A finite frequency sample or a rectangularized Dirichlet polynomial does
not supply the missing estimate.

Combining these disjoint contributions gives the complete comparison

    | ||Gamma[c]|| - ||Tlo_(Y,R,L,Omega)|| | <<_(a,q,r)
       Y^(2(1-a)) + D_a(X)
       + X^(1-a)(1+log X)/R + X^(1-a)(1+log X)^2/Omega.

The original nonprincipal source obeys the same formula with b=chi,c=alpha.
No comparison with a different detector's native norm is asserted.

Choose `0<a<gamma<1`, `gamma>1/2`, and
`0<nu<min(gamma-a,gamma-1/2)`. Put
`delta=(gamma-a-nu)/(2(1-a))`, `omega=1-gamma+2nu`,
`Y=floor(X^delta)`, `R=floor(X^omega)`, `Omega=X^omega`.
Then 0<delta<1/2. The Type I exponent is gamma-a-nu, the high-gcd and
high-frequency exponents are gamma-a-2nu before logarithms, and the
diagonal is strictly smaller. All these errors fit below the target.
What remains is exactly

    OPEN-LOW: ||Tlo_(Y,R,L,Omega)||
                 <<_(chi,epsilon) X^(gamma-a+epsilon)
              for every epsilon>0 and all L.

Parameters are fixed before X. The exponent gamma must be common to all
fixed characters; constants and onset may depend on chi and the fixed
repair prime. For these same cutoffs, the complete comparison makes
OPEN-LOW equivalent to the corresponding full-source growth bound up to
the displayed smaller error. Naming it does not create an arithmetic gain.

The following exact corridors use a=1/2:

| conditional c | gamma | nu | delta | omega | d,e exponent cap | ell exponent cap | paid exponent | open X exponent |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| .12515 | 17497/20000 | 1/20000 | 937/2500 | 501/4000 | 1563/2500 | 313/1250 | 937/2500 | 7497/20000 |
| 1/6 | 5/6 | 1/600 | 199/600 | 17/100 | 401/600 | 101/300 | 199/600 | 1/3 |
| 1/4 | 3/4 | 1/1000 | 249/1000 | 63/250 | 751/1000 | 251/500 | 249/1000 | 1/4 |

The first would improve current c11 by `10091/2500000000=.0000040364`
if OPEN-LOW and its complete return were supplied. Its required L-growth
exponent is .7497, below current .7497080728. All three remain conditional;
changing a alone does not save a power.

## G160. Every fixed character has a large isolated low-frequency sector

This independent extension identifies necessary cancellation. In either
source B(y)=1 for 1<=y<2. Let P_X be the unramified primes in
`sqrt(3X/5)<p<=sqrt(7X/10)`, set `c0=(1/2)log(5/4)`, and
`J=[L-c0,L]`. On J squared, `x=exp(t+u)` lies in `[4X/5,X]`,
whereas each product pp' lies in `(3X/5,7X/10]`. Thus
`8/7<=x/(pp')<5/3`, and B is exactly 1. Distinct ordered prime pairs
survive d,e>Y and gcd<=R for every corridor above.

The ordinary prime number theorem gives
`|P_X| ~ 2(sqrt(7/10)-sqrt(3/5))sqrt(X)/log X`;
removing finitely many ramified primes does not affect this asymptotic.
Only the ordinary PNT is used, not primes in progressions; see
[NIST DLMF 27.2.3](https://dlmf.nist.gov/27.2.E3).

Partition P_X into the finitely many values lambda of chi(p). At every
sufficiently large X some class has at least |P_X|/d primes, where d is
the size of the character's image on units. On pairs from that class,
`mu(p)mu(p')chi(p)chi(p')=lambda^2`, a constant of modulus 1.
The isolated sector's compression to J is therefore rank one with norm

    N_lambda(N_lambda-1) X^(-a)
         (exp(2a c0)-1)/(2a) >>_(chi,a) X^(1-a)/(log X)^2.

The large phase may vary with X. Finite pigeonhole gives one fixed phase
on an unbounded subsequence, not every phase for all X. No progression
equidistribution premise is hidden here.

This sector also survives the frequency cut: pp'>3X/5 forces ell=1 in
the entire observed cap, so its own endpoint/weighted coefficient mass
is O(X^(1-a)/(log X)^2). The same exact Fourier identity bounds its
high-frequency norm by `O(X^(1-a)/(Omega (log X)^2))`.
As Omega grows, its low-frequency part still has the displayed lower
bound. Hence isolated sectors cannot each obey the desired gamma<1 bound.

This is **not** a lower bound for the full signed Tlo, Gamma[c], Gamma[alpha]
or a native detector. Arithmetic selection is not an orthogonal operator
projection, and signed subset monotonicity is false. If OPEN-LOW holds,
the sum of the remaining low-frequency sectors must itself have norm at
least this order along that subsequence, by the reverse triangle inequality,
and must cancel the displayed sector. The next useful estimate must keep
this interaction rather than bound each sector separately.

## Verification and next estimate

Both complete reports, both exact helpers and both receipts were read.
The author checks fixed principal, complex and imprimitive characters,
literal convolution, squareful/nonunit behavior, endpoint arithmetic,
partitions and rational corridors. The independent helper uses different
characters and develops the all-character phase argument. Its finite
examples verify algebra, not the PNT, asymptotic norm estimates or OPEN-LOW.
No redundant helper rerun, formalization or kernel claim is substituted
for written mathematical review.

Twelve frozen artifacts and ten input pins are retained. Those ten include
seven mathematical sources, one historical index and two assignment records.
The index pin is bound to its exact [private research revision] Git blob, not overwritten to
match the advanced current index. Both authorship scopes are STOP/released.
No host-local claim is copied into canonical research.

The useful next target is a signed estimate for the full compressed
low-frequency operator, preserving the hyperbolic cap, endpoint and phase
interactions. G160 rules out sector-by-sector absolute payment. Compatible
mixed-detector or adaptive-cutoff components may be used only with a proved
transfer into this precise source. The 29-family/109-child portfolio and
all later mechanisms remain preserved; near gain, 1/6 and 1/4 remain live.

## Exact source and every omitted coefficient

Fix delta=1/100. Terms with |log(n/x)|>=delta L/2 have absolute Gaussian
tail O_A(X^-A), for every fixed A, after increasing X. The same holds with
any fixed divisor multiplicity: d3(n)<=C_epsilon n^epsilon and the Gaussian
lattice bound at a slightly wider variance pay the complete tail. Constants
depend on the requested fixed A,delta,tau. This is an actual bound, not a
finite truncation of the source definition.

In the retained central range, n<=2X^(1+delta/2)<z³ eventually. Every n
having two distinct prime divisors above z therefore has exactly two such
primes, each with valuation one. It has a unique form n=rpq with z<p<q.
Moreover r<=2X^(delta/2)/kappa²<z, so neither rough prime divides r and
f(rpq)=f(r). The omitted three-prime and repeated-rough-power cases all
lie in the paid Gaussian tail. This proves, after paying that tail,

    R_z(x)=sum_(r<=X^delta) f(r)
                 sum_(z<p<q) g(log(rpq/x)) + O_A(X^-A),       (CT3)

where the extended terms outside the central range have at most d3(n)
representations and are included in the same tail estimate. Every omitted
r>X^delta forces n>kappa²X^(1+delta), so its entire completion also has
the same divisor-weighted Gaussian bound. These statements apply to the
completed prime sum as well as the original coefficient field.

Replace p<q by half the ordered p,q sum, subtracting the actual p=q
diagonal. Its absolute size is O_tau(X^(1/2+delta/2)): ignoring primality
and the lower cutoff, the Gaussian lattice estimate after the substitution
u=2log(p/sqrt(x/r)) gives sum_p g(log(rp²/x))<=C_tau sqrt(x/r).
Summing r<=X^delta proves this bound. It is o(X/L³). No coefficient for
p² is falsely identified with the two-distinct-prime source.

Use the conductor-bounded natural free core only for the witness; it has

When V>=20W/21, z<=V/20 and
(89/100)V-(21/25)W>=4W/525. Thus the free theorem applies with reserve.
Root counting costs Z^s, and

    s+Ec(V,z)=Ec(W,z)-(6Ac-1)s, 6Ac-1>=6869/6250>0.

When V<20W/21 the old unmarked density plus actual high-bin slot price
gives exponent rho W+delta z-(6rho-1)s, with s>W/126. Since G<=3kz,

    (19/54-1/6-3k(.68))/21-1/5000
      =112003/257985000 >0.

Bounded/free fixed-inducing cores have actual raw population

## [restricted research revision]-Q1: nine strata, their normal spaces and a nonsimple boundary

For H={(n(x)a(t),n(y)a(t),n(x+y)a(t))} acting on (P1)^3 in characteristic
different from2, the finite chart has d=z3-z1-z2 transforming to t^2 d.
There is one geometric open orbit d!=0, one d=0 orbit, three single-infinity
orbits, three double-infinity curves and the all-infinity point. The review
gives every stabilizer. Normal weights are +2 at d=0, -2 at each
single-infinity orbit, (-2,-2) at each curve and (-2,-2,-2) at the point.
Unipotents act trivially on these first-order quotients, not necessarily
on higher jets. The open stabilizer is mu2; source fibers still carry its
central-character condition.

Odd nonarchimedean local fields have four open square classes, hence12
rational orbits; finite fields of odd order have10. Replacing H(F) by the
F-points of its effective algebraic quotient would erase real information.
The eight product Bruhat charts do not form the H-orbit decomposition.

There are four boundary divisors: three coordinate infinities and
D0: Z3 W1 W2-Z1 W2 W3-Z2 W1 W3=0. Three divisors meet at each boundary
curve in a two-dimensional normal space. At the deepest point D0 has
equation w1w2-w1w3-w2w3=0, an ordinary quadratic-cone singularity. The
boundary is not simple normal crossings. Counting strata or divisors
does not supply a basis of equivariant germs or justify a matrix size.

The group is nonunimodular: left Haar measure is dx dy d*t/|t|^4,
with modular function |t|^-4. The open orbit has invariant measure
dz1 dz2 dd/|d|^3; G^3/H does not acquire an invariant measure thereby.
Source fibers, Mellin character, density and specialization must be fixed
before converting normal weights to a spectral exponent.

statement:
# [private research revision]: complete operator returns and an actual detector repair

Root accepts G149–G151 at the scopes below, after full author and independent
review reads. The written analytic endpoint remains
`c11=312864909/2500000000=.1251459636`, with boundary
`gamma11=.8748540364`. No arithmetic power saving is proved in this cycle.
The useful additions are a complete off-diagonal Hankel return, a fully
priced matching return and an actual two-variable detector whose principal
branch obstruction can be repaired exactly. These distinguish workable
interfaces from assumptions that would already solve the old problem.

The [author](wild58/report.md), [independent review](wild58-review/report.md)
and [retention manifest](retention-manifest.json) preserve all thirty seeds,
six author tests, three developments and two independent audits. Thirty-three
frozen files and thirteen mathematical source pins match their original
bytes. Actual host-local claims are excluded. The original 29-family/109-child
portfolio and later additions remain intact. F0/analytic ancestry,
positive-slot uniformity and external definition/import/admission remain open.
There is no formalization, kernel replay, new proof packet or public record claim.

## G149. The full logarithmic Hankel growth criterion

Fix an ordinary Dirichlet character chi, with squareful and ramified zeros
kept literally, and put

    M(x) = sum_(n<=x) mu(n) chi(n),       M(x)=0 for x<1,
    h_a(v) = exp(-a v) M(exp(v)),         v>=0, 0<a<1.

Let Gamma_(a,L) be the full Hankel operator on L2(0,L) with kernel h_a(t+u),
and K_a(L) its operator norm. For complex chi use the bounded bilinear form

    B_a(f,g) = integral integral h_a(t+u) f(t) g(u) dt du.

Conjugating one test input identifies its norm with the usual operator
norm. It does not conjugate chi or replace the arithmetic source by an
absolute value. Both variables and every off-diagonal rectangle are present.

If sup_L K_a(L)<infinity, density extends B_a to L2(0,infinity) twice.
For Re(z)>0 the vector E_z(t)=exp(-zt) is holomorphic with
norm squared 1/(2Re(z)). Consequently Q(z)=B_a(E_z,E_z) is holomorphic,
and initially for s=a+z, Re(s)>1, absolute convergence gives

    Q(z) = integral_0^infinity v M(exp(v)) exp(-s v) dv
         = -d/ds [1/(s L(s,chi))].                         (G149.1)

A zero rho of L with Re(rho)>a would give a pole of the derivative on the
right. Since a>0, rho is not zero; its pole cannot be removed by the factor
s or by differentiation. Meromorphic identity continuation contradicts
the holomorphy of Q. The principal-character pole instead gives a zero of
1/L and causes no false obstruction. The conclusion covers every fixed
finite height and the literal imprimitive L function. Constants may depend
on the fixed character; no growing-conductor or height-uniform growth
estimate has been inferred.

### Every rectangular block is paid

This is the substantive completion of the growth adapter. Write I_j=[j,j+1).
Opposite translations send the I_i by I_j rectangle to the square
[(i+j)/2,(i+j)/2+1) in both coordinates, preserving t+u. Therefore the
unweighted block norm is at most K_a((i+j)/2+1). Passing to a heavier
weight sigma>a multiplies it by at most exp(-(sigma-a)(i+j)). If

    K_a(L) <= C exp(2 eta L),       eta>=0, all L>0,

the sum of the norms of all blocks is bounded by

    C exp(2 eta) [1-exp(-(sigma-a-eta))]^(-2),
    provided sigma>a+eta.                                  (G149.2)

The sum is a deliberately coarse sufficient bound for the full bilinear
form: each block input norm is bounded by the norm of its complete input.
It includes arbitrarily unbalanced rectangles, not only a diagonal strip.
Apply (G149.1) at the heavier weight, taking sigma<1 when needed. Thus for
one fixed 0<a<=gamma<1 the complete hypothesis

    K_a(L) <<_(chi,epsilon) exp(2(gamma-a+epsilon)L)
    for every epsilon>0 and all L>0                         (OPEN-HK)

for every fixed ordinary character excludes all L zeros in Re(s)>gamma.
For any desired sigma>gamma choose epsilon<sigma-gamma first. Values
above one are already in the absolute Euler-product domain; arbitrarily
small positive margins cover the boundary. Alternatively uniformly bounded
Hankel forms for a sequence a decreasing to gamma give the same return.

At a=1/2, the current first-gain threshold for the exponential growth
coefficient is strictly less than .7497080728. The candidate gamma=.87485
would require coefficient .7497 and return c=.12515, a gain .0000040364.
The 1/6 and 1/4 targets require coefficients 2/3 and 1/2. These are
conditional targets. The elementary |M(x)|<=x gives coefficient
2(1-a), namely one at a=1/2, and supplies no gain.

### What can and cannot supply that estimate

The exact Hilbert–Schmidt square is

    integral_0^(2L) w_L(v) exp(-2av) |M(exp(v))|^2 dv,
    w_L(v)=v for v<=L, and 2L-v for L<=v<=2L.

Bounding this positive energy reimports the familiar complete energy
problem. Operator norm can in principle be smaller: the nonarithmetic
kernel exp(i(t+u)^2) has operator norm at most sqrt(pi), by extension and
Plancherel at frequency 2t, whereas its Hilbert–Schmidt norm is L. This
functional example supplies no estimate for mu(n)chi(n).

For the single model kernel R exp(lambda(t+u)), the singular value is
|R| integral_0^L exp(2Re(lambda)t)dt. Critical modes grow linearly and
unstable modes exponentially. This is not a license to decompose or truncate
an infinite arithmetic pole expansion without paying the complement.

The exact arithmetic form also reads

    B_a(f,g) = sum_n mu(n)chi(n)
               integral_(t+u>=log n) exp(-a(t+u))f(t)g(u)dtdu

for compactly supported inputs. Extending h_a by zero to the negative line,

    (partial_v+a) h_a = sum_n mu(n)chi(n)n^(-a) delta_(log n).

The atom at n=1 is retained. On compactly supported smooth inputs in the
positive half-line its pairing with f*g is a B_a(f,g)-B_a(f',g).
This gives an H1 by L2 bound from the Hankel bound, not a converse or a
native H estimate. Credit the broad operator/observability and reciprocal
return ancestry, including [W29](../creative/round29-review.md),
[W50 energy](../[private research revision]/wild50-integration.md) and
[W54 prediction](../[private research revision]/wild54-integration.md). The new credit is the
specific complete source interface and its balanced-block growth return.

## G150. Complete matching displacement, with the old rank equivalence retained

Let V have basis the squarefree q-units n<=X, parity mu(n), and all diagonal
character actions W_chi(n)=chi(n). An odd differential d with d squared
zero commuting with every character must preserve each reduced residue
class: the characters separate that finite group. Write E_a,O_a for the
two parity counts and I_a=E_a-O_a. Hodge decomposition then gives

    dim ker(dd*+d*d) >= R_q(X) := sum_a |I_a(X)|.

Matching min(E_a,O_a) opposite signs within each residue attains equality;
unit arrows give nonzero spectral gap one. The gap alone says nothing
about the residual rank. Orthogonality gives the exact comparisons

    max_chi |M_chi(X)| <= R_q(X) <= sum_chi |M_chi(X)|
                                      <= phi(q) max_chi |M_chi(X)|.

These are already [[private research revision] G135](../[private research revision]/wild55-integration.md).
Do not count this reformulation as a new weaker arithmetic prerequisite.
For example q=5,X=80 has residue indices (0,-3,-4,1), hence minimum rank
eight; a fourteen-state rank of a particular construction is not universal.

For one neutral prime r=1 mod q, the exact pairing m with rm, r not
dividing m, has residual rank

    d_q (r-1)/(r+1) X + O_(q,r)(sqrt(X)),
    d_q = zeta(2)^(-1) product_(p|q) p/(p+1).

The square-divisor expansion proves the squarefree q-unit count
d_q X+O_q(sqrt(X)). If only one chi is being preserved, chi(r)=1 suffices;
otherwise the multiplier 1-chi(r) must remain. This linear-rank obstruction
belongs to the named neutral-prime rule, not to every differential.

### A full future-partner return

In each reduced residue class there are infinitely many negative squarefree
integers (primes) and positive ones (a fixed r=1 mod q times different
primes in that class). Only infinitude of primes in each reduced progression
is imported here; see [NIST DLMF 27.11.9](https://dlmf.nist.gov/27.11.E9).
No prime-distribution error estimate is used. Thus a fixed global
same-residue pairing of the two signs exists. Orient each pair (u,v) by
mu(u)=1, mu(v)=-1 and set a=min(u,v), b=max(u,v). Define

    D_q(X) = sum_(X<=a<2X) (b-a),       X=1,2,4,... .

Every future partner is included, even when b is much larger than 2X.
For a common 0<gamma<1, the full hypothesis

    D_q(X) <<_(q,epsilon) X^(1+gamma+epsilon)
    for every epsilon>0 and every fixed q                 (OPEN-D)

implies ordinary zero exclusion in Re(s)>gamma. Indeed, initially Re(s)>1,
absolute regrouping gives

    1/L(s,chi) = sum_pairs chi(u)(u^(-s)-v^(-s)).

For sigma=Re(s)>0 the difference is bounded by
|s|(b-a)a^(-sigma-1). Summing dyadic shells with epsilon below a compact
set's horizontal margin gives normal convergence on Re(s)>gamma. The
identity L F=1 continues meromorphically, excluding zeros and permitting
the reciprocal zero at a principal pole. All fixed finite heights and the
literal imprimitive factors are covered; no uniform growth assertion follows.

Monotone same-residue pairing has crossing count R_q(t). Tonelli identifies
the total *clipped* interval length in [A,B] with integral_A^B R_q(t)dt.
That is not the complete D_q(A): omitted future portions and intervals
entering from earlier shells matter. Under G135's existing summatory/rank
bound with gamma>1/2, endpoints grow proportionally to their rank k and
pair displacement is O(k^(gamma+epsilon)); the complete D bound follows.
This adapter has not evaded the original arithmetic difficulty.

The global neutral-prime rule has the unconditional full cost

    D_q(X) = (r-1) sum_(X<=m<2X,(m,qr)=1) mu(m)^2 m
           = (3/2)(r-1)d_(qr) X^2 + O_(q,r)(X^(3/2)).

Partial summation of the squarefree count proves it, with the positive main
coefficient intact. Thus this rule cannot meet the positive-cost target for
any gamma<1. Other matchings or signed displacement estimates remain open.
Near/1/6/1/4 cost exponents are respectively below1.8748540364,11/6,7/4.
The new useful bill is complete future-partner cost and this actual rule's
failure; G135, W01 signed transport and [private research revision] priced coupling retain credit.

## G151. An actual two-variable repair and two fully priced detector interfaces

### The squarefree lift and its principal branch obstruction

Define, initially Re(s),Re(t)>1,

    F_chi(s,t) = sum_(m,n>=1) c(m,n)m^(-s)n^(-t),
    c(m,n) = mu(mn)chi(mn)2^(-omega(mn)),

with zero coefficient when mn is not squarefree. Natural ramified zeros,
the prime two when unramified, and c(1,1)=1 all remain. Unique allocation
of every prime to one of the two coordinates gives

    F_chi(s,t) = product_p [1-chi(p)(p^(-s)+p^(-t))/2],
    F_chi(s,s) = 1/L(s,chi).

On every finite hard product cutoff, the complete diagonal coefficient of
k is exactly mu(k)chi(k), since a squarefree k has 2^omega(k) allocations.
This is an actual source identity. Its absolute convergence cone is exactly
Re(s)>1 and Re(t)>1: the prime terms on either coordinate axis force the
two prime series, and their convergence suffices. Finite ramification
does not alter this cone.

For x=chi(p)p^(-s),y=chi(p)p^(-t), on both real parts greater than1/2 put

    log G(s,t) = sum_p [log(1-(x+y)/2)
                       - (1/2)log(1-x) - (1/2)log(1-y)].

Power-series logarithms are legitimate since |x|,|y|<1. The linear terms
cancel and the quadratic term is (x-y)^2/8; compactly uniform bounds by
a constant times |x| squared+|y| squared give normal convergence.
Thus G is holomorphic and nowhere zero there, G(s,s)=1, and initially

    F_chi(s,t)^2 L(s,chi)L(t,chi) = G(s,t)^2.                (G151.1)

For principal chi fix a safe real t0>1. Since L(s,chi) has a simple pole
at1, the right side of F(s,t0)^2=G(s,t0)^2/[L(s)L(t0)] has a zero of order
one at s=1. A square of a holomorphic function has even vanishing order.
Hence this particular F cannot be holomorphic near (1,t0), and cannot
extend to the whole product half-plane Re(s),Re(t)>gamma for
1/2<gamma<1, even if zero exclusion is already known. The diagonal itself
is consistent: both reciprocal factors there have the same zero.

This actual obstruction redirects the lift, rather than rejecting all
two-variable detectors. A sloping tube, different source or explicit pole
normalization remains possible. The exact simple repair B=F squared keeps
its genuine two-variable convolution coefficients

    b(m,n) = sum_(d|m,e|n) c(d,e)c(m/d,n/e),
    B(s,t) = G(s,t)^2/[L(s,chi)L(t,chi)],
    B(s,s) = 1/L(s,chi)^2.

These b are not the original c. For fixed1/2<gamma<1, holomorphy of B on
the whole product half-plane is equivalent to zero exclusion for L in
Re(s)>gamma. Fixing t0 and nonvanishing G proves the forward implication;
holomorphic1/L, including its principal-pole zero, proves the converse.
No growth estimate or coefficient cancellation follows from this equivalence.
This is a corrected exact return, not an independent gain or a claimed
literature priority.

### Fixed native H packets: commuting operations still have a mixed bill

Use the exact Eisenstein source in
[[private research revision] h-joint Sections1–2](../[private research revision]/h-joint/report.md), including long
prime ideals pi,pi' of distinct rational norms, original orientations and
bad-place data, complete ordered short g,g' including equality, the complex
core, rational gcd screen, both rooted mark weights, both projectors and
independent heights. The coefficient systems remain
a(n)=alpha(n)eta(n)chi_n(lambda)^(-2)gamma_2(n) and
xi(g)=alpha(g)^3 eta(g)^3. Nothing is replaced by an integer-norm or
positive-divisor surrogate.

For M=pi*pi',Q=q_M the finite group
(O/M) times(O/pi) times(O/pi') has size Q squared. Its unitary transform
F has factor1/Q and phases -Rh/M-Ps/pi+P's'/pi'. The literal dual kernel is

    K = b(pi)conjugate(b(pi')) zeta_CRT
        chi_pi(h)^3 chi_pi'(h)^3 chi_pi(s)^2 chi_pi'(s')^4,

with all natural zeros. Put kappa=conjugate(K) and take inner product linear
in the first argument. The complete raw packet is <F W,kappa>.

Freeze this packet except a designated smooth row profile rho_i and cap A_j.
Write W_ij=rho_i 1_(A_j)W0, where W0 is the source formula with that factor
omitted, retaining the full union of the caps. No division by a profile or
removal of its zeros occurs. Then exactly

    Delta H = <F[(rho1-rho0)(1_A1-1_A0)W0],kappa>,
    |Delta H| <= ||(rho1-rho0)1_(A1 symmetric-difference A0)W0||_2 ||kappa||_2.

The multiplication operations commute, but their four-corner finite
difference need not vanish. A zero operator commutator is not a small
rectangle-flux estimate. A true row translation V_delta instead satisfies

    [P_A,V_delta]W(R,...) = (1_A(R)-1_A(R-delta))W(R-delta,...),

and changes both rooted-projector arguments. This is distinct from the
accepted [restricted research revision] adapter, which moves only the smooth profile from R/sqrt(K)
to (R+P+P')/sqrt(K), leaving sharp support and projectors in place. No
inter-scale map between varying prime-pair groups has yet been constructed.
The finite corner example is algebraic evidence, not an arithmetic lower bound.

The return still requires the entire raw target
G K [N+L+(NL)^(2/3)] sqrt(Omega1 Omega2) P_orig, then physical multiplication
by N^(-1)G^(-2) exactly once. Every corner, commutator and outside complement
must be paid. No .004 H gain follows. The genuine inter-scale idea remains
open, with [G89](../[private research revision]/wild48-integration.md) and
[G136](../[private research revision]/wild55-integration.md) ancestry retained.

### Two delay channels: local division versus a finite-height floor

For the complete fixed Gaussian field with Mellin transform
exp(tau s squared/2)/L(s,chi), physical dilation
D_lambda U(x)=U(x)-lambda^beta U(x/lambda) has multiplier
m_lambda(s)=1-lambda^(beta-s). Complete every-epsilon shell L2 bounds
of exponent gamma on lambda=2,3 give holomorphic channel transforms to
Re(s)>gamma, retaining the complete source and Gaussian left tail.

The multipliers have just one common zero, s=beta, simple for each.
Consequently these bounds exclude zeros in the target half-plane except
possibly a simple real zero at beta. A multiple zero still leaves a pole.
Independently excluding beta or adding another paid channel closes that
exception. Local division away from beta needs no global positive floor.
This retains the [principal Gaussian return](../[private research revision]/principal-gaussian-integration.md)
and [G109 bank analysis, including its G47 exception](../[private research revision]/sol04-integration.md).

Simultaneous recurrence prevents any all-height positive floor for a fixed
positive weighted sum of the squared multipliers. A finite-height replacement
is available. With kappa=log(2)log(3)/(2pi), 0<t0<=|t|<=T,

    max(|m_2(beta+it)|,|m_3(beta+it)|)
      >= min(2t0 log(3)/pi,
             4exp(-kappa T)/((log(2)+log(3))sqrt(3))).

For t>0 choose nearest nonnegative integers k,l to t log(2)/(2pi),
t log(3)/(2pi). If both vanish, the larger phase error is at least
t0 log(3). Otherwise 3^k and2^l are distinct integers, so the logarithmic
gap is at least exp(-kappa T)/sqrt(3). Combining the two phase errors and
2|sin(e/2)|>=2|e|/pi for |e|<=pi proves the bound; symmetry covers t<0.
The exponential price is deliberately coarse and yields no arithmetic
channel bound or uniform limit as T increases.

The retained weighted-degree and hidden-tail examples are narrowly scoped:
exp(i sin(t)) with weight A(1+epsilon cos(t)) has weighted crossing total
2A epsilon despite degree zero; exp(rho v)1_(v>=A) has Laplace transform
exp(-(s-rho)A)/(s-rho). Neither is a counterexample for actual native H or
an all-scale Möbius invariant. They identify unpaid weighted amplitude
and tail-continuation assumptions only.

## Evidence, selection and next mathematical use

The author froze thirty substantive cards before detailed history. The three
deliberate choices were26/19/25. Literal all-group p<.10 and p<.01 predicates,
followed by previous-choice exclusions, produced pools24/11/25; three
independent stored draws selected17/27/11. All eligible cards were retained,
without semantic exclusions or rerolls. The critic's blind priority and
uniform orders fixed protected22 and uniform08. Final selection was recorded
after receiving outcomes but is mechanically forced by those earlier orders;
this chronology is disclosed. Author final work ended36 seconds past its
16:15 deadline. Both author and reviewer stopped and released their own claims.

The independent finite checks cover840 residue cases,12 neutral partitions,
1024 complete lift-diagonal coefficients and five mixed-corner examples.
They support exact algebra, not infinite analytic claims. Root read the
arguments and helpers without rerunning unchanged tests. Historical hashes
of the index/proof are observations of their then-current bytes, not claims
that those mutable documents still have those hashes.

OPEN-HK is the most distinct quantitative target here: seek cancellation
in the actual signed Hankel form before a Hilbert–Schmidt majorant. OPEN-D
has a complete bill but substantial G135-equivalent difficulty. The repaired
lift is a valid object for mixed/chained detector work, with its convolution
source and product-domain requirement explicit. None can be inserted into
native H without its own source transfer. The active [private research revision] actual mixed
inverse attack continues separately; no signed R22 sector or physical
complement is removed by this cycle.

## 4. Amplifiers, comparison, joint Cauchy and actual radii

Set s=17/500, e=1/5000, k=309/1000, r=9/2-C=33/250 and b_j=s+je, j=0,...,30. At t=z/M=s choose j=1; otherwise choose b_(j-1)<t<=b_j. Set

    a_j/M=k b_j, sigma_j=3a_j,
    A/M<=A_j=min(2N+b_j,1-(C-1)b_(j-1)),
    g/M<=g_j=r b_j,
    g=(n1+n2+(9/2)z-M)_+.

The amplifier is selected from original slot width before rows, transforms, extraction, bins and scale derivatives. Both equal-product rectangles use the same j. The ceiling loss is paid even at the left endpoint. On a cell the cap envelope increases, so use its upper endpoint; the capacity envelope decreases, so use its lower endpoint. Each bounds every point of the cell; their minimum is therefore a valid upper bound, without asserting it equals the true continuous maximum. The thirty choices have

    a_min/M=52839/5000000, a_max/M=309/25000,
    A_max=4401/5000, g_max=33/6250.

A common relative mesh below a_min/(10M) implies every eta_mesh<sigma_j/(6M), separates original prime scales from amplifier pools eventually, and may be reduced to fit all budgets. The pool stays (Z^a_j/2,Z^a_j]. Excluding row, projector, support and mask primes removes O(log Z) choices; the eventual prime count absorbs these. The representation factor (Mmax+2sigma)/(sigma/6) is bounded over this finite atlas and adds no power. Also 7a_max/M=.08652<1/4, with reserve 4087/25000.

Choose the atlas and common loss/mesh first; fix the finite original slot system and arithmetic family; take the maximum of thirty thresholds and finite smooth/height orders, including all four derivative pairs. The original data and live scales follow that threshold. In an endpoint amplitude class the selector's I, hence z and j, remain fixed during the plain scale suprema. No derivative crosses an atlas boundary and no growing reconstruction label is introduced.

For comparison take L=M/4. Both original plains exceed L. Preserve the whole-product character, two profiles, natural slots and masks in the two equal-product rectangles. For the comparison alone, exact Euler deletion costs Z^o(1); its first plain is at most M/4. Reflect the second only if its length exceeds M/2. The exact natural-character reflection/restoration gives retained second length <=M/2+xi; lower annuli have summable central weights and upper tails are rapid. Therefore the old budget is

    M/4+M/2+(9/2)(M/25)+xi=.93M+xi,

with reserve .07M. Nonempty subunit scales are clipped by bounded dilation. Empty slot families use unrestricted nonprincipal zero-slot input. No newly chosen indicator is put inside Poisson summation of the original centered difference.

In the first transform keep the complete signed projector and all first common labels inside the Hilbert direct sum. Write c,d,p,R,E,s0 for source widths, B_c=(3c-5d-R)_+/6 and B_d its exchanged version. The required side bounds are

    sum_lambda N_C,lambda << Z^(p+A-c+R+E+B_c+epsilon),
    sum_lambda N_D,lambda << Z^(p+A-d+R+E+B_d+epsilon).

The outside power M-A-R/2-E and joint Cauchy give total exponent

    M+p-(c+d)/2+R/2+(B_c+B_d)/2 <= M

by the source primewise balance. Per-label branches retain -s0 and multiply once by Z^(p+s0+epsilon); the high branch proves the joint bounds directly. No independent label count follows them.

The main physical ball has logarithmic exponent

    Kmain=K0+(d-c)_++6a+omega,
    K0=2A-c-d+R+E-M.

Here omega includes retained-frequency padding and positive support-doubling reserve. This covers the genuine amplified first range. Error branches keep their own exponent

    K0+max(d-c-2w+w_o,0)+3a+delta1+reserve.

Substituting the main radius gives nominal second width

    M'=M-(c-d)_+-6a-omega-g2+t2,

and the exact identity

    (A-c-c2-M')-(A-M)
      =6a+omega-min(c,d)-(c2-g2)-t2 <=6a+omega.

The second projector, signed priority allocation, extraction scalars and clipping remain intact. Its inner allowance Delta=b2-p2+B_c+a is at least a. These are original-source radius and normalization identities, not optimized declarations.

## 2. Development 1: exact free-word reconstruction and its price (W52-27)

Fix a Dirichlet character chi modulo q, including its zeros. Let S be the squarefree q-units at most N. For n in S put a_n=mu(n)chi(n), so |a_n|=1. A free word representing n orders its k=omega(n) distinct prime factors. There are exactly k! such words, and **every one has the same arithmetic sign and phase** a_n.

Let W_N be the counting Hilbert space of all such words, and A_N=l2(S). Define P e_w=e_n. On the n-fiber, P is the sum functional and has norm sqrt(k!). Hence

    ||P|| = max_(n in S) sqrt(omega(n)!).                         (W1)

The minimum-norm right inverse sends e_n to (1/k!)sum_(w->n)e_w, of squared norm 1/k!. Equal signed word amplitudes without the 1/k! factor project to k! a_n, not a_n. Antisymmetric word components lie in ker P, so cancellation there does not change the surviving scalar coefficient.

For the minimum-norm lift R a and the full arithmetic readout P*1, Cauchy has price

    sqrt(sum_(n in S)1/omega(n)!)
       * sqrt(sum_(n in S)omega(n)!) >= |S|.                    (W2)

This is not an artifact of choosing factorial weights. More generally, let H be an orthogonal sum of fibers H_n. Suppose u_n,v_n in H_n satisfy <u_n,v_n>=1, using the convention linear in the first slot. The exact source and observable are U=sum a_n u_n and V=sum v_n. Then <U,V>=M_chi(N), but

    ||U||||V|| >= sum_(n in S)||u_n||||v_n|| >= |S|.             (W3)

The first inequality is scalar Cauchy and the second is the individual extraction identity. This covers arbitrary Hilbert geometry **within** each orthogonal integer fiber and any exact diagonal rescaling. It does not cover an operator creating correlations between different n, an arithmetic-specific estimate for <U,V>, or a nonlinear argument.

For completeness, the certificate floor has exponent one:

    |S| = kappa_q N + O_q(sqrt N),
    kappa_q=(phi(q)/q) product_(p not dividing q)(1-p^-2)>0.     (W4)

Expand mu(n)^2=sum_(d^2|n)mu(d). Coprimality forces (d,q)=1; the number of m<=N/d^2 with (m,q)=1 is (phi(q)/q)N/d^2+O_q(1). Summing the floor errors to sqrt N and completing the d^-2 series each costs O_q(sqrt N). The product is positive because sum p^-2 converges. This proves W4 without a prime-distribution theorem.

The N=210 checks give |S|=129,85,106 for q=1,4,5; the corresponding raw Cauchy prices are about158.409,93.659,122.349. These check the finite formula only. W1--4 are the proof. The maximal-headroom hope of importing free-word orthogonality therefore fails at its specified generic projection step. A redesigned method must estimate interaction between **different integer fibers** before generic Cauchy. The old ordered-prime operator already avoids k! overcounting and still owes its actual signed readout; this result supplies no improvement to it.
title: 2. Development 1: exact free-word reconstruction and its price (W52-27)
