## 5. The phase survives, and its identity-cell germ is nonzero

For a_u(x)=1_O(x)u^floor(v(x)/2), |u|=1, exterior completion E preserves
its interior values. Negative valuations are invisible to (4), by (7).
Summing paired annuli gives (1) exactly.

The difference of two phase readouts is

    J_s(Ea_u)-J_s(Ea_v)
      =(1-z) A z^2 (u-v)/[(1-Au z^2)(1-Av z^2)].       (9)

It is not identically zero when u!=v. In particular the t-derivative at0
is i log(Q)(1-z)A z^2/(1-Az^2)^2. This proves that the actual coefficient
constraints and the same H-character line do not force the phase to be
constant. Neither the already-known compact projection nor a new source
twist has been used.

The poles in the local Mellin variable satisfy

    chi2(p)u Q^(1-2s0)=1, Re(s0)=1/2,
    Res_(s=s0) J_s(Ea_u)=(1-Q^(-s0))/(2 log Q).        (10)

Their absolute residues lie between (1-Q^-1/2)/(2 log Q) and
(1+Q^-1/2)/(2 log Q). They are nonzero for EVERY |u|=1. Phase changes their
imaginary position, not their real part. These local poles at1/2 are not
hypothetical global zeta zeros and do not by themselves prohibit a bound
at exponent .874864 or smaller.

For finitely many distinct u_j, a linear combination of (1) with coefficients
independent of s has disjoint pole sets for the different j. Vanishing of every
geometric-series pole forces every coefficient to vanish. It cannot also retain
the normalized constant coefficient1. This is a finite phase-span obstruction
to becoming the primitive local space, not an obstruction to the Hilbert
vector return. The hard squarefree vector itself gives 1-z.
In particular these identity-cell meromorphic readouts span an infinite-
dimensional space as u varies. A proposed finite-rank boundary reduction must
explain what its additional transport does to this already visible family;
finite rank of the missing relative map is not disproved by this fact alone.

For a positive probability measure on the phase circle, exact scalar
primitive recovery requires integral u^r dnu(u)=0 for every r>=1. The
negative moments are conjugates, so Fourier uniqueness forces normalized
Haar measure. Finite positive quadrature cannot impose all those conditions.
For example averaging the Nth roots of unity yields

    (1-z)/(1-(A z^2)^N),                              (11)

which removes the first N-1 repeated-square levels but leaves a geometric
tail. Independent local phase averages reproduce hard deletion and expose
its original arithmetic energy; they are not the common scalar t-family's
signed cancellation estimate.

# [private research revision]: complete large-common-factor payment in the Liouville source

Accept G182-G184 after the [author proof](large-gcd/report.md), independent
[review](large-gcd-review/report.md) and stronger
[complete proof](large-gcd-review/support.md), followed by controller
reconstruction. The [retention manifest](retention-manifest.json) binds
fourteen original files and eleven source inputs. Both writers stopped
and normally released their own claims. No formalization was performed.

The accepted source-relative value remains
c11=312864909/2500000000=.1251459636. The density license still comes from
the preceding c10 family; F0/analytic ancestry, original positive-slot
uniformity and external definition/import/admission obligations remain
open. The new theorem pays a complete complementary source, but the
retained signed arithmetic estimate is unproved.

## G182. Complete masked large-gcd theorem

Fix b>1, an integer k>=4 and B0. For X>=2, real G>=1, bounded sequences
|a1(d)|,|a2(e)|<=1, |b0(l)|<=B0, and an arbitrary complex mask
|theta(d,e,l)|<=1 fixed before live x varies, put

    v_G(n)=sum_(d e l=n, gcd(d,e)>G) a1(d)a2(e)b0(l)theta(d,e,l),
    F_G(x)=sum_(n>=1) v_G(n) exp(-n/x^b-i(n/x)^k).

Then on the full real shell [X,2X], with measure dx/x,

    ||F_G||_1+||F_G||_2
      <<_(b,k,B0,epsilon) X^epsilon [X/G+X^(b/2)/sqrt(G)].     (G182.1)

The constant is uniform in every sequence, mask and real G, with no upper
polynomial cap on G. The mask may depend on X,G and all tuple labels;
it may not depend on live x. Natural zeros, shared primes, strict or
closed arithmetic cuts and output-dependent support all fit this scope.
This is a full source norm theorem, not a pointwise bound or monotonicity
claim for signed subsets.

Write r_G(n)=#{r>G:r^2 divides n}. Exact root collisions give

    sum_(n<=Y)r_G(n) <=2Y/G,
    sum_(n<=Y)r_G(n)^2
      =sum_(r,s>G)floor(Y/lcm(r,s)^2) <=16Y/G.                (G182.2)

For the second bound set r=gu,s=gv,(u,v)=1. The two lower bounds on
r,s give g>G/min(u,v). Summing g^-2 leaves
(2Y/G)sum min(u,v)/(u^2v^2)<16Y/G. Equal roots, multiple square
representations and the strict endpoint r>G are included.

Every ordered tuple has exact gcd r, so d=ru,e=rv,(u,v)=1. Dropping
coprimality only in an absolute upper bound leaves at most d3(n/r^2)
factorizations. Thus for each fixed eta>0,

    |v_G(n)| << n^eta r_G(n),
    sum_(n<=Y)|v_G(n)| <<Y^(1+eta)/G,
    sum_(n<=Y)|v_G(n)|^2 <<Y^(1+2eta)/G.                    (G182.3)

The needed local multiplicity estimate is, for an interval I of length h
inside [cN,CN],

    sum_(n in I)r_G(n) <<h/G+N/G^2.                         (G182.4)

Reverse n=r^2 l: at most CN/G^2 positive l occur, and each permissible
real r interval has length O(h/(sqrt(N)sqrt(l))). Sum length plus one.
This is valid for all G>=1, including h<1, singleton endpoints and empty
blocks. The stronger old alternative with error min(N^(1/3),N/G^2)
is valid but unnecessary for this refinement.

A smooth nonnegative majorant of the shell, followed by two integrations
by parts, bounds the complete kernel by

    exp(-c(n+m)/X^b) min(1,[X^k/|n^k-m^k|]^2),              (G182.5)

with the minimum set to one on the diagonal. The derivative of the phase
has no stationary point on the fixed positive support. Damping
derivatives are fixed polynomials absorbed by a weaker exponential.
Exponential convergence justifies the full infinite expansion.

Pay n<=X pointwise by X^(1+eta)/G. Norm triangle pays its entire
interaction with the remaining source. On each bounded-overlap
comparable high block n,m~N>=cX, put H=X^k/N^(k-1). The local count
and full coefficient mass give the positive absolute pair bound

    exp(-cN/X^b)N^(2eta)[HN/G^2+N^2/G^3].

The integer kernel row sum O(1+H), collision bound and
2|v_n v_m|<=|v_n|^2+|v_m|^2 give, on the SAME pair majorant,

    exp(-cN/X^b)N^(2eta)(N/G)(1+H).

Taking the minimum bounds that block by the common factor times

    X^k/(G^2 N^(k-2))+N/G
                   +min(N^2/G^3,X^k N^(2-k)/G).             (G182.6)

The local +1 term keeps the diagonal when H<1; off-diagonal integer
distances start at one. Alternatively, separate the exact diagonal
first, reserving N/G solely for it, and use the O(H) off-diagonal row
sum. Both arguments retain all multiplicities and ordered pairs.

Absorb the coefficient loss using actual damping:

    N^(2eta)e^(-cN/X^b) <<X^(2b eta)e^(-cN/(2X^b)).

This avoids any illicit G^eta<=X^epsilon assumption when G is enormous.
The last two branches in (G182.6) meet at N_*=X G^(2/k); their entire
dyadic sum is

exactly. Fix an ordinary chi modulo q and an unramified prime p. Put

zeros. The p^2 coefficient is -p chi(p)^2. The two complete cofactors

    b0(n)=chi(n)[1-p1_(p|n)-p1_(p^2|n)+p^2 1_(p^3|n)],

       #{ordered(d,e):de=m,d>U(n),e>V(n),gcd(d,e)<=G}.

    h/600-1/1000-1/4000=219737987/3000000000000>0.

Above Z^(h+10^-10), the original raw absolute exponent has the form B_raw+(h+zeta0)(1+epsilon)-zeta0*v+epsilon. This pays arbitrarily large negative power without applying a central-row density estimate there.

The three contour frequencies remain independent. The reciprocal denominator is bounded after the complete original w-inversion. The principal poles are separately extracted; joining segments keep reciprocals inside their buffered zero-free regions or on the global line. The Gaussian controls its own height and the other Mellin transforms have arbitrary fixed polynomial decay. Raw unseparated numerator/conductor-height bounds have a fixed polynomial Z-degree before tail orders are selected; sufficiently high fixed order gives Z^B T^-N. Neither arithmetic indicators nor a row-selected discontinuous cutoff are differentiated. No reciprocal zero or nonprincipal pole is crossed without the original source accounting.

The common-saving quantifiers are decisive. From mu and the fixed strictly positive margins first choose real buffers, moment/parent-width loss, capacity decrement and amplitude mesh. Choose a finite positive original slot system totaling ell with each slot smaller than d0 times every required relative mesh; its minimum fixes mu_P. For each fixed target afterward choose S, the fixed anchor/dictionary and finite internal moment/profile/Sobolev orders. ## 7. Trying actual squarefree averaging in the localized Gram

The next attempted repair keeps the signed mu(a)mu(b) and uses only the arithmetic square mu(g)^2. This is the source of the global half-power error in(7); it is natural to test whether the same averaging works after localization. The following restricted theorem identifies the precise loss.

For an integer H>=1, let E_(N,H) be the part of E_arc(N) with reduced quotients a=n/g,b=m/g both <=H. This is a symmetric signed sector, not necessarily a positive energy. For H<=N, define

    J_(a,b)=integral_(1/min(a,b))^infinity v^(-2r)
               integral_0^(1/q) Phi(av u)conjugate(Phi(bv u))du dv,

    D_H=sum_(a,b<=H; (a,b)=1; (ab,q)=1)
        mu(a)mu(b)chi(a)conjugate(chi(b))
            delta(abq) J_(a,b)/(ab)^r.

Then, for every fixed epsilon>0,

    E_(N,H)=N^(-2r)D_H
             +O_(q,r,epsilon)(N^(-2r-1/2)H^(3/2+epsilon)),
    |D_H|<<_(q,r) H.                               (22)

These statements do not use a hypothetical Mobius correlation estimate. To prove them, keep g as the variable carrying mu(g)^2 and substitute x=u/N. For each reduced pair a,b the summand before the outer coefficient is

    N^(-2r-1) sum_(g>N/min(a,b); (g,abq)=1)
                     mu(g)^2 F_(a,b)(g/N),
    F_(a,b)(v)=v^(-2r) integral_0^(1/q)
                          Phi(av u)conjugate(Phi(bv u))du.

Apply(5) by partial summation. Boundedness and the Lipschitz bound for Phi give, almost everywhere,

    |F(v)|<=C_(q,r)v^(-2r),
    |F'(v)|<=C_(q,r)[v^(-2r-1)+(a+b)v^(-2r)].

With m=min(a,b), the error for that pair is at most

    C_(q,r) 2^omega(abq) N^(-2r-1/2)
       [m^(2r-1/2)+(a+b)m^(2r-3/2)]/(ab)^r.

For a<=b, summing the first term gives O(H^(3/2+epsilon)); the part involving b uses sum_(a<=b<=H)b^(1-r), which gives the same bound (an inessential logarithm when r=2 is absorbed by epsilon). The part involving a is no larger than the first term. This proves the error in(22). The main term satisfies |J_(a,b)|<=C min(a,b)^(2r-1); after a<=b, summing a^(r-1)b^(-r) gives O(H), proving the second bound. The derivative jumps of the periodic Bernoulli functions do not contribute hidden atoms: Phi is continuous and Lipschitz, so the displayed first derivative bounds suffice for absolute-continuity partial summation.

This is where the tempting global proof changes. In(7), complete-period Fourier orthogonality supplies an extra factor (ab)^(-r), making the density-error sum convergent over every quotient. In the localized sector that factor is absent, and the accumulated error is H^(3/2+epsilon). At H on the order of N, the error returns to N^(1-2r+epsilon), with no power gain. Moreover H=N still omits a,b>N; those contain the genuinely small-gcd pairs in the finite core and cannot be called a negligible tail. For comparison, choosing H=N^(1-2c-kappa) makes both parts of(22) smaller than the desired energy. This only covers a sector already included in the paid large-gcd region g>N/H; it is not a new endpoint improvement.

Thus there is a proved, uniform arithmetic sector approximation, but using it at the scale needed for the full source requires a new cancellation or density-discrepancy estimate. The failed extension is quantitative: one must improve the H^(3/2) accumulated error, and control the omitted large quotients, rather than simply quote squarefree equidistribution. No assertion that equality in this coarse error is an impossibility theorem is made.

statement:
## G78. Uniform depth and the full physical tail

Let a(n)=mu(n)chi(n), ell(n)=chi(n), m_Y(n)=a(n)1_(n<=Y),
and use Dirichlet convolution below.
Set d_Y=delta-ell*m_Y. For fixed b>1 choose a fixed integer Y>=2 with

    eta=zeta(b)Y^(1-b)/(b-1)<1.
    Q_k=m_Y*(delta+d_Y+...+d_Y^(*(k-1))).

The inverse identity a*ell=delta gives, for every k>=1,

    a-Q_k=a*d_Y^(*k),
    Q_k(n)=a(n) for n<(Y+1)^k,
    sup_k sum_n |Q_k(n)|n^(-b) <= zeta(b)/(1-eta),
    sup_k sum_n |a(n)-Q_k(n)|n^(-b)
        <= B_b=zeta(b)(1+1/(1-eta)).

These include complex and ramified characters. The support inequality is
strict. Q_k is a polynomial in infinite arithmetic series, generally not
a finite-support Dirichlet polynomial. Newton doubling reaches Q_(2^r)
in O(log log X) formal stages; this is not a computational complexity bound.

For g_tau(v)=(2 pi tau)^(-1/2)exp(-v^2/(2tau)), let

    U(x)=sum a(n)g_tau(log(n/x)),
    N_X=2X exp(C sqrt(log X)),
    k_X=floor(log N_X/log(Y+1))+1,
    V_X(x)=sum Q_(k_X)(n)g_tau(log(n/x)).

The full tail, with no hidden cutoff of Q_k, obeys

    sup_(X<=x<=2X)|U(x)-V_X(x)|
      <= B_b sup_(X<=x<=2X, n>=N_X) n^b g_tau(log(n/x))
      << X^(b-C^2/(2tau)+o(1)).

A power-of-two depth at least k_X has
the same bound. Concretely b=2,Y=4 give eta<1/2, Q norm<4 and B_b<6.
C=sqrt(3tau) pays the complete error at X^(1/2+o(1)), so for every
fixed gamma>1/2 the every-shell norm bound for V_X is equivalent to that
for U, allowing every positive epsilon loss. Return to fixed U before
using its Mellin transform exp(tau s^2/2)/L(s,chi).

The inverse algebra and prefix are AH20/W43 ancestry; uniform depth and
the complete tail are the new increment. No gamma<.874861 estimate of
V_X is proved. The old absolute-norm obstruction at b<=1 remains valid
at its own scope and does not contradict this b>1 tail argument.
title: G78. Uniform depth and the full physical tail

### B1. Exact centered source

Now use the distinct ORDINARY source a(n)=mu(n)chi(n), for a fixed ordinary Dirichlet character modulo q. Retain a(1)=1, prime2, squareful zeros and every character zero. Set M(x)=sum_(n<=x)a(n), psi_chi(y)=sum_(d<=y)Lambda(d)chi(d), and delta_chi=1 for principal chi and0 otherwise. [restricted research revision]/W55 C1-C3 already proves

    R_chi(x)=sum_(d<=x)Lambda(d)chi(d)M(x/d),
    M(x)log x=int_1^x M(t)dt/t-R_chi(x).                     (B1)

The inverse formula with unit/head terms and its complete zero return are prior credit. W64 does not relabel that identity or the old divergent absolute kernel as new.

For integer N>=2 and any floor-invariant input f(t)=f_floor(t), define the pole-centered functional

    J_N(f)=sum_(d<=N)Lambda(d)chi(d)f_(floor(N/d))
                    -delta_chi int_1^N f_(floor(N/u))du.     (B2)

The continuous measure du has Mellin transform1/(s-1), so it is exactly the principal logarithmic-derivative pole subtraction. At finite N its endpoints are literal. The complete return is

    R_chi(N)=J_N(M)+delta_chi int_1^N M(N/u)du.               (B3)

In particular the restored principal term cannot be dropped. It equals N sum_(n<=N)a(n)/n-M(N), including the endpoint n=N correctly.

Merge equal integer quotients BEFORE absolute values. For1<=m<N let

    L_m=N/[m(m+1)],
    c_m=psi_chi(N/m)-psi_chi(N/(m+1))-delta_chi L_m.

Then exactly

    J_N(f)=sum_(m=1)^(N-1)c_m f_m.                           (B4)

The lower interval endpoint is strict and the upper inclusive. The state m=N contributes zero, since its only possible atom is d=1 with Lambda(1)=0 and its continuous interval has length0 after clipping at1. Thus neither an independent-error norm before merging nor a lost unit term is being used here.

For0<beta<1 and a prefix Y<N define the scaled norm on remaining independent states by

    C_(beta,Y)(N)=N^(-beta)sum_(m>Y,m<N)|c_m|m^beta.           (B5)

This is the exact operator norm under |f_m|<=m^beta and f_m=0 for m<=Y: choose f_m=m^beta conj(c_m)/|c_m| at nonzero c_m. A fixed known prefix is a separately known affine contribution; differences of admissible continuations have this zero-prefix form.

statement:
## 4. Uniform wildcard S23: an explicit compact certificate algorithm and its exact limit

This replacement goes upstream to the actual periodic character, using the G128 normalization. Let delta=1 for a principal character and 0 otherwise, r=delta phi(q)/q, A(x)=sum_(n<=x)chi(n), and b(t)=A(e^t)-r e^t. Periodicity gives |b|<=q. The actual function

    F_chi(s)=((s-1)/(s+1))^delta L(s,chi)/s                  (15)

has exactly the ordinary L zeros in Re s>0, with multiplicity. At the principal pole its removable value is r/2, which is nonzero. A nonprincipal character receives no extraneous s-1 factor. All imprimitive factors and all heights are retained.

Its causal Laplace source is explicit:

    f(t)=b(t)                                      nonprincipal,
    f(t)=r e^-t+b(t)-2 integral_0^t e^(-(t-u))b(u)du principal,
    |f(t)|<=C_q=1+3q,
    F_chi(s)=integral_0^infinity e^(-st)f(t)dt, Re s>0.       (16)

The algebra follows from L(s)/s=r/(s-1)+Laplace(b). It is also the exact source already proved in G128. No arbitrary Mobius tail is substituted for a fixed character.

For T>0 let F_T be the integral in (16) through T. On Re s>=sigma0>0,

    |F-F_T|<=C_q e^(-sigma0 T)/sigma0,
    |F'(s)|<=C_q/sigma0^2.                                 (17)

Both follow directly by integrating the full absolute tail or t e^(-sigma0 t). Let a compact rectangle K lie in Re>=sigma0. Cover it with finitely many cells of center z_j and radius at most d_j, with the segment from z_j to each point of its cell lying in K. Suppose certified numerical values v_j obey |v_j-F_T(z_j)|<=epsilon_j. Then the entirely finite test

    |v_j| > epsilon_j+C_q e^(-sigma0 T)/sigma0
                         +(C_q/sigma0^2)d_j    for every j   (18)

proves that F, hence L, has no zeros anywhere in K. This pays source truncation, point evaluation and interpolation, not just the sampled points. The finite integrals can be bounded from the literal character period and its known jumps at log n; interval evaluation supplies the epsilon_j. No efficiency claim is made about the number of terms through e^T.

If F is nonzero on K, its minimum modulus m_K is positive. Refine d_j and epsilon_j to zero and increase T until the three terms in (18) are small compared with m_K. Uniform convergence ensures that this finite certificate eventually succeeds. If K contains a zero, the sound test cannot succeed. This is a semidecision algorithm for the zero-free compact property, not a proof that its inputs satisfy that property.

For one common 0<gamma<1 take the increasing exhaustion

    K_m={gamma+1/m<=Re s<=m+2, |Im s|<=m}, m>=1.

Successful certificates for every K_m exclude every zero in Re>gamma. This is a complete all-height logical bridge, with no interchange of a height supremum and a pointwise limit. The missing input is a theorem that these certificates succeed for **every m** at some gamma<.8748540364. The adaptive procedure alone does not prove termination of all stages; finitely many completed rectangles cannot certify the entire half-plane.

Given an independently established lower margin m_K, a sufficient source cutoff is T>=sigma0^-1 log(8C_q/(sigma0 m_K)), and a sufficient cell radius is <=m_K sigma0^2/(8C_q), with point error <=m_K/8. Then |v_j|>=3m_K/4 while the test's right side is <=3m_K/8. Those budgets identify the unknown margin. They do not conjure it from finite data. A fixed character's finite period determines the entire function; the synthetic finite-prefix pole completions of G118 are therefore not counterexamples within this actual-character class. They only explain why a weaker finite-relaxation argument would be insufficient.

The normalized compact procedure is compatible with G130's obstruction to raw principal finite-polynomial global contraction. It supplies a correct constructive algorithm and error bill at a narrower scope. It is mostly a concrete composition of G128 and elementary compactness, not a new arithmetic estimate. No numerical rectangle was run here because that would not address the unresolved all-m premise or improve c.
title: 4. Uniform wildcard S23: an explicit compact certificate algorithm and its exact limit

statement:
## G149. The full logarithmic Hankel growth criterion

Fix an ordinary Dirichlet character chi, with squareful and ramified zeros
kept literally, and put

    M(x) = sum_(n<=x) mu(n) chi(n),       M(x)=0 for x<1,
    h_a(v) = exp(-a v) M(exp(v)),         v>=0, 0<a<1.

Let Gamma_(a,L) be the full Hankel operator on L2(0,L) with kernel h_a(t+u),
and K_a(L) its operator norm. For complex chi use the bounded bilinear form

    B_a(f,g) = integral integral h_a(t+u) f(t) g(u) dt du.

Conjugating one test input identifies its norm with the usual operator
norm. It does not conjugate chi or replace the arithmetic source by an
absolute value. Both variables and every off-diagonal rectangle are present.

If sup_L K_a(L)<infinity, density extends B_a to L2(0,infinity) twice.
For Re(z)>0 the vector E_z(t)=exp(-zt) is holomorphic with
norm squared 1/(2Re(z)). Consequently Q(z)=B_a(E_z,E_z) is holomorphic,
and initially for s=a+z, Re(s)>1, absolute convergence gives

    Q(z) = integral_0^infinity v M(exp(v)) exp(-s v) dv
         = -d/ds [1/(s L(s,chi))].                         (G149.1)

A zero rho of L with Re(rho)>a would give a pole of the derivative on the
right. Since a>0, rho is not zero; its pole cannot be removed by the factor
s or by differentiation. Meromorphic identity continuation contradicts
the holomorphy of Q. The principal-character pole instead gives a zero of
1/L and causes no false obstruction. The conclusion covers every fixed
finite height and the literal imprimitive L function. Constants may depend
on the fixed character; no growing-conductor or height-uniform growth
estimate has been inferred.

### Every rectangular block is paid

This is the substantive completion of the growth adapter. Write I_j=[j,j+1).
Opposite translations send the I_i by I_j rectangle to the square
[(i+j)/2,(i+j)/2+1) in both coordinates, preserving t+u. Therefore the
unweighted block norm is at most K_a((i+j)/2+1). Passing to a heavier
weight sigma>a multiplies it by at most exp(-(sigma-a)(i+j)). If

    K_a(L) <= C exp(2 eta L),       eta>=0, all L>0,

the sum of the norms of all blocks is bounded by

    C exp(2 eta) [1-exp(-(sigma-a-eta))]^(-2),
    provided sigma>a+eta.                                  (G149.2)

The sum is a deliberately coarse sufficient bound for the full bilinear
form: each block input norm is bounded by the norm of its complete input.
It includes arbitrarily unbalanced rectangles, not only a diagonal strip.
Apply (G149.1) at the heavier weight, taking sigma<1 when needed. Thus for
one fixed 0<a<=gamma<1 the complete hypothesis

    K_a(L) <<_(chi,epsilon) exp(2(gamma-a+epsilon)L)
    for every epsilon>0 and all L>0                         (OPEN-HK)

for every fixed ordinary character excludes all L zeros in Re(s)>gamma.
For any desired sigma>gamma choose epsilon<sigma-gamma first. Values
above one are already in the absolute Euler-product domain; arbitrarily
small positive margins cover the boundary. Alternatively uniformly bounded
Hankel forms for a sequence a decreasing to gamma give the same return.

At a=1/2, the current first-gain threshold for the exponential growth
coefficient is strictly less than .7497080728. The candidate gamma=.87485
would require coefficient .7497 and return c=.12515, a gain .0000040364.
The 1/6 and 1/4 targets require coefficients 2/3 and 1/2. These are
conditional targets. The elementary |M(x)|<=x gives coefficient
2(1-a), namely one at a=1/2, and supplies no gain.

### What can and cannot supply that estimate

The exact Hilbert–Schmidt square is

    integral_0^(2L) w_L(v) exp(-2av) |M(exp(v))|^2 dv,
    w_L(v)=v for v<=L, and 2L-v for L<=v<=2L.

Bounding this positive energy reimports the familiar complete energy
problem. Operator norm can in principle be smaller: the nonarithmetic
kernel exp(i(t+u)^2) has operator norm at most sqrt(pi), by extension and
Plancherel at frequency 2t, whereas its Hilbert–Schmidt norm is L. This
functional example supplies no estimate for mu(n)chi(n).

For the single model kernel R exp(lambda(t+u)), the singular value is
|R| integral_0^L exp(2Re(lambda)t)dt. Critical modes grow linearly and
unstable modes exponentially. This is not a license to decompose or truncate
an infinite arithmetic pole expansion without paying the complement.

The exact arithmetic form also reads

    B_a(f,g) = sum_n mu(n)chi(n)
               integral_(t+u>=log n) exp(-a(t+u))f(t)g(u)dtdu

for compactly supported inputs. Extending h_a by zero to the negative line,

    (partial_v+a) h_a = sum_n mu(n)chi(n)n^(-a) delta_(log n).

The atom at n=1 is retained. On compactly supported smooth inputs in the
positive half-line its pairing with f*g is a B_a(f,g)-B_a(f',g).
This gives an H1 by L2 bound from the Hankel bound, not a converse or a
native H estimate. Credit the broad operator/observability and reciprocal
return ancestry, including [W29](../creative/round29-review.md),
[W50 energy](../[private research revision]/wild50-integration.md) and
[W54 prediction](../[private research revision]/wild54-integration.md). The new credit is the
specific complete source interface and its balanced-block growth return.

Multiplying by conj(z) and taking real parts yields exactly

 int_(-infinity)^infinity e^(-2gamma y)g(log n-y)^2dy=e^(tau gamma^2)*n^(-2gamma)/(2sqrt(pi*tau))

## 4. Quantitative effect and remaining arithmetic

Every retained tuple now has

 de>L, l<n/L<=M/L=X^((3/2)(1-gamma)).                           (21)

At the old high endpoint B(M)=eta X^((5gamma-3)/2), so its old cofactor cap was eta^(-1)X^(3(1-gamma)). The new exponent is half that value. In the balanced case tau=1/2 the inverse floor is X^(gamma/2) throughout, improving the old high-end exponent (5gamma-3)/4 by3(1-gamma)/4. These are proved source restrictions, not new zero-free constants.

For gamma11 the new cofactor exponent is .1877189454; at the illustrative nearer gamma=.8748 it is .1878; at gamma=5/6 it is1/4; at gamma=3/4 it is3/8. The corresponding balanced inverse floors have exponents gamma/2. All targets are retained; none of their core estimates is proved here.

The exact merged coefficient in (18) is

 sum_(ml=n)a(m)b0(l)
   #{ordered(d,e):de=m,d>U,e>V,gcd(d,e)<=G}.                    (22)

It follows from complete multiplicativity a(d)a(e)=a(de), including shared primes and natural zeros. There is no squarefree deletion or Hecke transfer. Full norm cancellation is still needed in this coefficient.

### 4.1 The deliberately coarse complete first-gain test

Take the balanced cuts and gamma>6/7, covering gamma11 and .8748. To test a bounded-coefficient bilinear estimate, first remove the gcd cutoff from the WHOLE finite core using G182, paying X^(gamma+epsilon). Decompose its finite original d,e,l,n ranges dyadically; O(log^4 X) labels suffice. There is no continuum sampling. On a cell n~N>=X, d~D,e~E, DE l~N, relabel the two original colors if needed so D>=E. Both are at least a fixed multiple of X^(gamma/2). Keep the sharp product cutoff N<del<=2N (intersected with the actual M endpoint) and both lower inverse cuts.

For fixed l and x, Cauchy in d leaves the exact signed e-correlation with an inner d sum. For e'=e+h, the difference-phase derivative in d has size

 T h/(DE), T=(N/X)^6,

and is monotone. Its maximum is O(T/D). Since N<=M and gamma>6/7,

 T<=X^(3(1-gamma))=o(X^(gamma/2))<=o(D).

The discrete first-derivative bound therefore gives

 |K_(e,e+h)| <<min(D,DE/(T h)).                               (23)

The d interval is the intersection of the two original product intervals and the fixed dyadic/lower-cut interval, hence one interval or empty. Its endpoints are kept. Summing all h and both orders, and retaining the diagonal, yields

 |sum_(d,e in cell) a(d)a(e)f_x(del)|
  <<DE [E^(-1/2)+T^(-1/2)sqrt(log(2E))],                       (24)

up to harmless bounded-variation partial summation for the actual damping. On these cells n<=M<X^(3/2), the damping and its first needed variations are uniformly bounded. More explicitly it may be kept inside K and the original Cauchy amplitudes; the same Abel bound holds. No estimate for signed Liouville correlations was used in obtaining (24).

Summing |b0(l)| with DE~N/l and all dyadic labels gives the full n~N contribution bounded by

 X^epsilon [N X^(-gamma/4)+X^3/N^2].                          (25)

The first exponent over N<=M is r-gamma/4=3/2-3gamma/4, <=gamma exactly when gamma>=6/7. The second is <=X^gamma only when N>=X^((3-gamma)/2)=M. Thus the coarse test pays the diagonal throughout but fails on the interior transition, returning O(X^(1+epsilon)) when all N>=X are summed. Outputs L<n<X also cost at most X^(1+epsilon) by the actual coefficient bound. The paid gcd complement adds X^(gamma+epsilon). This is a complete failed first-gain calculation, not a claim that an unproved bilinear bound succeeds.

### 4.2 Actual arithmetic repair attempted; precise surviving inequality

Before taking absolute values in (23), Cauchy gives D times a Gram expression with diagonal <=DE and off-diagonal

 B_(l,x)=2 Re sum_(e<e' in cell) a(e)conjugate(a(e'))
          sum_(d in I_e intersect I_e') exp(-i[(del/x)^6-(de'l/x)^6])
                times the actual two damping factors.                      (26)

The natural zeros are retained. Its actual coefficient is lambda(ee')chi(e)conjugate(chi(e')), not an independent sign. The outer eliminated a(d) was bounded only by Cauchy, with no coprimality hypothesis.

A SUFFICIENT stronger arithmetic repair, for EVERY finite-core cell L<n<=M (including the cells with N<X), fixed l and every real x, would be the one-sided bound

 B_(l,x) <= C_epsilon D E^2 X^epsilon (X^gamma/N)^2.             (27)

The diagonal already fits: E is at least a fixed positive multiple of X^(gamma/2), while (N/X^gamma)^2<=X^(3(1-gamma)) up to a fixed cell factor. Then (24) improves to DE X^(gamma+epsilon)/N, and summing the full original labels/cofactors would prove the target X^(gamma+epsilon). Uniformity in those labels, every epsilon and all large shells is essential. This is a concrete sufficient correlation estimate, not asserted to be the weakest one.

 X^(6-2gamma)/N^4=(M/N)^4,                                    (28)

up to logarithms. For L<=N<X, the coarse bound B<<DE^2 misses by (N/L)^2; this low transition is INCLUDED in the open requirement(27), not silently paid by its high-frequency version. # Shared-zero coupling, primitive conductor, and a completed signed target



## 1. Outcome and dependency boundary

The accepted calibration is **c10=.12514596**, source-relative to PR9/Gao. The earlier c11=.1251459636 and the amplitude-conditioned theorem are UNDER REVIEW and are not premises here. This pass does not iterate their kappa bootstrap.

There are two proved source-relative improvements to the organization of OPEN-J:

1. A buffered zero whose **actual primitive conductor** is at most U^(89/100) has a shorter shared plain witness. Using that fact with the original marked inverse theorem gives an explicit weighted-density exponent smaller by at least **W/5000** than the accepted nonlinear G envelope. A sixth-power lift proves the same saving for the complete raw subclass having a high zero of primitive conductor at most Z^((21/25)W), with z<=W/21. All complementary rows retain their old complete bounds. No theorem forces every hard row into this subclass.
2. The completed mollifier tails for different cutoffs have the **same value at the actual common zero**. Their weighted Gram matrix on zero rows is asymptotically rank one. Fixed normalized combinations or products give no new power in their zero signal; an ambient mixed-moment gain remains possible. This is an actual-zero identity, not the preceding scalar saturation construction. Keeping their full signed coefficients instead removes the requirement to select individual inverse/plain witnesses. The complete sixth-power diagonal of the resulting norm is paid explicitly. Its remaining **one-sided signed cross-class sum** is a precise, unrestricted-row replacement for OPEN-J.

The second target has direct conditional returns at c=1/6 and c=1/4 with fixed cutoffs 2 and 3. These returns do not extrapolate the old physical geometry past its limitations. They use the completed detector directly and include the principal-pole correction. The required signed arithmetic bound is **OPEN**. No larger c is established in this report.

F0/analytic ancestry, original positive-slot uniformity, and exact external root-L-function/import/admission bindings stay OPEN. The new elementary identities and contour reductions do not close those dependencies. The source-relative density assertion uses the existing witness and inverse-moment contracts; the higher-ceiling return states its new input explicitly.

## 2. Exact sources and what they permit

The primary PR9 source is pinned at `58344dfdbe756cf2f743da1908ffe0582418cf5b`, local paper SHA256 `2b4c67c3e817d7854ee57e451cea1789c8a4a1d03a72ddb83b980421167096d8`. The Gao source is pinned at `ca182b70ac2aee2d053d679b4ddf1233883f9eef`. Source dates printed in the documents and the current receipt time are distinct. `checks.json` binds the exact inspected bytes and the accepted [restricted research revision]/[restricted research revision] boundaries. Current proof/index are navigation snapshots and can change during root integration.

The actual interfaces read for this pass are:

* PR9 B0.3--5, lines 151--182: centrally normalized inverse M and plain S; MI admits arbitrary bounded row-independent prime coefficients; MP has the restricted canonical pool, relative characters, common slot profile, eligibility and mesh order.
* B0.7--9, lines 197--240: exact sixth-power restoration, natural zeros, injectivity, and the inverse scale/height supremum.
* B0.13--20, lines 242--342: buffered maxima, reciprocal and reflected plain bounds, common-zero product witness, and cutoffs fixed before row witnesses. B0.19 retains the full signed Mobius convolution before dyadic selection.
* B3.3--8 and B3.31--41: common-profile separation before live indices, actual-ratio tails, precise coefficient families, and full mask removal. B3.6 expressly permits no arbitrary extra coefficient on its canonical column. Thus a divisor convolution cannot be inserted into UM merely because its coefficients are divisor bounded.
* The actual SupportedWitness, SimultaneousSupport and WitnessRows files retained in the formalizer packet: one label, one zero, one real part and one common witness frequency; r+m>=t up to the prescribed tolerance. These are source inspections only; no formal tool was run or new kernel assertion made.
* Accepted `[restricted mathematical source]`: the exact canonical anchor/mask bridge and nonlinear G. Accepted `[restricted provenance path] research revision]-drafts/valuation-review/report.md`: complete c10 source/return, Hval, old complementary branches and their admission boundary.

Fix one original parent translate and finite dictionary. Slot supports, canonical ray quotient, relative characters, original profile and natural zero extensions stay fixed. Whole conjugation, when needed, conjugates every fixed/live factor and reflects the zero height; it does not conjugate only the fixed label. A witness label is re-anchored by the accepted [restricted research revision] identity using the same original pool and quotient. No new arbitrary-mask MP is asserted.

Let U=Z^W, v=z/W<=1/20 and delta in [17/25,7/10]. The physical bin supplies the pointwise upper bound U^(delta v+small) for the squared product of any original slot subcollection, with its polynomial height factor. The larger internal witness box can have a larger maximum. Its witness bounds may be weakened to the physical delta; that internal maximum is not used as a replacement upper slot price. All statements below have an arbitrary final epsilon and a finite factor (1+T)^J. Constants and thresholds may depend on the subsequently fixed dictionary and profiles. No conductor-uniform constant is claimed.

Write the accepted free/raw density exponent as

    Eold(delta;W,z)=rho(delta)W+delta z-G_delta(W,z),
    rho=1-10delta/[3(5-2delta)],  k=rho+delta-1,
    G_delta(W,z)=min(3kz, a_delta W+b_delta z),
    a_delta=2delta(5-6delta)^2/[3(5-2delta)(115-54delta)],
    b_delta=14delta(5-6delta)/(115-54delta).                 (J1)

This is the accepted K=9/2 envelope. No pending smaller-kappa input enters J1 or the following argument.

## 3. What the primitive conductor tells the shared witness

Suppose the witnessing nonprincipal presentation has primitive conductor norm Q<=U^lambda. Its additional Euler holes have polynomial radical norm, and its fixed conductor factors are absorbed in the preallocated small width loss. In the buffered zero-free region, the primitive L-function has the same positive-real zeros as the presentation. Its upper-line bound is the same B0.14 bound after restoring/deleting the Euler factors.

The primitive functional equation on the reflected line gives

    |S(U^m)|^2 << U^[delta min(m,lambda-m)+small] (1+T)^J. (J2)

Here is the conductor and hole calculation. On Re s=a+small the centrally normalized Mellin integral contributes N^(a-1/2+small). On Re s=1-a-small the functional equation contributes Q^(a-1/2+small), and central normalization contributes N^(1/2-a-small). Squaring produces respectively delta m and delta(lambda-m). The original removed Euler factors are evaluated on a fixed positive half-plane, since a stays in a compact subset below one. Their products cost at most U^epsilon uniformly for polynomial radical norm. They do not replace Q by the displayed modulus or by Q times the radical. All independent heights remain in the finite smooth orders. At larger analysis heights the usual polynomial factors are retained.

This is a statement about the **primitive conductor of the actual complete character**, including its fixed label and moving factors. Phase cancellation is not permission to reduce the presented width elsewhere. A fixed puncture changes the zeros of the presentation at Re s=0 but does not change this primitive conductor or the positive-real zero. A moving twist can change Q and must be measured again.

The original common product lower bound and inverse upper bound imply

    r<=t+small, r+m>=t-small,
    m<=lambda/2+small,
    |M(U^r)|^2 >= U^(delta r-small).                       (J3)

Indeed if m>lambda/2, J2 and B0.20 give
delta(r+m)<=delta r+delta(lambda-m)+small, hence
2m<=lambda+small/delta. The lower bound delta>=.68 pays the denominator. If the internal bin has a larger delta', first perform this comparison at delta', then weaken the inverse lower bound to the physical delta. This preserves the smaller m cap. There is no probabilistic independence or second label count.

The cutoff is fixed in the conductor class before witnesses. One may select a low-conductor witnessing label because the label set is already finite; fix that label before applying a moment and sum the finite label bounds. Membership in the positive high-row subset is not inserted into a Poisson identity. Principal inducing characters are excluded from this contour argument. Their pre-existing fixed/finite source branches remain separate.

## 4. A uniform strictly better density for a concrete class

Set lambda0=89/100. Consider the free high rows for which at least one actual buffered high zero has a witnessing primitive conductor Q<=U^lambda0. Define, before witnesses,

    t=1+(3delta/5)(lambda0-2v),
    r0=t-lambda0/2,
    Ac(delta)=1-delta+lambda0 delta(1/2-3delta/5),
    Ec(delta;W,z)=Ac(delta)W+(6delta^2/5)z.                (J4)

On the whole rectangle delta in [.68,.70], v in [0,.05],

    1<t<3/2, r0>1/2,
    1-2v-r0>=33/2500>1/100.                              (J5)

The supported inverse length obeys r>=r0 up to the small budget. For r<=1, choose an original slot subcollection of width just below
min(v,(1-r)/2). The choice depends on frozen lengths and witness dyads, not the live row. The existing fine mesh loses at most one slot width. The second MI inequality has a fixed reserve because r>=1/2 and v<=1/20. Dividing the inverse witness, applying MI to the marked subset and paying the remaining actual slots pointwise gives

    I(r)=1-delta r+delta[v-(1-r)/2]_+,   r<=1.            (J6)

Both pieces decrease with r. By J5, I(r0)=1-delta r0. This elementary use of MI is derived here; it does not import the preceding pending amplitude-conditioned theorem. It needs no conditioned amplitude grade and no marked-plain theorem.

For r>=1, the old unmarked sixth-power inverse amplification and the full slot pointwise price give

    L(r)=1/6+(5/6-delta)r+delta v.

This increases with r and is at most L(t). The cutoff J4 satisfies the exact balance

    1-delta r0=L(t)=Ec(delta;1,v).                        (J7)

Thus every inverse-length regime is covered. The witness dyad union, separate rowwise heights/real powers and all required derivative profiles are covered by the source scale/Sobolev supremum. No improved moment is called on a descendant. The resulting actual free-row estimate is

    sum_(high,eligible,free; low-conductor zero) |Q_u|^2
       << Z^[Ec(delta;W,z)+epsilon] (1+T)^J.              (J8)

It is a strict improvement on the accepted weighted density:

    Ec(delta;W,z) <= Eold(delta;W,z)-W/5000.              (J9)

For a transparent exact certificate, Eold is the maximum of
rho W+(delta-3k)z and (rho-a_delta)W+(delta-b_delta)z.
It suffices to subtract Ec+W/5000 from the SECOND expression. Clear the positive denominator 3(5-2delta)(115-54delta). `check.py` constructs that polynomial directly from J1 and J4 and gives all positive rational Bernstein coefficients on the entire two-dimensional box. It also certifies the cutoff/capacity/root-decay gates and the two exact J7 identities. There are seven positive polynomial certificates, 35 coefficients and twelve exact illustrative values. The examples are not the continuum proof.

The primitive conductor information is substantive. It can occur with c_s=d_s=b2=rbar=0: for example, a dual free row with a prime of valuation two has a primitive conductor contribution of one prime norm but row norm contribution of its square. This describes legal geometry, not the existence of a high zero. It is distinct from Hval's common-support gain. Conversely a squarefree natural row can have Q comparable to its full norm. Empty common support alone does not force J8.

## 5. Full raw subclass and the priced complement

For raw width W and z<=W/21, define the subclass by the existence of a high buffered zero of primitive conductor

    Q <= Z^((21/25)W).                                   (J10)

Write the actual row w=u b^6 with u free and the original unit retained. Freeze b before the free-core sum. All added holes remain in the ACTUAL slots. Construct witnesses with the conductor-bounded natural free-core presentation (and the fixed dictionary puncture), whose positive-real zero and primitive conductor agree with the raw presentation. Do not insert the potentially large b-radical into the witness modulus and then claim a V-scale modulus bound. The extra slot mask is a fixed row-independent prime coefficient, permitted by MI; the accepted slot-only deletion identity also retains it. Thus no actual slot is replaced by its unpunctured version. Set s=log_Z Nb and V=W-6s.

On V>=20W/21, z<=V/20 and

    (89/100)V-(21/25)W >= (4/525)W.

Hence J10 implies the free hypothesis with its fixed positive padding. J8 gives Ec(V,z). Counting b costs Z^s, while

    s+Ec(V,z)=Ec(W,z)-(6Ac-1)s,

and 6Ac-1 is uniformly positive. The dyadic root sum converges at its original W-scale exponent. Natural holes are handled at their actual fixed root before the free norm; no unpunctured coefficient is substituted. The norm uses the MI arbitrary-coefficient permission together with the original physical pointwise price. It does not require transporting a conditioned amplitude class through a signed deletion.

For V<20W/21 use the old raw/free unmarked high-bin count and the original slot pointwise price. Its exponent is at most

    rho W+delta z-(6rho-1)s,

with s>W/126. Since G<=3kz<=kW/7, a uniform reserve after paying the W/5000 saving is

    [(19/54-1/6-3k(.68))/21]-1/5000
      =112003/257985000 >0.                             (J11)

Bounded free windows and fixed-inducing free cores retain the old finite-core count and their applicable high-bin pointwise slot bound; their exponent W/6+delta z fits this larger tail reserve. A principal or artificial source branch not possessing that bin bound is not reclassified as J10: its original physical estimate is retained. Thus the stated raw **high-bin** subclass, with the same pointwise hypotheses as the accepted G input, satisfies

    sum_(J10,raw high eligible rows) |Q_w|^2
       << Z^[Eold(delta;W,z)-W/5000+epsilon] (1+T)^J.     (J12)

The complement is explicitly the high rows with no such low-conductor witnessing zero. The old complete Eold bound pays that complement. This is a partition with a genuine stronger estimate on one piece, not a uniform strengthening of Eold on their union.

For the physical application, a row condition can be imposed only on the actual positive child norm after the full first reconstruction, fixed missing radical, second signed projector, clipped rectangle recovery and existing Cauchy normalization. One must test J10 on the complete primitive character of that norm. Its definition cannot be attached to an earlier abstract row and assumed to survive conjugation of only one factor, moving character multiplication, or a changed puncture presentation. Whole-character conjugation preserves Q. Fixed added holes preserve primitive Q. Other changes require their actual character calculation.

If a complete paired term has both positive factors in the licensed subclass, their Cauchy average retains the saving at the corresponding actual widths; if only one factor is so restricted, only half its exponent saving is available. The original joint label measure is extracted once, never again for this restriction. A signed projector is not assumed to preserve a positive amplitude/row class. If a sector cannot be separated in this way, discard this new gain and use the full accepted bound. This supplies no assertion that every physical paired term gains W/5000.

All low and far-high bins, first/second zero, extracted errors, fixed-inducing physical K_phys^(5/6), actual 6a/9a radii, shortage and no-slot complements, weighted Euler shifts including zero capacity, four independent profiles, negative nonempty windows, principal residue and supremum feedback therefore remain exactly the accepted c10 argument. No exceptional centered M/24 reserve is spent. Since the complementary large-conductor class is still binding, no c11 or other endpoint is inferred from J12. All-height thresholds follow the old order: fixed loss and finite mesh, then dictionary/profiles and smooth orders, then the small internal height exponent, final tail order and eventual scale. Above that polynomial height range use the original absolute bound with a larger polynomial factor.

## 6. The actual common-zero identity before witness selection

The higher-ceiling exploration starts from the exact B0.19 source rather than its chosen dyadic pair. Let phi be any fixed nonprincipal presentation, with its original zero extension and S-omission. Choose a smooth V, one on [0,1] and zero on [2,infinity). For fixed t>0 put R=U^t and

    C_R(s)=sum_d mu(d) phi(d) V(Nd/R)(Nd)^(-s),
    A_R(n)=sum_(d|n) mu(d)V(Nd/R).                        (J13)

All ideals in this formula avoid the same fixed S. Multiplicativity includes nonunit zeros; no coprimality division is made. Hence

    L^S(s,phi) C_R(s)=sum_n phi(n) A_R(n)(Nn)^(-s)

on its absolute half-plane. The coefficient at the unit is one, and A_R(n)=0 for 1<Nn<=R. This is a statement about the full signed divisor sum. Its individual dyadic inverse/plain pieces need not vanish.

Choose Y=U^B with B fixed sufficiently large, and define the completed tail

    D_R(s)=sum_(Nn>R) phi(n) A_R(n)(Nn)^(-s)exp(-Nn/Y). (J14)

For any prescribed A>0 and t in a fixed bounded positive range, B can be fixed so that at every retained actual zero rho with Re rho in a compact subinterval of (1/2,1),

    D_R(rho)=-1+O(U^(-A)).                              (J15)

The error is uniform in the source polynomial conductor/mask ranges and sufficiently small polynomial height range; outside it a polynomial height factor is retained. Indeed Mellin inversion gives the integral of
Y^z Gamma(z)L^S(rho+z,phi)C_R(rho+z). Shift from Re z=2 to -1/4. There is no nonprincipal pole, and the Gamma residue at zero is L^S(rho,phi)C_R(rho)=0. On that fixed strip the L-function and finite C_R have a fixed polynomial conductor/height/scale bound. The remainder is Y^(-1/4) times that polynomial. Choose B after its raw power and before tail orders. The unit is exp(-1/Y)=1+O(U^(-B)); increasing B pays both errors. Natural Euler holes on this positive strip cost a small power. The exponential permits truncation at Nn<=U^(B+1), with error smaller than every fixed negative power, including every required fixed derivative.

For t in [1,3/2], this is the precise completion behind B0.19. The identity itself permits ANY fixed bounded t; the interval restriction comes from the subsequent individual witness/moment strategy, not the contour identity. Thus t=2 or 3 below is a new detector input, not an illegal application of Lemma 1W at those cutoffs.

Fix any finite list t_1,...,t_h BEFORE rows and zeros, and use the same selected zero and character for all cutoffs. On a high-row set with nonnegative weights w_u, put M=sum_u w_u. J15 gives

    sum_u w_u D_j(rho_u) conjugate(D_k(rho_u))
       =M+O(U^(-A)M),
    sum_u w_u |sum_j c_j D_j(rho_u)|^2
       =|sum_j c_j|^2 M+O(U^(-A)||c||_1^2 M).            (J16)

The finite coefficient vector is row independent and has fixed bounded mass. The same identities hold with w_u the actual squared slot product and retained diagonal contractions. This is exact shared-zero coherence of completed tests. An average with sum c_j=1 preserves the full signal, while a difference with sum c_j=0 annihilates it. A product of finitely many completed tests likewise has its prescribed constant signal. Combining these cutoffs gives no additional power of U in that signal. J16 alone makes NO independence/dependence claim for a probability law on the unrestricted rows.

This does not prove that selected dyadic witnesses coincide for different cutoffs, or that every witness pair is correlated with every slot amplitude. It does not forbid a mixed moment or signed cross-scale cancellation on the UNRESTRICTED row family. It redirects the proposed all-cutoff strategy: any counting gain needs a new ambient mixed estimate; it cannot be obtained by crediting an extra power to the zero signal. This is an actual source-level restriction on signal extraction, not an impossibility theorem for joint zero density.

## 7. A complete signed norm that replaces the witness prerequisite

Fix t, B and the finite terminal cutoff as above. For each original natural row and fixed dictionary label, use D_R(s) and multiply by the actual slot product. After a whole conjugation if needed, the row character orientation is common. Re-anchor the fixed slot coefficients using the existing exact dictionary identity. Then the finite expression is literally

    D_R(s) Q_u = sum_l b_l(s) psi_u(l),
    b_l(s)=U^(-v/2) sum_(nP=l) A_R(n) nu(n)(Nn)^(-s)
                      exp(-Nn/Y) alpha(P).              (J17)

Here P is the product of one prime from each ORIGINAL disjoint slot pool, alpha retains every individual fixed ray coefficient, smooth weight, norm power and independent slot height, and Nn>R. Every fixed puncture and natural character zero stays in the summand. The displayed expression uses ideal products, so different tuples with the same ideal l are merged WITH their signs before taking a norm. The coefficient b_l is independent of the live row; its common real part/height parameter is not chosen separately for each coefficient. The finite label and whole-conjugation union has only its original fixed cost.

Take a fixed two-variable Sobolev norm in s on the required real/height rectangle to dominate evaluation at each row's selected zero. Its derivatives introduce only powers of log Nn and bounded polynomials in the height; since Nn<=U^(B+1), they are absorbed in epsilon and the finite height factor. Slot heights stay independent of s. Denote the resulting positive complete row norm by N_t(U). It has no zero-event restriction on its summation; the exact original natural/eligible row range, or the explicitly enlarged range in Section 9, is part of its definition.

J15 and this Sobolev evaluation give a genuine sufficient density input:

    N_t(U) << U^(Eold(delta;1,v)-xi+epsilon)(1+T)^J
      => weighted high-row mass has the same bound.     (J18)

This is an explicit coefficient norm, not a restatement of a count of zeros. It removes the need to choose inverse/plain witnesses, their intersection event and their length cutoff. It is also NOT supplied by UM, MI, MP or the canonical energy theorem: b_l contains the full signed divisor convolution A_R, which is outside those coefficient contracts. Triangle-expanding its divisor factors loses precisely the correlation being sought. No moving coefficient is hidden in a profile seminorm.

## 8. The complete sixth-power diagonal is already paid

The relevant diagonal is not merely l=l'. Write l=c a^6 with c sixth-power-free. Distinct roots a,b have the same sextic row phase away from their natural zeros. Omitting these pairs would leave a large unpriced stationary sector. We include EVERY pair whose sixth-power-free ideal part c agrees, keep its fixed-character phases and zero masks, and bound this whole sector absolutely.

For sigma in a compact subset of (1/2,1), fixed t and slot count, divisor counting in J17 gives

    |b_l(s)| << U^((sigma-1/2)v+epsilon) (Nl)^(-sigma),
    b_l=0 unless Nl >= c_0 U^(t+v).                     (J19)

The fixed positive c_0 depends only on annular endpoints. Each tuple P|l has divisor-many possibilities because the pools are disjoint and finite in number. A_R(n) is divisor bounded; no averaging cancellation is used in J19. Independent height derivatives only change its finite seminorm factor. Fixed extra holes restrict the support. The exponential can be bounded by one, and its tail is already paid.

The following elementary ideal estimate supplies the entire root sum. For H>=2 and sigma>1/2,

    sum_(c sixth-free) [sum_(a: Nc Na^6>=H)
                         (Nc Na^6)^(-sigma)]^2
       << H^(1-2sigma+epsilon).                        (J20)

For Nc>H, the inner root sum is at most a constant times (Nc)^(-sigma), since 6sigma>1. Summing its square costs H^(1-2sigma). For Nc<=H, ideal counting gives the root tail
(H/Nc)^(1/6-sigma); the inner sum is at most
H^(1/6-sigma)(Nc)^(-1/6). Its square summed over c<=H costs
H^(1/3-2sigma) H^(2/3)=H^(1-2sigma). Divisor factors are absorbed by a small decrease in sigma, uniformly on the compact range. No squarefree-density assumption is used. Six units or fixed ray classes change constants only.

The row count is U^(1+epsilon). Natural zeros may differ between ca^6 and cb^6 but are contractions; they are not canceled. Combining J19--20 with H comparable to U^(t+v) pays the entire sixth-power diagonal of the squared norm by

    D6_t(U) << U^[1-(2sigma-1)t+epsilon](1+T)^J.         (J21)

The slot power cancels exactly:
(2sigma-1)v+(1-2sigma)(t+v)=-(2sigma-1)t.
This includes collisions nP=n'P', unequal sixth-power roots, fixed ray phases and zero powers. It does not assert that the remaining kernel is oscillatory in every restricted source state; any additional fixed-inducing coincidence remains in the next target.

Expand the complete squared Sobolev norm and split it into this same-c sector and the complement. Call the complement O6_t(U); it is the REAL signed sum of all ordered cross-class terms, or twice the real part of one ordering. Keep the exact row kernel, eligibility, zero masks and each inner product of derivative coefficients. Then

    N_t(U)=D6_t(U)+O6_t(U).                              (J22)

D6_t denotes the actual within-class contribution, not its positive majorant; J21 bounds its absolute value. The only missing input is a ONE-SIDED upper bound on O6_t, with no absolute value on each pair. The complete row norm itself is nonnegative. Replacing O6_t by a sum of absolute cross terms is a stronger and unnecessary requirement.

At t=4/3 and delta in [.68,.70], the diagonal exponent is at most 7/75. The old density exponent is at least rho>=19/54. Therefore its gap is at least

    19/54-7/75=349/1350.

Thus, for ANY fixed 0<xi<=1/4, the explicit open estimate

    O6_(4/3)(U) << U^[Eold(delta;1,v)-xi+epsilon](1+T)^J (OPEN-C)

would imply J18. Even at xi=1/4 the diagonal reserve is 23/2700. A much smaller positive xi is a sufficient first-gain input. This is a ceiling for a potential DENSITY saving, not a claimed zero-free constant c=1/4 or an estimated off-diagonal sum. It is not bounded in this report. The old positive moments do not imply it.

## 9. Higher-ceiling direct returns, including the principal pole

There is a separate direct route that does not use Gao's physical geometry. Take z=0 and enlarge the positive norm to ALL natural nonprincipal rows q_u<=U, explicitly including fixed-inducing rows and the unit row. For a fixed target eta, the unit row is its fixed character, with the original finite Euler deletions. This enlargement is part of the NEW arithmetic hypothesis; the old eligible positive-slot theorem does not provide it.

Suppose the exact cross-class sum for this completed detector and its finite Sobolev derivatives satisfies, for every fixed target/dictionary and every epsilon>0,

    O6_t(U) <= C_epsilon,T U^(-nu+epsilon),  nu>0,       (OPEN-H)

on a fixed real rectangle containing a proposed zero, with sigma>=a>1/2. Assume delta_a t=(2a-1)t>1. The diagonal J21 is then a negative power. Choose epsilon less than both gaps. The complete norm tends to zero, so its unit-row value tends to zero. But at an actual nonprincipal zero rho, J15 gives D_R(rho)->-1. This is a contradiction. Constants and thresholds can depend on the fixed target and its bounded height rectangle; no uniform conductor constant or attained family supremum is needed. If the hypothesis holds for every fixed family at the same a, the zero-free boundary a is common.

Concrete permitted pairs are:

| Conditional target | a | t | diagonal exponent 1-(2a-1)t |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| any first improvement near c10 | 1-c with c just above .12514596 | 2 | 4c-1<0 |
| c=1/6 | 5/6 | 2 | -1/3 |
| c=1/4 | 3/4 | 3 | -1/2 |

The input OPEN-H, not the arithmetic table, is the unproved step. These cutoffs are legal for the completed identity; they are not calls to the supported-witness theorem outside [1,3/2]. They bypass the old ell<1/5 and ell<x<=y bottlenecks by changing the detector before that physical return.

For the principal-target version, OPEN-H must apply to ALL natural rows INCLUDING the principal unit row; the nonprincipal-only norm would omit the target. Use the following pole-neutralized kernel on that enlarged family. The unmodified contour WOULD cross the L-function pole at z=1-rho. Its residue cannot be discarded. Insert the factor (s+z-1) into the Mellin integral, and use the exact tail

    D_R^P(s)=sum_(Nn>R) phi(n)A_R(n)(Nn)^(-s)
                          [s-1+Nn/Y]exp(-Nn/Y).        (J23)

The factor cancels the simple principal pole. At a nontrivial zero rho the Gamma residue still vanishes, and the unit term tends to rho-1. Consequently

    D_R^P(rho)=1-rho+O(U^(-A)).                         (J24)

Its signal is nonzero for every fixed rho!=1. The added kernel and all its fixed derivatives satisfy the same coefficient/diagonal bounds with a polynomial height constant: x exp(-x) is bounded, and exponential tails remain rapid. OPEN-H for this modified principal detector therefore gives the same conditional zero exclusion, with the pole at one explicitly allowed. Do not use J23 for nonprincipal s=1: the unmodified J14 has signal -1 there and is the correct test. The ordinary known right-boundary/pole treatment and the exact Hecke-to-ordinary Euler-factor lift remain the accepted source transfer. The imprimitive deleted factors have no zeros in Re s>0 and are retained throughout. No new Hecke scope or external root-definition identification is inferred.

This direct argument has no circular beta_* choice and no physical Euler-shift or reflected-annulus prerequisite. It asks instead for a much stronger signed arithmetic estimate INCLUDING fixed rows. Merely excluding those rows would remove the target unit row and invalidate the return. This is the strongest obstruction to treating OPEN-H as an already supplied average bound.

## 10. Status and review

No c increase is proved. J12 pays a concrete small-conductor subclass; the near-full-conductor complement retains its old bound. OPEN-C and OPEN-H remain unproved signed arithmetic estimates. The exact helper supplies seven positive polynomial certificates and35 Bernstein coefficients, not a proof of either open estimate. See `review-notes.md` for the preserved failed shortcuts, verification scope and attribution. All final artifacts require full readback/hash, own claim release and independent review before integration.

Credit remains with OpenAI, Hailey Collet, Akash Levy, Zhongpai Gao with AI assistance and the accepted source/review authors. No literature-priority, kernel, admission or public-record claim is made.

Let \(\mathcal E\) be the union of (PH5) and (PH16), always with \(R>1\). Combining their absolute estimates with the paid coherent discrepancy and PC11 gives, for the original small-true-gcd covariance,
\[
\boxed{
\mathcal C_<
=\mathcal C_{<,\,(\lambda,\mu)\notin\mathcal E,\ R>1}
+O_\epsilon\!\left(Z^\epsilon Y^{-1}P_a^{1/6}\right).
}
\tag{PH30}
\]
More explicitly the surviving nonzero-relative-conductor pairs satisfy both
\[
R^{9/4}>QYF,\qquad R^3>P_aF^5,
\tag{PH31}
\]
and, if \(\mathfrak p_{\mathrm{coh}}=1\), also
\[
R^{3/2}>(QY)^{2/3}F,\qquad R>P_a^{1/3}F^2.
\tag{PH32}
\]
The remaining arithmetic obligation is to bound this **actual signed** residual by \(Z^\epsilon Y^{-1}P_a^{1/6}\), retaining all original phases, marks, embeddings, profiles and heights. No estimate for it is asserted here.

In particular, all squarefree outer pairs have \(F=1\) and \(\mathfrak p_{\mathrm{coh}}=1\). Their high-\(R\) portion remains. In the unembedded main completed range one may take \(n=n'=1\), disjoint squarefree marked cores \(c,c'\asymp ZL\), and squarefree source columns \(a,b\asymp Y\) coprime to them. Then the true core gcd is one and
\[
R\asymp Y^2(ZL)^2,\qquad F=1.
\tag{PH33}
\]
These are surviving configurations of the actual coefficient support. They identify the remaining problem without replacing the field by arbitrary vectors. The exponent-three embedding exception can likewise leave \(F=1\), so an outer-power cutoff alone would misclassify that residual.

Independent review should focus on: the all-prime divisor identity (PH3) and the exponent-three exception; use of the accepted weighted mass at a strictly buffered exponent; the restricted exponent-zero mass (PH14), where principal powers at conductor primes are retained; exact physical normalization in (PH11); conductor-dyad summation under the curved restrictions; and the individual-mass versus linear-functional distinction in (PH25)-(PH28). A supplemental finite support check used \(q=7\), outer exponents \(0\le\alpha,\beta\le18\), the three embedding pairs \((s,t)=(0,0),(1,0),(0,1)\), and column exponents from zero through seven, with the original column zeros imposed. All 577 surviving configurations had minimum row valuation exactly \(\kappa_p\); all 460 with nonzero relative exponent had one exact row valuation. The 28 surviving column/embedding exponent-three configurations had \(\kappa_p=0\). The check uses the exact local valuation formulas and supplies a consistency check, not a substitute for Section 2's argument.
