# W54: a character-source prediction certificate, with its exact unpaid limit

Status: author research, not root acceptance. No larger zero-free constant is proved. Three related developments combine R11 (control realization), X26 (highest-reach polynomial architecture), and the protected wildcard X28 (interpolation debt). Their useful output is a completely specified sufficient criterion using the ordinary character's bounded summatory staircase, an elementary causal realization, finite positive Gram matrices, and a paid full tail. The missing statement is convergence of a particular prediction error to zero. Positivity, stable polynomial roots, finite interpolation, and finite computations do not establish that convergence.

The other three selected cards have precise duplicate obstructions: R16 continuation-state compression, F04 sharp-prefix holonomy, and X30 weighted topology. These do not retire their broader signed alternatives. All 30 original cards remain in `seeds.json`; the 24 not selected for first tests remain untested. No original family or child is deleted or relabeled.

## 1. Frozen scope, chronology, and calibration

The independently generated seeds use the frozen c10=.12514596, theta10=.87485404 premise. The immutable recipe and prefix hashes are recorded in those seeds. The entire 22,138-byte seed file was read back and hashed before history intake; its SHA-256 is `1e7231eb76b25a6c9d92ed25d2ae9f7c7fa5d1fa640b1e33470899bcd01dc191`. A seed-only receipt went to root for critic preparation. No critic wake was sent then.

Reservations were R11 strongest bridge, X26 highest plausible reach, X30 most different. All 30 cards passed the light coherence screen; related cards were retained rather than quietly excluded. Each strict threshold used its literal fraction across ALL groups. The ordered p<.10 pool contained 22 cards, the next p<.01 pool 12, and the remaining wildcard pool 25. The selected zero-based indices were 9,0,23, yielding R16,F04,X28. The latter two are respectively a free-group rare card and a group-six wildcard. There were no rerolls.

Each complete conditional pool was saved, fully read, and hashed before its own entropy. Before the second draw, the initial seed-replay plan was prospectively corrected to fresh per-stage OS entropy, so even later conditional pools preceded their entropy. The original entropy description and completed first draw remain unchanged; `entropy-2.json` and `entropy-3.json` record this correction. All seeds, pools, entropy and draw files are immutable receipts. `draw.py` is the final executed procedure, not a claim that the initial plan was identical.

Append-only calibration received from root during development: c11=312864909/2500000000=.1251459636 is now root accepted relative to the SAME PR9/Gao source contracts, with theta11=.8748540364. The source is `[restricted provenance path] mathematical source]`. New first-gain comparisons therefore use gamma<.8748540364. The frozen seeds and draws have not changed. F0/analytic ancestry, original positive-slot uniformity and external definition/binding/admission obligations remain open. This calibration supplies no arithmetic estimate below theta11.

 This report claims no cache result.

## 2. D1 / R11: an actual ordinary-character source and exact realization

Fix one ordinary Dirichlet character chi modulo q, with its natural zero values. Put delta=1 for the principal character and 0 otherwise, r=delta*phi(q)/q, and

    A(x)=sum_(n<=x) chi(n),
    b(t)=A(exp(t))-r exp(t),  t>=0.

Periodicity gives |b(t)|<=q. No Mobius cancellation is used. For Re(s)>1, summation by parts gives

    H(s)=integral_0^infinity b(t) exp(-s t) dt
        =L(s,chi)/s-r/(s-1).                           (1)

The integral continues H holomorphically to Re(s)>0 because b is bounded. Define the pole-normalized source

    F_chi(s)=((s-1)/(s+1))^delta L(s,chi)/s.            (2)

For nonprincipal chi this is L/s. For principal chi the apparent singularity at 1 is removable, with F_chi(1)=r/2 !=0. On Re(s)>0, s and s+1 do not vanish; (2) has exactly the natural L zeros in that half-plane, with multiplicity. No artificial zero at 1 is added for nonprincipal characters.

Its literal causal inverse-Laplace source is

    f(t)=b(t)                                  if delta=0,
    f(t)=r exp(-t)+b(t)-2 integral_0^t exp(-(t-u))b(u)du
                                               if delta=1.       (3)

Indeed for delta=1, F=r/(s+1)+(s-1)H/(s+1). Thus F=Laplace(f) on Re(s)>0. In both cases |f(t)|<=C_q:=1+3q. The n=1 contribution is included in A; values at the isolated log(n) jumps do not affect these integrals. All imprimitive Euler factors remain in L. This is an ordinary-character construction; no number-field or changing-conductor transfer is asserted.

For principal chi, cancellation of the r terms in (3) gives the particularly concrete identity, with x=exp(t),

    f(log x)=(2/x)sum_(n<=x) n chi(n)-A(x).            (3a)

It follows from integral_1^x A(v)dv=sum_(n<=x)chi(n)(x-n). At q=1 and m=floor(x), this is m(m+1-x)/x, hence 0<=f<=1 at every x>=1. The zeta source is therefore a positive bounded staircase; one may replace C_q by 1 in its tail bounds. Positivity alone cannot establish the desired complex zero exclusion: the positive bounded source exp(-bt)+C exp(-b(t-T))1_(t>=T), with b>0,C>1, has transform (1+C exp(-sT))/(s+b) and zeros on Re(s)=log(C)/T>0. This toy only defeats a positivity-only inference; it says nothing adverse about the additional arithmetic structure in (3a).

Fix 0<gamma<1 and a=2-gamma, so a>gamma and the safe anchor is s0=gamma+a=2. Set

    s(z)=gamma+a(1+z)/(1-z),
    z(s)=(s-gamma-a)/(s-gamma+a),
    F(z)=F_chi(s(z)), F0=F(0)=F_chi(2) !=0.           (4)

The Euler product in Re(s)>1 proves F0!=0. The bound |F_chi(s)|<=C_q/Re(s) puts F in H-infinity of the disk, hence H2. Define, on L2(0,infinity),

    f_gamma(t)=exp(-gamma t)f(t),
    h(t)=sqrt(2a) integral_0^t exp(-a(t-u))f_gamma(u)du,
    Qv(t)=v(t)-2a integral_0^t exp(-a(t-u))v(u)du,
    ell0(t)=sqrt(2a)exp(-a t).                         (5)

Q is an isometry: after zero extension its Fourier multiplier is
(it-a)/(it+a), of modulus one. Q*ell0=0 by direct integration and ||ell0||=1. For any polynomial p, Laplace transformation of p(Q)h gives

    sqrt(2a)/(w+a) * p((w-a)/(w+a)) * F_chi(gamma+w).

The circle change of variable t=a cot(theta/2), followed by Fourier Plancherel, proves the exact identities

    ||p(Q)h||_L2^2 = ||p F||_H2^2,
    ||p(Q)h-F0 ell0||_L2^2 = ||p F-F0||_H2^2.         (6)

The factor is exact: dtheta/(2pi)=a dt/[pi(a^2+t^2)] in absolute orientation, and the Fourier Plancherel convention is ||v||_2^2=(1/(2pi))integral|vhat(t)|^2dt. Also <h,ell0>=F0 under the inner product linear in the first entry. These give a literal source, state update and positive output; no guessed finite-dimensional realization is substituted.

**First decisive control test.** A bounded positive metric mI<=P<=MI cannot make Q*PQ<=kappa P for any kappa<1: iteration would give m||v||^2<=kappa^n M||v||^2 while ||Q^n v||=||v||. Thus an equivalent-norm contraction of the complete state is impossible. This is not an obstruction to source-specific signed combinations p(Q)h. Their relevant information is the actual correlations <Q^j h,Q^k h>, not the unrestricted norm of Q. It refines the old source-versus-multiplier distinction with a fully formed ordinary-character source; it supplies no contraction estimate.

## 3. D2 / X26: finite prediction gap with a full zero bridge

For each integer N>=0 define

    d_N = min_(deg p<=N,p(0)=1) ||p F||_H2^2,
    Delta_N=d_N-|F0|^2.                               (7)

The constant coefficient of pF is F0. Orthogonality of Taylor coefficients therefore gives exactly

    Delta_N=min_(p(0)=1,deg p<=N)||pF-F0||_H2^2>=0.    (8)

The minimum exists uniquely. The Gram matrix G_N is strictly positive because a nonzero polynomial times the nonzero analytic F cannot vanish identically. To make conjugations unambiguous, set

    (G_N)_(j,k)=integral over the circle conjugate(z^j F) z^k F dtheta/(2pi),
    0<=j,k<=N.

Then ||pF||^2=p*G_N p and

    d_N=1/(G_N^(-1))_(0,0).                           (9)

It is Toeplitz. Formula (6) also gives its entries as integral_0^infinity conjugate(Q^j h) Q^k h dt. There is no unsigned replacement inside these correlations. Delta_N decreases with N, but its limit is not yet known to be zero.

**Sufficient arithmetic criterion.** If for every fixed ordinary chi the above Delta_N tends to zero for one common gamma, then every such L is zero-free in Re(s)>gamma, with the principal pole treated as above. Thus gamma<theta11 would give a first gain, gamma=5/6 would give c=1/6, and gamma=3/4 would give c=1/4. Constants, rates and onset may depend on chi. Even a non-effective qualitative limit suffices; no conductor-uniform estimate or high-height-uniform convergence rate is assumed.

Proof: let w=z(rho) be any supposed L zero in that half-plane. It lies in the disk and is not zero, because s(0)=2 is zero-free. For every admissible p, e=pF-F0 has e(0)=0 and e(w)=-F0. Taylor Cauchy--Schwarz gives

    |F0|^2<=||e||_H2^2 |w|^2/(1-|w|^2),
    Delta_N >= |F0|^2(1-|w|^2)/|w|^2 >0.             (10)

This contradicts Delta_N->0. The argument fixes one arbitrary zero, so it covers every height without exchanging a height supremum and a limit. Conversely, this report does not claim that nonvanishing alone implies the prediction limit; singular-inner issues need not be settled for the sufficient direction.

For rho=beta+iT, d=beta-gamma>0, formula (10) is explicitly

    Delta_N >= |F0|^2 * 4a d / ((d-a)^2+T^2).          (11)

This prices high-height invisibility. A fixed positive residual bound cannot cover the whole half-plane; it becomes weak like T^-2 for a fixed horizontal gap. A genuine limit to zero would exclude each fixed zero. No finite successful computation proves that limit.

### 3a. Formation and every tail are paid from periodicity

From (3)-(5), let

    H0=sqrt(2a) C_q/(a-gamma),
    K=1+2a/(a-gamma).

Then |h(t)|<=H0 exp(-gamma t), and induction gives
|Q^j h(t)|<=H0 K^j exp(-gamma t). For the truncated Gram G_N^(T),

    |(G_N-G_N^(T))_(j,k)|
       <=H0^2 K^(j+k) exp(-2gamma T)/(2gamma),
    0<=G_N-G_N^(T)<=eta_N(T) I,
    eta_N(T)=(N+1)H0^2 K^(2N)exp(-2gamma T)/(2gamma). (12)

The second inequality follows from the first entrywise bound and the PSD tail Gram. It exposes the growing-degree cost instead of calling a finite matrix the full source. To bound the actual error without any inverse-condition-number assumption, take a specific p with p0=1, put C_p=sum_(j=0)^N |p_j|K^j, and use

    ||pF-F0||^2 <= integral_0^T |p(Q)h-F0 ell0|^2dt
       +H0^2 C_p^2 exp(-2gamma T)/gamma
       +2|F0|^2 exp(-2a T).                           (13)

This is the squared triangle inequality only on the tail. On a finite interval, b(t)=A(n)-r exp(t) for log n<=t<log(n+1); (3) and (5) are elementary exponential integrals. Thus a finite witness has a fully specified ordinary arithmetic source and certifiable tails. It still must make the complete interior integral small. Taking T large while leaving the interior unchanged does not advance (8).

The coarsest sufficient new input is an actual sequence of polynomials p_m and truncations T_m for which the complete right side of (13) tends to zero, for each fixed chi at a common gamma below theta11. No such sequence is constructed here. The apparent replacement of a power bound by an o(1) limit changes the representation, not the established arithmetic difficulty.

### 3a(ii). A cheaper coherent source approximation, and a principal tail theorem

The K^N bound above is not intrinsic. If h_tilde is any fully specified L2 approximation with ||h-h_tilde||<=tau, the isometry of Q gives, for EVERY polynomial p,

    ||p(Q)h-p(Q)h_tilde||<=tau sum_j |p_j|.            (13a)

Consequently the exact residual is at most the fully computed residual of h_tilde plus this price. Each Gram-entry error is at most tau(||h||+||h_tilde||), independent of j,k. The matrix operator error is at most N+1 times that number. These are signed-source approximation bounds, not a positive-semidefinite comparison of the two source Grams. The simple choice h_tilde=h*1_[0,T] has tau<=H0 exp(-gamma T)/sqrt(2gamma). Its filtered output is NOT truncated: after T, Q^j h_tilde has its complete exponential-polynomial tail, which is explicitly computable from the finite convolution states at T. This retains the omitted future response and avoids K^N. The coefficient sum and the main residual remain payable.

For q=1, this can be improved unconditionally. Suppose 1/2<gamma<1, put lambda=a-gamma=2-2gamma in (0,1), and D_lambda=(2-lambda)/(4(1-lambda)). With u={x}, identity (3a) becomes

    f(log x)=1/2+B(x)-V(x)/x,
    B(x)=1/2-{x}, V(x)={x}(1-{x}).                    (13b)

The continuous periodic primitive of B starting at x=1 is P(x)=V(x)/2, with 0<=P<=1/8. Integration by parts gives, for x>=1,

    |integral_x^infinity y^(lambda-1)(f(log y)-1/2)dy|
       <=D_lambda x^(lambda-1).                      (13c)

Indeed the B term is at most x^(lambda-1)/4: one endpoint term at most x^(lambda-1)/8 and one integrated term of the same bound. The V/y term is at most x^(lambda-1)/[4(1-lambda)]. Thus, for a real constant C_lambda defined by the convergent subtracted integral,

    h(t)=sqrt(2a)/(2lambda) exp(-gamma t)
         +sqrt(2a) C_lambda exp(-a t)+R(t),
    |R(t)|<=sqrt(2a)D_lambda exp(-(gamma+1)t).          (13d)

No unknown L reciprocal enters this constant or proof. For a FINITE source approximation no infinite constant is needed: let A0=sqrt(2a)/(2lambda), keep h unchanged on [0,T], and for t>T use

    h_tilde_T(t)=A0 exp(-gamma t)
       +(h(T)-A0 exp(-gamma T))exp(-a(t-T)).           (13e)

The finite prefix and value h(T) completely determine this continuation. Comparing (13d) at t and at T, or using the tail integral in (13c), proves

    ||h-h_tilde_T||_2
       <=D_lambda[1+sqrt(a/(gamma+1))]
                        exp(-(gamma+1)T).            (13f)

For the second term, the error in the coefficient C_lambda estimated at T is at most D_lambda exp(-(1-lambda)T); its L2 tail contributes D_lambda exp(-(gamma+1)T), because a+1-lambda=gamma+1. The R tail contributes the other displayed term. Combining (13a) and (13f) pays the complete omitted principal source after any finite polynomial filter, with a coefficient-sum price and faster decay. The fixed-gamma constant blows up as gamma decreases to 1/2; no endpoint claim at 1/2 follows. All three calibration targets here lie strictly above 1/2.

The sharper D_lambda above is specific to q=1. A coarser extension covers EVERY fixed ordinary character. For nonprincipal chi, A(x) is q-periodic; write it as m_chi+B_chi(x), where m_chi is its period mean. Then B_chi has mean zero, |B_chi|<=2q, and its primitive starting at 1 has modulus at most 2q^2. There is no V term below.

For principal chi, put B0(x)=A(x)-r x, let beta be its period mean, and D(x)=integral_1^x(B0(y)-beta)dy. These are q-periodic and |D|<=2q^2. Formula (3a) gives EXACTLY

    f(log x)=m_chi+B_chi(x)+V_chi(x)/x,
    m_chi=-beta, B_chi=B0-beta,
    V_chi=r+2beta-2D(x).                              (13g)

Here |B_chi|<=2q, its primitive is D, and |V_chi|<=1+2q+4q^2. Thus (13c) holds with f-1/2 replaced by f-m_chi and the admissible coarse constant

    D_chi=4q^2                                  nonprincipal,
    D_chi=4q^2+(1+2q+4q^2)/(1-lambda)             principal.     (13h)

The first 4q^2 pays the endpoint and integral of the bounded primitive; the V/x term pays the second price. The same proof gives (13d)-(13f) for every fixed chi after replacing A0 by sqrt(2a)m_chi/lambda and D_lambda by D_chi. Complex character values and natural zeros are retained. For q=1 use the much sharper explicit D_lambda rather than (13h). For example gamma=3/4 gives a=5/4,lambda=1/2 and principal q=1 source error at cutoff X=exp(T) at most (3/4)(1+sqrt(5/7))X^(-7/4), before the explicit coefficient-sum price in (13a).

This is an actual source-tail theorem for the ordinary-character family, not a prediction or Mobius estimate. All fixed-q constants are allowed. The fixed-gamma constants blow up as gamma decreases to 1/2; no endpoint claim there follows. A family zero-free claim still requires the full prediction limit for each fixed ordinary chi. A fast source approximation does not imply that the limit in (8) is zero.

### 3b. Strongest objection: stable optimal polynomials are automatic

Let p_N minimize (7). If p_N=(z-lambda)q has a root, variation by zq is admissible because it has zero constant term. Orthogonality gives

    ||qF||^2-lambda <qF,zqF>=0.

Multiplication by z is an isometry and equality in Cauchy--Schwarz is impossible for nonzero qF and zqF. Hence |lambda|>1. Every finite minimizer is therefore zero-free on the closed disk for EVERY nonzero F with F0!=0, including sources that have interior zeros. This proves that “the optimized polynomials are stable” is not an arithmetic result. It is a universal optimization property.

For the exact toy F(z)=1-z/r with real r>0, G_N is tridiagonal with diagonal 1+r^-2 and adjacent entries -r^-1. Its size-m determinant is D_m=sum_(k=0)^m r^(-2k), including D_0=1 for the empty determinant. Therefore

    d_N=D_(N+1)/D_N,
    lim d_N = r^-2 if 0<r<1, and 1 if r>=1.            (14)

At r=1, Delta_N=1/(N+1). At r=1/2, Delta_N tends to 3, although every optimizing polynomial is stable and the Gram spectrum is uniformly bounded between (1/r-1)^2 and (1/r+1)^2. More strongly, G_N(r)=r^(-2)G_N(1/r), so the entire sequence of constrained optimizing polynomials is IDENTICAL for an interior zero r and the exterior zero 1/r. Their coefficients or root locations alone cannot distinguish the two cases; the scalar residual normalization is essential. For the inner toy F=(z-r)/(1-rz), 0<r<1, the complete Gram is exactly the identity and d_N=1 for all N, while |F0|^2=r^2. Matrix positivity and good conditioning do not pay the prediction gap either. These are toy obstructions to the stated inference, not lower bounds on the actual character source.

This is classical optimal-polynomial approximation, not a literature novelty. The primary paper by Beneteau, Khavinson, Liaw, Seco and Sola, *Orthogonal polynomials, reproducing kernels, and zeros of optimal approximants*, arXiv:1509.04807v2 (17 September 2015), Theorem 3.2 and sections 5-6, establishes the related universal zero-free property and cyclicity/Gram framework: https://arxiv.org/pdf/1509.04807 . Our constrained p0=1 version is proved above. The contribution proposed for the QRH record is the literal ordinary-character source (2)-(5), complete tail (12)-(13), calibration and scoped failure; not a new general Hardy theorem.

## 4. D3 / protected wildcard X28: interpolation does not remove residual debt

Suppose an admissible polynomial p also satisfies p(z_j)F(z_j)=F0 at finitely many nodes, with multiplicity allowed. Include z=0 once, since p0=1 already enforces that node. Nodes used as safe data must correspond to known nonzero L values, for example Re(s_j)>1. Let

    B(z)=product_j (z-z_j)/(1-conjugate(z_j)z).

The complete residual e=pF-F0 is divisible by B, and e/B belongs to H2 with the same norm: for finitely many zeros this follows by analytic division and the unit boundary modulus of B. At a hypothetical zero w of F not among the safe nodes,

    ||e||^2 >= |F0|^2(1-|w|^2)/|B(w)|^2.             (15)

The reproduction-kernel bound for H2 proves this directly. When B=z, it is (10). When the first m Taylor conditions are exactly fitted, B=z^m and the floor is |F0|^2(1-|w|^2)|w|^(-2m). Extra exact sample matches do not themselves make the full error smaller; they can force a larger invisible complement. This is compatible with the old invariant-subspace correction: no artificial additional norm cost is charged for dividing an error already known to lie in BH2. Equation (15) is the resulting point-evaluation bound for the divided error, not a claim that inner division expands its norm.

The exact example F=1-z/r and the Taylor inverse p_N=sum_(j=0)^N(z/r)^j gives

    e(z)=-(z/r)^(N+1), ||e||^2=r^(-2N-2).             (16)

It fits every Taylor condition through degree N at the safe origin, while its full residual grows if the source has an interior zero r<1. At r=1/2, N=4 it is 1024. The complete complement, not interpolation precision at the sampled nodes, detects the obstruction. For a fixed high zero, (11) and |w|^(-2m) show a fixed-anchor scale m of order T^2/(beta-gamma) for order-one exponential amplification. This is consistent with N29's older moving-anchor analysis; it is not a new all-height estimate.

The live escape is a signed arithmetic estimate for the full residual in (13), possibly using a nontrivial safe-node geometry and the exact divided residual. Conditioning, source formation and the complete tail must be included. No such estimate is proved.

## 5. The other three first tests, with exact scope

**R16, sieve trellis.** A state recording only coarse parity/residue cannot determine the remaining support. At N=21, y=5, the normalized future laws for histories 2 and 3 are 1-z7; for 5,6,10,15 they are 1; history 1 has 1-z7-z11-z13-z17-z19. Signed reconstruction gives M(21)=-2. Keeping amplitudes distinct from normalized laws is essential. This repeats G105, including its O(sqrt N) lawful-state count and open complete signed contraction. It does not establish complexity or square-root cancellation. No extra development credit is requested.

**F04, rare free-group holonomy.** For true sharp prefixes, V_p V_q e_n=V_q V_p e_n=e_(pqn) exactly when pqn<=N, and both vanish otherwise. Thus the proposed prime-shift holonomy is zero; zero curvature supplies no norm gain. The diagonal projector onto numbers whose primes are <=y also commutes with the diagonal size projector, so merely comparing those two diagonal filtrations does not produce an anomaly. Non-divisor-closed masks can fail to commute but owe the omitted source. This is the exact Sol04 S09/G69 ancestry. Adjoints, noncausal transports, and a different paid boundary remain live; they were not developed here.

**X30, divisor simplex.** On one unramified prime p, the augmented simplex has e_p in degree one and e_empty in degree zero, with d(e_p)=e_empty. Weighting by chi(p) and 1 is a chain map only if chi(p)=1. Its putative weighted Euler trace 1-chi(p) can therefore be nonzero even though this augmented complex is acyclic. For chi(p)=-1 it is 2. Thus the weighted arithmetic parity sum is not automatically a homology trace. A product cutoff introduces the same unpaid weighted boundary; the principal case needs the reduced Euler characteristic with its empty face. This repeats A-SIMPLICIAL and the Sol04 topology audit, and does not rule out a different coefficient-exact complex with a genuinely cheaper signed boundary.

`checks.py` and `checks.json` retain exact finite determinant, inverse-interpolation, continuation, prefix and weighted-chain calculations. `tail-checks.py` and `tail-checks.json` add exact periodic decompositions for principal, nonprincipal and complex-character components, plus isometry-vector checks and a separately labeled numerical tail diagnostic. They validate indexing and the displayed finite examples only. Infinite formation and return claims rest on the proofs above, not finite data.

## 6. Ancestry, functional signatures, and disposition

History was consulted only after seed freeze and draw selection. The current navigation/proof, creative-lane/protocol and progress scorecard were read in bounded source slices, and the relevant exact ancestry was checked in the early and later attempt ledgers, [private research revision] G103-G105, [private research revision] G106-G108, [private research revision] G109/S09/S38, and W37 D03/T17. These identify existing Hardy residual, Cayley/Laguerre, storage, lawful-state, prefix and simplicial mechanisms. Broader search hits are pointers, not claims of full inspection of every original archive.

The full 29-family/109-child portfolio remains as recorded in `[restricted mathematical source]`, `[restricted mathematical source]`, `[restricted mathematical source]`, and their coverage records. No stable ID or untested historical disposition is superseded. W54's source-specific exact certificate is offered for comparison with F21.H/N1, F23.C, F26.L, N29.L/N1, U-VARIATIONAL, and W37's feedback/storage work. It is not claimed new merely because its control notation differs.

Two further exact comparisons matter. `[restricted mathematical source]` already corrects the finite-inner geometry: its original source lies in BH, division by B is an isometry there, and equality with all of BH was never supplied. Equation (15) retains that correction. `[restricted mathematical source]` already pays arithmetic tails by bounded primitives of periodic floor-coefficient fluctuations, while retaining the leading mean/variance and cross terms. Therefore the method behind (13c)-(13h) is an adaptation of an existing periodic-primitive method to this particular pole-normalized character source and its causal continuation; no novelty of that general tail method is claimed. These comparisons prevent the better formation bound from being mistaken for either a new inner-factor penalty or cancellation of the prediction residual.

| Development | Object and transformation | Mechanism | First unpaid estimate | Proved return |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| D1 / R11 | Pole-normalized L/s -> bounded character staircase -> causal Q realization | Signed output projection; Q itself is isometric | Source-specific correlations needed for a small residual | Exact H2/L2 norm identity, all ordinary-character zeros preserved |
| D2 / X26 | Actual source Toeplitz Gram, constrained finite prediction | Positive full residual with exact scalar anchor | Delta_N -> 0 at one common gamma<theta11 | Every natural zero at every height excluded; tail and principal pole paid |
| D3 / X28 | Safe-node interpolation, exact finite Blaschke division | Evaluation of the full divided residual | A complete arithmetic upper bound beating (15) | Explicit zero-dependent lower floor and return, no sample-only inference |

R11 survives as a precise realization/obstruction, X26 as a conditional high-ceiling source criterion with paid formation/tail, and X28 as a protected wildcard residual certificate. They are one coherent architecture with three bounded developments, not three independent arithmetic discoveries. R16/F04/X30 are duplicate scoped failures with live escapes. F01,F02,F03,F05,F06,F07,F08,F09,F10,R12,R13,R14,R15,R17,R18,R19,R20,X21,X22,X23,X24,X25,X27,X29 remain untested.

Next mathematical action: work on the actual bounded staircase correlations in (7), or construct an explicit polynomial sequence whose complete residual tends to zero, using (13a)-(13h) to pay source approximation efficiently. First use gamma=.874854 or another fixed number below theta11 and retain every coefficient and tail. Merely plotting stable roots, finding positive Grams, increasing truncation T, or fitting more safe samples is already known insufficient. There is no evidence yet that this prediction limit is easier than the original zero problem. The source-tail refinement removes a formation cost; no arithmetic exponent gap is reduced in this report, and no new c, theorem admission, formalization or packet is claimed.

statement:
## 4. Independent proof of B, including offsets and exact lags

Let |a(n)|<=1 for positive integers and a(n)=0 otherwise. Fix tau>0, real X>=1 and integer H>=1. Define

    B_H(k) = sum_{j=0}^{H-1} a(k-j),
    w_X(k) = exp(-log(k/X)^2/(4 tau)),
    E_a(X,H) = (1/H) sum_{k>=1} |B_H(k)|^2 w_X(k).

The sum has every positive endpoint and both Gaussian tails; bounded coefficients guarantee absolute convergence. There is no dyadic support truncation. Put ell=log 2 and

    K_tau = exp(ell^2/(3 tau))
              [exp(tau/3+4 ell/3)/sqrt(3 pi tau) + 1/(pi tau)].

Then

    sup_{X<=x<=2X} |F_a(x)|
      <= sqrt(K_tau (X/H+1) E_a(X,H)) + 2H g_tau(0).       (B)

For a residue representative r in {1,...,H}, the intervals (k-H,k], with positive k congruent to r, partition all positive integers after zero extension at the initial block. Replace g_tau(log(n/x)) by its value at the block's right endpoint, giving V_r(x). The total variation of t -> g_tau(log(t/x)) on (0,infinity) is 2g_tau(0), because it increases from zero to its maximum and then decreases to zero. Each interval contains at most H integers, so the sum of absolute replacement errors is at most H times the total variation. This proves |F_a(x)-V_r(x)| <= 2H g_tau(0), including the first partial block and the infinite tails.

Set u=log(x/X) in [0,ell] and v=log(k/X). The Cauchy quotient is

    g_tau(v-u)^2 / w_X(k)
       = (2 pi tau)^(-1)
          exp(-3v^2/(4 tau) + 2uv/tau - u^2/tau).

As a function of t=k/X>0 this is positive and unimodal. Its supremum is exp(u^2/(3 tau))/(2 pi tau). Integrating in t introduces the Jacobian exp(v); completion of the square gives its integral

    exp(tau/3 + 4u/3 + u^2/(3 tau)) / sqrt(3 pi tau).

The independent helper checks both square-completion identities as polynomial identities over exact rational coefficients. A positive unimodal function sampled at spacing H/X has sum bounded by (X/H) times its integral plus twice its maximum: compare adjacent intervals on each monotone side of the peak, leaving at most two peak samples. Uniformly in u in [0,ell], this is at most K_tau(X/H+1). Thus, with E_r the unnormalized energy on one offset grid,

    |V_r(x)| <= sqrt(K_tau(X/H+1) E_r).

Average the approximations over r and use concavity of the square root. Since (1/H)sum_r E_r = E_a(X,H), this proves (B) with the asserted normalization. There is no lost factor H, and no sign assumption on cross terms. A logarithmic shell L2 norm is also bounded by sqrt(log 2) times the same supremum bound.

The exact expansion, retaining its moving weight, is

    E_a(X,H) = (1/H) sum_{|h|<H} sum_{n>=max(1,1-h)}
       a(n) conjugate(a(n+h))
       sum_{j=max(0,h)}^{min(H-1,H-1+h)} w_X(n+j).        (L)

Indeed, in B_H(k)conjugate(B_H(k)), write n=k-j and h=j-l. The restrictions 0<=j,l<=H-1 are equivalent to the displayed j bounds, and positivity of n,n+h gives the n bound. Then k=n+j. This is a bijection of summation indices, and absolute convergence permits rearrangement. It does not replace the inner weight by a fixed triangular coefficient. The helper independently preserves every symbolic monomial a_n conjugate(a_m) w_k in an offset/direct/lag spot check, but this general bijection is the proof.

statement:
### 5a. Extension of balanced-residue mass to the COMPLETE tail

For a fixed residue vector e, the actual coefficients (including the `Nc>U^(6/5)` projection if desired) satisfy

    sum_(l/l' congruent e mod sixth powers)
       |partial b_l(s) partial' b_l'(s)|
        << H_J U^[-(2sigma-1)t+epsilon] H^(-1/2).     ([restricted research revision])

Here partial and partial' are any two of the finite required derivative operators. This proves cross-dyad as well as same-dyad control. To see it, put Nl in a dyad L and Nl' in a possibly different dyad L'. For each choice of signs of the actual nonzero valuation differences, write

    l=g a x^6,  l'=g b y^6,  (a,b)=1,
    N(ab)>=H.

At a prime of residue e, its exponent in ab is e or 6-e according to that sign. All additional multiples of six are in x,y. Taking g to be the actual gcd gives an exact representation; then allowing all x,y only overcounts. There are at most `2^omega(q1q2q3)` sign choices. For fixed a,b,x,y the number of g is at most

    min(L/[Na (Nx)^6], L'/[Nb (Ny)^6])
       <= sqrt(LL')/[sqrt(Nab) (Nx)^3 (Ny)^3].

If either upper cutoff is below one, the actual set is empty. Summing x,y uses the convergent ideal zeta series at3. Multiplying by (C7) gives the dyadic bound

    H_J U^((2sigma-1)v+epsilon)
       (LL')^(1/2-sigma) H^(-1/2).

Both L,L' start at `c0 U^(t+v)`. Since sigma>1/2, the TWO geometric tail sums converge with total

    [U^(t+v)]^(1-2sigma).

The slot power cancels, leaving exactly ([restricted research revision]). This step is what an invocation of the old single-annulus RM-A would omit. The cutoff has been merged before this decomposition; A_R is never triangle-expanded into individual divisor witnesses. Derivative logarithms are paid by a small decrease of sigma. The finite terminal support makes the sign count and all divisor factors subpower uniformly; no infinite sum of conductor dyads with a nondecaying bound is asserted.

On dyadic ranges of Q1,Q2,Q3 there are at most `(Q1Q2Q3)^(1+epsilon)` residue vectors. Thus their combined coefficient mass is

    << H_J U^[-(2sigma-1)t+epsilon] (Q1/Q3)^(1/2).     ([restricted research revision])

This already pays all q1=1 classes, including mixed quadratic/cubic characters of GLOBAL order6. Global order6 is not by itself the hard class.

statement:
# Actual common-prime valuations and a stronger support bound

COMPLETED BOUNDED SOURCE DEVELOPMENT, awaiting independent review; no new accepted constant. Calibration: accepted c8=.12514261. The controller reports independent approval of frozen [restricted research revision] .12514475 and its restricted marked-plain theorem at 08:40 UTC, with root intake still pending; neither is root-accepted. This scope does not alter those files or contact their critic. All statements retain the same source-relative analytic-base, positive-slot uniformity and comparison-root-definition obligations.

The source is PR9 at 58344dfdbe756cf2f743da1908ffe0582418cf5b and Gao PR15 at ca182b70ac2aee2d053d679b4ddf1233883f9eef. The decisive passages are PR9 B3.50--56 (full first common support and joint target), PR15 SignedReconstruction (both actual row residues and canceled natural holes), and PhysicalLocalAssembly LA.4, LA.11--13. The PR9 printed inverse-xi phase is used only with the already reviewed correction +xi_r(ab); the C-side coefficient is tau(a)chi_a(er)xi_r(a). This is the convention independently supported by Gao's two signed residues. No formalization, kernel, external provider/model, child, canonical, tracker or Git mutation occurs here.

## 1. The relaxed equality is not an arithmetic configuration

At a first common prime write i>=1,j>=1 for its COMPLETE multiplicities in the two full columns, including both plain variables and every slot incidence. Let l_p=log_Z Np. For the C orientation put t=(i-j) mod6. The actual factors are

    t=0: r=0,e=0,r0=0;
    t=1,2,3,4: r=1,e=t+1,r0=0;
    t=5: r=1,e=0,r0=1.

Here r records the active radical, e the exponent in F, and r0 an ACTIVE prime whose row phase cancels. Inactive t=0 does not contribute an exponent 1 to F: it belongs to the old common puncture, with its optional mask-divisor contribution e_mask accounted separately by E. At t=5 the source's sixth power is its natural coprimality mask, not the constant one. The D orientation exchanges i,j and has residue 1-t; this is exactly the same table applied to its own ordered multiplicities. Whole-character conjugation preserves the integer row norm and its natural zeros; it is not a change of only the parent phase.

Thus c=sum i l_p, d=sum j l_p, R=sum r l_p, L=sum e l_p, R0=sum r0 l_p. These identities precede density, projectors or positivity. The earlier relaxed equality R=min(c,d), (c-d)_+=min(c,d), L=5R would force c=2d, every j=1 and every common prime active. L=5R would also force i-j=4 mod6, so every i>=5. Then c>=5d, a contradiction for nonempty support. No possible mixture of primes repairs that contradiction. The empty-support case remains a separate density-controlled configuration.

## 2. A primewise certificate that handles every mixture

Use rho=1-10delta/[3(5-2delta)], delta in [17/25,7/10]. Retain the actual source support line

    E1=(1-rho)(c-d)_+-delta c-(1+rho)R-E-Bc+rho L+R0,
    Bc=(3c-5d-R)_+/6, E>=0.                          (1)

Let f_t=(1+rho)r-rho e-r0. In order t=0,...,5 its values are

    0, 1-rho, 1-2rho, 1-3rho, 1-4rho, rho.            (2)

For c<=d, (c-d)_+=Bc=0. Since f_t>=1-4rho and i>=1 while 1-4rho<0, each f_t>=(1-4rho)i. Therefore

    -E1 >= (delta+1-4rho)c+E.                         (3)

For c>=d define

    Hplus=delta-(6+27rho)/37,
    lambda=(9-15rho)/37 in [0,1/6],
    u=(19rho-4)/37>0.

Since Bc>=lambda(3c-5d-R), it suffices to prove, prime by prime,

    (19rho-4)(i+2j)+(28+52rho)r-37rho e-37r0 >=0.      (4)

This is an actual valuation inequality, not a free optimization of c,d,R,L. The minimum possible i+2j for t=1,2,3,4,5 is respectively 4,5,6,7,5. For t=4 equality at 7 occurs precisely at (i,j)=(5,1) or (1,3). For the other active residues, substituting their minimum gives respectively

    12+54rho, 8+36rho, 4+18rho, 0, 147rho-29,

all nonnegative on the stated range. Inactive t=0 contributes (19rho-4)(i+2j)>0. Adding multiples of six to i or j increases (4) because u>0. This proves the unbounded-valuation assertion, not merely a finite table.

To check the dual algebra directly, subtract Hplus c from -E1, use c>=d, and then Bc>=lambda(3c-5d-R). Its coefficients of c,d become u,2u, and the remaining prime terms are (28+52rho)r/37-rho e-r0. Summing (4) proves

    -E1 >= Hplus c+E, c>=d.                          (5)

Consequently every actual signed side obeys

    E1 <= -Hval(delta)c-E,
    Hval=min(delta+1-4rho, delta-(6+27rho)/37).         (6)

Both displayed alternatives increase with delta. Their equality occurs at rho=43/121, equivalently delta=585/839. On the whole interval,

    Hval>=Hval(17/25)=1166/6825=.17084249... .         (7)

This exceeds both accepted eta_old(delta)=2(rho+delta-1) and the pending marked-plain eta_plus(delta)=(458/193)(rho+delta-1), whose maxima occur at delta=.68. Hence the support coefficient ceases to limit either density input.

## 3. Legal local equality patterns and what they do not establish

For (3), choose good first common primes outside every fixed bad modulus, with C=P,D=P^3. The C side has t=4,r=1,e=5,r0=0 at each such prime; E=0 is a term of the complete inactive-mask expansion. Thus c<=d and equality holds in the coefficient calculation (3). Every residual factor retains the P-puncture, and the effective row contains F=P^5. No natural zero is suppressed.

For (5), choose disjoint good prime products U,V and set

    C=U^5 V, D=U V^3,
    log_Z NU=13t, log_Z NV=9t, t>0.

Then c=74t,d=40t,R=22t,L=110t,R0=E=0, Bc=0. Every prime is of type (5,1) or (1,3), so (4) is an equality and the resulting coefficient equals Hplus. Exact equality of two distinct prime-product logarithms is not claimed; dyadic sectors approximate these ratios arbitrarily closely as the scale grows, with the original aggregate support tolerance. This is sufficient to test the supremal exponent geometry.

These patterns are compatible with the actual enclosing width and child width for sufficiently small fixed t: W=M-R-(c-d)_++L-6a=M+54t-6a, while M'=M-34t-6a-omega-g2+t2. The requirement NF<=Z^W reduces to 56t<=M-6a, which is strict for small t. For the first pattern it reduces to c<=M-6a. Allocate the displayed powers to original plain variables at sufficiently small support widths; choose residual prime support disjoint from them. All frozen-prime and canceled-prime zeros remain literal. A rectangle made empty by an allocation stays zero, as permitted by B3.50; no assertion that every allocated rectangle is simultaneously nonzero is needed. The second common support/projector can be empty without violating these coefficient constraints.

These are legal valuation/width configurations, not assertions that a character with a zero in the selected high bin exists or that a full oscillatory norm saturates its estimate. Further improvement beyond (6) may come from coupled columns, spectral information or actual label scarcity. The proof here only determines the best support coefficient supplied by these first-valuation inequalities.

## 4. Transfer the whole density gain in the actual paired units

The first numerical consequence uses only the ACCEPTED [restricted research revision] weighted-density theorem. Its raw form, for an actual signed row bound W and a live slot product Q of total width z_j, is

    sum_high |Q_w|^2 << Z^[rho W+(delta-eta_old)z_j+epsilon] H_J,
    eta_old=2k, k=rho+delta-1, 0<=z_j<=W/21.          (8)

H_J denotes the allowed polynomial in the independent input heights. This theorem already includes all inverse-length regimes, literal natural holes, fixed translating character and the raw sixth-power sum. This scope does not claim a new proof of those imports. The new estimate (6) is inserted into their ORIGINAL source ledger, not into an unweighted population estimate.

Let z_1,z_2 be the two surviving slot widths after the complete second projector and let rbar=(r_clip,1+r_clip,2)/2. Put zbar=(z_1+z_2)/2. Exact extraction gives

    E2<=-delta b2-t2,
    zbar>=z-c-b2-rbar-small, 0<=z_j<=z+small.         (9)

The clipped plains additionally save delta rbar. These are the [restricted research revision] transport inequalities from PR9 B3.65--69, including its two extraction scalars and the dyadic count of the second projector. That projector is NOT asserted to divide w. The first-label count was already incorporated jointly in LA.13; it is not multiplied in again. Cauchy on the two actual slot products changes the paired exponent by eta zbar, not by twice that amount. The first-label Cauchy average later preserves the same per-side bound. Both normalization scalars, both whole rectangles and both orientations are unchanged.

Take eta=eta_old or, CONDITIONAL on [restricted research revision] Sections 1--4, eta=eta_plus=(458/193)k. Both decrease on [.68,.70] and their maxima are

    eta_old(q)=782/6825,
    eta_plus(q)=179078/1317225, q=17/25.

Both are below Hval(q)=1166/6825 and below delta. Let s0=c+b2+rbar. If s0>=z, (6) and the old projector/plain savings already save at least eta z. If s0<z, use the ACTUAL enclosing width

    W=M-R-(c-d)_++Lc-6a >= M-c-6a > M-z-6a.

Here a is the main amplifier length; it is not a density parameter. The exact atlas below has

    M-6a>22z.                                      (10)

Consequently every z_j<=z lies below W/21; (8) applies at its supported width. Old savings plus density save at least

    eta s0+eta(z-s0)-small=eta z-small.              (11)

No estimate at a width smaller than a nonempty support is used. Aggregate endpoint errors, one greedy overshoot and the norm-window padding enter the existing small budget; the strict width gap makes (10) stable. The actual child width M'=M-(c-d)_+-6a-omega-g2+t2 is retained for the positive old-moment call. W is its signed enclosing ROW width, not a replacement child width.

In particular the new paired support saving equals the density coefficient eta. The earlier retained-Bc relaxation supplied only min(delta-3rho/2,eta)z. The difference comes from the integer-valuation certificate (4), not a reoptimization of that relaxed scalar program.

## 5. A further conditional transfer of the nonlinear marked-plain gain

This section is separate from the accepted-density route. It assumes the NEW [restricted research revision] marked-plain source lemma and its all-regime/raw-lifting proof, independently approved according to the controller but still pending root intake at this writing. It does not mistake the accepted marked-INVERSE theorem for that marked-PLAIN theorem.

The stronger [restricted research revision] raw theorem has gain

    G_delta(W,v)=min(3k v, A_delta W+B_delta v),
    A_delta=2delta(5-6delta)^2/[3(5-2delta)(115-54delta)],
    B_delta=14delta(5-6delta)/(115-54delta).           (12)

Its range is 0<=v<=W/21. [restricted research revision] proves the free estimate for v/W<=1/20 by a partially marked plain fourth moment and the accepted marked inverse estimate; the short, middle and long inverse regimes are all included. Its raw sixth-power sum uses the original holes, decay 6(rho-A_delta)-1>0 in the near range, and tail reserve rho-1/6-3k>0 in the complementary range, including bounded or fixed-inducing free cores. Those source assumptions and their fixed-dictionary/height quantifiers remain necessary here.

It would be WRONG to replace [G(W,z_1)+G(W,z_2)]/2 by G(W,zbar): G is concave. Instead fix the ORIGINAL z. For 0<=v<=z, G(W,v)/v is decreasing in v, so

    G(W,v)>=(v/z)G(W,z).                            (13)

The zero endpoint follows directly. G is nondecreasing and A_delta-Lipschitz in W. Write V=M-6a. In the case s0<z of Section 4, W>=V-c>21z. Consequently, after the actual Cauchy average,

    [G(W,z_1)+G(W,z_2)]/2
      >= [G(V,z)/z]zbar-A_delta c,                 (14)

because zbar<=z. This uses each slot product at its actual width and charges the possible row-width reduction c once.

Throughout the atlas z/M in [17/500,1/25]. Both A_delta and B_delta decrease on [.68,.70]. For A, its logarithmic derivative is

    1/delta-12/(5-6delta)+2/(5-2delta)+54/(115-54delta)<0;

bound the three positive terms at their interval maxima and the negative term at -12/(.92)=-300/23. For B, the derivative numerator is 14(575-1380delta+324delta^2)<0; that quadratic decreases throughout this interval. At q,

    A_q=17986/13356525, B_q=5474/48925,
    Kmax=A_q/(17/500)+B_q=2023402/13356525.

In particular

    Hval(q)-A_q-Kmax=6166/342475>0.                 (15)

Since V<=M and delta>=q>Kmax, all support/projector/plain costs in (14) are paid: (6), (9) and zbar>=z-s0 give a total saving at least G(V,z). If s0>=z, Hval(q)z alone is greater than G(V,z)<=Kmax z. Thus, in EVERY support configuration, including empty common support,

    final paired gain >= G_delta(M-6a,z)-small.     (16)

Also Kmax<3k(.70), so the affine branch in (12) is active at V,z for this whole atlas. The gain in (16) is therefore exactly

    A_delta(M-6a)+B_delta z.                       (17)

This is a genuinely stronger use of the source estimate, with its row-width cost paid by the new valuation reserve. It neither averages a concave gain in the wrong direction nor declares unused common support available when it is empty.

## 6. Three complete rational returns

All three routes are source-relative candidates. The first depends on the accepted [restricted research revision] density and the new valuation proof above. The last two additionally depend on the pending marked-plain theorem. All retain the same imported analytic-base/F0, positive-slot uniformity and comparison-root-definition obligations as c8. No acceptance or public-record claim is made here.

Use q=17/25, K=9/2, Ka=34/21, alpha=1/400000 and 600 consecutive cells

    b_j=17/500+j/100000, j=1,...,600,
    g_j=B-1+(K-Lambda)b_j,
    a_j=Ka g_j+alpha,
    A_j=B-(Lambda-1)b_(j-1).                        (18)

These prove the common-profile local moment with capacity x1+x2+Lambda z<=B M for both plains at least M/4. The accepted comparison has plain lengths M/4,M/2 and z<=M/25, leaving 7M/100 in its old 9/2 budget. All rows of the WHOLE centered difference use the same smooth cutoffs and coefficients. The old uncentered complements remain old moments. No high-bin estimate is substituted per label for a jointly counted target.

For the two linear-density gains, put D=q+(5-6rho(q))Ka and

    B0=14200/14361,
    B=B0-3/500000=7099956917/7180500000,
    Lambda=19312/4787-eta(q)/D.                     (19)

This gives Lambda=57614/14361 for accepted eta_old and 11107910/2771673 for pending eta_plus. At q the z-coefficient cancels exactly. The local high margin is

    1-rho(q)-q A_j-a_j(5-6rho(q))+eta(q)b_(j-1)>0.

For (17), put C=5-6rho(q)+6A_q, D=q+C Ka. Exact cancellation gives

    B0=(1-rho(q)+A_q+C Ka)/D=6250/6319,
    B=B0-3/500000=3124981043/3159500000,
    Lambda=(q+(9/2)C Ka-B_q)/D=25362/6319.          (20)

Its local high margin is

    1-rho(q)-q A_j-a_j(5-6rho(q))
          +A_q(1-6a_j)+B_q b_(j-1)>0.

For ALL delta in [q,.70], the high margin increases. Without the new gain its derivative is bounded below by

    50(1-6 a_max)/[3(5-2q)^2]-A_max.

For a linear gain subtract at most mult*139/12150, with mult=2 or 458/193. For (17), use A_delta'>=-15A_q and

    B_delta'>=14(575-1380(.70)+324(.70)^2)/(115-54(.70))^2.

The exact positive remainder is recorded for each route. Thus q controls the entire new high interval. For delta>=.70 the OLD unweighted high estimate is positive at .70 and increasing, up to the original delta<=3/4 cutoff supplied by the imported initial 7/8 theorem. No stronger high-density input outside its range is assumed. Bins straddling the chosen cutoffs use their original fine upper-endpoint padding.

The exact atlas also checks the low margin a(1-4q/3)-2qg/9; the three extraction-error reserves a/4-g/6,13a/4-g/6,4a-g/6; the second zero 1-A-5a; main exceptional 1-A-4a; error exceptional 1-A-9a; amplifier bound 1/4-7a; and (10). All 600 cells are checked as rational numbers. Affineness also explains why their extreme cells suffice mathematically. None of these branches is replaced by a numerical density experiment.

The physical return parameters are:

| Route | c | h | Euler split t0 | plain cap N | slot cap z_safe |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| accepted density + new valuations | .12514477 | .795396 | .001 | .4224 | .0372 |
| pending marked-plain linear gain | .12514558 | .795407 | .00103 | .4222 | .03723 |
| pending marked-plain exact gain | .12514596 | .795383 | .00104 | .4222 | .03724 |

Every terminating decimal in this table is an exact rational. Put theta=1-c, ell=4c-1/3, x=1+ell-h, y=h-2ell, kappa=1-2c, d_-=h-.001, d_+=h+10^-12 and d0=1/200. The OLD contour padding .001 remains unchanged; t0 is an independent Euler-shift split. All rows satisfy

    0<ell<x<y<2x, y<1/2<h<2y, 1/6<ell<1/5, h>4ell.

The exact near-row capacities are

    n=1-y/d+t, z_A=(B-2n)/Lambda,
    k_new(d)=[2y-(2-B)d]/Lambda,
    k_old(d)=(2y-d)/(6kappa).                        (21)

For d in [d_-,d_+] and 0<=t<=t0, the checked endpoints give .41<n<N and .034<z_A<z_safe<.04. The new moment is used only in its certified window. If a plain shortens below .41, the old budget is .41+N+(9/2)z_safe<1. If selected supply shortens below .034, its old budget is 2N+(9/2)(.034)<1. The exact reserves are respectively 1/5000 and 11/5000 in the accepted route; 53/200000 and 13/5000 in the linear pending route; 11/50000 and 13/5000 in the exact pending route. Fixed parent padding, derivative-profile pairs and the original denominator retain their source allocation, chosen below these strict reserves. The empty selected family uses the eligible unrestricted zero-slot moment, with both Fourier heights, not a hidden positive-capacity hypothesis.

ALL Euler shifts are paid. The weighted Euler coefficient mass carries the original damping U^(-delta t/2), once. For t<=t0, the capacity loss t*q_amp/Lambda is paid since q_amp<=delta/2 and Lambda>1. For larger t define b=2y/d-1 and

    S_b(t)=t/2-[(b-(1-B))/Lambda-max(0,(b-2t)/(9/2))]/4.

This is continuous and has slopes 7/18 and 1/2 on its positive-capacity and zero-capacity pieces. The exact enclosure b<=803/5000 has S_b(t0)>0 in each route, proving all t>=t0 including the clipped zero-capacity range. Support bounds keep actual plain exponents below the source unrestricted range. The old t0=.001 FAILS in the two conditional routes even at their actual b maxima; increasing the split and rechecking n,z is essential. The original coarse slot cap .0372 also FAILS there. These failures are preserved numerically, not discarded.

The remaining physical checks in each receipt are detector and lower-scale supply; ell-d_+ z_max>0; ell/d_+>4/21; the old/new junction; d_+ extension; the far-old and small-row bounds; both principal contour displacements; and the old/new supremum feedback constants. Their formulas are transcribed from the written [restricted research revision] forward return, not inferred from a formal theorem signature. See the explicit named rational values in the receipts and the numerator below.

For endpoint delta in [0,3/4], p in [0,1/2] define

    Dp=3-p-2p/(3kappa), P=2(1-p)(1-p/(3kappa)),
    V=5/6-delta, J=V Dp+delta P,
    RJ=(1-delta)J+delta P V/2,
    N_d=J[theta-saving-(1+delta)/2-13h/75+y/2+ell/2
            -ell delta p+(9/100)d+delta p k(d)/2]
         -(3/4)d RJ.                               (22)

J>1/10 on the rectangle. This bidegree-(2,3) polynomial is strictly positive with k_new at d=h and saving10^-10, k_old at d=d_- and saving10^-5, and k_old at d=1/2 and saving10^-3. The receipts cover the ENTIRE rectangle by rational tensor Bernstein boxes with every coefficient positive. Counts are 18/6/1 boxes (300 coefficients) for the accepted route and 20/6/1 (324 coefficients) for each conditional route. Ordinary Python Fraction arithmetic constructs them by exact interpolation, checks an additional exact evaluation per box, and subdivides until positive; this is not formal proof-assistant work.

The old margin is affine in d between 1/2 and d_-. The new margin is affine between d_- and h and has positive old/new junction. Its d-slope is less than 2, so the h certificate extends to d_+ by the reserved 10^-10 saving. Below 1/2 the same source convex old bound applies, including the checked d0 margin. The explicit feedback bounds are old<1/8 and new<1/50, with the actual supremum parameter charged as in [restricted research revision]. Thus the source's target-uniform contradiction applies after the common small budgets, fixed slot dictionary, all height/seminorm orders and eventual scale threshold are chosen in that order. The source-relative conclusion is zero exclusion with each stated c, subject to that route's imports and independent validation of the present source.

## 7. Failures, ceilings and the next mathematical target

The rational receipts retain the failed next grid value for each plane and h: .12514478, .12514559 and .12514597 each gives a NEGATIVE unsaved numerator at a stated rational delta and p=1/2. These are failures of those fixed returns, not universal upper bounds. Floating locators suggested the tested candidates but do not certify them. A first attempt to use SymPy failed because that package is absent; no installation or provider call was made. A pure-Python finite-difference Newton locator supplied the optional third trial only. The final evidence is exact rational arithmetic and the written analytic argument.

The remaining empty-common-support sector is real: select residual prime factors pairwise coprime, outside all fixed bad moduli, and use no first or second common support. Then c=d=b2=rbar=0, W=M-6a, and the support reserve is exactly zero. It admits nonempty column coefficient sums with all required natural zeros and projectors intact. This is NOT an assertion that zeros in the high bin exist; it identifies the exact source configuration where (6) has nothing further to give. The density input must supply the next gain there. The legal equality patterns of Section 3 separately show why one cannot improve the valuation coefficient indefinitely by treating the columns as arbitrary independent scalar supports.

A next sufficient source target is a strictly stronger JOINT bound for the two actual surviving slot products after the complete second projector, or a stronger marked-plain witness moment in the same fixed ray pool. It must improve the paired gain beyond (12) on this empty-common-support sector. An estimate for unrelated characters or one which drops the projector has no such consequence. [restricted research revision]'s failed full-marking construction, which pays exact restoration and becomes worse in its inverse/plain crossover, remains a useful obstruction; this scope does not revive it under a new name. The direct arithmetic change here is the allowed residue geometry and its support payment in (14).

The current certified physical range ell<1/5 already restricts this return to c<2/15. More structurally, ell<x<=y and x+y=1-ell force ell<1/3, hence c<1/6 under ell=4c-1/3. These are limitations of THIS physical architecture, not universal barriers to a zero-free constant. Reaching 1/6 requires a new physical return or new geometric range; 1/4 requires a more substantial replacement, since ell would be 2/3 while the two plain lengths sum to 1/3. Density gains alone cannot erase these inequalities.

## 8. Evidence, attribution and closure boundary

The actual signed valuation residues, child reconstruction, whole-product twists, common masks and both projectors come from PR9 B3.50--69 and Gao PR15 SignedReconstruction/PhysicalLocalAssembly, not from a finite experimental table. PR15 source headers are dated 11 October 2026; source receipt time is a separate event. The initial density and moment ancestry remain the pinned sources' responsibility, with their already recorded open applicability boundaries. The new all-integer primewise certificate (4), impossibility of the relaxed equality, full-density support transfer and the conditional nonlinear transfer are new in this local research record. No claim of literature priority is made.

The complete endpoint mechanism is the written [restricted research revision] return, continued through accepted [restricted research revision] weighted projector transport and [restricted research revision]/c8 plane assembly. [restricted research revision] supplies only the pending marked-plain lemma for the two conditional routes. Its files remain unchanged. ## 4. Exact divisor-check dual and a complete signed target

See erasure.md for all indices and proofs. Let S be squarefree q-units through N, let E contain those <=Y and H the rest. The exact inverse checks are

    sum_(d in H,d|m)chi(m/d)a_d=b_m,
    b_m=-sum_(d in E,d|m)mu(d)chi(d)chi(m/d), m in H.

The restricted incidence matrix has inverse mu(m/d)chi(m/d) because H is divisor-interval convex. Its unique summatory dual is

    lambda_m=sum_(k<=N/m,(k,m)=1)mu(k)chi(k),
    M_chi(N)=M_chi(Y)+sum_(m in H)lambda_m b_m.          (R1)

The moving coprimality and natural zeros remain literal. For Y=floor(sqrt N), the exposed sum costs at most sqrt N, and every dual argument is short. This does not make its full scalar cheap.

For independent row errors of maximum magnitude1, the exact scalar norm is sum_H|lambda_m|. All squarefree unit m>N/2 have lambda_m=1. Thus for Y<=N/2 it lies between kappa_q N/2-O_q(sqrt N) and N(1+log N). The lower bound survives adding every convolution row through N, squareful rows and zero information, since terminal unknown m appears only in its own row. This is a norm obstruction, not a lower bound on the signed arithmetic sum.

The strongest objection to a mere worst-case certificate is answered using the actual coefficients. Every terminal unramified prime p has lambda_p=1 and b_p=-chi(p). For P_N=sum_H|lambda_m b_m|, therefore, an all-N bound P_N=O(N^gamma), gamma<1, would force convergence of sum_p1/p by grouping primes into dyadic intervals. Euler's finite-product argument contradicts that. Conversely P_N<=N(1+log N)^2. Hence its limsup exponent is exactly1 for every fixed chi and every choice1<=Y_N<=N/2. This is not a pointwise linear lower bound and not a signed lower bound. It specifically rejects paying R1 by its complete absolute coefficient price.

A fixed-character M bound can control lambda's moving prime omissions using an explicit finite Euler removal, with product_(p|m)(1-p^-alpha)^-1=N^o(1) uniformly for m<=N and fixed alpha>0. The proof is included, so no arbitrary growing-conductor theorem is assumed. It still supplies no strict gain in the summed absolute price.

The surviving complete signed target is

    |sum_(m squarefree,(m,q)=1,sqrt N<m<=N)lambda_m b_m|
       <<_(chi,epsilon) N^(gamma+epsilon)              (R2)

for every epsilon and all large N, common 1/2<gamma<gamma0. R1 and sqrt-N payment return exactly the original M bound. The usual absolutely convergent inverse identity on Re(s)>1, followed by partial summation and holomorphic continuation, excludes every zero on Re(s)>gamma. Write L=log X, Y=floor(X^.495), b(ell)=(-1)^(ell+1),
m_Y(n)=mu(n)1_(n<=Y), u_Y=mu-m_Y and q_2=delta_1-2delta_2.
Since mu*b=q_2, the exact convolution identity is

    u_Y*u_Y*b=A-2(m_Y*q_2)+m_Y*m_Y*b.                      (G4)

With S_tau(y)=sum_(ell>=1)b(ell)g_tau(log(ell/y)), it gives

    G_tau(x)=R_Y(x)+2L_Y(x)-I_Y(x),
    R_Y(x)=sum_(d,e>Y)mu(d)mu(e)S_tau(x/(de)),
    I_Y(x)=sum_(d,e<=Y)mu(d)mu(e)S_tau(x/(de)).            (G5)

L_Y is the short m_Y*q_2 term, supported at n<=2Y. Shared primes,
zero Möbius coefficients, both strict lower cuts and every alternating
restoration sign remain literal. The short Gaussian term is not zero.
On [X,2X] it is at most

    O_tau(Y exp(-(.505L-log2)^2/(2tau))),                  (G6)

and hence smaller than every fixed negative power of X. Absolute
convergence before cancellation follows from the d_3(n) majorant.

Here is the estimate that permits growing cutoffs without an unspecified
smoothness constant. Extend h(t)=g_tau(log t) by zero for t<=0. It is
Schwartz and flat at zero. Cauchy's formula on |z-t|=t/2 gives

    ||h^(m)||_1 <= K_tau 4^m m! exp(tau*(m-1)^2/2),
    K_tau=exp((pi^2/8+(log2)^2/2)/tau), m>=1.             (G7)

To check the constant, substitute t=e^v after Cauchy's formula and bound
exp((log2)|v|/tau) by the sum of its two signed exponentials. The two
Gaussian integrals give exactly the extra factor converting 2^m to4^m.
Alternating Poisson summation samples half-integers, so for m>=2,

       *exp(-(m-1)log y+tau*(m-1)^2/2).                  (G8)

Complete the ell sum before imposing an ell cutoff. With one common

statement:
### B1. Proof with all offsets, tails, and mixed terms

For each r in{1,...,H}, partition the integer line into blocks(k-H,k] whose positive right endpoints k are congruent to r modulo H, and use the zero extension on the initial partial block. Set

  V_r(x)=sum_{k>=1,k congruent r mod H} B_H(k)g_tau(log(k/x)).

The total variation of t -> g_tau(log(t/x)) on(0,infinity) is2g_tau(0). On one block, replacing each value at n by its right endpoint value costs at most H times the variation on that block. Summing disjoint blocks proves

  |F_a(x)-V_r(x)|<=2H*g_tau(0)

uniformly in x. This pays the complete replacement error, including the first block and both infinite tails; no summatory cancellation was used.

For u=log(x/X) in[0,ell] and v=log(k/X), the Cauchy weight quotient is

  g_tau(v-u)^2 / exp(-v^2/(4*tau))
    =(2*pi*tau)^(-1) exp(-3v^2/(4*tau)+2uv/tau-u^2/tau).

As a function of t=k/X this is positive and unimodal. Its integral over t>0 equals

  exp(tau/3+4u/3+u^2/(3*tau))/sqrt(3*pi*tau),

and its supremum is exp(u^2/(3*tau))/(2*pi*tau). A positive unimodal function sampled on a grid of spacing H/X has sum at most(X/H) times its integral plus twice its supremum: split at the maximum and compare each monotone tail with adjacent grid integrals. Thus the quotient sum on every offset grid is at most K_tau*(X/H+1).

Writing E_r=sum_{k congruent r}|B_H(k)|^2w_X(k), Cauchy gives |V_r(x)|<=sqrt(K_tau*(X/H+1)*E_r). Average the identity F_a=V_r+error over all r and apply Jensen to sqrt(E_r). Since H^(-1)sum_r E_r=E_a, inequality(B) follows. This proves a supremum, so the log-shell L2 norm is also at most sqrt(log2) times its right side. No omitted cross terms are estimated as though positive.

For clarity the EXACT arithmetic content of E is

  E_a(X,H)=(1/H) sum_{|h|<H}
    sum_{n>=max(1,1-h)} a(n)conjugate(a(n+h))
    *sum_{j=max(0,h)}^{min(H-1,H-1+h)}w_X(n+j).       (L)

Indeed B_H(k)=sum_{j=0}^{H-1}a(k-j); write n=k-j and h=j-l in its square. All sums converge absolutely. Formula(L) includes every diagonal, both signs of every lag, and the exact moving weight. Replacing the inner weight by(H-|h|)w_X(n) would introduce an error not used or hidden here. A bounded exact check accompanies the report solely to guard these indices, not to certify the analytic theorem.

statement:
## 4. Uniform negative lines and all completion errors

For 1<=j<=K, the completed face is

    T_{j,K}(y)=sum_{ell>=1} chi^{*(j-1)}(ell)phi_r(log(ell/y)).

Its initial Mellin integrand is

    exp(tau s^2/2)(1-s)^r L(s,chi)^(j-1)y^s.              (4)

The only potential pole of L is the principal pole at 1; its order j-1 is canceled because r>=j-1. Imprimitive Euler factors multiply this expression and are not removed. Zeros introduce no division. Thus the multiplier in (4) is entire. For fixed finite X,K and any finite horizontal width, ordinary vertical growth and Gaussian decay justify the full contour shift before estimating its dependence on K and the new line. No exchange of an infinite-height limit with an uncontrolled growing order is needed.

Here is an independent derivation of the critical negative-line estimate. For a primitive character of conductor q0 and parity a0 in {0,1}, its completed functional equation gives

    L(s,chi0)=omega (q0/pi)^(1/2-s)
        Gamma((1-s+a0)/2)/Gamma((s+a0)/2) L(1-s,bar chi0),

where |omega|=1. Reflection and duplication turn the Gamma ratio into

    2^s Gamma(1-s)/sqrt(pi) times sin(pi s/2) or cos(pi s/2).

At s=-B+it, B>=1, the Gamma integral yields

    |Gamma(B+1-it)| <= Gamma(B+1),

the trigonometric factor is at most exp(pi|t|/2), and the right-hand L-series is bounded by zeta(1+B)<=zeta(2). All remaining conductor factors are bounded by C_{q0}^{B+1}. For an imprimitive character, each extra factor has modulus at most 1+p^B<=2p^B, giving a fixed product absorbed in C_q^{B+1}. The same formula includes primitive conductor 1, namely zeta. Therefore

    |L(-B+it,chi)| <= C_q^{B+1} Gamma(B+1) exp(pi|t|/2).  (5)

This is uniform for all real B>=1 and all heights, with q fixed. The Gamma integral bound is deliberately coarse but valid; it is not a fixed-B Stirling estimate being reused at a moving B.

On the shifted line, bound |1+B-it|^r by (B+1)^r exp(K|t|/(B+1)). Raising (5) to j-1 gives a linear |t| exponent O(K). Integrating it against exp(-tau t^2/2) costs exp(O_tau(K^2)). The remaining factors, using log Gamma(B+1)<=O((B+1)log(B+2)), give

    |T_{j,K}(y)| <= exp(-B log y + tau B^2/2
       + C_{q,tau}[K(B+1)log(B+2)+K^2+Klog(K+2)]).        (6)

This bound is uniform in j and includes the j=1 face. It does not take a finite logarithm of a zero kernel. If y>=exp(Z), choose B=Z/tau for sufficiently large Z. The first two terms are at most -Z^2/(2tau), so

    |T_{j,K}(y)| <= exp(-Z^2/(2tau)
       +C_{q,tau}[K(Z+1)log(Z+2)+K^2+Klog(K+2)]).         (7)

In band I with Z=V or W, the negative scale is L^(4/3), whereas KZlog Z=O(Llog L). In band II it is L(log L)^2, whereas KZlog Z=O(Llog L), K^2=O(L/(log L)^2), and Klog K=O(sqrt(L)). Thus in both bands it beats every fixed multiple of L uniformly after a q,tau-dependent threshold.

All four discarded regions are paid as follows.

1. For every lower face j<K, its short product is at most Y^(K-1)<=Xe^(-V), so y=x/product>=e^V. There are at most Y^j tuples. Summing every binomial coefficient and all j costs exp(O(L+K)); (7) absorbs this.
2. In the all-large term, the full product n is at least (Y+1)^K>Xe^V. For x<=2X, v=log(n/x)>V-log 2. Bound its absolute coefficient by d_{2K-1}(n). Split (3)'s Gaussian in two; one half supplies exp(-c_tau V^2), and the other is at most C_tau exp(-2v). The complete remaining sum is x^2 zeta(2)^(2K-1). This pays every plain factor and the entire product tail.
3. For short products below Xe^(-W), (7) applies with Z=W. Their number is at most Y^K<=exp(L+V), again absorbed.
4. For short products above 2Xe^W, y=x/product<e^(-W). Thus log(ell/y)>W for every plain product ell>=1. The same split Gaussian and ell^(-2) sum give a bound exp(-c_tau W^2+O(Klog K+K)) times the number of short tuples. No unestimated plain-factor cutoff remains.

Consequently, for every fixed A>0, in both bands,

    sup_{X<=x<=2X} |F_{K-1}(x)-C^bal_{X,K}(x)|
        =O_{A,q,tau}(X^(-A)),                             (8)

with the sign and source defined by (1)--(2). The same estimates separately bound C-C^bal and F_r-C. This matters when the later Mellin bound is first applied to the uncapped C. No subunit Mertens hypothesis was used in this completion theorem.

More generally, these particular bounds suffice when K tends to infinity and K^2 log L=o(L), together with a future-compatible choice of order family. This is a sufficient asymptotic comparison, not an optimal boundary or an impossibility statement at equality.
