buffered Mertens consequence. This report does not assert S3 on the
boundary beta=theta_G, does not make its constants uniform as eta
tends to zero, and does not identify the new endpoint's pending formal
replay with a completed kernel receipt.

Here is the needed uniform dependence on r; it is not a hereditary
bound asserted for an arbitrary masked coefficient family. Define h_r
by its local generating factors, z=p^(-s):

    H_{r,p}(z)=(1-z)^(-2),                 p|3r;
    H_{r,p}(z)=(1-2z)/(1-z)^2,             p not |3r.

The latter equals 1-sum_{j>=2}(j-1)z^j. The exact finite coefficient
identity is f_r=h_r*mu. At beta>1/2 its absolute norm satisfies

    B_r(beta):=sum_a |h_r(a)|a^(-beta)
      = product_{p|3r}(1-p^(-beta))^(-2)
        product_{p not |3r}
           [1+p^(-2beta)/(1-p^(-beta))^2]
      <= C_beta product_{p|r}(1-p^(-beta))^(-2)
      <= C_(beta,delta) r^delta                         (S4)

for every fixed delta>0. The second product converges because
2beta>1. For the last inequality, the factor at sufficiently large p
is <=p^delta; the finite set of smaller primes contributes one fixed
constant. Prime 3 is always in the first product, and prime 2 is
handled by the displayed applicable local factor. There is no division
by 1-2*2^(-s), hence no hidden prime-two pole in this bound.

Finite convolution of S3 gives, for every t>=1,

    |sum_{n<=t}f_r(n)| <= C_beta t^beta B_r(beta).       (S5)

For 0<t<1 this sum is zero. Abel summation over the entire half-line,
with both endpoint limits paid by the Gaussian, then gives

    |F_r(y)| <= C_(beta,tau) B_r(beta)y^beta,
    E_r(Y) <= C_(beta,tau)B_r(beta)^2 Y^(2beta).         (S6)

Indeed the derivative integral is
y^beta integral_R e^(beta v)|g_tau'(v)|dv<infinity.
The same proof works for each fixed log derivative. Independently,
|f_r|=1 gives the UNIFORM-IN-r left-tail estimate

    |F_r(y)| <= C_(A,tau)y^A, 0<y<=2, for every A>0.   (S7)

This estimate, not an r-dependent bound carried to arbitrarily large
r, pays the entire small-scale tail below.

## 2. Exact full signed gcd sector, before any positivity step

For real D>=1 define the including-diagonal signed scalar

    T_>=D(X)=sum_{gcd(m,n)>=D} f(m)f(n)K_X(m,n).        (S8)

Write m=ga,n=gb with (a,b)=1 and insert
1_{(a,b)=1}=sum_{q|a,b}mu(q). Equation S2 gives the exact identity

    T_>=D(X)=sum_{g>=D}sum_{q>=1}mu(q) E_{gq}(X/(gq))
            =sum_{r>=1} A_D(r)E_r(X/r),
    A_D(r)=sum_{g|r,g>=D}mu(r/g).                       (S9)

Each square contains the WHOLE f_{gq} field, not a selected positive
subfamily of the original f correlation. Its sign in S9 is mu(q).
The crucial cancellation f_g(q)^2=1 is performed on the actual
coefficients before estimating the squares. The integer condition
g>=D is literal, equivalent to g>=ceil(D).

Absolute rearrangement is legitimate before the signed cancellation.
For fixed x in [X,2X], a positive majorant is

    sum_{r>=1}d(r)[sum_{u>=1}g(log(ru/x))]^2<infinity.

The inner sum is O_tau(x/r) when r<=2X and is O_(A,tau)((x/r)^A)
for r>2X. Therefore the majorant is locally integrable, including all
q,g and all prime powers. This justifies Fubini and S9 with no finite
cap, no tail assumed away and no infinite-series continuation.

**Theorem S-GCD.** For every epsilon>0, uniformly for X>=2 and ALL
real D>=1,

    |T_>=D(X)| <= C_(beta,tau,epsilon)
                        X^(2beta+epsilon)D^(1-2beta).  (S10)

Proof: first take the r=gq<=X part of the absolute majorant in S9.
By S4--S6, B_r^2<=C_epsilon X^epsilon, so this part is bounded by

    C X^(2beta+epsilon)
        sum_{g>=D}g^(-2beta)sum_{q>=1}q^(-2beta)
     <= C X^(2beta+epsilon)D^(1-2beta).

If D>X that first part is empty. For r>X use S7 and |A_D(r)|<=d(r).
With R=max(X,D), any A>beta+1, and a sufficiently small delta>0,
the remainder is at most

    C X^(2A) sum_{r>=R} d(r)r^(-2A)
      <= C_delta X^(2A)R^(1-2A+delta).

When D<=X this is O(X^(1+delta)), absorbed by the proposed bound
because D^(1-2beta)>=X^(1-2beta). When D>X, division by
X^(2beta+epsilon)D^(1-2beta) leaves at most X^(delta-epsilon),
provided delta<=epsilon and 2A-2beta>delta. This proves S10 uniformly,
even for D larger than every prescribed power of X.

### 2.1 The true diagonal and the complete complement

The diagonal retained by S8 is precisely

    Delta_>=D(X)=sum_{n>=D}K_X(n,n)>=0.                 (S11)

It satisfies the same S10 bound without the epsilon: for D<=X use
Delta_all=O_tau(X); for D>X use the Gaussian bound
K_X(n,n)<=C_A(X/n)^(2A) and sum it, choosing A>beta. Thus the actual
off-diagonal sector

    Q_>=D(X)=sum_{m!=n;gcd(m,n)>=D}f(m)f(n)K_X(m,n)

also satisfies S10 after subtracting S11. No sign is assigned to
Q_>=D, T_>=D or their complements.

Let Q_<D use the exact complementary conditions m!=n, gcd(m,n)<D.
Then, for every fixed theta>0,

    Q_off(X)=Q_<X^theta(X)
       +O_epsilon(X^(2beta-(2beta-1)theta+epsilon)).    (S12)

All ordered cross terms between the original integers remain in
exactly one of these two scalar sectors. There is no field partition
whose mixed terms have been omitted.

For a desired gamma>1/2, choose

    theta > (2beta-2gamma)/(2beta-1).                   (S13)

Then OPEN-F3 is equivalent to the ONE-SIDED estimate
Q_<X^theta(X)<=C_epsilon X^(2gamma+epsilon), for every epsilon>0
and all sufficiently large dyadic X. Necessity and sufficiency both
follow from S12 and its absolute error, allowing a smaller epsilon in
the fixed strict margin. Current-proof G25--G31 then supplies the
already proved complete zero-exclusion return c=1-gamma. No new c is
proved here because this remaining signed estimate is OPEN.

The inherited beta=.8749, gamma=.87449, theta=.0011 gives exponent
1.74897522, matching the numerical exponent of W36 but for this
DIFFERENT actual f3 sector. Using beta=.87489=theta_G+.0000034 gives
1.748955242, below 1.74898 by .000024758. In the limit beta down to
theta_G (a limiting threshold, not a boundary-line bound), S13 is:

| Desired gamma | Strict lower threshold for theta |
| --- | --- |
| .87449 | 661/624811 = .001057919914982... |
| 5/6 | 623299/5623299 = .110842229801403... |
| 3/4 | 624433/1874433 = .333131672351052... |

For any chosen theta strictly beyond the displayed limiting value,
choose a fixed sufficiently small eta>0 first, then epsilon. Neither
eta nor beta varies with X.

### 2.2 Both height variables

S9 is derived in the physical variable, so no height interaction is
ever deleted. For an explicit height readout, on any fixed a>1 put

    D_r(s)=sum_n f_r(n)n^(-s),
    B_r(t)=exp(tau(a+it)^2/2)D_r(a+it),
    J_a(v)=integral_0^log2 exp((2a+iv)u)du.

Absolute Mellin inversion gives

    E_r(Y)=Y^(2a)/(2pi)^2 integral_R integral_R
      B_r(t)conj(B_r(t'))Y^(i(t-t'))J_a(t-t') dt dt'.   (S14)

One may keep a>1 here; no shifted-contour statement is needed for the
sector theorem. S9 therefore contains every r, both independent t,t',
and the same local-window kernel J_a. Replacing the double integral by
t=t', or dropping signed mu(q), is not part of the proof.

## 3. The remaining signed problem and a paid prime-switch error

Two exact forms of the complete low-gcd complement are useful.
First, without any positive squares or auxiliary divisor insertion,

    Q_<D(X)=2 sum_{1<=g<D} sum_{h>=1}
       sum_{a>=1;(a,h)=1}
          f_g(a(a+h)) K_{X/g}(a,a+h).                  (S15)

The equality uses b=a+h and coprimality (a,b)=(a,h)=1, so
f_g(a)f_g(a+h)=f_g(a(a+h)). The factor 2 restores both orders.
There are no diagonal terms in S15. Every h and all prime powers in
a(a+h) remain. This is an actual signed shifted-correlation target,
not the absolute sum of the shifted correlations.

Second, including its precisely specified small diagonal,

    T_<D(X)=sum_{r>=1} a_D(r)E_r(X/r),
    a_D(r)=sum_{g|r,g<D}mu(r/g),
    Q_<D=T_<D-Delta_<D.                                (S16)

For D>1, a_D(1)=1; for 1<r<D, a_D(r)=0; for r>=D,
a_D(r)=-A_D(r). If D=2, then a_D(r)=mu(r). The actual open scalar
therefore already has a signed outer sum of whole nonnegative
energies. Bounding every E_r and summing its absolute coefficient
gives the old exponent, including the r=1 copy of the unknown E_1.
This is the precise point where an apparent positive-square reduction
fails to create a gain. It is not an impossibility theorem about S15.

The following coefficient-aware estimate strengthens this reduction
without pretending to control that r=1 term.

For p not dividing 3r, define

    U_{r,p}(y)=sum_{n>=1;p not |n} f_r(n)g(log(n/y)),
    V_{r,p}(y)=sum_{j>=1}U_{r,p}(y/p^j).

The local p coefficients give EXACTLY

    F_r=U_{r,p}-V_{r,p},
    F_{rp}=U_{r,p}+V_{r,p},
    E_{rp}(Y)-E_r(Y)
       =4 integral_Y^(2Y)U_{r,p}(y)V_{r,p}(y)dy/y.     (S17)

Every prime power p^j is in V, and the V^2 terms cancel before any
absolute value is taken. In particular S17 is a signed covariance;
there is no general sign assertion or deletion of its negative part.

The coefficient series for U_{r,p} divided by the mu series has the
same factors as S4 except that its p factor is (1-z)^(-1).
Since (1-p^(-beta))^(-1) is uniformly bounded for p>=2, S4--S6 give

    |U_{r,p}(y)| <= C_(beta,tau,delta)r^delta y^beta,
    |V_{r,p}(y)| <= C r^delta y^beta
                            p^(-beta)/(1-p^(-beta)).

Thus, uniformly in r,p,Y,

    |E_{rp}(Y)-E_r(Y)|
          <= C_delta r^delta Y^(2beta)p^(-beta).       (S18)

Delta in S18 is arbitrary after renaming the exponent in the squared
S4 bound. The full prime-power tail j>J is bounded in exactly the
same way with p^(-beta) replaced by p^(-(J+1)beta).

Let P>=3 and let s_P(r)=product_{p<=P}p^v_p(r), the COMPLETE small-
prime part. Telescoping the switches at the distinct primes >P gives

    |E_r(Y)-E_{s_P(r)}(Y)|
        <= C_delta r^delta Y^(2beta)
                          sum_{p|r;p>P}p^(-beta).     (S19)

This is a direct estimate on the literal arithmetic family. It is not
an unrestricted operator norm or a comparison with an invented
independent-sign sequence.

**Theorem S-STATE.** For any fixed delta>0 sufficiently small, uniformly
in D>=1, P>=3 and X>=2,

    | T_<D(X)
       -sum_{r>=1}a_D(r)E_{s_P(r)}(X/r) |
          <= C_delta X^(2beta)P^(1-3beta+delta).        (S20)

Proof: |a_D(r)|<=d(r). Insert S19, absorb its r-loss and d(r) into
r^delta (choosing the earlier losses smaller), and sum absolutely:

    X^(2beta) sum_{r>=1}r^(-2beta+delta)
                          sum_{p|r;p>P}p^(-beta)
      = X^(2beta) zeta(2beta-delta)
                          sum_{p>P}p^(-3beta+delta)
      <= C_delta X^(2beta)P^(1-3beta+delta).

Choose delta<min(2beta-1,3beta-1). Using all integers to bound the
last prime sum is sufficient; no prime theorem is used. This is also
the complete error in the off-diagonal version after subtracting the
UNCHANGED Delta_<D. It includes every switch covariance in S17 and
all prime-power tails.

For P=X^kappa, this error lies below X^(2gamma) if

    kappa > (2beta-2gamma)/(3beta-1),                   (S21)

with a strict margin for delta. For beta=.87489, gamma=.87449,
kappa=.0005 gives exponent 1.748967665 before the selectable loss.
The inherited beta=.8749 can instead use kappa=.00051, yielding
1.748971403. The limiting thresholds as beta down to theta_G are
.000488225288765... for gamma=.87449, .051153191168596... for 5/6,
and .153738770418274... for 3/4. These are ERROR thresholds, not
proved bounds for the remaining scalar.

Putting S12 and S20 together gives a fully paid equivalent target at
any theta,kappa satisfying their strict inequalities:

    L_{D,P}(X):=sum_r a_D(r)E_{s_P(r)}(X/r),
    Q_off(X)=L_{D,P}(X)-Delta_all(X)
               +T_>=D(X)+O(X^(2beta)P^(1-3beta+delta)). (S22)

Consequently a one-sided X^(2gamma+epsilon) estimate for L_{D,P}, with
D=X^theta and P=X^kappa, would suffice and is equivalent within these
paid errors. The fixed original f3 detector is what enters the zero
return: the moving P is never inserted into a claimed fixed Mellin
transform.

**Important limit of S22.** It is not a lower-complexity theorem for
the unknown detector merely because its auxiliary labels use small
primes. The r=1 summand is still E_1(X), and absolute estimation of all
other r yields only the already paid tail. An independent argument
must exploit the complete scalar S15 or a genuinely new joint
covariance estimate. S20 quantitatively pays high-prime CHANGES in the
auxiliary fields; it does not pay their common unsolved component.
Large primes remain in every base f3 coefficient; only the locations
where that base prime sign has been switched to +1 are simplified.

When P>=D, there is a further exact bookkeeping factorization. Write
r=st with s P-smooth and all prime factors of t>P. Then

    a_D(st)=a_D(s)mu(t),
    L_{D,P}(X)=sum_{s P-smooth}a_D(s)
                  sum_{t P-rough}mu(t)E_s(X/(st)).     (S23)

If t has a square factor its right side and left side are both zero,
because every g<D dividing r lies wholly in s. The identity retains
all smooth prime powers and the exact g<D edge. Removing the rough
Möbius filter, changing its scale while freezing the wrong P, or
declaring it contractive would add an unpaid assertion. S23 does not
improve the preceding limit.

## 4. Exact rational rays: successful cancellation, bounded reach

This was tested as an alternative to the self-containing square sum
S16. It removes the f_r fields entirely from its inner arithmetic sum.
Let (a,b)=1, R=rad(ab/3^v_3(ab)), and define the WHOLE ray scalar

    Ray_{a,b}(X)=sum_{d>=1} f(ad)f(bd)K_X(ad,bd).

At every p|R, exactly one of a,b contains p. The two coefficients
therefore give the exact local factor 2*1_{p|d}-1. Thus

    f(ad)f(bd)=product_{p|R}(2*1_{p|d}-1)
       =mu(R)sum_{k|R;k|d}(-2)^omega(k).               (S24)

This is true for every prime exponent of a,b,d; prime 3 contributes
nothing. Set nu=tau/2 and

    T_nu(y)=sum_{l>=1}g_nu(log(l/y)).

The original Gaussian product identity now gives the exact finite
divisor readout

    Ray_{a,b}(X)=mu(R)g_{2tau}(log(a/b))
       sum_{k|R}(-2)^omega(k)
          integral_0^log2 T_nu(Xe^u/(k sqrt(ab)))du.    (S25)

No positivity was used in obtaining S24--25. Its average coefficient
over one period R is the signed rational number

    c(a,b)=product_{p|R}(2/p-1).                        (S26)

In particular c(a,b)=0 whenever 2 divides ab. If R=2Q with Q odd,
the inner expansion can instead retain the prime-two sign exactly:

    Ray_{a,b}(X)=mu(R)g_{2tau}(log(a/b))
       sum_{k|Q}(-2)^omega(k)
          integral_0^log2 S_nu(Xe^u/(k sqrt(ab)))du,    (S27)

where S_nu(y)=sum_{l>=1}(-1)^(l+1)g_nu(log(l/y)).
Every k is odd, so the alternating sign survives d=kl unchanged.

For each fixed N, Poisson summation of the Schwartz function
t -> g_nu(log t), extended by zero for t<=0, gives

    T_nu(y)=e^(nu/2)y+O_(N,nu)(y^(-N)),
    S_nu(y)=O_(N,nu)(y^(-N)),                    y>=1. (S28)

The zero extension is smooth and flat at zero; each ordinary
derivative is a polynomial in log t times a power of t^-1 and the
Gaussian, hence rapidly decreasing at both ends. The Fourier tails
in ordinary Poisson and in its half-integer translate prove S28.
This is the same fixed-order Poisson mechanism already validated for
the W35 profile, applied to nu=tau/2, not a new analytic-tail principle.

It follows, uniformly when R sqrt(ab)<=X^(1-delta), delta>0 fixed,
that

    Ray_{a,b}(X)
      =e^(tau/4) X/sqrt(ab) g_{2tau}(log(a/b))c(a,b)
       +O_(N,tau)(3^omega(R) X^(-delta N)).             (S29)

The main constant uses integral_0^log2 e^u du=1. Summing S29 over
ANY subset of these coprime rays still gives an arbitrarily negative
power error after choosing N: there are at most O(X^2 log X) pairs,
R<=X, and 3^omega(R)<=R^2. In particular the COMPLETE sector

    (a,b)=1, a!=b, 2|ab,
    rad(ab/3^v_3(ab))*sqrt(ab)<=X^(1-delta),
    m=ad,n=bd, d>=1

has signed scalar O_(A,delta,tau)(X^(-A)) for every A>0. Both signs
and ALL common-multiplier values d are essential. A sharp truncation
in d would create endpoint terms; none is silently discarded here.

### 4.1 The first decisive size test

This exact cancellation does NOT reach the central primitive-pair
region. In fact its entire low-radical ray sector is already cheap
by a positive count, making it unsuitable as the main new saving.
For T>=1 and every s>1/3,

    sum_{(a,b)=1;R(ab)sqrt(ab)<=T}sum_{d>=1}K_X(ad,bd)
                  <= C_(s,tau) X T^s.                (S30)

To prove this, sum the common multiplier using T_nu(y)<=C_nu y,
valid for all y>0, and bound g_{2tau} by its maximum. There are
2^omega(n) ordered coprime factorizations ab=n, including every
prime power. Rankin's inequality reduces the desired weighted count
to T^s times

    sum_n 2^omega(n) R(n)^(-s)n^(-(1+s)/2),
    R(n)=rad(n/3^v_3(n)).

Its local factor at 3 is
1+2*3^(-(1+s)/2)/(1-3^(-(1+s)/2)). At p!=3 it is

    1+2*p^(-(1+3s)/2)/(1-p^(-(1+s)/2)).

The product converges precisely in the sufficient region s>1/3.
Hence with T=X^(1-delta), S30 costs only
X^(4/3-delta/3+epsilon), already below all three advertised near,
5/6 and 3/4 scalar targets. The stronger alternating-ray theorem is
real arithmetic cancellation, but does not enlarge the currently
unpaid region at those targets.

For the genuinely hard rays a,b comparable to X and essentially
squarefree, R sqrt(ab) is of size X^3 while the common-multiplier
scale X/sqrt(ab) is of size 1. S28 cannot be used there. Estimating
each divisor term in S25 separately loses the original signs and
returns an error of order one per ray, potentially X^(2+epsilon)
in total. Thus the promising next calculation is a JOINT signed sum
of S25 over those a,b (or equivalently S15 over balanced shifts),
not another one-ray periodic average. No such joint bound is proved
in this report.

The special ray a=b=1 is the actual diagonal; S29 gives its sharper
check

    Delta_all(X)=e^(tau/4)g_{2tau}(0)X+O_A(X^(-A)).     (S31)

It is excluded from the off-diagonal sector above. S31 is a constant
check, not an improved moment estimate.

## 5. What is new here, what was reused, and the next live estimate

The main gain in this bounded attack is S10--S13: a direct estimate for
an ACTUAL f3 scalar sector that the existing W36 result explicitly did
not cover. It comes with a uniform modified-coefficient proof, all
prime powers, all common divisors, the diagonal, the entire tail,
both heights, and the full signed complement. It supplies no complete
moment exponent. Its numerical threshold resembles W36 because both
ultimately sum a common-factor weight of degree -2beta, but the
underlying arithmetic sources and masks are different.

S17--S21 add an exact prime-switch covariance and a quantitative
P^(1-3beta) source-change error, before making any positive estimate.
This provides a usable bound for such changes inside the actual
Möbius expansion, not a claim that its unsolved common component is
smaller. The exact shifted target S15 is preferable to treating the
r=1 self-copy in S22 as a solution.

The following components are reused or elementary adaptations:

- MG9--16 already provide the buffered Mertens/coprimality mechanism
  and Möbius extraction of an original-source gcd. S4 proves the
  different all-prime-power f_r multiplier required here; no new
  general Möbius-inversion principle is claimed.
- [private research revision] GC1--GC20 and its independent review already establish the
  fixed f3 detector, its original-cell comparison and complete
  zero-exclusion return. Their inverse kernels and all-dyad
  equivalence are imported, not rederived as a new result.
- W36/R36.4 pays an aggregate shared-prime overlap in FOUR ORIGINAL
  squarefree factors. S10 is not inferred by restricting that signed
  estimate. It is proved directly for the TWO full f3 integers.
- W35's fixed-order Gaussian Poisson mechanism supplies S28. The
  rational-ray arithmetic identity and its zero prime-two mean are
  checked here, but S30 demonstrates the limited reach of that route.
- The attempt index and its [private research revision]--52/early/late subdivisions were
  inspected for gcd extraction, valuation/dilation, signed incidence,
  prime-state, shifted-correlation and Gaussian predecessors. No
  priority in the external literature is asserted.

The first unpaid calculation is specific. For a chosen gamma and
theta satisfying S13, estimate the ENTIRE signed S15 on all large
dyadic X at exponent 2gamma. In the difficult part, g can be 1,
a and h are both comparable to X, and a(a+h) has a large radical.
Neither the periodic average in d, the high-gcd bound, nor the
auxiliary-prime switch bound supplies cancellation there. A purported
joint estimate must retain f_g(a(a+h)), (a,h)=1, the actual Gaussian
weight, and the complete sum of shifts. Replacing the signs by a
character, independent random variables or a positive majorant would
change this arithmetic problem.

This is a real remaining arithmetic estimate, not a missing source-
comparison or analytic-tail condition. The near gamma=.87449 target
and the larger gamma=5/6 and 3/4 targets remain open.

## 6. Evidence and freeze record

The adjacent `arithmetic-check.py` uses only exact integers and rational
numbers. Its readback `arithmetic-check.json` records all checks true:
8,000 coefficient/convolution pairs; 18,000 nested coefficient triples;
seven exact finite gcd/shift cutoffs (including a noninteger cutoff and
an empty high-gcd range); 121 prime-switch identities with every
available prime-power term; 17,950 rational-ray coefficient cases;
nine exact full-period means; and 2,000 small-prime-factorization cases.

Those finite tests check transcription and endpoints. They do not
prove S3, the asymptotic estimates, a new zero-free constant, or formal
kernel acceptance. The analytic evidence is the displayed proof.

## 3. Uniform row completion with the actual forced scale

Let \(\psi_{\mathfrak h}\) be primitive at every good prime of \(\mathfrak h\), extended by zero there. Since \(\xi\) is nonprincipal and has coprime fixed conductor, \(\xi\psi_{\mathfrak h}\) has zero complete mean, including when \(\mathfrak h=1\). Multiplication of the row by a good element coprime to \(\mathfrak h\) changes only a unit scalar in the character.

For every \(h>0\), a rotation of the profile in (XM6) obeys
\[
\left|\sum_{m\in\mathcal O}
\xi(m)\psi_{\mathfrak h}(m)f_v(m/\sqrt h)\right|
\ll (1+|v|)^{J_0}\min(\sqrt{q_{\mathfrak h}},h).
\tag{XM10}
\]
The term at zero is zero because the profile is supported away from zero.

For the first bound, Poisson gives, up to fixed constants and a fixed rotation, the majorant
\[
\frac h{\sqrt{q_{\mathfrak h}}}
\sum_{\ell\ne0}
\left|\widehat f_v\!\left(\sqrt{h/q_{\mathfrak h}}\,\ell\right)\right|.
\tag{XM11}
\]
If \(h/q_{\mathfrak h}\le1\), two-dimensional lattice counting and a fixed Schwartz seminorm bound the sum by \(O((1+|v|)^{J_0}q_{\mathfrak h}/h)\). If \(h/q_{\mathfrak h}\ge1\), choose Fourier decay of order greater than two; the result is again at most \(O((1+|v|)^{J_0}\sqrt{q_{\mathfrak h}})\). Fixed calibration levels change only the constants in these comparisons.

For the second bound, direct lattice counting in the fixed annulus gives \(O(h)\) when \(h\ge1\). For \(h<1\), the sum is empty below a fixed positive scale; on the remaining bounded interval, increasing the fixed constant gives the same \(O(h)\) estimate. No zero vector is counted. This proves (XM10).

In particular, for \(0\le\rho\le1\),
\[
|\mathrm{row}(h)|
\ll (1+|v|)^{J_0}
q_{\mathfrak h}^{(1-\rho)/2}h^\rho.
\tag{XM12}
\]
The proof never drops the divisor inside \(h\).

# [private research revision]: an actual old/new detector transfer with paid prime tails

The [W42 author](wild42/report.md) and [independent review](wild42-review/report.md)
establish a two-way transfer between PR9's literal principal signal and the
ideal Möbius Gaussian. The controller accepts these complete source identities,
their quantitative tails and the reviewer additions below. They make the
user's original mix-and-match proposal concrete for these arithmetic sources.
They prove no improved complete moment or additional c. The fixed-family
calibration used here is written c5=.125136, with new kernels still pending.

## 1. Literal source identity and both norm directions

Fix K=Q(omega), one original finite-order trivial-infinity Hecke character
eta and its fixed finite exclusions S. All coefficient zeros remain. At a
prime ideal outside S put Q=Np, t=Q^-1, D=eta(p)Q^-s and
R=conjugate(alpha(p))^6 eta(p)^6 Q^(3-6s), using PR9's primary-generator phase.
PR9 B0.35 and B0.36 give exactly

    H_p=(1-t^2)[1+t(D-R)/(1-D)]/(1-R),
    C_S=product_(p notin S)(1-Q^-2), H=C_S h,
    Mellin(P_eta)(s)=exp((s-5/6)^2) H(s)/L_K^S(s,eta),
    P_eta(x)=x^k f_eta(x).                              ([restricted research revision]-P1)

This is the principal signal, not the physical probe J_eta, its compensator
or J_eta-f_eta. The Euler H is also distinct from the short-divisor H
hypothesis. Its constant C_S differs from the physical residue scalar c_S.

For every sigma>2/3, h and its exact convolution inverse j have finite
absolute ideal coefficient mass A_sigma and B_sigma. This follows by
expanding the literal denominator 1-(1-t)D-tR: its absolute geometric
ratio is below1, and both local corrections are
O_sigma(Q^(-1-sigma)+Q^(3-6sigma)). All prime powers are included. Thus
H and its reciprocal are holomorphic and nonzero on Re(s)>2/3. The
coefficient of p^6 has size bounded below by (1-Q^-1)Q^3-Q^-1, so this
particular absolute mass diverges at sigma<=2/3. That is not a universal
barrier to stronger zero exclusion or to signed estimates.

Let U_eta,tau(x)=sum_a mu_K(a)eta(a)g_tau(log(Na/x)), with the same exclusions.
The exact two identities, including the width, shift and normalization, are

    P_eta(x)=C_S exp(25/36) sum_a h(a)U_eta,2(exp(-5/3)x/Na),
    U_eta,2(x)=C_S^-1 exp(-25/36)
                         sum_a j(a)P_eta(exp(5/3)x/Na). ([restricted research revision]-P2)

For ||F||_sigma=sup_(X>0)X^-sigma||F||_[X,2X], the forward constant is
C_S exp(25/36-5sigma/3)A_sigma and the reverse constant is
C_S^-1 exp(-25/36+5sigma/3)B_sigma. Minkowski pays each actual dilated shell;
Gaussian left tails and two adjacent dyadic shells cover the full range.
Complete every-epsilon exponents are equivalent for gamma>=2/3; the edge
uses positive weight buffers and asserts no exact-power endpoint norm.
The Gaussian Mellin multiplier never vanishes, so a complete gamma bound
has its own all-height zero return. A common family conclusion requires the
same gamma for every fixed target, with target-dependent constants allowed.

For ordinary chi, eta(a)=chi(Na) has
L_K(s,eta)=L(s,chi)L(s,chi chi_-3), including all presented-modulus zeros.
After restoring the finite exclusions, convolve U_eta,2 with the Gaussian
field of the periodic mean-zero sequence
d_psi(n)=psi(n)-2*1_(2|n)psi(n/2), psi=chi chi_-3. At any fixed extra width
delta>0 this kernel has finite weighted L1 norm at every real weight.
The output is the ordinary field with literal coefficients
mu(n)chi(n)-2*1_(2|n)mu(n/2)chi(n/2), width2+delta and numerator1-2^(1-s).
This is a paid forward ordinary-character adapter, not an inverse heat
operation, width1 estimate or transfer from one ordinary target to every eta.

## 2. Retaining only a small correction-prime range

Extract E(s)=L_K^S(s+1,eta) and the literal sixth-power series
V6(s)=product_(p notin S)(1-R)^-1. Their coefficients and inverse coefficients
have finite absolute mass at sigma>2/3. With h=E V6 Rhat,

    rhat_p-1=[t(1-t)D^2-tR+t^2DR]/(1-D).              ([restricted research revision]-P3)

Both Rhat and its inverse converge in absolute coefficient mass for sigma>1/2.
The COMPLETE omitted-prime product obeys

    ||Rhat_>P-1||_sigma << P^(-2sigma)+P^(3-6sigma).  ([restricted research revision]-P4)

The product majorant includes every interaction among omitted primes. E and
V6 retain every prime; the finite Rhat product retains every valuation.
For the inherited beta=.8749, define W with transform exp(s^2)h/L and
What_P with transform exp(s^2)E V6 Rhat_<=P/L. Then

    ||W-What_P||_[X,2X] << X^beta P^(-2beta).         ([restricted research revision]-P5)

The inherited beta norm is justified from the accepted fixed-family premise:
lattice residue counting gives polynomial L growth, the zero-free buffered
disks give polynomial reciprocal growth, and Gaussian Mellin shift gives
the complete U beta norm. Holomorphy alone is not used as a growth estimate.

At P=max(2,X^theta), a full signed What_P gamma norm with
beta-2beta theta<gamma returns that same original gamma exponent. The
complete cross-energy error is at most2||What_P||||W-What_P||+||W-What_P||^2.
No favorable cross term is dropped. Conversely, the original U gamma bound
pays the approximant uniformly above2/3. It is an equivalent but concretely
different arithmetic target.

For gamma=.8748 (conditional c=.1252), theta>1/17498 suffices. Choosing
theta=1/16000 leaves error exponent.8747906375 and margin749/80000000.
Targets1/6 and1/4 require theta>1247/52494 and1249/17498 respectively.
All these are strict sufficient conditions; the signed moment remains open.
The author/review also preserve the weaker first extraction, with error
X^beta P^(4-6beta), rather than confusing its coefficient list with What_P.

## 3. Simultaneous and chained use

The two complete fields have the same exponent threshold in this range.
Their source representations and partial estimates can differ, which is why
the paid transfer is useful. The [[private research revision] hybrid construction](../[private research revision]/hybrid-detector-integration.md)
already prices chaining, simultaneous banks and fixed-piece harvesting.
Combining them requires these exact source maps and every coefficient cost;
no PR15 local moment, physical J-f error or arbitrary signed-submask estimate
is automatically imported by ([restricted research revision]-P2).

For a fixed linear combination of the source-normalized pair, the multiplier
is1-lambda h(s). Choosing lambda=1/h(rho) cancels a simple reciprocal pole.
Shellwise unconstrained energy optimization therefore need not preserve the
zero signal. A useful joint estimate must keep a nonzero numerator and pay
its full signed cross energy. Two scalar zero responses alone also do not
force a positive exterior Gram determinant.

The protected audit repairs the latter proposal with a different object.
For F(s)=exp(s^2)/L(s) and G(s)=a0^-s F(s), a0>1 fixed,

    F G'-F' G=-(log a0)a0^-s exp(2s^2)/L(s)^2.       ([restricted research revision]-P6)

Its numerator never vanishes. The exact physical field has coefficients
(mu_K*mu_K)(a)eta(a) and Gaussian width4 at the displayed dilation. A
complete bound excludes every original zero, including multiple zeros.
All four ideal indices and signed interactions remain in its energy. It is
not the original Hilbert-space wedge norm; its complete new moment is open.
General tensor/fractional-source ancestry remains, with the exact ideal
coefficient and derivative-determinant return distinguished.

## 4. A single fixed sparse mask with an explicit error

The uniform audit proves a probabilistic source approximation. Fix
0<kappa<1 and independent Bernoulli I_a with p_a=(Na)^(-kappa), once for all
ideals. Set Utilde(x)=sum_a I_a (Na)^kappa mu_K(a)eta(a)g_tau(log(Na/x)).
Every realization defines a complete field with polynomially bounded
coefficients. No new Euler product is assigned to this nonmultiplicative mask.
Exact variance and ideal counting give

    E ||Utilde-U||_[X,2X]^2 << X^(1+kappa).           ([restricted research revision]-P7)

Markov plus Borel--Cantelli on dyads yields, almost surely, error exponent
(1+kappa)/2+epsilon for every positive epsilon. A separate exponential
count bound gives retained support O(X^(1-kappa)) on every large norm dyad.
A countable intersection supplies one fixed mask for all prescribed fixed
characters, finite masks and widths, with no conductor-uniform constants.
The error Mellin transform is holomorphic to the right of(1+kappa)/2,
so it cannot cancel the original reciprocal poles there.

At kappa=.749 the support exponent is.251 and the limiting error exponent
is.8745. Choosing actual error exponent.8747 leaves room below target.8748.
The full signed sparse-field target would give c=.1252, but is equivalent
to the original target and remains open. Retained coefficients near X are
amplified by X^.749. The exact identity E||Utilde||^2=||U||^2+variance shows
why sparsity or unbiasedness alone yields no gain. This is a probability-one
existence theorem, not an explicit certified good mask, operational random
draw, finite computational proof or faster algorithm.

All [30 frozen cards](wild42/seeds.md), six first tests, both developments and
independent audits24/29 are preserved. Twenty-two cards remain untested.
Author pools were serialized before every literal all-group draw. The critic
knew the six selections before freezing its audits but read no outcomes;
that chronology is retained without reroll. Source identities, probabilistic
lemmas and exact finite checks are distinct from the still-open arithmetic
moment and from the full new-endpoint kernel evidence.

### 6.1 Use the existing label average to pay every row repetition

There is a second use of the cubic sieve which DOES retain all sixth-power rows. In literal PR9 B3.6, the squarefree f weight depends only on f, while the puncture, prime lists and all n coefficients are independent of f. For each fixed k apply B2.25 to the f,n pair with character chi_n(f)^4. Both are squarefree; cubic reciprocity/conjugation changes only fixed ray phases. The squared coefficient mass is(7) before its f-dependent phase is inserted, and multiplication by chi_n(k) is a contraction. The bound w(f)<<Z^epsilon permits positive enlargement of this f norm. Summing all O(Z^M) k rows and retaining the original Z^(-V) gives

    E(N,V,M) <<H_J Z^(E_label(M,N,V)+epsilon),
    E_label=M+max{0,N-V,(2N-V)/3}.                    (22)

This is uniform in the actual common puncture even if its norm grows. Unlike the pointwise-in-f bound(8), it is NOT asserted with arbitrary f-dependent column coefficients or f-dependent punctures. No moving label is inserted into a fixed Hecke twist: the entire squarefree label family is summed by the cubic sieve. A common smooth profile is separated on its original ambient box by B3.3, with an absolutely integrable fixed measure, before this argument.

The same estimate holds for the normalized f-average of the completed source(10), with X=Z^N. For fixed b, the phase chi_(cb^3)(f)^4 equals chi_c(f)^4 1_((b,f)=1), including all zeros. The b-phase in the k variable is also a contraction. The c coefficient mass is <<X^epsilon/q_b^2. Thus the joint positive (f,k) norm for this fixed b is bounded by

    H_J(UXZ^V)^epsilon U q_b^(-2)
       [Z^V+X/q_b^3+(Z^V X/q_b^3)^(2/3)].

Minkowski over b costs only a logarithmic power on the first term and convergent series on the others; divide the final squared norm by Z^V. This proves(22) for the complete label-averaged theta source too. In this proof every k row, including principal and pure sixth-power rows, is counted once. Their cancellation is supplied by the actual f-average, not by declaring them absent.

Consequently the canonical norm and the corresponding completed average obey the minimum of(8)/(12) and(22). In particular V>=2N gives O(Z^(M+epsilon)) for ANY N in the fixed polynomial range, with all original whole-index marks and common punctures. At N=M,V=2M this improves the full-row sixth-order exponent7M/6 to M. It also holds at Q=4M, where the older sufficient canonical gate F-M-Q>0 fails. This is a complete, different local mechanism using a neglected existing library component; it needs only PR9's licensed squarefree cubic sieve. No claim of first global novelty is made from absence of this formula in the inspected index. For the original physical compensator, f=1 and V=0, so(22) costs M+N and supplies no gain. Other canonical uses must retain and pay the V<2N complement; no complete physical covering argument was found here.

For the literal canonical target E<=Z^(F+epsilon), F=N+V, formula(8) gives the following complete sufficient gate, independent of Q and of total mark width for each fixed slot count:

    V>=M-N                 for 0<=N<=M/2,
    V>=5M/6-2N/3           for M/2<=N<=M,
    V>=M/6                 for N>=M.                 (23)

Equality is allowed in this direct estimate; an induction demanding a positive reserve must impose its own strict version. Formula(22) improves some interior exponents, but does NOT enlarge(23): E_label<=F is equivalent to V>=max{M-N,M/2,(3M-N)/4}, which implies(23) in each displayed range. This explicit boundary comparison prevents interpreting the paid label average as another automatic MP improvement. The sixth-free version has a different long-column boundary V>=max(0,M/3-N/6) for N>=M; applying that boundary to all rows would omit exactly the repeated-row cost. At V=0, neither new all-row bound reaches the canonical target for any M>0. The original unlabeled canonical branch therefore remains essential, even though the new gate removes Q from some labeled regions.

statement:
## 1. The local-set theorem

For a fixed ordinary Dirichlet character, let

    F(z)=sum_n mu(n)chi(n) g_tau(log n-z),   tau>0 fixed.

All natural zeros remain. The complete series is entire and satisfies
|F(u+iv)|<=C exp(u+v^2/(2tau)) for u>=0, with a Gaussian real left tail.
Fix 0<gamma<1 and 0<=kappa<1/2. Suppose for EVERY epsilon>0 there are
constants c_epsilon,C_epsilon>0 such that for EVERY sufficiently large
integer j a measurable E_j subset [j,j+1] satisfies

    |E_j|>=c_epsilon j^-kappa,
    ess sup_(y in E_j)|F(y)|<=C_epsilon exp((gamma+epsilon)j). ([restricted research revision]-V1)

Then the full field is O_epsilon(exp((gamma+epsilon)y)) on the real
axis and L(s,chi) has no zero in Re(s)>gamma. The converse follows
from the full-field bound; this is an equivalent observation criterion,
not a proof that the arithmetic hypothesis holds. Fixed positive-length
intervals also work. Arbitrarily shrinking intervals need another proof.
No missing logarithmic intervals, density-one substitute, finite sample
or selected signed subfield is permitted.

Here is the mechanism, including the errors. A complex polynomial of
degree N on a unit interval obeys

    sup_I |P| <= (4e/delta)^N ess sup_E |P|,  |E|>=delta.

Quantile Lagrange interpolation proves this for complex values. Given
a prior complex bound C(1+|v|)^K exp(bu+v^2/(2tau)), expand to
N=ceil(2(b-gamma)j/log j) on Cauchy radius sqrt(tau(N+1)). Both Taylor
remainders are multiplied by the interpolation factor. The resulting
single-step exponent is h=gamma+2kappa(b-gamma), with subexponential
loss. The calculation at kappa>=1/2 gives no improvement by THIS
method; it is not an impossibility theorem for other sampling arguments.

The bilateral Mellin identity

    integral_R F(y)exp(-sy)dy = exp(tau s^2/2)/L(s,chi)

first excludes zeros to the right of h. Only AFTER this exclusion is
the improved complex bound replenished. Ordinary character summation
gives polynomial growth of L on fixed positive half-planes. Regularize
the principal pole by (s-1)L, choose a zero-free logarithm on a disk
centered at2+it, and use Borel--Caratheodory with a positive fixed disk
gap. This proves polynomial reciprocal growth on every fixed line
b>h. Gaussian Mellin inversion then restores the complex bound at b.
Thus h_m=gamma+(2kappa)^m(B-gamma). For each output epsilon choose a
FINITE m and positive intermediate buffers; no infinite limiting
constant or circular reciprocal assumption is used.

## 6. The actual common-zero identity before witness selection

The higher-ceiling exploration starts from the exact B0.19 source rather than its chosen dyadic pair. Let phi be any fixed nonprincipal presentation, with its original zero extension and S-omission. Choose a smooth V, one on [0,1] and zero on [2,infinity). For fixed t>0 put R=U^t and

    C_R(s)=sum_d mu(d) phi(d) V(Nd/R)(Nd)^(-s),
    A_R(n)=sum_(d|n) mu(d)V(Nd/R).                        (J13)

All ideals in this formula avoid the same fixed S. Multiplicativity includes nonunit zeros; no coprimality division is made. Hence

    L^S(s,phi) C_R(s)=sum_n phi(n) A_R(n)(Nn)^(-s)

on its absolute half-plane. The coefficient at the unit is one, and A_R(n)=0 for 1<Nn<=R. This is a statement about the full signed divisor sum. Its individual dyadic inverse/plain pieces need not vanish.

Choose Y=U^B with B fixed sufficiently large, and define the completed tail

    D_R(s)=sum_(Nn>R) phi(n) A_R(n)(Nn)^(-s)exp(-Nn/Y). (J14)

For any prescribed A>0 and t in a fixed bounded positive range, B can be fixed so that at every retained actual zero rho with Re rho in a compact subinterval of (1/2,1),

    D_R(rho)=-1+O(U^(-A)).                              (J15)

The error is uniform in the source polynomial conductor/mask ranges and sufficiently small polynomial height range; outside it a polynomial height factor is retained. Indeed Mellin inversion gives the integral of
Y^z Gamma(z)L^S(rho+z,phi)C_R(rho+z). Shift from Re z=2 to -1/4. There is no nonprincipal pole, and the Gamma residue at zero is L^S(rho,phi)C_R(rho)=0. On that fixed strip the L-function and finite C_R have a fixed polynomial conductor/height/scale bound. The remainder is Y^(-1/4) times that polynomial. Choose B after its raw power and before tail orders. The unit is exp(-1/Y)=1+O(U^(-B)); increasing B pays both errors. Natural Euler holes on this positive strip cost a small power. The exponential permits truncation at Nn<=U^(B+1), with error smaller than every fixed negative power, including every required fixed derivative.

For t in [1,3/2], this is the precise completion behind B0.19. The identity itself permits ANY fixed bounded t; the interval restriction comes from the subsequent individual witness/moment strategy, not the contour identity. Thus t=2 or 3 below is a new detector input, not an illegal application of Lemma 1W at those cutoffs.

Fix any finite list t_1,...,t_h BEFORE rows and zeros, and use the same selected zero and character for all cutoffs. On a high-row set with nonnegative weights w_u, put M=sum_u w_u. J15 gives

    sum_u w_u D_j(rho_u) conjugate(D_k(rho_u))
       =M+O(U^(-A)M),
    sum_u w_u |sum_j c_j D_j(rho_u)|^2
       =|sum_j c_j|^2 M+O(U^(-A)||c||_1^2 M).            (J16)

The finite coefficient vector is row independent and has fixed bounded mass. The same identities hold with w_u the actual squared slot product and retained diagonal contractions. This is exact shared-zero coherence of completed tests. An average with sum c_j=1 preserves the full signal, while a difference with sum c_j=0 annihilates it. A product of finitely many completed tests likewise has its prescribed constant signal. Combining these cutoffs gives no additional power of U in that signal. J16 alone makes NO independence/dependence claim for a probability law on the unrestricted rows.

This does not prove that selected dyadic witnesses coincide for different cutoffs, or that every witness pair is correlated with every slot amplitude. It does not forbid a mixed moment or signed cross-scale cancellation on the UNRESTRICTED row family. It redirects the proposed all-cutoff strategy: any counting gain needs a new ambient mixed estimate; it cannot be obtained by crediting an extra power to the zero signal. This is an actual source-level restriction on signal extraction, not an impossibility theorem for joint zero density.

statement:
# [private research revision]: a complete parity-adapted Jordan source

W65 and its independent review supply an ordinary-character replacement
source whose principal far tail is removed exactly. Its divisor kernel
decays exponentially at infinity and vanishes to a prescribed odd order
at zero; the full source is exponentially small as X tends to zero.
A logarithmic upper divisor cutoff is paid for
principal as well as nonprincipal characters. An explicit future-scale
inverse preserves the full exponent problem. The signed middle and
off-diagonal estimates remain open; this is no increase of c and no
repair of PR15's unfinished Hecke weighted-source theorem.

The numerical comparison target is the CONDITIONAL source-relative
c11=312864909/2500000000, gamma11=1-c11. The construction below does
not assume that benchmark theorem: its identities, elementary tail
bounds and conditional returns hold in their stated ordinary-character
scope. See the [source-status correction](../imports/qrtracker-20261013/pr15-status-clarification.md).
The [author](author/report.md), [independent review](review/report.md)
and [blind audits](review/blind-audits.md) are retained unchanged.
Their older endpoint language is subject to that correction.

## G215. Exact source, complete localization and all-height return

Fix an ordinary Dirichlet character chi modulo its PRESENTED modulus q,
including every natural nonunit zero. Let chi(-1)=(-1)^a and fix r>=2
with r congruent to a modulo2. The choices r=2 for even chi and r=3 for
odd chi suffice. All q,chi,r and the filter order below are fixed before
the scale, target height and implied constants. There is no growing-q,
growing-r or Hecke-family assertion.

Define the Jordan coefficient and Laplace source by

    J_r(n)=sum_(d|n) mu(d)(n/d)^r
          =n^r product_(p|n)(1-p^(-r)),
    F(X)=sum_(n>=1) chi(n)J_r(n) exp(-n/X).          (1)

Inclusion-exclusion counts primitive r-tuples modulo n and proves the
coefficient formula. Squareful values are deliberate: this source does
not claim to retain squarefree Möbius support. Absolute convolution
gives L(s-r,chi)/L(s,chi) on Re s>r+1, with all inducing factors.

Put m_q=phi(q)/q for principal chi and0 otherwise,
A=m_q r!/L(r+1,chi), and E(X)=F(X)-A X^(r+1). The Euler product
defines the reciprocal at r+1 without an unproved strip assumption.
For t>0 set

    H(t)=sum_(n>=1)chi(n)e^(-nt)
        =[sum_(v=1)^q chi(v)e^(-vt)]/[1-e^(-qt)],
    f(t)=(-d/dt)^r H(t),
    g(t)=f(t)-m_q r! t^(-r-1).

Absolute convergence of the original double series and of the
subtracted reciprocal series at r+1 proves the COMPLETE identity

    E(X)=sum_(d>=1) mu(d)chi(d)g(d/X).               (2)

The principal main coefficient is for the presented modulus, not its
primitive conductor. No finite Euler correction is suppressed.

For q>1 residue reflection gives H(-t)=-chi(-1)H(t).
For q=1 the extra constant is -1, removed by r differentiations.
The parity choice makes the regular part of f odd; its possible
principal pole is odd too. Thus g(t)=O(t), g'(t)=O(1) at zero.
At infinity f,f'=O(e^(-t)); principal g retains exactly the algebraic
tail -m_q r!t^(-r-1). Consequently

    |g(t)| <= C min(t,t^(-r-1)),  E(X)=O(X), X>=1.   (3)

The actual complete low/high absolute prices, for alpha<1<beta, are
O(X^(2alpha-1)) and O(X^(r+1-r beta)) at d<=X^alpha and d>X^beta.
For gamma in(0,1), alpha=(1+gamma)/2 and beta=1+(1-gamma)/r
pay both at X^gamma. The middle is still signed and unpaid.

Now fix b=2 and m>=0, put T h(t)=h(2t), D G(X)=G(X/2), and

    P_m(T)=product_(j=0)^(m-1)(I-2^(-(2j+1))T),
    B_r(T)=I-2^(r+1)T,
    K(t)=P_m(T)B_r(T)g(t)=P_m(T)B_r(T)f(t),
    Phi(X)=P_m(D)B_r(D)E(X)=P_m(D)B_r(D)F(X).

The empty product is identity. The B_r factor kills the principal
algebraic tail and the main term exactly. P_m removes the first m
odd Taylor powers. Therefore

    Phi(X)=sum_(d>=1) mu(d)chi(d)K(d/X),             (4)
    K(t)=O(t^(2m+1)), K'(t)=O(t^(2m)) as t->0,
    K(t)=e^(-t)+O(e^(-2t)),
    K'(t)=-e^(-t)+O(e^(-2t)) as t->infinity.         (5)

The coefficient of the slowest exponential is chi(1)1^r=1, since
every other dilation has argument at least2t. This also proves K
is nonzero. Equation (4) keeps exactly the original outer mu(d)chi(d).
Even when2 divides q, these are literal scale dilations: no chi(2)
is factored out, and the expanded output coefficients are not falsely
assigned the old support. Phi can be evaluated from F without knowing A.
It is O(X) at infinity and O(e^(-1/X)) at zero.

For any fixed gamma in(0,1), set

    alpha=1-(1-gamma)/(2m+2),
    Cmid(x)=sum_(x^alpha<d<=2x log x)mu(d)chi(d)K(d/x).

For every sufficiently large real x, the three disjoint ranges
d<=x^alpha, x^alpha<d<=2x log x, d>2x log x cover all divisors.
The first absolute price is
x^(-(2m+1)) sum_(d<=x^alpha)d^(2m+1)=O(x^gamma).
The last is O(sum_(d>2x log x)e^(-d/x))=O(x^-1).
Rounding the real cut changes only a fixed constant. Thus

    Phi(x)=Cmid(x)+O(x^gamma).                       (6)

The cuts decompose ONE fixed source; they do not create a different
Mellin profile at each x. The weakest return used here is the complete
dyadic-shell L1 hypothesis

    integral_X^(2X)|Cmid(x)| dx/x
       <<_(chi,r,m,epsilon) X^(gamma+epsilon)       (7)

for every epsilon>0 and all sufficiently large dyadic X, at one common
gamma across every fixed ordinary chi. A full shell L2 bound implies
(7); no favorable signed subset is substituted for the whole norm.
For m=1 the paid lower exponents are .9687135091 at gamma11,
.9687 at gamma=.8748,23/24 at gamma=5/6, and15/16 at gamma=3/4.
The full upper cutoff is2x log x in every case. These are explicit
complement budgets, not estimates of Cmid.

To establish the all-height return, ordinary functional equations,
trivial-zero parity and exact inducing factors give

    L(s-r,chi) !=0 for 0<Re s<=1.                   (8)

Indeed -r<Re(s-r)<=1-r lies between consecutive parity trivial zeros,
and the extra finite factors have zeros only on Re(s-r)=0.
The q=1 zeta case is treated separately at its negative even zeros.
These standard inputs are recorded in [DLMF25.15](https://dlmf.nist.gov/25.15)
and [DLMF25.10](https://dlmf.nist.gov/25.10); the source reflection above
is derived directly.

On Re s>r+1, finite scaling in the absolutely convergent transform gives

    Mellin(Phi)(s)=Gamma(s)Q_mr(s)L(s-r,chi)/L(s,chi),
    Q_mr(s)=(1-2^(r+1-s))
             product_(j=0)^(m-1)(1-2^(-(s+2j+1))).  (9)

Here Mellin(Phi)=integral_0^infinity Phi(X)X^(-s)dX/X.
The first factor cancels the actual principal numerator pole at r+1;
its zeros lie on Re s=r+1. The other zeros lie on negative odd
real-part lines. Hence Q_mr is nonzero in the entire target strip,
including Re s=1. Gamma(s) has no pole or zero there.

The unconditional O(X) and small-X exponential bounds make the full
integral holomorphic for Re s>1. Under (7), equation (6) supplies the
same shell L1 bound for Phi. Sum dyadic integrals on each compact subset
of Re s>gamma, choosing epsilon below its distance to gamma. Derivatives
only insert logarithmic powers. The small-X contribution is entire.
Continuation therefore preserves

    L(s,chi) Mellin(Phi)(s)
        =Gamma(s)Q_mr(s)L(s-r,chi), Re s>gamma.      (10)

A hypothetical zero in gamma<Re s<=1 contradicts (8)–(10); the Euler
product covers Re s>1. The principal pole at1 is allowed and has the
compensating transform zero. Normal convergence on every compact
handles every finite height without assuming a uniform height bound
or that a bare zero-free strip implies a sharp Mertens estimate.

The arithmetic hypothesis (7) remains OPEN. A common gamma<gamma11
would beat the conditional numerical benchmark in the ordinary-family
scope. Targets c=.1252,1/6,1/4 mean gamma=.8748,5/6,3/4 respectively.
No ordinary-to-Hecke or original-Gaussian source transfer is inferred.

## G216. Exact recovery, actual absolute cost and complete diagonal

Let E_m=P_m(D)E. The proved coarse bound E_m(Y)=O(Y), together with
Phi(X)=E_m(X)-2^(r+1)E_m(X/2), gives for every J>=1

    E_m(X)=2^(-J(r+1))E_m(2^J X)
           -sum_(j=1)^J 2^(-j(r+1))Phi(2^j X).

The first term is O(X2^(-Jr)), so the FULL future-scale inverse is

    E_m(X)=-sum_(j>=1)2^(-j(r+1))Phi(2^j X).        (11)

Every future scale remains. For gamma<r+1 and sufficiently small
epsilon, a complete exponent gamma+epsilon pays the series with
ratio2^(-(r+1-gamma-epsilon))<1. Changing variables in each dyadic
shell proves the same statement in L1. Conversely finite shifts of
E_m imply the Phi bound. Thus their complete every-epsilon exponent
classes are equivalent. The possible homogeneous mode X^(r+1) is
excluded by the actual O(X) bound, not discarded. Shorter support
alone is not a weaker arithmetic obligation.

The complete arithmetic absolute cost also stays linear. Elementary
square-divisor inversion, with all coprimality factors, gives

    Q_q(y)=sum_(n<=y,(n,q)=1)mu(n)^2
          =kappa_q y+O_q(sqrt y),
    kappa_q=zeta(2)^(-1) product_(p|q)(1+1/p)^(-1)>0.

For the original g, for P_m(T)g, and for K, the function absolute value
is absolutely continuous and its a.e. derivative is bounded by the
absolute derivative of the kernel. Both tails give finite
integral_0^infinity sqrt(t)|K'(t)|dt. Stieltjes summation therefore proves

    sum_n |mu(n)chi(n)K(n/X)|
      =kappa_q X integral_0^infinity|K(t)|dt+O(sqrt X). (12)

The integral is positive by the e^(-t) coefficient in (5). For g and
P_m(T)g, use their nonzero principal algebraic tail or nonprincipal
slowest exponential instead. This is a lower asymptotic for the
ACTUAL absolute price, not a lower bound on the signed field or M_chi.
Full triangle inequality cannot yield a fixed sublinear exponent.
Full Abel summation from any known |M_chi(y)|<<y^beta yields only
X^beta integral t^beta|K'(t)|dt; it preserves beta. The bounded
non-arithmetic sequence n^beta-(n-1)^beta tests that operator limitation,
without purporting to refute cancellation of mu chi.

There is an explicit principal normalization. At q=1,r=2,m=0,
v=e^(-t), f(t)=v(1+v)/(1-v)^3, and

    K_0(t)=f(t)-8f(2t)=v(1-v)/(1+v)^3
           =(1/4)tanh(t/2)sech^2(t/2)>0.           (13)

The numerator identity is
v(1+v)^4-8v^2(1+v^2)=v(1-v)^4.
Substitute u=tanh(t/2), dt=2du/(1-u^2), to obtain

    integral K_0(t)dt=integral_0^1 u/2 du=1/4,
    integral K_0(t)^2dt
        =integral_0^1 (u^2-u^4)/8 du=1/60.          (14)

Consequently the literal field
Phi_0(X)=F_(1,2)(X)-8F_(1,2)(X/2)=sum mu(n)K_0(n/X) has

    sum_n |mu(n)K_0(n/X)|=X/(4zeta(2))+O(sqrt X),
    sum_n mu(n)^2 K_0(n/X)^2=X/(60zeta(2))+O(sqrt X). (15)

The second is its POINTWISE squared diagonal. Integrating over a
complete shell dx/x gives X/(60zeta(2))+O(sqrt X).
The full energy retains both ordered off-diagonal orientations:
for this real principal kernel it is the diagonal plus twice the
signed sum over m<n. Absolute convergence on each shell justifies
expansion; no cross term is omitted. The diagonal is not a lower
bound for the full square. For gamma>1/2 its exponent1 is already
below2gamma; the complete cross estimate remains the substantive task.
An energy exponent below1.7497080728 would clear the current numerical
target; the displayed targets .8748,5/6,3/4 ask for1.7496,5/3,3/2.
None of these full signed estimates is proved here.

## G217. Actual-source obstructions and their exact scopes

The companion developments are retained because they rule out specific
repairs without declaring broader approaches exhausted.

First, the higher-arity source is the already known W01/W35/W48-R6
construction. Write a=mu chi,h=chi,m=a1_(n<=U),u=a-m,
q_p=delta_1-p chi(p)delta_p and b_p=q_p*h, with fixed unramified p.
Dirichlet convolution gives, with every zero and repeated prime kept,

    q_p^(k-1)*a=u^k*b_p^(k-1)
      +sum_(j=1)^k(-1)^(j+1)binom(k,j)m^j*q_p^(k-j)*b_p^(j-1). (16)

For fixed k>=2,0<delta<=1,U=X^((1-delta)/k), all short products are
at most X^(1-delta), up to fixed p-shifts. The cofactor series
(1-chi(p)p^(1-s))L(s,chi) is entire. Its fixed Gaussian transform can
be moved to any fixed negative line; the Gaussian dominates vertical
polynomial growth and the finite coefficient counts. This pays all
restoration terms on complete real shells. The j=1 delta-cofactor
term has direct Gaussian decay. No growing-k assertion follows.

For principal chi, products of k distinct unramified primes in
[X^(1/k),2^(1/k)X^(1/k)], excluding p, have hard coefficient exactly
(-1)^k k!. Every long factor must contain one prime, so the cofactor
is1. Fixed-proportion prime counts give order X/log^k X such products,
all on one shell. Their selected same-sign Gaussian field therefore
has linear exponent, including its normalized shell L1/L2 norm.
This blocks paying that proper sector separately; other sectors may
cancel it. Fixed k prime counts follow by partial summation from
[Selberg's PNT, theorem1.1](https://www.math.lsu.edu/~mahlburg/teaching/handouts/2014-7230/Selberg-ElemPNT1949.pdf).
The restriction U>=1 is necessary for the k! coefficient and the
vanishing of lower-degree cells: if delta>1, U<1 and u=a, the hard
source collapses to q_p^(k-1)*a. The raw author's wider claim is
corrected here; the convolution identity itself remains valid.

Second, fixed nonnegative compact smoothing and deletion of finitely
many activity layers do not repair the shrinking zero disk. Fix
continuous compactly supported w>=0 with w(0)>0 and w>=c>0 on some
[a,b],0<a<b. For principal chi modulo fixed q, let

    C_j(X)=sum_(n squarefree,(n,q)=1,omega(n)=j)w(n/X),
    Z_X^[ell](z)=C_0+C_ell z^ell+sum_(j>ell)C_j z^j,

where ell>=1 is fixed; this DELETES layers1,...,ell-1.
We have C_0->w(0)>0, total mass O(X), and, by products of ell
distinct primes in the fixed scaled interval,
C_ell>>X/log^ell X. Unique factorization costs only fixed ell!.
At R=(2C_0/C_ell)^(1/ell), eventually R<1, and

    |C_0+C_ell z^ell|>=C_0 for |z|=R,
    |sum_(j>ell)C_j z^j|<=O(X)R^(ell+1)
       =O(X^(-1/ell)log^(ell+1)X)=o(1).             (17)

Rouche gives exactly ell roots of the COMPLETE polynomial inside R.
All higher degrees are paid together. A scale-independent positive
radius for the logarithm at0 is unavailable. A weight vanishing on
a neighborhood of0 has C_0=0 eventually and no such logarithm at all;
this last observation is not a statement about every w with w(0)=0.
Restoring the original signed endpoint requires the deleted signed
layers; their individual absolute prices have linear exponent, but
their signed sum has not been lower-bounded. Signed or moving weights,
growing ell, exact deflation and another normalized object remain
outside this obstruction. These are activity zeros, not L-function
zeros. G106's sharp-cutoff root and G120/G145's normalization costs
remain the earlier mechanisms, with this specified extension.

The two independent pre-outcome audits add further scope checks.
For A_chi(x)=sum_(n<=x)chi(n)phi(n), every unramified prime p produces
a jump of magnitude p-1. No continuous background can have uniform
error O(x^gamma), gamma<1, on every large real x: left limit and
value at p would give p-1<=2Cp^gamma. The coefficient at1 and the
principal count2A_1(x)-1 are retained. An r-fold Riesz smoothing has
the exact transform L(s-1,chi)/[L(s,chi)s(s+1)...(s+r)], with its
principal terms and numerator nonvanishing still required for a return.
The parity Jordan construction addresses that numerator issue for its
own different source; it does not erase the sharp jump.

For the complete replica audit, on K squarefree q-units let
a_n=mu(n)chi(n). Exactly

    sum_(m<n)|a_m-a_n|^2=K^2-|M_chi(x)|^2.           (18)

Thus the useful estimate is a one-sided LOWER bound near K^2, not
positivity alone. For a simple d-regular graph on these K vertices,
1<=d<=K/2, adjacency A_G, compare
Ltilde=(K/d)(dI-A_G) with Lcomplete=KI-11*. The constant eigenvalue
is d and tr(A_G^2)=Kd, so

    ||Ltilde-Lcomplete||
      >=K sqrt((K-d)/(d(K-1)))>=K/sqrt(2d).          (19)

The source-independent error certificate K times this operator norm
cannot prove error O(x^(2gamma+epsilon)) unless
d>=x^(4-4gamma-2epsilon) up to fixed constants, since K~kappa_q x.
Before small losses the degree exponents are .5005838544 at gamma11,
2/3 at5/6, and1 at3/4. The last excludes every fixed-power sublinear
degree under an every-epsilon target, but not x^(1-o(1)).
This is a limitation of the stated regular-graph uniform certificate,
not a lower bound for its error on the actual Möbius vector or a
claim about weighted/nonregular graphs. A source-specific signed
comparison and the complete one-sided deficit remain open.

## Evidence, ancestry and the next arithmetic estimate

Root read the complete author and independent-review reports, both
blind audits, diagnostic source and receipts, and the relevant literal
G106/G120/G145/W48-R6 ancestry. Root reconstructed the parity reflection,
nonvanishing strip, full Mellin continuation, every tail, future-scale
inverse, positive kernel integrals, squarefree Stieltjes costs, entire
Rouche remainder and regular-graph trace argument. The primary DLMF
and Selberg statements were tool-read; no downloaded web hash or
literature-priority claim is invented.

The original30 cards, all literal pools/draws and entropy, six tests and
both pre-outcome audits are preserved. Author choicesS02/S26/S23 and
randomS10/S22/S19 came from pools24/11/25. Reviewer auditsS17/S24 froze
before outcomes; prior mathematical exposure was declared. S26 is an
exact G145 duplicate, not a new Fock estimate. The two raw G130 Bellman
references are corrected to G129 without modifying source bytes.

Retained finite checks cover six Jordan-character cases, parity,
24arity cases, complete activity coefficients, fixed filters and
rational cut budgets. The failed predetermined circle
q=6,X=2001/2,ell=3,R=1/2,margin-11095/16008 remains. Eleven successful
finite circles are not an asymptotic proof. The fractions in (14) are
proved by substitution; merely assigning them in a helper is not
integration evidence. No unchanged successful diagnostic was rerun.
Original missed deadlines and capacity/backoff history remain retained.

Potential is moderate as an explicit alternate arithmetic source and
low for a coefficient-blind norm attack. The complete logarithmic far
cutoff removes a real nuisance for principal characters, while (11)
shows exactly what remains equivalent. The strongest useful next action
is a source-specific estimate of Cmid in (7), or the FULL signed cross
form associated with (15). Positive triangle prices, endpoint filtering,
a spectral name or another Mellin equivalence alone cannot supply it.
The broader portfolio and all untested seeds remain available.

statement:
## 3. Double compensation is coefficient-exact

Fix one ordinary character chi modulo q, with its natural zero extension,
and a fixed prime p not dividing q. Let a(n)=lambda(n)chi(n), h(n)=chi(n),
and s(r^2)=chi(r)^2, with s zero off squares. Define

    q1=delta_1-p chi(p)delta_p,
    q2=delta_1-p chi(p)^2 delta_(p^2), v=q1*q2,
    b=v*h, g=a*s, c=v*g.

At a prime power, summing the alternating Liouville coefficients against h
gives s. Thus a*h=s, a*b=v*s, and a*a*b=v*a*s=c, with no coprimality
condition. Complete multiplicativity a(d)a(e)=a(de) includes nonunits and
all shared primes. It is not the false corresponding identity for mu.

For Re z>1, absolute Euler products give

    D_c(z)=P_p(z)J_p(z)L(2z,chi^2)^2/L(z,chi),
    P_p(z)=1-chi(p)p^(1-z),
    J_p(z)=1-chi(p)^2 p^(1-2z).

The two nontrivial coefficients of q2 are at 1 and p^2, and the second
coefficient is -p chi(p)^2, not -p^2 chi(p)^2. This distinction is necessary
for root cancellation and puts J_p's zeros precisely on Re z=1/2.
L(2z,chi^2) is finite and nonzero on Re z>1/2 by its absolutely convergent
Euler product. Its possible principal pole is on the excluded boundary.

Explicitly,

    b(n)=chi(n)[1-p1_(p|n)-p1_(p^2|n)+p^2 1_(p^3|n)],
    beta(r)=chi(r)^2(1-p1_(p|r)),
    (q2*s)(r^2)=beta(r).

b has period p^3 q, and beta has period pq; both have zero mean. For b,
first use the ordinary mean-zero compensator q1*h and then its p^2-dilate.
For beta, a nonprincipal chi^2 has zero period sum, while a principal chi^2
has exactly cancelling unrestricted and p-divisible root counts. These
arguments include ramified zero values. The short source v*s=q1*(q2*s)
retains two distinct physical rows, with multipliers d and pd and respective
weights 1 and -p chi(p). Their root cutoffs need not agree.
title: 3. Double compensation is coefficient-exact

statement:
### Full divisor-bounded tail

If |v_n|<=A_eta n^eta and 2eta<k-2, the complete tail satisfies

    ||sum_(n>M)v_n f_x(n)||_2^2
      <<_(b,k,eta) A_eta^2
          [X^(b(1+2eta))+X^k M^(2-k+2eta)].    (91.2)

Use a nonnegative C2 majorant equal to one on the original shell,
supported in [1/2,4], with flat endpoints. After v=u^(-k), the
off-diagonal amplitude and two derivatives are uniformly bounded:
powers of A=(n+m)/X^b are absorbed by exp(-cA). Two integrations by
parts give the kernel

    min(1,(X^k/|n^k-m^k|)^2).

For m<n, n^k-m^k>=n^(k-1)(n-m). Writing delta=X^k/n^(k-1), the
full sum over gaps of min(1,(delta/gap)^2) is O(delta), including
delta<1. Sum n^(2eta)delta over n>M; the damped diagonal supplies
the first term in (91.2). Finite expansions followed by summable
domination justify the infinite calculation. Both orientations and
every cross are included; no off-diagonal part is dropped.

For 1/2<gamma<1, b<=2gamma and

    r=(k-2gamma)/(k-2), M=X^r,

(91.2) gives an O(X^(gamma+epsilon)) tail in L2 and L1 for every
epsilon>0, choosing eta after epsilon. This includes b=2gamma.
The tail proof needs no r<b restriction; damping helps when r>=b.

statement:
## 4. Natural-zero increments and a fixed-source strengthening

The strongest immediate objection is that independent quotient states need not be cumulative inputs. The author's B3 successfully addresses that objection at the stated synthetic scope. Write

    Q_q(t)=sum_(n<=t)mu(n)^2 1_((n,q)=1)
          =kappa_q t+O_q(sqrt t),
    kappa_q=zeta(2)^(-1) product_(p|q) p/(p+1)>0.

This follows by mu^2(n)=sum_(e^2|n)mu(e), counting q-unit multiples, and paying all O_q(sqrt t) errors and the square-divisor tail. Fix1/2<beta<1 and0<alpha<(1-beta)/(2-beta). For each unramified prime power d<=N^alpha take m_d=floor(N/d), H_d=floor(m_d^beta/8) and

    B_d(n)=max(0,H_d-|Q_q(n)-Q_q(m_d)|).

The density formula first confines support to n comparable to m_d and then to |n-m_d|=O_q(H_d), uniformly, since sqrt(m_d)=o(H_d). Its increments have modulus at most mu(n)^2 1_((n,q)=1), with exact zero at every natural-zero site. The nearest-center spacing is at least N/[d(d+1)]-1. Relative support width is O_q(N^(beta-1)d^(2-beta))=o(1) uniformly; supports and their increment boundaries are disjoint and stay away from0,N.

Under u->floor(N/u), each support is within o(1) of d, including the floor error O(d^2/N). Thus d is its ONLY integer contact. Every supported n is comparable to m_d, and H_d<=n^beta eventually. Put F_n=sum_d conj(chi(d))B_d(n). Then |F_n|<=n^beta and |F_n-F_(n-1)|<=mu(n)^2 1_((n,q)=1). Every discrete contact contributes exactly Lambda(d)H_d. For nonprincipal chi there is no drift. For principal chi each bump is nonnegative and its entire continuous integral is at most H_d times its o(1) inverse-support width, at most Lambda(d)H_d/2 eventually. Hence

    J_N(F) >= c_(q,beta,alpha) N^(beta+alpha(1-beta)) >0.

Here J_N(F) is real with the chosen phases. All bumps lie above a constant times N^(1-alpha), so any prescribed growing zero-error prefix N^theta with theta<1-alpha survives. Taking alpha smaller handles each fixed theta<1. Additional zeros outside the supports are allowed; neither the actual Mobius signs nor multiplicativity is asserted. The finite helper uses smaller heights H about m^(7/8)/128 at one N; it checks conventions only, and is not evidence for the all-N asymptotic beyond the written proof.

INDEPENDENT STRENGTHENING. For each fixed chi,beta,alpha as above there is ONE infinite synthetic sequence b(n), independent of the evaluation cutoff, such that

    |b(n)|<=mu(n)^2 1_((n,q)=1),
    F(n)=sum_(j<=n)b(j), |F(n)|<=n^beta,
    |J_(N_j)(F)| >= c N_j^(beta+alpha(1-beta))

along an increasing sequence N_j->infinity. One may prescribe any finite initial zero prefix. For principal chi the construction can use real b(n) in{-1,0,1}. This removes the objection that ONLY cutoff-dependent inputs cause the failure, while still making no claim about actual Mobius coefficients.

Proof: use the preceding compact bump family G_j at a sufficiently large N_j, taking N_j so large that its entire support and both increment boundaries lie above the previous support and above N_(j-1). This is possible because its lowest center tends to infinity like N_j^(1-alpha), while its largest center is at most N_j/2+o(N_j). Each G_j vanishes before and after its block and has K_j=J_(N_j)(G_j)>0 with the preceding lower bound. Suppose F_old is the sum of earlier blocks. Choose z_j=J_(N_j)(F_old)/|J_(N_j)(F_old)| when that value is nonzero, and z_j=1 otherwise. Add z_j G_j. By linearity,

    |J_(N_j)(F_old+z_j G_j)|=|J_(N_j)(F_old)|+K_j>=K_j.

Every later support lies above N_j and hence changes no state sampled by J_(N_j). The locally finite sum F=sum_j z_j G_j is therefore a single well-defined cumulative input. Disjoint increment boundaries preserve its magnitude and natural-zero increment bounds. Put b(n)=F(n)-F(n-1); telescoping gives the required cumulative identity. In the principal case induction makes F_old and its J value real, so z_j is+1 or-1 and all increments remain0,+1,-1. This proves the claim without assuming cancellation in the earlier blocks or any prime-distribution estimate.

The fixed-sequence strengthening does NOT retain F(m)=0 for every m<=N_j^theta at infinitely many j with theta>0: that would force F identically zero. The author's cutoff-dependent version retains that separate property. Neither version imposes the actual inverse-convolution law or the prescribed mu(n)chi(n) signs. These qualifications are necessary.
title: 4. Natural-zero increments and a fixed-source strengthening

## 5. Development11/15: phase geometry keeps a complete native Gram bill

Keep the original same-scale distinct-rational-norm degree-one prime packet over the Eisenstein field, every ordered short pair including equality, the complete bounded short core h((g,g')), both rooted mark arrays, projectors1_(P,Rg)=1 and1_(P',Rg')=1, original sharp endpoints, natural zeros, ray/unit factors and both independent heights. The exact transformed kernel contains

    chi_pi(h)^3 chi_pi'(h)^3 chi_pi(s)^2 chi_pi'(s')^4
       *b(pi)conjugate(b(pi'))*zeta_(pi,pi'),             (23)

on its actual nonzero set. The CRT root zeta is not set to1. Its unitary native Fourier factor is1/Q on a group of size Q^2, Q=q_pi q_pi'. These source conventions are inherited from [private research revision]/JN/JNR, not recomputed or replaced by a rational model here.

Freeze original finite supports and heights first and fold ALL scalar sums into the exact bilinear mark matrix T. With v_P=u_1(P)/sqrt(q_P), w_P'=u_2(P')/sqrt(q_P'), the literal source is v*Tw after the appropriate harmless conjugate convention, and ||v||^2=Omega1, ||w||^2=Omega2. T contains every projector, all short signs and the original prime-pair weights. Integrating the original height measures is a separate literal linear operation; an inequality integrated by absolute variation must pay that variation and the original profile seminorms. This finite matrix representation does not claim that long-prime coefficients are freely adjustable.

For diagonal unitaries U,V, rephasing T to UTV* and transporting inputs to Uv,Vw preserves the same scalar and every singular value:

    ||UTV*||_(2->2)=||T||_(2->2).                       (24)

If the input coefficients are held fixed instead, that operation changes the native source. Thus a gauge construction cannot by itself improve the existing norm. Gauge-invariant cycle frustration can still support an independent estimate. The exact two-by-two diagnostic, with four entries of modulus1 and cycle phase Phi, gives

    ||T||^2=2+2|cos(Phi/2)|.                            (25)

For a flat cycle it is4; for phase pi it is2. This is a synthetic matrix calculation illustrating the missing arithmetic information, not evidence that a particular native H cycle has either value. Fixed-factor reduction alone also does not buy an asymptotic power Z^-.004.

The natural real-segment enclosure in card15 is Z=sum_j[-z_j,z_j]. Its directional support is sum_j|Re(e^-itheta z_j)|. It is not an enclosure for arbitrary independent complex coefficients |a_j|<=1: z_1=1,a_1=i already lies outside[-1,1]. Retaining instead the TRUE bilinear constraint a_PP'=conjugate(v_P)w_P' restores the rank-one matrix domain; the supremum over the unit product ball is exactly ||T||. Equivalently its convex hull is the nuclear-norm unit ball, as a finite singular-value decomposition shows. No phase saving has been produced by changing the enclosure's name.

A precise sufficient arithmetic test, stronger than necessary but preserving the actual full coefficients, is

    M=max_j [sum_i |T_ij|^2
                  +sum_(k!=j)|sum_i conjugate(T_ij)T_ik|],

This follows from the row/column Schur bound for the Hermitian Gram matrix. The inner i-sum stays SIGNED until its prescribed absolute value. Expanding it retains both copies of each short core, all projector crosses, actual phase cycles and both sets of native heights. Entrywise magnitudes or isolated cycle counts do not establish(26)'s required size.

For the [private research revision] raw target, the sufficient requirement is

    M <= Z^epsilon [G K (N+L+(NL)^(2/3)) P_orig]^2.     (27)

Only after the raw form is bounded is the original outside factor N^-1 G^-2 applied once. statement:
### No lost zeros in the numerator

Primitive L-functions have no zeros in Re(z)<0 except their real trivial zeros at the negative integers of the corresponding parity. The imprimitive completion is the primitive function times the exact finite factors 1-chi*(p)p^(-z). These factors have zeros only on Re(z)=0. Consequently our parity choice gives

    L(s-r,chi) != 0  whenever 0<Re(s)<=1.              (B9)

Indeed -r<Re(s-r)<=1-r lies strictly between consecutive trivial zeros, and is negative. Gamma(s) also has no zero or pole there. The functional equation and finite-factor formulas used here are the standard [DLMF 25.15.4-8](https://dlmf.nist.gov/25.15). This statement handles all heights and all presented moduli; no uniformity in growing q is used.

Suppose for every epsilon>0 and all large real X that

    E_(chi,r)(X)=O_(chi,epsilon)(X^(gamma+epsilon))      (B10)

at one common gamma<gamma11 for every fixed ordinary chi, with r chosen as above. Then L(s,chi) has no zeros with Re(s)>gamma, with the principal pole at 1 retained.

Here is the full Mellin justification. Initially on Re(s)>r+1,

    Mellin(F)(s)=Gamma(s)L(s-r,chi)/L(s,chi).

Split at X=1, subtract A X^(r+1) only in the large-X integral and add A/(s-r-1). By (B7) the resulting expression continues to Re(s)>1 except the indicated main-term pole. On 1<Re(s)<r+1 it equals the ordinary full integral of E. At X down to zero, F decays faster than every power and E=-A X^(r+1)+that remainder. Hypothesis (B10) therefore makes

    H(s)=integral_0^infinity E(X)X^(-s) dX/X

holomorphic on gamma<Re(s)<r+1, locally uniformly with every fixed derivative. Choose epsilon below each compact set's distance to gamma. Continuation of the product identity gives

    L(s,chi)H(s)=Gamma(s)L(s-r,chi).                   (B11)

By (B9), a zero in gamma<Re(s)<=1 contradicts (B11). The Euler product excludes Re(s)>1. At the principal pole, H has the compensating zero; it is not discarded as a bad point. This proof does not require assuming a bare zero-free strip already supplies a sharp Mertens bound. It proves a replacement detector's own sufficient return.

For gamma=.8748 the conditional target c=.1252 would exceed c11 by .0000540364. The basic r=2 principal cuts are alpha=.9374 and beta=1.0626. For gamma=5/6 they are 11/12 and 13/12; for gamma=3/4 they are 7/8 and 9/8. These are paid complementary regions, not successful estimates of their middle sum.

## 6. The strongest arithmetic obstruction: an actual semiprime corner

The mean-zero restoration is not oscillatory in every active range. Exactly B(y)=1 for 1<=y<2, since b(1)=1 and there are no other terms. Thus the top product band exp(v)/2<de<=exp(v) in H9 sees no restoration cancellation. Its coefficient remains the signed self-convolution of the actual long Möbius factors.

There is a quantified principal-character obstruction to treating its prime-prime portion as an independently affordable sector. Fix q, use its principal chi, and let P_X be the unramified primes in

    sqrt(3X/5) < p <= sqrt(7X/10).

For any of the H15 choices, these primes exceed Y for all large X. Let J=[L-c,L], with c=(1/2)log(5/4). On J by J, x=exp(t+u) lies in [4X/5,X], while every ordered distinct p,p' in P_X has product in (3X/5,7X/10]. Therefore 1<x/(pp')<2, and its FULL restoration sum equals1. Since mu(p)mu(p')chi(pp')=1, the exact isolated sector kernel on that square is

    |P_X|(|P_X|-1) exp(-a(t+u)).                      (H16)

The prime number theorem [NIST DLMF27.2.3](https://dlmf.nist.gov/27.2.E3), verified in the primary source, gives |P_X| asymptotic to
2(sqrt(7/10)-sqrt(3/5))sqrt(X)/log X. Removing fixed ramification changes nothing. Testing on exp(-at) restricted to J therefore gives the lower bound

    ||isolated actual sector|| >=
      |P_X|(|P_X|-1) X^-a (exp(2ac)-1)/(2a)
      >>_(a) X^(1-a)/(log X)^2.                     (H17)

This sector cannot separately meet X^(gamma-a+epsilon) for gamma<1 and sufficiently small epsilon. The statement concerns an ACTUAL restriction of H9, with its full restoration, not a synthetic oscillatory example. It is NOT a lower bound for the entire T, Gamma[c], Gamma[a], or T^lo. These distinct-prime pairs have gcd1, so they survive both paid arithmetic-sector removals. Moreover their own sharp-cutoff Fourier high-frequency norm is O(X^(1-a)/(Omega (log X)^2)): in H11 their weighted coefficient mass and endpoint are each O(X^(1-a)/(log X)^2). Hence H17 also survives on the ISOLATED low-frequency prime-pair operator when Omega tends to infinity. Other actual arithmetic sectors may cancel it, and they must remain jointly inside OPEN-LOW. No positivity or signed-subset inheritance is invoked. The useful reopening condition is an estimate for their joint low-frequency operator, retaining those cross-sector cancellations; the pure prime-prime sector itself is not a viable separately paid target.
