# [private research revision]: all-source forced-row bounds for the actual mixed linear probe

**Status: independently accepted by c21_forced_rows within the stated inputs and restricted linear-probe scope.** The claims below are relative to the exact inherited I-SEXTIC fields and ordinary smooth character Poisson stated here. They pay restricted parts of the original compensated linear probe. They do not estimate the remaining high-relative-conductor physical covariance and do not improve the accepted constant \(c_0=0.125113352960035869\ldots\).

Author: c20_triple_cayley. Prepared against published [private research revision] revision 0f532e01fdf8ad934dce69ba14fe0ddc4fba51b5 and the accepted [private research revision] FR proof.

## 1. Exact sources and input contract

Internal sources:

- [Main manuscript B0.21--B0.25](../../zeta_zero_free_validated_merged.md#b03-the-physical-probe-signed-gram-bound-and-compensator): the actual probe, the \(Y^{-3/2}\) additive source, the outside \(Q^{-1/2}\), the original profiles and the exact finite compensator.
- [T06.1--T06.3 and T06.6](../[private research revision]/[restricted mathematical source]#t06-the-complete-same-core-sextic-square-function): every embedded branch, the completed coefficient \(q_c^{-1/2}q_n^{-1}\), actual marked weight \(K_D\), and its uniform rapid envelope.
- [PC1--PC5](../[private research revision]-continuation/physical-covariance.md): exact prime-power Gauss support, natural zeros, fixed-place factors and primitive character completion.
- [FR3, FR6--FR10 and FR19](../[private research revision]/physical-forced-rows.md): interpolation with the actual forced divisor, including principal multiples of six. The current FR file records independent review; this record proves its separate linear application.

External provenance is pinned throughout to CrossNox commit
\[
\texttt{f677cc0a820bb2aff86bb4cbe783d076f5c097db}.
\]

- [gram_mixed.tex, lines 17--31](https://github.com/CrossNox/quasi-riemann-hypothesis-extension/blob/f677cc0a820bb2aff86bb4cbe783d076f5c097db/[restricted mathematical source]): raw source and completed-coefficient conventions.
- [Lines 145--240](https://github.com/CrossNox/quasi-riemann-hypothesis-extension/blob/f677cc0a820bb2aff86bb4cbe783d076f5c097db/[restricted mathematical source]): the active/passive split and compact row profile.
- [Lines 287--373](https://github.com/CrossNox/quasi-riemann-hypothesis-extension/blob/f677cc0a820bb2aff86bb4cbe783d076f5c097db/[restricted mathematical source]): the all-source Ramanujan identity and the nonsummable sixth-power tail in the unweighted refined count.
- [GramMixedArithmetic.lean](https://github.com/CrossNox/quasi-riemann-hypothesis-extension/blob/f677cc0a820bb2aff86bb4cbe783d076f5c097db/lean/GramMixedArithmetic.lean): the local transform and calibrated complete-mean identities. Its declarations do not assert the analytic block theorem proved below. No Lean rebuild is claimed.

The external identities are used as evidence and are derived in the local calculation below. The new estimate is the combination of that exact single-source reduction with a forced-row weight and its summable squareful-source Euler series.

**I-SEXTIC-XM.** Work over \(\mathcal O=\mathbb Z[\omega]\), with the original fixed excluded prime set \(S\), one primary generator for every good ideal, and the original finite unit/ray sectors. Write \(q_a=Na\). At each good prime the residue character has exact order six. Natural zero extensions, including those for positive exponents divisible by six, are retained. The fixed calibration \(\xi\) has fixed conductor, is nonprincipal, and is coprime to every good moving modulus. The original finite ray split puts source/completed reciprocity phases in row-independent coefficients; the only moving row character is \(\chi_A(m)\). All such coefficients have the inherited unit or fixed bounded size.

The source profiles \(W_0,W_1\) are the original smooth positive-annulus profiles; the completed profile is
\[
V(x)=\frac{1}{2\sqrt\pi}\exp(-(\log x)^2/4).
\]
The fixed slot count, fixed profile supports and fixed arithmetic data do not grow with \(Z\). The prime-slot weights are the actual bounded smooth weights, or their inherited divisor-bounded majorants.

**I-POISSON-XM.** Ordinary Poisson summation on the Eisenstein lattice is available for a primitive character of good conductor \(\mathfrak h\), multiplied by this fixed calibration. Its complete zero frequency is zero and its Gauss transform has modulus \(O_S(\sqrt{q_{\mathfrak h}})\). Section 3 gives the resulting row estimate, including subunit row scales. No I-HECKE, I-ZETA, Dedekind nonvanishing or higher moment estimate is used.

All scale parameters in the final probe application are in fixed polynomial ranges, with \(Q_D,Y_D\ge1\). Estimates for individual completed dyads are stated with their own small factors \((YCTNH_0Q)^\eta\), before summing the original infinite profile tails. This avoids treating infinite completed labels as polynomially bounded.

## 2. Three different conductors and the actual linear field

Retain exactly
\[
Q=q_{b_*}XY,\quad P_a=Y^2/Q,\quad
Y_D=Y/q_D,\quad Q_D=Q/q_D^2,\quad
L=\prod_iP_i,\quad L_D=P_{\mathcal J^c},\quad N_D=ZL_D.
\tag{XM1}
\]
Here \(D\) is the original product in the embedded slot subset \(\mathcal J\); \(q_D\asymp P_{\mathcal J}\), with constants depending only on the fixed slot supports. The ideal \(J\) below is a cube label, not this slot subset. The fixed factor \(q_{b_*}\) is never set to one.

For a source \(s\) and one completed index \(A=IJ^3\), with \(I\) squarefree, define
\[
\mathfrak h(s,A)=
\prod_{\substack{p\notin S\\v_p(A)-v_p(s)\not\equiv0\ (6)}}p,
\qquad h_{\rm act}(s,A)=q_{\mathfrak h(s,A)}.
\tag{XM2}
\]
It is the active conductor of a single mixed row, on its surviving local support. It is not the hybrid norm hypothesis \(\mathcal H\). It is also not PC's relative conductor
\[
R=q_{\prod_{\ell_p\ne0}p},\qquad
\ell_p=v_p(A)-v_p(A')-v_p(a)+v_p(b)\pmod6,
\tag{XM3}
\]
which occurs after multiplying two completed fields and their two outer Gauss factors.

Let \(x_s=q_s/Y\). The exact additive coefficient in T06.2 obeys
\[
Y^{-1}x_s^{-1/2}q_s^{-1/2}
=Y^{-3/2}x_s^{-1}.
\tag{XM4}
\]
Mellin inversion of the original \(W_0(q_m/(Qx_s))\) therefore produces the source polynomial
\[
\mathcal A_{\sigma,v}(m;Y)
=Y^{-3/2}\sum_{s\in\sigma}
c_\sigma(s)W_1(x_s)x_s^{-1+iv}g_s(-m).
\tag{XM5}
\]
Here \(g_s\) is the unnormalized source Gauss sum and \(c_\sigma\) retains exactly \(\chi_s(b_*)/(\tau\xi(s))\) and the row-independent finite phases. In particular it is bounded uniformly in \(s\). Any further finite sector index, including the completed ray \(t\) in T06.2, is suppressed in this notation. Its source phase \(R(t,s)\) and the corresponding constraint on the completed labels are both retained. Splitting the source into its finitely many rays makes this a finite sum of the displayed products; the subsequent bounds discard a ray restriction only after taking a positive majorant.

Because \(W_0,W_1\) have fixed positive-annulus supports, choose one smooth compact cutoff \(\Omega\) in a positive annulus, equal to one on all their possible physical-row products. Then the row function is exactly
\[
f_v(z)=\Omega(|z|^2)|z|^{-2iv}.
\tag{XM6}
\]
It has fixed-order Schwartz seminorms bounded by a polynomial in \(1+|v|\). The cutoff does not alter the physical sum.

The completed coefficient in our original field is
\[
\frac{\lambda(I,J)}{\sqrt{q_I}\,q_J}K_D(IJ^3),
\qquad |\lambda(I,J)|\ll_S1.
\tag{XM7}
\]
There is no additional power of a complementary marked product in \(K_D\). In the external window convention, for \(x=q_A/T\),
\[
\frac{q_J^{1/2}}{T^{1/2}}W(x)
=\frac{x^{1/2}W(x)}{\sqrt{q_I}\,q_J}.
\tag{XM8}
\]
Thus our completed profile on a \(q_A\asymp T\) dyad corresponds to \(W(x)=x^{-1/2}\) times that original dyadic profile. Since \(x\) stays in a fixed annulus, this is an exact change of window with bounded seminorms, not a lost coefficient or a change of the detector.

Every branch of the compensated probe is consequently a finite sum over the original ray sectors of
\[
(-1)^{|\mathcal J|}\omega_Dq_D^{-3/2}Q_D^{-1/2}
\int_{\mathbb R}\widehat W_0(iv)\,
\mathcal M_D(v)\,\frac{dv}{2\pi},
\tag{XM9}
\]
where \(\mathcal M_D\) is the raw row sum of (XM5), the completed coefficients (XM7), and \(\xi(m)f_v(m/\sqrt{Q_D})\). The element embedding \(m'=D^2m\) is injective. It introduces no density or Jacobian in this discrete linear sum.

## 3. Uniform row completion with the actual forced scale

Let \(\psi_{\mathfrak h}\) be primitive at every good prime of \(\mathfrak h\), extended by zero there. Since \(\xi\) is nonprincipal and has coprime fixed conductor, \(\xi\psi_{\mathfrak h}\) has zero complete mean, including when \(\mathfrak h=1\). Multiplication of the row by a good element coprime to \(\mathfrak h\) changes only a unit scalar in the character.

For every \(h>0\), a rotation of the profile in (XM6) obeys
\[
\left|\sum_{m\in\mathcal O}
\xi(m)\psi_{\mathfrak h}(m)f_v(m/\sqrt h)\right|
\ll (1+|v|)^{J_0}\min(\sqrt{q_{\mathfrak h}},h).
\tag{XM10}
\]
The term at zero is zero because the profile is supported away from zero.

For the first bound, Poisson gives, up to fixed constants and a fixed rotation, the majorant
\[
\frac h{\sqrt{q_{\mathfrak h}}}
\sum_{\ell\ne0}
\left|\widehat f_v\!\left(\sqrt{h/q_{\mathfrak h}}\,\ell\right)\right|.
\tag{XM11}
\]
If \(h/q_{\mathfrak h}\le1\), two-dimensional lattice counting and a fixed Schwartz seminorm bound the sum by \(O((1+|v|)^{J_0}q_{\mathfrak h}/h)\). If \(h/q_{\mathfrak h}\ge1\), choose Fourier decay of order greater than two; the result is again at most \(O((1+|v|)^{J_0}\sqrt{q_{\mathfrak h}})\). Fixed calibration levels change only the constants in these comparisons.

For the second bound, direct lattice counting in the fixed annulus gives \(O(h)\) when \(h\ge1\). For \(h<1\), the sum is empty below a fixed positive scale; on the remaining bounded interval, increasing the fixed constant gives the same \(O(h)\) estimate. No zero vector is counted. This proves (XM10).

In particular, for \(0\le\rho\le1\),
\[
|\mathrm{row}(h)|
\ll (1+|v|)^{J_0}
q_{\mathfrak h}^{(1-\rho)/2}h^\rho.
\tag{XM12}
\]
The proof never drops the divisor inside \(h\).

## 4. Exact reduction of every source power

Write the source uniquely as \(s=tu\), with \(t\) squarefree, \(u\) squareful and \((t,u)=1\). Put
\[
\mathfrak d_u=u/\operatorname{rad}(u),\qquad
\mathfrak r_u=\prod_{\substack{p\mid u\\6\nmid v_p(u)}}p,\qquad
\mathfrak e_u=\prod_{\substack{p\mid u\\6\mid v_p(u)}}p,
\]
\[
D_u=q_{\mathfrak d_u},\quad R_u=q_{\mathfrak r_u},\quad
E_u=q_{\mathfrak e_u},\quad U=q_u=D_uR_uE_u.
\tag{XM13}
\]

For a prime with source exponent \(a\ge2\), lifting the defining Gauss sum from \(p^a\) to \(p\) forces \(p^{a-1}\mid m\). If \(p\mid A\), the natural zero of \(\chi_A(m)\) then makes the mixed summand identically zero. Thus all survivors have \((u,A)=1\). This is a consequence of the original zero extension, not a new coprimality restriction.

After \(m=d_u z\), the nonprincipal local factor is \(q_p^{a-1}\) times a primitive Gauss sum of modulus \(\sqrt{q_p}\), times \(\chi_p(z)^{-a}\). At a principal exponent \(6\mid a\), the factor instead is
\[
q_p^{a-1}(q_p1_{p\mid z}-1).
\tag{XM14}
\]
Consequently, up to a unit scalar independent of \(z\),
\[
g_s(-d_uz)=
D_u\tau_{t,r_u}\chi_{t,r_u}(z)^{-1}
\prod_{p\mid\mathfrak e_u}(q_p1_{p\mid z}-1),
\qquad |\tau_{t,r_u}|=\sqrt{q_tR_u}.
\tag{XM15}
\]
The character on \(t\) has exponent one and the one on \(\mathfrak r_u\) has source exponent modulo six. All these exponents are nonzero.

Let \(\mathfrak h_0\) be the active radical from \(t,I,J\), and let
\(\mathfrak b_{\rm pas}=\operatorname{rad}(tIJ)/\mathfrak h_0\). Because \((u,tA)=1\), the full active conductor is the coprime product
\[
\mathfrak h=\mathfrak r_u\mathfrak h_0.
\tag{XM16}
\]
The primes of \(\mathfrak e_u\) are not inserted into the passive unit mask; their exact factors are (XM14).

Expand the Ramanujan product over \(f\mid\mathfrak e_u\), and the passive mask over \(b\mid\mathfrak b_{\rm pas}\). The full arithmetic row becomes
\[
\eta_{s,A}D_u\tau_{t,r_u}
\sum_{f\mid\mathfrak e_u}\mu(\mathfrak e_u/f)q_f\,\xi(f)\psi_{\mathfrak h}(f)
\sum_{b\mid\mathfrak b_{\rm pas}}\mu(b)\xi(b)\psi_{\mathfrak h}(b)
\sum_{z\in\mathcal O}\xi(z)\psi_{\mathfrak h}(z)
f_v(d_ufbz/\sqrt Q).
\tag{XM17}
\]
Here \(\eta_{s,A}\) is a row-independent unit incorporating the actual CRT phases, source factors, \(\chi_A(d_u)\) and \(\xi(d_u)\). The ideals \(f,b\) are coprime to \(\mathfrak h\) and to the calibration conductor. Their displayed character values therefore have modulus one. The last row has norm scale exactly
\[
h=Q/(D_uq_fq_b).
\tag{XM18}
\]
This proves the local identity needed for all sources, including sixth powers and all principal/nonprincipal mixtures.

## 5. Dyadic theorem and the summable squareful-source mass

Fix dyads \(q_s\asymp Y,\ q_I\asymp C,\ q_J\asymp N\), with \(I\) squarefree, \(C,N,Y\ge1\), and \(CN^3\asymp T\). Completed windows have bounded absolute value in their fixed annulus. Source phases and any extra row-independent label mask have modulus at most a fixed constant. One may retain any subset of these labels throughout the proof. No step below requires \(Y\ll T\), so completed dyads in the original lower Gaussian tail are covered as well.

For \(h_{\rm act}\le H_0\), apply (XM12) to (XM17). The passive divisor sum satisfies \(\sum_{b\mid\mathfrak b_{\rm pas}}q_b^{-\rho}\le\tau(\mathfrak b_{\rm pas})\). The principal divisor sum obeys
\[
\sum_{f\mid\mathfrak e_u}q_f^{1-\rho}
\le E_u^{1-\rho}\tau(\mathfrak e_u)
\qquad(0\le\rho\le1).
\]
After allowing a small divisor factor, the row bound is
\[
\ll (1+|v|)^{J_0}(YT)^\eta
Q^\rho H_0^{(1-\rho)/2}
D_u^{1-\rho}E_u^{1-\rho}\sqrt{q_tR_u}.
\]
Since \(q_t\asymp Y/U\), its last three arithmetic factors are
\[
D_u^{1-\rho}E_u^{1-\rho}\sqrt{q_tR_u}
\asymp \sqrt Y\,U^{1/2-\rho}R_u^{\rho-1/2}.
\tag{XM19}
\]

For a fixed \(u\), put \(g=(t,I)\). Every prime in \(t/g\) or \(I/g\) has a nonzero exponent after adding \(3v_p(J)\): the unequal squarefree exponents differ by one, and a multiple of three cannot cancel that difference modulo six. These two ideals and \(\mathfrak r_u\) are pairwise coprime. Therefore
\[
\frac{q_tq_I R_u}{q_g^2}\le h_{\rm act}\le H_0.
\tag{XM20}
\]
For a gcd dyad \(q_g\asymp G\), positive ideal counting gives
\[
\#\{(t,I):q_t\asymp Y/U,\ q_I\asymp C,\ (t,I)\asymp G\}
\ll \frac{YC}{UG}.
\]
Summing the dyads \(G\gg\sqrt{YC R_u/(UH_0)}\) gives
\[
\#(t,I)\ll
\min\!\left(\frac{YC}{U},
\sqrt{\frac{YC H_0}{UR_u}}\right).
\tag{XM21}
\]
If the lower gcd threshold is below one, the second expression is at least the first. If the reduced \(t\)-annulus is empty, there is no term. Reduced scales in a fixed bounded interval below one are covered by enlarging constants. Thus no false count at a subunit source scale is used.

There are \(O(N)\) cube labels \(J\). Their actual completed weight costs
\[
N\frac{N^{1/2}}{T^{1/2}}\asymp C^{-1/2}.
\tag{XM22}
\]
Multiplying (XM19), the second count in (XM21), (XM22), and the source normalizer \(Y^{-3/2}\) yields
\[
|\mathcal M_{C,N;\,u,h_{\rm act}\le H_0}|
\ll (1+|v|)^{J_0}(YT)^\eta
\frac{Q^\rho H_0^{1-\rho/2}}{\sqrt Y}
U^{-\rho}R_u^{\rho-1}.
\tag{XM23}
\]
The Euler series of the last factor is
\[
\sum_{u\ {\rm squareful}}U^{-\rho}R_u^{\rho-1}
=\prod_{p\notin S}
\left(1+
\sum_{\substack{a\ge2\\6\nmid a}}q_p^{-1-(a-1)\rho}
+\sum_{j\ge1}q_p^{-6j\rho}\right).
\tag{XM24}
\]
It converges for every fixed \(\rho>1/6\). Nonprincipal powers start with exponent \(1+\rho>1\); principal powers start with exponent \(6\rho>1\). Divisor losses in (XM23) may be bounded first by \((YT)^\eta\), since \(U\ll Y\) and all passive labels are bounded by \(YT\) on the dyad. They do not alter the convergent Euler exponents.

We obtain the new all-source theorem
\[
\boxed{
|\mathcal M_{C,N;\,h_{\rm act}\le H_0}|
\ll_{\rho,\eta}
(1+|v|)^{J_0}(YT)^\eta
\frac{Q^\rho H_0^{1-\rho/2}}{\sqrt Y},
\qquad 1/6<\rho\le1 .
}
\tag{XM25}
\]
The exponent \(J_0\) depends only on fixed profile seminorms. The estimate remains valid with bounded row-independent label masks; this includes overlaps when combining paid sectors. Arbitrary row-dependent masks are not allowed.

If \(Q,Y,H_0\) are in fixed polynomial ranges, choose
\(\rho=1/6+\delta_\epsilon\), with a fixed positive \(\delta_\epsilon\) sufficiently small for the prescribed loss. Since \(H_0\ge1\),
\[
Q^\rho H_0^{1-\rho/2}
\le Q^{1/6}H_0^{11/12}Q^{\delta_\epsilon}.
\]
After the completed-profile summation proved next, this gives
\[
\boxed{
|\mathcal M_{D;\,h_{\rm act}\le H_0}|
\ll_\epsilon (1+|v|)^{J_0}Z^\epsilon
\frac{Q_D^{1/6}H_0^{11/12}}{\sqrt{Y_D}}.
}
\tag{XM26}
\]
No contour or Euler series is evaluated on the divergent endpoint \(\rho=1/6\). The constant can depend on the chosen positive buffer.

## 6. Actual marks, every completed dyad and both infinite tails

For the embedded subset \(D\), retain exactly
\[
K_D(A)=
\sum_{\substack{U'\mid A\ {\rm in\ complementary\ slots}\\(U',D)=1}}
\omega_{U'}\overline{\eta(U')}V(q_A/(Zq_{U'})).
\tag{XM27}
\]
The symbols \(U'\) and \(u\) are unrelated: the former is a marked product and the latter is the squareful source part. The number of marked tuples dividing \(A\) is divisor-bounded. Also \(q_{U'}/L_D\) lies in a fixed compact multiplicative interval. Hence, for any prescribed small \(\eta>0\),
\[
|K_D(A)|\ll_\eta q_A^\eta E(q_A/N_D),
\tag{XM28}
\]
where \(E\) is nonnegative and decays faster than every power at both endpoints. This follows directly from the original Gaussian and bounded marked weights. In particular there is no separate count by the total complementary slot lengths and no factor \(q_{U'}^{-1/2}\).

On each \(q_A\asymp T\) dyad, (XM8) permits (XM25) with a bounded compact completed window, multiplied by \(T^\eta E_*(T/N_D)\), where \(E_*\) is another two-sided rapid envelope. For fixed \(T\), the number of nonempty pairs of core/cube dyads \(C,N\ge1\), \(CN^3\asymp T\), is \(O(1+\log(2T))\). Their bounded overlap and all unit choices cost only fixed constants or logarithms.

For every fixed \(\alpha>0\),
\[
\sum_{\substack{T=2^j\\j\ge0}}
(1+\log(2T))^B T^\alpha E_*(T/N_D)
\ll_{\alpha,B} N_D^\alpha(1+\log(2N_D))^B
\tag{XM29}
\]
when \(N_D\ge1\). To verify it, write \(T/N_D\) on geometric intervals. Above one use rapid upper-tail decay stronger than \(\alpha+B+2\); below one use rapid lower-tail decay stronger than \(B+2\). The resulting geometric sums converge, uniformly in the fractional position of \(N_D\) between dyads. A power of \(\log(2T)\) is bounded by a power of \(\log(2N_D)\) plus a fixed power of \(|\log(T/N_D)|\), which is absorbed by the same endpoint decay.

The finitely many bounded lower dyads include the unit ideal. The upper dyads are not truncated. Small powers of arbitrarily large \(A\) are absorbed using (XM29), with \(N_D\) polynomial in \(Z\). Source divisor losses contribute only \(Y_D^\eta\). Choose all these losses sufficiently small before fixing the final \(\epsilon\). This proves the full original-profile statement (XM26).

The passage from finite completed truncations agrees with the original field. Indeed, ideal counting and the same rapid envelope give, for every fixed small \(\eta>0\),
\[
\sum_{I,J}\frac{q_{IJ^3}^{\eta}}{\sqrt{q_I}\,q_J}
E(q_Iq_J^3/N_D)
\ll_\eta N_D^{1/2+\eta}\sum_Jq_J^{-5/2}<\infty.
\]
For the inner \(I\)-sum this uses the bound at scale \(N_D/q_J^3\); its subunit scales follow from rapid upper-tail decay. Source labels and physical rows are finite on their original annuli, and the Mellin density is integrable. Thus the original sum is absolutely defined before the sharper row estimates; taking its completed truncations and passing to the limit is legitimate.

All bounds were taken after the exact row calculation. The signed phases and the exact masks remain in the defining field; only their actual coefficient magnitudes were majorized. Thus the argument applies to a restricted linear probe without replacing its defining marks by an unrelated coefficient sequence.

The Mellin integral in (XM9) is now absolutely controlled by
\[
\int_{\mathbb R}|\widehat W_0(iv)|(1+|v|)^{J_0}\,dv<\infty.
\tag{XM30}
\]
This proves the all-height passage with the original window. Any real inverse completed height appears only as a modulus-one label phase and never needs differentiation. If it is integrated in the original inverse representation, its original rapidly decreasing density remains available. The proof does not create a moving profile depending on the chosen labels.

## 7. Exact all-branch linear-probe transfer

More generally let \(B_{\rm tar}>0\) be a fixed polynomial scale factor and suppose the cutoff in each nonempty branch satisfies
\[
1\le H_{0,D}\le Q_D^{10/11}B_{\rm tar}^{12/11}.
\tag{XM31}
\]
Then (XM26) gives a raw bound \(Q_DY_D^{-1/2}B_{\rm tar}Z^\epsilon\). The outside factor in (XM9) is
\[
|\omega_D|q_D^{-3/2}Q_D^{-1/2}
=\frac{|\omega_D|}{\sqrt Q\sqrt{q_D}}.
\]
Its product with the raw bound is exactly
\[
|\omega_D|q_D^{-2}\sqrt{Q/Y}\,B_{\rm tar}Z^\epsilon.
\tag{XM32}
\]
The source and row scales are those of this branch. There is no substitution of the common physical \(Q\) for \(Q_D\) inside its row estimate.

For each fixed slot subset, the original prime weights give
\[
\sum_D|\omega_D|q_D^{-2}
\ll_\epsilon Z^\epsilon
\prod_{i\in\mathcal J}\sum_{q_p\asymp P_i}q_p^{-2}
\ll_\epsilon Z^\epsilon\prod_{i\in\mathcal J}P_i^{-1}
\ll_\epsilon Z^\epsilon.
\tag{XM33}
\]
Bounded smooth weights and divisor-bounded variants are included by choosing smaller losses. There are finitely many subsets. Thus the original compensated linear probe restricted atomwise, in each branch, by (XM31) obeys
\[
\boxed{
|I^{\rm comp}_{\rm low\ act}|
\ll_\epsilon Z^\epsilon\sqrt{Q/Y}\,B_{\rm tar}.
}
\tag{XM34}
\]
This is an absolute bound after each arithmetic row sum, so an extra bounded row-independent label mask is permitted throughout.

Two useful choices are:

- \(B_{\rm tar}=P_a^{-\delta}\), \(\delta\ge0\): the all-source band
  \(h_{{\rm act},D}\le Q_D^{10/11}P_a^{-12\delta/11}\) costs
  \(Z^\epsilon\sqrt{Q/Y}P_a^{-\delta}\).
- \(B_{\rm tar}=P_a^{1/12}\): the band
  \(h_{{\rm act},D}\le Q_D^{10/11}P_a^{1/11}\) costs
  \(Z^\epsilon\sqrt{Q/Y}P_a^{1/12}\), the linear scale corresponding to the sufficient covariance target \(Y^{-1}P_a^{1/6}\).

If a displayed cutoff is below one, the corresponding good-conductor sector is empty. No nonempty branch with subunit conductor is introduced.

## 8. Existing large-cube branch, with its all-marked physical map

For completeness, the external all-source large-cube estimate also has a direct coefficient-preserving transfer. Here is the short proof needed to use its actual tails and marks.

For fixed squareful \(u\), use (XM17) with ordinary completion \(\sqrt{h_{\rm act}}\), and retain
\[
h_{\rm act}\le q_tR_u C N\ll YCN/(D_uE_u).
\]
The Gauss amplitude and principal divisor sum are at most
\[
D_u\sqrt{q_tR_u}\sum_{f\mid\mathfrak e_u}q_f
\ll (YT)^\eta\sqrt{YD_uE_u}.
\]
Their product with completion is therefore at most
\((YT)^\eta Y\sqrt{CN}\), independently of \(u\). There are \(O(YC/U)\) source/core pairs and \(O(N)\) cube labels. Multiplying their coefficients gives
\[
|\mathcal M_{C,N;u}|
\ll (1+|v|)^{J_0}(YT)^\eta
\frac{C\sqrt{YN}}U.
\]
The series \(\sum_{u\ {\rm squareful}}U^{-1}\) converges, proving
\[
|\mathcal M_{C,N}|
\ll (1+|v|)^{J_0}(YT)^\eta
C\sqrt{YN}
\asymp(1+|v|)^{J_0}(YT)^\eta T\sqrt Y\,N^{-5/2}.
\tag{XM35}
\]
This proof retains every source power.

Restrict \(q_J\ge N_0\ge1\), with \(N_0\) polynomial in \(Z\). The sum of \(N^{-5/2}\) over cube dyads \(N\gtrsim N_0\) is \(O(N_0^{-5/2})\). Summing \(T\) against (XM28), using the version of (XM29) with one extra factor \(T\), gives
\[
|\mathcal M_{D;\,q_J\ge N_0}|
\ll (1+|v|)^{J_0}Z^\epsilon
N_D\sqrt{Y_D}\,N_0^{-5/2}.
\tag{XM36}
\]
There is no assumption that the original Gaussian is compactly supported near \(N_D\).

Since \(N_Dq_D\asymp ZL\), multiplication by the physical branch factor and summation using (XM33) yield
\[
\boxed{
|I^{\rm comp}_{q_J\ge N_0}|
\ll_\epsilon Z^\epsilon
\frac{ZL\sqrt Y}{\sqrt Q\,N_0^{5/2}}.
}
\tag{XM37}
\]
In particular it costs \(Z^\epsilon\sqrt{Q/Y}B_{\rm tar}\) when
\[
N_0\gtrsim (ZLY/(QB_{\rm tar}))^{2/5}.
\tag{XM38}
\]
If the right side is below one, take \(N_0=1\). The low-active and large-cube sectors can be combined by disjointizing their intersection, because both proofs allow bounded row-independent label masks.

## 9. Exact remaining estimate and limitations

The useful new ingredient is (XM25)--(XM34), not a claim that the squarefree-source \(H_0/\sqrt Y\) bound already held for all sources. At \(\rho=0\), the refined fixed-\(u\) calculation would give \(H_0/(\sqrt Y R_u)\). For \(u=b^6\), \(R_u=1\); its sum is not subpower. The forced row scale supplies \(U^{-\rho}\), and (XM24) prices precisely what is needed. It incurs the explicit \(Q^\rho\) cost. Thus the sharper all-source \(H_0/\sqrt Y\) estimate remains open.

FR resolves the same local principal-power sparsity issue in a different aggregate. Its normalized local kernel
\[
q^{a/2}1_{p^a\mid r}-q^{a/2-1}1_{p^{a-1}\mid r}
\]
is the normalized form of (XM14) with its forced \(p^{a-1}\) support. FR multiplies two such kernels and combines shared divisors by their maximum. Here there is one source Gauss kernel and one completed character, so the single-source counting and the optimum interpolation endpoint are different.

No relative-conductor inclusion suitable for PC follows from one small active conductor. For example, take coprime good cores \(A=p,A'=q\) and outer labels \(a=pw,b=qw\), with \(w\) coprime to \(pq\). Both individual active conductors can be \(\operatorname{rad}(w)\), arbitrarily large, while their relative conductor is one. Conversely one small active conductor can pair with a large one and leave large relative conductor. Calibration cancels against its conjugate in the covariance, whereas it remains nonprincipal in the linear row calculation.

Accordingly neither (XM34) nor (XM37) proves a new sector of PC's atom-pair covariance beyond the current FR theorem. The target
\[
\mathcal C_{<,\,R>(QY)^{4/9}}
\ll Y^{-1}P_a^{1/6}Z^\epsilon
\tag{OPEN-XM-COV}
\]
at small true core gcd remains unproved here. T07's true-gcd conductor and its I-HECKE-dependent tail are unchanged.

There is instead an exact alternative linear residual: with \(B_{\rm tar}=P_a^{1/12}\), retain in every branch
\[
h_{{\rm act},D}>Q_D^{10/11}P_a^{1/11},
\qquad
q_J\lesssim (ZLY/(QP_a^{1/12}))^{2/5},
\tag{OPEN-XM-LIN}
\]
with the original source/core/cube repetitions, marks, phases, profiles and all heights. Bounding that remaining signed linear sum by
\(Z^\epsilon\sqrt{Q/Y}P_a^{1/12}\) would complete this alternative estimate for the probe. The present argument does not bound it. No lower bound for a completed-row norm and no arbitrary independent coefficient replacement has been used.

## 10. Independent-review contract

Independent review accepted the following consequential steps:

1. (XM4)--(XM9): the source \(Y^{-3/2}\), completed half-power/window identity, \(Q_D^{-1/2}\), \(q_D^{-3/2}\), and discrete embedding map.
2. (XM10)--(XM18): fixed calibration remains nonprincipal; both exact Ramanujan coefficients survive; \(f,b\) are coprime to the active conductor; the row norm scale is \(Q/(D_uq_fq_b)\), including subunit scales.
3. (XM20)--(XM25): the gcd-count factor \(R_u^{-1/2}\), the cube coefficient \(C^{-1/2}\), and the exact Euler weight \(U^{-\rho}R_u^{\rho-1}\), with a strictly buffered \(\rho>1/6\).
4. (XM27)--(XM30): marks are bounded through the actual \(K_D\), with no new slot-length factor; all core/cube dyads and both Gaussian tails are included; all-height integration uses only fixed profile seminorms.
5. (XM31)--(XM38): each embedded branch uses its own \(Q_D,Y_D\), the final weight is \(|\omega_D|q_D^{-2}\), and the large-cube tail sum uses the first moment of the original rapid envelope.
6. The conclusion is an absolute estimate for restricted linear probes. It does not promote the high-relative-conductor covariance, the hybrid hypothesis, or a larger zero-free constant.

The independent review was an argument check, separate from document integrity. No broader covariance or zero-free claim was accepted.

## 5. Two representations of each actual far annulus

On rows outside the paid prefix set, F7 implies |F_R,u(rho_u)|>=1/2 for large U. Decompose the original product norm n into a smooth fixed dyadic partition, retaining the full factor1-H(Nn/L), the exponential and the terminal cutoff. There are O(log U) nonempty product annuli. For at least one fixed annular scale X=U^ell the actual polynomial T_X,u has magnitude at least U^(-tau), for any preassigned small tau after the common thresholds. Its scale is above t+lambda-o(1). The precise original profile, including both transition cutoffs, remains common.

For any such annular weight W_X(Ndm), the two finite representations are

    T_X,u=sum_(d,m)mu(d)phi_u(d)phi_u(m)(Ndm)^(-s)
                              V(Nd/R)W_X(Ndm),
    T_X,u=-sum_(d,m)mu(d)phi_u(d)phi_u(m)(Ndm)^(-s)
                           [1-V(Nd/R)]W_X(Ndm).        (F14)

Both equations hold for every row, not only zero rows. No d,m coprimality is inserted. The first has d<=2R; the second has d>R. The missing common prime factors retain their natural zeros. Original slots can subsequently multiply either entire expression without changing their pool or coefficient.

Split d,m into smooth dyads and apply B3.3 to the coupled product weight before live row selection. A nonempty subunit dyad is replaced by length zero with a bounded dilation, exactly as in B3.3; it contains only boundedly many ideals. All Euler derivatives of V(Ax),1-V(Ax),1-H(A'xy) and exp(-A''xy) are bounded uniformly in positive dilation parameters on fixed annuli. Tail orders are chosen after the raw polynomial bounds. The two representations therefore each supply a saturated product of the source polynomials M and S, with one common frequency inside that pair. The selected frequencies for the two representations need not agree and are not identified.

Write (r_-,m_-) for a selected product from the first representation and (r_+,m_+) for one from the second. With errors O(tau),

    r_-<=t, r_+>=t,
    r_-+m_-=ell=r_++m_+,
    |M_-(U^r_- )S_-(U^m_- )|^2>=U^[delta ell-O(tau)],
    |M_+(U^r_+ )S_+(U^m_+ )|^2>=U^[delta ell-O(tau)]. (F15)

The real power is the same actual sigma_u for both products. Common-profile Fourier powers can translate their heights independently. The inverse profiles retain V or1-V at the original R. Inverse profiles are not redefined after shortening or saturation. All lengths are initially in a fixed polynomial range determined by B, so B0.15 and the free inverse moment are applicable; this is not an invocation of Lemma1W with an unlicensed truncation.

Comparing F15 with F4 first forces m_-,m_+<=1/2+O(tau), since delta>=17/25. Dividing by the other factor's pointwise upper bound then gives all four witness inequalities

    |M_-(U^r_-)|^2>=U^[delta r_- -O(tau)],
    |S_-(U^m_-)|^2>=U^[delta m_- -O(tau)],
    |M_+(U^r_+)|^2>=U^[delta r_+ -O(tau)],
    |S_+(U^m_+)|^2>=U^[delta m_+ -O(tau)].              (F16)

This is the same saturated-witness reasoning as the literal B0.17--20, now applied separately to two exact presentations of one fixed far annulus. It keeps their dependence. In particular, ell>t+1/2 plus a fixed margin cannot support the original product at a zero: every original m then exceeds1/2 by a margin, and F4 makes the annular contribution too small. All such far annuli are accounted for; they are not an unpaid long-product tail.

Finite dyads and label choices are handled by a union bound. The Fourier continuum and rowwise real/height parameters use the source's common finite measure and Sobolev bound, with their prescribed seminorms and polynomial height costs. No moving arithmetic coefficient is absorbed into that measure. If desired fix a deterministic admissible choice among the saturated witnesses; the bounds below also cover the union of every easy witness, so the choice cannot conceal an unpaid population.

## 3. L1–10: the complete signed logarithmic criterion

### 3.1 Green comparison and the loss

Translate a maximizer t0 to0. A length-one interval I containing0 lies in [-1,1]. Put h=f/f(0), A=log(B/|f(0)|), v=A-log|h|. If f is analytic on a neighborhood of the closed disk of radius R>=16 and has no boundary zero, then v>=0 and

    v(z)=H(z)+sum_a G_R(z,a),
    G_R(z,a)=log |(R^2-conj(a)z)/(R(z-a))|,
    v(0)=A.                                                  (Q1)

The sum is finite and counts multiplicities. Removing the disk Blaschke factors proves the identity; H is the positive harmonic extension of the nonnegative boundary data. The logarithmic singularities at real zeros are integrable. Since f(0) is nonzero, a=0 never occurs.

For H, the Poisson kernel gives H(t)<=((R+1)/(R-1))H(0). For a zero with |a|<=sqrt R,

    G_R(t,a)-G_R(0,a)
      =log|1-conj(a)t/R^2|+log|a|-log|t-a|.

The first term is <=R^(-3/2). If |a|<=2, the integral of -log|t-a| on any unit interval is <=1+log2: setting Im(a)=0 can only increase it, and centering the real singularity maximizes it. Adding log|a|<=log2 leaves a bound below4. If |a|>2, |t-a|>=|a|-1 gives a pointwise log ratio <=log2. Since G_R(0,a)>=.5 log R, the integrated difference is at most (8/log R)G_R(0,a).

For |a|>sqrt R the Green function is positive harmonic on the smaller disk. Its Harnack ratio is at most (sqrt R+1)/(sqrt R-1)<=1+8/log R. The same larger factor bounds the ratio for H. Summing Q1 proves precisely

    integral_I log|f| >= log|f(0)|
                       -(8/log R) log(B/|f(0)|).             (Q2)

No assumed zero separation, zero density, multiplicity cap or positivity of f enters. Boundary zeros can be avoided by choosing a radius within the allowed interval; discrete zeros prohibit only finitely many radii there. The proof is stronger evidence than the author's finite Green samples, which are only diagnostics.

For fixed coefficients with A_b=sum |a_n| n^(-b)<infinity, completing the square yields

    |F(z)| <= (2pi tau)^(-1/2) A_b
       exp(b Re z+tau b^2/2+(Im z)^2/(2tau)).                 (Q3)

It also proves locally uniform convergence and entire analyticity. For f3(n)chi(n), b>1 suffices and |a_n|<=1. Let M_j=max_[j,j+1]|F| and J_j=integral_[j,j+1]log|F|. The nonzero Mellin transform on Re(s)>1 proves F is not identically zero; therefore J_j is finite and M_j>0. Choose R in[sqrt j,2sqrt j] avoiding boundary zeros. Q3 gives log B <=(b+2/tau)j+O(sqrt j+1). Thus

    (1+eta_j)log M_j <= J_j+eta_j log B,
    eta_j=8/log R=O(1/log j).                                (Q4)

For each fixed gamma, J_j<=(gamma+epsilon)j+C_epsilon on EVERY sufficiently large integer interval implies log M_j<=(gamma+epsilon)j+O(j/log j). Use a smaller epsilon first. The reverse bound J_j<=log M_j is immediate. Constants are fixed before j grows. Negative contributions near zeros cannot mask a larger exponential maximum in this fixed Gaussian class.

There is also an immediate complete-moment equivalence worth making explicit. Jensen on a unit interval gives

    J_j <= .5 log integral_[j,j+1]|F(u)|^2 du.                (Q5)

A fixed number of complete dyadic log shells covers that interval. Consequently an all-shell moment exponent gamma implies the signed-log bound; Q4 returns the pointwise exponent, which implies the moment bound. Every-epsilon allowances absorb the fixed coverings and o(j) loss. Thus L6 is a new exact description of the same exponent problem, not evidence that the arithmetic hypothesis is weaker in consequence. Finite intervals, a subsequence, or an average over j do not suffice.

### 3.2 Literal coefficients and zero return

Write z_p=chi(p)p^(-s), with chi(p)=0 at ramified primes. f3 has value-1 at every positive p-power for p!=3 and+1 at every 3-power. Therefore

    D_chi(s)=sum f3(n)chi(n)n^(-s)=N_chi(s)H_chi(s)/L(s,chi),
    N_chi=1-2z_2,
    H_2=(1-z_2)^(-2), H_3=(1-z_3)^(-2),
    H_p=(1-2z_p)/(1-z_p)^2, p>=5.                           (Q6)

This checks all powers, including2 and3, rather than substituting a squarefree or completely multiplicative surrogate. Both H and its inverse have absolutely summable coefficients at each fixed weight sigma>1/2: large-prime local corrections start at z_p^2 and 2/sqrt5<1. Their finite small-prime factors have no pole or zero in that half-plane. If2 is unramified the zeros of N have real part1; if it is ramified N=1. Thus N H is nonzero for1/2<Re(s)<1 at every finite height.

On Re(s)>1 absolute Gaussian Fubini gives

    integral_R F_chi(u)e^(-su)du=exp(tau s^2/2)D_chi(s).    (Q7)

The original left Gaussian tail pays this integral and every fixed s-derivative on compacta as u->-infinity. An all-interval bound at gamma pays the right tail locally uniformly for Re(s)>gamma. This proves holomorphic continuation of the left side without assuming reciprocal polynomial growth in an unbounded strip. Multiply by L and continue on gamma<Re(s)<1. At any zero there the right numerator in Q6–7 is nonzero, contradiction, with multiplicities included. The principal pole at1 is outside that open strip and cannot be silently divided through; the inherited known right edge is separate. No uniform-in-height reciprocal estimate was used for this one-way return.

Each fixed ordinary character needs its own arithmetic bound. Integer CRT below gives neither an ideal theorem nor a growing-conductor estimate. The general analytic Q2–4 applies to a fixed ideal Gaussian only after its absolute norm-series bound and original pole bridge are established separately. The current original Eisenstein family is not imported by name alone.

For the present source, gamma<.874861 would improve the accepted c6; gamma=5/6 and3/4 conditionally return the respective open1/6 and1/4 strips. No such new gamma is proved. W21-T29 was an UNTESTED logarithmic-action seed for a different compact detector; W21-T28's smooth-signal counterexample remains valid under its weaker smoothness hypotheses. W38's exceptional-dyad construction is also not overturned. W39 and [private research revision] observation already used Gaussian analytic growth. The proposed delta is the signed Green comparison and its explicit every-interval return, with these ancestors retained.

### 3.3 The finite upper certificate

L8 is a correct uniform tail bound when the integer cutoff N>=exp(j+1). The function t->g_tau(log t-u) is decreasing for t>=N and u in[j,j+1], so the omitted sum is bounded by its integral from N. Completing the square under t=exp(v) gives

    T_(N,j)=exp(j+1+tau/2)
       barPhi((log N-j-1-tau)/sqrt tau).                    (Q8)

For b>1 the derivative bound is also correct. Writing w=b tau+t bounds
|w| exp(-t^2/(2tau))/tau by b+1/sqrt(e tau); summing n^(-b)<=1+1/(b-1) gives the author's explicit K_j. For any certified T>=T_(N,j)>0, log(|F_N|+T) is K_j/T-Lipschitz even through zeros. The midpoint quadrature error on length1 is K_j/(4MT). Certified absolute evaluation errors delta_k then give L10 with the correct upper inequality. This does not interchange log and an uncontrolled small additive error.

Choosing N=ceil(exp(j+1+C sqrt j)) with a strict C^2/(2tau)>1-gamma+eta margin permits T=exp((gamma-eta)j) eventually. Choosing M>=exp((b-gamma+2eta)j) makes the quadrature error O(exp(-eta j)). It is a finite, potentially costly per-interval certificate, not an all-j algorithmic proof of its arithmetic success. G63/Sol02 auditS31 already own complete Gaussian finite-tail/quadrature methodology; the logarithmic regularization and Q2 are the useful present adaptation.

## 4. C, D and E: useful failures in their exact scopes

### C: actual rough-prime zero law

The full two-variable product `(1-z)(1-w)` has no zero in the open unit polydisk; deleting its top face gives `1-z-w`, with the zero (1/2,1/2). For k singleton variables the maximal common open polydisk radius is 1/k, by the triangle inequality and the equal-coordinate witness. This is an elementary coefficient calculation, not an application of Lee–Yang theory.

The actual polynomial `sum_(n<=5)mu(n)n^-s=1-2^-s-3^-s-5^-s` is negative at 1 and positive at 2, with positive derivative on the real line. Its unique real zero above 1 belongs to this cutoff polynomial; it says nothing contradictory about 1/zeta.

For the stronger scalable example, retain exactly

    H_N(s)=sum_(n<=N, P^-(n)>sqrt N)mu(n)n^-s
          =1-sum_(sqrt N<p<=N)p^-s.                    (R12)

P^-(1)=infinity. Any composite with every prime factor strictly above sqrt N exceeds N; equality at a lower prime boundary is excluded. For large N this source also has the actual f3 values, since all retained nonunit primes exceed 3. Thus the prime-power, strict-endpoint and sign identities are literal.

The only external analytic input needed is `pi(t)=li(t)+o(t/log t)`, a consequence of the prime number theorem stated in [NIST DLMF 27.12](https://dlmf.nist.gov/27.12#E5), independently opened on 12 October 2026. No latest-error claim or power saving is imported. Put `L=log N`, `f_lambda(t)=t^(-1+lambda/L)`, with lambda in a fixed compact set. Stieltjes integration against the prime-counting error E gives endpoint errors `o(1/L)` and

    |integral_(sqrt N)^N E(t)f_lambda'(t)dt|
       <= C sup_(t>=sqrt N)(|E(t)|log t/t)
                    integral_(sqrt N)^N dt/(t log t)=o(1).

The constants are uniform on that compact lambda set. Substitution `t=N^v` in the main term gives

    sum_(sqrt N<p<=N)p^(-1+lambda/L)
       =I(lambda)+o(1), I(lambda)=integral_(1/2)^1 e^(lambda v)dv/v.
                                                               (R13)

I(0)=log2<1, I is strictly increasing, and I tends to infinity. Its unique positive solution I(lambda*)=1 traps the finite crossing by uniform convergence. The finite prime sum decreases strictly with real s, is >1 at s=0 and eventually <1 at s=1. Therefore its unique positive crossing satisfies

    sigma_N=1-lambda*/log N+o(1/log N), lambda*>0.      (R14)

The numerical lambda value is diagnostic only. R14 is a complete written proof based on R13. It refutes blanket inheritance of Euler-product nonvanishing by these precise rough cutoff cells. It also exhibits an exact wall between the unit term and the aggregate prime block that a tropical argument must pay. It does not show that every tropical decomposition or compensated partition source fails, or estimate the complete signed f3 Gaussian energy. The omitted small-prime/composite contributions may be indispensable cancelling terms.

### D: exact but already credited

`V_P=exp(sum_(p<=P)p^-s) product_(p<=P)(1-p^-s)` has

    log V_P=-sum_(p<=P)sum_(j>=2)p^(-js)/j,
    (1-z)e^z=1-sum_(j>=2)(j-1)z^j/j!.

These converge normally, with upper and lower modulus bounds on each `Re s>=rho>1/2`, since the first-prime channel was removed. Restoring it is not paid by bounding higher clusters. Under the separate open fixed-power prime-counting error, integration including the prime-2 atom gives

    D(s)=s integral_2^infinity [pi(u)-li_2(u)]u^(-s-1)du,
    1/zeta(s)=(s-1)V(s)exp(-J(s)-D(s)),
    J'(s)=(1-2^(1-s))/(s-1),

with J's constant fixed on Re s>1. The displayed derivative is entire after the removable value at 1, and the factor s-1 handles the principal pole. This matches W36 R36.20–22 verbatim in mathematical content, already credited to [private research revision] A12/W21 there. Ordinary PNT is not the missing fixed-power bound. No additional high-ceiling result is awarded to selected07.

### E: exact finite decoder obstruction

If a syndrome fibre contains opposite parities x,y, `delta_x-delta_y` lies in the kernel of all unsigned fibre sums but has nonzero signed parity readout. If parity is retained, normalized disjoint fibre rows `1_F/sqrt(|F|)` reconstruct it with coefficients `epsilon(F)sqrt(|F|)`, squared norm `sum|F|=2^k`. Both statements are exact. They concern arbitrary inputs on a uniform cube, not a lower bound on the actual detector. A source-specific decoder with a separately paid restricted input class remains open. W38/W41 already require the unexposed arithmetic parity covariance; E does not erase it.

## 4. The other sextic mechanisms: restriction, probe correlation, numerator and calibration

### F04.H — Short-divisor H

The baseline reflected estimate has \((K+NB)B\{N+L+(NL)^{2/3}\}\); H replaces \(K+NB\) by \(K\) for the actual family in
\[
K<NB\le KZ^{.006322},\qquad u_h=z_a,
\]
with every frozen physical branch, three cusp sources, powerful part, phase, mask, original profile and polynomial height. The accepted saved geometry is
\[
(\ell,\tau,x,y,h)\approx
(.170813789154,.006321367462,.374341141388,.461166436920,.796472647766).
\]
Its physical and numerator inequalities are jointly certified. Changing only a physical term or using the old numerator at a new stationary point is insufficient.

All-source large common quadratic cores are paid. For the **infinity/\(b=1\) projected branch**, both removed diagonals and projected divisors \(q_e\ge N/K\) are paid; the remaining short range contains \(e=1\). This localization is not automatically a reduction of every other source. The exact column is
\[
f(e)\chi_R(e)^3
\sum_P {a(P)\over\sqrt{q_P}}1_{(R,P)=1}\chi_P(e)^{-2}
\sum_{\substack{u\ \mathrm{sf}\\(u,e)=1}}
\mu(u)\Xi_R(u)g_{-1}(u,e^4R^3P^4)W(eu,P).
\tag{H-col}
\]
Retain both pair exclusions \(u\ne v\) and \(Pu\ne Qv\). The Fourier-index norm \(E^4K^3L^4\) is not automatically the conductor. At divisor scale \(E\), a row-character conductor can be \((N/E)^2\), with dual norm \((N/E)^2/K\). A pointwise complete-sum bound does not price the original window.

Three honest children remain. **Restriction after mark averaging:** estimate the actual normalized theta column at its moving horosphere, after summing rows/marks, rather than using its global source norm. **Coupled reciprocity:** retain the Möbius coefficient, Gauss variable, mark and row through a two- or three-variable transform; pass the known two-/three-prime cocycle tests. A smaller arithmetic child completes the u-sum at fixed sparse index before any sieve, keeping μ(u)Ξ_R(u) and all collision masks; its cost must still fit the original u-window. **Short-divisor interpolation:** seek an \(E\)-dependent improvement on \(N/(KE)\), beginning at the lowest dyad; a partial bound matters only after all dyads fit the complete certificate. New higher-cover or trace-formula machinery must first produce H-col with its exact local data.

### F04.P — Full probe correlation, distinct from a raw Gram improvement

The raw A-Gram has a real positive exceptional term \((Q/Y)P_a^{1/6}\). Its Cauchy excess in the original geometry is \((y-x)/12\). This does not lower-bound the compensated pairing against the actual theta B-field. A direct coefficient-specific pairing theorem is therefore a legitimate alternative to improving the raw energy.

The rigorous conditional target is **PROBE** in §2. A14 contains the complete checked constants; .1255 requires a uniform probe saving .0006, only part of the Cauchy excess at that certified geometry. The quantities called “sixth-power frequencies” depend on the pair in the Gram expansion. No coordinate vector \(A^{(6)}\) or bilinear projection onto it has been constructed. The first task for a narrower pairing conjecture is an exact polarization or positive-operator factorization, or a direct theta-paired identity whose sum equals the full probe. Until then, estimate the full probe.

A stronger saving can always be weakened to a smaller one. The detached stationary window obtained by insisting on equality \(\sigma=(y-x)/12\) does not forbid incremental consequences of a hypothetical stronger theorem. Also retain the old numerator's \(b>.87\) applicability wall; the displayed PROBE certificates do not establish a route to arbitrary \(c\).

### F04.N / F12 — Correlated numerator witness

The numerator statistic, inverse witness and prime-slot witnesses live on the same amplitude class. Their current treatment can discard correlation. Form their exact common-row mixed moment, with every shift and scale supremum from M B0.41–44, before Hölder. A useful alternative statement says that rows saturating the numerator cannot simultaneously saturate the inverse and mark witnesses, with a quantitative total contribution bound.

At \(c=.12551,\tau=0\), B's stationary calculation suggests an additional \(U^{-.0021657669\ldots}\) in the binding numerator class near \((\delta,p)=(.46930669,1/2)\). This is a diagnostic target, not a global certificate or proved slack. Read the actual leading term first. The truncated convolution \(\sum_{de=n}\mu(d)W(d/D)V(e/E)\) retains a long edge; \(\mu*\mathbf1=\delta\) cannot cancel independent cutoffs. If a useful signed main term survives, rerun the full certificate with the old bound on complementary classes. If the leading statistic already matches its budget, stop that particular comparison and try a genuinely joint large-values statement.

### F09/F11/F16 — Adaptive probes and mixed compensators

The retained object is the full positive **physical-field** Gram \(G_Z\), principal map \(P\), and growing nuisance map \(E\). Minimize physical energy under \(PW=p\), or use A04's calibrated separation in the true coefficient metric. Singular ranges and nullspaces must be checked before pseudoinversion. A-dependent weights remain open; the rejected A-independent componentwise construction kills both physical principal aliases. A frozen single-column toy can cancel its own signal and is not a viable test.

Try a small family of genuinely distinct A-dependent weights on two unfrozen completed classes; alternatively penalize expensive modes rather than annihilating them; or pair two different embedded slot patterns. In each case keep the mixed numerator covariance and subpower coefficient/profile costs. For embeddings \(D,E\), common rows are \([D,E]^2r\), while original rows are \(e^2r,d^2r\); quotient squares create moving cubic marks. Same-tuple subset supports are disjoint, but cross-tuples can overlap. Regrouping all marks was already allowed and still has completed length \(ZL\).

A derivative or additional Euler jet is admissible only after its principal residue is nonzero and its six valuation classes, nonunit zeros, repeated-prime levels and worst numerator witness are computed. Changing constants inside the old exponent certificate cannot raise \(c\). This cluster is medium-term: finite feasibility screens are cheap, but growing-family conditioning is the missing theorem.

# W55 independent review: paid moving Riesz comparison and two parked audits



**Verdict.** Retain A2-A3 as a useful, source-exact, second-order moving-Riesz-to-fixed-exponential comparison. Its constants, full complements, natural character zeros and shell return are valid. Retain B as a complete fixed-modulus/all-character rank-matching equivalence, within established transport ancestry. Retain C as an exact signed renewal criterion and a scoped failure of absolute small gain. None proves the remaining arithmetic estimate, a native H bound or a new c. I found no material mathematical error in the final developed statements. The inaccurate S09 seed equation and S21 subcomplex suggestion were already explicitly corrected by the author without changing the seed record.

Independent protected S28 yields a precise conservation obstruction for ordinary two-marginal couplings, an exact finite total-variation dual, and a paid repair using the actual divisor inverse and its full signed interval response. Independent uniform S15 yields exact resonant-mode elimination with all feedback and source terms; its application to the literal H tensor is still unbuilt. These are scoped audit additions, not arithmetic improvements or new general inversion/Schur methods.

The accepted written source-relative calibration is c11=312864909/2500000000=.1251459636, theta11=.8748540364. A first gain needs a proved common gamma<theta11; the corresponding raw squared-energy threshold is 1.7497080728. F0/analytic ancestry, inherited positive-slot uniformity and external definitions/import/admission remain OPEN. The old actual positive-slot receipt is separate. W55 receives no credit for the accepted endpoint.

## 1. Frozen evidence, selection and independent chronology

Author report: 29,324 bytes, SHA256 `a746782750a6d0d5c07eb687b55ab90296028d5eaf0a0e367e85ecf0aef74a43`. Author manifest: `2fa56c887c5a607a2e6573cdaad45c889c347ae067d27b99f751bac5fb6515cc`; it binds fourteen artifacts. All fourteen complete byte streams were independently read, hash-verified and decoded; JSON was parsed and Python syntax parsed. The entire report, seed packet, selection code, check code and relevant source material were model-read. The large numeric receipt was fully parsed/hash-bound; not every numeric row was printed to the model. I did not run an author helper or alter an author receipt.

Author STOP/release/absence was observed before intake. Its freeze is 11:44:29 UTC and final readback/release verification 11:45:13. The sole final wake is not evidence of theorem acceptance. The existing critic claim, acquired at 11:28:41 after W54 release, was retained rather than reacquired or replaced.

My seed-only preparation froze at 11:32:40, before author selections or outcomes were read. Its five original files total 12,228 bytes; their hashes and the original full thirty-card data remain unchanged. `prep-freeze.json` SHA256 is `168035a7fcb75981d6a77f97e763ee0f2516372699fadeeafc3102a15dcda5fb`. The priority begins S28,S27,S24,S15. A single saved uniform rank in [0,30!) was decoded into one complete permutation; its beginning is S19,S15,S18,S26. No entropy was generated during final review. At 11:46:28 the mechanical exclusion of the six author tests selected **protected S28** and **uniform S15**. S19 is skipped because the author tested it. Both original orders, the full pool and all probabilities are retained, not rerolled. The author wake's abstract and manifest had arrived before this mechanical selection; the priority and random ordering had already been frozen before outcomes. The outcome-bearing report was read only afterward.

The author's literal sampling is correct. Deliberate S03/S24 are removed first. All remaining groups contribute to the strict p<.10 pool of 23; saved byte12 gives index12/S19. The remaining strict p<.01 pool has12; byte205 gives index1/S10. S14 is then reserved as most different. The remaining wildcard pool has25; byte16 gives index16/S21. Each pool hash matches its draw receipt. The byte acceptance cutoffs are253,252,250, respectively, so the recorded uniform sampler is unbiased; there were no rejected bytes or rerolls. S08's p=1/10 and S18's p=1/100 are correctly excluded at their strict boundaries. There was no group-based exclusion of rarer cards. The author used two deliberate strongest cards; the frozen recipe imposes no contradictory numerical reservation rule. Typicalities are subjective generation labels, not probabilities that a theorem is true.

The six first tests remain S03,S24,S19,S10,S14,S21; only S03/S24/S10 were developed. My two parked audits do not retroactively increase the author's test count. S09's later algebra screen is separately identified. All thirty cards remain below, including the untested ones.

## 2. A: independent proof audit and exact limits

Fix an ordinary Dirichlet character chi, including principal, imprimitive and complex characters, with its natural zeros. Put a(n)=mu(n)chi(n), M(t)=sum(n<=t)a(n),

    E(x)=sum(n>=1)a(n)exp(-n/x),
    R_r(N)=sum(n<=N)a(n)(1-n/N)^r,
    B_r(x)=R_r(rx),  V_r(x)=2B_(2r)(x)-B_r(x).

At n=N the Riesz weight is zero. There is no squarefree or unramified sector substituted for the actual full coefficient sequence: those zeros are supplied by a itself.

### 2.1 Fixed field and all-height return

For Re s>1, absolute Fubini and t=n/x give exactly

    Mellin(E)(s)=Gamma(s)/L(s,chi),
    Mellin(R_r)(s)=Gamma(s)Gamma(r+1)/(Gamma(s+r+1)L(s,chi)).

For fixed r>0 the latter multiplier is holomorphic and nonzero on Re s>0. The beta integral and Gamma's absence of zeros are independently supported by [DLMF 5.12.1](https://dlmf.nist.gov/5.12) and [DLMF 5.2](https://dlmf.nist.gov/5.2). These sources support the special-function facts; the arithmetic identities follow from the displayed coefficient calculation.

If, for every epsilon>0 and every sufficiently large dyadic X, the L2(dx/x) norm of the fixed field on [X,2X] is O_chi,epsilon(X^(gamma+epsilon)), then on any compact subset of Re s>gamma choose epsilon smaller than the distance to gamma. Cauchy-Schwarz makes its Mellin integral and every log-weighted derivative converge uniformly on that compact set. E is O(exp(-1/x)) near zero, while a fixed R_r vanishes for N<1. Thus the transform is holomorphic throughout Re s>gamma. Multiplication by L and meromorphic continuation from Re s>1 gives the nonzero numerator identity. At every L-zero in that half-plane it is contradictory. The principal pole at1 is a pole of L, not a zero; the transformed reciprocal cancels it. No bounded-height limitation, assertion of reciprocal growth on an unproved zero-free line, or unjustified contour shift is needed.

This is the established detector/Mellin route, also explicit in Sol04-D12 and earlier Riesz work. It is not a new hard-desmoothing theorem. Constants may depend on the individual fixed chi and modulus. No growing-conductor or Eisenstein/Hecke claim follows.

### 2.2 Global derivative estimate, including both finite cutoffs and infinity

Assume explicitly |M(t)|<=C t^beta, beta>0. The unconditional choice is beta=1,C=1. For real r>=2, k_r(u)=(1-u/r)_+^r has derivative -(1-u/r)^(r-1) on (0,r) and zero beyond r; it is absolutely continuous and its derivative joins continuously at r.

For 0<=u<=r/2 write z=(r-1)log(1-u/r)+u and A=u-u^2/2. The log series gives

    z<=u/r,  |z|<=(u+u^2)/r,
    |z-A/r|<=(u^2/2+2u^3/3)/r^2.

The last error is the positive u^2/(2r^2) correction together with the entire order>=3 log tail. Since exp(-u)exp(max(z,0))<=exp(-u/2), Taylor with its full real remainder gives

    |k'_r+exp(-u)| <= (5u+u^2)exp(-u/2)/r,
    |k'_r+exp(-u)(1+A/r)| <= P(u)exp(-u/2)/r^2,
    P(u)=12u^2+4u^3+u^4.

The second short-range estimate actually needs at most u^2+(5/3)u^3+u^4/2 in place of P. On u>=r/2, including u>r, use |k'_r|<=exp(-u/2) on its support and zero outside. Multiplying the second claimed estimate by r^2 costs at most 2r^2+r|A|<=10u^2+u^3<=P, since r<=2u. The first estimate there follows from 2<=4u/r. This independently verifies the global bound; it is not an inference from the author's floating grid.

Abel integration is exact:

    sum_n a(n)h(n/x)=-int_0^infty M(xu)h'(u)du.

The zero/infinity boundary terms vanish for the kernels at hand. Integrating u^beta times the first bound gives

    |B_r-E|<=C K1(beta)x^beta/r,
    K1=5*2^(beta+2)Gamma(beta+2)+2^(beta+3)Gamma(beta+3).

Write k'_r=-exp(-u)(1+A/r)+e_r. The A/r terms cancel exactly in 2k'_(2r)-k'_r+exp(-u), leaving at most (2/4+1)P exp(-u/2)/r^2. Therefore

    |V_r-E|<=(3/2)C K2(beta)x^beta/r^2,
    K2=12*2^(beta+3)Gamma(beta+3)
        +4*2^(beta+4)Gamma(beta+4)+2^(beta+5)Gamma(beta+5).

At beta=1 these constants are K1=176, K2=11904, and the second bound has coefficient17856. They are coarse but uniform for all x>0 and real r>=2. The proof includes the branch rx<n<=2rx, the endpoint integers, and the entire infinite exponential tail. Squaring V requires 4|B_(2r)|^2+|B_r|^2-4Re(B_(2r)conj(B_r)); these signed cross terms cannot be dropped. The exact checker verifies these finite conventions, while the preceding proof covers all scales.

### 2.3 Moving shell and price of the observed scale

On a shell [X,2X], freeze r_X=max(2,ceil(X^delta)). The pointwise and shell-L2 error is O(X^(beta-2delta)), with a common constant independent of X/r_X. Consequently the every-epsilon exponent-gamma shell estimates for V_(r_X) and the fixed E are equivalent when beta-2delta<=gamma. First compare to E; only then take its fixed Mellin transform. A moving-r field has no direct fixed-r Mellin identity. Nor is the difference of two beta/Gamma quotients automatically nonzero. The author's explicit order of operations correctly avoids both objections.

Using beta=1, a buffered first-gain choice is delta=.063 and any .874<gamma<.8748540364, for example gamma=.87485. This is conditional on the complete signed V moment. The raw upper cutoff on [X,2X] is 4r_X X, of order X^(1+delta), so a bound N^eta at that raw cutoff gives exponent (1+delta)eta only if its constants are uniform in the moving order. The positive decreasing-integral estimate |B_r|<=rx/(r+1)<=x, hence |V_r|<=3x, gives only exponent1. No gain appears merely by increasing r.

The author's prospective 1/6 and 1/4 rows, delta=.084 and .126, have errors .832 and .748 respectively and are arithmetically consistent. The optional beta=.874855 variant is an EXTRA summatory input; the value c11 alone is not its proof. The written result covers fixed extrapolation order two, not an arbitrarily growing extrapolation order or an unpriced uniform-height Gamma asymptotic.

**Retention judgment:** A is a useful quantitative adapter if another method controls the growing finite signed polynomial. The general binomial/exponential approximation and cancellation of a first asymptotic term are familiar analytic mechanisms. Its value here is the explicit global, actual-source error and complete shell return, not novelty of extrapolation itself or a new arithmetic front. No stronger new-source estimate is present.

## 3. B: rank matching, all characters and all missing end ranks

For a fixed modulus q and each unit residue a, list the mu=+1 integers u_(a,k) and mu=-1 integers v_(a,k) increasingly. For 1/2<gamma<1 the author's three-way equivalence is valid:

    every chi mod q: M_chi(x)=O(x^gamma)
      <=> every unit a: M_(q,a)(x)=O(x^gamma)
      <=> both lists infinite and |u_(a,k)-v_(a,k)|=O(k^gamma).

The first equivalence uses the exact finite character transform, with conj(chi(a))/phi(q) in the inverse. It requires ALL characters of q, not just one convenient character. Nonunits remain zeros, and imprimitive and complex characters participate normally.

For the forward geometric implication, the full squarefree progression count is

    Q_(q,a)(x)=d_q x+O_q(sqrt(x)),
    d_q=(q*zeta(2))^-1 product_(p|q)(1-p^-2)^-1>0.

Expanding mu^2 as sum_(d^2|n)mu(d), only (d,q)=1 contributes. Each inner progression has x/(q d^2)+O(1) elements; the sqrt(x) individual errors and completed d^-2 tail give the stated error. Thus each signed counting function is d_q x/2+O(x^gamma). Its monotone inverse is 2k/d_q+O(k^gamma); the positive density also proves both lists infinite. The restriction gamma>1/2 pays the squarefree-density error. This review retains the stated range and claims no quantitative uniform-in-q estimate.

Conversely, a rank pair crossing x has k<=x, length<=C x^gamma, and its lower endpoint in (x-C x^gamma,x]. Different pairs have different lower endpoints, so the signed crossing count has modulus<=C x^gamma+1. This proves the full discrepancy estimate without rearranging an infinite sum. With every-epsilon notation, first choose an epsilon keeping gamma+epsilon<1; larger epsilons follow trivially.

For u_k<v_k the exact identity Q(v_k)-Q(u_k)=M(v_k)+M(u_k) is correct, and both right-hand terms are nonnegative; reversing the orientation reverses these signs. A finite experiment only matches ranks through min(P(N),N(N)); the omitted endpoint count is |M(N)|. Our independent finite check reconstructs every cutoff from completed crossing pairs AND these end ranks. No finite observed maximum distance proves the infinite criterion.

The monotone finite matching minimax claim follows by uncrossing on the line. G65 already derives a feature-matching cost from an inherited summatory exponent, paying the unmatched ghost; W22 already prices total mass. G76/G94 price the first-prime boundary. B adds a clean two-sided AP/all-character formulation with a self-contained squarefree count, not a better matching estimate or a new family. A first gain still requires an actual exponent gamma<theta11 for every k and every unit residue of each fixed q. Obtaining gamma=theta11 from the accepted theorem and feeding it back gives no improvement.

## 4. C: exact renewal and a stronger elementary check on absolute small gain

With a(n)=mu(n)chi(n), Dirichlet convolution gives

    a log=-a*(Lambda chi),
    R(x)=sum_(d<=x)Lambda(d)chi(d)M(x/d)=-sum_(n<=x)a(n)log n.

Every prime power and natural zero is retained. Finite Abel summation gives

    M(x)log x=int_1^x M(t)dt/t-R(x),
    M(x)=1-R(x)/log x-int_2^x R(t)dt/[t(log t)^2], x>=2.

The constant1 is forced by a(1)=1 and R(2-)=0. This can also be checked by Stieltjes integrating dM=-dR/log t; it is not a guessed integration constant. For gamma>0, R=O(x^gamma log x) implies M=O(x^gamma), and the first identity proves the converse. The statements carry every-epsilon losses. This is an equivalent complete target, not a weaker arithmetic hypothesis.

The positive kernel sum S_gamma(X)=sum_(d<=X)Lambda(d)|chi(d)|d^-gamma has infinite limiting mass for 0<gamma<=1. Indeed sum Lambda(d)floor(X/d)=log(floor X!), so S_1(X)>=log X-O_q(1). Removing each ramified prime-power ray costs only a finite constant. This is a positive-operator norm obstruction, never a lower bound for the signed R.

One can strengthen the author's normalized claim without a prime-number theorem. Put Y=exp(sqrt(log X)). Since Lambda(d)<=log d,

    S_1(Y)<=sum_(d<=Y)log(d)/d
            <=(1/2)(log Y)^2+O(log Y)
            =(1/2)log X+O(sqrt(log X)).

Hence S_1(X)-S_1(Y)>=(1/2+o(1))log X. For each fixed 0<gamma<1,

    S_gamma(X)/log X
      >=(1/2+o(1))*exp((1-gamma)sqrt(log X)) -> infinity.

Thus even division of this finite positive renewal kernel by log X gives no fixed subunit norm below1. At gamma=1 its lower limiting ratio is at least1. This excludes the specified absolute small-gain estimate. It does not exclude signed cancellation, compatible-source norms, or a different probabilistic representation with its complete correction paid. The coarse identity |R(x)|<=sum log n<=x log x returns only exponent1.

S09's equation a*(chi log)=-(a log) was false in the initial seed. The correct left side is Lambda chi. At n=4, chi=1, it equals log2 while -(mu(4)log4)=0. The author correctly uses a*(Lambda chi)=-(a log) in C. This is an explicit failed seed algebra screen, not an undeclared seventh completed first test or permission to change the original seeds.

The retained G78/G81/G92/G112 renewal/inverse lineage and newly integrated G116 signed hard-region localization remain relevant. C does not replace the full correlation by independent jumps or give the hard-region estimate of G116. No new inverse family or positive-contraction route is established.

## 5. Other three selected tests and strongest scope restrictions

**S19.** A finite-prime inverse m_Y has m_Y*chi equal to chi(n) on Y-rough n and zero otherwise, with value1 at n=1. Thus delta-m_Y*chi is exactly -chi(n) for n>1, P^-(n)>Y. This retains prime powers and ramified zeros. Its absolute Dirichlet norm diverges at sigma<=1, already on the unramified primes. The known b>1 growing-depth inverse with a separately paid physical tail remains available; the trivial norm below1 fails. This is the [restricted research revision]-W4/G78 boundary. The later G117 fixed-preconditioner theorem also covers this obstruction at its all-scale scope. No lower bound for the actual signed field follows.

**S14.** For T=[[rho,1],[0,rho]], d=1-rho^2, the reported positive P satisfies P-T*PT=I. Direct algebra gives det P=d^-2+d^-4 and trace P~2d^-3; hence lambda_max~2d^-3, lambda_min~(1/2)d^-1 and sqrt(cond P)~2/d as rho approaches1. The contraction inferred solely from this identity is sqrt(1-1/lambda_max). At rho=1 the eigenvalue1 forbids strict contraction in any positive metric. This prices a diagnostic's near-resonant conditioning; it is not a native-H transfer construction or an arithmetic lower bound. The exact checker used rho=1/3 and3/4, independently of the author's rho=1/2 case.

**S21.** The product-cutoff squarefree family IS a simplicial complex. For an unramified prime p, with T_p(x)=sum_(n<=x,p not dividing n)mu(n)chi(n), the full identity is

    M(x)=T_p(x)-chi(p)T_p(x/p)
        =sum_(x/p<n<=x,p not dividing n)mu(n)chi(n)
           +(1-chi(p))T_p(x/p).

At q=5 with chi(2)=i, x=p=2, the value is1-i, the pure boundary is0 and the entire value lies in the twist bulk. The branch chi(p)=1 has no bulk term, but that does not transfer to all characters. For q=1,p=2 the unsigned boundary count is (2/pi^2)x+O(sqrt x), while its signed value is M(x). The classical complex/Betti correspondence is supported by [Bjorner, A Cell Complex in Number Theory, Theorem3.1](https://arxiv.org/abs/1101.5704). The result is already in A-SIMPLICIAL/W27, G94 and the frozen W54-X30 audit. No new topology theorem or all-topology impossibility follows. More global revisiting matchings stay eligible if their signed cost is actually proved.

## 6. Protected S28: source-exact signed coupling audit

The seed proposes a joint signed coupling of additive and multiplicative filtrations, with a small total-variation defect. Its p=1/2000/high-ceiling status was protected before outcomes. A distinction between ordinary marginals and weighted divisor constraints is essential.

### 6.1 Conservation and the full finite dual

A usual finite signed or complex coupling has equal total row and column masses. If its additive marginal is a(n), 1<=n<=N, while its multiplicative marginal is (a*chi)(n)=delta_(n=1), the two totals are M_chi(N) and1. Such a coupling can exist only when M_chi(N)=1. At N=2, q=1 the totals are0 and1; for the quartic mod5 character they are1-i and1. A ghost/remainder repairing this particular mismatch must carry M_chi(N)-1. This refutes only that conservative interpretation, not a weighted, nonconservative divisor identity.

For a feasible version, partition {1,...,N} into additive cells I_i and another partition C_j. Let E contain precisely permitted nonempty intersections and let

    Z^0_ij=sum_(n in I_i intersect C_j)a(n),
    r_i=sum_j Z^0_ij, c_j=sum_i Z^0_ij.

Both marginal totals are now M. The exact minimum-TV problem has dual

    inf_(rows r, columns c, support E) sum_E |Z_ij|

## R8. Uniform27: weighted four-cycles, not an unpriced frustration count

This is my independent uniform audit. Use the same ACTUAL rectangular T and two separate mark spaces. Its Hermitian dilation is bipartite even if the two supports happen to use the same numerical labels. It has no triangular cycle. Identifying those two copies and inventing a triangle would change the bilinear source. Four-cycles are the first relevant loops in this representation.

For distinct input columns j,k let

    b_i=conjugate(T_ij)T_ik,  s_jk=sum_i |b_i|,
    eta_i=b_i/|b_i| for b_i!=0,
    psi_jk=sum_(i<l,b_i b_l!=0) |b_i||b_l||eta_i-eta_l|^2.

Each nonzero term uses four actual nonzero edges. An original masked-out or naturally zero entry contributes zero; no division at that zero occurs. Expansion gives the exact identity

    |(T*T)_jk|^2=s_jk^2-psi_jk.                       (A27.1)

Indeed the diagonal terms agree, and each pair's difference is2|b_i||b_l|(1-Re(eta_i conjugate(eta_l))). Its phase is the actual four-cycle product

    conjugate(T_ij)T_ik T_lj conjugate(T_lk)

divided by its modulus. It is invariant under transported row/column unitary gauges. The original source must be transported with that gauge; fixing it instead changes H. Every short-core interference already folded into each T entry is retained. Replacing T by separate positive cores before forming these b_i would be a different identity with a different cost.

G75's full Hermitian Gram row bound now reads

    ||T||^2 <= max_j [sum_i |T_ij|^2
                +sum_(k!=j) sqrt(s_jk^2-psi_jk)].       (A27.2)

All radicands are nonnegative by(A27.1). Thus bounding the entire right side by B0^2, uniformly with the source gates in R6, returns the raw H target by Cauchy and then its single physical factor. A Schatten alternative also includes the whole complement:

    ||T||^4 <= tr((T*T)^2)
       =sum_j (sum_i |T_ij|^2)^2
           +sum_(j!=k)(s_jk^2-psi_jk).                 (A27.3)

The diagonal term never disappears. These are exact native-source identities and sufficient returns, not evaluations of native cycle phases or an arithmetic lower bound. I have not constructed a numerical ideal packet with a specified nonzero cycle. The bounded Gaussian-integer matrices in checks.json verify conjugations and zero-edge conventions only; they are expressly synthetic. The triangle test, by contrast, is settled exactly by the source's bipartite structure.

For a2-by-2 unit-entry block the full Gram computation gives ||T||^2=2+2|cos(Phi/2)|. The prior G75 critic already records this formula, so it earns no new theorem credit here. A frustrated four-cycle can remove that block's off-diagonal Gram entry, but says nothing by itself about the weight on other edges or coherent components. Adding a disjoint large coherent block preserves the frustrated loop and makes that block dominate the norm; this is a generic diagnostic, not an alleged native embedding. Gauging a spanning tree removes its phases and leaves its coherent mass. W40's long rank-one cycle result also prevents promoting a fixed small-cycle loss to a macroscopic power loss.

To get a power saving through(A27.2), the actual weighted deficits must control EVERY significant Gram row together with the diagonal, at the required square-level exponent. A fixed positive fraction of a few cycle counts gives at most a constant comparison in that component. The complete arithmetic condition remains open. This is a precise realization/reparametrization of U-FLUX/G75's signed-Gram obligation, not a new independent cancellation estimate. Source-compatible loop summation, nonlocal cycles and genuinely mixed phase estimates remain eligible.

## 3. Exact pair support and the actual folded diagonal

Define the positive-kernel Gram

\[
 J_\delta(N,M;X)=\int_X^{2X}
 V_\delta(N/x)V_\delta(M/x)\frac{dx}{x}.
 \tag{DP13}
\]

It vanishes unless

\[
 e^{-\delta}X\le N,M\le2e^\delta X,
 \quad |\log(N/M)|\le2\delta,
 \quad |N-M|\le C\delta X.
 \tag{DP14}
\]

Hence, exactly and with all signs retained,

\[
 \int_X^{2X}|F_{A,\delta}(x)|^2\frac{dx}{x}
 =\sum_{N,M}A(N)A(M)J_\delta(N,M;X).
 \tag{DP15}
\]

There is no undeclared selection of favorable shifts. In the original mu representation the kernel is

\[
 J_\delta(n,m)-2J_\delta(2n,m)
 -2J_\delta(n,2m)+4J_\delta(2n,2m).
 \tag{DP16}
\]

Its pair-ratio bands are n/m near 1, 2 and 1/2. DP1 reindexes their complete sum, including exact ratio resonances, into DP15. It is incorrect to retain only the original n=m terms of DP16 as the diagonal of DP15.

We can compute the folded diagonal independently. The elementary squarefree count in odd integers is

\[
 \sum_{m\le z\atop m\text{ odd}}\mu(m)^2
 =\frac{2}{3\zeta(2)}z+O(\sqrt z).
 \tag{DP17}
\]

For completeness expand mu(m)^2=sum_{d^2|m}mu(d), with d and m odd. Counting odd multiples gives z/(2d^2)+O(1); the main Euler sum over odd d is (1-2^{-2})^{-1}/zeta(2), and its truncated tail and the O(1) terms cost O(sqrt z). Thus DP8 gives

\[
 \sum_{N\le z}A(N)^2
 =\frac{2}{3\zeta(2)}
 \left(1+\frac92+\frac44\right)z+O(\sqrt z)
 =\frac{13}{3\zeta(2)}z+O(\sqrt z).
 \tag{DP18}
\]

The diagonal is therefore exactly

\[
 \begin{split}
 \sum_N A(N)^2J_\delta(N,N;X)
 &=\frac{13X}{3\zeta(2)}
       \int_0^\infty V_\delta(u)^2\,du
   +O\!\left(\sqrt X\int_0^\infty V_\delta(u)^2\frac{du}{u}\right)\\
 &=\frac{13X}{3\zeta(2)\delta}
       \int k(v)^2e^{\delta v}\,dv
   +O\!\left(\frac{\sqrt X}{\delta}\right)
 \asymp \frac X\delta.
 \end{split}
 \tag{DP19}
\]

Interchange the sum and the u integral first and apply DP18 on [Xu,2Xu]. This keeps the counting error uniform for arbitrarily small delta; differentiating the kernel in a partial-summation error would introduce an unnecessary loss. The asymptotic is uniform for 0<delta<=delta0 and X sufficiently large. It is a diagonal computation, not a lower bound for the whole signed energy.

For a=.87449 the diagonal is payable with a strict power margin whenever eta<.74898. This is three times the range allowed by separately paying the single-window first-derivative diagonal. Cross terms remain unestimated in both comparisons.

For untwisted f3 each literal coefficient is ±1. Let `phi_n(v)=g_kappa(v)g_tau(log(n/X)-v)`, in the Hilbert space with norm H^-r. The squared feature distance is

    d_r(n,m)²=J(n,n)+J(m,m)-2J(n,m),

with J exactly R5. It is not just a function of log(n/m): the radial factors b_n,b_m are essential. This is nonnegative because it is a Hilbert distance, not merely because J has positive entries.

Take `N=floor(X exp(C sqrt(log X)))` and ghost position `x_*=X exp(D sqrt(log X))`, fixed D>C, with `C²,D²>2sigma(1+A)`. The exact feature norm is `||phi_n||_2=sqrt(g_(2nu)(0))b_n`, so the omitted **entire** tail is

    sum_(n>N)||phi_n||_(H^-r)
       <= X^(1-C²/(2sigma)+o(1))=O(X^-A),              (R7)

after using the strict margin. Integral comparison includes the `exp(C sqrt(log X))` factor in o(1). The compensating charge has magnitude at most N and its own feature norm `O(X^(-D²/(2sigma)))`, hence is also below the same chosen error. Both bounds are uniform in all r>=0. The real ghost label is auxiliary, not an invented arithmetic atom.

Add charge `-sum_(n<=N)f3(n)` at that label. Positive and negative measures now have equal mass `M=max(number of original positive atoms, number of original negative atoms)<=N`. For any nonnegative plan pi with exactly those marginals,

    balanced field = sum_(n,m) pi(n,m)(phi_n-phi_m),
    N_r(X) <= sqrt(M C_r(X))+O(X^-A),
    C_r(X)=sum_(n,m)pi(n,m)d_r(n,m)².                  (R8)

The Hilbert Cauchy–Schwarz step retains all field cross terms through its upper bound. It does not assume equal original sign counts or drop an unmatched cell. Since `M<=X^(1+o(1))`, a genuine complete all-scale `C_(r_X)(X)<<_epsilon X^(q+epsilon)`, q>-1, gives A's eta=(1+q)/2 and therefore

    gamma=(1+q+d)/2.                                  (R9)

For a fixed complex ordinary character, split the actual coefficients into real and imaginary signed measures, including their zero values. Each needs its own exact plan and balancing ghost and a B4 cost bound; two fixed triangle constants do not alter R9. B2's explicit rank-matching construction is stated for untwisted f3, not silently as a uniform twisted/ideal theorem.

### Reconstructing the baseline, including the end ranks

Assume the accepted **buffered** fixed-source summatory input `S(t)=O(t^beta)`, `1/2<beta<1`. For c6 any fixed beta>.874861 is permitted by the retained premise; beta=.874861 itself is not supplied.
