The excess O(N^beta) ranks lie in `[N-O(N^beta),N]`, so the ghost does not arbitrarily collect interior mass.

Writing w=log(n/X), differentiate the exact product expression:

    ||d phi_w/dw||_2² = b(w)² g_(2nu)(0)
             [w²/sigma²+alpha²/(2nu)].                 (R10)

The mixed integral vanishes since `integral g_nu g_nu'=0`. The paired log distance is `O(n^(beta-1))`; integrating the derivative gives a cost bounded by

    C n^(2beta-2)(1+w²)exp(-c w²)

for a fixed c>0 after a harmless variance enlargement. To justify it uniformly even when X and n are widely separated, absorb `|w|n^(beta-1)` into `epsilon*w²+C_epsilon` above a fixed initial threshold. The finitely many smaller n have superpower Gaussian decay. Summing over n about X yields `O(X^(2beta-1))`: the logarithmic variable leaves an integrable `exp((2beta-1)w-cw²)(1+w²)`.

The excess ghost pair costs are `O(X^(beta-C²/sigma+o(1))+X^(beta-D²/sigma+o(1)))`, below that bound after choosing the already free fixed tail constants. Thus

    C_r(X)<<X^(2beta-1), uniformly for all r>=0.         (R11)

R9 returns beta for d=0; positive d gives the weaker beta+d/2. R11 is an upper bound on one plan, not an optimal-cost lower bound. It leaves open a better source-specific plan. Matched-Max MM-D2 already owns monotone log transport with a paid ghost; this adaptation earns the exact new metric and full f3 Gaussian-tail accounting, not a second discovery of the transport method. W41's single-prime-edge obstruction is not contradicted: these pairs may have arbitrary near-one ratios.

**Verdict B:** accept B1–9 with these quantifiers. The required new cost is strictly `q+d<.749722`; none is proved. Large-r attenuation alone does not deliver that estimate. No native H kernel, masks, projectors, Gauss roots or its physical normalization have been identified with this new Gaussian metric, so no H-branch gain may be imported or added.

### The physical improvement

PH keeps the common forced ideal inside the divisor interpolation instead
of estimating every pair by F=1. For a dyadic block with relative conductor
R at most T and forced norm F at least V, it proves

\[
\sum |\mathcal C|
\ll \frac{Z^\epsilon}{Y}
\min\left\{\frac{T^{3/4}}{\sqrt Q\,V^{1/3}},
                 \frac{T^{1/2}}{V^{5/6}}\right\}.
\]

The common ideal is
\([d(a)/(d(a),e^2),d(b)/(d(b),d^2)]\), where
\(D=Gd,E=Ge,(d,e)=1\), and \(d(a)=a/\operatorname{rad}(a)\).
Thus relative conductor, individual active conductor, forced norm and
true gcd remain different parameters. The exact prime-mark-supported
example in PH reaches relative exponent .66233287384 beyond FR's
.57629956232 cutoff. It demonstrates additional supported paid sectors,
not a lower bound for covariance. The F=1 complement is still substantial.

statement:
## 4. S02: the critical logarithmic prime cutoff with its margin paid

This develops the actual G173 Gaussian logarithmic source, not a new generic resolvent. Fix tau>0, ordinary chi mod q and 1/2<gamma<1. Set

    g(v)=(2pi tau)^(-1/2)exp(-v^2/(2tau)),
    U(y)=sum_(n>=1)mu(n)chi(n)g(log n-y), z(y)=e^(-gamma y)U(y).

Local convergence, derivatives and the left Gaussian tail follow from the absolute Gaussian majorant. The coefficient identity is

    mu(n)chi(n)log n = -sum_(d|n)chi(d)Lambda(d)mu(n/d)chi(n/d).

It retains every prime power. It gives exactly

    tau z'+(y+tau gamma)z+K_(1,gamma)z+K_(2,gamma)z=0,
    K1 z(y)=sum_p chi(p)log p p^(-gamma)z(y-log p),            (C1)

with K2 the j>=2 prime-power delays. For I_R=int_0^R y|z|^2 and E_R=int_0^R|z|^2,

    (tau/2)(|z(R)|^2-|z(0)|^2)+I_R+tau gamma E_R=Q1+Q2,
    Qj=-Re int_0^R conjugate(z) Kj z.                         (C2)

G173 proves |Q2|<=eta I_R+B_eta for every eta>0 using the summable higher-power coefficient norm and the fixed past. It also pays the same-output prime diagonal D_R=O(1), since its nonnegative weights sum at each squarefree q-unit n to at most log n and the whole-line Gaussian integral is a constant times n^(-2gamma). These facts are reused exactly.

### A. New paid interface

For fixed a>0 take

    b=1/(1-gamma), Y_a(y)=a(1+y)^b, y>=0,
    kappa(a,gamma)=a^(1-gamma)/(1-gamma).                     (C3)

Equality belongs to the small-prime sector. Let Q_small use precisely p<=Y_a(y). Then for every eta>0,

    |Q_small(R)| <= [kappa(a,gamma)+eta] I_R+B_eta,a,chi,tau,  (C4)

for every R, with B using only a fixed bounded interval of the actual source and its left tail. It does not require any unknown future bound.

Proof: PNT and partial summation give

    S_gamma(t)=sum_(p<=t)log p p^(-gamma)
                 ~t^(1-gamma)/(1-gamma).

Thus the row sum at y is (kappa+o(1))y. Apply 2|z(y)z(y-log p)|<=|z(y)|^2+|z(y-log p)|^2. For the column put v=y-log p. The mask implies log p<=log a+b log(1+y)=o(y); hence v/y->1 uniformly over all admitted primes as y->infinity. More explicitly, for any fixed small epsilon>0, eventually y<=v/(1-epsilon), so the column is bounded by

    S_gamma(a(1+v/(1-epsilon))^b)
       <=[kappa/(1-epsilon)+o(1)]v.

Choose epsilon and the tail onset to absorb both errors into eta. The remaining y are bounded and have only finitely many permitted primes and a bounded past interval. Their contribution is B. No second factor2 survives in the asymptotic coefficient; both rows and columns were counted. PNT is used only in this classical scalar prime-weight sum. Replacing it by G173's theta(t)<=4(log2)t gives the entirely elementary, weaker coefficient 4(log2)kappa and the same cutoff power.

This is larger eventually than the G173 cutoff ((2+y)/log(e^2+y))^b, by a growing logarithmic factor. The price is a nonzero, explicitly budgeted kappa; the old cutoff had relative bound0. It is not legitimate to enlarge that mask while retaining its old arbitrarily small price.

### B. Full conditional return, including the debit

Define H_a,R as the COMPLETE p>Y_a(y), n!=pm off-diagonal expansion of Q1, with the original coefficients

    -Re[conjugate(mu(n)chi(n))*chi(p)*mu(m)chi(m)]
      *log p*e^(-2gamma y)*g(log n-y)*g(log(pm)-y),           (C5)

summed over all m,n and integrated over0<=y<=R. Both infinite sums, the diagonal complement, both independent arithmetic labels and all character zeros remain. Its diagonal D_a,R is the same nonnegative bounded type as G173 for this new exact mask.

Suppose, for this a and some delta>kappa(a,gamma),

    H_a,R <=(1-delta) I_R+B_chi, all sufficiently large R.     (C6)

Set eta=(delta-kappa)/4 in(C4) and the higher-power payment. Equations(C2),(C5) give, after adjusting the initial constant,

    (tau/2)|z(R)|^2+[(delta-kappa)/2]I_R+tau gamma E_R<=B'.   (C7)

Thus U(y)=O_chi(e^(gamma y)). Its bilateral transform continues normally on Re s>gamma, equals exp(tau s^2/2)/L(s,chi) initially on Re s>1, and this nonzero Gaussian numerator excludes every ordinary L-zero there. The principal pole and imprimitive factors are handled exactly as in G173. One common gamma is chosen before characters and possible zeros; a,delta,constants and onsets may depend on fixed chi. No growth-uniform height or conductor estimate is supplied.

At gamma=.87485,5/6,3/4 the critical powers b are 20000/2503,6,4. A coarse choice a=[delta(1-gamma)/2]^(1/(1-gamma)) spends exactly kappa=delta/2. Conditional c values remain .12515,1/6,1/4. No(C6) is proved. This pays a larger restricted sector with its exact hard complement, but supplies no endpoint increase.

### C. The coefficient is sharp even for a one-sided arbitrary-input form

This checks the strongest affordable objection: perhaps the absolute estimate wastes the sign so badly that a generic one-sided operator argument could pay a much larger range. For the principal character that hope fails at this level.

Let T->infinity, L_T=sqrt T, Y_T=a(1+T)^b, t_T=pi/log Y_T, and take the test function

    f_T(y)=e^(i t_T y) 1_[T,T+L_T](y).

This is an arbitrary-input test, not the actual z. Delays for admitted primes are O(log T), so only O(log T) of the interval is lost at its left edge. On the rest, conjugate(f_T(y))f_T(y-log p)=p^(-i t_T). Under the positive weights log p p^(-gamma), the mass with p<=Y_T^(1-epsilon) is negligible compared with S_gamma(Y_T). For all the remaining mass, t_T log p lies between (1-epsilon)pi and pi+o(1). First let T grow, then epsilon decrease. Therefore

    -Re int conjugate(f_T)K_small f_T
       /int y|f_T|^2 -> kappa(a,gamma).                     (C8)

The finite q-exclusions do not change the limit. Uniformly across the window Y_a(y)/Y_T->1, and the edge loss is O(log T/sqrt T), so neither alters it. This attains the same leading one-sided coefficient as(C4). If the cutoff power b'>1/(1-gamma), the same test gives a ratio asymptotic to a^(1-gamma)T^(b'(1-gamma)-1)/(1-gamma), which diverges. Consequently no bounded one-sided relative-form certificate on arbitrary inputs can pay such a supercritical power. This does not lower-bound the actual source's Q_small or H_a,R; it leaves arithmetic source-specific cancellation open.

The attempted weakest coarse estimate of the FULL hard part still fails: granting only |U(y)|<=C e^(beta y), gamma<beta<1, absolute prime summation produces scale exponent 1+beta-2gamma, versus 2beta-2gamma for I_R. The gap1-beta remains, as G173 already records. The exact logarithmic equation and the new critical interface do not supply the missing signed saving. Treating its inverse resolvent as bounded across a possible L-zero would merely assume the conclusion.

## G174. Actual cutoff boundaries and the price of a positive observation

Let S_N be the squarefree q-units n<=N. On its orthonormal basis define
B_p e_n=chi(p)e_(pn) when p does not divide n and pn<=N, zero otherwise.
Distinct insertions commute: their product exists in both orders exactly
when prn fits. The divisor-closed cutoff does not create noncommutative
independence. Ordered fermionic boundaries are different operators.

For p!=r the mixed adjoint commutator is exactly

    C_pr=B_p^*B_r-B_rB_p^*,
    C_pr e_(pm)=-conjugate(chi(p))chi(r)e_(rm),
    m squarefree, (m,qpr)=1,
    N/(pr)<m<=min(N/p,N/r),                                (7)

and zero elsewhere. The lower endpoint is strict and upper endpoints
inclusive. It is a phased negative partial isometry, norm1 if its domain
is nonempty. For a_N=sum_(S_N)mu(n)chi(n)e_n, every character phase cancels:

    <a_N,C_pr a_N>=-#domain(7).

With profile f, the exact contraction is instead
-sum_m conjugate(f(rm))f(pm). Complex profiles cannot be replaced by
positive counts. For the k unramified primes in(N/2,N], the sum over
ordered p!=r is -D_chi(J_k-I_k)D_chi^*. The actual vector -D_chi1 has
eigenvalue-(k-1) and quadratic value-k(k-1). A transported gauge preserves
it. This rejects the specified unweighted independence shortcut.

The reviewer preserves a genuine escape: if external weights lambda_p
are allowed, the same terminal contraction becomes

    <a_N,sum_(p!=r)conjugate(lambda_p)lambda_r C_pr a_N>
      =sum_p|lambda_p|^2-|sum_p lambda_p|^2.                (8)

For two primes, weights(1,1),(1,-1),(1,i) give-2,+2,0. Thus the unweighted
obstruction does not exclude all signed compensation. G164's positive
ordered E=B^*B result has different hypotheses. The complete readout is
still a_N=product_p(I-B_p)e_1 and M_chi(N)=<1,a_N>; bounding commutators
alone does not estimate it.

A second result concerns a precise positive certificate. For the principal
character modulo fixed q, partition S_N by its complete set of prime
divisors<=sqrt N. The empty cell is

    C0={1} union {p:sqrt N<p<=N,p not dividing q}.

If L counts those primes and Q=#S_N, its signed sum is1-L. For any
partition P, Cauchy gives

    |M(N)|<=sqrt(Q E(P)),
    E(P)=sum_(C in P)|sum_(n in C)mu(n)|^2/|C|.

The displayed observation and every refinement satisfy

    E(P)>=(L-1)^2/(L+1)=L-3+4/(L+1).                       (9)

Refinement only increases conditional-square energy. Square-divisor
counting gives Q=kappa_q N+O_q(sqrt N),
kappa_q=(6/pi^2)product_(p|q)p/(p+1)>0. Elementary binomial counting gives
pi(N)>>N/log N: each prime's factor in binomial(2m,m) is at most2m,
while the binomial is at least4^m/(2m+1). Removing sqrt N and finitely
many ramified primes leaves L>>_q N/log N. Therefore the NUMERIC RIGHT
SIDE sqrt(Q E(P)) is at least a constant times N/sqrt(log N).

This positive certificate cannot prove a fixed power below1. Its proposed
every-epsilon energy target N^(2gamma-1+epsilon) is false for gamma<1;
the current first-gain threshold is2gamma11-1=.7497080728. This is no
lower bound for |M|. Signed cross-pattern interactions, coarsening,
unrelated syndromes and nonprincipal phase cancellation remain available.
A finite syndrome example with identical syndrome law and opposite parity
bias is only a model illustration, not a broader arithmetic impossibility.

G103/G117/G145/G162 and the precise [restricted research revision]-[restricted research revision] positive certificate results
retain their separate scopes. Cell-constant projections can connect widely
separated primes, so this argument is not merely G167's short-offset
global positivity hypothesis under a different name.

statement:
## D48. Native Gaussian innovation, then a paid all-block replacement

### The actual close-point Gram and its normalization

For n in[X,2X], set s=log(n/X), epsilon=log(1+1/n),
v_s(u)=g_tau(s-u) on0<=u<=log2. The literal physical Gram G22 is
<v_s,v_t>; every coefficient is the actual f3(n), including all powers.
The Schur pivot of v_(s+epsilon) against v_s is

    p_s(epsilon)=||v_(s+epsilon)||^2
           -|<v_s,v_(s+epsilon)>|^2/||v_s||^2
      =epsilon^2 [||v_s'||^2
           -|<v_s,v_s'>|^2/||v_s||^2]+O_tau(epsilon^3).  (D48.1)

Taylor expansion is uniform on the compact s-range, and
v_s'/v_s=-(s-u)/tau is nonconstant on a positive-length interval.
The bracket is ||v_s||^2 Var_(v_s^2)(u)/tau^2>0,
continuous with a positive compact minimum. Hence p_s~n^-2
uniformly. The Gram's largest eigenvalue is bounded above/below,
so its condition number is comparable to n^2. This is a native
kernel statement, not a f3 energy lower bound. Whitening the Gram
can amplify a unit coefficient error by order n.

The source-adapted alternative keeps the cheap difference mode
explicit and never inverts the Gram. This changes S48's original
orthogonal-prime-word proposal after source intake; the seed remains
unaltered and the salvage is attributed to this development.

### A whole-field replacement with every difference and tail paid

Let a(n) be ANY fixed complex sequence with |a(n)|<=1. Later take
a(n)=f3(n), or f3(n)chi(n) with its actual zero extension. For an
integer B>=1 define right-closed blocks ((j-1)B,jB], j>=1,

    b_B(j)=sum_((j-1)B<n<=jB)a(n),
    V_B(x)=sum_(j>=1)b_B(j)g_tau(log(jB/x)),
    F_a(x)=sum_(n>=1)a(n)g_tau(log(n/x)).

All these infinite sums converge absolutely on compact x-ranges
by the Gaussian majorant; b_B(j) has modulus at most B. Put
k_x(t)=g_tau(log(t/x)), t>0. Its total variation on(0,infinity)
is exactly2g_tau(0). On one block,

    sum_(n in block)|k_x(n)-k_x(jB)|
       <= B integral_((j-1)B)^(jB)|k_x'(t)|dt.

Indeed every segment[n,jB] lies in the block and at most B
integer segments cover a point. At t=0 the Gaussian is flat and
has limit0, so the first block has no omitted endpoint. Summing
ALL blocks yields the uniform, coefficient-preserving bound

    |F_a(x)-V_B(x)|<=2B g_tau(0), x>0.                 (D48.2)

This prices every within-block signed detail, including the infinite
high-n tail, with no exceptional or unmatched class deleted. It is
not an estimate of a positive submask. Squaring afterwards retains
all ordered block interactions; norm triangle has paid both mixed
terms and the difference square at the field level.

For every parent dyadic X fix B_X=floor(X^theta),0<=theta<gamma,
and use that same B_X for ALL x in[X,2X]. D48.2 implies the exact
every-epsilon equivalence

    ||F_a||_[X,2X]<<X^(gamma+epsilon)
      iff ||V_(B_X)||_[X,2X]<<X^(gamma+epsilon).         (D48.3)

Use a smaller epsilon than gamma-theta. No Mellin continuation of
the MOVING block source is inferred; the fixed source is recovered
by D48.2 first. All n and their signs/zeros occur once in b_B.

For actual f3, B=2 makes the arithmetic coefficient explicit:

    b_2(j)=f3(2j-1)+(1-2*1_(2 not dividing j))f3(j).    (D48.4)

This preserves f3's valuation rule: multiplying by2 flips its sign
only if2 was absent. Thus even the pair source is not an independent
random-sign source or a squarefree source. With a fixed chi,
b_2(j)=f3(2j-1)chi(2j-1)+f3(2j)chi(2j); all ramified zeros remain.

There is also a direct fixed-B pole-preserving transform. Write
e_B(n)=B ceil(n/B) and initially on Re s>1 let

    D_B(s)=sum_(j>=1)b_B(j)(jB)^-s,
    E_B(s)=sum_(n>=1)a(n)[n^-s-e_B(n)^-s].             (D48.6)

Since0<=e_B(n)-n<B, the integral of the derivative of t^-s gives
|n^-s-e_B(n)^-s|<=|s|B n^(-Re s-1). Thus E_B converges absolutely
and locally normally on Re s>0, including fixed s-derivatives
(their extra log powers are summable). Coefficient rearrangement
on Re s>1 gives D_B=D_a-E_B. For fixed ordinary chi this becomes

    L(s,chi)D_B(s)=W_chi(s)-L(s,chi)E_B(s).           (D48.7)

If the fixed-B Gaussian block field has a complete moment exponent
gamma>.5, its Mellin transform continues D_B to Re s>gamma.
At a hypothetical L-zero rho there, D48.7's left side and its
second right term vanish, while W_chi(rho) does not. This proves
the direct fixed-B zero return; additive holomorphic error, rather
than an Euler-product guess, preserves the reciprocal poles. At
B=2 the source uses exactly b_2 from D48.4. Moving B_X still uses
D48.2--3 before continuation, so no changing transform is invented.

The pair difference sector alone is O_tau(1). Its complete signed
sum mode b_2 remains the entire arithmetic problem. Large B reduces
the number of block coordinates in a paid finite Gaussian window
to X^(1-theta+o(1)), but b_B(j) can be as large as B. No complexity
or amplitude reduction is asserted from coordinate count alone.

### Ordinary-character zero return and concrete high ceilings

For a(n)=f3(n)chi(n), current [restricted research revision]/W41 A13 gives initially on Re s>1

    sum_n a(n)n^-s=W_chi(s)/L(s,chi),
    W_chi(s)=(1-2chi(2)2^-s)
      /[(1-chi(2)2^-s)^2(1-chi(3)3^-s)^2]
      *product_(p>=5)(1-2chi(p)p^-s)/(1-chi(p)p^-s)^2.   (D48.5)

At ramified primes chi(p)=0 the factor is exactly1. The infinite
product and inverse converge normally for Re s>.5, since their
nonconstant terms start at p^-2s and2p^-sigma<1 at p>=5,sigma>.5.
Denominators have zeros only at Re s=0; prime2 numerator zeros
are on Re s=1. Hence W_chi is nonzero and holomorphic in.5<Re s<1.
Gaussian Mellin transformation gives exp(tau s^2/2)W_chi/L.
D48.3 plus dyadic Cauchy--Schwarz continues that FIXED transform to
Re s>gamma. Multiplication by L and the identity theorem exclude
zeros gamma<Re s<1. The principal pole is excluded; usual right-edge
facts complete zero exclusion. Constants depend on each fixed chi;
no growing conductor/angular assertion or new Eisenstein adapter.

Thus the weakest complete hypothesis used here is a full signed
block-field shell norm for ALL large dyadic X, with its frozen parent
B_X and every epsilon. Examples:

| gamma | Conditional c | theta | norm error | margin gamma-theta |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| .8748 | .1252 | .8 | X^.8 | .0748 |
| 5/6 | 1/6 | .8 | X^.8 | 1/30 |
| 3/4 | 1/4 | .7 | X^.7 | .05 |

NONE of these block moments is proved. A sufficient but stronger
pointwise estimate |b_(B_X)(j)|<=B_X X^(-(1-gamma)-eta)
through the relevant Gaussian window would give a power gain after
paying Gaussian tails; it is not available and is more than D48.3
requires. A baseline bound on block sums of size X^beta yields only
the positive aggregate exponent1+beta-theta, which is worse than
beta when theta<1. No arithmetic debt is hidden by compression.

Ancestry: actual-source transport W03/SBG, matchedHigh A05,
matchedMax log-transport, native finite observations and physical
readout warning [restricted research revision]/W41. The proof is elementary variation/Abel
summation, not a new functional-analysis theorem. The narrow new
record claim is the all-block, entire actual f3/zero-extended-character
replacement with UNIFORM O(B) error, explicit pair coefficient and
own complete zero return. Search may find an earlier identical
source specialization; if so merge provenance, not count another result.

Functional signature: full fixed f3*chi field / exact consecutive
block masses and endpoint readout / cheap within-block innovations /
unpaid complete signed block moment / O(X^theta) return to the fixed
field before Mellin zero exclusion. Next action: test an arithmetic
identity for b_2 or b_B retaining the sum mode. Generic whitening or
separate positive block bounds cannot supply it.

## 4. Harvest different estimates and merge them rigorously

Choose fixed bounded ideal masks p_1,p_2,p_3 with sum_j p_j=1. Let F_k^(j)
be the field with coefficients p_j(m)B_m. Their individual Dirichlet series
need not detect zeros. Suppose different methods can estimate:

- the old compact field F_old^(1);
- the simultaneous bank A_beta F_new^(2);
- the four-channel Gaussian bank G^(3).

Then the exact complete field is

    F_G=S_gn S_no F_old^(1)
        +S_gn R_a(A_beta F_new^(2))
        +(R_a in both indices)G^(3).

The all-shell bound is the sum of the three proved bounds multiplied by
C_gn C_no, C_gn sqrt(2/A), and2/A respectively. This is a concrete realization
of the user's proposed mixture of chaining, simultaneous analysis and
parallel merging. The fixed pieces sum back to the original detecting field.
It is a sufficient route; the needed piece estimates have not been proved.

An X-dependent completed list C_X is not a fixed mask in this theorem. Its
coefficients at every shifted scale, and every mismatch and remainder, must
be paid separately. Growing partitions also pay their size and mass. If the
only available estimates depend on cancellation between different pieces,
the triangle inequality above may lose precisely what is needed; retain and
estimate the full cross terms instead.

statement:
## 5. Finite signed core with every complement paid

The source estimate can be put into an explicitly finite arithmetic form without using the old moment machinery. Choose fixed kappa>0 with 2c+kappa<1 and set

    G=ceil(N^(2c+kappa)),
    T=ceil(N^(1+2c/(2r-1)+kappa)),
    R_N,T=sum_(N<n<=T) a(n)n^(-r)Phi(nx).

Define the incomplete-period Gram kernel

    K_N(n,m)=integral_0^(1/(qN)) Phi(nx)conjugate(Phi(mx))dx,

and its signed small-gcd core

    C_N,T,G=sum_(N<n,m<=T; gcd(n,m)<G)
        a(n)conjugate(a(m))(nm)^(-r) K_N(n,m).        (15)

The natural zeros of both coefficients remain. The pair set is symmetric, so(15) is real, but it need not be nonnegative. The required bound is the one-sided estimate

    C_N,T,G <= A_(chi,r,epsilon,kappa)
                   N^(1-2r-2c+epsilon).             (16)

Here A is a positive constant independent of N. This is neither an absolute bound on the real core nor an absolute-value estimate on each pair. The parameters are frozen as the displayed functions of N before any summand or cancellation is inspected.

The kernel itself has a finite description: the Bernoulli representation expresses each Phi as a fixed finite sum of periodic polynomials, and on this bounded interval their finitely many breakpoints give an exact piecewise-polynomial integral. No Fourier-height truncation is being called exact.

The large-gcd complement costs

    sum_(n,m>N; gcd(n,m)>=G) |a(n)a(m)|(nm)^(-r)|K_N(n,m)|
       <<_r N^(1-2r)/G+N^(-2r).                     (17)

Indeed |Phi|<=2zeta(r) and the interval has length at most1/N. Write n=ga,m=gb and drop coprimality only for this positive upper bound. For G<=g<=N the resulting summand is at most C_r N^(2-2r)g^(-2); for g>N its sum is O_r(N^(1-2r)). Multiplication by1/N proves(17). The diagonal, squareful gcds, zero terms and all far indices are included, never renamed as cancellation. For the chosen G, both terms lie strictly below the target in(16), because gamma>1/2.

The infinite completion error is exactly R_T, whose squared global norm is O_(q,r)(T^(1-2r)) by(7), or just by its absolute gcd bound. Thus

    E_arc(N)<=2||R_N,T||_(L2[0,h])^2+2||R_T||_(L2[0,1])^2.

The second term is O(N^(1-2r-2c-(2r-1)kappa)). Combining(16), (17) and this inequality proves(10) without estimating a cross term against an unpaid global field. There is no hidden infinity in the proposed core, no derivative of a moving cutoff, and no character deletion or phase normalization.

Conversely, if(10) holds, this same completion inequality in the reverse direction bounds the finite field, and(17) bounds its removed large-gcd sector. Therefore(16), for these choices, is also equivalent to(10) up to epsilon losses. This is another exact encoding of the hard Mertens bound, with a useful finite complement contract; it is not by itself an arithmetic saving.

The exact complete budgets are as follows. The energy improvement needed over the unconditional global norm is N^(-2c), independent of r. Ignoring the freely chosen positive kappa in the completion cutoff:

| Target c | Required energy gain | T exponent, r=2 | T exponent, r=3 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| .125139 (incumbent at assignment) | .250278 | 1+.250278/3 | 1+.250278/5 |
| .125140 (c7, accepted during this pass) | .250280 | 1+.250280/3 | 1+.250280/5 |
| 1/6 | 1/3 | 10/9 | 16/15 |
| 1/4 | 1/2 | 7/6 | 11/10 |

A strict first improvement over the accepted c therefore needs(16) with c strictly larger than that accepted value; an equality of an auxiliary reserve is not an impossibility theorem. No row in this table asserts(16).

The stronger .12514261 supplement is still unaccepted. Thus the first-gain comparison for this completed pass is c>.125140, not merely c>.125139. The initial calibration above is retained as history. ## 4. Complete Gaussian, smooth, and prime-power tails

A useful elementary bound is, uniformly for every y>0,

    sum_(m>=1) g_tau(log(m/y)) <=C_tau y.             (F17)

For y>=1 use the integrable function h(u)=g_tau(log u), u>0, extended flatly by0 at0, and its finite total variation: the Riemann-sum error is bounded by the variation, giving C(y+1)<=C'y. For0<y<1, g_tau(log(m/y))<=C_tau(y/m)^2, so the sum is O(y^2)<=O(y). The same proof applies to g_(2tau). Hence

    sum_(m>=1, |log(m/y)|>=W) g_tau(log(m/y))
              <=C_tau y exp(-W^2/(4tau)),             (F18)

because g_tau(u)1_(|u|>=W)<=sqrt(2)exp(-W^2/(4tau))g_(2tau)(u).

Use the FIXED cuts

    delta=1/100,  Q=delta L, R_0=X^delta, W=delta L.   (F19)

First, the entire fully smooth field in F6 is at most

    C_tau x^(1-1/t) Z_z(1-1/t)
              <=C_tau Xt exp(-L/t).                  (F20)

This follows from the bounded function exp((1-1/t)u)g_tau(u); its bound is uniform for3/4<=1-1/t<=1.

Second, every integer of the form p^k has a unique prime base and exponent. The positive sum over p>z,k>=1 is therefore bounded by the integer sum F17. ALL rough terms with r>R_0, including every k, have total absolute field at most

    C_tau X sum_(r>R_0,r in S(z))1/r
              <=C_tau Xt exp(-Q/t).                  (F21)

This is the needed full source tail, without an unproved signed majorant or a loss from repeating prime powers.

For r<=R_0 and k>=2 choose the FIXED sigma=3/4. The positive series

    sum_(p,k>=2)p^(-3k/4)<infinity

converges. The Gaussian exponential bound therefore gives

    sum_(p>z,k>=2)g_tau(log(p^k/y))<=C_tau y^(3/4).

Summing over the retained cores,

    sum_(r<=R_0,r in S(z)) sum_(p>z,k>=2)
                      g_tau(log(rp^k/x))
        <=C_tau X^(3/4)R_0^(1/4) Z_z(1)
        <=C_tau t X^(.7525).                          (F22)

Thus all higher powers are negligible at the asserted main-term scale, but they were not declared absent. No core product at Re s=3/4 is used; the factor R_0^(1/4) returns the core weight to1/r.

Finally retain only -W<log(rp/x)<=W in the k=1 term. F18 pays its entire omitted Gaussian tails by

    C_tau Xt exp(-W^2/(4tau)).                         (F23)

The boundary -W itself can be included in the discarded tail, so subsequent Stieltjes endpoint conventions are literal. The outer field still contains every original Gaussian term through these quantified error estimates.

statement:
## D04. Moving rough f3 detector with a paid cofactor head

### D04.1 Exact object, powers and signs

Fix tau>0 and an ordinary Dirichlet character chi modulo q, with its literal extension chi(n)=0 when gcd(n,q)>1. Constants may depend on this fixed chi; no growing-conductor statement is intended. Define

    f(n)=mu(rad(n/3^v3(n))),
    F_chi(x)=sum_(n>=1) f(n)chi(n)g_tau(log(n/x)).

The zeta case is chi=1. This is the exact existing f3 field when chi=1; it is not a squarefree surrogate. For a finite prime set P contained in {p>=5:p does not divide q}, define

    f_(P,chi)(n)=f(n)chi(n)1_(gcd(n,product P)=1),
    V_(P,chi)(x)=sum_n f_(P,chi)(n)g_tau(log(n/x)),
    a_(P,chi)(r)=f(r)chi(r)1_(every prime divisor of r lies in P),
    a_(P,chi)(1)=1.

Unique decomposition n=r v into its FULL P-smooth part r and P-rough part v proves

    f(n)chi(n)=sum_(r|n) a_(P,chi)(r)f_(P,chi)(n/r),
    F_chi(x)=sum_(r P-smooth) a_(P,chi)(r)V_(P,chi)(x/r).   (D04.1)

Only one term is nonzero in the coefficient convolution, but all r occur in the field sum. At a deleted prime the local a-series is

    1-sum_(v>=1)chi(p)^v z^v=(1-2chi(p)z)/(1-chi(p)z).

Repeated powers have coefficient -chi(p)^v, not zero. This is the important difference from the older mu-based D35, whose reconstruction has finite squarefree support. Replacing this factor by 1-chi(p)z would be incorrect.

For any sigma>0 its absolute weighted mass is exactly

    W_P(sigma)=sum_r |a_(P,chi)(r)|r^-sigma
              =product_(p in P)(1-p^-sigma)^-1.           (D04.2)

The field identity is absolutely justified: use the Gaussian positive integer sum and, for example, sigma>1 in (D04.2). Local convergence, derivatives and shell rearrangements then follow by Gaussian decay. It is an equality of the actual signed field, not domination by a favorable subfamily.

### D04.2 The coarsest sufficient moving-source hypothesis used here

Fix 1/2<gamma<1, 0<sigma<gamma, A>0 and 0<delta<1 such that

    A(1-sigma)<1,
    q_head:=sigma+delta(1-sigma)<gamma.                  (D04.3)

For every large dyadic X, put z_X=(log X)^A and

    P_X={p prime:5<=p<=z_X, p does not divide q}.

This parent X and P_X stay frozen while the argument x varies over [X,2X] and while every cofactor shell is estimated. Assume, for every epsilon>0,

    ||V_(P_X,chi)||_(L2([U,2U],dx/x))
       <= C_epsilon U^(gamma+epsilon)
    for ALL real U with X^delta<=U<=X,                  (OPEN-D04)

with constants independent of X,U. This includes the complete norm of the signed rough source; it is not a norm of only primes or one rough depth. No conclusion is drawn from V_(P_U,chi) at its own changing cutoff. The latter is a different field and is not the premise.

**Conditional return theorem.** OPEN-D04 and (D04.3) imply, for every epsilon>0,

    ||F_chi||_(L2([X,2X],dx/x)) <<_epsilon X^(gamma+epsilon).
                                                               (D04.4)

Proof of the price: for fixed 0<sigma<1, p>=5 implies

    log W_(P_X)(sigma)
       <= C_sigma sum_(p<=z_X) p^-sigma
       <= C'_sigma z_X^(1-sigma)
       =O((log X)^(A(1-sigma)))=o(log X).               (D04.5)

Comparison with ALL integers suffices; no prime-distribution estimate, calibrated random sign or external cancellation claim enters. Thus W=X^o(1), uniformly in the parent X.

Split (D04.1) at R=X^(1-delta), without rounding ambiguity: short r satisfy r<=R, long r satisfy r>R. For r<=R the exact real cofactor shell U=X/r lies in [X^delta,X]. Minkowski and OPEN-D04 give

    ||sum_(r<=R) a(r)V(./r)||_[X,2X]
       <= C_epsilon X^(gamma+epsilon)
                       sum_(r<=R)|a(r)|r^(-gamma-epsilon)
       <= C_epsilon X^(gamma+epsilon) W_(P_X)(sigma).

The last inequality uses gamma+epsilon>sigma and r>=1. For each arbitrarily small output epsilon, apply the premise with a smaller epsilon and absorb (D04.5).

For r>R, t=x/r<=2X^delta. The positive Gaussian integer sum satisfies

    sum_(n>=1)g_tau(log(n/t)) <<_tau t, t>=1,
    sum_(n>=1)g_tau(log(n/t)) <<_(tau,sigma) t^sigma, 0<t<1.

For the first bound compare the positive profile with its integral and bounded maximum; integral equals t exp(tau/2). For the second use Gaussian left-tail decay (or multiply by t^-sigma and take the bounded supremum on (0,1]). Consequently, uniformly for 0<t<=2X^delta,

    |V_(P_X,chi)(t)|
       <= C_(tau,sigma) X^(delta(1-sigma)) t^sigma.

This estimate uses ONLY coefficient modulus <=1 and includes every small-scale term and every character zero. Hence the entire long-r head is bounded pointwise by

    C X^(delta(1-sigma)) x^sigma
                  sum_(r>R)|a(r)|r^-sigma
       <= X^(q_head+o(1)).                              (D04.6)

The shell has fixed logarithmic length, so this also bounds its L2 norm. Equation (D04.3) gives a fixed positive margin below gamma. Norm triangle proves (D04.4). If the full energy is expanded afterwards, every r,r' interaction is retained; the triangle proof has already paid both mixed terms and the head square. No positivity deletion, inherited masked moment, height truncation, projector commutation or baseline-beta scalar shortcut is needed.

This coarse head price is not optimal or an equality impossibility. It removes the bounded-x source hypothesis at the stated delta/sigma cost.

### D04.3 Complete zero-exclusion return for each fixed ordinary character

Initially for Re s>1, absolute Fubini gives

    Mellin(F_chi)(s)=exp(tau*s^2/2) D_chi(s),
    D_chi(s)=sum_n f(n)chi(n)n^-s=H_chi(s)/L(s,chi),
    H_(chi,p)(s)=(1-2chi(p)p^-s)/(1-chi(p)p^-s)^2, p!=3,
    H_(chi,3)(s)=(1-chi(3)3^-s)^-2.                    (D04.7)

At p|q these are literally 1. At p>=5 the factors begin at degree two and their Euler product converges absolutely, locally uniformly on Re s>1/2. Their numerators have zeros only on Re s=log_p 2<1/2 when chi(p)!=0; denominators only on Re s=0. Prime 2 is separate: its possible numerator zeros lie on Re s=1. Prime 3 has no numerator. Thus H_chi is holomorphic and nonzero throughout 1/2<Re s<1. This accounts for all exceptional local factors instead of discarding them.

The Gaussian left tail is paid uniformly by the bounded coefficient majorant. Equation (D04.4), dyadic Cauchy-Schwarz and summation show that the Mellin integral is holomorphic on Re s>gamma. Multiplying the identity by L(s,chi), initially where it is defined, continues it to this domain with the usual meromorphic treatment of the principal pole. Any L-zero rho with gamma<Re rho<1 contradicts the nonzero right side exp(tau*rho^2/2)H_chi(rho). The accepted right boundary completes zero exclusion Re s>gamma; the principal pole at 1 is excluded. This is an all-height argument: no moving zero height, finite grid or angular uniformity is substituted.

For chi=1, this agrees with the existing f3/Gaussian return G28--G31. The displayed ordinary-character extension is derived here from its own exact zero-extended coefficient transform. No new finite-order Eisenstein Hecke transfer is proved here; that scope still needs its established exact adapter.

### D04.4 Explicit near and high-ceiling budgets

| Desired gamma | Conditional c | A | sigma | delta | q_head | gamma-q_head | A(1-sigma) |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2187/2500=.8748 | 313/2500=.1252 | 6 | 17/20 | 1/10 | 173/200=.865 | 49/5000 | 9/10 |
| 5/6 | 1/6 | 5 | 41/50 | 1/20 | 829/1000 | 13/3000 | 9/10 |
| 3/4 | 1/4 | 3 | 7/10 | 1/10 | 73/100 | 1/50 | 9/10 |

Every parameter is fixed once and for all. OPEN-D04 at its row's gamma, for all epsilon and all parent/cofactor shells specified above, is still unpaid. These costs do not turn the table into a theorem at those constants.

For any A<1/(1-gamma), one can choose sigma<gamma sufficiently close to gamma with A(1-sigma)<1 and then choose a sufficiently small positive delta. Thus this head-paid theorem retains the strict coarse cutoff ceiling of matched-Max D35 while removing its complete all-scale-source prerequisite. For actual f3, the reconstruction is infinite over smooth prime powers and is not the finite squarefree inverse from D35.

### D04.5 Baseline consistency and the strongest objection

The exact inverse to a has at an excluded prime the series

    (1-chi(p)z)/(1-2chi(p)z)
       =1+sum_(v>=1)2^(v-1)chi(p)^v z^v.

For log_5 2<sigma<1 its absolute mass is

    B_P(sigma)=product_(p in P)(1-p^-sigma)/(1-2p^-sigma),
    log B_P(sigma)=O_sigma(z^(1-sigma)).                (D04.8)

Hence V_(P,chi)=b_(P,chi)*F_chi as an absolutely justified field identity in a sufficient weighted range, with ALL powers retained. In the zeta case the inherited buffered bound F(t)<<t^beta with beta=.8749 therefore gives

    |V_(P_X,1)(t)| <<_beta t^beta B_(P_X)(beta).

Whenever A(1-beta)<1 this is a subpower-cost bound. On t>=X^delta, the parent-X subpower factor can be absorbed in t^epsilon. It reproduces only the baseline beta exponent; it does NOT give the smaller gamma in OPEN-D04. Exact prime conditioning is an equivalence at fixed cutoff and does not generate the needed arithmetic saving. The new theorem saves a *range obligation*, not the open full signed exponent. At the near row A=6 the baseline cost exponent is 6(1-.8749)=.7506<1.

Functional signature: actual f3*chi rough field; full smooth-part reconstruction with a paid small-cofactor head; cancellation remains in the complete signed rough field; first unpaid estimate OPEN-D04 uniformly on X^delta<=U<=X with frozen parent cutoff; proved return gamma plus q_head/complement cost. Closest record ancestry is matched-Max D35, inherited smooth-state A4/A5 and current G28/G29. Novelty claimed only for this explicit f3 all-power/head-paid contract relative to the inspected sources, not a new rough-detector architecture or literature priority.

Next decisive mathematical action: attack OPEN-D04 for one row with the full rough f3 coefficient, or compare the all-power source against a tractable signed rough-depth band. A prime-only norm or source at its own U-cutoff is insufficient. The lower-head debt is already paid; re-proving it is not the next bottleneck.
title: D04. Moving rough f3 detector with a paid cofactor head

statement:
### 2.4 A finite upper certificate that does not ignore zeros or tails

There is a direct constructive form of L6(i). For integer N>=exp(j+1), let F_N retain precisely n<=N. The decreasing positive tail and t=exp(v) give the explicit uniform bound on I_j=[j,j+1]

    |F-F_N|<=T_(N,j)
      =exp(j+1+tau/2) barPhi((log N-j-1-tau)/sqrt tau), (L8)

where barPhi is the standard normal upper tail. This bound applies to every fixed ordinary chi because |f3 chi|<=1. Choose any certified T>=T_(N,j), T>0. Then log|F|<=log(|F_N|+T), even at zeros. For b>1, differentiating the Gaussian and completing the square gives

    sup_Ij |F_N'|<=K_j,
    K_j=(2pi tau)^(-1/2)(1+1/(b-1))
        exp(b(j+1)+tau b^2/2)[b+1/sqrt(e tau)].        (L9)

Here sum n^-b<=1+1/(b-1), and sup_w |w|exp(-w^2/(2tau))=sqrt(tau/e). Consequently log(|F_N|+T) is K_j/T-Lipschitz, also through zeros. At the M equal-subinterval midpoints u_k, if a numerical enclosure has |F_N(u_k)-v_k|<=delta_k, then the rigorous one-sided certificate is

    J_j <= (1/M)sum_k log(|v_k|+delta_k+T)+K_j/(4MT). (L10)

No interchange of log and a small additive error is assumed. ### A.3 Merging integer states changes the operator norm

For a floor-invariant F, floor(t/p)=floor(floor(t)/p). At an integer root N, group (R2) by m=floor(N/d), p=P^+(d). For d>1 write d=pu with P^+(u)<p. The exact fibre coefficient is

    C_(N,chi)(m,p)
      =-chi(p) sum_(N/[p(m+1)]<u<=N/(pm), P^+(u)<p)
                         mu(u)chi(u).                     (R5)

The lower endpoint is STRICT, upper inclusive, u=1 is retained and there is no imposed independence between its terms. Consequently

    E(N,1)=Delta(N,1)+sum_(p,m) C_(N,chi)(m,p)Delta(m,p).   (R6)

For integer r>=1 and exact integer collar m<=p^r, the exact independent-state norm, N>1, is

    B_(r,chi)(N)=1+sum_(p,m>p^r)|C_(N,chi)(m,p)|.         (R7)

Triangular back substitution realizes arbitrary merged defects; conjugate phases attain (R7). The integer collar can be larger than the corresponding real collar, since floor(t)<=p^r allows t<p^r+1. The surviving integer states are nevertheless a subset of the real noncollar states, so B<=N_(r,q) is valid. An exponent-one LOWER bound cannot pass through this grouping.

The concrete collision is correct. At N=20196,m=18,p=17, the smooth squarefree u in the interval (20196/(17*19),66] are exactly65 and66. Their Mobius values are+1,-1. Equivalently d=1105 and1122 have signs-1,+1 and the same integer state outside the r=1 collar. Their principal coefficient cancels to0. With the real character modulo4 it is-1, and with chi(2)=i modulo5 it is i. My independent exact checks verify all three. The example proves that cross-depth coalescence is real; it supplies no common-character bound.

This correction is part of the accepted result, not an optional caveat. A depth-tagged implementation can destroy the cancellation it is supposed to exploit. No new lower exponent or improved upper exponent for (R7) is proved.

### 2.2 Global derivative estimate, including both finite cutoffs and infinity

Assume explicitly |M(t)|<=C t^beta, beta>0. The unconditional choice is beta=1,C=1. For real r>=2, k_r(u)=(1-u/r)_+^r has derivative -(1-u/r)^(r-1) on (0,r) and zero beyond r; it is absolutely continuous and its derivative joins continuously at r.

For 0<=u<=r/2 write z=(r-1)log(1-u/r)+u and A=u-u^2/2. The log series gives

    z<=u/r,  |z|<=(u+u^2)/r,
    |z-A/r|<=(u^2/2+2u^3/3)/r^2.

The last error is the positive u^2/(2r^2) correction together with the entire order>=3 log tail. Since exp(-u)exp(max(z,0))<=exp(-u/2), Taylor with its full real remainder gives

    |k'_r+exp(-u)| <= (5u+u^2)exp(-u/2)/r,
    |k'_r+exp(-u)(1+A/r)| <= P(u)exp(-u/2)/r^2,
    P(u)=12u^2+4u^3+u^4.

The second short-range estimate actually needs at most u^2+(5/3)u^3+u^4/2 in place of P. On u>=r/2, including u>r, use |k'_r|<=exp(-u/2) on its support and zero outside. Multiplying the second claimed estimate by r^2 costs at most 2r^2+r|A|<=10u^2+u^3<=P, since r<=2u. The first estimate there follows from 2<=4u/r. This independently verifies the global bound; it is not an inference from the author's floating grid.

Abel integration is exact:

    sum_n a(n)h(n/x)=-int_0^infty M(xu)h'(u)du.

The zero/infinity boundary terms vanish for the kernels at hand. Integrating u^beta times the first bound gives

    |B_r-E|<=C K1(beta)x^beta/r,
    K1=5*2^(beta+2)Gamma(beta+2)+2^(beta+3)Gamma(beta+3).

Write k'_r=-exp(-u)(1+A/r)+e_r. The A/r terms cancel exactly in 2k'_(2r)-k'_r+exp(-u), leaving at most (2/4+1)P exp(-u/2)/r^2. Therefore

    |V_r-E|<=(3/2)C K2(beta)x^beta/r^2,
    K2=12*2^(beta+3)Gamma(beta+3)
        +4*2^(beta+4)Gamma(beta+4)+2^(beta+5)Gamma(beta+5).

At beta=1 these constants are K1=176, K2=11904, and the second bound has coefficient17856. They are coarse but uniform for all x>0 and real r>=2. The proof includes the branch rx<n<=2rx, the endpoint integers, and the entire infinite exponential tail. Squaring V requires 4|B_(2r)|^2+|B_r|^2-4Re(B_(2r)conj(B_r)); these signed cross terms cannot be dropped. The exact checker verifies these finite conventions, while the preceding proof covers all scales.

## 6. Cross-gcd and short-cofactor preparation at the energy level

Start from \(\|B_X^{(W)}\|_2^2\). In its quartic expansion retain

\[
(d_i,d_j)^{\langle W\rangle}<R/W
\quad(ij\in\mathcal E).
\tag{PO38}
\]

The complementary union implies \((d_i,d_j)\ge R/W\) for some
cross edge. Every condition here, including the two internal
conditions in (PO33), is a bounded function of the original six
gcds. Hence it stays fixed on the original prime-incidence variables
through the cancellation in
[MG21--MG30](../[private research revision]-continuation/mobius-gcd.md#5-original-prime-incidence-and-masks-for-all-gcds).
Apply the positive shared-incidence majorant only after that
cancellation. It bounds the entire signed complementary union by

\[
O_\epsilon\bigl(X^{2b+\epsilon}(R/W)^{1-2b}\bigr)
=O_\epsilon(X^{\beta+\epsilon}),\qquad
\beta=2b+\frac{1-2b}{700}
=\frac{6120551}{3500000}=1.748728857142\ldots .
\tag{PO39}
\]

The fixed incidence mask can be dropped in the final positive
majorant; it is not differentiated or recomputed in auxiliary
coprimality variables. Thus this use is uniform in \(W\).

Now impose all cofactor conditions in (PO11). For one edge let
\(A^W_{ij}\) be the event that some \(a,b\mid W\) and
\(r,s\le J\) violate that condition. This event depends only on
the original pair \((d_i,d_j)\). Write
\(d_i=u_iD_i,d_j=u_jD_j\) as in (PO10). A violation implies

\[
|r'd_i-s'd_j|\le W\Delta,\qquad
r'=raW/u_i,\quad s'=sbW/u_j,\qquad
1\le r',s'\le JW^2.
\tag{PO40}
\]

The displayed multipliers are integers. Thus the actual bad-pair
set is contained in an ordinary rational-strip union with
multiplier limit \(JW^2\) and tolerance \(W\Delta\). These are
only logarithmic enlargements, and \(W\Delta\le Y/2\) for large

The proof of [SP9 and SP15--SP17](../[private research revision]/mobius-separated-products.md#2-uniform-divisor-masks-in-one-and-two-möbius-sums)

\((h,D)\). The remaining condition is a bounded coefficient
\(a_{(e,h)}\). SP9 estimates the two unfrozen Möbius sums uniformly
in all those functions. The fixed pair's mask is then retained
while bounding its count by the larger union in (PO40). This is
not a restriction of a signed estimate to an arbitrary subset.

\(O_\epsilon(X^{b+1/2+\epsilon}(\Delta+1))\).

absolute intersection count, with (PO40), is
\(O(XL^C(\Delta+1)^2)\). This proves for the full signed union

\[
O_\epsilon\left(
X^{b+1/2+\epsilon}(\Delta+1)
+X^{1+\epsilon}(\Delta+1)^2\right)
=O_\epsilon(X^{1.7489+\epsilon}+X^{1.748+\epsilon}).
\tag{PO41}
\]

Sharp individual endpoints remain those of (PO7), and all weights
in the two-variable Abel estimate are the original \(\Xi\) factors
with their \(O(L^{12})\) mixed Euler seminorms. The cofactor mask is
independent of \(\ell,m\), so those finite sums can be kept inside

# W64 independent unselected audits BEFORE author outcomes

These are the two audits mandated by the immutable seed-only orders. Author identity-only intake gave S06,S18,S11,S24,S10,S04. Therefore the protected audit is S30 and the distinct uniform audit is S17. No author test conclusion, report, helper, outcome or final manifest has been read. The original missed deadline remains; final closeout target02:15UTC13Oct. These audits concern the actual seed statements and precisely delimited constructions, not a claimed proof of a new c.

## A. Protected S30: rough polymers with the entire signed smooth core

Fix an ordinary Dirichlet character chi modulo q with natural zeros. For real x>=1 and y>=2 write

    M_chi(x)=sum_(n<=x)mu(n)chi(n),
    S_(y,chi)(t)=sum_(a<=t,Pplus(a)<=y)mu(a)chi(a),

where1 belongs to the smooth set and S_y(t)=0 for t<1. A prime at y belongs to the smooth set. Every squarefree n has a UNIQUE decomposition n=ab into its y-smooth part a and y-rough part b. They are coprime. Consequently the complete identity is

    M_chi(x)=sum_(b<=x,Pminus(b)>y)mu(b)chi(b) S_(y,chi)(x/b). (A1)

The b=1 term is included. Squareful b has coefficient zero; a shares no prime with b. All character zeros are literal, and n=x is included. For y=x^eta with fixed0<eta<1, b has k<1/eta prime factors unless b=1, since each factor is STRICTLY greater than y. At the integer endpoint k eta=1, that k-sector is empty; no endpoint term is lost. Thus this is an exact finite-depth polymer expansion with a moving smooth core, not a model gas.

The proposed coarse absolute outer budget, STILL retaining all cancellation inside each smooth core, is

    B_eta(x)=sum_(b<=x,Pminus(b)>x^eta)mu(b)^2 |chi(b)|
                                      |S_(x^eta,chi)(x/b)|. (A2)

For sufficiently large x, every unramified prime p in(x/2,x] is eligible, because x^eta<x/2. Its inner argument lies in[1,2), so its ENTIRE signed smooth core equals1. Therefore

    B_eta(x)>=pi(x)-pi(x/2)-O_q(1) >>_q x/log x.             (A3)

This applies to EVERY fixed ordinary character, not just the principal character, because absolute |chi(p)|=1 on unramified primes. The elementary identity and the constant inner prefix are exact; the displayed asymptotic lower bound uses the ordinary prime asymptotic. It was independently rechecked in [NIST DLMF27.12.4-5](https://dlmf.nist.gov/27.12) in this audit (turn264view0); no progression or conductor-uniform theorem is used. It can be replaced by any fixed-ratio quantitative prime-interval lower bound.

The same obstruction survives the usual shell-Minkowski version, not merely a single-point triangle inequality. Freeze y=X^eta on x in[X,2X], or use y=x^eta. For all sufficiently large X and every unramified prime p in(X,3X/2], the full b=p summand has inner smooth prefix1 on x in[3X/2,2X]. The argument x/p belongs to[1,2), apart from excluded/measure-zero endpoints. Its L2(dx/x) norm is at least sqrt(log(4/3)). Thus the SUM OF COMPLETE POLYMER NORMS is >>_q X/log X. The same holds in L1, with log(4/3). No internal smooth prefix was replaced by an unsigned coefficient count.

This is a lower bound on the proposed positive outer certificate ONLY. The full source in(A1) retains the complex factors mu(b)chi(b) and the cross terms between ALL b. Equation(A3) is emphatically not a lower bound for |M_chi|, its shell norm or a signed polymer Gram. Grouping distinct polymers before taking norms could evade it; its complete signed cost is then the new arithmetic obligation.

A complete square observation is exactly

    |M_chi(x)|^2=sum_(b,c eligible)mu(b)chi(b)conj(mu(c)chi(c))
                         S_y(x/b)conj(S_y(x/c)).             (A4)

This includes b=c, b=1/c=1 and both cross orientations. It is the appropriate place to seek a saving; isolated small-polymer or diagonal bounds do not control it. If the FULL signed(A1), or its complete every-epsilon shell L1 observation, is O(x^(gamma+epsilon)) for common gamma>.5, standard absolute dyadic Mellin convergence continues1/L on Re(s)>gamma. Moving y creates no extra Mellin factor because(A1) equals the original Mertens source pointwise. A bound on only the smooth term or one polymer sector has no such return.

For eta>1/2 there is at most one large prime, and(A1) specializes to

    M_chi(x)=S_(x^eta,chi)(x)
             -sum_(x^eta<p<=x)chi(p)M_chi(x/p).             (A5)

Indeed x/p<x^(1-eta)<x^eta, so the inner smooth cutoff is vacuous. This is exact G166-type prime removal, with the original small-argument Mertens source and M_chi(1)=1 retained. It is not a new short-source arithmetic theorem. More generally absolute bounds |S_y(t)|<=C t^beta only give O_beta(Cx) by summing b^-beta for beta<1; (A3) shows the lack of a power is real for the positive certificate, even if the small prefixes were otherwise favorable.

Disposition before author outcomes: **coarse positive polymer budget obstructed; complete signed polymer mechanism remains open.** The useful exact refinement is that retaining signed smooth cores internally does not rescue the outer Minkowski price. Prime-removal/matching ancestry is substantial (G166, G173-G175); no literature or project-wide novelty is claimed. Next action must retain cross-polymer cancellation in(A4), or group polymers with a proved complete signed estimate.

## B. Uniform S17: the full feedback denominator and the missing native map

The seed proposes neighboring native H packets as a feedback state. Accepted G136 already retains the exact two-block recursion, and G151 says no compatible inter-scale map between changing prime-pair groups has been constructed. Its fixed native packet is an Eisenstein source, NOT an ordinary mu or positive-divisor surrogate: retain original coefficients a(n)=alpha(n)eta(n)chi_n(lambda)^(-2)gamma2(n), xi(g)=alpha(g)^3 eta(g)^3, distinct rational long-prime norms, both short-core orders including equality, natural zeros, both projectors, rooted marks, masks, independent heights, CRT/angular data and1/Q Fourier normalization. A bijective ambient state transfer cannot simply be assumed; an embedding/projection needs its full discarded or forced complement. This is an ambient dimension observation, not a lower bound on a source-only state reduction.

Here is a completely priced conditional feedback lemma, to state what an actual scale construction would need. For a fixed finite compatible map, let

    T=[[a,b],[c,D]], z_(j+1)=T z_j+f_j, z_j=(alpha_j,eta_j).

Take r>||D||, K=(r-||D||)^(-1), and define the Schur denominator

For |w|>=r the reverse triangle inequality gives |s(w)|>=Delta. Hence T has no eigenvalue there, and on |w|=r its resolvent norm is at most

                 +C_r sum_(k<j)r^(j-k)||f_k||.             (B6)

Every forcing and initial mode is retained. More favorable signed feedback may replace(B4), but must ensure no Schur zero throughout |w|>=r and pay its contour minimum. A contour bound without controlling exterior poles does not suffice. A varying family T_j needs product/Volterra control; applying this stationary lemma separately to each step is invalid without a proved common metric or compatible product estimate.

The first decisive diagnostic reproduces the known G136 obstruction:

    T=[[1,e],[e,0]], e>0, D=0,

The innovation block vanishes, yet the scalar observable grows. The exact recurrence is alpha_(j+1)=alpha_j+e^2 alpha_(j-1). To use(B6) in actual H, construct the exact compatible state maps, price every projector/mask translation defect and both boundary forcing channels, bind r^j to the physical scales, and sum all packet readouts with their true norms. The full raw target remains G Kphys [N+L+(NL)^(2/3)] sqrt(Omega1 Omega2) P_orig, followed by physical N^(-1)G^(-2) exactly once. This is exact completion over ALL e and l before any physical cut. It
does not factor a physical mask or discard shared primes. Explicitly,

    h_p(1)=0, h_p(p)=-chi(p),
    h_p(j)=-chi(j)(1-p 1_(p|j)) for j not in {1,p}.

Thus |h_p(j)|<=p-1, with all character zeros retained. It is periodic
only outside the two finite corrections; treating it as a zero-mean
periodic sequence everywhere would be wrong.

Define the complete finite asymmetric core

    A_p,chi,X(x)=sum_(d>A,j>=2,L<dj<=M)
                     mu(d)chi(d) h_p(j) f_x(dj).     (R12)

Its cofactor bound is j<=M/(A+1)<<X^(r-u), and its coefficients are
bounded by (p-1)d_2(n). Both physical endpoints remain sharp. Applying

For p not dividing n, its untruncated coefficient has the exact form

For distinct primes r,s not dividing pq this becomes

### 2.3 Fixed-field convolution identities

The coefficient series for A is

    sum A(n)n^(-s) = (1-2^(1-s))/zeta(s),   Re(s)>1.

Multiplying the local factors in (2.1)--(2.4) gives the exact
Dirichlet convolution identities

    A = k_6 * f_3,                 f_3 = j_6 * A,
    k_6 * j_6 = delta_1.                                  (2.8)

Consequently, for every x>0,

    G_tau(x) = sum_{m>=1} k_6(m) F_6(x/m),
    F_6(x)   = sum_{m>=1} j_6(m) G_tau(x/m).               (2.9)

These are genuine field identities, not only formal Mellin ratios.
Indeed |f_3(n)|=1 and |A(n)|<=3. For c>1, either rearranged
double sum is bounded by a constant times

    x^c (sum_m |a(m)|m^(-c)) (sum_n n^(-c)) < infinity,

where a is k_6 or j_6. This proves pointwise and local uniform
absolute convergence of the rearrangement.

The long-factor cumulative source is exactly

    sum_(d,e>Y,de<=x) alpha(d)alpha(e) B(x/(de)).     (R9)

It includes the ordered pairs, their shared primes and the complete restoration sum. The product cap gives d,e<=X/(Y+1) and ell<=X/(Y+1)^2; the individual bounds do not replace the joint condition de ell<=X.

Partition (R9) into d=e, then d!=e with gcd(d,e)>R, then its remaining d!=e, gcd<=R sector. These are disjoint and exhaustive, including equality at the gcd threshold in the last sector.

The diagonal is bounded in modulus by C_b sqrt(x), even though chi(d)^2 need not be nonnegative. Its kernel is dominated by `C_b e^[(1/2-a)(t+u)]`. Cauchy--Schwarz in each variable bounds the full operator by C_b D_a(X). This is H9a. At a=1/2 the value is L; at a<1/2 its exponent is 1/2-a; at a>1/2 it is bounded. No squareful contribution of this component was discarded.

For the off-diagonal high-gcd sector write d=gu,e=gv with g the actual gcd, then discard (u,v)=1 only inside a positive count. Since

    # {(u,v):uv<=w} <=w(1+log w),

the total number with gcd>R is at most

    x(1+log x)sum_(g>R)g^(-2)
       <<x(1+log x)/R.                              (R10)

Take |B|<=C_b only after its complete restoration sum. The resulting kernel is dominated by a constant times `(1+log X)e^[(1-a)(t+u)]/R`. Its rank-one envelope has norm O_a(X^(1-a)), proving H9b. Phi_hat(X q_k/(q_d q_a q_b)). All coprimality and nonunit masks remain.
Here c_d is the corresponding Ramanujan sum. Resolving it and using
the existing cubic sieve after taking absolute values gives the
available upper-bound cost

\[
\mathcal M(X,D)\ll(XD)^\delta
 [X+D+X^{2/3}D^{2/3}+X^{1/3}D]. \tag{R3}
\]

An apparent diagonal of the dual positive Mobius norm is not a new
main term of the off-diagonal transform: its complete ell-projector
cancels by sum_(ell|a) mu(ell)=0 for a>1.

The accepted individual Mobius bounds pay the principal dual packet
at cost

\[
(XD)^\delta X^{2/3}D^{2b_0-4/3}. \tag{R4}
\]

For k=zj, z|d, principal induction requires dzj to be a cube outside
S. Thus j contains z(d/z)^2, leaving O((H/C^2)^(1/3)) rows up to
divisor and fixed-S losses. The common-core dyad has weight
C^(1-2b0+delta), which is summable. This is an upper-bound budget,
not a lower bound for the actual signed packet.

At D=X, (R3) costs X^(4/3), while (R4) costs
X^(1.0831066274...). At D=X^2 they cost respectively X^(7/3) and
X^(1.4995465882...). The target is X^(35/32); the latter two excesses
are 119/96 and 0.4057965882... . At D=X^2 the dual length is H=X^3.
Its nonprincipal signed bilinear target is X^(131/32+delta), whereas
the generic positive certificate costs X^(16/3+delta).

## 8. Literal physical input, modulus padding, and every shortening

The physical family is the fixed SourcePrincipal S base, natural row zeros, and the complete conjugated reflected product. The actual `PhysicalMomentInput` identities show the slot is the conjugate of the negative-orientation canonical amplitude; its common profile is conjugate F.W, its real annular power is 33/50, and each original height becomes minus Im(z_i). Both reflected plain profiles remain independent. These are coefficient equalities on the natural family, not arbitrary-twist moment substitutions.

`Physical-SourceState.weighted_source_exceptional_norm` bounds each fixed-inducing free row by a fixed norm depending on the fixed family. Therefore every growing retained dyad d>=d0=1/200 excludes it eventually, even though a convenience theorem elsewhere uses exponent 1/100. The actual fixed-norm bound suffices for any fixed d0>0. Small nonprincipal rows are separately paid below; principal rows are not deleted by this observation.

A normalization detail deserves explicit retention. `finite_physical_pair_positiveAt` allows a fixed parent-modulus padding nu with norm(eta)<=U^nu and width 1+nu; it does not assert that the fixed parent modulus equals one. Choose nu>0 from the common real/moment-loss budget before the target, and raise its target-dependent threshold afterward. Normalizing the source width by 1+nu slightly raises its absolute lower cutoffs to .41(1+nu) and .034(1+nu). The old short-plain reserve below then loses at most .41nu; the short-slot reserve loses at most .153nu. Both are strictly positive for sufficiently small nu, and the shaped inequality 2n+Lambda z<=B implies <=B(1+nu). Upper cutoffs only relax. Nominal local lower margins stay positive when nu is smaller than those margins. Thus all three scale regions remain covered; the extra U^nu is part of the requested moment loss. The same treatment covers fixed-conductor, annular and scale-box padding without moving a hypothesis silently.

For the endpoint take

    h=3969737987/5000000000,
    ell=11/3-4theta=7838/46875,
    x=5598946039/15000000000, y=6892893961/15000000000,
    kappa_*=2theta-1=23429/31250,
    d_-=h-.001, d_+=h+10^-10, t0=.001.

Then x+y=1-ell, 0<ell<x<y<2x, y<.5<h<2y, 1/6<ell<1/5 and h>4ell. The probe inequalities are y-2x+ell=-598946039/5000000000 and 1+3ell-2(x+y)=-1537/9375. With k_probe=5/6-x/3-ell/6, the exact physical boundary is (5x+y)/12=theta-k_probe.

For d in [d_-,d_+] and free Euler shift exponent t in [0,t0], put n=1-y/d+t and choose capacity just below

    z_A=(B-2n)/Lambda,
    d z_A(0)=[2y-(2-B)d]/Lambda.                  (R4)

The intercept charge (1-B) must be present. Exact monotonicity gives

    n_min=5001320000/11894213961,
    n_max=402258337237/952737117000,
    z_min=71106755506391/1995746075835750,
    z_max=51907630715077/1423737411131700.

Thus .41<n_min<=n_max<N=.4223 and .034<z_min<=z_max<.0365<.04. The upper margins are N-n_max=825472721/9527371170000 and .0365-z_max=1175695824601/28474748222634000. All padding and a fixed capacity decrement are chosen smaller than these and the row saving. N is an endpoint upper bound, not a new restriction on transformed children.

Apply the original `zero_error_whole_slots` directly to z_A. Include all original widths w_i=ell_i/d in L=ell/d; errors have zero gain. Let q=L^(-1)sum_i w_i g_i=delta p with 0<=g_i<=delta/2 and 0<=p<=1/2. For sufficiently short individual slots and z_A<=L, the selector returns one positive-main subset I for the entire amplitude class with

    z_I<=z_A,
    |product_(i in I) Q_i|^2 >= U^(2q z_A-delta mesh-small).

If positive-main supply is exhausted, its full gain qL>=qz_A is enough. Neither positive-main width at least z_A nor insertion of zero-gain factors is justified or needed. This fixed I is used for every plain derivative.

All actual shortening is covered, with cutoff equality harmless:

1. If z_I<=.034, old budget 2N+4.5(.034)=.9976, reserve 3/1250.
2. If z_I>=.034 and either actual plain<=.41, old budget .41+N+4.5(.0365)=.99655, reserve 69/20000, symmetrically.
3. Otherwise both actual plains lie in [.41,N] and .034<=z_I<.04, with their sum plus Lambda z_I at most 2n+Lambda z_A=B; use the interior theorem.
4. If I is empty, the unrestricted physical zero-slot input applies, with no sum-of-plains gate.

With the small modulus/width padding described above, move these cutoffs together and spend the displayed reserve portions. Separate two-variable Sobolev recovery on the resulting rectangles uses exactly four profile pairs. Boundary scales do not create a missing region. The selection gain remains at target z_A even in either old-moment complement. Holder gives exponent 1/4+3R/4-q z_A/2.

Supply has ample exact margins: ell-d_+z_max=78740857190181221448997/569494964452680000000000>0, ell/d_+-4/21=44751148/2223053273>0, 2ell-1/3=17/15625>0, and 4ell-y=1046582013/5000000000>0. For d<.5 invoke the original selector, not its d>=.5 convenience wrapper: L>=2ell>1/3>1/(6kappa) for kappa>=.7. statement:
## 2. Development A: an entire Gaussian can be observed on small local sets

Use the NORMALIZED fixed kernel

    g_tau(v)=(2 pi tau)^(-1/2) exp(-v^2/(2tau)), tau>0.

The cards used its unnormalized version; multiplication by the fixed positive constant changes none of their exponents. For ordinary chi put

    a_n=mu(n)chi(n), F(z)=sum_(n>=1) a_n g_tau(log n-z).      (W39.1)

All natural zeros of mu and chi remain. This is the complete unmasked sum. Local uniform absolute convergence proves F entire. Writing z=u+iv gives

    |F(u+iv)| <= C_tau exp(u+v^2/(2tau)), u>=0.              (W39.2)

Indeed the positive sum of g_tau(log n-u) is at most its integral over t>0 plus twice its maximum, because that function of t is unimodal. The integral is exp(u+tau/2), and u>=0 absorbs the fixed maximum. For u<=0 the same series is O_tau(exp(-u^2/(2tau))), since log n>=0. This also pays the entire left Mellin tail.

### A1. Elementary measurable-set interpolation, including complex values

Let P be a complex polynomial of degree at most N>=1 on an interval I of length1. If a measurable E subset I has measure delta>0 and |P|<=m almost everywhere on E, then

    sup_I |P| <= (4e/delta)^N m.                           (W39.3)

Here is a proof rather than an external Remez citation. Replace E by the closed set {|P|<=m} intersect I, whose actual measure Delta is at least delta. Choose N+1 quantile points x_0<...<x_N at cumulative-measure levels (j+1/2)Delta/(N+1). The cumulative distribution is1-Lipschitz, so

    x_j-x_i >= (j-i)delta/(N+1).

The quantile points lie in the closed set. Lagrange interpolation and |x-x_i|<=1 give

    sum_j |ell_j(x)|
      <= ((N+1)/delta)^N sum_j 1/[j!(N-j)!]
      = ((N+1)/delta)^N 2^N/N! <= (4e/delta)^N.

The inequality N!>=(N/e)^N follows by integrating log t. If m is only an essential supremum, enlarge it arbitrarily and pass to the limit. Thus no real-polynomial sign assumption is used.

### A2. The single-step exponent, with the Taylor remainder paid first

Assume an entire F satisfies, for fixed b>gamma and constants C,K,

    |F(u+iv)| <= C(1+|v|)^K exp(bu+v^2/(2tau)), u>=0.      (W39.4)

Suppose every sufficiently large integer j has a measurable E_j subset [j,j+1] such that

    |E_j| >= c j^(-kappa),
    ess sup_(u in E_j)|F(u)| <= C_0 exp(gamma j),           (W39.5)

where c>0, kappa>=0 are fixed. Then

    sup_[j,j+1]|F| <= exp((gamma+2kappa(b-gamma)+o(1))j).   (W39.6)

For kappa>=1/2 the direct bound b may be better; no gain is asserted there.

Proof. Set

    N=ceil(2(b-gamma)j/log j), c_j=j+1/2,
    R=sqrt(tau(N+1)).

For large j, the disk |z-c_j|<=R lies in Re z>=0 and R>1. Its maximum is at most

    C(1+R)^K exp(b(j+1/2+R)+R^2/(2tau)).

Let P_N be the Taylor polynomial at c_j. On |z-c_j|<=1/2, Cauchy's coefficient bound gives the full remainder

    r_j <= M_R (1/(2R))^(N+1)/(1-1/(2R)),
    log r_j <= b j - (N/2)log N + O_(b,tau,K)(N+sqrt N)
             = gamma j + o(j).                           (W39.7)

The source bound on E_j therefore gives |P_N|<=C_0 exp(gamma j)+r_j there. Apply W39.3 BEFORE discarding r_j:

    sup_I |F| <= L_j C_0 exp(gamma j)+(L_j+1)r_j,
    log L_j <= N log(4e/c)+kappa N log j
             =2kappa(b-gamma)j+o(j).                     (W39.8)

This proves W39.6 and prices both amplified remainders. The statement with an arbitrary epsilon allowance in W39.5 has the same limiting exponent, by choosing its epsilon before the desired output epsilon. Constants may depend on all fixed parameters.

In particular a fixed positive measure in EVERY unit interval (kappa=0) preserves gamma for any bounded-coefficient Gaussian, with no meromorphic input. This is an analytic statement about the whole field, not a signed coefficient submask estimate.

### A3. Why the ordinary L-function replenishes the complex bound

For Re s>1, absolute Fubini gives

    integral_R F(y)e^(-s y)dy=exp(tau s^2/2)/L(s,chi).     (W39.9)

If F(y)<<_epsilon exp((h+epsilon)y) for every epsilon>0 as y tends to +infinity, its left Gaussian tail makes the integral holomorphic on Re s>h, including every fixed s derivative. Multiply by L and continue from Re s>1. At any zero rho in this domain, the left product would vanish while exp(tau rho^2/2) does not. A principal pole at1 is separately removable in the reciprocal and creates no false zero exclusion. Hence there are no L zeros in Re s>h.

Conversely, if a fixed ordinary L has no zeros in Re s>h, with h>0, then for EVERY fixed b>h and tau>0 the very same F satisfies W39.4 for some C,K. We need only polynomial growth of 1/L on the fixed line, and derive it here to avoid an unproved inverse-bound assumption.

For a nonprincipal ordinary character, its periodic partial sums are O_q(1). Abel summation gives

    L(s,chi)=s integral_1^infinity A_chi(t)t^(-s-1)dt,
    |L(s,chi)| <= q |s|/Re s, Re s>0.                   (W39.10)

For a principal character A_chi(t)=ct+O_q(1); subtract ct in this integral. It gives the simple principal pole and a polynomial upper bound for P(s)=(s-1)L(s,chi) on every closed positive strip. In the nonprincipal case put P=L. The finite imprimitive Euler factors stay literal and are nonzero on Re s>0.

Fix h<b<2; b>=2 is trivial. Around 2+it take an outer disk of radius R_0=2-(h+b)/2 and inner radius r_0=2-b. The outer disk is zero-free for P, lies in Re s>h, and the gap R_0-r_0=(b-h)/2 is fixed. An analytic logarithm log P exists on that disk. Choose its value at the center to have imaginary part in [-pi,pi]. The absolutely convergent Euler product at2 bounds |L(2+it)| above and away from0; the regularizing factor changes its logarithm by O(log(2+|t|)). Thus |log P(2+it)|=O(log(2+|t|)). The polynomial upper bound for P gives Re log P<=C log(2+|t|) throughout the disk. The elementary Borel--Caratheodory inequality now bounds |log P(b+it)| by C_(h,b,q) log(2+|t|), proving

    |1/L(b+it,chi)| <= C(1+|t|)^K.                       (W39.11)

For completeness put f=log P, choose M>sup Re f, and set g=M-f. Then Re g>0 and H(z)=(g(z)-g(0))/(g(z)+conj(g(0))) maps the disk into the unit disk and vanishes at its center. Schwarz gives |H(z)|<=r_0/R_0 on the inner disk. The triangle inequality then bounds |g(z)| by (R_0+r_0)/(R_0-r_0) times |g(0)|. Since M and |f(0)| are O(log(2+|t|)), the stated bound for f follows. A compact low-height region is absorbed into C. Uniform bounds hold across a fixed closed horizontal strip by using the smallest gap; the reciprocal has a zero at the principal pole, not a singularity.

Mellin inversion on a line >1, followed by a contour shift to b, now gives for all complex z

    F(z)=(2pi)^(-1) integral_R
       exp(tau(b+it)^2/2) exp((b+it)z)/L(b+it,chi) dt.    (W39.12)

Horizontal sides vanish by the Gaussian exp(-tau t^2/2), with W39.11; locally uniform convergence also proves the identity for complex z. Completing the square in -tau t^2/2-tv gives

    |F(u+iv)| <= C exp(bu+v^2/(2tau)) (1+|v|)^K,

which is W39.4. Neither a conjectured Möbius Mertens bound nor subpower height growth was required. The polynomial degree K may worsen at each fixed iteration; W39.7 absorbs it, since only finitely many iterations are used for a chosen output epsilon.

### A4. The self-improving local-set theorem

**Theorem W39-A (ordinary).** Fix tau>0, an ordinary Dirichlet character chi, 0<gamma<1, and 0<=kappa<1/2. Suppose for every epsilon>0 and every sufficiently large integer j there exists a measurable E_j subset [j,j+1] with

    |E_j| >= c_epsilon j^(-kappa),
    ess sup_(u in E_j) |sum_n mu(n)chi(n)g_tau(log n-u)|
        <= C_epsilon exp((gamma+epsilon)j).              (W39.13)

Then L(s,chi) has no zeros in Re s>gamma. Moreover the COMPLETE fixed Gaussian obeys |F(u)|<<_epsilon exp((gamma+epsilon)u) at every large real u. The E_j may depend on chi, epsilon and j; their existence and bounds are arithmetic hypotheses, not selected from an observed favorable subsequence.

Proof. Put r=2kappa<1 and h_m=gamma+r^m(1-gamma). Initial W39.2 supplies b=1. A2 and A3 prove zero exclusion and the all-scale Gaussian bound at limiting exponent h_1. Inductively zero exclusion above h_m replenishes W39.4 for every b>h_m; apply A2 with suitably small fixed epsilon margins to get h_(m+1). For any requested sigma>gamma, choose a finite m with h_m<sigma and margins smaller than sigma-h_m. The Mellin return excludes every zero with Re rho>gamma. The same finite argument, or W39.12 on b in (gamma,gamma+epsilon), gives the final all-scale bound. No limit of constants or moving number of iterations is taken inside an estimate.

Any fixed positive interval length can replace1, by rescaling W39.3 and changing only fixed constants in W39.7. The coefficient2 in the SINGLE-STEP loss is proved, not asserted optimal. This method gives no improvement from kappa>=1/2. It neither proves a counterexample there nor excludes a stronger arithmetic observability theorem.

If a prior fixed buffered exponent B is already available, replace1 by B in h_m. With kappa=1/4, B approaching .874872 and gamma=.87449, the first limiting exponent is .874681; the limit is .87449. Starting only from1 gives h_m=.87449+2^(-m)*.12551, crossing .874872 at m=9. These are CONDITIONAL returns from W39.13, not newly proved constants. The same hypothesis at gamma=5/6 or3/4 supplies the corresponding all-height targets.

### A5. The stated Eisenstein Hecke family, with fixed-conductor quantifiers

Let K=Q(sqrt(-3)), O_K its Eisenstein lattice, and psi a fixed finite-order Hecke character of trivial infinite type, extended by zero on ideals not coprime to its fixed PRESENTED ray modulus f. Include any specified finite deleted primes in f; it need not be the minimal conductor. Define

    F_psi(z)=sum_(nonzero integral ideals a)
                 mu_K(a)psi(a)g_tau(log N(a)-z).          (W39.14)

Use the literal ideal Möbius coefficient: squareful ideals give zero. This is not the ordinary integer coefficient transplanted by notation.

All needed analytic facts in Re s>1/2 follow from an elementary fixed-lattice argument. The triangular Eisenstein lattice has covering radius <1 after norm normalization, giving the Euclidean division algorithm and hence every ideal is principal. There are six units. The weight psi((alpha)), with its conductor zeros, is a bounded periodic function of alpha modulo f, invariant under units. A nonprincipal character has mean zero over the finite residue group; the principal character has its actual positive coprimality mean. Decompose the norm disk N(alpha)<=X into fixed f-lattice cells. Complete cells contribute the appropriate mean; only O_f(sqrt X+1) boundary cells remain. Dividing by6 gives

    sum_(N(a)<=X) psi(a) = c_psi X+O_f(sqrt X+1),         (W39.15)

where c_psi=0 for nonprincipal psi. The zero lattice vector is excluded and changes only O(1). In particular the total ideal count is O(X). Abel summation of W39.15 gives L(s,psi) meromorphic for Re s>1/2, with only the principal simple pole at1, and a polynomial upper bound on every closed strip inside that domain after regularizing the pole. The Euler product on Re s>1 is nonzero. All constants here depend on the fixed conductor; no uniform moving-conductor estimate follows.

Thus the proof A1--A4 applies word for word for any fixed gamma>1/2, choosing every replenishment disk inside Re s>1/2. The disk radius in A3 can be shortened if necessary, or use h>gamma>1/2 directly. Ideal counting supplies W39.2; ideal Euler inversion supplies W39.9; the natural conductor zeros and finite omitted factors remain in every identity.

**Theorem W39-H.** For EACH fixed member of exactly the finite-order, trivial-infinite-type Eisenstein Hecke family, W39.13 with W39.14 in place of F and gamma>1/2 implies zero exclusion Re s>gamma and the full all-scale Gaussian bound. Constants and thresholds may depend on that member. An assertion for every member requires W39.13 separately for every member, or an independently proved family-uniform hypothesis. Angular/infinite-order characters are outside this theorem. This covers the proposed near,1/6 and1/4 targets at the level of a quantitative conditional return.

The family identification agrees with [restricted mathematical source] opening statement. The older I-HECKE package in [restricted mathematical source] is not used to assume a better reciprocal bound: W39.15 and the disk argument establish the particular analytic prerequisites used here.

### A6. A literal f3 corollary for the current arithmetic target

The current source has f3(p^k)=-1 for p!=3 and k>=1, while f3(3^k)=1. Thus on Re s>1 its exact series is

    sum_n f3(n)n^(-s) = B(s)/zeta(s),
    B(s)=(1-2^(1-s)) H(s),
    H(s)=(1-2^(-s))^(-2)(1-3^(-s))^(-2)
         *product_(p>=5) (1-2p^(-s))/(1-p^(-s))^2.       (W39.16)

The p>=5 factors start in degree2; both H and 1/H converge absolutely and are bounded on every closed half-plane Re s>=b>1/2. The latter nonvanishing uses 2/sqrt5<1. The p=2,3 factors are separate. B has its explicitly retained zeros on Re s=1 and none in1/2<Re s<1. This is exactly the G28 multiplier of current-proof, not a new coefficient family.

If the fixed Gaussian F3(z)=sum_n f3(n)g_tau(log n-z) satisfies the small-set hypothesis W39.13 for 1/2<gamma<1, its Mellin identity excludes zeta zeros in gamma<Re s<1; the standard zero-free region Re s>=1 supplies the right edge, as in the retained G2 return. Replenishment uses W39.11 for1/zeta and the bounded actual B multiplier. Therefore A4 proves the same all-scale exponent gamma for F3. Its square moment on each dyadic x shell follows immediately; the existing G28--G31 return then applies with all f3 prime powers and the full signed off-diagonal sum intact.

This supplies the explicit alternative **OPEN-F3-VALLEY(gamma,kappa)**: establish W39.13 for the complete f3 field in EVERY unit logarithmic interval, for any fixed kappa<1/2. It is equivalent, with epsilon buffers, to the all-scale Gaussian exponent and hence to the current moment target at gamma>1/2. No estimate for a selected coefficient mask, a positive subblock or a density-one collection of intervals supplies this hypothesis.

### A7. Relation to earlier objections and exact remaining gate

W01 card12 and W21-T28 proposed thick observation sets. R21.27 constructed a smooth bump train with a genuine Mellin pole and good sets of fixed measure; that function is not entire of Gaussian growth. W39.7 is the missing quantitative analyticity input, not a contradiction to that result. W38-18/R38 section4 gives a bounded-integer-coefficient Gaussian with a larger exponent on sparse complete shells. Its kth positive block has log n in [v_k,v_k+log2]; throughout |u-v_k|<=2 every such term is at least g_tau(3), so its M_k terms give a positive multiple of exp(beta v_k). That neighborhood contains a whole integer unit interval and therefore fails W39.13 when gamma<beta. We require small sets INSIDE every interval, not a density-one set of wholly good intervals. The polynomial-density bootstrap additionally uses the actual meromorphic L-function, which that counterexample does not supply.

The novelty claimed is the proved local-measure exponent formula and its meromorphic replenishment/iteration, including the literal fixed-Hecke and f3 returns. It is novelty in the inspected project record, not a literature-priority assertion. A theorem estimating the actual sets E_j at a new gamma is still entirely open. No arithmetical reason for W39.13 has been proved in this batch.
