## 1. New mathematics and exact remaining targets



GC removes a comparison prerequisite, not the primitive-cell estimate or same-shell complement cost. At p2,3, K_p=(1-z)^2,H_p=(1-z)^-2; at p>=5, K_p=(1-z)^2/(1-2z),H_p=(1-2z)/(1-z)^2. Excluding3 is necessary for the >1/2 absolute threshold. Weighted shell Minkowski pays Gaussian left tails and uses the correct cutoff at each scale.

For OPEN-F3, the exact shell kernel is K_X(m,n)=integral_X^(2X)g_tau(log(m/x))g_tau(log(n/x))dx/x. Its true diagonal is O(X). Required off-diagonal bound is ONE-SIDED sum_(m!=n)f_3(m)f_3(n)K_X(m,n)<=C X^(2gamma+epsilon), all large dyads/every epsilon, gamma>=1/2. No absolute value inside that sum, random-sign premise, sign deletion or favorable subfamily. The norm then returns c=1-gamma. To exceed the newly controller-accepted c_G now requires gamma<.8748866; old frozen first-gain threshold was1-c0=.874886647039964130944614... . Convenient gamma=.87449/c=.12551 and higher ceilings5/6 or3/4 remain CONDITIONAL.

At a=.75, coarse moment.2498 and target.24898 remain the frozen comparison; old first-gain frontier approaches.24977329407992826... with positive buffer. PR15 does not supply the Gaussian target. No measured coverage fraction follows from tail or kernel-sector counts.

## 2. Useful failures and exact reopening conditions

| Tested move | Exact failure, preserved scope | Coherent reopening |

The reason for the last term is worth retaining. For a cofactor dyad Nm~U^y with 0<=y<=lambda+o(1), the inverse length lies between t and t+lambda-y. The inverse squared norm has exponent 1/6+(5/6-delta)(t+lambda-y). The Hilbert triangle over m contributes (1-delta)y, leaving its largest combined value at y=lambda. This gives S11. Triangle followed by Cauchy--Schwarz proves exactly this norm statement. The different shifts in the two geometric sums do not permit moving the two separate suprema inside a single shell supremum.

For d0=(D2,D3), d1=(-D3,D2), h1=R and h2=(-w3E3^+,w2E2^-), multiplication of the commuting operators gives d1d0=0, h1d0=I, d0h1+h2d1=I and d1h2=I. The literal B3 coefficients are correct. If n=2^k m, m odd, D2F has chi(n)f(m) times1,-3,1,1,... at k=0,1,2,... . D3F has chi(n)mu(rad(n)), on ALL integers and powers. Mellin numerators are respectively N2^2J and N2N3J. In a3<Re(s)<1 they have no zero, but the half-plane bridge is most cleanly made by reconstructing M. Every same-channel signed cross term remains in its complete square; the joint energy does not authorize deleting an arithmetic sector.

The author's B4 is an all-large-dyadic joint energy bound with exponent2gamma+epsilon, a3<gamma<.874861. It bounds the separate buffered norms, hence reconstructs F. Conversely two finite dilations give B4 from F. Thus B4 is an equivalent full arithmetic target. The positive buffers pay the all-scale norm and, when invoked, global weighted integrability. This exponent conclusion survives the constant qualification.

On global L2(x^-2sigma dx/x), the row multiplier of R is (w2/m2,w3/m3), m_p=1-2chi(p)p^(-sigma-it). Its norm is at most A^-1/2, attained in the supremum as both phases approach their minimizing values. The continuous orbit with frequencies log2,log3 is dense because their ratio is irrational. The two sums give RY=C_R x^sigma. Hence the upper bound is sharp. The mixed stable directions, unequal critical lines and explicit all-prime D3F channel are a valid scoped adaptation; abstract Koszul exactness is not new arithmetic.

statement:
# [private research revision]: quadratic classes in the cubic square-row moment

**Status: independently accepted relative to the stated inherited inputs.**
Derived by `c20_cubic`; independently reviewed by `c20_triple_cayley`. The new
estimate below uses the existing fixed-datum UM theorem, not Guo's
unproved short-row hypothesis. It pays an explicitly selected part of
the actual Poisson-transformed C--C form. It does not pay the dominant
moving squarefree dual class or the whole signed remainder. No change
to `b0 = .874886647039964131...` or `c0` is claimed.

## 1. Inputs, ownership and the precise gain

Write `M` for [the merged manuscript](../../zeta_zero_free_validated_merged.md),
`CP` for [cubic packets](../cubic-packets.md), and use the
normalizations of [BC](../[private research revision]/cubic-mobius-core-moment.md),
[DQ](../[private research revision]/cubic-dual-classes.md), and
[PS](../[private research revision]/parameter-and-square-row-interfaces.md).
Ideal columns occur once through good primary generators. Element rows
retain every unit and every fixed-prime valuation. All characters have
their original zero extensions.

The inputs are M (B0.3), **UM**, and its common-scale consequence (B0.8);
the original coefficient and Poisson identities CP21--CP25; and the
original rapid two-endpoint column profile `W0` and Schwartz row kernel
`Rhat`. Fixed finite ray components have the scope already separated in
BC section 8. In particular, the core twists used here have finite
order. The angular cube factor remains outside the core moment.
This is a deduction relative to those inherited inputs. No uniform
Hecke moment in a new family is postulated. **I-HECKE is used only for
the numerical comparison in section 6, not for the new estimate.**

Fix `0<gamma<1`, `0<delta<1-gamma`, a fixed finite collection
`mathscr D` of quadratic square classes, and

\[
1\le K\le D^{1-\delta},\qquad
\Lambda^3=\frac{D^{1-\delta}}{\max(K,D^\gamma)}.
\tag{SR1}
\]

A class is represented by a fixed element `d`, squarefree away from
the fixed primes, with fixed unit and fixed-prime parity choices.
It consists of the nonzero rows `n=d a^2`, with all allowed `a`.
There is **no** imposed `(d,a)=1`. One may also retain any subset of
these rows, such as the cube-free ones.

Let `Q_CC[mathscr D,Lambda;>D^gamma]` mean the exact C--C Poisson
expression restricted to

* the original squarefree cores `q_c,q_e>D^gamma`;
* the original outside cube labels `q_B,q_E<=Lambda`;
* after the C--C forced frequency is written `h=R0 n` as in CP23--CP25,
  the rows `n` in these fixed quadratic classes.

Every total-column coprimality condition is retained. The independently accepted
estimate is

\[
\boxed{
 |Q_{CC}[\mathscr D,\Lambda;>D^\gamma]|
 \ll_{\mathscr D,\delta,\gamma,\epsilon,\mathrm{orig}}
 D^{2+\epsilon}.}
\tag{SR2}
\]

The same proof permits additional row-independent frozen deletion
ideals of polynomial norm, with subpower costs, and the prescribed
fixed profile/height parameters with a common polynomial height cost.
It does not permit arbitrary row-dependent coefficients or growing
families of square-class representatives in the implied constant.

This is a genuine infinite dual-row subfamily: for a fixed `d`, its
rows of norm at most H number `O_d(H^(1/2))`. On the cube-free part
`n=d a^2`, with `a` squarefree and coprime to fixed `d`, the moving
good conductor has size comparable to `sqrt(q_d H)`. Thus the estimate
is not obtained by freezing the full dual conductor.

## 2. Moving deletion ideals can be removed without moving the datum

Fix the full zero-extended presentation of a finite-order character
`omega`, and write

\[
\begin{split}
A_u^R(X;F)
 =\sum_{(m,R)=1}\mu(m)\omega(m)\chi_m(u)F(q_m/X),\\
M_u^R(X;F)=X^{-1/2}A_u^R(X;F).
\end{split}
\]

The underlying fixed S restriction is understood. For every finite
ideal R, the exact inverse deletion identity is

\[
\boxed{
\begin{split}
A_u^R(X;F)
 &=\sum_{\operatorname{rad}(a)\mid R}
       \omega(a)\chi_a(u)A_u(X/q_a;F),\\
M_u^R(X;F)
 &=\sum_{\operatorname{rad}(a)\mid R}
       \frac{\omega(a)\chi_a(u)}{\sqrt{q_a}}
           M_u(X/q_a;F).
\end{split}}
\tag{SR3}
\]

Here `a` ranges over all powers supported on R, not just its squarefree
divisors. For a prime dividing R the coefficient identity is
`sum_{j=0}^v mu(p^(v-j))=0` for `v>=1`; outside R it is the original
Möbius coefficient. Multiplicativity, including zeros, proves SR3.
In particular no `(a,u)=1` hypothesis is added. For compact annular F
only finitely many `a` occur; for the original rapid profile the double
sum converges absolutely, by its large-argument bounds.

For every fixed `epsilon>0`,

\[
\sum_{\operatorname{rad}(a)\mid R}q_a^{-1/2}
 =\prod_{p\mid R}(1-q_p^{-1/2})^{-1}
 \ll_\epsilon q_R^\epsilon.
\tag{SR4}
\]

Indeed each sufficiently large-prime factor has logarithm at most
`epsilon log q_p`; the finitely many smaller primes contribute a
constant. No conductor-dependent reciprocal L-function is invoked.

Apply Minkowski in the positive row Hilbert space to SR3. The phases
have modulus at most one. M (B0.8), or the same Sobolev argument for
the fixed common profile, then gives

\[
\sum_{u\ne0}\Omega(q_u/H)|M_u^R(X;F)|^2
 \ll H(HXq_R)^\epsilon\mathcal S(F)^2,
 \qquad H\ge X^{1+\vartheta},
\tag{SR5}
\]

for fixed `vartheta>0` and a fixed nonnegative rapid row majorant
`Omega`. The statement is uniform in R. The fixed datum remains
`omega,S`; R has not been absorbed into it. Dyadic row majorization
uses UM inside a fixed larger polynomial range. Above that range,
absolute row and column counting, with an arbitrarily high Schwartz
power, pays the rest of the infinite row tail. Subunit column
scales are bounded directly. Smooth height twists cost a fixed power
of the height, as in M (B0.3), rather than a conductor-dependent order.

We shall use SR5 with the stronger slack `H>=X D^delta`, `X<=D`.
This also allows the original noncompact two-endpoint profiles. For
detail, split them into fixed-annulus profiles. Column annuli up to
`D^(delta/4) X` still satisfy UM with a smaller fixed positive margin
(one can use `vartheta<delta/8`). Higher annuli have arbitrarily small
mass by the original rapid endpoint bounds: absolute column counting
and the `O(H)` row-majorant mass suffice. The same argument applies to
each required Euler derivative. There is no change of the original
Mellin root. All profile constants used here are finite seminorm and
endpoint constants of the prescribed original family.

## 3. A fixed quadratic class changes the actual row index

PS15 gives the actual dual core character

\[
\psi_n(c)=\nu(c)\overline{\chi_c(n^2)}.
\]

Since sextic characters are zero-extended, the following identity is
valid also at every nonunit:

\[
\boxed{
 n=d a^2\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \overline{\chi_c(n^2)}
   =\chi_c(n)\rho_d(c),\qquad
 \rho_d(c)=\chi_c(d)^3.}
\tag{SR6}
\]

On units, `bar chi(n^2)=chi(n)^4=chi(n)chi(n)^3`, and
`chi(d a^2)^3=chi(d)^3 chi(a)^6`. The extra sixth-power factor is
`1_(c,a)=1`, already enforced by `chi_c(n)`. If a prime divides both
c and n, both sides vanish. This proves the assertion without an
unjustified deletion of natural zeros or an assumption `(d,a)=1`.

For fixed d, cubic/sextic reciprocity and the fixed ray separation make
`rho_d` a fixed finite-order quadratic Hecke character with its full
zero-extended presentation. Primes dividing fixed d may be added to
the fixed datum because the original row character already vanishes
there. This does not apply to a d that grows with the scales.

Therefore, on this class, the centrally normalized original cubic
Möbius polynomial is **exactly** the sextic polynomial with fixed
twist `nu rho_d` and row `u=n`. Its row norm is H, not H squared.
This is a different identity from retaining the original fixed twist
and writing `u=n^2`, which has norm H squared as in PS15--PS18.

For fixed d, SR5 consequently yields

\[
\boxed{
 \sum_{\substack{n\ne0\\n\in[d]_2}}
 \Omega(q_n/H)
 \left|X^{-1/2}\sum_{(c,R)=1}
    \mu(c)\psi_n(c)F(q_c/X)\right|^2
 \ll_{d,\nu,\epsilon} H(HXq_R)^\epsilon\mathcal S(F)^2.}
\tag{SR7}
\]

Positive enlargement now runs over all sextic rows **of norm H**
with the single fixed twist `nu rho_d`. Rows sharing primes with d,
a, R, or the core retain their original zeros. A finite collection
of classes and all six unit choices cost only a fixed constant.

## 4. The complete common-gcd projector and both opposite masks

For fixed component characters `nu_1,nu_2`, define
`psi_{j,n}(c)=nu_j(c) bar chi_c(n^2)` and, for common profiles F,G,

\[
\begin{split}
\mathcal P_n(C,E;R_1,R_2)
 =\sum_{\substack{c,e\ {\rm sf}\\(c,e)=1\\
                    (c,R_1)=(e,R_2)=1}}
 \mu(c)\mu(e)\psi_{1,n}(c)\overline{\psi_{2,n}(e)}
 \sqrt{q_cq_e}\,F(q_c/C)G(q_e/E).
\end{split}
\tag{SR8}
\]

F and G are allowed to be different complex profiles. In particular
this is not declared to be a positive quadratic form. The moment
estimate is

\[
\boxed{
 \left|\sum_{n\in[d]_2}w_n\mathcal P_n(C,E;R_1,R_2)\right|
 \ll HCE(HCEq_{R_1}q_{R_2})^\epsilon\mathcal S(F)\mathcal S(G),}
\tag{SR9}
\]

provided `|w_n|<=Omega(q_n/H)` and
`H>=max(C,E)D^delta`, with `1<=C,E<=D`. Polynomial height costs
are understood. The weight may retain any additional row-only mask.

To prove it, insert the **whole** projector
`1_(c,e)=1 = sum_{g|c,e} mu(g)` before Cauchy--Schwarz, and set
`c=gm,e=gk`. The residual masks are exactly
`(m,gR_1)=(k,gR_2)=1`, with `(g,R_1R_2)=1` outside. The core
Möbius factors give `mu(m)mu(k)`, while the projector leaves `mu(g)`.
The row factor at g is

`nu_1(g) bar nu_2(g) |bar chi_g(n^2)|^2`.

It retains `1_(g,n)=1`. On the fixed class its expression via SR6
is the same factor. No missing conductor or support condition is
restored by hand later.

Put `F_1(x)=sqrt(x)F(x)`, and take the conjugate of the second
profile when writing its normalized polynomial. The exact norm
factor in this projector term is

\[
\frac{CE}{q_g}
 M^{gR_1}_{1,n}(C/q_g;F_1)
 \overline{M^{gR_2}_{2,n}(E/q_g;\overline{\sqrt{x}G(x)})}.
\tag{SR10}
\]

This conjugation preserves the displayed G, and so also preserves
the original same-complex-z product if the profiles have previously
been Mellin-separated. It does not replace such a product by a
single absolute square.

Apply Cauchy--Schwarz in n and SR7 separately to these two factors.
Both masks may move with g, at the subpower cost proved in SR3--SR5.
The g sum is harmonic, not a new power:

\[
 \sum_gq_g^{-1+O(\epsilon)}
     \min(1,(C/q_g)^A)\min(1,(E/q_g)^A)
 \ll_{A,\epsilon}(CE)^\epsilon.
\tag{SR11}
\]

For subunit residual scales the endpoint factors follow directly
from rapid decay. Decrease all preliminary epsilons before summing.
This proves SR9 and prices the entire signed projector. It is not a
statement about an original physical sector with a large common gcd.

## 5. Insert the original C--C coefficient and sum the outside cubes

The actual source is

`C_k(c B^3)=beta(c) theta_c(k) xi(B) q_B`.

There is no `(B,k)` mask. Total-column coprimality is precisely
`(c,e)=(c,E)=(e,B)=(B,E)=1`; overlaps `(c,B)>1` and `(e,E)>1`
are allowed. Here B,E are the outside cube labels; the symbol
`E_*` below is a core scale, to avoid confusing them.

For the whole C--C part, CP23 has
`E(h)=mu(c)mu(e) q_R0 1_(R0|h)`. In CP24--CP25 set `h=R0 n`.
The factor q_R0 cancels its normalization, and
`eta(R0) bar eta(R0 n)=bar eta(n)` on its original support.
Consequently the exact C--C prefactor and kernel, in CP's normalization,
are

\[
\begin{split}
\frac{K(q_Bq_E)^4}{D^2}\xi(B)\overline{\xi(E)}
\sum_{n\ne0}\widehat R\!\left(\frac{K(q_Bq_E)^3q_n}{D^2}\right)
\sum_{\substack{c,e\ {\rm sf}\ (c,e)=1\\(c,E)=(e,B)=1}}
 &\sqrt{q_cq_e}\,\mu(c)\mu(e)\psi_n(c)\overline{\psi_n(e)}\\
 &\cdot\overline{W_0(q_cq_B^3/D)}W_0(q_eq_E^3/D).
\end{split}
\tag{SR12}
\]

The original nonunit-core restriction and finite unit/ray projectors
are understood. For estimates, the latter separate into their
prescribed finite fixed-character families and bounded row selectors.
All element rows are retained. The transformed zero row is absent
because the original coprime nonunit cores give a nonprincipal
character. We do not apply the nonprincipal identity to an added
principal unit pair.

For fixed B,E set

\[
 C_* =D/q_B^3,\qquad E_*=D/q_E^3,\qquad
 H=\frac{D^2}{K(q_Bq_E)^3}=\frac{C_*E_*}{K}.
\tag{SR13}
\]

The outside prefactor in SR12 is exactly `q_B q_E/H`. The opposite
deletions in SR9 are `R_1=E,R_2=B`. They do not introduce either
forbidden own-column exclusion. The original angular factors have
modulus one and may now be bounded in absolute value; no moving
angular L-function is used.

By SR1,

\[
\min(C_*,E_*)\ge D^\delta\max(K,D^\gamma),\qquad
\frac{H}{\max(C_*,E_*)}
 =\frac{\min(C_*,E_*)}{K}\ge D^\delta.
\tag{SR14}
\]

Thus SR9 applies with the original profiles, using a rapid positive
majorant for `|Rhat|`, with all row tails included. It pays this cube
pair by

\[
 \frac{q_Bq_E}{H}\,H C_*E_*D^\epsilon
 =\frac{D^{2+\epsilon}}{(q_Bq_E)^2}.
\tag{SR15}
\]

The complete sum over `q_B,q_E<=Lambda`, with `(B,E)=1` still in
place before positive bounds, is affordable since
`sum_B q_B^(-2)<infinity`. This proves the bound for the full
transformed core sums.

Here is the justification for the sharp original cutoff
`q_c,q_e>D^gamma`. SR14 implies that the removed low-core profiles
have argument at most `D^(-delta)`. Every required endpoint bound is
available for the *original* W0. For example, for each A,

\[
 \sum_{q_c\le D^\gamma}\sqrt{q_c}
       |W_0(q_c/C_*)|
 \ll_A D^{3\gamma/2-A\delta}.
\tag{SR16}
\]

The other absolute core sum is `O(D^(3/2))`. The row-majorant mass
is `O(H)`, cancelling the `H^(-1)` in the physical prefactor; and
`sum_{q_B,q_E<=Lambda}q_Bq_E << Lambda^4 <= D^(4/3)`.
Choose A after the desired error exponent and fixed delta. The
removed terms, including any algebraically added unit core, are
`O(D^(-N))` for any fixed N. Both-low terms are handled in the same
way. This is an estimate of the already transformed expression,
not a functional equation asserted for a principal row. It establishes
SR2 with the actual sharp core cutoff. No sharp common-profile
moment is being assumed. Large core and cube tails inside the stated
sector retain W0's rapid bounds; the sector does not include cube
labels exceeding Lambda.

## 6. Size of the new payment and the primitive-row obstruction

At `gamma=1/4`, `K=D^.87653`, and the fixed choice `delta=.02`,

\[
 \Lambda=D^{.03449},\qquad
 \min(C_*,E_*)\ge D^{.89653}.
\tag{SR17}
\]

This is a part of the double-large-core C--C range well beyond BC's
small-core band. It includes both ordered columns, moving outside
cubes and their opposite deletions, the full common-gcd projector,
and every row in each chosen quadratic class. Even the bare cube
pair `B=E=1` illustrates a power improvement: separate I-HECKE
Möbius bounds, with `b>b0`, and the `O(H^(1/2))` class count give
only `D^(2b+epsilon) sqrt(K)`. Its limiting exponent at the displayed
K is `2.188038294079928...`; SR2 gives `2+epsilon`. This comparison
is solely an upper-bound comparison, not a lower bound for that
class's actual sum.

The result does **not** extend by declaring d to be a moving datum.
For a squarefree dual row n, its quadratic square class has
representative `d=n`. At a good prime p dividing n, the quotient
needed to replace `bar chi_c(n^2)` by `chi_c(n)` is the ramified
quadratic character `chi_c(p)^3`. A fixed finite family of twists
unramified at p cannot provide it. On local units such twists are
trivial on inertia, while this quotient has order two. Deletion
masks are also identically one on these units. Thus the exact inverse
deletion identity does not turn a moving ramified quadratic twist
into a fixed datum. This is a local obstruction to the proposed
**freeze-the-conductor and use the short-row moment** shortcut.

There is a second, quantitative obstruction even if one grants
uniform constants for every `nu rho_d`. Separate estimates

\[
 \sum_{u\asymp H}|M_{\nu\rho_d,u}(D)|^2\ll H
 \quad\hbox{for each }d
\]

alone bound the moving diagonal `u=d`, `q_d~H`, only by `H^2`.
An array `M_{d,u}=sqrt(H) 1_(u=d)` satisfies every such separate
estimate and saturates that diagonal bound. This logical example
is not asserted to be a Möbius counterexample; it proves that the
separate moment inequalities, even uniformly stated, do not imply
the desired diagonal estimate. At the balanced physical
normalization `D^2/H`, this shortcut costs `D^2 H`.

The exact remaining primitive-row target is still a joint diagonal
moment, with the normalized columns, original masks and projector
described above:

\[
\boxed{
 \sum_{\substack{q_n\asymp H\\n\ {\rm squarefree}}}
 \left|D^{-1/2}\sum_{(c,R)=1}\mu(c)\nu(c)
       \rho_n(c)\chi_c(n)F(q_c/D)\right|^2
 \ll T^A H(DHq_R)^\epsilon,\qquad H=D^2/K.}
\tag{SR18}
\]

One must keep the full projector when using this as a covariance
input. A quadratic large sieve cannot simply be applied to
`rho_n(c)`: its accompanying factor `chi_c(n)` also depends on n,
and their product is exactly the original cubic character. Guo's
fixed-datum short-row assertion is unproved in any event; the new
theorem above does not use it. At the present physical balanced
length H>D, ordinary inherited UM already suffices for the fixed
classes, whereas the moving diagonal is a different estimate.

The projection in SR2 is made in the **actual C--C Poisson formula**.
It is not an identification with a piece of II. In particular, no
frequency in the whole II subtraction is removed, no fixed-class
residue is identified with II, and no positivity of the signed
kernel is assumed. Subtracting the paid SR2 contribution leaves
the remaining double-large-core C--C Poisson rows and outside
cubes, **minus the original whole II**. The large primitive class
of DQ12 remains in that remainder.

## Source and review anchors

* M, B0.1 notation and (B0.3): zero extensions, fixed finite-order
  twists, common norm profiles and polynomial height dependence;
  UM immediately following (B0.3), and (B0.8) for common scales.
* CP21--CP25: original completed coefficient, exact total-column
  masks, forced full-period C--C frequency and its single product
  kernel. SR12 is the C--C specialization of these formulas.
* BC, input scope and sections 5--8: finite core twists, original
  fixed component families and the complete common-core projector.
  This packet uses SR3 rather than absorbing a deletion into S.
* PS15--PS18: the unchanged fixed-twist representation uses row
  `u=n^2`; SR6 explains precisely when a different *fixed* twist
  permits row `u=n` instead. The two statements do not conflict.
* DQ9 and DQ12: compulsory continuation addbacks and the unresolved
  primitive band. None of those addbacks is paid by relabeling SR2.

Independent review accepted SR3's all-power convolution, SR6 at shared
primes, the exact `CE/q_g` in SR10, the cancellation of R0 and all norm
factors in SR12--SR15, and SR16's sharp-cutoff error. The unchanged
reviewed source and independent review are retained under
`[restricted provenance path] mathematical source]`; the promotion receipt binds their
hashes to this canonical record. SR18 remains open.

statement:
## R7. Blind protected S19: full occupation clusters and a scoped absolute-expansion obstruction

The seed proposes prime-coincidence clusters in an actual source correlation. Here is an explicit ordinary-character realization retaining every valuation zero. Let n be uniform on {1,...,N}. For every prime p<=N put c_p=chi(p), including c_p=0 at ramification, and

    U_p(n)=-(1+c_p)1_(p|n)+c_p 1_(p^2|n).

Then 1+U_p equals 1 at valuation zero, -c_p at valuation one, and zero at every valuation at least two. Therefore

    product_(p<=N)(1+U_p(n))=mu(n)chi(n),
    Z_N(z)=E_N product_p(1+z_p U_p),
    Z_N(1)=M_chi(N)/N.                               (R7.1)

Ramified primes and squareful terms have not been dropped or modeled by independent Bernoulli variables. The true measure is finite counting with its cutoff correlations. For distinct p,r the first moments are exactly

    m_p=[-(1+c_p)floor(N/p)+c_p floor(N/p^2)]/N,
    m_pr=[(1+c_p)(1+c_r)floor(N/(pr))
          -(1+c_p)c_r floor(N/(pr^2))
          -c_p(1+c_r)floor(N/(p^2r))
          +c_p c_r floor(N/(p^2r^2))]/N.             (R7.2)

The distinct-prime connected coefficient in the formal log is m_pr-m_p m_r. The coefficient of z_p^2 is already -m_p^2/2, although Z_N is multiaffine. Thus summing only distinct-prime cumulants does **not** reconstruct the complete log. The exact formal expansion is

    log Z_N(z)=sum_(j>=1)(-1)^(j-1)/j
                     [sum_(A nonempty)m_A z_A]^j,
    m_A=E_N product_(p in A)U_p.

It includes overlapping/repeated clusters. Analytic convergence at the physical activity needs a separate theorem; formal equality is not that theorem.

The seed's two-copy version also has an exact full return. With independent uniform n,m, define

    V_p(n,m)=U_p(n)+conjugate(U_p(m))
                            +U_p(n)conjugate(U_p(m)).

Then E product_p(1+V_p)=|M_chi(N)/N|^2, including every diagonal and off-diagonal pair. Its single-prime moment is |1+m_p|^2-1. Its distinct two-prime connected coefficient is

    |1+m_p+m_r+m_pr|^2-|1+m_p|^2 |1+m_r|^2.          (R7.3)

This follows by expanding the complete four factors before taking expectations. A bound on the full two-copy contraction by N^(2gamma-2+epsilon) would give the original M bound; estimating a selected connected component or a different weighted correlation does not supply that complete estimate. No transfer to a Gaussian or native H kernel is asserted.

There is a useful actual-cutoff obstruction to the most direct absolute cluster route. Take q=1 and H_N={p:sqrt N<p<=N}; set all other activities to zero and all activities in H_N equal t. Each n<=N contains at most one such prime, and its square cannot divide n. Hence exactly

    Z_H(t)=1-B_N t,
    B_N=(2/N)sum_(sqrt N<p<=N)floor(N/p).             (R7.4)

The ordinary PNT, independently checked in [NIST DLMF 27.2.3](https://dlmf.nist.gov/27.2.E3), and partial summation give sum_(sqrt N<p<=N)1/p=log 2+o(1). The floor error divided by N is at most pi(N)/N=o(1). Thus B_N->2 log 2>1, and Z_H has a real zero t_N=1/B_N inside (0,1) for every sufficiently large N. At N=100 the exact values are B_N=27/25 and t_N=25/27.

Therefore log Z_H about t=0 has Taylor radius t_N<1, and the absolute cluster sum sum_(j>=1)B_N^j/j diverges at t=1. No absolutely convergent log power series on the full unit activity polydisc can describe this finite arithmetic marginal. The independent two-copy generating polynomial with separate activities is Z_H(t)conjugate(Z_H(t)), so the same zero survives that literal two-copy restriction. This does not automatically refute every collapsed or reorganized replica variable.

The obstruction concerns a **partial occupation marginal**, not the full Mertens sum. Conditioning on low primes, resumming the high-prime block before a signed estimate, or using another expansion domain remain open. They must retain the resulting complete signed cross term. It would be incorrect to promote the marginal zero, or its negative physical value 1-B_N, to an L-zero or a lower bound for |M|.

**Ancestry and usefulness:** G145 already has a high-prime clique zero blocking one naive cluster expansion, W51 has complete cutoff-fugacity roots, and W38/[restricted research revision] retain complete cumulant/occupation laws. The present audit is a source-specific version with the actual all-integer valuation mask, floor-weighted cofactors and an explicit two-copy return. It is not a new general cluster method or an arithmetic saving. [restricted research revision] G154 and [restricted research revision] G160 independently reinforce the need to keep cross-sector cancellation; they do not prove the proposed full cluster estimate.

The all-comparable finite-cutoff matching cut D2 is also correct; its architecture is broader than one cone, while its lower bound is weaker than the linear count already known for more restricted Morse matchings.

## R2. Complete source and the matching return

Fix an ordinary Dirichlet character chi modulo a FIXED q. Set a(n)=mu(n)chi(n), with squareful and ramified zeros literally retained, and M(x)=sum(n<=x)a(n). This is the rational squarefree source, not f3 and not an ideal coefficient system. Its absolute Dirichlet series is initially valid for Re(s)>1; the Euler inverse is exactly1/L(s,chi).

Suppose ONE global disjoint pairing of squarefree q-units satisfies a(u)=-a(v) and |u-v|<=C_chi min(u,v)^theta, with0<=theta<1. Suppose its unmatched count below x is O_(chi,epsilon)(x^(delta+epsilon)) for every epsilon>0. Constants, onsets and the pairing may depend on the fixed character. Finitely many exceptional pairs contribute a fixed bound.

A pair crossing x has distinct lower endpoint in [x-C_chi x^theta,x]; there are at most C_chi x^theta+1 such lower integers. Both-below pairs cancel exactly, not just in real part. Therefore

    |M(x)| <= C_chi x^theta + O_(chi,epsilon)(x^(delta+epsilon))+O_chi(1).

For gamma=max(theta,delta)>0, s integral_1^infinity M(x)x^(-s-1)dx and every complex derivative converge normally on Re(s)>gamma. On each compact choose epsilon smaller than its positive horizontal margin; logarithmic derivative factors are then summable. The function equals1/L initially on Re(s)>1. Meromorphic identity gives L F=1 throughout the connected half-plane. A regular zero of L is impossible because F is holomorphic there. A principal pole instead forces a reciprocal zero, which is allowed. This treats every fixed finite height and the actual imprimitive L, with no asserted uniform conductor/height growth. It imports no unproved reciprocal bound on the proposed new line.

For all characters modulo a fixed q, opposite mu signs and equal reduced residue suffice. The example6 and11 modulo5 has coefficients1 and-1 for EVERY character mod5. More generally mp and mrs work under the author's distinct-prime, squarefree/coprime and p=rs mod q conditions. The actual displacement m|p-rs| remains. A two-coordinate swap cannot reverse principal mu; a three-coordinate nondivisibility exchange can. These facts do not supply a complete pairing or control its leftovers.

At gamma=.87485 the conditional c=.12515 would improve c11 by10091/2500000000=.0000040364;5/6 and3/4 would return1/6 and1/4. These are unpaid conditional targets. Separate finite-cutoff matchings cannot be silently glued into the global pairing used above. The newer accepted [private research revision] G150 already retains a different complete future-partner displacement criterion, with G135 rank/summatory ancestry; M1-M3 is not a new analytic zero-return mechanism.

## R3. Universal complex toggles: correct, with the cube scope retained

For nonempty C in a finite unramified prime universe and w(S)=(-1)^|S|chi(product S), direct cancellation of common factors gives

    w(S xor C)/w(S)
      =(-1)^|C| product_(p in C)chi(p)
                    product_(p in S intersect C)chi(p)^(-2).

The ratio is-1 for EVERY cube state S exactly when every chi(p)^2=1 on C and (-1)^|C|product_C chi(p)=-1. Necessity follows from the empty state and one singleton at a time; sufficiency is immediate. There is no division by a ramified value: those primes are excluded from this unit cube and their natural zero remains in the global arithmetic source.

For the actual quartic character mod5 with chi(2)=i,chi(3)=-i,chi(11)=1, the toggle {2,3,11} sends1 to66 with opposite a, but sends2 to33 with the SAME coefficient-i. State-specific6<->11 is still valid. Thus a product-one checksum alone does not license the universal odd toggle. My exhaustive finite check covers all4^3 prime phase assignments, all seven nonempty toggles and all eight states:448 universal criteria agree.

The criterion is on the complete Boolean cube. A cutoff-restricted set of states may admit other local exchanges; failure on the full cube does not exclude them. The principal parity/row-space dichotomy is ordinary binary linear algebra, and the cutoff boundary is still unpaid. Credit the existing parity/Walsh/character-phase lineage. C2 is a useful explicit source constraint, not a claimed new coding theorem.

## R4. Short-edge isolation: accepted proof and exact reach

Let n be squarefree and m any distinct positive integer. Put g=gcd(n,m). The divisibility g|(n-m) gives g<=|n-m|. If |n-m|<=C min(n,m)^theta, then

    n/g >= n/(C min(n,m)^theta) >= C^(-1)n^(1-theta).

There is no missing factor for an incoming edge or an endpoint outside [X,2X]. For squarefree n, n/g is exactly the product of the primes of n not dividing m. If at most d such primes may be lost, and every prime of n is<=y, then n/g<=y^d. Hence n^(1-theta)>C y^d forbids EVERY such neighbor. This covers squareful or nonunit auxiliary integers because the restriction is imposed at the squarefree endpoint n irrespective of orientation. If that endpoint restriction were dropped for incoming edges, this proof would not apply.

Fix q,C,d,theta, and choose a FIXED integer k>d/(1-theta). Products of k distinct primes in (X^(1/k),(2X)^(1/k)] are squarefree, lie in(X,2X], and eventually avoid all fixed prime divisors of q. Their maximal prime y=(2X)^(1/k) satisfies

    n^(1-theta)/(C y^d)
       >= (C 2^(d/k))^(-1) X^(1-theta-d/k) -> infinity.

They are therefore isolated in the entire permitted graph for every sufficiently large X. This is a strict power comparison; equality k=d/(1-theta) gives no conclusion from this argument. The same assertion survives a bounded family of radii and subpower inflation of C after choosing a fixed positive exponent margin. It does not supply uniformity for unbounded k or growing d.

The prime input is only pi(t)~t/log t, independently checked in the official [NIST DLMF27.12](https://dlmf.nist.gov/27.12), equations4-5. At FIXED k it gives

    t_X ~ k(2^(1/k)-1) X^(1/k)/log X.

Unique factorization makes the vertex count exactly binomial(t_X,k), hence

    |V_X| ~ A_k X/(log X)^k,
    A_k=[k(2^(1/k)-1)]^k/k! >0.

Neither short-interval prime estimates nor character prime equidistribution are used. Fixed q is essential: the argument does not give an onset uniform in a conductor allowed to contain all the selected primes. The possibly tiny A_k and large onset affect constants, not the exponent-one absolute obstruction.

At every isolated vertex a=div F+r implies r(n)=a(n), for ANY complex edge flow whose divergence is defined. Since |a(n)|=1,

    sum_(X<n<=2X)|r(n)| >= |V_X|.

No disjointness, positivity, bound on edge coefficients or acyclicity is needed for this local conclusion. Iterated bounded short steps cannot start at an isolated vertex. For every delta<1, X/(log X)^k divided by X^delta tends to infinity, so the full absolute residual cannot have that power bound. To refute an every-epsilon exponent delta choose epsilon<(1-delta)/2.

The author's d=3 margins are correct: k24 at theta17497/20000 gives3/20000; k19 at5/6 gives1/114; k13 at3/4 gives1/52. At current gamma11, k24 still works with exact margin364909/2500000000. My additional exact check examines all344 short neighbors of four actual squarefree integers, including133 squareful ghost neighbors; none permits only one deleted prime under theta1/2,C1. This supports indexing and the optional-ghost scope, not the PNT asymptotic proof.

**Strongest objection, retained.** For principal chi the isolated k-prime layer has constant sign(-1)^k. This is a signed statement about that layer only. Other isolated layers and the rest of r can cancel it. C8 gives neither a lower bound for |sum r(n)| nor for |M(x)|. With nonreal chi even one fixed-k layer need not have coherent phase. Growing turnover, truly long edges, a different auxiliary transfer, or a direct signed estimate of the complete isolated complement remain eligible. No entire coding, coupling or multiscale family is rejected.

The record delta is this all-fixed-radius graph/complex-flow obstruction on actual integers, including its exact endpoint price. It refines U-PRIME-CHAIN/U-TRANSPORT and the coded/Walsh portfolio. It should not be renamed as an improved arithmetic exponent or a literature-priority claim.

## R5. Comparable matching cut: correct and separately limited

D1 is the existing exact prime split

    M_chi(X)=A_p(X)-chi(p)A_p(X/p)
            =B_p(X)+(1-chi(p))A_p(X/p),
    A_p(Y)=sum_(n<=Y,p not dividing n)mu(n)chi(n).

Squareful terms vanish and no character defect is dropped. Choosing chi(p)=1 removes the displayed interior term but supplies no estimate for B_p. G144 already retains this identity and its twist/gauge limitations.

Inside the finite squarefree q-unit set n<=X, a terminal prime p in(X/2,X] has exactly one distinct comparable vertex:1. It has no other divisor and no proper multiple within the cutoff. In any disjoint comparable-vertex pairing at most one terminal prime can be matched. Therefore the unmatched count is at least their number minus one. Character phase restrictions can only remove eligible pairs, so the bound survives them. For standard NONNEGATIVE fractional matching with vertex capacity1, the sum of the terminal primes' incident weights is at most the capacity of1; the same lower bound applies to residual mass. An unrestricted complex flow is not a fractional matching in that sense.

PNT gives terminal count~X/(2log X) for fixed q. No Morse acyclicity was used. The obstruction includes adaptive pivots and comparable pairs differing by several primes. It does not apply to arbitrary shared-vertex linear homotopies, noncomparable pairs, or partners beyond the finite cutoff. In particular it is not by itself a lower bound on the global future-partner cost of G150. The complete global M1 return and this finite graph statement must remain distinct.

Comparison with retained W59 evidence matters. The frozen W59 critic's S12 argument already bounds every acyclic single-prime Morse matching by homology, giving a LINEAR critical count; its source proof is independent review evidence pending root's integration at this intake. W57/G144 gives a linear bill for a specified cone. D2 is quantitatively weaker but applies without acyclicity and to arbitrary comparable pairs, so it is not wholly the same architecture. The unproved signed critical readout remains unaffected in all versions. My twelve exact terminal-neighborhood checks include q1/5/8/12 and three cutoffs, without rerunning the author's maximum-matching calculations.

## R6. Four selected first tests, with original source conventions

For native H freeze every finite component packet and both independent heights. The literal ideal coefficients are

    a(n)=alpha(n)eta(n)chi_n(lambda)^(-2)gamma_2(n),
    xi(g)=alpha(g)^3 eta(g)^3.

The field is Eisenstein, with original primary/fixed-ray/six-unit/bad-place data. Keep distinct long prime ideals of distinct rational norms and both strict-far orientations, equal-norm exclusions, every ordered short pair including equality, actual complex h((g,g')), rational gcd screen, both projectors1_(P,Rg)=1 and1_(P',Rg')=1, natural zeros, all original profiles and height factors. The joint kernel has chi_pi(h)^3 chi_pi'(h)^3 chi_pi(s)^2 chi_pi'(s')^4 b(pi)conjugate(b(pi'))zeta_CRT, unitary factor1/Q on its Q^2-point group. It is not a rational mu-chi kernel.

To fix the root/conjugation convention, put v_P=u1(P)/sqrt(q_P), w_P'=u2(P')/sqrt(q_P'), and define K by the literal scalar sum v_P K_PP' conjugate(w_P'). Then H=w*Tv with T=K^T, ||v||^2=Omega1, ||w||^2=Omega2. Root weights are accounted in v,w ONCE; all remaining source factors stay in T. Saying the packet retains rooted marks does not insert those roots a second time in T. This is the corrected G75 convention, read from the earlier independent source review.

The raw target is

    B0 sqrt(Omega1 Omega2),
    B0=G K0 [N+L+(NL)^(2/3)] P_orig.

K0 is the original row parameter, not a new kernel norm. Afterward apply N^(-1)G^(-2) exactly once. P_orig includes the original kernel/component/profile costs. Uniform packet bounds still need the original height integration, linear tails, all component interactions and other H branches; neither this review nor the author pays them anew.

**28 — invalid proposed source constraint, valid diagnosis.** The original mark arrays are independent. They do not satisfy u(pn)=-chi(p)u(n) merely because rational mu chi does. If two coordinates are actually allowed, assigning1 and0 violates that relation; if not, that putative coordinate relation provides no constraint there. This is an interface test, not a constructed numerical native-H counterexample. An upstream relation could matter after a proved full transport through the ideal source and its boundaries. **26 — scoped positive-MGF impossibility, valid.** The literal Hermitian dilation

    A_phi=[[0,e^(i phi)T],[e^(-i phi)T*,0]]

has eigenvalues plus/minus each nonzero singular value of T. Its realification is indefinite when T is nonzero. A positive probability MGF of a real linear auxiliary variable has positive semidefinite log Hessian at zero, equal to its covariance; a locally finite MGF has the required moments. It cannot equal exp(y^T B y) for this indefinite real B on a neighborhood of zero. This does not exclude nonlinear couplings or complex measures.

Diagonalizing B gives the exact complex Gaussian formula in H1. Absolute value inside that expectation replaces B by B_+; its ratio to the exact positive exponential is exp(y^T B_- y). The imaginary phase cost has not vanished. No phase lower bound or arithmetic saving is deduced from the synthetic two-dimensional example.

**25 — tensor torsion calculation, valid.** For Re(s)>0, a=1-chi(p)p^-s and b=1-chi(r)r^-s are nonzero. The based complex C->C^2->C has d2=(-b,a)^T and d1=(a,b). It is exact. Using boundaries a e0 and(-b,a) and the indicated lifts gives determinants a,-a,1; the alternating ratio is-1, so torsion is1 up to sign in either reciprocal convention. At p2,r3,s2 the desired ab is2/3. I independently checked the convention in [Hutchings2002, AppendixA](https://math.berkeley.edu/~hutching/pub/rt3/rt3.pdf), DefinitionA.1/PropositionA.2; the finite determinant derivation is explicit here. A direct sum can store the product, and the cutoff triangle has homology instead of the proposed acyclic torsion. These are scoped failures, not a theorem against every arithmetic torsion detector.

**30 — full cyclic compression, valid but largely standard.** The finite Hermitian Krylov span through dimensionD is invariant by Cayley-Hamilton; its orthogonal complement is invariant by adjointness. Hence QAP=PAQ=0 and the claimed Feshbach self-energy is zero on its resolvent domain. Full cyclicity can occur, but the author's determinant-18 example is synthetic and says nothing about actual native cyclic dimension. For a UNIT source line, the Schur resolvent is [z-a-b*(z-D)^(-1)b]^-1; coefficients1/z+a/z^2+(a^2+||b||^2)/z^3 preserve the source moment. For source(w,v), a=2Re(e^(i phi)H)/(||w||^2+||v||^2). For source(0,v), the second moment is||Tv||^2/||v||^2. The rescue is a full spectral/source estimate, not an automatic saving from compression.

## R7. Protected20: an exact Schur reduction must retain the completion

This is my independent development of the forced protected seed, not an author result. Apply it to the ACTUAL T in R6 after freezing packet, height pair and any proposed scale partition of its input coordinates. Write T=[T_R,T_E], v=(u,z), and let Pi be the orthogonal projection onto ran T_E in the output space. No assumption that that range is easy, small or character-neutral is made. Orthogonality gives the exact source identity

    ||Tv||^2 = ||(I-Pi)T_R u||^2
               +||Pi T_R u+T_E z||^2.                 (A20.1)

The first Gram matrix is the generalized Schur complement

    S=T_R*(I-Pi)T_R
     =A-B D^dagger B*,
    A=T_R*T_R, B=T_R*T_E, D=T_E*T_E.                   (A20.2)

To justify the singular case without a hidden inverse: ker D=ker T_E and B annihilates that kernel. Thus ran B* is contained in ran D, and T_E D^dagger T_E*=Pi. The identities follow from the finite singular-value decomposition; no arbitrary range condition is assumed away. S is positive semidefinite. In a true energy Gram matrix the fill-in satisfies0<=B D^dagger B*<=A; it cannot be treated as a free negative contribution making the full energy negative.

For a priced resolvent alternative put D_lambda=D+lambda I, lambda>0, and S_lambda=A-B D_lambda^-1 B*. Then exactly

    v*Gv = u*S_lambda u
       +(z+D_lambda^-1 B*u)*D_lambda(z+D_lambda^-1 B*u)
       -lambda||z||^2,       G=T*T.                   (A20.3)

G+diag(0,lambda I) is positive semidefinite, hence S_lambda>=0. Expansion verifies every cross term and the final subtraction. The inverse costs at most1/lambda, or the sharper actual spectral distance, only if that inverse representation is used; the projection formula itself has norm1 and does not inherently require an inverse blowup. Conversely, replacing the full completion by a small Schur term would be a false upper bound. A small S controls a conditional/minimized energy, while z is the original source coordinate, not a free minimizer.

The three-column algebra diagnostic

    T=[[1,1,1],[0,epsilon,-epsilon]], R={first column},
    E={second,third}, epsilon!=0

has ran T_E equal to the whole two-dimensional output and therefore S=0. With u1,z0, however, ||Tv||^2=1 and the completion is1. This is a synthetic obstruction to discarding a term, not a native-H lower bound. Four exact rational checks at epsilon1/5,lambda0 or1/7 verify(A20.3), including nonzero eliminated source coordinates. At lambda1/7 the retained Schur scalar is1/15; the remaining14/15 for that source is explicit.

**Complete native return.** A sufficient arithmetic statement for each literal packet is

    ||(I-Pi)T_R u||^2+||Pi T_R u+T_E z||^2
       <= B0^2 (||u||^2+||z||^2)                      (OPEN-SC)

for all actual admissible v, with the original uniformities and profile costs. Cauchy with w then gives |H|<=B0 sqrt(Omega1 Omega2), followed by the single physical factor and remaining original summations. More selective estimates may retain projections of w in the bilinear identity, but must price both projected source terms. Scale-dependent partitions change all these blocks and sources; no derivative, height or transition uniformity follows from pointwise algebra. Fill-in between originally disallowed edges is a derived sum through the original matrix, not permission to replace original masks by a new arithmetic graph.

OPEN-SC is essentially the full source-energy bill written after elimination, not a demonstrated weaker hypothesis. It may organize a source-specific estimate, but all principal complements remain. Prior U-VARIATIONAL/F08.N2, W51/G107 arbitrary-partition source injection and G75 complete-Gram contracts retain credit. The present explicit Gram/projection form resolves this seed's completion question; it is not a new general Schur method or a power gain. ## R8. Uniform27: weighted four-cycles, not an unpriced frustration count

This is my independent uniform audit. Use the same ACTUAL rectangular T and two separate mark spaces. Its Hermitian dilation is bipartite even if the two supports happen to use the same numerical labels. It has no triangular cycle. Identifying those two copies and inventing a triangle would change the bilinear source. Four-cycles are the first relevant loops in this representation.

For distinct input columns j,k let

    b_i=conjugate(T_ij)T_ik,  s_jk=sum_i |b_i|,
    eta_i=b_i/|b_i| for b_i!=0,
    psi_jk=sum_(i<l,b_i b_l!=0) |b_i||b_l||eta_i-eta_l|^2.

Each nonzero term uses four actual nonzero edges. An original masked-out or naturally zero entry contributes zero; no division at that zero occurs. Expansion gives the exact identity

    |(T*T)_jk|^2=s_jk^2-psi_jk.                       (A27.1)

Indeed the diagonal terms agree, and each pair's difference is2|b_i||b_l|(1-Re(eta_i conjugate(eta_l))). Its phase is the actual four-cycle product

    conjugate(T_ij)T_ik T_lj conjugate(T_lk)

divided by its modulus. It is invariant under transported row/column unitary gauges. The original source must be transported with that gauge; fixing it instead changes H. Every short-core interference already folded into each T entry is retained. Replacing T by separate positive cores before forming these b_i would be a different identity with a different cost.

G75's full Hermitian Gram row bound now reads

    ||T||^2 <= max_j [sum_i |T_ij|^2
                +sum_(k!=j) sqrt(s_jk^2-psi_jk)].       (A27.2)

All radicands are nonnegative by(A27.1). Thus bounding the entire right side by B0^2, uniformly with the source gates in R6, returns the raw H target by Cauchy and then its single physical factor. A Schatten alternative also includes the whole complement:

    ||T||^4 <= tr((T*T)^2)
       =sum_j (sum_i |T_ij|^2)^2
           +sum_(j!=k)(s_jk^2-psi_jk).                 (A27.3)

The diagonal term never disappears. These are exact native-source identities and sufficient returns, not evaluations of native cycle phases or an arithmetic lower bound. I have not constructed a numerical ideal packet with a specified nonzero cycle. The bounded Gaussian-integer matrices in checks.json verify conjugations and zero-edge conventions only; they are expressly synthetic. The triangle test, by contrast, is settled exactly by the source's bipartite structure.

For a2-by-2 unit-entry block the full Gram computation gives ||T||^2=2+2|cos(Phi/2)|. The prior G75 critic already records this formula, so it earns no new theorem credit here. A frustrated four-cycle can remove that block's off-diagonal Gram entry, but says nothing by itself about the weight on other edges or coherent components. Adding a disjoint large coherent block preserves the frustrated loop and makes that block dominate the norm; this is a generic diagnostic, not an alleged native embedding. Gauging a spanning tree removes its phases and leaves its coherent mass. W40's long rank-one cycle result also prevents promoting a fixed small-cycle loss to a macroscopic power loss.

To get a power saving through(A27.2), the actual weighted deficits must control EVERY significant Gram row together with the diagonal, at the required square-level exponent. A fixed positive fraction of a few cycle counts gives at most a constant comparison in that component. The complete arithmetic condition remains open. This is a precise realization/reparametrization of U-FLUX/G75's signed-Gram obligation, not a new independent cancellation estimate. Source-compatible loop summation, nonlocal cycles and genuinely mixed phase estimates remain eligible.

# W54 independent review: exact prediction target, paid source, unpaid arithmetic



## Verdict and calibration

Accept R11/X26/X28 as one coherent, source-specific conditional architecture. The literal ordinary-character pole correction, causal realization, full Gram/residual identities, source-tail continuation and finite-inner floor are valid at their stated ranges. The full prediction limit remains OPEN. Stable minimizer roots, well-conditioned positive Grams and exact finite interpolation do not prove it. The faster tail theorem pays formation, not the prediction error. R16/F04/X30 are valid scoped duplicate failures.

The independent addition below proves that, for this actual source, prediction convergence is **equivalent** to absence of L-zeros in the target half-plane. It also gives the exact limiting gap as a product over those zeros. This uses classical Hardy factorization and a proved absence of a singular-inner factor for the normalized character source; it is not an arithmetic estimate or a new general Hardy theorem. The protected X23 audit obtains the exact signed divisor Bellman certificate and proves a quadratic price for its specified diagonal terminal-majorant class. The uniform F06 audit rules out global strict finite-polynomial contraction for the raw principal L source, while preserving compact/strip and pole-normalized escapes.

Root-accepted written source-relative calibration is c11=312864909/2500000000=.1251459636, theta11=.8748540364. ## Evidence, chronology and sampling

Author report: 27,772 bytes, SHA256 `8088921479041a0aa802ed1905bd80a9bd73faed0914497d2d6a45d7c4674174`. Author freeze: `38e9c9f2c00c40b7213d0063ddf981e040477cb4d1b5b50cf70a8475f59a48f0`, timestamp 11:02:36.625906 UTC; author STOP/release/absence was supplied in the sole final wake.  All 30 seed cards and the maintained index were read before W54 outcomes or author selections. ## 1. Literal character source and causal realization

Fix one ordinary Dirichlet character chi modulo q with its natural zero extension. Let delta=1 for a principal character and 0 otherwise, r=delta*phi(q)/q, A(x)=sum_(n<=x)chi(n), and b(t)=A(exp t)-r exp t. Periodicity gives |b|<=q. For Re s>1,

    integral_0^infinity exp(-st)b(t)dt=L(s,chi)/s-r/(s-1).

The left side extends holomorphically to Re s>0. The report's source is exactly

    F_chi(s)=((s-1)/(s+1))^delta L(s,chi)/s.            (R1)

At a principal pole s=1 the removable value is r/2, nonzero. A nonprincipal character receives no artificial (s-1) factor. Thus all and only the natural L-zeros in Re s>0 survive, with multiplicity. Finite imprimitive factors and ramified zeros were not removed or filled in. The causal inverse Laplace source is

    f=b                                      nonprincipal,
    f(t)=r exp(-t)+b(t)-2 integral_0^t exp(-(t-u))b(u)du
                                             principal.      (R2)

It is bounded by C_q=1+3q. For principal chi, exact Abel summation gives

    f(log x)=2/x sum_(n<=x)n chi(n)-A(x)
            =A(x)-2/x integral_1^x A(y)dy.             (R3)

In particular q=1 gives m(m+1-x)/x for m=floor x, including the correct endpoint jumps. Positivity of that one source is not zero exclusion: a nonnegative delayed source exp(-bt)+C exp(-b(t-T))1_(t>=T) has transform (1+C exp(-sT))/(s+b), with zeros of positive real part when C>1. This is a toy counterexample to the inference, not an arithmetic lower bound.

For 0<gamma<1 set a=2-gamma and s(z)=gamma+a(1+z)/(1-z). The anchor is s(0)=2, where F0=F_chi(2) is nonzero by the absolutely convergent Euler product. Put f_gamma(t)=exp(-gamma t)f(t),

    h=sqrt(2a) exp(-a t)*f_gamma,
    Qv=v-2a exp(-a t)*v,
    ell0(t)=sqrt(2a)exp(-at).                          (R4)

The convolution is causal on [0,infinity). Q is an L2 isometry because its boundary Laplace multiplier is (it-a)/(it+a). Its full output tail is retained. The Cayley change of variables has measure a/[pi(a^2+t^2)]dt, exactly matching the sqrt(2a)/(w+a) Laplace factor. Hence, for every finite polynomial p,

    ||p(Q)h||_2^2=||p F||_H2^2,
    ||p(Q)h-F0 ell0||_2^2=||p F-F0||_H2^2,             (R5)

where F(z)=F_chi(s(z)). Also Q*ell0=0 and ||ell0||=1. These identities include all cross terms and complex phases. They are not comparisons of entrywise magnitudes. No uniformly equivalent positive metric P can have Q*PQ<=kappa P with kappa<1: iteration and Q's isometry contradict mI<=P<=MI. This is an unrestricted multiplier obstruction; it leaves source-specific output cancellation intact, as in W37 D03.

## 2. Exact finite prediction and every-height return

Let

    d_N=min_(p0=1,deg p<=N)||pF||_H2^2,
    Delta_N=d_N-|F0|^2=min||pF-F0||_H2^2.              (R6)

The constant coefficient makes the second equality exact. With
G_jk=integral conjugate(z^j F) z^k F dm, the norm is p*Gp; this fixes the complex conjugation convention. G is strictly positive definite and Toeplitz. The constrained minimum is 1/(G^-1)_00. Delta_N is nonnegative and decreases with N; positive definiteness alone gives no useful limiting gap.

If rho=beta+iT is any L-zero with beta>gamma, then w=(rho-gamma-a)/(rho-gamma+a) is a disk zero distinct from0. The residual has constant coefficient0 and takes value -F0 at w. The reproducing-kernel bound on zH2 yields

    Delta_N>=|F0|^2(1-|w|^2)/|w|^2
       =|F0|^2*4a(beta-gamma)/[(beta-gamma-a)^2+T^2].  (R7)

Therefore Delta_N->0 for EACH fixed ordinary chi at one common gamma excludes every zero at every finite height in Re s>gamma. There is no exchange of N-limit and a height supremum, and no uniform-in-q claim. The positive floor decays as T^-2, so a finite nonzero residual cannot alone certify an unbounded-height half-plane. No Hecke, angular or growing-conductor transfer is supplied.

### Independent completion: the criterion is exactly equivalent for this source

The classical inputs used here are canonical inner/outer factorization and cyclicity of outer functions. Their statements, including the singular-inner measure representation, are given in Garcia and Ross, *Model spaces: a survey*, Theorems2.12,2.16,2.20 and formula2.10. The following constrained minimization and source-specific boundary argument are proved here. [Primary source](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1312.5018).

For any nonzero F in H-infinity with F0!=0, write F=I O, I inner and O outer. The closure of polynomial multiples of F is I H2. Any limit g=Iu of admissible pF still has g(0)=F0, hence u(0)=F0/I(0)=O(0); I(0)!=0. Thus ||g||^2>=|O(0)|^2. Conversely, outer cyclicity gives polynomials q_k with Fq_k->I O(0). Continuity of evaluation at0 gives q_k(0)->1; rescaling q_k/q_k(0) provides admissible polynomials with the same limit. Monotonicity over all degrees therefore proves

    d_infinity=|O(0)|^2=|F0|^2/|I(0)|^2,
    Delta_infinity=|F0|^2(|I(0)|^-2-1).              (R8)

For an arbitrary bounded analytic source, absence of disk zeros is insufficient: a nonconstant singular inner factor still causes a gap. We now remove that possibility for (R1), rather than silently assuming it.

F extends holomorphically across every circle point zeta other than1: its finite Cayley image has real part gamma>0, where (R1) is holomorphic. The boundary zeros away from1 are isolated and form a countable set. In the factorization F=B S_nu O the outer factor is bounded by ||F||_infinity. The singular factor has nontangential limit0 at nu-almost every point, so boundedness of B and O implies F also has limit0 there. Analytic continuation consequently forces nu to be supported on those countably many boundary zeros together with1. It is thus purely atomic.

An atom of mass c>0 at zeta gives along z=r zeta

    |F(r zeta)|<=||F||_infinity exp[-c(1+r)/(1-r)].    (R9)

At zeta!=1 this contradicts the finite order of a zero of the continued nonzero analytic function. At zeta=1, put sigma=s(r). The literal Dirichlet series gives L(sigma,chi)->1 and therefore F_chi(sigma)~1/sigma. Since (1+r)/(1-r)=(sigma-gamma)/a, this too contradicts (R9). All atoms vanish, and nu=0. This proof uses the actual coefficient chi(1)=1 and the pole-corrected source, not a generic zero-free Hardy assumption.

Accordingly I is, up to a unimodular constant, exactly the Blaschke product over the L-zeros rho_j with Re rho_j>gamma, counted with multiplicity. Let w_j=z(rho_j). The bounded-source Blaschke condition and F0!=0 make the product below positive. Equations(R8)-(R9) give the exact census

    Delta_infinity=|F0|^2[product_j |w_j|^-2-1].       (R10)

The empty product is1. Each nonempty factor is>1. Thus Delta_N->0 if and only if this fixed L_chi has no zero in Re s>gamma. Zeros on the boundary are allowed and create no atom. This adds the converse missing from the cautious author formulation. It proves no convergence rate or arithmetic estimate: the complete prediction target has precisely the original zero-exclusion difficulty at this source. Applying it to every fixed chi at a common gamma gives exactly the corresponding ordinary-character family statement, with no growing-q uniformity inferred.

## 3. Complete source tails and finite computation

For 0<gamma<1, H0=sqrt(2a)C_q/(a-gamma) and K=1+2a/(a-gamma) give |Q^j h(t)|<=H0 K^j exp(-gamma t). The complete Gram tail after T is positive semidefinite and at most

    (N+1)H0^2 K^(2N) exp(-2gamma T)/(2gamma) I.

The residual tail is at most H0^2(sum_j |p_j|K^j)^2 exp(-2gamma T)/gamma +2|F0|^2 exp(-2aT). These pay both the source and anchor tails; omitting filtered future responses would be invalid.

A coherent source approximation ||h-h_tilde||<=tau instead gives, by the isometry of Q,

    ||p(Q)(h-h_tilde)||<=tau sum_j|p_j|.              (R11)

Each Gram-entry error is at most tau(||h||+||h_tilde||), and the operator error is at most N+1 times that quantity. This is an absolute operator-error bound, not a positive-semidefinite ordering between two source Grams. Even if h_tilde vanishes after T, its filtered Q^j outputs have full exponential-polynomial tails that must be retained.

The sharper actual-source continuation is valid for 1/2<gamma<1, with lambda=a-gamma=2-2gamma in(0,1). For q=1, writing u={x},

    f(log x)=1/2+B(x)-V(x)/x,
    B=1/2-u, V=u(1-u), primitive(B)=V/2.             (R12)

The primitive is bounded by1/8. Integration by parts, including its lower endpoint, and absolute integration of V/x give

    |integral_x^infinity y^(lambda-1)(f(log y)-1/2)dy|
       <=D_lambda x^(lambda-1),
    D_lambda=(2-lambda)/[4(1-lambda)].                (R13)

Consequently h(t)=A0 exp(-gamma t)+C exp(-at)+R(t), where A0=sqrt(2a)/(2lambda), |R(t)|<=sqrt(2a)D_lambda exp(-(gamma+1)t). Keep h exactly on[0,T] and continue by

    h_tilde(t)=A0 exp(-gamma t)
       +(h(T)-A0 exp(-gamma T))exp[-a(t-T)]           (t>T).

The difference is R(t)-R(T)exp[-a(t-T)]. Its two L2 norms prove, with no unknown infinite constant required,

    ||h-h_tilde||<=D_lambda[1+sqrt(a/(gamma+1))]
                       exp[-(gamma+1)T].            (R14)

For every nonprincipal chi, A(x) is q-periodic. Take m_chi its mean and B=A-m_chi, whose mean-zero primitive is bounded by2q^2. For a principal character put B0=A-rx, beta its mean, D(x)=integral_1^x(B0-beta); then exactly

    f(log x)=m_chi+B_chi(x)+V_chi(x)/x,
    m_chi=-beta, B_chi=B0-beta,
    V_chi=r+2beta-2D(x).                              (R15)

Here |D|<=2q^2, |V|<=1+2q+4q^2. The same proof yields(R13)-(R14) with A0=sqrt(2a)m_chi/lambda and D_chi=4q^2 for nonprincipal chi, or 4q^2+(1+2q+4q^2)/(1-lambda) for principal chi. It works componentwise for complex chi and retains natural zeros. Exact checks include the quartic character modulo5 and its induced, zero-extended character modulo20. Fixed-q constants are allowed; the constant blows up at gamma=1/2 and no endpoint claim follows.

This is a useful source formation theorem, specifically adapting [private research revision]'s bounded-periodic-primitive method. Combining(R14) with(R11) still charges sum|p_j| and the entire computed signed residual. It does not imply Delta_N->0. A degree/cutoff schedule must pay the displayed coefficient growth; arbitrarily increasing N at a fixed T is not justified.

## 4. Finite optimizer and interpolation obstructions

Every constrained minimizer is zero-free on the closed disk for every nonzero source F with F0!=0. If p=(z-lambda)q, variation by zq is admissible. Orthogonality and the strict Cauchy--Schwarz inequality for qF,zqF imply |lambda|>1. Thus root stability is automatic. This is classical optimal-polynomial approximation; the report's p0=1 version is directly proved, and no literature novelty is assigned. [Beneteau et al., arXiv:1509.04807v2, Theorem3.2 and cyclicity discussion](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1509.04807).

For F=1-z/r, r>0, the Gram is tridiagonal with diagonal1+r^-2 and off-diagonal-r^-1. The size-m determinant is D_m=sum_(k=0)^m r^-2k, with D_0=1 for the empty matrix; hence d_N=D_(N+1)/D_N. Its limit is r^-2 for r<1 and1 for r>=1. At r=1, Delta_N=1/(N+1). Because G(r)=r^-2G(1/r), the entire constrained minimizer sequences coincide for r and1/r despite their different interior zero geometry. Coefficient or root geometry alone cannot recover the normalized gap. For the finite-inner toy F=(z-r)/(1-rz), the Gram is I, d_N=1 and Delta_N=1-r^2. Good conditioning has the same limitation.

For X28 take the complete residual e=pF-F0 and a finite Blaschke product B for all exactly fitted safe nodes, including0 and multiplicities. Then e belongs to BH2 and ||e/B||=||e||. At a hypothetical source zero w distinct from those nodes,

    ||e||^2>=|F0|^2(1-|w|^2)/|B(w)|^2.              (R16)

This is evaluation of the divided residual, not an extra norm charge for inner division. For B=z^m it recovers the stated floor. The Taylor inverse to1-z/r gives e=-(z/r)^(N+1), with norm squared r^-2N-2: perfect finite Taylor matching can coexist with a growing complete complement. A fixed-anchor amplification at height T needs degree of order T^2/(beta-gamma); no all-height estimate is extracted. This preserves the exact W22 correction and N29 source geometry. A different paid node geometry or actual full-residual upper bound remains live.

## 5. Independent protected audit X23: an exact divisor Bellman contract

This audit was selected from the original seed before outcomes. It is separate from the author's six tests. Set a(n)=mu(n)chi(n), c(n)=chi(n), so a*c=delta on all integers, including ramified zeros and all prime powers. The exact sequential recurrence is

    a(1)=1; a(n)=-sum_(d|n,d<n)a(d)chi(n/d).

Let x_n=(a(1),...,a(n)) and let T_n append that divisor row to x_(n-1). Its entries are literally -chi(n/d)1_(d|n), not unsigned incidence weights. With ell_N=(1,...,1), M_chi(N)=ell_N x_N.

For Hermitian matrices P_n>=0, possibly depending on N, a complete Bellman certificate consists of

    P_N>=ell_N*ell_N,
    T_n*P_nT_n<=P_(n-1)+E_n.                         (R17)

The E_n may be Hermitian signed debts. Evaluating on the actual source and telescoping gives

    |M_chi(N)|^2<=x_1*P_1x_1
                      +sum_(n=2)^N x_(n-1)*E_n x_(n-1).     (R18)

The whole actual right side must be bounded. Replacing every debt by a positive bound is a sufficient but possibly wasteful choice, not part of the identity. A bound O_(chi,epsilon)(N^(2gamma+epsilon)) for every epsilon and all N returns M=O(N^(gamma+epsilon)) after relabeling epsilon. Abel/Mellin continuation of sum mu(n)chi(n)n^-s then excludes L-zeros in Re s>gamma at every height; the principal pole is matched by a zero of the reciprocal. The same gamma is required for every fixed ordinary chi. No cancellation is proved merely by writing(R17).

The seed specifically proposes testing only reachable states. For that formulation, it is enough to require each inequality in(R17) after evaluation on the actual x_(n-1), and the terminal inequality only on x_N; the identical telescoping proof gives(R18). Global matrix inequalities are a stronger sufficient certificate, not an inferred property of the reachable set. Even a diagonal terminal form can then escape the quadratic global price below: at N=2,chi=1, x=(1,-1) has output0, so the zero form is sufficient on that state. The uninformative choice D=|M_chi(N)|^2 I/K also has the exact reachable energy but already requires the unknown output. A finite usable description of reachability and a noncircular signed bound remain the live high-ceiling part of X23.

The exact no-debt backward metric is instructive. Define a row, for d<=n,

    w_(N,n)(d)=sum_(j<=n/d)chi(j) M_chi(floor(N/(dj))).       (R19)

To verify it without missing a tail, start from an arbitrary prefix x_1,...,x_n. Set b(k)=sum_(d|k)x_d chi(k/d) for k<=n and b(k)=0 for k>n. The continuation is b*(mu chi), and its sum through N is sum_(k<=n)b(k)M_chi(floor(N/k)). Reordering gives(R19). Hence w_(N,N)=ell_N, w_(N,n-1)=w_(N,n)T_n, and w_(N,1)=M_chi(N). The matrices P_n=w_(N,n)*w_(N,n) satisfy(R17) with E_n=0, but P_1=|M_chi(N)|^2. This exact certificate is circular unless constructed/bounded by new arithmetic information. It shows precisely where the full signed response resides.

A concrete restricted class already has exponent-two cost. Even remove every forced-zero coordinate at the terminal time: I={n<=N:mu(n)chi(n)!=0}, K=|I|. Every remaining actual source coordinate has modulus1. A positive diagonal D dominating ell_I*ell_I must satisfy sum_(i in I)1/d_i<=1. Consequently its actual terminal energy is sum_i d_i>=K^2; equality is attained by d_i=K. Natural zeros do not erase this cost. Direct squarefree counting gives

    K=kappa_q N+O_q(sqrt N),
    kappa_q=1/zeta(2) product_(p|q)(1+1/p)^-1>0.      (R20)

Indeed sum_(d<=sqrt N,(d,q)=1)mu(d) times the number of q-units m<=N/d^2 gives the formula; the coprime-prefix error and the convergent d^-2 tail each cost O_q(sqrt N). Thus a diagonal terminal majorant on this active subspace costs Theta_q(N^2). This is NOT a lower bound on |M_chi(N)|^2 or on every reachable/source-specific Bellman certificate. Signed off-diagonal geometry remains live. It is the actual divisor-source specialization of the known U-VARIATIONAL/W38 magnitude-only SDP obstruction, with the exact adjoint response and conditional return now stated.

## 6. Independent uniform audit F06: a raw principal half-plane obstruction

The seed proposes finite Dirichlet-polynomial Bezout approximants with a globally uniform contracting remainder. Preserve that precise formulation. Let chi be principal, 0<gamma<1, and P(s)=sum_(n<=D)c_n n^-s any finite Dirichlet polynomial. Suppose R=1-L(s,chi)P(s) is holomorphic and bounded on the WHOLE half-plane Re s>gamma. Its pole at1 forces P(1)=0. P identically0 already has ||R||=1; otherwise this zero is isolated.

There are unbounded translations T_k for which exp(-iT_k log n)->1 simultaneously for the finitely many frequencies in P. This follows by recurrence in a finite torus, or the elementary simultaneous pigeonhole approximation: a periodic orbit gives unbounded exact returns, and an infinite orbit gives arbitrarily close unbounded returns. Therefore P(s+iT_k)->P(s) uniformly on compact sets. Choose a disk centered at1 of radius less than1-gamma whose boundary has no P-zero. Rouche's theorem supplies a zero of P(s+iT_k) in that disk for large k. Translated back, these are zeros of P with real part>gamma and unbounded heights, away from the unique L-pole at1. statement:
## G188. A complete periodic-cofactor estimate

Fix bounded mean-zero Q-periodic b, X>=2 and any finite real D>=1. All A_m are fixed before x in [X,2X], with |A_m|<=A.
Write f_x(n)=exp(-n/x^(3/2)-i(n/x)^6) and use shell measure dx/x.
Then the theorem is

    H_D(x)=sum_(m<=D) A_m sum_(l>=1)b(l)f_x(ml),
    ||H_D||_1+||H_D||_2 << A(D+X^(3/4))log^4(2X).          (G188.1)

Constants retain only Q and ||b||inf (and the fixed cutoff). For D
bounded by a fixed power of X, divisor-bounded A_m replace the logarithm
by X^epsilon, for every epsilon after choosing the divisor loss. There is no growing-period, live-x coefficient or
arbitrary output/cofactor mask permission.

Take a fixed smooth nonincreasing phi equal1 on[0,1], zero on[2,infinity)
and w(t)=phi(t/2)-phi(t). The exact identity

    1=phi(n/X)+sum_(j>=0)w(n/(2^j X))                     (G188.2)

retains all transitions and the infinite damped tail. On the low part,
rows m<=delta_Q X have nonzero Fourier derivatives separated from
integers, including the last increment, for a sufficiently small fixed
delta_Q. Discrete first derivative and Abel summation give O_Q(1).
Larger active low rows have m<=2X and at most 2/delta_Q terms, so each
costs O_Q(1) trivially. All low rows cost O(A min(D,X))<=O(AD).

On a high block N=2^jX, rows m>4N are exactly empty. Remove these
before Poisson and use the frozen interval [M,2M) intersect[1,D]
intersect[1,4N]. In particular m/N<=4. Put T=(N/X)^6.
Poisson, with b expanded at period Q, gives EXACTLY

    sum_l b(l)w(ml/N)f_x(ml)=(1/m)sum_(h in Z)beta_h I_(h/m)(x),
    I_r=int_0^infinity w(n/N)e^(-n/x^(3/2))
                  exp(i[2pi r n/Q-(n/x)^6])dn.             (G188.3)

The periodic beta_h obey beta_(Qj)=0. Both signs and every alias remain.
For r>0, the critical point and its phase are

    n_r=(pi r/(3Q))^(1/5)x^(6/5),
    phase=5(pi/(3Q))^(6/5)r^(6/5)x^(6/5),
    second derivative=-30n_r^4/x^6.

Choose an ambient near range c_QT/N<=r<=C_QT/N before x or live labels,
wide enough to contain every stationary point meeting [N,4N]. The
rescaled phases form a compact nondegenerate family. Smooth stationary
phase, including smooth support crossings, yields

    I_r=Z_r exp(i*kappa_Q*r^(6/5)x^(6/5)-i*pi/4)
                      +O((N/T)e^(-cN/X^(3/2))),
    Z_r=sqrt(pi/15)x^3 n_r^(-2)w(n_r/N)e^(-n_r/x^(3/2)).   (G188.4)

Its uniformity follows from a compact Morse change and bounded damped
amplitude derivatives. Sharp stationary endpoints are not erased:
the argument completes the entire source before using smooth blocks.

Let H_m=mT/N. Near aliases number O(1+H_m), and any nonempty near bank
has H_m bounded below, so their total remainder after1/m is O(1)
with damping. Negative and small nonstationary aliases have rescaled
derivative comparable T; two integrations by parts give O(T^-1) after
summing them. The entire large-alias tail sums (m/N)h^-2, costing
O(T^-1) or O(m/N). Thus the whole transformed row has a damped O(1)
error, and the row-block error is O(AM e^(-cN/X^(3/2))).

Reduce r=h/m=u/v, so m=vj,h=uj. The ENTIRE Z_r and phase depend only
on r,N,x. The only remaining separate m factor is1/m. Consequently

    C_(u/v)=sum_(vj in original row block) A_(vj)beta_(uj)/(vj)

is x-independent and |C_(u/v)|<<A/v. All original truncations, Fourier
zeros and collisions are retained. Since u>=1 and r<=C_QT/N,
v>=N/(C_QT), while v<=2M. Therefore

    sum_r |C_r|^2 << A^2 sum_(max(1,N/(C_QT))<=v<=2M)
                         (vT/N+1)/v^2
                    << A^2(T/N)log(2M).                    (G188.5)

The lower denominator bound is essential; dropping it introduces an
unpaid N^2/T term.

For x=Xz, the first two needed amplitude bounds are
|Z_r|+|dZ_r/dz|<<(N/sqrt T)e^(-cN/X^(3/2)). Distinct r,s have phase
derivative comparable N|r-s|. One integration by parts retains both
shell endpoints and bounds their full inner product by

    (N^2/T)e^(-cN/X^(3/2))min(1,1/(N|r-s|)).               (G188.6)

The diagonal uses the same estimate with minimum1. Distinct reduced
fractions with denominators<=2M are separated by1/(4M^2). There are
J<<M+M^2T/N, and the full kernel row sum is
O(1+(M^2/N)log(2+J)). Applying2|C_r C_s|<=|C_r|^2+|C_s|^2 to the
entire pair sum and using(G188.5) proves

    ||whole (M,N) block||_2^2
         <<A^2 e^(-cN/X^(3/2))(N+M^2)log^2(2N).             (G188.7)

The already bounded row error is included by norm triangle. Summing
whole blocks in norm retains all cross terms. Since M<=4N, all
logarithms are O(log(2N)) without a log D. For fixed N, M sums to
O(min(D,N)), while the sqrt N part acquires at most log(2N). Thus the
whole high source is at most

    A sum_(N=2^jX)e^(-cN/X^(3/2))
        [sqrt N log^2(2N)+min(D,N)log(2N)].

The two sums are bounded by X^(3/4)log^2(2X) and D log^2(2X).
The infinite damped tail converges; finite-measure Cauchy gives L1.
This proves the arbitrary finite D extension, independently developed
by the reviewer and reconstructed by root. It does not assert an
infinite undamped coefficient bank or a different phase theorem.

## 5. Dyadic theorem and the summable squareful-source mass

Fix dyads \(q_s\asymp Y,\ q_I\asymp C,\ q_J\asymp N\), with \(I\) squarefree, \(C,N,Y\ge1\), and \(CN^3\asymp T\). Completed windows have bounded absolute value in their fixed annulus. Source phases and any extra row-independent label mask have modulus at most a fixed constant. One may retain any subset of these labels throughout the proof. No step below requires \(Y\ll T\), so completed dyads in the original lower Gaussian tail are covered as well.

For \(h_{\rm act}\le H_0\), apply (XM12) to (XM17). The passive divisor sum satisfies \(\sum_{b\mid\mathfrak b_{\rm pas}}q_b^{-\rho}\le\tau(\mathfrak b_{\rm pas})\). The principal divisor sum obeys
\[
\sum_{f\mid\mathfrak e_u}q_f^{1-\rho}
\le E_u^{1-\rho}\tau(\mathfrak e_u)
\qquad(0\le\rho\le1).
\]
After allowing a small divisor factor, the row bound is
\[
\ll (1+|v|)^{J_0}(YT)^\eta
Q^\rho H_0^{(1-\rho)/2}
D_u^{1-\rho}E_u^{1-\rho}\sqrt{q_tR_u}.
\]
Since \(q_t\asymp Y/U\), its last three arithmetic factors are
\[
D_u^{1-\rho}E_u^{1-\rho}\sqrt{q_tR_u}
\asymp \sqrt Y\,U^{1/2-\rho}R_u^{\rho-1/2}.
\tag{XM19}
\]

For a fixed \(u\), put \(g=(t,I)\). Every prime in \(t/g\) or \(I/g\) has a nonzero exponent after adding \(3v_p(J)\): the unequal squarefree exponents differ by one, and a multiple of three cannot cancel that difference modulo six. These two ideals and \(\mathfrak r_u\) are pairwise coprime. Therefore
\[
\frac{q_tq_I R_u}{q_g^2}\le h_{\rm act}\le H_0.
\tag{XM20}
\]
For a gcd dyad \(q_g\asymp G\), positive ideal counting gives
\[
\#\{(t,I):q_t\asymp Y/U,\ q_I\asymp C,\ (t,I)\asymp G\}
\ll \frac{YC}{UG}.
\]
Summing the dyads \(G\gg\sqrt{YC R_u/(UH_0)}\) gives
\[
\#(t,I)\ll
\min\!\left(\frac{YC}{U},
\sqrt{\frac{YC H_0}{UR_u}}\right).
\tag{XM21}
\]
If the lower gcd threshold is below one, the second expression is at least the first. If the reduced \(t\)-annulus is empty, there is no term. Reduced scales in a fixed bounded interval below one are covered by enlarging constants. Thus no false count at a subunit source scale is used.

There are \(O(N)\) cube labels \(J\). Their actual completed weight costs
\[
N\frac{N^{1/2}}{T^{1/2}}\asymp C^{-1/2}.
\tag{XM22}
\]
Multiplying (XM19), the second count in (XM21), (XM22), and the source normalizer \(Y^{-3/2}\) yields
\[
|\mathcal M_{C,N;\,u,h_{\rm act}\le H_0}|
\ll (1+|v|)^{J_0}(YT)^\eta
\frac{Q^\rho H_0^{1-\rho/2}}{\sqrt Y}
U^{-\rho}R_u^{\rho-1}.
\tag{XM23}
\]
The Euler series of the last factor is
\[
\sum_{u\ {\rm squareful}}U^{-\rho}R_u^{\rho-1}
=\prod_{p\notin S}
\left(1+
\sum_{\substack{a\ge2\\6\nmid a}}q_p^{-1-(a-1)\rho}
+\sum_{j\ge1}q_p^{-6j\rho}\right).
\tag{XM24}
\]
It converges for every fixed \(\rho>1/6\). Nonprincipal powers start with exponent \(1+\rho>1\); principal powers start with exponent \(6\rho>1\). Divisor losses in (XM23) may be bounded first by \((YT)^\eta\), since \(U\ll Y\) and all passive labels are bounded by \(YT\) on the dyad. They do not alter the convergent Euler exponents.

We obtain the new all-source theorem
\[
\boxed{
|\mathcal M_{C,N;\,h_{\rm act}\le H_0}|
\ll_{\rho,\eta}
(1+|v|)^{J_0}(YT)^\eta
\frac{Q^\rho H_0^{1-\rho/2}}{\sqrt Y},
\qquad 1/6<\rho\le1 .
}
\tag{XM25}
\]
The exponent \(J_0\) depends only on fixed profile seminorms. The estimate remains valid with bounded row-independent label masks; this includes overlaps when combining paid sectors. Arbitrary row-dependent masks are not allowed.

If \(Q,Y,H_0\) are in fixed polynomial ranges, choose
\(\rho=1/6+\delta_\epsilon\), with a fixed positive \(\delta_\epsilon\) sufficiently small for the prescribed loss. Since \(H_0\ge1\),
\[
Q^\rho H_0^{1-\rho/2}
\le Q^{1/6}H_0^{11/12}Q^{\delta_\epsilon}.
\]
After the completed-profile summation proved next, this gives
\[
\boxed{
|\mathcal M_{D;\,h_{\rm act}\le H_0}|
\ll_\epsilon (1+|v|)^{J_0}Z^\epsilon
\frac{Q_D^{1/6}H_0^{11/12}}{\sqrt{Y_D}}.
}
\tag{XM26}
\]
No contour or Euler series is evaluated on the divergent endpoint \(\rho=1/6\). The constant can depend on the chosen positive buffer.
