## 4. Development B / W49-24: a sharp-cutoff matching exhausts itself after one prime

Fix any prime p0 with chi(p0)=1, and take an increasing eligible list p0<p1<... with chi(pj)=1. Work on the actual finite support

    V_x={n<=x: mu(n)!=0, (n,q)=1}.

At each prime p, match all still-unmatched pairs {m,pm} with p not dividing m and pm<=x. These pairs have exactly opposite a values; no phase or square-zero term is altered. At the FIRST stage all such p0-pairs are removed. The unmatched support is exactly

    U_x={n in V_x: p0 not dividing n, x/p0<n<=x}.           (B1)

Every n divisible by p0 was paired with n/p0. Every p0-free n<=x/p0 was paired upwards. This proves B1, including its endpoints.

No later eligible prime can connect two vertices of U_x. If m in U_x then pj*m>x for pj>p0. Equivalently, deleting pj from another surviving integer leaves a number below x/p0, which was already removed. Thus the entire increasing-prime greedy matching terminates after its first stage, regardless of list length. In particular

    M_chi(x)=sum_(x/p0<n<=x, (n,p0)=1)mu(n)chi(n).          (B2)

The surviving signed boundary is the COMPLETE original Mertens sum. Increasing the number of greedy primes yields no additional cancellation in this construction. B2 is also immediate from the classical one-prime decomposition; the new test is the exact failure of the proposed iterative greedy improvement, not a new prime-toggle principle.

The absolute unmatched mass is a positive proportion of x. For fixed Q=qp0,

    #{n<=t: mu(n)!=0,(n,Q)=1}=kappa_Q t+O_Q(sqrt t),
    kappa_Q=(phi(Q)/Q) product_(p not dividing Q)(1-p^-2)>0.

Proof: use mu(n)^2=sum_(d^2|n)mu(d), count the inner integers coprime to Q by (phi(Q)/Q)u+O_Q(1), sum O_Q(1) over d<=sqrt t, and pay the d^-2 tail by O(sqrt t). Consequently

    #U_x=kappa_(qp0)(1-1/p0)x+O_(q,p0)(sqrt x).           (B3)

For q=1,p0=2 this is (2/pi^2)x+O(sqrt x). This is an unsigned certificate cost, not a signed lower bound. A theorem for the signed boundary in B2 at exponent gamma is exactly a theorem for M_chi at that exponent, with no transfer loss; none has been proved here.

G76 concerns an all-power f3 matching on the COMPLETE Gaussian source, with unmatched Q^2 divisibility and a signed edge readout. B1 concerns squarefree mu support, cancellation of unweighted sharp-cutoff pairs BEFORE retaining their boundary, and a particular increasing-prime greedy algorithm. These are different constructions. B1 does not refute G76, arbitrary adaptive matchings, close one-prime/two-prime swaps, or matching with a separately priced unmatched source. U-PRIME-CHAIN, W01-C, W03-A and W44/G65 remain the relevant ancestry.

The useful next action would be a source-exact rule that revisits previously matched vertices or uses close-ratio prime/product swaps and proves a smaller full signed boundary. Merely appending primes to this greedy list is closed as a research route.

L=log X. For fixed 1/3<rho_0<=rho<=rho_1<1/2 and a fixed buffered
mu-Mertens exponent 1/2<beta<1, set eta=(1-2rho_1)(1-beta)/4. Then

    R_(X^rho)(x)=C_f e^(tau/2) B(rho) x/L^3
                        +O(X/L^4+X^(1-eta)L),
    C_f=9log2 product_(p>=5)(1-1/(p-1)^2),
    B(rho)=2log((1-rho)/rho)-2/(1-rho)-1/(1-rho)^2.     (G37)

B is negative and strictly decreasing. Thus the actual band from
X^(3/8) to X^(2/5) is positive, with coefficient
C_f e^(tau/2)[79/225+2log(10/9)]. This sign differs from G35's
subpower bands. The complete tail above any fixed rho_plus>1/2 is
O_A(X^-A), so the band from a fixed rho<1/2 to rho_plus is negative.
No uniformity through rho=1/2 or moving transition has been proved.

The proof uses the actual f=h*mu convolution and the double zero of
its reciprocal series at1: signed reciprocal core moments are0,0,2C_f.
The two-rough-prime source identity is exact only below z^3; its
outside discrepancy, all repeated powers and the artificial p=q
diagonal are paid. Signed Abel summation removes large cores before
both sharp PNT substitutions. A signed Taylor remainder and its
derivative, not an unsigned harmonic estimate, pay O(X/L^4).

There is a separate theorem needing no Mertens or complete-F input.
For fixed tau>0 and kappa>=1, define the absolutely convergent profile

    J(v)=integral_v^infinity e^u(u-v)g_tau(u)du,
    Phi(q)=sum_(r>=1)f3(r)/r J(log(rq)).

Then uniformly on the full shell,

    R_(kappa sqrt(X))(x)=2x/L^2 Phi(kappa^2 X/x)
                                      +O(X/L^3).      (G38)

For kappa^2>=2e^(3tau), Phi(q)>=(3/4)J(log q)>0 throughout
q in [kappa^2/2,kappa^2]. Consequently, for fixed rho_plus>1/2,

    T_(X^rho_plus)-T_(kappa sqrt(X))
       =2x/L^2 Phi(kappa^2 X/x)+O(X/L^3)>0.            (G39)

All continuous-core extension tails and both Stieltjes errors are
absolute here. The global prime-density expansion, after scaling
p,q by sqrt(X), has integrable error O(L^-3); its unordered factor
1/2 times density4/L^2 gives2. The r=1 term dominates the entire
r>=2 profile by a factor at least4/3. This is fixed-kappa positivity,
not a uniform assertion for moving kappa or every threshold jump.

Both source theorems retain all Gram entries, the true original O(X)
diagonal and both independent heights. For the exact split in G36,
b=||R|| is comparable to X/L^d, with d=3 in G37 and d=2 for the
positive G38 profile. A full new 1/2<gamma<.8748540364 requires BOTH

    |a-b| << X^(gamma+epsilon),
    1+rho << X^(2gamma-2+epsilon)L^(2d).               (G40)

The baseline near cancellation normalized by actual b^2 is distinct
from the additional O(1/L) error introduced by a leading profile.
Neither a logarithmic asymptotic nor its rank-one leading Gram closes
G40 at new power precision. The fixed full-field convolution return
applies after reconstructing F; arbitrary moving masks inherit none.

For the fixed complete Gaussian field F(x), with coefficients a(n) satisfying
sum |a(n)|n^-B<infinity, take fixed tau,kappa>0 and define sigma=tau+kappa,
nu=tau*kappa/sigma, alpha=kappa/sigma. The localized field
W_X(v)=g_kappa(v)F(Xe^v) has exact expansion

    W_X(v)=sum_n a(n)g_sigma(log(n/X))g_nu(v-alpha log(n/X)).

Consequently its Fourier transform has Gaussian envelope
C X^B exp(-nu t^2/2). For the full inhomogeneous negative norm N_r=||W_X||H^-r,
the exact signed double sum uses

    J_r,X(n,m)=b_n b_m E_r,nu(alpha log(n/m)),
    b_n=g_sigma(log(n/X)),

where E is the positive Gaussian-mixture kernel from the report. Positivity
of that kernel does not permit removal of the signed coefficient products.
All n,m, prime powers and natural character zeros remain. Its diagonal is
O(X) for bounded coefficients and O(X^(1+epsilon)) for divisor bounds.

For every T>0,

    ||W_X||2 <= (1+T^2)^(r/2) N_r + C X^B exp(-nu T^2/2).

The high-frequency tail is NOT multiplied by the negative-norm inverse
weight. If d=limsup r_X loglog X/log X is finite and every sufficiently

# [private research revision]: short arithmetic moves and the complete signed remainder

Root accepts G161–G163 after complete mathematical intake of the
[W60 author](wild60/report.md) and [independent critic](wild60-review/report.md).
The main advance is a source-specific obstruction to fixed prime-factor
replacement budgets, even for complex flows. It redirects local matching
and coding constructions toward growing replacement counts or signed
estimates. It is not a lower bound for a full signed Möbius sum.

The accepted written value remains `c11=312864909/2500000000=.1251459636`,
with `gamma11=2187135091/2500000000=.8748540364`. The density constant
`K=28114053/6250000` retains preceding-c10 same-family ancestry.
Inherited analytic, positive-slot-uniformity and external-admission
obligations remain open. No formalization, new packet or public-record claim.

## G161. A fixed replacement budget leaves a large actual residual

Fix an ordinary character chi modulo a fixed q. The arithmetic source is
`a(n)=mu(n)chi(n)`, with squareful and nonunit zeros and n=1 retained.
It is distinct from the Eisenstein native-H coefficient system below.

Suppose every allowed edge {n,m}, n!=m, obeys
`|n-m|<=C min(n,m)^theta`, where `C>0`, `0<=theta<1`, and at each
squarefree endpoint at most a fixed d>=1 of its prime factors are deleted
when moving to the other endpoint. The restriction applies independently
at each squarefree endpoint, regardless of flow orientation. Auxiliary
squareful/nonunit integer vertices are permitted under this same rule.

Let g=gcd(n,m). Since g divides n-m,

    g<=|n-m|,       n/g >= C^(-1)n^(1-theta).

For squarefree n, the quotient n/g is exactly the product of its deleted
prime factors. If every prime of n is at most y, the budget implies
`n/g<=y^d`. Thus `n^(1-theta)>C y^d` makes n isolated in the entire graph,
including edges to integers outside the current shell or cutoff.

Choose a fixed integer `k>d/(1-theta)`. Products of k distinct primes in
`(X^(1/k),(2X)^(1/k)]` lie in `(X,2X]`, are squarefree, and eventually
avoid every prime dividing the fixed q. With `y=(2X)^(1/k)`,

    n^(1-theta)/(C y^d)
      >= C^(-1)2^(-d/k) X^(1-theta-d/k) -> infinity.

Every such product is therefore isolated for every sufficiently large X.
The ordinary prime number theorem gives, for this fixed k,
`t_X ~ k(2^(1/k)-1)X^(1/k)/log X` primes in the interval.
Unique factorization gives exactly binomial(t_X,k) products, hence

    |V_X| ~ A_k X/(log X)^k,
    A_k=[k(2^(1/k)-1)]^k/k! >0.

Only the ordinary PNT is used; see [NIST DLMF §27.12](https://dlmf.nist.gov/27.12).
There is no progression equidistribution, short-interval theorem, growing-k
substitution or uniformity in a modulus that can absorb those primes.
The constant may be tiny and the onset large, without changing the exponent.

For any complex flow F on this graph with defined divergence, an exact
source decomposition `a=div F+r` has `r(n)=a(n)` at every isolated n.
Therefore

    sum_(X<n<=2X)|r(n)| >= |V_X|.

No positivity, disjointness, bounded flow coefficients or acyclicity is
required. Repeated short steps cannot start at an isolated vertex.
This rules out `O_(epsilon)(X^(delta+epsilon))` absolute residual bounds
for delta<1: choose epsilon<(1-delta)/2. A bounded collection of budgets
is covered by its maximum; subpower inflation of C is absorbed by a
slightly larger fixed theta<1 before choosing k. No conclusion is claimed
for an unbounded d or k without a separate quantitative argument.

| displacement exponent theta | d | k | strict margin 1-theta-d/k |
|---|---|---|---|
| 17497/20000=.87485 | 3 | 24 | 3/20000 |
| current gamma11 | 3 | 24 | 364909/2500000000 |
| 5/6 | 3 | 19 | 1/114 |
| 3/4 | 3 | 13 | 1/52 |

For principal chi, the isolated k-prime layer has constant sign (-1)^k.
This does not control its cancellation with the other layers or the rest
of r. For complex chi, even that layer need not have constant phase.
There is no resulting lower bound for `|sum r|`, `|M_chi|`, a full detector
norm or a zero-free exponent. A viable local construction must instead
pay a growing number of deleted primes, at least
`((1-theta)log n-log C)/log y` at a y-smooth endpoint, or retain the full
signed interaction with other sectors. Long edges and different auxiliary
transfers also remain eligible. This is a record-relative refinement of
U-PRIME-CHAIN/U-TRANSPORT and the coding portfolio, not a literature claim.

### Character phase and the complete conditional return

For a finite set of unramified primes and `w(S)=(-1)^|S|chi(product S)`,
an exact toggle C has

    w(S xor C)/w(S) = (-1)^|C| product_(p in C)chi(p)
                                  product_(p in S intersect C)chi(p)^(-2).

It equals -1 for every state of the full Boolean cube exactly when
`chi(p)^2=1` for each p in C and `(-1)^|C|product_C chi(p)=-1`.
Necessity uses the empty state and each singleton; sufficiency is substitution.
No ramified character value is inverted. A cutoff-restricted state set can
have additional exchanges; this universal-cube test does not forbid them.
For the quartic character modulo 5 with chi(2)=i,chi(3)=-i,chi(11)=1,
the toggle {2,3,11} reverses 1 and 66 but gives the same coefficient -i
at 2 and 33. The state-specific exchange 6<->11 remains valid.

The global matching return is retained from transport ancestry. Suppose
one global disjoint pairing has opposite actual coefficients, the above
displacement exponent theta, and unmatched count
`O_(chi,epsilon)(x^(delta+epsilon))` for every epsilon>0. Pairs wholly
below x cancel exactly. Crossing pairs have distinct lower endpoints in
`[x-C x^theta,x]`, so

    |M_chi(x)| <= C x^theta+O_(chi,epsilon)(x^(delta+epsilon))+O_chi(1).

For a common `gamma=max(theta,delta)>0`, normal convergence of
`s integral_1^infinity M_chi(x)x^(-s-1)dx` and its derivatives on
Re s>gamma gives continuation of the actual reciprocal 1/L(s,chi).
Choose epsilon below each compact's horizontal margin. The meromorphic
identity L F=1 excludes regular zeros there; a principal pole forces
a reciprocal zero and is allowed. Imprimitive Euler factors and every
fixed height remain literal. Constants/onsets may depend on fixed chi.
Different finite-cutoff matchings do not automatically form this global
pairing. The bound is conditional, not supplied by the algebra.
Gamma=.87485,5/6,3/4 would return c=.12515,1/6,1/4; the near conditional
gain over current c11 is 10091/2500000000. G161 blocks the fixed-budget
construction's absolute unmatched premise, not all possible signed returns.

## G162. All finite comparable matchings have a terminal-prime cut

In the finite squarefree q-unit set n<=X, each unramified prime p in
`(X/2,X]` has exactly one distinct comparable vertex, namely 1.
It has no other divisor and no proper multiple inside the cutoff.
Every disjoint pairing along divisibility therefore leaves at least
`#{X/2<p<=X,p not dividing q}-1` terminal primes unmatched.
For a nonnegative fractional matching with vertex capacity 1, their total
incident weight is also at most the capacity of 1; the same bound applies
to unmatched mass. Character restrictions can only remove edges.

Ordinary PNT makes this asymptotic to X/(2 log X), for fixed q.
No acyclicity is used: the result covers adaptive pivots and comparable
pairs differing by several primes. It does not apply to arbitrary complex
shared-vertex homotopies, incomparable pairs or partners beyond the cutoff.
It is not a lower bound on G150's global future-partner displacement cost.

The exact decomposition `M_chi(X)=A_p(X)-chi(p)A_p(X/p)` with
`A_p(Y)=sum_(n<=Y,p not dividing n)mu(n)chi(n)` is already G144 ancestry.
Choosing chi(p)=1 does not bound the remaining boundary term.
The new cut has wider matching scope but a weaker numerical lower bound
than the linear count for G144's specified cone. W59's additional homology
argument remains separately frozen, root-pending evidence; this acceptance
does not promote it. Incomparable exchanges such as 6<->11 avoid this cut,
but bounded short replacements still face G161.

## G163. Exact native Schur and four-cycle bills

These independent audits clarify complete costs, rather than provide
an arithmetic saving. Freeze an actual finite native-H packet and its two
independent heights. Keep the Eisenstein primary/fixed-ray/six-unit/bad-place
data, distinct-rational-norm long primes, both orientations, every ordered
short pair including equality, bounded complex h, rational gcd screen,
both projectors, natural zeros, all profiles and CRT phases.
The source contract is [[restricted research revision] §1](../[private research revision]/h-joint/report.md), with the
corrected matrix convention in [G75 review R10–R11](../[private research revision]/wild46-review/report.md).

Specifically, `v_P=u1(P)/sqrt(q_P)`, `w_P'=u2(P')/sqrt(q_P')`,
and the scalar sum `sum v_P K_PP' conjugate(w_P')` is `H=w* T v`
with `T=K^T`. The rooted marks are in v,w **once**. Every other original
factor is in T. This explicit reviewer convention controls the author's
compressed Section5 wording that could double-count the roots.
The raw target is `B0 sqrt(Omega1 Omega2)`, where
`B0=G K0[N+L+(NL)^(2/3)]P_orig`, K0 is the original row parameter and
P_orig the actual profile/component costs. Apply `N^(-1)G^(-2)` once
afterward. Full heights, tails, components and other branches remain due.

For a partition `T=[T_R,T_E]`, `v=(u,z)`, let Pi be the output projection
onto ran T_E. Then, exactly,

    ||Tv||^2 = ||(I-Pi)T_R u||^2 + ||Pi T_R u+T_E z||^2,
    S=T_R*(I-Pi)T_R=A-B D^dagger B*,
    A=T_R*T_R, B=T_R*T_E, D=T_E*T_E.

The singular case follows from ker D=ker T_E, B annihilating this kernel,
and `T_E D^dagger T_E*=Pi`. Thus S>=0 and the fill-in is bounded by A.
For `D_lambda=D+lambda I`, lambda>0, there is also the exact completion

    v*(T*T)v = u*(A-B D_lambda^(-1)B*)u
      +(z+D_lambda^(-1)B*u)*D_lambda(z+D_lambda^(-1)B*u)
      -lambda ||z||^2.

A small Schur term alone does not bound the full source: z is fixed,
not freely minimized. The projection has norm 1, while an inverse
representation must pay its own spectral distance. For the synthetic
matrix `[[1,1,1],[0,e,-e]]`, e!=0, eliminating columns 2,3 makes S=0,
yet the source u=1,z=0 has energy 1 in the completion. This is an algebra
diagnostic, not an evaluated native packet. A sufficient OPEN-SC is the
sum of both displayed squared norms <=`B0^2(||u||^2+||z||^2)` with all
original uniformities. It is the full source bill after elimination.
Prior [G107](../[private research revision]/wild51-integration.md) and U-VARIATIONAL retain credit.

For two distinct input columns j,k, put
`b_i=conjugate(T_ij)T_ik`, `s_jk=sum_i|b_i|`,
`eta_i=b_i/|b_i|` only on nonzero entries, and
`psi_jk=sum_(i<l)|b_i||b_l||eta_i-eta_l|^2` over active pairs.
Expansion gives

    |(T*T)_jk|^2 = s_jk^2-psi_jk,
    ||T||^2 <= max_j [sum_i|T_ij|^2
                         +sum_(k!=j)sqrt(s_jk^2-psi_jk)],
    ||T||^4 <= sum_j (sum_i|T_ij|^2)^2
                         +sum_(j!=k)(s_jk^2-psi_jk).

The phase is the four-edge product
`conjugate(T_ij)T_ik T_lj conjugate(T_lk)` divided by its modulus.
Natural-zero entries contribute zero without division. The Hermitian
dilation is bipartite on two separate mark spaces, so it has no triangular
cycle even if the numerical labels coincide. Transported unitary gauges
preserve this four-cycle invariant; fixing source vectors while gauging
the matrix changes H. Short-core interference must remain inside each T entry.

An arithmetic bound on the complete Gram-row expression by B0 squared,
or on the complete fourth-moment expression by B0 to the fourth power,
would suffice. The diagonal and every significant coherent component
remain. A few frustrated cycles or a constant local deficit do not supply
a power saving. The 2-by-2 unit-entry formula `2+2|cos(Phi/2)|` is already
G75, and [W40's retained phase-length scope](../[private research revision]/reviewed-library-integration.md)
remains relevant. No native phase values were numerically evaluated here.

## Other tested cards, sampling and verification

- Card28: rational `a(pn)=-chi(p)a(n)` is not a licensed constraint on
  independent native-H mark arrays. An upstream transported relation remains open.
- Card26: a nonzero Hermitian bilinear dilation has positive and negative
  eigenvalues. A locally finite positive real linear MGF has positive
  semidefinite log Hessian at zero, so cannot represent that indefinite
  quadratic exponential. Complex Gaussian linearization is exact but
  taking modulus loses its imaginary-phase cancellation; nonlinear or
  complex alternatives are not excluded as families.
- Card25: the two-prime based complex with maps `(-b,a)^T` and `(a,b)`
  has torsion 1 up to sign, not ab. The finite determinant calculation uses
  the alternating convention in [Hutchings (2002), Appendix A](https://math.berkeley.edu/~hutching/pub/rt3/rt3.pdf).
  A direct sum stores the product but does not create cutoff cancellation;
  a truncated nonacyclic complex requires a different readout.
- Card30: the full Hermitian cyclic subspace is reducing, so its proposed
  Feshbach self-energy vanishes. Source-line projection has a nontrivial
  Schur resolvent, whose first/second moments still contain H or ||Tv|| squared.
  The spectral estimate remains unpaid. The full-cyclicity example is synthetic.

These failures retain their specified realizations and reopening conditions;
they do not retire whole detector, coding, spectral or complex-field families.
All 30 seed cards are retained, including the corrected-but-frozen Card10
notation: the left side should be a(pn), not bare mu(pn).
Six author tests are28/23/12/26/25/30. Literal all-group pools25/15/25
and indices21/11/24 produce26/25/30 with immutable entropy and no reroll.
Independent priorities and permutation froze before outcome intake;
mechanical exclusions force protected20 and uniform27. The persistence
receipt followed report intake, as disclosed, rather than claiming an
earlier receipt. Twenty-two remaining cards are untested in this round.

Thirty frozen artifacts, twelve reviewer source bindings and fifteen author
source bindings are retained in the [manifest](retention-manifest.json).
Historical mutable sources bind to exact Git blobs. The host-local claim
receipt is checked in place and excluded; its manifest hash entry remains
as provenance. Both STOPs and own releases were reconciled.
Both complete reports/helpers and exact receipts were read, together with
literal native source/ancestry slices and the primary external inputs.
No helper was rerun for reassurance. Finite matching, phase, endpoint,
Schur and cycle diagnostics support indexing/algebra, not the asymptotic
PNT-based proof, an actual native-H evaluation or a stronger c.

The next mathematical target is an exact growing-replacement interaction
or a signed bound on the complete smooth isolated complement coupled to
the larger-prime exchanges. Its displacement, phases and full return must
all be paid. Chained and simultaneous components remain usable through
proved transfers. Original 29 families/109 children and later work survive.

## 2. Development A: an entire Gaussian can be observed on small local sets

Use the NORMALIZED fixed kernel

    g_tau(v)=(2 pi tau)^(-1/2) exp(-v^2/(2tau)), tau>0.

The cards used its unnormalized version; multiplication by the fixed positive constant changes none of their exponents. For ordinary chi put

    a_n=mu(n)chi(n), F(z)=sum_(n>=1) a_n g_tau(log n-z).      (W39.1)

All natural zeros of mu and chi remain. This is the complete unmasked sum. Local uniform absolute convergence proves F entire. Writing z=u+iv gives

    |F(u+iv)| <= C_tau exp(u+v^2/(2tau)), u>=0.              (W39.2)

Indeed the positive sum of g_tau(log n-u) is at most its integral over t>0 plus twice its maximum, because that function of t is unimodal. The integral is exp(u+tau/2), and u>=0 absorbs the fixed maximum. For u<=0 the same series is O_tau(exp(-u^2/(2tau))), since log n>=0. This also pays the entire left Mellin tail.

### A1. Elementary measurable-set interpolation, including complex values

Let P be a complex polynomial of degree at most N>=1 on an interval I of length1. If a measurable E subset I has measure delta>0 and |P|<=m almost everywhere on E, then

    sup_I |P| <= (4e/delta)^N m.                           (W39.3)

Here is a proof rather than an external Remez citation. Replace E by the closed set {|P|<=m} intersect I, whose actual measure Delta is at least delta. Choose N+1 quantile points x_0<...<x_N at cumulative-measure levels (j+1/2)Delta/(N+1). The cumulative distribution is1-Lipschitz, so

    x_j-x_i >= (j-i)delta/(N+1).

The quantile points lie in the closed set. Lagrange interpolation and |x-x_i|<=1 give

    sum_j |ell_j(x)|
      <= ((N+1)/delta)^N sum_j 1/[j!(N-j)!]
      = ((N+1)/delta)^N 2^N/N! <= (4e/delta)^N.

The inequality N!>=(N/e)^N follows by integrating log t. If m is only an essential supremum, enlarge it arbitrarily and pass to the limit. Thus no real-polynomial sign assumption is used.

### A3. Why the ordinary L-function replenishes the complex bound

For Re s>1, absolute Fubini gives

    integral_R F(y)e^(-s y)dy=exp(tau s^2/2)/L(s,chi).     (W39.9)

If F(y)<<_epsilon exp((h+epsilon)y) for every epsilon>0 as y tends to +infinity, its left Gaussian tail makes the integral holomorphic on Re s>h, including every fixed s derivative. Multiply by L and continue from Re s>1. At any zero rho in this domain, the left product would vanish while exp(tau rho^2/2) does not. A principal pole at1 is separately removable in the reciprocal and creates no false zero exclusion. Hence there are no L zeros in Re s>h.

Conversely, if a fixed ordinary L has no zeros in Re s>h, with h>0, then for EVERY fixed b>h and tau>0 the very same F satisfies W39.4 for some C,K. We need only polynomial growth of 1/L on the fixed line, and derive it here to avoid an unproved inverse-bound assumption.

For a nonprincipal ordinary character, its periodic partial sums are O_q(1). Abel summation gives

    L(s,chi)=s integral_1^infinity A_chi(t)t^(-s-1)dt,
    |L(s,chi)| <= q |s|/Re s, Re s>0.                   (W39.10)

For a principal character A_chi(t)=ct+O_q(1); subtract ct in this integral. It gives the simple principal pole and a polynomial upper bound for P(s)=(s-1)L(s,chi) on every closed positive strip. In the nonprincipal case put P=L. The finite imprimitive Euler factors stay literal and are nonzero on Re s>0.

Fix h<b<2; b>=2 is trivial. Around 2+it take an outer disk of radius R_0=2-(h+b)/2 and inner radius r_0=2-b. The outer disk is zero-free for P, lies in Re s>h, and the gap R_0-r_0=(b-h)/2 is fixed. An analytic logarithm log P exists on that disk. Choose its value at the center to have imaginary part in [-pi,pi]. The absolutely convergent Euler product at2 bounds |L(2+it)| above and away from0; the regularizing factor changes its logarithm by O(log(2+|t|)). Thus |log P(2+it)|=O(log(2+|t|)). The polynomial upper bound for P gives Re log P<=C log(2+|t|) throughout the disk. The elementary Borel--Caratheodory inequality now bounds |log P(b+it)| by C_(h,b,q) log(2+|t|), proving

    |1/L(b+it,chi)| <= C(1+|t|)^K.                       (W39.11)

For completeness put f=log P, choose M>sup Re f, and set g=M-f. Then Re g>0 and H(z)=(g(z)-g(0))/(g(z)+conj(g(0))) maps the disk into the unit disk and vanishes at its center. Schwarz gives |H(z)|<=r_0/R_0 on the inner disk. The triangle inequality then bounds |g(z)| by (R_0+r_0)/(R_0-r_0) times |g(0)|. Since M and |f(0)| are O(log(2+|t|)), the stated bound for f follows. A compact low-height region is absorbed into C. Uniform bounds hold across a fixed closed horizontal strip by using the smallest gap; the reciprocal has a zero at the principal pole, not a singularity.

Mellin inversion on a line >1, followed by a contour shift to b, now gives for all complex z

## 3. Development B: the exact variance price of a signed path

This executes C04's one/two-prime test and gives a useful scoped obstruction. Let a finite signed or complex sum be Z=sum_(alpha in A) w_alpha, with all zero weights removed. A one-path importance estimator picks alpha with probability p_alpha>0 and returns W=w_alpha/p_alpha. It is unbiased and

    E|W|^2=sum_alpha |w_alpha|^2/p_alpha >= V^2,
    V=sum_alpha |w_alpha|,
    E|W-Z|^2 >= V^2-|Z|^2.                              (W39.17)

This is Cauchy--Schwarz applied to |w|/sqrt p and sqrt p. Equality holds exactly for p_alpha=|w_alpha|/V. It is the optimum over ALL sampling laws, not merely independent prime laws. If N independent paths are averaged, the exact optimum mean-squared error is (V^2-|Z|^2)/N. This is an RMS/variance assertion, not an information-theoretic bound for every algorithm or every high-probability estimator.

For a finite set of primes P, z_p=chi(p)p^(-s), the exact Euler reciprocal expansion has w_S=(-1)^|S| product_(p in S)z_p. Every subset, including the empty subset and repeated cross terms in the square, is retained. Then

    Z=product_(p in P)(1-z_p), V=product_(p in P)(1+|z_p|).

The optimizing law factorizes with inclusion probability |z_p|/(1+|z_p|). For ONE prime, the two outcomes are1/(1-r) and -z/r and

    E|W|^2=1/(1-r)+|z|^2/r >=(1+|z|)^2.                 (W39.18)

For TWO primes, independence under the optimum law gives

    E|W|^2=(1+|z_p|)^2(1+|z_q|)^2,
    |Z|^2=|1-z_p-z_q+z_pz_q|^2.                        (W39.19)

The negative one-prime terms and positive two-prime term have not been replaced by independent mean-zero noise. For principal chi at real s, 0<z_p<1, the relative second moment is product((1+z_p)/(1-z_p))^2. Already the finite law can have large phase cancellation; a formal random representation is no variance bound.

There is a direct ACTUAL Gaussian application. For fixed ordinary chi of modulus q, choose weights

    w_n=mu(n)chi(n)g_tau(log n-y), n>=1.

They are absolutely summable. Monotone truncation extends W39.17 to this countable law, and V(y)=sum_(squarefree n,(n,q)=1) g_tau(log n-y). Elementary squarefree counting gives

    count_(n<=X)(mu(n)^2 1_(n,q)=1)
       =d_q X+O_q(sqrt X), d_q>0.                      (W39.20)

To verify it, use mu(n)^2=sum_(d^2|n)mu(d), impose (d,q)=1 and count the remaining integers coprime to q by their fixed periodic density; the O_q(1) error over d<=sqrt X and the convergent1/d^2 tail each cost O_q(sqrt X). The density equals (phi(q)/q) sum_((d,q)=1)mu(d)/d^2>0 by its absolutely convergent Euler product. Gaussian Stieltjes summation consequently gives

    V(y)=d_q exp(tau/2)e^y+O_(q,tau)(e^(y/2)),           (W39.21)

using the exact Gaussian integral and its derivative. Natural zeros of chi and mu are included; this is not random-Möbius modeling.

If the desired actual cancellation has |F(y)|<=e^(gamma y), gamma<1, then the optimum independent sample mean needs at least order exp(2(1-gamma)y) samples to achieve RMS absolute error at most a fixed multiple of exp(gamma y). Indeed insert W39.21 into W39.17 and divide by N; for large y the |F|^2 term is lower order. This statement is conditional on the desired small mean, not evidence that it holds. For a relative RMS tolerance delta when F!=0, the exact requirement is N>=(V^2/|F|^2-1)/delta^2.

For the matrix operator norm, the same factor uses the l2 norms of the positive weighted row and column vectors by the Frobenius bound. Formula W39.28, rather than an unweighted Taylor tail, is the physical scalar budget. If that positive prefactor is at most exp(C_1 L), Z<=C_2 L and r=ceil(C_3 L), then Stirling's elementary bound r!>=(r/e)^r gives exponent at most

    [C_1+C_2+C_3 log(e C_2/C_3)+o(1)]L.

A sufficiently large fixed C_3 makes it less than -A L for any prescribed fixed A. These conditions hold for fixed-width O(sqrt L) log bins whose product center and physical y differ by O(sqrt L), with the actual finite coefficient masses bounded by exp(O(L)). Thus a polylogarithmic-size signed expansion can pay any fixed analytic power error in that bounded setting. This is a finite analytic compression, not a fast algorithm for its arithmetic inputs.

Every term of W39.27 is still a signed, moving-endpoint arithmetic moment of growing degree. When multiple bins or heights are recombined, their full cross Gram is required; bounding one moment or dropping off-block terms does not estimate the whole detector. The current W35 Gaussian/Fourier machinery already provides other finite analytic representations. No independent saving or additional paid sector is claimed for this representation. Its useful conclusion is that exact-rank growth alone is not the decisive obstruction; the exact signed contractions and their joint norm are.

## 5. The other three selected first tests

### T-F05: the natural divisor-poset normal operator squares conditioning

On the exact squarefree diamond {1,p,q,pq}, put u=chi(p)p^(-s), v=chi(q)q^(-s). The convolution matrix and its exact inverse are

    Z=[[1,0,0,0],[u,1,0,0],[v,0,1,0],[uv,v,u,1]],
    U=[[1,0,0,0],[-u,1,0,0],[-v,0,1,0],[uv,-v,-u,1]].    (W39.29)

Both products ZU and UZ equal I; the pq inverse coefficient is +uv, not a deleted cross term. If the proposed Hodge metric is the natural normal operator L=Z*Z, then

    lambda_min(L)=lambda_-(|u|)lambda_-(|v|),
    lambda_-(r)=(2+r^2-r sqrt(4+r^2))/2,
    ||Z^(-1)||=lambda_min(L)^(-1/2).                     (W39.30)

This follows from the tensor product of the two local matrices [[1,0],[u,1]], whose two squared singular values are lambda_-(|u|),lambda_+(|u|) with product1. The local chi phases are unitarily removable. Positivity therefore does not improve this inverse conditioning; it squares it. A different genuine chain complex would require a proof that its Laplacian solution reproduces the original inverse/readout. The test does not rule out such a new construction and is not a bound on the full arithmetic detector. Broader finite-inverse/readout limitations were already established in Sol match01 Max Astra review AM19--AM21 and current-proof G32; those receive prior credit.

### T-D02: translated-field Gram determinants miss a dangerous rank-one mode

Let v_j(t)=F(t+h_j), and G_jk=integral_I v_j(t)conj(v_k(t))w(t)dt with w>=0. For F(t)=A exp(rho t),

    G_jk=|A|^2 exp(rho h_j+conj(rho)h_k)
                    integral_I exp(2 Re(rho)t)w(t)dt.    (W39.31)

It has rank1, so every determinant of size>=2 is zero despite arbitrary positive Re(rho). For F=Ae^(rho1 t)+Be^(rho2 t), rank is at most2. With two shifts, its determinant is exactly

    |AB|^2 |e^(rho1 h1+rho2 h2)-e^(rho2 h1+rho1 h2)|^2
      *[J11 J22-|J12|^2],
    Jkl=integral_I e^((rho_k+conj(rho_l))t)w(t)dt.       (W39.32)

As rho2 approaches rho1, both factors vanish quadratically for a nondegenerate interval and distinct shifts; the determinant is fourth order in the frequency/exponent separation. Thus determinant-only SMALL upper bounds cannot exclude a single growing mode. A trace or coercive observable retaining that mode is necessary and needs its own arithmetic estimate. This is a diagnostic of the stated translated-field Gram detector, NOT a counterexample to the distinct reciprocal Hankel D3 construction or an actual-Möbius lower bound.

### T-B05: the exact mask defect includes both mixed terms

For any original split F=U+V in the actual physical Hilbert space,

    ||F||^2-||U||^2=2 Re<U,V>+||V||^2.                  (W39.33)

An inherited upper bound for ||F|| therefore gives no upper bound for ||U|| without a lower bound on the right-hand defect. Two opposite equal profiles give F=0 and ||U||>0, the simplest diagnostic. The first actual-coefficient two-label Gaussian cell uses mu(1)=1, mu(2)=-1 for the principal character modulo1 (zeta):

    U(y)=g_tau(y), V(y)=-g_tau(y-log2).

On the full unweighted y line, ||U||^2=g_(2tau)(0), and

    ||U+V||^2=2 g_(2tau)(0)[1-exp(-(log2)^2/(4tau))].    (W39.34)

For tau>log2/4, including tau=1, this is smaller than ||U||^2. The coefficient signs and both mixed terms are literal. This finite cell is not claimed to lower bound or model the whole uncut Möbius field; it refutes only automatic inheritance from the generic Hilbert identity, while retaining the exact defect that an actual mask proof must pay. W35/current-proof already forbid this shortcut, so no new-sector credit is taken.

### C. Strong objection: the actual output is not power-small

For principal chi and fixed 0<rho<1, b_X is nonnegative. For any fixed squarefree q-unit d,

    b_X(d) >= rho^k(d)lambda[pi(X/d)-O_(q,d)(1)]
            >>_(q,d,rho) X/log X.                            (A8)

Only cofactor primes m not dividing dq were used. Thus any unweighted l2 or l1 certificate for the full b_X has exponent at least1. Removing a FIXED finite list of labels does not repair it: choose one fixed d outside that list. This is an actual arithmetic lower bound for that positive output norm, not for M or the signed readout. Growing deletions, weighted norms, exact signed centering and correlations with the removed labels remain possible; their reconstruction must be paid.

At rho=1 the map is the identity; ||b||_2 is of order sqrt X, but ||h||_2 is also of order sqrt X, so Cauchy still gives exponent1. More generally, on the principal basis b(d)<=1+lambda X/d and hence ||b||_2^2<=2X+4lambda^2X^2. Taking lambda<=X^-1/2 gives a small l2 norm but no improvement of the full readout estimate. This upper calculation is deliberately coarse and already exposes the missing covariance rather than disguising it as a channel gain.

The useful reopening target is a growing, signed, explicitly evaluable centering btilde with the complete residual in (A7), not merely a positive small-prime model. Fixed-rho inversion is affordable; constructing that arithmetic centering remains open.

statement:
## 7. A new unconditional paid sector: large median factors

For a<b<c and delta>0,

    0<=V_delta(a,b,c)^2 <= a^(-4delta)b^(-2delta).       (D15)

This inequality is useful before summing coefficients. There is a finite constant K_tau such that, for every y>0,

    sum_(n>=1) g_tau(log(n/y)) <=K_tau y.

One elementary proof partitions log(n/y) into intervals [j,j+1), uses at most exp(j+1)y integers in each interval, and sums exp(j+1) times the supremum of the Gaussian on that interval. The resulting bilateral series converges, uniformly in y.

The same ordered-factor inequality also gives the stronger-than-divisor absolute mass bound

    sum_(n<=t)|h_chi,delta(n)|
       <=t zeta(1+4delta)zeta(1+2delta)
       <=t zeta(9/5)zeta(7/5),                           (D15a)

uniformly on I: sum the last factor by floor(t/(ab)) and enlarge the two remaining ranges. This is compatible with the absolute obstruction D6; it supplies no exponent below one.

Let Y be a positive integer. The complete original-tuple sector b>Y consequently satisfies, uniformly for x>0, chi, and delta in I,

    sum_(a<b<c; b>Y)
      |mu(a)mu(b)mu(c)chi(abc)| V_delta(a,b,c)^2
                                  g_tau(log(abc/x))
       <= K_tau x sum_a a^(-1-4delta)
                         sum_(b>Y) b^(-1-2delta)
       <=(5/2)K_tau zeta(9/5) x Y^(-2/5).               (D16)

Here 1+4delta>=9/5, 2delta>=2/5, and the b tail is at most Y^(-2delta)/(2delta)<=(5/2)Y^(-2/5). The c>b restriction was enlarged only at this absolute upper-bound step. Natural character zeros, shared primes and all actual tuple signs are otherwise retained.

Take

    Y_X=floor(X^(63/200))=floor(X^.315).

For X large enough that Y_X>=X^.315/2, D16 proves

    sup_(delta in I) ||H_chi,delta-H_chi,delta; b<=Y_X||_[X,2X]
                   <<_tau X^(437/500)=X^.874.           (D17)

The norm here is L2(dx/x). This is an unconditional new field-tail estimate for this changed determinant source. It is not an estimate for any SP or original W35 subfamily. In particular, .874<.87449<.8748866, so this complete median complement is affordable for the stated first-gain target without using Mobius cancellation.

The surviving sector b<=Y_X still includes a=1,b=2 and every corresponding negative cross term. D17 does not imply that the surviving sector is small, or that the determinant creates cancellation within a given output.

statement:
## UR7. Fixed delta=2: norm 20 and the complete inverse readout

This argument is separate from small-shift D20. It applies to any coefficient sequence with `|a(n)|<=1`, a(1)=1 and `|a(2)|=1`. At delta=2 the `(1,2)` cofactor coefficient is

    c2=(9/256)a(2),
    C2(s)=c2 2^(-s)(1+R(s)),

where R has dilation arguments `r=mn/2>=3/2`. If coefficients with a repeated product coalesce, taking the sum of their absolute tuple weights remains an upper bound. On Re s=-1,

    sum_r |R_r|r
      <= [sum_(m<n) (mn)^(-3)(m^(-2)-n^(-2))^2]/(9/128)-1.

The denominator is exactly the first `(1,2)` term. Expanding the square and pairing `(m,n)` with `(n,m)` gives the exact positive sum `zeta(3)zeta(7)-zeta(5)^2`. There is no dropped factor of two. Integral bounds on the zeta tails at cutoff 32 give the rational upper bound in D23. The independent script recomputes it with exact fractions and verifies

    q_R <= .9468750294472809... <19/20,
    1/(1-q_R)<20.

The displayed decimal is diagnostic only; the comparison is exact rational arithmetic. Since `r^(-Re s)<=r` for Re s>=-1,

    |C2(s)| >= |c2|2^(-Re s)(1-q_R)
                    >=(9/5120)2^(-Re s).

The cofactor is therefore nonzero throughout that entire half-plane at all heights.

In the weighted discrete measure algebra with norm `sum|b_r|r`, multiplicative convolution is submultiplicative. Hence

    nu=sum_(j>=0)(-R)^(star j),
    sum_r |nu_r|r <=1/(1-q_R)<20.

All nonidentity atoms have r>=3/2. Repeated labels are coalesced by signed summation, never deleted. Local finiteness of the inverse support is genuine: if a product of atoms is at most X, every atom is at most X, its integer numerator mn is at most 2X, and there are at most `log X/log(3/2)` factors. Thus the sum over r<=X is finite.

Let `M_tau(x)=sum a(n)g_tau(log(n/x))`. The cofactor multiplication means

    H2(x)-E2^g(x)=c2 [(1+R)*M_tau](x/2),

where `[R*M](y)=sum R_r M(y/r)`. Applying nu therefore gives the exact direction of the dilation in D25:

    M_tau(x)=c2^(-1)sum_r nu_r [H2(2x/r)-E2^g(2x/r)].

Absolute convergence can be checked without a formal inversion argument: M has at most linear growth, H2 at most polynomial/logarithmic growth, and their Gaussian left tails are uniform on bounded positive intervals. On `0<t<=T`, each is bounded by `C_T t^(-1)`. Thus at fixed x the nu field sums are bounded by a constant times `sum|nu_r|r`, and the double convolution is absolutely convergent by the product of the corresponding weighted norms. Inserting the coefficient identity for `nu*(1+R)` is legitimate.

For the finite version, `|e2(n)|<=4d3(n)n^(-2)` gives `E2^g(t)=O_epsilon(t^(-1+epsilon))` for every t>0. For 0<epsilon<1,

    sum_r |nu_r| |E2^g(2x/r)|
       <<x^(-1+epsilon) sum_r |nu_r|r^(1-epsilon)
       <<X^(-1+epsilon), X<=x<=2X.

For the omitted H2 part r>X, the argument t=2x/r lies below 4; the Gaussian left tail gives `|H2(t)|<=C/t` on `(0,4]`. Consequently

    sum_(r>X)|nu_r| |H2(2x/r)|
                     <=C/(2x) sum_(r>X)|nu_r|r=O(X^(-1)).

This proves D26 with its entire infinite complement. The r cutoff is applied to the fixed source H2, not to a source whose cutoff is frozen at the wrong x scale.

For odd-modulus ordinary characters the condition `|a(2)|=1` is automatic. For even moduli, the explicit repair a(2):=-1 changes F by the entire function `(chi(2)-1)2^(-s)=-2^(-s)`, retaining every pole and its principal part. The corresponding original physical field differs by one Gaussian atom, which is smaller than any power of X on `[X,2X]`. The repaired coefficients generally are not `mu(n)chi(n)` and their determinant must not use the unmodified D4 factorization; the author makes this distinction. The small-shift theorem and D20 use the original ordinary characters, without repair.

This anchor is an invertible filter of the original Gaussian arithmetic, not a proof of an improved moment. For example, at any fixed gamma>-1, a global power bound on H2 (with its harmless left tail) transfers to M through `sum|nu_r|r^(-gamma)<=20` and the paid E term. Conversely a bound on M transfers to H2 through the absolutely summable cofactor coefficients. An inverse formula alone cannot supply either improved bound, and delta=2 cannot be substituted for the required interval `[1/5,1/4]` without a new argument.

statement:
## 3. Two dilation filters, sharp frame constants and causal reconstruction

Fix beta<gamma, preferably with a fixed positive gap. For lambda=2 or 3 set

    D_lambda F(x)=F(x)−lambda^beta F(x/lambda),
    d_lambda(s)=1−lambda^(beta−s).                         (H7)

On Re s=a>beta let r_lambda=lambda^(beta−a), q_lambda=1−r_lambda. Then

    q_lambda <= |d_lambda(a+i y)| <= 1+r_lambda.

Each individual filter is already nonzero in Re s>beta. Its zeros lie on Re s=beta. The common zeros of d_2,d_3 consist only of s=beta, since a nonzero common imaginary part would imply 2^m=3^n for nonzero integers. This common-zero observation is valid, but it adds no zero coverage in our target half-plane: either filter already covers it.

On L²_a define A_beta F=(D_2F,D_3F). Plancherel, including arbitrary H fibers, gives the exact frame inequalities

    A(a,beta)||F||² <= ||A_beta F||² <= B(a,beta)||F||²,
    A=q_2²+q_3²,
    B=(1+r_2)²+(1+r_3)².                                 (H8)

The constants are sharp as operator bounds. The lower symbol value occurs at frequency zero; the upper supremum is B by irrationality of log 2/log 3 and density of the corresponding phases. Equality need not be attained by a nonzero L² function.

There is an explicit left inverse using only past scales, not deconvolution of a smoothing kernel:

    E_lambda G(x)=sum_(j>=0) lambda^(j beta) G(x/lambda^j),
    ||E_lambda||_(L²_a)<=q_lambda^(−1),
    w_lambda=q_lambda²/A,
    R_a(G_2,G_3)=w_2 E_2G_2+w_3 E_3G_3.                  (H9)

Then R_a A_beta=I and ||R_a||_(L²_a(H²)→L²_a(H))=A^(−1/2). The proof is the convergent geometric inverse for each translation, followed by Cauchy–Schwarz:

    sum_lambda |w_lambda/d_lambda(s)|²
       <= sum_lambda q_lambda²/A² =1/A.

At zero frequency equality holds. The multipliers w_lambda/d_lambda(s) are holomorphic for Re s>beta, so this reconstruction also respects the analytic Mellin identity. The frequently used canonical frame inverse, conjugate(d)/sum|d|² on one vertical line, need not furnish this holomorphic extension; H9 does.

For physical fields, the telescoping boundary lambda^(J beta)F(x/lambda^J) vanishes: eventually exactly for compact fields, and rapidly for Gaussian fields. Thus H9 reconstructs them even when global target integrability is what is being proved. On all-shell norms, N_a(E_lambda G)<=q_lambda^(−1)N_a(G); consequently

    N_a(R_a G)<= A^(−1/2)
       [N_a(G_2)²+N_a(G_3)²]^(1/2)
       <= sqrt(2/A) N_a^bank(G).                          (H10)

Here N_a^bank uses the joint H² shell norm. The last sqrt(2) accounts for component suprema possibly occurring at different shells; the sharp global L² constant must not be silently asserted for a shell supremum. This harmless fixed factor does not alter an exponent. Fixed beta and any fixed reconstruction weights summing to one give a causal identity; choosing weights at a chosen a optimizes its global bound.

For delta=a−beta→0+, A=delta²[(log2)²+(log3)²]+O(delta³). Thus the frame inverse costs approximately 1/[delta sqrt((log2)²+(log3)²)]. A product D_2D_3 instead costs 1/(q_2q_3), of order delta^(−2). A fixed bank is better conditioned than this serial product, but no exponent saving follows from that fixed constant. Choosing beta within X^(−kappa) of a would incur an X^kappa bank cost, or X^(2kappa) for the product, and would also change the source with X. Keep beta fixed. At a=.874864 and beta=.75 the receipt evaluates these constants explicitly.

All filters act in scale, independently of t. They preserve the exact coefficients, excluded-prime convention and phase parameter. They do not turn the phase into a Hecke twist on the squarefree factor.

## Sextic rectangle candidate: exact, but insufficient

sextic_optimization tested a coefficient-specific multiplicative
rectangle; review_sextic independently checked the identity and
the failed transfer. For the actual f=conjugate(alpha)gamma2 nu,
B1.11 gives f(ax)=f(a)f(x)chi_x(a)^4. Thus, when a,b,x,y are
squarefree good and all four cross pairs are coprime,

\[
f(ax)f(by)\overline{f(ay)f(bx)}
=K(a,x)\overline{K(b,x)}K(b,y)\overline{K(a,y)},
\quad K(a,x)=\chi_x(a)^4.
\]

No coprimality within (a,b) or (x,y) is needed. Same row/mark and
short-divisor phases cancel on units; their collision zeros remain.
Mixed row/mark pairs leave the separated phase
Omega(x)conjugate(Omega(y)), with
Omega=chi_R^3 chi_R'^(-3) chi_P^(-2) chi_Q^2.
There is no residual quadratic reciprocity sign.

For fixed Cartesian squarefree sets of lengths M,X and nonnegative
weights w_a,v_x<=1, the existing cubic large sieve gives

\[
\sum_{a,b}w_aw_b
\left|\sum_xv_xK(a,x)\overline{K(b,x)}\right|^2
\ll (MX)^\epsilon MX\{M+X+(MX)^{2/3}\}.
\]

Fix b, apply the sieve to v_x conjugate(K(b,x)), whose squared mass
is O(X), then sum O(M) rows b. The balanced M=X=N^(1/2) bound is
N^(5/3+epsilon). This is a complete rectangle, not an estimate for
the original signed two-column form with its two equality exclusions.

In a genuinely factorable marked Type II component, the reassembly
z=xP and divisor Cauchy give only

\[
|F_R^{\mathrm{II}}|^2
\ll Z^\epsilon N\{M+XL+(NL)^{2/3}\},\qquad MX=N.
\]

Summing rows leaves an unaffordable large factor beyond KN.
Balanced factorization also omits prime and unbalanced Type I
columns. The masks u!=v and Pu!=Qv provide no established inequality
transferring their signed energy to the rectangle. The candidate
therefore supplies no saving for H. Its other branches remain open.
No additional conditional H label or changed exponent certificate
is warranted.

\[
 \ell de\le e^\delta x\le2e^{9/8}X<8X.
 \tag{DPR11}
\]

Since ell>=1, this proves the fixed cap de<=8X, independently
of x before averaging. Both d and e are still greater than Y.
Extra pairs under that cap can be identically zero on part of
the shell; they must nevertheless keep their complete Poisson
series until a truncation error is paid.

Apply DPR8 separately to every pair under this finite cap,
with t=de/x. The outside factor is -x/(de), and the
argument of the Fourier transform is nu*x/(2de).
This proves DP28, including its sign, factor two in the
frequency denominator, both ordered factor positions and
every positive and negative odd frequency. No assertion
t<=delta is needed for this exact Poisson identity; that
inequality was needed only for the earlier Type I estimate.

For the full truncation, set
s_*=de/(X delta), beta_x=x/X and
L=X^tau max(1,s_*). Here e^(-1)<=beta_x<=2e.
The absolute omitted contribution for one pair is at most

\[
 \frac{C_B}{\delta s_*}
 \sum_{|\nu|>L}
       (1+c|\nu|/s_*)^{-B},
 \tag{DPR12}
\]

where the positive c is fixed over the whole shell. Extending
from odd frequencies to all integers only enlarges this
positive estimate. For sufficiently large X, L>=s_* and
L>=1. The integral test gives
sum_(|nu|>L) |nu|^(-B) <= C_B L^(1-B), with literal real
cutoffs handled by a fixed constant. Therefore DPR12 is at most

\[
 \begin{cases}
 C_B\delta^{-1}X^{-\tau(B-1)},&s_*\ge1,\\
 C_B\delta^{-1}s_*^{B-1}X^{-\tau(B-1)},&0<s_*<1.
 \end{cases}
 \tag{DPR13}
\]

The second extra factor is at most one. This calculation shows
where the apparent factor de disappears; it is not hidden in
a uniform Fourier estimate. There are at most
sum_(d<=8X) floor(8X/d)=O(X log(2X)) ordered pairs under
the cap, even before d,e>Y and the Mobius zeros are imposed.
Also delta_X^(-1)<=X^eta. Summing DPR13 gives

\[
 C_B X^{1+\eta-\tau(B-1)}\log(2X).
 \tag{DPR14}
\]

For a requested R, choose a fixed B with
tau(B-1)>R+2+eta. This is O_R(X^(-R)) after all pairs
and all omitted frequencies are summed. Constants may
depend on the fixed tau. The cutoff itself satisfies
L<=8X^tau/delta_X up to a fixed constant, since de<=8X,
and thus has the stated range O(X^(eta+tau)).
The use of X instead of the integration variable x in
the cutoff is harmless because beta_x stays in a fixed
positive compact interval.

Finally u=e^(delta v), du=delta e^(delta v)dv, gives

\[
 \widehat V_\delta(\xi)
   =\int_{-1}^1 k(v)e^{\delta v}
                  e^{-2\pi i\xi e^{\delta v}}\,dv.
 \tag{DPR15}
\]

The original delta^(-1) amplitude cancels precisely this
Jacobian delta. DP30 therefore has neither a missing width
factor nor a wrong phase. Since the profile is real,
the negative-frequency terms are the conjugates of the
positive-frequency terms. This does not remove their
arithmetic cancellation obligation.

The absence of a zero frequency in one alternating
restoration sum does not exclude opposite-frequency
resonances after two such sums are multiplied in the
energy. All those products remain in DPR16--OPEN;
no mean-zero-to-small-energy inference is made.

DP28 with the cutoff DP29 is consequently equivalent,
up to an arbitrarily small uniform power error, to the
same F_(A,delta_X) in OPEN-DP. The omitted Type I and
frequency errors are uniform before integration.
They also remain negligible in the energy: the norm
triangle inequality suffices, and the errors can be made
smaller than any requested power. No pointwise bound on
an unestimated reciprocal sum is needed to justify that
norm comparison.

statement:
## 3. Survivors11/22: an exact signed Walsh codec with a paid tail

### 3.1 Actual prime law and orthogonal coefficients

Let P be any finite set containing2 and excluding3. Put Q=product_(p in P)p,

    a_P(n)=product_(p in P)(1-2*1_(p|n)),
    r_P(n)=f3(n)a_P(n), R_(P,chi)(u)=sum_n r_P(n)chi(n)g_tau(log n-u).

Thus f3=a_P r_P pointwise, |r_P chi|<=1 and r_P(pn)=r_P(n) for p in P, including all powers. Let pi be the product law of B_p with q_p=1/p. Define

    Z_p=(B_p-q_p)/sqrt(q_p(1-q_p)),
    m_p=1-2q_p, v_p=2sqrt(q_p(1-q_p)), Z_S=product_(p in S)Z_p.

Then the exact Boolean identity is

    a_P(B)=sum_(S subset P) A_S Z_S,
    A_S=(-1)^|S| product_(p in S)v_p product_(p notin S)m_p. (C1)

The Z_S are an orthonormal basis under pi, and sum A_S^2=1. Since m_2=0 and v_2=1, A_S=0 unless2 is in S. Positive-prime-power occupancy is used; the squarefree law1/(p+1) is not used.

For an integer D>=0 set q_D(B)=sum_(|S|<=D)A_S Z_S. The exact discarded squared norm is

    rho_D^2=E_pi |a_P-q_D|^2=Pr(K>D),
    K=sum_(p in P) Y_p, Pr(Y_p=1)=nu_p=4(p-1)/p^2.     (C2)

The Y_p are independent auxiliary Bernoulli variables encoding coefficient ENERGY, not a claim that the arithmetic tail is random. In particular Y_2=1 deterministically. If lambda=sum nu_p and D+1>=lambda, its elementary exponential-moment bound is

    rho_D^2 <= (e lambda/(D+1))^(D+1).                (C3)

Indeed E exp(tK)=product(1+nu_p(e^t-1))<=exp(lambda(e^t-1)); use t=log((D+1)/lambda), then drop the extra exp(-lambda). The exact finite Poisson-binomial tail is available and often sharper.

### 3.2 Full integer projection and exact dilation realization

Let Z(u)=sum_n g_tau(log n-u), and let mu_u(n)=g_tau(log n-u)/Z(u). Under the already proved full-pattern CRT theorem (W41 B2), for a moving P=P_X with Q<=X^(1-delta), fixed delta>0, the occupancy law under mu_u has L1 distance epsilon_X=O_(A,delta,tau)(X^-A) from pi, uniformly for u in[log X,log(2X)]. All patterns, including rare ones, are included. Z(u)=exp(tau/2)e^u+O_A(X^-A).

The pointwise identity sum_S Z_S(B)^2=1/pi(B)<=Q and Cauchy give |q_D(B)|<=sqrt Q. Hence |a_P-q_D|^2<=4Q and the actual-law discarded energy is at most rho_D^2+4Q epsilon_X. Cauchy with |r_P chi|<=1 therefore proves the uniform, COMPLETE field comparison

    |F_chi(u)-F_(P,D,chi)(u)|
      <=Z(u)[rho_D+2sqrt(Q epsilon_X)],
    F_(P,D,chi)(u)=sum_n q_D(B(n))r_P(n)chi(n)g_tau(log n-u). (C4)

The source is constructive and retains all rough-tail signs. Define the exact dilation D_p V(u)=V(u-log p). Since r_P(pn)=r_P(n), divisibility gives

    sum_(p|n) r_P(n)chi(n)g_tau(log n-u)=chi(p)D_p R_(P,chi)(u).

Substitute this into C1 to obtain

    F_(P,D,chi)
      =sum_(|S|<=D) (-2)^|S| product_(p notin S)m_p
          product_(p in S)(chi(p)D_p-q_p I) R_(P,chi). (C5)

At D=|P| the polynomial factors exactly as product_(p in P)(I-2chi(p)D_p), and C5 equals the original F_chi. No prime power, character zero, Gaussian tail, shifted scale or negative cross term is deleted. At smaller D, C4 pays the full reconstruction error. Because every surviving S contains2, the coded field retains the exact factor I-2chi(2)D_2. Its P and D may move with X, so the zero return is through C4 and the ORIGINAL fixed F_chi, not a Mellin transform of a moving detector.

### 3.3 Error budget and surviving arithmetic target

For any desired gamma in(1/2,1), put c=1-gamma. Choose P_X and D_X with Q<=X^(1-delta) and

    Pr(K>D_X)<=X^(-2c-eta)                            (C6)

for a fixed eta>0. Then C4 has size O(X^(gamma-eta/2))+O_A(X^-A). Thus a complete shell bound ||F_(P,D,chi)||_2<<_epsilon X^(gamma+epsilon) is sufficient for the same original exponent gamma and its full zero exclusion.

A coarse explicit order suffices. If P is contained in primes<=z with z<=C log X, the elementary integer harmonic bound gives lambda<=4(1+log z)=O(loglog X). For any fixed eta>0,

    D_X=ceil((2c+eta) log X/loglog X)                  (C7)

makes C3 at most X^(-2c-eta+o(1)), so C6 holds with any smaller positive buffer, for example eta/2; if D_X>=|P| the error is simply zero. Near the current endpoint this coefficient is about.250278; for c=1/6 it is1/3, and for c=1/4 it is1/2. One must also select P to satisfy its literal Q bound; P may be fixed or the maximal prime prefix under that bound. C7 is a sufficient asymptotic bound, not a claim that a fixed small degree is adequate. The finite exact tail in C2 is the preferred constructive certificate.

To expose the rare22 drift, let m(B;u)=E_mu_u[r_P(n)chi(n)|B(n)=B], so |m|<=1. Up to the paid full-pattern error,

    F_chi/Z=sum_S A_S mhat_S,
    mhat_S=E_pi[m Z_S].                              (C8)

Degree truncation leaves the exact retained scalar sum_(|S|<=D) A_S mhat_S. Bounding its corresponding low-degree m-energy by X^(-2c+epsilon) would suffice by Cauchy. This is a deterministic signed conditional-response estimate, not a concentration conclusion. Coarse orthogonality gives only <=1 and hence field exponent1. The exact legal reference example m=a_P has norm1 and E_pi[a_P m]=1 despite independent exposed bits and E_pi a_P=0. Random revelation therefore does not create the required saving. C2–7 pay the CODEC error but leave its arithmetic retained response open.

Relative to W41 B1–6/G54, the new candidate delta is the explicit degree-energy law, certified truncation error and literal centered-dilation reconstruction. It does not replace the existing full covariance problem by exposed marginal independence. No claim of literature novelty is made for Walsh expansions, Chernoff bounds or sieve truncation.

# Mathematical proof handoff for external formalization

## User objective and division of work

On 12 October 2026 UTC the user requested a record-setting-ready mathematical
proof, especially after the candidate c6=.125139 is independently accepted,
while the other research lanes continue. The proof must attain the highest
validated c and select compatible components from recent versions to make
external formalization easier. The controller and **all its sub-agents are
expressly excluded from performing formalization**. This is a mathematical
proof-writing and handoff assignment, not a Lean implementation or replay job.

The user moving the laptop is not a pause. Preserve current work, ownership,
deadlines and completed handoffs through any interruption.

## Exact result to prepare

The current accepted written result is c5=7821/62500=.125136; its full new
formalization is pending. Candidate c6=125139/1000000=.125139 is under
independent analytic review and must not yet replace it. If accepted, its
zero-free boundary is theta=1-c6=874861/1000000=.874861. The record declaration
uses **theta**, not c. Both fractions are reduced.

The public comparison target is every natural modulus q with q nonzero,
every complex Dirichlet character modulo q, and every complex s with
theta<Re(s), retaining the exception not(chi=1 and s=1), for the actual
Dirichlet L-function. The proof must connect its definitions to that target,
including imprimitive characters, finite Euler factors and the s=1 cases.
The extra fixed trivial-infinity Eisenstein Hecke result must be stated
separately with its exact scope and retained credit.

Fixing each character before constants is compatible with this universal
statement. It does not excuse moving a common geometric saving or mesh past
the target in a global-supremum argument. Every such quantifier order must
be explicit. In particular, the norm-lift product argument must account for
a possible pole of the companion factor at s=1.

## Selection rule for the coherent proof

1. Preserve the highest completely validated endpoint; simplification cannot
   silently weaken c or strengthen a hypothesis.
2. Begin with the shortest complete chain of actual source estimates,
   density/marked descendants, physical return and zero exclusion. Reuse the
   pinned PR9 framework and Gao PR15 only through exact compatible contracts.
3. Prefer an older, simpler argument when it still proves the needed lemma at
   that endpoint. Keep only indispensable new source changes. State a direct
   interface lemma whenever definitions, normalizations or parameter ranges
   differ; a shared symbol or formal component is not sufficient compatibility.
4. Isolate finite rational inequalities from analytic arguments. Give exact
   ranges, constants, denominator positivity and complete complementary cases.
   Supply immutable certificates with a mathematical explanation of what they
   establish. Search output and a checked finite atlas do not prove an imported
   analytic estimate.
5. Present one forward proof, a dependency table with source pins, and a small
   list of external formalization obligations. Research history, stronger
   unused lemmas and speculative detectors remain in the library, linked from
   an appendix rather than required by the main theorem.
6. Keep mathematical acceptance, the external formalization, independent
   kernel verification, catalogue admission and a record claim distinct.

## Pinned admission contract supplied by the user

Source: [CONTRIBUTING.md at 3a24415f348af0f0a092064b30f0127c5ae7d096](https://github.com/GTimG/QuasiRiemannTracker/blob/3a24415f348af0f0a092064b30f0127c5ae7d096/CONTRIBUTING.md),
Git blob1447bfa5b0c8cd69e2cd86fb79ef37c1591f0196, retrieved through the
GitHub connector. The complete receipt is retained locally. The user requests
preparation to this contract; this source is not authority to submit or run it.

The active admission path requires an independent maintainer's offline Linux
run of the exact statements and definitions through Comparator and all three
kernels (Lean, NanoDa, con-ron), with only propext, Classical.choice and
Quot.sound permitted. The receipt binds the complete source, dependency and
checker pins, repository, PR number, exact head, stable result ID and exact
theta. Every changed head needs new independent admission. The described
signed service awaits commissioning and is not an available substitute.

The eventual record package needs accurate authorship, attribution, compatible
license and reproduction instructions, an immutable new proof snapshot, exact
bound and a correctly truncated decimal distinguishable from the strongest
then framework-verified entry. Existing proof snapshots and historical evidence
remain immutable. Proof/result changes and maintenance/admission infrastructure
changes belong to separate PRs. These are external handoff requirements;
neither a new PR nor a record-setting status is claimed or authorized here.

Before any eventual submission, its owner must recheck the live verified
frontier and admission rules. A better c than the present written baseline is
not itself evidence of a new independently verified public record.

## Present preparation state

C6=125139/1000000, theta6=874861/1000000, has been accepted after complete
independent and controller written review. The [source argument and evidence](gao-density-extension-integration.md)
are retained. The [component map](proof-component-selection/report.md)

250-cell prefix must be replaced where needed. The forward c6 proof is now
being assembled and independently compared for mathematical equivalence.
This brief records the delivery contract, not completed external formalization
or readiness for record admission.

Use the original sixth-power-free natural rows, all unit sectors, finite
dictionary, one complete orientation and original nonnegative row majorant.
The actual product Q_u of prime slots retains its canonical pools, relative
ray coefficients, smooth profiles, bounded real powers, independent heights,
fixed punctures and natural zeros. Shared primes are allowed. No new mask,
moving conductor or arbitrary inverse coefficient is licensed.

Set

    17/25 <= delta <= 7/10, a=(1+delta)/2, 0<=v<=1/20,
    K=28114053/6250000, t=33/25, lambda=1/2500,
    eta=1/1000, R=U^t, L=U^(t+lambda), Y=U^B.

K retains its preceding-family ancestry; it is not recomputed from c11.
The physical bin gives |Q_u|^2 << H_J U^(delta v+epsilon).
H_J denotes the retained finite seminorm and polynomial-height factors.
All numerical cutoffs precede live rows. Fixed inducing exceptions are
paid separately below.

For the original V, equal to one on [0,1] and zero on [2,infinity), put

    A_R(n)=sum_(d|n) mu(d)V(Nd/R),
    D_R,u(s)=sum_(Nn>R) phi_u(n)A_R(n)(Nn)^(-s)e^(-Nn/Y),
    P_R,u(s)=sum_(Nn>R) phi_u(n)A_R(n)(Nn)^(-s)
                                    e^(-Nn/Y)H(Nn/L),
    F_R,u=D_R,u-P_R,u,

where H is fixed, one on [0,1] and compactly supported. The character is
the actual attaining natural presentation. A principal inducing character
with extra zeros is not a nonprincipal presentation.

The completed identity from [restricted research revision] Section6 applies to every fixed bounded t:
at an actual nonprincipal zero, D_R,u(rho_u)=-1+O(U^(-A_tail)). Mellin
inversion of the exponential and a contour shift from 2 to -1/4 give this
identity. The Gamma residue at zero vanishes; no L-pole is crossed.
The finite inverse polynomial and ordinary Hecke strip bounds have fixed
polynomial costs, paid by choosing B afterward. The unit is e^(-1/Y)
before being isolated. The terminal cutoff at U^(B+1) and its finite
derivative tails are paid before raw row/slot amplification. This value
identity asserts no vanishing derivative at a zero.

For every nonunit ideal n, with no coprimality or squarefree assumption,

    A_R(n)=-sum_(dm=n) mu(d)[1-V(Nd/R)].                 (1)

The unit is excluded from (1). Thus P is an inverse sum with complementary
cofactor Nm << L/R. Define N0(P) as its complete positive tensor Sobolev
norm over the original free rows, real interval [a,1] and enlarged height
box, with derivatives partial_sigma^i partial_tau^j, i,j in {0,1}.
The fixed real width is bounded below. Then

    N0(P) << H_J U^(J_t+epsilon),
    J_t=1/6+(5/6-delta)t+(1-delta)lambda.               (2)

Here are the costs in (2). For a fixed cofactor m, inverse dyads have
R << D << L/Nm. Separate the coupled smooth profile on its full ambient
box before a live cofactor, row or height is chosen, as in PR9 B3.3.
Freeze the original R inside that profile during inverse-scale restoration.
The centrally normalized inverse moment is U^(1/6)D^(5/6+epsilon);
d^(-s) contributes D^(-delta) in its square. Since 5/6-delta>0,
Hilbert triangle over dyads is dominated by D~L/Nm. The outside character
is a contraction even at shared primes and natural zeros. The norm is at most

    H_J^(1/2) U^(1/12+epsilon)L^((5/6-delta)/2)
                 sum_(Nm<<L/R) (Nm)^(-11/12).

The exponent is exactly -a-(5/6-delta)/2=-11/12. Ideal counting including
the unit gives (L/R)^(1/12); squaring yields (2). Finite derivatives cost
logarithms and the same fixed height factors. No cofactor cancellation is
assumed. Positive evaluation bounds the rows with |P(rho_u)|>=1/4;
only afterward apply the physical slot bound. Their weighted count is
O(H_J U^(J_t+delta v+epsilon)). This is not a bound for the full marked
ambient norm with a cheaper coefficient than its licensed 5v/3.

Retain the [restricted research revision] density envelope

    h=5-2delta, rho=1-10delta/(3h), k=rho+delta-1,
    D_K=15K-10-6Kdelta,
    a_K=delta(5-6delta)^2/(3h D_K),
    b_K=2delta(5-6delta)(K-1)/D_K,
    G=min(3kv,a_K+b_K v), E_K=rho+delta v-G.

Throughout the closed delta/v rectangle,

    E_K-J_t-delta v > eta.                             (3)

It suffices to replace G by a_K+b_K/20. After subtracting eta and
multiplying by the positive 3h D_K, substitute delta=17/25+x/50.
The cubic Bernstein coefficients are

    31963522910683/488281250000000,
    51570739970441/146484375000000,
    2180434156111/3662109375000,
    97268801733/122070312500,

all positive. This is a continuous-interval argument, not a sampled grid.
The earlier t=4/3 failure at delta=17/25,v=1/20,lambda=0 remains
`-228190682/298987653375`. The replacement t pays this whole slot range

## Development23: source coefficients, exact dual and the surviving signed target

Set N=floor X, S={n<=N: mu(n)!=0, (n,q)=1}, E={n in S:n<=Y}, H=S\E, with1<=Y<=N/2. The unknown actual coefficients are a_d=mu(d)chi(d), d in H. The convolution a*chi=delta, with natural character zeros and all integer rows, gives on m in H

    sum_(d in H,d|m) chi(m/d)a_d = b_m,
    b_m = -sum_(d in E,d|m) mu(d)chi(d)chi(m/d).

The set H is order-convex inside divisor intervals: if d,m in H and d|k|m, then k in H. Consequently the square matrix Z_(m,d)=chi(m/d)1_(d|m) has the literal inverse W_(m,d)=mu(m/d)chi(m/d)1_(d|m): its product entry is chi(m/d)sum_(d|k|m)mu(k/d), equal to delta_(m,d). An arbitrary principal submatrix need not inherit an inverse; interval convexity supplies the justification here.

Its unique scalar dual is

    lambda_m = sum_(k<=N/m,(k,m)=1) mu(k)chi(k),
    M_chi(N)=M_chi(Y)+sum_(m in H) lambda_m b_m.          (R1)

The final pairing is bilinear, with no complex conjugation. The conjugate enters only the adversarial norm witness below. Squarefreeness removes k sharing a prime with m; chi removes every ramified prime. No correction is hidden in those masks. For Y=floor(sqrt N), every lambda argument is short, but the number, dependence and terminal values of the duals still matter.

There are two distinct unconditional price results.

1. Independent row errors eta_m in the square system have scalar norm sum_H|lambda_m| from ell-infinity to C. Equality is attained by eta_m=conj(lambda_m)/|lambda_m| when lambda_m!=0. Every squarefree q-unit m>N/2 has lambda_m=1. Thus the norm is at least kappa_q N/2+O_q(sqrt N) and at most N(1+log N). Its exponent is1, uniformly for Y<=N/2. Adding all squareful convolution rows up to N cannot remove the terminal price: a variable a_m with m>N/2 appears only in row m. Any exact linear certificate for the scalar sum must assign coefficient1 to that row. This conclusion concerns independent equation errors and the specified full-row linear formulation; it does not allow errors in the actual arithmetic source or exclude nonlinear restrictions on them.

2. On the actual source, define P_N=sum_H|lambda_m b_m|. Every unramified prime N/2<p<=N has lambda_p=1 and b_p=-chi(p), so P_N is at least the number of those primes. Also |b_m|<=tau(m), |lambda_m|<=N/m, giving P_N<=N(1+log N)^2. If P_N were O(N^alpha) for any fixed alpha<1 on all large N, its values at N=2^j would force convergence of sum_p1/p, a contradiction. It does not prove a pointwise order-N lower bound for every N, and it does not lower-bound the signed right side of (R1).

The possible growing-conductor objection is explicitly paid for the particular omissions at hand. For any m,

    lambda_m(T)=sum_(r<=T, p|r => p|m) chi(r) M_chi(T/r).  (R2)

All powers of primes dividing m occur in r; omitting them would be false. A fixed-character bound |M_chi(t)|<=C t^alpha, with fixed0<alpha<1, implies

    |lambda_m(T)| <= C T^alpha product_(p|m)(1-p^(-alpha))^(-1).

For m<=N the product is exp(O_alpha((log(2N))^(1-alpha)))=N^o(1). Split primes at log(2N), majorize small primes by all integers, and bound the number of large prime factors by log N/log2. The estimate is uniform in m; it uses no theorem uniform over arbitrary growing primitive moduli. This correct paid estimate still does not beat either complete absolute-price obstruction.

## 9. Endpoint interface: mesh before target, uniformity in live scales

**Classification: the required local uniformity is supported by the proof, subject to retaining the exact fixed-family scope. It does not prove the separate endpoint continuation.**

The potentially fatal order would be to choose the physical slot mesh only after the eventual target character's density height degree. The written proof does not need that order. Its low-branch positive margin `4M/225000`, high margin `M/100`, all three error margins and the comparison/exceptional margins are uniform on the fixed local window and contain no dictionary size or height degree. Choose a numerical error budget from these margins and `epsilon`, then the physical bin/slot mesh and canonical support reserves, before the eventual target family and finite slot list. One greedy prefix overshoot uses one mesh allowance. After the finite slot list is fixed its aggregate support tolerance tends to zero as `Z` grows; it is not a permanent loss charged per slot.

Only afterward fix the finite target dictionary and slot system, choose their density/profile height degrees, choose `tau_out` sufficiently small for those degrees and the fixed minimum positive width, choose Fourier-tail orders and the eventual threshold. All of these may depend on that fixed target/system. None changes the earlier positive slot widths or the final continuation strip. The density's *internal* detector mesh/exponent are auxiliary to its proof; they do not require resetting the original physical slots. A very small eventual `tau_out` merely raises the threshold and allowable finite orders.

For the endpoint lane's moving row exponent `d`, shift `t`, selected subsets, actual plain scales and relative slot widths `ell_i/d`, normalize the local theorem at `U=Z^d`, so `M=1`. The endpoint's retained `d` lies in a fixed compact interval bounded away from zero, the original finite positive slot widths are fixed, and therefore each surviving normalized `ell_i/d` lies in a compact positive interval. There are finitely many subsets, and the plain exponents and free shift range remain in the asserted bounded geometry. The source moment statements already quantify over profiles and scales with a common seminorm control. Natural fixed conductor padding, uniform polynomial-mask Euler bounds, common ambient Fourier boxes, bounded bin counts and bounded-exponent raw counts supply constants/orders/thresholds uniformly over these compact choices. Fix them **before** the live `d,t`, subsets, scales, masks and heights. A common `U0` translates to the common original threshold `Z>=U0^(1/d_min)`.

A pointwise assertion with one uncontrolled `Z0(d,t)` for each live pair would not suffice. This review does not endorse such an assertion: the normalization and the displayed uniform compact ranges are necessary. Likewise, the dictionary cannot grow with `Z`, `d`, a common-support label, or `w`; the signed-row reconstruction must keep all such arithmetic movement in the literal integer row and masks. The endpoint may choose constants after the target family, but cannot recompute its fixed exclusion ideal from a moving child anchor or select its original minimum width from that target.

## 3. W47-15: uniform growing depth, complete Gaussian restoration

Use arithmetic convolution *, identity δ, (\ell_\chi(n)=\chi(n)), and (m_Y(n)=\mu(n)\chi(n)\mathbf1_{n\le Y}), for one fixed integer Y≥2. In the Banach algebra
\[
 \|a\|_b=\sum_{n\ge1}|a(n)|n^{-b},\quad b>1,
\]
let (d_Y=\delta-\ell_\chi*m_Y=\ell_\chi*((\mu\chi)\mathbf1_{n>Y})). Choose Y so
\[
 \eta={\zeta(b)Y^{1-b}\over b-1}<1.
\]
Then — with actual zeros at every ramified prime —
\[
 \|d_Y\|_b\le\eta,\quad \|m_Y\|_b\le\zeta(b),\quad d_Y(n)=0\ (n\le Y).
\]
For every integer k≥1 define
\[
 Q_k=m_Y*(\delta+d_Y+\cdots+d_Y^{*(k-1)}).
\]
The exact identities are
\[
 \delta-\ell_\chi*Q_k=d_Y^{*k},\qquad
 \mu\chi-Q_k=(\mu\chi)*d_Y^{*k}. \tag{R7}
\]
Consequently equality with μχ holds **strictly below** ((Y+1)^k), and
\[
 \sup_k\|Q_k\|_b\le{\zeta(b)\over1-\eta},\qquad
 \sup_k\|\mu\chi-Q_k\|_b\le
 B_b:=\zeta(b)\left(1+{1\over1-\eta}\right). \tag{R8}
\]
The stronger decaying bound (\zeta(b)\eta^k) also follows from R7 but is unnecessary. (Q_k) is a finite polynomial in an **infinite Dirichlet series**, generally not a finite-support Dirichlet polynomial. All its coefficients remain in the physical readout.

For (N_X=2X\exp(C\sqrt{\log X})), take
\[
 k_X=\left\lfloor{\log N_X\over\log(Y+1)}\right\rfloor+1.
\]
This ensures the strict threshold is greater than (N_X), including exact integer-power cases. Newton doubling (P_0=m_Y), (P_{r+1}=2P_r-\ell_\chi*P_r*P_r) gives (P_r=Q_{2^r}). Replacing (k_X) by the least power of two at least (k_X) preserves R8. The number of formal Newton stages is (O(\log\log X)); no arithmetic-operation complexity claim follows.

Set (V_X(x)=\sum_n Q_{k_X}(n)g_\tau(\log(n/x))), with the power-of-two option equally valid. For x∈[X,2X], full tail support and R8 give
\[
 |U_\chi(x)-V_X(x)|\le B_b\sup_{n\ge N_X}n^b g_\tau(\log(n/x)).
\]
For large X the exponent (bv-v^2/(2\tau)) decreases for (v\ge C\sqrt{\log X}\ge b\tau), whence
\[
 \sup_{X\le x\le2X}|U_\chi(x)-V_X(x)|
 \ll_{b,Y,C,\tau}X^{b-C^2/(2\tau)}e^{bC\sqrt{\log X}}
 =X^{b-C^2/(2\tau)+o(1)}. \tag{R9}
\]
This prices **all** n, not an arbitrary hard truncation of (Q_k). Weighted absolute convergence also proves each physical readout is well-defined. If (b-C^2/(2\tau)<\gamma), triangle inequalities in both directions prove that the complete shell estimates R2 for (V_X) and U are equivalent, with all ε buffers. Return to the fixed U before applying R3; the Mellin transform of a varying (V_X) is not a substitute.

The concrete constants are valid: b=2, Y=4 give (\zeta(2)<2), η<1/2, “Q norm <4” and (B_b<6), uniformly in k and χ. Choosing (C=\sqrt{3\tau}) makes R9 (X^{1/2+o(1)}), sufficient for every fixed γ>1/2. The actual initial coefficients are (1,-\chi(2),-\chi(3),0) at 1,2,3,4. Character zeros do not invalidate the endpoint support statement; they can make a specific first eligible coefficient vanish.

This does not contradict the old absolute-norm failure at exponents ≤1. For a nonzero finite preconditioner M, let d₀ be its least nonzero index and take unramified primes p beyond its support. At d₀p, the residual coefficient is (-M(d_0)\chi(p)): all smaller divisors have zero coefficient. Thus its absolute σ-norm diverges for σ≤1. This does not bound a signed physical readout. The present proof uses fixed b>1 and lets the Gaussian tail pay the gap to γ<1.

Ancestry is exact: matched-Astra section AH12/formula AH20 already contains Newton's inverse algebra and strict prefix; [restricted research revision]-W2/W43.2--4 already contains the truncated-prefix geometric identity, fixed-k rough-coefficient obstruction and opposite support regime. **The increment is R8 uniformly in depth plus R9 and its full fixed-source return**, not the algebra. W43's fixed-k absolute lower bound does not remain a growing-k contradiction with constants suppressed. No γ<.874861 estimate for V is provided. The existing arithmetic question has a concrete new representation and a paid tail, not a weaker proved hypothesis.
