## 2. Development04: unsmoothed energy and a full character return

Fix an ordinary Dirichlet character chi modulo q, extended by zero exactly on nonunits, and put a(n)=mu(n)chi(n). Complete multiplicativity, including zero values, gives

    (a*chi)(n)=chi(n) sum_(d|n) mu(d)=delta_(n=1).        (E1)

Let M_chi(x)=sum_(n<=x)a(n), and for every real X>=1 define

    E_chi(X)=integral_1^X |M_chi(x)|^2 dx/x
      =sum_(m,n<=X) a(m) conjugate(a(n))
                            log(X/max(m,n)).            (E2)

Proof: the pair (m,n) is present exactly when x>=max(m,n). The finite integral of its indicator is the displayed logarithm. Integer upper endpoints have zero weight when max(m,n)=X; no half-weight convention occurs. The terminal log X contribution is part of E2. The pair kernel is a positive Gram kernel, but its signed off-diagonal summands need not be positive.

**Energy-to-zero-exclusion theorem.** Suppose 0<gamma<1 is common to all ordinary characters and, for each fixed chi and every epsilon>0,

    E_chi(X) <= C_(chi,epsilon) X^(2gamma+epsilon)       (E3)

for all sufficiently large real X (or merely all sufficiently large dyadic X, by positivity/monotonicity). Then L(s,chi) has no zeros in Re(s)>gamma. Principal poles retain their usual separate meaning. Constants and thresholds may depend on chi; no growing-conductor uniformity is assumed.

Proof: H_chi(s)=integral_1^infinity M_chi(x)x^(-s)dx/x. On a compact subset with Re(s)>=sigma0>gamma, choose 0<epsilon<2(sigma0-gamma). Cauchy–Schwarz on [2^j,2^(j+1)] bounds the absolute integral, including any fixed number k of s-derivatives, by

    O_(chi,epsilon,k)( (j+1)^k
                       2^(j(gamma+epsilon/2-sigma0)) ).

Its sum converges locally uniformly. Thus H_chi is holomorphic on Re(s)>gamma. Absolute summation first gives sH_chi(s)=1/L(s,chi) on Re(s)>1, since integral_n^infinity x^(-s)dx/x=n^(-s)/s. Meromorphic continuation of L and the identity theorem give

    L(s,chi) sH_chi(s)=1                               (E4)

throughout the connected half-plane, with the principal pole treated meromorphically. A zero of L there contradicts E4 because sH_chi is holomorphic and s!=0. Every finite height belongs to this open half-plane; no unproved uniform moving-height estimate is used. Natural imprimitive Euler factors were never stripped from a or L. This proves the theorem.

Extracting a pointwise bound from E3 using only |a|<=1 generally loses an exponent; this proof does not perform that extraction. It returns directly to a reciprocal L-function. Conversely a complete Mertens bound at gamma trivially supplies E3. I do not claim a new equivalence theorem beyond these two stated implications.

There is an exact fixed-modulus version of the high-ceiling trace idea. For all phi(q) characters modulo one FIXED q, orthogonality gives

    Ebar_q(X)=(1/phi(q)) sum_(chi mod q) E_chi(X)
      =sum_(m,n<=X; (mn,q)=1; m==n mod q)
                   mu(m)mu(n) log(X/max(m,n)).           (E5)

This retains all characters, including imprimitive ones and the principal character. It is an exact finite-family positive average, not an average over growing moduli or a statement about most characters. Each E_chi<=phi(q) Ebar_q. Consequently an E3-type bound for Ebar_q for EVERY FIXED q with one common gamma suffices for EVERY FIXED chi; the factor phi(q) is an allowed constant.

The literal diagonal is

    D_q(X)=sum_(n<=X;(n,q)=1)mu(n)^2 log(X/n)=O_q(X).    (E6)

One can sharpen this elementarily to D_q(X)=d_q X+O_q(sqrt(X)+1), with d_q=(phi(q)/q) product_(p not dividing q)(1-p^(-2))>0, by inserting mu(n)^2=sum_(d^2|n)mu(d), counting units, and integrating their O_q(sqrt X) summatory error. An additive constant can be absorbed into the error. This sharpening is not needed for the bridge.

Thus a precise remaining input, sufficient whenever gamma>1/2, is

    OFF_q(X):=sum_(m!=n<=X; (mn,q)=1; m==n mod q)
              mu(m)mu(n) log(X/max(m,n))
       <= C_(q,epsilon) X^(2gamma+epsilon)              (E7)

for every fixed q, every epsilon>0 and all large X. There is no absolute value inside the signed sum and no deletion of negative terms. E7 is OPEN. At q=1 it already contains the unsolved complete Möbius energy, so this finite-family repair creates no free cancellation.

Calibration: a first gain requires 2gamma<1.749720=43743/25000. Targets c=1/6 and 1/4 require gamma=5/6 and 3/4, hence squared-energy exponents 5/3 and 3/2. The elementary absolute bound E_chi(X)<= (X^2-1)/2 leaves a first-gain saving strictly greater than .250280 in the squared exponent. These are sufficient budgets, not achieved estimates. No numerical experiment is being counted as a reduction of that gap.

The finite check uses the genuinely complex order-four character modulo 5, including its zeros, at N=60. It compares exact integer coefficients of every log j in E2 with the integral of the step function: all 3,600 ordered pairs agree, including terminal log60 coefficient 13. This checks indexing only.

# W45: signed geometric means and an exact prime-state codec

Final author report under owned scope; source-relative c6=.125139 is unchanged. No formalization, kernel work, canonical edits or tracker/Git mutations were performed. Deadline 2026-10-12T03:45:00Z. This report is evidence for independent review, not acceptance of a new zero-free constant.

## 1. Frozen scope and allocation

The recipe is `[restricted provenance path] mathematical source]`, SHA256 `21d22f84783cf65c52fcb7f4c3ec5cb7822db66760d2c05ead0721a027e792b8`. All30 cards were frozen before reading old research: `seeds.json`, SHA256 `44daac36603a32f0d97364e762779095c3a536a88d0e6185be7dde65c640e363`. The six groups and all original uncalibrated typicality labels remain intact. The free groups include numerically rare cards and are included in the strict-threshold pools.

Deterministic reservations19 (bridge),03 (high reach),11 (different mechanism) were saved before drawing. The21-member p<.1 pool selected22 at zero-based rank12; the13-member remaining p<.01 pool selected20 at rank3; the25-member wildcard pool selected02 at rank1. Each exact pool was serialized/read/hashed before its draw, and all256-bit RNG outputs and rejection boundaries are retained. There were no rejections or rerolls. `first-tests.md` retains all six outcomes. Development lines are19;11+protected rare22;03+protected rare20. Wildcard02 has an exact local pole-order result only.

The true coefficient is f3(n)=mu(rad(n/3^v3(n))). Thus f3(p^k)=-1 for every k>=1 and p!=3, while f3(3^k)=1. It is neither squarefree-supported nor completely multiplicative. The fixed complete field is

    F_chi(u)=sum_(n>=1) f3(n) chi(n) g_tau(log n-u),
    g_tau(v)=(2pi tau)^(-1/2) exp(-v^2/(2tau)), tau>0 fixed.

Ordinary characters are fixed and retain chi(n)=0 at ramified n. No growing-conductor or ideal analogue is inferred from integer CRT. The existing full Gaussian return is current-proof G1–3,G25–31; the literal fixed-character numerator is also derived in Section2 below.

## 2. Survivor19: a signed geometric-mean return

### 2.1 A local logarithmic comparison, with a proof

Let I be any real interval of length1, let t0 in I, and let f be analytic on a neighborhood of the closed disk |z-t0|<=R, R>=16. Assume f(t0)!=0, choose B>=sup_disk |f|, and let M=|f(t0)|. If there are no boundary zeros, then

    integral_I log|f(t)|dt
      >= log M - (8/log R) log(B/M).                    (L1)

Boundary zeros are avoided by choosing a nearby radius; the application below permits any R in a whole growing interval. Interior real zeros have integrable logarithmic singularities. The identically-zero case is excluded by f(t0)!=0.

Translate t0 to0 and set h=f/f(t0), A=log(B/M)>=0. Then v=A-log|h| is a nonnegative superharmonic function in the disk, with v(0)=A. Its elementary disk factorization/Poisson formula is

    v(z)=H(z)+sum_a G_R(z,a),
    G_R(z,a)=log|(R^2-conj(a)z)/(R(z-a))|,              (L2)

where a runs through zeros with multiplicity and H is the positive harmonic extension of the nonnegative boundary values of v. This identity follows by removing each disk Blaschke factor, then applying the harmonic Poisson formula to the nonvanishing quotient. There are finitely many zeros in the closed disk. No external estimate is imported.

For a positive harmonic function on the disk, the explicit Poisson kernel gives H(t)<=((R+1)/(R-1))H(0) for |t|<=1. This factor is at most1+8/log R.

For |a|<=sqrt R, subtraction at0 gives

    G_R(t,a)-G_R(0,a)
      =log|1-conj(a)t/R^2|+log|a|-log|t-a|.

The first term is at most R^(-3/2). If |a|<=2, the integral of -log|t-a| over any unit interval is at most1+log2: removing Im(a) only increases it, and the largest real logarithmic potential is obtained when Re(a) is at the interval midpoint. Thus the integrated difference is less than4. If |a|>2, the triangle inequality bounds the second difference pointwise by log2, again giving less than4. Meanwhile G_R(0,a)=log(R/|a|)>=.5 log R. Hence

    integral_I G_R(t,a)dt <= (1+8/log R)G_R(0,a).

For |a|>sqrt R, G_R(.,a) is positive harmonic in |z|<sqrt R. Its Poisson-kernel bound is (sqrt R+1)/(sqrt R-1)<=1+8/log R for R>=16. Integrating L2 now gives integral_I v<=(1+8/log R)v(0), which is L1. This proof does not assume a zero separation or multiplicity bound.

### 2.2 Applying L1 to the COMPLETE Gaussian

For any coefficients with A_b=sum |a_n|n^-b<infinity at a fixed b>0, the completed square yields the entire bound

    |sum a_n g_tau(log n-z)|
      <= (2pi tau)^(-1/2) A_b
          exp(b Re z+tau b^2/2+(Im z)^2/(2tau)).       (L3)

For f3*chi take any b>1; all coefficients have modulus at most1. Let

    M_j=max_(u in[j,j+1]) |F_chi(u)|,
    J_j=integral_j^(j+1) log|F_chi(u)|du.              (L4)

The field is nonzero (its Mellin transform is nonzero on an absolute-convergence line), so M_j>0. Choose t0 at a maximizer and a radius R_j in[sqrt j,2sqrt j] containing no boundary zero. L3 bounds log B_j<=(b+2/tau)j+O_(b,tau,a)(sqrt j+1). With eta_j=8/log R_j=O(1/log j), L1 gives the exact inequality

    (1+eta_j) log M_j <= J_j+eta_j log B_j.            (L5)

Consequently, for every fixed gamma, the following EVERY-interval statements are equivalent:

    (i) J_j <= (gamma+epsilon)j+C_epsilon
        for every epsilon>0 and every sufficiently large integer j;
    (ii) M_j <<_epsilon exp((gamma+epsilon)j).          (L6)

The reverse implication is immediate. For the forward implication insert(i) into L5; its extra term is O(j/log j)=o(j), with every buffer fixed before j grows. Negative logarithms near real zeros are retained and cannot hide a larger exponential maximum. Missing intervals and finite numerical samples do not satisfy(i).

This supplies the nonconcentration condition absent from the earlier logarithmic-action card W21-T29, for this fixed Gaussian analytic class. It is stronger in input form than the positive logarithmic criterion: no log(1+|F|) or truncation of negative logarithms is required. It does not assert that a bound for a finite truncated field passes through log near its zeros.

### 2.3 Complete return, thresholds and remaining arithmetic

For Re s>1 absolute Fubini gives

    integral_R F_chi(u)e^(-su)du
      =exp(tau s^2/2) D_chi(s),
    D_chi(s)=N_chi(s) H_chi(s)/L(s,chi),
    N_chi(s)=1-2chi(2)2^-s.                            (L7)

For z=chi(p)p^-s, the local H factors are (1-z)^-2 at p=2,3 and (1-2z)/(1-z)^2 at p>=5. At a ramified prime z=0 exactly. Both H and H^-1 converge absolutely on each fixed half-plane Re s>=sigma>1/2, because the large-prime factors start with z^2 and2/sqrt5<1. N has no zeros in1/2<Re s<1; if2 is ramified it is1. The fixed Gaussian exponential never vanishes.

Under L6 with gamma>1/2, the right u-tail makes L7 holomorphic for Re s>gamma. The left Gaussian tail is paid exactly as in G2, including all fixed s-derivatives on compacta. Multiply by L and continue the identity. Any zero with gamma<Re s<1 would force the nonzero numerator N H exp(tau s^2/2) to vanish, including multiple zeros. The known right edge supplies the remaining boundary. Each fixed character requires its own L6; no average over characters substitutes for it.

Thus the complete new input is the signed geometric-mean bound L6(i) for every large unit log interval. Any gamma<.874861 gives a first gain, gamma=5/6 gives c=1/6, and gamma=3/4 gives c=1/4. The analytic return loses only o(j), so a coarse upper bound on J_j/j below.874861 would suffice even in a route aspiring to3/4. No such arithmetic bound is proved. The trivial absolute Gaussian estimate gives J_j<=j+O(1); the accepted buffered calibration only reproduces the existing endpoint. A fixed empirical mean or an assertion that most signs are random pays none of the required gap.

The same analytic L1–6 lemma applies to any fixed complete ideal Gaussian for which an absolute norm series and its original pole bridge have separately been established. This is an analytic conditional interface, not an integer-CRT proof for ideals.

### 2.4 A finite upper certificate that does not ignore zeros or tails

There is a direct constructive form of L6(i). For integer N>=exp(j+1), let F_N retain precisely n<=N. The decreasing positive tail and t=exp(v) give the explicit uniform bound on I_j=[j,j+1]

    |F-F_N|<=T_(N,j)
      =exp(j+1+tau/2) barPhi((log N-j-1-tau)/sqrt tau), (L8)

where barPhi is the standard normal upper tail. This bound applies to every fixed ordinary chi because |f3 chi|<=1. Choose any certified T>=T_(N,j), T>0. Then log|F|<=log(|F_N|+T), even at zeros. For b>1, differentiating the Gaussian and completing the square gives

    sup_Ij |F_N'|<=K_j,
    K_j=(2pi tau)^(-1/2)(1+1/(b-1))
        exp(b(j+1)+tau b^2/2)[b+1/sqrt(e tau)].        (L9)

Here sum n^-b<=1+1/(b-1), and sup_w |w|exp(-w^2/(2tau))=sqrt(tau/e). Consequently log(|F_N|+T) is K_j/T-Lipschitz, also through zeros. At the M equal-subinterval midpoints u_k, if a numerical enclosure has |F_N(u_k)-v_k|<=delta_k, then the rigorous one-sided certificate is

    J_j <= (1/M)sum_k log(|v_k|+delta_k+T)+K_j/(4MT). (L10)

No interchange of log and a small additive error is assumed. Taking N=ceil(exp(j+1+C sqrt j)) with C^2/(2tau)>1-gamma+eta allows the deliberately coarser T=exp((gamma-eta)j) for all sufficiently large j; choose a strict extra margin in C if needed. With M>=exp((b-gamma+2eta)j), the quadrature error is O(exp(-eta j)). This is a finite per-interval algorithm and an explicit full error budget. It is not a proof that its arithmetic upper certificate is <=(gamma+epsilon)j for every large j. A finite run proves only its inspected intervals.

## 3. Survivors11/22: an exact signed Walsh codec with a paid tail

### 3.1 Actual prime law and orthogonal coefficients

Let P be any finite set containing2 and excluding3. Put Q=product_(p in P)p,

    a_P(n)=product_(p in P)(1-2*1_(p|n)),
    r_P(n)=f3(n)a_P(n), R_(P,chi)(u)=sum_n r_P(n)chi(n)g_tau(log n-u).

Thus f3=a_P r_P pointwise, |r_P chi|<=1 and r_P(pn)=r_P(n) for p in P, including all powers. Let pi be the product law of B_p with q_p=1/p. Define

    Z_p=(B_p-q_p)/sqrt(q_p(1-q_p)),
    m_p=1-2q_p, v_p=2sqrt(q_p(1-q_p)), Z_S=product_(p in S)Z_p.

Then the exact Boolean identity is

    a_P(B)=sum_(S subset P) A_S Z_S,
    A_S=(-1)^|S| product_(p in S)v_p product_(p notin S)m_p. (C1)

The Z_S are an orthonormal basis under pi, and sum A_S^2=1. Since m_2=0 and v_2=1, A_S=0 unless2 is in S. Positive-prime-power occupancy is used; the squarefree law1/(p+1) is not used.

For an integer D>=0 set q_D(B)=sum_(|S|<=D)A_S Z_S. The exact discarded squared norm is

    rho_D^2=E_pi |a_P-q_D|^2=Pr(K>D),
    K=sum_(p in P) Y_p, Pr(Y_p=1)=nu_p=4(p-1)/p^2.     (C2)

The Y_p are independent auxiliary Bernoulli variables encoding coefficient ENERGY, not a claim that the arithmetic tail is random. In particular Y_2=1 deterministically. If lambda=sum nu_p and D+1>=lambda, its elementary exponential-moment bound is

    rho_D^2 <= (e lambda/(D+1))^(D+1).                (C3)

Indeed E exp(tK)=product(1+nu_p(e^t-1))<=exp(lambda(e^t-1)); use t=log((D+1)/lambda), then drop the extra exp(-lambda). The exact finite Poisson-binomial tail is available and often sharper.

### 3.2 Full integer projection and exact dilation realization

Let Z(u)=sum_n g_tau(log n-u), and let mu_u(n)=g_tau(log n-u)/Z(u). Under the already proved full-pattern CRT theorem (W41 B2), for a moving P=P_X with Q<=X^(1-delta), fixed delta>0, the occupancy law under mu_u has L1 distance epsilon_X=O_(A,delta,tau)(X^-A) from pi, uniformly for u in[log X,log(2X)]. All patterns, including rare ones, are included. Z(u)=exp(tau/2)e^u+O_A(X^-A).

The pointwise identity sum_S Z_S(B)^2=1/pi(B)<=Q and Cauchy give |q_D(B)|<=sqrt Q. Hence |a_P-q_D|^2<=4Q and the actual-law discarded energy is at most rho_D^2+4Q epsilon_X. Cauchy with |r_P chi|<=1 therefore proves the uniform, COMPLETE field comparison

    |F_chi(u)-F_(P,D,chi)(u)|
      <=Z(u)[rho_D+2sqrt(Q epsilon_X)],
    F_(P,D,chi)(u)=sum_n q_D(B(n))r_P(n)chi(n)g_tau(log n-u). (C4)

The source is constructive and retains all rough-tail signs. Define the exact dilation D_p V(u)=V(u-log p). Since r_P(pn)=r_P(n), divisibility gives

    sum_(p|n) r_P(n)chi(n)g_tau(log n-u)=chi(p)D_p R_(P,chi)(u).

Substitute this into C1 to obtain

    F_(P,D,chi)
      =sum_(|S|<=D) (-2)^|S| product_(p notin S)m_p
          product_(p in S)(chi(p)D_p-q_p I) R_(P,chi). (C5)

At D=|P| the polynomial factors exactly as product_(p in P)(I-2chi(p)D_p), and C5 equals the original F_chi. No prime power, character zero, Gaussian tail, shifted scale or negative cross term is deleted. At smaller D, C4 pays the full reconstruction error. Because every surviving S contains2, the coded field retains the exact factor I-2chi(2)D_2. Its P and D may move with X, so the zero return is through C4 and the ORIGINAL fixed F_chi, not a Mellin transform of a moving detector.

### 3.3 Error budget and surviving arithmetic target

For any desired gamma in(1/2,1), put c=1-gamma. Choose P_X and D_X with Q<=X^(1-delta) and

    Pr(K>D_X)<=X^(-2c-eta)                            (C6)

for a fixed eta>0. Then C4 has size O(X^(gamma-eta/2))+O_A(X^-A). Thus a complete shell bound ||F_(P,D,chi)||_2<<_epsilon X^(gamma+epsilon) is sufficient for the same original exponent gamma and its full zero exclusion.

A coarse explicit order suffices. If P is contained in primes<=z with z<=C log X, the elementary integer harmonic bound gives lambda<=4(1+log z)=O(loglog X). For any fixed eta>0,

    D_X=ceil((2c+eta) log X/loglog X)                  (C7)

makes C3 at most X^(-2c-eta+o(1)), so C6 holds with any smaller positive buffer, for example eta/2; if D_X>=|P| the error is simply zero. Near the current endpoint this coefficient is about.250278; for c=1/6 it is1/3, and for c=1/4 it is1/2. One must also select P to satisfy its literal Q bound; P may be fixed or the maximal prime prefix under that bound. C7 is a sufficient asymptotic bound, not a claim that a fixed small degree is adequate. The finite exact tail in C2 is the preferred constructive certificate.

To expose the rare22 drift, let m(B;u)=E_mu_u[r_P(n)chi(n)|B(n)=B], so |m|<=1. Up to the paid full-pattern error,

    F_chi/Z=sum_S A_S mhat_S,
    mhat_S=E_pi[m Z_S].                              (C8)

Degree truncation leaves the exact retained scalar sum_(|S|<=D) A_S mhat_S. Bounding its corresponding low-degree m-energy by X^(-2c+epsilon) would suffice by Cauchy. This is a deterministic signed conditional-response estimate, not a concentration conclusion. Coarse orthogonality gives only <=1 and hence field exponent1. The exact legal reference example m=a_P has norm1 and E_pi[a_P m]=1 despite independent exposed bits and E_pi a_P=0. Random revelation therefore does not create the required saving. C2–7 pay the CODEC error but leave its arithmetic retained response open.

Relative to W41 B1–6/G54, the new candidate delta is the explicit degree-energy law, certified truncation error and literal centered-dilation reconstruction. It does not replace the existing full covariance problem by exposed marginal independence. No claim of literature novelty is made for Walsh expansions, Chernoff bounds or sieve truncation.

## 4. Survivors03/20: actual Gaussian forcing defeats an uncut prime resolvent

### 4.1 The exact high-ceiling certificate and all its costs

Let P>=5 and retain all primes<=P. Let f_P(n)=f3(n) if every prime factor of n is<=P and0 otherwise, and

    V_P(u)=sum_n f_P(n)g_tau(log n-u),
    E_P(s)=(1-3^-s)^-1 product_(p<=P,p!=3)(1-2p^-s)/(1-p^-s). (R1)

Unlike a squarefree-only partition function, this includes every prime power. For sigma>0 it has an absolutely convergent finite-prime Dirichlet series and

    ||exp(-sigma u)V_P(u)||_L2(R)^2
      =exp(tau sigma^2)/(2pi) integral_R exp(-tau t^2)|E_P(sigma+it)|^2dt. (R2)

This is Parseval after absolute Mellin Fubini. Let P_X>=2X exp(C sqrt(log X)). All integers n<=P_X occur with their exact original f3 coefficient, while missing nonsmooth n lie in a full Gaussian tail. The elementary |f3|<=1 Gaussian estimate gives

    sup_(log X<=u<=log2X) |F(u)-V_(P_X)(u)|
       <=X^(1-C^2/(2tau)+o(1)).                      (R3)

Thus a global source norm in R2 bounded by P^kappa would yield shell exponent sigma+kappa (P_X=X^(1+o(1))), with R3 paid by choosing C. At sigma=.6, the weakest first-gain budget is kappa<.274861; c=1/6 allows kappa<.233333..., and c=1/4 allows kappa<.15. These are honest full-return headrooms, not isolated Euler-factor savings. For other sigma>.5, the budget is gamma-sigma.

### 4.2 Source-sensitive obstruction at shrinking height

For each fixed1/2<sigma<1 and sufficiently large P, R2 instead grows faster than EVERY power of P. The obstruction occurs at heights t approximately pi/log P, which approach0, so Gaussian frequency suppression does not help.

For p>=5 the uniformly convergent local logarithm gives

    log|(1-2p^-s)/(1-p^-s)|=-Re(p^-s)+O_sigma(p^-2sigma).

The sum of errors is bounded independently of P and small t. The finite p=2,3 factors are bounded above and away from zero near t=0 for fixed sigma in(1/2,1). Hence

    log|E_P(sigma+it)|=-Re sum_(p<=P) p^(-sigma-it)+O_sigma(1). (R4)

The ordinary PNT, verified in [Johnston–Yang, arXiv:2204.01980v2, Corollary1.3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2204.01980), supplies pi(y)~y/log y. Stieltjes partial summation or the substitution y=P exp(-v) gives, uniformly for a in[5pi/6,7pi/6],

    sum_(p<=P) p^(-sigma-ia/log P)
      =(P^(1-sigma)/log P)[exp(-ia)/(1-sigma)+o_sigma(1)]. (R5)

For completeness, one may first restrict y>=P^b for fixed b in(0,1), where the PNT error is uniform; the omitted y<=P^b is O(P^(b(1-sigma))) and is negligible. In the main integral, v=log(P/y) has limiting density exp(-(1-sigma)v); a/log P tends to0 uniformly, which yields R5 by a bounded tail split. No zero-free conjecture is used.

Since cos a<=-sqrt3/2 on that interval, R4–5 imply for all sufficiently large P and all those t=a/log P,

    log|E_P(sigma+it)| >= [1/(2(1-sigma))] P^(1-sigma)/log P. (R6)

The t-interval has length pi/(3log P) and its Gaussian factor tends uniformly to1. Consequently

    ||exp(-sigma u)V_P||_2
      >= c_(sigma,tau)(log P)^(-1/2)
           exp([1/(2(1-sigma))]P^(1-sigma)/log P).    (R7)

For rigor one can reduce the positive constant in R7 slightly when absorbing finite factors; the stated R6 already has fixed slack relative to sqrt3/2. Every polynomial allowance in R3 fails for this uncut global norm, including the large c=1/4 budget. This is an ACTUAL f3 finite-prime/Gaussian-source obstruction, stronger than a generic operator-norm example. It does not lower-bound the true full field on x~P: the global norm can be dominated by remote smooth-number scales. It does not disprove a causal, physically restricted signed resolvent.

### 4.3 Protected rare20 and the viable changed object

On H_sigma=L2(R,exp(-2sigma u)du), each prime dilation has norm p^-sigma. The weighted prime factor is (I-2D_p)(I-D_p)^-1. In finite multiplicative truncations D_p is nilpotent and every factor has spectrum{1}; therefore the finite spectrum does not price physical transient growth. On the full space the Fourier multiplier in R2 records precisely the missing norm. R7 shows that merely retaining signs and replacing a singular-value bound by an uncut resolvent bound cannot fit the actual source budget.

The viable changed target is the causal readout

    ||1_[log X,log2X] V_(P_X)||_2 << X^gamma,          (R8)

or a finite signed transfer whose output is exactly this restriction and whose discarded remote-scale feedback is explicitly paid. R3 gives its complete return without a global-norm hypothesis. R8 remains an open actual arithmetic estimate; no spectral-radius claim pays it. A useful next calculation is a Schur/compression identity for this exact output, retaining the two off-block feedback terms, to determine whether the obstruction R7 lives wholly in a removable remote-scale block or couples back at power cost. The previous Schur-complement lower-bound warning remains in force.

The R7 calculation is a distinct source-sensitive failure bound in this record. Its ancestry is W41-28's unrenormalized Euler failure, U-FUGACITY/U-DETERMINANT and finite nilpotent resolvent attempts. It does not claim a general no-go theorem for renormalized Euler products or nonnormal arithmetic operators.

## 5. Wildcard02 local result

At a zero rho of multiplicity m, write L(s)=(s-rho)^m u(s), u(rho)!=0. Then L(s)^-k=(s-rho)^(-km)u(s)^-k. For finitely many distinct positive k, the largest k with a nonzero constant coefficient supplies the unique highest Laurent order. A holomorphic nonvanishing Gaussian multiplier preserves it. Thus fixed pole-order amplification gives qualitative noncancellation but no reduction of the x^Re(rho) threshold. An inverse Mellin residue has x^rho times a polynomial of degree km-1 in log x. The new reciprocal-power arithmetic and cross-Gram estimates are unpaid, so this first test does not merit a third independent arithmetic development.

# W66 independent unselected audits, before outcome intake

Selection receipt audit-selection.json SHA256 11b3a8d67ba32b21891ff9f80a0d71cbac2cef934a76b6944964e1e805bb28e6. The author tests S01,S02,S21,S23,S28,S30 are excluded. Frozen priority first skips S30 and selects protected S06. Frozen uniform order starts S04, which is untested and distinct. No new entropy. Only author selection metadata has been read; neither report nor outcomes has been opened. These are independent developed audits, not judgments of the author's tests.

## Protected S06: exact chirp insertion and its reconstruction price

The seed proposes inserting a quadratic additive-phase integral equal to one, reorganizing a multiplicative fiber, and paying the full inverse. The following establishes a genuine limitation of positive payment, while keeping signed recombination open.

Let z=a-i*kappa with a>0 and kappa real. Use the analytic square root on Re z>0. For every real t,

I_z(t) = sqrt(z/(2*pi))*exp(t^2/(2*z)) * integral_R exp(-z*u^2/2+i*t*u) du = 1.       (A1)

The integral is absolutely convergent. The Gaussian Fourier formula follows first for real z>0 by differentiation in t and its value at zero, then by analytic continuation in the right half-plane; convergence is locally dominated there. Thus (A1) is an exact insertion, not a putative oscillatory identity with unrecorded tails.

Its fully absolute price is EXACTLY

P_z(t) = (|z|/a)^(1/2) exp(a*t^2/(2*|z|^2)).                                      (A2)

Indeed take the modulus outside the integral and integrate exp(-a*u^2/2). For a target range |t|<=T, T>0, put E=a*T^2/(2*|z|^2)>0 and C=|kappa|*T^2/(2*|z|^2). C is the magnitude of the quadratic phase in the exterior prefactor at T. Then

P_z(T)=(1+(C/E)^2)^(1/4)*exp(E) >= sqrt(C)*exp(E)/sqrt(E) >= sqrt(2*e*C).             (A3)

The last minimization is exact: exp(E)/sqrt(E) is minimized at E=1/2. For C=0 the lower bound is vacuous; P>=1 remains true. Consequently a power-sized exterior chirp C=X^delta carries at least sqrt(2e)*X^(delta/2) if the whole insertion is paid absolutely. Choosing parameters to keep P bounded keeps C bounded. This does not preclude a signed or L2 use of the integral, and is not a lower bound for a Mobius sum.

For any FINITE actual source sum sum_n a_n*w_n, set t=t(n) and insert (A1) term by term, retaining a_n=mu(n)chi(n), natural zeros, every original projector, mask and weight. Interchange with the integral is then valid. Infinite extensions need a separate integrable majorant: the exterior exp(a*t(n)^2/(2|z|^2)) may defeat the original damping. Neither a formal Fresnel limit a->0 nor repeated use of a finite identity pays that tail.

A finite additive version makes the complete channel Gram explicit without this convergence issue. Let Q be an odd prime, A nonzero modulo Q, e_Q(t)=exp(2*pi*i*t/Q), c=(4A)^(-1) mod Q, and G_A=sum_v mod Q e_Q(A*v^2). Completing the square gives

sum_v e_Q(A*v^2+t*v)=G_A*e_Q(-c*t^2),   |G_A|^2=Q.                               (A4)

The second identity follows by writing |G_A|^2 as sum_(v,w) e_Q(A(v-w)(v+w)) and using the bijection (v,w)->(v-w,v+w), then character orthogonality. No distributional limit or unverified Gauss-sum phase is used. Thus for B_r=sum_(n congruent r mod Q) a_n*w_n,

F_v=sum_r B_r*e_Q(c*r^2+v*r),
S=sum_r B_r=G_A^(-1)*sum_v e_Q(A*v^2)*F_v,
sum_v |F_v|^2=Q*sum_r |B_r|^2,
|S|^2=Q^(-1)*sum_(v,w) e_Q(A(v^2-w^2))*F_v*conj(F_w).                            (A5)

The retained all-channel cross terms in the last line are indispensable. Cauchy gives |S|^2<=sum_v|F_v|^2. This generic bound is SHARP: B_r=1 for all r gives |S|^2=Q^2=sum_v|F_v|^2. It is an ambient coherent example, not a claim that the actual arithmetic source realizes B_r=1. Natural zeros in the actual source remain inside B_r and are not changed by the identity.

If t=mn, an individual channel introduces the mixed four-point phase

c*(m^2-m'^2)*(n^2-n'^2)+v*(m-m')*(n-n').                                         (A6)

This may be curved off its degeneracy sets. But summing all channels in (A4) restores the original entrywise multiplier 1. Curvature in one channel is therefore not evidence that the full signed Gram improved; its complete source-dependent estimate and inverse bill must be proved together. An acceptable new sufficient target would bound either the exact signed Gram in (A5), or all F_v with a total budget paying Cauchy and every original complement. A bound for each channel with constants growing in Q cannot be substituted into a growing-Q bank without their cost.

Verdict: (A1)-(A6) are exact developed components and a quantitative absolute-price obstruction. S06 survives only as a search for actual cross-channel cancellation; no power estimate, changed conductor theorem, or new c follows. Existing curved-source, four-cycle and paid-transfer ancestry applies. Novelty asserted here is only this explicit preparation calculation in our record, not literature priority.

## Uniform S04: what a positive character-pair detector preserves

For a fixed ordinary Dirichlet character chi, write F_chi(s)=1/L(s,chi). On Re s>1 the coefficient identity gives

F_barchi(s)=conj(F_chi(conj(s))),                                                 (B1)

and the relation continues wherever the meromorphic reciprocals are defined. A pole of F_chi at rho=beta+i*tau induces a pole of F_barchi at conj(rho), not automatically at rho. Substituting F_barchi(conj(s)) creates an antiholomorphic expression, not a new holomorphic two-component Dirichlet series. This distinction is essential at nonzero heights.

Set f(s)=(F_chi(s),F_barchi(s))^T near a possible rho and suppose its leading singular term is v*(s-rho)^(-m), v nonzero. Let A(s) be continuous there, with W=A^*A. Then

lim_(s->rho) |s-rho|^(2m) ||A(s)f(s)||^2 = v^*W(rho)v.                            (B2)

This follows simply by multiplying out the leading Laurent vector. W positive semidefinite does not force a nonzero limit: it may kill v. A sufficient source-independent signal condition is W(rho)>=delta*I with delta>0. More economically one may prove a lower bound just on all actual residue directions, but that remains a source obligation. For a finite bank use sum_j A_j^*A_j instead; every associated source and cross term must be retained in its arithmetic estimate.

For example |z1+z2|^2+|z1-z2|^2=2(|z1|^2+|z2|^2). Either single observation can miss a direction; the pair restores it at the original norm scale. For a real character, F_chi=F_barchi identically and the difference detector is exactly zero, including at every possible pole. This is an exact counterexample to positivity plus one difference observation being a universal detector.

The corresponding actual arithmetic pair is particularly restrictive. At every real x>=1,

M_chi(x)=sum_(n<=x) mu(n)chi(n),  M_barchi(x)=conj(M_chi(x)),
||(M_chi(x),M_barchi(x))||^2=2|M_chi(x)|^2.                                     (B3)

This retains all natural zeros and all sharp real endpoints. It also holds with common REAL weights. With a complex phase, conjugating chi alone is insufficient: the phase must also be conjugated to use (B3). At heights, the conjugate partner has the opposite height. Neither a changing height nor a complex source weight can be silently dropped.

Here is a complete conditional return for this exact pair, to avoid stopping at local detection. Fix 0<gamma<1 and the ordinary character. If for every epsilon>0 and every X>=2,

integral_X^(2X) ||(M_chi(x),M_barchi(x))|| dx/x <<_(chi,epsilon) X^(gamma+epsilon), (B4)

then dyadic summation gives locally normal convergence of integral_1^infinity M_chi(x)x^(-s-1) dx on Re s>gamma. Indeed on a compact set with Re s>=gamma+2epsilon, each dyadic tail is O(2^(-j*epsilon)); the finite initial integral is harmless. It is holomorphic there, including all finite heights. On Re s>1 partial summation gives s times this integral =1/L(s,chi). Uniqueness of meromorphic continuation therefore excludes zeros of L in Re s>gamma. At s=1 the principal L pole produces a ZERO of its reciprocal and remains permitted. Imprimitive natural zeros are already in chi; no conductor-uniform constant is asserted. This is a complete sufficient return, not a proof of (B4).

By (B3), (B4) is exactly the scalar shell-L1 estimate up to sqrt(2). A uniformly well-conditioned positive change of coordinates is quantitatively comparable; a degenerating observation needs its inverse loss. For instance A_X=diag(X^(-eta),1), f_X=(X^beta,0)^T reduces the observed exponent by eta while leaving the original first component unchanged. This ambient example proves the need to pay observation conditioning, not an arithmetic lower bound.

Verdict: local Laurent residue coverage and full scalar-to-pair return are rigorous; conjugate-height and principal-pole qualifications are explicit. The elementary positive pair gives no exponent advantage over the actual scalar source. A useful survivor would be a genuinely different source-specific observation with proved residue coverage and a strictly cheaper COMPLETE arithmetic norm. Existing paired-detector, observation and bank work is ancestry; no novelty or c increase is inferred from (B1)-(B4) alone.

### M1. Probability space, support, and summatory calibration

A Steinhaus variable is uniform on the complex unit circle. All epsilon_p and I_p are mutually independent. Initially set a(n)=mu(n)^2 product_{p|n}v_p; delete every prime dividing q and replace finitely many other prime values by their prescribed unit values. This is ordinary multiplicativity, not complete multiplicativity. It gives exactly the asserted squareful and ramified zeros, a(1)=1, and modulus one on every remaining squarefree integer. Prescribing all primes up to any fixed bound matches the full finite prefix of any particular mu*chi source with that conductor support.

Put P={p:I_p=1}. For b>beta,

  E sum_{p in P}p^(-b)=sum_p p^(-(b+1-beta))<infinity.

Consequently, almost surely, sum_{p in P}p^(-b)<infinity for every rational b>beta, hence every real b>beta. In particular sum_{p in P}1/p<infinity. For any b in(beta,1), # {p in P:p<=x} <= x^b sum_{p in P}p^(-b)=O_b(x^b). Neither statement uses a prime-number theorem.

Let a0(n)=mu(n)^2 product_{p|n}epsilon_p. For n!=m, E[a0(n) conjugate(a0(m))]=0, and E|a0(n)|^2<=1. The same holds after multiplying by any fixed ordinary character psi. A useful elementary maximal estimate for such orthogonal variables is

  E max_{m<=2^k}|sum_{n<=m}a0(n)psi(n)|^2 <= (k+1)^2 2^k.

Indeed, decompose each initial segment into at most k+1 disjoint dyadic blocks, apply Cauchy, then bound its sum of block squares by the sum over every block on every dyadic level. The expectation of the total on each level is at most2^k. Markov's inequality at threshold2^{k(1/2+eta)} and Borel--Cantelli give, for every eta>0,

  M0,psi(x)=O_{eta,psi}(x^(1/2+eta))

almost surely. Intersect the probability-one events for rational eta>0 and the countable set of ordinary characters. We retain one outcome on this intersection throughout the argument.

At a changed prime, the exact local quotient is

  (1+v z)/(1+epsilon z)
    =1+sum_{j>=1}(v-epsilon)(-epsilon)^(j-1)z^j.

Its nonconstant coefficient moduli are at most2. Therefore a=a0*d as a Dirichlet convolution, with

  sum_n |d(n)|n^(-b)
   <= finite_factor * product_{p in P}(1+2p^(-b)/(1-p^(-b)))<infinity

for every b>beta. Deleting the finitely many primes of q or imposing finitely many values adds quotients analytic and absolutely convergent for b>0. Complete multiplicativity of psi gives a psi=(a0 psi)*(d psi), where juxtaposition is pointwise multiplication and the star here is Dirichlet convolution. All occurrences of the literal mu*chi source elsewhere in this report mean the pointwise coefficients mu(n)chi(n). Choosing eta with1/2+eta<b now gives

  |sum_{n<=x}a(n)psi(n)|
   <= C x^b sum_{d<=x}|d(d)|d^(-b) =O_b(x^b).

In this display d(d) denotes the convolution coefficient at integer d, not a divisor-counting function. Thus the claimed beta+epsilon bound holds for every epsilon>0 (larger exponents are harmless). Abel summation also proves

  sum_{n<=x}a(n)psi(n)n^(it)
      =O_{epsilon,psi}((1+|t|)x^(beta+epsilon))

uniformly for all real t. Any fixed number of log n factors costs x^epsilon after shrinking the original epsilon. Constants depend on the chosen outcome and fixed character; this is not a conductor-uniform theorem.

### 3.3 Sum t only now; cubic sieve in the original n

At fixed f,b,Delta, the polynomial R12 depends on t,m only through
the original product n=tm. All its COEFFICIENTS are independent
of n,t,k. Since t is a divisor of the same squarefree n,

    sum_(t~T,m original) |M_(i,Delta,f,b)(tm)|^2
       <= Z^epsilon sum_(n sf,q_n<<N) |M_(i,Delta,f,b)(n)|^2
       << Z^epsilon S(N,L/q_Delta) q_Delta Omega_(i,Delta).
                                                               (R17)

The second inequality is precisely the accepted cubic sieve M
B2.25 with one coefficient vector for the live n. Any remaining
source-only constraints are enlarged only in the first positive
inequality. The same reasoning retains fixed arbitrary V_i because
their exact contribution was R7 and was bounded only after R14.

There is no O(T) multiplicity: for a fixed n, t|n yields only
tau(n) possibilities. There is no moving quadratic-row coefficient:
k has already been removed before R17. A separate cubic bound of
length N/T for each t would generally waste a T-label or mark
factor, but it is not the argument in either frozen source.

There are O_orig(G/q_f) possible b, with empty and bounded quotient
ranges interpreted as in JPS. Multiplying R17 into R16 cancels
q_Delta against the squared original mark root. Finally

    sum_Delta Omega_(i,Delta)
       <= sum_P tau(P)|u_i(P)|^2/q_P
       << Z^epsilon Omega_i.                         (R18)

Replacing K/q_Delta by K and S(N,L/q_Delta) by S(N,L) increases
the positive bound. We have therefore proved

    sum_(t~T) |r_w(t)| sum_(R original) |V_(i,t,f)(R)|^2
       << Z^epsilon (G/q_f)
          (K+NG/(T q_f)) S(N,L) Omega_i,              (R19)

where V is the literal fixed-t,f vector R8, including its independent
norm phase. This is BGC10/HA11, with the profile envelopes temporarily
normalized as in the accepted JPS proof.

For the fixed mu*chi Gaussian M, V_gamma=(D-gamma)M, left Gaussian
decay gives

    |M(x)|^2=2x^(2gamma) integral_0^x t^(-2gamma)
                       Re(conjugate(M(t))V_gamma(t))dt/t.

Shell integration introduces the complete kernel
W_(gamma,X)(t)=((2X)^(2gamma)-max(X,t)^(2gamma))/(2gamma) for0<t<=2X.
Every arithmetic pair remains with bracket log(mn/t^2)/(2tau)-gamma.
This condition is exactly the original energy. Indefinite storage
|M|^2-kappa|DM|^2 can be negative on high-imaginary-frequency modes and
therefore an upper storage bound alone cannot control |M|^2. This mode
test is not the construction of an actual zero or arithmetic lower bound.

statement:
### Orientation-sensitive rectangular means

Suppose for the same physical family one has
\[
\mathcal M(A,B)\ll T^C(AB)^\delta
\min_j A^{r_j}B^{s_j},\qquad r_j,s_j\ge0.
\]
Summing over \(AB^2\le X\) gives exponent
\[
R=\max_{0\le z\le1/2}\min_j\{r_j(1-2z)+s_jz\}.
\]
Every bound is nondecreasing in \(A\), so the outer maximum is on \(AB^2=X\). Only endpoints and intersections of the finitely many affine lines need checking. Dyads cost logarithms.

A fixed-\(b\) estimate \(Y^{1+\eta+\delta}q_b^{\nu+\delta}\) yields an all-physical-row exponent \(1+\eta\) if \(\nu<1+2\eta\): a \(b\)-dyad \(B\) contributes \(X^{1+\eta+\delta}B^{\nu-1-2\eta+O(\delta)}\).

The hypothetical pointwise model \(|F_{ab^2}|\ll q_aq_b^{1/2}\) gives rectangular mean \(A^3B^2\), and hence \(X^{3-4z}\). It reaches \(X^{35/32}\) only for \(z\ge61/128\). Combining it with the weak fixed-\(b\) exponent \(\nu=3/2,\eta=3/32\) gives worst exponent \(85/69>35/32\). These are exact limitations of the supplied upper bounds, not lower bounds for actual means. [BA D4.]
title: Orientation-sensitive rectangular means

## 6. General curved scaling, retained for a different future estimate

For any FIXED b>1 and 0<gamma<1, the complete every-epsilon shell bound
for V_b with exponent 2gamma implies zero exclusion on Re s>gamma.
Choose a finite K with 1-(b-1)K<gamma. Equation (2.2) then has a
holomorphic remainder throughout that half-plane. Start with the known
zero-free half-plane Re s>1 and descend in strips of width b-1. In
each next strip all k>=1 shifted reciprocals in (2.2) are already
holomorphic. Since A_b,0(s)=Gamma(s)exp(-i*pi*s/2) has no zero for
Re s>0, the unshifted reciprocal is holomorphic there too. Finitely
many steps reach Re s>gamma; equivalently continue to any compact
sub-half-plane Re s>=gamma+delta and then let delta>0 vary. The
argument retains every shifted reciprocal rather than declaring it
an error on a region where it may have poles.

Here b, K and the source itself are fixed before x tends to infinity.
There is no claim for b depending on x or for constants uniform as
b decreases to 1. Taking b<3/2 might reduce the raw diagonal price,
but the same coarse absolute Type II term x^(b+1) still gives no
subunit pointwise exponent. Thus this generalization does not evade
the identified arithmetic cost by parameter tuning.
title: 6. General curved scaling, retained for a different future estimate

## 5. Low/high branches, missing labels and all-height scope

Low indicators are imposed only after both transforms on positive allocated child energies. RC's `commonChild_energy` and `common_clipped_energy` permit the keep predicate. Use the actual moving child character with the original fixed anchor Q_*; do not insert that child into the anchor. In each fixed parent translate mask transport preserves the literal row gate and positive-real zeros. Whole-character conjugation reflects height; conjugating only its fixed factor would change the family.

A removed canonical slot of width dz costs squared exponent (7/10+O(buffer))dz in a low bin. Greedily remove slots until old 9/2 capacity holds or the slots run out. Drop the low indicator only after this payment and use the old full eligible family. Exhaustion uses unrestricted zero-slot input even if the plain sum exceeds the width. Bounded prime lengths are estimated directly; the large-length contour premise is not applied at length one.

Actual canonical width minus M', denoted d_*, can be negative after support cancellation; only d_*<=delta2 is known. For 0<=v<=1,

    d_*+v(F-d_*)_+ <=delta2+v F_+.

Use v=7/45 and nominal defect F<=g+6a+small losses. The low reserve is a/15-7g/45. On case j its normalized lower bound is exactly b_j/3000, with minimum 57/5000000. This pays frequency/support padding, one greedy overshoot, bin buffering and aggregate finite-slot losses by choosing a smaller common budget. The slot list is fixed before the final threshold; there is no growing count hidden in that aggregate budget.

For high bins delta in [7/10,3/4], set rho=1-10delta/[3(5-2delta)]. The actual nonzero row is w=u0 e F_c G_c V h'. Active left/right residues are 1+t and 1-t modulo six, and a zero residue retains the natural puncture. Retain u0 among six fixed unit sectors. With canceled active radical width R0 and L_c=log_Z NF_c, L_c<=5(R-R0), and the actual support gives

    log_Z Nw<=W+small losses,
    W=M-R-(c-d)_++L_c-6a.

Every genuine second common prime and the first projector divides w. The missing first common radical has width <=p-R-E+R0. For fixed w and missing radical the remaining common labels, including arbitrary valuations, are divisor-many by the source Rankin product estimate. A finite valuation table alone would not prove this. The second residual projector need not divide w; its dyadic count is paid by the two extraction scalars and original priority allocation. A possibly zero extracted character value stays outside, and no new coprimality condition is imposed on quotient plains.

The fixed-dictionary density has a threshold before all heights and live norm bounds, and primitive conductor O_fixed(Nw). Polynomial Euler holes are separate from that conductor and dictionary size. Within the actual parent translate, the upper buffered zero maximum controls each surviving factor; a member of a fixed finite list realizes the lower maximum needed for density. A union over that fixed list costs a constant; a union over live arithmetic labels is not taken. Sixth-power lifting converges because rho>=2/7>1/6. Thus the joint count is

    Z^(rho W+p-R-E+R0+epsilon)(1+T)^J.

A slightly negative nominal W with a supported row is enlarged to its O(epsilon) supported bound. If the supported bound is negative, the range is empty. No nonempty integral row range is assigned a population bound below one.

The source pointwise factor and outside normalization yield this excess over the joint side target:

    M(rho-1)+delta A+a(5-6rho)
    +(1-rho)(c-d)_+-delta c-(1+rho)R-E-B_c+rho L_c+R0
    +g2-t2-(1+delta)b2+small losses.

Using min(c,d)>=p>=R, L_c<=5(R-R0), rho+delta>1 and 5rho>1 bounds the middle line by

    (4rho-1-delta)p-E-B_c <=-79p/270-E-B_c.

The last line is <=-delta b2-t2. The remaining normalized reserve is

    H_j(delta)=1-rho-delta A_j-k b_j(5-6rho).

Its derivative is 50(1-6k b_j)/(3(5-2delta)^2)-A_j, bounded below by 237658/759375>0. Hence its minimum is at delta=.7, where

    H_j(.7)=-7/135+(1157/750)b_(j-1)-(247/300)e.

It increases with j and has global minimum 5861/13500000, including the actual ceiling loss 247/1500000. Bins crossing .7 belong to the buffered low branch, whose O(buffer) loss is paid. Density is used only when the lower edge is at least .7; its range has not been enlarged.

For all-height recovery, finite Euler factors and their reciprocals and fixed derivatives cost U^epsilon on a fixed positive-real strip and are nonzero there. Natural zeros remain in the coefficient identities. Profiles separate on a common ambient logarithmic box before live labels. Euler derivatives of K(B product y_i^e_i) are uniform in B>0, so larger a_j gives no hidden power in a smooth seminorm. The weighted Fourier integral is taken in the direct-sum Hilbert space of rows and labels and charges their count once. Coprimality, valuation and zero-bin indicators are never differentiated.

The density's internal detector exponents precede its finite height order. Choose a distinct small external height exponent afterward to fit (1+T)^J in the same reserve. Internal smooth orders are chosen backward through the fixed transform graph; external Fourier-tail orders follow raw polynomial bounds. Arbitrarily larger input heights use absolute polynomial U-bounds absorbed by a sufficiently large fixed polynomial in those input heights. This retains independent plain, slot and witness heights without selecting a detector anew for each row.

## Fixed object and quantifiers

Use the original Eisenstein field, primary/unit convention, fixed excluded
set and finite dictionary. Write
\(\phi_u(n)=\nu(n)\psi_u(n)^{\pm1}\), retaining natural zeros. The fixed
factor \(\nu\) need not have order six; it remains in column coefficients
when the row character is summed. For fixed smooth profiles put

\[
M_u(D;W)=D^{-1/2}\sum_n\mu(n)\phi_u(n)W(Nn/D).
\]

Let Q be the actual product of the original prime slots. Their pools are
pairwise disjoint, their coefficients and natural zeros are unchanged,
and \(P_0=\prod_iP_i=U^v\), \(0\le v\le1/20\).
The slot pools may intersect either inverse. The elementary bound is
\(\sup_u|Q_u|^2\ll H_JU^{v+\epsilon}\). If inverse orientation is reversed,
align the **entire** slot product at the positive norm, including its
coefficients, zeros and heights; individual slot switching is unavailable.

The norm sums nonzero sixth-power-free rows in a fixed nonnegative smooth
enclosing ball of scale U, with the licensed fixed ray/unit sectors. A
row divisor weight is dominated before expansion and Poisson. An
arbitrary row selector, zero predicate or signed physical projector is
not admitted into that free-row Poisson identity.

The physical box supplied by [G147–G148](../[private research revision]/far-complement-integration.md)

The internal buffer \(\delta_b\) may exceed .70; extract the signal there

Use the existing common mesh and buffer **before** eventual arithmetic
family and slot choices. Then fix the allowed dictionary/slot data,

fixed at U and is not differentiated. Write q/h sums over a fixed global
support bound and use Hilbert Minkowski before the rowwise supremum.
For a common product profile, B3.3 fixes its Fourier measure on the whole

distinct. Choose derivative orders backward through the bounded

For reference, with \(h=5-2\delta\), put

\[

D_K=15K-10-6K\delta,
\]
\[

Here \(E_K\ge\rho\ge19/54\), because

## 6. Both source constant-term factors: the exceptional point matters

Use xi for the Eisenstein parameter, distinct from the detector Mellin s.
The primary zero-frequency quotient supplies the good-prime factor

    C_p(xi)=(1-Q^(3-4xi))/(1-Q^(4-4xi)).               (12)

Algebraically its expansion is
1+(1-Q^-1) sum_(r>=1) Q^(4r(1-xi)) in its convergence region.
This is the source constant-term Euler factor, not a verified matrix entry
on the relative H-boundary. It is a necessary scalar normalization check for
any proposed spherical source intertwiner. The two ordinary source
constant-term expansions contain C_p(xi1)C_p(xi2). At the residue point,

    C_p(5/4)=1+Q^-1,
    C_p(3/4)=0,
    C_p(3/4+e)=-4 log(Q)/(Q-1)*e+O(e^2).              (13)

Multiplying (9) by just the forward scalar factors at5/4 cannot erase its
nonconstant direction: their product is (1+Q^-1)^2. This does not describe
the full intertwiner action on Whittaker functionals. The reflected exceptional
point has zeros. It is not legitimate to insert a scalar0 from (13) and
declare the opposite boundary absent: one must specify the inducing
representations, maps on the selected Whittaker functionals, normalized
intertwiners, and order of taking the two exceptional specializations.
Dividing by that zero changes the normalization and requires a limit.

Thus this calculation locates actual scalar data and the actual singular
parameter issue. It does not identify a two-by-two relative matrix. The
global 24-cusp functional equation and its special bad-place factors do
not provide that identification, either. The two prescribed source vectors
cannot simply be substituted for the two basis vectors of a guessed matrix.
In particular the seed-dependent linear combinations of the cusp coefficients
must remain attached to these Euler factors; a particular combined constant
term can vanish. No uncancelled global period boundary follows from (13).

There is a further exact distinction between two meanings of Weyl action.
The compact representative w is in K_p and fixes each unramified source
vector. On the unary factor its action is Fourier, up to the stated fixed
unit Weil scalar, so the completed selected tensor is also fixed after that
normalization. But w H w^-1 has lower rather than upper unipotents and is
not H. This vector symmetry is not a relative scattering formula. Nor is
right translation by w the principal-series intertwining integral M(xi),
which changes the inducing parameter and transports Whittaker functionals.
Both source intertwiners still require that transport before specialization.
title: 6. Both source constant-term factors: the exceptional point matters

statement:
## R4. Short-edge isolation: accepted proof and exact reach

Let n be squarefree and m any distinct positive integer. Put g=gcd(n,m). The divisibility g|(n-m) gives g<=|n-m|. If |n-m|<=C min(n,m)^theta, then

    n/g >= n/(C min(n,m)^theta) >= C^(-1)n^(1-theta).

There is no missing factor for an incoming edge or an endpoint outside [X,2X]. For squarefree n, n/g is exactly the product of the primes of n not dividing m. If at most d such primes may be lost, and every prime of n is<=y, then n/g<=y^d. Hence n^(1-theta)>C y^d forbids EVERY such neighbor. This covers squareful or nonunit auxiliary integers because the restriction is imposed at the squarefree endpoint n irrespective of orientation. If that endpoint restriction were dropped for incoming edges, this proof would not apply.

Fix q,C,d,theta, and choose a FIXED integer k>d/(1-theta). Products of k distinct primes in (X^(1/k),(2X)^(1/k)] are squarefree, lie in(X,2X], and eventually avoid all fixed prime divisors of q. Their maximal prime y=(2X)^(1/k) satisfies

    n^(1-theta)/(C y^d)
       >= (C 2^(d/k))^(-1) X^(1-theta-d/k) -> infinity.

They are therefore isolated in the entire permitted graph for every sufficiently large X. This is a strict power comparison; equality k=d/(1-theta) gives no conclusion from this argument. The same assertion survives a bounded family of radii and subpower inflation of C after choosing a fixed positive exponent margin. It does not supply uniformity for unbounded k or growing d.

The prime input is only pi(t)~t/log t, independently checked in the official [NIST DLMF27.12](https://dlmf.nist.gov/27.12), equations4-5. At FIXED k it gives

    t_X ~ k(2^(1/k)-1) X^(1/k)/log X.

Unique factorization makes the vertex count exactly binomial(t_X,k), hence

    |V_X| ~ A_k X/(log X)^k,
    A_k=[k(2^(1/k)-1)]^k/k! >0.

Neither short-interval prime estimates nor character prime equidistribution are used. Fixed q is essential: the argument does not give an onset uniform in a conductor allowed to contain all the selected primes. The possibly tiny A_k and large onset affect constants, not the exponent-one absolute obstruction.

At every isolated vertex a=div F+r implies r(n)=a(n), for ANY complex edge flow whose divergence is defined. Since |a(n)|=1,

    sum_(X<n<=2X)|r(n)| >= |V_X|.

No disjointness, positivity, bound on edge coefficients or acyclicity is needed for this local conclusion. Iterated bounded short steps cannot start at an isolated vertex. For every delta<1, X/(log X)^k divided by X^delta tends to infinity, so the full absolute residual cannot have that power bound. To refute an every-epsilon exponent delta choose epsilon<(1-delta)/2.

The author's d=3 margins are correct: k24 at theta17497/20000 gives3/20000; k19 at5/6 gives1/114; k13 at3/4 gives1/52. At current gamma11, k24 still works with exact margin364909/2500000000. My additional exact check examines all344 short neighbors of four actual squarefree integers, including133 squareful ghost neighbors; none permits only one deleted prime under theta1/2,C1. This supports indexing and the optional-ghost scope, not the PNT asymptotic proof.

**Strongest objection, retained.** For principal chi the isolated k-prime layer has constant sign(-1)^k. This is a signed statement about that layer only. Other isolated layers and the rest of r can cancel it. C8 gives neither a lower bound for |sum r(n)| nor for |M(x)|. With nonreal chi even one fixed-k layer need not have coherent phase. Growing turnover, truly long edges, a different auxiliary transfer, or a direct signed estimate of the complete isolated complement remain eligible. No entire coding, coupling or multiscale family is rejected.

The record delta is this all-fixed-radius graph/complex-flow obstruction on actual integers, including its exact endpoint price. It refines U-PRIME-CHAIN/U-TRANSPORT and the coded/Walsh portfolio. It should not be renamed as an improved arithmetic exponent or a literature-priority claim.
title: R4. Short-edge isolation: accepted proof and exact reach

## G74. A spectral gap can leave the entire arithmetic sign harmonic

For each distinct p|n,p!=3, take C0 with one even basis vector and C1
with two odd vectors, both mapped to the even vector. Its Laplacian has
eigenvalues 2,2,0, one odd harmonic state and supertrace -1. Tensoring
over distinct primes gives one harmonic state of parity omega_(p!=3)(n),
uniform positive gap 2 and a complement homotopy of norm <=1/sqrt(2).
Repeated powers add no cube; p=3 contributes a trivial factor.

With the actual chi(n)g(log(n/x)) weights, complete trace convergence
follows from 3^omega(n/3^v3(n))<=n^2. For every t>=0,

    F=Tr(Gamma W exp(-t Delta))=Tr(Gamma W P_harmonic).

The inverse/homotopy only acts on I-P, so the gap gives no bound on F.
Its absolute harmonic price is (phi(q)/q) exp(tau/2)x+O_(q,tau)(1),
an upper-certificate obstruction, not a lower bound on the signed field.
Different-integer matching requires a separate weighted readout estimate.

The direct complete Gaussian scalar is also not positive-real on its
proposed right half-plane: at s=4+it, Re D(s)>=2/3 for each of F,B,U,
since the coefficient of 1 is 1 and the remaining absolute mass is <=1/3.
At t=pi/(4 tau), exp(tau s^2/2) has negative real phase, so the real part
of the Mellin observable is strictly negative. This excludes this literal
scalar realization only; a different/vector readout must prove its return.

## 4. Original profiles, row tails and uniform orders

The preceding proofs used annular columns and a row ball only to display the powers. They extend to the prescribed original family without a new arithmetic premise.

Use a fixed annular partition \(F_j(y)=F(2^j y)\vartheta(y)\). The exact central normalization is

\[
\mathcal M_n^R(X;F,\mathcal I)
=\sum_j2^{j/2}
 \mathcal M_n^R(2^jX;F_j,\mathcal I).
\tag{MQ16}
\]

Every fixed weighted seminorm of \(F_j\) decreases as \(2^{-A|j|}\), for arbitrarily large fixed \(A\), with a fixed polynomial height cost. Apply Minkowski to the positive joint row norm. The column powers in MQ4--MQ5 are \(0,1,2/3,(2b+1)/3\); all are bounded. Consequently the factors \(2^{j/2}\), the scale powers and their subpower losses are summable against the endpoint decay. One does not need a UM length margin on the enlarged annuli.

For a subunit column scale \(0<X<1\), direct summation gives
\(|\mathcal M_n^R(X;F,\mathcal I)|\ll_A X^A\), uniformly in the character, \(R\), and interval. The number of rows with \(q_n\le H,\ q_d\le\Delta\) is \(O((H\Delta)^{1/2})\). These facts also provide arbitrary subunit endpoint factors when a projector divisor exceeds a core scale.

For the original row majorant, keep all \(q_n\le H\) as one ball and decompose only its upper tail into dyads \(q_n\asymp2^jH\), \(j\ge0\). Apply the ball bounds at \(2^{j+1}H\), with the same frozen \(\Delta\). Their powers in the row scale are at most \(1/2\), up to an arbitrarily small loss, so the Schwartz decay sums the tail. Every fixed-prime valuation and unit remains included. No row conductor is substituted for the row norm at this step.

These arguments use a fixed finite profile order, chosen from \(b\), the requested loss and the prescribed profiles before any scale or arithmetic label varies. Original Mellin height twists cost a fixed polynomial, absorbed by the original rapid Mellin densities. The original product profile and its Mellin roots are unchanged in the signed expression. Partitions occur only inside positive estimates. No Type I theorem is invoked on a partitioned or sharply modified profile.

## G220. Complete finite covariance and the limiting-bank alternative

For a fixed finite Q coprime to S, coefficientwise Euler factors give

    U_Q(x)=sum_(d Q-smooth)eta(d)U(x/q_d),
    U(x)=sum_(d|Q)mu(d)eta(d)U_Q(x/q_d).                   (220.1)

Both are complete absolutely formed Gaussian identities. For every
sigma,delta>0, prod_(p|Q)(1-q_p^-sigma)^-1<<q_Q^delta: split off finitely
many small primes and bound each remaining factor by q_p^delta. Thus
an all-shell exponent gamma>0 for U implies the same exponent uniformly
for polynomial-size Q, with arbitrarily small extra loss and small
shifted scales retained. Conversely, Jensen, (218.5) and the fixed Euler
inverse recover U from a complete positive-bank L2 bound, when the FIELD
error gate is paid. Hence those bank and U shell-L2 exponent classes are
equivalent. This does not identify L1 with L2.

For f-only let p_F(d)=N_F^-1#{f in Fset:(f,d)=1},
K_X(a,b)=integral_X^(2X)g(log(q_a/x))g(log(q_b/x))dx/x and
c_a=mu_R(a)eta(a)1_((a,S)=1). The exact finite bank is

    B_F^sf=sum_(a,b)c_a conjugate(c_b)K_X(a,b)p_F(rad(ab)). (220.2)

The squared averaged FIELD instead has kernel p_F(a)p_F(b). These
kernels differ by the entire label covariance. No independent-prime
model is used at finite F. On the actual squarefree coefficient support,

    A(rad(ab))=A(a)A(b)sum_(d|gcd(a,b))q_d^-1.

Therefore the limiting bank has the exact positive feature expansion

    B_infty(X)=sum_(d squarefree,(d,S)=1)q_d^-1 ||V_d||_2^2,
    V_d(x)=sum_(d|a)c_a A(a)g(log(q_a/x)).                (220.3)

The d=1 term is ||W_A||_2^2, and all other terms are the full limiting
label variance. Absolute Gaussian majorants justify every rearrangement:
after the divisor expansion the absolute factor is A(rad(ab))<=1.

Replacing the FINITE kernel by this limit costs

    |B_F^sf-B_infty| << X^2 F^-1/2 log(2F)              [K],
    |B_F^sf-B_infty| << X^2 F^-1/2(1+log(2+X))^2        [Z]. (220.4)

Indeed the avoidance-probability error at rad(ab) is bounded by the
product of its separate divisor majorants, and each Gaussian sum is
O(x), or O(x log(2+x)) over Z. Thus this ENERGY replacement needs v>=4c
at exponent2-2c, whereas the FIELD comparison only needs v>=2c. Keeping
(220.2) exact avoids this extra approximation.

There is also a fully paid DIRECT limiting-bank return. If W_A has an
all-shell L2 exponent sigma>0, remove the primes of d from its weighted
Euler product. The inverse factors are(1-A_p eta(p)q_p^-s)^-1, whose
l1_sigma cost is at most C_(sigma,delta)q_d^delta. For squarefree d,

    V_d(x)=mu(d)eta(d)A(d)W_(A,d)(x/q_d).

Hence for any0<delta<sigma,

    B_infty(X) <= C ||W_A||_(sigma,2)^2 X^(2sigma)
                    sum_d q_d^(-1-2sigma+2delta).        (220.5)

The sum converges by A_R(T)<<T, and every d and small shifted scale is
included. Conversely B_infty>=||W_A||_2^2, followed by the fixed inverse
in G218. Thus B_infty and U have the same every-epsilon L2 exponent class
for gamma>0. Estimating B_infty directly would need no finite-F limit
error, but its ENTIRE infinite hole family must then be paid. This
corollary does not permit substituting a finite-bank bound without(220.4),
and supplies no arithmetic saving. It leaves the exact signed finite
field/Gram and the direct limiting bank as distinct lawful targets.
title: G220. Complete finite covariance and the limiting-bank alternative

statement:
## 3. A uniformly paid adaptive completion theorem

All convolutions below are Dirichlet convolutions; a(n)=mu(n)chi(n)
is a pointwise product. Fix 1/2<gamma<1, integer k>2, and
1<b<=2gamma. Put

    r=(k-2gamma)/(k-2), L=X^gamma, M=X^r,
    eta=1/(100kpq), B_X(n)=min(L,eta X^k/n^(k-1)).

No u>0 hypothesis is needed for this theorem; it is useful when
comparing to the earlier constant-cut core. Fix tau in[0,1], or allow
tau=tau_X in that interval with its choice frozen before x varies.
Define U_X(n)=B_X(n)^tau and V_X(n)=B_X(n)^(1-tau).
At tau=0 or1 use the literal convention B^0=1, even if B<1.
All comparisons against these positive real numbers are literal.

For each n, let m_{U(n)}(d)=a(d)1_(d<=U(n)); define m_V likewise.
This notation describes a family of coefficientwise finite identities,
not convolution by one global sequence with a moving index. Set

    Q_U(n)=sum_(d e=n) q_p(e)a(d)1_(d<=U(n)),
    Q_V(n)=sum_(d e=n) q_p(e)a(d)1_(d<=V(n)),
    S_tau(n)=sum_(d e l=n,d<=U(n),e<=V(n)) a(d)a(e)b_p(l),
    R_tau(n)=sum_(d e l=n,d>U(n),e>V(n)) a(d)a(e)b_p(l).

Then, at EVERY positive integer n,

    c_p(n)=Q_U(n)+Q_V(n)-S_tau(n)+R_tau(n).       (3.1)

Proof: for that n alone freeze both real cutoffs and apply
(a-m_U)*(a-m_V)*b_p=c_p-q_p*m_U-q_p*m_V+m_U*m_V*b_p.
This uses a*h=delta1, including all character-zero values. Freezing
separately at each n proves (3.1); replacing it by a global convolution
identity with a moving cutoff would not be valid. The formula remains
true when one or both cutoffs are below1. Every ordered factor pair,
shared prime and squareful compensation term is retained.

Claim (new restricted estimate): uniformly over tau in[0,1] and every
real x in[X,2X],

    |sum_n S_tau(n)f_x(n)| <<_(p,q,k) X^gamma,    (3.2)
    sum_n (|Q_U(n)|+|Q_V(n)|) <<_p X^gamma.      (3.3)

The sums in (3.2)-(3.3) have finite support for fixed X. For (3.3),
d<=U(n)<=L^tau whenever d>=1 is admissible (U may be below1),
and q_p is supported at1,p. Thus the Q_U support has n<=pL^tau,
and its absolute sum is at most(p+1)floor(L^tau); the V estimate is
the same with exponent1-tau. This proves (3.3), including endpoints.

For (3.2), fix an admissible pair d,e. It has
d<=L^tau and e<=L^(1-tau), so there are at most L pairs. For
0<tau<1 put W=max(d^(1/tau),e^(1/(1-tau))). The further condition
is B_X(de*l)>=W, hence the allowed l form exactly the single prefix

    1<=l<= (eta X^k/W)^(1/(k-1))/(de).           (3.4)

No rounding replacement is made. At tau=0 require d=1 and take W=e;
at tau=1 require e=1 and take W=d. Empty and one-term rows are allowed.
In every case de<=W, because d<=W^tau,e<=W^(1-tau).
If the row is nonempty, its whole real interval satisfies

    de (de*t)^(k-1) <= eta X^k.                 (3.5)

The exact Q=pq periodic sequence b_p has zero mean and Fourier
expansion sum_(j=1)^(Q-1) beta_j exp(2pi i jl/Q), with
sum|beta_j|<=pQ. In the j-th mode the phase is

    F_j(t)=jt/Q-(de*t/x)^k/(2pi).

It has a decreasing derivative; its correction from j/Q is at most
k eta/(2pi)<1/(2Q) by (3.5), uniformly on the FULL real shell.
Thus its derivative and each integer increment between row atoms lie
in[1/(2Q),1-1/(2Q)]. The elementary discrete summation argument of
G152 (or the identity g(v)=1/(exp(2pi iv)-1)=-1/2-(i/2)cot(pi v)
followed by summation by parts) bounds every prefix by O(Q).
The total variation of cotangent on this interval supplies the bound;
there is no continuous-integral substitute at an integer resonance.
Abel summation against the ACTUAL decreasing exp(-de*t/x^b) costs
at most twice this prefix bound. Each complete row is O_(p,q,k)(1).
At most L rows prove (3.2). There is no unpriced stationary region:
it belongs to R_tau under (3.1), not to this source.

This is different from replacing the old scalar u by gamma in a
rectangular certificate. The physical upper endpoint in (3.4) moves
with the pair d,e. The full small source is proved pointwise; it does
not acquire an unbounded row above M and does not need a tail repair.

O_(A_0,tau)(sqrt L log L)=o(L); Type I and the genuine short term
are smaller still. In particular

    ||G_tau-Z_X||_(L2([X,2X],dx/x))
       <<_(epsilon,A_0,tau,a) X^(-A_0+epsilon).          (G20)

The same holds for the finite physical field using G13. The four
diagonals, subpower restoration, O(sqrt L) bins and O(sqrt L) height
window survive. Eventually T_X>Y^2 since .01L>kappa sqrt L.
Constants and thresholds depend on the fixed choices; A_0, tau and a
may not vary with X in this theorem. A literal O(X^(-A_0)) follows
by applying G20 with A_0+1.

A simple working choice is **tau=1, kappa=C=D=2, a=3/4**.
All discarded fields then have exponent -1. For every fixed gamma>0,
the norm triangle inequality makes OPEN-GC equivalent to G3 up to
the usual arbitrary epsilon. This removes the old positive analytic
error floor from this architecture. It does not estimate Q_X.

For a scalar comparison, the inherited calibration
M(t)=O(t^beta), beta=.8749, implies |G_tau(x)|<<x^beta by Abel
summation and an exponentially weighted Gaussian derivative integral.
If a field approximation error is X^(q+o(1)), q<beta, then

    | ||G_tau||_2^2-||R||_2^2 | <=X^(beta+q+o(1)).       (G21)

Both ordered mixed terms and the error square are included. With G19,
q=-A_0. For an especially low target, G20's norm equivalence avoids

## The explicit arithmetic estimate sufficient for a gain

Let sigma be fixed with1/2<sigma<1 and write

  M_Y(s)=sum_(n<=Y) mu(n)chi(n)n^(-s).

The uncapped source(N2) has the exact Mellin representation

  C_(X,K)(x)=(-1)^(K+1)/(2pi i) integral_(sigma)
    e^(tau s^2/2)(1-s)^(K-1)L(s,chi)^(K-1)M_Y(s)^K x^s ds. (N17)

The contour can be moved from2 to sigma without residue: the pole at1 has been canceled, and M_Y is a finite polynomial. Define the nonnegative quantity

  H_(X,K)(sigma)=integral_R e^(-tau t^2/2)
    |1-sigma-it|^(K-1)|L(sigma+it,chi)|^(K-1)
                             |M_Y(sigma+it)|^K dt.         (N18)

Then ||C_(X,K)||_shell <=C_(sigma,tau) X^sigma H_(X,K). The difference from C^bal is already paid by(N4). Therefore the uniform estimate H<=X^(eta+epsilon) supplies(N14) with gamma=sigma+eta, and hence a zero-exclusion return, whenever1/2<gamma<1. We require all large scales and the specified orders, not numerical samples. The exponential threshold within this explicit sufficient estimate is

  eta<b6-sigma.                                             (N19)

At sigma=3/4 the first-gain threshold is eta<.124861. A concrete c=.125140 would require eta=.124860; c=1/6 requires eta=1/12; c=1/4 requires eta=0, always allowing every positive epsilon. These are OPEN sufficient estimates, not candidates certified by this report. The uniform K-band is a convenient sufficient family; no assertion is made that it is logically the weakest possible hypothesis over all architectures.

To obtain a common ordinary-character constant, the hypothesis must hold for EVERY fixed positive integer q and every complex ordinary character chi modulo q with the SAME gamma; its constants and onset may depend on that fixed character. A bound for one character supplies only that L-function's conclusion. No finite list of conductors or extension to Hecke data is inferred. Fix gamma and the finite source choices before taking large-scale thresholds; then choose the epsilon buffers needed for each target s with Re(s)>gamma.

The all-height obligation in(N18) is inexpensive but real. On this fixed line one-step summation of the periodic character, or the Hurwitz representation for the principal case, gives |L(sigma+it,chi)|<=C_(q,sigma)(1+|t|). Also |M_Y|<=C_sigma Y^(1-sigma). Put T_X=3sqrt(log X/tau). Since Klog(K+T_X)=o(log X), the entire |t|>T_X contribution is at most

  Y^(K(1-sigma)) exp(-tau T_X^2/2+o(log X))
    =X^(1-sigma-9/2+o(1))=O(X^-3).                         (N20)

For example absorb the polynomial into a Gaussian tail by maximizing its logarithm; beyond T_X its derivative is dominated by -tau t. This is not permission to discard the height band |t|<=T_X. The same estimate pays any larger height cap.

First coarse arithmetic attempt: retain any b>b6 with b<1 for which M_chi(z)<<z^b is supplied. For sigma<b, partial summation gives

  |M_Y(sigma+it)|<=C_(b,chi,sigma)(1+|t|)Y^(b-sigma).

Inserting this in(N18) and integrating the Gaussian times its polynomial yields

  H<=Y^(K(b-sigma)) exp(O_(b,chi,sigma,tau)(Klog(K+2)))
    =X^(b-sigma+o(1)).                                    (N21)

Thus the actual available summatory estimate gives back b, not b/K. At sigma=3/4 it approaches eta=.124861 from above and supplies no first gain. This failed coarse bound is retained because it is the strongest cheap original-data comparison, not a numerical parameter scan.

## 5. The growing-conductor branch exposed by rational frequencies

There is a substantive limitation beyond a diagonal heuristic. Let P
be prime with P not dividing the fixed modulus of chi and let (a,P)=1.
For Re s>1, direct finite character orthogonality gives the EXACT identity

 D_(a/P),chi(s):=sum_n mu(n)chi(n)e(an/P)n^(-s)
   = (1/(P-1)) sum_(psi mod P) psi(a) tau(conjugate(psi))
                                  /L(s,chi*psi)
      -chi(P)P^(-s)/L(s,chi*psi0).                    (5.1)

Here tau(conjugate(psi))=sum_(u=1)^(P-1)conjugate(psi(u))e(u/P),
psi0 is the principal character mod P, and products mean the ordinary
character on the common modulus with natural zeros. The first term
is precisely the P-unit part. For the omitted multiples n=Pm,
mu(Pm)=-mu(m)1_(P not dividing m); their phase is 1. This gives
the second term, including the zero at P^2, and proves (5.1).
Since tau(psi0)=-1, the psi0 coefficient can equivalently be written

       [-1/(P-1)-chi(P)P^(-s)]/L(s,chi*psi0),
       L(s,chi*psi0)=(1-chi(P)P^(-s))L(s,chi).

The curve includes x=P/(2*pi), where its additive phase is e(-n/P),
so a=-1 and the damping length is (P/(2*pi))^(3/2). Thus the proposed
complete source hypothesis encounters genuine growing-modulus twisted
L-functions. Bounds with constants depending arbitrarily on each fixed
character do NOT supply uniform control of this branch. No separately
reviewed low-conductor joint-density claim is imported here. Individual
uniform twist bounds plus absolute Gauss-sum summation can lose up to
square-root P; collective signed control, or a direct source proof,
would have to avoid that loss. Formula (5.1) is not used to claim that
such a loss is necessary for the actual signed sum.

This explains why the attractive diagonal exponent 3/2 in the source
energy is only a target. Neither fixed-conductor zero exclusion nor
discarding the nonprincipal twists proves it. Conversely, these
auxiliary twists do not change the scope of the completed return:
Section 3 itself excludes zeros of each original fixed L(s,chi), with
all heights and its principal pole exception paid.
