## 2. A1–13: independently reconstructing the infinite spectral core

Fix tau>0 and sigma>1/2, both independent of X. Write

    f(n)=mu(rad(n/3^v3(n))),
    F(x)=sum_n f(n)g_tau(log(n/x)).

In particular f(p^k)=-1 for every p!=3 and k>=1, while f(3^k)=1.
There are no squarefree zeros. On l2(N),

    T(m,n)=f(mn)(mn)^(-sigma),
    ||T||_HS^2=zeta(2sigma)^2.                            (R41-A1)

This is a real self-adjoint compact operator for an absolute reason, not a
cancellation estimate. For p!=3 put q=p^(-2sigma), R=q/(1-q). On the span
of e0 and (p^(-sigma k))_(k>=1)/sqrt(R), the literal local operator is

    H(R)=[[1,-sqrt(R)],[-sqrt(R),-R]].

For all positive exponent pairs i,j, f(p^(i+j))=-1, explaining the lower
right -R. At3 the operator is w3 w3^T, w3(k)=3^(-sigma k), k>=0.
The nonzero eigenvalues for p!=3 are

    lambda_+/-=(1-R +/- sqrt(1+6R+R^2))/2.

Set c=1/(lambda_++R). Direct substitution in
lambda^2-(1-R)lambda-2R=0 proves

    0<c<1, lambda_+=1+cR,
    1-c=c(1+c)R,
    u(0)=(1+c^2R)^(-1/2),
    u(k)=-c p^(-sigma k)u(0), k>=1.                     (R41-A2)

Since sum_p R_p<infinity, product lambda_p^+ converges to a finite positive
number and product u_p(0)>0. For finite sets J increasing to the primes
at least5, embed product_(p in J)u_p in the usual finite-support exponent
basis, with vacuum at all other primes. The inner product of two nested
such unit vectors is product_(p newly included)u_p(0), tending to1.
They are therefore Cauchy in l2. This explicitly constructs their limiting
unit vector u; it does not assume a complete infinite tensor eigenbasis.

The finite-prime semigroup projection P_J retains *all exponents* at its
primes, including2,3. T_J=P_J T P_J tends to T in HS norm by dominated
convergence of R41-A1. It is finite rank even though its semigroup index set
is infinite. Finite local spectral decomposition is consequently legitimate.
For 0<R<1,

    r(R)=|lambda_-|/lambda_+
        =(sqrt(1+6R+R^2)-(1-R))/(sqrt(1+6R+R^2)+(1-R)),
    d[(1-R)/sqrt(1+6R+R^2)]/dR
        =-4(1+R)/(1+6R+R^2)^(3/2)<0.

Thus1>r2>r5>r7>... . Each nonzero tensor eigenvalue is the leading
positive product times a product of distinct negative ratios. The two
largest moduli correspond to the empty set and {2}; the third is {5}.
Any product with at least two ratios is smaller than r5. The resulting core

    B=H2 tensor (w3 w3^T)
         tensor [(product_(p>=5)lambda_p^+) |u><u|]       (R41-A3)

has rank2. It is optimal in both operator and HS norm. For the operator
norm lower bound, any rank-at-most2 competitor kills a unit vector in the
span of the first three singular vectors. Its error there is at least the
third singular value. For HS norm, projection onto its output space captures
at most the first two squared singular values: diagonalize T_J^2 and use
weights in[0,1] summing to at most2. The displayed truncation attains both
finite bounds. Its positive-vector and eigenvalue products converge, so
B_J tends to B in HS norm. Compression of any fixed rank2 competitor still
has rank at most2 and cannot increase either error norm. Taking J to infinity
proves both claimed global optimalities. This resolves the author's stated
strongest infinite-compression concern without an omitted completeness step.

The first column, with every sign and small-prime factor retained, is

    B(n,1)=C_sigma b_sigma(n)n^(-sigma),
    C_sigma=product_(p>=5)lambda_p^+/(1+c_p^2R_p)>0,
    b(2^k)=-1, b(3^k)=1, b(p^k)=-c_p for p>=5,k>=1.      (R41-A4)

The products defining C converge absolutely in their deviations from1;
the O(R_p) bound already suffices. This is the actual spectral column.
It is not obtained by replacing the source's primes by independent signs.

At p>=5 the local Dirichlet series of f and b are, respectively,
(1-2z)/(1-z) and (1-(1+c_p)z)/(1-z). Their ratio and inverse are

    A_p(z)=1+(1-c_p)sum_(k>=1)2^(k-1)z^k,
    D_p(z)=1-(1-c_p)sum_(k>=1)(1+c_p)^(k-1)z^k.          (R41-A5)

At2 and3 both factors are1. For each fixed rho>1/2, the absolute
nonconstant local coefficient sums are bounded by

    (1-c_p)p^(-rho)/(1-2p^(-rho))
        <=C_(sigma,rho)p^(-2sigma-rho).

The denominators are uniformly positive since p>=5, and the prime sum
converges. Positive Euler majorants therefore prove, with no analytic
continuation premise,

    b=a*f, f=d*b, a*d=delta1,
    sum_n (|a(n)|+|d(n)|)n^(-rho)<infinity.              (R41-A6)

This prices both inverse directions. Suppressing either direction would
weaken the important conclusion from equivalence to mere sufficiency.
Prime2 is kept exactly; replacing its kernel by the generic factor would
change the source's boundary zero and can introduce an unaffordable pole.

The coefficient bounds |b|,|f|<=1 and these weighted sums justify the
Gaussian convolution identities absolutely. For example, choose rho>1
for Fubini and bound the positive coefficient majorant Z(t)<=C t^rho
on all t>0, with the Gaussian left tail
paying t<=1. For the sharp exponent use the all-real-shell norm

    ||V||_rho=sup_(T>0)T^(-rho)||V||_(L2([T,2T],dx/x)).

Minkowski bounds convolution by sum|a(n)|n^(-rho); the analogous d bound
gives the converse. Large dyadic estimates extend to real shells using
two neighboring dyadic intervals; finitely many middle scales and Gaussian
left tails supply the other values of T. Consequently for fixed gamma>.5,
with the usual every-epsilon allowance on all sufficiently large shells,

    ||sum_n b(n)g_tau(log(n/x))||_[X,2X] <<_epsilon X^(gamma+epsilon)
       iff ||F||_[X,2X] <<_epsilon X^(gamma+epsilon).     (R41-A7)

For precision one applies the weighted theorem at rho=gamma+epsilon/2,
starting with a smaller epsilon in the hypothesized bound. The moment form
with exponent2gamma+epsilon is equivalent after renaming epsilon. There is
no deletion of any cross term and no inheritance by arbitrary masks.

With w_x(n)=n^sigma g_tau(log(n/x)), the physical readout is exactly

    F(x)=<w_x,T e1>,
    C_sigma Bfield(x)=<w_x,B e1>.

The squared norm of w is the sum of n^(2sigma)g_tau(log(n/x))^2.
Comparison with its Gaussian integral gives O(x^(2sigma+1)); the sum's
maximum term costs only O(x^(2sigma)), so the bound also covers lattice
discretization for x>=1. Hence a column error epsilon_X has shell readout
O(X^(sigma+.5)epsilon_X). The stated sufficient budget

    epsilon_X << X^(gamma-sigma-.5)                     (R41-A8)

is correct. It is an upper-bound interface, not a necessary lower bound
for every arithmetic residual. At sigma=.75 the proposed gamma=.874864,
5/6,3/4 give exponents -.375136,-5/12,-1/2. The fixed nonzero spectral
residual does not acquire decay as X grows. Nor does optimal low rank make
its retained column easy: R41-A7 is exactly the full OPEN-F3 problem. A
different signed spectral combination may still be useful if its complete
readout is estimated. No general impossibility of operator methods follows.

### Fixed ordinary characters and the nonvanishing numerator

For a fixed ordinary character chi, including zeros at ramified primes,
complete multiplicativity gives

    chi b=(chi a)*(chi f), chi f=(chi d)*(chi b).

All products with chi on the right are coefficientwise before Dirichlet
convolution. Their absolute weighted norms do not increase. In particular
the exact equivalence extends separately to each fixed character, not
uniformly in a growing conductor. On the unit-index subspace the operator
is D_chi T^(q) D_chi; this is left and right unitary multiplication, **not**
unitary conjugation. Singular values are preserved, while self-adjointness
need not be. If2 is unramified, the core is optimal rank2; if2 is ramified,
the stated all-positive core is optimal rank1. It is not then claimed to
be optimal rank2. Prime3 is rank1 when present, absent when ramified.
Extending by zero returns exactly the missing rows/columns and coefficients.

Direct local multiplication, not an analogy to zeta, gives

    sum_n chi(n)f(n)n^(-s)=W_chi(s)/L(s,chi), Re s>1,
    W_chi(s)=(1-2chi(2)2^-s)
       /[(1-chi(2)2^-s)^2(1-chi(3)3^-s)^2]
       *product_(p>=5)(1-2chi(p)p^-s)/(1-chi(p)p^-s)^2. (R41-A9)

A ramified factor equals1. Each generic factor differs from1 by
-z^2/(1-z)^2, z=chi(p)p^-s. On Re s>=rho>.5 the generic product and its
inverse converge normally and are uniformly bounded: 2p^-rho<1 for p>=5
and the local deviations are summable. Denominators have no zeros for
Re s>0. The retained prime-two numerator has zeros only on Re s=1.
Thus W_chi is holomorphic and nonzero in .5<Re s<1.

The Mellin transform initially is exp(tau s^2/2)W_chi/L. An all-scale
Gaussian norm exponent gamma>.5 continues the transform holomorphically
to Re s>gamma, including every fixed height, by shell Cauchy–Schwarz;
logarithmic derivatives are paid by a small positive exponent buffer and
the Gaussian left tail. Multiply by the continued L-function before
evaluating at a possible zero. The identity theorem gives a nonzero right
side at every point gamma<Re s<1, contradicting any such zero. The known
right-edge result finishes the half-plane assertion; the principal pole
at1 is retained. There is no assumed all-height reciprocal bound hiding
in this direction of the argument. A hypothesis must be proved for each
fixed chi to earn that character's conclusion. No such new bound is proved.

**Ancestry:** W29's trace-class product tensor and Sobolev readout already
separate compactness from arithmetic evaluation; its odd local block has
lower-right0 and its prime-two block is different. AM18–21 already separate
finite divisor-inverse conditioning from actual readout. G28–32 and the
reviewed Sol D04 supply existing weighted-reconstruction interfaces.
W41's admitted delta is the explicit all-prime-power f3 optimal core and
its two weighted inverse kernels; the abstract spectral facts and Mellin
return are not new broad mechanisms.

## 3. B1–6: actual occupations and the complete unexposed covariance

Let P be any finite prime set containing2 and excluding3, Q=product P,
a_P(n)=product_(p in P)(1-2*1_(p|n)), and r_P(n)=f(n)a_P(n).
The identity f=a_P r_P is pointwise. Both factors retain all valuations;
r_P consists of exactly the primes outside P other than3. The complete
period mean of a_P is product(1-2/p)=0. No squarefree probability law
is used.

For any Q-periodic a of mean0 and |a|<=1, let its discrete Fourier
coefficients be b_k, k=1,...,Q-1. They satisfy |b_k|<=1. With
h(t)=g_tau(log t), zero-extended to t<=0, ordinary Poisson and m>=2
integrations by parts give

    |sum_n a(n)h(n/x)|
       <=2 zeta(m)(Q/(2pi))^m x^(1-m)||h^(m)||_1.       (R41-B1)

Indeed the reindexing r=Qj-k is one-to-one over nonzero integers not
divisible by Q. Its absolute m-series is bounded by2zeta(m); there is
no lost extra factor Q. Flatness of h at0 pays every boundary term.
This is a direct periodic-source calculation, not a masked application
of a completed alternating field.

For fixed0<delta<1 and Q<=X^(1-delta), even one fixed sufficiently large
m proves any prescribed negative power uniformly on [X,2X]. The stronger
displayed bound with m=2+floor(delta log X/tau) is also valid, because
the *explicit* G7 contract bounds its growing derivative order:

    ||h^(m)||_1<=K_tau 4^m m! exp(tau(m-1)^2/2).

Substitution bounds the logarithm by
-delta^2(log X)^2/(2tau)+O_(delta,tau)(log X loglog X).
Constants are independent of the actual list P, but depend on the fixed
delta and tau. Thus F_P=sum a_P(n)g_tau(log(n/x)) is O_A(X^-A) for every
fixed A. Shrinking delta with X or changing tau is not part of the theorem.

Put Z=sum g_tau(log(n/x))=exp(tau/2)x+O_A(x^-A), by period1 Poisson,
and use the actual positive all-integer measure mu_x(n)=g_tau(log(n/x))/Z.
Each prime-occupation pattern indicator is Q-periodic, with CRT mean

    pi_P(s)=product_(s_p=1)1/p *product_(s_p=0)(1-1/p).

Apply R41-B1 to indicator-minus-mean, of absolute size at most1. The
normalization is exact: its Gaussian sum divided by Z is the difference
between actual pattern probability and pi_P(s). Summing over all patterns
costs at most2^|P|<=Q<=X. Increasing the prescribed negative power once
pays this factor, so the full L1 pattern error is O_(A,delta,tau)(X^-A),
uniformly over the full shell and every permitted P. No rare pattern was
discarded and no division by a possibly tiny individual pi_P(s) was used.
This is an absolute joint-law error, not a relative conditional-law estimate.

W38 used a squarefree Gaussian measure, giving occupation1/(p+1) and a
logarithmic partial-parity bias. W41's measure is on all integers, giving
1/p and the prime-two zero mean. Both statements are valid at their
different sources; W41 does not repair or disprove W38's result.

Define the explicit bilinear covariance

    C_P=E[a_P r_P]-E[a_P]E[r_P].

Then, without approximation,

    F=Z C_P+F_P E[r_P].                                  (R41-B2)

Since |E r_P|<=1 and Z is comparable to X throughout the shell, for any
chosen permitted family P_X the complete field estimate is equivalent to

    integral_X^(2X)|C_(P_X)(x)|^2 dx/x
                       <<_epsilon X^(2gamma-2+epsilon). (R41-B3)

Both directions follow from the norm triangle with the uniform rapidly
small F_P error; the gamma>.5 restriction is needed for the existing
zero return, not for this elementary covariance identity. Keeping P={2}
already yields the equivalence. For example, with p_j=Pr(1_(2|n)=j) and
m_j=E[r_{2}|1_(2|n)=j], direct expansion gives
C_{2}=2p0p1(m0-m1). The exposed even/odd probabilities are close to1/2;
their *conditional rough means* still carry the full problem.

More generally, m_P(s)=E[r_P|s] satisfies

    C_P=sum_s Pr(s)(a_P(s)-E[a_P])m_P(s).                (R41-B4)

All these conditional means and signed interactions remain. The accurate
unconditional product law bounds none of their needed cancellation.
For a fixed ordinary chi replace r_P by chi r_P, including zero values.
The positive law stays unchanged, the explicitly bilinear formula stays
valid, |r|<=1 still pays the error, and R41-A9 supplies the exact return.
No character independence, pair-mask domination or ideal-norm transfer
is implied. The covariance target uses the fixed F for Mellin continuation,
not the moving periodic field.

## 4. Other actual first tests and their limits

**09: single-prime transport.** Each edge n<->pn has log length at least
log2, so any transport carrying M units solely on such edges costs at
least M log2. The actual f3 summatory bound with fixed .874865<beta<1
follows from its paid convolution with the original detector coefficients
and the buffered Möbius bound. Hence positive and negative unit counts on

and exp(it log(N+1)) on[-T,T] have Gram eigenvalues1+/-|sinc(TDelta)|,
Delta=log(1+1/N). For0<TDelta<=1 the small one is at most

**28: unrenormalized finite Euler product.** On real0<sigma<1 the positive
products product_(p<=P)(1-p^-sigma) tend to0. Prime harmonic divergence
alone proves this: otherwise inverse finite Euler products would stay
bounded while eventually containing each arbitrarily long harmonic sum.
But the paired alternating series eta(sigma)>0, and
1/zeta(sigma)=(1-2^(1-sigma))/eta(sigma)<0. These products do not converge
to the continued reciprocal on that interval. This kills the specified

## 5. Protected parked audit20: an exact observability test

This is critic mathematics, selected before outcomes. It tests the seed's

Let the observation map on coefficients be E:C^N->C^m and the target

    |a*alpha|^2<=C||E alpha||^2 for every alpha
      iff a belongs to range(E*),
    C_min=a*G^dagger a.                                  (R41-O1)

Necessity follows by taking alpha in ker E: a must annihilate that kernel,
equivalently lie in range(E*). On its orthogonal complement diagonalize G,

including every fixed polynomial density. Isolated samples satisfy neither

## 6. Uniform parked audit25: rescue the checksum and price its return

    (A v)(n)=sum_(k<=n)v(k),
    (D v)(n)=sum_(d|n)v(d),
    C_N=A D-D A.

They preserve all integer labels. Counting the same divisibility relation

### 3.3 Actual-norm cancellation is stronger than leading Gram data

For ANY exact two-part split F=T+R with ||F||<=C X^beta, write
b=||R||. Then

    <T,R>=-b^2+<F,R>,
    ||T||^2=b^2+O(b X^beta+X^(2beta)).                (R3.5)

These are exact identities plus Cauchy--Schwarz. If b is comparable
to X/L^d, the Gram of (T,R), normalized by the ACTUAL b^2, is

    [[1,-1],[-1,1]]
       +O(X^(beta-1)L^d+X^(2beta-2)L^(2d)).           (R3.6)

For the fixed-power split, d=3 and b~(-B(rho))N_X. If instead one
normalizes by its leading asymptotic norm, an additional error
O(L^-1+X^(-eta)L^4) enters. That is distinct from the power-small
accepted-full-field error in (R3.6).

For the critical split with kappa^2>=2exp(3tau), define

    W_kappa(x)=2x/L^2 Phi(kappa^2 X/x),
    N_kappa^2=||W_kappa||^2
       =4X^2/L^4 integral_1^2 s Phi(kappa^2/s)^2 ds.

The positive finite integral is fixed. By (R2.1),
||R_z-W_kappa||=O(X/L^3), so b is comparable to X/L^2. Therefore
(R3.6) holds with d=2. Normalizing by N_kappa^2 introduces a separate
O(1/L) asymptotic error. The accepted F bound additionally gives
T_z=-W_kappa+O(X/L^3+X^beta), a negative leading prefix; that last
prefix statement explicitly uses F, unlike the positive band (R2.9).

Finally, let a=||T|| and r_X=Re<T,R>/(ab). Cauchy--Schwarz gives
r_X>=-1, and exactly

    ||F||^2=(a-b)^2+2ab(1+r_X).                       (R3.7)

For 1/2<gamma<.874872, the desired full norm estimate with arbitrary
epsilon allowance is equivalent, after renaming epsilon, to BOTH

    |a-b|<=C_epsilon X^(gamma+epsilon),
    1+r_X<=C_epsilon X^(2gamma-2+epsilon)L^(2d),      (R3.8)

where d=3 for a fixed-power split and d=2 for the stated positive
critical profile. Necessity follows from the two nonnegative terms
in (R3.7). Sufficiency follows from a,b comparable to X/L^d; without
separately invoking F for that comparability, the first proposed
bound itself forces a comparable to the directly known b.

The present source theorems do not prove (R3.8) at a new gamma. The
accepted beta yields only its existing baseline. A field remainder
O(X/L^4) or O(X/L^3) remains larger than X^gamma for every fixed
gamma<1; writing a leading cancellation does not estimate its actual
residual at the required power precision. These are upper-bound
limitations, not lower bounds for the actual residual.

If (R3.8) were proved at such a gamma, (R3.7), the true O(X) diagonal,
and current-proof G29--G31 would return the COMPLETE fixed-field
moment and its zero exclusion. The fixed convolution equivalence is
used only after reconstructing F. It gives no hereditary equivalence
for the moving rough masks, SP/RN or pair02 subfamilies, arbitrary
Hecke twists, or selected low-gcd signed submasks.

## D04. Smooth the literal Gaussian four diagonals with every collar paid

### Exact source and replacement

Use current-proof G11--G20, with tau=1,kappa=C=D=2,a=3/4 and Y=floor(X^.495). Keep each original bin I_i, its actual intersection with Y<d<=Dmax, all ordered pairs i+j=-2,-1,0,1, mu(d), the complete alternating ell source and eta(s)=(1-2^(1-s))zeta(s). Native interval endpoints/cap inclusions are not redefined. There are O(sqrt(log X)) ordered components. On every nonempty bin the endpoint sizes D_i obey

    X^(.495+o(1))<=D_i<=X^(.505+o(1)),
    D_i D_j=X^(1+o(1)) on every retained ordered pair.       (D04.1)

Here D_i is its actual upper endpoint; clipping changes these only by subpower factors. This follows from Y, Dmax=B_X/(Y+1) and each of the four bin diagonals. None is an SP smooth-state bin.

Fix0<delta<.495. For each exact interval choose a C-infinity function psi_i(v) with0<=psi_i<=1, supported within its real interval, equal to1 away from collars of lengths endpoint*X^-delta at both endpoints. For a very short clipped interval the collars may cover it completely; setting psi_i=0 is allowed. Then on the integers the difference from the original indicator is supported in the two collars, including every integer endpoint whose convention differs. There is no missing endpoint atom. The collar contains O(D_i X^-delta+1) integers; its n-values are D_i X^o(1). Such functions exist from a fixed C-infinity step with derivatives vanishing at its endpoints. Their k-th log derivatives cost O_k(X^(k delta)); derivative constants are NOT free subpower costs.

Define finite literal polynomials

    U_i(s)=sum_(d in I_i)mu(d)d^-s,
    V_i(s)=sum_(d>=1)mu(d)psi_i(d)d^-s,
    Delta_i=U_i-V_i.

The new source is a deliberately changed mask. Its differences remain explicit. For the accepted buffered rational Mertens bound M(t)=O(t^beta), take the conservative beta=8749/10000. At a=3/4, Abel summation at both original endpoints gives

    |U_i(a+it)| << (1+|t|)D_i^(beta-a),
    |Delta_i(a+it)| << X^(-delta+o(1))D_i^(1-a).           (D04.2)

The second inequality uses only |mu|<=1 and the full collar count. Because delta<.495, D_iX^-delta tends to infinity and absorbs the+1 endpoints. It makes no assumption of Möbius short-interval cancellation. The empty/clipped-bin case is included.

Put

    Zpsi_X(x)=(2pi)^-1 integral_[-T,T]
      exp((a+it)^2/2)eta(a+it)
         sum_(i+j=-2,...,1)V_i(a+it)V_j(a+it)x^(a+it)dt,
    T=2sqrt(log X).

This retains all ordered interactions and both independent height variables when its square is expanded. It does not introduce H projectors or claim anything about the distinct H form. No ell-dependent source mask has been smuggled into G8/G9.

### Complete norm error

The exact signed product difference is

    U_iU_j-V_iV_j=Delta_i U_j+U_i Delta_j-Delta_i Delta_j. (D04.3)

Use |eta(a+it)|<=|a+it|/a, the fixed Gaussian exp(-t^2/2) and Plancherel of the inverse Mellin transform with the difference restricted to[-T,T]. It is valid for arbitrary L2 Fourier data; there is no truncation error in this step. The shell factor costs at most(2X)^a. Equations D04.1--2 therefore give

    ||Z_X-Zpsi_X||_[X,2X]
       << X^(q_smooth+o(1)),
    q_smooth=max(101/200+(99/200)beta-delta,1-2delta).   (D04.4)

For example X^a D_i^(1-a)D_j^(beta-a) equals
D_i D_j^beta X^o(1). The maximal allocation puts exponent.505
on the trivial collar factor and.495 on the beta factor; the reverse
single-boundary term has the same maximum. The double-boundary term
costs X^(1-2delta+o(1)). The component count and all Gaussian height
polynomials are subpower. This prices EVERY replaced endpoint and
their ordered mixed interactions, rather than dropping a boundary square.

Current G20 pays ||G-Z_X|| at exponent-1+epsilon. Thus

    ||G-Zpsi_X||_[X,2X] << X^(q_smooth+epsilon)+X^(-1+epsilon). (D04.5)

For any fixed gamma>.5 and q_smooth<gamma, the every-epsilon norm target
||Zpsi_X||<<X^(gamma+epsilon) is equivalent to the original complete
Gaussian shell norm target. Choose epsilon smaller than the fixed
margin to use the triangle inequality in both directions. No global
Mellin transform of the moving psi family is asserted: D04.5 returns
to the fixed G BEFORE zero exclusion.

All choices are fixed once per target, with constants depending on
them. Exact conservative budgets using beta=.8749:

| gamma | Conditional c | delta | first collar exponent | double collar exponent | gamma-q_smooth |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| .8748 | .1252 | .064 | .8740755 | .872 | .0007245 |
| .87449 | .12551 | .064 | .8740755 | .872 | .0004145 |
| 5/6 | 1/6 | .106 | .8320755 | .788 | .001257833333... |
| 3/4 | 1/4 | .19 | .7480755 | .62 | .0019245 |

These are PAID COMPLEMENT budgets, not achieved moments. OPEN-SMOOTH
is the complete signed norm of Zpsi_X at its row's gamma for every
epsilon and all sufficiently large dyadic X. It is still open. The
original Gaussian pole-exclusion return is G1--G3 after D04.5.
No fixed-character or Hecke completion is deduced from a zeta-only
alternating source: those need their exact existing adapters.

Strongest objection: endpoint smoothing is often paid back by derivatives.
Here the collars are paid without derivatives; an ensuing analytic proof
of OPEN-SMOOTH must STILL debit X^(k delta) for k-th cutoff derivatives.
Even this smooth source has |V_i|<=|U_i|+|Delta_i| and only reproduces
the baseline moment exponent absent new signed arithmetic cancellation.
It is not a power gain generated by smoothness. Near gamma=.87449,
any proposed integration-by-parts saving must outweigh its.064-per-
derivative loss and establish the full two-height/component norm.

Ancestry: U-SCALE, old thin-annulus TA and native sharp-mask/Sobolev
adapters, plus W35's literal Gaussian completion. TA concerns a different
capped three-Möbius source and is not imported as this estimate. [restricted research revision]
hybrid smoothing changes fixed kernels and is not the same moving
endpoint collar. The narrow claimed delta is this explicit literal
four-diagonal replacement and complete numerical complement price;
no literature novelty claim or new cancellation mechanism.

Functional signature: actual G11 interval factors / interior endpoint
tapers / retain signed four-diagonal sum / unpaid OPEN-SMOOTH / fixed-G
return with q_smooth and all height/TypeI/product complements paid.
Next action: seek a genuine two-height mean for these smooth factors
whose derivative cost fits the fixed margin, or stop if it cannot beat
the original sharp mean. Re-proving the collar bound is not arithmetic progress.

# Written proof component selection at the validated frontier

Status at selection: **c5 = 7821/62500 = .125136**, boundary **theta5 = 54679/62500 = .874864**, is the highest accepted written endpoint supplied to this lane. Candidate c6 = .125139 remains under separate review. This is a dependency and simplification packet, not the final mathematical proof, a claim of formal verification, or a record submission. The controller will choose the endpoint after the frozen review. No proof-assistant work, kernel jobs, changing c6 drafts, provider calls, or canonical writes were performed here.



## 1. Selection decision

Use the original PR9 arithmetic, reflection, old moments, compensated probe and zero-return architecture; Gao's PR15 actual-source transport and two-transform argument; and the accepted [restricted research revision] strictly interior affine local theorem plus its complete endpoint certificate. Earlier [restricted research revision]/[restricted research revision]/[restricted research revision]/[restricted research revision] endpoint theorems are useful provenance, but none is needed as an intervening numerical theorem. The original 7/8 initialization is needed; its later quartic fixed-point optimization is not needed as an endpoint premise.

This is source-proved reuse, subject to the pinned base contracts. It does not assert that an exponent ledger alone proves the new local estimate, or that existing individually compiled components already form the complete endpoint proof. The accepted [restricted research revision] independent review supplies the integration evidence. The new work in this packet is the exact symbolic simplification in §4 and the c5-only finite-prefix restriction, not an independent reproof of every PR9 analytic import.

A shortest coherent exposition can have five mathematical modules: (i) conventions and imported base estimates; (ii) actual-source affine local moment; (iii) physical selector, complements and weighted shifts; (iv) complete rational endpoint certificate and feedback; (v) common-saving Mellin contradiction and ordinary-character transfer. Keep finite arithmetic and reflection proofs in a pinned dependency appendix, rather than repeating them in every module. “Imported” must identify exact hypotheses and source, not leave an unnamed stronger moment assumption.

## 2. Minimal dependency graph and the contracts it must retain

| ID | Required mathematical object and exact scope | Selected source |
|---|---|---|
| F0 | Eisenstein conventions, natural extended sextic rows, fixed character family, beta-star and the unconditional 7/8 initialization | PR9 T0, B0.1, B1.1, B2.1 |
| F1 | Finite Gauss identities, reciprocity and imprimitive local zeros, with unit sectors and conductor factors | PR9 B1.1–B1.3, B4 |
| F2 | Completed reflection, whole-index marks, both collision masks and marked reflected-energy estimate | PR9 B2.2–B2.6, especially B2.35–B2.41 |
| F3 | UM and MI, original positive-slot MP with price 6 kappa, unrestricted MP0; the plain induction is independent of the inverse induction | PR9 B0.1, B3.1–B3.4 |
| G0 | Finite fixed dictionary, natural conductor, signed reconstructed row and natural row zeros; uniform masks and Fourier transport inside the joint norm | PR15 `SignedReconstruction.tex`, `FixedDictionaryBridge.tex`, `FourierMaskTransport.tex` |
| G1 | Unmarked density for that fixed dictionary and polynomial height costs; raw sixth-power lifting | PR15 `PlainUnmarkedDensity.tex` |
| G2 | Actual comparison rectangles, two transforms, joint label Cauchy, paid low deletion, joint high count, extracted errors, zero terms, fixed-inducing and principal terms | PR15 `PhysicalLocalAssembly.tex`; accepted [restricted research revision] review §§3–7 replaces its local numerical region |
| A | Strictly interior affine local moment with fixed atlas, common profiles and four derivative pairs | [restricted research revision] integration/source report; independent review §§3–8 |
| P | Literal reflected physical input, original whole-slot selector, all shortening complements, Euler shifts and conductor-weighted mass | PR9 B0.41–B0.44; PR15 `RestrictedCanonicalSource.tex`, `PhysicalScaleShortening.tex`, `EndpointAssembly.tex`; [restricted research revision] review §§8–9 |
| E | Current rational geometry, all rows and tails, exact polynomial certificate, actual kappa feedback | [restricted research revision] review §§10–11 and independent coefficient receipt |
| R | Target-independent Delta, nonvanishing Mellin numerator, supremum contradiction, imprimitive factors and ordinary-character transfer | PR9 B0.7, T2–T4; [restricted research revision] review §11 |

Edges: F0,F1→F2; F1,F2→F3; F0,F1,F3→G0,G1; F2,F3,G0,G1→G2; G2 plus the new atlas arithmetic→A; F0,F1,F3,A→P; F0,P plus the rational certificate→E; F0,F1,E plus the original probe/continuation identities→R. G2 uses only old MP/MP0 in descendants, never A recursively. Base proofs remain a directed chain, not an induction on the improved endpoint.

The actual paired moment in A is

    sum_(k eligible) |S_(k,1)(Z^n1) S_(k,2)(Z^n2) Q_(k,I)|^2
        << Z^(M+epsilon) H_J,       U=Z^M,

with the source radial majorant. It holds for the fixed natural row family, actual `Q_* = internalQ(Q,eta0)` nonzero/proper/contained in (72), literal non-FixedInducingRow gate, canonical prime pools, one common slot profile, allowed relative ray characters, and independent plain heights. Common polynomial-size punctures are row-independent after outer labels are frozen. The same statement holds for the four profile pairs needed by two-variable scale recovery. It is not a theorem for arbitrary coefficients, arbitrary row-dependent profiles, arbitrary growing parent conductors, or arbitrary subfamilies selected before reflection.

For the selected strict interior let

    Lambda=8379/2009=171/41,  B=199499/200900.

Use .41M≤n1,n2≤.44M, .034M≤z≤.04M and

    (n1+n2)/M + Lambda z/M ≤ B.

The closed plane 2009(n1+n2)+8379z≤1995M is stronger as a source theorem, but its epsilon-dependent limiting atlas is unnecessary for this endpoint. Keeping the single fixed interior atlas avoids an extra limiting argument while preserving c5 exactly.

## 3. Simplifications that are valid, and shortcuts that are not

**Remove numerical ancestors as premises.** [restricted research revision] used price 4.498, [restricted research revision] 4.405, [restricted research revision] 4.38, [restricted research revision] 4.368 with an original plain cap .4223. [restricted research revision] supplies the current affine region directly. Carry forward their resolved source obligations, not their endpoint constants or all their alternative envelopes. Containment of the [restricted research revision] polygon in [restricted research revision] is a provenance check, not a lemma needed for the final contradiction.

**Use fixed 9/2 only where its role permits.** The old source moments in the local descendants can take the safe coefficient 9/2 from beta-star≤7/8. The physical endpoint marked count and its feedback still require kappa=2 beta-star−1. Freezing kappa=3/4 throughout would change the endpoint estimate and is not justified by the present certificate.

**State the genuine MP0 contract directly.** The all-free-row density proof has a legacy dummy zero-profile slot used for a source adapter. An exposition can state the resulting no-slot theorem directly, with its unrestricted bounded lengths, independent heights, nonprincipal-inducing exclusion and fixed-family constants. This is a representational simplification; one must not import the different all-free-row length penalty into the physical MP0 application.

**Keep one fixed-family height contract.** Density chooses its own internal detector exponent, then returns a polynomial height degree. The endpoint later chooses a separate external height exponent small enough for that degree. Record this order once and cite it, instead of pretending a single universal small height exponent serves every fixed target and every source estimate.

**Do not remove marks or label structure.** In F2 the mark divides the whole index c n^3, c and n may share primes, and the mark may meet the row. The whole-index split and both collision masks are required. The unmarked norm of size (HN)^epsilon(H+H^2/N) does not replace the marked estimate. Likewise, low bins are imposed only on the allocated positive children after both transforms; deletion is paid before the indicator is dropped. They are not hereditary through Poisson transformation.

The high branch uses the actual signed row and both orientations. Its natural primitive conductor is ≤ a fixed K times the row norm, with a fixed finite translated dictionary and natural nonunit zeros. A mere existence of an abstract character gives no such conductor bound. The first projector is part of the joint row reconstruction; the second projector need not divide that row and is paid through its extraction scalars. A density bound followed by another independent first-label count would overcharge; dropping that count before proving the joint reconstruction would undercharge. These are substantive identities, not bookkeeping one may omit.

The original-data amplification theorem requires sigma>0 and mesh<sigma/6; it does not require an additional unsupported upper-smallness bound on sigma. Its prime pool, normalization and threshold precede live data. Its actual changed retained ball is needed; assigning a smaller nominal radius to the old ball does not prove an estimate. The exceptional energy keeps K_phys^(5/6). Preserve the two original principal residue scalars and their actual u=1 row.

## 4. New exact simplification of the fixed atlas

Write S=(n1+n2)/M, t=z/M, g/M=(S+(9/2)t−1)_+. For e=1/100000, alpha=1/400000 and b_j=.034+je, the existing cell b_(j−1)<t≤b_j has

    g_j=B−1+(9/2−Lambda)b_j,
    a_j/M=(7/3)g_j+alpha,
    A_j=B−(Lambda−1)b_(j−1),       1≤j≤600.

Use j=1 also at t=.034. Here g_j>0 and A/M≤A_j. The main low reserve is exactly

    (a_j/M)/15−7g_j/45 = alpha/15 = 1/6000000.

The main high reserve at its worst parameter .7 is

    H_j=35/54−(7/10)A_j−(26/9)(a_j/M).

Its coefficient of b_j vanishes because

    (7/10)(Lambda−1)=(182/27)(9/2−Lambda).

Thus every cell has the same high reserve

    H_j=(1995−2009B)/270−(7/10)(Lambda−1)e−(26/9)alpha
       =1687/221400000 > 0.

No 600-case enumeration is needed to prove these two inequalities. This cancellation explains why A_j and a_j must remain paired. Taking their maxima separately destroys it and gives the wrong error estimate.

The other displayed fixed-inducing/zero obligations 1−A_j−k a_j/M are affine in j. The slopes of A_j+k a_j/M per cell are respectively

    k=4: −1/1025000;   k=5: 11/1640000;   k=9: 307/8200000.

Consequently their minima are at j=1 for k=4 and j=600 for k=5,9, giving exactly the accepted reserves

    15135217/200900000, 1975539/32144000, 2900439/803600000.

This permits a universal cell-index argument with a few endpoint checks. It does not eliminate the actual finite choice of amplifier, the source transforms, other error inequalities, or the separate bidegree-(2,3) endpoint certificate. The source already supplies positive margins for the remaining errors; they should be imported explicitly or proved with their actual formulas, not inferred from these three inequalities.

**Optional c5-only prefix.** At the current physical geometry, z_I≤z_A≤51907630715077/1423737411131700<.0365. Therefore the new-moment branch uses at most the first 250 original cells. The exact unpadded upper cell index is 246, but 250 is a simpler robust prefix with a round upper bound. Keep the original e, b_j, a_j, A_j formulas unchanged. All global 600-cell lower bounds remain valid on this subset, and the finite maximum over source thresholds can be restricted to the subset.

For parent width 1+nu, normalize t'=z_I/(1+nu). The new-moment branch begins at the moved cutoff .034(1+nu), so t'≥.034, while t'≤z_A<.0365. The prefix remains valid. Upper plain cutoffs only relax; lower plain cutoffs move together to .41(1+nu). For c5, nu≤10^−8 is below the displayed nominal positive lower margins, and the old complements still retain their positive reserves after .153nu and .41nu charges. Also require nu smaller than the independently chosen common loss budget; 10^−8 is a cap, not a replacement for that choice. Real scale/capacity padding is chosen within the accepted positive margins before the target. Do not transfer this prefix claim to c6 without its actual width and padding audit.

`check_selection.py` checks exactly these rational identities, c5 geometry/corners, complement reserves and the finite-prefix bound. It does not reproduce a large author computation or claim analytic/formal verification.

## 5. Endpoint interface that cannot be shortened away

The accepted c5 geometry is

    h=3969737987/5000000000, ell=7838/46875,
    x=5598946039/15000000000, y=6892893961/15000000000,
    kappa_*=23429/31250, d0=1/200,
    d_-=h−.001, d_+=h+10^−10, t0=.001.

It has ell=11/3−4theta, x=1+ell−h, y=h−2ell and k_probe=5/6−x/3−ell/6, so (5x+y)/12=theta−k_probe. In the shaped interval set n=1−y/d+t and z_A=(B−2n)/Lambda. The physical gain is governed by

    d z_A(0)=[2y−(2−B)d]/Lambda.

Retain the intercept loss 1−B. The selected subset I is common to the whole amplitude class and all four derivatives. If L=ell/d and q=L^−1 sum_i w_i g_i=delta p, where 0≤g_i≤delta/2 and 0≤p≤1/2, the selector yields gain at the target capacity z_A even if the positive-main supply is exhausted. It supplies z_I≤z_A; it does not supply z_I≈z_A or positive-main width ≥z_A. Errors have zero gain.

Every shortening requires one of four gates: short slot uses old budget 2(.4223)+(9/2)(.034)=.9976; short plain uses .41+.4223+(9/2)(.0365)=.99655; the remaining region uses A; empty I uses unrestricted MP0 with no affine sum gate. Their reserves are 3/1250 and 69/20000 before the stated padding charges. Below d=.5 use the original selector, not its d≥.5 convenience wrapper. Its supply inequalities, positive original slot widths and total ell are retained.

For shifts, use the original decomposition h0 h_r≲Y, combined conductor and weighted coefficient mass

    sum |c_u(h0,h_r)| h0^(delta/2) << U^epsilon.

At small shift t, damping minus gain loss is t(delta/2−q/Lambda)≥0. At large shifts use the old clipped capacity; its payment function is continuous with slopes 7/18 and 1/2, and at t0 has reserve ≥73/4189500. At zero capacity use the physical MP0 adapter, whose actual reflected scales remain bounded by the original support. An unweighted Euler deletion estimate or a second repeated-prime conductor charge cannot replace this argument.

For the finite certificate use D=3−p−2p/(3kappa_*), P=2(1−p)(1−p/(3kappa_*)), V=5/6−delta, J=VD+delta P and R=1−delta+delta PV/(2J). On 0≤delta≤3/4, 0≤p≤1/2, J≥288935/1686888. The shaped exponent is

    G=(1+delta)/2+13h/75−y/2−ell/2+ell q
      +d(1/4+3R/4−17/50)−q[2y−(2−B)d]/(2Lambda).

The old-row expression replaces its last term with −q min(d,2y−d)/(12kappa_*). The retained receipt provides all 204 coefficients of J(theta−v−G), bidegree at most (2,3), on 10/6/1 rectangles at shaped d=h, old d=h−.001, old d=.5, with savings 10^−6,10^−5,10^−3 respectively. Nonnegative Bernstein basis plus the exact covering of the closed rectangle proves the inequalities. Affinity covers middle d; old-row convexity covers d0≤d≤.5; derivative ≤2 pays d_+−h. Keep floor, small nonprincipal, principal-contour and far-row reserves. Finite coefficient positivity alone is not this complete return.

Most importantly, take kappa=2 beta-star−1, with mu=beta-star−theta. The actual shift kappa−kappa_*=2mu costs less than 2mu/50 locally and 2mu/8 on old rows. Hence the saving below beta-star improves by at least 24mu/25 and 3mu/4. No zero at the supremum is assumed. statement:
## 2. The actual matrix and its coefficients

Let chi be any ordinary Dirichlet character, with its original natural zeros. Zeta is the character of modulus one. Put

    F_chi(s)=1/L(s,chi),
    a_chi(n)=mu(n)chi(n),
    I=[1/5,1/4],
    D_chi,delta(s)=det [F_chi(s+(i+j)delta)]_(0<=i,j<=2).       (D1)

Initially Re s>1 and delta>0 are real. All relevant Dirichlet series converge absolutely. Write

    V_delta(a,b,c)
      =(a^(-delta)-b^(-delta))
       (a^(-delta)-c^(-delta))
       (b^(-delta)-c^(-delta)).                              (D2)

The matrix in D1 is the sum over n of the rank-one matrices

    a_chi(n)n^(-s) v_n v_n^T,
    v_n=(1,n^(-delta),n^(-2delta))^T.

Finite Cauchy--Binet, followed by absolute convergence, gives

    D_chi,delta(s)=sum_(a<b<c)
      mu(a)mu(b)mu(c)chi(abc) V_delta(a,b,c)^2 (abc)^(-s)
      =sum_n h_chi,delta(n)n^(-s).                          (D3)

There is no conjugation in this analytic determinant. Conjugation is introduced only in the eventual physical energy. The factors are ordered by their integer sizes, and the strict inequalities a<b<c are part of the coefficient definition. Shared primes are allowed. Squareful individual factors have their actual zero Mobius coefficients. No coprimality or squarefree-output condition has been inserted.

Let lambda(n)=(-1)^Omega(n). For every nonzero tuple, including shared primes,

    mu(a)mu(b)mu(c)=lambda(abc).

Consequently the coalesced coefficients have the useful exact form

    h_chi,delta(n)=chi(n)lambda(n) W_delta(n),
    W_delta(n)=sum_(a<b<c; abc=n; a,b,c squarefree)
                         V_delta(a,b,c)^2 >=0.             (D4)

This is a coefficient-aware simplification, not an independence assumption: the whole sign is Liouville parity of the output, and different outputs still interact. For all delta>0, |h_chi,delta(n)|<=d_3(n); that majorant is uniform on I.

Every prime-power output is zero. Indeed if n=p^k, the only possible nonzero squarefree factors are 1 and p, so three distinct factors do not exist. At a product of two distinct primes there is exactly the tuple (1,p,q):

    h_delta(pq)
      =(1-p^(-delta))^2(1-q^(-delta))^2
                             (p^(-delta)-q^(-delta))^2.    (D5)

Here and below omission of chi means zeta. In particular, for odd primes p,

    h_delta(2p)
      =(1-2^(-delta))^2(1-p^(-delta))^2
                             (2^(-delta)-p^(-delta))^2.

It tends to (1-2^(-delta))^2 2^(-2delta)>0 uniformly for delta in I.

## 4. Original labels, jumps, restoration and masks

The predicate \(A_z\) is defined using distinct primes; individual
Möbius zeros still eliminate nonsquarefree factors. On its one-large-prime
support there is a unique representation \(d=Dp\), where \(D\) is
squarefree \(z\)-smooth and \(p>z\) is prime, and \(\mu(d)=-\mu(D)\).
The two-factor sign is therefore \(\mu(D)\mu(E)\), with no extra sign.

For a prime \(p\), let \(B_p(n)={\bf1}_{p\mid n,\ \omega_p(n)=1}\).
Directly counting primes before and after this threshold gives
\[
 A_{p^-}=A_p-B_p,\qquad
 \Psi_p-\Psi_{p^-}
  =B_p(d)A_p(e)+A_p(d)B_p(e)-B_p(d)B_p(e).           \tag{RNR9}
\]
The last term counts a shared threshold prime once. There is no
coprimality between \(d,e\), between their cores, or between the two
large primes. The rule remains a predicate identity even at Möbius
zeros, which continue to contribute zero.

On nonzero RNR1 labels, \(d,e<B/Y\). Two primes greater than
\(\sqrt{B/Y}\) in either factor would have product exceeding that
factor. Hence \(\Psi_{\sqrt{B/Y}}=1\) there. The terminal identity
\(P_{\sqrt{B/Y}}=S\) is exact, but its \(X^{.2525+o(1)}\) scale is
outside the proved asymptotic range.

Define
\[
 K(v)=\sum_{\ell\ge1}b(\ell)k(\log(\ell v)).
\]
Alternating Poisson gives a smooth profile supported in \([0,e]\),
flat to every fixed order at zero, with every fixed absolute logarithmic
moment finite. Initially for \(\Re s>1\), absolute integration gives
\[
 \int_0^\infty K(v)v^{s-1}\,dv=M(s)(1-2^{1-s})\zeta(s).
\]
The left side continues entirely by flatness and compact support.
The pole at1 on the right is canceled. Consequently
\[
 \int K(v)\,dv=(\log2)M(1)>0.                        \tag{RNR10}
\]
This identity includes the full alternating spectrum. It does not
assert \(K(v)\ge0\) or justify absolute integration of the separate
unpaired restoration terms at \(s=1\).

For \(x\in J_X\), every active original profile has
\(de\ell\le ex\le2e^2X<B\). Thus extending the restoration cap adds
zero profiles on this shell. SP8 is then applicable to
\((1-E)\Psi_z\), and also to its zero/one-large-prime subclasses:
these are bounded original-pair masks independent of \(\ell\) and
fixed while \(x\) varies. It gives
\[
 P_z(x)=\sum_{d,e>Y}\mu(d)\mu(e)(1-E(d,e))\Psi_z(d,e)K(de/x)
           +O_A(X^{-A})                             \tag{RNR11}
\]
for each fixed \(A\), uniformly in \(z,x\).
All original product-bin endpoints are retained in the definition;
their removal is paid by this estimate. No derivative of the arithmetic
mask is used, and no restoration-dependent mask is authorized.

statement:
# [private research revision]: exact recovery from an imaginary Hankel shift

The [source](high-ceiling/report.md) and [independent review](high-ceiling-review/report.md)
prove an exact recovery formula and its finite approximation for each fixed
ordinary Dirichlet character, with its specified modulus and natural zeros.
The controller read both full arguments and accepted HC2–HC8 with the four
qualifications in review R10. This removes moving-median and cofactor-selection
requirements for this new readout. It gives no arithmetic gain, no estimate
for the older D20 moment and no Hecke or growing-conductor conclusion.

## Exact signed source and coefficient

Write a(n)=mu(n)chi(n), F(s)=1/L(s,chi), z=delta+i theta. Cauchy–Binet gives

    det[F(s+(i+j)z)]_(0<=i,j<=2)
      =sum_(u<v<w) a(u)a(v)a(w)V_z(u,v,w)^2(uvw)^(-s).

The square is analytic, not a squared modulus. Its36 signed permutation
occurrences have exponent patterns024,033,114,123,222. Replacing (uvw)^(-s)
by the fixed Gaussian g(log(uvw/x)) defines H(theta,x), with a uniform
absolute bound O_delta(x). For EVERY unramified prime p, its frequency p^2
has the exact coefficient

    B_(p^2)(x)=a(p)[M(x/p)-g(log(p/x))-a(p)g(log(p^2/x))],
    M(y)=sum_n a(n)g(log(n/y)).                         (HC-I1)

There is one contributing monomial per distinct set {1,p,c}. Squareful
outputs, free composites divisible by p, complex phases and both excluded
atoms remain. Choose the least unramified p. The entire coefficient then
lies on the face (1,p,c), c>p.

With h=1/(4p^2), the nonnegative probability kernel

    K_h(theta)=3h/(8pi) sinc(h theta/4)^4

has Fourier support [-h,h]. Thus P_p U=integral_R K_h exp(2i theta log p)U
extracts p^(-2delta)B_(p^2). The associated rank-one orthogonal projection
obeys Pythagoras and retains the entire signed c,d correlation. Its full-line
median-complement projection vanishes. This is a statement about a linear
functional; it supplies no pointwise arithmetic positivity, zero complement
energy or hereditary signed-submask estimate.

## Finite face, costs and equivalence

Fix delta=3/5, truncate product pc to
[X exp(-2sqrt(log X)),2X exp(2sqrt(log X))], and theta to |theta|<=X^(1/5).
Both product tails cost X^(-1+o(1)). The missing theta mass is at most
64/(pi h^3 T^3); its source cost is O_chi(X^(2/5)). In particular truncated
median leakage is paid, not declared zero. Let J_X be the literal finite
face field, P_X its phase-weighted integral and

    Q_X=integral_(|theta|<=X^(1/5)) K_h(theta)
                         integral_X^(2X)|J_X(theta,x)|^2 dx/x dtheta.

The coherent square of P_X has both theta variables and all ordered mixed
terms; Cauchy–Schwarz gives ||P_X||_2^2<=Q_X. More strongly, direct expansion
of V_z(1,p,c)^2 gives

    J_X(theta,x)=A(theta)M(x/p)+R_X(theta,x),
    A(theta)=a(p)p^(-2z)(1-p^(-z))^2,
    |R_X|<<_(chi,epsilon) X^(2/5+epsilon).

The four shifted terms, both removed atoms and both product tails are
included. |A| is bounded above and away from zero uniformly in theta.
For E_M(X)=integral_(X/p)^(2X/p)|M(y)|^2 dy/y and
b_X=integral_(|theta|<=X^(1/5))K_h|A|^2, the exact norm comparison is

    |sqrt(Q_X)-sqrt(b_X E_M(X))|<=r_X,
    0<c_chi<=b_X<=C_chi, r_X<<X^(2/5+epsilon).         (HC-I2)

Consequently, for each fixed gamma>2/5, all-scale Q_X<<X^(2gamma+epsilon)
is equivalent to the original Gaussian square-moment estimate at that
exponent. This is an exact arithmetic obstruction to treating twist
orthogonality alone as a saving. L1 readout and L1 Gaussian bounds have
their own equivalence; no equivalence between L1 and L2 is asserted.

The24 monomials with every exponent positive form a transform holomorphic
on Re(s)>2/5 and a field O(X^(2/5+epsilon)). Their unconditional comparison
with the full field costs X^(7/5+epsilon) for the two mixed terms. Under a
target norm X^gamma the cost is instead X^(gamma+2/5+epsilon), with error
square X^(4/5+epsilon). The unconditional bound pays the1/6 and1/4 target
comparisons; the half-strip comparison requires the hypothesized target
norm. Any detected pole lies in the12-term free sector, but an individual
fixed-theta cofactor can still vanish.

## Conditional return and direction

An all-scale L1 bound for P_X at any fixed gamma>2/5 first recovers the
ONE fixed M. Its Mellin transform is exp(s^2/2)/L(s,chi), with an entire
left tail and locally convergent right integral for Re(s)>gamma. The
nonvanishing multiplier excludes every L-zero in that open half-plane,
at every height. Constants may depend on the fixed character. The stronger
Q_X estimate suffices; neither estimate is proved here. The prospective
gamma=5/6,3/4,1/2 returns remain conditional.

The discovery pass also rejects the specific fractional future growth map
s-A(1-s)^alpha, 0<alpha<1: its high-zero signals move arbitrarily far left.
It does not reject all future filters. Existing fixed-alpha renewal
contracts remain valid, with no new signed contraction.

The incumbent remains the separately accepted written c2=.125128. The
decisive next step is an actual estimate for the complete signed arithmetic,
or a different source that both changes that obligation and retains an
all-height return. Finite polynomial checks corroborate the algebra; they
are not uniform arithmetic or formal-kernel proofs.
title: [private research revision]: exact recovery from an imaginary Hankel shift

### Isolated root: accept with the stated absolute constants

For a polynomial Z=1+Az+R, put lambda=B/|A|^2. Assume |A|>=8 and lambda<=1/8, with sum|c_k|<=B for R=sum_(k>=2)c_k z^k. Since |z|<=1 implies |R(z)|<=B|z|^2, on |z|=2/|A| one has

    |1+Az|>=1,    |R(z)|<=4lambda<=1/2.

Rouche gives exactly one zero counted with multiplicity in that disk. If B>0, on the circle centered at -1/A of radius2lambda/|A|,

    |1+Az|=2lambda,
    |R(z)|<=lambda(1+2lambda)^2<=25lambda/16<2lambda.

This small disk lies inside the first and inside |z|<1. Hence the same unique root alpha is simple, and

    |A alpha+1|<=2lambda,
    (1-2lambda)/|A|<=|alpha|<=(1+2lambda)/|A|.       (R2)

B=0 gives the exact linear root. All other zeros are outside the larger disk, so alpha is the unique nearest root. No unproved reality assumption enters the complex-character case.

Factor the ENTIRE polynomial as Z(z)=(1-z/alpha)Q(z), Q(0)=1. This exact division is important: a truncated reciprocal series would not establish the endpoint formula. From (R2),

    |1+1/alpha|>=4|A|/5-1>=|A|/2,
    |1+1/alpha|<=1+4|A|/3<=2|A|.

Thus

    (|A|/2)|Q(-1)|<=|M(N)|<=2|A||Q(-1)|.           (R3)

The constant checks include the extremal |A|=8,lambda=1/8. These are rigorous inequalities, independently checked also with rational arithmetic; no numerical root approximation is needed.

statement: # W52: paid localization of signed renewal errors No strict increase in c is proved. The frozen seed calibration was c9=500579/4000000=.12514475, theta9=.87485525; the appended root correction advances the incumbent to c10=.12514596, theta10=.87485404, with the same stated source and admission obligations. The useful new candidate is a paid localization of G92's **merged integer-state** renewal error: for the r=1 exact collar, the complete short-cofactor coefficient mass costs O(N^(2/3)); primes at most (log(2N))^A cost O_epsilon(N^(1-1/A+epsilon)), A>1. The error price multiplies these counts by the full defect bound D_N. The remaining signed error has p<(N)^(1/3), pm. Its arithmetic bound and a suitable approximate solution remain open. Two other developments quantify failed certificates. An orthogonal lift that keeps different integers in separate fibers cannot improve a generic Cauchy readout below the squarefree-unit count. No fixed finite Dirichlet-polynomial preconditioner can contract the full gamma-weighted supremum space at 0n)e_w, of squared norm 1/k!. Equal signed word amplitudes without the 1/k! factor project to k! a_n, not a_n. Antisymmetric word components lie in ker P, so cancellation there does not change the surviving scalar coefficient. For the minimum-norm lift R a and the full arithmetic readout P*1, Cauchy has price sqrt(sum_(n in S)1/omega(n)!) * sqrt(sum_(n in S)omega(n)!) >= |S|. (W2) This is not an artifact of choosing factorial weights. More generally, let H be an orthogonal sum of fibers H_n. Suppose u_n,v_n in H_n satisfy =1, using the convention linear in the first slot. The exact source and observable are U=sum a_n u_n and V=sum v_n. Then =M_chi(N), but ||U||||V|| >= sum_(n in S)||u_n||||v_n|| >= |S|. (W3) The first inequality is scalar Cauchy and the second is the individual extraction identity. This covers arbitrary Hilbert geometry **within** each orthogonal integer fiber and any exact diagonal rescaling. It does not cover an operator creating correlations between different n, an arithmetic-specific estimate for , or a nonlinear argument. For completeness, the certificate floor has exponent one: |S| = kappa_q N + O_q(sqrt N), kappa_q=(phi(q)/q) product_(p not dividing q)(1-p^-2)>0. (W4) Expand mu(n)^2=sum_(d^2|n)mu(d). Coprimality forces (d,q)=1; the number of m<=N/d^2 with (m,q)=1 is (phi(q)/q)N/d^2+O_q(1). Summing the floor errors to sqrt N and completing the d^-2 series each costs O_q(sqrt N). The product is positive because sum p^-2 converges. This proves W4 without a prime-distribution theorem. The N=210 checks give |S|=129,85,106 for q=1,4,5; the corresponding raw Cauchy prices are about158.409,93.659,122.349. These check the finite formula only. W1--4 are the proof. The maximal-headroom hope of importing free-word orthogonality therefore fails at its specified generic projection step. A redesigned method must estimate interaction between **different integer fibers** before generic Cauchy. The old ordered-prime operator already avoids k! overcounting and still owes its actual signed readout; this result supplies no improvement to it. ## 3. Development 2: no finite preconditioner in the full sup norm (W52-02) For gamma>0 let B_gamma contain all functions f on [1,infinity), extended by zero below1, with norm sup_(x>=1)x^-gamma|f(x)|. For a sequence c define the locally finite dilation operator (T_c f)(x)=sum_(n<=x)c(n)f(x/n). Its extended operator norm, allowing infinity, is exactly ||T_c||_(B_gamma->B_gamma)=sum_(n>=1)|c(n)|n^-gamma. (W5) The upper bound is the triangle inequality. For the lower bound, fix K, take x=K and assign f(K/n)=(K/n)^gamma conjugate(c(n))/|c(n)| for nonzero c(n), n<=K, and zero elsewhere. The arguments K/n are distinct, ||f||<=1, and x^-gamma T_cf(x)=sum_(n<=K)|c(n)|n^-gamma. Let K increase. The same infinite-space lower bound holds if f must be constant on each integer interval [j,j+1). For a fixed finite prefix n<=K, take a separate integer X tending to infinity with X>K(K+1). The values floor(X/n), n<=K, are distinct and each has no other integer n' in its quotient fiber. Put f on those intervals equal to floor(X/n)^gamma times the aligning phase, and zero elsewhere. The resulting ratio tends to the finite prefix in W5. This does **not** identify any single finite-X floor-merged norm with the unmerged price. It shows that arbitrary floor-invariant inputs over all scales still attain every fixed coefficient prefix. Let b be any fixed finitely supported complex sequence, with support at most B, and set r=delta-b*chi. **Finite-preconditioner obstruction.** At every 0B not dividing q, r(p)=-b(1)chi(p). Its prime contribution to W5 is infinite. Indeed sum_p 1/p diverges: otherwise the finite products product_(p<=Y)(1-1/p)^-1 would stay bounded, whereas each dominates the harmonic sum through Y. Removing finitely many ramified primes does not change divergence, and p^-gamma>=p^-1. Thus ||T_r||=infinity in this case. Natural zeros are kept, never divided out. The certificate would have a genuine complete return if it existed. Since a*chi=delta, T_chi M_chi=1, M_chi=T_b 1+T_r M_chi. (W6) If ||T_r||=kappa<1 and T_b1 in B_gamma, the Banach inverse supplies U=(I-T_r)^-1T_b1 and ||U||<=||T_b1||/(1-kappa). This identifies U with the actual M_chi **without assuming M_chi is already in B_gamma**: kappa<1 forces b(1)!=0, and W6 determines the function successively on integer intervals from its smaller x/n arguments. The small interval [1,2) gives U=1, and induction gives U=M_chi. The zero-exclusion return is in section5. The negative theorem is only for a fixed finite b and the full arbitrary-input weighted supremum norm. It does not forbid an infinite cancellation-sensitive inverse, a changing preconditioner with a completely paid return, or an invariant space restricted by real arithmetic constraints. Nor does it follow merely from a finite matrix being triangular. Checks with b(n)=mu(n)chi(n), n<=30, verify r(p)=-chi(p) for all36 primes in(30,210] and q=1,4,5; they do not replace the divergence proof. ## 4. Development 3: a paid complement in merged integer renewal (W52-01) ### 4.1 The inherited exact source, with all endpoints Fix an ordinary complex Dirichlet character chi modulo q. Let P^-(1)=infinity and P^+(1)=1. On integer states m>=1 and lower prime threshold p, define R(m,p)=sum_(n<=m,P^-(n)>p)mu(n)chi(n). At the root the threshold is1. Least-prime factorization gives exactly R(m,p)=1-sum_(p=1 suppose F equals R on the exact collar m<=p^r. That collar is descendant-closed: a child has m'=floor(m/ell)<=m and ell>p, so m'<=ell^r. Thus Delta=0 throughout the collar. In particular for r=1 the collar value is1; for r>1 it generally is not1. G92's finite triangular inverse and integer merging give F(N,1)-M_chi(N) =Delta(N,1)+sum_(p prime,m>p^r) C_N(m,p)Delta(m,p), C_N(m,p)=-chi(p) sum_(N/[p(m+1)]m, and v>m also. Consequently any nonempty fiber containing u<=m is a singleton even before the smoothness and squarefree restrictions. A fiber can never mix a short cofactor with a long one. This is valid for every character; a natural zero simply makes its coefficient zero. Let S_r(N) be the number of active squarefree q-unit paths d=pu whose cofactor satisfies u<=m=floor(N/(pu)) and m>p^r. For every such path, p u^2<=N, p^(r+1)u=2)min(sqrt(N/j),N/j^(r+1)) <= (4+1/r) N^((r+1)/(2r+1)). (W10) To check the constant, split at J=ceil(N^(1/(2r+1))). The first sum is at most2sqrt(NJ), at most2sqrt(2)N^((r+1)/(2r+1)); the tail is at most N/(r J^r). The displayed larger constant covers all N>=1. Because W9 proves these are genuine singleton fibers, their exact absolute coefficient mass is S_r(N), with no removed cross-depth cancellation. If D_N bounds |Delta(m,p)| at all active prime states, their total error is at most (4+1/r)D_N N^((r+1)/(2r+1)). (W11) For r=1 this is5D_N N^(2/3), already below the incumbent exponent. This is a bound on a specified complement of the defect transfer, not on the remaining Mobius sum. ### 4.3 Paying the small-prime complement Fix A>1 and let Y_N=(log(2N))^A. After removing the short singleton fibers, consider active fibers with p<=Y_N. Every associated d=pu is squarefree and has P^+(d)=p<=Y_N. Thus the absolute coefficient mass of their whole contribution is bounded by Psi_sf(N,Y_N)=#{d<=N:d squarefree,P^+(d)<=Y_N}. For any01-1/A. Since A(1-sigma)<1, the exponential in W12 is N^o(1). Hence, for every epsilon>0, Psi_sf(N,Y_N) <<_(A,epsilon) N^(1-1/A+epsilon). (W13) There is no assertion of a small finite-N constant, and no estimate of cancellation inside this sector. The logarithmic cutoff is frozen at the root N in every term of this partition. The exact finite price W12 remains available if the asymptotic threshold is too large. ### 4.4 The remaining region and exact return Every remaining path has u>m>p^r. Since N>=pum>pm^2>p^(2r+1), its state satisfies Y_Np^r imply omega(u)>=r+1 for squarefree u; these paths have at least r+2 prime factors in d. All such statements concern this restricted support; no unsigned lower bound for the whole merged norm is inferred. Define H_F(N) to be the complete signed sum C_N(m,p)Delta(m,p) over the remaining fibers, using W8 literally. Empty fibers and natural zeros remain zero. There is no extra absolute value inside H_F. W8 partitions exactly as F(N,1)-M_chi(N)=Delta(N,1)+E_short(N)+E_small(N)+H_F(N), |E_short|+|E_small| <=D_N[(4+1/r)N^((r+1)/(2r+1))+Psi_sf(N,Y_N)]. (W15) This is a complete paid complement: the short singleton and small-prime classes are disjoint, and every remaining active class is in W14. In particular all p>=N^(1/(2r+1)) are already paid by W11. W15 does not replace the actual merged C_N by independent path errors. **Conditional arithmetic contract.** Fix r>=1, A>1, and a common gamma with max((r+1)/(2r+1),1-1/A)0 and all sufficiently large integer N satisfy D_N <<_(chi,epsilon) N^epsilon, |F(N,1)|+|Delta(N,1)|+|H_F(N)| <<_(chi,epsilon) N^(gamma+epsilon). (W16) Root-dependent F is allowed, provided W7--8 and all three bounds hold on that same root's entire reachable state system. Then W13--16, after choosing smaller epsilon allowances, prove M_chi(x)<<_(chi,epsilon)x^(gamma+epsilon) for every sufficiently large real x. The integer result extends through floor x. Section5 gives the full ordinary-character zero exclusion. Examples of **unproved target contracts**, with every complement already priced: | Proposed gamma | r,A | Paid exponent before epsilon | Consequent c if W16 were proved | |---|---|---|---| | .87 | 1,7 | 6/7 | .13 | | 5/6 | 1,5 | 4/5 | 1/6 | | 3/4 | 1,3 | 2/3 | 1/4 | These are not new endpoint claims. No F satisfying W16 has been constructed. The old terminal-only approximation has an unbounded defect, so W11--16 cannot be applied to it as if D_N were bounded. Choosing F=R makes the defect zero but leaves F(N,1)=M_chi(N), which is circular and supplies no progress. Root-value control, root-defect control, and the **complete signed** hard-region error are separate unpaid requirements. The principal character remains in scope; complex-character phase averaging is not an admissible substitute. The next mathematical action is now narrower: construct an approximation with a subpower full defect, or exploit the correlation between its actual defect and the signed smooth interval coefficient in W8 **inside W14**. The paid short/small sectors should not be reinvestigated unless the approximation's defect price changes. A bound only for each depth, each prime, or an averaged character does not establish W16. ## 5. Full zero-exclusion bridge For completeness, suppose the common-gamma every-epsilon/every-large-x M_chi bound has actually been proved for every fixed chi. For Re s>gamma, A_chi(s)=s integral_1^infinity M_chi(x)x^(-s-1)dx (W17) is holomorphic. On each compact subset choose an epsilon below its distance from gamma; the bound also controls all differentiated logarithmic factors. On Re s>1, absolute Dirichlet convergence and a*chi=delta give A_chi(s)=1/L(s,chi). Analytic continuation of L A=1 excludes every zero of the actual L(s,chi) in Re s>gamma. For a principal character its pole at1 corresponds to a zero of A, and does not obstruct this identity. The actual character, including nonunit zeros, is used throughout, so no imprimitive factor is silently restored or removed. Every height is included by holomorphy of the entire half-plane. Constants may depend on chi; no moving-conductor or Hecke-family extension is asserted. W17 is a proved implication, not a proof of its unproved arithmetic premise. The incumbent analytic framework is not used to manufacture W16, and none of its source obligations is declared discharged by these calculations. ## 6. The other three first tests **W52-14, determinant-line H stimulus: scoped failure of the raw object.** The actual JN source is a complete signed sesquilinear sum with b(pi)conjugate(b(pi')), the CRT phase, h-characters of exponent3, mark exponents2 and4, both full pre-Fourier projectors, original rooted mark arrays and distinct-norm deletion. An SDP encoding only those independent constraints cannot improve this optimum. statement:
## R3. CRT supply, uniform AP error and sharp stated thresholds

For half-bandwidth h>=1 choose distinct primes p_r>h, p_r not dividing q, for every 0<|r|<=h. With

    Q=q product_r p_r^2,
    n=1 (mod q), n=-r (mod p_r^2),

CRT gives a coprime class a0 modulo Q: p_r cannot divide r. Every allowed shifted neighbor is squareful. The source at n retains modulus one, and its character equals 1. Nothing about the sign of mu(n) was needed.

For any coprime residue a0 mod Q, expand mu(n)^2=sum_(d^2|n)mu(d). Only d coprime to Q contribute. For d<=sqrt N the compatible progression has modulus Qd^2 and count N/(Qd^2)+error of modulus at most one. The total counting error is at most floor(sqrt N). The omitted Euler main tail is at most 2 sqrt N/Q for N>=4. Therefore

    count = (N/Q) product_(p not dividing Q)(1-p^-2)
                    + error of modulus <= 3 sqrt N,
    count >= N/(2Q)-3 sqrt N.                       (R3.1)

The product is >=1/zeta(2)>1/2; for instance the elementary integral comparison gives sum_(n>=2)n^-2<1. This proves the uniform-in-Q estimate actually used. No asymptotic in a moving arithmetic progression or PNT in progressions was imported. If Q is too large, the displayed lower bound is simply uninformative, as it should be.

Deleting the at most 2h endpoint integers gives

    K >= max(0,N/(2Q)-3 sqrt N-2h).                  (R3.2)

The elementary prime allocation is also valid. The central binomial coefficient lies between 4^m/(2m+1) and (2m)^pi(2m), because each prime's contribution to its factorization is at most 2m. This proves pi(x) >= c x/log x for sufficiently large x, and hence permits 2h primes above h and outside a fixed ramified set below C_q h log(2h). Enlarging C_q handles bounded h. Thus

    log Q <= log q+4h log(C_q h log(2h)).

For h=o(log N/loglog N), K=N^(1-o(1)). For h=floor(kappa log N/loglog N), with fixed 0<kappa<1/8, the lower bound is N^(1-4kappa-o(1)); precisely that restriction makes the AP main term dominate sqrt N. This argument is uniform over N-dependent banded P, but q stays fixed. It is not an estimate uniform in growing conductor.

Consequently a certificate energy O_(chi,epsilon)(N^(2gamma+epsilon)) for every epsilon requires kappa >= (1-gamma)/4. A strict improvement below gamma11 therefore requires kappa > .0312864909. At .8748, 5/6 and 3/4 the necessary thresholds are respectively .0313, 1/24 and 1/16. They are necessary widths only. The O/small-o errors do not prove anything at an equality threshold, and the theorem makes no such assertion.

For arbitrary symmetric offsets D_N in [-(N-1),N-1] minus {0}, let k=|D_N|. Assign each r a distinct prime not dividing qr. At each assignment there are at most k-1 previously used primes and omega(q)+floor(log_2 N) other forbidden primes. The first

    J=k+omega(q)+floor(log_2 N)+1

primes suffice, uniformly over the actual offsets, even if chosen after seeing the arithmetic source. Their sizes are O(J log(2J)). Therefore

    log Q <= log q+2k log(C J log(2J)).

All allowed neighbors **inside** [1,N] are squareful; outside neighbors are irrelevant, so there is no endpoint deletion. This proves K=N^(1-o(1)) when k=o(log N/loglog N), and K>=N^(1-2kappa-o(1)) when k~kappa log N/loglog N with 0<kappa<1/4. A target gamma requires kappa >= (1-gamma)/2 in that regime. In particular strict gain needs kappa > .0625729818; the .8748, 5/6, 3/4 thresholds are .0626, 1/12, 1/8.

Here k counts **all distinct offsets used anywhere in the matrix**, including both signs. A uniformly bounded row degree with a large union of offsets is not covered. Long prime-dilation edges in particular do not satisfy this small-offset-bank assumption just because a few edges leave each vertex. The arbitrary-offset result is stronger than merely bounding the maximum shift, but it is not a theorem against arbitrary sparse metrics.

For P=D+E >= ell ell*, D>=0 with the prescribed local support and E Hermitian with ||E||<=eta, retain the author's complete correction:

    a*Pa >= K^2-eta(K+N).                            (R3.3)

Indeed ell_I*D_II ell_I >= K^2-eta K, D has no actual I-cross terms and a nonnegative complementary energy, while a*Ea>=-eta||a||^2>=-eta N. PSD of D is essential here. When K=N^(1-o(1)), a fixed gamma<1 target forces eta>=N^(1-o(1)); small individual entries do not establish a small operator norm. The source-dependent and signed nonlocal escapes remain open.

**Record delta:** the matrix isolation principle is elementary, but its uniform actual squarefree supply for arbitrary small offset banks and its explicit nonlocal bill are useful new refinements of the retained diagonal norm obstruction. W60's different bounded-prime-edit/short-edge graph isolation is related ancestry, not the same hypothesis or counting argument. No literature-priority claim is justified.

### 4.1 Full collision and local multiplicity, with endpoints

Let r_G(n)=#{r>G:r^2|n}. Its first moment is <=2Y/G. The exact second-moment identity is

 sum_(n<=Y)r_G(n)^2
  =sum_(r,s>G)floor(Y/lcm(r,s)^2) <=16Y/G, Y>=1.               (LG2)

Every sum on the left and the nonzero part on the right is finite. In the inequality write r=g u,s=g v,(u,v)=1. The condition is g>G/min(u,v). For every t>0, sum_(g>t)g^(-2)<=2/t. Thus the right side is at most (2Y/G)sum_(u,v>=1)min(u,v)/(u^2v^2). The last series is <=2sum_u u^(-1)sum_(v>=u)v^(-2)<=4sum_u u^(-2)<8. This proves the stated constant16 without discarding collisions. Nonintegral Y/G, r=s and repeated/shared prime powers are included. Equality r=G, if integral, remains in the good source.

For fixed c,C>0, an interval I subset[cN,CN] of length h satisfies

 sum_(n in I)r_G(n) <<_(c,C) h/G+E_N,
 E_N=min(N^(1/3),N/G^2),                                (LG3)

whenever 1<=G<=sqrt(CN). If G>sqrt(CN) the sum is zero. To verify the inherited W24 count: if G<=N^(1/3), sum G<r<=N^(1/3) with count<=h/r^2+1. For larger r, reverse the summation to l=n/r^2<=CN^(1/3). The real root interval for each l has length O(h/(sqrt(N)sqrt(l))); length plus one gives O(h/N^(1/3)+N^(1/3)). If G>N^(1/3), reverse all roots and use l<=CN/G^2, giving O(h/G+N/G^2). This is a PAIR count (r,l), with multiplicities. Closed endpoints and h<1 are paid by the length-plus-one terms; if the block is nonempty N/G^2>=1/C, so no unpriced isolated endpoint remains. The global mass is O(N/G), by (LG2)'s first-moment version.

Writing d=r u,e=r v with r the EXACT gcd assigns every original ordered tuple once. At a given r^2|n, its remaining number of factorizations is at most d_3(n/r^2). Hence for every fixed eta>0

 |v_G(n)| <= B_0 d_3(n)r_G(n) <<_(eta,B_0) n^eta r_G(n),
 sum_(n<=Y)|v_G(n)| << Y^(1+eta)/G,
 sum_(n<=Y)|v_G(n)|^2 << Y^(1+2eta)/G.                    (LG4)

No coprimality was inserted between r,u,v,l beyond the defining (u,v)=1, and this last condition was only dropped in a POSITIVE upper bound. All tuple masks remain literal; the majorant counts every possible root, not only its largest or prime root. This is coefficient domination, not norm monotonicity under a signed subset.

## 1. Source and quantifier contract

Fix an ordinary Dirichlet character (\chi), with its **natural zero extension**, and (\tau>0). Write
\[
 g_\tau(u)=(2\pi\tau)^{-1/2}e^{-u^2/(2\tau)},\qquad
 U_\chi(x)=\sum_{n\ge1}\mu(n)\chi(n)g_\tau(\log(n/x)).
 \tag{R1}
\]
All Gaussian fields here include every integer and the entire tail. A shell exponent (\gamma) means, for every (\epsilon>0),
\[
 \|U_\chi\|_{L^2([X,2X],dx/x)}\ll_{\chi,\tau,\epsilon}X^{\gamma+\epsilon}
 \quad\hbox{on every sufficiently large dyadic shell}. \tag{R2}
\]
For a family conclusion the same exponent must hold for **each** fixed character; constants may depend on it. One fixed character does not establish the family. No uniform growing-conductor or angular family is obtained.

The forward zero return is direct. Gaussian decay handles (x\to0); Cauchy--Schwarz on every large shell makes the Mellin integral holomorphic for Re s>γ. Initially for Re s>1 it equals
\[
 \int_0^\infty U_\chi(x)x^{-s}\,dx/x
       ={e^{\tau s^2/2}\over L(s,\chi)}. \tag{R3}
\]
The numerator has no zeros. Analytic continuation excludes every zero of this fixed (L) in Re s>γ, at every height; a principal (L)-pole gives a reciprocal zero and is not an obstruction. Constants need not be uniform in height to get this holomorphic half-plane conclusion. This direction uses the complete moment and does not import an unsupported reciprocal vertical-growth or Phragmen--Lindelof estimate. No converse from zero exclusion to the moment is claimed here. A moving approximant first returns to the **fixed** R1, and only then uses R3.

The original H form remains a different source. At every use below it retains its actual (a(\pi)=\alpha(\pi)\widetilde g_3(\pi)\eta(\pi)), (\xi(g)=\alpha(g)^3\eta(g)^3), complete g,g′ and core sums, both rooted mark-row projectors, common mark arrays, sharp annuli/windows, natural zeros, two orientations deleted at equal rational norm, ray/angular data and height profiles. The literal far mask is
\[
 q_\pi\ne q_{\pi'},\qquad |q_\pi-q_{\pi'}|>\lfloor Z^{.05}\rfloor. \tag{R4}
\]
Both the original complements and the outside squared scalar (N^{-1}G^{-2}) must be restored once. A fixed-u,v subpacket does not replace the full g,g′ form.
