statement:
## Uniform estimates paying all growing faces

For r>=0 and real v, Cauchy's formula on the complex unit circle about v gives

  |g_tau^(j)(v)|<=j! C_tau exp(-v^2/(2tau)+|v|/tau).

Summing binom(r,j)j! and weakening the Gaussian exponent yields

  |phi_r(v)|<=exp(C_tau(r+1)log(r+2)) exp(-v^2/(4tau)).       (N5)

This estimate holds for all r,v; constants depend on fixed tau only. It explicitly replaces any fixed-derivative O_r notation. The same argument with weighted Gaussian integrals pays fixed additional derivatives when needed; none are required in(N4).

For 1<=j<=K define the completed face kernel

  T_(j,K)(y)=sum_(ell>=1) chi^{*(j-1)}(ell)
                                      phi_(K-1)(log(ell/y)).

Initially on Re(s)=2 its Mellin representation is

  T_(j,K)(y)=(1/(2*pi*i)) integral e^(tau*s^2/2)
                       (1-s)^(K-1)L(s,chi)^(j-1)y^s ds.   (N6)

The integrand apart from y^s is entire: the only possible pole of L is its principal pole at1, of order j-1, and K-1>=j-1 cancels it. Imprimitive finite Euler factors are not deleted. Natural zeros cause no division and no pole. On any finite vertical strip, standard polynomial bounds for L and Gaussian decay justify shifting the line completely to Re(s)=-B, for every real B>=1. For each finite X,K,B the horizontal limits are taken before the uniform estimates below.

Here is a uniform negative-line estimate sufficient for this growing order. For fixed q and every B>=1,t real,

  |L(-B+it,chi)|<=C_q^(B+1) Gamma(B+1) exp(pi*|t|/2).      (N7)

For a primitive character this follows from its functional equation, the integral bound |Gamma(B+1-it)|<=Gamma(B+1), and the absolutely convergent bound |L(1+B-it,bar chi)|<=zeta(2). The trigonometric factor costs at most2exp(pi|t|/2). For imprimitive chi, its finitely many factors1-chi_0(p)p^(B-it) contribute at most2^omega(q)q^B, absorbed into C_q^(B+1). The ordinary zeta functional equation gives the q=1 case. Thus q stays fixed; no growing-conductor claim is hidden.

On the shifted line, |1+B-it|^(K-1)<=(B+1)^(K-1)exp(K|t|/(B+1)). Combine(N7) and the Gaussian, and complete the square in |t|. Stirling's elementary upper bound for Gamma(B+1) gives

  log |T_(j,K)(y)|
   <=-B log y+tau B^2/2
       +C_(q,tau)[K(B+1)log(B+2)+K^2+K log(K+2)]           (N8)

after increasing the constant, uniformly in1<=j<=K. At a zero value of the kernel the inequality is interpreted as an upper bound, not a finite logarithm assertion. Equivalently exponentiate the right side to avoid that notation entirely.

For every y>=exp(Z), with Z>=1, choose B=Z/tau once for the entire range (or B=max(1,Z/tau)). Then for sufficiently large Z,

  |T_(j,K)(y)|
    <=exp(-Z^2/(2tau)+C_(q,tau)[K(Z+1)log(Z+2)+K^2+Klog(K+2)]). (N9)

When Z is V or W and K lies in the specified band, Z is comparable to L^(2/3), Z^2 is comparable to L^(4/3), while K Z log Z=O(L log L). Hence(N9) is at most exp(-c_(q,tau)L^(4/3)) for all large L, uniformly in j,K, with some positive c. No unspecified factorial depending on a growing order has been discarded.

For a lower face j<K, d_1...d_j<=Y^(K-1)<=X exp(-V), so x/(d_1...d_j)>=exp(V). Its at most Y^j tuples, all binomial coefficients, and the K-1 faces together cost at most exp(O(L+K)); this is absorbed by the negative L^(4/3) exponent. Therefore the sum of every lower face is smaller than any prescribed inverse power of X.

For the all-large term in(N1), n>=product_i d_i>=(Y+1)^K>X exp(V), so n/x>exp(V-log2). Apply(N5), split its Gaussian decay into two halves, and use exp(-v^2/(8tau))<=C_tau exp(-2v). Since

  sum_n d_(2K-1)(n)n^-2=zeta(2)^(2K-1),

the entire absolute tail is at most

  X^2 exp(-c_tau V^2+O_tau(Klog(K+2)+K))=O_(A,q,tau)(X^-A). (N10)

This includes every plain factor, both character and Möbius zeros, all mixed prime powers, and the Gaussian tail beyond any finite cap. No fixed-K divisor estimate is borrowed uniformly without its dependence.

Finally remove the two product tails from(N2). Below Xexp(-W), use(N9) with Z=W and the bound Y^K<=exp(L+V) for the number of ordered d-tuples. Above2Xexp(W), all log(ell/y)>=W, where y=x/(d_1...d_K). Apply(N5) and the same n^-2 argument just to the K-1 plain factors; sum over at mostY^K short tuples. Both errors are exp(-c L^(4/3)+O(L log L)) and thus arbitrarily small powers. Together with(N1), the sign(-1)^(K+1) in(N2), and the lower faces this proves(N4).

This is an actual arithmetic source estimate: the discarded complete fields are uniformly negligible as K grows. It is not an estimate of a mask borrowed from the old Type I theorem, and it does not turn the surviving source into a proved arithmetic gain.

# [private research revision]: complete fugacity deflation and signed prime-block returns

Accept W51's precisely scoped results below. **No increase in c follows.**
The highest accepted written c10=.12514596 remains the complete
[[private research revision] return](../[private research revision]/valuation-integration.md), relative to its
unchanged analytic and external admission obligations. No formalization
or new proof packet was undertaken.

The full [author](wild51/report.md) and [independent review](wild51-review/report.md)
were read by root. The [manifest](retention-manifest.json) binds28 frozen
content/manifest files. All30 seeds, six tests03/16/23/18/09/01, developments
23/03, protected25/uniform19 audits and22 untested cards remain. Original
c8/c9 calibrations stay in the immutable reports; current thresholds below
follow their proved ordinary-character returns. No new literature priority
is asserted for these standard analytic/algebraic ingredients.

## G106. Isolated root of the complete cutoff polynomial

Fix an ordinary character chi, with its natural nonunit zeros, and define

    Z_N(z)=sum_(n<=N,mu(n)^2=1)chi(n)z^omega(n)
          =1+A_N z+R_N(z),
    A_N=sum_(p<=N)chi(p),
    B_N=#{n<=N:mu(n)^2=1,(n,q)=1,omega(n)>=2}.

Then sum_(k>=2)|C_k|<=B_N<=N, and Z_N(-1)=M_chi(N) exactly. This is
the entire hard-cutoff polynomial, not the Euler product over primes<=N.

For Z=1+Az+R, sum|c_k|<=B, |A|>=8 and lambda=B/|A|^2<=1/8,
Rouche on |z|=2/|A| gives exactly one root counted with multiplicity:
the linear term has modulus>=1 and |R|<=4lambda<=1/2. For B>0,
on the circle centered at -1/A with radius2lambda/|A|,
|R|<=lambda(1+2lambda)^2<=25lambda/16<2lambda. Thus this same root
alpha is simple, uniquely nearest to0, and

    |A alpha+1|<=2lambda,
    (1-2lambda)/|A|<=|alpha|<=(1+2lambda)/|A|.

B=0 gives alpha=-1/A directly. Every circle is within |z|<1, so the
quadratic remainder bound is valid. Exact polynomial division gives
Z(z)=(1-z/alpha)Q(z), Q(0)=1, and the complete endpoint comparison

    (|A|/2)|Q(-1)|<=|Z(-1)|<=2|A||Q(-1)|.

The lower bound uses |1/alpha|-1>=4|A|/5-1>=|A|/2; the upper uses
1+4|A|/3<=2|A|. No truncated reciprocal or approximate root is substituted.

For the principal character of fixed q, A_N=P_N is the unramified prime
count. The elementary bound
4^m/(2m+1)<=binom(2m,m)<=(2m)^pi(2m), with m=floor(N/2), yields
P_N>>_q N/log N. Therefore all large N satisfy the lemma, and

    alpha_N=-P_N^(-1)(1+O_q((log N)^2/N)).

Reality follows from conjugation and uniqueness; alpha_N<0. The local
Taylor series log Z_N at0 has radius exactly |alpha_N|. This rules out a
fixed zero-free disk and the straight real path to-1 for these polynomials.
It leaves complex paths, exact deflation and different smoothing eligible.
A fugacity zero is not an L-function zero or a lower bound for M(N).

For every-epsilon exponents, the principal endpoint comparison implies

    M_chi0(N)<<N^(gamma+epsilon)
      iff Q_N(-1)<<N^(gamma-1+epsilon).

A bounded deflated endpoint is insufficient. First gain beyond c10 needs
decay beyond N^(-.12514596), with strict every-epsilon buffering. Targets
1/6 and1/4 require the corresponding power decays.

For arbitrary fixed chi, select the root branch exactly when |A_N|>=8
and |A_N|^2>=8B_N. Otherwise |1-A_N|=O(sqrt N), and
M_chi(N)=1-A_N+R_N(-1). Hence for1/2<gamma<1 the COMPLETE criterion

    root branch: |A_N Q_N(-1)|<<_(chi,epsilon)N^(gamma+epsilon),
    non-root branch: |R_N(-1)|<<_(chi,epsilon)N^(gamma+epsilon)

is equivalent to the all-N Mertens exponent gamma. Arbitrary branch
switches are allowed; neither branch or any exceptional cutoff is omitted.
One common gamma for every fixed ordinary chi gives all-height zero
exclusion through s integral_1^infinity M_chi(x)x^(-s-1)dx=1/L(s,chi),
initially on Re(s)>1 and then by meromorphic identity on Re(s)>gamma.
The principal pole becomes a reciprocal zero. Constants/onsets may depend
on chi; no growing-conductor or Hecke transfer follows.

At gamma=.8748 the conditional c=.1252 exceeds c10 by.00005404;
the non-root prime sector costs exponent1/2. This is a complete conditional
budget, not an achieved bound. The equivalent signed inputs remain OPEN.

There is also a necessary second-root consequence. If an actual principal
Mertens bound of exponent1-c is supplied for every epsilon, then
Q_N(-1)<<N^(-c+epsilon). Since a squarefree integer with D primes is at
least(D+1)!, deg Z_N<=(1+o(1))log N/loglog N. Factoring all roots of Q,
one factor |1+1/zeta| is at most |Q(-1)|^(1/deg Q). For every eta>0,
some root distinct from alpha_N consequently satisfies

    |zeta_N+1|<=2(log N)^(-c+eta)

for all large N. If Q(-1)=0 the conclusion is immediate; degree0 is
eventually excluded by the assumed decay. The upper degree bound has the
right direction because log|Q(-1)| is negative. One root near-1 is not
sufficient: every other factor is still unpaid. No bare strip statement
is silently promoted to the required pointwise Mertens input.

The older fugacity/continued-power/cluster and small-face roots retain
ancestry. The useful increment is the full large-cutoff root with explicit
constants and a two-branch, fully paid deflated source contract.

## G107. Exact divisor elimination and the real-cutoff repair

For indices1..N let C(m,n)=chi(n/m)1_(m|n) and
A(m,n)=mu(n/m)chi(n/m)1_(m|n). Exact convolution gives CA=AC=I.
For ANY retained set R containing1, with complement E, put

    S=C_RR-C_RE C_EE^-1 C_ER,
    v=1_R-C_RE C_EE^-1 1_E.

Then S^-1=A_RR and M_chi(N)=e1^T S^-1 v. A prefix has zero return
C_ER but still the full deleted source injection. An interleaved partition
need not: at N=6,chi=1,R={1,6}, S=[[1,-1],[0,1]],v=(-2,1),readout=-1.
Acyclicity forbids returning to the same vertex, not paths between two
different retained vertices. G69's chronological zero-feedback scope stays.

For a prime endpoint p, the coefficient of arbitrary source input w_p
in the root output remains -chi(p) under every exact partition. It may
still cancel against other signed endpoints. The finite chain inverse
sum_k(-[C-I])^k restores each individual mu coefficient, not cancellation
between integers.

For a=mu chi, b_U=a1_(n<=U), r_U=delta-b_U*chi, convolution gives

    a=sum_(j=0)^(k-1)b_U*r_U^(*j)+a*r_U^(*k).

**Use support at least(floor(U)+1)^k for real U>=1.** The author's
(U+1)^k requires integer U. At U=3/2,chi=1,r_U(2)=-1 and
r_U^(*2)(4)=1, although4<25/4. The frozen author text is preserved;
this correction governs reuse. Intermediate squareful terms remain:
at U=5, r_U(12)=1 while(b_U*r_U)(12)=0.

For p>U prime and k>=2, the entire endpoint lies in the first residual
layer, with coefficient -chi(p). A principal-character absolute certificate
itemizing these endpoints pays >>N/log N when U<=N^u, fixed u<1.
This obstructs that unmerged absolute price only, not a signed Schur norm,
the Mertens sum, weighted observations or cross-endpoint cancellation.

Anchored future telescoping and the full mixed filter
M(x)-2M(x/2)-3M(x/3)+6M(x/6) are retained as duplicate-level identities.
They require the stated subunit-growth boundary input. Commutation for
every function gives no new arithmetic magnitude estimate.

## G108. Complete prime-block interactions and descendant errors

The protected25 audit defines H_B(t)=sum_(d|P_B,d<=t)mu(d)chi(d), where
P_B is the product of a finite prime block. Unique coprime factorization
gives the complete contraction

    M_chi(X)=sum_(m<=X,(m,P_B)=1)mu(m)chi(m)H_B(X/m).

For p<r and h_p(t)=1-chi(p)1_(t>=p), the exact missing interaction is

    H_{p,r}(t)-h_p(t)h_r(t)=-chi(p)chi(r)1_(r<=t<pr).

Thus naive product replacement discards the signed cofactor interval
-chi(p)chi(r)sum_(X/(pr)<m<=X/r,(m,pr)=1)mu(m)chi(m).
The strict lower/inclusive upper endpoints and ramified zeros are essential.
For principal p=2,r=3, H takes values1,0,-1,0 on the four successive
cutoff intervals. An everywhere-positive Gibbs model or finite real
logarithmic potential cannot represent it. The absolute discarded price
is X/(2pi^2)+O(sqrt X), from squarefree-unit density3/pi^2 and interval
length X/6. This does not lower-bound the signed interval.

All higher interactions remain: the coefficient for S subset B,|S|>=2
is(-1)^|S|chi(p_S)z_S[1_(p_S<=t)-1_(max S<=t)]. No pairwise closure
or positivity follows. Any approximation must bound BOTH its entire
signed contraction and the entire signed error before the Mertens return.
Moving blocks also require uniform constants in their actual choice.

The uniform19 audit uses the exact largest-prime state
S_chi(x,y)=sum_(n<=x,P+(n)<=y)mu(n)chi(n), with n=1. It satisfies

    S_chi(x,y)=1-sum_(p<=min(x,y))chi(p)S_chi(x/p,p^-).

For any approximation F define
Delta_F=F-1+sum_p chi(p)F(x/p,p^-). Finite substitution gives

    F(x,y)-S_chi(x,y)=Delta_F(x,y)
      +sum_(2<=d<=x,mu(d)^2=1,P+(d)<=y)
          mu(d)chi(d)Delta_F(x/d,P-(d)^-).

All strict descendant states, signs and natural zeros survive. Merge equal
integer states with their signed coefficients before taking absolute values.
This is the smooth/largest-prime version of the existing renewal ancestry.
Inserting F=x^rho without its y state cannot test an arithmetic spectral
mode: already S(t,2^-)=1. Finite Euler polynomials have no zeros on
Re(s)>0, but their infinite continuation/identification below1 is not
licensed by that finite fact. The complete signed defect estimate remains.

## Acceptance and next action

Root accepts the written proofs with the real-U correction. Independent
exact checks cover complex/imprimitive characters, fractional endpoints,
root-bracket constants, Schur injection, prime-block interactions and every
descendant in the finite renewal identity. They establish indexing and
coefficient evidence only; no fitted exponent or finite spectrum is used.
All original pools/draws remain; literal eligible candidates from all groups
were included. The critic's immutable priorities/permutation preceded
outcome intake, with author reservations already exposed. No helper was
rerun merely for reassurance.

A useful next step must estimate the complete deflated endpoint and its
composite complementary branch, or the actual signed interaction/defect
contraction. Root-location plots, bounded Q, absolute prime pricing and
state counts do not supply that estimate. Preserve the full29-family/
109-child portfolio, near gains,1/6 and1/4; no restricted failure retires
neighboring signed mechanisms or transfers a saving to another detector.

### 2.1 An exact smooth partition, not a replacement cutoff

Choose a fixed smooth nonincreasing phi on[0,infinity), phi=1 on[0,1], phi=0 on[2,infinity). For every positive n,

 1=phi(n/X)+sum_(j>=0) w(n/(2^j X)), w(t)=phi(t/2)-phi(t).        (3)

Here w is smooth, supported in[1,4], and nonnegative. Every overlap/transition is retained with its exact weight. The identity telescopes; for each n only boundedly many high terms are nonzero. Damping permits interchanging the complete sums. No original sharp cutoff is approximated by (3).

For the low part, expand b(l)=sum_(j=1)^(Q-1) beta_j exp(2pi i jl/Q). Its zero coefficient vanishes. On ml<=2X (and the extra last integer increment, lying below3X) the nonlinear phase increment in l is O(m/X), uniformly for x in[X,2X]. Since m<=X^alpha0, this is <1/(4Q) for all sufficiently large X. Each nonzero Fourier mode has monotone derivative separated from every integer by at least1/(2Q). Discrete first-derivative summation gives O_Q(1) for every prefix; Abel summation with phi(ml/X)exp(-ml/x^(3/2)), of bounded total variation, preserves that bound. Summing |A_m| gives O(AD). The finitely bounded initial-X range enters the fixed constant.

## 9. Remaining fields and complete zero-exclusion return

Small nonprincipal rows below Z^d0, including fixed-conductor and finite-unit rows, keep the original global-line estimate with reserve

    -13h/75+y/2-63d0/50=21464387121/250000000000>1/20.

The genuine principal row remains u=1. Its two residue scalars give the same f_eta; other units retain their actual nonprincipality tests. The principal remainders have reserves y/4, h/24 and mu_P, choosing 0<mu_P<.87 min_i ell_i after the finite positive original slots are fixed. Explicit contour margins are

    y/20-(1+h)/1000-1/4000=314003484089/15000000000000>0,
    h/600-1/1000-1/4000=219737987/3000000000000>0.

Rows above Z^(h+10^-10) use the raw absolute estimate with term B0+(h+zeta0)(1+epsilon)-zeta0 v+epsilon. With fixed zeta0=10^-10, choose a sufficiently large fixed positive line parameter v before the final threshold for the desired negative power. Constants may be large, but there is no new asymptotic loss or central-density assumption.

Off-height fields retain the three independent contour frequencies, complete original w-inversion, joining segments and separately extracted principal poles. The Gaussian controls its frequency; the other Mellin transforms have arbitrarily high fixed polynomial decay. Assign fixed fractions of each buffered height window. On joining segments reciprocals remain inside the zero-free buffer or on the global line. Raw unseparated numerator and conductor-height bounds have fixed polynomial Z-degree before external integration-by-parts order is chosen; then a sufficiently large fixed order pays Z^B T^-N. No arithmetic indicator is differentiated and no reciprocal zero or nonprincipal pole is crossed without the source's accounting.

Order of choices is essential. From mu and fixed positive margins, first choose common real budgets, moment loss, capacity decrement, amplitude mesh and a finite original slot system totaling ell. Slots are smaller than d0 times every needed relative mesh, and the positive minimum slot determines mu_P. Choose a single Delta>0 below fixed fractions of mu, every retained/fallback reserve, y/4,h/24,mu_P and the small-row reserve, also Delta<mu/4. These numerical choices precede the target eta.

For each fixed target only afterward choose its exclusion set S, anchor/dictionary and finite internal moment, profile and Sobolev orders. The density's internal detector exponent was already fixed. Choose a distinct small positive external height exponent to absorb its target-dependent height degree into the same common reserve, external tail orders next, and the eventual threshold last. Constants, orders and thresholds may depend on eta. Delta and the original slots do not. A finite atlas maximum changes no common power saving.

The original compensated probe and numerator assembly give

    J_eta-f_eta <<_eta Z^(beta_*-k_probe-Delta),
    J_eta <<_eta Z^(theta-k_probe+epsilon).

Since Delta<mu/4, sufficiently small epsilon gives the same first bound for f_eta. At Z tending to zero the original defining Mellin line moves arbitrarily far right. Thus

    integral_0^infinity f_eta(Z) Z^(-s+k_probe) dZ/Z

is holomorphic for Re(s)>beta_*-Delta and equals, initially on Re(s)>1,

    exp((s-5/6)^2) H_eta(s)/L^S(s,eta).

If chi is nonprincipal choose p1 with chi(p1)!=1; such a prime exists because any unit integer with nontrivial character value has a prime factor with nontrivial value.     integral_X^(2X) |T_tau_X,p,chi,X(x)| dx/x
         <<_(chi,p,gamma,epsilon) X^(gamma+epsilon)     (7.1)

for EVERY epsilon>0, at one common gamma<gamma11 chosen before the character and any candidate zero. The auxiliary tau_X may depend on epsilon; (5.6) is uniform in it and C is fixed. Constants and onsets depend only on fixed data and epsilon. Every real shell point, the complete merged integer coefficient, all squareful terms, the low/high complements and natural character zeros have their stated treatment. A sufficient stronger input is the full squared norm O(X^(2gamma+epsilon)); no converse is claimed. No selected-projection estimate replaces (7.1).

For gamma>=3/4, (5.6) transfers (7.1) to the FIXED function C_p,chi. Conversely, that full C norm hypothesis implies (7.1) for every allowed tau. This comparison concerns norm hypotheses; it is not an assertion that the latter are equivalent to zero exclusion.

Here is the full detector implication. With t=1/x put

    H_p(z)=integral_0^infinity C_p,chi(1/t)t^(z-1)dt.

From (7.1) and (5.6), H is holomorphic on Re(z)>gamma: on a compact subset choose epsilon smaller than its real-part buffer and sum dyadic shells. Each fixed derivative adds only powers of log x, paid by the remaining buffer. At x near0, the polynomially bounded coefficients and exp(-n/x^(3/2)) give superpolynomial decay. This part does not depend on a target height.

To identify H, first work on Re(z)>3/2, choosing the divisor-loss exponent small enough for absolute Fubini. For each n, the clockwise contour rotation in [restricted research revision] gives

    integral_0^infinity e^(-nt^(3/2)-i(nt)^6)t^(z-1)dt
      =A0(z)n^(-z)+R_n(z),
    A0(z)=Gamma(z/6)e^(-i*pi*z/12)/6,
    |R_n(z)| <<_K n^(-Re(z)-1/2)

on every compact K contained in Re(z)>0, with the corresponding holomorphic derivative majorants. As |c(n)|<<_delta n^delta for every delta>0, the sum E_p(z)=sum c(n)R_n(z) is normally holomorphic on Re(z)>1/2. Consequently

                    L(2z,chi^2)^2/L(z,chi)+E_p(z).    (7.2)

The small fixed rotation, principal powers and signs are those in [restricted research revision]; no real-axis Taylor expansion with an unpaid infinite integral is used. For nonprincipal chi, the same two-prime argument at nonzero height uses chi(p)'s finite roots of unity: a common zero would again force a rational log ratio, unless the height is0. Our p1 choice excludes the zero at height0. Thus the covering pair pays the whole half-plane and preserves the pole exception.

## 5. Cube-core middle estimate: quadratic energy plus original-color control

Factor uniquely ell=kappa*t^3*z^6, kappa cubefree and t squarefree. Its valuation rule is v(kappa)=v(ell) mod3, v(t)=floor(v(ell)/3) mod2, v(z)=floor(v(ell)/6). Every overlap is allowed: for example a prime of valuation4 lies in both kappa and t. The exact zero-preserving character identity is

    chi_m(ell)^eta=chi_m(kappa)^eta chi_m(t)^3
                                      *1_((m,z)=1).   (5.1)

The factor chi_m(t)^3 is real and unchanged by eta=-1. A vanished sixth-power phase still has its displayed natural hole. For fixed kappa,z the actual inner coefficient is (2.2), multiplied by chi_m(kappa)^eta and the z-puncture. Its squared mass is (2.3). There is no imposed (kappa,t), (kappa,z), or (t,z) coprimality.

PR9 B2.24 supplies the squarefree quadratic Hecke sieve of price T0+X. Its explicit family check at lambda, fixed primary square classes modulo4 and finite ray reciprocity are part of the contract used here. Both live variables m and t are squarefree. The primary [Goldmakher-Louvel Theorem1.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1112.1642) requires precisely such a Hecke family; we use PR9's verification, not a generic residue-symbol analogy. Arbitrary inner coefficients independent of t are permitted. Consequently the t-energy for Nt<=T0 is <=H_J U^epsilon(T0+X).

Put B=(H_A/Nkappa)^(1/3), so T0=B/(Nz)^2. For large z there is a second bound: (2.4) at every t, including its new z-hole, gives energy <=H_J U^epsilon T0*S0. Both bounds permit the same frequency-only selectors. Split z at Z>=1. Ideal counting gives

    sum_(Nz<=Z) [B/(Nz)^2+X] << B+XZ,
    sum_(Nz>Z) B*S0/(Nz)^2 << B*S0/Z.

There is no missing repeated-row cost XZ. Clip Z=sqrt(B*S0/X) to the actual interval [1,sqrt(B)]. If the optimum is below1, use the all-pointwise bound B*S0<=sqrt(B*S0*X). If above sqrt(B), the all-quadratic bound B+Xsqrt(B)<=B+sqrt(B*S0*X). Thus for all nonempty scales, with no S0<=X hypothesis,

    sum_(t,z) |B_f(kappa*t^3*z^6)|^2
        << H_J U^epsilon [B+sqrt(B*S0*X)].              (5.2)

In (5.2) each value is evaluated with its actual z-puncture and whole source coefficient. After fixing z the coefficient is independent of t, which is exactly the sieve permission. The long-z estimate remains on the original two colors and actual remaining slots. A general arbitrary merged coefficient would not have (2.4), so both inputs are necessary.

Summing cubefree kappa up to C by ideal counting costs

    H_A^(1/3) C^(2/3)+sqrt(S0*X)H_A^(1/6) C^(5/6).     (5.3)

Cauchy between the independently allocated copies is taken at this positive outer energy. Restoring (2.1) and O(A) a labels gives

    U^(5/6+tau/6) A^(-4) N0^(-1/6)sqrt(S0)
                                      (Nf)^(-3/2) C^(5/6).

statement:
## 4. Power-paid small-divisor theorem for the actual completed source

Fix gamma,k,b satisfying

    1/2<gamma<1, integer k>2, 1<b<=2gamma,
    r=(k-2gamma)/(k-2),
    u=k-(k-1)r=2gamma-r>0.                              (4.1)

For the main near/1/6/1/4 examples use b=3/2,k=6. Set

    eta0=1/(100*k*p*q),
    U=V=floor(sqrt(eta0)*X^(u/2)),  M=X^r.              (4.2)

All quantities are chosen from the ORIGINAL shell X, before x varies.
For sufficiently large X, U,V>=1. The floor only decreases UV and
never changes its upper bound eta0*X^u. Then for every epsilon>0,

    ||S_p,U,V||_1+||S_p,U,V||_2
          <<_(chi,p,b,k,gamma,epsilon) X^(gamma+epsilon). (4.3)

This is an unconditional estimate of the ACTUAL small-divisor source,
uniform on the entire shell in its finite part. It uses no Möbius
cancellation in d,e and no unproved character moment.

To prove it, first restrict the physical integer n=de*l to n<=M.
For D=de<=UV, expand the zero-mean periodic b_p in its finite Fourier
series modulo Q=pq:

    b_p(l)=sum_(j=1)^(Q-1) beta_j e(j*l/Q),
    sum |beta_j|<=p*Q.

Every row has phase

    F_j(t)=j*t/Q-(D*t/x)^k/(2pi).

On 1<=t<=M/D its derivative is decreasing and satisfies

    0<=k*D^k*t^(k-1)/(2pi*x^k)
       <=k*UV*M^(k-1)/(2pi*X^k)
       <=k*eta0/(2pi)<1/(2Q).

The equality of powers here is EXACTLY u+(k-1)r=k. Hence F_j' stays
between 1/(2Q) and 1-1/(2Q); it never crosses an integer.

For completeness the needed first-derivative estimate is elementary.
For integer t, Delta_t=F_j(t+1)-F_j(t) is monotone and stays in that
same interval whenever both endpoints lie in the row. Put z_t=e(F_j(t))
and g(v)=1/(e(v)-1)=-1/2-(i/2)cot(pi v). Then
z_t=g(Delta_t)(z_(t+1)-z_t). Summation by parts bounds every row prefix
by the endpoint terms plus the total variation of g along a monotone
interval. Both are O(Q), since |sin(pi v)| is bounded below at its
endpoints and cot is monotone. A final unpaired atom costs1. This proves
the bound for every real upper cutoff, not only integer or sampled x.

Abel summation with the actual decreasing exp(-D*l/x^b) multiplies
that bound by at most2. The Fourier expansion therefore gives O_p,q(1)
for each row, uniformly for all real x in the shell and all d,e<=U,V.
Summing |mu(d)chi(d)mu(e)chi(e)|<=1 proves

    |S_(n<=M)(x)| <<_(p,q) U*V <<_(p,q,k) X^u.          (4.4)

Since r>1>gamma, u=2gamma-r<gamma. The remaining n>M portion of S
has coefficients bounded by p*d_3(n) and is paid by (3.2). This proves
(4.3), INCLUDING the region in which the row's discrete frequency can
approach an integer. It is not dropped, estimated by the row lemma
outside its range, or assigned a fictitious zero value.

The complete short terms in (2.1) cost O_p(U+V)=O(X^(u/2)), hence are
also paid. This is the substantive combination with the accepted tail
theorem: its generic bound is used only on a genuine, completely retained
complement; the new small-divisor cancellation occurs before that split.

The argument does not authorize U=V=X^.495, nor UV=X^gamma. At fixed
k,gamma its demonstrated nonstationary condition is UV<<X^u. Beyond it
the current proof has a discrete alias/stationary range. Vanishing of
this reserve is not an impossibility theorem for other estimates.

### Exact identity and signs

The convolution identity a*chi=delta gives, including every prime power,

    a(n) log n = -sum_(d|n) a(n/d) chi(d) Lambda(d).

For a squareful local exponent the last two surviving prime-power terms cancel. Omitting prime powers would change the actual source. Since tau U'(y)+yU(y)=sum a(n)log n g(log n-y),

    tau U'+yU+K1 U+K2 U=0,
    K1 U=sum_p chi(p)log p U(y-log p),
    K2 U=sum_p sum_(j>=2) chi(p)^j log p U(y-j log p).

After weighting, delays d carry chi(d)Lambda(d)d^(-gamma). Define

    I_R=int_0^R y|z(y)|^2dy, E_R=int_0^R |z(y)|^2dy,
    Qj(R)=-Re int_0^R conjugate(z(y))(Kj,gamma z)(y)dy.

The exact energy equation is

    (tau/2)(|z(R)|^2-|z(0)|^2)+I_R+tau*gamma*E_R=Q1+Q2.       (R1)

In particular the derivative boundary and drift have the signs required for absorption. This identity is inherited Gaussian renewal/logarithmic-source algebra, not a new family.

## Exact two-scale localization and the coarse budget

For sharp sums M_B(x)=sum_(n<=x)a_B(n), suppose a single set B=B_N has min B>sqrt N. In R1 every divisor d involving two primes of B exceeds N. Therefore, exactly at every real 1<=x<=N,

    M(x)=M_B(x)-sum_(p in B,p<=x)chi(p)M(x/p).        (R5)

The inner source is the ORIGINAL M: x/p<min B, so no B-prime can divide its index. This is a useful exact localization of the correction, not a replacement by an independently favorable rough source. If B contains no prime <=x the sum is empty. At x=p the inner unit M(1)=1 remains.

Take fixed 1/2<alpha<b<1 and B_N subset (N^alpha,N^b], and assume a bound |M(t)|<=C t^beta for 1<=t<=N^(1-alpha). Absolute treatment of the correction gives the deliberately coarse but rigorous estimate

    sum_(p in B_N)|M(N/p)|
      <= C N^beta sum_(n<=N^b)n^-beta
      <= C[1+1/(1-beta)] N^[beta+b(1-beta)],          (R6)

for 0<beta<1. No PNT is needed. At fixed beta, the best limiting b>1/2 gives exponent (1+beta)/2, which is LARGER than beta. Consequently even an improved estimate for M_B(N) does not improve the current exponent using this absolute correction. Even GRANTING a prior beta just above the current source-relative .8748540364 leaves a correction exponent above .9374270182; that prior estimate is not claimed proved here. This is a bound produced by a method, not a lower bound for the actual signed correction.

If an independently proved small-scale beta were available, reaching gamma through R6 would require beta<(gamma-b)/(1-b). As b decreases to1/2 the conditions approach:

|returned gamma|c|necessary beta for this sufficient absolute method in the b->1/2 limit|
|---|---|---|
|.87485|.12515|beta<.74970|
|5/6|1/6|beta<2/3|
|3/4|1/4|beta<1/2|

These are deliberately coarse budgets for a source estimate that is NOT supplied. A purported 3/4 small-scale input would miss even the current near target after this correction. Assuming the final improved exponent at all smaller scales merely to pay R5 would be circular unless a genuine induction with strict contraction and initial data is proved; R6 gives no such contraction.

The signed opportunity is the FULL joint difference in R5 or R4. For the same shell, U=U_B-C_B exactly, where C_B is the whole restoration field. Therefore

    ||U||^2=||U_B||^2+||C_B||^2-2Re<U_B,C_B>.         (R7)

No component may be erased because one bound is favorable. R2 offers compatibility of overlapping prime removals, but its vanishing determinant does not force the relative phase or magnitude in R7 at the required power precision. For bivariate or multi-block formulations every overlap cofactor and ordered cross term stays in this identity.

## R9. The actual prime-corner obstruction, and a stronger character scope

For 1<=y<2 the complete restoration sum is B(y)=b(1)=1, for both b=kappa*chi and the original nonprincipal choice b=chi. This exact initial interval retains the real arithmetic source.

Let P_X be the unramified primes in `(sqrt(3X/5),sqrt(7X/10)]`, and put `c0=(1/2)log(5/4)`, J=[L-c0,L]. For large L this is a subinterval of (0,L). On J^2,

    4X/5<=e^(t+u)<=X,
    3X/5<pp'<=7X/10,
    8/7<=e^(t+u)/(pp')<5/3.

Hence every ordered distinct prime pair has complete restoration sum one. It exceeds Y because delta<1/2, has gcd1, and survives the paid diagonal/high-gcd removals. The ordinary prime number theorem gives

    |P_X|~2(sqrt(7/10)-sqrt(3/5))sqrt(X)/log X.

Removing the finitely many ramified primes has no asymptotic effect. For principal chi the isolated kernel on J^2 is exactly `|P_X|(|P_X|-1)e^[-a(t+u)]`. Its compressed rank-one norm is

    |P_X|(|P_X|-1)X^(-a)(e^(2ac0)-1)/(2a),          (R14)

so the full isolated operator has norm at least a positive constant times X^(1-a)/(log X)^2. This proves H16--H17, including its normalization and rectangular support.

**Independent extension to all fixed characters.** Let d=|image(chi on q-units)|, a fixed finite integer. Partition P_X by the actual value chi(p). One class P_(X,lambda) has at least |P_X|/d members. For its distinct pairs,

    mu(p)mu(p')chi(p)chi(p')=lambda^2,
    |lambda^2|=1.

Consequently its isolated kernel on J^2 is exactly the same rank-one kernel multiplied by the constant phase lambda^2 and with P_X replaced by that class. The operator norm is unchanged by a unit phase. Thus for every sufficiently large X, SOME actual phase-class sector has norm

    >>_(a,chi) X^(1-a)/(log X)^2.                    (R15)

No estimate for primes in residue classes is needed: ordinary PNT plus the finite pigeonhole suffices. The selected lambda may depend on X. On any unbounded sequence such as X=2^j, one fixed lambda occurs on an unbounded subsequence. Therefore at least one FIXED character-phase sector cannot obey the desired all-X power bound for any gamma<1 and epsilon<1-gamma. Do not strengthen this to a claim that every fixed phase has that size for every X without an additional distribution theorem.

The obstruction also survives its own frequency cut. For this sector every pp'>3X/5, so de ell<=X forces ell=1 on the ENTIRE observed interval, not just J^2. Its total atom mass and endpoint, after weight n^(-a), are O_(a,chi)(X^(1-a)/(log X)^2). Applying the exact endpoint formula (R11) to the isolated source gives

    ||T^hi_(phase sector)||
       <<X^(1-a)/[Omega(log X)^2].                  (R16)

Reverse triangle between its full and high-frequency operators gives the lower bound (R15) also for the isolated low-frequency operator once Omega tends to infinity. Every H15 corridor has that property. This applies to the original nonprincipal route as well as the repaired all-character route.

The logical limitation is essential. Arithmetic isolation is a change of coefficients, not an orthogonal projection on the full operator. Norms do not have a signed-subset monotonicity. Thus (R15) is NOT a lower bound for T, Gamma[c], Gamma[alpha], the entire T^lo, or native H. If OPEN-LOW does hold, writing `T^lo=P^lo+Rest^lo` shows by reverse triangle that Rest^lo must itself have norm of order at least X^(1-a)/(log X)^2 along the selected subsequence, despite their small sum. This is a precise necessary cross-sector cancellation, not its proof. It redirects an attempt to pay each prime/composite sector independently; it does not reject the joint operator strategy.

## 3. D2 / S21: exact cutoff insertion algebra and coherent boundary

This section concerns the ordinary squarefree source, not the Eisenstein native-H tensor. Let S_N={n<=N:mu(n)^2=1,(n,q)=1}, with orthonormal basis e_n. For each unramified prime p define

    B_p e_n=chi(p)e_(pn) if p does not divide n and pn<=N; otherwise0.

Distinct B_p,B_r COMMUTE: if prn<=N and gcd(n,pr)=1 both orders give chi(pr)e_(prn), and otherwise both vanish. The divisor-closed cutoff cannot manufacture a noncommutative insertion effect. Fermionic ordering changes the operator and requires its own readout; the exterior construction of S13 cannot be substituted silently.

For p!=r the mixed commutator C_pr=B_p^*B_r-B_rB_p^* has the exact action

    C_pr e_(pm)=-conjugate(chi(p))*chi(r)e_(rm)
      if mu(m)^2=1,(m,qpr)=1,
         N/(pr)<m<=min(N/p,N/r); otherwise0.            (11)

At the lower endpoint equality gives zero because both paths exist. The upper endpoints are included. The proof compares the two paths: insertion first needs prm<=N, while deletion first needs only pm,rm<=N. No term with a square or nonunit is restored. C_pr is a phased negative partial isometry, so its norm is1 when this exact domain is nonempty and0 otherwise.

Let a_N=sum_(n in S_N)a(n)e_n. With the usual conjugate-first inner product,

    <a_N,C_pr a_N>=-#{m in the domain of(11)}.           (12)

Indeed a(pm)=-chi(p)a(m), a(rm)=-chi(r)a(m), and every character phase cancels. This is an actual all-fixed-character coherence result, including complex and imprimitive chi, not an arbitrary phase model or a changing-conductor construction. With a general scalar profile f, replace a(n) by a(n)f(n); the contraction is exactly

    -sum_(m in domain)conjugate(f(rm))*f(pm).            (13)

For a real nonnegative profile it has one sign. General profiles must retain their products; this is not a signed-subset inequality.

In particular take the k unramified primes in(N/2,N]. On their span each C_pr is -conjugate(chi(p))*chi(r)|r><p|. Therefore the sum over ordered distinct p,r is unitarily conjugate to -(J_k-I_k), with eigenvalue -(k-1) on the ACTUAL source vector(-chi(p))_p and eigenvalue1 on its orthogonal complement. Its operator norm is k-1 for k>=2. The actual quadratic value is -k(k-1), not a square-root-size random fluctuation. A phase gauge changes neither this value nor the norm if it transports the source too.

This rejects the literal independence/orthogonality shortcut for this boundary algebra. It does not bound M_chi below, does not reject indefinite or source-specific compensation across other sectors, and does not establish a native-H phase value. The complete source return remains

    a_N=product_(p<=N,p not|q)(I-B_p)e_1,
    M_chi(N)=<sum_(n in S_N)e_n,a_N>.                   (14)

Every prime occurs once, insertion products commute, and the n<=N cutoff is exact. A proved bound |(14)|<<_(chi,epsilon)N^(gamma+epsilon) for every fixed chi/all large N gives zero exclusion through s int_1^infinity M_chi(x)x^(-s-1)dx, with the same principal/imprimitive/all-height argument as above. No such readout estimate follows from(11)-(13). This is the unpaid full complementary term; a bound only on commutators is insufficient.

Ancestry: W27/W59 cover the exterior cutoff/homology mechanism; G145 covers free-word abelianization and SORTED creation commutators with a different operator. Here B_p permits insertion at every absent prime and its mixed adjoint boundary is given explicitly by(11). G160's other all-character phase obstruction and G162's terminal-prime matching cut are related; neither is asserted to be this operator identity. This distinction, not a claim of a new broad family, is the proposed incremental record value.

statement:
# [private research revision] headroom A: spectral observation and a quartic replacement kernel

Status: author mathematical handoff for independent review, 11 October2026. No increase over the supplied written analytic c4=25027/200000=.125135 is proved. Its boundary is gamma4=174973/200000=.874865. PR9/Gao credit and the earlier c0 kernel evidence remain separate. Author owns only this ignored draft tree; root owns canonical integration, tracker and Git.

The selected mechanism combines the newly accepted W39 complete-field observation idea with a previously considered but unused quantitative spectral inequality. Its concrete new output is an improved observation theorem: the complete fixed Gaussian can be controlled from sets of measure exp(-o(sqrt(j))) in every logarithmic unit interval. In particular EVERY fixed polynomial j^-kappa is admissible, with no kappa<1/2 restriction and no reciprocal bootstrap. A more general paid gap-versus-density condition permits missing unit intervals. The arithmetic observation hypothesis remains open. This is broader stated observation geometry in the inspected project record, not a claim of literature novelty or an automatic c gain.

A quartic-kernel replacement further allows logarithmic density loss o(j^(3/4)), with its own complete Mellin return and a separate open arithmetic input.

## 1. Exact analytic class and primary ingredient

Fix tau>0 and g_tau(v)=(2*pi*tau)^(-1/2) exp(-v^2/(2*tau)). Let a_n be arbitrary complex coefficients for which

    A_b := sum_(n>=1) |a_n| n^(-b) < infinity             (A1)

for one fixed real b. Set

    F(u)=sum_(n>=1) a_n g_tau(log n-u).

All applications below have b=2 available. The complete series, with its actual zeros/signs, is used throughout; no arithmetic labels or signed interactions are deleted. The same proof applies to an ideal sum with n replaced by its norm and A_b replaced by the absolute ideal Dirichlet series.

Use the Fourier convention hat h(t)=integral_R h(u)e^(-itu)du. Completing the square termwise gives h(u)=e^(-bu)F(u) in L1(R) intersect L-infinity(R), and absolute Fubini gives

    hat h(t)=exp(tau*(b+it)^2/2) sum_n a_n n^(-b-it),
    |hat h(t)| <= M exp(-tau*t^2/2), M=e^(tau*b^2/2)A_b.  (A2)

For example |h|<=g_tau(0)M and ||h||_1<=M. Thus this spectral envelope follows on the original absolutely convergent line. No zero-free reciprocal estimate, contour shift or improved Mertens bound is hidden in A2.

The only imported analytic inequality is Kovrijkine's quantitative Logvinenko--Sereda theorem, Theorem1 in *Some results related to the Logvinenko--Sereda theorem*, arXiv:math/0012186v1 (19 December2000), pages1--2; its p=infinity proof and explicit constants are on pages7--8: <https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0012186>. In the needed form, if E is (delta,a)-thick (every interval of length a meets E in measure at least delta*a), and a bounded function P has Fourier support in an interval of length B, then

    ||P||_infinity <= (C/delta)^[C(aB+1)] ||P||_(L-infinity(E)). (A3)

C is universal. More explicitly, the source's page8 gives the p=infinity lower bound (delta/100)^(33*a*B+1); its angular-frequency convention is consistent with the displayed Bernstein bound B/2 on page2. Thus one may use (100/delta)^(33*a*B+1) in A3. The asymptotic proof needs only the universal form. [private research revision]'s high-ceiling-discovery.md listed this paper as an observability comparison but did not use its theorem. W39 instead used single-interval Taylor/Remez interpolation and expressly did not claim its coefficient2 optimal. The present composition is distinct from that single-interval proof.

## 2. Full observation theorem and both paid tails

**Theorem A.** Suppose A1 holds with b>gamma. For every epsilon>0 and every sufficiently large integer k, suppose there is a measurable E_k subset [k,k+1] such that

    |E_k| >= delta_k >0,
    log(1/delta_k)=o(sqrt(k)),
    ess sup_(u in E_k)|F(u)| <= C_epsilon exp((gamma+epsilon)k). (A4)

The little-o condition is uniform as k tends to infinity; its sequence and the sets may depend on epsilon. Then, for every epsilon>0,

    |F(u)| <<_epsilon exp((gamma+epsilon)u), u>=0.        (A5)

All constants may depend on the fixed coefficient sequence, b,tau,gamma and epsilon. No reciprocal meromorphic input is needed for A4=>A5.

Proof. Fix an observation allowance eta>0 with d=b-gamma-eta>0. For each large integer j put r_j^2=sqrt(j) and

    H_j(u)=h(u) exp(-(u-j)^2/(2*r_j^2)).

The Fourier convolution of A2 with the Gaussian window gives exactly the uniform majorant

    |hat H_j(t)| <= M r_j/sqrt(tau+r_j^2)
                      * exp(-sigma_j*t^2/2),
    sigma_j=tau*r_j^2/(tau+r_j^2) >= tau/2               (A6)

for large j. This estimate is independent of the center j. The exact square identity is

    tau*x^2+r_j^2*(t-x)^2
      =(tau+r_j^2)*(x-r_j^2*t/(tau+r_j^2))^2+sigma_j*t^2.

In the convolution integral multiplication's factor1/(2pi) is canceled by the two Gaussian integral normalizations. The phase from the translated window has modulus1.

Choose

    T_j=sqrt(4*(b-gamma+2)*j/tau),
    P_j(u)=(2pi)^(-1) integral_[-T_j,T_j] hat H_j(t)e^(itu)dt.

P_j is bounded with Fourier support [-T_j,T_j], and Gaussian tail integration yields

    ||H_j-P_j||_infinity <= C exp(-(b-gamma+2)j).         (A7)

For a literal estimate the preceding tail is at most M/[pi*sigma_j*T_j] times exp(-sigma_j*T_j^2/2). Thus A7 pays the entire omitted frequency field before applying A3.

Let m0=floor(j/2), m1=ceil(3j/2), I_j=[m0,m1+1], and

    S_j=(R\I_j) union (union_(m0<=k<=m1) E_k),
    delta_j^*=min_(m0<=k<=m1) delta_k.

Every real interval of length2 contains an integer unit interval. S_j is therefore (delta_j^*/2,2)-thick. The uniform little-o in A4 implies log(1/delta_j^*)=o(sqrt(j)). Applying A3 to P_j costs

    Lambda_j=(200/delta_j^*)^(132*T_j+1)=exp(o(j)).     (A8)

On E_k in I_j, the observation bound and b>gamma+eta imply

    |H_j(u)| <= C_eta exp(-d*u-(u-j)^2/(2*r_j^2))
              <= C_eta exp(-d*j+d^2*sqrt(j)/2).          (A9)

Replacing k by u in A4 costs only a fixed factor. The second bound is the exact completed square. On the artificially added exterior R\I_j, A2 gives

    |H_j(u)| <= ||h||_infinity
                  exp(-(j/2-1)^2/(2*sqrt(j)))
               = exp(-j^(3/2)/8+O(sqrt(j))).             (A10)

This explicitly pays the part of the thick set on which no arithmetic small-value information was assumed. In particular no unobserved complement is declared small by interpolation.

Now A3, A7 and the norm triangle inequality give

    ||H_j||_infinity
      <= Lambda_j ||H_j||_(L-infinity(S_j))
                  +(Lambda_j+1)||H_j-P_j||_infinity
      <= exp(-(b-gamma-eta)j+o(j)).                     (A11)

The sampling factor multiplies BOTH the observation error and the frequency remainder. For u in[j,j+1], its Gaussian window is at least exp(-1/(2sqrt(j))); multiply A11 by e^(bu), choose eta before the requested output allowance, and absorb o(j). This proves A5 on every sufficiently large real u. Compact u is absorbed into the constant. QED.

The proof's exponent ledger is explicit: source exponent gamma+eta; localization cost d^2/(2sqrt(j)) per unit j; sampling cost O((sqrt(j)+1)log(C/delta_j^*))/j; frequency tail exponent at most gamma-2 after undoing e^(-bu); exterior tail tends to minus infinity after normalization. Hence the analytic losses tend to0 for every fixed gamma<b, including gamma=5/6 and3/4. There is no positive transfer floor.

## 3. Gap-versus-density extension

The same proof needs only the following local geometry around each large center j. For fixed epsilon, let a_j>=1,0<d_j<=1 and let E^(j) be a measurable subset of [j/2,3j/2] on which |F(u)|<=C_epsilon exp((gamma+epsilon)u). Require that every interval of length a_j contained in this range meets E^(j) in measure at least d_j*a_j, and require

    (a_j+1) log(C/d_j) = o(sqrt(j)).                    (A12)

Add the whole exterior. For j large, a_j=o(sqrt(j)) and the central range is longer than4a_j. Every interval of length2a_j either contains an a_j interval inside the central range, or has at least a_j length in the exterior. The augmented set is (d_j/2,2a_j)-thick. A3 costs exp[O((a_j*sqrt(j)+1)log(C/d_j))]=exp(o(j)). The same two tails and the same completed-square source bound prove A5.

Examples: a_j=j^alpha and d_j=exp(-j^theta) are sufficient whenever alpha+theta<1/2 (alpha>=0,theta>0). With d_j bounded below, gaps o(sqrt(j)) are allowed; with polynomial density, it suffices that a_j log(j)=o(sqrt(j)). The sets must satisfy the stated local geometric contract at every large center. A density-one list of globally good shells alone does not imply it.

There is also an explicit finite-loss version at the critical density. Suppose the sets in A4 instead obey log(1/delta_k)<=(D+o(1))*sqrt(k), for a fixed D>=0, at source exponent gamma_src<b. In the proof replace I_j by the integer-ended interval with endpoints j+/-j^(7/8)+O(1), and use T_j=t*sqrt(j), t>0. The exterior tail is now exp(-j^(5/4)/2+o(j^(5/4))); sigma_j=tau+O(j^(-1/2)); and log(delta_j^*)^(-1)<=(D+o(1))*sqrt(j). Thus the complete output exponent is at most

    max{gamma_src+132*D*t, b-tau*t^2/2+132*D*t}.        (A16)

All displayed exponents allow an arbitrarily small positive buffer. In particular t=sqrt(2*(b-gamma_src)/tau) gives

    gamma_out=gamma_src+132*D*sqrt(2*(b-gamma_src)/tau). (A17)

This follows from the same source, localization and frequency tails, and does not assume a fixed-thickness theorem for a varying set. For the bounded ordinary/f3 coefficients and the fixed ideal count one may take any fixed b>1. Hence the strict condition

    gamma_src+132*D*sqrt(2*(1-gamma_src)/tau)<gamma4     (A18)

already gives a first-gain contract, by then choosing b>1 sufficiently close to1. This is a sufficient cost, not an optimal constant. The width tau is the SAME fixed Gaussian in the observation hypothesis; increasing it would change the arithmetic input. Subcritical A4 has D=0 and avoids this finite penalty entirely.

## 4. Literal arithmetic returns and the first-gain contract

For fixed ordinary chi, set a_n=mu(n)chi(n), with all Möbius/conductor zeros. A1 holds at b=2. Explicitly |F(u)|<=A_b*g_tau(u) for u<=-max(tau*b,0): in each term the factor exp(b*v)g_tau(v-u), v=log(n)>=0, is then decreasing in v. Thus the entire left Gaussian tail is integrable against e^(-su) for every complex s. On Re s>1 the complete Mellin identity is

    integral_R F(u)e^(-su)du = exp(tau*s^2/2)/L(s,chi).  (A13)

A5 makes the left side holomorphic on Re s>gamma. Multiply by L and continue; its principal pole at1 is separately removable in the reciprocal. The exponential multiplier never vanishes. Thus A4 (or A12) at0<gamma<1 excludes L zeros in Re s>gamma, with the known principal pole excluded.

For each fixed finite-order, trivial-infinity Eisenstein Hecke character psi, use the literal ideal sum mu_K(a)psi(a)g_tau(log N(a)-u), with the presented-modulus zero extension. The absolute ideal count is O(X), so A1 holds at2; W39's fixed lattice proof supplies the needed meromorphic continuation on Re s>1/2 and its principal pole convention. For gamma>1/2, the identical transform proof gives the same result. Constants depend on the fixed member; no moving-conductor or angular uniformity is asserted.

For the literal multiplicative f3 field, f3(1)=1, f3(p^k)=-1 for p!=3,k>=1 and f3(3^k)=1. Retain its exact multiplier

    sum_n f3(n)n^(-s)=B(s)/zeta(s),
    B(s)=(1-2^(1-s)) H(s),
    H(s)=(1-2^(-s))^(-2)(1-3^(-s))^(-2)
           *product_(p>=5)(1-2p^(-s))/(1-p^(-s))^2.      (A14)

H and1/H are holomorphic and bounded on every closed half-plane strictly to the right of1/2; the p>=5 factors start at degree2 and2/sqrt(5)<1. Thus B has no zero in1/2<Re s<1. A4/A12 for F3 at gamma>1/2 supplies the ordinary-zeta return, retaining the zeros of1-2^(1-s) on Re s=1 and using the established right edge. It also gives its full signed square moment immediately; no hereditary signed-submask comparison is used.

**OPEN-A(gamma):** prove the actual complete field satisfies A4, or the weaker local geometry A12, for every epsilon>0. A concrete single choice is

    |E_k| >= exp(-sqrt(k)/log(k+2)),
    ess sup_Ek |F| <<_epsilon exp((gamma+epsilon)k)       (A15)

in every large integer interval. A15 for any gamma<.874865 gives a further gain. At gamma=.874864 it would give c=.125136; gamma=5/6 gives1/6 and gamma=3/4 gives1/4. These are conditional returns, not achieved constants. The coarse analytic estimates above clear all transfer costs. The coarse arithmetic bound, including the accepted buffered calibration |F|<<exp((gamma4+epsilon)u), does not establish A15 at any smaller gamma.

## 5. First arithmetic tests: what the weaker input does and does not buy

**Available calibration.** Take any fixed buffered beta>gamma4 from the accepted premise. Abel summation of the complete mu*chi coefficients against the Gaussian and its first derivative gives both |F(u)| and |F'(u)| bounded by C_beta exp(beta*u) in the existing ordinary-character scope. This is the same complete-source calibration used in the living proof; no masked estimate is inferred. With the requested gamma<gamma4, its direct bound on E_k is still exp(beta*k), exceeding the A4 target by exp((beta-gamma)k). Taking a smaller observation set does not turn an upper bound into cancellation.

Even GRANTING an exact real zero in every unit interval, that derivative bound only guarantees a neighborhood of width of order exp(-(beta-gamma)k) on which |F|<=exp(gamma*k). Its negative logarithm has order k, not o(sqrt(k)). This test does not upper-bound the actual small-value measure; it proves that the available zero-plus-first-derivative argument falls short. Section6 gives a rigorous Gaussian counterexample with exact natural coefficient zero support, so analytically produced valleys alone cannot fill the missing arithmetic estimate.

**Short-interval cancellation.** The Matomaki--Radziwill theorem compares normalized short averages of a real bounded multiplicative function to its long average, with an explicit logarithmic error. Theorem1 in <https://arxiv.org/pdf/1501.04585> (v4, 15 October2017) retains that long average and the error C' loglog(h)/log(h). With h<=X this supplied error is not a negative power of X. Even a hypothetical direct Gaussian reconstruction with no additional loss would leave X times that normalized error, not X^gamma. Moreover a bound for local increments is not a bound for the complete Gaussian's long-average component. This primary theorem therefore does not establish A15; its arithmetic exceptional-set theorem is not being relabeled as observation sets for F. Complex/Hecke cases need their own stated extensions and are not inferred here.

The current original f3 rough/prefix identity must also remain complete: root's accepted [private research revision] source proves a large RR term and opposite restoration in the full hard mask. No small value of one chosen threshold piece supplies A4 for their sum. I used that result only to reject deletion of the restoration, not as a new leading-log obstruction or a new estimate.

The useful change is therefore at the exact input contract: future arithmetic work may now aim for very narrow valleys, or sparse but locally well-distributed valleys under A12. It need not prove W39's kappa<1/2 geometry. There is still no established arithmetic reason that these valleys exist at a new gamma. The next decisive arithmetic calculation is a lower bound for the measure of {u in[k,k+1]: |F(u)|<=exp((gamma+epsilon)k)} for the COMPLETE mu*chi or f3 field, at a threshold satisfying A4; sign-change counting alone is inadequate.

## 6. Square-root density is a genuine analytic boundary

This section proves a scoped obstruction, not an assertion about the actual Möbius signs. It strengthens a generic smooth-signal counterexample to the same fixed Gaussian and bounded integer coefficients, even preserving the squarefree and fixed-conductor ZERO SUPPORT.

**Theorem B.** Fix tau>0, an integer q>=1 and1/2<gamma<beta<1. There exist real a_n in{-1,0,1}, with a_1=1 and |a_n|=mu(n)^2*1_((n,q)=1) EXACTLY, a constant d>0, and sets E_j subset[j,j+1] of measure pi^(-1)exp(-d*sqrt(j)) such that

    F(u)=sum_n a_n g_tau(log n-u) << exp(beta*u),
    limsup_(u->infinity) log(1+|F(u)|)/u = beta,
    ess sup_Ej |F| <= exp(gamma*j) for every large j.    (B1)

The a_n are deliberately NOT claimed multiplicative or equal to mu(n)chi(n). Consequently this cannot refute an arithmetic improvement. It does show that A4's sub-square-root logarithmic density loss cannot be replaced by an arbitrary O(sqrt(j)) loss using Gaussian regularity, coefficient boundedness and natural zeros alone.

Proof. Put R^2=2tau, s^2=R^2-tau=tau and

    C0=tau*R^2*pi^2/(2*s^2)=tau*pi^2,
    a=sqrt(1-beta)/(2*pi*sqrt(tau)).

Choose integer centers J_k=J0+4^k, with the positive integer J0 sufficiently large, and even N_k=2 floor(a*sqrt(J_k)/2). Define the entire target, nonnegative on the real line,

    V(u)=sum_(k>=1) exp(beta*J_k)
             exp(-(u-J_k)^2/(2*R^2)) sin^(N_k)(pi*u).   (B2)

Gaussian domination gives locally uniform convergence. Since |sin(pi*u)|<=1 on R, completing the square and summing the separated Gaussian envelopes give V(u)<<exp(beta*u). At u=J_k+1/2 its kth summand is exp(beta*J_k-1/(8*R^2)); every other summand is nonnegative. Hence V's growth exponent is exactly beta.

For real xi, direct Gaussian Fourier inversion proves

    g_tau * [ (R/s) exp(tau*R^2*xi^2/(2*s^2))
                  exp(-v^2/(2*s^2)) exp(i*R^2*xi*v/s^2) ](u)
       = exp(-u^2/(2*R^2)) exp(i*xi*u).                 (B3)

Here convolution is in the logarithmic variable. To check B3 without a transform convention ambiguity, write R^2=tau+s^2. The quadratic coefficient of v in the convolution exponent is -R^2/(2tau*s^2), the linear coefficient is u/tau+iR^2*xi/s^2, and the constant is -u^2/(2tau)+tau*R^2*xi^2/(2s^2). Completing the square gives exactly -u^2/(2R^2)+i*xi*u; the Gaussian prefactor is (R/s)*sqrt(s^2/R^2)=1.

Expand sin^N(pi*u) into its N+1 frequencies pi(N-2l). The absolute sum of its Fourier coefficients is1. Applying B3 to each frequency gives a real inverse density B_N with

    |B_N(v)| <= (R/s) exp(C0*N^2) exp(-v^2/(2*s^2)).   (B4)

Set b(v)=sum_k exp(beta*J_k) B_(N_k)(v-J_k). Because C0*a^2=(1-beta)/4, completing the square gives

    sup_v e^(-v)|exp(beta*J_k)B_(N_k)(v-J_k)|
        <= C exp(-3(1-beta)J_k/4).                     (B5)

The same bound for its v derivative has only a polynomial factor in J_k: differentiating the Gaussian contributes |v-J_k|/s^2 and the frequency contributes at most R^2*pi*N_k/s^2; their weighted Gaussian suprema have the asserted polynomial cost. The series of these bounds converges. Enlarge J0 so that f(t)=b(log t)/t satisfies |f(t)|<=d_q/4 for all t>0, where d_q>0 is the squarefree coprime density. Its derivative obeys |f'(t)|<=C/t, since d/dv[e^-v b(v)] is uniformly bounded.

Absolute Fubini, B3--B5 and Gaussian domination show

    integral_0^infinity f(t)g_tau(log t-u)dt = V(u).    (B6)

For u>=0, omitting0<t<1 changes this by O(exp(-u^2/(2tau))): use |b(v)|<=C e^v on v<0 and complete the original Gaussian square. This is a paid left-domain error, not a fictitious integer coefficient at n<1.

Let z_n=mu(n)^2 1_((n,q)=1). The elementary fixed-q squarefree count is

    Q_q(x)=sum_(n<=x)z_n=d_q*x+O_q(sqrt(x)).            (B7)

It follows by expanding mu(n)^2=sum_(r^2|n)mu(r), using the fixed periodic coprimality count and the convergent1/r^2 tail; W39.20 independently records exactly this input. Define real w_n=z_n*f(n)/d_q, so |w_n|<=1/4. Partial summation using B7 and |f'|<=C/t gives

    sum_(n<=x)w_n-integral_1^x f(t)dt=O(sqrt(x)).       (B8)

Round the cumulative sums W(N)=sum_(n<=N)w_n while preserving the parity of the integer Q_q(N):

    A(N)=Q_q(N)+2 floor((W(N)-Q_q(N))/2+1/2),
    a_n=A(n)-A(n-1), A(0)=0.                          (B8a)

Then |A(N)-W(N)|<=1. If z_n=0, both Q_q and W are unchanged, so a_n=0. If z_n=1, the argument of floor changes by (w_n-1)/2 in[-5/8,-3/8], so its change is either0 or-1; consequently a_n is either+1 or-1. This proves the exact natural zero support and B8 remains true for a_n. The rounding rule is deterministic, including its tie convention.

Stieltjes summation against g_tau(log t-u) now gives

    |F(u)-V(u)| <= C exp(u/2), u>=0.                   (B9)

Indeed the boundary at infinity vanishes, and the error integral is at most a constant times

    integral_1^infinity sqrt(t) |d[g_tau(log t-u)]|
       <= C_tau exp(u/2) integral_R e^(v/2)|v|g_tau(v)dv,

with the fixed1/t derivative and1/tau absorbed correctly into C_tau. The finite lower endpoint and B6's left tail are smaller. Since gamma>1/2, B9 will be below the desired observation threshold; since beta>1/2, it preserves the peak exponent.

Finally choose d=2sqrt(2)(beta-gamma)/a and E_j=[j,j+pi^(-1)exp(-d*sqrt(j))]. For u in E_j, |sin(pi*u)|<=exp(-d*sqrt(j)). Every center J_k in[j/2,2j] has N_k>=a*sqrt(j/2)-2, so its sine factor is at most

    exp(-2(beta-gamma)j+O(sqrt(j))).                   (B10)

Sum the remaining Gaussian envelopes as in B2. These centers contribute at most exp((2gamma-beta)j+O(sqrt(j))). Centers outside[j/2,2j] contribute O(exp(-c*j^2)), using their distance from u and the separated Gaussian sum. Combine with B9: both terms are eventually below exp(gamma*j). The lower bound at J_k+1/2 and the upper beta envelope give all of B1. If necessary multiply every a_n by-1 to arrange a_1=1; all statements in B1 use absolute values and are preserved. QED.

This is different from W38's sparse positive block example: that example has whole bad logarithmic intervals and fails the every-interval observation condition. B1 has tiny observations in EVERY unit interval, with the original Gaussian and exact natural zero support. The obstruction is zero multiplicity of order sqrt(j) per interval in the continuous target packets, preserved as narrow valleys after integer realization. This is not a rank, variance or leading-log argument.

The counterexample can ALSO retain any preassigned buffered Mertens calibration. Given beta<b_cal<1, reduce a if necessary so that

    eta=C0*a^2 < min{(1-beta)/4, b_cal-beta}.

All preceding estimates remain valid, with d changed to 2sqrt(2)(beta-gamma)/a; B5 only improves. The inverse density now obeys

    |b(v)| <= C sum_k exp((beta+eta)J_k)
                         exp(-(v-J_k)^2/(2*s^2))
            <= C' exp((beta+eta)v), v>=0,

again by the completed-square bound for separated centers. From B8 and the parity rounding,

    |sum_(n<=X) a_n|
      <= |integral_0^(log X) b(v)dv|+O(sqrt(X))
       =O(X^(beta+eta))=O(X^b_cal).                    (B11)

Thus gamma<beta<b_cal=gamma4 may be chosen: the construction satisfies even a stronger unbuffered version of the accepted summatory calibration, together with exact natural zeros, but its Gaussian exponent is still beta>gamma. This remains a NONMULTIPLICATIVE sequence. It specifically prevents a proof from extracting the new subcritical observation hypothesis from baseline summatory growth, bounded coefficients and the natural support alone. It does not prevent an argument using the actual multiplicative signs.

## 7. A changed source with a weaker observation geometry

**Theorem C (quartic replacement).** Define the fixed real, even, SIGNED kernel

    K(x)=(2pi)^(-1) integral_R exp(-t^4+itx)dt,
    F4(u)=sum_n a_n K(log n-u).

Under A1 with b>gamma, Theorem A remains true for F4 with the weaker geometric requirement log(1/delta_k)=o(k^(3/4)). The arithmetic values in the hypothesis are those of F4, not F. For the three literal coefficient fields in Section4 its Mellin multiplier is exp(-s^4), so the same zero-exclusion return holds in their respective domains.

Here is a complete proof of the new costs. Contour translation t->t+iy, y having the sign of real x, gives

    -Re(t+iy)^4-y*x <= -t^4/2+17*y^4-y*x.

The vertical closing sides vanish as their real part tends to infinity. Choose |y|=(|x|/68)^(1/3). Thus

    |K(x)|<=C exp(-c*|x|^(4/3)), c=51/68^(4/3)>0.      (C1)

Fixed derivatives have the same contour bound with an additional polynomial factor. This justifies every exponentially weighted real integral. The bilateral Laplace transform of K is exp(-s^4): both sides are entire in s by C1 and agree on the imaginary axis by Fourier inversion. In particular K(0)>0. It cannot be nonnegative: its second moment is0, whereas K is continuous and positive near0. Weighted absolute Fubini gives h4(u)=e^(-bu)F4(u) in L1 intersect L-infinity and

    hat h4(t)=exp(-(b+it)^4) sum_n a_n n^(-b-it),
    |hat h4(t)|<=A_b*exp(17*b^4)*exp(-t^4/2).           (C2)

For localization take r=j^(1/8), W_j(u)=K((u-j)/r)/K(0) and the pointwise product H_j(u)=h4(u)W_j(u). Its Fourier convolution has a uniform quartic envelope: for r>=1,

    x^4/2+r^4*(t-x)^4 >= t^4/32+(r^4/2)*(t-x)^4.

The integral of the last exponential is O(1/r), canceling the window transform's factor r. Hence |hat H_j(t)|<=C_b A_b exp(-t^4/32). Cut at T_j=[32*(b-gamma+2)*j]^(1/4); the full omitted frequency tail is O(T_j^(-3)exp(-(b-gamma+2)j)).

Use exactly the augmented thick set I_j,S_j from Section2. Its LS cost is still (200/delta_j^*)^(132*T_j+1)=exp(o(j)), now under log(1/delta_k)=o(k^(3/4)). On the observed set, with d=b-gamma-eta>0, C1 bounds H_j by

    C exp(-d*u-c*|u-j|^(4/3)/r^(4/3))
      <= C exp(-d*j+[27*d^4/(256*c^3)]r^4)
       =exp(-d*j+O(sqrt(j))).                          (C3)

On the unobserved exterior its bound is O(exp(-c'*j^(7/6))); both it and the multiplied frequency tail are therefore paid. For u in[j,j+1], W_j(u)->1 uniformly, hence |W_j(u)|>=1/2 eventually. The norm triangle inequality used in A11 now proves the full exponent gamma for F4. This establishes the asserted transfer without positivity of K.

For u sufficiently negative, A1 and C1 give |F4(u)|<=C A_b exp(-c*|u|^(4/3)) by maximizing exp(bv-c(v+|u|)^(4/3)) over v>=0. Thus its entire left Mellin tail is paid, and absolute convergence on Re s>1 gives exp(-s^4) times the SAME Dirichlet series in A13/A14. The multiplier never vanishes. This proves the arithmetic return, including the original modulus zeros and f3 p2/p3 factors.

A concrete OPEN-C(gamma) input is |E_k|>=exp(-k^(3/4)/log(k+2)) and ess sup_Ek|F4|<<_epsilon exp((gamma+epsilon)k), in every large unit interval. Any gamma<.874865 improves the current c under this input; 5/6 and3/4 retain their conditional returns. Abel summation of the accepted buffered Mertens bound still only gives F4,F4'=O(exp(beta*u)), beta>gamma4: its guaranteed valley width exp(-(beta-gamma)j) fails even this weaker contract. The Gaussian small-value hypothesis, positive RR law and Theorem B are not automatically inherited by this changed kernel. OPEN-C requires a new actual-source arithmetic estimate.

## 8. Discovery choices, provenance and next action

The initial five seeds are retained in worklog.md. They were written after brief current-proof/index intake and before this detailed development; this lane does not claim a history-blind generation experiment. Distinct architectures considered were:

| Architecture | Credible route and actual screen | Disposition |
|---|---|---|
| Spectral localization of the complete Gaussian, then observation on shrinking arithmetic sets | W39 supplies the correct complete-field question; the previously listed but unused Kovrijkine ingredient gives quantitative global sampling. Theorem A proves the missing variable-density localization, A16--18 price its critical version, and Theorem B tests its boundary with exact natural support. | Selected and developed. No positive transfer floor for gamma>1/2; OPEN-A remains arithmetic. |
| Extremal arithmetic approximation in a Hardy space | F21.H already has the conditional all-height residual32/15, norm20/9 gate reaching1/4. W22/FG remove an unnecessary finite-inner evaluation penalty and constructively retain the norm tail. These make approximate certificates worth revisiting, but a finite computation has no all-height return by itself. | Recombination candidate, not claimed new; no lower actual residual proved here. Do not rerun the old equivalent gate as discovery. |
| Short-interval multiplicative cancellation aggregated into a whole Gaussian | A sufficiently accurate arithmetic exceptional-set theorem could supply A4/A12 and hence any retained target; Section5 tests the actual published MR input, keeping its long-average mode and logarithmic error. | Exact input mismatch proved for the proposed direct use. A power-scale error AND control of the complete long mode would reopen it. |
| Prime-dilation or nonlocal signed evolution | Existing DP/N28 exact noncommon multipliers preserve the zero signal; short signed recurrences might be more accessible than a full norm. The elementary mode F(u)=e^(rho*u) is multiplied by e^(rho*h)-e^h under F(u+h)-e^h F(u), which cannot improve its exponent unless its signal is killed. | Old multiplier return retained; no new arithmetic contraction established. A fixed profile/evolution rephrasing alone is subsumed. |
| Completed-L heat deformation or a positive resolvent detector | F26.H/F26.R target a different observable and potentially broad confinement. The record already keeps the exact backward-heat/compensator obstruction; positive smoothing provides a forward estimate, while return to the original zeros is the missing direction. | Protected high-ceiling seed, but no complete return from a new deformation was obtained here. No numerical ceiling assigned. |

The selected result uses fixed absolute Dirichlet convergence, not the supplied baseline, for its spectral envelope. That is the decisive structural difference from the finite reciprocal bootstrap. Its conditional c=1/6 and1/4 returns are literal consequences of the same theorem, without changing projectors or profile widths, but no arithmetic evidence currently favors those inputs.

Lean verification performed: direct completion of both Gaussian squares, exact bandwidth/thickness constants against the primary source, complete tail exponents, Mellin multipliers and endpoint conventions, deterministic parity rounding and the fixed-q squarefree discrepancy. No broad test suite or numerical cancellation experiment was used. These derivations are author evidence, not independent review or canonical acceptance.

Frozen-input hashes are recorded in manifest.json. The mathematical source pointers are W39 Sections2--3 and W39.20 (local observation, fixed ideal continuation and squarefree count), its independent R39-A review (the nonoptimal kappa<1/2 boundary), the accepted [private research revision] f3 hard-region author/reviewer reports, W38 review Section4 (the different whole-bad-interval counterexample), [private research revision] high-ceiling-discovery.md (prior LS mention), and F21/F26/N28 in the attempt index. Historical c2/c3 examples in these sources are not reused as current improvements. The current deadline and exposed settings evidence remain in worklog.md.

Primary sources checked on11 October2026: Kovrijkine's sole arXiv version math/0012186v1, submitted19 December2000, with its exact infinity-norm inequality on printed page8; and Matomaki--Radziwill arXiv:1501.04585v4, revised15 October2017, Theorem1. Formula A3 is the sole external theorem imported into the new analytic proof. Theorem B's power-sine idea is related to the sharpness example immediately after the source's inequality, but the inverse-Gaussian realization, exponentially separated amplitudes, every-interval geometry and exact-squarefree-support parity rounding are developed here. This states ancestry, not a literature novelty claim.

**Preferred next decisive calculation:** choose ONE actual coefficient field and estimate its complete sublevel measure at some gamma<.874865. The quartic source's OPEN-C has the weaker geometry; the Gaussian source retains A4/A12/A18 and its existing arithmetic library. A route from sign changes or isolated values must quantify valley width. For a Gaussian argument, test whether it distinguishes the actual multiplicative signs from Theorem B's exact-support nonmultiplicative sequence. If not, it cannot prove the desired subcritical contract. That obstruction and the Gaussian hard-region law require a new proof for K. No further generic interpolation improvement is needed for any fixed polynomial density.

### 4.1 The exact high-ceiling certificate and all its costs

Let P>=5 and retain all primes<=P. Let f_P(n)=f3(n) if every prime factor of n is<=P and0 otherwise, and

    V_P(u)=sum_n f_P(n)g_tau(log n-u),
    E_P(s)=(1-3^-s)^-1 product_(p<=P,p!=3)(1-2p^-s)/(1-p^-s). (R1)

Unlike a squarefree-only partition function, this includes every prime power. For sigma>0 it has an absolutely convergent finite-prime Dirichlet series and

    ||exp(-sigma u)V_P(u)||_L2(R)^2
      =exp(tau sigma^2)/(2pi) integral_R exp(-tau t^2)|E_P(sigma+it)|^2dt. (R2)

This is Parseval after absolute Mellin Fubini. Let P_X>=2X exp(C sqrt(log X)). All integers n<=P_X occur with their exact original f3 coefficient, while missing nonsmooth n lie in a full Gaussian tail. The elementary |f3|<=1 Gaussian estimate gives

    sup_(log X<=u<=log2X) |F(u)-V_(P_X)(u)|
       <=X^(1-C^2/(2tau)+o(1)).                      (R3)

Thus a global source norm in R2 bounded by P^kappa would yield shell exponent sigma+kappa (P_X=X^(1+o(1))), with R3 paid by choosing C. At sigma=.6, the weakest first-gain budget is kappa<.274861; c=1/6 allows kappa<.233333..., and c=1/4 allows kappa<.15. These are honest full-return headrooms, not isolated Euler-factor savings. For other sigma>.5, the budget is gamma-sigma.

statement:
### Uniform discrepancy, including periods beyond the row range

For every bounded smooth annular profile family on the Eisenstein lattice,
\[
\sum_{e\mid m}\Psi(m/\sqrt Q)
-\frac{Q}{q_e}\int_{\mathbb C}\Psi
=O_\Psi(1), \tag{A01.4}
\]
with the fixed lattice covolume included and uniformly in \(Q,e\).

To prove it, rotate and scale the ideal lattice by a generator of \(e\), and put \(L=(Q/q_e)^{1/2}\). For \(L\ge1\), Poisson bounds the nonzero dual sum by
\[
O_N\!\left(L^2\sum_{\xi\ne0}(1+L|\xi|)^{-N}\right)=O(1)
\]
for fixed \(N>2\). For \(L<1\), the compact annulus meets only \(O(1)\) lattice points and its continuous mass is \(O(L^2)\). Fixed residue classes satisfy the same argument. This proves (A01.4) with \(K_S\) and its actual zero average.

Applying this to (A01.3), each pair's row sum minus its complete zero mode is \(O(YZ^\epsilon)\) times fixed profile seminorms.

statement:
## G227. An actual twisted inverse and its cofactor-resolved observation

Fix an ordinary Dirichlet character chi modulo a fixed positive integer q.
Let S_N={a<=N: a squarefree, (a,q)=1}, ordered increasingly, with N>=1 an
integer. Write E_ad=1_(d|a) and M=diag(mu(a)). Every divisor interval of S_N
is complete, so finite Mobius inversion gives E^-1=M E M. With

    A_chi=E diag(mu(d) conjugate(chi(d))) E^T,
    (A_chi)_ab=prod_(p|(a,b))(1-conjugate(chi(p))),

the diagonal is invertible because |chi(d)|=1 on the actual labels. Therefore

    (A_chi^-1)_ab=mu(a)mu(b)
                   sum_(d in S_N,[a,b]|d)mu(d)chi(d).       (227.1)

The pairing and transpose are bilinear. A_chi is generally complex symmetric,
not Hermitian. Its (1,1) inverse entry is exactly M_chi(N)=sum_(n<=N)mu(n)chi(n).
Simply phase-gauging the real coprimality matrix would leave that observed
inverse entry untwisted, so it does not establish (227.1).

Put g=(a,b), l=[a,b]. Writing d=lm in (227.1), squarefreeness forces (m,l)=1,
and mu(a)mu(b)mu(l)=mu(g). Hence

    (A_chi^-1)_ab=mu(g)chi(l) M_(chi,lq)(N/l),
    M_(chi,h)(y)=sum_(m<=y,(m,h)=1)mu(m)chi(m).             (227.2)

This is zero for l>N. In particular the first inverse row and complete
residual identity, for ANY proposed column z and r=e1-A_chi z, are

    R_N(a)=chi(a) M_(chi,aq)(N/a),  |R_N(a)|<=floor(N/a),
    M_chi(N)=z1+sum_(a in S_N) R_N(a)r(a),
    B_N(z):=sum_a |R_N(a)r(a)|
       <=W_N(z):=N sum_a |r(a)|/a.                         (227.3)

All coordinates remain. If r is supported on a>N/H, H>=1, this costs at most
H||r||1. A global inverse operator norm is therefore an unnecessarily large
default price for a residual known to live on large labels. The exact signed
sum in (227.3) remains available; its absolute bound is only a sufficient bill.

For fixed 0<gamma<1, a complete every-epsilon bound for |z1|+B_N(z), or the
stronger explicit |z1|+W_N(z), by N^(gamma+epsilon) gives the same Mertens
bound. The alternative every-epsilon integral_1^X |M_chi(t)|^2 dt/t bound
by X^(2gamma+epsilon) also suffices. On each dyadic shell Cauchy bounds
the Abel integral and all its fixed derivatives, with a positive exponent
buffer on any compact subset of Re(s)>gamma. The normally convergent function

    s integral_1^infinity M_chi(t)t^(-s-1)dt

equals 1/L(s,chi) on Re(s)>1. Continuing the identity with L excludes regular
zeros in Re(s)>gamma at every finite height. At the principal pole s=1 the
reciprocal has a zero. Natural character zeros stay in the coefficients.
Constants may depend on the fixed character and epsilon; no growing-conductor
or Hecke assertion follows. This is a complete return from an OPEN estimate.

Two concrete inverse cautions survive. In the principal N=2 case the signed
coprimality matrix [[1,-1],[-1,0]] is invertible but its nuisance block [0]
is singular and its inverse (1,1) entry is0. A Schur formula requiring that
block inverse fails. On m distinct prime labels the matrix is J-I, full rank
for m>=2, while rank-one J has operator residual1 and scalar residual at most
||u||2||v||2. Exact rank alone therefore does not rule out a paid approximation.
title: G227. An actual twisted inverse and its cofactor-resolved observation

## R7. Original slots inside the positive norm

Let Q_u be the actual source product of original disjoint prime slots, with total width v<=1/20 and one common orientation. Its individual fixed relative characters are absorbed in its bounded row-independent coefficients as permitted by MI. Retain all prime zeros and original supports. For this paragraph the mesh is sufficiently fine for the retained [restricted research revision] marked inverse amplification; it is fixed in terms of loss and bounded ranges before the eventual dictionary, slot count, profiles and heights.

That retained estimate has exponent

    E_MI(1,r,v)=1/6+(5/6)max(1,r+2v,(2r+8v)/3).

In R9 every active inverse dyad has r>=t+o(1)>1 and r>=2v. Thus its maximum is r+2v, up to the fixed endpoint tolerance. Keeping Q_u inside the same Hilbert norm in R10 adds exactly5v/3. The scalar phi_u(m) remains a contraction even when m shares primes with a slot; no coprimality fiction is needed. Applying the same proof yields

    Nv(P Q) << H_J U^[J(delta,lambda)+5v/3+epsilon].     (R13)

Here Nv is likewise a squared norm and includes the same detector Sobolev variables and, if required, finitely many additional derivatives in the independent slot parameters. Their heights, real powers and common profiles keep the existing source order. No arbitrary amplitude mask is imported into the moment. R13 is a complete positive norm statement, not a statement about a chosen signed subset of its expansion.
