## 6. Principal, finite, small, large, and off-height terms

The new geometry satisfies
\[
 0<\ell<x<y<2x,\quad x+y=1-\ell,\quad
 y<1/2<h<2y,\quad \theta=11/12-\ell/4>.87.
\]
The relevant additional compensated-probe inequalities are
\[
 y-2x+\ell=-597590039/5000000000<0,
\]
\[
 1+3\ell-2(x+y)=-123299/750000<0.
\]
Therefore the positive-part term in B0.27 vanishes and the compensated probe exponent is
\((5x+y)/12=\theta-k\), with
\(k=5/6-x/3-\ell/6\). Division by \(c_SA(Z)\) costs only a fixed power of \(\log Z\).

The unchanged source identifies exactly u=1 as the principal numerator row. Other units are nonprincipal by the source's explicit ray test; nonunit sixth-power-free rows have nontrivial tame inertia. B0.35–B0.36 identify both residue scalars and the same signal \(f_\eta\). Enlarging a fixed cutoff makes \(H_\eta\) analytic and \(|H_\eta-1|\le1/2\) on \(\Re s\ge.87\).

The w- and z-contour remainders and the prime-product approximation have respective common power reserves \(y/4,\ h/24,\ \mu_P\), where one may choose \(0<\mu_P<.87\min_i\ell_i\). The prime-product approximation is used only on its residue locus, not below its justified real line. The quotient-free correction avoids any assumed nonvanishing of local correction factors.

For \(q_u\le Z^{d_0}\), including finite nonprincipal units and fixed-inducing exceptions, use the original global lines, not a central-row density estimate. The B0.56 relative exponent is
\[
 \frac{13h}{75}-\frac y2+\frac{63d_0}{50}
 =-\frac{21483987121}{250000000000}<-1/20.
\]
For \(q_u>Z^{h+\zeta_0}\), B0.57 has exponent
\[
 B_0+(h+\zeta_0)(1+\epsilon)-\zeta_0 v+\epsilon,
 \qquad B_0=x/2+1+y.
\]
After fixing \(\zeta_0=10^{-10}>0\), choosing a sufficiently large *fixed* v gives any prescribed negative power. It need not be a moderate numerical v; its resulting finite height costs are chosen before the eventual threshold.

The independent external frequency coordinates are \(\Im(s+z),\Im z,\Im w\). The Gaussian handles the first; the Mellin weights have arbitrary decay in the other two. The source controls the raw unseparated correction before tail-dependent separation, with a bound \(Z^{B'}T^{-N}\) whose raw power \(B'\) is fixed before N. Joining segments keep the reciprocal on its retained zero-free buffer or the global zero-free line. The nonprincipal numerator has no crossed pole; the principal poles were separately extracted. The full w-inversion remains on its original absolute line for the retained numerator estimate.

These are inherited analytic inputs. Checking their numerical domains under the new geometry is not an independent proof of the upstream contour construction, and no local mock or supporting Lean component is being treated as one.

## 6. Quantitative core caps and complete residual

Use, on each ORIGINAL nominal a0 dyad A,

    C_sq(A)=U^(13/40) A^(24/5),
    C_cu(A)=U^(3/4) A^(24/5).                        (16)

For every collision/hole summand retain the full original kernel up to(5). Apply SQ first, CU outside SQ, then retain HARD when BOTH caps fail. All cores refer to the literal ideal(Delta*ell). This is an exact signed partition of that mask-expanded Poisson expression, not a positive norm assertion. It is independent of the artificial f label. The signed d sum and every original collision label remain in the complementary term.

The A powers of the two second terms become zero, costing only logarithmic dyads. SQ0 gains A^(3/5), SQ cross A^(3/10), CU0 A^(1/5), CU cross A^(1/10). Summing A<<U^(1/6), and including(13)-(14), gives these deliberately coarse bounds:

| Term | Full exponent, bounded on the whole physical box |
|---|---|
| SQ0 | <=161/120+2tau/3 |
| SQ cross | <=263/160+5tau/12 |
| CU0 | <=77/60+tau/3 |
| CU cross | <=431/240+tau/4 |
| SQ2 | 53/48+(r+s+v)/3+tau/6 |
| CU2 geometric | 35/24+(r+s)/6+v/3+tau/6 |
| CU2 remaining linear | 11/8+s/3+v/3+tau/6 |

The first four have positive spare after subtracting from123353/67500 and reserving1/500 for ALL auxiliary losses and1/200 for the retained saving. For the last three compare with delta(r+s)+rho. Their minimum occurs at delta=17/25,r=17/20,s=33/25,v=1/20: the r,s derivatives are positive and the delta derivative is >=21481/24300>0. Raw gaps before tau/6 are respectively

    23813/2730000, 2768/170625, 2768/170625+1/200.

After tau/6, auxiliary1/500 and retained1/200, the first two spares are177/113750 and8241/910000; the third is larger by1/200. All fixed profile, divisor, finite-place, dyadic, height and geometric losses can be divided within that single auxiliary allowance, fixing orders before the eventual U threshold. The original independent height operators, including -W/2-yW', remain in H_J. This inherits rather than repairs positive-slot uniformity.

Let R_N,hard be EXACTLY the Hcol!=1 part of C6 after the paid principal block is removed, written via(3)-(8), with 0<N(ell)<=H_c and BOTH core inequalities in(16) failed. This includes all retained collision-site patterns, the complete signed hole expansion and all original masks. Equations(1)-(16) propose

    R_nonunique=R_N,hard+O(H_J U^(T-1/200+epsilon)).   (17)

The old conductor deletions in(1) are included in the error rather than silently imposed on the new inner sequences. The residual is therefore a new exact-source representation with a paid transfer, not the assertion that every retained original nonunique pair is small.

On Hcol=1 the same calculation reduces to the preceding unique-source SQ/CU calculation. Combine it with accepted G185-G186's larger unique low band N(ell)<=U^(39/25) and genuine far tail. If R_U,hard is the original unique middle where BOTH caps fail, then

    ||F_<||_U^2=R_U,hard+R_N,hard
                         +O(H_J U^(T-1/200+epsilon)). (18)

For R_N,hard there is NO claimed general low-band payment up to U^(39/25); its range starts at the first nonzero frequency and the core failures themselves impose its lower restrictions. The d-dependent signed frequency representations are retained in full. Large squarefree first-dual ideals can have both cores equal to the full ideal, so the hard complement is substantial and open.

## Preserved interfaces and scoped audits

These are useful exact contracts and corrections, not new arithmetic
savings or claims of novelty over their recorded ancestry.

**D12, full logarithmic primitive.** Put
B(x)=sum_(n<=x) a(n) log(x/n)=integral_1^x M(t)dt/t, zero below1.
Its Mellin transform is 1/(s^2 L(s,chi)) for Re(s)>1. A complete
dyadic B energy O(X^(2gamma+epsilon)), 0<gamma<1, makes that transform
and every fixed derivative holomorphic in Re(s)>gamma by shell
Cauchy-Schwarz and locally uniform summation. The meromorphic identity
s^2 L H=1 excludes all zeros there. It retains imprimitive factors and
the principal pole; no conductor-uniform constants are assumed.

In logarithmic variables b''=sum_n a(n)delta_log(n), INCLUDING the n=1
atom. The Gaussian return is U(exp v)=integral b(u)g_tau''(u-v)du, with
both integrations by parts and tails paid. Its complete weighted kernel
cost is at most exp(tau sigma^2/2)(sigma^2+2/tau). Hence no loss in
gamma is required for zero exclusion. The separate pointwise sharp
finite-difference route B=O(x^beta) -> M=O(x^((beta+1)/2)) is valid but
unnecessary for this purpose. The differential-kernel mechanism is
standard [restricted research revision] ancestry; its original rational coefficient source differs.
No improved B estimate is supplied.

**D22, exact prime operator and its actual source.** For finite
unramified P, product_(p in P)(I-chi(p)D_p)1_(x>=1) equals
sum_(d|product P,d<=x) mu(d)chi(d). With every unramified prime<=N it
is M(x) throughout x<=N; N>=2X pays a full physical shell. Ramified
factors are identity. No fixed Mellin identity is assigned to a moving P.

For coefficient shifts S_p e_n=p^-sigma e_(pn) with the cutoff pn<=N,
each T_p=I-chi(p)S_p is unit triangular. Its determinant1 gives no
contraction. A two-state singular value is (sqrt(4+r^2)+r)/2>1,
r=p^-sigma. On a full tensor box 0<=k_p<=K, coefficients
product_p(-chi(p))^k_p give the projected squared ratio

    product_(p in P) [1+K(1+p^-sigma)^2]/(K+1).

The finite witness requires N>=(product P)^K. Letting K tend to
infinity for FIXED P proves the infinite coefficient-space norm
product_p(1+p^-sigma); it does not assign that limit to a growing finite
matrix. For 0<sigma<=1 the product diverges as P grows, but this is not
a specified power of N or an obstruction to every affordable restricted
moving-prime regime. The actual e1 column has bounded weighted l2 norm
for sigma>1/2, while its sharp readout costs X^(sigma+1/2)>X.
Neither unrestricted witness lower-bounds the actual signed Mertens sum.
The independent complex chi mod5 box check gives 451/162. Pair02/W38
are direct ancestry; the all-power f3 source of G69 is different.

**S09, true prefixes commute.** Truncated shifts V_p,V_q both map e_n
to e_(pqn) exactly when pqn<=N; both intermediate indices then fit.
They commute for every N. The non-divisor-closed mask {1,2,6} can fail
commutation, but it omits the real n=3 source and must restore that
complement. This does not exclude every other projected construction.

**S38, ordinary trace is not the sharp readout.** For N>=pX,

    [P_X,chi(p)V_p]e_n
      =-chi(p)1_(X/p<n<=X)e_(pn).

This strictly raises indices, so its product on either side with any
finite Dirichlet-convolution matrix has ordinary trace zero. Inserting
the exact inverse-convolution matrix does not create a Mertens detector.
The actual coordinate sum on the coefficient source is instead
-chi(p)[M(X)-M(X/p)]. With quartic chi mod5, p=2,X=4,N=8, it equals1
while the trace is0. A complete signed difference bound at exponent
gamma>0 would return M by telescoping with cost1/(1-p^-gamma); that
window estimate is unpaid. Adjoints, noncausal operators or a different
trace are eligible only with their full new identity and costs.

Other preserved tests include the correct prime recurrence
M=R_p-chi(p)R_p(./p) and its full inverse; finite absolute Euler prices
do not uniformly bound an infinite bank for gamma<=1. The one-prime
weighted topological trace 1-chi(p) is not an ordinary chain-map trace
unless the weight commutes with the boundary. The principal scalar uses
minus the REDUCED Euler characteristic, including the empty face.
Unrestricted Gaussian Gram bounds cost X^2 and do not lower-bound
the signed arithmetic energy. All are scoped, with their live escapes
retained; no untested card is relabeled impossible.

## D02 and the seven other first tests

For the actual finite Gaussian Gram M at distinct positive integer labels, M is positive definite: dividing a vanishing finite Gaussian combination by its common Gaussian leaves a sum of distinct real exponentials, whose derivative Vandermonde is nonsingular. This also covers complex source coefficients. Near singularity is compatible with exact positive definiteness.

The determinant lemma gives det(M+lambda cc*)/det M=1+lambda c*M^-1c. The desired energy is c*Mc. With v=Mc the corrected ratio is exactly1+lambda c*Mc. The repaired rank-one determinant and the shell Fredholm rank-one version encode the same original energy, not a weaker arithmetic input. Approximate Mc is subject to inverse-Gram amplification. The actual Gaussian tail or G13/G20 source error must be paid before a finite ratio returns to the fixed detector. D48's small pivot explains a possible primal/dual ratio of order X^4 in an innovation direction; it does not assert that literal f3 occupies that direction.

S08's matrix[[1,-1],[-1,1]] with c=(1,1) refutes monotonicity under deleting negative cross terms, at generic matrix scope. S06's irrational log2/log3 blocks the stated one-common-exponential polynomial substitution; multivariable resultants need their own diagonal restriction and height/error costs. S18 has not made arbitrary complex n^-s algebraic, and no denominator/conjugate height bound is supplied. These are failed bridges, not global impossibility theorems.

S46's unit-coefficient convolution recurrence forces mu. For general ordinary chi the recurrence contains chi(r) and yields mu(n)chi(n); matrix enlargement with the same scalar inverse cannot change it. A different nonlinear readout remains untested. S37 and S49 unitary gauges preserve norms, and zero-extended character values cannot be replaced by unit phases. A genuine cocycle also needs its loop products to match. S41's exact commutator is [C_Y,D_p]e_n=-1_(Y/p<n<=Y)e_(pn); the given p=2,Y=2 vector has quadratic form-1 despite trace0. Actual masked-boundary defects remain unpaid. These seven tests are independent of the three main developments and retain their narrow failure scopes.

### 7.1 The complete compensator is longer than the new useful range

In PR9 B0.25–27 a subset of original slots of width d has

    M'=M-2d, z'=ell-d, N'=1+ell-d, 0<=d<=ell.

At the accepted [restricted research revision] geometry, ell=313594727/1875000000, M=1-ell and 1/6<ell<1/5. Thus N'-M'=2ell+d>0, so(12) costs N'+M'/6. The retained B0.26 applies because N'-(M'+2z')=3d>=0, and costs

    E_old=M'+max(0,-1+5ell+d)/4.

The difference obeys

    E_new-E_old=(1+11ell)/6+2d/3-max(0,-1+5ell+d)/4
                 >17/36-1/20=19/45>0.              (18)

Indeed the first term is greater than17/36, and the positive part is below1/20. This holds for EVERY rescaled subset, including the empty subset, before its common outside coefficient and tuple count are applied. Taking the old/new minimum therefore never improves this entire compensator family. The important negative subset coefficient and the old -d saving are retained; replacing every energy by an artificial M' target was not used.

### 4.2 Local and shortened-scale branches

Use the exact geometry
\[
 \ell=626701/3750000,\quad h=3969737987/5000000000,\quad
 y=h-2\ell,\quad x=1+\ell-h.
\]
For \(d\in[h-10^{-3},h+10^{-10}]\) and
\(t=\log_Uh_0\in[0,10^{-3}]\), the nominal reflected upper length is
\[
 n(d,t)=1-y/d+t,\qquad z_A(t)=(1-2n(d,t))/C.
\]
Reserve a small common capacity decrement and annular/scale-box padding. Before these losses the exact edges supplied by the source are
\[
 n_-=\frac{4998608000}{11894213961},\qquad
 n_+=\frac{402041377237}{952737117000},
\]
\[
 .41<n_-\le n_+<.422,\qquad
 .03<z_-\le z_+<.0355.
\]
The upper margins are approximately \(1.43651\cdot10^{-5}\) in n and \(4.22098\cdot10^{-5}\) in z. The loss budget must fit these tighter edges, as well as the local theorem's larger window.

Let \(x_1,x_2\) be the actual nonnegative plain lengths after clipping nonempty subunit annuli by bounded dilation. There are exactly the following needed cases:

| Actual selected width/scales | Estimate | Capacity verification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| \(z_I<.03\), any \(x_i\le.422\) | Incumbent \(9/2\) positive moment, or MP0 if empty | \(x_1+x_2+(9/2)z_I\le .844+.135=.979\) |
| \(.03\le z_I\le.0355\), some \(x_j<.41\) | Incumbent \(9/2\) moment | \(.41+.422+(9/2)(.0355)=1-33/4000\) |
| \(.03\le z_I\le z_A(t)\), both \(x_i\ge.41\) | New local moment | \(x_i<.44,\ z_I<.04,\ x_1+x_2+Cz_I\le2n+Cz_A\le1\) |

Equalities at .03 or .41 cause no gap because the estimates overlap. The old coefficient is \(6\kappa\le9/2\), so the displayed stronger old capacity checks imply the actual incumbent condition.

The logarithmic scale region is covered by a high/high rectangle and two low-coordinate rectangles. The two-variable supremum estimate is applied separately on them. Its four derivative profile pairs preserve the supports, and there are only \(O((\log U)^2)\) scale boxes. This is why scale shortening needs no extension of the new local moment below .41. The strict old reserves allow all fixed annular and box errors.

By (E1), all three cases retain the gain at the same target capacity. Hölder gives
\[
 \sum_{\rm class}|S_u|
 \ll U^{1/4+3R_\kappa/4-qz_A(t)/2+\epsilon}.
\]
Indeed the moment controls the fourth power of the plain factor times the squared selected product; dividing by (E1) and taking a fourth root produces exactly \(qz_A/2\). The full main-product upper bound is still \(Z^{\ell q+o(1)}\).

## Primary-source screen, ancestry, and next useful action

Tao, *The logarithmically averaged Chowla and Elliott conjectures for two-point correlations*, arXiv1509.05422v4 (29July2016), Theorem1.2 and Corollary1.5, was verified from the primary PDF at https://arxiv.org/pdf/1509.05422v4 . It gives qualitative fixed-linear-form logarithmic conclusions under the stated hypotheses; no power-uniform growing-lag estimate(A) is extracted. The Matomaki--Radziwill--Tao--Teravainen--Ziegler Annals197(2023) primary abstract, https://annals.math.princeton.edu/2023/197-2/p03 , describes higher uniformity in short intervals on average; the displayed qualitative o(XH) scale alone does not establish(A). These papers motivate the screen, not a claimed new input. No outside theorem is needed for Theorem M beyond elementary probability, orthogonality, Abel summation, ordinary zeta continuation/growth, and Gaussian Mellin inversion, all used explicitly above.

The relevant local ancestry is [private research revision] headroom-A's calibrated coarse countermodels; headroom-B's fixed-grid and primitive-pair alternatives; W24's square-divisor source; W27's finite-prime/global-inversion distinction; [private research revision] detector transfers; and the accepted [private research revision] W43/Sol02 complete projection/block returns. The current proof and attempt index were consulted for scope and duplicates. This report neither reaudits the original PR9/PR15 local theorem nor treats relative algebra as an independent arithmetic saving. Source hashes in the receipt bind the exact files inspected, with read limits recorded rather than claiming every line was reread. Credit for the accepted route remains with Gao and the project's documented contributors, including Hailey Collet, Akash Levy, and OpenAI-assisted work; outside-paper credit remains with the named authors.

Decision: retain Theorems M and B for independent review as a substantive source-specific obstruction plus an exact high-ceiling replacement contract. Do not promote any c, do not call(A) proved, and do not spend a new pass merely tuning theta. The next arithmetic development target is the full weighted signed sum(L) for the actual mu*chi prime law, uniformly through |h|<X^theta, with the explicit exponent e<.749722+theta. A proof using global convolution inversion must show where it destroys Theorem M's coherent pole; a proof using a short-window result must supply the rate and growing-lag uniformity. Finite prime checks, fixed-lag qualitative limits, and rank compression cannot supply that missing step.

The strongest useful completed result of this pass is the exact multiplicative countermodel and forced energy lower bound(O). It materially sharpens the earlier coarse-source obstruction and redirects the live short-window route to a specific global arithmetic input. Every candidate above has a stated disposition; no result is represented as a solution of the full zero-free problem.

statement:
### 3.3 Explicit constants: no free growing-color import

One can make the constant in(12) explicit. Let D=max(1,||b||_infinity,
sup_y|sum_(n<=y)b(n)|). Write C_t for a permissible constant. The proof above gives

    C_1<=D,
    C_t<=D^t+sum_(m=1)^(t-1)binom(t,m)C_m[Dm]^(t-m),
    C_t<=(2D)^t(t!)^2.                                    (18a)

For the last inequality, insert the induction bound and divide by(2D)^t(t!)^2.
With j=t-m each summand is at most2^(-j)/j!, since m!m^j<=t!. Their sum is less
than e^(1/2)-1, while the D^t term supplies at most1/(2^t(t!)^2); together they are
less than1 for t>=2. This pays every binomial overlap and does not assert the
factorial upper bound is optimal.

Let c_(t,a)=[z^a](1+tz)(1-z)^t and define the actual absolute Euler price

    Gabs_t(sigma)=prod_l[1+sum_(a=2)^(t+1)|c_(t,a)|l^(-a sigma)].

For t fixed it is finite whenever sigma>1/2. For FIXED1/2<sigma<1 a coarse explicit
growing-t estimate is

    log Gabs_t(sigma) <= C_sigma t^(1/sigma) log(2t), t>=2.  (18b)

To prove it, split at Y=t^(1/sigma). For l>Y use
|c_(t,a)|<=t^a(1/a!+1/(a-1)!) and t*l^(-sigma)<1, so the local logarithm is
O(t^2 l^(-2sigma)). Summing over ALL integers beyond Y bounds the total by
O_sigma(t^(1/sigma)). For l<=Y the local absolute series is at most
(1+t l^(-sigma))(1+l^(-sigma))^t. Its logarithm is at most
log(1+t)+t*l^(-sigma); summing over all integers up to Y gives the stated bound.
Ramified primes only reduce this absolute price. This is an upper bound, not a
lower-bound obstruction to a sharper estimate.

For any sigma>1/2 with sigma>=1-1/t, the actual constant in the t>=1 term of(16)
can therefore be bounded by

    (2D)^t(t!)^2 Gabs_t(sigma)(1+p^(1-sigma))^(J-t).         (18c)

The last factor is the COMPLETE summatory price of v_(p,J-t), retaining every
p^a argument and its coefficient p^a. The low-color combination also carries the
explicit factors binom(J+1,t+1) from(19); its t=0 term is at most
(J+1)(1+p)^J. For fixed J these are harmless fixed constants. For a growing J they
must all be paid; neither the sublinear chain degree nor the factor1/k! in(2)
makes them automatically subpower. In particular the bound(18b) at a fixed target
sigma can grow too quickly at J comparable to log x/loglog x. This is the price
of the actual proof, not a theorem ruling out a better growing-color argument.

statement:
## 3. Protected S29: a stable prime state still needs a signed observation theorem

### 3.1 The exact countable realization and the first-test correction

On the Hilbert space of squarefree q-units with increasing prime labels, for sigma>1/2 let

    T_sigma e_n=sum_(p>P+(n), p not dividing q)
                         chi(p)p^-sigma e_(np),   P+(1)=1.

Distinct parents have disjoint k-step descendants. Therefore, with S_sigma=sum_(p not dividing q)p^-2sigma<infinity,

    ||T_sigma^k||^2 <= S_sigma^k/k!,
    v_sigma=(I+T_sigma)^-1 e_1,
    v_sigma(n)=mu(n)chi(n)n^-sigma.                           (11)

The Neumann series converges in operator norm; T is quasinilpotent. This is B22/G145 ancestry, not a new theorem or an essential-spectrum failure. It directly answers the first affordable question in the protected seed. The actual squareful and nonunit coefficients are zero because those vertices are absent, not replaced by free signs.

The physical output is

    M_chi(N)=Lambda_(N,sigma)v_sigma,
    Lambda_(N,sigma)u=sum_(n<=N)n^sigma u_n.

Squarefree q-unit counting and partial summation give
||Lambda||^2 ~ kappa_q N^(2sigma+1)/(2sigma+1), with kappa_q>0. Thus the naive norm price has exponent sigma+1/2>1. G117/G145 already rule out repairing this by arbitrary positive diagonal reweighting. Section 2 now covers much more than diagonal weights: under the congruence W=diag(n^sigma), a banded terminal majorant for Lambda becomes precisely a banded majorant for ell on the physical a=Wv. The cost is unchanged. This is a source-sensitive refinement of the observation obstruction, not a saving from the stable state.

### 3.2 An exact prime-graph storage identity, including the harmonic part

Here is a concrete alternative that uses the long multiplicative edges rather than a short additive metric. Let S={n<=N:mu(n)^2=1,(n,q)=1}. Use all edges n--np with p not dividing nq and np<=N, with arbitrary positive weights w_e. This graph is connected through divisors to 1. Let L be its ordinary weighted graph Laplacian and U=diag(a_n) on S. Then |a_n|=1, and

    L_a=U L U*,
    x*L_a x=sum_(n--np) w_e |x_(np)+chi(p)x_n|^2,
    L_a a=0.                                                (12)

Every edge relation is the literal arithmetic one. Squareful and nonunit vertices contribute zero to the original output and are not assigned artificial inverse equations here. The complete graph and all its retained endpoints are specified.

For lambda>0 and eta>0 define the anchored storage

    H=lambda L_a+eta e_1 e_1*.

It is positive definite, and its actual source energy is exactly a*Ha=eta. A successful global majorant H>=ell ell* would therefore prove |M_chi(N)|^2<=eta. Its full criterion, however, is

    H>=ell ell*  iff  |M_chi(N)|^2/eta+E_N/lambda <=1,
    E_N=f_R* (L_RR)^-1 f_R,  f=U*ell, R=S minus {1}.        (13)

E_N>=0 includes the entire signed Green contraction. For N=1 it is zero. To prove (13), use the rank-one criterion ell*H^-1ell<=1 and conjugate by U. Solve (lambda L+eta e_1e_1*)x=f. Summing all coordinates gives x_1=(sum f)/eta. Writing x=x_1 ell+y with y_1=0 gives y_R=(L_RR)^-1 f_R/lambda. Consequently

    f*x=|sum f|^2/eta+f_R*(L_RR)^-1 f_R/lambda,

and sum f=conjugate(M_chi(N)). No off-diagonal Green terms or zero mode have been removed.

If M!=0, feasibility requires lambda>E_N and

    eta >= |M_chi(N)|^2/(1-E_N/lambda).                      (14)

If M=0, lambda>=E_N suffices for any eta>0, with equality allowed. If lambda<E_N no eta works. These edge cases prevent treating the complementary Green cost as a free or strictly contractive term.

A graph gap may help bound E_N. It cannot remove the first term of (13): the actual arithmetic vector is exactly the harmonic state. This supplies a sharp finite version of the older G74 harmonic-mode warning, now with the literal squarefree ordinary-character graph, an explicit positive complement and arbitrary edge weights. It is a legitimate high-ceiling architecture only if a noncircular method proves the complete majorant at eta<<N^(2gamma+epsilon). The formula does not provide that method. It is not a claim that all prime graphs, indefinite storage or source-restricted observers fail.

For gamma=.8748,5/6,3/4 the necessary complete storage exponents are respectively 1.7496,5/3,3/2 (allow every epsilon). Mere boundedness of (I+T)^-1, a graph gap, vanishing edge defects or finite numerical feasibility does not establish any of these targets. The next mathematical action is to estimate nonlocal signed observation structure, or a proved reachable-state class that avoids the global majorant, while retaining the full Green/harmonic reconstruction.

statement:
## 2. The fixed Gaussian and the interpolation step

Fix tau>0. Write g_tau(v)=(2*pi*tau)^(-1/2) exp(-v^2/(2tau)).
For a fixed ordinary character chi use the complete coefficients
a_n=mu(n)chi(n), including both natural sets of zeros, and

    F(z)=sum_(n>=1) a_n g_tau(log n-z).                    (R39.1)

The supplied cards used the raw Gaussian; multiplying by the fixed
sqrt(2*pi*tau) changes no exponent. It does change heat derivatives
when tau varies, as the independent C05 audit below records.

Absolute local uniform convergence makes R39.1 entire. For z=u+iv,
the modulus of each kernel is exp(v^2/(2tau)) times its real kernel.
The positive integer sum is bounded by its integral plus twice its
maximum: as a function of the real integer variable the Gaussian is
unimodal, so partitioning on the two sides of its maximum proves
that elementary sum-integral bound. Its integral is exp(u+tau/2).
For u>=0 this proves |F(u+iv)|<=C_tau exp(u+v^2/(2tau)).
For real u<=0, factoring exp(-u^2/(2tau)) leaves a summable
series bounded by its value at u=0. This pays the left Mellin tail.
Every fixed derivative has the same local convergence justification.

### R39-A. Complex-polynomial interpolation is valid

For a complex polynomial P of degree <=N on a unit interval, with
|P|<=m almost everywhere on a measurable set of measure >=delta,
the bound

    sup_I |P| <= (4e/delta)^N m                            (R39.2)

is valid. Use the closed sublevel set of P, of measure Delta>=delta,
and choose its N+1 interior measure quantiles. Its distribution
function is 1-Lipschitz, so x_j-x_i>=(j-i)delta/(N+1). The Lagrange
denominator at node j is at least
(delta/(N+1))^N j!(N-j)!, while each numerator factor on I is <=1.
The sum of absolute interpolation weights is therefore at most
((N+1)/delta)^N 2^N/N! <=(4e/delta)^N. Complex values require no
extra sign or real-root assumption. Essential suprema are handled
by enlarging m and taking a limit. The case N=0 is immediate.

Now suppose a fixed complex-growth bound is available:

    |F(u+iv)| <= C(1+|v|)^K exp(bu+v^2/(2tau)), u>=0,    (R39.3)

with fixed b>gamma. In every sufficiently large integer interval
I_j=[j,j+1], suppose a measurable E_j has measure >=c j^-kappa and
essential supremum <=C_0 exp(gamma j). The same conclusion holds
with arbitrarily small exponent allowances, as specified below.

Take N=ceil(2(b-gamma)j/log j), center j+1/2 and radius
R=sqrt(tau(N+1)). For large j, the whole disk lies in u>=0.
The maximum on that disk has logarithm

    <=bj+R^2/(2tau)+bR+O(K log(1+R)+1).

Cauchy's coefficient estimate for the Taylor polynomial P_N gives
on the whole real interval the **complete** remainder

    r_j <= M_R (1/(2R))^(N+1)/(1-1/(2R)),
    log r_j <= bj-(N/2)log N+O(N+sqrt N+K log N)
             =gamma j+o(j).                             (R39.4)

The o(j) includes the positive j*loglog j/log j correction; it is
not silently removed before interpolation. On E_j, |P_N| is at
most C_0 exp(gamma j)+r_j. Apply R39.2 to P_N and then add the
remainder outside E_j. Both errors survive:

    sup_I |F| <= L_j C_0 exp(gamma j)+(L_j+1)r_j,
    log L_j <= 2kappa(b-gamma)j+o(j).

Thus the complete output exponent is

    gamma+2kappa(b-gamma).                               (R39.5)

This verifies W39.3--8, including the coefficient 2 and both
amplified remainders. It does not prove this coefficient optimal.
For kappa>=1/2 this estimate does not improve the prior b; it is
not an impossibility theorem for all observation methods.

For kappa=0, a fixed positive measure in **every** unit interval
already preserves gamma for an arbitrary bounded-coefficient fixed
Gaussian. A derivative bound for each fixed order does not suffice
in its place: this proof uses orders N growing like j/log j and a
quantitative complex bound on disks of radius about sqrt(j/log j).
A merely fixed-width analytic strip likewise does not give R39.4.

## 7. Actual signs and the terminal Gaussian complement

Let u=(1-rho)/rho. For 1/3<rho<1/2, 1<u<2 and

    B(rho)=2log u-3-4/u-1/u^2.

Its derivative with respect to u is positive, and its maximum in this
range is `2log2-21/4<0`. Equivalently,

    B'(rho)=-2/(1-rho)-2/rho
                       -2/(1-rho)^2-2/(1-rho)^3<0. ([restricted research revision])

Thus R_(X^rho)(x) is eventually negative uniformly on the whole shell,
and the literal band (C4) is eventually positive. These are signs of
the complete actual fields, not of individual prime jumps.

For the explicit example,

    B(3/8)=2log(5/3)-144/25,
    B(2/5)=2log(3/2)-55/9,

which proves (C5) algebraically. At rho=2/5 the actual prefix, if its
leading term is obtained using the accepted bound for F, has coefficient
`C_f[55/9-2log(3/2)]`. Extrapolating the [private research revision] subpower formula would
instead give `C_f*(5/2)*exp(-gamma_E)`, because its product constant is
`3 exp(-gamma_E) product_(p>=5)(1-1/(p-1)^2)`. These are plainly different.
No such extrapolation was authorized by [private research revision]; the present calculation
identifies its concrete late-range failure and the reversed band sign.

For every fixed b>1/2, the source condition omega_(X^b)(n)>=2 forces
`n>X^(2b)`. The full Gaussian lattice tail therefore gives

    R_(X^b)(x)=O_A(X^(-A))                           ([restricted research revision])

for any fixed A, uniformly on [X,2X]. This is an approximate terminal
statement with its whole tail paid, not a finite exact cutoff of the
uncapped source. It is independent of a full-F bound.

Consequently, for fixed 1/3<a<1/2<b, the actual added band across the
half-power transition satisfies

    T_(X^b)-T_(X^a)=R_(X^a)-R_(X^b)
      =C_f exp(tau/2)B(a)x/L^3
                         +O(X/L^4+X^(1-kappa)L),    ([restricted research revision])

and is eventually NEGATIVE. Thus a complete finite portion of the late
flow has positive bands inside the two-prime range and a negative band
when the last rough-prime pair becomes Gaussian-negligible. A uniform
negative-drift argument extending the earlier subpower regime cannot
describe these actual coefficients.

No assertion is made at rho=1/2 itself or in a shrinking neighborhood
of it. There the available core length and the support edge of phi_t
meet, so the uniform corridor used in ([restricted research revision]) disappears. This is a real
remaining transition problem, not a value obtained by taking a limit
in (C3). Similarly, the proof does not cross rho=1/3, where a third
rough-prime occurrence can enter the original Gaussian central range.

                                    H^(-2beta)Y^(1-beta),
 ||F_gs^[theta]||^2 << H_J U^(1+epsilon)D^beta
                           G^(-beta)H^(-2beta)Y^(1-beta). (3.3)

The second bound includes the entire weighted intersection subtraction,
F_s^[theta]=(M S_bad Q)^[theta]-F_gs^[theta]. Thus it is not a signed-subset
comparison. All mixed terms are paid by Hilbert triangle. Inserting the
pointwise loss before the absolute convolution is precisely why the old
G,H powers survive, including arbitrary shared-prime valuations.

Finally C=F^[theta]-F_g^[theta]-F_s^[theta] EXACTLY. Equations(2.6),(3.3) give

 ||C||_Omega^2 << H_J U^(1+epsilon)D^beta
   [ A^(-beta)+(G^(-beta)+H^(-2beta))Y^(1-beta) ].     (3.4)

At A=U^(2eta),Y=G=U^(4eta),H=U^(2eta), the three savings are

   2beta eta, (8beta-4)eta, (8beta-4)eta.

Since beta>=.68-small>2/3, all are at least2beta eta, with fixed reserve over
eta. At the limiting beta=.68 these are1.36eta and1.44eta. Thus

 ||B_c^[theta] Q||_Omega^2
          << H_J U^(1+beta*m-2beta*eta+epsilon).       (3.5)

This is an actual estimate for the COMPLETE band-weighted residual, preserving
every ordered tuple and sign. It is not a new canonical-column assumption.

For comparison with a possible sharper upstream repeat-product cut, the proof
has the following precisely conditional interface. Suppose a removed source
has an exact divisor-block decomposition with the SAME shortened plain factors
and absolute MI coefficient mass O(U^epsilon T^(-beta/2)). Then(3.2) changes
its squared norm by at most Y^(1-beta). The corresponding core bound becomes
U^(1+epsilon)D^beta[A^(-beta)+T^(-beta)Y^(1-beta)]. If T=U^(4eta), the same
budget applies. This does not prove that product-cut premise, duplicate its
independent proof, or assume its acceptance. Our actual statement(3.5) uses
only the explicitly stated G,H core and retains its pending dependency.

statement:
## 2. Whole coefficient, prior common profile, and exact roots

The inherited primitive pair has good conductor nn', local exponents 1 and 5, and no zero-frequency contribution. Primes shared by ell and a source factor give primitive Fourier zeros, including slot primes. Fixed row ray restrictions modulo a disjoint fixed modulus preserve this good-prime zero by CRT. Original principal inducing rows have not been deleted.

G185's finite identities give, apart from nu(n)conjugate(nu(n')),

    e=-1: R(n,n')chi_n(-1)conjugate(G(n))G(n')
           a0(n)conjugate(a0(n'))chi_n(ell)conjugate(chi_n'(ell)),
    e=+1: R(n,n')G(n)conjugate(G(n'))chi_n'(-1)
           conjugate(a0(n))a0(n')conjugate(chi_n(ell))chi_n'(ell).

The CRT ratio R is the fixed ray sign; the finite dictionary separates these factors. Both signs are retained. In particular the common-source extraction law is a0(fm)=a0(f)a0(m)chi_m(f)^4, or its full conjugate. A second cross-copy cubic phase is not being suppressed.

Extend the displayed formal product expression to individually squarefree columns, and insert the FULL identity sum_(f|n,f|n')mu(f). Artificial noncoprime pairs cancel pointwise, including inverse-slot and slot-slot coincidences. A frequency selector independent of f survives this identity unchanged. There is no assertion of imprimitive Poisson on the added pairs.

For fixed f, write n=fm,n'=fm'. Each column is squarefree, so m,m' avoid f. Each prime of f is assigned to one of its actual original inverse colors or named slots, independently on the two sides. Write f=f1 f2 fP=g1 g2 gP. Both residual product scales equal

    X=(D1/q_f1)(D2/q_f2)(P0/q_fP)=N0/q_f
     =(D1/q_g1)(D2/q_g2)(P0/q_gP).

All assigned slot tests and coefficients are retained. At fixed slot depth, both allocation counts together are bounded by tau(f)^C. No equality between the two shortened inverse pairs is assumed.

For one fixed allocation, finite dictionary entry and common Fourier component, the entire residual column is

    B_f(ell)=X^(-1/2) sum_(m sf) c_f(m) chi_m(ell)^eta,
    eta in {1,-1}.                                      (V2)

Here c_f is the ACTUAL sum over all residual original factorizations m=xyP, with their separate profiles and slot labels. It includes a0(m) or its conjugate, fixed ray factors, the appropriate f twist, and the a/f holes. For fixed squarefree m, each prime has at most j+2 places. Slot restrictions only reduce this count, even though a named slot may contain at most one prime. Thus |c_f(m)|<=H_J tau(m)^C and

    X^(-1) sum_(q_m~X)|c_f(m)|^2 << H_J U^epsilon.        (V3)

Indeed tau(m)^C<<_eta q_m^eta, and the ideal count is O(X). Choose eta after the fixed polynomial cap on X. Assigned f-slot choices have already been paid outside; they are not paid again as a new P0 mass. This is uniform in each separate allocation, fixed punctures and modulus-one twists. Empty windows stay empty. A nonempty nominal subunit scale differs from one by only a fixed support factor, so clipping gives a bounded dilation, including X near one.

The whole coefficient being divisor bounded is sufficient for these TWO arbitrary-sequence sieves. It remains insufficient for PR9 B3.6, whose canonical merged coefficient forbids such an extra weight. No canonical reflected-energy extension is used.

PR9 B3.3 separates the profile on the original ambient normalized inverse/individual-slot box on both copies, with nominal a,ell dyads A,H. Its kernel argument is C*y_ell/(y_a^6 product(y_source)), C=UH/(A^6N0^2). Euler derivatives are uniformly bounded in C by fixed Schwartz seminorms. The measure is fixed BEFORE a,f,kappa,b,t,z and slot choices. Only then substitute the factorizations. Extracted imaginary powers have modulus one; original real roots occur in the profile once. The resulting c_f may depend on nominal A,H and the fixed Fourier component, but not on the live sieve row. Enlarging a positive frequency energy uses this one separated extension, not a newly chosen row-dependent profile.

Both unnormalized residual columns are sqrt(X) times (V2). Hence the original U/(q_a^6 N0^2) becomes EXACTLY

    [U/(q_a^6 N0^2)]sqrt(X)sqrt(X)
        =U/(q_a^6 N0 q_f).                             (V4)

The real ratio N0/sqrt(q_n q_n') becomes X/sqrt(q_m q_m'), still a bounded profile factor. It supplies neither an extra q_f nor a second inverse q_f. The common frequency twist is |chi_f(ell)|^2=1_((f,ell)=1), an outer restriction; no division by this zero is made.

For a selector w on frequencies, scalar Cauchy bounds sum w B_left conjugate(B_right) by the product of the square roots of two POSITIVE energies with weight |w|. Only then is the frequency set enlarged. The two columns keep distinct coefficients and independent allocations, but have the same upper X and common S0 below. Their energy prices are not multiplied a second time.

statement:
### Fixed-cutoff restoration before applying UM

GS5 allows every fixed finite S containing the character's entire defining-modulus support and the primes above 6. M B0.1 additionally describes a sufficiently large fixed small-prime cutoff. One must not silently enlarge S in the defining GS5 polynomial.

Choose a fixed enlargement \(S'\) sufficient for the inherited UM proof, and let \(\mathfrak t\) be the squarefree product of the primes in \(S'\setminus S\). Freeze \(S'\) after the requested loss has been chosen, independently of all scales, rows and roots. Write \(M^S\) and \(M^{S'}\) for the two presentations. Unique splitting of a squarefree column gives exactly
\[
M^S_v(E;W)=\sum_{d\mid\mathfrak t}
 \mu_K(d)\nu(d)\chi_d(v)q_d^{-1/2}
 M^{S'}_v(E/q_d;W).
\tag{R1}
\]
The original columns and their zeros are restored by this identity. The multipliers depending on v have modulus at most one; their finite total absolute mass is fixed. Cauchy or the Hilbert triangle inequality therefore transfers UM and its scale-maximal version from \(S'\) to the exact original S. For positive scales below 2 use the finite-column bound. The same argument applies to the log-scale derivative profile. No moving prime enters the fixed datum, and all extra constants and derivative orders have permitted dependence on the original fixed datum and the requested loss.

If the intended inherited UM is already explicitly stipulated for every such S, R1 merely records its compatibility with the printed M convention. Either way it removes the ambiguity without weakening GS5's quantifier.

The needed formulation of the inherited amplification is slightly more uniform than writing \(D=U^r\): the core scale U may be bounded, so r need not be bounded. For every fixed \(B\ge1\) and every \(\eta>0\), UM implies
\[
\sum_{\substack{0<q_v\le U\\v\ {\rm sixth\mbox{-}power\mbox{-}free}}}
|M_v(E;W)|^2
\ll_{\nu,S,I,B,\eta}
(2DU)^\eta
\left(U+U^{1/6}E^{5/6}\right)\|W\|_{C^J(I)}^2
\tag{NP4}
\]
for \(D\ge2\), \(1\le U\le D^B\), and \(0<E\le D\). The same estimate holds after restricting to \(\mathcal R_\nu\).

Here sixth-power-free means every prime-ideal valuation lies in \(\{0,1,\ldots,5\}\), including primes in S. All units are retained. There are only finitely many possible S-supported parts of such a core; they cause no varying conductor in the fixed datum.

For completeness, first take \(E\ge2\). Fix a small \(\vartheta>0\) in terms of the requested loss and put
\[
V=\max(2U,E^{1+\vartheta}),\qquad
P=(V/U)^{1/6}.
\tag{NP5}
\]
There are \(\gg_S P\) good ideals \(\mathfrak a\), prime to S, with \(q_{\mathfrak a}\le P\). Choose one generator \(\alpha\); \(\alpha^6\) does not depend on the choice, since every Eisenstein unit has sixth power one. The exact M B0.7 identity is
\[
M_v(E;W)=
\sum_{d\mid\operatorname{rad}\mathfrak a}
\frac{\mu_K(d)\psi_v(d)}{\sqrt{q_d}}
M_{v\alpha^6}(E/q_d;W).
\tag{NP6}
\]
No condition \((v,\mathfrak a)=1\) is imposed. The original natural zeros prove NP6 also at shared primes. The squared absolute divisor mass is \(O_\delta(q_{\mathfrak a}^{\delta})\) for every \(\delta>0\).

The map \((v,\mathfrak a)\mapsto v\alpha^6\) is injective for sixth-power-free v. Valuations modulo six recover v's ideal and the quotient recovers \(\mathfrak a\); \(\alpha^6\) being fixed then recovers v's unit. The S-part of v is unchanged because the amplifier is good.

The scale-maximal UM statement used here is
\[
\sum_{0<q_w\le V}\sup_{0<F\le E}|M_w(F;W)|^2
\ll (2EV)^\delta V\|W\|_{C^{J_1}(I)}^2,
\qquad V\ge E^{1+\vartheta}.
\tag{NP7}
\]
It is M B0.8. It can also be checked directly: logarithmic differentiation replaces W by \(-W/2-xW'\), Sobolev on unit log-scale intervals uses UM for those two common profiles, and the \(O(\log(2E))\) intervals cost a small power. The subunit scales are empty below \(1/b\), and the remaining bounded scales contain finitely many ideals. All orders are fixed before E, U or any amplifier varies.

Averaging NP6 over the amplifiers, applying divisor Cauchy, and then using injectivity and NP7 gives
\[
\sum_{v\ {\rm sixth\mbox{-}power\mbox{-}free}}^{q_v\le U}|M_v(E;W)|^2
\ll (2EV)^{O(\delta)}\frac VP\|W\|_{C^{J_1}}^2
=(2EV)^{O(\delta)}U^{1/6}V^{5/6}\|W\|_{C^{J_1}}^2.
\tag{NP8}
\]
Since \(U\le D^B\), E and V lie in fixed polynomial ranges relative to D. Choose \(\vartheta,\delta\) sufficiently small in terms of \(B,\eta\); NP5–NP8 then give NP4 with \(E^{5/6}\), absorbing \(E^{5\vartheta/6}\) into the displayed loss. For \(E<2\), either the annulus is empty or \(E\ge1/b\) and only \(O_I(1)\) columns occur, giving \(O_I(U\|W\|_\infty^2)\). This proves NP4 uniformly, including \(U\asymp1\).

The argument uses all rows on the right side of NP7. If one starts with nonprincipal cores, multiplication by a sixth power changes only deletions, so \(\psi_{v\alpha^6}^*=\psi_v^*\). Positive enlargement to all rows is therefore legitimate and does not replace a nonprincipal family by a different coefficient family.

### 4.1 Exact bin geometry and permissible source tails

The bins satisfy

    sqrt(Z) exp(iH) <= d < sqrt(Z) exp((i+1)H),
    Y<d<=Dmax.

Their left edges are included, their right edges are excluded,
and the real Dmax cap is retained. Therefore:

- If i+j<-2, then i+j<=-3 and de<Z exp(-H)=T.
- If i+j>=-2, then de>=Z exp(-2H).
- Once H>log 2, J_Z=floor(1+log 2/H)=1. If i+j>1,
  then de>=Z exp(2H)>2Z exp(H)=B.
- If d>Dmax and e>Y is an integer, then e>=Y+1 and de>B;
  the same holds with d and e interchanged.

Thus all original pairs omitted by GC17 lie either in the paid
low-product source or in the paid upper tail. There is no assertion
that the four-diagonal rectangle has exactly the same product cap.
Its included products can range from Z exp(-2H) to below Z exp(3H).

For low products the common derivative order
m=1+floor(kappa sqrt(L)/tau) in R35.4 gives

    |S_tau(y/(de))|
       <= exp(-kappa^2 L/(2tau)+O(sqrt(L)log L))

whenever y in [Z,2Z] and de<=T. Summing at most Z(1+log Z)
ordered labels gives Z^(-A_0+o(1)). The omitted-label mask and the
coprime/6 mask are bounded and independent of ell, so this bound
applies to the actual omitted labels after each alternating sum is
completed. An ell-dependent truncation cannot be inserted first.

For total indices n>B, the absolute coefficient majorant is d_3(n)
for every relevant original-pair subset, including the primitive
rectangle. Its summatory bound is t(1+log t)^2. Stieltjes summation
against the decreasing Gaussian gives, uniformly for Z<=y<=2Z,

    sum_{n>B}d_3(n)g_tau(log(n/y))
      <= y integral_H^infinity
             e^v(1+log y+v)^2 |g_tau'(v)|dv
      = Z^(1-kappa^2/(2tau)+o(1))
      = Z^(-A_0+o(1)).                                  (C7)

The identity e^v exp(-v^2/(2tau))
=exp(tau/2)exp(-(v-tau)^2/(2tau)) proves the exponent, with
the remaining factors contributing O(sqrt(L)+log L) to its
logarithm. The real cap and strict n>B condition are preserved.

These two bounds independently reproduce GC18. Once that complete-
restoration estimate has been used, removing n=de*ell>B costs (C7)
again. For retained rectangular pairs de>=Z exp(-2H), so the exact
remaining restoration bound is

    ell<=B/(Z exp(-2H))=2 exp(3H).                       (C8)

## 8. Fixed components and completion of the original row integral

Fixed column ray refinements give finitely many twists of the angular
sums and the two core characters. The angular-sum characters retain
nonzero infinity type and fixed conductor. The two core characters
in (BC13) remain finite order, with the moving conductor and natural
zeros described in (BC12). Arbitrary angular core twists are not
included in this assertion.

Fixed-place row factors on `Re z=a>0` have finite Fourier expansions
in the finitely many values `eta(p)`, `p in S`. The coefficients are
bounded on that line; valuation progressions keep their actual
geometric denominators. After the functional equation, these
expansions add fixed twists to (BC12). Thus merely bounding a local
factor before the core cancellation is not required.

If a required component includes a fixed finite-order row twist, CRT
changes the root number by fixed-modulus phases in `c,e`. Expand that
finite ray function into products of fixed core characters. Its good
Gauss factors are those already canceled in (BC8). The primitive
moving conductor remains `ce`, and the dual core-twist conductor is
bounded by a fixed multiple of `rad(mathfrak n)`. The same masked
Möbius argument applies. No moving deletion is absorbed into `S`.

The exponent `2b/3+1/6` in (BC6) is positive, so summing all
opposite-core dyads, including the unbounded upper tail, costs
`D^(2b/3+1/6+epsilon)`. For the union sector use the disjoint rectangles
`{q_c<=C}` and `{q_c>C, q_e<=C}`. Each restriction is a one-variable
endpoint, so (BC13) and partial summation apply. In each rectangle,
sort the two dyadic scales by swapping the columns in the estimate;
do not introduce a nonseparable condition `q_c<=q_e`. The smaller
dyadic scale is `O(C)`, including boundary dyads. Summing its positive
power up to `O(C)` proves (BC1).

Choose the fixed positive `a` sufficiently small that `K^a`, the dual
truncation loss, and all preliminary norm powers fit the final loss.
This is possible for every fixed polynomial bound `K<=D^B`. The
rapid vertical decay of `R_tilde` on that fixed positive line absorbs
the polynomial heights. No original Mellin root has been shifted or
discarded: the auxiliary angular shifts are residue-free, and the row
shift stays strictly positive with nonprincipal row L-functions.

statement: ## 3. Development A / W49-02: the exact renewal defect and its sharp cost ### A1. Original signed recurrence For t>=1 and y>=1, define R_chi(t,y)=sum_(n<=t, P^-(n)>y) mu(n)chi(n), with P^-(1)=infinity. Partition every squarefree n>1 by its least prime p; its remaining factor has all primes strictly greater than p. This proves the finite identity R_chi(t,y)=1-sum_(y=1. Suppose the approximation is exact on the descendant-closed collar t<=y^r. (A4) Every child of a collar state remains in the collar, so Delta=0 there. Conversely zero defect there and the terminal values determine exactness by finite induction. For r>1, exact collar values include all relevant shorter prime products; they are not all equal to1. Define N_(r,q)(x)=#{d<=x: mu(d)!=0, (d,q)=1, d P^+(d)^r < x}. (A5) The d=1 convention is as above. The strict inequality follows from the inclusive exact collar; changing it would alter equality states. For arbitrary independently bounded complex defects on the remaining REAL-SCALE states (x/d,P^+(d)), the exact norm of the map Delta -> E(x,1), from state sup norm to scalar absolute value, is N_(r,q)(x). The upper bound is A3 and the triangle inequality. For equality set Delta(x/d,P^+(d))=conjugate(mu(d)chi(d)) on every counted state and zero elsewhere. Each coefficient then contributes1. Because real-scale states are distinct, this assignment is consistent; the triangular recurrence realizes it by some F. It may depend on the chosen x. This is an operator/error-budget obstruction, **not** a construction of the actual error of a specific arithmetic approximation and **not** a lower bound for M_chi. It does not impose the natural further invariant F(t,y)=F(floor(t),y). Integer-state coalescence changes the norm and is treated in A5. The collar is a useful exactness assumption: without it, even terminal errors could trivially inject almost x coefficients. The following obstruction persists after those terminal values and any fixed-depth collar are exact. ### A3. Sharp power at each path depth For fixed positive integer k and fixed r>=1, let N_(k,r,q)(x) count the integers in A5 with omega(d)=k. Then C_(k,r,q) x^(k/(k+r))/(log x)^k <= N_(k,r,q)(x) <= x^(k/(k+r)) (A6) for all sufficiently large x, with a positive constant C. Thus its exact power exponent is k/(k+r). Upper bound: every prime factor of d is <=P^+(d), so P^+(d)>=d^(1/k). The condition d P^+(d)^rinfinity) log N_(r,q)(x)/log x =1. (A7) For any proposed gamma<1, choose k with k/(k+r)>gamma. Uniform O(1) local defect enclosures, even with exact A4, therefore do not imply an O(x^gamma) output error by this UNMERGED unsigned certificate. The statement allows every fixed r; it says nothing about a suitably growing r with its own exact-collar cost, or about structured correlated defects. In particular it does not rule out the exact signed integer-state compression below. At r=1, bounded defects through depth K contribute at most (K+1) max|Delta| x^(K/(K+1)) (A8) for fixed K>=1 and x>1, including d=1. The first integer depths outside several targets are: | Desired gamma | Bounded-defect depths paid by A8 | First deeper exponent above gamma | |---|---|---| | .87486, giving conditional c=.12514 | k<=6, exponent6/7 | k=7, exponent7/8=.875 | | 5/6, giving conditional c=1/6 | k<=5 | k=6, exponent6/7 | | 3/4, giving conditional c=1/4 | k<=3 | k=4, exponent4/5 | At the current boundary b6, 7/8-b6=.000139; at gamma=.87486 the difference is .00014. This numerical proximity is a feature of THIS worst-case defect calculus, not an explanation of the incumbent proof or a universal 1/8 barrier. Arbitrarily deep paths still require payment and approach exponent1. ### A4. A real attempt at a coarse approximate state, and what fails The tempting initial approximation F0(t,y)=1 on t<=y and0 on t>y has exactly correct terminal values. At each nonterminal state its defect is Delta0(t,y)=-1+sum_(y=t)chi(p). (A9) The equality p^2=t is included: the child t/p=p is terminal. For the principal q=1 character and y=1 this defect is asymptotic to t/log t by ordinary PNT. Thus simply setting the putatively cancelling bulk to zero produces a large, actual prime-count defect. It does not satisfy the O(1) premise of A8. Keeping more exact terminal layers produces explicit signed prime-product boundary terms; no estimate of their complete accumulated defect below the target was found. A usable constructive criterion now has a precise form. For each x and character, exhibit an explicit F with |F(x,1)|<=7 complement** remains. This is not an estimate of an original Mertens submask. The next mathematical action is to construct a prime-pair or convolution-compatible F whose residual has a proved signed cancellation relation; independent local error bars cannot replace that relation. No such F and A10 theorem are supplied here. The exact norm/depth result is narrower and more quantitative than G81's 2^r arbitrary-history linear-state obstruction: it concerns approximate recursive evaluation on the stated real-scale path states, with the terminal collar already exact. Its novelty is only relative to the inspected record; the recurrence and finite inverse are standard. ### A5. The strongest objection produces an exact signed compression The actual rough sum depends on t only through floor(t), and floor(t/p)=floor(floor(t)/p). A natural approximation can preserve that invariant. Fix an integer root N and write F(t,y)=f(floor(t),y). Its Delta also has that form. Group A3 by m=floor(N/d) and p=P^+(d), keeping every sign. For d>1 the COMPLETE coefficient of Delta(m,p) is C_(N,chi)(m,p) =-chi(p) sum_(N/[p(m+1)]=1 here), only m>p^r survives. Its exact independent INTEGER-state sup-norm cost is B_(r,chi)(N)=1+sum_(p,m>p^r)|C_(N,chi)(m,p)|, N>1. (A13) This follows by assigning each nonzero merged coefficient its conjugate phase; finite triangular back substitution again realizes the chosen defects. A13 is not generally equal to the real-state count A5. Its upper bound by the corresponding unmerged count is valid; the exponent1 lower argument cannot be transferred through the signed fibre sums. A bound for A13 would require actual smooth-Mobius interval cancellation, and no new exponent for it is proved here. There is real, source-exact cancellation in this compression. For the principal q=1 character, take N=20196, p=17 and m=18. The interval in A11 is 20196/(17*19)

# [private research revision]: parameter and square-row interfaces

10 October 2026. Derived by `c20_cubic`; **independently reviewed by `c21_all_branch_h` within the stated scopes.** This file records three bounded deductions from the
current canonical inputs. It does not change the accepted
`c0 = 0.125113352960035869...`, assert a new paid physical sector, or give a
lower bound for an actual arithmetic sum.

## Sources and input scope

Write M for `zeta_zero_free_validated_merged.md` in the repository root.
The exact inputs are M (B0.37)--(B0.44), including the actual fixed
finite-ray coefficient family, natural zero extensions, disjoint physical
prime slots, strict moment reserves, and common-profile height seminorms;
(B0.45)--(B0.49), the accepted geometry; (B0.46)/(B0.55), the averaged
physical numerator; (B0.27) and (S.5), the direct/reflected majorants.
M (B3.40) admits kappa in compact subsets of `(1/2,1]`, subject to its
zero-free input `beta_* <= (1+kappa)/2`. No arbitrary moving-conductor
fourth moment is an input.

The comparison sources, treated as evidence rather than authority, are:

- Shunia, pinned commit `c3abed0cae8fdb0090c12b0e4d20aea68b6e067d`,
  [compensated_half_plane_refinement.tex](https://github.com/jshunia/rhtm/blob/c3abed0cae8fdb0090c12b0e4d20aea68b6e067d/compensated_half_plane_refinement.tex),
  selected-row bound and exact capacities. Its stated plain-moment range
  is `[13/18,1]`; the sharper supply calculation below uses `[13/18,3/4]`.
- Liu, [arXiv 2610.12234v1](https://arxiv.org/html/2610.12234v1), Sections
  9 and 22, Proposition 25.1. The useful transfer is the positive affine
  certificate method. The high constraint below is QRH's averaged-numerator
  constraint, not Liu's pointwise-numerator constraint.
- [BC](../[private research revision]/cubic-mobius-core-moment.md), especially
  BC5, BC7--BC13 and BC18: actual core moment, ordinary row FE, root-number
  cancellation, moving finite twists, and remaining double-large cores.
- [DQ](cubic-dual-classes.md), DQ1--DQ3 and DQ10--DQ12: exact dual cube
  decomposition, natural zeros, and the proposed weighted cubic-sieve
  comparison. DQ remains separately awaiting review; the algebraic
  square-row obstruction below does not assume acceptance of DQ's polar
  or sieve estimates.

All `epsilon` losses are chosen with fixed positive reserves. Constants
may depend on the fixed target, fixed excluded set, fixed profiles, and
fixed compact parameter ranges. Heights cost `T^A` for a fixed seminorm
order A; reducing a physical height exponent does not erase a moving
arithmetic conductor or change the norm of the row index.

## PS1. A smaller sufficient prime supply

Assume `13/18 <= kappa <= 3/4`, `0 <= delta <= kappa`, and the moment
hypothesis above. Put `q=delta p`, `0<=p<=1/2`, `c=1/(3kappa)`.
For a witness length `1<=t<=3/2`, the canonical count lines are

\[
A_I(r)=1-\delta\{p+(1-p)r\},\qquad
A_P(t-r)=1-\delta\{cp+2(1-cp)(t-r)\}.
\tag{PS1}
\]

Their crossing is

\[
r_*(t)=\frac{2(1-cp)t+cp-p}{3-p-2cp}.
\tag{PS2}
\]

The denominator is positive. The crossing increases with t; at t=1 it
decreases with p since its derivative has numerator `c-1<0`. Therefore

\[
r_*(t)\ge\frac{3-c}{5-2c}
=\frac{9\kappa-1}{15\kappa-2}\ge\frac{23}{37}.
\tag{PS3}
\]

The last function decreases with kappa, with derivative
`-3/(15kappa-2)^2`, and takes value `23/37` at `kappa=3/4`.
Also `1/3<=t-r_*(t)<=1/2`: the quantity increases with t, equals 1/2
at t=3/2, and at t=1 exceeds 1/3 by
`(1-c)p/[3(3-p-2cp)]`.

For the inverse witness `r>=r_*`, the requested capacity
`z=(1-r)/2-nu`, where positive, is at most `7/37-nu`, and

\[
1-r-2z=2\nu,\qquad
3-2r-8z=2r-1+8\nu\ge9/37+8\nu.
\tag{PS4}
\]

For the plain witness `r<=r_*`, its actual `m>=t-r` has capacity at most
`(1-2m)/(6kappa)<=1/(18kappa)<=1/13<7/37`. Small/nonpositive capacities
use the unmarked estimates with the same fixed small losses as B0.38--39.
Whole-slot selection loses at most one mesh interval; choose the mesh
after fixing the supply margin and before all final small-power losses.

Consequently **supply `L>7/37` by a fixed positive amount suffices for the
existing B0.40 row count** on this restricted kappa range. Its exponent is
unchanged:

\[
R_\kappa(\delta,p)=1-\delta+
\frac{\delta C_\kappa(p)(5/6-\delta)}
 {2(5/6-\delta+\delta C_\kappa(p))},\quad
C_\kappa(p)=\frac{2(1-p)(1-p/(3\kappa))}{3-p-2p/(3\kappa)}.
\tag{PS5}
\]

This is a limited strengthening of the convenient `L>4/21` supply
condition. The canonical geometry already has `ell0/h0>1/5`, so it
does not improve the accepted endpoint or the physical numerator bound.

## PS2. Fixed-input affine certificate for the current majorants

Let ell0 be the root in `(0.16712007850680,0.16712007850682)` of

`927 ell^4 - 3135 ell^3 + 2433 ell^2 + 275 ell - 100 = 0`.

Set

\[
b_0=11/12-\ell_0/4,\quad
\kappa_0=(5-3\ell_0)/6,\quad
\delta_0=\frac{25-60\ell_0+27\ell_0^2}
 {6(5+4\ell_0-3\ell_0^2)}.
\tag{PS6}
\]

The input kappa is fixed at kappa0 throughout this proposition. Consider
geometry `M=x+y`, `h=1+ell-x>0`, `x,y>ell>0`, `h<=2y`, for which the
original moment/profile hypotheses and capacities are admissible. Use
the original direct majorant, including the empty-subset branch and
the triangle summation of rescaled compensator subsets, and use the
unchanged B0.46 averaged-numerator majorant for every amplitude class.

The proposition concerns what these upper-bound formulas can certify.
It does not assert that the actual sums or row counts attain any of them.
In particular, a new coefficient-specific estimate for the later paid
or unpaid sectors could change the formulas and evade the proposition.

First, S.5 with `N=1+ell,z=ell` gives the three branches

\[
k(M,\ell)=\max\{0,(1+3\ell-2M)/4,M+\ell-1\}.
\tag{PS7}
\]

The hypotheses `x,y>ell` imply `ell<M/2`, as required in S.5. A fourth
branch `(3ell-1)/2`, appearing in Liu's broader packaging, is redundant
here: it is nonpositive for `ell<=1/3`; otherwise `M+ell-1>3ell-1`.
The Gram majorant contains `(y-x)/12`. With the original signal exponent
`C(B)=B-5/6+x/3+ell/6`, the empty-subset direct estimate therefore demands

\[
B\ge L_0:=5/6+M/12-\ell/6,\qquad
B\ge L_K:=1/3+7M/12+\ell/3.
\tag{PS8}
\]

These are necessary constraints for certification by that majorant,
not necessary conditions for the actual physical probe to be small.

At the fixed critical class `delta=delta0,p=1/2,q=delta0/2`, B0.48 gives

\[
R_{\kappa_0}(\delta_0,1/2)=5/9+\delta_0/(18\kappa_0).
\tag{PS9}
\]

Write `a=(1+delta0)/2`. B0.46 at d=h is

\[
F(h)=a-y/2-\ell/2+\ell q
 +h(1/12+3R/4)-\frac q{12\kappa_0}\min(h,2y-h).
\tag{PS10}
\]

Since `min(h,2y-h)<=2y-h`, set

\[
A=1/2+\delta_0/(12\kappa_0),\qquad
C=\delta_0/2+\delta_0/(12\kappa_0).
\]

Substitution of PS9 and `h-y=1+ell-M` yields

\[
F(h)\ge H_4:=1+C-AM+C\ell.
\tag{PS11}
\]

Equality holds for `h/2<=y<=h`. The regime `h<=2y` is retained because
the original positive-length numerator capacity is not asserted beyond
it. No extension to inadmissible reflected scales is made.

Let `W=1+4A+4C` and

\[
w_0=\frac{8A+14C}{3W},\quad
w_K=\frac{4A-2C}{3W},\quad w_H=\frac1W.
\tag{PS12}
\]

These weights are positive and sum to one. Direct algebra gives

\[
(w_0+7w_K)/12-Aw_H=0,\qquad
-w_0/6+w_K/3+Cw_H=0.
\tag{PS13}
\]

Thus `w0 L0+wK LK+wH H4` is independent of M and ell. Evaluate it at
`M=1-ell0,ell=ell0`. Then `L0=LK=b0`; the second identity in B0.48,

\[
\delta_0=\frac{\kappa_0(5-9\ell_0)}
 {6\kappa_0+(6\kappa_0+2)\ell_0},
\]

gives `H4=b0`. Consequently

\[
\boxed{\max\{L_0,L_K,H_4\}\ge
w_0L_0+w_KL_K+w_HH_4=b_0.}
\tag{PS14}
\]

This proves the claimed fixed-input barrier, including admissible
`M+ell>1`. It does not cover an improved arithmetic majorant, changed
observable, or a different kappa input/feedback theorem. In particular,
it is not a universal obstruction to increasing c0. Approximate weights
are `(0.6453188308,0.1251133530,0.2295678162)`; the proof uses PS12--14,
not numerical optimization.

## PS3. Cubic twists occupy square-indexed sextic rows

Fix the original finite ray component and finite excluded set S. Away
from S write `theta_c=chi_c^2` for the cubic and sextic characters, both
extended by zero at nonunits. For the actual dual core twist,

\[
\psi_n(c)=\theta_c(\lambda)\overline{\theta_c(n)}
=\nu(c)\overline{\chi_c(n^2)},\qquad
\nu(c)=\theta_c(\lambda).
\tag{PS15}
\]

The fixed lambda phase is handled only in its prescribed fixed finite
family. A dual row with `q_n~H` becomes a sextic index `u=n^2` with
`q_u~H^2`. If n is cube-free then u is sixth-power-free. The primitive
good conductor may be `rad(n)`; this does not change the indexing norm
in a moment summed over `q_u~U`. The same distinction is recorded in
[private research revision] T01's conventions and the BC natural-zero argument.

On the balanced bare outside-cube piece, freeze each permitted external
incidence/deletion mask R and profile before applying a positive moment.
Define the centrally normalized polynomial

\[
M_n=D^{-1/2}\!
\sum_{q_c\asymp D,\ (c,R)=1}
\mu(c)\nu(c)\overline{\chi_c(n^2)}W(c).
\tag{PS16}
\]

Here W includes only the original annular/common norm and fixed-ray
profiles, independent of n; row-natural zeros remain in the character.
For unequal columns and common-core projector divisor g the same
argument uses the residual lengths and masks in BC, not arbitrary
pair-dependent coefficients. For `n=d kappa^3`, the exact identity has
the additional mask `(c,kappa)=1`; no condition `(d,kappa)=1` is imposed.

Let `mathcal M_u` denote the same sum with `bar chi_c(u)` in place of
`bar chi_c(n^2)`, so `M_n=mathcal M_(n^2)`. The whole sextic-row UM/MI
estimate, when its length and mask hypotheses hold, permits the
positive enlargement

\[
\sum_{q_n\asymp H}^{\mathrm{cube\text{-}free}}|M_n|^2
\le O(1)\sum_{q_u\asymp H^2}^{(6)}|\mathcal M_u|^2
\ll T^A H^{2+\epsilon}.
\tag{PS17}
\]

The fixed O(1) is the generator multiplicity, absent for ideal indexing.
At `H=D^2/K`, `K<=D^.87653`, one has `D<H`, so the unmarked short-length
condition `D<=U^(1/2)` with `U=H^2` is not the difficulty. The lost factor
is row density: the requested family has O(H) indices inside a family
of O(H^2) indices. Positivity alone cannot recover that factor.

The physical balanced covariance has normalization `D^2/H` after PS16.
Thus this import gives only `T^A D^(2+epsilon) H`, not `D^(2+epsilon)`.
Even this statement concerns its CC piece; it supplies no identification
of a dual class with the original signed whole II subtraction.

A sufficient genuinely new interface for this primitive band would be

\[
\sum_{q_n\asymp H}^{\mathrm{cube\text{-}free}}|M_n|^2
\ll T^A H(DH)^\epsilon,
\tag{PS18}
\]

with all the actual masks above, the two columns' common-core projector,
the BC weighted outer sums, and a common polynomial height bound.
Equivalently one may seek the corresponding exact bilinear estimate
before positive enlargement. PS18 is **not proved here** and is not a
consequence of an unweighted plain fourth moment or pointwise I-HECKE.
The remaining double-large-core CC minus whole II remains open.

## Review boundary

PS1--5 are a capacity refinement using existing MI/MP; PS6--14 are an
exact algebraic obstruction for explicitly unchanged upper-bound
formulas; PS15--18 identify the exact index/conductor mismatch and the
missing square-row moment. None grants positive semidefiniteness to a
gcd-filtered covariance or replaces same-complex-z products by absolute
squares. The independent review accepted PS8's empty-subset scope, PS11's min inequality and capacity domain, and PS17's actual row index. PS17 also follows directly from M (S.2), with U=H^2, column length D<=sqrt(U), and coefficient energy O(1); the frozen row-independent R-mask is permitted there.

Reviewed source SHA-256: `ae28cc5ee9efc3aa2dc1b37f24fa91f790ccacff1d9d1efdb7827272f9939edf`. Review owner: `c21_all_branch_h`.

## Finite face, costs and equivalence

Fix delta=3/5, truncate product pc to
[X exp(-2sqrt(log X)),2X exp(2sqrt(log X))], and theta to |theta|<=X^(1/5).
Both product tails cost X^(-1+o(1)). The missing theta mass is at most
64/(pi h^3 T^3); its source cost is O_chi(X^(2/5)). In particular truncated
median leakage is paid, not declared zero. Let J_X be the literal finite
face field, P_X its phase-weighted integral and

    Q_X=integral_(|theta|<=X^(1/5)) K_h(theta)
                         integral_X^(2X)|J_X(theta,x)|^2 dx/x dtheta.

The coherent square of P_X has both theta variables and all ordered mixed
terms; Cauchy–Schwarz gives ||P_X||_2^2<=Q_X. More strongly, direct expansion
of V_z(1,p,c)^2 gives

    J_X(theta,x)=A(theta)M(x/p)+R_X(theta,x),
    A(theta)=a(p)p^(-2z)(1-p^(-z))^2,
    |R_X|<<_(chi,epsilon) X^(2/5+epsilon).

The four shifted terms, both removed atoms and both product tails are
included. |A| is bounded above and away from zero uniformly in theta.
For E_M(X)=integral_(X/p)^(2X/p)|M(y)|^2 dy/y and
b_X=integral_(|theta|<=X^(1/5))K_h|A|^2, the exact norm comparison is

    |sqrt(Q_X)-sqrt(b_X E_M(X))|<=r_X,
    0<c_chi<=b_X<=C_chi, r_X<<X^(2/5+epsilon).         (HC-I2)

Consequently, for each fixed gamma>2/5, all-scale Q_X<<X^(2gamma+epsilon)
is equivalent to the original Gaussian square-moment estimate at that
exponent. This is an exact arithmetic obstruction to treating twist
orthogonality alone as a saving. L1 readout and L1 Gaussian bounds have
their own equivalence; no equivalence between L1 and L2 is asserted.

The24 monomials with every exponent positive form a transform holomorphic
on Re(s)>2/5 and a field O(X^(2/5+epsilon)). Their unconditional comparison
with the full field costs X^(7/5+epsilon) for the two mixed terms. Under a
target norm X^gamma the cost is instead X^(gamma+2/5+epsilon), with error
square X^(4/5+epsilon). The unconditional bound pays the1/6 and1/4 target
comparisons; the half-strip comparison requires the hypothesized target
norm. Any detected pole lies in the12-term free sector, but an individual
fixed-theta cofactor can still vanish.

statement:
## 3. A complete divisor-bounded tail lemma

The accepted independent review Section7 proves a smooth positive
majorant for the ORIGINAL sharp shell [X,2X]. The following extension
keeps the divisor-bounded coefficients needed in (2.1). It is proved
here rather than silently applying its bounded-coefficient statement.

For fixed b>1,k>2 and |v_n|<=A_eta*n^eta, with 2eta<k-2, define

    B_M(x)=sum_(n>M)v_n f_x(n).

Then, for every real shell-fixed M>=2,

    ||B_M||_2^2 <<_(b,k,eta) A_eta^2
          [X^(b(1+2eta))+X^k M^(2-k+2eta)],              (3.1)

where every norm in this report uses dx/x on the FULL real shell.

Proof. Use the accepted C^2 function phi>=1 on [1,2], supported on
[1/2,4], and majorize the full |B_M|^2 before expansion. Two integrations
by parts give the weighted kernel bound

    |K_phi(n,m)| <<_(b,k) min(1,(X^k/|n^k-m^k|)^2).

The moving damping is differentiated: on the fixed transformed support
every A-polynomial times exp(-cA), A=(n+m)/X^b, is uniformly bounded.
For n>m, n^k-m^k>=n^(k-1)(n-m); also n^eta*m^eta<=n^(2eta).
With delta_n=X^k/n^(k-1), summing the complete lower row gives

    sum_(h>=1)min(1,(delta_n/h)^2)<<delta_n.

Thus BOTH off-diagonal orientations cost at most
O(A_eta^2 X^k sum_(n>M)n^(1-k+2eta)), which is the second term in (3.1).
The diagonal retains its exponential damping and costs
O(A_eta^2 sum n^(2eta) exp(-c n/X^b))=O(A_eta^2 X^(b(1+2eta))).
Absolute convergence first justifies finite-square expansion; the displayed
summable bounds justify the infinite limit. This proves the full tail
norm, including all interactions within that tail. In a subsequent
triangle inequality with the core, this complete norm pays its cross
effect; no individual signed cross is asserted positive.

## 3. The weighted free-row detector

Fix delta in [17/25,7/10]. Consider free rows of width W in an actual eligible parent translate, with a nonprincipal member of its fixed dictionary having a zero of real part at least (1+delta)/2 at height <=T. In addition require the physical-bin slot bound

    |Q_u|^2 << Z^[delta z+epsilon] H_J                 (5)

on these rows. The product must be the actual source prime slots with their original smooth/ray coefficients and holes, for which the existing buffered-bin prime estimate gives (5). A bounded bin padding in delta is absorbed in epsilon. The family is not enlarged to characters on which a slot becomes principal. For z<=W/20, the claimed weighted estimate is

    sum_these_free_rows |Q_u|^2
      << (1+T)^J Z^[rho(delta)W+gamma(delta)z+epsilon],
    gamma(delta)=delta(5/3+2delta)/(5-2delta),
    eta(delta)=delta-gamma(delta)
              =4delta(5/6-delta)/(5-2delta).             (6)

In particular eta(17/25)=782/6825 and eta(7/10)=14/135. This saves a fixed positive multiple of the actual slot width compared with applying unmarked density and (5) separately.

Proof. Normalize W=1 and write v=z/W<=1/20. Choose

    t=(5-4delta v)/(5-2delta),                          (7)

before selecting witnesses. It lies in [1,3/2]. Apply the existing supported-witness construction and partition by its finite label and two dyads. Up to arbitrarily small source tolerances it gives

    r+m>=t, r<=t, 0<=m<=1/2,
    |M_u(Z^r)|^2>=Z^(delta r),
    |P_u(Z^m)|^2>=Z^(delta m).                         (8)

The inverse and plain factors have the source's common real part/frequency and common profile. Their rowwise real part/frequency is paid by its usual polynomial Sobolev factor.

An important height/bin issue is explicit here. The density proof may build a new internal buffered bin whose zero maximum exceeds the original physical maximum or .85. Its actual witness lower exponent delta_b is at least the prescribed delta-O(e). Use the weaker inequalities (8), and keep the cutoff (7) fixed at the prescribed delta. Do not substitute delta_b into (5). Lemma 1W allows any cutoff chosen before witnesses; its saturation m<=1/2 follows using the actual delta_b and the incumbent 7/8 upper bound. Thus no unsupported upper zero bound at the larger internal height is required.

Divide (2) by the inverse witness, or divide the old unmarked inverse/plain moments by their witnesses and then apply (5). The weighted count exponent is bounded by the minimum of

    U(r)=max(1,(1+5r)/6)-delta r+delta v,
    A(r)=1/6+(5/6)max(1,r+2v,(2r+8v)/3)-delta r,
    P(r)=1-2delta(t-r)+delta v.                         (9)

Using m>=t-r is favorable in the third bound. The source bound max(1,2m) differs from one only by its prescribed small witness tolerance. All such tolerances, dyadic partitions and finite dictionary factors are charged before the final epsilon.

Here is the full r-range calculation. Supported r>=t-1/2>4/5, so r>=2v. Hence (2r+8v)/3<=r+2v. Set R=1-2v.

* For r<=R, A=1-delta r. It crosses P at r_b=(2t-v)/3. The better of them is at most S=1-(2/3)delta t+(1/3)delta v. The crossing is before R: 2t+5v<=3 is equivalent to (5-6delta)-(25-18delta)v>=0, bounded below on the full rectangle by 81/500.
* For R<=r<=1, A=1/6+(5/6-delta)r+5v/3 increases, whereas U=1-delta r+delta v decreases. Their crossing r_c=1-(2-6delta/5)v has value C=1-delta+delta(3-6delta/5)v. The quantity rho+gamma v-C, after multiplication by the positive 3(5-2delta)/delta, is

      (5-6delta)-(40-42delta+36delta^2/5)v.

  This is at least 1923/31250>0 on delta in [.68,.70], v<=.05. Thus this transition, which cannot be omitted, lies below the claimed envelope.
* For r>=1, use U. It increases since delta<=.70<5/6, and its maximum at r=t is L=1/6+(5/6-delta)t+delta v.

The chosen t makes S=L=rho+gamma v. This proves all detector lengths, including boundaries and v=0. The interval lower bounds just given are algebraic bounds on continuous rectangles; critical-point checks in check.py are supplementary.

Fix moment/seminorm degrees before the internal detector exponent tau_d, just as in PR15. If T is at most the internal power threshold, the buffered construction, height Sobolev bounds and finite dyadic partition fit the final power loss. If T exceeds it, ideal counting and the absolute bound |Q|^2<<Z^(z+epsilon) are absorbed by increasing the final polynomial degree J (take a degree at least 2/tau_d on these compact ratios). This yields a common threshold before T. The separate physical height exponent is chosen only after that returned J. Fixed conductor multipliers change constants; they are not growing powers.

## HC5. Twenty-four monomials and both ordered mixed terms are paid

Exactly 12 ordered permutation pairs in HC2.3 have a zero exponent: choose its coordinate in 3 ways and the other two entries of each permutation in 2 ways each. The remaining 24 have every exponent >=1. Let H_free denote the 12 terms with an untwisted factor and H_pos the other 24, retaining their ORIGINAL signs. Then H=H_free+H_pos.

For the latter Dirichlet coefficients,

    |b_pos,z(n)|<=24 d_3(n)n^(-delta).                         (HC5.1)

The generous ordered-factor count includes squareful outputs and repeated representations. It is an upper bound, not a coefficient identity. It gives absolute convergence of D_pos on Re s>1-delta. Also, for x>=1 and every epsilon>0,

    |H_pos(x)|<<_(delta,epsilon) x^(1-delta+epsilon),           (HC5.2)

uniformly in theta and chi. Indeed, write each Gaussian summand as n^(-1-epsilon)x^(1-delta+epsilon) times exp((1-delta+epsilon)v)g(v), v=log(n/x). This last factor has finite supremum, and sum d_3(n)n^(-1-epsilon)=zeta(1+epsilon)^3.

Fix delta=3/5. For ANY nonnegative theta weight w_X of mass at most 1, use dx/x on [X,2X]. HC2.5 and HC5.2 imply

    ||H||_(w_X,x)<<X,   ||H_free||_(w_X,x)<<X,
    ||H_pos||_(w_X,x)<<_epsilon X^(2/5+epsilon),
    | ||H||^2-||H_free||^2 |<<_epsilon X^(7/5+epsilon).          (HC5.3)

The exact energy difference is 2 Re <H_free,H_pos>+||H_pos||^2. Both ordered mixed terms are retained. Their coarse exponent is 1+2/5=7/5 and the square exponent is 4/5. No Mertens premise is used. This applies to K_h and its truncated windows; it also applies with the SAME tuple/product masks on every monomial, since the absolute bounds survive restrictions.

The exponent 7/5 is below the quarter-strip energy target 3/2 and sixth-strip target 5/3. It is NOT below the half-strip energy target 1. Conditional norm transfer for the latter is possible: a retained norm O(X^(1/2+epsilon)) instead gives mixed exponent 9/10+epsilon.

D_pos is holomorphic on Re s>2/5 by HC5.1. All zero-detecting poles of D in the quarter-strip region therefore reside in D_free. Its exact free-factor formula is

    D_free(s,z)=sum_(m<n) a(m)a(n)(mn)^(-s-2z)(m^(-z)-n^(-z))^2
                              [F(s)-a(m)m^(-s)-a(n)n^(-s)].    (HC5.4)

Fix the zero-exponent label and square the two by two Vandermonde of the other labels. The free label ranges over every integer except m,n, yielding both displayed collision corrections. Each unordered triple has three possible free labels, each with four monomials, reproducing all 12 terms. HC5.4 is first justified on Re s>1; further analyticity is asserted only where established.

Deleting all 12 free-factor terms leaves a function already holomorphic in the target half-plane. It removes the determinant pole detector along with the difficult arithmetic. HC5 is a paid signed-source remainder, not payment for HC3.2.
