## G6 — p<.01, sieve/information construction from obstruction

### W40-26 — Sieve syndrome with exact erasure completion; p=.009
O: Label each integer/prime configuration by its divisibility syndrome at selected small primes; use an error-correcting partition to retain separated syndromes and reconstruct omitted cells exactly.
B: An exact syndrome expansion with a small weighted erasure return might extend a restricted coprime-sector saving to the complete form.
T: Two-prime inclusion-exclusion table with signed coefficients and all repeated/gcd cases; derive the missing-cell price.
X: The erased syndrome may concentrate all difficult mass, and cardinality sparsity is not weighted norm sparsity.
R: Explicit full complementary return target, potentially useful for local exceptional sectors.

### W40-27 — Overlap cancellation as a Möbius code; p=.007
O: Treat overlapping sieve restrictions as parity-check equations on a Boolean lattice; Möbius inversion yields a signed reconstruction with coefficients chosen to cancel dominant overlap defects.
B: A short exact reconstruction could keep a useful restricted estimate while controlling its complement by lower-complexity overlaps.
T: Derive the three-restriction reconstruction and minimize the l1 reconstruction norm subject to exactness on every cell.
X: Exactness on the all-bad cell can force unit or larger complement weight, so no unconditional gain follows.
R: Exact identity and an optimization obstruction; possible gain only with a separately proved all-bad bound.

### W40-28 — Parity-homology cancellation of collision patterns; p=.004
O: Build a chain complex of repeated-prime collision patterns, with signed boundary maps encoding merging/splitting of indices.
B: Exact cancellation of boundary pairs could leave only a small homology sector, replacing a divisor-pattern count by a topological obstruction count.
T: Three-index collision lattice: write the boundary signs and test d squared equals zero against actual multiplicities.
X: Actual arithmetic coefficients need not respect the chosen incidence signs, so abstract homology may be unrelated.
R: Hard upstream route to connected-pattern cancellation; precise coefficient compatibility is the first gate.

### W40-29 — Phase list-decoding inequality; p=.006
O: Regard near-aligned arithmetic phases as codewords; list-decoding bounds would limit how many prime configurations can coherently reinforce any target phase.
B: A weighted cap on coherent lists at every phase and scale could directly power-save the complete ordered H sum.
T: Derive the exact relationship between a phase-arc concentration bound and the magnitude of the complex sum, including clustered antipodes.
X: A fixed arc occupancy bound below one is only a constant saving; a power saving needs scale-dependent discrepancy or cancellation.
R: New quantitative arithmetic target or proof that a coding analogy cannot deliver the missing exponent.

### W40-30 — CRT orthogonal-array detector; p=.008
O: Choose a family of local residue weights forming an orthogonal array, then combine them by CRT into a signed detector whose low-order collision projections vanish exactly.
B: Vanishing low-order correlations could lower the required full moment while a separately controlled high-order tail retains the zero signal.
T: Construct the smallest two-prime array and test its average against a fixed multiplicative character and its shifted copies.
X: Orthogonality may kill the fixed-character signal or require moduli growing too quickly for the transfer.
R: High ceiling replacement detector, with an explicit signal-versus-cancellation tradeoff.

End of initial seeds. No first-test outcomes have been computed or used in these cards.

# [private research revision]: independent review of the literal f3 late flow



## Disposition and current worklog

**Accept the frozen author's fixed-power theorem C3--C5, its terminal
band, and its complete return interface under the expressly stated
buffered Mertens input. Accept the controller's separate critical-window
theorems CT1, CT2 and CT8 with their stated fixed-parameter scopes.**
I reconstructed both arguments from the actual coefficient, rather than
assuming the source identifications or the asserted cancellations. No
material sign, constant, source, or uniformity error was found.

The fixed-power complement is negative of order X/(log X)^3 for every
fixed compact subinterval of 1/3<rho<1/2. Its increasing-threshold bands
inside that interval are positive. At z=kappa sqrt(X), sufficiently
large FIXED kappa instead gives a positive complement and a positive
band to any fixed-power threshold above sqrt(X), of order X/(log X)^2.
The two asymptotics have different scopes. Neither is uniform through
their intervening moving-parameter transition.

The controller candidate's compressed continuous-tail assertion in CT5
is valid; Section 2.3 below supplies an explicit positive-integral bound
after summing all cores. Its second Stieltjes replacement is also valid:
one applies the one-variable estimate inside the existing positive
integral. No missing product error or signed cancellation is needed.

Completed: source and valuation reconstruction; all omitted-source,
Gaussian, core, prime-power and prime-counting tails; the fixed-power
double zero and signed Abel remainder; constants and band signs; full
scalar, true diagonal, both heights, and remaining mismatch conditions.
Remaining mathematical work is the stronger full-field power estimate,
not a repair to either reviewed theorem. Root retains integration,
canonical files, tracker and Git. No such shared state was written here.

During final handoff the controller advanced the accepted WRITTEN
endpoint in current-proof to c2=15641/125000=.125128, with boundary
.874872, relative to the pinned PR9/Gao inputs. Its new complete
formalization/kernel replay remains separate. At review start the
record held c1=391/3125=.12512 and boundary .87488; those values remain
historical provenance in the frozen author report. This f3 review
supplies no new c and does not independently certify the separate
endpoint argument or formalization.

## 0. Exact source, accepted inputs, and common Gaussian bounds

Throughout tau>0 is fixed, and

    g(u)=(2 pi tau)^(-1/2) exp(-u^2/(2 tau)),
    f(n)=mu(rad(n/3^v_3(n))),
    F(x)=sum_n f(n) g(log(n/x)).

Every positive power of a prime other than 3 contributes exactly one
minus sign; powers of 3 contribute +1. Thus |f(n)|=1, f is
multiplicative, and f is not completely multiplicative. Let omega_z
count DISTINCT prime divisors greater than z, retaining all valuations,
and define the original fields

    T_z(x)=sum_(omega_z(n)<=1) f(n)g(log(n/x)),
    R_z(x)=sum_(omega_z(n)>=2) f(n)g(log(n/x)).

Then F=T_z+R_z exactly, on the uncapped positive integers. All shell
norms and inner products below use dx/x on the CLOSED shell X<=x<=2X.
No endpoint convention for integration changes the pointwise uniformity.

The fixed-order PNT input is, for each chosen fixed N,

    pi(v)=li(v)+O_N(v/(log v)^N),  v>=2.

N is selected before X tends to infinity. Neither argument needs an
order depending on X. The fixed-power theorem additionally uses the
accepted buffered assertion M(u)=sum_(n<=u)mu(n)=O_beta(u^beta),
where 1/2<beta<1 is fixed. In the current application beta is a fixed
number ABOVE .874872; beta=.8749 is still a permissible concrete choice
already supported by the earlier accepted input used in this review.
There is no assertion at the unbuffered boundary, nor uniformity as
beta approaches that boundary. The critical-window theorem needs no
Mertens or complete-field estimate at all.

The elementary Gaussian lattice bound is

    sum_(n>=1) g(log(n/y)) <= C_tau y,  y>0.             (R0.1)

For example, comparison with the integral plus the maximum of the
unimodal function of n proves it for y>=1; the same comparison and
g(log(1/y))=O_tau(y) prove it for y<1. The maximum issue when the peak
lies below 1 is thus paid. Completing the square gives the identical
bound after a fixed exponential weight in log(n/y).

If |log(n/x)|>=W, split half the Gaussian decay off as
exp(-W^2/(4 tau)), leaving a Gaussian of variance 2 tau. Consequently,
for fixed epsilon>=0,

    sum_(|log(n/x)|>=W) n^epsilon g(log(n/x))
      <= C_(tau,epsilon) x^(1+epsilon) exp(-W^2/(4 tau)). (R0.2)

For W=c log X-O(1), c>0 fixed, this is O_A(X^-A) for every fixed A,
uniformly on the full shell. Any fixed divisor multiplicity is covered
by d_k(n)<=C_(k,epsilon)n^epsilon. These are bounds for the complete
tails, not declarations that a numerical truncation equals the field.

## 1. Fixed-power complement: independent proof and signs

Fix 1/3<rho_0<=rho<=rho_1<1/2 and set

    L=log X,  z=X^rho,
    delta=(1-2 rho_1)/4,  eta=delta(1-beta)>0,
    C_f=9 log 2 * product_(p>=5)(1-1/(p-1)^2),
    B(rho)=2 log((1-rho)/rho)-2/(1-rho)-1/(1-rho)^2.

The reviewed statement is

    R_(X^rho)(x)=C_f exp(tau/2) B(rho) x/L^3
                  +O(X/L^4+X^(1-eta)L),                (R1.1)

uniformly for rho in this fixed compact interval and X<=x<=2X.
Constants can depend on tau,beta,rho_0,rho_1. In particular they are
not uniform as either compact endpoint reaches 1/3 or 1/2.

### 1.1 The actual f core, not an inherited Gaussian-mask estimate

For Re s>1 the literal Euler factors give

    D(s)=sum_n f(n)n^(-s)=H(s)/zeta(s),
    H(s)=(1-3^(-s))^(-2)
          product_(p!=3) (1-2p^(-s))/(1-p^(-s))^2.

At p!=3, the H factor is

    1-sum_(j>=2)(j-1)p^(-js),

and at p=3 its coefficients are j+1. Thus H has an absolutely
convergent Dirichlet series h for Re s>1/2, including absolute
convergence of sum |h(r)|r^(-beta). The coefficient identity is
f=h*mu. Directly using the accepted Mertens input therefore proves

    A_f(u)=sum_(n<=u)f(n)=O_beta(u^beta).               (R1.2)

This step uses no bound for F and no inversion of the vanishing
prime-two factor. It is the r=1 instance of the accepted actual f_r
convolution in [private research revision] Gaussian S1--S7.

H has a simple zero at 1 from p=2. Its p=2 derivative is 4 log 2;
the p=3 factor is 9/4; the remaining factors multiply to the positive
product in C_f/(9 log 2). Hence

    H'(1)=C_f,  D(s)=C_f(s-1)^2+O((s-1)^3).

The second zero is the zero of 1/zeta(s), not another finite-prime
factor. By (R1.2), the ordinary-order reciprocal sums and their first
two logarithmic derivatives converge at 1, giving

    sum_r f(r)/r=0,
    sum_r f(r)log r/r=0,
    sum_r f(r)(log r)^2/r=2C_f.                        (R1.3)

These sums are generally CONDITIONAL. For j=0,1,2 their tails after R
are O_beta(R^(beta-1)(1+log R)^j), by Abel summation. Taking absolute
values of these reciprocal moments would destroy the proof.

### 1.2 Exact two-prime source and all source-completion errors

Let nu=(3rho_0-1)/2>0 and U=X^(1+nu). Then U<z^3 for all rho in the
chosen interval and large X. If n<=U has at least two distinct primes
above z, it has exactly two, say p<q; each occurs to the first power.
Its unique factorization n=rpq has r<z, so (r,pq)=1 and f(n)=f(r).
Conversely every such factorization below U has the original source
coefficient. It follows that the two-prime completion is EXACT below U:

    f(n)1_(omega_z(n)>=2)
      =sum_(z<p<q, pq|n) f(n/(pq)),   n<=U.            (R1.4)

Above U the identity can fail, and we do not use it there. The number
of representations is at most d_3(n), so (R0.2) pays the whole
discrepancy. Thus

    R_z(x)=sum_(z<p<q) sum_(r>=1) f(r)g(log(rpq/x))
                  +O_A(X^-A).                        (R1.5)

This pays every term with three rough primes and every repeated rough
prime power. It preserves every valuation in the original source.
The frozen author's outside-range witnesses are correct: at z=5,
n=7^2*11 gives original +1 versus completion -1, and n=7*11*13 gives
original -1 versus completion -3. The equality is not global.

### 1.3 Signed large-core tail, including its lower boundary

Put R=floor(X^delta). For any y>0, integration by parts using (R1.2)
gives

    |sum_(r>R) f(r)g(log(r/y))|
      <= C_beta y^beta Q_beta(log(R/y)),
    Q_beta(v)=exp(beta v)g(v)
                 +integral_v^infinity exp(beta w)|g'(w)|dw. (R1.6)

The first term pays the actual boundary -A_f(R)g(log(R/y)). Q_beta
is bounded for v<=0 and decays faster than every exp(-Bv) for v>=0.
For Y>=1, splitting integers k at Y and then into dyadic intervals,
using sum_(k<=V)d(k)<=C V log(2V), yields

    sum_k d(k)k^(-beta)Q_beta(log(k/Y))
       <= C_beta Y^(1-beta)log(2Y).                   (R1.7)

Apply this with y=x/(pq), k=pq and Y=x/R. Summing (R1.6) over every
actual p<q, and only then majorizing by d(k), bounds the entire removed
core by

    C x R^(beta-1)log(2x/R)=O(X^(1-eta)L).            (R1.8)

This is cancellation of the actual unrestricted f(r) core furnished by
(R1.4)--(R1.5). It is not a bound for an arbitrary smooth or masked core.

### 1.4 Unordered primes, both Stieltjes replacements, and density

After r<=R, replace p<q by half the ordered sum and subtract half
the p=q sum. Even with all cores, its absolute value is bounded using
(R0.1) by

    sum_(p>z)sum_r g(log(rp^2/x))
       <= C_tau x sum_(p>z)p^(-2)<=C_tau X/z.          (R1.9)

Thus no square-prime coefficient is misidentified as a two-distinct-
prime coefficient.

For y=x/r, fixed p>z, and a chosen fixed N, Stieltjes integration by
parts with the PNT error gives

    |sum_(q>z)g(log(pq/y))
       -integral_z^infinity g(log(pv/y))dv/log v|
      <= C_(tau,N) (y/p)L^(-N) H_1(log(pz/y)),
    H_1(a)=exp(a)g(a)+integral_a^infinity exp(w)|g'(w)|dw. (R1.10)

This includes the endpoint -[pi(z)-li(z)]g(log(pz/y)); it has the
correct convention even if z itself is prime. The endpoint at infinity
vanishes. Log v>=rho_0 L throughout; no upper cap is being smuggled in.

H_1 is bounded on the negative half-line and rapidly decreasing on the
positive half-line. The integer harmonic majorant therefore gives

    sum_(p>z)p^(-1)H_1(log(pz/y))
       <= C[1+log_+(y/z^2)]<=C L.

The first prime replacement costs O_N(y L^(1-N)). For the second,
exchange the positive q-integral and the p-sum and apply the same
one-variable error estimate inside that integral. The remaining
integral is

    integral_z^infinity H_1(log(vz/y))dv/(v log v),

which is also O(L), and in fact the factor 1/log v gives a stronger
bound here. This proves the same stated error for the second
replacement. There is no omitted error-product term: these are two
sequential exact replacements with their respective errors bounded.
Summing absolute errors over r<=R introduces only sum 1/r=O(L).
N=8 consequently pays both by O(X/L^6).

Write t=log z=rho L and define the NONNEGATIVE density

    phi_t(A)=A^(-1)log((A-t)/t),  A>2t,
    phi_t(A)=0,                  A<=2t.

The exact unordered continuous density follows from

    (1/2)integral_t^(A-t) ds/[s(A-s)]
       =A^(-1)log((A-t)/t).

With w=log(pq/y), the Jacobian is y exp(w). Combining all preceding
errors, the actual source is

    R_z(x)=x integral_R exp(w)g(w)
        sum_(r<=R) f(r)/r phi_t(log x+w-log r)dw
       +O(X^(1-eta)L+X/z+X/L^6)+O_A(X^-A).            (R1.11)

This establishes the constant 1 in front of phi_t; a second factor 2
must not be inserted after the unordered density calculation.

### 1.5 The decisive signed Taylor remainder

Take W=delta L. For |w|<=W and r<=R,

    log x+w-log r >= (1-2delta)L >2rho_1 L.

The distance from the density edge is at least 2delta L. On this
range phi_t^(j)=O(L^(-1-j)) for j<=3, uniformly in the stated compact
rho interval. Globally phi_t=O(1/t); together with sum_(r<=R)1/r=O(L)
this pays the discarded |w|>W portion of (R1.11) by (R0.2).

Put A=log x+w and v=log r. Taylor's theorem gives

    phi_t(A-v)=phi_t(A)-v phi_t'(A)+(v^2/2)phi_t''(A)+e_A(v),
    |e_A(v)|<=C v^3/L^4,  |e_A'(v)|<=C v^2/L^4.

The valid summation of the last term is SIGNED Abel summation:

    sum_(r<=R)f(r)e_A(log r)/r
      =A_f(R)e_A(log R)/R
       -integral_1^R A_f(u)[e_A'(log u)-e_A(log u)]du/u^2.

By (R1.2), its absolute value is O_beta(L^-4): the integral of
exp(-(1-beta)v)(v^2+v^3) over v>=0 is finite, and the boundary has
the same bound. An unsigned harmonic summation of v^3/L^4 would
not give this result.

Complete only the three signed polynomial moments using (R1.3) and
their stated tails. The outcome, uniformly on the retained w range, is

    sum_(r<=R) f(r)/r phi_t(A-log r)
       =C_f phi_t''(A)+O(L^-4+R^(beta-1)/L).           (R1.12)

The Gaussian integration then replaces phi_t''(log x+w) by phi_t''(L)
with O(L^-4), because log(x/X) is bounded and the third derivative
has the stated bound. This replacement is done on |w|<=W; it does
not extend a derivative formula through the nonsmooth density edge.
Only the constant value is subsequently integrated over the full
Gaussian, with an already paid tail. The integral of exp(w)g(w) is
exp(tau/2).

Direct differentiation gives

    phi_t''(A)=2log((A-t)/t)/A^3
                 -2/[A^2(A-t)]-1/[A(A-t)^2],
    phi_(rho L)''(L)=B(rho)/L^3.

This proves (R1.1). The extra X/z error is absorbed there since
eta<rho_0. The core-moment tail X R^(beta-1)/L is smaller than the
earlier signed large-core error. Every log and power error is accounted
for before the asymptotic sign is read off.

### 1.6 Band signs, terminal tail, and scope

If u=(1-rho)/rho is in (1,2), then

    B(rho)=2log u-3-4/u-1/u^2<2log 2-21/4<0,
    B'(rho)=-2/(1-rho)-2/rho
                 -2/(1-rho)^2-2/(1-rho)^3<0.

Thus R_(X^rho) is eventually negative uniformly on any stated compact
rho interval. For fixed 1/3<a<b<1/2, exact coefficient subtraction
gives

    T_(X^b)-T_(X^a)=R_(X^a)-R_(X^b)
      =C_f exp(tau/2)[B(a)-B(b)]x/L^3
        +O(X/L^4+X^(1-eta)L)>0.                       (R1.13)

For a=3/8,b=2/5 the positive factor is exactly

    B(a)-B(b)=79/225+2log(10/9)=.5618321424267637... .

The decimal is only an evaluation of an already positive closed
formula. It is not evidence for an asymptotic. For every fixed c>1/2,
omega_(X^c)(n)>=2 implies n>X^(2c), so (R0.2) proves

    R_(X^c)(x)=O_A(X^-A).                              (R1.14)

It follows without a complete-field bound that the band from any
fixed a in (1/3,1/2) to any fixed c>1/2 is NEGATIVE of order X/L^3.
There is no finite terminal threshold for the uncapped Gaussian;
(R1.14) is a full-tail bound instead.

The previous [private research revision] subpower range stops at
log z<=L/(1000log L); its actual bands have the opposite sign in the
specified comparison. No interpolation between the two theorems has
been proved. Below rho=1/3 the third rough prime can enter the central
source. At rho=1/2 the growing complete reciprocal-core approximation
used in (R1.12) is no longer uniform. Neither boundary is included in
(R1.1).

## 2. Square-root threshold: independent proof of CT1, CT2 and CT8

Here kappa>=1 and tau>0 are FIXED, z=kappa sqrt(X), L=log X,
s=x/X in [1,2], and

    J(v)=integral_v^infinity exp(u)(u-v)g(u)du,
    Phi(q)=sum_(r>=1) f(r)/r J(log(rq)),  q>0.

The reviewed result is

    R_z(x)=2x/L^2 Phi(kappa^2 X/x)+O_(tau,kappa)(X/L^3). (R2.1)

No Mertens estimate, complete-field norm, or conditional reciprocal
moment is used in this section. All core bounds here are absolute.

### 2.1 Source and finite rectangle

Set d=1/100. The original terms with |log(n/x)|>=dL/2 have size
O_A(X^-A), including a fixed divisor multiplicity, by (R0.2). In the
retained range n<=2X^(1+d/2)<z^3 eventually. The proof of (R1.4)
therefore applies literally: exactly two distinct rough primes,
each to valuation one, n=rpq, p<q, and

    r<=2X^(d/2)/kappa^2<z,
    f(rpq)=f(r).

For sufficiently large X this r is <=X^d. Extending the prime sum
for these cores outside the retained range costs at most the same
d_3(n)-weighted Gaussian tail. Thus CT3 is correct. A core r>X^d
in the completed source would force
n>kappa^2 X^(1+d), which is also entirely in the paid upper tail.

Let B_X=X^(1/2+2d). Eventually B_X>z. If p>B_X or q>B_X, the other
rough prime is >z and n>kappa X^(1+2d). Consequently truncating both
primes to (z,B_X] costs another complete Gaussian/divisor tail. No
sharp central-product restriction need remain during the PNT step.

When replacing p<q by half the ordered rectangle, the actual p=q
diagonal must be subtracted. The candidate's O(X^(1/2+d/2)) estimate
for r<=X^d is valid. One can also use (R1.9) with all cores to get
the stronger bound O_tau(X/z)=O_(tau,kappa)(sqrt(X)). Either is
o(X/L^4). This is a paid artificial diagonal, not an identification
of its coefficients with the source.

### 2.2 Two PNT substitutions with all boundary terms

Fix N=10. For fixed r and q, put w(p)=g(log(rpq/x)). On the finite
rectangle log p is comparable to L and E(p)=pi(p)-li(p) obeys
|E(p)|<=C_N p/L^N. Exact Stieltjes integration by parts on (z,B_X]
therefore gives the error

    [E(p)w(p)]_z^(B_X)-integral_z^(B_X)E(p)w'(p)dp.

The two endpoint terms each have absolute size at most
C x/(rqL^N), since p g(log(rpq/x))=(x/(rq))exp(u)g(u).
The integral has the same bound because

    integral_z^(B_X) p|w'(p)|dp
       <=(x/(rq))integral_R exp(u)|g'(u)|du.

Hence CT4 holds with the sharp exclusion p>z, including prime z.
Summing its absolute errors over actual q in the rectangle and
r<=X^d uses just two harmonic bounds and costs O(X/L^(N-2)).

After this first replacement, exchange the existing p integral and
the q sum. Apply the same estimate to the q sum for each real p in
that integral. Its error is C x/(rpL^N). Integrating against dp/log p
is bounded by integrating dp, so the p integral of 1/p is O(L).
The core harmonic sum is O(L) again. This pays the second replacement
by O(X/L^(N-2)). In fact the retained log p denominator improves
that estimate, but is unnecessary. These two errors are bounded in
sequence; there is no assumption that pi errors multiply benignly.
Coefficient signs remain solely in the main term.

### 2.3 Explicit absolute extension to every core and prime integral

After the substitutions the main term is half of the ordered positive
prime-density integral, summed with f(r). For large X, log p,log q
are >1. To bound any omitted integral it therefore suffices to remove
those denominators and replace f by its absolute value 1.

There is a direct bound that does not appeal to a discrete divisor
count for continuous variables. With t=pq,

    integral_(p,q>=z) g(log(rpq/x))dpdq
       =integral_(z^2)^infinity log(t/z^2)g(log(rt/x))dt.

Write a=z^2/x=kappa^2/s in [kappa^2/2,kappa^2] and put u=log(rt/x).
Tonelli gives the exact positive full-core formula

    sum_r integral_(p,q>=z) g(log(rpq/x))dpdq
      =x integral_(log a)^infinity exp(u)g(u) W_a(u)du,
    W_a(u)=sum_(1<=r<=exp(u)/a) (u-log(ar))/r.          (R2.2)

Every summand of W_a is nonnegative. The harmonic bound and
0<=u-log(ar)<=u-log a show

    W_a(u)<=C_kappa(1+u_+)^2,  u>=log a.              (R2.3)

If r>X^d, then u>=dL+log a. If p>B_X or q>B_X while the other is
>=z, then u>=2dL+log(kappa/s), since r>=1. Thus every integral added
when extending cores and prime limits is bounded by the right side
of (R2.2) restricted to u>=dL-O_kappa(1). By (R2.3) its size is
O_A(X^-A) for any fixed A. This pays all continuous extension tails
uniformly on the closed x shell, including overlaps between removed
sets. No cancellation among cores is used.

Combining these bounds, the discrete source tails, both PNT errors,
and the diagonal gives the exact CT5 approximation

    R_z(x)=(1/2)sum_r f(r)
       integral_(p,q>z) g(log(rpq/x))dpdq/(log p log q)
                  +O_(tau,kappa)(X/L^4).              (R2.4)

The O(X/L^4) term comfortably includes the O(X/L^8) PNT errors and
the O(sqrt(X)) diagonal. It is valid before the density expansion.

### 2.4 Global density error, complete core, and exact coefficient 2

Set p=sqrt(X)v, q=sqrt(X)w with v,w>=kappa>=1. For a=L/2 and
b=log v,c=log w>=0, elementary subtraction gives

    |1/((a+b)(a+c))-1/a^2| <= (b+c)/a^3.

This is a GLOBAL inequality, not a Taylor series on a bounded prime
rectangle. It replaces the prime density by 4/L^2 with an error at
most 8(log v+log w)/L^3. The error is integrable over every core:

    sum_r integral_(v,w>=kappa)
       (1+log v+log w)g(log(rvw/s))dvdw < C_(tau,kappa). (R2.5)

For full details, set y=vw. The r-th integral in (R2.5) is

    integral_(kappa^2)^infinity
       (1+log y)log(y/kappa^2)g(log(ry/s))dy.

Now put v_r=log(rkappa^2/s) and log(y/kappa^2)=h>=0. This equals

    kappa^2 integral_0^infinity
       exp(h)(1+2log kappa+h)h g(h+v_r)dh.

For any fixed B>0, the bound g(u)<=C_(tau,B)exp(-(B+2)u), valid for
all real u by completing the square, bounds this by C r^(-B-2)
uniformly in s. Summing r proves (R2.5), including the finite small
cores. It also proves absolute and compact-q uniform convergence of
the series defining Phi. No conditional moment has been completed.

The leading integral without the logarithmic weight is exactly

    integral_(v,w>=kappa) g(log(rvw/s))dvdw
       =integral_(kappa^2)^infinity log(y/kappa^2)g(log(ry/s))dy
       =(s/r)J(log(rkappa^2/s)).                      (R2.6)

The factors in (R2.4) are therefore: unordered 1/2, Jacobian X,
prime density 4/L^2, and (s/r) from (R2.6). Their product is
2x/(rL^2), giving exactly (R2.1). The full density error is
O(X/L^3) by (R2.5). All constants are uniform in x, but no moving
kappa or varying tau uniformity has been proved or claimed.

### 2.5 Positivity and the complete band to a terminal threshold

Completing the Gaussian square gives, exactly,

    J(v)=exp(tau/2)integral_0^infinity h g(h+v-tau)dh>0.

For v>=3tau and a>=0, pointwise comparison of the positive integrand
proves

    J(v+a)/J(v)
       <=exp(-(v-tau)a/tau-a^2/(2tau))<=exp(-2a).     (R2.7)

Consequently, if q>=exp(3tau), the entire r>=2 contribution to Phi
has absolute size at most

    J(log q)sum_(r>=2)r^(-3)
       <=J(log q)[1/8+integral_2^infinity t^(-3)dt]
       =(1/4)J(log q).

Since f(1)=1,

    Phi(q)>=(3/4)J(log q)>0.                         (R2.8)

The condition kappa^2>=2exp(3tau) makes this true for every
q=kappa^2/s with 1<=s<=2. Its lower bound on this compact interval
is a fixed positive number. Thus R_z is eventually positive and
comparable to X/L^2 uniformly on the full shell. For other fixed
kappa>=1, (R2.1) still holds, but this review asserts no sign based
on (R2.8).

For any fixed rho_plus>1/2, (R1.14) applies and X^rho_plus>z
eventually. Exact coefficient subtraction gives

    T_(X^rho_plus)-T_(kappa sqrt(X))
      =R_(kappa sqrt(X))-R_(X^rho_plus)
      =2x/L^2 Phi(kappa^2 X/x)+O(X/L^3).              (R2.9)

Under the stated positivity condition this whole actual band is
eventually positive of order X/L^2. No full F estimate was used to
prove (R2.1), (R2.8), or (R2.9). A sign for a prefix T_z would be a
different conclusion, requiring control of F. Neither result says
that each individual prime-threshold jump has the same sign.

## 3. Complete Gram, scalar, heights, and the remaining power target

### 3.1 Fixed finite partition and exact original diagonal

Only now use (R1.2) with Gaussian Abel summation to deduce the accepted
pointwise F(x)=O_beta(x^beta), hence ||F||=O(X^beta). This direction
of dependence matters: F did not furnish (R1.2) or the signed core
moments. Let a=3/8,b=2/5,c=3/5 and partition the actual coefficient
family into

    C_0=T_(X^a),
    C_1=T_(X^b)-T_(X^a),
    C_2=T_(X^c)-T_(X^b),
    C_3=R_(X^c).

The supports of their coefficients c_i(n) are disjoint and exhaustive;
each coefficient is f(n) or 0. Their sum is exactly F. Define

    V_X(x)=C_f exp(tau/2)x/L^3,
    N_X^2=||V_X||^2=(3/2)C_f^2 exp(tau)X^2/L^6,
    v=(-B(a), B(a)-B(b), B(b), 0),  sum_i v_i=0.

For the eta of a compact interval containing a,b, the reviewed
asymptotics give, with

    epsilon_X=L^(-1)+X^(-eta)L^4+X^(beta-1)L^3,

the COMPLETE finite Gram approximation

    ||C_i-v_i V_X||<=C epsilon_X N_X,
    <C_i,C_j>=[v_i v_j+O(epsilon_X)]N_X^2,  all i,j.  (R3.1)

The first two leading coefficients are positive and the third is
negative. In particular the C_0,C_1 leading cross term is positive;
both have negative leading cross terms with C_2. Both ordered mixed
directions are retained. The leading matrix has a null sum direction,
but its logarithmic relative error is much larger than the desired
full-field power scale. It cannot by itself improve ||F||.

For the original current-proof G22 kernel,

    K_X(m,n)=integral_X^(2X)
           g(log(m/x))g(log(n/x))dx/x,

absolute convergence gives

    <C_i,C_j>=sum_(m,n)c_i(m)c_j(n)K_X(m,n).           (R3.2)

Indeed the absolute double series is bounded by integral (sum_n g)^2
=O(X^2), using (R0.1). The full true diagonal is

    Delta_all=sum_n K_X(n,n)=O_tau(X),

because g_tau(u)^2 is a constant times g_(tau/2)(u). Each piece's own
diagonal is bounded by Delta_all; every cross diagonal is exactly
zero because its supports are disjoint. Thus the COMPLETE original
off-diagonal scalar is exactly

    Q_off(X)=sum_(i,j)<C_i,C_j>-Delta_all.             (R3.3)

No diagonal in auxiliary r,p,q labels can replace this n=m diagonal.
No negative off-diagonal summand is deleted. The corresponding true
diagonal subtraction and exact Gram identity hold for any finite
threshold partition, including one with the critical threshold.

### 3.2 Both original heights, without a diagonal-height shortcut

For fixed sigma>1 and each coefficient family frozen at its chosen X,
put D_i(s)=sum_n c_i(n)n^(-s). Then |D_i(sigma+it)|<=zeta(sigma).
Using the convention <U,V>=integral conjugate(U)V dx/x, the exact
double-Mellin expression is

    <C_i,C_j>=(2pi)^(-2)integral_R integral_R
      exp(tau(sigma-it_1)^2/2) exp(tau(sigma+it_2)^2/2)
      conjugate(D_i(sigma+it_1))D_j(sigma+it_2)
      [integral_X^(2X)x^(2sigma+i(t_2-t_1))dx/x]dt_1dt_2. (R3.4)

The absolute Gaussian factors are constant times
exp(-tau(t_1^2+t_2^2)/2); hence both height integrals and all
interchanges are justified on their full real lines. This checks the
conjugation, sign of t_2-t_1, and normalization. The moving masked
D_i are not substituted for the fixed full detector's holomorphic
zero-detection argument.

### 3.3 Actual-norm cancellation is stronger than leading Gram data

For ANY exact two-part split F=T+R with ||F||<=C X^beta, write
b=||R||. Then

    <T,R>=-b^2+<F,R>,
    ||T||^2=b^2+O(b X^beta+X^(2beta)).                (R3.5)

These are exact identities plus Cauchy--Schwarz. If b is comparable
to X/L^d, the Gram of (T,R), normalized by the ACTUAL b^2, is

    [[1,-1],[-1,1]]
       +O(X^(beta-1)L^d+X^(2beta-2)L^(2d)).           (R3.6)

For the fixed-power split, d=3 and b~(-B(rho))N_X. If instead one
normalizes by its leading asymptotic norm, an additional error
O(L^-1+X^(-eta)L^4) enters. That is distinct from the power-small
accepted-full-field error in (R3.6).

For the critical split with kappa^2>=2exp(3tau), define

    W_kappa(x)=2x/L^2 Phi(kappa^2 X/x),
    N_kappa^2=||W_kappa||^2
       =4X^2/L^4 integral_1^2 s Phi(kappa^2/s)^2 ds.

The positive finite integral is fixed. By (R2.1),
||R_z-W_kappa||=O(X/L^3), so b is comparable to X/L^2. Therefore
(R3.6) holds with d=2. Normalizing by N_kappa^2 introduces a separate
O(1/L) asymptotic error. The accepted F bound additionally gives
T_z=-W_kappa+O(X/L^3+X^beta), a negative leading prefix; that last
prefix statement explicitly uses F, unlike the positive band (R2.9).

Finally, let a=||T|| and r_X=Re<T,R>/(ab). Cauchy--Schwarz gives
r_X>=-1, and exactly

    ||F||^2=(a-b)^2+2ab(1+r_X).                       (R3.7)

For 1/2<gamma<.874872, the desired full norm estimate with arbitrary
epsilon allowance is equivalent, after renaming epsilon, to BOTH

    |a-b|<=C_epsilon X^(gamma+epsilon),
    1+r_X<=C_epsilon X^(2gamma-2+epsilon)L^(2d),      (R3.8)

where d=3 for a fixed-power split and d=2 for the stated positive
critical profile. Necessity follows from the two nonnegative terms
in (R3.7). Sufficiency follows from a,b comparable to X/L^d; without
separately invoking F for that comparability, the first proposed
bound itself forces a comparable to the directly known b.

The present source theorems do not prove (R3.8) at a new gamma. The
accepted beta yields only its existing baseline. A field remainder
O(X/L^4) or O(X/L^3) remains larger than X^gamma for every fixed
gamma<1; writing a leading cancellation does not estimate its actual
residual at the required power precision. These are upper-bound
limitations, not lower bounds for the actual residual.

# Independent review of the [private research revision] nonlinear ordinary-character source



## 1. Decision and what this pass earns

**Recommend accepting the author's analytic claims, at their stated
quantifiers. No new c is established.** In particular:

* The literal source with sixth-power phase has the claimed reciprocal-L
  leading term and an absolutely normally convergent remainder on Re s>1/2.
* The complete sharp-shell energy compression includes both orders of every
  core/tail cross term. The stated actual squarefree-unit tail asymptotic
  and full-energy lower bound follow.
* The published Green--Tao theorem supplies the fixed-degree, coefficient-
  uniform logarithmic estimate used here. It supplies no positive power.
* CORE1 is a complete sufficient L1 input and is equivalent to this source's
  full-shell L1 bound, with all complements paid. It is weaker than the L2
  premise; the L2 lower floor does not disprove CORE1 below that floor.

The substantive gain in the research architecture is a new source whose
**entire long tail and all crosses have a proved summable price**, followed
by an actual arithmetic logarithmic improvement. This is more than writing
an unknown full norm in different notation. It still leaves a genuine
arithmetic power gap in the transition near n~X. The norm equivalence alone
does not close that gap or show that it is easier than a Mertens problem.

Independent additions proved below are: a positive smooth shell majorant
which removes the logarithm from complete tail norm bounds; an explicit
cutoff-dependent squarefree tail main term with square-root density error;
and a fixed-parameter extension showing how to pay the detector/complements
for every fixed gamma>1/2, including a fully priced conditional c=2/5
example. These are new deductions in this review, not claims of literature
priority or new arithmetic power cancellation.

Current comparison remains c11=312864909/2500000000=.1251459636,
theta11=.8748540364. F0/analytic ancestry, original positive-slot uniformity
and external definition/import/admission remain OPEN. This review concerns
ordinary Dirichlet characters only; it adds no Hecke or conductor-uniform
scope. A complete new bound must have gamma<theta11 to give a first gain.

## 2. Exact source and Mellin reconstruction

Fix one ordinary complex Dirichlet character chi modulo q. Set
a_n=mu(n)chi(n), including all squareful and nonunit zeros. For fixed b>1
and integer k>2 define, for every real x>0,

    W_(b,k),chi(x)=sum_(n>=1) a_n exp(-n/x^b-i(n/x)^k).

Absolute convergence is immediate at each x and locally uniform in x>0.
The selected author source is b=3/2,k=6. The phase contains n^k, while the
damping contains n; confusing them changes the reciprocal-L shifts.

For sigma=Re s>0, write

    I_n(s)=integral_0^infinity exp(-nt^b-i(nt)^k)t^(s-1)dt
          =n^(-s) integral_0^infinity
                    exp(-n^(1-b)v^b-iv^k)v^(s-1)dv.

All powers use the principal branch. Choose a FIXED
0<alpha<min(pi/(2b),pi/(2k)). On the clockwise sector from 0 to -alpha,
Re(v^b)>0 and |exp(-iv^k)|<=1. On a large arc the damping is at most
exp(-n^(1-b)R^b cos(b alpha)); for each n this beats the polynomial arc
factor. The small arc tends to zero for sigma>0. Uniformity on compact
s-sets is sufficient here; a large-arc bound uniform in n is not needed
to rotate each term before forming the normally convergent remainder.

On v=r exp(-i alpha), the oscillatory modulus is
exp(-r^k sin(k alpha)). Taylor's integral remainder obeys

    |exp(-z)-sum_(j<K)(-z)^j/j!|<=|z|^K/K!, Re z>=0.

Consequently

    I_n(s)=sum_(j<K) A_j(s)n^(-s-(b-1)j)+R_(n,K)(s),
    A_j(s)=(-1)^j Gamma((s+bj)/k)
                       exp(-i*pi*(s+bj)/(2k))/(k j!),

and

    |R_(n,K)(s)| <= n^(-sigma-(b-1)K) exp(alpha Im s)
       Gamma((sigma+bK)/k)
       /[k K! sin(k alpha)^((sigma+bK)/k)].                 (R1)

The sign of the phase and the gamma exponential are correct. The gamma
coefficient comes from u=i v^k, followed by rotation of a decaying gamma
ray in the right half-plane. The relevant integrals and their s-derivatives
are locally dominated by powers of r times exp(-c r^k), with log factors;
this proves holomorphy of each remainder. On every compact subset of
sigma>max(0,1-(b-1)K), (R1) gives a summable n-majorant. Hence
R_chi,K=sum a_n R_(n,K) is normally holomorphic there.

The absolute Fubini calculation is performed ONLY first on sigma>b:

    integral_0^infinity sum_(n>=1)exp(-nt^b)t^(sigma-1)dt
       =Gamma(sigma/b)zeta(sigma/b)/b.

Thus for H(s)=integral_0^infinity W(1/t)t^(s-1)dt,

    H(s)=sum_(j<K) A_j(s)/L(s+(b-1)j,chi)+R_chi,K(s).     (R2)

For b=3/2,k=6,K=1,

    H(s)=Gamma(s/6)exp(-i*pi*s/12)/(6L(s,chi))+R_chi,1(s), (R3)

where the remainder is holomorphic on sigma>1/2. A_0 is holomorphic and
nonzero on sigma>0. The actual character and all its Euler holes survive;
no primitive-character replacement is made.

Suppose that a FIXED gamma>1/2 satisfies, for every epsilon>0 and every
sufficiently large dyadic X,

    integral_X^(2X)|W(x)| dx/x <<_(chi,epsilon)X^(gamma+epsilon). (L1)

On a compact set with sigma>=gamma+eta, choose epsilon<eta and sum shells.
Factors (log x)^j for each fixed s-derivative are absorbed by the remaining
geometric buffer. The x near zero complement is bounded by
1/(exp(x^(-b))-1), so it is integrable against every fixed Mellin power.
H is therefore holomorphic throughout sigma>gamma. The L2 premise
integral|W|^2 dx/x<<X^(2gamma+epsilon) implies (L1) by Cauchy--Schwarz.

Identity (R3), initially on sigma>3/2, then continues the reciprocal
holomorphically to sigma>gamma. A zero of the ordinary meromorphic L there
would create a pole of its reciprocal, impossible since A_0 has no zero.
The principal pole at s=1 instead creates a reciprocal zero and is allowed.
Imprimitive Euler factors were already included. Each arbitrary compact
height range is covered, so this reaches every finite height without
assuming a height-uniform constant. For all fixed characters the common
gamma is chosen first; constants and onsets may depend on chi and epsilon.

This implication uses the ordinary analytic L-function and does not itself
resolve the project's external root-definition/import obligation. Neither
a reverse Mertens theorem nor equivalence to zero exclusion is being
asserted for this shell norm.

## 3. Sharp-shell energy: signs, boundaries and the complete complement

For this subsection |a_n|<=1 may be arbitrary. Put N=X^b. Absolute
convergence of the damped square gives

    E(X)=sum_(n,m>=1) a_n conjugate(a_m) K_X(n,m),
    K_X(n,m)=integral_1^2 exp(-(n+m)/(N u^b))
                     exp(-i(n^k-m^k)/(X^k u^k))du/u.

In particular K_X(m,n)=conjugate(K_X(n,m)); one must retain both orders
when estimating a real cross energy. Let A=(n+m)/N and v=u^(-k). The
kernel becomes the Fourier integral on [2^(-k),1] with positive amplitude

    B_A(v)=exp(-A v^(b/k))/(k v).

Its derivative is negative. Endpoint sum plus total variation is
2B_A(2^(-k))<=2^(k+1)/k. One integration by parts therefore proves

    |K_X(n,m)|<=C_(b,k) min(1,X^k/|n^k-m^k|), n!=m.       (R4)

The changing damping has been differentiated, not frozen. For n>m,

    n^k-m^k=(n-m)sum_(j=0)^(k-1)n^(k-1-j)m^j
             >=n^(k-1)(n-m).

For a real shell-fixed M>=2, the pairs outside n,m<=M are exactly those
with max(n,m)>M. Summing both orientations gives

    E(X)=E_<=M(X)+D_>M(X)+O_(b,k)(X^k M^(2-k)log(2M)),   (R5)
    D_>M=sum_(n>M)|a_n|^2 K_X(n,n)>=0.

Indeed sum_(n>M)n^(1-k)sum_(h<n)1/h<<M^(2-k)log(2M).
There is no missing low/high strip, equality-boundary atom or distant
physical tail. For real M, n<=M and n>M partition integers exactly.
The summable majorant, since k>2, justifies passage from finite squares.
Also D_>M<<_b X^b by geometric summation before the u-integral.

Thus E_<=M<=E+O(X^k M^(2-k)log(2M)), as well as the forward upper bound
in the author report. This use of D_>M>=0 is legitimate only after (R5).
The same off-diagonal argument restricted to n,m>M gives an actual tail
norm estimate. It is this tail estimate, not a pointwise truncation, that
pays the weaker L1 complement below.

For b=3/2,k=6,M=X^r, the error exponent is 6-4r and diagonal exponent
3/2. At r=19/16, 6-4r=5/4; M itself has exponent19/16<5/4. The author's
selected error budget is correct. The cutoff need not be optimized for
this statement to be valid.

## 4. Actual squarefree-unit diagonal and floor

For the literal coefficients, |a_n|^2=mu(n)^2 1_((n,q)=1). Using
mu(n)^2=sum_(d^2|n)mu(d) gives

    A_q(y):=sum_(n<=y)|a_n|^2=d_q y+O_q(sqrt y),
    d_q=zeta(2)^(-1) product_(p|q)p/(p+1)>0.               (R6)

For each d<=sqrt y with (d,q)=1 the remaining count is
(phi(q)/q)y/d^2+O_q(1); the total counting error and the omitted absolutely
convergent Euler-product tail are O_q(sqrt y). This proves (R6) equally
for principal, nonprincipal and imprimitive fixed characters.

Stieltjes partial summation against exp(-2t/(Nu^b)), uniformly in 1<=u<=2,
therefore yields

    D_all(X)=C_(q,b)N+O_(q,b)(sqrt N),
    C_(q,b)=d_q(2^b-1)/(2b).

Deleting n<=M costs O(M), so (R5) proves exactly the author's

    E(X)=E_<=X^(19/16)(X)+C_(q,3/2)X^(3/2)
                                  +O_q(X^(5/4)log X).   (R7)

The tail alone has that main term and error as well. Positivity of the
remaining core in (R7) NOW proves
E(X)>=(C_(q,3/2)+o(1))X^(3/2). Thus a full every-epsilon L2 premise with
gamma<3/4 is impossible for this fixed source: choose epsilon strictly
below 3/2-2gamma. Gamma=3/4 is not ruled out. There is no corresponding
L1 impossibility proved here, and no assertion about other sources.

**Independent refinement: retain the diagonal cutoff explicitly.** For
any real M>=2, define the positive quantity

    Q_(q,b)(X,M)=(d_q N/2) integral_1^2
                    u^(b-1) exp(-2M/(Nu^b))du.           (R8)

Then, uniformly in M,

    D_>M(X)=Q_(q,b)(X,M)+O_(q,b)(sqrt N).                 (R9)

To prove this, integrate (R6) on the open interval (M,infinity). The
boundary error is O_q(sqrt M exp(-lambda M)) and the integral error is
O_q(lambda integral_M^infinity sqrt t exp(-lambda t)dt), where
lambda=2/(Nu^b). Each is O_q(lambda^(-1/2))=O_(q,b)(sqrt N).
The continuous main term is d_q exp(-lambda M)/lambda. This also handles
integral M, because A_q(M) includes that atom and the tail excludes it.

Combining with (R5) gives the sharper, explicit complete identity

    E(X)=E_<=M(X)+Q_(q,b)(X,M)
                   +O_(q,b,k)(X^(b/2)+X^k M^(2-k)log(2M)). (R10)

The same formula without E_<=M holds for the tail's own squared norm.
For b=3/2,k=6,M=X^(4/3), the cross exponent is2/3, below3/4, hence

    E(X)=E_<=X^(4/3)(X)+Q_(q,3/2)(X,X^(4/3))+O_q(X^(3/4)),
    E_>X^(4/3)(X)=Q_(q,3/2)(X,X^(4/3))+O_q(X^(3/4)).     (R11)

No logarithm remains in this particular error because X^(2/3)log X is
O(X^(3/4)). Q/N tends to C_(q,3/2), but replacing Q by C N prematurely
would lose its explicit cutoff correction of order X^(4/3). This is an
actual arithmetic tail theorem, not an estimate of the hard transition
core or a better zero-free constant.

## 5. Primary arithmetic import and what its uniformity buys

The operative source is Green--Tao, *The Mobius function is strongly
orthogonal to nilsequences*, Annals of Mathematics175(2012),541--566,
[Theorem1.1, printed542--543](https://annals.math.princeton.edu/wp-content/uploads/annals-v175-n2-p03-p.pdf).
I independently read the complete theorem across those pages through the
primary web PDF text. It gives arbitrary fixed logarithmic decay for
bounded Lipschitz functions on fixed rational nilmanifold data, uniformly
in polynomial sequences of fixed degree; constants are ineffective.

Use the circle with a degree-six abelian filtration (G_0=...=G_6=R,
and G_j trivial for j>=7), and fixed sine/cosine
functions. Their complex combination gives

    sum_(n<=Y)mu(n)e(P(n)) <<_A Y(log(2Y))^(-A), deg P<=6,

uniformly in the REAL coefficients of P, with A fixed in advance. A fixed
two-dimensional torus with a dummy coordinate is an equivalent realization.
There is no equidistribution hypothesis in this final theorem. No
growing-degree or growing-A uniformity is imported.

Literal finite Fourier expansion of chi is

    chi(n)=sum_(ell=0)^(q-1)c_ell e(ell n/q),
    c_ell=q^(-1)sum_(a mod q)chi(a)e(-ell a/q).

It preserves the zero values and has sum|c_ell|<=q. The polynomial for
each mode is P(n)=ell n/q-n^6/(2*pi*x^6), so all real x are covered.
For prefixes Y<=M, Y<sqrt M costs sqrt M; otherwise log(2Y) is comparable
to log M. The supremum of these prefixes is O_(q,A)(M(log M)^(-A)).
Abel summation with the actual positive decreasing exp(-n/x^(3/2)) has
uniformly bounded endpoint-plus-variation cost, for every x>0. Hence

    |W_<=M(x)| <<_(q,A) M(log M)^(-A).

With M=X(log X)^B, the author's B=(D+2)/4 and
A=B+(D+2)/2 give core logarithmic exponent -D-2 and complete sharp
off-diagonal exponent -D-1. Therefore

    E(X)<<_(q,D)X^(3/2)+X^2(log X)^(-D)                  (R12)

for every fixed D>0. This genuinely uses arithmetic, but the exponent2
exceeds 2theta11 by .2502919272. Cauchy--Schwarz yields the actual full
L1 bound X^(3/4)+X(log X)^(-D), after using2D in(R12); its power gap is
c11. D depending on X would invalidate the import and these constants.

The independently inspected [Gao--Zhao v2 Theorem1.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2212.09241v2)
explicitly assumes GRH and averages a quadratic-character family. It is
correctly excluded from the argument. Its theorem is on PDF page index1
(printed page2). The Green--Tao GRH power-decay remark is likewise unused.
No local PDF binary or image-byte inspection/hash is claimed; primary
theorem text was available through web reads.

## 6. Complete CORE1 and CORE contracts

Fix0<c<=1/4, gamma=1-c and r=1+c/2. On each dyadic shell, freeze
L=X^gamma and M=X^r BEFORE varying x in[X,2X]. Write exactly

    W=A+T+B,
    A=sum_(n<=L)a_n exp(-n/x^(3/2)-i(n/x)^6),
    T=sum_(L<n<=M)a_n exp(-n/x^(3/2)-i(n/x)^6),
    B=sum_(n>M)a_n exp(-n/x^(3/2)-i(n/x)^6).

The low prefix has both L1 and L2 norm O(X^gamma). From the tail-only
version of(R5),

    ||B||_2^2 << X^(3/2)+X^(6-4r)log X
                <<X^(2gamma)log X,

since6-4r=2gamma and gamma>=3/4. Thus ||B||_1<<X^gamma sqrt(log X).
The triangle inequality in either direction, W=A+T+B or T=W-A-B,
proves the every-epsilon L1 equivalence

    ||T||_1 <<_(chi,c,epsilon)X^(gamma+epsilon)
       if and only if
    ||W||_1 <<_(chi,c,epsilon)X^(gamma+epsilon).           (R13)

No core/tail cross term is required for an L1 triangle argument: the FULL
tail function is paid in L2 before Cauchy--Schwarz. CORE1 is therefore
complete, including the whole real shell. Combining(R13) with(R3) gives
zero exclusion in Re s>1-c, with the exact scope stated inSection2.

Similarly, the L2 triangle inequality gives equivalence of CORE and full
energy at every-epsilon exponent2gamma. Alternatively the author's
reverse proof via(R5) and D_>M>=0 is valid. L2 implies L1 because the
shell has fixed logarithmic measure, but no reverse implication is claimed.

The exact conditional targets are:

| c | gamma | upper cutoff r | full energy exponent |
|---|---|---|---|
|313/2500=.1252|2187/2500=.8748|5313/5000=1.0626|2187/1250=1.7496|
|1/6|5/6|13/12|5/3|
|1/4|3/4|9/8|3/2|

The first row exceeds c11 by135091/2500000000. No row's arithmetic core
bound is proved. The last row is compatible with, rather than contradicted
by, the actual L2 floor.

## 7. Independent improvement: a complete tail norm without log loss

The logarithm in(R5) comes from the boundary terms of a sharp observation
interval. It is avoidable for UPPER NORM bounds while retaining the original
sharp shell and sharp coefficient cutoff. No arithmetic estimate is needed.

Define h(t)=0 for t<=0, h(t)=10t^3-15t^4+6t^5 for0<t<1, and h(t)=1 for
t>=1. Let phi(u)=h(2u-1)h((4-u)/2). Then phi is nonnegative, compactly
supported on[1/2,4], C^2, and equals1 throughout[1,2]. For the tail B,

    ||B||_(L2[X,2X],dx/x)^2
      <=integral_0^infinity phi(u)|W_>M(Xu)|^2 du/u.      (R14)

This is positivity of the complete squared function, not positivity of
individual off-diagonal entries. After v=u^(-k), the weighted kernel has
amplitude phi(v^(-1/k)) exp(-A v^(b/k))/(k v), A=(n+m)/N.
Its support is a fixed compact subset of(0,infinity). The amplitude and
its first derivative vanish at the support endpoints. Its L1 norm and
second-derivative L1 norm are bounded uniformly for all A>=0: derivatives
produce at most a fixed-degree polynomial in A times exp(-cA).
Two integrations by parts therefore give

    |K_phi(n,m)|<=C_(b,k)(1+|n^k-m^k|/X^k)^(-2).         (R15)

For n>m, put delta_n=X^k/n^(k-1). Independently of its size,

    sum_(h>=1)min(1,(delta_n/h)^2)<<delta_n.

For delta_n<1 this follows from sum h^(-2); for delta_n>=1 split at
h=delta_n. Thus the complete weighted tail off-diagonal costs
O_(b,k)(X^k M^(2-k)), with no logarithm. The weighted diagonal is O_b(N).
Consequently the ORIGINAL sharp-shell tail obeys

    ||W_>M||_2^2 <<_(b,k) X^b+X^k M^(2-k).              (R16)

All coefficients are still arbitrary with |a_n|<=1. The damped infinite
sum and every real x were retained. This proves the complete generic bound
E(X)<<_(b,k)X^2+X^b by taking M=X and using the norm triangle inequality.
For b=3/2,k=6 and the cutoffs inSection6, both omitted pieces have L1
and L2 norm O(X^gamma), without any logarithm or epsilon.

Therefore the equivalences in(R13) and its L2 version also hold for exact
big-O exponents, should such a core estimate become available. This is a
cleaner complement contract, not a new arithmetic power gain. It does NOT
remove the log from the sharp signed identity(R5): the positive majorant
proves an upper norm estimate, whereas(R5) uses a different kernel.

The generic exponent2 at b=3/2 is sharp in bounded arrays. The author's
array a_n=1 for n<=floor(X/2), zero otherwise, has a uniformly positive
real part of size X throughout[X,2X], so E>>X^2. Its dependence on X
and failure to be the actual Mobius sequence are essential qualifications.

## 8. Independent high-ceiling continuation with every cost specified

The L2 floor at3/4 belongs to b=3/2. It is not an intrinsic ceiling of
nonlinear-phase detectors. The following fixed-parameter theorem follows
from(R1),(R2),(R16); it is a conditional architecture, not an exponent gain.

Fix any gamma with1/2<gamma<1. Choose once and for all

    1<b<=2gamma,
    integer k>2 with r=(k-2gamma)/(k-2)<b,
    integer K>=1 with 1-(b-1)K<gamma.                    (R17)

Such choices always exist. Define the SAME kind of global source
W_(b,k),chi and the shell-fixed core X^gamma<n<=X^r. Its low prefix costs
O(X^gamma), and(R16) gives the complete tail L2 bound

    ||W_>X^r||_2^2<<X^b+X^(k+(2-k)r)<=C X^(2gamma).

Thus complete shell L1 is equivalent to the core L1 target, and likewise
for L2. All infinite tails and every shell point remain covered.

The Mellin return uses ALL finite shifts in(R2). Set delta=b-1. The
remainder is holomorphic on sigma>gamma by(R17), as are A_j there. Starting
from the Euler-product reciprocal on sigma>1, suppose 1/L is holomorphic
on sigma>a. On sigma>max(gamma,a-delta), each shifted reciprocal with
j>=1 is already holomorphic. Solving(R2) for the unshifted reciprocal,
using nonzero A_0, extends it to that next strip. A finite number of steps
reaches sigma>gamma. The argument handles principal poles and natural
zeros exactly as before. No rightmost zero at an attained height or
uniformity in all heights is assumed.

For a concrete higher-ceiling example choose

    gamma=3/5, c=2/5, b=11/10, k=12, K=5, r=27/25.

Then the remainder boundary is1/2; tail energy exponents are11/10 and6/5;
both are at most2gamma=6/5. The complete OPEN premise is

    for every epsilon>0 and every sufficiently large dyadic X,
    integral_X^(2X) |sum_(X^(3/5)<n<=X^(27/25)) mu(n)chi(n)
                  exp(-n/x^(11/10)-i(n/x)^12)| dx/x
                       <<_(chi,epsilon) X^(3/5+epsilon). (OPEN-HIGH)

If proved for every fixed ordinary character at this common exponent,
it would give zero exclusion in Re s>3/5. None of this arithmetic premise
is proved here. The fixed-degree Green--Tao theorem still yields only
X^b+X^2(log X)^(-D) for the energy, by the same cutoff argument with
fixed k. Thus the actual coarse estimate still misses this target by a
power. The example prices the weakest developed norm input; it does not
make c=2/5 more plausible than a nearer gain.

More generally k may be chosen as a sufficiently large fixed integer
after gamma and b. One must not let k, K, b or logarithmic strength move
with X: the contour, smooth-kernel and imported arithmetic constants all
depend on them. At gamma=1/2 there is no b with1<b<=2gamma, so this theorem
does not supply the boundary itself. There is no claim of uniformity as
gamma decreases to1/2 or of a theorem obtained by taking that limit.

## 9. Strongest surviving objection and next action

The polynomial phase is slow on n~X. Its difference over a unit n-step
there is O(1/X); increasing the fixed degree changes a constant, not that
power. The absolute Gram price or curvature alone therefore cannot create
the missing cancellation in the transition. The bounded-array example
proves the generic exponent2 cannot be improved by this method. It is not
a lower bound for actual Mobius, and it does not retire arithmetic routes.

The complete kernel for an actual signed core is still
mu(n)mu(m)chi(n)conjugate(chi(m))K_X(n,m), with both indices inside the
same sharp interval. A bilinear/nilsequence/inverse-theorem attack must
retain the sum's complete interactions. Merely improving the already paid
far-frequency tail repeats a solved component. Uniform logarithmic
polynomial orthogonality includes the zero polynomial; replacing its log
saving by a power would itself require much stronger arithmetic. The
specific moving polynomial here might admit a sharper argument, but no
such bound follows from the imported theorem.

The next decisive target is therefore the actual CORE1 at gamma=.8748
on X^.8748<n<=X^1.0626 over the ENTIRE shell, or a sufficient signed L2
bound there. Near gains remain preferable first tests;1/6 and1/4 are fully
priced, andSection8 keeps a precisely conditional larger ceiling visible.
No norm-equivalence, favorable review, finite calculation or generic
counterexample is counted as a numerical c increase.

## 10. Evidence and limits

The author report was read fully in ecedde+d43cb8, its helper in d43cb8,
its receipt in9a74a9 and manifest/source receipt in b4a08c. The helper was

confirmed in turn153view0. Screenshot requests returned reference handles;

are written here; no external Hilbert inequality or large sieve is assumed.

The separate lean helper verifies exact source hashes, algebraic budgets
and the explicit smooth cutoff's endpoint/derivative conditions. Such

## 4. An indefinite covariance cannot be used as a positive calibration Gram

**False generic implication.** Adaptive minimization needs the complete positive physical-field Gram, its principal map, nuisance constraints, nullspace and inverse projected separation. The signed coprime form or incomplete outer field cannot replace it. Gcd restriction is not generally positive: two identical normalized vectors have all-ones Gram, but the small-gcd mask for two large coprime core labels leaves \(\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)\), with eigenvalues \(1,-1\). A localized zero form is therefore not automatically a positive projection. T07 removes the paid complete zero form globally. Retain the physical Gram and prove separation, or estimate the localized signed covariance directly. [BA D6; SA Parts III–V; A04/A15.]

# Independent review: completed cross-class reduction



## 1. Verdict and exact scope

**Recommend accepting the source reduction C5--[restricted research revision], with the precise finite-completion and positive-norm interpretations below. No new zero-free constant is proved.** The accepted boundary remains

    c11=312864909/2500000000=.1251459636,
    theta11=2187135091/2500000000=.8748540364.

The useful result is a smaller arithmetic prerequisite. At t=4/3, the complete merged Mobius coefficient permits removal of every column whose sixth-free ideal core has norm at most U^(6/5). In the remaining completed positive norm, the entire same-sixth-power class and the off-class union

    Q<=U^(6/5)  or  Q1/Q3<=U^(1/2)

are bounded below the current E_K density exponent with a saving exceeding 1/100. This accounts for unequal roots, unequal column scales, every original prime slot, and the low/high cross terms. The genuinely signed region left in [restricted research revision] is unproved. A bound for it would give the stated improved *source density input*, still requiring its complete licensed physical use before a numerical c claim.

Three scope requirements should travel with the result:

1. The signed residual is the expansion of a specified smooth positive majorant norm, chosen before pair expansion. One cannot put a high-zero or amplitude-selected indicator into its Poisson kernel. Domination of an original subset occurs on the full positive norm, not on signed pair sectors.
2. Apply the pair classification to the polynomially terminated completed expression after its genuine tail is paid. The infinite completed detector is recovered through that positive-norm error. The proof must not claim a uniform U^epsilon bound for arbitrarily large residue vectors merely by ignoring exponential decay.
3. For a direct OPEN-H return, retain the actual target unit row with weight at least one and all required fixed-inducing rows. The numerical cuts here are paid against E_K, not against a negative exponent. They are not a proved OPEN-H estimate.

These are explicit readings of the author's Sections2,3,6,9 and the retained [restricted research revision] review, rather than changes to the frozen formulas. I found no mathematical counterexample or failed analytic step in this bounded source reduction. Its raw-row aside is restricted to a fixed finite list of excluded sixth-power-core families; it is not a theorem about every physical descendant family.

The source-relative F0/analytic ancestry, original positive-slot uniformity, and exact external L-function definition/import/admission obligations remain OPEN. No new formalization, kernel verification, public-record verification, growing-dictionary uniformity, or literature-priority claim is made. No exceptional centered M/24 reserve is used.

## 2. Sources and independent evidence

The entire author report, helper and numerical receipt were read. Its six content pins and seven named source pins agree with their exact bytes. I did not execute or import the author helper. Primary inspection included:

* PR9 commit `58344dfdbe756cf2f743da1908ffe0582418cf5b`, local `paper.md`: T1 conventions, B0.13's fixed dictionary/nonprincipality statement, B1.6--11, and B3.1--6, especially the literal masked primitive Poisson formula B3.5 and the prohibition on extra canonical column coefficients in B3.6.
* PR15 commit `ca182b70ac2aee2d053d679b4ddf1233883f9eef`, `PlainUnmarkedDensity.tex`: the natural coefficient dictionary and conductor-bounded representative, whole-character conjugation, the fixed finite exceptional set on free rows, and the explicit ideal count bounded by 128x.
* The frozen [restricted research revision] review Sections6--8: completed zero identity, exact tensor Sobolev norm, full sixth-class root sum, target unit row and principal-pole correction.
* Accepted `[restricted mathematical source]`: fixed K=28114053/6250000, its origin from the independently accepted c10 SAME-family bound, and the current G_K/E_K formula. K is not recalibrated from c11.
* The existing external merged research note Section2.5, RM-A through RM15: the balanced relative-residue mass and masked Poisson mechanisms already present there. The author correctly credits these as ancestry.

These are inspected local source bytes, not a new live upstream or admission claim. Current proof/index/creative files were navigation snapshots; active controller edits were left untouched. Exact source and author pins are in `receipt.json` and `source-notes.json`.

The independent `verify.py` uses rational polynomial coefficients and Bernstein conversion on the whole delta interval. It checks four strictly positive cleared-denominator margin polynomials after spending xi=1/100 and the maximum real buffer. Two further nonnegative polynomial certificates establish the stated strictly positive derivative floors. There are 18 Bernstein coefficients: 16 positive and two zero endpoint coefficients belonging to the derivative-floor certificates. The floors themselves are positive. This is whole-interval evidence, not a sampled grid.

It also verifies the exact delta-minus-3k identity, both coefficients of the low-core exponent, six scalar values, 588 radical plateau cases, 896 merged-slot support cases, 4096 two-prime gcd/root representations including unequal scales, 3920 natural-zero cases in exact Q[z]/(z^2-z+1) arithmetic, and ten nonprincipal local character sums. All checks passed. The finite tests are diagnostic support; the proofs of the infinite sums and row bound are below. They do not establish OPEN-[restricted research revision], a physical transfer, or any new c. No repeated endpoint atlas was run.

## 3. Actual coefficient and positive source contract

Fix the original finite natural character dictionary, its bad-prime set S, one complete orientation, and its fixed admissible slot system. Ideal columns use primary generators; element rows retain all six units. Each column avoids S. The presentation is

    phi_u(n)=nu(n)psi_u(n),  psi_u(n)=chi_n(u)^(+/-1).

The fixed nu remains in the coefficient even when its order does not divide six. The symbol includes all natural zeros. A whole conjugation changes every corresponding factor; conjugating only nu is not permitted. The natural representative and its ordinary L-function, not an unspecified row-character existence choice, supply the completed zero identity.

Use the exact original disjoint prime pools, common profiles, individual ray factors, normalized bounded real powers, independent heights, and frozen coprimality holes. Their product is

    Q_u=U^(-v/2) sum_P alpha(P)psi_u(P),
    0<=v=sum_i z_i<=1/20.                              (R1)

P contains one prime from each original pool. With no slots P=1 and v=0. Shared primes between n and P are allowed; complete multiplicativity with zero extension still holds. Fixed slot count, annuli and profile controls give NP comparable to U^v and divisor-many tuple representations. Slot coefficients are independent of the live row. This does not introduce a new permission to apply UM, MI or MP to a merged coefficient.

Let R=U^t, Y=U^B and let V be the actual cutoff, one on [0,1] and zero on [2,infinity). Put

    A_R(n)=sum_(d|n) mu(d)V(Nd/R),
    D_R,u(s)=sum_(Nn>R) phi_u(n)A_R(n)(Nn)^(-s)e^(-Nn/Y).

The reviewed completion gives D_R,u(rho)=-1+O(U^(-A)) at an actual zero of the same natural nonprincipal character in the retained rectangle. Nonprincipal here refers to the primitive inducing character. Extra natural Euler holes do not turn a primitive principal character into a nonprincipal one. The contour argument and its choice of B are inherited exactly; no assertion that derivatives vanish at a zero is made.

For the norm analysis first terminate at Nn<=U^(B+1), using a fixed bounded terminal cutoff if desired. The discarded genuine exponential tail is smaller than any fixed U-power after all required fixed derivatives. First fix the raw row, slot and height powers, then choose its error order. A crude polynomial bound on the retained expression pays any cross term with the discarded tail. Thus the original completed norm and its finite version differ by an arbitrarily small absolute power error. All subsequent classifications concern that finite version; extending its positive bounds to infinite ideal sums is safe.

After merging equal nP=l with their signs, write

    F_u(s)=D_R,u(s)Q_u=sum_l b_l(s)psi_u(l),
    b_l(s)=U^(-v/2) sum_(nP=l,Nn>R)
       A_R(n)nu(n)(Nn)^(-s)e^(-Nn/Y)alpha(P).           (R2)

The terminal cutoff is understood in R2 during expansion. It only contracts the bounds used here. Every natural zero and frozen hole remains in the actual expression. For a required fixed derivative, compact sigma interval in (1/2,infinity), and polynomial terminal support,

    |partial b_l(s)| << H_J U^((sigma-1/2)v+epsilon)
                              (Nl)^(-sigma),
    Nl>=L0=c0 U^(t+v) when b_l!=0.                    (R3)

This is a divisor bound on the actual coefficient. Norm differentiation supplies logarithms; normalized profile and height differentiation supplies the fixed seminorms and a polynomial H_J. Polynomial support allows their small powers to be allocated to epsilon with constants fixed before the actual height. One can alternatively lower sigma slightly in convergent majorants. No live arithmetic coefficient or growing slot count is hidden inside H_J; constants may depend on the fixed slot system.

Choose a smooth nonnegative radial Phi at least one on the requested row ball, fixed before expansion. The main row family consists of all nonzero sixth-power-free elements, with precisely the fixed-dictionary exclusions, or with that finite exceptional set retained. PR15 proves the excluded free set is finite because its prime support is fixed and each valuation is at most five. Removing it is not the same as removing all small rows.

For a fixed positive-width real interval I, with lower edge at least (1+delta)/2-h0 and 0<=h0<=10^(-5), use

    N(F)=sum_(u free,eligible) Phi(Nu/U)
      sum_(i,j in {0,1}) integral_I integral_[-T-1,T+1]
         |partial_sigma^i partial_tau^j F_u(s)|^2
           d tau d sigma.                            (R4)

Finite extra derivatives, labels and orientations mean the corresponding finite sum. An original nonnegative row weight bounded by U^epsilon and row subset may be dominated by R4 before expansion. Their signed residual is not asserted to be dominated pair by pair. The majorant's fixed width and Sobolev constants are retained. Row-dependent profile selection, moving ray dictionaries, or arbitrary amplitude masks are not new licensed inputs.

## 4. Radical cancellation and complete low-core payment

For n!=1 and N(rad n)<=R, every contributing squarefree d divides rad n and has Nd<=R. Therefore V(Nd/R)=1, and

    A_R(n)=sum_(d|rad n) mu(d)=0.                     (R5)

This is exact at the endpoint N(rad n)=R. It does not require n to be squarefree or Nn<=R. Inactive nonsquarefree divisors have mu=0. A single separated divisor dyad would not retain this identity. Natural omissions cause no problem: if phi_u(n) is nonzero, all its divisors have the same permitted prime support; if it is zero, the fully multiplicative convolution is zero already.

If b_l is nonzero, some retained summand in R2 has A_R(n)!=0. Since rad n divides rad l,

    N(rad l)>R.                                      (R6)

Write l=c a^6 with c sixth-power-free as an ideal. Then rad l=rad(ca), so N(rad l)<=Nc Na. Thus every contributing small-core column obeys Na>R/Nc. This is a substantially stronger restriction than the size-only Na>(R/Nc)^(1/6).

For C0=U^lambda<R, form the exact merged-column projection F_lo with Nc<=C0. Apply R3 and natural zeros only as contractions. For every individual row, every required derivative, and the entire real rectangle,

    |partial F_lo,u(s)|
      << H_J U^((sigma-1/2)v+epsilon)
           sum_(Nc<=C0) (Nc)^(-sigma)
              sum_(Na>R/Nc) (Na)^(-6sigma)
      << H_J U^((sigma-1/2)v+epsilon)
                      R^(1-6sigma) C0^(5sigma).      (R7)

The first ideal tail is O(A^(1-6sigma)) for A>=1 by the source's linear ideal count and partial summation. Its exponent is safely convergent on the fixed real interval. After substitution, the remaining c sum is bounded by sum_(Nc<=C0)(Nc)^(5sigma-1), which is O(C0^(5sigma)). Extending c to all ideals only enlarges the upper bound. All sixth-power roots, late column scales, unit cores, shared slot primes and exceptional rows are included.

There are O(U) element rows in the fixed ball. Integrating R7 and its derivative versions yields

    N(F_lo) << H_J U^[1+2t(1-6sigma)+10sigma lambda
                              +(2sigma-1)v+epsilon]. (R8)

At t=4/3, lambda=6/5, its derivative with respect to sigma is -4+2v<0. At the nominal edge sigma=(1+delta)/2 the exponent is

    L_lo=5/3-2delta+delta v.                           (R9)

A downward buffer h0 raises it by (4-2v)h0<=4h0. For F_hi=F-F_lo, the Hilbert norm satisfies

    N(F)^(1/2)<=N(F_hi)^(1/2)+N(F_lo)^(1/2).          (R10)

Squaring gives a fixed factor two, which has no power cost. This pays every low/high cross term, regardless of sign. It never divides by Q_u or assumes an amplitude lower bound. This is the decisive response to the concern that a paid low-low sector might leave unpaid crosses. The same pointwise projection is valid on a target unit row; a direct-return application still has to pay its different exponent.

## 5. Independent derivation of the complete relative mass

For a pair l,l', use the actual valuation differences e_p in Z/6Z. Define pairwise coprime radicals q1,q2,q3 from e_p in {1,5}, {2,4}, {3}, and

    Q_i=Nq_i, Q=Q1 Q2 Q3, H=Q1 Q2^2 Q3^3.           (R11)

The complete residue vector, not merely the three norm values, specifies one relative character. At a good prime every nonzero local exponent has a nonprincipal character of conductor that prime. Fixed ray factors only modify fixed S-data and cannot cancel a good conductor prime. e=0 is the same ideal class modulo sixth powers, with all its natural holes retained.

Here is a derivation of [restricted research revision] that does not rely on a same-dyad estimate. For each choice of signs of the nonzero actual valuation differences, represent

    l=g a x^6, l'=g b y^6, (a,b)=1, Nab>=H.          (R12)

Take g as the actual ideal gcd. At a nonzero residue prime the remaining exponent in a or b is e_p or 6-e_p according to the sign; all multiples of six, including differences at zero-residue primes, go into x or y. This reconstructs every actual pair. Allowing arbitrary x,y afterward only overcounts. The number of sign choices is at most 2^omega(q1q2q3), a subpower on the polynomial terminal support. No coprimality between g and a,b is needed or imposed.

Put A=Na(Nx)^6 and B'=Nb(Ny)^6. The lower column support R3 requires

    Ng>=M=max(1,L0/A,L0/B').

The ideal count gives sum_(Ng>=M)(Ng)^(-2sigma)<<M^(1-2sigma), uniformly on the compact interval sigma>1/2. Since M>=L0/sqrt(A B') and 1-2sigma<0,

    (A B')^(-sigma) sum_(Ng>=M)(Ng)^(-2sigma)
       << L0^(1-2sigma) (A B')^(-1/2)
        = L0^(1-2sigma) (Nab)^(-1/2)

This remains true if L0/sqrt(A B')<1: M>=1 and the exponent has the required sign. The two root sums converge absolutely at exponent3. Multiplying by U^((2sigma-1)v+epsilon) from R3 and paying the finite sign choices gives

      << H_J U^[-(2sigma-1)t+epsilon] H^(-1/2).       (R14)

The slot exponent cancels exactly because L0 is comparable to U^(t+v). R13 simultaneously prices all unequal scales and unequal roots. It also independently justifies the author's two convergent dyadic sums. There is no omitted g=1 branch, no arbitrary equality of column lengths, and no root diagonal restricted to l=l'. The projection to high cores only contracts this absolute mass.

In dyadic Q1,Q2,Q3 ranges, ideal counting and the finite residue choices give at most (Q1Q2Q3)^(1+epsilon) vectors. Multiplying their H^(-1/2) bounds yields

    total coefficient mass
      << H_J U^[-(2sigma-1)t+epsilon](Q1/Q3)^(1/2).  (R15)

This is the completed, original-slot version of external RM-A/RM7. The balanced-residue mechanism itself was already present in that source. Global character order six does not imply Q1>1: local exponents2 and3 at different primes give global order6 but Q1=1. The claimed ratio sector correctly includes those easier characters.

## 6. Literal Poisson, natural holes and eligibility

The row phase is exactly

    psi_u(l) conjugate(psi_u(l'))
       =xi_e(u) 1_((u,E_(l,l'))=1).                  (R16)

E includes all primes in ll' whose relative phase became trivial, as well as retained fixed omissions not already enforced by the primitive conductor. In particular exponent0 or6 does not remove a natural zero at a shared prime. The norm of E is bounded by a fixed polynomial on the terminated expression. Fixed nu-values stay in b_l and do not enter this row character.

For e!=0, xi_e is nonprincipal outside S. Read literally, PR9 B3.5 gives a primitive transform with prefactor V/sqrt(Q), unit-modulus normalized Gauss sum, and dual argument V Nh/Q. Its dual zero term vanishes. Writing a=V/Q, radial Schwartz decay and lattice counting give

    a sum_(h!=0)|F Phi(a Nh)|<<_Phi 1.

Hence the unrestricted primitive sum is O_Phi(sqrt(Q)). Ordinary counting gives O_Phi(V). For a scale below a fixed positive threshold there are no nonzero elements in the compact original support; this handles small V without incorrectly bounding a nonzero row by a quantity tending to zero. Thus

    |sum_w xi_e(w)Phi(Nw/V)|<<min(V,sqrt(Q)).          (R17)

Fixed ray restrictions are expanded only through their licensed finite characters. Their fixed conductor factors and complete deleted zeros remain. Nonunit fixed-S sectors, when present, can first be separated by their finitely many free-row S-valuations; their scales and phases have fixed costs. This is not a Poisson rule for an arbitrary row selector.

Impose the row condition by the exact identity

    1_(u sixth-free)=sum_(b^6|(u)) mu(b).

Write u=b^6w with the source's generator/unit convention. Rows are nonzero; adding w=0 for nonprincipal Poisson contributes zero. The sextic relative factor on b^6 is one if coprime, zero otherwise; any fixed ray phase is retained and bounded in modulus. A common row hole or the pair hole forces additional coprimality with b. Dropping that restriction after absolute values only enlarges the bound. Expand the remaining complete hole on w using d|rad E. Its inner scale is exactly U/((Nb)^6 Nd), so R17 yields

Both are O(X^(1/6)Q^(5/12)). If the split lies below one, the whole tail is O(X), and X<=X^(1/6)Q^(5/12). Therefore the full bound is

            product_(p|E)(1+(Np)^(-1/6)).

The product is O_epsilon((NE)^epsilon): finitely many small primes cost a fixed constant, and each larger factor is at most (Np)^epsilon. Polynomial NE permits a requested U^epsilon loss.       << H_J U^epsilon min(U,U^(1/6)Q^(5/12)).        (R18)

The fixed-inducing free exclusions cost O_fixed(1) when removed, and the right side is at least a constant for U,Q>=1. They may equally be retained. The optional raw-row statement is also valid in its stated narrow scope. Masked primitive Poisson costs U^epsilon min(U,sqrt(Q)); deleting a fixed list of core families v a^6 costs O_fixed(U^(1/6)). For Q<=U^2 both fit U^(1/6)Q^(5/12), and for Q>U^2 the trivial U bound applies. This says nothing about unverified moving physical exclusions or a growing list of cores.

## 7. Paid sectors and current whole-interval margins

      min(U(Q1/Q3)^(1/2),

The pair hole varies with l,l', but R18 is uniform in those holes, so it can be taken outside the absolute coefficient mass. Integration over the real/height rectangle and its finite derivative list only modifies H_J. Terminal polynomial support gives O((log U)^3) triples; there is no infinite nondecaying sum of conductor ranges.

For Q<=V, use H>=Q in R14. There are only divisor-many assignments of residues to any radical q. Partial summation of the ideal count gives

        << V^(11/12+epsilon).

## 8. Exact residual and conditional return

In the finite expansion of N(F_hi), let R_hi be the real ordered cross-class sum, including its actual derivative coefficient inner products and R18's *actual* kernel, restricted to

    Nc>U^(6/5), Nc'>U^(6/5),

These conditions are invariant under swapping l and l', so conjugate pairs make the sum real. All coefficients, orientations, zeros and phases are preserved. The exact split is

    N(F_hi)=D_hi+P_hi+R_hi,

where D_hi is the full same-class contribution and P_hi is the disjoint paid off-class union. We have an absolute upper bound on P_hi and the positive majorant for D_hi. A one-sided upper bound on R_hi is sufficient; individual remaining pairs need not be small or negative.

    R_hi<=H_J U^[E_K(delta,v)-xi+epsilon]             (OPEN-[restricted research revision])

Constants may depend on the fixed source data and requested loss; the final threshold precedes the height. Restoring the completed tail preserves R23. The remaining sector contains actual completed coefficients. With no slots and distinct good primes p,p' of norm above2R, A_R(p)=A_R(p')=1 because V(1/R)=1 and V(Np/R)=0. The fixed unit row cannot be removed from a direct target norm. On raw rows a^6, the same coprime phase coherence survives with natural zeros at shared primes. the unconditional estimate

    D_X=T-A_p,

This is an actual difference of finite signed arithmetic sources. For
principal chi and u>1/2, (R15) shows that D_X contains exactly the
author's ordered-prime-pair cell B_X on those semiprime integers: T has
its two ordered factorizations and A_p has zero coefficient. Set

    K_X=D_X-B_X.

K_X is the explicit remaining signed coefficient difference, including
every other divisor/cofactor label and both physical cuts. Then

    ||B_X+K_X||_j <<_epsilon X^(gamma+epsilon), j=1,2. (R17)

For any fixed epsilon<1-gamma, this is o(||B_X||_j). Hence
||K_X||_j/||B_X||_j tends to 1. In L2, with inner product dx/x,

    Re <B_X,K_X>=-||B_X||_2^2
                       +O(||B_X||_2 X^(gamma+epsilon)). (R18)

The normalized real correlation therefore tends to -1. There is also
