## 5. Uniform audit S19: the largest-prime state is indispensable

The seed seeks a signed renewal residual that excludes every complex power mode. To test it against actual arithmetic, define the smooth source

    S_chi(x,y)=sum_(n<=x,P^+(n)<=y)mu(n)chi(n),

with n=1 included and P^+(1)=1. Below a prime p, write p^- for the STRICT restriction that all prime factors are<p. Factor each squarefree n>1 by its largest prime p; its cofactor m has P^+(m)<p. Therefore

    S_chi(x,y)
      =1-sum_(p<=min(x,y))chi(p) S_chi(x/p,p^-).       (R16)

Repeated p is excluded by the strict cofactor cutoff, not by an extra unproved distribution assumption. Ramified p gives zero. The complete source is M_chi(x)=S_chi(x,x).

There is an exact defect return for any proposed approximation F on these descendant states. Let

    Delta_F(x,y)
      =F(x,y)-1+sum_(p<=min(x,y))chi(p)F(x/p,p^-).

Successively substitute(R16); the prime thresholds strictly decrease, so every nontrivial path has distinct primes in decreasing order and terminates. Such paths correspond one-to-one to squarefree products. Subtracting the equations for F and S gives

    F(x,y)-S_chi(x,y)
      =Delta_F(x,y)
       +sum_(2<=d<=x,mu(d)^2=1,P^+(d)<=y)
          mu(d)chi(d) Delta_F(x/d,P^-(d)^-).          (R17)

This is a finite identity. It retains ALL descendant errors, their signs and the final strict prime threshold. For integer x one can use floor-invariant states; composed floors satisfy floor(floor(N/d)/p)=floor(N/(dp)). Equal states must be merged with their signed coefficients BEFORE any absolute estimate, exactly as in G92. The present order is largest-prime/smooth rather than least-prime/rough; it is not a new triangular inverse principle.

An x-only power F(x,y)=x^rho has defect

    Delta_F(x,y)
      =x^rho[1+sum_(p<=min(x,y))chi(p)p^(-rho)]-1.    (R18)

This is not a spectral equation for the global Mertens sum. A hypothesis about M(x)=S(x,x) alone does not identify S(x/p,p^-) with (x/p)^rho, nor make its cofactor errors small. Already S_chi(t,2^-)=1 for every t>=1, regardless of t^rho. The missing cofactor state is actual arithmetic information. Inserting a power into the wrong reduced state and declaring its nonzero residual incompatible with the source would omit exactly the errors summed in(R17).

For a finite prime set p<=y, the full uncut smooth Dirichlet polynomial is

    E_y(s)=product_(p<=y)(1-chi(p)p^(-s)).

Every unramified factor has zeros only on Re(s)=0, since |chi(p)|=1; ramified factors equal1. Thus all these finite products are zero-free on Re(s)>0. Nevertheless finite-prime nonvanishing alone proves nothing about continuation of the INFINITE source there. Initially Re(s)>1, the full absolutely convergent product is1/L(s,chi); outside that domain, the required normal convergence/identification or other complete source bound is an extra obligation. A nonzero finite product is not a pole-exclusion theorem for the infinite arithmetic inverse.

This distinguishes two limits the seed must not merge: for fixed y, S(x,y) becomes the finite product of(1-chi(p)) once x exceeds the product of all allowed primes; for the desired M(x), y=x grows and new cofactor states never stop appearing. Neither the fixed finite-polynomial spectrum nor a single real power test supplies an all-height synthesis theorem.

There is a concrete conditional return. At y=x, if F(x,x) is O_(chi,epsilon)(x^(gamma+epsilon)) and the COMPLETE signed right side of(R17) is of that order, then M_chi(x) has the same bound. All fixed ordinary characters, every epsilon, all sufficiently large real x and one common gamma are required; section2 gives the zero return. Arbitrary imaginary parts of a hypothetical rho and every boundary are thereby handled by an actual bound, not by mode classification alone.

No signed defect estimate or exclusion of a hypothetical arithmetic zero is proved. The audit supplies the exact state, full error contraction and the finite/infinite distinction. G81/G92 renewal and integer merging, the old RN/SP hierarchy and full contour/spectral-return cautions already contain the broader principles. There is no inherited exponent-one lower bound for this merged actual signed contraction.

    sum_((m,n)>=D) K_X(m,n)
       <= sum_(integer d>=D) integral [sum_a g(log(da/x))]^2 dx/x
       <= C X^2 sum_(d>=D)d^-2 <= C X^2/D.                 (R27)

Every original pair is counted at least at d=gcd(m,n). Positive
overcounting is permissible here, and R2 pays the entire infinite
divisor tail. R27 is a positive mass bound for ANY bounded
coefficients, distinct from the signed unpartitioned G33 estimate.

Let Q_hard(u,v) use exactly the mask in R25: m!=n, gcd(m,n)<D,
|m-n|/gcd(m,n)>H, and m,n in the original I_X. Its difference from
the uncut scalar has the absolute bound

    E=X^2/D+XH log(2D)+X+X^-4,                            (R28)

by R27, R24, the true diagonal, and the original window tail.
These masks are compatible and are the SAME for all four pieces.
Thus the whole rough scalar, not merely its g=1 subfamily, satisfies

    Q_hard(R,R)=||R||^2+O(E),
    Q_hard(F,R)=O(X^(1+beta)+E),
    Q_hard(T,R)=-Q_hard(R,R)+O(X^(1+beta)+E),
    Q_hard(R,T)=Q_hard(T,R),
    Q_hard(T,T)=Q_hard(R,R)+O(X^(1+beta)+E).                (R29)

For the FR line, use the actual accepted full field F(x)<<X^beta
and the elementary |R(x)|<=C X, then pay R28. For TT, combine
the exact four-piece identity with ||F||^2=O(X^(2beta)); this error
is absorbed in X^(1+beta). No hereditary estimate on an arithmetic
submask is used. R7--R6 give ||R||^2 asymp X^2/L^4, or one can
use the already accepted critical-source theorem at this fixed
kappa. Its leading function is uniformly positive here.

For any FIXED theta>0 and 0<=alpha<1, D=X^theta,H=X^alpha give
E=o(X^2/L^4). Since beta<1, all remaining errors in R29 are also
o(X^2/L^4). Therefore the COMPLETE all-g<D hard RR scalar is
positive and comparable to X^2/L^4; its complete mixed TR and RT
scalars have the opposite sign and comparable magnitude. This is
A29b, and it is not inferred from a positive g=1 subcollection.

When theta<1/2, eventually D<z. A shared rough prime would divide
the literal gcd and force it to be at least z, contradicting the
hard mask. Thus central retained RR pairs again have four distinct
rough primes. This extra assertion requires theta<1/2; it is not
claimed for all theta>0. The three displayed budgets satisfy it.

The cost X^2/D need not be small enough for a desired full power
budget X^(2gamma). Its role here is to be small compared with the
particular obstruction size X^2/L^4. Confusing these uses would
overclaim the result. Likewise, R29 is compatible with extensive
full-field cancellation: the leading RR,TR,RT,TT terms have signs
+,-,-,+ and cancel in their full sum. There is no full-energy lower
bound from R29.

statement:
# Actual R4 nonunique companion: complete collision labels and paid power-core sectors



**Result proposed:** the square-core/cube-core payment extends to the COMPLETE nonunique companion after an exact collision decomposition. Its actual shared-prime labels are not the artificial mutual-divisor label f. Their prices must be recalculated. Most converge; the remaining deficient powers are paid using the original within-column and four cross-copy gcd caps. Both independent inverse heights, every original slot, all collisions and natural zeros remain. The surviving signed companion is a specified large-square/large-cube first-dual core on each collision/hole summand. No bound for that complete remainder is claimed.

This materially changes the previous residual: the earlier SQ/CU argument touched only the coprime squarefree pair source. The present argument extracts every other valuation pattern, includes its primitive mixed-order conductor and canceled-phase holes, and sums all collision labels. A naive transplant of the old f^-1 factor, or an unchanged S0 bound in the limiting cube term, does not prove this result.

## 1. Inputs, source and relation to R_nonunique

Initial source-pins.json was frozen before substantive analysis, SHA256 f7ac849581c70dcd602b4a9bd3371ba93f8b32f1151938102c4e454fc7fea3b3. Its11 inputs include the exact assignment, G179-G181, G185-G187, PR9, G155-G157 and the prior independently frozen R4-middle review. The full then-current attempt-index was read. The assignment recorded that earlier review as pending root integration. During final audit the controller added [private research revision]/G204-G206; its complete integration was then read, and all initially pinned mathematical bytes still matched. Only the contextual index changed. This NEW nonunique proof remains a candidate; it reconstructs the needed prices rather than treating review agreement as admission. The source-recheck records the exact change.

Use precisely the free-row norm of G179-G181:

    F_u=M_u(D1;W1,t1)M_u(D2;W2,t2)Q_u,
    D1=U^r, D2=U^s, P0=U^v, N0=D1D2P0.

There are two independent inverse heights and a common real parameter. Q is the original ordered product of disjoint prime-slot pools, with its original coefficients, heights, profiles and natural zeros. Pools can meet the inverses. The entire right column is conjugated. Retain both complete sextic orientations e=+1,-1, the original fixed S, primary/ray/unit dictionary, nonzero sixth-free row enclosure and prior domination of row divisor weights. This inserts no physical projector or moving row selector.

Retain exactly

    17/25<=delta<=7/10, 17/20<r<47/50,
    33/25<s<141/100, s-r>3/8, 0<=v<=1/20,
    T=delta(r+s)+E_K, K=28114053/6250000,
    E_K>=rho=1-10delta/[3(5-2delta)], T>=123353/67500.

Use G=U^(1/5), H11=D1/U^(1/2), H22=D2/U^(3/4), H12=H21=U^(3/5). Let C6 be the exact paired scalar with both within-column inverse gcds<G and all four cross-copy inverse gcds<H_ij, but BEFORE the diagonal/low-conductor/ratio deletions. G179-G181 give ||F_<||^2=C6+O(H_J U^(T-1/200+epsilon)). Fully squarefree coprime merged columns automatically satisfy these six cuts and the high-conductor cuts. Consequently

    C6_nonunique=R_nonunique+P_old,
    |P_old|<<H_J U^(T-1/200+epsilon),                 (1)

where P_old is exactly the already paid complete diagonal and two conductor sectors, with the six cuts retained. G181's c_abs majorant permits those restrictions. This is equality of signed forms with a proved error, not signed-subset norm monotonicity. It allows the following argument to work on C6 without introducing a joint product-norm conductor selector into its inner coefficients.

## 2. Exhaustive collision decomposition before any new divisor extension

At a good prime p, each original inverse occurs at most once by its Mobius factor, and at most one slot occurs on each side by disjoint pools. Write a=v_p(n), b=v_p(n'), 0<=a,b<=3. Preserve the full original site incidence, not only (a,b). There are six aggregated sites: inverse1,inverse2,slot on each copy; named slots and pool tests further restrict their allocations.

A prime is a collision prime exactly when a+b>=2. Let h_ab be the squarefree product of primes of that type, for the13 pairs (a,b) with0<=a,b<=3 and a+b>=2. These13 ideals are pairwise coprime. Keep all their site allocations and original coefficients. Put

    Lc=product h_ab^a, Rc=product h_ab^b, D=N(Lc Rc),
    L=N(Lc), R=N(Rc),
    k=product_(a!=b)h_ab, E=product_(a=b>=1)h_ab,
    Kc=N(k), Hcol=product h_ab.

Then uniquely n=Lc*x, n'=Rc*y, where x,y are squarefree, pairwise coprime and prime to Hcol. Every prime of x occurs in ONE original left site; every prime of y in ONE original right site. Thus this is an exact tuple decomposition, including all shared slots and inverse-slot coincidences. Nonunique means Hcol!=1. All six gcd tests are now predicates on the collision labels and their site allocations alone.

The independent original slot allocations have divisor multiplicity tau(Hcol)^C at fixed slot depth. A prime cannot be placed in a slot unless its original pool/coefficient allows it. No count of arbitrary factorizations replaces those masks. Absolute upper bounds may subsequently discard impossible allocations, paying this fixed divisor power.

There are three useful support facts:

    N(h_20),N(h_02) << G P0;
    N(h_11) << N0;
    N(h_11^(ij)) < H_ij,                              (2)

where h_11^(ij) contains precisely the type(1,1) primes assigned to inverse i on the left and inverse j on the right. The first follows from G157's n/rad(n)<C G P0 on each column; h_20 or h_02 divides that defect. The second follows because h_11 divides both original merged columns. The third follows because those primes divide the actual original inverse gcd on that edge. All fixed annular constants are retained. These are upper support bounds, not signs or probabilistic assertions.

For every row u, including its natural zeros,

    chi_n(u)^e conjugate(chi_n'(u)^e)
     =psi_k(u) chi_x(u)^e conjugate(chi_y(u)^e)
                              1_((u,E)=1),           (3)
    psi_k=product_(a!=b) chi_p^(e(a-b)).

Every nonzero local exponent is +/-1,+/-2 or+/-3, hence nonprincipal primitive at its good prime. The primitive good conductor is kxy. Equal positive valuations cancel phase but keep the hole in E. In particular chi_p(u)^a conjugate(chi_p(u)^a) is the UNIT INDICATOR, not the constant1. The fixed nu(n)conjugate(nu(n')) stays in the actual coefficients; no order-six claim is made about nu.

If kxy=1 then x=y=1 and every a=b, so n=n'. Conversely the full relative principal class is the complete merged diagonal in this bounded-valuation source. Its absolute coefficient mass is O(H_J U^epsilon), by G181's c_abs bound; its row contribution is O(H_J U^(1+epsilon)). This pays that whole class before claiming zero-frequency absence. Original principal inducing rows of the physical family have not been discarded.

## 3. Primitive mixed-order Poisson, all holes, and both roots

Expand sixth-freeness with sum_(a0^6|u)mu(a0), retaining (a0,Hcol*x*y)=1, and expand the canceled-phase hole by sum_(d|E,d|u/a0^6)mu(d). Since d is prime to kxy, its character value is a unit; this does not divide out any zero. Put u=a0^6 d z. The row scale is U/(N(a0)^6 N(d)), and primitive Poisson applies to psi_k chi_x^e conjugate(chi_y^e), with conductor kxy. Nonprincipal summands have zero Fourier term at ell=0 and at primes shared by ell and that conductor.

Write q_d=N(d), q_a=N(a0). General CRT gives the normalized Gauss factor

    gamma(psi_k;k) gamma_e(x) gamma_-e(y)
       *psi_k(xy) chi_x(k*y)^e chi_y(k*x)^(-e).        (4)

The core cross ratio chi_x(y)^e chi_y(x)^(-e) is the fixed PR9 ray sign. Every remaining k interaction is a product of a function of x and a function of y. Its modulus is one on actual coprime supports. The mixed gamma(psi_k;k) also has modulus one; it is not replaced by a cuspidal coefficient or by gamma_1(k).

The actual inverse Mobius signs on residual x,y obey the same whole-slot sign identity as G185. Applying PR9 B1.10 leaves exactly the two G185 orientations: for e=-1, a0(x)conjugate(a0(y)) with chi_x(-1)conjugate(G(x))G(y); for e=+1, conjugate(a0(x))a0(y) with G(x)conjugate(G(y))chi_y(-1), together with the retained fixed ray sign. Multiply these by (4)'s separated k twists and all original collision coefficients. The factor psi_k(d)chi_x(d)^e chi_y(d)^(-e) from the hole expansion is also separated. Both orientations remain present.

Before extending coprimality or taking an absolute Fourier integral, pay the genuine far tail. On q_a~A, the original conductor is comparable to Kc N0^2/(L R). Fix tau=1/1000 and a fixed support constant C_* large enough. The retained cap is

    H_c=C_* U^tau A^6 q_d Kc N0^2/(U L R).          (5)

It is literal on each original collision/hole summand, fixed before the artificial f extension below. For ell beyond it the actual Schwartz argument is >c U^tau. PR9 B3.4 and the complete original tuple count pay the tail by

    O(H_J U^(149/30+epsilon-tau(B-1))).

Indeed the primitive prefactor of one original pair is U/(q_a^6 q_d N0 sqrt(Q)), Q=N(kxy)<=C N0^2. Its absolute frequency sum above that argument is bounded by this prefactor times (1+q_a^6 q_d Q/U)U^(-tau(B-1)). There are O(N0^2 U^epsilon) original paired tuples, O(U^(1/6)) a0 labels and only divisor-many d per tuple. The raw cost is at most U^(1/6)(U N0+N0^2)U^epsilon, bounded by U^(149/30+epsilon). This also covers H_c<1: then the entire nonzero lattice tail is treated by the same bound. Choose finite B after this raw count. No Poisson-frequency tail is discarded after algebraic extension.

For coprime squarefree x,y the pair coefficient and primitive root have prefactor

    U sqrt(LR)/(q_a^6 q_d N0^2 sqrt(Kc)),             (6)

with bounded original norm ratios kept in the smooth profile. Extend this displayed product expression formally to individually squarefree x,y prime to Hcol, and insert the COMPLETE identity sum_(f|x,f|y)mu(f). It kills every artificial noncoprime pair. The six gcd predicates remain their original collision-label predicates; they are not recomputed on the artificial f pairs. The frequency/collision/hole selectors are independent of f. Thus cancellation remains exact, with no imprimitive Poisson assertion on added pairs.

Write x=f m, y=f m', F=N(f). Independently allocate every f prime to its original inverse color or named surviving slot on each side. With all original shortenings, the two residual product scales are

    X_L=N0/(L F), X_R=N0/(R F).                      (7)

They need not agree. Both allocation multiplicities cost tau(f)^C. Each normalized column is an actual squarefree divisor/slot sum, with squared mass O(H_J U^epsilon), after dividing its coefficient squared mass by X_i. PR9 B1.11 and the fixed k,d,Hcol twists leave separated arbitrary sequences on that copy's two ORIGINAL inverse colors. The other copy is not a sieve variable. All punctures and natural zeros remain. Empty scales remain empty; nonempty subunit nominal scales have bounded clipping cost.

Restoring BOTH unnormalized roots is decisive:

    (6)*sqrt(X_L X_R)=U/(q_a^6 q_d N0 sqrt(Kc) F).   (8)

There is no additional L^-1, R^-1 or common-collision f^-1 factor. The real norm ratios remain once in the common profile. The complete Gauss extraction also leaves only unit f twists and the outer natural hole1_((f,ell)=1), never division by it.

Fix nominal dyads for a0,d,ell and all finitely many collision-norm coordinates before choosing live arithmetic labels. On their full ambient boxes the kernel is K(U q_ell L R/(q_a^6 q_d Kc q_n q_n')); its Euler derivatives are uniformly controlled for every nominal scaling constant. PR9 B3.3 therefore fixes one weighted Fourier measure first, including each original real root once. Only then substitute labels and allocations. No f-dependent profile or selector is introduced. All sharp masks remain outside the smooth separation. The number of such dyadic coordinates is bounded at fixed slot depth, hence costs a subpower.

The formal core extension may include the unit pair x=y=1 when k=1. Subtract this rank-one block explicitly; it is the already paid merged diagonal. Its FULL absolute Poisson-frequency sum, even after frequency selection, costs O(H_J U^(1+epsilon)): for one diagonal coefficient the a0,d sum is bounded by sum_(a0,d|E)(U/(q_a^6 q_d)+1)<<U^(1+epsilon), using q_a<<U^(1/6); then sum the complete c_abs(n)^2 mass. This legitimizes the unit-core subtraction without falsely declaring its zero frequency absent.

## 4. Licensed core energies and the six exact prices

The two external permissions are the same primary sources independently checked in the preceding same-context review: [Dunn2403.13151v3, Section4](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.13151v3), version23June2025, permits arbitrary squarefree inner coefficients and unrestricted cubic outer variable, with energy B^(1/3)(B+X). [Goldmakher-Louvel1112.1642v2, Definition1/Theorem1.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1112.1642v2),31May2012, permits arbitrary coefficients for its squarefree quadratic Hecke family with energy B+X. The actual quadratic family is PR9 B2.24, including its lambda correction, primitive conductor convention and fixed ray splitting. No cuspidal theorem, canonical B3.6 extension, [restricted research revision]-MQ I-C3CF or I-HECKE assumption is imported.

Fix the original S-supported clearing element Delta. Power cores mean the integral IDEAL (Delta*ell), retaining its unit and fixed-place representatives. At fixed collision labels, coefficient twists from k,d and either orientation do not depend on the live sieve variable. All finite S parts and rays are split first; unrestricted S powers have only logarithmic count under the polynomial cap. Primes in the conductor sharing ell supply zero, not a growing gcd multiplier.

For SQ write (Delta*ell)=kappa2*b^2, kappa2 squarefree, with no disjointness assumed. The kappa2 symbol is fixed on the inner coefficient; the b symbol is cubic, unrestricted. For a cap C, its summed positive energy on column i is

    A_s+X_i B_s,
    A_s=H_c^(2/3) C^(1/3), B_s=H_c^(1/6) C^(5/6),  (9)

up to H_J U^epsilon. Middle, priority and conductor holes remain outer restrictions. Scalar Cauchy is applied before enlarging these positive frequency sets. Because X_L and X_R differ, retain all three terms

    sqrt((A_s+X_L B_s)(A_s+X_R B_s))
     <=A_s+B_s sqrt(X_L X_R)
                 +sqrt(A_s B_s)(sqrt(X_L)+sqrt(X_R)). (10)

For CU write (Delta*ell)=kappa3*t^3*z^6, kappa3 cubefree and t squarefree, retaining ALL overlaps. Its exact symbol is chi_m(kappa3)^eta chi_m(t)^3 1_((m,z)=1), times the fixed Delta/unit factor. Fix kappa3,z before averaging t. The hole at z is mandatory: a prime of valuation6 has zero original symbol on a source divisible by that prime. Dropping the hole would replace zero by one.

Let l_i1,l_i2,l_iP be the norms extracted by collision labels from the two original inverses and slots on side i; their product is L or R. Ignore additional f shortening only for upper bounds. The original-color pointwise bound is

    S_i=P0/l_iP *[D1/l_i1+D2/l_i2
                              +(D1D2/(l_i1 l_i2))^(2/3)]. (11)

It survives z holes and every fixed collision/f/a0 puncture, since these separate across the actual colors and original slots. It is not a theorem for an arbitrary joint coefficient matrix. In particular S_i<=C S0, S0=P0(D1D2)^(2/3), using s<2r,r<2s.

For fixed kappa3 put B=(H_c/N(kappa3))^(1/3). The short z sum costs B+X_i Z and the long sum B S_i/Z. Clipping Z=sqrt(B S_i/X_i) to[1,sqrt(B)] gives B+sqrt(B S_i X_i) in ALL regimes, including S_i>X_i. After kappa3 summation the column energy is

    A_c+Z_i B_c,
    A_c=H_c^(1/3) C^(2/3), B_c=H_c^(1/6) C^(5/6),
    Z_i=sqrt(S_i X_i).                               (12)

Use (10) with X_i replaced by Z_i, keeping both mixed terms.

Restore (8), O(A) row-divisor labels and all allocations. The following table omits only H_J U^epsilon and records each remaining factor exactly. The two cross rows occur once for each side i, with L_i=L or R.

| Term | U,A,N0 factor | Collision factor | F,q_d factor | Core factor |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SQ0 | U^(1/3+2tau/3) A^-1 N0^(1/3) | Kc^(1/6) D^(-2/3) | F^-1 q_d^(-1/3) | C^(1/3) |
| SQ2 | U^(5/6+tau/6) A^-4 N0^(1/3) | Kc^(-1/3) D^(-2/3) | F^-2 q_d^(-5/6) | C^(5/6) |
| SQ cross i | U^(7/12+5tau/12) A^(-5/2) N0^(1/3) | Kc^(-1/12) D^(-5/12) L_i^(-1/2) | F^(-3/2) q_d^(-7/12) | C^(7/12) |
| CU0 | U^(2/3+tau/3) A^-3 N0^(-1/3) | Kc^(-1/6) D^(-1/3) | F^-1 q_d^(-2/3) | C^(2/3) |
| CU2 | U^(5/6+tau/6) A^-4 N0^(-1/6) | Kc^(-1/3) D^(-5/12)(S_L S_R)^(1/4) | F^(-3/2) q_d^(-5/6) | C^(5/6) |
| CU cross i | U^(3/4+tau/4) A^(-7/2) N0^(-1/4) | Kc^(-1/4) D^(-1/4) L_i^(-1/4) S_i^(1/4) | F^(-5/4) q_d^(-3/4) | C^(3/4) |

All d sums over divisors of E cost a subpower, with positive reciprocal exponents. F^-1 is harmonic up to its polynomial support and divisor losses; every other F exponent is >1. Both independent f allocations and every collision-site allocation are paid by fixed divisor powers before these sums.

All caps needed here are frozen polynomial bounds: q_d Kc<=N(Hcol)<=sqrt(LR), q_a<<U^(1/6), L,R<<N0 and F<<N0. In particular(5) is at most a fixed multiple of U^(2(r+s+v)+tau). Choose each divisor loss after these bounds and the fixed number of coordinates/slots, before all eventual thresholds. No conductor-dependent hidden power is allowed in the arbitrary-sequence sieve contracts.

## 5. Complete collision-label sums, including the limiting four edges

Write h=a+b and k0=1_(a!=b) for one collision prime type. A positive local exponent w means weight N(h_ab)^(-w). Dropping mutual coprimality only enlarges positive majorants after the exact identities.

SQ0 has w=2h/3-k0/6>=7/6. SQ2 has w=2h/3+k0/3>=4/3. Both complete13-label sums converge after small divisor losses. For the left SQ cross, w=5h/12+k0/12+a/2. Its ONLY exponent<=1 is type(0,2), w=11/12. The right cross is its transpose. By(2), their complete cost is at most (G P0)^(1/12)U^epsilon.

CU0 has w=h/3+k0/6. Only(1,1) has exponent2/3 and(2,0),(0,2) exponent5/6. All others exceed1. Its complete cost is at most

    N0^(1/3) (G P0)^(1/3) U^epsilon.                 (13)

For a CU cross, use S_i<=C S0 only here. The left weight is w=(h+a+k0)/4. The deficient types are(1,1) and(0,2), each3/4; type(0,3) is harmonic, and all others exceed1. Its cost is

    N0^(1/4) (G P0)^(1/4) U^epsilon,                 (14)

and the right is transposed. Harmonic/divisor losses are included, not declared convergent.

For CU2 an unchanged S0 bound would leave the type(1,1) sum at exponent5/6 and lose a large power. Instead expand (11) into its three positive components on EACH side and use subadditivity of the quarter power. Before these factors, w=5h/12+k0/3. Every type except(1,1) already has exponent>1. For a type(1,1) prime, a linear D1 component gives an extra1/4 if the prime is in inverse1 or a slot, and zero if it is in inverse2; the D2 component swaps those roles. The geometric component gives1/6 at either inverse and1/4 at a slot.

Thus a term with any geometric component has at worst harmonic exponent1. Both linear components leave exponent5/6 ONLY when the shared prime is in the two omitted inverse sites. Those are exactly the four original cross-copy edges. Equation(2) gives cost H_ij^(1/6), including arbitrary other shared primes and all overlaps. No new edge independence or missing lcm assumption is used; the complete positive label sum is relaxed only after each actual edge's support bound has been applied.

After slot factors, N0^(-1/6) and these label sums, the possible CU2 scale factors are bounded by

    P0^(1/3) *[(D1D2)^(1/6)
                +D1^(1/3)U^(-1/8)
                +D2^(1/3)U^(-1/12)
                +(D1D2)^(1/12)U^(1/10)
                +D1^(1/4)+D2^(1/4)].                (15)

Every displayed term except D2^(1/3)U^(-1/12) is dominated by (D1D2)^(1/6) throughout the physical box. The remaining term is kept and priced separately below. This is where the original same-index H11 cutoff is actually used. Replacing the whole merged coefficient by a generic arbitrary sequence would not supply (11) or this saving.

## 6. Quantitative core caps and complete residual

Use, on each ORIGINAL nominal a0 dyad A,

    C_sq(A)=U^(13/40) A^(24/5),
    C_cu(A)=U^(3/4) A^(24/5).                        (16)

For every collision/hole summand retain the full original kernel up to(5). Apply SQ first, CU outside SQ, then retain HARD when BOTH caps fail. All cores refer to the literal ideal(Delta*ell). This is an exact signed partition of that mask-expanded Poisson expression, not a positive norm assertion. It is independent of the artificial f label. The signed d sum and every original collision label remain in the complementary term.

The A powers of the two second terms become zero, costing only logarithmic dyads. SQ0 gains A^(3/5), SQ cross A^(3/10), CU0 A^(1/5), CU cross A^(1/10). Summing A<<U^(1/6), and including(13)-(14), gives these deliberately coarse bounds:

| Term | Full exponent, bounded on the whole physical box |
|---|---|
| SQ0 | <=161/120+2tau/3 |
| SQ cross | <=263/160+5tau/12 |
| CU0 | <=77/60+tau/3 |
| CU cross | <=431/240+tau/4 |
| SQ2 | 53/48+(r+s+v)/3+tau/6 |
| CU2 geometric | 35/24+(r+s)/6+v/3+tau/6 |
| CU2 remaining linear | 11/8+s/3+v/3+tau/6 |

The first four have positive spare after subtracting from123353/67500 and reserving1/500 for ALL auxiliary losses and1/200 for the retained saving. For the last three compare with delta(r+s)+rho. Their minimum occurs at delta=17/25,r=17/20,s=33/25,v=1/20: the r,s derivatives are positive and the delta derivative is >=21481/24300>0. Raw gaps before tau/6 are respectively

    23813/2730000, 2768/170625, 2768/170625+1/200.

After tau/6, auxiliary1/500 and retained1/200, the first two spares are177/113750 and8241/910000; the third is larger by1/200. All fixed profile, divisor, finite-place, dyadic, height and geometric losses can be divided within that single auxiliary allowance, fixing orders before the eventual U threshold. The original independent height operators, including -W/2-yW', remain in H_J. This inherits rather than repairs positive-slot uniformity.

Let R_N,hard be EXACTLY the Hcol!=1 part of C6 after the paid principal block is removed, written via(3)-(8), with 0<N(ell)<=H_c and BOTH core inequalities in(16) failed. This includes all retained collision-site patterns, the complete signed hole expansion and all original masks. Equations(1)-(16) propose

## 1. Definitions and absolute rearrangements

Fix tau > 0 throughout. For x > 0, put

    g_tau(v) = (2 pi tau)^(-1/2) exp(-v^2/(2 tau)),
    b(l) = (-1)^(l+1),
    S_tau(y) = sum_{l >= 1} b(l) g_tau(log(l/y)),
    A(n) = mu(n) - 2 1_{2|n} mu(n/2),
    G_tau(x) = sum_{n >= 1} A(n) g_tau(log(n/x)).

For every integer Y >= 1, the original cell under review is exactly

    R_{6,Y}(x) = sum_{d,e > Y; (d,e)=1; (de,6)=1}
                    mu(d) mu(e) S_tau(x/(de)).             (1.1)

The lower cuts are strict, the sum is over ordered pairs, and the
Möbius coefficients are not replaced by nonzero surrogates.

Write uniquely

    n = 2^a 3^b q,       (q,6)=1,
    r(n) = rad(q),
    beta(a) = 1 if a=0, and -1 if a>=1.

Use rad(1)=1 and mu(1)=1. The proposed fixed field is

    f_3(n) = mu(rad(n/3^{v_3(n)}))
           = beta(a) mu(rad(q)),
    F_6(x) = sum_{n >= 1} f_3(n) g_tau(log(n/x)).           (1.2)

In particular f_3(n) is always +1 or -1, including prime powers.
The exponent v_3(n) is the exact nonnegative 3-adic valuation.

All label rearrangements below are absolutely justified before
cancellation. The uncut (d,e,l) sum is dominated by

    sum_{n >= 1} d_3(n) g_tau(log(n/x)) < infinity.

For example, for every c > 1,

    g_tau(log(n/x)) <= C_{c,tau} x^c n^(-c),
    C_{c,tau} = (2 pi tau)^(-1/2) exp(tau c^2/2),

and sum d_3(n)n^(-c)=zeta(c)^3 is finite. This also proves local
uniform convergence. No product or height truncation is needed here.

# [private research revision]: a narrow simultaneous-witness target with its complete source return

Accept G137–G139 at the scopes below. The [author](wild56/REPORT.md),
[independent review](wild56-review/report.md) and
[retention manifest](retention-manifest.json) preserve 29 original files
and five immutable mathematical source bindings. Current written
c11=312864909/2500000000=.1251459636 is unchanged. The new arithmetic
hypotheses remain OPEN, as do inherited F0/analytic ancestry, original
positive-slot uniformity and external definition/import/admission.
No formalization, kernel work, new packet or public-record claim follows.

## G137. A restricted inverse moment can pay both witness branches

Use the exact [[private research revision]](../[private research revision]/density-integration.md) family and
[[private research revision]](../[private research revision]/joint-density-integration.md) same-character,
same-zero witness contract. Freeze K=28114053/6250000=4.49824848 from
the accepted c10 SAME-family input; it is not the physical kappa and
is not recalibrated from c11. Keep the original labels, natural holes
and coefficient zeros, independent slot heights, derivative profiles,
positive grades, finite dictionary and common thresholds. A signed
projector does not automatically preserve a joint-witness restriction.

Normalize the free width to 1, write d=delta in[.68,.70], v=z/W, and
retain r<=t, r+m>=t, m<=1/2 from the original witnesses. Their bounds are

    I(r)=1-d r+d[v-(1-r)/2]_+,
    P(m)=1-2d m+d[v-(1-2m)/K]_+,
    L(t)=1/6+(5/6-d)t+d v.

The long inverse branch is bounded by L(t). Put

    u=2d(K-1)/K, alpha=u/(d+u)=2(K-1)/(3K-2),
    D=15K-10-6Kd,
    t_A=(5-6dv)/(5-2d),
    t_B=[15K-10-6d-12d(K-1)v]/D,
    t_*=max(t_A,t_B),
    r_*(t)=min(2t/3,[u t+d(1/K-v)]/(d+u)).

These are the old complete separate-moment cutoff and short crossing.
The minimum of the crossing locations is required because P is the
maximum of its two affine pieces. Near the crossing I is in its
full-fit piece 1-dr. The old short maximum Q_*(t)=1-d r_*(t) is the
maximum of decreasing affine functions with slope magnitudes 2d/3
and d alpha. At t_* it agrees with the long bound E0(1,v).

Fix 0<eta<=.001 and the SAME cutoff t=t_*-eta BEFORE witnesses.
The new hypothesis J_eta^all is a saving eta in the ORIGINAL inverse
moment restricted to actual rows that also carry the large plain
witness of that SAME character and zero, only when

    |r-r_*(t)|<=2eta,   0<=v<=1/20.

After dividing by the inverse spike this gives I(r)-eta. Require it
uniformly in every original source parameter and every actual live
positive child list where it is used. It is not supplied by separate
moments, witness independence, a changed prime pool or the rank-one
shared-zero signal in G115. This hypothesis is OPEN.

Here is its paid implication. Across the plain kink the increasing
function P(t-r) has slopes between u and 2d. If the new crossing moves
left by h, then eta=(d+b_eff)h for b_eff in[u,2d]. Its value falls by
b_eff h>=alpha eta, and h<2eta. Outside the window, the old minimum
has already fallen by at least 2d eta>=alpha eta. This remains valid
beyond adjacent pieces by monotonicity. Thus the entire short maximum
is at most Q_*(t)-alpha eta. Moving t down by eta increases Q_* by at
most (2d/3)eta, while it decreases the long branch by (5/6-d)eta.
On the full d interval,

    alpha-2d/3>=2/15,   5/6-d>=2/15.

Therefore the COMPLETE free-row envelope improves by (2/15)eta W.
Keeping the old cutoff would leave the long branch unchanged and
would not prove this conclusion.

The independent 20-by-25 exact rational interval enclosure covers
d in[.68,.70], v in[0,.05], eta in[0,.001], including both sides of
the plain kink and zero slot width. It verifies the entire length
window has r>1/2, 0<m<1/2, 1<t<3/2 and r+2v<1. The last gate and
r>1/2 also imply 2r+8v<3. Its full-fit reserve exceeds .01017.
The original fine mesh and all finite losses are fixed below positive
reserves before witnesses. Since m>=t-r>t-1>0 in the short regime,
bounded/zero-length plain witnesses cannot create an omitted short
branch; long and unrestricted exceptional cases keep their source bounds.

For raw w=u_core b^6, freeze b, preserve its holes and set
s=log_Z Nb, V=W-6s. Define

    rho=1-10d/[3(5-2d)], k=rho+d-1,
    a_K=d(5-6d)^2/[3(5-2d)D],
    b_K=2d(5-6d)(K-1)/D,
    E0(W,z)=rho W+d z-min(3kz,a_K W+b_K z).

For V>=20W/21 and 0<=z/W<=1/21 the free ratio z/V<=1/20.
The two W-slopes of E0 are rho and rho-a_K, so

    E0(W-6s,z)<=E0(W,z)-6(rho-a_K)s.

Counting all roots costs Z^s. The conditional exponent is therefore

    E0(W,z)-(2/15)eta W
      -[6(rho-a_K-(2/15)eta)-1]s.

The bracket exceeds 1.10376 on the complete box. In the remaining
V<20W/21 range, s>W/126 and the OLD unmarked tail pays the gain with
reserve [(rho-1/6-3k)/21-(2/15)eta]W>.00109398W. Original bounded
free windows and fixed-inducing free cores retain their actual raw
populations and fit this reserve; they are not declared finite raw sets.
Consequently J_eta^all implies the complete source-relative bound

    Z^[E0(W,z)-(2/15)eta W+epsilon] H_J,
    0<=z/W<=1/21.

At eta=.001 the conditional saving is W/7500. A sharper version on
.034<=z/W<=.05 retunes t=t_B-12(K-1)eta/D and gives
C_J eta W, C_J=2(5-6d)(K-1)/D>=7/50. Its narrower hypothesis does
not imply J_eta^all. Both versions and their checks are preserved.

No numerical endpoint is assigned. Every child saving uses its actual
width. Support loss, signed reconstruction, extraction scalars,
amplifiers, local plane, complete physical rectangle, Euler shifts
including zero capacity, principal residues and actual-supremum
feedback still need integration. The unchanged architecture's c<2/15
barrier cannot reach 1/6 or 1/4 by this envelope alone. The decisive
next estimate is the actual inverse moment on this same-zero,
large-plain subset, not another optimization of the old separate bounds.

## G138. Full integral persistence and fixed versus moving readouts

Use the augmented squarefree complex with deg(e_n)=omega(n),
ordered prime-deletion differential and C(x)=0 for x<1. For each odd
squarefree m set b_m=e_(2m), z_m=d b_m=e_m-e_2 wedge d e_m.
Every correction has index 2m/p<m. This gives an integral
unitriangular basis at EVERY real cutoff, with d b_m=z_m and d z_m=0.
Thus the entire persistence module splits into intervals [m,2m) in
augmented degree omega(m), including [1,2) in degree 0 (reduced -1).
Inclusions are identity while an interval survives and zero at death.
This is a direct filtered-basis proof, not an imported barcode theorem.
Classical static topology retains its Björner/W27 attribution.

All logarithmic lifetimes equal log2. The map H(C(x))->H(C(2x)) is
zero, although M(3)=-1. A selection of longer-lived classes deletes
the signal. For fixed alpha in[1/2,1), write

    O_chi(x)=sum_(odd n<=x) mu(n)chi(n),
    R_alpha,chi(x)=O_chi(x)-O_chi(alpha x),
    M_chi(x)=O_chi(x)-chi(2)O_chi(x/2).

Character weighting is an arithmetic readout, not a commuting chain
map. Include chi(2)=0, every natural zero and the n=1 atom. On Re s>1,

    Mellin R=(1-alpha^s)/[s(1-chi(2)2^-s)L(s,chi)].

Both extra factors are nonzero on Re s>0. A COMPLETE every-epsilon
dyadic L2 bound at exponent 2gamma therefore excludes zeros Re s>gamma
for every fixed ordinary character at every height, with common gamma
and character-dependent constants. The left tail vanishes below 1;
dyadic Cauchy–Schwarz pays holomorphy and its derivatives. The principal
pole is a meromorphic point and actual imprimitive factors remain.
Pointwise reconstruction is the finite-for-each-x sum
O_chi(x)=sum_j R_alpha,chi(alpha^j x), costing (1-alpha^gamma)^-1.
Unsigned rank remains [4(1-alpha)/pi^2]x+O(sqrt x).

For T(x)=x-x^(1-eta), 0<eta<1, the arithmetic difference
R_eta(x)=O_chi(x)-O_chi(T(x)) is bounded trivially by x^(1-eta)+1.
Its persistence interpretation starts at x>=2^(1/eta); the initial
bounded interval is paid separately. Iteration until x<2 takes at
most 2+2^(k eta) steps in the dyadic band [2^k,2^(k+1)). Thus a
uniform pointwise R_eta=O(x^gamma), gamma>=0, only gives
O_chi=O(x^(gamma+eta)). The odd constant comparison source proves
this black-box loss can be sharp; it is not a Möbius lower bound.
At eta=1/4 a first gain needs gamma<.6248540364. The trivial .75
readout does not supply it. Keep the signed-window target OPEN.

## G139. A finite detector bank and actual-law audit targets

For the same Gaussian field U_chi, let S U(x)=U(x/2), a=15/8,
b=31/16, D_a=U-a S U and D_b=U-b S U. Retain the literal delayed
coefficient mu(n/2)chi(n/2), including ramification. Exactly

    U=31D_a-30D_b,
    |u-av|^2+|u-bv|^2
      =|u|^2/1861+(1861/256)|v-(976/1861)u|^2.

This sharp two-value algebraic cost is not claimed sharp in the
arithmetic family. The two individual multiplier zero lines differ;
31(1-a2^-s)-30(1-b2^-s)=1 removes their common-zero defect without
division near either zero. A complete positive bank energy at exponent
2gamma gives U energy and its nonvanishing Gaussian Mellin return.
Conversely U energy bounds both bank energies using the adjacent x/2
shell. The fixed bank is equivalent in exponent to U; its arithmetic
moment is OPEN. A moving separation comparable to X^-eta costs eta
in amplitude, 2eta in energy. The generic u=x,v=x/2 example pays this
bill and makes no arithmetic lower-bound claim.

The critic's protected card29 uses the ACTUAL uniform integers 1..N,
a(n)=mu(n)chi(n), K_N=sum|a(n)|^2 and exact prime-valuation cells.
With X_j=E[a|F_j], Delta_j=X_j-X_(j-1),

    K_N/N-|M_chi(N)/N|^2
      =sum_(j<=J) E|Delta_j|^2+E|a-X_J|^2.

The unrevealed residual is mandatory. Revealing all primes<=N makes
it zero. A lower variance bound within O(N^(2gamma-2+epsilon)) of
K_N/N is equivalent to the desired M bound, not an easier consequence
of concentration around an unknown mean. Hermitian 2-by-2 dilation
has the same identity under normalized trace. A useful actual-source
variance estimate remains eligible; Bernoulli independence is not assumed.

The independent uniform card13 gives the exact finite entropy price:
if a finite word space contains the actual word w*, pi(w*)>0 and t>0,
then E(w*)<=[log sum_w pi(w)e^(tE(w))+log(1/pi(w*))]/t.
On a relaxed K-sign source, t=1/(4K) gives partition function<=sqrt2,
but the actual-word mass 2^-K leaves O(K^2), not a subcritical energy.
Fixing every arithmetic constraint makes the class singleton and the
partition bound circular. An intermediate correlated class needs BOTH

and coefficient zeros cannot be omitted.

The other author tests retain the precise relaxed parity/row-span

## Evidence and disposition

## 3. Fixed finite scale filtering cannot remove that leading energy

Fix 0<lambda_1<...<lambda_J and complex coefficients c_j, not all zero. Put

    F_N=sum_(j=1)^J c_j R_floor(lambda_j N).

Take the first nonzero coefficient, relabelled c_1. Choose a fixed B strictly between lambda_1 and min(2lambda_1,lambda_2), interpreting lambda_2=infinity if no later scale exists. On the positive-frequency interval

    floor(lambda_1 N)<k<=BN

for sufficiently large N, only the first source can have a nonzero Fourier coefficient, and its contribution is c_1 mu(k)chi(k)/k^r. Floor errors affect only O(1) endpoints and can alternatively be avoided by choosing a slightly smaller B. Equation(5) therefore gives

    ||F_N||_2^2 >= c(q,r,B,lambda_1)|c_1|^2 N^(1-2r)

for large N, with a strictly positive constant. An upper bound of the same order follows from(7) and the triangle inequality.

There is also a uniform lower constant when sum|c_j|^2=1, allowing the coefficients to depend on N while the finite scales remain fixed. Otherwise take a violating sequence and a convergent subsequence of coefficient vectors. Its limit is nonzero. The difference of the fields has norm o(N^(1/2-r)) by the individual upper bounds, contradicting the just-proved lower bound for the limit vector. Thus

    inf_(sum|c_j|^2=1) ||sum c_j R_floor(lambda_jN)||_2^2
       >=c_(q,r,lambda_1,...,lambda_J) N^(1-2r)       (9)

eventually. No uniform lower constant is asserted as J grows or scales collide. This does not prohibit a growing-order or shrinking-spacing construction; it rules out the actual fixed finite cancellation proposed in this pass, including normalized N-dependent coefficients. It is stronger than observing merely that the scalar coefficient in(7) is positive.

## 3. A uniform canonical column bound with all moving fixed labels

Consider exactly PR9 B3.6, with a0(n)=bar(alpha(n))gamma_2(n), squarefree n, fixed f for the row sum, fixed puncture rho, original product mark d_I(n), and fixed finite-ray nu. Its centrally normalized coefficient has squared mass

    Z^(-N) sum_(n sf) |a0(n)nu(n)rho(n)chi_n(f)^4
                         d_I(n)W(q_n/Z^N)|^2 << Z^epsilon. (7)

For good squarefree n, |a0(n)|=1. A fixed-depth product mark is bounded by a divisor power. The puncture and all natural zeros are contractions. Hence the bound is UNIFORM in the moving fixed f and puncture, without paying their logarithmic widths V,Q in the sieve operator. They may not depend on the currently summed row. Applying(1) and then the exact all-row lift proves

    E(N,V,M) << H_J Z^(E_all(M,N)+epsilon),
    E_all(M,N)=max{M,N+M/6,5M/6+N/3,M/3+5N/6}.        (8)

Here E is the original normalized positive f-average of B3.6. The count of its divisor-bounded nonnegative f-weights is Z^(V+epsilon), canceled by its exact Z^(-V). No second label count occurs. For a sixth-power-free row norm, replace N+M/6 by N; that is a different norm, not a bound asserted for E. Fixed f-dependent column masks also obey the same pointwise-in-f argument, although later source reconstructions retain their own stronger independence requirements.

For M>0 the all-row envelope has the simple exact form

    E_all(M,N)=M                         (0<=N<=M/2),
                5M/6+N/3                 (M/2<=N<=M),
                N+M/6                    (N>=M).       (9)

This is a complete canonical source estimate. In particular E(M/2,V,M)<<Z^(M+epsilon) uniformly over every actual mark and fixed puncture. At N=M, V=M/3, the new cost is7M/6, strictly below the old target F=N+V=4M/3 by M/6. It remains valid, for example, at Q=M, where the old B3.7 sufficient gate F-M-Q-z0>0 is false. This does not refute that older theorem; it supplies a distinct sufficient bound on a specified source in an uncovered parameter region. Whether that region is a bottleneck in the complete physical argument is a separate question.

statement:
## 4. W40-25: metric content of holonomy and a long-cycle obstruction

This is a rank-one projector laboratory, not a model asserted for native H. Let v_0,...,v_m=v_0 be unit vectors in a complex Hilbert space, with all a_j=<v_(j-1),v_j> nonzero. Put

    C=product_(j=1)^m a_j, theta=arg C,
    r_j=|a_j|.

Choose phases u_j of v_j successively so <u_(j-1),u_j>=r_j. Then u_m=exp(-i theta)u_0. Consequently

    4 sin^2(theta/2)=||u_m-u_0||^2
       <=m sum_j ||u_j-u_(j-1)||^2
       =2m sum_j(1-r_j).

Using log r<=-(1-r) proves the exact bound

    |C|<=exp(-2 sin^2(theta/2)/m).                  (W40.13)

An overlap zero already makes C=0; no phase is then assigned. This proof retains the original ordered overlaps, rather than replacing phase by an unexplained spectral gap.

The triangle test corrects a possible overstatement in the seed's objection. For three unit vectors with pairwise overlap magnitudes a,b,c and cyclic phase theta, Gram positivity gives

    1-a^2-b^2-c^2+2abc cos theta>=0.

If a,b,c>=q>0, then

    1-cos theta <=(1-q^2)^2/(2q^3),                (W40.14)

because1-a^2-b^2-c^2+2abc=(1-b^2)(1-c^2)-(a-bc)^2. Thus a fixed nonzero phase on a fixed triangle DOES force metric loss. Merely saying Berry phase has no metric content would be false. A phase tending to0 is a different statement.

The genuinely decisive growing-cycle test is explicit. For N>=3 set

    v_j=(1,exp(2pi i j/N))/sqrt2, 0<=j<=N,
    P_j=v_j v_j*.

Every adjacent overlap is exp(pi i/N)cos(pi/N), including the closing edge. Hence

    C_N=Tr(P_0 P_1 ... P_(N-1))=-cos(pi/N)^N,
    arg C_N=pi,
    |C_N|=1-pi^2/(2N)+O(N^-2).                    (W40.15)

The ordered product operator norm is cos(pi/N)^(N-1), also tending to1. Its nonzero eigenvalue is the same cyclic trace C_N. Exact nontrivial holonomy therefore does not give a uniform contraction once cycle length grows. The N^-1 scale in W40.13 is qualitatively necessary. This is not the earlier scalar-coboundary flatness example: the phase here is genuinely pi.

For a hypothetical exact path representation whose scalar weight FACTORS into at least M cyclic overlap amplitudes C_j times a remaining coefficient, suppose each cycle has length<=m0 and |sin(theta/2)|>=s0>0. Let V_X be the sum of the absolute remaining coefficients. Multiplication of W40.13 would then give

    absolute aggregate <=V_X exp(-2 M s0^2/m0).      (W40.16)

To gain X^-delta from this particular estimate needs M>=delta*m0*log X/(2s0^2). A closed block P_0 P_1 ... P_(m-1) P_0 has norm |C|; an unclosed product generally has a different norm, as W40.15 explicitly shows. Thus the scalar factorization or closed-block premise is essential. This is a conditional toy return, not a claim that native H possesses such paths. Additive H edge sums are not automatically products of projectors.

The actual [private research revision] H object retains quadratic/cubic roots, fixed CRT and angular phases, natural zeros, both projectors, the complete signed short core, independent heights, sharp original supports, every exceptional branch and the far complement. None is represented by P_j here. Before W40.16 can touch H, one must derive an equality or dominated readout with those exact objects and pay the full complementary path mass. No original-prime H deficit is reduced by this laboratory.

Functional signature: ordered rank-one projector cycle; gauge-invariant cyclic product; metric triangle inequality and logarithmic product loss; unpaid native representation and cycle coverage; exact length-dependent laboratory bound and counterexample. U-FLUX and W07 seed15 are explicit ancestors; the claimed delta is the quantitative N-dependent obstruction, not discovery of holonomy.
title: 4. W40-25: metric content of holonomy and a long-cycle obstruction

## Exact algebra in the user's convention

For jz=conj(z)j and j^2=-1, direct multiplication gives

    (A+Bj)(C+Dj) = (AC-B conj(D)) + (AD+B conj(C))j.

Consequently M(q)=[[z,w],[-conj(w),conj(z)]] is multiplicative,
M(conj(q))=M(q)^*, and

    M(q)^* M(q)=N(q) I,  det M(q)=N(q)=|z|^2+|w|^2.

Here N is the squared Euclidean norm, as in the user's notation. Taking
determinants proves N(pq)=N(p)N(q). In particular

    |AC-B conj(D)|^2 + |AD+B conj(C)|^2
      = (|A|^2+|B|^2)(|C|^2+|D|^2).                 (Q1)

These calculations fix the signs and conjugations without relying on
matrix-convention matching. The standard algebraic framework and
norm/determinant correspondence are also in Keith Conrad's
[Quaternion Algebras, section2](https://kconrad.math.uconn.edu/blurbs/ringtheory/quaternionalg.pdf),
consulted13October2026. The arguments below are explicit deductions here,
not claims quoted from that source.

For a nonnegative measure dnu and square-integrable expressions in (Q1),
write E=AC-B conj(D) and T=AD+B conj(C). Integration gives

    integral |E|^2 dnu
      = integral (|A|^2+|B|^2)(|C|^2+|D|^2) dnu
        - integral |T|^2 dnu.                     (Q2)

A certified upper bound P for the first integral and lower bound L for
the complete companion energy give the useful upper bound P-L for the
target. Both bounds must have enough joint precision to leave the desired
remainder. Dropping T gives only P. Thus the concrete opening is an exact
factorization of an actual QRH target with an estimable companion, including
all masks, coefficients, support, heights and residual terms. Positivity
alone supplies neither that factorization nor the required lower bound.

For an arbitrary two-channel lift with the original coefficients in its
first channel, additivity gives the equally exact identity

    N(sum_n (a_n+b_n j))=|sum_n a_n|^2+|sum_n b_n|^2. (Q3)

There is no cancellation between the two nonnegative channel energies.
This does not forbid estimating the pair more effectively through an
additional structure. It specifies what that new estimate must pay.

## R8. All-scale physical return excludes zeros at every height

Fix an ordinary chi and a fixed gamma>2/5. Suppose, for EVERY epsilon>0 and all sufficiently large dyadic X,

    integral_X^(2X)|P_X(x)| dx/x <<_(chi,epsilon) X^(gamma+epsilon). (R8.1)

The stronger condition Q_X<<X^(2gamma+epsilon) implies R8.1 by R6.6 and Cauchy--Schwarz in the shell, whose measure is log 2. Neither is proved. Equation R6.3 first returns R8.1 to ONE fixed M(y), on the complete covering [X/p,2X/p], because its error exponent 2/5 is below gamma.

For Re s>=sigma>gamma, choose epsilon<sigma-gamma and sum the weighted L1 bounds over shells. This proves absolute convergence of integral_1^infinity M(x)x^(-s)dx/x, locally uniform on compact sub-half-planes. Every complex derivative brings a power of log x, absorbed by the strict gap sigma-gamma-epsilon, so the integral is holomorphic at every height. No estimate uniform as |Im s| tends to infinity is needed for that analytic statement.

For 0<x<=1 and n>=1,

    (log n-log x)^2 >= (log n)^2+(log x)^2.

The sum of exp(-(log n)^2/2) is finite. Thus |M(x)| has a Gaussian left tail, and its Mellin integral from 0 to 1 is entire with all logarithmic derivatives. On Re s>1 absolute Fubini and v=log(n/x) give exactly

    integral_0^infinity M(x)x^(-s)dx/x
                         =exp(s^2/2) sum_n a(n)n^(-s)
                         =exp(s^2/2)/L(s,chi).             (R8.2)

The exponential multiplier is nonzero. Meromorphic continuation of the ordinary L-function and the identity theorem now imply that its reciprocal is holomorphic on Re s>gamma. Every zero of L there, including a multiple zero at any height, would give a pole of 1/L and contradict this conclusion. A principal pole at 1 gives a zero of the reciprocal and presents no exception. Natural imprimitive Euler factors were present in the coefficients throughout; no even-modulus atom repair or primitive-conductor substitution occurs.

All parameters delta=3/5, p and h are fixed before X. The proof never Mellin-transforms a field whose caps change with X. It uses the physical recovery to M first, then sums all its shells. It neither interchanges a meromorphic continuation with an uncontrolled theta integral nor chooses theta depending on a zero. No exceptional cofactor set, conductor-uniform inverse or finite-height cutoff remains.

For a useful strip one takes 2/5<gamma<1. A theorem with the same gamma for EVERY ordinary character gives the common conditional constant c=1-gamma; constants and starting scales may depend on that fixed character. A zeta-only estimate gives a zeta-only conclusion. A modulus growing with X is not covered by these character-dependent estimates. The boundary Re s=gamma is not excluded. No Hecke family follows from this ordinary-character calculation.

    alpha=max(gamma tau,gamma(1-tau)) <= a_gamma of(4A.6). (5.1)

This corridor is nonempty: it contains1/2 for gamma>=3/4. In fact tau lies strictly between0 and1, and alpha<1 uniformly for each fixed gamma<1. Let U(n)=B(n)^tau and V(n)=B(n)^(1-tau). With cuts frozen separately for each original n, define

    Q_U(n)=sum_(d e=n,d<=U(n)) a(d)(v*s)(e),
    S_tau(n)=sum_(d e l=n,d<=U(n),e<=V(n)) a(d)a(e)b(l),
    R_tau(n)=sum_(d e l=n,d>U(n),e>V(n)) a(d)a(e)b(l).

Then the EXACT coefficient identity is

    c(n)=Q_U(n)+Q_V(n)-S_tau(n)+R_tau(n).               (5.2)

Proof: expand (a-a_U)*(a-a_V)*b at that n and use a*b=v*s and a*a*b=c. This is an identity with frozen cut values, not one globally fixed-cut convolution. Natural character zeros, all square powers, every ordered pair, strict complements and both short terms are retained.

For Q_U fix d<=X^(gamma tau) and retain both q1 labels e=1,p. Its row is a(d)q1(e) sum_r beta(r)f_x(edr^2)1_(d<=B(edr^2)^tau). Since B decreases, this is one shell-fixed prefix, possibly empty. The stronger COMPLETE cross-row bound (4A.1), with D=X^(gamma tau), gives instead

Apply the same theorem to Q_V with D=X^(gamma(1-tau)). The coefficient at the second physical row is -p chi(p); neither it nor its prefix is merged incorrectly with the first. Condition (5.1) pays both short sources, their square aliases and every cross-row coincidence.

    ||sum_(n>M) v_n f_x(n)||_2^2
      << A_delta^2 [X^((3/2)(1+2delta))+X^6 M^(-4+2delta)]. (5.5)

The diagonal and both cross orientations are included in this positive majorant. Since3/2<=2gamma and6-4r_gamma=2gamma, choose delta after epsilon. Define the literal finite core

    T_tau,p,chi,X(x)=sum_(L<n<=M) R_tau(n) f_x(n),

## 2. A complete direct return, and the proposed code graph

Fix an ordinary Dirichlet character chi modulo q and retain a(n)=mu(n)chi(n), including every squareful/nonunit zero. Let S_q be the squarefree q-units, including1. No ideal/arithmetic-H source is substituted for this rational source. Write M_chi(x)=sum_(n<=x)a(n).

**Matching return.** Suppose there is a disjoint pairing of some members of S_q, with each pair (u,v) satisfying

    a(u)=-a(v),  |u-v|<=C_chi min(u,v)^theta,  0<=theta<1.       (M1)

Finitely many exceptional pairs may be charged separately. Suppose the unmatched count through x is O_(chi,epsilon)(x^(delta+epsilon)) for every epsilon>0, with delta<1. All pairs are in one global pairing; separate unrelated finite-cutoff matchings are not being silently glued.

Every pair wholly below x cancels exactly. A pair crossing x has its lower endpoint in [x-C_chi x^theta,x], so at most C_chi x^theta+1 distinct pairs cross. Coefficient moduli are1. Consequently

    |M_chi(x)| <= C_chi x^theta + O_(chi,epsilon)(x^(delta+epsilon))+O_chi(1).
                                                                  (M2)

Thus a common gamma=max(theta,delta)>0 gives the every-epsilon M bound. For Re(s)>gamma the integral

    F_chi(s)=s integral_1^infinity M_chi(x)x^(-s-1) dx              (M3)

converges locally uniformly with all derivatives: choose the epsilon below the compact's distance to gamma, and absorb powers of log x. On Re(s)>1 it is exactly1/L(s,chi). The identity L F=1 continues meromorphically to the whole half-plane. A regular zero of L there is impossible. A principal pole at1 forces the reciprocal zero and causes no zero-exclusion exception. This covers every finite height and every imprimitive character directly, with its actual Euler-factor zeros retained. Constants/onsets may depend on each fixed chi. No growing-conductor estimate is asserted.

For simultaneous characters modulo a fixed q, sufficient edge conditions are mu(u)=-mu(v) and u=v mod q. They imply a(u)=-a(v) for every character; squareful and nonunit states still have zero mass. The matching hypothesis is OPEN at every improved exponent.

A plausible coded realization uses small symmetric differences of prime sets. For distinct unramified primes p,r,s and a squarefree m coprime to prs,

    u=mp, v=mrs, p=rs mod q
    => mu(u)chi(u)=-mu(v)chi(v).                              (M4)

These are three-coordinate exchanges between incomparable integers. For example6 and11 cancel for all characters modulo5. One-prime toggles are divisibility edges; two-coordinate exchanges preserve mu's sign and cannot cancel the principal source. A three-coordinate exchange is the first possible nondivisibility cancellation of this kind. Its geometric bill is m|p-rs|, not merely the Hamming length3. A complete matching must retain the common-cofactor and coprimality conditions, all unmatched states, and every cutoff crossing.

For targets gamma=.87485,5/6,3/4, M1-M2 with theta,delta<=gamma would give respectively c=.12515,1/6,1/4. The first would exceed c11 by10091/2500000000. These are conditional numerical returns; no matching input is supplied. The point of the next result is that **fixed code radius cannot supply the required absolute unmatched budget**, even if the codewords and flow coefficients are otherwise arbitrary.

## 6. Uniform audit W44-12: actual code fibres, not uniform bits

Let P be k primes and x their binary presence vector, u=(1,...,1). For a full-row-rank binary syndrome matrix A and weights w(x), Fourier expansion of the exact fibre indicator gives

    sum_(Ax=s)(-1)^(u.x)w(x)
       =2^-ell sum_(lambda in F2^ell)(-1)^(lambda.s)
                         hat w(u+A^T lambda),          (R20)

where `hat w(v)=sum_x(-1)^(v.x)w(x)`. Uniform fibres annihilate parity precisely when u is outside the row space, but for actual cutoff/Gaussian weights R20 asks for the indicated high-order Fourier coefficients. The dual-distance assertion alone does not make them zero.

Use the literal all-integer prime-presence factor with **P={2,5,7}**:

    a_P(n)=product_(p in P)(1-2*1_(p|n)),
    S(n)=1_(2|n).

The code syndrome is the first coordinate, so u=(1,1,1) is outside its row space. In the fictitious uniform bit cube each fibre has parity sum zero. In the actual residue system mod70, however, each syndrome has 35 residues and

    sum_(1<=n<=70, S(n)=0)a_P(n)=15,
    sum_(1<=n<=70, S(n)=1)a_P(n)=-15,
    E[a_P|S=s]=(-1)^s*(1-2/5)*(1-2/7)=(-1)^s*3/7.   (R21)

CRT gives independent Bernoulli occupation probabilities 1/p, not 1/2. With uniform residue measure the best mean-square decoder q(S) is this conditional expectation. Therefore

    inf_q E|a_P-q(S)|²=1-9/49=40/49.                 (R22)

This is an exact statement on an actual arithmetic partial-sign factor. It is not a bound on the complete f3 Gaussian field. It also allows the precise comparison that a small-dimensional syndrome is a substantial-loss representation of this partial parity, even though its uniform-cube fibre sums vanish.

The same bias and residual have a direct physical Gaussian meaning. Extend `h(t)=g_tau(log t)` by zero on t<=0; it is Schwartz and flat at zero. Fixed-period Poisson summation gives, for every residue a mod70 and every prescribed A>0,

    sum_(n>=1, n=a mod70)h(n/x)
       =x e^(tau/2)/70+O_(A,tau)(x^-A).               (R23)

Here `integral_0^infinity h(t)dt=e^(tau/2)` and arbitrary Fourier decay pays the nonzero frequencies. Dividing by `Z(x)=sum_n h(n/x)=x e^(tau/2)+O_A(x^-A)` transfers R21/R22 to this actual positive Gaussian occupation law, with superpower-small error. This uses a fixed period and makes no growing-coordinate or conductor claim.

Finally restore the full source rather than identifying a_P with f3. For any fixed ordinary chi, including its natural zeros, put

    r_P(n)=f3(n)a_P(n)chi(n),
    b_x(S)=E_x[a_P|S], c_x(S)=E_x[r_P|S],

where E_x uses the normalized positive Gaussian law at the physical x. Then exactly

    F_(f3 chi)(x)/Z(x)
       =E_x[b_x(S)c_x(S)]
          +E_x[(a_P-b_x(S))(r_P-c_x(S))].              (R24)

Every integer, prime power, sign, ramified zero and unexposed tail term remains in r_P. The second term is the full conditional covariance, not zero by code orthogonality. The first term can also cancel; neither term may be substituted for the full square moment. Writing Q(x) for the entire right side, the exact remaining target is

    integral_X^(2X) |Q(x)|² dx/x <<_epsilon X^(2gamma-2+epsilon).

With all mixed square terms retained and every sufficiently large dyadic X covered, this is equivalent to the original complete Gaussian squared-moment exponent2gamma, because Z(x) is asymptotic to a positive constant times x. This is a restated exact target, not a new estimate.

An exact independent residue check confirms R21/R22. With the literal f3 and zero-extended real character mod3 on n<=70, the finite analogue of R24 has full mean `-3/70`, predictable part `9/490` and conditional covariance `-3/49`; these add exactly. It demonstrates that the covariance is present, not its infinite-scale size. G54/W41 and W38 already own the general parity/occupation obligation; the new audit is this explicit binary-code source instance and quantified partial-sign loss. **Disposition:** uniform-fibre annihilation fails for the arithmetic law. A restricted decoder with a new bound for both terms in R24 remains open, and no full-f3 lower bound is claimed.

statement:
## UR3. Pole cofactor: exact expansion, nontriviality and multiplicities

Direct expansion of the 3 by 3 determinant gives

    D_delta=C_delta F+E_delta,
    C_delta=F(s+2delta)F(s+4delta)-F(s+3delta)^2,
    E_delta=-F(s+delta)^2F(s+4delta)
            +2F(s+delta)F(s+2delta)F(s+3delta)
            -F(s+2delta)^3.

This agrees with D7, including all three complementary terms. A second two-column Cauchy--Binet identity yields

    C_delta(s)=sum_(m<n) a(m)a(n)(mn)^(-s-2delta)
                                      (m^(-delta)-n^(-delta))^2.

Let rho be fixed with sigma=Re rho>4/5, and let p be the least prime not dividing the specified modulus. It is also the least integer n>1 with a(n) nonzero. For real delta tending to infinity, the `(1,p)` summand is

    -chi(p)p^(-rho-2delta)(1-p^(-delta))^2.

It dominates the entire remaining series, not only finitely many initial terms. For `(1,n)` with n>=p+1, divide the elementary tail bound

    sum_(n>=p+1) n^(-sigma-2delta)
      <=(p+1)^(-sigma-2delta)
                       [1+(p+1)/(sigma+2delta-1)]

by the leading magnitude. The result tends to zero geometrically. For m>=p, the remaining sum is bounded by

    1/(sigma+2delta-1) sum_(m>=p) m^(1-2sigma-6delta).

After division by `p^(-sigma-2delta)`, this is at most

    p^(1-sigma-4delta)/(sigma+2delta-1)
                 [1+p/(2sigma+6delta-2)]

for sufficiently large delta, up to the factor `(1-p^(-delta))^(-2)` tending to one. It also tends to zero. These estimates permit constants depending on the fixed p and rho; no height-uniform lower bound has been inferred.

As a function of complex delta, `C_delta(rho)` is analytic in the connected half-plane where `Re(rho+j delta)>1`, j=2,3,4. This domain contains I and all sufficiently large positive real delta. The preceding asymptotic proves that it is not identically zero. Its real zeros on I are isolated, hence measure zero. This works for imprimitive characters with their specified modulus, not just their primitive conductor.

The only useful wording precision is to express the pole statement by its leading Laurent term. If

    F(s)=b_(-m)(s-rho)^(-m)+O((s-rho)^(-m+1)), b_(-m)!=0,

then, when `C_delta(rho)!=0`, D has leading term

    C_delta(rho)b_(-m)(s-rho)^(-m).

This is the exact multiple-zero statement. It does not identify the complete residue of a higher-order pole with that one factor; derivatives of C may affect lower Laurent coefficients. This precision requires no change in the author's theorem or exponent.

    U(x)=V_(a,T)(x)+H_(a,b,T)(x)+Z_(a,b,T)(x)+R_(b,T)(x), (R22)
    V=(1/(2pi i)) integral_(a-iT)^(a+iT)M(s)x^s ds,
    H=(1/(2pi i))[integral_(a+iT)^(b+iT)M(s)x^s ds

The signs follow by orienting the right side upward, top leftward, left downward and bottom rightward. The principal pole of L at1 gives a ZERO of1/L, not a residue. Conservation of flux therefore does not set it to zero. For canonical F the additional N_chi H_chi is nonzero at every candidate with1/2<Re rho<1; its Re1 zeros still require the existing right boundary.

The COMPLETE right-line height tail is cheap without a new arithmetic premise. Absolute reciprocal coefficients on b give |1/L(b+it)|<=zeta(b). Gaussian tail integration yields

          <=C_(b,tau) X^b T^-1 exp(-tau T^2/2).    (R24)

For target gamma<1 and delta>0, choose any boundary-admissible

Neither reciprocal integral is bounded here at a proposed new target. Boundary admissibility alone does not control a near-zero denominator. The complete residue sum, with multiplicities, remains. A FIXED nonempty finite residue packet with maximal real part sigma_*>gamma cannot itself be O(X^gamma) on all shells. Let d be the largest m-1 among its roots with real part sigma_*. In u=log x, division by e^(sigma_*u)u^d leaves a nonzero finite leading exponential sum with distinct frequencies Im rho. On an interval of length log2 its weighted Gram matrix is positive definite: vanishing on an interval forces every coefficient0 by differentiation/Vandermonde. Modulating the coefficients by e^(i Im(rho)log X) preserves their Euclidean norm. The smallest FIXED Gram eigenvalue gives a positive lower bound; lower-real-part/lower-degree terms vanish after normalization. Thus this fixed packet has norm>=c X^sigma_*(log X)^d for all sufficiently large X. This is conditional on those zeros' existence, not an assertion that such zeros exist. Its constants are NOT uniform as T, the number of zeros or their separation changes; it supplies no all-height lower bound for the growing T_X packet.

The correct gluing target is the COMPLETE V+H+Z, differing from U only by(R24). Its signed bound below theta6 would suffice and is equivalent in exponent to the original U problem. ## 3. Independent reconstruction of the actual square-short input

The relevant accepted source is [restricted research revision]'s FULL single-square proof (author Section4, reviewer Section4), with its explicit fixed-phase continuation (author Section8, reviewer final discussion). It is not the specialized degree6 collision bound alone.

For fixed mean-zero Q0-periodic beta, 1<=a0<=pX^alpha0 with fixed alpha0<1, and every frozen root prefix R in [0,infinity], set F=(X/a0)^k and R0=c0 F^(1/(2k-1)). On r<=R0 each nonzero Fourier phase has derivative

    j/Q0 - (k/pi)(a0/x)^k r^(2k-1).

Choose c0 fixed so the correction stays below 1/(4Q0), including the final increment. R0 tends to infinity uniformly; a finite initial X range enters the constant. Discrete first derivative and Abel summation pay the complete low prefix by O(1), using the actual exp(-a0 r^2/x^b) and the exact endpoint min(R,R0).

For the entire remaining root prefix, a smooth nonnegative majorant of the original x shell and two integrations by parts give the full kernel

    exp(-c a0(r^2+s^2)/X^b)
       min(1,[F/|r^(2k)-s^(2k)|]^2).

The diagonal is O(X^(b/2)a0^-1/2). For r>s>R0, the difference is at least r^(2k-1)(r-s); summing all positive gaps and then r costs

    F sum_(r>R0) r^(-(2k-1)) << F^(1/(2k-1)).

Both orientations, all high roots and the low/high cross term are paid. Arbitrary prefix R only restricts a positive absolute upper bound; it is not a signed norm monotonicity claim. If b>=2k/(2k-1), then for a0>=1 this high off-diagonal price is at most the diagonal price. Therefore

    ||sum_(r<=R) beta(r) f_x(a0 r^2)||_(1,2)
        << 1+X^(b/4)a0^-1/4.                             (3.1)

At b=3/2,k=12 the condition is 3/2>=24/23. The literal source has beta(r)=chi(r)^2(1-p 1_(p|r)), period pq, mean zero, natural zeros retained. It has physical multipliers d and pd with coefficients 1 and -p chi(p), respectively. Applying (3.1) to BOTH rows and summing d<=D gives

    ||Q_D||_(1,2) << D+X^(3/8)D^(3/4).                  (3.2)

Every required root prefix, including infinity, is permitted. For D=X^(5/12), the two exponents are 5/12 and 11/16, both below 5/6. No assertion f_x(pn)=f_(x/p)(n) is used; that scaling would be false for b>1.

### 4.2 Both-short bound under the fixed pair mask

Extend h(t)=g_tau(log t) for t>0 by h(t)=0 for t<=0.
The Gaussian beats every power at both t=0 and t=infinity after
any fixed number of derivatives, so h is Schwartz and flat at zero.
For Fourier transform hhat(xi)=integral_R h(t)exp(-2 pi i t xi)dt,
Poisson summation with the alternating character gives

    S_tau(y) = -y sum_{k in Z} hhat(y(k+1/2)).             (4.3)

There is no zero frequency. For each fixed M>1, Schwartz decay
and summability of |k+1/2|^(-M) imply

    |S_tau(y)| <= C_{M,tau} y^(1-M),       y>=1.

Equivalently, for each fixed A>0,

    |S_tau(y)| <= C_{A,tau} y^(-A),        y>=1.           (4.4)

Now take X>=1, x in [X,2X], theta=.495 and
Y=Y_X=floor(X^theta). Then

    x/(de) >= X/Y^2 >= X^(.01) >= 1

for d,e<=Y. Taking absolute values only after completing each
alternating l-sum yields

    |B_Y(x)| <= C_{A,tau} Y^2 (X/Y^2)^(-A)
             <= C_{A,tau} X^(.99-.01 A).                 (4.5)

The pair mask (d,e)=1, (de,6)=1 and the Möbius signs are fixed
independently of l, so this argument is valid under that mask.
It does not assert inheritance under an arbitrary l-dependent mask.
For any prescribed N>0, choose A>=100(N+.99); then

    sup_{X<=x<=2X}|B_{Y_X}(x)| <<_{N,tau} X^(-N).        (4.6)
