statement:
# W67 independent review: exact representations and a cofactor-resolved residual



## Decision

Accept the author's three surviving components with their stated scopes: the exact squarefree character inverse and conditional Mertens-energy return; the completely masked Walsh representation and paid Gaussian complements; and the normalization/defect bill for a unitary dilation. None proves an arithmetic saving. The signed local transfer has no singular-value advantage over its absolute gate; indefinite conserved flux does not control its expanding null vector; a Cayley transform retains its inverse observation cost. These are limited obstructions, not impossibility theorems for complete signed sources.

The Gaussian Walsh result is a principal/zeta source result. It is not an all-character extension of that detector. The twisted matrix is complex symmetric in general, not Hermitian. The inverse-entry estimate remains the original arithmetic estimate in different coordinates. Current c11=312864909/2500000000=.1251459636, theta11=.8748540364, is unchanged, with its inherited F0, positive-slot and external-admission obligations open.

The independent addition gives a cofactor formula and weighted residual certificate, plus an N/log N absolute prime obstruction to its simplest truncation. Constructing a better complete certificate remains open; neither a zero-free gain nor literature priority is claimed.

Two corrections concern evidence labels rather than the identities: the author's cited parity-syndrome discussion is in the closing discussion of G174, immediately before G175; and its complex-character helper uses the conjugate convention to its displayed matrix. The latter tests the conjugate character from the same family, but is not literally the displayed chi-labelled identity. Our independent check uses the displayed convention.

## Blind sequence and sampling

exposure.md declares extensive previous QRH/W64/W66 exposure and no remembered direct W67 outcomes. Complete seeds and the index through [private research revision] preceded preparation; the [private research revision] delta was read after audits. No fresh-context claim is made.

The frozen priority and independent uniform permutation both range over all 30 cards. After root's sole final wake, the author selection-only records revealed six tested cards: S02, S27, S15, S11, S24, S21. The first unselected priority card was S28; the first distinct unselected card in the saved uniform order was S09. audit-selection.json froze these choices. Both were developed, completely read and frozen at 03:36:53 UTC before the author report was first read. No redraw, author-outcome-based substitution, or wildcard reservation occurred. audits.md SHA256 248777cbe248d03d27b7fffcc38910a32f60cc8ca7250debeb91c61562db79e6 and audit-freeze.json SHA256 cd7c206dad2524ebd803f5310f8fcf08678f6d358c1a8eb13e0dae5f61296daf bind the pre-outcome findings.

The author's eight pre-draw duplicate screens were expressly allowed by its original assignment; they are not a hidden numerical-group restriction. Its eligible pools have sizes 18,10,17 and span every eligible group under the literal thresholds. Saved rejection draws choose S11,S24,S21. The review replay is deterministic and requests no entropy. Subjective generation typicality is not truth probability, and uniform card sampling is not uniform sampling over mathematics. The original incoherent entropy-only S30 branch remains in the seeds.

## 1. Reconstructing the arithmetic inverse

Fix an ordinary Dirichlet character chi modulo q, including the principal character. Let S={a<=N: mu(a) is nonzero and (a,q)=1}. This divisor-closed set removes natural zeros before inverses are taken; it is not a replacement of chi at ramified primes. Order S increasingly and let E_ad=1_{d|a}, M=diag(mu(a)). Then E^{-1}=MEM, because the squarefree divisor interval is a Boolean lattice. Thus

    C=E M E^T,             C_ab=1_{(a,b)=1},
    K=M C M,               K_ab=mu(ab),
    K^{-1}=E^T M E,        (K^{-1})_ab=sum_{d in S, [a,b]|d} mu(d).

All factors are finite and invertible. C and K have inertia given by the positive and negative diagonal entries of M, by real congruence, and determinant product_{a in S} mu(a). In particular (K^{-1})_11 is the principal-character Mertens sum. Multiplying K on both sides by diag(chi(a)) does not change its inverse (1,1) entry and therefore does not create the desired twist.

The author's correct twisted construction is instead

    A_chi = E diag(mu(d) conjugate(chi(d))) E^T,
    (A_chi)_ab = product_{p|(a,b)} (1-conjugate(chi(p))),
    (A_chi^{-1})_ab
      = mu(a)mu(b) sum_{d in S,[a,b]|d} mu(d)chi(d).            (1)

The inverse diagonal factor is mu(d)chi(d), since |chi(d)|=1 on S. Multiplication by E^{-1} gives the displayed sign, with no complex conjugation silently introduced into E^T. Consequently (A_chi^{-1})_11=M_chi(N). For complex chi this is a symmetric bilinear construction; neither Hermitian inertia nor a unitary Cayley transform follows.

The Schur warning is real: at N=2 in the principal case, K=[[1,-1],[-1,0]] is invertible and its inverse (1,1) entry is zero, while the nuisance block [0] is singular. A Schur formula requiring that block's inverse is unavailable. Conversely, exact rank alone does not prohibit approximation: on m distinct prime labels the subblock is J-I, of full rank m for m>=2, yet rank-one J has operator error 1 and scalar error at most ||u|| ||v||. These are compatible facts.

The energy assumption

    integral_1^X |(A_chi,floor(t)^{-1})_11|^2 dt/t
      <<_{chi,epsilon} X^{2 gamma+epsilon}                   (2)

for every epsilon>0 and all sufficiently large dyadic X gives a normally convergent Mellin integral s integral_1^infinity M_chi(t)t^{-s-1}dt on Re(s)>gamma, by Cauchy on each dyadic shell. In Re(s)>1 it is 1/L(s,chi); analytic continuation excludes zeros throughout Re(s)>gamma. For the principal character s=1 is a pole of L and a zero of its reciprocal, not an excluded zero. Compact subsets, hence every finite height, are covered without a height cutoff; constants may depend on the fixed character and compact set. There is no conductor-uniform assertion. This is a valid return from (2), but (2) is literally Mertens energy, not a newly proved estimate.

Redheffer's determinant provides relevant ancestry, not this exact A_chi formula: the classical matrix with entries 1 when i|j or j=1 has determinant M(n), as recorded in [Vaughan's primary paper, introduction](https://personal.science.psu.edu/rcv4/personal/Publications/REDCONF.pdf). No eigenvalue theorem from that paper is needed or imported here.

## 2. Independent development: cofactor-resolved residual transfer

For squarefree a,b in S put g=(a,b), l=[a,b], and define the literal cofactor sum

    M_{chi,lq}(y)=sum_{m<=y,(m,lq)=1} mu(m)chi(m).

Writing d=lm in (1), squarefreeness forces (m,l)=1. Since mu(a)mu(b)mu(l)=mu(g), exact complete entries are

    (A_chi^{-1})_ab = mu(g)chi(l) M_{chi,lq}(N/l).             (3)

The right side is zero when l>N. In particular the entire first row is

    R_chi,N(a)=chi(a) M_{chi,aq}(N/a),     |R_chi,N(a)|<=N/a.  (4)

This is an identity for finite coprimality masks, not a claim of uniform estimates for growing-conductor L-functions. Large labels are short cofactor sums; small labels can retain the original hard arithmetic.

For any proposed approximate column z on S, with its COMPLETE residual r=e_1-A_chi z, the exact reconstruction is

    M_chi(N)=z_1 + sum_{a in S} R_chi,N(a) r_a,
    |M_chi(N)-z_1| <= N sum_{a in S} |r_a|/a.                 (5)

No projection or residual coordinate can be omitted. If r is supported on a>N/H, H>=1, (5) is at most H||r||_1. Thus a full global inverse norm is an unnecessarily expensive default bill for residuals concentrated at large labels. The stronger exact signed residual sum in (5) remains available; its absolute majorant is only a sufficient certificate.

A precise sufficient open input is: for every fixed ordinary chi, every epsilon>0 and every sufficiently large integer N, construct z=z_{chi,N,epsilon} on the ACTUAL S such that

    |z_1| + N sum_{a in S} |(e_1-A_chi z)_a|/a
       <<_{chi,epsilon} N^{gamma+epsilon}.                  OPEN-RES

This implies the pointwise Mertens bound and the same all-height zero exclusion as above. First improvement requires gamma<.8748540364; gamma=5/6 and gamma=3/4 are the conditional 1/6 and 1/4 targets. No vector satisfying this budget is constructed. An algorithm computing the exact inverse is not evidence that its observed coordinate is small. The criterion remains hard even though its residual payment is more precise.

The cheapest candidate demonstrates the danger. Set

    z_T=E^{-T}(chi(d) 1_{d<=T})_{d in S},   1<=T<=N.

Then z_T,1=M_chi(T) and

    r_T(a)=1_{a=1}-sum_{d|a,d<=T}mu(d)
          =sum_{d|a,d>T}mu(d).                               (6)

Residual support is indeed confined to a>T. But for T<=N/2 and primes p in (N/2,N] not dividing q, r_T(p)=-1 and R_chi,N(p)=chi(p). Therefore

    sum_a |R_chi,N(a)r_T(a)| >= #{N/2<p<=N : p does not divide q}
                               ~ N/(2 log N).               (7)

The weaker explicit budget in (5) is at least as large. The ordinary prime number theorem suffices; only finitely many excluded primes divide fixed q. [DLMF 27.12.4-5](https://dlmf.nist.gov/27.12) records this classical asymptotic. The same conclusion holds for a cutoff <=beta N with any fixed beta<1 after shortening the prime interval. Equation (7) is an absolute-price obstruction for this specified truncation, NOT a lower bound for the signed residual, M_chi, or a general certificate. This preserves the real opportunity: construct a residual aligned with the actual signs, or eliminate the prime residual through a new complete arithmetic correction while paying every new coordinate.

Six finite exact matrix cases, q=1 and the quartic character modulo 5 at N=2,12,24, independently verify the literal displayed convention, (3), and (6)'s reconstruction for T=1,floor(N/2),N. Arithmetic values are small Gaussian integers, exactly represented; the algebra above supplies the general proof. No unchanged author diagnostic was rerun.

## 3. Fully masked Gaussian Walsh transform

This development uses the existing principal Gaussian coprime source G25-G30, not the new Liouville source or a Hecke-family source. Fix tau>0. Put Y=floor(X^.495), B_X=2X exp(C sqrt(log X)), and use the finite prime set 5<=p<=B_X. For squarefree incidence labels u,v with d(u),d(v) their products, the actual gate is

    K(u,v)=(-1)^{|u|+|v|}1_{u and v have disjoint prime support}.

The full mask W_x retains d(u)>Y, d(v)>Y, d(u)d(v)<=B_X and the entire sum

    sum_{l<=B_X/(d(u)d(v))} (-1)^{l+1}
              g_tau(log(d(u)d(v)l/x)).

Thus Z=sum_{u,v} K(u,v)W_x(u,v) is exactly the output-truncated ordered-pair source. No squarefree, shared-prime, small-prime, endpoint, sign or l-factor is changed. With the unnormalized two-variable Walsh transform on k primes,

    Z=2^{-2k} sum_{alpha,beta} Khat(alpha,beta) What_x(alpha,beta). (8)

For the signed one-prime gate T=[[1,-1],[-1,0]] and H=[[1,1],[1,-1]], H T H=[[-1,1],[1,3]]. Every local transformed entry is nonzero. Orthogonality proves (8), not sparsity of the complete arithmetic mask. The huge global prime set is part of the identity and is not replaced by the much smaller set dividing one integer.

The complements are quantitatively paid. The full output coefficient has a d_3 majorant. Uniformly for every real x in [X,2X], the discarded Gaussian tail n>B_X is

    |P_Y(x)-Z(x)| <= X^{1-C^2/(2 tau)+o(1)}.

This follows by logarithmic substitution in the Gaussian tail, including the counting Jacobian; the term C sqrt(log X) is absorbed into the o(1) exponent. Fix C large enough that this exponent is strictly below the chosen gamma>1/2. G27 gives the complete source comparison |P_Y-F_6| << X^{.495+delta} with fixed delta<gamma-.495. All parameters are fixed before the shell variable varies. Finite initial X is harmless in the Mellin return.

The last fixed Euler convolution in G28 must also stay present. At p=2,3 its direct factor is (1-z)^2 with inverse (1-z)^{-2}; at p>=5 it is (1-z)^2/(1-2z) with inverse (1-2z)/(1-z)^2. The infinite-prime factors start in degree two, and 2/sqrt(5)<1, giving absolute coefficient convergence in every Re(s)>1/2 for both directions. The exceptional p=2 coefficients in the original source are 1,-3,2; they are not silently changed to an ordinary squarefree factor. Apply these fixed convolutions to fixed complete fields, not to a prime set or cutoff that changes with the integration variable.

Accordingly an every-epsilon COMPLETE shell L2 bound of size X^{gamma+epsilon} for (8), on every large dyadic shell and with dx/x, transfers by triangle and the fixed convolution to the original Gaussian field. Its exact Mellin multiplier exp(tau s^2/2)(1-2^{1-s})/zeta(s) yields the G3 conclusion gamma<Re(s)<1. The compensator is nonzero there; the line Re(s)=1 is handled only by the inherited classical boundary statement, with s=1 the principal pole exception. Compact-strip normal convergence covers every finite height. This is a valid conditional zeta return; it does not supply a gain for every ordinary character without an actual corresponding character-source theorem and bound.

Neither the entire dual sum nor its required exponent has been estimated. A Cauchy bound after Walsh is not new cancellation, and a subset of transformed modes is not a bound for the full signed contraction. The actual contribution is an exact alternative place to formulate the open estimate with its tails already priced.

## 4. Dilation, flux and observation costs

If A=alpha P U Q where U is unitary and P,Q contractions, alpha>=||A|| follows directly. For a contraction C the Halmos dilation

    U_C=[[C,(I-CC*)^{1/2}],[(I-C*C)^{1/2},-C*]]

is unitary, so alpha=||A|| is achievable for a single finite operator after normalization. This is standard, independently checked against [Robinson, Theorems 1-2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1803.09329). It removes no arithmetic norm. Repeated compression must retain the returning defect: for selfadjoint C, U_C^2=I while C^2=I-(I-C^2). Thus compression of the second power is not the square of the first compression. The author's scalar matrix residual bound and complete-mask Frobenius alternative are correct when all defect and boundary terms remain included.

For S11, diagonal sign gauge relates T to the unsigned disjointness gate [[1,1],[1,0]], so their singular values agree. This refutes an automatic local singular-radius improvement, not cancellation after arithmetic boundary contraction.

For S15 the exact indefinite metric J=[[-2,-1],[-1,2]] satisfies T^T J T=-J; hence T^2 preserves J. The eigenvector (phi,-1), phi=(1+sqrt(5))/2, has zero J-flux and expands by phi under T. Conserved indefinite flux alone cannot bound its positive coordinate observation. This is an actual local-gate counterexample to the stated inference, not a theorem that every indefinite arithmetic construction fails.

For S21 a finite selfadjoint K has unitary V=(K-iI)(K+iI)^{-1}, but

    (I-V)^{-1}=(I-iK)/2,
    ||(I-V)^{-1}||=sqrt(1+||K||^2)/2.

Thus the observation inverse retains growth. For the general complex A_chi above, the selfadjoint hypothesis is absent. No dissipativity theorem or continuation is licensed merely by writing a Cayley expression.

## 5. Pre-outcome audits and novelty

Protected S28 gives an exact orthogonal diagonalization of the coprimality tensor, with eigenvalues (-1)^j phi^{k-2j}, multiplicity binomial(k,j), gate condition number phi^{2k}, and basis condition number 1. The full transformed boundary remains in audits.md; its generic Frobenius bill is 3^{k/2}||W||_F. A product-only mask generates mu(n)chi(n)2^{omega(n)}, not the Mertens coefficient. The subpower cost on ONE divisor cube cannot be transferred to the global prime set. The golden-ratio local spectrum is already in W01/W09; the useful audit content is the full boundary and cost accounting.

Uniform S09 reuses G165's exact prime-adjoining constraints. Their kernel on the connected squarefree q-unit graph is span(a), a_v=mu(v)chi(v). For any complete detector w, the unit coefficient in an exact tree certificate is forced to be M_w=sum w_v a_v, and

    inf_{lambda,t} [|lambda|+||w-lambda e_1-B^T t||_1]=|M_w|.

The lower bound pairs with the unimodular kernel vector; the upper bound uses its annihilator. audits.md proves the full subtree formula and approximate-constraint price. This warns against hiding the target in a certificate; it does not prohibit constructive arithmetic certificates. False periodicity was not introduced.

The reviewed index and ancestry already contain variational/Schur formulations, transfer compensation, parity blindness, exact prime-adjoining constraints, Hankel realizations and finite Cayley observations. ### 1.6 Band signs, terminal tail, and scope

If u=(1-rho)/rho is in (1,2), then

    B(rho)=2log u-3-4/u-1/u^2<2log 2-21/4<0,
    B'(rho)=-2/(1-rho)-2/rho
                 -2/(1-rho)^2-2/(1-rho)^3<0.

Thus R_(X^rho) is eventually negative uniformly on any stated compact
rho interval. For fixed 1/3<a<b<1/2, exact coefficient subtraction
gives

    T_(X^b)-T_(X^a)=R_(X^a)-R_(X^b)
      =C_f exp(tau/2)[B(a)-B(b)]x/L^3
        +O(X/L^4+X^(1-eta)L)>0.                       (R1.13)

For a=3/8,b=2/5 the positive factor is exactly

    B(a)-B(b)=79/225+2log(10/9)=.5618321424267637... .

The decimal is only an evaluation of an already positive closed
formula. It is not evidence for an asymptotic. For every fixed c>1/2,
omega_(X^c)(n)>=2 implies n>X^(2c), so (R0.2) proves

    R_(X^c)(x)=O_A(X^-A).                              (R1.14)

It follows without a complete-field bound that the band from any
fixed a in (1/3,1/2) to any fixed c>1/2 is NEGATIVE of order X/L^3.
There is no finite terminal threshold for the uncapped Gaussian;
(R1.14) is a full-tail bound instead.

The previous [private research revision] subpower range stops at
log z<=L/(1000log L); its actual bands have the opposite sign in the
specified comparison. No interpolation between the two theorems has
been proved. Below rho=1/3 the third rough prime can enter the central
source. At rho=1/2 the growing complete reciprocal-core approximation
used in (R1.12) is no longer uniform. Neither boundary is included in
(R1.1).

statement:
## 1. The balanced Möbius energy: coincidences and large internal gcd

Use exactly T09's fixed profile
\[
V(u)=e^{-u-u^{-1}},\qquad \phi(u)=(uV(u))'
 =(1-u+u^{-1})e^{-u-u^{-1}},
\]
and its frozen dyad cutoffs
\[
L=\log X,\quad Y=\lfloor\sqrt X/L^2\rfloor,\quad
T_l=X/L^4,\quad T_u=XL^2,\quad J=\lceil8L^6\rceil.
\]
Write \(w_X(q)=\rho(q/T_l)\chi(q/T_u)\), with the original cutoffs
\(0\le w_X\le1\). T09.2 has already proved, with full endpoint and
fixed-derivative control,
\[
S_\phi(x)=\mathcal B_X(x)+O_A(X^{-A}),\qquad X\le x\le2X.
\]
No cutoff varies with \(x\) in the arguments below.

### Exact coalescence of all product coincidences

Define
\[
A_Y(q)=\sum_{\substack{de=q\\d,e>Y}}\mu(d)\mu(e),\qquad
\beta_X(n)=\sum_{\substack{\ell\mid n\\\ell\le J}}
w_X(n/\ell)A_Y(n/\ell).
\]
Then \(\mathcal B_X(x)=\sum_n\beta_X(n)\phi(n/x)\) exactly.
The coefficient \(A_Y(q)\) vanishes unless \(q\) is cube-free. Otherwise
write uniquely \(q=g^2k\), where \(g,k\) are coprime squarefree integers.
Every nonzero factorization is \(d=ga,e=gb\), \(ab=k\). Consequently
\[
\boxed{A_Y(g^2k)=\mu(k)
\sum_{a\mid k}1_{\{Y/g<a<gk/Y\}}.} \tag{AD1}
\]
This is an exact shared-prime formula, not a replacement by coprimality.
The repeated prime signs cancel, while their square factors remain.

Retain T09's full kernel
\[
K_X(m,n)=\int_X^{2X}\phi(m/x)\phi(n/x)\,\frac{dx}{x}.
\]
With \(A=m+n\), \(B=m^{-1}+n^{-1}\), put
\(I_\nu=\int_X^{2X}x^{\nu-1}e^{-A/x-Bx}\,dx\). Direct multiplication
of the two actual profiles gives
\[
K_X(m,n)=mnI_{-2}-AI_{-1}
 +(1-m/n-n/m)I_0+BI_1+(mn)^{-1}I_2. \tag{AD2}
\]
The endpoints are unchanged. In particular, the kernel has no short-shift
support. Products and shifts of order \(X\) remain.

The complete energy is exactly
\[
E_B(X)=\sum_n\beta_X(n)^2K_X(n,n)
 +2\sum_{h\ge1}\sum_n\beta_X(n)\beta_X(n+h)K_X(n,n+h).
\]
Since \(|\beta_X(n)|\le d_3(n)\), \(d_3(n)^2\le d_9(n)\), and the
profile decays exponentially at both ends, divisor counting and partial
summation prove
\[
\boxed{\sum_n\beta_X(n)^2K_X(n,n)
\ll X(\log(2X))^8.} \tag{AD3}
\]
For completeness, the local inequality used here is
\(\binom{j+2}{2}^2\le\binom{j+8}{8}\). It holds at \(j=0\);
the ratio of successive right/left quotients is
\((j+9)(j+1)/(j+3)^2\ge1\). Multiplicativity proves the divisor
inequality. The estimate pays all coincidences \(\ell de=mf g\),
including distinct factorizations, rather than only identical triples.

### An elementary comparison bound, strengthened below

Let \(\mathcal B_{X,\ge H}\) retain the exact terms with
\((d,e)\ge H\), \(H\ge2\). Then
\[
\boxed{\sup_{X\le x\le2X}|\mathcal B_{X,\ge H}(x)|
 \ll XH^{-1}\log^2(2X),\qquad
\|\mathcal B_{X,\ge H}\|_{L^2(dx/x)}^2
 \ll X^2H^{-2}\log^4(2X).} \tag{AD4}
\]
Indeed write the exact gcd as \(g\), so \(d=ga,e=gb\). Only after
this partition, take absolute values and enlarge by dropping squarefree
and coprime restrictions, the smooth cutoffs and \(\ell\le J\):
\[
|\mathcal B_{X,\ge H}(x)|
\le\sum_{g\ge H}\sum_{a,b,\ell\ge1}
 |\phi(\ell g^2ab/x)|
=\sum_{g\ge H}\sum_{r\ge1}d_3(r)|\phi(g^2r/x)|.
\]
For every \(T>0\),
\[
\sum_{r\ge1}d_3(r)|\phi(r/T)|\ll T\log^2(2+T).
\]
For \(T\ge1\), partial summation proves this; for \(T<1\),
the exponential upper tail is stronger. Sum \(g^{-2}\) to obtain AD4.
All finite cutoffs and shared-prime terms were retained before passing to
a positive majorant; there is no omitted complementary product range.

For any fixed \(1/2<a<1\), choose \(H=X^{1-a}\). Triangle inequality
in \(L^2([X,2X],dx/x)\) makes the full target
\(E_B(X)\ll X^{2a+\epsilon}\) equivalent, up to arbitrary losses,
to that target for \(\mathcal B_{X,<H}\). This handles the cross terms
with the discarded sector as well. At \(a=.87449\), every internal
gcd \(g\ge X^{.12551}\) is therefore affordable at exponent
\(1.74898\). In the residual exact factorization,
\[
g<X^{.12551},\qquad a,b>Y/g\gg X^{.37449}/\log^2X.
\]
The use of \(a,b\) as factor labels in this display is separate from the
fixed detector exponent \(a=.87449\).

The sharper [signed gcd pruning theorem]([private research revision]-continuation/mobius-gcd.md)
now replaces this elementary cutoff in the active target. Using only the
accepted fixed Mertens exponent \(b=7/8>b_0\), it proves
\[
\|\mathcal B_{X,\ge H}\|_2^2
\ll X^{2b+\epsilon}H^{2-4b},
\qquad |Q_{\rm cross\ bad}(H,R;X)|
\ll X^{2b+\epsilon}R^{1-2b}.
\]
The second expression is the signed union of all four large cross-gcd
events, with the internal cuts retained. Its proof freezes the original
prime-incidence masks, cancels the four singleton Möbius variables, and
only then uses a positive numerical union majorant.

Choose \(H=X^{1/1400}\), \(R=X^{1/700}\). Both exponents are
\(4897/2800\), below \(1.74898\) by exactly \(9/175000\). Internal removal
uses the \(L^2\) triangle inequality, not an unproved affordable additive
error between the squared energies. The active open estimate is
**OPEN-MG** in that proof: the exact full signed quartic form with both
internal gcds below \(H\) and all four cross gcds below \(R\). Every
original endpoint, short third factor, broad product difference and
Möbius sign remains. No larger \(c\) follows from these sector bounds.

## 1. Reconstructing the actual source and every character phase

Fix an ordinary Dirichlet character chi modulo q, with its natural zeros; q=1 is allowed. Fix an integer r>=2 with chi(-1)=(-1)^r. Put a(n)=mu(n)chi(n),

    Phi(x)=sum_(k in Z\{0}) chi(k)e(kx)/k^r,
    R_N(x)=2cos(2pi x)-sum_(n<=N) a(n)n^(-r)Phi(nx).

Absolute convergence follows from r>1. For a frequency k!=0 the infinite dilated sum has coefficient

    chi(k)k^(-r) sum_(n|abs(k))mu(n).

This uses chi(n)chi(k/n)=chi(k) also when the value is zero. The coefficients at k=1 and k=-1 are both 1 by the parity condition. Thus the infinite target is exactly 2cos(2pi x), and R_N is the full n>N tail. In particular its Fourier coefficients vanish for 0<|k|<=N; in N<|k|<=2N the only eligible divisor is |k|, yielding mu(|k|)chi(k)/k^r. Negative frequencies carry the same coefficient as their positive partners, even for an odd or complex chi, because the denominator sign and parity cancel.

Let n=ga,m=gb,(a,b)=1. Orthogonality of Phi(nx) and Phi(mx) forces Fourier indices bj and aj. Therefore

    <Phi(nx),Phi(mx)> = 2L(2r,chi0) chi(b)conj(chi(a))/(ab)^r.

After multiplying by a(n)conj(a(m))/(nm)^r, the phase factor is

    chi(ga)conj(chi(gb))chi(b)conj(chi(a))
       = |chi(g)|^2 |chi(a)|^2 |chi(b)|^2.

It is 1 exactly when (nm,q)=1 and zero otherwise. A nonzero Mobius term also requires a,b,g squarefree and (g,ab)=1. The resulting global signed norm is exactly

    2L(2r,chi0) sum_(a,b coprime; (ab,q)=1)
      mu(a)mu(b)/(ab)^(2r)
      *sum_(g>N/min(a,b); (g,abq)=1)mu(g)^2/g^(2r).       (R1)

All series here are absolutely convergent. No inducing modulus or primitive replacement was made. The cancellation of character phases is a property of the COMPLETE-PERIOD Gram. In the localized gcd representation the outer factor chi(a)conj(chi(b)) remains; cancelling it there would be incorrect. The author retains it in D_H.

## PS1. A smaller sufficient prime supply

Assume `13/18 <= kappa <= 3/4`, `0 <= delta <= kappa`, and the moment
hypothesis above. Put `q=delta p`, `0<=p<=1/2`, `c=1/(3kappa)`.
For a witness length `1<=t<=3/2`, the canonical count lines are

\[
A_I(r)=1-\delta\{p+(1-p)r\},\qquad
A_P(t-r)=1-\delta\{cp+2(1-cp)(t-r)\}.
\tag{PS1}
\]

Their crossing is

\[
r_*(t)=\frac{2(1-cp)t+cp-p}{3-p-2cp}.
\tag{PS2}
\]

The denominator is positive. The crossing increases with t; at t=1 it
decreases with p since its derivative has numerator `c-1<0`. Therefore

\[
r_*(t)\ge\frac{3-c}{5-2c}
=\frac{9\kappa-1}{15\kappa-2}\ge\frac{23}{37}.
\tag{PS3}
\]

The last function decreases with kappa, with derivative
`-3/(15kappa-2)^2`, and takes value `23/37` at `kappa=3/4`.
Also `1/3<=t-r_*(t)<=1/2`: the quantity increases with t, equals 1/2
at t=3/2, and at t=1 exceeds 1/3 by
`(1-c)p/[3(3-p-2cp)]`.

For the inverse witness `r>=r_*`, the requested capacity
`z=(1-r)/2-nu`, where positive, is at most `7/37-nu`, and

\[
1-r-2z=2\nu,\qquad
3-2r-8z=2r-1+8\nu\ge9/37+8\nu.
\tag{PS4}
\]

For the plain witness `r<=r_*`, its actual `m>=t-r` has capacity at most
`(1-2m)/(6kappa)<=1/(18kappa)<=1/13<7/37`. Small/nonpositive capacities
use the unmarked estimates with the same fixed small losses as B0.38--39.
Whole-slot selection loses at most one mesh interval; choose the mesh
after fixing the supply margin and before all final small-power losses.

Consequently **supply `L>7/37` by a fixed positive amount suffices for the
existing B0.40 row count** on this restricted kappa range. Its exponent is
unchanged:

\[
R_\kappa(\delta,p)=1-\delta+
\frac{\delta C_\kappa(p)(5/6-\delta)}
 {2(5/6-\delta+\delta C_\kappa(p))},\quad
C_\kappa(p)=\frac{2(1-p)(1-p/(3\kappa))}{3-p-2p/(3\kappa)}.
\tag{PS5}
\]

This is a limited strengthening of the convenient `L>4/21` supply
condition. The canonical geometry already has `ell0/h0>1/5`, so it
does not improve the accepted endpoint or the physical numerator bound.

statement:
## Theorem M: a calibrated multiplicative obstruction

For every fixed tau>0, fixed q>=1, numbers 1/2<gamma<beta<b6, and any finite prescribed prime values of modulus one away from q, there exists one multiplicative complex sequence a with a(1)=1 and |a(n)|=mu(n)^2*1_((n,q)=1), matching those prime values, such that:

- its summatory function is O_epsilon(x^(beta+epsilon)), with the same bound for every fixed ordinary-character twist;
- every fixed nondegenerate pair of positive affine forms has vanishing normalized Cesaro two-point correlation, both with and without conjugation;
- its complete fixed Gaussian is C_tau*x^beta+O(x^sigma) for every fixed sigma in(1/2,beta), with C_tau nonzero.

Consequently the accepted summatory calibration, exact multiplicativity, natural squareful/ramified zeros, arbitrary finite prime checks and even these stronger qualitative pair correlations do not imply a first-gain complete Gaussian estimate. The sequence is not mu*chi and does not preserve its global prime-sign law. The theorem is a precise restriction on a proposed use of coarse data, not an obstruction to the actual arithmetic problem.

Construction: independent Steinhaus epsilon_p and independent Bernoulli I_p with mean p^(beta-1); put v_p=1 when I_p=1, otherwise epsilon_p, then impose the finite prescriptions. The centered prime series gives an exact meromorphic factorization D_a(s)=zeta(s+1-beta)H(s), with H analytic and nonvanishing on Re(s)>1/2. The rare changed-prime set has summable reciprocal mass and summable sigma-mass for every sigma>beta. The complete proof follows.

### M1. Probability space, support, and summatory calibration

A Steinhaus variable is uniform on the complex unit circle. All epsilon_p and I_p are mutually independent. Initially set a(n)=mu(n)^2 product_{p|n}v_p; delete every prime dividing q and replace finitely many other prime values by their prescribed unit values. This is ordinary multiplicativity, not complete multiplicativity. It gives exactly the asserted squareful and ramified zeros, a(1)=1, and modulus one on every remaining squarefree integer. Prescribing all primes up to any fixed bound matches the full finite prefix of any particular mu*chi source with that conductor support.

Put P={p:I_p=1}. For b>beta,

  E sum_{p in P}p^(-b)=sum_p p^(-(b+1-beta))<infinity.

Consequently, almost surely, sum_{p in P}p^(-b)<infinity for every rational b>beta, hence every real b>beta. In particular sum_{p in P}1/p<infinity. For any b in(beta,1), # {p in P:p<=x} <= x^b sum_{p in P}p^(-b)=O_b(x^b). Neither statement uses a prime-number theorem.

Let a0(n)=mu(n)^2 product_{p|n}epsilon_p. For n!=m, E[a0(n) conjugate(a0(m))]=0, and E|a0(n)|^2<=1. The same holds after multiplying by any fixed ordinary character psi. A useful elementary maximal estimate for such orthogonal variables is

  E max_{m<=2^k}|sum_{n<=m}a0(n)psi(n)|^2 <= (k+1)^2 2^k.

Indeed, decompose each initial segment into at most k+1 disjoint dyadic blocks, apply Cauchy, then bound its sum of block squares by the sum over every block on every dyadic level. The expectation of the total on each level is at most2^k. Markov's inequality at threshold2^{k(1/2+eta)} and Borel--Cantelli give, for every eta>0,

  M0,psi(x)=O_{eta,psi}(x^(1/2+eta))

almost surely. Intersect the probability-one events for rational eta>0 and the countable set of ordinary characters. We retain one outcome on this intersection throughout the argument.

At a changed prime, the exact local quotient is

  (1+v z)/(1+epsilon z)
    =1+sum_{j>=1}(v-epsilon)(-epsilon)^(j-1)z^j.

Its nonconstant coefficient moduli are at most2. Therefore a=a0*d as a Dirichlet convolution, with

  sum_n |d(n)|n^(-b)
   <= finite_factor * product_{p in P}(1+2p^(-b)/(1-p^(-b)))<infinity

for every b>beta. Deleting the finitely many primes of q or imposing finitely many values adds quotients analytic and absolutely convergent for b>0. Complete multiplicativity of psi gives a psi=(a0 psi)*(d psi), where juxtaposition is pointwise multiplication and the star here is Dirichlet convolution. All occurrences of the literal mu*chi source elsewhere in this report mean the pointwise coefficients mu(n)chi(n). Choosing eta with1/2+eta<b now gives

  |sum_{n<=x}a(n)psi(n)|
   <= C x^b sum_{d<=x}|d(d)|d^(-b) =O_b(x^b).

In this display d(d) denotes the convolution coefficient at integer d, not a divisor-counting function. Thus the claimed beta+epsilon bound holds for every epsilon>0 (larger exponents are harmless). Abel summation also proves

  sum_{n<=x}a(n)psi(n)n^(it)
      =O_{epsilon,psi}((1+|t|)x^(beta+epsilon))

uniformly for all real t. Any fixed number of log n factors costs x^epsilon after shrinking the original epsilon. Constants depend on the chosen outcome and fixed character; this is not a conductor-uniform theorem.

### M2. Exact continuation and complete Gaussian readout

Before the finite changes, E v_p=theta_p=p^(beta-1). The centered independent variables xi_p=v_p-theta_p have mean zero and variance at most1. Apply the same dyadic maximal proof to the sequence equal to xi_p on primes and zero on composites. Almost surely,

  S(x)=sum_{p<=x}xi_p=O_eta(x^(1/2+eta))

for every eta>0. Abel summation then defines

  Z(s)=sum_p xi_p p^(-s)=s integral_1^infinity S(x)x^(-s-1) dx

holomorphically on Re(s)>1/2. On every fixed closed vertical strip with left edge sigma0>1/2 it satisfies |Z(s)|<=C(1+|Im s|), after choosing eta<sigma0-1/2.

For Re(s)>1 the absolutely convergent Euler product D_a(s)=sum a(n)n^(-s)=product_p(1+v_p p^(-s)) satisfies

  D_a(s)=zeta(s+1-beta) H(s),

where H is the exponential of

  Z(s)
  +sum_p sum_{j>=2} (-1)^(j+1) v_p^j p^(-js)/j
  -sum_p sum_{j>=2} p^(-j(s+1-beta))/j.

Both double tails converge absolutely and locally uniformly on Re(s)>1/2: their leading prime exponents are2 Re(s)>1 and2(Re(s)+1-beta)>1. Hence H is holomorphic and nonvanishing there, with |H(s)|<=exp(C(1+|Im s|)) on every fixed closed vertical strip. The finitely many deletions or prescriptions multiply H by factors1/(1+v_p p^(-s)) or(1+v'_p p^(-s))/(1+v_p p^(-s)). They are analytic and nonzero on Re(s)>0, with bounded modulus on any such strip; the conclusions persist. Thus D_a has a simple pole at beta with nonzero residue H(beta). No supposition about zeta zeros is needed.

Normalize the fixed Gaussian by

  g_tau(u)=(2*pi*tau)^(-1/2) exp(-u^2/(2*tau)),
  F_a(x)=sum_{n>=1}a(n)g_tau(log(n/x)).

Absolute convergence follows from |a(n)|<=1. Mellin inversion on any line Re(s)>1 gives

  F_a(x)=(1/(2*pi*i)) integral e^(tau*s^2/2)D_a(s)x^s ds.

Shift to any fixed sigma in(1/2,beta). Zeta has at most polynomial growth on the fixed strip in question, for example by Euler--Maclaurin summation; H has the exponential bound above. The factor exp(-tau*t^2/2) therefore pays the entire infinite-height integral and both horizontal sides. The sole pole crossed is beta. This proves

  F_a(x)=e^(tau*beta^2/2)H(beta)x^beta+O_sigma(x^sigma).

The leading constant is nonzero. This is the complete Gaussian, with no height truncation or omitted tails. The same proof permits fixed derivatives. As x tends to zero, the original absolutely convergent sum is smaller than every positive power of x: for each A>1 use g_tau(log(n/x))<=C_A(x/n)^A. This pays the other end of later Mellin transforms.

### M3. Fixed affine correlations, including conjugation

Take fixed positive-slope affine forms L_i(n)=A_i n+B_i, integer coefficients, A_i>0, with A1 B2-A2 B1!=0. Finitely many n for which a form is nonpositive may be discarded. First change only a fixed finite set F of prime values; include primes of q. Write Q=product_{p in F}p and D=2^{|F|}. On a nonzero term write L1(n)=d r, L2(n)=e s, with d,e|Q and r,s squarefree and coprime to Q. Any ramified or squareful zero is simply omitted.

After conditioning on all random values at primes in F, the remaining conjugated monomial is epsilon(r/s); the unconjugated monomial is epsilon(rs). Distinct positive rational ratios, respectively distinct positive integer products, are orthogonal under the remaining Steinhaus variables. For a fixed ratio r/s and fixed d,e, the equation L1(n)/L2(n)=(d/e)(r/s) has at most one n, because the determinant is nonzero. A monomial class therefore contains at most D^2 terms. For a fixed product rs and fixed d,e, the quadratic equation L1(n)L2(n)=de*rs has at most two n, giving at most2D^2 terms. Coefficients arising from finite prime values or fixed character weights have modulus at most1. Consequently, for either correlation sum C_N,

  E |C_N|^2 <= 2D^2 N+O_F(1).

Markov and Borel--Cantelli along N=j^2 show C_{j^2}/j^2 tends to zero almost surely; bounded summands fill the gaps, since(j+1)^2-j^2=O(j). Take the countable intersection over finite F, integer affine pairs, and fixed ordinary character weights. The estimate is uniform over conditioned finite prime phases, since only their moduli entered.

Now transfer to the infinite random set P. Truncate it at Y, along with the fixed prescriptions and primes of q. The infinite and truncated sequences can differ at a positive integer only if some p in P above Y divides it. For a fixed form A n+B, put the finitely many p|A into the truncation. Each remaining p has at most N/p+1 roots with n<=N and p<=C N. The density of exceptional n is therefore at most

  sum_{p in P,p>Y}1/p + O(#P(CN)/N).

The second term tends to zero by the bound O(N^b), b<1; the first tends to zero as Y tends to infinity. Products of two bounded terms change by at most2 on the union of their exceptional sets. First take N to infinity, then Y to infinity. Both asserted Cesaro correlations vanish. This argument is compatible with the probability-one events of M1 and M2 because the whole list is countable. It produces one fixed outcome, not a new sequence at each scale.

In particular, for every FIXED integer H>=1,

  (1/N) sum_{m<=N}|sum_{j=1}^H a(m+j)|^2 -> H d_q,

where d_q=product_{p|q}(1-1/p) product_{p not dividing q}(1-1/p^2)>0 is the squarefree coprime density. Off-diagonal terms vanish by M3; the diagonal follows by the elementary squarefree density computation. There is no uniformity for growing H. Ordinary Cesaro cancellation also implies the qualitative logarithmic fixed-form conclusions by partial summation, including long logarithmic intervals with length parameter tending to infinity. It does not establish every nonpretentiousness hypothesis of an outside theorem, nor its quantitative uniformities.

### M4. Finite masks and what the obstruction actually excludes

Every feasible fixed valuation pattern on a finite set of unramified primes has Dirichlet series D_a(s) multiplied by a product of factors1/(1+v_p p^(-s)) for valuation0 and v_p p^(-s)/(1+v_p p^(-s)) for valuation1. These factors are nonzero at beta. Every such individual masked complete Gaussian retains a nonzero beta mode. An arbitrary signed combination of masks can cancel that mode only by making its combined multiplier vanish at beta; a return to the original source must then repay the missing signal. The full exact recombination retains it. Patterns at ramified primes that require positive valuation are identically zero and are not called feasible.

This strengthens the relevant [private research revision] coarse calibrated countermodel by imposing genuine multiplicativity, exact natural zero support, arbitrary finite prime prescriptions, all fixed character-twist summatory bounds, and vanishing fixed affine correlations. W27 already constructed a multiplicative real-sign source with a prescribed finite prefix and poles inside the baseline strip; multiplicativity itself is therefore not new here. W27 explicitly left quantitative partial-sum/height calibration unproved. The addition here is the simultaneous proven calibration, fixed affine correlation cancellation, and forced growing-window energy lower bound, at the cost of allowing complex unit phases. This is not a strengthening in real-valuedness. It retains W24/W27's warning about global inversion. It is not a counterexample within the actual mu*chi family: at infinitely many unramified primes its unit value differs from -chi(p), and its Dirichlet convolution inverse is not the prescribed character source. Real-valuedness is also not asserted. Thus a proof using the global Möbius prime law, exact convolution inverse, or sufficiently uniform quantitative correlations can escape the obstruction. This is a scoped mathematical test of a proposed mechanism, not a general impossibility statement.

### 1.1 The actual f core, not an inherited Gaussian-mask estimate

For Re s>1 the literal Euler factors give

    D(s)=sum_n f(n)n^(-s)=H(s)/zeta(s),
    H(s)=(1-3^(-s))^(-2)
          product_(p!=3) (1-2p^(-s))/(1-p^(-s))^2.

At p!=3, the H factor is

    1-sum_(j>=2)(j-1)p^(-js),

and at p=3 its coefficients are j+1. Thus H has an absolutely
convergent Dirichlet series h for Re s>1/2, including absolute
convergence of sum |h(r)|r^(-beta). The coefficient identity is
f=h*mu. Directly using the accepted Mertens input therefore proves

    A_f(u)=sum_(n<=u)f(n)=O_beta(u^beta).               (R1.2)

This step uses no bound for F and no inversion of the vanishing
prime-two factor. It is the r=1 instance of the accepted actual f_r
convolution in [private research revision] Gaussian S1--S7.

H has a simple zero at 1 from p=2. Its p=2 derivative is 4 log 2;
the p=3 factor is 9/4; the remaining factors multiply to the positive
product in C_f/(9 log 2). Hence

    H'(1)=C_f,  D(s)=C_f(s-1)^2+O((s-1)^3).

The second zero is the zero of 1/zeta(s), not another finite-prime
factor. By (R1.2), the ordinary-order reciprocal sums and their first
two logarithmic derivatives converge at 1, giving

    sum_r f(r)/r=0,
    sum_r f(r)log r/r=0,
    sum_r f(r)(log r)^2/r=2C_f.                        (R1.3)

These sums are generally CONDITIONAL. For j=0,1,2 their tails after R
are O_beta(R^(beta-1)(1+log R)^j), by Abel summation. Taking absolute
values of these reciprocal moments would destroy the proof.

## A. Protected S30: rough polymers with the entire signed smooth core

Fix an ordinary Dirichlet character chi modulo q with natural zeros. For real x>=1 and y>=2 write

    M_chi(x)=sum_(n<=x)mu(n)chi(n),
    S_(y,chi)(t)=sum_(a<=t,Pplus(a)<=y)mu(a)chi(a),

where1 belongs to the smooth set and S_y(t)=0 for t<1. A prime at y belongs to the smooth set. Every squarefree n has a UNIQUE decomposition n=ab into its y-smooth part a and y-rough part b. They are coprime. Consequently the complete identity is

    M_chi(x)=sum_(b<=x,Pminus(b)>y)mu(b)chi(b) S_(y,chi)(x/b). (A1)

The b=1 term is included. Squareful b has coefficient zero; a shares no prime with b. All character zeros are literal, and n=x is included. For y=x^eta with fixed0<eta<1, b has k<1/eta prime factors unless b=1, since each factor is STRICTLY greater than y. At the integer endpoint k eta=1, that k-sector is empty; no endpoint term is lost. Thus this is an exact finite-depth polymer expansion with a moving smooth core, not a model gas.

The proposed coarse absolute outer budget, STILL retaining all cancellation inside each smooth core, is

    B_eta(x)=sum_(b<=x,Pminus(b)>x^eta)mu(b)^2 |chi(b)|
                                      |S_(x^eta,chi)(x/b)|. (A2)

For sufficiently large x, every unramified prime p in(x/2,x] is eligible, because x^eta<x/2. Its inner argument lies in[1,2), so its ENTIRE signed smooth core equals1. Therefore

    B_eta(x)>=pi(x)-pi(x/2)-O_q(1) >>_q x/log x.             (A3)

This applies to EVERY fixed ordinary character, not just the principal character, because absolute |chi(p)|=1 on unramified primes. The elementary identity and the constant inner prefix are exact; the displayed asymptotic lower bound uses the ordinary prime asymptotic. It was independently rechecked in [NIST DLMF27.12.4-5](https://dlmf.nist.gov/27.12) in this audit (turn264view0); no progression or conductor-uniform theorem is used. It can be replaced by any fixed-ratio quantitative prime-interval lower bound.

The same obstruction survives the usual shell-Minkowski version, not merely a single-point triangle inequality. Freeze y=X^eta on x in[X,2X], or use y=x^eta. For all sufficiently large X and every unramified prime p in(X,3X/2], the full b=p summand has inner smooth prefix1 on x in[3X/2,2X]. The argument x/p belongs to[1,2), apart from excluded/measure-zero endpoints. Its L2(dx/x) norm is at least sqrt(log(4/3)). Thus the SUM OF COMPLETE POLYMER NORMS is >>_q X/log X. The same holds in L1, with log(4/3). No internal smooth prefix was replaced by an unsigned coefficient count.

This is a lower bound on the proposed positive outer certificate ONLY. The full source in(A1) retains the complex factors mu(b)chi(b) and the cross terms between ALL b. Equation(A3) is emphatically not a lower bound for |M_chi|, its shell norm or a signed polymer Gram. Grouping distinct polymers before taking norms could evade it; its complete signed cost is then the new arithmetic obligation.

A complete square observation is exactly

    |M_chi(x)|^2=sum_(b,c eligible)mu(b)chi(b)conj(mu(c)chi(c))
                         S_y(x/b)conj(S_y(x/c)).             (A4)

This includes b=c, b=1/c=1 and both cross orientations. It is the appropriate place to seek a saving; isolated small-polymer or diagonal bounds do not control it. If the FULL signed(A1), or its complete every-epsilon shell L1 observation, is O(x^(gamma+epsilon)) for common gamma>.5, standard absolute dyadic Mellin convergence continues1/L on Re(s)>gamma. Moving y creates no extra Mellin factor because(A1) equals the original Mertens source pointwise. A bound on only the smooth term or one polymer sector has no such return.

For eta>1/2 there is at most one large prime, and(A1) specializes to

    M_chi(x)=S_(x^eta,chi)(x)
             -sum_(x^eta<p<=x)chi(p)M_chi(x/p).             (A5)

Indeed x/p<x^(1-eta)<x^eta, so the inner smooth cutoff is vacuous. This is exact G166-type prime removal, with the original small-argument Mertens source and M_chi(1)=1 retained. It is not a new short-source arithmetic theorem. More generally absolute bounds |S_y(t)|<=C t^beta only give O_beta(Cx) by summing b^-beta for beta<1; (A3) shows the lack of a power is real for the positive certificate, even if the small prefixes were otherwise favorable.

2||Q_X||||U-Q_X||+||U-Q_X||^2, rather than deleting either complement.

| Conditional target gamma | beta | a,b0 | E2 exponent | EK exponent |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| .87486 (c=.12514) | .874862 | 1/50000,1/50000 | .87485949724 | .87485950276 |
| 5/6 (c=1/6) | .874862 | 1/3,1/3 | 312431/375000 | 624931/750000 |
| 3/4 (c=1/4) | .874862 | 1,101/100 | 187431/250000 | 37437569/50000000 |

At the first target the strict minimum margin is 12431/25000000000.
The support of k is powerful away from 2,3, giving O(sqrt R) nonzero

is a representation count, not an evaluation algorithm or cancellation.
For 1/2<gamma<1, the every-epsilon bounds for Q_X and fixed U are

statement:
# [private research revision] independent review of the hard-covariance interval argument



## Verdict and current checkpoint

**Accept SF2 and SF11 at the report's explicitly restricted source scope,
as consequences of the already admitted cubic sieve M B2.25.** I find no
missing arithmetic factor in SF5, SF7 or SF10. The simultaneous interval
estimate is genuinely proved; it is stronger than applying [private research revision] D2
separately to each interval. The complete strict far mask, and also its
entire complementary near mask, cost only fixed powers of logarithms.
They do not cost the number of intervals or a power of the gap width.

More explicitly, the new interval overhead can be bounded by
`O(log^2(2N))` for SF2 and `O(log^3(2N))` for SF11, before absorption into
`Z^epsilon`. This is a polylogarithmic loss, not an assertion of exactly
one logarithm. The proof below also specifies a valid order of triangle
and Cauchy when a bounded paired row weight depends on both short labels.
Neither clarification changes the stated estimate.

**No new original-prime saving, full H theorem, or c increase follows.**
The optimized positive method certificate still has deficit
`.673880911641069319333...`; the accepted joint H certificate's deficit
is separately `.004`. These are different upper-bound calculations.
Neither is a lower bound on the arithmetic covariance. The accepted
written `c_G=.1251134`, its pending endpoint/kernel work, and the old
`c0` kernel certificates receive no new validation from this review.

Completed: full frozen-report read; exact source binding; independent
SF5/SF7/SF10 reconstruction; original-mask, roots, ordered-interaction,
profile and two-height return; pressure arithmetic; finite SF5 incidence
checks. No mathematical repair is required. Remaining work is the final
whole-artifact readback, hash, explicit STOP and release of this claim.
The Gaussian report remains frozen and unchanged.

## 1. Exact review object and dependencies

The reviewed report is
`[restricted provenance path] research revision]-drafts/hard-covariance/report.md`, 26,429 bytes, SHA-256
`3e29aad381d47ce0820734515ad0202af0faf3f31d25a5753e6397544919481c`.
Its complete text was read. I also read the complete
`check_interval_identity.py` and `interval-evidence.json` beside it.
The latter verifies the author's integer SF8 calculation, not an
analytic bound. I did not execute that script in its author's tree,
because it writes its receipt there.

The mathematical source comparison used:

- `[restricted mathematical source]`, B1--4, C1--2,
  D1--6 and E: the actual coefficients, scalar bilinear bound, complete
  two-cutoff identity, old additive-phase obstruction, separate near-band
  payment, and original return.
- `[restricted mathematical source]` (JPS), JPS1--13 and
  Section 8/JPS32: the literal source/domain, all-prime extension,
  complete short-core inversion, both inert mixed terms, common
  profiles, roots, independent heights and whole tails.
- `zeta_zero_free_validated_merged.md` (M), B2.21--25 and B2.37--40:
  common profile separation, whole lattice tail, exact squarefree-ideal
  cubic sieve domain, and retained dual-root normalization.

The cubic sieve is an accepted source dependency, not re-proved here.
No external theorem, provider, new worker or model-consensus argument
was used. The source files' full hashes and byte counts, including the
author's script and receipt, are in `review-evidence.json`. They match
the corresponding bindings in the author's receipt. The independent
Gaussian report's original size and hash were also verified unchanged.

## 2. Independent proof of the SF5 simultaneous step

Fix the original row R, short source g, mark array, normalized separated
profile component, and one original norm height. Keep the original
ideal labels d,e even when several ideals have the same integer norm.
Write the exact SF1 summand in the form

    V_I = sum_e B(e) sum_(d; q_d q_e in I) F_d(e),

with the original d/e supports retained. The source long interval is
intersected with I. At this point F_d(e) may be any complex entries;
its arithmetic structure is only used at the cubic-sieve step below.
Let

    B_2 = sum_e |B(e)|^2,
    X_J(e) = sum_(d; q_d in J) F_d(e).

Take ONE binary tree on a containing integer interval for the d dyad,
padded to a power of two. Write ell_D for its depth plus one. Missing
integer norms have zero coefficient. Repeated ideal norms remain
different d labels selected by the same integer interval. In either
case each d occurs in exactly one node at every tree level.

For fixed e, multiplication by q_e>0 preserves order. Thus the selected
integer d norms for I_j are an interval, obtained by intersecting the
d support interval with `(I_j intersect original long interval)/q_e`.
Represent this integer interval by its canonical disjoint tree cover
`C(e,j)`, with at most `2 ell_D` nodes. Empty intervals contribute no
nodes. Strict or non-strict real endpoints are first evaluated on the
integer norm lattice; no approximation is needed.

Since the I_j are pairwise disjoint as norm sets, their selected d-norm
sets at this fixed e are disjoint. In particular every fixed tree node
J occurs in at most one `C(e,j)`. This remains true with gaps in the
attainable norms. There is no assertion that covers for DIFFERENT e
are disjoint; they need not be, and the following inequality does not
require it.

Apply Cauchy in e, separately inside each j, and then add j:

    sum_j |V_(I_j)|^2
      <= B_2 sum_e sum_j |sum_(J in C(e,j)) X_J(e)|^2
      <= 2 ell_D B_2 sum_e sum_j sum_(J in C(e,j)) |X_J(e)|^2
      <= 2 ell_D B_2 sum_J sum_e |X_J(e)|^2.          (R1)

The last step counts a node at most once AT THAT e. It is precisely the
step which prevents an interval-count loss. With the actual
`B_2 << Z^epsilon E`, (R1) is SF5. No additive phase in q_d q_e has been
separated, and no arbitrary-input operator bound has been substituted
for an arithmetic assertion: (R1) is an elementary incidence/Cauchy
step, followed below by the actual admitted arithmetic sieve.

The correct scope is worth making explicit. Coefficients and the common
profile on one side are the SAME across that side's interval outputs.
The intervals can be chosen arbitrarily, and the two sides can have
independent interval families, coefficients and heights. SF2 does not
permit choosing a new coefficient array or new separating density for
each j. Nothing in SF8/SF10 requires that stronger, unproved scope.

## 3. Actual arithmetic grouping, zeros and SF7 mass

In the actual source of [private research revision] D1, define

    A_J(t) = sum_(P d=t; q_d in J)
       u(P)/sqrt(q_P) c(d)a(d) chi_R(d)^3 chi_P(d)^4
       1_(P,Rg)=1 1_(d,g bar(g))=1,

with every original P,d support and separated finite/profile factor.
The remaining e coefficient is exactly

    B(e)=b(e)a(e)chi_R(e)^3 1_(e,g bar(g))=1.

The native cocycle `a(de)=a(d)a(e)chi_d(e)^4` is used on coprime d,e.
Its zero extension at noncoprimality is retained in the displayed
character. The factor `chi_P(d)^4` vanishes when (P,d)>1; hence every
nonzero t=Pd is a squarefree IDEAL. The e-dependent cubic factors are

    chi_P(e)^4 chi_d(e)^4 = chi_t(e)^4.

Their zeros at (e,t)>1 supply both original collisions (e,P)>1 and
(e,d)>1. The original row factor on e remains in B, including its zero.
The projector `(P,Rg)=1` is literal in A_J. No residual projector is
silently added or removed, and no inverse character is taken at zero.
These observations establish

    X_J(e)=sum_t A_J(t)chi_t(e)^4.                    (R2)

The A_J are independent of live e. The outer e family and inner t family
meet M B2.25's good primary squarefree-ideal domain, after the fixed
finite ray resolution already allowed in [private research revision] D2. Exponent 4 is the
conjugate cubic character; the source explicitly admits conjugation and
the opposite orientation. Original upper dyads are contained in balls
of lengths O(E), O(LD). Their fixed constants do not change the exponent.
There is no requirement that their INTEGER norms be squarefree, and no
new exclusion of inert or rational prime factors. Fixed e restrictions
can be bounded by a containing positive outer sum.

Consequently, for every tree node J,

    sum_e |X_J(e)|^2
      << Z^epsilon S(E,LD) sum_t |A_J(t)|^2.          (R3)

For SF7, apply divisor Cauchy only after grouping the actual t:

    |A_J(t)|^2
      <= tau(t) sum_(P d=t; q_d in J)
          |u(P)|^2/q_P |c(d)|^2,

where modulus-one native factors and zero masks have now legitimately
been bounded by one. The normalized profile envelopes are included in
c or in the eventual profile mass. Since t has polynomially bounded
norm, its divisor count costs an allocated `Z^epsilon`. Summing t,J
and counting each d once at each of the ell_D levels gives

    sum_J sum_t |A_J(t)|^2
      << Z^epsilon ell_D
         (sum_P |u(P)|^2/q_P)(sum_(d original) |c(d)|^2)
      << Z^epsilon ell_D D Omega.                    (R4)

The last mass bound is exactly the source-only divisor-bounded
coefficient allowance already used in [private research revision] D4. It applies to the
actual Type-I/Type-II coefficients, with their signs and prime supports.
Repeated norms do not increase the tree multiplicity: this count is
over the original ideals, not over distinct norm values.

The physical root in (R4) is `q_P^(-1/2)`. If written using
`q_t^(-1/2)`, it must be multiplied by `q_d^(1/2)`. Thus the D in
`D Omega` is real and cannot disappear. The factor length D is also
distinct from a mark/row collision divisor Delta. Keeping the projector
literal avoids any incomplete Delta inversion.

Combining (R1)--(R4), and using DE comparable to N, proves the explicit
version

    sum_j |V_(I_j)|^2
      << Z^epsilon N ell_D^2 S(E,LD) Omega.          (R5)

Reversing d,e is permitted by the same even reciprocity as in [private research revision]
D2, with both actual supports and coefficients retained. It yields
`N ell_E^2 S(D,LE) Omega`. The minimum of the TWO completed bounds may
be taken. Since ell_D,ell_E are O(log(2N)), this implies SF2 with
`T=min{S(E,LD),S(D,LE)}` and at most two logarithms. A unit dyad uses a
one-node tree and ell=1. No nonunit factorization of a prime is inferred.

## 4. Exact far and near reconstruction; proof of SF10

First regroup each linear block at the ORIGINAL integer norm m=q_n,
retaining the sum over all ideal labels of norm m. This is only a
regrouping of a finite sum, and does not treat an ideal as an integer.

For H>=0 integer, if H exceeds the maximum original norm difference,
the strict far set is empty. Otherwise H=O(N) in this common original
N dyad. Choose a containing power-of-two interval for x=m and y=m'+H;
it has width O(N), hence O(log(2N)) tree levels. For internal nodes J,

    1_(m>m'+H)
      = sum_J 1_(m in J_R) 1_(m' in J_L-H).          (R6)

For x>y the two values have one unique lowest common ancestor, with
x in its right child and y in its left. This is the unique contributing
node. For x<=y no node contributes. Thus (R6) is exact, including x=y
and all endpoints. On a given level the right-child intervals are
pairwise disjoint; the left-child intervals remain pairwise disjoint
after translation by -H.

The reverse condition `m'>m+H` has its OWN identical construction with
the two sides exchanged. For independent arrays it must not be silently
replaced by a conjugate or twice a real part. Adding the two exact
formulas gives `1_(|m-m'|>H)`. Both ideal orientations at equal rational
norm, and the actual diagonal, are absent. This is an exact exclusion,
not an estimate of only the pairs n=n'.

Now keep the original true short-core scalar. Its complete inversion is

    h((g,g')) = sum_(f|g,g') r_h(f),
    r_h(f) = sum_(a|f) mu(f/a)h(a),
    |r_h(f)| <= tau(f)                             (R7)

for |h|<=1. The core is still (g,g'), not a core recomputed from de.
Every original g window, rational-primitivity/opposite restriction,
finite phase, and perpendicular mask is retained. For active f,
q_f is O(G), and the number of original g divisible by f is O(G/q_f),
including bounded or unit ranges. Inactive f contributes zero.

At one fixed tree level and one f, let I_j,J_j be the paired disjoint
interval families in (R6). For a fixed pair g,g', put

    X_j(R)=xi(g)A_1(g)chi_R(g)^3 V_(I_j),1(R,g),
    Y_j(R)=xi(g')A_2(g')chi_R(g')^3 V_(J_j),2(R,g').

Every factor shown here is the original one. For any bounded normalized
row weight w, Cauchy in the JOINT finite coordinates (R,j) gives

    |sum_R,j w(R) X_j(R) conjugate(Y_j(R))|
      <= (sum_R,j |w(R)| |X_j(R)|^2)^(1/2)
         (sum_R,j |w(R)| |Y_j(R)|^2)^(1/2).          (R8)

There are O(K) original rows. Apply (R5) uniformly to each fixed R,g,
and use its independent counterpart on side two. Triangle over the
O(G/q_f) short labels on each side then gives

    << Z^epsilon K (G/q_f)^2 N
       ell_(side 1) ell_(side 2) sqrt(T T')
       sqrt(Omega_1 Omega_2) P_orig.                 (R9)

Here each side chooses the better completed d/e orientation, and each
ell is bounded by O(log(2N)). Equivalently one may first form each
short-source linear vector and use Minkowski in (R,j), as the report
does. The original common separated row weight permits that order.

For clarity, even if a bounded paired row weight depends on BOTH g,g',
one can put triangle over the ordered g,g' pairs BEFORE (R8), retaining
their individual weight inside (R8). This proves the identical bound
(R9) with no factorization assumption on that bounded short-pair row
weight. A new arbitrary mask depending jointly on live m,m' is NOT
covered by this clarification; only the original core and the exact
interval mask have been treated.

The zero of chi_R(f)^3 is present in the original X/Y until their
positive norms; no cancellation of that zero has occurred. Signs of
r_h are likewise present in (R7) until triangle is explicitly taken.
Summing the complete f expansion costs

    sum_f tau(f)/q_f^2 < infinity,

or the weaker allowed subpower factor. The convergence follows, for
example, by ideal counting and a divisor bound with any exponent <1.
There is no unreturned low/high-f remainder. Summing O(log(2N)) levels
and the two ordered orientations proves

    |C_far[h]| << Z^epsilon K G^2 N sqrt(T T')
                 sqrt(Omega_1 Omega_2) P_orig,       (R10)

with explicit additional interval overhead at most O(log^3(2N)). This
is SF11. Independent interval choices on the two sides cost no interval
count because (R8) pairs their vectors in the same node coordinate and
SF2 controls each entire disjoint family separately.

Finally, before any estimate the full complementary mask satisfies

    C_near = C_all - C_(m>m'+H) - C_(m'>m+H).         (R11)

C_all has the same bound from a single interval and the same full core
inversion; each strict orientation is paid above. Equation (R11) pays
ALL pairs with |m-m'|<=H, including distinct ideals of equal norm and
the diagonal. It is valid for independent arrays and both heights.
It gives no inherited estimate for an arbitrary submask of C_near.
The auxiliary near term `(H+1)L` in [private research revision] D6 is therefore unnecessary
at this restricted scope. The sharper original-prime near-graph theorem
remains separate and is not used on composites here.

## 5. Profiles, heights and every complementary return

The interval proof is carried out first at finite original cutoffs and
one normalized separated component. For an actual smooth original
profile C(de), separate it by its ONE common logarithmic Fourier/Mellin
density. Minkowski is applied in the Hilbert space of ALL outputs j,
or (R,j) when appropriate. The same density is used for every output;
there is no endpoint-specific or row-specific density. The norm factor
`q_(de)^(it)=q_d^(it)q_e^(it)` has modulus one, so (R3)--(R5) are uniform
in that original height. The second side has its OWN independent height
and density; no equality between them is assumed.

Original sharp long-norm endpoints are intersected with I_j before
forming the integer covers. No large derivative or additive product
phase is introduced. Fixed finite-ray restrictions are separated by
their existing finite character resolution. Native angular and Gauss
factors remain in a(d),a(e). The common-profile factor includes the
original linear envelope `min(Y^(1/4),(1+Y)^(-A))` ON EACH SIDE, with
the original root scaling and finite/six-unit component masses. This is
M B2.22/JPS Section 8, with the new finite interval output coordinate.

The following are the actual return obligations, and they are preserved:

1. **Original scalar and roots.** The physical outside squared scalar
   remains `N^(-1)G^(-2)`. Multiplying (R10) by it gives
   `Z^epsilon K sqrt(T T') sqrt(Omega_1 Omega_2) P_orig`.
   The target is `K S(N,L)/(N G)` with those same masses. No d,t,tree
   or Fourier root can be divided out. If the row/mark projector is
   separately expanded, EVERY Delta child retains its linear root
   `q_Delta^(-1/2)` and residual mark mass at most
   `q_Delta Omega_Delta`; this review does not replace that exact
   accounting or shorten N through Delta.

2. **Signed cutoff identity and ordered interactions.** [private research revision] B1--3
   hold pointwise in the ORIGINAL R,P,g,n. Restricting to any interval
   commutes with the identity, so both sides of every rectangle retain
   I+II before a positivity step. Their covariance has all four ordered
   terms (I,I),(I,II),(II,I),(II,II), and all pairs of actual factor
   dyads, including unit/nonunit pairs. On eligible semiprimes the
   normalized linear coefficients remain 1,-1; their pair matrix is
   still 1,-1,-1,1. The interval tree does not break that cancellation.
   The two mixed terms cannot be omitted. Conversely the SF11 positive
   estimate does not itself exploit their eventual cancellation.

3. **All-prime to degree-one return.** Recombine ALL cutoff terms at
   original n first. Then JPS11 gives exactly
   `C_11=C_all,all-C_inert,all-C_all,inert+C_inert,inert`.
   The complete inert square and BOTH ordered mixed terms cost

       Z^epsilon G^2(K+N)
       [sqrt(N)L + {S(N,L)sqrt(N)L}^(1/2)]
       sqrt(Omega_1 Omega_2) P_orig.

   This is SF18/JPS6; the explicit JPS12 completion gates apply on
   EACH eligible dyad. No inert fibre theorem is assumed.

4. **Transport and unit Jacobi subtraction.** Once the original
   degree-one scalar is restored, its already accepted raw budgets are

       Z^epsilon G^2(K+N)S(N,L)sqrt(L/K),
       Z^epsilon G^2 K L/N,

   with the same masses, exactly SF19/JPS32. The complete-unit signs
   remain. These payments do not bound the unpaid fluctuation or
   transform the Jacobi mean into a short-core density.

5. **Whole tails and both heights.** Remove whole original discarded
   lattice/source/root tails by M B2.23/B2.37--40 before using a positive
   row enlargement. Added divisor factors and finitely many logarithms
   cost a fixed polynomial majorant; choose the original Schwartz order
   after that polynomial and the desired error. Pair one WHOLE tail
   with the FULL other side first, then choose that order. This pays
   both ordered mixed tails and the squared tail. The original rapid
   densities handle both independent infinite height tails. No sharp
   row annulus is differentiated, and no single weak-seminorm uniformity
   is asserted. The finite tree creates no new unreturned tail.

6. **Restricted theorem domain and other branches.** The report retains
   `N>C_orig(K+L+G^2)`, `C_orig G<A_0`, `1<=L<=sqrt(N)`, `G>=1`, and the
   evaluated perpendicular all-prime extension. Within-source masks,
   the original true core, matching corrections, total-index selectors
   and paid-source complements are not recomputed on auxiliary
   composites. Other source branches, dyads outside this domain, cusp
   coefficients, cube sources and global correction returns remain
   unchanged and unpaid by this theorem. Original equal-norm terms
   removed before defining this hard packet retain their own global
   obligations. None is claimed to follow from (R10) or (R11).

Thus the new result repairs exactly the sharp-mask cost in the restricted
bilinear estimate. The old [private research revision] source identities and their complete
return remain valid and available; this review does not delete or
rewrite any of them.

## 6. Pressure arithmetic and the unchanged arithmetic obstruction

For DE=N, both cubic bounds contain the same mixed term:

    (E LD)^(2/3)=(D LE)^(2/3)=(NL)^(2/3).

Thus T>= (NL)^(2/3), independent of the split. Taking
`D=sqrt(N/L)`, `E=sqrt(NL)` makes E=LD and attains this order, since
`S(E,LD)=2 sqrt(NL)+(NL)^(2/3)` and NL>=1. This is a lower bound on the
available positive CERTIFICATE, not on the covariance itself.

At the stated pressure parameters

    k=.835507578307735986...,
    nu=k+.003, gamma=.001,
    ell=.170813789153867993...,

S(N,L) is comparable to N. Dividing the raw (R10) certificate by the
required `G K S(N,L)` gives optimized scale `G(NL)^(2/3)` and exponent

    gamma + (2/3)(nu+ell)
      = .673880911641069319333... .                  (R12)

The eliminated old near-band contribution had exponent
`gamma+.05+ell=.221813789153867993...`; it was smaller. With a
hypothetical two-linear-term cubic bound the same fixed-row argument
would still have exponent `.5056606837308019895...`. Even replacing
the row count K by K^(1/2) in this certificate leaves
`.256127122487201326333...`. These are diagnostics of this particular
order of inequalities, not universal requirements on a future H proof.

For comparison the actual established joint bound is

    G(K+NG)S(N,L),

whose ratio to `G K S(N,L)` is `1+NG/K`; its pressure exponent is
`nu+gamma-k=.004`. The surplus of (R12) over that incumbent is
`.669880911641069319333...`. No comparison of these upper bounds gives
arithmetic cancellation or a new zero-free constant.

On an original prime, the normalized Type-I coefficient is one and
Type-II is zero; the source stays in the unit cell D=1,E comparable N.
Since L<=sqrt(N),

    T(1,N;L)=min{S(N,L),S(1,NL)} comparable to N.

The new certificate is then `K G^2 N^2`, target-relative `GN`, exponent
`.839507578307735986...`. Recombining all signed allocations first
restores the accepted original-prime bound and its `.004` deficit;
it does not shorten the live prime source. The next arithmetic target
is therefore a genuinely joint original-row interval-vector or signed
I/II estimate BEFORE the positive fixed-R loss. The proven interval
adapter would return its exact far mask, but supplies no such estimate.

## 7. Evidence, limits and frozen handoff

The mathematical evidence is the complete independent derivation
(R1)--(R12) and its source-contract comparison above. The author's
15,148-pair SF8 receipt was inspected as finite endpoint evidence only.
Its complete script correctly counts both strict orientations, checks
levelwise disjoint translated families and writes the stated receipt.

The separate owned `check_sf5.py` checks the NEW critical SF5 incidence
and Cauchy step with exact Gaussian-integer matrix entries. It exhausts
two-cut interval partitions and a gapped subfamily for small supports,
including a unit support, missing norms, duplicate ideal-norm labels,
duplicate e norms and non-power-of-two original supports. The check
passed 5,736 matrix/interval cases, 16,772 fixed-e incidence checks and
14 exact per-label tree membership checks. Both displayed Cauchy
inequalities were evaluated with integer arithmetic; there are no
floating-point tolerances or random-sign assumptions. It also verifies
the quoted pressure arithmetic from the explicitly TRUNCATED decimal
inputs, and binds all reviewed source files by bytes and SHA-256.

This finite check is not a numerical cubic large-sieve proof, native
Gauss-sum experiment, test of the true prime vector, or substitute for
the analytic derivation. It addresses the simultaneous interval count
which the author's SF8 endpoint check does not test. All assertions
passed, and the Python process returned exit code zero despite its
existing harmless launcher-location warning.



Controller handoff: SF2/SF11 are sound restricted improvements over
[private research revision] D2/D6. Record the explicit polylog scope and the original common
coefficient/profile condition. Keep the full signed prime problem,
the `.004` incumbent deficit, all other H branches and c_G endpoint
work open. The final full readback/hash and explicit STOP establish the
frozen artifact; release applies only to `[private research revision]-hard-review`.

# [private research revision]: retained support reserve and restricted marked-plain density

The highest accepted written, source-relative endpoint is now
**c9=500579/4000000=.12514475**, theta9=3499421/4000000=.87485525.
It improves c8 by107/50000000=.00000214 and Gao's .1251134 by627/20000000.
The complete endpoint uses the retained first-support reserve and the
already accepted weighted density. The separate marked-plain theorem
below is useful library material and is not a premise of this endpoint.

This retains PR9 commit58344dfdbe756cf2f743da1908ffe0582418cf5b and Gao PR15
commitca182b70ac2aee2d053d679b4ddf1233883f9eef, including their fixed finite-order,
trivial-infinity Eisenstein Hecke scope. The norm lift gives every fixed
ordinary complex Dirichlet character, with natural zeros and principal pole
handled separately. F0/analytic ancestry, original positive-slot uniformity,
external root-definition binding and external admission remain OPEN. No
formalization, kernel run or public-record admission is claimed.

Full [author development](retained-support/report.md),
[independent reconstruction](retained-support-review/report.md),
[exact independent receipt](retained-support-review/receipt.json) and
[twelve-file retention manifest](retention-manifest.json) are retained
byte-for-byte. Root read the complete source and independent reports and
independent checker. The reviewer reconstructed the changed argument without
executing or importing the author helper. Unchanged source contracts are
imported only at the explicitly reviewed [restricted research revision]/[restricted research revision] boundaries.

Work on the original Eisenstein ideals/primary generators with their fixed excluded set, finite dictionary, ray and unit conventions. Write `phi_u(n)=nu(n) psi_u(n)^(+1 or -1)`, completely multiplicatively including zero values. The normalized inverse polynomial is

```
M_u(D;W)=D^(-1/2) sum_n mu(n) phi_u(n) W(Nn/D).
F_u=M_u(D1;W1) M_u(D2;W2) Q_u,   D1=U^r, D2=U^s.
```

`W1=W1(sigma,t1;.)` and `W2=W2(sigma,t2;.)` keep the common real parameter and separate height coordinates `t1,t2`. They are never identified. `Q` is the entire original slot product, with all its own heights. Slot pools are mutually disjoint but may meet either inverse. Their fixed coefficients and all natural zeros stay in place. If orientation is aligned at a positive norm, the complete slot product is conjugated as licensed; there is no individual slot switching. Total slot length `P0=U^v`, `0<=v<=1/20`, and

```
sup_u |Q_u|^2 << H_J U^(v+epsilon).
<X,Y>_U = sum_u Phi(Nu/U) X_u overline(Y_u),   ||X||_U^2=<X,X>_U.
```

The rows are the original nonzero sixth-power-free free rows in a fixed nonnegative smooth enclosing ball. Original divisor-bounded row weights are dominated before expansion. No zero, amplitude, moving-row or signed physical-projector selector enters the moment or Poisson transform. `H_J` retains finite seminorm and height factors.

The sole cancellation input below is the licensed canonical single-inverse moment, with its actual coefficients:

```
||M(E;W)||_U^2 << H_J U^epsilon J(E),
J(E)=U+U^(1/6)E^(5/6).                                      (R1)
```

UM slack is chosen first. For nonempty subunit scales, the fixed profile endpoint bounds the scale away from zero; smaller scales are empty. The direct bound `|M(E)|<<H_J sqrt(E)` therefore holds uniformly on all nonempty windows after enlarging the fixed constant. Polynomially bounded moving punctures are repaired by the exact identity

```
M_u^(R)(E)=sum_(h R-smooth) phi_u(h)/(Nh)^(1/2) M_u(E/Nh),
sum_(h R-smooth) (Nh)^(-1/2)
 = product_(p|R)(1-(Np)^(-1/2))^(-1) <<_epsilon (NR)^epsilon. (R2)
```

Each original annulus sum is finite; allowing the full positive mass only enlarges its bound. No zero value of `phi` is divided out. R1 is never applied directly to a merged divisor-profile coefficient or an arbitrary projected coefficient.

## 3. Direct integral, absolute order and the variable-cost correction

Let I=[X,2X] with measure dx/x. Use a measurable real Hilbert field H_x
and its direct-integral space Hcal=L2(I;H_x). Each v_a must be an admitted
measurable square-integrable section. The field T_x:H_x->R^2 must be
measurable on sections, common across all indices, with norm bounded
by a measurable L_x and C_I=int_I L_x^2 dx/x<infinity. Then

    Tcal(v)=int_I T_x v(x)dx/x, ||Tcal||<=sqrt(C_I).       (3)

Bochner integrability in the finite-dimensional target follows from
Cauchy-Schwarz. Recovery may hold almost everywhere; the countable
index set permits a common full-measure set. Apply(1) to these sections:

    C_I sum_(a,b)|int_I <v_a(x),v_b(x)>dx/x|
       >=(1/2)(sum_a|int_I c_a K(q_a/x)dx/x|)^2.          (4)

If L_x<=L essentially, C_I<=L^2 log2, proving draft R3 with constant1/2.
The inner product is the REAL Hilbert inner product. For complex or
quaternion lifts it is the real part of the conventional Hermitian
product; a complex-modulus absolute price is larger and also obeys the
floor. Absolute values in(4) are AFTER each complete shell integration.
No exchange with pointwise absolute values was used.

For countably many labels the same finite-subset limit proves(4), even
when its left side is infinite. For the concrete lower bounds below it
is enough to retain finitely many central labels. No convergence of an
unbounded-lift global sum is required. Failure of square integrability
is a failure to define this certificate, not permission to apply(4).

Important correction: C_I is the cost of Tcal, the AVERAGED functional.
It is not in general the norm squared of v(x)->T_x v(x) from shell L2
to shell L2. On a measurable E of shell measure epsilon, take H_x=R,
T_x=epsilon^-1/2 1_E and v=epsilon^-1/2 1_E. Then C_I=1 and ||v||_2=1,
but ||T_x v||_2^2=epsilon^-1. The averaged functional remains bounded
as(3) says. Thus an energy-return argument may use a uniform ess-sup L,
giving ||sum_a T_x v_a||_2^2<=L^2||sum_a v_a||_2^2, but must not replace
L^2 by C_I without another source-specific estimate.

A lawful variable-cost alternative is to use w_a(x)=L_x v_a(x) in Hcal
and T'_x=T_x/L_x (set0 where L_x=0), provided each w_a is square
integrable. It changes the after-integration Gram to
sum_(a,b)|int_I L_x^2<v_a,v_b>dx/x|. Its common readout has norm at most1
pointwise. This is a different PAID Gram, not C_I times the old Gram.
