## 2. Sources and independent evidence

The entire author report, helper and numerical receipt were read. Its six content pins and seven named source pins agree with their exact bytes. I did not execute or import the author helper. Primary inspection included:

* PR9 commit `58344dfdbe756cf2f743da1908ffe0582418cf5b`, local `paper.md`: T1 conventions, B0.13's fixed dictionary/nonprincipality statement, B1.6--11, and B3.1--6, especially the literal masked primitive Poisson formula B3.5 and the prohibition on extra canonical column coefficients in B3.6.
* PR15 commit `ca182b70ac2aee2d053d679b4ddf1233883f9eef`, `PlainUnmarkedDensity.tex`: the natural coefficient dictionary and conductor-bounded representative, whole-character conjugation, the fixed finite exceptional set on free rows, and the explicit ideal count bounded by 128x.
* The frozen [restricted research revision] review Sections6--8: completed zero identity, exact tensor Sobolev norm, full sixth-class root sum, target unit row and principal-pole correction.
* Accepted `[restricted mathematical source]`: fixed K=28114053/6250000, its origin from the independently accepted c10 SAME-family bound, and the current G_K/E_K formula. K is not recalibrated from c11.
* The existing external merged research note Section2.5, RM-A through RM15: the balanced relative-residue mass and masked Poisson mechanisms already present there. The author correctly credits these as ancestry.

These are inspected local source bytes, not a new live upstream or admission claim. Current proof/index/creative files were navigation snapshots; active controller edits were left untouched. Exact source and author pins are in `receipt.json` and `source-notes.json`.

The independent `verify.py` uses rational polynomial coefficients and Bernstein conversion on the whole delta interval. It checks four strictly positive cleared-denominator margin polynomials after spending xi=1/100 and the maximum real buffer. Two further nonnegative polynomial certificates establish the stated strictly positive derivative floors. There are 18 Bernstein coefficients: 16 positive and two zero endpoint coefficients belonging to the derivative-floor certificates. The floors themselves are positive. This is whole-interval evidence, not a sampled grid.

It also verifies the exact delta-minus-3k identity, both coefficients of the low-core exponent, six scalar values, 588 radical plateau cases, 896 merged-slot support cases, 4096 two-prime gcd/root representations including unequal scales, 3920 natural-zero cases in exact Q[z]/(z^2-z+1) arithmetic, and ten nonprincipal local character sums. All checks passed. The finite tests are diagnostic support; the proofs of the infinite sums and row bound are below. They do not establish OPEN-[restricted research revision], a physical transfer, or any new c. No repeated endpoint atlas was run.

## 5. Independent root and label calculation; literal core caps

Restore (V4), both allocation counts, and O(A) original a labels. Writing F=q_f, the four resulting terms on an a-dyad are

| Term | U power | A power | N0/source power | F power | Core power |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SQ1 | 1/3+2tau/3 | -1 | N0^(1/3) | -1 | C^(1/3) |
| SQ2 | 5/6+tau/6 | -4 | N0^(1/3) | -2 | C^(5/6) |
| CU1 | 2/3+tau/3 | -3 | N0^(-1/3) | -1 | C^(2/3) |
| CU2 | 5/6+tau/6 | -4 | N0^(-1/6)sqrt(S0) | -3/2 | C^(5/6) |

For example SQ2 has prefactor U A^(-5)/(N0 F), coefficient mass price X=N0/F, and H_A^(1/6)=U^(tau/6-1/6) A N0^(1/3). This directly gives F^(-2), not F^(-1). CU2 instead has sqrt(X), hence F^(-3/2). Both square roots from scalar Cauchy were already used to produce one common positive-energy price; none is omitted or added here.

The full f sum with tau(f)^C costs a subpower for F^(-1), and converges after a sufficiently small divisor loss for F^(-2), F^(-3/2). The support has F<<N0. The original A sums over 1<<A<<U^(1/6) are geometric and bounded at these negative exponents. All original assigned/surviving slots have already been counted. Since s<2r and r<2s,

    S0 << P0(D1D2)^(2/3),
    N0^(-1/6)sqrt(S0) << (D1D2)^(1/6)P0^(1/3).

The four terms reproduce exactly the author's SQ and CU formulas. This validates the complete label calculation, not just a favorable numerical exponent.

Take C_sq=U^(13/40), C_cu=U^(3/4). Define SQ first, CU outside SQ, and HARD when both caps fail, all on the literal (Delta*ell) and original middle. It is an exhaustive disjoint signed partition. It does not enlarge a signed scalar by positivity.

For the two second terms, comparing with T>=delta L+rho gives respectively

    (delta-1/3)L+rho-5/6-v/3-(5/6)(13/40)-tau/6,
    (delta-1/6)L+rho-5/6-v/3-(5/6)(3/4)-tau/6.

Both lower comparisons increase in L and delta: the latter derivative is L-50/[3(5-2delta)^2]>=21481/24300>0. They decrease with v. At delta=17/25,L=217/100,v=1/20, their raw margins before tau are 23813/2730000 and 2768/170625. After tau/6, a combined auxiliary allowance 1/500 and retained 1/200, the positive spares are exactly 177/113750 and 8241/910000. First terms are far below the target: their exponents are at most 149/120+2tau/3 and 133/300+tau/3. Thus the author's same-margin equality (6.1) is justified by these retained contracts.

All logarithmic dyad/finite-place counts and arbitrarily small divisor/sieve losses can be assigned within that combined allowance. The common weighted Fourier L1 bounds only require finitely many derivative orders; they introduce no compulsory positive U-power. This preserves original height operators, including -W/2-yW', and both independent height coordinates. Constants are fixed before the eventual threshold and suprema. This bookkeeping inherits rather than repairs the open positive-slot uniformity ancestry.

# [restricted research revision] discovery-first sieve headroom

Status: mathematical development completed, independent review pending. No new zero-free constant is established. The marked-plain proposal has a factor-of-two length error and does not replace the accepted MP gate. The already retained manuscript Appendix S.1 contains the correctly dimensioned short adapter; that ancestry is essential. This report develops uniform estimates for the actual canonical Gauss and completed theta columns, including moving fixed labels, punctures, and the full sixth-power row cost. It proves useful local improvements, then shows explicitly why these bounds miss the current physical bottleneck. Freeze/STOP and ownership receipts are separate.

## Source and discovery record

Read the stable prefix, frozen [restricted research revision] problem and assignment in that order; their hashes matched the controller packet. The primary preprint is Alexandre de Faveri, *Optimal large sieve for fixed order characters*, arXiv:2610.04045v1, submitted 2 October 2026, [versioned primary text](https://arxiv.org/html/2610.04045v1). The local HTML SHA256 is 7639be04b4023701377a4a339f2392994afdada8624b8f39e863fab7cbae91d4. Theorem1.1, Sections2.3–2.5 and the root-coupling discussion were read. This is an external preprint theorem, not an independently reproduced proof or an admitted QRH import.

The old source is PR9 commit58344df, local paper SHA256 2b4c67c3e817d7854ee57e451cea1789c8a4a1d03a72ddb83b980421167096d8. The literal B0.3–5, B2.1, B2.4–6, B3.1–8 and B3.40 contracts, current attempt index, [restricted research revision]/G99 and [restricted research revision]/G110–111 were inspected. Seven distinct initial mechanisms are retained in discovery.md. Detailed history was consulted after that slate. The independent [restricted research revision] lanes are not inputs to this report.

**Ancestry correction:** zeta_zero_free_validated_merged.md Appendix S.1 already cites this exact external theorem, gives the sixth-power row/column lifts, and records r+z<=1/2 and 2m+z<=1/2. It expressly says these miss the binding witnesses. The discovery is a renewed audit/application, not first discovery of that theorem in the project. The older S.1 text and the present fixed-family audit are separate from a successful full physical return.

## 1. Bind the actual family before applying the theorem

Write q_a=N(a), K=Q(omega), O=Z[omega]. Work on ideal columns avoiding the fixed S, containing primes above6 and the fixed conductors. The primary generator is congruent to1 modulo3. PR9 uses psi_u(b)=chi_b(u), including zero at every shared prime; phi_u=nu psi_u^e, e=+1 or-1. The fixed nu may have order not dividing6.

The imported bound for sixth-power-free ideal rows and columns is

    T(A,B)=A+B+A^(5/6)B^(1/3)+A^(1/3)B^(5/6),
    sum_a^(6) |sum_b^(6) lambda_b chi_a(b)|^2
      <<_(fixed data,epsilon) (AB)^epsilon T(A,B) sum_b|lambda_b|^2. (1)

Here chi_a is the family constructed with fixed n,K,S,ray modulus and representatives in the cited Sections2.3–2.5. In this class-number-one field choose the representative generators m_E to be their global primary generators. If a=(x)E g^6 with x=1 modulo the fixed ray modulus, choose a primary generator g_0 of the fractional ideal g. Then x m_E g_0^6 and the primary a_0 generate the same ideal and are both1 modulo3; their quotient is a unit congruent to1 modulo3, hence1. Therefore the defining residue symbol is exactly (a_0/b)_6 on coprime labels. Its prescribed zero extension agrees at every shared prime. This gives the PR9 orientation directly, without suppressing a reciprocity factor.

For a different permissible generator convention, splitting the finitely many S-unit classes modulo sixth powers gives fixed column twists; no growing conductor is hidden in them. Rows containing fixed S-primes are split into their valuation residues0,...,5 and sixth powers. Units give six fixed column phases. The fixed nu multiplies lambda_b. The opposite orientation is obtained by conjugating the entire inner sum and its coefficients, not by silently dropping nu. The reverse residue-symbol orientation, when needed, is handled by PR9's fixed modulo36 reciprocity sectors. These operations retain the natural zeros and cost only fixed constants or small powers.

The matrix theorem allows arbitrary fixed column coefficients. It does not allow an arbitrary array lambda_(a,b). Fixed row restrictions may be dropped only from the positive outer norm. Smooth rowwise heights are addressed separately below. Source family binding does not prove the external theorem or complete its definition/import/admission obligations.

## 2. General normalized columns and the correct MP dimension

Let F_u be a product of J fixed normalized polynomials with lengths X_1,...,X_J and bounded row-independent coefficients, all in one common phi_u orientation. The actual plain factors and original prime slots are examples. Put B=product X_j. Multiplication gives

    F_u=sum_b lambda_b psi_u(b)^e,
    lambda_b=B^(-1/2) sum_(b_1...b_J=b) product_j c_j(b_j),
    support q_b << B,  |lambda_b| << B^(-1/2) d_J(b).     (2)

Fixed nu, the original slot characters, different smooth profiles and independent norm heights stay in c_j. Every ordered tuple and every collision remains. A common puncture means the exact zero coefficient1_((b,R)=1). Disjoint slot pools do not imply that a slot is disjoint from a plain factor. In particular, a plain prime power p^5 and its slot p contribute a sixth-power column with the original p-hole; it is not the constant character1.

Write b=d h^6 uniquely, with d sixth-power-free; there is NO condition(d,h)=1. For a fixed h,

    psi_u(dh^6)=psi_u(d)1_((u,h)=1),
    sum_d |lambda_(dh^6)|^2 << B^epsilon q_h^(-6).        (3)

The second estimate follows from (2), ideal counting q_d<<B/q_h^6 and the divisor bound. Apply(1) to each fixed h and drop the h-row restriction only in the positive norm. Minkowski then sums q_h^(-3), which converges over ideals. Thus for sixth-power-free rows q_u<<U,

    sum_u^(6)|F_u|^2 << (UB)^epsilon T(U,B).             (4)

For ALL rows write u=a e^6, retaining units and S-parts as above. The identity is psi_(ae^6)(b)=psi_a(b)1_((b,e)=1). For fixed e this is a fixed column mask, so(4) applies at row length U/q_e^6. Summing e gives

    sum_(0<q_u<<U)|F_u|^2 << (UB)^epsilon T_all(U,B),
    T_all=U+B U^(1/6)+U^(5/6)B^(1/3)+U^(1/3)B^(5/6).  (5)

The B U^(1/6) term comes from the number of sixth-power roots. It cannot be removed by relabeling them as a finite set. No principal or fixed-inducing row has been discarded. Both(4),(5) are O(U^(1+epsilon)) when B<=U^(1/2).

For the literal marked plain fourth moment, F_u=S_u(U^m)^2 Q_(u,I), so B=U^(2m+v), v=sum z_i. For two independent plains it is U^(n1+n2+v). Consequently the direct short gate is

    2m+v<=1/2, or n1+n2+v<=1/2.                       (6)

The proposed m+v<=1/2 pertains to |S Q|^2, not |S|^4|Q|^2. It cannot replace 2m+6kappa v<=1. The actual accepted local window n1,n2 in[.41M,.44M], v in[.034M,.04M] has total length at least.854M, strictly outside(6). The inverse counterpart r+v<=1/2 is likewise already in equation(S.4) and misses the binding r near.9. This failed candidate is retained in its exact scope.

## 3. A uniform canonical column bound with all moving fixed labels

Consider exactly PR9 B3.6, with a0(n)=bar(alpha(n))gamma_2(n), squarefree n, fixed f for the row sum, fixed puncture rho, original product mark d_I(n), and fixed finite-ray nu. Its centrally normalized coefficient has squared mass

    Z^(-N) sum_(n sf) |a0(n)nu(n)rho(n)chi_n(f)^4
                         d_I(n)W(q_n/Z^N)|^2 << Z^epsilon. (7)

For good squarefree n, |a0(n)|=1. A fixed-depth product mark is bounded by a divisor power. The puncture and all natural zeros are contractions. Hence the bound is UNIFORM in the moving fixed f and puncture, without paying their logarithmic widths V,Q in the sieve operator. They may not depend on the currently summed row. Applying(1) and then the exact all-row lift proves

    E(N,V,M) << H_J Z^(E_all(M,N)+epsilon),
    E_all(M,N)=max{M,N+M/6,5M/6+N/3,M/3+5N/6}.        (8)

Here E is the original normalized positive f-average of B3.6. The count of its divisor-bounded nonnegative f-weights is Z^(V+epsilon), canceled by its exact Z^(-V). No second label count occurs. For a sixth-power-free row norm, replace N+M/6 by N; that is a different norm, not a bound asserted for E. Fixed f-dependent column masks also obey the same pointwise-in-f argument, although later source reconstructions retain their own stronger independence requirements.

For M>0 the all-row envelope has the simple exact form

    E_all(M,N)=M                         (0<=N<=M/2),
                5M/6+N/3                 (M/2<=N<=M),
                N+M/6                    (N>=M).       (9)

This is a complete canonical source estimate. In particular E(M/2,V,M)<<Z^(M+epsilon) uniformly over every actual mark and fixed puncture. At N=M, V=M/3, the new cost is7M/6, strictly below the old target F=N+V=4M/3 by M/6. It remains valid, for example, at Q=M, where the old B3.7 sufficient gate F-M-Q-z0>0 is false. This does not refute that older theorem; it supplies a distinct sufficient bound on a specified source in an uncovered parameter region. Whether that region is a bottleneck in the complete physical argument is a separate question.

## 4. Actual completed theta coefficients and their sixth-power extraction

The PR9 completed source is

    T_I(X;u)=sum_(c sf,b) a0(c) nu(c)bar(alpha(b))^3nu(b)^3
       psi_u(cb^3) chi_(cb^3)(f)^4 rho(cb^3)
       d_I(cb^3) V(q_c q_b^3/X)/(sqrt(q_c) q_b).         (10)

This retains shared c,b primes, the entire-index mark and both natural holes. Additional fixed row-independent coefficient phases or restrictions may be retained. Every ideal A=cb^3 has at most one such representation: its local exponents modulo3 are0 or1 and determine c. Thus writing A=d h^6 gives d=c b0^3 with c,b0 squarefree, possibly sharing primes, and b=b0h^2. The allowed residual exponents of d are0,1,3,4. At fixed h, the complete coefficient vector on d obeys

    sum_d |lambda_(dh^6)|^2
      << X^epsilon q_h^(-4)
          sum_(b0 sf) q_b0^(-2) sum_(q_c<<X/q_h^6) q_c^(-1)
      << X^epsilon q_h^(-4).                           (11)

Phases from h remain in lambda; its collisions with f,rho or u remain exact zero restrictions. Applying(1) and Minkowski now sums q_h^(-2), again convergent. The same all-row extraction gives

    sum_u^(6)|T_I(X;u)|^2 << H_J (UX)^epsilon T(U,X),
    sum_(0<q_u<<U)|T_I(X;u)|^2
                           << H_J (UX)^epsilon T_all(U,X). (12)

This is an estimate of the actual completed source, not an arbitrary coefficient claim about its reflected descendants. It treats all marks without expansion because the complete mark is divisor bounded. Fixed f and puncture remain uniform. The unmarked original bound is U+U^2/X; the comparisons and physical return are given below. Rapid decay at both profile endpoints permits dyadic annular decomposition: choose decay after all raw powers, apply the annular estimate on each complete dyad, and sum its norm by Minkowski. No incomplete tail is dropped.

The finite number of independent smooth/height parameters has a fixed-order Sobolev bound. A derivative only replaces a profile by an Euler derivative or adds a bounded-log factor on its annulus. Prove(7)/(11) uniformly for these finitely many derivative profiles, integrate the corresponding positive norms over the fixed real parameter boxes and the height box, and then take rowwise suprema. The cost is a fixed polynomial H_J in the heights, not U to a height-dependent exponent. Arbitrary row-dependent arithmetic masks cannot be justified this way.

## 5. Complete local comparison, including the existing reflection bound

For the unmarked source with f=1 and no extra puncture, combine(12) with PR9 B2.43. With n=N/M and M>0, the smaller complete exponent is

    E_hyb/M=1                    (0<=n<=1/2),
              5/6+n/3             (1/2<=n<=7/8),
              2-n                 (7/8<=n<=1),
              1                   (n>=1).             (13)

Thus the full unmarked completed source has energy at most U^(9/8+epsilon), uniformly in X in fixed polynomial ranges, and at most U^(1+epsilon) outside U^(1/2)<X<U. At X=U^(7/10), the old exponent is13/10 and the new one16/15, a saving7/30. At X=U^(7/8), both give9/8. These are upper-bound improvements for the entire sum, not selected favorable terms. The old side of this minimum is not extended to new moving f or punctures without its own proof. The new side(12) is uniform in those labels.

For marked sources with no extra f or puncture, the exact already retained Appendix S.2 equation(S.5) exponent is

    E_old=M+max{0,(N+2z-2M)/4,M+2z-N}, 0<=z<=M/2.     (14)

One may take min(E_old,E_all). In particular N=7M/10,z=M/25 gives old exponent69M/50 and new16M/15. This compares against the existing out-of-range reflection extension, not merely against a missing theorem. Its marks remain on the whole completed index. The estimates have fixed-data constants and fixed finite height order; no claim is made that they resolve the original common-mesh/positive-slot bootstrap quantifiers.

## 6. Distinct lower-order sectors with their full class count

Let u be sixth-power-free away from S. Write u=t a^2 uniquely with t squarefree and a cube-free; there is no condition(t,a)=1. For each fixed t and each b in(10),

    psi_(ta^2)(cb^3)=psi_t(cb^3) psi_a(c)^2 1_((a,b)=1). (15)

The b factor is a row restriction only after taking the positive norm for fixed b. All t-phases, f-phases, marks and punctures stay in the c coefficients. Those coefficients have squared mass <<X^epsilon/q_b^2 on q_c<<X/q_b^3. The n=3 specialization of the imported theorem gives the cube-free cubic operator A+B+(AB)^(2/3). Apply it in the a,c variables, with A=(U/q_t)^(1/2); use Hilbert Minkowski over b. The U-part costs sum_(q_b<=X^(1/3))1/q_b=O(log X), and the B and mixed parts have even more decay. Summing the actual t ideals with q_t<=Delta proves

    sum_(q_u<=U, u six-free, q_t(u)<=Delta)|T_I(X;u)|^2
      <<H_J(UX)^epsilon[(U Delta)^(1/2)+X Delta
                          +U^(1/3)X^(2/3)Delta^(2/3)]. (16)

The unique decomposition includes every row in this sector, with bounded unit multiplicity. Natural zeros when t and a share primes stay in(15). Fixed S-residues give fixed phases and logarithmic counts as before.

Similarly write u=t a^3, where t is cube-free and a squarefree. For fixed t,b, the a-character in(10) is psi_a(c)^3 psi_a(b)^3. The last factor is a scalar of modulus at most one depending only on the row, so it may be dropped in the positive norm. The c columns are squarefree, and PR9 B2.24's quadratic Hecke sieve gives A+B, A=(U/q_t)^(1/3). The same b-Minkowski argument and full t count yield

    sum_(q_u<=U, u six-free, q_t(u)<=Delta)|T_I(X;u)|^2
      <<H_J(UX)^epsilon[U^(1/3)Delta^(2/3)+X Delta].   (17)

In both formulas 1<=Delta<=U. These are applications to the actual completed coefficients and all whole-index marks. They do not estimate arbitrary separately reflected arrays. The important ancestry is [restricted research revision]/MQ4, which already proves the same scalar expression as(16) for a different actual cubic Mobius source. Freezing a growing class and summing it is not a new principle; the present calculation checks its compatibility with(10).

For example X=U^(7/10),Delta=U^(3/10) gives O(U^(1+epsilon)) in both(16),(17), better than(12) on those sectors. But the t>Delta sector remains: generic squarefree u has t=u in both decompositions. It is not sparse merely because small-t classes are paid. Sixth-power repetitions also remain for a full-row claim; apply their exact e-lift and count them, or retain(12). No union of these two paid sectors covers every row, and no c increase is inferred.

### 6.1 Use the existing label average to pay every row repetition

There is a second use of the cubic sieve which DOES retain all sixth-power rows. In literal PR9 B3.6, the squarefree f weight depends only on f, while the puncture, prime lists and all n coefficients are independent of f. For each fixed k apply B2.25 to the f,n pair with character chi_n(f)^4. Both are squarefree; cubic reciprocity/conjugation changes only fixed ray phases. The squared coefficient mass is(7) before its f-dependent phase is inserted, and multiplication by chi_n(k) is a contraction. The bound w(f)<<Z^epsilon permits positive enlargement of this f norm. Summing all O(Z^M) k rows and retaining the original Z^(-V) gives

    E(N,V,M) <<H_J Z^(E_label(M,N,V)+epsilon),
    E_label=M+max{0,N-V,(2N-V)/3}.                    (22)

This is uniform in the actual common puncture even if its norm grows. Unlike the pointwise-in-f bound(8), it is NOT asserted with arbitrary f-dependent column coefficients or f-dependent punctures. No moving label is inserted into a fixed Hecke twist: the entire squarefree label family is summed by the cubic sieve. A common smooth profile is separated on its original ambient box by B3.3, with an absolutely integrable fixed measure, before this argument.

The same estimate holds for the normalized f-average of the completed source(10), with X=Z^N. For fixed b, the phase chi_(cb^3)(f)^4 equals chi_c(f)^4 1_((b,f)=1), including all zeros. The b-phase in the k variable is also a contraction. The c coefficient mass is <<X^epsilon/q_b^2. Thus the joint positive (f,k) norm for this fixed b is bounded by

    H_J(UXZ^V)^epsilon U q_b^(-2)
       [Z^V+X/q_b^3+(Z^V X/q_b^3)^(2/3)].

Minkowski over b costs only a logarithmic power on the first term and convergent series on the others; divide the final squared norm by Z^V. This proves(22) for the complete label-averaged theta source too. In this proof every k row, including principal and pure sixth-power rows, is counted once. Their cancellation is supplied by the actual f-average, not by declaring them absent.

Consequently the canonical norm and the corresponding completed average obey the minimum of(8)/(12) and(22). In particular V>=2N gives O(Z^(M+epsilon)) for ANY N in the fixed polynomial range, with all original whole-index marks and common punctures. At N=M,V=2M this improves the full-row sixth-order exponent7M/6 to M. It also holds at Q=4M, where the older sufficient canonical gate F-M-Q>0 fails. This is a complete, different local mechanism using a neglected existing library component; it needs only PR9's licensed squarefree cubic sieve. No claim of first global novelty is made from absence of this formula in the inspected index. For the original physical compensator, f=1 and V=0, so(22) costs M+N and supplies no gain. Other canonical uses must retain and pay the V<2N complement; no complete physical covering argument was found here.

For the literal canonical target E<=Z^(F+epsilon), F=N+V, formula(8) gives the following complete sufficient gate, independent of Q and of total mark width for each fixed slot count:

    V>=M-N                 for 0<=N<=M/2,
    V>=5M/6-2N/3           for M/2<=N<=M,
    V>=M/6                 for N>=M.                 (23)

Equality is allowed in this direct estimate; an induction demanding a positive reserve must impose its own strict version. Formula(22) improves some interior exponents, but does NOT enlarge(23): E_label<=F is equivalent to V>=max{M-N,M/2,(3M-N)/4}, which implies(23) in each displayed range. This explicit boundary comparison prevents interpreting the paid label average as another automatic MP improvement. The sixth-free version has a different long-column boundary V>=max(0,M/3-N/6) for N>=M; applying that boundary to all rows would omit exactly the repeated-row cost. At V=0, neither new all-row bound reaches the canonical target for any M>0. ## 7. The actual physical return and the remaining quantitative gap

The current source-relative value remains c11=312864909/2500000000 and gamma11=2187135091/2500000000. K=28114053/6250000 remains licensed from preceding-c10 SAME-family ancestry. ### 7.1 The complete compensator is longer than the new useful range

In PR9 B0.25–27 a subset of original slots of width d has

    M'=M-2d, z'=ell-d, N'=1+ell-d, 0<=d<=ell.

                 >17/36-1/20=19/45>0.              (18)

The accepted return already retains common-profile suprema, all four profile pairs, Euler restoration and tails, exhausted positive supply, empty selection, and zero capacity with MP0. None is removed or assigned the positive-slot improvement. Fixed-inducing, principal and naturally zero rows also remain under their original proofs. ### 7.3 New density is not a stronger count in the binding interval

For the untwisted sixth-order family actually stated in the preprint's Corollary1.5, put delta=2sigma-1. In 1/3<=delta<=5/6 its saving in the row count is

    D6(delta)=3delta(6delta-1)/(60delta-36delta^2-10).   (19)

### 7.4 The simplest genuinely joint test is still too expensive

Use the actual [restricted research revision]/G155–157 separated-witness source M(U^r)M(U^s)Q with r+s>217/100, delta in[17/25,7/10], 0<=v<=1/20.     b-T >= (1-delta)(r+s+v)-rho

For verification, the last expression is minimized at v=0,r+s=217/100,delta=7/10; its delta derivative is negative across the interval. The all-row exponent b+1/6 is still larger. This is failure of the proposed upper-bound price, not an energy lower bound or an impossibility theorem. In particular, enlarging the coefficient family alone cannot solve the current signed joint core.

An actual new route must bound the WHOLE remaining signed source, not its separate absolute projector summands. [restricted research revision]/G186 specifies R_nonunique+R_middle, after its paid low/far terms, with target O(H_J U^(T-xi)) for one uniform xi>0. Its physical return still requires both signed projectors, original family reconstruction, all roots and holes, inducing/principal/zero branches, detector tails, clipped rectangles, shortenings and common suprema. ## 2. A local coefficient factor supplies the pole-killing zero

Let e_r be the sequence supported at r with value one. Set kappa=e_1-2e_2 and A=kappa*mu, with Dirichlet convolution. This proves DP1, including the exact local values

\[
 A(2^jm)=
 \begin{cases}
 \mu(m),&j=0,\\
 -3\mu(m),&j=1,\\
 2\mu(m),&j=2,\\
 0,&j\ge3,
 \end{cases}
 \qquad m\text{ odd}.
 \tag{DP8}
\]

In particular |A(n)|<=3; odd-square factors still give their natural zero. In Re s>1,

\[
 \sum_n\frac{A(n)}{n^s}
 =\frac{1-2^{1-s}}{\zeta(s)}.
 \tag{DP9}
\]

Equivalently,

\[
 F_{A,\delta}(x)
 =\sum_n\mu(n)\{V_\delta(n/x)-2V_\delta(2n/x)\}.
 \tag{DP10}
\]

The two-lobe profile psi_delta(u)=V_delta(u)-2V_delta(2u) has integral zero in du, exactly. Its Mellin multiplier is (1-2^{1-s})M(delta s). No factor delta^{-1} was used to normalize this zero at s=1. This does not contradict the single-contiguous-window obstruction: psi_delta has two lobes whose centers have fixed logarithmic separation log 2. After the exact reindexing DP10, the kernel is again a single narrow bump, but its arithmetic coefficient is A rather than mu.

Here is the complete zero-exclusion bridge. Suppose for every epsilon>0, uniformly over all sufficiently large dyadic X,

\[
 \int_{e^{-1}X}^{2eX}
 |F_{A,\delta_X}(x)|^2\frac{dx}{x}
 \ll_\epsilon X^{2a+\epsilon}.
 \tag{OPEN-DP}
\]

DP6 proves the same bound for the fixed master F_{A,1} on [X,2X]. Its Mellin integral

\[
 \mathscr F(s)=\int_0^\infty F_{A,1}(x)x^{-s}\frac{dx}{x}
 \tag{DP11}
\]

is holomorphic in Re s>a: the function vanishes for x<e^{-1}, and dyadic Cauchy--Schwarz plus the displayed bound gives locally uniform absolute convergence at infinity. For Re s>1 finite-kernel absolute convergence permits interchange, giving

\[
 \mathscr F(s)=M(s)\frac{1-2^{1-s}}{\zeta(s)}.
 \tag{DP12}
\]

The numerator is nonzero for a<Re s<1. Indeed M has no zero there, and |2^{1-s}|>1. Analytic continuation of zeta(s) times DP12 then excludes every zeta zero in that strip. The accepted baseline already excludes zeros on Re s>=1 (the pole at 1 is not a zero), so OPEN-DP implies nonvanishing throughout Re s>a. No bound at a moving contour, no boundary-line claim and no new Hecke input is used. Taking a=.87449 would give c=.12551, strictly above c0, **only if OPEN-DP is proved**.

## 9. Approximation, wavelets, damping and the source resolvent

### F08.A / F19.A — Actual modular-residue capture

In \(H_\sigma=L^2((0,1),x^{2\sigma-1}dx)\), use
\(f_n(x)=\{1/(nx)\}-n^{-1}\{1/x\}\). On the k-th reciprocal interval, \(f_n=(k\bmod n)/n\). Its Gram is exactly \((2\sigma)^{-1}\) times regression under
\(\Pr(K=k)=k^{-2\sigma}-(k+1)^{-2\sigma}\). Closure of 1 in the arithmetic span gives \(c=1-\sigma\); begin just below \(b_0\), with \(\sigma=4/5\) a later structural target.

For nested least-squares spaces,
\[
d_{2N}^2=d_N^2-q_N^*C_N^\dagger q_N.
\]
A relative capture \(q^*C^\dagger q\ge\delta_jd^2\) with \(\sum_j\delta_j=\infty\) suffices; no fixed positive fraction is necessary. Finite-prefix interpolation and the first-shell inverse are paid. Future tails contain actual Mertens increments. The crude tail estimate only closes above \(1/(2-b_0)\approx.8888\), worse than the baseline. Repeated restarted fits are not an infinite compatible chain.

A09's optimally damped real correction has gain \((F_N+\Re J_N)^2/(F_N+T_N)\); this can improve a step when exact refitting loses norm, but leaves earlier-shell error. A convergent scheme must revisit constraints or use recomputed projections. Higher integrability is useful only for the *actual residual*, with an exponent beating the heavy-tail probability and all subsequent repetitions.

### F08.N1 — New pass 2: admissible residue wavelets and multiresolution correction

Gemini's zero-mean wavelet suggestion cannot replace the arithmetic span by arbitrary functions: that would make approximation trivial while destroying the zeta transfer. A valid wavelet must be an explicit finite combination of \(f_n\), for example balanced \(nf_n-mf_m\) with \(m,n>N\), which vanishes on the fitted prefix. Orthogonalize a **block of those arithmetic differences** in the exact heavy-tail Gram, retaining its later periodic repetitions.

The first missing lemma is a quantitative block-capture and leakage statement, not wavelet orthogonality. One workable target is a compatible sequence with \(\sum\delta_j=\infty\) and total later-shell leakage at step j at most a fixed fraction of its captured energy. Analyze two consecutive blocks, then the infinite tail, with certified smallest Gram eigenvalues. If exact prefix preservation produces intolerable leakage, switch to damped overlap corrections and carry the residual on the old blocks. This differs from the original first-shell inverse by forcing the next-shell/tail interaction into the theorem. An ordinary wavelet basis or a numerical pseudoinverse without a coefficient map earns no progress.

### F08.R / F26.R — The arithmetic source resolvent

For positive summable weights define
\[
K_w=\sum_{n\ge2}w_n(f_n\otimes f_n),\quad
R_w(\lambda)=\langle1,\lambda(K_w+\lambda I)^{-1}1\rangle.
\]
A08 gives \(R_w(\lambda)\to d_\infty^2\). Thus source-specific \(o(1)\) is an exact alternative to capture. Compact positivity gives no uniform spectral gap; the spectral-mass estimate must include the atom at zero. Exponential weights plus a power resolvent rate force an unnecessarily strong exponential finite-index approximation; polynomial weights \(n^{-1-\alpha}\) are the better first choice.

**New pass 2 refinement, F08.N2:** try dyadic block weights chosen *before* observing the unknown residual, then bound the source spectral measure by a block Schur recursion. The target is an explicit summable tail/resolvent inequality preserving the zero atom, not the smallest eigenvalue of the entire compact operator. Compare its penalty to the admissible residue-wavelet coefficients. This merges two supplied constructions at their exact quantitative obstruction rather than treating compactness as cancellation.

Finite positive truncation gives a certified upper bound on the full resolvent by operator monotonicity. A finite bound yields honest bounded-height zero exclusions through \(R_w(\lambda)\ge2(\beta-\sigma)/|\rho|^2\); it does not give all-height nonvanishing. Conditioning and Gram-entry/tail evaluation must be certified. Randomized-residue criteria carry an independent coefficient-tail condition, which may not be dropped.

## 4. Reconstruction of the author's crucial S10 estimate

Keep the original ordered inverse and slot tuple labels, even if their merged ideal agrees. Set `G=U^(1/5)`. Let `F_>` retain `N gcd(d1,d2)>=G` and `F_<` retain its strict complement, so `F=F_<+F_>` as tuple polynomials. For squarefree ideals `q1,q2`, let `P_(q1,q2)F` insert `q1|d1,q2|d2`. This is linear coefficient projection on the original tuples, not a row projection or an orthogonal projection in the row norm.

For fixed integer `A>=2`, write `w_A(q)=tau(q)^A` and

```
D_A(X)=sum_(q1,q2 squarefree) w_A(q1)w_A(q2)
                         ||P_(q1,q2)X||_U^2.              (R4)
```

All label sums have one fixed global cap covering the scale box, with empty terms zero. This energy is not assumed bounded by `||X||^2`.

Finite divisor inversion gives, for any real `H>=1`,

```
a_H(q)=sum_(d|q,Nd>=H) mu(q/d),
sum_(q|g) a_H(q)=1_(Ng>=H),
|a_H(q)|<=tau(q),  a_H(q)=0 if Nq<H.                        (R5)
```

Retaining signs and normalization, G155's extraction is

```
F_> = sum_f a_G(f) phi_u(f)^2/(Nf)
              M_u^(f)(D1/Nf) M_u^(f)(D2/Nf) Q_u.           (R6)
```

Only squarefree `f` can occur. For fixed f put `E_i=D_i/Nf`, write `d_i=f x_i`, and decompose `q_i=g_i h_i`, where `g_i=gcd(q_i,f)|f` and `(h_i,f)=1`. The condition `q_i|d_i` is exactly `h_i|x_i`; its projected inverse is

```
mu(h_i) phi_u(h_i)/(Nh_i)^(1/2)
                   M_u^(f h_i)(E_i/Nh_i;W_i).             (R7)
```

No coprimality between `h1,h2`, no restriction on their overlap with slots, and no character inversion are introduced. The `g_i` label weights cost `sum_(g|f)tau(g)^A << (Nf)^epsilon`. For fixed `h1,h2`, the first inverse is bounded trivially with its actual mask, the second by R2 then R1. Their squared row norm, before slot cost, is

```
<< H_J U^epsilon E1/(Nh1)^2
       [ U/(Nh2) + U^(1/6) E2^(5/6)/(Nh2)^(11/6) ].        (R8)
```

The divisor-weighted `h1^-2` and `h2^(-11/6)` sums converge after arbitrarily small auxiliary losses. The finite `h2^-1` sum costs subpower, not a reciprocal cutoff. Including Q and the f-divisor weights, the vector for fixed f in the full row x q1 x q2 Hilbert space has squared norm `<<H_J U^(v+epsilon) E1 J(E2)`.

Now use Minkowski in that entire space on R6, including the row multiplier `phi_u(f)^2`, whose modulus is at most one. On `Nf~X`, `sum |a_G(f)|/Nf << X^epsilon`. The square root bound decreases like a positive power of X; the dyadic tail starts at G. After factoring out `H_J^(1/2) U^(v/2+epsilon)`, its two terms are bounded by constants times

```
sqrt(D1 U) G^(-1/2+epsilon),
sqrt(D1) U^(1/12) D2^(5/12) G^(-11/12+epsilon).
```

Squaring proves, for every fixed A,

```
D_A(F_>) << H_J U^(v+epsilon) (D1/G) J(D2/G).               (R9)
```

This reconstruction pays the apparent extra q-label bill. Replacing R9 by the unprojected G155 norm would not justify later cuts. Its dominant exponent is `v+r+5s/6-1/5`, with raw gap

```
T-(v+r+5s/6-1/5)
 >=rho+(47/20)delta-393/200 >=2809/273000>1/100.            (R10)
```

The finite diagnostic in Section 11 checks R7 with actual ideal Möbius signs and natural zeros. R8-R10 are analytic arguments, not consequences of that diagnostic.

For S13 define the augmented cutoff complex K_X with one basis vector e_S for each finite set of unramified primes with product<=X, including the empty set. Its parity is |S|, deletion is the usual oriented d, and Delta=dd*+d*d. The set is downward closed, so d^2=0 with no omitted boundary. Let Gamma be parity. The odd operator d+d* maps the positive lambda-eigenspaces of Delta bijectively between parities, by division by sqrt(lambda). Thus, with det_even/det_odd,

    sdet(I+z Delta)=1,
    sdet(z I+Delta)=z^(Str I)=z^(M_chi0(X)).                 (19)

The first ratio's logarithmic derivative is zero; the second is M_chi0(X)/z. The entire signed principal source sits in the zero-mode power. A gap does not bound that exponent. This is a specified finite determinant realization answering the earlier undefined-torsion objection, not an impossibility theorem about every regularized torsion.

For a general character, D_chi e_S=chi(product S)e_S has Str D_chi=M_chi(X), but

    [D_chi,d]e_S=sum_(p in S) orientation(p,S)
                    chi(product(S)/p)(1-chi(p))e_(S minus p).

It is not generally a chain map. Even the weighted first Laplacian trace keeps its complete edge defect:

    Str(D_chi Delta)=sum_(n,p: np<=X, mu(n)^2=1,
                                      (np,q)=1,p not|n)
                          mu(n)chi(n)(1-chi(p)).             (20)

Each edge contributes its lower and upper diagonal incidences. This is not the original source unless a separate normalization and complementary return is proved. For a principal character it is zero, consistently with (19). No hidden weighted determinant is identified with 1/L.

S11's actual fixed-prime cone, for p not dividing q, yields A(X)=sum_(n<=X,p not|n)mu(n)chi(n), B(X)=A(X)-A(X/p), and

    M(X)=B(X)+(1-chi(p))sum_(j>=1)B(X/p^j).                 (21)

The complete positive-exponent reconstruction factor is 1+|1-chi(p)|/(p^gamma-1). This is G144 ancestry, including its character commutator; a small geometric boundary rank is not supplied.

    [P_X,chi(p)V_p]e_n=-chi(p)1_(X/p<n<=X)e_(pn).

Its ordinary trace, also after multiplication by a finite causal divisor-convolution matrix, is zero. Its actual coordinate readout is -chi(p)[M(X)-M(X/p)]. A complete bound for that interval returns M by telescoping with factor 1/(1-p^-gamma), gamma>0. This is already Sol04's S38 calculation. Keep the literal current source

    f(n)=mu(rad(n/3^v_3(n))),
    F(x)=sum_(n>=1)f(n)g_tau(log(n/x)),
    Z(x)=sum_(n>=1)g_tau(log(n/x)).

Every prime power other than3 contributes one minus sign; every power of3 contributes+1. There are no coefficient zeros in f. The fixed normalized Gaussian and all valuations remain. The accepted buffered Mertens input, transferred by the actual Euler convolution in [private research revision] R1.2, gives F(x)=O_beta(x^beta) for a fixed beta=.8749<1. No new exponent is used.

Fix an arbitrary A>0 and choose C=sqrt(2tau(A+2)). On a complete shell X<=x<=2X set

    B_X=ceil(2X exp(C sqrt(log X))).

The positive Gaussian tail gives uniformly

    sum_(n>B_X)g_tau(log(n/x))=O_A(X^-A).           (W40.8)

Indeed integral comparison on the decreasing tail reduces it to x exp(tau/2) times the normal tail above C sqrt(log X)-tau, plus the first term, of exponent1-C^2/(2tau)+o(1)=-A-1+o(1). This pays f's entire omitted tail too.

Let A_B be the finite commutative *-algebra generated by the exact prime-presence projections e_p(n)=1_(p|n), p<=B_X, p!=3, acting on integers1<=n<=B_X. Its atoms are radical patterns away from3; different valuations in one atom remain summed. Define the signed functional

    ell_B(phi)=sum_(n<=B_X) f(n)g_tau(log(n/x))phi(n).

A positive functional nu means nu(phi*phi)>=0 for every phi in this exact algebra. Let it be a positive correction and require ell_B+nu to be positive. The odd-parity projector

    Q_-=(1-product_(p<=B_X,p!=3)(1-2e_p))/2

is in A_B and has value1 exactly when f(n)=-1. Thus0<=Q_-<=1 and

    nu(1)>=nu(Q_-)>=-ell_B(Q_-)
       =sum_(n<=B_X,f(n)=-1)g_tau(log(n/x))=:N_B.

Equality is attained by the positive functional supported on exactly those negative-sign atoms, with those original weights. Hence

    min nu(1)=N_B=(Z_B-F_B)/2.                      (W40.9)

This is an exact dual certificate, not a dimension estimate. A positive dilation or noncommutative extension retaining the same projections cannot evade it: its restriction still obeys0<=Q_-<=1. The result does NOT forbid a positive state with a separate signed/unitary observable insertion, as in W38, or a restricted operator system omitting Q_-.

If the correction delta is allowed to be signed, its TOTAL MASS is not the right cost: delta=-ell_B has mass-F_B and kills the functional. Its functional norm (total variation on this finite commutative algebra) still satisfies ||delta||>=|delta(Q_-)|>=N_B whenever ell_B+delta is positive, because ||Q_-||=1. The same positive correction attains equality. Thus W40.9 also gives the minimum norm of an unrestricted signed correction; it does not falsely identify signed total mass with norm.

The positive lattice sum is elementary:

    Z(x)=exp(tau/2)x+O_tau(1).                       (W40.10)

The integral over positive real n is exp(tau/2)x. A unimodal sum-integral comparison costs at most twice the fixed maximum of g_tau. This modest O(1) error is enough; the stronger Poisson estimate in frozen f3 A33 is not needed. Combining W40.8--10 and the accepted F bound gives

    min nu(1)=exp(tau/2)x/2+O_beta,tau(x^beta),      (W40.11)

uniformly on the whole shell. After normalization by Z_B, the repair price tends to1/2. In particular no correction of size O(X^gamma), gamma<1, can make this full functional positive. Subtracting the correction afterwards restores a signed term of order x; declaring it an auxiliary harmless state is not a paid return.

### 3.1 Exact retained escape: the price depends on the test algebra

For a subset P of the available prime coordinates let C_S be its Boolean atoms and w_S=ell_B(1_(C_S)). Positivity on just that smaller algebra has exact correction price

    N_P=sum_S max(-w_S,0)
       =(sum_S |w_S|-F_B)/2.                        (W40.12)

The same atomwise proof establishes this formula. Refining P can only increase sum|w_S| by the triangle inequality. The empty algebra costs max(-F_B,0); the full algebra costs W40.11. Thus a restricted positive realization remains a legitimate different target, but it must demonstrate that its small collection of tests still preserves the zero-exclusion readout. No finite-marginal independence or signed-submask inheritance follows.

This is where the rare candidate remains viable as useful mathematics after its original small-repair hope fails: W40.9/12 quantify the exact tradeoff between retained observables and correction mass. They give a concrete rejection test for a proposed GNS completion and a precise reopening condition. W39.17--21 already prove the related one-path variance and unsigned mass for mu*chi, and W38 supplies parity on a positive state. W40 claims no new total-variation principle; its source-specific contribution is the actual f3 prime-presence repair certificate and restricted-algebra monotonicity.

Functional signature: complete f3 diagonal functional; positive correction on its prime-presence algebra; parity projection is the dual witness; unpaid arithmetic/control of a sufficient restricted algebra; no new moment return or c.

## 5. Complete return, the first-gain budget, and exact limitations

For a new floor-invariant approximation to prove an ordinary-character
improvement, it suffices, for each fixed q, each character chi modulo q,
and every epsilon>0, to construct F (possibly scale dependent) and prove
for ALL large integer N that

    |F(N,1)| <<_(q,chi,epsilon) N^(gamma+epsilon),
    |Delta(N,1)+sum_(p,m)C_(N,chi)(m,p)*Delta(m,p)|
                       <<_(q,chi,epsilon) N^(gamma+epsilon).           (13)

The exact identity then gives M_chi(N)<<N^(gamma+epsilon); nonintegral
x is covered by floor(x). A still weaker joint signed estimate is possible,
but merely rewriting that full expression as M_chi supplies no estimate.
Equation(13) states the two complete inputs that this attempted approximate
source would actually need. A fixed collar is a way to make some Delta
terms exactly zero, not permission to omit the rest.

For a concrete first target one can set

    c*=125143/1000000=.125143,
    gamma*=874857/1000000=.874857,

strictly improving the current accepted c8=.12514261. This is ONLY a
conditional target; (13) is not proved at gamma*. The near,1/6,1/4 targets
correspond to gamma*,5/6,3/4 respectively. In our actual prime-band tests,
the error exponent is

    theta(u,r)=(u+1)/(u+r+1)=1-r/(u+r+1).

It exceeds a target 1-c precisely when

    u>r/c-r-1.                                           (14)

For any proposed fixed gamma<1 choose such a fixed u with the appropriate
nonzero derivative, then choose epsilon<theta-gamma. Fixed logarithmic
factors cannot absorb the resulting positive power gap. This is an
inequality about the tested certificate, not an assertion that equality
in a separate strict-reserve argument is impossible for epsilon-loss moments.

The crude independent-state certificate is |error|<=B*||Delta||_infinity.
TheoremA shows its power cost is1 even with integer coalescence, so a
uniform bounded-defect premise alone cannot reach ANY of these targets.
The signed fixed-profile repair in theoremC has the same limiting power
cost despite arbitrary fixed-order vanishing moments. At a selected u
where theta>gamma, a scalar amplitude multiplying that profile would need
a power at least N^(gamma-theta), up to the displayed logarithms, to meet
the target. No such arithmetic amplitude estimate is supplied.

For completeness the zero return itself is elementary and all-height.
If M_chi(x)<<x^(gamma+epsilon) for each epsilon>0, then

    H_chi(s)=s*integral_1^infinity M_chi(t)t^(-s-1)dt

is holomorphic for Re s>gamma. On each compact subregion, choose epsilon
smaller than its distance to the boundary; all fixed derivatives are paid
by the convergent extra powers of log t. On Re s>1, absolute Euler
multiplication gives H_chi(s)L(s,chi)=1, using actual mu(n)chi(n) and its
ramified zeros. Analytic continuation preserves the identity, excluding
the usual principal pole at s=1. Thus no L-zero lies in Re s>gamma; for
an imprimitive fixed character the omitted Euler factors have zeros only
on Re s=0, outside this positive half-plane. No finite-height truncation
or uniform-in-conductor assertion is silently added. To obtain a theorem
for every ordinary character, (13) must hold for EACH fixed one, not only
the principal class tested here. No new Eisenstein/Hecke or external
root-L-function definition binding is proved.

TheoremsA--C are unconditional arithmetic statements relative only to the
published friable asymptotic and ordinary PNT. They do not use the PR15
source-relative endpoint as an input. Conversely they do not close any
PR9/Gao source/import/admission obligation. All original descendants,
valuations, joint labels, common-saving choices, Euler shifts, shortening
complements and exceptional returns remain with their accepted original
proofs. This pass replaces none of them and claims no saving from ignoring
them. The inherited ordinary/Eisenstein scope and contributor credits are
unchanged; the current written c remains c8.

The useful next mathematical question is now sharper than G92's open B
norm: construct residuals with an actual cancellation relation across
prime bands, or an N-dependent family whose full growing-order estimate
and restoration are proved. Trying to bound the unrestricted merged norm,
or adding another fixed quotient moment, cannot provide the desired power.
Moving collars remain possible only with their full exact-collar source
cost. Nonprincipal fixed characters may behave differently; the proof
does not retire a separate nonprincipal-only source estimate.

## 10. Direct source-resolvent consequence

This also rules out a purely reweighted Schur/resolvent repair of the same dictionary. For any positive summable weights v_n and any fixed finite arithmetic seed set E with positive weights u_n, define

 K= sum_(n>=1) v_n (w_(q,n) tensor w_(q,n))
           +sum_(n in E) u_n(f_n tensor f_n).

Because |w_(q,n)|<=q-1, K is positive trace class and

 ker K=(W_q+span{f_n:n in E})^perp.

For the actual target 1 the spectral theorem, exactly as in A08.2, gives

 lim_(lambda down to0) <1,lambda(K+lambda I)^(-1)1>
   = ||P_(ker K)1||^2
   = dist(1,W_q+span{f_n:n in E})^2 >0.                    (B18)

For no seeds this limit is at least J_(q,sigma), and the same lower bound holds for the resolvent at every lambda>0. The failure survives polynomial, exponential or predetermined dyadic-block reweighting, arbitrary finite truncation strategies, and arbitrarily slow proposed o(1) rates. It is the target's genuine positive zero atom for this exact arithmetic dictionary; compactness is not being used as a surrogate for an arithmetic theorem. Adding unbounded genuinely new arithmetic directions is the surviving repair.

This recombines the proved A08 spectral identity with the exact SW34 wavelet source, giving the weakest complete first-gain test a decisive negative answer: even o(1), without a specified power or contraction rate, is impossible for this fixed grid. The larger A08 operator using all original f_n, the variable-ratio A09 correction, and arbitrary-ratio F08 remain open and are not subject to B18's dictionary restriction.

## G223. Critical small-prime payment with its exact margin debit

Use the complete ordinary-character source of
[G173](../[private research revision]/wild62-integration.md): fixed tau>0,1/2<gamma<1,

    a(n)=mu(n)chi(n), g(v)=(2*pi*tau)^-1/2 exp(-v^2/(2tau)),
    U(y)=sum_(n>=1)a(n)g(log n-y), z(y)=e^(-gamma y)U(y),
    I_R=int_0^R y|z|^2, E_R=int_0^R |z|^2.

The coefficient identity a(n)log n=-sum_(d|n)chi(d)Lambda(d)a(n/d)
retains ALL prime powers, including cancellation at squareful n. It gives

    tau z'+(y+tau gamma)z+K1 z+K2 z=0,
    K1 z(y)=sum_p chi(p)log p p^-gamma z(y-log p),
    (tau/2)(|z(R)|^2-|z(0)|^2)+I_R+tau gamma E_R=Q1+Q2,
    Qj=-Re int_0^R conjugate(z)Kj z.                         (223.1)

G173 pays |Q2|<=eta I_R+B_eta for every eta>0 by its summable j>=2
coefficient norm, the complete Gaussian past and a fixed initial interval.
No unknown future bound is used. The same-output prime diagonal is
nonnegative and O(1): its coefficient is1 precisely at squarefree
q-units n=pm, the prime log-weights sum to at most log n, and

    int_R e^(-2gamma y)g(log n-y)^2dy
      =e^(tau gamma^2)n^(-2gamma)/(2sqrt(pi*tau)).

Here is a larger paid small-prime region. Fix a0>0 and set

    b=1/(1-gamma), Y(y)=a0(1+y)^b,
    kappa=a0^(1-gamma)/(1-gamma).

Assign equality to p<=Y(y). PNT and partial summation give
S_gamma(t)=sum_(p<=t)log p p^-gamma~t^(1-gamma)/(1-gamma).
The row sum is(kappa+o(1))y. Apply2|z(y)z(y-log p)|<=|z(y)|^2+|z(y-log p)|^2.
For the column put v=y-log p; the mask gives log p=O(log y), so for
any epsilon>0 and all large y, y<=v/(1-epsilon). Its column sum is at
most S_gamma(a0(1+v/(1-epsilon))^b)<=(kappa/(1-epsilon)+o(1))v.
Both half factors are present. The bounded initial region has finitely
many primes and a fixed bounded source interval. Therefore

    |Q_small(R)|<=(kappa+eta)I_R+B_eta, every R>=0.          (223.2)

The elementary theta(t)<=4(log2)t instead gives4(log2)kappa. This
critical mask is larger than G173's logarithmically reduced mask, but
its nonzero debit must be retained; it does not inherit the old zero
relative price or an unproved hard estimate for another mask.

Let H_a0,R be the ENTIRE p>Y(y), n!=pm expansion with literal summand

    -Re[conjugate(a(n))chi(p)a(m)] log p e^(-2gamma y)
                 *g(log n-y)g(log(pm)-y),                  (223.3)

integrated over0<=y<=R, all m,n>=1. Gaussian majorants justify the
compact-interval sums; diagonal and every complementary source remain.
If THIS jointly chosen mask has constants delta>kappa,B_chi,R0_chi with

    H_a0,R<=(1-delta)I_R+B_chi, every R>=R0_chi,             (223.4)

then pay eta=(delta-kappa)/4 in(223.2) and the higher powers to obtain

    (tau/2)|z(R)|^2+((delta-kappa)/2)I_R+tau gamma E_R<=B'.  (223.5)

Thus U(y)=O_chi(e^(gamma y)). Its complete bilateral transform equals
e^(tau s^2/2)/L(s,chi) initially on Re s>1 and continues normally to
Re s>gamma; the numerator never vanishes. This excludes every zero
at every finite height there, preserves the principal pole and all
natural zeros, and assumes no height-uniform numerator lower bound.
Gamma is common across the family; a0,delta and constants may depend
on a fixed character. This is a one-way ordinary-source return.

Choosing a0=[delta(1-gamma)/2]^(1/(1-gamma)) spends kappa=delta/2;
it does NOT manufacture the margin for the resulting mask. The targets
c=.12,.12515,1/6,1/4 require gamma=.88,.87485,5/6,3/4 and critical powers
25/3,20000/2503,6,4. The .12515 target exceeds conditional c11 by.0000040364.
None of the corresponding complete inequalities(223.4) is proved.

The generic leading coefficient is sharp even for a one-sided form.
For principal chi take arbitrary test input
f_T(y)=exp(i*pi*y/log Y_T)1_[T,T+sqrt T], Y_T=a0(1+T)^b.
Delays lose only O(log T/sqrt T) relative overlap, Y(y)/Y_T->1 uniformly,
and prime-weight mass below Y_T^(1-epsilon) is negligible. On the rest
the real phase tends to-1 as T then epsilon tend to their limits. Hence
-Re<f_T,K_small f_T>/int y|f_T|^2->kappa. A supercritical fixed power b'
instead gives asymptotic kappa T^(b'(1-gamma)-1), which diverges.
These are arbitrary inputs, not the actual z, and do not lower-bound its
signed form. Even granting |U(y)|<=C e^(beta y), gamma<beta<1, the

## 5. Development19: the sharp information in an exterior-area certificate

This is the protected uniformly drawn p<.10 candidate (also p<.01).
Its first test rejects the inference from a positive amount of exterior
area to a power saving. Its viable salvage is an exact quantitative
certificate with all missing trace and dimension costs displayed.

Let T be ANY finite complex matrix, d the dimension of its input space,
A=T^*T, t=tr A, and

    e2=sum_(i<j)lambda_i(A)lambda_j(A)
      =(t^2-tr(A^2))/2 = ||exterior^2 T||_HS^2.              (20)

Zero singular values are included in d; the identity is Cauchy-Binet or
an immediate computation in a singular basis. If d=1, e2=0 and there is
no exterior information. If t=0, T=0. Otherwise d>=2 and

    ||T||_op^2 <= [t+sqrt((d-1)((d-1)t^2-2d e2))]/d.        (21)

Proof: let lambda=||T||_op^2. Cauchy on the other d-1 eigenvalues gives
`tr(A^2)>=lambda^2+(t-lambda)^2/(d-1)`; solve the quadratic using
lambda>=t/d. Equality holds when the other eigenvalues are equal. Thus
(21) is sharp using only t,e2,d. A generic lower bound on area without
an upper trace bound is useless: A=diag(M,1) has e2=M and lambda=M.

For a desired bound ||T||_op<=B, a sufficient certificate is

    t/d <= B^2 <= t,
    e2 >= (t^2-B^4-(t-B^2)^2/(d-1))/2.                     (22)

If B^2>=t, the trace bound alone suffices. If B^2<t/d, no matrix with
that trace can meet the proposed bound. In normalized form, with
`p=tr(A^2)/t^2` and delta=B^2/t in [1/d,1], condition (22) is

    p <= delta^2+(1-delta)^2/(d-1).                         (23)

When 1/d is negligible relative to delta^2, a power-small desired delta
requires p approximately delta^2, equivalently exterior mass within
O(delta^2) of its limiting maximum t^2/2. In general the 1/d term in (23)
must remain. A fixed nonzero fraction of exterior area gives only a
constant bound. Calling an area lower bound a generic anti-alignment
gain hides exactly this cost.

### Exact contact with the original far H form

At fixed original scales, finite ray components and BOTH independent
height variables, normalize original mark arrays by v_i(P)=u_i(P)/sqrt(q_P).
The complete finite far-packet form is a bilinear matrix pairing
`v_2^* T_H v_1`, with each entry DEFINED as its coefficient in the original
form. In constructing that entry retain the complete original g,g' and
row sums, bounded true-core weight, phases a(pi),xi(g), both projectors,
natural zeros, original sharp caps, and exact far mask
`q_pi!=q_pi'`, `|q_pi-q_pi'|>floor(Z^.05)`. There is no altered coefficient,
new positive submask, or renamed prime statistic in this definition.

Then `||v_i||_2^2=Omega_i`. Taking T=T_H in (22), with
`B=Z^epsilon G K S(N,L) P_orig` and the actual original profile factors,
would pay this raw packet. Multiplying once by the original physical
factor `N^-1 G^-2` gives its established physical return. To pay the
all-g packet this criterion must hold for its complete T_H; a fixed-u,v
matrix is not the all-g union. It must also hold with the actual integrable
height/profile growth and the already stated source-tail restorations.
Neither a uniform trace bound nor the exterior bound (22) is proved here.

The matrix T_H may be non-Hermitian; using A=T_H^*T_H is essential.
The far mask itself is not a positive projector. At the SOURCE-index
level it removes every diagonal prime pair. Every Hermitian real part
of that masked coefficient matrix has trace zero; unless zero, it has
both signs. This source-level statement is not an assertion that the
mark-space matrix T_H has zero trace. It does rule out silently applying
PSD Gram arguments directly to the far-mask matrix.

A second abstract test makes the issue visible. A perfectly orthogonal
feature matrix V=I_d has maximal normalized exterior mass. Inserting a
complete off-diagonal source mask M=J_d-I_d leaves `V M V^*=M`, whose
operator norm is d-1. For a symmetric mask omitting at most B0 neighbors
per row, the constant-vector Rayleigh quotient is at least d-1-B0.
This is a matrix counterexample to a mask-free inference, NOT an assertion
that native H features equal V or a lower bound for their signed pairing.

If, purely conditionally, a Frobenius normalization required an amplitude
gain Z^(-.004), it would correspond to delta=Z^(-.008), and (23) asks for
purity about Z^(-.016)+1/d. The existing .004 all-g operator deficit is
not itself such a Frobenius normalization; no actual H gain is credited
to that illustrative exponent conversion. The next real calculation is
the full signed arithmetic trace and fourth contraction of T_H, with all
original indices. These are new estimates to prove, not positivity bonuses.

statement:
# Independent review: actual integrated Hankel source



## R1. Verdict

**Accept H1--H17 at their stated restricted/conditional scopes.** I independently reconstructed the actual convolution identities, the integrated plain-L2 Type I bound, every arithmetic and frequency complement, the sharp endpoint formula and the all-character replacement-source return. I found no mathematical defect requiring an author amendment. None of these results proves OPEN-LOW, OPEN-HK, a new Möbius cancellation exponent or a larger zero-free constant.

The substantive surviving result is the complete comparison

    | ||Gamma[c]_(a,L)||-||T^lo_(Y,R,L,Omega)|| |
      << Y^[2(1-a)] + D_a(X)
           +X^(1-a)(1+log X)/R
           +X^(1-a)(1+log X)^2/Omega,                (R1)
    X=e^(2L), D_a(X)=int_0^L e^[2(1/2-a)t]dt.

It is for the literal changed coefficient c and a full compressed low-frequency operator, with its hyperbolic cap, signs and sharp endpoint. Nonprincipal characters also have an original-source version with c(n)=mu(n)chi(n), using the original periodic character as restoration. The two routes are distinct.

The author's isolated principal prime-corner obstruction is correct. Section R9 below strengthens it to **every fixed ordinary character**, including complex and imprimitive characters, using only the same prime number theorem and a finite phase pigeonhole. A phase class may depend on X; a fixed phase works on an unbounded subsequence. This is an obstruction to paying arithmetic sectors separately. It is never a lower bound for the entire signed source or for its whole low-frequency operator.

Current source-relative c11=`312864909/2500000000=.1251459636`, gamma11=`2187135091/2500000000=.8748540364`, is unchanged. F0/analytic ancestry, inherited positive-slot uniformity and external definition/import/admission remain open. The replacement return explicitly retains the accepted safe region at Re(s)>=1. No public-record or kernel acceptance is asserted. Root owns integration.

## R2. Exact evidence and ancestry

The entire frozen author report is 19409 bytes, SHA256 `cf9a7b69782081d12c5d40fd2d8394e141f3950ffc161afdd0257e793ae45f2e`; its manifest SHA256 is `15aa0ec8db18c64608b361f4f601418f656592c0a53ceff8c34e6c138d4a11f0`. All five manifest-bound files were fully read and their hashes verified. All ten locally retained source pins matched the author receipts at independent intake; the current read is recorded in `input-receipt.json`. That is byte evidence, not proof of a mathematical assertion or of fresh upstream publication.

I read the complete [restricted research revision] G149--G151 integration; the exact G149 review section; W29 review Section7, R29E1--E7; and the DP21--DP24 source passage. These establish the relevant boundary:

* DP21 owns the reciprocal convolution, and DP22 the period-two mean-zero repair.
* W29 R29E1--E7 pays a smooth atomic form on H0^r by derivatives and alternating Poisson. It retains all ordered factors and restores the full signed operator.
* G149 owns the integrated full-rectangle Hankel growth return and the balanced-block argument. It is not a new result of this author packet.
* The present addition is a direct full plain-L2 Type I estimate for the integrated source, the complete sharp-endpoint frequency complement, and the actual isolated prime-sector obstruction. It does not transfer a Sobolev estimate to plain L2 by assertion.

The ordinary prime number theorem used solely in the corner obstruction was independently checked at [NIST DLMF 27.2.3](https://dlmf.nist.gov/27.2.E3). No prime number theorem in progressions, zero-density estimate or uniform growing-modulus result is imported. The inspection date 2026-10-12 is not a claim about the theorem's publication date. Broad source/operator ancestry and the prior authors retain credit; there is no literature-priority claim. Credit also remains with the project participants, OpenAI, Hailey and Akash.

## R3. Literal coefficients, all zeros and the Type I theorem

To avoid the author's overloaded a, write alpha(n)=mu(n)chi(n), and use a only for the real weight, 0<a<1. An ordinary Dirichlet character is extended by zero at nonunits. It is completely multiplicative even there. Hence

    (alpha*chi)(n)=chi(n)sum_(d|n)mu(d)=delta_1(n).

For alpha0=alpha 1_(n<=Y) and alpha1=alpha-alpha0, convolution in the full sequence ring gives

    alpha=2alpha0-alpha0*alpha0*chi+alpha1*alpha1*chi. (R2)

Both ordered factors and all shared primes are present. This is not a coprime convolution. Individual pieces may fail to vanish at squareful n; their complete signed recombination restores alpha's squareful and ramified zeros. The n=1 term is retained. The identity holds for real cutoffs through their floor, and in particular for integer Y as used here.

For a restoration sequence b with partial sum B(y), zero for y<1 and bounded in modulus by C_b, extend

    h_b(v)=e^(-av)B(e^v)1_(v>=0).

Then ||h_b||_1<=C_b/a. For each k>=1,

    e^[-a(t+u)]B(e^(t+u)/k)
       =k^(-a)h_b(t+u-log k).                       (R3)

Reflect an input g on (0,L) into (-L,0), zero-extend it to the real line, and convolve with the translated h_b. Restriction back to (0,L) has norm at most one. Young's L1--L2 bound therefore proves that the full square operator in (R3) has norm at most C_b k^(-a)/a. Translation costs no norm, and no differentiability of g or endpoint trace is required. This argument includes every rectangle of the original square.

Triangle over d,e<=Y now gives

    ||Gamma[alpha0*alpha0*b]_(a,L)||
       <=(C_b/a)(sum_(d<=Y)|alpha(d)|d^(-a))^2
       <<_(a,b)Y^[2(1-a)].                           (R4)

Cancellation in B is used before the absolute sum over d,e. Replacing b by |b| would destroy the uniform C_b and would not prove (R4). An atom z(n) gives L1 mass |z(n)|n^(-a)/a, so its finite sum costs that weighted atomic mass.

For every nonprincipal chi modulo q, including imprimitive ones, the complete period sum is zero and |sum_(n<=y)chi(n)|<=q. Apply (R4) to b=chi and the atom bound to 2alpha0 in (R2). This proves H4 for the original alpha source, with a constant depending on a,q, uniformly in L and Y. No long-factor cancellation was assumed.

The principal exception is real. At Y=1 the removed sequence is 2delta_1-chi. For principal chi its partial sum is `-(phi(q)/q)x+O_q(1)`, and its integrated kernel has the rank-one part `-(phi(q)/q)e^[(1-a)(t+u)]`. The bounded partial-sum remainder has bounded operator norm by (R3). Reverse triangle gives exactly the author's exponential norm asymptotic, including O_(a,q)(1). This term cannot receive a gamma<1 budget in isolation. It is not a lower bound for the complete signed source.

## R4. Dilation repair: exact source and periodicity

Fix one prime r not dividing q, before the asymptotic variable and every live test. Let

    kappa=delta_1-r chi(r)delta_r,
    c=kappa*alpha, b=kappa*chi.

Then, with the indicated integer divisibility,

    c(n)=mu(n)chi(n)-r chi(r)1_(r|n)mu(n/r)chi(n/r),
    b(n)=chi(n)-r chi(r)1_(r|n)chi(n/r).             (R5)

In particular c is not alpha. It may be nonzero at squareful n containing r^2. Since r is prime to q, a ramified n makes both terms zero; no imprimitive Euler factor has been erased. The factor r in the multiplier is necessary for the principal mean to cancel.

The second term of b has period qr, as does the first. Summing one whole period gives zero: for nonprincipal chi both complete character sums vanish; for principal chi, chi(r)=1 and the two means coincide. More explicitly, if

    C_chi(y)=1_(chi principal)(phi(q)/q)y+E_chi(y),
    |E_chi(y)|<=q,

then

    B(y)=C_chi(y)-r chi(r)C_chi(y/r),
    |B(y)|<=q(1+r).                                 (R6)

This also holds at y<1 with the declared zero partial sum. Complex phases require no positivity. Convolving (R2) by kappa gives H7 with exactly the altered c and b. The weighted atom mass of the two kappa coefficients is 1+r^(1-a), yielding

    ||Gamma[c]-Gamma[alpha1*alpha1*b]||
       <=(2/a)(1+r^(1-a))A_Y+(q(1+r)/a)A_Y^2,
    A_Y=sum_(d<=Y)|alpha(d)|d^(-a).

The difference of norms is bounded by this operator difference. This proves H8; there is no positivity assertion about either signed summand.

## R5. Complete quantitative return of the changed source

Initially Re(s)>1, the actual Dirichlet series is

    C(s)=sum_n c(n)n^(-s)=m_r(s)/L(s,chi),
    m_r(s)=1-chi(r)r^(1-s).                          (R7)

The coefficients are bounded by 1+r, so all initial integrals, series and one s derivative converge absolutely. The accepted G149 exponential test therefore gives

    Q(z)=-d/ds [m_r(s)/(sL(s,chi))], s=a+z.         (R8)

Its growth adapter applies to this source without a new arithmetic hypothesis beyond the stated full Gamma[c] norm bound. For intervals I_i,I_j of length one, opposite translations preserve t+u and put their rectangle in the square with upper endpoint (i+j)/2+1. If K_a(L)<=C exp(2eta L), multiplying by the heavier weight sigma>a gives a block cost `C exp(2eta) exp[-(sigma-a-eta)(i+j)]`. Summing all i,j is finite for sigma>a+eta. This includes arbitrarily unbalanced rectangles. It uses no positivity or self-adjointness of the source: for complex chi the bilinear form is turned into the usual operator norm by conjugating a test input, not chi.

Consequently the every-epsilon/all-L growth bound with eta=gamma-a+epsilon gives holomorphy of Q in Re(s)>gamma, taking epsilon below the desired horizontal margin before summing. Constants may depend on the fixed character, r, real weight and loss.

Because |chi(r)|=1, every zero of m_r lies exactly on Re(s)=1. At a zero rho of L with gamma<Re(rho)<1, m_r(rho) is nonzero and rho is nonzero. If the L zero has multiplicity j, the quantity inside the derivative in (R8) has a genuine order-j pole and its derivative has an order-(j+1) pole with nonzero leading coefficient. Meromorphic identity continuation contradicts Q's holomorphy. No cancellation is supplied by differentiation.

This proves the claimed strip exclusion only below Re(s)=1 directly from this single multiplier. The packet explicitly invokes the already accepted source-relative exclusion for Re(s)>=1 to cover that line and the outer region. That is a legitimate retained assumption, and its inherited obligations remain visible. It must not be silently dropped: a hypothetical L zero on a multiplier zero could be canceled in (R7). The principal pole at s=1 is not a zero; its reciprocal is holomorphic with a zero and causes no false contradiction. Natural imprimitive factors remain literal throughout. The argument supplies every fixed finite height, not a height-uniform lower bound or a growing-conductor constant.

For nonprincipal chi one may instead retain H4 and the original reciprocal G149 return, which has no m_r cancellation issue. The report correctly separates this original-source route from the repaired all-character route. No norm comparison returning Gamma[c] to Gamma[alpha] for principal chi is assumed.

## R6. Diagonal and high gcd: all restoration labels are included

The long-factor cumulative source is exactly

    sum_(d,e>Y,de<=x) alpha(d)alpha(e) B(x/(de)).     (R9)

It includes the ordered pairs, their shared primes and the complete restoration sum. The product cap gives d,e<=X/(Y+1) and ell<=X/(Y+1)^2; the individual bounds do not replace the joint condition de ell<=X.

Partition (R9) into d=e, then d!=e with gcd(d,e)>R, then its remaining d!=e, gcd<=R sector. These are disjoint and exhaustive, including equality at the gcd threshold in the last sector.

The diagonal is bounded in modulus by C_b sqrt(x), even though chi(d)^2 need not be nonnegative. Its kernel is dominated by `C_b e^[(1/2-a)(t+u)]`. Cauchy--Schwarz in each variable bounds the full operator by C_b D_a(X). This is H9a. At a=1/2 the value is L; at a<1/2 its exponent is 1/2-a; at a>1/2 it is bounded. No squareful contribution of this component was discarded.

For the off-diagonal high-gcd sector write d=gu,e=gv with g the actual gcd, then discard (u,v)=1 only inside a positive count. Since

    # {(u,v):uv<=w} <=w(1+log w),

the total number with gcd>R is at most

    x(1+log x)sum_(g>R)g^(-2)
       <<x(1+log x)/R.                              (R10)

Take |B|<=C_b only after its complete restoration sum. The resulting kernel is dominated by a constant times `(1+log X)e^[(1-a)(t+u)]/R`. Its rank-one envelope has norm O_a(X^(1-a)), proving H9b. This is a bound on the entire isolated operator; cross terms need no separate squared-energy assertion because the subsequent comparison uses operator triangle. It is an ordinary-integer result, not payment of an Eisenstein/native H sector.

## R7. Fourier compression and the sharp endpoint

Let C_Y(n) denote precisely the remaining masked coefficient in Section R6, including its gcd mask, and S_Y its partial sum. The observed causal kernel is

    k(v)=e^(-av)S_Y(e^v)1_(0<=v<=log X).

It gives the exact remaining operator on (0,L)^2. For s=a+i tau, integrate each cumulative atom, which is a finite operation:

    int_(log n)^(log X) e^(-sv)dv
       =(n^(-s)-X^(-s))/s, n<=X.

Thus

    hat k(tau)=[sum_(n<=X)C_Y(n)n^(-s)-X^(-s)S_Y(X)]/s. (R11)

No half-weight convention at integers changes this Lebesgue integral. The atom at n=X has zero contribution; the corresponding t=u=L corner is a null set. Noninteger X uses its exact floor in both sums. The endpoint term is essential, and the author has retained it.

Use |b(ell)|<=1+r and discard masks only for the positive upper bound. Summing ell first gives

    sum_(n<=X)|C_Y(n)|n^(-a)
       <<_(a,r)X^(1-a)sum_(de<=X)1/(de)
       <<X^(1-a)(1+log X)^2.                        (R12)

The actual partial sum is smaller than the corresponding absolute restoration count: `|S_Y(X)|<=C_b X(1+log X)`. Both numerator terms of (R11) are consequently bounded. Since a is fixed and positive,

    |hat k(tau)|<<_(a,q,r)X^(1-a)(1+log X)^2/(1+|tau|).

Split this whole symbol by the two indicators |tau|<=Omega and >Omega, on the full real line. Plancherel says that each is a bounded full-line multiplier with norm at most its supremum. Reflection, zero extension and compression all have norm one. Therefore

    ||T^hi||<<X^(1-a)(1+log X)^2/Omega.             (R13)

The low-frequency kernel is no longer causal or compactly supported. That is harmless because it is defined as the full-line multiplier followed by the stated compression, not as a guessed local kernel. The two compressed pieces sum exactly to the original observed operator. Every coupled time rectangle remains. No square-root gain is inferred from a scalar average.

In particular OPEN-LOW concerns the complete symbol (R11) before compression, or more weakly its complete compressed operator. A sup-norm bound for that symbol is sufficient but is not an equivalent necessary condition on the compressed operator. The author states this distinction correctly. Omitting the endpoint, dropping the mixed hyperbolic cap, or asserting norm monotonicity under a signed arithmetic restriction would invalidate the proof; none occurs.

Combining the genuine operator differences from R4, R6 and (R13) yields (R1). It is valid also on the original nonprincipal source with b=chi and C_b=q. There are no unpriced principal, unit, short-factor, diagonal, high-gcd or high-frequency pieces within this stated source decomposition.

## R8. Corridor costs and exact remaining assumption

Fix 0<a<gamma<1, gamma>1/2, and 0<nu<min(gamma-a,gamma-1/2). Set for large X

    delta=(gamma-a-nu)/[2(1-a)],
    omega=1-gamma+2nu,

Both high-gcd and high-frequency powers are X^(gamma-a-2nu); their logarithms fit the spare nu. If a<1/2, the diagonal's exponent 1/2-a is strictly smaller than gamma-a-nu. If a=1/2 its logarithm is smaller than that positive power, and if a>1/2 it is bounded. This proves the author's common error exponent for all permitted a, not only a=1/2.

Removing the finitely many ramified primes has no asymptotic effect. For principal chi the isolated kernel on J^2 is exactly `|P_X|(|P_X|-1)e^[-a(t+u)]`. Its compressed rank-one norm is

so the full isolated operator has norm at least a positive constant times X^(1-a)/(log X)^2. This proves H16--H17, including its normalization and rectangular support.

**Independent extension to all fixed characters.** Let d=|image(chi on q-units)|, a fixed finite integer. Partition P_X by the actual value chi(p). One class P_(X,lambda) has at least |P_X|/d members. For its distinct pairs,

    >>_(a,chi) X^(1-a)/(log X)^2.                    (R15)
