## 4. Development26: the exact fermionic Ward defect is coherent

This develops the most-different reserved card after its two-prime test.
It is a source-compatible obstruction to a specified supersymmetric
averaging mechanism, not an impossibility theorem for operator methods.
Finite exterior encoding is prior work (R31/T26 and U-DETERMINANT); the
calculation here identifies the proposed spectral-gap defect explicitly.

Let P be a finite ordered set of primes. Use the 2^|P|-dimensional basis
e_S, S subset P, with parity (-1)^|S|. Creation a_p^* inserts p when absent,
with sign (-1)^(number of elements of S preceding p), and is zero when p
is present. Its adjoint removes p. Direct basis checking gives the CAR
relations `{a_p,a_q^*}=delta_pq I`, `{a_p,a_q}=0`. Arithmetic hard-core
insertion without that sign COMMUTES at distinct primes; fermionic
creation ANTICOMMUTES. On the two-prime vacuum the two creation orders
give opposite signs, while multiplying the two integer prime labels
does not. An ordering string cannot simply be dropped.

For arbitrary w_p not all zero put

    Q=sum_p w_p a_p^*, W=sum_p |w_p|^2,
    Q^2=0, QQ^*+Q^*Q=W I.                                  (16)

For any even matrix Z, finite-dimensional supertrace cyclicity gives

    W Str(Z)=Str(Q^*[Q,Z]).                                 (17)

Proof: multiply the anticommutator in (16) by Z. Since Q and Q^* are
odd and Z is even, `Str(QQ^*Z)=-Str(Q^*ZQ)`; the remaining term is
`Str(Q^*QZ)`. This proves (17), with the ordinary commutator [Q,Z].
The positive spectral gap W has not yet estimated its defect.

For the Euler diagonal `Z(s)e_S=product_(p in S)z_p e_S`,
`z_p=chi(p)p^-s`, one has

    Str Z(s)=product_(p in P)(1-z_p)=: E_P(s).

Every off-diagonal p!=q term in the right side of (17) has zero trace,
and its p=p term is EXACTLY

    Str(conj(w_p)a_p [w_p a_p^*,Z(s)])=|w_p|^2 E_P(s).        (18)

All prime contributions are positively weighted copies of the same
Euler product. Their triangle inequality is equality, so normalization
by W yields no prime averaging or spectral-gap saving. In Re(s)>0,
E_P(s) is nonzero; hence Z(s) cannot commute with a nonzero Q of this
form. The putative supersymmetric cancellation premise fails precisely
at the arithmetic weight, not at an unexplained analytic remainder.

The more important statement retains the ACTUAL Gaussian. Set

    Z_y e_S=chi(n_S)g_tau(log n_S-y)e_S, n_S=product_(p in S)p,
    U_P(y)=Str Z_y=sum_(n squarefree, p|n=>p in P)
                              mu(n)chi(n)g_tau(log n-y).     (19)

For each fixed p, partitioning subsets according to whether they contain
p shows that the p=p supertrace in (17) is exactly `|w_p|^2 U_P(y)`.
Indeed it is the sum over S not containing p of
`(-1)^|S| [Z_y(S)-Z_y(S union {p})]`; these are ALL the terms of U_P,
with their actual signs, characters and Gaussian shifts. Mixed terms
still have zero diagonal. Thus the entire Ward defect is `W U_P(y)`:
the apparent new observable is the old signed field, once per prime.

This is not confined to an artificial fixed cutoff. If P contains every
prime <=`2X exp(C sqrt(log X))`, all omitted integers exceed that bound.
Since each coefficient has modulus at most1, the complete omitted
Gaussian tail is `X^(1-C^2/(2tau)+o(1))` on [X,2X], by the elementary
integral bound for sum g_tau(log(n/x)). Taking C sufficiently large
restores U to any prescribed smaller error. Ramified character zeros
are retained automatically; squarefree support is exactly right for U.
This does not identify the Fock construction with the different f3 field.

Hence a bound on the full Ward defect better than theta6 would be a
restatement of the complete reciprocal-detector estimate. Bounding the
individual prime defects gives no gain. A viable different route would
need a genuinely different Q/observable whose complete boundary is
provably cheaper, plus its exact coefficient recovery. No such boundary
was produced. The finite two-prime check and the source-level proof agree.

Subsequent source comparison also found the frozen W46 Section4 weighted
Hodge/spectral-gap obstruction. It was still under independent review at
intake and is not used as a theorem dependency here. Its per-integer f3
harmonic realization differs from this prime-subset reciprocal-U Ward
identity, but the shared lesson is the same unpaid weighted defect. The
two must not be counted as independent arithmetic progress.

### 6.2 A paid weighted-divisor repair and its complete return

The actual multiplicative equations use a weighted triangular map, not a conservative coupling. On {1,...,N} define

    C_(n,d)=chi(n/d)1_(d divides n),
    A_(n,d)=mu(n/d)chi(n/d)1_(d divides n).

Both diagonals are1 and AC=CA=I, because a*chi=delta in Dirichlet convolution for a(n)=mu(n)chi(n). All prime powers and natural zeros occur. For any candidate vector v set e=Cv-e_1. Then v-a=Ae, exactly. For every integer interval (L,U] within [1,N],

    sum_(L<n<=U)v_n - [M(U)-M(L)]
      =sum_(k<=U)e_k [M(floor(U/k))-M(floor(L/k))].       (S28-R)

This follows by finite divisor summation, grouping n=kd before taking any norm. For L=0 it reads sum v-M(N)=sum e_k M(floor(N/k)). There is no independent-error assumption, missing k=1 source term, or endpoint smoothing. The checker validates complex and ramified examples with full intervals.

Consequently a proved O(N^(gamma+epsilon)) bound for BOTH the candidate readout sum v and the entire signed response on the right implies the same bound for M(N), with the usual all-scale/common-character quantifiers and the all-height Mellin return. This is a legitimate repair target, but its response is not automatically cheap. For unrestricted complex errors with weighted TV sum w_k|e_k|, the exact scalar operator norm is

    max_(k<=N) |M(floor(N/k))|/w_k.

Triangle gives the upper bound and an error supported at a maximizing k with aligning phase attains it. The k=1 term already contains M(N). The unconditional alternative is at most N sum |e_k|/k, with exponent1 in that generic price. Restrictions on actual compatible defects can escape this norm obstruction; they must be stated and proved. This is the established paid inverse/adjoint principle (G107 and W54-X23), now written for the seed's literal two-filtration ambition, not a new inverse family or a proof that all signed couplings fail.

## 2. General normalized columns and the correct MP dimension

Let F_u be a product of J fixed normalized polynomials with lengths X_1,...,X_J and bounded row-independent coefficients, all in one common phi_u orientation. The actual plain factors and original prime slots are examples. Put B=product X_j. Multiplication gives

    F_u=sum_b lambda_b psi_u(b)^e,
    lambda_b=B^(-1/2) sum_(b_1...b_J=b) product_j c_j(b_j),
    support q_b << B,  |lambda_b| << B^(-1/2) d_J(b).     (2)

Fixed nu, the original slot characters, different smooth profiles and independent norm heights stay in c_j. Every ordered tuple and every collision remains. A common puncture means the exact zero coefficient1_((b,R)=1). Disjoint slot pools do not imply that a slot is disjoint from a plain factor. In particular, a plain prime power p^5 and its slot p contribute a sixth-power column with the original p-hole; it is not the constant character1.

Write b=d h^6 uniquely, with d sixth-power-free; there is NO condition(d,h)=1. For a fixed h,

    psi_u(dh^6)=psi_u(d)1_((u,h)=1),
    sum_d |lambda_(dh^6)|^2 << B^epsilon q_h^(-6).        (3)

The second estimate follows from (2), ideal counting q_d<<B/q_h^6 and the divisor bound. Apply(1) to each fixed h and drop the h-row restriction only in the positive norm. Minkowski then sums q_h^(-3), which converges over ideals. Thus for sixth-power-free rows q_u<<U,

    sum_u^(6)|F_u|^2 << (UB)^epsilon T(U,B).             (4)

For ALL rows write u=a e^6, retaining units and S-parts as above. The identity is psi_(ae^6)(b)=psi_a(b)1_((b,e)=1). For fixed e this is a fixed column mask, so(4) applies at row length U/q_e^6. Summing e gives

    sum_(0<q_u<<U)|F_u|^2 << (UB)^epsilon T_all(U,B),
    T_all=U+B U^(1/6)+U^(5/6)B^(1/3)+U^(1/3)B^(5/6).  (5)

The B U^(1/6) term comes from the number of sixth-power roots. It cannot be removed by relabeling them as a finite set. No principal or fixed-inducing row has been discarded. Both(4),(5) are O(U^(1+epsilon)) when B<=U^(1/2).

    2m+v<=1/2, or n1+n2+v<=1/2.                       (6)

The proposed m+v<=1/2 pertains to |S Q|^2, not |S|^4|Q|^2. It cannot replace 2m+6kappa v<=1. ### A2. Uniform first- and second-order comparison

Suppose, as an explicit input, |M_chi(t)|<=C_chi t^beta for all t>0, where beta>0. Taking beta=1,C_chi=1 is unconditional. A stronger buffered summatory bound may be substituted only if its own source contract is available; it is not inferred here merely from the number c11.

For real r>=2 define

    k_r(u)=(1-u/r)_+^r,
    B_r(x)=R_r(rx)=sum_n a(n) k_r(n/x),
    V_r(x)=2B_(2r)(x)-B_r(x),
    A(u)=u-u^2/2,
    K1(beta)=5*2^(beta+2)Gamma(beta+2)+2^(beta+3)Gamma(beta+3),
    K2(beta)=12*2^(beta+3)Gamma(beta+3)
             +4*2^(beta+4)Gamma(beta+4)+2^(beta+5)Gamma(beta+5).

Then, uniformly in all x>0 and r>=2,

    |B_r(x)-E_chi(x)| <= C_chi K1(beta) x^beta/r,
    |V_r(x)-E_chi(x)| <= (3/2)C_chi K2(beta) x^beta/r^2.  (A2)

No coefficient tail, moving-order constant, last integer or second branch has been suppressed. V_r includes the support out to2rx and both ordered cross terms in any squared norm. Its literal coefficient weight is2(1-n/(2rx))_+^(2r)-(1-n/(rx))_+^r.

Proof. For0<u<r, k_r'(u)=-(1-u/r)^(r-1); for u>r it is0. The function is continuous and absolutely continuous, and for r>=2 its derivative also matches0 at r. On0<=u<=r/2 let

    z_r(u)=(r-1)log(1-u/r)+u.

The log series gives z_r<=u/r,

    |z_r| <= (u+u^2)/r,
    |z_r-A(u)/r| <= (u^2/2+2u^3/3)/r^2.                (A3)

Indeed the terms of order>=3 have absolute sum at most
(r-1)(u/r)^3/[3(1-u/r)] <=2u^3/(3r^2). Using
|exp(z)-1-z|<=(z^2/2)exp(max(z,0)) proves

    |k_r'(u)+exp(-u)| <=(5u+u^2)exp(-u/2)/r,
    |k_r'(u)+exp(-u)[1+A(u)/r]|
                       <=P(u)exp(-u/2)/r^2,             (A4)
    P(u)=12u^2+4u^3+u^4.

Here the first inequality on the short range even holds with u+u^2. For u>=r/2 use |k_r'|<=exp(-u/2) on its support and0 outside, and r<=2u. After multiplying the proposed second inequality by r^2, the two constant terms cost at most8u^2, the u/r term at most2u^2 and the u^2/(2r) term at mostu^3. This is bounded by P(u). The first inequality follows there from2<=4u/r. Thus (A4) holds on the entire positive half-line, including the part beyond the finite support.

Abel/Stieltjes integration, with vanishing endpoint terms, gives

    sum_n a(n)h(n/x)=-int_0^infty M_chi(xu)h'(u)du.       (A5)

Apply (A4) to h=k_r-exp(-u), then integrate u^beta times its bound. For the second line write k_r'=-exp(-u)[1+A(u)/r]+e_r; the A/r terms cancel exactly in2k_(2r)'-k_r'+exp(-u). The complete remainder is at most(2/4+1)P exp(-u/2)/r^2. Its integral is(3/2)K2(beta)/r^2. This proves (A2), including the infinite exponential tail. Constants are deliberately coarse and explicit; their finiteness and uniformity matter more than their size.

### 5.1 Two-mode recurrence and precision

Fix lambda>1. In the toy two-state evolution, the signal and nuisance
coordinates evolve by diag(lambda^rho,lambda^beta), with real beta and
complex rho. The scalar observation is

    y_j=A lambda^(rho*j)+B lambda^(beta*j).

Applying T-lambda^beta I gives eigenvalues lambda^rho-lambda^beta and0,
so the scalar counterterm is exactly

    y_(j+1)-lambda^beta y_j
       =A(lambda^rho-lambda^beta)lambda^(rho*j).     (A10)

It kills the nuisance, but preserves the signal's growth exponent when
the multiplier is nonzero. Signal is also killed when
rho=beta+2pi i k/log lambda. If Re rho>=beta+eta, the normalized
multiplier |1-lambda^(beta-rho)| is uniformly at least1-lambda^-eta;
on Re rho=beta it can vanish. There is no general exponent improvement
from the recurrence identity itself.

For a scale-dependent coefficient c_j=lambda^beta(1+epsilon_j), the
pure nuisance B lambda^(beta*j) leaves residual
-B epsilon_j lambda^(beta*(j+1)). To bound this by C lambda^(gamma*j)
with gamma<beta and fixed nonzero B requires

    |epsilon_j| <= C' lambda^(-(beta-gamma)*j).      (A11)

Merely epsilon_j tending to0 or having finite sum does not imply that
power-rate accuracy. This is an exact necessity for the stated toy;
it is not a universal obstruction to every nonlinear renormalization.

In addition to (4.1), first take b=3/2,k=6 and gamma>=3/4 for the

unramified compensator prime p use (4.2), and define the literal finite sum

    T_p,chi,X(x)=sum_(d>U,e>V,L<de*l<=M)
        mu(d)mu(e)chi(de*l)(1-p*1_(p|l))
        exp(-de*l/x^(3/2)-i(de*l/x)^6).                  (5.1)

The sum includes ALL positive integer l, both ordered d,e variables,
noncoprime pairs and both sharp physical cuts. Each original mu factor
and character zero is left in place. No arithmetic projector or residue
class has been deleted. The internal period is the actual pq, not the
primitive conductor.

The n<=L portion of R costs O_(p,eta)(L^(1+eta)) by its divisor bound.
The n>M portion costs O(X^(gamma+epsilon)) in both L1 and L2 by (3.2).
Equation (2.1), (4.3) and the complete short-term bound then give

    ||C_p-T_p,chi,X||_j <<_(chi,p,gamma,epsilon)
                                  X^(gamma+epsilon), j=1,2. (5.2)

All constants are uniform over the entire real shell and every dyadic X
above a fixed onset. In particular an every-epsilon bound at exponent
gamma for T is equivalent to that bound for C_p, separately in L1 and
L2. L2 implies L1; the converse is not asserted. The price of each full
complement is an actual norm, so the triangle inequality pays every
interaction with T and between the removed terms. No independent height
has been identified with another, and no square expansion drops a cross.

The weakest complete developed premise is the L1 bound for a fixed
TWO-PRIME bank, for every fixed ordinary chi:

    for each p in {p1,p2}, for every epsilon>0,
    integral_X^(2X)|T_p,chi,X(x)|dx/x
                   <<_(chi,p,gamma,epsilon)X^(gamma+epsilon). (OPEN-T)

The primes are fixed once for chi BEFORE epsilon,X or a target zero.
They are distinct and unramified. If chi is nonprincipal choose p1 with
chi(p1)!=1; such a prime exists, since a unit integer with nontrivial
chi-value factors into unramified primes. For a principal character any
two distinct unramified primes suffice. No theorem uniform in growing q
or primes is claimed. A sum of the two L1 norms is equivalent to these
two premises with constants changed; there is no unpriced bank readout.

Here is the complete detector return, including the line Re s=1. The
accepted contour calculation applies termwise to c_p, whose coefficients
are bounded. At K=1,b=3/2,k=6 it gives on the initial absolute half-plane
sigma>3/2, and then by continuation,

    H_p(s)=integral_0^infinity C_p(1/t)t^(s-1)dt
          =A_0(s) P_p(s)/L(s,chi)+E_p(s),

    P_p(s)=1-chi(p)*p^(1-s).                            (5.3)

E_p is normally holomorphic for sigma>1/2, by the accepted remainder
bound multiplied by p+1. A_0 is holomorphic and nonzero for sigma>0.
From (OPEN-T) and (5.2), shell summation with epsilon smaller than a
compact real-part margin makes H_p holomorphic on sigma>gamma. The
x tending to zero complement is bounded by (p+1)/(exp(x^(-b))-1).
It pays every fixed Mellin derivative. All finite heights are covered by
arbitrary compacts; no uniform bound as |Im s| tends to infinity is used.

Every zero of P_p has sigma=1. The two polynomials P_p1,P_p2 have no
common zero with nonzero imaginary part: because chi-values are roots
of unity, a common zero 1+it would make both t*log(p_j)/(2pi) rational.
For t!=0 this makes log(p1)/log(p2) rational, contradicting unique prime
factorization. At t=0 a common zero requires chi(p1)=chi(p2)=1. The
choice of p1 excludes this for nonprincipal chi. For principal chi it
leaves only s=1, the allowed pole, not a zero. Thus (5.3) for the TWO
fixed sources excludes every zero of the actual meromorphic L throughout
sigma>gamma, with the principal pole exception retained. This argument
does not silently import nonvanishing on the entire line sigma=1.

The actual imprimitive L and its finite Euler holes occur throughout.
Their Re s=0 zeros do not enter this half-plane, but no factor has been
removed in obtaining (5.3). The common gamma is selected before chi;

is ordinary-character scope only, with no new Hecke or conductor-uniform
claim and no resolution of the external root-definition/admission issue.

The exact useful rows are:

|313/2500=.1252|2187/2500|5313/5000|687/1000|687/2000|939/2500|

### F08.N1 — New pass 2: admissible residue wavelets and multiresolution correction

Gemini's zero-mean wavelet suggestion cannot replace the arithmetic span by arbitrary functions: that would make approximation trivial while destroying the zeta transfer. A valid wavelet must be an explicit finite combination of \(f_n\), for example balanced \(nf_n-mf_m\) with \(m,n>N\), which vanishes on the fitted prefix. Orthogonalize a **block of those arithmetic differences** in the exact heavy-tail Gram, retaining its later periodic repetitions.

The first missing lemma is a quantitative block-capture and leakage statement, not wavelet orthogonality. One workable target is a compatible sequence with \(\sum\delta_j=\infty\) and total later-shell leakage at step j at most a fixed fraction of its captured energy. Analyze two consecutive blocks, then the infinite tail, with certified smallest Gram eigenvalues. If exact prefix preservation produces intolerable leakage, switch to damped overlap corrections and carry the residual on the old blocks. This differs from the original first-shell inverse by forcing the next-shell/tail interaction into the theorem. An ordinary wavelet basis or a numerical pseudoinverse without a coefficient map earns no progress.

## 3. Author Section A: the fixed-arity source and its proper-sector test

Write a=mu chi, h=chi, m=a 1_(n<=U), u=a-m, so a*h=delta_1 with all presented-modulus zeros literal. For fixed k>=2 and an unramified prime p set q_p=delta_1-p chi(p)delta_p and b_p=q_p*h. Binomial expansion and a*h=delta_1 prove

    q_p^(k-1)*a = u^k*b_p^(k-1)
      +sum_(j=1)^k (-1)^(j+1) binom(k,j)
          m^j*q_p^(k-j)*b_p^(j-1),                  (R1)

where powers and products are Dirichlet convolution and b_p^0=delta_1. The coefficient p chi(p) matters for this version. Older R6's unphased choice also has a mean-zero periodic cofactor in its stated setting: nonprincipal chi already has mean zero, and principal chi(p)=1. These are not competing normalizations.

The cofactor series B_p(s)=(1-chi(p)p^(1-s))L(s,chi) is entire. For fixed k, 0<delta<=1 and U=X^((1-delta)/k), every restoration product in (R1) is at most X^(1-delta), up to fixed p-shifts. For a positive fixed Gaussian width, the Mellin factor exp(tau s^2/2) dominates polynomial vertical growth on each fixed line. Shift the entire B_p(s)^j integral to a sufficiently negative fixed line; its scale is at least a fixed multiple of X^delta. Every fixed coefficient count and shift has a polynomial cost absorbed by choosing that line farther left. The j=1 delta-cofactor term instead has direct super-polynomial Gaussian decay. These operations justify the full real-shell restoration. Constants depend on k, delta, p, q and the demanded power; nothing establishes growing k. This is the recorded W01/W35 and W48/R6 construction.

For principal chi, take n to be a product of k distinct primes in [X^(1/k),2^(1/k)X^(1/k)], excluding ramified primes and p. Each exceeds U eventually. Since U>=1, every long factor is at least 2; a factorization into k long factors must allocate one prime to each, leaving cofactor 1. The hard coefficient is exactly (-1)^k k!. Fixed-proportion prime counts give at least a constant times X/log^k X such products in [X,2X]. Their Gaussian weights are uniformly bounded below throughout a fixed real shell, so their selected same-sign field has that lower bound pointwise, and hence in normalized shell L1 or L2. The whole hard field can cancel against other cells. This is a decisive obstruction to separately paying this particular sector at a smaller power, not to a complete signed estimate.

The author's stated delta>0 alone is insufficient for that coefficient and its Omega(n)<k support claim. If delta>1 then U<1, m=0 and u=a, so R_k=q_p^(k-1)*a; on p-free n its coefficient is mu(n)chi(n), rather than the k! expression, and lower-degree terms survive. The selected principal sector still has linear exponent, but the displayed exact coefficient needs the restriction above. This is an explicit correction, not an unrecorded change to the frozen author source.

Selberg's 1949 theorem (1.1), theta(x)~x, gives the fixed-interval prime count by partial summation; no short-interval or increasing-k uniformity is used. Source: [Selberg's original paper](https://www.math.lsu.edu/~mahlburg/teaching/handouts/2014-7230/Selberg-ElemPNT1949.pdf), printed p.305, read 13 October 2026. The page was tool-read, not downloaded and byte-hashed.

# W48 — higher-order return from the same complete window energy

**Written result for independent review; no increased zero-free constant is proved.** The accepted source-relative endpoint remains c6=125139/1000000=.125139, theta6=.874861. The main result removes the first-order O(H) approximation ceiling in the existing G72 short-window interface. It uses precisely the same complete arithmetic energy and pays all endpoint and tail errors. That energy is still unestimated at any improved exponent.

## Current checkpoint

- Objective: useful rigorous progress beyond the frozen c6 premise, for every fixed ordinary Dirichlet character and all heights; no growing-conductor extension.
- Owner/checkout: W48, current task [private operational identifier omitted], QRH Windows checkout. Exclusive writer scope `[restricted provenance path] research revision]-drafts/wild48`; controller owns canonical state, tracker and Git.
- Completed: 30 seeds and suffixes frozen before detailed history; three deterministic reservations, then three full-pool uniform draws; all six first tests; exact source deduplication; one substantive return refinement and its countermodel consequence; exact finite indexing and rational budget checks.
- Constraints: no children, external model providers, formalization, kernel work, canonical research edits, tracker or Git writes. All source coefficients, natural zeros and complete windows remain literal.
- Author mathematics and exact checks are complete. Independent review and the complete actual-arithmetic window bound remain OPEN. The final receipt records whole-file readback/hashes; the normal own-claim release result is reported in the handoff.
- Next mathematical action: prove a quantitative bound for the exact growing-window energy in (1), using the global Möbius prime law or its exact convolution inverse. Fixed-lag cancellation and generic multiplicativity are insufficient, as the strengthened countermodel consequence shows.

## 1. Frozen sampling and ancestry

The immutable recipe `w48-astra-[private research revision].json` has SHA-256 cfdc230e0d9eb589c0379a25c65531b780555cffdc59b2c721e3b714a3a40971. Before history, `seeds.md` froze all30 cards and exact additional prompt suffixes: SHA-256 e9beb23f22f9122d095dee41cb45089ab4065a05586429cdeed9386276f14fdc. Its p labels are subjective typicality judgements, not validity probabilities. The four substantive semantic stimuli were used, with no binary exploration and no claim of uniform sampling over mathematics.

Reservations 04 (best bridge), 03 (highest plausible reach), 22 (most different) were frozen in `reservations.json`, SHA-256 4abb056b849bd753b2488d7cf16bc9869785435442f67469571106a739536624. A single local CPython random.Random instance used the recipe's fixed integer seed. Each exact sorted remaining pool was written and SHA-256 hashed before its randrange draw:

| Draw | Literal eligibility, every group | Size | Zero-based draw | Card |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| 1 | all remaining p<.10 | 23 | 9 | 16 |
| 2 | all remaining p<.01 | 10 | 0 | 20 |
| 3 | all remaining cards | 25 | 1 | 02 |

No reroll, group exclusion, pre-reserved wildcard, threshold equality or post-outcome label change occurred. The seed-only hash event was sent to the controller once at the freeze. Exact pool hashes and interpreter information are in `selection-receipt.json`. The six tests and their original failed/duplicate continuations are preserved in `first-tests.md`.

Only necessary operating policy, the frozen problem and recipe were read before seeds. After the freeze I read the common index/current proof/creative portfolio and pilot protocol/decision, then the exact relevant sources. The first proposed 04 autocorrelation deletion already occurs in G22/G42. The refined development below starts from the later, different G72 window-energy return; this is an explicit change of continuation within selected card04, not a rewritten seed or a seventh test.

The protected high-ceiling03 was developed far enough to compute exact one-prime and tensor norms, then compared with the stronger existing AM18--AM21 finite-inverse theorem and its readout obstruction. It supplies no new coercivity result. Card22 reproduces W01's fixed-arity identity and [private research revision]'s triple identity. Card02 reproduces W22/R35's normalized fractional source and its unchanged exponent. These failures were resolved before concentrating on the window correction. Broad operator, homological, Jensen and fractional vocabulary is not credited as novelty.

## 2. Exact source and statement of the refined return

Fix tau>0. Let a(n) be ANY complex sequence with |a(n)|<=1 for n>=1, extended by zero for n<=0. For x>0 put

    g(v)=(2 pi tau)^(-1/2) exp(-v^2/(2 tau)),
    f_x(t)=g(log(t/x)) for t>0, and f_x(t)=0 for t<=0,
    F_a(x)=sum_(n>=1) a(n) f_x(n).

All the series below converge absolutely. The exact existing G72 objects are

    B_H(k)=sum_(j=0)^(H-1) a(k-j),
    w_X(k)=exp(-log(k/X)^2/(4 tau)),
    E_a(X,H)=(1/H) sum_(k>=1) |B_H(k)|^2 w_X(k).             (1)

Here H is an integer >=1, and every k>=1 is retained. In particular the first partial block, the zero extension, all character zeros and both infinite tails are part of (1). Its exact signed correlation expansion is the G72 expansion; no triangular constant weight is substituted and no cross term is removed.

Let h_tau(t)=g(log t), extended by zero for t<=0, and define the finite constants

    J_j(tau)=integral_0^infinity |h_tau^(j)(t)| dt,
    ell=log 2,
    K_tau=sqrt(2 pi tau) exp(tau/2)+2,
    C_(tau,r)=(2^r-1) sqrt(K_tau/(2 pi tau))
                       exp(3 ell^2/(2 tau)).

The zero extension of h_tau is C-infinity and Schwartz: each derivative on t>0 is t^(-j) times a fixed polynomial in log t times the Gaussian. This also proves every J_j finite, without an unspecified scale-dependent smoothness constant.

**Theorem W48.1 (fixed-order corrected window return).** For each integer r>=1, X>=1 and integer H>=1 satisfying 2rH<=X,

    sup_(X<=x<=2X) |F_a(x)|
      <= C_(tau,r) sqrt((X/H) E_a(X,H))
       + ((H-1)/2)^r [J_r X^(1-r)+J_(r+1) X^(-r)]
       + rH (2^r-1) g(0)
            exp(-log(X/(2rH))^2/(2 tau)).                    (2)

All constants are independent of a,X,H. The integer r and tau are fixed parameters; this statement does not claim controlled constants for r growing with X. Unlike a formal inverse of a box kernel, the proof gives an exact finite identity and a separately bounded residual. The positive energy in (1) is unchanged.

## 3. Proof with the actual endpoints and complete tails

### 3.1 Exact finite operator identity

On test functions on the positive integers define the forward average

    (T_H f)(n)=(1/H) sum_(j=0)^(H-1) f(n+j),
    Q_r(T)=sum_(j=0)^(r-1)(I-T)^j
          =sum_(k=0)^(r-1) (-1)^k binom(r,k+1) T^k.

The polynomial identity

    T Q_r(T)+(I-T)^r=I                                     (3)

is exact. The sum of absolute coefficients of Q_r is 2^r-1. Each T_H^k is a positive probability average of forward shifts between0 and k(H-1), with endpoints included. Thus every shift in Q_r lies between0 and (r-1)(H-1).

Set psi_x=Q_r(T_H)f_x and R_x=(I-T_H)^r f_x. Absolute summability and the zero extension give the exact adjoint relation

    F_a(x)=(1/H) sum_(k>=1) B_H(k) psi_x(k)
                         +sum_(n>=1) a(n) R_x(n).          (4)

Indeed, replacing k by n+j in the first sum gives sum_n a(n)T_H psi_x(n). Terms with n<=0 vanish; no negative index or first-block correction is silently dropped. Equation (3) proves (4). The forward shifts, rather than backward shifts, are essential here.

### 3.2 The corrected main term uses the same energy

First restrict the main sum to k>=rH. Every shift j occurring in psi obeys0<=j<rH<=k. Write v=log(k/X). For X<=x<=2X,

    log((k+j)/x)=v+b,   |b|<=ell.

Consequently

    f_x(k+j)^2/w_X(k)
      =(2 pi tau)^(-1)
         exp([-3v^2/4-2bv-b^2]/tau)
      <=(2 pi tau)^(-1) exp(3ell^2/tau) exp(-v^2/(2tau)). (5)

The last inequality follows from 2|bv|<=v^2/4+4b^2. Using the absolute coefficient sum of Q_r, (5) applies to |psi_x(k)|^2 with the extra factor (2^r-1)^2.

For any positive unimodal function with maximum1, its positive-integer sum is at most its integral plus2. Substituting k=X exp(v) therefore gives

    sum_(k>=1) exp(-log(k/X)^2/(2tau))
       <=X sqrt(2 pi tau) exp(tau/2)+2 <=K_tau X.           (6)

Weighted Cauchy--Schwarz, using the ENTIRE sum defining E and restricting only the test-function norm, now yields

    |(1/H) sum_(k>=rH) B_H(k) psi_x(k)|
          <= C_(tau,r) sqrt((X/H) E_a(X,H)).               (7)

For the remaining indices1<=k<rH use |B_H(k)|<=H. Every positive argument of f_x in psi is <2rH<=X<=x, where f_x increases toward its maximum. Thus this whole part is at most

    rH (2^r-1) g(0) exp(-log(X/(2rH))^2/(2tau)).           (8)

This is why the extremely small w_X(k) near k=1 causes no uncontrolled inverse-weight factor. Applying (5) indiscriminately there would be false for long windows. The explicit split pays that strongest endpoint objection.

### 3.3 Repeated differences pay the complete residual

For a nonnegative shift j,

    f(n)-f(n+j)=-integral_0^j f'(n+u)du.

Iterating this representation for (I-T_H)^r expresses R_x(n) as (-1)^r times the average, over j_1,...,j_r in {0,...,H-1}, of the integral of f_x^(r)(n+u_1+...+u_r) over0<=u_i<=j_i. No derivative is taken of a sharp arithmetic cutoff.

For every absolutely continuous integrable f with integrable derivative and every v>=0,

    sum_(n>=1) |f(n+v)| <= ||f||_(L1(0,infinity))
                                  +||f'||_(L1(0,infinity)). (9)

To prove (9), compare f(n+v) with f(t) on each interval[n+v-1,n+v], integrate, then sum the disjoint intervals. They all lie in[0,infinity). Applying (9) to f_x^(r), using the derivative scaling f_x^(r)(t)=x^(-r)h_tau^(r)(t/x), proves

    sum_(n>=1)|R_x(n)|
       <= ((H-1)/2)^r [J_r x^(1-r)+J_(r+1) x^(-r)]
       <= ((H-1)/2)^r [J_r X^(1-r)+J_(r+1) X^(-r)].        (10)

The coefficient ((H-1)/2)^r is the exact product of average shift lengths. This bound includes the whole positive integer line, hence the complete right tail. The smooth zero extension pays the left endpoint. Equations (7),(8),(10) prove (2). H=1 is included: the residual vanishes exactly and B_1=a.

## 4. Quantitative return, headroom and the still-open estimate

Let0<theta<1 be fixed, H=floor(X^theta), and r be fixed. For all sufficiently large X, 2rH<=X. The last term of (2) is O_A(X^-A) for each fixed A>0, because its logarithm has the negative quadratic leading term

    -(1-theta)^2 (log X)^2/(2tau).

The complete residual in (10) is O_(tau,r)(X^(1-r(1-theta))). Suppose, for every epsilon>0 and all large dyadic X,

    E_a(X,floor(X^theta)) <<_epsilon X^(e+epsilon).          (OPEN-W)

Then Theorem W48.1 gives the complete fixed-source exponent

    gamma_r=max((1-theta+e)/2, 1-r(1-theta)).               (11)

The exponent epsilon is harmless because the hypothesis supplies every epsilon. This is a sufficient implication, not an asserted converse or an equivalence of all high-frequency information. For any fixed target gamma>(1-theta+e)/2 one can choose a fixed r with1-r(1-theta)<gamma. Endpoint equality also gives the usual every-epsilon exponent.

For a(n)=mu(n)chi(n), where chi is any fixed ordinary Dirichlet character, the zero extension and all ramified zeros remain exactly those in (1). No primitive-character replacement or growing-conductor bound is used. Initially on Re(s)>1,

    integral_0^infinity F_a(x)x^(-s)dx/x
                         =exp(tau s^2/2)/L(s,chi).        (12)

The x<=1 tail is Gaussian, by |a(n)|<=1 and log n>=0. A dyadic L2 bound at the exponent in (11), obtained from (2), makes the complete Mellin integral holomorphic on Re(s)>gamma_r. Multiplying (12) by L continues the identity. At any zero of L that is not its principal pole, the left product would vanish while exp(tau s^2/2) does not. This excludes every such zero in that half-plane, at every finite height and every multiplicity. The principal pole at1 is explicitly excepted; 1/L has a removable zero there. Constants may depend on fixed chi and tau; the exponent must be common to all fixed chi. Natural imprimitive Euler-factor zeros are never divided away.

Thus to improve c6 it is sufficient to prove OPEN-W for every fixed chi with

    e < .749722+theta,
    1-r(1-theta)<.874861.                                  (13)

The old G72 return additionally required theta<.874861 because its residual exponent was theta. The fixed-r correction removes that extra restriction, for every fixed theta<1. It does NOT weaken the required energy saving at a given theta: since |B_H|<=H and sum w_X=O_tau(X), the absolute bound has e=1+theta. The gap to first gain remains exactly

    (1+theta)-(.749722+theta)=.250278=2c6.                  (14)

No part of that arithmetic gap is paid here. The existing independent fixed-lag/qualitative estimates must not be promoted to OPEN-W.

The following examples all ASSUME e=1, which is unproved for the actual complete energy in the displayed ranges:

| theta | fixed r | main exponent | residual exponent | conditional gamma | conditional c |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| .26 |1| .87 | .26 | .87 | .13 |
| 1/3 |1| 5/6 | 1/3 | 5/6 | 1/6 |
| 1/2 |1| 3/4 | 1/2 | 3/4 | 1/4 |
| 4/5 |2| 3/5 | 3/5 | 3/5 | 2/5 |
| 9/10 |5| 11/20 | 1/2 | 11/20 | 9/20 |
| 49/50 |25| 51/100 | 1/2 | 51/100 | 49/100 |

The first three are already reachable by G72. The last three show the enlarged analytic headroom of the SAME energy condition; the near,1/6,1/4 research targets remain valid. For e=1, first-order G72 has minimum gamma=2/3 at theta=2/3. Fixed-order corrections allow gamma arbitrarily close to1/2 by taking theta<1 close to1 and choosing r once. This is conditional analytic reach, not evidence that e=1 becomes easier at those lengths and not a proof at theta=1.

## 5. A stronger consequence for the existing multiplicative countermodel

Reuse exactly the accepted G71 source, without treating it as actual Möbius arithmetic. It is one bounded squarefree-supported multiplicative sequence a with arbitrary finitely prescribed unit prime values, the inherited every-fixed-character calibration and fixed-affine qualitative cancellation, and

    F_a(X)=C X^beta+O(X^sigma),
    C!=0, 1/2<sigma<beta<theta6.                           (15)

Its existence and all those properties are credited to `[restricted mathematical source]` and its frozen author/reviewer proofs. The present implication uses only bounded coefficients and (15); it introduces no new random construction or external result.

**Corollary W48.2.** For this same source, every fixed0<theta<1 satisfies

    E_a(X,floor(X^theta)) >>_(a,tau,theta) X^(2beta-1+theta) (16)

on every sufficiently large X. Choose once r>(1-beta)/(1-theta). Then both residual terms in (2) are o(X^beta). By (15), its left side is at least |F_a(X)|>=|C|X^beta/2. Subtract the residuals, square (7)'s remaining bound, and use H asymptotic to X^theta to obtain (16).

G72 previously obtained this consequence only for theta<beta, where O(H) was smaller than the pole signal. The fixed-order correction extends it to the ENTIRE fixed sublinear range theta<1, including theta>=beta. One source is used throughout: no uncountable probabilistic intersection is needed, because (16) is a deterministic consequence of the already selected source's single asymptotic (15).

For example, with beta=.8747 and theta=.9, (16) has exponent1.6494. Any proposed e=1 window law, or any e<1.6494, fails for this source despite its calibration and fixed-form cancellations. More generally, for a proposed gamma<theta6 select beta between max(gamma,1/2) and theta6. Its lower exponent exceeds2gamma-1+theta by2(beta-gamma)>0 at every fixed theta<1. This is a strict-gap obstruction; equality is not settled.

It remains a SCOPED countermodel. At infinitely many primes it lacks the exact Möbius law a(p)=-chi(p), and it lacks the prescribed convolution inverse a*chi=delta. A source-specific theorem using either can escape. Neither (16) nor the generic operator tests lower-bound the actual mu(n)chi(n) Gaussian field.

## 6. The other selected mechanisms and all30 dispositions

The precise six first tests are in `first-tests.md`. Card20's explicit normalized Blaschke factor is a useful all-height diagnostic: an anchor value and any positive uniform modulus budget permit a forbidden zero at arbitrarily large height. It refutes the proposed purely geometric dual on that function class, not an arithmetic L-function statement. The root source ancestry is F21/F22 and W22/R33; no literature novelty is claimed. Card16's dominance certificate cannot see height-dependent cancellation at all. The source-exact H cards were not selected and no original H coefficient, phase, projector, mask or endpoint was altered.

## 7. Evidence, limitations and precise next action

`check_window.py` performs three exact rational finite tests of (3),(4), with actual mu(n) times the mod4 character, including H=1 and r=5. They pass and expose the forward/backward orientation and endpoint conventions. `check-window.json` also verifies the table's rational exponents and the unchanged gap125139/500000. These checks verify finite indexing and arithmetic only; Sections2--5 contain the analytic proof. No numerical sample is called a uniform theorem.

The useful addition in this record is the same-energy higher-order return and the resulting expansion of the countermodel obstruction from theta<beta to all theta<1. Fixed-arity, fractional, finite inverse, Gaussian Gram and general inner-factor ideas have explicit prior credit. A targeted search found no earlier same-G72-energy correction in the read sources, but this is not a claim of literature priority or an exhaustive literature survey. No unverified external niche theorem is imported; the new statements are proved here and the reused model is bound to the accepted project source.

The strongest objection was the inverse Gaussian weight near k=1: shifted test functions can be much larger than the original weight for long H. Equations(8),(10) explicitly pay that region instead of using a false uniform ratio. Box-filter zeros do not invalidate the finite identity; their effect remains in the residual, whose smallness uses smoothness and fixed theta<1. The theorem does not extend to H comparable to X merely by continuity, to growing r, or to incomplete/adaptively masked energies. A bound for the energy averaged over a sparse set of scales is also insufficient for (12).

The next mathematical obligation is concrete: for a fixed theta (including a long-window choice if useful), prove for every fixed chi and every epsilon that the exact full weighted square in(1) is O(X^(e+epsilon)), with e<.749722+theta. An estimate must exploit the exact global Möbius prime law/convolution identity and retain all growing lags in its complete weight. At theta=.9, for example, e<1.649722 and any fixed r>=2 meet the first-gain residual condition; e=1 with r=5 would instead give the much stronger conditional gamma=.55. Neither bound is proved or presumed. A fixed-H limit, multiplicative random model, unsigned sector or one-height estimate does not fill this obligation.

Source fingerprints, whole-file readback and the final stopped-writer/release evidence are recorded separately in the small final receipts. Controller and critic should verify the analytic statements before any canonical integration. No tracker or Git handoff is performed by this author.

## G126. Exact whole-shell bank with two branches paid

For prime P not dividing q and (a,P)=1, finite multiplicative
orthogonality, including the ramified multiples n=Pm, gives on Re s>1

    sum_n mu(n)chi(n)e(an/P)n^(-s)
      =1/(P-1)sum_(psi modP)psi(a)tau(conjugate psi)/L(s,chi psi)
       -chi(P)P^(-s)/L(s,chi psi0).                    (4)

The sign psi(a) and negative correction are substantive. The latter uses
mu(Pm)=-mu(m)1_(P not dividing m), retaining all P^2 and character zeros.
Since tau(psi0)=-1, its reciprocal contains exactly
L(s,chi psi0)=(1-chi(P)P^(-s))L(s,chi). Fixed-character constants cannot
be silently summed uniformly over these growing moduli.

More usefully, freeze any unramified prime P comparable to X before
varying x over the ENTIRE shell [X,2X]. Let
w_P(x)=x^(-b)+i(1/x-2*pi/P). Absolute convergence and the same finite
orthogonality prove

    V_b,chi(x)=G_P,chi(x)+B_P,chi(x),
    G_P,chi(x)=1/(P-1)sum_(psi!=psi0)psi(-1)tau(conjugate psi)
                                      F_(chi psi)(w_P(x)),
    B_P,chi(x)=-F_(chi psi0)(w_P(x))/(P-1)
                               -chi(P)F_(chi psi0)(P w_P(x)).     (5)

The common profile and every shell point are retained, even where its
residual imaginary part vanishes. Because |F_eta(w)|<=1/Re w,

    |B_P,chi(x)|<=x^b/(P-1)+x^b/P<<X^(b-1).           (6)

Thus BOTH the principal Gauss branch and ramified branch are paid
without a growing-conductor estimate. For gamma>=b-1 the every-epsilon
whole-shell L1 target for V is equivalent to that for G; likewise for
the L2 energy via the triangle inequality of square-root norms. At b=3/2
all proposed targets exceed1/2. Choosing P separately for each shell
changes the representation, not the global Mellin source. All remaining
chi psi are nonprincipal when (P,q)=1.

The coherent bank G is still unbounded at the desired exponent. Taking
absolute values term by term can spend sqrt(P) in Gauss weights. That
is a certificate cost, not a lower bound on its true signed sum. The
complete common-profile bank is the precise new arithmetic target.

## 2. Literal arithmetic source and the correct zero-exclusion return

Put H_sigma=L2((0,1),x^(2sigma-1)dx), 0<sigma<1, and

    f_n(x)={1/(nx)}-n^(-1){1/x},   n>=1,   f_1=0.

On the reciprocal cell 1/(k+1)<x<=1/k, write 1/x=k+u, 0<=u<1.
Then {1/(nx)}=(k mod n+u)/n and {1/x}=u. Consequently

    f_n(k)=(k mod n)/n,
    ||F||_sigma^2=(1/(2sigma)) sum_(k>=1)
          [k^(-2sigma)-(k+1)^(-2sigma)] |F(k)|^2.          (R1)

Endpoints have zero measure. This is an infinite heavy-tail norm, not a finite
prefix norm. Every finite combination of the bounded f_n belongs to H_sigma.

For E_s(F)=integral_0^1 F(x)x^(s-1)dx, Cauchy-Schwarz gives

    ||E_s||^2=1/[2(Re(s)-sigma)],   Re(s)>sigma.             (R2)

The representing vector, using an inner product linear in its first variable,
is v_s(x)=x^(conjugate(s)-2sigma). Direct integration for Re(s)>1 gives

    integral_0^1 {theta/x}x^(s-1)dx
       =theta/(s-1)-theta^s zeta(s)/s,   0<theta<=1.

One way to verify this is to write {theta/x}=theta/x-floor(theta/x) and integrate
each indicator 1_(x<=theta/j). The absolutely convergent sum of their integrals
is theta^s zeta(s)/s. Subtract theta times the theta=1 identity. Holomorphic
continuation of the bounded source integral to Re(s)>0 yields

    E_s(f_n)=zeta(s)(n^(-1)-n^(-s))/s.                     (R3)

The removable value at s=1 is log(n)/n. Thus a zeta zero rho with Re(rho)>sigma
annihilates the closed original f_n span, but E_rho(1)=1/rho is nonzero.
Closure of 1 in that original span therefore suffices to exclude such zeros.
This uses neither a converse Nyman-Beurling theorem nor any Mertens input.
It excludes the open half-plane; no unproved boundary-line claim is made.

For an integer q>=2 define w_(q,n)=q f_(qn)-f_n. The actual cell value and Mellin
transform are

    w_(q,n)(k)=floor(k/n) mod q,
    E_s(w_(q,n))=(1-q^(1-s))zeta(s)n^(-s)/s.               (R4)

In particular the wavelets vanish on k<n and are bounded by q-1. The argument
allows all n>=1; this is a larger dictionary than any SW34 construction with
n>=N>=2, so the lower bounds apply to those constructions as well.

# Cofactor residuals, their exact depth threshold and complete observation costs

13 October 2026. The controller reconstructed the complete W67
[author](wild67/report.md), [independent review](wild67-review/report.md),
[two pre-outcome audits](wild67-review/audits.md), and the new independent
[residual review](residual-review/report.md), all STOPPED/normally released.
The [retention manifest](retention-manifest.json) binds original cards, samples,
partials and finite checks separately. No unchanged diagnostic was rerun.

The benchmark c11=312864909/2500000000=.1251459636 remains CONDITIONAL
SOURCE-RELATIVE. PR15's complete stronger weighted theorem and endpoint are
unfinished; F0, positive-slot uniformity and external admission remain open.
The statements below prove no new c and supply no PR15 repair. Ordinary-character
and principal-Gaussian scopes are separated throughout.

## G227. An actual twisted inverse and its cofactor-resolved observation

Fix an ordinary Dirichlet character chi modulo a fixed positive integer q.
Let S_N={a<=N: a squarefree, (a,q)=1}, ordered increasingly, with N>=1 an
integer. Write E_ad=1_(d|a) and M=diag(mu(a)). Every divisor interval of S_N
is complete, so finite Mobius inversion gives E^-1=M E M. With

    A_chi=E diag(mu(d) conjugate(chi(d))) E^T,
    (A_chi)_ab=prod_(p|(a,b))(1-conjugate(chi(p))),

the diagonal is invertible because |chi(d)|=1 on the actual labels. Therefore

    (A_chi^-1)_ab=mu(a)mu(b)
                   sum_(d in S_N,[a,b]|d)mu(d)chi(d).       (227.1)

The pairing and transpose are bilinear. A_chi is generally complex symmetric,
not Hermitian. Its (1,1) inverse entry is exactly M_chi(N)=sum_(n<=N)mu(n)chi(n).
Simply phase-gauging the real coprimality matrix would leave that observed
inverse entry untwisted, so it does not establish (227.1).

Put g=(a,b), l=[a,b]. Writing d=lm in (227.1), squarefreeness forces (m,l)=1,
and mu(a)mu(b)mu(l)=mu(g). Hence

    (A_chi^-1)_ab=mu(g)chi(l) M_(chi,lq)(N/l),
    M_(chi,h)(y)=sum_(m<=y,(m,h)=1)mu(m)chi(m).             (227.2)

This is zero for l>N. In particular the first inverse row and complete
residual identity, for ANY proposed column z and r=e1-A_chi z, are

    R_N(a)=chi(a) M_(chi,aq)(N/a),  |R_N(a)|<=floor(N/a),
    M_chi(N)=z1+sum_(a in S_N) R_N(a)r(a),
    B_N(z):=sum_a |R_N(a)r(a)|
       <=W_N(z):=N sum_a |r(a)|/a.                         (227.3)

All coordinates remain. If r is supported on a>N/H, H>=1, this costs at most
H||r||1. A global inverse operator norm is therefore an unnecessarily large
default price for a residual known to live on large labels. The exact signed
sum in (227.3) remains available; its absolute bound is only a sufficient bill.

For fixed 0<gamma<1, a complete every-epsilon bound for |z1|+B_N(z), or the
stronger explicit |z1|+W_N(z), by N^(gamma+epsilon) gives the same Mertens
bound. The alternative every-epsilon integral_1^X |M_chi(t)|^2 dt/t bound
by X^(2gamma+epsilon) also suffices. On each dyadic shell Cauchy bounds
the Abel integral and all its fixed derivatives, with a positive exponent
buffer on any compact subset of Re(s)>gamma. The normally convergent function

    s integral_1^infinity M_chi(t)t^(-s-1)dt

equals 1/L(s,chi) on Re(s)>1. Continuing the identity with L excludes regular
zeros in Re(s)>gamma at every finite height. At the principal pole s=1 the
reciprocal has a zero. Natural character zeros stay in the coefficients.
Constants may depend on the fixed character and epsilon; no growing-conductor
or Hecke assertion follows. This is a complete return from an OPEN estimate.

Two concrete inverse cautions survive. In the principal N=2 case the signed
coprimality matrix [[1,-1],[-1,0]] is invertible but its nuisance block [0]
is singular and its inverse (1,1) entry is0. A Schur formula requiring that
block inverse fails. On m distinct prime labels the matrix is J-I, full rank
for m>=2, while rank-one J has operator residual1 and scalar residual at most
||u||2||v||2. Exact rank alone therefore does not rule out a paid approximation.

## G228. The sharp depth of a low-omega-completed inverse column

Fix 0<beta<1. For 1<=T<=beta N and an integer k>=0 define

    F_(T,k)(d)=1_(d<=T OR omega(d)<=k),
    z=E^-T (chi(d) F_(T,k)(d))_d.

The first row of E^-T is mu(d), and multiplying by A_chi cancels chi against
its conjugate. Using sum_(d|a)mu(d)=1_(a=1) gives the exact identities

    z1=sum_(d in S_N)mu(d)chi(d) F_(T,k)(d),
    r(a)=sum_(d|a,d>T,omega(d)>k)mu(d).                     (228.1)

If omega(a)=k+1 and a>T, all proper divisors are included, so r(a)=mu(a).
For a>N/2 its cofactor observation is exactly R_N(a)=chi(a).
Let b_k be the product of the first k primes not dividing q, b_0=1, and put
alpha=max(beta,1/2). Every prime p in (alpha N/b_k,N/b_k] not dividing b_k q
gives a distinct actual coordinate a=b_k p with |R_N(a)r(a)|=1. Thus

    B_N(z)<=W_N(z),
    B_N(z)>=#{alpha N/b_k<p<=N/b_k : p prime, p not|b_k q}. (228.2)

The second line is an exact finite inequality, possibly zero for small N.
For fixed k, the ordinary prime number theorem gives the lower asymptotic
(1-alpha)N/(b_k log N). Correcting primes, semiprimes or any other fixed number
of omega layers has not made this absolute residual small at any exponent<1.

There is also a matching upper bound for growing depth. Set h=k+1,
H_N=sum_(m<=N)1/m and A_N=sum_(p<=N)1/p, including conductor primes if desired.
Taking the absolute value in (228.1) and exchanging the finite divisor sums,

    W_N(z)<=N H_N sum_(d<=N,d squarefree,omega(d)>=h)1/d
           <=N H_N sum_(j>=h) A_N^j/j!
           <=N H_N exp(A_N) A_N^h/h!.                     (228.3)

An unordered j-prime set occurs j! times in A_N^j. Admitting repeated primes
and products above N only enlarges the positive sum. The last inequality
uses (h+r)!>=h!r!. This pays EVERY residual coordinate and is uniform in T.

Ordinary PNT and partial summation give p_j~j log j and A_N=O(loglog N).
The [NIST reference](https://dlmf.nist.gov/27.12) records the prime asymptotics;
the consequences here are derived from them. Removing fixed q's finitely
many primes changes indices by a bounded amount, so log b_k~k log k as k grows.
If k~kappa log N/loglog N for fixed 0<kappa<1, then
b_k=N^(kappa+o(1)), while its largest prime is O(log N). The prime interval
in (228.2) lies above all these factors eventually; its endpoint is
N^(1-kappa+o(1)). PNT on a fixed-ratio interval, together with (228.3) and
log(h!)=h log h-h+O(log h), proves

    B_N(z)=N^(1-kappa+o(1)),  W_N(z)=N^(1-kappa+o(1)).      (228.4)

These are logarithmic exponents, uniform for 1<=T<=beta N, not fixed-k
logarithmic asymptotic formulas. If k=o(log N/loglog N), both exponents are1.

More generally fix ONE sequence k_N>=0 and ONE cutoff sequence
1<=T_N<=beta N for all sufficiently large N, independently of epsilon. For 0<gamma<1,

    B_N(z_N)<<_epsilon N^(gamma+epsilon) for EVERY epsilon>0
    iff W_N(z_N)<<_epsilon N^(gamma+epsilon) for EVERY epsilon>0
    iff liminf_N k_N loglog N/log N >= 1-gamma.             (228.5)

For sufficiency, bound the nonnegative tail in (228.3) at any smaller depth
a log N/loglog N with 0<a<1-gamma and then let a approach1-gamma according
to epsilon. For necessity, if the liminf is smaller, choose such an a above
it. Along infinitely many N the primorial is at most N^(a+o(1)), so (228.2)
has exponent at least1-a, contradicting a sufficiently small fixed epsilon.
No short-interval or growing-modulus prime theorem is used.

Equality in (228.5) is sufficient for the residual bill alone. It does not
pay z1. In fact, with D_N the number of omitted coefficients,

    z1=M_chi(N)-sum_(d in S_N,d>T,omega(d)>=h)mu(d)chi(d),
    D_N<=sum_(n<=N)binom(omega(n),h)
        =sum_(d<=N,d squarefree,omega(d)=h)floor(N/d)
        <=N A_N^h/h!.                                    (228.6)

Once (228.5) holds, the every-epsilon exponent-gamma estimate on z1 is
equivalent to that on M_chi(N). The retained coordinate still carries the
arithmetic problem. At the c11 benchmark the residual's threshold is
liminf k_N loglog N/log N >= .1251459636; the full certificate is still open.

The lower bounds concern COMPLETE ABSOLUTE bills of this SPECIFIC column
family. They do not lower-bound the complete signed residual, Mertens sum,
any arbitrary approximant or a Gaussian energy. Higher residual layers need
not have a common sign: for k=1,T=11,a=30, r(30)=mu(15)+mu(30)=0.

The ancestry is the first-unpaid-layer argument in W43/[restricted research revision] and [restricted research revision]'s
fixed-layer circle obstruction. W43's Newton defect includes prime powers
and factorial multiplicities; at T=1,k=1 its order-two defect at pq is2,
where (228.1) is1. G78/G83-G85 already paid their own growing-order Gaussian
restoration, so that older obligation is not reopened. The new scoped result
is the cofactor certificate's exact depth threshold and its remaining z1
obligation, rather than a new generic lesson about truncation.

## G229. A full Walsh source with its Gaussian and Euler returns paid

This section concerns the principal coprime Gaussian P_Y of G25-G30. Fix
tau>0, Y=floor(X^.495), B_X=2X exp(C sqrt(log X)), with fixed C>0. The Boolean
cube uses ALL primes5<=p<=B_X. For labels u,v put d(u)=prod_p p^u_p and

    K(u,v)=(-1)^(|u|+|v|)1_(u and v disjoint),
    W_x(u,v)=1_(d(u)>Y,d(v)>Y,d(u)d(v)<=B_X)
      *sum_(ell<=B_X/(d(u)d(v)))(-1)^(ell+1)
           g_tau(log(d(u)d(v)ell/x)).

Then Z_X(x)=sum K W_x is the literal output-truncated ordered source.
Shared-prime zeros, p=2,3 exclusions, both strict cuts and every ell sign
remain. With K_0 cube sites and an unnormalized Walsh transform in BOTH
variables, finite orthogonality proves

    Z_X(x)=2^(-2K_0) sum_(alpha,beta) Khat(alpha,beta) What_x(alpha,beta).
                                                               (229.1)

There is no complex conjugation in this bilinear identity. Locally,
H=[[1,1],[1,-1]], T=[[1,-1],[-1,0]], and H T H=[[-1,1],[1,3]]. All four
dual gate entries are nonzero. Sparsity of the complete transformed mask
would require its own theorem; the global prime cube is not one divisor cube.

The original d3 coefficient majorant bounds the discarded output field,
uniformly on x in[X,2X], by X^(1-C^2/(2tau)+o(1)). The counting Jacobian
is included in that exponent. Choose C with this exponent below the desired
gamma>1/2. G27 independently pays |P_Y-F6|<<X^(.495+delta), delta<gamma-.495.
G28 then uses fixed Euler convolutions and their inverses, with direct
factor (1-z)^2 at2,3 and (1-z)^2/(1-2z) at p>=5. Their weighted absolute
coefficient sums converge for every fixed sigma>1/2; the original exceptional
prime2 coefficients1,-3,2 remain. Apply this norm transfer to the FIXED F6
and G_tau fields, then apply each shell's own frozen Y comparison.

Thus a COMPLETE every-epsilon shell L2 bound for (229.1) at exponent gamma
would return the original fixed Gaussian G3 and its zeta zero exclusion.
The changing finite cube has no independently asserted Mellin transform.
Both copies, all dual modes, their cross terms and the complementary field
remain. An ordinary-character or Hecke extension is an additional theorem.
No arithmetic estimate for the whole right side has been proved.

## G230. Paid ambient realizations and two independent audits

If A=alpha P U Q with U unitary and P,Q contractions, alpha>=||A|| follows
by submultiplicativity. For C=A/alpha a contraction, the Halmos block
[[C,(I-CC*)^(1/2)],[(I-C*C)^(1/2),-C*]] is unitary; the defect intertwining
identity proves it directly. It realizes the optimum alpha=||A||. For
selfadjoint C its square is I, whereas C^2=I-(I-C^2); repeated use must
retain the returning defect or intermediate physical projections. A
source-specific approximation remains possible, with the full scalar
residual bounded by delta||u||2||v||2 when its operator error is delta.

The signed local gate T is a diagonal sign gauge of [[1,1],[1,0]], so their
singular values agree. The indefinite J=[[-2,-1],[-1,2]] satisfies T^TJT=-J,
yet v=(phi,-1), phi=(1+sqrt5)/2, is J-null and Tv=phi v. Conserved flux
does not bound that positive observation. For a selfadjoint K, the Cayley
unitary V=(K-iI)(K+iI)^-1 has (I-V)^-1=(I-iK)/2 and inverse norm
sqrt(1+||K||^2)/2. No selfadjoint claim is licensed for complex A_chi.

The protected S28 audit diagonalizes the disjointness gate orthogonally.
For K_0 sites its eigenvalues are (-1)^j phi^(K_0-2j), with binomial
multiplicity, and squared Frobenius norm3^K_0. Writing the FULL physical
boundary in that basis preserves its Frobenius norm; the generic contraction
bill is3^(K_0/2)||W||F. A product-only weight counts each ordered prime
allocation and produces mu(n)chi(n)2^omega(n), not the original Mertens
coefficient. A single n-divisor cube has omega(n)=O(log n/loglog n);
that does not bound the global prime set of every n<=X.

The uniform S09 audit uses the connected prime-adjoining graph on S_N.
For (Bf)_(n,pn)=f(pn)+chi(p)f(n), write f(n)=a(n)g(n), a(n)=mu(n)chi(n).
Then ker B=span(a). In ANY complete identity w=lambda e1+B^T t, pairing
with a forces lambda=sum_n w_n a(n). A rooted prime-deletion tree constructs
t from complete signed subtree sums. If r=w-lambda e1-B^Tt, then

    |sum_n w_n a(n)|<=|lambda|+||r||1,
    inf_(lambda,t)(|lambda|+||w-lambda e1-B^Tt||1)=|sum_n w_n a(n)|.
                                                               (230.1)

The upper equality chooses the exact signed target as lambda; the lower is
the triangle inequality. This leaves constructive arithmetic certificates
eligible, but feasibility alone hides the original target in a coordinate.

All these bills concern their named positive, absolute or generic ambient
arguments. They leave complete signed arithmetic cancellation open. The
review's S28/S09 audits froze before author outcomes, and all30 original
cards and dispositions remain in the retained source reports. Conditional
c11 and the separate PR15/F0/positive-slot/external-admission gaps are unchanged.

# [private research revision]: actual rough-mask covariance in the hard primitive-shift region



## Current checkpoint

Objective: estimate the complete G34 signed low-gcd shift scalar, or
prove a concrete actual-source obstruction that changes a live attempt.
The assignment locked the input to c2=.125128; c3=.125133 was under
review at assignment and is not used here. A new target relative to
that baseline must have gamma<.874872. Every Mertens exponent is
fixed beta>.874872; the inherited .8749 remains available.

Read: current-proof G31--G40, [private research revision] threshold integration and independent
review, maintained attempt index and F01/N28 source sections, W38 R38.5
and its actual-law scope. Prime-dilation correlation repeats [private research revision] S24
and receives no new credit. The two distinct attacks retained here are:

1. Localize literal rough-mask covariance into low gcd and long primitive
   shifts, paying all removed regions by positive Gaussian counting.
2. Expose the prime-two phase with its actual conditional remaining
   coefficient and test whether this yields contraction.

The first attack has a source-specific obstruction: the accepted critical
rough complement has a self-correlation of order X^2/log^4 X INSIDE the
hard region, even after high gcd and every fixed sublinear primitive-shift
range are removed. This is a lower bound for that explicit arithmetic
submask, never for the full f3 energy. The opposing prefix/complement
cross term survives there too. Its proof uses an exact actual norm rather
than replacing a norm by a leading Gram.

The second attack has an exact conditional self-copy: after exposing
prime 2, the remaining coefficient ignores prime 2, and its even branch
is the same coefficient at half scale. The resulting signed dilation
identity is invertible at every exponent below 1. Marginal balancing
alone creates no contraction. Its finite future-scale remainder and
target-dependent depth are priced explicitly below.

No new full-field exponent or c is claimed. The completed sections below
supply the actual coprime obstruction, uniform mixed estimate, exact
G34 mask/height return, error budgets and reopening conditions. The
compact helper checks finite source identities and rational budgets;
it does not verify an asymptotic estimate. Final freeze/readback and
claim release are recorded in the handoff after the complete report.

## 1. Surviving result: a complete actual coprime rough block is large

The completed result below is stronger than the initial low-gcd plan:
it concerns gcd EXACTLY ONE. It supplies a counterexample to a concrete
dispersion lemma on the ACTUAL coefficient source, not a general-input
operator bound and not a lower bound for the full f3 energy.

Fix tau>0. Let g(u)=(2pi tau)^(-1/2)exp(-u^2/(2tau)), and retain

    f(n)=mu(rad(n/3^v3(n))),
    K_X(m,n)=integral_X^(2X)g(log(m/x))g(log(n/x))dx/x.

Choose a FIXED kappa with kappa^2>=2exp(3tau), and set z=kappa sqrt(X),
L=log X. Let A_R(n)=1_(omega_z(n)>=2), A_T=1-A_R. The original fields
R,T,F have coefficients f A_R,f A_T,f, respectively, so F=T+R exactly.
Threshold masks are frozen throughout x in the CLOSED shell [X,2X].
No moving kappa or tau assertion is used.

For bounded real source coefficients u(n),v(n), write

    C_1(u,v)=sum_((m,n)=1)u(m)v(n)K_X(m,n).             (A1)

Subscripts R,T,F indicate the foregoing literal coefficient families.
This coprime scalar is NOT asserted to be a positive semidefinite form.
Its diagonal contains only m=n=1. R(1)'s coefficient is zero; hence
C_1(R,R), C_1(T,R) and C_1(F,R) contain no true diagonal at all.

Define the positive, full two-prime fields

    V(x)=sum_(z<p<q)g(log(pq/x)),
    U(x)=sum_(r>=2)sum_(z<p<q)g(log(rpq/x)).           (A2)

Every core valuation is included in U. The core r=1 is isolated only
inside the following complete bounds; the theorem does not replace
the original source by that favorable family.

**Theorem A (actual coprime obstruction).** For all sufficiently large X,

    C_1(R,R) >= (1/3)||V||^2 - C_(tau,kappa)X^(3/2),
    C_1(R,R) <= (16/9)||V||^2,
    ||V||^2 asymp_(tau,kappa) X^2/L^4.               (A3)

Thus this ENTIRE signed rough-mask coprime scalar is positive and
comparable to X^2/L^4. Its coefficients are the actual f3 signs.
The lower bound does not require Mertens, a full-field estimate, or
independence of primes. The only analytic input is the accepted fixed-
order PNT used for the independently reviewed critical source theorem.

For an explicit long-shift statement, put

    W_X=log2+sqrt(24tau L),
    I_X=[X exp(-W_X),X exp(W_X)],
    H_X=X/L^6.

Let C_1^H use additionally m,n in I_X, m!=n and |m-n|>H_X. Then

    C_1^H(R,R) >>_(tau,kappa) X^2/L^4.              (A4)

Every integer in this restricted source has exactly two distinct
rough primes, each to the first power. The FOUR rough primes in
every retained pair are all distinct. All residual core valuations,
all coprime cores, all long shifts and both orders are still present.

Using only the already accepted fixed buffered exponent beta, the
opposing interaction is also forced in this same hard region:

    C_1^H(T,R)=-C_1^H(R,R)
                    +O_(beta,tau,kappa)(X^(1+beta)+X^2/L^6),
    C_1^H(T,R) <= -c_(tau,kappa) X^2/L^4             (A5)

for some fixed c_(tau,kappa)>0 and all sufficiently large X.
The reverse ordered scalar C_1^H(R,T) equals C_1^H(T,R) by symmetry
and remains in every full reconstruction.

This refutes the proposed separate-piece estimate

    |C_1^H(R,R)|+|C_1^H(T,R)| << X^(2gamma+epsilon)

for every fixed gamma<1, by choosing 0<epsilon<2-2gamma. Even the
one-sided upper bound on C_1^H(R,R) is false at those exponents.
Thus the proposed assertion quantified over EVERY epsilon>0 fails.
It does NOT refute the
complete signed target G31/G34: the two displayed pieces must cancel
with their actual complementary pieces before any positivity step.

## 2. Complete positive-core bounds needed for A3

The following bounded-coefficient version of the accepted critical
PNT argument is proved here to avoid a masked-transfer assumption.
For arbitrary coefficients |c(r)|<=1 define the COMPLETED source

    S_c(x)=sum_(r>=1)c(r)sum_(z<p<q)g(log(rpq/x)).

Uniformly over such c and the closed shell,

    S_c(x)=2x/L^2 sum_(r>=1)c(r)/r J(log(r z^2/x))
                                      +O_(tau,kappa)(X/L^3), (A6)
    J(v)=integral_v^infinity exp(u)(u-v)g(u)du.

This is a linear prime-density estimate with an absolute error; it
asserts no arithmetic cancellation for arbitrary c. Here are the
complete bounds establishing its applicable uniformity.

Choose delta=1/100 and P_X=X^(.52). Terms with r>X^delta force
rpq>kappa^2 X^(1+delta); terms with p or q>P_X force
rpq>kappa X^(1.02). Their total, with |c|<=1 and all representation
multiplicities, is a complete divisor-weighted Gaussian upper tail,
O_A(X^-A) for every fixed A. This follows from d_3(n)<<_epsilon
n^epsilon and the Gaussian tail bound proved below in (A11).

On r<=X^delta and z<p,q<=P_X replace the unordered pair by half the
ordered pair and subtract its actual p=q diagonal. Even with all r,
that diagonal has positive cost

    sum_(p>z)sum_(r>=1)g(log(rp^2/x))
       <=C_tau x sum_(p>z)p^-2 <= C_(tau,kappa)sqrt(X).

For each fixed N, the PNT input is pi(v)-li(v)=O_N(v/log^N v).
Use N=10 before X varies. Stieltjes summation for fixed r,q on
(z,P_X] gives BOTH endpoint terms and the derivative integral, each
bounded by C x/(rqL^N). Indeed p g(log(rpq/x)) is bounded by Cx/(rq),
and the derivative integral is at most
(x/(rq))integral exp(u)|g'(u)|du. The lower endpoint is excluded
correctly even when z is prime. Summing errors over retained r,q
costs at most two harmonic factors O(L^2). Replace the other prime
sum inside the already continuous first-prime integral; the same
bound and both endpoints give a second O(X/L^8) error. There is no
unpriced product of PNT errors.

Extend the continuous integral to all r,p,q by an ABSOLUTE bound.
Put a=z^2/x in [kappa^2/2,kappa^2]. After dropping denominators
log p,log q>=1, the full positive expression is exactly

    x integral_(log a)^infinity exp(u)g(u)
            sum_(r<=exp(u)/a)(u-log(ar))/r du.

The inner sum is at most C_kappa(1+u_+)^2. Every term added by an
omitted core or prime endpoint forces u>=.01L-O_kappa(1), so the
whole continuous extension is O_A(X^-A). This explicitly pays the
infinite core, not only a finite-core rectangle.

Finally scale p=sqrt(X)v, q=sqrt(X)w, with v,w>=kappa>=1. Globally,

    |1/[(L/2+log v)(L/2+log w)]-4/L^2|
                       <=8(log v+log w)/L^3.

The sum over all r of the resulting positive error integral is
finite uniformly in x/X in [1,2]. With u=log(rvw/(x/X)), a fixed
Gaussian exponential majorant bounds each core integral by C_B r^-B
for any chosen B>1. The leading integral for that core is exactly
(x/(Xr))J(log(rz^2/x)). The factors unordered 1/2, Jacobian X and
density 4/L^2 give the coefficient 2x/L^2. This proves (A6), uniformly
in all bounded c, using only absolute errors at this stage.

Take c=1_(r=1) and c=1_(r>=2), respectively. Put

    q_x=z^2/x,   V_0(x)=2x/L^2 J(log q_x).

Then

    V=V_0+O(X/L^3),
    U=2x/L^2 sum_(r>=2)r^-1 J(log(rq_x))+O(X/L^3).   (A7)

For v>=3tau, completing the Gaussian square in J gives, for b>=0,

    J(v+b)/J(v)
       <= exp(-(v-tau)b/tau-b^2/(2tau)) <= exp(-2b).

Since q_x>=exp(3tau), the entire r>=2 main term is at most V_0/4:

    sum_(r>=2)r^-1 J(log(rq_x))
       <=J(log q_x)sum_(r>=2)r^-3 <=(1/4)J(log q_x).  (A8)

The last numerical bound follows from 1/8+integral_2^infinity t^-3dt
=1/4. J is continuous and strictly positive on the fixed compact
q_x interval, so V_0 is uniformly comparable to X/L^2. Consequently

    0<=U(x)<=V(x)/3,
    V(x) asymp_(tau,kappa) X/L^2                     (A9)

for all sufficiently large X, uniformly on the closed shell. The
constant 1/3 deliberately leaves room for the O(1/L) density errors.
No new logarithmic profile is claimed as the lane's result: (A6)--(A9)
are the positive-core estimates needed for the coprime obstruction.

## 3. Exact source and the actual gcd-one projection

Whenever n<z^3 and omega_z(n)>=2, its source is uniquely n=rpq,
p<q both greater than z, each of valuation one, and r<z. Since z>3,
f(n)=f(r). All powers in r remain. For n>=z^3 the two-prime completion
can fail; its coefficient multiplicity is at most d_3(n). The complete
Gaussian discrepancy is O_A(X^-A). Thus, with full infinite sums,

    R(x)=V(x)+S_(f 1_(r>=2))(x)+O_A(X^-A),
    |S_(f 1_(r>=2))(x)|<=U(x).                      (A10)

This is the same exact central source as the accepted critical theorem;
its all-core absolute estimates were proved separately above.

The elementary lattice and tail bounds used throughout are

    sum_n g(log(n/y)) <=C_tau y, y>0,
    sum_(|log(n/y)|>=W)n^epsilon g(log(n/y))
       <=C_(tau,epsilon)y^(1+epsilon)exp(-W^2/(4tau)). (A11)

Completing the Gaussian square proves the tilted bound; comparison
with the integral plus total variation proves the lattice bound for
y>=1, and g(log(n/y))<=C(y/n)^2 handles y<1. The same argument works
for every fixed Gaussian variance needed here.

For I_X in Theorem A and x in [X,2X], an integer outside I_X has
|log(n/x)|>=W_X-log2. Summing the product kernel therefore gives

    sum_(m or n outside I_X) K_X(m,n)=O_tau(X^-4).   (A12)

This follows from X^2 exp(-(W_X-log2)^2/(4tau))=X^-4. The cutoff is
X^(1+o(1)); for large X every n in I_X satisfies n<z^3, and its two-
prime core is <exp(W_X)/kappa^2<z. Hence the preceding factorization
is literal on every retained pair, not an asymptotic identification.

Consider the noncoprime part of R's squared norm. If m,n in I_X share
a rough prime p>z, their entire positive kernel mass is at most

    sum_(p>z) integral_X^(2X)
                 [sum_(a>=1)g(log(pa/x))]^2dx/x
       <=C_tau X^2 sum_(p>z)p^-2 <=C X^2/z.         (A13)

This includes all rough-prime coincidences and all original same-
integer diagonals. Overcounting simultaneous shared primes is harmless
only here, in the explicitly positive error bound.

If a retained pair is noncoprime but shares NO rough prime, any common
prime divides both small cores r,s. Indeed neither core can contain a
prime greater than z. Both cores are therefore >=2. The absolute
contribution of ALL such pairs is bounded by ||U||^2; enlarging to
every pair of completed r,s>=2 sources only increases this positive
bound. This argument uses the actual gcd, not a hereditary estimate
for a projected f_r field. It keeps primes 2 and 3 and every valuation.

Combining this with (A12)--(A13),

    |sum_((m,n)>1)f(m)f(n)A_R(m)A_R(n)K_X(m,n)|
                 <=||U||^2 + C X^(3/2)+O(X^-4).      (A14)

By (A9)--(A10), R>=V-U+O_A(X^-A)>0 on the shell. Consequently

### Comparison, Cauchy and low bins

The equal-product comparison uses lengths M/4 and n1+n2-M/4. Exact mask deletion and reflection of its long factor give old capacity at most

`M/4+M/2+(9/2)(M/25)+xi=93M/100+xi`.

The old comparison therefore retains reserve `7M/100`, with identical product, whole character, independent heights and profiles. Empty slots use the old unrestricted theorem.

The first-transform outside exponent is `M-A-R/2-E`. Keep its labels inside Hilbert Cauchy. The C-side joint target is

`sum_lambda N_(C,lambda) << Z^(p+A-c+R+E+B_c+eta)`,

where `B_c=(3c-5d-R)_+/6`, and similarly with c,d exchanged. The primewise balance `B_c+B_d<=c+d-2p-R` makes the geometric mean, including the outside factor, at most `Z^(M+eta)`. There is no later first-label multiplicity.

At the actual radius the identities remain

```
M'=M-(c-d)_+-6a_j-omega-g2+t2,
(A-c-c2-M')-(A-M)
  =6a_j+omega-min(c,d)-(c2-g2)-t2 <= 6a_j+omega,
Delta=b2-p2+B_c+a_j >= a_j.
```

Low bins are imposed only on positive allocated child energy after both transforms. They are not differentiated or passed through Poisson. Delete original slots at squared price `.7+O(e)` per width, hence `7/45+O(e)` per old-capacity defect, then drop the paid indicator and apply the old canonical moment. Exhaustion invokes the unrestricted old zero-slot case; no plain-sum gate is invented.

The actual width discrepancy `d_*` may be negative. For `d_*<=delta2`, `0<=s<=1`, use

`d_*+s(F-d_*)_+ <= delta2+sF_+`.

Thus the combined actual-width and deletion cost is controlled by the same nominal defect, including support padding and one greedy mesh overshoot. The low reserve is

```
a_j/15-(7/45)g_j M
  = M b_j (k/15-7r/45)
  = M b_j/4500.
```

Its exact minimum is **151M/22500000**, exceeding the report's conservative **M/150000**. All small losses must be chosen from a strict fraction of this common budget and the requested epsilon. The frozen proof does so. The original per-label `-s0` allowance and `Z^(p+s0+eta)` label count still give the joint target, rather than an additional loss after Cauchy.

## 6. The signed cubic route after physical cube-row restriction

T05 applies to the original root-preserving profiles and their allowed derivatives. An arbitrary multiplicative norm twist moves the paid Mellin root and requires a new residue calculation.

Use \(u_Y=\delta-m_Y*\mathbf1\), with convolution identity \(\delta\), and
\(I=-m_Y*m_Y*\mathbf1\), \(R=2m_Y+\mu*u_Y*u_Y\). The paid Type I theorem concerns the whole form. T05 now separately proves the **physical cube-row projection** of that Type I form:
\[
|P_{\rm cub}\mathcal Q[I,I]|
\ll(DKY)^\epsilon D^{4/3}K^{2/3}Y^4.
\]
At \(K=D^{.8765},Y=D^{.01}\), its exponent is \(1.957666\ldots\). Thus the principal-cube remainder equals the actual projected C–C term up to an affordable error. The accepted C–C bound is still \(D^{2+2(c-c_0)+\epsilon}\); it has no new saving. At .1255 the excess is .000773294…, while the generic nonprincipal term \(D^2K^{1/3}\) loses .292166… . Both obligations must be closed.

**F01.N2 — New pass 1, principal-source separation.** Use T05's exact internal coefficient, including densities only at primes outside the squarefree core, to compute the projected C–C minus I–I Mellin polar part with the same profile. Test whether the new principal reduction exposes an independent residue/main term that can be paired with a nonprincipal residual. A bare small-core identity \(I_Y(c)=-\mu(c)\) cannot be substituted into a completed \(ct^3\) coefficient; its cube descendants change the density and cutoff. The first missing estimate remains genuine principal cancellation, not that invalid truncation.

**F02.P — Coupled large-prime packets.** Above the cube threshold a squarefree core has at most two large primes and no cube-label prime is that large. Each packet sharing its designated prime has zero self-covariance under total-column coprimality. Cross packets contain \(\overline{\mathfrak G(p)}\vartheta_p(mk)\), with moving parameter as large as \(DK/(Pq_B^3)\). Keep the opposite column and row live through Poisson, subtract the principal geometric term and preserve the exact common period \(rab\), not just conductor \(ab\). Distinct children use product-variable dispersion with exact divisor fibres, two-large-prime short cofactors, or an unequal cutoff matching a real conductor asymmetry. An arbitrary coefficient can compensate the character; even a hypothetical individual \(P^{5/6}\) bound loses after absolute summation.

**F01.R — Unequal cutoffs and connected returns.** With \(R_*=Y_1Y_2\), the extended whole Type I cost is
\[
D^{5/3}K^{1/3}+D^{4/3}K^{7/12}R_*^2+DKR_*.
\]
At \(k=.87653\), \(\log_DR_*<.07767875\) is affordable; \((.01,.065)\) is a legitimate trial. Gemini's suggested large cutoffs do not fit this budget. Third-order \((\Pi,U,C)\) identities have a negative double-collision term and a pure cube triple collision, but also retain a long outer \(\mathbf1\)-convolution and the rough coefficient \(-2\). Pair collision levels inside one signed covariance; stop after one new layer unless it gives a globally cheaper range. Higher return depth is not a default research strategy.

**F05.P / F10.A — Actual polar projection and signed asymptotics.** Identify the actual residual coefficients before projecting. The model overlap \(\langle\beta\sqrt W,\overline{\mathfrak G}\nu\sqrt W\rangle=\sum\mu\bar\nu W\) is a calibration, not an automorphic theorem. Even the optimistic baseline untwisted overlap leaves exponent about 2.04195 when used to pay the generic nonprincipal loss. Moving residual twists cost conductor. A viable child evaluates a *signed difference* of residual/main terms with every cross term, instead of bounding two positive masses. A successful stronger asymptotic might support \(K>D\), but a new detector/completion and polar transfer must then be proved; the existing cubic range gives no universal ceiling.
