### N27 — Finite incidence, including its completed version

The exact finite trace is
\[
\mathcal T(K,G;s)=\sum_{q_k\le KG}\|\mathbf D_k(s)\|^2
\sum_{\substack{g\mid\operatorname{rad}_{=1}(k)\\q_k/K\le q_g\le G}}q_g^{-2\sigma}.
\tag{FIN-weight}
\]
The radical contains primes of valuation **exactly one**. For \(k>K\) this demands a real intermediate divisor; large prime rows are absent when \(G\le K\). For \(k\le K\), \(g=1\) remains. Formal divisor counting does not prove the sought \(K^{1+u}G^v\) bound. T08 proves the transfer throughout \(u,v\ge0,3u+v<1\), not only the narrower B domain \(v\le u<1/4\).

T01 applied to the finite \((g,h)\)-vector gives the same exponents for the common-F-completed incidence norm. This is a new merger consequence: no separate completion-removal prerequisite remains for N27 either. It does not supply a period realization or the incidence saving.

**New proved corridor reduction (T08).** It is enough to prove FIN for every \(K\) and \(1\le G\le C K^\gamma\), for a fixed dyadic constant \(C\), where \(\gamma=(1-u)/(2+v)>1/3\), with the full family/strip/profile hypotheses. The detector only uses \(G=\max(K^{1/3},KD^{-1/2})\) at a strictly interior row exponent; whole-profile tails close by the blockwise enlargement proved in T08. Thus the formerly provisional \(K^{.431}\) target is now the exact sufficient corridor exponent \(28/65\) for \((u,v)=(1/8,1/32)\). This is a real reduction of the needed uniform range, not an energy saving. Partition the first-admissible-divisor attack inside this corridor before asking for a larger G range.

**N27.P:** sum one forced-prime dyad \(g\sim E\) before row expansion; retain the common-core masks and aim to save divisor exponent \(v\), not merely estimate every index through \(KE\). **N27.D:** partition by the first admissible divisor in \([q_k/K,G]\), controlling overlapping divisor-rich classes exactly. **N27.X:** handle exceptions by their actual FIN-weight and amplitude, not cardinality alone. The prototype \((u,v)=(1/8,1/32)\) needs a substantial \(g=1\) mean but tolerates a weaker row exponent than OM's \(3/32\).

**N27.N1 — New pass 1, signed selector before divisor Cauchy.** Reconstruct the finite h-by-divisor bilinear kernel at the precise place FD's transfer takes a divisor norm. Keep the completed selector coefficients
\(x_{g/d}\prod_{p\mid d}(1-x_p)\beta(d)\vartheta_d(h)q_d^{-s}\), with all outside zeros, and test whether an actual signed selector energy is cheaper than FIN-weight. The first missing lemma is an exact sufficient transfer for that smaller energy; cancellation between divisors cannot be assumed merely because coefficients alternate. This is a genuine escape from demanding the positive trace only if the full detector and tails close. It is not a second name for N27.P.

statement:
# [private research revision] independent review: fixed-ratio source obstruction and paired detectors

**Verdict: ACCEPT the restricted mathematical results B1–B18.** The literal
fixed-ratio arithmetic-wavelet span has a positive distance from the target 1,
even after any fixed finite arithmetic patch. Its source resolvent has a genuine
positive atom at zero. The full-lattice floor and the complete-height paired
multiplier estimate are valid. The support and terminal-jump convention needed
in B9 is stated explicitly below; it is already part of SW34 and does not require
a mathematical change to the candidate.

No improvement in c is proved. The current written c4=.125135, first-gain target
.125136, and later targets 1/6 and 1/4 are benchmarks, not inputs to the proofs.
The obstruction is unconditional for this restricted dictionary at every fixed
0<sigma<1. It is not an impossibility theorem for the full f_n source, arbitrary
balanced arithmetic differences, or joint growing q=2,3 families. No Gaussian,
H-covariance, character, conductor, or inherited-mask estimate follows.



## 1. Frozen source and acceptance boundaries

The reviewed source is [restricted provenance path] research revision]-drafts/headroom-b/report.md, **19907 bytes**,
SHA256 **dc02a32360e36695105ecfa63ab2b8d146b24f40719ed36e78e0892044fcb31d**.
Its freeze-manifest.json is **4776 bytes**, SHA256
**37c7b6526c790190cde88a09079a13b0aad382af8cdcf4ad8e45af5a4f89ca0b**.
Both bindings match the assigned frozen inputs. The whole report, manifest,
author helper, finite evidence and seed checkpoint were read. The author's
helper was not executed in its frozen directory.

| Candidate claims | Independent disposition |
|---|---|
| B1–B3: literal source, norm and Mellin factor | Accept; independently integrated below. |
| B4–B8: complete signed closure and every fixed finite seed | Accept; no bounded-coefficient or seed-conditioning assumption is needed. |
| B9: renewal extension and repair contract | Accept with the inherited zero extension and terminal jump explicit. Growing two-grid capture remains open. |
| B10–B12: full nonreal-lattice projection floor | Accept as a lower bound, not an identification of the entire annihilator or exact source distance. |
| B13–B15: unique prefix coefficients and full-tail RMS growth | Accept; actual arithmetic, with every natural Mobius zero retained. |
| B16–B17: common-signal two-grid recovery and Gaussian comparison | Accept on the stated line Re(s)=1, with tau>tau'>0; no local-energy or Hardy-membership transfer. |
| B18: source-resolvent zero atom | Accept for the exact fixed dictionary with positive summable weights and fixed finite seeds. |

The independent finite helper supplements the proofs; it does not establish an
infinite closure, asymptotic estimate, or zero-free region. Source snapshots and
read scopes are bound in this review's freeze manifest.

## 2. Literal arithmetic source and the correct zero-exclusion return

Put H_sigma=L2((0,1),x^(2sigma-1)dx), 0<sigma<1, and

    f_n(x)={1/(nx)}-n^(-1){1/x},   n>=1,   f_1=0.

On the reciprocal cell 1/(k+1)<x<=1/k, write 1/x=k+u, 0<=u<1.
Then {1/(nx)}=(k mod n+u)/n and {1/x}=u. Consequently

    f_n(k)=(k mod n)/n,
    ||F||_sigma^2=(1/(2sigma)) sum_(k>=1)
          [k^(-2sigma)-(k+1)^(-2sigma)] |F(k)|^2.          (R1)

Endpoints have zero measure. This is an infinite heavy-tail norm, not a finite
prefix norm. Every finite combination of the bounded f_n belongs to H_sigma.

For E_s(F)=integral_0^1 F(x)x^(s-1)dx, Cauchy-Schwarz gives

    ||E_s||^2=1/[2(Re(s)-sigma)],   Re(s)>sigma.             (R2)

The representing vector, using an inner product linear in its first variable,
is v_s(x)=x^(conjugate(s)-2sigma). Direct integration for Re(s)>1 gives

    integral_0^1 {theta/x}x^(s-1)dx
       =theta/(s-1)-theta^s zeta(s)/s,   0<theta<=1.

One way to verify this is to write {theta/x}=theta/x-floor(theta/x) and integrate
each indicator 1_(x<=theta/j). The absolutely convergent sum of their integrals
is theta^s zeta(s)/s. Subtract theta times the theta=1 identity. Holomorphic
continuation of the bounded source integral to Re(s)>0 yields

    E_s(f_n)=zeta(s)(n^(-1)-n^(-s))/s.                     (R3)

The removable value at s=1 is log(n)/n. Thus a zeta zero rho with Re(rho)>sigma
annihilates the closed original f_n span, but E_rho(1)=1/rho is nonzero.
Closure of 1 in that original span therefore suffices to exclude such zeros.
This uses neither a converse Nyman-Beurling theorem nor any Mertens input.
It excludes the open half-plane; no unproved boundary-line claim is made.

For an integer q>=2 define w_(q,n)=q f_(qn)-f_n. The actual cell value and Mellin
transform are

    w_(q,n)(k)=floor(k/n) mod q,
    E_s(w_(q,n))=(1-q^(1-s))zeta(s)n^(-s)/s.               (R4)

In particular the wavelets vanish on k<n and are bounded by q-1. The argument
allows all n>=1; this is a larger dictionary than any SW34 construction with
n>=N>=2, so the lower bounds apply to those constructions as well.

## 3. Complete signed fixed-grid obstruction and finite seeds

Let W_q be the H_sigma-closed complex span of all w_(q,n). For k!=0 set

    s_k=1+2pi i k/log q.

Zeta is holomorphic at these nonreal points, so every wavelet has E_(s_k)=0.
At the excluded real point s=1, however, (1-q^(1-s))zeta(s) has value log q.
The real pole cancellation does not erase the nonreal lattice.

For every W in W_q, continuity and (R2) imply

    ||1-W||_sigma^2 >= 2(1-sigma)/|s_k|^2,   k!=0.        (R5)

This lower bound is for the entire signed function in the infinite norm. It
already allows arbitrary complex coefficients, negative cross terms, complete
future repetitions, changing finite supports, and norm limits. It does not
come from replacing an arithmetic sum by its absolute majorant.

For q=2, log2>2/3 and pi<22/7 imply 2pi/log2<66/7. Thus

    ||1-W||_sigma^2 > (98/4405)(1-sigma).                 (R6)

The exact strict floors at c=1-sigma are respectively

| c benchmark | R6 floor |
|---|---|
| .125135=25027/200000 | 1226323/440500000 |
| .125136=7821/62500 | 383229/137656250 |
| 1/6 | 49/13215 |
| 1/4 | 49/8810 |

They are positive norm constants, not exponent losses that can be added to a
Gaussian or H budget. The frame fails even before asking for a first gain.

Now fix a finite E and S=sum_(n in E)c_n f_n. If 1-S were in W_q, evaluation at
every s_k would force

    zeta(s_k) P(s_k)=1,
    P(s)=sum_(n in E)c_n(n^(-1)-n^(-s)).                   (R7)

Remove n=1 terms. If r=|E|>0, set alpha_n=log n/log q. For every integer Q>=2,
the Q^r+1 orbit points j(alpha_n)_n modulo one occupy only Q^r coordinate boxes
of side 1/Q. Subtracting two points gives 1<=k<=Q^r and
max_n ||k alpha_n||<=1/Q. If these selected k have a bounded subsequence as
Q tends to infinity, a fixed nonzero k has all phases integral. Then P(s_k)=0,
contradicting R7. Otherwise pass to an unbounded subsequence. There

    |P(s_k)| <= (2pi/Q) sum_(n in E)|c_n|/n.               (R8)

The elementary estimate |zeta(1+it)|=O(log(2+|t|)) is sufficient. It follows
from, for integer N>=1 and Re(s)>0, s!=1,

    zeta(s)=sum_(n<=N)n^(-s)+N^(1-s)/(s-1)
                   -s integral_N^infinity {u}u^(-s-1)du.

This identity follows by integrating the floor counting function first in
Re(s)>1 and then continuing the absolutely convergent fractional-part tail.
Taking N=ceil|t| for |t|>=1 bounds the finite sum by O(log(2+|t|)) and both other
terms by O(1). Since log k<=r log Q and q is fixed, R8 gives
zeta(s_k)P(s_k)=O_(S,q)(log Q/Q), tending to zero. This contradicts R7.
The case E empty was already excluded by R5.

Finally W_q+span{f_n:n in E} is closed: it is the orthogonal sum of W_q and the
finite-dimensional image of that seed span under I-P_(W_q). Hence

    dist(1,W_q+span{f_n:n in E}) > 0.                     (R9)

This last step is essential. It converts failure for each fixed S into failure
for arbitrary sequences of refitted seed coefficients, including unbounded
ones. The proof does not give a useful numerical constant uniformly over all
finite sets E, and the candidate correctly does not claim one. For a specified
S, R2 and R7 give exactly the candidate's evaluable supremum B8.

Any fixed finite collection of q=3 wavelets is a finite collection of original
f_n combinations, so it cannot repair W_2. Conversely the theorem says nothing
against an unbounded supply of new directions. If ratios are powers b^j of one
integer base, the identity

    w_(b^j,n)=sum_(r=0)^(j-1) b^r w_(b,b^r n)

places the enlarged family inside W_b. Merely adding more such widths preserves
the obstruction.

## 4. Independent full-lattice projection calculation

The candidate's B10 is stronger than a single evaluation and has the correct
normalization. Write a=1-sigma, h=log q, and I_q(u)=(q^u-1)/u, with I_q(0)=h.
The isometry

    UF(y)=e^(-sigma y)F(e^(-y))

sends H_sigma to L2(0,infinity). It sends the Riesz vectors v_(s_k) to
e^(-a y)e^(2pi i k y/h). Their closed span for k!=0 is exactly

    e^(-a y) phi(y mod h),   integral_0^h phi(r)dr=0,

because the induced periodic weight

    W(r)=e^(-2ar)/(1-e^(-2ah))

is bounded above and below on [0,h]. Thus closure of the nonconstant Fourier
polynomials is the zero-unweighted-mean space, even in this weighted norm.
Pairing the target U1=e^(-sigma y) against these functions folds the half-line
into

    H(r)=e^(-r)/(1-e^(-h)),

where a+sigma=1. In L2(W dr), the representing function of this folded pairing
is H/W. The orthogonal complement of the zero-mean space is span{1/W}, not the
constant functions. Projection therefore gives

    J=integral_0^h H^2/W
           -(integral_0^h H/W)^2/(integral_0^h 1/W)
     =(1-q^(-2a))/(1-q^(-1))^2
          *[I_q(-2sigma)-I_q(1-2sigma)^2/I_q(2a)].         (R10)

Strict Cauchy-Schwarz gives J>0, since H is not constant on an interval of
positive length. The definition I_q(0)=h covers sigma=1/2 without a singularity.
Each vector projected onto annihilates W_q, so ||1-W||^2>=J for every W in W_q.
No assertion that these vectors exhaust W_q's orthogonal complement is needed.

This derivation retains the full infinite lattice, not a finite Gram truncation.
The candidate's illustrative decimals are not used as certificates. R6 provides
the independent exact rational certificates when a numerical floor is wanted.

## 5. Exact SW34 extension, all repetitions, and actual escaping tails

For B9, the contract inherited from SW34 must remain literal: N>=2;
R is supported on N<=k<2N and is zero elsewhere; and

    d_n=R(n)-R(n-1),   N<=n<=2N.

In particular d_(2N)=-R(2N-1) is included. The candidate's notation references
this contract; omitting its terminal jump would invalidate the identity.
For every k,

    w_(q,n)(k)=sum_(j>=1) [1-q 1_(q|j)] 1_(jn<=k).

All terms relevant to this k are finite. Summing d_n over
N<=n<=min(2N,floor(k/j)) telescopes to R(floor(k/j)), including when floor(k/j)
is beyond 2N because the total jump sum is zero. Consequently

    sum_(n=N)^(2N) d_n w_(q,n)(k)
      =sum_(j>=1) b_q(j) R(floor(k/j)),
    b_q(j)=1-q 1_(q|j).                                  (R11)

This is zero on k<N and equals R(k) on N<=k<2N. It also retains every later
shell. For q=2, b_q(j)=(-1)^(j-1), exactly SW35. SW38's second-shell identity
is preserved, but it never paid the whole norm. For a combined two-grid
extension, R1 applied to |F_2+F_3|^2 contains all four ordered terms
F_2 conjugate(F_2), F_2 conjugate(F_3), F_3 conjugate(F_2), F_3 conjugate(F_3).
No cross-grid tail identity or saving is inherited from the separate formulas.

The independent helper includes a negative control: N=3, R(5)=1, R zero
elsewhere. At k=6 the correct q=2 extension is 0, whereas dropping d_6 gives 1.
Thus this is a real convention, not cosmetic notation. It is a clarification of
the candidate's imported definition, not a counterexample to its stated source.

For the unique prefix fit let

    a_q(n)=sum_(j>=0:q^j|n) q^j mu(n/q^j).

The finite convolution a_q*b_q=delta_1 follows by multiplying the inverse
geometric series sum_j q^j delta_(q^j) with delta_1-q delta_q, and then using
mu*1=delta_1. This works for composite q too; no multiplicativity of a_q is
assumed. Therefore, for k<=N,

    H_(q,N)(k)=sum_(n<=N)a_q(n)w_(q,n)(k)
             =sum_(ell<=k)(a_q*b_q)(ell)=1.               (R12)

The matrix indexed by k,n<=N is triangular with diagonal 1, so these coefficients
are uniquely forced in that finite dictionary. For q=2 and odd m, only the top
two powers can contribute when r>=1:

    a_2(m)=mu(m),
    a_2(2^r m)=2^r mu(m)+2^(r-1)mu(2m)
              =2^(r-1)mu(m).

In particular squareful m still give the actual zero coefficients. The error
1-H_(q,N) is supported on k>N, a set of H_sigma measure
(N+1)^(-2sigma)/(2sigma), while its complete squared norm is at least R10. Its
conditional RMS there is therefore at least

    sqrt(2sigma J) (N+1)^sigma.                           (R13)

This proves the stated source-specific tail growth, without a Mertens premise.
Pointwise prefix convergence does not control the infinite weighted norm.

## 6. Source-resolvent consequence, including the atom at zero

For fixed q, a fixed finite E, positive weights v_n with sum v_n<infinity,
and positive u_n on E, define the exact operator

    K=sum_(n>=1) v_n(w_(q,n) tensor w_(q,n))
         +sum_(n in E)u_n(f_n tensor f_n).

It is positive trace class because ||w_(q,n)||^2<=(q-1)^2/(2sigma). Its
quadratic form is a sum of nonnegative weighted squared inner products, so

    ker K=(W_q+span{f_n:n in E})^perp.

For the spectral measure of the actual target 1, dominated convergence gives

    <1,lambda(K+lambda I)^(-1)1>
       =integral_[0,infinity) lambda/(t+lambda) dmu_1(t)
       ->mu_1({0})
       =||P_(ker K)1||^2>0.                              (R14)

The integrand is exactly 1 at t=0 and tends to 0 at positive t. Hence every
lambda>0 resolvent value is already at least that atom. With no seeds, the atom
is at least J. With seeds it is still positive by R9, but J is not automatically
a lower bound for the patched source.

Changing positive summable weights cannot change this kernel. Polynomial,
exponential or predetermined block weights are covered when they satisfy the
stated positivity and summability. Every finite truncation from the same fixed
dictionary has span inside the full one and inherits the distance floor. This
does not cover a growing finite seed set that introduces infinitely many new
directions. The full original f_n resolvent remains open.

This uses the generic A08.2 spectral identity, already paid in the old record.
The new deduction is the strictly positive atom for the literal fixed-ratio
wavelet source. It is neither a generic compactness obstruction nor a failure
of an upper-budget estimate.

## 7. Paired q=2,3 conditioning: exact scope, all heights and two heights

Define the entire normalized factors

    B_q(s)=(1-q^(1-s))/(s-1),   B_q(1)=log q.

Their nonreal zero lattices have no common point: equality of the phases would
give a nontrivial equality between integer powers of 2 and 3. This observation
alone has N28 ancestry. The candidate additionally pays a coarse effective
conditioning bound sufficient for Gaussian height cutoffs.

Here is an independent verification of its constants. For t>=1 let
delta=max_(q=2,3)|1-e^(-it log q)| and choose nearest nonnegative integers m,n
to t log2/(2pi), t log3/(2pi). Let the two phase errors be e_2,e_3. The sine
chord bound on [-pi,pi] gives |e_q|<=pi delta/2. If delta<1/2, m,n cannot both
be zero: otherwise t log3<=pi/4<log3. Unique factorization gives 3^m!=2^n, and
the integral of 1/u between these distinct integers implies

    |m log3-n log2| >= 1/max(3^m,2^n)
       >=3^(-1/2)exp(-t log2 log3/(2pi)).

The phase-error identity gives the upper bound delta log6/4 for the same
quantity. Thus delta>=4 exp(-t log2 log3/(2pi))/(sqrt3 log6)>=e^(-t)/2.
If delta>=1/2 the last inequality is immediate. Dividing by t proves
max_q|B_q(1+it)|>=e^(-t)/(2t). Negative t follow by conjugation.
For |t|<=1, the chord bound instead gives
|B_q(1+it)|>=2 log q/pi; in particular B_2>1/4 and B_3>1/2 in modulus.
Consequently, for T>=1 and |t|<=T,

    S(t)=|B_2(1+it)|^2+|B_3(1+it)|^2
       >=e^(-2T)/[4(1+T)^2].                             (R15)

For a measurable common V(t), define W_q(t)=B_q(1+it)V(t). Pointwise,

    V(t)=sum_(q=2,3) m_q(t)W_q(t),
    m_q(t)=conjugate(B_q(1+it))/S(t),
    |V(t)|^2<=S(t)^(-1)sum_q|W_q(t)|^2.                  (R16)

On [-T,T] this recovery has L2 operator norm at most 2(1+T)e^T. On the whole
line R15's proof gives S(t)^(-1)<=4(1+|t|)^2e^(2|t|). For tau>tau'>0 put
Delta=tau-tau'. Then (1+u)^2<=e^(2u) and 4u-Delta u^2<=4/Delta imply
the explicit bound

    integral_R |e^(tau(1+it)^2/2)V(t)|^2 dt
      <=4 exp(Delta+4/Delta) sum_(q=2,3)
            integral_R |e^(tau'(1+it)^2/2)W_q(t)|^2 dt.  (R17)

This independently proves B17 with all heights paid. Extended integrals are
allowed; when the right side is finite it gives the asserted finite left side.
The constant depends on the positive Gaussian-width gap. It is not a bound
with tau'=tau. Indeed S(t)<=8/t^2 for nonzero t; choosing V supported in
[T,T+1] disproves an equal-width inequality with a fixed constant for arbitrary
V as T tends to infinity. This is a useful precise limit of the stated lemma.

At T=D sqrt(log X), fixed D, the recovery coefficient bound and the product of
two such bounds are X^o(1). This observation pays multiplier coefficients; it
does not prove an original physical Gaussian energy comparison.

To display the missing distinction, on a finite height interval let
P(x)=integral a(x,t)V(t)dt and K(t,t')=integral a(x,t)conjugate(a(x,t'))dnu(x),
under hypotheses allowing the indicated finite integrals. Substitution of R16
gives the exact expansion

    ||P||^2=sum_(q,r in {2,3}) integral integral
       K(t,t') m_q(t) conjugate(m_r(t'))
       W_q(t) conjugate(W_r(t')) dt dt'.                 (R18)

There are four ordered grid pairs and two independent heights. Neither R15 nor
R17 replaces K(t,t') by its diagonal. A local physical norm, arithmetic mask,
or limiting whole-height version of this local formula needs its own valid
comparison and tail theorem. The candidate expressly reserves these steps.

The exact actual-source common-signal interface is also worth recording. For
the SAME finite coefficient list c_n in the two grids, put A(s)=sum c_n n^(-s).
Then R4 gives

    Mellin(sum c_n w_(q,n))(s)=B_q(s)V(s),
    V(s)=((s-1)zeta(s)/s)A(s).                            (R19)

Thus the paired recovery really can apply to a common arithmetic source, not
just an arbitrary abstract vector. However independently fitted lists give
A_2 and A_3, hence generally different V_2 and V_3. R16 cannot be applied to
them as a common V without a new identity. Moreover the recovered expression
in R19 is not automatically in the required unweighted half-plane Hardy space
or the original physical source class: the multiplier contains s-1, and the
boundary inverse uses conjugation. B17 establishes only the stated weighted
line norm. These restrictions are necessary to interpret simultaneous
detectors accurately.

## 8. Complete reopening contract and ancestry

For the surviving joint arithmetic option, choose nested finite spaces V_j
spanned by specified original wavelets with q=2,3 (and, if desired, a fixed
finite original seed). Let r_j=1-P_(V_j)1, d_j^2=||r_j||^2, and let U_j be the
orthogonalized newly added block in V_(j+1) intersect V_j^perp. Then

    d_(j+1)^2=d_j^2-g_j,   g_j=||P_(U_j)r_j||^2.

Equivalently, for the block map A_j with orthogonalized columns spanning U_j,
its full Gram C_j=A_j^*A_j and
q_j=A_j^*r_j give g_j=q_j^* C_j^dagger q_j. The dagger respects the true
nullspace. A sufficient quantitative target is

    g_j>=delta_j d_j^2,   0<=delta_j<=1,
    sum_j delta_j=infinity.                              (R20)

Unless a residual has already vanished, iterating gives
d_j^2<=d_0^2 product_(i<j)(1-delta_i), tending to zero. All entries here are
the complete R1 Gram, including every later reciprocal cell and every ordered
cross-grid product. A sequence of independently restarted prefix fits is not
this compatible projection chain. Neither artificial-zero removal nor
separate grid conditioning supplies R20.

The alternative exact gate is o(1) of the source resolvent for the enlarged
dictionary, with positive summable weights fixed as part of that source and
with its zero atom included. Any vanishing rate would suffice. At
sigma=.874864 either complete gate would imply the first-gain zero exclusion;
at sigma=5/6 or 3/4 it would give the corresponding later target. These are
conditional returns, not achieved estimates.

The source comparisons establish the following scope and deduplication.

* **SW33–SW41:** SW34 is the exact q=2 dictionary studied here. SW38 proves one
  leakage shell; SW41 says the absolute future-tail bound diverges at
  sigma<=1 and explicitly leaves signed capture open. R5/R9/R10/R14 now rule
  out full signed capture of 1 by this dictionary, including any fixed finite
  starting arithmetic patch. That is stronger than the old majorant failure.
* **F08.A/N1/N2, F19.A, A08–A09:** These already supply the original source,
  heavy-tail Gram, capture and resolvent gates. Their arbitrary balanced
  differences n f_n-m f_m, including A09's varying m=2N, are larger families.
  The new restricted obstruction does not close those proposals. The spectral
  theorem by itself and the generic capture identity earn no new credit.
* **N28.D/C:** Two discrete dilations b=2,3 already avoid a common unwanted
  nonreal multiplier zero for Delta_b M=M(bx)-b^alpha M(x); continuum dilations
  already have quantitative calibration. Common scale 6 was not a contraction.
  The non-common-zero principle is therefore inherited. The present positive
  source floor, fixed-finite-seed obstruction, literal inverse coefficients
  and the specific B_q Gaussian conditioning are distinct statements about a
  different actual source, not a newly proved Mobius energy estimate.
* **The old SW two-grid theorem is different:** its shell-start set is
  {2^j,3*2^j}, with consecutive ratios 3/2 and 4/3, and it compares affine,
  Mertens and continuum energies under an inherited growth premise. These are
  overlapping shell grids, not the two arithmetic wavelet dilation families
  q=2 and q=3. Their energy equivalence cannot simply be substituted into R20.
* **W22/R22:** R22.4–R22.11 prove legitimate finite known-zero division for the
  actual divisible Hardy source and its changed target. They do not identify
  the arithmetic span with the ambient inner ideal or prove Gram capture.
  That result supplies no permission to divide out the present artificial
  lattice while leaving both the original target 1 and its norm gate unchanged.
  The Mellin transform of 1-W has value 1/s_k at every artificial zero, so it is
  not divisible there. Even a single such division would have a pole. Changing the
  target to make a division legal would require a new calibrated zero return.

For the user's simultaneous-detector idea, the exact useful analogy is narrow:
one wavelet grid has blind Mellin frequencies which the other grid sees, and a
common underlying signal admits the paid joint recovery R16–R19. The arithmetic
work is still to control that common signal or prove full joint capture. Pooling
separately bounded or separately fitted detector outputs supplies neither.
This review claims no literature novelty beyond the comparison with the exact
maintained local sources.

## 9. Independent evidence, limitations and final handoff

check_review.py performs exact rational checks of the literal fractional-part
values (7500 cases), wavelets (30000), convolution inverses (512), prefix cells
(136), signed renewal components (3864), and all four ordered complex grid terms
(480). It includes composite q=4,6, the terminal-jump negative control, and the
four exact rational floors. The run completed with exit code 0 and its sibling
check_review_output.json records the result. The pre-existing Python launcher
warning about C:\Python314\python.exe did not prevent execution. No floating
point test or truncated lattice is used to prove R5–R20.

The remaining mathematical work is precisely the complete enlarged-source
capture or resolvent estimate in Section 8, with a fixed target sigma. No
surviving proof of that estimate was found or claimed in this review. No fatal
error was found in the candidate. The only source clarification needed for a
standalone restatement is the B9 support/zero-extension/terminal-jump convention.

Review is mathematically complete. The final operations are full artifact
readback, immutable hash/manifest receipt, own-claim release and explicit STOP.
Root alone owns promotion, canonical records, endpoint replay and publication.

# [private research revision] independent review of the merged GPT6-Pro consultation

Frozen review scope: the COMPLETE retained 4,912-line, 311,255-byte source, SHA256 5998db643c6d3f477fcb9c06c6d349f6eae5c7505dc90e9ed7588a005aea4146. References of the form S8.2/L3541 identify its section and numbered line. The separate Concrete Progress note is outside this assignment. Parent owns integration; this report changes no accepted theorem.

The accepted written analytic endpoint used when this review began was c4=25027/200000=.125135, theta4=.874865, relative to the pinned PR9/Gao PR15 inputs. Its new endpoint formalization and independent kernel replay remain pending; old c0 has a separate three-kernel receipt. Preserve Zhongpai Gao's local-refinement credit and OpenAI / Hailey Collet / Akash Levy's framework, source and numerator credit. The merged source's historical c0 and proposed C=4.45 are not current endpoints.

Current-baseline amendment: the controller has since accepted c5=7821/62500=.125136, theta5=54679/62500=.874864, in [restricted mathematical source] which I read. This separate affine-window result is not produced by the consultation. The historical c4 ledger below is retained; against c5 the first strict target is a=.874864-eta for fixed eta>0. The illustrative a=.87486 still improves by .000004. The limiting complete square/moment exponents are now 1.749728/.249728, the quartic period exponent is -1.625136, and the Mayer boundary is .437432. Stable absolute square-dilation transfer at the current boundary requires tau>.125136. The buffered beta=.874866 used below remains admissible. New-endpoint formalization/replay and original family/credit qualifications remain unchanged.

## Decision

Retain the consultation as a component library. Its most substantial distinct constructions are the Fourier-fixed exterior completion R4E, the repeated-square phase family R4V, and the centered Mayer feedback R4D. I independently checked their relevant algebra/return, verified the essential primary imports, and derived the next Mayer feedback identity below. None supplies the missing arithmetic estimate. The coherent hook model, augmented factorial flux and adaptive true-gcd return are useful secondary survivors. Growing-depth Liouville is a legitimate open completion problem, with a nonlocal return that the proposed moving family does not yet satisfy.

The source's own ordinary-proof labels are evidence, not acceptance. The companion component-index.json maps all numbered sections, substantial subclaims, and audit programs, with exact duplication/supersession and the remaining debt. Entries classified as source-claim were inspected but not fully independently reproved. A scoped obstruction never means the full QRH route is impossible.

I read the current proof, both complete attempt ledgers covering all 29 families/109 children, [private research revision]–57 attempt deltas, creative records and source provenance. Exact searches found no prior Mayer/R4E/R4V/hook/factorial-flux/adaptive-gcd construction in the canonical research record. Earlier continued-fraction, detector-vector, graph, function-field and inverse-operator ideas are ancestry, not duplicates of these formulas. No literature-priority claim is made.

## Complete targets (c4 ledger, with current c5 amendment above)

There is no smallest strict improvement. For any fixed eta>0, a=.874865-eta is the first-gain growth target; all epsilon losses must be absorbed in a fixed positive buffer. The illustrative a=.87486 would return c=.12514, a gain .000005. The following are complete targets, not proved bounds.

| Target | First gain: a=.87486 | c=1/6 | c=1/4 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Full arithmetic dyadic norm X^(a+epsilon) | .87486 | 5/6 | 3/4 |
| Full signed square energy exponent 2a | 1.74972 | 5/3 | 3/2 |
| Optional complete two-height moment on Re(s)=3/4, exponent 2a-3/2 | .24972 | 1/6 | 0 |
| Quartic R=X^(-5/2)F norm exponent a-5/2 | -1.62514 | -5/3 | -7/4 |
| Mayer resonance exclusion to Re(s)>a/2 | .43743 | 5/12 | 3/8 |
| Attenuation required for stable absolute square convolution | tau>.12514 | tau>1/6 | tau>1/4 |

The limiting c4 square/moment exponents were 1.74973/.24973, not the source's 1.749773294.../.249773294.... The c5 values are recorded in the amendment above. The Gaussian full-field completion has no fixed positive error floor. Older SP replacements with norm error q=.87407 can only return max(a,q): they cannot reach 1/6 or 1/4. The unpruned factorial/Riesz and quartic constructions must use their own full sources and tails.

The quartic family proves a statement for zeta_Q(i), hence ordinary zeta (and its quadratic factor). It does not automatically extend the project's whole fixed ordinary/Eisenstein-Hecke family endpoint. A twisted construction and its complete norm are separate obligations. Mayer is likewise an ordinary-zeta route. Do not replace the globally scoped accepted c4 with a zeta-only conditional comparison.

## A. Exterior completion: valid local progress, exact global gap

At a good place of residue size Q, write b_j=1_(pi^j O), with vol(O)=1 and Fourier(b_j)=Q^(-j)b_(-j). The proposed

    f=(1+Q^-2)b_0-b_2-Q^-2 b_-2

is Fourier-fixed, equals 1_O-1_(pi²O) on O, and has value and integral zero. Direct integration gives

    ||f||²=1-Q^-4, <f,b_0>=1-Q^-2,
    ||f-b_0||²=2Q^-2-Q^-4.

More generally, for even a supported in O, A=int a,

    E(a)=a+Fourier(a)-A b_0,
    E(a)|O=a, Fourier(E(a))=E(a),
    ||E(a)||²=2||a||²-|A|².

Proof: Fourier(a) is the constant A on O; Fourier²a=a; <a,Fourier(a)>=|A|², which gives the norm formula. This verifies R4E1–4 and R4V6–8 without a representation-theoretic assumption. Ten finite exact rational cases independently checked these identities.

The chosen restricted tensor converges because sum_p Q^-2 converges. This is not convergence of a product of operators on all vectors: the local operator deviations are O(Q^-1). Nelson's Theorem2/(16), in the updated primary text, explicitly uses GLOBAL evenness. Thus the fixed odd archimedean vector paired with an odd bad-place vector is eligible, and the stated factor-2 theta norm identity applies to finite Schwartz approximations. This is a bounded underlying automorphic L2 construction, before the moving restriction. [Nelson](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00209-020-02665-8).

The source-support argument is also sound at its stated finite stage. Invariance under n(O) forces a local Whittaker coefficient to have integral frequency. The selected frequency is a fixed unit times m², so a negative valuation of m kills both fixed quartic source coefficients. Exterior values therefore do not change the equal-square arithmetic coefficient. The averaging must be adelic (or explicitly finite-unipotent); a fractional archimedean frequency cannot be inserted into the old complex torus and assigned its old orthogonality.

The radial uniqueness claim is correct. A radial difference supported outside O is invariant under translations by O. Its Fourier transform is supported in O; Fourier-fixedness then makes the difference zero. Consequently failure of this vector's coupled boundary cancellation cannot be repaired by another radial Fourier-fixed extension of the same interior mask.

The essential quartic imports were checked: DDHLv4 (3.11) contains the conjugate-prime factor, and (4.39) gives the square relation with two ray components. Their prime normalization/CRT gives Q1, with natural zeros at nonsquarefree moduli. The later paper (6.16) states unrestricted fourth-power periodicity, (6.18) the signed square relation, and Proposition8.2 supplies a nonzero seed. This uses no conjectural generic quartic coefficient formula. [DDHLv4](https://arxiv.org/html/2306.11875v4), [de Faveri–Dunn–Hoffstein v1](https://arxiv.org/html/2607.07911v1).

Cheapest decisive next calculation: one good prime, the actual two quartic unramified source vectors, actual ray/angular line, and E(a). Compute BOTH relative orbit boundary germs, including the source intertwiners and their scalar factors. Require unchanged identity output 1-Q^-s and test whether the geometric mode 1-chi2(p)Q^(1-2s) disappears. Fourier symmetry of the unary factor alone is insufficient. If the bad germ survives, radial exterior adjustment is exhausted; if it vanishes, a uniform relative-distribution/restriction estimate with the exponent in the table is still required. Neither a Hilbert limit nor a tempered tensor supplies it.

Exact ancestry: F15.S/G and [restricted research revision] distinguish one-vector convergence from period continuity; F25.C and [restricted research revision]-T01 price deletion/division. R4E is a new explicit representative in an invisible arithmetic subspace. It repairs the unary Fourier-support mismatch of this source's R3Q10; it does not supersede those global obstructions.

## B. Both detectors: the numerator-moving vector and paid transfers

### The family really preserves the denominator

For K=Q(i), fixed excluded primes S and chi2((d))=alpha(d)^2, let F_K(X)=sum_c mu_K(c) k(log(Nc/X)). Then the source's family is exactly

    F_t(X)=sum_d chi2(d) Nd^(1+it) F_K(X/Nd²),
    Mellin F_t(s)=M(s) L_K^S(2s-1-it,chi2)/zeta_K^S(s).

Every ideal has unique m=c d² with c squarefree; c and d need NOT be coprime. At squarefree m, d=1 and the coefficient is unchanged. This is not an ordinary Hecke twist of the whole denominator.

The return assumes M(s) is nonzero on the required Re(s)>a. Merged lines48–54 stipulate the inherited profile and its zero-free range without reproducing that profile or proof; I have not identified it with another detector merely by notation. This remains an explicit input, including for a=3/4. A possible fully specified replacement is the infinite convolution of uniform probability densities on [-2^-j,2^-j], j>=1: it is C-infinity, supported in [-1,1], with M(s)=product_j sinh(2^-j s)/(2^-j s), nonzero for Re(s)>0. Normal convergence follows from sum_j 2^-2j<infinity; arbitrarily many box factors give arbitrary Fourier decay. Using this replacement requires the actual period and arithmetic estimate for this fixed profile, not transfer of an unspecified profile's bound.

For a fixed positive-length bounded I, a bound

    int_I ||F_t||²_[X,2X] dt << X^(2a+epsilon)

gives an L2(I)-valued holomorphic Mellin transform for Re(s)>a, by dyadic Cauchy–Schwarz. Continue the multiplication identity with zeta_K^S(s). At any hypothetical zero rho with Re(rho)>a, its left side is zero; its right side is the vector

    N_rho(t)=M(rho)L_K^S(2rho-1-it,chi2).

This vector is nonzero: the fixed L-function cannot vanish on a vertical interval without vanishing identically, and M is nonzero by the explicit profile hypothesis above. This handles arbitrary finite multiplicity and proves the strict half-plane without dividing by a scalar numerator. The arithmetic moment, including all d,e and ideal/source cross terms, is still open.

### Uniform readout, finite parameters, and actual costs

At a fixed rho, set m_rho=max_(t in I)|N_rho(t)| and D_rho=max_(t in I)|N'_rho(t)|. If D_rho>0, a one-sided interval of length

    ell=min(|I|/2,m_rho/(2D_rho))

has |N_rho|>=m_rho/2. Hence ||N_rho||²>=ell*m_rho²/4. If D_rho=0 the exact lower bound is |I|m_rho². These are positive quantities; no claimed numerical all-height lower bound is hidden.

For a fixed compact strip/height window K0 lying in the relevant half-plane, m0=min_(s in K0)max_I|N_s|>0 and D0=max_(K0 x I)|N'_s|<infinity. The same formula gives a uniform compact-window bound. A grid with mesh <=m0/(2D0) then captures at least m0/2 at one node for every s in K0; equal-weight squared readout costs at worst m0²/(4N). This is an effective prescription only once certified bounds for m0,D0 are supplied. The consultation supplies no explicit bound as the height window tends to infinity. Its qualitative pole contradiction does not need one. A quantitative contour or resolvent argument WOULD need that additional height cost.

Parameter order matters:

* Fix I before the scale X. The continuum norm is a complete sufficient target.
* A single unspecified generic t already avoids simultaneous masking at every zeta_K zero: each fixed rho has a discrete bad-t set, and their union is countable. This is an existence statement, not a certified named phase or an estimate for that phase. Fubini applied to all rational positive epsilon values can extract an almost-everywhere scalar return from the continuum norm.
* A preselected finite explicit list has no established global noncommon-zero guarantee here. On each fixed compact window a finite list exists by the preceding bound. Growing the height window requires renewing its capture certificate.
* Finite moving quadrature can approximate the continuum ARITHMETIC energy cheaply. On x in [X,2X], the compact kernel gives Nd<=sqrt(2eX), so F_t is an exponential polynomial with frequencies in [0,Lambda], Lambda=.5 log(2eX), and total coefficient mass O(X log X). Thus |F_t|² has frequencies in [-Lambda,Lambda]. An N-node Gauss rule on I is exact to degree2N-1 and has positive weights summing |I|. Taylor's integral remainder gives error at most

      C_I X² log²X [e Lambda |I|/(4N)]^(2N).

  Taking N=C_A log X with a sufficiently large fixed C_A pays any prescribed X^-A error, uniformly in x; integrate dx/x afterwards. This is O(log X) parameter samples with no exponent loss. Nodes depend on X; they approximate the fixed interval norm and are not a claim about finitely many fixed detectors. All within-sample square-divisor cross terms remain.

### The exact obstruction to a free overlap transfer

Using the same physical weighted shell norm as current-proof G28, absolute Minkowski on F_t costs

    sum_d Nd^(1-2a),

which diverges for every a<=1. Truncating at Nd<=sqrt(X) costs X^(1-a), cancelling the gain X^a and yielding only X (logarithms at the boundary). Uniform local Hilbert norms do not remove this arithmetic restriction cost. A scalar phase has correlations int_I exp(it log(Nd/Ne))dt, a sinc kernel, not independent-prime orthogonality. Equal norms are fully coherent, and nearby log norms have large overlap.

There is a stable attenuated equivalence, which identifies precisely the easy case. Put

    F_(tau,t)(X)=sum_d chi2(d) Nd^(1-2tau+it) F_K(X/Nd²).

For fixed a+tau>1, both this convolution and its Dirichlet inverse are bounded on the global weighted shell norm. Their absolute constants are at most

    sum_d Nd^(-(2a+2tau-1))=zeta_K^S(2a+2tau-1),

with the inverse using mu_K(d)chi2(d)Nd^(1-2tau+it). These bounds are uniform for real t. They also hold for a Hilbert-valued t-family. Their Mellin numerator lies in Re(2s-1+2tau)>1 for Re(s)>a. Thus the attenuated family has a safe numerator but the same arithmetic exponent problem as F_K. Strictly crossing the threshold costs tau>c; equality is not covered. This is an exact counterpart of the older W26 shifted-reciprocal safe-region equivalence, with a different square-dilation exponent.

For the unattenuated phase family the denominator-only return is a real addition to F25.E/N28's noncommon-multiplier idea: it moves an auxiliary arithmetic L-function without moving the zeta denominator. The sufficient moment is not weaker in its required power. It may permit a better coupled period estimate; it does not inherit one.

### Rational Riesz/Gaussian connection

The factorial detector uses precisely the current rational coefficient A(n)=mu(n)-2*1_(2|n)mu(n/2). Let R(y)=F2(e^y), with F2(x)=sum_(n<=x) A(n)(1-n/x)^2. Distributionally,

    D(D+1)(D+2)R=2 sum_n A(n) delta_(log n),  D=d/dy.

Therefore the fixed Gaussian is exactly

    G_tau(e^y)=h_tau * R(y),
    h_tau=.5 D(D+1)(D+2)g_tau.

Every exponentially weighted L1 norm of h_tau is finite. Shell Minkowski gives a paid Riesz-to-Gaussian transfer at any fixed growth exponent with the usual left-tail/neighbor-shell treatment. The naive reverse multiplier contains exp(tau*t²/2) on a vertical line and is unbounded; a reverse arithmetic implication would need a zero-return/contour argument, not bounded Gaussian deconvolution.

This rational identity does not identify Q(i)'s F_K with A(n). zeta_K= zeta L(.,chi_-4), and ideal coefficients are a Dirichlet convolution of the two reciprocal coefficient sequences; they are different arithmetic fields. No Gaussian/compact component mask, signed subset, or current f3 bound is inherited by the quartic period. The other review owns the direct compact-to-Gaussian hierarchy.

Stacking Gaussian with a scalar compact smoother of the same A has no independent numerator benefit when each multiplier already is nonzero. A positive sum of their complete energies is at least either component energy; mixed scalar readouts need all cross terms and a calibrated nonvanishing numerator. The phase family above is the specific genuinely complementary-numerator opportunity.

Cheapest decisive test: compute the one-prime COUPLED relative boundary germ on E(a_(p,t)) as an identity in u=Q^(it), not only at t=0. Then seek one uniform finite-prime/finite-valuation L2(I x [X,2X]) estimate with all crosses. The local vector norm bound and this report's quadrature pay approximation costs, but not the moving relative restriction. There is no independent arithmetic cancellation assumption.

## C. Centered Mayer feedback: exact return and a new next-return formula

Mayer's primary source defines L_s on A_infinity(|z-1|<3/2), gives its nuclear meromorphic continuation and Z_mod(s)=det(1-L_s)det(1+L_s). A nontrivial Riemann zero rho yields a zero at s=rho/2 and hence a +1 OR -1 eigenvalue. The source's sign-specific correspondence is explicitly conjectural there; retaining both signs is essential. [Mayer, pp.3–5,8–9](https://archive.mpim-bonn.mpg.de/id/eprint/346/1/preprint_1990_86.pdf).

For Re(s)>0 the centered operator

    Q_s f(z)=sum_(n>=1)[(n+z)^(-2s)f(1/(n+z))-n^(-2s)f(0)]

converges locally normally. Its rank-one completion is L_s=Q_s+zeta(2s)Pi. At s=rho/2, L_s=Q_s exactly. Relative to f=c+g, g(0)=0,

    Q_s = [[0,ell_s],[h_s,Ktilde_s]],
    h_s(z)=sum_n[(n+z)^(-2s)-n^(-2s)],
    ell_s g=sum_n n^(-2s)g(1/n).

Here Ktilde subtracts the value at zero in both branches; its grouped tail is n^(-2Re(s)-2). The source's first feedback is

    ell_s h_s=sum_k d(k)[(k+1)^(-2s)-k^(-2s)].

Independent further deduction, with w=2s:

    ell_s Ktilde_s h_s
      = sum_(m,n,k>=1) [
          (kmn+k+m)^(-w)-(kmn+k)^(-w)
          -(kmn+m)^(-w)+(kmn)^(-w)].

To derive it, substitute h into the two Ktilde branches, evaluate z=1/m, then multiply by m^-w. Group each four-term mixed difference BEFORE rearranging. With N=kmn the bracket equals int_0^k int_0^m w(w+1)(N+u+v)^(-w-2)du dv. Hence, for sigma=Re(s)>0,

    |ell Ktilde h|
      <= |2s(2s+1)| zeta(2sigma+1)^2 zeta(2sigma+2).

This proves absolute convergence of the grouped triple sum. For real s>0 it is positive, whereas the first feedback is negative. At complex height no positivity remains. Nine independent exact finite nested-operator/triple-sum checks passed; the infinite convergence is the displayed analytic bound. The O(|s|²) absolute estimate is not a contraction.

If lambda-Ktilde_s is invertible, a lambda=+/-1 resonance requires

    lambda=ell_s(lambda-Ktilde_s)^(-1)h_s.

If that block is not invertible, the full block eigen-equation must be retained; Schur elimination cannot discard that case. A sufficient target is uniform exclusion of both resonances on a/2<Re(s)<.5, all heights, plus the already accepted outside region. For example a bound ||Ktilde_s||<1-eta together with both feedback magnitudes <1 would suffice, but no such bound is available. The spectral exclusion by itself is a reformulation, not a weaker proved arithmetic target.

The real C1 restriction can be used one way: a holomorphic eigenfunction restricts to a nonzero real-interval function, so exclusion on a correctly defined larger real space excludes the holomorphic eigenfunction. An arbitrary real-space eigenvalue need not lift. The continued-fraction phase derivative contains a nonzero branch determinant; this distinguishes it from commuting scalar dilations, but it does not supply a high-height estimate.

Cheapest decisive work: evaluate the next grouped returns and their actual two-branch phase degeneracy at the target strips, retaining the parabolic tail. Long-branch absolute tails at N about |t| cost |t|^(1-2sigma), while the fixed complex-disk supremum may cost exponentially in |t|. A real-space oscillatory return estimate must address both; another finite truncation spectrum is not all-height exclusion. Exact ancestry is F24.X's scattering half-parameter warning and F14/F26 transfer programs; the explicit centered operator and shifted-divisor feedback are distinct.

## D. Secondary survivors and quantitative reopen conditions

**Factorial flux.** R2S/R3F is distinct from fixed-order DYADIC-r and N28, and from the later moving Bessel two-root filter. Its full A-source is retained. For every fixed B in {8^j,9^j:j>=1}, the old beta=.874866 is admissible relative to c4; choose R>B^beta. The augmented H_R contains every forward cell with weight R^-2j and obeys

    H_R'=-2 Re Q_R,
    |Q_R|<=R sqrt(H_R(H_R-||e0||²))<=R H_R.

Thus the good-time bound -Re Q_R<=s H_R+C exp(2d t), with sqrt(B)<d<s<B^a, and bad-time upper density delta satisfying s+(R-s)delta<=B^a, is a complete sufficient target. The ordinary diagonal and exact dilation diagonal are paid; all other arithmetic crosses are not. Truncate j linearly in t using the old exponent, not a desired-exponent norm.

For the explicit choice R=2B^beta, s=(B^a+sqrt B)/2, the allowed bad fraction is

    delta < (B^a-s)/(R-s).

At B=8 this is about .213017/.174775/.112883 for the three target columns. A sufficient good-time first-cell fraction is respectively .867027/.881683/.905451. These numbers are diagnostic evaluations of an exact formula, not observed arithmetic frequencies. All powers of 8 and 9 remain required; the allowance shrinks like B^(a-beta) at large B. Source replacement errors would create their own exponent floor. The graph-profile compatibility is useful but does not prove the required transport identity or comparison norm.

The source's density-one argument is in entire FILTER TIME, with exponential accuracy and degree proportional to time. It is not contradicted merely by W38's sparse bad physical dyads, which concern a different regularity/clock. Its actual arithmetic small-values hypothesis is still unproved. W39's every-log-interval Gaussian theorem is another valid, differently quantified return, not a substitute.

**Adaptive true-gcd weights.** This is not current W36/G33's paid large-gcd scalar mask, nor mark-adaptive native H selection. On a global/truncated weighted shell space the source's tail operator with r>R0 has norm at most q_a=sum_(r>R0)r^-2a. If q_a<1, its inverse costs (1-q_a)^-1, even for bounded x-dependent tail weights, provided the finite head is 1 at r=1 and zero at 2..R0. The minimal-excess criterion is an exact nonlinear formulation of the needed cancellation, not an algorithm that proves it.

R0=1,2,4 suffice respectively in the three target columns; numerical integral-comparison intervals for q_a are [.962799778,.962799879], [.808542598,.808542815], [.941371368,.941372369]. Elementary upper certificates are sum_(n=2)^5 n^-1.74972+5^(-.74972)/.74972<.992 for the first column; q<3/(2*2^(2/3))<1 for the second; and q<integral_4^infinity x^(-3/2)dx=1 for the third. The numerical intervals are diagnostics, not outward-rounded formal certificates. For the signed mu-gcd truncation with beta=.874866, tail X^beta R^-beta is below X^a when R=X^rho and rho>(beta-a)/beta: thresholds .0000068582, .047473175, .142725858. The unweighted tail uses the larger denominator 2beta-1: .0000080029, .055396684, .166547513. Every retained true-gcd term and both norm/scalar crosses remain. A useful next step must specify an actual arithmetic weight rule that meets the whole-core bound; favorable gcd labels do not suffice.

**Coherent hook model.** For 0<=R<t and odd primitive function-field characters, inverse coefficients are complete symmetric functions h_d and plain coefficients are (-1)^n e_n. Their partial convolution equals

    sum_(d=0)^R h_d (-1)^(t-d)e_(t-d)
      =(-1)^(t-R) s_(R+1,1^(t-R-1)).

I checked 108 exact examples using the independent Jacobi–Trudi determinant. Haar U(N) character orthogonality gives squared norm1 if the partition length t-R<=N, and zero otherwise; total degree>N is allowed. Keating–Rudnick (8.7) verifies the odd-primitive inverse-L/symmetric-power normalization. It averages the appropriate full character family in a large-field setting, not the fixed-order sextic number-field rows. [Keating–Rudnick](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1504.03444).

Cheapest decisive test: derive the exact geometric monodromy and conductor/height weights of the ACTUAL fixed-order6 inverse/plain family, with its finite ray and natural-zero restrictions. Until then there is no paid number-field JM exponent to compare with c4, 1/6 or 1/4. A Haar norm1 model is not that estimate. Sawin–Whitehead Theorem3.10 explicitly requires gcd(n,Mii+n/2)|Mij; for the proposed inverse node n=6,Mii=3,coupling1 this requires 6|1 and fails. The alternate Dirichlet-node theorem assumes Mii=0. This rejects the displayed matrix, not all MDS realizations. [Sawin–Whitehead](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2507.08662).

**Growing-depth Liouville.** Fixed-r completion and a global weighted-space inverse are coherent. At a>.5 the return constant is

    C_a <= zeta(2a)/[(a-.5)(2^(1-a)-1)].

Depth r about kappa log X/loglog X makes C_a^r subpower. It does not justify evaluating an r-dependent source on one physical shell: the kappa inverse uses FUTURE scales 2^j x and the square inverse uses past scales. All these evaluations must use the same fixed-r source before inversion. Near-total short truncation forces growing Mellin shifts and derivative/zeta constants; a fixed-r arbitrary-power error is not uniform there. The Gamma ratio's r^(2rs) is a physical shell shift X^(2kappa), not a free saving. First decisive object: a simultaneous length-simplex completion with explicit r-dependent errors and a global/family-consistent return. No complete first-gain target cheaper than full X^a control is currently established.

**JM and numerator hybrid.** Sixth-power collisions and the relative-conductor mass lemma are useful scoped tools. The source's OPEN-JM6 retains the generic coprime squarefree Q1 about L² front; global order6 alone does not define the hard piece, because Q1=1 mixed quadratic/cubic cases are paid. NJ2 is valid algebra for independently proved count and physical-moment improvements on the SAME amplitude class. Its .003024... margin belongs to old binding parameters and is not a c increment. The promised some c>c0 is not automatically some c>c4. Rebuild the current endpoint dictionary and every complementary branch before admitting any current gain. No 1/6 or 1/4 complete certificate follows from the displayed local JM claim.

## Provenance, verification and limitations

The complete retained source and its five embedded Python audit programs were read as untrusted research evidence. They use bounded elementary finite checks, but their recorded counts/results are source reports; I did NOT execute them merely to reproduce tables. Their first/second-round computations and any absent supplements remain separate from this review's own checks. References [A] and [B] are named and hashed in the merged source, but their original separate byte files/computation supplements were not supplied here; I cannot certify the merge against those originals. The root-retained source-manifest binds the actual merged file.

Essential primary imports independently inspected: DDHLv4, de Faveri–Dunn–Hoffsteinv1, updated Nelson, Mayer's MPI/90-86, Keating–Rudnick, Sawin–Whitehead. The general sextic large-sieve formula in de Faveri–Dunn–Hoffstein (1.9) is expressly a conjectural expectation; their text says it proves no n>=5 result. Other source anchors (FG descent, spherical/tempered induction, trace-function bounds, graph expansion, Remez, MR/MRT, quantum limits, entropy rigidity, topology/Morse, Gamma/Redheffer) remain retained citations with the source's stated scope; this review does not claim to have independently verified them all. None is used here as an available global QRH estimate.

Own bounded_checks.py ran once successfully. It checks 10 local completion cases, 9 exact next Mayer returns, and 108 hook identities; bounded-check-results.json preserves the results and explicitly labels floating target diagnostics. The analytic proofs above, not finite sample counts, justify infinite statements. No Lean, NanoDa, Comparator, con-ron, native endpoint replay, provider-model route, Git or tracker mutation was performed.

Recommended next allocation: first the one-prime coupled quartic boundary computation, simultaneously parameterized by u=Q^(it); second the actual centered-Mayer return on a real function space with an explicit high-height tail budget; third an actual arithmetic good-time mechanism for augmented factorial flux. Keep the hook model and adaptive-gcd criterion available as concrete tools. Do not allocate another endpoint optimization to the already superseded C=4.45 claim.

## G167. Global positive majorants need sufficiently nonlocal interactions

Fix an ordinary character χ modulo fixed q and the literal vector
a_n=μ(n)χ(n),1≤n≤N, including natural zeros. Write ℓ=(1,…,1). A global
terminal certificate is a Hermitian matrix

\[
P\succeq\ell\ell^*,\qquad |M_\chi(N)|^2\le a^*Pa.       \tag{96.1}
\]

P may depend arbitrarily on χ,N and the actual source. The same results
hold after restricting to the nonzero source support, provided original
integer labels still determine matrix offsets. A certificate required
only on a separately proved reachable-state class is a different condition
and is not ruled out.

For a partition into blocks B_j, set b_j=∑_{n∈B_j}a_n. The exact optimum is

\[
\inf_{P\text{ block diagonal},\ P\succeq\ell\ell^*}a^*Pa
   =\left(\sum_j|b_j|\right)^2.                        \tag{96.2}
\]

Rotate one scalar phase on each block to align its sum. This leaves the
block-diagonal energy unchanged, while (96.1), which holds on all inputs,
forces the lower bound. Conversely use block weights
(∑|b_j|)/|b_j| times ℓ_jℓ_j*, with weighted Cauchy. Zero-sum blocks receive
an arbitrarily small reciprocal-weight share and a limit; if all sums
vanish the energy zero is attainable. This is an infimum statement, not a
claim of universal attainment or invertibility.

Suppose I consists of K squarefree q-units isolated from every other
nonzero source coordinate by P's permitted off-diagonal support. Then
P_II is diagonal, all actual I-to-complement cross terms vanish, and
P_II≽ℓ_Iℓ_I* implies ∑_{n∈I}P_nn≥K². Since |a_n|=1 on I and the
complementary principal block is positive semidefinite,

\[
a^*Pa\ge K^2.                                          \tag{96.3}
\]

This is a certificate cost, not |Mχ(N)|≥K. The dense admissible matrix
P=ℓℓ* has exactly the actual energy |Mχ(N)|² and retains distant signed
cross terms.

### Uniform arithmetic supply

For half-bandwidth h≥1, choose distinct primes p_r>h, p_r∤q, for each
0<|r|≤h. Impose

\[
n\equiv1\pmod q,\quad n\equiv-r\pmod{p_r^2},\quad
Q=q\prod_r p_r^2.
\]

The residue a_0 modulo Q is coprime to Q. Every shifted neighbor n+r is
squareful. For any coprime residue modulo any Q, square-divisor expansion
gives the explicit uniform estimate, N≥4,

\[
\#\{n\le N:n\equiv a_0\pmod Q,\ \mu(n)^2=1\}
=\frac NQ\prod_{p\nmid Q}(1-p^{-2})+R,\qquad
|R|\le3\sqrt N.                                       \tag{96.4}
\]

There are at most √N counting errors, each at most1, for d²|n with
(d,Q)=1. The omitted Euler tail contributes at most2√N/Q. The product is
at least1/ζ(2)>1/2. Deleting at most2h endpoint indices produces

\[
K\ge\max(0,N/(2Q)-3\sqrt N-2h).                        \tag{96.5}
\]

No prime theorem in progressions is used. The elementary central-binomial
bounds 4^m/(2m+1)≤binom(2m,m)≤(2m)^{π(2m)} supply π(x)≫x/log x:
each prime contributes at most2m to that factorization. Thus the required
2h primes can lie below C_q h log(2h), and

\[
\log Q\le\log q+4h\log(C_qh\log(2h)).                 \tag{96.6}
\]

For h=o(log N/loglog N), (96.3)–(96.6) force root cost N^{1−o(1)}.
For h=⌊κ log N/loglog N⌋ with fixed0<κ<1/8, they give
sqrt(a*Pa)≥N^{1−4κ−o(1)}. The upper restriction ensures the main term in
(96.5) dominates √N. Fixed h gives K≫_{q,h}N.

More generally let D_N be a symmetric set of permitted nonzero offsets,
all of absolute value at most N−1, and let k=|D_N|. Assign each r a
distinct prime not dividing qr. At any assignment at most
k−1+ω(q)+⌊log₂N⌋ primes are forbidden, so the first
J=k+ω(q)+⌊log₂N⌋+1 primes suffice. Their sizes are O(J log(2J)). The same
CRT construction gives

\[
\log Q\le\log q+2k\log(CJ\log(2J)),\qquad
K\ge\max(0,N/(2Q)-3\sqrt N).                           \tag{96.7}
\]

Neighbors outside the cutoff are irrelevant; no endpoint deletion is
needed. Hence k=o(log N/loglog N) also forces root cost N^{1−o(1)}, and
k∼κ log N/loglog N,0<κ<1/4, gives N^{1−2κ−o(1)}. Offsets may be large,
move with N, or be chosen after seeing the source. Crucially k counts
the **total union of offsets**, including both signs. Bounded row degree
with many distinct offsets is not covered; neither are general prime
dilation graphs merely because their rows are sparse.

For a target root exponent γ, the necessary thresholds are κ≥(1−γ)/4
for half-bandwidth and κ≥(1−γ)/2 for the offset union:

| Target | Half-bandwidth coefficient | Total-offset coefficient |
|---|---:|---:|
| Strict improvement over c11 | >.0312864909 | >.0625729818 |
| c=.1252 | ≥.0313 | ≥.0626 |
| c=1/6 | ≥1/24 | ≥1/12 |
| c=1/4 | ≥1/16 | ≥1/8 |

These are necessary widths, not sufficient savings or claims at an
unresolved equality threshold. q stays fixed.

### The complete nonlocal correction

Let P=D+E≽ℓℓ*, with D≽0 having the preceding support and E Hermitian,
||E||≤η in Euclidean operator norm. The exact same isolated set gives

\[
a^*Pa\ge K^2-\eta(K+N).                                \tag{96.8}
\]

The principal inequality costs ηK; the whole source error costs
η||a||²≤ηN. Positivity of D's complementary block is essential.
For K=N^{1−o(1)}, a fixed root exponent γ<1 therefore requires a
nonlocal correction with norm at least N^{1−o(1)} along this bound.
Small individual entries do not imply a small operator cost. Nonlocal
signed metrics, signed debts and proved source-only inequalities remain
eligible.

## H: a useful failed bilinear replacement

The [late H source](h-original-prime-covariance.md) is accepted in its stated
restricted scope after controller reconstruction of B1--4 and D1--7. Its
two-cutoff von Mangoldt identity is classical. On actual primes only the
unit Type-I term survives; on large semiprimes the signed I/II coefficients
are1 and-1. Their four covariance entries1,-1,-1,1 must remain. An external
common-factor amplifier changes the long length, characters, zeros and
normalization, and leaves the same.004 pressure deficit even under a
generous hypothetical normalization.

In the derived bilinear bound, the mark root stays q_P^(-1/2) after
t=P d. Its squared coefficient mass is D*Omega, not Omega. The cubic
sieve gives N min{S(E,LD),S(D,LE)}*Omega. Sharp product endpoints cost
only logarithms via an integer-exact smooth Fourier cut. The additive
far-mask phase is not separable; its explicit cross ratio differs from1.
Paying the whole near band separately gives the additional(H0+1)L term.
Original n,g,g', independent heights and the physical N^-1 G^-2 stay fixed.

Even the optimal factor split leaves the mixed cubic term(NL)^(2/3).
Its target-relative exponent.6738809116 is much worse than.004. Removing
that mixed term would still leave the separate positive proof cost
G sqrt(NL). These are failures of particular upper-bound methods, not
lower bounds on the true covariance. The next useful H estimate must
retain joint row cancellation or signed unit/nonunit/Type-II interactions;
the all-branch return and other original prime pairs remain unpaid.

The gain over written [private research revision] is `3/1000000`. No formalization was performed;
upstream independence, exact external-target binding and new-endpoint kernel

## 1. Source-range conclusion, established before reading the new author

The fixed-dictionary unmarked density argument extends to

\[
  33/40\le a\le7/8,\qquad 13/20\le\delta=2a-1\le3/4,
  \qquad \rho(\delta)=1-\frac{10\delta}{3(5-2\delta)}.
\]

The actual supported witness requires `51/100<a<=1`; the unmarked count

## 3. D1 — a one-sided subpower finite-volume pressure criterion

Fix an ordinary Dirichlet character chi modulo q. Put delta=1 if chi is principal and0 otherwise. Throughout use chi(p)=0 at every ramified prime, without deleting this convention. For y>=2 and Re(s)>0 define the single holomorphic logarithm

    J_y(s)=integral_2^y u^-s/log(u) du,
    H_y(s)=delta J_y(s)+sum_(p<=y) log(1-chi(p)p^-s),       (1)
    Q_y(s)=exp(H_y(s)),

where each log is its absolutely convergent local power series -sum_(k>=1)chi(p)^k p^(-ks)/k. The finite prime sum is holomorphic and Q_y is nonzero on Re(s)>0. These are actual prime factors, not an unrestricted replacement coefficient sequence. The continuous term is explicit; it does not subtract the unknown prime sum.

On Re(s)>1, Q_y converges absolutely to exp(delta J_infinity(s))/L(s,chi). Define the entire nonvanishing function B by

    B(s)=(s-1)exp(J_infinity(s)) on Re(s)>1,
    B'(s)/B(s)=(1-2^(1-s))/(s-1),                         (2)

with its constant fixed at one real point>1. The quotient on the right is entire after its removable value log2 at1, proving the claimed extension. Equivalently, for z=(s-1)log2,

    B(s)=exp(-gamma_E)/log2 * exp(-sum_(n>=1)(-z)^n/(n n!)).

NIST DLMF6.6.2 confirms the exponential-integral series used in this optional explicit formula: https://dlmf.nist.gov/6.6.E2 . The proof can use(2) alone.

The exact initial identity is

    (s-1)^delta L(s,chi) lim_y Q_y(s)=B(s)^delta.          (3)

For principal chi modulo q, (s-1)L(s,chi) is holomorphic and nonzero at1, with value product_(p|q)(1-1/p). Thus(3) explicitly keeps the original pole; it does not assume it away. For nonprincipal chi delta=0. Imprimitive local factors have their natural zeros on Re(s)=0 and are retained throughout.

### D1.1 One-sided local criterion

**Proposition.** Fix1/2<a<1. Suppose that for every compact K contained in Re(s)>a, every epsilon>0, and all sufficiently large integer k,

    integral_K log^+|Q_(2^k)(s)| dA(s)
           <= C_(chi,K,epsilon) 2^(k epsilon).           (LP_a)

Here dA is ordinary planar area and log^+u=max(0,log u). It suffices to assume this on a countable exhaustion by closed rectangles with interior in the half-plane. Then L(s,chi) has no zero in Re(s)>a. If the same a works for each fixed ordinary chi, this gives a common c=1-a, with character-dependent constants and onset. LP_a is OPEN at every proposed a<theta10.

**Proof, including the missing continuation.** Write h_k=H_(2^k). The positive part of the harmonic function Re(h_k) is subharmonic. The area mean inequality on a disk of fixed radius r gives

    (Re h_k(z))_+ <= (pi r^2)^-1
                    integral_(|w-z|<=r) (Re h_k(w))_+ dA(w).

Thus LP_a gives a local upper bound Re h_k=O_(K,epsilon)(2^(k epsilon)). At a fixed real b>1 the exact series in(1) makes h_k(b) bounded, including its imaginary part. The Borel-Caratheodory disk inequality

    sup_(|z-c|<=R/2)|f(z)|
       <=3|f(c)|+2 sup_(|z-c|<=R) Re f(z)

and a finite overlapping-disk chain from b yield

    sup_K |h_k| <= C_(K,epsilon) 2^(k epsilon)             (4)

for every compact K in the connected half-plane. A harmless absolute constant can be added on the right of the disk inequality when the displayed supremum is negative; alternatively use its maximum with0. All chain geometry is fixed before k grows. This step shows why an uncontrolled imaginary additive constant cannot enter: the actual logarithm is anchored at b.

Let f_k=h_(k+1)-h_k. On every compact subset of Re(s)>1, the omitted prime interval and the continuous integral give

    |f_k(s)| <= C_b 2^(-k(b-1)) when Re(s)>=b>1.          (5)

The integer majorant sum_(n>2^k)n^-b suffices; no prime theorem is used. Meanwhile(4) gives local O(2^(k epsilon)) growth for every epsilon>0. These two facts imply exponential decay of f_k on EVERY fixed compact in Re(s)>a. For completeness: start with a disk in Re(s)>1 where(5) has exponent -d<0. A chain of disks with radii r,2r,4r inside the half-plane propagates decay by Hadamard's three-circle inequality. An inner bound2^(-kd_j) and outer bound2^(k epsilon) give a middle bound2^(-k(d_j-epsilon)/2). For a chain of N disks choose epsilon<d/2^(N+1); then every resulting d_j remains positive. Finite covers handle an arbitrary compact. Constants depend on the compact and do not depend on k.

Hence sum_k f_k converges locally uniformly, and h_k has a holomorphic limit H on Re(s)>a. Q=exp(H) is holomorphic and nonzero. On Re(s)>1 it has the required initial value; the identity theorem extends(3) throughout Re(s)>a. Its right side never vanishes, so a zero of L at any fixed height is impossible, with every multiplicity covered. At1 the principal pole has already been canceled by its explicit factor. This proves the proposition.

**What is weaker and what is not.** LP_a allows any fixed logarithmic power in the positive pressure and even arbitrary subpower growth of the finite cutoff. It asks neither for a uniform O(1) finite-volume bound nor a lower pressure bound. The analytic anchor and rapidly converging dyadic increments force actual local convergence. It is nevertheless a complete all-dyadic-cutoff arithmetic hypothesis, not finite evidence, a density-of-good-volumes hypothesis, or a claim that independence proves cancellation. A finite isolated zero is visible to this return, unlike T24's bulk statistic.

### D1.2 A fixed-power quantitative return

There is also a usable budget without an unspecified analytic-continuation loss. Fix a>0,kappa>=0 with a+kappa<1. Assume, for every epsilon>0, some fixed A>=0 and C exist such that for every dyadic y>=2 and all real t,

    |H_y(a+it)| <= C(1+|t|)^A y^(kappa+epsilon).          (P_a,kappa)

A and C may depend on chi and epsilon but not on y,t. This is a separate, two-sided line hypothesis with global height control; it is NOT inferred from LP_a. It implies zero exclusion in Re(s)>a+kappa.

To prove it, choose b>1 and divide f_k(s) by(s+D)^m with D>1 and integer m>A. On the left strip boundary its modulus is O(y^(kappa+epsilon)); on the right it is O(y^(1-b)) by(5). Finite sums in(1) are uniformly bounded in t for each fixed y on the closed strip, so the usual three-lines proof applies after this polynomial denominator; there is no missing horizontal boundary. It gives, locally in t,

    |f_k(s)| << (1+|t|)^m y^E,
    E=((kappa+epsilon)(b-sigma)+(1-b)(sigma-a))/(b-a).     (6)

The exponent is negative when

    sigma > r_b(kappa+epsilon),
    r_b(kappa)=(b kappa+(b-1)a)/(kappa+b-1).

For kappa>0 and a+kappa<1,

    r_b(kappa)=a+kappa+
              kappa(1-a-kappa)/(kappa+b-1) -> a+kappa.   (7)

For any compact with sigma>a+kappa, first fix a sufficiently large finite b and then a sufficiently small epsilon. The dyadic increments sum geometrically; the proof of(3) completes the return. The boundary line is excluded only strictly, as required. The case kappa=0 uses any b>1 and a positive epsilon buffer before its limit.

| Conditional target | a | kappa | Resulting c=1-a-kappa |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| a concrete first gain |3/4|78/625=.1248|313/2500=.1252|
| high-headroom target |3/4|1/12|1/6|
| high-headroom target |2/3|1/12|1/4|

The first row would improve c10 by1351/25000000=.00005404. It requires kappa<theta10-3/4=3121351/25000000=.12485404. This is a conditional target, not an obtained exponent.

**Deliberately coarse actual bound.** Directly from(1), for0<a<1,

    |H_y(a+it)| <= C_a sum_(n<=y)n^-a
                  + integral_2^y u^-a/log2 du
                <= C'_a y^(1-a),                       (8)

uniformly in t. It gives a+kappa=1 and therefore NO improvement. Grouping only the already summable higher-prime-power terms at a>1/2 does not improve(8)'s singleton exponent. The arithmetic saving is precisely what remains open.

**Sharpness of the abstract budget.** For gamma=a+kappa<1 and kappa>0, take the synthetic holomorphic logs

    h_k^*(s)=sum_(j=1)^k 2^(j(gamma-s))/j.

They satisfy the left power budget and the right dyadic-tail budget used above. On Re(s)>gamma their exponentials tend to1/(1-2^(gamma-s)), which has a pole at gamma. Thus these analytic hypotheses alone cannot improve the strict boundary a+kappa. This is not an arithmetic counterexample: the logs are not prime sums. It checks that the return has no hidden unearned saving.
