# Independent R4 review: original-color cubic sieve after primitive Poisson



**Review conclusion:** the proposed restricted bound survives this independent review, relative to the explicitly retained PR9 finite identities, common-profile conventions and G181 source. I found no missing cross-copy gcd condition, extra conductor gcd factor, or lost power in the two-root normalization. The cubic large sieve is used on legitimate separated original colors. This is evidence for controller review, not automatic acceptance or an endpoint theorem.

The author proves a useful actual-source low-first-dual payment. The complete high-dual core and nonunique terms remain open and signed. Current c11=.1251459636, analytic ancestry, positive-slot uniformity and external admission are unchanged. The reviewer additionally makes the nearby-band and decaying far-tail consequences explicit; these are consequences of this source estimate and the existing Schwartz rule, not separate claims of arithmetic novelty.

## 1. Frozen inputs and the exact scope reviewed

Before substantive analysis, source-pins.json froze 19 local inputs at 22:48:10 UTC, SHA256 a0daefcaaea6ef0c85fdde3d6a1e68216f552c7c73c494f9e7233709fbd4c86c. At that point the only difference from the author's initial pins was the disclosed controller-owned reservation update. At final recheck, the controller had also appended [private research revision] context to attempt-index/current-proof. The exact diff concerns a distinct ordinary Liouville large-gcd source and explicitly denies a transfer to this Hecke R4 source; no reviewed mathematical input changed. The original pins remain immutable, and source-recheck.json records the two contextual changes. The author sentinel was independently absent before this reviewer acquired a fresh claim. No old W63 file or canonical file was edited by this reviewer.

Principal inputs read were the complete author report and helper/receipt; G179-G181; the actual G156-G157 relative-conductor source; PR9 B1.1-B1.11, B2.11-B2.15, B2.24-B2.25, B2.35-B2.40, B3.1-B3.8 and B3.31-B3.39; relevant current index entries; and the exact early [restricted research revision]-MG and [restricted research revision]-HG sources. Supplemental pins retain the last two files. The unconditional HB contract was independently checked against its primary paper.

Write q_z=N(z), D1=U^r, D2=U^s, P0=U^v and N0=D1 D2 P0. The original inverse profiles W1,W2 retain one common real parameter and two independent heights t1,t2. Q retains its ordered disjoint slot pools, original bounded coefficients, all heights, product profile, and possible intersections with the inverses. The entire right copy is conjugated. For one complete orientation e in {1,-1}, use

    phi_u(n)=nu(n) chi_n(u)^e,
    F_u=M_u(D1;W1) M_u(D2;W2) Q_u.

All characters remain zero on nonunits, even for powers zero or six. Rows are the original nonzero sixth-power-free free-row enclosure with its fixed smooth ball weight. This is not permission to insert an arbitrary physical row projector. Original divisor row weights have already been dominated before the signed expansion, exactly as G179 specifies.

R_unique is the actual ordered-pair part of R4 for which both merged columns n,n' are squarefree and (n,n')=1. In this subclass all within-copy and cross-copy inverse gcds equal one. Its slots are also disjoint from every other prime in the same merged column. For sufficiently large U, q_n,q_n' are within fixed original annular factors of N0, so Q1=q_n q_n', Q2=Q3=1, and G181's high-conductor and ratio cuts hold automatically. The equality n=n' is impossible on this coprime subclass once the large inverse windows exclude the unit column. No additional pair mask is being relaxed here.

The source coefficient is exactly

    F_sf,u=(-1)^j N0^(-1/2) sum_(n sf) mu(n)nu(n)chi_n(u)^e A(n),
    A(n)=sum_(original P|n) b_tilde(P)
             sum_(d1 d2=n/P) W1(q_d1/D1;t1) W2(q_d2/D2;t2),
    b_tilde(P)=b(P) conjugate(nu(P)).                    (R1)

Here P retains its ordered slot labels. Since nu(P) is a unit on these S-good columns, its conjugate is legitimate; no natural row zero is divided out. The sign identity is mu(d1)mu(d2)=(-1)^j mu(n), not independent randomness in the two inverse signs. R_nonunique=R4-R_unique is the complete signed complement.

## 2. Primitive Poisson and both orientations

For each actual pair define psi(u)=chi_n(u)^e conjugate(chi_n'(u)^e). At every good prime of nn', its local exponent is 1 or 5. Thus psi is primitive and nonprincipal on its full good conductor nn'. In particular it is not principalized by the fact that some individual inducing row may have a principal character.

The finite identity

    1_(u sixth-power-free)=sum_(a^6|u) mu(a)

is used on the original nonzero row support. Setting u=a^6 z leaves the exact natural mask (a,nn')=1 and row scale U_a=U/q_a^6. The original ball gives q_a<<U^(1/6). Extending z to include zero in Poisson is harmless because psi(0)=0. It does not delete any original nonzero row.

For a primitive character and the prescribed additive pairing, the finite Fourier transform is

    sum_(x mod nn') psi(x)e(ell x/(nn'))
       =sqrt(q_n q_n') gamma(psi;nn') conjugate(psi(ell)). (R2)

It is zero when ell shares any good conductor prime, including ell=0. This is a zero, not a square-root gcd loss. In particular a fixed original slot prime dividing ell kills the term.

The CRT factor is worth computing rather than inferring from a norm. With x=n' y+n y', it is

    chi_n(n')^e chi_n'(n)^(-e)=R(n,n'),                 (R3)

where R is the fixed ray sign of B1.1-B1.5. Sextic reciprocity makes the ratio a sign, and e=1 or -1 gives the same sign. There is no additional variable cubic phase between the two copies.

Put a0(n)=conjugate(alpha(n)) gamma_2(n). B1.10 gives

    mu(n)gamma_1(n)=conjugate(a0(n))G(n),
    mu(n)gamma_-1(n)=a0(n)chi_n(-1)conjugate(G(n)).     (R4)

Consequently, before the finite ray expansion, the exact arithmetic factor from the two mu signs, Gauss sum and dual character is

    e=-1:
      R(n,n') chi_n(-1) conjugate(G(n))G(n')
        *a0(n)conjugate(a0(n'))chi_n(ell)conjugate(chi_n'(ell));
    e=+1:
      R(n,n') G(n)conjugate(G(n'))chi_n'(-1)
        *conjugate(a0(n))a0(n')conjugate(chi_n(ell))chi_n'(ell). (R5)

The source factor nu(n)conjugate(nu(n')) is still present. G, chi_n(-1) and R are fixed ray data, so their finite expansion produces a finite sum of separated column factors. It does not exchange W1 with W2 or either of their height coordinates.

Fixed ray/unit row restrictions do not spoil (R2). One can see this directly by combining the good conductor c=nn' with a coprime fixed S-supported modulus m0. CRT factors the finite transform of psi times any fixed m0-periodic row function into the primitive good transform and a bounded fixed-modulus transform. The good factor is still zero at a frequency divisible by a good prime. Factors involving c modulo m0, and psi(m0), belong to a finite dictionary and separate between n and n'. After u=a^6 z the periodic row function may also depend on a's fixed residue class; retain that class or its bounded coefficient. This has a fixed cost, not a power of q_a. Clearing the fixed dual denominator must rescale the cutoff with its fixed comparison constant. The author defines the cutoff on the actual fixed dual lattice, which avoids an equality claim between two differently normalized cutoffs.

The original pair coefficient contributes N0^(-1); primitive Poisson contributes U_a/sqrt(q_n q_n'). Their product is

    U_a/N0^2 * [N0/sqrt(q_n q_n')].                    (R6)

The bracket is part of the smooth profile on the original compact normalized source supports. The radial kernel keeps its exact argument U_a q_ell/(q_n q_n'), with the prescribed fixed factors. It is not replaced by a hard support condition.

Define R_unique,<=Y by the literal condition 0<q_ell<=Y in this exact expansion, where Y is fixed before live a,ell,n,n', slots or height suprema. The complementary dual sum is retained in full. Pair transposition and complete conjugation preserve this radial frequency condition; hence the scalar pieces can be made real without positivity. This is not signed-subset norm monotonicity.

## 3. Why the common-divisor expansion really separates the copies

After (R5), extend its displayed product expression, profile and formal product conductor to all individually squarefree n,n' in their original tuple supports. This is only an algebraic extension. No imprimitive Poisson identity is asserted on the added noncoprime pairs. Then insert

    1_((n,n')=1)=sum_(f|n, f|n') mu(f).                (R7)

For a pair with nontrivial common divisor the FULL sum is zero. Thus it removes every forbidden cross-copy coincidence, including inverse-inverse, inverse-slot and slot-slot coincidences. It is stronger than merely reinstating the four inverse gcd cuts. No cross-copy coprimality may be separately dropped in an individual summand; all of it has already been represented by (R7).

Write n=fm,n'=fm'. Individual squarefreeness forces (f,m)=(f,m')=1. The exact extraction law is

    a0(fm)=a0(f)a0(m)chi_m(f)^4.                       (R8)

Both columns have the SAME f but not necessarily the same assignment of its primes. Their frequency factors give

    chi_f(ell)conjugate(chi_f(ell))=1_((f,ell)=1),      (R9)

and no division by chi_f occurs. Residual f-punctures and the a-puncture remain in each column. Every common-prime label carries its original sign mu(f).

For each column, allocate each prime of f to its actual inverse color or actual original slot. Because that column is squarefree the assignment is unique for a specified original tuple. Summing over possible assignments is a reindexing with at most (j+2)^omega(f) choices on each side; their PRODUCT is bounded by tau(f)^C for fixed j. An assigned slot prime keeps its coefficient and its pool membership; an unassigned slot retains its original pool.

The precise two independent maps are

| Copy | Original inverse 1 | Original inverse 2 | Assigned slots | Residual product scale |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| left | d1=f1 x, length D1/q_f1 | d2=f2 y, length D2/q_f2 | fP | X_f=N0/q_f |
| right | d1'=g1 x', length D1/q_g1 | d2'=g2 y', length D2/q_g2 | gP | X_f=N0/q_f |

Here f=f1 f2 fP=g1 g2 gP, with pairwise coprime factors within each allocation. The first HB application uses only x,y. The second uses only x',y'. None of xx',xy',yx',yy' is an HB variable. Nonempty nominal subunit windows are clipped by bounded original annular factors; genuinely empty windows remain empty.

For fixed surviving slot tuple P, the remaining column m=x y P has

    a0(xyP)=a0(x)a0(y)a0(P)chi_y(x)^4 chi_x(P)^4 chi_y(P)^4. (R10)

The last two factors carry the P-punctures and separate. The x,y coprimality is supplied by the zero of chi_y(x)^4, even though the exponent is not one. All f,a,ell punctures and finite ray factors separate once those labels and P are fixed. This is the essential structured coefficient fact. It authorizes a separated bilinear coefficient alpha_x beta_y, not an arbitrary joint matrix.

## 4. Common profile before labels; actual HB and slot payment

The coupled profile is separated on the ambient box of the ORIGINAL inverse and individual slot normalized norms on both sides, together with q_a/A and q_ell/H on fixed dyads. Its kernel is

    K(C*y_ell/[y_a^6 product(y_original_columns)]),
    C=UH/(A^6 N0^2).                                  (R11)

PR9 B3.3 fixes the Fourier measure on that entire box before choosing a,f,ell or a slot tuple. C depends only on nominal scales. Euler derivatives are uniformly bounded in C>0 by Schwartz seminorms. Only afterward substitute d1=f1 x and the other extracted forms. Their extracted imaginary powers have modulus one. The original real inverse roots enter the profile once. Sharp arithmetic masks and the first-dual cutoff stay outside the smooth separation.

The two original heights stay on their own inverse profiles. Products of their fixed polynomial seminorm bounds can be absorbed in a larger H_J. This is finite-order bookkeeping under the existing source contract; it does not close the independently open positive-slot uniformity ancestry.

The primary unconditional cubic-sieve statement is [Dunn-Radziwill, Theorem 9.1 and (1.11)](https://arxiv.org/html/2109.07463v3): both the outer and inner variables are squarefree primary Eisenstein elements, and the inner coefficient is an arbitrary sequence independent of the outer variable. Its bound has size D+E+(DE)^(2/3), times (DE)^epsilon and the inner squared coefficient mass. The upper bound is unconditional. The paper's GRH-dependent optimality lower bounds are not used. Cubic reciprocity and conjugation give the orientation chi_y(x)^4. No squarefree restriction on the separate first-dual frequency ell is needed here, because ell is a fixed coefficient parameter in each HB application.

Set S(D,E)=D+E+(DE)^(2/3). For bounded separated coefficients, Cauchy in x and HB give

    |(DE)^(-1/2) sum_(x,y sf) alpha_x beta_y chi_y(x)^4|^2
       <= H_J (DE)^epsilon S(D,E).                    (R12)

Indeed the two coefficient squared masses cost O(D), O(E); central normalization cancels their product. Fixed punctures are zero coefficients or restrictions of the positive outer sum. Their conductor sizes do not enter the HB constant. This is why an arbitrary large ell causes no hidden gcd or conductor loss.

On a given allocation put D1'=D1/q_f1, D2'=D2/q_f2, P'=P0/q_fP. The normalized complete residual column is

    B_f(ell)=(P')^(-1/2) sum_(original surviving P) b_P
                   [normalized two-inverse bilinear sum at D1',D2']. (R13)

Each bracket satisfies (R12). Ideal counting and the retained bounded slot coefficients give sum_P |b_P|<<H_J(P')^(1+epsilon). Thus pointwise triangle, followed by squaring, yields

    |B_f(ell)|^2 << H_J U^epsilon P' S(D1',D2')
                  << H_J U^epsilon P0 S(D1,D2).        (R14)

Assigned slot coefficients are already outside with modulus at most their original fixed profile bound. The discrepancy between P' and the product of the surviving nominal slot lengths is bounded by the original annular constants; it is kept in the profile. Natural holes at ell, f and a remain contractions throughout. The conjugate-side estimate has its own shortened lengths and follows separately. Its product with the left side is bounded by their geometric mean, without identifying their profiles.

This is an admissible HB argument after actual tuple conditioning. The forbidden B3.6 canonical merged-coefficient estimate is not needed at any step of (R12)-(R14).

## 5. The two-root calculation and complete label costs

Let T_left and T_right be the unnormalized residual column sums. By definition each is X_f^(1/2) times its centrally normalized B_f, where X_f=N0/q_f on BOTH allocations. Restoring both normalizations in (R6) gives the exact scalar factor

    [U/(q_a^6 N0^2)] sqrt(X_f X_f)
       =U/(q_a^6 N0 q_f).                             (R15)

The real bracket N0/sqrt(q_n q_n') is still in the profile; after extraction it is X_f/sqrt(q_m q_m'), bounded on the residual evaluation points. It supplies no extra power of q_f. The normalization neither loses q_f^(-1) nor produces q_f^(-2).

Every allocation on each side has been counted before the following absolute sums:

    sum_(q_a<<U^(1/6)) q_a^(-6) << 1,
    sum_(q_f<<N0) tau(f)^C/q_f <<_epsilon U^epsilon,
    #{ell:0<q_ell<=Y} << Y.                            (R16)

The second sum is harmonic, not absolutely convergent uniformly in its cap. Use tau(f)^C<<_eta q_f^eta and O(X) ideal counting, then choose eta after the fixed polynomial scale cap. Both independent allocation counts are inside C. The field, fixed S, finite dictionaries, endpoint constants and original profile orders have their stated fixed costs. No average over physical row families is introduced.

Equations (R14)-(R16), with the full common Fourier integral restored, prove

    |R_unique,<=Y| << H_J U^(1+epsilon) Y/(D1 D2)
                           S(D1,D2),                 (R17)

for any fixed polynomial cap on Y. The P0 in (R14) cancels the original P0 in N0. Slots have been paid by triangle, not erased. This proof bounds a complete signed scalar sector after exact identities; it does not bound the sum of absolute values of its original pair terms.

On the actual parameter box, s<2r and r<2s, so S(D1,D2)<<U^(2(r+s)/3). Taking Y=U^(3/2) gives exponent 5/2-(r+s)/3. The independent rational check reproduces

    T-[5/2-(r+s)/3] >= 857/16875 > 1/20,               (R18)

using the coarse accepted T>=123353/67500 and r+s>217/100. Auxiliary geometric, arithmetic and Fourier losses can be chosen inside that fixed slack, as the author states.

## 6. Reviewer consequence: a nearby band and the actual decaying tail

The following are consequences of (R17) and the existing source tail rule, not a new full R4 estimate or an independent mathematical cycle.

First, let Y=U^kappa. Using E_K>=rho, the raw margin is at least

    (delta+1/3)(r+s)+rho-1-kappa.

Its derivative in delta is at least 217/100-625/486=21481/24300>0 on the physical box. Thus its lower endpoint is at delta=17/25 and r+s=217/100, giving

    kappa_* =268943/170625,
    margin >= kappa_*-kappa.                           (R19)

For example kappa=39/25=1.56 pays not just the author's cutoff but its adjacent band, with raw margin 2768/170625>.0162. A margin 1/100 remains after sufficiently small combined losses. This merely spends some of the already proved room; it supplies no new cancellation input.

Second, PR9's rule following B3.4 requires discarding tails on the genuine arithmetic expression before extending a coprime sum or taking an absolute Fourier integral. A direct raw estimate suffices. Fix a bounded-overlap dyadic partition q_a~A before live labels, and write L_A=A^6N0^2/U. Each copy has at most O(H_J N0 U^epsilon) original inverse/slot tuples by ideal counting. The two central roots and the primitive Poisson factor together are O(U/(q_a^6 N0^2)) on their original supports. Primitive Gauss factors have modulus one; masks can only reduce this absolute bound. Thus the genuine coprime sector, for q_ell~H, satisfies

    |R_(A,H)| <= sum |genuine source terms in that dyad|
       << H_J U^(1+epsilon) A^(-5) H
                    [1+H/L_A]^(-B).                  (R20)

This uses O(A) possible a and O(H) frequencies. It keeps the full kernel, every original mask and both heights; no mutual-gcd extension or common Fourier separation is used in this tail bound. All derivative orders and raw-factor powers are fixed before choosing B.

For fixed tau>0, summing the dyadic frequencies H>U^tau L_A in (R20) costs at most

    H_J U^epsilon A N0^2 U^(-tau(B-1)).               (R21)

Here L_A>>1 throughout the actual box, so no small-radius lattice term is missing. Summing A<<U^(1/6), and using r+s<47/20 and v<=1/20, bounds all these tails by

    H_J U^(149/30+epsilon-tau(B-1)).                   (R22)

The exponent 149/30 is a deliberately coarse raw-factor budget:
1/6+2(r+s)+2v<=149/30. For any desired M, a finite B>1+(149/30+M+1)/tau makes (R22) O(H_J U^(-M)), taking epsilon<1. Fixed support factors are absorbed in the tail threshold or a small geometric pad. This is the existing B3.4 tail principle applied to this literal source, not a new arithmetic estimate. Only after this tail is paid do we use the algebraic extension and common-profile separation on the retained finite region.

Consequently the full high term may be replaced, up to this proved rapidly decaying tail, by the exact middle region

    U^(39/25)<q_ell<=U^tau A^6 N0^2/U                 (R23)

inside each original a-dyad. The upper threshold depends only on its nominal dyad and original scales. This keeps the prior common-profile separation valid. The lowest natural dual scale has exponent 2(r+s+v)-1>3.34, so (R23) remains a very large unpaid region. For the largest a-dyads its cap can approach U^(4.8+tau). Nothing in (R20)-(R22) bounds that central high-frequency mass.

The exact complementary statement is therefore R4=R_nonunique+R_middle+R_low+R_far, with R_low paid by (R19), R_far paid by (R22), and the SUM R_nonunique+R_middle still open. These pieces can have either sign. This refinement closes only the decaying infinite tail and states precisely which finite middle remains.

## 7. Supporting identities, failed shortcut, and novelty

The two-color Mellin mark eta_(z,w)(n)=product_(p|n)(q_p^(-z)+q_p^(-w)) is the correct ordered-divisor weight on squarefree n. Two variables are needed. Coprime extraction preserves it multiplicatively. A forced-slot division is legitimate on separated real contours Re z=kappa, Re w=-kappa, since the two summands then have unequal magnitudes; on coincident real contours that division may fail. The author's divisor/small-power price is sufficient at fixed depth.

The algebraic cube-inversion identity remains valid with an arbitrary whole-index mark: for fixed n c^3, the mark is independent of h|c, so sum_(h|c)mu(h) kills c!=1. This does not license the terminal reflected-energy input. Extending eta to whole prime powers gives a unitary two-color decomposition of the completed index, whose coupling is

    chi_(A2)(A1)^4=chi_(n2)(n1)^4,
    A_i=n_i b_i^3, (A1,A2)=1.                          (R24)

The cross cubic phase survives; e.g. the author's norm7/norm13 primary primes give omega. It is not a product of two independent theta sums. PR9's terminal RE reflects the specified theta coefficient source and its permitted product-prime marks, not this arbitrary eta-weighted convolution. The missing structured terminal theorem is properly labelled open. Even the unchanged hypothetical one-inverse exponent at length r+s misses the current target by at least 1867/27000. That is a failure of the proposed estimate's price, not a lower bound on actual R4.

The bivariate Euler identity product_p(1-X_p-Y_p)=(L_u(s1)L_u(s2))^(-1) product_p[1-X_pY_p/((1-X_p)(1-Y_p))] is also exact on the absolute lines. Its correction converges absolutely when both real parts stay positive and their sum stays above one. It neither supplies the joint fourth moment nor permits crossing a zero. These supporting identities are useful retained failures, not assumptions used to smuggle in (R17).

G155-G157 already isolated the original two-inverse source, relative conductor and signed residual. G179-G181 already paid the four-cross-gcd union and its intersections. [restricted research revision]-MG uses a different rational completed Mertens source and cannot be transferred just because it has four gcds. The exact early [restricted research revision]-HG theorem concerns a quadratic relative-core source with specific squarefree low duals, true-core selectors and separated B2.29 coefficients. It is a genuine antecedent for the strategy, but it does not directly imply (R17). Here the Poisson character has good exponents 1 and 5; the two HB variables are original inverse colors, and ell need not be squarefree. The useful new record is the complete source-specific application and its normalization/slot accounting. No literature priority is claimed.

## 8. Evidence, complete return, and next action

The author's helper and receipt were read rather than blindly treated as theorem evidence. Their 551616 extraction checks use a phase gauge satisfying the known cocycle; they do not independently verify actual finite Gauss orientations. This review added that independent decisive check with the literal additive character e(z)=exp(2 pi i Tr(z/lambda)), primary primes of norms7,13,19,31, and their composite conductors.

check_review.py/check-receipt.json record eight actual Gauss columns, 24 complete relative orientations, 216 primitive dual-frequency checks (including nonunits and zero), 32 arbitrary fixed-ray-selector zero checks, and 10000 exact independent allocation pairs. The largest complex residual was 2.334110243043934e-15. The allocation and rational-price calculations are exact; floating Gauss checks are diagnostics. The proofs above use CRT, primitive character orthogonality, the cited finite identities and the actual unconditional HB theorem. No finite experiment proves an infinite moment bound or an endpoint.

Combining (R17) with G181 yields the author's complete equality

    ||F_<||_U^2=R_nonunique+R_unique,high
                     +O(H_J U^(T-1/200+epsilon)).     (R25)

The reviewer refinement can replace R_unique,high by R_middle from (R23), with the paid far tail retained in the error. A one-sided upper bound for the SUM of the two surviving signed terms is still needed. If it had fixed margin xi>0, G181 would give free OPEN-MIX with every strict margin below min(xi,1/200), and the actual two inverse signals and counted prefix would leave a counting margin below min(xi,1/200,1/2000). No possibly zero slot is divided out.

This would still not finish the physical zero-exclusion return. Both signed physical projectors, family reconstruction, root/slot holes, exceptional and inducing rows,6a/9a radii,K_phys,5/6 amplification, clipped rectangles, shortenings, Euler shifts, principal branches, actual suprema, the common mesh and all genuine detector tails retain their licensed obligations. Buffered internal witnesses can exceed delta=.70; their signal extraction cannot be replaced by the weaker physical-bin inequality. The centered reserve is unspent. No xi-to-c map, near endpoint,1/6 or1/4 result is established.

The next meaningful arithmetic target is the actual middle first-dual region (R23), preserving both colors, the full Schwartz kernel, the independently allocated mutual label and the nonunique companion term. An argument that first merges the colors and then applies the canonical B3.6 permission, discards a natural dual zero, or silently replaces the signed remainder by a positive norm would reopen a gap already excluded here. A structured terminal theorem could help, but its quantitative strength must also beat the failed merged price.

## 6. Independent uniform audit F06: a raw principal half-plane obstruction

The seed proposes finite Dirichlet-polynomial Bezout approximants with a globally uniform contracting remainder. Preserve that precise formulation. Let chi be principal, 0<gamma<1, and P(s)=sum_(n<=D)c_n n^-s any finite Dirichlet polynomial. Suppose R=1-L(s,chi)P(s) is holomorphic and bounded on the WHOLE half-plane Re s>gamma. Its pole at1 forces P(1)=0. P identically0 already has ||R||=1; otherwise this zero is isolated.

There are unbounded translations T_k for which exp(-iT_k log n)->1 simultaneously for the finitely many frequencies in P. This follows by recurrence in a finite torus, or the elementary simultaneous pigeonhole approximation: a periodic orbit gives unbounded exact returns, and an infinite orbit gives arbitrarily close unbounded returns. Therefore P(s+iT_k)->P(s) uniformly on compact sets. Choose a disk centered at1 of radius less than1-gamma whose boundary has no P-zero. Rouche's theorem supplies a zero of P(s+iT_k) in that disk for large k. Translated back, these are zeros of P with real part>gamma and unbounded heights, away from the unique L-pole at1. At each such point R=1. Thus

    sup_(Re s>gamma)|1-L(s,chi)P(s)|>=1,              (R21)

or that supremum is infinite if the pole was not removed. No finite member can attain global strict contraction, and no sequence of such finite members can have global uniform remainders tending to0. For example P=1-2^(1-s) has the explicit zeros 1+2pi i k/log2; no numerical zeta evaluation is needed.

The principal member alone defeats this raw full-half-plane formulation of an all-character family criterion. It does not rule out a criterion only on an open strip gamma<Re s<1, one vertical line, compact-by-compact convergence, infinite filters, or the normalized source(R1). In particular W37 D03 already used an open strip with the pole outside it; applying(R21) to that earlier claim would be wrong. Zeros of changing finite polynomials may escape to higher heights, so locally uniform convergence remains logically possible. A locally uniform full residual tending to0 would still exclude any L-zero in its domain by evaluation there, but no arithmetic estimate or quantitative Mertens bound has been proved. This is a source-specific almost-periodicity/Rouche obstruction, not a universal Bezout failure.

statement:
## Complex-height and multiplicative-source requirements

At a fixed complex s, the pointwise matrix M(F(s)+G(s)j) has positive
determinant |F(s)|^2+|G(s)|^2. Its conjugate entries are generally
antiholomorphic. More precisely, a holomorphic matrix-valued function
whose values remain in this quaternionic real subalgebra on a connected
complex open set is constant: its entries include F, G, conj(F), conj(G),
so both functions and their conjugates are holomorphic and their complex
derivatives vanish. This is compatible with using the matrix pointwise in
energy integrals, but it prevents silently using its positive norm as a
nonconstant holomorphic determinant in a Mellin or zero-exclusion argument.

On a reflection-invariant domain define F#(s)=conj(F(conj(s))) and similarly
G#. The genuinely holomorphic lift

    H(s)=[[F(s),G(s)],[-G#(s),F#(s)]]

has determinant F(s)F#(s)+G(s)G#(s). It agrees with the positive norm on
the real axis, not generally at complex heights. For example F(s)=s,
G(s)=1 gives determinant s^2+1, which vanishes at s=+/-i although the
pointwise quaternion norm is |s|^2+1>0. Also, pointwise positivity of the
pair would only exclude simultaneous zeros of F and G; recovering
nonvanishing of F requires an additional implication.

Finally a genuine homomorphism Q(mn)=Q(m)Q(n) from positive integers
under multiplication has commuting images, since mn=nm. Commuting
quaternions lie in one complex slice unless all are real: fix a nonreal
image a+u; the imaginary part v of every commuting quaternion satisfies
u cross v=0, so it belongs to R+R u. Thus this particular way of importing
noncommutativity collapses to a complex-valued source. The same restriction
applies to the prime images of an ordinary coprime-multiplicative source.
An ordered prime product or a noncommutative indexing object is a different
source and needs its own exact scalar return. No assertion is made that
every possible quaternionic construction has this obstruction.
title: Complex-height and multiplicative-source requirements

### 3.1 A direct periodic hyperbola estimate

If b is any fixed bounded periodic sequence with mean zero, then for every fixed
integer t>=1,

    sum_(n<=x)b^(*t)(n) <<_(b,t) x^(1-1/t), x>=1.            (12)

For t=1 this is bounded partial sums. For t>1 set Y=x^(1/t). Every tuple with
product<=x has at least one coordinate<=Y. Inclusion-exclusion on those t events
gives a sum over j=1,...,t chosen short coordinates. For j<t, apply the induction
hypothesis to the remaining t-j coordinates, with beta=1-1/(t-j). Taking absolute
values ONLY on the chosen short coordinates costs at most

    C x^beta [sum_(n<=Y)|b(n)|n^(-beta)]^j
      << x^beta Y^(j(1-beta))=x^(1-1/t).

For j=t the product constraint is automatic since every coordinate<=Y. That term
is exactly(sum_(n<=Y)b(n))^t=O(1), not Y^t. Every overlap is retained with its
inclusion-exclusion sign. This proves(12), with real endpoints and fixed t constants.
No unproved divisor-problem exponent or growing-t uniformity is imported.

statement:
## 3. A fixed quadratic class changes the actual row index

PS15 gives the actual dual core character

\[
\psi_n(c)=\nu(c)\overline{\chi_c(n^2)}.
\]

Since sextic characters are zero-extended, the following identity is
valid also at every nonunit:

\[
\boxed{
 n=d a^2\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \overline{\chi_c(n^2)}
   =\chi_c(n)\rho_d(c),\qquad
 \rho_d(c)=\chi_c(d)^3.}
\tag{SR6}
\]

On units, `bar chi(n^2)=chi(n)^4=chi(n)chi(n)^3`, and
`chi(d a^2)^3=chi(d)^3 chi(a)^6`. The extra sixth-power factor is
`1_(c,a)=1`, already enforced by `chi_c(n)`. If a prime divides both
c and n, both sides vanish. This proves the assertion without an
unjustified deletion of natural zeros or an assumption `(d,a)=1`.

For fixed d, cubic/sextic reciprocity and the fixed ray separation make
`rho_d` a fixed finite-order quadratic Hecke character with its full
zero-extended presentation. Primes dividing fixed d may be added to
the fixed datum because the original row character already vanishes
there. This does not apply to a d that grows with the scales.

Therefore, on this class, the centrally normalized original cubic
Möbius polynomial is **exactly** the sextic polynomial with fixed
twist `nu rho_d` and row `u=n`. Its row norm is H, not H squared.
This is a different identity from retaining the original fixed twist
and writing `u=n^2`, which has norm H squared as in PS15--PS18.

For fixed d, SR5 consequently yields

\[
\boxed{
 \sum_{\substack{n\ne0\\n\in[d]_2}}
 \Omega(q_n/H)
 \left|X^{-1/2}\sum_{(c,R)=1}
    \mu(c)\psi_n(c)F(q_c/X)\right|^2
 \ll_{d,\nu,\epsilon} H(HXq_R)^\epsilon\mathcal S(F)^2.}
\tag{SR7}
\]

Positive enlargement now runs over all sextic rows **of norm H**
with the single fixed twist `nu rho_d`. Rows sharing primes with d,
a, R, or the core retain their original zeros. A finite collection
of classes and all six unit choices cost only a fixed constant.
title: 3. A fixed quadratic class changes the actual row index

## 3. Actual arithmetic grouping, zeros and SF7 mass

In the actual source of [private research revision] D1, define

    A_J(t) = sum_(P d=t; q_d in J)
       u(P)/sqrt(q_P) c(d)a(d) chi_R(d)^3 chi_P(d)^4
       1_(P,Rg)=1 1_(d,g bar(g))=1,

with every original P,d support and separated finite/profile factor.
The remaining e coefficient is exactly

    B(e)=b(e)a(e)chi_R(e)^3 1_(e,g bar(g))=1.

The native cocycle `a(de)=a(d)a(e)chi_d(e)^4` is used on coprime d,e.
Its zero extension at noncoprimality is retained in the displayed
character. The factor `chi_P(d)^4` vanishes when (P,d)>1; hence every
nonzero t=Pd is a squarefree IDEAL. The e-dependent cubic factors are

    chi_P(e)^4 chi_d(e)^4 = chi_t(e)^4.

Their zeros at (e,t)>1 supply both original collisions (e,P)>1 and
(e,d)>1. The original row factor on e remains in B, including its zero.
The projector `(P,Rg)=1` is literal in A_J. No residual projector is
silently added or removed, and no inverse character is taken at zero.
These observations establish

    X_J(e)=sum_t A_J(t)chi_t(e)^4.                    (R2)

The A_J are independent of live e. The outer e family and inner t family
meet M B2.25's good primary squarefree-ideal domain, after the fixed
finite ray resolution already allowed in [private research revision] D2. Exponent 4 is the
conjugate cubic character; the source explicitly admits conjugation and
the opposite orientation. Original upper dyads are contained in balls
of lengths O(E), O(LD). Their fixed constants do not change the exponent.
There is no requirement that their INTEGER norms be squarefree, and no
new exclusion of inert or rational prime factors. Fixed e restrictions
can be bounded by a containing positive outer sum.

Consequently, for every tree node J,

    sum_e |X_J(e)|^2
      << Z^epsilon S(E,LD) sum_t |A_J(t)|^2.          (R3)

For SF7, apply divisor Cauchy only after grouping the actual t:

    |A_J(t)|^2
      <= tau(t) sum_(P d=t; q_d in J)
          |u(P)|^2/q_P |c(d)|^2,

where modulus-one native factors and zero masks have now legitimately
been bounded by one. The normalized profile envelopes are included in
c or in the eventual profile mass. Since t has polynomially bounded
norm, its divisor count costs an allocated `Z^epsilon`. Summing t,J
and counting each d once at each of the ell_D levels gives

    sum_J sum_t |A_J(t)|^2
      << Z^epsilon ell_D
         (sum_P |u(P)|^2/q_P)(sum_(d original) |c(d)|^2)
      << Z^epsilon ell_D D Omega.                    (R4)

The last mass bound is exactly the source-only divisor-bounded
coefficient allowance already used in [private research revision] D4. It applies to the
actual Type-I/Type-II coefficients, with their signs and prime supports.
Repeated norms do not increase the tree multiplicity: this count is
over the original ideals, not over distinct norm values.

The physical root in (R4) is `q_P^(-1/2)`. If written using
`q_t^(-1/2)`, it must be multiplied by `q_d^(1/2)`. Thus the D in
`D Omega` is real and cannot disappear. The factor length D is also
distinct from a mark/row collision divisor Delta. Keeping the projector
literal avoids any incomplete Delta inversion.

Combining (R1)--(R4), and using DE comparable to N, proves the explicit
version

    sum_j |V_(I_j)|^2
      << Z^epsilon N ell_D^2 S(E,LD) Omega.          (R5)

Reversing d,e is permitted by the same even reciprocity as in [private research revision]
D2, with both actual supports and coefficients retained. It yields
`N ell_E^2 S(D,LE) Omega`. The minimum of the TWO completed bounds may
be taken. Since ell_D,ell_E are O(log(2N)), this implies SF2 with
`T=min{S(E,LD),S(D,LE)}` and at most two logarithms. A unit dyad uses a
one-node tree and ell=1. No nonunit factorization of a prime is inferred.

## R2. Source reconstruction, multiplicities and absolute control

Fix an ordinary Dirichlet character chi with its SPECIFIED modulus q, its natural zero extension and a(n)=mu(n)chi(n). Put F(s)=1/L(s,chi), z=delta+i theta with delta>0 fixed, and g(v)=(2 pi)^(-1/2)exp(-v^2/2). Initially Re s>1. Every shifted reciprocal entry has an absolutely convergent Dirichlet series, and

    [F(s+(i+j)z)]_(0<=i,j<=2)
       = sum_n a(n)n^(-s) v_n v_n^T,
    v_n=(1,n^(-z),n^(-2z))^T.

Finite Cauchy--Binet followed by absolute convergence therefore gives

    D_z(s)=sum_(u<v<w) a(u)a(v)a(w)V_z(u,v,w)^2(uvw)^(-s),
    V_z(u,v,w)=(u^(-z)-v^(-z))(u^(-z)-w^(-z))(v^(-z)-w^(-z)).    (R2.1)

There is exactly ONE term for each unordered three-element set, written in its unique increasing order. There is no factor 3! or 1/3!, and the Vandermonde orientation disappears on squaring. Its square is analytic: replacing it by |V_z|^2 would change every subsequent frequency identity.

A live label is squarefree and coprime to q. Labels may share primes and their product may be squareful. Complete multiplicativity gives

    a(u)a(v)a(w)=chi(uvw)lambda(uvw)

on every live tuple. For complex z the remaining Vandermonde weight is generally complex; the real-shift positivity of W_delta cannot be imported. No output representation, natural character zero, shared divisor or valuation is deleted.

Expand the two Vandermondes with independent permutations alpha,beta of (0,1,2). Each term has coefficient sgn(alpha)sgn(beta) and exponents e_j=alpha_j+beta_j. There are 36 ordered permutation pairs. Independently multiplying the three squared differences and collecting terms gives exactly:

| Sorted exponent pattern | Distinct ordered exponent vectors | Coefficient of each | Raw permutation multiplicity |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| (0,2,4) | 6 | +1 | 6 |
| (0,3,3) | 3 | -2 | 6 |
| (1,1,4) | 3 | -2 | 6 |
| (1,2,3) | 6 | +2 | 12 |
| (2,2,2) | 1 | -6 | 6 |

Thus 19 collected monomials encode all 36 signed occurrences. There are 12 occurrences with a zero exponent and 24 with all exponents positive. The counts are not counts of distinct collected monomials; the author uses the larger correct absolute multiplicity bounds.

For u<v<w, rearrangement bounds each single permutation product in modulus by u^(-2delta)v^(-delta), so each squared-expansion term is bounded by u^(-4delta)v^(-2delta). There is an absolute constant K satisfying

    sum_(n>=1) g(log(n/y)) <= K y, y>0.                       (R2.2)

Indeed, on j<=log(n/y)<j+1 there are at most e^(j+1)y positive integers; this bound also holds when the upper endpoint is below 1. Summing that number times the supremum of g on [j,j+1] gives a convergent bilateral Gaussian series. Summing the last label first then proves

    sum_(u<v<w; alpha,beta) |a(u)a(v)a(w)|
       product n_j^(-delta e_j) g(log(uvw/x))
       <=36 K zeta(1+4delta)zeta(1+2delta)x,  x>0.           (R2.3)

The analogous positive weighted count up to product t is at most 36 zeta(1+4delta)zeta(1+2delta)t: count w by t/(uv). These bounds are uniform in theta and chi and survive arbitrary term restrictions as ABSOLUTE bounds. They do not assert monotonicity of a signed norm.

Define H(theta,x) by replacing (uvw)^(-s) in R2.1 with g(log(uvw/x)). With integer r=product n_j^(e_j), R2.3 permits grouping

    H(theta,x)=sum_(r>=1) r^(-delta)B_r(x)e^(-i theta log r),
    sum_r r^(-delta)|B_r(x)| <= C_delta x.                 (R2.4)

A group B_r may contain an infinite free-label sum, but it converges absolutely at fixed x. The Fourier series is uniformly absolutely convergent in theta. All subsequent full-line integrations and bounded theta limits are consequently legitimate.
title: R2. Source reconstruction, multiplicities and absolute control

0\le\rho,\chi\le1,\quad

\chi|_{(0,1]}=1,\quad \chi|_{[2,\infty)}=0.
\end{gathered}
\tag{SF4}

\(2\le W\le\sqrt L\), allowed to depend on \(X\) and frozen on its

u_i=(d_i,W),\qquad d_i=u_iD_i,\qquad (D_i,W)=1.
\tag{SF5}

\[
\begin{gathered}
(D_1,D_2)<H/W,\qquad(D_3,D_4)<H/W,\\
(D_i,D_j)<R/W\quad(ij\in\mathcal E),\\
|r\alpha D_i-s\beta D_j|>\Delta
\quad\left(ij\in\mathcal E,\ \alpha,\beta\mid W,\ 1\le r,s\le J\right).
\end{gathered}
\tag{SF6}

of the selected-prime allocations \(u_i\); the individual endpoints,

Set

\[

K_X(n,n')=\int_X^{2X}\phi(n/x)\phi(n'/x)\,\frac{dx}{x}.
\tag{SF7}

&\cdot w_X(de)w_X(fh)\,
\sigma_W(\ell de)\sigma_W(mfh)
1_{|\ell de-mfh|>P_{\rm gap}}\\
&\cdot\phi(\ell de/x)\phi(mfh/x)\,\frac{dx}{x}.
\end{split}
\tag{SF8}
\]

There is no reciprocal \(\ell\) or \(m\) weight. Both upper

## Full sector and exact residual

For polynomial \(1\le T\le Z^C\), the full estimate, including arbitrary outer powers, actual marks, unequal embeddings, and bounded row-independent masks, is
\[
\boxed{\sum_{R\le T}|C_{\lambda\mu}-Z_{\lambda\mu}|
 \ll_{\epsilon,C} Z^\epsilon\frac{L^{5/3}T}{QY^{2/3}}.} \tag{HC1}
\]
The sum is the absolute atom-pair sum in the PC convention; for \(R>1\), the complete zero \(Z_{\lambda\mu}\) vanishes. Consequently PC15 becomes
\[
\mathcal C_< =\mathcal C_{<,R>T}
 +O_\epsilon\!\left(Z^\epsilon\left[Y^{-1}
 +\frac{L^{5/3}T}{QY^{2/3}}\right]\right). \tag{HC2}
\]
For the target \(Y^{-1}P_a^{1/6}Z^\epsilon\), the exact affordable threshold is
\[
\boxed{T_* = \frac{QY^{-1/3}P_a^{1/6}}{L^{5/3}}
 =\left(\frac{Q}{L^2}\right)^{5/6}.} \tag{HC3}
\]
At the saved geometry, where \(X=Z^x,Y=Z^y,L=Z^\ell\), write
\[
T_*=q_{b_*}^{5/6}Z^{\tau_*^{\rm rad}},\qquad
\tau_*^{\rm rad}=\frac56(x+y-2\ell)
=\frac{12347}{30000}=0.4115666666666666\ldots.
\]
This decimal is the **scale exponent**, not the exact finite-\(Z\) logarithm:
\(\log_ZT_*=\tau_*^{\rm rad}+\tfrac56\log_Zq_{b_*}\).
The old PC14 affordable threshold has scale exponent
\(0.21799823482243477\ldots\). In particular \(R\le Z^{2/5}\) is paid with a strict scale-exponent margin \(0.0115666\ldots\).

statement:
## 6. Protected parked audit30: causal Schur elimination and escaping mass

This audit uses the author's actual finite-prime source, not a toy PSD matrix. Fix finite P and write, on H_sigma=L2(R,e^(-2sigma u)du), sigma>0,

    A_P=product_(p<=P)(I-D_p),
    B_P=product_(p<=P,p!=3)(I-2D_p),
    V_P=A_P^(-1)B_P g_tau.                                (S1)

Here g_tau is even, so g_tau(u)=g_tau(-u), the n=1 source. Each D_p is the causal delay u->u-log p with norm p^(-sigma). Thus A_P is boundedly invertible by convergent causal geometric series for this finite prime set. Its inverse has exactly the positive P-smooth coefficients1. Expanding S1 yields literal f_P, including all powers. Equivalently, the coefficient identity is

    mu_(P-smooth,squarefree) * f_P
       = (-2)^omega(n) 1_(n squarefree, primes<=P, 3 not dividing n). (S2)

Let U=log X, V=log(2X), and split the u-axis into L=(-infinity,U), I=[U,V], R=(V,infinity). A causal delay never carries a future input to an earlier output. Thus A_P and B_P are lower triangular in this time decomposition. Moreover their II blocks are the identity: every nonidentity delay has log d>=log2, so cannot connect two points of I except a measure-zero endpoint. Consequently, with b=B_P g_tau,

    (V_P)_L=(A_P)_LL^(-1)b_L,
    (V_P)_I=b_I-(A_P)_IL(A_P)_LL^(-1)b_L.                 (S3)

All LR/IR future-input blocks are zero. The relevant Schur feedback product is exactly zero, and the II Schur complement is I. The surviving past injection in S3 is not zero and has not been estimated. This is a source-exact answer to the parked card's “unit feedback eigenvalue” first test: that proposed obstruction is absent for this natural causal split, while the difficult signed forcing remains. One cannot infer a small solution from the trivial complement. The prior T37 PSD completion-of-squares objection remains correct for its different quadratic elimination; no nonnegative residual is being dropped here.

The naive separate estimate of the inverse past propagation is costly. The full H_sigma norm of A_P^(-1) is

    product_(p<=P)(1-p^(-sigma))^(-1),                    (S4)

because its Fourier multiplier attains that upper value at t=0. The left-half-line compression has the same norm: first truncate its positive, absolutely summable weighted convolution to finitely many delays, test a long weighted plateau far to the left, and then let the convolution truncation increase. The omitted tail has arbitrarily small operator norm for fixed P. For fixed sigma<1, PNT makes the logarithm of S4 asymptotic to P^(1-sigma)/((1-sigma)log P). So this easy bound is superpolynomial too. Cancellation between b_I and the entire past injection, or a source-specific bound on their sum, is indispensable. Splitting them and paying the generic inverse recreates the old obstacle.

There is a sharper localization of R7. Uniformly in P, |f_P(n)|<=1, so for u>=0,

    |V_P(u)|<=sum_n g_tau(log n-u)<=C_tau e^u.

This follows by comparing the positive unimodal summand with its integral plus a bounded maximum. For u<=0, expand the Gaussian square: n^(u/tau)<=1 and sum_n exp(-(log n)^2/(2tau))<infinity, giving |V_P(u)|<=C_tau exp(-u^2/(2tau)). Therefore for every fixed T>0 and1/2<sigma<1,

    ||1_(u<=T log P)e^(-sigma u)V_P||_2
                       <=C_(sigma,tau,T) P^(T(1-sigma)).  (S5)

Combining S5 with R7 and orthogonality of the two half-line projections proves

    ||1_(u>T log P)e^(-sigma u)V_P||_2
          /||e^(-sigma u)V_P||_2 -> 1                    (S6)

for EVERY fixed T. The superpolynomial norm escapes beyond x=P^T for any fixed polynomial scale. This is a proved strengthening of “may be remote smooth-number scales”; it uses no new arithmetic cancellation. With P_X=X^(1+o(1)), the physical shell is in the polynomial-scale part and cannot be assigned the global lower bound. The forward causal formulation S3 has no return from those later output scales.

The useful survivor is therefore the exact signed scalar in S3, measured on I, with the R3 tail restored. Its complete exponent gamma is equivalent to the original F exponent when C is chosen to put R3 below gamma. A source-specific upper bound for S3 remains OPEN. No contraction or cheap Schur complement has supplied one. Relative to the index, S1–3 adapt the existing finite incidence/Schur machinery, while S5–6 are a precise new localization consequence of W45's actual-source obstruction. Independent finite checks verify S2 and the exact blocks through n=96, primes2/3/5/7; the continuous and asymptotic arguments above, not that finite check, prove S1–6.

statement:
## 2. Gaussian spectral input and every-interval observation

Let tau>0 be fixed and use the normalized kernel

    g_tau(v)=(2pi tau)^(-1/2) exp(-v^2/(2tau)).

Assume A_b=sum_n |a_n|n^-b<infinity at one fixed real b>gamma. No
multiplicativity, sign assumption or zero-free estimate is needed here.
Put F(u)=sum_n a_n g_tau(log n-u), h(u)=exp(-bu)F(u), and use
hat h(t)=integral h(u)exp(-itu)du. If v=log n, the nth contribution to h
is a_n n^-b phi_b(u-v), where phi_b(w)=exp(-bw)g_tau(w). Thus

    ||h||_1 <= M,  ||h||_infinity <= g_tau(0)M,
    hat h(t)=exp(tau(b+it)^2/2) sum_n a_n n^(-b-it),
    |hat h(t)|<=M exp(-tau t^2/2),
    M=exp(tau b^2/2)A_b.                                  (R2)

These follow by absolute Fubini on the original absolute line, for either
sign of b. In particular h is globally bounded even on the unobserved left
half-line. The same proof works for a sum over ideals and their norms when
the corresponding absolute ideal series is finite.

Fix an observation allowance eta>0 with d=b-gamma-eta>0. The chosen eta is
held fixed while j tends to infinity. Set r_j^2=sqrt(j) and

    H_j(u)=h(u)exp(-(u-j)^2/(2r_j^2)).

The Fourier transform of the window is
sqrt(2pi)r_j exp(-r_j^2 t^2/2)exp(-ijt). In the product convolution,
the factor 1/(2pi), this normalization, and the Gaussian integral give

    |hat H_j(t)|<=M r_j/sqrt(tau+r_j^2) exp(-sigma_j t^2/2),
    sigma_j=tau r_j^2/(tau+r_j^2).                         (R3)

This is uniform in the center j. The phase exp(-ij(t-x)) has modulus one;
there is no unpriced exponential dependence on j. For large j, sigma_j>=tau/2.
The completed-square identity in A6 is exact.

Write B=b-gamma+2>0 and take T_j=sqrt(4Bj/tau). Define P_j by restricting
the inverse Fourier integral of H_j to [-T_j,T_j]. It is bounded with that
Fourier support. Absolute Fourier inversion and the Gaussian tail give

    e_j:=||H_j-P_j||_infinity
       <= M/(pi sigma_j T_j) exp(-sigma_j T_j^2/2)
       <= C exp(-Bj).                                    (R4)

The possible prefactor r_j/sqrt(tau+r_j^2) is at most one. This is the
whole frequency remainder, before amplification.

For each sufficiently large integer k, choose the hypothesized E_k in
[k,k+1], with measure at least delta_k and bound C_eta exp((gamma+eta)k).
Necessarily 0<delta_k<=1. For center j use integer endpoints
m0=floor(j/2), m1=ceil(3j/2), and

    I_j=[m0,m1+1],
    S_j=(R\I_j) union union_(m0<=k<=m1)E_k,
    delta_j^*=min_(m0<=k<=m1)delta_k.

Every real interval of length two contains a complete integer unit interval.
That unit interval either carries one of the chosen E_k or lies in the
added exterior. Hence S_j is (delta_j^*/2,2)-thick. For the fixed eta,
log(1/delta_k)=o(sqrt(k)) implies
log(1/delta_j^*)=o(sqrt(j)) uniformly over this finite moving range: all
its k are comparable to j and eventually past the same little-o threshold.
R1 therefore has amplification

    Lambda_j=(200/delta_j^*)^(132T_j+1)=exp(o(j)).          (R5)

On the genuine observation sets, replacing k by u costs only a fixed
factor, even when gamma+eta is negative. Completing the real square gives

    |H_j(u)|<=C_eta exp(-du-(u-j)^2/(2r_j^2))
              <=C_eta exp(-dj+d^2 sqrt(j)/2).             (R6)

On the added exterior, use the global bound for h in R2, not an assumed
arithmetic estimate:

    |H_j(u)|<=C exp(-(j/2-1)^2/(2sqrt(j)))
              =exp(-j^(3/2)/8+O(sqrt(j))).                (R7)

The sup norm inequality and the triangle inequality now give the full
ledger

    ||H_j||_infinity
       <=Lambda_j ||H_j||_(L-infinity(S_j))+(Lambda_j+1)e_j
       <=exp(-dj+o(j)).                                  (R8)

Both the artificial exterior and the frequency remainder have been multiplied
by Lambda_j before they are discarded. Undoing exp(-bu) on [j,j+1] and the
window, whose minimum there is exp(-1/(2sqrt(j))), proves

    sup_[j,j+1]|F(u)|<=exp((gamma+eta)j+o(j)).              (R9)

For any requested output epsilon>0, first choose
0<eta<min(epsilon/2,(b-gamma)/2), then take j sufficiently large to absorb
o(j). All constants may depend on that fixed choice and the coefficient
sequence. Covering all large real u and absorbing a compact interval proves
Theorem A. There is no diagonal sequence in eta, no variable iteration
count, and no meromorphic reciprocal input in this step.

Every fixed polynomial density k^-kappa qualifies, for any fixed kappa>=0.
This supersedes the geometric restriction in W39's particular Taylor proof;
it does not contradict W39, which expressly left that restriction nonoptimal.

### The complete-zero form and the precise unpaid covariance

Let \(\mathcal E_0\) be the inherited positive complete-zero form. Its *whole* compensated value is \(O(Y^{-1}Z^\epsilon)\). The same estimate holds for the direct sum of its same-core values:
\[
 \sum_c\mathcal E_0(S_c,S_c)\ll Y^{-1}Z^\epsilon,
 \qquad |\mathcal C_{\ne,0}|\ll Y^{-1}Z^\epsilon. \tag{T06.9}
\]
To justify the first assertion despite moving masks, truncate completed columns, choose one common residue period, and at each residue and continuous row point apply
\[
 \left|\sum_t\mathcal A_{D,t}B_{D,c,t}\right|^2
 \le |\{t\}|Z^\epsilon B(q_c/N_D)^2\sum_t|\mathcal A_{D,t}|^2.
\]
Only then average residues and integrate rows. The unmarked outer zero form has only its equal-column term, of size \(Q_D/Y_D\), by M B1.16. Equation (T06.6) and the residue-density/Jacobian isometry from [restricted research revision] AA19 give the first assertion. Rapid tails control differences of truncations in this positive completion. Polarize after that limit; subtracting the same-core value from the paid whole value proves the second assertion. This argument assumes no common finite period for an infinite family.

Thus the sufficient new estimate is the one-sided bound
\[
 \mathcal C_{\ne,\rm nz}:=
 \sum_{c\ne c'}\{\langle S_c,S_{c'}\rangle-\mathcal E_0(S_c,S_{c'})\}
 \ll Y^{-1}P_a^{1/6}Z^\epsilon. \tag{OPEN-COV}
\]
It remains unproved. Cauchy over the \(O(Q)\) physical rows would then give
\[
 |I_\eta^{\rm comp}|\ll Z^{x/2+(y-x)/12+\epsilon},
\]
the physical estimate used by the inherited \(c=.12551\) conditional certificate. The available same-core theorem supplies only one summand of this implication.

statement:
## 2. A1–13: independently reconstructing the infinite spectral core

Fix tau>0 and sigma>1/2, both independent of X. Write

    f(n)=mu(rad(n/3^v3(n))),
    F(x)=sum_n f(n)g_tau(log(n/x)).

In particular f(p^k)=-1 for every p!=3 and k>=1, while f(3^k)=1.
There are no squarefree zeros. On l2(N),

    T(m,n)=f(mn)(mn)^(-sigma),
    ||T||_HS^2=zeta(2sigma)^2.                            (R41-A1)

This is a real self-adjoint compact operator for an absolute reason, not a
cancellation estimate. For p!=3 put q=p^(-2sigma), R=q/(1-q). On the span
of e0 and (p^(-sigma k))_(k>=1)/sqrt(R), the literal local operator is

    H(R)=[[1,-sqrt(R)],[-sqrt(R),-R]].

For all positive exponent pairs i,j, f(p^(i+j))=-1, explaining the lower
right -R. At3 the operator is w3 w3^T, w3(k)=3^(-sigma k), k>=0.
The nonzero eigenvalues for p!=3 are

    lambda_+/-=(1-R +/- sqrt(1+6R+R^2))/2.

Set c=1/(lambda_++R). Direct substitution in
lambda^2-(1-R)lambda-2R=0 proves

    0<c<1, lambda_+=1+cR,
    1-c=c(1+c)R,
    u(0)=(1+c^2R)^(-1/2),
    u(k)=-c p^(-sigma k)u(0), k>=1.                     (R41-A2)

Since sum_p R_p<infinity, product lambda_p^+ converges to a finite positive
number and product u_p(0)>0. For finite sets J increasing to the primes
at least5, embed product_(p in J)u_p in the usual finite-support exponent
basis, with vacuum at all other primes. The inner product of two nested
such unit vectors is product_(p newly included)u_p(0), tending to1.
They are therefore Cauchy in l2. This explicitly constructs their limiting
unit vector u; it does not assume a complete infinite tensor eigenbasis.

The finite-prime semigroup projection P_J retains *all exponents* at its
primes, including2,3. T_J=P_J T P_J tends to T in HS norm by dominated
convergence of R41-A1. It is finite rank even though its semigroup index set
is infinite. Finite local spectral decomposition is consequently legitimate.
For 0<R<1,

    r(R)=|lambda_-|/lambda_+
        =(sqrt(1+6R+R^2)-(1-R))/(sqrt(1+6R+R^2)+(1-R)),
    d[(1-R)/sqrt(1+6R+R^2)]/dR
        =-4(1+R)/(1+6R+R^2)^(3/2)<0.

Thus1>r2>r5>r7>... . Each nonzero tensor eigenvalue is the leading
positive product times a product of distinct negative ratios. The two
largest moduli correspond to the empty set and {2}; the third is {5}.
Any product with at least two ratios is smaller than r5. The resulting core

    B=H2 tensor (w3 w3^T)
         tensor [(product_(p>=5)lambda_p^+) |u><u|]       (R41-A3)

has rank2. It is optimal in both operator and HS norm. For the operator
norm lower bound, any rank-at-most2 competitor kills a unit vector in the
span of the first three singular vectors. Its error there is at least the
third singular value. For HS norm, projection onto its output space captures
at most the first two squared singular values: diagonalize T_J^2 and use
weights in[0,1] summing to at most2. The displayed truncation attains both
finite bounds. Its positive-vector and eigenvalue products converge, so
B_J tends to B in HS norm. Compression of any fixed rank2 competitor still
has rank at most2 and cannot increase either error norm. Taking J to infinity
proves both claimed global optimalities. This resolves the author's stated
strongest infinite-compression concern without an omitted completeness step.

The first column, with every sign and small-prime factor retained, is

    B(n,1)=C_sigma b_sigma(n)n^(-sigma),
    C_sigma=product_(p>=5)lambda_p^+/(1+c_p^2R_p)>0,
    b(2^k)=-1, b(3^k)=1, b(p^k)=-c_p for p>=5,k>=1.      (R41-A4)

The products defining C converge absolutely in their deviations from1;
the O(R_p) bound already suffices. This is the actual spectral column.
It is not obtained by replacing the source's primes by independent signs.

At p>=5 the local Dirichlet series of f and b are, respectively,
(1-2z)/(1-z) and (1-(1+c_p)z)/(1-z). Their ratio and inverse are

    A_p(z)=1+(1-c_p)sum_(k>=1)2^(k-1)z^k,
    D_p(z)=1-(1-c_p)sum_(k>=1)(1+c_p)^(k-1)z^k.          (R41-A5)

At2 and3 both factors are1. For each fixed rho>1/2, the absolute
nonconstant local coefficient sums are bounded by

    (1-c_p)p^(-rho)/(1-2p^(-rho))
        <=C_(sigma,rho)p^(-2sigma-rho).

The denominators are uniformly positive since p>=5, and the prime sum
converges. Positive Euler majorants therefore prove, with no analytic
continuation premise,

    b=a*f, f=d*b, a*d=delta1,
    sum_n (|a(n)|+|d(n)|)n^(-rho)<infinity.              (R41-A6)

This prices both inverse directions. Suppressing either direction would
weaken the important conclusion from equivalence to mere sufficiency.
Prime2 is kept exactly; replacing its kernel by the generic factor would
change the source's boundary zero and can introduce an unaffordable pole.

The coefficient bounds |b|,|f|<=1 and these weighted sums justify the
Gaussian convolution identities absolutely. For example, choose rho>1
for Fubini and bound the positive coefficient majorant Z(t)<=C t^rho
on all t>0, with the Gaussian left tail
paying t<=1. For the sharp exponent use the all-real-shell norm

    ||V||_rho=sup_(T>0)T^(-rho)||V||_(L2([T,2T],dx/x)).

Minkowski bounds convolution by sum|a(n)|n^(-rho); the analogous d bound
gives the converse. Large dyadic estimates extend to real shells using
two neighboring dyadic intervals; finitely many middle scales and Gaussian
left tails supply the other values of T. Consequently for fixed gamma>.5,
with the usual every-epsilon allowance on all sufficiently large shells,

    ||sum_n b(n)g_tau(log(n/x))||_[X,2X] <<_epsilon X^(gamma+epsilon)
       iff ||F||_[X,2X] <<_epsilon X^(gamma+epsilon).     (R41-A7)

For precision one applies the weighted theorem at rho=gamma+epsilon/2,
starting with a smaller epsilon in the hypothesized bound. The moment form
with exponent2gamma+epsilon is equivalent after renaming epsilon. There is
no deletion of any cross term and no inheritance by arbitrary masks.

With w_x(n)=n^sigma g_tau(log(n/x)), the physical readout is exactly

    F(x)=<w_x,T e1>,
    C_sigma Bfield(x)=<w_x,B e1>.

The squared norm of w is the sum of n^(2sigma)g_tau(log(n/x))^2.
Comparison with its Gaussian integral gives O(x^(2sigma+1)); the sum's
maximum term costs only O(x^(2sigma)), so the bound also covers lattice
discretization for x>=1. Hence a column error epsilon_X has shell readout
O(X^(sigma+.5)epsilon_X). The stated sufficient budget

    epsilon_X << X^(gamma-sigma-.5)                     (R41-A8)

is correct. It is an upper-bound interface, not a necessary lower bound
for every arithmetic residual. At sigma=.75 the proposed gamma=.874864,
5/6,3/4 give exponents -.375136,-5/12,-1/2. The fixed nonzero spectral
residual does not acquire decay as X grows. Nor does optimal low rank make
its retained column easy: R41-A7 is exactly the full OPEN-F3 problem. A
different signed spectral combination may still be useful if its complete
readout is estimated. No general impossibility of operator methods follows.

### Fixed ordinary characters and the nonvanishing numerator

For a fixed ordinary character chi, including zeros at ramified primes,
complete multiplicativity gives

    chi b=(chi a)*(chi f), chi f=(chi d)*(chi b).

All products with chi on the right are coefficientwise before Dirichlet
convolution. Their absolute weighted norms do not increase. In particular
the exact equivalence extends separately to each fixed character, not
uniformly in a growing conductor. On the unit-index subspace the operator
is D_chi T^(q) D_chi; this is left and right unitary multiplication, **not**
unitary conjugation. Singular values are preserved, while self-adjointness
need not be. If2 is unramified, the core is optimal rank2; if2 is ramified,
the stated all-positive core is optimal rank1. It is not then claimed to
be optimal rank2. Prime3 is rank1 when present, absent when ramified.
Extending by zero returns exactly the missing rows/columns and coefficients.

Direct local multiplication, not an analogy to zeta, gives

    sum_n chi(n)f(n)n^(-s)=W_chi(s)/L(s,chi), Re s>1,
    W_chi(s)=(1-2chi(2)2^-s)
       /[(1-chi(2)2^-s)^2(1-chi(3)3^-s)^2]
       *product_(p>=5)(1-2chi(p)p^-s)/(1-chi(p)p^-s)^2. (R41-A9)

A ramified factor equals1. Each generic factor differs from1 by
-z^2/(1-z)^2, z=chi(p)p^-s. On Re s>=rho>.5 the generic product and its
inverse converge normally and are uniformly bounded: 2p^-rho<1 for p>=5
and the local deviations are summable. Denominators have no zeros for
Re s>0. The retained prime-two numerator has zeros only on Re s=1.
Thus W_chi is holomorphic and nonzero in .5<Re s<1.

The Mellin transform initially is exp(tau s^2/2)W_chi/L. An all-scale
Gaussian norm exponent gamma>.5 continues the transform holomorphically
to Re s>gamma, including every fixed height, by shell Cauchy–Schwarz;
logarithmic derivatives are paid by a small positive exponent buffer and
the Gaussian left tail. Multiply by the continued L-function before
evaluating at a possible zero. The identity theorem gives a nonzero right
side at every point gamma<Re s<1, contradicting any such zero. The known
right-edge result finishes the half-plane assertion; the principal pole
at1 is retained. There is no assumed all-height reciprocal bound hiding
in this direction of the argument. A hypothesis must be proved for each
fixed chi to earn that character's conclusion. No such new bound is proved.

**Ancestry:** W29's trace-class product tensor and Sobolev readout already
separate compactness from arithmetic evaluation; its odd local block has
lower-right0 and its prime-two block is different. AM18–21 already separate
finite divisor-inverse conditioning from actual readout. G28–32 and the
reviewed Sol D04 supply existing weighted-reconstruction interfaces.
W41's admitted delta is the explicit all-prime-power f3 optimal core and
its two weighted inverse kernels; the abstract spectral facts and Mellin
return are not new broad mechanisms.
