# [private research revision] joint-window: independent source review and a smaller joint-cut core



## 1. Verdict and limits

Recommend the author's two restricted-row estimates and exact complementary source as written, relative to the literal PR9/[restricted research revision]/[restricted research revision] hypotheses. The shared-prime lcm sum retains BOTH claimed powers; its proof does not require independent divisibility. The same internal buffered grade must remain in the plain lower and shortened-plain upper bounds until their division. The fully marked MI, including its two capacity gates and every original slot, is genuinely available after each shortening. No new arbitrary-column moment is being assumed in these estimates.

The review additionally proves a joint cutoff using

    F(a,b)=N(a,b) * (N s_2(b))^2.

Its entire high part has squared norm at most

    H_J U^(1+beta*m+epsilon) T^(-beta),                 (R1)

when F(a,b)>=T. This uses a new two-variable divisor inversion and the author's complete lcm mass estimate, rather than a product-of-independent-divisibility heuristic. On a suitable actual dominance class it saves delta*log_U(T) in the ORIGINAL inverse moment. At T=U^(4eta), the complementary coefficient has

    N(n/rad(n)) < U^(4eta) NP,                         (R2)

halving the author's unmarked repeat-factor width 8eta while retaining the same pre-loss saving (68/25)eta. Both the original paid classes can be kept before applying this additional class. The surviving signed core still carries more than half the same product witness. Its full moment remains OPEN.

These are actual-source proper-row-subclass results. They neither construct a high zero nor prove that any paid class is nonempty. A small repeat factor is a support restriction, not a bound for its signed divisor-profile coefficient. There is no full row cover, improved raw envelope, new local plane, endpoint gain, or claim that any signed projector preserves a row class. The written source-relative c11=.1251459636 and density K=28114053/6250000 remain unchanged, with their preceding-c10 SAME-family license, F0/analytic ancestry, positive-slot uniformity and external admission obligations still open. No formalization or kernel work occurred.

## 2. Literal source contract and the same buffered grade

Use exactly PR9 B0.3--4 and B3.31: the Eisenstein ideal sum with primary/unit convention, fixed excluded set S, natural character zeros, one entire orientation

    phi_u(n)=nu(n) psi_u(n)^(+/-1),
    M_u(E)=E^(-1/2) sum_n mu(n)phi_u(n)W_I(Nn/E),
    S_u(E)=E^(-1/2) sum_n phi_u(n)W_P(Nn/E).

The fixed finite phase nu need not have order six. Let Q_u be the unchanged product of original disjoint prime slots, with total width v and all its individual fixed coefficients, canonical pools, holes and independent heights. In MI these coefficients may be arbitrary bounded row-independent coefficients; this is not a permission for arbitrary coefficients in MP or in the canonical column energy B3.6. The original re-anchoring to a witness label is the accepted [restricted research revision]/[restricted research revision] interface, not a new assumption that unrelated labels have the same zero.

Fix physical delta in[17/25,7/10], v in[0,1/20], 0<eta<=1/1000 and G137's cutoff t=t_*(delta,v)-eta BEFORE witnesses. Restrict to its crossing window |r-r_*(t)|<=2eta with the already allocated endpoint padding, r+m>=t-small and 0<=m<=1/2+small. Fix a witness label, internal bin and dyads R=U^r,D=U^m before their norm. The original finite unions and logarithmic dyad counts cost the already allocated small loss. Omega consists of the licensed nonprincipal supported-witness rows in this window; no all-length extension is claimed. Principal, artificial and fixed-inducing exceptional branches are not inserted into Omega. H_J denotes a fixed polynomial in the original height bounds; it is independent of the arithmetic thresholds G,H and T used below, and its degree may increase between inequalities.

PR9 B0.13 constructs a finite internal bin with a<=B_i<a+e and B_(i+1)<a+2e. The actual zero has a<=Re(rho)<a+e in the retained box. Write beta=2a-1. The internal grade can exceed the physical delta, but beta>=delta-small and beta lies in a fixed compact subset of(0,1); the preceding source-relative SAME-family bound supplies beta<=3/4 here. B0.19--20 first gives the SAME-character, SAME-real-power and SAME-height product spike with this beta. Dividing by its two B0.15 upper bounds gives B0.18 at this beta, before any weakening. In particular

    |S_u(D)|^2 >= D^beta U^(-epsilon_det).             (R3)

For every actual shortened E<=C D the direct, unreflected Mellin line Re(s)=a+6e in B0.15 gives

    |S_u(E)|^2 <= H_J U^(epsilon_det) E^beta.          (R4)

The fixed real powers and finite derivative profiles are carried in the same common smooth tests. Shortening E does not select another bin, height, zero or character. The direct line is sufficient even if a small endpoint tolerance leaves m just above 1/2. There is no need to claim an improved reflected-conductor estimate. Fixed positive-strip deleted Euler factors of polynomial radical size cost U^epsilon; they retain their natural zeros. For subunit E, a nonempty annulus forces E>=c>0, so R4 holds by a fixed constant; smaller E are empty.

Using D^delta as the only spike while retaining E^beta in R4 would lose D^(beta-delta). That would invalidate the claimed small saving. The author avoids this error. In the review below beta cancels at the D scale, and only then is beta weakened to delta in the saved exponent. No internal grade replaces the physical upper slot price.

## 3. Fully marked MI after every shortening

The two literal gates are

    r'+2v <= 1-c1,     2r'+8v <= 3-c2.                (R5)

G137 already supplies fixed reserves throughout its whole crossing window, including v=0 and both sides of the plain kink. The first reserve exceeds .01017 before its allocated fine losses. In all divisor expansions here the inverse scale is R/(Nq Nh), with h supported on q and any already fixed inverse puncture. Thus r'<=r, up to harmless fixed endpoint constants; both inequalities improve. A nonempty nominal negative length is replaced by length zero with a bounded dilation of its common profile. At zero length, 2v<=1/10 and 8v<=2/5 still satisfy both gates. This is not an unmarked UM application with a missing U^v slot price.

Consequently the original positive norm gives

    ||M_u(E)Q_u||^2_(all original rows)
       <= H_J U^(1+epsilon),  0<E<=C R.               (R6)

The original radial/divisor weight is nonnegative and either bounded or paid by its U^epsilon majorant before use. The restricted set Omega is enlarged only after R4 has been applied pointwise and the remaining summand is a positive M*Q norm. No zero-conditioned Poisson identity is used.

Here is a precise way to retain rowwise smooth parameters. For each finite parameter rectangle, apply tensor Sobolev to F_u=M_u(E;W_I)Q_u, sum its nonnegative derivative norms, and use MI on each derivative profile. Real/height derivatives insert bounded logarithms of normalized norms; scale derivatives replace W by -W/2-yW'. Slot derivatives act on their original coefficients/profiles, and the slot heights are never equated to the common witness height. The finite parameter integrations have polynomial height cost. Log-scale intervals cost only logarithms. Arithmetic q,h cutoffs are fixed at U before derivatives; put all sums in one polynomial outer box and let the original profiles give zero outside support. This avoids differentiating a moving arithmetic endpoint.

The cutoff inside the inverse profile also remains exact. If W_I(y) includes V_le(R y/U^t), after a=qh c and E=R/(Nq Nh) its old argument is V_le(R(c/E)/U^t). Thus the very same function of its normalized variable is used. Its Euler derivatives have uniform bounds: the derivatives of V_le are supported on its fixed transition annulus. No moving divisor coefficient is absorbed into this profile.

For heights, fix the small loss, bounded length ranges and finite smooth/Sobolev orders first, obtaining an internal height degree J0. Choose the source's internal small polynomial height range sufficiently small for these orders. The literal B0.14--15 retained contours use the original buffered dictionary; discarded tails are U^B T_ht^(-N), with all polynomial q,h,k counts included in B before N is chosen. When an external height is below the internal floor U^tau, use the buffered dictionary at that floor and choose tau so its internal cost U^(J0*tau) fits epsilon. Above the internal range, the original absolute polynomial bound is paid by enlarging the final external height degree J. This enlarged J is not fed back into the internal floor charge. The eventual external physical height exponent is chosen after this final degree. These choices retain the source's internal bin and its own beta; they do not equate beta to the physical slot price. This is the [restricted research revision]/[restricted research revision] order, not an identification of the internal and physical height exponents. No new high-height theorem or full physical return is inferred.

The dominance signal in later sections concerns the original chosen functions at their actual parameters. It is not asserted for derivatives of that signal. Derivatives occur inside the positive Sobolev majorant for R6. A later positive child uses its own actual profile, zero and slot list; a parent's dominance label cannot be inherited through a signed expansion.

## 4. Exact restorations and the author's two estimates

For an ideal q define

    A_G(q)=sum_(d|q, Nd>=G) mu(q/d).

Then sum_(q|g) A_G(q)=1_(Ng>=G), A_G(q)=0 below G, and |A_G(q)|<=tau(q). Since the original inverse index a is squarefree, every contributing q|a is squarefree. With a=qc,b=qd the author's exact identity is

    B_g=sum_(q sf) A_G(q)mu(q)phi(q)^2/(Nq)
                    M^(q)(R/Nq) S(D/Nq).              (R7)

M^(q) has the extra condition (c,q)=1. The b/q index has no such condition. The original profiles and all character zeros remain literal.

The mask is restored by the full q-smooth series

    M^(q)(E)=sum_(h q-smooth) phi(h)/sqrt(Nh) M(E/Nh). (R8)

At p|q, its local inverse coefficient is mu*(1,1,1,...), which equals the unit sequence. Every p^j is necessary. Complete multiplicativity with zero extensions proves R8 even when p is a row hole. For each actual annulus the sum is finite. After taking absolute values its full mass is at most

    product_(p|q) (1-(Np)^(-1/2))^(-1) <= C_e (Nq)^e.

Separate finitely many small primes, then bound each remaining factor by (Np)^e. A polynomial fixed inverse puncture can be included with q; its total mass is still a freely allocated U^epsilon. Slots keep their original frozen holes in MI's bounded coefficients. No quotient of a possibly zero character value is taken.

Hilbert Minkowski, R4 and R6 give

    ||B_g Q|| <= H_J U^(1/2+epsilon) D^(beta/2)
        sum_(Nq>=G) (Nq)^(-1-beta/2+small)
      <= H_J U^(1/2+epsilon) D^(beta/2) G^(-beta/2).   (R9)

Ideal counting on dyadic shells is O(X), from the underlying fixed lattice. Extracted row-dependent character phases have absolute value at most one and act only as contractions in the positive norm; they do not become new MI column coefficients. All divisor, restoration and finite-support losses are extracted as U^epsilon before a convergent positive extension. Squaring gives the first author estimate. The q^-1 alone would not yield this power; the same-bin shortened plain contributes the additional q^(-beta/2).

For s_2(b)=product_p p^floor(v_p(b)/2), k|s_2(b) iff k^2|b. The corresponding exact expansion is

    S_bad(D)=sum_(Nk>=H) A_H(k)phi(k^2)/(Nk)
                              S(D/(Nk)^2).

Here k is not squarefree. R4 and ideal counting give

    |S_bad(D)| <= H_J U^epsilon D^(beta/2) H^(-beta),  (R10)

including all prime powers and equality at H. This pays M S_bad Q by R6. It does not by itself pay the signed subtraction of the large-gcd intersection.

For that intersection let q be squarefree and L=lcm(q,k^2). At each prime write i=v_p(q) in{0,1} and j=v_p(k)>=0. Then

    v_p(L)=max(i,2j)=i+2j-min(i,j),
    L=q k^2/(q,k).

Writing a=qc,b=Ld gives exactly the author's formula (15), with coefficient A_G(q)A_H(k)mu(q)phi(qL)/sqrt(Nq NL), inverse M^(q)(R/Nq), and plain S(D/NL). No coprimality between c and d is inserted. After R8, R4 and R6 the remaining positive weight is, in norm notation,

    w_beta(q,k)=q^(-1/2)L^(-(1+beta)/2)
       =q^(-1-beta/2)k^(-1-beta)(q,k)^((1+beta)/2).    (R11)

Its local factors are p^(-1-beta/2) for i=1,j=0; p^(-j(1+beta)) for i=0; and p^(-1/2-j(1+beta)) for i=1,j>=1. These exhaust all valuations. In particular q=k=p has weight p^(-3/2-beta), not p^(-2-3beta/2). The falsely independent lcm would omit the positive correction p^((1+beta)/2).

For fixed q, put d=(q,k), k=de. Drop only positive coprimality restrictions after the exact split. Uniformly for beta in its compact interval,

    sum_(Nk>=H) k^(-1-beta)(q,k)^((1+beta)/2)
      <= C sum_(d|q) d^(-(1+beta)/2)
                         max(1,H/Nd)^(-beta)
      <= C H^(-beta) sum_(d|q) d^((beta-1)/2)
      <= C H^(-beta) tau(q).                          (R12)

For Nd<=H, this is the e-tail from H/Nd. For Nd>H, use the complete e sum and the inequality d^(-(1+beta)/2)<=H^(-beta)d^((beta-1)/2). Thus large common divisors are included, not silently omitted. beta<1 makes the remaining divisor exponent negative. Combining R11--12 with q-tail counting proves

    sum_(q sf,Nq>=G,Nk>=H) w_beta(q,k)
       <= U^epsilon G^(-beta/2) H^(-beta)              (R13)

on the actual polynomial support; bounded divisor weights and the restoration mass are included in the small loss. Therefore

    ||B_gs Q||^2 <= H_J U^(1+beta*m+epsilon)
                                 G^(-beta)H^(-2beta).

Now B_s=M S_bad-B_gs is an exact signed difference. Hilbert triangle, not signed-subset monotonicity, proves the author's second bound since G>=1. I found no missing shared-prime exponent in this step.

## 5. Author's actual row partition and its unchanged complement

B=B_g+B_s+B_c is a disjoint partition of original (a,b) tuples, with equality on the high sides. It is not an orthogonal row decomposition. The row classes are

    Omega_g: |B_g|>=|B|/4;
    Omega_s: outside Omega_g and |B_s|>=|B|/4;
    Omega_c: the rest.

On the first class, |M|^2<=16|B_g|^2/|S|^2; on the second use B_s. R3 cancels D^beta from the corresponding squared norms. Their original inverse moments thus save beta*g and 2beta*h, then delta*g and 2delta*h after allocating the small buffer losses. Q is never divided out. The classes are disjoint, and positivity permits restriction of each already bounded norm to its class.

On the whole remaining class, |B_c|>|B|/2 by triangle and the strict complementary inequalities. The source tuple cuts remain N(a,b)<G and Ns_2(b)<H. Because a is squarefree,

    ab/rad(ab)=(a,b)*b/rad(b),
    b/rad(b) divides s_2(b)^2.

The intrinsic repeat factor is therefore <G H^2. With the original squarefree slot product P, the repeat factor is multiplied by (P,ab), of norm at most NP. This verifies the author's support statements even when equal products have many signed representations.

The identity does not make the resulting coefficient canonical. On the coprime squarefree unmarked part the divisor profile contains

    mu(n)nu(n)/(RD)^(1/2)
       * sum_(b|n) mu(b)W_I(N(n/b)/R)W_P(Nb/D),       (R14)

with the actual tuple cut. The common height/real power combines its norm twists, but the signed divisor-profile factor remains. PR9 B3.6 explicitly forbids an additional coefficient on its squarefree column; B3.39 also has its actual mu(n) coefficient. Neither may be applied to R14 by renaming it. A two-prime product on separated inverse/plain annuli already prevents dyadwise mu*1 cancellation; this is a coefficient example, not a constructed high-zero row or lower bound for the full moment.

The author's complete coarse comparison is correct: R4 and R6 give ||B Q||^2<=H_J U^(1+beta*m+epsilon); triangle with B_g,B_s gives the same for B_c. Division by R3 leaves U^(1+epsilon). It does not save eta on Omega_c. The raw roots, low/high and fixed-inducing branches, both projectors, missing radicals, joint-label count, all clipped rectangles, extraction scalars, actual6a/9a radii, physical K_phys^(5/6), shortage/no-slot families, weighted Euler shifts including zero capacity, principal terms and common-Delta return all retain their OLD estimates. The M/24 reserve is unspent.

## 6. Independent development: one joint cutoff pays a smaller core

Keep every source parameter and profile just verified. Fix T=U^rho, rho>0 in a bounded range, before witnesses. Define the actual tuple sector

    B_T: F(a,b)=N(a,b)*(Ns_2(b))^2 >= T,
    C_T: F(a,b)<T.

These are signed subpolynomials of the original B, before coefficient merging, and B=B_T+C_T exactly. The intrinsic repeat factor alone is NOT substituted for F: different (a,b) representations of the same n may have different F.

For arbitrary ideals q,k define the two-variable divisor coefficient

    A_T(q,k)=sum_(d|q,e|k) mu(q/d)mu(k/e)
                                      1_(Nd*(Ne)^2>=T).

Two successive divisor inversions prove, for every pair of ideals g,s,

    sum_(q|g,k|s) A_T(q,k)=1_(Ng*(Ns)^2>=T).           (R15)

Furthermore |A_T(q,k)|<=tau(q)tau(k), and A_T(q,k)=0 unless Nq*(Nk)^2>=T: every divisor norm is at most its parent's norm. No multiplicativity of this threshold function is asserted.

Apply R15 to g=(a,b),s=s_2(b). Only squarefree q survive the original mu(a). With the SAME L=lcm(q,k^2), the complete expansion is

    B_T=sum_(q sf,k) A_T(q,k)mu(q)phi(qL)/sqrt(Nq NL)
                         M^(q)(R/Nq) S(D/NL).         (R16)

This includes every q/k collision and all their powers and zeros; it is the same literal substitution a=qc,b=Ld as the intersection, with a different coupled coefficient. Its inverse mask is restored by R8, and every original slot remains inside R6. The actual q,k and restoration sums have a common fixed polynomial support bound before norms/derivatives. All divisor and restoration factors can therefore be extracted as U^epsilon, with their shares chosen beforehand.

Partition the remaining positive (q,k) mass into dyadic boxes

    Q0<=Nq<2Q0,   K0<=Nk<2K0,

where Q0,K0>=1. A nonzero term requires Q0 K0^2>=T/8. On each box, enlarge only the positive weight to q>=Q0,k>=K0 and apply R13. Its entire coefficient mass is

    <=U^epsilon Q0^(-beta/2) K0^(-beta)
     =U^epsilon (Q0 K0^2)^(-beta/2)
     <=C U^epsilon T^(-beta/2).                       (R17)

There are O((log U)^2) boxes on the fixed polynomial support. Sum those bounds by Hilbert Minkowski. The factor8 has bounded beta-dependent cost, and logarithms are assigned a separate small loss. Equations R4, R6 and R16 therefore give exactly R1:

    ||B_T Q||_Omega^2
       <=H_J U^(1+beta*m+epsilon) T^(-beta).

No cancellation in A_T was used, and no independently distributed q/k hypothesis was used. The complete shared-prime correction is paid within each box by R12. Equality F=T belongs to B_T. Empty sectors and terminal/subunit scales obey the same conventions as the author.

On any actual class where |B_T|>=|B|/2, R3 gives

    sum w_u |M_u(R)Q_u|^2
       <=H_J U^(1-beta*rho+epsilon)
       <=H_J U^(1-delta*rho+epsilon).                 (R18)

On its complement, |C_T|>|B|/2. Every tuple contributing to C_T has

    N(ab/rad(ab)) <= F(a,b)<T,
    N(abP/rad(abP))<T NP,                             (R19)

which remains an intrinsic necessary support condition after signed merging.

At rho=4eta, the minimum inverse saving before losses is (17/25)*4eta=(68/25)eta, with reserve (43/25)eta above the requested eta. This is the same reserve as the author's g=4eta,h=2eta. The new unmarked core width is4eta rather than8eta; with slots it is4eta+v rather than8eta+v. The source cutoff and proof do not use a new scalar optimization or strengthen MI itself.

To preserve every previously paid row, first retain Omega_g and Omega_s exactly as in Section5. On their complement define Omega_T by |B_T|>=|B|/2 and use R18; all remaining rows have the C_T half-signal. These three paid classes are disjoint and each retains the same desired eta saving at rho=4eta. Their positive union costs only a fixed factor. The final complementary row class is a subset of the old Omega_c. A tuple satisfying F<T also satisfies N(a,b)<T and Ns_2(b)<sqrt(T), so its coefficient support is a subset of the author's old core for G=T,H=sqrt(T).

This last inclusion concerns tuples only. It does NOT imply that the new dominance class contains either old dominance class: added signed terms can cancel. Keeping the old classes first is the valid way to retain their already proved coverage. Nor is ||C_T Q||<=||B_c Q|| claimed. A smaller signed coefficient support need not have a smaller norm.

The complete coarse cost still fails to close the core. C_T=B-B_T, so R4/R6 and R1 give ||C_T Q||^2<=H_J U^(1+beta*m+epsilon), and its half-signal plus R3 again leaves the old U^(1+epsilon). The near-coprime squarefree divisor-profile sector R14 has F=1 and survives every T>1. Its full same-zero signed estimate is the remaining arithmetic obligation. The new support reduction does not prove it is easier or grant canonical admissibility.

## 7. Evidence, ancestry, and disposition

The full current attempt index was read, including the [restricted research revision] entry present at review intake. Its exact bytes and HEAD are in intake-receipt.json. [restricted research revision] G155 supplies the divisor inversion and all-power mask restoration; G157 supplies the strategy of an intrinsic repeat-factor reduction. [restricted research revision]/[restricted research revision] supply the internal-bin, rowwise-height and positive-child restrictions; G137 supplies the fixed cutoff and whole crossing window. These are retained prerequisites, not new results. [restricted research revision]'s four cross-copy gcd analysis concerns a different two-inverse paired source; [restricted research revision]'s ordinary Liouville large-gcd theorem and [restricted research revision]--104's dual/cofactor work do not imply this inverse/plain same-bin estimate. No literature novelty is claimed.

The author's useful new application is precisely the SAME-bin shortened plain estimate with fully marked MI, followed by the complete square-divisor intersection. The review's added result is R15--19: a coupled threshold whose shared-prime coefficient mass is paid in full and whose complementary repeated-prime support is smaller. It is not an acceptance of a whole physical improvement.

One independent helper, joint_cut_check.py, was written and executed once in this review's owned directory. It imports no author code. It checks the new two-variable cutoff in a free ideal monoid with three distinct prime labels, including two with equal norm. Across five thresholds and three phase/zero choices it verifies 15,000 tuple cases, 42,831 nonzero shared-prime terms and 396 exact boundary cases. It retains complete signed merged coefficients, two disjoint slot choices with collisions, nonconstant norm profiles, natural zero phases and the repeat-factor support. The receipt includes the local valuation exponents and the negative control showing the missing factor under the false independent lcm. No floating-point asymptotic fit is used.

These finite checks verify universal algebra only. Their monoid phases are not certified Hecke high rows; they do not prove B0.15, MI, its admission, row existence, or an asymptotic saving. The analytic proofs are Sections2--6 relative to the named source contracts. The original author's five-group receipt was inspected and retained, not rerun for reassurance. All original and review failed or limiting routes remain visible; no negative or missing row case was redrawn.

Recommended integration: accept the author's two proper-class estimates and the review's joint-cut theorem at their exact source-relative scopes, with the full signed C_T moment and complete physical return explicitly OPEN. Preserve c11 and K unchanged. The next useful work is a signed correlation estimate for the actual divisor-profile coefficient on the same buffered large-plain rows, with every original mask, height, live slot and complementary term. Another separate-moment or scalar envelope calculation cannot supply that estimate.

## G67. Signed logarithmic bounds return the complete exponent

For f analytic near |z-t0|<=R, R>=16, f(t0)!=0, and any unit interval I
containing t0, let B>=sup_disk|f|. Avoid boundary zeros by varying R. Then

    integral_I log|f(t)|dt
      >=log|f(t0)|-(8/log R)log(B/|f(t0)|).

The proof uses the nonnegative superharmonic function
log(B/|f|), its positive harmonic part and the complete disk Green sum over
zeros with multiplicity. Near zeros have integrated Green excess at most4
and center Green value at least(log R)/2; far zeros and the harmonic part
obey the explicit Harnack bound. Real logarithmic singularities are integrable.
No zero separation, multiplicity cap or discarded negative logarithm is used.

For coefficients with sum|a_n|n^-b finite, the fixed Gaussian is entire and

    |F(z)| <= (2pi tau)^(-1/2)sum|a_n|n^-b
               exp(b Re z+tau b^2/2+(Im z)^2/(2tau)).

Choose t0 at a maximum on [j,j+1] and R in[sqrt j,2sqrt j]. Writing
M_j=max|F| and J_j=integral_j^(j+1)log|F| gives

    (1+eta_j)log M_j <= J_j+eta_j log B_j,
    eta_j=O(1/log j), log B_j=O(j).

Consequently J_j<=(gamma+epsilon)j+C_epsilon on EVERY sufficiently large
integer interval, for every epsilon>0, is equivalent in exponent to the
complete pointwise bound and the complete all-shell L2 bound. Jensen proves
the moment-to-log direction; the Green comparison returns the maximum with
only O(j/log j) loss. Sparse intervals or an average over j do not suffice.
This settles W21-T29's missing nonconcentration question for this complete
Gaussian class. It does not defeat the old smooth-signal or exceptional-dyad
counterexamples under their different hypotheses.

The actual Mellin numerator is

    integral_R F_chi(u)e^(-su)du=exp(tau s^2/2) N_chi(s)H_chi(s)/L(s,chi),
    N_chi=1-2chi(2)2^-s,
    H_2=(1-z_2)^-2, H_3=(1-z_3)^-2,
    H_p=(1-2z_p)/(1-z_p)^2 (p>=5), z_p=chi(p)p^-s.

H and its inverse converge absolutely for each fixed Re(s)>1/2. The finite

With T>=T_(N,j)>0, an explicit derivative bound K_j, M midpoint samples v_k
and absolute errors delta_k,

All parameters and sufficient asymptotic cutoff/sample budgets are in

## 3. S30: complete parity/size compression and a uniform positive-norm obstruction

Retain the actual cutoff polynomial, not an untruncated Euler product:

    Z_chi,X(z)=sum_(n in D_X)chi(n)z^k(n),
    P_chi,X,rho(z)=sum_(d in D_X)b_chi,X(d)z^k(d)
                 =Z_chi,X(lambda+rho z).                      (B1)

Thus P(-R_rho)=M_chi(X). For nonprincipal chi the coefficients contain the full erased character phase from (A5); they need not be positive. The local prime/size generating product

    product_(p<=X,p not|q)(1+z chi(p)p^(-s))

records every squarefree subset, including products exceeding X. Recovering Z requires the exact product-size projection. This projection cannot be omitted before evaluation at z=-1. Equation(B1) already performs that projection coefficientwise, so no Perron tail or sharp-endpoint convention is borrowed for free. The proposed joint transform has not made the size boundary independent of parity.

For any polynomial P of degree at most K_X, normalized circle Parseval and Cauchy give

    |P(-R_rho)| <= [sum_(j=0)^K_X R_rho^(2j)]^(1/2)
                    *||P(e^(it))||_(L2(dt/2pi)).              (B2)

At fixed rho this transfer costs X^o(1). It would therefore be enough to prove the whole circle norm at a new exponent. The following actual principal source calculation rules out this particular sufficient estimate.

### A. The prime layer survives every retention schedule

For principal chi write P(z)=sum_j beta_j z^j. All beta_j>=0. Every unramified prime contributes lambda+rho z; therefore, for EVERY 0<rho<=1, even X-dependent,

    beta_0+beta_1 >= pi_q(X),
    ||P(e^(it))||_2^2=sum_j beta_j^2 >= pi_q(X)^2/2.           (B3)

Since pi_q(X)~X/log X, this circle norm cannot be O(X^(gamma+epsilon)) for gamma<1 and every epsilon. This is stronger than just noting R_rho>1: even a small inverse cost and adaptive retention do not remove the coherent positive prime mass. It obstructs an uncentered scalar/cardinality circle certificate, not the value P(-R_rho), which retains cancellations between all coefficients.

### B. Finitely many original degree layers cannot repair it

Remove all original terms with k(n)<=r, where r is fixed, before the affine substitution. The remaining polynomial is

    P^(>r)(z)=sum_(n in D_X,k(n)>r)(lambda+rho z)^k(n)         (B4)

for principal chi. Fix k=r+1. Products of k distinct unramified primes in ((X/2)^(1/k),X^(1/k)] lie in (X/2,X] and are distinct. PNT gives at least c_k X/(log X)^k such products for all large X. Each contributes the same degree-k polynomial, with nonnegative coefficients summing to1. Its coefficient l2 norm is at least1/sqrt(k+1). Other layers only increase every coefficient. Hence, uniformly over every retention schedule,

    ||P^(>r)(e^(it))||_2 >>_(q,r) X/(log X)^(r+1).            (B5)

This rejects finite original-layer subtraction as a repair of the positive circle norm. It does not cover exact deflation with signed quotient coefficients, growing r, or a full signed combination of the retained and removed layers. In particular it does not refute G106's actual root/quotient return. The selected fixed-k layer is used only to lower-bound a nonnegative coefficient norm, never the signed arithmetic sum.

### C. What the high-ceiling idea retains

The complete multivariate inverse (A2) and scalar transfer(B2) cost subpower at fixed rho. That is a usable quantitative fact; it avoids declaring the architecture impossible because of the number of available primes. Its simplest global positive norm is nevertheless impossible by(B3), and every fixed original-layer repair is blocked by(B5). A candidate must retain a growing signed boundary/correction and establish its complete contraction. This is a precise restriction on the proposed realization, not a failure of all joint transforms, coding methods or c=1/4 mechanisms.

An observation deleting output labels has a separate exact limitation. If an output coordinate n is unobserved, the vector C_rho delta_n produces zero in every observed coordinate, while its parity readout equals (-R_rho)^k(n), not zero. This synthetic linear-algebra witness is not an alternative Mobius source; it shows why an observer restricted to selected syndromes requires a source-specific bound for the full missing readout.
title: 3. S30: complete parity/size compression and a uniform positive-norm obstruction

## 2. A complete squarefree-chain estimate, and what it does not do

Let F_0=1 and F_j=sum_(k=1)^j k!S(j,k) for j>=1. Each ordered set partition is
encoded injectively by a permutation with cuts: order each block internally and
concatenate its blocks, retaining the cuts. Therefore

    F_j<=2^(j-1)j! for j>=1.                                (5)

For EVERY fixed sigma>1,

    sum_(n squarefree) F_(omega(n)) n^(-sigma)<infinity.      (6)

Here is an elementary proof paying every depth. Let w_p=p^(-sigma). Choose a
FINITE prime cutoff Y_sigma such that R_sigma=sum_(p>Y_sigma)w_p<1/4. Let r be the
number of primes up to Y_sigma. Write e_j for the elementary symmetric function
of the w_p. Splitting small and large primes,

    e_j(all)=sum_(a+b=j,0<=a<=r)e_a(small)e_b(tail),
    e_b(tail)<=R_sigma^b/b!.

Multiplying by(5), each fixed a contributes at most a constant times

    sum_(b>=0) (2R_sigma)^b (a+b)!/b!.

This converges, since the factorial ratio is a polynomial of degree a in b.
There are only r+1 choices of a. This proves(6), without silently imposing a
fixed chain depth, a maximum-number-of-primes model, or independent prime choices
inside the original n<=X cutoff. Rankin's inequality now yields the COMPLETE bound

    sum_(n in D_X) F_(omega(n)) <<_(q,epsilon) X^(1+epsilon). (7)

The left side is the permanent of the principal squarefree Redheffer matrix, and
is an upper bound for the absolute sum of every twisted determinant contribution.
Moreover1+sum_k |A_k| is bounded above by this expression after the coefficientwise
triangle, with equality for principal chi. Thus all roots, all depths and all chain
multiplicities have been included. This is sharper than importing the unrestricted
integer-factorization permanent exponent into this different squarefree matrix.
The unrestricted theorem is not contradicted.

The exponent1 is sharp for this positive price. Indeed it contains |D_X|. Expanding
mu^2(n)=sum_(d^2|n)mu(d), and counting q-units in each inner interval, gives

    |D_X|=delta_q X+O_q(sqrt X),
    delta_q=(phi(q)/q)prod_(p not dividing q)(1-p^(-2))>0.    (8)

The O(sqrt X) includes the tail of sum mu(d)/d^2 and every floor endpoint. Hence
no absolute-chain bound of order X^gamma with gamma<1 can close the intended gain.
This does NOT lower-bound the determinant or any complete signed source.

There is a second precise warning against a semigroup shortcut. Set U=diag(chi(n))
on D_X; it is unitary. Then U B_chi U^(-1)=B_1, while the rank-one closing column
becomes Uv. If J=diag((-1)^omega(n)), then J B_1 J=-B_1. Therefore

    exp(-B_1)=J exp(B_1)J,
    ||exp(-B_chi)||_(2->2)=||exp(B_1)||_(2->2).              (9)

The minus sign is not Hilbert-space dissipation. In fact compress the Hermitian
part of -B_1 to the span of e and the normalized sum of unramified prime coordinates.
Its two-by-two offdiagonal has magnitude sqrt(pi_q(X))/2, so its largest eigenvalue
is at least that quantity. A uniform contraction for this particular exponential
fails already at its derivative at time0. The character remains in the endpoint
vector; discarding that interaction is not a fixed-character arithmetic estimate.
title: 2. A complete squarefree-chain estimate, and what it does not do

## G68. Exact degree energy and the retained arithmetic response

Let P contain2 and exclude3, Q=product P, q_p=1/p, and
a_P(n)=product_(p in P)(1-2*1_(p|n)). Set r_P=f3 a_P so that
f3=a_P r_P and r_P(pn)=r_P(n) for every p in P and every power. Under the
exact product reference law, Z_p=(B_p-q_p)/sqrt(q_p(1-q_p)). The expansion

    a_P=sum_S A_S Z_S,
    A_S=(-1)^|S| product_(p in S)2sqrt(q_p(1-q_p))
                      product_(p notin S)(1-2q_p)

has degree-energy polynomial

    sum_S A_S^2 z^|S|=product_p[(1-nu_p)+nu_p z],
    nu_p=4(p-1)/p^2.

Thus the discarded squared norm rho_D^2 is exactly Pr(K>D) for an
auxiliary Poisson-binomial ENERGY variable. It is not a random model of
arithmetic phases. nu_2=1 forces every nonzero term to contain2.

For the full Gaussian integer law, the existing W41/G54 CRT theorem gives
L1 error epsilon_X=O_A(X^-A) when Q<=X^(1-delta), delta>0 fixed.
The truncated polynomial q_D has |q_D|<=sqrt Q, so the complete error is

    |F_chi-F_(P,D,chi)| <= Z(u)[rho_D+2sqrt(Q epsilon_X)],
    Z(u)=sum_n g_tau(log n-u)~exp(tau/2)e^u.

Its literal realization, with D_pV(u)=V(u-log p), is

    F_(P,D,chi)=sum_(|S|<=D)(-2)^|S| product_(p notin S)(1-2/p)
                    product_(p in S)(chi(p)D_p-I/p) R_(P,chi).

Every shifted scale, cross term, power, sign and ramified zero survives.
At full degree this is exactly F_chi. If rho_D^2<=X^(-2c-eta), c=1-gamma,
the coded and original complete norms have the same exponent gamma.
The fixed original field supplies the pole bridge; no Mellin transform is
assigned to a shell-dependent detector.

With primes<=z<=C log X, the coarse harmonic bound gives
lambda=sum nu_p=O(loglog X). The sufficient degree
D=ceil((2c+eta)log X/loglog X) gives rho_D^2<=X^(-2c-eta+o(1)); retain a
smaller positive buffer. If D>=|P| the discarded part is zero. The leading
coefficients are .250278,1/3,1/2 for c6,1/6,1/4. The literal Q restriction
still applies. This does not justify small fixed degree or a cheap state count.

The retained scalar, or a stronger bound for its conditional rough-response
energy, remains OPEN. Marginal independence and entropy cannot supply it:
the bounded-response toy m=a_P correlates perfectly while the exposed bits
are independent. W38/W41/W44 ancestry remains; the new contribution is the
exact degree law, fully paid truncation and literal centered-dilation formula.

# Centered exceptional rows: valuation reserve and its exact limit

[private research revision] accepts G86 after full author, independent reviewer and controller
reads. Frozen sources and normal own-claim releases were verified. The
review report was saved before its deadline; receipt/freeze/release closed
late after preserved stream failures. The accepted endpoint is unchanged.

The [author](exceptional-valuation/report.md) and [independent review](exceptional-valuation-review/report.md)
derive the following refinement of the actual pinned PR9/Gao source.
The stronger estimate concerns centered equal-product differences only.
It requires an independently proved opposite-side **joint** first-label
Gauss target. It is not a per-label high-bin theorem, a free recursive gain,
or an uncentered estimate. Written source-relative c6=.125139 is unchanged.

## Literal character convention

For the ordered C times conjugate-D product, let
xi=product_P chi_P^(i-j) on the active common radical r. With the source
Gauss convention, CRT gives

    G_(xi chi_a conjugate(chi_b))(rab,h)
      =xi(ab) chi_a(rb) conjugate(chi_b(ra))
         G_xi(r,h) G(a,h) conjugate(G(b,-h)).

Thus the first coefficients are
tau_C(a)=tau(a)chi_a(er)xi(a) and
tau_D(b)=tau(b)chi_b(er)conjugate(xi(b)). At a good first common prime,
their exponents are 1+i-j and1-i+j modulo6. This is old D.10's convention
and is independently derived by Gao's SignedReconstruction.tex.

PR9's displayed inverse factor with unchanged G_xi is a repairable
written phase inconsistency. Inverting xi or exchanging sides requires
the entire character/conjugation convention to change consistently.
The current source-relative endpoint's norm bounds admit both correctly
reconstructed signed row classes, with unchanged costs; the new forced
residue gain does depend on the corrected C orientation. No claim about
proof-assistant implementation follows from this written identity repair.

## Forced valuation count and centered return

Let T1 sum the least residues (-1-i+j) mod6 on C-side first active common
primes, and5 on its first mask primes, weighted by log_Z of prime norm.
Let T2 sum the forced second-common residues (-v_P(G_c V)) mod6. Natural
zeros ensure that the two genuine common supports are disjoint. Frozen
scalars that vanish stay zero; artificial terms of the residual projector
do not become genuine common primes or frequency divisors.

Within a fixed outer row presentation and fixed unit/ray sector, an
exceptional frequency has (h')=h0 v^6, with h0 fixed and
N(h0)>=Z^(T1+T2). In the actual enclosing ball
N(h')<=Z^(m'+delta2), the count is

    #h' << Z^((m'+delta2-T1-T2)/6+o(1)),

and it is empty if the fixed initial norm exceeds that ball. Do not add
an unjustified1 or identify the enclosing ball width with a possibly
smaller canonical child width. Nonexceptional imports keep their original
width correction.

The all-multiplicity proofs establish

    F2_sharp >= b2,
    F1_sharp+S >= c+w-3sigma-5delta1/6,
    S=c+d-2p-R-Bc-Bd >=0.

For example, the four F2 local values are i+ceil(i/6), i+floor(i/6),
7k-1 when i=6k, and i+k-1 for i>j0=6k. Each is at least its actual
b2 value. These are proofs for every multiplicity, not finite tests.

The centered equal-product input has each original plain length at least
L=M/4. Its two rectangles have identical whole-product characters,
natural masks and norm powers. Set x=min(c2,d2) and r_*=(L-c-w-x)_+.
The leading lattice term cancels. Both projectors and extraction scalars
are retained, with their exact cost bounded using

    t_- -r1-r2-(r_*-r1)_+
      =(t_--r2)-max(r_*,r1) <= omega2-r_*.

Since b2>=x, this yields F1_sharp+F2_sharp+r_*+S>=M/4-loss.
The refined exceptional excess is therefore at most
A-13M/12+S+loss, alongside the old A-M+loss bound. Pair the better
joint bound with the independently established opposite-side target.
The original first-label Cauchy outside exponent M-S/2 gives

    M-S/2+(A-M+loss)/2+min(0,S-M/12)/2
      <= M-M/24+(A-M+loss)/2.

S is spent exactly once. Terms with both sides exceptional may use the
refinement on one side and the full target on the other. This describes
a positive Cauchy upper bound, not an orthogonal decomposition of the
original signed row norm.

The actual physical main retains loss4a and its radius
K_main=K0+(d-c)_++6a+omega, density ell=a. Extracted errors retain
loss9a, their original radius, squared extraction coefficients, normalized
prime average and phases including sixth-power punctures. Accordingly
the main/error parent exponents gain M/24 with their old4a/9a costs.
The first zero frequency, added zero Gauss row and genuine second diagonal
are separate; none obtains a new saving here.

## Why this does not raise c by itself

The unchanged low/high assembly permits a nonexceptional sector with
both common supports empty, all their widths zero, and s=t=1. It need
not attain the upper estimates or contain a particular high zero to be
a required sector of the proof. Its main values remain M'=M-6a,
Delta=a and W=M-6a. At q0=17/25, rho0=103/273 the old reserves are

    low  = (7/75)a-(34/225)g,
    high = (170/273)M-(17/25)A-(249/91)a.

Low>=0 still requires a>=(34/21)g. Eliminating a leaves the original
constraint even if every exceptional contribution were zero. A positive
nonexceptional/nonexceptional term cannot be reduced by subtracting an
exceptional reserve. Thus this is a useful restricted theorem and an
exact obstruction within the present assembly, not a full-norm gain.

A separate low-bin saving tau would permit reducing a by75tau/7 and
improve the high reserve by (249/91)(75tau/7). A new high density or a
changed actual amplifier radius/density relation could also change the
tradeoff. These are genuine transfer targets; the valuation count supplies
none of them. The active slot-weighted density proposal is a separate
candidate requiring its own full proof and independent validation.

The pinned source imports, positive-slot uniformity, finite dictionary,
root-definition binding and old-c0 kernel status remain distinct. No
formalization, new c or external record admission is claimed.

## 7. Actual diagonal and a sharp obstruction to termwise absolute pricing

For every fixed q, the squarefree unit count satisfies

       Q_q(Y)=sum_(n<=Y)mu(n)^2 1_((n,q)=1)
             =d_q Y+O_q(sqrt Y),
       d_q=(1/zeta(2)) product_(p|q)(1+1/p)^(-1)>0.       (7.1)

This follows elementarily from mu(n)^2=sum_(d^2|n)mu(d): restrict
(d,q)=1, count the remaining integers coprime to q with error O_q(1),
and bound the d>sqrt Y tail of the absolutely convergent sum d^(-2).
Partial summation gives

 sum_n |a(n)|^2 exp(-2n/x^b)=d_q x^b/2+O_q(x^(b/2)).

The full source energy is the absolutely convergent double series

       E_b,chi(X)=sum_(n,m) a(n)conjugate(a(m)) K_X(n,m),
       K_X(n,m)=integral_1^2
         exp(-(n+m)/(X^b*u^b)) exp(-i(n-m)/(X*u)) du/u.   (7.2)

Absolute Fubini is licensed by the damping and |a|<=1. Its actual
diagonal contribution is therefore

       d_q(2^b-1)X^b/(2b)+O_q(X^(b/2)).                 (7.3)

For b=3/2 this is the target scale of the conditional quarter energy,
with every character-zero loss included in d_q. It is NOT a lower
bound for E: off-diagonal terms can cancel a diagonal contribution.

There is nevertheless an unconditional lower bound for the TERMWISE
ABSOLUTE off-diagonal price, using the actual coefficients, not an
arbitrary sequence. For every fixed b>1 and ordinary chi,

       sum_(n!=m)|a(n)a(m)K_X(n,m)| >>_(q,b) X^(b+1).   (7.4)

To prove it, set N=X^b and partition the integer interval [N,2N] into
consecutive bins of length at most H=floor(X/4). By (7.1), the total
number A of squarefree units there is d_q N+O_q(sqrt N+1). If there
are B=O(N/H+1) bins and A_j such integers in bin j, Cauchy gives
sum_j A_j^2>=A^2/B >>_q NH. Subtract the A diagonal pairs; since
H tends to infinity, there are still >>_q NH ordered distinct pairs.
For each, |n-m|<=X/4 and n+m<=4X^b, whence

       Re K_X(n,m)>=exp(-4)cos(1/4)log 2>0.

At squarefree units |a(n)a(m)|=1. Summing only these pairs proves
(7.4), with the full remaining infinite sum nonnegative after absolute
values. No assertion about the signs of mu(n)mu(m) is made.

At b=3/2 this price is at least X^(5/2), matching the exponent of the
coarse energy certificate. Thus any proof that prices the actual
near-diagonal pairs separately by absolute value cannot reach even
the first-gain energy exponent below 1.7497080728. This is stronger
than identifying a diagonal heuristic and narrower than excluding
signed dispersion: it explicitly leaves collective cancellation among
these actual squarefree pairs eligible. Natural character zeros do
not evade the obstruction for ANY fixed ordinary character.

The pointwise estimate (4.1) still uses the actual mu convolution law;
(7.4) concerns a different, absolute Gram price and is not claimed
to prove sharpness of the true source magnitude. In particular this
pass is not solely a new norm counterexample: it supplies the paid
moving-source return and an actual arithmetic power saving, then
identifies exactly why its coarse method stops short.
title: 7. Actual diagonal and a sharp obstruction to termwise absolute pricing

## R42.5. The inherited beta norm has a legitimate all-height source

D26 assumes ||U_eta,2||_beta<infinity, beta=.8749, strictly above .874864. This follows from the accepted source-relative fixed-family zero-free statement with a positive buffer, but requires more than a bare assertion that 1/L is holomorphic. The needed argument is already proved in W39 review R39-C/R39-E, `[restricted mathematical source]`.

For completeness, periodic residue weights on the Eisenstein lattice give sum_(Na<=T)eta(a)=c_eta T+O_eta(sqrt T+1), after dividing by the six units and retaining the finite mask. The principal c_eta is positive and the nonprincipal mean is zero. Abel summation gives meromorphic continuation and polynomial upper growth on each fixed strip Re s>1/2, regularizing a principal L by s-1. The regularized function is nonzero on Re s>.874864. At centers 2+it, Euler products bound its logarithm by O(log(2+|t|)). Choose an outer disk wholly to the right of the accepted boundary and an inner disk reaching the fixed line beta. The elementary positive-real-part/logarithm estimate (or Borel--Caratheodory in precisely these disks) bounds the entire inner logarithm by C log(2+|t|). Thus 1/L has polynomial growth uniformly on beta<=Re s<=2, at every height. The principal regularization is undone explicitly.

Shifting the inverse Mellin integral from2 to beta now has vanishing horizontal sides because exp(-t^2) dominates that polynomial. It gives U_eta,2(x)=O_eta,beta(x^beta) for x>=1; the direct Gaussian left tail pays x<=1. These are fixed-target constants. No Phragmen--Lindelof assumption, new reciprocal theorem, conductor-uniform estimate, or attained zero supremum is required. The result is calibrated to the accepted written premise, whose new kernels remain pending.

statement:
## 1. Discovery before selection

Three distinct mechanisms were compared before the full index read.

1. A larger finite mean-zero compensator bank could couple the terminal
   prime/cofactor cells. Its immediate difficulty is algebraic: if a
   convolution compensator v has v(1)=1, then (v-v*chi)(r)=-chi(r)
   for every prime r, independently of v(r). Simply adding normalized
   compensators therefore does not remove the prime cofactor source.
   A vanishing first coefficient only moves the first nonzero source.
   This is a test of finite compensators, not a no-go for all banks.
2. Exact prime extraction or higher completion could redistribute the
   long Mobius variable before absolute values. Primary work on Ramare
   identities and short intervals keeps a genuine restricted cofactor,
   prime-square correction and extraction error. The available stated
   theorems supply logarithmic savings; they cannot be substituted for
   the desired power. A paid source-specific extraction remains viable.
3. Change the *geometry of completion*, not its scalar parameters.
   The accepted proof uses a rectangular cutoff chosen for the worst
   physical product M. A cutoff depending on the physical integer n
   can retain the discrete Fourier gap separately on every row. The
   key issue is whether the moving cutoff still leaves an interval in
   each cofactor row and whether the short terms remain affordable.
   Both appear to hold for the explicit decreasing phase surface below.

Selected mechanism3: develop a nonrectangular exact completion, then
test a signed cutoff bank rather than treating the resulting region
reduction as an arithmetic saving. Potential conditional reach remains
near gains,1/6,1/4 (and fixed gamma>1/2 with the earlier finite-shift return).

The complete current attempt index was read after this comparison.
Relevant ancestry is R35 completion, G140-G142 nonlinear tail/return,
and the full independently reviewed G152-G154 asymmetric completion.
The latter review was read in full. No novelty is claimed for those
identities or for a mere equivalent-norm restatement. The proposed new
piece is the uniformly paid curved cutoff, allowing a longer actual
Mobius prefix in the difficult n~X region.

statement:
## 3. Development A: independent verification and its strongest objection

### A.1 Finite signed inverse and exact collar

For t>=1,y>=1, define R(t,y)=sum_(n<=t,P^-(n)>y)a(n), with P^-(1)=infinity. Unique least-prime factorization of each nonzero squarefree term gives

    R(t,y)=1-sum_(y<p<=t) chi(p) R(t/p,p).                  (R1)

The strict next-prime threshold removes repeated primes, and ramified prime edges have zero weight. R(t,y)=1 when t<=y. For any approximate state F on the finite descendant set, put

    Delta(t,y)=F(t,y)-1+sum_(y<p<=t)chi(p)F(t/p,p).

Then E=F-R satisfies (I+T)E=Delta. T is nilpotent on that finite graph: along a path primes strictly increase and their product is at most the root x. Expanding the finite inverse yields

    E(x,1)=sum_(d<=x)mu(d)chi(d)Delta(x/d,P^+(d)), P^+(1)=1.  (R2)

Each squarefree product corresponds to exactly one increasing path; all its partial products are admissible. This establishes signs, endpoints, n=1 and every natural zero. It is a signed sum across all depths.

For fixed r>=1 the collar t<=y^r is descendant-closed. Exact values there force Delta=0; conversely zero collar defects and terminal induction force exact values. At r>1 those exact values include shorter products and are not identically1.

On the distinct real-coordinate states (x/d,P^+(d)), the sup-norm to scalar norm for arbitrary independently bounded complex defects outside this collar is EXACTLY

    N_(r,q)(x)=#{d<=x: mu(d)!=0,(d,q)=1,d P^+(d)^r<x}.      (R3)

Triangle inequality proves the upper bound. Assigning the conjugate unit phase of mu(d)chi(d) at each counted state attains it, and finite back substitution realizes those defects by an F. The assignment may depend on x; it is not a single actual arithmetic approximation with that error, nor a lower bound for M_chi. Distinct real t coordinates are crucial.

### A.2 Fixed-depth exponent and what it actually rules out

At fixed positive depth k, P^+(d)>=d^(1/k), so d P^+(d)^r<x implies d<x^(k/(k+r)). Conversely choose k distinct unramified primes in (Y,2Y], Y=x^(1/(k+r))/4; their products satisfy the strict inequality. Ordinary prime supply gives

    c_(k,r,q) x^(k/(k+r))/(log x)^k
       <= N_(k,r,q)(x) <= x^(k/(k+r)).                     (R4)

I checked the primary external input: [Johnston--Yang, arXiv:2204.01980v2, Corollary1.3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2204.01980), PDF page2, version dated 20 April2022. Its prime-counting estimate implies the ordinary asymptotic needed for a fixed dyadic prime interval. No explicit onset, sharp numerical constant or fixed zero-free strip from that paper is imported.

Because (R4) holds for every FIXED k and N_(r,q)(x)<=x, its logarithmic exponent is1 for every fixed r. Thus the UNMERGED independent local-error certificate cannot imply an output exponent below1, even after exact fixed-depth terminal collars. It does not forbid correlated errors, increasing r with its paid collar complexity, or signed state coalescence.

For r=1, depths0 throughK cost at most (K+1)||Delta||_infinity x^(K/(K+1)). Depths<=6 have exponent6/7; depth7 has7/8. Relative to current theta7=.874860 their gap is .000140. This is a feature of this particular worst-case norm, not an explanation of the PR9/Gao endpoint or a universal1/8 barrier. At target5/6 depths<=5 are paid, and at3/4 depths<=3; all deeper signed paths still require control.

The real-state approximation F0(t,y)=1_(t<=y) has actual nonterminal defect

    Delta0(t,y)=-1+sum_(y<p<=t,p^2>=t)chi(p).

For principal q=1,y=1 this is asymptotic to t/log t, so it does not satisfy a bounded-defect premise. The integer-invariant variant f0(m,y)=1_(m<=y) instead has the SHARP condition p(p+1)>m, because floor(m/p)<=p. It still has a macroscopic principal prime defect. Thus correcting the floor invariant does not rescue this particular crude approximation, while its effect on the GENERAL error norm remains essential.

### A.3 Merging integer states changes the operator norm

For a floor-invariant F, floor(t/p)=floor(floor(t)/p). At an integer root N, group (R2) by m=floor(N/d), p=P^+(d). For d>1 write d=pu with P^+(u)<p. The exact fibre coefficient is

    C_(N,chi)(m,p)
      =-chi(p) sum_(N/[p(m+1)]<u<=N/(pm), P^+(u)<p)
                         mu(u)chi(u).                     (R5)

The lower endpoint is STRICT, upper inclusive, u=1 is retained and there is no imposed independence between its terms. Consequently

    E(N,1)=Delta(N,1)+sum_(p,m) C_(N,chi)(m,p)Delta(m,p).   (R6)

For integer r>=1 and exact integer collar m<=p^r, the exact independent-state norm, N>1, is

    B_(r,chi)(N)=1+sum_(p,m>p^r)|C_(N,chi)(m,p)|.         (R7)

Triangular back substitution realizes arbitrary merged defects; conjugate phases attain (R7). The integer collar can be larger than the corresponding real collar, since floor(t)<=p^r allows t<p^r+1. The surviving integer states are nevertheless a subset of the real noncollar states, so B<=N_(r,q) is valid. An exponent-one LOWER bound cannot pass through this grouping.

The concrete collision is correct. At N=20196,m=18,p=17, the smooth squarefree u in the interval (20196/(17*19),66] are exactly65 and66. Their Mobius values are+1,-1. Equivalently d=1105 and1122 have signs-1,+1 and the same integer state outside the r=1 collar. Their principal coefficient cancels to0. With the real character modulo4 it is-1, and with chi(2)=i modulo5 it is i. My independent exact checks verify all three. The example proves that cross-depth coalescence is real; it supplies no common-character bound.

This correction is part of the accepted result, not an optional caveat. A depth-tagged implementation can destroy the cancellation it is supposed to exploit. No new lower exponent or improved upper exponent for (R7) is proved.

### A.4 Remaining sufficient input and credit

For each x and fixed chi, produce an explicit approximate F with small root value and bound the COMPLETE (R2), or its floor-invariant (R6), by x^(gamma+epsilon) at every scale. Their exact difference then gives (R0). If Delta is uniformly bounded with r=1, near the current boundary one may remove depths<=6 at O(x^(6/7)); the entire signed depth>=7 complement remains. That is a defect expansion, not an already paid sector of the original arithmetic sum.

The least-prime recurrence and finite triangular inverse are classical. U-FUGACITY/RN, W36 and G81 already supply signed renewal and complete-source obligations. Relative to the inspected record, W49 adds the explicit collar-dependent k/(k+r) price and its necessary real/integer-state distinction, including the concrete cancellation. G81's 2^r arbitrary-history linear-state statement does not already supply (R7), and conversely (R3) does not refute G81's permitted source-specific closures.

statement:
## 2. Theorem H: whole short-coefficient / periodic-cofactor source

Fix a bounded Q-periodic sequence b of mean zero, a fixed0<=alpha0<1, X>=2 and real1<=D<=X^alpha0. Let A_m be arbitrary complex coefficients fixed before x. If |A_m|<=A, define the absolutely convergent complete source

 H_D(x)=sum_(1<=m<=D) A_m sum_(l>=1)b(l)f_x(ml).

Then, with a fixed power of the logarithm (power4 is more than sufficient),

 ||H_D||_1+||H_D||_2
   <<_(Q,alpha0,||b||inf) A [D+X^(3/4)] log^4(2X).                (H)

For any divisor-bounded family |A_m|<<_eta m^eta for every eta>0, this gives

 ||H_D||_(1,2) <<_epsilon X^epsilon[D+X^(3/4)].                   (H')

Constants include the family constants and fixed data. Choose eta after epsilon. There is no growing-period, live-x coefficient or arbitrary cofactor/output-mask license. All integer endpoints in m<=D are exact. A may depend on X; it is explicitly charged.

### 2.1 An exact smooth partition, not a replacement cutoff

Choose a fixed smooth nonincreasing phi on[0,infinity), phi=1 on[0,1], phi=0 on[2,infinity). For every positive n,

 1=phi(n/X)+sum_(j>=0) w(n/(2^j X)), w(t)=phi(t/2)-phi(t).        (3)

Here w is smooth, supported in[1,4], and nonnegative. Every overlap/transition is retained with its exact weight. The identity telescopes; for each n only boundedly many high terms are nonzero. Damping permits interchanging the complete sums. No original sharp cutoff is approximated by (3).

For the low part, expand b(l)=sum_(j=1)^(Q-1) beta_j exp(2pi i jl/Q). Its zero coefficient vanishes. On ml<=2X (and the extra last integer increment, lying below3X) the nonlinear phase increment in l is O(m/X), uniformly for x in[X,2X]. Since m<=X^alpha0, this is <1/(4Q) for all sufficiently large X. Each nonzero Fourier mode has monotone derivative separated from every integer by at least1/(2Q). Discrete first-derivative summation gives O_Q(1) for every prefix; Abel summation with phi(ml/X)exp(-ml/x^(3/2)), of bounded total variation, preserves that bound. Summing |A_m| gives O(AD). The finitely bounded initial-X range enters the fixed constant.

### 2.2 Complete Poisson expansion and every nonstationary frequency

Fix a high output scale N=2^j X and a row block I_M=[M,2M) intersect[1,D], with dyadic M. Put T=(N/X)^6>=1 and define

 beta_h=Q^(-1)sum_(r mod Q)b(r)exp(-2pi i hr/Q), h in Z.

It is periodic, |beta_h|<=||b||inf and beta_h=0 for h divisible by Q. Poisson on the smooth compactly supported positive-variable function, extended by zero, gives exactly

 sum_l b(l)w(ml/N)f_x(ml)
   =(1/m)sum_(h in Z) beta_h I_(h/m)(x),
 I_r(x)=integral_0^infinity w(n/N)exp(-n/x^(3/2))
              exp(i[2pi r n/Q-(n/x)^6])dn.                       (4)

This includes both signs and every integer alias, not just one period. The h=0 term is exactly zero. For r>0 there is one positive critical point,

 n_r(x)=(pi r/(3Q))^(1/5)x^(6/5),
 Phi_r(n_r)=kappa_Q r^(6/5)x^(6/5),
 kappa_Q=5(pi/(3Q))^(6/5), Phi_r''(n_r)=-30n_r^4/x^6.            (5)

Choose fixed positive c_Q,C_Q so that r in R_N=[c_Q T/N,C_Q T/N] includes every critical point that can meet[1,4]N for every x in[X,2X], and leaves a fixed derivative gap outside it. One explicit choice is c_Q=3Q/(128pi), C_Q=6Q*4^5/pi. This frequency range is chosen BEFORE x and BEFORE individual live labels. In rescaled variable n=Nt, the positive near phases form a compact smooth family with one nondegenerate stationary point in a fixed positive compact interval. The derivative of order2 at that point is bounded away from zero. All derivatives of the damped amplitude of any fixed needed order are O(exp(-cN/X^(3/2))), after absorbing fixed polynomial factors.

The uniform first stationary term is therefore

 I_r(x)=Z_r(x)exp(i kappa_Q r^(6/5)x^(6/5)-i pi/4)
            +O_Q((N/T)exp(-cN/X^(3/2))), r in R_N,              (6)
 Z_r(x)=sqrt(pi/15) x^3 n_r(x)^(-2)
                     w(n_r(x)/N)exp(-n_r(x)/x^(3/2)).

The deliberately weak O(T^-1) remainder is sufficient. To justify its uniformity, localize near the unique critical point with one fixed-width smooth partition; the Morse change y=sgn(t-t0)sqrt(|Phi(t)-Phi(t0)|/T) has uniformly bounded inverse derivatives on this compact family. The Gaussian/Fresnel leading integral gives (6); subtract its value at zero and integrate the residual, or use one further Taylor term, to get O(T^-1). Away from that neighborhood two integrations by parts suffice. When t0 is outside the support of w the main coefficient is zero; its approach to the smooth support edge is covered by the same uniform estimate. No sharp edge is present. This is the standard one-dimensional nondegenerate stationary-phase calculation, with all varying parameters restricted as stated.

For completeness, let H_m=mT/N. The number of positive near aliases is O(1+H_m). If any such integer h exists, H_m>=c>0, so their combined remainder after the prefactor1/m is

 O((N/(mT))(1+H_m)exp(-cN/X^(3/2)))=O(exp(-cN/X^(3/2))).         (7)

Outside R_N, negative and small positive aliases with |h|=O(H_m) have derivative of size T after n-scaling. Two integrations by parts give O((N/m)T^-2) per alias, with damping. There are O(H_m) such nonzero integers when present, hence total O(T^-1). For |h|>C H_m the derivative has size |h|N/m; two integrations by parts give O((m/N)h^-2). Its entire two-sided tail is O(T^-1) if H_m>=c, and O(m/N) if H_m<c. Since m<=X^alpha0 and N>=X, all these costs are O(1), with damping retained. Enlarging fixed constants covers intermediate finitely sized ranges. Thus the whole transformed row equals the stationary bank in (6) plus a uniform damped O(1) error. After summing the block, the error is O(AM exp(-cN/X^(3/2))). There is no unpaid frequency tail or endpoint.

### 2.3 Exact coincident aliases and their coefficient energy

For a near alias write h/m=u/v in lowest terms, u,v positive and coprime. Then m=vj,h=uj. Crucially the ENTIRE function Z_(h/m)(x), including its support and damping, depends only on u/v,N,x. The ONLY separate original-m factor is1/m in (4). Thus define the x-independent grouped coefficient

 C_(u/v)=sum_(j>=1: vj in I_M) A_(vj) beta_(uj)/(vj).             (8)

The complete stationary bank is exactly

 sum_(r=u/v in R_N, v<=2M) C_r Z_r(x)
                       exp(i kappa_Q r^(6/5)x^(6/5)-i pi/4).   (9)

Truncation m<=D, skipped aliases beta_h=0, all coincidences and arbitrary coefficient phases stay in (8). There is no averaging or assumption that beta_(uj) is constant. Since j lies in a factor2 interval, |C_(u/v)|<<A||b||inf/v. Also u>=1 and r<=C_Q T/N force v>=N/(C_Q T). Counting possible positive numerators and then dropping coprimality only in an upper bound gives

 sum_r |C_r|^2
  << A^2||b||inf^2 sum_(max(1,N/(C_Q T))<=v<=2M)
                     [vT/N+1]/v^2
  << A^2||b||inf^2 (T/N)log(2M).                              (10)

The lower denominator cutoff is essential. Without it the +1 term would falsely leave N^2/T in the final energy. The sum v^-2 from that cutoff is O(min(1,T/N)), which is <=O(T/N) in both regimes. If the denominator range is empty there is no main bank.

### 2.4 Full real-shell energy, moving amplitude and all cross terms

Write x=Xz,1<=z<=2. For j=0,1,

 |d^j/dz^j Z_r(Xz)| << (N/sqrt(T))exp(-cN/X^(3/2)), r in R_N.    (11)

Indeed n_r(Xz)~N where w or its derivative is nonzero, dn_r/dz=(6/5)n_r/z, and all damping derivatives are fixed polynomials in N/X^(3/2), absorbed by a weaker exponential. This proves the required variation bound after the exact separation (8); no m-dependent amplitude has been pulled through a sum.

For two distinct r,s in R_N, the derivative in z of their phase difference has magnitude comparable to N|r-s|, because

 X^(6/5)(T/N)^(1/5)=N.

Its second derivative is a bounded multiple of its first. One integration by parts, including BOTH actual shell endpoints z=1,2, yields

 |integral_X^(2X) Z_r(x)conjugate(Z_s(x))
       exp(i kappa_Q(r^(6/5)-s^(6/5))x^(6/5)) dx/x|
 << (N^2/T)exp(-cN/X^(3/2)) min(1,1/[N|r-s|]).                  (12)

On the exact diagonal use the same scale with the minimum1. The spacing of distinct reduced fractions with v<=2M is at least1/(4M^2). If J is their number, ordering them therefore gives a complete absolute kernel row sum

 <<1+(M^2/N)log(2+J), J<<_Q M+M^2 T/N.                         (13)

Use 2|C_r C_s|<=|C_r|^2+|C_s|^2 on the COMPLETE pair sum, with both orientations and the diagonal. Combining (10)-(13), and log(2+J)<<_Q log(2N) for N>=X>=2,M<=X, proves

 ||stationary bank||_2^2
   << A^2 exp(-cN/X^(3/2))[N+M^2]log^2(2N).                   (14)

Adding the full error (7) by the norm triangle gives the same bound for the entire (M,N) block, with constants enlarged. No signed-subset norm comparison is used.

### 2.5 Summing all blocks and proving H

Sum (14) in norm over dyadic M<=D and N=2^j X, retaining every block in (3). The M contributions sum geometrically to O(D) for each N; their damping sum contributes O(log(2X)). The sqrt(N) contributions sum with actual damping to O(X^(3/4)log(2X)), multiplied by at most O(log(2D)) row blocks. The far infinite N tail converges exponentially; no polynomial truncation is imposed. The low part costs O(AD). Fixed logarithmic powers are bounded by log^4(2X). Finite-measure Cauchy gives L1 from L2. This proves H and H'. All low/high, inter-row and inter-block interactions are paid by norm inequalities after each whole source estimate.

# [private research revision]: paid renewal localization and exact certificate boundaries

Accept G116-G118 at the scopes below, from the complete
[W52 author](wild52/report.md) and [independent review](wild52-review/report.md).
The [manifest](retention-manifest.json) preserves32 original files, including
all30 seeds, immutable pools/draws, preparation, reports/checks and original
problem/recipe. One host-local claim snapshot remains at its original local
path, bound by hash; its contents are not copied into Git. The historical
c9 seeds and c10 reports remain unchanged. Current c11=.1251459636 is
recalibrated only through the proved common-gamma return. No new c follows.

F0/analytic ancestry, positive-slot uniformity and external definition/import/
admission remain OPEN. These results prove no native-H or Gaussian saving,
Hecke/growing-conductor extension, formalization or public record.

## 1. G116: a complete paid complement for integer renewal

Fix an ordinary Dirichlet character chi modulo q, retaining natural zeros.
Let P^-(1)=infinity and P^+(1)=1. The inherited G92 source is

    R(m,p)=sum_(n<=m,P^-(n)>p)mu(n)chi(n)
          =1-sum_(p<ell<=m,ell prime)chi(ell)R(floor(m/ell),ell).

For a floor-invariant approximation F define its ACTUAL defect

    Delta(m,p)=F(m,p)-1
        +sum_(p<ell<=m)chi(ell)F(floor(m/ell),ell).

Assume F=R on the exact collar m<=p^r, fixed integer r>=1. The collar is
descendant-closed, so Delta=0 there; for r>1 its value is generally not1.
Finite triangular inversion, with floors composed before grouping, gives

    F(N,1)-M_chi(N)=Delta(N,1)+sum_(p,m>p^r)C_N(m,p)Delta(m,p),
    C_N(m,p)=-chi(p)
      sum_(N/[p(m+1)]<u<=N/(pm),P^+(u)<p)mu(u)chi(u).

Signs, nonunit zeros, root term and half-open endpoints are literal. This
identity and the N=20196 cancellation are inherited G92, not new credit.

If distinct integers u<v lie in the same interval, then
mv<=N/p<(m+1)u, whence m(v-u)<u and u>m. Thus a fiber containing a
cofactor u<=m is a SINGLETON, even before smoothness/squarefree/zero masks.
No fiber mixes short and long cofactors.

For each active short path d=pu, m=floor(N/d)>p^r and u<=m give
pu^2<=N and p^(r+1)u<N. Dropping restrictions only in the positive count,

    S_r(N)<=sum_(j>=2)min(sqrt(N/j),N/j^(r+1))
          <=(4+1/r)N^alpha_r, alpha_r=(r+1)/(2r+1).

Split at J=ceil(N^(1/(2r+1))). The initial part is at most2sqrt(NJ)
and the tail at most N/(rJ^r); the stated constant covers N>=1. On q-units
the singleton coefficient has absolute value1. If D_N bounds EVERY active
prime-state defect, the full short contribution costs at most D_N S_r(N).
This is an all-depth price, not a fixed-depth truncation.

Freeze Y_N=(log(2N))^A at the ROOT, A>1. Remove the short fibers first;
the remaining p<=Y_N paths are squarefree Y_N-smooth integers d<=N.
For0<sigma<1 their total absolute coefficient mass is at most

    Psi_sf(N,Y)<=N^sigma product_(p<=Y)(1+p^-sigma)
        <=N^sigma exp(1+Y^(1-sigma)/(1-sigma)).

Choose sigma just above1-1/A. Then A(1-sigma)<1, giving for every epsilon
Psi_sf(N,Y_N)<<N^(1-1/A+epsilon). The onset may be large; this is not a
small finite-N constant. The finite bound remains available.

All remaining fibers satisfy

    Y_N<p<N^(1/(2r+1)), p^r<m<sqrt(N/p), u>m,
    P^+(u)<p, omega(u)>=r+1.

Indeed N>=pum>pm^2>p^(2r+1), and a squarefree u with at most r primes
below p would be<p^r. In particular all larger primes have already been
paid. Let H_F be the ENTIRE signed C_N Delta sum over this hard region.
The exact disjoint partition is

    F(N,1)-M_chi(N)=Delta(N,1)+E_short+E_small+H_F,
    |E_short|+|E_small|
      <=D_N[(4+1/r)N^alpha_r+Psi_sf(N,Y_N)].

There is no absolute value inside H_F and no independence of defects.
The independent review supplies the useful weaker conditional contract:
for fixed d>=0, common gamma<1, every fixed chi/every epsilon/all large N,

    D_N<<N^(d+epsilon),
    d+max(alpha_r,1-1/A)<gamma,
    |F(N,1)|+|Delta(N,1)|+|H_F(N)|<<N^(gamma+epsilon).

Splitting epsilon among products proves M_chi(x)<<x^(gamma+epsilon) for
all large real x. Root-dependent F is allowed, provided each root uses
one F and its actual defects on the entire reachable system. No consistency
between different roots is required. No such F and hard-region estimate
has been constructed. F=R leaves the unknown Mertens sum at the root;
the terminal-only approximation does not have a free bounded defect.

For r=1,A=3, the paid exponent is2/3. At the CURRENT boundary a first gain
can allow

    d < theta11-2/3 =1561405273/7500000000,
    d+2/3 < gamma < theta11=.8748540364.

Using A=3 instead of A=7 makes a smaller paid small-prime sector and a
larger hard remainder; it is not a gain for an unchanged H_F. At gamma=5/6
with r=1,A=5 one may take d<1/30; at gamma=3/4 with r=1,A=3, d<1/12.
These conditional1/6 and1/4 returns do not establish their premises.

The zero-exclusion bridge is complete: s integral_1^infinity
M_chi(x)x^(-s-1)dx is holomorphic on Re s>gamma, including all compact-set
derivatives after choosing epsilon with room. It equals1/L(s,chi) on
Re s>1; continuation of L times this function=1 excludes every zero in
the half-plane. A principal pole at1 becomes a reciprocal zero, not an
excluded L-zero. Natural imprimitive factors and all heights remain.
Constants may depend on each fixed ordinary chi; no Hecke extension follows.

G112's principal full merged norm exponent1 is compatible with this result:
G116 pays restricted sectors, leaving the whole signed hard-region
correlation. It neither disproves the principal norm result nor obtains a
natural-residual lower bound from it.

## 2. G117: two precisely scoped certificate obstructions

For squarefree q-units n<=N, put a_n=mu(n)chi(n). All k! orderings of its
k prime factors have the SAME arithmetic sign/phase. The map summing a
word fiber to n has norm sqrt(k!), while its minimum-norm right inverse
averages with1/k!. Its generic Cauchy price is

    sqrt(sum_n1/omega(n)!) sqrt(sum_n omega(n)!) >= #S.

More generally, for orthogonal integer fibers H_n with
<u_n,v_n>=1 (linear first slot), U=sum a_nu_n and V=sum v_n have
<U,V>=M_chi(N), but ||U||||V||>=sum||u_n||||v_n||>=#S.
The square-divisor identity gives

    #S=kappa_q N+O_q(sqrt N),
    kappa_q=(phi(q)/q) product_(p not dividing q)(1-p^-2)>0.

This is a floor on a PRODUCT-OF-NORMS certificate, not on M_chi. Arbitrary
geometry within fibers and exact diagonal rescaling cannot remove it;
correlations between different integers or a source-specific scalar estimate
remain outside the obstruction. Ordered-word/readout ancestry is retained.

For B_gamma, all f=0 below1 with norm sup_x x^-gamma|f(x)|, the dilation
T_c f(x)=sum_(n<=x)c(n)f(x/n) has extended norm
sum_n|c(n)|n^-gamma. Triangle gives the upper bound and alignment on
distinct x/n attains each finite prefix. This also holds on the all-scale
FLOOR-INVARIANT space: for fixed K take X>K(K+1), so each floor(X/n),n<=K,
is a singleton fiber among ALL n'<=X. Assign its aligning value and let
X tend to infinity. This does not identify one finite-X merged norm with
an unmerged price.

For any fixed finitely supported complex b, set r=delta-b*chi. If b(1)=0,
r(1)=1 implies ||T_r||>=1. Otherwise r(p)=-b(1)chi(p) for every
unramified prime beyond its support, and sum_p p^-gamma diverges for
0<gamma<=1. Divergence follows from the elementary Euler-product/harmonic
sum argument at gamma=1; finitely many ramified omissions do not matter.
Thus this full norm cannot certify a strict contraction.

Were ||T_r||<1 possible, the return would be legitimate:
T_chi M=1 gives M=T_b1+T_rM. The Banach solution is identified with actual
M by induction on integer intervals, since b(1)!=0 and all other x/n<x;
one need not assume M initially belongs to B_gamma. The premise fails,
not that identification. Infinite/moving preconditioners with fully paid
tails, arithmetic invariant spaces and signed norms remain eligible.

## 3. G118: finite-prefix and all-layer audits

The protected audit25 names an exact finite relaxation. Fix principal
chi0 mod q, K, and w_q(n)=mu(n)^2 1_((n,q)=1). Impose the true first K
inverse coefficients, all squareful/ramified zeros, real |b(n)|<=1, and
a fixed consistent old summatory envelope Cx^beta. For
1/2<gamma<sigma<beta<1 choose T>=K with |M_chi0(K)|<=CT^beta/2,
nonzero real t, and0<lambda<=min(1,(C sigma/2)T^(beta-sigma)). Set

    b(n)=mu(n)chi0(n) for n<=K; b(n)=0 for K<n<=T;
    b(n)=lambda w_q(n)n^(sigma-1)cos(t log n) for n>T.

Every finite convolution equation up to K and every stated zero mask
holds. For x>=T, the absolute tail is at most(lambda/sigma)x^sigma,
so the fixed Cx^beta envelope survives; the known prefix and middle
interval do also. T and |t| can be arbitrarily large.

Yet D_q(z)=sum_n w_q(n)n^-z has continuation

    D_q(z)=kappa_q z/(z-1)
       +z integral_1^infinity[sum_(n<=x)w_q(n)-kappa_q x]x^(-z-1)dx

on Re z>1/2. The error is holomorphic and the pole at1 has residue kappa_q.
The constructed series B(s) is a finite entire correction plus
(lambda/2)[D_q(s+1-sigma-it)+D_q(s+1-sigma+it)]. It has genuine poles
sigma+it and sigma-it, each residue lambda kappa_q/2. These are synthetic
completion poles, NOT L-zeros. The sequence violates global convolution
and multiplicativity: at a prime beyond T the convolution residual is
1+b(p)!=0. The result rejects only sufficiency of the stated finite
relaxation; full arithmetic or proved all-height tail constraints may repair it.

The uniform audit09 retains every squarefree layer and p-free cofactor.
Let B_k(X)=sum_(n<=X,omega(n)=k)mu(n)chi(n). Inserting one prime gives

    k B_k(X)=-sum_(p<=X)chi(p) B_(k-1)^(p)(X/p).

Each k-factor squarefree n has exactly k parents. Summing all layers yields

    M_chi(X)=1-sum_(p<=X)chi(p)
       sum_(m<=X/p,p not dividing m)mu(m)chi(m)/(omega(m)+1)
      =1-sum_(p<=X)chi(p) integral_0^1 G_(p,X)(t)dt,
    G_(p,X)(t)=sum_(m<=X/p,p not dividing m)mu(m)chi(m)t^omega(m).

All degrees, product caps, endpoints and natural zeros remain. The COMPLETE
coefficientwise absolute edge price is exactly the number of squarefree
q-units2<=n<=X: each n has k edges of weight1/k. It is
kappa_q X+O_q(sqrt X)-1, not a bound below for the signed flux. Factorial
layer rescaling requires the inverse factorial readout and does not remove
that price. Signed correlations between cofactor responses remain open.

For any proposed Gtilde define Atilde by replacing G in that root formula
and E by the FULL signed difference. Then M=Atilde+E exactly. Bounding
BOTH complete contractions by X^(gamma+epsilon), with the usual every-
character/every-epsilon/all-large-X quantifiers, gives the same Mellin return.
Root-dependent approximations must return to this fixed source before
continuation. Selected primes, central degrees or separate variances do not
pay the full error.

The separate logarithmic identity also retains every prime power:

    M_chi(X)log X=integral_1^X M_chi(t)dt/t
       -sum_(p^j<=X,j>=1)chi(p)^j log p M_chi(X/p^j).

It follows coefficientwise from the full log-derivative convolution.
Prime powers restore squareful cancellations; deleting them would not be
the p-free insertion identity above. Neither identity supplies a contraction.

## 4. Selection, evidence and remaining work

Author first tests01/02/27/14/30/22; developments27/02/01. Independent
protected25/uniform09 audits use the frozen pre-outcome orders. All other
22 cards remain untested. Pools contain every eligible card under literal
p<.10 and p<.01 across groups; all original entropy and exclusions remain.
The critic replayed the three saved draws without redrawing. Subjective
typicality is not probability of success.

The independent exact checks cover12 merged partitions, including complex
and imprimitive characters, nonzero hard contributions and actual collars;
6all-scale floor witnesses;9full flux/prime-power cases;4finite prefixes.
The author retains18 partition cases plus fiber/preconditioner/flatness
screens. Finite Y=3 exercises the partition and is not the asymptotic
log-power cutoff. These checks support identities, not the missing estimates.
Root read both full reports, all three mathematical helpers and sampling
code. No unchanged helper rerun or formal tool occurred.

Card14 failed its raw structure screen because no native determinant-line
object was defined, not because all such objects are impossible. Card30's
independent-disc optimum does not survive as an arithmetic lower bound
after integer merging. Card22 proves only bare q-unit character flatness,
not simplification of native H's phases/projectors. Preserve these boundaries,
all original sources and credits, the29-family/109-child portfolio, near
improvements,1/6 and1/4.

Next: construct an affordable F with actual root and hard-region controls,
or prove a complete signed cofactor-flux estimate. The positive defect budget
is available, but no arbitrary-input norm or synthetic tail substitutes for
these arithmetic requirements.
