## 2. Reconstructing the actual tensor before any conductor estimate

The source is the Eisenstein field with its fixed bad primes, original primary generators, ray resolution and finite unit coefficients. Long variables are the original degree-one good prime ideals pi,pi' in their same-scale N windows, with distinct rational norms. Both orientations of an equal rational norm are excluded by the original screen. Original short sources g,g' are squarefree, good and rationally primitive with norms of order G, and include every ordered pair, including g=g'. The common ideal core is the original bounded complex function h((g,g')), not its unit-core child or a positive substitute.

JSR1--3 and the current JPS3 interface retain

```
a(n)=alpha(n) eta(n) chi_n(lambda)^(-2) gamma_2(n),
xi(g)=alpha(g)^3 eta(g)^3,
Omega_i=sum_P |u_i(P)|^2/q_P,
S(N,L)=N+L+(NL)^(2/3),
target=G K S(N,L) sqrt(Omega_1 Omega_2) P_orig.
```

Here `P_orig` consists of the actual two kernel scalars, component coefficients and weighted profile seminorms. It is not a new unit coefficient. The outside squared physical scalar is `N^(-1)G^(-2)`, exactly once. The hard domain is `N>C_orig(K+L+G^2)`, `C_orig G<A0`, `1<=L<=sqrt(N)`, together with the actual fixed endpoint constants and original screens. The inherited pressure block has

`k=.835507578307735986...`, `nu=k+.003`, `gamma=.001`, `ell=.170813789153867993...`.

The new claims keep that block; they do not silently substitute the latest endpoint parameters. Here S is comparable to N. The full all-branch H comparison still has the .004 deficit documented in the [private research revision] controller review and [private research revision] original-prime report.

At a good prime, write `tau_j=sqrt(q) gamma_j`. Additive inversion is

`chi(y)^j=(tau_j/q) sum_x chi(x)^(-j) e(-xy/pi)`.

It holds also at y=0, where both sides vanish. For a unit, evaluate the sum as `tau_(-j) chi(-y)^j` and use `tau_j tau_(-j)=q chi(-1)^j`. Inverting the row exponent 3 and first mark exponent 4 cancels the native gamma_2 against gamma_4, giving

```
a(pi) chi_pi(R)^3 chi_pi(P)^4
 = b(pi)/q_pi * sum_(r,s) chi_pi(r)^3 chi_pi(s)^2
                         e(-(Rr+Ps)/pi),
b(pi)=alpha(pi) eta(pi) chi_pi(lambda)^(-2) gamma_3(pi).
```

M B1.1--5 and JNR1 identify gamma_3 as fixed-ray data. The angular alpha factor remains. Conjugating the second side changes the second mark exponent to 4 and its additive sign to plus. The CRT row index is `h=r*pi'-r'*pi`; its root is

`zeta=chi_pi((pi')^(-1))^3 chi_pi'(-pi^(-1))^3`.

It has modulus one and is retained. For `Q=q_pi q_pi'`, the finite product group has `Q^2` elements, and its unitary transform has factor `1/Q`. That is exactly the product of the two local `1/q` factors. There is no remaining Q factor, extra square root, Jacobian or division by six.

The whole short sum, including `chi_R(uv)^3`, its natural zeros, both projectors and every original component coefficient, can be folded into W(R,P,P') before transforming. This is legal for all g,g', not only the fixed-u,v presentation in JN: the finite Fourier identity is linear, and the uncertainty estimates use only support and injectivity. In particular the two projectors remain

`1_(P,Rg)=1` and `1_(P',Rg')=1`

with both actual `q_P^(-1/2)` roots. No sign or diagonal short pair is lost on recombination.

The native transformed kernel is

`chi_pi(h)^3 chi_pi'(h)^3 chi_pi(s)^2 chi_pi'(s')^4`.

Its exact nonzero set U has `(h,pi*pi')=1`, `s!=0 mod pi`, `s'!=0 mod pi'`. The fixed phases and the angular factors do not alter that zero set.

statement:
## G92: exact defect expansion, collar prices and integer cancellation

Fix an ordinary Dirichlet character chi modulo q and retain all natural
zeros. For t,y>=1 define

    R(t,y)=sum_(n<=t,P^-(n)>y)mu(n)chi(n), P^-(1)=infinity.

Least-prime factorization gives the finite signed recurrence
R(t,y)=1-sum_(y<p<=t)chi(p)R(t/p,p). For any approximation F on the
reachable states put Delta=F-1+sum chi(p)F(t/p,p). The nilpotent
triangular inverse is exactly

    F(x,1)-M_chi(x)
      =sum_(d<=x)mu(d)chi(d)Delta(x/d,P^+(d)), P^+(1)=1.

The strict prime ordering excludes repeated primes, n=1 remains, and
every path corresponds to one squarefree product. For fixed r>=1 the
collar t<=y^r is descendant-closed. Exact collar values eliminate its
defects; for r>1 these values are not all1.

On the distinct REAL-coordinate states, the exact independent defect
sup-norm price is

    N_(r,q)(x)=#{d<=x:mu(d)!=0,(d,q)=1,d P^+(d)^r<x}.

The triangle bound is attained by conjugate phases, realizable through
finite back substitution. This construction concerns independent errors
at a chosen root, not actual Mertens values. At fixed positive depth k,

    C_(k,r,q)x^(k/(k+r))/(log x)^k
       <=N_(k,r,q)(x)<=x^(k/(k+r)).

The upper bound uses P^+(d)>=d^(1/k); the lower bound chooses k distinct
unramified primes in(Y,2Y], Y=x^(1/(k+r))/4, using ordinary PNT. Hence
log N_(r,q)(x)/log x tends to1 for each fixed r. This rules out a power
improvement from that unmerged independent-error certificate alone.
It does not rule out correlated errors or growing collars with paid costs.

For an integer root N and floor-invariant F, equal states must instead
be merged BEFORE absolute values. For d>1 put d=pu with P^+(u)<p.
The complete coefficient of Delta(m,p), m=floor(N/d), is

    C_(N,chi)(m,p)=-chi(p)
       sum_(N/[p(m+1)]<u<=N/(pm),P^+(u)<p)mu(u)chi(u).

The full defect is Delta(N,1)+sum C_(N,chi)(m,p)Delta(m,p). For an
exact integer collar m<=p^r, integer r>=1 and N>1, the independent
INTEGER-state norm is

    B_(r,chi)(N)=1+sum_(p,m>p^r)|C_(N,chi)(m,p)|.

One has B<=N_(r,q), but the exponent-one lower bound does not survive
signed grouping. At N=20196,p=17,m=18 the only smooth squarefree u
are65 and66, with opposite Mobius signs. Their principal coefficient
cancels; it is-1 for the real character modulo4 and i for chi(2)=i
modulo5. These are actual cross-depth arithmetic fibres, not random signs.
No improved upper bound or exponent-one lower bound for B is proved.

The crude exact-terminal approximation has a principal defect of order
t/log t, so it fails even the bounded-defect premise. If a different
floor-invariant F has small root value and its COMPLETE signed defect
is O(x^(gamma+epsilon)) at every scale, the same holds for M_chi.
With bounded defects and r=1, depths through6 cost O(x^(6/7)); the
entire deeper signed complement remains. At the current boundary the
depth7 excess is7/8-theta8=.00014261, a property of this error norm,
not a universal barrier or an explanation of the incumbent proof.
title: G92: exact defect expansion, collar prices and integer cancellation

For principal chi and all sufficiently large X, take distinct primes
d,e in I_X=(sqrt(X)/2,sqrt(X/2)], with l=1. They are automatically
unramified, exceed the balanced U,V, and satisfy L<de<=M since
X/4<de<=X/2, gamma<1 and r>1. Their coefficient is +1 in each source.
If J(X) is the number of primes in I_X, the ordinary prime number theorem
gives

    J(X)~2(1/sqrt(2)-1/2)sqrt(X)/log X.

The selected ordered-pair source B_X has J(X)(J(X)-1) terms. Uniformly
on the whole shell,

    Re B_X(x)>=exp(-X^(1-b)/2) cos(2^(-k)) J(X)(J(X)-1).

Thus ||B_X||_1 and ||B_X||_2 are both comparable to X/log^2 X. This is
actual arithmetic, not an arbitrary coefficient example. It obstructs
any positive triangle budget that pays this selected cell separately at
X^(gamma+epsilon), for fixed gamma<1 and epsilon<1-gamma. It also
obstructs paying every cell separately in a partition that contains
this particular cell.

It does NOT prove a lower bound for the full dyadic d,e box, T, R or C_p.
An unselected box contains other Mobius signs. It does not establish a
principal/nonprincipal family obstruction beyond the stated principal
cell. The author's phrase about a dyadic factor block should be used
with this arithmetically selected-cell qualification in integration.

The coefficient-only argument gives the complete O(X^(1+epsilon))
bound, and the accepted Green–Tao import gives only

    ||T||_1 << X^(gamma+epsilon)+X(log X)^(-D)

for each fixed D. The second dilated sum f_x(pn) has fixed degree and

## 2. Large common divisor: exact signs, all holes, and the bin saving

For an ideal q define

    A_G(q)=sum_(d|q, Nd>=G) mu(q/d).

Ideal divisor inversion gives the exact identity

    1_(Nk>=G)=sum_(q|k) A_G(q),
    A_G(q)=0 if Nq<G,       |A_G(q)|<=tau(q).             (8)

Because a is squarefree, every contributing q|a is squarefree. With a=qc,
mu(qc)=mu(q)mu(c)1_(c,q)=1. There is no coprimality condition on b/q. Thus

 B_g(u)=sum_(q sf,Nq>=G) A_G(q)mu(q)phi_u(q)^2/(Nq)
           M_u^(q)(R/Nq) S_u(D/Nq),                    (9)

where M^(q) has the extra column condition (c,q)=1. Every q up to the literal
profile endpoint remains; q can meet a slot, the row or a fixed hole. Character
zeros are retained in phi_u(q)^2; no phase is divided out or reduced to a unit.

To avoid an illicit moving-mask MI input, restore the inverse exactly:

    M_u^(q)(E)=sum_(k supported on primes of q)
                   phi_u(k)/(Nk)^(1/2) M_u(E/Nk).       (10)

At each p|q the local convolution mu*1 is1 at exponent0 and0 otherwise.
Consequently(10) includes ALL k=p^j and preserves natural zeros even at shared
row primes. It is finite on an actual annulus. Its absolute mass is

    prod_(p|q)(1-(Np)^(-1/2))^(-1) <<_epsilon (Nq)^epsilon.
                                                               (11)

Small primes supply a fixed constant and each sufficiently large prime factor
is at most (Np)^epsilon. A fixed polynomial extra inverse puncture, if not
already part of the licensed natural character, is restored by the same formula
over q times that puncture; its complete mass is again U^epsilon. Actual slot
holes remain in their fixed bounded coefficients, as permitted by MI. This is
the existing [restricted research revision] restoration device, here used on ONE inverse and an unchanged
plain factor; it is not claimed as a new general divisor identity.

Apply Hilbert Minkowski to(9),(10), then use the SAME-bin plain bound(2) and
the fully marked moment(3). The outside phases are contractions. This gives

 ||B_g Q||_Omega
   << H_J U^(1/2+epsilon) D^(beta/2)
          sum_(Nq>=G) tau(q)^(O(1)) (Nq)^(-1-beta/2)
   << H_J U^(1/2+epsilon) D^(beta/2) G^(-beta/2).
                                                               (12)

The last estimate follows from ideal counting on dyadic shells, uniformly for
beta in a fixed positive compact interval. Every q-shell count is present: the
factor(Nq)^(-1) in(9) alone would only yield logarithmic mass; the additional
power comes precisely from the shortened plain sum at the same buffered zero.
Squaring proves the first part of(5). A mere trivial plain bound would give
U D/G instead and need a much larger G. This use of(2) is the substantive
same-zero improvement of the [restricted research revision]-style decomposition.
title: 2. Large common divisor: exact signs, all holes, and the bin saving

## G209. All thirteen collision types and the exact mixed-order source

At each good prime record its six original site incidences: two inverses
and at most one slot on each copy. Each occupancy is zero or one.
For the thirteen types (a,b) with 0<=a,b<=3 and a+b>=2, let h_ab be the
squarefree product of primes of that type. The h_ab are pairwise coprime;
all named-slot tests and original coefficients remain attached. Define

    Lc=product h_ab^a, Rc=product h_ab^b,
    L=N(Lc), R=N(Rc), D=LR,
    k=product_(a!=b) h_ab, Kc=N(k),
    E=product_(a=b>=1) h_ab, Hcol=product h_ab.

Every pair uniquely has n=Lc*x,n'=Rc*y, with x,y squarefree, mutually
coprime and prime to Hcol. All six gcd predicates now depend only on
collision labels and incidences. Nonunique means Hcol!=1.

For either complete orientation e=+1 or -1, including natural zeros,

    chi_n(u)^e conjugate(chi_n'(u)^e)
      = psi_k(u) chi_x(u)^e conjugate(chi_y(u)^e) 1_((u,E)=1),
    psi_k = product_(a!=b) chi_p^(e(a-b)).

The good primitive conductor is kxy; each nonzero local exponent has
order 6,3 or2. Equal valuations leave a unit-indicator hole, not one.
The principal class kxy=1 is the entire merged diagonal and is paid
before zero-frequency vanishing. Its full row cost is
O(H_J U^(1+epsilon)) by the c_abs squared-mass bound.

Expand sixth-freeness with a0^6|u, retaining (a0,Hcol*x*y)=1, then expand
the full canceled-phase hole with d|E. Put qa=N(a0),qd=N(d).
Primitive Poisson and CRT preserve the mixed Gauss factor at k,
both residual orientations, separated k,d twists and every zero.

Fix an ORIGINAL a0-dyad qa~A and tau=1/1000. The literal retained cap is

    Hc = C_* U^tau A^6 qd Kc N0^2/(U L R).

Before any artificial extension, the complete genuine far tail is
O(H_J U^(149/30+epsilon-tau(B-1))); choose finite B after the raw count.
On the fractional dual lattice, emptiness uses its fixed least positive
norm. Hc<1 alone does not mean empty. Clearing by the fixed S-supported
Delta changes comparison constants; the original selector is unchanged.

Only then insert the COMPLETE mutual-divisor identity on x,y. For
x=fm,y=fm',F=N(f), allocate f separately through the original colors and
slots on both copies. The unequal residual lengths are

    XL=N0/(L F), XR=N0/(R F).

Both unnormalized roots give precisely

       = U/(qa^6 qd N0 sqrt(Kc) F).

Actual collision labels are not artificial f labels. No extra reciprocal

statement:
# [private research revision] H: adaptive conductor obstruction and sparse-graph transport

The controller accepts the [author argument](h-joint/report.md) and
[independent reconstruction](h-joint-review/report.md) at their restricted
scopes. Both complete reports and helpers were read. Fifteen source
bindings were verified, and a separate root replay of the independent
implementation reproduced its receipt byte for byte:72 local conductor
equivalences,78 exact Jacobi identities and four pressure-box corners.
Three changing status documents were restored to their digest-verified
historical snapshots for that replay; the twelve mathematical/provenance
sources were unchanged. No endpoint premise was replaced by the newer c4.

These results redirect a norm-approximation strategy and remove a
transport prerequisite for an existing graph estimate. They do not
prove the complete H covariance, reduce its .004 pressure deficit,
give a signed-pairing lower bound, or establish a new c or kernel result.

## The actual tensor and adaptive conductor selection

Keep the original same-scale, distinct-rational-norm degree-one prime
packet over the Eisenstein field, original bounded short core and every
ordered short pair, including equality. Both rooted mark arrays,
projectors, natural zeros, ray/unit coefficients, fixed bad places and
independent heights stay literal. The exact native joint transform has
unitary factor1/Q, Q=q_pi q_pi', on a group of size Q^2 and kernel

    chi_pi(h)^3 chi_pi'(h)^3 chi_pi(s)^2 chi_pi'(s')^4.

Its fixed CRT phase and angular factors remain. Its nonzero set U is
(h,pi*pi')=1,s!=0 mod pi,s'!=0 mod pi'. The complete signed short sum
is folded into W before taking any norm. The physical row support has
O(K) elements; each mark support has O(L), with original injection gates.

For bounded integral lifts define a2(h) from odd good-prime valuations
and a3(s) from good-prime valuations nonzero modulo3. The order-two and
order-three subgroups of Z/6 intersect only at zero. Thus shared good
primes cannot cancel the quadratic row factor, and the exact good finite
primitive conductors are

    f1=lcm(a2(h),a3(s)), f2=lcm(a2(h),a3(s')).

Canceled conductor factors still retain their natural imprimitive zeros.
Fixed bad and angular data are separate; this identity does not give a
finite-order theorem for the full moving angular kernel.

The bounded row lifts with q_a2(h)<=D number O(sqrt(QD)): write
(h)=a_S a b^2, with finitely many bad-prime parity choices a_S and
good squarefree q_a<=D, then use ideal counting and partial summation.
All squares and arbitrary bad-prime powers are included. This is an
ideal count, not a count of squarefree rational norms.

Any selector, even one depending on transformed marks and coefficients,
which retains points with min(q_f1,q_f2)<=D lies inside that row-only
set. Enlarge its positive squared mass first, then apply row Cauchy
and both mark Plancherel identities. This proves

    ||1_U 1_(min(q_f1,q_f2)<=D) W_hat||_2^2
       <= C K sqrt(D)/N ||W||_2^2.

The original separate row injections and mark Cauchy give eligible mass
at least[1-C(1+L)/N]||W||_2^2. If W is nonzero, the corresponding
eligible fraction is bounded by the displayed ratio. If W=0 no nonzero
fraction is claimed. The adaptive selector itself need not commute with
Fourier transformation: only the containing row set does.

At the inherited pressure block N/K=Z^.003, a fixed captured fraction
requires D at least a constant times Z^.006. The product-conductor
version requires q_f1 q_f2 budget at least a constant times Z^.012.
D=Z^.004 or product budget Z^.008 captures O(Z^(-.001)) of eligible
squared mass. These are necessary norm-approximation thresholds, not
sufficiency at equality or lower bounds for H. The numerical .004
conductor example is unrelated to the .004 physical deficit.

The statement is for the unprojected tensor and bounded lifts. The
accepted kernel-invariant orbit projection can discard tensor norm while
preserving its signed pairing. Unbounded alternative lifts or a new basis
also require their own paid support and moving weights. These escapes
remain open; the obstruction does not rule out signed cancellation.

## Transport and common-unit centering of an inherited graph bound

Put S=N+L+(NL)^(2/3). The original raw target is
G K S sqrt(Omega1 Omega2) P_orig, where Omega_i=sum|u_i(P)|^2/q_P
and P_orig contains the actual profiles, coefficients and scalar gains.
The outside physical factor is N^(-1)G^(-2), applied once.

The previously accepted JSR19 bound for graphs with both degrees<=B is

    |C_E| <= Z^epsilon G^(2+103/359) B K^(231/359)
                         N^(103/359) S sqrt(Omega1 Omega2) P_orig.

The graph may be frozen with each original short pair, but must be
independent of live rows and marks. This raw graph bound is inherited
credit. Its full signed projector expansion retains both roots, all
D,D' cross terms and the lcm Schur bound.

Move only the smooth row factor from R/sqrt(K) to(R+P+P')/sqrt(K);
every sharp support stays on the original variables. Its global smooth
extension has difference bounded by C sqrt(L/K)||grad rho||. Counting
O(G^2) short pairs, O(NB) edges and O(K) rows, and paying both rooted
mark sums by L sqrt(Omega1 Omega2), gives

    |C_E^tr-C_E| <= C G^2 K N B L sqrt(L/K)
                            sqrt(Omega1 Omega2) P_orig.

No sharp indicator is differentiated and no signed-submask monotonicity
is assumed. This coarse estimate is enough for the stated sparse graphs.

The actual common-unit Jacobi numerator has two square-root Jacobi
factors and denominator

    product_(p|pi*pi') [q_p^2-3q_p+3-1_(p|T)].

Both local convolution signs cancel. The ratio is O(N^-3), including
exceptional totals. The absent local factor begins as an unrestricted
constant; unit insertion is justified by the actual small-mark support.
Counting all mark off-diagonals and graph edges yields

    |M_E^(J,tr)| <= C G^2 K B L/N^2 sqrt(Omega1 Omega2) P_orig.

The sharp row remains R=T-P-P'. The original injection
Q>C_orig(K+L) makes the transported smooth factor constant on each
occupied residue-total fibre. No additional Fourier or unit normalization
appears. The centered form is C_E^tr-M_E^(J,tr).

All three terms are paid by the original target when, with a fixed buffer,

    B <= K^(128/359) N^(-103/359) G^(-462/359),
    G B L sqrt(L/K)<=1, G B L/N^3<=1.

At B=floor(Z^.055) their relative pressure exponents are approximately
-.00103535,-.1055331,-2.288709. All corners of the wider rational
box .8355<=k<=.8356,.1708<=ell<=.1709,nu=k+.003 retain strict savings.
This is an adapter for the inherited pressure block, not a new endpoint
solution. Multiplication by N^-1 G^-2 gives the complete physical bound
Z^epsilon K S/(NG) sqrt(Omega1 Omega2) P_orig.

Both original preprojection corrections vanish on this prime packet by
support. They are not removed from composite or other branches. Both
ordered heights are integrated against their actual product separation
densities, whose weighted L1 moments pay the radial/gradient powers.
Complete source tails are bounded before transport; both mixed tails
and the double tail are paid. The transported object retains the original
discarded tail or its exact correction. Unbounded heights are not hidden
in epsilon and a shifted tail is not given its old argument by assertion.

Actual primary-generator displacement graphs of squared radius Y have
degree O(Y+1), so Y of order Z^.055 supplies admissible strict-far
examples without a prime-density assumption. The complement remains
its exact unestimated signed form. Covering a full bipartite graph with
degree-B layers needs at least max(m,m')/B layers; absolute summation
recovers the full degree cost. That method limitation is not an H lower
bound.

The useful next target is the complete signed high-conductor/orbit
aggregate with moving prime-pair weights, or the original far complement
with its roots, short core and both projectors. Other scale pairs,
prime/composite and composite/composite interactions, inert and exceptional
branches remain obligations of full H.

statement:
### 2.2 Isolated squarefree coefficients force a banded price

Let h>=1 be an integer. Call n in [h+1,N-h] isolated if n is squarefree, n=1 mod q, and every n+r with 0<|r|<=h is nonsquarefree. Let I be any set of such indices and K=|I|. If P in (1) has half-bandwidth h, namely P_nm=0 when |n-m|>h, then

    a*Pa >= K^2.                                            (3)

Indeed, |a_n|=1 for n in I, every other actual nonzero source coordinate is more than h away from it, and distinct members of I are more than h apart. Hence the actual cross terms between I and its complement vanish, and P_II is diagonal. The principal submatrix inequality P_II>=ell_I ell_I* implies, by evaluation on ell_I, sum_(n in I)P_nn>=K^2. The remaining principal block is PSD. Its actual energy is nonnegative, so (3) follows. This proof retains all squareful and nonunit zeros; no cancellation outside I is discarded as an assertion about M.

Here is a completely elementary supply of such indices. For each r in {-h,...,-1,1,...,h}, choose a distinct prime p_r>h not dividing q. Set

    Q=q product_r p_r^2,
    n=1 mod q,     n=-r mod p_r^2 for every r.                (4)

CRT gives one residue a0 modulo Q and gcd(a0,Q)=1: p_r cannot divide r, and the q-residue is 1. Every shifted n+r is squareful. Count squarefree n in this residue. The exact expansion mu(n)^2=sum_(d^2|n)mu(d), with only gcd(d,Q)=1 contributing, gives uniformly in Q and a0,

    #{n<=N:n=a0 mod Q, mu(n)^2=1}
      = (N/Q) product_(p not dividing Q)(1-p^-2)+O(3 sqrt N),
      >= N/(2Q)-3 sqrt N,       N>=4.                        (5)

For completeness, truncate d at floor(sqrt N). Each compatible congruence modulo Qd^2 costs at most 1 in its count, hence at most sqrt N total. The omitted main sum costs at most 2 sqrt N/Q. Its Euler product is at least 1/zeta(2)>1/2, using sum_(n>=2)n^-2<1. Take I to be the resulting squarefree indices in [h+1,N-h]. Deleting the at most 2h endpoint integers leaves

    K >= max(0, N/(2Q)-3 sqrt N-2h).                         (6)

Neither a prime distribution theorem nor a hypothesis about mu cancellation is needed for (3)-(6).

The primes in (4) can be chosen <=C_q h log(2h). One elementary proof of the needed supply uses

    4^m/(2m+1) <= binom(2m,m) <= (2m)^pi(2m).

Each prime contributes at most 2m to the binomial's factorization, since every term of its valuation sum is 0 or 1. This gives pi(x)>>x/log x. Choosing C_q large supplies 2h distinct primes above h and outside the fixed ramified set. Consequently

    log Q <= log q+4h log(C_q h log(2h))
           =(4+o(1))h log h                    as h->infinity. (7)

For any h_N=o(log N/loglog N), (6) gives K=N^(1-o(1)). Every matrix in (1) with that bandwidth therefore has

    sqrt(a*Pa) >= N^(1-o(1)).                                (8)

For h_N=floor(kappa log N/loglog N), fixed 0<kappa<1/8, it instead gives

    K >= N^(1-4kappa-o(1)),
    sqrt(a*Pa) >= N^(1-4kappa-o(1)).                         (9)

The restriction kappa<1/8 is the range in which the explicit AP main term dominates the sqrt N error. Fixed h gives the stronger K>>_(q,h)N. These are all-large-N certificate statements with fixed q; the constants do not purport to be uniform as q grows.

Thus a bound a*Pa <<_(chi,epsilon) N^(2gamma+epsilon) through this class requires kappa>=(1-gamma)/4 in the regime of (9). This is only a necessary width, never a sufficient arithmetic saving.

| Proposed source exponent gamma | Desired c=1-gamma | Necessary kappa for this bandwidth class |
|---|---:|---:|
| A strict gain below .8748540364 | >.1251459636 | >.0312864909 |
| .8748 | .1252 | >=.0313 |
| 5/6 | 1/6 | >=1/24 |
| 3/4 | 1/4 | >=1/16 |

These tests deliberately include a coarse near gain, 1/6 and 1/4. None is obtained.

### 2.2 Exact minimum over all character-preserving pairings

For each unit residue a modulo q define

    E_a(X)=#{n<=X:n squarefree,n=a mod q,mu(n)=1},
    O_a(X)=#{n<=X:n squarefree,n=a mod q,mu(n)=-1},
    I_a(X)=E_a(X)-O_a(X).

Consider ANY odd differential d on V_X satisfying d^2=0 and commuting with every
W_chi modulo q. Characters separate unit residue classes: if an n,m matrix entry
of d is nonzero then chi(n)=chi(m) for every chi, whence n=m mod q. Thus d splits
into the residue blocks. Since W_chi is unitary, d* also commutes with W_chi, and
the harmonic subspace of Delta=dd*+d*d splits in the same way.

For each residue block the even-minus-odd harmonic dimension is I_a(X). One
elementary proof decomposes the finite complex into im d, im d* and ker Delta:
the first two have equal dimensions with opposite parity, via d restricted to
im d*. Therefore

    dim ker Delta >= R_q(X):=sum_(a mod q,(a,q)=1)|I_a(X)|.       (19.3)

This lower bound is attained. In each residue class pair the first
min(E_a,O_a) even/odd basis vectors in increasing order and use the two-state
differential above. The remaining |I_a| vectors are harmonic and all positive
eigenvalues equal1. Thus the EXACT minimum harmonic dimension in this class of
differentials is R_q(X), with an attaining gap1 realization whenever any pairs exist.

Character orthogonality gives

    M_chi(X)=sum_a chi(a)I_a(X),
    I_a(X)=1/phi(q) sum_(chi mod q) conjugate(chi(a)) M_chi(X),
    max_chi |M_chi(X)| <= R_q(X)
       <= sum_chi |M_chi(X)| <= phi(q)max_chi |M_chi(X)|.         (19.4)

For each fixed q these are fixed constants. Therefore a power bound for the
optimal unsigned harmonic rank is equivalent to the same common power bound for
all characters modulo q. A gap theorem alone is vacuous here: gap1 was obtained
without bounding R_q. Optimizing the differential has not made an independent
arithmetic estimate. This conclusion is limited to this complete source and
character-preserving finite parity complexes; it does not prohibit a different
signed readout, a noncommuting differential with a paid commutator, or a new
analytic source.

Late source audit: the newly integrated [private research revision] G135 already proves the full
fixed-modulus character/residue discrepancy equivalence, its increasing-rank
matching version, and the exact unmatched-index price. The finite Hodge minimum
above is an operator formulation of that same index bill. It is not a new
arithmetic matching principle or an independent cancellation mechanism. This
overlap was found after the original seeds and random selections were frozen;
none of their eligibility or choices has been revised.

The exact diagnostic at X=80,q=5 gives indices (0,-3,-4,1) in residues1,2,3,4.
The minimum harmonic rank is8. The four character traces are -6,-1+i,8,-1-i,
exactly equal to the corresponding literal M_chi(80). A neutral-prime r=2
complex for the principal character has14 harmonic states instead. This checks
the finite indexing and shows why a14-state rank floor from one complex is not
valid for every changed differential. No asymptotic saving follows from80.

## 3. Finite reconstruction and complete scalar error: GC15--GC16

        + sum_{r>X/X_0} k(r)F_tau(x/r).                  (C3)

For the first sum, Z>=X_0>=1 and (C1) imply

    sup_{0<t<=2X_0} t^(-sigma)|F_tau(t)|<infinity.        (C4)

alone would not imply (C4) at zero. Hence the second sum is bounded

pointwise, uniformly on the complete shell, with all small scales
included. It does not require an arithmetic moment assumption.

For GC16, the inherited Mertens premise gives

    sum_{n<=t}A(n)=M(t)-2M(t/2)=O(t^beta).

       << X^(beta+1/2+epsilon/2)+X^(1+epsilon)
       << X^(1.3749+epsilon).                           (C6)

Both ordered mixed terms and the error square are covered. The
last inequality uses beta>1/2. This allocation works for every
epsilon>0, without silently treating the error as a squared error
alone. The exponent 1.3749 is below the stated target 1.74898.

If Q_X is one of the complete original W35 finite-band or
four-diagonal scalars, R35.17 and (C5) give an additional comparison
error X^(beta-A_0+o(1)). Adding it to (C6) preserves the displayed
1.3749+epsilon comparison. This says nothing about a new exponent
for ||R_X||_2 itself. For a lower target, the two-way norm theorem
remains the valid return even if this baseline scalar estimate is
too crude.

## 4. Four diagonals, source caps, heights and reconstruction

Fix A_0>0, tau>0 and the constants

    kappa=C=sqrt(2 tau(1+A_0)),
    D=sqrt(2(1+A_0)/tau).

For each local real scale Z let L=log Z, H=kappa sqrt(L),
Y=floor(Z^.495), T=Z exp(-H), B=2Z exp(H), and
Dmax=B/(Y+1). All assertions below are for sufficiently large Z;
fixed lower scale ranges are absorbed in constants where needed.

### 4.1 Exact bin geometry and permissible source tails

The bins satisfy

    sqrt(Z) exp(iH) <= d < sqrt(Z) exp((i+1)H),
    Y<d<=Dmax.

Their left edges are included, their right edges are excluded,
and the real Dmax cap is retained. Therefore:

- If i+j<-2, then i+j<=-3 and de<Z exp(-H)=T.
- If i+j>=-2, then de>=Z exp(-2H).
- Once H>log 2, J_Z=floor(1+log 2/H)=1. If i+j>1,
  then de>=Z exp(2H)>2Z exp(H)=B.
- If d>Dmax and e>Y is an integer, then e>=Y+1 and de>B;
  the same holds with d and e interchanged.

Thus all original pairs omitted by GC17 lie either in the paid
low-product source or in the paid upper tail. There is no assertion
that the four-diagonal rectangle has exactly the same product cap.
Its included products can range from Z exp(-2H) to below Z exp(3H).

For low products the common derivative order
m=1+floor(kappa sqrt(L)/tau) in R35.4 gives

    |S_tau(y/(de))|
       <= exp(-kappa^2 L/(2tau)+O(sqrt(L)log L))

whenever y in [Z,2Z] and de<=T. Summing at most Z(1+log Z)
ordered labels gives Z^(-A_0+o(1)). The omitted-label mask and the
coprime/6 mask are bounded and independent of ell, so this bound
applies to the actual omitted labels after each alternating sum is
completed. An ell-dependent truncation cannot be inserted first.

For total indices n>B, the absolute coefficient majorant is d_3(n)
for every relevant original-pair subset, including the primitive
rectangle. Its summatory bound is t(1+log t)^2. Stieltjes summation
against the decreasing Gaussian gives, uniformly for Z<=y<=2Z,

    sum_{n>B}d_3(n)g_tau(log(n/y))
      <= y integral_H^infinity
             e^v(1+log y+v)^2 |g_tau'(v)|dv
      = Z^(1-kappa^2/(2tau)+o(1))
      = Z^(-A_0+o(1)).                                  (C7)

The identity e^v exp(-v^2/(2tau))
=exp(tau/2)exp(-(v-tau)^2/(2tau)) proves the exponent, with
the remaining factors contributing O(sqrt(L)+log L) to its
logarithm. The real cap and strict n>B condition are preserved.

These two bounds independently reproduce GC18. Once that complete-
restoration estimate has been used, removing n=de*ell>B costs (C7)
again. For retained rectangular pairs de>=Z exp(-2H), so the exact
remaining restoration bound is

    ell<=B/(Z exp(-2H))=2 exp(3H).                       (C8)

### 4.2 Complete Mellin scalar and height tails

Let a in (0,1) be fixed. The entire Mellin transform of S_tau is
E_tau(s)eta(s), obtained first at Re(s)>1 and then by continuation
using the Gaussian left tail and rapid right decay. Therefore the
finite primitive pair polynomial C_ij^6 gives

    P_Z^rect(y)=(2pi)^(-1)integral_R D_Z^6(t)y^(a+it)dt.

No interchange of the alternating Dirichlet series on Re(s)=a<1
is needed. Squaring and integrating on the actual local shell gives
exactly GC19, with kernel

    [ (2Z)^(2a+i(t-t'))-Z^(2a+i(t-t')) ]
                  / [2a+i(t-t')].                      (C9)

The denominator has nonzero real part 2a; in particular t=t' does
not create a singularity. Gaussian height decay and the finite pair
polynomial justify the double integral absolutely. Neither the
gcd condition nor the two independent heights factor out.

The alternating partial sums of b have modulus at most one, giving
|eta(a+it)|<=|a+it|/a. Also, because all retained products are below
Z exp(3H), absolute pair summation gives

    sum_{all retained ordered pairs} (de)^(-a)
       <<_a (Z exp(3H))^(1-a) (1+log(Z exp(3H))).

This estimate safely enlarges the subset of integer pairs; no
arithmetic cancellation is used. Multiplication by y^a gives
Z^(1+o(1)). The remaining tail integral has Gaussian factor
exp(-tau t^2/2) times a fixed polynomial in t. Cutting at
|t|=D sqrt(log Z) therefore costs

    Z^(1-tau D^2/2+o(1))=Z^(-A_0+o(1)).                ([restricted research revision])

For the capped coefficient Fourier form, the finite absolute mass
is at most B(1+log B)^2=Z^(1+o(1)); its Gaussian height tail gives
the same exponent. These are two paid field presentations, not an
assertion that their arithmetic coefficients are termwise equal.

### 4.3 Outer reconstruction and all cross terms

After choosing X_0 beyond the fixed four-diagonal geometry threshold,
replace each local P source in (C3) by its rectangular, capped or
height-truncated approximation. The local extra error satisfies
Z^(-A_0+o(1)); hence for each fixed sigma>1/2 it is bounded by
C_sigma Z^sigma uniformly for Z>=X_0. Compact lower scale ranges
can be absorbed using absolute coefficient bounds. Summing with
|k(r)| and (C2) reproduces GC15's X^(1/2+epsilon) global error.
It does not assert an X^(-A_0) error after the outer reconstruction.

The source-tail estimates are applied locally before the r sum.
A global d_3 majorant for the reconstructed coefficients is neither
needed nor established. This avoids misusing the original label
majorant after a new arithmetic convolution.

The exact all-height reconstructed Mellin amplitude is GC20:

    D_X^rec(t)=E_tau(a+it)eta(a+it)
       sum_{r<=X/X_0}k(r)r^(-a-it)
          sum_{i+j=-2,-1,0,1}C_ij^6(a+it;X/r).          ([restricted research revision])

The r^(-a-it) factor follows from (x/r)^(a+it); omitting its phase
would change the field. Its exact local Gram uses (C9) with Z=X.
Expanding the two finite outer sums therefore retains every
r,r',i,j,i',j' interaction with both independent heights.

If each local field is height truncated, the summand for r contains
its own indicator 1_{|t|<=D sqrt(log(X/r))}. The conjugate summand
for r' has its own indicator at t'. There is no collapse to one
height or to a common local cutoff. The field error bound followed
by the Hilbert-space inequality (C6) prices all mixed terms together.

Although ([restricted research revision]) uses non-dyadic scales X/r, this creates no new
hypothesis: (C1) and the tail estimates are uniform for real local
scales. When only all-dyad arithmetic bounds are assumed, transport
first uses the fixed F_tau field as in GC14. Directly covering a
varying-cutoff P family by two dyads would require an extra argument
and is not used.

### 4.4 Optional finite f_3 readout

The author's optional finite window T<n<=B applies directly to
F_tau. Since |f_3(n)|=1 and y>=Z,

    sum_{n<=T}|f_3(n)|g_tau(log(n/y))
       <=T g_tau(-H)
       <<_tau Z^(-A_0)exp(-H).                          ([restricted research revision])

The upper tail follows from (C7), even with the smaller bounded-
coefficient majorant. The capped Fourier polynomial has at most B
unit-magnitude coefficients, so ([restricted research revision]) also applies to its height
tail. All three optional tails are paid with the same fixed width.

For integration, retain the scope distinction: this finite f_3
readout approximates F_tau to a negative-power error. Its relation
to the primitive P source still passes through the small-radical
boundary error (C1), which is O(Z^(.495+delta)). The two finite
coefficient lists are not asserted equal or negative-power close
without that boundary. The author's equivalence statement is valid
with this distinction.

## 5. The old arithmetic exponent is preserved: GC21--GC22

The identity 1_{(d,e)=1}=sum_{q|d,e}mu(q) is finite coefficientwise.
Under (de,6)=1, write d=qu,e=qv. Nonzero Möbius terms require q
squarefree and (uv,6q)=1. The coefficient is

    mu(q)mu(qu)mu(qv)=mu(q)^3 mu(u)mu(v)
                    =mu(q)mu(u)mu(v).

There is no residual (u,v)=1 constraint. This proves GC21 with
its actual divided sharp intervals, including their open/closed
endpoints. MG9--MG10 give, for each eta>0,

    sum_{n<=U;(n,c)=1}mu(n)<<_{beta,eta}U^beta c^eta.

Abel summation on any of those intervals, with 0<a<beta, yields

    |V_{i,q}(a+it)|
       <<(1+|t|)(6q)^eta(D_i^*/q)^(beta-a).

For a nonempty interval D_i^*/q>=1, so the endpoints introduce
no small-scale exception. The integral of u^(beta-a-1) is paid
because beta-a>0. Inserting both factors leaves the convergent
positive series

    sum_q q^(-2beta+2eta),       0<eta<beta-1/2.

This proves GC22 with constants independent of the bins, q and t.
At a=.75 the inherited one-height bound is .2498; the target is
.24898. Their difference .00082 remains unpaid. This absolute
reconstruction does not supply the missing signed correlation.

## 6. Independent proof of the actual-coefficient operator obstruction

Use exactly GC23: N=floor(B_X), a fixed real sigma>=0,

    L_sigma(c)_{n,m}=1_{m|n}c(n/m)(n/m)^(-sigma),
    W_X(v)(x)=sum_{n<=N}n^sigma v_n g_tau(log(n/x)).

Input norm is unweighted l2({1,...,N}); output norm is L2(dx/x)
on [X,2X]. The matrix product satisfies

    L_sigma(c)L_sigma(d)=L_sigma(c*d).                   ([restricted research revision])

Every intermediate divisor lies between m and n<=N, so finite
truncation removes no term. Hence all three finite identities in
GC24 follow from mu*1=delta_1, b*mu=q_2 and b*mu*mu=A. These
algebraic identities do not yet control W_X.

Let c_X be the literal W35 coefficient with d,e>Y, de>T and
de*ell=n<=N. It has the exact support property

    c_X(q)=0 for every integer q<=T.                    ([restricted research revision])

At e_1 the readout is the capped coefficient field. R35.17 pays
its difference from G_tau; the omitted A-tail is at most three
times the bounded-coefficient Gaussian upper tail. Thus

    ||W_X[L_sigma(A)-L_sigma(c_X)]e_1||_2
       << X^(-A_0+o(1)),                               ([restricted research revision])

independently of sigma. The powers n^sigma and n^(-sigma) cancel
exactly at this input. This verifies GC25 including the A cap.

For the full operator define

    a_tau=2 exp(4tau),       b_tau=4 exp(4tau),
    M_X={m in N:a_tau X<=m<=b_tau X}.

For sufficiently large X, M_X is contained in {1,...,N}, because
B_X/X=2 exp(H) tends to infinity. Also, for m in M_X,

    mT >=2 exp(4tau) X^2 exp(-H)>2X exp(H)>=N           ([restricted research revision])

eventually; the sufficient inequality is log X+4tau>2H. Since
H=kappa sqrt(log X), this holds for all sufficiently large X.

If a nonzero c_X quotient contributed in column m, ([restricted research revision]) would
force q>T, so n=mq>mT>N. Therefore every such column of
L_sigma(c_X) is identically zero. This is an exact support
statement, not an estimate for a generic replacement sequence.

The A-column has readout

    W_X L_sigma(A)e_m
       =m^sigma sum_{q<=N/m}A(q)g_tau(log(qm/x)).        ([restricted research revision])

This equality checks the weighting: (mq)^sigma q^(-sigma)
=m^sigma, with no remaining q-weight. Put u=log(m/x). For all
m in M_X and X<=x<=2X,

    4tau<=u<=4tau+log 4.

For every q>=2 the exact Gaussian ratio is

    g_tau(u+log q)/g_tau(u)
      =q^(-u/tau)exp(-(log q)^2/(2tau))<=q^(-4).       ([restricted research revision])

Use the actual A(1)=1 and |A(q)|<=3. The remaining signed terms,
however truncated at N/m, have absolute sum at most

    3 sum_{q>=2}q^(-4)
       <=3[1/16+integral_2^infinity t^(-4)dt]
       =5/16.

Consequently ([restricted research revision]) is uniformly at least

    (11/16)m^sigma g_tau(u)
       >=(11/16)a_tau^sigma X^sigma
                           g_tau(4tau+log 4)>0.         ([restricted research revision])

Here sigma>=0 is used in the displayed lower bound, and tau,
sigma are fixed before X varies. The constant may be small as
tau varies; no uniformity in moving tau is claimed.

For large X, |M_X|>=a_tau X/2. The positive vector

    v_m=|M_X|^(-1/2)1_{m in M_X}

has l2 norm one. The c_X columns vanish, while all A readouts
have the same positive lower bound ([restricted research revision]) throughout the shell.
Thus

    ||W_X[L_sigma(A)-L_sigma(c_X)]||_{l2->L2}
      >= c_(tau,sigma) X^(sigma+1/2),                   ([restricted research revision])

with one admissible explicit constant

    c_(tau,sigma)=(11/16)a_tau^(sigma+1/2)
                   g_tau(4tau+log 4)sqrt((log 2)/2)>0.

This independently proves GC26. The exact finite cap, original
prime-two coefficients, original product cut and zero modulation
height are all retained. No finite numerical experiment is needed
for this asymptotic lower bound; the eventual support inequalities
and Gaussian ratio provide the decisive calculation.

The difference between ([restricted research revision]) and ([restricted research revision]) is the point of the result.
The witness vector is supported at high indices, whereas the
actual arithmetic input is e_1. The result refutes only the claim
that the small error at e_1 can be promoted to a small unrestricted
l2-to-physical-L2 operator norm. It is not a lower bound for
G_tau, F_tau, P_Y, their scalar energies, or a domain restricted
by a separately proved arithmetic condition. It also does not
contradict the weighted all-dyad function-space bound GC13.

## 7. Integration limits and final verification record

The author has supplied a valid quantitative reconstruction of the
complete fixed detector, beyond a formal Euler identity. The moving
cutoff cost and cross-dyad transport are paid separately. This removes
the need for an additional conjectural comparison with all original
common-prime and fixed-small-prime complements when using this route.
It does not show that the unweighted literal complement is small on
one shell, or that a signed subfamily's energy is dominated by the
complete source's energy.

The finite f_3 correlation in the independent review's Section 8,
or the exact primitive local Gram GC19, remains the next arithmetic
target. Its coefficient signs, complete local kernel, both heights,
ordered interactions and all-large-dyad quantifier must be retained.
The convolution norm bounds preserve a proved exponent; they do
not create a strict contraction.

This lane verified source bytes/hashes, exact algebra and endpoints,
quantified Gaussian source tails, the two-term field reconstruction,
the scalar mixed terms, the complete reconstructed amplitude, the
imported coprime Mertens premise, and the finite positive-column
operator witness. It did not run a broad suite or repeat numerical
Möbius sampling, neither of which would establish the open moment.

Only this new comparison artifact was written. The first independent
review remains frozen; the author and imported sources were read
only. No agents, provider calls, tracker, shared-state or Git writes
were performed. Full final readback, byte count, SHA256 and STOP
are supplied in the controller handoff.

# [restricted research revision] high-ceiling exercise: paid linear readout versus absolute Gram

Root-owned mathematical draft. Current conditional source-relative c11
=.1251459636; PR15 stronger source and endpoint remain unfinished. This
exercise begins after [restricted research revision] and before admission of [restricted research revision], which triggers
the prior pass cadence. It is distinct from the completed07:31 source
repair pass and the preceding positive-hole corollary review.

Discovery and priority, before independent review:

1. Growing-dimensional quaternion/Hilbert lifts: [restricted research revision] G221 left a
dimension/readout tradeoff. Test the strongest objection that a common
linear recovery itself forces the full absolute price, independently of
dimension. This is the chosen candidate: a precise obstruction could
remove a misleading apparent high-ceiling escape.
2. Full signed quaternion companion lower bound: exactly the desired
Jordan L2 estimate, with future-scale inverse already paid. Remains
credible only with an actual source-specific correlation estimate.
3. Oscillatory nonprincipal joint-label kernels: G225's positive-mask
floor does not apply. Must construct a true fixed zero signal and pay
all label covariance and recovery, rather than selecting one small entry.
4. W66 prime-dependent deletion plus growing signed centering: exact
subpower inverse criterion is favorable, but both signed approximant
and complete residual remain to be bounded. Positive diagonal norms fail.
5. Critical prime-flux cutoff: a larger mask pays kappa and demands a
jointly proved hard-complement margin delta>kappa. An arbitrary-input
resolvent cannot assume the missing arithmetic contraction.
6. Nonlinear determinant/companion comparisons: norm multiplicativity
remains exact, but an upper norm estimate alone pays both components.
No common linear readout theorem below rules out a signed nonlinear
identity with complete all-height detection and inverse costs.

Potential: routes2-6 could in principle return c=.12 (useful source
repair), .12515 (above conditional c11),1/6,1/4 if their full named
estimates hold. Route1 is tested now because it decides whether growing
dimension or delayed absolute values are genuine escapes for this class.
No rank count, norm identity, or outcome-free hope is counted as a saving.

## Candidate dimension-free lemma

Let H be ANY real Hilbert space, T:H->R^2 a bounded real-linear map of
norm L>0, and v_a a finite family. Write y_a=T v_a, and

    B_abs = sum_(a,b) |<v_a,v_b>|,  M = sum_a |y_a|.

Claim:

    L^2 B_abs >= (4/pi^2) M^2.                         (R1)

If all y_a are on one fixed real line, improve4/pi^2 to1. The family
may already contain arbitrary positive weights, source coefficients,
phases, masks and scale factors. No dimension or upper bound on |v_a|
is assumed. For an infinite family apply the finite statement to every
finite subset; the nonnegative sums give the corresponding extended
inequality. Finite B_abs needs no stronger unconditional convergence
claim for the vector sum.

Proof attempt. Average |u_alpha dot y_a| over the unit circle to obtain
(2/pi)|y_a|. Some alpha therefore satisfies sum|u_alpha dot y_a|
>=2M/pi. Set ell=u_alpha dot T, so ||ell||<=L, and take real signs
epsilon_a=sign(ell(v_a)). Then

    (sum |ell(v_a)|)^2 = |ell(sum epsilon_a v_a)|^2
      <= L^2 ||sum epsilon_a v_a||^2
      <= L^2 sum_(a,b)|<v_a,v_b>|.

This proves(R1). For collinear images choose the common unit direction.
This uses the complete ordered Gram, not its actual signed sum, not a
termwise domination |Tva dot Tvb|<=L^2|va dot vb| (which is false).

## Pointwise actual-source consequence

For a scalar complex source F(x)=sum_a c_a K(q_a/x), suppose v_a(x)
is any real-Hilbert lift with T_x v_a(x)=c_a K(q_a/x), common T_x across
all a, norm L_x. Then(R1) gives

    L_x^2 sum_(a,b)|<v_a(x),v_b(x)>|
       >=(4/pi^2) [sum_a |c_a K(q_a/x)|]^2.             (R2)

For G221's quaternion v_a=w_a(xi_a+t_a j), first-complex-coordinate
projection has L_x=1. Thus the old C-dependent rank-four floor can be
strengthened WITHOUT an upper bound on t_a, even in arbitrary dimension
with a common paid linear readout. Dimension alone cannot cure this
particular positive price. With fixed bounded L, the full or retained
middle source of G221 has a quadratic price. This is not an actual signed
energy lower bound and not a general ban on nonlinear detectors.

## Absolute values after shell integration

Let I=[X,2X] with dx/x and ell_I=log2. Suppose v_a(x) belongs to a
measurable real Hilbert bundle, each v_a is square integrable, and T_x
is a measurable common real-linear recovery to C with ||T_x||<=L,
such that T_x v_a(x)=c_a K(q_a/x). Work in the direct-integral Hilbert
space. The common map

    Tcal(v)=integral_I T_x v(x) dx/x

has norm at most L sqrt(log2). Its image on v_a is

    c_a J_X(q_a), J_X(t)=integral_X^(2X) K(t/x) dx/x.

Thus(R1) implies

    L^2 log2 sum_(a,b)|integral_I <v_a(x),v_b(x)> dx/x|
       >=(4/pi^2) [sum_a |c_a J_X(q_a)|]^2.             (R3)

The left side takes absolute values only AFTER integration, with all
ordered pairs. x-dependent lifts or readouts are allowed, provided the
common map and its displayed bound hold. Variable L_x can instead pay
integral_I L_x^2 dx/x. Do not replace that reconstruction bill by1.

For the G218 positive Gaussian K=g_tau(log t), every q_a,x in[X,2X]
has K bounded below. All S+ natural-zero primes remain. G225's count
gives sum |c_a J_X(q_a)| >> X/log(2X) uniformly on polynomial holes;
with no moving holes the fixed squarefree count gives >>X. Therefore
the paid price is at least quadratic up to logarithms after integration,
even for arbitrary-dimensional or x-dependent lifts of these fields.
Positive mixtures are handled by their actual nonnegative p(a), not by
assuming the joint covariance kernel equals the product kernel.

Possible Jordan extension to challenge, not yet assumed: for any fixed
continuous real kernel K with suitable tails, put J(t)=int_1^2 K(t/u)du/u.
If K is not identically zero and tends to0 at infinity, J cannot vanish
identically: J=0 implies K(t)=K(t/2) by differentiating the logarithmic
integral, hence K=0 by scaling to infinity. A fixed interval where |J|>0
then gives sum_(sf q-units n)|J(n/X)| >>X by the fixed squarefree count.
For the retained-middle source, this interval eventually lies inside
the complete middle mask uniformly across x, provided the G215 mask
exponents/cutoffs permit it. Audit those exact source conditions; don't
assume this for arbitrary oscillatory or X-dependent profiles.

If bounded lifts additionally give total diagonal O(X) (as in G221),
subtracting it preserves the off-diagonal floor. Without a diagonal
bound claim only the TOTAL absolute price; enormous lifts may put the
whole bill on the diagonal. L may grow and must be paid in recovery.

## Weakest return and deliberately coarse test

For a complete shell-L2 source target gamma=1-c, c>0, any strategy
using this complete absolute Gram followed by its common linear
readout pays an energy exponent at least2 (logarithmic refinements
do not change it), whereas the required exponent is2-2c. Its deficit
is2c: .24 at c=.12; .2502919272 at conditional c11; .25030 at c=.12515;
1/3 at c=1/6;1/2 at c=1/4. This tests the deliberately coarse sufficient
price; it is not a lower bound on F or a proof of zero exclusion.

The surviving targets must use cancellation before the complete pairwise
absolute sum, a materially different/nonlinear readout with paid return,
or source-dependent relations not captured by this certificate. A matrix
determinant or Hilbert lift does not by itself provide such a bound.

## Independent review assignment



Independently prove or refute(R1)-(R3), challenge common-readout and
absolute-order details, check exact G221/G215 kernel/middle scope and
G225 positive-hole comparison. Search the maintained index for previous
readout/Gram/conditioning versions; novelty may only be scoped reuse.
Name any assumptions missing for infinite/direct-integral use. Develop
only a useful bounded correction; no c claim. Read current [restricted research revision] sources
and this draft; W66 integration belongs to root. Finish with full readback,
hash allowlist, STOP, normal exact OWN release and verified absence.

## 6. What arithmetic estimate is still missing

The theorem above removes the need to establish an independent
compensation estimate between the primitive cell and all of its
original common-prime/small-prime complements. Their return is the
explicit weighted convolution GC12, with the genuine boundary cost
GC8 and reconstruction error GC15. It does NOT bound the primitive
source below the accepted exponent, and it does NOT say that its
literal complement is a small field on the same shell.

The accepted arithmetic input still gives only beta=.8749. Its
available estimate on the new primitive component can be reconstructed
directly, without a hereditary mask assertion. Insert
1_{(d,e)=1}=sum_{q|d,e}mu(q); retain q squarefree and (q,6)=1.
Write d=qu,e=qv. Natural Mobius zeros impose (uv,6q)=1, and there is
no remaining (u,v)=1 condition. Therefore

    C_ij^6(s;Z)=sum_{q>=1;(q,6)=1}mu(q)q^(-2s)
                         V_(i,q)(s)V_(j,q)(s),
    V_(i,q)(s)=sum_{qu in I_i(Z);(u,6q)=1}mu(u)u^(-s). (GC21)

The coefficient is mu(q)^3=mu(q), not a positive replacement, and
the exact divided interval endpoints are retained. MG9--MG10 give
uniform coprime partial sums O_(eta)(U^beta*(6q)^eta). Abel summation
on the actual interval, for any fixed 0<a<beta, then gives

    |V_(i,q)(a+it)|
      <<_(a,beta,eta) (1+|t|)(6q)^eta
                                     (D_i^*/q)^(beta-a),

whenever the divided interval is nonempty. Here
D_i^*=min(Dmax_Z,sqrt(Z)*exp((i+1)*H_Z)), with the unchanged sharp
interval I_i(Z) inside this real enclosing endpoint. Summing the convergent
q^(-2beta+2eta) series, with eta<beta-1/2, proves

    |C_ij^6(a+it;Z)|
      <<(1+|t|)^2 (D_i^*D_j^*)^(beta-a).               (GC22)

All constants are uniform in the original bins and in t. At a=.75,
the resulting Gaussian one-height moment bound has exponent
2beta-2a=.2498, exactly the prior available exponent. The target
gamma=.87449 still requires .24898. Neither GC21 nor the absolute
q-series supplies the missing .00082. No termwise sign deletion,
suppression of t!=t', or collapse of the four diagonals is licensed.

Equivalently, GC10--GC13 transfer the original baseline to F_tau;
they preserve the exponent. The first coefficient of both arithmetic
operators is 1, so a norm bound for the reconstruction is not a strict
contraction of the retained source. A gain still requires arithmetic
cancellation in its complete signed moment. This is the precise
remaining obligation, rather than an unproved claim that the
primitive source is automatically smaller.

statement:
## G226. A dimension-free obstruction after paying a common linear readout

This develops the user's quaternion proposal beyond the G221 bounded
rank-four argument. Root's [discovery and initial proof](linear-readout/root-draft.md)
tested growing dimension and delayed absolute values as possible escapes.
The [independent review](linear-readout/review.md) sharpened the initial
constant4/pi^2 to the sharp1/2 and clarified the complex-kernel and
variable-readout scopes. The earlier argument remains historical evidence.

Let H be ANY real Hilbert space, T:H->R^2 a bounded real-linear map with
norm L, and(v_a) a finite family. Define y_a=T v_a,
M=sum_a|y_a| and B=sum_(a,b)|<v_a,v_b>|, with all ordered pairs. Then

    L^2 B >= M^2/2.                                      (226.1)

No dimension or upper bound on individual vectors appears. To prove it,
let u_a=y_a/|y_a| when y_a!=0 and u_a=0 otherwise. Define A:R^2->H by
A e_j=sum_a u_(a,j)v_a. Its Hilbert-Schmidt norm satisfies

    ||A||_HS^2=sum_(a,b)<v_a,v_b><u_a,u_b><=B,
    TA=sum_a |y_a|u_a u_a^T,
    M^2/2<=trace((TA)^2)=||TA||_HS^2<=L^2||A||_HS^2.

The positive2x2 operator has trace M and squared eigenvalue sum at least
M^2/2. This proves(226.1). Equality occurs for
T=identity on R^2, v_1=e_1,v_2=e_2. If all images lie on one real line,
the constant improves to1. More generally a target R^r gives the sharp
constant1/r, depending on OUTPUT dimension rather than lift dimension.
This is not the false termwise inequality
|<Tv_a,Tv_b>|<=L^2|<v_a,v_b>|.

Separate maps per index do not meet this hypothesis: v_i=e_i in R^n,
T_i(v)=v_i gives B=n, M=n and separate norms1. The COMMON recovery
v->sum_i v_i has norm sqrt(n), restoring the missing bill.

For an infinite family, apply(226.1) to every finite subset and take
nonnegative limits. No convergence of an infinite vector sum is needed
for this extended inequality. Each vector and readout must still exist.
The result includes arbitrary dimension, additional quaternion components,
and X-dependent choices of the common map, once its norm is paid.

Pointwise, if T_x v_a(x)=c_a K(q_a/x), then

    L_x^2 sum_(a,b)|<v_a(x),v_b(x)>|
       >=(1/2)[sum_a|c_a K(q_a/x)|]^2.                    (226.2)

For the G221 quaternion lift w_a(xi_a+t_a j), first-complex-coordinate
projection has L_x=1. Thus the actual full/middle source has quadratic
pointwise absolute price even WITHOUT a bound on t_a. The old necessary
dimension/readout tradeoff remains valid but is weaker: growing the
dimension does not reduce the price after a common linear recovery is paid.

There is a corresponding after-integration theorem. Put I=[X,2X],
measure dx/x and length ell=log2. Let v_a belong to its direct-integral
real Hilbert space, and let T_x be measurable common recovery maps with
essential supremum norm L_X<infinity on the shell. Assume

    T_x v_a(x)=c_a K(q_a/x),
    J(t)=int_1^2 K(t/u)du/u.

The common map Tcal(v)=int_I T_x v(x)dx/x has norm at most L_X sqrt(ell)
and sends v_a to c_a J(q_a/X). Apply(226.1) in the direct integral:

    L_X^2 ell sum_(a,b)|int_I <v_a(x),v_b(x)>dx/x|
       >=(1/2)[sum_a |c_a J(q_a/X)|]^2.                  (226.3)

All absolute values on the left are AFTER pair integration. A fixed
common ambient H is sufficient; measurable Hilbert bundles also work
when the stated direct integral and maps are well defined. It suffices
to apply the argument to finite central subsets; infinite absolute prices
then dominate those finite ones. Arbitrary x-dependent lifts are allowed.

The variable bound int_I ||T_x||^2 dx/x also bounds Tcal's squared norm,
but it does NOT automatically pay full shell-L2 reconstruction. For the
actual source-energy certificate the uniform L_X above is sufficient:
||sum_a T_x v_a||_(L2)^2<=L_X^2||sum_a v_a||_(L2(H))^2<=L_X^2 B_after
when the sums/convergence required for that upper estimate are justified.
If no such finite reconstruction bill is available, do not claim a
source upper bound from the averaged-functional inequality alone.

The right side has quadratic order for the exact Jordan source, including
its retained middle. Its fixed kernel is generally COMPLEX for nonreal
chi, and G215 gives K(t)=e^-t+O(e^-2t), so K is continuous, nonzero and
tends to0 at infinity. More generally these three properties imply J is
not identically zero: in logarithmic coordinates J'=K(t)-K(t/2); J=0
would force K(t)=K(2t), hence K=0 by repeated scaling to infinity.
Choose a fixed interval[a,b] in(0,infinity) on which |J|>=k>0. The
fixed-q squarefree count gives

    sum_(d>=1)|mu(d)chi(d)J(d/X)| >>_(q,K) X.              (226.4)

For G215's middle, d in[aX,bX] lies in x^alpha<d<=2x log x for EVERY
x in[X,2X] once X is large, because alpha<1. Thus these central vectors
have exactly the same integrated image c_d J(d/X); they alone prove the
same lower bound in(226.3). No omitted tail, principal main term or
varying-cutoff identity has been discarded. The actual compensated K,
not the uncentered Jordan source, is used.

For the G218 Gaussian, positivity directly gives |J(t)| bounded below
on[1,2]. Fixed holes give mass >>X; polynomial-sized holes, or their
positive normalized field averages, give >>X/log(2X) by G225, with all
presented character zeros retained. Applying(226.3) separately to each
hole also permits a positive average of its complete lifted price.
No arbitrary oscillatory joint-label kernel is identified with that
positive-mask construction.

These are TOTAL-price lower bounds. To conclude the same for the absolute
off-diagonal, also pay the diagonal. In G221's bounded lifts with fixed
C, sum_a int_I ||v_a||^2=O(C^2 X), so the quadratic lower bound survives
its removal. Without such a bound an unbounded lift may move the bill
onto its diagonal; no off-diagonal assertion is then made.

The complete returned shell-L2 target gamma=1-c requires energy exponent
2-2c. The paid source-index absolute-Gram price above has exponent at
least2, leaving deficit2c: .24 at c=.12, .2502919272 at conditional c11,
.25030 at c=.12515,1/3 at c=1/6 and1/2 at c=1/4. G215/G218 supply their
own L2-to-L1 and all-height returns; the price theorem proves none of
the necessary signed estimates and imports no cross-family transfer.

The scope matters: one vector per actual source coefficient, a common
linear recovery, the COMPLETE pairwise absolute Gram, and a paid norm.
Cancellation inside blocks before the absolute value, full signed
companion comparisons, nonlinear reconstruction, or genuinely different
X-dependent profiles with a proved return remain open. The theorem is
not a lower bound on the actual signed source energy. It strengthens
G221's finite-dimensional price and closes its generic after-integration
escape for these fixed Gaussian/Jordan profiles and common recoveries;
it does not reject quaternion or matrix approaches as a whole.
