# Independent W44 review: exact Gaussian return, transport cost and two parked audits

The analytic implications in A and B are valid in their stated fixed-source scopes. A supplies a complete moving-order criterion with the sufficient return `gamma=eta+d/2`; only `d=0` is proved equivalent, at the same exponent, to the original complete Gaussian moment. B gives an exact source transport certificate, including the balancing charge and infinite tail. Its constructed plan recovers the buffered baseline and proves no improvement. C proves a genuine rough-prime cutoff zero approaching 1; it is a counterexample to inherited cutoff stability, not a lower bound for the full field. D is the explicitly credited regularization duplicate. E is a correct arbitrary-input finite decoder obstruction.

There is no new arithmetic estimate and no new c. The controller's accepted written `c6=.125139`, its original fixed ordinary/Eisenstein scope, and pending new endpoint kernels remain the premises. The separate old endpoint receipt is not a receipt for new kernels. W44 did not contribute that endpoint change. Current sufficient first-gain conditions are `eta+d/2<.874861` and `q+d<.749722`.

The independent protected audit is **W44-30**, and the uniform audit is **W44-12**. They add exact source calculations and qualified obstructions below. Neither proves that every possible perturbative or coding construction fails. No extra model-provider route, child, canonical, tracker, Git, or proof-assistant work was used. Controller acceptance and integration remain separate.

## 1. Scope, chronology and immutable inputs



 The author manifest records final content at `02:45:50.906360Z`, same-context recovery after stream error `[private operational identifier omitted]`, and no repeated selection. These are author-recorded events, not independently measured transport latency. The final wake was received and this review began before the observed `02:51:00Z` clock. Actual final readback/freeze and claim-release receipts accompany this report.

Exact author inputs, all under `[restricted provenance path] research revision]-drafts/wild44/`:

| Input | Bytes | SHA-256 |
|---|---:|---|
| report.md | 32759 | `43cd4167c154a305d1bf61eecd9c58cf61764ca17b251eca746e7cfd62d2529f` |
| manifest.json | 9184 | `42f74843bbabcafd1d7c09475c74309a3f2006b6ef63bcd01a971acbf7e34c26` |
| seeds.json | 22246 | `b75eb1435a6e841d169003bc165eb4e7613a5037a9312b3904dac6fa0f1f0cf4` |

All 13 files listed in the manifest were read completely as bytes, decoded, and checked against both lengths and hashes; the manifest itself was separately hash-bound. The entire 327-line report was read. Draw/check scripts were inspected without executing them. In particular the author's `checks.json` binds an earlier report hash, and the final report explicitly identifies the later explanatory edits; this is not represented as a numerical run against final bytes. The final manifest binds the final report, and the independent analytic review uses those final bytes.

The full collective attempt map and retained review history govern novelty: all original 29 families/109 child IDs remain, with later [private research revision]–59 obligations. Relevant exact sources were inspected again: current-proof G25–32/G53–54; [private research revision] MM-D2 and MM-[restricted research revision]; W36 R36.20–22; Sol01 S45/S51; and current portfolio entries. W43's newly reviewed Newton and nonalgebra results also constrain audit30. A compact index is navigation, not evidence that every historical seed was tested.

### Literal selection and independent audit freeze

The author reserved 08 strongest, 07 reach and 24 most different. The p labels are uncalibrated typicality judgments, not truth probabilities or measured token probabilities. Exact strict numerical pools, reconstructed independently from **all** seed groups with only prior exclusions, are:

| Draw | Eligible count | Saved zero-based index | Result |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| p<.10 | 24 | 12 | W44-18 |
| p<.01 | 13 | 2 | W44-17 |
| all remaining | 25 | 8 | W44-11 |

The .10 pool includes groups 1–6; the .01 pool includes groups 2–6, with no omitted qualifying group-1 card. Pool bytes/hashes, numerical labels, exclusions and selected entries match. The code uses one `secrets.randbelow(cardinality)` call per saved draw and exclusive receipt creation. Receipts record zero rerolls. OS entropy was not saved as a replayable seed: the review verifies exact pools and saved indices, not an invented entropy replay or an independent reconstruction of the author's whole tool chronology. The seed file's recipe digest is `ad761b6b8d2e82e9d1154bdaa702d9c4d13141bdddb2a78c43bd586399fbb549`. The author honestly discloses historical orientation in required lane instructions before its detailed-history freeze boundary.

Our ALL30 pool and priority were frozen/read back at `02:43:16.972308Z`, SHA `9c6d0ce11f01bc5437e5eb2751a25c881c50cba6e9b755ed0014f01d652f4738`. One independently drawn integer in `[0,30!)`, factorial-unranked to a uniform full permutation, was saved at `02:43:49.328893Z`, SHA `40c19472fd70b65c41db08c9ccfea480d14385747b4147bd72e32c96ffd7cf19`. Pool, rank seed, complete permutation and reasons remain unchanged. Both orders preceded this reviewer's exposure to author selections or outcomes. They did **not** precede all author development: the later author manifest records a report prefix already saved at 02:35. The guarantee is independent pre-intake commitment, not a fabricated global clock ordering.

No selection-only event reached this critic. After the sole final handoff summary, but before reading the full report, the frozen rule excluded exactly `08,07,24,18,17,11`. It chose first priority **30**, then first eligible uniform-permutation entry **12**, excluding 30. `audit-selection.json` is 812 bytes, SHA `16c3ac8237e00ef20b2944c1beb0fbfc356d2a9f49a26711a86d3bd540269e9a`. No new draw, post-outcome preference or reroll occurred. Both were author-untested cards; they are now independently audited rather than retrospectively counted as author tests.

## 2. A: exact Gaussian source and the moving-order return

Fix `tau,kappa>0`, the actual sequence `a(n)`, and a fixed `B>0` with `C_B=sum |a(n)|n^-B<infinity`. Ideals can replace integers only with the same explicit norm-weighted absolute hypothesis. Put

    F(x)=sum_n a(n) g_tau(log(n/x)),
    W_X(v)=g_kappa(v) F(X exp(v)),
    sigma=tau+kappa, nu=tau*kappa/sigma, alpha=kappa/sigma,
    w_n=log(n/X), b_n=g_sigma(w_n).

Completing the square gives exactly

    g_kappa(v)g_tau(w-v)=g_sigma(w)g_nu(v-alpha*w).       (R1)

The prefactors agree because `kappa*tau=sigma*nu`. The v², vw and w² coefficients respectively give `1/kappa+1/tau=1/nu`, `alpha/nu=1/tau` and `1/sigma+alpha²/nu=1/tau`. There is no missing normalization or X-power. With Fourier transform `hat f(t)=integral f(v)e^(-itv)dv`,

    hat W_X(t)=e^(-nu*t²/2) sum_n a(n)b_n e^(-i alpha*t*w_n),
    sum_n |a(n)|b_n <= C_B X^B e^(sigma*B²/2)/sqrt(2pi*sigma).
                                                               (R2)

This is an absolutely justified formula at every real Fourier height. It comes from the original convergent coefficient sum, not an assumed reciprocal continuation. For fixed real/complex compact windows, Gaussian decay also justifies the differentiations used here.

For every real `r>=0`, define `N_r²=(2pi)^-1 integral (1+t²)^-r |hat W_X(t)|² dt`. Splitting at any `T>=1` and applying R2 to the **unweighted W tail** proves

    ||W_X||_2 <= (1+T²)^(r/2) N_r(X)
                  + C X^B e^(-nu*T²/2).                (R3)

The inverse Sobolev factor does not multiply the high-frequency tail. This is the decisive response to the general objection that a negative norm conceals high frequencies. The inequality would be false without an envelope of this kind for arbitrary functions.

If `d=limsup r_X loglog X/log X<infinity`, choose the fixed cutoff constant `M>2(B+A)/nu` and `T²=M log X`. Then

    (1+M log X)^(r_X/2) <= X^(d/2+epsilon)

eventually for every epsilon>0, while the tail is `O(X^-A)`. Hence an every-epsilon bound `N_(r_X)(X)<<X^(eta+epsilon)` on **every sufficiently large dyadic shell**, with constants independent of X, gives

    ||F||_(L2([X,2X],dx/x)) << X^(eta+d/2+epsilon).      (R4)

The division by the fixed positive minimum of `g_kappa` on `[0,log2]` costs only a constant. The kernel parameters, source, B and buffers are fixed before X; r may move as stated. Good subsequences or a finite screen are insufficient.

The converse is correctly proved at the **unshifted** exponent eta: since `N_r<=||W_X||_2`, decompose the v-line into intervals `[k log2,(k+1)log2]`. The shell moment assumption controls the field there at scale `X2^k`; the summation over k is finite after Gaussian weighting. For small scales x<=1,

    |F(x)| <= C exp(-(log x)²/(2tau)),

because `(log n-log x)² >= (log n)²+(log x)²` and the remaining weighted coefficient sum is finite by C_B. Compact scales are handled by normal convergence. Thus there is no missing left-tail or shifted-shell assumption. This proves the stated equivalence when `d=0`. For positive d, the report supplies only R4 and that unshifted converse; it proves neither a shifted equivalence nor sharpness of the loss on actual arithmetic sources.

### Exact scalar and zero return

The Gamma integral yields, for r>0,

    E_(r,nu)(z)=1/Gamma(r) integral_0^infinity
       q^(r-1)e^-q g_(2(nu+q))(z)dq,
    E_(0,nu)(z)=g_(2nu)(z).

Its Fourier multiplier is exactly `e^(-nu*t²)(1+t²)^-r`, with the `(2pi)^-1` inversion factor already in the Gaussian. Consequently

    N_r² = sum_(n,m) a(n)conj(a(m)) b_n b_m
               E_(r,nu)(alpha log(n/m)).               (R5)

The double series converges absolutely since `E(z)<=E(0)<=g_(2nu)(0)` and `sum |a|b<infinity`. All ordered pairs, powers and natural character zeros remain. E is positive, but this does not make the coefficient products nonnegative or authorize removal of negative cross terms. For bounded coefficients the true diagonal is `O(X)` uniformly in r; divisor-bounded coefficients permit the stated epsilon allowance. The diagonal can be paid below `X^(2eta)` only with the corresponding eta>1/2 buffer; positivity is not a substitute for cancellation at smaller eta.

For `a(n)=mu(n)chi(n)` the character twist is pointwise. The symbol `*` in later coefficient identities denotes Dirichlet convolution. Mellin Fubini first on Re s>1 gives

    integral_0^infinity F(x)x^-s dx/x = e^(tau*s²/2)/L(s,chi).

R4 plus dyadic Cauchy–Schwarz gives absolute locally uniform Mellin convergence on `Re s>gamma=eta+d/2`; the small-x Gaussian bound handles zero. Multiplying the meromorphic identity by L excludes any zero in that half-plane. A principal pole at 1 is handled by the usual cancelling zero of the reciprocal, not treated as an L-zero. This proof covers arbitrarily large finite heights without requiring an unproved uniform reciprocal growth estimate on a continued line. No X-dependent source was Mellin transformed.

For the literal f3 twist, an explicit scope check is useful. Its prime-power values are `f3(p^j)=-1` for p!=3,j>=1, and `f3(3^j)=1`. With `z_p=chi(p)p^-s`, the numerator in `D_(f3 chi)=W_chi/L(s,chi)` is

    W_chi = (1-2z_2)/[(1-z_2)²(1-z_3)²]
               product_(p>=5) (1-2z_p)/(1-z_p)².        (R6)

Zero-extended ramified factors mean z_p=0. The p>=5 product converges normally and is nonzero for Re s>1/2; the p2 factor can have zeros on Re s=1, not in `1/2<Re s<1`. Thus the paid f3 return is valid in the open target strip, with the already known right boundary retained. One must not claim that W_chi is nonzero everywhere on the line Re s=1. This qualification agrees with the established G28/G53 source returns and requires no modification to A's useful claim.

For the original ideal Möbius coefficient, the analogous Mellin identity has numerator 1 and its own Hecke L-function. A separately proved full ideal moment is required; an ordinary f3 estimate does not imply it. Fixed ordinary characters and the originally specified fixed finite-order trivial-infinity Hecke family are the available scopes. No angular, growing-conductor, or generic-character uniformity follows from notation alone.

**Verdict A:** accept R1–R6 and A1–13/A10 as a conditional analytic interface. The exact complete R5/A13 arithmetic bound remains open. Fixed-order negative norms and Gaussian spectral localization are prior; the useful increment here is the exact localized source, arbitrary moving order and explicit `d/2` budget, not a new negative-norm mechanism or a proved weaker arithmetic exponent. The Sol01 S45 norm was on a raw finite atomic measure over the full line; it is not this already smoothed and localized norm.

## 3. B: full source transport and its actual cost

For untwisted f3 each literal coefficient is ±1. Let `phi_n(v)=g_kappa(v)g_tau(log(n/X)-v)`, in the Hilbert space with norm H^-r. The squared feature distance is

    d_r(n,m)²=J(n,n)+J(m,m)-2J(n,m),

with J exactly R5. It is not just a function of log(n/m): the radial factors b_n,b_m are essential. This is nonnegative because it is a Hilbert distance, not merely because J has positive entries.

Take `N=floor(X exp(C sqrt(log X)))` and ghost position `x_*=X exp(D sqrt(log X))`, fixed D>C, with `C²,D²>2sigma(1+A)`. The exact feature norm is `||phi_n||_2=sqrt(g_(2nu)(0))b_n`, so the omitted **entire** tail is

    sum_(n>N)||phi_n||_(H^-r)
       <= X^(1-C²/(2sigma)+o(1))=O(X^-A),              (R7)

after using the strict margin. Integral comparison includes the `exp(C sqrt(log X))` factor in o(1). The compensating charge has magnitude at most N and its own feature norm `O(X^(-D²/(2sigma)))`, hence is also below the same chosen error. Both bounds are uniform in all r>=0. The real ghost label is auxiliary, not an invented arithmetic atom.

Add charge `-sum_(n<=N)f3(n)` at that label. Positive and negative measures now have equal mass `M=max(number of original positive atoms, number of original negative atoms)<=N`. For any nonnegative plan pi with exactly those marginals,

    balanced field = sum_(n,m) pi(n,m)(phi_n-phi_m),
    N_r(X) <= sqrt(M C_r(X))+O(X^-A),
    C_r(X)=sum_(n,m)pi(n,m)d_r(n,m)².                  (R8)

The Hilbert Cauchy–Schwarz step retains all field cross terms through its upper bound. It does not assume equal original sign counts or drop an unmatched cell. Since `M<=X^(1+o(1))`, a genuine complete all-scale `C_(r_X)(X)<<_epsilon X^(q+epsilon)`, q>-1, gives A's eta=(1+q)/2 and therefore

    gamma=(1+q+d)/2.                                  (R9)

For a fixed complex ordinary character, split the actual coefficients into real and imaginary signed measures, including their zero values. Each needs its own exact plan and balancing ghost and a B4 cost bound; two fixed triangle constants do not alter R9. B2's explicit rank-matching construction is stated for untwisted f3, not silently as a uniform twisted/ideal theorem.

### Reconstructing the baseline, including the end ranks

Assume the accepted **buffered** fixed-source summatory input `S(t)=O(t^beta)`, `1/2<beta<1`. For c6 any fixed beta>.874861 is permitted by the retained premise; beta=.874861 itself is not supplied. The G28 inverse coefficients transfer the buffered Möbius/A input to f3. Then counts of ± signs are `t/2+O(t^beta)`. Equal rank pairing satisfies `p_k,m_k asymp k` and `|p_k-m_k|=O(k^beta)`, uniformly up to N. The excess O(N^beta) ranks lie in `[N-O(N^beta),N]`, so the ghost does not arbitrarily collect interior mass.

Writing w=log(n/X), differentiate the exact product expression:

    ||d phi_w/dw||_2² = b(w)² g_(2nu)(0)
             [w²/sigma²+alpha²/(2nu)].                 (R10)

The mixed integral vanishes since `integral g_nu g_nu'=0`. The paired log distance is `O(n^(beta-1))`; integrating the derivative gives a cost bounded by

    C n^(2beta-2)(1+w²)exp(-c w²)

for a fixed c>0 after a harmless variance enlargement. To justify it uniformly even when X and n are widely separated, absorb `|w|n^(beta-1)` into `epsilon*w²+C_epsilon` above a fixed initial threshold. The finitely many smaller n have superpower Gaussian decay. Summing over n about X yields `O(X^(2beta-1))`: the logarithmic variable leaves an integrable `exp((2beta-1)w-cw²)(1+w²)`.

The excess ghost pair costs are `O(X^(beta-C²/sigma+o(1))+X^(beta-D²/sigma+o(1)))`, below that bound after choosing the already free fixed tail constants. Thus

    C_r(X)<<X^(2beta-1), uniformly for all r>=0.         (R11)

R9 returns beta for d=0; positive d gives the weaker beta+d/2. R11 is an upper bound on one plan, not an optimal-cost lower bound. It leaves open a better source-specific plan. Matched-Max MM-D2 already owns monotone log transport with a paid ghost; this adaptation earns the exact new metric and full f3 Gaussian-tail accounting, not a second discovery of the transport method. W41's single-prime-edge obstruction is not contradicted: these pairs may have arbitrary near-one ratios.

**Verdict B:** accept B1–9 with these quantifiers. The required new cost is strictly `q+d<.749722`; none is proved. Large-r attenuation alone does not deliver that estimate. No native H kernel, masks, projectors, Gauss roots or its physical normalization have been identified with this new Gaussian metric, so no H-branch gain may be imported or added.

## 4. C, D and E: useful failures in their exact scopes

### C: actual rough-prime zero law

The full two-variable product `(1-z)(1-w)` has no zero in the open unit polydisk; deleting its top face gives `1-z-w`, with the zero (1/2,1/2). For k singleton variables the maximal common open polydisk radius is 1/k, by the triangle inequality and the equal-coordinate witness. This is an elementary coefficient calculation, not an application of Lee–Yang theory.

The actual polynomial `sum_(n<=5)mu(n)n^-s=1-2^-s-3^-s-5^-s` is negative at 1 and positive at 2, with positive derivative on the real line. Its unique real zero above 1 belongs to this cutoff polynomial; it says nothing contradictory about 1/zeta.

For the stronger scalable example, retain exactly

    H_N(s)=sum_(n<=N, P^-(n)>sqrt N)mu(n)n^-s
          =1-sum_(sqrt N<p<=N)p^-s.                    (R12)

P^-(1)=infinity. Any composite with every prime factor strictly above sqrt N exceeds N; equality at a lower prime boundary is excluded. For large N this source also has the actual f3 values, since all retained nonunit primes exceed 3. Thus the prime-power, strict-endpoint and sign identities are literal.

The only external analytic input needed is `pi(t)=li(t)+o(t/log t)`, a consequence of the prime number theorem stated in [NIST DLMF 27.12](https://dlmf.nist.gov/27.12#E5), independently opened on 12 October 2026. No latest-error claim or power saving is imported. Put `L=log N`, `f_lambda(t)=t^(-1+lambda/L)`, with lambda in a fixed compact set. Stieltjes integration against the prime-counting error E gives endpoint errors `o(1/L)` and

    |integral_(sqrt N)^N E(t)f_lambda'(t)dt|
       <= C sup_(t>=sqrt N)(|E(t)|log t/t)
                    integral_(sqrt N)^N dt/(t log t)=o(1).

The constants are uniform on that compact lambda set. Substitution `t=N^v` in the main term gives

    sum_(sqrt N<p<=N)p^(-1+lambda/L)
       =I(lambda)+o(1), I(lambda)=integral_(1/2)^1 e^(lambda v)dv/v.
                                                               (R13)

I(0)=log2<1, I is strictly increasing, and I tends to infinity. Its unique positive solution I(lambda*)=1 traps the finite crossing by uniform convergence. The finite prime sum decreases strictly with real s, is >1 at s=0 and eventually <1 at s=1. Therefore its unique positive crossing satisfies

    sigma_N=1-lambda*/log N+o(1/log N), lambda*>0.      (R14)

The numerical lambda value is diagnostic only. R14 is a complete written proof based on R13. It refutes blanket inheritance of Euler-product nonvanishing by these precise rough cutoff cells. It also exhibits an exact wall between the unit term and the aggregate prime block that a tropical argument must pay. It does not show that every tropical decomposition or compensated partition source fails, or estimate the complete signed f3 Gaussian energy. The omitted small-prime/composite contributions may be indispensable cancelling terms.

### D: exact but already credited

`V_P=exp(sum_(p<=P)p^-s) product_(p<=P)(1-p^-s)` has

    log V_P=-sum_(p<=P)sum_(j>=2)p^(-js)/j,
    (1-z)e^z=1-sum_(j>=2)(j-1)z^j/j!.

These converge normally, with upper and lower modulus bounds on each `Re s>=rho>1/2`, since the first-prime channel was removed. Restoring it is not paid by bounding higher clusters. Under the separate open fixed-power prime-counting error, integration including the prime-2 atom gives

    D(s)=s integral_2^infinity [pi(u)-li_2(u)]u^(-s-1)du,
    1/zeta(s)=(s-1)V(s)exp(-J(s)-D(s)),
    J'(s)=(1-2^(1-s))/(s-1),

with J's constant fixed on Re s>1. The displayed derivative is entire after the removable value at 1, and the factor s-1 handles the principal pole. This matches W36 R36.20–22 verbatim in mathematical content, already credited to [private research revision] A12/W21 there. Ordinary PNT is not the missing fixed-power bound. No additional high-ceiling result is awarded to selected07.

### E: exact finite decoder obstruction

If a syndrome fibre contains opposite parities x,y, `delta_x-delta_y` lies in the kernel of all unsigned fibre sums but has nonzero signed parity readout. If parity is retained, normalized disjoint fibre rows `1_F/sqrt(|F|)` reconstruct it with coefficients `epsilon(F)sqrt(|F|)`, squared norm `sum|F|=2^k`. Both statements are exact. They concern arbitrary inputs on a uniform cube, not a lower bound on the actual detector. A source-specific decoder with a separately paid restricted input class remains open. W38/W41 already require the unexposed arithmetic parity covariance; E does not erase it.

## 5. Protected audit W44-30: full omitted-prime residual and inverse readout

The seed proposed homological perturbation of a finite Euler inverse, with the omitted-prime/cutoff operator treated as a small correction. Test the literal ordinary reciprocal source before abstract chain language. Let S be all primes <=Y, `m_S(n)=mu(n)1_(all prime factors of n lie in S)`, and let `1(n)=1`. Then

    (1*m_S)(n)=1_(P^-(n)>Y),
    e_S=delta_1-1*m_S=-1_(n>1, P^-(n)>Y).              (R15)

The first identity is inclusion–exclusion over the S-primes dividing n. It retains all rough prime powers and products, not only singleton primes. For a fixed ordinary character replace the two coefficient sequences by chi and `m_S chi`; the error becomes `-chi(n)1_(n>1,P^-(n)>Y)`, with literal zeros. Multiplicativity of chi proves the identity without removing a ramified term by hand.

In the convolution Banach algebra with norm `sum |a(n)|n^-sigma`, the exact error norm is

    ||e_S||_sigma=product_(p>Y)(1-p^-sigma)^-1-1       (R16)

when sigma>1, and is infinite for every sigma<=1. For fixed Y, the divergence needs no new PNT: the progression `n=1 mod product_(p<=Y)p` is rough and has positive density. For a fixed character also use `n=1 mod q` so its absolute value is 1. Thus no small absolute coefficient norm exists in the desired strip. Even a growing cutoff `Y<=N/2` leaves a finite-prefix lower bound

    ||e_S 1_(n<=N)||_sigma >= sum_(N/2<p<=N, p>Y)p^-sigma
       >> N^(1-sigma)/log N,                           (R17)

for fixed sigma<1 and sufficiently large N when Y<=N/2, by PNT. Fixed conductor exclusions remove only finitely many primes. This blocks that specific Neumann norm at the target exponents; it is not a lower bound for a signed physical field or every operator norm.

For every finite K, form the exact convolution polynomial

    v_K=m_S*(delta_1+e_S+...+e_S^(*K-1)).
    1*v_K=delta_1-e_S^(*K),
    mu=v_K+mu*e_S^(*K).                                (R18)

Twisting every coefficient by chi gives the identical character formulas. All omitted-prime interactions occur in the remainder. Initially on Re s>1, `M_S=product_(p<=Y)(1-chi(p)p^-s)` and `E=1-L M_S` give

    V_K=M_S sum_(j=0)^(K-1)E^j=(1-E^K)/L.             (R19)

At any hypothetical L-zero rho with Re rho>0, M_S(rho) is nonzero and E(rho)=1. The finite approximation is holomorphic there, with `V_K(rho)=K M_S(rho)`; its apparent reciprocal pole is cancelled. The remainder `E^K/L` retains the pole. Thus neither finite exact inversion nor a nilpotent finite divisor matrix supplies zero exclusion. Gaussian smoothing R18 is legitimate for fixed S,K by absolute coefficient bounds, but its complete remainder must still be controlled on every physical shell. A moving S or K additionally needs uniform constants and tails.

There is also a precise functional-space warning: in a unital Banach algebra of analytic functions with continuous evaluation at rho, multiplicativity of that evaluation gives `r_spectral(E)>=|E(rho)|=1`. A genuine submultiplicative norm with `||E||<1` throughout a region would already exclude such a zero; it cannot be assumed as free input. This does not prohibit a newly proved source-restricted contraction.

The finite check independently verifies all coefficients of R15/R18 through n=240, for Y=5, K=1,2,3,4, both untwisted and with the zero-extended character mod3. It proves only those finite identities; R15–19 have the written general proofs above. The geometric identity and lost-pole test overlap W43's actual Möbius Newton result; absolute inverse warnings and physical readout costs are already G32/MM-[restricted research revision]/W26/W36. The added audit makes this seed's full rough residual and intended norm explicit. **Disposition:** the default absolute perturbative inverse fails; a quantitatively paid different norm/physical contraction remains untested. No full-family impossibility or c gain is asserted.

## 6. Uniform audit W44-12: actual code fibres, not uniform bits

Let P be k primes and x their binary presence vector, u=(1,...,1). For a full-row-rank binary syndrome matrix A and weights w(x), Fourier expansion of the exact fibre indicator gives

    sum_(Ax=s)(-1)^(u.x)w(x)
       =2^-ell sum_(lambda in F2^ell)(-1)^(lambda.s)
                         hat w(u+A^T lambda),          (R20)

where `hat w(v)=sum_x(-1)^(v.x)w(x)`. Uniform fibres annihilate parity precisely when u is outside the row space, but for actual cutoff/Gaussian weights R20 asks for the indicated high-order Fourier coefficients. The dual-distance assertion alone does not make them zero.

Use the literal all-integer prime-presence factor with **P={2,5,7}**:

    a_P(n)=product_(p in P)(1-2*1_(p|n)),
    S(n)=1_(2|n).

The code syndrome is the first coordinate, so u=(1,1,1) is outside its row space. In the fictitious uniform bit cube each fibre has parity sum zero. In the actual residue system mod70, however, each syndrome has 35 residues and

    sum_(1<=n<=70, S(n)=0)a_P(n)=15,
    sum_(1<=n<=70, S(n)=1)a_P(n)=-15,
    E[a_P|S=s]=(-1)^s*(1-2/5)*(1-2/7)=(-1)^s*3/7.   (R21)

CRT gives independent Bernoulli occupation probabilities 1/p, not 1/2. With uniform residue measure the best mean-square decoder q(S) is this conditional expectation. Therefore

    inf_q E|a_P-q(S)|²=1-9/49=40/49.                 (R22)

This is an exact statement on an actual arithmetic partial-sign factor. It is not a bound on the complete f3 Gaussian field. It also allows the precise comparison that a small-dimensional syndrome is a substantial-loss representation of this partial parity, even though its uniform-cube fibre sums vanish.

The same bias and residual have a direct physical Gaussian meaning. Extend `h(t)=g_tau(log t)` by zero on t<=0; it is Schwartz and flat at zero. Fixed-period Poisson summation gives, for every residue a mod70 and every prescribed A>0,

    sum_(n>=1, n=a mod70)h(n/x)
       =x e^(tau/2)/70+O_(A,tau)(x^-A).               (R23)

Here `integral_0^infinity h(t)dt=e^(tau/2)` and arbitrary Fourier decay pays the nonzero frequencies. Dividing by `Z(x)=sum_n h(n/x)=x e^(tau/2)+O_A(x^-A)` transfers R21/R22 to this actual positive Gaussian occupation law, with superpower-small error. This uses a fixed period and makes no growing-coordinate or conductor claim.

Finally restore the full source rather than identifying a_P with f3. For any fixed ordinary chi, including its natural zeros, put

    r_P(n)=f3(n)a_P(n)chi(n),
    b_x(S)=E_x[a_P|S], c_x(S)=E_x[r_P|S],

where E_x uses the normalized positive Gaussian law at the physical x. Then exactly

    F_(f3 chi)(x)/Z(x)
       =E_x[b_x(S)c_x(S)]
          +E_x[(a_P-b_x(S))(r_P-c_x(S))].              (R24)

Every integer, prime power, sign, ramified zero and unexposed tail term remains in r_P. The second term is the full conditional covariance, not zero by code orthogonality. The first term can also cancel; neither term may be substituted for the full square moment. Writing Q(x) for the entire right side, the exact remaining target is

    integral_X^(2X) |Q(x)|² dx/x <<_epsilon X^(2gamma-2+epsilon).

With all mixed square terms retained and every sufficiently large dyadic X covered, this is equivalent to the original complete Gaussian squared-moment exponent2gamma, because Z(x) is asymptotic to a positive constant times x. This is a restated exact target, not a new estimate.

An exact independent residue check confirms R21/R22. With the literal f3 and zero-extended real character mod3 on n<=70, the finite analogue of R24 has full mean `-3/70`, predictable part `9/490` and conditional covariance `-3/49`; these add exactly. It demonstrates that the covariance is present, not its infinite-scale size. G54/W41 and W38 already own the general parity/occupation obligation; the new audit is this explicit binary-code source instance and quantified partial-sign loss. **Disposition:** uniform-fibre annihilation fails for the arithmetic law. A restricted decoder with a new bound for both terms in R24 remains open, and no full-f3 lower bound is claimed.

## 7. All 30 dispositions and novelty limits

Exactly six author first tests remain six. The other 24 remain author-untested; the independent review develops only 12 and 30 among them. The table does not turn an objection or nearest prior into a new test.

| W44 ID | Author status and independent disposition |
|---|---|
| 01 | Untested cutoff mixtures; new feasible kernel class and exact optimization return needed beyond positive averaging. |
| 02 | Untested fractional Riesz unsmoothing; retain fixed-character heights, principal pole and the already paid forward transfers. |
| 03 | Untested winding budget; integer signal does not price the full arbitrary-height contour. |
| 04 | Untested conditional expectation; G54 already retains the complete residual covariance. |
| 05 | Untested prime finite differences; actual mask commutator and derivative losses remain, with U-PRIME-CHAIN/W37 ancestry. |
| 06 | Untested reflected reciprocal detector; exact gamma/conductor factors and coupled zero response still needed. |
| 07 | Tested D; correct regularization/counterterm duplicate, no new singleton bound. |
| 08 | Developed A; accept exact moving-order interface and conditional return, complete signed A13 open. |
| 09 | Untested finite analytic syndrome; holomorphic interpolation remains an objection, not a native all-height disproof. |
| 10 | Untested negative-index interpolation; F23/F26 source positivity/index budget remains unpaid. |
| 11 | Tested E; accept scoped arbitrary-input decoder obstruction, restricted arithmetic decoder open. |
| 12 | Author-untested; independent uniform audit R20–24 rejects uniform-bit transfer and retains exact arithmetic covariance. |
| 13 | Untested displacement rank; distinguish finite matrix representation from G32/MM-[restricted research revision] physical readout and tail. |
| 14 | Untested information comparison; proper marginals cannot certify global signed parity by themselves. |
| 15 | Untested matching; B supplies a possible full metric, but Hall deficits, unmatched mass and phase need proof. |
| 16 | Untested harmonic-measure selection; analytic flux constraints do not automatically dominate source coefficients. |
| 17 | Tested/developed with24 in C; accept actual rough-cutoff zero law, no universal tropical impossibility. |
| 18 | Tested/developed B; accept complete feature transport contract and credited baseline, better cost open. |
| 19 | Untested quasiconformal dilation; the d-bar correction and zeros are not paid by a geometric stretch. |
| 20 | Untested Schur geometry; eliminating a nonnegative residual gives a lower bound, with no signed upper gain supplied. |
| 21 | Untested cutoff gas; D handles only the independent higher-prime-power duplicate, not connected cutoff interactions. |
| 22 | Untested determinant/spectral flow; actual entries, local source construction and complete scalar return needed. |
| 23 | Untested cumulant frustration; W38/W41 provide related proper-marginal failures, not a new arithmetic estimate. |
| 24 | Tested/developed C; accept exact cutoff stability failure, altered compensated stable sources remain possible. |
| 25 | Untested current switching; union preservation alone does not preserve all product masks and character phases. |
| 26 | Untested homotopy; U-PRIME-CHAIN/W37/Sol S51 retain the cutoff boundary and no free physical contraction. |
| 27 | Untested persistence; actual weighted long bars and their return still unbounded. |
| 28 | Untested twisted cover; projection/right-inverse norms and retained hard component remain necessary. |
| 29 | Untested Koszul assembly; individual acyclicity does not price mixed faces or complete cross terms. |
| 30 | Author-untested; independent protected audit R15–19 rejects the default absolute Neumann norm and tracks the retained pole; alternative source norm open. |

The useful admission is a new **contract** for the localized field, its paid transport adaptation, and a quantitative actual-prime **failure** of a cutoff stability proposal. These should be indexed beside, not in place of, the earlier valid negative-norm, transport, covariance, Newton and regularization results. D and the geometric identity in audit30 receive duplicate credit explicitly. No general statistical-mechanical, topological, coding or high-ceiling avenue is declared impossible.

## 8. Verification, remaining work and final handoff

`independent-check.py` ran once successfully and wrote `independent-checks.json` (5559 bytes, SHA `d9c09569ea7d651e4c21a7450f4d2aa81d1406d8c689d906dfa037b1e7af30d8`). It checked all immutable author files, strict all-group pools and saved indices, our original factorial permutation and fixed audit choices, exact rational Gaussian constants, literal rough-cutoff support including square endpoints, exact finite ordinary/twisted Neumann coefficient identities, arithmetic code fibres/covariance, and current rational conditional budgets. It ran no author helper and changed no author receipt. The analytic proofs above, not finite checks or model agreement, carry the infinite and all-height conclusions.

The displayed conditional examples remain arithmetically correct: eta=.87449,d=.0007 returns .87484; eta=5/6,d=.08 returns131/150; eta=.75,d=.24 returns.87. Their claimed c values are conditional, with no new arithmetic input here. A13 must still be estimated on every large shell, or B4 must be proved with the entire source and `q+d<.749722`. The audit variants likewise retain their explicit remainder/covariance obligations. Existing endpoint kernels remain pending under the controller's separate work.

No material algebraic repair to A–E is required. The qualifications that must survive integration are: no positive-d exponent equivalence; no unproved optimal transport cost; no deletion of signed cross terms or ghost; no whole-field consequence from the rough-cell zero; no numerator nonvanishing assertion on Re s=1; no ordinary-to-ideal or growing-conductor transfer; and no reinterpretation of an untested card as disproved.

Work view at closeout: mathematical review, source/hash verification, all30 dispositions and both fixed audits are complete. Final whole-file readback and immutable content hashes are recorded in `final-freeze.json`; the exact claim-release receipt is recorded separately. Following that freeze and release this reviewer stops writing this scope. Root alone decides canonical integration. No further author wake or outcome polling is needed.

## 3. Complete fixed integer-color sectors are actually paid

This is an arithmetic estimate, not just a new norm for M_chi. For a FIXED integer
t>=0 set

    f_t(n)=mu^2(n) t^omega(n) chi(n), with f_0=delta1.         (10)

Choose a fixed unramified prime p and a fixed integer J>=2. Put

    v_(p,J)=(delta1-p chi(p)delta_p)^(convolution J),
    P_p(s)=1-chi(p)p^(1-s),
    b_p(n)=chi(n)(1-p1_(p|n)).                              (11)

The actual b_p is bounded, periodic modulo pq, and has mean zero, including for
principal and imprimitive characters. Its partial sums are O_(p,q)(1). All
coefficients of v are literal: at p^a they are binom(J,a)(-p chi(p))^a for0<=a<=J.

### 3.1 A direct periodic hyperbola estimate

If b is any fixed bounded periodic sequence with mean zero, then for every fixed
integer t>=1,

    sum_(n<=x)b^(*t)(n) <<_(b,t) x^(1-1/t), x>=1.            (12)

For t=1 this is bounded partial sums. For t>1 set Y=x^(1/t). Every tuple with
product<=x has at least one coordinate<=Y. Inclusion-exclusion on those t events
gives a sum over j=1,...,t chosen short coordinates. For j<t, apply the induction
hypothesis to the remaining t-j coordinates, with beta=1-1/(t-j). Taking absolute
values ONLY on the chosen short coordinates costs at most

    C x^beta [sum_(n<=Y)|b(n)|n^(-beta)]^j
      << x^beta Y^(j(1-beta))=x^(1-1/t).

For j=t the product constraint is automatic since every coordinate<=Y. That term
is exactly(sum_(n<=Y)b(n))^t=O(1), not Y^t. Every overlap is retained with its
inclusion-exclusion sign. This proves(12), with real endpoints and fixed t constants.
No unproved divisor-problem exponent or growing-t uniformity is imported.

### 3.2 Squarefree local correction and the full convolution

On Re s>1,

    sum_n f_t(n)n^(-s)=prod_l(1+t chi(l)l^(-s))
                     =L(s,chi)^t G_t(s),
    G_t(s)=prod_l[(1+t z_l)(1-z_l)^t], z_l=chi(l)l^(-s).      (13)

The local polynomial has constant coefficient1 and zero linear coefficient.
For each FIXED t its coefficient series g_t has

    sum_n |g_t(n)| n^(-sigma)<infinity for every sigma>1/2.  (14)

This follows by multiplying the absolutely convergent local absolute series:
the first nonconstant power is l^(-2sigma), higher powers are finite, and all
ramified local factors equal1. There is no assertion that the product is nonzero;
only absolute convergence and holomorphy of G_t in this half-plane are used.

For0<=t<=J the exact convolution identity is

    v_(p,J)*f_t=b_p^(*t)*v_(p,J-t)*g_t,                     (15)

with the t=0 case interpreted directly as the finite sequence v_(p,J).
Combining(12)-(14), and paying every finite p-shift, gives

    |sum_(n<=x)(v_(p,J)*f_t)(n)|
      <<_(p,q,J,epsilon) x^(max(1/2,1-1/t)+epsilon)          (16)

for t>=1; the t=0 sum is O_(p,J)(1). To see the exponent when1-1/t>1/2,
sum |g_t(d)|d^(-(1-1/t)) using(14). At t=1 or2 use sigma=1/2+epsilon and
(x/d)^beta<=x^sigma/d^sigma for d<=x. Thresholds, constants and epsilon choices
are fixed before x. No output interval, p-valuation, or cofactor complement is
thrown away.

Let a_0=delta1 and for k>=1 define

    a_k(n)=mu^2(n)chi(n) k! S(omega(n),k).

The exact finite-difference identity

    a_k=sum_(t=0)^k(-1)^(k-t)binom(k,t) f_t                (17)

therefore pays the COMPLETE first J chain sectors, after the COMMON fixed filter:

    |sum_(n<=x) [v_(p,J)*sum_(k=0)^J(-1)^k a_k](n)|
       <<_(p,q,J,epsilon) x^(beta_J+epsilon),
    beta_J=max(1/2,1-1/J).                                  (18)

Every low sector uses the same filter P_p^J. Choosing a different filter for each
t and subtracting the results would not prove(18);(15) explicitly keeps the
remaining P powers. This estimate applies to principal as well as nonprincipal
ordinary characters and preserves their natural zeros. It is not a theorem for
native Hecke coefficients or q growing with x.

### 3.3 Explicit constants: no free growing-color import

One can make the constant in(12) explicit. Let D=max(1,||b||_infinity,
sup_y|sum_(n<=y)b(n)|). Write C_t for a permissible constant. The proof above gives

    C_1<=D,
    C_t<=D^t+sum_(m=1)^(t-1)binom(t,m)C_m[Dm]^(t-m),
    C_t<=(2D)^t(t!)^2.                                    (18a)

For the last inequality, insert the induction bound and divide by(2D)^t(t!)^2.
With j=t-m each summand is at most2^(-j)/j!, since m!m^j<=t!. Their sum is less
than e^(1/2)-1, while the D^t term supplies at most1/(2^t(t!)^2); together they are
less than1 for t>=2. This pays every binomial overlap and does not assert the
factorial upper bound is optimal.

Let c_(t,a)=[z^a](1+tz)(1-z)^t and define the actual absolute Euler price

    Gabs_t(sigma)=prod_l[1+sum_(a=2)^(t+1)|c_(t,a)|l^(-a sigma)].

For t fixed it is finite whenever sigma>1/2. For FIXED1/2<sigma<1 a coarse explicit
growing-t estimate is

    log Gabs_t(sigma) <= C_sigma t^(1/sigma) log(2t), t>=2.  (18b)

To prove it, split at Y=t^(1/sigma). For l>Y use
|c_(t,a)|<=t^a(1/a!+1/(a-1)!) and t*l^(-sigma)<1, so the local logarithm is
O(t^2 l^(-2sigma)). Summing over ALL integers beyond Y bounds the total by
O_sigma(t^(1/sigma)). For l<=Y the local absolute series is at most
(1+t l^(-sigma))(1+l^(-sigma))^t. Its logarithm is at most
log(1+t)+t*l^(-sigma); summing over all integers up to Y gives the stated bound.
Ramified primes only reduce this absolute price. This is an upper bound, not a
lower-bound obstruction to a sharper estimate.

For any sigma>1/2 with sigma>=1-1/t, the actual constant in the t>=1 term of(16)
can therefore be bounded by

    (2D)^t(t!)^2 Gabs_t(sigma)(1+p^(1-sigma))^(J-t).         (18c)

The last factor is the COMPLETE summatory price of v_(p,J-t), retaining every
p^a argument and its coefficient p^a. The low-color combination also carries the
explicit factors binom(J+1,t+1) from(19); its t=0 term is at most
(J+1)(1+p)^J. For fixed J these are harmless fixed constants. For a growing J they
must all be paid; neither the sublinear chain degree nor the factor1/k! in(2)
makes them automatically subpower. In particular the bound(18b) at a fixed target
sigma can grow too quickly at J comparable to log x/loglog x. This is the price
of the actual proof, not a theorem ruling out a better growing-color argument.

# [private research revision]: same-bin joint cut and a smaller signed core

Accept G197-G198 relative to the literal PR9/[restricted research revision]/[restricted research revision] source contracts.
The [author](joint-window/report.md) pays two actual dominance classes;
the [independent review](joint-window-review/report.md) proves an additional
coupled cutoff that halves the remaining repeated-prime exponent. This
does not cover every row or improve c11=.1251459636. The full signed
complement and inherited admission obligations remain OPEN.

## Exact source and quantifiers

Use Eisenstein ideals with the original primary/unit convention, excluded
set S, natural character zeros and entire orientation
phi_u(n)=nu(n)psi_u(n)^(+/-1). The fixed finite phase nu need not have order6.
For R=U^r,D=U^m, retain the centrally normalized polynomials

    M_u(R)=R^(-1/2) sum_a mu(a)phi_u(a)W_I(Na/R),
    S_u(D)=D^(-1/2) sum_b phi_u(b)W_P(Nb/D),  B_u=M_u(R)S_u(D).

Q_u is the unchanged product of original disjoint prime slots, total width v,
with their individual coefficients, pools, holes, profiles and independent
heights. Q is never divided out. Fix delta in[17/25,7/10], v in[0,1/20],
0<eta<=1/1000. Choose [G137's cutoff](../[private research revision]/wild56-integration.md)
t=t_*(delta,v)-eta BEFORE witnesses. Work in its entire crossing window
|r-r_*(t)|<=2eta with the prescribed endpoint padding. The actual saturated
witness has r+m>=t-small and m<=1/2+small. All unions over labels, internal
bins and dyads have their existing small losses. No all-length claim follows.

The licensed nonprincipal supported rows Omega have ONE internal grade beta,
with beta>=delta-small and beta<=3/4, and the same character, real power and
height in both factors. Literal PR9 B0.13-20 supplies

    |S_u(D)|^2 >= D^beta U^(-epsilon_det),
    |S_u(E)|^2 <= H_J U^(epsilon_det) E^beta,  E<=C D.       (1)

Use the direct unreflected Mellin line for every shortened E, including the
small tolerance above m=1/2. Nonempty subunit annuli have E bounded below;
smaller annuli are empty. H_J is a fixed polynomial in original heights.
Keeping beta until division is essential: replacing only the lower grade
by delta would leave an unpaid D^(beta-delta).

PR9 B3.31 gives the fully marked MI bound

    ||M_u(E)Q_u||^2_all <= H_J U^(1+epsilon), E<=C R,       (2)
    r'+2v<=1-c1,  2r'+8v<=3-c2.

G137 supplies positive margins throughout the whole window; shortening
improves both gates. Bounded negative lengths are clipped only by bounded
dilations, and at length0 the two gates retain ample slack. This uses all
original slots, not an unmarked estimate with an unpaid slot price.

Tensor Sobolev applies (2) to each derivative of the original smooth
profiles and independently varying height coordinates. Arithmetic cutoffs
are fixed in U first, with a common polynomial outer box; the profiles
vanish off their exact support. Fixed punctures are restored as below.
Choose smooth orders/internal height losses before the final external
height degree. Include all polynomial divisor counts in U^B before choosing
the discarded-tail order N in U^B T_ht^(-N). The [restricted research revision]/[restricted research revision] internal floor is
not charged with the enlarged external degree. No new uniform high-height
or growing-conductor theorem is imported. A positive child uses its own
actual witness; a dominance class is not inherited through a signed split.

## G197. Two paid classes with complete shared-prime cost

For an ideal q define A_G(q)=sum_(d|q,Nd>=G) mu(q/d). Then
sum_(q|g)A_G(q)=1_(Ng>=G), A_G(q)=0 below G and |A_G(q)|<=tau(q).
Since a is squarefree, the high-gcd piece is exactly

    B_g=sum_(q sf) A_G(q)mu(q)phi(q)^2/(Nq)
                      M^(q)(R/Nq) S(D/Nq).                (3)

The extra inverse mask is restored by the COMPLETE q-smooth series

    M^(q)(E)=sum_(h q-smooth) phi(h)/sqrt(Nh) M(E/Nh).

All powers and natural zeros remain. Its absolute mass is at most
product_(p|q)(1-(Np)^(-1/2))^(-1) <<_epsilon (Nq)^epsilon.
Polynomial fixed inverse punctures are handled in the same way. Extracted
row phases are contractions after taking a positive norm, never new MI
column coefficients. Minkowski, (1)-(2) and ideal counting give

    ||B_g Q||^2_Omega << H_J U^(1+beta*m+epsilon) G^(-beta). (4)

Let s2(b)=product_p p^floor(v_p(b)/2). The high-square plain part is
sum_(Nk>=H) A_H(k)phi(k^2)/(Nk) S(D/(Nk)^2), with k unrestricted.
Its pointwise absolute bound is H_J U^epsilon D^(beta/2)H^(-beta).
The intersection with the high-gcd part uses L=lcm(q,k^2)=q k^2/(q,k):

    B_gs=sum_(q sf,k) A_G(q)A_H(k)mu(q)phi(qL)/sqrt(Nq NL)
                         M^(q)(R/Nq) S(D/NL).             (5)

Norm notation suppresses N only in the following positive mass:

    w_beta(q,k)=q^(-1-beta/2) k^(-1-beta) (q,k)^((1+beta)/2).

At q=k=p the local weight is p^(-3/2-beta); falsely independent divisibility
would miss p^((1+beta)/2). Put d=(q,k),k=de. The complete k-tail satisfies

    sum_(Nk>=H) k^(-1-beta)(q,k)^((1+beta)/2)
      << H^(-beta) sum_(d|q) d^((beta-1)/2)
      <= H^(-beta) tau(q).                               (6)

For d<=H use the e-tail; for d>H use the complete e-sum and
d^(-(1+beta)/2)<=H^(-beta)d^((beta-1)/2). Thus every large common divisor
is paid. The q-tail supplies G^(-beta/2), including all divisor/restoration
losses on the polynomial support. Squaring yields

    ||B_gs Q||^2 << H_J U^(1+beta*m+epsilon) G^(-beta)H^(-2beta).

Define B_s=M S_bad-B_gs and B_c=B-B_g-B_s. Hilbert triangle proves
||B_sQ||^2<<H_J U^(1+beta*m+epsilon)H^(-2beta). No signed-subset
monotonicity is asserted. Partition actual rows by |B_g|>=|B|/4, then
|B_s|>=|B|/4 outside the first class, then the remainder. Dividing (4)
and its B_s counterpart by the SAME lower bound (1) gives original inverse
moment savings delta*log_U(G) and 2delta*log_U(H), after losses.

At G=U^(4eta),H=U^(2eta), each pre-loss saving is at least(68/25)eta.
The remaining B_c has magnitude>|B|/2 and unmarked repeat factor<GH^2.
Every original slot remains, so the full repeat factor is<GH^2 NP.

## G198. A coupled cutoff halves the residual repeat width

Fix T before witnesses. Split original tuples by
F(a,b)=N(a,b)*(Ns2(b))^2>=T, obtaining B=B_T+C_T. The two-variable inverse

    A_T(q,k)=sum_(d|q,e|k) mu(q/d)mu(k/e)1_(Nd*(Ne)^2>=T)

satisfies sum_(q|g,k|s)A_T(q,k)=1_(Ng*(Ns)^2>=T), is divisor bounded,
and vanishes unless Nq*(Nk)^2>=T. Thus (5) is the exact expansion of B_T
with A_G A_H replaced by A_T. It retains every collision and natural zero.

In each dyadic q,k box with Q0 K0^2>=T/8, the COMPLETE tail estimate (6)
and its q-tail give mass <<U^epsilon Q0^(-beta/2)K0^(-beta)
<<U^epsilon T^(-beta/2). There are only O(log^2 U) supported boxes.
Minkowski and (1)-(2) prove

    ||B_T Q||^2_Omega << H_J U^(1+beta*m+epsilon)T^(-beta). (7)

An independent root check splits q=dq',k=dk',d=(q,k): after extracting
(D0^3 Q0 K0^2)^(-beta/2), the common-divisor box mass leaves
D0^((beta-1)/2), summable since beta<1. This confirms why the shared-prime
correction is harmless here rather than silently absent.

Keep the two original paid row classes FIRST. Outside them, add the class
|B_T|>=|B|/2. Equation(7) and (1) save delta*log_U(T) in the ORIGINAL
inverse moment on this third, disjoint class. All remaining rows satisfy
|C_T|>|B|/2. For every surviving tuple, since a is squarefree,

    ab/rad(ab)=(a,b)*b/rad(b),  b/rad(b) divides s2(b)^2,
    N(abP/rad(abP)) < T NP.                               (8)

At T=U^(4eta), the pre-loss saving is again at least(68/25)eta, exceeding
eta by(43/25)eta. The unmarked repeat width decreases from8eta to4eta;

improvement at the same calibration, not a new norm ordering between cores.

## 8. Exact residual and conditional return

In the finite expansion of N(F_hi), let R_hi be the real ordered cross-class sum, including its actual derivative coefficient inner products and R18's *actual* kernel, restricted to

    Nc>U^(6/5), Nc'>U^(6/5),
    Q>U^(6/5), Q1/Q3>U^(1/2).                        (R22)

These conditions are invariant under swapping l and l', so conjugate pairs make the sum real. All coefficients, orientations, zeros and phases are preserved. The exact split is

    N(F_hi)=D_hi+P_hi+R_hi,

where D_hi is the full same-class contribution and P_hi is the disjoint paid off-class union. We have an absolute upper bound on P_hi and the positive majorant for D_hi. A one-sided upper bound on R_hi is sufficient; individual remaining pairs need not be small or negative.

Consequently, for any fixed 0<xi<=1/100, if the *unproved* contract

    R_hi<=H_J U^[E_K(delta,v)-xi+epsilon]             (OPEN-[restricted research revision])

holds for every required fixed natural family, positive majorant, slot system, real rectangle and height list, R10 and R21 give

    N(F)<=H'_J U^[E_K(delta,v)-xi+epsilon].            (R23)

Constants may depend on the fixed source data and requested loss; the final threshold precedes the height. Restoring the completed tail preserves R23. For large heights, the originally retained absolute estimates with an enlarged fixed height polynomial cover the outer range. statement:
## 3. Development07: exact trace loss, realized by Dirichlet characters

Fix a positive integer q0. For squarefree n<=X coprime to q0, let z(n)=product_(p|n)z_p on the product unit torus over primes p<=X not dividing q0. Define

    P_X(z)=sum_(n<=X;(n,q0)=1)mu(n)z(n),
    Q_q0(X)=sum_(n<=X;(n,q0)=1)mu(n)^2.

Orthogonality of distinct prime monomials gives

    ||P_X||_(L2(torus))^2=Q_q0(X).                      (T1)

More generally, evaluation at any unit phase has norm sqrt(Q_q0(X)) on the Q_q0(X)-dimensional squarefree polynomial space: Cauchy gives the upper bound, and coefficients conjugate to that phase attain it. For the PARTICULAR coefficients mu(n), choose z_p=-1 at every unramified prime p<=X. Then mu(n)z(n)=mu(n)^2, so

    P_X(z)=Q_q0(X),
    |P_X(z)|/||P_X||_2=sqrt(Q_q0(X)).                   (T2)

The elementary squarefree count used after E6 gives Q_q0(X)=d_q0 X+O_q0(sqrt X), with positive d_q0. This is the maximal power loss X^(1/2), not X^o(1).

This bad phase can be realized by actual ordinary characters at every finite scale, not only by a nonperiodic multiplicative toy.

**Finite real-character realization lemma.** Given X>=2, a fixed q0, and arbitrary signs epsilon_p in {+1,-1} for primes p<=X not dividing q0, there is a real Dirichlet character chi modulo q0 D such that

    chi(p)=epsilon_p for p<=X, p not dividing q0,
    chi(n)=0 iff gcd(n,q0)>1 for every n<=X.             (T3)

Globally chi has its natural additional zeros at prime divisors of D; these are retained, not filled in.

Proof: choose an odd positive D congruent to 1 mod 4. At2, when unramified and prescribed, take D==1 mod 8 for epsilon_2=+1 and D==5 mod 8 for epsilon_2=-1. For each odd prime p<=X not dividing q0 choose a nonzero residue r_p with Legendre symbol (r_p/p)=epsilon_p and require D==r_p mod p. Require D==1 mod p for any other prime p dividing q0, and for ramified primes<=X. These CRT conditions are consistent and make D coprime to q0 and to every prime<=X. One may take any positive representative. Set chi(n)=1_(n,q0)=1 (n/D), where (n/D) is the Jacobi symbol. It is a real Dirichlet character modulo q0 D. Generalized quadratic reciprocity gives (p/D)=(D/p) because D==1 mod 4; the supplementary law handles 2. Thus T3 follows, and every prime divisor of D is>X. No prime-in-progression existence theorem, squarefree D assumption, primitive-character assertion or factorization of D is required. The Jacobi-character and reciprocity facts are explicitly recorded in [NIST DLMF §27.9](https://dlmf.nist.gov/27.9), verified2026-10-12.

Taking epsilon_p=-1 realizes T2 for a genuine chi, with a=mu chi and the GLOBAL exact identity a*chi=delta. Thus full finite convolution identities plus exact squarefree support do not supply a CHARACTER-UNIFORM bound

    |M_chi(X)| <= C X^eta ||P_X||_2,
    eta<1/2,                                          (T4)

with C independent of chi and X. In particular a universal eta<.374860=.874860-1/2 cannot be deduced merely by declaring the coherent phase trace to be random-like. The quarter-strip aspiration eta=1/4 encounters the same obstruction. The finite test at X=120 constructs

    D=10666004750947751128137555211484342435842576157,
    M_chi(120)=Q_1(120)=75,

checks all 120 convolution identities, and obtains trace-ratio-squared 75. This is an indexing witness, not the proof of the asymptotic norm statement.

**Essential quantifier limitation.** The requested result allows C_chi and X0_chi. Our character varies with X, and may have enormous modulus. T4 therefore does NOT rule out a fixed-character estimate with any eta<1/2, does NOT refute the accepted c7, and is weaker in asymptotic scope than G71. It rules out a particular conductor-independent transfer shortcut. A proof that uses the actual fixed modulus to link large primes is not refuted.

Indeed the corrected finite-group lift gives, for one fixed modulus q,

    (1/phi(q))sum_(chi mod q)|sum_(n<=X)mu(n)chi(n)|^2
      =sum_(r mod q;(r,q)=1)|sum_(n<=X;n==r mod q)mu(n)|^2,
    |M_chi(X)| <= sqrt(phi(q)) ||M_.(X)||_(average L2).  (T5)

The trace factor is now an acceptable fixed constant. Its ambient norm is no longer Q_q(X)^(1/2): the full same-residue Möbius correlations remain. Integrating T5 yields exactly E5–E7. This is the paid repair; it supplies no estimate for the new norm.

For completeness, constraints (b*chi)(n)=delta_(n=1) only for n<=Y force b(n)=mu(n)chi(n) only for n<=Y, by the unit-diagonal triangular recursion. Higher coordinates remain unconstrained by those LINEAR equations. In a squarefree coefficient Hilbert space the homogeneous free-coordinate evaluation norm is the square root of the number of allowed coordinates aboveY. Imposing full multiplicativity is an additional nonlinear restriction; the arbitrary-free-coordinate observation does not claim otherwise. T3 shows that even full arithmetic multiplicativity does not prevent bad finite traces when the character/modulus is free to change.

statement:
## 1. Exact ordinary-character source

Fix an ordinary complex Dirichlet character chi modulo q>=1, including imprimitive and principal characters with their usual zeros. Let r>=2 be a fixed integer with chi(-1)=(-1)^r. Thus r=2 for an even character and r=3 for an odd one suffice. Write e(x)=exp(2 pi i x), a(n)=mu(n)chi(n), and

    Phi(x)=sum_(k in Z, k!=0) chi(k) e(kx)/k^r,
    D_N(x)=sum_(n<=N) a(n)n^(-r)Phi(nx),
    E(x)=e(x)+e(-x)=2cos(2pi x),
    R_N(x)=E(x)-D_N(x).

All sums defining Phi and D_infinity converge absolutely and uniformly because r>1. Complete multiplicativity, including character zeros, gives at every positive or negative frequency k

    Fourier(D_infinity)(k)=chi(k)k^(-r) sum_(d|abs(k))mu(d).

The parity choice makes the two surviving coefficients at k=+1,-1 equal to1. Consequently D_infinity=E pointwise, and

    R_N(x)=sum_(n>N) a(n)n^(-r)Phi(nx).                 (1)

There is no discarded height, future tail, exceptional zero bin or inducing-conductor shift in this exact periodic identity. q, chi and r are fixed before N tends to infinity. The restriction to ordinary integer characters is explicit; no Eisenstein or Hecke analogue is asserted.

For abs(k)<=N, R_N has zero Fourier coefficient. For N<abs(k)<=2N,

    Fourier(R_N)(k)=chi(k)mu(abs(k))/k^r.              (2)

The latter follows because the only divisor exceeding N is abs(k) itself. These are actual squarefree coefficients, not a random-sign replacement.

For n,m>=1, g=gcd(n,m), Fourier orthogonality gives

    <Phi(nx),Phi(mx)>_[0,1]
      =2 L(2r,chi0) chi(m/g) conjugate(chi(n/g))
         *g^(2r)/(nm)^r,                             (3)

where chi0 is the principal character modulo q. When multiplied by a(n)conjugate(a(m))/(nm)^r, the character phase cancels for (nm,q)=1, and otherwise the term is zero. Thus

    ||R_N||_2^2=2L(2r,chi0)
      sum_(n,m>N; (nm,q)=1) mu(n)mu(m)
         gcd(n,m)^(2r)/(nm)^(2r).                    (4)

Every double series is absolutely convergent; the same calculation applies to finite tails and passes to the limit by dominated convergence. Equation(4) does not discard the off-diagonal signs.

## G129. Actual divisor Bellman identity and a scoped price

Set a(n)=mu(n)chi(n), c(n)=chi(n). Their Dirichlet convolution is delta
on every integer, with ramified zeros retained. Thus a(1)=1 and
a(n)=-sum_(d|n,d<n)a(d)chi(n/d). Let x_n=(a(1),...,a(n)) and T_n
append this exact signed divisor row. With ell_N=(1,...,1), a sufficient
Hermitian Bellman certificate is

    P_n>=0, P_N>=ell_N*ell_N,
    T_n*P_nT_n<=P_(n-1)+E_n.

The debts E_n may be signed. Evaluation on the actual source telescopes:

    |M_chi(N)|^2<=x_1*P_1x_1
          +sum_(n=2)^N x_(n-1)*E_n x_(n-1).        (15)

An O_(chi,epsilon)(N^(2gamma+epsilon)) bound on the entire right side
gives Mertens exponent gamma and ordinary zero exclusion by Abel
continuation. For a reachable-state version, inequalities need hold
only after evaluation on the actual x; global matrix inequalities are
a stronger sufficient condition, not an assumption forced on that route.

The exact backward row is

    w_(N,n)(d)=sum_(j<=n/d)chi(j)M_chi(floor(N/(dj))). (16)

For an arbitrary prefix, form b(k)=sum_(d|k)x_d chi(k/d) for k<=n,
and0 for k>n. Its unique recurrence continuation is b*(mu chi).
Sum through N and reorder to obtain(16). Hence w_(N,N)=ell_N,
w_(N,n-1)=w_(N,n)T_n and w_(N,1)=M_chi(N). The no-debt metric
P_n=w_(N,n)*w_(N,n) is exact but starts with the unknown |M(N)|^2.
It locates the missing signed response; it is not a noncircular estimate.

Even after deleting all forced-zero coordinates, a global diagonal
terminal majorant has exponent-two price. Let I={n<=N:a(n)!=0}, K=|I|.
For D=diag(d_i)>0, D>=ell_I*ell_I is equivalent to sum 1/d_i<=1.
The actual terminal energy is sum d_i>=K^2, with equality d_i=K.
Squarefree q-unit counting gives

    K=kappa_q N+O_q(sqrt N),
    kappa_q=zeta(2)^-1 product_(p|q)(1+1/p)^-1>0.

Expand squarefreeness as sum_(d^2|n)mu(d), count q-units, and pay the
sqrt N counting errors and d^-2 tail. The resulting Theta_q(N^2)
price applies to this specified global diagonal class only. It is not
a lower bound on Mertens sums or every source-specific reachable metric.
Signed off-diagonal geometry and a usable reachability description remain
open. This specializes the earlier magnitude-only obstruction to the
literal divisor cocycle and its complete adjoint.

Use the original Eisenstein ideals, primary/unit convention, fixed excluded

## HC8. Decisive test: the finite face estimate is equivalent to the original signed field

The return map does not show the proposed moment is easier. Test the selected mechanism further. Write u=p^(-z), v=c^(-z). Multiplication gives exactly

    V_z(1,p,c)^2=(1-u)^2[
      u^2-2u(u+1)v+(u^2+4u+1)v^2-2(u+1)v^3+v^4].              (HC8.1)

The full face J thus has leading term

    a(p)u^2(1-u)^2
         [M(x/p)-g(log(p/x))-a(p)g(log(p^2/x))],

plus four terms with free coefficients a(c)c^(-jz), j=1,2,3,4, and the displayed polynomial coefficients. These four terms are uniformly O_(chi,epsilon)(x^(1-delta+epsilon)) for x>=1, by the weighted Gaussian bound in HC5.2 and |c^(-jz)|<=c^(-delta). Every sign is retained in the identity; an absolute bound is sufficient for this remainder.

The leading scalar is bounded above and away from zero uniformly in theta:

    p^(-2delta)(1-p^(-delta))^2
       <=|u^2(1-u)^2|<=p^(-2delta)(1+p^(-delta))^2.             (HC8.2)

At delta=3/5 the remainder has power 2/5+epsilon. The product cap changes the field by O(X^(-1+o(1))). The truncated K_h mass tends to 1 and is >=1/2 for sufficiently large X by HC6.2. Thus for each fixed gamma>2/5, the following ALL-SCALE statements are equivalent, with character-dependent constants and every epsilon>0:

    Q_X<<X^(2gamma+epsilon) for every sufficiently large dyadic X;
    integral_(X/p)^(2X/p)|M(y)|^2dy/y<<X^(2gamma+epsilon)
                                  for every sufficiently large dyadic X. (HC8.3)

Forwards, apply HC8.1--HC8.2 in the joint positive-weight Hilbert norm, divide by the fixed lower bound and absorb the complete 2/5 error. Backwards, use the fixed upper bound and triangle inequality. Both directions preserve mixed terms by norm inequalities. HC7.1 likewise has the same all-scale exponent as the corresponding M L1 estimate, directly from HC6.3. Moving to a determinant has not manufactured arithmetic cancellation.

This is stronger than the earlier positive absolute semiprime obstruction: it is exact signed bounded recovery from the ACTUAL determinant and its finite physical source, valid for complex ordinary characters, with a reverse finite-face estimate. It also identifies more than the statement "D20 is open": an entire theta-frequency diagonal retains every original pair correlation; a fixed median suffices for its readout; finitely many prime-square deletions do not cure it. This is a statement about the location and strength of the required arithmetic input, not a lower bound on the true size of M or H.

The next bottleneck is cancellation in this free-factor signed channel, or a new source/readout retaining all-height zero information after eliminating it. Theta orthogonality, prime-power annihilation, finite-frequency deletion and the now-paid 24 shifted terms do not supply that estimate. Removing the entire free-factor sector loses the relevant determinant poles by HC5. A new coupling that actually pays the free factor would be substantive; it is absent from this bounded pass.

### D04.1 Exact object, powers and signs

Fix tau>0 and an ordinary Dirichlet character chi modulo q, with its literal extension chi(n)=0 when gcd(n,q)>1. Constants may depend on this fixed chi; no growing-conductor statement is intended. Define

    f(n)=mu(rad(n/3^v3(n))),
    F_chi(x)=sum_(n>=1) f(n)chi(n)g_tau(log(n/x)).

The zeta case is chi=1. This is the exact existing f3 field when chi=1; it is not a squarefree surrogate. For a finite prime set P contained in {p>=5:p does not divide q}, define

    f_(P,chi)(n)=f(n)chi(n)1_(gcd(n,product P)=1),
    V_(P,chi)(x)=sum_n f_(P,chi)(n)g_tau(log(n/x)),
    a_(P,chi)(r)=f(r)chi(r)1_(every prime divisor of r lies in P),
    a_(P,chi)(1)=1.

Unique decomposition n=r v into its FULL P-smooth part r and P-rough part v proves

    f(n)chi(n)=sum_(r|n) a_(P,chi)(r)f_(P,chi)(n/r),
    F_chi(x)=sum_(r P-smooth) a_(P,chi)(r)V_(P,chi)(x/r).   (D04.1)

Only one term is nonzero in the coefficient convolution, but all r occur in the field sum. At a deleted prime the local a-series is

    1-sum_(v>=1)chi(p)^v z^v=(1-2chi(p)z)/(1-chi(p)z).

Repeated powers have coefficient -chi(p)^v, not zero. This is the important difference from the older mu-based D35, whose reconstruction has finite squarefree support. Replacing this factor by 1-chi(p)z would be incorrect.

For any sigma>0 its absolute weighted mass is exactly

    W_P(sigma)=sum_r |a_(P,chi)(r)|r^-sigma
              =product_(p in P)(1-p^-sigma)^-1.           (D04.2)

The field identity is absolutely justified: use the Gaussian positive integer sum and, for example, sigma>1 in (D04.2). Local convergence, derivatives and shell rearrangements then follow by Gaussian decay. It is an equality of the actual signed field, not domination by a favorable subfamily.

## 6. Uniform audit13: cutoff tensor rank and the complete signed return

The initial seed correctly warns that the multiplicative threshold may defeat a proposed compression. The following calculation specifies both what is compressible and what must be paid. Work at an integer N>=1 and one fixed ordinary chi. Partition ALL unramified primes<=N into two disjoint sets L,R. Let u_i list the squarefree L-products<=N and v_j list the squarefree R-products<=N, both including1 and sorted increasingly. Ramified factors correspond to zero source coefficients and are removed as zero rows/columns; they are not inverted.

Write R_N and C_N for the row/column counts and define

    T_(ij)=1_(u_i v_j<=N),
    alpha_i=mu(u_i)chi(u_i), beta_j=mu(v_j)chi(v_j).

Unique coprime factorization gives the exact COMPLETE ordinary source

    M_chi(N)=alpha^T T beta.                             ([restricted research revision])

No prime beyond the partition is missing: every prime factor of a contributing n<=N is<=N. On the retained unit rows and columns |alpha_i|=|beta_j|=1. Thus the full coefficient tensor diag(alpha)Tdiag(beta) has exactly the rank and singular values of T, including complex characters. Phases can still cancel in the final scalar([restricted research revision]); equal matrix singular values do not remove that possibility.

Let t_i=#{j:v_j<=N/u_i}. Each row of T is the prefix vector of length t_i. Let0<h_1<...<h_d be its distinct positive lengths and h_0=0. Exactly,

    rank(T)=d,
    T=sum_(ell=1)^d a_ell b_ell^T,
    (a_ell)_i=1_(t_i>=h_ell),
    (b_ell)_j=1_(h_(ell-1)<j<=h_ell).                    ([restricted research revision])

The displayed decomposition proves rank<=d. Choose one actual row of each length h_i and the actual columns numbered h_j. Their submatrix is L_d=(1_(j<=i)), whose determinant is1. This proves rank>=d without generic-position, random-prime or numerical-rank assumptions. Because t_i is a function of floor(N/u_i),

    d<=#{floor(N/u):1<=u<=N}<=2 floor(sqrt N).            ([restricted research revision])

The final bound follows by splitting u<=sqrt N and u>sqrt N. It is an exact O(sqrt N) representation, consistent with G105's continuation-state count. It is not a polylogarithmic rank theorem or an estimate for the contracted arithmetic field.

There is a rigorous price for losing these threshold directions. L_d^(-1) is the bidiagonal matrix with1 on its diagonal and-1 immediately below. Its Euclidean operator norm is at most2, since it is I minus a truncated shift. Hence ||L_d v||>=||v||/2. Restrict any rank-r approximation T_r, r<d, to the selected d by d submatrix. Its kernel has dimension at least d-r. On an orthonormal basis of that kernel, the restricted approximation error has squared norm at least1/4 per vector. Therefore

    ||T-T_r||_F^2 >= (d-r)/4,
    ||T-T_r||_op >=1/2,                                 ([restricted research revision])

where the second inequality uses one kernel vector. Restriction cannot increase either norm. The same conclusions hold for the character-weighted tensor, by unitary diagonal multiplication. This needs no asymptotic lower bound for d and no unproved supply of specially arranged primes. It is a deterministic instance-wise obstruction to arbitrarily accurate norm approximation below the actual rank.

It does NOT lower-bound |M_chi(N)| or the signed scalar error. The exact source return for a proposed T_r is

    M_chi(N)=alpha^T T_r beta+alpha^T(T-T_r)beta,
    |alpha^T(T-T_r)beta|
                   <=sqrt(R_N C_N)||T-T_r||_op
                   <=sqrt(R_N C_N)||T-T_r||_F.           ([restricted research revision])

Every entry, including leakage outside u_i v_j<=N from the approximation, belongs to this error. A singular-value tail is useful only with its full readout factor or a stronger actual signed contraction bound. If a proposed sufficient Frobenius budget X^(gamma+epsilon)/sqrt(R_N C_N) tends to zero, ([restricted research revision]) forces r>=d eventually. That conditional observation is not a claim that the ratio tends to zero for every partition. One-sided trivial partitions can have tiny rank and simply leave the original Mertens sum in the other factor.

The exact decomposition offers a more arithmetic target than a bare rank estimate:

    M_chi(N)=sum_(ell=1)^d
       [sum_(i:t_i>=h_ell)mu(u_i)chi(u_i)]
       [sum_(j:h_(ell-1)<j<=h_ell)mu(v_j)chi(v_j)].       ([restricted research revision])

All smooth-prime restrictions, band endpoints and phases are explicit. If only selected ell are retained, the omitted signed sum of the other rectangles is the exact remainder. Bounding BOTH the retained scalar and this entire signed remainder by N^(gamma+epsilon), for every epsilon/all large N and each fixed chi with common gamma, returns to([restricted research revision]). Abel/Mellin continuation of s integral_1^infinity M_chi(x)x^(-s-1)dx then excludes L-zeros in Re s>gamma. The principal pole yields the permitted reciprocal zero at1. A moving partition is allowed only with bounds uniform in its actual choice before this return; no moving tensor is itself analytically continued.

This is a complete source/return audit, not an algorithmic complexity result. W37 threshold/state ideas, W39 full polynomial readout, G105 exact floor-state compression and W52's integer-fiber/readout cautions are close ancestry. The explicit rank witness and signed rectangle formula preserve the seed's potentially useful source-specific low-rank or residual-cancellation route. No approximate arithmetic compression theorem has been proved.

### 2.1 Exact block optimum

For any partition into nonempty coordinate blocks B_j, write b_j=sum_(n in B_j)a_n and B=sum_j|b_j|. Then

    inf_(P block diagonal, P>=ell ell*) a*Pa = B^2.           (2)

For the lower bound, multiply a by one scalar phase on each block so that its block sums align. The quadratic energy of a block-diagonal P is unchanged, while its required readout majorant becomes B^2. For the upper bound when every b_j!=0, take block P_j=(B/|b_j|)ell_j ell_j*. Weighted Cauchy gives P>=ell ell* because sum_j |b_j|/B=1, and its actual energy is B^2. Zero block sums are handled by assigning them an arbitrarily small share of this reciprocal-weight budget and taking a limit. If every b_j=0, any sufficiently large finite block weight attains energy zero. Thus (2) is an infimum; no invertibility or false universal attainment is assumed.

This is an exact signed-block target. Optimizing a positive block metric cannot improve on the complete sum of absolute block sums. It extends G129's singleton/diagonal optimum; it does not estimate those block sums.

      phi_r(log(d1...dK ell1...ell_(K-1)/x))

      +O(K(B+1)log(B+2)+K^2+Klog(K+2))],

## R6. Complete product tails, finite theta leakage and exact energy

Fix delta=3/5, p and h before X. For sufficiently large dyadic X set

    A_X=X exp(-2 sqrt(log X)), B_X=2X exp(2 sqrt(log X)),
    T_X=X^(1/5),
    J_X(theta,x)=a(p)sum_(c>p; A_X<=pc<=B_X)
                        a(c)V_(delta+i theta)(1,p,c)^2g(log(pc/x)),
    P_X(x)=integral_(-T_X)^(T_X) K_h(theta)e^(i omega theta)J_X(theta,x)dtheta.
                                                                    (R6.1)

Both real product boundaries are included. Natural zeros, squarefree composites, repeated prime factors in pc, and every signed pair interaction remain. There is no moving median cutoff and no implicit transfer from the old real interval [1/5,1/4].

The positive weighted product count on the face is bounded by the full R2.3 counting constant times t, uniformly in theta. If n=pc<A_X and x>=X, g(log(n/x))<=const X^(-2). The entire lower tail is consequently O(A_X X^(-2))=O(X^(-1)exp(-2 sqrt(log X))). For n>B_X and x<=2X, log(n/x)>=2 sqrt(log X). Stieltjes integration against an O(t) counting function bounds the upper tail by its endpoint term and

    C x integral_(2 sqrt(log X))^infinity e^v(1+v)g(v)dv
                                                =X^(-1+o(1)).

Completing the square in -v^2/2+v proves this exponent. Thus the entire product complement of J_X is O(X^(-1+o(1))) uniformly in theta and x on the shell. No individual large output or overlapping complement is omitted.

The sinc inequality |sin t|<=1 gives the exact majorant

    K_h(theta)<=96/(pi h^3 theta^4),
    integral_(|theta|>T) K_h(theta)dtheta<=64/(pi h^3 T^3). (R6.2)

Using J=O_delta(x), the missing theta range costs O_chi(X T_X^(-3))=O_chi(X^(2/5)). Integrating the product-tail estimate over the retained weight costs no extra T_X factor because its mass is at most 1. Combining R3.1 and R4.6 therefore gives

    P_X(x)=p^(-2delta)a(p)
       [M(x/p)-g(log(p/x))-a(p)g(log(p^2/x))]
               +O_chi(X^(2/5))+O_chi(X^(-1+o(1))).          (R6.3)

The constants may depend on q through p and h, but not on X or theta. If one uses the truncated full H instead, its median-complement projection equals MINUS the omitted full-line theta tail by R4.5. The bound |H_(median>p)|<=C_delta x from the absolute source majorant prices that leakage by the same O_chi(X^(2/5)). Thus exact full-line annihilation has not been confused with zero finite-window leakage.

The author's positive sufficient energy is exactly

    Q_X=integral_(-T_X)^(T_X) K_h(theta)
                             integral_X^(2X)|J_X(theta,x)|^2 dx/x dtheta. (R6.4)

It retains both independent free indices c,d with their literal masks, a(c)conjugate(a(d)), |a(p)|^2=1, and V_z(1,p,c)^2 conjugate(V_z(1,p,d)^2). The Gaussian overlap has the exact normalization

    g(log(pc/x))g(log(pd/x))
      =g_2(log(c/d))g_(1/2)(log(p sqrt(cd)/x)),              (R6.5)

where g_tau(v)=(2 pi tau)^(-1/2)exp(-v^2/(2tau)). The two sides have common prefactor 1/(2 pi); completing the square verifies their exponents. No c!=d term is deleted.

By contrast ||P_X||_2^2 has two independent twist variables theta,eta, including the phase e^(i omega(theta-eta)) and ALL products of the two analytic squares and their conjugates. Cauchy--Schwarz in theta with truncated mass m_X<=1 gives

    ||P_X||_2^2 <= m_X Q_X <= Q_X.                          (R6.6)

## DQ1--DQ2. Exact cube classes and their natural zeros

Every dual ideal has a unique factorization

\[
 n=d\kappa^3,\qquad d\text{ cube-free}.
 \tag{DQ1}
\]

There is no condition `(d,kappa)=1`. Writing `d=d1 d2^2`, the two `di` are
squarefree and coprime. The primitive good conductor of the cubic character
induced by `d` is `rad(d)=d1 d2`, not generally `d`.

The root-cancelled core character is
`psi_n(c)=theta_c(lambda) overline(theta_c(n))`. Thus

`psi_(d kappa^3)(c)=psi_d(c) 1_(c,kappa)=1`.

The first factor retains every natural zero from `d`, including a prime whose
exponent in `d` is two; the second retains all cube-factor zeros. For one
surviving pair `(c,e)` and fixed `d`,

\[
 \sum_\kappa\overline\eta(d\kappa^3)q_{d\kappa^3}^{z-1}
 =\overline\eta(d)q_d^{z-1}Z_{ce}(3-3z),\qquad
 Z_{ce}(s)=\zeta_K(s)\prod_{p\mid ce}(1-q_p^{-s}).
 \tag{DQ2}
\]

This fixed-class series converges absolutely for `Re z<2/3`. It includes the
fixed-prime row factors. One can first derive the full dual-series identity
on `Re z<0` and then continue each fixed class. The sum of all continued
classes is not asserted to converge normally on a positive `z` line.
