## 6. Protected independent audit13: lawful source-state merging

The seed asks for prime-exponent/zero/size states merged only when their signed continuation laws agree. I provide an exact weighted construction, then identify what it does NOT prove.

Fix integer N, threshold y and one fixed chi modulo q. Write a(n)=mu(n)chi(n). Each nonzero squarefree n<=N factors uniquely as n=de, with every prime of d<=y and every prime of e>y. Let

    D_y(N)={d<=N:a(d)!=0, P^+(d)<=y},
    E_y(N)={e<=N:a(e)!=0, P^-(e)>y},

with1 in both sets. For d in D_y(N), let its normalized formal continuation be

    V_d(z)=sum_(e in E_y(N),de<=N)a(e) z(e), 
    z(e)=product_(p|e)z_p, p>y.                         (R11)

The prefix amplitude a(d) is stored separately. This is a weighted state model: a zero prefix is an absorbing zero state; parity and character phase remain in that amplitude. At z_p=1 the exact original sharp source is

    M_chi(N)=sum_(d in D_y(N))a(d)V_d(1).               (R12)

No density, independence hypothesis, Gaussian replacement or repeated-prime term is introduced.

Distinct squarefree future monomials are independent on the prime torus and also on the Boolean sign cube. Therefore V_d=V_d' as continuation polynomials if and only if

    {e in E_y(N): e<=floor(N/d)}
      ={e in E_y(N): e<=floor(N/d')}.                    (R13)

All coefficients on that support are nonzero by construction, so different supports cannot cancel as polynomials. Equal integer quotients are sufficient; one can also merge different quotients if the intervening interval contains no eligible future e. Conversely, parity and zero flags without the remaining size information do not establish (R13).

This criterion has a useful actual example. Take N=21,y=5 and principal chi. The seven prefix histories and three continuation classes are

| Prefix histories | Normalized law | Sum of prefix amplitudes |
|---|---|---:|
|1|1-z7-z11-z13-z17-z19|1|
|2,3|1-z7|-2|
|5,6,10,15|1|2|

Thus M(21)=(-4)+(-2)*0+2=-2. Prefixes2 and3 really merge despite different products. Prefixes2 and5 have the same odd parity/nonzero status but different continuation laws. This is an actual coefficient calculation, not an arbitrary-state counterexample.

For any N, floor(N/d) has at most2 floor(sqrt N) distinct positive values: split d<=sqrt N from d>sqrt N. Consequently at one fixed prime-processing stage there are at most that many nonzero normalized classes, plus a possible dead state for histories already beyond N. This is a rigorous finite-cutoff upper bound. It is NOT an exponential-in-the-prime-count lower bound and does not contradict G81, whose independent Gaussian history functions and arbitrary-history preservation are different requirements.

A precise linear-rank qualification is available. Order the distinct support sets in (R13) by inclusion. They are nested, all contain1, and each successive difference is nonempty. Choosing one monomial from each difference makes a triangular coefficient matrix with nonzero diagonal. Hence their r normalized continuation polynomials are linearly independent. Any linear state preserving arbitrary combinations of THESE r laws requires dimension at least r. This says nothing comparable about a single fixed arithmetic sum, nonlinear encoding, approximate closure, or cancellations after all z are specialized to1.

The formal sign variations have an actual finite-character interpretation: multiply the base chi by the real Jacobi character from section3 prescribed to be+1 on low primes and arbitrary signs on high primes through N. The low prefix amplitudes and all original q zeros are preserved through N, while the future monomials take those signs. Extra zeros beyond N remain. This justifies the finite-family interpretation of (R13); again the auxiliary modulus varies and supplies no fixed-character asymptotic lower bound.

Reconstruction after lawful merging is completely explicit. For each class C put W_C=sum_(d in C)a(d) and keep its common V_C. Then

    M_chi(N)=sum_C W_C V_C(1).                           (R14)

All cross terms of the squared sum are needed for an energy target. A small number of classes bounds neither the W_C amplitudes nor their coherent correlations with V_C. At moving real X use N=floor X and retain the cell changes at integers; the exact identity alone supplies no favorable scale evolution.

Equivalently, the standard prime-sieve recurrence on the closed quotient set is

    S_j(m)=S_(j-1)(m)-chi(p_j)S_(j-1)(floor(m/p_j)),
    S_0(m)=1_(m>=1),

where S_j sums mu(n)chi(n) over n<=m supported on the first j distinct primes. Since floor(floor(N/d)/p)=floor(N/(dp)), the quotient set is closed under these transitions. Taking all primes<=N returns M_chi(N) exactly. The stage count, amplitudes, and the complete signed final contraction remain; the O(sqrt N) state count is not a runtime claim or square-root cancellation estimate.

This rescues an exact source interface from the seed while refusing an unsupported contraction. Classical quotient/sieve dynamic programming, RN, G68/G81 and W49's floor-state correction are ancestry. The specific continuation-class criterion is the present audit's explanation of permissible merging, not a new general automaton family. A further result would have to bound (R14), or its COMPLETE all-scale energy, at a common gamma<theta8. None is supplied.

                       + O(H_J U^(T-1/200+epsilon)).          (R)

Here R_U,hard is the accepted unique middle outside both original-A core caps, and R_N,hard is the complete signed nonunique collision/hole expression outside both caps. The second term has no imported unique-sector low-band cutoff. Its frequencies begin at the actual first nonzero point of the fixed dual lattice. Both orientations and every signed hole term remain.

A useful independent simplification is the explicit nine-component certificate in section5. It reduces the limiting CU2 scale factor, up to a fixed constant and small powers, to

                     max(1,U^((s-r-1/2)/6)).                (S)

This shows precisely where the remaining linear component matters. It is a sharpening of the payment description, not a new bound on the signed hard sum. No new c follows. One endpoint clarification is required in reading the author's shorthand: on a fractional dual lattice, “H_c<1” alone is not the criterion that the retained nonzero set is empty. This changes only fixed constants, not (R), its exponents, or its retained source. Do not silently turn this clarification into a changed frequency selector.

## 1. Fixed source and the paid transfer back to C6

Use the exact source of G179-G181/G185-G187 on Eisenstein ideals with their fixed good-prime set, primary/unit convention and finite ray dictionary:

The two inverse factors have their original Mobius signs, independent heights and common real parameter. Q is the original ordered product of disjoint prime-slot pools; its coefficients need not be multiplicative. A slot pool can meet either inverse. The right column is conjugated in full. Both sextic orientations e=1,-1 are retained, including every natural zero. The free-row enclosure is the original nonzero sixth-power-free smooth row set. Dominate original row divisor weights first; do not insert a signed physical projector or a moving row selector.

Retain

    17/25<=delta<=7/10, 17/20<r<47/50,
    33/25<s<141/100, s-r>3/8, 0<=v<=1/20,

    T>=123353/67500, K=28114053/6250000.

These are the accepted source ranges, not permission to extrapolate to delta=2/3 or1/2. Set G=U^(1/5), H11=D1/U^(1/2), H22=D2/U^(3/4), and H12=H21=U^(3/5). Let C6 retain both strict within-column inverse gcd cuts<G and all four strict cross-copy inverse gcd cuts<Hij, before the old diagonal and conductor removals.

G179-G181 prove ||F_<||^2=C6+O(H_J U^(T-1/200+epsilon)). The exact complete tuple majorant is

Their exponents are respectively1,109/60,9/5. These are absolute upper bounds for those complete sectors. A pair of coprime squarefree merged columns has no collision, meets all six cuts, and has Q1 comparable to N0^2, Q2=Q3=1. Since r+s>2.17, it also lies outside the paid conductor sectors for sufficiently large U with fixed support constants. Consequently

    C6_nonunique = R_nonunique + P_old,

This transfer is essential: the new argument works on C6 without imposing a joint original-conductor selector on its inner coefficient matrix. Equation(1) pays that difference explicitly.

## 2. Exact local decomposition, holes and the principal block

At a good prime, the six aggregated original sites are inverse1, inverse2, slot on each of two copies. Each site has occupancy0 or1. Named slots retain their separate pool tests and coefficients; impossible allocations stay zero. If a and b are the sums of the three occupancies on each copy, then0<=a,b<=3.

The thirteen collision types are the pairs(a,b) with a+b>=2. Let h_ab be the squarefree ideal formed from primes of that type. All h_ab are pairwise coprime and their complete original-site incidences remain attached. Define

    Lc=product h_ab^a, Rc=product h_ab^b,
    L=N(Lc), R=N(Rc), D=LR,
    k=product_(a!=b)h_ab, Kc=N(k),
    E=product_(a=b>=1)h_ab, Hcol=product h_ab.

Every actual pair is uniquely n=Lc*x, n'=Rc*y, where x,y are squarefree, mutually coprime, and prime to Hcol. Their primes occur in exactly one original site. The nonunique sector is exactly Hcol!=1. The six gcd cuts depend only on these actual collision ideals and their site incidences, not on residual singleton primes.

On every row, including conductor primes,

    chi_n(u)^e conjugate(chi_n'(u)^e)
       =psi_k(u) chi_x(u)^e conjugate(chi_y(u)^e)
                                                 1_((u,E)=1),
    psi_k=product_(a!=b)chi_p^(e(a-b)).                       (2)

The nonzero exponent e(a-b) lies in{+/-1,+/-2,+/-3}. It has order6,3 or2 and is nonprincipal primitive at that good prime. Equal positive valuations cancel phase but preserve the unit indicator. Thus the primitive good conductor is kxy, while E is a genuine canceled-phase hole. The fixed nu factors stay in the source coefficients; they are not assumed to have order six.

The full relative principal case kxy=1 forces x=y=1 and all collision valuations equal, hence n=n'. Conversely the complete merged diagonal has that form, up to the retained fixed unit/ray conventions. Its row cost is O(H_J U^(1+epsilon)) using c_abs. Pay it before invoking zero frequency vanishing. A fixed ray expansion may have nontrivial fixed-place pieces; this does not erase the whole diagonal payment or remove any original principal/inducing family.

The support bounds used later are valid:

    N(h20),N(h02) << G P0;   N(h11)<<N0;
    N(h11^(ij))<Hij.                                        (3)

For the first, write a column d1=gx,d2=gy with squarefree pairwise-coprime g,x,y and squarefree slot product P. Its defect n/rad(n) equals g times a divisor of P, hence is <C G P0. A type(2,0) prime divides the left defect and type(0,2) the right. For the second, h11 divides both original merged columns. For the last, the indicated type(1,1) prime set divides the ORIGINAL inverse gcd on edge ij. Strict original endpoints and fixed annular constants remain; relaxing a positive majorant to a closed upper support is harmless.

## 3. Poisson, the genuine tail, and both true roots

Expand sixth-freeness by mu(a0) with a0^6|u and retain(a0,Hcol*x*y)=1. This restriction is legitimate before expansion because the omitted original terms are zero. Expand the E-hole completely with sum_(d|E,d|u/a0^6)mu(d), and put u=a0^6 d z. Write qa=N(a0), qd=N(d). As d is prime to kxy, its character value is a unit on the actual source. No natural zero is divided out.

Primitive Poisson at scale U/(qa^6 qd), using PR9 B3.5, has zero dual term for the nonprincipal primitive character in(2), and zero at every good conductor-sharing frequency. General CRT gives

    gamma(psi_k;k) gamma_e(x) gamma_-e(y)
       psi_k(xy) chi_x(ky)^e chi_y(kx)^(-e).                 (4)

The x-y factor is the fixed sextic reciprocity ray sign. The remaining interactions with k factor into an x function and a y function. The mixed normalized Gauss factor has modulus one and is not replaced by a fixed-order Gauss coefficient at k. The d twist separates in the same way. All frequency-dependent psi_k factors stay in the outer weight or its natural-zero restriction.

The residual inverse signs equal mu(x) and mu(y), times the fixed slot-count signs and original extracted collision coefficients. PR9 B1.10 gives the two accepted G185 orientations after defining a0(x)=conjugate(alpha(x))gamma_2(x). For e=-1 the residual Gauss factors are a0(x)conjugate(a0(y)) with chi_x(-1)conjugate(G(x))G(y); for e=1 they are conjugate(a0(x))a0(y) with G(x)conjugate(G(y))chi_y(-1). Fixed ray signs, nu corrections and all collision and slot coefficients remain. B1.11 later supplies the same within-column cubic cocycle in each orientation, conjugated as appropriate.

The genuine conductor norm is comparable to Q=Kc N0^2/(LR). Fix tau=1/1000, an ORIGINAL a0 dyad qa~A and a sufficiently large fixed support constant C_*. The retained cutoff is exactly

    Hc=C_* U^tau A^6 qd Kc N0^2/(U L R).                    (5)

It depends on original collision/hole labels and the original A, not on artificial f. Outside(5), the actual Schwartz argument exceeds c U^tau. The genuine one-pair prefactor is U/(qa^6 qd N0 sqrt(Q)). PR9 B3.4 gives a tail factor bounded by(1+qa^6 qd Q/U)U^(-tau(B-1)). Before extension there are O(N0^2 U^epsilon) original tuple pairs, O(U^(1/6)) possible a0, and divisor-many d. Since Q<<N0^2, the total raw price is at most

    H_J U^(1/6+epsilon)(U N0+N0^2)
                          U^(-tau(B-1))
       << H_J U^(149/30+epsilon-tau(B-1)).                  (6)

Choose finite B after this count. This includes the lattice-counting1, rather than assuming every dual scale is large. On a fixed fractional lattice, keep all points with N(ell)<=Hc; the empty-set threshold is its fixed least positive norm. Using N(Delta)Hc in a cleared-lattice energy only changes fixed comparison constants. No term is discarded merely because Hc<1.

Only after this tail is paid, extend the separated product formula to individually squarefree x,y prime to Hcol and insert the COMPLETE sum_(f|x,f|y)mu(f). It annihilates every artificially added noncoprime pair. Old collision predicates are held at their original labels; recomputing them on x,y would destroy this cancellation. The frequency cutoff and both core selectors are independent of f.

Allocate each f prime independently to its actual residual inverse color or surviving named slot on EACH copy. Slot coefficients and masks remain, with divisor-bounded multiplicity. With F=N(f), the residual product lengths are genuinely unequal:

    XL=N0/(L F), XR=N0/(R F).

The pair prefactor before normalized columns is U sqrt(LR)/(qa^6 qd N0^2 sqrt(Kc)). Restoring both unnormalized roots gives exactly

    U sqrt(LR)/(qa^6 qd N0^2 sqrt(Kc)) sqrt(XL XR)
                  =U/(qa^6 qd N0 sqrt(Kc) F).               (7)

In particular a true shared type(1,1) collision is NOT another artificial f. There is no extra reciprocal L or R in(7).

For fixed allocations a merged residual coefficient is a sum over original factorizations, of divisor-bounded multiplicity and bounded individual magnitude. The total number of permitted color/slot tuples is O(Xi U^epsilon) at its independently shortened scales. Hence its normalized squared mass is O(H_J U^epsilon). This proof uses the actual product slot family, not an arbitrary joint coefficient matrix. Truly empty scales stay empty; nonempty nominal scales below one are clipped only by bounded original annular ratios.

Fix all nominal norm boxes first, including a0,d,ell and collision norms. The kernel on the full ambient normalized box is the original Schwartz function of U N(ell)LR/(qa^6 qd Kc N(n)N(n')). Euler derivatives are bounded uniformly in its nominal positive scale. PR9 B3.3 therefore chooses one weighted Fourier measure before live labels. Real inverse roots occur once; new imaginary norm powers distribute multiplicatively through the original colors. Sharp masks remain outside the smooth separation. There is no f-dependent density or selector, and both original height seminorms remain.

Factorization can formally reintroduce x=y=1 when k=1. Subtract that rank-one block explicitly. For each diagonal coefficient its full absolute Poisson sum, including zero frequency, costs

    sum_(qa<<U^(1/6), d|E) [U/(qa^6 qd)+1]<<U^(1+epsilon).

The c_abs squared-mass bound then pays the entire correction, even with a frequency selection. Thus the factorized energy need not pretend its unit-core row is nonprincipal.

## 4. Licensed energies and unequal-length price reconstruction

[Dunn, arXiv2403.13151v3, Theorem4.1 and Corollary4.2](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.13151v3) allow an arbitrary squarefree primary inner sequence and an unrestricted cubic outer variable. The normalized energy price is B^(1/3)(B+Xi), up to the stated small powers. The outer variable need not be squarefree. Reciprocity and fixed units/rays permit the needed orientation; this uses Section4, not the paper's cuspidal coefficient results.

[Goldmakher-Louvel, arXiv1112.1642v2, Definition1 and Theorem1.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1112.1642v2) give price B+Xi for the squarefree quadratic family with arbitrary inner coefficients. PR9 B2.24 identifies the ACTUAL family: the lambda correction, primitive inducing convention, trivial infinite type, finite reciprocity group and equal-class coprime product conductor are essential. Fixed k,d and hole twists go into arbitrary sequences or positive outer restrictions, not into a new conductor-dependent sieve family.

For square cores write(Delta ell)=kappa2 b^2, with kappa2 squarefree and arbitrary b; overlap is allowed. For each fixed kappa2, the b symbol is cubic. Summing through core cap C gives each normalized column energy

    As+Xi Bs,
    As=Hc^(2/3)C^(1/3), Bs=Hc^(1/6)C^(5/6).                (8)

Fixed N(Delta) factors are retained in the comparison constant. Only nonempty ranges kappa2<=N(Delta)Hc use the sieve; extending the positive bound to C does not assert a theorem at an empty subunit B.

For cube cores write(Delta ell)=kappa3 t^3 z^6, with kappa3 cubefree and t squarefree, keeping all overlaps. The exact symbol includes chi_m(kappa3)^eta chi_m(t)^3 1_((m,z)=1). The z-hole must be kept even at a sixth power. For fixed kappa3,z, apply the quadratic theorem over t with that fixed puncture in the inner sequence.

Let l_i1,l_i2,l_iP be the collision norms extracted from the two original inverse colors and slots on side i. Their product is L or R. Ignoring additional f shortenings only for an upper bound, the pointwise color estimate is

    Si=(P0/l_iP)[D1/l_i1+D2/l_i2
                            +(D1D2/(l_i1 l_i2))^(2/3)].     (9)

To justify it, expand the fixed remaining slots and apply B1.11 to each actual color pair. The only live coupling is the cubic symbol between those two colors. All collision/a0/f/z and fixed-frequency punctures separate into zero coefficients or restrictions of the positive outer norm. PR9 B2.25 permits these arbitrary one-color sequences. Triangle over normalized slots costs the remaining slot length after squaring. This remains true with independent heights and either complete conjugation orientation. It supplies no permission for arbitrary two-color matrix coefficients.

For B=(Hc/N(kappa3))^(1/3), split z at Z. Short repetitions cost B+Xi Z; long repetitions cost B Si/Z. If sqrt(B Si/Xi) lies in[1,sqrt(B)], balance the two. Below1 use the pointwise bound throughout; above sqrt(B) use the sieve throughout, noting Si>Xi. Each regime is bounded by B+sqrt(B Si Xi). Summing cubefree kappa3 gives

    Ac+Zi Bc,
    Ac=Hc^(1/3)C^(2/3), Bc=Hc^(1/6)C^(5/6),
    Zi=sqrt(Si Xi).                                         (10)

For unequal positive x,y, scalar Cauchy gives

    sqrt((A+xB)(A+yB))
       <=A+B sqrt(xy)+sqrt(AB)(sqrt(x)+sqrt(y)).              (11)

Apply(11) with x=XL,y=XR in SQ and x=ZL,y=ZR in CU. Both mixed terms in EACH sector are necessary in this chosen upper bound. No equality of the shortened lengths is imposed.

Multiplying by(7), summing O(A) a0 labels, and substituting(5) produces the following complete monomials. D=LR; each cross row occurs for i=L and i=R. Only fixed constants,H_J and allocated small powers are omitted.

| Term | Restored price |
|---|---|
| SQ0 | U^(1/3+2tau/3) A^-1 N0^(1/3) Kc^(1/6) D^(-2/3) F^-1 qd^(-1/3) C^(1/3) |
| SQ2 | U^(5/6+tau/6) A^-4 N0^(1/3) Kc^(-1/3) D^(-2/3) F^-2 qd^(-5/6) C^(5/6) |
| SQ cross i | U^(7/12+5tau/12) A^(-5/2) N0^(1/3) Kc^(-1/12) D^(-5/12) L_i^(-1/2) F^(-3/2) qd^(-7/12) C^(7/12) |
| CU0 | U^(2/3+tau/3) A^-3 N0^(-1/3) Kc^(-1/6) D^(-1/3) F^-1 qd^(-2/3) C^(2/3) |
| CU2 | U^(5/6+tau/6) A^-4 N0^(-1/6) Kc^(-1/3) D^(-5/12) (SL SR)^(1/4) F^(-3/2) qd^(-5/6) C^(5/6) |
| CU cross i | U^(3/4+tau/4) A^(-7/2) N0^(-1/4) Kc^(-1/4) D^(-1/4) L_i^(-1/4) Si^(1/4) F^(-5/4) qd^(-3/4) C^(3/4) |

The author table is correct. Our independent exact vector calculation derives all eight monomials from(7)-(11), rather than rerunning its local finite-field diagnostics. Every qd exponent is negative. The complete d|E divisor sums cost a small power; F^-1 is only harmonic up to its polynomial cap, while other F sums converge after sufficiently small divisor losses. qd Kc<=N(Hcol)<=sqrt(LR), L,R<<N0, F<<N0 and qa<<U^(1/6) provide the needed fixed polynomial caps before epsilon shares and derivative orders are chosen.

## 5. All collision sums and the nine original-color components

For one collision type put h=a+b>=2 and k0=1_(a!=b). A reciprocal norm exponent w>1 is summable over its squarefree ideal, after a small divisor loss. At w=1 the sum is harmonic up to its fixed polynomial support and must be paid. Norm exponents<1 need a genuine support bound.

The SQ0 and SQ2 exponents are 2h/3-k0/6 and2h/3+k0/3, with minima7/6 and4/3. Both complete thirteen-label sums converge. The left SQ cross exponent is5h/12+k0/12+a/2. Its only deficient type is(0,2), exponent11/12, giving(GP0)^(1/12); the right orientation transposes it.

CU0 has exponent h/3+k0/6. Its deficient types are(1,1) at2/3 and(2,0),(0,2) at5/6. Equation(3) gives N0^(1/3)(GP0)^(1/3). For the left CU cross, use Si<=C P0(D1D2)^(2/3), valid on the retained box. Its exponent is(h+a+k0)/4: (1,1),(0,2) cost3/4, while(0,3) is harmonic. The total extra cost is N0^(1/4)(GP0)^(1/4), with the transpose on the right.

For CU2 before Si, w=5h/12+k0/3. Only type(1,1), with w=5/6, can fail summability. Expand each quarter power of the THREE positive terms in(9). For a type(1,1) prime:

* A linear D1 component contributes an extra1/4 when its site is inverse1 or a slot, and zero at inverse2; D2 swaps the roles.
* A geometric component contributes1/6 at either inverse and1/4 at a slot.

Thus any geometric component leaves at worst a harmonic exponent. A pair of linear components is deficient ONLY if the shared prime occupies both omitted inverse sites. There are exactly four such configurations, with complete product norm bounded by the corresponding original Hij. Each has weight exponent5/6 and costs Hij^(1/6). Other collision patterns remain summable. Dropping their mutual coprimality enlarges only a positive majorant after all exact identities and support bounds. No independent-edge assumption is made.

The complete nine-component certificate is particularly transparent. Remove the common factor P0^(1/3); after N0^(-1/6) and collision summation, the remaining factors are

| Left/right component | Deficient edge, if any | Remaining factor |
|---|---|---|
| D1,D1 |22| D1^(1/3) U^(-1/8) |
| D2,D2 |11| D2^(1/3) U^(-1/12) |
| D1,D2 or D2,D1 |21 or12| (D1D2)^(1/12) U^(1/10) |
| D1,geometric or geometric,D1 |none; harmonic allowed| D1^(1/4) |
| D2,geometric or geometric,D2 |none; harmonic allowed| D2^(1/4) |
| geometric,geometric |none| (D1D2)^(1/6) |

Every entry except D2,D2 is bounded by(D1D2)^(1/6) on the full closed outer r,s rectangle. The remaining ratio is exactly U^((s-r-1/2)/6). This proves(S) and confirms that dropping the D2,D2 term would be unjustified where s-r>1/2. The exact helper checks these affine inequalities on all rectangle vertices; the table and local powers supply their proof. This refinement does not turn a positive price into a lower bound or establish a signed hard-sector saving.

## 6. Adaptive original-A caps, reserves and full signed complement

Keep the literal source selectors

    Csq(A)=U^(13/40) A^(24/5),
    Ccu(A)=U^(3/4) A^(24/5).                                (12)

SQ has priority; CU is selected outside SQ. HARD fails both. Each test is on the ideal(Delta ell), with its unit and fixed-place representatives retained. Its A is the original nominal row-divisor dyad. The selector is fixed before f and commutes with the complete mutual-divisor identity. A selector depending on f does not: for an artificial common prime the full weights1-1 cancel, whereas keeping only the f=p term leaves-1.

The A powers after(12) are3/5 for SQ0,3/10 for SQ cross,1/5 for CU0,1/10 for CU cross and zero for SQ2/CU2. Sum A<<U^(1/6), including every nominal dyad. The four coarse exponents are

    SQ0: 161/120+2tau/3;
    SQ cross: 263/160+5tau/12;
    CU0: 77/60+tau/3;
    CU cross: 431/240+tau/4.

These follow by inserting the exact support prices above and using r+s+v<=12/5. The remaining terms have exponents

    SQ2: 53/48+(r+s+v)/3+tau/6;
    CU2 geometric: 35/24+(r+s)/6+v/3+tau/6;
    CU2 linear: 11/8+s/3+v/3+tau/6.                         (13)

Against delta(r+s)+rho, the latter differences increase in r,s and delta and decrease in v. The delta derivative is at least217/100-625/486=21481/24300>0. Their limiting endpoint is delta=17/25,r=17/20,s=33/25,v=1/20, which is compatible with the remaining inequalities. Before tau/6 their exact gaps are23813/2730000,2768/170625, and2768/170625+1/200. Reserving tau/6, auxiliary1/500 and retained1/200 leaves177/113750,8241/910000 and12791/910000. The four coarse terms also have positive spare using T>=123353/67500; the smallest of those is13159/540000 for CU cross.

Fixed support constants and the fixed Delta lattice conversion are absorbed by the eventual threshold, not silently deleted from equalities. Split the single auxiliary allowance among all divisor, Fourier, dyadic, ray, finite-place and height losses after the polynomial caps and fixed slot depth are known. The finite profile orders work backwards through the bounded argument. Both original height operators, including -W/2-yW', remain in H_J. This inherits the positive-slot uniformity contract; it does not repair it.

Define R_N,hard by the Hcol!=1 part of C6 after the complete principal block is paid, using(2)-(7), the literal finite cap0<N(ell)<=Hc, and BOTH failures in(12). Preserve the full signed sum over d|E, all collision-site assignments, all original masks, both orientations and the complete coefficients. Equations(1)-(13) yield the first identity(R). Combining with accepted G204-G206 gives its second identity.

No nonunique analogue of the unique low band N(ell)<=U^(39/25) is established. The new companion has its own collision/hole-dependent frequency cut and starts at the actual first nonzero frequency. Large squarefree first-dual ideals can have both cores equal to their full norm, so the hard complement remains substantial. A bound for one of its signed pieces cannot be subtracted monotonically from another.

## 7. What remains open, evidence and provenance

The required next arithmetic input is a one-sided bound for the SUM

    R_U,hard + R_N,hard <= H_J U^(T-xi+epsilon),
                         some fixed xi>0,                  OPEN-HARD

uniform over the retained data and actual parameter suprema. An absolute bound is stronger. Under OPEN-HARD, the paid free-row transfer preserves any strict margin below min(xi,1/200); the two actual inverse witnesses and counted prefix retain only a margin below min(xi,1/200,1/2000). A possibly zero slot is never divided out.

This is not the full ordinary-character zero-exclusion return. Both signed physical projectors, family reconstruction, root/slot holes, exceptional and inducing rows, principal poles and imprimitive factors,6a/9a radii,K_phys,5/6 amplifier prices, clipped rectangles, shifted/shortened families, common mesh, actual suprema and genuine detector tails remain. No xi-to-c theorem is proved here. Nearer gains,1/6 and1/4 remain research targets, not consequences of this restricted payment. No growing-conductor conclusion or Hecke-family replacement for the final ordinary-character quantifiers is claimed.

Credit G155-G157 for the collision support and natural relative holes, G179-G181 for the six exact cuts and complete c_abs transfer, G185-G187 for the primitive source and original-color bound, and G204-G206 for the unique-sector square/cube strategy and original-A caps. [private research revision]'s moving quadratic/sixth-repeat method is an antecedent on a different cubic Mobius source; its additional I-C3CF/I-HECKE inputs are not used. The new useful result in the author candidate is payment of the full actual nonunique collision companion. The independent additions are the complete eight-monomial derivation, the explicit nine-component edge certificate and(S), and the fixed fractional-lattice endpoint clarification. No literature-priority claim is made.

Initial reviewer source pins froze before substantive analysis. Seven author artifacts match their frozen hashes; their source metadata and full worklog were read. The present check_prices.py ran once, native49fd6b, exit0 at04:30:10UTC: exact eight-price restoration and all nine CU2 component certificates passed. This is algebraic bookkeeping evidence, not an infinite-sieve proof. The mathematical arguments and versioned primary permissions are stated above.

## 5. Raw roots, masks, exceptional cores and the complement

For the raw subclass assume that an actual high character has Q<=Z^((21/25)W), with z<=W/21. Write w=u b^6, retaining the original unit, and freeze b before the free-row sum. Put s=log_Z Nb and V=W-6s. Original natural zeros give phi_w(n)=phi_u(n) times the indicator of (n,b)=1. In the witness use the conductor-bounded natural free-core presentation, whose positive-real zero and primitive conductor are unchanged by these Euler deletions. On every actual slot retain its b-hole. MI's arbitrary bounded fixed prime coefficient permission includes that hole; no new arbitrary-mask MP theorem is needed.

For V>=20W/21, z<=V/20 and

    (89/100)V-(21/25)W >= (4/525)W.

This strictly positive padding licenses the free theorem. Counting roots in the s-dyad costs Z^s. Since Ec is affine,

    s+Ec(V,z)=Ec(W,z)-(6Ac-1)s,
    6Ac-1>=6869/6250>0.

Thus the main root sum keeps Ec(W,z). The proof does not assign a V-scale modulus bound to the potentially much larger b-radical. Fixed natural-constructor constants are paid before the final threshold, and the root holes remain on the actual columns.

For V<20W/21 use the accepted old unmarked free density and the physical price of the punctured slot product. Its exponent is bounded by rho W+delta z-(6rho-1)s, with s>W/126. Since rho>=19/54 and k decreases on [.68,.70], the remaining uniform margin after paying G<=3kz and W/5000 is exactly

    (19/54-1/6-3k(.68))/21-1/5000
      =112003/257985000 >0.                            (R6)

Bounded free windows and fixed-inducing free cores have their actual raw population O(Z^(W/6+small)), not a falsely fixed raw cardinality. If the required physical high-bin pointwise bound holds, their exponent W/6+delta z fits R6 with room. Any principal/artificial source branch without that upper-price hypothesis retains its original estimate and is not asserted to belong to this restricted theorem.

It follows that the actual raw high eligible subclass satisfies

    sum |Q_w|^2 << Z^[Eold(delta;W,z)-W/5000+epsilon] H_J. (R7)

The complementary high rows, having no low-conductor high character of the specified kind, retain Eold. Their union has not been improved uniformly. A primitive conductor near the full row norm remains permitted; the existence of a repeated prime valuation describes legal conductor savings but does not construct a high zero or a saturating row.

For a physical application, impose the restriction only after the actual signed reconstruction has produced its positive child norm: freeze the missing radical, preserve both full projectors and every clipped rectangle, count joint labels once, and measure Q on that complete character. Whole-character conjugation and fixed Euler holes preserve Q; an additional moving character does not automatically do so. If both Cauchy factors are in licensed subclasses, their respective exponent savings are averaged. If only one is restricted, only half its saving enters. If a signed sector cannot be separated into these positive restrictions, use the old bound. This retains the original source without a hereditary row-class assumption.

All other c10 branches remain unchanged: first/second zero, low and far-high bins, extracted errors, FI costs with actual 6a/9a radii and K_phys^(5/6), shortage/no-slot complements, all four independent profiles, weighted Euler shifts including zero capacity, principal residue and supremum feedback. None is silently assigned R7. Fine mesh and loss choices precede the fixed family/profile list; their finite height orders precede the small internal height exponent; raw powers precede tail orders and the final threshold. Larger heights use the original absolute bound with a larger polynomial height factor.

## Frozen source contract

Write q_n for ideal norm. All ideals use M's actual good primary and
fixed finite-ray conventions, with squarefreeness on ideals rather than
integer norms. The infinity coefficient and short coefficient are

    a(n)=alpha(n) eta(n) chi_n(lambda)^(-2) gamma_2(n),
    xi(g)=alpha(g)^3 eta(g)^3,
    a(de)=a(d)a(e)chi_d(e)^4                 ((d,e)=1).

The zero extension supplies the zero at shared d,e. On a separated
linear side the actual characters and projector are

    chi_R(ng)^3 chi_P(n)^4 1_(P,Rg)=1,

with mark coefficient u_i(P)/sqrt(q_P) independent of live n,g,R,
two independent arrays and independent height variables. Put

    Omega_i=sum_P |u_i(P)|^2/q_P,
    S(N,L)=N+L+(NL)^(2/3).

The two perpendicular product masks are (n,g)=(n,bar(g))=1.
They belong to the evaluated JPS auxiliary extension. The original
short-core weight remains h((g,g')); it is never recomputed from an

statement:
## 8. Uniform critic audit S10: one compact sensor, all heights, paid stability

S10 proposed complementary compact Mellin sensors. A single explicit box already gives a one-way nonvanishing bridge on any positive half-plane; stable reconstruction is a different question. For fixed h>0, extend M_chi(x)=0 for x<1 and define

    S_h(x)=int_0^h M_chi(x exp(-u))du
          =sum_(n<=x)mu(n)chi(n) min(h,log(x/n)).                (R15)

At n=x the weight is zero; at n=x exp(-h) it is h. The unit, all natural zeros and complete moving cofactor region are included. Absolute integration for Re(s)>1 gives

    int_1^infinity S_h(x)x^(-s)dx/x
       =(1-exp(-h*s))/(s^2 L(s,chi)).                          (R16)

Fix 0<gamma<1. If for each fixed ordinary chi and every epsilon>0 the COMPLETE S_h(x) is O_(chi,epsilon)(x^(gamma+epsilon)) at all sufficiently large x, the left side is holomorphic on Re(s)>gamma. Multiplying by L gives the nonzero factor (1-exp(-h*s))/s^2 there. Its nontrivial numerator zeros have Re(s)=0, and s=0 is outside this domain. Therefore no L-zero can occur anywhere in Re(s)>gamma. Principal poles are treated meromorphically as in Section 2; imprimitive factors and natural zeros were never removed. This is an all-finite-height argument, not a finite-height screen, and it uses no lower multiplier bound uniform in height. The complete arithmetic sensor bound remains open.

For stability, on a weighted log L2 line with fixed sigma>0 the convolution multiplier is

    K_h(s)=(1-exp(-h*s))/s,
    (1-exp(-h*sigma))/|sigma+it|<=|K_h(sigma+it)|
       <=(1+exp(-h*sigma))/|sigma+it|.                         (R17)

Consequently a bounded global inverse on unrestricted weighted L2 is impossible without a derivative cost. Precisely, with S(y)=S_h(e^y),

    S'(y)=M_chi(e^y)-M_chi(e^(y-h)) almost everywhere.

The causal inverse for this DIFFERENCE has weighted L2 norm at most (1-exp(-h*sigma))^(-1), by the geometric sum of backward translations. Its input is e^(-sigma*y)S'(y), not merely e^(-sigma*y)S(y); equivalently the weighted derivative is f'+sigma f. The derivative factor in (R17) has not disappeared. The unweighted pointwise telescoping ends when y-jh<0 and is exact away from the jump endpoints. All sums can instead be interpreted distributionally at endpoints.

More generally a finite bank of compact L1 kernels has multipliers tending to zero as |t| tends to infinity on each such line. To see this without any number-theoretic hypothesis, approximate each weighted kernel in L1 by finite interval step functions: each step's Fourier integral tends to zero, and the approximation error uniformly bounds the multiplier error. Thus a fixed finite weighted sum of squared multiplier magnitudes also tends to zero. Fourier packets concentrated near large heights show there is no positive global lower frame bound on unrestricted weighted L2. This says nothing against the one-way pole bridge, the actual arithmetic source, a bank with derivatives/atoms, or a scale-dependent bank with separately paid costs.

The main lesson is exact: complementary zeros are not necessary for this positive half-plane box sensor, but a cheap stable reconstruction has not been obtained. W22's smoothing and G109's complete fixed-bank/difference Mellin returns own the general mechanism. This source-specific compact formula is a useful explicit interface, not a new analytic family. Its arithmetic estimate and any adapter to native H remain open. The independent finite check of (R15) used exact formal log-prime coefficients, not floating integration.

statement:
## 9. A separate quantitative anchor: delta=2 really has an inverse

This section is an additional concrete completion of the parked cofactor problem, not the arithmetic estimate for the small-shift interval I. First take zeta. More generally its proof works for any Dirichlet-series coefficients |a(n)|<=1, a(1)=1, |a(2)|=1. Put delta=2. Formula D8 has leading term

    c_2 2^(-s),  c_2=(9/256)a(2),
    C_2(s)=c_2 2^(-s)(1+R(s)).                           (D22)

The remaining generalized Dirichlet series is supported on dilations r=mn/2>=3/2. At Re s=-1, its absolute coefficient norm is bounded by

    ||R||_(-1)
      <= [zeta(3)zeta(7)-zeta(5)^2]/(9/128)-1 <19/20.  (D23)

Proof: the positive identity

    sum_(m<n) (mn)^(-3)(m^(-2)-n^(-2))^2
                        =zeta(3)zeta(7)-zeta(5)^2

follows by expanding the square and pairing (m,n) with (n,m); diagonal terms are zero. The first term m=1,n=2 equals 9/128. Every other coefficient of the actual cofactor is bounded by its positive counterpart. Division by the first coefficient proves D23, uniformly in every imaginary height.

The final strict inequality has a small exact rational certificate. Let S_j=sum_(n=1)^32 n^(-j), j=3,5,7. Integral comparison gives zeta(j)<=S_j+1/((j-1)32^(j-1)) and zeta(5)>=S_5. Exact integer arithmetic verifies

    (S_3+1/(2*32^2))(S_7+1/(6*32^6))-S_5^2
                                               <351/2560,

where 351/2560=(1+19/20)(9/128). The script stores the exact positive rational difference; its decimal diagnostic for the resulting upper bound on ||R||_(-1) is .9468750294472809. That decimal is not used as the proof.

In particular, C_2(s) has no zero in Re s>=-1 and

    |C_2(s)| >=(9/5120)2^(-Re s).                       (D24)

Define the coefficient dilation measure (real signed for zeta)

    nu=sum_(j>=0)(-R)^(star j).

Convolution is multiplication of the positive dilation arguments, with all repeated labels coalesced only by summation. D23 gives

    sum_r |nu(r)|r <=20,  support(nu) subset {1} union [3/2,infinity).

For delta=2, the complementary E in D7 has coefficients bounded by 4d_3(n)n^(-2), hence its Gaussian field is O_epsilon(x^(-1+epsilon)). If M_tau(x)=sum_n a(n)g_tau(log(n/x)), and H_2 is the D3 field for this a, physical Mellin convolution gives the exact reconstruction

    M_tau(x)=c_2^(-1)sum_r nu(r)
                  [H_2(2x/r)-E_2^g(2x/r)].             (D25)

Absolute field convergence follows first from the Gaussian kernel and the weighted coefficient norms, and the displayed bounds extend the identity to all x>0. This is an actual physical readout, not an operator-norm identification with an unrelated functional.

There is a finite version on X<=x<=2X:

    M_tau(x)=c_2^(-1)sum_(r<=X)nu(r)H_2(2x/r)
                                      +O_epsilon(X^(-1+epsilon)). (D26)

Indeed the E sum is bounded using sum|nu(r)|r^(1-epsilon)<=20. For r>X, the H arguments lie below 4; the Gaussian left tail gives H_2(t)=O(t^(-1)) on 0<t<=4, and its omitted sum is O(X^(-1)sum|nu|r). The r<=X sum is finite: each nonidentity factor is at least 3/2, its depth is bounded by log X/log(3/2), and each factor's numerator mn is at most 2X. This prices the complete small-scale tail, with no frozen moving cutoff substituted at the wrong scale.

For ordinary odd-modulus characters, |a_chi(2)|=1, so the same anchor proof is immediate. For even moduli this specific delta=2 anchor can be obtained by the explicit finite atom repair a(2):=-1, leaving every other a_chi(n) unchanged. This corresponds to adding the entire function (chi(2)-1)2^(-s) to 1/L. It does not change its poles and its physical discrepancy is a single Gaussian left-tail term. The determinant coefficients in that auxiliary variant must use the repaired a exactly; they are not silently identified with chi(n)W_delta(n). The main averaged theorem and D20 require no such repair and preserve all original character zero extensions.

D25--26 are useful quantitative bridges, but also clarify the objection: the large-shift determinant is a stably invertible signed dilation filter of the ordinary Mobius field, up to a paid error. Its missing prime outputs cannot by themselves reduce the exponent. The new small-shift averaged target is retained as an explicit arithmetic problem, without calling this anchor an arithmetic solution.

## The exact cutoff defect is a positive boundary Gram

Let w_j be arbitrary complex weights, W=sum|w_j|^2>0, d=sum w_j c_j. Write Pi=Pi_N, Q=I-Pi, D=Pi d Pi and B=Q d Pi. The cutoff is divisor-closed: Q d^* Pi=0 and Pi d Q=0. Consequently

    D^2=0,
    D^*D+DD^*=W Pi-B^*B,       0<=B^*B<=W Pi.          (F4)

Proof: expand the full CAR identity d^*d+dd^*=WI between Pi's. The missing lowering term Pi d Q d^* Pi is zero. The other missing term is precisely B^*B. The same divisor-closure proves D^2=Pi d^2 Pi=0. No orthogonality between distinct boundary insertion paths is asserted: B^*B retains their signed off-diagonal overlaps.

Put Gamma e_S=(-1)^|S|e_S, Str(T)=Tr(Gamma T), and T_chi e_S=chi(n_S)e_S on Pi's range. Finite-dimensional cyclicity and the oddness of D give

    W M_chi(N)=Str(T_chi B^*B)+Str([T_chi,D^*]D).       (F5)

Indeed Str(T_chi(D^*D+DD^*))=Str((T_chi D^*-D^*T_chi)D). The diagonal version of F5 is the fully explicit formula

    W M_chi(N)=sum_(p in P)|w_p|^2 [
      sum_(N/p<n<=N,p not|n) mu(n)chi(n)
      +(1-chi(p))sum_(n<=N/p,p not|n)mu(n)chi(n)].      (F6)

Each bracket separately equals M_chi(N), by splitting the p-free and p-divisible terms. The strict lower bound and inclusive upper bound are exact even when N/p is integral. In the principal case the bulk term vanishes. For nonreal or negative chi(p) it generally does not. Ramified primes were removed from P; their original source coefficients remain zero. Character-dependent weights may be chosen, but neither term may be discarded.

The classical squarefree-complex/Euler-characteristic interpretation is not new: Bjorner's https://arxiv.org/pdf/1101.5704 studies that complex and its Betti numbers. [restricted research revision] G79 already records an exterior Ward identity; [restricted research revision] G118 retains all parity layers; [restricted research revision] retains the twisted prime-toggle bulk. The newly integrated [restricted research revision]/G144 also explicitly owns the character-gauge/cone correction; G145 retains the complete prime/composite readout. F1–F6 isolate the ordering correction and positive cutoff Gram in this proposal; their familiar cores receive no new arithmetic or literature-novelty credit.

There is an additional exact scope check. For all characters of one presented modulus q, the unramified state space is the same, T_chi is unitary, and

    d_chi=sum_p chi(p)w_p c_p=T_chi d T_chi^*,
    D_chi=T_chi D T_chi^*,   E_chi=T_chi E T_chi^*.      (F6a)

Thus simply putting character phases on the differential preserves every singular value, Laplacian eigenvalue and Betti dimension. It does not turn M_chi into a character-sensitive spectral index. The source dependence is the inserted observable T_chi and its commutator in F5. This is not an obstruction to a bound uniform over characters of fixed q; it identifies what a bare spectral calculation has omitted.

Weights supported only on primes with chi(p)=1 make the character commutator vanish. That legitimate specialization still has the full positive boundary price below; the bulk term is not claimed unavoidable for every choice of weights.

## G96. The complete shrinking-arc return and finite signed core

For fixed 0<c<1/2, gamma=1-c, let h=1/(qN). The every-integer-N input

    E_arc(N)=integral_0^h |R_N(x)|^2 dx
       <<_(chi,r,epsilon)N^(1-2r-2c+epsilon)

is equivalent, up to arbitrary epsilon losses, to the full Mertens bound
M_chi(X)<<X^(gamma+epsilon) at every real X. It remains OPEN for an
improvement over c8. Its equivalent notation does not establish a gain.

Finite Fourier inversion of chi and the Bernoulli formula show that Phi
is a single polynomial of degree<=r on[0,1/q], with nonzero constant
beta=2L(r,chi). An endpoint reproducing polynomial p_r satisfies
integral_0^1 p_r(u)u^j du=1_(j=0), j<=r, and ||p_r||_2=r+1.
For O_N f=integral_0^1 p_r(u)f(hu)du and
T_N=sum_(n>N)a(n)n^-r, this gives

    beta T_N=O_N R_N-eta_N, eta_N=O(h^(r+1)),
    |O_N R_N|<=(r+1)sqrt(qN)E_arc(N)^(1/2),
    M_chi(N)=1/L(r,chi)-N^r T_N
                +r integral_1^N t^(r-1)T_floor(t)dt.

Every original n<=N stays in the same first polynomial cell. The reverse
implication uses global Lipschitz continuity of Phi and Abel summation
on the entire infinite tail; derivative jumps add no point masses.
The full Mertens bound then gives holomorphic1/L on Re(s)>gamma at every
height by its Mellin integral. Original imprimitive factors remain; the
principal pole at1 is excluded from the zero-free statement.

Choose fixed kappa>0 with2c+kappa<1, and set

    G=ceil(N^(2c+kappa)),
    T=ceil(N^(1+2c/(2r-1)+kappa)),
    K_N(n,m)=integral_0^h Phi(nx)conj(Phi(mx))dx,
    Core_N=sum_(N<n,m<=T,(n,m)<G)
                  a(n)conj(a(m))(nm)^-r K_N(n,m).

The exact remaining input is the one-sided bound
Core_N<<N^(1-2r-2c+epsilon). Core_N is real, not necessarily positive.
The complete large-gcd absolute price is
O(N^(1-2r)/G+N^-2r), including diagonal and all far terms. The infinite
completion is exactly R_T and has squared norm O(T^(1-2r)). The squared
triangle inequality pays every cross term without an unpaid global norm.
Both costs are strictly below the target, and the reverse comparison gives
equivalence. Positivity of the full finite energy also bounds Core_N from
below by minus the paid complement, so an absolute bound on the WHOLE
core is equivalent here. Absolute values on individual pairs are not.

The missing energy gain is2c, independent of fixed r. Current first gain
requires strictly more than.25028522. At c=1/6 the completion exponents
before kappa are10/9 for r2 and16/15 for r3; at c=1/4 they are7/6 and11/10.

is>=A/(2N) for N<n,m<=(1+eta)N, where
A=integral_0^(1/q)|Phi(u)|^2du>0. Lipschitz continuity proves this from
the value at equal scales. Squarefree q-unit density and the O(N^2/G)
large-gcd pair count imply an absolute-pair price>>N^(1-2r), even with

## 3. D2: all prime blocks, all complements

Fix a nonprincipal ordinary chi. PB partitions EVERY unramified prime into finite disjoint blocks B and U, with fixed m,C, |B|<=m, r_B=min B, diameter<=C r_B^(1-eta), exact sum_(p in B)chi(p)=0, and U(x)<=C x^delta_U. Constants and block size may depend on chi; exponent bounds for a claimed common strip must be common across the covered characters. Finitely many exceptions are included in U.

On a compact with Re s>=sigma0>max(1/2,1-eta,delta_U),

    |sum_(p in B)chi(p)p^(-s)|
      =|sum_(p in B)chi(p)(p^(-s)-r_B^(-s))|
      <=m C |s| r_B^(-sigma0-eta).                       (C7)

This follows by integrating the derivative -s u^(-s-1) on each real interval. Every block has a distinct integer anchor, so the resulting series converges. All j>=2 logarithmic terms are independently dominated by C_sigma0 sum_(n>=2)n^(-2sigma0), and the entire U contribution converges by its counting bound. Hence the full logarithm, ordered by complete blocks, converges locally uniformly. Its exponential agrees with1/L in Re s>1, and LQ=1 continues throughout the claimed half-plane. All complex phases, all prime powers, all natural zeros and every height remain present.

The three omitted tails beyond the defined complete-block anchor cutoff Y are respectively

    O_K(Y^(1-sigma0-eta)),
    O_K(Y^(1-2sigma0)),
    O_K(Y^(delta_U-sigma0)).                              (C8)

Each omitted block has every prime>Y, which justifies the second tail; the third retains every unmatched prime. Anchors<=Y can include primes above Y, but this is the specified source ordering, with initial agreement in the absolute-convergence region. No product cap on Mobius integers is being erased. G108 concerns a different hard-cutoff marginal and retains its nontrivial cofactor interactions; it is not D2's source.

### 3.1 Critic reduction to pointwise prime discrepancy and natural cutoffs

For the useful range0<eta<=1, define A_chi(x)=sum_(p<=x)chi(p). Each fully included block has zero total. An incomplete block crossing x has

    x-C x^(1-eta)<r_B<=x,

because r_B<=x<max B<=r_B+C r_B^(1-eta). There are at most C x^(1-eta)+1 possible distinct integer anchors, and each partial block contributes at most m in modulus. Therefore PB implies the fully natural-cutoff bound

    |A_chi(x)|<=m(C x^(1-eta)+1)+U(x)
              =O_chi(x^(1-eta)+x^delta_U+1).             (C9)

This is a power bound for the actual singleton prime-character sum, not merely for selected pairs. Abel summation of(C9), followed by the already summable higher powers, yields precisely the same gamma_B=max(1/2,1-eta,delta_U) zero return. Thus D2 is an explicit sufficient structural contract for the classical prime-discrepancy route. Its analytic implication is not an independent new family of cancellation; a proof of PB would still be substantial new arithmetic.

It also pays the natural-product boundary. The difference between the complete-block cutoff with r_B<=Y and the ordinary prime cutoff p<=Y consists only of the above crossing blocks. Their omitted primes lie just above Y, there are O_chi(Y^(1-eta)+1) of them, and each log(1-chi(p)p^(-s)) is O_K(Y^(-sigma0)). The difference is

    O_K(Y^(1-eta-sigma0)+Y^(-sigma0)),                   ([restricted research revision])

which tends to zero in the same strict region. Hence, under PB in this range, the natural finite Euler products also converge there with their full cutoff boundary paid. This strengthening uses the actual diameter/count assumptions, not a formal rearrangement. No claim about natural-cutoff convergence under LP alone follows.

For a principal character every unramified phase is1, so there is no nonempty balanced block. An unmatched set containing all such primes cannot have exponent<1. The complete ordinary-character objective is therefore not solved by nonprincipal PB: a separate principal input such as D1 is still mandatory. The first-gain requirements eta>.12514596 and delta_U<.87485404 are correct, but completely open in this packet. Approximate balance would introduce an additional full block-residual sum; it cannot be substituted into(C7) at zero cost.
