statement:
## 4. Both height variables and the remaining signed scalar

Fix 0<a<1. For each retained ordered component set

    U_i(s)=sum_(d in I_i)mu(d)d^(-s),
    eta(s)=(1-2^(1-s))zeta(s),
    D_ij(t)=exp(tau*(a+it)^2/2)*eta(a+it)
               *U_i(a+it)U_j(a+it).                    (G14)

The Mellin transform of S_tau is exp(tau*s^2/2)eta(s). Prove this
first on Re s>1 by absolute Fubini, then use its two rapidly decaying
tails to continue before moving the line. An absolutely divergent
ell Dirichlet series is never interchanged on a<1. Mellin inversion
and Plancherel give

    G_ij(x)=(2*pi)^(-1)integral_R D_ij(t)x^(a+it)dt,
    integral_0^infinity |G_ij(x)|^2 x^(-2a)dx/x
       =(2*pi)^(-1)integral_R |D_ij(t)|^2dt.              (G15)

For T=D*sqrt L, define

    Z_X(x)=(2*pi)^(-1)integral_[-T,T]
                    [sum_(i+j=-2,...,1) D_ij(t)]x^(a+it)dt,
    Q_X=integral_X^(2X)|Z_X(x)|^2 dx/x.                 (G16)

Equivalently Q_X is (2pi)^(-2) times the double integral over
[-T,T]^2 of the complete product

    [sum D_ij(t)] conj([sum D_i'j'(t')])
       *((2X)^(2a+i(t-t'))-X^(2a+i(t-t')))/(2a+i(t-t')). (G17)

Every component interaction, complex phase and both independent height
variables remain. The diagonal t=t' has the continuous value of the
displayed kernel; no principal-value convention is needed.

The alternating partial sums imply |eta(a+it)|<=|a+it|/a.
Absolute interval sums and D_i^*D_j^*<=X exp(3kappa sqrt L) then pay
the entire omitted height field by

    X^(1-tau*D^2/2+o(1)).                               (G18)

This proof uses no moving-height Mertens or Hecke estimate.

The required arithmetic statement is now explicit:

**OPEN-GC:** for all sufficiently large dyadic X and every epsilon>0,
prove Q_X <<_epsilon X^(2gamma+epsilon), with these exact coefficients,
bins and fixed parameters. No current theorem supplies a new gamma.

The stronger sufficient **OPEN-GM** asks, for every retained ordered
component, integral_R |D_ij(t)|^2dt <<_epsilon
X^(2gamma-2a+epsilon), uniformly over its moving interval endpoints.
The O(sqrt L) count is subpower, so Cauchyâ€“Schwarz makes it sufficient.
It is not necessary: a proof may use negative cross-component terms.

statement:
# [private research revision]: a complete two-prime estimate below the old band

G207-G208 pay a fifth disjoint class of actual same-zero witness rows,
relative to the retained PR9/[restricted research revision]/[restricted research revision]/G137 contracts. The complete signed
complement retains one eighth of the original signal. Pure large-prime
plain columns still survive, and no complete row cover or increase in
`c11=.1251459636` follows.

The [author](outside-band/report.md) and [independent review](outside-band-review/report.md)
give the full proofs. Root checked both reports, the literal coefficient,
profile and marked-moment permissions, every collision and shared valuation,
and the complete removed-source subtraction. Ancestry, original positive-slot
uniformity and external definition/import/admission remain open. No new
formalization, kernel result or public-record claim is made.

## Literal source and the new weight

Retain [G197-G198](../[private research revision]/joint-cut-integration.md) and
[G199-G200](../[private research revision]/prime-band-integration.md): original Eisenstein
ideals, primary/unit convention, excluded S, fixed phase, common full
orientation `phi_u=nu psi_u^(+/-1)`, character zeros and independent slot
heights. Keep centrally normalized inverse M(R), plain S(D) and all old
prime slots Q of total width v. Write `R=U^r,D=U^m,B=M(R)S(D)`.

Fix `delta in[17/25,7/10]`, `0<eta<=1/1000`, `0<=v<=1/20`, and
G137's cutoff `t=t_*(delta,v)-eta` BEFORE witnesses. Use the entire
crossing window `|r-r_*(t)|<=2eta` and its original fine padding.
One internal buffered grade beta is retained in both

    |S_u(D)|^2 >= D^beta U^(-epsilon_det),
    |S_u(E;V)|^2 << H_J U^epsilon_det E^beta, E<=C D.

It satisfies `beta>=delta-small`, `beta<=3/4`. The direct retained Mellin
line pays every shortened scale; no reflected or shifted lower spike is
substituted. Nonempty subunit annuli are bounded dilations. The fixed
number of old slots is enlarged by TWO before final thresholds and heights.

Put `Z=U^eta,A=Z^2,Y=T=Z^4` and let J contain the good prime IDEALS
with `Z<=N(p)<A`. It is disjoint from the previous CLOSED band `[A,Y]`.
For `N(b)>1`, define the ordered-pair weight

    omega(b) = [log N(b)]^-2
          sum_(p,q in J, pq|b) log N(p) log N(q),
    omega(1)=0.

When p=q, its pair occurs once if and only if `p^2|b`, regardless of
additional valuation. With radical logarithm ell_rad,J and the sum d_1,J
of squared prime logarithms at valuation exactly one, the exact identity is

    omega(b)=[ell_rad,J(b)^2-d_1,J(b)]/[log N(b)]^2.

The old theta counts the logarithmic mass in `[A,Y]`. Therefore

    0<=omega(b)<=(1-theta(b))^2<=1-theta(b).

This is a coefficient statement. It gives no ordering of signed norms.
Every superscript below means multiplication on the original tuple
coefficients BEFORE signed merging.

## G207: full product, collisions and weighted removal

Let `V_D,2(x)=W_P(x)[log D/log(Dx)]^2`. Its finite derivatives are
uniformly controlled on the original positive-m annulus. The exact
convolution is

    S^[omega](D)=(log D)^-2 sum_(p,q in J)
       log N(p) log N(q) phi_u(pq)/sqrt(N(p)N(q))
                              S(D/[N(p)N(q)];V_D,2).

For distinct p,q in dyads P1,P2, separate the common three-coordinate
profile before live rows, primes or colors. With `E=D/(P1 P2)`,
`P1^-1/2 P2^-1/2 E^-1/2=D^-1/2` exactly. The fixed prime coefficients
are `log N(p)/log U`, extracting only the bounded scalar `(log U/log D)^2`.
Scale differentiation changes no arithmetic pool or coefficient.

Apply the same-bin shortened plain estimate first, then marked MI with
the two additional slots. Each new width is at most `2eta`; the first
gate adds at most `8eta`, the second at most `32eta`. G137 gives
`r+2v<=1-.01017`, so their remaining margins are at least

    217/100000 and 39417/50000

at the largest eta and v, before prescribed fine losses. The off-diagonal
dyad has squared price `H_J U^(1+epsilon)D^beta(P1 P2)^(-beta)`.

The collision payment is complete. Each distinct new prime can equal at
most one old slot prime; two such equalities remove different old slots
because the old supports are disjoint. For an equality, the actual old
and new scales are comparable, and its normalizers have absolute mass
`sum_p(P_i N(p))^-1/2 <<1`. Both shortened plain savings remain.
The extracted phase `phi_u(p)^2` is a positive-norm contraction with its
zero retained. The inverse is never declared coprime to that prime.
Remaining equality exclusions are fixed row-independent prime supports.

For the surviving h distinct prime variables, one normalized random
coloring on the UNION of their prime-IDEAL pools gives

    1_(p_1,...,p_h all distinct)
       =h^h E_color product_i 1_(color(p_i)=i).

The cost is the fixed h^h, not the number of colorings. Equal-norm
different ideals remain different labels. Empty and one-slot cases use
their literal products. This exhausts old/new support intersections.

For p=q, leave the COMPLETE old Q and inverse inside MI. After applying
the shortened plain bound, the dyadic absolute mass is
`sum_p (log N(p)/log D)^2 N(p)^(-1-beta) <<U^epsilon P^(-beta)`.
Its squared price saves `Z^(-2beta)`, including p=q equal to an old
slot or inverse prime. Hilbert triangle over all patterns and dyads proves

    ||M S^[omega] Q||^2_Omega
         <<H_J U^(1+epsilon)D^beta Z^(-2beta).        (1)

Now pay the entire removed source B_T. G198 keeps the exact
`L=lcm(q0,k^2)` and complete q0-smooth inverse restoration, with norm
coefficient mass `T^(-beta/2)U^epsilon`. The plain multiplier is
omega(Lc), rather than omega(c). For d=pq, set `h=d/gcd(d,L)`.
Primewise valuations give `d|Lc` if and only if `h|c`, so the exact
extracted plain block equals

    S_(omega,L)(E)=(log D)^-2 sum_(p,q in J)
       log N(p)log N(q) phi_u(h)N(h)^(-1/2)
                                      S(E/N(h);V_D,2), E=D/N(L).

For p=q, h is p^2,p,1 when the valuation in L is 0,1,at least2.
No character is divided out. The denominator is exact because
`log(N(L)N(c))=log(D(N(c)/E))`. All residual cofactor valuations remain.

After the same plain bound, ideal counting and `N(L)<=C D` give uniformly

    |S_(omega,L)(D/N(L))|
       <<H_J U^epsilon (D/N(L))^(beta/2) A^(1-beta).

The squared cost is `A^(2(1-beta))=Y^(1-beta)`, once. Insert this inside
the FULL G198 coefficient convolution before absolute values, keeping every
shared prime and inverse restoration. Then

    ||B_T^[omega]Q||^2
       <<H_J U^(1+epsilon)D^beta T^(-beta)Y^(1-beta).

The exact signed identity `C_T^[omega]=B^[omega]-B_T^[omega]` and triangle
now give the COMPLETE core estimate

    ||C_T^[omega]Q||^2
       <<H_J U^(1+epsilon)D^beta
                         [Z^(-2beta)+T^(-beta)Y^(1-beta)]
       <<H_J U^(1+beta*m-2beta*eta+epsilon).          (2)

At beta=17/25 the two savings are `34eta/25` and `36eta/25`.
Their difference is positive since beta>2/3 with a reserved buffer.
This pays a genuinely new pair-divisibility source below the old band.

## G208: exact pair mass and a fifth actual row class

The reviewer sharpens the uniform block calculation. Write

    s=(1+beta)/2, w_p=log N(p)/log D,
    I=sum_(p in J,p|L)w_p,
    V=sum_(p in J,p not|L)w_p N(p)^(-s).

Then the EXACT positive pair mass is

    A_L=sum_(p,q in J)w_p w_q N(pq/gcd(pq,L))^(-s)
       =(I+V)^2-sum_(p in J,v_p(L)=1)w_p^2[1-N(p)^(-s)]
       <=(I+V)^2.                                  (3)

Distinct pairs factor. On the diagonal, valuation0 contributes p^(-2s),
valuation1 contributes p^(-s), and valuation at least2 contributes1.
Only the middle case differs from the diagonal of `(I+V)^2`. This proves
(3), including all p=q and shared-prime cases, with no extra diagonal loss.
Since `I<=1+O(1/log D)` and `V<<U^epsilon A^((1-beta)/2)`, it also
reproves the uniform block bound above. It is a sharper label-specific
positive mass, not a new global power saving or signed contraction.

Keep all FOUR previously paid classes FIRST. Their remaining actual rows
have `|C_T^[1-theta]|>|M(R)S(D)|/4`. On that complement, define

    Omega_pair={u: |C_T^[omega](u)|>=|M_u(R)S_u(D)|/8}.

Divide (2) by the ORIGINAL same-beta plain spike. Its D^beta cancels
before beta is weakened to physical delta, giving

    sum_(Omega_pair)w_u |M_u(R)Q_u|^2
         <<H_J U^(1-2delta*eta+epsilon).             (4)

Q is never divided out. This fifth class is disjoint by construction;
its preloss reserve above the requested eta is `9eta/25`.
Every remaining row satisfies

    |C_T^[1-theta-omega]|>|M(R)S(D)|/8,
    N(n/rad n)<T NP,
    0<=1-theta(b)-omega(b)<=1-theta(b).               (5)

Band prime squares remain absent. Lower-band prime squares are retained
and were paid explicitly in (1)-(3). The repeat support is a necessary
tuple consequence, not an intrinsic signed merged-coefficient projection.

For an actual surviving tuple with every prime factor of b in J, put
`e_b=eta log U/log N(b)`. Its repeat bound gives
`ell_rad,J(b)>log N(b)-4eta log U`, while
`d_1,J(b)<=2eta log U log N(b)`. In the source's positive-m range,
this yields `0<=1-omega(b)<=10e_b`. This is useful coefficient damping
but only a constant factor at fixed eta; it gives no signed power saving.

The full coarse norm is paid by the complete difference

    C_T^[1-theta-omega]=C_T-C_T^[theta]-C_T^[omega].

It still gives only `H_J U^(1+epsilon)` for the inverse moment after
division. Good prime plain ideals above Y with coprime squarefree inverse
tuples have F=1 and theta=omega=0. They survive unchanged. This is a
coefficient example, with no claim that it supplies a high-zero row.

## Heights, the hard residual and limits

Factor the original witness twist into the three norm coordinates before
separating the height-free smooth kernel. Its Fourier measure is fixed
before every live label or coloring. Within retained height padding use
the same-bin shortened plain upper bound. On its full Fourier complement,
absolute ideal counting is bounded by `E^(beta/2)(1+|tau|)^J1` using the
original internal height floor; integrate that polynomial against the SAME
kernel with sufficiently high fixed decay. The extra kernel order does
not enlarge the already fixed MI height degree. Keep the exact ordering
of smooth losses, internal floor, final external degree and physical height
exponent. Original raw-count-before-decay tails, real powers, independent
slot heights, fixed punctures and zero/short scales remain paid.

The remaining target is the full signed estimate

    ||C_T^[1-theta-omega]Q||^2_Omega_rem
         <<H_J U^(1+beta*m-eta+epsilon),              OPEN-OUT-PAIR

or another complete arithmetic estimate with the same original inverse
moment return. Together with the disjoint paid classes it would imply
G137's J_eta^all. This is still OPEN.

The author's serious large-prime extraction test identifies a precise
limitation. An absolute inverse-divisor shell of width kappa costs U^kappa
in the squared norm. Adding a plain prime of width lambda requires
`kappa>2lambda-g`, `g=1-r-2v`, so its available saving is at most
`beta lambda-max(0,2lambda-g)`. It fails for `lambda>=g/(2-beta)`.
An inverse prime has no assumed intermediate divisor; this complement
cannot be removed by an unproved divisor cover. Coherent extraction is
not ruled out.

Root also checked the optional G90 comparison left secondary by the
reviewer: at delta=beta=7/10,v=0,eta=.001,
`t=12491/9000,r=2t/3,m=t/3,lambda=m`, the licensed amplified exponent
is `1/6+(79/30)m=1121789/810000>1`. This says only that this available
bound does not close that sector. It is not an arithmetic lower bound.

All physical roots/counts, missing radicals, extraction scalars, BOTH
signed projectors, joint labels, clipped rectangles, actual6a/9a radii,
fixed-inducing K_phys^(5/6), principal terms, old-only children, short/no-slot
alternatives, Euler shifts including zero capacity and common-Delta return
retain their original payment. Each positive child needs its own witness;
signed projection need not preserve the class. Paired gains average under
Cauchy. M/24 is unused. G137's unchanged architecture retains its c<2/15
ceiling; 1/6 and1/4 need an upstream replacement and its complete return.

## Evidence

The [manifest](retention-manifest.json) preserves14 original evidence/input
files,12 exact source bindings and the prior raw scorecard. Both owners
normally released their claims. Root read the full reports and helper,
the one saved finite receipt, G137/G198/G199-G200/G90, and literal PR9
B0.3-20,B3.3,B3.6,B3.31. The finite receipt checks625 coefficient cases,
82,944 shared-valuation extractions,336 coloring cases,16,384 complete
signed tuples, gate arithmetic and the G90 example; none was rerun.
These support finite algebra, while analytic acceptance rests on the
named source-relative contracts. Preserve the review's original missed
deadline and its explicitly bounded source audit. c11 and its inherited
obligations remain unchanged.

statement:
## 6. Ancestry and live repair condition

W43.2-4 / [restricted research revision]-W2 already establish the fixed-depth lesson for literal Newton/geometric reciprocal completion. With d_Y=delta-1*m_Y and Q_(Y,j)=m_Y*(delta+d_Y+...+d_Y^(*(j-1))), its residual is d_Y^(*j). On a Y-rough squarefree integer with exactly j prime factors it equals (-1)^j j!. Counting such products yields a full absolute Gaussian obstruction of exponent 1 at fixed j. Its complete signed complement and reciprocal feedback cannot be omitted.

The present family is not literally that Newton column. It uses the coefficient w(d)=mu(d)F_(T,k)(d) and residual delta-1*w restricted to the actual squarefree divisor downset. For example, with T=1, k=1 and a product of two distinct primes, (5) is +1, whereas the order-2 Newton residual d_1*d_1 is +2. More generally the present first unpaid layer is (-1)^(k+1), while the Newton order-(k+1) rough layer has the extra (k+1)! factor. W43 also includes nonsquarefree integers and a Gaussian readout; here mixed small-prime/large-prime labels are legitimate, the field is finite, and R(a)=chi(a) exactly on a>N/2. statement:
## 5. Literal application to the accepted compensated source

This section imports exactly [restricted research revision] G176-G178; it does not replace the pinned PR9/Gao analytic ancestry or enlarge a Hecke family. Fix an ordinary Dirichlet character chi modulo a positive integer q, naturally zero off the units, and fixed unramified p. Write a=lambda chi, h=chi, s(r^2)=chi(r)^2 with s zero off squares. Retain

 q1=delta_1-p chi(p)delta_p,
 q2=delta_1-p chi(p)^2 delta_(p^2), v=q1*q2,
 b=v*h, g=a*s, c=v*g=a*a*b.                              (LC1)

In particular q2's coefficient is -p chi(p)^2, not -p^2 chi(p)^2. The original b is bounded by (p+1)^2 and has zero mean and period p^3q. The root sequence beta(r)=chi(r)^2(1-p1_(p|r)) has zero mean and period pq. Their compensations and all their cross terms remain unchanged. The Euler series is

 D_c(z)=P_p(z)J_p(z)L(2z,chi^2)^2/L(z,chi),
 P_p(z)=1-chi(p)p^(1-z), J_p(z)=1-chi(p)^2p^(1-2z).       (LC2)

For a fixed 3/4<=gamma<1 set L=X^gamma, M=X^((6-2gamma)/4), Q=p^3q, eta0=1/(6000Q), B(n)=min(L,eta0 X^6/n^5). Choose tau in the CLOSED range

 max(gamma tau,gamma(1-tau)) <= (11gamma-3)/8,             (LC3)

before live real x; U(n)=B(n)^tau, V(n)=B(n)^(1-tau). The original exact decomposition is c=Q_U+Q_V-S_tau+R_tau, with

 Q_U(n)=sum_(de=n,d<=U(n))a(d)(v*s)(e),
 S_tau(n)=sum_(d e l=n,d<=U(n),e<=V(n))a(d)a(e)b(l),
 R_tau(n)=sum_(d e l=n,d>U(n),e>V(n))a(d)a(e)b(l).

Q_V is the other ordered short slot. The full source is C(x)=sum c(n)f_x(n). The old complete core is T=sum_(L<n<=M)R_tau(n)f_x(n).

Now define G=X^(1-gamma) and impose ONE additional literal tuple condition:

 T_small(x)=sum_(L<n<=M) f_x(n)
     sum_(d e l=n,d>U(n),e>V(n),gcd(d,e)<=G)a(d)a(e)b(l). (LC4)

The difference T-T_small is precisely Theorem LG with the frozen mask
1_(L<de l<=M)1_(d>U(de l))1_(e>V(de l)). It includes every cofactor, squareful output and multiplicity admitted by that mask. No averaging of the gcd, merged-output truncation or live-x-dependent mask has been substituted. By (LG1),

 ||T-T_small||_j << X^(gamma+epsilon), j=1,2,             (LC5)

because X/G=X^gamma and X^(3/4)/sqrt(G)=X^(1/4+gamma/2)<=X^gamma. All constants are uniform in tau satisfying (LC3), since the mask theorem is uniform.

For clarity, the COMPLETE difference C-T_small is the sum of the two full short-slot sources, minus the full small-double source, plus the original R_tau at n<=L, its entire damped tail n>M, and the new finite-core large-gcd source. The inherited short-slot estimate is

 ||Q_D||_2^2 << D^2+X^(6/11)D^(16/11)+X^(3/4)D^(1/2)
                    +min(X^(3/5)D^(7/5),X^(15/16)D^(1/2)).

At D=X^alpha and alpha<= (11gamma-3)/8, its four norm exponents are all <=gamma. Both ordered slots therefore cost X^gamma. The small-double source is paid by the actual zero-mean b, its period Q, and the unchanged derivative-gap cutoff eta0. Its treatment has not been reapplied to the gcd-restricted source, where that periodicity might be broken. The old low core uses |R_tau(n)|<=(p+1)^2d_3(n). The full high core has squared norm O(X^(3/2+epsilon)+X^6 M^(-4+epsilon)); its two exponents are <=2gamma for gamma>=3/4. The new source costs (LC5). These complete-source estimates and norm triangle give

 ||C-T_small||_(L^j([X,2X],dx/x))
        <<_(p,q,gamma,epsilon) X^(gamma+epsilon), j=1,2. (LC6)

Every low/high, short/plain, two-short and good/bad interaction is paid at the norm level. No unconditional scalar energy-error formula is asserted. Equality at each exponent boundary is allowed because the theorem is stated for every epsilon. An intermediate strict-reserve failure would not prove impossibility at equality.

The retained merged coefficient is exactly

 R_small(n)=sum_(m l=n)a(m)D_(U(n),V(n);G)(m)b(l),
 D_(U,V;G)(m)=#{ordered(d,e):de=m,d>U,e>V,gcd(d,e)<=G}.   (LC7)

Complete multiplicativity a(d)a(e)=a(de) holds for shared primes and natural zeros; it is used only for Liouville in (LC7). No unrestricted Mobius merge is inferred. Every common factor up to G, every squareful m, and both orderings remain. All exact gcds greater than G were paid, including composite products of small common primes. The result does not impose primality or pairwise coprimality with l. It is a new restriction inside the oscillatory core, not an improvement only to its already paid far tail.

The coarse absolute finite-core sum would cost M/G up to X^epsilon and require delta=log_X G >= (3/2)(1-gamma). The collision-only intermediate bound in Section2 would require delta>=(6/5)(1-gamma). The full local-count-plus-collision proof permits delta=1-gamma. These comparisons are bounds for this SAME within-source integer gcd, not the physical Hecke cross-copy gcd of [restricted research revision]. No independent-height/projector theorem is imported into an arbitrary coefficient class; (LG1) has its own elementary proof. Natural unitary coefficient twists can occur in its bounded weights, but the analytic return below concerns a fixed ordinary character.

## 1. Discovery comparison before selection

1. **Logarithmic prime convolution.** The literal identity
   mu(n)log n=-(mu*Lambda)(n) couples actual prime powers and Möbius signs.
   Subtracting the continuous principal prime law suggests a signed Volterra
   equation. However, its prime discrepancy convolved with mu has not been
   estimated, and the absolute weighted kernel grows for every gamma<1.
   A baseline prime-number error cannot be silently substituted for the
   required bilinear error. Retained as a possible distinct upstream attack;
   this pass does not advertise the convolution identity as a saving.

2. **Growing phase bank.** Averaging exp(-it(n/x)^k) over a long t-window
   improves frequency separation, but the Mellin signal scales as
   t^(-s/k). Removing the slow t~1 sector changes the physical scale to
   x/t^(1/k); reconstruction/normalization remains a real cost. A generic
   second-moment bound alone does not pay that sector. Not selected.

3. **Actual multiplicative extraction.** Ramaré/Kátai-type prime extraction
   could use mu(pm)=-mu(m) for p not dividing m. In the transition the
   cofactor interval shrinks as p grows, keeping (pm/x)^k of order one.
   Close prime rows retain coherent correlations. A complete extraction
   must keep prime divisibility exceptions and the numbers without a
   selected prime. This remains a distinct route, not disproved here.

4. **Mean-zero completion plus the nonlinear phase — selected.** The old
   q2=delta1-2delta2 completion turns the long free cofactor into the
   genuinely alternating sequence b(l)=1-2*1_(2|l). Its literal row
   retains an additive frequency pi while the polynomial phase is slow.
   The new nonlinear tail bound can pay the entire region where that
   frequency separation fails. This may remove an actual small-divisor
   sector at a power threshold for every fixed character, including the
   principal one. It is an arithmetic identity plus an estimate, rather
   than a new name for the full norm. The surviving signed large-divisor
   term will still need a new estimate.

Outside-primary discovery inspected Matomäki–Teräväinen's published
short-interval Möbius theorem and extraction lemma, as detailed in
Section7. The row estimate below is proved directly. No external
power-saving theorem has been imported.

### 4.1 Small-radical bound

For every delta>0,

    C_delta := sum_{n>=1} n^(-delta)/r(n)
      = (1-2^(-delta))^(-1)(1-3^(-delta))^(-1)
          product_{p>=5}
             (1 + p^(-1-delta)/(1-p^(-delta)))
      < infinity.                                       (4.1)

prime contribution is O_delta(p^(-1-delta)), a summable series.
The finitely many remaining factors are finite and positive.
This proves (4.1) without any uniformity as delta tends to zero.

Using 1_{r(n)<=Y}<=Y/r(n) and the exact Gaussian supremum,

    g_tau(log(n/x)) <= C_{delta,tau} x^delta n^(-delta),

gives, uniformly for every x>0 and every integer Y>=1,

    |U_Y(x)| <= C_{delta,tau} C_delta Y x^delta.           (4.2)

This includes all n, however large relative to x, and all powers
of 2 or 3. There is no finite-height replacement hidden in (4.2).

## Complete fixed-block return

For any gamma>0, finite B gives

    sum_d |e_B(d)|d^-gamma=product_(p in B)(1+p^-gamma),
    sum_m |r_B(m)|m^-gamma=product_(p in B)(1-p^-gamma)^(-1). (R3)

Both are finite. If U is the fixed Gaussian or exponential field formed from a, and U_B the same fixed kernel with a_B, R1 yields

    U(x)=sum_d e_B(d) U_B(x/d),
    U_B(x)=sum_m r_B(m) U(x/m).                        (R4)

Absolute Fubini follows on a sufficiently right half-plane from the bounded original coefficients and the finite-prime geometric series; it also follows directly for these rapidly decaying kernels. Minkowski on the all-real-shell norm sup_(T>0) T^-gamma ||U||_[T,2T] gives exactly the two constants R3. Small scales have their genuine decaying tails. Thus fixed-block exponents agree, with the usual positive epsilon buffers; a finite block has no automatic exponent saving.

Every E_B is nonzero in Re(s)>0 because |chi(p)p^-s|<1. For a precise field return, take U_B(x)=sum_n a_B(n) exp(-n/x), or use exp(-(n/x)^2). Use shell norm L^2([T,2T],dx/x). If that norm is O_(chi,epsilon)(T^(gamma+epsilon)) for all large T and every epsilon>0, then the small-x exponential tail and Cauchy--Schwarz on dyadic shells make its Mellin integral holomorphic for Re(s)>gamma. For Re(s)>1 that integral is respectively Gamma(s)/(L(s,chi)E_B(s)) or Gamma(s/2)/(2L(s,chi)E_B(s)). The gamma factors never vanish in Re(s)>gamma>0. Multiplication by the literal meromorphic L and nonzero E_B gives zero exclusion there at every finite height. Principal poles and imprimitive factors remain in that identity. This supplies a complete return but no field estimate. If B varies with X, all R3 constants and all shifted-shell U_B hypotheses must remain uniform and be paid; one cannot take a different fixed-B Mellin transform on each shell. A same-shell statement at X alone is insufficient for R4.

    gamma_1(n)=mu(n)G(n)*conjugate(a0(n)),
    A_R(n)gamma_1(n)=G(n)*conjugate(a0(n))*mu(n)A_R(n).   (R3)

The fixed ray function G is not the two-variable Gauss sum. Since n is squarefree, mu(n)mu(d)=mu(n/d), hence

    mu(n)A_R(n)=sum_(m|n)mu(m)V(Nn/(Nm R))
              =-sum_(m|n)mu(m)[1-V(Nn/(Nm R))].          (R4)

The last step again requires n!=1. Both complementary cofactors survive when the two sides of an ordered square are transformed. R4 cannot be transported to arbitrary valuations: for the formal prime-square example n=p^2, R=Np, its left side is0 and its last right side is-1 when Np>=2. R2, which retains mu(n/m), does hold there. The helper records the corresponding n=4,R=2 example.

The new coefficient mu(n)A_R(n) is not a fixed ray character or an original product mark. Its amplitude need not be one: if n is the product of three distinct primes of norms<=R with every pair product norm>=2R, then A_R(n)=1-3=-2 and mu(n)A_R(n)=2. This is an algebraic conditional example, not a claim about a particular prime pool. Even a divisor bound does not meet PR9 B3.6, which explicitly permits no further coefficient on n.

Thus the author's refusal to apply the canonical Gauss energy directly is correct. A later reconstruction may freeze a complementary factor and pay the complete punctures, fourth-power labels, profiles and count, but that reconstruction has not been proved for the whole transformed source here. Treating a moving-modulus Gauss sum as a fixed-modulus character for a second ordinary Poisson application is likewise unjustified.
title: R4. Squarefree Gauss transfer and its scope

## C. Where the original-order positive argument stops

Keep n through the quadratic Cauchy step as required. At fixed
short-core inversion label f and mark/row label Delta the quadratic
column is j=n b, g=f b, of norm O(NG/q_f), with its actual zeros.
For B2, summing ALL decompositions at a given n before Cauchy gives
exactly a(n)lambda(n), not a coefficient at N/U. The residual mark
polynomial is at this same n:

    M_(Delta,f,b)(n)=sum_Q u(Delta Q)/sqrt(q_Q)
                  1_(Q,f b)=1 chi_Q(n)^4,             (C1)

with the inherited fixed supports, combined Delta characters and
outside q_Delta^(-1/2). The original n stays live when applying the
cubic sieve. In particular its sieve length remains N. Independent
source heights and cyclic phases used for the exact far mask are
bounded column factors at this step, as in JPS19--24.

The resulting proved bound is still

    |C_prime[h]| << Z^epsilon G(K+NG)S(N,L)
                         sqrt(Omega_1 Omega_2)P_orig. (C2)

It has the correct coefficients, roots, projectors and original
prime projection, but it does not save a positive power. Applying
the same method separately to I and II is no stronger: their
normalized coefficients are divisor-bounded, while the negative
terms in B3 have been lost. This locates the failure before any
claim about a reduced column length. No full H theorem, Hecke
prime theorem, spectral theorem or arbitrary-mask inheritance is
being used.

The next calculation tests whether the retained cubic interaction
can give a useful alternative estimate BEFORE this original-order
argument. Its different positive step is displayed explicitly and
is not inserted into C1 with a changed meaning of n.

## A06. Fixed-degree polynomial detrending still detects zeros

**PROVED CONDITIONAL TRANSFER.** Source: BA D8. Let \(M(x)=\sum_{n\le x}\mu(n)\), fix \(r\ge0\), and suppose, for every \(\epsilon>0\),
\[
 \inf_{\deg P\le r}\int_N^{2N}|M(x)-P(x)|^2dx
       \ll_{\epsilon,r}N^{2a+1+\epsilon},\qquad 0<a<1. \tag{A06.1}
\]
Then \(\zeta(s)\ne0\) for \(\Re s>a\). To prove this, choose
\(\phi=\psi^{(r+1)}\), \(\psi\in C_c^\infty(1,2)\), and set
\(T_\psi(N)=\int_1^2M(Nu)\phi(u)\,du\).
Polynomial moments vanish, so Cauchy gives \(T_\psi(N)\ll N^{a+\epsilon}\). Initially for \(\Re s>1\),
\[
 \int_0^\infty T_\psi(N)N^{-s}\frac{dN}{N}
 =\frac{\int_1^2\phi(u)u^sdu}{s\zeta(s)}.
\]
The left side is holomorphic for \(\Re s>a\). Integration by parts makes the numerator
\((-1)^{r+1}s(s-1)\cdots(s-r)\int\psi(u)u^{s-r-1}du\).
At any possible nontrivial zero in that half-plane its polynomial factor is nonzero, and a localized \(\psi\) makes the integral nonzero. This contradicts holomorphy. Euler nonvanishing handles \(\Re s>1\); the line \(\Re s=1\) is covered by the accepted baseline.

The discrete version follows because a fixed-degree least-squares fit to \(|M(n)|\le2N\) has scaled coefficient norm \(O_r(N)\); it varies by \(O_r(1)\) on a unit interval. Interpolation costs \(O_r(N)\), affordable for \(a>0\). Growing degree is a different hypothesis: its calibration can increasingly approximate the very power \(x^\rho\) one must detect.
title: A06. Fixed-degree polynomial detrending still detects zeros

statement:
# W42: paid comparison of the old principal signal and a fixed Gaussian detector

## Current checkpoint and scope



The accepted written analytic incumbent is **c5=7821/62500=.125136**, relative to pinned PR9/Gao PR15; new-endpoint formalization/kernel replay remain pending. Old c0's independent kernels are separate. This report proves no increase in c and no full signed Gaussian/f3/short-divisor-H estimate.

Two closely linked developments survive:

1. **D02:** an exact, two-way, coefficient-paid comparison of PR9's old principal signal with the ideal Möbius Gaussian, at every exponent greater than 2/3. A separate explicit periodic convolution returns ordinary Dirichlet Gaussian detectors. This is a source identity and norm transfer, not an imported arithmetic saving.
2. **D26 (protected rare draw):** strip off the known factor L(s+1,eta), then retain only correction primes of norm at most P. The complete omitted correction first has a rigorous norm error O(X^beta P^(4-6beta)) for 2/3<beta<1 under the inherited full Gaussian beta bound. Extracting the literal sixth-power factor as well sharpens this to O(X^beta P^(-2beta)) for beta>3/4; see D26.4. All powers of retained primes remain. Both explicit finite-prime targets have quantitative near/1/6/1/4 returns and remain OPEN.

The original phase alpha(p), all character zeros and the fixed exclusions remain literal. The Euler correction named H_eta below is **not** the separate short-divisor hypothesis H; no statement about its projectors or covariance is inferred here.

## 1. Frozen exploration, source contact and six tests

`seeds.md` contains all 30 cards and original p labels, frozen and fully read back before detailed history. SHA256 d336e16f016813388887c843e1a3aaeded8675094b08ddf2b160251edb2c8120. The problem and immutable recipe hashes match the assignment. Six selections, in order: **01,02,04,26,28,16**. The protected bridges were 01/02; the sequential literal-threshold draws were 04 (p<.10), 26 (p<.01), then most-different 28, wildcard 16. Every eligible card from every group entered its literal stratum. Pools were frozen before draws, with no reroll. `selection-results.json` SHA256 dd6b40a8c2e428b5791e825611c5fac2cf16a5b36d71c6ead3da103f7f45d5d8. Root received both freezes before outcomes.

Afterward I used the maintained 29-family/109-child navigation and the early/late/[private research revision]/[private research revision] source pointers, current proof, [private research revision] integration, PR9's actual paper B0.35--36/B0.62, the ordinary ideal dictionary, W35's calibrated Gram identity, W31's free quotient, and W40's actual prime-projection audit. No claim is made to have reread every historical proof. Relevant ancestors are F01/F09/F11/F16, N28, U-FILTRATION, W31 R31.30, W35 T1/T3 and current G28--30. The claimed delta is the literal PR9 Euler correction and its priced prime tail, not general convolution/Gram theory or literature priority.

**T01, two-witness convex duality.** Let Gamma be a positive definite 2x2 Hermitian Gram and v a nonzero required complex signal vector. The least quadratic cost among w with v* w=1 is 1/(v* Gamma^-1 v), by weighted Cauchy--Schwarz; the optimizer is Gamma^-1 v/(v* Gamma^-1 v). For a singular positive semidefinite Gram, a nonzero component of v in ker(Gamma) permits a zero-cost feasible vector. Otherwise v lies in its range and the same formula uses the Moore--Penrose inverse. The case v=0 is infeasible. For two copies of one reciprocal L-function the pole residues are proportional to their multiplier values, so v is not an independent two-zero constraint. This is useful bookkeeping with F09/F11 ancestry, not an estimate. D02 identifies the actual multiplier.

**T02, paid transfer.** The direct source calculation is D02 below. It passes: neither a kernel replacement nor the source's qualitative |H_eta-1|<=1/2 statement is used as a substitute for a coefficient norm. The full physical J_eta-f_eta comparison remains outside this transfer.

**T04, prime-power quotient.** This card's phrase 'prime powers' includes primes. For actual rational f3, the prime-power field equals minus the smoothed prime sum, apart from the prime 3 and a higher-power O(X^(1/2+epsilon)) term. By the prime number theorem and fixed Gaussian integration, the field is asymptotic to -exp(tau/2)x/log x, uniformly for x in [X,2X]. The inherited F3=O(X^beta), beta<1, then forces the complementary field to have the opposite leading term. Erasing that source is not a power-small error; the cross term is essential. This is a scoped actual-source failure, consistent with existing rough/mixed-opposition results. Erasing only powers of degree at least two costs O(X^(1/2+epsilon)) but leaves primes and the hard signed energy. No claim about an arbitrary prime-power orthogonal projection follows from this support calculation.

**T26, prime-factor conditional coupling.** W40's exact four-label Gaussian weights (1,2,2,1) at p=2,q=5 give covariance -1/12 and correlation -1/3: independent prime revelation is not legitimate. Rather than assume that drift vanishes, D26 uses the exact deterministic local factors of the old/new transfer and pays every unrevealed prime. This is a specified constructive repair of the seed's coupling premise, not a stochastic independence theorem.

**T28, free-product shadow.** In degree j the word-to-commutative quotient has norm sqrt(j!), and actual Möbius signs are constant on each j!-word fiber. W31 R31.30 already proves this exact test; at j=2 the two words pq/qp have equal signs and reinforce. No hidden cancellation is created by the free model. This duplicate failure stops the naive transfer; arithmetic estimates for the actual symmetric lift remain open.

**T16, two-detector susceptibility.** For actual shell fields U,V, put E0=||U||^2, E1=||V||^2 and C=<U,V>, with <U,V>=integral U conjugate(V). If E1>0,

    ||U-lambda V||^2 = E0-|C|^2/E1 + E1 |lambda-C/E1|^2.       (T16)

Both terms must be paid. A shellwise optimizer can change with X and does not itself define a fixed zero detector. For the source-normalized D02 pair take U=M_eta,2 and V=C_S^-1 exp(-25/36)P_eta(exp(5/3)x), so V has Mellin transform h(s) times that of U. Their combined multiplier is 1-lambda h(s): choosing lambda=1/h(rho) annihilates a simple pole at the proposed zero rho. An unconstrained energy optimizer can therefore destroy the signal. Fixed coefficients with a nonzero multiplier at rho retain the ordinary Mellin return, but their full signed cross energy is open. This adds a source-specific warning to the inherited W35 identity, not a third substantive development or a no-go theorem for simultaneous use.

## 2. D02: literal Euler correction and two-way norm transfer

### D02.1 Frozen source and normalization

Let K=Q(omega), and use PR9's primary-generator/ideal dictionary (one representative per nonzero ideal, no extra factor six). Fix one finite-order, trivial-infinity Hecke character eta and the source's finite exclusion S, including its conductor and primes above 6. All ideals below are coprime to S; equivalently coefficients are zero on every excluded prime power. Constants may depend on this fixed data. No growing-conductor or angular-family theorem is asserted.

For each remaining prime ideal p, let Q=Np, alpha(p)=p/|p| in the source's primary-generator convention, t=Q^-1, and, temporarily, z=Q^-s. Write

    a=eta(p), b=conjugate(alpha(p))^6 eta(p)^6,
    D=a z, R=b Q^3 z^6,     |a|=|b|=1.

PR9 B0.35 is exactly

    H_p(s)=(1-t^2)/(1-R) * (1+t(D-R)/(1-D)).                 (2.1)

Let C_S=product_(p notin S)(1-Q^-2)>0 and normalize H=C_S h. Then

    h_p = [1-(1-t)D-tR]/[(1-D)(1-R)].                       (2.2)

This scalar C_S is unrelated to PR9's physical residue scalar c_S in B0.36. Neither is suppressed by normalization. PR9's k is also retained: define P_eta(x)=x^k f_eta(x). Its transform is

    Mellin(P_eta)(s)=exp((s-5/6)^2) H_eta(s)/L_K^S(s,eta).   (2.3)

This is the **principal signal**. The physical probe J_eta, its compensator, all nonprincipal rows and their moment estimates are different objects.

### D02.2 Absolute coefficient and inverse budgets

For sigma>2/3 put d=Q^-sigma and r=Q^(3-6sigma). Since r<Q^-1 and d<Q^-2/3, the local Dirichlet-series weighted coefficient norms satisfy

    ||h_p-1||_sigma <= [r+t(d+r)/(1-d)]/(1-r) =: B_p^+,
    ||h_p^-1-1||_sigma
       <= [t d+(1-t)r+d r]/[1-(1-t)d-t r] =: B_p^-.       (2.4)

The first bound follows from (2.1) after removing 1-t^2. For the second, subtract 1 from (1-D)(1-R)/(1-(1-t)D-tR); the numerator is -tD-(1-t)R+DR. Its denominator is expanded in its actual convergent geometric series. Indeed

    (1-t)d+t r <= Q^(-2/3)+Q^-2 <= 2^(-2/3)+1/4 <1.

No local zero is hidden in the inverse. Both B_p^+ and B_p^- are

    O_sigma(Q^(-1-sigma)+Q^(3-6sigma)).                    (2.5)

Ideal counting N_K(T)=O_K(T) implies convergence of their sums. Therefore there are multiplicative, exact ideal coefficients h(a), j(a), with h*j=delta_1 and

    A_sigma=sum_a |h(a)| Na^-sigma <infinity,
    B_sigma=sum_a |j(a)| Na^-sigma <infinity.              (2.6)

For example A_sigma<=product(1+B_p^+) and B_sigma<=product(1+B_p^-). The products converge locally uniformly for Re s>2/3. Thus **the literal H_eta and its reciprocal are holomorphic and nonzero there**, with this coefficient proof; the source's previously used .87 half-plane is not the limit of this Euler correction. This does not extend the physical contour boxes, source moments or PR9 endpoint argument.

There is a real boundary to this absolute method. The exact sixth coefficient is

    h(p^6)=t a^6+(1-t)b Q^3.                              (2.7)

Its magnitude is at least (1-Q^-1)Q^3-Q^-1. The prime-ideal harmonic series diverges (equivalently, use the source's prime ideal theorem), so sum |h(a)|Na^-sigma diverges for sigma<=2/3. This only obstructs the stated absolute coefficient norm. It is not a lower bound on the signed Gaussian field or a universal c<=1/3 barrier.

### D02.3 Exact fixed-field identity

Set

    M_eta,tau(x)=sum_a mu_K(a) eta(a) g_tau(log(Na/x)),
    g_tau(v)=(2*pi*tau)^(-1/2) exp(-v^2/(2tau)).

The source zeros at S and the Möbius squarefree zeros remain exact. Absolute convergence and Gaussian tails justify all coefficient identities. For Re s>1,

    Mellin(M_eta,tau)(s)=exp(tau*s^2/2)/L_K^S(s,eta).

Since exp((s-5/6)^2)=exp(25/36) exp(-5s/3) exp(s^2), (2.3) gives

    P_eta(x)=C_S exp(25/36)
                  sum_a h(a) M_eta,2(exp(-5/3)x/Na),
    M_eta,2(x)=C_S^-1 exp(-25/36)
                  sum_a j(a) P_eta(exp(5/3)x/Na).          (2.8)

The real shift, width 2, scalar and original ideal coefficients are all necessary. These are absolutely convergent field identities, first checked on an absolute Mellin line and then by unique inversion. Polynomial coefficient growth follows already from any fixed absolute line, so the Gaussian also supplies direct locally uniform convergence. Composing the two series is justified on that line and by the same positive majorants.

For real-shell norm

    ||F||_[X,2X]=(integral_X^(2X)|F(x)|^2 dx/x)^(1/2),
    ||F||_sigma=sup_(X>0) X^-sigma ||F||_[X,2X],

Minkowski gives the paid estimates

    ||P_eta||_sigma <= C_S exp(25/36-5sigma/3) A_sigma ||M_eta,2||_sigma,
    ||M_eta,2||_sigma <= C_S^-1 exp(-25/36+5sigma/3) B_sigma ||P_eta||_sigma. (2.9)

Every x/Na shell has its own scale. No moving arithmetic cutoff is kept at an incorrect parent scale. Gaussian left tails pay bounded/small shells; at most two adjacent dyadic shells cover a real shell. Thus the complete all-dyad moments for P_eta and M_eta,2 are equivalent at every exponent gamma>2/3, also with the usual every-positive-epsilon quantifier. At gamma=2/3 the every-epsilon version follows by using (2.9) at sigma=gamma+epsilon; no exact-power endpoint norm is asserted.

A bound for M_eta,2 with exponent gamma makes its Mellin integral holomorphic on Re s>gamma by dyadic Cauchy--Schwarz, including derivatives on smaller half-planes. Its Gaussian left tail pays zero. The multiplier never vanishes, so every zero of the same L_K^S in that region is excluded; its possible pole at 1 is allowed. This supplies the complete conditional zero return, independently of an unproved covariance claim. To recover a common boundary for the original entire fixed-family scope, the proposed moment hypothesis must hold for **each** fixed target with the same gamma and every positive epsilon; constants, exclusions and large-X thresholds may depend on the target. A result for one eta alone excludes zeros only for that target.

### D02.4 An explicit ordinary-Dirichlet return, with a paid width change

Here is a concrete bridge to the rational Gaussian architecture, rather than an identification of different coefficient lists. Fix an ordinary Dirichlet character chi with its actual zero extension, set psi=chi*chi_-3, and let eta(a)=chi(Na). Euler factors give

    L_K(s,eta)=L(s,chi)L(s,psi).                          (2.10)

At a split rational prime the two ideal factors equal the two same-sign Dirichlet factors; at an inert prime the product is (1-chi(p)^2 p^-2s)^-1; at 3 only the chi factor survives. Zeros at primes dividing the presented modulus persist on both sides. This proves the identity without an inferred primitive reduction.

First restore the fixed excluded ideal primes in M_eta,2 by the finite polynomial product_(p in S)(1-eta(p)Np^-s). Its inverse is the corresponding finite product of geometric series, absolutely summable at every positive weight. Thus the restoration has fixed cost and leaves the exponent unchanged. Call the resulting complete field M_eta,2^full.

Fix any delta>0 and put B(s)=1-2^(1-s). Define the **actual periodic** sequence and fixed field

    d_psi(n)=psi(n)-2*1_(2|n) psi(n/2),
    K_psi,delta(y)=sum_(n>=1) d_psi(n) g_delta(log(n/y)).

If psi has period q, d_psi has period 2q and total sum zero over that period, including when psi is principal. Poisson summation of the zero-extended Schwartz function g_delta(log t) on each residue class gives K_psi,delta(y)=O_A(y^-A) for every fixed A as y tends to infinity; the zero Fourier mode vanishes. Its left tail is Gaussian. Equivalently, m integrations by parts bound it by C_(m,q,delta)y^(1-m), with m fixed after A. Consequently

    I_(gamma,psi,delta)=integral_0^infinity |K_psi,delta(y)| y^-gamma dy/y <infinity (2.11)

for every fixed real gamma. The Mellin transform of K is exp(delta*s^2/2)B(s)L(s,psi), first on Re s>1; pole cancellation at s=1 is literal, not asserted away.

The multiplicative integral convolution therefore satisfies

    integral_0^infinity M_eta,2^full(x/y) K_psi,delta(y) dy/y
       = sum_n [mu(n)chi(n)-2*1_(2|n)mu(n/2)chi(n/2)]
                    g_(2+delta)(log(n/x)) =: G_chi,2+delta(x).             (2.12)

This numerator is B(s), not 1-2chi(2)2^-s; the second coefficient is written explicitly to avoid that error. It reduces exactly to current G1 when chi=1, at the permitted fixed width 2+delta. Minkowski and (2.11) give

    ||G_chi,2+delta||_gamma <= I_(gamma,psi,delta) ||M_eta,2^full||_gamma.   (2.13)

All convolution tails and shell dilations are paid. The new width is fixed before X. No inverse heat operation or estimate at width 1 is inferred. Since B has no zero in 0<Re s<1, this is a full conditional ordinary-Dirichlet zero return. The ideal result already covers each fixed finite-order trivial-infinity Hecke target. It does not create a growing-conductor assertion.

This comparison shows a legitimate way easier **complete** estimates from the old principal signal could help the new detector. It says nothing that permits transplanting PR15 local moments to G13, F3 or the short-divisor H form without their missing arithmetic source adapters.

## 3. D26: pay unrevealed correction primes after removing a known L-factor

### D26.1 Exact local repair

The naive tail of h_p-1 contains the prime coefficient tD and costs P^-sigma. Remove it by the exact, absolutely bounded factor

    E(s)=L_K^S(s+1,eta),
    H_eta(s)=C_S E(s) Rcal(s),
    r_p(s)=(1-tD) h_p(s).                               (3.1)

This E is not assumed small: its coefficient mass at sigma is sum_a Na^(-1-sigma), and its inverse has the same positive majorant. Both are finite for sigma>0. Every power and phase remains in

    r_p-1=(1-t)[tD^2+R(1-(1+t)D)]/[(1-D)(1-R)].          (3.2)

In particular the coefficient at p is zero, and that at p^2 is t(1-t)a^2. The original p^6 contribution remains; it is not converted to an arbitrary Gaussian kernel error.

For sigma>2/3,

    ||r_p-1||_sigma
       <= (1-t)[t d^2+r(1+(1+t)d)]/[(1-d)(1-r)]
       = O_sigma(Q^(-1-2sigma)+Q^(3-6sigma)).             (3.3)

The inverse r_p^-1=h_p^-1/(1-tD) has a corresponding summable local bound; hence finite products and their inverses have coefficient norms bounded uniformly in their prime cutoff. This follows either from the direct product or from (2.6) and the E factor. No randomness, conditional independence or martingale drift estimate is used.

Let Rcal_<=P and Rcal_>P be the literal products over Q<=P and Q>P, respectively. ALL valuations at retained primes are included. By ideal counting and partial summation,

    sum_(Q>P) ||r_p-1||_sigma
       <<_sigma P^(-2sigma)+P^(4-6sigma).

For 2/3<sigma<1 the second term dominates, and the product estimate yields

    ||r_>P-delta_1||_sigma <<_sigma P^(4-6sigma).          (3.4)

For bounded P enlarge the fixed constant. For large P use product(1+b_p)-1<=exp(sum b_p)-1. All omitted interactions among large primes are included in that product; (3.4) is not a sum retaining only one missing prime.

### D26.2 Complete field approximation and cross terms

Let W_P be the fixed field at a specified prime cutoff P whose Mellin transform is

    Mellin(W_P)(s)=exp(s^2) E(s) Rcal_<=P(s)/L_K^S(s,eta). (3.5)

The fully corrected field W has the same transform with Rcal in place of Rcal_<=P. By (2.8), P_eta is exactly C_S exp(25/36) times W at the fixed dilation exp(-5/3). Thus no physical scale normalizer is lost.

Assume the inherited complete M_eta,2 bound ||M_eta,2||_beta<infinity for one fixed 2/3<beta<1. This is the source-level calibrated bound furnished by the accepted fixed-family zero-free premise with a positive buffer; it is not a new exponent. The coefficient convolution norm, uniform finite-product mass and (3.4) give

    ||W-W_P||_[X,2X] << X^beta P^(4-6beta).               (3.6)

This holds for every X>0 and P>=2 with one constant for fixed eta,S,beta. It therefore remains valid at P_X=X^theta. Define q=beta-theta(6beta-4). Then the complete error is O(X^q).

If an actual source estimate proves

    ||W_(X^theta)||_[X,2X] <<_epsilon X^(gamma+epsilon)    (OPEN-W42)

for every large dyadic X, and q<gamma, (3.6) gives W, then P_eta and M_eta,2, the same gamma exponent. D02 supplies the fixed-family zero-exclusion return. Conversely a complete gamma bound for M gives OPEN-W42 because the weighted norms of E Rcal_<=P are uniformly bounded at each gamma+epsilon>2/3. In the stated range this remains an equivalent arithmetic target, not a weaker exponent theorem.

The full mixed energy is explicitly retained. For R_X=W-W_P,

    ||W||^2=||W_P||^2+2 Re<W_P,R_X>+||R_X||^2,
    | ||W||^2-||W_P||^2 |
       <=2 ||W_P|| ||R_X||+||R_X||^2.                  (3.7)

Under OPEN-W42 the right side is O(X^(gamma+q+epsilon)+X^(2q)); both terms are below the target 2gamma with a positive buffer. Using only the inherited beta bound would instead pay beta+q, which is coarser and is not needed for the norm implication. No negative cross term is dropped and no different detector savings are added.

### D26.3 Quantitative returns and first useful next estimate

Use beta=8749/10000=.8749, strictly above the accepted boundary .874864, so 6beta-4=6247/5000. Any strict theta larger than the displayed threshold pays the full tail below gamma:

| Desired conditional c | gamma=1-c | threshold theta>(beta-gamma)/(6beta-4) |
|---|---:|---:|
| current c5, as a comparison | 54679/62500 | 9/312350 |
| near gain .1252 | 2187/2500 | 1/12494 |
| 1/6 | 5/6 | 1247/37482 |
| 1/4 | 3/4 | 1249/12494 |
| formal absolute-boundary target 1/3 | 2/3 | 1/6, with every-epsilon norm convention |

The c5 row is not a proof of an additional gain; the other rows are conditional targets. Constants depend on the fixed positive gaps. A convenient **first-gain test** is theta=1/10000, gamma=2187/2500. Then q=43738753/50000000=.87477506 and gamma-q=1247/50000000=.00002494. Proving the full original-sign OPEN-W42 with this P_X would yield c=.1252. No such bound is proved here.

The reduced coefficient family is completely constructive: start with mu_K*eta, convolve with eta(a)/Na (the actual E factor), then multiply the finite set of exact r_p local series (3.2), retaining all valuations and original S zeros. A physical Gaussian truncation can subsequently be paid from any absolute coefficient line, but no finite cap is required for (3.5)--(3.7). It must not be confused with G13's two-Möbius/alternating-restoration list.

The next subsection gives a second, more accurate approximation by paying another explicit global factor. The two approximants have different coefficient lists; neither is substituted into the other's source estimate.

### D26.4 Sixth-power extraction and the stronger paid target

Keep the source's b(p) and R=b(p)Q^(3-6s) exactly, and define

    V6(s)=product_(p notin S)(1-R)^-1,
    h(s)=E(s) V6(s) Rhat(s),
    rhat_p=(1-R)(1-tD)h_p.

This is a defined Euler series, not an appeal to an unproved estimate for an angular character. Its coefficients are b(a)(Na)^3 supported at the sixth-power ideals a^6, where b is the completely multiplicative extension of the specified prime values. Thus the absolute coefficient mass of V6 at sigma is sum_a Na^(3-6sigma), finite for sigma>2/3. Its inverse is supported at a^6 with coefficients mu_K(a)b(a)(Na)^3 and has the same positive majorant. These constants are paid in the norm transfer.

The exact local identity is

    rhat_p-1 = [t(1-t)D^2-tR+t^2DR]/(1-D).               (3.8)

For sigma>1/2 its weighted coefficient norm is

    ||rhat_p-1||_sigma
      <= [t(1-t)d^2+t r+t^2 d r]/(1-d)
      = O_sigma(Q^(-1-2sigma)+Q^(2-6sigma)).             (3.9)

The inverse obeys the same large-Q order. Explicitly, writing N=1-(1-t)D-tR,

    rhat_p^-1=(1-D)/[(1-tD)N],
    ||rhat_p^-1-1||_sigma
      <= [t(1-t)d^2+t r+t^2 d r]
         /[(1-t d)(1-(1-t)d-t r)].                     (3.10)

Here r<1, and (1-t)d+t r<(1-t)Q^-1/2+t<1. All local inverses are legitimate. The sums of (3.9)--(3.10) converge for sigma>1/2. In particular Rhat and its inverse have finite coefficient norms there. ### D1b. Every large principal cutoff has a collapsing root

For the principal character modulo fixed q, put P_N=pi(N)-#{p<=N:p|q}. Here A_N=P_N and the C_k are nonnegative integers. For every sufficiently large N, P_N>=8 and B_N/P_N^2<=1/8, so D1a applies to the **whole** polynomial.

The requisite prime lower bound needs no PNT input. For m>=1,

    binom(2m,m)>=4^m/(2m+1).

Each p-adic valuation of that binomial is at most floor(log(2m)/log p), since each term floor(2m/p^j)-2floor(m/p^j) is 0 or 1. Consequently

    binom(2m,m) <= (2m)^pi(2m),
    pi(2m) >= [2m log 2-log(2m+1)]/log(2m).

Taking m=floor(N/2) and removing the fixed finite set dividing q gives P_N >>_q N/log N. Hence lambda_N<=N/P_N^2=O_q((log N)^2/N), and

    alpha_N=-P_N^(-1)[1+O_q((log N)^2/N)],
    |alpha_N|=O_q(log N/N),
    |1+1/alpha_N|=P_N[1+O(lambda_N+1/P_N)].            (D1.4)

This strengthens the old finite face examples in one precise direction: no fixed-radius zero-free disk about z=0 survives for the complete principal hard-cutoff polynomials. The Taylor series of the branch of log Z_N based at 0 has radius exactly |alpha_N|, because alpha_N is the unique nearest zero and is simple. A straight real interpolation from 0 to -1 crosses a zero for every sufficiently large N.

**Scope:** this does not prohibit an N-dependent complex path avoiding the root, a signed contour representation, analytic continuation with explicit factors removed, or a different smoothed polynomial. A zero of Z_N is not a zero of L(s,chi). The result supplies no lower bound on |M_chi(N)|.

Deflating the root does not by itself supply a power saving. For principal chi, D1.3 and P_N=N^(1+o(1)) show that, for each fixed gamma and every epsilon>0,

    M_chi(N)=O_(q,epsilon)(N^(gamma+epsilon))
      iff Q_N(-1)=O_(q,epsilon)(N^(gamma-1+epsilon)).   (D1.5)

The elementary bounds P_N>>N/log N and P_N<=N suffice for this every-epsilon equivalence. Thus a bounded Q_N(-1) only gives a near-linear bound. A near gain requires the deflated endpoint to decay faster than N^(-.12514261), in the every-epsilon sense; targets c=1/6 and 1/4 require N^(-1/6+epsilon) and N^(-1/4+epsilon), respectively. This is the precise remaining cancellation, not a proved estimate.

statement:
## 2. D1 / S02: an exact inverse exposes what the boundary must reconstruct

Fix N>=1 and an ordinary character chi modulo q. Let S={a<=N:mu(a)!=0,(a,q)=1}, ordered increasingly and including1. This is divisor closed. Put E_(a,d)=1_(d|a), M=diag(mu(a)). Elementary divisor inversion gives

    E^(-1)=M E M.

Indeed its (a,b) entry in the product is the sum of mu(d/b) over b|d|a, equal to delta_(a,b). Define the coprimality matrix C and its signed version K by

    C_(a,b)=1_((a,b)=1)=sum_(d|a,d|b)mu(d),
    C=E M E^T,             K=M C M=(mu(ab))_(a,b).

Every shared-prime zero is literal. Since E is triangular with unit diagonal, C and K are invertible of full rank |S| and determinant product_(a in S)mu(a). Their real inertia is the number of positive and negative mu(a), by congruence. In particular their signature equals sum_(a in S)mu(a); this is an identity, not an estimate for that sum.

The COMPLETE inverse of K is especially revealing:

    (K^(-1))_(a,b)=sum_(d in S; lcm(a,b)|d)mu(d).          (1)

Proof: invert M E M E^T M and substitute E^(-1)=M E M; the result is E^T M E. Thus (K^(-1))_(1,1) is the full principal-character Mertens sum with precisely the q zeros. This is an actual arithmetic inverse, not an arbitrary-matrix counterexample. At N=2,q=1 it is zero although K is invertible; the nuisance block indexed by a>1 is zero. Therefore eliminating that block by an assumed invertible Schur complement already fails in an actual smallest source.

For a general character the simple phase gauge diag(chi(a)) K diag(chi(a)) does NOT put the twisted Mertens sum in its (1,1) inverse entry: that entry stays the untwisted sum. A different ambient matrix is required. Define

    A_chi=E diag(mu(d)conj(chi(d))) E^T,
    (A_chi)_(a,b)=product_(p|(a,b))(1-conj(chi(p))).

Only unramified squarefree labels occur; hence every diagonal factor inverted has modulus1. Exact inversion gives

    (A_chi^(-1))_(a,b)
      =mu(a)mu(b) sum_(d in S; lcm(a,b)|d)mu(d)chi(d),
    (A_chi^(-1))_(1,1)=M_chi(N):=sum_(n<=N)mu(n)chi(n).   (2)

This twisted matrix has changed local entries: it is not the original coprimality projector when chi(p)!=1. In particular it is generally complex symmetric, not Hermitian. No Hermitian inertia or positivity assertion is made for it.

Here is its quantitative bridge. If for every fixed chi, every epsilon>0 and all sufficiently large dyadic X, one common 0<gamma<1 satisfies

    integral_1^X |(A_(chi,floor t)^(-1))_(1,1)|^2 dt/t
       <<_(chi,epsilon) X^(2gamma+epsilon),              (3)

then ordinary L(s,chi) is zero free in Re(s)>gamma, with the principal pole at1 permitted. By (2) this is exactly the G103 complete Mertens-energy hypothesis. On each dyadic shell Cauchy-Schwarz bounds the integral of |M_chi(t)|t^(-sigma)dt/t by O(X^(gamma-sigma+epsilon)); summing proves locally uniform holomorphy for sigma>gamma, with derivatives. Initially on sigma>1,

    1/L(s,chi)=s integral_1^infinity M_chi(t)t^(-s-1)dt.

Continuation of the product with L gives the conclusion at every finite height. Constants may depend on the fixed character. This includes natural imprimitive zeros; it asserts no growing-conductor estimate. First gain needs gamma<.8748540364; gamma=5/6 and3/4 give the prospective1/6 and1/4 targets. Equation (3) is wholly OPEN and is exactly as difficult as that scalar energy, not a new proof.

Two cautions distinguish exact memory from useful approximation. On m distinct unramified prime labels, K=J_m-I_m, so its rank is m and singular values are m-1,1,...,1 (m>=2). Yet the rank-one approximation J_m has error operator norm1. For arbitrary boundary vectors u,v its omitted scalar is -u^T v, bounded by ||u||_2||v||_2. Thus a large exact state count does NOT rule out a useful paid approximation; the diagonal correction may be inexpensive. This is a genuine escape from an overstated rank obstruction.

On a complete k-prime divisor cube, the unsigned local gate B=[[1,1],[1,0]] has eigenvalues phi and -1/phi, phi=(1+sqrt5)/2. Tensoring gives eigenvalues (-1)^j phi^(k-2j), multiplicity binomial(k,j), all nonzero. The signed gate is T=D B D, D=diag(1,-1), so its singular values agree exactly. This local spectrum was already recorded in W01/W09. The useful addition here is the full divisor-closed inverse (1)-(2), the corrected twisted construction, and the explicit distinction between exact rank and scalar residual cost. No literature priority is claimed; classical divisor inversion and Redheffer-type matrix representations are ancestors. Vaughan's primary paper documents a different determinant representation and does not supply a bound for (3): https://personal.science.psu.edu/rcv4/personal/Publications/REDCONF.pdf .

## 7. The complete problem reduces to one coprime cell

The [coprime reconstruction]([private research revision]/gaussian-coprime-reconstruction.md),
[independent derivation]([private research revision]/gaussian-coprime-independent-review.md)
and [frozen-source comparison]([private research revision]/gaussian-coprime-comparison.md)
give an alternative with every missing comparison paid. Put

    P_Y(x)=sum_(d,e>Y; (d,e)=1; (de,6)=1)
                    mu(d)mu(e)S_tau(x/(de)),
    f_3(n)=mu(rad(n/3^v_3(n))),
    F_6(x)=sum_(n>=1)f_3(n)g_tau(log(n/x)).               (G25)

Here f_3 is multiplicative, takes only the values +1 and -1, and is
not completely multiplicative. Every positive prime power other than
a power of3 contributes one minus sign. This explicitly chosen cell
is not justified by positivity or by an assumed hereditary moment.

Write n_(6)=n/(2^v_2(n)3^v_3(n)). The uncut pair coefficient is
b(n)mu(rad(n_(6)))=f_3(n). In the one-short sum the inner divisor
sum vanishes unless the short divisor is exactly rad(n_(6)). Thus

    P_Y=F_6-2J_Y+I_Y^prim,
    J_Y(x)=sum_n f_3(n)1_(rad(n_(6))<=Y)g_tau(log(n/x)). (G26)

The both-short term I_Y^prim has the same negative-power bound as G8:
the new pair mask is independent of ell. For every fixed delta>0,

    sum_n n^(-delta)/rad(n_(6))
      =prod_(p|6)(1-p^(-delta))^(-1)
       *prod_(p>=5)[1+p^(-1-delta)/(1-p^(-delta))]<infinity.

Together with 1_(rad<=Y)<=Y/rad and the bounded Gaussian exponential
weight, this proves |J_Y(x)|<<_(delta,tau)Y*x^delta. Therefore, on
every real shell X<=x<=2X with its own Y=floor(X^.495),

    |P_Y(x)-F_6(x)| <<_(delta,tau) X^(.495+delta).       (G27)

To recover the whole detector, let k,h be Dirichlet convolution
inverses with Euler factors (z=p^(-s))

    K_p=(1-z)^2,             H_p=(1-z)^(-2),  p=2,3;
    K_p=(1-z)^2/(1-2z),      H_p=(1-2z)/(1-z)^2, p>=5.

The nonconstant factors start at z^2 for p>=5. Since2/sqrt(5)<1,
both sums sum_r |k(r)|r^(-sigma) and sum_r |h(r)|r^(-sigma) converge
for each fixed sigma>1/2. The separate factors at2 and3 are essential.
Direct coefficient identities, including A's original prime-two
coefficients1,-3,2, give

    A=k*f_3,  f_3=h*A,
    G_tau(x)=sum_r k(r)F_6(x/r),
    F_6(x)=sum_r h(r)G_tau(x/r).                         (G28)

These are absolutely justified field identities. For
||V||_sigma=sup_(T>0) T^(-sigma)||V||_(L2([T,2T],dx/x)),
Minkowski gives ||sum c(r)V(./r)||_sigma
<=sum |c(r)|r^(-sigma)||V||_sigma. Both fixed fields have Gaussian
left tails; two neighboring dyadic shells cover every real shell.
Apply this norm theorem to G_tau and F_6, and only then apply G27
on each shell with its own frozen Y. It follows that, for gamma>1/2,

    ||G_tau||_[X,2X] << X^gamma on all large dyadic X
      iff ||F_6||_[X,2X] << X^gamma
      iff ||P_floor(X^.495)||_[X,2X] << X^gamma.          (G29)

The equivalence also holds with an arbitrary epsilon allowance at
gamma=1/2. No exact-power endpoint equivalence there is established.
Convolving a moving-cutoff family with its cutoff held wrong is not
part of this proof.

There is a finite quantitative reconstruction. Fix X_0>=2 and set

    R_X(x)=sum_(r<=X/X_0) k(r)
                      P_floor((X/r)^.495)(x/r).
    ||G_tau-R_X||_[X,2X] <<_epsilon X^(1/2+epsilon).     (G30)

For r<=X/X_0 use G27 and the weighted k norm. For the remaining r,
the fixed F_6 field has bounded t^(-sigma)F_6(t) on0<t<=2X_0;
this pays the whole small-scale tail. Four local product diagonals,
finite caps and height windows transfer by G9--G20 before the outer
r sum. Expanding the resulting scalar retains every r,r' interaction
and both heights, each with its own local window. Under the inherited
beta=.8749 calibration, the complete scalar error in G30 is
O_epsilon(X^(1.3749+epsilon)), including both mixed terms.

The cleanest remaining arithmetic target is therefore

**OPEN-F3:** for a fixed gamma<1-c11=.8748540364, every epsilon>0 and all large
dyadic X, prove

    sum_(m!=n) f_3(m)f_3(n)K_X(m,n)
           <= C_(epsilon,tau,gamma) X^(2gamma+epsilon). (G31)

K_X is exactly G22, now with the full uncut f_3 coefficient family.
Its true diagonal is O_tau(X). Absolute convergence justifies this
complete signed expansion. No absolute value inside the sum, deletion
of negative terms, favorable subfamily selection or random-sign
assumption is allowed. For gamma>=1/2, G31 is equivalent to the
complete moment target and hence supplies the zero-exclusion return.
An optional finite Gaussian window has paid tails, but its coefficient
list is not identical to the primitive pair list in G25.

The general finite-inverse shortcut is ruled out in a precise scope.
For the actual capped W35 coefficient c_X, weighted divisor matrices
L_sigma(c) and physical Gaussian readout W_X satisfy

    ||W_X[L_sigma(A)-L_sigma(c_X)]e_1||_2 << X^(-A_0+o(1)),
    ||W_X[L_sigma(A)-L_sigma(c_X)]||_(ell2->L2)
                      >>_(tau,sigma) X^(sigma+1/2),     (G32)

for fixed sigma>=0. The lower bound uses positive high-index columns
where the actual product cutoff makes c_X vanish. It does not lower
bound the true detector or contradict G29. A restricted arithmetic
operator argument would require its own readout estimate.

## G187. Exact merged structure and why its simpler proposed price fails

The actual two-color squarefree mark is

    eta_(z,w)(n)=product_(p|n)(q_p^(-z)+q_p^(-w)).

It retains independent Mellin/height variables. Forced-slot division can
use Re z=kappa,Re w=-kappa, where every factor has modulus at least
q_p^kappa(1-q_p^(-2kappa))>0. On equal real contours it can vanish.
The cost is divisor bounded times n^kappa at fixed depth; natural character
zeros are not divided out. Coprime extraction is multiplicative, and
algebraic cube inversion works for any whole-index mark, because the
sum over h|c cancels at fixed completed index nc^3.

Extending eta(p^a)=q_p^(-az)+q_p^(-aw) gives a unitary two-color split
of the completed theta index. Its cross coefficient remains

    chi_(A2)(A1)^4=chi_(n2)(n1)^4,
    A_i=n_i b_i^3, (A1,A2)=1.

The actual norm7/norm13 prime example gives the nontrivial phase omega.
Thus the completed system is a coupled coprime theta convolution. PR9's
terminal reflected-energy theorem does not authorize this arbitrary
eta-weighted source. Cube inversion is not the missing analytic gate.

Even granting the unchanged canonical single-inverse exponent
e(L)=(1+5L)/6 at L=r+s would not suffice. Since E_K<=rho+delta v,

    e(r+s)-T>=1/6+(5/6-delta)(r+s)-rho-delta v
             >=1867/27000>.0691.

The endpoint for this lower bound is delta=.7,r+s=2.17,v=.05;
at v=0 the gap is703/6750. This is failure of a proposed upper-bound
price, not a lower bound on R4. Extending only the coefficient contract
would leave the quantitative problem open.

For completeness, on absolute lines the original coprime signed product
has Euler factors1-X_p-Y_p, with X_p=phi_u(p)q_p^(-s1),Y_p=phi_u(p)q_p^(-s2).
It equals [L_u(s1)L_u(s2)]^(-1) times the correction with local factor
1-X_pY_p/[(1-X_p)(1-Y_p)]. Its coefficient at positive exponents a,b
is -phi_u(p)^(a+b), with zero at just one positive exponent. The
correction is absolutely convergent when both real parts remain positive
and their sum exceeds one. It supplies no fourth moment or zero crossing.

statement:
## 2. W9-W17: accept the complete merged-state localization

Fix an ordinary Dirichlet character chi modulo q, retaining every nonunit zero, and let a(n)=mu(n)chi(n). Let P^-(1)=infinity and P^+(1)=1. At integer states,

    R(m,p)=sum_(n<=m,P^-(n)>p)a(n),
    R(m,p)=1-sum_(p<ell<=m,ell prime)chi(ell)R(floor(m/ell),ell).

Each squarefree integer has a unique least prime and a strictly larger-prime cofactor. The increasing path ordering excludes repetitions. For any F on the entire reachable state system,

    Delta(m,p)=F(m,p)-1+sum_(p<ell<=m)chi(ell)F(floor(m/ell),ell).

Subtract the equations and finitely back-substitute. Every path corresponds to one squarefree d with sign mu(d)chi(d); composed floors equal floor(N/d). Writing d=pu with p=P^+(d) gives the literal merged coefficient

    C_N(m,p)=-chi(p)
       sum_(N/[p(m+1)]<u<=N/(pm),P^+(u)<p)mu(u)chi(u).       (C1)

The lower endpoint is strict and the upper weak. No extra coprimality mask or independent path phase is inserted. The source is ordinary mu, not the distinct all-power f3. Root d=1 contributes Delta(N,1), never an assumed vanishing term.

For fixed INTEGER r>=1, the exact collar m<=p^r is descendant-closed. A child m'=floor(m/ell)<=m<=p^r<ell^r. If F=R there then Delta=0 there. For r>1 the collar includes nontrivial prime contributions and cannot be replaced by1. This leaves the exact G92 formula

    F(N,1)-M_chi(N)=Delta(N,1)+sum_(p,m>p^r)C_N(m,p)Delta(m,p).
                                                               (C2)

This recurrence and merging are inherited, not new W52 credit.

### Singleton proof and all-depth count

If distinct u<v lie in the SAME integer interval(C1), then

    m v<=N/p<(m+1)u,  so m(v-u)<u.

Since v-u>=1, u>m. Consequently any fiber containing a cofactor<=m is a singleton even before smoothness, squarefreeness or character masks. This applies whichever member is smallest. No short/long mixture can occur. A ramified value may make the singleton coefficient zero, but never creates an additional nonzero path.

For a short active path d=pu with u<=m=floor(N/d) and m>p^r,

    p u^2<=N,       p^(r+1)u<N.

Thus, dropping arithmetic restrictions only in this positive count,

    S_r(N)<=sum_(j>=2)min((N/j)^(1/2),N/j^(r+1))
          <=(4+1/r)N^alpha_r,  alpha_r=(r+1)/(2r+1).           (C3)

Split at J=ceil(N^(1/(2r+1))). The initial part is at most2sqrt(NJ)<=2sqrt(2)N^alpha_r; the tail is at most N/(rJ^r)<=N^alpha_r/r. The stated larger constant works for every N>=1. Integer counts may be rounded down; the real upper envelopes remain valid. For q-units every singleton has absolute coefficient1, so S_r is its exact coefficient mass. The whole short contribution is at most D_N S_r when D_N bounds ALL active prime-state defects.

This is an ALL-depth price. It is not the old fixed-depth x^(k/(k+r)) estimate, and no unmerged exponent-one lower bound survives this grouping. It also does not estimate cancellation among the remaining merged coefficients.

### Small primes and hard region

Freeze Y_N=(log(2N))^A at the ROOT, A>1. After removing the singleton class, each path in p<=Y_N has squarefree d<=N and largest prime<=Y_N. Triangle only on this paid complement yields mass at most

    Psi_sf(N,Y_N)<=N^sigma product_(p<=Y_N)(1+p^-sigma)
                 <=N^sigma exp(1+Y_N^(1-sigma)/(1-sigma)).     (C4)

For any fixed0<sigma<1, log(1+t)<=t and comparison with the integer integral prove the bound. Given epsilon, choose sigma just above1-1/A, strictly below both1 and1-1/A+epsilon/2. Then A(1-sigma)<1 and the exponential is N^o(1). Hence Psi_sf<<_(A,epsilon)N^(1-1/A+epsilon). Constants and onset can be large; no practical finite-N savings are inferred from this asymptotic.

Every remaining fiber contains only u>m>p^r. From N>=pum>pm^2>p^(2r+1),

    Y_N<p<N^(1/(2r+1)),    p^r<m<sqrt(N/p),    u>m.           (C5)

Its squarefree u has all primes<p; if omega(u)<=r its product would be<p^r, a contradiction. Thus omega(u)>=r+1 and omega(d)>=r+2. Large primes p>=N^(1/(2r+1)) are already paid by(C3), not discarded.

Let H_F be the ENTIRE signed sum(C1)Delta over this remaining set. Empty/zero coefficients remain zero. Then

### 3.1 The known absolute-norm failure

For any nonzero fixed finite Dirichlet polynomial M with least nonzero
coefficient m(d0), let r=delta-l_chi*m, where l_chi(n)=chi(n). If p exceeds
the support of m and p does not divide q, the only supported nonzero
divisor contribution to r(d0 p) is d0. Hence

    r(d0 p)=-m(d0)chi(p).

The absolute weighted residual norm diverges for sigma<=1. Indeed the
prime harmonic series diverges: if sum_p 1/p converged, the products
product_(p<=P)(1-1/p)^-1 would be bounded, although their positive
expansions eventually contain every finite harmonic partial sum. Removing
finitely many primes does not fix divergence, and p^-sigma>=p^-1 for
sigma<=1. This is the established W29 obstruction, now read in its exact
scope. It does not lower-bound a signed Gaussian output or prohibit
an algebra at a different exponent.

    d=sum_p w_p c_p, D=Pi d Pi, B=(I-Pi)d Pi, E=B^*B.

The exact relations, proved in `fock-boundary.md`, are

    D^2=0, D^*D+DD^*=W Pi-E, 0<=E<=W Pi.             (A)

If p_* is the least ACTIVE prime, meaning w_(p_*)!=0 and all smaller weights vanish, then

    multiplicity of the eigenvalue W of E
      = #{n<=N:mu^2(n)=1,(n,q)=1,p_* not|n,n>N/p_*}. (B)

This is exact for every choice of the other weights, and allows p_*>N. The proof uses the actual divisor-closed cutoff. Its upper p_*-free states form a subcomplex U killed by D; the quotient pairs lower p_*-free states with their p_*-multiples and contracts by w_(p_*)^-1 c_(p_*)^*. Thus H(D)=U as graded vector spaces. Finite Hodge decomposition and (A) identify U's dimension with the W eigenspace. This does not identify arithmetic signs with positive spectral mass.

Let kappa_q=prod_(p|q)(1-1/p)prod_(p not|q)(1-1/p^2). Elementary square-divisor counting, with a finite-small-prime/large-prime split, gives for fixed q and all sufficiently large N, UNIFORMLY over every active prime and moving set of weights,

    (kappa_q/8) WN <= Tr(E) <= WN,
    multiplicity_W(E) >= (kappa_q/8)N.               (C)

Consequently ||E||=W at those scales. An upper bound that first discards all grading and uses only Tr(E) cannot produce a sublinear Mertens exponent. Nor can a proposed ambient spectral gap E<=(1-delta)W Pi hold. These are obstructions to those sufficient methods, **not lower bounds on the actual signed source, Gaussian moment or native H form**.

The complete arithmetic response remains

    W M_chi(N)=Str(T_chi E)+Str([T_chi,D^*]D),        (D)

where T_chi e_S=chi(n_S)e_S and the grading is (-1)^|S|. Equivalently its p-th summand is |w_p|^2 times

    sum_(N/p<n<=N,p not|n)mu(n)chi(n)
      +(1-chi(p))sum_(n<=N/p,p not|n)mu(n)chi(n).     (E)

Every bracket is exactly M_chi(N). The second term vanishes for principal characters, but not generally. Supporting weights only on chi(p)=1 is legitimate and kills the bulk; (C) still holds. Simply inserting chi(p) in d is unitary conjugation by T_chi and leaves all singular values unchanged. A character-sensitive estimate must retain the observable in (D).

The source can also be encoded by the single prescribed product

    (I-chi(p_1)c_(p_1))...(I-chi(p_r)c_(p_r)) e_empty,

with the largest index acting first. This is a VALID bare-fermion encoding. Uniformly averaging all orderings instead removes every degree>=2 source coefficient. Restoring their parity signs restores the identical original vector, so that order average supplies no free cancellation. The missing complete composite readout and boundary overlaps remain paid terms. A failed common gauge does not refute the valid fixed-order representation.

For q=1, p_*=2 the critical count is classical; [Bjorner, Theorem3.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1101.5704) verifies the squarefree-complex ancestor. The occupation-sign/CAR conventions are verified against [Bravyi--Kitaev, Eqs.(1)--(2)](https://arxiv.org/pdf/quant-ph/0003137). In this record [restricted research revision]/G79, [restricted research revision]/G118, [restricted research revision]/G135, and especially [restricted research revision]/G144--145 already own exterior, parity-layer, cone, gauge and composite-readout cores. ### 3.1 Actual coefficients, powers, masks and absolute convergence

Fix tau>0 and one ordinary chi modulo q, with natural chi(n)=0 on nonunits. Define f(n)=mu(rad(n/3^v3(n))) and F_chi(x)=sum f(n)chi(n)g_tau(log(n/x)). For P subset of primes>=5 not dividing q, write n=rv with r its complete P-smooth part. This is a unique decomposition, including repeated prime powers, n=1 and nonunit v. Therefore f(n)chi(n)=a_P(r)f(v)chi(v), and the coefficient convolution a_P*f_P equals the sequence n -> f(n)chi(n). The exact field identity is

    F_chi(x)=sum_(r P-smooth) a_P(r)V_P(x/r).

At p in P, a_P(p^j)=-chi(p)^j for EVERY j>=1. Its local series is (1-2chi(p)z)/(1-chi(p)z); replacing it with1-chi(p)z would change the actual source. Since chi(p) has modulus1 on P, sum |a_P(r)|r^-sigma equals product(1-p^-sigma)^-1 exactly. Prime3 is never removed; prime2 remains in the source; q-divisor terms keep their literal zero extension. There is no squarefree surrogate, free gcd restriction or altered character scope.

Absolute field rearrangement can be proved without assuming OPEN-D04: choose a weight s0>1, use the bounded t^-s0 positive Gaussian integer field on all t>0, and sum |a_P(r)|r^-s0. This handles even t=x/r tending to0 and gives local uniform convergence. For a fixed parent X, P is finite. Infinite powers do not require a finite compact-support argument. The later norm decomposition splits that very same exact identity.
