statement:
## G215. Exact source, complete localization and all-height return

Fix an ordinary Dirichlet character chi modulo its PRESENTED modulus q,
including every natural nonunit zero. Let chi(-1)=(-1)^a and fix r>=2
with r congruent to a modulo2. The choices r=2 for even chi and r=3 for
odd chi suffice. All q,chi,r and the filter order below are fixed before
the scale, target height and implied constants. There is no growing-q,
growing-r or Hecke-family assertion.

Define the Jordan coefficient and Laplace source by

    J_r(n)=sum_(d|n) mu(d)(n/d)^r
          =n^r product_(p|n)(1-p^(-r)),
    F(X)=sum_(n>=1) chi(n)J_r(n) exp(-n/X).          (1)

Inclusion-exclusion counts primitive r-tuples modulo n and proves the
coefficient formula. Squareful values are deliberate: this source does
not claim to retain squarefree Möbius support. Absolute convolution
gives L(s-r,chi)/L(s,chi) on Re s>r+1, with all inducing factors.

Put m_q=phi(q)/q for principal chi and0 otherwise,
A=m_q r!/L(r+1,chi), and E(X)=F(X)-A X^(r+1). The Euler product
defines the reciprocal at r+1 without an unproved strip assumption.
For t>0 set

    H(t)=sum_(n>=1)chi(n)e^(-nt)
        =[sum_(v=1)^q chi(v)e^(-vt)]/[1-e^(-qt)],
    f(t)=(-d/dt)^r H(t),
    g(t)=f(t)-m_q r! t^(-r-1).

Absolute convergence of the original double series and of the
subtracted reciprocal series at r+1 proves the COMPLETE identity

    E(X)=sum_(d>=1) mu(d)chi(d)g(d/X).               (2)

The principal main coefficient is for the presented modulus, not its
primitive conductor. No finite Euler correction is suppressed.

For q>1 residue reflection gives H(-t)=-chi(-1)H(t).
For q=1 the extra constant is -1, removed by r differentiations.
The parity choice makes the regular part of f odd; its possible
principal pole is odd too. Thus g(t)=O(t), g'(t)=O(1) at zero.
At infinity f,f'=O(e^(-t)); principal g retains exactly the algebraic
tail -m_q r!t^(-r-1). Consequently

    |g(t)| <= C min(t,t^(-r-1)),  E(X)=O(X), X>=1.   (3)

The actual complete low/high absolute prices, for alpha<1<beta, are
O(X^(2alpha-1)) and O(X^(r+1-r beta)) at d<=X^alpha and d>X^beta.
For gamma in(0,1), alpha=(1+gamma)/2 and beta=1+(1-gamma)/r
pay both at X^gamma. The middle is still signed and unpaid.

Now fix b=2 and m>=0, put T h(t)=h(2t), D G(X)=G(X/2), and

    P_m(T)=product_(j=0)^(m-1)(I-2^(-(2j+1))T),
    B_r(T)=I-2^(r+1)T,
    K(t)=P_m(T)B_r(T)g(t)=P_m(T)B_r(T)f(t),
    Phi(X)=P_m(D)B_r(D)E(X)=P_m(D)B_r(D)F(X).

The empty product is identity. The B_r factor kills the principal
algebraic tail and the main term exactly. P_m removes the first m
odd Taylor powers. Therefore

    Phi(X)=sum_(d>=1) mu(d)chi(d)K(d/X),             (4)
    K(t)=O(t^(2m+1)), K'(t)=O(t^(2m)) as t->0,
    K(t)=e^(-t)+O(e^(-2t)),
    K'(t)=-e^(-t)+O(e^(-2t)) as t->infinity.         (5)

The coefficient of the slowest exponential is chi(1)1^r=1, since
every other dilation has argument at least2t. This also proves K
is nonzero. Equation (4) keeps exactly the original outer mu(d)chi(d).
Even when2 divides q, these are literal scale dilations: no chi(2)
is factored out, and the expanded output coefficients are not falsely
assigned the old support. Phi can be evaluated from F without knowing A.
It is O(X) at infinity and O(e^(-1/X)) at zero.

For any fixed gamma in(0,1), set

    alpha=1-(1-gamma)/(2m+2),
    Cmid(x)=sum_(x^alpha<d<=2x log x)mu(d)chi(d)K(d/x).

For every sufficiently large real x, the three disjoint ranges
d<=x^alpha, x^alpha<d<=2x log x, d>2x log x cover all divisors.
The first absolute price is
x^(-(2m+1)) sum_(d<=x^alpha)d^(2m+1)=O(x^gamma).
The last is O(sum_(d>2x log x)e^(-d/x))=O(x^-1).
Rounding the real cut changes only a fixed constant. Thus

    Phi(x)=Cmid(x)+O(x^gamma).                       (6)

The cuts decompose ONE fixed source; they do not create a different
Mellin profile at each x. The weakest return used here is the complete
dyadic-shell L1 hypothesis

    integral_X^(2X)|Cmid(x)| dx/x
       <<_(chi,r,m,epsilon) X^(gamma+epsilon)       (7)

for every epsilon>0 and all sufficiently large dyadic X, at one common
gamma across every fixed ordinary chi. A full shell L2 bound implies
(7); no favorable signed subset is substituted for the whole norm.
For m=1 the paid lower exponents are .9687135091 at gamma11,
.9687 at gamma=.8748,23/24 at gamma=5/6, and15/16 at gamma=3/4.
The full upper cutoff is2x log x in every case. These are explicit
complement budgets, not estimates of Cmid.

To establish the all-height return, ordinary functional equations,
trivial-zero parity and exact inducing factors give

    L(s-r,chi) !=0 for 0<Re s<=1.                   (8)

Indeed -r<Re(s-r)<=1-r lies between consecutive parity trivial zeros,
and the extra finite factors have zeros only on Re(s-r)=0.
The q=1 zeta case is treated separately at its negative even zeros.
These standard inputs are recorded in [DLMF25.15](https://dlmf.nist.gov/25.15)
and [DLMF25.10](https://dlmf.nist.gov/25.10); the source reflection above
is derived directly.

On Re s>r+1, finite scaling in the absolutely convergent transform gives

    Mellin(Phi)(s)=Gamma(s)Q_mr(s)L(s-r,chi)/L(s,chi),
    Q_mr(s)=(1-2^(r+1-s))
             product_(j=0)^(m-1)(1-2^(-(s+2j+1))).  (9)

Here Mellin(Phi)=integral_0^infinity Phi(X)X^(-s)dX/X.
The first factor cancels the actual principal numerator pole at r+1;
its zeros lie on Re s=r+1. The other zeros lie on negative odd
real-part lines. Hence Q_mr is nonzero in the entire target strip,
including Re s=1. Gamma(s) has no pole or zero there.

The unconditional O(X) and small-X exponential bounds make the full
integral holomorphic for Re s>1. Under (7), equation (6) supplies the
same shell L1 bound for Phi. Sum dyadic integrals on each compact subset
of Re s>gamma, choosing epsilon below its distance to gamma. Derivatives
only insert logarithmic powers. The small-X contribution is entire.
Continuation therefore preserves

    L(s,chi) Mellin(Phi)(s)
        =Gamma(s)Q_mr(s)L(s-r,chi), Re s>gamma.      (10)

A hypothetical zero in gamma<Re s<=1 contradicts (8)–(10); the Euler
product covers Re s>1. The principal pole at1 is allowed and has the
compensating transform zero. Normal convergence on every compact
handles every finite height without assuming a uniform height bound
or that a bare zero-free strip implies a sharp Mertens estimate.

The arithmetic hypothesis (7) remains OPEN. A common gamma<gamma11
would beat the conditional numerical benchmark in the ordinary-family
scope. Targets c=.1252,1/6,1/4 mean gamma=.8748,5/6,3/4 respectively.
No ordinary-to-Hecke or original-Gaussian source transfer is inferred.

## R3. Literal coefficients, all zeros and the Type I theorem

To avoid the author's overloaded a, write alpha(n)=mu(n)chi(n), and use a only for the real weight, 0<a<1. An ordinary Dirichlet character is extended by zero at nonunits. It is completely multiplicative even there. Hence

    (alpha*chi)(n)=chi(n)sum_(d|n)mu(d)=delta_1(n).

For alpha0=alpha 1_(n<=Y) and alpha1=alpha-alpha0, convolution in the full sequence ring gives

    alpha=2alpha0-alpha0*alpha0*chi+alpha1*alpha1*chi. (R2)

Both ordered factors and all shared primes are present. This is not a coprime convolution. Individual pieces may fail to vanish at squareful n; their complete signed recombination restores alpha's squareful and ramified zeros. The n=1 term is retained. The identity holds for real cutoffs through their floor, and in particular for integer Y as used here.

For a restoration sequence b with partial sum B(y), zero for y<1 and bounded in modulus by C_b, extend

    h_b(v)=e^(-av)B(e^v)1_(v>=0).

Then ||h_b||_1<=C_b/a. For each k>=1,

    e^[-a(t+u)]B(e^(t+u)/k)
       =k^(-a)h_b(t+u-log k).                       (R3)

Reflect an input g on (0,L) into (-L,0), zero-extend it to the real line, and convolve with the translated h_b. Restriction back to (0,L) has norm at most one. Young's L1--L2 bound therefore proves that the full square operator in (R3) has norm at most C_b k^(-a)/a. Translation costs no norm, and no differentiability of g or endpoint trace is required. This argument includes every rectangle of the original square.

Triangle over d,e<=Y now gives

    ||Gamma[alpha0*alpha0*b]_(a,L)||
       <=(C_b/a)(sum_(d<=Y)|alpha(d)|d^(-a))^2
       <<_(a,b)Y^[2(1-a)].                           (R4)

Cancellation in B is used before the absolute sum over d,e. Replacing b by |b| would destroy the uniform C_b and would not prove (R4). An atom z(n) gives L1 mass |z(n)|n^(-a)/a, so its finite sum costs that weighted atomic mass.

For every nonprincipal chi modulo q, including imprimitive ones, the complete period sum is zero and |sum_(n<=y)chi(n)|<=q. Apply (R4) to b=chi and the atom bound to 2alpha0 in (R2). This proves H4 for the original alpha source, with a constant depending on a,q, uniformly in L and Y. No long-factor cancellation was assumed.

The principal exception is real. At Y=1 the removed sequence is 2delta_1-chi. For principal chi its partial sum is `-(phi(q)/q)x+O_q(1)`, and its integrated kernel has the rank-one part `-(phi(q)/q)e^[(1-a)(t+u)]`. The bounded partial-sum remainder has bounded operator norm by (R3). Reverse triangle gives exactly the author's exponential norm asymptotic, including O_(a,q)(1). This term cannot receive a gamma<1 budget in isolation. It is not a lower bound for the complete signed source.

# [private research revision] upstream lane: an arithmetic Hankel determinant with a paid return

Status: mathematical draft for independent review; no increase in the zero-free constant is proved. Accepted written analytic benchmark: Gao's c_G=.1251134, with the new endpoint/kernel replay still pending. The old c0=.125113352960035869... has its separate three-kernel receipt. This packet neither changes those statuses nor uses an open Gaussian estimate as an accepted premise.



## Current checkpoint

- Objective: turn a genuinely open upstream component into an actual coefficient-exact zero detector, challenge its strongest cheap obstruction, and leave one exact quantitative arithmetic target.
- Selected component: W36-02/R36.10's parked adjugate-residue determinant. That source proves only the general residue identity, leaving the correlated arithmetic matrix, nonvanishing and nonlinear readout unpaid.
- Completed: an explicit reciprocal Hankel matrix; its Vandermonde coefficients and prime-power cancellations; a decisive actual-coefficient obstruction to an absolute-value gain; a parameter-averaged signed variant with a complete all-height zero-exclusion theorem; an unconditional median-factor tail at exponent .874; finite Gaussian caps, every signed Gram term, and a first-gain target; and a separate fixed-shift anchor whose normalized cofactor inverse has norm at most 20 on a weighted dilation space.
- Not proved: the complete signed D3 moment, any improvement beyond c_G, superiority over OPEN-GC/OPEN-F3, or formal-kernel certification.
- Evidence: the proofs below; check_exact.py and exact-receipt.json provide finite exact arithmetic and a rational bound only.
- Next mathematical action: independently review the averaged pole bridge and then estimate the complete signed finite scalar (D20), with the coalesced Liouville signs and all short-pair interactions retained.

## 1. Choice, history, and what is actually new here

Read: [restricted mathematical source] with the supplied c_G correction; [restricted mathematical source] [restricted mathematical source] and its early, late and [private research revision] detail; W01's fixed-arity construction; W35's Gaussian completion; W36 R36.10; and the [private research revision] discovery's multiplicative-Hankel/wrong-readout comparison.

An initial higher-arity completion idea was stopped after finding the stronger W01-A fixed-arity detector/recovery construction. It is not counted as a new result. The present finite 3-by-3 determinant is also not a claim that every operator called Hankel is new. It has a different, fully stated readout from the bounded multiplicative-Hankel operator previously rejected for using the wrong coefficient functional.

The incremental content over W36 R36.24 is concrete: the matrix consists of actual reciprocal-L translates; its coefficients are derived before norms; the pole cofactor is shown nontrivial as an analytic shift family; averaging in the fixed shift parameter solves the otherwise unpaid exceptional-cofactor problem; the changed arithmetic field is finite up to paid errors; and one strong fixed shift has a quantitative, absolutely convergent inverse. No trace regularization, omitted prime compensator, determinant positivity, or model consensus enters.

This uses ordinary Cauchy--Binet, Dirichlet convolution and elementary complex analysis. No literature-priority claim is made. No external mathematical theorem beyond the standard Dirichlet-series/Euler-product framework is imported.

## 2. The actual matrix and its coefficients

Let chi be any ordinary Dirichlet character, with its original natural zeros. Zeta is the character of modulus one. Put

    F_chi(s)=1/L(s,chi),
    a_chi(n)=mu(n)chi(n),
    I=[1/5,1/4],
    D_chi,delta(s)=det [F_chi(s+(i+j)delta)]_(0<=i,j<=2).       (D1)

Initially Re s>1 and delta>0 are real. All relevant Dirichlet series converge absolutely. Write

    V_delta(a,b,c)
      =(a^(-delta)-b^(-delta))
       (a^(-delta)-c^(-delta))
       (b^(-delta)-c^(-delta)).                              (D2)

The matrix in D1 is the sum over n of the rank-one matrices

    a_chi(n)n^(-s) v_n v_n^T,
    v_n=(1,n^(-delta),n^(-2delta))^T.

Finite Cauchy--Binet, followed by absolute convergence, gives

    D_chi,delta(s)=sum_(a<b<c)
      mu(a)mu(b)mu(c)chi(abc) V_delta(a,b,c)^2 (abc)^(-s)
      =sum_n h_chi,delta(n)n^(-s).                          (D3)

There is no conjugation in this analytic determinant. Conjugation is introduced only in the eventual physical energy. The factors are ordered by their integer sizes, and the strict inequalities a<b<c are part of the coefficient definition. Shared primes are allowed. Squareful individual factors have their actual zero Mobius coefficients. No coprimality or squarefree-output condition has been inserted.

Let lambda(n)=(-1)^Omega(n). For every nonzero tuple, including shared primes,

    mu(a)mu(b)mu(c)=lambda(abc).

Consequently the coalesced coefficients have the useful exact form

    h_chi,delta(n)=chi(n)lambda(n) W_delta(n),
    W_delta(n)=sum_(a<b<c; abc=n; a,b,c squarefree)
                         V_delta(a,b,c)^2 >=0.             (D4)

This is a coefficient-aware simplification, not an independence assumption: the whole sign is Liouville parity of the output, and different outputs still interact. For all delta>0, |h_chi,delta(n)|<=d_3(n); that majorant is uniform on I.

Every prime-power output is zero. Indeed if n=p^k, the only possible nonzero squarefree factors are 1 and p, so three distinct factors do not exist. At a product of two distinct primes there is exactly the tuple (1,p,q):

    h_delta(pq)
      =(1-p^(-delta))^2(1-q^(-delta))^2
                             (p^(-delta)-q^(-delta))^2.    (D5)

Here and below omission of chi means zeta. In particular, for odd primes p,

    h_delta(2p)
      =(1-2^(-delta))^2(1-p^(-delta))^2
                             (2^(-delta)-p^(-delta))^2.

It tends to (1-2^(-delta))^2 2^(-2delta)>0 uniformly for delta in I.

## 3. Cheap decisive objection, and the surviving variant

The attractive initial thought was that a rank-three determinant removes the dense prime output and might therefore permit a crude absolute estimate. D5 decisively rejects that inference for the actual coefficients. The 2p channel has weights bounded below by a positive constant for all sufficiently large p, uniformly on I.

More precisely, for any sigma<=1,

    sum_n |h_delta(n)| n^(-sigma)=infinity                 (D6)

because its 2p subseries dominates a fixed positive multiple of sum_p p^(-sigma). Euler's divergence of sum_p 1/p suffices. Thus the absolute Gaussian field cannot satisfy an all-dyad power bound X^gamma with gamma<1: positive Mellin Fubini would then make D6 finite at some gamma<sigma<1. The same obstruction applies to the positive 2p field alone. This is an actual arithmetic obstruction, not an arbitrary-sign toy or a lower bound for the complete signed determinant field.

The viable variant keeps the whole signed field and averages its energy in a fixed real shift interval. That averaging has a precise purpose: a single cofactor can vanish at a hypothetical zero, while the analytic cofactor family cannot vanish identically. It does not assert random signs, a negative average energy, or cancellation among representations of the same squarefree output. The latter representations actually have the same sign by D4.

## 4. An explicit cofactor and its nontriviality

Expanding D1 at its upper-left entry gives exactly

    D_delta(s)=C_delta(s)F(s)+E_delta(s),
    C_delta(s)=F(s+2delta)F(s+4delta)-F(s+3delta)^2,
    E_delta(s)=-F(s+delta)^2F(s+4delta)
                +2F(s+delta)F(s+2delta)F(s+3delta)
                -F(s+2delta)^3.                           (D7)

The chi subscript is understood throughout D7. Every sign and all three complementary terms are retained. This is a determinant of Mellin-side reciprocal entries, not the determinant of three physical Gaussian fields.

For a point rho with Re rho>4/5 and delta in I, all shifted entries in C_delta and E_delta lie in Re s>1. They are therefore holomorphic at rho. The coefficient of any pole of F at rho is exactly C_delta(rho), with the same pole order whenever that coefficient is nonzero.

There is a second Cauchy--Binet formula:

    C_delta(s)=sum_(m<n) mu(m)mu(n)chi(mn)
       (mn)^(-s-2delta)(m^(-delta)-n^(-delta))^2.           (D8)

Let p be the least prime not dividing the specified modulus of the ordinary character (equivalently the least integer n>1 with a_chi(n) nonzero). Along real delta tending to infinity, the unique first term is

    -chi(p)p^(-rho-2delta)(1-p^(-delta))^2.

The ratio of the remaining absolute sum to its magnitude tends to zero. For the m=1 terms use the tail sum over n>=p+1, whose ratio is bounded by a constant times

    (p/(p+1))^(2delta) [1+(p+1)/(Re rho+2delta-1)].

For m>=p, use (m^(-delta)-n^(-delta))^2<=m^(-2delta) and sum

    sum_(m>=p) m^(-Re rho-4delta)
               sum_(n>m) n^(-Re rho-2delta).

After division by p^(-Re rho-2delta), this also tends to zero by an integral comparison. Constants here may depend on the fixed p and rho; no quantitative height assertion is extracted from this asymptotic.

Thus delta -> C_delta(rho) is a nonzero analytic function on the connected half-plane in delta where all its displayed reciprocal arguments have real part >1. It has only isolated real zeros in I. This proves the exact nonvanishing property needed below. We do not assume a uniform lower bound for |C_delta(rho)| on I.

For an imprimitive character, p means the least prime not dividing the specified modulus, so its natural Euler zeros are respected. The distinction from a primitive conductor does not change the argument; the coefficient definition a_chi is authoritative.

## 5. A complete averaged zero-exclusion theorem

Fix tau>0 once, independently of X, and set

    g_tau(v)=(2*pi*tau)^(-1/2) exp(-v^2/(2tau)),
    H_chi,delta(x)=sum_n h_chi,delta(n)g_tau(log(n/x)).    (D9)

The series, and each fixed x-derivative, converge locally uniformly. The uniform d_3 majorant gives a Gaussian left tail as x tends to zero. Absolute Mellin Fubini on Re s>1 yields

    integral_0^infinity H_chi,delta(x)x^(-s) dx/x
          =exp(tau*s^2/2)D_chi,delta(s).                 (D10)

**Theorem D3.** Fix 4/5<gamma<1. Suppose for an ordinary chi, every epsilon>0 and all sufficiently large dyadic X,

    integral_I integral_X^(2X) |H_chi,delta(x)|^2 dx/x ddelta
                  <<_(chi,epsilon,tau) X^(2gamma+epsilon). (D11)

Then L(s,chi) has no zero in Re s>gamma. Its principal pole at one is not asserted to be a zero. If D11 holds for every ordinary chi at the same gamma, this gives the common zero-free constant c=1-gamma, with constants permitted to depend on chi.

Proof, including the exceptional parameter issue: choose a rational sigma_0>gamma and epsilon<2(sigma_0-gamma). Summing the weighted dyadic inequalities in D11 gives

    integral_I integral_1^infinity
       |H_chi,delta(x)|^2 x^(-2sigma_0) dx/x ddelta <infinity.

Tonelli implies that for almost every fixed delta this weighted square integral is finite. Cauchy--Schwarz then makes its Mellin integral holomorphic on Re s>sigma_0; logarithmic derivatives follow on compact sub-half-planes. Intersect over a countable sequence sigma_0 decreasing to gamma. The common Gaussian left tail completes holomorphy on Re s>gamma for almost every fixed delta in I.

For each hypothetical zero rho in that half-plane, D8 shows that the bad set {delta in I:C_delta(rho)=0} has measure zero. The zeros of a nonzero meromorphic L-function form a countable set. Remove the union of these bad sets, and the null set from the preceding Fubini step. At any remaining delta, all shifted entries in D7 are holomorphic throughout Re s>gamma (because gamma+1/5>1), and the cofactor is nonzero at every hypothetical zero there. A zero of multiplicity m would therefore give a pole of order m in D_delta, contradicting D10 and the holomorphic Mellin integral. The exponential multiplier never vanishes.

There is no finite-height cutoff in this proof, no selection of delta depending on X, no assertion that an average bound holds pointwise for every delta, and no missing residue from the principal pole: 1/L is holomorphic there. A fixed full-measure set of parameters is used after the all-scale summation. Countably many ordinary characters can also be intersected if desired; this does not require a conductor-uniform norm constant.

## 6. The complementary analytic term is really small

Although D11 is stated directly for the determinant field, D7 helps calibrate what is and is not gained. Write e_chi,delta for the Dirichlet coefficients of E_delta. For delta in I,

    |e_chi,delta(n)| <=4 d_3(n)n^(-delta),
    sum_n |e_chi,delta(n)| n^(-4/5-epsilon)
                                      <=4 zeta(1+epsilon)^3. (D12)

Each product in E has three factors, the least of its shifts is at least delta, and |mu chi|<=1; this proves the first bound, including its multiplicity 1+2+1. Since delta>=1/5, it proves the second uniformly. Therefore its Gaussian physical field obeys

    |E_chi,delta^g(x)| <<_(epsilon,tau) x^(4/5+epsilon)   (D13)

on all positive x after adjusting a fixed constant; the left tail is better. This uses g_tau(v)<=C_(tau,sigma) exp(-sigma v), with sigma=4/5+epsilon, and the D12 weighted coefficient norm. All three signed complementary fields are paid together, not deleted singly by an unproved cancellation.

The cofactor coefficients are absolutely summable with weight r^(-beta), uniformly for delta in I, whenever beta>3/5. D8 and its majorant prove this because beta+2delta>1. Thus the inherited Mertens calibration beta=.8749 gives

    H_chi,delta(x) <<_(chi,epsilon,tau) x^(beta+epsilon)  (D14)

if the corresponding accepted character Mertens bound is supplied. For zeta the current proof supplies that calibration explicitly. D14 is a comparison, not an improvement. The limiting accepted exponent is beta_0=1-c_G=.8748866 with any fixed positive buffer. The required arithmetic gain below remains genuine.

## 7. A new unconditional paid sector: large median factors

For a<b<c and delta>0,

    0<=V_delta(a,b,c)^2 <= a^(-4delta)b^(-2delta).       (D15)

This inequality is useful before summing coefficients. There is a finite constant K_tau such that, for every y>0,

    sum_(n>=1) g_tau(log(n/y)) <=K_tau y.

One elementary proof partitions log(n/y) into intervals [j,j+1), uses at most exp(j+1)y integers in each interval, and sums exp(j+1) times the supremum of the Gaussian on that interval. The resulting bilateral series converges, uniformly in y.

The same ordered-factor inequality also gives the stronger-than-divisor absolute mass bound

    sum_(n<=t)|h_chi,delta(n)|
       <=t zeta(1+4delta)zeta(1+2delta)
       <=t zeta(9/5)zeta(7/5),                           (D15a)

uniformly on I: sum the last factor by floor(t/(ab)) and enlarge the two remaining ranges. This is compatible with the absolute obstruction D6; it supplies no exponent below one.

Let Y be a positive integer. The complete original-tuple sector b>Y consequently satisfies, uniformly for x>0, chi, and delta in I,

    sum_(a<b<c; b>Y)
      |mu(a)mu(b)mu(c)chi(abc)| V_delta(a,b,c)^2
                                  g_tau(log(abc/x))
       <= K_tau x sum_a a^(-1-4delta)
                         sum_(b>Y) b^(-1-2delta)
       <=(5/2)K_tau zeta(9/5) x Y^(-2/5).               (D16)

Here 1+4delta>=9/5, 2delta>=2/5, and the b tail is at most Y^(-2delta)/(2delta)<=(5/2)Y^(-2/5). The c>b restriction was enlarged only at this absolute upper-bound step. Natural character zeros, shared primes and all actual tuple signs are otherwise retained.

Take

    Y_X=floor(X^(63/200))=floor(X^.315).

For X large enough that Y_X>=X^.315/2, D16 proves

    sup_(delta in I) ||H_chi,delta-H_chi,delta; b<=Y_X||_[X,2X]
                   <<_tau X^(437/500)=X^.874.           (D17)

The norm here is L2(dx/x). This is an unconditional new field-tail estimate for this changed determinant source. It is not an estimate for any SP or original W35 subfamily. In particular, .874<.87449<.8748866, so this complete median complement is affordable for the stated first-gain target without using Mobius cancellation.

The surviving sector b<=Y_X still includes a=1,b=2 and every corresponding negative cross term. D17 does not imply that the surviving sector is small, or that the determinant creates cancellation within a given output.

## 8. Finite caps and the exact signed scalar

Fix tau=1 for a concrete target and let L=log X,

    B_X=2X exp(2sqrt L),
    A_X=X exp(-2sqrt L).

Uniformly in delta in I, the complete absolute product tails abc>B_X and abc<A_X are X^(-1+o(1)). Use D15a and Gaussian tail integration; the weaker majorant |h_delta(n)|<=d_3(n), with sum_(n<=t)d_3(n)<=t(1+log t)^2, also suffices. For the lower tail, n<=A_X gives log(x/n)>=2sqrt L on the whole shell; integration against the same counting function gives the same exponent. The constants, floors and sufficiently-large thresholds are fixed; the coefficient majorant is independent of chi and delta.

Define the finite field using the literal conventions

    Z_chi,delta,X(x)=sum_(a<b<c; b<=Y_X;
                           A_X<=abc<=B_X)
      mu(a)mu(b)mu(c)chi(abc) V_delta(a,b,c)^2
                                      g_1(log(abc/x)).   (D18)

Equality at either real product cap is included. At the median cap b<=floor(X^.315) is included. The complete complement is the union already paid in D16 and the two product tails; overlap only makes the triangle bound easier. Thus

    (integral_I ||H_chi,delta-Z_chi,delta,X||_[X,2X]^2 ddelta)^(1/2)
                         << X^.874+X^(-1+o(1)).         (D19)

Within D18, c>=A_X/Y_X^2>=X^.37 exp(-2sqrt L). Neither a nor b receives an invented lower cut: the short-factor faces, especially (1,2,c), remain in full.

For n in [A_X,B_X], let w_delta,X(n) be the sum of V_delta^2 over the exact tuples in D18 with abc=n and individually squarefree factors. Then the coefficient is chi(n)lambda(n)w_delta,X(n). The exact target is

    Q_D3,chi(X)=sum_(A_X<=n,m<=B_X)
       chi(n)conjugate(chi(m))lambda(nm) K_X(n,m)
                     integral_I w_delta,X(n)w_delta,X(m) ddelta
                  <<_(chi,epsilon) X^(1.74898+epsilon). (D20)

The family hypothesis is for every ordinary chi, every epsilon>0, and all sufficiently large dyadic X; constants and thresholds may depend on chi and epsilon. A bound only for zeta is only a zeta conclusion.

Here K_X(n,m)=integral_X^(2X) g_1(log(n/x))g_1(log(m/x)) dx/x, equivalently

    K_X(n,m)=g_2(log(n/m))
          *integral_0^(log2)g_(1/2)(u-log(sqrt(nm)/X))du.

Both independent output indices and every tuple-pair interaction remain. The real-shift average is part of the new norm, so there are no omitted cross-delta terms: D20 is exactly integral_I ||Z_delta||^2. For a complex character the conjugation above is essential. No subset of its signed scalar is presumed positive. The Gaussian kernel and the integrated weight are nonnegative, but the coefficient product is signed/complex.

The parameter weight is also elementary and finite. Expand each Vandermonde square as

    sum_(alpha,beta permutations of (0,1,2))
       sign(alpha)sign(beta) product_(j=1)^3 n_j^(-delta*(alpha_j+beta_j)).

For a tuple pair, every resulting term is r^(-delta), with the exact positive integer r obtained from the six labels and their displayed integer exponents. Its integral is

    J(r)=(r^(-1/5)-r^(-1/4))/log r, r>1;
    J(1)=1/20.                                          (D20a)

Thus the finite signed scalar can be written without numerical quadrature or an unspecified profile, using at most 36 squared-Vandermonde terms per triple and all 1296 ordered products per tuple pair. This expansion is an identity, not permission to replace the signed sum by the absolute sum of its terms.

By D19, D20 implies D11 with gamma=.87449, hence the conditional zero-free constant c=.12551, which would exceed c_G. The complete moment remains open; the tail estimate alone supplies no increased constant.

For comparison under the inherited beta=.8749 zeta calibration, the difference between the full and finite averaged squared energies is at most

    X^(beta+.874+epsilon)+X^(2*.874+epsilon)
       << X^(1.7489+epsilon).                            (D21)

This includes both mixed terms and the error square. Its exponent is below 1.74898. The norm argument D19 is sufficient without invoking that calibration; D21 simply records the complete scalar accounting. No percentage of the old source is claimed paid.

The diagonal of D20 is at most X^(1+o(1)): |h|<=d_3 and d_3(n)^2<=d_9(n) suffice with the fixed Gaussian shell weight. Thus the remaining obstruction is a signed off-diagonal correlation of the explicit weighted Liouville outputs, including the 2p channels and their complements.

## 9. A separate quantitative anchor: delta=2 really has an inverse

This section is an additional concrete completion of the parked cofactor problem, not the arithmetic estimate for the small-shift interval I. First take zeta. More generally its proof works for any Dirichlet-series coefficients |a(n)|<=1, a(1)=1, |a(2)|=1. Put delta=2. Formula D8 has leading term

    c_2 2^(-s),  c_2=(9/256)a(2),
    C_2(s)=c_2 2^(-s)(1+R(s)).                           (D22)

The remaining generalized Dirichlet series is supported on dilations r=mn/2>=3/2. At Re s=-1, its absolute coefficient norm is bounded by

    ||R||_(-1)
      <= [zeta(3)zeta(7)-zeta(5)^2]/(9/128)-1 <19/20.  (D23)

Proof: the positive identity

    sum_(m<n) (mn)^(-3)(m^(-2)-n^(-2))^2
                        =zeta(3)zeta(7)-zeta(5)^2

follows by expanding the square and pairing (m,n) with (n,m); diagonal terms are zero. The first term m=1,n=2 equals 9/128. Every other coefficient of the actual cofactor is bounded by its positive counterpart. Division by the first coefficient proves D23, uniformly in every imaginary height.

The final strict inequality has a small exact rational certificate. Let S_j=sum_(n=1)^32 n^(-j), j=3,5,7. Integral comparison gives zeta(j)<=S_j+1/((j-1)32^(j-1)) and zeta(5)>=S_5. Exact integer arithmetic verifies

    (S_3+1/(2*32^2))(S_7+1/(6*32^6))-S_5^2
                                               <351/2560,

where 351/2560=(1+19/20)(9/128). The script stores the exact positive rational difference; its decimal diagnostic for the resulting upper bound on ||R||_(-1) is .9468750294472809. That decimal is not used as the proof.

In particular, C_2(s) has no zero in Re s>=-1 and

    |C_2(s)| >=(9/5120)2^(-Re s).                       (D24)

Define the coefficient dilation measure (real signed for zeta)

    nu=sum_(j>=0)(-R)^(star j).

Convolution is multiplication of the positive dilation arguments, with all repeated labels coalesced only by summation. D23 gives

    sum_r |nu(r)|r <=20,  support(nu) subset {1} union [3/2,infinity).

For delta=2, the complementary E in D7 has coefficients bounded by 4d_3(n)n^(-2), hence its Gaussian field is O_epsilon(x^(-1+epsilon)). If M_tau(x)=sum_n a(n)g_tau(log(n/x)), and H_2 is the D3 field for this a, physical Mellin convolution gives the exact reconstruction

    M_tau(x)=c_2^(-1)sum_r nu(r)
                  [H_2(2x/r)-E_2^g(2x/r)].             (D25)

Absolute field convergence follows first from the Gaussian kernel and the weighted coefficient norms, and the displayed bounds extend the identity to all x>0. This is an actual physical readout, not an operator-norm identification with an unrelated functional.

There is a finite version on X<=x<=2X:

    M_tau(x)=c_2^(-1)sum_(r<=X)nu(r)H_2(2x/r)
                                      +O_epsilon(X^(-1+epsilon)). (D26)

Indeed the E sum is bounded using sum|nu(r)|r^(1-epsilon)<=20. For r>X, the H arguments lie below 4; the Gaussian left tail gives H_2(t)=O(t^(-1)) on 0<t<=4, and its omitted sum is O(X^(-1)sum|nu|r). The r<=X sum is finite: each nonidentity factor is at least 3/2, its depth is bounded by log X/log(3/2), and each factor's numerator mn is at most 2X. This prices the complete small-scale tail, with no frozen moving cutoff substituted at the wrong scale.

For ordinary odd-modulus characters, |a_chi(2)|=1, so the same anchor proof is immediate. For even moduli this specific delta=2 anchor can be obtained by the explicit finite atom repair a(2):=-1, leaving every other a_chi(n) unchanged. This corresponds to adding the entire function (chi(2)-1)2^(-s) to 1/L. It does not change its poles and its physical discrepancy is a single Gaussian left-tail term. The determinant coefficients in that auxiliary variant must use the repaired a exactly; they are not silently identified with chi(n)W_delta(n). The main averaged theorem and D20 require no such repair and preserve all original character zero extensions.

D25--26 are useful quantitative bridges, but also clarify the objection: the large-shift determinant is a stably invertible signed dilation filter of the ordinary Mobius field, up to a paid error. Its missing prime outputs cannot by themselves reduce the exponent. The new small-shift averaged target is retained as an explicit arithmetic problem, without calling this anchor an arithmetic solution.

## 10. Checks, limitations, and handoff boundary

At delta=2, check_exact.py verifies D3=D7 coefficientwise through n=240 for zeta and five explicit character/finite-repair coefficient sequences, including natural zero cases before the stated repair. It checks the -9/256 cofactor coefficient for the repaired sequences, the 2p formula at eight primes, and the strict rational inequality in D23. These checks catch signs, the Vandermonde square, tuple distinctness and the nonlinear readout expansion. They do not establish D11/D20, verify the small-shift interval by experiment, establish height uniformity by experiment, or prove a theorem via numerical evidence. The analytic arguments above supply their stated uniformity.

Exact receipt: exact-receipt.json, SHA-256 e74777a27523be5853dcb2522422c8dff89f4c5d3d01494aafb00fc14795886d at the completed check. A final full readback and hashes will accompany the handoff. No child, provider route, task message, publication, tracker mutation or Git write was used.

The strongest remaining objection is substantive: the full determinant energy still contains a hard long-Mobius channel, and D4 makes parity cancellation explicit rather than solving it. Neither the prime-power zeros, parameter averaging, nor the paid median tail proves an exponent gain. A next lane should attack D20 only if it has a source-specific signed estimate, or use the now-complete determinant/cofactor bridge for a materially different arithmetic input. Repeating the generic adjugate identity or the prime-output deletion would add nothing.

Acceptance proposed for review: (i) exact determinant/Vandermonde source and actual absolute-value obstruction; (ii) the averaged all-height pole bridge; (iii) the median and finite-cap estimates with full signed complement; and (iv) the fixed-shift nonvanishing/inverse anchor. The complete D3 arithmetic moment remains OPEN.

    ||D_R Q|| <= ||D_prefix Q||+||D_far Q||            (S13)

pays all prefix/far crosses once both complete positive norms are paid. It does not bound a chosen signed prefix/far sector separately. statement:
## S17: Farey transfer and the literal discontinuous observable

Fix an ordinary Dirichlet character chi modulo q with natural zeros.
Define the complete denominator-weighted primitive count

    A_chi(x)=sum_(1<=b<=x) chi(b) #{1<=a<=b:gcd(a,b)=1}
            =sum_(b<=x) chi(b) phi(b), phi(1)=1.

The equality retains a=b=1. For b>1 the endpoint a=b is not primitive.
Using phi(n)=sum_(d|n)mu(d)(n/d) gives the exact finite decomposition

    A_chi(x)=sum_(d<=x)mu(d)chi(d)
                    sum_(m<=x/d) m chi(m).                       (A1)

Multiplicativity is valid even at ramified factors, so no character zero
is divided out. On Re(s)>2 the absolutely convergent Dirichlet series is

    sum_n chi(n)phi(n)n^-s=L(s-1,chi)/L(s,chi).                    (A2)

Both (A1) and (A2) are exact. No Euclidean-algorithm spectral theorem has
yet been shown to apply to their observable. In the principal q=1 case,
the count of primitive ordered pairs 1<=a,b<=x is 2A_1(x)-1. This follows
by reflecting across the diagonal and retaining its unique point (1,1).

**Actual-source discontinuity obstruction.** Let B be any continuous
complex-valued function on [1,infinity). For each prime p not dividing q,
the jump of A_chi at p has modulus p-1. If
|A_chi(x)-B(x)|<=C x^gamma for every sufficiently large REAL x, then taking
the left limit and value at p and using continuity gives

    p-1 <= 2C p^gamma.                                         (A3)

There are arbitrarily large primes outside the finite set dividing q.
Thus gamma<1 is impossible in this precise pointwise norm. The same proof
works for every fixed ordinary chi, not merely a changing conductor or
a synthetic sequence. It does NOT obstruct an averaged count, a Riesz
source, a discontinuous explicitly paid boundary term, or a different
observable. It is not a lower bound on M_chi.

This pinpoints the missing transfer in a naive dynamical-gap proposal.
After dividing the count by x^2, the actual jumps have order 1/x at primes.
A continuous approximation with error O(x^(gamma-2)), gamma<1, is still
impossible. Any claim using a Banach space embedded in that uniform norm
must either smooth first or retain the jump channel. Mixing alone cannot
remove it. This statement does not assume that every transfer space has
such an embedding.

For principal q=1, elementary Möbius inversion already gives

    A_1(x)=x^2/(2 zeta(2))+O(x log(2x)).                         (A4)

Indeed sum_(m<=y)m=(floor(y)^2+floor(y))/2=y^2/2+O(y);
the finite d-sum in (A1) costs O(x sum_(d<=x)1/d), and extending the
main coefficient sum mu(d)/d^2 costs at most O(x). These are complete
estimates including real floors and the d>x tail. They show exactly where
a coarse absolute inversion stops; the inadequate upper bound alone is
not a signed lower bound.

**A lawful smoothed repair.** For integer r>=1 put

    R_r(x)=1/r! sum_(n<=x)chi(n)phi(n)(x-n)^r.

For Re(s)>2, Fubini and the beta integral give

    integral_1^infinity R_r(x)x^(-s-r-1)dx
       = [L(s-1,chi)/L(s,chi)]/[s(s+1)...(s+r)].                 (A5)

The lower limit may be replaced by zero since R_r=0 there. At x=n the
new summand is zero; thus R_r is continuous. Every normalization factor
and each endpoint is explicit. Suppose an explicitly known source P_r
has a meromorphic transform and that the COMPLETE difference satisfies

    integral_X^(2X)|R_r(x)-P_r(x)|dx/x
        <<_(chi,r,epsilon) X^(r+gamma+epsilon)                 (A6)

for every epsilon>0 and all sufficiently large dyadic X. Summing the
shell transforms, including any fixed s derivatives, continues the
remainder normally to Re(s)>gamma. All finite initial intervals are
entire. At a hypothetical L-zero rho, (A5) contradicts this continuation
only if the numerator L(rho-1,chi) is nonzero and P_r's transform has no
matching pole there. Those conditions must be proved for the actual
family; this audit does not import a functional equation or a dynamical
gap theorem without its hypotheses. The principal pole/main terms must
be included in P_r. This is a conditional source return, not an estimate
of (A6), and not a completed Mertens inversion.

Verdict: the raw continuous-boundary uniform transfer fails on the actual
source at every gamma<1. The smoothed or boundary-completed dynamics route
remains live, with (A5)-(A6) its concrete unpaid interface. Near gamma11,
5/6 and 3/4 all require the same complete exponent budget r+gamma; no new c.

statement: # W49 — least-prime error propagation and complete arithmetic boundary tests Written mathematical submission for independent review, 12 October 2026. The accepted research premise remains c6=125139/1000000=.125139, with boundary b6=.874861. **No larger zero-free constant or improved actual arithmetic exponent is proved here.** The main potentially useful increment is an exact residual calculus for least-prime renewal, including its sharp depth-by-depth error amplification. Two further bounded developments give a precise greedy-matching failure and a complete prime-square-mask return. Their elementary identities have substantial ancestry; no literature priority is claimed. ## 1. Frozen selection and development allocation All30 initial cards used only the frozen problem, recipe and operating policy. Their six groups of five retain numerical cap misses and one unknown/incoherent draw. The p labels are uncalibrated typicality judgments, never success probabilities. `selection-plan.json` was saved before the deterministic local draws. Each numerical pool contains EVERY unreserved card below its literal threshold regardless of prompt group. Selection was without replacement or content rerolls; all pools, hash draws and leftovers remain in `selections.json`. The six selected IDs are W49-02 and W49-16 (two strongest bridges), W49-24 (most different), W49-23 (p<.10 draw), W49-22 (p<.01 draw), and W49-06 (remaining wildcard). One seed-only event carrying paths, hashes and IDs was sent to root before results. Detailed proof/history intake began only after the freeze. Exactly three mechanisms received development: A/02, B/24, C/06. The high-ceiling renewal route A received the substantive error analysis first. The protected rare draws 23/22 were tested on their actual contracts; 23 duplicates an already proved graph decomposition and 22 has a flat fixed-pair mixed phase. Those specific failures do not prohibit a different source-compatible graph or a cross-pair phase mechanism. The wildcard06 survives as a complete conditional adapter and is retained with its ancestry. ## 2. Common arithmetic and complete zero return Fix an ordinary Dirichlet character chi modulo q. ## 2. W43-02: the signed summatory norm really is not a generic algebra

For0<sigma<1 define ||a||_[sigma]=sup_(x>=1)x^(-sigma)|sum_(n<=x)a(n)|. Let A(d)=(-1)^(d+1)/2 for1<=d<=N and0 outside, a(d)=A(d)-A(d-1). Then |a|<=1, support<=N+1 and ||a||<=1/2. Fix an integer H satisfying H>=4(N+1)^2 and H^(1-sigma)>=16(N+1)^(2-sigma). Put t_d=floor(H/d),1<=d<=N+1. These integer knots are distinct.

Prescribe B(t_d)=sign(a(d))*t_d^sigma and B(0)=B(2H)=0; interpolate linearly and take b(n)=B(n)-B(n-1). Absolute linear interpolation stays below the concave envelope t^sigma, even when adjacent signs differ. Hence ||b||<=1. Between adjacent reciprocal knots, spacing is at least H/(4d^2), while peak difference is at most2(H/d)^sigma; the slope is at most8H^(sigma-1)d^(2-sigma)<=1/2. The outer segments have slope<=1. Thus |b(n)|<=1, with finite support. Both endpoint half-coefficients of a are retained.

At the single physical endpoint H the divisor identity gives

    sum_(n<=H)(a*b)(n)=sum_d a(d) B(floor(H/d))
                        =sum_d |a(d)| t_d^sigma.

Since t_d>=H/(2d), the normalized output is at least2^(-sigma)sum_(d=2)^N d^(-sigma), which tends to infinity. The domain norms are bounded uniformly. No uniform convolution-algebra constant exists on this finite-sequence class. For H comparable to N^((2-sigma)/(1-sigma)), the constructed partial sum has order at least H^(1/(2-sigma)); the exponent calculation is sigma+(1-sigma)^2/(2-sigma)=1/(2-sigma).

The claim is valid as a sequence of finite examples. It is not a single fixed infinite arithmetic sequence violating an exponent, and not an actual Mobius counterexample. In particular, using a source-specific norm, additional correlations, or a more structured renewal operator remains logically possible. Integer rounding of the peaks loses at most the number of knots; it does not affect the divergence. The author's rational7/8 examples are supporting certificates, not the uniform proof. This is a sharper obstruction than simply saying that an absolute l1 norm loses signs, but it does not rule out every signed feedback scheme.

Fix 0<a<1. For each retained ordered component set

    U_i(s)=sum_(d in I_i)mu(d)d^(-s),
    eta(s)=(1-2^(1-s))zeta(s),
    D_ij(t)=exp(tau*(a+it)^2/2)*eta(a+it)
               *U_i(a+it)U_j(a+it).                    (G14)

The Mellin transform of S_tau is exp(tau*s^2/2)eta(s). Prove this
first on Re s>1 by absolute Fubini, then use its two rapidly decaying
tails to continue before moving the line. An absolutely divergent
ell Dirichlet series is never interchanged on a<1. Mellin inversion
and Plancherel give

    G_ij(x)=(2*pi)^(-1)integral_R D_ij(t)x^(a+it)dt,
    integral_0^infinity |G_ij(x)|^2 x^(-2a)dx/x
       =(2*pi)^(-1)integral_R |D_ij(t)|^2dt.              (G15)

For T=D*sqrt L, define

    Z_X(x)=(2*pi)^(-1)integral_[-T,T]
                    [sum_(i+j=-2,...,1) D_ij(t)]x^(a+it)dt,
    Q_X=integral_X^(2X)|Z_X(x)|^2 dx/x.                 (G16)

Equivalently Q_X is (2pi)^(-2) times the double integral over
[-T,T]^2 of the complete product

    [sum D_ij(t)] conj([sum D_i'j'(t')])
       *((2X)^(2a+i(t-t'))-X^(2a+i(t-t')))/(2a+i(t-t')). (G17)

Every component interaction, complex phase and both independent height
variables remain. The diagonal t=t' has the continuous value of the
displayed kernel; no principal-value convention is needed.

The alternating partial sums imply |eta(a+it)|<=|a+it|/a.
Absolute interval sums and D_i^*D_j^*<=X exp(3kappa sqrt L) then pay
the entire omitted height field by

    X^(1-tau*D^2/2+o(1)).                               (G18)

This proof uses no moving-height Mertens or Hecke estimate.

The required arithmetic statement is now explicit:

**OPEN-GC:** for all sufficiently large dyadic X and every epsilon>0,
prove Q_X <<_epsilon X^(2gamma+epsilon), with these exact coefficients,
bins and fixed parameters. No current theorem supplies a new gamma.

The stronger sufficient **OPEN-GM** asks, for every retained ordered
component, integral_R |D_ij(t)|^2dt <<_epsilon
X^(2gamma-2a+epsilon), uniformly over its moving interval endpoints.
The O(sqrt L) count is subpower, so Cauchy–Schwarz makes it sufficient.
It is not necessary: a proof may use negative cross-component terms.

1. Under \(\mu=\beta_*-\theta>0\), fix the geometric/retained reserves, row extension, requested moment loss, amplitude rounding and capacity decrement. Obtain the old and new common meshes and choose one finite original slot system meeting them on \(d\ge d_0\). This fixes a common positive minimum slot width and hence \(\mu_P>0\).
2. Choose real contour/detector buffers and a common positive improvement \(\Delta\) below fixed fractions of the retained reserve, \(\mu\), \(y/4,\ h/24,\ \mu_P\), and the small-row saving. Reduce it so \(\Delta<\mu/4\). These choices precede the target.
3. For each primitive target \(\eta\), fix S, the arithmetic dictionary and all finitely many moment, profile and Sobolev orders. Choose a target-dependent \(\tau>0\) small enough that the polynomial height factors at \(T=3Z^\tau\) fit the same already reserved power losses, as well as the source retained-height restrictions. The local theorem's internal detector exponent is distinct from this external \(\tau\).
4. Choose the external tail order after \(\tau\) and its raw polynomial bound, then one target-dependent asymptotic threshold. At that threshold fixed conductors, exceptional rows, annular constants and finite logarithmic losses are all accommodated.

The new local input must not impose an additional target-independent lower bound on the external \(\tau\) that conflicts with step 3. Its stated arbitrary-height polynomial allowance is adequate; the older detector/contour compatibility is part of the pinned B0.7 input.

The result is
\[
 J_\eta(Z)-f_\eta(Z)\ll_\eta Z^{\beta_*-k-\Delta},
 \qquad J_\eta(Z)\ll_\eta Z^{\theta-k+\epsilon}.
\]
With \(\epsilon<\mu/4\) and the above \(\Delta\), the same improved exponent bounds \(f_\eta\). At zero, the defining Mellin line can be moved arbitrarily far right, giving \(f_\eta(Z)=O_{\eta,A}(Z^{A-k})\). Thus
\[
 \int_0^\infty f_\eta(Z)Z^{-s+k}\,\frac{dZ}{Z}
\]
is holomorphic for \(\Re s>\beta_*-\Delta\) and equals
\[
 e^{(s-5/6)^2}H_\eta(s)/L^S(s,\eta)
\]
on the initial half-plane. Because \(\beta_*-\Delta>\theta>.87\), its numerator cannot cancel any zero of L in the asserted continuation region. The principal pole is separately excluded/regularized. Fixed Euler factors are nonzero for \(\Re s>0\).

The exact source contract confirms this quantifier order. PrimitiveProbeContract in Continuation.lean quantifies over each primitive target and only then chooses its masked presentation, H and J and their Big-O estimates. UniformCommonProbe first chooses common positive \(\omega,\sigma\) under \(\theta<\beta_*\). Its continuation margin is
\[
 \min(\beta_*-\theta-\omega,\sigma)>0.
\]
beta_le_of_common_probe then selects a primitive zero sufficiently near the supremum and invokes that target's contract. It never assumes the supremum is attained. A common exclusion boundary, rather than a conductor-uniform numerical Big-O constant, is what this contradiction needs.

This does **not** establish a quantitative estimate uniform while target conductors grow with Z. No such estimate is needed for the all-family nonvanishing conclusion, and no substitution of fixed-character nonvanishing for a common power saving is being made.

For an imprimitive Hecke presentation, T2.1 is
\[
 L_{\mathfrak m}(s,\eta)=L(s,\eta^*)
 \prod_{\mathfrak p\mid\mathfrak m,\ \mathfrak p\nmid\mathfrak f}
 (1-\eta^*(\mathfrak p)(N\mathfrak p)^{-s}).
\]
Every finite factor is nonzero in \(\Re s>0\). This covers arbitrary presented finite-order Hecke characters with trivial infinity type, using the ordinary family dictionary already checked at the pinned source. It does not include angular/infinite-order families.

For any complex Dirichlet character modulo \(q\ge1\), its norm lift has modulus \(q\mathcal O\), is trivial on global units because they have norm one, and has ideal coefficient \(\chi(N\mathfrak a)\). The fetched Hecke/Dirichlet source proves these exact identifications and
\[
 L_K(s,\eta_\chi)=L(s,\chi)L(s,\chi\chi_{-3})
\]
away from 0 and 1, using its actual common-modulus companion character.
Split, inert, ramified and imprimitive local factors all agree: the inert product is \((1-\chi(p)^2p^{-2s})^{-1}\), the ramified prime 3 contributes only the original character's factor, and primes dividing q are omitted on both sides. In \(\theta<\Re s<1\), both Dirichlet factors are finite and the Hecke product is nonzero, hence the first factor is nonzero. At \(\Re s\ge1\), the classical all-character theorem handles the conclusion with the principal-pole exception, avoiding a zero-times-pole argument at 1.

Continuation.dirichlet_of_hecke implements exactly that split. Its zeta_of_hecke also handles Mathlib's assigned value at 1; the ordinary analytic conclusion here retains the pole exception. Neither primitivity nor reality of the Dirichlet character is assumed.

## 2. The two independently frozen unselected audits

The full proofs are in blind-audits.md, preserved unchanged. Their operative conclusions are as follows.

### S17: sharp primitive/Farey observable and its actual jump obstruction

For a fixed ordinary character, the denominator-weighted primitive count is

    A_chi(x)=sum_(b<=x) chi(b) phi(b)
            =sum_(d<=x) mu(d)chi(d) sum_(m<=x/d) m chi(m).

The coefficient at 1 is retained. Its absolutely convergent Dirichlet series is L(s-1,chi)/L(s,chi) for Re(s)>2. For q=1 the ordered coprime pair count is 2A_1(x)-1, including the diagonal pair (1,1).

At every unramified prime p, A_chi has a jump of magnitude p-1. Therefore no continuous background B(x) can satisfy |A_chi(x)-B(x)|=O(x^gamma) uniformly on every large real x when gamma<1: compare the left limit and value at p. This is an actual-character sharp-observable obstruction. It does not forbid averages, a smoothed count, or a discontinuous background whose full recovery cost is paid. The elementary principal estimate A_1(x)=x^2/(2 zeta(2))+O(x log x) includes all floor errors and the reciprocal tail.

An r-fold Riesz smoothing has Mellin quotient L(s-1,chi)/[L(s,chi)s(s+1)...(s+r)]. A complete smoothed residual bound can supply a return only after the principal terms and possible numerator zeros are paid. That is a conditional bridge, not an estimate. The author's parity-adapted higher-dimensional Jordan numerator subsequently supplies a useful source-specific repair of this numerator issue; the blind sharp-jump obstruction remains valid in its own scope.

### S24: complete replica determinant and sparse-graph certificate cost

On the K squarefree q-units at most x, put a_n=mu(n)chi(n), so |a_n|=1. Exactly

    sum_(m<n) |a_m-a_n|^2 = K^2-|M_chi(x)|^2.

For the principal character this is 4K_+K_-. Positivity alone does not give the required lower bound K^2-O(x^(2gamma+epsilon)). That one-sided deficit is the full signed arithmetic problem.

For a simple d-regular graph on these K vertices, 1<=d<=K/2, let Ltilde=(K/d)(dI-A) and Lcomplete=KI-J. From tr(A^2)=Kd and the constant eigenvalue d,

    ||Ltilde-Lcomplete||
      >= K sqrt((K-d)/(d(K-1))) >= K/sqrt(2d).

Thus a uniform operator-norm comparison paying the quadratic error by K times this norm needs d at least x^(4-4gamma-o(1)), since K is a positive constant times x plus O(sqrt x). At gamma11 the degree exponent is .5005838544; at 5/6 it is 2/3; at 3/4 it is 1. The latter rules out every fixed-power saving d<=x^(1-delta) by this certificate, not x^(1-o(1)) under epsilon losses. It is not a lower bound for the actual Möbius vector's signed error, nor a theorem about weighted/nonregular constructions.

The finite independent checks support exact identities and indexing only: actual principal, complex and imprimitive character replica identities and three graph trace examples. The asymptotic statement follows from the displayed proof, not samples.

### Test17: an exact original-H coding calculation

Use JN7-JN10 with the whole d sum already recombined. For one distinct-norm
prime pair, Q=q_pi q_pi', the finite group has size Q^2, and its literal
phase-character kernel is

    K(h,s,s')=chi_pi(h)^3 chi_pi'(h)^3
                         chi_pi(s)^2 chi_pi'(s')^4.          (24)

The full native term pairs this with W_hat, its fixed CRT/ray factor and
both outside prime coefficients. The Fourier transform has normalization
1/Q, is unitary, and retains the plus sign on the conjugate mark in JN7.
The exact support U consists of h unit modulo pi*pi', s unit modulo pi,
s' unit modulo pi', so

    |U|=(q_pi-1)^2(q_pi'-1)^2, ||K||_2=sqrt(|U|).           (25)

A syndrome that records only these unit/nonunit bits is constant on U.
The mean of K on U is ZERO because the s character chi_pi^2 is nontrivial.
Its full conditional variance is therefore1, not0. The entire pairing
survives in the conditional covariance with W_hat. Cauchy gives
`|sum_U K W_hat|<=sqrt(|U|)||1_U(W_hat-mean_U W_hat)||_2`,
with no new norm saving. If a richer syndrome records K itself, covariance
can vanish but the complete original sum moves into its predictable term.
It is not eliminated. The law of total expectation keeps both pieces.

For the affordable actual residue-field test, take a degree-one prime of
norm7. Choose the order-six character orientation chi(3)=exp(2pi i/6),
where3 is a primitive root in F7; conjugating the character conjugates
the following phases and preserves their distinction.
The unit residues s=1 and3 have identical unit syndrome but cubic phases
1 and exp(2pi i/3). Complete summation of chi(s)^2 over all six units is0.
Using norm13 for the second prime and h=s'=1 leaves that exact difference.
This is a local kernel fact, not a claim about the full global Hecke weight.

The metric part of the first test is equally literal: for every good
prime pi of norm>3, s=1 and2 are both units and have the SAME unit
syndrome, while their native mark frequencies differ by1/pi, of complex
absolute value q_pi^(-1/2). Taking larger pi makes distinct frequencies
arbitrarily close inside that one fiber. On the nonzero kernel support
the unit syndrome is constant, so it cannot itself separate frequency
packets. This rejects that concrete coding choice; a richer arithmetic
code would need a proved metric relation and its full covariance return.

An arbitrary test vector W_hat=conj(K) on U would saturate Cauchy, showing
why no coefficient-free code theorem can improve it. That vector is NOT
asserted to satisfy native row/mark supports. The existing JN and [private research revision]
uncertainty bounds supply stronger actual-support restrictions; their
remaining signed pairing is precisely what would have to be estimated.
This is a source-specific version of the existing W44 conditional-covariance
warning, not a new coding family or an actual H lower bound.

statement:
## 0. The theorem retained, the new results, and their dependencies

The accepted starting theorem remains the strongest zero-free conclusion in this integration:
\[
 \boxed{\zeta(s)\ne0\quad(\Re s>b_0,\ s\ne1),\qquad
 c_0=1-b_0=0.1251133529600358690553859994698193505\ldots .}
\]
Here \(\ell_0\) is the root in \((.16712007850680,.16712007850682)\) of
\[
 927\ell^4-3135\ell^3+2433\ell^2+275\ell-100=0,\qquad
 c_0=\frac1{12}+\frac{\ell_0}{4}.
\]
This theorem is the user-accepted research premise, at frozen revision
c06e952f6512f78a15016c97533c104551acaef8. **No larger \(c\) is established by the combined submissions or by this merge.** The new content consists of complete reductions, proved sector estimates, corrected conditional transfers, and sharper descriptions of the first unpaid estimates. A conditional transfer is proved as an implication; its energy or cancellation hypothesis is not thereby proved.

The development has three linked parts. T01–T05 repair the completed cubic mean and signed-current interfaces. T06–T07 isolate the genuinely unpaid part of the full sextic physical energy. T08–T10 give more economical sufficient hypotheses for those currents and for independent Möbius/theta detectors. The auxiliary record contains additional restricted estimates, identities, calibration formulas, counterexamples and numerical certificates. The portfolio uses these results as inputs and keeps unproved constructions separate.

### Accepted input packages

No inherited theorem is re-proved here merely to establish the accepted baseline. These are the precise inherited packages invoked by the new arguments; their source pointers resolve in document 06.

| Input | Content used here | Exact inherited source |
|---|---|---|
| **I-ZETA** | The displayed zero-free half-plane; its buffered Möbius/reciprocal estimates when explicitly needed | M, opening theorem and B0; original summary §§1–2 |
| **I-HECKE** | The stronger supplied theorem for every primitive finite-order Hecke character over \(\mathbb K=\mathbb Q(\omega)\), with principal pole allowed; on fixed buffered lines \(\Re s>b_0\), subpower conductor/height bounds for the \(L\)-function and its reciprocal, with the stated finite-deletion conventions | M B0.1, B0.50–B0.51 and its inherited analytic package; SA Part IV's use of that package |
| **I-FD** | Independent holomorphy of the uncompleted finite ray families for \(\Re s>1/2\); coarse polynomial growth; exact forced-divisor identities; large-divisor energies and common-profile separation | FD (1)–(3), (49), (59), (65)–(73), §19 |
| **I-CURRENT** | The actual primitive cubic-current realizations, raised STF/Wilson estimates, and removal of the former gamma-height loss; only the components actually realized | [restricted research revision] AB1–AB16, especially AB12 and AB15; [restricted research revision]'s retained corrections |
| **I-CUBIC** | Exact completed column coefficients, signed coprime Gram, both zero terms, physical Poisson normalization and the current-to-zero transfer | M §§2–3 and Appendix M; CP (14)–(27) |
| **I-SEXTIC** | The actual compensated physical probe, every embedded field and fixed ray sector, the signed outer Gram, the positive complete-zero form, the original numerator and contour transfer | M B0.21–B0.27 and B1; [restricted research revision] Y1–Y9c; [restricted research revision] AA14–AA20; SG's saved geometry |
| **I-DETECTOR** | Exact fixed Möbius-profile and triple-convolution Mellin identities, original smoothing cutoffs and endpoint bounds | [restricted research revision] V1–V10; [restricted research revision] Z13–Z18 |

I-HECKE is stronger than I-ZETA. Its use in the sharper T07 tail and A03 prime estimate is explicitly marked. Those conclusions are proved **relative to that inherited Hecke package**, rather than inferred from Riemann-zeta nonvanishing alone. The fixed angular Hecke character in the cubic completion is not finite order; its entire continuation and fixed-strip polynomial growth are a different, fixed-conductor input. These distinctions must survive subsequent integration.

### Notation and uniformity

In the cubic/sextic sections, indices are good primary ideals, with one generator per ideal, in \(\mathbb K\). Write \(q_a=Na\), \(Q_p=Np\), and let \(S\) be the fixed excluded prime set. Units and valuations modulo three at the fixed primes are included in a finite vector of components. Every component orbit is closed under the ray switches specified in FD. Characters are extended by zero at nonunits. Squarefree cores and cube labels may share primes; no coprimality is imposed unless it comes from the exact identity.

The physical row \(h=ab^2\) has norm \(q_aq_b^2\), its primitive good conductor has norm \(q_aq_b\), and a reduced sixth-order Fourier index can be \(a^4b^2\). These quantities are never interchangeable. In particular, a prime of norm \(Q\) has inverse physical row \(p^2\) of norm \(Q^2\).

The symbol \(\xi\) follows the source formula locally: it denotes the fixed angular character in the cubic completion, the original fixed probe character in the sextic field, and the completed Riemann xi function only in the explicitly labeled auxiliary geometric sections. Write \(\xi_{\rm ang}\) when a distinction is needed. Rational Möbius sums in T09–T10 are indexed by positive integers. \(T=2+|t|\) denotes analytic height.

Every arbitrary-loss bound holds for each positive loss after its buffers, profiles, finite sectors and derivative orders are fixed. Constants may depend on these fixed data; a polynomial height order may not depend on a moving conductor, length or height. The original smooth product profiles, their tails, fixed bad places and all marked slots are retained. A finite trace is never replaced by an infinite trace without an additional theorem.

### Dependency map and proof locations

| New result | Available conclusion | First unpaid step |
|---|---|---|
| T01–T02 | Extract a fixed holomorphic completion without changing a mean exponent; alternatively pass a common completed ordinary mean directly into the selector transfer | The ordinary mean, with actual current/component realization |
| T03–T04 | Reduce all physical rows to cube-free rows; pay the actual inverse-prime-square sector | Ordinary/composite and mixed-orientation mean |
| T05 | Full physical cube-row Type I projection with exponent \(4/3+(2/3)k+4y\) | Principal C–C improvement and the complete nonprincipal signed remainder |
| T06–T07 | Full same-core square function; cancellation in a large true-gcd tail with the actual prime weights | OPEN-SMALL-GCD, including gcd one |
| T08 | Two-exponent finite-incidence transfer, common-completion equivalence and exact sufficient divisor corridor | The finite-incidence energy on that corridor |
| T09 | Fixed-profile scale \(L^2\) and compact-profile triple criteria, with exact smoothing and endpoint control | Their signed arithmetic energy estimates |
| T10 | Two-dilation and continuum-dilation criteria; quantitative continuum multiplier calibration | The arithmetic difference energy |

Proofs below supersede the overlapping source formulations. The auxiliary results and the separate failure record preserve useful alternatives without reproducing these proofs. Status, provenance, duplicate claims and independently checked new merger results are catalogued in document 06.


### The cubic families used in T01–T05

Use good primary ideal indices in the Eisenstein field, one generator per ideal, and norm `q`. The fixed excluded set is `S`. Element units and valuations modulo three at fixed primes form additional finite components. A finite ray orbit must be closed under the switches in FD (3). Characters always retain their nonunit zero. Let
\[
D_h(s)=\sum_{c\ {\rm sf,good}}\beta(c)\vartheta_c(h)q_c^{-s},\qquad
\beta(c)=\mu(c)\overline{\mathfrak G(c)},\quad |\beta(c)|=1.
\]
FD (1) gives, for squarefree good `g`,
\[
D_h^{(g)}(s)=\beta(g)\vartheta_g(h)q_g^{-s}D_{gh}(s).
\tag{T0}
\]
For an individual `A_{nu,h}` the right side switches `nu` to `nu R_g`; it is not legitimate to ignore that switch. FD (49) supplies separate holomorphy of the required uncompleted families for `Re s>1/2`; FD (59) supplies coarse, uniform polynomial row/height growth there. These are independent prerequisites, not conclusions inferred by division from a completed current.

statement:
## 2. D1: full polynomial, explicit constants and both branches

Throughout fix one ordinary Dirichlet character chi modulo q, with its original nonunit zeros. Write a(n)=mu(n)chi(n). The complete hard-cutoff polynomial is

    Z_N(z)=sum_(n<=N,mu(n)^2=1)chi(n)z^omega(n)
          =1+A_N z+R_N(z),
    A_N=sum_(p<=N)chi(p),
    B_N=#{n<=N:mu(n)^2=1,(n,q)=1,omega(n)>=2}.       (R1)

Every coefficient obeys the author's bound sum_(k>=2)|C_k|<=B_N<=N. Z_N(-1)=M_chi(N) exactly, including n=1, squareful zeros and ramified zeros. This is not the Euler product over p<=N, which would add integers above N.

### Isolated root: accept with the stated absolute constants

For a polynomial Z=1+Az+R, put lambda=B/|A|^2. Assume |A|>=8 and lambda<=1/8, with sum|c_k|<=B for R=sum_(k>=2)c_k z^k. Since |z|<=1 implies |R(z)|<=B|z|^2, on |z|=2/|A| one has

    |1+Az|>=1,    |R(z)|<=4lambda<=1/2.

Rouche gives exactly one zero counted with multiplicity in that disk. If B>0, on the circle centered at -1/A of radius2lambda/|A|,

    |1+Az|=2lambda,
    |R(z)|<=lambda(1+2lambda)^2<=25lambda/16<2lambda.

This small disk lies inside the first and inside |z|<1. Hence the same unique root alpha is simple, and

    |A alpha+1|<=2lambda,
    (1-2lambda)/|A|<=|alpha|<=(1+2lambda)/|A|.       (R2)

B=0 gives the exact linear root. All other zeros are outside the larger disk, so alpha is the unique nearest root. No unproved reality assumption enters the complex-character case.

Factor the ENTIRE polynomial as Z(z)=(1-z/alpha)Q(z), Q(0)=1. This exact division is important: a truncated reciprocal series would not establish the endpoint formula. From (R2),

    |1+1/alpha|>=4|A|/5-1>=|A|/2,
    |1+1/alpha|<=1+4|A|/3<=2|A|.

Thus

    (|A|/2)|Q(-1)|<=|M(N)|<=2|A||Q(-1)|.           (R3)

The constant checks include the extremal |A|=8,lambda=1/8. These are rigorous inequalities, independently checked also with rational arithmetic; no numerical root approximation is needed.

### Principal characters: an actual whole-cutoff collapse

For chi0 modulo fixed q, A_N=P_N=pi(N)-#{p<=N:p|q}; all C_k are nonnegative integers. The elementary central-binomial argument is correct:

    4^m/(2m+1)<=binom(2m,m)<=(2m)^pi(2m).

For the upper bound each p-adic valuation is a sum of0-or1 terms, at most floor(log(2m)/log p), so each prime contributes at most2m. With m=floor(N/2), fixed q removes only finitely many primes. Consequently

    P_N>>_q N/log N,    lambda_N<=N/P_N^2<<_q(log N)^2/N.

No PNT or distribution of primes in progressions is needed. Eventually the root hypotheses hold for EVERY integer N, not merely a selected face or subsequence. Conjugation and uniqueness make alpha_N real; (R2) then makes it negative and

    alpha_N=-P_N^(-1)(1+O_q((log N)^2/N)).            (R4)

The Taylor series of the local branch log Z_N at0 has radius exactly |alpha_N|. Its derivative Z'_N/Z_N has a nonremovable pole there, while no closer zero exists. Thus no fixed zero-free disk about0 survives, and the straight negative-real path to-1 crosses a zero for large N. This is not a prohibition on every complex path, exact deflation, signed contour or changed smoothing. Fugacity zeros are not L-function zeros.

Using N/log N<<P_N<=N in (R3), the EVERY-EPSILON statements are equivalent:

    M_chi0(N)<<_(q,epsilon)N^(gamma+epsilon)
      iff Q_N(-1)<<_(q,epsilon)N^(gamma-1+epsilon).   (R5)

For the forward implication choose a smaller internal epsilon to absorb log N; the reverse uses P_N<=N. Boundedness of Q_N(-1) therefore gives no subunit Mertens exponent. The full signed deflated endpoint still needs a power decay.

### Complementary characters and all-height return: accept, without deleting a branch

For each N use the root branch exactly when |A_N|>=8 and |A_N|^2>=8B_N. Otherwise

    |A_N|<=max(8,sqrt(8B_N))<=8+sqrt(8N),
    M_chi(N)=1-A_N+R_N(-1).                          (R6)

For fixed1/2<gamma<1, the complete two-branch hypothesis is

    non-root branch: |R_N(-1)|<<_(chi,epsilon)N^(gamma+epsilon);
    root branch:    |A_N Q_N(-1)|<<_(chi,epsilon)N^(gamma+epsilon).
                                                               (OPEN-FD)

It is equivalent to the full all-integer Mertens exponent for this chi: (R6) pays the unit/prime complement at exponent1/2; (R3) handles the root branch with absolute constants. The reverse follows by subtraction in (R6) and the lower inequality in (R3). Arbitrary branch switches are allowed, but every sufficiently large N in BOTH branches is required. It is not enough to prove a principal, density-one, averaged-character or root-branch-only estimate.

The all-height return is complete. If the same gamma works for every fixed ordinary chi and every epsilon, then

    F_chi(s)=s integral_1^infinity M_chi(x)x^(-s-1)dx

is holomorphic on Re(s)>gamma. M_chi(x)=M_chi(floor x), so the integer estimates cover all real x. On each compact subset choose epsilon below its distance from the boundary; derivatives merely introduce integrable logarithms. On Re(s)>1, absolute interchange and (mu chi)*chi=delta give F=1/L. The meromorphic identity L F=1 then excludes zeros throughout the half-plane. A principal pole is a removable reciprocal zero, not an excluded zero; s=0 is outside this positive half-plane. Every fixed height and every imprimitive character is retained. Constants/onsets may depend on chi. There is no growing-conductor or Hecke extension.

OPEN-FD is an exponent-equivalent new representation, not a weaker proved arithmetic estimate. Exact root isolation is mathematically constructive, but neither efficient computation nor an error bound for numerically approximated Q(-1) is supplied.

### D1d: the second-root inference is valid but only necessary

For a fixed principal character, assume a supplied all-N Mertens bound of exponent1-c for every epsilon, c>0. Then (R5) gives |Q_N(-1)|<=C_epsilon N^(-c+epsilon).

If a squarefree integer has D prime factors, it is at least (D+1)!, because its j-th prime is at least j+1. Integrating log t gives

    deg Z_N<=(1+o(1))log N/loglog N.

Write d=deg Q_N. For sufficiently large N, d=0 is incompatible with the endpoint decay because Q(0)=1; if Q(-1)=0, select that root immediately. Otherwise all roots zeta_j are nonzero and

    |Q_N(-1)|=product_(j=1)^d |1+1/zeta_j|.

Some factor is at most |Q_N(-1)|^(1/d). The direction of the degree inequality is correct: because the logarithm of the product is negative, an UPPER bound on d gives the required upper bound on this factor. Given0<eta<c, first fix a small internal epsilon and then absorb log C_epsilon and the degree o(1). Eventually

    |1+1/zeta_j|<=(log N)^(-c+eta)=delta_N.

Since delta_N<1/2, |zeta_j|<=1/(1-delta_N), hence

    |zeta_j+1|<=2(log N)^(-c+eta).                    (R7)

This root is distinct from alpha_N, which tends to0. Multiplicities and every other deflated factor are retained. One root near-1 is NOT sufficient for a power saving: the remaining product can overwhelm its small factor. The proof is conditional on the supplied Mertens bound; a numerical root plot or a bare zero-free-strip statement is not silently substituted for that input.

### Novelty and strongest objection

U-FUGACITY, W07/W09/W22, W30's continued-power branch obstruction, W31 T21/T28 and W34's cluster price are direct ancestry. Independent source reads confirm the distinction: W31 T21 has the full SMALL polynomial1+3z+z^2; T28's shrinking radius1/m is on a selected prime face. W09's physical multivariate instability extends to the full polynomial, but its explicit negative diagonal root belongs to a five-prime FACE and its source explicitly preserves that limitation.

D1 supplies the stated large-N root of the complete ordinary squarefree one-variable polynomial, with constants, and couples its exact deflation to a fully paid character-adaptive criterion. This precise combination was not found in the maintained entries and targeted source passages. statement:
## 2. Full observation theorem and both paid tails

**Theorem A.** Suppose A1 holds with b>gamma. For every epsilon>0 and every sufficiently large integer k, suppose there is a measurable E_k subset [k,k+1] such that

    |E_k| >= delta_k >0,
    log(1/delta_k)=o(sqrt(k)),
    ess sup_(u in E_k)|F(u)| <= C_epsilon exp((gamma+epsilon)k). (A4)

The little-o condition is uniform as k tends to infinity; its sequence and the sets may depend on epsilon. Then, for every epsilon>0,

    |F(u)| <<_epsilon exp((gamma+epsilon)u), u>=0.        (A5)

All constants may depend on the fixed coefficient sequence, b,tau,gamma and epsilon. No reciprocal meromorphic input is needed for A4=>A5.

Proof. Fix an observation allowance eta>0 with d=b-gamma-eta>0. For each large integer j put r_j^2=sqrt(j) and

    H_j(u)=h(u) exp(-(u-j)^2/(2*r_j^2)).

The Fourier convolution of A2 with the Gaussian window gives exactly the uniform majorant

    |hat H_j(t)| <= M r_j/sqrt(tau+r_j^2)
                      * exp(-sigma_j*t^2/2),
    sigma_j=tau*r_j^2/(tau+r_j^2) >= tau/2               (A6)

for large j. This estimate is independent of the center j. The exact square identity is

    tau*x^2+r_j^2*(t-x)^2
      =(tau+r_j^2)*(x-r_j^2*t/(tau+r_j^2))^2+sigma_j*t^2.

In the convolution integral multiplication's factor1/(2pi) is canceled by the two Gaussian integral normalizations. The phase from the translated window has modulus1.

Choose

    T_j=sqrt(4*(b-gamma+2)*j/tau),
    P_j(u)=(2pi)^(-1) integral_[-T_j,T_j] hat H_j(t)e^(itu)dt.

P_j is bounded with Fourier support [-T_j,T_j], and Gaussian tail integration yields

    ||H_j-P_j||_infinity <= C exp(-(b-gamma+2)j).         (A7)

For a literal estimate the preceding tail is at most M/[pi*sigma_j*T_j] times exp(-sigma_j*T_j^2/2). Thus A7 pays the entire omitted frequency field before applying A3.

Let m0=floor(j/2), m1=ceil(3j/2), I_j=[m0,m1+1], and

    S_j=(R\I_j) union (union_(m0<=k<=m1) E_k),
    delta_j^*=min_(m0<=k<=m1) delta_k.

Every real interval of length2 contains an integer unit interval. S_j is therefore (delta_j^*/2,2)-thick. The uniform little-o in A4 implies log(1/delta_j^*)=o(sqrt(j)). Applying A3 to P_j costs

    Lambda_j=(200/delta_j^*)^(132*T_j+1)=exp(o(j)).     (A8)

On E_k in I_j, the observation bound and b>gamma+eta imply

    |H_j(u)| <= C_eta exp(-d*u-(u-j)^2/(2*r_j^2))
              <= C_eta exp(-d*j+d^2*sqrt(j)/2).          (A9)

Replacing k by u in A4 costs only a fixed factor. The second bound is the exact completed square. On the artificially added exterior R\I_j, A2 gives

    |H_j(u)| <= ||h||_infinity
                  exp(-(j/2-1)^2/(2*sqrt(j)))
               = exp(-j^(3/2)/8+O(sqrt(j))).             (A10)

This explicitly pays the part of the thick set on which no arithmetic small-value information was assumed. In particular no unobserved complement is declared small by interpolation.

Now A3, A7 and the norm triangle inequality give

    ||H_j||_infinity
      <= Lambda_j ||H_j||_(L-infinity(S_j))
                  +(Lambda_j+1)||H_j-P_j||_infinity
      <= exp(-(b-gamma-eta)j+o(j)).                     (A11)

The sampling factor multiplies BOTH the observation error and the frequency remainder. For u in[j,j+1], its Gaussian window is at least exp(-1/(2sqrt(j))); multiply A11 by e^(bu), choose eta before the requested output allowance, and absorb o(j). This proves A5 on every sufficiently large real u. Compact u is absorbed into the constant. QED.

The proof's exponent ledger is explicit: source exponent gamma+eta; localization cost d^2/(2sqrt(j)) per unit j; sampling cost O((sqrt(j)+1)log(C/delta_j^*))/j; frequency tail exponent at most gamma-2 after undoing e^(-bu); exterior tail tends to minus infinity after normalization. Hence the analytic losses tend to0 for every fixed gamma<b, including gamma=5/6 and3/4. There is no positive transfer floor.

### Completed small-divisor source

Assume u=k-(k-1)r=2gamma-r>0 and put eta_0=1/(100kpq).
For ANY real U,V>=1 with UV<=eta_0 X^u,

    ||sum_n S_(U,V)(n)f_x(n)||_1
      +||sum_n S_(U,V)(n)f_x(n)||_2
               <<_(p,q,b,k,gamma,epsilon) X^(gamma+epsilon). (91.3)

On n<=M, expand b_p in its nonzero Fourier modes j/Q. For D=de,
the phase as a function of the cofactor is

    F_j(t)=jt/Q-(Dt/x)^k/(2pi).

Since D<=UV and Dt<=M, its derivative correction is at most
k UV M^(k-1)/(2pi X^k)<=k eta_0/(2pi)<1/(2Q).
Thus F_j' and each discrete phase increment lie monotonically between
1/(2Q) and 1-1/(2Q). Summation by parts with
1/(exp(2pi i v)-1)=-1/2-(i/2)cot(pi v) bounds every prefix by O(Q).
Abel summation preserves that bound under the actual decreasing damping.
This includes empty and one-term prefixes. Summing all ordered d,e costs
O_(p,q)(UV)=O(X^u); u<gamma. The complete n>M contribution is (91.2).
No Fourier gap is asserted beyond M. Also U+V<=UV+1 pays the short
terms, uniformly in the asymmetric choices.

This is an actual unrestricted small-product estimate, not an arbitrary
coefficient model. It does NOT allow UV=X^gamma without a new argument.
