## 6. Transfer to the actual C--C Poisson sector

Fix the original outside cube labels \(B,E\). CP23--CP25 force \(h=R_0n\) in the C--C part. Their complete finite transform, Poisson normalization and phase give exactly SR12, with outside factor

\[
\frac{K(q_Bq_E)^4}{D^2}=\frac{q_Bq_E}{H},\qquad
C_*=\frac{D}{q_B^3},\quad E_*=\frac{D}{q_E^3},
\quad H=\frac{C_*E_*}{K}.
\tag{MQ21}
\]

The factor \(q_{R_0}\) in the forced transform cancels its period normalization; \(\eta(R_0)\overline{\eta(R_0n)}=\overline{\eta(n)}\), including zeros. There is no new density factor upon reindexing the forced sublattice. The surviving core weight is \(\sqrt{q_cq_e}\mu(c)\mu(e)\) with the original conjugate \(W_0(q_c/C_*)\) and \(W_0(q_e/E_*)\). Thus MQ17--MQ20 apply without changing any source power.

Retain exactly

\[
(c,e)=(c,E)=(e,B)=(B,E)=1.
\]

The opposite deletion ideals are \(R_1=E,R_2=B\). Own-column intersections \((c,B)>1\) and \((e,E)>1\) remain allowed. M (2.8) supplies no extra \((B,k)\) mask. The outside angular factors \(\xi(B)\overline{\xi(E)}\) are retained until their absolute values are bounded by one.

For \(\kappa=1\) or \(\kappa=\kappa_b\), define the **nominal, cube-pair-dependent** cutoff

\[
\boxed{\Delta_\kappa(B,E)
=\frac{H}{\max(C_*,E_*)^\kappa}.}
\tag{MQ22}
\]

It depends only on the outside cube pair and the original scale \(D,K\), not on the live cores or the projector divisor. Select

* \(q_{d(n)}\le\Delta_1(B,E)\), with \(n\) sixth-power-free away from \(S\); or
* \(q_{d(n)}\le\Delta_{\kappa_b}(B,E)\), with every row repetition.

Pairs whose cutoff is below one have an empty sector. A nonempty sector automatically has \(C_*,E_*\ge1\): when \(\max(C_*,E_*)<1\), MQ22 is at most \(\max(C_*,E_*)^{2-\kappa}/K<1\); otherwise a smaller core scale below one also makes MQ22 below one. Here \(K\ge1\) and \(1\le\kappa<2\).

Use MQ20 with the unchanged sharp original nonunit core intervals, in particular \(q_c,q_e>D^\gamma\). This costs a cube pair by

\[
\frac{q_Bq_E}{H}\,H C_*E_*D^\epsilon
=\frac{D^{2+\epsilon}}{(q_Bq_E)^2}.
\tag{MQ23}
\]

The original \((B,E)=1\) is present before taking this positive bound. Sum the absolutely convergent \(\sum_{B,E}(q_Bq_E)^{-2}\). The selected sector, including all its original column and row tails, is therefore \(O(D^{2+\epsilon})\).

The sharp core cutoff is handled directly by the allowed intervals in the sieve and Hecke partial summation. No artificial principal unit-core pair was added, so no nonprincipal Poisson identity is asserted there. Equivalently, in the numerical ranges below its removal would be a rapid lower-profile error, but that alternative is not needed for the proof.

The union of the two sectors is also paid: use the sixth-power-free sector first and apply the all-repetition bound to its complement. This is a disjoint row-selector decomposition, not an assumption of positivity for the signed C--C form. It can likewise be combined with the previously paid SR sectors by removing their overlap through row-only selectors.

statement:
## 2. Principal characters: all q-smooth powers and moments are required

Fix q. For p larger than every prime factor of q, define

    W_q(x,p-)=sum_(n<=x;P+(n)<p;(n,q)=1)mu(n).

The exact Euler convolution is

    W_q(x,p-)=sum_(d q-smooth) W(x/d,p-),                  (V2)

with W(t,p-)=0 for t<1. Here q-smooth means every prime dividing d divides q, and includes arbitrary powers, not just divisors of the radical. At each ell|q, convolution with 1+ell^(-s)+ell^(-2s)+... cancels the factor 1-ell^(-s); all remaining primes below p keep their original Mobius factors. This proves (V2) coefficientwise, with the natural principal-character zeros retained.

Put A_q(s)=product_(ell|q)(1-ell^(-s))^(-1). For fixed eta in (0,1),

    sum_(q-smooth d>D)1/d <=D^(-eta) A_q(1-eta).

The omitted d>D part of (V2) therefore costs at most xD^(-eta). Choose D=(log p)^B with fixed B sufficiently large for the chosen K. For d<=D, the shift (log d)/(log p) tends to zero uniformly, so the same estimate applies on a slightly larger fixed compact still above K+1. Taylor expansion of omega^(j)(u-log d/log p) and the convergent moments

    sum_(q-smooth d)(-log d)^ell/d=A_q^(ell)(1)

give

    W_q(x,p-)=x sum_(j=1)^K b_(j,q)omega^(j)(u)/(log p)^(j+1)
                   +O_(I,K,q)(x/(log p)^(K+2)),           (V3)
    sum_(j>=1)b_(j,q)z^j=A_q(1+z)/((1+z)zeta(1+z)),
    b_(1,q)=A_q(1)=q/phi(q).

The signs in the Taylor product match because both the shift and A_q's derivative moments carry (-log d)^ell. Completing each truncated moment to all d costs a fixed logarithmic tail and is paid by increasing B. Taylor remainders use finitely many bounded derivatives on the compact neighborhood. The highest needed derivative can have only bounded one-sided jumps there; the preceding derivative is locally Lipschitz, which suffices for the stated remainder. No growing-divisor or growing-q uniformity is used.

This argument applies to the principal character only. It does not justify replacing W_q with a nonprincipal twisted friable sum or retaining the same positive leading factor for such a twist.
title: 2. Principal characters: all q-smooth powers and moments are required

## 11. Strongest obstruction and what was not proved

The saving in Section 5 comes from two actual shorter inverse scales after a common divisor is extracted. The large q label count is precisely canceled by the normalization 1/Nq before its shortened-scale saving is used. This is a legal use of an old moment on its original mu coefficient; it is not a scalar high-bin localization. It removes an actual nontrivial portion of the paired source before pair expansion and gives an explicit limiting complement. This cut is not the old low relative-conductor cut: factors d1=qa,d2=qb give n=q^2ab, while an independently factored n' can have large unique-prime support on both sides. The within-column q may be large while Q1 and Q1/Q3 are also large. This is a statement about permissible factor patterns, not a quantitative high-zero realization.

Small gcd includes the entirely coprime squarefree sector. With no slots and squarefree n, its merged coefficient has the exact form

    (D1D2)^(-1/2) mu(n) nu(n)
      sum_(d|n) W1(Nd/D1) W2(N(n/d)/D2),             (11.1)

with the two independent twists in their respective W factors and the retained dyadic supports. The identity `mu(d)mu(n/d)=mu(n)` does not remove this divisor-profile coefficient. At untwisted nonnegative profiles its divisor weight is nonnegative after the fixed phase `mu(n)nu(n)` is factored out; at independent heights it has a genuinely different divisor phase. Neither case makes it an admitted one-inverse B3.6 coefficient. Natural common-product dependence supplies no identity collapsing (11.1) to the old source moment.

The generic relative squarefree coprime n,n' sector has Q1 comparable to N0^2 and Q2=Q3=1. It survives both (9.1) cuts, and its underlying tuples can also have small within-column gcd. This is an algebraic admissible sector, not a claim that some actual high-zero row realizes its maximal norm. The proven absolute envelope there is `U N0` (up to a subpower), which is far larger than T_mix. This shows why the present positive bounds do not complete the task; it is not a lower bound on the true signed residual and not an impossibility theorem.

An attempted direct use of MI on `mu*mu`, or an average of the two independent witness heights as though they were the same variable, fails at the literal source contract. A common zero creates dependence, not independent rarity. Conversely the exact covariance identity of the two full annular inverse/plain presentations from G147 is retained but does not itself bound this inverse/inverse product. No target-unit cancellation or full norm lower bound is asserted here.

The next consequential estimate is (9.2) on the actual small-gcd, high-Q1 coefficient, or a source identity that genuinely changes that coefficient while paying its complementary terms. A further clean coprime Poisson transform alone retains the same absolute conductor loss and does not supply it. This report leaves that estimate OPEN rather than promoting a partial source gain to a new density or endpoint.

## 4. Development06: a source-exact polylogarithmic Gaussian compression

This develops the viable wildcard instead of allowing all slots to become generic negative examples. It changes the representation of the full fixed Gaussian, not its coefficients or pole return.

Fix tau>0 and a bounded complex coefficient sequence |a(n)|<=1. In the intended application a(n)=f3(n)=mu(rad(n/3^v3(n))) from current G25/G31, including every prime power and its actual prime3 exception. Put

    F_a(x)=sum_(n>=1)a(n)g_tau(log(n/x)), L=log X.

Fix an arbitrary desired error power A>0. Let

    C=sqrt(2tau(A+2)),
    j_-=-ceil(C sqrt L), j_+=ceil(log2+C sqrt L)-1,
    N_X={n in N: j_-<=log(n/X)<j_++1},
    m=ceil(2(A+2)L/log L),
    I_j={n in N_X: j<=log(n/X)<j+1}.                (P1)

Endpoint conventions are literal: all outer and inner cuts are left closed/right open, and the outer cuts are aligned with complete unit log bins. This expands the nominal Gaussian window by less than one unit at either end; the complete tails are still paid below. Empty bins contribute no space. For each nonempty I_j let P_j be the orthogonal projection in the actual finite counting space ell2(I_j) onto the values of real polynomials in t_n=log(n/X)-j of degree<m. If a bin has fewer than m points, take its entire value space. No continuous-density replacement enters this definition. Put P_X=direct_sum P_j, a_X=a|_(N_X), and

    F_X^proj(x)=sum_(n in N_X)(P_X a_X)(n)
                                      g_tau(log(n/x)).

**W43.5.** Uniformly for all coefficient sequences |a|<=1 and x in[X,2X], for all sufficiently large X depending only on A,tau,

    |F_a(x)-F_X^proj(x)| <= C_(A,tau) X^(-A),
    rank(P_X)=O_(A,tau)(L^(3/2)/log L).              (P2)

All discarded source terms, all within-bin residuals and every cross-bin interaction are included in this approximation. It is not a hereditary submask inequality, an unrestricted infinite-column operator estimate, or a claim that the projected coefficients remain bounded by1.

Proof of tails. Below the lower cap, log(n/x)<=-C sqrt L; counting at most X exp(-C sqrt L) terms bounds that tail by X^(1-C^2/(2tau)+o(1)). Above the upper cap, Gaussian integral comparison after n=x exp(v) gives the same exponent. Both are X^(-A-1+o(1)), hence O(X^-A) after a fixed buffer. The bound uses |a|<=1 and needs no arithmetic cancellation.

Proof of projection error. Let c be any real number. On a complex circle |z|=R,

    |g_tau(c+z)| <= (2pi tau)^(-1/2) exp(R^2/(2tau)).

The negative real square has simply been dropped; the inequality is uniform in c. Cauchy's coefficient formula bounds the tail after degree m-1, for0<=t<1 and R=sqrt(tau m)>=2, by

    eps_(tau,m) <= 2(2pi tau)^(-1/2)
                           (e/(tau m))^(m/2).          (P3)

For u=log(x/X) in[0,log2], take c=j-u. The sampled Gaussian vector v_x(n)=g_tau(log(n/X)-u) has a degree<m polynomial approximant on every I_j with pointwise error eps_(tau,m). Since an orthogonal projection has the best ell2 error,

    ||(I-P_X)v_x||_2 <= sqrt(#N_X) eps_(tau,m).

Self-adjointness and ||a_X||_2<=sqrt(#N_X) now imply

    |sum_(N_X)(a_X-P_Xa_X)(n)v_x(n)|
       <= #N_X eps_(tau,m).                           (P4)

Complex coefficients cause no problem: conjugate the real Gaussian vector in the Hermitian pairing. Since #N_X<=2e X exp(C sqrt L) and

    log eps_(tau,m)=-(A+2)L+o(L),

(P4) is X^(-A-1+o(1)). There are at most2C sqrt L+O(1) nonempty bins, each of dimension at most m. This proves both parts of(P2).

**Complete finite target.** Choose any real orthonormal basis q_alpha of range(P_X), each basis vector supported on one original bin, and define the exact signed source moments and readouts

    c_alpha(X)=sum_(n in N_X)a(n)q_alpha(n),
    V_alpha(x)=sum_(n in N_X)q_alpha(n)g_tau(log(n/x)),
    Kproj_(alpha,beta)=integral_X^(2X)
                            V_alpha(x)V_beta(x) dx/x.

Then

    F_X^proj=sum_alpha c_alpha V_alpha,
    ||F_X^proj||_2^2=c* Kproj c.                       (P5)

Kproj is a finite positive Gram matrix, but the off-diagonal source contributions are still signed or complex. Equation(P5) retains all of them. For every fixed gamma>0, (P2) gives equivalence, with arbitrary epsilon allowances, between the full F_a norm bound O(X^(gamma+epsilon)) and the corresponding bound for c* Kproj c. The number of source moments is polylogarithmic; their sizes and correlated phases remain an arithmetic problem.

For literal f3 and fixed gamma>1/2, combine this equivalence with current G28/G29/G31, whose two absolutely summable convolution inverses and small-scale tails are already proved. A bound

    c* Kproj c <<_epsilon X^(2gamma+epsilon)

on every sufficiently large dyadic X excludes zeros in Re(s)>gamma by that exact existing return. No additional Gaussian/H saving is added. The explicit first-gain condition is gamma<.874864; the targets5/6 and3/4 remain available. This is a complete reformulation, not proof of its input.

**A simpler but stronger sufficient input.** The Hilbert-Schmidt estimate on the finite readout W_X gives

    ||W_X||^2 <= sum_(n in N_X)||v_n||_2^2
       <= (log2)/(2pi tau) #N_X = X^(1+o(1)).

Consequently it suffices to prove the positive source-moment bound

    E_X:=sum_alpha |c_alpha|^2=||P_Xa_X||_2^2
       <<_epsilon X^(2gamma-1+epsilon).                (P6)

This requires actual cancellation in every retained polynomial statistic and can be stronger than(P5), because it discards the favorable cross-bin readout interference. It is not claimed necessary. At the limiting present gamma=.874864, the exponent in(P6) is .749728, with a strict decrease and positive buffer needed for an improvement. At gamma=5/6 it is2/3; at gamma=3/4 it is1/2. These are exponents for E_X, NOT the old OPEN-GM normalization or H's .004 deficit despite a numerical resemblance.

The only unconditional bound supplied by bounded coefficients alone is E_X<=#N_X=X^(1+o(1)); this returns gamma=1 and falls short. Thus the deliberately coarse Hilbert-Schmidt estimate is paid, while an improved arithmetic input is explicitly unpaid. No independence, random signs, numerical fit or local PNT is substituted for(P5)/(P6).

**W43.6 (growing-degree baseline calibration).** If the actual sequence additionally satisfies sum_(n<=t)a(n)=O(t^beta) for a fixed beta>1/2, then

    E_X << X^(2beta-1+o(1)).                           (P7)

This pays the growing polynomial degree at the inherited exponent; it creates no saving. Here is an elementary proof avoiding a tacit uniform orthogonal-polynomial constant. A polynomial p of degree<m on[0,1] satisfies

    ||p'||_infinity <= D_m ||p||_infinity,
    D_m=m(2e)^m,

by Lagrange interpolation at the equally spaced nodes j/(m-1): differentiate each Lagrange product, bound each numerator factor by1 and sum denominators using sum_j 1/(j!(d-j)!)=2^d/d!, d=m-1. The bound d!>=(d/e)^d completes it. For m=1 the derivative is0. Near a point of maximal modulus, a one-sided interval of length1/(2D_m) has modulus at least half that maximum. Consequently sup|p|^2<=8D_m integral_0^1|p|^2.

On the COMPLETE unit bin R<=n<eR, summation against the counting function gives

    sum |p(log(n/R))|^2
      =R integral_0^1 |p(t)|^2 e^t dt
         +O(sup|p|^2+Var(|p|^2)).

The error is at most O(D_m^2) integral|p|^2. Here log D_m=O(m)=o(L), while R>=X exp(-C sqrt L-1); hence for all large X the discrete squared norm dominates (R/2) integral|p|^2, uniformly over the bins. Every discrete unit vector q therefore has sup|q|+Var(q) <=R^(-1/2) exp(O(m)). Abel summation, with both sharp endpoints, gives

    |sum_(R<=n<eR) a(n)q(log(n/R))|
      << R^(beta-1/2) exp(O(m)).

Summing squares over the polylogarithmically many basis vectors proves(P7). No source variation is bounded by a continuous-density model; that comparison is used only for the finite polynomial basis norm, with its error explicitly controlled.

For actual f3, the buffered Mobius estimate and the coefficient convolution f3=h*A from G28 give the needed summatory O(t^beta): the h weighted absolute sum converges for beta>1/2. Thus(P7) rigorously calibrates the new finite criterion at every fixed beta>.874864. It leaves precisely the strict exponent improvement unpaid. Alignment of the outer bins in(P1) matters here; it avoids unpriced arbitrarily short terminal bins. This calibration is an additional source-specific interface, not a claim that generic compression cancels parity.

**Connection to the information card and decisive limitation.** If only constants are retained on each bin, then

    ||P_0a_X||_2^2=sum_j |sum_(n in I_j)a(n)|^2/#I_j.

For a real sign source under the uniform law on N_X, this equals #N_X times the exact conditional-bias energy E|E(S|bin)|^2. The higher-degree space in(P1) is an orthogonal polynomial projection, not a conditional expectation onto a sigma-algebra. Distinguishing these is essential. Complete divisor/radical information encodes the f3 sign and leaves bias energy1; the projection must discard enough such information AND have its readout error paid. P3/P4 pay the latter, while P5/P6 state exactly what is missing for the former.

**Ancestry and intended use.** W38 already gives a full parity law, its zero return and an unexposed-parity obstruction. W39's observation theorem already uses optimized Cauchy/Taylor degree of order L/log L. Its original C01 source, W39.22--28, was then read directly: it compresses a signed two-factor product matrix through exp(-uv/tau), paying both weighted l1 masses, and already states that polylogarithmic analytic rank is affordable. Those ideas are credited; the broad compression mechanism is not a fresh discovery. The present concrete adaptation is a single full-source discrete orthogonal projection, its uniform source-to-Gaussian residual, positive source-moment criterion(P6), and explicit no-loss buffered calibration(P7). The elementary rank improvement is not a new arithmetic sector, and the kernel approximation is not claimed novel in the literature.

Functional signature: full fixed bounded-coefficient Gaussian (specialize to actual f3); block orthogonal projection onto discrete log polynomials; cancellation is retained in finitely many signed moments and their complete Gram; first unpaid input is(P5), or stronger(P6); proved return is arbitrary-power approximation and existing G28/G29 zero exclusion conditional on the full finite estimate.

## 9. Every original free Euler shift and the empty-slot end

Keep the exact original coefficient expansion

\[
 X_u\ll_S(U/Y)h_0,\qquad
 \sum_{h_0,h_r}|c_u(h_0,h_r)|h_0^{\delta/2}\ll U^\epsilon,
 \qquad h_0\ll Y.                              \tag{17}
\]

h_r is already charged to the SAME combined-conductor deficit controlling X_u; there is no second charge. Euler restoration only shortens scales and retains its absolute coefficient mass.

For 0<=t<=.001, z_A(t)=z_A(0)-2t/C, so

\[
 \delta t/2+q[z_A(t)-z_A(0)]/2
 =t(\delta/2-q/C)\ge0
\]

because q<=delta/2. For every t>=.001, let b=2y/d-1, with 0<b<=9/50, and use the old comparison

\[
 z_o(t)=\max(0,(b-2t)/(9/2)),\qquad
 S_b(t)=t/2-(b/C-z_o(t))/4.
\]

Before clipping, S_b(t)=7t/18-b(1/C-2/9)/4; after clipping its slope is 1/2. It is continuous and increasing. At the first shift,

\[
 S_b(.001)\ge7/18000-(9/200)(1/C-2/9)
 =2747/15858000>1/6000.                        \tag{18}
\]

The [private research revision] reserve 1/4000 is not reused. Since q<=delta/2 and b/C-z_o(t)>=0,

\[
 \delta t/2+qz_o(t)/2-qz_A(0)/2
 \ge\delta S_b(t)\ge0.
\]

The actual old coefficient 6kappa<=9/2 allows at least this comparison capacity. When it vanishes, apply the ACTUAL unrestricted physical empty-slot theorem at individual scales <=U^2. Indeed h0<<Y makes each nominal reflected exponent <=1+o(1). There is no affine plain-sum condition or extra positive-part loss. ## 6. What the new lower edge changes in the strict ledger

Let the lower slot edge be s and `C=9/2-r`. At the actual geometric point `t=s`, `n1=n2=(1-Cs)/2`, the strictly positive low reserve requires

`a/M>(7/3)rs`.

Substitute its boundary into the high reserve at delta=.7. The result is

`-7/135+s[49/20-(2009/270)r]`.

Hence simultaneous strictly positive low/high reserves require

`r < (1323/2-14/s)/2009`, equivalently **`C>(8379+14/s)/2009`**,

whenever this geometric point belongs to the permitted plain window. At the present `s=17/500`, it does, and the boundary is

```
Ccrit=21349/4879 = 4.375691740110678...,
rcrit=1213/9758,
(a/M)crit=1213/123000,
n1=n2=122151/287000 in (.41,.44).
```

At equality both reserves are zero at that actual point; increasing a makes high negative and decreasing a makes low negative. Thus this is an obstruction to a **fixed strictly positive reserve argument**, including an atlas choosing one amplifier there. It is not a proof that an epsilon-loss moment or an epsilon-dependent construction at equality is impossible. No equality-case theorem is claimed.

For this fixed s the strict range is also sufficient for the same local proof: fix `Ccrit<C<9/2`; choose `k>7r/3` sufficiently close to its lower bound that the continuous high expression is positive at s. One can take k<.3. Its coefficient in t is then positive, so s is the worst continuous point. Choose a sufficiently fine finite ceiling grid to pay `(26/9)k*step`. Low and first-error coefficients are positive (at the lower k boundary the latter is `5r/12`); the others are larger. Also `C-1-9k>Ccrit-3.7>0`, `7k*.04<.084<.25`, and `A<.89`, `a/M<.012` imply a positive uniform high derivative. All terminal costs therefore remain strictly paid for a sufficiently fine fixed grid. This argument is for each fixed C, not a parameter varying with Z.

The explicit thirty-case construction has `C-Ccrit=1051/243950>0`. It does not use a limit. The changed-window gain is balanced by the old short-slot fallback: with safe plain upper bound .423 its strict condition is

`s < (1-2*.423)/(9/2)=77/2250=.034222222...`.

Our .034 edge leaves reserve .001. This is a reusable limitation of that particular safe-envelope fallback, not an impossibility of choosing a sharper safe envelope or another argument. No further tuning is part of this candidate.

statement:
## G202. Centered quotient norm and one fixed cumulative source

Now use a separate ordinary Dirichlet character chi modulo fixed q, with
a(n)=mu(n)chi(n), a(1)=1 and literal natural zeros. Write M(x)=sum_(n<=x)a(n),
psi_chi(y)=sum_(d<=y)Lambda(d)chi(d), and delta=1 for principal chi and
zero otherwise. The exact [[restricted research revision] renewal identity](../[private research revision]/wild55/report.md)
is prior credit:

    R(x)=sum_(d<=x)Lambda(d)chi(d)M(x/d)=-sum_(n<=x)a(n)log n,
    M(x)log x=int_1^x M(t)dt/t-R(x).

For integer N>=2 and floor-invariant f define the centered functional

    J_N(f)=sum_(d<=N)Lambda(d)chi(d)f_floor(N/d)
                     -delta int_1^N f_floor(N/u) du.

The pole-subtraction measure is du. The restored principal term is exactly
N sum_(n<=N)a(n)/n-M(N); it cannot be dropped. Merge equal quotient states
before taking absolute values:

    J_N(f)=sum_(1<=m<N)c_m f_m,
    c_m=psi_chi(N/m)-psi_chi(N/(m+1))-delta N/[m(m+1)].

The lower interval endpoint is strict. State m=N contributes neither a
nonzero discrete atom nor positive continuous length. The exact norm for
|f_m|<=m^beta and f_m=0 at m<=Y, with 0<beta<1, is

    C_(beta,Y)(N)=N^(-beta) sum_(Y<m<N)|c_m|m^beta.

Set D=floor(min(sqrt(N)/4,N/[4(Y+1)])). Each unramified prime power
2<=d<=D has a distinct cell m=floor(N/d)>Y of length
N/[m(m+1)]<=d^2/(N-d)<=1/8, containing d alone. Therefore

    C_(beta,Y)(N)>=2^(-beta-1)
                    sum_(d<=D,(d,q)=1)Lambda(d)d^(-beta)
                  >>_(q,beta) D^(1-beta).

The lower estimate needs only an elementary Chebyshev bound: prime
valuations of binomial(2n,n) give psi(2n)>=2n log 2-log(2n+1), and deleting
the finitely many q-prime-power rays costs O_q(log D). For Y=floor(N^theta),
0<=theta<1, even C/log N grows at least as
N^((1-beta)min(1/2,1-theta))/log N. This is a merged centered norm bound,
not a lower bound for J_N(M), R, or M.

The obstruction survives cumulative inputs with honest natural-zero
increments. For 1/2<beta<1 and 0<alpha<(1-beta)/(2-beta), let

    Q_q(t)=sum_(n<=t)mu(n)^2 1_((n,q)=1)
          =kappa_q t+O_q(sqrt t),
    kappa_q=zeta(2)^(-1) product_(p|q)p/(p+1)>0.

For each unramified prime power d<=N^alpha, put m_d=floor(N/d),
H_d=floor(m_d^beta/8) and
B_d(n)=max(0,H_d-|Q_q(n)-Q_q(m_d)|). The squarefree density formula follows
by inserting sum_(e^2|n)mu(e), counting q-units, and paying every square-divisor
error and tail. It places each bump within m_d+O_q(H_d). The support-width
to nearest-center spacing ratio is O_q(N^(beta-1)d^(2-beta))=o(1).
Supports and increment boundaries are disjoint. Their inverse images
under u->floor(N/u) have width o(1), so each has exactly the integer
contact d; the floor error O(d^2/N) also tends uniformly to zero.

The compact synthetic sum G_N(n)=sum_d conjugate(chi(d))B_d(n) satisfies
|G_N(n)|<=n^beta and |G_N(n)-G_N(n-1)|<=mu(n)^2 1_((n,q)=1).
Every discrete atom contributes Lambda(d)H_d. For principal chi the full
continuous subtraction costs at most half this for sufficiently large N;
for nonprincipal chi it is absent. Thus

    J_N(G_N) >= c N^(beta+alpha(1-beta)) >0.

Independent strengthening: choose N_j increasingly so that each whole
bump block G_j, including its increment boundary, lies above N_(j-1)
and above the preceding support. If F_old is the earlier sum, choose
z_j=J_(N_j)(F_old)/|J_(N_j)(F_old)| when nonzero and z_j=1 otherwise.
Then |J_(N_j)(F_old+z_jG_j)|=|J_(N_j)(F_old)|+J_(N_j)(G_j).
Later blocks change no state sampled at N_j. Hence ONE locally finite
F=sum_j z_jG_j and b(n)=F(n)-F(n-1) satisfy

    |b(n)|<=mu(n)^2 1_((n,q)=1),  |F(n)|<=n^beta,
    |J_(N_j)(F)|>=c N_j^(beta+alpha(1-beta)).

Any fixed finite zero prefix can be prescribed. For principal chi, the
phases may be +/-1 and b(n) belongs to {-1,0,1}. A growing zero prefix
at infinitely many N_j would force F identically zero and is NOT claimed.
Only the cutoff-dependent construction retains that separate property.
Neither construction has the prescribed Möbius signs, multiplicativity,
or the actual inverse-convolution law. Those are the remaining structures
that a successful arithmetic argument must use.
title: G202. Centered quotient norm and one fixed cumulative source

statement:
### 2.1 LP_a and the disk chain

Write h_k=H_(2^k). The author assumes, for every compact K in Re s>a and every epsilon>0, eventually in k,

    integral_K (Re h_k)_+ dA <= C_(K,chi,epsilon) 2^(k epsilon).
                                                               (LP_a)

Closed rectangles from a countable exhaustion suffice because any fixed finite disk chain lies inside one larger rectangle. This is a two-dimensional area hypothesis on the complete sequence, not values on finitely many curves or favorable cutoffs.

1. Positive part of the harmonic function Re h_k is subharmonic. Applying its area mean inequality on fixed disks contained in a slightly larger compact gives a local upper bound Re h_k<=C2^(k epsilon). No lower pressure bound is assumed.
2. At one fixed real b>1, the exact series in(C1) bounds the full complex h_k(b) uniformly in k. Borel-Caratheodory on a disk, in the safe form

       sup_(D(c,R/2))|h_k| <=3|h_k(c)|
                              +2 max(0,sup_(D(c,R)) Re h_k),

   and finitely many overlapping disks propagate this anchor. Hence sup_K|h_k|=O_(K,epsilon)(2^(k epsilon)). Constants and chain length may depend on K and chi. An imaginary constant cannot float because the actual logarithm at b is fixed.
3. f_k=h_(k+1)-h_k is O_b(2^(-k(b-1))) on Re s>=b>1, uniformly in height: the integer tail bounds the prime interval and the continuous integral. Elsewhere every fixed compact has O(2^(k epsilon)) growth.
4. Choose a finite chain with outer4r disks inside Re s>a, successive centers at distance<=r. A2r decay disk at one center contains the next inner r disk. Three-circle interpolation from r to2r inside4r gives

       d_(j+1)=(d_j-epsilon)/2,
       d_j=d_0/2^j-epsilon(1-2^(-j)).                    (C4)

   Taking epsilon<d_0/2^(N+1) before invoking LP for the finite N-step chain makes every d_j positive. Multiplicative constants also propagate, but remain independent of k. A finite cover handles any desired compact.

Thus sum_k f_k converges locally uniformly. Its sum plus h_1 is a holomorphic limit H; Q=exp(H) is nonzero. Applying(C3) proves zero exclusion Re s>a at every fixed height and for every multiplicity. A compact around any finite alleged zero is covered; no unsupported passage from finitely many heights to all heights occurs. Uniformity in growing q or growing height is not claimed. A common a for each fixed ordinary chi, with chi-dependent constants and onset, is exactly the stipulated family scope.

The proposition is correct as stated for1/2<a<1. Its complex-analytic proof actually needs only0<a<1; the1/2 threshold enters the simpler singleton comparison below. This harmless conditional extension does not make LP true at any additional a.

**Necessary qualification of the apparent weakness.** For this exact anchored sequence and its known right-half-plane dyadic decay,

    LP_a  <=>  h_k converges locally uniformly on Re s>a. (C5)

The forward implication was just proved; the reverse follows from local boundedness, which gives LP with an O_K(1) right side. For a>1/2, put

    R_(2,y)(s)=sum_(p<=y)sum_(j>=2)chi(p)^j p^(-js)/j.

R_(2,y) converges locally uniformly and absolutely in Re s>1/2, with all ramified terms zero. The centered singleton sum is

    sum_(p<=2^k)chi(p)p^(-s)-delta J_(2^k)(s)
                                      =-h_k(s)-R_(2,2^k)(s).

Consequently LP_a is also equivalent to local uniform convergence of THIS centered DYADIC prime sum. This is not a proved equivalence between bare zero exclusion and LP, nor an unproved assertion about every intermediate natural cutoff. It explains the relation to W36 R36.21-R36.22: the explicit vacuum and prime-discrepancy return already exist; the new interface replaces an assumed pointwise counting estimate by a one-sided local pressure criterion and pays the analytic continuation. Syntactically permitted subpower growth is forced down to bounded convergence under the other exact hypotheses. No arithmetic exponent gap has thereby shrunk.
title: 2.1 LP_a and the disk chain

### D04.3 Complete zero-exclusion return for each fixed ordinary character

Initially for Re s>1, absolute Fubini gives

    Mellin(F_chi)(s)=exp(tau*s^2/2) D_chi(s),
    D_chi(s)=sum_n f(n)chi(n)n^-s=H_chi(s)/L(s,chi),
    H_(chi,p)(s)=(1-2chi(p)p^-s)/(1-chi(p)p^-s)^2, p!=3,
    H_(chi,3)(s)=(1-chi(3)3^-s)^-2.                    (D04.7)

At p|q these are literally 1. At p>=5 the factors begin at degree two and their Euler product converges absolutely, locally uniformly on Re s>1/2. Their numerators have zeros only on Re s=log_p 2<1/2 when chi(p)!=0; denominators only on Re s=0. Prime 2 is separate: its possible numerator zeros lie on Re s=1. Prime 3 has no numerator. Thus H_chi is holomorphic and nonzero throughout 1/2<Re s<1. This accounts for all exceptional local factors instead of discarding them.

The Gaussian left tail is paid uniformly by the bounded coefficient majorant. Equation (D04.4), dyadic Cauchy-Schwarz and summation show that the Mellin integral is holomorphic on Re s>gamma. Multiplying the identity by L(s,chi), initially where it is defined, continues it to this domain with the usual meromorphic treatment of the principal pole. Any L-zero rho with gamma<Re rho<1 contradicts the nonzero right side exp(tau*rho^2/2)H_chi(rho). The accepted right boundary completes zero exclusion Re s>gamma; the principal pole at 1 is excluded. This is an all-height argument: no moving zero height, finite grid or angular uniformity is substituted.

For chi=1, this agrees with the existing f3/Gaussian return G28--G31. The displayed ordinary-character extension is derived here from its own exact zero-extended coefficient transform. No new finite-order Eisenstein Hecke transfer is proved here; that scope still needs its established exact adapter.

## 5. Uniform audit09: exact parity-layer flux and its unreduced absolute price

This seed tries to couple adjacent squarefree parity layers with factorial weights. The exact source can be derived before testing any Poisson analogy. For every fixed ordinary complex chi, define

    B_k(X)=sum_(n<=X,omega(n)=k)mu(n)chi(n),
    B_j^(p)(Y)=sum_(m<=Y,omega(m)=j,p does not divide m)mu(m)chi(m).

Squareful terms vanish automatically. Every squarefree n with k>=1 prime factors has exactly k representations n=pm with p not dividing m. Each obeys a(pm)=-chi(p)a(m). Hence

    k B_k(X)=-sum_(p<=X)chi(p)B_(k-1)^(p)(X/p).              ([restricted research revision])

Natural zeros remain in both factors; no division by chi occurs. Prime powers cannot be inserted as new squarefree directions. All degrees0<=k<=D_X, where D_X is the actual maximal squarefree degree below X, are retained. Sum([restricted research revision])/k to obtain the complete root flux

    M_chi(X)=1-sum_(p<=X)chi(p)
       sum_(m<=X/p,p does not divide m)
                     mu(m)chi(m)/(omega(m)+1).               ([restricted research revision])

This is an exact deletion-edge normalization, not a new arithmetic estimate. Equivalently, with the full p-free cofactor polynomial

    G_(p,X)(t)=sum_(m<=X/p,p does not divide m)
                            mu(m)chi(m)t^omega(m),

one has

    M_chi(X)=1-sum_(p<=X)chi(p) integral_0^1 G_(p,X)(t)dt.    ([restricted research revision])

Every coefficient, the strict p-free restriction, hard product cap, degree and endpoint is present. There is no independent-prime replacement and no restriction to central degrees. These are finite polynomials, so the integral is literal; no logarithm through a fugacity zero is taken.

The full coefficientwise absolute price of([restricted research revision]) is EXACTLY

    sum_(p,m:pm<=X,p not dividing m)
              |chi(p)mu(m)chi(m)|/(omega(m)+1)
       = #{2<=n<=X:mu(n)!=0,(n,q)=1}.                        ([restricted research revision])

For each nonzero n the k parent edges each have weight1/k. This proves the equality without asymptotics. By W4 it is kappa_q X+O_q(sqrt X)-1. Thus the natural degree normalization removes ordering multiplicity but leaves the entire exponent-one positive mass. It does not make the actual signed sum large. Cancellations between different n or correlated p-free responses are precisely what a useful method must exploit.

Factorial rescaling cannot by itself change this conclusion. Replacing a layer by B_k/k! requires the compensating readout k! to recover M; one must estimate the resulting correlated arithmetic scalar, not declare the normalized coefficients to be a smaller source. The k=1 prime layer is itself unchanged by1!, and central-layer concentration does not settle its compensation by composites. Pair02 word/readout results, W52 W1-W4 and prior factorial-flux constructions are the exact broader ancestry;([restricted research revision])-([restricted research revision]) specialize the full ordinary sharp cutoff and its zero masks.

There is a complete useful approximation interface. For any proposed cofactor polynomials or integrable functions Gtilde_(p,X), put

    Atilde(X)=1-sum_(p<=X)chi(p) integral_0^1 Gtilde_(p,X)(t)dt,
    E(X)=-sum_(p<=X)chi(p) integral_0^1
                                   [G_(p,X)-Gtilde_(p,X)](t)dt.

Then M_chi(X)=Atilde(X)+E(X). Bounds for BOTH complete signed contractions at X^(gamma+epsilon), for every fixed chi and every epsilon/all sufficiently large X with common gamma, yield the Mellin return of section2. If the cofactor approximation depends on X, this formula returns to the fixed source BEFORE continuation. An absolute error bound might suffice but must pay([restricted research revision]) when it treats all edges independently. A favorable variance, central-layer fit, or a small error at each selected prime without its summed price does not prove the required statement.

A related exact log-weight check exposes another easy omission. For the ordinary source,

    a(n)log n=-sum_(p^j|n,j>=1)chi(p)^j log p a(n/p^j).

This follows by comparing the coefficient of each formal log p, including n divisible by p^2: the j=1 and j=2 terms can cancel to restore mu(p^2)=0. Summing and applying Abel summation gives

    M_chi(X)log X=integral_1^X M_chi(t)dt/t
       -sum_(p^j<=X)chi(p)^j log p M_chi(X/p^j).              ([restricted research revision])

The prime-power terms are essential in this different convolution representation, even though the original a has squarefree support. Discarding them is not the same identity as([restricted research revision]), which explicitly excludes p in its cofactor. No spectral contraction or cancellation bound is inferred from([restricted research revision]).

The audit preserves the high-reach idea of estimating an actual signed edge flux. What fails is the specific claim that adjacent-layer bookkeeping, factorial normalization, or independent absolute edge control already supplies a power saving. A complete arithmetic estimate for([restricted research revision])'s signed cofactor responses remains open.

## G148. The unresolved joint estimate and the exact dependence obstruction

OPEN-SEP would bound the actual B_sep mass in (8) by
H_J U^(E_K-xi+epsilon), uniformly in its source quantifiers for some xi>0.
It would give the smaller of xi and 1/2000 after allocating losses.
It is unproved; a c gain also needs the complete raw/positive-child and
physical endpoint return.

A stronger sufficient OPEN-MIX is

    sum_(clean natural free u)|M_-(U^r_-)|^2
                       |M_+(U^r_+)|^2 |Q_u|^2
      << H_J U^(delta(r_-+r_+)+E_K-xi+epsilon).        (9)

It must cover all compatible profiles in (6), the same actual natural
character, one common real parameter and TWO independent inverse heights.
The finite Sobolev derivatives must dominate rowwise suprema. Its positive
row majorant precedes any zero predicate; only the fixed inducing
exceptions already paid above may be omitted. The actual slots, their
relative phases and zero extensions remain. Divide (9) by both inverse
witness lower bounds, never by a possibly zero slot.

Old MI does not supply (9). The merged inverses have a two-divisor
coefficient, schematically mu*mu, with their profiles and shared primes.
It is not the canonical one-inverse column permitted by B3.6. Divisor
boundedness or separated lengths alone cannot grant that source theorem.

Nor do the marginal scalar bounds already force a gain. At v=0 choose

    ell=5/(5-2delta), r_-=2ell/3, m_-=ell/3,
    r_+=ell, m_+=0.

All three relevant marginal exponents equal rho:

    1-delta r_-=1-2delta m_-
               =1/6+(5/6-delta)r_+.

These lengths lie strictly in (6) and outside the easy set at e=rho-eta.
This is a feasible scalar exponent model, not an arithmetic realization
or a counterexample to (9).

Finally, the two full annular sums without the minus sign in (4) obey
T_<+T_>=0 coefficient by coefficient. Against a common nonnegative row
weight their covariance is exactly -||T_<||^2. Multiplying marginal
rarities as if the constructions were independent is therefore invalid.
This exact dependence itself supplies no cancellation saving: both
completed detectors still carry the same constant signal at a zero.
The useful next task is a source-specific joint estimate retaining that
dependence and all shared-prime terms.

No old signed R22 sector or prefix/far cross term has been removed.
Both physical projectors, clipped rectangles, actual label/missing-radical
counts, shortened scales/zero capacity, Euler shifts, extracted errors,
FI/zero/low/far-high branches, raw-root tails, 6a/9a radii,
K_phys^(5/6), principal residue and common-Delta feedback remain under
their existing contracts. The centered M/24 reserve is unspent.

The independent helper's thirteen interval certificates have 53 positive
Bernstein coefficients and three exact identities. Root read the complete
author/review/helpers, certificates and relevant source contracts without
rerunning unchanged helpers. Finite divisor/zero diagnostics are distinct
from the written infinite proof and establish no OPEN-MIX estimate.
Both original lanes stopped and released their own claims. The full
29-family/109-child portfolio, later ideas, near gains,1/6 and1/4 remain.

statement:
## G222. Exact prime-deletion inversion and the full signed readout

Fix an ordinary Dirichlet character chi modulo q and real X>=1. Let D_X
be the squarefree q-units n<=X, including1. It is a divisor downset.
For each unramified prime choose0<rho_p<=1, lambda_p=1-rho_p,
R_p=(2-rho_p)/rho_p. With row d and column n in D_X, define

    B(d,n)=1_(d|n) prod_(p|d)rho_p prod_(p|n/d)lambda_p,
    C(d,n)=1_(d|n) prod_(p|n)rho_p^-1 prod_(p|n/d)(-lambda_p).
                                                               (222.1)

Empty products and0^0 are1. Every intermediate divisor e between d,n
remains in D_X. Expanding BC or CB factors over primes of n/d, giving
the cancellation(lambda_p-lambda_p) at each missing prime and diagonal1.
Consequently both products equal the identity. Absolute column sums give

    ||B||_(1->1)=1,
    V(X):=||C||_(1->1)=max_(n in D_X) prod_(p|n)R_p.          (222.2)

For uniform fixed rho, V=R^K_X, K_X=max_D omega(n). The factorial bound
n>=(omega(n)+1)! implies K_X<=(1+o(1))log X/loglog X, so V=X^o(1).
The size downset is essential: a full prime cube would give the wrong
exponential price. Uniform moving rho_X=(log X)^-b instead costs
X^(b+o(1)); the matching lower factor count follows from primorials and
the ordinary [prime number theorem](https://dlmf.nist.gov/27.12).

For a FIXED prime-dependent sequence, the exact criterion is

    V(X)=X^o(1) iff log R_p/log p ->0.                       (222.3)

Necessity uses the column n=p at X=p. For sufficiency, given epsilon>0
choose P with R_p<=p^epsilon for p>P. Then the product is at most
[prod_(p<=P,p not|q)R_p]n^epsilon. The constant is independent of X.
Thus rho_p=min(1,(log p)^-b), b>0, may tend to0 while inversion remains
subpower. This is different from assigning the SAME rho_X to all primes.
For arbitrary X-dependent choices, the maximum in(222.2), not(222.3),
is the bill. No prime theorem is needed for the fixed-sequence criterion.

Apply B to nu(n)=chi(n) on D_X. The actual output and observer are

    b_X(d)=chi(d)prod_(p|d)rho_p
      *sum_(m<=X/d,(m,dq)=1)mu(m)^2 chi(m)prod_(p|m)lambda_p,
    h(d)=prod_(p|d)(-R_p),
    M_chi(X)=sum_(d in D_X)h(d)b_X(d).                       (222.4)

The cofactor phase chi(m), every natural zero, unit and cutoff remain.
Indeed summing over d|n gives prod_(p|n)(lambda_p-rho_p R_p)=mu(n).
The readout is bilinear, without a conjugation. For ANY full approximant
btilde_X, with e_X=b_X-btilde_X, one has

    |M_chi(X)|<=|sum_d h(d)btilde_X(d)|+V(X)||e_X||_1.       (222.5)

Under(222.3), complete every-epsilon bounds at exponent gamma for BOTH
right-hand quantities before the subpower loss give the same exponent
for M. Under a moving inverse cost X^b, the residual must pay b.
A selected label or omitted error does not have this return. No such
arithmetic approximation has been constructed here.

For one common gamma in(0,1) and every fixed ordinary character, this
Mertens estimate continues s int_1^infinity M_chi(x)x^(-s-1)dx=1/L(s,chi)
normally to Re s>gamma after an epsilon buffer. The continued identity
LF=1 excludes all regular zeros at every finite height. The principal
pole at1 becomes a reciprocal zero; imprimitive zeros and modulus
conventions remain those of [DLMF25.15](https://dlmf.nist.gov/25.15).
Constants and onsets may depend on the fixed character. No growing-q
uniformity or native Eisenstein-source transfer follows.

The inverse is affordable, but positive readout certificates fail in an
exact broader sense. For principal chi, b_X(d)>0, even when some rho_p=1,
because n=d contributes. For ANY moving retentions and positive diagonal
weights w_d,

    P_abs=sum_d |h(d)|b_X(d)
       =sum_(n in D_X)prod_(p|n)(3-2rho_p),
    #D_X<=P_abs<=3^K_X #D_X=X^(1+o(1)),
    ||w h||_2 ||b_X/w||_2>=P_abs.                          (222.6)

The minimum is attained by w_d^2=b_X(d)/|h(d)|. The same lower bound
holds for any conjugate Holder pair. The fixed-q squarefree count
#D_X=kappa_q X+O_q(sqrt X), kappa_q=(phi(q)/q)prod_(p not|q)(1-p^-2)>0,
follows by expanding mu^2 and counting q-units; it needs no PNT.
Thus arbitrary adaptive diagonal weights cannot make this principal
separable certificate power-small. This does not bound the signed readout
from below or exclude nonlocal signed norms or growing signed centering.

Uniform rho also gives the exact cutoff polynomial

    P_X(z)=sum_d b_X(d)z^omega(d)=Z_X(lambda+rho z),
    Z_X(z)=sum_(n in D_X)chi(n)z^omega(n), P_X(-R)=M_chi(X).
                                                               (222.7)

Its circle evaluation costs at most sqrt(sum_(j<=K_X)R^(2j)), subpower
for fixed rho. For principal chi all coefficients are nonnegative and
the prime layer has beta_0+beta_1>=pi_q(X), hence ||P_X||_circle>=pi_q(X)/sqrt2.
Deleting every original degree<=r, for fixed r, does not fix that norm:
products of r+1 distinct primes in((X/2)^(1/(r+1)),X^(1/(r+1))] supply
at least const X/log(X)^(r+1) mass in r+2 nonnegative coefficients.
Their l2 norm is at least mass/sqrt(r+2), uniformly in moving retention.
Other original layers only increase coefficients. This is a norm
obstruction, not an alternating-sum lower bound; signed quotient and
growing-layer methods survive. With varying rho_p there is generally no
single scalar z representing h: retain the labeled/multivariate readout.
title: G222. Exact prime-deletion inversion and the full signed readout

## 7. Reviewer extension: remove the principal far tail exactly

Keep the fixed ordinary chi and parity r above. Fix b=2 and m>=0 once; b>1 also works, but b=2 makes the shell inverse literal. Define

    A_r(T)=I-b^(r+1)T,
    J(t)=P_m(T_b)A_r(T_b)g(t),
    Phi(X)=P_m(D_b)A_r(D_b)E(X).

Since A_r(T_b)t^(-r-1)=0 and A_r(D_b)X^(r+1)=0,

    J=P_m(T_b)A_r(T_b)f,
    Phi=P_m(D_b)A_r(D_b)F
       =sum_(d>=1) mu(d)chi(d)J(d/X).                (N1)

These are exact complete finite-shift identities. In particular the source can be evaluated from F without knowing or subtracting A. No inducing factor is discarded. If b=2 divides the presented modulus, the finite shifts are still literal source shifts: one must not artificially factor out chi(2) or assert that merged output coefficients have the old support. The outer coefficient in (N1) remains exactly mu(d)chi(d), with its natural zeros.

The polynomial P_m annihilates the first m odd regular Taylor monomials. Thus J(t)=O(t^(2m+1)), J'(t)=O(t^(2m)) near zero. Since the constant coefficient of the full dilation polynomial is 1 and every other argument is b^j t with j>=1,

    J(t)=e^(-t)+O(e^(-min(2,b)t)) as t tends to infinity,
    J'(t)=-e^(-t)+O(e^(-min(2,b)t)).                 (N2)

The coefficient of e^(-t) is chi(1)1^r=1. These estimates hold for principal and nonprincipal characters alike. They give global bounds with fixed constants, Phi(X)=O(X) for X>=1, and Phi(X)=O(e^(-1/X)) near zero by its finite-F representation. The latter also follows directly from the exponential tail in (N1).

For 0<gamma<1 put alpha=1-(1-gamma)/(2m+2). For every sufficiently large real x, the exact disjoint split is

    d<=x^alpha;     x^alpha<d<=2x log x;     d>2x log x.

The first part is bounded absolutely by

    C x^(-(2m+1)) sum_(d<=x^alpha) d^(2m+1)
       <=C' x^((2m+2)alpha-(2m+1))=C' x^gamma.

For the last part, (N2) and the geometric series give

    sum_(d>2x log x) |mu(d)chi(d)J(d/x)|
       <=C sum_(d>2x log x)e^(-d/x)=O(x^-1).         (N3)

Integer rounding changes only a fixed constant. Every omitted divisor is covered and no favorable sign is used. Therefore, writing the literal moving middle sum as C_mid(x),

    Phi(x)=C_mid(x)+O(x^gamma),
    C_mid(x)=sum_(x^alpha<d<=2x log x) mu(d)chi(d)J(d/x). (N4)

The moving cuts decompose one fixed profile; they do not define a new Mellin source on each shell. A complete shell L1 sufficient estimate, weaker than a pointwise estimate, is

    integral_X^(2X) |C_mid(x)| dx/x
        <=C_(chi,r,m,epsilon) X^(gamma+epsilon)       (N5)

for every epsilon>0 and every sufficiently large dyadic X. Equations (N3)–(N4) pay the complete low/high contributions by the triangle inequality. They do not infer norm monotonicity from a signed subset. A full L2 bound implies (N5) by Cauchy; if expanding L2, every off-diagonal pair and both orientations must remain.

For m=1 the paid lower exponent and the upper cutoff are:

| gamma | alpha | full upper cutoff | interpretation |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2187135091/2500000000 | 9687135091/10000000000 | 2x log x | current calibration, no strict gain |
| 2187/2500=.8748 | 9687/10000=.9687 | 2x log x | conditional c=.1252 |
| 5/6 | 23/24 | 2x log x | conditional c=1/6 |
| 3/4 | 15/16 | 2x log x | conditional c=1/4 |

The complete (N5), at a common gamma<gamma11 for each fixed ordinary character, is still unproved. No claim is based on optimizing these scalar cuts.

statement:
## G128. Source, prediction and an exact zero census

Fix an ordinary Dirichlet character chi modulo q with natural zero
extension. Write delta=1 for the principal character and0 otherwise,
r=delta*phi(q)/q, A(x)=sum_(n<=x)chi(n), b(t)=A(exp t)-r exp t.
Periodicity gives |b|<=q. Abel summation initially for Re s>1 gives

    H(s)=integral_0^infinity exp(-st)b(t)dt
        =L(s,chi)/s-r/(s-1).

The integral continues H to Re s>0. Use the literal normalized source

    F_chi(s)=((s-1)/(s+1))^delta L(s,chi)/s.       (1)

At the principal pole its removable value is r/2, nonzero. Nonprincipal
characters receive no spurious factor s-1. All natural L-zeros in Re>0
and their multiplicities survive. No Hecke or growing-conductor transfer
is asserted. The causal inverse Laplace source is

    f(t)=b(t)                                       nonprincipal,
    f(t)=r exp(-t)+b(t)-2 integral_0^t exp(-(t-u))b(u)du
                                                   principal. (2)

Thus |f|<=C_q=1+3q. For principal chi, direct substitution gives

    f(log x)=2/x sum_(n<=x)n chi(n)-A(x)
            =A(x)-2/x integral_1^x A(y)dy.            (3)

For q=1 this is m(m+1-x)/x, m=floor x, a bounded nonnegative source.
Positivity is insufficient: the bounded positive delayed exponential
exp(-bt)+C exp(-b(t-T))1_(t>=T), C>1, has Laplace transform
(1+C exp(-sT))/(s+b) and zeros with positive real part log(C)/T.
That is a counterexample to a positivity-only inference, not an
arithmetic lower bound for (3).

Fix0<gamma<1, a=2-gamma, s(z)=gamma+a(1+z)/(1-z). Put
F(z)=F_chi(s(z)), F0=F_chi(2)!=0, the latter by the convergent Euler
product. F belongs to H-infinity since |F_chi(s)|<=C_q/Re s. Define

    f_gamma(t)=exp(-gamma t)f(t),
    h(t)=sqrt(2a) integral_0^t exp(-a(t-u))f_gamma(u)du,
    Qv=v-2a exp(-a t)*v,      ell0(t)=sqrt(2a)exp(-at),

with causal convolution on[0,infinity). Q is an L2 isometry: its boundary
Laplace multiplier is (it-a)/(it+a). Also Q*ell0=0 and ||ell0||=1.
The Cayley Jacobian a/[pi(a^2+t^2)] and Plancherel give exactly

    ||p(Q)h||_2^2=||pF||_H2^2,
    ||p(Q)h-F0 ell0||_2^2=||pF-F0||_H2^2.           (4)

Every output tail and cross term is included. No equivalent positive
metric mI<=P<=MI can give Q*PQ<=kappa P with kappa<1: iterate and
use Q's isometry to contradict m<=kappa^n M. This does not prohibit
source-specific signed polynomial cancellation.

Define the constrained prediction problem

    d_N=min_(p(0)=1,deg p<=N)||pF||^2,
    Delta_N=d_N-|F0|^2=min ||pF-F0||^2.              (5)

The equality follows from the exact constant coefficient. The full
Toeplitz Gram has G_jk=integral conjugate(z^jF)z^kF dm, so its quadratic
form is p*Gp. G is positive definite and d_N=1/(G^-1)_00. Delta_N>=0
decreases, but positivity supplies no convergence to zero.

For a hypothetical zero rho=beta+iT with beta>gamma set
w=(rho-gamma-a)/(rho-gamma+a), nonzero since the anchor2 is safe.
The complete error e=pF-F0 has e(0)=0, e(w)=-F0. Cauchy-Schwarz in zH2
therefore gives

    Delta_N>=|F0|^2(1-|w|^2)/|w|^2
       =4a|F0|^2(beta-gamma)/[(beta-gamma-a)^2+T^2]. (6)

A qualitative Delta_N->0 for each fixed chi at one common gamma
excludes every finite-height zero in Re>gamma. No exchange with a height
supremum is needed. A fixed nonzero residual bound does not suffice,
because the floor decays like T^-2.

The independent review proves the converse for this actual source.
The classical input is canonical inner/outer factorization and outer
cyclicity in H2; see Garcia and Ross, [Theorems2.12,2.16,2.20 and
formula2.10](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1312.5018). For F=IO, the closure of
polynomial multiples is IH2. Any admissible limit Iu has
u(0)=F0/I(0)=O(0), hence norm at least |O(0)|. Outer cyclicity gives
polynomials q_k with Fq_k->IO(0); evaluation at0 shows q_k(0)->1.
Renormalizing by these constants yields admissible approximants. Thus

    Delta_infinity=|F0|^2(|I(0)|^-2-1).             (7)

Here the singular inner factor is absent, for a reason specific to(1).
F continues across every boundary point except1. A singular measure in
its inner factor can be supported only on boundary zeros and1. One
direct justification: on each closed zero-free continued arc, |F| is
bounded below in an inner neighborhood, while |F|<=||F||_infinity
exp(-P[nu]). The Poisson integral of nu is consequently bounded there.
Weak boundary convergence then makes nu absolutely continuous on each
smaller arc; its singular restriction is zero. The remaining boundary
zeros away from1 are isolated and countable, so nu is purely atomic.
An atom c at zeta forces |F(r zeta)|<=||F||_infinity
exp[-c(1+r)/(1-r)]. At zeta!=1 this contradicts a finite-order analytic
zero; at1 it contradicts F_chi(sigma)~1/sigma as sigma->infinity,
which follows from chi(1)=1 and the literal Dirichlet series. Hence
nu=0. This also explains why mere zero-freeness would be insufficient
for an arbitrary bounded analytic source.

The inner factor is therefore exactly the Blaschke product of the
zeros rho_j in Re>gamma. With w_j their Cayley images,

    Delta_infinity=|F0|^2[product_j |w_j|^-2-1].     (8)

The product is positive and convergent by the bounded-source Blaschke
condition and F0!=0; multiplicities are retained. Boundary zeros create
no singular atom. Equation(8) makes Delta_N->0 equivalent to the
desired zero exclusion for this character. It is a precise criterion,
not a claim that the arithmetic difficulty has disappeared.

### A complete and faster source-tail bound

Let H0=sqrt(2a)C_q/(a-gamma), K=1+2a/(a-gamma). Then
|Q^j h(t)|<=H0 K^j exp(-gamma t). The omitted Gram beyond T is PSD
and at most (N+1)H0^2 K^(2N)exp(-2gamma T)/(2gamma) times I. For an
explicit polynomial, its complete squared error is at most

    integral_0^T |p(Q)h-F0 ell0|^2 dt
      +H0^2(sum_j |p_j|K^j)^2 exp(-2gamma T)/gamma
      +2|F0|^2 exp(-2aT).                           (9)

The exponential degree cost can instead be paid by a coherent source
approximation. If ||h-h_tilde||<=tau, the isometry gives

    ||p(Q)(h-h_tilde)||<=tau sum_j |p_j|.           (10)

Every Gram-entry error is <=tau(||h||+||h_tilde||), and its operator
error is at most N+1 times that amount. This is an absolute error,
not a PSD ordering of the two Grams. Even a compactly supported
h_tilde has full filtered future responses, which must be included.

For1/2<gamma<1 put lambda=a-gamma=2-2gamma in(0,1). At q=1, with
u={x}, f(log x)=1/2+B(x)-V(x)/x, B=1/2-u, V=u(1-u). The bounded
primitive of B is V/2, of norm<=1/8. Integrating by parts with its
lower endpoint, then paying V/x absolutely, proves

    |integral_x^infinity y^(lambda-1)(f(log y)-1/2)dy|
        <=D_lambda x^(lambda-1),
    D_lambda=(2-lambda)/[4(1-lambda)].              (11)

Thus h(t)=A0 exp(-gamma t)+C exp(-at)+R(t),
A0=sqrt(2a)/(2lambda), |R(t)|<=sqrt(2a)D_lambda exp(-(gamma+1)t).
Keep h unchanged on[0,T] and continue explicitly by

    h_tilde(t)=A0 exp(-gamma t)
       +(h(T)-A0 exp(-gamma T))exp[-a(t-T)]  for t>T.

Subtracting the expansions at t and T and paying both L2 tails yields

    ||h-h_tilde||<=D_lambda[1+sqrt(a/(gamma+1))]
                            exp[-(gamma+1)T].     (12)

No unknown infinite constant C is needed for this continuation.

All ordinary characters have the same construction. For nonprincipal
chi, A is q-periodic; subtract its mean m_chi. The mean-zero remainder
has primitive bounded by2q^2. For principal chi let B0=A-rx, beta its
period mean, D(x)=integral_1^x(B0-beta). Directly from(3),

    f(log x)=-beta+(B0(x)-beta)+(r+2beta-2D(x))/x.  (13)

The bounds |D|<=2q^2 and |r+2beta-2D|<=1+2q+4q^2 give(11)-(12)
with A0=sqrt(2a)m_chi/lambda and D_chi=4q^2 for nonprincipal chi,
or D_chi=4q^2+(1+2q+4q^2)/(1-lambda) for principal chi. Natural zeros
and complex components are retained. Fixed-q constants are allowed.
The constants blow up at gamma=1/2; no endpoint claim is made.

This adapts [private research revision]'s bounded-periodic-primitive method to the exact
pole-normalized source. It pays source formation, with the coefficient
sum in(10), but leaves the full signed prediction residual OPEN.

### Finite optimization and interpolation do not pay that residual

Every finite constrained minimizer has all roots outside the closed
disk, for any nonzero F with F0!=0. If p=(z-z0)q, variation by zq
preserves p(0)=1. Orthogonality and strict Cauchy-Schwarz for qF,zqF
give |z0|>1. This is classical optimal-polynomial ancestry; see
[Beneteau et al., Theorem3.2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1509.04807), with the
present constrained version proved directly in the retained report.

For F=1-z/r the size-m Gram determinant is sum_(k=0)^m r^(-2k),
so d_N is the ratio of the size N+1 and N determinants. Its limit is
r^-2 for r<1 and1 for r>=1. Grams for r and1/r differ by a scalar,
and hence give identical constrained minimizers despite different
interior zero geometry. For the inner source (z-r)/(1-rz), the Gram is
I while Delta_N=1-r^2. Stable roots and conditioning are insufficient.

If the full error e vanishes at finitely many safe nodes, including0,
form their finite Blaschke product B, including multiplicity. Then
e/B is in H2 with exactly the same norm, and at a hypothetical source
zero w away from those nodes,

    ||e||^2>=|F0|^2(1-|w|^2)/|B(w)|^2.             (14)

There is no extra norm charge for dividing an error already in BH2.
For F=1-z/r, its finite Taylor inverse gives e=-(z/r)^(N+1), so exact
finite matching can coexist with growing full error. Fixed-anchor
amplification at height T costs degree of order T^2/(beta-gamma).
Other node geometries remain eligible only with a paid full residual.
title: G128. Source, prediction and an exact zero census

statement:
### D1d: the second-root inference is valid but only necessary

For a fixed principal character, assume a supplied all-N Mertens bound of exponent1-c for every epsilon, c>0. Then (R5) gives |Q_N(-1)|<=C_epsilon N^(-c+epsilon).

If a squarefree integer has D prime factors, it is at least (D+1)!, because its j-th prime is at least j+1. Integrating log t gives

    deg Z_N<=(1+o(1))log N/loglog N.

Write d=deg Q_N. For sufficiently large N, d=0 is incompatible with the endpoint decay because Q(0)=1; if Q(-1)=0, select that root immediately. Otherwise all roots zeta_j are nonzero and

    |Q_N(-1)|=product_(j=1)^d |1+1/zeta_j|.

Some factor is at most |Q_N(-1)|^(1/d). The direction of the degree inequality is correct: because the logarithm of the product is negative, an UPPER bound on d gives the required upper bound on this factor. Given0<eta<c, first fix a small internal epsilon and then absorb log C_epsilon and the degree o(1). Eventually

    |1+1/zeta_j|<=(log N)^(-c+eta)=delta_N.

Since delta_N<1/2, |zeta_j|<=1/(1-delta_N), hence

    |zeta_j+1|<=2(log N)^(-c+eta).                    (R7)

This root is distinct from alpha_N, which tends to0. Multiplicities and every other deflated factor are retained. One root near-1 is NOT sufficient for a power saving: the remaining product can overwhelm its small factor. The proof is conditional on the supplied Mertens bound; a numerical root plot or a bare zero-free-strip statement is not silently substituted for that input.
title: D1d: the second-root inference is valid but only necessary

statement:
## 5. All core tails and the zero-large-prime class

The zero-large-prime class was not excluded from \(P_z\). If
\(d>Y\) is squarefree \(z\)-smooth, boundedness/support of the restored
\(K\) give at most \(CX/d\) as the absolute sum over all possible \(e\).
Thus either zero-large-prime class costs
\[
 CX\sum_{\substack{d>Y\\d\ z\text{-smooth squarefree}}}d^{-1}
 \ll Xt\,e^{-\log Y/t}.                             \tag{RNR12}
\]
The overlap can be counted twice in this positive upper bound.
Since \(\log Y=\theta L+O(X^{-\theta})\) and
\(L/t\ge\ell_0m^2\), this is \(O_A(XL^{-A})\) for every fixed \(A\).

For the complete one-large-prime pair write \(d=Dp,e=Eq\).
The number of ordered positive integer pairs \(pq\le ex/(DE)\)
bounds its restored prime sum by \(CX(1+L)/(DE)\).
This is valid when a divided scale is subunit too: the actual sum is
then empty. The one-core Rankin bound in §3, summed over either
large core and the unrestricted other core, gives for \(D>U\) or \(E>U\)
\[
 O\!\left(XLt^2e^{-Q/t}\right)=O_A(XL^{-A}).          \tag{RNR13}
\]
All masks remain present until this positive majorant. The bound is
on the restored \(K\); summing absolute \(\ell\)-terms instead would
lose the argument.

For \(D,E\le U=e^{L/m}\), the original lower cuts imply
\[
 p>Y/D\ge \exp((\theta-1/m)L+o(1))>z,
\]
and likewise for \(q\). The extra large-prime inequality is therefore
automatic, not discarded without a check. Furthermore
\(z\ge\exp(\ell_0^2)>(\log B)^{15/2}\) eventually, so every code-small
part of \(Dp\) lies in \(D\). Its uncapped code argument is at most
\[
 \frac{\lambda_0\log D}{h_0\log B}
 \le \frac{\lambda_0}{h_0m}\frac L{\log B}\longrightarrow0 .
\]
Every actual floor \(q_j(d),q_j(e)\) is zero after one sufficiently
large cutoff, uniformly in \(z\). The cutoff can be enormous because
\(h_0\) is small; no effective finite-size assertion is being made.

We obtain the exact-source approximation
\[
 P_z(x)=
 \sum_{\substack{D,E\le U\\D,E\ z\text{-smooth squarefree}}}
    \mu(D)\mu(E)\sum_{\substack{p>Y/D,\ q>Y/E\\p,q\ {\rm prime}}}
          K(DEpq/x)+O_A(XL^{-A}).                   \tag{RNR14}
\]
The thresholds \(Y/D,Y/E\) are real and strict, with the original
floor in \(Y\). Shared core primes and \(p=q\) remain.

RNR12–14 are errors at the asymptotic main-term scale. “Every fixed
logarithmic power” does **not** mean an \(X^{.87449}\) norm bound.
They are not new target-sized pruning errors for a modified source;
the literal full \(P_z\) remains the object throughout.
title: 5. All core tails and the zero-large-prime class

statement:
## 1. Literal input and the marked-plain eligibility bridge

Read PR9 paper B0.3--5, B0.7--9, B0.17--20 and B3.31--47; the decisive PLAIN contract is B3.40, lines 2177--2214. It permits two independent smooth plain profiles and independent heights, with the *same* canonical prime pool, one common slot profile, and individual relative ray characters. With kappa=3/4 its positive assertion is

    n1+n2+(9/2)z <= W
      => sum_eligible |S(Z^n1)S(Z^n2) Q|^2 << Z^(W+eps) H_J.       (MP)

Here W is row width plus presented moving-character width before cancellation, with an arbitrarily small separately charged padding for fixed conductor constants. The kept rows are the source's literal FixedInducingRow exclusion. Arbitrary prime subsets and arbitrary bounded coefficients are NOT included in MP. Those permissions belong to the marked INVERSE theorem and cannot be transferred to MP. The zero-slot assertion permits all nonprincipal inducing characters and unrestricted bounded plain lengths. The accepted incumbent beta_*<=7/8 licenses kappa=3/4; the present zero hypothesis, Re zero >=(1+delta)/2 with delta>=.68, licenses beta_*>=.51. No improved moment on a descendant is used.

The zero detector may choose a different fixed dictionary label from the slot parent. The following re-anchoring is therefore necessary, rather than an implicit arbitrary-coefficient extension.

Fix ONE parent translate from PR15 FixedDictionaryBridge, not a union of unrelated translates. Let its base character be tau0, its original anchor eta0, fixed ray modulus M0 and subgroup H, and original ray-quotient characters theta_i. The literal ideal is

    Q*=internalQ(M0 intersect (72),eta0)
      =M0 intersect (72) intersect q_eta0.

Thus Q* is contained in M0, (72), and q_eta0 in the ideal convention of the source. The original relative coefficient is nu_i=chi_theta_i eta0^(-1). Every possible witnessing label in this translate has, on Q*-units, the form tau0 kappa0 for a fixed Q*-ray character kappa0. The finite list and these representations are chosen before rows and scale.

Use the SAME primitive labels with their Q*-punctured presentations when running the supported-witness construction. This adds no primitive character and no label to the zero maximum: the extra finite Euler factors have no zeros in Re s>0. The natural-character detector already permits these fixed redundant Euler holes (B0.17--20). The conductor multiplier is fixed and absorbed in the explicitly charged fixed-width padding. Crucially, this is a choice made before witnesses, not a row-dependent change of character after seeing a large plain sum.

For the label tau_lambda=tau0 kappa0 set

    eta0'=eta0 kappa0,       nu_i'=chi_theta_i (eta0')^(-1).

Keep M0, H, EVERY theta_i, scale, profile, height and canonical pool unchanged. The pool is defined by the ray class modulo (M0,H), the fixed good-prime conditions and its scale cutoff, not by the anchor. This is also visible in the original profile-transfer-check.md pool definition, lines 17--105. On primes outside Q*, multiplicativity gives literally

    (tau_lambda psi_u)(p) nu_i'(p)
        =(tau0 psi_u)(p) nu_i(p).                         (1)

There is no division by a possibly zero value in this argument. At primes dividing Q*, the ORIGINAL coefficient vanishes: a prime dividing M0 is absent from the canonical good pool; a prime above 2 or 3 has the original m0 bad-prime zero; and a prime dividing q_eta0 has nu_i(p)=0. These exhaust the prime support of Q*. The new Q*-presentations vanish there too. At any other original hole (row radical, canceled moving factor, or common puncture) the same natural zero remains on both sides. Thus (1) is equality of actual prime polynomials, including zero coefficients, not merely equality of primitive characters away from their conductors.

Present kappa0 modulo Q*, retaining all its nonunit zeros, and present eta0' on that modulus. Since Q* is contained in q_eta0, this product presentation has its prescribed fixed modulus dividing Q*. Apply MP with input ideal Qinput'=Q*. Then

    internalQ(Qinput',eta0')=Q*.

The nonzero, proper, (72)-containment and original ray-modulus gates are unchanged. The source whole-row character is now tau_lambda psi_u; its fixed factor is separate from the anchor. No moving child character has been inserted into the anchor. The original ray quotient has not been enlarged and no Fourier character expansion has been used. PR15 FE1 removes a fixed mask from the inducing predicate; FE2 transports that predicate by a fixed Q*-character using an inverse plus its modulus mask, not cancellation at zeros. Consequently the original eligible rows are exactly the needed eligible rows for this MP application. The FI ideal stays Q*.

This proves the anchor bridge for the original finite parent translate. If the whole rectangle is conjugated, conjugate every fixed and live factor and reflect every relevant height. The conjugate ray characters remain characters of the SAME quotient, and the common profile is wholly conjugated. This does not replace conjugate(tau psi_u) by conjugate(tau) psi_u. Both signed orientations remain separate.

There is one further mismatch: the witness plain polynomial has its natural holes, while selected actual slots can have an extra fixed missing-radical puncture R. Write phi_u=tau_lambda psi_u for the COMPLETE witness row character. Do not apply MP with unequal common masks. Expand ONLY those extra slot punctures using the literal second identity B3.41, with its prime-pool support displayed:

    Q_i,R=Q_i,0 - Z^(-z_i/2) sum_(p|R, p in P_i^can) phi_u(p)nu_i'(p)
                         W(Np/Z^z_i)(Np/Z^z_i)^(-sigma_i+iv_i).   (2)

Retain this identity, its minus signs and zero scalars before applying Minkowski to the positive norm. The frozen phi_u(p) factors then have modulus at most one and can be discarded as diagonal contractions. Each remaining live product is an ORIGINAL canonical slot subcollection with its same profile. Its affine length only decreases. The total frozen coefficient mass is Z^o(1), uniformly for polynomial NR, exactly as B3.41; its central factor is comparable to (Np)^(-1/2) on the annulus. If no slots remain, use the old unrestricted zero-slot theorem on the same nonprincipal rows. This proves MP for natural witness plains and the actually punctured marked slots without asserting a mismatched-mask theorem or changing prime coefficients. In the sixth-power lift below, the root and its added holes are fixed before the free-core sum, so the same proof applies.

statement:
## 8. Functional novelty, objections and next mathematical action

Within the inspected JPS/HPR record, the new functional step is
to resolve a divisor common to the TWO extracted labels at the
paired level, freeze it while taking the quadratic norm, and only
then regroup its positive output by the original n before the
cubic mark sieve. JPS18--24 grouped a live v into the actual
quadratic column v e b, retaining length NG; JPS21's early freezing
paid a full independent label triangle. The present pairing permits
length NG/q_t while paying only divisor multiplicity at the later
n stage. The short-core inversion f in JPS7/JPS20 is a different
already established operation.

The paired allocation identity R25 extends the one-source
JPS23 and the actual semiprime cancellation JPS26 to an arbitrary
extracted-label gcd weight. Standard Mobius inversion, the native
Gauss cocycle and the large sieves themselves are not new. The
review makes no literature-priority claim and imports no external
prime-distribution, Hecke, cuspidality or metaplectic hypothesis.
A and B count once for both this mechanism and the common
prime-cofactor contraction.

The strongest analytic objections were checked directly:

1. A hidden T count would arise from estimating each completed
   t norm separately. R16--17 instead sum by t|n while the original
   n remains live for the cubic sieve. The coefficients in R12
   are explicitly independent of n,t,k.
2. A moving row factor would invalidate a premature cubic sieve.
   R14 uses chi_k(tf)^3 only as a FIXED row factor at fixed t,f,
   removes the quadratic row first, and then invokes R17.
3. A missing mark root or incomplete collision projector would
   change the bound. The full Delta inversion supplies
   q_Delta^-1 in energy and q_Delta Omega_Delta in the cubic
   coefficient mass; the cancellation is explicit. No child
   reinstates a (Q,k) projector.
4. A false native source change would replace tm g^3 by m(tg)^3
   or reinterpret its core/corrections. Neither operation occurs.
   The original N,G roots and evaluated extension remain literal.
5. A signed-submask inference would not be justified. The new
   pair mask is expanded exactly and estimated afresh; the sharp
   far mask uses its whole finite Fourier expansion.
6. Prime-cofactor contraction in a single cell would be false.
   R27, not R25, is its coefficient. The unit/composite example
   supplies an exact failure witness.
7. Paying composite counterterms alone does not pay primes.
   R31 shows the original prime scalar remains in the low
   complement with coefficient one.

There is no analytic correction required to BGC1 at this scope.
For integration, attach the following explicit qualifications:

- Use the full-allocation qualification whenever citing BGC13--16
  or HA19--20, and cite HA28/R27 for a fixed label subset.
- Do not describe the paid high-gcd form as a physical H source
  subfamily or as new prime cancellation.
- Count the two branches once. HA17 is valid but dominated by
  the global grouped bound for the same original N.
- The remaining global low-gcd target is equivalent, modulo the
  already paid correction, to the retained original prime target;
  it is not automatically a simpler theorem.

The next genuinely informative mathematical action is narrower
than restating the global target. On the original pressure cells,
retain the literal coprime/small-gcd two-label coefficient R27
with its truncated b factors, original row character and both
marks through a proposed dispersion step. Derive and price a
new covariance identity that uses cancellation unavailable to
the two positive sieves above. Test that identity on the exact
unit/composite and common-prime-core coefficients before spending
time on its tails. If it supplies no bound beyond JPS17/JPS24,
this common-divisor mechanism has exhausted its present gain.
Any successful continuation must separately return the unit
self cell, all unit/nonunit cross cells and every remaining
small-gcd cell, plus the untouched original H obligations.

### B. Literal arithmetic coefficients and readout

Take nu_chi,X(n)=chi(n) on D_X, equivalently mu(n)^2 chi(n) with the full cutoff and zeros. Its output is

    b_chi,X(d)=rho^k(d) chi(d)
       *sum_(m<=X/d, (m,dq)=1) mu(m)^2 chi(m)lambda^k(m).       (A5)

The erased cofactor retains chi(m); replacing it by1 for a nonprincipal character changes the source. Exact inversion of the parity observer f(n)=(-1)^k(n) gives

    h_rho(d)=(-R_rho)^k(d),
    M_chi(X)=sum_(d in D_X)h_rho(d)b_chi,X(d).                  (A6)

Indeed, conditional on a squarefree n, the sum over d|n is
product_(p|n)(lambda+rho*(-R_rho))=(-1)^k(n). Hence every size boundary and complementary deletion pattern is included. Applying B instead to mu(n)chi(n) and reading total mass would preserve M trivially; that is not a smoothing gain.

For an arbitrary approximant btilde_X, keep e_X=b_X-btilde_X as a full signed vector. Then

    M_chi(X)=<h,btilde_X>+<h,e_X>,
    |<h,e_X>|<=R_rho^K_X ||e_X||_1.                           (A7)

For fixed rho, bounds for BOTH the entire first contraction and ||e_X||_1 by X^(gamma+epsilon) for every epsilon>0 imply the same every-epsilon bound for M, after splitting epsilon to absorb (A4). A selected output sector or a low-degree approximation without its full e_X is insufficient. For rho=(log X)^(-b), the residual exponent must instead pay b. This is a complete quantitative adapter, not a proved approximation theorem.

One common gamma<gamma11, for every fixed chi and all large real X, gives the ordinary all-height return through

    F_chi(s)=s integral_1^infinity M_chi(x)x^(-s-1) dx=1/L(s,chi)

initially on Re s>1 and then normally on Re s>gamma. Differentiated integrals converge on every compact after an epsilon buffer. The meromorphic identity L F=1 excludes regular zeros; the principal pole at1 becomes a reciprocal zero. No height-uniform bound or native-H implication is asserted. The analytic/Euler and imprimitive conventions are [DLMF25.15](https://dlmf.nist.gov/25.15). Targets gamma=.87485,5/6,3/4 would give c=.12515,1/6,1/4; the first conditional gain is .0000040364.
