## 6. Distinct lower-order sectors with their full class count

Let u be sixth-power-free away from S. Write u=t a^2 uniquely with t squarefree and a cube-free; there is no condition(t,a)=1. For each fixed t and each b in(10),

    psi_(ta^2)(cb^3)=psi_t(cb^3) psi_a(c)^2 1_((a,b)=1). (15)

The b factor is a row restriction only after taking the positive norm for fixed b. All t-phases, f-phases, marks and punctures stay in the c coefficients. Those coefficients have squared mass <<X^epsilon/q_b^2 on q_c<<X/q_b^3. The n=3 specialization of the imported theorem gives the cube-free cubic operator A+B+(AB)^(2/3). Apply it in the a,c variables, with A=(U/q_t)^(1/2); use Hilbert Minkowski over b. The U-part costs sum_(q_b<=X^(1/3))1/q_b=O(log X), and the B and mixed parts have even more decay. Summing the actual t ideals with q_t<=Delta proves

    sum_(q_u<=U, u six-free, q_t(u)<=Delta)|T_I(X;u)|^2
      <<H_J(UX)^epsilon[(U Delta)^(1/2)+X Delta
                          +U^(1/3)X^(2/3)Delta^(2/3)]. (16)

The unique decomposition includes every row in this sector, with bounded unit multiplicity. Natural zeros when t and a share primes stay in(15). Fixed S-residues give fixed phases and logarithmic counts as before.

Similarly write u=t a^3, where t is cube-free and a squarefree. For fixed t,b, the a-character in(10) is psi_a(c)^3 psi_a(b)^3. The last factor is a scalar of modulus at most one depending only on the row, so it may be dropped in the positive norm. The c columns are squarefree, and PR9 B2.24's quadratic Hecke sieve gives A+B, A=(U/q_t)^(1/3). The same b-Minkowski argument and full t count yield

    sum_(q_u<=U, u six-free, q_t(u)<=Delta)|T_I(X;u)|^2
      <<H_J(UX)^epsilon[U^(1/3)Delta^(2/3)+X Delta].   (17)

In both formulas 1<=Delta<=U. These are applications to the actual completed coefficients and all whole-index marks. They do not estimate arbitrary separately reflected arrays. The important ancestry is [restricted research revision]/MQ4, which already proves the same scalar expression as(16) for a different actual cubic Mobius source. Freezing a growing class and summing it is not a new principle; the present calculation checks its compatibility with(10).

For example X=U^(7/10),Delta=U^(3/10) gives O(U^(1+epsilon)) in both(16),(17), better than(12) on those sectors. But the t>Delta sector remains: generic squarefree u has t=u in both decompositions. It is not sparse merely because small-t classes are paid. Sixth-power repetitions also remain for a full-row claim; apply their exact e-lift and count them, or retain(12). No union of these two paid sectors covers every row, and no c increase is inferred.

### 6.1 Use the existing label average to pay every row repetition

There is a second use of the cubic sieve which DOES retain all sixth-power rows. In literal PR9 B3.6, the squarefree f weight depends only on f, while the puncture, prime lists and all n coefficients are independent of f. For each fixed k apply B2.25 to the f,n pair with character chi_n(f)^4. Both are squarefree; cubic reciprocity/conjugation changes only fixed ray phases. The squared coefficient mass is(7) before its f-dependent phase is inserted, and multiplication by chi_n(k) is a contraction. The bound w(f)<<Z^epsilon permits positive enlargement of this f norm. Summing all O(Z^M) k rows and retaining the original Z^(-V) gives

    E(N,V,M) <<H_J Z^(E_label(M,N,V)+epsilon),
    E_label=M+max{0,N-V,(2N-V)/3}.                    (22)

This is uniform in the actual common puncture even if its norm grows. Unlike the pointwise-in-f bound(8), it is NOT asserted with arbitrary f-dependent column coefficients or f-dependent punctures. No moving label is inserted into a fixed Hecke twist: the entire squarefree label family is summed by the cubic sieve. A common smooth profile is separated on its original ambient box by B3.3, with an absolutely integrable fixed measure, before this argument.

The same estimate holds for the normalized f-average of the completed source(10), with X=Z^N. For fixed b, the phase chi_(cb^3)(f)^4 equals chi_c(f)^4 1_((b,f)=1), including all zeros. The b-phase in the k variable is also a contraction. The c coefficient mass is <<X^epsilon/q_b^2. Thus the joint positive (f,k) norm for this fixed b is bounded by

    H_J(UXZ^V)^epsilon U q_b^(-2)
       [Z^V+X/q_b^3+(Z^V X/q_b^3)^(2/3)].

Minkowski over b costs only a logarithmic power on the first term and convergent series on the others; divide the final squared norm by Z^V. This proves(22) for the complete label-averaged theta source too. In this proof every k row, including principal and pure sixth-power rows, is counted once. Their cancellation is supplied by the actual f-average, not by declaring them absent.

Consequently the canonical norm and the corresponding completed average obey the minimum of(8)/(12) and(22). In particular V>=2N gives O(Z^(M+epsilon)) for ANY N in the fixed polynomial range, with all original whole-index marks and common punctures. At N=M,V=2M this improves the full-row sixth-order exponent7M/6 to M. It also holds at Q=4M, where the older sufficient canonical gate F-M-Q>0 fails. This is a complete, different local mechanism using a neglected existing library component; it needs only PR9's licensed squarefree cubic sieve. No claim of first global novelty is made from absence of this formula in the inspected index. For the original physical compensator, f=1 and V=0, so(22) costs M+N and supplies no gain. Other canonical uses must retain and pay the V<2N complement; no complete physical covering argument was found here.

For the literal canonical target E<=Z^(F+epsilon), F=N+V, formula(8) gives the following complete sufficient gate, independent of Q and of total mark width for each fixed slot count:

    V>=M-N                 for 0<=N<=M/2,
    V>=5M/6-2N/3           for M/2<=N<=M,
    V>=M/6                 for N>=M.                 (23)

Equality is allowed in this direct estimate; an induction demanding a positive reserve must impose its own strict version. Formula(22) improves some interior exponents, but does NOT enlarge(23): E_label<=F is equivalent to V>=max{M-N,M/2,(3M-N)/4}, which implies(23) in each displayed range. This explicit boundary comparison prevents interpreting the paid label average as another automatic MP improvement. The sixth-free version has a different long-column boundary V>=max(0,M/3-N/6) for N>=M; applying that boundary to all rows would omit exactly the repeated-row cost. At V=0, neither new all-row bound reaches the canonical target for any M>0. The original unlabeled canonical branch therefore remains essential, even though the new gate removes Q from some labeled regions.

### F08.R / F26.R — The arithmetic source resolvent

For positive summable weights define
\[
K_w=\sum_{n\ge2}w_n(f_n\otimes f_n),\quad
R_w(\lambda)=\langle1,\lambda(K_w+\lambda I)^{-1}1\rangle.
\]
A08 gives \(R_w(\lambda)\to d_\infty^2\). Thus source-specific \(o(1)\) is an exact alternative to capture. Compact positivity gives no uniform spectral gap; the spectral-mass estimate must include the atom at zero. Exponential weights plus a power resolvent rate force an unnecessarily strong exponential finite-index approximation; polynomial weights \(n^{-1-\alpha}\) are the better first choice.

**New pass 2 refinement, F08.N2:** try dyadic block weights chosen *before* observing the unknown residual, then bound the source spectral measure by a block Schur recursion. The target is an explicit summable tail/resolvent inequality preserving the zero atom, not the smallest eigenvalue of the entire compact operator. Compare its penalty to the admissible residue-wavelet coefficients. This merges two supplied constructions at their exact quantitative obstruction rather than treating compactness as cancellation.

Finite positive truncation gives a certified upper bound on the full resolvent by operator monotonicity. A finite bound yields honest bounded-height zero exclusions through \(R_w(\lambda)\ge2(\beta-\sigma)/|\rho|^2\); it does not give all-height nonvanishing. Conditioning and Gram-entry/tail evaluation must be certified. Randomized-residue criteria carry an independent coefficient-tail condition, which may not be dropped.

### Complete recovery and the raw-main cost

There is no free one-channel inverse. G216's actual O(Y) bound and lambda=2^(r+1)>2 give

    E_m(X)=-sum_(j>=1)lambda^(-j)Phi(2^j X).           (10)

The finite remainder is lambda^(-J)E_m(2^J X)=O(X2^(-Jr)), so every future scale is included and the homogeneous X^(r+1) solution is excluded by a proved source bound. For any beta<r+1, a complete bound ||Phi||_{Lp([Y,2Y])}<=C Y^beta at all sufficiently large dyadic Y implies, for p=1 or 2,

    ||E_m||_{Lp([X,2X])}
       <= C X^beta/[2^(r+1-beta)-1].                  (11)

Minkowski and the geometric series prove (11). Conversely finite shifts give Phi from E_m, and (3) gives Psi. Hence the COMPLETE every-epsilon exponent classes of Phi and the two-channel bank are equivalent. This is a cost calculation for the actual field, not a theorem that every new estimate for (7) is circular or useless.

Using raw F instead of E would hide a much larger problem. For principal chi put U=P_m(D)F, V=U(X/2). Their main coefficient is

    A_m=A product_(j<m)(1-2^(-(r+2j+2)))>0,
    U=A_m X^(r+1)+E_m(X), V=A_m X^(r+1)/lambda+E_m(X/2).

The first quaternion channel U-lambda V is still Phi. Its companion lambda U+V has main term A_m(lambda+lambda^(-1))X^(r+1). Both positive terms on the right side of the raw version of (6) have size X^(2r+2), with identical leading constant. A target X^(2gamma+epsilon) therefore requires relative deficit precision X^(2gamma-2r-2+epsilon) on that raw scale, not just removal of the leading coefficient. For r=2 this is X^(2gamma-6+epsilon). Cross terms involving the O(X) error still cost up to X^(r+2) before exact centering. Formula (1) performs the centering legitimately; the remaining arithmetic deficit in (9) is unpaid.

Under (7), G215's already paid outside-divisor terms and full Mellin identity supply ordinary all-height zero exclusion for Re s>gamma. The numerator Gamma(s)Q_mr(s)L(s-r,chi) has its established nonvanishing in the target strip, including Re s=1; the allowed principal pole is preserved. This uses the scalar Phi bound, not analytic continuation of N(q_X). The possible gain remains conditional on (7). No Hecke, varying-conductor or new independent-height transfer follows.

# Independent recovery review of the partial [private research revision] signed-core packet



## R1. Verdict and useful progress

**Accept the exact complementary-divisor identities S3--S9 and the clean-pair Poisson specialization S10, within their stated scope. The direct canonical-energy shortcut is invalid. No bound for the full signed residual and no larger zero-free constant are proved.**

This review completes the previously unfinished short-prefix estimate S11 from the literal old inverse moment. It proves two narrow consequences, both for the actual completed coefficient:

* With product cutoff L=U^(4/3+lambda), the unmarked positive prefix norm has exponent J=1/6+(5/6-delta)4/3+(1-delta)lambda. On actual buffered-bin rows whose prefix has size at least1/4, the original pointwise slot estimate gives weighted counting exponent J+delta v. For 0<=lambda<=1/2500 and 0<=v<=1/25, this is at most the current E_K-1/5000.
* Keeping the original slots inside the complete positive prefix norm costs5v/3. For the same lambda range and 0<=v<=1/200, that norm too is at most U^(E_K-1/5000+epsilon), with the usual finite smooth and height factors and the retained marked-amplifier mesh.

These are source estimates and a restricted counting implication. They do not delete a signed pair sector from R22. The far-product polynomial remains unbounded in the hard region. For the author's proposed whole v<=1/20 counting ledger, the exact failure at delta=17/25, v=1/20 is

    -228190682/298987653375 = -.000763211053781528... .      (R1)

The accepted source-relative constant therefore remains

    c11=312864909/2500000000=.1251459636,
    theta11=2187135091/2500000000=.8748540364,
    K=28114053/6250000.

K keeps its independently accepted preceding-family ancestry; it is not recalibrated from c11. The old F0/analytic ancestry, positive-slot uniformity, and exact external definition/import/admission obligations remain open. No public theorem, formalization or kernel verification is claimed.

## R2. Frozen evidence and source boundary

The entire author report was read, not just its handoff. Its 20097 bytes have SHA256 `d8dd9f689ae610ae48d8f2c7f120e5b93a4113b3b918f5bbc78426d69899a581`. All four content pins, its freeze SHA256 `abda4a2b90ab99ae14152582b021e9eb14d17d6195abaf80b59596422acfdf5f`, and all seven source pins matched. The author scope and prior review scopes were not changed. The original author has stopped and released its own claim.

The primary source actually inspected is PR9 commit58344dfdbe756cf2f743da1908ffe0582418cf5b, local `[restricted provenance path] mathematical source]`, SHA256 `2b4c67c3e817d7854ee57e451cea1789c8a4a1d03a72ddb83b980421167096d8`. Relevant read slices were lines124--240,242--294,920--1000,1770--1885,2080--2176 and2275--2350: conventions, natural-zero restoration, unmarked amplification and rowwise Sobolev, bin prime bounds, Gauss identities, common profiles, masked primitive Poisson, the exact canonical coefficient contract, MI/UM, and the first Poisson transform.

I also inspected the [restricted research revision] author marked-amplification proof and its frozen independent review, especially the complete restoration, scale supremum and order of profile/mesh choices. This is an already retained input. PR15 `PlainUnmarkedDensity.tex`, lines10--111, supplies the literal natural-row conventions, fixed finite exclusions and explicit ideal count<=128x used below; its bytes are separately pinned in `source-notes.json`. The other immutable sources and the [restricted research revision]/[restricted research revision] accepted review results remain the boundary for their unchanged claims; matching their bytes does not constitute a new transitive analytic proof. Broad/truncated rg output was navigation only. The deterministic helper is newly written in this review scope; no author helper exists or was run.

## R3. Exact convolution identities, including the exclusions

Take the literal smooth V with V=1 on[0,1] and V=0 on[2,infinity), R=U^(4/3), and

    A_R(n)=sum_(d|n) mu(d)V(Nd/R).

For every ideal n other than the unit, sum_(d|n)mu(d)=0. Subtraction and the bijection m=n/d give

    A_R(n)=-sum_(dm=n)mu(d)[1-V(Nd/R)]
          =-sum_(m|n)mu(n/m)[1-V(Nn/(Nm R))].             (R2)

This proof is valid at all valuations. The unit exception is essential: A_R(1)=1 for R>=1, while the displayed complementary sum is zero. In the completed tail n has norm>R, so that exception is absent. A summand in R2 is nonzero only if Nd>R; equality contributes zero. Under Nn<=C L the cofactor therefore satisfies Nm<C L/R, with C retained. No coprimality between d and m has been inserted.

For the actual complete multiplicative natural character phi_u=nu*psi_u in one whole orientation, phi_u(dm)=phi_u(d)phi_u(m) also at shared primes and nonunits. Thus multiplication by phi_u preserves R2 exactly. Every natural zero remains; it is not a coprime-only identity. Original slots can meet either factor.

If all proper divisors of n have norm at most R, their cutoff values are one, giving A_R(n)=mu(n)[V(Nn/R)-1]. This verifies S6 without assuming a least prime norm or an arithmetic density for such n. None of these formulas changes the existing inverse detector or its zero signal.

## R4. Squarefree Gauss transfer and its scope

On good squarefree n, the literal source says

    gamma_1(n)gamma_2(n)=mu(n)alpha(n)G(n),
    a0(n)=conjugate(alpha(n))*gamma_2(n), |gamma_2(n)|=1.

Consequently

    gamma_1(n)=mu(n)G(n)*conjugate(a0(n)),
    A_R(n)gamma_1(n)=G(n)*conjugate(a0(n))*mu(n)A_R(n).   (R3)

The fixed ray function G is not the two-variable Gauss sum. Since n is squarefree, mu(n)mu(d)=mu(n/d), hence

    mu(n)A_R(n)=sum_(m|n)mu(m)V(Nn/(Nm R))
              =-sum_(m|n)mu(m)[1-V(Nn/(Nm R))].          (R4)

The last step again requires n!=1. Both complementary cofactors survive when the two sides of an ordered square are transformed. R4 cannot be transported to arbitrary valuations: for the formal prime-square example n=p^2, R=Np, its left side is0 and its last right side is-1 when Np>=2. R2, which retains mu(n/m), does hold there. The helper records the corresponding n=4,R=2 example.

The new coefficient mu(n)A_R(n) is not a fixed ray character or an original product mark. Its amplitude need not be one: if n is the product of three distinct primes of norms<=R with every pair product norm>=2R, then A_R(n)=1-3=-2 and mu(n)A_R(n)=2. This is an algebraic conditional example, not a claim about a particular prime pool. Even a divisor bound does not meet PR9 B3.6, which explicitly permits no further coefficient on n.

Thus the author's refusal to apply the canonical Gauss energy directly is correct. A later reconstruction may freeze a complementary factor and pay the complete punctures, fourth-power labels, profiles and count, but that reconstruction has not been proved for the whole transformed source here. Treating a moving-modulus Gauss sum as a fixed-modulus character for a second ordinary Poisson application is likewise unjustified.

## R5. Independent reconstruction of the clean first Poisson formula

Let l,l' be coprime good squarefree nonunit ideals, with no slots or extra row selector in this statement. Define xi(k)=chi_l(k)*conjugate(chi_l'(k)) with its zeros and take compact radial Phi. The finite transform modulo ll' has CRT factor

    chi_l(l')*conjugate(chi_l'(l))=R(l,l'),

by the source's sign-valued reciprocity. Its other factors are the unnormalized Gauss sums of chi_l and conjugate(chi_l'). The latter equals the conjugate of the chi_l' Gauss sum at -h. This explains the sign -h without an absolute-value substitution. With source-normalized Gcal, ordinary row Poisson gives

    U/sqrt(Nl Nl') * R(l,l')
      *sum_h Gcal(l,h)conjugate(Gcal(l',-h))
                  F Phi(U Nh/(Nl Nl')).                 (R5)

This is also exactly the clean C=D=1 specialization of B3.52 before column central factors are added. Its U/sqrt(Nl Nl') prefactor includes the two unnormalized Gauss factors; U/(Nl Nl') would be wrong. The source Fourier pairing and lattice measure are retained.

Insert the exact sixth-free row projector sum_(b^6|(u))mu(b), where ideal b uses its primary generator and the residual element retains all six units. Writing u=b^6k gives chi_l(b^6)conjugate(chi_l'(b^6))=1_((b,ll')=1), including the natural zeros. Hence R5 becomes

    U/sqrt(Nl Nl') *sum_b mu(b)/(Nb)^6 *1_((b,ll')=1)
      *R(l,l')*sum_h Gcal(l,h)conjugate(Gcal(l',-h))
             F Phi(U Nh/((Nb)^6 Nl Nl')).                (R6)

Keep the original finite range Nb<=(C_Phi U)^(1/6). There is no multiplicity six for b; the units belong to k. Adding k=0 in Poisson is harmless here because the nonprincipal natural character is zero there. For squarefree l, Gcal(l,h)=gamma_1(l)conjugate(chi_l(h)), including zero at conductor nonunits; the frequency h=0 therefore vanishes. This verifies S10.

Fixed row ray restrictions require their finite character expansion, including the value at b^6. A fixed hole mask requires the full sum over d|rad(E), the factor mu(d)xi(d)/Nd and scale U/((Nb)^6 Nd). A density family omitting fixed-inducing free rows subtracts its actual finite row kernel. None is implicit in R6, and none licenses a zero-bin/amplitude selector as a Poisson weight. General shared support, slots, unequal roots and arbitrary valuations require the full source reconstruction, which R6 alone does not supply.

At l,l' of norm about L, the first dual scale is L^2/U. At L=U^(4/3) it is U^(5/3), larger than L. This is an exact scale obstruction to claiming a short frequency merely from high conductor. It does not preclude a more substantial signed transform.

## R6. A proved positive prefix lemma

Here is the additional source result completed in this review. It uses the accepted PR9 inverse moment, not a new arithmetic hypothesis.

Fix a finite natural dictionary and one whole orientation, smooth V as above, and a smooth prefix H with0<=H<=1, H=1 on[0,1] and H=0 beyond a fixed C>1. Put

    t=4/3, R=U^t, L=U^(t+lambda), Y=U^B,
    P_u(s)=sum_n phi_u(n)A_R(n)(Nn)^(-s)
                      exp(-Nn/Y)H(Nn/L).                (R7)

The n=1 term is omitted, equivalently restrict Nn>R since every other Nn<=R has A_R(n)=0. All n are ideals with the original natural prime support. B and an upper bound for lambda are fixed. No arbitrary growing inverse-coefficient mask is added. The lemma applies to all nonzero sixth-free element rows in a smooth ball, including units; any permissible subset can be removed after the positive norm is formed.

For delta in[17/25,7/10], set a=(1+delta)/2. On the fixed positive-width real interval I_delta=[a,1] and a height interval[-T-1,T+1], let N0(P) be the positive squared tensor Sobolev norm: sum of the squared L2 norms of derivatives partial_sigma^i partial_tau^j, i,j in{0,1}, summed over the free rows with a smooth nonnegative radial majorant. Explicitly,

    N0(P)=sum_free u Phi(Nu/U) sum_(i,j in{0,1})
       integral_(I_delta x[-T-1,T+1])
                       |partial_sigma^i partial_tau^j P_u|^2.

Its constants are uniform for these delta because 1-a>=3/20. Enlarging to finitely many higher derivatives only changes the finite orders. Then, for every epsilon>0,

    N0(P) << H_J U^[J(delta,lambda)+epsilon],
    J(delta,lambda)=1/6+(5/6-delta)t+(1-delta)lambda.     (R8)

H_J denotes fixed finite smooth seminorms and polynomial height cost. Any fixed endpoint constants are retained in these costs, and a sufficiently large final U threshold can follow the fixed dictionary and profiles. Taking a one-sided real interval avoids assuming a zero below the bin's lower endpoint; using a wider interval below a instead would require spending its real buffer explicitly.

Proof. R2 gives the exact finite coupled expression

    P_u(s)=-sum_(Nm<C L/R)phi_u(m)(Nm)^(-s)

because D is at least a fixed multiple of U^(4/3). A ball is handled by its row dyads; the displayed upper bound also pays their smaller scales and the unit window. long-prime norms and both excluded equal-norm orientations, both ordered
good primitive short ideals including equality, the actual complex core
and rational gcd screen, both original mark projectors and independent
heights, original masks and profiles. Its coefficient is
a_H(n)=alpha(n)eta(n)chi_n(lambda)^(-2)gamma_2(n), xi(g)=alpha(g)^3eta(g)^3.
With v_P=u1(P)/sqrt(q_P), w_P'=u2(P')/sqrt(q_P'), the entire signed scalar
kernel gives T=K^transpose, H=w^*Tv and ||v||^2=Omega1, ||w||^2=Omega2.
The raw target is B0 sqrt(Omega1 Omega2),
B0=G K0[N+L+(NL)^(2/3)]P_orig; physical N^(-1)G^(-2) is applied once.
No extra opposite-coprimality screen, selected source, or Mobius substitute
is inserted. The original range and all other branches remain obligations.

For any r>0 the self-adjoint dilation A=[[0,T^*],[T,0]] has a unitary
Cayley transform (A-irI)(A+irI)^(-1), without knowing ||T||<=r. Write

    D=(T^*T+r^2 I)^(-1),
    R=(T^*T-r^2 I)D, J=-2ir TD,
    R=R^*, R^2+J^*J=I, I-R=2r^2 D.

The exact returned input x=(I-R)^(-1)v obeys

    Tv=ir Jx,
    ||Tv||^2=r^2(||x||^2-||Rx||^2)
            =r^2(2Re<x,v>-||v||^2).                       (10)

Thus ||T||<=r iff R<=0, and the source-specific ||Tv||<=r||v|| iff
Re<x,v><=||v||^2. At r=B0>0 the latter suffices for the raw bound against
every allowed w, and is stronger than controlling one scalar pairing.
B0=0 needs that zero pairing directly. No arithmetic estimate for x is
proved. On a singular mode sigma, transmission is2r sigma/(sigma^2+r^2)
while the inverse is(sigma^2+r^2)/(2r^2). Small transmission can coexist
with a very expensive returned input. A known ||T||<=B only gives

For an approximation xhat, retain d=v-(I-R)xhat. The complete scalar is

    H=ir w^*J xhat+w^*T d.                                (11)

The residual is an actual native-source obligation. Compared with [restricted research revision]'s

## Development B: a mixed-direction Koszul bank on the actual radical field

Signature: object = two complete fixed-character radical fields D2 F and D3 F; transformation = commuting length-two Koszul complex with one future and one past inverse; cancellation = exact signed boundary contraction; first unpaid estimate = complete joint signed moment of both actual channels below theta6; proved return = fixed all-shell reconstruction for a3<gamma<1 and original zero exclusion. This develops the selected rare G6-06. Its abstract Koszul vocabulary is not a literature novelty claim.

Assume initially that2,3 are unramified and a3<sigma<1. Put

    b2=2*2^-sigma-1>0, b3=1-2*3^-sigma>0,
    A=b2^2+b3^2, w2=b2^2/A, w3=b3^2/A,
    R(Y2,Y3)=w2 E2^- Y2+w3 E3^+ Y3.                 (B1)

On the complete weighted shell space, exact shifted-shell Minkowski and Cauchy--Schwarz give

    ||R(Y2,Y3)||_sigma
       <= A^-1/2 (||Y2||_sigma^2+||Y3||_sigma^2)^1/2. (B2)

For actual F, R(D2 F,D3 F)=F follows from its accepted beta<1 large-scale boundary and its Gaussian left tail. If either prime is ramified, its D is I; using that channel alone has cost1. The two-channel construction then degenerates coherently and no reciprocal of chi(p)=0 is taken.

The complex and contraction are explicit:

    d0 V=(D2 V,D3 V), d1(Y2,Y3)=-D3 Y2+D2 Y3,
    h1=R, h2 Z=(-w3 E3^+ Z,w2 E2^- Z).

Commutation of dilations/inverses gives d1 d0=0, h1 d0=I,
d0 h1+h2 d1=I, and d1 h2=I. This is exactness with a quantitatively priced homotopy, not a proof that the arithmetic vectors are small.

The global weighted L2 norm uses integral_0^infinity |V(x)|^2 x^-2sigma dx/x. Under u=log x the multiplier of Dp is 1-2chi(p)p^(-sigma-it). The pointwise row pseudoinverse has norm at most A^-1/2. This constant is sharp: simultaneous phase alignment has arbitrarily close solutions since log2/log3 is irrational (no integer powers2^m=3^n), and the phases chi(2),chi(3) are fixed. Long smooth packets localized near such frequencies approach the lower value A. For trivial local phases t=0 already attains it. This sharpness concerns the unrestricted weighted function space, not an arithmetic lower bound or a favorable zero-height selection.

The actual channels are not invented coefficient lists. Writing n=2^k m, m odd,

    D2 F: chi(n) f3(m) times [1,-3,1,1,...] at k=0,1,2,3,...;
    D3 F: chi(n) mu(rad(n)), INCLUDING every prime and power. (B3)

These follow directly from f3(2^k)=-1 for k>=1 and f3(3^k)=+1. Both complete series have bounded coefficients (by3 and1 respectively), local Gaussian tails, and fixed Mellin transforms. The second changes the formerly positive prime3 to the ordinary radical minus sign. Its direct numerator includes N3; its zero line a3 is below both targets3/4 and5/6. The first adds another N2 factor but all its numerator zeros still lie on Re(s)=1. Hence both channels independently detect zeros in theta<Re(s)<1 when theta>a3; the reconstruction is stronger as a complete-field norm statement.

Suppose for each fixed chi and every epsilon>0 the COMPLETE joint channel energy satisfies

    ||D2 F||_[X,2X]^2+||D3 F||_[X,2X]^2
                    <<_(chi,epsilon) X^(2gamma+epsilon), (B4)

at all sufficiently large dyadic X, with a3<gamma<theta6. Use a fixed sigma between gamma and1, as close to gamma as needed; finitely many small shells and Gaussian tails pay the global shell norm. B1--2 return F's every-epsilon exponent gamma and T1 gives the ordinary-character zero exclusion. This includes every signed cross term WITHIN each channel and every original tail. The channel sum is positive and no negative source subfamily is deleted. Conversely the F bound gives B4 by two finite dilation costs; B4 is an equivalent arithmetic target in this range.

At gamma=3/4 the pair cost in B2 is approximately4.44, compared to prime2-only5.29. At5/6 it is approximately4.27, compared to8.17. At theta6 it is approximately3.97, compared to11.04. These are the limiting weight values; every-epsilon proofs use strictly buffered weights. The constants are fixed and improvement in a reconstruction constant is not an exponent gain. Both channel estimates remain OPEN. Cross-channel optimization may give a different target only with its full exact reconstruction and error paid.

Strongest objection: the algebraic homotopy can amount to the old causal bank in new language. G52 indeed supplies the bank/weighted inverse ancestry. The present delta is mixed stable directions with two DIFFERENT critical real parts1 and a3, the accepted large-scale boundary for its future component, and B3's actual all-prime radical channel. It proves no new arithmetic cancellation. The Grassmann/prime-complex selections that merely relabel parity are not counted as this theorem.

## 5. A general dyadic convolution lemma with its left-tail input

For a real alpha and a locally square-integrable function H on
(0,infinity), define

    D_H(T) = (integral_T^(2T)|H(x)|^2 dx/x)^(1/2),
    ||H||_{D_alpha} = sup_{T>0} T^(-alpha) D_H(T).         (5.1)

**Lemma.** Suppose ||H||_{D_alpha}<infinity and

    ||a||_{1,alpha} = sum_{m>=1}|a(m)|m^(-alpha)<infinity.

Then T_a H = sum_m a(m)H(./m) converges in L2 on every compact
subinterval of (0,infinity), and

    ||T_a H||_{D_alpha}
        <= ||a||_{1,alpha} ||H||_{D_alpha}.               (5.2)

If a*b=delta_1 and both weighted coefficient norms are finite,
T_a and T_b are mutually inverse bounded operators on this space.

*Proof.* The change of variable u=x/m gives exactly

    ||H(./m)||_{L2([T,2T],dx/x)} = D_H(T/m)
         <= ||H||_{D_alpha} T^alpha m^(-alpha).

Minkowski's inequality for finite partial sums gives (5.2).
The same estimate applied to tails proves convergence in shell L2,
hence locally in L2. For the inverse assertion, the double series
is absolutely summable in this norm because

    sum_{m,n}|a(m)b(n)|(mn)^(-alpha)
       = ||a||_{1,alpha}||b||_{1,alpha}<infinity.

Its reordering is therefore justified and gives T_b T_a=T_delta_1.
The proof includes every m>T and all of its arguments T/m<1. QED.

### 5.1 From large dyadic shells to all positive scales

Suppose alpha>0, H is locally square-integrable, and

    D_H(2^j) <= C 2^(j alpha)

for all sufficiently large integers j. This does not by itself
control the left tail. Assume additionally that for each fixed N>0,

    |H(x)| <= C_N x^N,                  0<x<=1.          (5.3)

Then ||H||_{D_alpha}<infinity. To see this, first absorb the finite
number of intermediate shells by local square integrability. If
2^j<=T<2^(j+1), the shell [T,2T] lies in the union of the two
dyadic shells starting at 2^j and 2^(j+1). Hence, for T>=1,

    D_H(T)^2 <= C^2(2^(2j alpha)+2^(2(j+1)alpha))
             <= C^2(1+2^(2alpha)) T^(2alpha).             (5.4)

For T<=1/2 choose N>=alpha in (5.3) and integrate x^(2N)
over [T,2T]. This gives D_H(T)<<T^N<<T^alpha. Compact scales
1/2<T<1 cause no problem. This proves the claim and accounts for
both non-dyadic shifts and the entire left tail.

### 5.2 The actual left tails of both fixed fields

Both fields satisfy the stronger uniform bound

    |F_6(x)| + |G_tau(x)|
      <= C_tau exp(-(log x)^2/(2 tau)),       0<x<=1.     (5.5)

Indeed log n>=0, -log x>=0, and

    (log n-log x)^2 >= (log n)^2+(log x)^2.

Use |f_3(n)|=1, |A(n)|<=3 and the finite sum
sum_n exp(-(log n)^2/(2 tau)). For every fixed N>0,

    exp(-(log x)^2/(2 tau))
       <= exp(tau N^2/2) x^N,              0<x<=1,

so (5.3) follows. This is an independently verified input for
each fixed field; no left-tail estimate for a dyad-varying R is
assumed or used.

## 3. Full divisor-bounded tail, including interactions

Here is an independent reconstruction of the needed extension of the
accepted bounded-coefficient lemma. For |v_n|<=A_eta n^eta, eta>0 and
2eta<k-2, let B_M(x)=sum_(n>M)v_n f_x(n). Then

    ||B_M||_2^2 << A_eta^2
        [X^(b(1+2eta))+X^k M^(2-k+2eta)].             (R2)

Use a fixed nonnegative C^2 majorant phi, supported on [1/2,4], equal to
1 on [1,2], with flat support endpoints. Such a function is given by the
accepted product of two quintic smooth steps. Majorize the full positive
square before expansion. With v=u^(-k), A=(n+m)/X^b, the transformed
amplitude is

    phi(v^(-1/k)) exp(-A v^(b/k))/(k v).

Its L1 norm and second derivative L1 norm are bounded uniformly for
A>=0: v is bounded away from zero and infinity on this support, and each
derivative is a fixed polynomial in A times exp(-cA). Thus two integrations
by parts, with their zero boundary terms, give

    |K_phi(n,m)| << min(1,(X^k/|n^k-m^k|)^2), n!=m.

For n>m, the gap is at least n^(k-1)(n-m). With delta=X^k/n^(k-1),
sum_(h>=1)min(1,(delta/h)^2)<<delta, including delta<1. Multiplying by
n^(2eta), summing n>M and including both orientations costs the second
term of (R2). The diagonal retains its damping and is bounded by
sum n^(2eta)e^(-c n/X^b), giving the first term. Prove the expansion on
finite squares first; the displayed summable majorants justify the
infinite limit. This treats every internal tail pair.

For 1/2<gamma<1, integer k>2 and 1<b<=2gamma, put

    r=(k-2gamma)/(k-2), M=X^r.

Then k+(2-k)r=2gamma, so (R2), Cauchy–Schwarz on the finite measure shell,
and eta chosen after epsilon prove

    ||B_M||_1+||B_M||_2 <<_epsilon X^(gamma+epsilon).   (R3)

This remains valid at b=2gamma. For example choose eta smaller than
epsilon/max(b,r,1), also preserving 2eta<k-2. Uniform divisor constants
make the estimate uniform in the changing cutoffs. In a later norm
triangle inequality, the entire tail norm pays its interaction with the
retained core. No signed cross is omitted or declared nonnegative.

    << X^epsilon[N X^(-5/24)+X^6/N^5].                    (193.1)

The diagonal reaches exponent33/40 at N=M, saving1/120 against5/6.
The second term reaches5/6 only at N=M; at N~X it still costs X. The low
interval L<N<X also has only the available trivial X bound. The complete
coarse calculation proves no first gain.

A sufficient one-sided arithmetic input is

    B_(l,x)<=C_epsilon D E^2 X^epsilon (X^(5/6)/N)^2       (OG12)

for EVERY original finite cell, each l and EVERY real x, including N<X and
N~X. The diagonal is already paid since E>>X^(5/12) and (N/L)^2<=X^(2/5).
OG12 would pay the whole cofactor sum and imply OPEN12. Negative B helps;
an absolute-value correlation estimate is stronger than required. Neither is
proved. The available high-block price misses by(M/N)^10; below X the gap
is(N/L)^2. The transition still requires a squared saving X^(1/3).

For general fixed k with balanced cuts and tail r=(k-2gamma)/(k-2), this
particular Cauchy diagonal is paid exactly when

    gamma>=4k/(5k-2).

Strict inequality is required for the coarse derivative non-aliasing test.
At gamma=5/6, degree11 is the smallest integer degree passing that strict
test; degree12 gives more reserve:

| k | Tail exponent r | Cofactor exponent r-gamma | Norm diagonal reserve |
|---|---|---|---|
| 11 | 28/27 | 11/54 | 1/216 |
| 12 | 31/30 | 1/5 | 1/120 |

The threshold tends to4/5, and cannot reach3/4 by this particular diagonal
majorant. This is not an obstruction to the actual signed source, another
norm argument or the1/4 target. Increasing k does not improve the transition
gap X^(2(1-gamma)). Constants are not uniform as k grows.

More generally the COMPLETE analytic core/source transfer holds for fixed
1/2<gamma<1,k>=4 and 2k/(2k-1)<=b<=2gamma. Its cofactor exponent is
k(1-gamma)/(k-2). For a Mellin return with b other than3/2 retain every
A_j(z)D_c(z+(b-1)j), j<K, with

    A_j=(-1)^j Gamma((z+bj)/k)e^(-i*pi*(z+bj)/(2k))/(k j!),
    1-(b-1)K<gamma,

and the accepted finite descending-strip argument. The analytic transfer
does not license omission of these terms or prove its arithmetic hypothesis.
At the current gamma11, degree12's cofactor exponent is .15017515632,
compared with .1877189454 at degree6, without a proved ordering of their norms.

## 5. Complete finite-core return and all-height numerator safety

For b=3/2,k=6 and gamma>=3/4 satisfying u>0, put L=X^gamma. The author
uses the balanced U,V in the exact finite source

    T_p,chi,X(x)=sum_(d>U,e>V,L<de*l<=M)
      mu(d)mu(e)chi(de*l)(1-p 1_(p|l)) f_x(de*l).      (R6)

For any permitted U,V, the n<=L part of R is bounded pointwise by
O_(p,eta)(L^(1+eta)), the n>M part by (R3), S by (R4), and both short
terms as above. Allocating eta after epsilon yields

    ||C_p-T_p,chi,X||_j <<_epsilon X^(gamma+epsilon),
    C_p(x)=sum c_p(n)f_x(n), j=1,2.                  (R7)

This is a full norm comparison; all interactions are paid. It gives
separate every-epsilon equivalences in L1 and L2. L2 implies L1 on the
shell; no reverse implication is supplied.

For completeness, reconstruct the analytic return rather than treating
it as a label. Put delta=b-1. Substitution v=nt in the Mellin integral
of f_(1/t)(n), followed by rotating v to argument -alpha with
0<alpha<min(pi/(2b),pi/(2k)), gives the finite expansion

    I_n(s)=sum_(j<K) A_j(s)n^(-s-delta*j)+R_(n,K)(s),
    A_j(s)=(-1)^j Gamma((s+bj)/k)
              exp(-i pi(s+bj)/(2k))/(k j!).          (R8)

On a compact subset of sigma>0 the remainder is bounded by

    n^(-sigma-delta*K) exp(alpha Im s)
    Gamma((sigma+bK)/k)
      /[k K! sin(k alpha)^((sigma+bK)/k)].           (R9)

Indeed Re(v^b)>0 along this ray, so the Taylor remainder of exp(-z) is
at most |z|^K/K! there; exp(-iv^k) supplies exp(-sin(k alpha)|v|^k).
The contour arcs vanish with these signs and positive real parts. These
bounds are local uniform statements, not a uniform-in-height assertion.
Normal summability after multiplication by |c_p(n)|<=p+1 holds on
sigma>max(0,1-delta*K). Initial absolute Mellin interchange holds for
sigma>b, using the original damping and sum n^(-sigma/b).

With P_p(s)=1-chi(p)p^(1-s), the actual Dirichlet series of c_p is
P_p(s)/L(s,chi). Hence for K=1,b=3/2,k=6,

    H_p(s)=integral_0^infinity C_p(1/t)t^(s-1)dt
      =Gamma(s/6)e^(-i pi s/12) P_p(s)/(6L(s,chi))+E_p(s), (R10)

where E_p is holomorphic for sigma>1/2. The gamma multiplier is
holomorphic and never zero for sigma>0.

Suppose the every-epsilon shell L1 bound X^(gamma+epsilon) holds for
(R6) on every sufficiently large dyadic X, for each of a fixed pair of
distinct primes p1,p2 not dividing q.
Then (R7) gives the same bound for C_p. Dyadic summation, with epsilon
below each compact real-part margin, makes H_p holomorphic on
sigma>gamma, including every finite Mellin derivative. The small-x end
is bounded by (p+1)/(exp(x^(-b))-1), so it is paid completely. Thus
P_p/L is holomorphic on this half-plane.

Every zero of P_p has real part 1. If 1+it is a common zero for p1,p2,
then t log(p_j)/(2pi) is rational, since chi(p_j) is a root of unity.
For t!=0 these are nonzero rationals, so log(p1)/log(p2) would be rational,
contradicting unique prime factorization. At t=0 a common zero requires
chi(p1)=chi(p2)=1. For nonprincipal chi, choose p1 with chi(p1)!=1:
a unit integer with nontrivial character value has such a prime factor.
Choose any distinct unramified p2. For principal chi the only surviving
common zero is s=1, where its ordinary L has its allowed pole, not a zero.

Accordingly any zero of L in sigma>gamma would make one of P_p/L
singular, a contradiction. This covers the entire line sigma=1 without
importing its nonvanishing. Imprimitive Euler holes are present in the
actual L throughout; their real-part-zero zeros are outside this region.
The common gamma is fixed before chi; the two primes, constants and
onsets may depend on that fixed chi. They do not depend on X, epsilon or
a proposed zero. No growing-conductor theorem follows.

For general fixed gamma>1/2, choose k with u>0, 1<b<=2gamma, and fixed K
with 1-(b-1)K<gamma. Every term
A_j(s)P_p(s+delta*j)/L(s+delta*j,chi) in (R8) is retained. Write
F_p=P_p/L. Starting with sigma>1, solve for F_p(s) successively in strips
of width delta using holomorphic H_p, the already known j>=1 shifts,
the normal remainder and nonzero A_0. A finite number of steps reaches
sigma>gamma. The two-prime argument then applies. There is no missing
requirement r<b for the tail estimate: if r>=b the damping only helps.
No statement at gamma=1/2 or for growing k,K is proved.

The exact rows, all CONDITIONAL on the remaining core bound, are:

| c | gamma | r | u | balanced cut exponent | asymmetric cut exponent | cofactor cap exponent |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
|.1252|2187/2500|5313/5000|687/1000|687/2000|687/1000|939/2500|
|1/6|5/6|13/12|7/12|7/24|7/12|1/2|
|1/4|3/4|9/8|3/8|3/16|3/8|3/4|

For each row the cofactor cap is O_(p,q,k)(X^(r-u)); floors prohibit a
unit-constant claim. The first conditional gain over c11 is exactly
135091/2500000000. None of these power premises is proved here.

# Independent W51 review: complete fugacity roots and exact prime-block returns



**Verdict.** Accept D1's isolated-root theorem, its principal full-cutoff consequence, the COMPLETE two-branch equivalent Mertens criterion, and the conditional second-root localization. None supplies the missing arithmetic estimate. Accept D2's arbitrary-partition source/readout identity, chain and cascade identities, and its explicitly restricted absolute prime-endpoint obstruction. Repair its support statement for real U by replacing U+1 with floor(U)+1, or explicitly assuming integer U. Retain S16/S18 as duplicate-level anchored inversions. No increased c follows.

Protected audit S25 constructs the exact prime-block marginal and every induced cutoff interaction. Already two primes produce a missing signed cofactor interval and a linear absolute price for one naive factorization; this does not disprove signed decimation. Uniform audit S19 derives the complete largest-prime renewal and defect return. A pure power inserted without its cofactor state does not test an actual spectral mode of the arithmetic source.

The original c8=.12514261 seed calibration is immutable. Endpoint acceptance is separate controller work; no endpoint, kernel, formalization, growing-conductor or Hecke-family gain is attributed to W51.

## 1. Source, selection and evidence chronology

The frozen author report is28,656bytes, SHA25682a6fcc8aee56cebc7c08045d505841b7187baa018c4a164dc797393b782aacf. Author freeze.json is SHA256413b3692a533756f666a6f414185b3ae341622d43f98e7da281b1a8dd1907b97, dated08:52:23.4357198UTC. Author reported normal own-claim release and absence at08:52:52. Exact source bindings are in source-receipt.json. No author artifact was changed.

All30 seeds, the recipe and compact problem were read before my outcome intake. Source seeds remain28,856bytes, SHA25649e5b066613303f6f2da07e71add4b09bef20233c6f3ebb0d547c59e356aca4c. One earlier acquire invocation failed at argument parsing because acquire does not accept the release-only --sentinel option; no claim mutation occurred, and the corrected acquisition is recorded. No ownership was impersonated.

My seed-only priority and ALL30 pool are SHA256d421500c164eaa1361e1efbaa407cf4f1e6f89ee4df96cd1bf05276f3ccc455f. Priority is

    23,25,28,20,21,04,17,22,14,24,10,29,19,26,08,
    12,13,15,03,30,16,05,18,07,06,01,09,02,11,27.

One secrets.randbelow(30!) rank162122117310635357650942048745306 was saved at08:28:08.534820 before its permutation was decoded. The resulting ALL30 uniform order is

    19,10,23,25,12,08,17,26,15,06,21,11,24,07,14,
    09,20,05,30,03,29,18,04,01,27,13,02,22,16,28.

The inverse rank was verified. audit-order.json is SHA256d4ed9623458baa752a1589b51109fe7761e27445260d54edf44df9e56c5056f4. prep-freeze.json froze at08:29:43.163252, SHA256aff003c48c4524a9fc9201e415ad0981d3f4e9f12c0b082f0269eeae7c265bfb; all five listed preparation files remain unchanged. Only author reservations03/16/23 were known to this critic then. Its random draws had already happened, but their results were not read or used in my preparation.

At08:54:40.740045, the final manifest's six selections03/16/23/18/09/01 were mechanically excluded. Priority skips23 and selects **protected25**; the uniform order starts at **19**, which is distinct and unselected. audit-selection.json is SHA256c8b73384dff625615c03e19491a61f71ad79ba1360e3575fcff9341b1c910a7c. This happened before report intake. The sole author wake included a mathematical abstract; neither ordering nor exclusion rule changed in response. No redraw occurred.

Author sampling also passes independent replay. The literal ALL-group pools have sizes23,11,25; SHA256 counters0,1,2 are accepted and give indices11,0,0, selecting18,09,01. The p<.01 pool correctly includes S09 from group2 and S20 from group4. No numerical group exclusion or replacement is present. The helper requires the exact pool file to exist and match before consuming a draw and refuses an existing draw receipt. Separate pool files/readback hashes and each draw's binding are present; the claimed separate-tool-call chronology is author-recorded, not independently reconstructed native prompt telemetry. The deterministic replay verifies the existing choices, not fresh random samples.

## 2. D1: full polynomial, explicit constants and both branches

Throughout fix one ordinary Dirichlet character chi modulo q, with its original nonunit zeros. Write a(n)=mu(n)chi(n). The complete hard-cutoff polynomial is

    Z_N(z)=sum_(n<=N,mu(n)^2=1)chi(n)z^omega(n)
          =1+A_N z+R_N(z),
    A_N=sum_(p<=N)chi(p),
    B_N=#{n<=N:mu(n)^2=1,(n,q)=1,omega(n)>=2}.       (R1)

Every coefficient obeys the author's bound sum_(k>=2)|C_k|<=B_N<=N. Z_N(-1)=M_chi(N) exactly, including n=1, squareful zeros and ramified zeros. This is not the Euler product over p<=N, which would add integers above N.

### Isolated root: accept with the stated absolute constants

For a polynomial Z=1+Az+R, put lambda=B/|A|^2. Assume |A|>=8 and lambda<=1/8, with sum|c_k|<=B for R=sum_(k>=2)c_k z^k. Since |z|<=1 implies |R(z)|<=B|z|^2, on |z|=2/|A| one has

    |1+Az|>=1,    |R(z)|<=4lambda<=1/2.

Rouche gives exactly one zero counted with multiplicity in that disk. If B>0, on the circle centered at -1/A of radius2lambda/|A|,

    |1+Az|=2lambda,
    |R(z)|<=lambda(1+2lambda)^2<=25lambda/16<2lambda.

This small disk lies inside the first and inside |z|<1. Hence the same unique root alpha is simple, and

    |A alpha+1|<=2lambda,
    (1-2lambda)/|A|<=|alpha|<=(1+2lambda)/|A|.       (R2)

B=0 gives the exact linear root. All other zeros are outside the larger disk, so alpha is the unique nearest root. No unproved reality assumption enters the complex-character case.

Factor the ENTIRE polynomial as Z(z)=(1-z/alpha)Q(z), Q(0)=1. This exact division is important: a truncated reciprocal series would not establish the endpoint formula. From (R2),

    |1+1/alpha|>=4|A|/5-1>=|A|/2,
    |1+1/alpha|<=1+4|A|/3<=2|A|.

Thus

    (|A|/2)|Q(-1)|<=|M(N)|<=2|A||Q(-1)|.           (R3)

The constant checks include the extremal |A|=8,lambda=1/8. These are rigorous inequalities, independently checked also with rational arithmetic; no numerical root approximation is needed.

### Principal characters: an actual whole-cutoff collapse

For chi0 modulo fixed q, A_N=P_N=pi(N)-#{p<=N:p|q}; all C_k are nonnegative integers. The elementary central-binomial argument is correct:

    4^m/(2m+1)<=binom(2m,m)<=(2m)^pi(2m).

For the upper bound each p-adic valuation is a sum of0-or1 terms, at most floor(log(2m)/log p), so each prime contributes at most2m. With m=floor(N/2), fixed q removes only finitely many primes. Consequently

    P_N>>_q N/log N,    lambda_N<=N/P_N^2<<_q(log N)^2/N.

No PNT or distribution of primes in progressions is needed. Eventually the root hypotheses hold for EVERY integer N, not merely a selected face or subsequence. Conjugation and uniqueness make alpha_N real; (R2) then makes it negative and

    alpha_N=-P_N^(-1)(1+O_q((log N)^2/N)).            (R4)

The Taylor series of the local branch log Z_N at0 has radius exactly |alpha_N|. Its derivative Z'_N/Z_N has a nonremovable pole there, while no closer zero exists. Thus no fixed zero-free disk about0 survives, and the straight negative-real path to-1 crosses a zero for large N. This is not a prohibition on every complex path, exact deflation, signed contour or changed smoothing. Fugacity zeros are not L-function zeros.

Using N/log N<<P_N<=N in (R3), the EVERY-EPSILON statements are equivalent:

    M_chi0(N)<<_(q,epsilon)N^(gamma+epsilon)
      iff Q_N(-1)<<_(q,epsilon)N^(gamma-1+epsilon).   (R5)

For the forward implication choose a smaller internal epsilon to absorb log N; the reverse uses P_N<=N. Boundedness of Q_N(-1) therefore gives no subunit Mertens exponent. The full signed deflated endpoint still needs a power decay.

### Complementary characters and all-height return: accept, without deleting a branch

For each N use the root branch exactly when |A_N|>=8 and |A_N|^2>=8B_N. Otherwise

    |A_N|<=max(8,sqrt(8B_N))<=8+sqrt(8N),
    M_chi(N)=1-A_N+R_N(-1).                          (R6)

For fixed1/2<gamma<1, the complete two-branch hypothesis is

    non-root branch: |R_N(-1)|<<_(chi,epsilon)N^(gamma+epsilon);
    root branch:    |A_N Q_N(-1)|<<_(chi,epsilon)N^(gamma+epsilon).
                                                               (OPEN-FD)

It is equivalent to the full all-integer Mertens exponent for this chi: (R6) pays the unit/prime complement at exponent1/2; (R3) handles the root branch with absolute constants. The reverse follows by subtraction in (R6) and the lower inequality in (R3). Arbitrary branch switches are allowed, but every sufficiently large N in BOTH branches is required. It is not enough to prove a principal, density-one, averaged-character or root-branch-only estimate.

The all-height return is complete. If the same gamma works for every fixed ordinary chi and every epsilon, then

    F_chi(s)=s integral_1^infinity M_chi(x)x^(-s-1)dx

is holomorphic on Re(s)>gamma. M_chi(x)=M_chi(floor x), so the integer estimates cover all real x. On each compact subset choose epsilon below its distance from the boundary; derivatives merely introduce integrable logarithms. On Re(s)>1, absolute interchange and (mu chi)*chi=delta give F=1/L. The meromorphic identity L F=1 then excludes zeros throughout the half-plane. A principal pole is a removable reciprocal zero, not an excluded zero; s=0 is outside this positive half-plane. Every fixed height and every imprimitive character is retained. Constants/onsets may depend on chi. There is no growing-conductor or Hecke extension.

OPEN-FD is an exponent-equivalent new representation, not a weaker proved arithmetic estimate. Exact root isolation is mathematically constructive, but neither efficient computation nor an error bound for numerically approximated Q(-1) is supplied.

### D1d: the second-root inference is valid but only necessary

For a fixed principal character, assume a supplied all-N Mertens bound of exponent1-c for every epsilon, c>0. Then (R5) gives |Q_N(-1)|<=C_epsilon N^(-c+epsilon).

If a squarefree integer has D prime factors, it is at least (D+1)!, because its j-th prime is at least j+1. Integrating log t gives

    deg Z_N<=(1+o(1))log N/loglog N.

Write d=deg Q_N. For sufficiently large N, d=0 is incompatible with the endpoint decay because Q(0)=1; if Q(-1)=0, select that root immediately. Otherwise all roots zeta_j are nonzero and

    |Q_N(-1)|=product_(j=1)^d |1+1/zeta_j|.

Some factor is at most |Q_N(-1)|^(1/d). The direction of the degree inequality is correct: because the logarithm of the product is negative, an UPPER bound on d gives the required upper bound on this factor. Given0<eta<c, first fix a small internal epsilon and then absorb log C_epsilon and the degree o(1). Eventually

    |1+1/zeta_j|<=(log N)^(-c+eta)=delta_N.

Since delta_N<1/2, |zeta_j|<=1/(1-delta_N), hence

    |zeta_j+1|<=2(log N)^(-c+eta).                    (R7)

This root is distinct from alpha_N, which tends to0. Multiplicities and every other deflated factor are retained. One root near-1 is NOT sufficient for a power saving: the remaining product can overwhelm its small factor. The proof is conditional on the supplied Mertens bound; a numerical root plot or a bare zero-free-strip statement is not silently substituted for that input.

### Novelty and strongest objection

U-FUGACITY, W07/W09/W22, W30's continued-power branch obstruction, W31 T21/T28 and W34's cluster price are direct ancestry. Independent source reads confirm the distinction: W31 T21 has the full SMALL polynomial1+3z+z^2; T28's shrinking radius1/m is on a selected prime face. W09's physical multivariate instability extends to the full polynomial, but its explicit negative diagonal root belongs to a five-prime FACE and its source explicitly preserves that limitation.

D1 supplies the stated large-N root of the complete ordinary squarefree one-variable polynomial, with constants, and couples its exact deflation to a fully paid character-adaptive criterion. This precise combination was not found in the maintained entries and targeted source passages. Credit is an increment within this record, not a claim of literature priority or new general complex analysis. The binomial, Rouche, factor-product and Mellin principles are standard.

The strongest objection survives: Q_N(-1) and the non-root composite remainder may merely encode the original cancellation less transparently. The report explicitly recognizes that OPEN-FD is equivalent to the original exponent. Neither a path avoiding alpha_N, a bounded Q, one localized root near-1, nor a finite experiment pays the complete arithmetic input.

## 3. D2 and selected duplicates

For C(m,n)=chi(n/m)1_(m|n) and A(m,n)=mu(n/m)chi(n/m)1_(m|n), every intermediate divisor lies inside1..N, so CA=AC=I with natural zeros. For ANY retained R containing1, E its complement,

    S=C_RR-C_RE C_EE^-1 C_ER,
    v=1_R-C_RE C_EE^-1 1_E,
    S^-1=A_RR,    M_chi(N)=e_1^T S^-1 v.             (R8)

C_EE is unit upper triangular even for an interleaved set. Reordering into blocks does not remove the true injection. For a prefix, C_ER=0 but v still contains the deleted source. For N=6,chi=1,R={1,6}, S=[[1,-1],[0,1]], v=(-2,1), and the readout is-1. The two deleted paths1->2->6 and1->3->6 give return2. An acyclic graph can connect different retained vertices through deleted vertices; only a return to the SAME vertex is prohibited. This correctly limits G69's zero-feedback assertion to its chronologically separated causal split.

If an unramified prime p is retained, no strict intermediate divisor exists between1 and p. Thus S(1,p)=chi(p) and S^-1(1,p)=-chi(p). If p is deleted, the coefficient of its arbitrary endpoint input w_p still equals A(1,p)=-chi(p). Exact elimination cannot remove that source coefficient; it can still merge it with OTHER signed endpoint contributions. No lower bound on the whole signed functional follows.

Writing T=C-I gives C^-1=sum_k(-T)^k with T^k=0 for2^k>N. Its coefficients are chi(n/m) times ordered factorizations of n/m into k factors>=2. Counts at6,12,30 are(1,2),(1,4,3),(1,6,6), with signed totals1,0,-1. At a prime only the first layer survives. This is classical incidence inversion and restores individual mu coefficients, not cross-integer cancellation.

For b_U=a1_(n<=U), r_U=delta-b_U*chi, the exact convolution identities are

    a=b_U+a*r_U,
    a=sum_(j=0)^(k-1)b_U*r_U^(*j)+a*r_U^(*k).         (R9)

They include squareful intermediate terms and repeated factors. At principal U=5, r_U(12)=1 and (b_U*r_U)(12)=0; deleting the former because mu(12)=0 breaks the expansion. At prime p>U, r_U(p)=(b_U*r_U)(p)=-chi(p), while r_U^(*j)(p)=0 for j>=2. For k>=2 the first residual layer retains that endpoint.

**Required support correction:** r_U^(*k) vanishes below (floor(U)+1)^k for real U>=1. The author's (U+1)^k is valid when U is integer; its surrounding cutoff proposals do not consistently impose that restriction. The discrepancy is real: for U=3/2,chi=1, r_U(2)=-1 and r_U^(*2)(4)=1, although4<(U+1)^2=25/4. This changes no identity, endpoint obstruction or claimed c; it repairs the exact support statement.

For fixed principal q an absolute certificate itemizing prime endpoints pays at least pi(N)-O_q(1), or pi(N)-pi(U)-O_q(1) in the first residual layer. With U<=N^u, fixed u<1, the binomial lower bound and pi(U)<=U give a price>>N/log N. This obstructs that absolute certificate only. It is not a lower bound for M, for an arbitrarily merged Schur residual, or for weighted Gaussian/native-H observations.

S16's finite future telescope is exact:

    M(x)=b^-J M(b^J x)-sum_(j=1)^J b^-j F_b(b^j x),
    F_b(x)=M(x)-bM(x/b).

The boundary vanishes under its STATED subunit-growth anchor (or M=o(x)); a forcing bound x^gamma, gamma<1, costs1/(b^(1-gamma)-1). For every-epsilon inputs the denominator uses gamma+epsilon after choosing that exponent<1. The source anchor must actually be available; it is not deduced from a strip slogan.

For the principal character modulo1, S18's ordinary jump coefficients at n=1,2,3,6 are1,-3,-4,12; these differ from the dilation weights and from mu. The complete mixed field is M(x)-2M(x/2)-3M(x/3)+6M(x/6). Commutation holds for every function; two anchored future inversions give the product of their fixed costs and no arithmetic estimate. W31/G47/G52/G70/G73 and older future-inverse ancestry retain priority. The ordinary sharp source is an adaptation, not a new inverse family.

## 4. Protected audit S25: decimation with all induced interactions

The high-reach seed proposes integrating out a prime block in a signed squarefree gas while keeping the cutoff. The correct object can be constructed exactly; a positive or independent-product replacement cannot be imported.

Fix a finite block B of distinct primes and P_B=product_(p in B)p. Let a(n)=mu(n)chi(n), with its actual zeros. Define

    H_B(t)=sum_(d|P_B,d<=t)a(d),    H_B(t)=0 if t<1.

Every squarefree n factors uniquely as d m, where d|P_B and (m,P_B)=1. These factors are coprime, so a(dm)=a(d)a(m), including zero cases. Consequently for every real X>=1,

    M_chi(X)=sum_(m<=X,(m,P_B)=1)a(m)H_B(X/m).       (R10)

All d subsets and all remaining cofactors are present. This is an exact finite decimation, not an independence approximation. If B changes with X the identity still holds separately at each X; any quantitative constants and full return then have to be uniform in that changing block.

For two primes p<r, t>=1,

    H_{p,r}(t)=1-chi(p)1_(t>=p)-chi(r)1_(t>=r)
                   +chi(p)chi(r)1_(t>=pr).

Let h_p(t)=1-chi(p)1_(t>=p). The exact induced two-prime interaction is

    H_{p,r}(t)-h_p(t)h_r(t)

## 2. Split into a bank and reconstruct without undoing smoothing

Fix beta below the desired growth exponent, with a fixed positive gap, and
set

    D_lambda F(x)=F(x)-lambda^beta F(x/lambda), lambda=2,3.
    A_beta F=(D_2 F,D_3 F).

On a weighted Mellin line Re(s)=a>beta, write
r_lambda=lambda^(beta-a), q_lambda=1-r_lambda and

    A=q_2²+q_3² >0.

The bank has sharp global weighted-L2 lower bound
||A_beta F||²>=A||F||². An explicit analytic, causal left inverse is

    E_lambda G(x)=sum_(j>=0)lambda^(j beta)G(x/lambda^j),
    w_lambda=q_lambda²/A,
    R_a(G_2,G_3)=w_2 E_2G_2+w_3 E_3G_3,
    R_a A_beta=I.

It uses only past scales; the compact/Gaussian left tails pay the telescoping
boundary. Its exact global weighted-L2 norm is A^(-1/2). For the all-shell
norm N_a(F)=sup_(X>0)X^(-a)||F||_[X,2X], the joint-bank bound is at most
sqrt(2/A), with the extra factor accounting for component suprema occurring
on different shells. Every operator acts as the identity on H.

An every-epsilon growth statement does not imply global weighted integrability
at its limiting exponent. Use N_a directly, or choose a strictly buffered
line and a smaller epsilon before invoking the global frame bound.

This reconstruction is not Gaussian deconvolution. The forbidden reverse
smoothing maps remain unbounded. At beta=a the simple inverse and positive
frame bound fail. Near that boundary the bank inverse costs order
(a-beta)^(-1); a serial product of both filters costs order(a-beta)^(-2).
This is a conditioning advantage of the bank, not an arithmetic power gain.

## 5. The other four first tests

**13, sampled relative homology.** The exact principal relative index is M_chi0(X)-M_chi0(X/Y). Total reduced Betti dimensions satisfy b(K_X,K_(X/Y))>=b(K_X)-b(K_(X/Y)) by the long exact sequence. The explicit cone count then gives a linear lower bound for every fixed Y>1. More generally the sum of unsigned relative Betti masses along ANY finite filtration is at least the endpoint Betti mass minus the starting one. If the starting mass is o(X), finer annuli do not pay the full unsigned bill. Character weighting still needs its commutator. This is a first-test extension of the known topology/persistence obstruction, not an additional development or a rejection of signed annular cancellation.

**26, sampled free-Fock crossing debt.** Words pq and qp represent the same actual squarefree integer with the same coefficient sign and phase. Their summing map is(1,1), norm sqrt2. Averaging a correct coefficient equally over both words makes its input norm1/sqrt2, exactly offsetting the readout price. For k distinct primes there are k! same-phase words. More generally G117's orthogonal-fiber inequality gives a product-of-norms bill at least the number of squarefree units. Distinct-prime word projection retains squareful zeros but does not create cancellation across integers. This is the exact existing sorted-word/G117 obstruction; no new Fock result or free-law arithmetic transfer is credited. A source-specific cross-integer estimate remains eligible.

**16, indefinite signature.** For principal chi, J=diag(mu(n)) on squarefree units has signature M_chi0(N). Every invertible congruence preserves its inertia, so changing divisor-incidence coordinates does not bound the signature. Pairing positive and negative directions into neutral planes leaves at least |M| directions; a power bound for that remainder would itself be a new arithmetic input. For general complex phases, the Hermitian dilation [[0,A],[A*,0]] has symmetric eigenvalues +/- singular values and signature0, regardless of Tr(A). At q=3,N=5 the actual diagonal A is I_3, M=3, while the dilation signature is0. Restoring the signal needs a weighted off-diagonal readout with its own estimate. The proposed signature shortcut therefore fails; an actual arithmetic pairing bound is open.

**20, cutoff polymer cumulants.** For independent formal prime activities z_p,

    Z_X=1+sum_p z_p+sum_(p<r,pr<=X)z_p z_r+...,
    log Z_X=sum_p z_p-(1/2)sum_p z_p^2
                       -sum_(p<r,pr>X)z_p z_r+degree>=3.

Repeated powers in log Z are formal cumulants and must cancel on exponentiation; they cannot be interpreted as new squareful Mobius coefficients. On the high-prime sector p>sqrt X, the exact restricted partition function is1+sum z_p. For r such primes and principal activities z_p=-t, it is1-r t. Its logarithmic Taylor series has radius1/r and cannot be evaluated at t=1 when r>=2. The actual two-prime example X=5,{3,5} already has a zero at t=1/2. The counts r_X are unbounded along a sequence: a uniform bound on #primes in(sqrt X,X] would give pi(X)=O(loglog X) and make sum_p1/p converge. Thus a naive absolute cluster expansion cannot supply an all-large-X theorem.

One may integrate the high-prime clique exactly:

    M_chi(X)=M_chi, P+<=sqrt X(X)
                 -sum_(sqrt X<p<=X)chi(p)M_chi(X/p).

Every high prime occurs at most once; its cofactor is<sqrt X, so shared-prime and squareful issues are paid in this identity. Both the smooth sector and the complete signed high-prime contraction remain. This is largest-prime renewal/G81 ancestry, not a fresh gain. No third extended development was justified after this decisive screen.

g\mid\operatorname{rad}_{=1}(k)\\
q_g\le G,\ q_k/q_g\le K}}

The radical contains only primes of valuation exactly one. This is an equality after summing the full finite orbit: the component switches are permutations/unitary phases. For \(G\le K\), prime rows above \(K\), pure prime squares above \(K\), and pure cubes above \(K\) receive zero weight. A positive ordinary mean through \(KG\) charges rows absent from this incidence. ## 4. Author Sections B–C: exact Jordan source and return

Fix an ordinary character chi modulo q, including its natural zeros. Set chi(-1)=(-1)^a. Choose once r>=2 with r congruent to a modulo 2; r=2 or 3 suffices. Define

    J_r(n)=sum_(d|n) mu(d)(n/d)^r
          =n^r product_(p|n)(1-p^(-r)),
    F(X)=sum_(n>=1) chi(n)J_r(n) exp(-n/X).

Inclusion-exclusion counts primitive r-tuples and proves the coefficient identity, including squareful n. Complete multiplicativity, also when a factor is zero, gives the series L(s-r,chi)/L(s,chi) on Re(s)>r+1. This is a replacement source, not an assertion that J_r retains Möbius support.

Let m_q=phi(q)/q for principal chi and 0 otherwise, A=m_q r!/L(r+1,chi), and E(X)=F(X)-AX^(r+1). The full pole coefficient includes the presented-modulus Euler factors. For t>0,

    H_chi(t)=(sum_(v=1)^q chi(v)e^(-vt))/(1-e^(-qt)),
    f(t)=(-d/dt)^r H_chi(t),
    g(t)=f(t)-m_q r! t^(-r-1).

Absolute convergence before subtraction and of the reciprocal series at r+1 proves

    E(X)=sum_(d>=1) mu(d)chi(d)g(d/X).                (R2)

No conditionally convergent reciprocal or missing Euler correction is hidden in this equality.

Residue reflection gives H_chi(-t)=-chi(-1)H_chi(t) for q>1. For q=1 the additional constant is -1, killed by differentiation. The parity choice makes the regular part of f odd. A principal character is even, so its pole t^(-r-1) is odd as well. Consequently g is regular and odd at zero, g(t)=O(t), g'(t)=O(1). At infinity f,f'=O(e^(-t)), and principal g retains exactly -m_q r!t^(-r-1); nonprincipal g has no algebraic tail. Thus |g(t)|<=C min(t,t^(-r-1)). All constants are fixed-character constants.

It follows unconditionally that E(X)=O(X), and, for real X,

    sum_(d<=X^alpha) |mu(d)chi(d)g(d/X)|=O(X^(2alpha-1)),
    sum_(d>X^beta) |mu(d)chi(d)g(d/X)|=O(X^(r+1-r beta)). (R3)

For 0<gamma<1, alpha=(1+gamma)/2 and beta=1+(1-gamma)/r pay these complete ranges at X^gamma. Nonprincipal characters already allow the upper cutoff C X log X. The whole signed middle, with its literal endpoints and profile, remains unpaid.

The primitive functional equation and trivial-zero description imply L(z,chi*) has no zeros in Re(z)<0 other than its real parity trivial zeros. The inducing-modulus correction is exactly the finite product 1-chi*(p)p^(-z); each nontrivial such factor has its zeros on Re(z)=0. Therefore

    L(s-r,chi) != 0 for 0<Re(s)<=1.                  (R4)

The strip -r<Re(s-r)<=1-r misses those trivial zeros because r has the chosen parity. For q=1 this uses the corresponding zeta fact. Gamma(s), not Gamma(s-r), is regular and nonzero in the target strip. Primary references: [DLMF 25.15.4–8](https://dlmf.nist.gov/25.15) and [25.10](https://dlmf.nist.gov/25.10), read 13 October 2026; the reflection and elementary source estimates above are independently derived. These inputs exclude numerator cancellation at every finite height, not only at real s.

Here is the complete conditional return. For Re(s)>r+1, Mellin(F)=Gamma(s)L(s-r)/L(s). Subtract the principal main term only from the integral over X>=1 and add A/(s-r-1). By E=O(X) this continues initially to Re(s)>1 with its indicated pole. On 1<Re(s)<r+1 it equals the full integral of E, since near zero E=-AX^(r+1)+O(e^(-1/X)). If for every epsilon>0 the complete E obeys O(X^(gamma+epsilon)), that full integral is holomorphic on gamma<Re(s)<r+1. On compact sets choose epsilon below the distance to gamma; logarithmic factors for differentiation are summable. Hence

    L(s,chi) Mellin(E)(s)=Gamma(s)L(s-r,chi).

Equations (R4) and the Euler product rule out zeros with Re(s)>gamma. The principal pole at 1 is retained; the Mellin transform has a compensating zero there. This proof does not assume that an abstract zero-free strip automatically gives a sharp Mertens estimate. Constants need no uniformity as the target imaginary part varies: holomorphy on every compact set establishes every finite height.

To check the author's absolute-price obstruction, use

    Q_q(y)=sum_(n<=y,(n,q)=1) mu(n)^2
          =kappa_q y+O_q(sqrt y),
    kappa_q=(1/zeta(2)) product_(p|q)(1+1/p)^(-1)>0.

This follows by square-divisor inclusion-exclusion, with the finite coprimality factors retained. The function |g| is absolutely continuous and its a.e. derivative is bounded by |g'|; the integral of sqrt(t)|g'(t)| is finite. Stieltjes summation therefore gives the actual full price

    sum_n |mu(n)chi(n)g(n/X)|
       =kappa_q X integral_0^infinity |g(t)|dt+O(sqrt X). (R5)

The integral is positive: a principal kernel has its nonzero algebraic tail, while every nonprincipal kernel has leading e^(-t) since chi(1)=1. This is an actual-source absolute lower asymptotic, not a lower bound for E or M.

For fixed b>1 and m>=0 let T_b g(t)=g(bt), D_b E(X)=E(X/b), and

    P_m(T)=product_(j=0)^(m-1)(I-b^(-(2j+1))T).

The author's K_m=P_m(T_b)g kills the first m odd Taylor powers, has O(t^(2m+1)) at zero and retains the principal algebraic tail. Its Mellin multiplier is product_j(1-b^(-(s+2j+1))), with zeros only on the negative odd real-part lines. The same return applies. The low cutoff becomes alpha=1-(1-gamma)/(2m+2), the old high cutoff remains, and the complete absolute price is again a positive constant times X. Abel summation preserves any already available Mertens exponent; it does not improve it. The bounded toy input n^beta-(n-1)^beta tests the claimed universal exponent bootstrap, not the actual Möbius sequence. For principal r even and 0<beta<1 its Mellin constant is nonzero by (R4) and the multiplier, so the toy retains exponent beta.

statement:
## 3. The conductor factor and bounded-lift counting proof

Choose a fixed bounded fundamental cell for each principal quotient lattice, with `q_h<=C Q` and `q_s,q_s'<=C N`. Rotating this standard cell preserves the constant. This hypothesis does not permit arbitrarily skewed cells or unbounded representatives chosen to change conductors for free.

At a good prime ideal p, set `A=v_p(h)`, `B=v_p(s)` and `B'=v_p(s')`. JN17 and JNR5 give reciprocal prime-variable exponents `3A+2B` and `3A+4B'` modulo six. There is an algebraic proof beyond the 216 tests: `3A` lies in the order-two subgroup `{0,3}` of Z/6, while `2B` and `4B'` lie in its order-three subgroup `{0,2,4}`. Those subgroups intersect only at zero. Therefore each sum vanishes exactly when both its factors vanish:

```
3A+2B=0 mod 6 iff A is even and B=0 mod 3;
3A+4B'=0 mod 6 iff A is even and B'=0 mod 3.
```

At these good, tame primes the nontrivial local residue character has conductor p, and a zero exponent has no good conductor there. Fixed supplementary data affects only the original fixed bad set. Consequently the exact good primitive finite conductors are

```
f1_good=lcm(a2(h),a3(s)),
f2_good=lcm(a2(h),a3(s')),
```

where a2 records odd good valuations and a3 records good valuations nonzero modulo three. Both contain a2(h). This proof includes shared factors of h and s: the cubic factor cannot cancel an odd quadratic factor. A canceled good conductor factor still retains its original imprimitive natural zero; it does not become an unrestricted constant. No ordinary finite-order Hecke theorem for the full angular kernel is inferred.

For `1<=D<=C Q`, let E_D be the nonzero row representatives with `q_a2(h)<=D`. Unique ideal factorization gives

`(h)=a_S * a * b^2`,

with a good squarefree, `q_a<=D`, and a_S one of finitely many squarefree products of fixed bad primes. All arbitrary higher bad-prime powers occur in b^2. For each a_S,a, the norm bound permits at most `O(sqrt(Q/q_a))` ideals b. The Eisenstein class number one and its six units give only a fixed number of generators for each resulting ideal. Thus

```
#E_D <= C_S sqrt(Q) sum_(q_a<=D) q_a^(-1/2)
     <= C_S sqrt(QD).
```

The second inequality follows directly from `#ideals(q<=x)=O(x)` and partial summation: the boundary is O(sqrt(D)) and the integral is `O(integral_1^D t^(-1/2) dt)`. Enlarging from good squarefree a to all ideals is a positive counting bound, not an arithmetic coefficient replacement. For larger D the trivial `#E_D<=Q` is available. This establishes [restricted research revision].3 with no hidden epsilon loss or rational-integer squarefree proxy.

This conductor declaration is local to each frozen prime pair and each chosen integral lift. Pair-dependent Fourier arguments `h/(pi*pi')`, `s/pi`, `s'/pi'` still move. The factorization does not produce a common prime-independent coefficient after regrouping.
title: 3. The conductor factor and bounded-lift counting proof

## 2. Exact completion and rapidly paid complementary fields

Write L=log X, Y=floor(X^.495), b(ell)=(-1)^(ell+1),
m_Y(n)=mu(n)1_(n<=Y), u_Y=mu-m_Y and q_2=delta_1-2delta_2.
Since mu*b=q_2, the exact convolution identity is

    u_Y*u_Y*b=A-2(m_Y*q_2)+m_Y*m_Y*b.                      (G4)

With S_tau(y)=sum_(ell>=1)b(ell)g_tau(log(ell/y)), it gives

    G_tau(x)=R_Y(x)+2L_Y(x)-I_Y(x),
    R_Y(x)=sum_(d,e>Y)mu(d)mu(e)S_tau(x/(de)),
    I_Y(x)=sum_(d,e<=Y)mu(d)mu(e)S_tau(x/(de)).            (G5)

L_Y is the short m_Y*q_2 term, supported at n<=2Y. Shared primes,
zero MÃ¶bius coefficients, both strict lower cuts and every alternating
restoration sign remain literal. The short Gaussian term is not zero.
On [X,2X] it is at most

    O_tau(Y exp(-(.505L-log2)^2/(2tau))),                  (G6)

and hence smaller than every fixed negative power of X. Absolute
convergence before cancellation follows from the d_3(n) majorant.

Here is the estimate that permits growing cutoffs without an unspecified
smoothness constant. Extend h(t)=g_tau(log t) by zero for t<=0. It is
Schwartz and flat at zero. Cauchy's formula on |z-t|=t/2 gives

    ||h^(m)||_1 <= K_tau 4^m m! exp(tau*(m-1)^2/2),
    K_tau=exp((pi^2/8+(log2)^2/2)/tau), m>=1.             (G7)

To check the constant, substitute t=e^v after Cauchy's formula and bound
exp((log2)|v|/tau) by the sum of its two signed exponentials. The two
Gaussian integrals give exactly the extra factor converting 2^m to4^m.
Alternating Poisson summation samples half-integers, so for m>=2,

    |S_tau(y)| <=2K_tau zeta(m)(4/pi)^m m!
       *exp(-(m-1)log y+tau*(m-1)^2/2).                  (G8)

Complete the ell sum before imposing an ell cutoff. With one common
order m=1+floor(.01L/tau), G8 pays I_Y by
exp(-(.01L)^2/(2tau)+O_tau(L log L)), including its Y^2 ordered labels.

For a fixed kappa>0, one common order
m=1+floor(kappa*sqrt L/tau) instead proves

    sum_(d,e>Y,de<=X exp(-kappa sqrt L))
       |mu(d)mu(e)S_tau(x/(de))|
       <= X^(1-kappa^2/(2tau)+o(1)).                     (G9)

The same estimate allows any bounded multiplier independent of ell.
It is not hereditary under arbitrary ell-dependent masks.

For fixed C>0 put B_X=2X exp(C sqrt L). Since
sum_(n<=t)d_3(n)<=t(1+log t)^2, Gaussian tail integration gives

    sum_(n>B_X)d_3(n)g_tau(log(n/x))
       <= X^(1-C^2/(2tau)+o(1))                         (G10)

uniformly on [X,2X]. This pays all omitted labels, including interacting
groups. No assumed cancellation occurs in this tail.

### 3.2 Quadratic sieve with t fixed

After the specified common profile separation, the fixed-t,f,Delta
row sum has the form, up to its fixed row multiplier,

    sum_(j sf) chi_k(j)^3
       sum_(mb=j) c_(i,t,f,Delta)(m,b) M_(i,Delta,f,b)(tm).
                                                               (R14)

The coefficient c contains the native a(m), xi(fb), exact b_(i,t),
chi_t(m)^4, R11, original product windows/masks, normalized profiles
and the norm-gap phase when present. It does NOT depend on k or Q.
Its bounded normalized modulus has only fixed divisor growth.
Thus the inner coefficient of the actual j is independent of the
quadratic row. M B2.24 applies with factor

    K/q_Delta + NG/(T q_f).                           (R15)

Only after that sieve, Cauchy over mb=j costs tau(j). It is not a
triangle over all m, t, or extracted divisors. The resulting positive
sum permits the bounded source factors in c to be discarded.
This is the first place chi_t(m)^4, C_i(tm), the native coefficients
and a unit far phase are replaced by their moduli.

For nonnegative weights w_t<=tau(t), the fixed-Delta bound for the
sum of fixed-t norms is consequently at most

    Z^epsilon q_Delta^(-1)
       (K/q_Delta+NG/(T q_f))
       sum_(t~T,m,b original) |M_(i,Delta,f,b)(tm)|^2. (R16)

The weights w_t, |b_(i,t)(m)|^2 and tau(j) have separate small-power
allowances. They are each bounded by fixed divisor powers in the
retained polynomial ranges. This suppression costs no T power.
