statement:
## G218. A genuine cofactor average with a fixed zero detector

Let R mean positive integers or nonzero integral ideals of K=Q(omega).
Write q_a=a or N(a). Fix a finite prime set S, tau>0 and one ordinary
Dirichlet character eta or finite-order trivial-infinity Hecke character.
All natural zero primes of the PRESENTED character remain. For the sextic
application S contains the primes above6. Let Q be a finite radical
coprime to S and put

    g(v)=(2*pi*tau)^(-1/2) exp(-v^2/(2tau)),
    U_Q(x)=sum_a mu_R(a)eta(a)1_((a,SQ)=1)g(log(q_a/x)),
    U=U_1.                                                (218.1)

These are complete infinite sums. Norm-Euclidean division in the
triangular lattice makes every Eisenstein ideal principal. The covolume
sqrt(3)/2 and six units give A_K(T)=kappa T+O(sqrt T),
kappa=pi/(3sqrt3); A_Z(T)=T+O(1). The first count remains valid at0<T<1
because the count is zero and T<=sqrt T. In particular A_R(T)<<T for
T>=1, |U_Q(x)|<<x uniformly in Q, and the small-x Gaussian tail is smaller
than every fixed power. No Moebius cancellation is used in these bounds.

Take the exact finite sets

    Fset={f squarefree:F<q_f<=2F,(f,S)=1},
    Eset={e:q_e<=E,(e,S)=1},
    P_FE(x)=(N_F N_E)^(-1)sum_(f,e)U_rad(fe)(x).             (218.2)

Shared f,e primes and every e valuation are allowed. The counts N_F,N_E
are their actual cardinalities, comparable to F,E once the fixed-S
threshold is passed. Freeze F,E throughout each shell. For a radical Q,
write h(Q)=prod_(p|Q)(1-q_p^-1), D(Q)=prod_(p|Q)(1+q_p^-1)^-1 and
S_a(Q)=sum_(d|Q)q_d^-a. Inclusion-exclusion followed by
mu^2(n)=sum_(r^2|n)mu(r) gives, uniformly in Q and for T>=1,

    A_Q^sf(T)=kappa T D(Q)/zeta_K(2)
                  +O(sqrt T log(2T)S_1/2(Q))             [K],
    A_Q^sf(T)=T D(Q)/zeta(2)+O(sqrt T d(Q))               [Z]. (218.3)

Indeed the lattice errors sum to sqrt T S_1/2(Q)sum_(q_r<=sqrt T)q_r^-1;
the omitted main tail is O(sqrt T). The integer floor errors are at most
sqrt T d(Q). The main coefficient uses h(Q)prod_(p|Q)(1-q_p^-2)^-1=D(Q).
There is no Q<=T restriction. The T>=1 qualification corrects the raw
author's tiny-T log(2T) notation; its uses at F,E are unaffected.

The squarefree-f and unrestricted-e avoidance probabilities have main
terms A(a)=prod_(p|a,p notin S)q_p/(q_p+1) and
B(a)=prod_(p|a,p notin S)(q_p-1)/q_p. Division by the EXACT sample counts
retains the same error order. Their errors add when multiplying, since
all four probabilities/main terms lie in[0,1]. Define the ONE fixed field

    W_w(x)=sum_a mu_R(a)eta(a)1_((a,S)=1)w(a)g(log(q_a/x)),
    w_p=(q_p-1)/(q_p+1).                                  (218.4)

Then, uniformly for x>0 and sufficiently large F,E,

    |P_FE-W_w| << x log(2F)(F^-1/2+E^-1/2)                [K],
    |P_FE-W_w| << x(1+log(2+x))(F^-1/2+E^-1)              [Z]. (218.5)

Both source tails are included: sum_(q_a<=T)S_1/2(rad a)<<T follows by
divisor summation and sum_d q_d^-3/2<infinity; the integer analogue is
sum_(n<=T)d(rad n)<<T log(2T). Partial summation against the entire
Gaussian gives(218.5). For x<1, writing L=log(1/x) separates a factor
exp(-L^2/(2tau)), which dominates every required fixed power.

The boundary cases are DIFFERENT fixed sources, not substitutions into
the two-sided limiting density. With e=1, let P_F^sf=N_F^-1 sum_f U_f;
its weight is A_p=q_p/(q_p+1) and its sole error is the F term above.
With f=1 and an unrestricted e average the weight is1-q_p^-1 and its
sole error is the E term. This preserves the unit cofactor explicitly.

For any of these three weights w_p=1-delta_p, delta_p is respectively
2/(q_p+1),1/(q_p+1),1/q_p. On Re s>1, absolute Fubini gives

    Mellin W_w(s)=exp(tau*s^2/2)H_w(s)/L^S(s,eta),
    H_w=prod_(p notin S)(1-w_p z_p)/(1-z_p),
    z_p=eta(p)q_p^-s.                                     (218.6)

Both H_w and its inverse have coefficient series in every l1_sigma,
sigma>0. Their local expansions are

    H_p=1+delta_p sum_(j>=1)z_p^j,
    H_p^-1=1-delta_p sum_(j>=1)w_p^(j-1)z_p^j.

The nonconstant absolute mass is O_sigma(q_p^(-1-sigma)); all local
denominators/numerators are nonzero on that half-plane. The normally
convergent inverse proves global nonvanishing. Eta(p)=0 contributes1.
The full Gaussian convolution identities W_w=h*U and U=h_inv*W_w use
V(x/q_d), with cost sum_d|h(d)|q_d^-sigma in the norm

    ||V||_(sigma,p)=sup_(X>0)X^-sigma||V||_(Lp([X,2X],dx/x)), p=1,2.

Formation is justified at sigma=1 before an unproved smaller exponent is
used. The small shifted scales have already been paid. Thus these FIXED
fields have equal every-epsilon shell exponent classes for gamma>0.

For gamma=1-c in(0,1), an every-epsilon complete shell L1 bound
||P_FE||_1<<X^(gamma+epsilon), with F=X^v,E=X^r fixed across the shell,
returns to W_w when v>=2c and r>=2c over K, or v>=2c and r>=c over Z.
For f-only, v>=2c suffices in both rings. Equality allows the displayed
logarithms through the every-epsilon convention. First pass to the fixed
field, then Mellin transform. Large-shell dyadic summation and the left
Gaussian tail prove normal convergence of all fixed derivatives on
Re s>gamma. The continued identity L^S Mellin W_w=exp(tau*s^2/2)H_w
excludes every zero there; the possible principal pole at1 is preserved.
Finite omitted Euler factors only have zeros on Re s=0.

For an ordinary-family conclusion gamma must be common to every positive
modulus/character, while constants and onsets may depend on the fixed
member. The ideal-field version covers only the stated Hecke family and
does not prove the ordinary premise. No moving cutoff is assigned a fixed
Mellin transform. All these returns need the still-OPEN signed L1 bound.

statement:
## 7. A bounded signed cutoff bank cannot remove every semiprime cell

This is a new exact obstruction for the enlarged adaptive family,
not an arbitrary coefficient countermodel. Fix gamma in(1/2,1), J>=1
and Lambda>=1. For each X choose at most J parameters tau_j,X in[0,1]
and complex weights lambda_j,X with

    sum_j lambda_j,X=1, sum_j |lambda_j,X|<=Lambda. (7.1)

They may vary with X but are fixed before real x varies. For one fixed
p, form T_bank=sum_j lambda_j T_tau_j,p,chi,X. Equation (4.3) gives
the complete unconditional comparison

    ||C_p-T_bank||_ell <<_epsilon Lambda X^(gamma+epsilon), ell=1,2. (7.2)

Thus this is a legitimate extension of OPEN-AD, not an unpriced
averaging operation. For the obstruction in the rest of this section
take chi to be PRINCIPAL; (7.2) itself holds for every fixed chi.
Write c=1-gamma and t_j=gamma tau_j. At an
integer n=r s with distinct large primes r,s not dividing pq,
n in(X/4,X/2], the adaptive product is exactly X^gamma. Both cutoff
complements exclude1, even when one cutoff equals1. The ONLY residual
factorizations are(r,s,1) and(s,r,1). If alpha=log r/log X and one
temporarily replaces log s/log X by1-alpha, the coefficient profile is

    F_X(alpha)=sum_j lambda_j[
       1_(t_j<alpha<t_j+c)+1_(gamma-t_j<alpha<1-t_j)]. (7.3)

Endpoint equalities will be avoided by fixed margins, not rounded away.
For all alpha in[0,1], F_X(1-alpha)=F_X(alpha), |F_X|<=2Lambda, and
the exact integral identity is

    integral_0^1 F_X(alpha)dalpha =2c.             (7.4)

Each of the two intervals for a single t_j has length c and lies
inside[0,1]. This proves (7.4), including endpoint cutoffs. In
particular no normalized signed bank can annihilate every semiprime
profile. The conclusion does not require weights to be nonnegative.

Here is the quantitative actual-arithmetic form. Set delta=c/(4Lambda).
Discarding alpha in[0,delta] and[1-delta,1] removes at most c from
the integral of Re F_X. By symmetry,

    integral_delta^(1/2) Re F_X(alpha)dalpha >= c/2.

The portion where Re F_X<c/2 contributes at most c/4 to this upper
half-length interval. Since Re F_X<=2Lambda, the subset on which
Re F_X>=c/2 has measure at least c/(8Lambda). The at most4J endpoints
of (7.3) cut the interval into at most4J+1 constant open pieces.
At least one such piece I has length

    |I|>=ell0=c/[8Lambda(4J+1)], and Re F_X|I>=c/2. (7.5)

Trim one quarter from each end. The remaining [alpha_X,beta_X] has
length at least ell0/2; its endpoints are uniformly separated from
0,1/2 and all relevant breakpoints by at least a fixed positive amount
depending only on c,J,Lambda. (If I abuts1/2, the trim supplies that
margin.) For large X, |log(n/X)|/log X<=log4/log X is smaller than
the breakpoint margin. Thus for primes

    X^alpha_X<r<=X^beta_X,
    X/(4r)<s<=X/(2r),                             (7.6)

the ACTUAL merged bank coefficient equals the SAME complex number
z_X=F_X|I, without a limiting approximation. In particular |z_X|>=c/2.
The primes are distinct and automatically avoid fixed pq for large X.
The core lower/upper physical cuts hold because gamma<1<r (the latter
r here denotes the exponent from Section4, not the prime variable).

Ordinary PNT uniformly for arguments at least a fixed positive power
of X gives, for each prime r in (7.6), at least C X/(r log X) eligible
s, for a uniform C>0. Partial summation of the same PNT yields
sum_(X^alpha_X<r<=X^beta_X, r prime)1/r
=log(beta_X/alpha_X)+o(1), uniformly on the compact allowed endpoint
range. Since beta_X-alpha_X>=ell0/2, the resulting distinct integers
in (7.6) number at least C_(gamma,J,Lambda) X/log X. This invokes no
short-interval or progression-uniform prime theorem: the s intervals
have fixed ratio2, and all endpoints stay polynomially large.

Let B_bank,X be the arithmetic projection of T_bank onto precisely
these integers, retaining their ENTIRE merged coefficients z_X. Rotate
by the unit complex number conjugate(z_X)/|z_X| only for the norm
calculation. For all real x in[X,2X],

    Re[conj(z_X)/|z_X| B_bank,X(x)]
      >=|z_X| exp(-X^(1-b)/2) cos(2^(-k)) # (7.6).

Both its L1 and L2 norms are therefore

    ||B_bank,X||_1, ||B_bank,X||_2 >> X/log X.     (7.7)

This is uniform over every bank satisfying fixed J,Lambda. It covers
moving cut choices and complex signed weights, not only a fixed
positive average. It refutes an argument that pays every arithmetically
selected semiprime cell separately at X^(gamma+epsilon), epsilon<c.
It does NOT lower-bound T_bank, C_p, an unselected factor box, or a
bank with unbounded J or Lambda. Full signed cancellation against the
complement remains possible and necessary. A mask selecting (7.6)
cannot be inserted for free into (7.2); that would be exactly the
invalid norm-monotonicity step exposed by (7.7).

The concrete redirect is to couple these cells with their composite
partners BEFORE a triangle or positive-square budget, or to prove a
new estimate for a genuinely growing bank with its operator and return
costs. A bounded normalized cutoff bank alone cannot remove the need.

## R7. The two-sided finite-face equivalence is exact at the stated exponents

Put u=p^(-z), v=c^(-z). Direct polynomial multiplication gives

    V_z(1,p,c)^2=(1-u)^2[
      u^2-2u(u+1)v+(u^2+4u+1)v^2-2(u+1)v^3+v^4].          (R7.1)

The leading free-label coefficient is A(theta)=a(p)u^2(1-u)^2. Each other term contains a(c)c^(-jz), j=1,2,3,4. Its absolute Gaussian sum is O_(chi,epsilon)(x^(1-delta+epsilon)): use |c^(-jz)|<=c^(-delta), bounded polynomial coefficients in u, and the calculation of R5.2 with d_3 replaced by 1. Thus all FOUR remaining terms are paid uniformly in theta. Both excluded labels are retained as the explicit Gaussian atoms in R3.1.

For x in [X,2X], combining these bounds with the complete product tail gives the useful exact decomposition

    J_X(theta,x)=A(theta)M(x/p)+R_X(theta,x),
    sup_(theta,x) |R_X(theta,x)| <<_(chi,epsilon) X^(2/5+epsilon). (R7.2)

The two removed atoms decay faster than any fixed negative power on this shell and are included in R_X, as is X^(-1+o(1)). No theta truncation error is needed for this POINTWISE decomposition of the finite source. Its constants remain uniform on the expanding window because every estimate was uniform on the full real line.

Let

    alpha=p^(-2delta)(1-p^(-delta))^2>0,
    beta=p^(-2delta)(1+p^(-delta))^2,
    E_M(X)=integral_(X/p)^(2X/p) |M(y)|^2 dy/y,
    b_X=integral_(-T_X)^(T_X) K_h(theta)|A(theta)|^2 dtheta.

The reverse triangle inequality for 1-u proves alpha<=|A(theta)|<=beta at EVERY theta. R6.2 gives m_X>=1/2 for sufficiently large X, with a threshold allowed to depend on chi. Hence

    alpha^2/2 <= b_X <= beta^2.                             (R7.3)

Apply the Hilbert triangle and reverse triangle inequalities to R7.2 in L2(K_h 1_(|theta|<=T_X) dtheta dx/x). If r_X denotes the norm of R_X, then r_X<<_(chi,epsilon)X^(2/5+epsilon) and

    (sqrt(b_X E_M(X))-r_X)_+ <= sqrt(Q_X)
                                  <= sqrt(b_X E_M(X))+r_X. (R7.4)

This is the requested explicit two-sided comparison; it retains every source, cross term and error. Squaring the original decomposition also gives

    |Q_X-b_X E_M(X)| <=2 sqrt(b_X E_M(X))r_X+r_X^2.

For each fixed gamma>2/5, with every epsilon>0 and all sufficiently large dyadic X, R7.3--R7.4 prove

    Q_X <<_(chi,epsilon) X^(2gamma+epsilon)
      IFF
    E_M(X) <<_(chi,epsilon) X^(2gamma+epsilon).             (R7.5)

Take epsilon sufficiently smaller than the requested energy buffer and, when a strict comparison is desired, than gamma-2/5. The original shell variable can be replaced by standard dyadic y-shells: the fixed p merely shifts the dyadic covering, and each shell meets at most two adjacent shells of the other covering, with fixed scale factors. No subsequence estimate is substituted.

Separately, R6.3 and the reverse L1 triangle inequality prove that the all-scale L1 exponent of P_X is equivalent to the corresponding L1 exponent of M on those shifted shells whenever gamma>2/5. This does NOT make L1 and L2 growth estimates equivalent. R6.6 supplies only the stated sufficient implication from Q_X to the L1 readout.

The equivalence R7.5 is with the original Gaussian field M, not with the old D20 real-shift moment or a pointwise unsmoothed Mertens estimate. It proves that this proposed finite face energy has exactly the unresolved arithmetic strength claimed by the author. It supplies no upper bound on E_M, no lower bound contradicting cancellation, and no new arithmetic saving.

statement:
## 2. The proposed cover: a precise gauge obstruction

Let G=(Z/qZ)^* and put one regular G-register on every face. On basis e_(S,g), define

    d_cov e_(S,g)=sum_j (-1)^(j-1)e_(S minus {p_j},g p_j).

Residues commute, so d_cov^2=0. The bijective relabeling

    U e_(S,g)=e_(S,g n(S))

conjugates d_cov to d tensor I: deleting p and replacing g by gp leaves g n(S) unchanged. Thus the cover is a disjoint gauge copy of the original complex, not a new contracting complex. Equivalently, in the Fourier sector spanned on each face by sum_g chi(g)^(-1)e_(S,g), its differential is

    d_chi e_S=sum_j (-1)^(j-1)chi(p_j)e_(S minus {p_j}).

This is D_chi^(-1) d D_chi. Every character sector has exactly one chain basis vector per face. Its Euler index is therefore sum_S(-1)^|S|=M_chi0(X), where chi0 is principal modulo q, independently of chi. Changing this differential cannot change those chain dimensions. The same conclusion holds for any differential on these fixed finite Fourier chain groups.

A small actual-character counterexample is q=3, chi(1)=1, chi(2)=-1, X=5. The unit squarefree faces are empty,{2},{5}. Their untwisted index is 1-1-1=-1, whereas M_chi(5)=1+1+1=3. The Fourier complex has boundary row (-1,-1), but its index remains -1. Thus assigning prime phases to the differential does not supply the required return.

A conserved residue label h=g n(S) gives a chain-map insertion chi(h), but tracing over the full regular register gives zero for nonprincipal chi. Restricting to an anchored slice g=1 recovers the desired weights and loses commutation. This is an exact choice of readout, not a growing-conductor objection or a mere missing dimension factor.
title: 2. The proposed cover: a precise gauge obstruction

statement:
### 5.1 Exact evaluation of the new envelope

For N,V>=0, 0<=L<=N. Define

    E0=min{C(M,N), M+L},
    P=(M+5N+L)/6.

Then

    E_mix=E0,
      unless L>=N/2 and N-L<=M;
    E_mix=max{E0,P} when both conditions hold.         (R11)

This is a continuous endpoint formula; including equality in either condition causes no jump. Here is a proof on the entire interval, not a numerical grid. For 0<=t<=N/2, C(t,N)=N. After the repetition count, the sieve branch is M/6+N-t/6, decreasing, while the label branch is M/6+5t/6+L, increasing. Their crossing is t=N-L. It lies in the actual interval precisely when the conditions in R11 hold, and its common value is P. The endpoint t=0 is no larger than the crossing if it exists; otherwise the minimum is increasing up to the relevant endpoint.

For N/2<=t<=N, C=t/3+5N/6; for N<=t<=2N, C=5t/6+N/3; for t>=2N, C=t. After adding (M-t)/6, these branches have slopes1/6,2/3,5/6, respectively. They and the label branch are increasing, so their minimum achieves its largest value at t=M whenever this portion is present. This gives E0 and proves R11, including truncated intervals M<N/2. The case N=0 follows by the same endpoint formula.

## Full tails and uniformity

The positive smooth-core product is O(t) at 1-1/t. The elementary
Gaussian lattice bound sum_m g(log(m/y))<=C y holds for every y>0.
Together they pay the complete large-core tail, with no squarefree
restriction and no lost prime-power multiplicity. The retained higher
prime powers have convergent norm at 3/4 and total cost
C t X^(.7525). The fully smooth field and the omitted Gaussian tails
are separately bounded; neither is declared absent.

For r<=X^.01 and |u|<=.01log X, both sharp prime endpoints are in
[X^.98,2X^1.01]. Ordinary fixed-order PNT therefore gives the complete
Stieltjes error, including both endpoint atoms, of size
C (x/r)(log X)^(-10). This needs no relative short-interval theorem.

With K=floor(L/(16t)), the unsigned Taylor remainder is at most
C xt/L *15^(-K). Signed moments are completed before their estimation.
The completion error is C xt/L *exp(-.005L/t); consecutive factorial
terms have ratio below 1/7. Under t<=L/(1000log L), its ratio to the
desired relative t^2/L^2 error is bounded by

    L^3 exp(-.005L/t) <= L^(-2).

The large-core ratio is at most L^(-6); the remaining listed tails
are smaller or directly polynomially negligible. These checks close
the stronger uniform statement rather than just the original fixed-B
case. The rational Gaussian denominator is expanded only where it
is bounded below by .99L; it is never extended across its pole.

## 8. Strongest objections and remaining review boundary

The high count cannot be improved by simply dropping the slot maximum from the old unmarked theorem. Equation (2), proved with exact Euler restoration and a slot-disjoint prime pool, is the necessary new estimate. Its middle r interval and long-inverse complement are retained in (9); omitting them would give an unjustified larger saving. The internally reconstructed zero bin need not have the physical bin's upper endpoint: section 3 explicitly weakens its witnesses to the prescribed lower delta while retaining the physical slot bound separately.

A weighted estimate cannot be applied to arbitrary row-varying punctures or a changing character dictionary. Section 5 freezes the genuinely missing radical, uses natural zeros for all support already in w, handles its divisor-many subsets, and leaves the second projector outside the row reconstruction. That reduction, and the exact width/frozen-slot inequality (14), are the highest-priority independent review targets. If either fails at the actual coefficients, the candidate endpoint is not established; the free/raw weighted-density result remains a separately useful proposed lemma.

The briefly tested smaller-power Gauss amplifier did not provide a free shortcut. For p coprime to a column, G(u,hp^k)=overline(chi_u(p))^k G(u,h); compensating with chi_u(p)^k changes the column character. For 1<=k<=5 these p-dependent polynomials cannot be merged into the single positive norm that supplies the source's Z^-a density factor. After second Poisson their row contains p^k j with its natural hole, restoring the apparent radius change. This diagnoses that attempted modification only; it is not a general impossibility theorem for correlated amplifiers.

No full transitive audit is claimed. The oldest analytic contracts remain the explicit source-relative imports of the forward proof. The independent reviewer must inspect the new inverse amplification, the all-range weighted witness argument, the raw lifting and literal projector transfer before using the numerical return. The numerical check alone cannot supply any of those analytic statements.

statement:
## G160. Every fixed character has a large isolated low-frequency sector

This independent extension identifies necessary cancellation. In either
source B(y)=1 for 1<=y<2. Let P_X be the unramified primes in
`sqrt(3X/5)<p<=sqrt(7X/10)`, set `c0=(1/2)log(5/4)`, and
`J=[L-c0,L]`. On J squared, `x=exp(t+u)` lies in `[4X/5,X]`,
whereas each product pp' lies in `(3X/5,7X/10]`. Thus
`8/7<=x/(pp')<5/3`, and B is exactly 1. Distinct ordered prime pairs
survive d,e>Y and gcd<=R for every corridor above.

The ordinary prime number theorem gives
`|P_X| ~ 2(sqrt(7/10)-sqrt(3/5))sqrt(X)/log X`;
removing finitely many ramified primes does not affect this asymptotic.
Only the ordinary PNT is used, not primes in progressions; see
[NIST DLMF 27.2.3](https://dlmf.nist.gov/27.2.E3).

Partition P_X into the finitely many values lambda of chi(p). At every
sufficiently large X some class has at least |P_X|/d primes, where d is
the size of the character's image on units. On pairs from that class,
`mu(p)mu(p')chi(p)chi(p')=lambda^2`, a constant of modulus 1.
The isolated sector's compression to J is therefore rank one with norm

    N_lambda(N_lambda-1) X^(-a)
         (exp(2a c0)-1)/(2a) >>_(chi,a) X^(1-a)/(log X)^2.

The large phase may vary with X. Finite pigeonhole gives one fixed phase
on an unbounded subsequence, not every phase for all X. No progression
equidistribution premise is hidden here.

This sector also survives the frequency cut: pp'>3X/5 forces ell=1 in
the entire observed cap, so its own endpoint/weighted coefficient mass
is O(X^(1-a)/(log X)^2). The same exact Fourier identity bounds its
high-frequency norm by `O(X^(1-a)/(Omega (log X)^2))`.
As Omega grows, its low-frequency part still has the displayed lower
bound. Hence isolated sectors cannot each obey the desired gamma<1 bound.

This is **not** a lower bound for the full signed Tlo, Gamma[c], Gamma[alpha]
or a native detector. Arithmetic selection is not an orthogonal operator
projection, and signed subset monotonicity is false. If OPEN-LOW holds,
the sum of the remaining low-frequency sectors must itself have norm at
least this order along that subsequence, by the reverse triangle inequality,
and must cancel the displayed sector. The next useful estimate must keep
this interaction rather than bound each sector separately.
title: G160. Every fixed character has a large isolated low-frequency sector

statement:
## 4. Four diagonals, source caps, heights and reconstruction

Fix A_0>0, tau>0 and the constants

    kappa=C=sqrt(2 tau(1+A_0)),
    D=sqrt(2(1+A_0)/tau).

For each local real scale Z let L=log Z, H=kappa sqrt(L),
Y=floor(Z^.495), T=Z exp(-H), B=2Z exp(H), and
Dmax=B/(Y+1). All assertions below are for sufficiently large Z;
fixed lower scale ranges are absorbed in constants where needed.

### 4.1 Exact bin geometry and permissible source tails

The bins satisfy

    sqrt(Z) exp(iH) <= d < sqrt(Z) exp((i+1)H),
    Y<d<=Dmax.

Their left edges are included, their right edges are excluded,
and the real Dmax cap is retained. Therefore:

- If i+j<-2, then i+j<=-3 and de<Z exp(-H)=T.
- If i+j>=-2, then de>=Z exp(-2H).
- Once H>log 2, J_Z=floor(1+log 2/H)=1. If i+j>1,
  then de>=Z exp(2H)>2Z exp(H)=B.
- If d>Dmax and e>Y is an integer, then e>=Y+1 and de>B;
  the same holds with d and e interchanged.

Thus all original pairs omitted by GC17 lie either in the paid
low-product source or in the paid upper tail. There is no assertion
that the four-diagonal rectangle has exactly the same product cap.
Its included products can range from Z exp(-2H) to below Z exp(3H).

For low products the common derivative order
m=1+floor(kappa sqrt(L)/tau) in R35.4 gives

    |S_tau(y/(de))|
       <= exp(-kappa^2 L/(2tau)+O(sqrt(L)log L))

whenever y in [Z,2Z] and de<=T. Summing at most Z(1+log Z)
ordered labels gives Z^(-A_0+o(1)). The omitted-label mask and the
coprime/6 mask are bounded and independent of ell, so this bound
applies to the actual omitted labels after each alternating sum is
completed. An ell-dependent truncation cannot be inserted first.

For total indices n>B, the absolute coefficient majorant is d_3(n)
for every relevant original-pair subset, including the primitive
rectangle. Its summatory bound is t(1+log t)^2. Stieltjes summation
against the decreasing Gaussian gives, uniformly for Z<=y<=2Z,

    sum_{n>B}d_3(n)g_tau(log(n/y))
      <= y integral_H^infinity
             e^v(1+log y+v)^2 |g_tau'(v)|dv
      = Z^(1-kappa^2/(2tau)+o(1))
      = Z^(-A_0+o(1)).                                  (C7)

The identity e^v exp(-v^2/(2tau))
=exp(tau/2)exp(-(v-tau)^2/(2tau)) proves the exponent, with
the remaining factors contributing O(sqrt(L)+log L) to its
logarithm. The real cap and strict n>B condition are preserved.

These two bounds independently reproduce GC18. Once that complete-
restoration estimate has been used, removing n=de*ell>B costs (C7)
again. For retained rectangular pairs de>=Z exp(-2H), so the exact
remaining restoration bound is

    ell<=B/(Z exp(-2H))=2 exp(3H).                       (C8)

### 4.2 Complete Mellin scalar and height tails

Let a in (0,1) be fixed. The entire Mellin transform of S_tau is
E_tau(s)eta(s), obtained first at Re(s)>1 and then by continuation
using the Gaussian left tail and rapid right decay. Therefore the
finite primitive pair polynomial C_ij^6 gives

    P_Z^rect(y)=(2pi)^(-1)integral_R D_Z^6(t)y^(a+it)dt.

No interchange of the alternating Dirichlet series on Re(s)=a<1
is needed. Squaring and integrating on the actual local shell gives
exactly GC19, with kernel

    [ (2Z)^(2a+i(t-t'))-Z^(2a+i(t-t')) ]
                  / [2a+i(t-t')].                      (C9)

The denominator has nonzero real part 2a; in particular t=t' does
not create a singularity. Gaussian height decay and the finite pair
polynomial justify the double integral absolutely. Neither the
gcd condition nor the two independent heights factor out.

The alternating partial sums of b have modulus at most one, giving
|eta(a+it)|<=|a+it|/a. Also, because all retained products are below
Z exp(3H), absolute pair summation gives

    sum_{all retained ordered pairs} (de)^(-a)
       <<_a (Z exp(3H))^(1-a) (1+log(Z exp(3H))).

This estimate safely enlarges the subset of integer pairs; no
arithmetic cancellation is used. Multiplication by y^a gives
Z^(1+o(1)). The remaining tail integral has Gaussian factor
exp(-tau t^2/2) times a fixed polynomial in t. Cutting at
|t|=D sqrt(log Z) therefore costs

    Z^(1-tau D^2/2+o(1))=Z^(-A_0+o(1)).                ([restricted research revision])

For the capped coefficient Fourier form, the finite absolute mass
is at most B(1+log B)^2=Z^(1+o(1)); its Gaussian height tail gives
the same exponent. These are two paid field presentations, not an
assertion that their arithmetic coefficients are termwise equal.

### 4.3 Outer reconstruction and all cross terms

After choosing X_0 beyond the fixed four-diagonal geometry threshold,
replace each local P source in (C3) by its rectangular, capped or
height-truncated approximation. The local extra error satisfies
Z^(-A_0+o(1)); hence for each fixed sigma>1/2 it is bounded by
C_sigma Z^sigma uniformly for Z>=X_0. Compact lower scale ranges
can be absorbed using absolute coefficient bounds. Summing with
|k(r)| and (C2) reproduces GC15's X^(1/2+epsilon) global error.
It does not assert an X^(-A_0) error after the outer reconstruction.

The source-tail estimates are applied locally before the r sum.
A global d_3 majorant for the reconstructed coefficients is neither
needed nor established. This avoids misusing the original label
majorant after a new arithmetic convolution.

The exact all-height reconstructed Mellin amplitude is GC20:

    D_X^rec(t)=E_tau(a+it)eta(a+it)
       sum_{r<=X/X_0}k(r)r^(-a-it)
          sum_{i+j=-2,-1,0,1}C_ij^6(a+it;X/r).          ([restricted research revision])

The r^(-a-it) factor follows from (x/r)^(a+it); omitting its phase
would change the field. Its exact local Gram uses (C9) with Z=X.
Expanding the two finite outer sums therefore retains every
r,r',i,j,i',j' interaction with both independent heights.

If each local field is height truncated, the summand for r contains
its own indicator 1_{|t|<=D sqrt(log(X/r))}. The conjugate summand
for r' has its own indicator at t'. There is no collapse to one
height or to a common local cutoff. The field error bound followed
by the Hilbert-space inequality (C6) prices all mixed terms together.

Although ([restricted research revision]) uses non-dyadic scales X/r, this creates no new
hypothesis: (C1) and the tail estimates are uniform for real local
scales. When only all-dyad arithmetic bounds are assumed, transport
first uses the fixed F_tau field as in GC14. Directly covering a
varying-cutoff P family by two dyads would require an extra argument
and is not used.

### 4.4 Optional finite f_3 readout

The author's optional finite window T<n<=B applies directly to
F_tau. Since |f_3(n)|=1 and y>=Z,

    sum_{n<=T}|f_3(n)|g_tau(log(n/y))
       <=T g_tau(-H)
       <<_tau Z^(-A_0)exp(-H).                          ([restricted research revision])

The upper tail follows from (C7), even with the smaller bounded-
coefficient majorant. The capped Fourier polynomial has at most B
unit-magnitude coefficients, so ([restricted research revision]) also applies to its height
tail. All three optional tails are paid with the same fixed width.

For integration, retain the scope distinction: this finite f_3
readout approximates F_tau to a negative-power error. Its relation
to the primitive P source still passes through the small-radical
boundary error (C1), which is O(Z^(.495+delta)). The two finite
coefficient lists are not asserted equal or negative-power close
without that boundary. The author's equivalence statement is valid
with this distinction.
title: 4. Four diagonals, source caps, heights and reconstruction

statement:
# Independent complete large-gcd estimate for every fixed k >= 4

This is a proof addition to the [private research revision] author review, within the same bounded assignment. It uses the author's exact large-root collision lemma and the elementary reversed-root part of W24's local count. It does not prove cancellation in the actual small-gcd Liouville core or increase c. All norms use dx/x on [X,2X].

## Statement

Fix b>1, an integer k>=4 and B0<infinity. Let X>=2 and real G>=1. Let |a1(d)|,|a2(e)|<=1, |b0(l)|<=B0. Let theta(d,e,l) be any complex mask of modulus at most one, fixed before real x varies over the shell. It may depend arbitrarily on X,G and all three integer labels. Define

    v_G(n)=sum_(d e l=n, gcd(d,e)>G) a1(d)a2(e)b0(l)theta(d,e,l),
    F_G(x)=sum_(n>=1) v_G(n) exp(-n/x^b-i(n/x)^k).

Then for every epsilon>0,

    ||F_G||_2 + ||F_G||_1
       <<_(b,k,B0,epsilon) X^epsilon [X/G+X^(b/2)/sqrt(G)]. (S1)

The constant is independent of real G, every sequence, and every mask. There is no upper polynomial cap on G. This removes the extra X^(2k/(3k-2))/sqrt(G) term from the author's general-phase estimate whenever k>=4. At b=3/2,k=6 it gives the same two terms as the author. It is not a pointwise estimate and does not allow live-x-dependent masks.

## 1. Counts, collisions and literal tuples

Put r_G(n)=#{r>G:r^2 divides n}. The exact identities and estimates are

    sum_(n<=Y) r_G(n) <= 2Y/G,
    sum_(n<=Y) r_G(n)^2
      =sum_(r,s>G) floor(Y/lcm(r,s)^2) <=16Y/G.           (S2)

For the second inequality write r=gu,s=gv,(u,v)=1. Both root inequalities say g>G/min(u,v), and lcm(r,s)=guv. Since sum_(g>t)g^-2<=2/t for every t>0, removing coprimality in a positive sum gives at most

    (2Y/G) sum_(u,v>=1) min(u,v)/(u^2 v^2) <16Y/G.

The double series is bounded by 2 sum_u u^-1 sum_(v>=u)v^-2 <=4 zeta(2)<8. Infinite positive majorants are justified by convergence; the exact floor sum is finite. This retains equal roots, all collisions and real G's strict endpoint.

For an interval I in [cN,CN], with length h>=0, reverse the count n=r^2 l. There are at most CN/G^2 possible positive integers l. For each l the permitted real r interval has length at most C_(c,C) h/(sqrt(N)sqrt(l)). Length plus one, summed over l, yields

    sum_(n in I) r_G(n) <<_(c,C) h/G + N/G^2.            (S3)

This proof works for ALL G>=1, not only G>N^(1/3). If CN/G^2<1 the count is zero. Otherwise the N/G^2 term pays each isolated endpoint, including a singleton interval or h<1. The author's stronger minimum with N^(1/3) is valid, but is unnecessary for (S1).

Every actual ordered tuple has a unique exact r=gcd(d,e), d=ru,e=rv and (u,v)=1. At this r the number of remaining factorizations of n/r^2 is at most d3(n/r^2)<=d3(n). Consequently, for every fixed eta>0,

    |v_G(n)| <<_(eta,B0) n^eta r_G(n),
    sum_(n<=Y)|v_G(n)| << Y^(1+eta)/G,
    sum_(n<=Y)|v_G(n)|^2 << Y^(1+2eta)/G.                (S4)

The mask is preserved before this positive coefficient majorization. Coprimality is only dropped in an upper bound. No assertion about the norm of a signed subset is used.

## 2. Complete kernel and every pair

Choose fixed smooth nonnegative w supported in [1/2,3], w>=1 on [1,2]. Put f_x(n)=exp(-n/x^b-i(n/x)^k). For n!=m, two integrations by parts after x=Xu give

    |int w(x/X) f_x(n) conjugate(f_x(m)) dx/x|
      << exp(-c(n+m)/X^b) min(1,[X^k/|n^k-m^k|]^2),    (S5)

with the minimum equal to one when n=m. The phase derivative is a nonzero constant multiple of (n^k-m^k)u^(-k-1)/X^k. Every derivative of the real damping is a fixed polynomial in (n+m)/X^b times that damping; its polynomial is absorbed by decreasing c. Compact support eliminates boundary terms. Constants depend on fixed b,k,w. This is a continuous full-shell estimate.

Split at n<=X. By (S4), the full low source has pointwise magnitude O(X^(1+eta)/G), hence the same norm bound. Its entire interaction with the high source will be paid by norm triangle. All high-source expansions may first be finite; exponential damping and divisor bounds justify the limiting expansion and positive majorants.

Cover every comparable ordered high pair by a bounded-overlap collection [N/2,4N]^2, N>=c0 X dyadic. On a block put H=X^k/N^(k-1). The kernel factor is at most min(1,(H/|n-m|)^2). Let P_N be the positive absolute pair sum on this full block, including the diagonal. Equations (S3), (S4), and annuli about any integer center give

    P_N << exp(-cN/X^b) N^(2eta)
            [HN/G^2 + N^2/G^3].                         (S6)

For H>=1, the ball and doubling annuli have mass O(H/G+N/G^2), after summing their geometrically decaying weights. For H<1, the possible diagonal is paid by O(N/G^2); off-diagonal distances start at one and their weights give O(H^2/G+H^2 N/G^2), bounded by the same claimed quantity. Endpoint and empty intervals were included in (S3). Multiply the row bound by the full r_G mass O(N/G).

Independently, the integer-kernel row sum is O(1+H). Applying 2|v_n v_m|<=|v_n|^2+|v_m|^2 and (S2),(S4) to the SAME full positive pair sum gives

    P_N << exp(-cN/X^b) N^(2eta) (N/G)(1+H).            (S7)

Make constants and exponential rates common, then take the minimum. The inequality min(A+B,C+D)<=A+C+min(B,D) gives

    P_N << exp(-cN/X^b) N^(2eta)
       [ X^k/(G^2 N^(k-2)) + N/G
                 + min(N^2/G^3, X^k N^(2-k)/G) ].      (S8)

All distinct root representations and both ordered orientations were counted before this minimum. It does not compare two different signed sources.

One may also separate the exact diagonal first: it is at most the common factor times N/G. The off-diagonal integer row sum is O(H) even when H<1. Taking the minimum of (S6) and the off-diagonal bound HN/G then bounds all off-diagonal pairs by the first and last terms of (S8). Thus the X^b/G term below can be reserved solely for the diagonal.

## 3. Summation uniform even for superpolynomial G

Uniformity in unbounded G must not absorb a factor G^eta into X^epsilon. Instead absorb the whole coefficient loss using the actual damping:

    N^(2eta) exp(-cN/X^b)
         <<_(eta,b,c) X^(2b eta) exp(-cN/(2X^b)).        (S9)

After (S9), sum the first term of (S8) without damping, obtaining O(X^2/G^2) for k>2. The isolated N/G term sums with damping to O(X^b/G). For the last term, its increasing and decreasing branches meet at

    N_* = X G^(2/k) >= X.

Both geometric sums therefore give

    sum_(N dyadic>=c0 X) min(N^2/G^3,X^k N^(2-k)/G)
       <<_k X^2 G^(4/k-3) <= X^2/G^2       (k>=4).      (S10)

The fixed c0 only changes the constant. Equation (S10) includes k=4 with equality of the G exponents; no strict reserve is required. For 2<k<4 this proof leaves the larger term and does not give (S1).

For far ordered pairs, n~N and X<m<n/2, and also the reverse orientation, (S5) is at most O(X^(2k)N^(-2k)). Both the shell and cumulative coefficient masses are O(N^(1+eta)/G). Thus every far pair costs in total

    sum_(N dyadic>=c0 X) X^(2k)N^(2-2k+2eta)/G^2
        << X^(2+2eta)/G^2,                             (S11)

provided eta<k-1. This includes arbitrarily high n and all much smaller high partners. Interactions involving n<=X were already reserved for triangle.

Equations (S8)-(S11) prove a high squared norm at most

    C X^(2b eta)[X^2/G^2+X^b/G]+C X^(2+2eta)/G^2.

The low norm and triangle have the same scale. Choose eta>0 after epsilon, smaller than both epsilon/(2b) and (k-1)/2. Cauchy-Schwarz on finite logarithmic measure pays L1. This proves (S1), with the original masks and strict gcd endpoint intact.

## 4. A matching diagonal obstruction in the comparison class

The author already supplies the lower price X/G for 1<=G<=c sqrt(X): retain a1=a2=b0=1, d=e=r, G<r<=2G, r^2 l<=X/2. All phases lie in a fixed positive real sector and there are at least c'X/G triples.

The second term has its own comparison-class obstruction. Let Y=floor(X^b), with X sufficiently large, and 1<=G<=c sqrt(Y) for a small fixed c. Retain only d=e=r, G<r<=2G, Y/2<r^2 l<=Y. Let

    A_n=#{r in (G,2G]: r^2 divides n}, Y/2<n<=Y.

Length minus one for each r gives sum_n A_n >>Y/G (choose c small so each Y/(2r^2) is at least four). Hence sum A_n^2>=sum A_n>>Y/G. Give every retained tuple of output n the same sign epsilon_n in {-1,1}; this is a permitted fixed mask. For independent equiprobable signs, at each real x in [X,2X],

    E |sum epsilon_n A_n f_x(n)|^2 = sum A_n^2 |f_x(n)|^2 >>Y/G,
    E |sum epsilon_n A_n f_x(n)|^4 <=3 (sum A_n^2 |f_x(n)|^2)^2.

The fourth-moment inequality follows by enumerating even index multiplicities and remains true for complex f_x(n). Holder yields E|sum epsilon_n z_n| >= (sum |z_n|^2)^(1/2)/sqrt(3). Here |f_x(n)|>=e^-1 on the retained range. Integrate this pointwise expectation over the full shell. Fubini is finite, so at least one fixed sign choice satisfies

    ||F_G||_1 >> X^(b/2)/sqrt(G),

and its L2 norm has the same lower bound up to the fixed measure constant. This is an existence proof; no numerical random draw or average-source theorem is used.

These examples attain each displayed scale as a lower price in the broad bounded-mask class in its stated range. At b=3/2 each scale dominates the other in a nonempty parameter regime, so both terms are needed there. For other b one upper term may be redundant; no universal optimality claim for every b is made. These examples do NOT lower-bound the actual signed Liouville source, its small-gcd residual, or every admissible mask.

## 5. Consequence and boundary

With G=X^(1-gamma), (S1) pays the new large-gcd source by X^(gamma+epsilon) for k>=4 exactly under gamma>=b-1; its first term is X^gamma. This is a sufficient condition, and for 1/2<gamma<1 the diagonal example rules out a smaller exponent for the whole broad class if gamma<b-1. The inherited square-source, moving-cut, full-tail and Mellin constraints must STILL be satisfied separately. No new complete architecture at smaller k follows just from (S1), and no signed small-gcd power estimate is proved.

The next arithmetic task remains the author's literal OPEN-LCG, including every cofactor, ordered factorization, natural zero and full real shell. This proof simplifies and strengthens its paid complement; it is not a resolution of that task.
title: Independent complete large-gcd estimate for every fixed k >= 4

## Objection, sanity check, and remaining gap

The strongest objection to a careless argument is real: principal sixth powers cannot be assigned subpower total mass. Their Gauss amplitudes cancel the apparent \(r_i^{-3}\) decay. HC10 explicitly pays their count, producing the \((Y_DY_E)^{1/6}\) loss. Treating all \(d_0\)-powers as though they had the nonprincipal \(1/\operatorname{rad}(d_0)\) weight would give an unsupported stronger theorem.

A deterministic finite sanity check covered 157 surviving local configurations with unequal embedding valuations, core exponents zero or one, cube exponents through four, and outer exponents through eighteen. HC8 had no failures. This is only a finite arithmetic check; the local case argument above supplies the proof.

This does not improve the accepted \(c_0\). Generic coprime \(A,A',a,b\) can have \(R\asymp Y^2(ZL)^2\), far above both thresholds. The true-gcd conductor in T07 remains a separate object. The full physical residual is reduced to \(R>(Q/L^2)^{5/6}\), and its locally nonprincipal outer portion further to \(R>T_{\rm np}\). The same-core theorem, T07 tail, original numerator/contour transfer and all-height requirements are neither replaced nor strengthened here.

## 8. A coarse paid conditioning lemma for the surviving two-grid option

This analytic lemma is restricted to the paired multiplier; it supplies no arithmetic capture. Define the entire normalized factors

  B_q(s)=(1-q^(1-s))/(s-1),    B_q(1)=log q.

For every T>=1 and |t|<=T,

  |B_2(1+it)|^2+|B_3(1+it)|^2
        >= exp(-2T)/[4(1+T)^2].                           (B16)

Here is a direct coarse proof, avoiding an ineffective irrationality assertion. For |t|>=1 let delta=max(|1-exp(-it log2)|,|1-exp(-it log3)|). Choose the nearest integers m,n to t log2/(2pi), t log3/(2pi). By replacing t by |t|, assume t>0. Their phase errors are at most pi delta/2. If delta<1/2, m,n cannot both vanish, since that would imply t log3<=pi/4<log3, contrary to t>=1. Unique factorization gives 3^m!=2^n. Hence

  |m log3-n log2| >= 1/max(3^m,2^n)
       >= 3^(-1/2) exp(-t log2 log3/(2pi)).

On the other hand the phase-error relation bounds this logarithm by delta log6/4. Thus delta>=(4/(sqrt3 log6))exp(-t log2 log3/(2pi))>=exp(-t)/2. If delta>=1/2, the last bound also holds. Dividing by t proves max|B_q|>=exp(-t)/(2t). For |t|<=1, the elementary sine chord bound gives |B_2|>=2log2/pi>1/4. These bounds imply B16.

For any measurable V(t) and W_q(t)=B_q(1+it)V(t), the exact recovery is

  V(t)=sum_(q=2,3) conjugate(B_q) W_q / (|B_2|^2+|B_3|^2).

On |t|<=T this has spectral L2 norm cost at most 2(1+T)exp(T). A local physical square expansion must retain the four ordered grid pairs and the two independent heights; this recovery does not justify replacing that local square by its t=t' diagonal or by separate source pieces.

The complete-height Gaussian version is also paid: for every fixed tau>tau'>0,

 integral_R |exp(tau*(1+it)^2/2)V(t)|^2 dt
 <= C_(tau,tau') sum_(q=2,3)
       integral_R |exp(tau'*(1+it)^2/2)W_q(t)|^2 dt.         (B17)

Indeed the squared inverse cost is at most 4(1+|t|)^2 exp(2|t|) (for |t|<=1 the same chord bound gives |B_3|>=2log3/pi>1/2), and multiplying it by exp(-(tau-tau')t^2) is uniformly bounded. The harmless real Gaussian factor exp(tau-tau') is absorbed in the fixed constant. This proves the whole-height comparison, not merely a truncated statement with an unpaid tail.

At the current Gaussian height scale T=D sqrt(log X), the finite-height inverse coefficient cost and its two-height squared coefficient cost are X^o(1); this is not itself a local-energy inequality. Thus deliberately coarse elementary conditioning does not itself impose a fixed positive exponent loss for this paired multiplier. The missing theorem is still the exact original-source arithmetic approximation/capture with a coefficient construction and all cross-grid terms. B16-B17 alone do not transfer arbitrary local Gaussian energies, prove membership in the required half-plane Hardy space, or prove the open repair.
title: 8. A coarse paid conditioning lemma for the surviving two-grid option

## A02. Additional exact index and budget results

### Orientation-sensitive rectangular means

Suppose for the same physical family one has
\[
\mathcal M(A,B)\ll T^C(AB)^\delta
\min_j A^{r_j}B^{s_j},\qquad r_j,s_j\ge0.
\]
Summing over \(AB^2\le X\) gives exponent
\[
R=\max_{0\le z\le1/2}\min_j\{r_j(1-2z)+s_jz\}.
\]
Every bound is nondecreasing in \(A\), so the outer maximum is on \(AB^2=X\). Only endpoints and intersections of the finitely many affine lines need checking. Dyads cost logarithms.

A fixed-\(b\) estimate \(Y^{1+\eta+\delta}q_b^{\nu+\delta}\) yields an all-physical-row exponent \(1+\eta\) if \(\nu<1+2\eta\): a \(b\)-dyad \(B\) contributes \(X^{1+\eta+\delta}B^{\nu-1-2\eta+O(\delta)}\).

The hypothetical pointwise model \(|F_{ab^2}|\ll q_aq_b^{1/2}\) gives rectangular mean \(A^3B^2\), and hence \(X^{3-4z}\). It reaches \(X^{35/32}\) only for \(z\ge61/128\). Combining it with the weak fixed-\(b\) exponent \(\nu=3/2,\eta=3/32\) gives worst exponent \(85/69>35/32\). These are exact limitations of the supplied upper bounds, not lower bounds for actual means. [BA D4.]

### Reduced index and the conditional anisotropic calculation

On squarefree sixth-order Gauss columns, \(h=ab^2\) permits replacing \(h^4=a^4b^8\) by \(a^4b^2\). The quotient is \(b^6\); at column primes dividing \(ab\), both local nonprincipal Gauss sums are zero. This algebra gives reduced norm \(A^4B^2\). It supplies no arithmetic approximate functional equation.

If one separately grants the proposed AFE length \(C=A^2B\), dual control, coefficient mass, and the displayed anisotropic sieve bound in BB R04.a, substitution gives \(A^{7/3}B^{5/3}\) for \(A\ge B\) and \(A^{8/3}B^{4/3}\) for \(B\ge A\). In the latter region it fits the target \(A^{1+\eta}B^{2+2\eta}\) only if
\[
B\ge A^{(5-3\eta)/(2+6\eta)}.
\]
At \(\eta=3/32\), this is \(B\ge A^{151/82}\). At \(A=B\), its physical exponent is \(4/3\). The algebra is verified; exact applicability of the cited external sieve and the AFE remain separate obligations.


The full unequal-cutoff proof is A16. Fixed off-central incidence budgets are in T08.

## Return to the same fixed detector, with the full future integral

This return uses the retained source-relative summatory input for the chosen fixed ordinary character:

  M_chi(z)=sum_(n<=z) mu(n)chi(n) <<_(chi) z^b, b=7/8.       (N11)

The accepted boundary b6 is smaller than7/8. Where the original PR9 character/K scope has not been independently discharged, (N11) is an explicit hypothesis; this report neither resolves that issue nor widens it to Hecke characters. The algebra and estimates(N1)--(N10) themselves do not need(N11).

Abel summation and the derivative version of(N5) imply, for every integer r>=0 and x>=1,

  |F_r(x)|<=exp(C_(chi,tau,b)(r+1)log(r+2)) x^b.             (N12)

Indeed the relevant integral is bounded by x^b times the weighted integral of |phi_r'|; its e^(bv) factor is integrable against the weakened Gaussian. This pays the dependence on the derivative order.

Repeated integration by parts, with all future boundaries killed by b<1, gives the EXACT identity for each fixed integer r>=1:

  F(e^u)=1/Gamma(r) integral_0^infinity e^(-t)t^(r-1)
                                            F_r(e^(u+t)) dt. (N13)

At base scale X choose the even integer K=2ceil((log X)^(1/3)/2), and then keep r=K-1 FIXED throughout this integral. Do not replace r by a scale-dependent derivative inside the integration. For0<=t<=4log X, every dyadic Z meeting [Xe^t,2Xe^t] has log Z between log X-O(1) and5log X+O(1). Hence this fixed K lies in the band specified above for all those Z, for sufficiently large X; the lower margin is5^(-1/3)>1/2. At most two dyadic shells cover each shifted interval.

Suppose for some1/2<gamma<1 and every epsilon>0 the complete sources satisfy, uniformly over all sufficiently large dyadic Z and every EVEN K in the band,

  ||C^bal_(Z,K)||_(L2([Z,2Z],dx/x)) <<_(epsilon,chi,tau)
                                                     Z^(gamma+epsilon). (N14)

Use(N4) on those future shells and Minkowski in(N13). The portion t<=4log X is bounded by

  O(X^(gamma+epsilon))(1-gamma-epsilon)^(-r)
       =X^(gamma+epsilon+o(1)),                            (N15)

for epsilon<1-gamma. The remaining t>4log X is, by(N12), at most

  X^b exp(-4(1-b)log X+O_(chi,tau)(K log log X))
       =X^(5b-4+o(1))=X^(3/8+o(1)).                       (N16)

For the incomplete gamma tail used here, t^(r-1)e^(-(1-b)t) is decreasing once t>(r-1)/(1-b); bounding its logarithm at4log X and integrating a remaining exponential gives the displayed bound. The factorial and the prefactor in(N12) are also exp(O(K log log X)). Thus (N14) implies the SAME complete-shell bound for the original fixed F at exponent gamma+epsilon, after renaming epsilon. Every future scale and derivative-order constant has been paid.

The fixed field has a rapidly decreasing left tail. Its Mellin integral initially equals exp(tau s^2/2)/L(s,chi) for Re(s)>1. The complete-shell L2 bound and Cauchy--Schwarz make this Mellin integral holomorphic for Re(s)>gamma. Multiplying the continued identity by L(s,chi) excludes every zero there: the Gaussian factor never vanishes. The principal pole at1 is a zero of the reciprocal, not an excluded zero; it is handled by multiplying once by s-1 if using holomorphic products. This is a fixed ordinary-character, every-fixed-complex-s conclusion under its stated source hypotheses, not a fixed-height truncation. Constants may depend on q and chi. There is no uniform growing-conductor theorem, proof-assistant claim, or new identification with an unverified project root definition.

## 4. Why unsigned homology still costs exponent1

The rank of P is exactly

    H_q(X)=#{X/ell<n<=X: mu(n)^2=1, (n,q ell)=1}.

For every fixed integer r, the elementary square-divisor identity and coprime counting give

    #{n<=x:mu(n)^2=1,(n,r)=1}=kappa_r x+O_r(sqrt x),
    kappa_r=(phi(r)/r) product_(p not dividing r)(1-p^-2)>0.

Indeed expand mu(n)^2=sum_(d^2|n)mu(d), retain (d,r)=1, and use #{m<=t:(m,r)=1}=(phi(r)/r)t+O_r(1); the d>sqrt x tail costs O_r(sqrt x). Therefore

    H_q(X)=kappa_(q ell)(1-1/ell)X+O_q(sqrt X).         (T5)

This proves the linear unsigned bill without importing a topological theorem or a prime-counting asymptotic. It is a lower bound for the rank/absolute homology certificate, NOT for the signed B or M_chi. For q=1 the coefficient is 2/pi^2. This elementary cone account reconstructs an existing obstruction and is not counted as a new arithmetic estimate.

statement:
## 6. All finite logarithmic moments and exact quantifiers

For a fixed nonzero complex C1 profile compactly supported in (1,V), define

    m_j=integral h(v)v^(-2)(log v)^j dv.

A finite first nonzero moment m_J must exist. If all vanished, the finite complex measure h(v)v^(-2)dv would annihilate polynomials in log v. These are uniformly dense in continuous functions on its compact support, so the measure would be zero. Continuity then forces h=0, a contradiction.

In (V8), use (V3) through fixed order J+1. A term with source index j and Taylor index k has coefficient

    -b_(j,q)(-1)^k omega^(j+k)(u_p)/(k! L^(j+k+1))
       *integral h'(v)v^(-1)(log v)^k dv.

The last integral equals m_k-k m_(k-1), with m_(-1)=0. Every term with k<J vanishes. At the first surviving denominator L^(J+2), only j=1,k=J can contribute, yielding

    (-1)^(J+1) b_(1,q)m_J omega^(J+1)(u_p)/J!.

After prime summation the result is exactly

    response ~ [(q/phi(q))(-1)^(J+1)m_J/J!]
         omega^(J+1)(u)kappa_r N P^(-r)/(log P)^(J+3).   (V11)

The uniform source remainder costs O(A/L^(J+3)) per prime after total variation. The quadrature error O(A/(p^rL^2)) is smaller than every required fixed logarithmic order because r is fixed and positive. The u_p-u variation is O(1/log P) uniformly, so the leading derivative converges to its nonzero value at u. Complex m_J causes no problem: the ratio to the nonzero displayed complex main term tends to 1.

For every fixed k, omega^(k) is nonzero at arbitrarily large points. Beyond the finitely many differentiability transition points, if it vanished identically on a tail, omega would be a polynomial P there. In uP'(u)=P(u-1)-P(u), a positive-degree polynomial has left degree deg P and right degree deg P-1, a contradiction. A constant again propagates backwards and contradicts 1/u. This proves the needed existence without any numerical derivative test.

Thus Theorem C is valid with all its fixed parameters. More precisely: for every fixed nonzero h, q, r and gamma<1, choose a fixed u>J+2 with nonzero derivative and theta(u,r)=(u+1)/(u+r+1)>gamma. The resulting root-adapted family of residuals has magnitude asymptotic to a nonzero constant times N^theta/(log N)^(J+3), which exceeds N^(gamma+epsilon) for any sufficiently small positive epsilon<theta-gamma. The source estimate is never invoked at u=u(N).

This leaves open a particular construction restricted to bands for which theta<=gamma, cancellation among different prime bands, N-dependent profiles, and stronger dependencies among defects. The fixed-profile assertion is not a universal lower bound on signed errors of all approximations. Theorem B has endpoint-touching support [1,2], while C states compact support inside (1,V); B's separately proved endpoint vanishing suffices for its argument. No unsupported scope enlargement is needed to link them.

# W59 research handoff

Outcome: **no new arithmetic saving and no increase in c**. The accepted baseline c0=0.125113352960035869... remains a premise. The current written c11=0.1251459636 remains source-relative, with its existing analytic ancestry, uniformity and external admission gaps. This lane proves finite source identities and scoped method obstructions, supplies complete conditional zero-exclusion returns, and leaves the required signed estimate open.

The most useful result is an exact cutoff-boundary spectrum valid for arbitrary moving prime weights, including vanishing weights. It sharpens the obstruction to a positive spectral-gap shortcut while retaining the actual mu(n)chi(n) readout. Its topological core and character-gauge correction already have ancestors, including the [restricted research revision] integration that appeared during this lane. No literature novelty is claimed.

## Frozen generation and selection

Recipe and problem SHA-256 values were verified before writing. All 30 original cards were written in six groups of five: two free, two literal p<.10 and two literal p<.01, using the substantive sampled recipes. These fractions label generation typicality, not validity or calibrated success. The entire `seeds.md` was read and frozen BEFORE detailed proof/history reads, and its path/hash sent to the controller:

`289e8f6227eef7719e6bc86c4a832a23a2d09dff6bd88c8d2ad1786814b84b2d`.

Deliberate choices were reserved before entropy: strongest S04, protected highest-reach S22, most different S17. Exactly three independent uniform stages followed. Each COMPLETE textual pool was frozen/read/hashed before fresh OS entropy. All groups counted under the literal caps. There was no duplicate exclusion, reroll or selective replacement.

|stage|complete remaining pool|size|saved draw|
|---|---|---:|---|
|1|literal p<.10|22|S11 polygonal phase transport|
|2|literal p<.01 after S11|11|S23 coherent native-H dilation|
|3|all remaining after S11/S23|25|S07 squarefree cube gluing|

The pool and entropy artifacts preserve every eligible card and original outcome. `selection-plan.md` records the only exclusions: prior reservations and prior draws. The protected S22 calculation received substantive work first. Two survivors were developed: S22 joined with S07, and S04. The other 24 cards are untested, not rejected; their complete mechanisms remain available to the critic's separate protected/uniform unselected-card audit.

## Exact source and the protected result

Fix an ordinary character chi modulo q. Let a(n)=mu(n)chi(n) with squareful and nonunit coefficients zero. For finite unramified P containing every prime <=N not dividing q, use orthonormal subset states e_S, n_S=product_(p in S)p, and Pi=1_(n_S<=N). Missing integer coordinates stay zero. With ordered fermionic creations c_p, arbitrary complex w_p and W=sum|w_p|^2>0, put

    d=sum_p w_p c_p, D=Pi d Pi, B=(I-Pi)d Pi, E=B^*B.

The exact relations, proved in `fock-boundary.md`, are

    D^2=0, D^*D+DD^*=W Pi-E, 0<=E<=W Pi.             (A)

If p_* is the least ACTIVE prime, meaning w_(p_*)!=0 and all smaller weights vanish, then

    multiplicity of the eigenvalue W of E
      = #{n<=N:mu^2(n)=1,(n,q)=1,p_* not|n,n>N/p_*}. (B)

This is exact for every choice of the other weights, and allows p_*>N. The proof uses the actual divisor-closed cutoff. Its upper p_*-free states form a subcomplex U killed by D; the quotient pairs lower p_*-free states with their p_*-multiples and contracts by w_(p_*)^-1 c_(p_*)^*. Thus H(D)=U as graded vector spaces. Finite Hodge decomposition and (A) identify U's dimension with the W eigenspace. This does not identify arithmetic signs with positive spectral mass.

Let kappa_q=prod_(p|q)(1-1/p)prod_(p not|q)(1-1/p^2). Elementary square-divisor counting, with a finite-small-prime/large-prime split, gives for fixed q and all sufficiently large N, UNIFORMLY over every active prime and moving set of weights,

    (kappa_q/8) WN <= Tr(E) <= WN,
    multiplicity_W(E) >= (kappa_q/8)N.               (C)

Consequently ||E||=W at those scales. An upper bound that first discards all grading and uses only Tr(E) cannot produce a sublinear Mertens exponent. Nor can a proposed ambient spectral gap E<=(1-delta)W Pi hold. These are obstructions to those sufficient methods, **not lower bounds on the actual signed source, Gaussian moment or native H form**.

The complete arithmetic response remains

    W M_chi(N)=Str(T_chi E)+Str([T_chi,D^*]D),        (D)

where T_chi e_S=chi(n_S)e_S and the grading is (-1)^|S|. Equivalently its p-th summand is |w_p|^2 times

    sum_(N/p<n<=N,p not|n)mu(n)chi(n)
      +(1-chi(p))sum_(n<=N/p,p not|n)mu(n)chi(n).     (E)

Every bracket is exactly M_chi(N). The second term vanishes for principal characters, but not generally. Supporting weights only on chi(p)=1 is legitimate and kills the bulk; (C) still holds. Simply inserting chi(p) in d is unitary conjugation by T_chi and leaves all singular values unchanged. A character-sensitive estimate must retain the observable in (D).

The source can also be encoded by the single prescribed product

    (I-chi(p_1)c_(p_1))...(I-chi(p_r)c_(p_r)) e_empty,

with the largest index acting first. This is a VALID bare-fermion encoding. Uniformly averaging all orderings instead removes every degree>=2 source coefficient. Restoring their parity signs restores the identical original vector, so that order average supplies no free cancellation. The missing complete composite readout and boundary overlaps remain paid terms. A failed common gauge does not refute the valid fixed-order representation.

For q=1, p_*=2 the critical count is classical; [Bjorner, Theorem3.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1101.5704) verifies the squarefree-complex ancestor. The occupation-sign/CAR conventions are verified against [Bravyi--Kitaev, Eqs.(1)--(2)](https://arxiv.org/pdf/quant-ph/0003137). In this record [restricted research revision]/G79, [restricted research revision]/G118, [restricted research revision]/G135, and especially [restricted research revision]/G144--145 already own exterior, parity-layer, cone, gauge and composite-readout cores. The explicit least-ACTIVE-prime statement with zero/moving weights and the exact boundary-Gram eigenvalue is the scope retained from this calculation; it is an independently written specialization/extension, not a claim to have discovered a new topological theorem.

## Prime removal: complete reconstruction and coarse return

For finite unramified B set a_B(n)=a(n)1_((n,prod B)=1), e_B(d)=mu(d)chi(d)1_(d|prod B), and r_B(m)=chi(m) on ALL B-smooth integers, including prime powers. The exact convolution identities are

    e_B*r_B=delta_1, a=e_B*a_B, a_B=r_B*a,
    a_A*a_B=a_(A union B)*a_(A intersection B).       (F)

The overlapping channels have Dirichlet series F_B=1/(L E_B), E_B=prod_(p in B)(1-chi(p)p^-s). Their rank-one overlap equation is invariant under multiplication of every channel by an arbitrary common meromorphic scalar. It therefore cannot alone rule out a reciprocal-L pole. This objection does not exclude a genuine signed cross-channel estimate.

For fixed B, the exact absolute dilation-return constants at exponent gamma>0 are prod_(p in B)(1+p^-gamma) and prod_(p in B)(1-p^-gamma)^-1. All shifted shells and small-scale tails are retained. For a fixed exponential or Gaussian field, the Mellin transform is Gamma(s)/(L E_B) or Gamma(s/2)/(2L E_B); the shell L2 bound, nonvanishing gamma factors and E_B give the complete all-height return. Moving B does not authorize dropping the product costs, shifted-shell hypotheses or changes of Mellin field.

If min B>sqrt N, the first useful two-scale calculation is exact for every real 1<=x<=N:

    M(x)=M_B(x)-sum_(p in B,p<=x)chi(p)M(x/p).       (G)

The inner M is the ORIGINAL source. Its unit term survives at x=p. For B subset (N^alpha,N^b], 1/2<alpha<b<1, an independently supplied short-scale bound |M(t)|<=Ct^beta gives the coarse rigorous correction bound

    <= C[1+1/(1-beta)] N^[beta+b(1-beta)].            (H)

No PNT enters. As b decreases toward 1/2, the best exponent supplied by this absolute argument approaches (1+beta)/2, larger than beta. Even granting a prior beta just above the current source-relative .8748540364 leaves a correction exponent above .9374270182. This is a METHOD'S bound, not a lower bound for the signed correction.

|desired returned gamma|desired c|short beta needed by (H), limiting b down to 1/2|
|---|---|---|
|.87485|.12515|beta<.74970|
|5/6|1/6|beta<2/3|
|3/4|1/4|beta<1/2|

No such extra estimate was obtained. The surviving problem is the complete signed difference in (G), or its exact field norm ||U_B-C_B||^2 including both norms and the cross term. `renewal-overlap.md` retains all coefficients, overlap factors, endpoints and the quantitative return. Its finite Euler-factor ancestry is classical and already in [restricted research revision]/G81, [restricted research revision]/G92, [restricted research revision]/G108 and [restricted research revision]/G135.

## Other first tests and actual native-H limit

`first-tests.md` contains the exact sources, objections and useful calculations for every selected card.

|card|first decisive calculation|remaining status|
|---|---|---|
|S17 prime/logarithmic commutator|constant-preserving projections have commutator blind to the desired mean; actual principal modulo 3 source at N=12 has M=-2 while the chosen residue/interval projections commute|parked; complete common-mode arithmetic control absent|
|S11 polygonal transport|real/imaginary balanced transport retains all unmatched mass; log-kernel W1 cost already contains prefix imbalance; quadratic feature bound matches [restricted research revision]/G65|parked; no new low-cost source matching|
|S23 coherent H dilation|for exact K=T/r, Julia dilation splits the input squared norm into the channel and loss squared norms; near contraction requires near-complete source observability|general observation/coupling idea open; free-unitarity shortcut fails|
|S07 cube gluing|at primes 2,3,N=5 independent masks retain the omitted6-cell; exact cutoff differential joins S22 and keeps full boundary|developed with S22; no signed bound|

The native H test read the literal [restricted research revision]/[restricted research revision]/[restricted research revision] contracts. Its ideal source a(n)=alpha(n)eta(n)chi_n(lambda)^(-2)gamma_2(n), coprime cocycle a(de)=a(d)a(e)chi_d(e)^4, shared-prime zeros, short coefficient, both rooted arrays and projectors, CRT/angular data, original masks, signed core, independent heights, excluded equal-norm orientations, sharp gap and once-only N^-1G^-2 outside scalar are retained. The ordinary integer Fock vector is **not identified** with that Eisenstein tensor. No source-relative observability bound, native normalization r or transfer has been established. Neither (A) nor an abstract unitary dilation is an H saving.

## Conditional zero-exclusion return and exact remaining target

For each fixed chi, choose one allowed sequence (P_N,w_N) in (D). If for every epsilon>0 and all sufficiently large N its COMPLETE right-hand side is bounded by C_(chi,epsilon) W N^(gamma+epsilon), with ONE common gamma<2187135091/2500000000, then M_chi(N)<<_(chi,epsilon)N^(gamma+epsilon). Abel summation gives

    1/L(s,chi)=s integral_1^infinity M_chi(x)x^(-s-1)dx

on Re(s)>1, and the integral is holomorphic on Re(s)>gamma by a positive epsilon buffer. Multiplying by the actual meromorphic L continues the identity 1 and excludes its zeros there. This handles every finite height without choosing a maximum height. The principal pole is treated as a pole, and imprimitive Euler factors have their zeros only on Re(s)=0. Constants and onsets may depend on chi; gamma may not. This is a full CONDITIONAL bridge and supplies no estimate for (D).

The next mathematical action is to bound the full signed character-weighted boundary response, including its bulk commutator, or a source-specific observation that quantitatively returns it. A second eligible action is a genuinely signed joint-restoration estimate in (G). The positive trace, ambient spectral gap, overlap determinant, commutator-only mean bound and unitarity alone cannot pay those responses. Wider gluing/observability mechanisms have not been ruled out.

## Evidence, limits and review packet

`exact-checks.py` and its saved JSON passed nine finite CAR/cutoff/character-bulk/gauge/eigenspace checks for principal, complex and imprimitive actual characters, plus a delayed-active-prime case with smaller zero weights. Matrix ranks use exact Fraction elimination; bounded Gaussian-integer operations stay inside exact binary64 integer range. It also checks all 24 prime orderings for a four-prime example, convolution/overlap coefficients through 60 for three characters, R5 endpoints, the actual commutator example, dilation/cube examples and replay of the three saved draws. There was no new entropy in replay. These finite checks support signs/endpoints; the written proofs supply the universal claims. They do not prove an arithmetic saving or replace the conditional bridge's missing hypothesis.

`source-manifest.json` records exact local source hashes and read scopes, primary web references and immutable inputs. Navigation files changed during the lane; their final-observed hashes identify source bytes, not a claim that the initial blind seed generation used later material. `artifact-manifest.json` freezes the owned handoff files.

The critic should challenge (B)'s quotient contraction with smaller zero weights and moving active primes, (C)'s uniform prime split, the character-bulk and endpoint conventions, the full Mellin/Abel returns, the [restricted research revision] novelty boundary, and the distinction between scoped method obstruction and arithmetic impossibility. It should independently retain its full attempt index and audit protected/uniform unselected seeds rather than accepting our six tests as exhaustive. This report is evidence for controller review, not theorem acceptance.

## 3. An exact complementary-divisor identity

For every nonunit ideal n, the full ideal Mobius convolution is zero. Subtract it from the cutoff convolution to obtain

    A_R(n)=-sum_(d|n) mu(d)[1-V(Nd/R)]
          =-sum_(m|n) mu(n/m)[1-V(Nn/(Nm R))].       (S3)

This identity is valid for arbitrary valuations, not only squarefree n. Its nonzero summands have Nd>R, or equivalently Nm<Nn/R. Equality Nd=R contributes zero. If a common bounded smooth cutoff restricts Nn to at most C L, the cofactor is therefore shorter than C L/R. This is an actual support statement, with the endpoint constant retained. It is not obtained by taking absolute values of separate original inverse dyads.

Multiplying S3 by the actual multiplicative character gives

    phi_u(n)A_R(n)
      =-sum_(dm=n) mu(d)phi_u(d)phi_u(m)[1-V(Nd/R)]. (S4)

This holds with zero extensions even when d and m share primes. A frozen hole dividing n forces a zero on at least one factor; it must not be dropped. No coprimality between d and m is imposed. The original slots may meet either factor; their natural zeros remain those of the complete product. No slot pool has changed.

For a smooth prefix cutoff H(Nn/L) and the genuine exponential weight, S4 gives the exact finite expression

    D_prefix,u(s)
      =-sum_m phi_u(m)(Nm)^(-s)
          sum_d mu(d)phi_u(d)(Nd)^(-s)[1-V(Nd/R)]
              H(Nd Nm/L)exp(-Nd Nm/Y).               (S5)

Only Nm<C L/R contributes. The original product cutoff and terminal cutoff are retained inside the coupled smooth profile. Thus the moving m changes an evaluation point of that profile; it is not a license to insert arbitrary coefficients into the inverse moment. A legitimate later proof must separate the coupled profile on its fixed ambient box before choosing a live row or m, using PR9 B3.3. The outside scalar phi_u(m) is a contraction, including at nonunits.

This representation uses a long inverse factor d>R and a short unweighted cofactor m. It is a new presentation of the existing coefficient, not an additional zero detector. It needs no positivity or presumed independence of the two witnesses. It remains valid at the target unit and under whole conjugation.

As a limited exact observation, if every proper divisor of n has norm at most R, then

    A_R(n)=mu(n)[V(Nn/R)-1].                         (S6)

Indeed every proper divisor has cutoff value one, and their Mobius sum is -mu(n). This includes appropriate first product annuli determined by the least allowed prime norm. This record does not assume an unverified numerical value for that least norm, nor a uniformly populated prime annulus. Positive prime-pair terms at the unit are therefore not evidence against possible cancellation by the entire first-annulus inverse coefficient.

`M/4+M/2+(9/2)(M/25)+xi=93M/100+xi`.

Thus its reserve is `7M/100`. Products, whole characters, profiles, independent heights and common punctures agree. Nonempty subunit scales are clipped using the bounded annular rule; empty slots use the unrestricted old theorem.

The first-transform outside exponent is `M-A-R/2-E`. Its common labels, including the first projector, remain inside Hilbert Cauchy. With `B_c=(3c-5d-R)_+/6`, it suffices to prove

`sum_lambda N_(C,lambda) << Z^(p+A-c+R+E+B_c+eta)`,

and the exchanged assertion. Since `B_c+B_d<=c+d-2p-R`, the averaged exponent with the outside factor is at most M+eta. Per-label branches keep the original `-s0` allowance and pay the `Z^(p+s0+eta)` first-label count once. The high branch counts the joint labels directly. No multiplicity is appended afterward.

The actual main radius is

```
K_main=K0+(d-c)_+ +6a_j+omega,
K0=2A-c-d+R+E-M,
omega=delta_1+supportreserve,  2<=Z^supportreserve.
```

RC lines 130-139 and the exact common-radius interface provide genuine smooth domination at this ball. The three errors retain their own radius

`K0+max(d-c-2w+w_o,0)+3a_j+delta_1+supportreserve`.

They are not enlarged to the main radius. The physical scale stays positive even if its logarithmic exponent is negative; unsupported negative row windows are empty and supported bounded end windows receive the fixed padding. The second Poisson formula is applied at the actual radius. Fixed polynomial envelopes cover all thirty cases.

The exact main child identities remain

```
M'=M-(c-d)_+-6a_j-omega-g2+t2,
(A-c-c2-M')-(A-M)
  =6a_j+omega-min(c,d)-(c2-g2)-t2 <=6a_j+omega,

```

Original relative-character dictionaries, parent-translate separation, reciprocity/unit sectors, whole-product conjugation and height reflection are unchanged. Low-bin indicators are attached only to positive allocated child energy after both transforms. Slot removal has squared price `.7+O(e)` per width, hence old-capacity-defect price `7/45+O(e)`. The actual canonical width can be smaller than M'. If `d_*=M_actual-M'<=delta2`, then for `0<=s<=1`,

`d_*+s(F-d_*)_+ <= delta2+sF_+`.

This pays negative width differences as well as positive padding. Nominal low defect is at most `g+6a_j+eta`; the greedy removal overshoots by one mesh increment. Therefore the reserve before small losses is

 >= M b_j(k/15-7r/45)
 = M b_j/3000 >= 57M/5000000.

The strict reserve is **.0000114 M**. Choose aggregate padding, support, bin rounding, divisor and mesh costs from a sufficiently small fixed fraction of it and of epsilon. For a fixed finite slot list, per-slot losses are assigned from one aggregate budget. They are not multiplied by an uncontrolled slot count.

For the main high bins the signed reconstruction gives the actual nonzero row

`w=u0 e F_c G_c V h'`, `L_c=log_Z NF_c<=5(R-R0)`,

with formal-side residues `1+t_p` or `1-t_p` modulo six. Zero residue remains an Euler hole. The first projector and genuine second common primes divide w.  +(1-rho)(c-d)_+-delta c-(1+rho)R-E-B_c
