statement:
## 3. D2 / X26: finite prediction gap with a full zero bridge

For each integer N>=0 define

    d_N = min_(deg p<=N,p(0)=1) ||p F||_H2^2,
    Delta_N=d_N-|F0|^2.                               (7)

The constant coefficient of pF is F0. Orthogonality of Taylor coefficients therefore gives exactly

    Delta_N=min_(p(0)=1,deg p<=N)||pF-F0||_H2^2>=0.    (8)

The minimum exists uniquely. The Gram matrix G_N is strictly positive because a nonzero polynomial times the nonzero analytic F cannot vanish identically. To make conjugations unambiguous, set

    (G_N)_(j,k)=integral over the circle conjugate(z^j F) z^k F dtheta/(2pi),
    0<=j,k<=N.

Then ||pF||^2=p*G_N p and

    d_N=1/(G_N^(-1))_(0,0).                           (9)

It is Toeplitz. Formula (6) also gives its entries as integral_0^infinity conjugate(Q^j h) Q^k h dt. There is no unsigned replacement inside these correlations. Delta_N decreases with N, but its limit is not yet known to be zero.

**Sufficient arithmetic criterion.** If for every fixed ordinary chi the above Delta_N tends to zero for one common gamma, then every such L is zero-free in Re(s)>gamma, with the principal pole treated as above. Thus gamma<theta11 would give a first gain, gamma=5/6 would give c=1/6, and gamma=3/4 would give c=1/4. Constants, rates and onset may depend on chi. Even a non-effective qualitative limit suffices; no conductor-uniform estimate or high-height-uniform convergence rate is assumed.

Proof: let w=z(rho) be any supposed L zero in that half-plane. It lies in the disk and is not zero, because s(0)=2 is zero-free. For every admissible p, e=pF-F0 has e(0)=0 and e(w)=-F0. Taylor Cauchy--Schwarz gives

    |F0|^2<=||e||_H2^2 |w|^2/(1-|w|^2),
    Delta_N >= |F0|^2(1-|w|^2)/|w|^2 >0.             (10)

This contradicts Delta_N->0. The argument fixes one arbitrary zero, so it covers every height without exchanging a height supremum and a limit. Conversely, this report does not claim that nonvanishing alone implies the prediction limit; singular-inner issues need not be settled for the sufficient direction.

For rho=beta+iT, d=beta-gamma>0, formula (10) is explicitly

    Delta_N >= |F0|^2 * 4a d / ((d-a)^2+T^2).          (11)

This prices high-height invisibility. A fixed positive residual bound cannot cover the whole half-plane; it becomes weak like T^-2 for a fixed horizontal gap. A genuine limit to zero would exclude each fixed zero. No finite successful computation proves that limit.

### 3a. Formation and every tail are paid from periodicity

From (3)-(5), let

    H0=sqrt(2a) C_q/(a-gamma),
    K=1+2a/(a-gamma).

Then |h(t)|<=H0 exp(-gamma t), and induction gives
|Q^j h(t)|<=H0 K^j exp(-gamma t). For the truncated Gram G_N^(T),

    |(G_N-G_N^(T))_(j,k)|
       <=H0^2 K^(j+k) exp(-2gamma T)/(2gamma),
    0<=G_N-G_N^(T)<=eta_N(T) I,
    eta_N(T)=(N+1)H0^2 K^(2N)exp(-2gamma T)/(2gamma). (12)

The second inequality follows from the first entrywise bound and the PSD tail Gram. It exposes the growing-degree cost instead of calling a finite matrix the full source. To bound the actual error without any inverse-condition-number assumption, take a specific p with p0=1, put C_p=sum_(j=0)^N |p_j|K^j, and use

    ||pF-F0||^2 <= integral_0^T |p(Q)h-F0 ell0|^2dt
       +H0^2 C_p^2 exp(-2gamma T)/gamma
       +2|F0|^2 exp(-2a T).                           (13)

This is the squared triangle inequality only on the tail. On a finite interval, b(t)=A(n)-r exp(t) for log n<=t<log(n+1); (3) and (5) are elementary exponential integrals. Thus a finite witness has a fully specified ordinary arithmetic source and certifiable tails. It still must make the complete interior integral small. Taking T large while leaving the interior unchanged does not advance (8).

The coarsest sufficient new input is an actual sequence of polynomials p_m and truncations T_m for which the complete right side of (13) tends to zero, for each fixed chi at a common gamma below theta11. No such sequence is constructed here. The apparent replacement of a power bound by an o(1) limit changes the representation, not the established arithmetic difficulty.

### 3a(ii). A cheaper coherent source approximation, and a principal tail theorem

The K^N bound above is not intrinsic. If h_tilde is any fully specified L2 approximation with ||h-h_tilde||<=tau, the isometry of Q gives, for EVERY polynomial p,

    ||p(Q)h-p(Q)h_tilde||<=tau sum_j |p_j|.            (13a)

Consequently the exact residual is at most the fully computed residual of h_tilde plus this price. Each Gram-entry error is at most tau(||h||+||h_tilde||), independent of j,k. The matrix operator error is at most N+1 times that number. These are signed-source approximation bounds, not a positive-semidefinite comparison of the two source Grams. The simple choice h_tilde=h*1_[0,T] has tau<=H0 exp(-gamma T)/sqrt(2gamma). Its filtered output is NOT truncated: after T, Q^j h_tilde has its complete exponential-polynomial tail, which is explicitly computable from the finite convolution states at T. This retains the omitted future response and avoids K^N. The coefficient sum and the main residual remain payable.

For q=1, this can be improved unconditionally. Suppose 1/2<gamma<1, put lambda=a-gamma=2-2gamma in (0,1), and D_lambda=(2-lambda)/(4(1-lambda)). With u={x}, identity (3a) becomes

    f(log x)=1/2+B(x)-V(x)/x,
    B(x)=1/2-{x}, V(x)={x}(1-{x}).                    (13b)

The continuous periodic primitive of B starting at x=1 is P(x)=V(x)/2, with 0<=P<=1/8. Integration by parts gives, for x>=1,

    |integral_x^infinity y^(lambda-1)(f(log y)-1/2)dy|
       <=D_lambda x^(lambda-1).                      (13c)

Indeed the B term is at most x^(lambda-1)/4: one endpoint term at most x^(lambda-1)/8 and one integrated term of the same bound. The V/y term is at most x^(lambda-1)/[4(1-lambda)]. Thus, for a real constant C_lambda defined by the convergent subtracted integral,

    h(t)=sqrt(2a)/(2lambda) exp(-gamma t)
         +sqrt(2a) C_lambda exp(-a t)+R(t),
    |R(t)|<=sqrt(2a)D_lambda exp(-(gamma+1)t).          (13d)

No unknown L reciprocal enters this constant or proof. For a FINITE source approximation no infinite constant is needed: let A0=sqrt(2a)/(2lambda), keep h unchanged on [0,T], and for t>T use

    h_tilde_T(t)=A0 exp(-gamma t)
       +(h(T)-A0 exp(-gamma T))exp(-a(t-T)).           (13e)

The finite prefix and value h(T) completely determine this continuation. Comparing (13d) at t and at T, or using the tail integral in (13c), proves

    ||h-h_tilde_T||_2
       <=D_lambda[1+sqrt(a/(gamma+1))]
                        exp(-(gamma+1)T).            (13f)

For the second term, the error in the coefficient C_lambda estimated at T is at most D_lambda exp(-(1-lambda)T); its L2 tail contributes D_lambda exp(-(gamma+1)T), because a+1-lambda=gamma+1. The R tail contributes the other displayed term. Combining (13a) and (13f) pays the complete omitted principal source after any finite polynomial filter, with a coefficient-sum price and faster decay. The fixed-gamma constant blows up as gamma decreases to 1/2; no endpoint claim at 1/2 follows. All three calibration targets here lie strictly above 1/2.

The sharper D_lambda above is specific to q=1. A coarser extension covers EVERY fixed ordinary character. For nonprincipal chi, A(x) is q-periodic; write it as m_chi+B_chi(x), where m_chi is its period mean. Then B_chi has mean zero, |B_chi|<=2q, and its primitive starting at 1 has modulus at most 2q^2. There is no V term below.

For principal chi, put B0(x)=A(x)-r x, let beta be its period mean, and D(x)=integral_1^x(B0(y)-beta)dy. These are q-periodic and |D|<=2q^2. Formula (3a) gives EXACTLY

    f(log x)=m_chi+B_chi(x)+V_chi(x)/x,
    m_chi=-beta, B_chi=B0-beta,
    V_chi=r+2beta-2D(x).                              (13g)

Here |B_chi|<=2q, its primitive is D, and |V_chi|<=1+2q+4q^2. Thus (13c) holds with f-1/2 replaced by f-m_chi and the admissible coarse constant

    D_chi=4q^2                                  nonprincipal,
    D_chi=4q^2+(1+2q+4q^2)/(1-lambda)             principal.     (13h)

The first 4q^2 pays the endpoint and integral of the bounded primitive; the V/x term pays the second price. The same proof gives (13d)-(13f) for every fixed chi after replacing A0 by sqrt(2a)m_chi/lambda and D_lambda by D_chi. Complex character values and natural zeros are retained. For q=1 use the much sharper explicit D_lambda rather than (13h). For example gamma=3/4 gives a=5/4,lambda=1/2 and principal q=1 source error at cutoff X=exp(T) at most (3/4)(1+sqrt(5/7))X^(-7/4), before the explicit coefficient-sum price in (13a).

This is an actual source-tail theorem for the ordinary-character family, not a prediction or Mobius estimate. All fixed-q constants are allowed. The fixed-gamma constants blow up as gamma decreases to 1/2; no endpoint claim there follows. A family zero-free claim still requires the full prediction limit for each fixed ordinary chi. A fast source approximation does not imply that the limit in (8) is zero.

### 3b. Strongest objection: stable optimal polynomials are automatic

Let p_N minimize (7). If p_N=(z-lambda)q has a root, variation by zq is admissible because it has zero constant term. Orthogonality gives

    ||qF||^2-lambda <qF,zqF>=0.

Multiplication by z is an isometry and equality in Cauchy--Schwarz is impossible for nonzero qF and zqF. Hence |lambda|>1. Every finite minimizer is therefore zero-free on the closed disk for EVERY nonzero F with F0!=0, including sources that have interior zeros. This proves that “the optimized polynomials are stable” is not an arithmetic result. It is a universal optimization property.

For the exact toy F(z)=1-z/r with real r>0, G_N is tridiagonal with diagonal 1+r^-2 and adjacent entries -r^-1. Its size-m determinant is D_m=sum_(k=0)^m r^(-2k), including D_0=1 for the empty determinant. Therefore

    d_N=D_(N+1)/D_N,
    lim d_N = r^-2 if 0<r<1, and 1 if r>=1.            (14)

At r=1, Delta_N=1/(N+1). At r=1/2, Delta_N tends to 3, although every optimizing polynomial is stable and the Gram spectrum is uniformly bounded between (1/r-1)^2 and (1/r+1)^2. More strongly, G_N(r)=r^(-2)G_N(1/r), so the entire sequence of constrained optimizing polynomials is IDENTICAL for an interior zero r and the exterior zero 1/r. Their coefficients or root locations alone cannot distinguish the two cases; the scalar residual normalization is essential. For the inner toy F=(z-r)/(1-rz), 0<r<1, the complete Gram is exactly the identity and d_N=1 for all N, while |F0|^2=r^2. Matrix positivity and good conditioning do not pay the prediction gap either. These are toy obstructions to the stated inference, not lower bounds on the actual character source.

This is classical optimal-polynomial approximation, not a literature novelty. The primary paper by Beneteau, Khavinson, Liaw, Seco and Sola, *Orthogonal polynomials, reproducing kernels, and zeros of optimal approximants*, arXiv:1509.04807v2 (17 September 2015), Theorem 3.2 and sections 5-6, establishes the related universal zero-free property and cyclicity/Gram framework: https://arxiv.org/pdf/1509.04807 . Our constrained p0=1 version is proved above. The contribution proposed for the QRH record is the literal ordinary-character source (2)-(5), complete tail (12)-(13), calibration and scoped failure; not a new general Hardy theorem.

statement:
## 2. Exact weighted principal local kernels

At a coherent prime outside the completed columns, write
\[
\alpha=v_p(a),\quad\beta=v_p(b),\quad
s=v_p(e),\quad t=v_p(d),
\]
where \(s,t\in\{0,1\}\), \(st=0\), and \(q=q_p\). For a positive principal exponent \(j\), PC3 is
\[
G_j(-p^{2s}r)
=q^{j/2}\left(1_{p^{j-2s}\mid r}
-q^{-1}1_{p^{j-1-2s}\mid r}\right). \tag{FR6}
\]
All positive principal exponents here are at least six, so these divisor exponents are nonnegative.

Suppose \(\alpha>\beta\ge0\), both divisible by six. The larger exponent's support puts the smaller positive kernel on its constant branch, since their shifted thresholds differ by at least four. After division by \(q^{(\alpha+\beta)/2}\), the product is
\[
(1-q^{-1})^{1_{\beta>0}}
\left(1_{p^{\alpha-2s}\mid r}
-q^{-1}1_{p^{\alpha-1-2s}\mid r}\right). \tag{FR7}
\]
For a divisor weight \(q_k^{-\rho}\), its mass is at most
\[
q^{-\rho(\alpha-2s)}(1+q^{-1+\rho}). \tag{FR8}
\]
The case \(\beta>\alpha\) is symmetric.

For \(\alpha=\beta=j>0\), with \(s=t=0\), the normalized product is exactly
\[
(1-2/q)1_{p^j\mid r}+q^{-2}1_{p^{j-1}\mid r}. \tag{FR9}
\]
At an unequal embedding, the product instead is
\[
(1-q^{-1})
\left(1_{p^j\mid r}-q^{-1}1_{p^{j-1}\mid r}\right). \tag{FR10}
\]
Both have weighted mass at most \(q^{-j\rho}(1+q^{-1+\rho})\) when \(0<\rho\le1\).

These are products of the actual Ramanujan masks: shared divisors are combined using their maximum exponent before the coefficient mass is taken.

In particular, at \(\rho=1/2\), the one-sided unembedded \(j=6\) contribution, after the outer-annulus denominator \(q^{j/2}\), is
\[
q^{-3}+q^{-7/2}. \tag{FR11}
\]
The shifted embedded contribution is
\[
q^{-2}+q^{-5/2}. \tag{FR12}
\]
The \(p^5\) divisor never receives the \(q^3\) coefficient: its coefficient remains \(q^2\). Replacing it by the larger coefficient and minimum divisor would destroy the useful threshold.

Writing \(\alpha=6a,\beta=6b\), the normalized weighted principal local sum is \(O(q^{-3})\) away from embeddings, because
\[
\sum_{\substack{a,b\ge0\\a+b>0}}q^{-3\max(a,b)}
\ll q^{-3}.
\]
At an embedding prime its possible rebate is only \(q\), and the local sum is \(O(q^{-2})\). Higher principal powers are strictly more convergent. More generally these Euler sums converge for every \(\rho>1/6\), with uniformly bounded factors at the fixed number of embedding primes.

## Seven other author first tests and two critic audits

S01's original recurrence is FALSE. At x=4 the principal values M=-1,M(2)=0,R_2=0 and quadratic-mod3 values M=2,M(2)=2,R_2=1 contradict it. The repaired identity M=R_p-chi(p)R_p(./p), its finite power inverse, and S16's complete finite-P divisor/smooth inverses are correct. Their full absolute costs product(1+p^-gamma) and product(1-p^-gamma)^-1 diverge through all unramified primes at gamma<=1. Fixed-P and sufficiently restricted moving-P strategies remain eligible; unbounded is not synonymous with unaffordable at every-epsilon scale.

S58 is a valid actual-character counterexample: the acyclic two-term identity boundary has ordinary supertrace0, but weights(1,chi(2)) for fixed quadratic-mod3 give2. The weight operator is not a chain map. S51's product-cutoff scalar equals M, and for a principal character it is minus the reduced Euler characteristic, including the empty face. General character weights need full weighted boundaries and cannot borrow ordinary homological cancellation. S54's determinant1 only records a triangular diagonal; it controls neither off-diagonal singular growth nor the readout. A specified regularized infinite determinant remains eligible.

S31 and S26 correctly reuse G82: on squarefree units in[X,2X], every Gaussian Gram entry is at least log2*g_tau(log2)^2. The coherent all-ones quotient has orderX, and the unrestricted operator bound on the actual coefficient vector has bill orderX^2. This is not a lower bound for its signed scalar. No phase-restricted arithmetic uncertainty theorem or full dual certificate is disproved merely by this test.

Critic audit S09 proves that the true coefficient-prefix prime shifts commute for all N, p, q and ordinary chi, since pqn<=N puts both intermediate indices in the prefix. The literal four-sector rough reconstruction also commutes. This defeats the proposed noncommuting gap for that implementation. A non-divisor-closed mask can fail commutation, but the example{1,2,6} omits the actual n=3 source and must restore it. The shared critic already checked finite commutation within D22; this audit gives the all-prefix statement and its exact limitation.

Critic audit S38 computes [P_X,chi(p)V_p]e_n=-chi(p)1_(X/p<n<=X)e_(pn). Its ordinary trace after multiplication by any finite Dirichlet-convolution matrix is zero, since the product strictly raises indices. The actual summed-coordinate readout is -chi(p)[M(X)-M(X/p)]. With quartic-mod5, p=2,X=4,N=8 this readout is1 while the ordinary trace is0. A new bound on the full signed difference would return M by telescoping with cost1/(1-p^-gamma), gamma>0. That arithmetic estimate is unpaid. Adjoints, other projections or another source-compatible trace remain eligible after their identities and complements are specified. This is a precise scoped failure, not a universal commutator no-go.

statement:
## 2. S04: a quantitative actual-source obstruction to short-range positive metrics

Fix an ordinary Dirichlet character chi modulo q, with its natural nonunit zeros. Put a_n=mu(n)chi(n), 1<=n<=N, and let ell be the all-ones column. A global terminal certificate is a Hermitian matrix P satisfying

    P >= ell ell*, so |M_chi(N)|^2 <= a* P a.                 (1)

The inequality is a matrix inequality on all input vectors. All statements in this section also hold after deleting the forced-zero coordinates and restricting P and ell to S={n<=N:a_n!=0}; bandwidth is still measured in the original integer labels. The proofs use only that support and N as an upper bound on dimension. A certificate required only on a separately proved reachable class is a different, potentially weaker condition. P may depend arbitrarily on N, chi and the actual coefficients. No independence or ignorance restriction is imposed.

### 2.1 Exact block optimum

For any partition into nonempty coordinate blocks B_j, write b_j=sum_(n in B_j)a_n and B=sum_j|b_j|. Then

    inf_(P block diagonal, P>=ell ell*) a*Pa = B^2.           (2)

For the lower bound, multiply a by one scalar phase on each block so that its block sums align. The quadratic energy of a block-diagonal P is unchanged, while its required readout majorant becomes B^2. For the upper bound when every b_j!=0, take block P_j=(B/|b_j|)ell_j ell_j*. Weighted Cauchy gives P>=ell ell* because sum_j |b_j|/B=1, and its actual energy is B^2. Zero block sums are handled by assigning them an arbitrarily small share of this reciprocal-weight budget and taking a limit. If every b_j=0, any sufficiently large finite block weight attains energy zero. Thus (2) is an infimum; no invertibility or false universal attainment is assumed.

This is an exact signed-block target. Optimizing a positive block metric cannot improve on the complete sum of absolute block sums. It extends G129's singleton/diagonal optimum; it does not estimate those block sums.

### 2.2 Isolated squarefree coefficients force a banded price

Let h>=1 be an integer. Call n in [h+1,N-h] isolated if n is squarefree, n=1 mod q, and every n+r with 0<|r|<=h is nonsquarefree. Let I be any set of such indices and K=|I|. If P in (1) has half-bandwidth h, namely P_nm=0 when |n-m|>h, then

    a*Pa >= K^2.                                            (3)

Indeed, |a_n|=1 for n in I, every other actual nonzero source coordinate is more than h away from it, and distinct members of I are more than h apart. Hence the actual cross terms between I and its complement vanish, and P_II is diagonal. The principal submatrix inequality P_II>=ell_I ell_I* implies, by evaluation on ell_I, sum_(n in I)P_nn>=K^2. The remaining principal block is PSD. Its actual energy is nonnegative, so (3) follows. This proof retains all squareful and nonunit zeros; no cancellation outside I is discarded as an assertion about M.

Here is a completely elementary supply of such indices. For each r in {-h,...,-1,1,...,h}, choose a distinct prime p_r>h not dividing q. Set

    Q=q product_r p_r^2,
    n=1 mod q,     n=-r mod p_r^2 for every r.                (4)

CRT gives one residue a0 modulo Q and gcd(a0,Q)=1: p_r cannot divide r, and the q-residue is 1. Every shifted n+r is squareful. Count squarefree n in this residue. The exact expansion mu(n)^2=sum_(d^2|n)mu(d), with only gcd(d,Q)=1 contributing, gives uniformly in Q and a0,

    #{n<=N:n=a0 mod Q, mu(n)^2=1}
      = (N/Q) product_(p not dividing Q)(1-p^-2)+O(3 sqrt N),
      >= N/(2Q)-3 sqrt N,       N>=4.                        (5)

For completeness, truncate d at floor(sqrt N). Each compatible congruence modulo Qd^2 costs at most 1 in its count, hence at most sqrt N total. The omitted main sum costs at most 2 sqrt N/Q. Its Euler product is at least 1/zeta(2)>1/2, using sum_(n>=2)n^-2<1. Take I to be the resulting squarefree indices in [h+1,N-h]. Deleting the at most 2h endpoint integers leaves

    K >= max(0, N/(2Q)-3 sqrt N-2h).                         (6)

Neither a prime distribution theorem nor a hypothesis about mu cancellation is needed for (3)-(6).

The primes in (4) can be chosen <=C_q h log(2h). One elementary proof of the needed supply uses

    4^m/(2m+1) <= binom(2m,m) <= (2m)^pi(2m).

Each prime contributes at most 2m to the binomial's factorization, since every term of its valuation sum is 0 or 1. This gives pi(x)>>x/log x. Choosing C_q large supplies 2h distinct primes above h and outside the fixed ramified set. Consequently

    log Q <= log q+4h log(C_q h log(2h))
           =(4+o(1))h log h                    as h->infinity. (7)

For any h_N=o(log N/loglog N), (6) gives K=N^(1-o(1)). Every matrix in (1) with that bandwidth therefore has

    sqrt(a*Pa) >= N^(1-o(1)).                                (8)

For h_N=floor(kappa log N/loglog N), fixed 0<kappa<1/8, it instead gives

    K >= N^(1-4kappa-o(1)),
    sqrt(a*Pa) >= N^(1-4kappa-o(1)).                         (9)

The restriction kappa<1/8 is the range in which the explicit AP main term dominates the sqrt N error. Fixed h gives the stronger K>>_(q,h)N. These are all-large-N certificate statements with fixed q; the constants do not purport to be uniform as q grows.

Thus a bound a*Pa <<_(chi,epsilon) N^(2gamma+epsilon) through this class requires kappa>=(1-gamma)/4 in the regime of (9). This is only a necessary width, never a sufficient arithmetic saving.

| Proposed source exponent gamma | Desired c=1-gamma | Necessary kappa for this bandwidth class |
|---|---:|---:|
| A strict gain below .8748540364 | >.1251459636 | >.0312864909 |
| .8748 | .1252 | >=.0313 |
| 5/6 | 1/6 | >=1/24 |
| 3/4 | 1/4 | >=1/16 |

These tests deliberately include a coarse near gain, 1/6 and 1/4. None is obtained.

### 2.3 Pay the nonlocal correction instead of silently deleting it

Suppose P=D+E>=ell ell*, D>=0 has half-bandwidth h, E=E*, and ||E||<=eta in Euclidean operator norm. With the same K isolated actual coefficients,

    a*Pa >= K^2-eta(K+N).                                  (10)

The principal inequality gives sum_I D_nn>=K^2-eta K. Actual cross terms of D involving I vanish, its complementary energy is nonnegative, and a*Ea>=-eta||a||^2>=-eta N. This proves (10), including every correction term. If h=o(log N/loglog N), reducing the full root cost to a fixed exponent gamma<1 requires a nonlocal correction of norm at least N^(1-o(1)) along the lower-bound scale. Small entrywise errors are not enough unless their complete operator cost is also paid.

Scope: (3)-(10) do not lower-bound |M_chi(N)|. Distant isolated terms may cancel against other signed terms. Nonlocal metrics, signed debts and source-only inequalities escape this class. Prime-dilation edges are often long in additive distance, so the bandwidth theorem does not exclude them.

### 2.4 Arbitrary finite translation banks, including large shifts

More generally let D_N be any symmetric set of nonzero integer shifts with |r|<=N-1, and suppose P_nm=0 off the diagonal unless m-n is in D_N. Put k=|D_N|. For each r choose a distinct prime p_r not dividing qr, and impose n=1 mod q and n=-r mod p_r^2. The same CRT argument gives a coprime residue modulo Q=q product_r p_r^2. Every allowed neighbor that actually lies in [1,N] is squareful; neighbors outside that interval are irrelevant. No endpoint deletion is needed. Equation (3) holds for P with this support; (10) holds when its PSD part D has this support and the full E is paid. For the constructed set,

    K>=max(0,N/(2Q)-3 sqrt N).

The prime choices can be bounded uniformly in the actual shifts. At each choice, at most k-1 previously used primes and omega(q)+floor(log_2 N) divisors of qr are forbidden. The first J=k+omega(q)+floor(log_2 N)+1 primes therefore suffice. The elementary prime bound used above gives

    log Q <= log q+2k log(C J log(2J)).

Hence k=o(log N/loglog N) forces Q=N^o(1) and root certificate cost N^(1-o(1)), regardless of how large or data-dependent the allowed shifts are. If k~kappa log N/loglog N with 0<kappa<1/4, the cost is at least N^(1-2kappa-o(1)). A target gamma requires kappa>=(1-gamma)/2 in that range. This counts the TOTAL distinct allowed offsets, not the degree of each row; an arbitrary sparse graph with many different offsets is not covered. The near-local correction still has the full operator bill (10). A finite shift bank cannot escape the obstruction merely by moving its offsets far away.

## 6. Why direct canonical merging remains open

The narrow forbidden import is **equation(B3.6) in sectionB3.2**, not later sectionB3.6. Its squarefree column coefficient is exactly a0(n)nu(n)rho(n)chi_n(k)chi_n(f)^4 d_I(n), where d_I is an original finite product-prime mark. It explicitly permits no further coefficient on n.

For a squarefree unmarked n, double Mellin inversion of its original two-divisor profile gives the multiplicative weight

    eta_(z,w)(n)=product_(p|n)(q_p^(-z)+q_p^(-w)).        (6.1)

The two Mellin variables retain the two independent height coordinates and their original annuli; replacing them by one variable is not valid. With original slots the weight is sum_(P|n) b_tilde(P) eta_(z,w)(n/P). One may retain this deleted-prime form. If one instead factors eta(n), choose separated real contours Re z=kappa, Re w=-kappa, kappa>0 fixed and arbitrarily small. Then

    |eta_(z,w)(p)|>=q_p^kappa(1-q_p^(-2kappa))>0.

Division at forced slot primes is now legitimate and bounded by a fixed kappa-dependent factor per slot. No natural character value is divided out. Eta costs at most tau(n)q_n^kappa; choose kappa only after the bounded scale and finite-depth loss budgets. On coincident real contours eta(p) may vanish, so the same division would be invalid.

This structure survives a COPRIME extraction: eta(fn)=eta(f)eta(n). Thus the two exact Poisson transformations in PR9(B3.12)-(B3.29) retain eta or its conjugate on the residual column; extracted eta(f) factors have divisor/small-power cost. With a completed cube index, primes shared with its cube variable must first be assigned and extracted as in the original proof. These algebraic observations do not prove the full inductive estimate.

Cube inversion(B3.8) itself works for ANY mark d_*(A): on putting c=hb, d_*(nc^3) is independent of h|c and sum_(h|c)mu(h) kills c!=1. So cube inversion is not the missing analytic step. Choose the useful extension eta(p^a)=q_p^(-az)+q_p^(-aw), a>=1. Then eta(A) is the sum over unitary two-color splits A=A1 A2,(A1,A2)=1, with each entire prime power assigned to one color.

If A_i=n_i b_i^3 is the completed theta index, the exact cross coefficient is

    a0(n1n2)=a0(n1)a0(n2) chi_n2(n1)^4,
    chi_A2(A1)^4=chi_n2(n1)^4.                          (6.2)

The equality uses coprimality; cube exponents contribute multiples of6, whose zeros could not be erased without that condition. Thus the weighted completed source is a **coupled coprime convolution of two completed theta coefficient systems**, with the cross phase in(6.2). It is not a product of two independent theta sums. For actual primary primes -2-3omega and1-3omega of norms7 and13, chi_(1-3omega)(-2-3omega)^4=omega, already a nontrivial coupling.

The first unlicensed analytic gate is the terminal application of RE to this weighted completed theta source. PR9(B2.6)-(B2.15) reflects the specified theta Fourier coefficients and allowed product-prime masks. Its permission for a bounded remaining tuple coefficient arises AFTER slot assignment; it does not authorize multiplication of every primal Fourier coefficient by eta. No reflection law for the coupled source(6.2) has been proved here.

Two affordable checks delimit this attempt. For an uncompleted Gauss source with two fixed colors D=Z^x,E=Z^y and row cap Z^M, (4.2) gives energy at most Z^M[D+E+(DE)^(2/3)] up to small powers. This is exactly what pays the restricted sector above, but not the full first dual range. Alternatively, Cauchy over the shorter color, followed by canonical(B3.7) where its margins hold, costs Z^(x+y+min(x,y)). The whole shorter-color factor is real; label averaging in(B3.6) does not remove it.

Even an optimistic extension giving the unchanged single-inverse free-row exponent e(L)=(1+5L)/6 at merged inverse length L=r+s would not by itself meet the present target. Since EK<=rho+delta v,

    e(r+s)-T >= 1/6+(5/6-delta)(r+s)-rho-delta v
              >=1867/27000>.0691;                     (6.3)

with v=0 the lower gap is703/6750>.1041. The right side decreases in delta on this box, increases in r+s and decreases in v, so the bounds follow at delta=.7,r+s=2.17,v=.05 or0. This is an inadequacy of that merged-norm route, not a lower bound on actual R4 and not permission to dominate a signed subset by a full norm. A successful full approach must retain extra two-color/dual structure, or improve more than just the coefficient contract.

\]

The real saving \(\sigma\) is common; constants and polynomial height costs may depend on fixed targets/data as permitted in M B0.7. statement:
# Actual signed Hankel source: paid Type I and frequency complements

Status: actual restricted arithmetic estimates, with a complete remaining signed operator. **No bound for the remaining operator and no larger zero-free constant are proved.** The current source-relative c11=.1251459636 and gamma11=.8748540364 remain unchanged, including inherited ancestry, positive-slot uniformity and external admission obligations.

The useful result is a derivative-free Type I removal for the integrated plain-L2 Hankel operator, followed by a paid high-frequency complement. It uses the actual truncated reciprocal convolution, not a free coefficient model. Nonprincipal characters can use the original source directly. A literal fixed dilation of the original source supplies the all-character version. Its changed coefficients and zero-exclusion return are explicit. An actual positive semiprime corner shows why the remaining source cannot be paid one arithmetic sector at a time.

The exact convolution identity and prime-local mean-zero repair already occur in DP21--22 and W29 review Section7. Those ancestors paid a smooth atomic H0^r form using Poisson summation and derivatives. The claim here is their specific integrated plain-L2 completion, with a complete frequency complement and an actual large-sector obstruction. There is no literature-priority claim and no claimed transfer to native Eisenstein H.

## 1. Literal source and complete truncated identity

Fix an ordinary character chi modulo q, including principal or imprimitive characters. Put

    a(n)=mu(n)chi(n),       a0=a 1_(n<=Y), a1=a 1_(n>Y),
    1_chi(n)=chi(n),        Y>=1 an integer.

All squareful and nonunit zeros remain in a. Dirichlet convolution gives a*1_chi=delta_1, and hence the exact identity

    a = 2a0 - a0*a0*1_chi + a1*a1*1_chi.              (H1)

To check it, expand a1*a1*1_chi=(a-a0)^2*1_chi=a-2a0+a0*a0*1_chi. No coprimality filter is introduced between the two factors. Both ordered d/e placements and shared primes remain. Individual convolution terms need not inherit all original squareful zeros; H1 preserves them after its complete signed recombination.

For any sequence z let Z(x)=sum_(n<=x)z(n), zero for x<1, and let Gamma[z]_(a,L) denote the full Hankel operator with kernel exp(-a(t+u))Z(exp(t+u)) on L2(0,L). The fixed real weight a lies in (0,1); context distinguishes it from the coefficient sequence a(n) and its truncations a0,a1. Write X=exp(2L). Complex characters use the same bilinear convention as G149, without conjugating the source.

## 2. A shift lemma that pays a genuine Type I operator

Suppose a restoration sequence b has bounded partial sums

    B(y)=sum_(ell<=y)b(ell),  B(y)=0 for y<1,
    sup_(y>=0)|B(y)| <= C_b.

Extend h_b(v)=exp(-av)B(exp(v)) by zero for v<0. Then

    ||h_b||_L1(R) <= C_b/a.                            (H2)

For each integer k>=1 the kernel exp(-a(t+u))B(exp(t+u)/k) equals k^-a h_b(t+u-log k). Reflect and zero-extend one input to R, then apply the ordinary L1--L2 convolution inequality. Translation on R costs no norm. Thus its FULL L2(0,L) Hankel norm is at most C_b k^-a/a, independently of L and k. This argument retains all off-diagonal rectangles and uses no derivative or smoothness norm of the test functions.

For A_Y(a)=sum_(d<=Y)|mu(d)chi(d)|d^-a <= C_a Y^(1-a), H2 gives

    ||Gamma[a0*a0*b]_(a,L)|| <= (C_b/a) A_Y(a)^2
                              <<_(a,b) Y^(2(1-a)).   (H3)

This is an actual restricted arithmetic estimate: cancellation in the complete restoration partial sum B precedes absolute summation over the short factors. It is not obtained by replacing b(ell) with its magnitude.

For nonprincipal chi, finite-period orthogonality gives |sum_(n<=y)chi(n)|<=q. Take b=1_chi in H1. A finite atom z(n) contributes a shifted kernel with L1 norm |z(n)|n^-a/a, so

    | ||Gamma[a]_(a,L)|| - ||Gamma[a1*a1*1_chi]_(a,L)|| |
      <= (2/a)A_Y(a)+(q/a)A_Y(a)^2
      <<_(a,q) Y^(2(1-a)).                            (H4)

This directly concerns G149's ORIGINAL mu(n)chi(n) source for every fixed nonprincipal character. It does not assume cancellation in either long factor.

### The actual principal obstruction

Principal characters cannot simply inherit H4. At Y=1 their removed coefficient sequence is 2delta_1-1_chi, with partial sum 2-C_chi(x). Since C_chi(x)=(phi(q)/q)x+O(q), its Hankel operator contains a nonzero rank-one kernel -(phi(q)/q)exp((1-a)(t+u)), plus a uniformly bounded remainder. Its norm is therefore

    (phi(q)/q)(exp(2(1-a)L)-1)/(2(1-a))+O_(a,q)(1).

This is an ACTUAL source term of H1, not a toy kernel imported from elsewhere. A positive budget for that term misses every gamma<1. The full long-factor term may cancel it, so this is not a lower bound on M_chi or the complete source.

## 3. An all-character repair with its literal coefficients

Choose a fixed prime r not dividing q and set

    kappa=delta_1-r chi(r)delta_r,
    c=kappa*a,
    c(n)=mu(n)chi(n)-r chi(r)1_(r|n)mu(n/r)chi(n/r),
    b=kappa*1_chi,
    b(ell)=chi(ell)-r chi(r)1_(r|ell)chi(ell/r).       (H5)

The coefficient r is essential. This is a declared changed source, not c=a. Ramified zeros remain; c can be nonzero at some squareful integers, exactly as the displayed second term prescribes. Nothing silently discards those coefficients.

For every chi, b is periodic with period qr and mean zero. Write
C_chi(y)=delta_(chi principal)(phi(q)/q)y+E_chi(y), |E_chi(y)|<=q.
The principal main terms cancel because chi(r)=1 in that case; the nonprincipal main term is already zero. Thus

    B(y)=C_chi(y)-r chi(r)C_chi(y/r),
    |B(y)| <= q(1+r)=:C_b.                            (H6)

Convolving H1 with kappa gives the full identity

    c=2kappa*a0-a0*a0*b+a1*a1*b.                     (H7)

Let T_(Y,L)=Gamma[a1*a1*b]_(a,L). H2--H3 and the exact atomic mass of kappa give

    | ||Gamma[c]_(a,L)|| - ||T_(Y,L)|| |
       <= (2/a)(1+r^(1-a))A_Y(a)+(C_b/a)A_Y(a)^2
       <<_(a,q,r) Y^(2(1-a)).                         (H8)

In T the actual cumulative kernel is

    exp(-av) sum_(d,e>Y,de<=exp(v))
          mu(d)chi(d)mu(e)chi(e) B(exp(v)/(de)),
    v=t+u in [0,2L].                                 (H9)

Equivalently it is the full ordered d/e/ell sum with de ell<=exp(v). Exact bounds are d,e<=X/(Y+1), ell<=X/(Y+1)^2. Both inequalities and every cofactor label are retained. Removing ell=1, shared-prime terms or a selected prime class would change H9.

### Complete return of this replacement detector

Initially Re(s)>1, sum c(n)n^-s=m_r(s)/L(s,chi), with m_r(s)=1-chi(r)r^(1-s). The G149 full-rectangle argument applies to this integrated source because its coefficients are bounded by 1+r. Its exponential test gives

    Q(z)=-d/ds [m_r(s)/(sL(s,chi))], s=a+z.           (H10)

All zeros of m_r have Re(s)=1. If the full Gamma[c] growth is O_(chi,epsilon)(exp(2(gamma-a+epsilon)L)) for every epsilon, G149 makes Q holomorphic to Re(s)>gamma. Any L zero in gamma<Re(s)<1 produces an uncancelled pole in H10. The already accepted source-relative exclusion to the right of gamma11 covers Re(s)>=1; this safe-region input and its inherited obligations are explicitly retained. Hence the new complete growth estimate would exclude every L zero to the right of gamma<gamma11. The principal pole at1 is not a zero. All fixed finite heights and literal imprimitive factors remain. No height-uniform inverse bound is asserted. The argument does not assume a new arithmetic estimate from the old zero-free premise.

This is a new source's complete bridge, not an unproved norm comparison back to Gamma[a] for principal characters. For nonprincipal characters H4 alternatively stays with the original G149 operator.

## 3A. Two actual large-factor sectors are also paid

Decompose the exact H9 form into the diagonal d=e, the off-diagonal sector gcd(d,e)>R, and the remaining d!=e, gcd(d,e)<=R, for a fixed shell threshold R>=1. Every sector retains the WHOLE b-restoration before an absolute bound. There is no inference from a signed-subset norm inequality.

For the diagonal the cumulative coefficient is

    sum_(d>Y,d^2<=x) mu(d)^2 chi(d)^2 B(x/d^2),

of modulus at most C_b sqrt(x). Thus its full Hankel norm is bounded by

    C_b integral_0^L exp(2(1/2-a)t)dt.               (H9a)

At a=1/2 this is C_b L; below1/2 it is O(X^(1/2-a)), and above1/2 it is O(1). Shared-prime squareful contributions were retained and bounded, not silently declared zero.

For the high-gcd sector, writing d=gu,e=gv and dropping restrictions only inside a positive count gives

    #{d,e:de<=x,gcd(d,e)>R}
      <=sum_(g>R) #{u,v:uv<=x/g^2}
      <=x(1+log x)sum_(g>R)g^-2
      << x(1+log x)/R.

H6 and the rank-one exponential envelope therefore prove the FULL operator estimate

    ||T_(d!=e,gcd>R)||
      <<_(a,q,r) X^(1-a)(1+log X)/R.                 (H9b)

This includes every ordered high-gcd pair and every restoration index. It is a restricted actual-source theorem for the integrated ordinary-character detector; it is not payment of a native H gcd sector.

Let T^0_(Y,R,L) retain exactly d,e>Y, d!=e and gcd(d,e)<=R in H9. The complete norm difference from T is at most the sum of H9a and H9b. The remaining genuine low-gcd signed interaction has not been estimated.

## 4. An actual high-frequency complement, with its endpoint retained

Put C_(Y,R)(n)=sum_(de ell=n,d,e>Y,d!=e,gcd(d,e)<=R)mu(d)chi(d)mu(e)chi(e)b(ell), and S_(Y,R)(x)=sum_(n<=x)C_(Y,R)(n). These are exactly the remaining coefficients of T^0. To shorten formulas in this section write C_Y,S_Y for these MASKED coefficients; both masks remain in every sum. Keep the complete observed kernel

    k_(Y,X)(v)=exp(-av)S_Y(exp(v)) 1_(0<=v<=log X).

Its compressed Hankel operator is precisely T^0_(Y,R,L), since t+u ranges over [0,log X]. No time rectangle was removed. With Fourier convention hat k(tau)=integral_R k(v)exp(-i tau v)dv and s=a+i tau, direct integration of every finite cumulative atom gives

    hat k_(Y,X)(tau)
      = [F_(Y,X)(s)-X^-s S_Y(X)]/s,
    F_(Y,X)(s)=sum_(n<=X)C_Y(n)n^-s
      =sum_(d,e>Y,d!=e,gcd(d,e)<=R,de ell<=X)
           mu(d)chi(d)mu(e)chi(e)b(ell)(de ell)^-s.    (H11)

The second term in the numerator is the EXACT sharp upper endpoint. It cannot be omitted, even if a Dirichlet polynomial estimate looks favorable. An atom at n=X contributes zero to the numerator, agreeing with its support only at the corner t=u=L, a null set for this operator. The unit, natural zeros and ordered/shared factor terms are governed by H5/H7 without additional conventions.

The first actual price is

    sum_(n<=X)|C_Y(n)|n^-a
      <=(1+r)sum_(d,e>Y,de ell<=X)(de ell)^-a
      <<_(a,r) X^(1-a)(1+log X)^2.                  (H12)

Indeed sum_(ell<=X/(de))ell^-a <= C_a (X/(de))^(1-a), and the remaining sum is X^(1-a) sum_(de<=X)1/(de). Bounded B also yields |S_Y(X)|<=C_b #{d,e>Y:de<=X} << C_b X(1+log X). Thus both terms of the exact H11 numerator are paid, and

    |hat k_(Y,X)(tau)|
       <<_(a,q,r) X^(1-a)(1+log X)^2/(1+|tau|).

Define T^lo_(Y,R,L,Omega) and T^hi by multiplying this COMPLETE symbol by 1_(|tau|<=Omega) and 1_(|tau|>Omega), respectively, on the full line, then reflecting/zero-extending the input and compressing the output to (0,L). These are Fourier multiplier operators on L2(R) before compression; the low-frequency kernel need not be causal or supported in [0,log X]. Their sum on the observed square is exactly T^0; write T^lo and T^hi for this masked operator from now on. Plancherel and the norm-one reflection/extension/compression give

    ||T^hi|| <<_(a,q,r)
         X^(1-a)(1+log X)^2/Omega, Omega>=1.          (H13)

This estimate retains the sharp endpoint and the complete coupled product cap. It does not infer a square-root operator saving from a scalar average. The coefficient bound is deliberately absolute AFTER the genuine Type I cancellation; it is enough to pay this high-frequency complement.

Combining H8, H9a--b and H13 gives the complete norm comparison

    | ||Gamma[c]_(a,L)|| - ||T^lo_(Y,R,L,Omega)|| |
      <<_(a,q,r) Y^(2(1-a)) + D_a(X)
           +X^(1-a)(1+log X)/R
           +X^(1-a)(1+log X)^2/Omega,                (H14)

where D_a(X)=integral_0^L exp(2(1/2-a)t)dt, with its continuous value L at a=1/2.

For every nonprincipal character the same sector and frequency arguments may instead follow H4 with b=1_chi, C_b=q and c=a. Thus H14 also holds for the ORIGINAL mu(n)chi(n) source in that case, with those substitutions. The changed-source bridge H10 is needed here only to supply a single treatment that includes principal characters.

A low-frequency bound must therefore apply to the ENTIRE operator with symbol H11, including its endpoint subtraction and all signed interactions. A uniform bound on that full symbol for |tau|<=Omega is a stronger sufficient condition by Plancherel, not an equivalent replacement for the compressed operator target. Values at a few frequencies, dyadic diagonals or independently favorable arithmetic sectors do not suffice.

One can also factor the uncut causal kernel exactly as h_b convolved with the finite atomic measure sum_(d,e>Y,d!=e,gcd(d,e)<=R,de<=X)mu(d)chi(d)mu(e)chi(e)(de)^-a delta_(log(de)). The cap is hyperbolic, not the square of a rectangular polynomial. Estimating that unobserved infinite-tail extension directly gives a weaker frequency bill. H11 instead cuts the completed kernel at its true observed endpoint and explicitly pays the resulting defect. No factor or endpoint is silently dropped.

## 5. Quantitative first-gain and higher-reach corridors

Fix 0<a<gamma<1 with gamma>1/2 and a small positive margin nu<min(gamma-a,gamma-1/2). For large X set

    Y=floor X^delta, delta=(gamma-a-nu)/(2(1-a)),
    R=floor X^omega, Omega=X^omega, omega=1-gamma+2nu.             (H15)

Then H14 costs O_(a,q,r,nu)(X^(gamma-a-nu)): the diagonal is smaller by gamma-1/2, and the high-gcd and high-frequency terms have exponent gamma-a-2nu before their logarithms, which fit the spare nu. The unresolved complete estimate is only

    ||T^lo_(Y,R,L,Omega)|| <<_(chi,epsilon)
          X^(gamma-a+epsilon), X=exp(2L), all L.     (OPEN-LOW)

By H14 this is equivalent, at the stated big-O scale, to the complete Gamma[c] growth input. It returns zero exclusion through H10 and G149. It remains UNPROVED. Parameters are fixed before X and constants/onsets may depend on chi; gamma is common. At a=1/2 the following exact choices show the available budgets:

|gamma|c|nu|delta, lower d/e cutoff|upper d/e exponent|upper ell exponent|omega, gcd and frequency cutoffs|paid error exponent in X|open exponent in X|
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
|.87485|.12515|.00005|.37480|.62520|.25040|.12525|.37480|.37485|
|5/6|1/6|1/600|199/600|401/600|101/300|17/100|199/600|1/3|
|3/4|1/4|1/1000|249/1000|751/1000|251/500|63/250|249/1000|1/4|

The corresponding growth exponents in L are twice the last column: .7497, 2/3 and1/2. Only the first is just below the current .7497080728 threshold. These are conditional targets, not new constants. No power saving is obtained by decreasing a alone.

## 6. The strongest arithmetic obstruction: an actual semiprime corner

The mean-zero restoration is not oscillatory in every active range. Exactly B(y)=1 for 1<=y<2, since b(1)=1 and there are no other terms. Thus the top product band exp(v)/2<de<=exp(v) in H9 sees no restoration cancellation. Its coefficient remains the signed self-convolution of the actual long Möbius factors.

There is a quantified principal-character obstruction to treating its prime-prime portion as an independently affordable sector. Fix q, use its principal chi, and let P_X be the unramified primes in

    sqrt(3X/5) < p <= sqrt(7X/10).

For any of the H15 choices, these primes exceed Y for all large X. Let J=[L-c,L], with c=(1/2)log(5/4). On J by J, x=exp(t+u) lies in [4X/5,X], while every ordered distinct p,p' in P_X has product in (3X/5,7X/10]. Therefore 1<x/(pp')<2, and its FULL restoration sum equals1. Since mu(p)mu(p')chi(pp')=1, the exact isolated sector kernel on that square is

    |P_X|(|P_X|-1) exp(-a(t+u)).                      (H16)

The prime number theorem [NIST DLMF27.2.3](https://dlmf.nist.gov/27.2.E3), verified in the primary source, gives |P_X| asymptotic to
2(sqrt(7/10)-sqrt(3/5))sqrt(X)/log X. Removing fixed ramification changes nothing. Testing on exp(-at) restricted to J therefore gives the lower bound

    ||isolated actual sector|| >=
      |P_X|(|P_X|-1) X^-a (exp(2ac)-1)/(2a)
      >>_(a) X^(1-a)/(log X)^2.                     (H17)

This sector cannot separately meet X^(gamma-a+epsilon) for gamma<1 and sufficiently small epsilon. The statement concerns an ACTUAL restriction of H9, with its full restoration, not a synthetic oscillatory example. It is NOT a lower bound for the entire T, Gamma[c], Gamma[a], or T^lo. These distinct-prime pairs have gcd1, so they survive both paid arithmetic-sector removals. Moreover their own sharp-cutoff Fourier high-frequency norm is O(X^(1-a)/(Omega (log X)^2)): in H11 their weighted coefficient mass and endpoint are each O(X^(1-a)/(log X)^2). Hence H17 also survives on the ISOLATED low-frequency prime-pair operator when Omega tends to infinity. Other actual arithmetic sectors may cancel it, and they must remain jointly inside OPEN-LOW. No positivity or signed-subset inheritance is invoked. The useful reopening condition is an estimate for their joint low-frequency operator, retaining those cross-sector cancellations; the pure prime-prime sector itself is not a viable separately paid target.

## 7. Evidence, limits and handoff

The Type I estimates H3/H4/H8, actual diagonal/high-gcd estimates H9a--b and high-frequency complement H13 are proved above for the exact source. The small exact helper checks truncated-convolution coefficients, squareful/nonunit restoration, principal/complex/imprimitive periods, exact cumulative endpoints and the hyperbolic kernel factorization. Finite checks do not establish the asymptotic OPEN-LOW estimate. The only external analytic input in the restricted lower bound H17 is the stated prime-counting asymptotic; H2--H15 need neither a prime number theorem nor a Möbius saving.

Ancestry: DP21--22 owns the reciprocal convolution and period-two repair; W29 review R29E1--E7 owns the smooth Sobolev Type I route and its signed long-factor target. [restricted research revision] G149 owns the integrated full-rectangle growth return. The precise contribution submitted here is their actual plain-L2 Type I estimate, the complete hyperbolic high-frequency payment, the narrowed OPEN-LOW input and the actual positive semiprime-sector obstruction. Whether this merits a new mathematical cycle is the controller's decision; no cycle or theorem admission is asserted here.

No native H masks, coefficients or estimates are borrowed. No full mu(n)chi(n) arithmetic norm saving is obtained. The next work is a genuinely signed estimate for the complete low-frequency hyperbolic operator, or a replacement source whose equivalent complement can be paid with stronger arithmetic cancellation. Merely revisiting H10, improving a toy operator, or bounding the isolated positive prime sector cannot complete that task.

### 3.1 Green comparison and the loss

Translate a maximizer t0 to0. A length-one interval I containing0 lies in [-1,1]. Put h=f/f(0), A=log(B/|f(0)|), v=A-log|h|. If f is analytic on a neighborhood of the closed disk of radius R>=16 and has no boundary zero, then v>=0 and

    v(z)=H(z)+sum_a G_R(z,a),
    G_R(z,a)=log |(R^2-conj(a)z)/(R(z-a))|,
    v(0)=A.                                                  (Q1)

The sum is finite and counts multiplicities. Removing the disk Blaschke factors proves the identity; H is the positive harmonic extension of the nonnegative boundary data. The logarithmic singularities at real zeros are integrable. Since f(0) is nonzero, a=0 never occurs.

For H, the Poisson kernel gives H(t)<=((R+1)/(R-1))H(0). For a zero with |a|<=sqrt R,

    G_R(t,a)-G_R(0,a)
      =log|1-conj(a)t/R^2|+log|a|-log|t-a|.

The first term is <=R^(-3/2). If |a|<=2, the integral of -log|t-a| on any unit interval is <=1+log2: setting Im(a)=0 can only increase it, and centering the real singularity maximizes it. Adding log|a|<=log2 leaves a bound below4. If |a|>2, |t-a|>=|a|-1 gives a pointwise log ratio <=log2. Since G_R(0,a)>=.5 log R, the integrated difference is at most (8/log R)G_R(0,a).

For |a|>sqrt R the Green function is positive harmonic on the smaller disk. Its Harnack ratio is at most (sqrt R+1)/(sqrt R-1)<=1+8/log R. The same larger factor bounds the ratio for H. Summing Q1 proves precisely

    integral_I log|f| >= log|f(0)|
                       -(8/log R) log(B/|f(0)|).             (Q2)

No assumed zero separation, zero density, multiplicity cap or positivity of f enters. Boundary zeros can be avoided by choosing a radius within the allowed interval; discrete zeros prohibit only finitely many radii there. The proof is stronger evidence than the author's finite Green samples, which are only diagnostics.

For fixed coefficients with A_b=sum |a_n| n^(-b)<infinity, completing the square yields

    |F(z)| <= (2pi tau)^(-1/2) A_b
       exp(b Re z+tau b^2/2+(Im z)^2/(2tau)).                 (Q3)

It also proves locally uniform convergence and entire analyticity. For f3(n)chi(n), b>1 suffices and |a_n|<=1. Let M_j=max_[j,j+1]|F| and J_j=integral_[j,j+1]log|F|. The nonzero Mellin transform on Re(s)>1 proves F is not identically zero; therefore J_j is finite and M_j>0. Choose R in[sqrt j,2sqrt j] avoiding boundary zeros. Q3 gives log B <=(b+2/tau)j+O(sqrt j+1). Thus

    (1+eta_j)log M_j <= J_j+eta_j log B,
    eta_j=8/log R=O(1/log j).                                (Q4)

For each fixed gamma, J_j<=(gamma+epsilon)j+C_epsilon on EVERY sufficiently large integer interval implies log M_j<=(gamma+epsilon)j+O(j/log j). Use a smaller epsilon first. The reverse bound J_j<=log M_j is immediate. Constants are fixed before j grows. Negative contributions near zeros cannot mask a larger exponential maximum in this fixed Gaussian class.

There is also an immediate complete-moment equivalence worth making explicit. Jensen on a unit interval gives

    J_j <= .5 log integral_[j,j+1]|F(u)|^2 du.                (Q5)

A fixed number of complete dyadic log shells covers that interval. Consequently an all-shell moment exponent gamma implies the signed-log bound; Q4 returns the pointwise exponent, which implies the moment bound. Every-epsilon allowances absorb the fixed coverings and o(j) loss. Thus L6 is a new exact description of the same exponent problem, not evidence that the arithmetic hypothesis is weaker in consequence. Finite intervals, a subsequence, or an average over j do not suffice.

### 4.2 Complete Mellin scalar and height tails

Let a in (0,1) be fixed. The entire Mellin transform of S_tau is
E_tau(s)eta(s), obtained first at Re(s)>1 and then by continuation
using the Gaussian left tail and rapid right decay. Therefore the
finite primitive pair polynomial C_ij^6 gives

    P_Z^rect(y)=(2pi)^(-1)integral_R D_Z^6(t)y^(a+it)dt.

No interchange of the alternating Dirichlet series on Re(s)=a<1
is needed. Squaring and integrating on the actual local shell gives
exactly GC19, with kernel

    [ (2Z)^(2a+i(t-t'))-Z^(2a+i(t-t')) ]
                  / [2a+i(t-t')].                      (C9)

The denominator has nonzero real part 2a; in particular t=t' does
not create a singularity. Gaussian height decay and the finite pair
polynomial justify the double integral absolutely. Neither the
gcd condition nor the two independent heights factor out.

The alternating partial sums of b have modulus at most one, giving
|eta(a+it)|<=|a+it|/a. Also, because all retained products are below
Z exp(3H), absolute pair summation gives

    sum_{all retained ordered pairs} (de)^(-a)
       <<_a (Z exp(3H))^(1-a) (1+log(Z exp(3H))).

This estimate safely enlarges the subset of integer pairs; no
arithmetic cancellation is used. Multiplication by y^a gives
Z^(1+o(1)). The remaining tail integral has Gaussian factor
exp(-tau t^2/2) times a fixed polynomial in t. Cutting at
|t|=D sqrt(log Z) therefore costs

    Z^(1-tau D^2/2+o(1))=Z^(-A_0+o(1)).                ([restricted research revision])

For the capped coefficient Fourier form, the finite absolute mass
is at most B(1+log B)^2=Z^(1+o(1)); its Gaussian height tail gives
the same exponent. These are two paid field presentations, not an
assertion that their arithmetic coefficients are termwise equal.

# Independent W65 audits before author outcome intake

Selection at 2026-10-13T02:14:58Z used only deliberate IDs S02/S26/S23
and six-test IDs S02/S26/S23/S10/S22/S19. Frozen priority therefore selects
protected S17; frozen uniform order selects DISTINCT S24. No entropy was
generated again. This file is frozen before reading any author report,
test mathematics, checks, or outcomes. Prior exposure is in prep.md.

## S17: Farey transfer and the literal discontinuous observable

Fix an ordinary Dirichlet character chi modulo q with natural zeros.
Define the complete denominator-weighted primitive count

    A_chi(x)=sum_(1<=b<=x) chi(b) #{1<=a<=b:gcd(a,b)=1}
            =sum_(b<=x) chi(b) phi(b), phi(1)=1.

The equality retains a=b=1. For b>1 the endpoint a=b is not primitive.
Using phi(n)=sum_(d|n)mu(d)(n/d) gives the exact finite decomposition

    A_chi(x)=sum_(d<=x)mu(d)chi(d)
                    sum_(m<=x/d) m chi(m).                       (A1)

Multiplicativity is valid even at ramified factors, so no character zero
is divided out. On Re(s)>2 the absolutely convergent Dirichlet series is

    sum_n chi(n)phi(n)n^-s=L(s-1,chi)/L(s,chi).                    (A2)

Both (A1) and (A2) are exact. No Euclidean-algorithm spectral theorem has
yet been shown to apply to their observable. In the principal q=1 case,
the count of primitive ordered pairs 1<=a,b<=x is 2A_1(x)-1. This follows
by reflecting across the diagonal and retaining its unique point (1,1).

**Actual-source discontinuity obstruction.** Let B be any continuous
complex-valued function on [1,infinity). For each prime p not dividing q,
the jump of A_chi at p has modulus p-1. If
|A_chi(x)-B(x)|<=C x^gamma for every sufficiently large REAL x, then taking
the left limit and value at p and using continuity gives

    p-1 <= 2C p^gamma.                                         (A3)

There are arbitrarily large primes outside the finite set dividing q.
Thus gamma<1 is impossible in this precise pointwise norm. The same proof
works for every fixed ordinary chi, not merely a changing conductor or
a synthetic sequence. It does NOT obstruct an averaged count, a Riesz
source, a discontinuous explicitly paid boundary term, or a different
observable. It is not a lower bound on M_chi.

This pinpoints the missing transfer in a naive dynamical-gap proposal.
After dividing the count by x^2, the actual jumps have order 1/x at primes.
A continuous approximation with error O(x^(gamma-2)), gamma<1, is still
impossible. Any claim using a Banach space embedded in that uniform norm
must either smooth first or retain the jump channel. Mixing alone cannot
remove it. This statement does not assume that every transfer space has
such an embedding.

For principal q=1, elementary Möbius inversion already gives

    A_1(x)=x^2/(2 zeta(2))+O(x log(2x)).                         (A4)

Indeed sum_(m<=y)m=(floor(y)^2+floor(y))/2=y^2/2+O(y);
the finite d-sum in (A1) costs O(x sum_(d<=x)1/d), and extending the
main coefficient sum mu(d)/d^2 costs at most O(x). These are complete
estimates including real floors and the d>x tail. They show exactly where
a coarse absolute inversion stops; the inadequate upper bound alone is
not a signed lower bound.

**A lawful smoothed repair.** For integer r>=1 put

    R_r(x)=1/r! sum_(n<=x)chi(n)phi(n)(x-n)^r.

For Re(s)>2, Fubini and the beta integral give

    integral_1^infinity R_r(x)x^(-s-r-1)dx
       = [L(s-1,chi)/L(s,chi)]/[s(s+1)...(s+r)].                 (A5)

The lower limit may be replaced by zero since R_r=0 there. At x=n the
new summand is zero; thus R_r is continuous. Every normalization factor
and each endpoint is explicit. Suppose an explicitly known source P_r
has a meromorphic transform and that the COMPLETE difference satisfies

    integral_X^(2X)|R_r(x)-P_r(x)|dx/x
        <<_(chi,r,epsilon) X^(r+gamma+epsilon)                 (A6)

for every epsilon>0 and all sufficiently large dyadic X. Summing the
shell transforms, including any fixed s derivatives, continues the
remainder normally to Re(s)>gamma. All finite initial intervals are
entire. At a hypothetical L-zero rho, (A5) contradicts this continuation
only if the numerator L(rho-1,chi) is nonzero and P_r's transform has no
matching pole there. Those conditions must be proved for the actual
family; this audit does not import a functional equation or a dynamical
gap theorem without its hypotheses. The principal pole/main terms must
be included in P_r. This is a conditional source return, not an estimate
of (A6), and not a completed Mertens inversion.

Verdict: the raw continuous-boundary uniform transfer fails on the actual
source at every gamma<1. The smoothed or boundary-completed dynamics route
remains live, with (A5)-(A6) its concrete unpaid interface. Near gamma11,
5/6 and 3/4 all require the same complete exponent budget r+gamma; no new c.

## S24: full replica determinant and an ambient sparsification cost

Fix real x>=1. Let I={n<=x:mu(n)^2=1,(n,q)=1}, K=|I|, a_n=mu(n)chi(n),
and u_n=1 for n in I. All other original coordinates are exactly zero.
Their removal from this algebra does not alter M=sum_n a_n. Each retained
|a_n|=1, and the full 2-by-2 Gram determinant is

    det [[K, M],[conjugate(M),K]]=K^2-|M|^2
         =sum_(m<n in I)|a_m-a_n|^2=:D.                        (B1)

Expand each squared difference: the diagonal contribution is K(K-1),
and both cross orientations give |M|^2-K. No diagonal or cross term has
been discarded. Gram positivity says 0<=D<=K^2, which only gives |M|<=K.
For principal chi, with K_+ and K_- the two parity counts,

    D=4K_+K_-,  |M|^2=(K_+-K_-)^2.                            (B2)

Hence a useful determinant estimate is the ONE-SIDED lower bound
D>=K^2-C x^(2gamma+epsilon). A generic upper estimate on the replica norm
has the wrong direction. Counting squarefree units by
mu^2(n)=sum_(d^2|n)mu(d) gives K=kappa_q x+O_q(sqrt x), kappa_q>0;
all floor errors and the absolutely convergent d^-2 tail cost O_q(sqrt x).
The diagonal baseline therefore has exponent two. None of this lower-
bounds the actual signed M. It identifies the precise arithmetic task.

**New scoped check of sparse replica replacement.** Take ANY simple
undirected d-regular graph on these K vertices, 1<=d<=K/2, adjacency A_G,
and L_G=dI-A_G. The complete graph Laplacian is L_c=KI-uu*. A rescaled
edge observation has Laplacian L_t=(K/d)L_G. Its difference is

    L_t-L_c=-(K/d)[A_G-(d/K)uu*].                              (B3)

Let lambda_2,...,lambda_K be the remaining real adjacency eigenvalues,
including any further d-eigenvalues if the graph is disconnected.
Trace(A_G^2)=Kd, so sum_(j>=2)lambda_j^2=d(K-d). Consequently

    ||L_t-L_c|| >= K sqrt((K-d)/(d(K-1))) >= K/sqrt(2d).         (B4)

This is an exact trace argument, with no existence or quality claim about
expanders. The usual source-independent comparison
|a*(L_t-L_c)a|<=K||L_t-L_c|| cannot CERTIFY an error at most
C x^(2gamma+epsilon) unless

    d >= C'_(q,C) x^(4-4gamma-2epsilon).                      (B5)

The inference concerns the ceiling supplied by this uniform operator
norm method: its best possible norm times K is at least K^2/sqrt(2d).
It is NOT a lower bound on the error for the actual mu*chi vector. A
source-specific signed comparison may be far smaller and remains live.
Arbitrary weighted/nonregular sparsifiers are outside the stated theorem.

At current gamma11=.8748540364, the degree exponent in (B5), before
arbitrarily small losses, is .5005838544. At gamma=5/6 it is 2/3; at
gamma=3/4 it is 1, excluding degree O(x^(1-delta)) for any fixed delta>0
under an every-epsilon target. Degree x^(1-o(1)) is NOT excluded.
Thus a bounded-degree replica graph cannot cheaply inherit the full
readout merely through ambient spectral approximation. Paying its exact
source-specific discrepancy instead is the concrete repair target.

The COMPLETE inequality D>=K^2-C x^(2gamma+epsilon), if proved for every
fixed chi and all large x/every epsilon with common gamma<gamma11,
would give M_chi(x)<<x^(gamma+epsilon) (rename epsilon after the square
root). Abel summation then continues 1/L via
s integral_1^infinity M_chi(x)x^(-s-1)dx to Re(s)>gamma, with every finite
height, ramified zero and initial term preserved. Multiplying by L and
using the identity theorem excludes its zeros there; the principal pole
at1 is allowed. No such inequality is proved here.

Verdict: replica algebra alone removes no arithmetic obligation. The
specific regular-graph comparison has a quantified density cost; the
source-specific signed discrepancy and near-maximal replica energy are
still legitimate development targets. G121's cutoff rank and G164's
boundary trace are ancestry, not this exact graph calculation. No global
novelty or first-gain claim is made.

### Complementary characters and all-height return: accept, without deleting a branch

For each N use the root branch exactly when |A_N|>=8 and |A_N|^2>=8B_N. Otherwise

    |A_N|<=max(8,sqrt(8B_N))<=8+sqrt(8N),
    M_chi(N)=1-A_N+R_N(-1).                          (R6)

For fixed1/2<gamma<1, the complete two-branch hypothesis is

    non-root branch: |R_N(-1)|<<_(chi,epsilon)N^(gamma+epsilon);
    root branch:    |A_N Q_N(-1)|<<_(chi,epsilon)N^(gamma+epsilon).
                                                               (OPEN-FD)

It is equivalent to the full all-integer Mertens exponent for this chi: (R6) pays the unit/prime complement at exponent1/2; (R3) handles the root branch with absolute constants. The reverse follows by subtraction in (R6) and the lower inequality in (R3). Arbitrary branch switches are allowed, but every sufficiently large N in BOTH branches is required. It is not enough to prove a principal, density-one, averaged-character or root-branch-only estimate.

The all-height return is complete. If the same gamma works for every fixed ordinary chi and every epsilon, then

    F_chi(s)=s integral_1^infinity M_chi(x)x^(-s-1)dx

is holomorphic on Re(s)>gamma. M_chi(x)=M_chi(floor x), so the integer estimates cover all real x. On each compact subset choose epsilon below its distance from the boundary; derivatives merely introduce integrable logarithms. On Re(s)>1, absolute interchange and (mu chi)*chi=delta give F=1/L. The meromorphic identity L F=1 then excludes zeros throughout the half-plane. A principal pole is a removable reciprocal zero, not an excluded zero; s=0 is outside this positive half-plane. Every fixed height and every imprimitive character is retained. Constants/onsets may depend on chi. There is no growing-conductor or Hecke extension.

OPEN-FD is an exponent-equivalent new representation, not a weaker proved arithmetic estimate. Exact root isolation is mathematically constructive, but neither efficient computation nor an error bound for numerically approximated Q(-1) is supplied.

## 5. Raw rows and finite inducing cores

Write w=u v0^6, retaining its unit in free u. At fixed v0 the actual slots are the natural slots for u with the additional fixed holes at primes dividing v0. This is a row-independent puncture in that free sum, and its size is polynomial. The primitive positive-real zeros are unchanged. The pointwise estimate is still the original physical-row estimate; equivalently finite prime deletion changes a centrally normalized slot by O(P^(-1/2)log Z), paid by an arbitrarily small power. No sixth-power hole is erased.

Put s=log_Z Nv0 and V=W-6s. For V>=20W/21 and z<=W/21, one has z<=V/20, so (R9) applies. The root dyad count contributes s, giving

    rho W+gamma z-(6rho-1)s.

This is summable because rho>=19/54>1/6. The free width here stays uniformly positive relative to W. For V<20W/21, use the old unmarked free density with the physical pointwise slot price; the exponent is at most

    rho W+delta z-(rho-1/6)W/21
       <=rho W+gamma z.                               (R10)

The last comparison follows from z<=W/21 and
rho-1/6>=5/27>1/8>eta; the explicit slack is 13/216. For V below a fixed tiny fraction of W, use the absolute free count; its excess is absorbed by this slack. Remaining V have compact uniformity. Bounded free windows and fixed-inducing free cores cost Z^(W/6+delta z+epsilon). Their infinite raw sixth-power multiples are counted, not declared finite. Literal canonical eligibility is preserved.

Thus (R9) holds for the actual raw row family with z<=W/21. Constants depend on a fixed finite parent dictionary and the indicated profile orders, not a growing family of parent conductors. Whole-character conjugation and fixed unit sectors do not change this contract.

Write `M` for [the merged manuscript](../../zeta_zero_free_validated_merged.md),
`CP` for [cubic packets](../cubic-packets.md), and use the
normalizations of [BC](../[private research revision]/cubic-mobius-core-moment.md),
[DQ](../[private research revision]/cubic-dual-classes.md), and
[PS](../[private research revision]/parameter-and-square-row-interfaces.md).
Ideal columns occur once through good primary generators. Element rows
retain every unit and every fixed-prime valuation. All characters have
their original zero extensions.

The inputs are M (B0.3), **UM**, and its common-scale consequence (B0.8);
the original coefficient and Poisson identities CP21--CP25; and the
original rapid two-endpoint column profile `W0` and Schwartz row kernel
`Rhat`. Fixed finite ray components have the scope already separated in
BC section 8. In particular, the core twists used here have finite
order. The angular cube factor remains outside the core moment.
This is a deduction relative to those inherited inputs. No uniform
Hecke moment in a new family is postulated. **I-HECKE is used only for
the numerical comparison in section 6, not for the new estimate.**

Fix `0<gamma<1`, `0<delta<1-gamma`, a fixed finite collection
`mathscr D` of quadratic square classes, and

\[
1\le K\le D^{1-\delta},\qquad
\Lambda^3=\frac{D^{1-\delta}}{\max(K,D^\gamma)}.
\tag{SR1}
\]

A class is represented by a fixed element `d`, squarefree away from
the fixed primes, with fixed unit and fixed-prime parity choices.
It consists of the nonzero rows `n=d a^2`, with all allowed `a`.
There is **no** imposed `(d,a)=1`. One may also retain any subset of
these rows, such as the cube-free ones.

Let `Q_CC[mathscr D,Lambda;>D^gamma]` mean the exact C--C Poisson
expression restricted to

* the original squarefree cores `q_c,q_e>D^gamma`;
* the original outside cube labels `q_B,q_E<=Lambda`;
* after the C--C forced frequency is written `h=R0 n` as in CP23--CP25,
  the rows `n` in these fixed quadratic classes.

Every total-column coprimality condition is retained. The independently accepted
estimate is

\[
\boxed{
 |Q_{CC}[\mathscr D,\Lambda;>D^\gamma]|
 \ll_{\mathscr D,\delta,\gamma,\epsilon,\mathrm{orig}}
 D^{2+\epsilon}.}
\tag{SR2}
\]

The same proof permits additional row-independent frozen deletion
ideals of polynomial norm, with subpower costs, and the prescribed
fixed profile/height parameters with a common polynomial height cost.
It does not permit arbitrary row-dependent coefficients or growing
families of square-class representatives in the implied constant.

This is a genuine infinite dual-row subfamily: for a fixed `d`, its
rows of norm at most H number `O_d(H^(1/2))`. On the cube-free part
`n=d a^2`, with `a` squarefree and coprime to fixed `d`, the moving
good conductor has size comparable to `sqrt(q_d H)`. Thus the estimate
is not obtained by freezing the full dual conductor.

external factor changes length, twists, zeros and profiles (A2--4);

1.1 requires fixed theta>.55 and gives a logarithmic relative error;

frequency. Lemma 3.1 has restrictions on P,Q,H and an explicit

in its proof. These statements do not furnish the required power for
(R6) or (R12). Their errors cannot be silently relabeled as X^gamma.

version is imported here.

The only prime-counting input for (R19) and the author's obstruction is
ordinary PNT. I checked its statement at equation (1.1), printed 305,
in Selberg's original
[An Elementary Proof of the Prime-Number Theorem](https://www.math.lsu.edu/~mahlburg/teaching/handouts/2014-7230/Selberg-ElemPNT1949.pdf),
Annals 50 (1949), 305–313. Partial summation gives the fixed-proportion
interval counts used above. No short-interval or progression-uniform

small-divisor square for a Gaussian kernel with flatness and growing
derivative bounds. Those statements do not transfer to this nonlinear
kernel's discrete stationary frequencies. Conversely this pass does not
improve their Gaussian estimate. The valid new record is the nonlinear
restricted estimate, its completely paid complements, and the exact
asymmetric regrouping and scoped cancellation above. No literature
priority is asserted for the identities or the methods.

The positive-component and negative-cross conclusions have ancestry in
the project's earlier signed-source work. Their concrete arithmetic

representation; they do not retire those earlier architectures. The
finite two-prime argument is a clean boundary repair, not arithmetic

remain available at their recorded scopes.

n=720, exact integer/complex-character values, real cutoff endpoints,

budgets. It also verifies all nine immutable source pins. It ran once,

with the selected-cell wording qualification; accept (R4) for general

### D02.2 Absolute coefficient and inverse budgets

For sigma>2/3 put d=Q^-sigma and r=Q^(3-6sigma). Since r<Q^-1 and d<Q^-2/3, the local Dirichlet-series weighted coefficient norms satisfy

    ||h_p-1||_sigma <= [r+t(d+r)/(1-d)]/(1-r) =: B_p^+,
    ||h_p^-1-1||_sigma
       <= [t d+(1-t)r+d r]/[1-(1-t)d-t r] =: B_p^-.       (2.4)

The first bound follows from (2.1) after removing 1-t^2. For the second, subtract 1 from (1-D)(1-R)/(1-(1-t)D-tR); the numerator is -tD-(1-t)R+DR. Its denominator is expanded in its actual convergent geometric series. Indeed

    (1-t)d+t r <= Q^(-2/3)+Q^-2 <= 2^(-2/3)+1/4 <1.

No local zero is hidden in the inverse. Both B_p^+ and B_p^- are

    O_sigma(Q^(-1-sigma)+Q^(3-6sigma)).                    (2.5)

Ideal counting N_K(T)=O_K(T) implies convergence of their sums. Therefore there are multiplicative, exact ideal coefficients h(a), j(a), with h*j=delta_1 and

    A_sigma=sum_a |h(a)| Na^-sigma <infinity,
    B_sigma=sum_a |j(a)| Na^-sigma <infinity.              (2.6)

For example A_sigma<=product(1+B_p^+) and B_sigma<=product(1+B_p^-). The products converge locally uniformly for Re s>2/3. Thus **the literal H_eta and its reciprocal are holomorphic and nonzero there**, with this coefficient proof; the source's previously used .87 half-plane is not the limit of this Euler correction. This does not extend the physical contour boxes, source moments or PR9 endpoint argument.

There is a real boundary to this absolute method. The exact sixth coefficient is

    h(p^6)=t a^6+(1-t)b Q^3.                              (2.7)

Its magnitude is at least (1-Q^-1)Q^3-Q^-1. The prime-ideal harmonic series diverges (equivalently, use the source's prime ideal theorem), so sum |h(a)|Na^-sigma diverges for sigma<=2/3. This only obstructs the stated absolute coefficient norm. It is not a lower bound on the signed Gaussian field or a universal c<=1/3 barrier.

statement:
## 2. Exact full-energy compression, including every cross term

For this section only, coefficients may be any fixed complex sequence with
|a_n|<=1. Define N=X^b, X>=2. Expansion of the absolutely convergent square
gives the exact kernel

    K_X(n,m)=integral_1^2 exp(-(n+m)/(N u^b))
                       exp(-i(n^k-m^k)/(X^k u^k)) du/u.

For n!=m, put v=u^(-k). Integration by parts gives

    |K_X(n,m)| <= C_(b,k) min(1,X^k/|n^k-m^k|).              (5)

Indeed the amplitude on the fixed interval [2^(-k),1] is
exp(-A v^(b/k))/(kv), A=(n+m)/N. Its two endpoint values and the integral
of its derivative have a bound depending only on k. In fact this positive
amplitude is decreasing in v, so endpoint sum plus total variation equals
twice its value at 2^(-k), at most 2^(k+1)/k. The trivial integral bound is
log 2. Thus (5) is uniform in n,m,X and pays
the changing damping exactly, rather than freezing its profile.

For a real M>=2 let W_<=M be the same source with the SHARP, shell-fixed
cutoff n<=M, and define E_<=M by its whole-shell squared norm. Let

    D_>M(X)=sum_(n>M)|a_n|^2 K_X(n,n).

Every off-diagonal term not already in E_<=M has max(n,m)>M. Since for
integers n>m>=1,

    n^k-m^k >= n^(k-1)(n-m),

absolute summation of all these terms yields

    |E_chi(X)-E_<=M(X)-D_>M(X)|
      <= C_(b,k) X^k sum_(n>M) n^(1-k) sum_(h=1)^(n-1) 1/h
      <= C'_(b,k) X^k M^(2-k) log(2M).                     (6)

This pays the complete core/tail cross energy as well as the tail's
off-diagonal energy. In particular, it does NOT identify a diagonal with
a lower bound without first proving the error estimate. There is no
finite physical truncation and no discarded future tail. Taking limits
from finite sums is licensed by the damping and the summable majorant
in (6), since k>2. Also D_>M<=C_b X^b. Therefore

    E_chi(X) <= E_<=M(X)+C_b X^b
                       +C_(b,k)X^k M^(2-k)log(2M).          (7)

The same equation bounds E_<=M above by E_chi plus the error, because
D_>M>=0. Thus this is stronger than a norm triangle estimate and has no
unpriced cross term.

For k=6,b=3/2 and M=X^r the only paid exponents are

    diagonal 3/2; cross/tail off-diagonal 6-4r.             (8)

The earlier linear phase has no such summable n^(1-k) tail. This is the
substantive change of source geometry. Taking M=X in (7), E_<=M<=M^2 log2
gives the unconditional generic bound E_chi(X)<<X^2 log X+X^(3/2).
It already improves the old linear generic exponent 5/2, but does not
reach the first-gain threshold 1.7497080728.

## 8. Compensation: the three rates must remain distinct

The prefix asymptotic above is independent of the accepted ordinary
Mertens baseline. The compensation uses SP10 and \(F(x)\ll x^\beta\), giving
\(\|S\|_2\ll_\epsilon X^{\beta+\epsilon}\).
Put \(m_z=\|P_z\|_2\), \(n_z=\|Q_z\|_2\),
\(s_X=\|S\|_2\). Uniformly,
\[
 m_z\asymp X/(Lt^2),\qquad |m_z-n_z|\le s_X .
\]
For a sufficiently small fixed epsilon, \(s_X/m_z\to0\).
The one-sided normalization is
\[
 \frac{\Re\langle P_z,Q_z\rangle}{m_z^2}
 =-1+\frac{\Re\langle P_z,S\rangle}{m_z^2}
 =-1+O_\epsilon(X^{-.1251+\epsilon}Lt^2).           \tag{RNR22}
\]
The exponent here is linear, not doubled. For the symmetric energy,
\[
 \frac{2\Re\langle P_z,Q_z\rangle}{m_z^2+n_z^2}
 =-1+\frac{s_X^2}{m_z^2+n_z^2}
 =-1+O_\epsilon(X^{-.2502+\epsilon}L^2t^4).
\]
For \(\rho_z=\Re\langle P_z,Q_z\rangle/(m_zn_z)\),
\[
 0\le1+\rho_z
 =\frac{s_X^2-(m_z-n_z)^2}{2m_zn_z}
 \ll_\epsilon X^{-.2502+\epsilon}L^2t^4.            \tag{RNR23}
\]
The actual norms, not their asymptotic leading expressions, occur
in these exact identities. Renaming epsilon after squaring is
legitimate by starting with a smaller fixed epsilon.

For a complete target \(s_X\ll_\epsilon X^{\gamma+\epsilon}\),
\(\gamma=.87449\), both
\[
 |m_z-n_z|\ll_\epsilon X^{\gamma+\epsilon},\qquad
 1+\rho_z\ll_\epsilon X^{2\gamma-2+\epsilon}L^2t^4  \tag{RNR24}
\]
are necessary and together sufficient. Necessity follows from the
same identities and the reverse triangle inequality. For sufficiency,
the first estimate ensures \(n_z\asymp m_z\), and
\(s_X^2=(m_z-n_z)^2+2m_zn_z(1+\rho_z)\).
The improved squared rate would be \(-.25102\), still unproved.

This compensation algebra is already [restricted research revision] DR12–13. Its new input
here is the much deeper, actual current-SP prefix and the location
of its complementary labels. Canceling only RNR2's displayed main
term would leave an error bound of exponent1, not the required
field power. That is a limitation of the proved error bound, not
a lower bound for the actual error.

## G122. Radical support and all low/high crosses

If n!=1 and N(rad n)<=R, every squarefree divisor lies inside the plateau
of V. Thus exactly, including the endpoint,

    A_R(n)=sum_(d|rad n) mu(d)=0.                     (3)

Consequently b_l!=0 implies N(rad l)>R. Write l=c a^6 with c sixth-free.
Since rad l divides ca, Nc Na>R. This is stronger than the support
inequality Na>(R/Nc)^(1/6). It requires the merged convolution, not a
separated divisor dyad.

Project the actual merged columns onto Nc<=C0=U^lambda<R. For each row
and every required derivative, (1) gives

    |partial F_lo,u|
      << H_J U^((sigma-1/2)v+epsilon)
         sum_(Nc<=C0) (Nc)^(-sigma)
         sum_(Na>R/Nc) (Na)^(-6sigma)
      << H_J U^((sigma-1/2)v+epsilon) R^(1-6sigma) C0^(5sigma).

The source's linear ideal count proves the inner convergent tail by
partial summation. The outer sum is bounded by the integral of
x^(5sigma-1), with constants uniform on the fixed real interval. Extending
both positive sums to all ideals is allowed. All roots, late scales,
shared slot primes and exceptional rows are included. Therefore

    N(F_lo) << H_J U^[1+2t(1-6sigma)+10sigma lambda
                                      +(2sigma-1)v+epsilon].    (4)

At t=4/3,lambda=6/5, the exponent decreases with sigma, with derivative
-4+2v<0. Its nominal lower-edge value is

    L_lo=5/3-2delta+delta v.

A downward real buffer raises it by at most4h0. Every low/high cross term
is paid by the Hilbert triangle inequality

    sqrt(N(F))<=sqrt(N(F_hi))+sqrt(N(F_lo)).            (5)

Squaring costs only a fixed factor2. No slot-amplitude lower bound,
division by Q_u, or favorable sign of a cross term is used.
