## 5. R1–8 and wildcard02: exact failure scope

For finite P, f_P retains f3 on P-smooth integers and zero elsewhere. Its Euler series E_P has the author's factors at all prime powers and is absolutely convergent for Re(s)>0. Weighted Gaussian Fubini and Plancherel prove

    ||e^(-sigma u)V_P(u)||_2^2
      =e^(tau sigma^2)/(2pi)
         integral_R e^(-tau t^2)|E_P(sigma+it)|^2 dt.       (Q13)

For n<=P the coefficient is exactly f3(n). Taking P_X=ceil(2X exp(C sqrt(log X))) puts all missing coefficients in a decreasing full Gaussian tail, yielding R3 uniformly on the shell. If a polynomial bound ||e^(-sigma u)V_P||<=P^kappa were true, multiplying back by e^(sigma u) on that shell would return exponent sigma+kappa+o(1). The budgets at sigma=.6 are therefore .274861 for a strict first gain, .233333... for1/6, and .15 for1/4. The chosen upper growth of P_X is essential for those numerical costs.

The polynomial certificate is false at each fixed1/2<sigma<1. For p>=5, the absolutely convergent local logarithm gives

    log|(1-2p^(-s))/(1-p^(-s))|
          =-Re(p^(-s))+O_sigma(p^(-2sigma)).

The summed remainder is uniformly bounded. The2/3 factors are nonzero and bounded above/below near t=0 at fixed sigma in that open interval. Uniformly for a in[5pi/6,7pi/6], PNT partial summation gives

    sum_(p<=P)p^(-sigma-ia/log P)
      =P^(1-sigma)/log P * [e^(-ia)/(1-sigma)+o_sigma(1)]. (Q14)

I independently verified the primary input in [Johnston–Yang, arXiv:2204.01980v2, Corollary1.3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2204.01980), PDF page2, header20 April2022, accessed12 October2026. Only pi(y)~y/log y is used. No particular sharp error constant or their other zero-free claims are imported. To derive Q14, discard y<=P^b, b<1 fixed, at cost O(P^(b(1-sigma))); on the rest the PNT error is uniform. Put y=P e^(-v); bounded v contributes e^(-ia) times the integral of e^(-(1-sigma)v), and a fixed then growing v cutoff controls the tail uniformly in a. This justifies the moving height rather than citing a fixed-height asymptotic outside its range.

Since cos a<=-sqrt3/2, there is fixed slack for

    log|E_P(sigma+it)|
      >= P^(1-sigma)/(2(1-sigma)log P)

throughout a t interval of length pi/(3log P). Its Gaussian weight tends uniformly to1. Q13 gives R7 with a fixed positive prefactor, or a slightly smaller exponential constant if desired. The norm is larger than every P^kappa. The negative finite diagnostic at sigma=.874861,P=100000 is correctly retained: the result is asymptotic, with no claimed explicit onset.

This is actual f3/Gaussian forcing, beyond W41-28's nonconvergence of an unrenormalized Euler reciprocal. It does not prove a physical-shell lower bound, nor refute renormalization, a different source norm or causal restriction. Audit30 below further locates the failure. Finite divisor shifts being nilpotent, and Euler factors having finite spectrum{1}, do not control their norm or output. “Signed” alone does not repair the global certificate.

Wildcard02's local Laurent calculation is valid: if L(s)=(s-rho)^m u(s), distinct positive powers L^(-k) have distinct highest pole orders km, so a nonzero coefficient on the highest k cannot be canceled by the others with fixed constants. A nonvanishing Gaussian multiplier preserves it. Inverse Mellin gives x^rho times log-polynomials, not a lower x exponent. This is old amplification/pole-detection mechanism with new arithmetic powers and cross-Grams unpaid; there is no third independent arithmetic gain hidden in it.

# W66 independent review: affordable inversion, paid critical cutoff, open arithmetic

Decision: accept the finite deletion inverse, principal positive-circle obstruction and critical prime-cutoff form bound with its margin debit. No consequential gap found; no arithmetic power saving or new c follows. Current c11=312864909/2500000000=.1251459636, theta11=.8748540364 and inherited F0, positive-slot and external admission obligations remain unchanged.

Independent additions: an exact subpower inversion criterion for FIXED PRIME-DEPENDENT retention, and an exponent-one floor for every positive diagonal weighted Holder/Cauchy principal certificate, including moving retention/weights. Proofs are below; signed centering and the hard-prime inequality remain OPEN.

## 1. Intake, independent audits and sampling

Author report SHA256 821a9486e8c9b409037c89329aad2ef3e9d20ae86b49c3c179c1d1a57471b2fa was read completely (b523e6). ## 2. Independent reconstruction of the author's deletion and parity claims

Let D_X={n<=X:mu(n)^2=1,(n,q)=1}, including1, for fixed q and real X>=1. Let k(n)=omega(n), K_X=max_D k(n), 0<rho<=1, lambda=1-rho and R=(2-rho)/rho. Retain zero outside D_X. The channel and inverse, with ROW d and COLUMN n, are

 B(d,n)=1_(d|n) rho^k(d) lambda^(k(n)-k(d)),
 C(d,n)=1_(d|n) rho^(-k(n))(-lambda)^(k(n)-k(d)).                 (1)

For C B, the intermediate e contributes rho^(-k(e))*rho^k(e); the remaining sum over e/d is (lambda-lambda)^(k(n)-k(d)). For B C the analogous cancellation has the remaining rho^(k(d)-k(n)), which equals1 on the diagonal. Every intermediate divisor belongs to D_X. Thus BOTH products are the identity, with the endpoint rho=1 interpreted by0^0=1. Column sums give exactly ||B||_1=1 and ||C||_1=R^K_X.

Since the product of k distinct primes is at least(k+1)!, K_X<=(1+o(1))log X/loglog X. Fixed rho therefore costs X^o(1). This is the actual size-downset operator, not a full prime cube of dimension2^pi(X); charging exp(c*pi(X)) would be wrong. Conversely rho_X=(log X)^(-b), b>0, has R^K_X=X^(b+o(1)), using K_X~log X/loglog X from primorials and ordinary PNT. The asymptotic prime facts are verified in [DLMF27.12](https://dlmf.nist.gov/27.12), specifically27.12.1 and27.12.4-5. No progression, GRH or growing-q estimate is imported.

The actual input is nu(n)=chi(n) on D_X, not mu(n)chi(n). Its output is

 b_X(d)=rho^k(d)chi(d) sum_(m<=X/d,(m,dq)=1) mu(m)^2 chi(m)lambda^k(m).              (2)

The erased character phase and coprimality are forced, not optional. The observer h(d)=(-R)^k(d) satisfies sum_(d|n)h(d)B(d,n)=(-1)^k(n), since lambda-rho R=-1 at every prime. Hence <h,b_X>=M_chi(X), with ordinary bilinear evaluation, NO conjugation. The complete residual inequality is

 |M_chi(X)| <= |<h,btilde_X>| + R^K_X ||b_X-btilde_X||_1.                          (3)

Every-epsilon bounds on both terms at a common gamma give the full Mertens exponent for all real X and each fixed chi. A selected label set, nonprincipal phase deletion, or omitted approximation error invalidates this return. The construction supplies no such approximation.

Compressing by k(d) gives P_X(z)=Z_X(lambda+rho z), Z_X(z)=sum_D chi(n)z^k(n). This is an EXACT cutoff polynomial; the unrestricted finite Euler product contains products exceeding X and needs its size projection. Evaluation P_X(-R)=M_chi(X) and circle Parseval give |P_X(-R)|<=sqrt(sum_(j<=K)R^(2j)) ||P_X||_circle. At fixed rho the evaluation cost is subpower, but the required whole-circle estimate fails for the actual principal source.

Indeed principal coefficients beta_j are nonnegative and primes contribute lambda+rho z, so beta_0+beta_1>=pi_q(X) for every retention schedule. Thus ||P_X||_circle>=pi_q(X)/sqrt2. Removing all original degrees<=r, fixed integer r>=0, still leaves at least c_(q,r) X/(log X)^(r+1) products of r+1 distinct primes in((X/2)^(1/(r+1)),X^(1/(r+1))]. Each contributes a nonnegative degree-(r+1) coefficient vector of total mass1. Their sum has l2 norm at least its mass/sqrt(r+2). Remaining original layers add nonnegative coefficients. This verifies the author's lower bound uniformly even for X-dependent rho. It is a norm lower bound, NOT a lower bound for its alternating evaluation, not a rejection of growing signed deflation, and not a refutation of G106's exact quotient.

For fixed0<rho<1, cofactor primes give b_X(d)>>X/log X at every fixed label d. This particular lower bound excludes rho=1; the full observer norm is still due there.

## 3. Independent useful survivor: prime-dependent retention and optimal positive price

Fix for each unramified prime p a number0<rho_p<=1. Write lambda_p=1-rho_p and R_p=(2-rho_p)/rho_p. These choices are fixed as X varies for the subpower equivalence below; no common positive lower bound is required. For d,n in D_X define

 B(d,n)=1_(d|n) product_(p|d)rho_p product_(p|n/d)lambda_p,
 C(d,n)=1_(d|n) product_(p|n)rho_p^(-1) product_(p|n/d)(-lambda_p),
 h(d)=product_(p|d)(-R_p).                                                        (4)

All products over1 are1. Prime-by-prime binomial cancellation proves B C=C B=I, exactly as in(1), because D_X contains the entire divisor interval. The exact column sums and observer give

 ||B||_1=1,
 V(X):=||C||_1=max_(n in D_X) product_(p|n)R_p=max_D|h(n)|,
 M_chi(X)=sum_D h(d)b_chi,X(d),                                                   (5)

where b_chi,X(d)=chi(d)product_(p|d)rho_p times the ENTIRE sum over m<=X/d,(m,dq)=1 of mu(m)^2 chi(m)product_(p|m)lambda_p. This retains every natural zero, cofactor and sharp endpoint. It is an exact positive deletion channel acting on a complex source, not a randomness assumption on its factors.

**Exact fixed-prime criterion.** V(X)=X^o(1) if and only if log R_p/log p ->0 along unramified primes. Necessity: take X=p and the column n=p, obtaining R_p<=V(p). For sufficiency, fix epsilon>0 and choose P with R_p<=p^epsilon for p>P. Then every squarefree n<=X satisfies

 product_(p|n)R_p <= [product_(p<=P,p not|q)R_p] n^epsilon <= C_epsilon X^epsilon.  (6)

The finite product is independent of X. Since R_p>=1, this proves the equivalence with no prime theorem. It also proves the exact quantitative statement needed to absorb inversion into every-epsilon estimates. A fresh choice rho_p depending on X is NOT covered by this if-and-only-if criterion; then the maximum in(5) itself is the correct bill.

For example rho_p=min(1,(log p)^(-b)), fixed b>0, tends to0 yet has log R_p=O(1+loglog p)=o(log p), so inversion is subpower. This differs materially from setting the SAME rho_X=(log X)^(-b) at every prime, whose cost in the author's example is X^(b+o(1)). The former keeps small-prime information more faithfully. It is a permissible new source design with the same complete return, not an exponent saving by itself. Under(6), if BOTH |<h,btilde_X>| and ||b_X-btilde_X||_1 are O_(chi,epsilon)(X^(gamma+epsilon)) at every scale, (3) with V(X) proves M_chi(X)=O_(chi,epsilon)(X^(gamma+epsilon)). This arithmetic hypothesis is OPEN.

**Exact positive price, including arbitrary moving weights.** Now permit rho_p=rho_(p,X) to be arbitrary in(0,1] at each X; this next identity does not need the fixed-prime condition. For the PRINCIPAL source b_X(d)>0. Then

 P_abs(X):=sum_D |h(d)|b_X(d)
   =sum_(n in D_X) product_(p|n)(lambda_p+rho_p R_p)
   =sum_(n in D_X) product_(p|n)(3-2rho_p).                                        (7)

Every local factor is in[1,3), so

 #D_X <= P_abs(X) <= 3^K_X #D_X, hence P_abs(X)=X^(1+o(1)),                        (8)

uniformly over all these retention choices at the level of powers, for fixed q. The lower count #D_X=kappa_q X+O_q(sqrt X), kappa_q=(phi(q)/q)product_(p not|q)(1-p^(-2))>0, follows by mu^2(n)=sum_(r^2|n)mu(r), counting q-units in the inner interval, and bounding the r>sqrt X tail by sum r^-2. It needs no PNT. The upper uses only the factorial bound for K_X.

For EVERY positive diagonal weight w_d, even X-dependent and chosen using the source, Cauchy gives

 ||(w_d h_d)||_2 ||(b_d/w_d)||_2 >= sum_D |h_d|b_d=P_abs(X).                       (9)

This minimum is EXACTLY attained by w_d^2=b_d/|h_d|: b_d>0 because the original column n=d contributes product rho_p, and |h_d|>=1. The same lower bound follows for any conjugate Holder pair. Thus optimizing diagonal weights cannot make this raw principal readout power-small, even where inversion is affordable. This is stronger than the author's particular unweighted output/circle certificates, but only concerns those positive separable certificates. It does not exclude nonlocal signed norms, growing signed centering, cancellation between an approximant and its residual, or the original Mertens sum.

There is also a scalar-compression limit for varying rho_p: P_X(z)=sum_(n in D_X)product_(p|n)(lambda_p+rho_p z), so the author's positive prime-layer and fixed-original-layer obstructions still hold by coefficient mass. In general there is NO single z giving the full observer h(d); one must keep the multivariate or labeled readout(5). I do not import the uniform-rho affine formula into this extension.

Finite independent exact checks at X=40, q=1,3,6 and unequal rational retentions (including rho_2=1) confirm both matrix products, norm(5), the complete principal/quadratic readouts and equality(7). Script run once8894af, complete readbackb7022b; independent-checks.json is evidence for those finite cases only. Proofs(4)-(9), not that diagnostic, establish the general statements.

## 4. Critical small-prime payment and complete zero-exclusion return

I read the entire G173 section of [restricted mathematical source] SHA256 c79eb708286dda8231705ec3839ceadc195c170b926564e3f008d51d675e6078. Its source is a(n)=mu(n)chi(n), g(v)=(2*pi*tau)^(-1/2)exp(-v^2/(2*tau)), U(y)=sum a(n)g(log n-y), z=e^(-gamma y)U, fixed tau>0 and1/2<gamma<1. Differentiating g in y gives tau U'+yU=sum a(n)log n*g(log n-y), with the POSITIVE derivative sign shown. The convolution identity turns it into minus all prime-power delays, including j>=2. Completing the Gaussian square gives, exactly,

    J(v)=exp(tau/2)integral_0^infinity h g(h+v-tau)dh>0.

proves

       <=exp(-(v-tau)a/tau-a^2/(2tau))<=exp(-2a).     (R2.7)

Consequently, if q>=exp(3tau), the entire r>=2 contribution to Phi
has absolute size at most

    J(log q)sum_(r>=2)r^(-3)
       <=J(log q)[1/8+integral_2^infinity t^(-3)dt]
       =(1/4)J(log q).

Since f(1)=1,

    Phi(q)>=(3/4)J(log q)>0.                         (R2.8)

# [private research revision]: failed implications, corrected scopes, and surviving exits

The accepted baseline is unchanged. These records distinguish false identities, method-specific counterexamples, incomplete constructions, and open estimates. Full proofs are in the consolidated and auxiliary documents; the portfolio ledger carries the longer idea tree.

Source keys: **M** is the frozen merged proof; **Cj** its cycle-j review; **FD/CP/QD** the sixth-divisor/cubic-packet/quadratic-detector sources; **BA/BB** the A/B brainstorming derivations; **SA/SB/GS** the A/B/Grok solves; **BM** Gemini's brainstorm. The provenance inventory supplies paths. T01–T10 and A01–A18 label this merge.

## 1. Source convergence does not imply continuity of the continued period

**Method-specific obstruction.** Squared shell norms are proportional to \(Q^{-2j}\), while period coefficients have modulus \(Q^{(1-3\sigma)j}\). Thus the squared dual norm contains \(\sum_jQ^{(4-6\sigma)j}\): local boundedness fails for \(1/2<\sigma\le2/3\) at a nonzero base period. The joint-prime product extends failure to \(\sigma\le5/6\), with its nonzero comparison-period qualification. This is the full scalar functional on the specified shell span, not every one-vector restriction, changed graph norm, or squarefree source. Diagonal power weights cannot both repair continuity and retain that full source near the center. An escape must prove its actual source norm and calibrated period bound. [[restricted research revision] AC5–AC10; BB R09; A07.]

## 2. Potential zeros of a fixed completion factor are no longer a separate barrier

**Earlier rejection superseded; component matching remains compulsory.** BM §6 calls division by \(L^S(3s-1,\xi)\) fatal. T01 proves division with polynomial height cost from independent holomorphy, an Euler-product anchor and buffered disk bounds; applying it to an independently uncontinued \(1/\zeta\) would be circular. T02 also supplies a completion-preserving finite selector. Fixed angular division therefore costs no new conductor power. Individual ray components can nevertheless switch their natural completion: multiplying a formal vector by one factor does not identify an actual current period. Require a common convention or explicit restoration of switched factors. [BA R1; BB R01–R02; SB §2; BM R2.2/§6; T01–T02.]

## 3. Conductor, index, physical row length, and mean exponent are different quantities

**Bookkeeping correction, no new estimate.** For \(h=ab^2\), physical norm, primitive good conductor, and reduced sextic index are \(q_aq_b^2,q_aq_b,q_a^4q_b^2\). Reducing \(a^4b^8\) modulo sixth powers proves no AFE of length \(A^2B\). The hypothetical \(|F_{ab^2}|\ll q_aq_b^{1/2}\) gives mean \(A^3B^2\), physical exponent \(3-4z\) for \(B=X^z\); it reaches \(35/32\) only at \(z\ge61/128\). An exceptional set of size \(X^d\) with pointwise exponent \(B\) costs \(X^{d+2B}\), not \(X^{d+B}\). T08's finite incidence is not the infinite trace; its \(g=1\) term already demands a mean through \(K\). Seek the full orientation-sensitive or divisor-conditioned mean. [BA D4–D5/D10; BB R04.a/R05; FD §19; T03/T08; A02.]

## 4. An indefinite covariance cannot be used as a positive calibration Gram

**False generic implication.** Adaptive minimization needs the complete positive physical-field Gram, its principal map, nuisance constraints, nullspace and inverse projected separation. The signed coprime form or incomplete outer field cannot replace it. Gcd restriction is not generally positive: two identical normalized vectors have all-ones Gram, but the small-gcd mask for two large coprime core labels leaves \(\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)\), with eigenvalues \(1,-1\). A localized zero form is therefore not automatically a positive projection. T07 removes the paid complete zero form globally. Retain the physical Gram and prove separation, or estimate the localized signed covariance directly. [BA D6; SA Parts III–V; A04/A15.]

## 5. Paid coherent and same-core sectors do not pay the remaining covariance

**Restricted results proved; larger conclusion open.** BB R08 bounds the unembedded coherent aggregate after each pair's complete zero mode, including its product profile, is subtracted: raw \(O(Z^\epsilon)\), or \(O(Z^\epsilon/Y)\) for squarefree outer columns. Its all-marked extension has \(D=1\); individual frequencies and mixed embeddings are not covered. T06 pays the same-core square function, not cross-core covariance. T07 pays the full long-gcd covariance, not its zero/nonzero pieces separately. The remaining range includes gcd one with no long gcd variable. An embedded extension must derive coherence in actual rows \(e^2r,d^2r\), retain quotient-square marks and reprice coefficients. [BB R08.a–e; [restricted research revision] AA14–AA20; [restricted research revision] AB16; SA Parts III–V; T06–T07/A01.]

## 6. The proposed sixth-power spectral component is not yet defined

**First exact gap.** The label \(k=r^6\) occurs after a Gram expansion into column pairs, with profile \(\sqrt Q\,r^6/(ab)\); it is not a fixed spectral projection of \(A\). GS §2 acknowledges this, but §7 writes \(A^{(6)}\) paired with \(B\) without constructing it. The square-root exponents \(x/2,(y-x)/2,x/2+(y-x)/12\) correctly locate the excess when \(y<2x\), but do not decompose the probe. Retain the full-probe hypothesis \(|I_\eta^{\rm comp}|\ll Z^{x/2+(y-x)/12-\sigma+\epsilon}\). A localized version needs an exact bilinear identity/projector, addbacks and principal calibration. [GS §§2,7; M B0.22; A14.]

## 7. Grok's certificate is valid conditionally; its prose window and decimal claims need correction

**Certified implication, no arithmetic saving.** All 23 checks pass for five targets, strongest \(c=.128,\sigma=.004\), conditional on the full-probe bound for every required family/configuration with M B0.7's profiles, heights and bootstrap ordering. Replace the false derivative claim \(<.043\) by \(<.0441<1/20\); one certified bound is \(0.0440833871\ldots\). At \(c=.1255\), \(y-x=0.08753960844756839075\ldots\), so \(>.08753960845\) rounds the wrong way. The portable script repairs directed signed-rational conversion and output bounds; the original five tests remain valid. The detached window from forcing \(\sigma=(y-x)/12\) is only a saturated-geometry diagnostic: a stronger true estimate may be weakened. [GS §§1–4, scripts/certify_transfer.py; A14.]

## 8. The proposed Deligne saving has no derived trace family and misreads a local case

**Local error and unsupported global implication.** BM §6 assigns \(-q^{-1}\) to AB16 at \(\alpha=\beta=0\), which actually gives the constant kernel and only zero Fourier frequency. The \(-q^{-1}\) unit-frequency value requires equal positive valuations not divisible by six; equal positive multiples of six give \(1-2/q\). A universal local square-root saving is false. Nor does an incidence equation identify a nondegenerate hyper-Kloosterman family. Even a valid complete-sum bound must pay incomplete ranges, composite moduli, exceptional strata, marks and profiles. Derive the actual two-column additive/rational kernel and its conductor/degenerations before claiming \(N/K\). [BM R3.1, §§3,5–6; [restricted research revision] AB16; portfolio F17.T.]

## 9. The asserted prime-square Jacobi identity is false

**Explicit counterexample.** BM claims \(\chi_n(p^2)=\chi_n(-1)e_n(-4p)J_n(8p)\). The correct odd-squarefree identity is \(J_n(t)=\chi_n(-1)e_n(t/2)S(1,t^2/16;n)\), so the proposed right side is \(S(1,4p^2;n)\). At \(n=5,p=2\), it is \((3-\sqrt5)/2\ne1\). The Poisson argument fails before any estimate. BB R14's unit-\(v\) two-parameter identity and inverse-cubic pushforward survive as local constructions; a successor must insert its actual coefficients into a zeta-sensitive detector. [BM R4.1–R4.2, §5; BB R14.a–b; QD; A13.]

## 10. Quadratic characters at prime squares are principal on their unit rows

**Missing principal term and normalization.** For squarefree \(n\), \(\chi_n(p^2)=1_{(n,p)=1}\). If columns satisfy \(n\le2D<p\), every prime has the same weighted Mertens sum, so the moment is the prime count times \(|\sum_n\mu(n)W(n/D)|^2\). BM also omits the actual detector normalization and replaces all-row CM2 by prime-square rows. Its proposed estimate would itself be a strong Mertens theorem; square arguments provide no character oscillation. Retain QD's all-row reconstruction and finite prime-square restoration, or prove a separate normalized detector transfer. [BM R4.2/§3; QD; C9 C1; A13.]

## 11. Unequal cutoffs do not erase the rough return or survive completion for free

**Exact algebra retained; large scales unaffordable.** For \(m_i=\mu1_{n\le Y_i}\), \(u_i=\delta-m_i*\mathbf1\), with \(\delta\) the convolution identity, the identity is \(\mu=m_1+m_2-m_1*m_2*\mathbf1+\mu*u_1*u_2\), not an arbitrary three-factor return. Type I permits \(R=Y_1Y_2\) only at \(\log_D R<\min(1-k,(8-7k)/24)\); for \(k=.87653\), the second bound is .07767875. The proposed cutoff pair with exponents .01 and \(1/3\) has product exponent \(.34333\ldots\) and fails this budget. Fully rough columns \(c=pq,e=r\) retain discrepancy \(-2\) beyond every cutoff in a finite family. Outside cubes also shorten effective core lengths and alter densities, invalidating substitution of a bare small-core identity into a completed coefficient. T05 pays restricted Type I; the signed return remains open. [BM R1.1; BB R04.b; SA [restricted research revision]–[restricted research revision]; CP (20),(27); T05/A16–A17.]

## 12. A source theorem must match the actual coefficient and level family

**Hypothesis mismatch.** SA's smooth-prime gain uses the inherited strip for all relevant finite-order Hecke characters, not only rational zeta. Uniform nonprincipal distribution fails for the moving coefficient \(-\eta_k(p)w(p/P)\): testing against \(\bar\eta_k\) leaves a prime count. A condition \(D\le K\) misses the target \(K<D\); deleting every prime below a growing cutoff need not have the subpower cost of a polynomial-norm radical. An infinity/\(b=1\) H reduction also does not cover every branch or moving current level. The viable child restores resonant tests, retains actual coefficients/masks and proves a coupled estimate in the needed range. [SA Part VI DS1–DS3; [restricted research revision] AC10; FD; A03; portfolio F04.H.]

## 13. Profile annihilation can remove the signal, and moving twists can move a paid root

**Calibration and residue obligations.** T05's paid root \(\widehat W(1)=0\) moves under an arbitrary norm twist, requiring a new residue calculation. In the balanced detector, antisymmetrizing under \(d\leftrightarrow e\) kills the entire symmetric sum. Adaptive annihilators can likewise kill both principal aliases. Fixed roots do not remove every possible zeta pole. By contrast T09's actual Mellin factor is proved nonzero except at the harmless point one, and T10's two multipliers share only \(s=\alpha\), where \(\zeta(\alpha)\ne0\). Keep the calibrated identity and demonstrate retained signal before estimating energy. [SA [restricted research revision]–[restricted research revision]; BA D6/D10–D11; BB R06; [restricted research revision] V1–V10; T05/T09–T10/A04.]

## 14. Correct scale-energy transfers do not prove their power saving

**Open estimates; different scale conventions.** T09a asks for \(\int_X^{2X}|S_\phi|^2dx/x\ll X^{2a+\epsilon}\); its frozen-dyad formula preserves but does not bound that energy. T09b asks for \(\int_Y^{2Y}\int_1^2|P_r|^2dr\,dy/y\ll Y^{2(3-2a)-\epsilon}\) as \(Y\to0\), with \(a>5/6\) ensuring an absolutely convergent nonzero numerator. At \(a=.87449\), the squared exponents are respectively 1.74898 and 2.50204. Neither a Haar coordinate change nor Hölder proves signed triple cancellation. Absolute cube inversion's separate \(5/6\) barrier is an upper-budget limitation, not a lower bound on its signed inverse. Seek the actual signed energy or quantified angular cancellation. [BB R06–R07; BA D7; [restricted research revision]/[restricted research revision]; T09/A05.]

## 15. Compact positivity and one-step improvement do not prove arithmetic approximation

**Valid operator, missing arithmetic convergence.** For \(K_w=\sum_nw_n|f_n\rangle\langle f_n|\), \(R_w(\lambda)=\langle1,\lambda(K_w+\lambda I)^{-1}1\rangle\) tends to the squared distance from \(1\) to the closed arithmetic span. Compact positivity does not prove the sufficient condition \(R_w=o(1)\). Spectral mass must include the zero atom; infinite rank prevents a positive uniform gap, and \(R_w=o(\lambda)\) is impossible by the norm lower bound. Finite truncations certify only their finite-height consequences. An optimal scalar shell step may also freeze an earlier error. Retain the resolvent and least-squares identities; pursue admissible arithmetic wavelets, revisited blocks or cumulative capture. [BB R10–R11; C9 R6–R10; A08–A09.]

## 16. Fredholm regularization moves the unresolved prime term into a compensator

**Exact identity exposes the gap.** For \(T_s=\operatorname{diag}(p^{-s})\), \(\det(I-T_s)=1/\zeta(s)\) initially for \(\Re s>1\). The nonzero regularized determinant \(D_2(s)=\exp(-\sum_{m\ge2}m^{-1}\sum_pp^{-ms})\) extends to \(\Re s>1/2\), but \(1/\zeta(s)=D_2(s)e^{-P(s)}\), \(P(s)=\sum_pp^{-s}\). The compensator carries the unresolved continuation. Bounded similarity cannot change trace-class membership. A different arithmetic operator remains possible, provided its determinant identity and every compensator are controlled; record 15 is a separate valid construction. [BA D9; A12.]

## 17. Semidefinite Hermite–Biehler positivity and positive Fourier measure are insufficient

**Two generic countermodels.** The HB kernel of \(E_0=e^{-iz}\) is positive; multiplication by \(z^2+1\) preserves semidefiniteness but introduces the common upper zero \(i\) of \(E,E^\#\). Strict diagonal positivity or common-zero exclusion is essential. Positive Fourier measure also cannot reverse heat: \(H_t=2+e^t\cos z\), with \(\partial_tH_t=-\partial_z^2H_t\), has nonreal zeros before \(t=\log2\) and real zeros afterwards. Gaussian smoothing preserves the phenomenon, and frequency scaling makes the initial strip arbitrarily thin. An arithmetic xi theorem must use more than positivity. Fixed-degree eventual Jensen hyperbolicity likewise leaves an unbounded degree/shift range. [BB R12.a–b; A10; portfolio F23/F26.]

## 18. Raw prime coefficients and finite experiments cannot replace a limiting criterion

**Pole subtraction and all-height cost remain essential.** Cayley log-zeta and completed Laguerre coefficients give derivative-related versions of a valid criterion. Raw prime sums retain the known pole at one; demanding subexponential growth before principal/gamma subtraction is false even under RH. High zeros may be weak at moderate degree, and individual coefficient contributions can cancel. Radius optimization moves the prime/gamma weights and proves no finite-degree detection theorem. Scripts establish only their stated finite identities or interval inequalities; absent A-solve companion scripts are not independently rerun evidence. Keep the completed criterion and seek a uniform principal-subtracted estimate paying degree, height and radius. [BA D12; BB R13; SA verification claims; A11/A14.]

Let S_p V(x)=V(x/p), a_p=2chi(p), D_p=I-a_p S_p. For an unramified p and sigma below alpha_p=log2/log p, define

    E_p^- Y(x)=-sum_(j>=1) a_p^-j Y(p^j x).

Minkowski on EACH exact shifted real shell proves

    ||E_p^- Y||_sigma <= ||Y||_sigma/(2p^-sigma-1),
                      0<sigma<alpha_p.              (A1)

The series is convergent in local L2. D_p E_p^-=E_p^- D_p=I on this normed space by index cancellation; the latter equality on a source only known at another exponent requires its boundary. The exact finite formula is

    -sum_(j=1)^J a_p^-j D_p V(p^j x)
       = V(x)-a_p^-J V(p^J x).                        (A2)

The current accepted fixed-character baseline provides a buffered exponent beta with theta6<beta<1 for M and F. The standard fixed Gaussian shift is justified by polynomial reciprocal-L growth on a strictly buffered line, or by the fixed-character Mobius summatory input used in the source library. This is baseline evidence, not a new estimate. With p=2, a_p^-J M(p^J x) tends to zero in every fixed local shell since its norm is O_x(2^(-(1-beta)J)). If2 is ramified, D2=I and no inverse series is taken. Thus E2^- D2 M=M as an actual complete-field identity before assuming an improvement.

The T1 Dirichlet identity gives exactly

    F=J_chi * (D2 M),  D2 M=J_chi^-1 * F,             (A3)

where * denotes sum_r j(r)chi(r)V(x/r), with J_chi already including chi in its coefficients if that convention is used. Never twist twice. For either convention, absolute weighted mass at every sigma>1/2 pays every dilation and the Gaussian small-scale tail. This is the same literal K/H ancestry as G28, stated relative to M rather than A.

If F has the all-large-dyadic every-epsilon exponent gamma in (1/2,1), choose gamma<sigma<1 with sigma-gamma as small as needed. Complete small-scale F norms are finite because of its Gaussian tail. A3 and A1 give M at exponent sigma. Conversely M's complete gamma bound gives D2 M by the finite dilation cost 1+2*2^-sigma, then F by J's finite mass. Letting positive buffers shrink proves exact equality of every-epsilon exponent classes. Constants may blow up as sigma approaches1; no endpoint sigma=1 assertion.

The Mellin transform of M is exp(tau s^2/2)/L(s,chi), first on Re(s)>1. A complete shell exponent gamma makes its Mellin integral holomorphic in Re(s)>gamma, with the Gaussian left tail paid and dyadic Cauchy--Schwarz. Multiplying by L shows the nonvanishing exponential cannot coexist with ANY zero there. A principal pole at1 is not a zero and merely gives the reciprocal's zero. This bridge includes multiple zeros and all fixed heights; ramified factors stay literal. No numerator zero or signed tail is dropped.

At target gamma=5/6 or3/4, A1's prime2 costs are respectively 1/(2^(1/6)-1) and1/(2^(1/4)-1), approximately8.17 and5.29. At theta6 the cost is about11; it is fixed, not a power loss. Thus the coarsest sufficient high-ceiling input is simply the complete signed M Gaussian moment at5/6 or3/4. This is not easier by theorem; it is a concrete change of object with a fully paid return. It can combine representations only after their actual coefficient maps are respected.

An explicit second object is f2(n)=mu(rad(n/2^v2(n))). Its complete field F2 obeys D2 F2=D3 F. Both F2 and F have the accepted buffered beta<1 bound: their ratios to mu have only polynomial-growth finite-prime factors and quadratic-start odd-prime corrections absolutely summable at beta>theta6. A2 therefore proves

    F2=E2^- D3 F                                  (A4)

for unramified2; if2 is ramified the equality reduces to F2=D3 F. For sigma>a3, the causal inverse

    E3^+ Y=sum_(j>=0) (2chi(3))^j Y(x/3^j),
    ||E3^+||_sigma <=1/(1-2*3^-sigma)               (A5)

F2's numerator N3 has zeros at a3 only, so its direct zero exclusion above any such gamma is complete. A4 uses future scales rather than an impossible absolute causal inverse at2. Strongest objection: the future-scale inverse could covertly assume the very improvement being proved, or retain a homogeneous state. Signature: object = two complete fixed-character radical fields D2 F and D3 F; transformation = commuting length-two Koszul complex with one future and one past inverse; cancellation = exact signed boundary contraction; first unpaid estimate = complete joint signed moment of both actual channels below theta6; proved return = fixed all-shell reconstruction for a3<gamma<1 and original zero exclusion. Suppose for each fixed chi and every epsilon>0 the COMPLETE joint channel energy satisfies

                    <<_(chi,epsilon) X^(2gamma+epsilon), (B4)

## 3. Two compatible envelopes and fixed finite choices

Normalize to U=Z^M, hence M=1 for choosing fixed numerical data; retain M in ledgers. Put

```
r=9/2-C=33/250, k=309/1000,
b_j=17/500+j/5000, j=0,...,30.
```

For t=z/M use j=1 at t=.034 and otherwise the unique j with `b_(j-1)<t<=b_j`. Set `a_j/M=k b_j`, `sigma_j=3a_j`. The literal pool is `(Z^a_j/2,Z^a_j]` and the map is the source map h to h*p^6.

Writing S=(n1+n2)/M, one has `S<=2N` and `S<=1-Ct`. Therefore both pointwise bounds for A/M=S+t hold simultaneously. On the fixed cell use

```
A/M <= A_j=min(2N+b_j,1-(C-1)b_(j-1)),
g/M <= g_j=r b_j,
g=(n1+n2+(9/2)z-M)_+.
```

The opposite endpoint choices are intentional: the first envelope increases in t, while the second decreases. The minimum of these two cellwise upper bounds is still a valid upper bound for every point of the cell. There is no inference that min of endpoint values equals the true cell maximum. We use the conservative displayed envelope and price its real rounding. Also g/M<=r t, including when the actual old-capacity defect is zero, so g_j is a valid conservative bound.

The exact family satisfies

```
52839/5000000 <= a_j/M <= 309/25000,
max_j A_j=4401/5000=.8802,
max_j g_j=33/6250=.00528,
7 max_j(a_j/M)=2163/25000=.08652<1/4.
```

The actual continuous crossing is `t*=(1-2N)/C=37/1040=.035576923...`, inside cell 8. The conservative envelopes switch between cells 8 and 9. This explains why the worst high and terminal cases move away from the first cell. The proof checks them all rather than transferring [private research revision]'s monotonicity conclusion.

The larger k does not change the source conditions: all sigma_j are fixed positive numbers; a common mesh below `min_j(a_j/M)/10` implies the required sigma gap, and it can be reduced to fit the least reserve. Choose the thirty numerical cases first, then common small budgets and mesh from the requested loss and fixed compact geometry. Fix the finite original slot system and arithmetic family. ## Exact moving Bessel filter

Fix tau>0. Put f(u)=G_tau(e^u) with the exact G1 coefficients

    A(n)=mu(n)-2*1_(2|n)*mu(n/2),
    f(u)=sum_(n>=1) A(n)g_tau(log n-u).

The accepted baseline implies f(u)<<_epsilon exp((b0+epsilon)u) for u>=0.
Each b>b0 is fixed before its constant; there is no b=b0 bound or buffer
shrinking with u. This uses the ordinary Mertens consequence in the
canonical PR9 interface and [private research revision]'s accepted ordinary baseline use
([restricted mathematical source] opening and section OS).
Partial summation gives the f bound with the exact even correction A(n).
The left tail is Gaussian. Its bilateral Laplace transform in Re s>b0 is

    Phi(s)=exp(tau*s^2/2)*(1-2^(1-s))/zeta(s).

Here the continuation below 1 uses the accepted baseline, not absolute
Dirichlet convergence. Let F(s)=integral_0^infinity f(t)exp(-st)dt. Then
Phi(s)=F(s)+E(s), where E(s)=integral_(-infinity)^0 f(t)exp(-st)dt is entire.
In particular F is meromorphic with exactly the same zeta poles in 0<Re s<1.

For a fixed strength h>0, the distribution

    k_h(v)=delta_0(v)-1_(v>0) exp(-v)*sqrt(h/v)*J_1(2sqrt(hv))

has multiplier integral k_h(v)exp(sv)dv=exp[-h/(1-s)] for Re s<1.
For p=1-s,

    sqrt(h/v)J_1(2sqrt(hv))
      =sum_(k>=0) (-1)^k h^(k+1)v^k/(k!(k+1)!),
    integral_0^infinity exp(-pv)sqrt(h/v)J_1(2sqrt(hv))dv
      =sum_(k>=0) (-1)^k h^(k+1)/((k+1)!p^(k+1))
      =1-exp(-h/p).                                       (B0)

Absolute termwise integrals sum to exp(h/Re p)-1, so the interchange is
valid throughout Re p>0. The multiplier has no zeros there; its essential
singularity at 1 is not discarded or called entire.

For A>0 and u>=0 define the actual moving detector

    D_A(u)=f(u)-integral_0^infinity exp(-v)*sqrt(Au/v)
                    *J_1(2sqrt(Auv))*f(u+v)dv.                 (B1)

At u=0 the integral is zero. There are no omitted masks or coefficient
subfamilies: B1 acts on the full fixed Gaussian field. The real-argument
bound |sqrt(Au/v)J_1(2sqrt(Auv))|<=Au gives

    |D_A(u)|<=C_b exp(bu)*(1+Au/(1-b)), b0<b<1.             (B1a)

This proves absolute convergence and the initial half-plane for H. The parameter
A log x is intrinsic to this new detector; G2 cannot simply be asserted for
it. The following separate return calculation is therefore essential.

Let H(w)=integral_0^infinity D_A(u)exp(-wu)du. Swapping the triangular region
0<=u<=t in B1 gives H(w)=integral_0^infinity f(t)K_w(t)dt, where

    K_w(t)=exp(-wt)-exp(-t)*integral_0^t exp((1-w)u)
                     *sqrt(Au/(t-u))*J_1(2sqrt(Au(t-u)))du.

Expand J_1 in K and write p=q+1. For Re q sufficiently large, the integral
part before multiplication by exp(-t) has transform

    sum_(k>=0) (-1)^k A^(k+1)/((p+w-1)^(k+2)*p^(k+1))
       =A/((p+w-1)*(p*(p+w-1)+A)).

Subtracting this from 1/(q+w) gives

    integral_0^infinity K_w(t)exp(-qt)dt
       =(q+1)/((q+1)(q+w)+A).                              (B2)

If s1,s2 solve

    s1+s2=1+w,  s1*s2=w+A,
    w=phi_A(sj),  phi_A(s)=s-A/(1-s),
    sj=(1+w +- sqrt((1-w)^2-4A))/2,

then partial fractions and uniqueness of the ordinary Laplace transform
give K_w(t) as the corresponding combination of exp(-s1*t),exp(-s2*t).
For real w sufficiently large both roots lie to the right of b, yielding

    H(w)=[(1-s1)F(s1)+(s2-1)F(s2)]/(s2-s1).                (B3)

The identity holds on an open neighborhood of that real w and continues
meromorphically. The expression is symmetric
under exchanging roots. When F is holomorphic at their collision, the
apparent branch singularity cancels; its limit is F(s)-(1-s)F'(s).
This removes the initially suspected automatic branch-floor obstruction
for the full signed field. It does not remove genuine singularities of F.

If a zero rho maps to w=phi_A(rho), the other preimage is

    rho*=1-A/(1-rho).                                      (B4)

For any previously possible zero with Re rho<=b0 and 0<Re rho<1, choosing
0<A<c0^2 implies Re rho*>b0: write delta=1-Re rho>=c0 and use
A*delta/(delta^2+(Im rho)^2)<=A/delta<c0. Thus the second root lies in the
accepted zero-free half-plane. It cannot cancel the pole associated with
rho. Also phi_A'(rho)=1-A/(1-rho)^2 is nonzero there. This is one convenient
sufficient parameter condition, not a ceiling: finite-height information
allows larger A in the complete return below.

## 2. The fixed angular sums and the moving deletion

Put
\[
X_0=D^{1/3},\qquad Y_e=(D/q_e)^{1/3},
\]
and define
\[
\begin{aligned}
S_z^-(X)&=\sum_b\xi(b)q_b(q_b/X)^{3z}
                 \overline{W_0((q_b/X)^3)},\\
S_z^+(X)&=\sum_b\overline{\xi(b)}q_b(q_b/X)^{3z}
                 W_0((q_b/X)^3).
\end{aligned}
\tag{UC4}
\]
The established angular argument in
[CS8](../[private research revision]-continuation/cubic-sectors.md) gives,
uniformly for `Re z` in any fixed compact interval and for every fixed
`A > 0`,
\[
|S_z^\pm(X)|
\ll_A(1+|\Im z|)^{C_A}\min(X^A,X^{-A}).
\tag{UC5}
\]
For `X <= 1`, rapid upper-endpoint decay and ideal counting suffice.
For `X >= 1`, the auxiliary column Mellin integral contains the fixed
entire functions `L^S(w-1,xi)` or `L^S(w-1,bar xi)`, and its line moves
to `Re w=-A` without a residue. Their entire continuation and polynomial
growth on each fixed strip are supplied in
[[private research revision] T01](../[private research revision]/[restricted mathematical source]).
The Mellin transform of `u^(3z) W0(u^3)` has an imaginary translation
proportional to `Im z`; integration against the fixed angular function
therefore costs only a polynomial in `Im z`. This argument works on
every fixed compact interval of `Re z`, including the positive strip
used below.

Let `S_z^-(X;e)` be the first sum in (UC4) restricted to `(b,e)=1`.
Open this mask exactly:
\[
\boxed{
S_z^-(X;e)=
\sum_{r\mid e}\mu(r)\xi(r)q_r\,S_z^-(X/q_r).
}
\tag{UC6}
\]
The factor `q_r` is necessary. Formula (UC6), rather than a uniform
rapid-decay assertion for a moving-deleted angular function, prices
the moving deletion.

Insert the exact projector for `(B,E)=1` in (UC3), and write
`B=ell b`, `E=ell f`. The remaining first-column mask is
`(ell,e)=(b,e)=1`. The two angular factors at `ell` cancel. The column
expression after row Mellin inversion is exactly
\[
\begin{aligned}
T_e(z)
&=\sum_{(\ell,e)=1}\mu(\ell)q_\ell^2
 S_z^+(Y_e/q_\ell)S_z^-(X_0/q_\ell;e)\\
&=\sum_{(\ell,e)=1}\mu(\ell)q_\ell^2
 S_z^+(Y_e/q_\ell)
 \sum_{r\mid e}\mu(r)\xi(r)q_r
 S_z^-(X_0/(q_\ell q_r)).
\end{aligned}
\tag{UC7}
\]
The product is at the **same complex `z`**, not an absolute square.
In particular, with matching profiles,
`S_z^+(X)=conj(S_{bar z}^-(X))`. Both factors are bounded separately.

## Source and inherited payment

no signed physical projector is inserted.

T=delta(r+s)+E_K. Retain the exact parameter box

## G209. All thirteen collision types and the exact mixed-order source

At each good prime record its six original site incidences: two inverses
and at most one slot on each copy. Each occupancy is zero or one.
For the thirteen types (a,b) with 0<=a,b<=3 and a+b>=2, let h_ab be the

all named-slot tests and original coefficients remain attached. Define

## 7. A decisive failed finite-inverse inequality on the original data

One tempting shortcut is to use exact finite Dirichlet inversion and
then promote the tiny completed-field error to a tiny operator norm.
The second step is false for the literal W35 coefficients, even at
fixed Gaussian width and zero modulation height. The following proof
does not substitute a generic bounded-coefficient counterexample.

Fix sigma>=0. Let N=floor(B_X), and for any coefficient sequence c
define the N-by-N divisor-convolution matrix and Gaussian readout

    [L_sigma(c)]_(n,m)=1_(m|n)c(n/m)(n/m)^(-sigma),
    [W_X(v)](x)=sum_{n<=N} n^sigma v_n g_tau(log(n/x)),
                                          X<=x<=2X.   (GC23)

The input norm is ordinary l2 on {1,...,N}; the output measure is
dx/x. For the unit vector e_1,

    W_X L_sigma(c)e_1=sum_{n<=N}c(n)g_tau(log(n/x)).

The finite identities are exact:

    L_sigma(mu)L_sigma(1)=I,
    L_sigma(b)L_sigma(mu)=L_sigma(q_2),
    L_sigma(b)L_sigma(mu)^2=L_sigma(A).                (GC24)

Here q_2=delta_1-2delta_2. All factors contributing to an output n<=N
also lie <=N, so truncating the divisor matrices introduces no missing
coefficient in GC24. These identities supply no estimate for the
following output operator difference.

Take c_X(n) to be the EXACT finite literal W35 coefficient from R35.7:

    c_X(n)=sum_{de*ell=n; d,e>Y; de>T_X^prod}
                             mu(d)mu(e)b(ell), n<=N.

It vanishes whenever n<=T_X^prod. At the actual source vector e_1,
R35.17 together with its absolute A-tail bound proves

    ||W_X[L_sigma(A)-L_sigma(c_X)]e_1||_2
                                    << X^(-A_0+o(1)). (GC25)

But the full operator norm satisfies

    ||W_X[L_sigma(A)-L_sigma(c_X)]||_(l2->L2[X,2X])
                                    >=c_(tau,sigma)X^(sigma+1/2)
                                                        (GC26)

for all sufficiently large X. This is incompatible with a proposed
uniform operator version of GC25.

Proof: let M_X be the integers m in

    [2*exp(4tau)*X, 4*exp(4tau)*X].

For sufficiently large X this interval is inside {1,...,N}, since
B_X/X=2*exp(kappa*sqrt(log X)) tends to infinity. Its cardinality
is comparable to X, with constants depending only on tau. Every
column m in M_X of L_sigma(c_X) is zero: a nonzero quotient q would
require q>T_X^prod, whereas m*T_X^prod>N for all sufficiently large
X. This last inequality is just log X>2kappa*sqrt(log X)+O_tau(1).

The corresponding column for A has readout

    m^sigma sum_{q<=N/m}A(q)g_tau(log(qm/x)).           (GC27)

Uniformly for m in M_X and X<=x<=2X, log(m/x)>=4tau. Thus, for q>=2,

    g_tau(log(qm/x))/g_tau(log(m/x))
      =q^(-log(m/x)/tau)*exp(-(log q)^2/(2tau))
      <=q^(-4).

Using A(1)=1 and |A(q)|<=3, the q>=2 part in absolute value is at
most 3*sum_{q>=2}q^(-4) times the q=1 Gaussian. The elementary bound

    3*sum_{q>=2}q^(-4)
      <=3*(1/16+integral_2^infinity t^(-4)dt)=5/16

shows that GC27 is at least (11/16)*m^sigma*g_tau(log(m/x)).
The ratio m/x belongs to the fixed compact interval
[exp(4tau),4*exp(4tau)], so its Gaussian is bounded below by a
positive constant depending only on tau. Every one of these literal
columns is therefore >=c_(tau,sigma)X^sigma across the entire shell.

Use the positive unit vector |M_X|^(-1/2)*1_(m in M_X). Adding the
columns gives output >=c_(tau,sigma)X^(sigma+1/2) everywhere on the
shell; integration over logarithmic length log 2 proves GC26.
The finite cap, ordered coefficients, prime-two values and the strict
original product cut have all been retained.

This is a failure of a PARTICULAR unrestricted operator transfer. It
is not a lower bound for the actual source vector e_1, for the full
Gaussian detector, for the primitive field, or for its signed local
moment. It does not contradict GC13, which acts on the physical
all-dyad growth norm using specific arithmetic convolution identities.
It also does not rule out a source-sensitive operator estimate with
an independently justified domain. The reopening condition is such
a paid source-sensitive readout bound, or a new signed estimate for
the primitive moment in GC19. Finite inverse identities alone do not
provide it.

## G217. Actual-source obstructions and their exact scopes

The companion developments are retained because they rule out specific
repairs without declaring broader approaches exhausted.

First, the higher-arity source is the already known W01/W35/W48-R6
construction. Write a=mu chi,h=chi,m=a1_(n<=U),u=a-m,
q_p=delta_1-p chi(p)delta_p and b_p=q_p*h, with fixed unramified p.
Dirichlet convolution gives, with every zero and repeated prime kept,

    q_p^(k-1)*a=u^k*b_p^(k-1)
      +sum_(j=1)^k(-1)^(j+1)binom(k,j)m^j*q_p^(k-j)*b_p^(j-1). (16)

For fixed k>=2,0<delta<=1,U=X^((1-delta)/k), all short products are
at most X^(1-delta), up to fixed p-shifts. The cofactor series
(1-chi(p)p^(1-s))L(s,chi) is entire. Its fixed Gaussian transform can
be moved to any fixed negative line; the Gaussian dominates vertical
polynomial growth and the finite coefficient counts. This pays all
restoration terms on complete real shells. The j=1 delta-cofactor
term has direct Gaussian decay. No growing-k assertion follows.

For principal chi, products of k distinct unramified primes in
[X^(1/k),2^(1/k)X^(1/k)], excluding p, have hard coefficient exactly
(-1)^k k!. Every long factor must contain one prime, so the cofactor
is1. Fixed-proportion prime counts give order X/log^k X such products,
all on one shell. Their selected same-sign Gaussian field therefore
has linear exponent, including its normalized shell L1/L2 norm.
This blocks paying that proper sector separately; other sectors may
cancel it. Fixed k prime counts follow by partial summation from
[Selberg's PNT, theorem1.1](https://www.math.lsu.edu/~mahlburg/teaching/handouts/2014-7230/Selberg-ElemPNT1949.pdf).
The restriction U>=1 is necessary for the k! coefficient and the
vanishing of lower-degree cells: if delta>1, U<1 and u=a, the hard
source collapses to q_p^(k-1)*a. The raw author's wider claim is
corrected here; the convolution identity itself remains valid.

Second, fixed nonnegative compact smoothing and deletion of finitely
many activity layers do not repair the shrinking zero disk. Fix
continuous compactly supported w>=0 with w(0)>0 and w>=c>0 on some
[a,b],0<a<b. For principal chi modulo fixed q, let

    C_j(X)=sum_(n squarefree,(n,q)=1,omega(n)=j)w(n/X),
    Z_X^[ell](z)=C_0+C_ell z^ell+sum_(j>ell)C_j z^j,

where ell>=1 is fixed; this DELETES layers1,...,ell-1.
We have C_0->w(0)>0, total mass O(X), and, by products of ell
distinct primes in the fixed scaled interval,
C_ell>>X/log^ell X. Unique factorization costs only fixed ell!.
At R=(2C_0/C_ell)^(1/ell), eventually R<1, and

    |C_0+C_ell z^ell|>=C_0 for |z|=R,
    |sum_(j>ell)C_j z^j|<=O(X)R^(ell+1)
       =O(X^(-1/ell)log^(ell+1)X)=o(1).             (17)

Rouche gives exactly ell roots of the COMPLETE polynomial inside R.
All higher degrees are paid together. A scale-independent positive
radius for the logarithm at0 is unavailable. A weight vanishing on
a neighborhood of0 has C_0=0 eventually and no such logarithm at all;
this last observation is not a statement about every w with w(0)=0.
Restoring the original signed endpoint requires the deleted signed
layers; their individual absolute prices have linear exponent, but
their signed sum has not been lower-bounded. Signed or moving weights,
growing ell, exact deflation and another normalized object remain
outside this obstruction. These are activity zeros, not L-function
zeros. G106's sharp-cutoff root and G120/G145's normalization costs
remain the earlier mechanisms, with this specified extension.

The two independent pre-outcome audits add further scope checks.
For A_chi(x)=sum_(n<=x)chi(n)phi(n), every unramified prime p produces
a jump of magnitude p-1. No continuous background can have uniform
error O(x^gamma), gamma<1, on every large real x: left limit and
value at p would give p-1<=2Cp^gamma. The coefficient at1 and the
principal count2A_1(x)-1 are retained. An r-fold Riesz smoothing has
the exact transform L(s-1,chi)/[L(s,chi)s(s+1)...(s+r)], with its
principal terms and numerator nonvanishing still required for a return.
The parity Jordan construction addresses that numerator issue for its
own different source; it does not erase the sharp jump.

For the complete replica audit, on K squarefree q-units let
a_n=mu(n)chi(n). Exactly

    sum_(m<n)|a_m-a_n|^2=K^2-|M_chi(x)|^2.           (18)

Thus the useful estimate is a one-sided LOWER bound near K^2, not
positivity alone. For a simple d-regular graph on these K vertices,
1<=d<=K/2, adjacency A_G, compare
Ltilde=(K/d)(dI-A_G) with Lcomplete=KI-11*. The constant eigenvalue
is d and tr(A_G^2)=Kd, so

    ||Ltilde-Lcomplete||
      >=K sqrt((K-d)/(d(K-1)))>=K/sqrt(2d).          (19)

The source-independent error certificate K times this operator norm
cannot prove error O(x^(2gamma+epsilon)) unless
d>=x^(4-4gamma-2epsilon) up to fixed constants, since K~kappa_q x.
Before small losses the degree exponents are .5005838544 at gamma11,
2/3 at5/6, and1 at3/4. The last excludes every fixed-power sublinear
degree under an every-epsilon target, but not x^(1-o(1)).
This is a limitation of the stated regular-graph uniform certificate,
not a lower bound for its error on the actual Möbius vector or a
claim about weighted/nonregular graphs. A source-specific signed
comparison and the complete one-sided deficit remain open.

## HCR9. Norm transfer, cap cost and every signed interaction

If gamma>1/2 and q_v<gamma, HCR8.4 gives an error smaller than exp(gamma*u)
for all sufficiently large u after its fixed polynomial and square-root
factors are absorbed. Therefore the all-dyad, every-epsilon L1 bound

    integral_(log X)^(log(2X)) |Q_(A,V)(u)|du
       <= C_epsilon X^(gamma+epsilon)                    (HCR9.1)

implies HCR4.1. In fact the two L1 hypotheses are equivalent at that
exponent because the same additive error works in the reverse direction.
The analogous L2 hypotheses are equivalent by the norm triangle
inequality. No Cauchy--Schwarz loss in the field exponent occurs in
transferring between D_A f and Q. L2 implies L1; L1 need not imply L2.

The exact source choices are:

| A | gamma | V | q_v | gamma-q_v | Cap scale |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| .004 | .874484 | .004 | .8743996 | .0000844 | x^1.004 exp(sqrt(log x)) |
| .007 | .83332 | .34 | .832366 | .000954 | x^1.34 exp(sqrt(log x)) |
| .016 | .74995 | 1.01 | .748549 | .001401 | x^2.01 exp(sqrt(log x)) |

All q_v are strictly below gamma, and all gamma exceed 1/2. With the
author's V=1.01, the quarter target's source extending beyond x^2 is a real
cost, not a logarithmic tail. This table does not assert that 1.01 is the
smallest permissible V. The floor and bounded initial u interval do not
change it.

For the optional second moment set U=log X, L=log 2, and
N_max=N(U+L). Since N is increasing, its exact Gram is

    sum_(m,n<=N_max) a_m a_n
       *integral_U^(U+L) 1_(m<=N(u))*1_(n<=N(u))*W_u(m)*W_u(n)du.

This is B18. Kernels and coefficients are real. Both moving cap masks
must remain inside the integral. Expanding W_u(m)W_u(n) gives direct,
both direct/future cross terms, and the double future integral. Expanding
each a_n gives all four q_2 terms with multipliers 1,-2,-2,4 and their
correspondingly shifted integer caps. No diagonal, rough-prime mask,
projector, coprimality gate or positive subfamily can replace this Gram.
If a decomposition is introduced, every interaction or a proved
whole-field norm inequality must return it to HCR9.1/B18.

The author has not asserted a false signed-subfamily inference here.
The previous fixed-Gaussian four-diagonal/coprime results also do not
by themselves bound this new moment over a future range as long as
[x,x^(1+V)]. HCR8.1 and HCR3 are this replacement detector's own source
and return, which is why the reconstruction is meaningful despite that
remaining arithmetic difficulty.

## Group 3: multiplicative structure / noncommutative probability / coarse sector bound

**W41-11 | alternating conditional expectations | p=.04.** Treat independent prime blocks as conditional expectations E_j; multiply centered operators (I-E_j) before taking norms. Algorithm: reveal blocks, keep their alternating signs, telescope only commutator errors with the masks. First test: prove the exact decomposition with two noncommuting masks. Bridge: a cheap bound on total commutator mass pays the complement. Danger: arithmetic expectations do not commute. Reach: rigorous restricted sector with an explicit error ledger.

**W41-12 | noncommutative martingale budget | p=.065.** Encode a signed correlation as the trace of a product of prime-block martingale differences. A very coarse operator-norm bound might suffice if a large external scale budget survives. First test: construct matrices reproducing all signs exactly on four squarefree variables. Bridge: bound the trace plus a counted exceptional fiber sector. Danger: matrix dimension swallows the nominal gain. Reach: full moment improvement if dimension is subpower.

**W41-13 | free-product arithmetic surrogate | p=.009.** Replace prime-block interactions by freely independent operators, then use the defect from freeness as the sole arithmetic residual. First test: compare the first four joint moments for an exact toy divisor model. Bridge: a quantitative noncommutative Lindeberg replacement with an explicit total error. Danger: primes are commutative, so free independence may be structurally wrong. Preserve even an incoherent result. Reach: high-ceiling replacement representation.

**W41-14 | completely positive signed dilation | p=.007.** Dilate a signed coefficient operator into an off-diagonal corner of a positive block matrix; apply a coarse positive inequality to the dilation while recovering the sign in a chosen corner. First test: test whether the dilation norm equals or exceeds the original signed norm for a 2x2 example. Bridge: recover a zero detector without dimension/norm inflation. Danger: dilation only repackages absolute values. Reach: unlikely but potentially an exact positivity bridge.

**W41-15 | multiplicative stopping-time sector | p=.035.** Stop revealing primes when a local conditional variance becomes large. Bound the stopped good sector by martingale orthogonality and the bad sector by a very crude count paid from a larger budget. First test: define a deterministic stopping rule and prove the two sectors partition the actual coefficients. Bridge: original form equals controlled good plus completely priced bad. Danger: bad mass is not sparse. Reach: restricted theorem with a usable full return if stopping tails decay.

## 2. Partial marking, rather than an unavailable full-length improvement

Fix a physical buffered bin delta in [17/25,7/10], one eligible parent translate and the actual slot product Q of total width z. The bin upper edge bounds every original subproduct by its physical price Z^(delta times its width+small) H_J. The lower edge supplies a zero for a fixed dictionary label. All heights and buffered internal zero maxima are handled as in accepted [restricted research revision]: choose the detector cutoff t BEFORE witnesses and retain it even if the larger internal height box has a larger zero maximum. Only weaken witness lower bounds to the physical delta. Do not use that internal maximum as a new upper slot bound.

Normalize free-row width W=1 and put v=z/W<=1/20. Supported witnesses satisfy, with a preallocated small tolerance,

    r<=t, r+m>=t, 0<=m<=1/2,
    |M(Z^r)|^2>=Z^(delta r), |P(Z^m)|^2>=Z^(delta m).      (3)

The old plain fourth moment times the pointwise slot price used 1-2delta m+delta v. Instead fix the witness dyad m and greedily choose an original slot subcollection of width x just below

    min(v,(1-2m)/(9/2)).

The gap is at most ONE fine-mesh slot width, not an error per slot. The subset depends only on frozen lengths and dyads, not the live row. Apply (MP) with n1=n2=m to that subcollection; pay the complementary actual slots by their physical bin bound; only then enlarge the remaining positive norm to the full eligible family. Division by the fourth-power witness gives

    Pnew(m)=1-2delta m+delta [v-(1-2m)/(9/2)]_+.           (4)

For m slightly above 1/2 use no marked slots and the old unmarked exponent max(1,2m), paying the witness tolerance once. The two slopes of (4) in m are -2delta and -2delta(1-2/9), both negative. Thus m>=t-r gives the same expression with m=t-r. All four derivative-profile pairs are covered by MP's two independent plain profiles and the same selected subset.

For comparison, a full marked-plain amplification is possible but worse here. The exact Euler restoration at a slot-disjoint amplifier prime is

    S_u(D)=sum_(j>=0) phi_u(p)^j (Np)^(-j/2)
                         S_(up^6)(D/(Np)^j).

It is finite on annular support, also valid when p|u (then the displayed scalar is zero for j>0). Restore both plain factors, average over the fixed prime pool, use injectivity (u,p)->up^6 on free cores, and take the existing two-scale Sobolev supremum. The geometric coefficient mass is bounded. MP at enlarged width H=max(W,2m+(9/2)z)+small gives

    E_PM(W,m,z)=W/6+(5/6)max(W,2m+(9/2)z).               (5)

This is not the marked inverse exponent. At delta=.70,v=.05 and the binding m=442/965, the full amplified counting exponent is 36771/77200, the old pointwise exponent is 15199/38600, and partial marking gives 2939/7720. Full amplification is worse than the old bound by 6373/77200. More generally, beyond the unamplified capacity, its derivative with respect to marked width is 5(9/2)/6-delta>0 after crediting pointwise removal. Therefore the optimum of THIS amplification/pointwise strategy marks exactly the largest fitting subcollection. This is a useful failed construction, not a universal impossibility result.

## R6. Four selected first tests, with original source conventions

For native H freeze every finite component packet and both independent heights. The literal ideal coefficients are

    a(n)=alpha(n)eta(n)chi_n(lambda)^(-2)gamma_2(n),
    xi(g)=alpha(g)^3 eta(g)^3.

The field is Eisenstein, with original primary/fixed-ray/six-unit/bad-place data. Keep distinct long prime ideals of distinct rational norms and both strict-far orientations, equal-norm exclusions, every ordered short pair including equality, actual complex h((g,g')), rational gcd screen, both projectors1_(P,Rg)=1 and1_(P',Rg')=1, natural zeros, all original profiles and height factors. The joint kernel has chi_pi(h)^3 chi_pi'(h)^3 chi_pi(s)^2 chi_pi'(s')^4 b(pi)conjugate(b(pi'))zeta_CRT, unitary factor1/Q on its Q^2-point group. It is not a rational mu-chi kernel.

To fix the root/conjugation convention, put v_P=u1(P)/sqrt(q_P), w_P'=u2(P')/sqrt(q_P'), and define K by the literal scalar sum v_P K_PP' conjugate(w_P'). Then H=w*Tv with T=K^T, ||v||^2=Omega1, ||w||^2=Omega2. Root weights are accounted in v,w ONCE; all remaining source factors stay in T. Saying the packet retains rooted marks does not insert those roots a second time in T. This is the corrected G75 convention, read from the earlier independent source review.

The raw target is

    B0 sqrt(Omega1 Omega2),
    B0=G K0 [N+L+(NL)^(2/3)] P_orig.

K0 is the original row parameter, not a new kernel norm. Afterward apply N^(-1)G^(-2) exactly once. P_orig includes the original kernel/component/profile costs. Uniform packet bounds still need the original height integration, linear tails, all component interactions and other H branches; neither this review nor the author pays them anew.

**28 — invalid proposed source constraint, valid diagnosis.** The original mark arrays are independent. They do not satisfy u(pn)=-chi(p)u(n) merely because rational mu chi does. If two coordinates are actually allowed, assigning1 and0 violates that relation; if not, that putative coordinate relation provides no constraint there. This is an interface test, not a constructed numerical native-H counterexample. An upstream relation could matter after a proved full transport through the ideal source and its boundaries. W38's rational-source SDP and the old constrained-dual portfolio keep their credit and remain distinct.

**26 — scoped positive-MGF impossibility, valid.** The literal Hermitian dilation

    A_phi=[[0,e^(i phi)T],[e^(-i phi)T*,0]]

has eigenvalues plus/minus each nonzero singular value of T. Its realification is indefinite when T is nonzero. A positive probability MGF of a real linear auxiliary variable has positive semidefinite log Hessian at zero, equal to its covariance; a locally finite MGF has the required moments. It cannot equal exp(y^T B y) for this indefinite real B on a neighborhood of zero. This does not exclude nonlinear couplings or complex measures.

Diagonalizing B gives the exact complex Gaussian formula in H1. Absolute value inside that expectation replaces B by B_+; its ratio to the exact positive exponential is exp(y^T B_- y). The imaginary phase cost has not vanished. No phase lower bound or arithmetic saving is deduced from the synthetic two-dimensional example.

**25 — tensor torsion calculation, valid.** For Re(s)>0, a=1-chi(p)p^-s and b=1-chi(r)r^-s are nonzero. The based complex C->C^2->C has d2=(-b,a)^T and d1=(a,b). It is exact. Using boundaries a e0 and(-b,a) and the indicated lifts gives determinants a,-a,1; the alternating ratio is-1, so torsion is1 up to sign in either reciprocal convention. At p2,r3,s2 the desired ab is2/3. I independently checked the convention in [Hutchings2002, AppendixA](https://math.berkeley.edu/~hutching/pub/rt3/rt3.pdf), DefinitionA.1/PropositionA.2; the finite determinant derivation is explicit here. A direct sum can store the product, and the cutoff triangle has homology instead of the proposed acyclic torsion. These are scoped failures, not a theorem against every arithmetic torsion detector.

**30 — full cyclic compression, valid but largely standard.** The finite Hermitian Krylov span through dimensionD is invariant by Cayley-Hamilton; its orthogonal complement is invariant by adjointness. Hence QAP=PAQ=0 and the claimed Feshbach self-energy is zero on its resolvent domain. Full cyclicity can occur, but the author's determinant-18 example is synthetic and says nothing about actual native cyclic dimension. For a UNIT source line, the Schur resolvent is [z-a-b*(z-D)^(-1)b]^-1; coefficients1/z+a/z^2+(a^2+||b||^2)/z^3 preserve the source moment. For source(w,v), a=2Re(e^(i phi)H)/(||w||^2+||v||^2). For source(0,v), the second moment is||Tv||^2/||v||^2. The rescue is a full spectral/source estimate, not an automatic saving from compression.

## 3. Complete endpoint contract and target arithmetic

For b=3/2 suppose that, for every epsilon>0 and all sufficiently large
dyadic X,

       E_chi(X)=integral_X^(2X)|V_(3/2),chi(x)|^2 dx/x
                 <<_(chi,epsilon) X^(2gamma+epsilon),   (3.1)

where 1/2<gamma<1 is common to every fixed ordinary character required
by the family theorem. Constants and onsets may depend on chi and epsilon.
This is the COMPLETE source on every point of the physical shell, not a
sample grid, a truncated n sum, or a selection of additive major arcs.

For sigma>gamma, choose epsilon<2(sigma-gamma). Cauchy--Schwarz on
dyadic x shells proves convergence and locally uniform holomorphy of
integral_0^1 F_chi(t^(3/2)+it)t^(s-1)dt. At t>=1 the bound
|F_chi(t^(3/2)+it)|<=exp(-t^(3/2))/(1-exp(-t^(3/2))) pays the entire
upper tail. Thus H_chi is holomorphic on Re s>gamma. By (2.3), so is
1/L(s,chi), hence L has no zero there. More explicitly the continued
identity L(s,chi)[H_chi(s)-R_chi,1(s)]=Gamma(s)exp(-i*pi*s/2)
precludes a zero. For a principal character its pole at s=1 becomes a
zero of the reciprocal; the usual pole exception is retained.

Imprimitive L-functions are the inducing primitive L times their finite
Euler factors. We have used the exact original coefficients and L, so
all such factors are included; their zeros lie on Re s=0 and do not
create an unmentioned exception here. This is an ordinary-character
statement only. It neither resolves the project's external definition
bindings nor widens to Hecke characters or conductor-uniform bounds.

The weakest sufficient energy exponent for a first gain is any exponent
strictly smaller than 2theta11=1.7497080728 in the every-epsilon sense.

       gamma=5/6    -> c=1/6,    E << X^(5/3+epsilon);

but this is not a bound for E: signed off-diagonal terms remain.

in (3.1) is admissible because the return is on the open half-plane

silently upgraded to an L2 estimate. This weighted absolute Mellin

    b(n)=mu(n)chi0(n) for n<=K; b(n)=0 for K<n<=T;
    b(n)=lambda w_q(n)n^(sigma-1)cos(t log n) for n>T.

Every finite convolution equation up to K and every stated zero mask
holds. For x>=T, the absolute tail is at most(lambda/sigma)x^sigma,
so the fixed Cx^beta envelope survives; the known prefix and middle
interval do also. T and |t| can be arbitrarily large.

Yet D_q(z)=sum_n w_q(n)n^-z has continuation

    D_q(z)=kappa_q z/(z-1)
       +z integral_1^infinity[sum_(n<=x)w_q(n)-kappa_q x]x^(-z-1)dx

on Re z>1/2. The error is holomorphic and the pole at1 has residue kappa_q.
The constructed series B(s) is a finite entire correction plus
(lambda/2)[D_q(s+1-sigma-it)+D_q(s+1-sigma+it)]. It has genuine poles
sigma+it and sigma-it, each residue lambda kappa_q/2. These are synthetic
completion poles, NOT L-zeros. The sequence violates global convolution
and multiplicativity: at a prime beyond T the convolution residual is
1+b(p)!=0. The result rejects only sufficiency of the stated finite
relaxation; full arithmetic or proved all-height tail constraints may repair it.

The uniform audit09 retains every squarefree layer and p-free cofactor.
Let B_k(X)=sum_(n<=X,omega(n)=k)mu(n)chi(n). Inserting one prime gives

    k B_k(X)=-sum_(p<=X)chi(p) B_(k-1)^(p)(X/p).

Each k-factor squarefree n has exactly k parents. Summing all layers yields

    M_chi(X)=1-sum_(p<=X)chi(p)
       sum_(m<=X/p,p not dividing m)mu(m)chi(m)/(omega(m)+1)
      =1-sum_(p<=X)chi(p) integral_0^1 G_(p,X)(t)dt,
    G_(p,X)(t)=sum_(m<=X/p,p not dividing m)mu(m)chi(m)t^omega(m).

All degrees, product caps, endpoints and natural zeros remain. The COMPLETE
coefficientwise absolute edge price is exactly the number of squarefree
q-units2<=n<=X: each n has k edges of weight1/k. It is
kappa_q X+O_q(sqrt X)-1, not a bound below for the signed flux. Factorial
layer rescaling requires the inverse factorial readout and does not remove
that price. Signed correlations between cofactor responses remain open.

For any proposed Gtilde define Atilde by replacing G in that root formula
and E by the FULL signed difference. Then M=Atilde+E exactly. Bounding
BOTH complete contractions by X^(gamma+epsilon), with the usual every-
character/every-epsilon/all-large-X quantifiers, gives the same Mellin return.
Root-dependent approximations must return to this fixed source before
continuation. Selected primes, central degrees or separate variances do not
pay the full error.

The separate logarithmic identity also retains every prime power:

    M_chi(X)log X=integral_1^X M_chi(t)dt/t
       -sum_(p^j<=X,j>=1)chi(p)^j log p M_chi(X/p^j).

It follows coefficientwise from the full log-derivative convolution.

the p-free insertion identity above. Neither identity supplies a contraction.

## 3. Summation uniform even for superpolynomial G

Uniformity in unbounded G must not absorb a factor G^eta into X^epsilon. Instead absorb the whole coefficient loss using the actual damping:

    N^(2eta) exp(-cN/X^b)
         <<_(eta,b,c) X^(2b eta) exp(-cN/(2X^b)).        (S9)

After (S9), sum the first term of (S8) without damping, obtaining O(X^2/G^2) for k>2. The isolated N/G term sums with damping to O(X^b/G). For the last term, its increasing and decreasing branches meet at

    N_* = X G^(2/k) >= X.

Both geometric sums therefore give

    sum_(N dyadic>=c0 X) min(N^2/G^3,X^k N^(2-k)/G)
       <<_k X^2 G^(4/k-3) <= X^2/G^2       (k>=4).      (S10)

The fixed c0 only changes the constant. Equation (S10) includes k=4 with equality of the G exponents; no strict reserve is required. For 2<k<4 this proof leaves the larger term and does not give (S1).

For far ordered pairs, n~N and X<m<n/2, and also the reverse orientation, (S5) is at most O(X^(2k)N^(-2k)). Both the shell and cumulative coefficient masses are O(N^(1+eta)/G). Thus every far pair costs in total

    sum_(N dyadic>=c0 X) X^(2k)N^(2-2k+2eta)/G^2
        << X^(2+2eta)/G^2,                             (S11)

provided eta<k-1. This includes arbitrarily high n and all much smaller high partners. Interactions involving n<=X were already reserved for triangle.

Equations (S8)-(S11) prove a high squared norm at most

    C X^(2b eta)[X^2/G^2+X^b/G]+C X^(2+2eta)/G^2.

The low norm and triangle have the same scale. Choose eta>0 after epsilon, smaller than both epsilon/(2b) and (k-1)/2. Cauchy-Schwarz on finite logarithmic measure pays L1. This proves (S1), with the original masks and strict gcd endpoint intact.
