## 2. D1: the exact corrected source and continuation

Fix one ordinary Dirichlet character chi modulo q, with its natural zeros. Let delta=1 for a principal character and0 otherwise. For Re s>0,

    J_y(s)=integral_2^y u^(-s)/log(u) du,
    H_y(s)=delta J_y(s)+sum_(p<=y)log(1-chi(p)p^(-s)),
    Q_y(s)=exp(H_y(s)).                                  (C1)

Each logarithm is the fixed local power series -sum_(j>=1)chi(p)^j p^(-js)/j. This includes every prime power in the logarithm and every unramified prime, including2. A ramified prime contributes exactly0 to H and1 to Q. The finite product is nonzero on this half-plane; a modulus-q nonprincipal character is not silently replaced by a growing conductor or primitive-only family.

On Re s>1 the absolute Euler expansion gives Q_y -> exp(delta J_infinity)/L(s,chi). The exact differentiation is

    J_infinity'(s)=-2^(1-s)/(s-1),
    d/ds log[(s-1)exp(J_infinity(s))]
                         =(1-2^(1-s))/(s-1).             (C2)

The right side is entire, with value log2 at1. Its entire primitive, with one real basepoint value fixed, defines an entire nonzero B. The match on Re s>1 is exact, including the multiplicative constant. The optional expression

    B(s)=exp(-gamma_E)/log2 *
         exp[-sum_(n>=1)(-((s-1)log2))^n/(n n!)]

agrees with the [NIST exponential-integral series](https://dlmf.nist.gov/6.6.E2), independently checked. The continuation proof needs only(C2), so no unverified branch convention in that optional formula enters the argument.

The correct identity to continue is

    F_chi(s) Q(s)=B(s)^delta,
    F_chi(s)=(s-1)^delta L(s,chi).                        (C3)

F_chi is holomorphic in Re s>0. For principal chi, F_chi(1)=product_(p|q)(1-1/p), nonzero; the principal pole was paid explicitly. All finite imprimitive Euler factors are retained and have no zeros in Re s>0. Thus a holomorphic Q satisfying(C3) excludes every zero of L in the domain. No growth estimate for 1/L or Phragmen-Lindelof assumption is hidden here: this is an identity between holomorphic functions, initially known in the absolute-convergence half-plane. There is no Gaussian/f3, Eisenstein, conductor-uniform or native-H transfer in this packet.

### 2.1 LP_a and the disk chain

Write h_k=H_(2^k). The author assumes, for every compact K in Re s>a and every epsilon>0, eventually in k,

    integral_K (Re h_k)_+ dA <= C_(K,chi,epsilon) 2^(k epsilon).
                                                               (LP_a)

Closed rectangles from a countable exhaustion suffice because any fixed finite disk chain lies inside one larger rectangle. This is a two-dimensional area hypothesis on the complete sequence, not values on finitely many curves or favorable cutoffs.

1. Positive part of the harmonic function Re h_k is subharmonic. Applying its area mean inequality on fixed disks contained in a slightly larger compact gives a local upper bound Re h_k<=C2^(k epsilon). No lower pressure bound is assumed.
2. At one fixed real b>1, the exact series in(C1) bounds the full complex h_k(b) uniformly in k. Borel-Caratheodory on a disk, in the safe form

       sup_(D(c,R/2))|h_k| <=3|h_k(c)|
                              +2 max(0,sup_(D(c,R)) Re h_k),

   and finitely many overlapping disks propagate this anchor. Hence sup_K|h_k|=O_(K,epsilon)(2^(k epsilon)). Constants and chain length may depend on K and chi. An imaginary constant cannot float because the actual logarithm at b is fixed.
3. f_k=h_(k+1)-h_k is O_b(2^(-k(b-1))) on Re s>=b>1, uniformly in height: the integer tail bounds the prime interval and the continuous integral. Elsewhere every fixed compact has O(2^(k epsilon)) growth.
4. Choose a finite chain with outer4r disks inside Re s>a, successive centers at distance<=r. A2r decay disk at one center contains the next inner r disk. Three-circle interpolation from r to2r inside4r gives

       d_(j+1)=(d_j-epsilon)/2,
       d_j=d_0/2^j-epsilon(1-2^(-j)).                    (C4)

   Taking epsilon<d_0/2^(N+1) before invoking LP for the finite N-step chain makes every d_j positive. Multiplicative constants also propagate, but remain independent of k. A finite cover handles any desired compact.

Thus sum_k f_k converges locally uniformly. Its sum plus h_1 is a holomorphic limit H; Q=exp(H) is nonzero. Applying(C3) proves zero exclusion Re s>a at every fixed height and for every multiplicity. A compact around any finite alleged zero is covered; no unsupported passage from finitely many heights to all heights occurs. Uniformity in growing q or growing height is not claimed. A common a for each fixed ordinary chi, with chi-dependent constants and onset, is exactly the stipulated family scope.

The proposition is correct as stated for1/2<a<1. Its complex-analytic proof actually needs only0<a<1; the1/2 threshold enters the simpler singleton comparison below. This harmless conditional extension does not make LP true at any additional a.

**Necessary qualification of the apparent weakness.** For this exact anchored sequence and its known right-half-plane dyadic decay,

    LP_a  <=>  h_k converges locally uniformly on Re s>a. (C5)

The forward implication was just proved; the reverse follows from local boundedness, which gives LP with an O_K(1) right side. For a>1/2, put

    R_(2,y)(s)=sum_(p<=y)sum_(j>=2)chi(p)^j p^(-js)/j.

R_(2,y) converges locally uniformly and absolutely in Re s>1/2, with all ramified terms zero. The centered singleton sum is

    sum_(p<=2^k)chi(p)p^(-s)-delta J_(2^k)(s)
                                      =-h_k(s)-R_(2,2^k)(s).

Consequently LP_a is also equivalent to local uniform convergence of THIS centered DYADIC prime sum. This is not a proved equivalence between bare zero exclusion and LP, nor an unproved assertion about every intermediate natural cutoff. It explains the relation to W36 R36.21-R36.22: the explicit vacuum and prime-discrepancy return already exist; the new interface replaces an assumed pointwise counting estimate by a one-sided local pressure criterion and pays the analytic continuation. Syntactically permitted subpower growth is forced down to bounded convergence under the other exact hypotheses. No arithmetic exponent gap has thereby shrunk.

### 2.2 Separate line budget and its strict endpoint

The stronger height-sensitive input P_(a,kappa) is not derived from LP. It says, for every epsilon>0, some fixed A,C independent of y,t satisfy

    |H_y(a+it)|<=C(1+|t|)^A y^(kappa+epsilon)

for all dyadic y and every real t. Fix b>1, D>1, integer m>A, and apply three-lines to f_k(s)/(s+D)^m on a<=Re s<=b. The denominator has no pole in the strip. For each fixed y, the finite prime power-series sums and finite integral in(C1) are uniformly bounded in t on this closed strip. Division by the polynomial therefore supplies the required horizontal boundary control; no unproved uniform meromorphic reciprocal bound enters.

The exact exponent is

    E=[(kappa+epsilon)(b-sigma)+(1-b)(sigma-a)]/(b-a).

Without epsilon its zero is

    r_b=(b kappa+(b-1)a)/(kappa+b-1)
       =a+kappa+kappa(1-a-kappa)/(kappa+b-1).             (C6)

For a+kappa<1 and kappa>0, r_b decreases to a+kappa as b grows. For any fixed compact strictly to its right, choose finite b first, then a sufficiently small epsilon. E is strictly negative, so the increments sum. For kappa=0 the same buffered argument works with r_b=a. The ensuing limit uses(C3), proving exactly Re s>a+kappa. Bounds on a finite height interval or uncontrolled A=A_y do not meet this hypothesis.

The synthetic h_k^*(s)=sum_(j=1)^k2^(j(a+kappa-s))/j is a valid sharpness check at kappa>0: its left-line size is O(2^(k kappa)); its right increments satisfy the needed y^(1-b) budget since a+kappa<1. The limit exponential is1/(1-2^(a+kappa-s)), with a pole at the claimed strict boundary. It is not an arithmetic prime source. It prevents a free improvement of the abstract exponent, not an arithmetic theorem stronger than the input.

For a=3/4, kappa=78/625, the conditional c is313/2500=.1252. Its gain over root-accepted c10 is1351/25000000=.00005404. The corresponding first-gain test is kappa<.12485404. The1/6 and1/4 rows are also exact. The actual crude bound |H_y(a+it)|<=C_a y^(1-a) has a+kappa=1 and yields no useful strip. The author correctly does not replace this with a claimed estimate.

For p=q, remove that old slot and extract its prime exactly. Write P_i0 for its original central scale. The coefficient mass after applying R1 to S(D/Np) is bounded by

    sum_(p in intersection) (P_i0 Np)^(-1/2)
                  * (D/Np)^(beta/2)
       <=C D^(beta/2) P^(-beta/2),                   (R6)

because the fixed annuli force P_i0 comparable to P and there are O(P) prime ideals, by the elementary ideal count. The remaining old slots satisfy MI with strictly easier gates. The exact phase phi_u(p)^2 is a contraction, including its zero value. An inverse term may contain p; this interaction is left to the literal original MI and is not declared coprime. Thus the diagonal satisfies R5.

For p!=q, independently color the prime IDEALS of the finite original pool i with two fair colors. For the resulting disjoint sets E0,E1,

    1_(p!=q)=4 E_color[1_(p in E0)1_(q in E1)].       (R7)

For p=q the right side is zero; for distinct ideals its event has probability1/4. Distinct prime ideals of equal norm remain distinct color labels. Coloring by norm would fail: two different ideals of norm7 would always have the same color, incorrectly giving zero for their off-diagonal pair.

For each coloring, the two supports are now disjoint; every other original pool remains disjoint from both. Each coefficient is bounded, fixed and row independent. The SAME uniform MI estimate applies to every coloring, by B0.4/B3.31's arbitrary-coefficient contract. Hilbert Minkowski under the normalized probability measure gives

    ||4 E_color F_color|| <=4 E_color ||F_color||,

so the norm cost is4, not 2 raised to the pool size. Squaring changes only a fixed constant. This is a finite coefficient identity followed by a uniform moment estimate; no independence or randomness of character values is asserted. All natural zeros, fixed holes, original slot coefficients and independent heights remain in the colored sums.

A new prime cannot collide with two old slots because the original pools are disjoint. The above pieces therefore exhaust every new/old collision. For j>=2 in R2, first apply R1 to S(D/(Np)^j); only then take absolute values of the extracted prime sum. With the complete old Q retained inside MI, the dyadic coefficient mass is

### 3.1 Exact finite operator identity

On test functions on the positive integers define the forward average

    (T_H f)(n)=(1/H) sum_(j=0)^(H-1) f(n+j),
    Q_r(T)=sum_(j=0)^(r-1)(I-T)^j
          =sum_(k=0)^(r-1) (-1)^k binom(r,k+1) T^k.

The polynomial identity

    T Q_r(T)+(I-T)^r=I                                     (3)

is exact. The sum of absolute coefficients of Q_r is 2^r-1. Each T_H^k is a positive probability average of forward shifts between0 and k(H-1), with endpoints included. Thus every shift in Q_r lies between0 and (r-1)(H-1).

    F_a(x)=(1/H) sum_(k>=1) B_H(k) psi_x(k)
                         +sum_(n>=1) a(n) R_x(n).          (4)

Indeed, replacing k by n+j in the first sum gives sum_n a(n)T_H psi_x(n). Terms with n<=0 vanish; no negative index or first-block correction is silently dropped. Equation (3) proves (4). The forward shifts, rather than backward shifts, are essential here.

## 8. Euler holes, Fourier transport and all height costs

**Classification: the general analytic lemmas are elementary/proved; their use is compatible after the literal coefficient and joint-norm transfers.**

For a squarefree ideal `q`, `Nq<=Z^B`, and `|a_p|<=1`,

`E_q(s)=product_(p|q)(1-a_p(Np)^(-s))`

has no zeros for `Re s>0`. On `Re s>=sigma0>0`, `E_q`, `1/E_q` and every fixed derivative are `O(Z^epsilon)` uniformly in `q`, coefficients and height. Bound by the positive product at `sigma0/2`, put each sufficiently large factor below `(Np)^b`, and use a Cauchy disk of radius `sigma0/2`. This proves uniform deletion/restoration only after the exact Euler identity has been established. It does not provide conductor bounds or remove a principal pole, which is why the natural constructor and eligibility gates above are necessary.

For a normalized prime polynomial of scale `P>=1`, removal of primes dividing `q` costs at most `O(P^(-1/2) log(2Nq))`. This is `O(Z^epsilon)` on polynomial scales and is compatible with squared pointwise cost `P^delta Z^epsilon` for `delta>=0`. Logarithmic profile derivatives add only fixed log powers; imaginary heights have unit modulus. Arithmetic masks have not been discarded by positivity.

On a fixed compact box in logarithmic coordinates, uniformly bounded Euler derivatives of order `2r>J+d` give Fourier densities dominated by `C(1+|t|)^(-2r)`. Their `J`-weighted total mass is uniformly bounded. Minkowski is applied in the **joint** Hilbert space `directsum_lambda ell2(rows_lambda)`, possibly with nonnegative weights, after proving a joint arithmetic bound. Thus it costs the common measure's mass and no factor equal to the number of labels.

If the smooth continuous parameter varies as `A_lambda`, the individual densities need not be equal. Choose their common positive majorant `dmu=C(1+|t|)^(-2r)dt` first and write `f_(A_lambda)dt=a_lambda(t)dmu`, `|a_lambda|<=1`. Multiplication by these scalars is a diagonal contraction in the joint Hilbert space. This proves the claimed extension. It is used only for labels frozen outside the particular sum being Poisson-transformed. Discontinuous row, valuation, coprimality and zero-bin indicators stay inside the arithmetic vector and are never differentiated or inserted before a transform.

For actual kernels `K(A product y_i^e_i)`, Euler differentiation acts on `K` with fixed multipliers. Uniform source kernel seminorms, fixed compact cutoffs and normalized norm powers therefore provide the common profile control. Large frequency tails are paid by sufficiently high integration-by-parts order, using raw polynomial arithmetic bounds before an enlargement. These orders are finite and can be chosen after the density height degree.

For bounded physical input heights retain Fourier frequencies inside a still smaller portion of the `Z^tau_out` zero-height buffer. For arbitrary larger input heights, absolute counting gives a fixed polynomial `Z^D` on the bounded exponent geometry; a sufficiently large fixed polynomial in the largest height absorbs it. This avoids applying a detector at an uncontrolled height. Choosing derivative and height orders backward through the finite graph (two transforms and calls to old moments), then Fourier orders and finally the threshold, supplies a uniform statement for all independent heights and the four scale-derivative profile pairs.

## T01. Quantitative fixed-factor division — PROVED

**Provenance:** SA Part I §§3–6, (S5)–(S10); SB §2, (N1); BA R1; BB R02. The merged proof is the dimension-free disk argument; SA's longer circle/Blaschke argument is compatible and superseded here.

### Disk lemma

Let `g` be holomorphic near the closed disk `Omega=D(c,R)`, with `m=|g(c)|>0` and `M>=sup_Omega |g|`. Suppose `D(z,r)` lies in `Omega`, and `U` is a holomorphic map near the smaller closed disk into a finite-dimensional Hilbert space. Then
\[
\|U(z)\|^2\le
M^{-2}(M/m)^{2R^2/r^2}
\frac1{\pi r^2}\int_{D(z,r)}\|g(w)U(w)\|^2\,dA(w).
\tag{T01.1}
\]
The constant is independent of the vector dimension.

**Proof.** Put `u=log(M/|g|)`. It is nonnegative and locally integrable, including at zeros of `g`. The submean inequality for `log|g|`, integrated over radii about `c`, gives
\[
\int_\Omega u\,dA\le\pi R^2\log(M/m).
\]
If `U(z)=0` the conclusion is immediate. Otherwise choose a unit linear functional `ell` with `|ell(U(z))|=||U(z)||`. The logarithmic submean inequality for `ell(U)` gives
\[
\log\|U(z)\|^2
\le \operatorname{Avg}_{D(z,r)}\log\|gU\|^2
-2\log M+2\operatorname{Avg}_{D(z,r)}u.
\]
Use the preceding integral bound and concavity of logarithm, then exponentiate. Discrete zeros are harmless for the area integrals; the scalar identically-zero case cannot occur under the choice of `ell`. This proves the assertion without division at a zero. ∎

### Polynomial-height consequence

Suppose `F` is fixed and entire, has polynomial growth on every fixed vertical strip, and has a positive uniform lower bound on one fixed right-hand vertical line. For `s0=sigma+it` in a buffered strip, take a fixed small disk about `s0` and a larger fixed-radius disk anchored on that right-hand line. In (T01.1), `m` is bounded below and `M<<T^B`, `T=2+|t|`. Consequently
\[
\|U(s_0)\|^2\ll T^C\sup_{|s-s_0|\le r}\|F(s)U(s)\|^2.
\tag{T01.2}
\]
A completed vector estimate with arithmetic exponent `X^rho` therefore retains that exponent after extraction. The larger disk need only be a domain for `F`; only the smaller disk requires holomorphy and bounds for `U`.

Take `F(s)=L^S(3s-1,xi)`, where `xi` is the fixed nontrivial angular Hecke character. Entire continuation, fixed-strip polynomial growth, and the fixed-conductor functional equation are among the source inputs. The absolutely convergent Euler product gives the required lower bound on a right-hand line. For moving finite deletions,
\[
L^{(Sh)}(3s-1,\xi)=F(s)E_h(s),\qquad
E_h(s)=\prod_{p\mid h,\,p\notin S}(1-\xi(p)Q_p^{1-3s}).
\]
On `Re s>=a>1/2`, for every `delta>0`,
\[
|E_h(s)|+|E_h(s)|^{-1}\ll_{a,S,\delta}q_h^\delta.
\tag{T01.3}
\]
Indeed `|xi(p)Q_p^{1-3s}|<=Q_p^{-(3a-1)}<1`. For sufficiently large prime norms each local factor or inverse is at most `Q_p^delta`; the finitely many smaller primes contribute a fixed constant. Multiply over distinct primes only. This costs a subpower of the physical row norm as well because the conductor radical divides the row.

If the completed estimate is given on every fixed vertical line, obtain the local strip bound by choosing two fixed neighboring lines, scalarizing the finite row vector against an arbitrary unit functional, and applying three-lines after division by a sufficiently high power of `C+s`. FD (59) permits the strip maximum principle with no uncontrolled height growth. Recover the vector norm by taking the supremum over unit functionals. This does not introduce a dimension factor or replace a sum by a sum of rowwise suprema. Cauchy estimates give any fixed number of spectral derivatives on a smaller strip.

Thus completed and uncompleted means, with arbitrary positive exponent losses and every fixed buffer, have the same arithmetic exponent. A Lipschitz dependence of that exponent on `Re s` is handled by choosing the local radius inside the allocated loss.

**Limits:** separate holomorphy is essential; the lemma cannot prove holomorphy of `1/zeta` from a holomorphic product. It does not create a missing period realization, extend a primitive-current estimate to a missing ray component, handle a moving angular character without uniform hypotheses, or remove a gamma factor with exponential height behavior. [restricted research revision]'s gamma removal remains a necessary inherited step.

\tag{T03.2}

\le C_{\sigma,v,S}
\sum_{\substack{0<q_k\le X\\k\ {\rm cube-free}}}
q_k^{-v}\|\mathbf D_k(s)\|^2.
\tag{T03.3}

**Proof.** Normalize input/output by `q^{-v/2}`. The positive majorizing kernel for (T03.2) is

Choose `u,w>0`, `u+w=v`, `w>1/3`, and Schur weight `p_n=q_n^{u-v/2}`. For `h=h0 r^3`,

p_h^{-1}\sum_kA_{h,k}p_k

For arbitrary element rows, include unit and fixed-prime residue exponents modulo three in the finite vector, and sum remaining fixed-prime cube powers among `d`. Different components can use different fixed completions only after uncompleted extraction; a common scalar completion commutes directly with the identity.

## T07. Common-divisor cancellation with the actual prime marks

**Status: PROVED RELATIVE TO the inherited physical inputs; the sharper versions also use the explicitly imported all-finite-order Hecke strip I-HECKE.** They do not follow from a Riemann-zeta-only premise. Sources: SA Parts IV–V, CC1–CC40 and PM1–PM19. The original common-core mechanism occurs in inherited SG §8; the new scope here is the full physical compensator.

For \(G\ge1\) and a fixed smooth annular \(w\), localize the *true squarefree-core gcd*:

 \mathcal C(G)=\sum_{c\ne c'}w(q_{(c,c')}/G)\langle S_c,S_{c'}\rangle.
 \tag{T07.1}
\]
For every \(\epsilon>0\), the following upper bounds hold, with \(Y^{-1}\mathcal F_AZ^\epsilon\) suppressed:

| Assumptions on the marks and analytic input | Bound for \(|\mathcal C(G)|/(Y^{-1}\mathcal F_AZ^\epsilon)\) |
|---|---:|
| Absolute core counting, original mark envelope | \(ZL/G\) |
| Bounded marks in the original slots; ordinary smooth character Poisson | \(Z^{3/2}L^{5/2}/G^2\) |
| Bounded marks in those slots; I-HECKE | \(Z^{1+b_0/2}L^{3-b_0/2}/G^2\) |
| **Actual smooth product prime weights**; I-HECKE | \(Z^{1+b_0/2}L^{1+3b_0/2}/G^2\) |

The limiting exponents in the last two rows mean arbitrary-loss estimates obtained on fixed buffered lines. No contour passes along \(\Re s=b_0/2\).

### 1. The coupled character survives all mixed embeddings

For two branches write
\[
 D=G_*d,\quad E=G_*e,\quad(d,e)=1,
 \quad m'=[D,E]^2r,
 \quad c=gu,\quad c'=gv,
\]
where \(g,u,v\) are pairwise coprime squarefree cores and \(u\ne v\). The original rows are \(e^2r,d^2r\). The cubic Gauss cocycle and row characters give, respectively,
\[
 \gamma_2(gu)\overline{\gamma_2(gv)}
 =\gamma_2(u)\overline{\gamma_2(v)}\vartheta_g(v)\overline{\vartheta_g(u)},
\]
\[
 \chi_g(e^2r)\overline{\chi_g(d^2r)}
 =\vartheta_g(e)\overline{\vartheta_g(d)}.
\]
The angular and multiplicative core phases cancel, and the remaining quadratic-refinement phase is a fixed-ray factor by M B1.4. Consequently the moving character in \(g\) is exactly
\[
 \psi(g)=\vartheta_g(ve)\overline{\vartheta_g(ud)}, \tag{T07.2}
\]
times one of finitely many characters supported on the original fixed set. Natural zeros impose
\[
 (g,ruvde)=1,\qquad(u,e)=(v,d)=1. \tag{T07.3}
\]
These conditions imply \((ve,ud)=1\). Every good prime exponent in either product is one or two. Hence the good conductor is \(\operatorname{rad}(uvde)\), with norm \(R\ll q_uq_vq_dq_e\). Its character is nonprincipal unless all four labels are units, which would give the excluded equality \(c=c'\). A fixed-place twist cannot cancel a nontrivial good conductor. This argument is performed before row Poisson or outer-column Cauchy; the outer fields are independent of \(g\) after the finite ray split.

### 2. Squarefree sums and the two weaker cancellation bounds

The inherited smooth Poisson estimate, obtained by opening \(\mu^2(k)=\sum_{a^2\mid k}\mu(a)\), is
\[
 \sum_{k\ {\rm sf},(k,M)=1}\psi(k)W(q_k/K)
 \ll(KRq_M)^\epsilon\min(K,K^{1/2}R^{1/4}).
\]
Indeed an ordinary smooth character sum of length \(U\) is \(O(\min(U,\sqrt R))\); split the \(a\)-sum at \(q_a=\sqrt K R^{-1/4}\). Finite coprimality masks are kept during the opening and cost a subpower. For a forced squarefree divisor \(F\), substitution \(g=Fk\) therefore gives
\[
 \sum_{\substack{g\ {\rm sf},\,F\mid g\\(g,M)=1}}
 \frac{\psi(g)}{q_g}W(q_g/G)
 \ll(GRq_Mq_F)^\epsilon G^{-1/2}q_F^{-1/2}R^{1/4}. \tag{T07.4}
\]
Incompatible forced divisors give zero.

For the Hecke improvement fix \(b_0<b<1\), put \(\sigma=b/2\), and keep this choice fixed before varying scales. The inherited buffered bounds and the primitive functional equation give by three lines
\[
 |L(s,\psi)|\ll R^{(b-\Re s)/2+\epsilon}T^A,
 \qquad1-b\le\Re s\le b.
\]
Here \(\sigma\ge1-b\), since \(b>2/3\). The exact series is
\[
 \sum_{\substack{g\ {\rm sf},\,F\mid g\\(g,M)=1}}\psi(g)q_g^{-s}
 =\psi(F)q_F^{-s}\frac{L^S(s,\psi)}{L^S(2s,\psi^2)}

\]

\[
 \sum_{\substack{g\ {\rm sf},\,F\mid g\\(g,M)=1}}
 \frac{\psi(g)}{q_g}W(q_g/G)
 \ll(GRq_Mq_F)^\epsilon G^{\sigma-1}q_F^{-\sigma}R^{\sigma/2}T^A.
 \tag{T07.6}
\]
This has the same form as (T07.4), with \(\sigma=1/2\) in the Poisson case.

For bounded marks, assign each marked prime first to \(g\), then to its residual core, then to its cube label. This is a disjoint assignment even when cores and cubes share primes. Forced assignments give divisibility in \(g,u,v,n,n'\); priority exclusions stay inside \(M\). After applying (T07.4) or (T07.6), ideal counting gives
\[

 \ll H^{(1+\sigma)/2}q_A^{-1},
\]
and the cube exponents become \(1+3(1+\sigma)/2>1\). Every distinct marked prime pays at least \(q_p^{-\sigma}\). A slot marked once therefore costs at most \(P^{1-\sigma+\epsilon}\); a slot marked on both sides costs at most \(P^{2(1-\sigma)+\epsilon}\), including its equal-prime diagonal. The completed core/cube sums have bound
\[

 \tag{T07.7}
\]
This proves the two weaker cancellation rows after the outer/embedding accounting in §4 below. The actual profiles used in the \(g\)-sum are the annular gcd weight times the two original \(V\)-factors. Their derivatives on \(q_g\asymp G\) have the envelope factors \(E(Gq_uq_n^3/N_D)E(Gq_vq_{n'}^3/N_E)\). Divisor losses involving arbitrarily large columns are absorbed into these envelopes, so no compact truncation of the log-Gaussian is assumed.

### 3. The extra saving from the actual prime slots

For the original smooth/fixed-character prime weights, keep the assigned-to-\(g\) primes inside the transform. Set
\[
 \mathscr S_M(s)=\frac{L^S(s,\psi)}{L^S(2s,\psi^2)}
       \prod_{p\mid M,\,p\notin S}(1+\psi(p)q_p^{-s})^{-1},

\]
For \((F,M\mathfrak f_\psi)=1\), the exact forced series equals

\[

\]
Both leading good characters remain nonprincipal after every fixed-place factor. The inherited prime estimate therefore gives, for a fixed smooth annular \(w\), fixed real \(\Re a\), and a deleted radical \(B\),
\[

Fix \(u,v,n,n',r,D,E\) and a priority pattern. Marks assigned outside \(g\) have divisor-many choices, because they divide those fixed cores or cube labels. Freeze them first. \sum_{0<q_h\le K}\|\mathbf D_h^{(g)}(s)\|^2.
\]
Suppose \(u,v\ge0\), \(3u+v<1\), and, for every fixed positive central buffer \(e\), every arbitrarily small loss \(\delta>0\), and every required fixed component/deletion family,
\[
\mathcal T(K,G;\tfrac12+e+it)
\ll (KG)^\delta K^{1+u}G^v(1+|t|)^A. \tag{T08.1}
\]
The constants may depend on the fixed data, buffers and specified profile seminorms; \(A\) cannot depend on moving \(K,G,t\). This is a finite trace, never an infinite \(G\)-limit.

Then the inherited current satisfies, for \(1\le K,G\le D\),
\[
|\mathfrak Q(D,K)|
\ll_\rho(DK)^\rho
\left(
 DK^{1+u}G^v+DK+
 D^2K^{1/3}G^{-1}
 +D^{5/3}K^{2/3}G^{-2/3}
\right). \tag{T08.2}
\]
Consequently,
\[
k_*=\frac{1+v/2}{1+u+v},\qquad
c_{u,v}=\frac{k_*-1/2}{3}
       =\frac{1-u}{6(1+u+v)}. \tag{T08.3}
\]
The zero-free conclusion concerns the open half-plane. For any proposed zero inside it, use a strict interior row exponent \(k<k_*\). No boundary-line assertion is needed.

### Proof of the energy implication

For the whole completed column FD (68) gives
\[
S_h^{(g)}(w)=L^S(3w-1,\xi)
\sum_{d\mid g}x_{g/d}(w)
\prod_{p\mid d}(1-x_p(w))D_h^{(d)}(w),
\quad x_a(w)=\xi(a)q_a^{1-3w}.
\]
This selector includes primes shared by a squarefree core and its outside cube. At \(\Re w=1/2+e\),
\[
|x_a|^2=q_a^{-1-6e},\qquad
\prod_{p\mid d}(1+|x_p|)\ll q_d^\delta.
\]
Divisor Cauchy therefore reduces the finite whole-column trace to (T08.1) with cutoff \(G/q_a\le G\), followed by an absolutely convergent \(a\)-sum. The angular factor is incorporated into the original radial cube profile \(\Phi_V\) of FD (69), whose nonzero angular type makes its lower endpoint rapidly decreasing. It is not divided out. Finite Mellin shifts use inherited independent holomorphy and polynomial height bounds. Squaring costs \(D^{1+2e}\); choose \(e\) and preliminary losses sufficiently small in terms of final \(\rho\). This gives the first term of (T08.2).

FD (71)–(72) supplies the unchanged large-divisor energies. The three resulting weights are
\[
\frac{DK}{q_dq_aq_j},\quad
\frac{D^2K^{1/3}}{q_d^2q_a^4q_j^4},\quad
\frac{D^{5/3}K^{2/3}}{q_d^{5/3}q_a^3q_j^3}.
\]
Their sums over \(q_aq_d>G\), with the original finite supports, are the final three terms in (T08.2). The natural core-divisor and \(j\)-overlap conditions remain intact.

Finally, FD §19.3 separates the original common product kernel before applying positive Cauchy in the same divisor/row indices. This step preserves the signed coprime covariance, all original total-column profiles, radial norm twists and both separately paid zero terms. It does not apply a signed estimate to an arbitrarily partitioned profile.

Set \(G=\max(K^{1/3},KD^{-1/2})\). If \(K\le D^{3/4}\), the first term is at most
\[
D^{7/4+3u/4+v/4},
\]
which is strictly below \(D^2\) by \(3u+v<1\). If \(K=D^k\), \(k\ge3/4\), its exponent is
\[
1-v/2+k(1+u+v)<2
\]
for \(k<k_*\). Both tails are at most \(D^2\), and \(DK\le D^2\). Exact equality in a tail is harmless: M (2.18) asks for \(D^{2+\epsilon}\), with arbitrarily small loss. It does not require a power saving below \(D^2\) in every term. This proves the conditional current criterion and (T08.3).

### Exact incidence and what it selects

The extraction identity gives
\[
\mathcal T(K,G;s)=
\sum_{q_k\le KG}\|\mathbf D_k(s)\|^2
\sum_{\substack{
g\mid\operatorname{rad}_{=1}(k)\\
q_g\le G,\ q_k/q_g\le K}}
q_g^{-2\Re s}. \tag{T08.4}
\]
The radical contains only primes of valuation exactly one. This is an equality after summing the full finite orbit: the component switches are permutations/unitary phases. For \(G\le K\), prime rows above \(K\), pure prime squares above \(K\), and pure cubes above \(K\) receive zero weight. A positive ordinary mean through \(KG\) charges rows absent from this incidence. Conversely \(g=1\) still requires an ordinary mean through \(K\); counting divisors alone cannot prove the desired trace.

### New merge corollary: common-completed finite incidence is equivalent

Let \(\widetilde{\mathcal T}(K,G;s)=\sum_{g,h}\|F(s)\mathbf D_h^{(g)}(s)\|^2\), with exactly the same finite index set as \(\mathcal T\). On every buffered strip, (T08.1) is equivalent, up to arbitrary losses and a polynomial height factor, to its version for \(\widetilde{\mathcal T}\). In one direction multiply by the fixed polynomially bounded \(F\). In the other, apply T01 to the single finite holomorphic vector \((\mathbf D_h^{(g)})_{g,h}\); its estimate is dimension-free, and neighboring lines give the required local bound. Moving finite deletions cost at most \((KG)^\delta\). Thus no arithmetic exponent is lost by a **common scalar completion** of this finite incidence.

This completes a merger of T01 with the two-exponent transfer. The symbol \(F\mathbf D_h^{(g)}\) means completion of the forced squarefree-core series. It is not the whole-column selector \(S_h^{(g)}\), which additionally counts primes in the outside cube through T02. Nor does formal multiplication by \(F\) establish a missing current-period realization or align differently completed ray components. Those obligations remain exactly as stated in T01–T02.

### New merge corollary: only the actual divisor corridor is needed

It is enough to assume (T08.1), uniformly in all scales and fixed data, only for
\[
1\le G\le C K^\gamma,\qquad
\gamma=\frac{1-u}{2+v}
      =1-\frac1{2k_*}>\frac13, \tag{T08.5}
\]
where a fixed multiplicative constant \(C\) is harmless. This closes the profile obligation left open in BA's prototype corridor.

For annular equal-length columns, if \(K\le D^k\) and \(k<k_*\), then
\[
K^{1/3}\le K^\gamma,\qquad
KD^{-1/2}\le K^{1-1/(2k)}\le K^\gamma.
\]
The chosen selector split therefore never leaves (T08.5). The cube-selector formula only shortens \(G\).

For the original unbounded profiles, retain the exact common-kernel separation of FD §19.3. On a block of column lengths \(D_1,D_2\) and effective row length \(K'\), first set
\[
D_*=\max\{2,D_1,D_2,(K')^{1/k}\}.
\]
Use one common cutoff
\[
G=\max\{(K')^{1/3},K'D_*^{-1/2}\}.
\]
Then \(K'\le D_*^k\) and \(G\le(K')^\gamma\). Both positive column energies are bounded using the common larger scale \(D_*\); any support rescaling costs only fixed polynomial factors in \(D_*/D_i\), exactly of the kind allowed in the inherited positive profile bounds. Since \(K\le D^k\) and \(K'\) is the original row dyad times \(D_1D_2/D^2\),
\[
\frac{(K')^{1/k}}D
\ll \left(
\text{row-dyad factor}\,\frac{D_1}{D}\frac{D_2}{D}
\right)^{1/k}.
\]
Thus \(D_*/D\), and every rescaled-seminorm cost, is polynomial in the original scale ratios and their inverses. More explicitly, with \(r_i=D_i/D\) and normalized row-dyad factor \(R_{\rm row}\),
\[
 D_*/D\ll 1+r_1+r_2+(R_{\rm row}r_1r_2)^{1/k}.
\]
The retained rapid column tails and the rapid upper row Fourier tail sum these costs. Below \(R_{\rm row}=1\), this enlargement introduces no adverse negative power of \(R_{\rm row}\); the nonempty dyads with \(K'\ge1\) cost at most a logarithm in the scales. Effective row lengths below one use M §2.4's original Fourier-decay estimate. All epsilons are fixed before summing, and \(k\) is fixed strictly below \(k_*\). The full-profile conclusion therefore follows from the corridor hypothesis.

For \((u,v)=(1/8,1/32)\), the exact corridor is \(G\le CK^{28/65}\), and the conditional constant is \(14/111\). A slogan such as “control \(G\) near \(K^{.43}\)” is insufficient: (T08.5) requires every divisor cutoff below that boundary, all components and all height/profile uniformities.

### Exact numerical transfers and an off-central version

\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
(u,v)&c_{u,v}\\ \hline
(\eta,\eta)&(1-\eta)/(6(1+2\eta))\\
(1/8,1/32)&14/111\\
(1/8,1/64)&28/219\\
(1/8,0)&7/54\\
(1/10,1/12)&9/71
\end{array}
\]
At \(c=.1255=251/2000\),
\[
c_{u,v}>.1255\iff1753u+753v<247.
\]
At \(u=1/8\) this is \(v<223/6024\). The general range \(3u+v<1\) extends BB's unnecessarily restricted \(0\le v\le u<1/4\).

If a mean is available only on the fixed line \(1/2+e\), do not hide the cost \(D^{2e}\) in an arbitrary epsilon. A finite trace \(K^{1+u}G^v\) on that line instead gives
\[
k_{*,e}=\frac{1-2e+v/2}{1+u+v},\qquad
c_{u,v,e}=\frac{1-u-4e}{6(1+u+v)},
\]
provided \(8e+3u+v<1\). In the ordinary-mean deduction \(v=(u-2e)_+\), this is exactly BB R05.b's two cases.

SB §6's exact interior example is correct: at \(\eta=3/32\), \(k=8813/10000\), \(g=1907/5000\), the four exponents are
\[
639897/320000,\quad18813/10000,\quad57371/30000,\quad29999/15000.
\]
Their margins below two are \(103/320000,1187/10000,2629/30000,1/15000\). The prefactor loss \(\rho=10^{-6}\) costs \(18813/10^{10}\), less than each margin. This proves exponent feasibility after the missing mean only.

**Sources:** BA D5; BB R05.a–b and R01; SB §6; FD (65)–(73); M (2.14)–(2.18). Corridor closure (T08.5) is original to the merge and was independently checked in the mathematical merge.

## T09. Scale-\(L^2\) direct detectors

### T09a. One fixed Möbius profile

Let
\[
V(u)=e^{-u-u^{-1}},\quad
\phi(u)=(uV(u))',\quad
S_\phi(x)=\sum_{n\ge1}\mu(n)\phi(n/x).
\]
For \(0<a<1\), suppose for every \(\epsilon>0\) and every sufficiently large dyadic \(X\),
\[
\int_X^{2X}|S_\phi(x)|^2\,\frac{dx}{x}
\ll_\epsilon X^{2a+\epsilon}. \tag{T09.1}
\]
Then \(\zeta\) has no zeros in \(\Re s>a\).

Indeed, on \(\Re s\ge a+\delta\), Cauchy bounds the Mellin contribution of one shell by \(X^{-\delta+\epsilon/2}\). Taking \(\epsilon<2\delta\) makes the dyadic sum and every fixed complex derivative converge locally uniformly. At zero the function is exponentially small. Thus
\[
F(s)=\int_0^\infty S_\phi(x)x^{-s}\frac{dx}{x}
\]
is holomorphic for \(\Re s>a\). Initially \(F(s)=\Phi(s)/\zeta(s)\), where [restricted research revision] proves
\[
\Phi(s)=2(1-s)K_s(2).
\]
For completeness, a zero \(K_s(2)=0\) would give \(f(t)=K_s(2e^t)\), \(t\ge0\), with Dirichlet boundary and
\[
\int_0^\infty(|f'|^2+4e^{2t}|f|^2)\,dt
=-s^2\int_0^\infty|f|^2\,dt>0.
\]
Hence such \(s\) is purely imaginary. Therefore \(\Phi\) has no zeros in \(\Re s>0\) except \(1\). Continue
\[
(s-1)\zeta(s)F(s)=(s-1)\Phi(s).
\]
Any proposed zeta zero in \(\Re s>a\) contradicts the nonzero right side. No uniform lower bound for \(\Phi(\sigma+it)\) is used.

The exact positive scale kernel is
\[
\int_X^{2X}|S_\phi(x)|^2\frac{dx}{x}
=\sum_{m,n}\mu(m)\mu(n)
\int_1^2\phi(m/(Xt))\overline{\phi(n/(Xt))}\frac{dt}{t}.
\]
The arithmetic coefficients retain signs and all shared primes.

### The exact full shift kernel and its affordable diagonal

Define
\[
 K_X(m,n)=\int_1^2\phi(m/(Xt))\overline{\phi(n/(Xt))}\,\frac{dt}{t}.
\]
Absolute convergence, using the rapid decay of \(\phi\) at both ends, permits the exact regrouping
\[
 \int_X^{2X}|S_\phi(x)|^2\frac{dx}{x}
 =\sum_{n\ge1}\mu(n)^2K_X(n,n)
 +2\Re\sum_{h\ge1}\sum_{n\ge1}\mu(n)\mu(n+h)K_X(n,n+h).
 \tag{T09.1a}
\]
The diagonal is \(O(X)\): uniformly for \(1\le t\le2\), integer counting gives \(\sum_n|\phi(n/(Xt))|^2\ll X\), and then integrate in \(t\). It is separately affordable for \(a\ge1/2\), including every intended numerical target. For \(a<1/2\), cancellation between this diagonal and the off-diagonal would still be required. More generally,
\[
 |K_X(m,n)|\ll_A (1+m/X)^{-A}(1+n/X)^{-A}.
\]
This bound follows directly from the upper-end Schwartz bounds for each factor; the lower-end decay only improves it. It justifies the regrouping and tail truncations with explicit losses, but gives no short-shift support. When \(m,n\asymp X\), differences of order \(X\) remain. Thus the next sufficient estimate is for the complete signed weighted off-diagonal in (T09.1a), including shared-prime and product coincidences. A fixed-shift theorem alone does not establish (T09.1). This exact decomposition and diagonal bound are an additional merger result used in portfolio F01.N1.

### Frozen-dyad balanced finite form

Set, for large \(X\),
\[
L=\log X,\quad Y=\lfloor\sqrt X/L^2\rfloor,\quad
T_l=X/L^4,\quad T_u=XL^2,\quad J=\lceil8L^6\rceil.
\]
Use [restricted research revision]'s fixed smooth cutoffs \(\rho,\chi\), and define on \(x\in[X,2X]\)
\[
\mathcal B_X(x)=
\sum_{d,e>Y}\mu(d)\mu(e)
\rho(de/T_l)\chi(de/T_u)
\sum_{\ell\le J}\phi(\ell de/x).
\]
For every \(A>0\) and fixed Euler derivative order \(r\),
\[
(x\partial_x)^r\{S_\phi(x)-\mathcal B_X(x)\}
=O_{A,r}(X^{-A}). \tag{T09.2}
\]
This is a bounded extension of [restricted research revision] V7–V8, not a new cancellation estimate.

To prove it, apply the exact Möbius convolution identity with the same arithmetic cutoff \(Y\) throughout the dyad. The short Möbius term is exponentially small. In the Type-I term \(de/x\le L^{-4}\); lower removed Type-II products have \(de/x\le2L^{-4}\). [restricted research revision] V6's complete Poisson cancellation bounds these by \(e^{-cL^2}\) before truncating the \(\ell\)-sum. The infinite upper product tail has \(de/x\ge L^2/2\) and is likewise superpolynomially small after divisor counting. On the retained support \(Jde/x\ge4L^2\), so truncating \(\ell>J\) costs the same. There are \(O(XL^3)\) retained pairs, all with
\[
\sqrt X/L^2<d,e<2\sqrt X L^4.
\]
Every arithmetic cutoff is fixed on the dyad; differentiating only changes the smooth profile. The same endpoint estimates hold for each fixed Euler derivative. Replacing \(S_\phi\) by \(\mathcal B_X\) in (T09.1) changes energy by \(O_A(X^{-A})\) after reserving a larger preliminary \(A\).

At \(a=.87449\), the target squared-energy exponent is \(1.74898\). The gain over the inherited baseline squared-energy bound is \(0.000793294079928262\ldots\). The energy estimate remains open; averaging does not erase a hypothetical \(x^\rho\) mode.

### T09b. Compact-profile triple-convolution criterion

Let \(P_r(y)\) be the exact [restricted research revision] Z13–Z15 triple convolution, including equal-element projection, fixed good sectors, and all cube/core overlaps. For \(5/6<a<1\), suppose
\[
\int_Y^{2Y}\int_1^2|P_r(y)|^2\,dr\,\frac{dy}{y}
\ll_\epsilon Y^{\,2(3-2a)-\epsilon} \tag{T09.3}
\]
for every sufficiently small dyadic \(Y\) and every \(\epsilon>0\). Then \(\zeta_K^S\), and hence \(\zeta\), is zero-free in \(\Re s>a\).

Take \(H=L^2([1,2],dr)\) and \(P(y)=(P_r(y))_r\). Cauchy gives, on \(\Re s\ge a+\delta\),
\[
\left\|\int_Y^{2Y}P(y)y^{2s-3}\frac{dy}{y}\right\|_H
\ll Y^{2(\Re s-a)-\epsilon/2}.
\]
Choose \(\epsilon<4\delta\). The Bochner Mellin integral is holomorphic; large \(y\) decays exponentially uniformly on the compact \(r\)-interval. Initially its exact value is
\[
J_\bullet(s)
\frac{L^S(3s-3/2,\xi_{\rm ang})}{\zeta_K^S(s)},
\quad
J_r(s)=\int_0^\infty t^{2s}K_{1/3}(\kappa t)^2
K_{1/3}(\kappa rt)\,dt.
\]
For fixed \(\Re s>0\), \(r\mapsto J_r(s)\) is analytic on \(r>0\). [restricted research revision] Z16 proves a nonzero gamma-product limit for \(r^{1/3}J_r(s)\) as \(r\downarrow0\). Therefore \(J_r(s)\) cannot vanish almost everywhere on \([1,2]\); its \(H\)-norm is positive. The angular numerator is nonzero because \(3\Re s-3/2>1\). Continue the identity after multiplication by \((s-1)\zeta_K^S(s)\), and evaluate at a hypothetical zero. The right side is a nonzero vector, contradiction.

This removes the need for estimates uniform as \(r\to0\) or an individual zero-free kernel \(J_1\). It does not supply the arithmetic decay. At \(a=.87449\), the squared \(Y\)-exponent is \(2.50204\); \(N=Y^{-2}\) is a different scale.

**Sources:** BB R06–R07; [restricted research revision] V1–V10; [restricted research revision] Z13–Z18.

## T10. Two-dilation and continuum-dilation Möbius criteria

Fix \(0<\alpha<1\) and \(\Delta_bM(x)=M(bx)-b^\alpha M(x)\), where \(M(x)=\sum_{n\le x}\mu(n)\).

### Two discrete dilations

If for every \(\epsilon>0\) and all sufficiently large integers \(N\),
\[
\sum_{b\in\{2,3\}}\sum_{N\le n<2N}|\Delta_bM(n)|^2
\ll N^{2a+1+\epsilon},\qquad 0<a<1, \tag{T10.1}
\]
then \(\zeta\) is zero-free in \(\Re s>a\).

On a unit interval, \(|M(bx)-M(b\lfloor x\rfloor)|\le b\), while \(M(x)=M(\lfloor x\rfloor)\). Thus (T10.1) gives the continuous dyadic \(L^2(dx/x)\) estimate with an affordable \(O(1)\) error on a shell. The shell argument of T09 yields holomorphy of
\[
\int_0^\infty\Delta_bM(x)x^{-s}\frac{dx}{x}
=\frac{b^s-b^\alpha}{s\zeta(s)}. \tag{T10.2}
\]
Both multipliers can vanish only at
\[
s=\alpha+\frac{2\pi i m}{\log2}
 =\alpha+\frac{2\pi i n}{\log3}.
\]
The irrationality of \(\log2/\log3\) forces \(m=n=0\). The remaining real point \(\alpha\) is not a zeta zero: the alternating eta series is positive on \(0<s<1\), and \(1-2^{1-s}<0\). Thus at least one multiplier retains every prospective nontrivial zero. Their inverses need not be uniformly bounded in height.

The exact consistency identity is
\[
\Delta_2M(3x)-3^\alpha\Delta_2M(x)
=\Delta_3M(2x)-2^\alpha\Delta_3M(x).
\]
It gives no contraction or decay without a new arithmetic estimate.

### New continuum-dilation variant

Replace (T10.1) by
\[
\int_X^{2X}\int_2^3|\Delta_bM(x)|^2\,db\,\frac{dx}{x}
\ll X^{2a+\epsilon}. \tag{T10.3}
\]
The same conclusion follows by taking the Mellin integral in \(L^2([2,3],db)\). Its multiplier vector is \(m_s(b)=b^s-b^\alpha\). It vanishes as a vector only for \(s=\alpha\): a nonconstant exponential in \(\log b\) cannot be identically one on an interval.

This compact continuum also provides a useful quantitative calibration absent from the discrete two-multiplier claim. Put
\[
G_\alpha(s)=\int_2^3|b^s-b^\alpha|^2\,db.
\]
For \(\sigma\) in any fixed compact real interval,
\[
G_\alpha(\sigma+it)\gg1\qquad(|t|\ge1), \tag{T10.4}
\]
with a constant depending on that interval and \(\alpha\). Expanding the square, the cross term is
\[
2\Re\int_2^3 b^{\sigma+\alpha+it}\,db=O((1+|t|)^{-1}),
\]
uniformly in the compact \(\sigma\)-interval; the two diagonal integrals have a positive lower bound. This proves the assertion for large \(t\). Continuity and the absence of zeros prove it on the remaining compact set \(1\le|t|\le T_0\). Near \(s=\alpha\),
\[
G_\alpha(s)=|s-\alpha|^2
\int_2^3 b^{2\alpha}(\log b)^2\,db
 +O(|s-\alpha|^3).
\]
Thus the sole calibration zero is known and simple at the multiplier level; zeta is nonzero there. The proposed continuum energy is nevertheless an open Möbius estimate.

The same hypothesis has a quantitative consequence: on every compact strip \(a<\sigma_0\le\Re s\le\sigma_1\), with \(|\Im s|\ge1\),
\[
 |1/\zeta(s)|\ll_{\sigma_0,\sigma_1,\alpha}1+|\Im s|. \tag{T10.5}
\]
Indeed the shell bounds give an absolutely convergent Bochner Mellin integral \(F(s)\) whose norm is uniformly bounded on that strip; its defining norm integral has no imaginary-height growth. The exact identity is \(\|F(s)\|=\sqrt{G_\alpha(s)}/|s\zeta(s)|\). Combine it with (T10.4). This is conditional on the same open continuum energy, not on any additional arithmetic hypothesis.

On logarithmic scale, \(f(t)=e^{-\alpha t}M(e^t)\) converts \(\Delta_bM(e^t)\) to \(b^\alpha e^{\alpha t}[f(t+\log b)-f(t)]\). An averaged finite-difference/Poincaré approach is therefore an explicit next construction. It must estimate these actual increments, not invoke a generic inequality to create a Möbius power saving.

**Sources:** BA D11 for the discrete construction; continuum construction developed and independently proved during the merge.

# W42 independent seed freeze

Generated 2026-10-12 before reading detailed previous brainstorming, attempt outcomes or the current proof. Inputs: the assigned frozen problem, immutable W42 recipe, operating/ownership policy and the established six-test selection protocol. Reading the historical protocol-edit script supplied sampling instructions, not mathematical mechanism history. Deadline remains 00:55 UTC.

All p values below are rough, uncalibrated estimates of offering this **kind of mechanism** under the base brief before the rare instruction, against the full mechanism space. They are neither normalized shortlist probabilities nor evidence of validity, novelty or success. R/H/U denote overlapping restricted-result/hard-estimate/upstream-replacement reach. No mathematical success is claimed by these cards.

## Group 1: free invention, no cap

- **01. Two-witness convex duality** (p=.18; R/H/U). Object: a zero must satisfy two normalized detector witness constraints in one arithmetic Hilbert space. Bridge: the minimal cost of their simultaneous constraints is the inverse of their exact Gram matrix; a joint upper bound could beat either detector. Test: derive the two-constraint variational inequality with complex phase and cross term. Objection: the two detectors may not admit a common witness or comparable normalization.
- **02. Paid low-rank transfer** (p=.14; R/H). Object: approximate the hard detector coefficient map by a bounded map applied to the easier detector plus a residual. Bridge: transfer a proven norm estimate with explicit operator norm, residual norm and cross term. Test: derive the optimal quadratic transfer inequality and identify the required source identity. Objection: the residual may contain the entire arithmetic difficulty.
- **03. Local-moment support surgery** (p=.22; R/H). Object: partition the exact local moment into low multiplicity and collision-rich support. Bridge: use the newer local estimate only on the collision-poor region and count its complement. Test: symbolic exponent budget at the support cut. Objection: the known improvement may already optimize this partition, or the exceptional set dominates.
- **04. Prime-power quotient detector** (p=.08; R/U). Object: quotient the detector coefficient space by the span of prime powers, keeping exact prime contributions. Bridge: inverse Gram correction preserves the zero witness while shrinking variance. Test: finite exact coefficient projection and its witness leakage. Objection: removing prime powers may also remove the detectable zero signal.
- **05. Resonant mixed energy** (p=.12; H/U). Object: multiply rather than add the Gaussian and H detector witnesses on a common zero. Bridge: fourth or mixed moments constrain simultaneous largeness. Test: derive the mixed-moment exponent needed to exceed c5. Objection: multiplication increases length and forces an unproved cross-correlation estimate.

## Group 2: free invention, no cap

- **06. Localization through a common zero measure** (p=.075; R/H/U). Object: both detector outputs integrated against the same small disc or height-window measure of a hypothetical zero. Bridge: a partition of unity bounds bad sets for one detector by good sets for the other. Test: build a scalar counterexample showing whether marginal estimates alone control the joint bad set. Objection: their exceptional sets may coincide.
- **07. Sign-preserving scale martingale** (p=.065; R/H). Object: dyadic conditional expectations of the signed arithmetic coefficients, with projectors frozen in each increment. Bridge: orthogonal martingale differences might replace a triangle inequality by a square function. Test: compute the commutator of conditional expectation with the actual masks. Objection: arithmetic conditional expectations need not be orthogonal under the kernel form.
- **08. Endpoint convex envelope** (p=.16; R/H). Object: all known exact local exponents as affine functions of parameters. Bridge: a rigorous lower convex envelope can make unused estimates active near c5. Test: rational linear optimization without interpolation unless its norm hypothesis is paid. Objection: a visually favorable hull can combine incompatible parameter ranges.
- **09. Bootstrap only a zero neighbourhood** (p=.11; R/U). Object: bounds for L and its reciprocal restricted to a contour around an assumed zero. Bridge: self-improvement of local growth could force a contradiction without a global moment bound. Test: explicit analytic functions with one zero and admissible outer growth. Objection: standard maximum-principle bounds permit isolated zeros.
- **10. Reciprocal-energy obstruction map** (p=.045; R/H/U). Object: compute the least energy compatible with all available detector witness constraints. Bridge: its dual certificate identifies exactly which additional estimate would raise the constant. Test: finite-dimensional strong duality with approximate witness constraints and errors. Objection: finite truncation or an ill-conditioned Gram matrix can make the certificate nonuniform.

## Group 3: p<.10; original far-gap H phase/projectors; signed boundary state; counterexample

- **11. H boundary as a scattering port** (p=.032; R/H). Object: retain the boundary values of H blocks as a two-port indefinite energy rather than discarding their signs. Bridge: a Schur complement could isolate cancellation in interior modes. Test: a two-block signed kernel whose positive diagonal blocks coexist with adverse boundary coupling. Objection: the boundary state may need essentially full dimension.
- **12. Mask holonomy around a rectangle** (p=.018; R/H). Object: commute the two projectors and four shifted masks around a minimal arithmetic rectangle. Bridge: the resulting defect measures whether a proposed telescoping cancellation is exact. Test: a smallest-support signed example with nonzero loop defect. Objection: an abstract projector counterexample might not occur in the arithmetic family.
- **13. Phase reversal under a zero-preserving involution** (p=.024; R/H). Object: pair terms by an arithmetic involution preserving both support and zero extension. Bridge: antisymmetry leaves only fixed points. Test: list conditions for an involution on a single original prime block. Objection: the inverse or reciprocal mapping changes prime membership or the ordered interaction.
- **14. Adversarial phase transport on a tree** (p=.008; R/H). Object: assign edge phases on the interaction graph to align a spanning tree while recording cycle frustration. Bridge: a graph-theoretic lower bound exposes failure of universal phase-cancellation estimates. Test: three- and four-cycle examples with the exact projector constraints left symbolic. Objection: the original arithmetic phases are not freely assignable.
- **15. Boundary charge conservation** (p=.041; R/H). Object: view each zero extension as a signed jump measure at the support boundary. Bridge: discrete integration by parts leaves a bulk term and explicit boundary charge. Test: compare two neighbouring finite intervals with the actual sign convention. Objection: the boundary variation could cost the full original exponent.

## Group 4: p<.10; upstream object; spectral/statistical mechanics; projection back

- **16. Two-detector susceptibility matrix** (p=.026; R/H/U). Object: a 2x2 response matrix for detector outputs around the same assumed zero. Bridge: the least expensive joint response is a quadratic form in the inverse covariance. Test: obtain the exact cross-correlation threshold for a gain and a diagonal-normalization counterexample. Objection: covariance positivity does not imply the required sign or magnitude of the cross term.
- **17. Gibbs tilt at a hypothetical zero** (p=.019; R/U). Object: a probability measure tilted by the two detector signals. Bridge: a lower bound on relative entropy at a zero competes with an upper bound on the partition function. Test: optimize the two-variable exponential Markov inequality. Objection: available polynomial moments do not control exponential tails.
- **18. Detector transfer as a spectral gap** (p=.037; R/H/U). Object: the generalized eigenvalues of two exact coefficient quadratic forms. Bridge: a favorable restricted eigenvalue lets one detector pay the other's energy on the witness subspace. Test: derive the quotient-space eigenvalue criterion including the common nullspace. Objection: nullspace mismatch makes every global transfer constant infinite.
- **19. Ground-state deflation of a majorant** (p=.006; R/H/U). Object: explicitly remove the leading positive eigenmode of an absolute-value majorant while preserving the signed zero signal. Bridge: the second spectral value could lower the energy exponent. Test: rank-one deflation with a quantified witness-loss correction. Objection: the leading eigenvector may carry the whole signal.
- **20. Detector tensor at different temperatures** (p=.013; R/U). Object: two smoothing widths create a tensor-product response, with a diagonal projection back to the original arithmetic coefficients. Bridge: a projected tensor bound might force a stronger zero contradiction. Test: compute the exact diagonal-projection norm for finite coefficient spaces. Objection: the projection norm erases the gain.

## Group 5: p<.01; complex geometry/discrete optimization; dual certificate/variational principle

- **21. Holomorphic witness frame** (p=.004; R/H/U). Object: detector witnesses form local holomorphic frames of a rank-two bundle over the zero location. Bridge: a uniformly positive Gram determinant gives a frame-independent dual certificate. Test: calculate frame transition and condition-number costs on overlapping discs. Objection: determinant positivity alone gives no uniform lower bound.
- **22. Tropical bottleneck certificate** (p=.007; R/H/U). Object: exponent losses form a min-plus network whose paths are exact proof transfers. Bridge: a dual cut identifies a single arithmetic estimate with maximal marginal value. Test: derive a two-detector network with no illicit addition of unrelated gains. Objection: exponent networks discard constants, endpoint logs and incompatible hypotheses.
- **23. Complex phase-cover integer program** (p=.003; R/H). Object: partition the actual H phases into a finite cover of arcs and choose signs subject to projector constraints. Bridge: a dual packing certificate bounds coherent clusters. Test: exact small-instance feasibility and a worst-case cluster. Objection: phase concentration can be total, so a phase cover does not itself save powers.
- **24. Exterior-power detector** (p=.002; R/U). Object: wedge two independent coefficient witnesses; its norm squared is the Gram determinant. Bridge: a hypothetical zero may force nonzero exterior response while a mixed energy bound makes it small. Test: determine whether scalar zero constraints force any nonzero wedge at all. Objection: both responses may be collinear, making the wedge identically zero.
- **25. Analytic continuation of a dual optimizer** (p=.005; R/H/U). Object: the minimum-energy linear combination of detectors depends analytically on the hypothetical zero. Bridge: locally optimal combinations patch through bounded transition factors. Test: poles of the inverse Gram matrix and required determinant margin. Objection: optimizing separately at each zero can destroy admissible coefficient independence.

## Group 6: p<.01; multiplicative structure/noncommutative probability; constructive error budget

- **26. Prime-factor conditional coupling** (p=.006; R/H/U). Object: reveal prime factors sequentially and couple the two detector coefficient processes using the same filtration. Bridge: cross-variation controls transfer residuals while retaining the original multiplicative identities. Test: a two-prime model where marginal martingale bounds hold but cross-variation is maximal. Objection: finite-height averaging is not an independent-prime probability space.
- **27. Noncommutative mask dilation** (p=.004; R/H/U). Object: dilate the two projectors to commuting coordinate projections on a larger space. Bridge: an exact compression formula permits easier estimates upstairs with explicit dimension/normalization cost. Test: minimal dilation of two noncommuting rank-one projections. Objection: the compression cross term reintroduces the original difficulty.
- **28. Free-product shadow with defect audit** (p=.001; R/H/U). Object: compare multiplicative convolution to a free-product model and explicitly sum relation defects. Bridge: a moment bound upstairs transfers if the relation budget is below the target power saving. Test: count the first commutativity relation and its sign. Objection: ordinary integers are highly commutative, making the defect dominant.
- **29. Adaptive coefficient rejection sampling** (p=.003; R/H/U). Object: construct a sparse random detector retaining coefficients with probabilities chosen from both detectors' leverage scores. Bridge: unbiasedness plus a uniform concentration bound might reduce hard interactions. Test: exact second moment and deterministic realization cost. Objection: arithmetic adversarial correlations survive sampling, and a zero-dependent sample is inadmissible.
- **30. Multiplicative commutator detector** (p=.002; R/U). Object: commutators of truncated multiplication and two smoothing/projector operations isolate the noncommuting boundary signal. Bridge: an exact identity may detect a zero while annihilating the bulk diagonal. Test: compute the commutator for one prime and derive the missing zero-response term. Objection: multiplication operators commute before truncation; the surviving boundary may contain no useful signal.

## Frozen selection intent

Light coherence screen: all 30 are coherent enough for an affordable first test; a missing transfer is not an exclusion. No candidate is excluded based on p. Cards 01/16/21/25 share a joint-Gram theme but retain different explicit tests; 01 is the direct bridge, 16 is the proposed gain threshold, 21/25 are uniformity/holomorphy failure tests. Cards 02/18 share paid transfer but 18 specifically tests nullspace mismatch.

Protect strongest bridges 01 and 02. Use the recipe's existing integer seed 188016482515055114330975640748000702224 for sequential no-replacement uniform draws from **all** remaining literal p<.10 and then p<.01 cards, irrespective of original groups. Choose the most different remaining mechanism from priority 28,24,30,23,17. Then draw one wildcard from the entire unselected eligible pool. Freeze each conditional pool before drawing; never reroll. Develop at most three, protecting a viable rare or wildcard selection.

statement:
## 4. The sixth-root sum has only harmonic mass

Each nonzero Eisenstein element has a unique representation
\[
u=v\alpha^6,
\qquad v\ {\rm sixth\mbox{-}power\mbox{-}free},\quad
\mathfrak a=(\alpha)\ {\rm an\ integral\ ideal}.
\tag{NP13}
\]
Here \(\alpha^6\) is again independent of generator choice, and v contains the actual unit. Division of every valuation by six proves existence and uniqueness. Arbitrarily high S-valuations are included in \(\mathfrak a\). Moreover \(\psi_u^*=\psi_v^*\), so the nonprincipal restriction is constant along each sixth-power family.

For a row ball \(0<q_u\le R\), its cores satisfy \(q_v\le U_{\mathfrak a}=R/q_{\mathfrak a}^6\), and \(q_{\mathfrak a}\le R^{1/6}\). Squaring NP12 and summing these disjoint families gives
\[
\begin{split}
\sum_{\substack{0<q_u\le R\\u\in\mathcal R_\nu}}|M_u(D;W)|^2
\ll &(2DR)^\eta\|W\|_{C^J}^2\\
&\times\left[
R\sum_{\mathfrak a}\frac{\mathcal P_{1/2}(\mathfrak a)^2}{q_{\mathfrak a}^6}
+R^{1/6}D^{5/6}
 \sum_{q_{\mathfrak a}\le R^{1/6}}
 \frac{\mathcal P_{11/12}(\mathfrak a)^2}{q_{\mathfrak a}}
\right].
\end{split}
\tag{NP14}
\]
This holds for \(1\le R\le D^B\), for any fixed B. The first series converges: its local factor is
\(1+(1-q_p^{-1/2})^{-2}q_p^{-6}/(1-q_p^{-6})=1+O(q_p^{-6})\), with fixed small-prime constants.

The second sum costs only \(\log(2R)\), not a small power per root. For any fixed \(\sigma>0\), put
\[
b_\sigma(p)=(1-q_p^{-\sigma})^{-2}-1,\qquad
b_\sigma(p^j)=0\quad(j\ge2),
\]
extend multiplicatively on good ideals, and put \(b_\sigma(p)=0\) at primes in S. Then \(b_\sigma\ge0\),
\(\mathcal P_\sigma(\mathfrak a)^2=\sum_{d\mid\mathfrak a}b_\sigma(d)\), and
\[
\sum_d\frac{b_\sigma(d)}{q_d}
=\prod_{p\notin S}\left(1+\frac{b_\sigma(p)}{q_p}\right)<\infty
\]
because \(b_\sigma(p)=O_\sigma(q_p^{-\sigma})\). Using the ideal harmonic bound therefore proves
\[
\sum_{q_{\mathfrak a}\le A}\frac{\mathcal P_\sigma(\mathfrak a)^2}{q_{\mathfrak a}}
=\sum_{q_d\le A}\frac{b_\sigma(d)}{q_d}
  \sum_{q_m\le A/q_d}\frac1{q_m}
\ll_{\sigma,K,S}\log(2A).
\tag{NP15}
\]
This prices the root sum without moving any prime into the fixed datum. Combining NP14–NP15 yields
\[
\boxed{
\sum_{\substack{0<q_u\le R\\u\in\mathcal R_\nu}}|M_u(D;W)|^2
\ll (2DR)^\eta
\left[R+R^{1/6}D^{5/6}\log(2R)\right]\|W\|_{C^J}^2,
\quad 1\le R\le D^B .
}
\tag{NP16}
\]
The identical proof without the nonprincipal restriction gives NP16 for all nonzero rows. The first term has summable root mass; the second has harmonic root mass. Replacing the latter by an ambient root count would lose the claimed gain.
title: 4. The sixth-root sum has only harmonic mass

Retain both ordered good squarefree rationally primitive short ideals g,g', including g=g', the actual bounded complex core h((g,g')), and the rational gcd screen on their norms.     a_H(n)=alpha(n)eta(n)chi_n(lambda)^(-2)gamma_2(n),
    xi(g)=alpha(g)^3 eta(g)^3.

Every term keeps the original phases/profiles/masks, both projectors 1_(P,Rg)=1 and 1_(P',Rg')=1, and both independent separating heights. Put v_P=u1(P)/sqrt(q_P), w_P'=u2(P')/sqrt(q_P'); each root occurs once, ||v||^2=Omega1 and ||w||^2=Omega2. With the entire signed short-source sum folded into the scalar matrix K, set T=K^transpose so that the literal finite packet is H=w^*Tv. No positive divisor child replaces the common core. No extra opposite-coprimality screen is inserted.

The raw target is B0 sqrt(Omega1 Omega2), where

K0 denotes the original K scale, and P_orig retains the original kernel coefficients and weighted profile seminorms. The physical outside N^(-1)G^(-2) is applied exactly once afterward. # [private research revision]: curved additive source and complete signed Gauss bank

Accept G125–G127 from the frozen [author](curved-source/report.md) and
[independent review](curved-source-review/report.md). This recurring
headroom pass discovered a replacement detector, proved its quantitative
return, tried a coarse arithmetic estimate, and isolated the remaining
signed sum. No larger c is proved: c11=.1251459636 and all inherited
F0/analytic, positive-slot and external definition/import/admission
obligations remain unchanged. Scope is fixed ordinary Dirichlet characters,
including natural zeros, every finite height and the principal pole.

Five initial mechanisms were considered before selection: prime-dilation
disjointness, fugacity root deflation, weighted prime-block contraction,
rational Fourier observation, and separate additive wavelength/damping.
The selected last route extends W24's angular-contour seed with an actual
moving-source return. W21 supplied general peak-width ancestry. No
literature-priority claim or conductor-uniform theorem is made.

## G125. Exact curved return and actual coarse bound

For fixed b>1 define the literal infinite sources

    F_chi(z)=sum_(n>=1)mu(n)chi(n)exp(-nz), Re z>0,
    V_b,chi(x)=F_chi(x^(-b)+i/x).

For Re s>0 put I_n(s)=integral_0^infinity exp(-nt^b-int)t^(s-1)dt.
Substitute v=nt and rotate to arg v=-alpha, fixed0<alpha<pi/(2b).
The small arc vanishes; on the large arc exp(-n^(1-b)v^b) decays and
|exp(-iv)|<=1. On the new ray the Taylor remainder for exp(-z),Re z>=0,
is bounded by |z|^K/K!. Consequently

    I_n(s)=sum_(0<=k<K) A_k(s)n^(-s-(b-1)k)+R_n,K(s),
    A_k(s)=(-1)^k Gamma(s+bk)exp(-i*pi*(s+bk)/2)/k!,
    |R_n,K(s)|<=C_(b,K,C)n^(-Re s-(b-1)K),             (1)

uniformly on every compact C in Re s>0. The ray majorant is
exp(alpha Im s)Gamma(Re s+bK)/(K! sin(alpha)^(Re s+bK)). Thus the sum
of remainders is normally holomorphic for Re s>max(0,1-(b-1)K).
Absolute Fubini initially on Re s>b proves

    H_chi(s)=integral_0^infinity F_chi(t^b+it)t^(s-1)dt
      =sum_(k<K) A_k(s)/L(s+(b-1)k,chi)+R_chi,K(s).     (2)

Every L is the actual original ordinary character, with all Euler holes.
At b=3/2,K=1 the remainder is holomorphic for Re s>1/2, and the
multiplier Gamma(s)exp(-i*pi*s/2) has no zeros there. The sign of the
additive phase and that multiplier is fixed, not discarded.

A sufficient complete arithmetic input is, for everyepsilon>0 and every
large dyadic shell, with a common fixed gamma,

    integral_X^(2X)|V_b,chi(x)| dx/x <<_(chi,epsilon) X^(gamma+epsilon).
                                                               (OPEN-CURVE)

Constants and onset may depend on the fixed character. Shell L2 energy
bounded by X^(2gamma+epsilon) suffices by Cauchy–Schwarz. Dyadic summation
makes H holomorphic on Re s>gamma; the complementary t>=1 tail is paid by
exp(-t^b)/(1-exp(-t^b)). For b=3/2,gamma>1/2, (2) excludes every zero
there. The principal pole gives a zero of the reciprocal and is retained.
Imprimitive Euler factors were included from the start; their zeros lie
on Re s=0. No uniform bound over arbitrarily large imaginary parts is
asserted or needed: local holomorphy reaches each finite height.

For any fixed b>1,0<gamma<1 choose finite K with1-(b-1)K<gamma.
Starting from Re s>1, solve (2) successively on strips of width b-1:
all shifted reciprocals are already holomorphic on the next strip.
The same H and nonvanishing A_0 give the unshifted extension. Finitely
many steps reach Re s>gamma. Neither b nor K moves with x. No converse
equivalence to a Mertens bound has been proved.

At b=3/2, first gain needs gamma<theta11=.8748540364, or energy
exponent<1.7497080728. Conditional examples retain
gamma=.87485 (c=.12515), gamma=5/6 (c=1/6), gamma=3/4 (c=1/4).
They are open estimates, not accepted endpoints.

The pass proves the actual pointwise theorem

    V_(3/2),chi(x)<<_(chi,epsilon)x^(5/4+epsilon)        (3)

for every sufficiently large REAL x, including the whole infinite tail.
For its full proof use N=x^(3/2),T=N(log x)^2,U=V=floor(sqrt x), and
the all-integer convolution identity

    mu=mu_<=U+mu_<=V-mu_<=U*mu_<=V*1+mu_>U*mu_>V*1.

Both short sums cost O(sqrt x). Fixed-modulus additive Fourier inversion
preserves chi's zeros and reduces to beta=ell/q-1/(2*pi*x). For Y<=T,
the exact spacing estimates are

    sum_(d<=x)min(Y/d,1/(2||beta d||))<<_q x log(2x)+Y/x,
    sum_(h<=H)min(M,1/(2||beta h||))<<_q(H/x+1)(M+x log(2x)).

Split into q residue classes and blocks of length at most x. Phases in
each block move monotonically at spacing q/(2*pi*x); nearest points cost
the finite first argument, and the rest a harmonic sum. In the first
estimate a nontrivial zero crossing occurs only at d comparable to x,
so resonance costs Y/x. This includes noninteger real x and exact
resonance, not only generic phases.

The divisor-sized Type I coefficient, supported on d<=UV<=x, therefore
costs x^(1+epsilon). For Type II let b_d=sum_(c|d,c>V)mu(c).
In a box (M,2M]x(L,2L],md<=Y, Cauchy retains the COMPLETE Gram

    sum_(d,e)b_d conjugate(b_e)
       sum_(m in(M,2M],m<=Y/max(d,e))e(beta m(d-e)).

The inner set is one interval. Its diagonal and the second spacing bound
give squared cost

    T^epsilon [M^2 L+ML(L/x+1)(M+x log(2x))]
      <<T^epsilon(Y^2/U+Y^2/x+Yx)log(2x)<<x^(5/2+epsilon).

Summing the logarithmically many boxes proves the prefix bound uniformly
for Y<=T. Partial summation restores exp(-n/N), and the discarded tail
is O(N exp(-(log x)^2)), smaller than every fixed power. This proves (3).
The short terms and tail are paid for the target; BOTH Type I exponent1
and Type II exponent5/4 remain above theta11. A Type II improvement alone
would not complete a gain. Their full signed recombination is an eligible
weaker target. The pointwise saving is relative to damping length x^(3/2),
not the observation scale x.

The [Green–Tao primary source](https://aif.centre-mersenne.org/item/10.5802/aif.2401.pdf),
Lemma4.1, concerns a dyadic interval with UV<=N. Here the all-integer
identity restores both short terms and is separately derived from
mu*1=delta_1. The [BSZ theorem](https://publications.ias.edu/sites/default/files/disjointness%20b-s-z%20oct.pdf)
was discovery ancestry only; its fixed-parameter conclusion supplies no
uniform power saving under a shrinking parameter.

## G126. Exact whole-shell bank with two branches paid

For prime P not dividing q and (a,P)=1, finite multiplicative
orthogonality, including the ramified multiples n=Pm, gives on Re s>1

    sum_n mu(n)chi(n)e(an/P)n^(-s)
      =1/(P-1)sum_(psi modP)psi(a)tau(conjugate psi)/L(s,chi psi)
       -chi(P)P^(-s)/L(s,chi psi0).                    (4)

The sign psi(a) and negative correction are substantive. The latter uses
mu(Pm)=-mu(m)1_(P not dividing m), retaining all P^2 and character zeros.
Since tau(psi0)=-1, its reciprocal contains exactly
L(s,chi psi0)=(1-chi(P)P^(-s))L(s,chi). Fixed-character constants cannot
be silently summed uniformly over these growing moduli.

More usefully, freeze any unramified prime P comparable to X before
varying x over the ENTIRE shell [X,2X]. Let
w_P(x)=x^(-b)+i(1/x-2*pi/P). Absolute convergence and the same finite
orthogonality prove

    V_b,chi(x)=G_P,chi(x)+B_P,chi(x),
    G_P,chi(x)=1/(P-1)sum_(psi!=psi0)psi(-1)tau(conjugate psi)
                                      F_(chi psi)(w_P(x)),
    B_P,chi(x)=-F_(chi psi0)(w_P(x))/(P-1)
                               -chi(P)F_(chi psi0)(P w_P(x)).     (5)

The common profile and every shell point are retained, even where its
residual imaginary part vanishes. Because |F_eta(w)|<=1/Re w,

    |B_P,chi(x)|<=x^b/(P-1)+x^b/P<<X^(b-1).           (6)

Thus BOTH the principal Gauss branch and ramified branch are paid
without a growing-conductor estimate. For gamma>=b-1 the every-epsilon
whole-shell L1 target for V is equivalent to that for G; likewise for
the L2 energy via the triangle inequality of square-root norms. At b=3/2
all proposed targets exceed1/2. Choosing P separately for each shell
changes the representation, not the global Mellin source. All remaining
chi psi are nonprincipal when (P,q)=1.

The coherent bank G is still unbounded at the desired exponent. Taking
absolute values term by term can spend sqrt(P) in Gauss weights. That
is a certificate cost, not a lower bound on its true signed sum. The
complete common-profile bank is the precise new arithmetic target.

## G127. Energy, absolute price and point observation

For every bounded coefficient sequence, the same complete varying-damping
energy satisfies E_b(X)<<_b X^(b+1), without epsilon. Put
d=1/[2(2X)^b],G(z)=sum a_n exp(-dn)z^n,Delta=x^(-b)-d.
Then d<=Delta<=C_b d and the subharmonic Poisson inequality bounds
|G(exp(-Delta-i theta))|^2 by P_Delta*|G|^2,theta=1/x.
The kernels obey P_Delta<=C'_b P_d. Since dx/x<=2X|dtheta|,
enlarge the positive integral to a full period and use Parseval:

    E_b(X)<=C_b X sum_n |a_n|^2 exp(-2dn)<<X/d<<X^(b+1).

Variable damping was paid by Poisson domination, not replaced informally.
A scale-dependent diagnostic array a_n=exp(in/x0),n<=X^b,x0=3X/2,
has magnitude of order X^b on logarithmic width X^(1-b); it shows this
uniform bounded-array exponent is sharp. It is not a Möbius counterexample
or an assertion about one fixed infinite array. In particular exponent5/2
energy alone contains no arithmetic gain; the pointwise theorem (3) does.

For the ACTUAL a_n=mu(n)chi(n), square-divisor expansion gives
sum_(n<=Y)|a_n|^2=d_qY+O_q(sqrt Y), with
d_q=zeta(2)^(-1)product_(p|q)(1+1/p)^(-1)>0. In the exact energy kernel

    K_X(n,m)=integral_1^2 exp(-(n+m)/(X^b u^b))
                              exp(-i(n-m)/(Xu))du/u,

the diagonal is d_q(2^b-1)X^b/(2b)+O_q(X^(b/2)). It is not a lower
bound for total signed energy. Binning squarefree units in [X^b,2X^b]
into intervals of length X/4 produces order X^(b+1) distinct close pairs
by Cauchy. For them Re K>=exp(-4)cos(1/4)log2. Hence the ACTUAL
termwise-absolute off-diagonal price is at least a constant times
X^(b+1). One phase integration by parts also gives

    |K_X(n,m)|<=C_b exp(-c_b(n+m)/X^b)min(1,X/|n-m|),

so that price is at most O_b(X^(b+1)log(2X)). It obstructs that absolute
pricing method; aggregate signed cancellation remains eligible.

Finally |V_b'(x)|<<X^(2b-2) on an enlarged shell. A peak of height A
has width at least a constant times A/X^(2b-2). Its L2 and L1 masses
cost respectively A^3/X^(2b-1) and A^2/X^(2b-1). Thus whole-shell energy
exponent2gamma gives point exponent(2gamma+2b-1)/3; L1 exponent gamma
gives( gamma+2b-1)/2. At b=3/2 the quarter-energy target permits point
exponent7/6, not3/4. Isolated rational-frequency values therefore do not
inherit the same shell exponent and are not themselves an obstruction.

## Acceptance and next action

Root read complete author/reviewer reports and both helpers, reconstructed
all arguments, and checked primary scope and the named earlier ideas.
Ten frozen artifacts and five immutable source pins are in the
[manifest](retention-manifest.json). Exact finite checks cover the two
rational decompositions, full hyperbolic Gram, resonance and budgets.
No unchanged checks were rerun. These checks do not prove OPEN-CURVE.

Next seek a bound for the complete signed Type I/II combination, coherent
nonprincipal bank, or original shell L1 norm, below theta11. Preserve
the exact damping, every branch, natural zeros and all shell points.
The accepted pointwise gap is5/4-theta11=.3751459636; the generic energy
gap is5/2-2theta11=.7502919272. Neither is an available proof reserve.
Near gains,1/6 and1/4 remain explicit conditional targets. The next
recurring pass may replace this architecture; it must discover and develop
a promising mechanism before testing its weakest complete estimate.
