# Seventh-cycle review: vertical bounds and the sparse Fourier gate

9 October 2026. Started from clean local revision
06d45c9b11268caaada7f315191db4659e1541cd.
The controller owns records, Beads and serial Git writes; all six
[restricted mathematical source] agents were read-only. The native Goal remains active.
The user-accepted c0=0.125113352960035869... is unchanged. No stronger
zero-free theorem or milestone manuscript is claimed.

## New quantitative theorem

For every required fixed finite ray, every nonzero integral h, and
each fixed buffered strip 1/2+epsilon<=sigma<=B, write T=1+|t|.
The full sixth-order family and each norm sector satisfy

\[
|\Psi_{\nu,d}(h,\sigma+it)|+|\Psi_\nu(h,\sigma+it)|
\ll Tq_h^4+T^3q_h^{6-2\sigma}.
\]

All original fixed-prime valuations are allowed. The constants depend
on the fixed level, S, rays and strip, not h or t. Finite squarefree
extraction transfers this with an arbitrarily small q_h^delta loss.
The exact forced-divisor identities give explicit polynomial g,h
growth, with all outside collision zeros retained.

Combined with [private research revision] holomorphy, this justifies pole-free buffered
Mellin shifts for every finite row/divisor truncation. Summing the
coarse row powers over unbounded divisors is not justified. The
incidence mean, original product-kernel transfer and both moment
zero-frequency terms remain open.

The proof is in sixth-forced-divisors.md Sections 16--17, (50)--(59).
The controller derived fixed-argument Whittaker inversion;
review_cubic independently checked it. sixth_order supplied
the elliptic cutoff-resolvent construction. The controller supplied
the spinor spectral lower bound that makes the argument uniform at
all t; sixth_order and independent review_sixth checked that
identification and its constants. review_sixth then reviewed the
integrated theorem, including arithmetic powers and truncation limits.

At y_h=x/(2pi R_h), R_h=2q_h^2/sqrt(3), the exact local vector has
norm comparable to T^(-1)q_h^(2sigma-3). The large-order K expansion
has a dominant Gamma(w) term; its exponential size cancels the
Gamma(w+1) denominator. Compactness and whole-vector nonvanishing
handle bounded t. The x=2 leading constant is an asymptotic, not an
exact finite-height formula.

On the fixed arithmetic quotient the standard SU(2) type gives a
rank-two spinor bundle, with a flat unitary genuine twist. For
D=-(Omega1+Omega2),

\[
D=2\nabla^*\nabla-\tfrac32
=2\mathscr D_{\mathrm{spin}}^2+\tfrac32,\qquad
\lambda(w)=\tfrac32-2(w-\tfrac12)^2.
\]

Essential self-adjointness and compact-support form positivity imply
spec(D) is contained in [3/2,infinity). For v=sigma-1/2,
the distance of lambda(w) to this half-line is 2(v^2+t^2) if
|t|<=v and 4v|t| otherwise. It is at least v(v+|t|), giving
a resolvent bound O_epsilon(T^(-1)) for all t.
An initially suggested extra factor two in that lower bound was
withdrawn: t=v/2 disproves it. The stated weaker inequality suffices.

Subtract ALL incoming cusp terms with fixed cutoffs. The forcing
is compactly supported and O(T); the remaining outgoing and
nonconstant terms are L2 for each fixed parameter. The resolvent
therefore gives an O(1) L2 norm and O(T^2) covariant H2 norm.
Scaled Sobolev evaluation costs H^(3/2) at reduced cusp height H.
Adding the incoming part proves

\[
|E(g,w)|\ll H(g)^{\sigma+1/2}+T^2H(g)^{3/2}.
\]

The elementary bound H(n(z)a_y)<<1+y+y^(-1), uniform over the
finite components of the adelic Fourier integral, then gives the
displayed arithmetic estimate through Whittaker inversion.

Primary inputs:
[DLMF Bessel connection formula](https://dlmf.nist.gov/10.27.E4),
[I-series](https://dlmf.nist.gov/10.25.E2),
[Gamma asymptotics](https://dlmf.nist.gov/5.11),
[Melrose, twisted Lichnerowicz formula, Section 3.2](https://math.mit.edu/~rbm/18.199-S06/18.199-S06.pdf),
and [Braverman--Milatovic--Shubin, Theorem 2.3 and Corollaries 2.9--2.10](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0201231v3).
The cycle-6 KP realization supplies the actual Eisenstein family.

The earlier alternative Q=(Omega1-Omega2)/i was not used: formal
symmetry and centrality did not establish its proposed self-adjoint
domain and strong commutation. A separate compact-t cusp-propagation
argument also became unnecessary once the spinor lower bound was
proved. Neither alternative remains an active proof dependency.

## An exact formulation of the remaining prime mean

cubic_covariance derived and review_cubic independently accepted
Section 18, (60)--(64). The exact Whittaker integral is

\[
\int_0^\infty\|\mathbf W^+(h^4,y,w)\|^2
y^{3\sigma-3}\frac{dy}{y}
=C_\sigma(t)q_h^{-2\sigma},
\qquad C_\sigma(t)\asymp_\sigma T^{\sigma-2}>0.
\]

The complete positive Gamma formula is retained in (61).
Two Schlaefli integrals, a Gamma integral and a Beta integral prove
it directly; an exact half-order calculation checks its normalization.
No floating-point experiment is used as proof.

Partition primes by their finite ray R_p, sum the four norm sectors
within each family, and project onto p^4 Fourier frequencies.
Primary representatives make p to p^4 injective. If H4 is the sum
of those squared Fourier coefficients, Tonelli gives

\[
\sum_pq_p^{-2\sigma}|\Psi_{\nu R_p}(p,w)|^2
=\frac1{J^2C_\sigma(t)}
\int_0^\infty H_4(y,w)y^{3\sigma-3}\frac{dy}{y}.
\]

Both sides may still be infinite. The new identity is a target,
not a bound. The finite rays, nonunit zeros and J factor are exact.

Full Parseval alone leaves a factor P^(6-6sigma) on q_p asymptotic
to P at y=P^(-2). Even bounded full horosphere energy would leave
P^(3-6epsilon) near the central line. An artificial lacunary sequence
with coefficients Q_j^(3-2w) gives an explicit countertest:
its full Fourier energy is uniformly bounded in y for each fixed
1/2<sigma<3/2, yet its weighted prime mean diverges for sigma<=1.
The constants are uniform only on compact sigma substrips.
This is an inference obstruction, not an automorphic counterexample.

The next useful result must control the actual sparse p^4 projection
or its equivalent arithmetic prime mean. Replacing it by the full
Fourier sum before obtaining a saving loses the required information.

## Sextic rectangle candidate: exact, but insufficient

sextic_optimization tested a coefficient-specific multiplicative
rectangle; review_sextic independently checked the identity and
the failed transfer. For the actual f=conjugate(alpha)gamma2 nu,
B1.11 gives f(ax)=f(a)f(x)chi_x(a)^4. Thus, when a,b,x,y are
squarefree good and all four cross pairs are coprime,

\[
f(ax)f(by)\overline{f(ay)f(bx)}
=K(a,x)\overline{K(b,x)}K(b,y)\overline{K(a,y)},
\quad K(a,x)=\chi_x(a)^4.
\]

No coprimality within (a,b) or (x,y) is needed. Same row/mark and
short-divisor phases cancel on units; their collision zeros remain.
Mixed row/mark pairs leave the separated phase
Omega(x)conjugate(Omega(y)), with
Omega=chi_R^3 chi_R'^(-3) chi_P^(-2) chi_Q^2.
There is no residual quadratic reciprocity sign.

For fixed Cartesian squarefree sets of lengths M,X and nonnegative
weights w_a,v_x<=1, the existing cubic large sieve gives

\[
\sum_{a,b}w_aw_b
\left|\sum_xv_xK(a,x)\overline{K(b,x)}\right|^2
\ll (MX)^\epsilon MX\{M+X+(MX)^{2/3}\}.
\]

Fix b, apply the sieve to v_x conjugate(K(b,x)), whose squared mass
is O(X), then sum O(M) rows b. The balanced M=X=N^(1/2) bound is
N^(5/3+epsilon). This is a complete rectangle, not an estimate for
the original signed two-column form with its two equality exclusions.

In a genuinely factorable marked Type II component, the reassembly
z=xP and divisor Cauchy give only

\[
|F_R^{\mathrm{II}}|^2
\ll Z^\epsilon N\{M+XL+(NL)^{2/3}\},\qquad MX=N.
\]

Summing rows leaves an unaffordable large factor beyond KN.
Balanced factorization also omits prime and unbalanced Type I
columns. The masks u!=v and Pu!=Qv provide no established inequality
transferring their signed energy to the rectangle. The candidate
therefore supplies no saving for H. Its other branches remain open.
No additional conditional H label or changed exponent certificate
is warranted.

## State and validation

The proof review covered local asymptotics, spectral domains,
spinor flatness, exact spectral distance, all-cusp cutoffs,
finite-level constants, row exponents and the sparse projection.
Active text now distinguishes proved polynomial growth from the
unproved weighted mean. Historical reviews and supplied manuscripts
are preserved as provenance.

Beads remains the active checklist. The continuation, pole-energy
and polynomial-height prerequisites are complete in the stated scope.
The next action is the genuine prime-fourth-frequency estimate,
then the full incidence trace, common-kernel transfer and zero terms.
Cubic covariance and sextic short-divisor cancellation remain
alternative routes. The native research Goal remains active.

On the full closed rectangle `0<=delta<=3/4`, `0<=p<=1/2`, define

```
D=3-p-2p/(3kappa_*),
P=2(1-p)(1-p/(3kappa_*)),
V=5/6-delta,  J=VD+delta P,
R=1-delta+delta P V/(2J),  q=delta p.
```

```
G(d,c)=(1+delta)/2+13h/75-y/2-ell/2+ell*q
       +d(1/4+3R/4-17/50)-q(2y-d)/(2c).
```

Every coefficient is computed as a `Fraction`. Positive coefficients prove positivity on the entire box, not a sampled grid. Recursive bisection splits the longest normalized axis. The program checks exact area 3/8, containment and pairwise disjoint interiors as well as the construction. Its engine is retained from this lane's independent [private research revision] arithmetic; its present execution is **author evidence**, not a new independent implementation.

| h | `546/125` | `1/1000000` | 8 |

## 4. Developments11/15: retain the native phase matrix

The source is the same-scale distinct-rational-norm degree-one Eisenstein prime packet, not a rational or arbitrary phase matrix. Both ordered short sources including equality, the complete bounded h((g,g')), both rooted arrays, 1_(P,Rg)=1 and1_(P',Rg')=1, sharp endpoints, natural zeros, ray/unit data and BOTH independent heights remain. The transformed kernel is literally

    chi_pi(h)^3 chi_pi'(h)^3 chi_pi(s)^2 chi_pi'(s')^4
                 b(pi)conjugate(b(pi')) zeta_(pi,pi'). (R10)

The native group has Q^2 elements, Q=q_pi q_pi', and unitary Fourier factor1/Q. That is not an extra physical saving. These conventions and the raw target were compared with [restricted research revision] h-joint source/integration.

For a frozen finite packet write its coefficient kernel K_PP' so the scalar is sum v_P K_PP' conjugate(w_P'), v=u1/sqrt(q_P),w=u2/sqrt(q_P'). Then exactly H=w* K^T v. This fixes the author's “harmless conjugate convention”: conjugated input vectors may alternatively give v*Tw, but the actual coefficients cannot be conjugated without the corresponding convention. The mark norms remain Omega1,Omega2. Fold every other scalar/source label into this exact matrix before estimating. Integrated height-dependent bounds must pay the total variation of the original weights and their original profile seminorms.

Diagonal unitary rephasing with transported inputs preserves the scalar and every singular value. With fixed inputs it changes the source. The2-by-2 unit-entry norm squared2+2|cos(Phi/2)| is correct, but establishes no actual native cycle value or power saving. This is the old U-FLUX distinction.

The real zonotope sum[-z_j,z_j] misses independent complex coefficients: i is not in[-1,1]. Independent complex discs have support sum|z_j|. The actual rank-one bilinear domain instead has spectral-norm supremum; its convex hull is the nuclear-norm unit ball by singular-value decomposition. If original inputs have additional restrictions, this remains a sufficient relaxation, not a lower bound on the arithmetic source.

The valid sufficient Gram test is

    M=max_j {sum_i|T_ij|^2+
                  sum_(k!=j)|sum_i conjugate(T_ij)T_ik|},
    ||T||^2<=M.                                    (R11)

The inner sum stays SIGNED. Expansion keeps both short cores/projectors, all height pairs and actual phases. Hermitian Gram row and column absolute sums agree, yielding Schur's bound. The raw target is G K0 [N+L+(NL)^(2/3)] sqrt(Omega1 Omega2) P_orig, where K0 is the original row parameter. M bounded by the square of its coefficient factor suffices. Only afterward apply N^-1 G^-2 ONCE. A norm deficit Z^delta requires square-level gain Z^-2delta for this particular strategy; this is not a derivation of every historical H deficit. Full tails, other branches and the far complement remain. No bound of the necessary size for M is proved.

## 1. Exact replacement source: squarefree divisor incidence

Fix an ordinary Dirichlet character chi modulo a positive integer q, with its natural zero extension.
For real X>=1 use the literal finite downset

    D_X={n<=X: n squarefree, (n,q)=1}.

It is closed under positive divisors. Order it increasingly, put N=|D_X|, and let e
be the coordinate of1 and v=1-e. Define upper triangular matrices

    Z(d,n)=chi(n/d) 1_(d|n),
    B(d,n)=chi(n/d) 1_(n/d is prime), d,n in D_X,
    P=Z-I, R=Z+v e^T.                                      (1)

No zero character value is divided: excluded nonunits and nonsquarefree integers
already have mu(n)chi(n)=0. Matrix products preserve the original product-size
cutoff because every intermediate divisor of n belongs to D_X.

If j=omega(n/d), every path of j prime covers from d to n is a permutation of the
j distinct prime factors, and its character weight telescopes to chi(n/d).
Consequently

    B^k(d,n)=k! chi(n/d) 1_(d|n, omega(n/d)=k),
    exp(B)=Z, exp(-B)(d,n)=mu(n/d)chi(n/d)1_(d|n).            (2)

All exponentials are finite polynomials. This removes the factorial path cost
EXACTLY through1/k!, before any estimate; it does not create a contractive norm.
The determinant lemma, det Z=1 and(2) give

    det R=1+e^T Z^(-1)v=sum_(n<=X)mu(n)chi(n)=M_chi(X).       (3)

This is the character-twisted squarefree version of Wilf's finite-poset identity.
The downset restriction changes the ambient matrix, but not this scalar arithmetic
source. No old nonlinear/Hecke source is silently substituted into a prior theorem.

Let K=max_(n in D_X)omega(n). For X with K>=1, P^(K+1)=0, and

    A_k(X)=e^T P^k v
          =sum_(n in D_X,n>1)chi(n) k! S(omega(n),k),
    det(lambda I-R)=y^(N-K-1)
         [y^(K+1)-sum_(k=1)^K A_k(X)y^(K-k)], y=lambda-1.    (4)

Here S(j,k) is the Stirling number of the second kind. Indeed a strict divisor
chain is an ordered partition into k nonempty blocks of the distinct prime
factors. The resolvent determinant identity gives(4) first at y!=0 and then as a
polynomial identity. At least N-K-1 eigenvalues are1; it is not asserted that this
multiplicity is exact when a twisted leading coefficient cancels. At y=-1, all
chain depths together give the original mu sign. X below the first unramified
prime is the trivial one-dimensional case R=(1).

Since an integer with j distinct prime factors is at least(j+1)!, elementary
Stirling estimates give K=O(log(2X)/loglog(3X)). Small degree alone does not bound
the polynomial at y=-1 or the product of its nontrivial roots.

## 2. A complete squarefree-chain estimate, and what it does not do

Let F_0=1 and F_j=sum_(k=1)^j k!S(j,k) for j>=1. Each ordered set partition is
encoded injectively by a permutation with cuts: order each block internally and
concatenate its blocks, retaining the cuts. Therefore

    F_j<=2^(j-1)j! for j>=1.                                (5)

For EVERY fixed sigma>1,

    sum_(n squarefree) F_(omega(n)) n^(-sigma)<infinity.      (6)

Here is an elementary proof paying every depth. Let w_p=p^(-sigma). Choose a
FINITE prime cutoff Y_sigma such that R_sigma=sum_(p>Y_sigma)w_p<1/4. Let r be the
number of primes up to Y_sigma. Write e_j for the elementary symmetric function
of the w_p. Splitting small and large primes,

    e_j(all)=sum_(a+b=j,0<=a<=r)e_a(small)e_b(tail),
    e_b(tail)<=R_sigma^b/b!.

Multiplying by(5), each fixed a contributes at most a constant times

    sum_(b>=0) (2R_sigma)^b (a+b)!/b!.

This converges, since the factorial ratio is a polynomial of degree a in b.
There are only r+1 choices of a. This proves(6), without silently imposing a
fixed chain depth, a maximum-number-of-primes model, or independent prime choices
inside the original n<=X cutoff. Rankin's inequality now yields the COMPLETE bound

    sum_(n in D_X) F_(omega(n)) <<_(q,epsilon) X^(1+epsilon). (7)

The left side is the permanent of the principal squarefree Redheffer matrix, and
is an upper bound for the absolute sum of every twisted determinant contribution.
Moreover1+sum_k |A_k| is bounded above by this expression after the coefficientwise
triangle, with equality for principal chi. Thus all roots, all depths and all chain
multiplicities have been included. This is sharper than importing the unrestricted
integer-factorization permanent exponent into this different squarefree matrix.
The unrestricted theorem is not contradicted.

The exponent1 is sharp for this positive price. Indeed it contains |D_X|. Expanding
mu^2(n)=sum_(d^2|n)mu(d), and counting q-units in each inner interval, gives

    |D_X|=delta_q X+O_q(sqrt X),
    delta_q=(phi(q)/q)prod_(p not dividing q)(1-p^(-2))>0.    (8)

The O(sqrt X) includes the tail of sum mu(d)/d^2 and every floor endpoint. Hence

### 3.1 A direct periodic hyperbola estimate

If b is any fixed bounded periodic sequence with mean zero, then for every fixed
integer t>=1,

    sum_(n<=x)b^(*t)(n) <<_(b,t) x^(1-1/t), x>=1.            (12)

For t=1 this is bounded partial sums. For t>1 set Y=x^(1/t). Every tuple with
product<=x has at least one coordinate<=Y. Inclusion-exclusion on those t events

hypothesis to the remaining t-j coordinates, with beta=1-1/(t-j). Taking absolute

    C x^beta [sum_(n<=Y)|b(n)|n^(-beta)]^j
      << x^beta Y^(j(1-beta))=x^(1-1/t).

For j=t the product constraint is automatic since every coordinate<=Y. That term

inclusion-exclusion sign. This proves(12), with real endpoints and fixed t constants.
No unproved divisor-problem exponent or growing-t uniformity is imported.

bounded source-specific combination and the full estimates/limitations above are
new in this record, without any literature-priority claim.


## 7. Evidence, provenance and final state

Primary mathematical sources verified through web text in this pass:

- [Herbert S. Wilf, *The Redheffer matrix of a partially ordered set*](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0408263v1), arXiv submission19August2004; the served PDF title date is6October2018. Pages1-4 supply the finite-poset determinant/chain ancestry. Neither date is inferred from the local filename.
- [R. C. Vaughan, *On the eigenvalues of Redheffer's matrix I*](https://personal.science.psu.edu/rcv4/personal/Publications/REDCONF.pdf),1993, printed pp283-286. The full-integer characteristic calculation is ancestry; its spectral conclusions were not transferred to the squarefree/twisted matrix.
- [NIST DLMF, section27.12](https://dlmf.nist.gov/27.12), especially27.12.4-5, records the ordinary prime-count asymptotic. Only its much weaker pi(y)>>y/log y consequence is used for the actual projected family; no RH-conditional estimate or growing-modulus claim is used.

The 2025 Clement-Steinerberger Redheffer paper was also opened in discovery, but
no singular-vector or determinant estimate is imported from it. There is no local
PDF binary or pixel inspection claim. Exact local source hashes and read extents
are retained in source-evidence.json; web URLs/observations are not misrepresented
as local binary hashes.

The one execution of check.py passed four groups in native receipt96d9c6. It uses
exact Gaussian integers, including the quartic character modulo5, for the determinant,
prime-cover exponential, chain multiplicities and characteristic polynomial at
N+1 distinct integer arguments. It checks the Newton generating formula through
j=30 and J=1,...,8; full finite filtered convolutions through240; all p-valuation
formulas for j<=15 and a<=J+3; and exact Fraction budgets at the incumbent and all
three targets. Natural ramified zeros and complex character values remain. These
finite identities detect transcription errors; none proves the asymptotic bounds,
the all-height return, or the missing cancellation. No unchanged check was rerun.

Outcome: useful complete source estimates and a precise unpaid signed tail; no
new c. All earlier frozen scopes remain untouched. Final freeze/readback, own
claim release and the sole reserved reviewer wake are recorded separately; the
reviewer has another bounded review before beginning this one, and the original
01:05 author /01:35 reviewer deadlines have not changed.

# [private research revision] auxiliary mathematical results

This record supplements the consolidated manuscript. **The accepted constant remains \(c_0=0.125113352960035869\ldots\).** A proved identity, restricted sector or conditional criterion is not an improved zero-free theorem. All inherited input names, arithmetic conventions and source aliases are defined in documents 01 and 06.

| IDs | Mathematical role |
|---|---|
| A01–A03 | Coherent unembedded sextic estimate, orientation/index budgets, and smooth prime convolution with its resonance boundary |
| A04–A07 | Actual-probe calibration, cube inversion, fixed-degree detrending, and source-shell norm/period tests |
| A08–A09 | Exact arithmetic source resolvent and shell-correction/higher-moment alternatives |
| A10–A12 | Positivity/heat countermodels, one merged prime-coefficient criterion, and the Fredholm compensator trap |
| A13–A14 | Correct Jacobi identities, an open quadratic/triple hybrid, and checked conditional probe-saving geometry |
| A15–A18 | Gcd-localization counterexample, unequal Type I extension, completed-cutoff obstructions, and broad-cusp oldform screen |

The new proofs are given here. Unproved estimates are named at their first point of use. Document 05 records what failed and the permissible changed construction; document 03 develops those constructions as research tasks.


## A01. The coherent unembedded nonzero sextic aggregate

**Status:** proved restricted-sector estimate relative to the exact inherited raw field. It is not a bound for every nonzero frequency, the full compensated energy, or mixed embedded covariances.

Use the raw [restricted research revision] §5 field
\[
H(m)=Y^{-1}\sum_{a,A}c_{a,A}G_a(m)\chi_A(m)
W_0(q_m/(Qx_a)),
\quad
G_a(m)=q_a^{-1/2}g_{\chi_a}(a,-m),\quad x_a=q_a/Y,
\]
with exactly its original coefficients and all fixed sectors. Here \(A=cn^3\), \(c\) squarefree. Expand \(\sum_m|\xi(m)|^2|H(m)|^2\). Select pairs satisfying
\[
\frac{aA'}{bA}\in I_{\rm good}^{\,6}. \tag{A01.1}
\]
For every selected pair subtract its complete additive zero covariance in the AA19 sense, retaining the full continuous product profile. Denote the signed sum of differences by \(\mathcal E_{\ne,\rm coh}^{\rm raw}\). Then
\[
|\mathcal E_{\ne,\rm coh}^{\rm raw}|\ll_\epsilon Z^\epsilon. \tag{A01.2}
\]
If both good outer indices \(a,b\) are squarefree, the bound improves to \(Z^\epsilon/Y\). Physical energy includes the additional factor \(Q^{-1}\).

### Local masks and exact coherent incidence

At \(p\mid AA'\), write \(\alpha_p=v_p(a)\), \(\beta_p=v_p(b)\), \(d_p=v_p(A)-v_p(A')\pmod6\). AA14 forces \(\alpha_p,\beta_p\le1\) because the column character requires a unit row. The local row character exponent is \(d_p-\alpha_p+\beta_p\). Under (A01.1) it is zero and the factor is a unit scalar times \(1_{p\nmid m}\).

Since \(A=cn^3,A'=c'n'^3\), the difference between the two squarefree incidence differences lies in \([-2,2]\). It cannot cancel an odd multiple of three. Therefore, at those primes,
\[
\alpha_p-\beta_p=v_p(c)-v_p(c'),\qquad
v_p(n)-v_p(n')\equiv0\pmod2.
\]
Outside \(AA'\), the coherent condition is \(\alpha_p-\beta_p\equiv0\pmod6\), with the additional support restrictions below.

Consequently all surviving pairs admit the exact good-ideal parametrization
\[
c=gu,\ c'=gv,\quad
a=d_0ur_1^6,\ b=d_0vr_2^6,\quad
n=hs^2,\ n'=ht^2.
\]
Here \(g,u,v\) are pairwise coprime squarefree; \(h\) is squarefree; \((r_1,r_2)=1\); \((r_1r_2,AA')=1\); \((d_0,uv)=1\); and \(v_p(d_0)\le1\) at \(p\mid AA'\). Core/cube overlaps among \(g,u,v,h,s,t\) otherwise remain. In particular, \(r_i\) may share primes with \(d_0\) outside \(AA'\).

At a good prime outside \(AA'\), let \(E_j=1_{p^j\mid m}\), \(E_0=1\). Lifting a normalized local Gauss sum gives, for \(j\ge1\),
\[
G_j(m)=q^{j/2-1}1_{p^{j-1}\mid m}
\sum_{x\bmod p}^{*}\chi_p(x)^j
\psi_p(-mx/p^{j-1}).
\]
If \(6\nmid j\),
\[
|G_j(m)|^2=q^{j-1}(E_{j-1}-E_j).
\]
If \(6\mid j\),
\[
G_j(m)=q^{j/2-1}(qE_j-E_{j-1}),\quad
|G_j(m)|^2=q^{j-2}\{(q^2-2q)E_j+E_{j-1}\}.
\]
These explicitly retain principal-on-units spikes.

For unequal coherent valuations \(\alpha>\beta\), positive \(\beta\not\equiv0\pmod6\) gives disjoint supports. If \(\beta=0\), the principal formula for \(G_\alpha\) applies; if \(6\mid\beta>0\), \(G_\beta\) is constant on \(G_\alpha\)'s support. Every surviving local product is a linear combination of divisibility masks with coefficient \(\ell^1\) norm at most \(2q^{(\alpha+\beta)/2}\). CRT therefore writes the full good kernel as
\[
K_S(m)\sum_e b_e1_{e\mid m},\qquad
\sum_e|b_e|
\ll_\epsilon(q_aq_b)^{1/2}
(q_aq_bq_Aq_{A'})^\epsilon. \tag{A01.3}
\]
Here \(K_S\) belongs to the original fixed finite periodic family; no moving prime is placed in \(S\). If \(a,b\) are squarefree, the factor \((q_aq_b)^{1/2}\) is unnecessary.

### Uniform discrepancy, including periods beyond the row range

For every bounded smooth annular profile family on the Eisenstein lattice,
\[
\sum_{e\mid m}\Psi(m/\sqrt Q)
-\frac{Q}{q_e}\int_{\mathbb C}\Psi
=O_\Psi(1), \tag{A01.4}
\]
with the fixed lattice covolume included and uniformly in \(Q,e\).

To prove it, rotate and scale the ideal lattice by a generator of \(e\), and put \(L=(Q/q_e)^{1/2}\). For \(L\ge1\), Poisson bounds the nonzero dual sum by
\[
O_N\!\left(L^2\sum_{\xi\ne0}(1+L|\xi|)^{-N}\right)=O(1)
\]
for fixed \(N>2\). For \(L<1\), the compact annulus meets only \(O(1)\) lattice points and its continuous mass is \(O(L^2)\). Fixed residue classes satisfy the same argument. This proves (A01.4) with \(K_S\) and its actual zero average.

Applying this to (A01.3), each pair's row sum minus its complete zero mode is \(O(YZ^\epsilon)\) times fixed profile seminorms.

### Sum of the original coefficients

The modulus of a paired completed coefficient is
\[
\frac1{q_g\sqrt{q_uq_v}\,q_h^2q_s^2q_t^2}.
\]
For fixed \(d_0,r_1,r_2\), the outer annuli imply
\[
\sum_{u,v}(q_uq_v)^{-1/2}
\ll \frac{Y}{q_{d_0}(q_{r_1}q_{r_2})^3}.
\]
The original log-Gaussian profiles satisfy
\[
\sum_gq_g^{-1}|V(T_1q_g)V(T_2q_g)|\ll1
\]
uniformly in \(T_1,T_2>0\), by dyadic ideal counting and Cauchy. The \(h,s,t\) sums converge at norm exponent two, the \(r_i\) sums at exponent three, and \(\sum_{q_{d_0}\ll Y}q_{d_0}^{-1}\ll\log(2Y)\). Thus total absolute coefficient/profile mass is \(O(Y\log(2Y))\). Small powers of completed column lengths are absorbed in the original two-sided log-Gaussian envelope.

Multiplying by the raw prefactor \(Y^{-2}\) and the \(O(Y)\) per-pair discrepancy proves (A01.2). In the squarefree outer subcase that discrepancy is \(O(1)\), proving the stronger bound.

For a fixed number of all-marked slots at **unembedded \(D=1\)**, replace \(V\) by the exact AA18 kernel. Permitted divisors of \(A\) are divisor-bounded, and AA20 supplies a common envelope at scale \(ZP\). No extra tuple count or \(q_U^{-1/2}\) is inserted. The same proof applies.

**Unpaid:** nonprincipal good-character pairs, including their values at sixth-power additive frequencies; mixed embedded arguments \(e^2r,d^2r\); arbitrary \(A\)-dependent weights; growing slot counts; the full physical saving.

**Precise follow-up:** derive the actual embedded coherent row kernel first, with \(\operatorname{lcm}(D^2,E^2)\) and all character zeros. Once such a kernel is a fixed-sector divisibility combination, dilation introduces no difficulty for (A01.4), because \(1_{p^j\mid\lambda r}=1_{p^{(j-v_p(\lambda))_+}\mid r}\) and cannot increase coefficient \(\ell^1\) mass. The remaining problem is the correct character/coefficient incidence and total marked mass, not a blanket “long period” obstruction.

**Sources:** BB R08; [restricted research revision] AA14–AA20; [restricted research revision] AB16.

## A02. Additional exact index and budget results

### Orientation-sensitive rectangular means

Suppose for the same physical family one has
\[
\mathcal M(A,B)\ll T^C(AB)^\delta
\min_j A^{r_j}B^{s_j},\qquad r_j,s_j\ge0.
\]
Summing over \(AB^2\le X\) gives exponent
\[
R=\max_{0\le z\le1/2}\min_j\{r_j(1-2z)+s_jz\}.
\]
Every bound is nondecreasing in \(A\), so the outer maximum is on \(AB^2=X\). Only endpoints and intersections of the finitely many affine lines need checking. Dyads cost logarithms.

A fixed-\(b\) estimate \(Y^{1+\eta+\delta}q_b^{\nu+\delta}\) yields an all-physical-row exponent \(1+\eta\) if \(\nu<1+2\eta\): a \(b\)-dyad \(B\) contributes \(X^{1+\eta+\delta}B^{\nu-1-2\eta+O(\delta)}\).

The hypothetical pointwise model \(|F_{ab^2}|\ll q_aq_b^{1/2}\) gives rectangular mean \(A^3B^2\), and hence \(X^{3-4z}\). It reaches \(X^{35/32}\) only for \(z\ge61/128\). Combining it with the weak fixed-\(b\) exponent \(\nu=3/2,\eta=3/32\) gives worst exponent \(85/69>35/32\). These are exact limitations of the supplied upper bounds, not lower bounds for actual means. [BA D4.]

### Reduced index and the conditional anisotropic calculation

On squarefree sixth-order Gauss columns, \(h=ab^2\) permits replacing \(h^4=a^4b^8\) by \(a^4b^2\). The quotient is \(b^6\); at column primes dividing \(ab\), both local nonprincipal Gauss sums are zero. This algebra gives reduced norm \(A^4B^2\). It supplies no arithmetic approximate functional equation.

If one separately grants the proposed AFE length \(C=A^2B\), dual control, coefficient mass, and the displayed anisotropic sieve bound in BB R04.a, substitution gives \(A^{7/3}B^{5/3}\) for \(A\ge B\) and \(A^{8/3}B^{4/3}\) for \(B\ge A\). In the latter region it fits the target \(A^{1+\eta}B^{2+2\eta}\) only if
\[
B\ge A^{(5-3\eta)/(2+6\eta)}.
\]
At \(\eta=3/32\), this is \(B\ge A^{151/82}\). At \(A=B\), its physical exponent is \(4/3\). The algebra is verified; exact applicability of the cited external sieve and the AFE remain separate obligations.


The full unequal-cutoff proof is A16. Fixed off-central incidence budgets are in T08.

## A03. Smooth prime convolutions: a proved gain and its resonance boundary

**PROVED RELATIVE TO I-HECKE.** Source: SA Part VI, DS1–DS5. Fix \(0<c<c_0\), a nonprincipal finite-order Hecke character \(\chi\), and a fixed smooth annular \(w\). The buffered strip gives
\[
 \sum_{\mathfrak p}\chi(\mathfrak p)w(q_{\mathfrak p}/P)q_{\mathfrak p}^{it}
 \ll_{c,\epsilon,w}P^{1-c+\epsilon}
       (2q_{\mathfrak f_\chi}(2+|t|))^\epsilon. \tag{A03.1}
\]
For a direct proof, choose a fixed disk about \(1-c+it\) contained in \(\Re s>b_0\). The inherited subpower bounds for \(L\) and \(L^{-1}\), followed by Cauchy for \(L'\), give a subpower bound for \(L'/L\). Shift Mellin inversion of \(-L'/L\) to that line. Nonprincipality removes a pole at one. Prime powers contribute \(O(P^{1/2+\epsilon})\); insert \(1/\log q_{\mathfrak p}\) in the annular profile to remove the logarithmic weight. All conductor zeros remain.

For fixed \(j,r>0\), let
\[
 b_{\mathfrak b}=\mathbf1_{\mathfrak b\ {\rm sf}}
 \sum_{\mathfrak p_1\cdots\mathfrak p_j=\mathfrak b}
       \prod_iw_i(q_{\mathfrak p_i}/P_i),\quad
 \prod_iP_i\asymp B,\quad P_i\ge X^r .
\]
In every fixed polynomial conductor/height range and for a deleted radical \(q_R\le X^C\),
\[
 \sum_{(\mathfrak b,R)=1}b_{\mathfrak b}\chi(\mathfrak b)q_{\mathfrak b}^{it}
 \ll B X^{-rc+\epsilon}. \tag{A03.2}
\]
Apply (A03.1) in one prime variable and count the others absolutely. A prime equality or deletion in that variable saves at least \(X^r\) in the elementary product count; there are \(O_C(1/r)\) deleted primes of norm at least \(X^r\). Inclusion–exclusion restores squarefreeness. This proves the stated gain for the displayed untwisted fixed prime convolutions.

This result does not license the desired cubic dispersion substitution. Factoring a target column introduces a moving cubic twist in its short coefficient. The permitted test character can cancel that twist. On a prime subpacket with coefficient \(-\eta_k(p)w(q_p/B)\), testing against \(\overline{\eta_k}\) leaves a prime count of order \(B/\log B\). Thus the uniform nonprincipal-character hypothesis of the inspected dispersion theorem fails. Its raw lengths also require \(D\le K\), whereas the desired direct substitution has \(K<D\). Deleting all primes up to \(X^r\) is different from a radical of polynomial norm: the elementary Euler-product budget has logarithm \(O(X^{rc})\), not \(O(\log X)\). These are method-specific obstructions; a coupled resonance addback could still be useful.

## A04. Exact calibration of a family of adaptive probes

**PROVED finite-dimensional identity; the arithmetic saving is OPEN.** Source: BA D6. Let \(G>0\) be the Gram of actual *complete physical probes*, let \(Ev=0\) encode nuisance constraints, and let \(p^*v=1\) retain the principal signal. Set
\[
 A=EG^{-1/2},\quad b=G^{-1/2}p,\quad
 \Delta=b^*P_{\ker A}b.
\]
If \(\Delta>0\),
\[
 \inf_{Ev=0,\ p^*v=1}v^*Gv=\Delta^{-1},\qquad
 v=G^{-1/2}P_{\ker A}b/\Delta \tag{A04.1}
\]
attains equality. If \(\Delta=0\), the constraints are infeasible. Indeed \(w=G^{1/2}v\) lies in \(\ker A\) and \(b^*w=1\); Cauchy gives the lower bound and the displayed vector attains it.

For a semidefinite Gram, first check whether a null vector satisfying the nuisance conditions carries the signal; otherwise use a justified quotient/regularization. For multiple principal aliases the scalar calibration becomes a matrix range condition. The first missing theorem is a lower bound on projected principal separation with all coefficient, derivative, and height costs included. The indefinite coprime covariance and the incomplete outer A-field cannot replace \(G\).

## A05. Triple-convolution cube inversion and the \(5/6\) absolute barrier

**PROVED RELATIVE TO the inherited triple diagonal; signed improvement OPEN.** Source: BA D7, [restricted research revision] Z13–Z18. With fixed \(r>0\), absorb the common Bessel normalization into
\[
 H_r(t)=tK_{1/3}(\kappa t)^2K_{1/3}(\kappa rt),\qquad
 P_{{\rm sf},r}(y)=y^3\sum_{c\ {\rm sf,good}}\mu(c)H_r(\sqrt{q_c}y).
\]
The actual coefficient identity, allowing shared core/cube primes, gives
\[
 P_r(y)=\sum_B\xi_{\rm ang}(B)q_B^{-3}
                    P_{{\rm sf},r}(q_B^{3/2}y),\qquad
 P_{{\rm sf},r}(y)=\sum_B\mu(B)\xi_{\rm ang}(B)q_B^{-3}
                    P_r(q_B^{3/2}y). \tag{A05.1}
\]
This is ordinary convolution inversion of commuting dilations, justified absolutely at each fixed \(y>0\) by the Bessel tail.

If \(P_r(y)\ll y^{3-2a}\) at zero and decays rapidly at infinity, absolute inversion requires
\(\sum_Bq_B^{3/2-3a}<\infty\), exactly \(a>5/6\). Splitting at \(q_B=y^{-2/3}\) gives bounds \(y^{3-2a}\) for \(a>5/6\), \(y^{4/3}(1+|\log y|)\) at equality, and \(y^{4/3}\) below it. These are upper-budget limitations, not lower bounds on the signed inverse. An angular Möbius partial-sum bound \(O(U^\theta)\), with the needed derivative control, permits Abel summation when \(\theta<3a-3/2\). At \(a=3/4\) this asks for \(\theta<3/4\), a separate unpaid theorem. The numerical \(5/6\) shared with the source-shell obstruction does not identify their spaces.

## A06. Fixed-degree polynomial detrending still detects zeros

**PROVED CONDITIONAL TRANSFER.** Source: BA D8. Let \(M(x)=\sum_{n\le x}\mu(n)\), fix \(r\ge0\), and suppose, for every \(\epsilon>0\),
\[
 \inf_{\deg P\le r}\int_N^{2N}|M(x)-P(x)|^2dx
       \ll_{\epsilon,r}N^{2a+1+\epsilon},\qquad 0<a<1. \tag{A06.1}
\]
Then \(\zeta(s)\ne0\) for \(\Re s>a\). To prove this, choose
\(\phi=\psi^{(r+1)}\), \(\psi\in C_c^\infty(1,2)\), and set
\(T_\psi(N)=\int_1^2M(Nu)\phi(u)\,du\).
Polynomial moments vanish, so Cauchy gives \(T_\psi(N)\ll N^{a+\epsilon}\). Initially for \(\Re s>1\),
\[
 \int_0^\infty T_\psi(N)N^{-s}\frac{dN}{N}
 =\frac{\int_1^2\phi(u)u^sdu}{s\zeta(s)}.
\]
The left side is holomorphic for \(\Re s>a\). Integration by parts makes the numerator
\((-1)^{r+1}s(s-1)\cdots(s-r)\int\psi(u)u^{s-r-1}du\).

- With geometry fixed, \(\partial_\kappa F<1/20\) up to the accepted \(\kappa_0\).

If \(\beta_*>b\), write \(\mu=\beta_*-b\), and use \(\kappa=2\beta_*-1=\kappa_t+2\mu\). The derivative bound gives \(F_\kappa-\beta_*\le-.9\mu\). Convexity in the row exponent and the checked endpoint/floor margins complete the inherited numerator estimate. The physical saving gives \(J_\eta\ll Z^{b-k+\epsilon}\). M B0.7's original ordering of buffers, meshes, finite slots and small polynomial heights then gives the contradiction. No arithmetic estimate in (A14.1) is proved by the numerical certificate.

### Source-code inspection, execution, and corrected copy

The original script was inspected and independently executed. Every target passed all 23 checks; amplitude box counts were respectively 98017, 32449, 22269, 32265, 19093.

A corrected portable copy is included as checks/grok_transfer_certificate.py; its independent rerun is checks/grok_transfer_certificate_result.txt. It requires only Python's standard library. Corrections:

- Signed rational-to-Decimal rounding now uses the signed numerator directly. The original helper rounded negative nonterminating rationals in the wrong direction, although its only relevant negative test here was the exact terminating \(-1/50\), so the five original certifications were not affected.
- Printed slack/rate lower bounds use directed subtraction.
- Subdivision midpoints use directed addition and division; the original children still covered their parent in the actual run, but the revised arithmetic makes that coverage explicit.
- The geometry identity \(x+y+\ell=1\) is justified by its definitions and checked by an enclosure containing one, instead of a tolerance.
- An unused placeholder and the false comment that the quadratic's constant term was zero were removed.

The handoff's prose bound “uniform derivative \(<.043\)” is false. The maximum of its reported certified upper bounds is \(0.0440833871\ldots\), so use \(<.0441<1/20\). Several strict slack inequalities were rounded upward; the table above uses safe downward bounds. At \(c=.1255\),
\[
y-x=0.08753960844756839075\ldots,\qquad
\frac{y-x}{12}=0.00729496737063069923\ldots.
\]
Thus the supplied lower claim \(y-x>.08753960845\) is also an upward-rounding error. The ratio \(.0006/((y-x)/12)<.0823\) remains correct.

### Gram localization is not a vector projection

The three terms in B0.22's nonnegative majorant have square-root exponents
\[
\frac x2,\qquad \frac{y-x}{2},\qquad
\frac x2+\frac{y-x}{12}.
\]
The middle term is smaller than the first for \(y<2x\). This correctly identifies the \(P_a^{1/6}\) term as the sole excess in that majorant.

However the label \(k=r^6\) occurs after expanding pairs of outer columns, with profile argument \(\sqrt Q\,r^6/(ab)\). It is not a fixed additive spectral projection of \(A\). GS §2 states this caveat, but §7 then writes \(A^{(6)}\) without constructing it. Therefore the claimed “sixth-power portion of \(A\) paired with \(B\)” is **not presently a defined mathematical object**. Retain (A14.1), or construct an exact theta-paired bilinear identity/projector and prove its principal calibration before using that language. Positivity of a raw neutral-ray Gram does not refute a theta-specific cancellation estimate; it also does not define such a projection.

The claimed “full deletion permits only a detached window near \(.12937\)” is also too strong. That window is merely the diagnostic obtained by forcing equality \(\sigma=(y-x)/12\) and a particular stationary geometry. A stronger valid estimate may be deliberately weakened; for example the certified \(.1255\) geometry needs only \(\sigma=.0006\), much less than its full excess. The detached saturated-geometry window is not an obstruction to smaller improvements.

### New exact alternative to the fixed-point search

At fixed target \(\kappa\) and its chosen \(\delta\), put
\[
D_\kappa=3R'/4-1/(24\kappa),\quad
H_0=-1/(2D_\kappa),\quad
H_1=-(1/2+1/(6\kappa))/D_\kappa.
\]
Then \(h=H_0+H_1\ell\). Let
\[
A_\kappa=(2H_0-1)/12,\qquad
B_\kappa=(2H_1-3)/12,\qquad
\ell_b=4(c-1/12).
\]
The simultaneous equations \(\ell=\ell_b-4\sigma\), \(\sigma=\alpha(y-x)/12\) solve exactly as
\[
\sigma=
\frac{\alpha(A_\kappa+B_\kappa\ell_b)}
{1+4\alpha B_\kappa}, \tag{A14.2}
\]
whenever the denominator is nonzero. All capacity and rectangle constraints still require separate verification. This removes the need for a monotonicity-assuming binary search and is a new exact diagnostic simplification.

The resonant-coset, Pólya–Vinogradov-shaped, and generic \((Q+Z)\) comparisons in GS §5 are at most bookkeeping comparisons under their displayed models. The coset bound is not reconstructed there with full coefficients; do not promote it to a new uniform arithmetic lemma. The explicit algebraic comparisons at \(4/33\) are correct.

## A15. Gcd localization need not preserve positivity

**PROVED counterexample, new explicit formulation in this merge.** Choose distinct coprime core labels \(c_1,c_2\) with \(q_{c_i}>G_0>1\), and two identical nonzero vectors normalized to have Gram
\[
 B=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&1\end{pmatrix}.
\]
The small-gcd mask \(\mathbf1_{q_{(c_i,c_j)}<G_0}\) is
\(\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}\). Its entrywise product with \(B\) has eigenvalues \(1,-1\). Smooth weights with the same support separation give the same counterexample. Thus a positive complete-zero Gram cannot generically be bounded after gcd truncation by treating that truncation as a positive projection. This explains why T07 leaves the full small-gcd covariance and removes the already paid zero form only globally. It does not prove a negative eigenvalue for the particular arithmetic field.

## A16. Unequal Type I cutoffs

**PROVED bounded extension of the inherited Type I theorem.** Sources: BB R04b; M (3.15), (M.4)–(M.7), (M.35).

Let \(m_i=\mu1_{q\le Y_i}\), \(u_i=\delta-m_i*\mathbf1\), and \(R=Y_1Y_2\). Convolution algebra gives
\[
 \mu=m_1+m_2-m_1*m_2*\mathbf1+\mu*u_1*u_2.
\]
For the completed product Type I array \(a=-m_1*m_2\), one has support \(q_r\le R\), divisor-bounded coefficients, and prime valuations at most two. The unchanged central estimate M (3.15) costs
\(DK\|a\|_2^2\ll(DKR)^\epsilon DKR\).
The mixed estimate M (M.35) has outer weight
\(q_{\operatorname{rad}(rs)}^{1/2+\epsilon}/q_r\); the two divisor-weighted sums have sizes \(R^{1/2+\epsilon}\) and \(R^{3/2+\epsilon}\). Their product is \(R^{2+\epsilon}\). The double-residue factors \(q_r^{-1},q_s^{-1}\) have only subpower summed cost, exactly as in M (M.4)–(M.7). Therefore
\[
 |\mathfrak Q[I,I]|\ll(DKR)^\epsilon
 \{D^{5/3}K^{1/3}+D^{4/3}K^{7/12}R^2+DKR\}. \tag{A16.1}
\]
Both original Mellin roots and whole profiles remain in force. At \(K=D^k\), the two cutoff-dependent terms are affordable when
\[
 \log_D R<\min\{1-k,(8-7k)/24\}. \tag{A16.2}
\]
This enlarges the choice of decomposition geometry; it proves no improved remainder estimate.

## A17. Exact completed-cutoff and rough-column obstructions

**PROVED counterexamples and quantitative restricted bounds.** Sources: SA ([restricted research revision])–([restricted research revision]); CP (27); BB R04b.

The all-ideal identity \(I_Y(n)=-\mu(n)\) for \(q_n\le Y\) cannot be applied only to the squarefree core after completion. Take \(c=1,B=p\), with \(Q=q_p>Y\). Then \(I_Y(1)=I_Y(p^3)=-1\), and T05's exact density gives
\[
 \mathcal A_Y(1,p)
 =-1-Q^{-1/2}\overline{\xi_{\rm ang}(p)}(1-Q^{-1})\ne-1.
 \tag{A17.1}
\]
The stronger condition \(q_cq_B^3\le Y\) does imply
\(\mathcal A_Y(c,B)=-\mu(c)\): every sampled \(ct^3\) lies below the cutoff, and for \(t\ne1\) its Möbius value is zero. Cancellation therefore concerns small whole columns and requires both corresponding completed coefficients. It is not a cancellation of every small-core packet.

There is also a finite-cutoff averaging obstruction. Let \(c=pq,e=r\) for distinct good primes exceeding every cutoff in a fixed collection. Then \(I_Y(c)=I_Y(e)=-1\), while \(\mu(c)\mu(e)=-1\). Any normalized average of those cutoffs leaves
\[
 \mu(c)\mu(e)-I_Y(c)I_Y(e)=-2. \tag{A17.2}
\]
This rules out coefficientwise annihilation, not cancellation after summing columns with their actual phases.

The larger cutoff is not forbidden by the inherited Type I theorem: at \(K=D^k\), \(Y=D^y\), it permits
\[
 y<\min\{(1-k)/2,(8-7k)/48\}.
\]
For \(k=.8765\), the endpoint is \(.03884375\), whereas T05's complete cube-row restriction has a strict saving only for
\(y<(1-k)/6=.020583333\ldots\). That latter threshold is a limitation of its upper bound.

The bare outside-cube sector has a sharper rigorous estimate:
\[
 |P_{\rm cub}\mathfrak Q[I,I]_{B=E=1}|
 \ll_\epsilon(DKY)^\epsilon D^{2/3}K^{2/3}Y^4. \tag{A17.3}
\]
To prove it, repeat T05 without the outer cube sums and use the fixed-ray squarefree estimate on \(\Re s=1/2+\delta\). The two columns contribute \(D^{2+2\delta}Y^4\); row counting contributes \(K^{2/3}D^{-4/3}\). Choose the preliminary divisor loss below \(2\delta\) so its coprime-projector sum converges, then choose \(\delta\) inside the final epsilon. This gives (A17.3).

At \(k=.8765\), even the supremum over the admitted cutoff interval gives exponent \(11251/8000=1.406375\). These bounds do not produce a critical-sized II term available to offset the still-unpaid principal C–C contribution in the bare sector. This is an upper-budget comparison, not a lower bound on that C–C contribution.

## A18. Broad-cusp diagonal oldforms: exact support and scaling screen

**PROVED support and scaling identities; no new changed-current norm is established.** Sources: SA Part I §11, (S16)–(S19); [restricted research revision] AA21–AA23; [restricted research revision] AB14–AB15.

Let \(Q=q_p\), \(\Phi_r=\operatorname{diag}(p^r,1)\), and let the broad cusp be
\(\gamma=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&0\\C_0&1\end{smallmatrix}\right)\).
For nonnegative integer \(r\), choose \(p^rd_r-C_0b_r=1\), compatibly with the fixed level. Direct multiplication gives
\[
 \Phi_r\gamma=
 \begin{pmatrix}p^r&b_r\\C_0&d_r\end{pmatrix}
 \begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&p^r\end{pmatrix}
 \begin{pmatrix}1&-b_r\\0&1\end{pmatrix}. \tag{A18.1}
\]
The first source has frequency \(\mu n/p^r\), height \(Y/Q^{r/2}\), and its exact translated phase. The ordinary twisted second source has frequency \(\mu m/p^2\), height \(Y/Q\), and its multiplier vanishes if \(p\mid m\). Opposite frequency matching forces
\[
 m=p^{2-r}n. \tag{A18.2}
\]
Thus \(r=0\) and \(r=1\) vanish identically. A single-prime dilation does not restore the ordinary orientation.

At the first favorable dilation \(r=2\), unit indices are allowed and both heights are \(Y/Q\). Even assuming the fixed phases match the desired arithmetic coefficient, the invariant radial pairing is
\[
 \int J(Y/Q)Y^{2s}\frac{dY}{Y^3}
 =Q^{2s-2}\int J(y)y^{2s}\frac{dy}{y^3}. \tag{A18.3}
\]
Probability averaging cancels the horizontal Jacobian. Extraction therefore costs \(Q^{2-2\sigma}\), namely \(Q\) at the central edge, before any cost of a new current norm.

The source supports valuations \(0,1\pmod3\). For \(r=2+3j\), matching gives \(n=p^{3j}m\); the coefficient relation
\(\tau(p^{3j}m)=Q^{j/2}\tau(m)\), together with the first source's height factor \(Q^{-3j/2}\), leaves \(Q^{-j}\). Its favorable period factor is \(Q^{2s-2-j}\), worsening extraction. For \(r=3+3j\), the new squarefree prime contributes the inverse cubic phase that cancels the ordinary row twist, producing a principal good core rather than the desired ordinary one. For \(r=4+3j\), the forbidden local valuation makes it vanish.

For a negative dilation \(r=-m\), \(m\ge1\), use the projective representative \(\operatorname{diag}(1,p^m)\). The exact identity
\[
 \begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&p^m\end{pmatrix}\gamma
 =\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\p^mC_0&1\end{pmatrix}
  \begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&p^m\end{pmatrix}
\]
again gives first-source scale \(z/p^m,Y/Q^{m/2}\). The first unit-compatible case \(m=2\) has the same favorable radial cost. The available common cover
\(\Gamma_0(p^2)\cap\Gamma^0(p^m)\) has good-prime index
\(Q^{m+2}(1+Q^{-1})\); imposing its two off-diagonal divisibilities in the determinant-one matrices proves this count. At the broad cusp the width is \(p^{\max(m,2)}\), because conjugating its unipotent requires the same parameter to satisfy both divisibilities. Its available probability-normalized seed norm therefore has an additional cost of order \(Q^{\min(m,2)/2}\).

These are costs and support restrictions for the specified diagonal-oldform construction, not minimal-norm theorems for every source or cusp. General oldform combinations, non-diagonal constructions, and a test projected onto the actual current span remain possible, but require a better calibrated period-to-norm ratio and an actual norm estimate.

## 2. The added theta error is uniformly small

Applying SQ4--SQ7 to SC2 gives the exact decomposition

\[
\mathcal T_\sigma(R)=\mathcal M_\sigma(R)+\mathcal E_\sigma(R),
                                                               \tag{SC4}
\]

where \(\mathcal M_\sigma(R)\) is precisely SQ9--SQ10 with

\[
\mathfrak M(R;Q)=
\sum_{\substack{q_s\le R\\(s,Q)=1}}\frac{\mu(s)}{q_s}
\]

in place of its original \(\mathfrak M(S_0;Q)\). Nothing else in
the source main changes.

The SQ proof of the error works for **every** fixed ideal s, with
no upper bound on its norm. This uniformity needs three checks.

First, all logarithmic derivatives of \(E_\psi(y)\) are uniformly
bounded for every \(y>0\), by SQ5. In the compact normalized column,
dual-core, and divisor variables, changing \(q_s\) changes only the
unnormalized argument y. Hence the profile-separation mass and the
original height costs do not acquire a power of \(q_s\).

Second, \(\sqrt{Q_\psi}/\sqrt{F_S}\le1\) is still the exact SQ8
conductor cancellation. Fixed-place square-power tails have already
been included in t; no new family of fixed-place powers is counted.

Third, by the exact MO6 radical identity, the mask is
\((s,D\mathfrak A_i\mathfrak A_j)=1\). For fixed s it consists of
a fixed-place mask, a P-only mask, and an \((n,b)\)-only mask.
Thus it preserves mark independence, even for \(q_s>Z^C\). There is
no need to expand the divisors of s or pay \(q_s^\epsilon\). HG13a
still makes the g-profile factor external; the z allocations,
divisor-inside-column theta weights, and common g/d/z0 mass are
exactly those in SQ. In particular one is not choosing unrelated
coefficient sequences for each g.

Consequently, after the complete z and g/d budgets, the error of
one fixed s is \(\ll_{\epsilon,\mathrm{orig}}
Z^\epsilon\mathcal H/q_s^2\). The z1 sum still uses its original
allocation/density proof; the z0 sum stays inside the common column
mass. Summing ideal norms, using
\(\#\{s:q_s\le x\}=O_{\mathbb K}(x)\), proves

\[
\boxed{
|\mathcal E_\sigma(R_2)-\mathcal E_\sigma(R_1)|
\ll_{\epsilon,\mathrm{orig}}
\frac{Z^\epsilon\mathcal H}{R_1},
\qquad R_2\ge R_1\ge S_0.}
                                                               \tag{SC5}
\]

Thus the error has an absolutely summable s-tail in the proved
operator bound. The same assertion has not been made for the main
or for an unbounded sum of separate h0 main/error terms.

## 2. Exhaustive collision decomposition before any new divisor extension

At a good prime p, each original inverse occurs at most once by its Mobius factor, and at most one slot occurs on each side by disjoint pools. Write a=v_p(n), b=v_p(n'), 0<=a,b<=3. Preserve the full original site incidence, not only (a,b). There are six aggregated sites: inverse1,inverse2,slot on each copy; named slots and pool tests further restrict their allocations.

A prime is a collision prime exactly when a+b>=2. Let h_ab be the squarefree product of primes of that type, for the13 pairs (a,b) with0<=a,b<=3 and a+b>=2. These13 ideals are pairwise coprime. Keep all their site allocations and original coefficients. Put

    Lc=product h_ab^a, Rc=product h_ab^b, D=N(Lc Rc),
    L=N(Lc), R=N(Rc),
    k=product_(a!=b)h_ab, E=product_(a=b>=1)h_ab,
    Kc=N(k), Hcol=product h_ab.

Then uniquely n=Lc*x, n'=Rc*y, where x,y are squarefree, pairwise coprime and prime to Hcol. Every prime of x occurs in ONE original left site; every prime of y in ONE original right site. Thus this is an exact tuple decomposition, including all shared slots and inverse-slot coincidences. Nonunique means Hcol!=1. All six gcd tests are now predicates on the collision labels and their site allocations alone.

The independent original slot allocations have divisor multiplicity tau(Hcol)^C at fixed slot depth. A prime cannot be placed in a slot unless its original pool/coefficient allows it. No count of arbitrary factorizations replaces those masks. Absolute upper bounds may subsequently discard impossible allocations, paying this fixed divisor power.

There are three useful support facts:

    N(h_20),N(h_02) << G P0;
    N(h_11) << N0;
    N(h_11^(ij)) < H_ij,                              (2)

where h_11^(ij) contains precisely the type(1,1) primes assigned to inverse i on the left and inverse j on the right. The first follows from G157's n/rad(n)<C G P0 on each column; h_20 or h_02 divides that defect. The second follows because h_11 divides both original merged columns. The third follows because those primes divide the actual original inverse gcd on that edge. All fixed annular constants are retained. These are upper support bounds, not signs or probabilistic assertions.

For every row u, including its natural zeros,

    chi_n(u)^e conjugate(chi_n'(u)^e)
     =psi_k(u) chi_x(u)^e conjugate(chi_y(u)^e)
                              1_((u,E)=1),           (3)
    psi_k=product_(a!=b) chi_p^(e(a-b)).

Every nonzero local exponent is +/-1,+/-2 or+/-3, hence nonprincipal primitive at its good prime. The primitive good conductor is kxy. Equal positive valuations cancel phase but keep the hole in E. In particular chi_p(u)^a conjugate(chi_p(u)^a) is the UNIT INDICATOR, not the constant1. The fixed nu(n)conjugate(nu(n')) stays in the actual coefficients; no order-six claim is made about nu.

If kxy=1 then x=y=1 and every a=b, so n=n'. Conversely the full relative principal class is the complete merged diagonal in this bounded-valuation source. Its absolute coefficient mass is O(H_J U^epsilon), by G181's c_abs bound; its row contribution is O(H_J U^(1+epsilon)). This pays that whole class before claiming zero-frequency absence. Original principal inducing rows of the physical family have not been discarded.

statement:
## 3. Exact source and the actual gcd-one projection

Whenever n<z^3 and omega_z(n)>=2, its source is uniquely n=rpq,
p<q both greater than z, each of valuation one, and r<z. Since z>3,
f(n)=f(r). All powers in r remain. For n>=z^3 the two-prime completion
can fail; its coefficient multiplicity is at most d_3(n). The complete
Gaussian discrepancy is O_A(X^-A). Thus, with full infinite sums,

    R(x)=V(x)+S_(f 1_(r>=2))(x)+O_A(X^-A),
    |S_(f 1_(r>=2))(x)|<=U(x).                      (A10)

This is the same exact central source as the accepted critical theorem;
its all-core absolute estimates were proved separately above.

The elementary lattice and tail bounds used throughout are

    sum_n g(log(n/y)) <=C_tau y, y>0,
    sum_(|log(n/y)|>=W)n^epsilon g(log(n/y))
       <=C_(tau,epsilon)y^(1+epsilon)exp(-W^2/(4tau)). (A11)

Completing the Gaussian square proves the tilted bound; comparison
with the integral plus total variation proves the lattice bound for
y>=1, and g(log(n/y))<=C(y/n)^2 handles y<1. The same argument works
for every fixed Gaussian variance needed here.

For I_X in Theorem A and x in [X,2X], an integer outside I_X has
|log(n/x)|>=W_X-log2. Summing the product kernel therefore gives

    sum_(m or n outside I_X) K_X(m,n)=O_tau(X^-4).   (A12)

This follows from X^2 exp(-(W_X-log2)^2/(4tau))=X^-4. The cutoff is
X^(1+o(1)); for large X every n in I_X satisfies n<z^3, and its two-
prime core is <exp(W_X)/kappa^2<z. Hence the preceding factorization
is literal on every retained pair, not an asymptotic identification.

Consider the noncoprime part of R's squared norm. If m,n in I_X share
a rough prime p>z, their entire positive kernel mass is at most

    sum_(p>z) integral_X^(2X)
                 [sum_(a>=1)g(log(pa/x))]^2dx/x
       <=C_tau X^2 sum_(p>z)p^-2 <=C X^2/z.         (A13)

This includes all rough-prime coincidences and all original same-
integer diagonals. Overcounting simultaneous shared primes is harmless
only here, in the explicitly positive error bound.

If a retained pair is noncoprime but shares NO rough prime, any common
prime divides both small cores r,s. Indeed neither core can contain a
prime greater than z. Both cores are therefore >=2. The absolute
contribution of ALL such pairs is bounded by ||U||^2; enlarging to
every pair of completed r,s>=2 sources only increases this positive
bound. This argument uses the actual gcd, not a hereditary estimate
for a projected f_r field. It keeps primes 2 and 3 and every valuation.

Combining this with (A12)--(A13),

    |sum_((m,n)>1)f(m)f(n)A_R(m)A_R(n)K_X(m,n)|
                 <=||U||^2 + C X^(3/2)+O(X^-4).      (A14)

By (A9)--(A10), R>=V-U+O_A(X^-A)>0 on the shell. Consequently

    ||R||^2 >= integral (V-U)^2 dx/x +O_A(X^-A).

Subtract (A14) from this COMPLETE norm before taking a lower bound:

    C_1(R,R) >= integral(V^2-2VU)dx/x-C X^(3/2)
              >=(1/3)||V||^2-C X^(3/2).             (A15)

Every potentially negative r>=2 contribution was retained or bounded
by its full unsigned sum. In particular this is not a lower bound
obtained by simply selecting the r=s=1 positive family.

For the upper bound, the positive field of original rough integers is
at most V+U: every integer with at least two distinct rough primes is
counted at least once by the completed pair source. Thus the absolute
pair sum is <=||V+U||^2<=(16/9)||V||^2. Equation (A9) supplies the
stated size of ||V||^2. This proves A3 without any Mertens input.

The two losses in this proof are sharply different. X^(3/2) is an
UPPER bound for shared-rough-prime interactions, not their asserted
energy. The positive X^2/L^4 result in (A15) IS a lower bound for the
specified complete coprime rough-mask scalar. Neither is a lower bound
for the full f3 energy.
title: 3. Exact source and the actual gcd-one projection

## 4. A signed large-core tail, with its complete prime-pair sum

Let `R=floor(X^delta)`. For y>0, Abel summation and (C7) give

    |sum_(r>R) f(r)g(log(r/y))|
      <= C_beta y^beta Q_beta(log(R/y)),             ([restricted research revision])
    Q_beta(s)=exp(beta s)g(s)
                    +integral_s^infinity exp(beta v)|g'(v)|dv.

The boundary `-A_f(R)g(log(R/y))` is included in ([restricted research revision]). Q_beta is bounded
for s<=0 and decreases faster than any exponential as s tends to +infinity.
No roughness predicate has been attached to the core in this argument;
the exact extension ([restricted research revision]) is what makes the core coefficient f(r).

For Y>=1, elementary divisor counting gives

    sum_(k>=1) d(k) k^(-beta) Q_beta(log(k/Y))
          <= C_(beta,tau) Y^(1-beta)log(2Y).         ([restricted research revision])

Indeed `sum_(k<=T)d(k)<=T(1+log T)`. Partial summation treats k<=Y.
For k>Y, use dyadic intervals and a fixed exponentially decaying bound
on Q_beta; the resulting geometric series and its logarithmic factor
converge. This proves ([restricted research revision]) with no prime-distribution input.

Apply ([restricted research revision]) at y=x/(pq), sum all actual p<q, and bound their positive
majorant by all ordered positive integer factors k=pq. With Y=x/R>=1,
([restricted research revision]) proves the complete error

    |sum_(p<q,p,q>z) sum_(r>R) f(r)g(log(rpq/x))|
          <= C x R^(beta-1)log(2x/R)
          <= C X^(1-kappa)L.                        ([restricted research revision])

This prices the whole signed large-core tail, including all prime-pair
heights and the core endpoint. It is useful for the present asymptotic,
not itself a new Mertens exponent or the main new theorem.

### Every rectangular block is paid

This is the substantive completion of the growth adapter. Write I_j=[j,j+1).
Opposite translations send the I_i by I_j rectangle to the square
[(i+j)/2,(i+j)/2+1) in both coordinates, preserving t+u. Therefore the
unweighted block norm is at most K_a((i+j)/2+1). Passing to a heavier
weight sigma>a multiplies it by at most exp(-(sigma-a)(i+j)). If

    K_a(L) <= C exp(2 eta L),       eta>=0, all L>0,

the sum of the norms of all blocks is bounded by

    C exp(2 eta) [1-exp(-(sigma-a-eta))]^(-2),
    provided sigma>a+eta.                                  (G149.2)

The sum is a deliberately coarse sufficient bound for the full bilinear
form: each block input norm is bounded by the norm of its complete input.
It includes arbitrarily unbalanced rectangles, not only a diagonal strip.
Apply (G149.1) at the heavier weight, taking sigma<1 when needed. Thus for
one fixed 0<a<=gamma<1 the complete hypothesis

    K_a(L) <<_(chi,epsilon) exp(2(gamma-a+epsilon)L)
    for every epsilon>0 and all L>0                         (OPEN-HK)

for every fixed ordinary character excludes all L zeros in Re(s)>gamma.
For any desired sigma>gamma choose epsilon<sigma-gamma first. Values
above one are already in the absolute Euler-product domain; arbitrarily
small positive margins cover the boundary. Alternatively uniformly bounded
Hankel forms for a sequence a decreasing to gamma give the same return.

At a=1/2, the current first-gain threshold for the exponential growth
coefficient is strictly less than .7497080728. The candidate gamma=.87485
would require coefficient .7497 and return c=.12515, a gain .0000040364.
The 1/6 and 1/4 targets require coefficients 2/3 and 1/2. These are
conditional targets. The elementary |M(x)|<=x gives coefficient
2(1-a), namely one at a=1/2, and supplies no gain.

## G185. Primitive Poisson and the complete two-color sieve bound

On a squarefree merged column, the original coefficient is exactly

    F_sf,u=(-1)^j N0^(-1/2) sum_(n sf) mu(n)nu(n)chi_n(u)^e A(n),
    A(n)=sum_(original P|n) b(P)conjugate(nu(P))
                    sum_(d1 d2=n/P) W1(q_d1/D1;t1)W2(q_d2/D2;t2).

Slots retain their ordered labels. The sign is mu(d1)mu(d2)=(-1)^jmu(n);
the two inverse signs are not independent random variables. Since nu(P)
is a unit on the fixed good source, its conjugate is legitimate; no
natural row character value is divided out.

Expand the row indicator by sum_(a^6|u)mu(a), put u=a^6 z, and retain
(a,nn')=1. The row scale is U_a=U/q_a^6 with q_a<<U^(1/6). For actual
coprime squarefree n,n', psi=chi_n^e conjugate(chi_n'^e) is primitive
and nonprincipal at its full good conductor nn': its local exponents
are1 and5. Primitive Poisson therefore gives zero at ell=0 and at every
frequency sharing a good conductor prime. This does not remove a principal
original family. The normalized finite transform is

    sum_(x mod nn') psi(x)e(ell x/(nn'))
       =sqrt(q_n q_n') gamma(psi;nn') conjugate(psi(ell)).

The CRT factor chi_n(n')^e chi_n'(n)^(-e)=R(n,n') is the fixed ray sign
of PR9 B1.1-B1.5. It does not produce a variable cubic coupling across
copies. Set a0(n)=conjugate(alpha(n))gamma_2(n). PR9 B1.10 yields

    mu(n)gamma_1(n)=conjugate(a0(n))G(n),
    mu(n)gamma_-1(n)=a0(n)chi_n(-1)conjugate(G(n)).

Thus, apart from the retained nu(n)conjugate(nu(n')), the arithmetic
factors for e=-1 and e=1 respectively are

    R(n,n')chi_n(-1)conjugate(G(n))G(n')
         a0(n)conjugate(a0(n'))chi_n(ell)conjugate(chi_n'(ell));
    R(n,n')G(n)conjugate(G(n'))chi_n'(-1)
         conjugate(a0(n))a0(n')conjugate(chi_n(ell))chi_n'(ell).

Expand the fixed ray factors into the prescribed finite separated
dictionary. Fixed row restrictions modulo a disjoint S-supported modulus
retain primitive good-prime Fourier zeros by CRT. The dictionary may
depend on a's fixed residue class, with bounded cost. The first-dual cut
is on the actual fixed dual lattice; clearing a fixed denominator changes
its comparison constant and is not silently identified with the old cut.

The central pair coefficient and Poisson roots leave

    U/(q_a^6 N0^2),

with N0/sqrt(q_n q_n') retained in the smooth profile. Its radial kernel
keeps the exact argument U_a q_ell/(q_n q_n'), all original heights and
fixed factors. Before algebraic extension or an absolute Fourier integral,
pay the genuine far tail as proved in G186 below.

For fixed Y of at most a fixed polynomial size, define R_unique,<=Y by
the literal restriction0<q_ell<=Y in this exact expression. Pair
transposition with complete conjugation preserves that radial restriction;
the scalar can be kept real without assuming positivity.

Extend the displayed product expression and formal product conductor to
all individually squarefree n,n' in their original supports, then insert

    1_((n,n')=1)=sum_(f|n,f|n')mu(f).

The FULL identity kills every artificial noncoprime pair, including
inverse-slot and slot-slot intersections. No imprimitive Poisson theorem
is asserted on added pairs. Write n=fm,n'=fm'. Squarefreeness keeps
(f,m)=(f,m')=1 and

    a0(fm)=a0(f)a0(m)chi_m(f)^4,
    chi_f(ell)conjugate(chi_f(ell))=1_((f,ell)=1).

Each prime of f is allocated to its actual inverse color or original slot
on each side. The two allocations may differ. On one side f=f1 f2 fP,

    D1'=D1/q_f1, D2'=D2/q_f2, P'=P0/q_fP,
    X_f=D1'D2'P'=N0/q_f.

The other side has the same product X_f with independently shortened
color and slot lengths. Both allocation multiplicities together cost
tau(f)^C at fixed slot depth. Assigned slot coefficients and pool tests
remain present. Nonempty subunit nominal windows are clipped by bounded
original annular factors; truly empty windows stay empty.

Separate the full profile on the ambient original normalized norm box
BEFORE live labels, keeping its two real inverse roots once. On nominal
a- and ell-dyads A,H, the coupled kernel is

    K(C*y_ell/(y_a^6 product(y_original_columns))),
    C=UH/(A^6N0^2).

Its Euler derivatives are uniformly bounded for C>0 by fixed Schwartz
seminorms. PR9 B3.3 fixes the common Fourier measure first. Only then
substitute extracted factors; their imaginary powers have modulus one.
Sharp arithmetic masks and the dual cutoff stay outside the smooth
separation. Both original heights remain on their own profiles, with
the fixed finite-order H_J cost. This inherits, rather than resolves,
the open positive-slot uniformity ancestry.

For a fixed remaining slot tuple P, PR9 B1.11 gives

    a0(xyP)=a0(x)a0(y)a0(P)chi_y(x)^4 chi_x(P)^4 chi_y(P)^4.

All a,f,ell punctures, finite ray data and frequency twists separate
between x and y. Their coprimality is the natural cubic-symbol zero.
The two sieve variables are the original residual colors OF ONE COPY,
never a product mixing left and right columns.

The unconditional squarefree cubic large sieve, as stated in
[Dunn-Radziwill, equation1.11 and Theorem9.1](https://arxiv.org/html/2109.07463v3),
allows an arbitrary inner sequence independent of its outer variable,
with price D+E+(DE)^(2/3). Both variables are squarefree primary
Eisenstein elements. Cauchy and reciprocity/conjugation give

    |(DE)^(-1/2) sum_(x,y sf) alpha_x beta_y chi_y(x)^4|^2
       << H_J (DE)^epsilon [D+E+(DE)^(2/3)].

The two coefficient squared masses O(D),O(E) cancel the normalization.
Natural holes are zero coefficients or restrictions of the positive
outer sum. Ell is a fixed parameter here and need not be squarefree.
No arbitrary joint coefficient matrix or conductor-dependent loss is
admitted. No GRH refinement, optimality lower bound or cuspidal theorem
is imported into this noncuspidal source.

Triangle over the original surviving slots costs P' after squaring:
the normalized complete residual column B_f satisfies

    |B_f(ell)|^2 << H_J U^epsilon P'[D1'+D2'+(D1'D2')^(2/3)]
                << H_J U^epsilon P0[D1+D2+(D1D2)^(2/3)].

The other column has its own profile and allocation; use their geometric
mean. Restoring BOTH unnormalized roots contributes X_f, exactly

    [U/(q_a^6 N0^2)]sqrt(X_f X_f)=U/(q_a^6 N0 q_f).

The real profile ratio is X_f/sqrt(q_m q_m'), bounded on its actual
evaluation points, and produces no extra q_f power. All allocation
counts are paid before summing

    sum_a q_a^(-6)<<1,
    sum_(q_f<<N0)tau(f)^C/q_f<<_epsilon U^epsilon,
    #{ell:0<q_ell<=Y}<<Y.

The f-sum is harmonic up to small powers, not uniformly convergent.
Choose its divisor loss after the fixed scale cap. Restoring the complete
Fourier integral proves

    |R_unique,<=Y| << H_J U^(1+epsilon)Y/(D1D2)
                            [D1+D2+(D1D2)^(2/3)].       (G185)

The slot factor P0 cancels its denominator in N0 because it was paid.
This is a bound on a complete signed scalar sector after exact identities,
not on the absolute mass of its original pair expansion.
