A single-variable integer resultant does not apply to the literal source. Multivariable resultants need a quantitative diagonal restriction not present. Reject proposed first resultant bridge only. |
| S37 rare.03 | Source JN7 phase is an exact finite additive Fourier transform, and JN9 retains native Gauss characters/projectors. Coordinate transport represented by diagonal unit phases preserves the full L2/operator norm on nonzero support. Source-dependent cancellation would need an actual arithmetic defect estimate, not a gauge norm gain. Park as U-FLUX duplicate. |
| S48 rare.001 | The actual physical Gaussian Gram has an O(n^-2) adjacent-point innovation pivot. Exact block sums isolate uniformly cheap within-block differences and retain the full signed sum mode. Develop D48 as a source-adapted salvage; no unjustified Gram whitening. |
| S41 rare.001 | For shift D_p e_n=e_(pn), cutoff C_Y e_n=1_(n<=Y)e_n, [C_Y,D_p]e_n=-1_(Y/p<n<=Y)e_(pn). Trace0 does not mean quadratic form0: at p=2,Y=2,v=e1+e2+e4, v*[C_Y,D_p]v=-1. Existing A22/matchedHigh prime migration already prices the actual masks. Retain exact failure, do not redevelop same mechanism. |
| S49 wildcard | A phase coboundary representation is possible only if its loop products equal1. JN9 is not simplified by replacing native character/projector zeros with unit phases. Even a genuine coboundary is a unitary gauge and has identical norm. Existing U-FLUX/M41 ancestry; no source-specific nontrivial cocycle estimate produced. Park, not globally false. |

At most three substantive developments: D04, protected rare D48 and high-ceiling D02. S02 received its own complete attempted return before the easier representation module was selected. The other tests stopped at their decisive first calculation.

## D04. Smooth the literal Gaussian four diagonals with every collar paid

### Exact source and replacement

Use current-proof G11--G20, with tau=1,kappa=C=D=2,a=3/4 and Y=floor(X^.495). Keep each original bin I_i, its actual intersection with Y<d<=Dmax, all ordered pairs i+j=-2,-1,0,1, mu(d), the complete alternating ell source and eta(s)=(1-2^(1-s))zeta(s). Native interval endpoints/cap inclusions are not redefined. There are O(sqrt(log X)) ordered components. On every nonempty bin the endpoint sizes D_i obey

    X^(.495+o(1))<=D_i<=X^(.505+o(1)),
    D_i D_j=X^(1+o(1)) on every retained ordered pair.       (D04.1)

Here D_i is its actual upper endpoint; clipping changes these only by subpower factors. This follows from Y, Dmax=B_X/(Y+1) and each of the four bin diagonals. None is an SP smooth-state bin.

Fix0<delta<.495. For each exact interval choose a C-infinity function psi_i(v) with0<=psi_i<=1, supported within its real interval, equal to1 away from collars of lengths endpoint*X^-delta at both endpoints. For a very short clipped interval the collars may cover it completely; setting psi_i=0 is allowed. Then on the integers the difference from the original indicator is supported in the two collars, including every integer endpoint whose convention differs. There is no missing endpoint atom. The collar contains O(D_i X^-delta+1) integers; its n-values are D_i X^o(1). Such functions exist from a fixed C-infinity step with derivatives vanishing at its endpoints. Their k-th log derivatives cost O_k(X^(k delta)); derivative constants are NOT free subpower costs.

Define finite literal polynomials

    U_i(s)=sum_(d in I_i)mu(d)d^-s,
    V_i(s)=sum_(d>=1)mu(d)psi_i(d)d^-s,
    Delta_i=U_i-V_i.

The new source is a deliberately changed mask. Its differences remain explicit. For the accepted buffered rational Mertens bound M(t)=O(t^beta), take the conservative beta=8749/10000. At a=3/4, Abel summation at both original endpoints gives

    |U_i(a+it)| << (1+|t|)D_i^(beta-a),
    |Delta_i(a+it)| << X^(-delta+o(1))D_i^(1-a).           (D04.2)

The second inequality uses only |mu|<=1 and the full collar count. Because delta<.495, D_iX^-delta tends to infinity and absorbs the+1 endpoints. It makes no assumption of Möbius short-interval cancellation. The empty/clipped-bin case is included.

Put

    Zpsi_X(x)=(2pi)^-1 integral_[-T,T]
      exp((a+it)^2/2)eta(a+it)
         sum_(i+j=-2,...,1)V_i(a+it)V_j(a+it)x^(a+it)dt,
    T=2sqrt(log X).

This retains all ordered interactions and both independent height variables when its square is expanded. It does not introduce H projectors or claim anything about the distinct H form. No ell-dependent source mask has been smuggled into G8/G9.

### Complete norm error

The exact signed product difference is

    U_iU_j-V_iV_j=Delta_i U_j+U_i Delta_j-Delta_i Delta_j. (D04.3)

Use |eta(a+it)|<=|a+it|/a, the fixed Gaussian exp(-t^2/2) and Plancherel of the inverse Mellin transform with the difference restricted to[-T,T]. It is valid for arbitrary L2 Fourier data; there is no truncation error in this step. The shell factor costs at most(2X)^a. Equations D04.1--2 therefore give

    ||Z_X-Zpsi_X||_[X,2X]
       << X^(q_smooth+o(1)),
    q_smooth=max(101/200+(99/200)beta-delta,1-2delta).   (D04.4)

For example X^a D_i^(1-a)D_j^(beta-a) equals
D_i D_j^beta X^o(1). The maximal allocation puts exponent.505
on the trivial collar factor and.495 on the beta factor; the reverse
single-boundary term has the same maximum. The double-boundary term
costs X^(1-2delta+o(1)). The component count and all Gaussian height
polynomials are subpower. This prices EVERY replaced endpoint and
their ordered mixed interactions, rather than dropping a boundary square.

Current G20 pays ||G-Z_X|| at exponent-1+epsilon. Thus

    ||G-Zpsi_X||_[X,2X] << X^(q_smooth+epsilon)+X^(-1+epsilon). (D04.5)

For any fixed gamma>.5 and q_smooth<gamma, the every-epsilon norm target
||Zpsi_X||<<X^(gamma+epsilon) is equivalent to the original complete
Gaussian shell norm target. Choose epsilon smaller than the fixed
margin to use the triangle inequality in both directions. No global
Mellin transform of the moving psi family is asserted: D04.5 returns
to the fixed G BEFORE zero exclusion.

All choices are fixed once per target, with constants depending on
them. Exact conservative budgets using beta=.8749:

| gamma | Conditional c | delta | first collar exponent | double collar exponent | gamma-q_smooth |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| .8748 | .1252 | .064 | .8740755 | .872 | .0007245 |
| .87449 | .12551 | .064 | .8740755 | .872 | .0004145 |
| 5/6 | 1/6 | .106 | .8320755 | .788 | .001257833333... |
| 3/4 | 1/4 | .19 | .7480755 | .62 | .0019245 |

These are PAID COMPLEMENT budgets, not achieved moments. OPEN-SMOOTH
is the complete signed norm of Zpsi_X at its row's gamma for every
epsilon and all sufficiently large dyadic X. It is still open. The
original Gaussian pole-exclusion return is G1--G3 after D04.5.
No fixed-character or Hecke completion is deduced from a zeta-only
alternating source: those need their exact existing adapters.

Strongest objection: endpoint smoothing is often paid back by derivatives.
Here the collars are paid without derivatives; an ensuing analytic proof
of OPEN-SMOOTH must STILL debit X^(k delta) for k-th cutoff derivatives.
Even this smooth source has |V_i|<=|U_i|+|Delta_i| and only reproduces
the baseline moment exponent absent new signed arithmetic cancellation.
It is not a power gain generated by smoothness. Near gamma=.87449,
any proposed integration-by-parts saving must outweigh its.064-per-
derivative loss and establish the full two-height/component norm.

Ancestry: U-SCALE, old thin-annulus TA and native sharp-mask/Sobolev
adapters, plus W35's literal Gaussian completion. TA concerns a different
capped three-Möbius source and is not imported as this estimate. [restricted research revision]
hybrid smoothing changes fixed kernels and is not the same moving
endpoint collar. The narrow claimed delta is this explicit literal
four-diagonal replacement and complete numerical complement price;
no literature novelty claim or new cancellation mechanism.

Functional signature: actual G11 interval factors / interior endpoint
tapers / retain signed four-diagonal sum / unpaid OPEN-SMOOTH / fixed-G
return with q_smooth and all height/TypeI/product complements paid.
Next action: seek a genuine two-height mean for these smooth factors
whose derivative cost fits the fixed margin, or stop if it cannot beat
the original sharp mean. Re-proving the collar bound is not arithmetic progress.

## D48. Native Gaussian innovation, then a paid all-block replacement

### The actual close-point Gram and its normalization

For n in[X,2X], set s=log(n/X), epsilon=log(1+1/n),
v_s(u)=g_tau(s-u) on0<=u<=log2. The literal physical Gram G22 is
<v_s,v_t>; every coefficient is the actual f3(n), including all powers.
The Schur pivot of v_(s+epsilon) against v_s is

    p_s(epsilon)=||v_(s+epsilon)||^2
           -|<v_s,v_(s+epsilon)>|^2/||v_s||^2
      =epsilon^2 [||v_s'||^2
           -|<v_s,v_s'>|^2/||v_s||^2]+O_tau(epsilon^3).  (D48.1)

Taylor expansion is uniform on the compact s-range, and
v_s'/v_s=-(s-u)/tau is nonconstant on a positive-length interval.
The bracket is ||v_s||^2 Var_(v_s^2)(u)/tau^2>0,
continuous with a positive compact minimum. Hence p_s~n^-2
uniformly. The Gram's largest eigenvalue is bounded above/below,
so its condition number is comparable to n^2. This is a native
kernel statement, not a f3 energy lower bound. Whitening the Gram
can amplify a unit coefficient error by order n.

The source-adapted alternative keeps the cheap difference mode
explicit and never inverts the Gram. This changes S48's original
orthogonal-prime-word proposal after source intake; the seed remains
unaltered and the salvage is attributed to this development.

### A whole-field replacement with every difference and tail paid

Let a(n) be ANY fixed complex sequence with |a(n)|<=1. Later take
a(n)=f3(n), or f3(n)chi(n) with its actual zero extension. For an
integer B>=1 define right-closed blocks ((j-1)B,jB], j>=1,

    b_B(j)=sum_((j-1)B<n<=jB)a(n),
    V_B(x)=sum_(j>=1)b_B(j)g_tau(log(jB/x)),
    F_a(x)=sum_(n>=1)a(n)g_tau(log(n/x)).

All these infinite sums converge absolutely on compact x-ranges
by the Gaussian majorant; b_B(j) has modulus at most B. Put
k_x(t)=g_tau(log(t/x)), t>0. Its total variation on(0,infinity)
is exactly2g_tau(0). On one block,

    sum_(n in block)|k_x(n)-k_x(jB)|
       <= B integral_((j-1)B)^(jB)|k_x'(t)|dt.

Indeed every segment[n,jB] lies in the block and at most B
integer segments cover a point. At t=0 the Gaussian is flat and
has limit0, so the first block has no omitted endpoint. Summing
ALL blocks yields the uniform, coefficient-preserving bound

    |F_a(x)-V_B(x)|<=2B g_tau(0), x>0.                 (D48.2)

This prices every within-block signed detail, including the infinite
high-n tail, with no exceptional or unmatched class deleted. It is
not an estimate of a positive submask. Squaring afterwards retains
all ordered block interactions; norm triangle has paid both mixed
terms and the difference square at the field level.

For every parent dyadic X fix B_X=floor(X^theta),0<=theta<gamma,
and use that same B_X for ALL x in[X,2X]. D48.2 implies the exact
every-epsilon equivalence

    ||F_a||_[X,2X]<<X^(gamma+epsilon)
      iff ||V_(B_X)||_[X,2X]<<X^(gamma+epsilon).         (D48.3)

Use a smaller epsilon than gamma-theta. No Mellin continuation of
the MOVING block source is inferred; the fixed source is recovered
by D48.2 first. All n and their signs/zeros occur once in b_B.

For actual f3, B=2 makes the arithmetic coefficient explicit:

    b_2(j)=f3(2j-1)+(1-2*1_(2 not dividing j))f3(j).    (D48.4)

This preserves f3's valuation rule: multiplying by2 flips its sign
only if2 was absent. Thus even the pair source is not an independent
random-sign source or a squarefree source. With a fixed chi,
b_2(j)=f3(2j-1)chi(2j-1)+f3(2j)chi(2j); all ramified zeros remain.

There is also a direct fixed-B pole-preserving transform. Write
e_B(n)=B ceil(n/B) and initially on Re s>1 let

    D_B(s)=sum_(j>=1)b_B(j)(jB)^-s,
    E_B(s)=sum_(n>=1)a(n)[n^-s-e_B(n)^-s].             (D48.6)

Since0<=e_B(n)-n<B, the integral of the derivative of t^-s gives
|n^-s-e_B(n)^-s|<=|s|B n^(-Re s-1). Thus E_B converges absolutely
and locally normally on Re s>0, including fixed s-derivatives
(their extra log powers are summable). Coefficient rearrangement
on Re s>1 gives D_B=D_a-E_B. For fixed ordinary chi this becomes

    L(s,chi)D_B(s)=W_chi(s)-L(s,chi)E_B(s).           (D48.7)

If the fixed-B Gaussian block field has a complete moment exponent
gamma>.5, its Mellin transform continues D_B to Re s>gamma.
At a hypothetical L-zero rho there, D48.7's left side and its
second right term vanish, while W_chi(rho) does not. This proves
the direct fixed-B zero return; additive holomorphic error, rather
than an Euler-product guess, preserves the reciprocal poles. At
B=2 the source uses exactly b_2 from D48.4. Moving B_X still uses
D48.2--3 before continuation, so no changing transform is invented.

The pair difference sector alone is O_tau(1). Its complete signed
sum mode b_2 remains the entire arithmetic problem. Large B reduces
the number of block coordinates in a paid finite Gaussian window
to X^(1-theta+o(1)), but b_B(j) can be as large as B. No complexity
or amplitude reduction is asserted from coordinate count alone.

### Ordinary-character zero return and concrete high ceilings

For a(n)=f3(n)chi(n), current [restricted research revision]/W41 A13 gives initially on Re s>1

    sum_n a(n)n^-s=W_chi(s)/L(s,chi),
    W_chi(s)=(1-2chi(2)2^-s)
      /[(1-chi(2)2^-s)^2(1-chi(3)3^-s)^2]
      *product_(p>=5)(1-2chi(p)p^-s)/(1-chi(p)p^-s)^2.   (D48.5)

At ramified primes chi(p)=0 the factor is exactly1. The infinite
product and inverse converge normally for Re s>.5, since their
nonconstant terms start at p^-2s and2p^-sigma<1 at p>=5,sigma>.5.
Denominators have zeros only at Re s=0; prime2 numerator zeros
are on Re s=1. Hence W_chi is nonzero and holomorphic in.5<Re s<1.
Gaussian Mellin transformation gives exp(tau s^2/2)W_chi/L.
D48.3 plus dyadic Cauchy--Schwarz continues that FIXED transform to
Re s>gamma. Multiplication by L and the identity theorem exclude
zeros gamma<Re s<1. The principal pole is excluded; usual right-edge
facts complete zero exclusion. Constants depend on each fixed chi;
no growing conductor/angular assertion or new Eisenstein adapter.

Thus the weakest complete hypothesis used here is a full signed
block-field shell norm for ALL large dyadic X, with its frozen parent
B_X and every epsilon. Examples:

| gamma | Conditional c | theta | norm error | margin gamma-theta |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| .8748 | .1252 | .8 | X^.8 | .0748 |
| 5/6 | 1/6 | .8 | X^.8 | 1/30 |
| 3/4 | 1/4 | .7 | X^.7 | .05 |

NONE of these block moments is proved. A sufficient but stronger
pointwise estimate |b_(B_X)(j)|<=B_X X^(-(1-gamma)-eta)
through the relevant Gaussian window would give a power gain after
paying Gaussian tails; it is not available and is more than D48.3
requires. A baseline bound on block sums of size X^beta yields only
the positive aggregate exponent1+beta-theta, which is worse than
beta when theta<1. No arithmetic debt is hidden by compression.

Ancestry: actual-source transport W03/SBG, matchedHigh A05,
matchedMax log-transport, native finite observations and physical
readout warning [restricted research revision]/W41. The proof is elementary variation/Abel
summation, not a new functional-analysis theorem. The narrow new
record claim is the all-block, entire actual f3/zero-extended-character
replacement with UNIFORM O(B) error, explicit pair coefficient and
own complete zero return. Search may find an earlier identical
source specialization; if so merge provenance, not count another result.

Functional signature: full fixed f3*chi field / exact consecutive
block masses and endpoint readout / cheap within-block innovations /
unpaid complete signed block moment / O(X^theta) return to the fixed
field before Mellin zero exclusion. Next action: test an arithmetic
identity for b_2 or b_B retaining the sum mode. Generic whitening or
separate positive block bounds cannot supply it.

## D02. Rank-one determinant detector: an exact attempted bridge that fails to weaken the input

Take a finite actual Gaussian coefficient list, either capped G13
with its prescribed error G20 or the full f3 coefficients truncated
only AFTER paying the absolute Gaussian tail. Let M be its native
physical Gram, c the COMPLETE signed coefficient column (complex
twists use conjugate transpose). The original energy is E=c*Mc.
M is positive definite for distinct n: a finite linear combination
of Gaussian translates vanishing on a real interval is an entire
combination vanishing identically, and its distinct exponential
frequencies are linearly independent by the Vandermonde derivative
matrix. Thus its determinant is positive; it may be ill conditioned.

The naive rank-one detector has, for lambda>=0,

    det(M+lambda cc*)/det(M)=1+lambda c*M^-1c.          (D02.1)

It measures the DUAL source norm, not E. D48.1's actual consecutive
columns show an inverse-Gram cost of order X^2 on the cheap innovation
direction; its primal-to-dual ratio is order X^4. In general M=diag(epsilon,1),
c=(1,0) gives E=epsilon but c*M^-1c=1/epsilon.
This is an exact normalization failure, not an H counterexample.

To preserve the original scalar one must instead take v=Mc:

    det(M+lambda vv*)/det(M)=1+lambda c*Mc.             (D02.2)

Proof: det(M+lambda vv*)=det(M)det(I+lambda M^-1v v*),
and the last determinant is1+lambda v*M^-1v. With v=Mc
this is E. Every signed coefficient and every cross term is now
inside v, so no local determinant algebra pays the arithmetic.

For an infinite field the same construction is the finite-rank
operator I+lambda |F><F| on its shell Hilbert space, whose only
nontrivial eigenvalue is1+lambda||F||^2. Its determinant is therefore
the SAME complete moment. It is not an independently cheap detector.

Complete conditional return, with all finite leakage, fixing lambda=1:
choose physical truncation n<=2X exp(C sqrt(log X)) after exact f3
coefficients, C large fixed, so the Gaussian absolute tail is
X^(1-C^2/(2tau)+o(1)). For finite G13 use its existing G20 bound
instead, not the f3 coefficient list. Choose C so tail exponent is
strictly below desired gamma; norm triangle returns to the respective
fixed source. A bound for the corrected determinant ratio minus1
by X^(2gamma+epsilon) is then equivalent to that complete finite
source energy. For f3 the fixed convolution and D48.5 give ordinary-
character zero exclusion at gamma>.5. The prospective near gamma
.8748,5/6,3/4 each has room for C, but the determinant estimate is
literally OPEN-F3 in new notation. No weaker necessary input found.

Strongest objection resolved: M may become nearly singular. D02.2
is algebraically correct without a condition-number hypothesis but
requires the exact Mc. Approximating Mc incurs inverse amplification
and must be source-readout priced. A small det(M) is not a certificate
of a small source energy; arbitrary matrix rank compression loses
the vector that matters.

Ancestry: U-DETERMINANT, F08/F26 resolvents, W38 actual-law determinant
failure, [restricted research revision] reciprocal Hankel face-energy equivalence, and [restricted research revision] native
spectral core. This is a useful scoped failure/test, not an asserted
new determinant architecture or independent research gain. Next action
would need an actual signed determinant estimate that exploits Mc
more effectively than the Gram; none is supplied. Stop the naive
cc* proposal rather than launch another generic determinant calculation.

## Source coverage, quantitative limits and handoff

After seed freeze the author consulted the complete current-proof and
attempt-index navigation, [private research revision]/W41 source and the collective original/
late index mechanism entries, plus relevant exact source slices: G11--G32,
G31--G40, W41 A4--A13, JN1--JN9, matchedHigh A22/D2, TA, SBG and [restricted research revision]
hybrid smoothing. Small source searches are evidence of inspected ancestry,
not exhaustive literature novelty. The full29-family/109-child portfolio
is retained. No card is declared globally impossible because of an old
scoped failure. Root/critics own complete deduplication and admission.

D04 and D48 do not lower the .249728 Gaussian benchmark or the separate
full-H.004 deficit. They pay representation complements and move the
unchanged hard estimate to explicit smooth/bin or block-source objects.
No combined savings are added. D02 demonstrates why the proposed
determinant does not provide a new return with weaker arithmetic input.

Completed necessary exact checks verify selection-pool completeness, rational
collar budgets, source f3 pair coefficients, block identity on finite
lists and primal/dual determinant identities. They verify algebra and
budget arithmetic, NOT the unproved all-height moments. No external
claim requiring a primary-source citation is used in the proofs.

# Partial marked-plain density and the retained first-support reserve

Status: NEW, UNREVIEWED, source-relative mathematical development. The controller's accepted calibration is now c8=12514261/100000000=.12514261 (12 October 2026). The earlier frozen [restricted research revision] and [restricted research revision] files are unchanged. This report derives a stronger restricted weighted-density input from the literal old marked PLAIN theorem; it also retains a separate, previously discarded support term. A complete exact arithmetic return for their combined use gives the candidate

    c=500579/4000000=.12514475, theta=3499421/4000000=.87485525.

That candidate is not accepted by this report. Moreover, the endpoint can use the retained support term with the already accepted [restricted research revision] density, as explained below; its entire gain must not be credited to the new marked-plain lemma. The lemma is a strictly stronger analytic input in its own right. No proof assistant, formal code, kernel, provider, external model or child agent was used. The same imported F0/analytic ancestry, positive-slot uniformity and exact comparison-root-definition obligations remain outside this report's closure boundary.

Credit remains with OpenAI, Hailey Collet, Akash Levy and Zhongpai Gao with AI assistance as recorded in the source. PR9 is pinned at 58344dfdbe756cf2f743da1908ffe0582418cf5b and PR15 at ca182b70ac2aee2d053d679b4ddf1233883f9eef. The PR15 fragments are dated 11 October 2026. The forward map's 12 October 03:08:26 timestamp is a receipt, not a theorem date. Novelty here means a new argument in the inspected project record, not a literature-priority claim.

## 1. Literal input and the marked-plain eligibility bridge

Read PR9 paper B0.3--5, B0.7--9, B0.17--20 and B3.31--47; the decisive PLAIN contract is B3.40, lines 2177--2214. It permits two independent smooth plain profiles and independent heights, with the *same* canonical prime pool, one common slot profile, and individual relative ray characters. With kappa=3/4 its positive assertion is

    n1+n2+(9/2)z <= W
      => sum_eligible |S(Z^n1)S(Z^n2) Q|^2 << Z^(W+eps) H_J.       (MP)

Here W is row width plus presented moving-character width before cancellation, with an arbitrarily small separately charged padding for fixed conductor constants. The kept rows are the source's literal FixedInducingRow exclusion. Arbitrary prime subsets and arbitrary bounded coefficients are NOT included in MP. Those permissions belong to the marked INVERSE theorem and cannot be transferred to MP. The zero-slot assertion permits all nonprincipal inducing characters and unrestricted bounded plain lengths. The accepted incumbent beta_*<=7/8 licenses kappa=3/4; the present zero hypothesis, Re zero >=(1+delta)/2 with delta>=.68, licenses beta_*>=.51. No improved moment on a descendant is used.

The zero detector may choose a different fixed dictionary label from the slot parent. The following re-anchoring is therefore necessary, rather than an implicit arbitrary-coefficient extension.

Fix ONE parent translate from PR15 FixedDictionaryBridge, not a union of unrelated translates. Let its base character be tau0, its original anchor eta0, fixed ray modulus M0 and subgroup H, and original ray-quotient characters theta_i. The literal ideal is

    Q*=internalQ(M0 intersect (72),eta0)
      =M0 intersect (72) intersect q_eta0.

Thus Q* is contained in M0, (72), and q_eta0 in the ideal convention of the source. The original relative coefficient is nu_i=chi_theta_i eta0^(-1). Every possible witnessing label in this translate has, on Q*-units, the form tau0 kappa0 for a fixed Q*-ray character kappa0. The finite list and these representations are chosen before rows and scale.

Use the SAME primitive labels with their Q*-punctured presentations when running the supported-witness construction. This adds no primitive character and no label to the zero maximum: the extra finite Euler factors have no zeros in Re s>0. The natural-character detector already permits these fixed redundant Euler holes (B0.17--20). The conductor multiplier is fixed and absorbed in the explicitly charged fixed-width padding. Crucially, this is a choice made before witnesses, not a row-dependent change of character after seeing a large plain sum.

For the label tau_lambda=tau0 kappa0 set

    eta0'=eta0 kappa0,       nu_i'=chi_theta_i (eta0')^(-1).

Keep M0, H, EVERY theta_i, scale, profile, height and canonical pool unchanged. The pool is defined by the ray class modulo (M0,H), the fixed good-prime conditions and its scale cutoff, not by the anchor. This is also visible in the original profile-transfer-check.md pool definition, lines 17--105. On primes outside Q*, multiplicativity gives literally

    (tau_lambda psi_u)(p) nu_i'(p)
        =(tau0 psi_u)(p) nu_i(p).                         (1)

There is no division by a possibly zero value in this argument. At primes dividing Q*, the ORIGINAL coefficient vanishes: a prime dividing M0 is absent from the canonical good pool; a prime above 2 or 3 has the original m0 bad-prime zero; and a prime dividing q_eta0 has nu_i(p)=0. These exhaust the prime support of Q*. The new Q*-presentations vanish there too. At any other original hole (row radical, canceled moving factor, or common puncture) the same natural zero remains on both sides. Thus (1) is equality of actual prime polynomials, including zero coefficients, not merely equality of primitive characters away from their conductors.

Present kappa0 modulo Q*, retaining all its nonunit zeros, and present eta0' on that modulus. Since Q* is contained in q_eta0, this product presentation has its prescribed fixed modulus dividing Q*. Apply MP with input ideal Qinput'=Q*. Then

    internalQ(Qinput',eta0')=Q*.

The nonzero, proper, (72)-containment and original ray-modulus gates are unchanged. The source whole-row character is now tau_lambda psi_u; its fixed factor is separate from the anchor. No moving child character has been inserted into the anchor. The original ray quotient has not been enlarged and no Fourier character expansion has been used. PR15 FE1 removes a fixed mask from the inducing predicate; FE2 transports that predicate by a fixed Q*-character using an inverse plus its modulus mask, not cancellation at zeros. Consequently the original eligible rows are exactly the needed eligible rows for this MP application. The FI ideal stays Q*.

This proves the anchor bridge for the original finite parent translate. If the whole rectangle is conjugated, conjugate every fixed and live factor and reflect every relevant height. The conjugate ray characters remain characters of the SAME quotient, and the common profile is wholly conjugated. This does not replace conjugate(tau psi_u) by conjugate(tau) psi_u. Both signed orientations remain separate.

There is one further mismatch: the witness plain polynomial has its natural holes, while selected actual slots can have an extra fixed missing-radical puncture R. Write phi_u=tau_lambda psi_u for the COMPLETE witness row character. Do not apply MP with unequal common masks. Expand ONLY those extra slot punctures using the literal second identity B3.41, with its prime-pool support displayed:

    Q_i,R=Q_i,0 - Z^(-z_i/2) sum_(p|R, p in P_i^can) phi_u(p)nu_i'(p)
                         W(Np/Z^z_i)(Np/Z^z_i)^(-sigma_i+iv_i).   (2)

Retain this identity, its minus signs and zero scalars before applying Minkowski to the positive norm. The frozen phi_u(p) factors then have modulus at most one and can be discarded as diagonal contractions. Each remaining live product is an ORIGINAL canonical slot subcollection with its same profile. Its affine length only decreases. The total frozen coefficient mass is Z^o(1), uniformly for polynomial NR, exactly as B3.41; its central factor is comparable to (Np)^(-1/2) on the annulus. If no slots remain, use the old unrestricted zero-slot theorem on the same nonprincipal rows. This proves MP for natural witness plains and the actually punctured marked slots without asserting a mismatched-mask theorem or changing prime coefficients. In the sixth-power lift below, the root and its added holes are fixed before the free-core sum, so the same proof applies.

## 2. Partial marking, rather than an unavailable full-length improvement

Fix a physical buffered bin delta in [17/25,7/10], one eligible parent translate and the actual slot product Q of total width z. The bin upper edge bounds every original subproduct by its physical price Z^(delta times its width+small) H_J. The lower edge supplies a zero for a fixed dictionary label. All heights and buffered internal zero maxima are handled as in accepted [restricted research revision]: choose the detector cutoff t BEFORE witnesses and retain it even if the larger internal height box has a larger zero maximum. Only weaken witness lower bounds to the physical delta. Do not use that internal maximum as a new upper slot bound.

Normalize free-row width W=1 and put v=z/W<=1/20. Supported witnesses satisfy, with a preallocated small tolerance,

    r<=t, r+m>=t, 0<=m<=1/2,
    |M(Z^r)|^2>=Z^(delta r), |P(Z^m)|^2>=Z^(delta m).      (3)

The old plain fourth moment times the pointwise slot price used 1-2delta m+delta v. Instead fix the witness dyad m and greedily choose an original slot subcollection of width x just below

    min(v,(1-2m)/(9/2)).

The gap is at most ONE fine-mesh slot width, not an error per slot. The subset depends only on frozen lengths and dyads, not the live row. Apply (MP) with n1=n2=m to that subcollection; pay the complementary actual slots by their physical bin bound; only then enlarge the remaining positive norm to the full eligible family. Division by the fourth-power witness gives

    Pnew(m)=1-2delta m+delta [v-(1-2m)/(9/2)]_+.           (4)

For m slightly above 1/2 use no marked slots and the old unmarked exponent max(1,2m), paying the witness tolerance once. The two slopes of (4) in m are -2delta and -2delta(1-2/9), both negative. Thus m>=t-r gives the same expression with m=t-r. All four derivative-profile pairs are covered by MP's two independent plain profiles and the same selected subset.

For comparison, a full marked-plain amplification is possible but worse here. The exact Euler restoration at a slot-disjoint amplifier prime is

    S_u(D)=sum_(j>=0) phi_u(p)^j (Np)^(-j/2)
                         S_(up^6)(D/(Np)^j).

It is finite on annular support, also valid when p|u (then the displayed scalar is zero for j>0). Restore both plain factors, average over the fixed prime pool, use injectivity (u,p)->up^6 on free cores, and take the existing two-scale Sobolev supremum. The geometric coefficient mass is bounded. MP at enlarged width H=max(W,2m+(9/2)z)+small gives

    E_PM(W,m,z)=W/6+(5/6)max(W,2m+(9/2)z).               (5)

This is not the marked inverse exponent. At delta=.70,v=.05 and the binding m=442/965, the full amplified counting exponent is 36771/77200, the old pointwise exponent is 15199/38600, and partial marking gives 2939/7720. Full amplification is worse than the old bound by 6373/77200. More generally, beyond the unamplified capacity, its derivative with respect to marked width is 5(9/2)/6-delta>0 after crediting pointwise removal. Therefore the optimum of THIS amplification/pointwise strategy marks exactly the largest fitting subcollection. This is a useful failed construction, not a universal impossibility result.

## 3. Every inverse-length regime and the sharper free-row statement

Retain the accepted [restricted research revision] marked inverse moment, with its exact Euler-restoration proof and arbitrary-coefficient permission:

    E_MI(W,r,z)=W/6+(5/6)max(W,r+2z,(2r+8z)/3).

Write rho=1-10delta/[3(5-2delta)] and k=rho+delta-1=delta(5-6delta)/[3(5-2delta)]. The three available weighted-count exponents are

    U(r)=max(1,(1+5r)/6)-delta r+delta v,
    A(r)=1/6+(5/6)max(1,r+2v,(2r+8v)/3)-delta r,
    P(r)=1-2delta(t-r)+delta[v-(1-2(t-r))/(9/2)]_+.       (6)

Put v0=2(5-6delta)/(135-78delta). Choose, before witnesses,

    v<=v0: t=(5-6delta v)/(5-2delta), rb=2t/3;
    v>=v0: t=(115-12delta-84delta v)/(115-54delta),
             rb=(14t+2-9v)/23
               =[80-12delta-(45+30delta)v]/(115-54delta). (7)

These choices agree at v0. Direct substitution gives 1<=t<=3/2 and rb<=R:=1-2v. The latter difference has positive numerator 5-6delta-(30-24delta)v in the first case, at least 7/50 throughout the larger rectangle, and 35-42delta-(185-138delta)v in the second, at least 59/50. Supported r>=t-1/2>=1/2>2v, so the third term in A's maximum never exceeds r+2v.

For r<=R, A=1-delta r decreases and P increases, with its continuous kink included. They cross at rb; the choice v<=v0 is exactly the condition that all available slots fit at that crossing. Thus min(A,P)<=E:=1-delta rb throughout this range. For R<=r<=1, the increasing A and decreasing U cross at r_c=1-(2-6delta/5)v with value

    C=1-delta+delta(3-6delta/5)v.

For r>=1, U increases because delta<5/6, and its maximum at r=t is L=1/6+(5/6-delta)t+delta v. The choices (7) give L=E. No long-inverse or transition regime has been omitted.

The resulting gain relative to rho W+delta z is

    G_delta(W,z)=min(3k z, a_delta W+b_delta z),
    a_delta=2delta(5-6delta)^2/[3(5-2delta)(115-54delta)],
    b_delta=14delta(5-6delta)/(115-54delta).              (8)

In particular G_delta(1,v)/v is minimized at v=1/20. Its ratio to k there is (410-324delta)/(115-54delta), whose derivative is -15120/(115-54delta)^2. Hence

    G_delta(W,z) >= eta_plus(delta) z,
    eta_plus(delta)=(458/193)k(delta).                   (9)

This strictly improves the accepted eta_old=2k. The middle inverse regime also fits this linear envelope: for T=rho+(delta-eta_plus)v,

    T-C=k(1-(458/193)v)-delta(2-6delta/5)v
       >= (7/135)(1-(458/193)/20)
          -(7/10)(2-(6/5)(17/25))/20
        =2569/603125>0.                                 (10)

Thus all regimes prove the sufficient linear free-row theorem

    sum_bin,free |Q_u|^2
      << Z^[rho(delta)W+(delta-eta_plus(delta))z+eps] H_J,
      0<=z<=W/20, delta in [.68,.70].                    (11)

The exact E envelope (8) can also be retained: E<=T, and C is below E as well. To see the latter without a new optimization, E>=rho+(delta-3k)v, and

    rho+(delta-3k)v-C
      =k(1-3v)-delta(2-6delta/5)v
      >=(7/135)(17/20)-(7/10)(2-(6/5)(17/25))/20
      =889/337500>0.

All boundary values, including v=0, follow continuously. Fixed dictionary factors, the dyad partition, greedy overshoot, conductor padding and witness buffers enter one preallocated epsilon. The fine mesh is fixed before the eventual family, slot list and heights. Moment/seminorm degrees precede the internal detector height exponent; the eventual scale threshold precedes all T. Above the internal polynomial height threshold, absolute ideal counting and |Q|^2<<Z^(z+small) are absorbed by the final polynomial H_J, exactly as in the accepted [restricted research revision] proof. Independent slot and plain heights have not been identified.

## 4. Raw sixth-power lifting with the original zeros

For raw width W require z<=W/21. Write w=u b^6 with free u and its original unit, fix b, and retain the added natural holes at every prime dividing b. Put s=log_Z Nb and V=W-6s. Positive-real primitive zeros are unchanged; Q_w is literally Q_u with these fixed additional holes. Section 1 and (2), not a loss of these holes, license the free estimate.

If V>=20W/21, z/V<=1/20. The linear theorem's root sum has exponent

    rho W+(delta-eta_plus)z-(6rho-1)s.

It converges since rho>=19/54. For the stronger (8), its loss under width reduction is at most a_delta(W-V); hence the root sum instead decays by [6(rho-a_delta)-1]s. Uniformly a_delta<1/500, for example by bounding its positive numerator at delta=.70 and 5-6delta at .68 and its denominator at .70. Thus this decay is also strict.

If V<20W/21, use the old unmarked free density plus the ORIGINAL physical slot bound for the natural character. The available root-tail saving is (rho-1/6)W/21. It pays even the stronger gain because

    G<=3kz, z<=W/21,
    rho-1/6>=5/27 > 3k(.68)=391/2275,
    5/27-391/2275=818/61425>0.

Bounded free-core windows and fixed-inducing free cores are bounded by the raw population Z^(W/6+delta z+small), when not already excluded by the original FI predicate; they are not called a finite raw population. The same strict gap pays them. This proves the raw version of (11) and (8), with z<=W/21, uniformly for the fixed translate, fixed polynomial punctures, both whole orientations and all heights. No arbitrary mask varying with the free live row was admitted.

## 5. Retain Bc and transfer in the actual paired units

The physical ledger is PR15 PhysicalLocalAssembly LA.4 and LA.11--13, especially lines 137--152 and 295--364, and PR9 B3.65--69 for the COMPLETE second projector. Let c_s,d_s be first genuine support widths (unrelated to the zero-free constant), m=min(c_s,d_s), T=(c_s-d_s)_+. The actual signed enclosing row width remains

    W=M-R-T+Lc-6a, Lc<=5(R-R0), R<=m.

The actual child width remains M'=M-T-6a-omega-g2+t2 with its original enclosing correction. Neither width is silently substituted for the other. The source target includes

    Bc=(3c_s-5d_s-R)_+/6.

The first support line in LA.13 is

    E1=(1-rho)T-delta c_s-(1+rho)R-E-Bc+rho Lc+R0
       <=-a_s m-kT-E-Bc,
    a_s=delta-4rho+1.

Since Bc>=(T-m)_+/2, and 1/5<=rho<=2/5,

    a_s m+kT+(T-m)_+/2 >= h_s(m+T),
    h_s=(a_s+k)/2=delta-(3/2)rho.                      (12)

For T<=m the difference is (a_s-k)(m-T)/2=(2-5rho)(m-T)/2>=0. For T>=m it is (1-a_s+k)(T-m)/2=(5rho-1)(T-m)/2>=0. Thus E1<=-h_s c_s, with E and any surplus Bc still favorable. This uses the printed Bc; it is not an exceptional reserve. The scalar equality R=m,T=m,Lc=5R in this relaxation need not be physically attainable by prime valuations, so it is NOT asserted as a sharp arithmetic obstruction.

The second support line still obeys E2=g2-t2-(1+delta)b2<=-delta b2-t2. Apply the accepted literal [restricted research revision] transport of the weighted norm: keep both complete projectors, all signs, their zero extraction scalars, missing first radical and actual surviving slot lists. The first projector and genuine common labels reconstruct divisor-many from the actual signed row. The second projector is NOT a divisor of that row; freeze and allocate it with both original scalars before applying positivity. Its dyadic count is paid as in B3.69.

Let zbar=(z1+z2)/2 and rbar=(r_clip,1+r_clip,2)/2. Cauchy on the two actual live slot products with (11) replaces rho W+delta zbar by rho W+(delta-eta_plus)zbar in the SAME paired exponent. The original clipped plain lengths separately save delta rbar. Neither term spends the extraction scalars again. The accepted frozen-slot inequality remains

    zbar>=z-c_s-b2-rbar-small.

Put s0=c_s+b2+rbar. Since h_s<delta, the old support and projector terms save at least h_s s0. If s0>=z this already saves h_s z, with no density-width hypothesis. If s0<z, then W>=M-c_s-6a>=M-z-6a. Under the same tested gate M-6a>22z, each z_j<=z<W/21 is eligible, and combined saving is at least

    h_s s0+eta_plus(z-s0)-small
       >=min(h_s,eta_plus)z-small.                     (13)

h_s increases on [.68,.70], with derivative 1+25/(5-2delta)^2; eta_plus decreases there. Their endpoint bounds are

    h_s(.68)=519/4550,
    eta_plus(.70)=3206/26055 > 519/4550.

Therefore every configuration has uniform paired gain g0 z, g0=519/4550. DENSITY eta_plus is not itself the final paired gain. Although (8) is stronger pointwise, G is concave in z; replacing [G(W,z1)+G(W,z2)]/2 by G(W,zbar) would have the wrong inequality direction. We use the safe linear corollary.

All original C,D conventions remain: corrected +xi_r(ab), old D.10 C coefficient tau(a)chi_a(er)xi_r(a), both 1+t_p and 1-t_p active residues, canceled-residue holes, whole rectangle, independent heights, original prime average and original normalization scalars. The exceptional M/24 reserve is used nowhere; it remains restricted to its centered equal-product, L=M/4, independently established joint opposite-side target. The far delta>=.70 branch keeps its old costs.

The endpoint below does not isolate the new density lemma's contribution. With old eta=2k, (13) instead gives g_old(delta)=min(h_s,2k). At q=.68, 2k>h_s, so g_old(q)=g0. Both functions have derivative at least -139/243 on this interval (h_s'>0 and 2k'>=-139/243). Thus g_old(delta)>=g0-(139/243)(delta-q), including the minimum's corner. The high ledger's derivative reserve below exceeds (139/243)/25. Consequently the SAME local plane and endpoint already follow from retained Bc plus the accepted [restricted research revision] density, independently of Sections 1--4. Root independently supplied this same derivative check during development. This simpler complete source-relative consequence should be reviewed first; (11) separately gives the stronger density statement and a constant-gain proof.

## 6. One complete affine atlas and physical return

Use q=17/25, Ka=34/21, D=q+(5-6rho(q))Ka=81379/15925,

    B0=14200/14361, B=B0-3/500000=7099956917/7180500000,
    Lambda=19312/4787-g0/D=652975/162758.

Keep all 600 cells b_j=.034+j/100000, cell=1/100000, alpha=1/400000 and fix

    g_j=B-1+(9/2-Lambda)b_j,
    a_j/M=Ka g_j+alpha,
    A_j=B-(Lambda-1)b_(j-1).

The low reserve is unchanged, 7/30000000. The high reserve at q is

    1-rho(q)-qA_j-(5-6rho(q))a_j/M+g0 b_(j-1).

Its cell slope vanishes exactly. Its positive minimum is 335173651/152465950000000. The width reserve 1-6a_max/M-22/25 is 3950951383/100527000000>0. The derivative of the old high expression on [.68,.70] is at least 168582048655829/624348065250000, greater than 139/6075; this covers both the constant gain from (11) and the varying old gain discussed above. The old high margin at .70 is 673102219571/461418930000000>0, with its unchanged monotonicity up to .75. Buffered endpoints fit the preallocated aggregate loss.

Every other atlas expression is affine in b_j; both end cells certify all 600. The helper checks the original first/sixth/seventh extracted errors, second zero, original main/error fixed-inducing branches (4a/9a), amplifier size and width. No extracted error is amplified a second time. All original projector and comparison factors, 6a radius growth, omega, global error-slot price 3/4 and deletion rate 1/6 are retained. The narrowest source loss is allocated before choosing fine meshes and eventual thresholds, not after a live family is seen.

The rational physical geometry is

    h=159079/200000=.795395,
    ell=4c-1/3=501737/3000000,
    x=1+ell-h=34861/93750, y=h-2ell=1382711/3000000,
    kappa_*=2theta-1=1499421/2000000.

Keep d0=1/200,t0=1/1000,d_-=h-1/1000,d_+=h+10^-12, plain cutoff N=264/625 and slot cutoff safez=93/2500. The actual Euler b maximum is below 803/5000=.1606; this sharper enclosure is needed for the new Lambda. The old .161 enclosure failed the large-shift reserve although the actual b did not. The exact short-plain margin remains 1/5000, short-slot margin 11/5000, and large-shift reserve is 14398933/5876775000000>0. The latter uses the unchanged piecewise function

    S_b(t)=t/2-[(b-(1-B))/Lambda-max(0,(b-2t)/(9/2))]/4

with slopes 7/18 and 1/2, including its kink and clipped capacity zero. Small shifts use the original tq/Lambda payment. All physical height, Euler damping and repeated-power deficits are unchanged.

Capacities are C_new(d)=[2y-(2-B)d]/Lambda and C_old(d)=min(d,2y-d)/(6kappa_*). On the entire ORIGINAL detector rectangle 0<=delta<=3/4,0<=p<=1/2 define

    Dp=3-p-2p/(3kappa_*), P=2(1-p)(1-p/(3kappa_*)),
    V=5/6-delta, J=V Dp+delta P, RJ=(1-delta)J+delta P V/2,
    F=J[theta-saving-(1+delta)/2-13h/75+y/2+ell/2-ell delta p
        -d(1/4-17/50)+delta p C_d/2]-(3d/4)RJ.

The ordinary Fraction helper reconstructs the same degree-(2,3) tensor Bernstein numerator as the frozen return, without project-code imports. Exact positive boxes: d=h,new capacity,saving10^-10:18 boxes/216 coefficients; d=d_-,old,saving10^-5:6/72; d=1/2,old,saving10^-3:1/12. Thus all 300 coefficients over 25 boxes are positive. Each box also has an exact independent interior interpolation identity; recursive bisection preserves the whole closed rectangle. This is finite arithmetic evidence, not an analytic proof by itself.

The positive rational ledger also checks supply, selected-slot/plain ranges, geometry, shortening, large Euler shifts, old/new junction, d-extension, floor, far-old, small-row, principal contour and feedback margins. The same affine/convex row-width and reciprocal-contour return then applies in the c8 scope. The probe identity (5x+y)/12=theta-(5/6-x/3-ell/6) is exact. The transformed high-bin delta is distinct from the original detector rectangle's delta.

Attempts retained: c=.125145,h=.7954 with coarse Euler b=.161 first failed the large-shift margin by -165363/652975000000. Using b<=.1606 repairs that enclosure, but a floating locator then found the unsaved endpoint negative for c=.125145 even at its best searched h. The floating edge was approximately c=.1251447553574981,h=.795395388501003,delta=.4657409558974571,p=.5. The displayed rational trial .12514475,h=.795395 was then checked exactly over the whole rectangle. Floats only located a trial and establish neither global optimality nor any source theorem. Further exact failed-trial data are retained in arithmetic.json.

## 7. Closure boundary and next action

The proposed new analytic statement is (11), and its raw z<=W/21 version, with exact common profiles, same ray pool, fixed parent translate, original natural holes, both orientations, all inverse-length regimes and uniform heights. The decisive new move is partial use of the actual marked PLAIN theorem, not importing the marked INVERSE permission. The support estimate (12) is independent of that lemma and yields a simpler route to the displayed endpoint via accepted [restricted research revision] density.

This report does not audit the full transitive analytic base anew. The source-relative imported F0/analytic ancestry, positive-slot uniformity and root-definition binding keep their prior status. It does not claim a public record. Independent review should prioritize Sections 5--6: Bc in the actual joint target, accepted-density transfer and the complete endpoint. Separately challenge the new marked-plain fixed-anchor/puncture bridge, witness quantifiers and continuous envelope. Root alone decides acceptance and integration.

Within this physical return ell=4c-1/3 and the retained ell<1/5 range already limits its stated applicability to c<2/15. More fundamentally ell<x<=y and x+y=1-ell force ell<1/3 and hence c<1/6 for this probe geometry. These are limitations of the current architecture, not universal barriers to c=1/6 or1/4. A larger ceiling needs a new physical return or geometry, not merely optimizing this density coefficient. The useful next analytic target is a joint witness or prime-valuation refinement that survives the same physical projection and changes those structural constraints.

## 6. Reviewer development: larger caps on large original a-dyads

The preceding proof permits a core cap depending on the NOMINAL ORIGINAL a-dyad A, provided it is fixed before live a and before the mutual-divisor expansion, and independent of f and every source column. This follows from the same Cauchy/profile argument: G186 already has a middle boundary depending on A. Use the following two caps instead:

    C_sq(A)=U^(13/40) A^(24/5),
    C_cu(A)=U^(3/4) A^(24/5).                          (V12)

Use the same priority order and the same fixed Delta convention, separately within each original dyad. Keep the whole original a partition and its signs. These are sectors of that exact a/frequency expansion; no signed subset of a positive row norm is substituted.

Substitution into the table changes SQ1's A exponent to -1+(24/5)/3=3/5, CU1's to -3+2(24/5)/3=1/5, and BOTH second-term A exponents to -4+(5/6)(24/5)=0. Sum the first terms up to A<<U^(1/6); this costs respectively U^(1/10), U^(1/30). The second terms incur only the number of dyads, absorbed into the already allowed arbitrarily small loss. Consequently the four full exponents are bounded by

    SQ1: 161/120+2tau/3 = 4027/3000,
    CU1: 143/300+tau/3 = 477/1000,

and the SAME two second exponents as in Section5. The first terms still have large slack against the coarse T floor; the limiting square second term keeps exactly the same positive reserve. This independently proves that (V12) preserves error O(H_J U^(T-1/200+epsilon)). The elementary exact check in check_adaptive.py verifies these new powers and reserves; it is not an analytic sieve test.

Near the largest permitted a-dyads, the paid square and cube core exponents can approach 9/8 and 31/20. At A=1 they are the author's original 13/40 and 3/4. The upper middle boundary remains H_A, and any cap exceeding an available frequency range simply leaves no hard frequencies there. All caps remain polynomially bounded, so the same uniformity and finite S-part accounting apply.

Let R_hard,adapt be EXACTLY the original middle restricted, within each original a-dyad, by

    q_kappa2>U^(13/40) A^(24/5)
    AND q_kappa3>U^(3/4) A^(24/5).

Then the reviewed argument and this refinement give

    ||F_<||_U^2=R_nonunique+R_hard,adapt
                        +O(H_J U^(T-1/200+epsilon)).  (V13)

This is a corollary of the source-specific SQ/CU method, not another independent arithmetic mechanism or an endpoint. It uses genuine retained A-decay; a mere shift of the already paid low norm boundary is not being counted as new cancellation.

A superficially similar cap depending on the ARTIFICIAL mutual label f is not licensed as a restriction of the original scalar. For a pair with common gcd p, the complete divisor sum is 1-1=0. A selector which retains only f=p leaves -1. Thus an f-dependent partition can destroy exactly the cancellation making the coprime extension valid. The A-dependent caps avoid this objection because A exists before that extension and is common to every f summand for a fixed pair/frequency.

## 3. Protected upstream development: the character cover is gauge trivial

The complete proof and quantitative return are in topology.md. The actual squarefree q-unit cutoff complex has one face S per n=product S<=X, including the empty face, and character insertion D_chi e_S=chi(n)e_S. Its graded trace is exactly M_chi(X). Ordinary deletion has commutator

    [D_chi,d]e_S=sum_(p in S)orientation*chi(n/p)(1-chi(p))e_(S minus p).

The proposed residue cover uses a regular register g in(Z/qZ)^* and deletion (S,g)->(S minus p,gp). Its total residue g*n is conserved. Relabeling each basis state by that conserved residue conjugates the cover to copies of the untwisted complex. In a character Fourier sector, the differential is D_chi^-1 d D_chi, while the chain dimensions and Euler index remain those of the principal character. At q=3,X=5, the index is-1 but the required M_chi value is3. This is an actual fixed-character counterexample to the proposed index/readout identification.

The strongest repair attempt was to recover the weighted homology trace and charge its defect. The least unramified prime ell gives an exact cone contraction and

    M_chi(X)=B(X)+(1-chi(ell))A(X/ell),
    A(Y)=sum_(n<=Y,ell not dividing n)mu(n)chi(n),
    B(X)=A(X)-A(X/ell).

The complete quantitative inverse is

    M_chi(X)=B(X)+(1-chi(ell))sum_(j>=1)B(X/ell^j),

with exponent-alpha cost1+|1-chi(ell)|/(ell^alpha-1). Thus a complete signed critical-face estimate at any common gamma>0 returns the full M estimate with the same exponent. The critical rank itself is

    kappa_(q ell)(1-1/ell)X+O_q(sqrt X),

proved directly by the cone and square-divisor count. That unsigned bill is linear. The character commutator, prime-toggle identity, cone basis and shell return have close or exact ancestry in W27/W53/W54/W55/W56 and are credited accordingly. The specifically tested additional repair is the regular residue cover and its explicit gauge obstruction. No new arithmetic saving is claimed.

The next useful topological action must change the actual chain groups or create a signed interaction across arithmetic states, then prove its full trace/commutator budget. Merely assigning prime phases to deletion or passing to this cover's Fourier components cannot do that. A different construction is not ruled out by this test.

## Novelty, calibration and useful next work

D12's differential-kernel mechanism is standard and already represented by [restricted research revision]-C1, whose literal Riesz polynomial uses rational A(n), a different source. D22's finite prime representation is already Pair02/W38; G81 also gives a complete mu*chi largest-prime renewal. G69 concerns the DIFFERENT all-power f3 finite-Euler Gaussian source and proves a global norm whose mass escapes physical shells. It is useful related ancestry, not the same mu*chi coefficient norm or a physical-shell lower bound. S01/S16 are elementary Euler inverse ancestry; S31/S26 duplicate G82; S51/S58 retain prime-complex ancestry. No literature priority search or novelty claim is made.

D43's countable scope, exact buffered sum and boundary law are useful new local recording of a standard recurrence mechanism. Credit the author for those, the Sol critic for its uniform high-height estimate and extended infinite moment, and this Astra review for explicitly closing actual-Gaussian bank formation and retaining the gamma=beta every-epsilon return. The latter also agrees with existing G47's beta<=gamma exception rule. These are conditional interface/obstruction improvements, not a fourth author development or an arithmetic-gap reduction.

| Prospective target | Complete B/U energy required | Conditional c |
|---|---|---|
| Common gamma<.87485525 | X^(2gamma+epsilon), limiting exponent below1.74971050 | c>.12514475 |
| gamma=.87485 | X^(1.74970+epsilon) | .12515 |
| gamma=5/6 | X^(5/3+epsilon) |1/6|
| gamma=3/4 | X^(3/2+epsilon) |1/4|

All are every-epsilon, every sufficiently large scale and every fixed ordinary chi. They are raw B/U energies, not a renamed normalized G24/local PR9 moment. D22 requires the corresponding complete signed sharp readout. D43 can use the same target with any fixed beta<=gamma, retaining all bank terms. The lossy pointwise sharp-B route would require beta<.74971050 for the first current gain, but D12 does not require that loss. No table row is proved by this batch.

The most useful next arithmetic task is a complete signed B estimate, or a source-compatible signed window/covariance estimate with all source and readout costs explicit. Merely adding fixed positive summable critical channels cannot create a uniform frame gap. Conversely that obstruction is no reason to discard an actual endpoint bank moment if one can prove it. D22 offers an exact high-ceiling representation but no demonstrated advantage over the existing Gaussian/window interfaces. S34/S41 and the other parked proposals remain hypotheses, with their complete defects and complements payable; these audits provide no evidence that their general mechanisms are impossible.

Controller handoff: integrate only these scoped accepted statements and explicit refinements, preserve all immutable source history/counts and critic credit, and retain every arithmetic/input obligation. Final artifacts are bounded, fully read back and hashed in the review freeze. After that freeze this task releases only its own exact claim, verifies absence, sends one final packet to root and stops. No other agent is woken.
