statement:
# [private research revision]: growing quadratic classes in the actual cubic moment

**Status: independently accepted relative to the stated inputs.**
Derived by c20_triple_cayley; independent reviewer: c20_continuum. This packet proves two uniform growing-class sectors of the actual C--C Poisson form, relative to the inputs identified below. It does not prove SR18 for the moving squarefree diagonal or improve the zero-free constant.

**Retained scope.** The new joint estimates, the full common-gcd projector, opposite cube masks, sharp core cutoffs and outside cube sum are all priced below. The sixth-power-free sector uses the inherited cube-free cubic sieve. The extension to every sixth-power repetition additionally uses the explicitly inherited all-finite-order Hecke bound. No growing twist is supplied to fixed-datum UM.

## 1. Inputs and the new results

Use the notation of [M](../../zeta_zero_free_validated_merged.md), [CP](../cubic-packets.md), [BC](../[private research revision]/cubic-mobius-core-moment.md), and [the independently accepted SR packet](../[private research revision]/cubic-square-row-moment.md). The independent SR review, recorded in [[private research revision]](../review-cycle-23.md), checks the original CP normalization and fixed-class statement. Write \(q_a=Na\), and put \(\vartheta_c=\chi_c^2\) for the cubic character. Every power retains its nonunit zeros.

The exact inputs used here are:

* **I-C3CF:** M (5.15), the cubic sieve with cube-free ideal rows and columns, arbitrary column coefficients, and its stated finite ray/reciprocity variants:
  \[
  \sum_{q_a\le A}^{\mathrm{cube\!-\!free}}
  \left|\sum_{q_c\le X}^{\mathrm{cube\!-\!free}}
       z_c\vartheta_c(a)\right|^2
  \ll_\epsilon(AX)^\epsilon
       \{A+X+(AX)^{2/3}\}\sum_c|z_c|^2.
  \tag{MQ1}
  \]
  The actual columns below are squarefree. This is the cube-free theorem already stated in M, not an unmentioned extension of the squarefree-only version B2.25. Fixed column exclusions can be imposed through zero coefficients. Its constants do not depend on the arbitrary coefficients.

* **I-HECKE, used only for the all-repetition result:** the inherited all-primitive-finite-order zero-free strip with boundary \(b_0=.874886647039964131\ldots\), together with buffered conductor/height bounds for reciprocal Hecke functions, exact deleted factors, and finite profile orders. Relevant anchors are M Theorem B0 and (B0.14), and BC (BC13), including its interval-endpoint version. This is stronger than ordinary-zeta nonvanishing. It is explicitly required wherever the parameter \(b>b_0\) occurs.

* **I-CP:** M (2.8), (2.14)--(2.15) and CP (21)--(25), with the original coefficient, all total-column masks, fixed components, zero terms and single product kernel. Original column profiles and their fixed derivatives are rapid at both endpoints; the row Fourier profile is Schwartz. The fixed core twists have the finite-order scope of BC section 8. Angular outside-cube factors remain outside the core moment.

No assertion from the enlarged plain family M (B3.40) is silently applied to a Möbius polynomial. In particular, its moving-support contract does not identify a row-varying twist with fixed datum.

Write each nonzero element row in its quadratic class as

\[
n=d a^2,\qquad q_n=q_dq_a^2,
\tag{MQ2}
\]

where \(d\) is squarefree at every prime, with a prescribed unit representative modulo squares. The choice of generator for \(a\), modulo its bounded unit ambiguity, indexes every row with bounded multiplicity. There is no condition \((d,a)=1\). Separate the finitely many fixed-prime parity and unit choices; no moving prime is added to \(S\). Let \(d(n)\) denote this representative and use \(q_{d(n)}\) for its norm, rather than a character conductor.

For a frozen ideal \(R\), an interval \(\mathcal I\) of core norms, a fixed permitted finite-order twist \(\nu\), and an original common profile \(F\), set

\[
\mathcal M_n^R(X;F,\mathcal I)
=X^{-1/2}\!
 \sum_{\substack{c\ {\rm squarefree},\ (c,R)=1\\q_c\in\mathcal I}}
 \mu(c)\nu(c)\overline{\vartheta_c(n)}F(q_c/X).
\tag{MQ3}
\]

The original exclusion \(S\) is understood. The interval may have an infinite endpoint. Its endpoints are frozen independently of the row. For a fixed nonnegative Schwartz radial majorant \(\Omega\), let \(\mathcal E_6(H,X,\Delta)\) be the sum of \(|\mathcal M_n^R|^2\Omega(q_n/H)\) over \(q_{d(n)}\le\Delta\) and rows sixth-power-free **away from \(S\)**. Let \(\mathcal E_{\rm all}\) have the same class cutoff and every row valuation. All fixed-prime valuations and element units are retained in both definitions.

Uniformly for \(H,X,\Delta\ge1\), \(1\le\Delta\le H\), and frozen polynomial-norm deletion ideals, the new bounds are

\[
\boxed{\mathcal E_6(H,X,\Delta)
\ll_\epsilon (HX\Delta q_R)^\epsilon\mathscr S(F,\Omega)^2
\left\{(H\Delta)^{1/2}+X\Delta+
       H^{1/3}X^{2/3}\Delta^{2/3}\right\}.}
\tag{MQ4}
\]

For every fixed \(b_0<b<1\), I-HECKE additionally gives

\[
\boxed{\begin{split}
\mathcal E_{\rm all}(H,X,\Delta)
\ll_{b,\epsilon}(HX\Delta q_R)^\epsilon\mathscr S_b(F,\Omega)^2
\bigl\{&(H\Delta)^{1/2}+X\Delta+
       H^{1/3}X^{2/3}\Delta^{2/3}\\
       &+H^{1/6}X^{(2b+1)/3}\Delta^{5/6}\bigr\}.
\end{split}}
\tag{MQ5}
\]

These are estimates for the actual joint row family. The class representative is allowed to grow in the entire range being summed, and the constants are uniform in it. The first bound in particular gives

\[
\Delta\le H/X\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\mathcal E_6\ll H(HXq_R)^\epsilon.
\tag{MQ6}
\]

Put

\[
\kappa_b=\frac{4b+2}{5}>1.
\]

Then the all-repetition bound gives

\[
\Delta\le H/X^{\kappa_b}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\mathcal E_{\rm all}\ll H(HXq_R)^\epsilon.
\tag{MQ7}
\]

Fixed profile and height factors are suppressed in MQ6--MQ7. Their finite orders are uniform in every moving label. All preliminary losses are chosen below the final loss. No uniformity is asserted as \(b\) approaches \(b_0\).

## 2. The coupled \(d,a\) arithmetic and the sixth-power-free moment

The zero-preserving identity needed here is different from freezing the quadratic twist in SR6:

\[
\boxed{\overline{\vartheta_c(d a^2)}
       =\overline{\vartheta_c(d)}\,\vartheta_c(a).}
\tag{MQ8}
\]

On units it is the order-three identity \(\overline{z^2}=z\). At a prime dividing both the core and either \(d\) or \(a\), both sides are zero. Thus it is valid when \(d,a\) share primes. It is also valid at a prime where the combined exponent in \(d a^2\) is three: the canceled phase still has its natural zero.

First take an annular \(F\) and a sharp row ball \(q_n\le H\). Freeze \(d\). The inner coefficient for the cubic sieve in \(a\) is

\[
z_c=X^{-1/2}\mu(c)\nu(c)\overline{\vartheta_c(d)}
  \mathbf1_{(c,R)=1}\mathbf1_{q_c\in\mathcal I}F(q_c/X).
\]

Its squared coefficient mass is \(O_F(1)\), uniformly in \(d,R,\mathcal I\). The phase depending on \(d\) is a permitted arbitrary column coefficient in MQ1. It is not a new fixed character datum in UM.

If \(n=d a^2\) is sixth-power-free, \(a\) is cube-free. The exact cubic-sieve row length is

\[
A_d=(H/q_d)^{1/2}.
\]

It is the norm of \(a\), determined by MQ2; no conductor has replaced the norm of \(n\). MQ1 bounds the contribution for this \(d\) by

\[
(HX)^\epsilon\{(H/q_d)^{1/2}+X+
                         (HX^2/q_d)^{1/3}\}.
\]

Sum the squarefree representatives \(q_d\le\Delta\). Ideal counting gives

\[
\sum_{q_d\le\Delta}q_d^{-1/2}\ll\Delta^{1/2},\quad
\#\{d:q_d\le\Delta\}\ll\Delta,\quad
\sum_{q_d\le\Delta}q_d^{-1/3}\ll\Delta^{2/3}.
\tag{MQ9}
\]

This proves the three terms of MQ4. There is no extra Cauchy--Schwarz in \(d\), and no appeal to separate moments of size \(H\) for each twist.

For the stated version with every fixed-prime valuation, write the fixed-prime part of \(a\) as a member of the finite cube-free \(S\)-orbit times an \(S\)-supported cube. The finite orbit supplies fixed coefficient twists and exact bounded scale constants. Each remaining sixth-power row multiplier has norm \(q_t^6\). Replace \(H\) by \(H/q_t^6\) in the estimate just proved. The first and third terms have summable weights \(q_t^{-3}\) and \(q_t^{-2}\). The middle term counts at most a logarithmic power of \(H\), because \(t\) is supported on the fixed finite \(S\). That loss is included in \((HX)^\epsilon\). Element units give only finitely many components.

The original cut \((d,a)=1\), if a smaller cube-free-row sector is desired, is a restriction of the positive outer sum and may be retained. It was not assumed in the proof.

## 3. Pay every sixth-power repetition with the actual Möbius coefficients

Factor the square-root label uniquely as \(a=b_1t^3\), with \(b_1\) cube-free. Thus

\[
n=d b_1^2t^6,\qquad
q_n=q_dq_{b_1}^2q_t^6,\qquad
\overline{\vartheta_c(n)}
=\overline{\vartheta_c(d)}\vartheta_c(b_1)
 \mathbf1_{(c,t)=1}.
\tag{MQ10}
\]

Intersections among \(d,b_1,t\) are allowed. All fixed-prime powers and units are handled as above. The last mask in MQ10 is exact and is retained as the moving deletion \(Rt\). This is a row sixth-power extraction, not the outside theta-cube label \(B\) or \(E\) in CP.

Choose \(T\ge1\), to be optimized. For \(q_t\le T\), apply the proof of MQ4 at row scale \(H/q_t^6\), with the fixed deletion \(Rt\). Sum in \(t\). Since

\[
\sum_tq_t^{-3}<\infty,\qquad
\sum_tq_t^{-2}<\infty,\qquad
\#\{t:q_t\le T\}\ll T,
\]

the short-repetition energy is

\[
\ll (HX\Delta q_R)^\epsilon
\left\{(H\Delta)^{1/2}+X\Delta T+
                  H^{1/3}X^{2/3}\Delta^{2/3}\right\}.
\tag{MQ11}
\]

The \(\,X\Delta T\,\) term is retained. Discarding it would amount to omitting the repeated-row loss in an all-row cubic sieve.

For \(q_t>T\), use I-HECKE on the **actual Möbius polynomial**. For \(q_n\le H\), the primitive finite-order character inducing \(\nu\overline{\vartheta_c(n)}\) has conductor norm bounded by a fixed multiple of \(q_{\operatorname{rad}(d b_1)}\). The redundant natural zeros and the additional \(t\)-mask have total radical norm at most \(q_dq_{b_1}q_t\le H\), before cancellations. Deletions at \(R\) cost a further \(q_R^\epsilon\). Mellin inversion on a fixed line \(b>b_0\), with the reciprocal bound from M (B0.14), gives

\[
|\mathcal M_n^R(X;F,\mathcal I)|
\ll_{b,\epsilon}X^{b-1/2}(HXq_R)^\epsilon
\mathscr S_b(F).
\tag{MQ12}
\]

The estimate includes a principal inducing character: a pole of its \(L\)-function is a zero of the reciprocal, not a residue to be dropped. No zero-free statement for Dedekind or moving Hecke functions is inferred from an ordinary-zeta input here.

For completeness, a sharp interval in MQ12 is legitimate. The uniform interval form of BC13, or buffered Perron followed by partial summation, bounds the Möbius partial sum at \(U\) by \(U^{b+\epsilon}\) times the conductor/deletion subpower. Applying it to \(F(q_c/X)\mathbf1_{\mathcal I}\) gives endpoint terms and the integral of its derivative. Both cost \(X^{b+\epsilon}\) times a fixed weighted seminorm, uniformly in the interval endpoints. Thus the original sharp core cutoff causes no moving derivative order.

For each \(t\), the number of remaining pairs \((d,b_1)\) is bounded by

\[
\sum_{q_d\le\Delta}(H/(q_dq_t^6))^{1/2}
\ll (H\Delta)^{1/2}q_t^{-3}.
\]

Terms with a remaining norm bound below one are empty. Since
\(\sum_{q_t>T}q_t^{-3+\epsilon}\ll T^{-2+\epsilon}\), the long-repetition energy is

\[
\ll_{b,\epsilon}(HX\Delta q_R)^\epsilon
 X^{2b-1}(H\Delta)^{1/2}T^{-2}.
\tag{MQ13}
\]

Choose, up to fixed constants,

\[
T=\max\left\{1,\,
 X^{(2b-2)/3}(H/\Delta)^{1/6}\right\}.
\tag{MQ14}
\]

If the second quantity is at least one, the two variable terms balance and each costs

\[
H^{1/6}X^{(2b+1)/3}\Delta^{5/6}.
\]

If it is smaller than one, the long-repetition term at \(T=1\) is at most \(X\Delta\). This proves MQ5. Under \(\Delta\le H/X^{\kappa_b}\), the first three terms are at most \(H\), because \(\kappa_b>1\), and the last equals at most \(H\) by

\[
\frac{2b+1}{3}-\frac56\kappa_b=0.
\tag{MQ15}
\]

This is the asserted all-repetition joint estimate MQ7.

## 4. Original profiles, row tails and uniform orders

The preceding proofs used annular columns and a row ball only to display the powers. They extend to the prescribed original family without a new arithmetic premise.

Use a fixed annular partition \(F_j(y)=F(2^j y)\vartheta(y)\). The exact central normalization is

\[
\mathcal M_n^R(X;F,\mathcal I)
=\sum_j2^{j/2}
 \mathcal M_n^R(2^jX;F_j,\mathcal I).
\tag{MQ16}
\]

Every fixed weighted seminorm of \(F_j\) decreases as \(2^{-A|j|}\), for arbitrarily large fixed \(A\), with a fixed polynomial height cost. Apply Minkowski to the positive joint row norm. The column powers in MQ4--MQ5 are \(0,1,2/3,(2b+1)/3\); all are bounded. Consequently the factors \(2^{j/2}\), the scale powers and their subpower losses are summable against the endpoint decay. One does not need a UM length margin on the enlarged annuli.

For a subunit column scale \(0<X<1\), direct summation gives
\(|\mathcal M_n^R(X;F,\mathcal I)|\ll_A X^A\), uniformly in the character, \(R\), and interval. The number of rows with \(q_n\le H,\ q_d\le\Delta\) is \(O((H\Delta)^{1/2})\). These facts also provide arbitrary subunit endpoint factors when a projector divisor exceeds a core scale.

For the original row majorant, keep all \(q_n\le H\) as one ball and decompose only its upper tail into dyads \(q_n\asymp2^jH\), \(j\ge0\). Apply the ball bounds at \(2^{j+1}H\), with the same frozen \(\Delta\). Their powers in the row scale are at most \(1/2\), up to an arbitrarily small loss, so the Schwartz decay sums the tail. Every fixed-prime valuation and unit remains included. No row conductor is substituted for the row norm at this step.

These arguments use a fixed finite profile order, chosen from \(b\), the requested loss and the prescribed profiles before any scale or arithmetic label varies. Original Mellin height twists cost a fixed polynomial, absorbed by the original rapid Mellin densities. The original product profile and its Mellin roots are unchanged in the signed expression. Partitions occur only inside positive estimates. No Type I theorem is invoked on a partitioned or sharply modified profile.

## 5. Both moving masks and the whole common-gcd projector

Use the exact two-core expression SR8, allowing its original sharp lower core cut and two different complex common profiles:

\[
\mathcal P_n(C,E;R_1,R_2)
=\!\!\sum_{\substack{c,e\ {\rm sf},\ (c,e)=1\\
                     (c,R_1)=(e,R_2)=1}}
\mu(c)\mu(e)\psi_{1,n}(c)\overline{\psi_{2,n}(e)}
\sqrt{q_cq_e}\,F(q_c/C)G(q_e/E),
\tag{MQ17}
\]

where \(\psi_{j,n}(c)=\nu_j(c)\overline{\vartheta_c(n)}\). Retain each core norm in its original interval. Let \(w_n\) be any row weight dominated by \(\Omega(q_n/H)\), with the selected class cutoff and either the sixth-power-free restriction or all repetitions.

Insert the **entire** projector \(\sum_{g\mid c,e}\mu(g)\), then put \(c=gm,e=gk\). The residual masks are \((m,gR_1)=(k,gR_2)=1\), with \((g,R_1R_2)=1\) outside. The row multiplier is

\[
\nu_1(g)\overline{\nu_2(g)}
|\overline{\vartheta_g(n)}|^2,
\]

and retains \(\mathbf1_{(g,n)=1}\). The projector sign \(\mu(g)\) remains. There is no residual \((m,k)=1\) after this complete expansion.

With \(F_1(x)=\sqrt{x}F(x)\), the exact normalized factor is

\[
\frac{CE}{q_g}\,
\mathcal M^{gR_1}_{1,n}(C/q_g;F_1,\mathcal I_1/q_g)
\overline{\mathcal M^{gR_2}_{2,n}
 (E/q_g;\overline{\sqrt{x}G(x)},\mathcal I_2/q_g)}.
\tag{MQ18}
\]

This retains the same-complex-parameter product if a Mellin separation was used. It is not replaced by a positive square.

Let \(M_*=\max(C,E)\). If

\[
\begin{array}{ll}
\Delta\le H/M_* &: \text{sixth-power-free selection},\\
\Delta\le H/M_*^{\kappa_b} &: \text{all-repetition selection},
\end{array}
\tag{MQ19}
\]

then MQ6 or MQ7 applies to each residual length, since \(C/q_g\le C\) and \(E/q_g\le E\). Cauchy--Schwarz in the original selected rows gives \(H\) up to the stated subpowers. At subunit lengths use the direct endpoint estimate in section 4. The resulting \(g\)-mass is

\[
\sum_gq_g^{-1+O(\epsilon)}
 \min(1,(C/q_g)^A)\min(1,(E/q_g)^A)
\ll_{A,\epsilon}(CE)^\epsilon.
\]

Hence the actual selected covariance is

\[
\boxed{
\left|\sum_n w_n\mathcal P_n(C,E;R_1,R_2)\right|
\ll HCE(HCEq_{R_1}q_{R_2})^\epsilon,
}
\tag{MQ20}
\]

with the appropriate input and profile factors. Both moving masks have been retained uniformly. The proof bounds the complete signed gcd expansion; it does not mistake an auxiliary common-divisor block for a sector of the original coprime columns. Any additional row-only selector may be kept. Arbitrary pair-dependent column masks are outside this assertion.

## 6. Transfer to the actual C--C Poisson sector

Fix the original outside cube labels \(B,E\). CP23--CP25 force \(h=R_0n\) in the C--C part. Their complete finite transform, Poisson normalization and phase give exactly SR12, with outside factor

\[
\frac{K(q_Bq_E)^4}{D^2}=\frac{q_Bq_E}{H},\qquad
C_*=\frac{D}{q_B^3},\quad E_*=\frac{D}{q_E^3},
\quad H=\frac{C_*E_*}{K}.
\tag{MQ21}
\]

The factor \(q_{R_0}\) in the forced transform cancels its period normalization; \(\eta(R_0)\overline{\eta(R_0n)}=\overline{\eta(n)}\), including zeros. There is no new density factor upon reindexing the forced sublattice. The surviving core weight is \(\sqrt{q_cq_e}\mu(c)\mu(e)\) with the original conjugate \(W_0(q_c/C_*)\) and \(W_0(q_e/E_*)\). Thus MQ17--MQ20 apply without changing any source power.

Retain exactly

\[
(c,e)=(c,E)=(e,B)=(B,E)=1.
\]

The opposite deletion ideals are \(R_1=E,R_2=B\). Own-column intersections \((c,B)>1\) and \((e,E)>1\) remain allowed. M (2.8) supplies no extra \((B,k)\) mask. The outside angular factors \(\xi(B)\overline{\xi(E)}\) are retained until their absolute values are bounded by one.

For \(\kappa=1\) or \(\kappa=\kappa_b\), define the **nominal, cube-pair-dependent** cutoff

\[
\boxed{\Delta_\kappa(B,E)
=\frac{H}{\max(C_*,E_*)^\kappa}.}
\tag{MQ22}
\]

It depends only on the outside cube pair and the original scale \(D,K\), not on the live cores or the projector divisor. Select

* \(q_{d(n)}\le\Delta_1(B,E)\), with \(n\) sixth-power-free away from \(S\); or
* \(q_{d(n)}\le\Delta_{\kappa_b}(B,E)\), with every row repetition.

Pairs whose cutoff is below one have an empty sector. A nonempty sector automatically has \(C_*,E_*\ge1\): when \(\max(C_*,E_*)<1\), MQ22 is at most \(\max(C_*,E_*)^{2-\kappa}/K<1\); otherwise a smaller core scale below one also makes MQ22 below one. Here \(K\ge1\) and \(1\le\kappa<2\).

Use MQ20 with the unchanged sharp original nonunit core intervals, in particular \(q_c,q_e>D^\gamma\). This costs a cube pair by

\[
\frac{q_Bq_E}{H}\,H C_*E_*D^\epsilon
=\frac{D^{2+\epsilon}}{(q_Bq_E)^2}.
\tag{MQ23}
\]

The original \((B,E)=1\) is present before taking this positive bound. Sum the absolutely convergent \(\sum_{B,E}(q_Bq_E)^{-2}\). The selected sector, including all its original column and row tails, is therefore \(O(D^{2+\epsilon})\).

The sharp core cutoff is handled directly by the allowed intervals in the sieve and Hecke partial summation. No artificial principal unit-core pair was added, so no nonprincipal Poisson identity is asserted there. Equivalently, in the numerical ranges below its removal would be a rapid lower-profile error, but that alternative is not needed for the proof.

The union of the two sectors is also paid: use the sixth-power-free sector first and apply the all-repetition bound to its complement. This is a disjoint row-selector decomposition, not an assumption of positivity for the signed C--C form. It can likewise be combined with the previously paid SR sectors by removing their overlap through row-only selectors.

## 7. Numerical growing ranges and the exact remaining obligation

Put \(K=D^k\), restrict \(q_B,q_E\le D^\lambda\), and ask for every quadratic class with \(q_d\le D^\eta\). A sufficient uniform rectangular budget is

\[
\boxed{\eta+3\lambda\le 2-\kappa-k.}
\tag{MQ24}
\]

Indeed

\[
\Delta_\kappa(B,E)
=\frac{D^{2-\kappa}
 q_{\min(B,E)}^{\,3(\kappa-1)}}{K q_{\max(B,E)}^3}
\ge D^{2-\kappa-k-3\lambda}.
\]

The min/max notation in this formula refers to the two norms only. The sharper curved sector is still MQ22.

At the current cubic scale \(k=.87653\):

| Sector | Required arithmetic input | Bare-pair class cutoff | One uniform two-cube example |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sixth-power-free away from \(S\) | I-C3CF | \(q_d\le D^{.12347}\) | \(q_d\le D^{.05},\ q_B,q_E\le D^{.024}\), reserve \(.00147\) |
| Every repetition | I-C3CF and I-HECKE at \(b=7/8\), so \(\kappa=11/10\) | \(q_d\le D^{.02347}\) | \(q_d\le D^{.01},\ q_B,q_E\le D^{.004}\), reserve \(.00147\) |

Both examples allow the original double-large-core restriction \(q_c,q_e>D^{1/4}\). Their nominal smallest core scales are \(D^{.928}\) and \(D^{.988}\), respectively. The bounds concern a growing set of genuine classes, not a fixed finite family whose constants are left uncontrolled.

For the all-repetition bare pair at \(b=7/8\), the endpoint class cutoff has \(\Delta=D^{.02347}\), \(H=D^{1.12347}\), and the balancing repetition cutoff is \(T=D^{1/10}\). The short-repetition term \(X\Delta T\) and the long Möbius term \(X^{3/4}(H\Delta)^{1/2}T^{-2}\) are both exactly of order \(H\). This makes the repeated-row cost explicit. Choosing the fixed buffer \(b=.8749\) instead gives \(\kappa=1.09992\) and bare-pair cutoff \(D^{.02355}\); the limiting available exponent as \(b\downarrow b_0\) is \(.023560682368028695\ldots\), with constants fixed only after selecting a positive buffer.

The squarefree diagonal \(d=n,\ a=1,\ q_d\asymp H\) is **not** paid. In the bare pair, MQ6 reaches only \(d\le H/D\), and MQ7 only \(d\le H/D^{\kappa_b}\). The original direct cubic-sieve estimate on squarefree rows still contains

\[
H+D+(HD)^{2/3}.
\]

After the actual \(D^2/H\) covariance normalization, its last term is

\[
D^{8/3}H^{-1/3}=D^2K^{1/3}
=D^{2.292176666666\ldots}
\quad(k=.87653).
\tag{MQ25}
\]

That is the remaining upper-budget gap in the dominant primitive range, not a lower bound for the actual Möbius moment. The present proof avoids that range by genuinely summing the smaller quadratic representatives with their shorter square-root row variables. It has not frozen a moving ramified twist, invoked a conductor-uniform separate UM theorem, or identified a row conductor with the indexing norm.

The exact residual remains the unselected double-large-core C--C Poisson contribution, including the moving squarefree diagonal and the other cube-pair/class ranges, **minus the original whole II**. No II frequency, continuation addback, or Type I residue is reassigned. Closing SR18 for that actual residual, or obtaining an equivalent signed covariance estimate with both masks and the complete projector, is still an additional arithmetic obligation.

## Independent review

Independent review accepted the cube-free domain of MQ1; MQ8 and MQ10 at overlapping primes; all fixed-place and unit restoration; the three weighted \(d\)-counts; the retained \(X\Delta T\) term and uniform all-character premise in MQ12; the \(T^{-2}\) tail and balancing exponent; the interval and noncompact-profile uniformity; the exact \(CE/q_g\) and complete projector in MQ18; the unchanged CP normalization and opposite masks; and the summable physical cost MQ23. The input labels and the unchanged whole-II scope are part of the theorem.

The unchanged source and independent review are retained under
`[restricted provenance path] mathematical source]`. Their hashes and the canonical hash
are recorded in the promotion receipt; no mathematical repair was needed.

## 2. Contour rotation and absolute remainder

Fix b>1, delta=b-1, a_n=mu(n)chi(n), and

    F(z)=sum_(n>=1)a_n exp(-nz), Re z>0,
    V_b(x)=F(x^(-b)+i/x).

The series is normally convergent there, with |a_n|<=1 and the original
character zeros. For Re s>0 put

    I_n(s)=integral_0^infinity exp(-nt^b-int)t^(s-1)dt.

With v=nt and e=n^(-delta), this is n^(-s) times the integral of
exp(-iv-e v^b)v^(s-1). Choose a FIXED angle 0<alpha<pi/(2b) and use
principal powers on -alpha<=arg v<=0. For each e>0 the large joining arc
is dominated by exp(-e R^b cos(b alpha)), because the modulus of exp(-iv)
is at most one throughout that sector. The small arc tends to zero for
Re s>0. Thus rotation to v=r exp(-i alpha) is valid. On that ray
Re(v^b)>0 and |exp(-iv)|=exp(-r sin alpha).

The integral Taylor remainder for exp(-z), Re z>=0, has modulus at most
|z|^K/K!. Consequently, for every fixed positive integer K,

    I_n(s)=sum_(k=0)^(K-1) A_k(s)n^(-s-delta k)+R_(n,K)(s),
    A_k(s)=(-1)^k Gamma(s+bk)exp(-i*pi*(s+bk)/2)/k!,       (R1)
    |R_(n,K)(s)|<=C_(b,K,C)n^(-Re s-delta K).

The last estimate is uniform on each compact C in Re s>0. A valid
ray-integral majorant before taking its compact maximum is

    exp(alpha Im s) Gamma(Re s+bK)
      /[K! (sin alpha)^(Re s+bK)].

The coefficient integral can be evaluated by w=iv and rotation within
Re w>0. This gives precisely the phase in A_k; changing the sign of i/x
would conjugate the phase, so its sign is substantive. Every remainder
is holomorphic on Re s>0 by local integral domination. The n sum then
converges normally on Re s>max(0,1-delta K), including every finite
height. There is no claim of a bound uniform as |Im s| tends to infinity,
K grows, or b tends to 1.

Absolute Fubini initially holds on Re s>b, since the integral with the
oscillation removed is Gamma(sigma/b)n^(-sigma/b)/b. It gives

    H(s):=integral_0^infinity F(t^b+it)t^(s-1)dt
       =sum_(k=0)^(K-1) A_k(s)/L(s+delta k,chi)+R_K(s).   (R2)

This uses exactly the ordinary reciprocal L-series, with no artificial
Euler-factor deletion. Both sides have their usual meromorphic
continuations into the domain of the displayed remainder. In particular
at b=3/2, K=1,

    H(s)=Gamma(s)exp(-i*pi*s/2)/L(s,chi)+R_1(s),
    R_1 holomorphic on Re s>1/2.                         (R3)

The rotation was justified for each n first; the uniform remainder bound
then justifies the infinite summation. No interchange at e=0 on the
unrotated oscillatory ray, no Mertens estimate and no assumed zero-free
strip entered this argument.

The half-plane of this K=1 ABSOLUTE remainder is sharp as a generic
bounded-coefficient statement. For the diagnostic sequence a_n=1,
F(z)=1/(exp z-1). At b=3/2, as t decreases to zero,

    F(t^(3/2)+it)=-i/t+t^(-1/2)+O(1).

The first Mellin term is A_0(s)zeta(s); it removes the pole at 1 but has
no pole at 1/2. The difference therefore has a nonzero pole at 1/2.
This model does NOT assert a pole for the actual Mobius remainder or
obstruct use of K>=2. It checks the necessity of the author's domain
qualification without importing unproved arithmetic cancellation.

## 3. Complete Gram, scalar, heights, and the remaining power target

### 3.1 Fixed finite partition and exact original diagonal

Only now use (R1.2) with Gaussian Abel summation to deduce the accepted
pointwise F(x)=O_beta(x^beta), hence ||F||=O(X^beta). This direction
of dependence matters: F did not furnish (R1.2) or the signed core
moments. Let a=3/8,b=2/5,c=3/5 and partition the actual coefficient
family into

    C_0=T_(X^a),
    C_1=T_(X^b)-T_(X^a),
    C_2=T_(X^c)-T_(X^b),
    C_3=R_(X^c).

The supports of their coefficients c_i(n) are disjoint and exhaustive;
each coefficient is f(n) or 0. Their sum is exactly F. Define

    V_X(x)=C_f exp(tau/2)x/L^3,
    N_X^2=||V_X||^2=(3/2)C_f^2 exp(tau)X^2/L^6,
    v=(-B(a), B(a)-B(b), B(b), 0),  sum_i v_i=0.

For the eta of a compact interval containing a,b, the reviewed
asymptotics give, with

    epsilon_X=L^(-1)+X^(-eta)L^4+X^(beta-1)L^3,

the COMPLETE finite Gram approximation

    ||C_i-v_i V_X||<=C epsilon_X N_X,
    <C_i,C_j>=[v_i v_j+O(epsilon_X)]N_X^2,  all i,j.  (R3.1)

The first two leading coefficients are positive and the third is
negative. In particular the C_0,C_1 leading cross term is positive;
both have negative leading cross terms with C_2. Both ordered mixed
directions are retained. The leading matrix has a null sum direction,
but its logarithmic relative error is much larger than the desired
full-field power scale. It cannot by itself improve ||F||.

For the original current-proof G22 kernel,

    K_X(m,n)=integral_X^(2X)
           g(log(m/x))g(log(n/x))dx/x,

absolute convergence gives

    <C_i,C_j>=sum_(m,n)c_i(m)c_j(n)K_X(m,n).           (R3.2)

Indeed the absolute double series is bounded by integral (sum_n g)^2
=O(X^2), using (R0.1). The full true diagonal is

    Delta_all=sum_n K_X(n,n)=O_tau(X),

because g_tau(u)^2 is a constant times g_(tau/2)(u). Each piece's own
diagonal is bounded by Delta_all; every cross diagonal is exactly
zero because its supports are disjoint. Thus the COMPLETE original
off-diagonal scalar is exactly

    Q_off(X)=sum_(i,j)<C_i,C_j>-Delta_all.             (R3.3)

No diagonal in auxiliary r,p,q labels can replace this n=m diagonal.
No negative off-diagonal summand is deleted. The corresponding true
diagonal subtraction and exact Gram identity hold for any finite
threshold partition, including one with the critical threshold.

### 3.2 Both original heights, without a diagonal-height shortcut

For fixed sigma>1 and each coefficient family frozen at its chosen X,
put D_i(s)=sum_n c_i(n)n^(-s). Then |D_i(sigma+it)|<=zeta(sigma).
Using the convention <U,V>=integral conjugate(U)V dx/x, the exact
double-Mellin expression is

    <C_i,C_j>=(2pi)^(-2)integral_R integral_R
      exp(tau(sigma-it_1)^2/2) exp(tau(sigma+it_2)^2/2)
      conjugate(D_i(sigma+it_1))D_j(sigma+it_2)
      [integral_X^(2X)x^(2sigma+i(t_2-t_1))dx/x]dt_1dt_2. (R3.4)

The absolute Gaussian factors are constant times
exp(-tau(t_1^2+t_2^2)/2); hence both height integrals and all
interchanges are justified on their full real lines. This checks the
conjugation, sign of t_2-t_1, and normalization. The moving masked
D_i are not substituted for the fixed full detector's holomorphic
zero-detection argument.

### 3.3 Actual-norm cancellation is stronger than leading Gram data

For ANY exact two-part split F=T+R with ||F||<=C X^beta, write
b=||R||. Then

    <T,R>=-b^2+<F,R>,
    ||T||^2=b^2+O(b X^beta+X^(2beta)).                (R3.5)

These are exact identities plus Cauchy--Schwarz. If b is comparable
to X/L^d, the Gram of (T,R), normalized by the ACTUAL b^2, is

    [[1,-1],[-1,1]]
       +O(X^(beta-1)L^d+X^(2beta-2)L^(2d)).           (R3.6)

For the fixed-power split, d=3 and b~(-B(rho))N_X. If instead one
normalizes by its leading asymptotic norm, an additional error
O(L^-1+X^(-eta)L^4) enters. That is distinct from the power-small
accepted-full-field error in (R3.6).

For the critical split with kappa^2>=2exp(3tau), define

    W_kappa(x)=2x/L^2 Phi(kappa^2 X/x),
    N_kappa^2=||W_kappa||^2
       =4X^2/L^4 integral_1^2 s Phi(kappa^2/s)^2 ds.

The positive finite integral is fixed. By (R2.1),
||R_z-W_kappa||=O(X/L^3), so b is comparable to X/L^2. Therefore
(R3.6) holds with d=2. Normalizing by N_kappa^2 introduces a separate
O(1/L) asymptotic error. The accepted F bound additionally gives
T_z=-W_kappa+O(X/L^3+X^beta), a negative leading prefix; that last
prefix statement explicitly uses F, unlike the positive band (R2.9).

Finally, let a=||T|| and r_X=Re<T,R>/(ab). Cauchy--Schwarz gives
r_X>=-1, and exactly

    ||F||^2=(a-b)^2+2ab(1+r_X).                       (R3.7)

For 1/2<gamma<.874872, the desired full norm estimate with arbitrary
epsilon allowance is equivalent, after renaming epsilon, to BOTH

    |a-b|<=C_epsilon X^(gamma+epsilon),
    1+r_X<=C_epsilon X^(2gamma-2+epsilon)L^(2d),      (R3.8)

where d=3 for a fixed-power split and d=2 for the stated positive
critical profile. Necessity follows from the two nonnegative terms
in (R3.7). Sufficiency follows from a,b comparable to X/L^d; without
separately invoking F for that comparability, the first proposed
bound itself forces a comparable to the directly known b.

The present source theorems do not prove (R3.8) at a new gamma. The
accepted beta yields only its existing baseline. A field remainder
O(X/L^4) or O(X/L^3) remains larger than X^gamma for every fixed
gamma<1; writing a leading cancellation does not estimate its actual
residual at the required power precision. These are upper-bound
limitations, not lower bounds for the actual residual.

If (R3.8) were proved at such a gamma, (R3.7), the true O(X) diagonal,
and current-proof G29--G31 would return the COMPLETE fixed-field
moment and its zero exclusion. The fixed convolution equivalence is
used only after reconstructing F. It gives no hereditary equivalence
for the moving rough masks, SP/RN or pair02 subfamilies, arbitrary
Hecke twists, or selected low-gcd signed submasks.

# A far-source reduction to two separated inverse witnesses



## 1. Result and why the remaining input is different

Keep the accepted c11=312864909/2500000000=.1251459636 and preceding-family K=28114053/6250000. No feedback recalibration is made. The inherited F0/analytic ancestry, original positive-slot uniformity and external definition/import/admission obligations remain OPEN.

The exact far polynomial can be localized before merged pair expansion by using both presentations of the SAME annular coefficient. Its original divisor has a cutoff above; its complementary divisor has a cutoff below. Both presentations are equal up to sign for every row, including all natural zeros. On a buffered zero bin, a large annular value therefore gives two saturated inverse/plain pairs in the same character and product annulus. Existing inverse and plain moments pay all cases except a specific configuration of separated inverse scales.

For a convenient complete version across the original slot range 0<=v<=1/20, use a new fixed truncation

    t=33/25, R=U^t, lambda=1/2500, L=U^(t+lambda).       (F1)

The original smooth V and H are unchanged; only their declared scales differ. The completed zero identity is valid at this t. The actual prefix-active rows are now paid over this entire v range, with a strict algebraic margin exceeding1/1000 against the current E_K. This is a secondary payment. The main result is the complementary far localization.

After a weighted exceptional set bounded by

    H_J U^[E_K(delta,v)-1/2000+epsilon]                  (F2)

has been paid, every remaining nonfloor high row has compatible saturated pairs whose logarithmic scales satisfy

    17/20<r_-<47/50,       3/8<m_-<47/100,
    33/25<r_+<141/100,     0<=m_+<3/40,
    r_+ - r_->3/8,
    r_-+m_-=r_++m_+ + o(1).                            (F3)

The plus/minus subscripts name the two sides of the divisor cutoff, not the sextic orientation. The product scales come from the same actual annulus of D_far. Each pair has one common Fourier height and the same actual real part; the heights selected for the two representations can differ. They are retained as two independent height coordinates. The character and original slot system are the same. There is no assertion of statistical independence.

More precise adaptive bounds appear in F18--F19. The interval certificates hold on the whole delta range[17/25,7/10], not just its endpoints. The full complementary budget is explicit: prefix, all annular scales outside the localized window, all ordinary inverse/plain lengths outside the two ranges, finite free fixed-inducing rows, genuine completed and Fourier tails, labels, smooth profiles and heights are paid. What remains is an actual simultaneous-witness counting estimate on F3, or a sufficient mixed inverse moment stated in Section8. That estimate is OPEN. No generic signed pair sector of R22 has been deleted, and no negative-power OPEN-H norm is proved.

## 2. Exact source and parameter order

The entire accepted `[restricted mathematical source]` and its frozen independent `high-core-signed-review/report.md` were read. PR9 commit58344dfdbe756cf2f743da1908ffe0582418cf5b, literal B0.3, B0.7--16, B3.3, B3.31--39, supplies the inverse/plain polynomials, natural-zero reconstruction, rowwise Sobolev amplification and buffered-bin pointwise bounds. [restricted research revision]'s completed-source review Section6 explicitly permits every fixed bounded truncation t; it also retains the actual common-zero signal and tail order. The exact source bytes used are pinned in the receipts.

Work first on nonzero sixth-power-free element rows in a fixed smooth ball, with the original finite natural character dictionary. Ideal columns use primary generators and all six element units remain rows. Choose one whole orientation

    phi_u(n)=nu(n)psi_u(n),  psi_u(n)=chi_n(u)^(+/-1).

The fixed factor nu retains its actual order, conductor and natural omissions. All character powers preserve their zeros, including exponent0 and6. Original slots Q_u have total width v and their original disjoint prime pools, individual fixed relative characters, common profile, bounded real powers, independent heights and frozen holes. Shared primes between any cofactor, divisor and slot are allowed. No new prime support is introduced.

Rows belong to the original nonfloor buffered bin. Write a=(1+delta)/2; an attaining member phi_u has a zero rho_u=sigma_u+i gamma_u with sigma_u in[a,a+e_b), and the enlarged buffered maximum is below a+2e_b. The finite dictionary is fixed before live rows. The source B0.15 bounds every retained common smooth polynomial by

    |M_u(U^r)|^2 <= H_J U^[delta r+small],
    |S_u(U^m)|^2 <= H_J U^[delta min(m,1-m)+small].       (F4)

For inverse and plain polynomials, M and S are centrally normalized exactly as B0.3; bounded real powers and Fourier heights reside in the common profiles. Also retain the physical-bin pointwise bound

    |Q_u|^2 <= H_J U^[delta v+small].                   (F5)

F4--F5 use the same buffered dictionary and its admissible enlarged height range. They are not imposed on an arbitrary new family or on an arbitrary amplitude mask. A fixed finite union of attaining labels costs no power.

The proof order is fixed dictionary and bounded scale ranges; requested loss and bin buffer; original slot system/common profiles; the finite derivative/height orders; raw completion and Fourier-tail powers; final threshold and sufficiently small height exponent. Both Fourier coordinates needed below are included in the retained height budget before the buffered-bin estimates are applied. For larger heights use the original absolute counts with a larger fixed polynomial H_J. Thus the final threshold precedes the actual height. Constants can depend on fixed source data. No uniformity in a growing conductor or dictionary is claimed.

## 3. The exact polynomial, its far part and changing the truncation

Let V=1 on[0,1], V=0 on[2,infinity), as in the source, and

    A_R(n)=sum_(d|n)mu(d)V(Nd/R).

With Y=U^B the completed tail and its prefix/far split are

    D_R,u(s)=sum_(Nn>R)phi_u(n)A_R(n)(Nn)^(-s)e^(-Nn/Y),
    P_R,u(s)=sum_(Nn>R)phi_u(n)A_R(n)(Nn)^(-s)
                                     e^(-Nn/Y)H(Nn/L),
    F_R,u(s)=D_R,u(s)-P_R,u(s).                         (F6)

H is the same smooth function equal to one on[0,1], between zero and one, and zero beyond a fixed C. In particular the far coefficient is exactly multiplied by1-H(Nn/L). No sharp pair mask is substituted for it. Terminate genuinely at Nn<=U^(B+1), paying its exponentially small error before any pair expansion. This preserves every required derivative. The complete zero identity gives

    D_R,u(rho_u)=-1+O(U^(-A)).                          (F7)

Choose B after the polynomial costs from t and heights so the contour shift pays A. This is [restricted research revision]'s nonprincipal ordinary-L identity; no L-pole has been discarded.

The alternative t in F1 does not estimate the old R=U^(4/3) far norm by comparison. It supplies a different sufficient detector for the SAME high-row counting problem. For clarity, two truncations have the exact difference

    D_R0-D_R1 =sum_(d,m)mu(d)phi_u(dm)(Ndm)^(-s)e^(-Ndm/Y)
                       [V(Nd/R0)-V(Nd/R1)].            (F8)

The unit coefficient is zero in this difference. At the same actual nonprincipal zero it is O(U^(-A)), with a common B chosen for both fixed truncations. The difference is not asserted small in an ambient norm. Its prefix terms must be retained if comparing the two far polynomials. Our argument instead bounds all original high rows directly from F6--F7 at F1; therefore it also gives the corresponding counting implication for any old far-active subset. No old prefix or old far cross term is silently removed.

For every nonunit ideal n, the full Mobius convolution vanishes, giving

    A_R(n)=-sum_(dm=n)mu(d)[1-V(Nd/R)].                 (F9)

Complete multiplicativity preserves F9 at all valuations and shared primes. The unit is excluded throughout. Its nonzero complementary summands have Nd>R. This identity, not a claim of arbitrary-coefficient moment permission, is the new way we retain the unweighted cofactor.

## 4. Paying the prefix on the whole original slot range

The accepted [restricted research revision] proof of the unmarked positive prefix norm uses only t>1 in a fixed bounded range. Applying that same written argument at33/25 gives

    N0(P_R) <= H_J U^[J_t(delta,lambda)+epsilon],
    J_t=1/6+(5/6-delta)t+(1-delta)lambda.               (F10)

Here N0 is the complete squared tensor Sobolev norm on[a,1] times the retained height interval, summed over free rows with a nonnegative majorant. The real width is at least3/20. To make the change of t reviewable: F9 yields a sum over m<C L/R; the inner inverse dyad satisfies R<<D<<L/Nm. The centrally normalized old inverse bound is U^(1/6)D^(5/6); the weight d^(-s) multiplies its square by D^(-delta). Common-profile separation takes place on the full box before m or a row is chosen, with the original cutoff parameter R fixed during restoration. The outer sum is exactly

    U^(1/12) L^((5/6-delta)/2)
             sum_(Nm<C L/R)(Nm)^(-11/12).

The ideal count bounds it by U^(1/12)L^((5/6-delta)/2)(L/R)^(1/12); squaring proves F10. All mixed derivatives and independent heights retain their old costs. This is the full signed A_R coefficient before a positive estimate, not separate absolute original divisor dyads.

Let prefix-active rows satisfy |P_R,u(rho_u)|>=1/4. Positive Sobolev evaluation, then F5, gives their weighted count

    sum_prefix |Q_u|^2 <= H_J U^[J_t+delta v+epsilon].   (F11)

There is no prefix-active indicator in a Poisson sum. With the fixed K, define

    h=5-2delta, rho=1-10delta/(3h), k=rho+delta-1,
    D_K=15K-10-6Kdelta,
    a_K=delta(5-6delta)^2/(3h D_K),
    b_K=2delta(5-6delta)(K-1)/D_K,
    G=min(3kv,a_K+b_K v), E_K=rho+delta v-G.             (F12)

Throughout delta in[17/25,7/10], v<=1/20, the exact certificate proves

    E_K-(J_t+delta v)>eta, eta=1/1000.                  (F13)

The helper multiplies the sufficient lower bound rho-a_K-b_K/20-J_t-eta by3hD_K. After delta=17/25+x/50 its Bernstein coefficients are all positive; the smallest is31963522910683/488281250000000. Thus the old v=.05 obstruction at t=4/3 is not ignored: lowering this detector's t pays it with an explicit reserve. This choice does not raise c, because the remaining far rows are still present. All small losses spend less than eta/2, so F11 fits F2.

## 5. Two representations of each actual far annulus

On rows outside the paid prefix set, F7 implies |F_R,u(rho_u)|>=1/2 for large U. Decompose the original product norm n into a smooth fixed dyadic partition, retaining the full factor1-H(Nn/L), the exponential and the terminal cutoff. There are O(log U) nonempty product annuli. For at least one fixed annular scale X=U^ell the actual polynomial T_X,u has magnitude at least U^(-tau), for any preassigned small tau after the common thresholds. Its scale is above t+lambda-o(1). The precise original profile, including both transition cutoffs, remains common.

For any such annular weight W_X(Ndm), the two finite representations are

    T_X,u=sum_(d,m)mu(d)phi_u(d)phi_u(m)(Ndm)^(-s)
                              V(Nd/R)W_X(Ndm),
    T_X,u=-sum_(d,m)mu(d)phi_u(d)phi_u(m)(Ndm)^(-s)
                           [1-V(Nd/R)]W_X(Ndm).        (F14)

Both equations hold for every row, not only zero rows. No d,m coprimality is inserted. The first has d<=2R; the second has d>R. The missing common prime factors retain their natural zeros. Original slots can subsequently multiply either entire expression without changing their pool or coefficient.

Split d,m into smooth dyads and apply B3.3 to the coupled product weight before live row selection. A nonempty subunit dyad is replaced by length zero with a bounded dilation, exactly as in B3.3; it contains only boundedly many ideals. All Euler derivatives of V(Ax),1-V(Ax),1-H(A'xy) and exp(-A''xy) are bounded uniformly in positive dilation parameters on fixed annuli. Tail orders are chosen after the raw polynomial bounds. The two representations therefore each supply a saturated product of the source polynomials M and S, with one common frequency inside that pair. The selected frequencies for the two representations need not agree and are not identified.

Write (r_-,m_-) for a selected product from the first representation and (r_+,m_+) for one from the second. With errors O(tau),

    r_-<=t, r_+>=t,
    r_-+m_-=ell=r_++m_+,
    |M_-(U^r_- )S_-(U^m_- )|^2>=U^[delta ell-O(tau)],
    |M_+(U^r_+ )S_+(U^m_+ )|^2>=U^[delta ell-O(tau)]. (F15)

The real power is the same actual sigma_u for both products. Common-profile Fourier powers can translate their heights independently. The inverse profiles retain V or1-V at the original R. Inverse profiles are not redefined after shortening or saturation. All lengths are initially in a fixed polynomial range determined by B, so B0.15 and the free inverse moment are applicable; this is not an invocation of Lemma1W with an unlicensed truncation.

Comparing F15 with F4 first forces m_-,m_+<=1/2+O(tau), since delta>=17/25. Dividing by the other factor's pointwise upper bound then gives all four witness inequalities

    |M_-(U^r_-)|^2>=U^[delta r_- -O(tau)],
    |S_-(U^m_-)|^2>=U^[delta m_- -O(tau)],
    |M_+(U^r_+)|^2>=U^[delta r_+ -O(tau)],
    |S_+(U^m_+)|^2>=U^[delta m_+ -O(tau)].              (F16)

This is the same saturated-witness reasoning as the literal B0.17--20, now applied separately to two exact presentations of one fixed far annulus. It keeps their dependence. In particular, ell>t+1/2 plus a fixed margin cannot support the original product at a zero: every original m then exceeds1/2 by a margin, and F4 makes the annular contribution too small. All such far annuli are accounted for; they are not an unpaid long-product tail.

Finite dyads and label choices are handled by a union bound. The Fourier continuum and rowwise real/height parameters use the source's common finite measure and Sobolev bound, with their prescribed seminorms and polynomial height costs. No moving arithmetic coefficient is absorbed into that measure. If desired fix a deterministic admissible choice among the saturated witnesses; the bounds below also cover the union of every easy witness, so the choice cannot conceal an unpaid population.

## 6. Payment of every nonlocalized witness

For one inverse witness at length r, the old free inverse moment B0.9 and Sobolev give count exponent

    U_inv(r)=max(1,(1+5r)/6)-delta r.

For a plain witness, the literal unmarked fourth moment MP0 gives count exponent

    U_plain(m)=1-2delta m.                              (F17)

Multiply either count by F5, adding delta v. These estimates count an actual positive exceptional set; no zero-bin indicator is inserted into a Poisson kernel. They hold with the actual cutoff profiles V and1-V and the same natural character. The slot weights in this step use their original pointwise price, so no extra marked inverse coefficient or new slot is required.

Set e=E_K-delta v-eta=rho-G-eta, q=5/6-delta>0, and

    A=(1-e)/delta, C=(e-1/6)/q.                         (F18)

The exact certificates below show A<47/50<1<t<C throughout the whole rectangle. U_inv decreases on[0,1] and increases on[1,infinity), and

    U_inv(r)<=e for A<=r<=C;
    U_plain(m)<=e for m>=A/2.

Consequently the union of all rows having any saturated witness in one of these easy ranges has weighted mass <=H_J U^(E_K-eta+small). The source dyadic, profile, bin and height losses are chosen smaller than eta/2 in total. These rows are part of F2.

After that union is removed, the original inverse cannot use r>=C because r_-<=t<C; hence r_-<A. The complementary inverse cannot use r<=A because r_+>=t>A; hence r_+>C. Both plain witnesses have m<A/2. Since the two products have the same annulus, up to their fixed endpoint error,

    C-o(1)<ell<3A/2+o(1),
    ell-A-o(1)<m_-<A/2,
    0<=m_+<ell-C+o(1),
    r_+ - r_->C-A.                                    (F19)

These are the adaptive residual conditions. They prove much more than a large relative conductor: they specify two inverse scales and two very different unweighted cofactor scales in one actual character, with the original convolution and cutoff compatibility intact. They do not assert an improved probability merely because both witnesses exist.

All numerical inequalities are uniform, with strict room for the O(tau) length errors:

    A<47/50, C>33/25,
    C-A>3/8, 3A/2-C<3/40.                             (F20)

Choose tau after their positive minimum reserve. F19 then implies the coarse F3; r_->17/20 follows from ell>33/25 and m_-<47/100. Also ell<141/100 and r_+<141/100. The real cofactor separation m_--m_+ equals r_+-r_- up to the same endpoint error. Equality and bounded transition windows are not dropped: slightly padded classifications are paid first, and the strict coarse endpoints follow from the certified slack.

Here is the exact certificate construction, allowing independent reconstruction. Let Den=3hD_K, and

    N=(1-eta)Den-10delta D_K-delta(5-6delta)^2
                          -(3/10)delta h(5-6delta)(K-1).

Since G<=a_K+b_K/20, e>=N/Den. The four positive polynomials checked are

    (47/50)delta Den-(Den-N),
    N-Den/6-(33/25)Den q,
    delta(N-Den/6)-q(Den-N)-(3/8)Den delta q,
    (3/40)Den delta q-(3/2)q(Den-N)+delta(N-Den/6).

They imply F20 because increasing e decreases A, increases C and decreases3A/2-C. After delta=17/25+x/50, every Bernstein coefficient is positive. The receipt retains all coefficients, not a sampled grid. The least respective coefficients are

    43930113669/39062500000,
    2346540760291/19531250000000,
    16881490118129/19531250000000,
    91544989797/390625000000.

Den and k positivity, F13 and the fixed-row comparison are certified separately. Across eight polynomials the helper has30 positive Bernstein coefficients.

The residual has a further source simplification, not just a scale restriction. Its inverse and product dyads are outside every cutoff transition. The prefix certificate gives e>J_t, so

    C>t+(1-delta)lambda/q,
    C-(t+lambda)>lambda/(6q)>=1/2300,                 (F20a)

because q<=23/150 and lambda=1/2500. Thus ell>C-o(1) puts the entire retained product annulus beyond the fixed support of H(Nn/L), once U is large. Its H is exactly zero. Similarly r_-<47/50<t makes V(Nd/R) exactly one on the whole short inverse dyad, while r_+>C>t makes1-V(Nd/R) exactly one on the whole long inverse dyad. Fixed annular endpoint constants are absorbed by the strict gaps before the threshold. No claim about the transition rows is needed: those rows are already in the paid complement.

On the residual product annulus ell<141/100, the exponential may also be replaced by one with a fully paid error. The elementary coefficient bound |A_R(n)|<=d(n) and ideal counting give, uniformly per row and for the finite derivative list,

    |sum_(Nn~U^ell) phi_u(n)A_R(n)(Nn)^(-s)
                      W_X(Nn)[exp(-Nn/Y)-1]|
       <= H_J U^[(2-a)141/100-B+epsilon].             (F20b)

The same bound holds for either unmerged divisor presentation by the divisor bound. Squaring and summing rows, with trivial squared slot price U^(v+epsilon), adds1+v to twice that exponent. For a prescribed tail order A_tail>0, choose the common B also larger than A_tail+10; since a>=21/25, v<=1/20, this pays U^(-A_tail) norm error and all fixed logarithmic derivatives. The earlier completed contour identity's larger B requirement is retained. After replacement repeat the fixed annular witness extraction, including this one additional common profile family in the already paid easy-witness union. Thus the remaining selected witness products use ordinary annular inverse profiles, the common product-annulus profile and the original slots. Their two Fourier heights still need not agree.

This removes V only from the selected short and long inverse DYADS, where it is constant. It does not remove V from the full original divisor sum: doing that would replace its coefficient by mu*1=0 and destroy the detector. H and the exponential are removed from the residual product annulus by the separate exact-support and error arguments above. The original smooth detector is simplified only after its transition and tail terms have been accounted for.

## 7. Complete counted decomposition, rows, tails and original scope

For the original high-row weighted count in this fixed source window, the resulting rigorous implication is

    sum_high |Q_u|^2
       <= H_J U^[E_K-1/2000+epsilon]
          + sum_(u in B_sep)|Q_u|^2,                  (F21)

where B_sep consists of actual buffered rows admitting compatible F14--F16 witnesses in the strict coarse box F3 and the endpoint-padded adaptive box F19. Their profiles come from the exact original/complementary cutoff and the same annular far product; F20a--F20b justify the simplified residual presentation. The inequality counts a union of sets, so it does not require an artificial probability law or independent samples. The first term includes:

* Prefix-active rows, by F10--F13.
* Every far annulus for which either representation has an easy saturated inverse or plain witness, by F17--F19.
* Annuli too high for any original saturated product, the genuine exponential terminal tail, and the discarded common-profile Fourier tails.
* All finite dictionary/attaining labels, dyadic and scale-supremum costs, required real/height derivatives, bounded subunit windows and original natural zeros.

A fixed dictionary's exceptional sixth-free rows supported entirely on fixed primes form a fixed finite set, including its unit sectors. They can be kept as a separately counted complement even when a principal presentation prevents applying F4. The absolute original prime count gives |Q_u|^2<=H_J U^(v+epsilon), so their entire weighted mass is O_fixed(U^(v+epsilon)). This is well below F2: E_K>=rho>=19/54, v<=1/20; indeed delta-3k=4delta^2/h>0 and G<=3kv. No unit row is declared oscillatory. Where the original density family excludes these rows, the same calculation simply verifies that this separate restoration is affordable. If considering a fixed finite list of raw sixth-power-core families, their O(U^(1/6)) roots cost at most U^(1/6+v+epsilon), also below F2; the receipt verifies that strict comparison. This does NOT generalize F21 to an arbitrary raw moving-support family. Such a lift retains its existing normalization and natural-hole obligations.

For bounded U the threshold is enlarged and fixed constants pay the finite range. For heights beyond the retained small polynomial range the original row/slot absolute bound U^(1+v+epsilon) is absorbed by increasing the fixed power of(1+T). For the retained range, choose B after raw powers, the tail orders after B, and the final height exponent after the returned seminorm order. This is the same source order as the completed identity and buffered moments; a row or live height does not set a threshold.

There is no merged-pair projection in the proof of F21. All valuations, common factors and unequal roots/dyads occur in F14; no squarefree identity for mu(n)A_R(n) was used. Both signs in F14 are preserved. The identity differentiates exactly as needed in the common parameters. Prefix/far cross terms of an ambient positive norm are not claimed to have vanished. We bound the zero-event count by the actual signal and positive exceptional sets instead. The fixed product H remains part of every actual annular weight.

The original R22 signed norm and its old t=4/3 small-core/conductor payments remain unchanged. F21 is a different sufficient source reduction which covers the same high-row count if its remaining joint input is supplied. It must not be advertised as a bound for a selected R22 pair sector. Both physical projectors, clipped rectangles, moving-support reconstruction, genuine joint label counts, raw-root holes and tails, low/high/zero/extracted/fixed-inducing branches, actual6a/9a radii, physical K_phys^(5/6), no-slot/shortening complements, weighted Euler shifts including zero capacity, principal residue and common-Delta supremum feedback retain their accepted c11 contracts. None is repriced here and no centered M/24 reserve is spent.

## 8. The remaining estimate and a sufficient actual mixed moment

The weakest new counting target needed for a source improvement is

    sum_(u in B_sep)|Q_u|^2
           <= H_J U^[E_K-xi+epsilon], xi>0,            (OPEN-SEP)

for every original fixed family, bin, profile/height list and slot subset in the displayed range. Together with F21 this gives a source density saving min(xi,1/2000), after the usual loss allocation. It is conditional until OPEN-SEP is proved. A physical return must still use that input in its actual licensed family before any numerical c increase.

A concrete stronger sufficient arithmetic theorem avoids selecting zero rows inside a transform. For every compatible pair of inverse profiles arising from F14 and all original slots, prove on the clean natural free-row majorant

    sum_u |M_-(U^r_-)|^2 |M_+(U^r_+)|^2 |Q_u|^2
       <= H_J U^[delta(r_-+r_+)+E_K-xi+epsilon],        (OPEN-MIX)

with the necessary rowwise real-power and the TWO independent inverse-height suprema recovered through the finite source Sobolev derivatives. The fixed-inducing rows already paid in Section7 may be excluded by their fixed source condition; no high-zero indicator is inserted. On B_sep the two inverse witness lower bounds F16 divide this estimate to give OPEN-SEP. The actual annular and complementary profile compatibility may be retained; arbitrary coefficient arrays or an independently selected pair of characters are not requested. Original slots and their relative phases remain. A theorem for all such clean profiles is stronger than needed but unambiguous.

OPEN-MIX is a specific separated-length mixed inverse moment, not supplied by the old MI. Merging the inverse factors produces coefficients of the form

    sum_(d1 d2=n)mu(d1)mu(d2)W_-(Nd1/D_-)W_+(Nd2/D_+),

with shared-prime terms. Even without weights, the squarefree n coefficient is mu(n)2^omega(n); at a prime square the mu*mu coefficient is1 although mu(p^2)=0. Separated dyadic scales do not prohibit a shared prime in d1 and d2. Thus neither divisor boundedness nor the separated lengths licenses B3.31 or B3.6 on the merged coefficient. This is an actual source-family obstruction; a new mixed theorem or direct compatible covariance argument is necessary.

The precise signed interference is visible already before witness selection. If T_< and T_> denote the two unsigned-cutoff sums in F14, then

    T_< + T_> =0

term by term in the nonunit product coefficient, for every row. Therefore their actual cross covariance is minus the positive norm of T_<. This is a dependence identity, not a new saving; taking two independent absolute moment estimates cannot exploit that negative sign. Any covariance estimate must retain the actual profiles and common divisor convolution. This is the stronger objection to multiplying marginal density savings.

## 9. Failed shortcuts and the changed target

Several initially plausible routes were examined and are not used as results. A second clean coprime row Poisson transform still begins with dual length U^(5/3) at the old t=4/3 scale and leaves an inadmissible extra Gauss amplitude. It was not repeated as the main output. Merely increasing the positive prefix cutoff at fixed t charges(1-delta)lambda and eventually loses the existing envelope. Changing t without addressing the far source only moves the balance point; it does not improve the zero-free constant.

There is an exact scalar test for why the new simultaneous information is needed. With no slots and

    ell=5/(5-2delta), r_-=2ell/3, m_-=ell/3,
    r_+=ell, m_+=0,

all three marginal density exponents coincide:

    1-delta r_-=1-2delta m_-
       =1/6+(5/6-delta)r_+=rho.                       (F22)

These scales obey the new cutoff separation and lie inside the surviving coarse box. This does not construct an actual zero or a saturated arithmetic row, and it proves no lower bound for the true mixed norm. It does prove that retaining just the three stated marginal inequalities cannot yield a strict saving: their scalar feasible data still contain the old equality. The report's useful change is the rigorous reduction to the actual compatible mixed source where a new arithmetic estimate must act.

The cutoff change in F1 pays the original v<=.05 prefix and the far complement outside F3; it does not supply OPEN-SEP. For the original fixed t=4/3, the same proof gives F18--F19 at v<=1/25 using the already certified prefix gap. We do not use that narrower version to claim coverage of the larger slot window. The shorter truncation is explicit and its entire new prefix cost is paid in F13.

No direct OPEN-H return follows. Its target unit must remain with weight at least one and its total exponent must be negative. All positive counting exponents here are insufficient for that purpose. At a principal target the separate pole-annihilating kernel remains[s-1+Nn/Y]exp(-Nn/Y), with signal1-rho for rho!=1; a possible nonprincipal zero at1 keeps the unmodified signal-1. Nothing here identifies a new external root-LFunction definition. Near gains,1/6 and1/4 remain stronger conditional targets requiring their own full negative-power source estimate and complete scope.

## 10. Evidence, credit and handoff

`check.py` uses only standard-library Fraction arithmetic. It independently constructs all eight full-interval certificates, retaining30 positive Bernstein coefficients, six endpoint diagnostics and three exact scalar balance examples. It also checks1196 finite complementary-divisor cases and3588 natural-zero convolution cases. The ideal-convolution proof and source moment arguments above establish the infinite statements; these finite checks do not prove OPEN-MIX or a new endpoint. The helper writes a new receipt and refuses to overwrite it. No other writer's helper was executed or imported.

Primary source content was read in exact slices, and the entire accepted prefix integration and frozen prefix review were read. One initial Windows rg glob was corrected by using rg's own file filters. One later combined source/receipt output was truncated and is not claimed as a complete artifact read; final owned-artifact readback is separate and complete. No provider, child, formalization or kernel was used. Every old frozen scope, canonical file, tracker and Git state was left untouched.

Credit: OpenAI, Hailey Collet, Akash Levy, Zhongpai Gao with AI assistance, the pinned PR9/PR15 authors, the [restricted research revision]/[restricted research revision] completed-source work, and wild51's [restricted research revision] prefix proof and certificates. The divisor identity is elementary and no literature-priority claim is made. This lane supplies the two-sided annular witness reduction, whole-slot-window prefix reparameterization, complete coarse complement payment and precise separated inverse target. Acceptance and integration belong to the controller after independent review. Full readback/hash freeze, normal release of only the fresh own claim, absence verification, one final reviewer wake and STOP complete this lane.

## 1. G116: a complete paid complement for integer renewal

Fix an ordinary Dirichlet character chi modulo q, retaining natural zeros.
Let P^-(1)=infinity and P^+(1)=1. The inherited G92 source is

    R(m,p)=sum_(n<=m,P^-(n)>p)mu(n)chi(n)
          =1-sum_(p<ell<=m,ell prime)chi(ell)R(floor(m/ell),ell).

For a floor-invariant approximation F define its ACTUAL defect

    Delta(m,p)=F(m,p)-1
        +sum_(p<ell<=m)chi(ell)F(floor(m/ell),ell).

Assume F=R on the exact collar m<=p^r, fixed integer r>=1. The collar is
descendant-closed, so Delta=0 there; for r>1 its value is generally not1.
Finite triangular inversion, with floors composed before grouping, gives

    F(N,1)-M_chi(N)=Delta(N,1)+sum_(p,m>p^r)C_N(m,p)Delta(m,p),
    C_N(m,p)=-chi(p)
      sum_(N/[p(m+1)]<u<=N/(pm),P^+(u)<p)mu(u)chi(u).

Signs, nonunit zeros, root term and half-open endpoints are literal. This
identity and the N=20196 cancellation are inherited G92, not new credit.

If distinct integers u<v lie in the same interval, then
mv<=N/p<(m+1)u, whence m(v-u)<u and u>m. Thus a fiber containing a
cofactor u<=m is a SINGLETON, even before smoothness/squarefree/zero masks.
No fiber mixes short and long cofactors.

For each active short path d=pu, m=floor(N/d)>p^r and u<=m give
pu^2<=N and p^(r+1)u<N. Dropping restrictions only in the positive count,

    S_r(N)<=sum_(j>=2)min(sqrt(N/j),N/j^(r+1))
          <=(4+1/r)N^alpha_r, alpha_r=(r+1)/(2r+1).

Split at J=ceil(N^(1/(2r+1))). The initial part is at most2sqrt(NJ)
and the tail at most N/(rJ^r); the stated constant covers N>=1. On q-units
the singleton coefficient has absolute value1. If D_N bounds EVERY active
prime-state defect, the full short contribution costs at most D_N S_r(N).
This is an all-depth price, not a fixed-depth truncation.

Freeze Y_N=(log(2N))^A at the ROOT, A>1. Remove the short fibers first;
the remaining p<=Y_N paths are squarefree Y_N-smooth integers d<=N.
For0<sigma<1 their total absolute coefficient mass is at most

    Psi_sf(N,Y)<=N^sigma product_(p<=Y)(1+p^-sigma)
        <=N^sigma exp(1+Y^(1-sigma)/(1-sigma)).

Choose sigma just above1-1/A. Then A(1-sigma)<1, giving for every epsilon
Psi_sf(N,Y_N)<<N^(1-1/A+epsilon). The onset may be large; this is not a
small finite-N constant. The finite bound remains available.

All remaining fibers satisfy

    Y_N<p<N^(1/(2r+1)), p^r<m<sqrt(N/p), u>m,
    P^+(u)<p, omega(u)>=r+1.

Indeed N>=pum>pm^2>p^(2r+1), and a squarefree u with at most r primes
below p would be<p^r. In particular all larger primes have already been
paid. Let H_F be the ENTIRE signed C_N Delta sum over this hard region.
The exact disjoint partition is

    F(N,1)-M_chi(N)=Delta(N,1)+E_short+E_small+H_F,
    |E_short|+|E_small|
      <=D_N[(4+1/r)N^alpha_r+Psi_sf(N,Y_N)].

There is no absolute value inside H_F and no independence of defects.
The independent review supplies the useful weaker conditional contract:
for fixed d>=0, common gamma<1, every fixed chi/every epsilon/all large N,

    D_N<<N^(d+epsilon),
    d+max(alpha_r,1-1/A)<gamma,
    |F(N,1)|+|Delta(N,1)|+|H_F(N)|<<N^(gamma+epsilon).

Splitting epsilon among products proves M_chi(x)<<x^(gamma+epsilon) for
all large real x. Root-dependent F is allowed, provided each root uses
one F and its actual defects on the entire reachable system. No consistency
between different roots is required. No such F and hard-region estimate
has been constructed. F=R leaves the unknown Mertens sum at the root;
the terminal-only approximation does not have a free bounded defect.

For r=1,A=3, the paid exponent is2/3. At the CURRENT boundary a first gain
can allow

    d < theta11-2/3 =1561405273/7500000000,
    d+2/3 < gamma < theta11=.8748540364.

Using A=3 instead of A=7 makes a smaller paid small-prime sector and a
larger hard remainder; it is not a gain for an unchanged H_F. At gamma=5/6
with r=1,A=5 one may take d<1/30; at gamma=3/4 with r=1,A=3, d<1/12.
These conditional1/6 and1/4 returns do not establish their premises.

The zero-exclusion bridge is complete: s integral_1^infinity
M_chi(x)x^(-s-1)dx is holomorphic on Re s>gamma, including all compact-set
derivatives after choosing epsilon with room. It equals1/L(s,chi) on
Re s>1; continuation of L times this function=1 excludes every zero in
the half-plane. A principal pole at1 becomes a reciprocal zero, not an
excluded L-zero. Natural imprimitive factors and all heights remain.
Constants may depend on each fixed ordinary chi; no Hecke extension follows.

G112's principal full merged norm exponent1 is compatible with this result:
G116 pays restricted sectors, leaving the whole signed hard-region
correlation. It neither disproves the principal norm result nor obtains a
natural-residual lower bound from it.

# [private research revision]: signed logarithms, degree truncation and causal output

Accepted after complete author, independent and controller mathematical reads.
The [author](wild45/report.md) and [critic](wild45-review/report.md) remain
unchanged, with all30 cards, six author tests and two separate critic audits.
These results remove specific analytic prerequisites and reject a live global
norm certificate. They prove no new arithmetic exponent. The accepted written
endpoint remains c6=125139/1000000, theta6=.874861, relative to the pinned
PR9/Gao framework; external formalization and admission remain separate.

Throughout, f3(n)=mu(rad(n/3^v3(n))) includes prime2, every positive power,
and character zeros. The complete field is

    F_chi(u)=sum_(n>=1) f3(n)chi(n)g_tau(log n-u), tau>0 fixed.

An exponent gamma means its complete shell L2 NORM is
O_epsilon(X^(gamma+epsilon)); the squared norm has exponent2gamma.
Every character is fixed. An integer CRT calculation implies neither an
ideal-family result nor uniformity in a growing conductor.

## G67. Signed logarithmic bounds return the complete exponent

For f analytic near |z-t0|<=R, R>=16, f(t0)!=0, and any unit interval I
containing t0, let B>=sup_disk|f|. Avoid boundary zeros by varying R. Then

    integral_I log|f(t)|dt
      >=log|f(t0)|-(8/log R)log(B/|f(t0)|).

The proof uses the nonnegative superharmonic function
log(B/|f|), its positive harmonic part and the complete disk Green sum over
zeros with multiplicity. Near zeros have integrated Green excess at most4
and center Green value at least(log R)/2; far zeros and the harmonic part
obey the explicit Harnack bound. Real logarithmic singularities are integrable.
No zero separation, multiplicity cap or discarded negative logarithm is used.

For coefficients with sum|a_n|n^-b finite, the fixed Gaussian is entire and

    |F(z)| <= (2pi tau)^(-1/2)sum|a_n|n^-b
               exp(b Re z+tau b^2/2+(Im z)^2/(2tau)).

Choose t0 at a maximum on [j,j+1] and R in[sqrt j,2sqrt j]. Writing
M_j=max|F| and J_j=integral_j^(j+1)log|F| gives

    (1+eta_j)log M_j <= J_j+eta_j log B_j,
    eta_j=O(1/log j), log B_j=O(j).

Consequently J_j<=(gamma+epsilon)j+C_epsilon on EVERY sufficiently large
integer interval, for every epsilon>0, is equivalent in exponent to the
complete pointwise bound and the complete all-shell L2 bound. Jensen proves
the moment-to-log direction; the Green comparison returns the maximum with
only O(j/log j) loss. Sparse intervals or an average over j do not suffice.
This settles W21-T29's missing nonconcentration question for this complete
Gaussian class. It does not defeat the old smooth-signal or exceptional-dyad
counterexamples under their different hypotheses.

The actual Mellin numerator is

    integral_R F_chi(u)e^(-su)du=exp(tau s^2/2) N_chi(s)H_chi(s)/L(s,chi),
    N_chi=1-2chi(2)2^-s,
    H_2=(1-z_2)^-2, H_3=(1-z_3)^-2,
    H_p=(1-2z_p)/(1-z_p)^2 (p>=5), z_p=chi(p)p^-s.

H and its inverse converge absolutely for each fixed Re(s)>1/2. The finite
N zeros lie on Re(s)=1, or N=1 when2 is ramified. Full left Gaussian tails
and the improved right tail give continuation; multiplication by L excludes
zeros in gamma<Re(s)<1 without assuming reciprocal growth. The principal
pole and the known right boundary remain separate. A first gain needs
gamma<.874861; gamma=5/6 or3/4 gives the respective conditional targets.

The author also proves a finite upper certificate, preserving both zeros
and tails. For N>=exp(j+1), put

    T_(N,j)=exp(j+1+tau/2)barPhi((log N-j-1-tau)/sqrt tau).

With T>=T_(N,j)>0, an explicit derivative bound K_j, M midpoint samples v_k
and absolute errors delta_k,

    J_j <= M^-1 sum_k log(|v_k|+delta_k+T)+K_j/(4MT).

All parameters and sufficient asymptotic cutoff/sample budgets are in
author L8-L10 and critic Q8. This is a finite certificate for inspected
intervals. Its success on every large interval remains OPEN. Finite
quadrature ancestry includes G63; no new numerical evidence is promoted.

## G68. Exact degree energy and the retained arithmetic response

Let P contain2 and exclude3, Q=product P, q_p=1/p, and
a_P(n)=product_(p in P)(1-2*1_(p|n)). Set r_P=f3 a_P so that
f3=a_P r_P and r_P(pn)=r_P(n) for every p in P and every power. Under the
exact product reference law, Z_p=(B_p-q_p)/sqrt(q_p(1-q_p)). The expansion

    a_P=sum_S A_S Z_S,
    A_S=(-1)^|S| product_(p in S)2sqrt(q_p(1-q_p))
                      product_(p notin S)(1-2q_p)

    sum_S A_S^2 z^|S|=product_p[(1-nu_p)+nu_p z],
    nu_p=4(p-1)/p^2.

Thus the discarded squared norm rho_D^2 is exactly Pr(K>D) for an
auxiliary Poisson-binomial ENERGY variable. It is not a random model of
arithmetic phases. nu_2=1 forces every nonzero term to contain2.

    Z(u)=sum_n g_tau(log n-u)~exp(tau/2)e^u.

Its literal realization, with D_pV(u)=V(u-log p), is

    F_(P,D,chi)=sum_(|S|<=D)(-2)^|S| product_(p notin S)(1-2/p)
                    product_(p in S)(chi(p)D_p-I/p) R_(P,chi).

Every shifted scale, cross term, power, sign and ramified zero survives.
At full degree this is exactly F_chi. If rho_D^2<=X^(-2c-eta), c=1-gamma,
the coded and original complete norms have the same exponent gamma.

coefficients are .250278,1/3,1/2 for c6,1/6,1/4. The literal Q restriction

## G69. The global Euler norm fails; its mass escapes the physical scale

For P>=5 let f_P=f3 restricted to P-smooth integers and V_P its complete
Gaussian. Its exact finite Euler series, including all powers, is

    E_P(s)=(1-3^-s)^-1 product_(p<=P,p!=3)(1-2p^-s)/(1-p^-s).

For sigma>0 weighted Gaussian Fubini and Plancherel give

    ||e^(-sigma u)V_P||_2^2
      =e^(tau sigma^2)/(2pi) integral_R e^(-tau t^2)|E_P(sigma+it)|^2dt.

Choose P_X=ceil(2X exp(C sqrt(log X))). Missing coefficients lie entirely
in the Gaussian tail, so on the physical shell
|F-V_(P_X)|<=X^(1-C^2/(2tau)+o(1)). This exact choice also ensures
P_X=X^(1+o(1)); the author's lower bound on P_X alone did not ensure it.

for every fixed1/2<sigma<1 and every finite kappa.

Indeed at t=a/log P, uniformly for a in[5pi/6,7pi/6], ordinary PNT yields

    sum_(p<=P)p^(-sigma-ia/log P)
      =P^(1-sigma)/log P [e^(-ia)/(1-sigma)+o(1)].

The Euler logarithm is the negative real part of this sum plus O_sigma(1).
Its small-prime factors are bounded and nonzero. Integration over this
height interval proves

    ||e^(-sigma u)V_P||_2 >= C_(sigma,tau)(log P)^(-1/2)
                exp(P^(1-sigma)/(2(1-sigma)log P)).

Only pi(x)~x/log x is imported, as supplied by

Critic audit30 proves the decisive scope refinement. Uniformly in P,
|V_P(u)|<=C_tau e^u for u>=0 and <=C_tau exp(-u^2/(2tau)) for u<=0.
Hence for every fixed T>0,

    ||1_(u<=T log P)e^(-sigma u)V_P||_2=O(P^(T(1-sigma))),
    ||1_(u>T log P)e^(-sigma u)V_P||_2/||e^(-sigma u)V_P||_2 ->1.

    (V_P)_I=b_I-A_IL A_LL^-1 b_L.

The Schur feedback is exactly zero, but the past injection is not. The
generic norm of A_LL^-1 is product_p(1-p^-sigma)^-1, again superpolynomial

objections without reversing their valid quadratic inequalities.

## 6. The other three first tests

**W52-14, determinant-line H stimulus: scoped failure of the raw object.** The actual JN source is a complete signed sesquilinear sum with b(pi)conjugate(b(pi')), the CRT phase, h-characters of exponent3, mark exponents2 and4, both full pre-Fourier projectors, original rooted mark arrays and distinct-norm deletion. The card supplied no chain complex, determinant line, pair of valid native factorizations, transition map, or identified live positivity assertion. Those cannot be inferred from the word determinant. I therefore did not substitute an invented matrix and claim a native H counterexample. This first structure test leaves the raw recipe incoherent; the broad possibility of a properly defined factorization remains untested. No phase, mask, sign, mean subtraction or outside normalization was altered.

**W52-30, independent terminal leaves: tested, no new theorem credit.** For independent complex terminal errors |z_j|<=1, the exact scalar dual is sup|sum c_j z_j|=sum|c_j|, attained by phase alignment. An SDP encoding only those independent constraints cannot improve this optimum. But the arithmetic leaves are not all independent: G92's exact N=20196,p=17,m=18 fiber has u=65,66 and opposite principal signs, so its merged coefficient is0 while the independent leaf price is2. For chi modulo4 it is-1, and for the quartic chi modulo5 it is i, with the appropriate natural zero on the other term. The checks reproduce all three. The inference from the free-leaf dual to an arithmetic lower bound is invalid. A correct optimization must merge integer states first and impose actual arithmetic relations, leading back to W8/W14. This is a recovery of the existing G92 distinction, not a fourth development or an alleged failure of all SDP methods.

The exact depth-two screen, retaining every terminal leaf, is

    R(N,1)=1-sum_(p<=N)chi(p)
       +sum_(p<ell,p*ell<=N)chi(p)chi(ell)R(floor(N/(p*ell)),ell).

The independent terminal-error optimum is the number of q-unit prime pairs in this last sum. For N=30 and principal chi there are seven pairs: (2,3),(2,5),(2,7),(2,11),(2,13),(3,5),(3,7). The first true leaf is0 and the other six are1, so the exact expression is1-10+6=-3. The free error budget is7; it is not an estimate of the true leaf sum's cancellation. This small full tree identifies the missing information as relations between actual terminal values, not a better optimization of independent discs.

**W52-22, complex line bundle on the divisor hull: tested flatness, no gain.** On the q-unit squarefree divisor graph, the edge n->pn has multiplier chi(p). Products around every legal multiplicative square agree: chi(p)chi(ell)=chi(ell)chi(p)=chi(pell). The gauge g(n)=chi(n) trivializes this cocycle; it has modulus one on this support. Directions with chi(p)=0 are deleted as zero-weight directions, never divided by. The product cutoff is a diagonal support restriction and survives the gauge. Thus this bare bundle supplies no curvature or favorable geometric price; the signed parity and cutoff readout remain. This is an ordinary multiplicative-square calculation, not a simplification of JN's additive phases or its projectors. It leaves a different, explicitly coupled geometric construction open.
