The mathematical arguments were checked directly; no claim is made to have rerun absent files.

## 5. Brainstorming coverage and original development

Documents 03–04 retain **all 26 original families, three additional families and 109 stable child IDs**. The source crosswalk covers the original 21 named constructions and seven geometry branches as well as all four brainstorming groups. It includes proof ideas, restricted estimates, alternatives, failures, rejected shortcuts and expensive high-upside branches.

Semantic deduplication is at the level of objects and implications. The common ordinary-mean formulations are merged; finite incidence remains distinct from the infinite trace. The two completed prime criteria are proved equivalent. H, full physical covariance and direct theta pairing remain distinct until a valid kernel comparison exists. Rational Möbius energy and ideal triple energy likewise have no assumed norm equivalence.

**Pass 1, after the mathematical audits:** six developed attacks use the new state—small-gcd relative-conductor switching; core-direction calibration/two-slot cumulants; an exact partition joining paid sextic sectors; common-completed finite incidence on its proved corridor with a signed-before-Cauchy child; the full Möbius shift kernel; and the physical principal-cube Type I/C–C comparison.

**Pass 2, renewed breadth:** five changed constructions—continuum dilations; arithmetic-span wavelets; block-weight source resolvents; known-zero-inner-factor Hardy targets; and height-adaptive Cayley anchors. The exact log/derivative criterion merger is an additional cross-front result. Each has a first missing lemma, a decisive small calculation and a stop or fallback condition in document 03. New proven consequences were promoted into T08–T10 and A07/A11/A14/A15 rather than left inside speculative prose.

Priorities changed because the objects changed. Small-gcd full covariance is now first; H remains a separate second attack; frozen-dyad Möbius energy protects a genuinely different third mechanism. Completed means, compact-profile triple energy and the complete signed cubic route are immediate alternatives. Quadratic reconstruction, calibrated probes, residue approximation, exact operators and analytic geometry remain represented with precise gates.

## 6. Independent checks and reproducibility

The review was divided into cubic/completion/source, sextic/full-field, detector/geometry, and full-portfolio tasks, with cross-checks across those divisions. New T06–T07 algebra, actual prime-mark accounting, moving embeddings and endpoint allocation received an independent second read. T08's new corridor, full-profile summation and T10's continuum criterion also received an independent second read. Root checked the new auxiliary identities and the final cross-track consequences. This is a record of the work performed, not a substitute for the proofs supplied in documents 01–02.

The small checks directory is deliberately limited to reproducible finite evidence:

| File | What it establishes | What it does not establish |
|---|---|---|
| cubic_checks.py and cubic_exact_checks.json | 512 three-prime valuation tuples, 1,000 cube incidences including 784 shared-prime cases; eight exact mask-density identities; rational Type I and transfer budgets | An analytic mean or uniform cancellation |
| grok_transfer_certificate.py and grok_transfer_certificate_result.txt | Corrected outward interval certificate for all five conditional targets, including the global amplitude rectangle and other geometric margins | The full-probe hypothesis |
| inherited_H_geometry.py | Unchanged supplied exact certificate for the saved .12551 H geometry; used to check the new T07 tail exponents | A new [private research revision] result or a proof of H |
| verify_cycle20.py and verification_receipt.json | Exact new rational identities, finite counterexamples, corridor/exponent bookkeeping, all proof/family IDs, source and bundle consistency | Validation of inherited or new infinite analytic theorems by numerical testing |
| input_file_map.tsv, baseline_file_map.tsv, portfolio_source_crosswalk.json, claim_registry.json | Full input disposition, semantic aliases, stable claims and family/child coverage | Independent truth from agreement or metadata |

Run the scripts with Python 3; they use the standard library. The full interval certificate is the longest check. Its recorded output is the independently rerun corrected version. Small exact verification checks the receipt and relevant script hashes; it does not needlessly repeat every interval subdivision.

The original SA missing-script issue above is distinct from the supplied and executed GS certificate. Existing check receipts were read as source evidence; only independently executed or re-derived checks are described as such.

### External theorem checks

The primary source [dispersion.tex in the OpenAI cubic Gauss-sum preprint](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/main/preprints/An-unconditional-first-moment-for-cubic-Gauss-sums-September-25-2026/build/sections/dispersion.tex) was inspected on 2026-10-10. Its coefficient-distribution hypothesis and length range do not authorize SA's desired direct substitution. In the stated \(AB\asymp X\) range, \(X^{.32}\le B\le X^{.5}\); larger \(B\) uses a specified smooth-prime convolution family. Low-height logarithmic error is different from the power-saving averaged-height statement, which also restricts \(B\). The moving coefficient admits a resonant nonprincipal test, and raw substitution \(A=K,B=D\) would require \(D\le K\). A03 gives the exact surviving prime-convolution lemma and failed substitution. No new global saving is imported from this paper.

The [NIST DLMF Laguerre generating function, 18.12.13](https://dlmf.nist.gov/18.12#E13) was checked for A11. The displayed polynomial/generating-series expansions and cancellation are also derived in the auxiliary record. Other named spectral, Kloosterman or trace-function mechanisms remain proposals unless their exact inherited or supplied hypotheses are established here.

## 7. Reconciliation and compression

This integration is relative to the frozen cutoff, not a claim about any work Codex may have completed afterwards. On receipt, compare theorem statements, source definitions, constants and open gates to the current canonical workspace. Preserve a stronger valid newer result; replace a duplicate proof with a cross-reference; resolve a conflict at its first mathematical implication; update stable idea statuses without erasing useful rejected children.

The ZIP contains no original proof snapshot, duplicated agent manuscripts or repeated proofs. The proof and auxiliary records contain the newly checked mathematics; the portfolio and ledger carry a comparably substantial independent track. Compression removes repeated baseline material, duplicate proposals and rhetoric. The final size receipt gives both raw-combined and distinct-new-text denominators so the compression ratio is transparent. Completeness of proofs and the full idea tree took precedence over forcing a percentage cap.

             -sum_(j=1..K)(p chi(p))^-j G_(p,chi)(u+j log p).

Each character's inherited complete baseline b<1 kills the first term in

target strip; its homogeneous growth1 mode is excluded by the baseline.

retains ||F||^2+4|chi(2)|^2||D_2F||^2-4Re(chi(2)<D_2F,F>).

statement:
# [private research revision]: an actual late f3 complement and a reversal of renewal-band signs



## Current checkpoint and result

The new estimate concerns the WHOLE literal late complement at a fixed
power threshold, not another inherited gcd tail or a formal replacement
of the complete energy. It is proved directly on f3, using its exact
double Dirichlet zero at 1, the already accepted buffered Mertens bound
to price signed cores, and fixed-order PNT to evaluate two actual primes.
The main estimate below uses no bound for the full Gaussian field F or
its energy E1. It does use cancellation already supplied by the accepted
zero-free baseline through ordinary Möbius partial sums; avoiding a
Gaussian-field bound does not remove that baseline dependency.

For every fixed compact interval inside `1/3<rho<1/2`, the entire
`omega_(X^rho)(n)>=2` field has a NEGATIVE main term of order
`X/log^3 X`. Consequently, raising the threshold between two such fixed
powers gives a POSITIVE literal added band. This reverses the negative
subpower-threshold bands proved in [private research revision]. It is a concrete obstruction
to extending their inverse-log renewal law or their negative-band sign
through the late range. A threshold above X^(1/2) has a separately paid
Gaussian complement, giving a negative band across the final transition.

The proof, exact source comparison, complete signed Gram/return and
necessary finite checks are developed below. No new full-field power
estimate or zero-free constant is claimed. The current written endpoint
remains `c1=.12512`, with its formal replay obligations separate. A
positive buffer above `.87488` is mandatory in every Mertens use.

## 1. Literal statement

Fix tau>0 and write

    g(u)=(2 pi tau)^(-1/2) exp(-u^2/(2 tau)),
    f(n)=f3(n)=mu(rad(n/3^v3(n))),
    omega_z(n)=#{p>z:p divides n},
    F(x)=sum_n f(n)g(log(n/x)),
    T_z(x)=sum_(omega_z(n)<=1) f(n)g(log(n/x)),
    R_z(x)=F(x)-T_z(x)
          =sum_(omega_z(n)>=2) f(n)g(log(n/x)).        (C1)

All these sums retain every prime power and the full fixed Gaussian.
They converge absolutely before signs are used. The threshold z is
frozen with respect to x throughout the original shell `[X,2X]`.

Let

    C_f=9 log(2) product_(p>=5)(1-1/(p-1)^2)>0,
    B(rho)=2 log((1-rho)/rho)
                     -2/(1-rho)-1/(1-rho)^2.          (C2)

Fix `1/3<rho_0<=rho_1<1/2` and an admitted fixed Mertens exponent
`beta<1`. Set

    L=log X, delta=(1-2rho_1)/4,
    kappa=delta(1-beta)>0.

**Late-complement theorem.** Uniformly for rho in `[rho_0,rho_1]` and
the CLOSED shell `X<=x<=2X`, for all sufficiently large X,

    R_(X^rho)(x)
      = C_f exp(tau/2) B(rho) x/L^3
          + O_(tau,beta,rho_0,rho_1)(X/L^4
                                   +X^(1-kappa)L).   (C3)

One may keep the additional smaller error `O(X^(1-rho_0))` displayed
in the proof. It is absorbed in (C3), because kappa<rho_0. All constants
are independent of rho,x,X in this stated compact range. There is no
uniform assertion as rho approaches 1/3 or 1/2, or as beta approaches
the accepted boundary.

For every fixed `1/3<a<b<1/2`, (C3) and the exact identity in (C1) give

    T_(X^b)(x)-T_(X^a)(x)
      = C_f exp(tau/2)[B(a)-B(b)]x/L^3
            +O(X/L^4+X^(1-kappa)L),                  (C4)

using a compact range containing a,b. The coefficient in brackets is
strictly positive. This band theorem uses NO full-F or E1 estimate:
F cancels exactly before (C3) is applied.

A fully explicit example is a=3/8, b=2/5, so the threshold operation is
`z -> z^(16/15)`. Its leading coefficient in units `C_f exp(tau/2)` is

    B(3/8)-B(2/5)=79/225+2log(10/9)>0.                (C5)

By contrast, [private research revision] F36 proves a negative added band for the SAME fixed
logarithmic-threshold ratio 16/15 in its subpower range. The two claims
have disjoint hypotheses and are compatible. They demonstrate a real
change of sign in the actual arithmetic flow, not a sign inferred from
the nonnegative coefficient selector.

## 2. Accepted inputs and the actual double zero

Use the already accepted input

    sum_(n<=u) mu(n)=O_beta(u^beta), u>=1,            (C6)

with beta=.8749 as the inherited calibration, or
`beta=.87488+eta<1` with eta>0 FIXED under the current written endpoint.
The source of (C6) is the accepted buffered Mertens consequence of the
written zero-free baseline, recorded in [private research revision] Gaussian S3 and used
with the current `beta>1-c1` in current-proof G33. Thus the current
choice depends on the accepted c1 analytic input; the old fixed .8749
already suffices for this entire report. Neither choice is deduced
from a bound for F, from E1, or from this late-complement calculation.
No boundary-line Mertens bound is assumed. [private research revision] Gaussian S3--S5
directly prove from (C6), with all valuations retained,

    A_f(u):=sum_(n<=u) f(n)=O_beta(u^beta).           (C7)

This is used for the actual unmasked CORE coefficient f(r). It is never
asserted for a roughness-masked source. Its proof uses the absolutely
convergent h*mu convolution at beta>1/2, not an inverse of the prime-two
zero: explicitly, `|A_f(u)|<=C_beta u^beta sum_a |h(a)|a^(-beta)`.
Every cancellation estimate for cores in this report uses that same
accepted input (C6). All constants below may depend on the fixed beta
and its Mertens constant.

For Re s>1 the exact Dirichlet series is

    D(s)=sum_n f(n)n^(-s)=H(s)/zeta(s),
    H(s)=(1-3^(-s))^(-2)
           product_(p!=3)(1-2p^(-s))/(1-p^(-s))^2.  (C8)

The h-series for H converges absolutely on Re s>1/2; the finitely many
small-prime factors are kept literally. Equation (C7), by Abel
summation, continues D holomorphically to Re s>beta, with its fixed
derivatives on compact subsets. Near 1, the source identity (C8) and
the simple pole of zeta therefore give an exact DOUBLE zero:

    D(1)=D'(1)=0,       D''(1)=2C_f.                 (C9)

Here is the constant calculation. At p=2 the local H factor is
`(1-2z)/(1-z)^2`, z=2^(-s), whose derivative at s=1 is `4log2`.
The p=3 factor at 1 is 9/4. Each p>=5 contributes
`p(p-2)/(p-1)^2=1-1/(p-1)^2`. Thus H'(1)=C_f. The coefficient of s-1
in 1/zeta(s) is one, so D(s)=C_f(s-1)^2+O((s-1)^3), proving (C9).
Prime 3 and every power of 2 are essential to this calculation.

The reciprocal moments consequently converge in their ACTUAL signed
order and satisfy

    sum_r f(r)/r=0,
    sum_r f(r)log r/r=0,
    sum_r f(r)(log r)^2/r=2C_f.                      ([restricted research revision])

They are not absolutely convergent moments. Their convergence and all
tail estimates below follow from (C7). Replacing f by absolute values
before completing them would destroy the two cancellations.

The prime-distribution input is the already accepted fixed-order PNT
used in [private research revision] renewal F9, itself pinned to [private research revision]'s primary source:

    pi(v)-li(v)=O_N(v/(log v)^N), v>=2,              ([restricted research revision])

for every FIXED N. The proof below uses N=8, fixed before X varies.
There is no short-interval relative PNT, moving-order PNT, unproved
Hecke input or new provider contact.

## 3. Exact two-prime source in the Gaussian central range

Put `z=X^rho` and choose

    nu=(3rho_0-1)/2>0,       U=X^(1+nu).

For every rho in the compact range, U<z^3. If n<=U and omega_z(n)>=2,
then n has EXACTLY two distinct prime factors p<q above z, each with
valuation one. A third occurrence of a rough prime, including a repeated
one, would force n>z^3. Write n=rpq. Then

    r<=U/z^2<z,

so r automatically has no prime factor above z, and p,q do not divide r.
Since z>3 for all sufficiently large X,

    f(rpq)=f(r)f(p)f(q)=f(r).

This keeps every valuation in r; it is not a squarefree-core reduction.
Consequently, for n<=U, the original coefficient in R_z is EXACTLY

    sum_(p<q, p,q>z, pq|n) f(n/(pq)).                ([restricted research revision])

Extend the right side to the full Gaussian and define

    S_z(x)=sum_(z<p<q) sum_(r>=1) f(r)g(log(rpq/x)). ([restricted research revision])

The completion beyond U is paid, not asserted exact. For each n, the
number of selected prime pairs is at most omega(n)^2, hence at most a
fixed multiple of `(1+log n)^2`. The original coefficient is bounded
by one. Since `log(U/x)>=nu L-log2`, the complete Gaussian tail with
this polynomial/logarithmic multiplicity is O_A(X^(-A)) for any fixed
A>0, uniformly on the closed shell. For example, bound the multiplicity
by n^epsilon, dominate half of the Gaussian by its value beyond
`nu L/2`, and sum the other half with its finite tilted lattice moment.
The resulting fixed power of X times `exp(-c_(nu,tau)L^2)` is smaller
than every prescribed power. Thus

    R_z(x)=S_z(x)+O_A(X^(-A)).                       ([restricted research revision])

This accounts for all extra rough primes, all repeated rough prime
powers, and all labels introduced by extending ([restricted research revision]). There is no
uncapped finite-terminal assertion: the full tail is present in ([restricted research revision]).

The finite helper records explicit failures of ([restricted research revision]) ABOVE its range:
at z=5, n=7^2*11 and n=7*11*13, the global two-prime completion has the
wrong coefficient. Those are exactly the configurations priced by
([restricted research revision]), not silently ignored algebraic exceptions.

## 4. A signed large-core tail, with its complete prime-pair sum

Let `R=floor(X^delta)`. For y>0, Abel summation and (C7) give

    |sum_(r>R) f(r)g(log(r/y))|
      <= C_beta y^beta Q_beta(log(R/y)),             ([restricted research revision])
    Q_beta(s)=exp(beta s)g(s)
                    +integral_s^infinity exp(beta v)|g'(v)|dv.

The boundary `-A_f(R)g(log(R/y))` is included in ([restricted research revision]). Q_beta is bounded
for s<=0 and decreases faster than any exponential as s tends to +infinity.
No roughness predicate has been attached to the core in this argument;
the exact extension ([restricted research revision]) is what makes the core coefficient f(r).

For Y>=1, elementary divisor counting gives

    sum_(k>=1) d(k) k^(-beta) Q_beta(log(k/Y))
          <= C_(beta,tau) Y^(1-beta)log(2Y).         ([restricted research revision])

Indeed `sum_(k<=T)d(k)<=T(1+log T)`. Partial summation treats k<=Y.
For k>Y, use dyadic intervals and a fixed exponentially decaying bound
on Q_beta; the resulting geometric series and its logarithmic factor
converge. This proves ([restricted research revision]) with no prime-distribution input.

Apply ([restricted research revision]) at y=x/(pq), sum all actual p<q, and bound their positive
majorant by all ordered positive integer factors k=pq. With Y=x/R>=1,
([restricted research revision]) proves the complete error

    |sum_(p<q,p,q>z) sum_(r>R) f(r)g(log(rpq/x))|
          <= C x R^(beta-1)log(2x/R)
          <= C X^(1-kappa)L.                        ([restricted research revision])

This prices the whole signed large-core tail, including all prime-pair
heights and the core endpoint. It is useful for the present asymptotic,
not itself a new Mertens exponent or the main new theorem.

## 5. Uniform two-prime PNT, its diagonal and exact density

For retained r<=R put y=x/r. Thus

    X^(1-delta)<=y<=2X,  z>=X^rho_0,
    y/z^2>=X^(1-delta-2rho_1).

The last exponent is positive. Define the unordered prime kernel

    P_z(y)=sum_(z<p<q) g(log(pq/y)).

First replace it by half the ordered p,q sum. The exact subtracted
p=q diagonal, after summing all retained cores, has absolute size at
most

    (1/2)sum_(p>z) sum_(r>=1) g(log(rp^2/x))
      <= C_tau x sum_(p>z)p^(-2)
      <= C_tau X/z.                                ([restricted research revision])

Here the complete Gaussian lattice bound `sum_r g(log(r/u))<=C_tau u`
holds for all u>0, as proved in [private research revision] renewal F17. Thus the diagonal
is paid even at small scales and with all valuations in r.

For completeness, the following Stieltjes estimate justifies both
prime replacements with their sharp lower endpoint. Put

    H_1(s)=exp(s)g(s)+integral_s^infinity exp(v)|g'(v)|dv.

For fixed p>z, ([restricted research revision]), integration by parts on `(z,infinity)`, and
`log v>=rho_0 L` give

    |sum_(q>z)g(log(pq/y))
       -integral_z^infinity g(log(pv/y))dv/log v|
       <= C_N (y/p)L^(-N)H_1(log(pz/y)).              ([restricted research revision])

The boundary is `-[pi(z)-li(z)]g(log(pz/y))`; it is bounded by the
first term in H_1 and includes the case in which z is itself prime.
The endpoint at infinity is zero. H_1 is bounded on the negative axis
and rapidly decreasing on the positive axis. Bounding primes by
integers therefore gives

    sum_(p>z) p^(-1)H_1(log(pz/y))
         <= C[1+log_+(y/z^2)]<=C L.                 ([restricted research revision])

This follows by the harmonic sum up to y/z and an exponentially
decaying majorant above it. The analogous replacement of the outer
prime sum in the already continuous inner integral is bounded, after
Fubini, by

    C_N y L^(-N) integral_z^infinity
               H_1(log(vz/y))dv/[v log v]
       <= C_N y L^(1-N).

The last inequality uses the same harmonic integral and rapidly
decaying tail as ([restricted research revision]), and `1/log v<=1` for sufficiently large X.
Thus the two-prime error is at most `C_N y L^(1-N)`. Summing the
retained cores absolutely at this already priced PNT step costs only
`sum_(r<=R)1/r=O(L)`. With N=8 the TOTAL error is `O(X/L^6)`.
Both prime errors, their actual lower endpoints, and their interaction
are included; there is no use of independent prime signs.

The continuous ordered-pair integral can be evaluated exactly. Put
`t=log z=rho L`, `A=log y+w`. With `s=log u`, `log v=A-s`, the
Jacobian is `du dv=y exp(w) ds dw`. Its interior integral is

    (1/2)integral_t^(A-t) ds/[s(A-s)]
         =phi_t(A):=A^(-1)log((A-t)/t),  A>2t,       ([restricted research revision])

and zero when A<=2t. Consequently, after ([restricted research revision]), ([restricted research revision])--([restricted research revision]),

    R_z(x)=x integral_R exp(w)g(w)
             sum_(r<=R) f(r)/r phi_t(log x+w-log r)dw
          +O(X^(1-kappa)L+X/z+X/L^6)+O_A(X^(-A)).   ([restricted research revision])

This formula keeps the literal ordered-pair normalization and its
removed p=q diagonal. It is a derived source estimate, not a change
of the Gaussian kernel or an identification with the earlier SP source.

## 6. Signed Taylor completion; proof of the negative main term

Take W=delta L. For |w|<=W and r<=R, the arguments in ([restricted research revision]) obey

    log x+w-log r >= (1-2delta)L > 2rho_1 L.

All derivatives up to order three of phi_t on this corridor satisfy

    |phi_t^(j)(a)|<=C_(rho_0,rho_1,j)L^(-1-j).       ([restricted research revision])

This follows directly by scaling a=L u, t=L rho; the scaled compact
corridor stays a fixed positive distance above u=2rho. The original
cutoff definition phi=0 below 2t is not analytically continued across
its boundary.

Globally phi_t(a), defined by ([restricted research revision]) and zero below 2t, is bounded by
C/t. Therefore the WHOLE discarded |w|>W portion of ([restricted research revision]), even after
the absolute harmonic core sum, is bounded by a fixed power of X,L
times `exp(-c_(delta,tau)L^2)`. This pays both Gaussian ends before
the Taylor argument and does not extend a rational denominator across
a pole or a support boundary.

Set A=log x+w and v=log r in the retained integral. Write

    phi_t(A-v)=phi_t(A)-v phi_t'(A)
                  +(v^2/2)phi_t''(A)+e_A(v).

On 0<=v<=log R, Taylor's theorem and ([restricted research revision]) give

    |e_A(v)|<=C v^3/L^4,
    |e_A'(v)|<=C v^2/L^4.                           ([restricted research revision])

It would be WRONG to sum this error using `sum |f(r)|/r`; that would
erase the useful cancellation. Apply Abel summation instead:

    sum_(r<=R) f(r)e_A(log r)/r
      = A_f(R)e_A(log R)/R
        -integral_1^R A_f(u)
             [e_A'(log u)-e_A(log u)]du/u^2.         ([restricted research revision])

Both the endpoint and the integral are `O_(beta)(L^(-4))`, since
`sup_(v>=0) exp(-(1-beta)v)v^3` and
`integral_0^infinity exp(-(1-beta)v)(v^2+v^3)dv` are finite.
This is uniform in w,rho in the retained corridor. This second signed
Abel step, not a positive Taylor estimate, is essential.

Complete the three polynomial moments before evaluating them. Equation
(C7) gives, for each fixed j=0,1,2,

    |sum_(r>R) f(r)(log r)^j/r|
       <= C_(beta,j) R^(beta-1)[1+(log R)^j].        ([restricted research revision])

After multiplication by phi_t^(j), their combined error is at most
`C R^(beta-1)/L`. Inserting the exact moments ([restricted research revision]), the j=0 and j=1
terms vanish and the surviving term is

    sum_(r<=R) f(r)/r phi_t(A-log r)
       = C_f phi_t''(A)+O(L^(-4)+R^(beta-1)/L).      ([restricted research revision])

The positive 2C_f second moment meets the NEGATIVE curvature of the
actual two-prime density. There is no independent-sign premise and no
use of an unknown full energy in this cancellation.

Finally the tilted Gaussian has exact mass exp(tau/2) and finite first
absolute moment. Since log x=L+O(1) and phi_t''' is O(L^(-4)), ([restricted research revision])
and the already paid tails imply

    integral_(-W)^W exp(w)g(w)phi_t''(log x+w)dw
       =exp(tau/2)phi_t''(L)+O_tau(L^(-4)).          ([restricted research revision])

Direct differentiation gives

    phi_t''(A)=2log((A-t)/t)/A^3
                   -2/[A^2(A-t)]-1/[A(A-t)^2],
    phi_(rho L)''(L)=L^(-3)B(rho).                  ([restricted research revision])

Equations ([restricted research revision]), ([restricted research revision])--([restricted research revision]) prove (C3), with every core, prime power,
prime diagonal, sharp endpoint and Gaussian end accounted for.

Here is the complete error ledger, before convenient absorption:

| Source | Uniform field cost |
| --- | --- |
| Actual/completed source above U<z^3 | O_A(X^(-A)) for any fixed A |
| All signed cores r>R | O(X^(1-kappa)L) |
| Prime-pair p=q diagonal | O(X/z) |
| Both PNT replacements, N=8 fixed | O(X/L^6) |
| Full omitted tilted-Gaussian ends | O_A(X^(-A)) |
| Signed Taylor remainder | O(X/L^4) |
| Three signed moment completions | O(X^(1-kappa)/L) |
| Frozen-shell/tilted-Gaussian replacement | O(X/L^4) |

All constants are allowed to depend on the fixed compact rho interval,
tau,beta and the fixed accepted PNT constant. This ledger contains no
growing-order estimate or unsupported limit interchange.

## 7. Actual signs and the terminal Gaussian complement

Let u=(1-rho)/rho. For 1/3<rho<1/2, 1<u<2 and

    B(rho)=2log u-3-4/u-1/u^2.

Its derivative with respect to u is positive, and its maximum in this
range is `2log2-21/4<0`. Equivalently,

    B'(rho)=-2/(1-rho)-2/rho
                       -2/(1-rho)^2-2/(1-rho)^3<0. ([restricted research revision])

Thus R_(X^rho)(x) is eventually negative uniformly on the whole shell,
and the literal band (C4) is eventually positive. These are signs of
the complete actual fields, not of individual prime jumps.

For the explicit example,

    B(3/8)=2log(5/3)-144/25,
    B(2/5)=2log(3/2)-55/9,

which proves (C5) algebraically. At rho=2/5 the actual prefix, if its
leading term is obtained using the accepted bound for F, has coefficient
`C_f[55/9-2log(3/2)]`. Extrapolating the [private research revision] subpower formula would
instead give `C_f*(5/2)*exp(-gamma_E)`, because its product constant is
`3 exp(-gamma_E) product_(p>=5)(1-1/(p-1)^2)`. These are plainly different.
No such extrapolation was authorized by [private research revision]; the present calculation
identifies its concrete late-range failure and the reversed band sign.

For every fixed b>1/2, the source condition omega_(X^b)(n)>=2 forces
`n>X^(2b)`. The full Gaussian lattice tail therefore gives

    R_(X^b)(x)=O_A(X^(-A))                           ([restricted research revision])

for any fixed A, uniformly on [X,2X]. This is an approximate terminal
statement with its whole tail paid, not a finite exact cutoff of the
uncapped source. It is independent of a full-F bound.

Consequently, for fixed 1/3<a<1/2<b, the actual added band across the
half-power transition satisfies

    T_(X^b)-T_(X^a)=R_(X^a)-R_(X^b)
      =C_f exp(tau/2)B(a)x/L^3
                         +O(X/L^4+X^(1-kappa)L),    ([restricted research revision])

and is eventually NEGATIVE. Thus a complete finite portion of the late
flow has positive bands inside the two-prime range and a negative band
when the last rough-prime pair becomes Gaussian-negligible. A uniform
negative-drift argument extending the earlier subpower regime cannot
describe these actual coefficients.

No assertion is made at rho=1/2 itself or in a shrinking neighborhood
of it. There the available core length and the support edge of phi_t
meet, so the uniform corridor used in ([restricted research revision]) disappears. This is a real
remaining transition problem, not a value obtained by taking a limit
in (C3). Similarly, the proof does not cross rho=1/3, where a third
rough-prime occurrence can enter the original Gaussian central range.

## 8. Complete joint prefix/complement and Gram return

For this section alone, the accepted full-field baseline is used and
identified explicitly. Equation (C7), by ordinary Gaussian Abel
summation, gives pointwise `F(x)=O_(beta,tau)(X^beta)` and hence the
same bound for its shell norm. It follows from the EXACT identity
T_z=F-R_z and (C3) that

    T_(X^rho)(x)
      =-C_f exp(tau/2)B(rho)x/L^3
             +O(X/L^4+X^(1-kappa)L+X^beta).          ([restricted research revision])

This is not an independent improvement of F. Unlike (C3), (C4) and
([restricted research revision]), this prefix assertion uses that accepted full-field bound.

To expose every ordered interaction, choose the literal disjoint
partition at a=3/8, b=2/5, c=3/5:

    C_0=T_(X^a),
    C_1=T_(X^b)-T_(X^a),
    C_2=T_(X^c)-T_(X^b),
    C_3=R_(X^c).

These are original f(n) coefficients times disjoint 0/1 masks, with
all prime powers. Their sum is EXACTLY F. Define the common field

    V_X(x)=C_f exp(tau/2)x/L^3,
    N_X^2=||V_X||_[X,2X]^2
         =(3/2)C_f^2 exp(tau)X^2/L^6,
    (b_0,b_1,b_2,b_3)
      =(-B(a), B(a)-B(b), B(b), 0).                 ([restricted research revision])

The first two coefficients are positive; the third is negative;
their sum is zero. The new direct arithmetic estimates give C_1,C_2
and the negligible C_3 at these signs, without full F. C_0 uses ([restricted research revision]).
For this fixed partition,

    ||C_i-b_i V_X|| <= C epsilon_X N_X,
    <C_i,C_j>=[b_i b_j+O(epsilon_X)]N_X^2,           ([restricted research revision])
    epsilon_X=L^(-1)+X^(-kappa)L^4+X^(beta-1)L^3.

Every i,j pair, including both ordered mixed directions, is included.
In particular the C_0,C_1 leading cross term is POSITIVE, whereas both
have negative leading cross terms with C_2. There is no positivity
claim about arbitrary depth submasks. The complete covariance is the
sum of this ENTIRE Gram, not the sum of selected favorable entries.

For any of the actual coefficient pieces c_i(n), absolute convergence
gives exactly

    <C_i,C_j>=sum_(m,n) c_i(m)c_j(n)K_X(m,n),         ([restricted research revision])

with current-proof G22's ORIGINAL Gaussian kernel. Each own true
diagonal is O_tau(X); cross diagonals between the disjoint pieces
vanish because their coefficient supports are disjoint. In particular,
with the ORIGINAL full true diagonal Delta_all,

    Q_off(X)=sum_(0<=i,j<=3)<C_i,C_j>-Delta_all(X).

No negative off-diagonal term is deleted. For an explicit two-height
readout, fix sigma>1 and put `D_i(s)=sum_n c_i(n)n^(-s)`, with X and
all masks frozen. Absolute convergence gives

    <C_i,C_j>=(2pi)^(-2) integral_R integral_R
      exp(tau(sigma-it_1)^2/2) exp(tau(sigma+it_2)^2/2)
      conjugate(D_i(sigma+it_1)) D_j(sigma+it_2)
      [integral_X^(2X) x^(2sigma+i(t_2-t_1))dx/x]
      dt_1 dt_2.

The two original Gaussian height densities and both heights are
retained over the full real lines. At sigma>1, |D_i|<=zeta(sigma),
so both Gaussian integrals converge absolutely without an unpriced
height truncation. No diagonal-height substitution is used. These
moving masked series are not substituted for the fixed full detector
in the zero-exclusion argument.

For the actual two-part split T_z,R_z, put

    a_X=||T_z||, b_X=||R_z||,
    rho_X=Re<T_z,R_z>/(a_X b_X).

The new source theorem supplies `a_X,b_X` comparable to X/L^3 after
the explicitly stated accepted baseline for F. The exact identity is

    ||F||^2=(a_X-b_X)^2+2a_X b_X(1+rho_X).           ([restricted research revision])

Therefore a proposed full target `||F||<<_epsilon X^(gamma+epsilon)`,
with 1/2<gamma<.87488, is equivalent to BOTH requirements

    |a_X-b_X| <<_epsilon X^(gamma+epsilon),
    1+rho_X <<_epsilon X^(2gamma-2+epsilon)L^6,       ([restricted research revision])

after renaming epsilon. Necessity follows from the nonnegative terms
of ([restricted research revision]); sufficiency uses a_X,b_X comparable to X/L^3 and the same
identity. If proving sufficiency independently of the baseline, the
first bound itself makes a_X comparable to the directly known positive
b_X from (C3).
The known beta only supplies the corresponding baseline rates, not
the improved gamma rates. There is no circular use of E1 to prove a
new value of gamma.

The leading Gram in ([restricted research revision]) has a null sum direction, but its error is
not power-small at the requested scale. Even the field error X/L^4
is larger than X^gamma for every fixed gamma<1. Pairing that error
with a full partial field of size X/L^3 gives scalar error at scale
X^2/L^7; both ordered mixed errors and the error square must remain.
Neither a leading-rank cancellation nor deleting the positive C_0,C_1
cross term meets ([restricted research revision]).

If ([restricted research revision]) were actually improved, ([restricted research revision]), the true O(X) diagonal, and
current-proof G29--G31 would return the full fixed-field moment and
zero exclusion. Those accepted whole-field equivalences are applied
ONLY AFTER complete reconstruction of F. They do not transfer the
individual rough masks to the coprime pair or original four-factor
source. No high-gcd/radical signed-submask estimate is imported into
C_0,C_1,C_2 or R_z.

## 9. Novelty boundary, strongest obstruction and next action

The inspected [private research revision] renewal theorem explicitly stopped at
`log z<=log X/(1000loglog X)` and left the fixed-power late flow open.
Its finite-prime smooth core has a SIMPLE local zero and a first
derivative main term. The new fixed-power complement uses the FULL
unmasked core, whose Dirichlet series has a DOUBLE zero: the local
prime-two zero combines with the zeta reciprocal. The unrestricted
core becomes legitimate only after the exact two-prime source check
below z^3 and its fully paid Gaussian completion. This distinction is
the new source-specific mechanism; it is not a masked inheritance
from either the old renewal theorem or the full energy.

[private research revision] Gaussian S9--S23 and W37 R37.8 already pay ordinary/radical
high-overlap sectors. They do not imply the present masked source
estimate, nor does (C3) claim additional low-gcd coverage. W37 R37.4
has different d,e,ell boundary coefficients; its exact prime adapter
is not substituted for the present n,r,p,q source. The prior two-adic
representations likewise do not evaluate this late two-prime density.
No literature-priority claim is made; the novelty claim is scoped to
the inspected maintained record and the named unpaid continuation.

The strongest cheap objection is the possible loss of the reciprocal
core cancellation under absolute Taylor errors. Equations ([restricted research revision])--([restricted research revision])
resolve it using the actual partial sums (C7). The other dangerous
shortcut would declare the two-prime completion globally exact;
([restricted research revision])--([restricted research revision]) and the finite outside-range witnesses explicitly prevent
that error. The sign reversal then follows from an evaluated curvature,
not a random-phase heuristic or a positivity step.

What remains unpaid is the POWER precision of the complete joint norm,
not the sign or size of these late bands. A next useful calculation
would treat the shrinking transition near rho=1/2 with the actual
incomplete reciprocal moments and its Gaussian edge, or the full
joint residual in ([restricted research revision]). Such a calculation must preserve the finite
core boundary where the complete moments in ([restricted research revision]) cannot yet be used.
The present theorem rules out continuing the subpower negative-band
law as the needed stability principle. Repeating the Mertens tail
([restricted research revision]), or extending a fixed finite asymptotic expansion by assertion,
would not address the missing power-scale cancellation.

## 10. Evidence, scope and handoff

Read sources: current-proof G31--G36 and the f3/kernel definitions;
the complete [private research revision] attempt delta and maintained attempt index;
the literal [private research revision] renewal report including its source/PNT/moment
and whole-complement sections; the actual f_r/Mertens proof in the
[private research revision] Gaussian report; W37 R37.4/R37.8 and their source limitations.
Full byte counts and hashes are saved in `source-evidence.json`.

The small owned `check_source.py` verifies ([restricted research revision]) on every n<z^3 for
six finite thresholds, retaining all valuations: all 50,993 checked
coefficients agree, including 4,639 nonzero two-prime coefficients.
It also records the
two explicit failures outside that range, evaluates the exact positive
band formula (C5) with labeled finite precision, and binds the read
sources. This is algebra/endpoint evidence, not a numerical proof of
the asymptotic sign or of a stronger full energy. The mathematical
evidence for those scoped claims is the derivation (C6)--([restricted research revision]).

Author verdict: (C3)--(C5) and ([restricted research revision])--([restricted research revision]) are proved under the stated
accepted inputs, pending the controller's independent review. They
evaluate a previously unpaid literal late complement and establish
an actual band-sign reversal, with the full return and its limitation
in ([restricted research revision])--([restricted research revision]). They do not improve c1.

No providers, children, canonical writes, tracker/Git changes or
publication were used. Only this owned tree was written after the
fresh exact sentinel was acquired. Both earlier [private research revision] owned results
remain frozen. The final handoff binds the full readback and exact
hashes of this report and its evidence. Writing stops explicitly before
release of only this new claim.

## A11. One corrected coefficient criterion, with two arithmetic presentations

**PROVED exact criteria and their equivalence; the coefficient bounds are OPEN.** Sources: BA D12; BB R13. The explicit derivative merger below is new in this integration.

Put \(Z_0(s)=(s-1)\zeta(s)\), fix \(0<b<1\), and map the disk by
\[
 s_b(z)=b+(2-b)\frac{1+z}{1-z},\qquad
 \log\frac{Z_0(s_b(z))}{Z_0(2)}
       =\sum_{n\ge1}\ell_n(b)z^n
\]
near zero. Then
\[
 \limsup|\ell_n(b)|^{1/n}\le1
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \zeta(s)\ne0\quad(\Re s>b,\ s\ne1). \tag{A11.1}
\]
If the coefficients are subexponential, exponentiating their holomorphic disk series agrees with \(Z_0(s_b(z))/Z_0(2)\) by analytic continuation and cannot vanish. Conversely, a nonzero holomorphic function on the simply connected half-plane has a holomorphic logarithm. The canceled pole has \(Z_0(1)=1\).

Set \(\lambda=2(2-b)\), \(A=\lambda-1=3-2b\), and
\[
 P_n(x)=\sum_{k=1}^n\binom{n-1}{k-1}\frac{(-x)^k}{k!},\quad
 e^{-xz/(1-z)}=1+\sum_{n\ge1}P_n(x)z^n.
\]
The Euler expansion at \(s=2\) gives
\[
 \ell_n(b)=\frac{(-1)^{n+1}A^n+1}{n}
     +\sum_{p,m\ge1}\frac{p^{-2m}}m P_n(\lambda m\log p). \tag{A11.2}
\]
For each fixed \(n\) these sums converge absolutely. If
\(d\Pi=\sum_{p,m\ge1}m^{-1}\delta_{p^m}\), substitution \(t=\log x\) and integration of its finite polynomial show
\[
 \int_1^\infty x^{-2}P_n(\lambda\log x)\frac{dx}{\log x}
 =\sum_{k=1}^n\binom{n-1}{k-1}\frac{(-\lambda)^k}{k}
 =\frac{(-A)^n-1}{n}.
\]
The integrand is finite at the lower endpoint because \(P_n(\lambda\log x)=O(\log x)\). Hence the exponential principal term cancels *exactly*:
\[
 \boxed{\ell_n(b)=\int_1^\infty x^{-2}P_n(\lambda\log x)
              \left(d\Pi(x)-\frac{dx}{\log x}\right).} \tag{A11.3}
\]
The required bound is \(O_\delta(e^{\delta n})\) for every \(\delta>0\).
The accepted region gives only the radius
\[
 r_0=(2-b_0)/(2+b_0-2b),\qquad
 \limsup|\ell_n(b)|^{1/n}\le r_0^{-1}
\]
when \(b<b_0\); at \(b=.87449\) this is about \(1.00070508\), not one.

For a general anchor \(r>1-b\), let \(s(z)=b+r(1+z)/(1-z)\), and let \(a_n\) be the coefficients of \(s'(z)\xi'/\xi(s(z))\). Exactly the same analytic-continuation argument, now using the nonremovable logarithmic pole of a zero, proves
\[
 \limsup|a_n|^{1/n}\le1\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
                 \xi(s)\ne0\quad(\Re s>b). \tag{A11.4}
\]
The Laguerre generating function yields the prime part
\[
 a_n^{\rm prime}=-2r\sum_{m\ge2}\Lambda(m)m^{-b-r}
                  L_n^{(1)}(2r\log m). \tag{A11.5}
\]
It must be combined with the coefficients of
\[
 s'(z)\left\{\frac1{s(z)}+\frac1{s(z)-1}
       -\tfrac12\log\pi+\tfrac12\psi(s(z)/2)\right\}. \tag{A11.6}
\]
The zeta pole maps to \(z_1=(1-b-r)/(1-b+r)\in(-1,0)\). Its raw prime contribution is \(+z_1^{-n-1}\); \(s'/(s-1)\) contributes \(-z_1^{-n-1}\), plus its boundary term \(1/(1-z)\). The raw prime coefficients alone therefore cannot be the subexponential target, even under RH.

**New exact merger.** At \(r=2-b\), \(\xi(s)=\tfrac12s\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)Z_0(s)\). Therefore
\[
 a_n=(n+1)\ell_{n+1}(b)
 +[z^n]\,s_b'(z)\{1/s_b(z)-\tfrac12\log\pi+\tfrac12\psi(s_b(z)/2)\}.
 \tag{A11.7}
\]
The added function is holomorphic on the disk because \(\Re s_b>b>0\), so its coefficients are subexponential. Multiplication by \(n+1\) changes no exponential growth rate. The density-subtracted log criterion and the completed Laguerre criterion are thus equivalent arithmetic presentations at this anchor, not independent conjectural gains.

A zero \(\rho=\beta+i\gamma\) maps to
\[
 z_\rho=\frac{\rho-b-r}{\rho-b+r},\quad
 |z_\rho|^2=\frac{(\beta-b-r)^2+\gamma^2}{(\beta-b+r)^2+\gamma^2}.
\]
For fixed \(r\), its sensitivity exponent is
\(\log|z_\rho|^{-1}=2r(\beta-b)/\gamma^2+O_{b,r}(\gamma^{-4})\).
Degree of order \(\gamma^2/[r(\beta-b)]\) is needed even for order-one sensitivity, and individual coefficients can contain cancellation between zeros. A height-dependent anchor \(r\asymp|\gamma|\) changes this calibration but creates an additional uniform two-parameter coefficient problem; it is not supplied by the fixed-anchor criterion.

**New exact anchor optimization.** Put \(\delta=\beta-b>0\), and suppose \(\gamma\ne0\). The sensitivity at anchor \(r\) is
\[
 f(r)=\frac12\log\frac{(r+\delta)^2+\gamma^2}{(r-\delta)^2+\gamma^2},
\quad
 f'(r)=
 \frac{2\delta(\delta^2+\gamma^2-r^2)}
 {((r+\delta)^2+\gamma^2)((r-\delta)^2+\gamma^2)}.
 \tag{A11.8}
\]
The unique unconstrained maximum is \(r_*=\sqrt{\delta^2+\gamma^2}\), with
\[
 f(r_*)=\operatorname{artanh}(\delta/r_*)\sim\delta/|\gamma|.
\]
When \(r_*>1-b\), this is an admissible Euler anchor. Otherwise the admissible supremum occurs as \(r\downarrow1-b\). The displayed derivative proves both statements. At heights \(|\gamma|\asymp T\), the reciprocal sensitivity, which measures degree for order-one amplification of a *single zero's modulus*, changes from order \(T^2/(r\delta)\) for fixed \(r\) to \(T/\delta\). This does not prove finite-degree detection: contributions from different zeros can cancel, and a height-dependent anchor requires a bound uniform in both degree and \(r\), with the moving prime weights and gamma terms included. The case \(\gamma=0\) has a singularity at \(r=\delta\); a prospective zero with \(\beta\le1\) cannot make that point an admissible Euler anchor. The real interval \((0,1)\) is already zero-free. This is the proved calibration underlying portfolio N29.N1.
title: A11. One corrected coefficient criterion, with two arithmetic presentations

## 5. Insert the original C--C coefficient and sum the outside cubes

The actual source is

`C_k(c B^3)=beta(c) theta_c(k) xi(B) q_B`.

There is no `(B,k)` mask. Total-column coprimality is precisely
`(c,e)=(c,E)=(e,B)=(B,E)=1`; overlaps `(c,B)>1` and `(e,E)>1`
are allowed. Here B,E are the outside cube labels; the symbol
`E_*` below is a core scale, to avoid confusing them.

For the whole C--C part, CP23 has
`E(h)=mu(c)mu(e) q_R0 1_(R0|h)`. In CP24--CP25 set `h=R0 n`.
The factor q_R0 cancels its normalization, and
`eta(R0) bar eta(R0 n)=bar eta(n)` on its original support.
Consequently the exact C--C prefactor and kernel, in CP's normalization,
are

\[
\begin{split}
\frac{K(q_Bq_E)^4}{D^2}\xi(B)\overline{\xi(E)}
\sum_{n\ne0}\widehat R\!\left(\frac{K(q_Bq_E)^3q_n}{D^2}\right)
\sum_{\substack{c,e\ {\rm sf}\ (c,e)=1\\(c,E)=(e,B)=1}}
 &\sqrt{q_cq_e}\,\mu(c)\mu(e)\psi_n(c)\overline{\psi_n(e)}\\
 &\cdot\overline{W_0(q_cq_B^3/D)}W_0(q_eq_E^3/D).
\end{split}
\tag{SR12}
\]

The original nonunit-core restriction and finite unit/ray projectors
are understood. For estimates, the latter separate into their
prescribed finite fixed-character families and bounded row selectors.
All element rows are retained. The transformed zero row is absent
because the original coprime nonunit cores give a nonprincipal
character. We do not apply the nonprincipal identity to an added
principal unit pair.

For fixed B,E set

\[
 C_* =D/q_B^3,\qquad E_*=D/q_E^3,\qquad
 H=\frac{D^2}{K(q_Bq_E)^3}=\frac{C_*E_*}{K}.
\tag{SR13}
\]

The outside prefactor in SR12 is exactly `q_B q_E/H`. The opposite
deletions in SR9 are `R_1=E,R_2=B`. They do not introduce either
forbidden own-column exclusion. The original angular factors have
modulus one and may now be bounded in absolute value; no moving
angular L-function is used.

By SR1,

\[
\min(C_*,E_*)\ge D^\delta\max(K,D^\gamma),\qquad
\frac{H}{\max(C_*,E_*)}
 =\frac{\min(C_*,E_*)}{K}\ge D^\delta.
\tag{SR14}
\]

Thus SR9 applies with the original profiles, using a rapid positive
majorant for `|Rhat|`, with all row tails included. It pays this cube
pair by

\[
 \frac{q_Bq_E}{H}\,H C_*E_*D^\epsilon
 =\frac{D^{2+\epsilon}}{(q_Bq_E)^2}.
\tag{SR15}
\]

The complete sum over `q_B,q_E<=Lambda`, with `(B,E)=1` still in
place before positive bounds, is affordable since
`sum_B q_B^(-2)<infinity`. This proves the bound for the full
transformed core sums.

Here is the justification for the sharp original cutoff
`q_c,q_e>D^gamma`. SR14 implies that the removed low-core profiles
have argument at most `D^(-delta)`. Every required endpoint bound is
available for the *original* W0. For example, for each A,

\[
 \sum_{q_c\le D^\gamma}\sqrt{q_c}
       |W_0(q_c/C_*)|
 \ll_A D^{3\gamma/2-A\delta}.
\tag{SR16}
\]

The other absolute core sum is `O(D^(3/2))`. The row-majorant mass
is `O(H)`, cancelling the `H^(-1)` in the physical prefactor; and
`sum_{q_B,q_E<=Lambda}q_Bq_E << Lambda^4 <= D^(4/3)`.
Choose A after the desired error exponent and fixed delta. The
removed terms, including any algebraically added unit core, are
`O(D^(-N))` for any fixed N. Both-low terms are handled in the same
way. This is an estimate of the already transformed expression,
not a functional equation asserted for a principal row. It establishes
SR2 with the actual sharp core cutoff. No sharp common-profile
moment is being assumed. Large core and cube tails inside the stated
sector retain W0's rapid bounds; the sector does not include cube
labels exceeding Lambda.

statement:
## 3. The actual zeta failure and an independent stronger obstruction

### 3.1 Primary input and the author's bare normalization

I independently opened Johan Andersson's [arXiv:1010.0386](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1010.0386),
Theorem2 on PDF page2. It gives positive-lower-density vertical zeta
approximation to each continuous target on a compact empty-interior set
in .5<Re s<1 with connected complement, for each fixed positive error.
Only this stated theorem is imported. The visible v1 stamp is3 October2010;
the PDF title date is30 October2018. No literature-priority inference or
PDF-byte hash is manufactured from these dates or the web extraction.

Take I=[pi-delta,pi+delta], delta=1/40, s(theta)=2+R e^(i theta).
This simple compact arc has connected complement and lies in
[.6,.6+R delta^2/2] inside the universality strip. For each fixed M>=32,
the primary theorem supplies arbitrarily large t for which
zeta(s(theta)+it)=-M+e(theta), |e|<1 on the whole arc.

Absolute convergence at2 gives w=1/zeta(2+it), |w-1|<3/4, so
Re w>1/4 and |w|<7/4. For t>=40,
k=(s(theta)+it-1)/(1+it) has |k-1|<=R/40;
|w(k-1)|<1/16 and |wk|<2. Therefore

    Re[w k (-M+e)] < -M/4+M/16+2 <= -M/8.

The normalized negative mass is at least M/(320pi). Letting M vary
proves sup_t B(h_t)=infinity for P=(s-1)zeta. For each fixed budget,
bad heights have positive lower density after discarding t<40. There is
no quantitative relationship between M and the first such height here.
This disproves the bare sufficient budget without producing, assuming
or excluding any off-line zero. The anchor phase and pole-removing factor
were both paid; neither was replaced by1.

### 3.2 Critic theorem R40-E: every fixed finite Euler universe fails

The author's bare calculation explicitly leaves finite Euler products
untested. The following additional argument closes **all subsets of a
fixed finite prime set simultaneously**, including height-adaptive choices.
It still leaves genuinely unbounded prime universes or other multipliers
open. This strengthening belongs to this independent review.

Fix a finite set S of rational primes. For A subset S define
E_A(s)=product_(p in A)(1-p^-s), and

    h_(t,A)(z)=[(1+it+Rz)zeta(2+it+Rz)E_A(2+it+Rz)]
                       /[(1+it)zeta(2+it)E_A(2+it)].

Then

    sup_(t>=40) min_(A subset S) B(h_(t,A))=infinity. (R40.3)

Use the same fixed arc I. Put a_p=p^(-3/5) and define finite constants

    m=(1-R/40)/4 * product_S(1-a_p)/product_S(1+p^-2)>0,
    Q=7(1+R/40)/4 * product_S(1+a_p)/product_S(1-p^-2),
    D=R/(40-R)+R sum_S (log p)a_p/(1-a_p).

Let

    q_(t,A)(theta)=k_t(theta) w_t E_A(s(theta)+it)/E_A(2+it).

For every t>=40 and every A subset S, product triangle inequalities
give m<=|q|<=Q. The local factors never vanish on this arc. Differentiating
their logarithms along theta gives

    |d/dtheta arg q| <= D.                          (R40.4)

Indeed k'/k has modulus at most R/(40-R), each Euler term contributes
at most R(log p)a_p/(1-a_p), and both anchor factors are constant in
theta. An argument branch exists on the interval I; no global analytic
logarithm or zero-free half-plane is assumed.

Choose one integer N>D+80pi, fixed once S is fixed. On the arc prescribe
the continuous, nonvanishing target

    f_M(s)=M[-(s-2)/R]^N
          =M exp(iN(theta-pi)).

The same primary theorem gives a positive-lower-density set of t>=40
where |zeta(s+it)-f_M(s)|<1 uniformly. These heights are common to all
A; the target does not depend on A or the unknown anchor phase.
For each such pair (t,A), the phase
phi(theta)=N(theta-pi)+arg q_(t,A)(theta) is strictly increasing, with
N-D<=phi'<=N+D. Its total range has length greater than4pi. Consequently
it contains some complete phase interval [2pi/3+2kpi,4pi/3+2kpi].
The corresponding theta interval has length at least2pi/[3(N+D)].
On that interval cos phi<=-1/2. If M>=4Q/m, the actual boundary satisfies

    Re h_(t,A)(e^(i theta)) <= -Mm/2+Q <= -Mm/4.

Integration on that interval therefore gives, for EVERY A subset S,

    B(h_(t,A)) >= Mm/[12(N+D)].                    (R40.5)

The interval can depend on A; its length and lower bound do not. No
intersection of independently selected good-height sets is needed.
Since M is arbitrary, R40.3 follows, with positive lower density of
simultaneously bad heights for each fixed proposed budget. The proof
uses only the inspected universality theorem and the displayed bounds.

Thus a fixed finite Euler product, or switching among subsets of a
bounded prime universe, cannot repair this positivity route for zeta.
The constants m,Q,D depend on S; when S grows without bound with t,
this argument provides no uniform m or D and proves no such rejection.
It also does not reject all zero-preserving analytic normalizations,
or establish a corresponding universality theorem for the Hecke family.
The all-family proposal already needs zeta, so this zeta obstruction
is a necessary test of any proposed fixed-universe repair.

This is distinct from W24C's negative-prime-frequency test for a
constant-corrected logarithmic derivative on Re s>1. It is also distinct
from SC25's exact alternatives for a fractional-linear pole transform.
Their scoped failures and genuine escapes remain correct. The new
statement concerns the particular normalized holomorphic source above.

The return still requires the entire raw target

## 5. Full versus truncated allocation contraction

For a squarefree nonunit n and t|n,

    sum_(v|n,t|v) mu(v) log(q_n/q_v)
       = mu(t) sum_(z|n/t) mu(z) log(q_(n/t)/q_z)
       = mu(t) Lambda_K(n/t).                     (R24)

The unit cofactor contributes zero. The second side has the same
real Mobius/log coefficient; the two mu(t) factors multiply to
one. Hence completing ALL allowed allocations on both sides gives

    B_w(n,n')
       := sum_(v|n,v'|n') mu(v)mu(v') w((v,v'))
          log(q_n/q_v)log(q_n'/q_v')/(log q_n log q_n')

       = sum_(t|(n,n')) r_w(t)
          Lambda_K(n/t)Lambda_K(n'/t)
             /(log q_n log q_n').                 (R25)

This is BGC13=HA19. No sign, factorial, conjugate orientation or
root factor is missing. Ideals are ordered exactly as the original
two sides; there is no passage to unordered prime pairs.

On the actual far support q_n!=q_n', each nonzero cofactor is a
prime ideal because n,n' are squarefree. If n/t=p and n'/t=p'
then q_p!=q_p', so p and p' are distinct and coprime. It follows
that t=(n,n') is the unique possible surviving divisor. Thus R25
equals

    r_w(s) log(q_p)log(q_p')/(log(q_sp)log(q_sp')),
    n=s p, n'=s p', s=(n,n'), (s,pp')=1, q_p!=q_p'. (R26)

It is zero if the cofactors are not prime. Equal-norm conjugate
primes cannot create a second surviving orientation; the original
gap excludes them. Without that gap R25 is still correct, but the
unique-gcd simplification R26 is not the general diagonal formula.

The far selector in R26 is exactly
q_s |q_p-q_p'|>H0, equivalently
|q_p-q_p'|>floor(H0/q_s). This is equality of integer endpoint
conditions, not a smoothed replacement.

The native a(n), a(n'), row/mark factors, both short-source
coefficients, product profiles and original extension masks depend
on the full products after R2, not their allocation labels.
Therefore R25--26 multiply the actual decorated scalar unchanged.
This is original arithmetic, not an unweighted coefficient model.
It remains the EVALUATED auxiliary extension, not a theorem about
a redefined true core of sp and sp'.

For FIXED label sets V_1,V_2, the correct formula instead is

    B_w^(V_1,V_2)(n,n')
       = sum_(t|(n,n')) r_w(t)
          b_(1,t)(n/t)b_(2,t)(n'/t),                (R27)

with b as in R7, including the original log denominators. This is
HA28 and follows from the same exact substitution v=t z. The
second b is real for the stipulated indicator label sets; no
conjugation ambiguity occurs. If one were to introduce complex
label weights, the appropriate second-side conjugation would be
required, but neither reviewed theorem needs that extension.

Only for the FULL allowed label sets does

    b_(all,t)(m)=Lambda_K(m)/log(q_t q_m)            (R28)

reduce R27 to R25. One may not use BGC13/HA19 to identify a fixed
pressure-cell covariance with prime cofactors.

A decisive original-allocation check makes this distinction visible.
Take V_1=V_2={1}, w=1, and eligible squarefree composites
n=r p, n'=r p' with distinct-norm prime cofactors. Their unit-cell
allocation coefficient is exactly one: v=v'=1, each original
logarithmic ratio is one. The FULL coefficient R25 is zero,
since Lambda_K(rp)=Lambda_K(rp')=0. The missing nonunit allocation
terms provide that cancellation. For a nonunit cell containing
only r among the divisors, its paired coefficient is

    w(r) log(q_p)log(q_p')/(log(q_rp)log(q_rp')).     (R29)

It is nonzero when w(r)!=0. These are exact coefficient statements
on eligible support, not
energy lower bounds or assertions that every original array/window
is populated. They prove why the truncation correction matters.

Branch A's HA28 is therefore accepted as the required correction
to an otherwise overbroad pressure-cell use of HA19/HA20. Branch B
already states its contraction for the complete allocation sum;
no change to BGC13 itself is required. Its use as a falsification
test for any proposed cellwise estimate must respect R27.

        a(n)conj(a(m))(nm)^(-r)K_N(n,m).                 (R7)

      <<_r N^(1-2r)/G+N^(-2r).                         (R8)

The inherited Mellin identity can be checked directly for this same source. For a coefficient n, substitute u=nt in the integral of f_(1/t)(n)t^(z-1). It is

    n^(-z) integral_0^infinity
           exp(-n^(-1/2)u^(3/2)-iu^6)u^(z-1)du.

Initially absolute Fubini holds on Re z>3/2 with a small divisor buffer. Rotate clockwise by a fixed angle0<alpha<pi/12, using principal powers. The rotated sextic factor decays like exp(-c u^6), and the damping has nonnegative real exponent. On each compact set in Re z>0, expanding the damping once gives

    A0(z)n^(-z)+O_K(n^(-Re z-1/2)),

also locally with z derivatives and their logarithmic factors. Small and large arcs are paid by Re z>0 and the damping; the usual small fixed-angle argument near the unrotated edge supplies the large-arc limit. With |c(n)|<<_eta n^eta the summed error is normally holomorphic on Re z>1/2. Thus

          =A0(z)D_c(z)+E_p(z), E_p holomorphic for Re z>1/2. (R28)

A0 never vanishes on this half-plane. J_p has zeros only on Re z=1/2, and L(2z,chi^2) is finite and nonzero above that line. P_p zeros lie on Re z=1. statement:
### 3.2 Genuine selection and zero supply

For one amplitude class, let \(w_i=\ell_i/d>0\),
\(L=\sum_iw_i=\ell/d\), and \(0\le g_i\le\delta/2\).
Error slots have \(g_i=0\), but their widths remain in L. Set
\[
 q=\frac{\sum_iw_i g_i}{L}=\delta p,\qquad 0\le p\le1/2.
\]
When \(\delta=0\), q is zero and one may take p=0.

The generic zero_error_whole_slots theorem requires only
\(0\le z_A\le L\), the width mesh bound, these gain bounds, and zero error gains. It returns one subset I of positive-gain main slots, fixed for the amplitude class, with
\[
 z_I=\sum_{i\in I}w_i\le z_A,\qquad
 \sum_{i\in I}w_i g_i\ge qz_A-\frac{\delta}{2}{\rm mesh}.
\]
With the class's actual slot lower bounds this gives
\[
 \left|\prod_{i\in I}Q_i\right|^2
 \ge U^{\,2qz_A-\delta\,{\rm mesh}-o(1)}.       \tag{E1}
\]

This theorem has no positive-main-supply lower bound. If positive gains are exhausted, their total is qL, which is at least qz_A. The gain is therefore measured at the target capacity, even if the selected physical width is much smaller. Error factors or zero-gain main factors must not be reinserted in this lower-bounded product. Their actual amplitudes could vanish.

The source wrapper highData_weighted_selection has a \(d\ge1/2\) premise, but the generic theorem just inspected does not. The endpoint correctly uses the generic theorem on lower rows. For \(d<1/2\),
\[
 L>2\ell>1/3,\qquad
 z_{\rm old}\le1/(6\kappa)\le5/21<1/3.
\]
For other old rows the original supply inequality
\(\min(d,2y-d)\le y<4\ell\le6\kappa\ell\) suffices. The detector needs \(L>4/21\), checked at the largest retained d. The new local capacity is much smaller and satisfies the separately checked \(z_A<L\).

All actual original slot widths are positive. Consequently \(z_I=0\) means \(I=\varnothing\). If the generic nonnegative-width selection theorem is used elsewhere, that equivalence should not be silently generalized to zero-width slots.

A common-profile slot system can also be made explicit without arbitrary prime subsets: choose finitely many distinct positive \(\ell_i\), with sum \(\ell\) and maximum below \(d_0\) times the common mesh. For example normalize distinct numbers \(1+i/(2r)\), \(1\le i\le r\), to total \(\ell\), taking r sufficiently large. The minimum width is then positive and common to all targets. Fixed annuli at scales \(Z^{\ell_i}\) become disjoint at a single sufficiently large Z because the exponents are distinct. This preserves one common profile and the full canonical prime pools; it does not require slot-specific profiles.
title: 3.2 Genuine selection and zero supply

## 8. Independent high-ceiling continuation with every cost specified

The L2 floor at3/4 belongs to b=3/2. It is not an intrinsic ceiling of
nonlinear-phase detectors. The following fixed-parameter theorem follows
from(R1),(R2),(R16); it is a conditional architecture, not an exponent gain.

Fix any gamma with1/2<gamma<1. Choose once and for all

    1<b<=2gamma,
    integer k>2 with r=(k-2gamma)/(k-2)<b,
    integer K>=1 with 1-(b-1)K<gamma.                    (R17)

Such choices always exist. Define the SAME kind of global source
W_(b,k),chi and the shell-fixed core X^gamma<n<=X^r. Its low prefix costs
O(X^gamma), and(R16) gives the complete tail L2 bound

    ||W_>X^r||_2^2<<X^b+X^(k+(2-k)r)<=C X^(2gamma).

Thus complete shell L1 is equivalent to the core L1 target, and likewise
for L2. All infinite tails and every shell point remain covered.

The Mellin return uses ALL finite shifts in(R2). Set delta=b-1. The
remainder is holomorphic on sigma>gamma by(R17), as are A_j there. Starting
from the Euler-product reciprocal on sigma>1, suppose 1/L is holomorphic
on sigma>a. On sigma>max(gamma,a-delta), each shifted reciprocal with
j>=1 is already holomorphic. Solving(R2) for the unshifted reciprocal,
using nonzero A_0, extends it to that next strip. A finite number of steps
reaches sigma>gamma. The argument handles principal poles and natural
zeros exactly as before. No rightmost zero at an attained height or
uniformity in all heights is assumed.

For a concrete higher-ceiling example choose

    gamma=3/5, c=2/5, b=11/10, k=12, K=5, r=27/25.

Then the remainder boundary is1/2; tail energy exponents are11/10 and6/5;
both are at most2gamma=6/5. The complete OPEN premise is

    for every epsilon>0 and every sufficiently large dyadic X,
    integral_X^(2X) |sum_(X^(3/5)<n<=X^(27/25)) mu(n)chi(n)
                  exp(-n/x^(11/10)-i(n/x)^12)| dx/x
                       <<_(chi,epsilon) X^(3/5+epsilon). (OPEN-HIGH)

If proved for every fixed ordinary character at this common exponent,
it would give zero exclusion in Re s>3/5. None of this arithmetic premise
is proved here. The fixed-degree Green--Tao theorem still yields only
X^b+X^2(log X)^(-D) for the energy, by the same cutoff argument with
fixed k. Thus the actual coarse estimate still misses this target by a
power. The example prices the weakest developed norm input; it does not
make c=2/5 more plausible than a nearer gain.

More generally k may be chosen as a sufficiently large fixed integer
after gamma and b. One must not let k, K, b or logarithmic strength move
with X: the contour, smooth-kernel and imported arithmetic constants all
depend on them. At gamma=1/2 there is no b with1<b<=2gamma, so this theorem
does not supply the boundary itself. There is no claim of uniformity as
gamma decreases to1/2 or of a theorem obtained by taking that limit.

## 5. Complete G34 return, quantitative targets, masks, and both heights

For the UNPARTITIONED source, the accepted G33 with its separately
subtracted true diagonal gives the absolute high-gcd remainder

    Q_off(X)=Q_<D(X)
                  +O_epsilon(X^(2beta+epsilon)D^(1-2beta)). (A24)

This signed scalar bound is NOT transferred to the rough submask.
Our proof of the rough obstruction used the separate actual gcd-one
argument above. In the complete low-gcd scalar every term is exactly

    Q_<D=2 sum_(1<=g<D)sum_(h>=1)sum_((a,h)=1)
                         f_g(a(a+h))K_(X/g)(a,a+h). (A25)

It follows from m=ga,n=g(a+h), with g their literal gcd,
f(ga)f(g(a+h))=f_g(a)f_g(a+h)=f_g(a(a+h)), and
K_X(ga,g(a+h))=K_(X/g)(a,a+h). Primes dividing 3g have source
sign +1 at every positive valuation, exactly as in (A16).

For any ordered pair of threshold pieces i,j with original masks
A_i,A_j, their actual contribution to this g,h,a sum is

    f_g(a(a+h))K_(X/g)(a,a+h)
      [ A_i(ga)A_j(g(a+h)) + A_i(g(a+h))A_j(ga) ].  (A26)

For i=j the bracket gives the factor 2. For a full partition sum over
all ORDERED (i,j); each bracket is the two original integer orders of
that piece's scalar. For T,R one gets TT,TR,RT,RR, with TR=RT but
both retained. The masks use ga and g(a+h), not a and a+h, and the
original threshold z=kappa sqrt(X), not kappa sqrt(X/g). This keeps
the moving g/divisor dependence exact. The same original-scale rule
applies to I_X. All Gaussian weights are the original full kernel.

For the unpartitioned Q_<D, remove primitive shifts h<=H by positive
counting, using the all-Y estimate preceding (A21):

    absolute removed mass <=C_tau XH sum_(g<D)1/g
                           <=C_tau XH log(2D).      (A27)

The original integer window costs O(X^-4) in the whole scalar, not a
new error for each g, since the original pairs partition by their gcd.
Let Q_hard be (A25) with h>H and both original integers in I_X. Then

    Q_off=Q_hard+O_epsilon(X^(2beta+epsilon)D^(1-2beta)
                                    +XH log(2D)+X^-4). (A28)

This is the complete return with all g,h and complementary regions.
No sign is assigned to Q_hard or to the high-gcd scalar. The true
global diagonal is Delta(X)=sum_n K_X(n,n)=O_tau(X); it is absent
from every Q here and must be added ONCE when returning to ||F||^2.
The artificial p=q two-prime completion diagonal paid in Section 2
is a different object and cannot replace Delta.

Take D=X^theta,H=X^alpha, with

    theta>(2beta-2gamma)/(2beta-1),
    0<=alpha<2gamma-1.                               (A29)

The exact ONE-SIDED bound Q_hard<=C_epsilon X^(2gamma+epsilon), for
every epsilon>0 on all sufficiently large dyadic X, is equivalent to
OPEN-F3 for this fixed beta,gamma. Necessity and sufficiency follow
from (A28), taking smaller epsilon than the fixed strict margins.
At gamma>1/2 the diagonal also fits. The already proved G25--G31
full four-factor return includes the original signed convolution,
all local product diagonals and both independent heights; hence a
proof of this unpaid scalar would give c=1-gamma. This report proves
neither that scalar estimate nor a new c.
For the three displayed targets below, the inherited G30 reconciliation
cost O_epsilon(X^(1.3749+epsilon)), including both mixed terms, lies
strictly below X^(2gamma); the cited full return already pays its
finite caps, outer prime-power convolution, local diagonals and each
independent height window. No cheaper cost is assumed for them here.

Here are explicit budgets under ONLY the packet's c2 baseline, taking
beta=.874873=.874872+.000001. They are error-return budgets, not
estimates of Q_hard:

| gamma | theta | alpha | high-gcd exponent | short-shift exponent |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| .874871 | .000006 | .749740 | 1.749741501524 | 1.749740 |
| 5/6 | .111 | .66 | 1.666524194 | 1.66 |
| 3/4 | .334 | .49 | 1.499330836 | 1.49 |

For the first line 2gamma=1.749742, giving high-gcd margin
.000000498476 and short-shift margin .000002 before logs/epsilon.
The hypothetical c=.125129 would have improved the packet's c2 by
.000001. If a later incumbent supersedes c2, this line remains an
honest historical budget, not a proposed current promotion; use (A29)
with the desired smaller gamma. The 5/6 and 3/4 targets remain open.
The inherited beta=.8749 is equally permissible, with theta retuned
by (A29). No exponent is set on a Mertens boundary.

The gcd-one theorem alone would not rule out cancellation between
different g in a rough-mask scalar. A separate positive complement
estimate closes that possible escape for THIS complete hard mask:

    sum_((m,n)>=D)K_X(m,n)
       <=sum_(d>=D)integral[sum_a g(log(da/x))]^2dx/x
       <=C_tau X^2/D,                  ALL D>=1.    (A29a)

Each pair is counted by at least d=gcd(m,n); positive overcounting is
permitted only in this explicitly bounded error. The all-scale lattice
bound (A11) pays the whole infinite d tail. This is not G33 transferred
to a signed submask. Although X^2/D may exceed a target POWER budget,
it is o(X^2/L^4) for every fixed D=X^theta, theta>0.

Write Q_hard(u,v) for the ordered bilinear scalar with exactly the
complete mask in (A28). Its full uncut scalar differs by at most

    E=X^2/D+XH log(2D)+X+X^-4.

Here (A29a) pays high gcd, (A27) pays every short primitive shift,
O(X) pays the true diagonal, and (A12) pays the original integer
window. These bounds apply to any of our bounded coefficients, with
no hereditary signed estimate. By (A9)--(A10), ||R||^2 asymp X^2/L^4.
Also integral F R dx/x=O(X^(1+beta)) by the inherited actual F bound
and |R|<=sum_n g(log(n/x))<=C x. Therefore

    Q_hard(R,R)=||R||^2+O(E),
    Q_hard(F,R)=O(X^(1+beta)+E),
    Q_hard(T,R)=-Q_hard(R,R)+O(X^(1+beta)+E).        (A29b)

For ANY fixed theta>0 and 0<=alpha<1, D=X^theta,H=X^alpha give
E=o(X^2/L^4). Thus the COMPLETE all-g hard RR scalar is positive
of order X^2/L^4, and its actual TR scalar is negative of that order.
RT equals TR and both remain. Since ||F||^2=O(X^(2beta)), the same
exact reconstruction gives Q_hard(T,T)=Q_hard(R,R)+
O(X^(1+beta)+E). All four ordered interactions are thus accounted for.
For theta<1/2, as in every displayed budget, D<z eventually: two
retained integers cannot share a rough prime, since it would divide
their gcd. Hence every RR pair here also has four distinct rough
primes, with ALL allowed core gcds g<D and all valuations retained.

Consequently even a proposed separate-piece power estimate only for
the SUM over all g<D fails at every fixed gamma<1 and sufficiently
small epsilon. An escape via cancellation across g cannot make THIS
RR block power-small. The viable complete estimate must retain its
actual TT+TR+RT+RR cancellation, or change the partition with a fully
paid return. A29b is an actual partial-scalar lower bound, not a lower
bound for Q_hard(F,F) or full energy. A24/A28, with their stronger
unmasked high-gcd estimate, remain the quantitative new-power return.

Both height variables can be kept explicitly even after these masks.
Let c_i(n)=f(n)A_i(n), and let B_X(m,n) denote any one of the frozen
original pair masks above (coprime, gcd/shift/window, or no mask).
For sigma>1 define the absolutely convergent double Dirichlet series

    D_(ij,B)(s1,s2)=sum_(m,n>=1)
          B_X(m,n)c_i(m)c_j(n)m^-s1 n^-s2.

With s1=sigma+it1 and s2=sigma+it2, exact Gaussian Mellin inversion
g(log(n/x))=(2pi)^-1 integral exp(tau s^2/2)(x/n)^s dt
gives the full corresponding scalar as

    (2pi)^-2 integral_R integral_R exp(tau(s1^2+s2^2)/2)
       D_(ij,B)(s1,s2)
       [integral_X^(2X)x^(s1+s2)dx/x] dt1 dt2.      (A30)

The bound |D|<=zeta(sigma)^2 and the two independent factors
exp(-tau t1^2/2),exp(-tau t2^2/2) justify absolute Fubini. No
same-height replacement, truncation, window reassignment, missing
ordered interaction or conjugation assumption is involved. For real
coefficients changing t1 to -t1 gives the usual conjugated first-height
formula. All masks in D are frozen at the ORIGINAL X, including
A_R(dn) in (A18), and are never differentiated or continued. Finite
height truncations could be paid by their two Gaussian tails; none is
needed for (A30). The g,h form (A26) is a reindexing of this same
absolutely convergent scalar, not a different detector.

## 5. Complete first-gain return and a deliberately coarse test

Fix ONE gamma with1/2<gamma<gamma11 before characters and potential zeros. Choose
one fixed J>=2 satisfying beta_J<=gamma. Require, for EVERY fixed ordinary chi,
every epsilon>0, and the two fixed unramified primes described below,

    |T_(p,J)(x)| <<_(chi,p,J,epsilon) x^(gamma+epsilon)
    for every sufficiently large real x.                   (OPEN-RHCHAIN)

This is the weakest complete sharp-source estimate developed here. An L2 or
absolute-coefficient condition would be stronger, and is not silently substituted.
No claim is made that it is logically the weakest conceivable zero-free criterion.
A bound only on selected matrix eigenvalues, individual chain sectors, integer
samples with unbounded gaps, or one fixed epsilon is insufficient.

By(24), OPEN-RHCHAIN is equivalent to the same bound for the whole fixed filtered
Mertens source S_(p,J)(x)=sum_(n<=x)(v_(p,J)*mu chi)(n), within this exponent range.
It is not advertised as easier merely because it is a new encoding. What has
actually been proved is that its complete low chain sectors have a stronger power
bound(18), and its growing-depth residual has the exact nonfactorial coefficients
(19)-(22). The remaining bound itself is OPEN.

For completeness, all-height return is direct. Initially on Re s>1,

    P_p(s)^J/L(s,chi)
       =s integral_1^infinity S_(p,J)(x)x^(-s-1)dx.          (25)

This is ordinary summation by parts with all real endpoints, not a nonlinear
kernel or growing-profile transform. On each compact subset of Re s>gamma, choose
epsilon smaller than the distance to that line. The asserted source bound makes
the integral and its s derivatives locally normally convergent. The finite
initial interval is entire. Hence(25) continues holomorphically throughout
Re s>gamma; the identity with the original Dirichlet L-function follows from the
connected half-plane and the initial Re s>1 identity. No finite-height sampling or
uniform-in-height implied constant is needed. Ordinary L meromorphy is the only
standard continuation input; no power bound for its reciprocal is imported.

Zeros of P_p lie on Re s=1 because chi(p) is a root of unity. For two distinct
unramified primes p1,p2, a common nonzero-height P zero would force log p1/log p2
to be rational, impossible by unique factorization. For a nonprincipal chi choose
one covering prime with chi(p)!=1: factor a unit integer on which chi is nontrivial
to find such a prime. It covers height0. For a principal chi the pole at s=1 is the
allowed exception, and creates a zero of1/L rather than a contradiction. Thus a
fixed covering pair pays every exceptional numerator zero. The power J does not
change the locations. No natural character zero, ramified prime, principal pole,
Hecke enlargement or conductor-growing constant is removed.

The parameter bills are exact:

| Target gamma | Fixed J | Proved low-sector exponent beta_J | Conditional c |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 2187/2500=.8748 | 7 | 6/7 | .1252 |
| 5/6 | 6 | 5/6 | 1/6 |
| 3/4 | 4 | 3/4 | 1/4 |

At gamma=.8748 the conditional gain over c11 is135091/2500000000=.0000540364.
The current calibration gamma11 is also above6/7. Equality beta_J=gamma is valid
because the hypothesis and the proved transfer both retain EVERY epsilon. These
are conditional targets, not accepted endpoint improvements. The incumbent's
F0/positive-slot/external-binding qualifications remain open. A future proof of
this replacement source would need its own source/admission review; it does not
inherit an unearned Gao or native-Hecke license.

### 5.1 The entire coarse estimate fails by a specific power

For squarefree n, J^omega(n)=d_J(n), and off squarefree support the left side is0.
The elementary hyperbola upper bound sum_(n<=x)d_J(n)<<_J x(log(2x))^(J-1), together
with(22), gives

    sum_(n<=x)|r_J(n)| <<_J x(log(2x))^(J-1).

Paying ALL finite filter terms by triangle therefore proves the complete bound

    |T_(p,J)(x)| <<_(p,J) x(log(2x))^(J-1).                 (26)

Each p^a coefficient is binom(J,a)p^a, and its x/p^a argument supplies the cancelling
p^(-a); no filter endpoint has been ignored. This costs exponent1. It misses the
three target powers by1-gamma: .1252,1/6,1/4 respectively, plus logarithms. At the
current gamma11 the gap is .1251459636. The positive chain bound(7) has the same
power obstruction but a worse representation of the residual. Neither estimate
is a lower bound for T or S.

The next fixed color t=8 has only the coarse exponent7/8, exceeding gamma11 by
.0001459636 and gamma=.8748 by.0002. Improving that individual divisor estimate
would pay one more complete sector but would NOT establish OPEN-RHCHAIN: all higher
chain depths remain. This close numerical coincidence is explicitly not an endpoint
calculation. The pass does not claim novelty or a gain from optimizing that integer.

### 5.2 Every retained p-valuation and a real projected price

Write n=p^a m with p not dividing m and m squarefree, j=omega(m). The exact filtered
tail coefficient is, with binomial coefficients outside0,...,J interpreted as0,

 (v_(p,J)*r_J)(p^a m)
  =chi(p)^a chi(m) [(-p)^a binom(J,a)W_J(j)
                    +(-p)^(a-1)binom(J,a-1)W_J(j+1)],      (27)

where the second term is absent at a=0. It vanishes for a>J+1, and for nonsquarefree
m or a ramified factor in m. Formula(27) retains the two possible squarefree
predecessors (p^a removed or p^(a-1) removed), including a=J+1. Replacing its two
terms by independent signs would change the source. Conversely, deleting positive
or negative valuations is not a signed upper bound.

For a principal chi, the unramified p-free sector of(27) has the fixed sign from
(21), with coefficient(J+1)! at omega(n)=J+1. Choose a fixed squarefree product A
of J distinct primes avoiding pq. On the literal projected family n=A*l with l a
prime not dividing Apq, n<=x, the coefficient is the nonzero constant
(-1)^(J+1)(J+1)!. Chebyshev's lower bound pi(y)>>y/log y consequently gives a
projected summatory price >>_(A,J) x/log x. Only finitely many primes are excluded.
This is an actual arithmetic family, not an arbitrary-sign countermodel.

This lower price rules out paying every such projected component separately with
the desired power after fixed-depth subtraction. It does NOT lower-bound the full
filtered tail, which includes essential p-divisible cross-valuations and other
prime counts. The terminal-prime projection strategy is inherited from the earlier
[restricted research revision]/[restricted research revision]/[restricted research revision] obstruction family; its new role here is diagnostic for the exact
Newton tail, not an independent claimed discovery of that general obstruction.

### 5.3 A growing-depth escape is a new quantitative obligation

Taking J>=K(x) kills r_J(n) for every n<=x. This is an exact finite identity, not a
proof that a FIXED source has a power bound. It changes the filter P_p^J with x,
and all constants in(12)-(18) depend on J. Even if those constants were free,
the proved exponent1-1/J tends to1: at J comparable to log x/loglog x the nominal
saving is only logarithmic. Thus the present proof does not meet any fixed target
gamma<1 through a growing-depth substitution.

A successful growing scheme could still exist. It would need a fixed-power estimate
uniform over its growing t/J range, the actual growth of every hyperbola/Euler-product
constant, and a moving-filter observation/return that retains P_p(s)^J and both
prime branches. The countable-bank and growing-order library contains relevant
return interfaces, but none supplies this missing arithmetic bound. No claim of
impossibility is made from the failure of the present coarse estimate.
