statement:
# Independent sieve-headroom review and repetition-layer improvement



**Verdict.** The author's canonical, completed-theta and cubic-label estimates survive at their stated source-relative scopes. The corrected MP length, all sixth-power costs, counted lower-order classes and negative physical comparisons are valid. The new sixth-order theorem remains an external analytic import; none of its definition/import/admission obligations is declared closed.

A useful further result follows by taking the smaller of the sixth-order and label bounds on EACH exact row-repetition layer before summing those layers. It improves the sufficient all-row canonical boundary from V>=M/6 to V>=M/7 for N>=8M/7, with a continuous improvement already for M<N<8M/7. Both original canonical and complete label-averaged theta sources satisfy the estimate. No label or repeated row is omitted. At V=0 the new envelope is exactly the author's old all-row sieve envelope, so the physical bottleneck and c11 remain unchanged.

## 1. Sources, imported family and scope

The reviewed author report is [restricted provenance path] research revision]-drafts/sieve-headroom/report.md, SHA256 43c9bb54264a62fea956e00aca8f1ba7954627454df83d3880e77cab5b92d3e5. Its nine manifest-listed files and ten source pins matched at intake; the separate freeze manifest has SHA256 505a547f8a6cefb0f16f5f360f22f42133b1f6b09437685b19fd35c074a6cf93. Its claim was absent. Exact read scopes and final reconciliation are in source-evidence.json.

I checked the versioned primary [de Faveri preprint](https://arxiv.org/html/2610.04045v1), Theorem 1.1 and Sections 2.2-2.5, against the pinned local HTML, and Corollary 1.5 for the density comparison. For fixed n=6, K=Q(omega), excluded primes S and family construction data, the imported operator estimate is

    T_6(A,B)=A+B+A^(5/6)B^(1/3)+A^(1/3)B^(5/6),
    sum_(a sixth-free) |sum_(b sixth-free) lambda_b chi_a(b)|^2
       << (AB)^epsilon T_6(A,B) sum_b |lambda_b|^2.       (R1)

Both row and column indices are ideals avoiding S. All coefficients are fixed while the row is summed. This is not a theorem for an arbitrary row-column coefficient array. The old PR9 B2.24-25 squarefree quadratic/cubic sieves remain separate inputs. The local PR9 paper is the pinned commit58344df, not a mutable current-proof paraphrase.

The exact family binding can be made directly. In the class-number-one Eisenstein field, choose each generator m_(E0) in the preprint's finite representative construction to be the global primary generator of E0. Their prescribed products m_E are then primary generators of E. Enlarge the fixed ray modulus so x=1 modulo that modulus implies x=1 modulo3. If a=(x) E g^6 is the prescribed decomposition, choose a primary generator g0 of the fractional ideal g. The element x m_E g0^6 generates a and is primary. It equals the unique primary generator a0. Since (g,b)=1 in the definition, (x m_E/b)_6=(a0/b)_6. The zero definitions agree when (a,b)>1. This identifies chi_a(b) with PR9 psi_(a0)(b)=chi_b(a0), including natural zeros.

Choosing another permissible generator system gives only fixed S-unit classes modulo sixth powers; splitting those finitely many row sectors leaves fixed column twists. Nonprimary element rows contribute six unit sectors. Arbitrary S-valuations are split into residues modulo6 and S-supported sixth powers; the latter have only logarithmically many choices in a norm ball. Nothing growing is folded into an allegedly fixed ray character. A fixed nu, even of order not dividing6, remains in the column coefficients. For the opposite orientation conjugate the entire sum, including nu and every coefficient. Reverse symbol orientation, when used in the older sieves, requires the fixed reciprocity sectors.

Appendix S.1 of zeta_zero_free_validated_merged.md already contains this imported sieve and the short row/column adapter. It is credited ancestry. The full idea index through [private research revision] was read, followed by its sole concurrent [private research revision] addition concerning distinct translation/renewal/polymer certificates; the relevant [restricted research revision], [restricted research revision], [restricted research revision] and [restricted research revision] source statements were checked. Neither the elementary power extraction nor summing growing lower-order classes is a new principle. The additional review result below is the explicit original-source combination before the full repetition sum; no literature priority is claimed.

## 2. General columns, sixth powers and the actual fourth moment

For J fixed centrally normalized factors at scales X_j, their product has length B=product X_j and coefficients

    lambda_b=B^(-1/2) sum_(b1...bJ=b) product_j c_j(b_j),
    |lambda_b| << B^(-1/2) d_J(b).

The ordered multiplicities and ALL collisions are in this identity. Original prime pools need not be disjoint from a plain factor. Fixed twists, individual heights and the original common puncture stay in the coefficients. For example a plain p^5 term times a slot p produces p^6 with a p-hole, not the constant coefficient1.

Write b=d h^6 uniquely with d sixth-power-free, allowing (d,h)>1. The exact character identity is

    psi_u(d h^6)=psi_u(d) 1_((u,h)=1).

At fixed h, counting ideals d and using a divisor bound gives squared coefficient mass <<B^epsilon (Nh)^(-6). Apply R1 to this fixed vector; drop the h-row selector only from the resulting positive norm. Hilbert Minkowski costs sum_h (Nh)^(-3+epsilon), which converges. The sixth-free-row bound is therefore T_6(U,B), up to small powers.

For all rows u=a e^6, the exact identity instead gives the fixed column mask 1_((b,e)=1). R1 applies at A=U/(Ne)^6. Summing e with its actual count yields

    T_all(U,B)=U+B U^(1/6)+U^(5/6)B^(1/3)
                                  +U^(1/3)B^(5/6).    (R2)

The B U^(1/6) term records repeated rows; it cannot be dropped. The sums for the other monomials have weights (Ne)^(-6), (Ne)^(-5), (Ne)^(-2), respectively, and converge. Unit and fixed-prime restoration gives fixed or logarithmic factors. Every principal and fixed-inducing row is still present.

R2 is O(U^(1+epsilon)) for B<=U^(1/2). PR9 B0.5/B3.40 is the fourth moment |S|^4 |Q|^2, so its input to a second-moment sieve is S^2 Q. The correct length is B=U^(2m+v), or U^(n1+n2+v) for two different plain scales. The corrected short gate is

    n1+n2+v<=1/2.                                     (R3)

It does not replace the old n1+n2+6kappa v<=1 gate. This correction is already recorded in the append-only controller packet and Appendix S.1; no new MP theorem is asserted here.

## 3. Original canonical and completed coefficients

For the literal PR9 B3.6 norm put X=Z^N, U=Z^M, F=Z^V. It is

    E=F^(-1) sum_(f squarefree, Nf~F) w(f)
          sum_(0<Nk<<U) |C_f(k)|^2,
    C_f(k)=X^(-1/2) sum_(n squarefree)
      a0(n) nu(n) rho(n) chi_n(k) chi_n(f)^4
                                    d_I(n) W(Nn/X).    (R4)

Here rho(n)=1_((n,r_rho)=1), w is nonnegative and divisor bounded and depends only on f, and the original prime lists and coefficients are fixed through both averages. The twist nu, common puncture and n coefficients apart from the displayed residue symbols are independent of f and k. The canonical theorem in PR9 itself forbids a new n coefficient; the arguments here are applied to the displayed original coefficient vector, and do not silently alter that source declaration.

For squarefree good n, |a0(n)|=1. With a fixed number of slots, |d_I(n)| is divisor bounded. Thus the squared column mass in R4 is X^epsilon, uniformly in the fixed f and puncture. Natural zeros and fixed masks are contractions of this coefficient mass. R2 gives the author's canonical exponent

    E_all(M,N)=max{M,N+M/6,5M/6+N/3,M/3+5N/6}
      = M                         if 0<=N<=M/2,
        5M/6+N/3                  if M/2<=N<=M,
        N+M/6                     if N>=M.             (R5)

The normalized f count cancels F exactly up to a divisor small power. No factor F or puncture norm is charged twice. This pointwise-in-f proof also allows a fixed f-dependent column mask, but the later label and combined arguments do NOT allow that extension.

The actual completed source is

    T_f(X;k)=sum_(c squarefree,b)
      a0(c) nu(c) bar(alpha(b))^3 nu(b)^3
      psi_k(c b^3) chi_(c b^3)(f)^4 rho(c b^3)
                        d_I(c b^3) V(Nc (Nb)^3/X)
                        /[sqrt(Nc) Nb].              (R6)

No restriction (c,b)=1 is inserted. At each prime v_p(c b^3)=epsilon+3j, epsilon in{0,1}, so there is at most one representation of an ideal as c b^3 with c squarefree. Set b=b0 h^2, b0 squarefree. Then

    c b^3 = d h^6, d=c b0^3,
    v_p(d) in{0,1,3,4}.

The ideals c,b0,h can overlap. At fixed h the squared coefficient mass on d is bounded by

    X^epsilon (Nh)^(-4)
       sum_(b0 squarefree) (Nb0)^(-2)
       sum_(Nc<<X/(Nh)^6) (Nc)^(-1)
       << X^epsilon (Nh)^(-4).                       (R7)

Dropping the product constraint in this positive mass is lawful; it is not a comparison of two signed source norms. Whole-index marks retain every h prime. The factors nu(h^6), chi_(h^6)(f)^4 and rho(h^6) remain their exact phases or zeros. In particular the f-hole is not replaced by1. R1 and Minkowski cost sum_h (Nh)^(-2+epsilon), again convergent. This proves T_6(U,X) for sixth-free rows and T_all(U,X) for all rows of the COMPLETE sum R6. The author's (11)-(12) therefore survive.

Profiles in PR9 B2.1 are annular or rapidly decreasing with all Euler derivatives at both endpoints. For the latter, decompose the entire profile into annuli, apply the complete annular estimate and sum norms with the endpoint decay chosen after the raw powers. Nothing about the merely x^(1/4) lower-end decay of a reflected V-sharp profile licenses arbitrary substitution into this primal statement. Any separately reflected source must retain its own actual profile and tail proof.

For a fixed finite list of smooth parameters, real powers, heights and scales, prove the same coefficient bounds for their derivatives. On unit log-scale intervals, derivatives replace W by fixed Euler derivatives and add bounded-log factors; the number of intervals is logarithmic. Tensor Sobolev applied to the positive joint row norm controls rowwise suprema with a fixed polynomial height cost H_J. A common coupled profile is separated by B3.3 on its ambient box BEFORE e, f, rows or live prime labels are chosen. Its weighted Fourier L1 measure is fixed and integrates the required child height polynomial. Arithmetic masks remain outside this analytic device. Constants may depend on the fixed slot count and finite profile orders; no uniform positive-slot mesh has thereby been proved.

## 4. Label average, collisions and the existing local comparisons

For fixed k the f,n dependence in R4 is chi_n(f)^4. On good squarefree ideals this is a cubic symbol, up to conjugation and fixed ray sectors. PR9 B2.25 applies with row length F and column length X. The remaining phase chi_n(k) is a fixed coefficient contraction, even at natural zeros. The weight w(f)<<Z^epsilon may be removed only from the positive f norm. Counting all O(U) k and then dividing by F gives

    E << H_J Z^(M+L(N,V)+epsilon),
    L(N,V)=max{0,N-V,(2N-V)/3}.                       (R8)

This keeps every k, including pure sixth powers and principal inducing rows. It is a genuine average over the original f family, not a count of f with a fixed-twist estimate. It needs coefficients and puncture independent of f.

For the completed average of R6, fix b first. The exact identity is

    chi_(c b^3)(f)^4=chi_c(f)^4 1_((b,f)=1).

The k-phase from b and the f-hole are contractions of the positive joint (f,k) norm ONLY after fixing b and applying Hilbert Minkowski to the original b-sum. The squared c-coefficient mass is <<X^epsilon (Nb)^(-2), at c length X/(Nb)^3. The corresponding norm costs

    (Nb)^(-1) [F+X/(Nb)^3+(F X/(Nb)^3)^(2/3)]^(1/2).

The F term sums logarithmically over b; the other two have summable powers. Thus R8 also holds for the FULL completed average. Common whole-index product marks and common punctures are retained. Arbitrary f-dependent coefficients would invalidate this argument; so would dropping the b-hole before passing to a fixed-b positive norm.

The author's simpler whole-norm minimum min(E_all,M+L) and gate (23) are correct. For F_target=N+V, E_all<=F_target is exactly V>=M-N below N=M/2, V>=5M/6-2N/3 up to N=M, and V>=M/6 thereafter. The whole-norm label condition is V>=max{M-N,M/2,(3M-N)/4}; it indeed does not enlarge those three regions. Section5 improves this by taking the minimum before the repeated-row count, which is a different operation.

The old unmarked completed bound B2.43 is max(M,2M-N), only for f=r_rho=1. Its minimum with R5 gives the author's exact pieces: M up to N=M/2; 5M/6+N/3 up to N=7M/8; 2M-N up to N=M; and M thereafter. The maximal exponent is9M/8. The marked no-label/no-puncture comparison uses precisely Appendix S.2:

    M+max{0,(N+2z-2M)/4,M+2z-N}, 0<=z<=M/2.

At N=7M/10,z=M/25, the old and new exponents are69M/50 and16M/15. No old reflection bound is extended to a new label or puncture without its proof.

The lower-order sectors (16)-(17) also survive, on their declared sixth-free row set. For u=t a^2, take v_p(t)=v_p(u) mod2 and v_p(a)=floor(v_p(u)/2), so t is squarefree, a cube-free, and they may overlap. At fixed t,b,

    psi_(t a^2)(c b^3)=psi_t(c b^3) psi_a(c)^2
                                           1_((a,b)=1).

The imported cube-free cubic sieve at A=(U/Nt)^(1/2), B=X/(Nb)^3 and the fixed-b positive restriction give, after Minkowski and the full t count Nt<=Delta,

    (U Delta)^(1/2)+X Delta+U^(1/3)X^(2/3)Delta^(2/3).

For u=t a^3 use cube-free t and squarefree a; the b-phase is psi_a(b)^3, a scalar contraction at fixed b. The squarefree quadratic sieve gives U^(1/3)Delta^(2/3)+X Delta. The X Delta and all weighted t counts are indispensable. [restricted research revision]/MQ4 is prior ancestry for the first scalar expression in another source. Generic squarefree u has t=u in BOTH decompositions; their union is not a full row cover. These statements do not include arbitrary sixth-power repetitions without a further exact lift.

## 5. New complete bound: choose the estimate before counting repetitions

Keep the ORIGINAL joint (f,k) norms R4 or R6. For fixed good ideal e, write k=a e^6 with a sixth-power-free. Let A=U/(Ne)^6. Every coefficient acquires the exact whole-index mask 1_((index,e)=1). It is fixed during both remaining averages, so both preceding proofs apply to this SAME masked source:

    F^(-1) sum_f w(f) sum_(a sixth-free,Na<<A)
                       |source_f(a e^6)|^2
       << H_J Z^epsilon min{T_6(A,X), A Z^L}.         (R9)

The first bound fixes f and uses R1, or R7 for the completed coefficients. The second fixes a and applies the cubic f sieve as in R8. There is no assertion that a signed subset has smaller norm: these are two bounds on exactly the same complete positive joint norm. Fixed e may share primes with f, the puncture, c,b or a; all masks remain in each proof. In particular no coprimality (a,e)=1 is assumed.

The decomposition of every good k is unique at each valuation, with the units and fixed-prime sectors restored as in Section1. On a dyad Ne~Z^y there are O(Z^y) ideals e and residual row exponent t=M-6y. Sum the smaller uniform bound R9 on that dyad, then sum the O(log Z) dyads. Finite dyadic endpoint constants are absorbed by a previously chosen epsilon. Therefore BOTH complete sources obey

    E << H_J Z^(E_mix(M,N,V)+epsilon),
    E_mix = sup_(0<=t<=M) {
        (M-t)/6 + min[C(t,N), t+L(N,V)] },            (R10)
    C(t,N)=max{t,N,5t/6+N/3,t/3+5N/6}.

The factor (M-t)/6 is the FULL e count, not a square root or a normalized measure. Fixed S-supported powers contribute logarithmic multiplicity; their shortening may be discarded because both bounds are monotone in A. The completed h extraction is already fully summed within R9, before this e count. This avoids exchanging an unproved pointwise signed bound with an outer count.

R10 can also be used with smooth row majorants: retain the original lower row ball, decompose only a rapidly decaying upper tail, and sum the complete ball bounds. Coupled smooth profiles use the common measure described in Section3; positivity and Minkowski retain the whole source before either sieve is selected. All uniformity is for fixed polynomial scale ranges, fixed arithmetic construction data and fixed finite slot systems.

### 5.1 Exact evaluation of the new envelope

For N,V>=0, 0<=L<=N. Define

    E0=min{C(M,N), M+L},
    P=(M+5N+L)/6.

Then

    E_mix=E0,
      unless L>=N/2 and N-L<=M;
    E_mix=max{E0,P} when both conditions hold.         (R11)

This is a continuous endpoint formula; including equality in either condition causes no jump. Here is a proof on the entire interval, not a numerical grid. For 0<=t<=N/2, C(t,N)=N. After the repetition count, the sieve branch is M/6+N-t/6, decreasing, while the label branch is M/6+5t/6+L, increasing. Their crossing is t=N-L. It lies in the actual interval precisely when the conditions in R11 hold, and its common value is P. The endpoint t=0 is no larger than the crossing if it exists; otherwise the minimum is increasing up to the relevant endpoint.

For N/2<=t<=N, C=t/3+5N/6; for N<=t<=2N, C=5t/6+N/3; for t>=2N, C=t. After adding (M-t)/6, these branches have slopes1/6,2/3,5/6, respectively. They and the label branch are increasing, so their minimum achieves its largest value at t=M whenever this portion is present. This gives E0 and proves R11, including truncated intervals M<N/2. The case N=0 follows by the same endpoint formula.

### 5.2 A strictly larger all-row canonical sufficient region

For M>0 and the literal target exponent N+V, R10-R11 give exactly the following boundary for THIS upper envelope:

    E_mix<=N+V  iff  V>=g(M,N),
    g(M,N)= M-N                    (0<=N<=M/2),
             5M/6-2N/3             (M/2<=N<=M),
             (2M-N)/6              (M<=N<=8M/7),
             M/7                   (N>=8M/7).         (R12)

The word "exactly" concerns this proved upper-envelope criterion, not a lower bound for the true energy. Equality is valid with the usual Z^epsilon loss; an induction needing a strict reserve must impose a strict padded inequality.

For N<=M, sufficiency follows from E_mix<=E_all. Necessity for the envelope comes from its t=M endpoint: C(M,N) reaches N+V only at the old boundary, while M+L<=N+V requires V>=max{M-N,M/2,(3M-N)/4}, which is no weaker in these ranges.

For N>=M the proposed threshold is at most M/6. Check first 0<=V<=M/6; then L=N-V, t=N-L=V is present, and R11's crossing costs N+(M-V)/6. Paying it requires V>=M/7. The t=M endpoint has label branch M+N-V>N+V in this interval; its sieve branch requires V>=(2M-N)_+/6. Together these give max{M/7,(2M-N)/6}, with the switch at N=8M/7. At that threshold both branches are paid. Larger V only decreases E_mix and increases the target, proving sufficiency for every V. Smaller V fails one displayed envelope branch. This proves R12.

For example M=1,N=8/7,V=1/7 gives

    E_mix=9/7=N+V,
    E_all=55/42,
    E_label=2.

The gain over the previous sixth-order price is1/42, and the global label minimum alone gives no such gain. At N=2,V=1/7 the corresponding prices are15/7,13/6 and20/7. Common punctures of any fixed polynomial size are still allowed; this is genuinely outside the old V>=M/6 sufficient region, even when a large Q also defeats B3.7. No favorable puncture is selected after the row.

The mechanism is a valid complement payment: few repetitions are paid with the sixth-order sieve, many repetitions with the genuine label average, and EVERY intervening dyad is included by R10. It retains the original weights, characters, marks and natural zeros. It is not a theorem about freely conditioning coefficients on f. At V=0, L=N and R10 evaluates to E_all exactly. The repeated principal layers remain charged. In particular E_mix>N for every M>0: the unlabeled canonical target is still unpaid by this new family of estimates.

## 6. Full physical comparison and unresolved complements

The local improvement R12 must not be presented as a larger MP range or a larger zero-free constant. A future use in an induction would need the exact new child source and all original branches, masks, extraction scalars and returns. No such complete new induction is proved here.

**Compensator.** At the accepted [restricted research revision] geometry, ell=313594727/1875000000, M=1-ell, 1/6<ell<1/5. Every original subset of total width d in[0,ell] has M'=M-2d, z'=ell-d, N'=1+ell-d. Thus N'-M'=2ell+d>0 and N'-(M'+2z')=3d>=0. The older B0.26 energy is

    E_old=M'+max(0,-1+5ell+d)/4,

whereas R5 costs N'+M'/6. Their difference is

    (1+11ell)/6+2d/3-max(0,-1+5ell+d)/4 >19/45.       (R13)

Indeed the first term exceeds17/36 and the positive part divided by4 is less than1/20. This is uniform for the whole subset interval, including the empty subset. The common outside coefficient, exact negative signs, tuple count and old -d saving from B0.25-27 remain intact; the new larger energy cannot improve them. These physical sources have f=1,V=0, so the new R10 is exactly R5 here and does not alter this comparison. The lower-order sectors leave generic squarefree rows unaccounted for and cannot be substituted for the full energy.

**Numerator, shortening and exhausted capacity.** The accepted [restricted research revision] source uses two independent reflected plain lengths .41M<=n_i<=.44M and .034M<=v<=.04M on its local window. Their product length is at least.854M. The new fourth-moment gate R3 needs <=M/2. Its full-row price at .854M is1.118M, while the accepted original moment costs M. With no slots the pair still has total length at least.82M, so this does not replace the unrestricted old MP0 branch either.

PR9 B0.41-44 retains the exact h=h0 h_r Euler shifts, q_u/q_rad(u) allocation and weighted mass sum |c_u|h0^(delta/2)<<U^epsilon. The reflected scale is at most(U/Y)h0. The h0=1 critical branch already misses the new short gate; increasing h0 cannot repair it. Some conductor shortenings yield short cases, but the longer complementary cases remain. The common-profile suprema, both independent plain heights, four clipped profile pairs, shortage alternatives, empty selection, zero capacity, fixed-inducing/principal rows and original Euler tails keep their old proofs. A label average is absent from this physical source; one cannot insert it without reconstructing the signal.

**Density comparison.** Substituting n=6 and delta=2sigma-1 into the middle interval of the preprint's Corollary1.5 gives saving

    D6=3delta(6delta-1)/(60delta-36delta^2-10).

On 17/25<=delta<=7/10 the new row exponent 1-D6 exceeds the retained PR9 rho=1-10delta/[3(5-2delta)] by

    delta(312delta-252delta^2-55)
       /[3(5-2delta)(60delta-36delta^2-10)] >.17.

The concave numerator quadratic is at least39.92 and the denominator is positive and bounded as in the author report. Since delta v<=.035 and E_K<=rho+delta v, this does not improve the marked density input. It already fails on the uncontested untwisted subfamily. Neither arbitrary fixed-nu extension of that corollary nor uniform zero exclusion is inferred.

**Separated inverse source.** For the complete [restricted research revision] product M(U^r) M(U^s) Q, r+s>217/100, delta in[17/25,7/10], v<=1/20. The merged length exponent is b=r+s+v>2.17. Even on sixth-free rows R1 costs b; the required exponent is T=delta(r+s)+E_K. Its excess is at least

    (1-delta)(r+s+v)-rho >=8077/27000.                (R14)

The worst endpoint is delta=7/10,v=0,r+s=217/100; the delta derivative is negative on the full interval. The all-row cost is still larger. R10 does not apply an invented f-average to this source. Failure of this sufficient price is not a norm lower bound or an impossibility theorem for its actual signed coefficients.

The old [restricted research revision] one-sided signed target is the SUM R_nonunique+R_middle, after the already paid low/far pieces. It is still open, and its xi-to-c physical return is not supplied by an operator estimate for arbitrary merged columns. Neither the new local gate nor the counted lower-order sectors close that target.

The complete field-source targets retain all transfers: exponent gamma<.8748540364, equivalently squared-energy exponent<1.7497080728, would be needed to beat c11 by that route. For c=.12515 the target is gamma=.87485; for1/6 it is5/6; for1/4 it is3/4. These are target conversions, not newly proved bridges. The old compensator conditions ell<1/5 and ell<x<=y, x+y=1-ell remain architecture-specific restrictions, not universal barriers.

All earlier physical roots and their counts, missing radicals, original full characters, both signed projectors, real 6a/9a radii, extraction scalars, K_phys^(5/6), inducing and principal branches, old-only descendants, clipped rectangles, weighted Euler restoration, common mesh and suprema, actual detector tails and Delta-before-target/supremum choices remain unchanged. The centered M/24 reserve is unspent. The SAME-family licensing, F0/ancestry, original positive-slot uniformity and external admissions retain their prior status. No formal or kernel validation is asserted.

## 7. Evidence and disposition

The complete author report, discovery slate, both diagnostic scripts and receipts, freeze script, worklog, STOP and manifest were inspected. Their finite residue and exponent checks are diagnostic only; they do not verify the imported analytic theorem. No author script was imported or executed by this review.

The only new executable diagnostic checks the NEW R10-R12 envelope. It independently enumerates all affine intersections on each compact repetition interval using exact rationals, compares R11 and R12 on1,849 parameter pairs, and checks the explicit equality examples and V=0 complement. It ran once. The continuous proof is Section5; the finite check is not its replacement. A first source-print attempt encountered a Windows console encoding error; the omitted source slices were then read explicitly in UTF-8. No mathematics or source bytes were changed by that read failure.

Recommend accepting the author's original-source estimates (8),(11)-(18),(22)-(23) with their exact qualifications, and adding R9-R12 as the useful surviving review development. In particular the author's non-enlargement assertion for the WHOLE-NORM minimum remains true; the new region comes from a smaller estimate BEFORE summing exact repetitions. The complete unlabeled physical complement and all current signed arithmetic targets remain OPEN. The source-relative constant stays c11=312864909/2500000000=.1251459636, with K=28114053/6250000 and all prior obligations unchanged.

statement:
# W45 independent review: logarithmic return, complete codec and causal scope



## 1. Decision and exact evidence

Recommend retaining three mathematically valid, precisely limited developments. L1–7 prove an every-interval signed logarithmic criterion for the COMPLETE fixed Gaussian, with a complete zero return. C1–8 give the exact biased-Walsh degree-energy law, its full integer reconstruction error and its remaining signed response. R1–7 prove a source-specific superpolynomial failure of the uncut finite-Euler Gaussian norm. None estimates the required new arithmetic quantity or changes c6=.125139, theta6=.874861. New endpoint/kernel verification remains separate and pending.

Throughout, field exponent gamma means complete shell L2 norm O_epsilon(X^(gamma+epsilon)); the squared-energy exponent is2gamma after relabeling the epsilon buffer. A conditional c label describes the corresponding source's zero-exclusion target. A bound for only one ordinary character does not establish the original full-family theorem.

The useful distinctions are:

* The signed logarithmic criterion is equivalent in exponent to the complete Gaussian moment, not a proved weaker arithmetic exponent. It pays a previously missing analytic nonconcentration condition for this Gaussian class.
* The codec pays its discarded part, including the full CRT-law error. Its retained conditional rough response remains the complete difficult arithmetic. Marginal independence alone pays none of it.
* The Euler norm failure is for actual f3 forcing, not merely an ambient operator. It is a failure of a global norm certificate. Audit30 proves that its large mass escapes every polynomial physical scale and derives an exact causal block identity; it does not lower-bound the physical shell.
* Audit21 gives an actual f3 cocycle with a fully paid future inverse under the inherited sublinear baseline. This is an adaptation of existing future-resolvent machinery, with literal coefficient and boundary costs. A blanket assertion that every cocycle resonates at the hypothetical zero is false.

One minor quantifier repair is needed in R3's headroom sentence: its lower bound on P_X does not by itself imply P_X=X^(1+o(1)). For that conclusion choose, for example, P_X=ceil(2X exp(C sqrt(log X))), or explicitly impose log P_X/log X -> 1. No main theorem is rejected after that qualification. L6's phrase “stronger in input form” should mean a stronger return from an algebraically weaker signed-log hypothesis, not that a stricter arithmetic estimate has been established.

Manifest SHA-256 `8b8b4977b29229b408cef0ec20138897c18afd1f3361c9c331d0263641e74213`; its 21 listed files were independently read in full as bytes and matched for size/hash. Seeds SHA-256 `44daac36603a32f0d97364e762779095c3a536a88d0e6185be7dde65c640e363`. Author freeze is 03:31:23.860951 UTC. The full report, first tests, selection receipts, check source/results and relevant antecedents were read. Author scripts were not run or modified. `source-receipt.json` binds this intake; document hashes prove provenance, not a theorem.

The complete maintained index, original29-family/109-child library and later cycle history remain in context. Current index/current-proof and full [private research revision] delta were read during preparation, and the actual source passages needed below were revisited. Attribution is to precise local mechanisms; no literature-priority claim is made.

## 2. Sampling, chronology and all30 preservation

The author reserved19 (bridge),03 (reach),11 (different), then drew22 from all21 remaining p<.1 cards,20 from all13 remaining p<.01 cards, and02 from all25 remaining cards. Every pool contains eligible cards from all six groups. Independent Decimal comparisons reproduce the exact strict pools; the fixed seeded 256-bit stream, unbiased rejection boundaries, accepted indices12/3/1, saved hashes and pool-before-draw timestamps all agree. No candidate was removed because its mathematics failed; no rejection or reroll occurred. The seed labels are typicality prompts, not calibrated probabilities of success.

The six actual first tests are 19/03/11/22/20/02. There are three substantive lines:19,11+22,03+20. Wildcard02 received its exact Laurent-order test without being silently promoted. Both rare draws received genuine linked development.

My seed-only ALL30 priority pool froze at03:13:55.609600 UTC, SHA-256 `6c14fd419158a4dc6d2dca18139ebdddeda5d1446030df3e17f549df413a4703`. One independent uniform factorial-rank draw froze at03:14:43.497793 UTC, SHA-256 `30c1c20bf50bd9aa047042638f7ff98e8fc75e4cfb687c6f872bfd6484c2d2eb`. The original integer rank183623877542497363390511504210960 and full30 permutation are retained and reconstruct exactly. These commitments preceded my receipt of selections or outcomes; the author's selections had already occurred03:10, which I did not yet know. This is a pre-intake commitment, not a claim that the author had not begun development globally.

The final wake first supplied the six selections together with an outcome summary. Before reading the full report I mechanically applied the saved rule at03:33:39.232705 UTC: protected30 is the first priority entry outside the six; uniform21 is the first independent permutation entry outside the six and30. `audit-selection.json`, SHA-256 `64e4d846cc15c5f8bf15e76c56e5ad533f2824245b9d1732183f4dc04e2ed79a`, records that the summary was already visible. No choice or permutation was changed in response to it. Author21/30 were untested; the calculations in Sections6/7 are independent critic audits, not author successes.

## 3. L1–10: the complete signed logarithmic criterion

### 3.1 Green comparison and the loss

Translate a maximizer t0 to0. A length-one interval I containing0 lies in [-1,1]. Put h=f/f(0), A=log(B/|f(0)|), v=A-log|h|. If f is analytic on a neighborhood of the closed disk of radius R>=16 and has no boundary zero, then v>=0 and

    v(z)=H(z)+sum_a G_R(z,a),
    G_R(z,a)=log |(R^2-conj(a)z)/(R(z-a))|,
    v(0)=A.                                                  (Q1)

The sum is finite and counts multiplicities. Removing the disk Blaschke factors proves the identity; H is the positive harmonic extension of the nonnegative boundary data. The logarithmic singularities at real zeros are integrable. Since f(0) is nonzero, a=0 never occurs.

For H, the Poisson kernel gives H(t)<=((R+1)/(R-1))H(0). For a zero with |a|<=sqrt R,

    G_R(t,a)-G_R(0,a)
      =log|1-conj(a)t/R^2|+log|a|-log|t-a|.

The first term is <=R^(-3/2). If |a|<=2, the integral of -log|t-a| on any unit interval is <=1+log2: setting Im(a)=0 can only increase it, and centering the real singularity maximizes it. Adding log|a|<=log2 leaves a bound below4. If |a|>2, |t-a|>=|a|-1 gives a pointwise log ratio <=log2. Since G_R(0,a)>=.5 log R, the integrated difference is at most (8/log R)G_R(0,a).

For |a|>sqrt R the Green function is positive harmonic on the smaller disk. Its Harnack ratio is at most (sqrt R+1)/(sqrt R-1)<=1+8/log R. The same larger factor bounds the ratio for H. Summing Q1 proves precisely

    integral_I log|f| >= log|f(0)|
                       -(8/log R) log(B/|f(0)|).             (Q2)

No assumed zero separation, zero density, multiplicity cap or positivity of f enters. Boundary zeros can be avoided by choosing a radius within the allowed interval; discrete zeros prohibit only finitely many radii there. The proof is stronger evidence than the author's finite Green samples, which are only diagnostics.

For fixed coefficients with A_b=sum |a_n| n^(-b)<infinity, completing the square yields

    |F(z)| <= (2pi tau)^(-1/2) A_b
       exp(b Re z+tau b^2/2+(Im z)^2/(2tau)).                 (Q3)

It also proves locally uniform convergence and entire analyticity. For f3(n)chi(n), b>1 suffices and |a_n|<=1. Let M_j=max_[j,j+1]|F| and J_j=integral_[j,j+1]log|F|. The nonzero Mellin transform on Re(s)>1 proves F is not identically zero; therefore J_j is finite and M_j>0. Choose R in[sqrt j,2sqrt j] avoiding boundary zeros. Q3 gives log B <=(b+2/tau)j+O(sqrt j+1). Thus

    (1+eta_j)log M_j <= J_j+eta_j log B,
    eta_j=8/log R=O(1/log j).                                (Q4)

For each fixed gamma, J_j<=(gamma+epsilon)j+C_epsilon on EVERY sufficiently large integer interval implies log M_j<=(gamma+epsilon)j+O(j/log j). Use a smaller epsilon first. The reverse bound J_j<=log M_j is immediate. Constants are fixed before j grows. Negative contributions near zeros cannot mask a larger exponential maximum in this fixed Gaussian class.

There is also an immediate complete-moment equivalence worth making explicit. Jensen on a unit interval gives

    J_j <= .5 log integral_[j,j+1]|F(u)|^2 du.                (Q5)

A fixed number of complete dyadic log shells covers that interval. Consequently an all-shell moment exponent gamma implies the signed-log bound; Q4 returns the pointwise exponent, which implies the moment bound. Every-epsilon allowances absorb the fixed coverings and o(j) loss. Thus L6 is a new exact description of the same exponent problem, not evidence that the arithmetic hypothesis is weaker in consequence. Finite intervals, a subsequence, or an average over j do not suffice.

### 3.2 Literal coefficients and zero return

Write z_p=chi(p)p^(-s), with chi(p)=0 at ramified primes. f3 has value-1 at every positive p-power for p!=3 and+1 at every 3-power. Therefore

    D_chi(s)=sum f3(n)chi(n)n^(-s)=N_chi(s)H_chi(s)/L(s,chi),
    N_chi=1-2z_2,
    H_2=(1-z_2)^(-2), H_3=(1-z_3)^(-2),
    H_p=(1-2z_p)/(1-z_p)^2, p>=5.                           (Q6)

This checks all powers, including2 and3, rather than substituting a squarefree or completely multiplicative surrogate. Both H and its inverse have absolutely summable coefficients at each fixed weight sigma>1/2: large-prime local corrections start at z_p^2 and 2/sqrt5<1. Their finite small-prime factors have no pole or zero in that half-plane. If2 is unramified the zeros of N have real part1; if it is ramified N=1. Thus N H is nonzero for1/2<Re(s)<1 at every finite height.

On Re(s)>1 absolute Gaussian Fubini gives

    integral_R F_chi(u)e^(-su)du=exp(tau s^2/2)D_chi(s).    (Q7)

The original left Gaussian tail pays this integral and every fixed s-derivative on compacta as u->-infinity. An all-interval bound at gamma pays the right tail locally uniformly for Re(s)>gamma. This proves holomorphic continuation of the left side without assuming reciprocal polynomial growth in an unbounded strip. Multiply by L and continue on gamma<Re(s)<1. At any zero there the right numerator in Q6–7 is nonzero, contradiction, with multiplicities included. The principal pole at1 is outside that open strip and cannot be silently divided through; the inherited known right edge is separate. No uniform-in-height reciprocal estimate was used for this one-way return.

Each fixed ordinary character needs its own arithmetic bound. Integer CRT below gives neither an ideal theorem nor a growing-conductor estimate. The general analytic Q2–4 applies to a fixed ideal Gaussian only after its absolute norm-series bound and original pole bridge are established separately. The current original Eisenstein family is not imported by name alone.

For the present source, gamma<.874861 would improve the accepted c6; gamma=5/6 and3/4 conditionally return the respective open1/6 and1/4 strips. No such new gamma is proved. W21-T29 was an UNTESTED logarithmic-action seed for a different compact detector; W21-T28's smooth-signal counterexample remains valid under its weaker smoothness hypotheses. W38's exceptional-dyad construction is also not overturned. W39 and [private research revision] observation already used Gaussian analytic growth. The proposed delta is the signed Green comparison and its explicit every-interval return, with these ancestors retained.

### 3.3 The finite upper certificate

L8 is a correct uniform tail bound when the integer cutoff N>=exp(j+1). The function t->g_tau(log t-u) is decreasing for t>=N and u in[j,j+1], so the omitted sum is bounded by its integral from N. Completing the square under t=exp(v) gives

    T_(N,j)=exp(j+1+tau/2)
       barPhi((log N-j-1-tau)/sqrt tau).                    (Q8)

For b>1 the derivative bound is also correct. Writing w=b tau+t bounds
|w| exp(-t^2/(2tau))/tau by b+1/sqrt(e tau); summing n^(-b)<=1+1/(b-1) gives the author's explicit K_j. For any certified T>=T_(N,j)>0, log(|F_N|+T) is K_j/T-Lipschitz even through zeros. The midpoint quadrature error on length1 is K_j/(4MT). Certified absolute evaluation errors delta_k then give L10 with the correct upper inequality. This does not interchange log and an uncontrolled small additive error.

Choosing N=ceil(exp(j+1+C sqrt j)) with a strict C^2/(2tau)>1-gamma+eta margin permits T=exp((gamma-eta)j) eventually. Choosing M>=exp((b-gamma+2eta)j) makes the quadrature error O(exp(-eta j)). It is a finite, potentially costly per-interval certificate, not an all-j algorithmic proof of its arithmetic success. G63/Sol02 auditS31 already own complete Gaussian finite-tail/quadrature methodology; the logarithmic regularization and Q2 are the useful present adaptation.

## 4. C1–8: full biased-Walsh reconstruction and its price

For P containing2 and excluding3 set a_P(n)=product_(p in P)(1-2*1_(p|n)), r_P=f3 a_P. This is literally f3=a_P r_P and r_P(pn)=r_P(n) for p in P, including every exponent. The positive Gaussian measure is on ALL integers. Its product reference has q_p=1/p, not1/(p+1).

With Z_p=(B_p-q_p)/sqrt(q_p(1-q_p)), m_p=1-2q_p and v_p=2sqrt(q_p(1-q_p)), the identity1-2B_p=m_p-v_p Z_p gives

    a_P=sum_S A_S Z_S,
    A_S=(-1)^|S| product_(p in S)v_p product_(p notin S)m_p.

Orthonormality proves sum A_S^2=1. The degree energy generating polynomial is exactly

    sum_S A_S^2 z^|S|=product_p[(1-nu_p)+nu_p z],
    nu_p=4(p-1)/p^2.                                       (Q9)

Thus rho_D^2=sum_(|S|>D) A_S^2=Pr(K>D), with K a Poisson-binomial ENERGY variable; it is not an assumed random arithmetic phase. Since nu_2=1, all nonzero coefficients contain2. The author's Chernoff bound follows from E e^(tK)<=exp(lambda(e^t-1)), lambda=sum nu_p, t=log((D+1)/lambda)>=0. Dropping exp(-lambda) weakens it legitimately. For P={2,5,7}, an independent rational calculation over all70 integer residues gives degree energies[0,9/49,88/175,384/1225] and discarded energies[1,40/49,384/1225,0].

The full-pattern theorem used here is W41 B2/G54, not a heuristic independence statement. A periodic pattern indicator minus its exact density has its complete Gaussian Poisson error; summing every pattern retains arbitrary-power decay when Q=product P<=X^(1-delta), delta>0 fixed. Its positive normalization Z(u)=exp(tau/2)e^u+O_A(X^(-A)) is comparable to X. Constants are uniform in the chosen moving prime list under that Q restriction.

For every Boolean B,

    sum_S Z_S(B)^2=1/pi(B)<=Q,
    |q_D(B)|<=sqrt Q,
    |a_P(B)-q_D(B)|^2<=4Q.                               (Q10)

The L1-law error epsilon_X therefore changes the discarded squared energy by at most4Q epsilon_X. Applying Cauchy in the actual positive measure, with |r_P chi|<=1, proves the COMPLETE uniform field error

    |F_chi-F_(P,D,chi)|
      <=Z(u)[rho_D+2sqrt(Q epsilon_X)].                    (Q11)

No favorable occupancy pattern, complement or rough-tail phase was removed. The large possible sup norm of q_D is explicitly priced; it cannot be replaced by1. Since arbitrary powers are available for epsilon_X, multiplication by Q and then by Z is paid under the stated period restriction.

Divisibility and complete multiplicativity of the fixed character give

    sum_(p|n)r_P(n)chi(n)g_tau(log n-u)
       =chi(p) D_p R_(P,chi)(u), D_pV(u)=V(u-log p).

The same identity holds for an intersection of distinct primes, so expanding every centered factor gives exactly C5. Character zeros cause the corresponding shifted term to vanish; no division by chi(p) occurs. At full degree it factors as product_(p in P)(I-2chi(p)D_p)R and reconstructs the original field. At lower degree every nonzero term still contains the literal factor I-2chi(2)D_2, or the identity when2 is ramified. Every shifted scale and its infinite Gaussian tail remains.

Explicitly, with every complement taken inside P, the coded scalar is

    F_(P,D,chi)=sum_(S subset P, |S|<=D) (-2)^|S|
       * product_(p notin S)(1-2/p)
       * product_(p in S)(chi(p)D_p-I/p) R_(P,chi).         (Q11a)

Its complete squared norm retains every ordered pair of these terms and both shifted Gaussian profiles; no termwise absolute or diagonal estimate is substituted for it.

If rho_D^2<=X^(-2c-eta), c=1-gamma, Q11 is O(X^(gamma-eta/2))+O_A(X^(-A)). Thus the complete shell norm of the coded field at gamma implies the same exponent for the fixed original field; the reverse implication follows from the same error. This is an exponent equivalence for a chosen family satisfying the paid tail, not a free arithmetic estimate. No Mellin transform is assigned to a shellwise moving codec.

When p<=z<=C log X, the deliberately coarse integer harmonic estimate lambda<=4(1+log z)=O(loglog X) is valid. Substituting D=ceil((2c+eta)log X/loglog X) into Chernoff gives exponent-2c-eta+o(1). Use a smaller positive buffer, e.g. eta/2, for Q11; do not claim the exact same eta survives the o(1). If D>=|P| the omitted part is zero. The leading degree coefficients .250278,1/3,1/2 at the current,1/6,1/4 calibrations are correct. This is not a proof that small fixed degree or a small number of retained states suffices.

Finally m(B;u)=E_actual[r_P chi|B] has modulus<=1 but is unknown. Because |a_P m|<=1, replacing its outer distribution by pi costs at most epsilon_X, after which

    F_chi/Z=sum_S A_S E_pi[m Z_S]+O(epsilon_X).             (Q12)

A low-degree m-energy bound at X^(-2c+epsilon) is sufficient, but stronger than merely bounding its one retained scalar. All signed interactions are in that scalar; bounding energy can lose useful cancellation. The reference example m=a_P gives full correlation1 despite independent exposed bits and E_pi a_P=0. It is a legal bounded-response toy, not actual f3. Hence random revelation or marginal entropy supplies no arithmetic saving. Credit W38's source-law distinctions, W41/G54 full conditional covariance and W44 audit12; the present added contract is Q9–11 plus the literal centered-dilation realization.

## 5. R1–8 and wildcard02: exact failure scope

For finite P, f_P retains f3 on P-smooth integers and zero elsewhere. Its Euler series E_P has the author's factors at all prime powers and is absolutely convergent for Re(s)>0. Weighted Gaussian Fubini and Plancherel prove

    ||e^(-sigma u)V_P(u)||_2^2
      =e^(tau sigma^2)/(2pi)
         integral_R e^(-tau t^2)|E_P(sigma+it)|^2 dt.       (Q13)

For n<=P the coefficient is exactly f3(n). Taking P_X=ceil(2X exp(C sqrt(log X))) puts all missing coefficients in a decreasing full Gaussian tail, yielding R3 uniformly on the shell. If a polynomial bound ||e^(-sigma u)V_P||<=P^kappa were true, multiplying back by e^(sigma u) on that shell would return exponent sigma+kappa+o(1). The budgets at sigma=.6 are therefore .274861 for a strict first gain, .233333... for1/6, and .15 for1/4. The chosen upper growth of P_X is essential for those numerical costs.

The polynomial certificate is false at each fixed1/2<sigma<1. For p>=5, the absolutely convergent local logarithm gives

    log|(1-2p^(-s))/(1-p^(-s))|
          =-Re(p^(-s))+O_sigma(p^(-2sigma)).

The summed remainder is uniformly bounded. The2/3 factors are nonzero and bounded above/below near t=0 at fixed sigma in that open interval. Uniformly for a in[5pi/6,7pi/6], PNT partial summation gives

    sum_(p<=P)p^(-sigma-ia/log P)
      =P^(1-sigma)/log P * [e^(-ia)/(1-sigma)+o_sigma(1)]. (Q14)

I independently verified the primary input in [Johnston–Yang, arXiv:2204.01980v2, Corollary1.3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2204.01980), PDF page2, header20 April2022, accessed12 October2026. Only pi(y)~y/log y is used. No particular sharp error constant or their other zero-free claims are imported. To derive Q14, discard y<=P^b, b<1 fixed, at cost O(P^(b(1-sigma))); on the rest the PNT error is uniform. Put y=P e^(-v); bounded v contributes e^(-ia) times the integral of e^(-(1-sigma)v), and a fixed then growing v cutoff controls the tail uniformly in a. This justifies the moving height rather than citing a fixed-height asymptotic outside its range.

Since cos a<=-sqrt3/2, there is fixed slack for

    log|E_P(sigma+it)|
      >= P^(1-sigma)/(2(1-sigma)log P)

throughout a t interval of length pi/(3log P). Its Gaussian weight tends uniformly to1. Q13 gives R7 with a fixed positive prefactor, or a slightly smaller exponential constant if desired. The norm is larger than every P^kappa. The negative finite diagnostic at sigma=.874861,P=100000 is correctly retained: the result is asymptotic, with no claimed explicit onset.

This is actual f3/Gaussian forcing, beyond W41-28's nonconvergence of an unrenormalized Euler reciprocal. It does not prove a physical-shell lower bound, nor refute renormalization, a different source norm or causal restriction. Audit30 below further locates the failure. Finite divisor shifts being nilpotent, and Euler factors having finite spectrum{1}, do not control their norm or output. “Signed” alone does not repair the global certificate.

Wildcard02's local Laurent calculation is valid: if L(s)=(s-rho)^m u(s), distinct positive powers L^(-k) have distinct highest pole orders km, so a nonzero coefficient on the highest k cannot be canceled by the others with fixed constants. A nonvanishing Gaussian multiplier preserves it. Inverse Mellin gives x^rho times log-polynomials, not a lower x exponent. This is old amplification/pole-detection mechanism with new arithmetic powers and cross-Grams unpaid; there is no third independent arithmetic gain hidden in it.

## 6. Protected parked audit30: causal Schur elimination and escaping mass

This audit uses the author's actual finite-prime source, not a toy PSD matrix. Fix finite P and write, on H_sigma=L2(R,e^(-2sigma u)du), sigma>0,

    A_P=product_(p<=P)(I-D_p),
    B_P=product_(p<=P,p!=3)(I-2D_p),
    V_P=A_P^(-1)B_P g_tau.                                (S1)

Here g_tau is even, so g_tau(u)=g_tau(-u), the n=1 source. Each D_p is the causal delay u->u-log p with norm p^(-sigma). Thus A_P is boundedly invertible by convergent causal geometric series for this finite prime set. Its inverse has exactly the positive P-smooth coefficients1. Expanding S1 yields literal f_P, including all powers. Equivalently, the coefficient identity is

    mu_(P-smooth,squarefree) * f_P
       = (-2)^omega(n) 1_(n squarefree, primes<=P, 3 not dividing n). (S2)

Let U=log X, V=log(2X), and split the u-axis into L=(-infinity,U), I=[U,V], R=(V,infinity). A causal delay never carries a future input to an earlier output. Thus A_P and B_P are lower triangular in this time decomposition. Moreover their II blocks are the identity: every nonidentity delay has log d>=log2, so cannot connect two points of I except a measure-zero endpoint. Consequently, with b=B_P g_tau,

    (V_P)_L=(A_P)_LL^(-1)b_L,
    (V_P)_I=b_I-(A_P)_IL(A_P)_LL^(-1)b_L.                 (S3)

All LR/IR future-input blocks are zero. The relevant Schur feedback product is exactly zero, and the II Schur complement is I. The surviving past injection in S3 is not zero and has not been estimated. This is a source-exact answer to the parked card's “unit feedback eigenvalue” first test: that proposed obstruction is absent for this natural causal split, while the difficult signed forcing remains. One cannot infer a small solution from the trivial complement. The prior T37 PSD completion-of-squares objection remains correct for its different quadratic elimination; no nonnegative residual is being dropped here.

The naive separate estimate of the inverse past propagation is costly. The full H_sigma norm of A_P^(-1) is

    product_(p<=P)(1-p^(-sigma))^(-1),                    (S4)

because its Fourier multiplier attains that upper value at t=0. The left-half-line compression has the same norm: first truncate its positive, absolutely summable weighted convolution to finitely many delays, test a long weighted plateau far to the left, and then let the convolution truncation increase. The omitted tail has arbitrarily small operator norm for fixed P. For fixed sigma<1, PNT makes the logarithm of S4 asymptotic to P^(1-sigma)/((1-sigma)log P). So this easy bound is superpolynomial too. Cancellation between b_I and the entire past injection, or a source-specific bound on their sum, is indispensable. Splitting them and paying the generic inverse recreates the old obstacle.

There is a sharper localization of R7. Uniformly in P, |f_P(n)|<=1, so for u>=0,

    |V_P(u)|<=sum_n g_tau(log n-u)<=C_tau e^u.

This follows by comparing the positive unimodal summand with its integral plus a bounded maximum. For u<=0, expand the Gaussian square: n^(u/tau)<=1 and sum_n exp(-(log n)^2/(2tau))<infinity, giving |V_P(u)|<=C_tau exp(-u^2/(2tau)). Therefore for every fixed T>0 and1/2<sigma<1,

    ||1_(u<=T log P)e^(-sigma u)V_P||_2
                       <=C_(sigma,tau,T) P^(T(1-sigma)).  (S5)

Combining S5 with R7 and orthogonality of the two half-line projections proves

    ||1_(u>T log P)e^(-sigma u)V_P||_2
          /||e^(-sigma u)V_P||_2 -> 1                    (S6)

for EVERY fixed T. The superpolynomial norm escapes beyond x=P^T for any fixed polynomial scale. This is a proved strengthening of “may be remote smooth-number scales”; it uses no new arithmetic cancellation. With P_X=X^(1+o(1)), the physical shell is in the polynomial-scale part and cannot be assigned the global lower bound. The forward causal formulation S3 has no return from those later output scales.

The useful survivor is therefore the exact signed scalar in S3, measured on I, with the R3 tail restored. Its complete exponent gamma is equivalent to the original F exponent when C is chosen to put R3 below gamma. A source-specific upper bound for S3 remains OPEN. No contraction or cheap Schur complement has supplied one. Relative to the index, S1–3 adapt the existing finite incidence/Schur machinery, while S5–6 are a precise new localization consequence of W45's actual-source obstruction. Independent finite checks verify S2 and the exact blocks through n=96, primes2/3/5/7; the continuous and asymptotic arguments above, not that finite check, prove S1–6.

## 7. Uniform parked audit21: actual cocycle and a paid future inverse

The seed's strongest objection needs qualification. A fixed dilation filter resonates on a prescribed vertical line; it need not resonate at an arbitrary hypothetical zero. Take the same fixed complete F_chi and a prime p with chi(p)!=0. Define

    G_(p,chi)(u)=F_chi(u)-p chi(p)F_chi(u-log p).           (T1)

Its literal coefficient at n is f3(n)chi(n)-p chi(p)1_(p|n)f3(n/p)chi(n/p). For p!=3, write k=v_p(n). Relative to f3(n)chi(n), the factor is1 if k=0,1+p if k=1, and1-p if k>=2. For p=3 it is1 at k=0 and1-p thereafter. In particular p=2 gives coefficients1,-3chi(2),+chi(2)^2 at1/2/4, with the positive-power tail retained. These are NOT the original compact A coefficients1,-3,2. If chi(p)=0 then T1=F_chi and every divisible coefficient remains naturally zero. No ramified value is inverted.

Let a=p chi(p), h=log p. Finite telescoping is exact:

    F_chi(u)=a^(-K)F_chi(u+Kh)
                  -sum_(j=1..K)a^(-j)G_(p,chi)(u+jh).    (T2)

Use the inherited complete all-shell baseline ||F_chi||_[X,2X]<=C_b X^b for some fixed b<1. For the untwisted field this is already paid through G28; for another character this paragraph applies only when its own inherited bound is supplied. Then the first term of T2 tends to zero in L2 of every fixed shell, with bound C_b X^b p^(-K(1-b)). Thus

    F_chi(u)=-sum_(j>=1)(p chi(p))^(-j)G_(p,chi)(u+jh).  (T3)

If the COMPLETE G all-shell norm is <=C X^(gamma+epsilon), gamma+epsilon<1, Minkowski gives the explicit future cost

    ||F_chi||_[X,2X]
      <= C X^(gamma+epsilon)/(p^(1-gamma-epsilon)-1).     (T4)

Use exact real shells or their fixed dyadic covering. Conversely T1 costs at most1+p^(1-gamma-epsilon) times the corresponding F norm, up to that fixed covering. For every1/2<gamma<1, the two all-epsilon exponent statements are equivalent. The boundary uses the existing b<1, not the desired improved gamma, and the same fixed field is evaluated at all future scales. A moving prime, filter or profile would require a new uniform mismatch analysis.

The multiplier is1-p chi(p)p^(-s). Its zeros have Re(s)=1 when chi(p) is a unit, so it does not kill any hypothetical zero in1/2<Re(s)<1. Multiplying Q6 by it gives the full source zero return; at p=2 this adds a second copy of N_chi, both with zeros only on the right edge. The homogeneous resonant solutions have exponential real growth1 and are excluded by the actual baseline boundary. A naive past inverse at gamma<1 would diverge, but that does not refute the paid future inverse T3.

For example, at p=2 the exact shell energy is

    ||G_2||_I^2=||F||_I^2+4|chi(2)|^2||D_2F||_I^2
       -4 Re[chi(2) integral_I D_2F(u)overline(F(u))du].  (T5)

The mixed term and shifted shell remain. No fresh bound for T5 below gamma=.874861 has been proved, so no1/6 or1/4 arithmetic credit follows. This is a concrete repair of the seed's generic resonance worry and a complete actual-source contract, not a new mechanism family. W01-A/WA11–13, Sol wave01-c RCC3, Sol-match01-max [restricted research revision] and [private research revision]/G52 own the future/causal inverse ancestry. The special f3 coefficient table and explicit fixed-character masks are this audit's adaptation. The independent receipt verifies1920 exact coefficient cases, including nonreal chi5 and ramified chi4, and nine finite T2 identities over Gaussian rational coefficients. Infinite boundary decay and exponent equivalence are proved above, not inferred from those cases.

## 8. Every card's independent disposition

U means no author or critic mathematical test in this batch, not false. D/T refer to actual author development/test; A is a newly performed critic audit. All original seeds, typicalities and reach aspirations remain in the frozen source.

## 7. Controller observation: the full-cutoff contract is Mertens-equivalent

Credit the controller for identifying this additional equivalence, recorded in `[restricted provenance path] mathematical source]`. The argument below was reconstructed independently. The eta=0 endpoint and the parity-rounded N30 inversion are reviewer extensions. None proves the open bound.

Fix chi,tau and 1/2<sigma<=gamma<1, eta=gamma-sigma>=0. Suppose Q<<_epsilon X^(eta+epsilon) holds for **every sufficiently large real X** and every admissible even K in either one of the two bands. The forward proof only needs the particular admissible even-order choice at each integer Y displayed below; full-X uniformity supplies it. This is stronger in its cutoff quantifier than the dyadic-only sufficient family used in Section 5.

For every sufficiently large integer Y put u=log Y. To use band I choose

    K=2ceil(sqrt(u)/2),  X=Y^(K-1/2),  L=(K-1/2)u.

Then K/L^(1/3)->1, because K^2/u->1; hence K is admissible. The prescribed cutoff is exactly floor(exp(L/(K-1/2)))=Y. To use band II alone, choose instead

    K=2ceil(u/[8(log u)^2]),  X=Y^(K-1/2).

Here K~u/[4(log u)^2], L~u^2/[4(log u)^2], and sqrt(L)/log L~u/[4(log u)^2]~K. Again the admissibility ratio tends to 1, with ample room inside [2/5,2]. Both choices tend to infinity and hit every integer Y exactly. Integer rounding changes only O(1) in K.

Write P_Y(t)=M_Y(sigma+it), A=|P_Y(0)| and

    D_Y=C_sigma Y^(1-sigma)log Y >=1.

The elementary derivative bound |P_Y'(t)|<=D_Y holds for every real t. If A<1, the required upper bound is immediate since eta>=0. If A>=1, on |t|<=min(1,A/(2D_Y)) the amplitude is at least A/2. This interval has length at least 1/D_Y after increasing the fixed constant if necessary, and the Gaussian has a positive lower bound on [-1,1]. Therefore

    Q >= c_tau (A/2)^K / D_Y.

Combining with the assumed Q bound yields

    A <= 2(C_epsilon D_Y/c_tau)^(1/K)
                Y^((1-1/(2K))(eta+epsilon)).              (23)

For every requested delta>0, fix epsilon<delta/2 first. Then let Y tend to infinity. The derivative-width cost is Y^((1-sigma)/K) times (C log Y)^(1/K)=Y^o(1); the constant raised to 1/K and the factor 2 are also harmless. Thus

    |sum_{n<=Y} a(n)n^(-sigma)| <<_delta Y^(eta+delta)

for every integer Y, with the finite initial range absorbed. This remains valid at eta=0. Abel inversion of the weighted partial sums B(z) is exact:

    sum_{n<=Y} a(n)=Y^sigma B(Y)
                  -sigma integral_1^Y z^(sigma-1)B(z)dz.

It gives M_chi(Y)<<_delta Y^(gamma+delta). No prior subunit Mertens input was used.

Conversely, suppose this Mertens bound holds for every delta>0. For fixed sigma<=gamma, choose positive delta and use Abel summation to obtain

    |P_Y(t)| <<_delta (1+|t|)Y^(gamma-sigma+delta).

Integrating its Kth power against the fixed Gaussian costs exp(O_delta(Klog(K+2))). Uniformly in either allowed band, Klog Y<=L K/(K-1/2)=L+o(L), Klog K=o(L), and K tends to infinity. After allocating delta relative to epsilon, this proves Q<<X^(eta+epsilon). Thus the full-X Q contract is exponent-equivalent to Mertens, also at eta=0. By Section 6, the full-X one-sided Core contract is equivalent too.

The recovered Mertens bound immediately makes sum a(n)n^(-s) holomorphic on Re(s)>gamma by Abel summation, locally uniformly on compact subsets. It equals 1/L(s,chi) initially in Re(s)>1. The ordinary meromorphic continuation then excludes zeros in Re(s)>gamma, retaining the principal-pole exclusion and including nonprincipal s=1. This direct moment/core route has no N11 premise and needs no future-Gamma reconstruction. Its arithmetic difficulty has not decreased: the open exponent is exactly the desired improved Mertens exponent.

Do not apply (23) to a merely dyadic-X hypothesis. Dyadic cutoffs need not hit every integer Y; their gaps can have order Y/K and a positive-power absolute price. Neither trivial interpolation nor the choice X=Y^(K-1/2) is available there. The safe implication for the dyadic balanced-source/moment subfamily remains Section 5 under its growth input. No equivalence with that weaker sampling hypothesis has been proved here.

## Signed bands and what the Gram proves

The monotone coefficient selectors give literal disjoint threshold
bands. Their local jump condition is p|n and omega_p(n)=1. The
asymptotic doubled-cutoff band requires both t and 2t inside the
proved range and t tending to infinity. Under those conditions it
is -1/2 times the old prefix to relative o(1). Individual prime
jumps are not assigned that sign.

The Gaussian remains uncapped, so its exact terminal reconstruction
is dominated infinite telescoping, not a finite threshold identity.
The shell norm has leading factor 3/2 because
integral_X^(2X) x^2 dx/x=3X^2/2. The finite Gram includes every
off-diagonal entry. Killing its leading vector yields only the
stated logarithmic field error, with no new power saving.

For the actual complement R=F-T, write a=||T||, b=||R|| and d=||F||.
The exact identity

    d^2=(a-b)^2+2ab(1+rho)

retains both norm mismatch and the cosine defect. Normalization by
the actual a^2 gives the power-small Gram error from the previously
accepted full-field bound. Normalization by a leading asymptotic
does not preserve that rate. F50 correctly requires improvement of
both terms and is equivalent to the requested full-field bound,
with epsilon renamed. No masked convolution transfer is used.

The result directly fills the missing literal f3 rough-depth estimate.
Its leading field has exponent one even at the largest proved cutoff.

formal-kernel evidence are unchanged by this theorem.

statement:
## 4. Development23: the exact large-prime response diameter

Let X>=4, sqrt(X)<=y<=X, and prescribe completely multiplicative unit values z_p for p<=y, with z_p=0 at p|q0. For p>y, p not dividing q0, initially allow independent unit phases. Extend completely multiplicatively, put a_z(n)=mu(n)z(n), and set

    S_y(X)=sum_(n<=X; Pplus(n)<=y)a_z(n),
    A(t)=sum_(m<=t)a_z(m),        1<=t<=X/y<=y.

Here Pplus(1)=1, and A depends only on the fixed low-prime data. Every squarefree n<=X with a prime factor>y has exactly one such factor p, occurring once, and n=pm with m<=X/p<p. Hence its coefficient is exactly -z_p a_z(m), including the ramified zeros. Therefore

    M_z(X)=S_y(X)-sum_(y<p<=X; p not dividing q0)
                                      z_p A(X/p).       (P1)

Both the whole smooth sector and the whole complementary prime sector are retained. Repeated-prime terms vanish by mu, rather than being assigned arbitrary signs. No coprimality factor is missing because m<p.

Define R_y(X)=sum_(y<p<=X;p not dividing q0)|A(X/p)|. Independent phase alignment yields

    max_z |M_z(X)-S_y(X)|=R_y(X),
    max_(z,z') |M_z(X)-M_z'(X)|=2R_y(X).               (P2)

The first upper bound is the triangle inequality. To attain it in direction e^(it), choose z_p=-e^(it) conjugate(A(X/p))/|A(X/p)| when A!=0, and choose an arbitrary unit value when A=0. Opposite directions attain the diameter. If the low values are real signs, S_y and every A are real, and the choices z_p=-sign(A) and z_p=sign(A), with any sign at 0, give exactly S_y+R_y and S_y-R_y. T3 realizes both by actual real Dirichlet characters having identical low-prime data and the same ramified zeros up toX. In particular at least one has |M_chi(X)|>=R_y(X).

There is an exact endpoint-sensitive cofactor formula. With pi_q0(t) counting primes<=t not dividing q0,

    R_y(X)=sum_(1<=m<=floor(X/y)) |A(m)|
      [pi_q0(X/m)-pi_q0(max(y,X/(m+1)))].               (P3)

The lower prime endpoint is strict and the upper endpoint inclusive, exactly as floor(X/p)=m requires. The possible terminal empty interval contributes 0. For y<=X/2 the m=1 term alone gives

    R_y(X)>=pi_q0(X)-pi_q0(X/2).                       (P4)

For fixed q0 and growing X, ordinary PNT makes this (1/2+o(1))X/log X. Only the ordinary PNT is used here, not a character prime theorem or any zero-free improvement; its asymptotic is documented in [NIST DLMF §27.12](https://dlmf.nist.gov/27.12), verified2026-10-12. P1–P3 and the exact inequality P4 do not need PNT.

The finite checks include nontrivial natural ramification. For (X,y,q0)=(120,11,1), S=2,R=17 and the two character sums are 19,-15. For (120,11,3), S=1,R=15 and sums 16,-14. For (255,16,5), S=-2,R=38 and sums 36,-40. Every full enumeration agrees with P1–P3; the receipt stores the realizing moduli.

This is a precise obstruction to a phase-blind small-prime certificate that attempts to pay the complement at any fixed exponent<1 uniformly over its compatible characters. It is NOT an asymptotic counterexample for one fixed character and not a lower bound for its actual Mertens energy. The two realizing moduli generally differ, and the extra natural zeros beyondX are different.

There is also a simple reason the fixed-modulus escape is real. Two characters modulo one fixed q that agree on all primes<=q not dividing q agree on every unit residue: factor its least positive representative r<=q into those primes. The zero classes agree by the modulus. Thus once y>=q, the low-prime values determine the whole character. At y=sqrt X this happens for X>=q^2. The adversarial independent tail is then unavailable. A useful next estimate must exploit that global linkage, rather than claim P2 is an obstruction for all sufficiently large X at one fixed q.
title: 4. Development23: the exact large-prime response diameter

## 4. The new weight is a genuine part of the outside mass

For a plain ideal b write

    ell_rad,J(b)=sum_(p in J,p|b)log Np,
    d_1,J(b)=sum_(p in J,v_p(b)=1)(log Np)^2.

Exact ordered-pair expansion gives

    omega(b)=[ell_rad,J(b)^2-d_1,J(b)]/(log Nb)^2.     (8)

The diagonal is included exactly once when p^2|b, even if v_p(b)>2.
Thus no higher valuation is silently omitted: every such b appears in the
remaining cofactor sum. The weight is defined by divisibility of a pair,
not by choosing two independently labelled occurrences in b.

Let ell_J(b)=sum_(p in J)v_p(b)log Np. Since J=[Z,A) is disjoint from
the previous CLOSED band[A,Y],

    0<=omega(b)<=ell_J(b)^2/(log Nb)^2
                  <=(1-theta(b))^2<=1-theta(b).       (9)

Consequently B^[1-theta-omega]=B^[1-theta]-B^[omega]
is an exact subtraction from the old remaining coefficient. There is no
product theta*omega to estimate and no reintroduction of the old band.
In particular a plain ideal entirely supported on the old band still has
zero remaining coefficient.

This avoids an invalid shortcut: bounding M S^[omega] Q alone would not
bound the tuple-cut core by a signed-subset inequality. Section7 pays the
whole weighted removed source explicitly.

## 7. Complete counted decomposition, rows, tails and original scope

For the original high-row weighted count in this fixed source window, the resulting rigorous implication is

    sum_high |Q_u|^2
       <= H_J U^[E_K-1/2000+epsilon]
          + sum_(u in B_sep)|Q_u|^2,                  (F21)

where B_sep consists of actual buffered rows admitting compatible F14--F16 witnesses in the strict coarse box F3 and the endpoint-padded adaptive box F19. Their profiles come from the exact original/complementary cutoff and the same annular far product; F20a--F20b justify the simplified residual presentation. The inequality counts a union of sets, so it does not require an artificial probability law or independent samples. The first term includes:

* Prefix-active rows, by F10--F13.
* Every far annulus for which either representation has an easy saturated inverse or plain witness, by F17--F19.
* Annuli too high for any original saturated product, the genuine exponential terminal tail, and the discarded common-profile Fourier tails.
* All finite dictionary/attaining labels, dyadic and scale-supremum costs, required real/height derivatives, bounded subunit windows and original natural zeros.

A fixed dictionary's exceptional sixth-free rows supported entirely on fixed primes form a fixed finite set, including its unit sectors. They can be kept as a separately counted complement even when a principal presentation prevents applying F4. The absolute original prime count gives |Q_u|^2<=H_J U^(v+epsilon), so their entire weighted mass is O_fixed(U^(v+epsilon)). This is well below F2: E_K>=rho>=19/54, v<=1/20; indeed delta-3k=4delta^2/h>0 and G<=3kv. No unit row is declared oscillatory. Where the original density family excludes these rows, the same calculation simply verifies that this separate restoration is affordable. If considering a fixed finite list of raw sixth-power-core families, their O(U^(1/6)) roots cost at most U^(1/6+v+epsilon), also below F2; the receipt verifies that strict comparison. This does NOT generalize F21 to an arbitrary raw moving-support family. Such a lift retains its existing normalization and natural-hole obligations.

For bounded U the threshold is enlarged and fixed constants pay the finite range. For heights beyond the retained small polynomial range the original row/slot absolute bound U^(1+v+epsilon) is absorbed by increasing the fixed power of(1+T). For the retained range, choose B after raw powers, the tail orders after B, and the final height exponent after the returned seminorm order. This is the same source order as the completed identity and buffered moments; a row or live height does not set a threshold.

There is no merged-pair projection in the proof of F21. All valuations, common factors and unequal roots/dyads occur in F14; no squarefree identity for mu(n)A_R(n) was used. Both signs in F14 are preserved. The identity differentiates exactly as needed in the common parameters. Prefix/far cross terms of an ambient positive norm are not claimed to have vanished. We bound the zero-event count by the actual signal and positive exceptional sets instead. The fixed product H remains part of every actual annular weight.

The original R22 signed norm and its old t=4/3 small-core/conductor payments remain unchanged. F21 is a different sufficient source reduction which covers the same high-row count if its remaining joint input is supplied. It must not be advertised as a bound for a selected R22 pair sector. Both physical projectors, clipped rectangles, moving-support reconstruction, genuine joint label counts, raw-root holes and tails, low/high/zero/extracted/fixed-inducing branches, actual6a/9a radii, physical K_phys^(5/6), no-slot/shortening complements, weighted Euler shifts including zero capacity, principal residue and common-Delta supremum feedback retain their accepted c11 contracts. None is repriced here and no centered M/24 reserve is spent.

statement:
## A. A weaker complete moment with a paid moving-order return

### A1. Source, fixed localization and exact Fourier formula

Let a(n) be a fixed complex coefficient sequence with

    C_B=sum_(n>=1)|a(n)| n^(-B)<infinity                    (A1)

for some fixed B>0. Fix tau,kappa>0 independently of X. Put

    F(x)=sum_n a(n)g_tau(log(n/x)), h=log2,
    W_X(v)=g_kappa(v) F(X exp(v)),
    sigma=tau+kappa, nu=tau*kappa/sigma, alpha=kappa/sigma,
    w_n=log(n/X), b_X(n)=g_sigma(w_n).                     (A2)

Here g_t is the normalized Gaussian of variance t. This is the COMPLETE original field; no prime, pair, height, cutoff or sign is discarded. The Gaussian product identity is exactly

    g_kappa(v)g_tau(w-v)=g_sigma(w)g_nu(v-alpha*w).        (A3)

With hat f(t)=integral_R f(v)exp(-itv)dv, absolute Fubini gives

    hat W_X(t)=exp(-nu*t^2/2)
               sum_n a(n)b_X(n)exp(-i alpha*t*w_n).       (A4)

Indeed sum |a(n)|b_X(n)<=C_B X^B sup_w[e^(Bw)g_sigma(w)]
=C_B X^B exp(sigma B^2/2)/sqrt(2pi sigma). Thus for a constant C,

    |hat W_X(t)|<=C X^B exp(-nu*t^2/2), X>=1.            (A5)

This source-only bound is uniform at every real height. No continued Dirichlet series is interchanged on a nonabsolute line. All fixed derivatives and all displayed field series converge normally on compact real windows. The original ordinary a(n)=mu(n)chi(n), A(n)chi(n) or f3(n)chi(n) satisfy A1 for B>1; these are POINTWISE character twists, not Dirichlet convolutions, and ramified zeros remain literal. A sum over ideals is also covered verbatim by replacing n with its norm and assuming the corresponding absolute series, as holds for a fixed original Hecke coefficient family. This statement does not infer angular/growing-conductor uniformity.

For any real r>=0 define

    N_r(X)^2=(2pi)^(-1) integral_R
              (1+t^2)^(-r)|hat W_X(t)|^2 dt.             (A6)

At r=0 this is ||W_X||_2^2. For every T>=1,

    ||W_X||_2 <= (1+T^2)^(r/2) N_r(X)
                    + C' X^B exp(-nu*T^2/2).           (A7)

Split the Fourier integral at T; the Gaussian tail integral is at most a fixed constant times exp(-nu*T^2) for T>=1. Take square roots and use sqrt(a+b)<=sqrt(a)+sqrt(b). Crucially the tail in A7 is the tail of W itself, so it is not multiplied by an inverse Sobolev weight.

### A2. Lossless range and critical cost

Let r_X>=0 be arbitrary, and set

    d=limsup_(X->infinity) r_X loglog X/log X < infinity. (A8)

Suppose for every epsilon>0 and all sufficiently large DYADIC X,

    N_(r_X)(X) <<_epsilon X^(eta+epsilon), eta>0.         (A9)

Then

    ||F||_(L2([X,2X],dx/x))
         <<_epsilon X^(eta+d/2+epsilon)                 (A10)

on all sufficiently large dyadic shells. Proof: choose any A>0 and fix M>2(B+A)/nu. Set T=sqrt(M log X). The high part in A7 is O(X^-A). By A8,

    log[(1+M log X)^(r_X/2)]/log X <= d/2+o(1).

Finally g_kappa has a fixed positive minimum on [0,h], so the original shell norm is at most a fixed multiple of ||W_X||_2. All choices are frozen before X; epsilon in A9 is chosen smaller than the final requested buffer. No finite numerical sample or typicality label enters A10.

In particular r_X=o(log X/loglog X) has ZERO power loss. A fixed negative order, or one tending to infinity arbitrarily slowly below this threshold, gives the same every-epsilon exponent as the complete shell moment. This strengthens the fixed-order interpolation sketch without asserting a new arithmetic estimate.

The converse exponent implication is also exact: if the complete shell moment is O_epsilon(X^(eta+epsilon)), then N_(r_X)(X) has that bound for EVERY choice r_X>=0. Since N_r<=||W_X||_2, split the whole v-line into fixed dyadic-length intervals. On v in[kh,(k+1)h], the field argument lies on the shell of scale X2^k. The Gaussian g_kappa(v)^2 makes the sum of exp(2(eta+epsilon)kh) times its maximum on that interval finite. The assumed large-shell bound extends to all positive shells: on a bounded range use local convergence, and near zero the original source has a Gaussian left tail. To see that last assertion directly, write log n-log x>=0 for x<=1 and use (log n-log x)^2>=(log n)^2+(log x)^2, then A1. If the original hypothesis is only dyadic, two neighboring dyadic shells cover every shifted real shell. Hence

    d=0: A9 iff the original complete moment at eta,     (A11)

with the usual every-epsilon quantifiers. For d>0 we claim only the sufficient return A10 and the unshifted converse just proved, not exponent equivalence.

### A3. Exact signed kernel and diagonal

For r>0 let

    E_(r,nu)(z)=1/Gamma(r) integral_0^infinity
       q^(r-1)exp(-q) g_(2(nu+q))(z)dq,
    E_(0,nu)(z)=g_(2nu)(z).                              (A12)

The elementary Gamma integral for (1+t^2)^-r and the Gaussian Fourier transform prove that E is the inverse transform of exp(-nu*t^2)(1+t^2)^-r. It is real, even and strictly positive. The exact scalar is therefore

    N_r(X)^2=sum_(n,m>=1) a(n)conj(a(m)) J_(r,X)(n,m),
    J_(r,X)(n,m)=b_X(n)b_X(m)
                    E_(r,nu)(alpha log(n/m)).           (A13)

Absolute convergence follows from (sum |a|b_X)^2<infinity and E(0)<=g_(2nu)(0). Every coefficient, prime power, character zero and ordered interaction is retained. For actual f3, the products remain signed. Entrywise positivity of J does not permit dropping negative terms. If |a(n)|<=C0, the true diagonal is O(X), uniformly for every r>=0, since sum_n g_sigma(log(n/X))^2=O_sigma(X). One proof groups n into dyads about X and sums the resulting Gaussian bound; both log tails converge. Divisor-bounded coefficient families give the corresponding X^(1+epsilon), not a silently identical diagonal constant.

For fixed tau,kappa, the new arithmetic target is the COMPLETE A13 at exponent2eta, optionally subtracting the explicitly paid diagonal when eta>1/2. There is no subset positivity claim. The Gaussian localizer includes both left and right physical tails with their exact weights.

### A4. Quantitative zero return and deliberately coarse allowance

For a(n)=mu(n)chi(n), absolute Mellin Fubini on Re s>1 gives exp(tau*s^2/2)/L(s,chi). A10 and dyadic Cauchy--Schwarz continue this transform holomorphically for Re s>eta+d/2. Multiplying by L continues the identity; the Gaussian multiplier is nonzero. Thus zeros there are excluded, with the usual principal pole at1 excepted. For actual a(n)=f3(n)chi(n) use its already paid nonvanishing-numerator/inverse-convolution return, in the fixed ordinary-character scope, and require eta+d/2>1/2. For the original ideal source a(mathfrak a)=mu_K(mathfrak a)eta(mathfrak a), the same direct Mellin proof applies with its own complete moment input; no transfer from an ordinary source to an ideal source is inferred.

The weakest sufficient condition in this construction for a first gain is

    eta+d/2 < .874864.                                  (A14)

Useful examples, all CONDITIONAL on the corresponding complete signed A13 bound:

| Arithmetic norm eta | Moving-order d | Returned boundary | Returned c |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
|.87449|.0007|.87484|.12516|
|5/6|.08|131/150=.873333...|19/150=.126666...|
|3/4|.24|.87|.13|
|5/6|0|5/6|1/6|
|3/4|0|3/4|1/4|

These are genuine complete analytic loss budgets, not ambitious endpoint names. For example eta=.75 allows d<.249728 to exceed c5. They do NOT show that the new scalar is easier to estimate. The continued arithmetic estimate is still wholly open. At fixed frequency, (1+t^2)^-r has only subpower decay in this range, so the old low-frequency coherent component is not automatically removed.

Strongest objection: an H^-r norm can hide high frequencies. A5/A7 pay precisely that obstruction for this actual Gaussian class. S45's raw atomic H^-r norm is a different, stronger hypothesis and cannot be substituted for A6. The claim is not a generic H^-r-to-L2 inequality, and no claim of optimality for d/2 on actual arithmetic sources is made.
