## 2. Development03: source identity and complete return

Fix one ordinary Dirichlet character chi of its presented modulus q and one tau>0. All natural zeros remain. Write c_p=chi(p), D_pV(x)=V(x/p), and
     
    F=sum f3(n)chi(n)g_tau(log(n/x)),
    B=sum b(n)chi(n)g_tau(log(n/x)),
    U=sum mu(n)chi(n)g_tau(log(n/x)),
    f3(n)=product_(p|n,p!=3)(-1),
    b(n)=product_(p|n,p>=5)(-1).

These are COMPLETE fixed fields. f3 includes2, unlike b; every positive power of2 changes sign. No ideal, angular or growing-conductor extension follows.

For z_p=c_p p^-s the exact Euler factors are

    D_b=H/L,
    H_2=H_3=(1-z)^-2,
    H_p=(1-2z)/(1-z)^2, p>=5,
    K=H^-1, K_2=K_3=(1-z)^2,
    K_p=1+z^2/(1-2z), p>=5.                        (R1)

Thus for p>=5,j>=2, h(p^j)=-(j-1),k(p^j)=2^(j-2); both first-prime coefficients vanish. At2,3, h(p^j)=j+1 and k is1,-2,1,0,... . All signs matter. At sigma>1/2 the nonconstant absolute local masses are r^2/(1-r)^2 and r^2/(1-2r), r=p^-sigma. Since2*5^-sigma<1 and sum_p p^-2sigma converges, full H_sigma,K_sigma are finite. At2,3 their masses are(1-r)^-2 and(1+r)^2. Ramified factors equal1. These same normally convergent products prove H and K nonzero on Re(s)>1/2.

For ||V||_sigma=sup_(X>0)X^-sigma||V||_(L2([X,2X],dx/x)), initial absolute Gaussian Fubini and then Minkowski give

    U=T_k B, B=T_h U,
    ||U||_sigma<=K_sigma||B||_sigma,
    ||B||_sigma<=H_sigma||U||_sigma.                (R2)

The left Gaussian tail pays every small scale; two neighboring dyads cover an arbitrary dilated shell. This is old G28 compensation with the corrected source. It does NOT say k*f3=mu: in fact

    K*F=U-2c_2 D_2 U,

with prime-two coefficients1,-3c_2,2c_2^2. The old exceptional A source is distinct from ordinary mu.

At every integer, including powers and ramified zeros,

    F=(I-2c_2 D_2)B,
    Mellin(F)=exp(tau s^2/2)(1-2c_2 2^-s)H(s)/L(s,chi). (R3)

If c_2!=0 the extra numerator vanishes only on Re(s)=1; if c_2=0 it is1. It is not discarded on the right boundary. All strip returns use the separate existing right-edge facts.

For c=c_2!=0, finite substitution gives

    B(x)=(2c)^-J B(2^J x)
                    -sum_(j=1..J)(2c)^-j F(2^j x). (R4)

The boundary does not tend to0 merely from O(x). Each fixed character's inherited ||U||_beta<infinity, theta6<beta<1, transfers to B by(R2), and bounds that boundary by ||B||_beta X^beta 2^-J(1-beta). It tends to0 on every fixed shell. The future series therefore converges in shell L2, and for1/2<sigma<1,

    ||B||_sigma<=[2^(1-sigma)-1]^-1||F||_sigma,
    ||F||_sigma<=[1+2^(1-sigma)]||B||_sigma.         (R5)

When c=0, F=B and nothing is inverted. The inherited beta<1 excludes the homogeneous growth-one modes; the desired improved estimate is not used to kill them. This is the established future-inverse mechanism, now including W45/G70, applied to this literal b/f3 pair.

The inherited baseline needs growth as well as zero-free holomorphy. For fixed q, periodic summation gives polynomial vertical growth of L on positive strips. Choose a zero-free line strictly between theta6 and beta. Analytic log L on buffered disks centered at Re(s)>1, normalized there by the absolutely convergent Euler logarithm, has real part O(log(2+|t|)). Borel--Caratheodory on smaller disks gives |log L|=O(log(2+|t|)); remove the principal pole first. Hence1/L has polynomial growth on the beta line/intervening strip. Gaussian Mellin shifting gives U=O_(chi,tau,beta)(x^beta) for x>=1, and the left tail gives the global norm. This uses the ACCEPTED buffered premise only. Constants depend on chi and the gap; holomorphy at a proposed new gamma is not assumed. ### 2.1 Finite composition, both errors, and conditional targets

Let beta in(theta6,1), sigma0 in(1/2,beta), R=floor(X^b0), J=ceil(a log_2 X). The author's finite retained source is

    Q_X=-sum_(r<=R) k(r)chi(r)
                     sum_(j=1..J)(2c)^-j F(2^j x/r). (R6)

For c=0 use sum_(r<=R)k(r)chi(r)F(x/r). Each summand is the SAME COMPLETE field, not an integer truncation. Exact substitution gives U-Q_X=E_2+E_K, where

No mixed term or signed-submask cost disappears. The sharp r<=R endpoint is literal; moving cutoffs are never held fixed at the wrong dilation.

## 6. The balanced kernel retains the zero it would need to exclude

This is a diagnostic for the new fixed profile, with an actual
Mellin identity as well as a continuous model. It is not an
explicit formula for Mobius.

The entire Mellin transform of K satisfies

\[
\mathcal J(s)=\int_0^\infty K(t)t^{s-1}\,dt
            =\zeta(s)\Phi(s). \tag{V25}
\]

The endpoint bounds (V6) prove entireness; absolute interchange
first proves the equality for Re s>1, then continuation proves
it everywhere. The zero of Phi at 1 cancels zeta's pole.

Put q=Y^2/N and J_q(s)=int_q^infinity K(t)t^(s-1)dt.
For fixed continuous coefficient modes A d^(rho-1) and
B e^(tau-1), exact change of variables p=de gives, when rho!=tau,

\[
I_{\rho,\tau}:=AB\int_Y^\infty\int_Y^\infty
d^{\rho-1}e^{\tau-1}K(de/N)\,dd\,de
=\frac{AB}{\rho-\tau}
\left[Y^{\tau-\rho}N^\rho J_q(\rho)
-Y^{\rho-\tau}N^\tau J_q(\tau)\right]. \tag{V26}
\]

The equal-label limit, with B=A, is
A^2 N^rho[log(N/Y^2)J_q(rho)+J_q'(rho)].
For Y=floor(sqrt(N)/log^2 N), replacing J_q and a fixed
number of its derivatives by J costs O_M(N^(-M)), including
the displayed polynomial factors. Constants depend on the
fixed labels and derivative orders.

Distinct zeta-zero labels cancel in this model since both
J-values vanish. Equal simple labels instead leave
A^2 N^rho zeta'(rho)Phi(rho). For A=1/zeta'(rho), this is
N^rho Phi(rho)/zeta'(rho), precisely the individual pole
contribution. Here equal means rho=tau, not conjugate pairing.

Multiple zeros do not avoid the resonance. Differentiating
(V26) produces logarithmic density modes. At distinct labels
of orders m,n, derivatives j<m, k<n still cancel. At an
equal label of order m, the first nonzero derivatives have
j+k=m-1 and coefficient
AB N^rho j!k! J^(m)(rho)/m!. This follows by expanding the
leading divided difference (u^m-v^m)/(u-v). Higher derivatives
have additional terms. No simplicity assumption is needed
for this model obstruction.

For the ACTUAL Mobius coefficients and each fixed finite Y,
M_Y(s)=sum_(n<=Y)mu(n)n^(-s), Mellin inversion on c>1 gives

\[
\sum_{d,e>Y}\mu(d)\mu(e)K(de/N)
=\frac1{2\pi i}\int_{(c)}
\Phi(s)N^s
\left[\frac1{\zeta(s)}-2M_Y(s)+\zeta(s)M_Y(s)^2\right]\,ds.
\tag{V27}
\]

The bracket follows exactly from J(s)(1/zeta-M_Y)^2.
The last two terms are analytic at every zeta zero. Thus the
full polar part of this integrand equals that of Phi(s)N^s/zeta(s).
No contour shift across those poles, uniformly convergent
zero expansion, or summation of fixed-mode errors is asserted.
The extra cancellation found in (V26) does not bound the
remaining diagonal resonances or improve (V10).

Status: written results for independent review. No new arithmetic exponent or zero-free constant is established. The accepted source-relative bound remains c6=.125139, theta6=.874861. statement:
### N29 — Merge the prime-coefficient criteria; then vary the height geometry

A's density-subtracted log criterion and B's completed Laguerre criterion encode the same zero obstruction after a known analytic factor. Let \(Z(s)=(s-1)\zeta(s)\), \(s(z)=b+r(1+z)/(1-z)\), \(b>0\), \(b+r>1\). If \(\ell_n\) are the Taylor coefficients of \(\log Z(s(z))\), and \(a_n\) those of \(s'(z)\xi'/\xi(s(z))\), then
\[
a_n=(n+1)\ell_{n+1}+h_n,
\]
where \(h_n\) comes explicitly from the nonvanishing factor
\(\xi(s)/Z(s)=(s/2)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\). A11 supplies the exact formulas. They are complementary arithmetic representations, not independent zero-free criteria.

Subexponential coefficient growth is equivalent to zero-freeness in \(\Re s>b\). The prime-side objects are explicit density-subtracted polynomial/Laguerre integrals. The known pole at one produces an exponential raw-prime contribution canceled by completion; demanding a subexponential **raw** prime sum is false even under RH. The first analytic task is a complete principal-subtracted saddle/log-scale estimate with complementary ranges and gamma terms intact. A zero of height \(\gamma\) can require very large degree; finite coefficients do not prove the limiting growth bound.

**N29.N1 — New pass 2: height-adaptive Cayley anchoring.** For \(\rho=b+\delta+i\gamma\), \(\delta>0\), its disk image has
\[
\log|z_\rho|^{-1}
={1\over2}\log{(r+\delta)^2+\gamma^2\over(r-\delta)^2+\gamma^2}.
\]
At fixed r and large height this is \(2r\delta/\gamma^2+O(\gamma^{-4})\). For the intended high-height bands the unconstrained optimizer \(r=\sqrt{\delta^2+\gamma^2}\) satisfies the Euler-anchor requirement \(r>1-b\), and gives \(\operatorname{artanh}(\delta/r)\sim\delta/|\gamma|\). A height-band-adapted anchor \(r\asymp T\) therefore changes the degree needed for **order-one single-zero modulus amplification** from \(T^2/(r\delta)\) at fixed r to \(T/\delta\).

This is not a finite-degree detection theorem: zero contributions can cancel, and the coefficients now require two-parameter control in degree and r. The price is explicit: prime weights \(m^{-b-r}\), Laguerre argument \(2r\log m\), gamma contribution and endpoint costs all move. If the unconstrained optimizer lies below \(1-b\), the admissible supremum is instead at that boundary; the real-axis singular case is not an admissible Euler anchor at a prospective zero. The new missing lemma is a uniform principal-subtracted coefficient bound in a coupled degree/height regime, followed by a rigorous band-to-all-height transfer. Test the known pole cancellation and one off-line quartet first. If changing r merely moves the same exponential loss into the prime/gamma cancellation, keep the optimization as a diagnostic and stop the analytic claim.
title: N29 — Merge the prime-coefficient criteria; then vary the height geometry

This positive real2x2 matrix satisfies

    sum_(a,b) w_a w_b |xi_a dot xi_b|
       >=sum_(a,b)w_a w_b (xi_a dot xi_b)^2
       =trace(M_Q^2) >= W_Q^2/2.                         (7)

nonnegative eigenvalue inequality. The Mobius signs and character phases
in xi remain the ACTUAL ones. No replacement by positive coefficients
or equidistribution assumption is used. For a real-valued character all
nonzero xi are+1 or-1, so the pointwise single-Q price is W_Q^2 and the factor
1/2 improves to1. We do not claim a sharp constant for every other fixed

    w_a=|c_a|p(a)g(log(q_a/x)),

## 3. Positive row contour and exact root-number cancellation

Let `R` denote the original radial Fourier row kernel in M (2.15), and
`R_tilde` its one-variable Mellin transform. Initially on a single line
`rho>1`, absolute convergence gives
\[
\mathfrak Q_{C,E}
=\frac6{2\pi i}\int_{(\rho)}
\widetilde R(z)K^z\mathcal B_{C,E}(z)\,dz.
\tag{BC7}
\]
The factor six counts all associate rows. In the principal pure-cube
sector the same convention is `Z_row(z)=6 zeta_K(z)`; it is not an
S-deleted row sum.

For the retained coprime nonunit cores, the unit-neutral row character
is nonprincipal and its primitive good conductor is exactly `ce`.
Therefore its L-function is entire. The original row transform is
holomorphic for `Re z>0`. Move to `z=a+it`, `a>0`, without crossing a
pole. Fixed-prime row valuations remain included.

The exact functional equation and root-number calculation give
\[
L(z,\eta)
=A(z)(q_cq_e)^{1/2-z}\epsilon(\eta)L(1-z,\bar\eta),
\qquad
A(z)=3^{1/2-z}(2\pi)^{2z-1}
\frac{\Gamma(1-z)}{\Gamma(z)},
\]
and
\[
\boxed{
\beta(c)\overline{\beta(e)}\epsilon(\eta)
=\mu(c)\mu(e)\eta(\lambda).
}
\tag{BC8}
\]
The cross-prime reciprocity phase cancels on the original coprime
support. This supplies the two Möbius coefficients used below. Apply
the functional equation before taking absolute values.

## A05. Triple-convolution cube inversion and the \(5/6\) absolute barrier

**PROVED RELATIVE TO the inherited triple diagonal; signed improvement OPEN.** Source: BA D7, [restricted research revision] Z13–Z18. With fixed \(r>0\), absorb the common Bessel normalization into
\[
 H_r(t)=tK_{1/3}(\kappa t)^2K_{1/3}(\kappa rt),\qquad
 P_{{\rm sf},r}(y)=y^3\sum_{c\ {\rm sf,good}}\mu(c)H_r(\sqrt{q_c}y).
\]
The actual coefficient identity, allowing shared core/cube primes, gives
\[
 P_r(y)=\sum_B\xi_{\rm ang}(B)q_B^{-3}
                    P_{{\rm sf},r}(q_B^{3/2}y),\qquad
 P_{{\rm sf},r}(y)=\sum_B\mu(B)\xi_{\rm ang}(B)q_B^{-3}
                    P_r(q_B^{3/2}y). \tag{A05.1}
\]
This is ordinary convolution inversion of commuting dilations, justified absolutely at each fixed \(y>0\) by the Bessel tail.

If \(P_r(y)\ll y^{3-2a}\) at zero and decays rapidly at infinity, absolute inversion requires
\(\sum_Bq_B^{3/2-3a}<\infty\), exactly \(a>5/6\). Splitting at \(q_B=y^{-2/3}\) gives bounds \(y^{3-2a}\) for \(a>5/6\), \(y^{4/3}(1+|\log y|)\) at equality, and \(y^{4/3}\) below it. These are upper-budget limitations, not lower bounds on the signed inverse. An angular Möbius partial-sum bound \(O(U^\theta)\), with the needed derivative control, permits Abel summation when \(\theta<3a-3/2\). At \(a=3/4\) this asks for \(\theta<3/4\), a separate unpaid theorem. The numerical \(5/6\) shared with the source-shell obstruction does not identify their spaces.

statement:
## 2. A uniform sixth-power-free estimate down to bounded core scale

### Fixed-cutoff restoration before applying UM

GS5 allows every fixed finite S containing the character's entire defining-modulus support and the primes above 6. M B0.1 additionally describes a sufficiently large fixed small-prime cutoff. One must not silently enlarge S in the defining GS5 polynomial.

Choose a fixed enlargement \(S'\) sufficient for the inherited UM proof, and let \(\mathfrak t\) be the squarefree product of the primes in \(S'\setminus S\). Freeze \(S'\) after the requested loss has been chosen, independently of all scales, rows and roots. Write \(M^S\) and \(M^{S'}\) for the two presentations. Unique splitting of a squarefree column gives exactly
\[
M^S_v(E;W)=\sum_{d\mid\mathfrak t}
 \mu_K(d)\nu(d)\chi_d(v)q_d^{-1/2}
 M^{S'}_v(E/q_d;W).
\tag{R1}
\]
The original columns and their zeros are restored by this identity. The multipliers depending on v have modulus at most one; their finite total absolute mass is fixed. Cauchy or the Hilbert triangle inequality therefore transfers UM and its scale-maximal version from \(S'\) to the exact original S. For positive scales below 2 use the finite-column bound. The same argument applies to the log-scale derivative profile. No moving prime enters the fixed datum, and all extra constants and derivative orders have permitted dependence on the original fixed datum and the requested loss.

If the intended inherited UM is already explicitly stipulated for every such S, R1 merely records its compatibility with the printed M convention. Either way it removes the ambiguity without weakening GS5's quantifier.

The needed formulation of the inherited amplification is slightly more uniform than writing \(D=U^r\): the core scale U may be bounded, so r need not be bounded. For every fixed \(B\ge1\) and every \(\eta>0\), UM implies
\[
\sum_{\substack{0<q_v\le U\\v\ {\rm sixth\mbox{-}power\mbox{-}free}}}
|M_v(E;W)|^2
\ll_{\nu,S,I,B,\eta}
(2DU)^\eta
\left(U+U^{1/6}E^{5/6}\right)\|W\|_{C^J(I)}^2
\tag{NP4}
\]
for \(D\ge2\), \(1\le U\le D^B\), and \(0<E\le D\). The same estimate holds after restricting to \(\mathcal R_\nu\).

Here sixth-power-free means every prime-ideal valuation lies in \(\{0,1,\ldots,5\}\), including primes in S. All units are retained. There are only finitely many possible S-supported parts of such a core; they cause no varying conductor in the fixed datum.

For completeness, first take \(E\ge2\). Fix a small \(\vartheta>0\) in terms of the requested loss and put
\[
V=\max(2U,E^{1+\vartheta}),\qquad
P=(V/U)^{1/6}.
\tag{NP5}
\]
There are \(\gg_S P\) good ideals \(\mathfrak a\), prime to S, with \(q_{\mathfrak a}\le P\). Choose one generator \(\alpha\); \(\alpha^6\) does not depend on the choice, since every Eisenstein unit has sixth power one. The exact M B0.7 identity is
\[
M_v(E;W)=
\sum_{d\mid\operatorname{rad}\mathfrak a}
\frac{\mu_K(d)\psi_v(d)}{\sqrt{q_d}}
M_{v\alpha^6}(E/q_d;W).
\tag{NP6}
\]
No condition \((v,\mathfrak a)=1\) is imposed. The original natural zeros prove NP6 also at shared primes. The squared absolute divisor mass is \(O_\delta(q_{\mathfrak a}^{\delta})\) for every \(\delta>0\).

The map \((v,\mathfrak a)\mapsto v\alpha^6\) is injective for sixth-power-free v. Valuations modulo six recover v's ideal and the quotient recovers \(\mathfrak a\); \(\alpha^6\) being fixed then recovers v's unit. The S-part of v is unchanged because the amplifier is good.

The scale-maximal UM statement used here is
\[
\sum_{0<q_w\le V}\sup_{0<F\le E}|M_w(F;W)|^2
\ll (2EV)^\delta V\|W\|_{C^{J_1}(I)}^2,
\qquad V\ge E^{1+\vartheta}.
\tag{NP7}
\]
It is M B0.8. It can also be checked directly: logarithmic differentiation replaces W by \(-W/2-xW'\), Sobolev on unit log-scale intervals uses UM for those two common profiles, and the \(O(\log(2E))\) intervals cost a small power. The subunit scales are empty below \(1/b\), and the remaining bounded scales contain finitely many ideals. All orders are fixed before E, U or any amplifier varies.

Averaging NP6 over the amplifiers, applying divisor Cauchy, and then using injectivity and NP7 gives
\[
\sum_{v\ {\rm sixth\mbox{-}power\mbox{-}free}}^{q_v\le U}|M_v(E;W)|^2
\ll (2EV)^{O(\delta)}\frac VP\|W\|_{C^{J_1}}^2
=(2EV)^{O(\delta)}U^{1/6}V^{5/6}\|W\|_{C^{J_1}}^2.
\tag{NP8}
\]
Since \(U\le D^B\), E and V lie in fixed polynomial ranges relative to D. Choose \(\vartheta,\delta\) sufficiently small in terms of \(B,\eta\); NP5–NP8 then give NP4 with \(E^{5/6}\), absorbing \(E^{5\vartheta/6}\) into the displayed loss. For \(E<2\), either the annulus is empty or \(E\ge1/b\) and only \(O_I(1)\) columns occur, giving \(O_I(U\|W\|_\infty^2)\). This proves NP4 uniformly, including \(U\asymp1\).

The argument uses all rows on the right side of NP7. If one starts with nonprincipal cores, multiplication by a sixth power changes only deletions, so \(\psi_{v\alpha^6}^*=\psi_v^*\). Positive enlargement to all rows is therefore legitimate and does not replace a nonprincipal family by a different coefficient family.

## 3. Fully masked Gaussian Walsh transform

This development uses the existing principal Gaussian coprime source G25-G30, not the new Liouville source or a Hecke-family source. Fix tau>0. Put Y=floor(X^.495), B_X=2X exp(C sqrt(log X)), and use the finite prime set 5<=p<=B_X. For squarefree incidence labels u,v with d(u),d(v) their products, the actual gate is

    K(u,v)=(-1)^{|u|+|v|}1_{u and v have disjoint prime support}.

The full mask W_x retains d(u)>Y, d(v)>Y, d(u)d(v)<=B_X and the entire sum

    sum_{l<=B_X/(d(u)d(v))} (-1)^{l+1}
              g_tau(log(d(u)d(v)l/x)).

Thus Z=sum_{u,v} K(u,v)W_x(u,v) is exactly the output-truncated ordered-pair source. No squarefree, shared-prime, small-prime, endpoint, sign or l-factor is changed. With the unnormalized two-variable Walsh transform on k primes,

    Z=2^{-2k} sum_{alpha,beta} Khat(alpha,beta) What_x(alpha,beta). (8)

For the signed one-prime gate T=[[1,-1],[-1,0]] and H=[[1,1],[1,-1]], H T H=[[-1,1],[1,3]]. Every local transformed entry is nonzero. Orthogonality proves (8), not sparsity of the complete arithmetic mask. The huge global prime set is part of the identity and is not replaced by the much smaller set dividing one integer.

The complements are quantitatively paid. The full output coefficient has a d_3 majorant. Uniformly for every real x in [X,2X], the discarded Gaussian tail n>B_X is

    |P_Y(x)-Z(x)| <= X^{1-C^2/(2 tau)+o(1)}.

This follows by logarithmic substitution in the Gaussian tail, including the counting Jacobian; the term C sqrt(log X) is absorbed into the o(1) exponent. Fix C large enough that this exponent is strictly below the chosen gamma>1/2. G27 gives the complete source comparison |P_Y-F_6| << X^{.495+delta} with fixed delta<gamma-.495. All parameters are fixed before the shell variable varies. Finite initial X is harmless in the Mellin return.

The last fixed Euler convolution in G28 must also stay present. At p=2,3 its direct factor is (1-z)^2 with inverse (1-z)^{-2}; at p>=5 it is (1-z)^2/(1-2z) with inverse (1-2z)/(1-z)^2. The infinite-prime factors start in degree two, and 2/sqrt(5)<1, giving absolute coefficient convergence in every Re(s)>1/2 for both directions. The exceptional p=2 coefficients in the original source are 1,-3,2; they are not silently changed to an ordinary squarefree factor. Apply these fixed convolutions to fixed complete fields, not to a prime set or cutoff that changes with the integration variable.

Accordingly an every-epsilon COMPLETE shell L2 bound of size X^{gamma+epsilon} for (8), on every large dyadic shell and with dx/x, transfers by triangle and the fixed convolution to the original Gaussian field. Its exact Mellin multiplier exp(tau s^2/2)(1-2^{1-s})/zeta(s) yields the G3 conclusion gamma<Re(s)<1. The compensator is nonzero there; the line Re(s)=1 is handled only by the inherited classical boundary statement, with s=1 the principal pole exception. Compact-strip normal convergence covers every finite height. This is a valid conditional zeta return; it does not supply a gain for every ordinary character without an actual corresponding character-source theorem and bound.

Neither the entire dual sum nor its required exponent has been estimated. A Cauchy bound after Walsh is not new cancellation, and a subset of transformed modes is not a bound for the full signed contraction. The actual contribution is an exact alternative place to formulate the open estimate with its tails already priced.

# Actual middle frequencies with small square or cube cores



The actual finite middle of G186 has two further affordable arithmetic sectors. After clearing its fixed dual denominator, write the ideal of a nonzero frequency uniquely as kappa2*b^2, kappa2 squarefree, or kappa3*t^3*z^6, kappa3 cubefree and t squarefree. No pairwise coprimality is imposed on these factors. The proposed estimates below pay the middle frequencies satisfying

    N(kappa2)<=U^(13/40), OR N(kappa3)<=U^(3/4).

These are restrictions on the arithmetic power cores of the original frequency, not another enlargement of its paid low norm cutoff. They include frequencies throughout the natural middle scale. Their exact signed complement, together with ALL of R_nonunique, remains open. c11=.1251459636 and all analytic, positive-slot and external admission obligations are unchanged.

## 1. Frozen source, orientations and precise decomposition

The initial input manifest was frozen before this development: source-pins.json SHA256 ef6cd733c952ce668c368f95d93d77204214e86eed8e32f38a7c4af67ac9ebf5. It pins G185-G187, both reports, G179-G181, G155-G157, G147 ancestry, PR9 at58344dfdbe756cf2f743da1908ffe0582418cf5b and the index. The later root budget is supplemental unreviewed reconstruction, not an input theorem. Its two prices agree with the independently derived formulas saved in the author worklog before the second recovery. Root suggested the stronger core thresholds used here; their margins are checked below.

Keep the exact G185 source

    F_u=M_u(D1;W1,t1) M_u(D2;W2,t2) Q_u,
    D1=U^r, D2=U^s, P0=U^v, N0=D1 D2 P0,
    M_u(D;W)=D^(-1/2)sum_d mu(d)nu(d)chi_d(u)^e W(Nd/D).

Here e=+1 or -1 is the whole orientation; the right copy conjugates the complete product. The two original inverse heights stay independent. Q has its original ordered disjoint slot pools, original coefficients, heights and product profile, and possible intersections with the inverses. Every character retains its natural zero at nonunits, including powers0 and6. Keep the original sixth-power-free nonzero row enclosure, fixed smooth ball, finite ray/unit dictionaries and prior divisor-weight domination. No physical projector is added to a free-row norm.

Use the original physical box17/25<=delta<=7/10,17/20<r<47/50,33/25<s<141/100,s-r>3/8,0<=v<=1/20. Put L=r+s. Keep K=28114053/6250000 with its preceding-family license, rho=1-10delta/[3(5-2delta)] and the EXACT inherited T=delta L+E_K, E_K>=rho. In particular L>217/100, L<47/20 and T>=123353/67500. No signal at an internal buffered delta is replaced by this physical-bin bound.

R_unique is exactly the squarefree/coprime merged-column part of G181 R4. R_nonunique=R4-R_unique is unchanged. G186 applies the sixth-free identity sum_(a^6|u)mu(a), primitive Poisson, and a fixed dyadic partition Na~A. Its genuine far tail is paid BEFORE algebraic extension and absolute Fourier separation. Fix tau=1/1000 before labels. Let

    H_A=U^tau A^6 N0^2/U.

The middle is the literal frequency range U^(39/25)<N(ell)<=H_A in each original a-dyad, with its FULL Schwartz kernel. Fixed original support/dual-lattice constants remain in the cutoff or a sufficiently small geometric pad. G186's tail proof permits this fixed tau. The zero frequency is absent by the primitive relative character; this deletes no original principal family.

Fix once a nonzero S-supported element Delta clearing the original dual lattice. Define kappa2 and kappa3 from the integral ideal (Delta*ell). Use this literal convention in all selectors; do not identify these cutoffs with cores from a differently scaled frequency. The norm of Delta is fixed. Unit representatives and the S-parts are treated by the finite conventions detailed below.

In the character formula, clearing Delta supplies the coefficient chi_m(Delta)^(-eta). It is a unit because every source m is S-good; it is a fixed ray factor. This inverts no natural zero of ell or any moving label. The element unit in an ideal factorization is retained in the same finite dictionary.

Define R_sq as the middle with N(kappa2)<=U^(13/40). Define R_cu as the middle with N(kappa2)>U^(13/40) AND N(kappa3)<=U^(3/4). Let R_hard be the middle with BOTH core norms greater than these caps. This is an exhaustive disjoint priority partition of the original frequencies, independent of every live source column. All three scalars retain their signs and the full kernel. The estimates also apply with this priority selector present; that fact is proved through a positive outer energy AFTER Cauchy, not by signed-subset monotonicity.

## 2. The exact merged coefficient and what permission it needs

G185's complete mutual-gcd identity and finite ray expansion are retained. On each genuine primitive pair n,n', its two Gauss orientations, apart from nu(n)conjugate(nu(n')), are literally

    e=-1: R(n,n')chi_n(-1)conjugate(G(n))G(n')
           a0(n)conjugate(a0(n'))chi_n(ell)conjugate(chi_n'(ell)),
    e=+1: R(n,n')G(n)conjugate(G(n'))chi_n'(-1)
           conjugate(a0(n))a0(n')conjugate(chi_n(ell))chi_n'(ell).

Here a0(n)=conjugate(alpha(n))gamma_2(n). The CRT ratio R and the displayed G and chi(-1) factors have only the fixed ray dependence of PR9 B1.1-B1.11. They are expanded into the prescribed finite separated dictionary. No variable cubic coupling between copies is removed by assumption.

Extend the formal product expression to all individually squarefree columns, THEN insert the full sum_(f|n,f|n')mu(f). Artificial noncoprime pairs cancel pointwise in this COMPLETE sum, with the frequency selector still present. No imprimitive Poisson identity on added pairs is asserted. Put n=fm,n'=fm'. Each side independently allocates primes of f to its original two inverse colors or original slots:

    f=f1*f2*fP=g1*g2*gP,
    X=N0/Nf,
    (D1/Nf1)(D2/Nf2)(P0/NfP)=X,
    (D1/Ng1)(D2/Ng2)(P0/NgP)=X.

All assigned slot coefficients/pool tests remain. Both allocation multiplicities together are <=tau(f)^C at fixed original slot depth. Their normalization is EXACTLY

    U/[N(a)^6 N0 N(f)].                                  (2.1)

It follows from the old U/[N(a)^6 N0^2] and BOTH residual roots sqrt(X)*sqrt(X). The real factor X/sqrt(Nm Nm') stays in the common profile; it gives no extra Nf power. Imaginary norm powers extracted from either original height have modulus one. Natural frequency holes give

    chi_f(ell)conjugate(chi_f(ell))=1_((f,ell)=1).

No natural character value is divided out. The a-puncture and all remaining f-punctures stay in their own columns.

For one fixed allocation and one Fourier component, write the normalized residual column in its WHOLE merged index as

    B_f(ell)=X^(-1/2) sum_(m sf) c_f(m) chi_m(ell)^eta,
    eta=+1 or -1.                                       (2.2)

The actual c_f(m) contains a0(m) or its conjugate, fixed ray data, chi_m(f)^4 or its conjugate, the a/f punctures and the sum over ALL original residual ordered factorizations m=x*y*P. That sum keeps the shortened W1(t1), W2(t2), every remaining slot coefficient/profile and their pool tests. There is no replacement by independent signs or a model coefficient.

For a specified squarefree m, each prime can go to at most j+2 original places, at fixed j. Consequently the number of actual residual tuples is at most (j+2)^omega(m), and

    |c_f(m)| << H_J tau(m)^C,
    X^(-1) sum_(Nm~X) |c_f(m)|^2 << H_J U^epsilon.       (2.3)

This remains true with additional fixed punctures or a fixed multiplicative unit twist. It is uniform in the original f allocation, kappa, later z and all original heights at their fixed seminorm orders. Assigned slot choices were counted in tau(f)^C, not counted again here. Nonempty nominal subunit windows have bounded dilation; empty supports remain empty. Thus X may be clipped to1 at bounded cost. The factorizations have bounded original annular support, so ideal counting O(X) proves (2.3). No extra P0 squared mass is needed: the original slot labels are counted in each divisor-bounded merged coefficient.

The quadratic and cubic large sieves below explicitly permit an arbitrary inner sequence independent of the live OUTER frequency variable. They therefore permit (2.3). This is a different contract from PR9 B3.6, which still does NOT permit this coefficient. No extension of canonical terminal RE is asserted.

For a pointwise estimate used later, keep the unmerged original colors. On each side the two variables are x and y of lengths D1/Nf1,D2/Nf2, or x',y' of lengths D1/Ng1,D2/Ng2. They are never cross-copy products. G185 proves, uniformly under fixed additional holes,

    |B_f(ell)|^2 << H_J U^epsilon S0,
    S0=P0[D1+D2+(D1D2)^(2/3)].                         (2.4)

It follows from a0(xyP)=a0(x)a0(y)a0(P)chi_y(x)^4 chi_x(P)^4 chi_y(P)^4 and the squarefree cubic sieve on x,y, then triangle over ORIGINAL slots. A new z-puncture separates between x,y and those slots, so (2.4) also applies to the punctured coefficients used below.

## 3. Common profile and admissible frequency selectors

Use G185's common-profile construction on the ambient original normalized inverse/slot norm box on BOTH copies, with a and ell nominal dyads A,H. The kernel is K(C*y_ell/[y_a^6 product(y_original_columns)]), C=UH/(A^6N0^2). Its Euler derivatives are uniformly bounded by fixed Schwartz seminorms. The Fourier measure is fixed BEFORE live a,f,kappa,b,t,z or slot tuples. Then substitute the exact factorizations. Fourier powers in N(ell) become outer unit powers in the frequency factors; the two inverse height profiles remain on their own original colors. Restore the whole Fourier integral with its fixed weighted L1 mass.

The low/middle/far and power-core selectors are kept OUTSIDE smooth separation. For a fixed outer fiber, a frequency selector is a bounded weight w(b), or w(t) after fixing z. In a scalar correlation, Cauchy gives

    |sum_v w(v) B_left(v)conjugate(B_right(v))|
      <=[sum_v |w(v)||B_left(v)|^2]^(1/2)
        [sum_v |w(v)||B_right(v)|^2]^(1/2).

Only these positive outer energies are enlarged to a ball. The right copy has its own c_f and original independent color allocation; (2.3)-(2.4) apply to both with the SAME X,S0 upper bounds. This justifies a frequency-only priority selector. A selector depending jointly on a live source column and frequency would not be covered by this argument.

Fixed denominator, units and S-parts do not create a new growing loss. Clear Delta literally, split unit classes, and strip the S-supported part of a live outer variable. There are only O((log U)^|S|) such parts below the fixed polynomial cap. Their sixth-power residue twists are fixed finite dictionary data (exponents modulo6), and their norm factors shorten the live variable. Apply the monotone bounds below at that shorter length, then sum this logarithmic count. Bounded periodic outer factors from the original fixed row sectors have bounded modulus and are handled in the positive outer energy. On good primes all reciprocity phases are the original finite ray factors, resolved before the sieve. No moving prime is added to S. This retains any S-power with arbitrarily large valuation rather than pretending the dual is squarefree or S-good.

## 4. Square-core middle estimate: unrestricted cubic outer variable

Factor the integral frequency ideal as ell=kappa*b^2, kappa squarefree, allowing (kappa,b)>1; the fixed Delta/unit factors are understood literally as above. On every unit and nonunit,

    chi_m(ell)^eta=chi_m(kappa)^eta chi_m(b)^(2eta).     (4.1)

For fixed kappa the second factor is cubic. Absorb the first into the actual inner coefficient. Its squared mass still satisfies (2.3), independent of b. The common (f,ell)=1 restricts outer b and/or kills the fiber; source/slot intersections with b are exactly the natural zeros of the cubic symbol.

The precise unconditional input is [Dunn, arXiv2403.13151v3, Theorem4.1/Corollary4.2](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.13151v3): with squarefree primary inner m of length X and an arbitrary inner sequence, the unrestricted outer variable b of length B has energy bounded by

    (BX)^epsilon B^(1/3)(B+X) * inner squared mass.      (4.2)

Cubic reciprocity/conjugation supplies the orientation in (4.1), after the fixed ray handling just stated. This is Section4's large sieve, NOT the paper's cuspidal bilinear theorem. Neither squarefreeness of b nor an arbitrary joint matrix is assumed.

In an a-dyad the outer length is B<~(H_A/Nkappa)^(1/2). For a core cap C>=1, sum kappa by ideal counting. Using sum_(Nkappa<=C)Nkappa^(-2/3)<<C^(1/3) and sum Nkappa^(-1/6)<<C^(5/6), the complete positive fiber price is

    H_J U^epsilon [H_A^(2/3) C^(1/3)
                              +X H_A^(1/6) C^(5/6)].  (4.3)

Sharp middle restrictions and the core selector are allowed by Section3. Empty B<1 fibers contribute nothing; fixed bounded clipping costs are harmless. Both scalar sides satisfy (4.3), so Cauchy pays their product at this same price, not its square.

Restore (2.1), both allocation multiplicities, and O(A) original a labels. The exact dyad/f prices are

    U^(1/3+2tau/3) A^(-1) N0^(1/3) (Nf)^(-1) C^(1/3),
    U^(5/6+tau/6) A^(-4) N0^(1/3) (Nf)^(-2) C^(5/6).

The A sums are geometric and bounded. The f^-1 sum with tau(f)^C is harmonic up to an arbitrarily small power; the f^-2 sum converges after such a loss. Therefore the literal signed selected middle obeys

    |R_sq(C)| << H_J U^epsilon [
        U^(1/3+2tau/3) N0^(1/3) C^(1/3)
       +U^(5/6+tau/6) N0^(1/3) C^(5/6)].              (SQ)

All roots, original slots and both f allocations have been paid. This is an actual joint frequency/source estimate; replacing every frequency by (2.4) would give a larger price.

## 5. Cube-core middle estimate: quadratic energy plus original-color control

Factor uniquely ell=kappa*t^3*z^6, kappa cubefree and t squarefree. Its valuation rule is v(kappa)=v(ell) mod3, v(t)=floor(v(ell)/3) mod2, v(z)=floor(v(ell)/6). Every overlap is allowed: for example a prime of valuation4 lies in both kappa and t. The exact zero-preserving character identity is

    chi_m(ell)^eta=chi_m(kappa)^eta chi_m(t)^3
                                      *1_((m,z)=1).   (5.1)

The factor chi_m(t)^3 is real and unchanged by eta=-1. A vanished sixth-power phase still has its displayed natural hole. For fixed kappa,z the actual inner coefficient is (2.2), multiplied by chi_m(kappa)^eta and the z-puncture. Its squared mass is (2.3). There is no imposed (kappa,t), (kappa,z), or (t,z) coprimality.

PR9 B2.24 supplies the squarefree quadratic Hecke sieve of price T0+X. Its explicit family check at lambda, fixed primary square classes modulo4 and finite ray reciprocity are part of the contract used here. Both live variables m and t are squarefree. The primary [Goldmakher-Louvel Theorem1.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1112.1642) requires precisely such a Hecke family; we use PR9's verification, not a generic residue-symbol analogy. Arbitrary inner coefficients independent of t are permitted. Consequently the t-energy for Nt<=T0 is <=H_J U^epsilon(T0+X).

Put B=(H_A/Nkappa)^(1/3), so T0=B/(Nz)^2. For large z there is a second bound: (2.4) at every t, including its new z-hole, gives energy <=H_J U^epsilon T0*S0. Both bounds permit the same frequency-only selectors. Split z at Z>=1. Ideal counting gives

    sum_(Nz<=Z) [B/(Nz)^2+X] << B+XZ,
    sum_(Nz>Z) B*S0/(Nz)^2 << B*S0/Z.

There is no missing repeated-row cost XZ. Clip Z=sqrt(B*S0/X) to the actual interval [1,sqrt(B)]. If the optimum is below1, use the all-pointwise bound B*S0<=sqrt(B*S0*X). If above sqrt(B), the all-quadratic bound B+Xsqrt(B)<=B+sqrt(B*S0*X). Thus for all nonempty scales, with no S0<=X hypothesis,

    sum_(t,z) |B_f(kappa*t^3*z^6)|^2
        << H_J U^epsilon [B+sqrt(B*S0*X)].              (5.2)

In (5.2) each value is evaluated with its actual z-puncture and whole source coefficient. After fixing z the coefficient is independent of t, which is exactly the sieve permission. The long-z estimate remains on the original two colors and actual remaining slots. A general arbitrary merged coefficient would not have (2.4), so both inputs are necessary.

Summing cubefree kappa up to C by ideal counting costs

    H_A^(1/3) C^(2/3)+sqrt(S0*X)H_A^(1/6) C^(5/6).     (5.3)

Cauchy between the independently allocated copies is taken at this positive outer energy. Restoring (2.1) and O(A) a labels gives

    U^(2/3+tau/3) A^(-3) N0^(-1/3) (Nf)^(-1) C^(2/3),
    U^(5/6+tau/6) A^(-4) N0^(-1/6)sqrt(S0)
                                      (Nf)^(-3/2) C^(5/6).

The A sums converge, f^-1 costs only a small power, and f^-3/2 converges even with both divisor allocation multiplicities after a sufficiently small divisor loss. In the physical box s<2r and r<2s, S0<<P0(D1D2)^(2/3). Hence

    |R_cu(C)| << H_J U^epsilon [
        U^(2/3+tau/3) N0^(-1/3) C^(2/3)
       +U^(5/6+tau/6)(D1D2)^(1/6)P0^(1/3)C^(5/6)].   (CU)

The additional priority condition excluding R_sq depends only on kappa,t,z, hence remains an admissible outer selector throughout this proof. It is not a source-dependent mask discarded from a signed form.

## 6. Deliberately coarse complete prices and the remaining source

Write C=U^c. The two square exponents are

    1/3+(L+v)/3+c/3+2tau/3,
    5/6+(L+v)/3+5c/6+tau/6.

The two cube exponents are

    2/3-(L+v)/3+2c/3+tau/3,

With tau=1/1000, subtract tau/6. Reserve at most1/500 for ALL remaining finite geometric, arithmetic, Fourier and height losses combined. This yields the candidate complete equality

    ||F_<||_U^2=R_nonunique+R_hard
                         +O(H_J U^(T-1/200+epsilon)),  (6.1)

where R_hard is EXACTLY the original finite middle with BOTH core caps exceeded. G181/G186's paid pieces and genuine infinite far tail are included in the error. Neither R_nonunique nor R_hard is positive or separately assumed small. No part of the nonunique source was replaced by a primitive source.

# Independent review: arithmetic dilates and the localization deficit



## Decision and current comparison

**Recommend accepting the author's stated component results, with no increase in c.** I find no mathematical gap in the exact ordinary-character source, signed global asymptotic, fixed finite scale coercivity, complete shrinking-arc return, finite small-gcd core, actual absolute-kernel obstruction, or restricted squarefree-density approximation. Their quantifiers and complements are paid at the stated fixed-character scope. The required signed small-gcd estimate remains open and Mertens-equivalent. A favorable review does not establish that estimate.

The controller accepted c8=12514261/100000000=.12514261, theta8=.87485739 during this review. Its 07:40:05 UTC acceptance receipt was read completely and hash-bound in receipt.json. It retains the PR9/Gao source obligations and makes no formalization/admission claim. The frozen author's historical c7=.125140 calibration is correct for its completion time and must not be rewritten. The current first-gain target here is **c>.12514261**, equivalently gamma<.87485739; the required energy saving is strictly greater than .25028522. The 1/6 and 1/4 targets remain conditional possibilities, not achieved results.

The material research value is specific: an actual-mu source gives a positive signed global leading constant, and it rules out both a scalar-remainder positivity shortcut and every fixed finite normalized scale filter. This is stronger evidence than the previous non-Mobius countermodel. The finite core and its return are useful exact formulations, but by themselves do not reduce the arithmetic gap. The localized density calculation records a real accumulated cost instead of assuming full-period orthogonality survives localization.

I add three independent refinements below: the exact first-cell collapse for even nonprincipal characters; a quantitative limiting Gram matrix for fixed filters; and a paid test of adjacent shrinking-spacing filters. I also extend the absolute-kernel lower price to every fixed ordinary character. These are component/obstruction results, not a new zero-free bound or a claim of literature priority.

## Frozen evidence and independence

All five supplied author hashes matched exactly. The report, helper, helper output, source list and freeze were read in full. The author's check.py was never executed, because it writes into the frozen source scope. Its finite checks are evidence, not the proof of an asymptotic statement. The author report is 29,888 bytes, SHA256 8a4064f06d5cf14b2c745abcefe2d11825d7af83f57e851d884f5dce2cdfdbc2. The complete five-file pins and the c8 receipt pin are in the independently generated receipt.json.

The current attempt index and relevant current-proof/[private research revision] entries were consulted for the existing Gaussian moment equivalence and paid gcd-sector ancestry. Their then-current c7 text is superseded for calibration by the controller's later c8 acceptance, not by a reviewer inference. No c7/c8 author proof audit was duplicated, and no source-relative qualification was discharged by this review.

I independently checked the cited primary paper: Aistleitner, Berkes, Seip and Weber, *Convergence of series of dilated functions and spectral norms of GCD matrices*, Acta Arithmetica 168.3 (2015), DOI 10.4064/aa168-3-2. Published pp.228-229, Section3, equations(3.2)-(3.5), contain the classical Bernoulli/gcd identity and Hurwitz extension. These support the author's provenance description. No general spectral theorem is being imported for this localized arithmetic problem. [Published primary paper](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/82044), [arXiv version record](https://arxiv.org/abs/1407.5403v2).

 No author, canonical, tracker, Git, provider, child-agent or proof-assistant writes occurred. This statement makes no inference about provider cache TTL or settings changes.

## 1. Reconstructing the actual source and every character phase

Fix an ordinary Dirichlet character chi modulo q, with its natural zeros; q=1 is allowed. Fix an integer r>=2 with chi(-1)=(-1)^r. Put a(n)=mu(n)chi(n),

    Phi(x)=sum_(k in Z\{0}) chi(k)e(kx)/k^r,
    R_N(x)=2cos(2pi x)-sum_(n<=N) a(n)n^(-r)Phi(nx).

Absolute convergence follows from r>1. For a frequency k!=0 the infinite dilated sum has coefficient

    chi(k)k^(-r) sum_(n|abs(k))mu(n).

This uses chi(n)chi(k/n)=chi(k) also when the value is zero. The coefficients at k=1 and k=-1 are both 1 by the parity condition. Thus the infinite target is exactly 2cos(2pi x), and R_N is the full n>N tail. In particular its Fourier coefficients vanish for 0<|k|<=N; in N<|k|<=2N the only eligible divisor is |k|, yielding mu(|k|)chi(k)/k^r. Negative frequencies carry the same coefficient as their positive partners, even for an odd or complex chi, because the denominator sign and parity cancel.

Let n=ga,m=gb,(a,b)=1. Orthogonality of Phi(nx) and Phi(mx) forces Fourier indices bj and aj. Therefore

    <Phi(nx),Phi(mx)> = 2L(2r,chi0) chi(b)conj(chi(a))/(ab)^r.

After multiplying by a(n)conj(a(m))/(nm)^r, the phase factor is

    chi(ga)conj(chi(gb))chi(b)conj(chi(a))
       = |chi(g)|^2 |chi(a)|^2 |chi(b)|^2.

It is 1 exactly when (nm,q)=1 and zero otherwise. A nonzero Mobius term also requires a,b,g squarefree and (g,ab)=1. The resulting global signed norm is exactly

    2L(2r,chi0) sum_(a,b coprime; (ab,q)=1)
      mu(a)mu(b)/(ab)^(2r)
      *sum_(g>N/min(a,b); (g,abq)=1)mu(g)^2/g^(2r).       (R1)

All series here are absolutely convergent. No inducing modulus or primitive replacement was made. The cancellation of character phases is a property of the COMPLETE-PERIOD Gram. In the localized gcd representation the outer factor chi(a)conj(chi(b)) remains; cancelling it there would be incorrect. The author retains it in D_H.

## 2. Global asymptotic and the fixed-filter obstruction

The density of squarefree positive integers coprime to d is

    delta(d)=zeta(2)^(-1) product_(p|d) p/(p+1).

Expanding mu(g)^2=sum_(h^2|g)mu(h), restricting (h,d)=1 and counting the remaining coprime integers gives

    A_d(t)=delta(d)t+O(2^omega(d)sqrt(t)), t>=1.

The main constant is (phi(d)/d)sum_((h,d)=1)mu(h)/h^2, which equals the displayed delta(d). The truncation tail costs O(sqrt(t)); the coprime counting errors cost O(2^omega(d)sqrt(t)). Partial summation, including the boundary term at a real cutoff, gives

    sum_(g>t;(g,d)=1)mu(g)^2 g^(-2r)
      =delta(d)t^(1-2r)/(2r-1)
        +O_r(2^omega(d)t^(1/2-2r)).                       (R2)

Insert this into (R1) when min(a,b)<=N. The error sum is absolutely finite: for a<=b, using 2^omega(abq)<<_q (ab)^(1/4), its summand is at most a^(-1/4)b^(1/4-2r); summing b first leaves O(a^(1-2r)). The region min(a,b)>N contributes O(N^(2-4r)) both to the exact expression and to the proposed main term. This is smaller than N^(1/2-2r) for r>=2. Consequently the author's

    ||R_N||_2^2 = C_r(q)N^(1-2r)+O_(q,r)(N^(1/2-2r))

and its signed, absolutely convergent formula for C_r(q) are correct.

Parseval on both first bands and the same squarefree count give

    C_r(q)>=2delta(q)(1-2^(1-2r))/(2r-1)>0.

This positivity is proved without termwise positivity of the signed gcd series. It is independent of the particular chi at the fixed admissible r,q. Subtracting the scalar main term destroys the nonnegative-measure inequality that bounded an arc by the whole period. The half-power error is therefore not an arc estimate and does not give c=1/4.

For fixed 0<lambda_1<...<lambda_J, the author's earliest-nonzero-coefficient band argument is valid with floors. Choose B strictly between that lambda_j and min(2lambda_j,lambda_(j+1)); the positive interval after floor(lambda_j N) and before BN sees only that source. The squarefree count supplies a positive limiting mass. The finite-dimensional compactness argument extends this to all unit vectors of coefficients, including N-dependent ones: the uniformly bounded scaled norms make coefficient convergence imply convergence in scaled field norm. No uniformity as J grows or gaps close is obtained.

An independently derived quantitative strengthening makes this especially explicit. Define

    M_jk=2L(2r,chi0)/(2r-1)
      *sum_((a,b)=1;(ab,q)=1) mu(a)mu(b)delta(abq)/(ab)^(2r)
          *max(lambda_j/a,lambda_k/b)^(1-2r).              (R3)

The same summable majorants prove absolute convergence. For fixed scales,

    <R_floor(lambda_jN),R_floor(lambda_kN)>
      =N^(1-2r) M_jk + O_(q,r,lambda)(N^(1/2-2r)).         (R4)

To handle the floors, the exact threshold is max(floor(lambda_jN)/a,floor(lambda_kN)/b). Its difference from N times the threshold in (R3) is O(1/min(a,b)); the induced main-term error sums to O(N^(-2r)). Thresholds below 1 are handled by the same O(N^(2-4r)) outer tail. The matrix M is real symmetric by swapping a,b. It is positive definite by the earliest-band lower bound for every nonzero vector. Thus the scaled Gram matrix tends to a positive definite matrix at rate O(N^(-1/2)); its smallest eigenvalue is eventually at least half that of M. This proves the uniform coercivity with an explicit limiting object, but does not price growing J or colliding scales.

## 3. Full shrinking-arc observation and all-height return

Discrete Fourier inversion writes chi(k)=sum_(a mod q)c_a e(ak/q). The periodic Bernoulli identity, with its actual sign, is

    Phi(x)=-(2pi i)^r/r! sum_a c_a B_r({x+a/q}).

On 0<x<1/q this is one polynomial of degree at most r. The endpoints agree by continuity for r>=2; no measure or endpoint term is lost. Its constant is beta=2L(r,chi), nonzero by the absolutely convergent Euler product at r>1. This does not assume a zero-free half-plane to the left of 1.

Let h=1/(qN). The endpoint reproducing polynomial p_r satisfies

    integral_0^1 p_r(u)u^j du=1_(j=0), 0<=j<=r,
    integral_0^1 |p_r(u)|^2du=(r+1)^2.

The shifted Legendre construction proves both identities. Independent rational inversion of the moment matrix gives p_2=9-36u+30u^2 and p_3=16-120u+240u^2-140u^3, with squared norms 9 and 16. Since nhu<=1/q for every ORIGINAL n<=N, the observation O_Nf=integral p_r(u)f(hu)du gives exactly

    beta T_N=O_NR_N-eta_N,
    T_N=sum_(n>N)a(n)n^(-r),
    eta_N=O_N(2cos(2pi x))-2=O_r(h^(r+1)).                (R5)

The full observation price is (r+1)sqrt(qN) times the arc L2 norm. Therefore for fixed 0<c<1/2, gamma=1-c, the every-integer-N estimate

    integral_0^(1/qN)|R_N(x)|^2dx
      <<_(chi,r,epsilon)N^(1-2r-2c+epsilon)               (R6)

gives T_N<<N^(gamma-r+epsilon). The exact inverse

    M_chi(N)=1/L(r,chi)-N^rT_N
                  +r integral_1^N t^(r-1)T_floor(t)dt

then gives M_chi(X)<<X^(gamma+epsilon) for every real X. Conversely Phi is globally Lipschitz, including its r=2 derivative jumps, and Abel summation gives

    |R_N(x)|<<N^(gamma-r+epsilon)+|x|N^(gamma-r+1+epsilon)

on this arc. The derivative integral converges after choosing epsilon so gamma+epsilon<1. Squaring and integrating recovers (R6), with epsilon relabelled. This is a two-way equivalence, not merely an implication from an easier known estimate.

The Mellin integral s integral_1^infinity M_chi(t)t^(-s-1)dt is holomorphic on Re(s)>gamma and initially equals 1/L(s,chi). For nonprincipal characters the bounded periodic sums continue L to Re(s)>0; for principal characters the floor integral for zeta and the original finite Euler factors give a meromorphic function with its simple pole at 1. The reciprocal identity extends on the connected half-plane with that pole removed and excludes every zero there, with no height restriction or multiplicity exception. The principal point 1 remains a pole. Natural imprimitive factor zeros at Re(s)=0 were never divided away. No growing-conductor, Hecke or Eisenstein conclusion follows.

## 4. The finite signed core and paid complements

Fix kappa>0 with 2c+kappa<1, and set

    G=ceil(N^(2c+kappa)),
    T=ceil(N^(1+2c/(2r-1)+kappa)).

Let K_N(n,m)=integral_0^(1/qN)Phi(nx)conj(Phi(mx))dx and

    C_N=sum_(N<n,m<=T;gcd(n,m)<G)
        a(n)conj(a(m))(nm)^(-r)K_N(n,m).                 (R7)

The symmetric pair mask makes C_N real. The exact still-open hypothesis is the one-sided upper estimate C_N<<N^(1-2r-2c+epsilon) for every sufficiently large integer N and every epsilon>0, with constants allowed to depend on the fixed chi,r,kappa,epsilon. All signs, natural zeros, cutoffs and pairs are retained.

The large-gcd absolute price follows by |Phi|<=2zeta(r) and h<=1/N:

    sum_(n,m>N;gcd(n,m)>=G)|a(n)a(m)|(nm)^(-r)|K_N(n,m)|
      <<_r N^(1-2r)/G+N^(-2r).                         (R8)

For G<=g<=N the pre-h factor is O(N^(2-2r)g^(-2)); for g>N the total is O(N^(1-2r)). These bounds include the diagonal and all omitted far indices. The completion is exactly R_T, whose global squared norm is O(T^(1-2r)). The factor-two triangle inequality in L2 pays its interaction with the finite source, so no unpaid cross term is suppressed. These two costs lie strictly below the target for the displayed choices. The reverse triangle inequality in the same squared-norm form proves equivalence of the core condition and (R6).

A useful clarification: although the stated hypothesis is only an upper bound on a real signed core, positivity of the full finite energy and (R8) already give C_N>=-O(N^(1-2r)/G+N^(-2r)). Thus after paying that complement an absolute bound on the WHOLE real core is equivalent at the target scale. This does not permit absolute values on the individual pairs.

Current exact budgets, before the freely chosen positive kappa, are:

| Target c | Missing energy saving 2c | T exponent for r=2 | T exponent for r=3 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| .12514261 | .25028522 | 1+.25028522/3 | 1+.25028522/5 |
| 1/6 | 1/3 | 10/9 | 16/15 |
| 1/4 | 1/2 | 7/6 | 11/10 |

An increase requires a strict improvement on the first row, not equality. No row is proved. Raising a fixed r shortens the completion exponent but does not reduce the missing factor N^(-2c).

## 5. Local squarefree averaging: correct restricted theorem, unpaid extension

After n=ga,m=gb, the local integrand retains mu(a)mu(b)chi(a)conj(chi(b)); only mu(g)^2 is averaged. Write m0=min(a,b) and

    F_ab(v)=v^(-2r) integral_0^(1/q)Phi(av u)conj(Phi(bv u))du.

For a,b<=H<=N, the exact g sum starts at g>N/m0>=1 and is multiplied by N^(-2r-1)/(ab)^r. Boundedness and Lipschitz continuity give

    |F_ab(v)|<<v^(-2r),
    |F_ab'(v)|<<v^(-2r-1)+(a+b)v^(-2r) a.e.

Partial summation against A_(abq)(Nv)-delta(abq)Nv costs

    2^omega(abq) N^(-2r-1/2)
      [m0^(2r-1/2)+(a+b)m0^(2r-3/2)]/(ab)^r.           (R9)

The lower boundary and the integral of sqrt(v)|F'| are both included. Continuity prevents derivative jumps from adding point masses. For a<=b, the first sum is bounded by sum_(a<=H)a^(r-1/2+epsilon/2)sum_(b>=a)b^(-r+epsilon/2), giving H^(3/2+epsilon) after making the harmless divisor exponents smaller if necessary. The b part uses b^(1-r); at r=2 its logarithm has the same summed power and can be absorbed. The a part is bounded by the first. Thus the author's uniform restricted error N^(-2r-1/2)H^(3/2+epsilon) is valid. The main coefficient has absolute bound O(H), since |J_ab|<<m0^(2r-1).

Complete-period orthogonality supplied an additional (ab)^(-r) in (R1). The local calculation lacks it. Setting H~N therefore only recovers the unsaved N^(1-2r+epsilon) error; it is not an all-quotient estimate. Choosing H=N^(1-2c-kappa) makes both displayed sector costs smaller than the desired target, but those pairs satisfy g>N/H and lie in the already-paid large-gcd region. Quotients larger than H, including those above N, remain. The failure is an upper-bound limitation, not an asserted lower bound on density discrepancy and not a theorem excluding better signed summation.

## 6. Independent diagnostic: the first cell often collapses completely

This sharpened description follows from the same finite Bernoulli representation and does not assume Mertens cancellation.

For any EVEN chi, choose r=2 and let m_chi=q^(-1)sum_(j mod q)chi(j), with chi(0)=0 for q>1 and chi(0)=1 for q=1. On 0<=x<=1/q,

    Phi(x)=2L(2,chi)-2pi^2 m_chi x+2pi^2 chi(0)x^2.      (R10)

To prove this, expand B_2(x+a/q). Its x^2 coefficient is sum c_a=chi(0). For the linear coefficient, c_(q-a)=c_a and B_1(a/q) changes sign under a->q-a, so all nonzero indices pair off; the remaining a=0 term is -c_0/2=-m_chi/2. The constant is Phi(0)=2L(2,chi). Endpoint continuity gives the closed interval.

For every even NONPRINCIPAL character, both m_chi and chi(0) vanish. Hence Phi is exactly constant on the first cell, and for 0<=x<=1/(qN),

    R_N(x)=2L(2,chi) T_N +2cos(2pi x)-2.                 (R11)

The error term is O(N^(-2)). Consequently

    abs(sqrt(E_arc(N))-sqrt(h)*abs(2L(2,chi)T_N))
       << h^(5/2).                                     (R12)

This is the triangle inequality for the constant field and the explicit cosine error, with h=1/(qN). It shows directly that for this entire class the short-arc condition is a single weighted-tail bound, with a negligible deterministic remainder at every target c<1/2. The more elaborate localized Gram has not produced a separate known cancellation mechanism.

For odd chi and r=3, the first cell is

    Phi(x)=2L(3,chi)-4pi^2 L(1,chi)x^2.                  (R13)

Here chi is nonprincipal, so the cubic coefficient vanishes. The first derivative at 0 is zero by absolute convergence and parity. The second derivative at 0 is -8pi^2 L(1,chi). This last differentiation is legitimate: the finite additive Fourier expansion has no zero-frequency component, and the 1/k Fourier series is uniformly convergent near 0, away from its shifted jumps. Equivalently differentiate the finite Bernoulli expression. Only convergence of the nonprincipal L(1,chi) series is needed for this identity, not its nonvanishing. Thus the odd-character local field is determined by two finite weighted sums and the cosine target. This is a diagnostic reduction, not a proof of the required bounds on those sums.

Independent exact rational checks confirm the shapes for q=2 principal, q=5 real even, and q=3,4 odd after factoring their fixed Fourier constants. For example sum_(a=1)^4 chi_5(a)B_2(x+a/5)=4/25 exactly; B_3(x+1/3)-B_3(x+2/3)=2/27-x^2. These finite identities support the normalizations, while (R10)-(R13) are proved for all characters in their stated classes.

## 7. The absolute-kernel obstruction holds for every fixed character

The author's explicit q=1,r=2 example is correct. It extends without character-phase guessing. Let

    A=integral_0^(1/q)|Phi(u)|^2du>0,
    B=||Phi||_infinity, L=a global Lipschitz constant.

A>0 follows from the nonzero continuous value Phi(0). For 1<=a,b<=1+eta,

    |integral_0^(1/q)Phi(au)conj(Phi(bu))du-A|
       <=BL eta/q^2.

Choose a fixed eta>0 small enough that this is at most A/2. Then for N<n,m<=(1+eta)N,

    Re K_N(n,m)>=A/(2N), hence |K_N(n,m)|>=A/(2N).

The actual squarefree integers coprime to q in that interval number delta(q)eta N+O_q(sqrt(N)). At most O(N^2/G) ordered pairs have gcd>=G. Therefore, whenever G->infinity and T eventually exceeds (1+eta)N,

    sum_(N<n,m<=T;gcd(n,m)<G)
      |a(n)a(m)|(nm)^(-r)|K_N(n,m)| >>_(chi,r) N^(1-2r). (R14)

This includes imprimitive, principal, even, odd and complex characters with fixed q. It lower-bounds the absolute price, not the signed core or arc energy. All natural zeros are counted through the coprime squarefree density. Thus paying the localized kernel pairwise absolutely fails for each fixed character, rather than only for the principal test case. No uniform lower constant as q grows is asserted.

## 8. Developing the remaining growing-filter possibility

Fixed-filter coercivity leaves colliding scales open. A concrete test is the adjacent difference

    F_(N,H)=R_N-R_(N+H)=sum_(N<n<=N+H)a(n)n^(-r)Phi(nx),
    1<=H<=N, N,H integers.

This has an actual unconditional small global norm:

    ||F_(N,H)||_2^2 <<_(q,r) H N^(-2r).                 (R15)

Proof: the complete-period Gram has diagonal at most 2L(2r,chi0)H N^(-2r). For distinct n,m in the block, g=gcd(n,m) divides |n-m| and hence g<=H. For each g, the number of ordered distinct pairs of multiples in the block is at most 4H^2/g^2. Consequently the absolute off-diagonal contribution is

    <<N^(-4r)H^2 sum_(g<=H)g^(2r-2)
      <<H^(2r+1)N^(-4r),

which is at most O(H N^(-2r)). This uses the actual signed arithmetic field; positivity is only used for the upper bound on the off-diagonal error.

More precisely the squarefree count and variation of n^(-2r) give

    ||F_(N,H)||_2^2=2L(2r,chi0)delta(q)H N^(-2r)
      +O_(q,r)(N^(1/2-2r)+H^2N^(-2r-1)
                         +H^(2r+1)N^(-4r)).             (R16)

Thus if H=N^alpha with fixed 1/2<alpha<1, the leading constant is positive and the relative error tends to zero. Floors change no power. In particular H=N^(1-2c) gives the SAME formal energy saving N^(-2c) needed by (R6) for every 0<c<1/4. At c=1/4 the elementary density error is as large as the main term, so (R16) does not by itself give an asymptotic there; the upper bound (R15) still holds. This is a genuine favorable calculation for a growing filter, not a reason to stop at the fixed-filter theorem.

Its return fails in a precisely priced place. On a common arc of length 1/(2qN), partition (N,2N] into J~N/H adjacent blocks. The endpoint observation of each filtered field recovers beta times its short weighted sum, and costs O(sqrt(N)) in L2. Applying (R15) separately gives a bound O(sqrt(H)N^(1/2-r)) for each such sum. Reassembling the dyadic weighted tail by the triangle inequality costs J, leaving

    |sum_(N<n<=2N)a(n)n^(-r)|
       << N^(3/2-r) H^(-1/2).                         (R17)

If H=N^(1-2c), this is N^(1+c-r): after Abel inversion it would give gamma=1+c, not the target 1-c. It is weaker than the elementary bound for the whole tail. Estimating the joined field directly with its global norm restores gamma=1, still without a gain. Cauchy-Schwarz over block indices alone gives the same reassembly factor and does not supply signed cancellation. The small norm in (R15) is therefore real but cannot be spent twice while recovering the original signal.

This result rules out only this specified adjacent-difference reconstruction using separate norm bounds. It does not rule out a coupled growing filter, a signed reconstruction, or a better observation. Such a survivor must state its complete original-signal reconstruction and control its coefficient/conditioning cost before claiming the energy gain. The first affordable decisive calculation for another filter is this reconstruction cost, rather than another finite Gram norm optimization.

Accept as written components: the exact source and natural-zero phases; the positive signed global asymptotic; fixed finite normalized-filter coercivity; the full every-integer-scale localized/Mertens equivalence and all-height ordinary zero return; finite core with both complements paid; actual absolute-kernel lower price; and the restricted localized squarefree-density formula. A useful next mathematical action is to retain the signed incomplete-period kernel and find an estimate on its small-gcd/large-quotient sector that improves the current .25028522 energy deficit. ## 4. Protected audit25: a finite-prefix convex relaxation admits hidden poles

The high-reach card proposes separating zero-compatible coefficient data using finite convolution equations and a known tail envelope. A useful audit must name that body. If ALL equations a*chi=delta are imposed at ALL integers, the sequence is already uniquely mu chi; no free convex tail remains. If only finitely many equations are imposed, the following explicit completion identifies what that relaxation cannot certify.

Fix the PRINCIPAL character chi0 modulo any fixed q. Put w_q(n)=mu(n)^2 1_((n,q)=1), and let the first K coefficients be exactly a(n)=mu(n)chi0(n). For every n<=K, the finite equations

    sum_(d|n)b(d)chi0(n/d)=delta_(n,1)                         (C8)

force this prefix recursively, because chi0(1)=1. Conversely any tail beyond K leaves every equation(C8) unchanged. Preserve also ALL squareful and ramified zeros, real coefficients and the pointwise convex bound |b(n)|<=1.

Let1/2<gamma<sigma<beta<1. Suppose C>0 is consistent with the known prefix's summatory envelope, in particular |M_chi0(K)|<=C K^beta. Choose an integer T>=K with |M_chi0(K)|<=C T^beta/2. Choose

    0<lambda<=min(1, (C sigma/2) T^(beta-sigma)).

For any fixed nonzero real t, define the complete sequence

    b(n)=a(n)                              for n<=K,
    b(n)=0                                 for K<n<=T,
    b(n)=lambda w_q(n)n^(sigma-1)cos(t log n) for n>T.          (C9)

All claimed finite equations and global zero masks are exact. The coefficient bound holds because sigma<1 and lambda<=1. For K<=x<=T the sum is M_chi0(K), which obeys Cx^beta. For x>=T,

    |sum_(n<=x)b(n)|
      <=|M_chi0(K)|+lambda sum_(n<=x)n^(sigma-1)
      <= Cx^beta/2+(lambda/sigma)x^sigma<=Cx^beta.             ([restricted research revision])

The middle bound follows from the decreasing-function integral: sum_(n<=x)n^(sigma-1)<=x^sigma/sigma for0<sigma<1. Thus even a LITERAL old power envelope with a fixed consistent constant C survives, not merely a newly chosen big-O constant. The delay T can be arbitrarily large and t arbitrarily high.

Nevertheless its Dirichlet series has actual poles at sigma+it and sigma-it. This can be proved from the same elementary density used in W4, without a prime-distribution input. Write

    Q_q(x)=sum_(n<=x)w_q(n)=kappa_q x+O_q(sqrt x).

Initially Re z>1,

    D_q(z)=sum_n w_q(n)n^-z
          =kappa_q z/(z-1)+z integral_1^infinity
                                  (Q_q(x)-kappa_q x)x^(-z-1)dx.

The error integral is holomorphic for Re z>1/2, including its compact-set derivatives. D_q has one simple pole there, at z=1, with residue kappa_q>0. From(C9), initially Re s>sigma,

    B(s)=sum_(n<=K)a(n)n^-s
       +(lambda/2)[D_q(s+1-sigma-it)+D_q(s+1-sigma+it)
                  -sum_(n<=T)w_q(n)n^(sigma-1-s)
                         (n^(it)+n^(-it))].                 ([restricted research revision])

The finite terms are entire. Since t!=0, the other shifted D_q is regular at each of the two poles, so each residue is lambda kappa_q/2, nonzero. This gives meromorphic continuation at least to Re s>sigma-1/2. It is an exact analytic construction, not a numerical fit or an asserted L-zero. If t=0 is preferred, the single pole at sigma has residue lambda kappa_q.

**What this proves:** the convex relaxation consisting of the true finite prefix equations, all squarefree/nonunit masks, |b(n)|<=1 and the old summatory envelope contains pole-bearing completions beyond any proposed gamma<beta. A functional valid solely for that body cannot certify holomorphy of every compatible inverse candidate to the better line. Arbitrarily high t also defeats a conclusion that finitely many controlled heights cover all heights without a tail theorem.

**What it does not prove:** b is NOT the actual Mobius sequence and does not satisfy full convolution or global multiplicativity. For an unramified prime p>T, the full convolution residual is1+b(p), which is nonzero because |b(p)|<1. The actual L-function is fixed; these synthetic poles are not its zeros. Imposing the complete arithmetic equations, additional true tail correlations, or a stronger analytic constraint could exclude these completions. The audit does not rule out finite certificates that prove those additional facts by an independent theorem. It rejects only the asserted sufficiency of the specified relaxation.

This preserves the card's potential: identify an actual arithmetic constraint that removes(C9) and has a quantitatively paid all-height return. MH8's unpriced analytic tail, the standing finite-observation/readout cautions and W51's all-height source discipline are close ancestry. The explicit real, zero-masked, arbitrarily delayed completion with fixed-envelope control is the audit's concrete evidence; it is not a new general impossibility principle or a new literature claim.

## 3. Exact proposed column and prime witness

Fix 0<beta<1. Let k>=0 be an integer and 1<=T<=beta N; T may be real because only integer comparisons occur. Put

    F_(T,k)(d) = 1_(d<=T OR omega(d)<=k),
    z = E^(-T) (chi(d)F_(T,k)(d))_d.

Here E^(-T) means (E^T)^(-1). Its first row has entries mu(d), and D(chi F)=mu F. Therefore, with no missing or conjugated phase,

    z_1 = sum_(d in S_N) mu(d)chi(d)F_(T,k)(d),
    r(a) = sum_(d|a) mu(d)(1-F_(T,k)(d))
         = sum_(d|a, d>T, omega(d)>k) mu(d).                   (5)

The identity e_1(a)=sum_(d|a)mu(d) supplies the residual sign. Every coordinate with a<=T or omega(a)<=k vanishes. If omega(a)=k+1 and a>T, every proper divisor has omega<=k and is retained, so r(a)=mu(a).

Let p'_1<p'_2<... be the primes not dividing q, b_k=product_(j=1)^k p'_j, and b_0=1; use P^+(1)=1 when referring to a largest prime. Set c=max(beta,1/2), x=N/b_k, and

    P_(N,k) = {prime p : cx<p<=x and p does not divide b_k q}.

Every p in P_(N,k) gives a DISTINCT actual coordinate a=b_k p in S_N, with omega(a)=k+1, a>beta N>=T, and a>N/2. Since N/a<2, the cofactor sum in (3) has only m=1. Thus R(a)=chi(a), r(a)=mu(a), and |R(a)r(a)|=1. It follows, at EVERY finite N, that

    W(z) >= B(z) >= #P_(N,k).                                (6)

The count can of course be zero at small N or excessive k. No finite positivity or effective threshold is asserted.

The ordinary prime number theorem pi(x)~x/log x, and the equivalent p_j~j log j, are the only external asymptotic inputs. They are recorded in the authoritative [NIST DLMF 27.2.3-4](https://dlmf.nist.gov/27.2#E3), checked on 2026-10-13. All uses are fixed-ratio intervals, not short intervals or progressions. The following consequences are derived here.

For fixed k, excluded primes divide the fixed integer b_k q, and

    #P_(N,k) ~ (1-c)N/(b_k log N).                           (7)

For growing k, removing the finitely many prime divisors of fixed q shifts prime indices by a bounded amount. Hence p'_k~k log k, and summing logarithms gives

    log b_k = (1+o(1)) k log k                              (k->infinity).

If k=o(log N/loglog N), then log b_k=o(log N), x=N^(1-o(1)), and the prime count in (6) is N^(1-o(1)). This also covers bounded subsequences of k by (7).

If k~kappa log N/loglog N with FIXED 0<kappa<1, then

    b_k=N^(kappa+o(1)),
    x=N^(1-kappa+o(1)),
    p'_k=O(log N).

Thus cx eventually exceeds both p'_k and every prime divisor of q: the collision and ramification exclusions disappear from the interval. Ordinary PNT along this moving x gives

    #P_(N,k) ~ (1-c)x/log x = N^(1-kappa+o(1)).               (8)

Uniformity in a varying modulus is neither used nor available. A fixed fraction beta<1 is essential; T=N would have zero residual at every depth.

### F01.M — The fixed rational Möbius energy

Keep
\[
V(u)=e^{-u-1/u},\quad \phi(u)=(uV(u))',\quad
\Phi(s)=2(1-s)K_s(2),\quad
S_\phi(x)=\sum_n\mu(n)\phi(n/x).
\]
The fixed Mellin factor has no unwanted zeros in \(\Re s>0\). T09 proves that its dyadic L² energy suffices; no height-uniform reciprocal of \(\Phi\) is needed. Freeze the balanced decomposition throughout \(x\in[X,2X]\): \(Y=\lfloor\sqrt X/\log^2X\rfloor\), product windows \(X/\log^4X\) and \(X\log^2X\), and \(J=\lceil8\log^6X\rceil\). Complete Poisson cancellation precedes multiplicity truncation. The approximation is uniform with each fixed Euler derivative; changing floors during the average would require a separate error theorem.

**F01.N1 — New pass 1, separate the now-cheap diagonal from the actual energy kernel.** The exact target is
\[
E_\phi(X)=\sum_{m,n}\mu(m)\mu(n)K(m/X,n/X),
\qquad K(u,v)=\int_1^2\phi(u/t)\overline{\phi(v/t)}\,{dt\over t}.
\]
Rapid decay gives the elementary diagonal bound \(\sum_n\mu(n)^2K(n/X,n/X)\ll X\), comfortably below \(X^{1.74898}\). The unpaid object is the signed weighted aggregate
\[
2\Re\sum_{h\ge1}\sum_m\mu(m)\mu(m+h)K(m/X,(m+h)/X).
\]
Inserting the frozen balanced identity expresses it as four Möbius signs with coincidences \(\ell de=mfg\); preserve shared primes. Averaging on one log-scale octave does **not** confine \(h\) to a short interval: the kernel correlates a range of comparable ratios. Prove a gain for the complete weighted shift aggregate, or an exact partition whose complementary ranges are all affordable. A theorem for a few fixed shifts, or cancellation of only distinct spectral labels, cannot suffice.

Useful mechanisms are a product-difference dispersion keeping the short \(\ell,m\) variables, a low Mellin-frequency bound after smooth high-frequency tails are paid, and a rigorous comparison to the affine Green form. The latter comparison is presently open. Antisymmetrizing the two long factors kills the symmetric detector; removing an equal Mellin mode can remove the zeta pole being tested. Relative o(1) or logarithmic savings do not reach a fixed half-plane.

### A2. The single-step exponent, with the Taylor remainder paid first

Assume an entire F satisfies, for fixed b>gamma and constants C,K,

    |F(u+iv)| <= C(1+|v|)^K exp(bu+v^2/(2tau)), u>=0.      (W39.4)

Suppose every sufficiently large integer j has a measurable E_j subset [j,j+1] such that

    |E_j| >= c j^(-kappa),
    ess sup_(u in E_j)|F(u)| <= C_0 exp(gamma j),           (W39.5)

where c>0, kappa>=0 are fixed. Then

    sup_[j,j+1]|F| <= exp((gamma+2kappa(b-gamma)+o(1))j).   (W39.6)

For kappa>=1/2 the direct bound b may be better; no gain is asserted there.

Proof. Set

    N=ceil(2(b-gamma)j/log j), c_j=j+1/2,
    R=sqrt(tau(N+1)).

For large j, the disk |z-c_j|<=R lies in Re z>=0 and R>1. Its maximum is at most

    C(1+R)^K exp(b(j+1/2+R)+R^2/(2tau)).

Let P_N be the Taylor polynomial at c_j. On |z-c_j|<=1/2, Cauchy's coefficient bound gives the full remainder

    r_j <= M_R (1/(2R))^(N+1)/(1-1/(2R)),
    log r_j <= b j - (N/2)log N + O_(b,tau,K)(N+sqrt N)
             = gamma j + o(j).                           (W39.7)

The source bound on E_j therefore gives |P_N|<=C_0 exp(gamma j)+r_j there. Apply W39.3 BEFORE discarding r_j:

    sup_I |F| <= L_j C_0 exp(gamma j)+(L_j+1)r_j,
    log L_j <= N log(4e/c)+kappa N log j
             =2kappa(b-gamma)j+o(j).                     (W39.8)

This proves W39.6 and prices both amplified remainders. The statement with an arbitrary epsilon allowance in W39.5 has the same limiting exponent, by choosing its epsilon before the desired output epsilon. Constants may depend on all fixed parameters.

In particular a fixed positive measure in EVERY unit interval (kappa=0) preserves gamma for any bounded-coefficient Gaussian, with no meromorphic input. This is an analytic statement about the whole field, not a signed coefficient submask estimate.

## A10. Two exact countermodels for positivity-based geometric shortcuts

**PROVED counterexamples to generic implications; not counterexamples to an arithmetic theorem for \(\xi\).** Source: BB R12.

For \(h>0\), set \(E_h(z)=\xi(1/2+h-iz)\), where \(\xi\) now denotes the completed Riemann xi function. Real symmetry and the functional equation give \(E_h^\#(z)=\xi(1/2-h-iz)\). The correctly signed Hermite–Biehler kernel has diagonal
\[
 K_h(z,z)=\frac{|E_h(z)|^2-|E_h^\#(z)|^2}{4\pi\Im z}.
\]
Strict positivity for \(\Im z>0\) excludes zeros with \(\beta>1/2+h\), since \(\rho=\beta+i\gamma\) maps to
\(z=-\gamma+i(\beta-1/2-h)\). At \(h=0\) the two functions coincide, so strictness is impossible; the RH endpoint would require every \(h>0\).

Positive semidefiniteness alone does not exclude a common upper zero. The kernel of \(E_0(z)=e^{-iz}\) is
\[
 \frac{\sin(z-\bar w)}{\pi(z-\bar w)}
 =\frac1{2\pi}\int_{-1}^1e^{itz}\overline{e^{itw}}dt,
\]
hence positive. Multiplication by \(R(z)=z^2+1=R^\#(z)\) multiplies the kernel by \(R(z)\overline{R(w)}\), preserving positivity while introducing a zero at \(i\) in both functions. Strict diagonal positivity or a separately proved common-zero exclusion is essential.

A positive Fourier measure does not reverse the heat deformation. The measure
\(2\delta_0+(\delta_1+\delta_{-1})/2\) gives
\[
 H_t(z)=2+e^t\cos z,\qquad \partial_tH_t=-\partial_z^2H_t.
\]
Its measure and moment Hankel matrices are positive. Its zeros are nonreal for \(t<\log2\), double real at equality, and real simple for \(t>\log2\). For a smooth strictly positive density let
\[
 \rho_a(x)=2g_a(x)+[g_a(x-1)+g_a(x+1)]/2,\quad
 g_a(x)=(4\pi a)^{-1/2}e^{-x^2/(4a)}.
\]
Completing the square after multiplication by \(e^{tx^2}\), with \(d=1-4at>0\), gives
\[
 F_t(z)=d^{-1/2}e^{-az^2/d}
           \{2+e^{t/d}\cos(z/d)\}.
\]
Thus real zeros occur once \(t\ge\log2/(1+4a\log2)\), even though the initial zeros are nonreal. Scaling frequency makes the initial strip arbitrarily thin. An arithmetic reverse-stability theorem for xi remains a different open proposal.

RN's finite-Euler signed-moment method is reused with a different Euler product and a vanishing local factor. Their fresh inputs are the literal f3 prefix, its different constant/logarithmic order, its exact coefficient complement, and the new derivative estimates retaining full valuations. No literature-priority claim or exhaustive absence claim is made.

Current-proof G28--G30 supplies exponent equivalence for FULL F_6,G_tau and the original coprime cell, after their paid reconstruction. The moving predicate omega_z(n)<=1 does not commute with those Dirichlet convolutions, and no estimate for a correspondingly restricted A-source, pair source, or SP field follows from this report. Every such projection would require its own comparison.

OPEN-F3 remains the complete signed off-diagonal target G31. The present theorem proves an exponent-one partial field and genuine negative threshold bands.
