statement:
## G175. Two exact source returns with their inverse costs

### Native Cayley scattering

The protected critic audit S22 keeps the literal Eisenstein H source:
original primary/fixed-ray/six-unit/bad-place conventions, distinct rational
long-prime norms and both excluded equal-norm orientations, both ordered
good primitive short ideals including equality, the actual complex core
and rational gcd screen, both original mark projectors and independent
heights, original masks and profiles. Its coefficient is
a_H(n)=alpha(n)eta(n)chi_n(lambda)^(-2)gamma_2(n), xi(g)=alpha(g)^3eta(g)^3.
With v_P=u1(P)/sqrt(q_P), w_P'=u2(P')/sqrt(q_P'), the entire signed scalar
kernel gives T=K^transpose, H=w^*Tv and ||v||^2=Omega1, ||w||^2=Omega2.
The raw target is B0 sqrt(Omega1 Omega2),
B0=G K0[N+L+(NL)^(2/3)]P_orig; physical N^(-1)G^(-2) is applied once.
No extra opposite-coprimality screen, selected source, or Mobius substitute
is inserted. The original range and all other branches remain obligations.

For any r>0 the self-adjoint dilation A=[[0,T^*],[T,0]] has a unitary
Cayley transform (A-irI)(A+irI)^(-1), without knowing ||T||<=r. Write

    D=(T^*T+r^2 I)^(-1),
    R=(T^*T-r^2 I)D, J=-2ir TD,
    R=R^*, R^2+J^*J=I, I-R=2r^2 D.

The exact returned input x=(I-R)^(-1)v obeys

    Tv=ir Jx,
    ||Tv||^2=r^2(||x||^2-||Rx||^2)
            =r^2(2Re<x,v>-||v||^2).                       (10)

Thus ||T||<=r iff R<=0, and the source-specific ||Tv||<=r||v|| iff
Re<x,v><=||v||^2. At r=B0>0 the latter suffices for the raw bound against
every allowed w, and is stronger than controlling one scalar pairing.
B0=0 needs that zero pairing directly. No arithmetic estimate for x is
proved. On a singular mode sigma, transmission is2r sigma/(sigma^2+r^2)
while the inverse is(sigma^2+r^2)/(2r^2). Small transmission can coexist
with a very expensive returned input. A known ||T||<=B only gives
r/2+B^2/(2r)>=B after the crude reconstruction bound.

For an approximation xhat, retain d=v-(I-R)xhat. The complete scalar is

    H=ir w^*J xhat+w^*T d.                                (11)

The residual is an actual native-source obligation. Compared with [restricted research revision]'s
Julia realization, Cayley removes its known-contraction prerequisite but
exposes this inverse/error cost. It proves no H saving or new exponent.

### A compact sensor needs no positive-height numerator cover

The uniform critic audit S10 uses one fixed h>0 and M_chi(x)=0 for x<1:

    S_h(x)=int_0^h M_chi(x exp(-u))du
          =sum_(n<=x)mu(n)chi(n) min(h,log(x/n)).

The endpoints, unit and natural zeros remain. Absolute integration gives

    int_1^infinity S_h(x)x^(-s)dx/x
      =(1-exp(-hs))/(s^2 L(s,chi)), Re s>1.                (12)

If the COMPLETE S_h is O_(chi,epsilon)(x^(gamma+epsilon)) for every
epsilon>0 and all sufficiently large x, for one common0<gamma<1, the
left side is holomorphic on Re s>gamma. The factor(1-exp(-hs))/s^2 is
nonzero there: its nontrivial zeros have Re s=0, and s=0 is outside.
This gives the full ordinary-character all-height pole return, with the
principal-pole convention above. The arithmetic sensor estimate is open.

Stable reconstruction is a different requirement. On a weighted log L2
line sigma>0 the convolution multiplier K_h(s)=(1-exp(-hs))/s satisfies

    (1-exp(-h sigma))/|sigma+it| <= |K_h(sigma+it)|
      <=(1+exp(-h sigma))/|sigma+it|.

For S(y)=S_h(e^y), S'(y)=M_chi(e^y)-M_chi(e^(y-h)) almost everywhere.
The causal difference inverse costs at most(1-exp(-h sigma))^(-1) on
weighted L2, but its input is the derivative: if f=e^(-sigma y)S,
that input is f'+sigma f. Endpoints can be interpreted distributionally.
The derivative cost has not disappeared.

A finite bank of compact L1 kernels has multipliers tending to zero at
large heights on each such line, by step-function approximation and the
Fourier integral of an interval. Hence no fixed finite weighted sum of
squared multipliers has a positive global lower frame bound on unrestricted
weighted L2. This does not refute the one-way pole bridge, a bound on the
actual arithmetic source, atoms/derivatives, or a moving bank with paid
costs. W22/G109 retain the general smoothing/bank ancestry.

### 3.3 Repeated differences pay the complete residual

For a nonnegative shift j,

    f(n)-f(n+j)=-integral_0^j f'(n+u)du.

Iterating this representation for (I-T_H)^r expresses R_x(n) as (-1)^r times the average, over j_1,...,j_r in {0,...,H-1}, of the integral of f_x^(r)(n+u_1+...+u_r) over0<=u_i<=j_i. No derivative is taken of a sharp arithmetic cutoff.

For every absolutely continuous integrable f with integrable derivative and every v>=0,

    sum_(n>=1) |f(n+v)| <= ||f||_(L1(0,infinity))
                                  +||f'||_(L1(0,infinity)). (9)

To prove (9), compare f(n+v) with f(t) on each interval[n+v-1,n+v], integrate, then sum the disjoint intervals. They all lie in[0,infinity). Applying (9) to f_x^(r), using the derivative scaling f_x^(r)(t)=x^(-r)h_tau^(r)(t/x), proves

    sum_(n>=1)|R_x(n)|
       <= ((H-1)/2)^r [J_r x^(1-r)+J_(r+1) x^(-r)]
       <= ((H-1)/2)^r [J_r X^(1-r)+J_(r+1) X^(-r)].        (10)

The coefficient ((H-1)/2)^r is the exact product of average shift lengths. This bound includes the whole positive integer line, hence the complete right tail. The smooth zero extension pays the left endpoint. Equations (7),(8),(10) prove (2). H=1 is included: the residual vanishes exactly and B_1=a.

statement:
## HCR3. Independent reconstruction of the two-root transform

Let H(w)=integral_0^infinity D_A f(u) exp(-wu) du. For Re w>b, HCR2.1
and |B_(Au)(v)|<=Au make the triangular Fubini step absolutely valid:
the double absolute majorant is a constant times

    integral_0^infinity u exp(-(Re w-b)u)du
    * integral_0^infinity exp(-(1-b)v)dv < infinity.

Writing t=u+v gives H(w)=integral_0^infinity f(t)K_w(t)dt with

    K_w(t)=exp(-wt)-exp(-t)*integral_0^t exp((1-w)u)
                   *sqrt(Au/(t-u))*J_1(2sqrt(Au(t-u)))du.

In a far right q-half-plane, integrate the Bessel series term by term.
The k-th term in the transform of the second summand equals

    (-1)^k A^(k+1)/((q+w)^(k+2)*(q+1)^(k+1)).

Here the integrals of u^(k+1) and v^k cancel both factorials. The resulting
geometric series, initially where it converges absolutely, yields

    integral_0^infinity K_w(t)exp(-qt)dt
       = 1/(q+w)-A/((q+w)*((q+w)*(q+1)+A))
       = (q+1)/((q+1)*(q+w)+A).                           (HCR3.1)

Let s_1+s_2=1+w and s_1*s_2=w+A. Then the denominator is
(q+s_1)(q+s_2), and

    K_w(t)=[(1-s_1)exp(-s_1*t)+(s_2-1)exp(-s_2*t)]/(s_2-s_1).

For real w sufficiently large both roots have real part greater than b;
the smaller root tends to 1 from the right. In an open neighborhood of
such w we may integrate against f and obtain exactly

    H(w)=[(1-s_1)F(s_1)+(s_2-1)F(s_2)]/(s_2-s_1).         (HCR3.2)

The relation between each root and w is

    w=phi_A(s)=s-A/(1-s),
    s_(1,2)=(1+w +/- sqrt((1-w)^2-4A))/2.

The plus/minus ordering is immaterial. HCR3.2 is symmetric in the roots.
At a collision s_1=s_2=s with F regular, it tends to
F(s)-(1-s)F'(s). There is no forced branch singularity of the full field.
More generally a symmetric meromorphic divided difference descends
meromorphically through the quadratic cover. On compact w-sets its roots
remain bounded, so only finitely many poles of F occur. This gives a
single-valued meromorphic function R(w) on the whole plane. Applying the
same expression to the entire E gives an entire function of w, including
at collisions. The Gaussian left tail contributes no hidden branch pole.

For the displayed A values the collision roots 1+/-sqrt(A) are positive
real numbers where F is regular. Real zeta has no zero in (0,1), as also
follows from its alternating eta representation; it is nonzero for real
s>1. The reciprocal zeta factor is regular at 1. Larger A need not share
this collision simplification, but meromorphic descent still holds.

A useful independent sign/residue check is f(u)=exp(rho*u), Re rho<1.
Directly, D_A f(u)=exp(phi_A(rho)*u). Substitution of F(s)=1/(s-rho) in
HCR3.2 simplifies to 1/(w-phi_A(rho)), exactly. There is no extra Jacobian
or an additional unpriced exponential in this single-pole signal.
title: HCR3. Independent reconstruction of the two-root transform

statement:
### 5.3 Uniform gain is a separate question from qualitative return

Even the two incommensurate filters have no positive uniform joint gain
on the vertical line Re s=beta. Put alpha=log3/log2, irrational. Among
Q+1 fractional parts0,alpha,...,Q alpha, two lie in the same one of Q
equal bins. For some1<=q<=Q, distance(q alpha,Z)<=1/Q. At
t=2pi q/log2 the symbol for2 vanishes and that for3 has magnitude
at most2pi/Q. Along Q tending to infinity a subsequence of q is
unbounded, because any finite nonzero q has strictly positive distance
from an integer. Hence both symbols can be arbitrarily small at
unbounded heights without a common nonreal zero.

This disproves a fixed positive all-height gain for this filter pair.
It does NOT invalidate A13's fixed-zero analytic return: a nonzero
residue, however small, still contradicts holomorphy. Conflating these
two quantifiers would repeat an avoidable signal mistake.

For general x-dependent counterterms there is no single fixed symbol
A13. If c(x)=lambda^beta+e(x), the exact additional source is
-e(x)F_chi(x/lambda). Under an available F_chi=O(x^beta) bound, a
supremum bound e=O(X^(-(beta-gamma))) on the parent shell is sufficient
to pay that residual at gamma. This only prices the extra error; it
does not supply the desired norm of the constant-counterterm G_lambda.
The inherited f3 beta bound is not a known pure beta mode to cancel.

Ancestry remains fixed-filter/translated-detector and W22/W36 pole-safe
counterterm work. This audit's contribution is the explicit actual-f3
two-scale symbol, complete common-zero/multiplicity return and precise
distinction between qualitative return and uniform gain. It is not a
new family or an unconditional stable arithmetic fixed point.

### A complete and faster source-tail bound

Let H0=sqrt(2a)C_q/(a-gamma), K=1+2a/(a-gamma). Then
|Q^j h(t)|<=H0 K^j exp(-gamma t). The omitted Gram beyond T is PSD
and at most (N+1)H0^2 K^(2N)exp(-2gamma T)/(2gamma) times I. For an
explicit polynomial, its complete squared error is at most

    integral_0^T |p(Q)h-F0 ell0|^2 dt
      +H0^2(sum_j |p_j|K^j)^2 exp(-2gamma T)/gamma
      +2|F0|^2 exp(-2aT).                           (9)

The exponential degree cost can instead be paid by a coherent source
approximation. If ||h-h_tilde||<=tau, the isometry gives

    ||p(Q)(h-h_tilde)||<=tau sum_j |p_j|.           (10)

Every Gram-entry error is <=tau(||h||+||h_tilde||), and its operator
error is at most N+1 times that amount. This is an absolute error,
not a PSD ordering of the two Grams. Even a compactly supported
h_tilde has full filtered future responses, which must be included.

For1/2<gamma<1 put lambda=a-gamma=2-2gamma in(0,1). At q=1, with
u={x}, f(log x)=1/2+B(x)-V(x)/x, B=1/2-u, V=u(1-u). The bounded
primitive of B is V/2, of norm<=1/8. Integrating by parts with its
lower endpoint, then paying V/x absolutely, proves

    |integral_x^infinity y^(lambda-1)(f(log y)-1/2)dy|
        <=D_lambda x^(lambda-1),
    D_lambda=(2-lambda)/[4(1-lambda)].              (11)

Thus h(t)=A0 exp(-gamma t)+C exp(-at)+R(t),
A0=sqrt(2a)/(2lambda), |R(t)|<=sqrt(2a)D_lambda exp(-(gamma+1)t).
Keep h unchanged on[0,T] and continue explicitly by

    h_tilde(t)=A0 exp(-gamma t)
       +(h(T)-A0 exp(-gamma T))exp[-a(t-T)]  for t>T.

Subtracting the expansions at t and T and paying both L2 tails yields

    ||h-h_tilde||<=D_lambda[1+sqrt(a/(gamma+1))]
                            exp[-(gamma+1)T].     (12)

No unknown infinite constant C is needed for this continuation.

All ordinary characters have the same construction. For nonprincipal
chi, A is q-periodic; subtract its mean m_chi. The mean-zero remainder
has primitive bounded by2q^2. For principal chi let B0=A-rx, beta its
period mean, D(x)=integral_1^x(B0-beta). Directly from(3),

    f(log x)=-beta+(B0(x)-beta)+(r+2beta-2D(x))/x.  (13)

The bounds |D|<=2q^2 and |r+2beta-2D|<=1+2q+4q^2 give(11)-(12)
with A0=sqrt(2a)m_chi/lambda and D_chi=4q^2 for nonprincipal chi,
or D_chi=4q^2+(1+2q+4q^2)/(1-lambda) for principal chi. Natural zeros
and complex components are retained. Fixed-q constants are allowed.
The constants blow up at gamma=1/2; no endpoint claim is made.

This adapts [private research revision]'s bounded-periodic-primitive method to the exact
pole-normalized source. It pays source formation, with the coefficient
sum in(10), but leaves the full signed prediction residual OPEN.
title: A complete and faster source-tail bound

## A uniform coarse price, including moving weights

The diagonal of E=B^*B is

    E_(S,S)=sum_(p notin S, p*n_S>N)|w_p|^2.

Let kappa_q=product_(p|q)(1-1/p) product_(p not|q)(1-1/p^2)>0. For every fixed q, elementary square-divisor expansion gives

    #{n<=x:squarefree,(n,q)=1}=kappa_q x+O_q(sqrt x).  (F7)

For a fixed unramified p, the number C_p(N) of source states crossed by p is

    C_p(N)=kappa_q (p-1)/(p+1) N+O_(q,p)(sqrt N).     (F8)

To prove the needed UNIFORM lower bound for all p, first handle the finitely many p<4/kappa_q using F8. For every larger p, count squarefree q-units in (N/2,N] and remove at most N/p multiples of p. Every retained n crosses the cutoff because pn>N. Therefore, once N exceeds a q-dependent threshold,

    (kappa_q/8) N <= C_p(N) <= N    for EVERY p not|q,
    (kappa_q/8) WN <= Tr(E) <= WN.                    (F9)

Primes p>N are allowed in this statement: every represented n then crosses. Thus arbitrary nonnegative weighting, moving prime blocks, or normalization by W cannot make this particular positive boundary-trace certificate sublinear. Its normalized exponent is one, missing the near, 5/6 and 3/4 targets. It is NOT a lower bound on |Str(T_chi E)+Str([T_chi,D^*]D)|, M_chi, a Gaussian moment or native H.

F7 follows by writing mu^2(n)=sum_(d^2|n)mu(d), counting q-unit multiples of d^2 with O_q(1) error and completing the d^-2 sum. For F8 use the same count with modulus qp and subtract endpoints N and N/p; its density is kappa_q p/(p+1). This supplies an elementary proof rather than a reliance on a prime number theorem.
title: A uniform coarse price, including moving weights

### 2.2 Two PNT substitutions with all boundary terms

Fix N=10. For fixed r and q, put w(p)=g(log(rpq/x)). On the finite
rectangle log p is comparable to L and E(p)=pi(p)-li(p) obeys
|E(p)|<=C_N p/L^N. Exact Stieltjes integration by parts on (z,B_X]
therefore gives the error

    [E(p)w(p)]_z^(B_X)-integral_z^(B_X)E(p)w'(p)dp.

The two endpoint terms each have absolute size at most
C x/(rqL^N), since p g(log(rpq/x))=(x/(rq))exp(u)g(u).
The integral has the same bound because

    integral_z^(B_X) p|w'(p)|dp
       <=(x/(rq))integral_R exp(u)|g'(u)|du.

Hence CT4 holds with the sharp exclusion p>z, including prime z.
Summing its absolute errors over actual q in the rectangle and
r<=X^d uses just two harmonic bounds and costs O(X/L^(N-2)).

After this first replacement, exchange the existing p integral and
the q sum. Apply the same estimate to the q sum for each real p in
that integral. Its error is C x/(rpL^N). Integrating against dp/log p
is bounded by integrating dp, so the p integral of 1/p is O(L).
The core harmonic sum is O(L) again. This pays the second replacement
by O(X/L^(N-2)). In fact the retained log p denominator improves
that estimate, but is unnecessary. These two errors are bounded in
sequence; there is no assumption that pi errors multiply benignly.
Coefficient signs remain solely in the main term.

## 5. Kernel sign, quantitative contradiction, and open remainder

For \(x\in[X,2X]\), the profile arguments in this block satisfy

\[
\frac{11}5\le\frac nx\le\frac{483}{100},\qquad
\frac{24}5\le\frac{n'}x\le\frac{1023}{100}.
\tag{SF31}
\]

On the containing interval \([11/5,1023/100]\),
\(t-1-t^{-1}\ge41/55\) and \(t+t^{-1}<11\). Thus both
profiles are negative and, with the explicit constant
\(c_\phi=(41/55)e^{-11}>0\),

\[
|\phi(n/x)|,|\phi(n'/x)|\ge c_\phi,
\qquad K_X(n,n')\ge c_\phi^2\log2.
\tag{SF32}
\]

Different quadruples in (SF21) give different ordered pairs
\((n,n')\): unique factorization and the disjoint prime intervals
recover each of the four primes. Consequently the following is a
literal subsum of the exact coalesced signed form (SF12), with all
factorizations at each of its product pairs retained:

\[
\mathcal T_{X,W}:=
4\sum_{(p_1,p_2,p_3,p_4)\in\mathcal P_{X,W}}
K_X(Wp_1p_2,Wp_3p_4)
\gg\frac{X^2}{W^2L^4}>0.
\tag{SF33}
\]

It lower bounds \(\mathcal A_{X,W}\), proving the lower half of
(SF14). No positivity is asserted for the complement in
\(Q_W^{\rm sf}\).

For the upper half, the triangle inequality for (SF11) and (SF7)
bounds \(\mathcal A_{X,W}\) by the absolute raw form. There are
\(O(U_{\max}^4)=O(X^2L^{16})\) choices for the four long
factors, \(O(J^2)=O(L^{12})\) choices for the two third factors,
and every weight and profile is uniformly bounded. Integration
has measure \(\log2\). This gives \(O(X^2L^{28})\), as claimed.

The precise power loss against the desired target is

\[
2-2a=\frac{12551}{50000}=.25102.
\tag{SF34}
\]

Thus for every fixed \(0<\epsilon<12551/50000\),
\(\mathcal A_{X,W}\ll_\epsilon X^{2a+\epsilon}\) is false,
even with fixed \(W=2\), and uniformly moving permitted \(W\)
does not repair it. A fixed-product regrouping followed by a
triangle inequality cannot pay the remaining energy: (SF11)
already groups every admissible factorization at that pair.

This result has a different scope from the generic-coefficient
countermodel [SP30--SP34](../[private research revision]/mobius-separated-products.md#6-a-precise-limit-of-the-profile-moment-argument):
all coefficients here are actual \(\mu\), the local convolution
identity is used exactly, and the whole coefficient at the selected
completed-product pair is evaluated. It also differs from the
prime-square sector in PO14: that sector has \(c_p(v)=0\) for
\(v\ge2\); the present block has \(v=1\) at every selected prime
on both sides, with nonzero complete coefficient.

The signed target [OPEN-PO](../[private research revision]/mobius-prime-orbits.md#7-exact-residual-form-and-the-power-budget)
remains

\[
|Q_W^{\rm sf}|\ll_\epsilon X^{2a+\epsilon}.
\tag{OPEN-SF}
\]

If it holds for any fixed \(\epsilon<12551/50000\), then
\(Q_W^{\rm sf}-\mathcal T_{X,W}=-\mathcal T_{X,W}+o(\mathcal
T_{X,W})\). Hence its complement must supply cancellation of the
size in (SF33) across *different* completed-product pairs. This is
a necessary quantitative demand, not an estimate proved here.
The next arithmetic input must control such cancellation in the
\(W\)-free factors, for example through a convolution decomposition
that changes completed products and retains the finite endpoints.
A second selected-prime allocation identity at fixed products,
or the zero moment of a profile that has one sign on this block,
does not supply that input.

The imported internal-gcd preparation is still the norm comparison
PO35; it is not converted into an additive error between energies.
Only the separately established PO43 energy identity connects
(OPEN-SF) to that prepared norm. No height range, fixed cutoff,
cofactor multiplier range, or numerical zero-free constant changes.

## 6. Quantitative obstruction and exact arithmetic

Apply (B) to the single fixed model from M and set H=floor(X^theta), with theta<beta. The asymptotic at x=X gives |F_a(X)| >= c X^beta for every sufficiently large X, since its leading coefficient is nonzero. The O(H) replacement term is lower order. Because X/H+1 is comparable to X^(1-theta), squaring the remaining inequality yields

    E_a(X,H) >= c' X^(2beta-1+theta)                    (O)

for every sufficiently large X. The constants may depend on the fixed model and tau. This is not merely a subsequence lower bound.

Consequently an upper estimate E_a << X^(1+delta+epsilon) for every epsilon>0 is impossible when theta-delta > 2(1-beta). Choose epsilon strictly below the positive exponent gap. Equality is not excluded by this argument. More generally, if (A) would return a proposed exponent gamma<beta, then gamma>=theta and e<=2gamma-1+theta force e<2beta-1+theta, contradicting (O). The target must have gamma>=theta for the claimed return in the first place.

At theta=13/50, the exact comparisons are:

| Quantity | Exact value | Decimal |
|---|---:|---:|
| First-gain energy boundary | 504861/500000 | 1.009722 |
| Energy needed for gamma=.87449 | 50449/50000 | 1.00898 |
| Model beta | 8747/10000 | .8747 |
| Available weaker calibration | 2187/2500 | .8748 |
| Model's forced energy exponent | 5047/5000 | 1.0094 |
| Strict obstruction gap | 21/50000 | .00042 |

Here .87449 < .8747 < .8748 < b6. Thus the model satisfies the incumbent coarse summatory calibration and every fixed-H Cesaro energy limit, while blocking this growing-window target. For any proposed gamma<b6 in the meaningful range, choose beta between max(gamma,1/2) and b6 and a calibration exponent between beta and b6. This is a scoped obstruction to coarse-data proofs of a gain, not an impossibility for the arithmetic coefficients.

The conditional returns were also recomputed independently:

| theta | Assumed energy e | Returned gamma | Conditional c=1-gamma |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 13/50 | 1 | 87/100 | 13/100 |
| 1/3 | 1 | 5/6 | 1/6 |
| 1/2 | 1 | 3/4 | 1/4 |
| 3/5 | 11/10 | 3/4 | 1/4 |

Its gap to the first-gain boundary is exactly 2c6 = 125139/500000 = .250278, independently of theta. Qualitative o(XH) has no guaranteed fixed power saving and does not close this gap. This remains true even though the model has stronger fixed-form Cesaro cancellation than the qualitative logarithmic limits invoked as motivation.

## 3. Prime input, product size, and all-order Euler bounds

The only prime-distribution input is the fixed-order PNT already accepted in [private research revision] review §2:

    R(v)=pi(v)-li(v)=O_N(v/(log v)^N), v>=2,           (F9)

for each FIXED N. That review pins Johnston-Yang v2, Corollary1.3, to the stronger explicit bound 9.59v(log v)^.515 exp(-.8274 sqrt(log v)). This report uses F9 as that established primary input. No new provider call, short-interval relative PNT, or order N growing with X is used. N=10 suffices for the source approximation and is selected in advance; a separately chosen stronger fixed order gives any requested fixed rate in the prime-product asymptotic below.

Standard partial summation from F9 gives

    sum_(p<=z) log p/p <<t,
    p_z=product_(p<=z)(1-1/p)
          =(e^(-gamma_E)/t)[1+O_N(t^(-N))].           (F10)

For the stated rate, use a stronger fixed PNT order in the convergent error tail for sum1/p, exactly as in [private research revision] §2. Since

    (p-2)/(p-1)=(1-1/p)(1-1/(p-1)^2),

one has

    P(z)=3p_z product_(5<=p<=z)(1-1/(p-1)^2)
        =(kappa/t)[1+O_N(t^(-N))],
    kappa=3e^(-gamma_E)
                 product_(p>=5)(1-1/(p-1)^2)>0.        (F11)

The remaining convergent-product tail is O(1/z). In particular P(z) is comparable to1/t throughout t>=4. Also partial summation gives sum_(p<=z)log p/p=t+O(1), and the difference between p/((p-1)(p-2)) and1/p is O(1/p^2), proving D_z=2t+O(1).

For POSITIVE smooth cores with full valuations use

    Z_z(s)=product_(p<=z)(1-p^(-s))^(-1),

not the squarefree product from RN. On |s-1|<=1/t and t>=4, Re s>=3/4 and p^(1/t)<=e for p<=z. All relevant denominator factors are bounded away from zero. The factors1-2p^(-s) are also bounded away from zero for p>=5, since2*5^(-3/4)<1. Integrating their logarithmic derivatives from1 to s gives

    |Z_z(s)|<=C Z_z(1)<=Ct,
    |J_z(s)|<=C J_z(1)<=C P(z).                        (F12)

Indeed each derivative sum is at most C sum_(p<=z)log p/p<=Ct, and the integration length is at most1/t. The logs have analytic branches on this disk; the p=2 zero is excluded from J_z rather than hidden in a logarithm.

Write H_z(s)=(s-1)V_z(s). The quotient A_2(s)/(s-1) is analytic and uniformly bounded on |s-1|<=1/4, so

    V_z(1)=h_z,  sup_(|s-1|<=1/t)|V_z(s)|<=C h_z.

Cauchy's estimate yields, SIMULTANEOUSLY for every integer j>=1,

    |H_z^(j)(1)|<=C h_z j! t^(j-1).                  (F13)

There is no unspecified growing O_j constant. The simple p=2 zero saves one power of t, which is crucial at the derivative-main-term scale.

The positive tilt Z_z(1-1/t)<=Ct and u^j<=j!e^u give, for all j>=0,

    sum_(r in S(z)) (log r)^j/r <=Ct j!t^j.           (F14)

If R_0=e^Q>=1, splitting the exponential between the power and the tail gives

    sum_(r>R_0,r in S(z)) (log r)^j/r
          <=Ct e^(-Q/(2t)) j!(2t)^j,                 (F15)
    sum_(r>R_0,r in S(z)) 1/r <=Ct e^(-Q/t).          (F16)

For F15, pointwise use 1_(log r>Q)(log r)^j <= e^(-Q/(2t)) j!(2t)^j exp(log r/t). Thus these estimates pay the completion of all signed moments even when the Taylor degree grows. This adapts the finite-Euler method to full valuations; it is not an application of RN's squarefree-core formula.

## G153. Asymmetric completion and a one-Mobius core

The independent critic takes A=floor(eta_0 X^u), V=1. Since m_1=delta_1,

    (a-delta_1)*b_p=q_p-b_p=:h_p,
    R_(A,1)=u_A*h_p.

Explicitly h_p(1)=0, h_p(p)=-chi(p), and otherwise
h_p(j)=-chi(j)(1-p 1_(p|j)); |h_p(j)|<=p-1.
The two exceptional coefficients must remain. This h_p is not globally
periodic mean-zero after those corrections.

The actual asymmetric core is

    A_(p,chi,X)(x)=sum_(d>A,j>=2,L<dj<=M)
                    mu(d)chi(d)h_p(j)f_x(dj).            (91.6)

Its coefficients are bounded by (p-1)d_2(n); the literal cofactor cap is
j<=M/(A+1)<<_(p,q,k)X^(r-u), not a unit-constant cap. Applying (91.3)
with these cutoffs and retaining all complementary sources gives

    ||C_p-A_(p,chi,X)||_j<<X^(gamma+epsilon), j=1,2.       (91.7)

The same two-prime return applies. This is an exact simplification of the
remaining source, not a proof of its power bound.

When p does not divide n the merged residual coefficient is

    (u_A*h_p)(n)=-chi(n)sum_(d|n,A<d<n)mu(d).

It vanishes on primes. For distinct primes r,s not dividing pq it equals
chi(rs)(1_(r>A)+1_(s>A)); it vanishes when both primes are <=A.
This coefficient identity retains the original product cut and all signs.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| .1252 | 2187/2500 | 5313/5000 | 687/1000 | 687/2000 | 687/1000 | 939/2500 |
| 1/6 | 5/6 | 13/12 | 7/12 | 7/24 | 7/12 | 1/2 |
| 1/4 | 3/4 | 9/8 | 3/8 | 3/16 | 3/8 | 3/4 |

statement:
## 6. Deliberately coarse bounds and two failed repairs

The elementary positive estimate on(15) is

    |C_N,T,G|<=C_r h (sum_(n>N)n^(-r))^2
                <<_r N^(1-2r).                     (18)

It misses the c7 first-gain requirement by a power strictly exceeding .250280. Raising the fixed Bernoulli order r does not reduce that missing exponent: its apparent extra decay is exactly cancelled by the weighted-tail observation and Abel inverse. Formula(7) shows that a complete-period signed estimate cannot repair(18); even the exact signed energy has this same order.

The positivity failure is not just a hypothetical choice of signs. For q=1,r=2, Phi(x)=2pi^2 B_2({x}), where B_2(u)=u^2-u+1/6. The squared period norm of B_2 is integral B_2^2=1/180, and B_2 is globally Lipschitz with constant1 and supremum1/6. Put eta=1/120. If 1<=a,b<=1+eta,

    integral_0^1 B_2({au})B_2({bu})du
       >=1/180-eta/3=1/360.                         (19)

This follows by comparing each factor to B_2(u) using the stated Lipschitz and supremum bounds. Therefore, for every integer pair N<n,m<=(1+eta)N,

    K_N(n,m)>=pi^4/(90N).

There are asymptotically delta(1)eta N squarefree integers in this interval by(5). Pairs with gcd>=G are at most

    sum_(g>=G) floor((1+eta)N/g)^2
       <=(1+eta)^2N^2 sum_(g>=G)g^(-2)=O(N^2/G).

Thus, for any fixed positive power G of N, the actual absolute-pair price even after integrating the oscillatory kernel satisfies

    sum_(N<n,m<=T; gcd(n,m)<G)
       |a(n)a(m)|(nm)^(-2)|K_N(n,m)| >> N^(-3).     (20)

Here T eventually contains the fixed narrow interval, and all coefficients are the actual squarefree Mobius coefficients. Replacing mu(n)mu(m) by its absolute value loses exactly the needed power at the level of this route. Equation(20) does NOT lower-bound the signed core or the actual local energy. It rules out the specified absolute-kernel repair, not a cancellation theorem, and is compatible with RH.

Repair A was to subtract the computable leading term in(7), whose remainder already has the formal half-power needed for c=1/4. This fails as a positive localization argument. A difference of scalar energies has no inherited inequality controlling the energy on a subinterval. Implementing the subtraction as any fixed finite normalized linear combination of the underlying fields fails by(9). A growing-scale family remains outside(9) and would require its own observation and conditioning costs.

Repair B was to remove the first Fourier band, leaving a possibly smaller global source. At x=0 that actual band is

    B_N(0)=2 sum_(N<n<=2N)mu(n)chi(n)/n^r.           (21)

To bound(21) by N^(gamma-r+epsilon) for every integer N at a stronger gamma would already give the needed new Mertens estimate: sum(21) over N,2N,4N,... to obtain T_N with the same exponent, since gamma<r, and apply(14). Conversely a Mertens bound gives that estimate by Abel summation. Thus the removed band cannot be charged an improved bound as though it were an innocuous known error. Paying it only with the incumbent Mertens exponent returns at most the incumbent. The exact spectral gap does not exempt this entire band.

## 2. Exact local forcing, including the embedding exceptions

At a good prime put
\(\alpha=v_p(a),\ \beta=v_p(b),\ s=v_p(e),\ t=v_p(d)\).
The embeddings are squarefree, so \(s,t\in\{0,1\}\) and \(st=0\). The exponent in (PH3) is
\[
\kappa_p=\max\{0,\alpha-1-2s,\beta-1-2t\}.
\]
For every atom pair whose good local kernel is not identically zero, every nonzero row satisfies \(v_p(r)\ge\kappa_p\). Moreover PC4 can be formed so that every one of its divisor ideals \(k\) is divisible by \(\mathfrak f\).

Here is the complete local verification, before taking absolute values.

1. If \(p\mid AA'\), the original column zero extensions force \(r\) to be a unit and require \((A,e)=(A',d)=1\). The surviving outer exponents are
   \(\alpha\in\{0,1+2s\},\ \beta\in\{0,1+2t\}\).
   Thus \(\kappa_p=0\). A surviving embedded exponent three has **no** forced \(p\)-divisibility in the common row. This remains true when a column character is principal on units.
2. Outside \(AA'\), a positive nonprincipal outer exponent \(j\not\equiv0\pmod6\) forces the exact valuation \(j-1-2s\ge0\) on the first side, or \(j-1-2t\ge0\) on the second. A negative prescribed valuation makes that local kernel zero. If both sides are nonprincipal, their prescribed valuations must agree. If only one is nonprincipal, its prescribed valuation must lie in the support of the other side. For a surviving pair the resulting valuation is at least \(\kappa_p\).
3. A positive principal exponent \(j\equiv0\pmod6\) has the exact normalized kernel
   \[
   q^{j/2}1_{p^{j-2s}\mid r}
   -q^{j/2-1}1_{p^{j-1-2s}\mid r}.
   \]
   Its smallest supported valuation is \(j-1-2s\). Products of principal kernels combine divisors by their maximum. Consequently every term remains divisible by \(p^{\kappa_p}\). The lower divisor never receives the larger coefficient.
4. At a relative-conductor prime, some nonprincipal unit character remains. Outside \(AA'\), two principal-only outer factors cannot produce such a prime. If both outer factors are nonprincipal, the equality of their forced valuations gives \(\alpha-\beta=2(s-t)\). Away from an embedding this makes the prime coherent; at an unequal embedding it can leave exponent \(\pm2\pmod6\). This is the additional embedding-only active case. Its forced valuation is still exactly the one above.

At coherent primes an exact unit condition is expanded as a difference of two divisibility masks. Their exponents are \(\kappa_p\) and \(\kappa_p+1\), or larger. At conductor primes the primitive character supplies the unit condition and the forced valuation stays inside \(k\). CRT phases are units and are retained in PC4's coefficients. None of these operations can introduce a divisor exponent below \(\kappa_p\).

In particular,
\[
\mathfrak f\mid k\quad\hbox{for every term of PC4},\qquad
F\le q_aq_b\ll Y_DY_E\le Y^2.
\]
The original common row profile is supported in a fixed positive annulus \(q_r\asymp H\). Therefore a nonzero physical row also requires \(F\ll H\). These support assertions concern \(R>1\) covariances; an empty row sum is not being identified with a vanished coherent continuous zero.

## 4A. Paying interactions between all short rows together

A stronger bound combines the preceding prefix removal with W24's local count of LARGE SQUARE DIVISORS, including multiplicity. Let 1<=D<=X^alpha0 for fixed 0<=alpha0<1; let |u_d|<=1 be shell-fixed complex coefficients. For each d<=D and e=1,p choose ANY shell-fixed prefix endpoint R_(d,e), possibly empty or infinite, and set

    Q_D(x)=sum_(d<=D) u_d sum_(e=1,p) q1(e)
                    sum_(r<=R_(d,e)) beta(r) f_x(e d r^2).

Then the full source satisfies

    ||Q_D||_2^2 << D^2 + X^(6/11) D^(16/11)
                 + min(X^(3/4)D^(3/2),X^(5/4)D^(1/2)). (4A.1)

Constants depend only on fixed p,q,alpha0. No cancellation in u_d is assumed. This is a complete norm bound, not a comparison to a signed subset.

Proof, including multiplicity. Remove the low prefix r<=R0(ed)=c0(X/(ed))^(6/11) in each row exactly as in Section4. Its pointwise total is O(D), including both weighted e labels. Merge the remaining ACTUAL coefficients into z_X(n). If n=e d r^2 contributes then d<=D, hence r^2>=n/(pD); for each r and n each e determines at most one d. Thus

    |z_X(n)| <= C_p sum_(r^2|n, r^2>=n/(pD)) 1.       (4A.2)

This positive coefficient majorant retains every shared square, collision between d rows, q1 label, and character zero. Arbitrary prefix endpoints and the strict condition r>R0(ed) only reduce this positive count. They never justify comparing two signed norms. Every surviving n satisfies the STRICT lower bound

    n>N0=c0^2 p^(-1/11) X^(12/11)D^(-1/11).          (4A.3)

Indeed n=edr^2>c0^2 X^(12/11)(ed)^(-1/11). For fixed alpha0<1, N0/X tends to infinity. All initial X ranges are absorbed into fixed constants.

For a comparable block n in[N/2,4N], put T_N=sqrt(N/(8pD)) and w_N(n)=#{r>T_N:r^2|n}. Equation (4A.2) is bounded by C_p w_N(n). W24 R24.3-R24.4, now with ambient scale N and square-root threshold T_N, gives for ANY interval I in this block of length H

    sum_(n in I) w_N(n) << H sqrt(D/N)+E_N,
    E_N=min(N^(1/3),D),
    sum_(n in[N/2,4N]) w_N(n) << sqrt(ND).           (4A.4)

This counts PAIRS (r,m) with r^2 m=n. For completeness: if T_N<=N^(1/3), sum roots up to N^(1/3) by H/r^2+1, then reverse the larger roots by their complementary m; the latter root interval has length O(H/(sqrt(N)sqrt(m))). This costs H/T_N+N^(1/3). If T_N>N^(1/3), reverse all roots to get H/T_N+N/T_N^2. The global count is sum_(r>T_N)floor(4N/r^2)<<N/T_N. Fixed p factors are absorbed. Nonintegral thresholds, closed endpoints, H<1 and single-point intervals are covered by length-plus-one; E_N>=1. For large X, T_N>=1 by (4A.3).

Use the same positive smooth shell majorant. Two integrations by parts give the FULL integer kernel

    |K_X(n,m)| << exp(-c(n+m)/X^(3/2))
                    min(1,[X^6/|n^6-m^6|]^2),       (4A.5)

with the min interpreted as1 on the diagonal. For comparable n,m~N, |n^6-m^6|>=c N^5|n-m|. Put H_N=X^6/N^5. Apply (4A.4) to the central interval |m-n|<=H_N and both annuli of radii 2^j H_N. Their kernel weights are O(2^(-2j)). Summing gives, for EACH n,

    sum_(m~N) w_N(m) min(1,[H_N/|n-m|]^2)
          << H_N sqrt(D/N)+E_N.

This includes the diagonal with its full multiplicity and both orientations. Multiplying by the total outer mass in (4A.4) proves the comparable-block price

    << exp(-cN/X^(3/2))

## 7. Quartic localization, all amplified tails, and arithmetic return

Take r=j^(1/8), W_j(u)=K((u-j)/r)/K(0), H_j=h4 W_j. The Fourier transform
of W_j is r exp(-r^4t^4)exp(-ijt)/K(0). For r>=1, the estimate

    x^4/2+r^4(t-x)^4 >= t^4/32+(r^4/2)(t-x)^4            (R36)

follows from (x+y)^4<=8(x^4+y^4). For clarity, the latter has the exact
nonnegative remainder
(x-y)^2(7x^2+10xy+7y^2), and
7x^2+10xy+7y^2=2(x^2+y^2)+5(x+y)^2. The convolution of R35 with the
window therefore has bound C A_b exp(-t^4/32): integration of the remaining
exp(-r^4(t-x)^4/2) contributes O(1/r), cancelling the transform's factor r.
All constants are independent of j and its center.

Cut the Fourier integral at T_j=[32(b-gamma+2)j]^(1/4). The full error is

    ||H_j-P_j||_infinity
        <=C T_j^-3 exp(-(b-gamma+2)j).                    (R37)

Use the same integer-ended I_j, augmented set S_j and worst local density
as in Section 2. Under log(1/delta_k)=o(k^(3/4)), the sampling cost is

    Lambda_j=(200/delta_j^*)^(132T_j+1)=exp(o(j)).          (R38)

On observations with source allowance eta, put d=b-gamma-eta>0. R33 gives

    |H_j(u)|<=C exp(-du-c|u-j|^(4/3)/r^(4/3))
       <=C exp(-dj+27d^4 r^4/(256c^3))
        =exp(-dj+O(sqrt(j))).                            (R39)

The constant in the Legendre maximum is exact: maximize
d v-c v^(4/3)/r^(4/3) over v>=0 at
v=(3d/(4c))^3 r^4. The value is 27d^4r^4/(256c^3).

On the added exterior, global boundedness of h4 and R33 yield
O(exp(-c'j^(7/6))), since j^(4/3)/r^(4/3)=j^(7/6). This dominates both
the later exp(bj) factor and sampling exp(o(j)). R37 is likewise multiplied
by Lambda_j+1 before it is discarded. The same norm inequality as R8 then
proves the source exponent gamma. Finally, W_j(u) tends uniformly to one
on [j,j+1], by continuity of K at zero and r tending to infinity; hence
|W_j|>=1/2 there for large j. Dividing by the window is justified on the
target interval despite K's sign changes elsewhere.

All epsilon choices follow the same order as in Section 2: fix the output
allowance, choose eta with d>0, then take the scale large. Only a fixed
kernel and one absolute line are used. This proves Theorem C, including
the full spatial and frequency errors after amplification.

For the left Mellin tail, write u=-U. R33 and A_b give a bound by A_b times
the maximum of exp(bv-c(v+U)^(4/3)) over v>=0. For U sufficiently large
its derivative in v is negative; the maximum is at zero. Thus
F4(-U)=O(A_b exp(-cU^(4/3))). The right tail from the proved observation
return gives holomorphy on Re s>gamma. On Re s>1, the three literal
arithmetic transforms are respectively

    exp(-s^4)/L(s,chi),
    exp(-s^4)/L(s,psi),
    exp(-s^4)B(s)/zeta(s).                               (R40)

The same continuation argument as Section 4 now gives the stated zero
exclusions, with the same fixed-family domains, modulus zeros, principal
pole treatment, and actual p2/p3 multiplier. This proves the new detector's
own return. It does not import the Gaussian RR positivity, Gaussian hard
mask estimates, Gaussian small-value sets, or Theorem B into this signed
kernel. Each such transfer would require a separate argument.

Its nonzero prime-power coefficients are chi(p)^nu for nu=0 mod r and -chi(p)^nu for nu=1 mod r. This valid coupled construction is retained; no separate-layer norm is licensed.

For the principal character modulo1, each separated layer has D_(a_j)(z)=zeta(z)^(omega^j)H_j(z), with H_j analytic and nonzero near1: the logarithm of its Euler correction starts at prime powers of order2 and converges normally there. A nonzero finite Euler filter Q has integer order m at1, so QD_(a_j) has local factor (z-1)^(m-omega^j). For a noninteger omega^j this cannot be a single-valued holomorphic function near1. statement:
## T03. Cube-free physical-row lifting — PROVED, sharp operator threshold

**Provenance:** SB §3 (N2a)–(N2c), BA R2; BB R03 independently has a weaker but valid divisor-Cauchy proof. The weighted Schur proof is the strongest convenient version.

Write uniquely
\[
h=h_0r^3,\qquad h_0=ab^2,\quad a,b\ {\rm sf},\quad(a,b)=1,
\]
and let `U` be the product of primes dividing `r` but not `h0 S`. No coprimality between `r` and `ab` is imposed. The cubic symbol satisfies
\[
\vartheta_c(h)=\vartheta_c(h_0)1_{(c,U)=1}.
\]
At a prime already in `h0` both sides have the same zero; at an extra prime of `r`, the cube value is one only on units. Inclusion–exclusion and (T0) give
\[
D_h(s)=\sum_{g\mid U}\mu(g)\beta(g)\vartheta_g(h_0)q_g^{-s}D_{gh_0}(s).
\tag{T03.1}
\]
Crucially the outside character is evaluated at `h0`, not at the full `h`; the latter would incorrectly kill all nontrivial terms.

The incidences in this identity are equivalently and bijectively
\[
h=kg^2d^3,\qquad k\text{ cube-free},\quad
 g\mid\operatorname{rad}_{=1}(k),\quad d\text{ arbitrary}.
\tag{T03.2}
\]
From the first parametrization take `k=gh0`, `r=gd`; conversely take `h0=k/g`, `r=gd`. Prime valuations verify the inverse and uniqueness for a fixed pair `(h,k)`. In particular `q_k<=q_h`. Neither `(d,k)=1` nor `(d,g)=1` is allowed as an extra restriction.

For every `sigma>1/2` and `v>1/3`,
\[
\sum_{0<q_h\le X}q_h^{-v}\|\mathbf D_h(s)\|^2
\le C_{\sigma,v,S}
\sum_{\substack{0<q_k\le X\\k\ {\rm cube-free}}}
q_k^{-v}\|\mathbf D_k(s)\|^2.
\tag{T03.3}
\]
The vector includes the full finite ray/unit/fixed-prime orbit. Its ray blocks in (T03.1) are diagonal unit-modulus factors followed by a permutation, hence have norm at most one.

**Proof.** Normalize input/output by `q^{-v/2}`. The positive majorizing kernel for (T03.2) is
\[
A_{h,k}=q_g^{-\sigma-v}q_d^{-3v/2}.
\]
Choose `u,w>0`, `u+w=v`, `w>1/3`, and Schur weight `p_n=q_n^{u-v/2}`. For `h=h0 r^3`,
\[
p_h^{-1}\sum_kA_{h,k}p_k
=q_r^{-3u}\prod_{p\mid U}(1+Q_p^{u-\sigma}).
\]
Each sufficiently large prime dividing `r` but not `h0` contributes at most `Q^{-3u}+Q^{-2u-sigma}<=1`; a larger multiplicity only decreases it. Finitely many smaller primes give a fixed constant. Primes shared with `h0` contribute at most one. For a fixed cube-free column,
\[
p_k^{-1}\sum_hA_{h,k}p_h
\le\sum_dq_d^{-3w}
\prod_{p\mid\operatorname{rad}_{=1}(k)}(1+Q_p^{-\sigma-2w})
\le\zeta_{\mathbb K}(3w)\prod_p(1+Q_p^{-\sigma-2w})<\infty.
\]
Here `3w>1` and `sigma+2w>1`. Schur's test proves the bound for the block operator. To obtain (T03.3) without assuming an infinite actual mean, truncate the input at `X`; all output rows through `X` are unchanged because `q_k<=q_h`. ∎

For arbitrary element rows, include unit and fixed-prime residue exponents modulo three in the finite vector, and sum remaining fixed-prime cube powers among `d`. They only decrease the positive ideal majorant or multiply it by convergent fixed Euler factors. Different components can use different fixed completions only after uncompleted extraction; a common scalar completion commutes directly with the identity.

The threshold `v>1/3` is sharp for this universal lifting operator. An input supported only at `k=1` produces value one at every `h=d^3`, of squared weighted mass `sum_d q_d^{-3v}`, divergent at `v<=1/3`. This is not a lower bound for the actual arithmetic series.

If the cube-free cumulative mean has exponent `rho>1/3`, choose `1/3<v<rho`. Partial summation bounds the right side of (T03.3) by `X^{rho-v}T^A`; multiplication by `X^v` proves the same unweighted all-row exponent. The reverse implication follows by restriction. Thus the decisive mean can be formulated on
\[
h=ab^2,\qquad q_aq_b^2\le X.
\]
Its primitive good conductor has norm `q_aq_b`, a different quantity. T03 says nothing about FD's infinite forced-divisor trace or the continued scalar period on [restricted research revision]'s source-shell Hilbert span.
title: T03. Cube-free physical-row lifting — PROVED, sharp operator threshold

The first two-variable test is exact. Full squarefree Euler factors give (1-z)(1-w), zero-free for |z|,|w|<1. Deleting only the product face gives 1-z-w, which vanishes at z=w=1/2. Thus a product-size cutoff does not preserve that polydisk nonvanishing property. For k singleton variables, 1-sum z_j vanishes at every z_j=1/k; its maximal uniform open-polydisk radius is1/k, by the triangle inequality and this witness. No Lee--Yang theorem or unverified positivity theorem is imported.

There is also a literal arithmetic-curve failure: sum_(n<=5)mu(n)n^-s=1-2^-s-3^-s-5^-s. At s=1 this is-1/30, at s=2 it is positive, and its real derivative is strictly positive. It has a unique real zero in(1,2). This is a finite cutoff polynomial, not 1/zeta, and not a contradiction to the known zero-free half-plane of zeta.

More decisively, for a real parameter N tending to infinity define the legitimate rough squarefree subsource

    H_N(s)=sum_(n<=N; P^-(n)>sqrt(N)) mu(n)n^-s
          =1-sum_(sqrt(N)<p<=N) p^-s,                    (C1)

where P^-(1)=infinity. The strict lower prime cut and inclusive upper cut are literal. Every composite has either a repeated prime (mu=0) or two prime factors whose product exceeds N, so the identity is exact, including a possible prime at the lower endpoint being excluded. On this source f3(n)=mu(n) for N sufficiently large, since the only nonunit terms are primes>sqrt(N)>3.

There is a unique positive real zero sigma_N for all sufficiently large N, and

    sigma_N=1-lambda_*/log N+o(1/log N),
    integral_(1/2)^1 exp(lambda_* v)dv/v=1,
    lambda_*>0.                                         (C2)

Proof: for lambda in any fixed compact real interval, partial summation and the prime number theorem give, uniformly in lambda,

    sum_(sqrt(N)<p<=N) p^(-1+lambda/log N)
        = integral_(1/2)^1 exp(lambda v)dv/v+o(1).       (C3)

For completeness use pi(t)=li(t)+E(t), E(t)=o(t/log t), uniformly for t>=sqrt(N). The endpoint errors after multiplication by t^-1+lambda/logN are o(1/log N). The Stieltjes error integral is bounded by sup_(t>=sqrtN)|E(t)|log(t)/t times a fixed multiple of integral_sqrtN^N dt/(t log t), hence o(1), uniformly on compact lambda ranges. The main integral changes variables t=N^v exactly. This derivation imports only PNT, verified against [NIST DLMF27.12](https://dlmf.nist.gov/27.12), equations27.12.4--5, on12October2026.

At lambda=0 the limit is log2<1; the limit increases continuously to infinity as lambda increases. Its derivative integral_(1/2)^1 exp(lambda v)dv is positive. Hence lambda_* exists uniquely and is positive. Uniform convergence traps the unique finite-N crossing between lambda_*-epsilon and lambda_*+epsilon. The sum is strictly decreasing in real s, is greater than1 at s=0 for large N, and is below1 at s=1 eventually, proving the stated unique positive root and C2. In particular, for EVERY fixed gamma<1, sigma_N>gamma for all sufficiently large N.

This is not an arbitrary coefficient toy: it retains actual mu and f3 signs on a precisely specified rough cutoff. It refutes a blanket claim that such cutoff cells inherit zero-freeness from the full finite Euler product, or that tropical one-term dominance can cover them without a complementary-wall payment. At the zero the constant term and the entire prime block have exactly equal positive magnitudes and opposite signs. The omitted composite/small-prime fields are indispensable to any global argument. It does not lower-bound the complete signed Gaussian field and does not show that a separately compensated source cannot have a stable polynomial representation.

Next meaningful repair: construct a mask-compatible partition polynomial that includes the exact missing faces and prove a complete quantitative return; do not apply a stability theorem to C1. This counterexample is a useful failed high-ceiling proposal, not a c improvement. Its zero approaches1 logarithmically, while the target width is fixed.

statement:
## T10. Two-dilation and continuum-dilation Möbius criteria

Fix \(0<\alpha<1\) and \(\Delta_bM(x)=M(bx)-b^\alpha M(x)\), where \(M(x)=\sum_{n\le x}\mu(n)\).

### Two discrete dilations

If for every \(\epsilon>0\) and all sufficiently large integers \(N\),
\[
\sum_{b\in\{2,3\}}\sum_{N\le n<2N}|\Delta_bM(n)|^2
\ll N^{2a+1+\epsilon},\qquad 0<a<1, \tag{T10.1}
\]
then \(\zeta\) is zero-free in \(\Re s>a\).

On a unit interval, \(|M(bx)-M(b\lfloor x\rfloor)|\le b\), while \(M(x)=M(\lfloor x\rfloor)\). Thus (T10.1) gives the continuous dyadic \(L^2(dx/x)\) estimate with an affordable \(O(1)\) error on a shell. The shell argument of T09 yields holomorphy of
\[
\int_0^\infty\Delta_bM(x)x^{-s}\frac{dx}{x}
=\frac{b^s-b^\alpha}{s\zeta(s)}. \tag{T10.2}
\]
Both multipliers can vanish only at
\[
s=\alpha+\frac{2\pi i m}{\log2}
 =\alpha+\frac{2\pi i n}{\log3}.
\]
The irrationality of \(\log2/\log3\) forces \(m=n=0\). The remaining real point \(\alpha\) is not a zeta zero: the alternating eta series is positive on \(0<s<1\), and \(1-2^{1-s}<0\). Thus at least one multiplier retains every prospective nontrivial zero. Their inverses need not be uniformly bounded in height.

The exact consistency identity is
\[
\Delta_2M(3x)-3^\alpha\Delta_2M(x)
=\Delta_3M(2x)-2^\alpha\Delta_3M(x).
\]
It gives no contraction or decay without a new arithmetic estimate.

### New continuum-dilation variant

Replace (T10.1) by
\[
\int_X^{2X}\int_2^3|\Delta_bM(x)|^2\,db\,\frac{dx}{x}
\ll X^{2a+\epsilon}. \tag{T10.3}
\]
The same conclusion follows by taking the Mellin integral in \(L^2([2,3],db)\). Its multiplier vector is \(m_s(b)=b^s-b^\alpha\). It vanishes as a vector only for \(s=\alpha\): a nonconstant exponential in \(\log b\) cannot be identically one on an interval.

This compact continuum also provides a useful quantitative calibration absent from the discrete two-multiplier claim. Put
\[
G_\alpha(s)=\int_2^3|b^s-b^\alpha|^2\,db.
\]
For \(\sigma\) in any fixed compact real interval,
\[
G_\alpha(\sigma+it)\gg1\qquad(|t|\ge1), \tag{T10.4}
\]
with a constant depending on that interval and \(\alpha\). Expanding the square, the cross term is
\[
2\Re\int_2^3 b^{\sigma+\alpha+it}\,db=O((1+|t|)^{-1}),
\]
uniformly in the compact \(\sigma\)-interval; the two diagonal integrals have a positive lower bound. This proves the assertion for large \(t\). Continuity and the absence of zeros prove it on the remaining compact set \(1\le|t|\le T_0\). Near \(s=\alpha\),
\[
G_\alpha(s)=|s-\alpha|^2
\int_2^3 b^{2\alpha}(\log b)^2\,db
 +O(|s-\alpha|^3).
\]
Thus the sole calibration zero is known and simple at the multiplier level; zeta is nonzero there. The proposed continuum energy is nevertheless an open Möbius estimate.

The same hypothesis has a quantitative consequence: on every compact strip \(a<\sigma_0\le\Re s\le\sigma_1\), with \(|\Im s|\ge1\),
\[
 |1/\zeta(s)|\ll_{\sigma_0,\sigma_1,\alpha}1+|\Im s|. \tag{T10.5}
\]
Indeed the shell bounds give an absolutely convergent Bochner Mellin integral \(F(s)\) whose norm is uniformly bounded on that strip; its defining norm integral has no imaginary-height growth. The exact identity is \(\|F(s)\|=\sqrt{G_\alpha(s)}/|s\zeta(s)|\). Combine it with (T10.4). This is conditional on the same open continuum energy, not on any additional arithmetic hypothesis.

On logarithmic scale, \(f(t)=e^{-\alpha t}M(e^t)\) converts \(\Delta_bM(e^t)\) to \(b^\alpha e^{\alpha t}[f(t+\log b)-f(t)]\). An averaged finite-difference/Poincaré approach is therefore an explicit next construction. It must estimate these actual increments, not invoke a generic inequality to create a Möbius power saving.

**Sources:** BA D11 for the discrete construction; continuum construction developed and independently proved during the merge.
title: T10. Two-dilation and continuum-dilation Möbius criteria

## 4. Keep the conductor restriction during regularization

Fix a good radical \(\mathfrak r\). Split every label into its \(\mathfrak r\)-part and coprime part, and apply FR13 to the latter at
\[
U=Y_D/q_{a_R},\qquad V=Y_E/q_{b_R}.
\]
At conductor primes, first retain the exact forced valuation and original character zeros, then discard their additional weight \(q_{k_R}^{-1/2}\le1\). This is a positive bound after the row calculation, not a relaxation in the defining field.

Insert \(q^{-\eta(\alpha+\beta)}\), with fixed small \(\eta>0\), in the outer exponent sums. Its compensating global factor is absorbed in \(Z^\epsilon\) because the original outer annuli are polynomially bounded. For the HC4 Gauss size put
\[
P_p=\sum_{\substack{j\ge0\\6\mid j}}q^{-\eta j}
=\frac1{1-q^{-6\eta}},\qquad
N_p=\sum_{\substack{j>0\\6\nmid j}}q^{-1/2-\eta j}
\ll_\eta q^{-1/2},
\]
and let
\[
D_p=\frac{(1+q^{-1/2})^2}{(1-q^{-1})^2}
=1+O(q^{-1/2}).
\]
These are respectively the principal and nonprincipal outer weights
\(B_p(j)q^{-j/2-\eta j}\), and the full completed-column exponent mass.

The exact conductor condition \(\ell_p\ne0\) implies either a nonprincipal outer exponent or a nonzero completed-column exponent vector. Hence the allowed local mass is at most
\[
\bigl((P_p+N_p)^2-P_p^2\bigr)D_p
+P_p^2(D_p-1)
\ll_\eta q^{-1/2}. \tag{FR14}
\]
Enlarging to every nonzero exponent vector would be invalid at this step: principal-only outer vectors would lose this saving. They are excluded by \(\ell_p\ne0\).

The product of local constants has subpower size. Consequently
\[
\boxed{
\mathscr M_{\mathfrak r}^{(1/2)}
\ll_\epsilon Z^\epsilon\sqrt{Y_DY_E}\,R^{-1/2+\epsilon}.
} \tag{FR15}
\]
This proof also works with every fixed \(1/6<\rho\le1\).

## 5. W40-25: phase has metric content, with a cycle-length cost

For a closed chain of unit vectors, let C be the cyclic product of
nonzero overlaps, r_j their magnitudes and theta=arg C. Successive
phase choices make adjacent overlaps real positive and leave the last
vector e^(-i theta) times the first. Thus

    4sin^2(theta/2)<=m sum||u_j-u_(j-1)||^2
                         =2m sum(1-r_j).

Together with log r_j<=-(1-r_j), this proves
|C|<=exp[-2sin^2(theta/2)/m]. An overlap zero gives C=0 separately.
No spectral-gap premise is used.

For a fixed triangle the Gram determinant is
1-a^2-b^2-c^2+2abc cos theta>=0. The identity
1-a^2-b^2-c^2+2abc=(1-b^2)(1-c^2)-(a-bc)^2 implies the author's
(1-cos theta)<=(1-q^2)^2/(2q^3) when all three magnitudes are>=q>0.
Consequently a fixed nonzero triangle phase forces loss; the seed's
unqualified near-one objection needed this distinction.

The growing-cycle example is exact: v_j=(1,e^(2pi i j/N))/sqrt2 has
every adjacent overlap e^(pi i/N)cos(pi/N). Cyclic trace is
-cos(pi/N)^N, with phase pi and magnitude1-pi^2/(2N)+O(N^-2).
The ordered unclosed product norm has exponent N-1, not N. Closing
it with the initial projector restores norm|C|. These identities
justify the logarithmic number of bounded-length, nonflat closed
factors required by the proposed X^-delta product bound.

The factorized path premise is essential. Neither additive edge sums
nor a chain of unclosed operators automatically has that product norm.
Native H contains the actual roots, CRT and angular factors, complete
signed short core, both projectors, natural zeros, independent heights,
sharp original supports and exceptional/far components. None is mapped
to these laboratory projectors. The result gives a quantitative new
length-dependent obstruction within U-FLUX/W07 seed15 ancestry; it
proves no native-H saving or universal failure of a changed embedding.

## HC4. A positive bounded projector and complete median removal

Use the least unramified p for the simplest finite source. Define

    h=1/(4p^2), omega_p=2 log p,
    K_h(theta)=3h/(8*pi)[sin(h theta/4)/(h theta/4)]^4,           (HC4.1)

with its continuous value at zero. K_h is nonnegative, has mass 1, and its Fourier transform is supported on [-h,h]. For normalization, the sum of four uniforms on [-1,1] has density at zero

    [4^3-4*2^3]/(2^4*3!)=1/3.

Its characteristic function is sinc(t)^4, so the integral of sinc(t)^4 is 2*pi/3. Scaling t=h theta/4 gives HC4.1. Fourier support follows from the convolution support [-4,4]. This is also the elementary cubic B-spline Fourier calculation.

For any other integer r, |log(r/p^2)|>h: already log(1+1/p^2)>1/(p^2+1)>h, and the lower neighbor has larger logarithmic distance. Therefore

    P_p U(x)=integral_R K_h(theta)exp(i omega_p theta)U(theta,x)dtheta

is bounded by Cauchy--Schwarz and satisfies exactly

    P_p H(x)=p^(-2delta)B_(p^2)(x),                            (HC4.2)
    M(x)=a(p)^(-1)p^(2delta)P_p H(px)
                          +g(log(1/x))+a(p)g(log(p/x)).        (HC4.3)

The inverse is a fixed scalar, with |a(p)|=1. No cofactor exception, good-real-shift selection, atom repair, conductor-uniform lower bound or large-shift Neumann inverse is needed. The Dirichlet-side return follows from HC3.3 on Re s>1. No unrelated operator readout is substituted.

At every fixed x there is the exact weighted Pythagorean identity

    integral_R K_h|H|^2 dtheta
      =p^(-4delta)|B_(p^2)(x)|^2
       +integral_R K_h|H-p^(-2delta)B_(p^2)(x)exp(-i omega_p theta)|^2 dtheta.
                                                                    (HC4.4)

The cross term is zero by HC4.2. A proposed theta-energy bound must therefore control the complete signed square of HC3.2. It retains every ordered c,d pair with a(c)conjugate(a(d)). All those pairs are theta-diagonal because c,d have zero theta exponent. Frequency diagonalization is not output diagonalization.

At fixed x the Bohr mean also equals sum_r r^(-2delta)|B_r(x)|^2, by absolute convergence and averaging. This is not asserted as an estimate for a finite uniform theta window; its other frequency gaps can be small. The positive projector gives finite-window control without such an assertion.

Every contributing p^2-frequency tuple has median <=p. Thus

    P_p(H-H_(b<=p))=0.                                        (HC4.5)

For least unramified p, the only live tuples with b<=p have a=1,b=p,c>p. Put

    J_(delta,theta)(x)=a(p)sum_(c>p) a(c)
                      V_(delta+i theta)(1,p,c)^2g(log(pc/x)).  (HC4.6)

Then P_p J=P_p H. The ENTIRE b>p complement vanishes under the full-line readout, including its unbounded c range and common-divisor cases. This removes the moving median cutoff prerequisite for this recovery formula. It does not claim a hereditary norm bound for J from a full signed norm bound for H.

### 2.4 A primary-source universality test rejects the bare arithmetic target

The further strongest-objection test is decisive, not merely a weak available upper bound. For the bare zeta choice P(s)=(s-1)zeta(s),

    sup_(t real) B(h_t)=infinity.                   (W40.21)

External input: Johan Andersson, *Lavrent'ev's approximation theorem with nonvanishing polynomials and universality of zeta-functions*, arXiv:1010.0386, Theorem2, PDF page2. The theorem states uniform vertical approximation to any continuous target on a compact subset of1/2<Re s<1 having empty interior and connected complement, on a positive-lower-density set of positive shifts. The primary [paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1010.0386) was opened and its exact theorem inspected. Only that theorem is imported; it is not reproved here. Voronin's1975 original disk result was identified, but its full PDF fetch failed, so the argument binds to the accessible primary theorem above.

Here is the new application, including the anchor and principal-pole factors. Let R=7/5, delta=1/40, and

    K={2+R exp(i theta): |theta-pi|<=delta}.

This compact simple arc has empty interior and connected complement. Its real parts lie between.6 and.6+R delta^2/2<1, so it is strictly inside the universality strip. For any fixed M>=32, apply the cited theorem to the constant target-M with uniform error1. It gives arbitrarily large t with

    zeta(s+it)=-M+e(s), |e(s)|<1 for every s in K.

On the anchor line2 the absolutely convergent reciprocal series gives

    w_t=1/zeta(2+it),
    |w_t-1|<=sum_(n>=2)n^-2<3/4,
    Re w_t>1/4, |w_t|<7/4.

The elementary bound uses1/4+integral_2^infinity v^-2 dv=3/4; no unknown vertical phase is ignored. For s in K put k_t(s)=(s+it-1)/(1+it). If t>=40,

    |k_t-1|<=R/40=7/200,
    |w_t||k_t-1|<49/800<1/16,
    |w_t||k_t|<2.

Therefore the actual normalized P satisfies throughout the whole arc

    Re[k_t(s)w_t(-M+e(s))]
       <-M/4+M/16+2 <=-M/8.

Its negative boundary mass is consequently at least

    B(h_t)>= (2delta)/(2pi) * M/8 = M/(320pi).      (W40.22)

Since M is arbitrary, W40.21 follows. For any chosen finite budget, such bad heights even have positive lower density after discarding a bounded interval. The theorem does not produce a zero: zero-free analytic functions can have large real-part oscillation. It proves the proposed sufficient positivity condition is too strong for this bare normalization, independently of an off-line-zero assumption.

This is a distinct obstruction from W24's logarithmic-derivative phase witness. It uses actual zeta universality on a contour arc and explicitly pays division by zeta(2+it) and the(s-1) normalization. No result for a finite Euler multiplier, especially a height-adaptive one, is inferred: such a multiplier can rotate/change the arc and needs its own argument. The valid future question is whether a specified changed normalization both defeats this obstruction and has a small all-height negative-part estimate. An unspecified multiplier or finite successful samples do not supply that escape.

Functional signature: actual holomorphic pole-removed L; signed real-boundary decomposition; Poisson extremal weights; bare all-height hypothesis REFUTED by W40.21; changed-normalization estimate open; exact zero return W40-B retained. This is quantitative relative to F21/F22/F23 and SC25, not a literature-priority claim.

# Independent review: fixed-prime cancellation with a shrinking detector

**Canonical [private research revision] status:** Independent DPR1–17 review of the [fixed-prime narrow detector](dilation-pole-killing.md), accepted without repair. Every reciprocal frequency, factor range and ordered cross term remains in the unpaid energy. The final review bytes and explicit writing stop preceded a transport error; that later error does not replace the saved review evidence.

Frozen source: `[restricted provenance path] mathematical source]`, SHA256 `fa9e0a229e3a2e4fe10d6029efe480074aba0b89a8dde9735bb46e625808aba0`. The original bytes remain unchanged. Historical author workflow statements below describe the source packet at submission; this canonical status and the linked independent review govern its mathematical scope.



Frozen source:
