17,189 bytes, SHA256
BB75F77EE89C1E5BEA74AA5C3A570DA176B99D85D3616E1AAB1E76421E189B76.
The digest and length matched before review. DP labels below refer
only to those bytes. This review makes no c-improvement claim.

## Scope and quantifiers

The construction and the arithmetic hypothesis have separate
statuses. The claims to check are the explicit kernel, exact norm
transfer, fixed coefficient change, folded diagonal, negligible
Type I term and equivalent reciprocal-phase expression. OPEN-DP
is an unproved estimate on a complete signed energy.

The bridge fixes 0<a<b0 and eta>0 before X varies. OPEN-DP must
hold for every final epsilon>0 on every sufficiently large dyadic
X, with delta_X frozen on the entire enlarged shell. The
two-factor completion additionally fixes kappa0>0 with
eta+kappa0<1. Every requested error power R and truncation buffer
tau>0 is fixed before selecting a sufficiently large derivative
order B; B is then fixed before X or a factor/frequency varies.
Constants may depend on these fixed parameters and on k, but not
on X, x, the completion factors or the dual frequencies.

The sequence kappa=e_1-2e_2 and the positive number kappa0 have
different roles. Neither is varied to absorb an unpriced error.

## 1. Kernel and transfer: independent derivation

Let a_j=2^(-j), U_j uniform on [-a_j,a_j], and S=sum_j U_j.
Absolute convergence holds for every outcome because
sum_j |U_j|<=1. The characteristic functions converge on compact
t intervals to the characteristic function of S, by dominated
convergence. Each factor is sinc(a_j t). For any fixed integer
L, its first L factors satisfy

\[
 \left|\prod_{j=1}^L\frac{\sin(a_jt)}{a_jt}\right|
 \le C_L(1+|t|)^{-L};
 \qquad
 \left|\prod_{j>L}\frac{\sin(a_jt)}{a_jt}\right|\le1.
 \tag{DPR1}
\]

For |t|>=1 one may take a constant at least
prod_(j<=L) a_j^(-1); for bounded t enlarge that constant.
To obtain the m-th derivative of the density, choose L>m+1.
Fourier inversion then gives a continuous m-th derivative. This
proves k is C-infinity for every finite m, without a derivative
order that grows with J. The density represents a probability
law, is nonnegative and even, has mass one, and vanishes outside
[-1,1]. Smoothness on the whole real line includes flat boundary
jets at both support endpoints.

The bounded random variable S has entire Laplace transform
M(s)=E exp(sS). Independence first on finite partial sums and
dominated convergence give DP3. On any compact s set, the sum
of absolute deviations of the factors from one converges,
because it is bounded by a constant times sum_j 4^(-j).
Every individual factor is nonzero off the imaginary axis.
At such a fixed s, a summable-deviation product of nonzero
factors has a nonzero limit: the logarithms of its sufficiently
late factors converge absolutely. Thus M(s) is nonzero for
Re s>0. This is a qualitative nonvanishing statement; no
uniform lower bound on high vertical lines is asserted.

The tail after J has exactly the law 2^(-J)S, independently
of its first J uniforms. Hence k=h_J*k_delta at
delta=2^(-J), with h_J a probability density supported in
[-1+delta,1-delta]. Substituting v=log(n/x) gives DP5 with
the correct sign xe^t. All n appearing for a fixed x and all
t in that compact support lie in one finite set, so exchanging
the sum and the t integral needs no infinite arithmetic
convergence assumption.

The full weighted Jensen calculation is

\[
 \begin{split}
 \int_X^{2X}|F_{B,1}(x)|^2\frac{dx}{x}
 &\le\int h_J(t)
       \int_{Xe^t}^{2Xe^t}|F_{B,\delta}(y)|^2\frac{dy}{y}\,dt\\
 &=\int |F_{B,\delta}(y)|^2 w_X(y)\frac{dy}{y},\\
 w_X(y)&=\int h_J(t)1_{\{Xe^t\le y\le2Xe^t\}}dt.
 \end{split}
 \tag{DPR2}
\]

Here 0<=w_X<=1 and its support is inside [e^(-1)X,2eX].
This proves DP6 with constant one for every J. The variable
delta on this entire right side is the one selected using X,
not a width reselected using y. The floor in DP7 gives the
claimed inequalities exactly. No comparison of two different
moving widths has been used.

For OPEN-DP and any compact set Re s>=a+g, g>0, take
epsilon<2g. The contribution of [2^j,2^(j+1)] to the
absolute Mellin integral of F_(A,1) is at most
C_epsilon 2^(j(a+epsilon/2-Re s)). These bounds are summable;
extra fixed powers of log x remain summable on a smaller
positive gap. Since the function vanishes below e^(-1),
this proves locally uniform holomorphy in Re s>a.

In Re s>1, the substitution u=n/x gives the identity

\[
 \int_0^\infty V_1(n/x)x^{-s}\frac{dx}{x}
       =n^{-s}M(s).
 \tag{DPR3}
\]

The interchange with A(n) is absolutely convergent there
because |A(n)|<=3. Consequently DP12 is correctly normalized.
On a<Re s<1, the factor 1-2^(1-s) cannot vanish, since its
second term has modulus greater than one; M does not vanish
there either. The meromorphic identity
zeta(s) mathscr F(s)=M(s)(1-2^(1-s)) continues from Re s>1
to Re s>a. A zero of zeta inside that open strip would make
its left side zero and its right side nonzero. The accepted
baseline handles Re s>=1, including the distinction between
the pole at one and a zero. This proves the stated conditional
bridge, without a moving Mellin transform or a lower bound
for |M(s)| at large height.

## 2. Exact coefficient folding and all 2-adic resonances

For odd m, the only nonzero local values are
A(m)=mu(m), A(2m)=-3mu(m), A(4m)=2mu(m). All higher
2-adic valuations give zero, as do odd square factors.
This proves DP8 directly from DP1. Its Dirichlet series
multiplier is 1-2*2^(-s), giving DP9. Replacing N by 2n
in the second part of DP1 proves DP10 before any estimate.

The profile has logarithmic mass one:
integral V_delta(u)du/u=1. Its ordinary mass is M(delta).
Thus the ordinary integral of
V_delta(u)-2V_delta(2u) is exactly zero. There is no
additional inverse-width normalization of the vanishing
moment; the original bump still has amplitude delta^(-1).
The two lobes have the fixed logarithmic separation log 2.

Both entries of a nonzero Gram satisfy N/x,M/x in
[e^(-delta),e^delta]. This proves all support statements
DP14, with the stated absolute product-gap constant for
bounded delta. Expansion of the finite sum proves DP15
and DP16, including their cross coefficients -2,-2,4.

The exact identity at one completed index is

\[
 A(N)^2=\mu(N)^2+
       4\,1_{2\mid N}\mu(N/2)^2
       -4\,1_{2\mid N}\mu(N)\mu(N/2).
 \tag{DPR4}
\]

This explicitly accounts for the resonances N=n=2m and
N=2n=m in the original two-lobe representation. For even
m, mu(2m)mu(m)=0; for odd m it equals -mu(m)^2.
The usual squarefree density is 1/zeta(2), and the odd
squarefree density is 2/(3zeta(2)), each with error
O(sqrt z) by its elementary square-divisor expansion.
The three terms of DPR4 therefore contribute respectively

\[
 \frac{z}{\zeta(2)},\qquad
 \frac{2z}{\zeta(2)},\qquad
 \frac{4z}{3\zeta(2)}
 \quad\text{up to }O(\sqrt z).
 \tag{DPR5}
\]

Their sum is 13z/(3zeta(2)), independently confirming DP18.
Equivalently the local weights 1,9,4 at valuations 0,1,2
give (2/(3zeta(2)))(1+9/2+4/4).
Omitting the exact-ratio cross terms would give the wrong
constant 3/zeta(2). There are no unlisted higher 2-adic
resonances after the exact folding in DPR4.

Put S_A(z)=sum_(N<=z) A(N)^2 and C_A=13/(3zeta(2)).
Tonelli and u=N/x give the diagonal as

\[
 \int_0^\infty V_\delta(u)^2
       \{S_A(2Xu)-S_A(Xu)\}\frac{du}{u}
 =C_A X\int V_\delta(u)^2du
    +O\left(\sqrt X\int V_\delta(u)^2\frac{du}{u}\right).
 \tag{DPR6}
\]

Any endpoint atoms affect a measure-zero set of u. The omitted
factor sqrt(u) in the error is bounded on the fixed compact
support e^(-delta0)<=u<=e^delta0. Finally
integral V_delta^2 du=delta^(-1)integral k(v)^2 e^(delta v)dv
and integral V_delta^2 du/u=delta^(-1)||k||_2^2.
This proves DP19 uniformly even when delta X is small;
partial summation through derivatives of the narrow profile
is unnecessary. The error/main ratio is O(X^(-1/2)),
independent of delta. The diagonal remains a part of a
signed expansion, not a lower bound for its whole energy.

For a=.87449 its power is 1+eta and the strict diagonal
budget is eta<2a-1=.74898. The comparison with a separately
paid normalized first-derivative bump, whose diagonal power
is 1+3eta, is exactly the claimed factor-three interval
of allowed eta. This comparison provides no off-diagonal
cancellation estimate.

## 3. Completion and the absence of a Type I main term

Write u=mu_(<=Y), v=mu_(>Y). Expanding v*v*1 and using
mu*1=e_1 gives v*v*1=mu-2u+u*u*1 exactly at every integer.
Convolving with kappa yields

\[
 A=2\kappa*u-u*u*b+v*v*b,\qquad
 b(\ell)=1-2\,1_{2\mid\ell}=(-1)^{\ell+1}.
 \tag{DPR7}
\]

Every convolution is a finite divisor identity. It contains
ordered d,e, all repeated/shared primes, their original
Mobius zeros, and every restoration label ell. In particular
no coprimality between d and e has been introduced.

For 0<delta<=delta0, the compact support of V_delta lies
uniformly away from zero. Its zero extension is smooth.
The chain rule gives
||V_delta^(j)||_1 <= C_j delta^(-j):
the maximal derivative size is O(delta^(-j-1)), and the
support length is O(delta). The j=0 bound is O(1).
Integrating by parts j times therefore proves DP23 with
constants independent of delta.

With the source Fourier convention, alternating Poisson is

\[
 \sum_{\ell\ge1}(-1)^{\ell+1}V_\delta(\ell t)
 =-\frac1t\sum_{\nu\in\mathbb Z,\ \nu\ {\rm odd}}
                  \widehat V_\delta\left(\frac{\nu}{2t}\right).
 \tag{DPR8}
\]

It follows by first extending the physical sum to every
integer, where the added terms are zero, and modulating
the integer lattice by exp(pi i ell). Its dual lattice
is the half-integer lattice. The leading minus sign
comes from (-1)^(ell+1), not from the Fourier convention.
There is no zero frequency. The dual series converges
absolutely for each positive t.

For 0<t<=delta, DP23 with B>=2 bounds the right side by

\[
 C_Bt^{-1}(t/\delta)^B
       \sum_{\nu\ {\rm odd}}|\nu|^{-B}
 \ll_B t^{-1}(t/\delta)^B.
 \tag{DPR9}
\]

The term 2kappa*u has support <=2Y=o(X), outside every
narrow profile on the entire enlarged shell for large X.
For d,e<=Y, t=de/x and delta=delta_X satisfy
t/delta<=e X^(-kappa0). Also t^(-1)=x/(de)<=2eX/(de).
Summing the absolute bound in DPR9 hence costs only

\[
 C_B X(CX^{-\kappa_0})^B
       \left(\sum_{d\le Y}\frac1d\right)^2.
 \tag{DPR10}
\]

There is no missing factor Y^2: the inverse t factor
leaves the two harmonic denominators. Selecting
B>(R+2)/kappa0, for example, makes the error O_R(X^(-R)).
This proves DP25--26 uniformly in the enlarged shell at
its frozen width. All derivative orders and constants
are fixed before the arithmetic labels vary.

The surviving support ell*d*e<=e^delta x, d,e>Y, implies
d,e<=C X/(Y+1) and ell<=C X/(Y+1)^2. Since Y tends to
infinity, its floor changes only fixed constants, proving
DP27. Long individual factors and a polynomial restoration
range remain; their cancellation is not supplied by the
vanishing Type I term.

## 4. Finite product cap and the entire odd-frequency tail

For delta<=1/8 and x in [e^(-1)X,2eX], any nonzero
physical summand has

\[
 \ell de\le e^\delta x\le2e^{9/8}X<8X.
 \tag{DPR11}
\]

Since ell>=1, this proves the fixed cap de<=8X, independently
of x before averaging. Both d and e are still greater than Y.
Extra pairs under that cap can be identically zero on part of
the shell; they must nevertheless keep their complete Poisson
series until a truncation error is paid.

Apply DPR8 separately to every pair under this finite cap,
with t=de/x. The outside factor is -x/(de), and the
argument of the Fourier transform is nu*x/(2de).
This proves DP28, including its sign, factor two in the
frequency denominator, both ordered factor positions and
every positive and negative odd frequency. No assertion
t<=delta is needed for this exact Poisson identity; that
inequality was needed only for the earlier Type I estimate.

For the full truncation, set
s_*=de/(X delta), beta_x=x/X and
L=X^tau max(1,s_*). Here e^(-1)<=beta_x<=2e.
The absolute omitted contribution for one pair is at most

\[
 \frac{C_B}{\delta s_*}
 \sum_{|\nu|>L}
       (1+c|\nu|/s_*)^{-B},
 \tag{DPR12}
\]

where the positive c is fixed over the whole shell. Extending
from odd frequencies to all integers only enlarges this
positive estimate. For sufficiently large X, L>=s_* and
L>=1. The integral test gives
sum_(|nu|>L) |nu|^(-B) <= C_B L^(1-B), with literal real
cutoffs handled by a fixed constant. Therefore DPR12 is at most

\[
 \begin{cases}
 C_B\delta^{-1}X^{-\tau(B-1)},&s_*\ge1,\\
 C_B\delta^{-1}s_*^{B-1}X^{-\tau(B-1)},&0<s_*<1.
 \end{cases}
 \tag{DPR13}
\]

The second extra factor is at most one. This calculation shows
where the apparent factor de disappears; it is not hidden in
a uniform Fourier estimate. There are at most
sum_(d<=8X) floor(8X/d)=O(X log(2X)) ordered pairs under
the cap, even before d,e>Y and the Mobius zeros are imposed.
Also delta_X^(-1)<=X^eta. Summing DPR13 gives

\[
 C_B X^{1+\eta-\tau(B-1)}\log(2X).
 \tag{DPR14}
\]

For a requested R, choose a fixed B with
tau(B-1)>R+2+eta. This is O_R(X^(-R)) after all pairs
and all omitted frequencies are summed. Constants may
depend on the fixed tau. The cutoff itself satisfies
L<=8X^tau/delta_X up to a fixed constant, since de<=8X,
and thus has the stated range O(X^(eta+tau)).
The use of X instead of the integration variable x in
the cutoff is harmless because beta_x stays in a fixed
positive compact interval.

Finally u=e^(delta v), du=delta e^(delta v)dv, gives

\[
 \widehat V_\delta(\xi)
   =\int_{-1}^1 k(v)e^{\delta v}
                  e^{-2\pi i\xi e^{\delta v}}\,dv.
 \tag{DPR15}
\]

The original delta^(-1) amplitude cancels precisely this
Jacobian delta. DP30 therefore has neither a missing width
factor nor a wrong phase. Since the profile is real,
the negative-frequency terms are the conjugates of the
positive-frequency terms. This does not remove their
arithmetic cancellation obligation.

The absence of a zero frequency in one alternating
restoration sum does not exclude opposite-frequency
resonances after two such sums are multiplied in the
energy. All those products remain in DPR16--OPEN;
no mean-zero-to-small-energy inference is made.

DP28 with the cutoff DP29 is consequently equivalent,
up to an arbitrarily small uniform power error, to the
same F_(A,delta_X) in OPEN-DP. The omitted Type I and
frequency errors are uniform before integration.
They also remain negligible in the energy: the norm
triangle inequality suffices, and the errors can be made
smaller than any requested power. No pointwise bound on
an unestimated reciprocal sum is needed to justify that
norm comparison.

## 5. Unpaid arithmetic, objections and novelty relative to the record

The surviving explicit energy is

\[
 \int_{e^{-1}X}^{2eX}
 \left|
   \sum_{\substack{d,e>Y\\de\le8X}}\mu(d)\mu(e)
       \sum_{\ell\ge1}(-1)^{\ell+1}
                   V_{\delta_X}(\ell de/x)
 \right|^2\frac{dx}{x}
 \ll_\epsilon X^{2a+\epsilon}.
 \tag{DPR16--OPEN}
\]

It is exactly OPEN-DP in its completed form, with the
arbitrarily small DP26 error removed in norm. Every
ordered cross term of the displayed square is still
present. The finite product cap is inserted before
Poisson; an equally valid remaining object is DP28
with all odd frequencies through its paid DP29 cutoff.
Neither object is bounded in this review.

The stated examples have the following actual ranges:
with eta=.20, kappa0=.02, the factor cap is X^.61,
restoration length X^.22 and folded diagonal X^1.20;
with eta=.70 and the same kappa0, the caps become
X^.86, X^.72 and X^1.70. Both parameter choices satisfy
eta+kappa0<1 and the diagonal inequality eta<.74898
at a=.87449. These arithmetic ranges, including the
very long individual factors, are genuine costs.

For comparison with the derivative construction, take
the ordinary zero-mass profile
psi_delta=(1+u d/du)V_delta. Direct calculation gives

\[
 \int_0^\infty \psi_\delta(u)^2du
   =\delta^{-3}\int_{-1}^1
        (k'(v)+\delta k(v))^2e^{\delta v}dv
   \asymp\delta^{-3}
 \quad(\delta\longrightarrow0).
 \tag{DPR17}
\]

Here ||k'||_2>0 because a nonzero smooth compactly
supported probability density cannot be constant.
This independently verifies the normalization cost
used in DP's comparison; it is not an appeal to an
unreviewed construction. By contrast, the fixed
coefficient factor has the paid diagonal DPR6.

The quoted existing Mertens bound gives
sum_(n<=z) A(n)=M(z)-2M(z/2)=O(z^b).
Partial summation through V_delta costs its total
variation O(delta^(-1)), giving O(X^b/delta) on
the shell. This computation is correct and provides
no new exponent sufficient for DPR16--OPEN.
It is not a claim that this elementary bound is the
best possible one under every extra structural use
of the baseline.

The strongest objections I attempted were:

- **The probability transfer might hide an inverse width.**
  DPR2 exhibits the exact weight 0<=w_X<=1. It uses the
  same delta_X throughout the expanded shell. A theorem
  only for the varying width delta_y would not suffice
  without a further comparison, but it is not the
  hypothesis asserted in OPEN-DP.
- **The master multiplier could lose zeros at high heights.**
  DPR1--3 establish that M has no zero in Re s>0.
  Its possible small size there does not affect the
  qualitative holomorphic contradiction. No bounded
  inverse multiplier or quantitative high-height
  reciprocal-zeta estimate is claimed.
- **Folding could erase exact 2-adic resonances.**
  DPR4--5 retain the cross-density 4/(3zeta(2)), in
  addition to the direct density 3/zeta(2). The
  resulting 13/(3zeta(2)) is the correct constant.
  The natural zeros at valuation at least three
  and at odd square factors remain.
- **The Type I sum could recover a main term or a Y^2 cost.**
  DPR8 has only half-integer dual frequencies, and
  DPR10 retains both harmonic denominators. Fixed
  high derivative order prices the whole Type I
  sum uniformly. It does not give a bound for the
  surviving Type II energy.
- **The reciprocal expression could discard large
  factors or frequency tails.** DPR11 freezes a cap
  that contains every original physical term on
  the whole shell. DPR12--14 sum every omitted
  frequency and every ordered pair, including
  physically zero pairs added by the fixed cap.
  There is no unpriced cutoff dependence on x.
- **A positive kernel could turn its diagonal into
  a whole-energy lower bound.** A(N)A(M) has both
  signs. The diagonal calculation is a component
  cost; no lower bound on OPEN-DP's whole energy
  is used or accepted.

None produces a mathematical repair to DP1--30.
The surviving objection is substantive but already
acknowledged by the source: the new signed arithmetic
estimate is still hard and entirely unproved. Removing
a derivative normalization and the Type I zero-frequency
term does not control the complete long-factor energy.

### Comparison with T10 and N28

I read T10 in the [private research revision] consolidated proof and the
N28.C entry in the merged portfolio. T10 already
constructs discrete and continuous dilation criteria
for the actual Mertens function, identifies their
Mellin multipliers and proves the conditional
zero-exclusion bridge. N28.C develops their logarithmic
increment/overlap interpretation and explicitly keeps
the arithmetic cross-scale energy open.

DP's equality
F_(A,delta)(x)=F_(mu,delta)(x)-2F_(mu,delta)(x/2)
is the same broad dilation mechanism. The generic
shell-to-holomorphy proof is likewise old in that
record. In DP the extra local multiplier's zeros
lie on Re s=1, already outside the new target strip;
one fixed prime factor therefore suffices for the
qualitative bridge. This does not upgrade the
old open dilation energy to a theorem.

The specific checked combination is narrower:
an infinitely refinable compact probability kernel,
an exact frozen-width norm transfer, the fixed
arithmetic pole-killing factor, its fully folded
diagonal and the uniform alternating completion
with its capped reciprocal-frequency return.
Those particular identities and normalizations
are not furnished by the T10/N28 statements read.
The source correctly calls this a developed child
of that route, not a new portfolio family or a
literature-priority claim. The present acceptance
does not establish a broader novelty search.

## 6. Exact checks, bindings and verdict

An in-memory exact-integer Python check, with no
new script or data file, completed at exit code 0:

- All 4,096 indices 1<=n<=4096 satisfied the
  independent local formula DP8 and the resonance
  identity DPR4.
- For Y in {1,2,7,31,64}, direct finite Dirichlet
  convolution verified A=2kappa*u-u*u*b+v*v*b
  at every such n: 20,480 exact coefficient checks.
- Five signed integer profiles, supported through
  63,128,511,1024,4096 with W(n)=(37n mod17)-8,
  gave identical original and folded sums in DP10.
  Their values were 42,40,-106,330,471 respectively.

These tests corroborate coefficient signs and
folding only. They do not test a numerical
approximation to k, prove a uniform analytic
estimate, or supply evidence for OPEN-DP.
The analytic arguments above are the verification
of the kernel, Mellin continuation, diagonal
uniformity and frequency tails. The existing
Python launcher warning did not prevent the
successful exact checks; no configuration changed.

| Source path, relative to repository root | Read scope | Bytes | SHA256 |
|---|---|---:|---|
| [restricted provenance path] mathematical source] | All DP1--30, OPEN-DP and provenance; reviewed source | 17189 | BB75F77EE89C1E5BEA74AA5C3A570DA176B99D85D3616E1AAB1E76421E189B76 |
| [restricted mathematical source] | T10; prior dilation and conditional Mellin criteria | 67486 | 54F9692DE185D752C24C72ADF92BB4FD238ADD7D65C47ACF5917E9634C63E3F3 |
| [restricted mathematical source] | N28.C; prior continuum/overlap formulation and its open arithmetic | 69428 | 15A54DA3B83024F69DA0EF7657A105437CD51F5C7810F9395DA3A49B5339B40B |

The accepted baseline is used only in the explicitly
stated scope supplied by DP: its prior zero-free
region and buffered Mertens bound. Neither is
strengthened or independently re-proved here.
W21 is motivation, not an analytic input to the
proof just checked.

**Final independent verdict: ACCEPT DP1--30 at
the unchanged frozen source hash above.** The
acceptance includes their full parameter and
tail scope as detailed here. It requires no
mathematical source correction. The finite tests
are corroboration, not model consensus or a
substitute for the independent derivations.

OPEN-DP / DPR16--OPEN remains an unproved signed
energy estimate. The implication to c=.12551
at a=.87449 is conditional, and no c gain or
whole-energy lower bound is accepted.

after the final source-binding and byte readback;

## 3. Legal local equality patterns and what they do not establish

For (3), choose good first common primes outside every fixed bad modulus, with C=P,D=P^3. The C side has t=4,r=1,e=5,r0=0 at each such prime; E=0 is a term of the complete inactive-mask expansion. Thus c<=d and equality holds in the coefficient calculation (3). Every residual factor retains the P-puncture, and the effective row contains F=P^5. No natural zero is suppressed.

For (5), choose disjoint good prime products U,V and set

    C=U^5 V, D=U V^3,
    log_Z NU=13t, log_Z NV=9t, t>0.

Then c=74t,d=40t,R=22t,L=110t,R0=E=0, Bc=0. Every prime is of type (5,1) or (1,3), so (4) is an equality and the resulting coefficient equals Hplus. Exact equality of two distinct prime-product logarithms is not claimed; dyadic sectors approximate these ratios arbitrarily closely as the scale grows, with the original aggregate support tolerance. This is sufficient to test the supremal exponent geometry.

These patterns are compatible with the actual enclosing width and child width for sufficiently small fixed t: W=M-R-(c-d)_++L-6a=M+54t-6a, while M'=M-34t-6a-omega-g2+t2. The requirement NF<=Z^W reduces to 56t<=M-6a, which is strict for small t. For the first pattern it reduces to c<=M-6a. Allocate the displayed powers to original plain variables at sufficiently small support widths; choose residual prime support disjoint from them. All frozen-prime and canceled-prime zeros remain literal. A rectangle made empty by an allocation stays zero, as permitted by B3.50; no assertion that every allocated rectangle is simultaneously nonzero is needed. The second common support/projector can be empty without violating these coefficient constraints.

These are legal valuation/width configurations, not assertions that a character with a zero in the selected high bin exists or that a full oscillatory norm saturates its estimate. Further improvement beyond (6) may come from coupled columns, spectral information or actual label scarcity. The proof here only determines the best support coefficient supplied by these first-valuation inequalities.

## HCR7. Density suppression survives the fixed Gaussian, with limits

For the continuous unsmoothed model f_0(u)=exp(u)/u, u>0, the future
integral converges absolutely even at growth exponent 1: the bound
|J_1|<=1 leaves v^(-3/2) at large v. Using
1/(u+v)=integral_0^infinity exp(-r(u+v))dr and B0 gives exactly

    D_A f_0(u)=exp(u)*integral_0^infinity exp(-u*(r+A/r))dr
             =2sqrt(A)*exp(u)*K_1(2sqrt(A)*u).

The last identity follows from [DLMF 10.32.9](https://dlmf.nist.gov/10.32#E9),
or directly from r=sqrt(A) exp(t) and symmetry in t. The unique positive
saddle r=sqrt(A) yields

    D_A f_0(u) ~ sqrt(pi)*A^(1/4)*u^(-1/2)
                         *exp((1-2sqrt(A))*u).

In contrast, a fixed h gives exp(u-2sqrt(hu)) times u^(-3/4) and a fixed
constant. Substituting a moving strength into a fixed-order asymptotic
would not justify the result; the displayed exact integral does.

For the actual fixed smoothing of the density, put l=log 2 and

    P(u)=integral_l^infinity exp(y)/y*g_tau(y-u)dy.

For any fixed R>2sqrt(A), the identity 1/y=integral_0^infinity exp(-ry)dr
and completion of the Gaussian square give

    P(u)=integral_0^R c_tau(r)exp((1-r)u)dr + E_R(u),
    c_tau(r)=exp(tau*(1-r)^2/2),
    |E_R(u)| <= C*(exp((1-R)u)+exp(-c*u^2)),  u>=1.

The r>=R contribution is bounded by replacing 1/y by 1/l and integrating
the resulting full Gaussian. The missing y<l range for 0<=r<=R is
Gaussian-small, uniformly in that compact r interval. Filtering this
error costs at most O((1+u)exp((1-R)u))+O(poly(u)exp(-c'*u^2)).

For completeness, interchange of r and v in the main term needs a bound
near r=0. Compactness bounds c_tau(r), and
integral_0^R exp(-r(u+v))dr<=1/(u+v). Together with
|B_(Au)(v)|<=sqrt(Au/v) this is integrable at infinity; near zero use
|B_(Au)(v)|<=Au. Thus absolute Fubini holds, and the main term becomes

    integral_0^R c_tau(r)exp(u*(1-r-A/r))dr.

At its interior saddle r=sqrt(A), (r+A/r)''=2/sqrt(A). Laplace's method
therefore proves the precise constant

    D_A P(u) ~ exp(tau*(1-sqrt(A))^2/2)*sqrt(pi)*A^(1/4)
                   *u^(-1/2)*exp((1-2sqrt(A))*u).           (HCR7.1)

The model of the q_2 image of the prime portion of mu is
-P(u)+2P(u-log 2). Applying the SAME strength Au to this whole function
replaces c_tau(r) by (2^r-1)c_tau(r), so HCR7.1's constant is multiplied
by 2^sqrt(A)-1>0. This is correct despite the noncommutation in HCR2:
it does not shift the already filtered P, which would use the wrong
strength. The q_2 numerator has not been dropped.

None of this is a prime-sum asymptotic or a norm bound for a_n. Even a
granted pointwise prime remainder O(exp(bu)), b>b_* fixed, is sent by the
available estimate to O((1+u)exp(bu)), above all target exponents. A
continuous model cannot remove the rest of mu's signed coefficients or
their interactions. Nor is its saddle exponent a forced branch floor for
the full detector: HCR3's meromorphic full F is regular at the numerical
collision roots, and its symmetric branches cancel there. The density
model has a different singularity structure. No positivity inference
from a prime component to the full signed field is used or permitted.
title: HCR7. Density suppression survives the fixed Gaussian, with limits

Put S=(n1+n2)/M, t=z/M, A/M=S+t, and g/M=(S+4.5t-1)_+. The unchanged comparison and physical transforms give, apart from arbitrarily small allocated losses, the following main requirements for a normalized amplifier a/M:

If g>0, substituting the limiting low choice a/M=(7/3)g/M into the second expression and multiplying by 270 gives exactly

    1995 - 2009 S - 8379 t.                         (R1)

The coefficients follow from 270(.7+182/27)=2009 and 270(.7+(182/27)(9/2))=8379. This is a joint affine constraint, not a constant slot price with right side 1. Keeping its intercept is essential both here and in the physical selector.

Let

This simultaneously bounds the original geometric data without choosing the amplifier from a live plain scale. ## 5. Zero exclusion from any proved E9

For completeness, if the resulting bound M_chi(X)<<_(chi,epsilon)X^(gamma+epsilon) holds for every epsilon>0, partial summation defines

    F_chi(s)=s integral_1^infinity M_chi(x)x^(-s-1)dx

holomorphically on Re(s)>gamma, uniformly on compact subsets, with all fixed derivatives. On Re(s)>1 it is the absolutely convergent series sum mu(n)chi(n)n^-s=1/L(s,chi). The identity L(s,chi)F_chi(s)=1 continues wherever L is holomorphic in that half-plane, so L has no zero there. For principal chi, its simple pole at1 is excluded from this multiplication argument; F has the corresponding zero, and there is no zero of L at the pole. For imprimitive chi induced from chi*, the factors 1-chi*(p)p^-s omitted at ramified primes have modulus bounded away from zero on each compact subset of Re(s)>0, since any of their zeros has Re(s)=0. Thus the ordinary-character formulation already includes the exact imprimitive factors. This is an all-height analytic identity, not a low-height numerical test.

The continuation just used is elementary in this half-plane: for nonprincipal chi, its periodic partial sums are bounded, so Abel summation continues L to Re(s)>0. For principal chi, L(s,chi)=zeta(s)product_(p|q)(1-p^-s), and zeta(s)=s/(s-1)-s integral_1^infinity {x}x^(-s-1)dx is meromorphic on Re(s)>0 with its single pole at1. These formulas suffice for the identity-theorem return above.

All E9 hypotheses remain OPEN. No value of c is increased by the identities or error-norm calculation above.

## 1. Literal source and complete truncated identity

Fix an ordinary character chi modulo q, including principal or imprimitive characters. Put

    a(n)=mu(n)chi(n),       a0=a 1_(n<=Y), a1=a 1_(n>Y),
    1_chi(n)=chi(n),        Y>=1 an integer.

All squareful and nonunit zeros remain in a. Dirichlet convolution gives a*1_chi=delta_1, and hence the exact identity

    a = 2a0 - a0*a0*1_chi + a1*a1*1_chi.              (H1)

To check it, expand a1*a1*1_chi=(a-a0)^2*1_chi=a-2a0+a0*a0*1_chi. No coprimality filter is introduced between the two factors. Both ordered d/e placements and shared primes remain. Individual convolution terms need not inherit all original squareful zeros; H1 preserves them after its complete signed recombination.

For any sequence z let Z(x)=sum_(n<=x)z(n), zero for x<1, and let Gamma[z]_(a,L) denote the full Hankel operator with kernel exp(-a(t+u))Z(exp(t+u)) on L2(0,L). The fixed real weight a lies in (0,1); context distinguishes it from the coefficient sequence a(n) and its truncations a0,a1. Write X=exp(2L). Complex characters use the same bilinear convention as G149, without conjugating the source.

statement:
# [private research revision]: complete small-core C--C sectors

9 October 2026. Derived by the cubic lane and reviewed by the controller. The exact two-deletion expansion, column powers, core summation, nonprincipal conductor and positive row contour were checked. Finite algebra checks independently test both masks and detect the forbidden extra own-column restriction. No larger zero-free constant follows; c0 remains 0.125113352960035869... .

This continues [the one-unit-core estimate](cubic-unit-core.md).

The first estimate uses only ordinary Hecke convexity and the established
fixed angular continuation. The larger cutoff explicitly uses the
stronger accepted I-HECKE package. These scopes are separate below.

## 1. The complete ordered sectors and resulting cutoffs

Let `M` denote [the merged manuscript](../../zeta_zero_free_validated_merged.md).
For squarefree good cores `c,e>1`, let `Q_{<=C,*}` denote the original
C--C contribution in M (2.15) with `q_c<=C`. Let `Q_{min<=C}` include
both orientations with `min(q_c,q_e)<=C`. The other core is unrestricted.
The original full row sum, product profile, total-column coprimality,
and all required fixed components are retained.

For `D,K>=1`, `1<=C<=D`, every fixed `0<delta<1`, and every positive
loss `epsilon`, ordinary Hecke convexity gives
\[
\boxed{
|\mathfrak Q_{\le C,*}|,\ |\mathfrak Q_{\min\le C}|
\ll_{\delta,\epsilon}
K^\delta D^{11/6-\delta/2+\epsilon}C^{7/6-\delta/2}.
}
\tag{DC1}
\]
In particular, the entire band `min(q_c,q_e)<=D^(1/7)` costs
`D^(2+epsilon)` at `K<=D^.87653`.

Explicitly using **I-HECKE**, for fixed `b0<b<1`, gives
\[
\boxed{
|\mathfrak Q_{\le C,*}|,\ |\mathfrak Q_{\min\le C}|
\ll_{b,\epsilon}
K^{1-b}D^{5/6+b+\epsilon}C^{1/6+b}.
}
\tag{DC2}
\]
Here `b0=1-c0`. A fixed rational buffer `b=7/8` yields
\[
\boxed{
|\mathfrak Q_{\min\le C}|
\ll_\epsilon K^{1/8}D^{41/24+\epsilon}C^{25/24}.
}
\tag{DC3}
\]
At `K<=D^.87653`, this pays `C<=D^.1748164`. In particular,
\[
C=D^{1/6}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
|\mathfrak Q_{\min\le C}|
\ll D^{1.991510694444\ldots+\epsilon}.
\tag{DC4}
\]
The exponent in (DC4) is exactly `14338877/7200000` before the
arbitrary loss. Constants depend only on fixed profile seminorms,
fixed strip margins, and the specified fixed finite component family.
No uniformity for arbitrary moving angular types or additional
cube-dependent or row-dependent masks is asserted.

## 2. Both moving coprimality masks, exactly

For M (2.14)--(2.15), write `N1=c B^3`, `N2=e E^3`. The coefficient is
\[
\beta(c)\overline{\beta(e)}
\vartheta_c(k)\overline{\vartheta_e(k)}
\xi(B)\overline{\xi(E)}q_Bq_E.
\]
M (2.8) explicitly excludes an extra cube/row nonunit mask.
Total-column coprimality is exactly
\[
(c,e)=(c,E)=(e,B)=(B,E)=1.
\tag{DC5}
\]
There is no condition `(c,B)=1` or `(e,E)=1`.

Put `X_c=(D/q_c)^(1/3)` and `Y_e=(D/q_e)^(1/3)`. For the original
common column profile `W0`, define
\[
\begin{aligned}
S_z^-(X)&=\sum_b\xi(b)q_b(q_b/X)^{3z}
  \overline{W_0((q_b/X)^3)},\\
S_z^+(X)&=\sum_b\overline{\xi(b)}q_b(q_b/X)^{3z}
  W_0((q_b/X)^3).
\end{aligned}
\]
The original profile and its required Euler derivatives decrease
rapidly at both endpoints. Uniformly on every fixed compact interval
of `Re z`, the fixed angular argument gives
\[
|S_z^\pm(X)|
\ll_A(1+|\Im z|)^{C_A}\min(X^A,X^{-A}).
\tag{DC6}
\]
See [CS8](../[private research revision]-continuation/cubic-sectors.md) and
[T01](../[private research revision]/[restricted mathematical source]).
The auxiliary column Mellin functions are the fixed entire
`L^S(w-1,xi)` and `L^S(w-1,bar xi)`. Their shifts are residue-free;
the profile transform's vertical translation costs only a polynomial
in `Im z`. No moving deleted angular function is used in (DC6).

Open `(B,E)=1`, write `B=ell b`, `E=ell f`, and then open the two
remaining masks `(b,e)=1`, `(f,c)=1`. The exact column expression is
\[
\begin{aligned}
T_{c,e}(z)=\sum_{(\ell,ce)=1}\mu(\ell)q_\ell^2
&\left[\sum_{r\mid e}\mu(r)\xi(r)q_r
S_z^-\!\left(\frac{X_c}{q_\ell q_r}\right)\right]\\
{}\times&\left[\sum_{s\mid c}\mu(s)\overline{\xi(s)}q_s
S_z^+\!\left(\frac{Y_e}{q_\ell q_s}\right)\right].
\end{aligned}
\tag{DC7}
\]
The `ell` angular factors cancel. Both factors in (DC7) have the
**same complex `z`**. They are not replaced by an absolute square.
The residual cubes may overlap their own squarefree cores.

## 3. Column bound with both original tails

Let `E_N(u)=min(1,u^(-N))`. From (DC6), uniformly in `q_ell,q_r>=1`,
\[
q_r\left|S_z^-\!\left(\frac{X_c}{q_\ell q_r}\right)\right|
\ll_N(1+|\Im z|)^A\frac{X_c}{q_\ell}E_N(q_c/D).
\tag{DC8}
\]
For `q_c<=D`, use the global consequence `|S(u)|<<u`. For `q_c>D`,
the argument is at most `X_c<1`; choosing a small-scale exponent
`3N+1` in (DC6) gives the additional factor `X_c^(3N)`.

Norm-dyadic ideal counting gives, for any fixed `A>2`,
\[
\sum_\ell q_\ell\left|S_z^+\!\left(\frac{Y}{q_\ell}\right)\right|
\ll_A(1+|\Im z|)^{C_A}
\begin{cases}
Y^2,&Y\ge1,\\
Y^A,&Y<1.
\end{cases}
\tag{DC9}
\]
For `Y>=1`, split at `q_ell=Y`; both geometric tails are `O(Y^2)`.
For `Y<1`, use `Y^A sum_ell q_ell^(1-A)`.

Insert (DC8), sum the second factor by (DC9), and retain its divisor
norm. This proves
\[
\begin{aligned}
|T_{c,e}(z)|
&\ll_N(1+|\Im z|)^A X_cY_e^2\tau(e)
 \sum_{s\mid c}q_s^{-1}E_N(q_c/D)E_N(q_e/D)\\
&\ll_{N,\epsilon}(1+|\Im z|)^A
Dq_c^{-1/3}q_e^{-2/3}(q_cq_e)^\epsilon
E_N(q_c/D)E_N(q_e/D).
\end{aligned}
\tag{DC10}
\]
Thus the first moving deletion costs `tau(e)` and the second costs
`sum_(s|c) q_s^(-1)`. A moving conductor has not been hidden inside a
fixed angular continuation estimate. The symmetric bound follows by
interchanging the two columns. Both unbounded core/profile tails are
explicit in (DC10).

## 4. Full row conductor and a general summation lemma

For fixed coprime cores put `eta_(c,e)=vartheta_c bar(vartheta_e)`.
The complete unit sum annihilates the row series unless this character
is trivial on the six units. Otherwise
\[
\sum_{k\ne0}\eta_{c,e}(k)q_k^{-z}
=6L_{\mathbb K}(z,\eta_{c,e}),\qquad \Re z>1.
\tag{DC11}
\]
Its primitive good conductor is `ce`, as established in
[review [private research revision], section 1](../review-cycle-9.md).
Because `(c,e)=1` and both are nonunit, it is nonprincipal. The row
function is the full Hecke function, including all fixed-prime row
Euler factors and natural zeros at the good conductor primes.

Let `R=Phi_hat` be the original radial Schwartz row profile, written
as a function of the norm variable, and
`R_tilde(z)=integral_0^infty R(v)v^(z-1)dv`. The single original
row Mellin inversion is
\[
\mathfrak Q_{\le C,*}=\frac6{2\pi i}\int_{(\rho)}
\widetilde R(z)K^z
\sum_{\substack{1<q_c\le C,\ e>1\\
c,e\ {\rm sf},\ (c,e)=1\\
\eta_{c,e}|_{\mu_6}=1}}
\beta(c)\overline{\beta(e)}
L_{\mathbb K}(z,\eta_{c,e})T_{c,e}(z)\,dz,
\qquad \rho>1.
\tag{DC12}
\]
Initial exchanges are absolute. Shift only this row line to a fixed
positive `sigma`. There is no principal residue, and the contour does
not cross zero. The two rapid envelopes in (DC10) provide normal
convergence and absorb polynomial conductor growth throughout the
fixed strip. The row Mellin transform absorbs every polynomial height
cost. The original common profile and its Mellin roots are unchanged.

Suppose the available bound on the destination line is
\[
|L_{\mathbb K}(\sigma+it,\eta_{c,e})|
\ll(q_cq_e)^{h+\epsilon}(1+|t|)^A,\qquad h\ge0.
\]
Then the precise summation lemma is
\[
\boxed{
|\mathfrak Q_{\le C,*}|
\ll K^\sigma D^{4/3+h+\epsilon}C^{2/3+h}.
}
\tag{DC13}
\]
Indeed, since `|beta(c)beta(e)|=1`, the core sums in (DC10) cost
\[
\sum_{q_c\le C}q_c^{h-1/3+\epsilon}
\ll C^{h+2/3+\epsilon},\qquad
\sum_e q_e^{h-2/3+\epsilon}E_N(q_e/D)
\ll D^{h+1/3+\epsilon}.
\]
The second sum includes all `q_e>D`: its dyadic tail is a convergent
geometric sum once `N>h+1/3+epsilon`. Swapping the columns handles
the unrestricted `q_c>D` tail in the reverse orientation.

To cover `min(q_c,q_e)<=C`, split it disjointly into `q_c<=C` and
`q_c>C,q_e<=C`. The estimate applies to both, because the extra
core restriction can be dropped after absolute core summation.
This pays both ordered mixed terms without invoking positivity or
replacing them by diagonal squares. No cube-dependent mask is added.

## 5. Ordinary convexity and the separate I-HECKE improvement

Ordinary finite-order Hecke convexity gives
`h=(1-delta)/2` on `sigma=delta`, `0<delta<1`. It follows from the
ordinary functional equation in review [private research revision] and absolute
convergence, with small boundary margins allocated to `epsilon`.
Equation (DC13) therefore proves (DC1). For
`K<=D^k0`, `C=D^gamma`, its exponent is
\[
\frac{11}{6}+\frac{7\gamma}{6}
 +\delta\left(k_0-\frac12-\frac\gamma2\right).
\]
At `k0=.87653`, the useful optimum is `delta` approaching zero,
giving `gamma=1/7` with arbitrary losses. For example,
`gamma=1/8`, `delta=1/32` give the strict exponent
`1.988980104166666...`.

For the stronger statement, invoke precisely the inherited I-HECKE
strip bound displayed in [private research revision] T07:
\[
|L(\sigma+it,\eta)|
\ll q_{\mathfrak f_\eta}^{(b-\sigma)/2+\epsilon}(1+|t|)^A,
\qquad 1-b\le\sigma\le b,\quad b_0<b<1.
\]
Take the fixed positive line `sigma=1-b`, so `h=b-1/2`.
Equation (DC13) proves (DC2). The good conductor really is `ce`,
and all fixed factors affect only fixed constants on this strip.
This is a result relative to I-HECKE, not a consequence of ordinary
convexity or Riemann-zeta nonvanishing alone.

For `K<=D^k0`, `k0=.87653`, the limiting affordable cutoff is
\[
\boxed{
\gamma_*=
\frac{1/6+(1-k_0)c_0}{7/6-c_0}
=0.1748488627130781\ldots .
}
\tag{DC14}
\]
Choose `b>b0` close enough to `b0` in terms of the final loss,
allocate the other preliminary losses, and only then vary the scales.
This proves affordability at `C=D^gamma_*` with `D^(2+epsilon)`.
For the fixed rational buffer `b=7/8`, the exact cutoff is
`gamma=(7-3k0)/25=437041/2500000=.1748164`.

Within these available pointwise row bounds, the useful optimal line
is `1-b`: above it, the increased row-length cost dominates the
conductor saving at the relevant core ranges; below it, the
functional-equation conductor cost increases faster. The ordinary
convexity endpoint is similarly `delta` approaching zero. These are
limitations of the obtained upper budgets, not lower bounds for the
actual signed form.

## 6. Fixed components and the exact remaining gate

Fixed column ray refinements twist the angular sums by finitely many
fixed finite-order characters; their infinity types remain nonzero.
Any resulting divisor or common-cube phases have bounded magnitude.
Fixed-place row refinements preserve the nontrivial good conductor
`ce`; their exact local factors are bounded on each fixed positive
strip. Natural zeros, fixed-prime valuations, original profiles,
Mellin roots, and all prescribed fixed components remain accounted for.

Combining with the previously paid unit-core sectors leaves
\[
\boxed{
\mathfrak Q_{\rm rem}
=\mathfrak Q_{\substack{q_c>C\\q_e>C}}
-\mathfrak Q_{II}
+O_\epsilon\!\left(
DK^{1+\epsilon}+D^{11/6+\epsilon}
+K^{1-b}D^{5/6+b+\epsilon}C^{1/6+b}
\right).
}
\tag{DC15}
\]
The original signed II subtraction remains whole. At `C=D^(1/6)`
and `b=7/8`, the complete displayed error is
`O(D^(1.991510694444...+epsilon))` in the requested row range.
T05 remains the physical cube-row II theorem; it is not a whole
C--C estimate.

The next unpaid object is the actual double-large-core C--C term
minus II. For comparison, continuing this pointwise method to
`C=D^(1/5)` costs `D^(2.02619625038...+epsilon)` under the limiting
I-HECKE budget. It would require additional averaging or signed
cancellation. No increase of `c0` is established.

Source anchors: M (1.6), (2.8), (2.14)--(2.15); review [private research revision],
section 1 (unit average, full row Hecke function, primitive good
conductor and ordinary functional equation); [private research revision] T01 (fixed
angular continuation and height growth), T07 (the explicitly stronger
I-HECKE strip); CS6--CS9 in the accepted pure-cube packet; and
UC4--UC15 in the one-unit-core draft.

Accept W47-01's scale-drift identity and actual squarefree diagonal calculation; W47-26's exact finite Ward defect; W47-19's sharp trace/exterior/dimension certificate; and the **scoped** failures of the unit syndrome and frequency-curvature tests 17/22. Two qualifications are necessary:

## 1. Source and quantifier contract

Fix an ordinary Dirichlet character (\chi), with its **natural zero extension**, and (\tau>0). Write
\[
 g_\tau(u)=(2\pi\tau)^{-1/2}e^{-u^2/(2\tau)},\qquad
 U_\chi(x)=\sum_{n\ge1}\mu(n)\chi(n)g_\tau(\log(n/x)).
 \tag{R1}
\]
All Gaussian fields here include every integer and the entire tail. A shell exponent (\gamma) means, for every (\epsilon>0),
\[
 \|U_\chi\|_{L^2([X,2X],dx/x)}\ll_{\chi,\tau,\epsilon}X^{\gamma+\epsilon}
 \quad\hbox{on every sufficiently large dyadic shell}. \tag{R2}
\]
For a family conclusion the same exponent must hold for **each** fixed character; constants may depend on it. One fixed character does not establish the family. No uniform growing-conductor or angular family is obtained.

The forward zero return is direct. Gaussian decay handles (x\to0); Cauchy--Schwarz on every large shell makes the Mellin integral holomorphic for Re s>γ. Initially for Re s>1 it equals
\[
 \int_0^\infty U_\chi(x)x^{-s}\,dx/x
       ={e^{\tau s^2/2}\over L(s,\chi)}. \tag{R3}
\]
The numerator has no zeros. Analytic continuation excludes every zero of this fixed (L) in Re s>γ, at every height; a principal (L)-pole gives a reciprocal zero and is not an obstruction. Constants need not be uniform in height to get this holomorphic half-plane conclusion. This direction uses the complete moment and does not import an unsupported reciprocal vertical-growth or Phragmen--Lindelof estimate. No converse from zero exclusion to the moment is claimed here. A moving approximant first returns to the **fixed** R1, and only then uses R3.

The original H form remains a different source. At every use below it retains its actual (a(\pi)=\alpha(\pi)\widetilde g_3(\pi)\eta(\pi)), (\xi(g)=\alpha(g)^3\eta(g)^3), complete g,g′ and core sums, both rooted mark-row projectors, common mark arrays, sharp annuli/windows, natural zeros, two orientations deleted at equal rational norm, ray/angular data and height profiles. The literal far mask is
\[
 q_\pi\ne q_{\pi'},\qquad |q_\pi-q_{\pi'}|>\lfloor Z^{.05}\rfloor. \tag{R4}
\]
Both the original complements and the outside squared scalar (N^{-1}G^{-2}) must be restored once. A fixed-u,v subpacket does not replace the full g,g′ form.

## 2. W47-01: scale drift and the actual diagonal

Put (y=\log x), (h>0), (a=e^{\gamma h}), (E_j=\int_{jh}^{(j+1)h}|U(e^y)|^2dy), and (D(y)=U(e^{y+h})-aU(e^y)). Direct expansion gives
\[
 E_{j+1}-a^2E_j=\int_{jh}^{(j+1)h}(|D|^2+2a\Re(D\overline U))dy. \tag{R5}
\]
A bound $E_{j+1}-a^2E_j\le C_\epsilon e^{(2\gamma+\epsilon)jh}$ on **every** j yields the corresponding upper bound for $E_j$ by the geometric recurrence; conversely an energy bound implies that one-sided drift bound because $E_j\ge0$. Finite initial shells and fixed-h/dyadic covers cost constants. Density-one j is insufficient. A pure faster exponential has positive normalized drift $e^{2\beta h}-e^{2\gamma h}$, independently of its imaginary frequency; this is a diagnostic, not an actual zero construction.

For the fixed modulus q of the zero-extended character (not merely its primitive conductor), elementary squarefree counting gives
\[
 \sum_{n\le t}\mu(n)^2\mathbf1_{(n,q)=1}=\kappa_qt+O_q(\sqrt t),\quad
 \kappa_q=\prod_{p\mid q}(1-p^{-1})\prod_{p\nmid q}(1-p^{-2}).
\]
This follows by (\mu^2(n)=\sum_{d^2\mid n}\mu(d)), imposing gcd conditions before counting the remaining multiples. Partial summation with the full squared Gaussian gives
\[
 \sum_n\mu^2(n)|\chi(n)|^2 g_\tau(\log n-y)^2
 =\kappa_q {e^{\tau/4}\over2\sqrt{\pi\tau}}e^y+O_{q,\tau}(e^{y/2}). \tag{R6}
\]
The integrated diagonal therefore has leading drift proportional to (e^h-e^{2\gamma h}<0) when γ>1/2. This calculation is correct, including ramified zeros. It is not a lower bound for the signed total square, and it does not bound the off-diagonal contribution to R5. This is an exact adaptation of the existing scale/Lyapunov family, not a new arithmetic estimate.

## 3. W47-15: uniform growing depth, complete Gaussian restoration

Use arithmetic convolution *, identity δ, (\ell_\chi(n)=\chi(n)), and (m_Y(n)=\mu(n)\chi(n)\mathbf1_{n\le Y}), for one fixed integer Y≥2. In the Banach algebra
\[
 \|a\|_b=\sum_{n\ge1}|a(n)|n^{-b},\quad b>1,
\]
let (d_Y=\delta-\ell_\chi*m_Y=\ell_\chi*((\mu\chi)\mathbf1_{n>Y})). Choose Y so
\[
 \eta={\zeta(b)Y^{1-b}\over b-1}<1.
\]
Then — with actual zeros at every ramified prime —
\[
 \|d_Y\|_b\le\eta,\quad \|m_Y\|_b\le\zeta(b),\quad d_Y(n)=0\ (n\le Y).
\]
For every integer k≥1 define
\[
 Q_k=m_Y*(\delta+d_Y+\cdots+d_Y^{*(k-1)}).
\]
The exact identities are
\[
 \delta-\ell_\chi*Q_k=d_Y^{*k},\qquad
 \mu\chi-Q_k=(\mu\chi)*d_Y^{*k}. \tag{R7}
\]
Consequently equality with μχ holds **strictly below** ((Y+1)^k), and
\[
 \sup_k\|Q_k\|_b\le{\zeta(b)\over1-\eta},\qquad
 \sup_k\|\mu\chi-Q_k\|_b\le
 B_b:=\zeta(b)\left(1+{1\over1-\eta}\right). \tag{R8}
\]
The stronger decaying bound (\zeta(b)\eta^k) also follows from R7 but is unnecessary. (Q_k) is a finite polynomial in an **infinite Dirichlet series**, generally not a finite-support Dirichlet polynomial. All its coefficients remain in the physical readout.

For (N_X=2X\exp(C\sqrt{\log X})), take
\[
 k_X=\left\lfloor{\log N_X\over\log(Y+1)}\right\rfloor+1.
\]
This ensures the strict threshold is greater than (N_X), including exact integer-power cases. Newton doubling (P_0=m_Y), (P_{r+1}=2P_r-\ell_\chi*P_r*P_r) gives (P_r=Q_{2^r}). Replacing (k_X) by the least power of two at least (k_X) preserves R8. The number of formal Newton stages is (O(\log\log X)); no arithmetic-operation complexity claim follows.

Set (V_X(x)=\sum_n Q_{k_X}(n)g_\tau(\log(n/x))), with the power-of-two option equally valid. For x∈[X,2X], full tail support and R8 give
\[
 |U_\chi(x)-V_X(x)|\le B_b\sup_{n\ge N_X}n^b g_\tau(\log(n/x)).
\]
For large X the exponent (bv-v^2/(2\tau)) decreases for (v\ge C\sqrt{\log X}\ge b\tau), whence
\[
 \sup_{X\le x\le2X}|U_\chi(x)-V_X(x)|
 \ll_{b,Y,C,\tau}X^{b-C^2/(2\tau)}e^{bC\sqrt{\log X}}
 =X^{b-C^2/(2\tau)+o(1)}. \tag{R9}
\]
This prices **all** n, not an arbitrary hard truncation of (Q_k). Weighted absolute convergence also proves each physical readout is well-defined. If (b-C^2/(2\tau)<\gamma), triangle inequalities in both directions prove that the complete shell estimates R2 for (V_X) and U are equivalent, with all ε buffers. Return to the fixed U before applying R3; the Mellin transform of a varying (V_X) is not a substitute.

The concrete constants are valid: b=2, Y=4 give (\zeta(2)<2), η<1/2, “Q norm <4” and (B_b<6), uniformly in k and χ. Choosing (C=\sqrt{3\tau}) makes R9 (X^{1/2+o(1)}), sufficient for every fixed γ>1/2. The actual initial coefficients are (1,-\chi(2),-\chi(3),0) at 1,2,3,4. Character zeros do not invalidate the endpoint support statement; they can make a specific first eligible coefficient vanish.

This does not contradict the old absolute-norm failure at exponents ≤1. For a nonzero finite preconditioner M, let d₀ be its least nonzero index and take unramified primes p beyond its support. At d₀p, the residual coefficient is (-M(d_0)\chi(p)): all smaller divisors have zero coefficient. Thus its absolute σ-norm diverges for σ≤1. This does not bound a signed physical readout. The present proof uses fixed b>1 and lets the Gaussian tail pay the gap to γ<1.

Ancestry is exact: matched-Astra section AH12/formula AH20 already contains Newton's inverse algebra and strict prefix; [restricted research revision]-W2/W43.2--4 already contains the truncated-prefix geometric identity, fixed-k rough-coefficient obstruction and opposite support regime. **The increment is R8 uniformly in depth plus R9 and its full fixed-source return**, not the algebra. W43's fixed-k absolute lower bound does not remain a growing-k contradiction with constants suppressed. No γ<.874861 estimate for V is provided. The existing arithmetic question has a concrete new representation and a paid tail, not a weaker proved hypothesis.

## 4. W47-26: what the Ward defect actually costs

For a finite prime set \(\mathcal P\), use the exterior basis S and supertrace (\operatorname{Str}Z=\sum_S(-1)^{|S|}Z_{SS}). With the ordering strings in the CAR creators,
\[
 Q=\sum_{p\in\mathcal P}w_pa_p^*,\quad W=\sum_p|w_p|^2>0,
 \qquad Q^2=0,\quad QQ^*+Q^*Q=WI.
\]
For even Z, finite-dimensional supertrace cyclicity gives
\[
 \operatorname{Str}(Q^*[Q,Z])=W\operatorname{Str}Z. \tag{R10}
\]
For diagonal Z, mixed-prime traces vanish and **each individual prime term** is (|w_p|^2\operatorname{Str}Z). There is no square-root-of-prime-count cancellation among these terms.

Taking $Z_{SS}=\chi(n_S)g_\tau(\log(n_S/x))$, $n_S=\prod_{p\in S}p$, yields $\operatorname{Str}Z=U_{\mathcal P}(x)$, exactly the finite squarefree Gaussian field. Ramified χ makes corresponding entries zero. Taking Euler entries instead yields $\prod_p(1-z_p)$, with no zero for $|z_p|<1$; this is a finite-product diagnostic, not the physical zero theorem.

If $\mathcal P_X$ contains every prime up to $2X\exp(C\sqrt{\log X})$, every omitted squarefree n exceeds that cutoff. Direct summation of the bounded-coefficient Gaussian tail gives $|U-U_{\mathcal P_X}|\le X^{1-C^2/(2\tau)+o(1)}$ uniformly on the shell. Hence $D_X/W_X=U_{\mathcal P_X}$ has an exponent-equivalent return when this error is below γ. **Without division by W, raw defect exponents shift with its size.** Rescaling the weights already demonstrates why raw equivalence cannot be invariant. One may normalize $\sum|w_p|^2=1$, in which case the wording becomes literally valid.

The full boundary thus re-encodes the entire source; a spectral gap alone does not pay it. This scoped failure leaves room for a different differential with an independently cheaper total defect. Credit round31/T26's exterior supertrace and the related W46/Hodge defect now accepted in G74; neither their existence nor the current consensus proves a moment. The finite prime-subset U construction is not identical to W46's actual f3 channels.

## 5. W47-19: the sharp exterior criterion and its native limits

For a finite matrix T, let (A=T^*T\succeq0), d be its full input dimension, (t=\operatorname{tr}A), and
\[
 e_2={t^2-\operatorname{tr}A^2\over2}=\|\wedge^2T\|_{HS}^2.
\]
For d≥2 and t>0, Cauchy on the other d−1 eigenvalues gives
\[
 \lambda_{\max}(A)\le{t+\sqrt{(d-1)((d-1)t^2-2de_2)}\over d}. \tag{R11}
\]
Equality holds when all other eigenvalues coincide. The d=1 and t=0 cases must be handled separately. For (t/d\le B^2\le t), the sharp sufficient condition based only on these two moments is
\[
 e_2\ge {t^2-B^4-(t-B^2)^2/(d-1)\over2}. \tag{R12}
\]
If (p=\operatorname{tr}A^2/t^2), δ=B²/t, this is (p\le\delta^2+(1-\delta)^2/(d-1)). B²≥t needs only the trace; B²<t/d is impossible for a nonzero matrix with that trace. A constant area fraction is not a power saving: diag(M,1) already has large e₂ while its top eigenvalue grows like M. The dimension floor cannot be suppressed.

For the intended application, (T_H) must be the coefficient matrix of the **entire original form** after all the contractions and masks in R4, with (v_i(P)=u_i(P)/\sqrt{q_P}). Then \(\|v_i\|^2=\Omega_i\). The desired raw norm is
\[
 B\ll Z^\epsilon GK[\,N+L+(NL)^{2/3}\,]P_{\rm orig}, \tag{R13}
\]
with the actual profile/height factor and its paid family sum. Afterward the outside scalar (N^{-1}G^{-2}) is applied once. A single u,v/core child, a fixed height, a dense arbitrary-mode matrix or an extra unsigned deletion does not establish R13. Neither the required trace nor the fourth contraction/e₂ of this exact (T_H) is bounded here.

The far-mask clarification matters. Entrywise multiplication by a 0/1 mask is an idempotent self-adjoint operator on matrix entries. It **does not generally take PSD matrices to PSD matrices**. The mask's Hermitian matrix has zero diagonal; if nonzero, its zero trace forces both signs. A synthetic (J-I) mask has norm d−1 even when initial feature vectors are orthogonal; this illustrates the direction problem but is not a native-H lower bound. The general all-g pressure .004 is not automatically a saving relative to a Frobenius norm. The author's hypothetical purity calibration can be used only after an actual matching normalization is established.

## 6. Tests 17 and 22: native coefficients, signs and scoped failures

The exact JN7 transform has unitary factor (1/Q), (Q=q_\pi q_{\pi'}), on a group of size Q²:
\[
 \widehat W(h,s,s')={1\over Q}\sum_{R,P,P'}W(R,P,P')
 e(-Rh/(\pi\pi')-Ps/\pi+P's'/\pi'). \tag{R14}
\]
The plus sign in the second mark is conjugation. JN9's kernel is
\[
 K(h,s,s')=\chi_\pi(h)^3\chi_{\pi'}(h)^3
                 \chi_\pi(s)^2\chi_{\pi'}(s')^4. \tag{R15}
\]
The reciprocity phase ζπ,π′, both long-prime coefficients and the entire short-core sum remain attached. There is no additional Q factor. Both complete projectors precede or are fully recombined after this transform; equal-rational-norm pairs remain deleted. The common-unit Jacobi mean is subtracted with its existing paid cost, not asserted zero.

For the **particular unit/nonunit syndrome** in test17, its unit fiber has size ((q_\pi-1)^2(q_{\pi'}-1)^2). On it |K|=1 and K has mean zero, because the nontrivial cubic mark character averages to zero. Its conditional variance is therefore exactly 1. Already in the norm7 field, s=1 and s=3 have the same unit code but different cubic phase. Ramified zeros occur outside the proper unit fiber, not as omitted side conditions. The norm7/norm13 author count has all six exponents equally frequent (864 each); the mathematical mean-zero proof, not that finite count, establishes the stated scope.

The remaining pairing with the actual \(\widehat W\) is a full covariance. Cauchy's cost is \(\sqrt{|\mathcal U|}\,\|1_{\mathcal U}(\widehat W-\overline W_{\mathcal U})\|_2\). A richer code that includes K itself transfers the difficulty to the predictable mean. A synthetic \(\widehat W=\overline K\) can saturate Cauchy but need not belong to the native source. Thus there is no original-H lower bound or general coding impossibility.

For test22, the phase in R14 is affine **as a function of the frequency coordinates**, so its frequency Hessian is zero. Its joint dependence on physical and frequency variables is bilinear; no zero joint Hessian is claimed. Adjacent row frequencies are spaced $1/(\pi\pi')$, of modulus $Q^{-1/2}\asymp N^{-1}$; mark frequencies have scale $N^{-1/2}$. An artificial Hamming distance does not force separation of this native phase.

The exact complete source has row support at most (C_{\rm orig}K) modulo ππ′, because its original disk embeds without collisions when Q≫K. After summing every core child and applying both mark transforms, JN12 gives for every row-frequency set E of size J **independent of the mark coordinates**
\[
 \|1_E\widehat{\mathcal W}\|_2^2
 \le {C_{\rm orig}KJ\over Q}\|\widehat{\mathcal W}\|_2^2. \tag{R16}
\]
J≈N captures at most (O(K/N)) of the norm; at the cited box this is (O(Z^{-.003})). Capturing a fixed fraction needs J≳Q/K. This does not apply to an arbitrary adaptive mark-dependent set. It also does not estimate the signed pairing with the omitted frequencies, so it is neither an H bound nor an H lower bound. Both tests are useful native-source obstructions to the proposed shortcuts.

## 7. Protected audit W47-30: exact largest-prime renewal and the full covariance

This was chosen before author outcomes for high reach. Let (P^+(n)) be the largest prime factor and define
\[
 U_{<p}(z)=\sum_{P^+(m)<p}\mu(m)\chi(m)g_\tau(\log(m/z)),
\]
including m=1. Only squarefree products of primes below p contribute, so for each p this is a finite, possibly very large, exact sum. Unique largest-prime decomposition of every squarefree n>1 gives
\[
 U_\chi(x)=g_\tau(\log(1/x))-
                \sum_p\chi(p)U_{<p}(x/p). \tag{P1}
\]
Indeed n=pm, p=P⁺(n), p∤m, and μ(pm)χ(pm)=−χ(p)μ(m)χ(m). Natural zeros make the equality valid even at ramified primes. Absolute convergence of the original Gaussian sum justifies regrouping; no prime-independence assumption appears.

For (R_X=2X\exp(C\sqrt{\log X})), set (B_X(x)=\sum_{p\le R_X}\chi(p)U_{<p}(x/p)). An omitted largest prime implies n>R_X. Thus
\[
 U_\chi(x)=g_\tau(\log(1/x))-B_X(x)+E_X(x),\qquad
 \sup_{[X,2X]}|E_X|\le X^{1-C^2/(2\tau)+o(1)}. \tag{P2}
\]
The bounded-coefficient tail estimate follows by comparison with
$x\int_{C\sqrt{\log X}}^\infty e^v g_\tau(v)dv$, with a boundary term; the Gaussian exponent is decreasing there for large X. For $C=\sqrt{2\tau}$ this is $X^{o(1)}$, whereas the head term decays faster than every power. Consequently, for each γ>1/2 (indeed for any fixed positive γ), the every-shell norm bound for B_X is equivalent to R2 and returns through R3.

The exact norm target is the **entire** covariance
\[
 \|B_X\|_2^2=
 \sum_{p,q\le R_X}\chi(p)\overline{\chi(q)}
 \langle U_{<p}(x/p),U_{<q}(x/q)\rangle_{[X,2X]}. \tag{P3}
\]
All diagonal and off-diagonal terms are present. Conditioning on the largest prime has not centered or eliminated its future response. If an accepted buffered baseline (\|U\|_2\ll X^\beta), β<1, is used, P2 also gives an energy comparison error (O(X^{\beta+o(1)})), including the complete cross terms. This is below (X^{2\gamma}) for γ>1/2. The simpler norm comparison does not require that baseline.

There is a precise obstruction to one strong interpretation of “faithful small state.” For r fixed unramified primes, all (2^r) functions
\[
 \mu(n_S)\chi(n_S)g_\tau(\log n_S-y)
 =c_Sg_\tau(y)e^{(\log n_S)y/\tau},\qquad c_S\ne0,
\]
are linearly independent on every real interval. The numbers log n_S are distinct; successive derivatives give a Vandermonde determinant. Hence an exact **linear** state/readout preserving arbitrary combinations of every prime-subset history must have dimension at least (2^r). This is not a lower bound for a single fixed arithmetic sum, nonlinear compression or a source-specific approximate covariance closure. W41/G53's coefficient Hankel rank two does not contradict this physical Gaussian-readout statement.

Disposition: **new bounded audit development, promising but unbridged**. P1--P3 pay the exact source return and expose the missing signed covariance. They do not estimate it. Credit the existing renewal/fugacity state program, G53/G54's physical-response distinctions and the [private research revision] complete covariance work. The priority idea survives as a concrete arithmetic question; no generic martingale or state-count heuristic is accepted as its answer.

## 8. Uniform audit W47-11: heat trace, actual Gram and observation loss

Let A be a finite PSD matrix, d its dimension, (H(t)=\operatorname{tr}e^{-tA}) for t>0 and (D=d-H(t)). Then
\[
 H(t)\le(d-1)+e^{-t\lambda_{\max}(A)}.
\]
If D<1 this yields the sharp certificate
\[
 \lambda_{\max}(A)\le-{1\over t}\log(1-D). \tag{U1}
\]
Equality is attained by rank-one A. Thus a lower bound (H(t)\ge d-1+e^{-tB^2}) suffices for top eigenvalue ≤B². A mere **upper** heat-trace bound does not control high eigenvalues. In normalized form the required trace is within O(1/d) of 1. For d≥2 and (0<H\le d-1), no finite upper bound on the top eigenvalue follows from H alone: let that eigenvalue tend to infinity and choose the remaining exponentials in (0,1] with their sum tending to H (or adjusted exactly for each sufficiently large top eigenvalue). Any separate high-energy-remainder estimate must be supplied and paid.

The actual Gaussian source shows why an unrestricted operator certificate is too costly. Take the squarefree integers coprime to the character modulus q in [X,2X], of cardinality $d_X=\kappa_qX+O_q(\sqrt X)$, and their complete physical Gram
\[
 K_{mn}=\int_X^{2X}g_\tau(\log(m/x))g_\tau(\log(n/x))\,dx/x.
\]

## 4. Wildcard11 and bridge26: finite-height division versus a global floor

Let U_chi be the fixed complete Gaussian Mobius field with Mellin transform
exp(tau s^2/2)/L(s,chi), and D_lambda U(x)=U(x)-lambda^beta U(x/lambda), for
fixed lambda>1 and fixed real beta. Its exact multiplier is

    m_lambda(s)=1-lambda^(beta-s).                        (26.1)

The Gaussian left tail and fixed dilation are paid as in the complete source
construction; a complete every-epsilon shell L2 exponent gamma for D_lambda U
makes its Mellin integral holomorphic on Re(s)>gamma. This is a conditional
arithmetic assumption, not a consequence of changing the multiplier.

For lambda2=2 and lambda3=3, the common zeros of m2,m3 are exactly s=beta.
Indeed their zeros are on Re(s)=beta; a nonzero common height would make
log2/log3 rational and hence2^k=3^l for nonzero integers, impossible. At the real
point beta both vanish simply. Accordingly two complete channel bounds exclude
all L-zeros in Re(s)>gamma except possibly a SIMPLE real zero at beta. Higher
multiplicity would survive in both quotients. If beta is in an independently
proved zero-free region, e.g. beta>theta11 under the accepted premise, the
exception is already excluded. Locally away from beta one nonzero multiplier
suffices; no global quantitative lower bound in height is needed for that
analytic argument. This is existing G47/G109-style detector-bank ancestry.

The stronger positive-floor hope fails. On the critical line, for any fixed
positive weights w2,w3,

    inf_(t>=T) [w2|1-exp(-it log2)|^2+w3|1-exp(-it log3)|^2]=0

for every finite T. Pigeonholing points nL(log2,log3)/(2pi) modulo1 supplies
arbitrarily high simultaneous near-returns. [private research revision] already proves this for
every fixed summable bank and pays its complete source formation. The failure
does not refute local analytic division or source-specific signed estimates.

There is an elementary explicit finite-height replacement. Let0<t0<=T and
kappa=(log2 log3)/(2pi). For t0<=|t|<=T,

    max(|m2(beta+it)|,|m3(beta+it)|)
      >= min(2t0 log3/pi,
             4 exp(-kappa T)/((log2+log3)sqrt(3))).      (11.1)

Proof: by symmetry take t>0 and choose nearest nonnegative integers k,l to
t log2/(2pi), t log3/(2pi), with errors e2,e3 in[-pi,pi]. If both integers are
zero, max|e_j|=t log3>=t0 log3. Otherwise3^k and2^l are distinct integers, so

    |k log3-l log2| >=1/max(3^k,2^l)
       >=exp(-kappa T)/sqrt(3).

On the other hand it is at most (log2+log3)max(|e2|,|e3|)/(2pi).
Finally |1-exp(-ie)|=2|sin(e/2)|>=2|e|/pi for |e|<=pi. Combining these two
cases proves(11.1). The estimate is deliberately coarse and deteriorates
exponentially with T. It gives a concrete finite-height inverse price on the
critical line away from beta; it does not improve the exponent of either
arithmetic channel. A common real blind point remains and must be paid above.

### An elementary comparison bound, strengthened below

Let \(\mathcal B_{X,\ge H}\) retain the exact terms with
\((d,e)\ge H\), \(H\ge2\). Then
\[
\boxed{\sup_{X\le x\le2X}|\mathcal B_{X,\ge H}(x)|
 \ll XH^{-1}\log^2(2X),\qquad
\|\mathcal B_{X,\ge H}\|_{L^2(dx/x)}^2
 \ll X^2H^{-2}\log^4(2X).} \tag{AD4}
\]
Indeed write the exact gcd as \(g\), so \(d=ga,e=gb\). Only after
this partition, take absolute values and enlarge by dropping squarefree
and coprime restrictions, the smooth cutoffs and \(\ell\le J\):
\[
|\mathcal B_{X,\ge H}(x)|
\le\sum_{g\ge H}\sum_{a,b,\ell\ge1}
 |\phi(\ell g^2ab/x)|
=\sum_{g\ge H}\sum_{r\ge1}d_3(r)|\phi(g^2r/x)|.
\]
For every \(T>0\),
\[
\sum_{r\ge1}d_3(r)|\phi(r/T)|\ll T\log^2(2+T).
\]
For \(T\ge1\), partial summation proves this; for \(T<1\),
the exponential upper tail is stronger. Sum \(g^{-2}\) to obtain AD4.
All finite cutoffs and shared-prime terms were retained before passing to
a positive majorant; there is no omitted complementary product range.

For any fixed \(1/2<a<1\), choose \(H=X^{1-a}\). Triangle inequality
in \(L^2([X,2X],dx/x)\) makes the full target
\(E_B(X)\ll X^{2a+\epsilon}\) equivalent, up to arbitrary losses,
to that target for \(\mathcal B_{X,<H}\). This handles the cross terms
with the discarded sector as well. At \(a=.87449\), every internal
gcd \(g\ge X^{.12551}\) is therefore affordable at exponent
\(1.74898\). In the residual exact factorization,
\[
g<X^{.12551},\qquad a,b>Y/g\gg X^{.37449}/\log^2X.
\]
The use of \(a,b\) as factor labels in this display is separate from the
fixed detector exponent \(a=.87449\).

The sharper [signed gcd pruning theorem]([private research revision]-continuation/mobius-gcd.md)
now replaces this elementary cutoff in the active target. Using only the
accepted fixed Mertens exponent \(b=7/8>b_0\), it proves
\[
\|\mathcal B_{X,\ge H}\|_2^2
\ll X^{2b+\epsilon}H^{2-4b},
\qquad |Q_{\rm cross\ bad}(H,R;X)|
\ll X^{2b+\epsilon}R^{1-2b}.
\]
The second expression is the signed union of all four large cross-gcd
events, with the internal cuts retained. Its proof freezes the original
prime-incidence masks, cancels the four singleton Möbius variables, and
only then uses a positive numerical union majorant.

Choose \(H=X^{1/1400}\), \(R=X^{1/700}\). Both exponents are
\(4897/2800\), below \(1.74898\) by exactly \(9/175000\). Internal removal
uses the \(L^2\) triangle inequality, not an unproved affordable additive
error between the squared energies. The active open estimate is
**OPEN-MG** in that proof: the exact full signed quartic form with both
internal gcds below \(H\) and all four cross gcds below \(R\). Every
original endpoint, short third factor, broad product difference and
Möbius sign remains. No larger \(c\) follows from these sector bounds.

## 3. Complete source tails and finite computation

For 0<gamma<1, H0=sqrt(2a)C_q/(a-gamma) and K=1+2a/(a-gamma) give |Q^j h(t)|<=H0 K^j exp(-gamma t). The complete Gram tail after T is positive semidefinite and at most

    (N+1)H0^2 K^(2N) exp(-2gamma T)/(2gamma) I.

The residual tail is at most H0^2(sum_j |p_j|K^j)^2 exp(-2gamma T)/gamma +2|F0|^2 exp(-2aT). These pay both the source and anchor tails; omitting filtered future responses would be invalid.

A coherent source approximation ||h-h_tilde||<=tau instead gives, by the isometry of Q,

    ||p(Q)(h-h_tilde)||<=tau sum_j|p_j|.              (R11)

Each Gram-entry error is at most tau(||h||+||h_tilde||), and the operator error is at most N+1 times that quantity. This is an absolute operator-error bound, not a positive-semidefinite ordering between two source Grams. Even if h_tilde vanishes after T, its filtered Q^j outputs have full exponential-polynomial tails that must be retained.

The sharper actual-source continuation is valid for 1/2<gamma<1, with lambda=a-gamma=2-2gamma in(0,1). For q=1, writing u={x},

    f(log x)=1/2+B(x)-V(x)/x,
    B=1/2-u, V=u(1-u), primitive(B)=V/2.             (R12)

The primitive is bounded by1/8. Integration by parts, including its lower endpoint, and absolute integration of V/x give

    |integral_x^infinity y^(lambda-1)(f(log y)-1/2)dy|
       <=D_lambda x^(lambda-1),
    D_lambda=(2-lambda)/[4(1-lambda)].                (R13)

Consequently h(t)=A0 exp(-gamma t)+C exp(-at)+R(t), where A0=sqrt(2a)/(2lambda), |R(t)|<=sqrt(2a)D_lambda exp(-(gamma+1)t). Keep h exactly on[0,T] and continue by

    h_tilde(t)=A0 exp(-gamma t)
       +(h(T)-A0 exp(-gamma T))exp[-a(t-T)]           (t>T).

The difference is R(t)-R(T)exp[-a(t-T)]. Its two L2 norms prove, with no unknown infinite constant required,

    ||h-h_tilde||<=D_lambda[1+sqrt(a/(gamma+1))]
                       exp[-(gamma+1)T].            (R14)

For every nonprincipal chi, A(x) is q-periodic. Take m_chi its mean and B=A-m_chi, whose mean-zero primitive is bounded by2q^2. For a principal character put B0=A-rx, beta its mean, D(x)=integral_1^x(B0-beta); then exactly

    f(log x)=m_chi+B_chi(x)+V_chi(x)/x,
    m_chi=-beta, B_chi=B0-beta,
    V_chi=r+2beta-2D(x).                              (R15)

Here |D|<=2q^2, |V|<=1+2q+4q^2. The same proof yields(R13)-(R14) with A0=sqrt(2a)m_chi/lambda and D_chi=4q^2 for nonprincipal chi, or 4q^2+(1+2q+4q^2)/(1-lambda) for principal chi. It works componentwise for complex chi and retains natural zeros. Exact checks include the quartic character modulo5 and its induced, zero-extended character modulo20. Fixed-q constants are allowed; the constant blows up at gamma=1/2 and no endpoint claim follows.

This is a useful source formation theorem, specifically adapting [private research revision]'s bounded-periodic-primitive method. Combining(R14) with(R11) still charges sum|p_j| and the entire computed signed residual. It does not imply Delta_N->0. A degree/cutoff schedule must pay the displayed coefficient growth; arbitrarily increasing N at a fixed T is not justified.

statement:
## 3. Developed W60-12: exact phase compatibility and arithmetic isolation

### 3.1 A binary checksum does not automatically preserve a complex character

For a finite unramified prime set P and subset S, write w(S)=(-1)^|S| chi(product S). For a fixed nonempty toggle C,

    w(S symmetric_difference C)/w(S)
      =(-1)^|C| product_(p in C)chi(p)
                    product_(p in S intersect C)chi(p)^(-2).       (C1)

Therefore w(S xor C)=-w(S) for EVERY S if and only if

    chi(p)^2=1 for every p in C,
    (-1)^|C| product_(p in C)chi(p)=-1.                            (C2)

Necessity follows by comparing S empty with each singleton in C; sufficiency is substitution. The hypothesis product_C chi(p)=1 alone is insufficient for an odd toggle when nonreal phases occur.

Actual counterexample: take the primitive quartic character mod5 with chi(2)=i, chi(3)=-i, chi(11)=1 and C={2,3,11}. The empty subset pairs1 with66 with opposite coefficients. But {2} pairs2 with33, whose actual coefficients are BOTH -i. All four integers are squarefree5-units. The exact script checks all eight states. The restricted edge6<->11 is valid; a code must track the state as well as its syndrome.

For a binary matrix A and principal chi, if the parity vector1 lies in the row space of A, parity is constant on every syndrome class and there is no within-class sign cancellation. If it does not, the full uncut cube has balanced parity in every class: translate by an odd element of ker A. The multiplicative cutoff need not respect that translation. This is elementary code duality, not a new theorem about arithmetic cancellation. C1-C2 identify the extra phase failure for the actual complex coefficients.

### 3.2 Turnover lemma: a short move must replace a large factor

For distinct positive integers n,m, put g=gcd(n,m). Then

    g divides n-m, so g<=|n-m|.                                 (C3)

If C>0, 0<=theta<1, and |n-m|<=C min(n,m)^theta, it follows exactly that

    n/g >= C^(-1) n^(1-theta).                                  (C4)

When n is squarefree, n/g is the product of the prime factors deleted from n. If all those primes are <=y and at most d are deleted, then n/g<=y^d. Thus n has NO such neighbor whenever

    n^(1-theta)>C y^d.                                         (C5)

This argument allows m to be squareful or nonunit: adding zero-mass auxiliary integer states does not help when an edge may delete at most d of n's prime factors. In particular it applies to the usual squarefree Boolean Hamming radius<=d, whose number of deleted coordinates is<=d. No coefficient estimate or character-distribution assumption is used.

### 3.3 A large actual isolated set exists on every sufficiently large shell

Fix q, C>0, an integer d>=1, and 0<=theta<1. Precisely, every graph edge {n,m} must satisfy the displayed distance bound and delete at most d prime factors from EACH squarefree endpoint when passing to the other endpoint. This condition is independent of a flow's orientation; an incoming edge cannot bypass the source-side budget. Squarefree Hamming radius<=d satisfies it, and optional zero-mass integer vertices are allowed subject to the same endpoint rule. Choose an integer

    k > d/(1-theta),   y=(2X)^(1/k).                            (C6)

Let V_X contain all products of k DISTINCT primes in

    (X^(1/k),(2X)^(1/k)].

Each n in V_X is squarefree, X<n<=2X, and for large X is coprime to the fixed q. All its primes are<=y. Since1-theta-d/k>0, inequality C5 holds for every n in V_X once X is sufficiently large. Hence every such vertex is isolated in the entire short-move graph, including possible neighbors outside this shell or cutoff.

The ordinary prime number theorem gives, for this FIXED k,

    t_X=#primes in the displayed interval
       ~ k(2^(1/k)-1) X^(1/k)/log X.

Unique factorization counts distinct vertices exactly as binomial(t_X,k). Therefore

    |V_X| ~ A_k X/(log X)^k,
    A_k=[k(2^(1/k)-1)]^k/k! >0.                                (C7)

Only fixed-relative-width intervals are used, not a primes-in-short-interval theorem or a growing-k substitution. For the external input, the published PNT was checked in the official [NIST DLMF27.12, equations4-5](https://dlmf.nist.gov/27.12). All deductions C3-C7 are given here. The constants can be tiny and the onset large; both are permitted and neither changes the power obstruction.

It follows that ANY disjoint matching in this graph leaves at least A_k X/(2(log X)^k) actual unit-modulus source coefficients unmatched on [X,2X], for every sufficiently large X. The absolute unmatched mass cannot be O(X^delta) for ANY delta<1. Thus the fixed-radius candidate cannot meet M2, at a near gain,1/6,1/4, or any other power-saving target.

This extends beyond integral matching. For an arbitrary complex edge flow F supported on the same graph, let div F(n) be its net outgoing mass, whenever defined. In any exact source decomposition a=div F+r, an isolated vertex satisfies r(n)=a(n). Hence

    sum_(X<n<=2X)|r(n)| >= |V_X|.                               (C8)

No choice of complex flow weights, linear combinations of codewords, or repeated local steps removes an isolated vertex. Chaining cannot start there. The result still holds for any uniformly bounded family of radii and for subpower inflation of C, by first replacing theta by a fixed slightly larger number below1. It does NOT cover growing radii, genuinely long edges, nonlocal auxiliary states with a different exact transfer, or a bound retaining signed cancellation among the isolated states.

| Intended exponent theta | Fixed radius d | k used | Strict isolation exponent1-theta-d/k |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
|17497/20000=.87485|3|24|3/20000|
|5/6|3|19|1/114|
|3/4|3|13|1/52|

The first row has about X/(log X)^24 isolated24-prime products, all with principal coefficient+1. The next two rows use19- and13-prime products, with principal coefficient-1. This is a lower bound for the absolute residual and for those particular signed subcollections. It is NOT a lower bound for the complete signed residual or M_chi: different prime-count layers can cancel, and that cancellation remains an eligible arithmetic input.

### 3.4 What survives and what has changed

The remaining high-ceiling target is an exact phase-compatible interaction with enough **prime-factor turnover**, or a signed estimate for the smooth isolated complement coupled to other prime-count layers. At a vertex n with largest allowed deleted prime y, C4 requires at least

    ((1-theta)log n-log C)/log y

deleted prime factors. This is the quantity a growing code or multiscale construction must pay; a small Hamming distance by itself is the wrong budget. The concrete three-prime exchange M4 repairs the large-prime failure of deletion matchings but leaves the proved high-degree smooth obstruction. A future combined construction must estimate both parts and their signed interaction. No favorable coding distance or representation count pays that term.

Functional signature: actual squarefree mu-chi source; additive-near, bounded prime-turnover graph; exact coefficient cancellation/flow; C3 forces isolated high-degree products; complete unmatched-count return M1-M3. The new claimed record delta is C6-C8 for all fixed-radius local flows, plus the source-phase criterion C2 and explicit reopening condition. The general pairing return is existing transport ancestry. No literature priority is claimed.
