statement:
### S17: sharp primitive/Farey observable and its actual jump obstruction

For a fixed ordinary character, the denominator-weighted primitive count is

    A_chi(x)=sum_(b<=x) chi(b) phi(b)
            =sum_(d<=x) mu(d)chi(d) sum_(m<=x/d) m chi(m).

The coefficient at 1 is retained. Its absolutely convergent Dirichlet series is L(s-1,chi)/L(s,chi) for Re(s)>2. For q=1 the ordered coprime pair count is 2A_1(x)-1, including the diagonal pair (1,1).

At every unramified prime p, A_chi has a jump of magnitude p-1. Therefore no continuous background B(x) can satisfy |A_chi(x)-B(x)|=O(x^gamma) uniformly on every large real x when gamma<1: compare the left limit and value at p. This is an actual-character sharp-observable obstruction. It does not forbid averages, a smoothed count, or a discontinuous background whose full recovery cost is paid. The elementary principal estimate A_1(x)=x^2/(2 zeta(2))+O(x log x) includes all floor errors and the reciprocal tail.

An r-fold Riesz smoothing has Mellin quotient L(s-1,chi)/[L(s,chi)s(s+1)...(s+r)]. A complete smoothed residual bound can supply a return only after the principal terms and possible numerator zeros are paid. That is a conditional bridge, not an estimate. The author's parity-adapted higher-dimensional Jordan numerator subsequently supplies a useful source-specific repair of this numerator issue; the blind sharp-jump obstruction remains valid in its own scope.

statement:
## 4. Sharpening: an upper bound matches the lower exponent

ROOT's lower bound is valid but does not exhaust the readily provable result. Put h=k+1, H_N=sum_(m<=N)1/m, and A_N=sum_(p<=N)1/p. The latter sum may include conductor primes, which only enlarges the following upper bound.

Taking the triangle inequality in (5), exchanging finite sums, and dropping squarefree/coprimality restrictions only from the nonnegative inner sum gives

    W(z)
      <= N sum_(d in S_N, d>T, omega(d)>=h) (1/d)
                    sum_(m<=N/d, dm in S_N) 1/m
      <= N H_N sum_(d<=N, d squarefree, omega(d)>=h) 1/d
      <= N H_N sum_(j>=h) A_N^j/j!
      <= N H_N exp(A_N) A_N^h/h!.                            (9)

The elementary-symmetric-sum bound in the third line is valid because each unordered set of j distinct primes occurs j! times in A_N^j; allowing repeated primes and products above N enlarges the sum. For the final line use (h+r)!>=h!r! and sum over r>=0. This bound includes ALL residual coordinates and is uniform in every cutoff T>=1.

Partial summation from pi(t)=O(t/log t) gives A_N=O(loglog N), while H_N<=1+log N. If h~kappa log N/loglog N for fixed kappa>0, the elementary factorial estimate log(h!)=h log h-h+O(log h) yields

    log(H_N exp(A_N) A_N^h/h!) = -kappa log N+o(log N).

Combining (6), (8) and (9), for 0<kappa<1, proves

    B(z) = N^(1-kappa+o(1)),
    W(z) = N^(1-kappa+o(1)),                                (10)

uniformly for 1<=T<=beta N. The notation means that both logarithms divided by log N converge to 1-kappa. For k=o(log N/loglog N), (6) and the bound W<=N H_N exp(A_N) give exponent 1. No claim of a precise fixed-k logarithmic asymptotic for B or W is made.

A sharp sequence formulation is useful. Fix 0<gamma<1, fixed q and beta, and one integer sequence k_N>=0 and one cutoff sequence satisfying 1<=T_N<=beta N for all sufficiently large N. Neither sequence varies with the epsilon in the following statement. Then

    B(z_N) <<_epsilon N^(gamma+epsilon) for every epsilon>0
    iff W(z_N) <<_epsilon N^(gamma+epsilon) for every epsilon>0
    iff liminf_(N->infinity) k_N loglog N/log N >= 1-gamma.    (11)

Constants may also depend on the fixed q, beta and sequences. For sufficiency, fix 0<a<1-gamma; the liminf condition eventually puts k_N above a log N/loglog N. The nonnegative tail in (9) decreases with h, so its bound at that smaller depth is N^(1-a+o(1)). Let a approach 1-gamma according to epsilon. For necessity, if the liminf is smaller, choose 0<a<1-gamma above it and use infinitely many k_N<=a log N/loglog N. On that subsequence b_(k_N)<=N^(a+o(1)), its largest prime is O(log N), and the same fixed-ratio PNT count is at least N^(1-a-o(1)). This contradicts the claimed bound for any sufficiently small fixed epsilon.

Thus the original phrase 'equality is no sufficiency assertion' is correct as a description of what the LOWER-BOUND proof alone establishes, and remains essential for the COMPLETE |z_1|+bill certificate. With (9), equality IS sufficient for the residual bill alone. This distinction should be preserved if ROOT integrates the sharpening.
title: 4. Sharpening: an upper bound matches the lower exponent

statement:
## 3. Uniform finite Euler moments and the signed-core lemma

Put
\[
 \mathcal E_z(s)=\prod_{p\le z}(1-p^{-s}),\qquad
 \mathcal H_z(s)=\prod_{p\le z}(1+p^{-s}).
\]
Both are finite products. Their series run over squarefree \(z\)-smooth integers; no coprimality between two core positions is imposed.

For \(t\ge4\), on \(|s-1|\le1/t\), the local denominators in either logarithmic derivative are bounded away from zero:
\(|p^{-s}|\le p^{-3/4}\).
Moreover \(p^{|s-1|}\le e\), so RNR3 implies
\[
 \left|\log\frac{\mathcal E_z(s)}{p_z}\right|
 +\left|\log\frac{\mathcal H_z(s)}{h_z}\right|
 \le C|s-1|\sum_{p\le z}\frac{\log p}{p^{1-1/t}}\le C .
\]
The branches start at \(s=1\) on this simply connected zero-free disk. Cauchy's estimate therefore gives, **simultaneously for every integer \(j\ge0\)**,
\[
 |\mathcal E_z^{(j)}(1)|\le C p_z j!t^j,\qquad
 |\mathcal H_z^{(j)}(1)|\le C h_z j!t^j.             \tag{RNR4}
\]
There is no unrecorded \(O_j\) constant. These are finite entire products; no infinite signed series at \(s=1\) was interchanged.

The positive tilt gives
\[
 \mathcal H_z(1-1/t)\le C h_z,\qquad
 \sum_{D,E}\frac{(\log D+\log E)^j}{DE}
       \le C h_z^2 j!t^j,                            \tag{RNR5}
\]
because \(u^j\le j!e^u\). All sums in this section are over squarefree
\(z\)-smooth cores. For \(V\ge1\),
\[
 \sum_{D>V}D^{-1}\le C h_z e^{-\log V/t}.
\]
More particularly, with \(Q=\log U\),
\[
 {\bf1}_{\max(D,E)>U}(\log D+\log E)^j
 \le e^{-Q/(2t)}j!(2t)^j
           e^{(\log D+\log E)/t}.                   \tag{RNR6}
\]
Indeed the tail forces \(\log D+\log E>Q\); half of the exponential
pays that tail and half bounds the power. This also covers \(j=0\).

Now let \(\mathcal F(a,b)\) be uniformly analytic and bounded by \(M_0\)
on a fixed closed bidisc of radius \(r_0>0\), including a neighborhood of
that closed bidisc. Write
\(\mathcal F=\sum c_{ij}a^ib^j\), with
\(|c_{ij}|\le M_0r_0^{-i-j}\).
Assume \(2Q/L<r_0/2\) and set
\[
 K=\left\lfloor\frac{r_0L}{16t}\right\rfloor.
\]
For \(D,E\le U\), the remainder after total degree \(K-1\) is bounded by
\[
 2M_0r_0^{-K}
       \left(\frac{\log D+\log E}{L}\right)^K.
\]
Using RNR5, its **absolute** weighted sum is
\[
 \ll h_z^2 K!\left(\frac{t}{r_0L}\right)^K
 \le C h_z^2 16^{-K}.                               \tag{RNR7}
\]
The factor count at each degree causes no missing loss:
\(\sum_{i+j=k}a^ib^j\le(a+b)^k\) for nonnegative \(a,b\).

Complete each polynomial moment to all cores before bounding it.
RNR6 bounds the total-degree-\(k\) completion error by
\[
 C h_z^2e^{-Q/(2t)}k!
              \left(\frac{2t}{r_0L}\right)^k.
\]
The ratio of successive terms is at most \(1/8+o(1)\) for \(k<K\),
so their sum is \(O(h_z^2e^{-Q/(2t)})\).
The **completed signed** moments are exactly
\[
 \sum_{D,E}\frac{\mu(D)\mu(E)(\log D)^i(\log E)^j}{DE}
   =(-1)^{i+j}\mathcal E_z^{(i)}(1)\mathcal E_z^{(j)}(1).
\]
Their constant term is \(p_z^2\mathcal F(0,0)\). RNR4 bounds the other
terms by
\[
 C p_z^2\sum_{1\le k<K}(k+1)k!
                  \left(\frac{t}{r_0L}\right)^k
 \ll p_z^2\,\frac tL,
\]
since the successive ratio is \((k+2)t/(r_0L)<1/8\) eventually.
Thus
\[
 \sum_{D,E\le U}\frac{\mu(D)\mu(E)}{DE}
            \mathcal F(\log D/L,\log E/L)
 =p_z^2\left\{\mathcal F(0,0)+
 O\!\left(\frac tL+t^4e^{-c_{r_0}L/t}
                    +t^4e^{-Q/(2t)}\right)\right\}. \tag{RNR8}
\]
This rederives RN19. The \(t^4\) is exactly the allowed positive-to-signed
mass ratio \((h_z/p_z)^2\ll t^4\); it was not silently suppressed.

For the author's \(Q=L/m\) and \(t\le L/(\ell_0m^2)\),
\[
 L/t\ge\ell_0m^2,\qquad Q/t\ge\ell_0m,\qquad t^4\le L^4 .
\]
The two exponential terms are bounded respectively by
\(L^{4-c_{r_0}m^2}\) and \(L^{4-m/2}\).
For each requested fixed \(A\), these are \(O_A(L^{-A})\) uniformly.
Also \(2Q/L=2/m<r_0/2\) eventually.
This proves the growing-order assertion with explicit constants.
It is not a fixed-order asymptotic with \(K\) substituted afterward.
title: 3. Uniform finite Euler moments and the signed-core lemma

statement:
## 1. Fixed-power complement: independent proof and signs

Fix 1/3<rho_0<=rho<=rho_1<1/2 and set

    L=log X,  z=X^rho,
    delta=(1-2 rho_1)/4,  eta=delta(1-beta)>0,
    C_f=9 log 2 * product_(p>=5)(1-1/(p-1)^2),
    B(rho)=2 log((1-rho)/rho)-2/(1-rho)-1/(1-rho)^2.

The reviewed statement is

    R_(X^rho)(x)=C_f exp(tau/2) B(rho) x/L^3
                  +O(X/L^4+X^(1-eta)L),                (R1.1)

uniformly for rho in this fixed compact interval and X<=x<=2X.
Constants can depend on tau,beta,rho_0,rho_1. In particular they are
not uniform as either compact endpoint reaches 1/3 or 1/2.

### 1.1 The actual f core, not an inherited Gaussian-mask estimate

For Re s>1 the literal Euler factors give

    D(s)=sum_n f(n)n^(-s)=H(s)/zeta(s),
    H(s)=(1-3^(-s))^(-2)
          product_(p!=3) (1-2p^(-s))/(1-p^(-s))^2.

At p!=3, the H factor is

    1-sum_(j>=2)(j-1)p^(-js),

and at p=3 its coefficients are j+1. Thus H has an absolutely
convergent Dirichlet series h for Re s>1/2, including absolute
convergence of sum |h(r)|r^(-beta). The coefficient identity is
f=h*mu. Directly using the accepted Mertens input therefore proves

    A_f(u)=sum_(n<=u)f(n)=O_beta(u^beta).               (R1.2)

This step uses no bound for F and no inversion of the vanishing
prime-two factor. It is the r=1 instance of the accepted actual f_r
convolution in [private research revision] Gaussian S1--S7.

H has a simple zero at 1 from p=2. Its p=2 derivative is 4 log 2;
the p=3 factor is 9/4; the remaining factors multiply to the positive
product in C_f/(9 log 2). Hence

    H'(1)=C_f,  D(s)=C_f(s-1)^2+O((s-1)^3).

The second zero is the zero of 1/zeta(s), not another finite-prime
factor. By (R1.2), the ordinary-order reciprocal sums and their first
two logarithmic derivatives converge at 1, giving

    sum_r f(r)/r=0,
    sum_r f(r)log r/r=0,
    sum_r f(r)(log r)^2/r=2C_f.                        (R1.3)

These sums are generally CONDITIONAL. For j=0,1,2 their tails after R
are O_beta(R^(beta-1)(1+log R)^j), by Abel summation. Taking absolute
values of these reciprocal moments would destroy the proof.

### 1.2 Exact two-prime source and all source-completion errors

Let nu=(3rho_0-1)/2>0 and U=X^(1+nu). Then U<z^3 for all rho in the
chosen interval and large X. If n<=U has at least two distinct primes
above z, it has exactly two, say p<q; each occurs to the first power.
Its unique factorization n=rpq has r<z, so (r,pq)=1 and f(n)=f(r).
Conversely every such factorization below U has the original source
coefficient. It follows that the two-prime completion is EXACT below U:

    f(n)1_(omega_z(n)>=2)
      =sum_(z<p<q, pq|n) f(n/(pq)),   n<=U.            (R1.4)

Above U the identity can fail, and we do not use it there. The number
of representations is at most d_3(n), so (R0.2) pays the whole
discrepancy. Thus

    R_z(x)=sum_(z<p<q) sum_(r>=1) f(r)g(log(rpq/x))
                  +O_A(X^-A).                        (R1.5)

This pays every term with three rough primes and every repeated rough
prime power. It preserves every valuation in the original source.
The frozen author's outside-range witnesses are correct: at z=5,
n=7^2*11 gives original +1 versus completion -1, and n=7*11*13 gives
original -1 versus completion -3. The equality is not global.

### 1.3 Signed large-core tail, including its lower boundary

Put R=floor(X^delta). For any y>0, integration by parts using (R1.2)
gives

    |sum_(r>R) f(r)g(log(r/y))|
      <= C_beta y^beta Q_beta(log(R/y)),
    Q_beta(v)=exp(beta v)g(v)
                 +integral_v^infinity exp(beta w)|g'(w)|dw. (R1.6)

The first term pays the actual boundary -A_f(R)g(log(R/y)). Q_beta
is bounded for v<=0 and decays faster than every exp(-Bv) for v>=0.
For Y>=1, splitting integers k at Y and then into dyadic intervals,
using sum_(k<=V)d(k)<=C V log(2V), yields

    sum_k d(k)k^(-beta)Q_beta(log(k/Y))
       <= C_beta Y^(1-beta)log(2Y).                   (R1.7)

Apply this with y=x/(pq), k=pq and Y=x/R. Summing (R1.6) over every
actual p<q, and only then majorizing by d(k), bounds the entire removed
core by

    C x R^(beta-1)log(2x/R)=O(X^(1-eta)L).            (R1.8)

This is cancellation of the actual unrestricted f(r) core furnished by
(R1.4)--(R1.5). It is not a bound for an arbitrary smooth or masked core.

### 1.4 Unordered primes, both Stieltjes replacements, and density

After r<=R, replace p<q by half the ordered sum and subtract half
the p=q sum. Even with all cores, its absolute value is bounded using
(R0.1) by

    sum_(p>z)sum_r g(log(rp^2/x))
       <= C_tau x sum_(p>z)p^(-2)<=C_tau X/z.          (R1.9)

Thus no square-prime coefficient is misidentified as a two-distinct-
prime coefficient.

For y=x/r, fixed p>z, and a chosen fixed N, Stieltjes integration by
parts with the PNT error gives

    |sum_(q>z)g(log(pq/y))
       -integral_z^infinity g(log(pv/y))dv/log v|
      <= C_(tau,N) (y/p)L^(-N) H_1(log(pz/y)),
    H_1(a)=exp(a)g(a)+integral_a^infinity exp(w)|g'(w)|dw. (R1.10)

This includes the endpoint -[pi(z)-li(z)]g(log(pz/y)); it has the
correct convention even if z itself is prime. The endpoint at infinity
vanishes. Log v>=rho_0 L throughout; no upper cap is being smuggled in.

H_1 is bounded on the negative half-line and rapidly decreasing on the
positive half-line. The integer harmonic majorant therefore gives

    sum_(p>z)p^(-1)H_1(log(pz/y))
       <= C[1+log_+(y/z^2)]<=C L.

The first prime replacement costs O_N(y L^(1-N)). For the second,
exchange the positive q-integral and the p-sum and apply the same
one-variable error estimate inside that integral. The remaining
integral is

    integral_z^infinity H_1(log(vz/y))dv/(v log v),

which is also O(L), and in fact the factor 1/log v gives a stronger
bound here. This proves the same stated error for the second
replacement. There is no omitted error-product term: these are two
sequential exact replacements with their respective errors bounded.
Summing absolute errors over r<=R introduces only sum 1/r=O(L).
N=8 consequently pays both by O(X/L^6).

Write t=log z=rho L and define the NONNEGATIVE density

    phi_t(A)=A^(-1)log((A-t)/t),  A>2t,
    phi_t(A)=0,                  A<=2t.

The exact unordered continuous density follows from

    (1/2)integral_t^(A-t) ds/[s(A-s)]
       =A^(-1)log((A-t)/t).

With w=log(pq/y), the Jacobian is y exp(w). Combining all preceding
errors, the actual source is

    R_z(x)=x integral_R exp(w)g(w)
        sum_(r<=R) f(r)/r phi_t(log x+w-log r)dw
       +O(X^(1-eta)L+X/z+X/L^6)+O_A(X^-A).            (R1.11)

This establishes the constant 1 in front of phi_t; a second factor 2
must not be inserted after the unordered density calculation.

### 1.5 The decisive signed Taylor remainder

Take W=delta L. For |w|<=W and r<=R,

    log x+w-log r >= (1-2delta)L >2rho_1 L.

The distance from the density edge is at least 2delta L. On this
range phi_t^(j)=O(L^(-1-j)) for j<=3, uniformly in the stated compact
rho interval. Globally phi_t=O(1/t); together with sum_(r<=R)1/r=O(L)
this pays the discarded |w|>W portion of (R1.11) by (R0.2).

Put A=log x+w and v=log r. Taylor's theorem gives

    phi_t(A-v)=phi_t(A)-v phi_t'(A)+(v^2/2)phi_t''(A)+e_A(v),
    |e_A(v)|<=C v^3/L^4,  |e_A'(v)|<=C v^2/L^4.

The valid summation of the last term is SIGNED Abel summation:

    sum_(r<=R)f(r)e_A(log r)/r
      =A_f(R)e_A(log R)/R
       -integral_1^R A_f(u)[e_A'(log u)-e_A(log u)]du/u^2.

By (R1.2), its absolute value is O_beta(L^-4): the integral of
exp(-(1-beta)v)(v^2+v^3) over v>=0 is finite, and the boundary has
the same bound. An unsigned harmonic summation of v^3/L^4 would
not give this result.

Complete only the three signed polynomial moments using (R1.3) and
their stated tails. The outcome, uniformly on the retained w range, is

    sum_(r<=R) f(r)/r phi_t(A-log r)
       =C_f phi_t''(A)+O(L^-4+R^(beta-1)/L).           (R1.12)

The Gaussian integration then replaces phi_t''(log x+w) by phi_t''(L)
with O(L^-4), because log(x/X) is bounded and the third derivative
has the stated bound. This replacement is done on |w|<=W; it does
not extend a derivative formula through the nonsmooth density edge.
Only the constant value is subsequently integrated over the full
Gaussian, with an already paid tail. The integral of exp(w)g(w) is
exp(tau/2).

Direct differentiation gives

    phi_t''(A)=2log((A-t)/t)/A^3
                 -2/[A^2(A-t)]-1/[A(A-t)^2],
    phi_(rho L)''(L)=B(rho)/L^3.

This proves (R1.1). The extra X/z error is absorbed there since
eta<rho_0. The core-moment tail X R^(beta-1)/L is smaller than the
earlier signed large-core error. Every log and power error is accounted
for before the asymptotic sign is read off.

### 1.6 Band signs, terminal tail, and scope

If u=(1-rho)/rho is in (1,2), then

    B(rho)=2log u-3-4/u-1/u^2<2log 2-21/4<0,
    B'(rho)=-2/(1-rho)-2/rho
                 -2/(1-rho)^2-2/(1-rho)^3<0.

Thus R_(X^rho) is eventually negative uniformly on any stated compact
rho interval. For fixed 1/3<a<b<1/2, exact coefficient subtraction
gives

    T_(X^b)-T_(X^a)=R_(X^a)-R_(X^b)
      =C_f exp(tau/2)[B(a)-B(b)]x/L^3
        +O(X/L^4+X^(1-eta)L)>0.                       (R1.13)

For a=3/8,b=2/5 the positive factor is exactly

    B(a)-B(b)=79/225+2log(10/9)=.5618321424267637... .

The decimal is only an evaluation of an already positive closed
formula. It is not evidence for an asymptotic. For every fixed c>1/2,
omega_(X^c)(n)>=2 implies n>X^(2c), so (R0.2) proves

    R_(X^c)(x)=O_A(X^-A).                              (R1.14)

It follows without a complete-field bound that the band from any
fixed a in (1/3,1/2) to any fixed c>1/2 is NEGATIVE of order X/L^3.
There is no finite terminal threshold for the uncapped Gaussian;
(R1.14) is a full-tail bound instead.

The previous [private research revision] subpower range stops at
log z<=L/(1000log L); its actual bands have the opposite sign in the
specified comparison. No interpolation between the two theorems has
been proved. Below rho=1/3 the third rough prime can enter the central
source. At rho=1/2 the growing complete reciprocal-core approximation
used in (R1.12) is no longer uniform. Neither boundary is included in
(R1.1).

## 3. A concrete alternating construction

The following chain is legitimate:

    old compact family
      -> new compact family
      -> simultaneous 2/3 bank
      -> Gaussian bank
      -> common Gaussian family by R_a
      -> another simultaneous bank.

A two-level version has four channels

    G_ij=D_i S_gn D_j S_no F_old=D_iD_j F_G, i,j in{2,3}.

Applying R_a in each index recovers F_G with global cost A^(-1), or all-shell
cost at most2/A. At depth m the corresponding costs are A^(-m/2) and
(sqrt(2/A))^m. Multiply in every smoothing/shift cost as well. Fixed finite
depth costs a constant. Scale-dependent depth must have total cost X^o(1),
or debit its explicit power from the proposed saving. With a uniform stage
bound C>1, depth o(log X) suffices for a subpower product. Source and profile
choices must remain consistent throughout the reconstruction.

These particular scalar scale operators commute. Merely reordering them
cannot improve the exponent. Their value is that a different representation
may expose an arithmetic estimate that is hard to prove directly.

statement:
## R42.10. Uniform parked audit29: variance price and one fixed sparse field

First keep the full signs and kernel. For any finite vectors v_i in a Hilbert space, independent Bernoulli I_i with 0<p_i<=1, and F=sum v_i, set Fhat=sum I_i v_i/p_i. Then

    E Fhat=F,
    E||Fhat-F||^2=sum_i (p_i^-1-1)||v_i||^2=:V,
    E||Fhat||^2=||F||^2+V.                            (R42.22)

Every off-diagonal source cross survives in ||F||^2. Only the centered sampling errors are orthogonal in probability; the physical Gaussian kernel is not diagonalized. For w_i=||v_i||^2 and expected size m=sum p_i, Cauchy--Schwarz gives V>= (sum sqrt(w_i))^2/m-sum w_i. The exact constrained minimum has p_i=min(1,sqrt(w_i/lambda)), with lambda fixed by the budget, apart from zero-weight coordinates. This is the correct leverage cost, including saturated coordinates.

The same formula applies to the vector pair of actual detectors in a direct-sum Hilbert space, using one common mask. Their cross covariance is also changed by the same diagonal factors (p_i^-1-1); two separately sampled lists cannot silently be called one source. On a central shell the diagonal Gaussian weight for Na in[X,2X] is bounded above and below by positive constants. Squarefree allowed ideals have positive linear density: applying mu_K inclusion-exclusion to the fixed-mask lattice count gives C X+O(sqrt X log X), C>0. Hence the ideal Möbius component alone has the lower variance cost cX^2/m-C'X. The literal f3 field, with absolute coefficients1, gives the same obstruction immediately. For target gamma>1/2 and substantial sparsification, variance below X^(2gamma) needs m at least of order X^(2-2gamma). Adding a second detector can raise this cost.

The warning about a zero-dependent or separately resampled detector can be resolved constructively. The following is a mathematical existence/probability statement; **no new operational draw, explicit infinite mask or finite receipt is claimed**.

Fix once and for all 0<kappa<1. On all nonzero integral ideals choose independent I_a with

    p_a=(Na)^(-kappa),
    Utilde_eta,tau(x)=sum_a I_a (Na)^kappa mu_K(a)eta(a)
                                      g_tau(log(Na/x)). (R42.23)

The mask does not depend on a zero, x, a shell, eta, or an outcome. Coefficients have deterministic polynomial growth, so every realization defines the whole Gaussian field with its left tail and complex-log analyticity. Original coefficients and zero extensions are retained inside the explicit random multiplier. It is not multiplicative; no Euler product is assigned to its new coefficients.

Let E_eta=Utilde_eta,tau-U_eta,tau. Infinite versions of R42.22 follow by finite truncation and the Gaussian positive majorant. Ideal counting and a Gaussian square integral give, for X>=1,

    E ||E_eta||_[X,2X]^2
      =sum_a ((Na)^kappa-1)|mu_K(a)eta(a)|^2
                    integral_X^(2X)g_tau(log(Na/x))^2 dx/x
      <= C_(K,tau,kappa) X^(1+kappa).                 (R42.24)

For example summing in unit log bins bounds sum_a (Na)^kappa g_tau(log(Na/x))^2 by C x^(1+kappa) times a convergent Gaussian series. The constant needs no cancellation or proposed endpoint. This also proves convergence of the error in the probability/Hilbert norm; deterministic Gaussian bounds permit the displayed exchange.

Put h_kappa=(1+kappa)/2. For any e>h_kappa, Markov's inequality gives

    P(||E_eta||_[2^j,2^(j+1)]>2^(je))
          <=C 2^(-j(2e-1-kappa)).                   (R42.25)

The probabilities sum. The first Borel--Cantelli lemma, requiring no independence between shells, therefore gives almost surely ||E_eta||_[X,2X]=O_e(X^e) for all large dyadic X. Taking the countable intersection over rational positive losses gives every exponent h_kappa+epsilon for one realization. Gaussian left tails cover small x. Taking a further countable intersection over all fixed finite-order trivial-infinity characters, finite presented masks and prescribed widths preserves probability1. This supplies a common fixed mask for the original countable family, with target-dependent constants/thresholds; it supplies no conductor-uniform bounds.

The support is actually sparse. On the ideal norm shell[X,2X], expected retained count is at most C X^(1-kappa). If N_X is that count, independence gives E exp(N_X)<=exp((exp(1)-1)C X^(1-kappa)). Exponential Markov and summation over dyads show almost surely N_X=O(X^(1-kappa)). Thus the one mask has this support bound at every large dyad. Counting may include mu_K=0 ideals; removing them only reduces support. This is an asymptotic existence claim, not a finite computer validation of an infinite mask.

The exact zero return is now paid through the error, rather than inferred from unbiasedness. Mellin(E_eta) is holomorphic on Re s>h_kappa by R42.25 and its left tail. On an absolute line,

    Mellin(Utilde_eta,tau)(s)
       =exp(tau s^2/2)/L_K^S(s,eta)+Mellin(E_eta)(s).  (R42.26)

Consequently Utilde has the same reciprocal poles as the original field in that half-plane. If gamma>h_kappa and the **complete signed** Utilde norm is O_epsilon(X^(gamma+epsilon)) for every large dyad, the error with e<gamma and the triangle inequality give the original U gamma bound. Conversely an original gamma bound gives the sparse one. The Mellin formulation also directly proves the nonzero signal at all heights; no sparse Euler factor is invented. For the full family, the moment hypothesis must still be established separately for every fixed eta.

An exact near-target example is kappa=749/1000. The support exponent is251/1000=.251 and h_kappa=1749/2000=.8745. Choose e=8747/10000=.8747, strictly below gamma=2187/2500=.8748. The failure probability exponent in R42.25 is -1/2500, summable on dyads. A full signed sparse-field gamma estimate for each original fixed target would therefore give c=.1252, using the same Gaussian width and then D02 if desired. No such estimate is proved. The retained coefficients near norm X are amplified by X^.749, and R42.22 shows exactly why merely counting the sparse support or averaging its squared norm does not solve it. No faster algorithm, effective good mask, or canonical random choice is certified.

This develops the actual parked idea rather than discarding it after the variance objection. The probabilistic tools are standard; the source-specific common-mask, complete-error and zero-return contract is the bounded reviewer contribution. It neither contradicts W21/W38 nonmultiplicative counterexamples nor assumes those examples were multiplicative: here a calibrated approximation to the actual field is explicitly proved. Both old/new simultaneous use and any deterministic derandomization still require their actual coefficient/energy costs.

statement:
## 1. Exact analytic class and primary ingredient

Fix tau>0 and g_tau(v)=(2*pi*tau)^(-1/2) exp(-v^2/(2*tau)). Let a_n be arbitrary complex coefficients for which

    A_b := sum_(n>=1) |a_n| n^(-b) < infinity             (A1)

for one fixed real b. Set

    F(u)=sum_(n>=1) a_n g_tau(log n-u).

All applications below have b=2 available. The complete series, with its actual zeros/signs, is used throughout; no arithmetic labels or signed interactions are deleted. The same proof applies to an ideal sum with n replaced by its norm and A_b replaced by the absolute ideal Dirichlet series.

Use the Fourier convention hat h(t)=integral_R h(u)e^(-itu)du. Completing the square termwise gives h(u)=e^(-bu)F(u) in L1(R) intersect L-infinity(R), and absolute Fubini gives

    hat h(t)=exp(tau*(b+it)^2/2) sum_n a_n n^(-b-it),
    |hat h(t)| <= M exp(-tau*t^2/2), M=e^(tau*b^2/2)A_b.  (A2)

For example |h|<=g_tau(0)M and ||h||_1<=M. Thus this spectral envelope follows on the original absolutely convergent line. No zero-free reciprocal estimate, contour shift or improved Mertens bound is hidden in A2.

The only imported analytic inequality is Kovrijkine's quantitative Logvinenko--Sereda theorem, Theorem1 in *Some results related to the Logvinenko--Sereda theorem*, arXiv:math/0012186v1 (19 December2000), pages1--2; its p=infinity proof and explicit constants are on pages7--8: <https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0012186>. In the needed form, if E is (delta,a)-thick (every interval of length a meets E in measure at least delta*a), and a bounded function P has Fourier support in an interval of length B, then

    ||P||_infinity <= (C/delta)^[C(aB+1)] ||P||_(L-infinity(E)). (A3)

C is universal. More explicitly, the source's page8 gives the p=infinity lower bound (delta/100)^(33*a*B+1); its angular-frequency convention is consistent with the displayed Bernstein bound B/2 on page2. Thus one may use (100/delta)^(33*a*B+1) in A3. The asymptotic proof needs only the universal form. [private research revision]'s high-ceiling-discovery.md listed this paper as an observability comparison but did not use its theorem. W39 instead used single-interval Taylor/Remez interpolation and expressly did not claim its coefficient2 optimal. The present composition is distinct from that single-interval proof.

### 5.3 A growing-depth escape is a new quantitative obligation

Taking J>=K(x) kills r_J(n) for every n<=x. This is an exact finite identity, not a
proof that a FIXED source has a power bound. It changes the filter P_p^J with x,
and all constants in(12)-(18) depend on J. Even if those constants were free,
the proved exponent1-1/J tends to1: at J comparable to log x/loglog x the nominal
saving is only logarithmic. Thus the present proof does not meet any fixed target
gamma<1 through a growing-depth substitution.

A successful growing scheme could still exist. It would need a fixed-power estimate
uniform over its growing t/J range, the actual growth of every hyperbola/Euler-product
constant, and a moving-filter observation/return that retains P_p(s)^J and both
prime branches. The countable-bank and growing-order library contains relevant
return interfaces, but none supplies this missing arithmetic bound. No claim of
impossibility is made from the failure of the present coarse estimate.

statement:
## G152. A complete compensated small-divisor estimate and zero return

Fix an ordinary Dirichlet character chi modulo q, with all natural zeros,
and choose a fixed prime p not dividing q. Put Q=pq and use Dirichlet
convolution, with delta_m denoting the coefficient at m:

    a(n)=mu(n)chi(n),  h(n)=chi(n),  a*h=delta_1,
    q_p=delta_1-p chi(p)delta_p,
    b_p=q_p*h=chi(n)(1-p 1_(p|n)),
    c_p=q_p*a=a(n)-p chi(p)1_(p|n)a(n/p).

The Q-periodic b_p has mean zero. Indeed its complete sum is
p(1-chi(p)) sum_(r mod q)chi(r), zero by orthogonality or, for a
principal character, chi(p)=1. The unramified-prime hypothesis matters.
The changed c_p can be nonzero on squareful integers; retain these terms.
It has |c_p|<=p+1, and still vanishes on nonunits modulo q.

For fixed b>1 and integer k>2 define

    f_x(n)=exp(-n/x^b-i(n/x)^k),
    C_p(x)=sum_(n>=1)c_p(n)f_x(n),
    ||F||_j=(integral_X^(2X)|F(x)|^j dx/x)^(1/j), j=1,2.

All cutoffs depend on X, chi and fixed parameters, and are frozen before
real x varies. Use literal closed n<=U and strict n>U for real U.
The tempting identity f_x(pn)=f_(x/p)(n) is false when b>1.

With m_U=a 1_(n<=U), u_U=a-m_U, set

    S_(U,V)=m_U*m_V*b_p,  R_(U,V)=u_U*u_V*b_p.
    c_p=q_p*m_U+q_p*m_V-S_(U,V)+R_(U,V).        (91.1)

Every ordered factor pair and every cofactor remains. Each S or R
coefficient has absolute value <=p d_3(n)<<_(p,eta)n^eta, uniformly
in U,V. The two short terms cost O_p(U+V) in both shell norms.

### Full divisor-bounded tail

If |v_n|<=A_eta n^eta and 2eta<k-2, the complete tail satisfies

    ||sum_(n>M)v_n f_x(n)||_2^2
      <<_(b,k,eta) A_eta^2
          [X^(b(1+2eta))+X^k M^(2-k+2eta)].    (91.2)

Use a nonnegative C2 majorant equal to one on the original shell,
supported in [1/2,4], with flat endpoints. After v=u^(-k), the
off-diagonal amplitude and two derivatives are uniformly bounded:
powers of A=(n+m)/X^b are absorbed by exp(-cA). Two integrations by
parts give the kernel

    min(1,(X^k/|n^k-m^k|)^2).

For m<n, n^k-m^k>=n^(k-1)(n-m). Writing delta=X^k/n^(k-1), the
full sum over gaps of min(1,(delta/gap)^2) is O(delta), including
delta<1. Sum n^(2eta)delta over n>M; the damped diagonal supplies
the first term in (91.2). Finite expansions followed by summable
domination justify the infinite calculation. Both orientations and
every cross are included; no off-diagonal part is dropped.

For 1/2<gamma<1, b<=2gamma and

    r=(k-2gamma)/(k-2), M=X^r,

(91.2) gives an O(X^(gamma+epsilon)) tail in L2 and L1 for every
epsilon>0, choosing eta after epsilon. This includes b=2gamma.
The tail proof needs no r<b restriction; damping helps when r>=b.

### Completed small-divisor source

Assume u=k-(k-1)r=2gamma-r>0 and put eta_0=1/(100kpq).
For ANY real U,V>=1 with UV<=eta_0 X^u,

    ||sum_n S_(U,V)(n)f_x(n)||_1
      +||sum_n S_(U,V)(n)f_x(n)||_2
               <<_(p,q,b,k,gamma,epsilon) X^(gamma+epsilon). (91.3)

On n<=M, expand b_p in its nonzero Fourier modes j/Q. For D=de,
the phase as a function of the cofactor is

    F_j(t)=jt/Q-(Dt/x)^k/(2pi).

Since D<=UV and Dt<=M, its derivative correction is at most
k UV M^(k-1)/(2pi X^k)<=k eta_0/(2pi)<1/(2Q).
Thus F_j' and each discrete phase increment lie monotonically between
1/(2Q) and 1-1/(2Q). Summation by parts with
1/(exp(2pi i v)-1)=-1/2-(i/2)cot(pi v) bounds every prefix by O(Q).
Abel summation preserves that bound under the actual decreasing damping.
This includes empty and one-term prefixes. Summing all ordered d,e costs
O_(p,q)(UV)=O(X^u); u<gamma. The complete n>M contribution is (91.2).
No Fourier gap is asserted beyond M. Also U+V<=UV+1 pays the short
terms, uniformly in the asymmetric choices.

This is an actual unrestricted small-product estimate, not an arbitrary
coefficient model. It does NOT allow UV=X^gamma without a new argument.

### Complete core and all-height return

For b=3/2,k=6 and gamma>=3/4, set L=X^gamma and freeze
U=V=floor(sqrt(eta_0) X^(u/2)). For sufficiently large X these exceed
one. Define the full balanced core

    T_(p,chi,X)(x)=sum_(d>U,e>V,L<del<=M)
       mu(d)mu(e)chi(del)(1-p 1_(p|l))f_x(del).

Its low prefix costs O(X^(gamma+epsilon)) by the divisor bound; its
full tail, S and short terms are already paid. Consequently

    ||C_p-T_(p,chi,X)||_j << X^(gamma+epsilon), j=1,2.       (91.4)

Every-epsilon whole-shell bounds for T and C_p are equivalent separately
in L1 and L2. L2 is sufficient for L1; the converse is not inferred.

The G140 Mellin calculation applies to the bounded changed coefficients.
After v=nt and rotation by a fixed admissible angle alpha, it gives

    integral_0^infinity C_p(1/t)t^(s-1)dt
       =A_0(s)P_p(s)/L(s,chi)+E_p(s),
    A_0(s)=Gamma(s/6) exp(-i pi s/12)/6,
    P_p(s)=1-chi(p)p^(1-s),                              (91.5)

where E_p is holomorphic for Re s>1/2 and A_0 has no zero for Re s>0.
Initially the identity holds in an absolutely convergent right half-plane.
The rotated remainder is locally uniform at EVERY fixed height; constants
can depend on height and chi. At x down to zero,
|C_p(x)|<=(p+1)/(exp(x^(-b))-1). The hypothesized every-epsilon L1 shell
bound therefore makes the left side holomorphic on Re s>gamma.

Choose two distinct fixed unramified primes p1,p2. For a nonprincipal
character choose p1 with chi(p1)!=1: a unit with nontrivial character
value has a prime factor with nontrivial value. Each P_p zero has Re s=1.
A common zero 1+it with t!=0 would make both t log(p_j)/(2pi) nonzero
rationals, contradicting irrationality of log(p1)/log(p2). At t=0 the
chosen nonprincipal p1 prevents a common zero. For a principal character
the possible common point is its allowed L pole, not an ordinary zero.
Thus bounds for both fixed compensated cores exclude ALL ordinary zeros
with Re s>gamma. No line-one nonvanishing theorem is hidden in the return.
Actual imprimitive Euler holes stay present; their zeros lie on Re s=0.

More generally, for each fixed gamma>1/2 choose k large enough that u>0,
1<b<=2gamma, and fixed K with 1-(b-1)K<gamma. Retain ALL shifts
A_j(s)P_p(s+(b-1)j)/L(s+(b-1)j) in G140's K-term expansion.
Starting above Re s=1, finite-strip descent of width b-1 gives the same
return. No growing k,K, uniform limit gamma down to 1/2, or endpoint
theorem is claimed. This extends the previous conditional architecture;
its required arithmetic power premise remains open.
title: G152. A complete compensated small-divisor estimate and zero return

statement:
## 5. Strongest objection and what remains to be estimated

Empty common support is legal source geometry. It does not prove simultaneous saturation by actual high zeros, prime sums and witness polynomials. Nevertheless the scalar moment mechanism itself has a concrete extremizer, which explains why another application of its positive bounds cannot manufacture a uniform gain.

Fix delta,v, take q=delta and its optimal cutoff t*, short crossing r*,m*=t*-r*. Give an abstract positive class cardinality Z^(E-delta v), every slot squared amplitude Z^(delta z_i), and witnesses squared amplitudes Z^(delta r*) and Z^(delta m*). At the short crossing, the fully marked inverse norm and the optimally partially marked plain norm both have exponent exactly one. Every intermediate marking/amplification choice has an exponent at least those minima. This is a consistent scalar configuration for those inequalities; it is NOT an arithmetic construction.

For any other cutoff t<=t*, the same r*,m* is still allowed by r*<=1<=t and r*+m*>=t. For t>t*, the formal long configuration r=t,m=0 has weighted inverse exponent L(t)>=L(t*)=E. Thus optimizing t, all original slot subsets, those amplifications, and Hölder combinations of these positive moment inequalities cannot improve this particular one-witness envelope. Hölder averages cannot fall below the minimum of their input exponents. A simultaneous sequence of cutoffs, a true mixed moment or additional phase cancellation is not ruled out by this argument.

The common zero alone is not an independence hypothesis. The source deliberately constructs a saturated pair from one zero, with a common presentation and common height. Its original pointwise prime estimates permit large amplitudes of many slots in that presentation. Neither positivity nor the second-label count provides a new negative power; the label count has already been paid. Without a theorem controlling the intersection, claiming that the two witness events are independent would change the argument.

A concrete upstream target is a bound, uniform for the actual canonical family and dyads near the short crossing,

    sum_(high rows, |S_m|^2>=Z^(delta m-small)) |M_r Q|^2
          << Z^(W-sigma W+epsilon) (1+T)^J,             (OPEN-J)

with a positive sigma. An equivalent sufficient mixed estimate divides by the plain witness and seeks a saving over the pointwise price Z^(2delta m) times MI. It must keep the same witness label, natural holes, heights, profiles and signed source reconstruction. The inherited separate moments prove only sigma=0 here. A uniform neighborhood of a strict positive saving would allow the detector cutoff to rebalance against the long branch. No such estimate is established in this pass; no purported failure of actual arithmetic follows from the scalar extremizer.

The following improvement takes a different, completely licensed route. It does not purport to solve OPEN-J.

## 7. Protected audit W47-30: exact largest-prime renewal and the full covariance

This was chosen before author outcomes for high reach. Let (P^+(n)) be the largest prime factor and define
\[
 U_{<p}(z)=\sum_{P^+(m)<p}\mu(m)\chi(m)g_\tau(\log(m/z)),
\]
including m=1. Only squarefree products of primes below p contribute, so for each p this is a finite, possibly very large, exact sum. Unique largest-prime decomposition of every squarefree n>1 gives
\[
 U_\chi(x)=g_\tau(\log(1/x))-
                \sum_p\chi(p)U_{<p}(x/p). \tag{P1}
\]
Indeed n=pm, p=P⁺(n), p∤m, and μ(pm)χ(pm)=−χ(p)μ(m)χ(m). Natural zeros make the equality valid even at ramified primes. Absolute convergence of the original Gaussian sum justifies regrouping; no prime-independence assumption appears.

For (R_X=2X\exp(C\sqrt{\log X})), set (B_X(x)=\sum_{p\le R_X}\chi(p)U_{<p}(x/p)). An omitted largest prime implies n>R_X. Thus
\[
 U_\chi(x)=g_\tau(\log(1/x))-B_X(x)+E_X(x),\qquad
 \sup_{[X,2X]}|E_X|\le X^{1-C^2/(2\tau)+o(1)}. \tag{P2}
\]
The bounded-coefficient tail estimate follows by comparison with
$x\int_{C\sqrt{\log X}}^\infty e^v g_\tau(v)dv$, with a boundary term; the Gaussian exponent is decreasing there for large X. For $C=\sqrt{2\tau}$ this is $X^{o(1)}$, whereas the head term decays faster than every power. Consequently, for each γ>1/2 (indeed for any fixed positive γ), the every-shell norm bound for B_X is equivalent to R2 and returns through R3.

The exact norm target is the **entire** covariance
\[
 \|B_X\|_2^2=
 \sum_{p,q\le R_X}\chi(p)\overline{\chi(q)}
 \langle U_{<p}(x/p),U_{<q}(x/q)\rangle_{[X,2X]}. \tag{P3}
\]
All diagonal and off-diagonal terms are present. Conditioning on the largest prime has not centered or eliminated its future response. If an accepted buffered baseline (\|U\|_2\ll X^\beta), β<1, is used, P2 also gives an energy comparison error (O(X^{\beta+o(1)})), including the complete cross terms. This is below (X^{2\gamma}) for γ>1/2. The simpler norm comparison does not require that baseline.

There is a precise obstruction to one strong interpretation of “faithful small state.” For r fixed unramified primes, all (2^r) functions
\[
 \mu(n_S)\chi(n_S)g_\tau(\log n_S-y)
 =c_Sg_\tau(y)e^{(\log n_S)y/\tau},\qquad c_S\ne0,
\]
are linearly independent on every real interval. The numbers log n_S are distinct; successive derivatives give a Vandermonde determinant. Hence an exact **linear** state/readout preserving arbitrary combinations of every prime-subset history must have dimension at least (2^r). This is not a lower bound for a single fixed arithmetic sum, nonlinear compression or a source-specific approximate covariance closure. W41/G53's coefficient Hankel rank two does not contradict this physical Gaussian-readout statement.

Disposition: **new bounded audit development, promising but unbridged**. P1--P3 pay the exact source return and expose the missing signed covariance. They do not estimate it. Credit the existing renewal/fugacity state program, G53/G54's physical-response distinctions and the [private research revision] complete covariance work. The priority idea survives as a concrete arithmetic question; no generic martingale or state-count heuristic is accepted as its answer.

## HCR2. Fixed-strength identity and moving-strength definition

For h>=0 and v>0 set

    B_h(v)=sqrt(h/v)*J_1(2*sqrt(hv)).

Its continuous endpoint value is B_h(0)=h. The Bessel power series gives

    B_h(v)=sum_(k>=0) (-1)^k h^(k+1)v^k/(k!*(k+1)!).

For Re p>0 the sum of the absolute term integrals is
exp(h/Re p)-1. Hence

    integral_0^infinity exp(-pv) B_h(v) dv = 1-exp(-h/p).

This checks B0, including its sign. The atom delta_0 has full unit mass
on the half-line, so the multiplier of delta_0-exp(-v)B_h(v)dv is
exp(-h/(1-s)), Re s<1. It is nonvanishing on that half-plane and has an
essential singularity at s=1; it is not an entire multiplier.

The source's real-argument estimates |J_1(z)|<=1 and |J_1(z)|<=|z|/2 follow
from the integral representations for J_n and J_1. I checked the power
series and the relevant integral identities against [NIST DLMF 10.2.2](https://dlmf.nist.gov/10.2#E2)
and [DLMF 10.9.2, 10.9.4](https://dlmf.nist.gov/10.9). In particular
|B_h(v)|<=h for all v>=0, as used in the actual-field bounds.

Now fix A>0, independent of u, and define for u>=0

    D_A f(u)=f(u)-integral_0^infinity exp(-v) B_(Au)(v) f(u+v) dv.

At u=0 the integral is zero. If b_*<b<1 is fixed, then

    |D_A f(u)| <= C_b exp(bu)*(1+Au/(1-b)).                 (HCR2.1)

Thus the signed full field defines an absolutely convergent v-integral.
The later arithmetic expansion over n must respect how this definition
was obtained; it does not authorize absolute double summation over the
entire future v-range.

Putting h=Au into the fixed-h identity is legitimate at a FIXED u when
acting on an exponential. It does not turn D_A into a fixed convolution
operator or give its one-sided Laplace transform by multiplication. For
example, applying D_A to f(u-c) uses strength Au, whereas shifting
D_A f by c uses A(u-c). Those operators do not generally commute. This
also prevents automatic import of the previous fixed-Gaussian coprime
convolution equivalence. The author's separate return calculation below
is necessary and supplies the missing bridge.
title: HCR2. Fixed-strength identity and moving-strength definition

## 7. Primary sources, novelty boundaries and dispositions

The new outside source inspected is Kaisa Matomäki and Joni Teräväinen,
*On the Möbius function in all short intervals*, JEMS25(2023),1207–1225,
DOI10.4171/JEMS/1205, [published primary PDF](https://ems.press/content/serial-article-files/32826?nt=1).
Theorem1.1 (printed1208) has fixed theta>.55 and only a logarithmic
relative error H/(log x)^(1/3-epsilon). Theorem1.5 (printed1209) is
uniform in linear twist alpha for fixed theta>3/5, with the same type
of error. Lemma3.1 (printed1212) extracts a small prime with an explicit
H*log(P)/log(Q) error and size/support conditions; its square-divisibility
correction is paid in the proof. These exact statements were inspected
in primary web text, with the v2 arXiv text used to disambiguate OCR.
They motivate the separate extraction candidate but do not supply a
power bound for our two-long-variable sum. Summing their logarithmic
errors across an X-length transition still leaves exponent1. No claim
of a general character-twisted extension from those statements is used.

For (6.2) the only prime-distribution input is the ordinary prime number
theorem, with fixed-proportion intervals obtained by partial summation.
Its primary proof is Atle Selberg, *An Elementary Proof of the Prime-Number
Theorem*, Annals50(1949),305–313, [original article scan](https://www.math.lsu.edu/~mahlburg/teaching/handouts/2014-7230/Selberg-ElemPNT1949.pdf),
equation(1.1), printed305. No prime-in-short-interval or progression
uniformity is needed: deleting primes dividing one fixed q is finite.
The source is used for an obstruction to a separated budget, not for
an unproved Möbius cancellation estimate.

Local sources and exact SHA256 pins are in checks.json. The FULL accepted
nonlinear author/review and integration underpin the new source; this
pass independently rederived the character completion and new estimates.
The old Gaussian identity is R35.2 in
[restricted mathematical source] whose first108 lines were read here.
Its growing-derivative Gaussian argument R35.3–R35.7 already pays a
much larger small-divisor square for a DIFFERENT kernel. It cannot be
transferred to exp(-n/x^b-i(n/x)^k) merely by matching exponents: the
new kernel has actual discrete stationary frequencies in its long tail.
Conversely, this report does not improve that old Gaussian lemma or
claim priority for mean-zero completion itself.

What is newly established for the live nonlinear source is the combination:

* a full divisor-bounded tail estimate uniform in the changing original
  truncations, including every paired label;
* an unconditional completed small-divisor source estimate with product
  cutoff exponent u=2gamma-r and full norm O(X^(gamma+epsilon)), with
  the failing discrete-frequency region paid;
* a finite two-prime numerator bank and a complete signed two-long-factor
  input, including the principal boundary and all finite heights;
* an actual positive prime-pair component of that exact remaining source,
  identifying a specific coupling that the next estimate must preserve.

The first two points are useful source restrictions, not a solved full
moment. The finite return is conditional on OPEN-T; its equivalence to
the complete compensated norm does not make the arithmetic premise free.
The prime-pair obstruction retires only estimates that pay its norm
separately. It neither retires the architecture nor establishes a lower
bound for the actual full signed source.

Disposition of the four discovery candidates: logarithmic prime
convolution remains open at its signed prime-discrepancy input; the
growing phase bank has unpaid restoration/normalization and was not
developed into a theorem; multiplicative extraction remains eligible
but the inspected published log estimates miss the power budget; the
selected completion earns the restricted theorem above and a concrete
failed coarse test, with no numerical gain. All29 original families,
109 children and other valid components are retained, not silently
replaced or classified as disproved.

The strongest remaining objection is substantive: near n~X the phase
does not force power cancellation of the actual Möbius factors, and the
prime-pair cell proves that some truly signed cross-cell estimate is
necessary. The next credible development is a coupled evaluation of
that cell and its cofactor/composite compensators using exact convolution
or a source-specific bilinear input. A further tail refinement alone
would not address the remaining term and is not proposed as a new pass.

# [private research revision]: smooth and block detector transfers with explicit residuals

The controller fully read the [Sol High author](sol-post52-02/report.md),
[shared Sol High review](sol-post52-02-sol-review/report.md) and
[independent Astra review](sol-post52-02-astra-review/report.md). The exact
results below are accepted. No complete arithmetic exponent or increase
beyond written c6=.125139 is proved. The original60 cards, ten first tests,
three developments and both reviewers' pre-outcome audit evidence are retained.

One frozen Sol-review sentence uses 2gamma for a norm exponent. The correct
statement is norm exponent gamma, squared-norm exponent2gamma. This
integration corrects that notation without altering the historical report.

## [restricted research revision]-S1. Smooth collars preserve the literal four-diagonal problem

Use the exact G11--20 four-diagonal source, original mu/eta coefficients,
tau=1, kappa_C=D=2, a=.75 and Y=X^.495. Replace each sharp interval by
a smooth interior taper with collar width X^-delta, retaining both endpoint
atoms in its difference from the sharp interval. If U is the original bin,
V its tapered version and Delta=U-V, then

    UU-VV=Delta U+U Delta-Delta Delta.

The complete Gaussian-field norm of this difference has exponent

    q=max(.505+.495 beta-delta,1-2delta),

under the exact summatory input of the source proof. With the conservative
historical beta=.8749, delta=.064 gives q=.8740755. Thus any complete
tapered-field norm exponent gamma>q transfers to the original field, and
conversely. At gamma=.87449 the transfer has margin.0004145. For more
ambitious targets, delta=.106 gives q=.8320755<5/6, and delta=.19 gives
q=.7480755<3/4.

This is a complete moving-taper representation theorem. Derivatives of orderk
cost X^(k delta), so an analytic estimate using the taper must pay them.
Restore the original fixed detector before using Mellin/pole arguments;
the moving family is not silently one fixed Dirichlet series. The full
signed smooth moment is open. This result is in the stated zeta scope;
it does not establish a new Hecke or all-character estimate.

## [restricted research revision]-S2. Grouping every coefficient into blocks has a paid full-field error

For a fixed bounded sequence |a(n)|<=1, let
b_B(j)=sum_((j-1)B<n<=jB)a(n), and define

    V_B(x)=sum_(j>=1)b_B(j)g_tau(log(jB/x)).

The total variation of the Gaussian kernel on the positive real line is
2g_tau(0), so summing the blockwise displacement yields, for everyx,

    |F_a(x)-V_B(x)|<=2B g_tau(0).

All blocks, endpoints and both infinite tails are included. Taking
B_X=floor(X^theta) fixed within each shell, theta<gamma makes the complete
shell norm powergamma equivalent for F_a and V_(B_X). Block amplitudes
remain their actual sums and can be as large asB; the transfer supplies no
cancellation by itself.

For the literal f3 source, the two-point block is exactly

    b_2(j)=f3(2j-1)+(1-2*1_(2 does not divide j))f3(j).

For every fixed ordinary character, use the actual products f3(n)chi(n)
with their ramified zeros. For a fixedB, define

    E_B(s)=sum_n a(n)[n^-s-(B ceil(n/B))^-s].

The series is holomorphic in Re(s)>0, locally uniformly, and the block
Dirichlet series satisfies D_B=D_a-E_B. Thus it preserves poles and
principal parts in that half-plane. For actual f3 chi, D_a=W_chi/L(s,chi)
with W_chi nonzero in1/2<Re(s)<1; the proof retains the p=2 numerator
zeros on Re(s)=1, the p=3 denominator and every ramified factor. No
Eisenstein return is inferred. MovingB first returns to the fixed original
field by the uniform error; it is not inserted into this fixed-series identity.

The nearby two-point Gaussian Gram also has a Schur pivot of order n^-2
and condition number of order n^2. Whitening can amplify error by ordern.
This is a conditioning calculation, not a source-specific lower bound on
the f3 field or on nativeH.

## [restricted research revision]-S3. The determinant repair keeps the original hard energy

For a positive definite finite Gram M, the determinant lemma gives

    det(M+lambda cc*)/det(M)=1+lambda c*M^-1 c.

This is dual energy, not the desired primal energy c*Mc. Replacing c by
v=Mc repairs the identity to1+lambda c*Mc, so it keeps the entire original
moment obligation. Infinite limits also owe conditioning and tails. This
rules out the proposed shortcut, not every determinant architecture.

The seven other first tests preserve their exact failure scopes, including
unitary gauges, the proposed log2/log3 resultant, convolution-inverse
uniqueness, mu versus mu chi, trace-zero commutators with nonzero quadratic
form, and unjustified algebraicity at general complexs. The reports retain
each tested identity and broader variants that were not tested.

## [restricted research revision]-S4. A very small changed detector can erase the needed poles

The first review's protected auditS29 develops a changed additive source
c(n)=sum_(j=0)^r(-1)^j binom(r,j)a(n-jh), with fixed positive integersh,r
and the specified zero extension. All boundary terms are included. Its
complete Gaussian field is O(x^(1-r)), but its Dirichlet series is
holomorphic in Re(s)>1-r. For the actual mu chi source the expansion uses
reciprocals L(s+k,chi)^-1 only fork>=r: the original critical-strip poles
have disappeared. This diagnoses that additive construction. The original
multiplicative logarithmic S29 proposal is a different, unrefuted object.

## [restricted research revision]-S5. Two literal native JN contracts

The first review's uniform auditS52 retains both actual projectors and
natural Fourier zeros. Let q,q' be comparable toN, Q=qq', and use the
Q^2-point group with squared norm1/Q. A row-frequency set of sizeJ captures
at most CKJ/Q of the energy; the removed natural-zero contribution is at
most

    kappa=C[K(q+q'-1)/Q+L/q+L/q'].

At N=K Z^.003 this can be small. Norm-faithful capture requires
J comparable to Q/K; J=O(N) captures only O(Z^(-.003)). This obstructs
that proposed sparse norm compression. A dense adapted direction or a
scalar signedH estimate is not ruled out.

The independent Astra uniform auditS26 computes the actual simultaneous
negation of (h,s,s') in the JN kernel. Its eigenvalue is

    epsilon=(-1)^((q-1)/6+(q'-1)/6),

not uniformly-1. For example,13/19 has sign- and19/31 has sign+.
If T is simultaneous negation and R_epsilon f=(f+epsilon f composed T)/2,
then exactly

    sum K W_hat = sum K Fourier(R_epsilon W).

There is no extra conductor factor, root multiplicity or density credit.
Reflect the entire zero-extended source, including its ray and every mask;
any unmatched support stays in the residual. Contractivity alone gives no
power saving. The complete original signed prime-pair weights, rawH target,
normalization and all complementary branches still have to be bounded.
The finite407930-triple check supports the explicit algebra, not an
asymptotic estimate. This refines JN22--25.

## [restricted research revision]-S6. A finite signed Gaussian quadrature certificate

The independent protected auditS31 supplies a rigorous finite interface
for the actual source f3 chi. It is not an executed solver or an infinite
stream of certificates. For fixedtau, put ell=log2 and
K_tau=exp(tau)/sqrt(tau)+2/tau. On the shell,

    |d_y F(exp y)|<=2K_tau X.

A left-grid rule with N intervals has full L2(dx/x) error at most
2K_tau ell^(3/2)X/N. With R=ceil(2X exp(C sqrt(log X))), the upper tail is
at most

    T_X=2X exp(tau/2) tau/(C sqrt(log X)-tau)

statement:
## 2. Weighted coherent mass

Work first on the coherent primes using PC6:
\[
\begin{gathered}
c=gu,\quad c'=gv,\qquad n=hys^2,\quad n'=hxt^2,\\
a=d_0u x^3r_1^6,\qquad b=d_0v y^3r_2^6,\qquad
x\mid e,\ y\mid d.
\end{gathered} \tag{HC7}
\]
Retain every local support restriction before taking a positive majorant. Split \(d_0\) canonically as \(d_0=d_\circ f^6\): at a prime whose positive \(d_0\)-valuation is divisible by six, place its entire power in \(f^6\); place every other positive valuation in \(d_\circ\). In particular \((d_\circ,f)=1\). On the surviving coherent support,
\[
\boxed{B(a)B(b)=
\frac{q_{d_0}}{q_{\operatorname{rad}(d_\circ)}}
(q_{r_1}q_{r_2})^3q_xq_y.} \tag{HC8}
\]

The local justification includes the unequal embeddings:

- Away from \(de\), a prime dividing \(AA'\) forces unit \(r\) and outer exponents zero or one. A residual core incidence \(u\) or \(v\) cannot overlap \(d_0\) or a residual sixth power. Its \(B\)-factor is one.
- Away from \(AA'de\), coherence gives \(\alpha\equiv\beta\pmod6\). A common exponent \(j>0\) contributes \(q^{j-1}\) when \(6\nmid j\), and \(q^j\) when \(6\mid j\). Each residual sixth power contributes its cube to \(B(a)B(b)\), exactly as in HC8. Zero common exponent also has the stated factor.
- At \(p\mid e\), natural zeros require \(A\) to be a unit. If \(p\mid A'\), the unit row restricts outer exponents to \(\alpha\in\{0,3\}\), \(\beta\in\{0,1\}\). The coherent exponent-three case is precisely \(p\mid x\), contributing \(q_p\); \(d_0\) and residual sixth powers cannot overlap it. The case \(p\mid d\) is symmetric and contributes \(q_y\).
- At an embedding-only prime, coherent nonprincipal positive outer exponents would require both \(\alpha-\beta=\pm2\) and \(\alpha\equiv\beta\pmod6\); they cannot survive. Principal multiples of six remain covered by HC8.

This preserves the exponent-three embedding exception rather than imposing a squarefree outer restriction.

Temporarily write \(U=Y_D,V=Y_E\). The completed coefficient remains
\[
(q_g\sqrt{q_uq_v}\,q_h^2q_xq_yq_s^2q_t^2)^{-1}.
\]
The outer annuli give the original PC7 count
\[
\sum_{u,v}(q_uq_v)^{-1/2}
\ll\frac{\sqrt{UV}}
{q_{d_0}(q_xq_y)^{3/2}(q_{r_1}q_{r_2})^3}.
\]
After multiplying HC8, the remaining factors involving \(d_0,x,y,r_i\) are
\[
\frac{\sqrt{UV}}
{q_{\operatorname{rad}(d_\circ)}(q_xq_y)^{3/2}}. \tag{HC9}
\]
The sixth-power factors have not disappeared: their number must now be counted. Since \(u,v\) are nonzero ideals, the outer supports imply
\[
q_fq_{r_1}\ll\left(\frac{U}{q_{d_\circ}q_x^3}\right)^{1/6},
\qquad
q_fq_{r_2}\ll\left(\frac{V}{q_{d_\circ}q_y^3}\right)^{1/6}.
\]
Ideal counting and the convergent \(f\)-sum give
\[
\sum_{f,r_1,r_2}1
\ll(UV)^{1/6}q_{d_\circ}^{-1/3}(q_xq_y)^{-1/2}
\sum_fq_f^{-2}
\ll(UV)^{1/6}q_{d_\circ}^{-1/3}(q_xq_y)^{-1/2}. \tag{HC10}
\]
Dropping coprimality restrictions is harmless in this positive count. The remaining \(d_\circ\)-sum converges:
\[
\sum_{d_\circ}\frac1{q_{\operatorname{rad}(d_\circ)}q_{d_\circ}^{1/3}}
\le\prod_{p\notin S}\left(1+\sum_{j\ge1}q_p^{-1-j/3}\right)
<\infty. \tag{HC11}
\]
The \(x,y\) exponents have become two; the \(h,s,t\) exponents remain two.

As in PC8, sum the harmonic common-core variable \(g\) against the two original rapid envelopes before discarding their dependence. Its sum is uniform in both scales. Thus it can precede the displayed positive outer counts. The actual \(K_D,K_E\) marks remain bounded by T06's divisor envelope, with no extra slot count. Small powers of arbitrarily large completed columns are absorbed into the original two-sided rapid envelopes. All infinite cube tails and the unit ideal remain included. Consequently
\[
\boxed{\mathscr M_{\rm coh}^{B}(U,V)
\ll_\epsilon Z^\epsilon(UV)^{2/3}.} \tag{HC12}
\]

statement:
### A1. Fixed detector and the seed's unnecessary desmoothing loss

For a fixed ordinary Dirichlet character chi modulo q, including q=1, put a(n)=mu(n)chi(n), with chi zero on nonunits. Define

    M_chi(t)=sum_(n<=t) a(n),
    E_chi(x)=sum_(n>=1) a(n) exp(-n/x),       x>0,
    R_r(N)=sum_(n<=N) a(n)(1-n/N)^r,         r>0.

The endpoint n=N has weight0. These are the full coefficients, without a favourable sector or hidden coprimality change. Absolute Fubini for Re(s)>1 gives

    int_0^infty E_chi(x)x^(-s) dx/x = Gamma(s)/L(s,chi),
    int_0^infty R_r(N)N^(-s) dN/N
        = Gamma(s)Gamma(r+1)/[Gamma(s+r+1)L(s,chi)].       (A1)

For fixed r the multiplier in the second line is nonzero when Re(s)>0. Thus an every-dyadic L2(dx/x) exponent gamma>0 for either fixed field directly excludes zeros in Re(s)>gamma. Sharp recovery of M_chi is unnecessary. This is standard Mellin/Riesz ancestry, including [restricted research revision]-C1 and Sol04-D12, not new detector credit. The Beta integral and nonvanishing of Gamma are recorded in [DLMF5.12](https://dlmf.nist.gov/5.12) and [DLMF5.2](https://dlmf.nist.gov/5.2); the coefficient identities above are derived here by n/x substitution.

For completeness, if ||E_chi||_[X,2X] <<_(chi,epsilon) X^(gamma+epsilon) on every sufficiently large dyadic X, Cauchy-Schwarz and dyadic summation make its Mellin integral holomorphic for Re(s)>gamma, with all logarithmic derivatives. Near0 the absolute geometric sum is O(exp(-1/x)). Identity continuation gives L(s,chi)H(s)=Gamma(s). At an L-zero in that half-plane the left side vanishes and the right side does not. The pole of a principal L at1 is treated meromorphically; it is not a zero. This proof treats every fixed character separately, with constants allowed to depend on q and chi, and makes no growing-conductor assertion.

The open issue becomes quantitative when r grows: (A1) is not the Mellin transform of a field whose r varies with the physical shell. The following comparison restores a single fixed field first.
title: A1. Fixed detector and the seed's unnecessary desmoothing loss

statement:
## 1. Sharp dimension-free lemma

Let H be any real Hilbert space, T:H->R^2 bounded real-linear, ||T||=L,
and v_a a finite family. Put y_a=T v_a, M=sum_a|y_a| and
B=sum_(a,b)|<v_a,v_b>|, retaining every ordered pair. Then

    L^2 B >= M^2/2.                                      (1)

If all y_a lie on one real line, the constant improves to1. Cases L=0
or M=0 are immediate. The constant1/2 is optimal for the general lemma:
take H=R^2,T=Id,v_1=(1,0),v_2=(0,1). Then L=1,B=2,M=2.

Proof. Set u_a=y_a/|y_a| when y_a!=0 and u_a=0 otherwise. Define the
finite-rank operator A:R^2->H by A z=sum_a <u_a,z>v_a. Exactly,

    ||A||_HS^2=sum_(a,b)<v_a,v_b><u_a,u_b> <= B,
    T A=sum_a |y_a|u_a u_a^T.

The last matrix is positive2x2 with trace M. Thus

    M^2/2 <= ||TA||_HS^2 <= L^2||A||_HS^2 <= L^2 B.

This uses a common readout on the WHOLE family. It does not use the
false termwise inequality |<Tv_a,Tv_b>|<=L^2|<v_a,v_b>|. For collinear
images the same proof in a one-dimensional target gives M^2. Equivalently
choose the common real direction and sum its recovery-aligned real signs.
For a target R^r the same argument gives M^2/r; it depends on output
dimension, not the dimension of H. The r orthonormal output example
shows that constant is sharp. Only r=2 (or1) is needed here.

The draft's circle-average proof also works exactly as written and
proves its weaker4/pi^2. Preserve it as the historical derivation;
the Hilbert-Schmidt argument above supplies the sharper replacement.

For a countable family, apply(1) to every finite subset. Its nonnegative
absolute Gram sums and sum|y_a| then give the extended inequality. No
assertion about the infinite vector sum is required for this lower bound.
If B is infinite, that particular positive certificate is already infinite.
If a proof uses finite B to reconstruct a full vector sum, the tail bound
||sum_(a in F)v_a||^2<=sum_(a,b in F)|<v_a,v_b>| makes the net of finite
partial sums unconditionally Cauchy. This is a separate consequence, not
an assumption hidden in the lower-bound argument.

The common-readout condition is essential. In H=R^n take v_i=e_i and
let T_i(h)=h_i in a real output line. Each separate map has norm1 and
y_i=1, while B=n and M=n. There is no dimension-free conclusion using
those separate unit costs. The common map h->sum_i h_i has norm sqrt(n)
and pays exactly the missing factor. A changing lift/readout rescaling
likewise cannot remove its actual operator norm.
title: 1. Sharp dimension-free lemma

## 3. Column bound with both original tails

Let `E_N(u)=min(1,u^(-N))`. From (DC6), uniformly in `q_ell,q_r>=1`,
\[
q_r\left|S_z^-\!\left(\frac{X_c}{q_\ell q_r}\right)\right|
\ll_N(1+|\Im z|)^A\frac{X_c}{q_\ell}E_N(q_c/D).
\tag{DC8}
\]
For `q_c<=D`, use the global consequence `|S(u)|<<u`. For `q_c>D`,
the argument is at most `X_c<1`; choosing a small-scale exponent
`3N+1` in (DC6) gives the additional factor `X_c^(3N)`.

Norm-dyadic ideal counting gives, for any fixed `A>2`,
\[
\sum_\ell q_\ell\left|S_z^+\!\left(\frac{Y}{q_\ell}\right)\right|
\ll_A(1+|\Im z|)^{C_A}
\begin{cases}
Y^2,&Y\ge1,\\
Y^A,&Y<1.
\end{cases}
\tag{DC9}
\]
For `Y>=1`, split at `q_ell=Y`; both geometric tails are `O(Y^2)`.
For `Y<1`, use `Y^A sum_ell q_ell^(1-A)`.

Insert (DC8), sum the second factor by (DC9), and retain its divisor
norm. This proves
\[
\begin{aligned}
|T_{c,e}(z)|
&\ll_N(1+|\Im z|)^A X_cY_e^2\tau(e)
 \sum_{s\mid c}q_s^{-1}E_N(q_c/D)E_N(q_e/D)\\
&\ll_{N,\epsilon}(1+|\Im z|)^A
Dq_c^{-1/3}q_e^{-2/3}(q_cq_e)^\epsilon
E_N(q_c/D)E_N(q_e/D).
\end{aligned}
\tag{DC10}
\]
Thus the first moving deletion costs `tau(e)` and the second costs
`sum_(s|c) q_s^(-1)`. A moving conductor has not been hidden inside a
fixed angular continuation estimate. The symmetric bound follows by
interchanging the two columns. Both unbounded core/profile tails are
explicit in (DC10).
title: 3. Column bound with both original tails

## 1. A fixed detector with a complete zero-exclusion return

Fix tau>0 once, independently of all large parameters, and set

    g_tau(v)=(2*pi*tau)^(-1/2) exp(-v^2/(2*tau)),

      =exp(tau*s^2/2)*(1-2^(1-s))/zeta(s).                 (G2)

boundary completes the usual zero-free conclusion. The numerator's

Consequently **any proved gamma<1-c11=.8748540364 gives a further improvement**. The

Nearer targets, gamma=5/6 and gamma=3/4 remain worthwhile. Nothing below

changed with X does not automatically inherit G2's single holomorphic

### 1.4 Unordered primes, both Stieltjes replacements, and density

After r<=R, replace p<q by half the ordered sum and subtract half
the p=q sum. Even with all cores, its absolute value is bounded using
(R0.1) by

    sum_(p>z)sum_r g(log(rp^2/x))
       <= C_tau x sum_(p>z)p^(-2)<=C_tau X/z.          (R1.9)

Thus no square-prime coefficient is misidentified as a two-distinct-
prime coefficient.

For y=x/r, fixed p>z, and a chosen fixed N, Stieltjes integration by
parts with the PNT error gives

    |sum_(q>z)g(log(pq/y))
       -integral_z^infinity g(log(pv/y))dv/log v|
      <= C_(tau,N) (y/p)L^(-N) H_1(log(pz/y)),
    H_1(a)=exp(a)g(a)+integral_a^infinity exp(w)|g'(w)|dw. (R1.10)

This includes the endpoint -[pi(z)-li(z)]g(log(pz/y)); it has the
correct convention even if z itself is prime. The endpoint at infinity
vanishes. Log v>=rho_0 L throughout; no upper cap is being smuggled in.

H_1 is bounded on the negative half-line and rapidly decreasing on the
positive half-line. The integer harmonic majorant therefore gives

    sum_(p>z)p^(-1)H_1(log(pz/y))
       <= C[1+log_+(y/z^2)]<=C L.

The first prime replacement costs O_N(y L^(1-N)). For the second,
exchange the positive q-integral and the p-sum and apply the same
one-variable error estimate inside that integral. The remaining
integral is

    integral_z^infinity H_1(log(vz/y))dv/(v log v),

which is also O(L), and in fact the factor 1/log v gives a stronger
bound here. This proves the same stated error for the second
replacement. There is no omitted error-product term: these are two
sequential exact replacements with their respective errors bounded.
Summing absolute errors over r<=R introduces only sum 1/r=O(L).
N=8 consequently pays both by O(X/L^6).

Write t=log z=rho L and define the NONNEGATIVE density

    phi_t(A)=A^(-1)log((A-t)/t),  A>2t,
    phi_t(A)=0,                  A<=2t.

The exact unordered continuous density follows from

    (1/2)integral_t^(A-t) ds/[s(A-s)]
       =A^(-1)log((A-t)/t).

With w=log(pq/y), the Jacobian is y exp(w). Combining all preceding
errors, the actual source is

    R_z(x)=x integral_R exp(w)g(w)
        sum_(r<=R) f(r)/r phi_t(log x+w-log r)dw
       +O(X^(1-eta)L+X/z+X/L^6)+O_A(X^-A).            (R1.11)

This establishes the constant 1 in front of phi_t; a second factor 2
must not be inserted after the unordered density calculation.
