# [private research revision]: the actual Möbius core moment

9 October 2026. Derived by `c20_cubic`; **independently reviewed by `c20_short_h` within the stated inputs and scopes.** This records the complete BC1--BC18 packet and extends the accepted DC packet. No larger zero-free constant follows; the accepted value remains `c0 = 0.125113352960035869...`.

Independent review receipt: `c20_short_h` accepted the BC record within its stated input, conditional and restricted scopes. Reviewed source SHA-256: `bd30c4ee717d3abd6001d72be1c115d5c420ddfcd1006f32f90961a3c68c41cb`.

The earlier [small-core packet](../[private research revision]/cubic-small-cores.md) and its source proofs remain inputs.

## Inputs and exact scope

Write `M` for [the merged manuscript](../../zeta_zero_free_validated_merged.md),
`b0=1-c0`, and `q_a=Na`. Good ideal labels occur once via their primary
generators and avoid the fixed set `S`. Rows include all nonzero
Eisenstein integers, their six units, and all fixed-prime valuations.

The input hypotheses are:

1. M (2.14)--(2.15), with its original source coefficient, radial row
   kernel, common column profile, natural zeros, and total-column
   coprimality. The fixed original profile `W0` and its required Euler
   derivatives decrease rapidly at both endpoints. Its prescribed
   Mellin roots are retained.
2. The fixed angular Hecke continuation and polynomial fixed-strip
   growth in [private research revision] T01, and the resulting CS8 endpoint estimate,
   including each fixed number of Euler derivatives. The angular
   character has nonzero infinity type. It is not one of the moving
   finite-order characters below.
3. The ordinary finite-order row functional equation and the exact
   Gauss root-number cancellation in review-cycle-9, section 1. These
   are used with the full row L-function, not its S-deleted version.
4. **I-HECKE:** the explicitly inherited all-finite-order Hecke package
   on every fixed buffered line `Re s>b0`, including subpower
   conductor/height bounds for reciprocal L-functions and the stated
   finite-deletion conventions. This is stronger than I-ZETA. The new
   Möbius cancellation below does not follow from ordinary Hecke
   convexity or Riemann-zeta nonvanishing alone.

Take `D,K>=1`, fixed `B>0`, and `K<=D^B`. Every positive loss is
arbitrarily small. All preliminary losses and every positive contour
margin are fixed before varying the scales; there is no assertion of
uniform constants as a contour tends to zero. Constants may depend on
the buffered lines, the prescribed fixed component family, and finitely
many original-profile seminorms.

The exact columns are `N1=c B1^3`, `N2=e B2^3`, with squarefree cores
`c,e`. Their source coefficients are
\[
\mathcal C_k(cB_1^3)=\beta(c)\vartheta_c(k)\xi(B_1)q_{B_1},
\qquad \beta(c)=\mu(c)\overline{\mathfrak G(c)},\quad |\beta(c)|=1.
\]
There is no extra `(B1,k)` or `(B2,k)` nonunit mask. Total-column
coprimality is exactly
\[
(c,e)=(c,B_2)=(e,B_1)=(B_1,B_2)=1.
\]
Own-column core/cube overlap remains allowed. The sector in this packet
has `c,e>1`. Previously paid unit-core sectors are only restored in the
final residual; they are not re-proved here.

## 1. Candidate result and numerical budget

Let `Q_min<=C` denote the original C--C form restricted to
`c,e>1` and `min(q_c,q_e)<=C`. The candidate estimate is
\[
\boxed{
|\mathfrak Q_{\min(q_c,q_e)\le C,\ c,e>1}|
\ll_{b,\epsilon,B}
D^{7/6+2b/3+\epsilon}C^{4b/3-1/6},
\quad 1\le C\le D,\quad b_0<b<1.
}
\tag{BC1}
\]
This includes both orientations, all mixed terms, the unrestricted
opposite core and its upper tail, and the original column/row profiles.
In particular,
\[
b=\frac78:\qquad |\mathfrak Q_{\min\le C}|
\ll D^{7/4+\epsilon}C.
\tag{BC2}
\]
Thus the complete band `C=D^(1/4)` is affordable. The fixed admissible
buffer `b=.8749` gives
\[
|\mathfrak Q_{\min\le D^{1/4}}|
\ll D^{1.9999+\epsilon}.
\tag{BC3}
\]
The limiting affordable cutoff is
\[
\boxed{
\gamma_{**}=\frac{5-4b_0}{8b_0-1}
=\frac{1+4c_0}{7-8c_0}
=.2501133700944836\ldots .
}
\tag{BC4}
\]
The endpoint-looking statement chooses `b>b0` sufficiently close in
terms of the final loss, and only then varies `D`. It is a partial-sector
estimate and does not increase `c`.

## 2. The exact weighted moment

For `X>0` put
\[
\begin{aligned}
S_z^-(X)&=\sum_b\xi(b)q_b(q_b/X)^{3z}
 \overline{W_0((q_b/X)^3)},\\
S_z^+(X)&=\sum_b\overline{\xi(b)}q_b(q_b/X)^{3z}
 W_0((q_b/X)^3).
\end{aligned}
\]
Both sums and each required Euler derivative obey
`O_A(T^A0 min(X^A,X^(-A)))` on every fixed compact interval of
`Re z`, where `T=2+|Im z|`. Their Mellin proof uses only the fixed
entire angular functions `L^S(w-1,xi)` and `L^S(w-1,bar xi)`.

For `X_c=(D/q_c)^(1/3)`, `Y_e=(D/q_e)^(1/3)`, keep the exact DC7
expression
\[
\begin{aligned}
T_{c,e}(z)=\sum_{(\ell,ce)=1}\mu(\ell)q_\ell^2
&\left[\sum_{r\mid e}\mu(r)\xi(r)q_r
 S_z^-\!\left(\frac{X_c}{q_\ell q_r}\right)\right]\\
{}\times&\left[\sum_{s\mid c}\mu(s)\overline{\xi(s)}q_s
 S_z^+\!\left(\frac{Y_e}{q_\ell q_s}\right)\right].
\end{aligned}
\]
The two factors have the **same complex `z`**. They are not replaced
by an absolute square. Both moving opposite-column deletion factors
remain exact.

For core norm dyads `C<=E`, define
\[
\mathcal B_{C,E}(z)=
\sum_{\substack{c,e>1\ {\rm sf}\ (c,e)=1\\
                 \eta_{c,e}|_{\mu_6}=1}}
w_C(q_c/C)w_E(q_e/E)
\beta(c)\overline{\beta(e)}
L_{\mathbb K}(z,\eta_{c,e})T_{c,e}(z),
\quad \eta_{c,e}=\vartheta_c\overline{\vartheta_e}.
\tag{BC5}
\]
The norm weights are supported on fixed annuli. They may include an
actual sharp core-sector endpoint, handled by partial summation below.
They multiply the original profile. No Type-I theorem for modified
profiles is invoked.

Write `E_N(x)=min(1,x^(-N))`. For every final positive loss, choose a
fixed sufficiently small positive `a`. The moment estimate proved
below is
\[
\boxed{
|\mathcal B_{C,E}(a+it)|
\ll T^A D\,
C^{4b/3-1/6}E^{2b/3+1/6}
(DCE)^\epsilon
E_N(C/D)E_N(E/D).
}
\tag{BC6}
\]
This is a coefficient-specific estimate, not a stipulated uniform
Hecke moment.

## 3. Positive row contour and exact root-number cancellation

Let `R` denote the original radial Fourier row kernel in M (2.15), and
`R_tilde` its one-variable Mellin transform. Initially on a single line
`rho>1`, absolute convergence gives
\[
\mathfrak Q_{C,E}
=\frac6{2\pi i}\int_{(\rho)}
\widetilde R(z)K^z\mathcal B_{C,E}(z)\,dz.
\tag{BC7}
\]
The factor six counts all associate rows. In the principal pure-cube
sector the same convention is `Z_row(z)=6 zeta_K(z)`; it is not an
S-deleted row sum.

For the retained coprime nonunit cores, the unit-neutral row character
is nonprincipal and its primitive good conductor is exactly `ce`.
Therefore its L-function is entire. The original row transform is
holomorphic for `Re z>0`. Move to `z=a+it`, `a>0`, without crossing a
pole. Fixed-prime row valuations remain included.

The exact functional equation and root-number calculation give
\[
L(z,\eta)
=A(z)(q_cq_e)^{1/2-z}\epsilon(\eta)L(1-z,\bar\eta),
\qquad
A(z)=3^{1/2-z}(2\pi)^{2z-1}
\frac{\Gamma(1-z)}{\Gamma(z)},
\]
and
\[
\boxed{
\beta(c)\overline{\beta(e)}\epsilon(\eta)
=\mu(c)\mu(e)\eta(\lambda).
}
\tag{BC8}
\]
The cross-prime reciprocity phase cancels on the original coprime
support. This supplies the two Möbius coefficients used below. Apply
the functional equation before taking absolute values.

## 4. A polynomial dual truncation, including its error

At `Re(1-z)=1-a<1`, the dual L-series is not expanded as an infinite
absolutely convergent series. Take
\[
V(x)=\frac1{2\pi i}\int_{(d)}\frac{e^{w^2}}w x^{-w}\,dw,
\qquad d>a,
\]
and choose uniformly on the fixed core dyad
\[
N=(CE)^2T^4.
\]
This smoothing is bounded at zero and decreases faster than every
power at infinity. For every fixed `J>=2`,
\[
\begin{aligned}
L(1-z,\bar\eta)
={}&\sum_{\mathfrak n}\bar\eta(\mathfrak n)
q_{\mathfrak n}^{z-1}V(q_{\mathfrak n}/N)\\
&+O_J\!\left((CE)^{J+a-1/2}N^{-J}
T^{2J+2a-1}\right).
\end{aligned}
\tag{BC9}
\]
To prove this, start with the Mellin integral of
`L(1-z+w,bar eta) N^w exp(w^2)/w` on `Re w=d`. Its series there
converges absolutely. Shift to `Re w=-J`; only `w=0` contributes a
residue, since the dual L-function is nonprincipal. The ordinary
functional equation bounds the new line by conductor power
`(CE)^(J+a-1/2)` and height power `T^(2J+2a-1)` after integrating
the Gaussian vertical damping.

Since `|A(a+it)|<<T^(1-2a)`, multiplication by the outside
`A(z)(q_cq_e)^(1/2-z)` makes the error
\[
O_J((CE)^{-J}T^{-2J}).
\tag{BC10}
\]
DC10 and absolute core counting make this error harmless, retaining
both original core tails. Here `q_cq_e` and `CE` differ by fixed
dyadic constants only.

For the main series, ideal counting gives the absolute dual mass with
a subpower conductor cost:
\[
\sum_{\mathfrak n}q_{\mathfrak n}^{-1+a+\delta}
|V(q_{\mathfrak n}/N)|
\ll_{a,\delta}N^{a+\delta}.
\tag{BC11}
\]
Thus the truncation contributes only `(CE)^(O(a+delta))` and a
polynomial in `T`. The constants may deteriorate as `a` or `delta`
tends to zero. They need not be uniform there: both parameters are
fixed in terms of the final loss before any scale varies.

## 5. Moving finite twists, natural zeros, and masked Möbius sums

Insert the finite unit-neutral projector. For each dual ideal
`mathfrak n` and unit component `u0`,
\[
\eta(\lambda u_0)\bar\eta(\mathfrak n)
=\chi_{\mathfrak n,u_0}(c)
 \overline{\chi_{\mathfrak n,u_0}(e)},
\qquad
\chi_{\mathfrak n,u_0}(c)
=\vartheta_c(\lambda u_0)
 \overline{\vartheta_c(\mathfrak n)}.
\tag{BC12}
\]
Cubic reciprocity makes this a finite-order character in the good core
variable. Its primitive good conductor consists of the primes for
which `v_p(mathfrak n)` is nonzero modulo three, hence has norm at
most `q_mathfrak_n`.

**Primes dividing `mathfrak n` to a multiple of three still impose
natural zeros.** They remain finite deletions even when absent from
the primitive conductor. The supplementary twist at `lambda u0` has
fixed conductor. Arbitrary fixed-S valuations of the dual ideal do
not create a moving good conductor.

Let `h=1/2-z`. I-HECKE gives
\[
\sum_{\substack{m\\(m,M)=1}}
\mu(m)\chi_{\mathfrak n,u_0}(m)q_m^hF(q_m/U)
\ll
(q_{\mathfrak n}q_M)^\delta T^A
U^{b+\Re h+\delta}\mathcal S(F).
\tag{BC13}
\]
Here `S(F)` uses finitely many Euler derivatives on a fixed norm
annulus. The reciprocal series is `1/L^S(s,chi*)` with the additional
deleted Euler factors required by `M` and the natural zeros at
`rad(mathfrak n)`. Unramified deleted primes contribute factors
`(1-chi*(p)q_p^(-s))^(-1)`, bounded by a subpower of the deletion
norm on the fixed line `b>0`. The primitive reciprocal costs a
subpower of its actual conductor and height by I-HECKE. Buffered
Perron bounds and partial summation also permit a sharp interval
endpoint. All preliminary losses can be decreased independently.

No subpower bound for a moving angular L-function is used. The only
moving reciprocal functions in (BC13) have finite order.

## 6. Both opposite-column masks and the residual core coprimality

In the exact DC7 expression, write
\[
c=su,\qquad e=rv,\qquad r\mid e,\quad s\mid c.
\]
The exact restrictions become
\[
(r,s)=(\ell,rs)=1,\qquad
(u,rs\ell)=(v,rs\ell)=1,\qquad (u,v)=1.
\]
The condition `(ell,rs)=1` comes from the original `(ell,ce)=1` and
is retained here; it can be dropped only in the positive outer bound
at (BC16). All these variables are squarefree where forced by their
core factorizations. There is no own-column exclusion. The signs obey
\[
\mu(c)\mu(e)\mu(r)\mu(s)=\mu(u)\mu(v).
\tag{BC14}
\]
Retain the outside phases
`xi(r) bar xi(s) chi_mathfrak_n,u0(s) bar chi_mathfrak_n,u0(r)`
before bounding their magnitudes by one.

Open `(u,v)=1` with its complete Möbius projector and write the common
divisor in a projector term as `g`. The residual sums run separately
over `u/g` and `v/g`; their natural zeros and masks at `rs ell g`
are retained. Apply (BC13) to both. The outside `g^(2h)` and the two
rescaled lengths leave
\[
\sum_gq_g^{-2b+O(\delta)}\ll1,
\tag{BC15}
\]
because `b>1/2` and the preliminary loss is sufficiently small. With
fixed component twists, the extra `g` phase has modulus at most one.

This is an actual coprimality expansion of the coefficient-specific
Möbius product. It does not require a new Hecke moment assumption.

## 7. Sum the forced opposite incidences and preserve the tails

Put
\[
X=(D/C)^{1/3},\qquad Y=(D/E)^{1/3},\qquad X\ge Y,
\qquad H_A(x)=\min(x^A,x^{-A}).
\]
For fixed `r,s,ell,g`, the first angular argument depends smoothly on
`q_c/C` as `X/(q_ell q_r) (q_c/C)^(-1/3)`, and the second depends
smoothly on `q_e/E` as `Y/(q_ell q_s) (q_e/E)^(-1/3)`. The original
CS8 bounds and their Euler derivatives therefore supply the same
`H_A` envelopes to the seminorms in (BC13). The factors with imaginary
norm exponent cost only fixed powers of `T`.

After the two Möbius estimates, the remaining positive budget is
\[
\begin{aligned}
(CE)^{b+1/2-a+O(\delta)}
\sum_\ell q_\ell^2
&\sum_rq_r^{1-b}H_A\!\left(\frac X{q_\ell q_r}\right)\\
{}\times&\sum_sq_s^{1-b}H_A\!\left(\frac Y{q_\ell q_s}\right),
\end{aligned}
\tag{BC16}
\]
up to polynomial height and arbitrarily small norm powers. For
example, the outside `q_s^(1+h)` and the `u`-length power
`(C/q_s)^(b+h)` leave `q_s^(1-b)`. The `r` calculation is identical.
Thus neither opposite deletion has been replaced by a free divisor
count. Dropping the remaining restrictions on these positive outer
sums only enlarges them.

Ideal counting gives
\[
F_b(U):=\sum_rq_r^{1-b}H_A(U/q_r)
\ll
\begin{cases}
U^{2-b},&U\ge1,\\
U^A,&U<1.
\end{cases}
\]
For `X>=Y`, it follows that
\[
\sum_\ell q_\ell^2F_b(X/q_\ell)F_b(Y/q_\ell)
\ll X^{2-b}Y^{1+b}E_N(C/D)E_N(E/D).
\tag{BC17}
\]
For `Y>=1`, the range `q_ell<=Y` costs
\[
(XY)^{2-b}\sum_{q_\ell\le Y}q_\ell^{2b-2}
\ll (XY)^{2-b}Y^{2b-1}.
\]
The factor `Y^(2b-1)` is included. For `Y<q_ell<=X`, use the
small-argument bound in the second factor; for `q_ell>X`, use it
in both. These give the same budget when `A>b+1`. When `Y<1`, take
`A>=b+1+3N` to supply the displayed arbitrary upper-tail power.
When also `X<1`, the same choice supplies both tails since `b>1/2`.
Arbitrarily small outer norm powers are absorbed by increasing the
endpoint exponents and decreasing the preliminary losses.

The powers in (BC16)--(BC17), before the small `a,delta` losses, are
\[
(CE)^{b+1/2}(D/C)^{(2-b)/3}(D/E)^{(1+b)/3}
=D C^{4b/3-1/6}E^{2b/3+1/6}.
\]
Together with (BC11), this proves (BC6).

## 8. Fixed components and completion of the original row integral

Fixed column ray refinements give finitely many twists of the angular
sums and the two core characters. The angular-sum characters retain
nonzero infinity type and fixed conductor. The two core characters
in (BC13) remain finite order, with the moving conductor and natural
zeros described in (BC12). Arbitrary angular core twists are not
included in this assertion.

Fixed-place row factors on `Re z=a>0` have finite Fourier expansions
in the finitely many values `eta(p)`, `p in S`. The coefficients are
bounded on that line; valuation progressions keep their actual
geometric denominators. After the functional equation, these
expansions add fixed twists to (BC12). Thus merely bounding a local
factor before the core cancellation is not required.

If a required component includes a fixed finite-order row twist, CRT
changes the root number by fixed-modulus phases in `c,e`. Expand that
finite ray function into products of fixed core characters. Its good
Gauss factors are those already canceled in (BC8). The primitive
moving conductor remains `ce`, and the dual core-twist conductor is
bounded by a fixed multiple of `rad(mathfrak n)`. The same masked
Möbius argument applies. No moving deletion is absorbed into `S`.

The exponent `2b/3+1/6` in (BC6) is positive, so summing all
opposite-core dyads, including the unbounded upper tail, costs
`D^(2b/3+1/6+epsilon)`. For the union sector use the disjoint rectangles
`{q_c<=C}` and `{q_c>C, q_e<=C}`. Each restriction is a one-variable
endpoint, so (BC13) and partial summation apply. In each rectangle,
sort the two dyadic scales by swapping the columns in the estimate;
do not introduce a nonseparable condition `q_c<=q_e`. The smaller
dyadic scale is `O(C)`, including boundary dyads. Summing its positive
power up to `O(C)` proves (BC1).

Choose the fixed positive `a` sufficiently small that `K^a`, the dual
truncation loss, and all preliminary norm powers fit the final loss.
This is possible for every fixed polynomial bound `K<=D^B`. The
rapid vertical decay of `R_tilde` on that fixed positive line absorbs
the polynomial heights. No original Mellin root has been shifted or
discarded: the auxiliary angular shifts are residue-free, and the row
shift stays strictly positive with nonprincipal row L-functions.

## 9. Exact residual and the still-open large-core moment

Restoring the previously paid pure-cube and one-unit-core sectors gives
\[
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
\mathfrak Q_{\rm rem}
={}&\mathfrak Q_{q_c>C,\ q_e>C}-\mathfrak Q_{II}\\
&+O_\epsilon\!\left(
DK^{1+\epsilon}+D^{11/6+\epsilon}
+D^{7/6+2b/3+\epsilon}C^{4b/3-1/6}\right).
\end{aligned}
}
\tag{BC18}
\]
The whole signed II subtraction is retained. T05 pays its stated
physical cube-row piece only; this packet makes no new claim about
the rest of II and does not identify it with a transformed zero term.

For balanced largest cores `C=E=D`, the proved moment budget is only
\[
|\mathcal B_{D,D}(a+it)|\ll T^A D^{1+2b+\epsilon},
\]
whose limiting exponent is
`1+2b0=2.749773294079928...`. Thus the argument does not pay the
remaining double-large sector, and this budget should not replace a
better existing global sieve bound where that applies.

A concrete sufficient next estimate is (BC5), with its exact
`T_c,e`, bounded by
\[
|\mathcal B_{C,E}(a+it)|
\ll T^A D^{2+\epsilon}E_N(C/D)E_N(E/D)
\]
uniformly for the remaining core dyads, with `a` chosen as above.
At `C=E=D`, its dual formulation has the actual twists (BC12),
effective dual length `D^4 T^4`, primitive conductors at most
`q_mathfrak_n`, and weight
`q_mathfrak_n^(a-1) V(q_mathfrak_n/(D^4 T^4))`.
The present separate Möbius bounds leave a further required saving
`D^(2b0-1)=D^.749773294079928...`. That weighted average is open;
no uniform Hecke moment is asserted.

## Source anchors and review targets

- [M conventions and coefficients](../../zeta_zero_free_validated_merged.md):
  section 1, (1.4)--(1.6), (2.8), and (2.14)--(2.15). These supply the
  actual beta coefficient, full row convention, no cube/row mask, and
  original product profile.
- [Ordinary row series and root cancellation](../review-cycle-9.md):
  section 1, especially the displayed functional equation and (R1).
- [[private research revision] input ledger and T01](../[private research revision]/[restricted mathematical source]):
  I-HECKE at line 27 is explicitly stronger than I-ZETA; T01 supplies
  the separate fixed angular continuation. T05's scope remains as
  stated there.
- [Pure-cube packet CS6--CS8](../[private research revision]-continuation/cubic-sectors.md):
  the same-complex-z angular product, fixed angular endpoint proof,
  and full row convention.
- [Accepted one-unit-core packet](../[private research revision]/cubic-unit-core.md): previously
  paid full one-unit-core sectors, not re-proved here.
- [DC5--DC10](../[private research revision]/cubic-small-cores.md): exact two moving masks, the
  original `T_c,e`, and its absolute bound with both upper tails.

The independent-review checklist records the truncation and its
uniformity on a fixed small positive line, natural zeros at dual cube
prime powers, the complete coprimality projector after root
cancellation, the true forced-divisor powers in (BC16), the growing
ell mass in (BC17), and the finite-component factorization before
claiming the complete prescribed family. Independent review accepted the stated record and its scopes.

 Exact owned tree:

## 1. Frozen source, sampling and independent audit preparation

Preparation ended at 21:42:22; root later delivered the single final

## 2. The fixed Gaussian and the interpolation step

Fix tau>0. Write g_tau(v)=(2*pi*tau)^(-1/2) exp(-v^2/(2tau)).
For a fixed ordinary character chi use the complete coefficients
a_n=mu(n)chi(n), including both natural sets of zeros, and

    F(z)=sum_(n>=1) a_n g_tau(log n-z).                    (R39.1)

The supplied cards used the raw Gaussian; multiplying by the fixed
sqrt(2*pi*tau) changes no exponent. It does change heat derivatives
when tau varies, as the independent C05 audit below records.

Absolute local uniform convergence makes R39.1 entire. For z=u+iv,
the modulus of each kernel is exp(v^2/(2tau)) times its real kernel.
The positive integer sum is bounded by its integral plus twice its
maximum: as a function of the real integer variable the Gaussian is
unimodal, so partitioning on the two sides of its maximum proves
that elementary sum-integral bound. Its integral is exp(u+tau/2).
For u>=0 this proves |F(u+iv)|<=C_tau exp(u+v^2/(2tau)).
For real u<=0, factoring exp(-u^2/(2tau)) leaves a summable
series bounded by its value at u=0. This pays the left Mellin tail.
Every fixed derivative has the same local convergence justification.

### R39-A. Complex-polynomial interpolation is valid

For a complex polynomial P of degree <=N on a unit interval, with
|P|<=m almost everywhere on a measurable set of measure >=delta,
the bound

    sup_I |P| <= (4e/delta)^N m                            (R39.2)

is valid. Use the closed sublevel set of P, of measure Delta>=delta,
and choose its N+1 interior measure quantiles. Its distribution
function is 1-Lipschitz, so x_j-x_i>=(j-i)delta/(N+1). The Lagrange
denominator at node j is at least
(delta/(N+1))^N j!(N-j)!, while each numerator factor on I is <=1.
The sum of absolute interpolation weights is therefore at most
((N+1)/delta)^N 2^N/N! <=(4e/delta)^N. Complex values require no
extra sign or real-root assumption. Essential suprema are handled
by enlarging m and taking a limit. The case N=0 is immediate.

Now suppose a fixed complex-growth bound is available:

    |F(u+iv)| <= C(1+|v|)^K exp(bu+v^2/(2tau)), u>=0,    (R39.3)

with fixed b>gamma. In every sufficiently large integer interval
I_j=[j,j+1], suppose a measurable E_j has measure >=c j^-kappa and
essential supremum <=C_0 exp(gamma j). The same conclusion holds
with arbitrarily small exponent allowances, as specified below.

Take N=ceil(2(b-gamma)j/log j), center j+1/2 and radius
R=sqrt(tau(N+1)). For large j, the whole disk lies in u>=0.
The maximum on that disk has logarithm

    <=bj+R^2/(2tau)+bR+O(K log(1+R)+1).

Cauchy's coefficient estimate for the Taylor polynomial P_N gives
on the whole real interval the **complete** remainder

    r_j <= M_R (1/(2R))^(N+1)/(1-1/(2R)),
    log r_j <= bj-(N/2)log N+O(N+sqrt N+K log N)
             =gamma j+o(j).                             (R39.4)

The o(j) includes the positive j*loglog j/log j correction; it is
not silently removed before interpolation. On E_j, |P_N| is at
most C_0 exp(gamma j)+r_j. Apply R39.2 to P_N and then add the
remainder outside E_j. Both errors survive:

    sup_I |F| <= L_j C_0 exp(gamma j)+(L_j+1)r_j,
    log L_j <= 2kappa(b-gamma)j+o(j).

Thus the complete output exponent is

    gamma+2kappa(b-gamma).                               (R39.5)

This verifies W39.3--8, including the coefficient 2 and both
amplified remainders. It does not prove this coefficient optimal.
For kappa>=1/2 this estimate does not improve the prior b; it is
not an impossibility theorem for all observation methods.

For kappa=0, a fixed positive measure in **every** unit interval
already preserves gamma for an arbitrary bounded-coefficient fixed
Gaussian. A derivative bound for each fixed order does not suffice
in its place: this proof uses orders N growing like j/log j and a
quantitative complex bound on disks of radius about sqrt(j/log j).
A merely fixed-width analytic strip likewise does not give R39.4.

## 3. Reciprocal replenishment and the finite bootstrap

### R39-B. The Mellin identity gives actual zero exclusion

On Re s>1, absolute Fubini gives

    integral_R F(y) exp(-s y)dy=exp(tau*s^2/2)/L(s,chi).  (R39.6)

If F(y)=O_epsilon(exp((h+epsilon)y)) for every epsilon>0,
the right tail integral is holomorphic on Re s>h. Each fixed
s-derivative introduces a power of y, still integrable on compact
subsets by choosing epsilon inside the real-part margin. The left
Gaussian tail pays negative y. Multiplication by the meromorphic L
continues the identity from Re s>1. Any zero in Re s>h would force
the nonvanishing exponential to vanish. The principal pole at 1
instead forces a zero in the reciprocal and causes no false claim.
This argument covers unbounded heights; it is not a sample of zeros
or a contour truncated at a moving height.

### R39-C. The fixed-line reciprocal bound is proved after that step

For nonprincipal ordinary chi, periodic partial sums A_chi(x) are
O_q(1), so Abel summation continues L=s integral_1^infinity
A_chi(t)t^(-s-1)dt to Re s>0 and gives a polynomial upper bound.
For principal chi, write A_chi(t)=ct+E(t), E=O_q(1). Then

    L(s)=c*s/(s-1)+s integral_1^infinity E(t)t^(-s-1)dt.

Consequently P=L in the nonprincipal case and P=(s-1)L in the
principal case are holomorphic with polynomial upper growth on
every closed positive real-part strip. In the principal case
P(1)=c>0. All imprimitive factors remain; their zeros have real
part 0 and do not intrude on this domain.

Assume the zero-free conclusion already obtained above: Re s>h,
h>0. Fix h<b<2. At center 2+it choose outer radius
R_0=2-(h+b)/2 and inner radius r_0=2-b. The outer disk stays in
Re s>h; its positive gap is (b-h)/2. The regularized P is
holomorphic and nonzero there. Choose a local log f=log P whose
center imaginary part is in [-pi,pi]. The Euler product on Re s=2
bounds L above and away from zero. Together with the regularizing
factor this gives |f(2+it)|=O(log(2+|t|)). The polynomial upper
bound for P gives sup Re f=O(log(2+|t|)) on the disk.

Here is the quantitative log estimate. Choose positive
M>max(0,sup Re f), of size O(log(2+|t|)), and set g=M-f. Then Re g>0.
The map (g-g(center))/(g+conj(g(center))) takes the disk to the unit
disk and vanishes at its center. Schwarz's inequality bounds its
modulus by r_0/R_0 on the inner disk. Hence

    |g| <= (R_0+r_0)/(R_0-r_0) |g(center)|,
    |f| <= C_(h,b,q) log(2+|t|).

This proves |1/P(b+it)|<=C(2+|t|)^K. For principal chi multiply
by |b+it-1| to recover 1/L. Compact low heights are harmless.
The same fixed disks bound every point b<=Re s<=2, uniformly in
height. No Phragmen--Lindelof premise, conjectural reciprocal bound,
or conductor-uniform estimate has entered this argument. The
author's strip here must be understood as a fixed real-part strip
with all heights; the disk proof supplies exactly that bound.

Mellin inversion starts on Re s=2, where the Dirichlet series is
absolutely convergent. Shift to b. The integrand is holomorphic,
including at the principal pole's reciprocal zero. Horizontal sides
vanish because exp(-tau*t^2/2) beats the just-proved polynomial,
uniformly across b<=Re s<=2. Thus

    F(z)=(1/(2pi)) integral_R exp(tau*(b+it)^2/2)
                         exp((b+it)z)/L(b+it,chi)dt.     (R39.7)

For z=u+iv, completing the square gives
-tau*t^2/2-tv=-(tau/2)(t+v/tau)^2+v^2/(2tau).
The shifted Gaussian integral of (1+|t|)^K is bounded by
C_(tau,K)(1+|v|)^K. This proves R39.3 **for all v**, not just on
a fixed complex strip. It therefore supports the growing Cauchy
disks used in R39.4. All fixed derivatives follow by polynomial
factors of b+it under this same integral.

The possible circularity is resolved in the correct order:
interpolation first proves an improved real exponent; R39.6 first
proves the corresponding zero-free domain; only then does this disk
argument improve the complex bound for the next step.

### R39-D. Quantifiers in W39-A and protected audit E03

For W39-A take 0<gamma<1 and 0<=kappa<1/2 throughout.
Let P(h) mean the complete all-scale bound at h with every positive
exponent allowance. Write r=2kappa<1. The hypothesis supplies, for
every epsilon>0 and every sufficiently large j, sets E_j of measure
at least c_epsilon j^-kappa and values at most
C_epsilon exp((gamma+epsilon)j). These constants may depend on
epsilon and the fixed character, but not on j.

Starting with the unconditional complex bound at b=1, the first
interpolation proves P(h_1), h_1=gamma+r(1-gamma). R39.6 and R39.7
then give R39.3 for every fixed b>h_1. The next interpolation, with
sufficiently small fixed input allowances and b-h_1, proves
P(h_2), h_2=gamma+r^2(1-gamma). In general

    h_m=gamma+r^m(B-gamma),                              (R39.8)

where B=1 initially, or a separately available prior limiting
exponent B>gamma. The word limiting means an arbitrary positive
buffer is taken before using R39.3; no estimate on the exact
boundary line is presumed.

For any requested output margin eta>0, choose a finite m with
r^m(B-gamma)<eta/3. Then choose the finitely many b/input margins
small enough that their total contribution is <2eta/3. The hypothesis
allows each such choice. The resulting constants and initial scale
may worsen, but are fixed. There is no interchange of an infinite
iteration and an estimate. For kappa=0 the first step already gives
P(gamma). This proves W39-A, its all-scale conclusion, and exclusion
of every zero with Re rho>gamma. It asserts nothing on Re rho=gamma.

Protected E03 is therefore **accepted through A02's developed
argument**, including its suggested single-step formula. Its
pre-outcome protection was warranted by a genuine open hypothesis
left by the old density examples, but it is the same-batch overlap
already acknowledged by the author, not a seventh selected test or
independent theorem discovery. The improvement from R39.5 to the
final exponent gamma uses the actual meromorphic L package. It is
not granted to every generic bounded-coefficient entire function.

A fixed positive interval length can replace 1: the interpolation
numerators and Taylor radius costs change by fixed factors, leaving
R39.5 unchanged after rescaling. Shrinking lengths or a sparse
subsequence of intervals require a new argument. Finitely many
point samples have measure zero and meet no stated hypothesis.

The frozen illustration at kappa=1/4 and gamma=.87449 is correct:
from B=1, h_8=.8749802734375 and h_9=.87473513671875. Nine steps
cross both the old .874872 and current .874867 boundaries, entirely
conditionally. With the current limiting B=.874867, the first
midpoint is .8746785; the author's .874681 is the historical c2
midpoint. These arithmetic illustrations prove no small-value set
and no new c.

## 4. The fixed Eisenstein and literal f3 returns

### R39-E. The Hecke counting argument supplies the needed package

The statement is for each fixed finite-order Hecke character psi of
trivial infinite type over K=Q(sqrt(-3)), with a fixed **presented**
ray modulus f. Any fixed omitted Euler primes are included in f.
The coefficient is exactly mu_K(a)psi(a), over nonzero integral
ideals, including squareful and nonunit zeros.

The Eisenstein lattice with basis 1,omega has covolume sqrt(3)/2
and covering radius 1/sqrt(3)<1 in the norm N(alpha)=|alpha|^2.
Nearest-lattice division gives Euclidean division, hence class
number 1. Every nonzero ideal has exactly six generators. The
function psi((alpha)), extended by zero away from elements coprime
to f, is periodic modulo f and invariant under those six units.
A nonprincipal such Hecke character is a nontrivial character of
the residue-unit quotient, so its mean over O_K/f is zero. The
principal mean is |(O_K/f)^*|/N(f)>0.

Tile the disk |alpha|<=sqrt X by cells of the fixed f-lattice.
Complete cells contribute that residue mean. The O_f(sqrt X+1)
boundary cells have bounded total weight per cell. Exclude alpha=0
and divide by six. This proves

    sum_(N(a)<=X) psi(a)=c_psi X+O_f(sqrt X+1),
    c_psi=0 for nonprincipal psi,
    c_principal=(pi/(3sqrt(3))) |(O_K/f)^*|/N(f).         (R39.9)

The displayed constant follows from the unit disk's area and the
covolume; the exact value is not needed for the theorem, but its
positivity proves that the regularized principal pole is nonzero.
This is a fixed-lattice estimate, with no assertion that its error
is uniform in moving f. Nontrivial angular weights are not periodic
in these residue cells and are outside this proof.

In particular the positive ideal count is O(X). Integration by
parts against the real Gaussian, or summation in unit log bins,
then proves the same C_tau exp(u) positive majorant for u>=0 and
the same Gaussian left tail. The ideal sum is therefore entire
with the required complex bound. Euler inversion on Re s>1 gives
its exact Mellin transform exp(tau*s^2/2)/L(s,psi).

Abel summation of R39.9 gives a meromorphic continuation for
Re s>1/2 and a polynomial upper bound there after multiplying a
principal L by s-1. The residue is c_psi in the principal case.
Every replenishment disk may be kept strictly in Re s>1/2 when
gamma>1/2. The Euler product at 2 supplies the same center bounds.
Thus R39-A--D apply, proving W39-H without importing an improved
I-HECKE reciprocal estimate as a hidden premise.

The family agrees with root's stated finite-order, trivial-infinity
scope. This does not give a moving-conductor, angular or general
number-field theorem. A common zero-free conclusion for every
member requires the small-set hypothesis separately for every
member (or a separately proved uniform hypothesis). A zeta-only
small-set bound does not supply the family hypothesis.

### R39-F. f3 keeps its actual Euler factors and full signed return

The source f3 is multiplicative with f3(p^k)=-1 for every k>=1
and p!=3, and f3(3^k)=1. Thus its local Dirichlet factors are
(1-2z)/(1-z) for p!=3 and (1-z)^(-1) at 3. Dividing by the local
factor of 1/zeta gives exactly

    D3(s)=B(s)/zeta(s), B(s)=(1-2^(1-s))H(s),
    H(s)=(1-2^-s)^(-2)(1-3^-s)^(-2)
             product_(p>=5) (1-2p^-s)/(1-p^-s)^2.        (R39.10)

For p>=5 the linear term cancels. On Re s>=b>1/2, both local
logarithmic series have summable O_b(p^-2b) tails; 2*5^-b<1
excludes every numerator zero. H and its inverse are consequently
analytic, bounded and nonzero on that half-plane. The separate
factors at 2 and 3 are essential. B has its retained zeros on
Re s=1 and no zeros in 1/2<Re s<1.

For the complete F3(z)=sum_n f3(n)g_tau(log n-z), the actual Mellin
identity is exp(tau*s^2/2)B(s)/zeta(s). Holomorphy of this transform
above h excludes zeta zeros in h<Re s<1. The known zero-free right
edge, already available in the project, completes the conclusion;
one must not pretend B is nonvanishing on that edge. Replenishment
uses the independently established reciprocal bound for zeta and
the bounded actual B. R39-A--D therefore prove the f3 criterion for
every fixed gamma>1/2 and kappa<1/2.

This criterion is equivalent, with epsilon buffers, to the full
pointwise Gaussian exponent. The reverse direction simply takes
E_j to be the whole interval. It is also equivalent to the complete
Gaussian square-moment target in the stated range: pointwise bounds
give that moment; conversely, dyadic Cauchy--Schwarz gives holomorphy
of the Mellin transform, then zero exclusion and R39.7 give the
pointwise bound again. Thus equivalence is proved through the
actual meromorphic multiplier, not a generic L2-to-supremum claim.

Current-proof G28 separately gives A=k*f3, f3=h*A, with the
weighted absolute convolution norms finite for each sigma>1/2.
Their fixed-field identities transfer the complete moment; G27
and G29--31 price the moving cutoffs only in their stated order.
The original A(1),A(2),A(4)=1,-3,2 remain. The f3 moment expands
with its true O(X) diagonal and every signed ordered off-diagonal
term. No absolute value may be moved inside that scalar, no negative
term deleted, and no arbitrary submask inherits the valley theorem.

The resulting **OPEN-F3-VALLEY(gamma,kappa)** is an arithmetic
estimate on a measurable subset of **every** fixed log interval,
for the complete f3 sum and gamma<.874867, kappa<1/2. It is not
established by the accepted leading signed-band asymptotics,
independent-prime models, finite sampling, or density-one good
intervals. The f3 corollary supplies zeta's return; ordinary chi and
the Hecke family have their own separate full-field hypotheses.

## 5. Earlier failures remain correct in their actual scopes

W01 card12/U-SCALE and W21-T28 are the prior observation-set
ancestors. W21 R21.27 takes a nonzero smooth compact bump theta,
repeats it with exponential weights e^(beta*j*tau), and obtains
Laplace transform integral(theta(v)e^-sv)/(1-e^((beta-s)tau)).
Its positive numerator leaves a genuine pole at beta, while a
fixed fraction of every interval has value zero. The example is
smooth with bounds for every fixed derivative, but is not an
entire function of the Gaussian growth used in R39.4. Its original
review explicitly left arithmetic/analytic observability open.
W39 answers that narrower open question rather than refuting the
earlier counterexample.

W38-18 uses bounded integer block coefficients at log positions
v_k and retains a larger exponent beta on O(sqrt J) exceptional
dyads. Throughout |u-v_k|<=2, each of its M_k positive block terms
has weight at least g_tau(3), because its log displacement inside
the block is <=log 2. That neighborhood contains a complete integer
unit interval. For gamma<beta, choose an input epsilon smaller
than beta-gamma; on infinitely many such intervals the whole
field exceeds any fixed C_epsilon e^((gamma+epsilon)j).
No positive-measure good subset exists there. It fails precisely
W39's every-interval hypothesis and remains a valid obstruction
to discarding a sparse collection of whole bad intervals.

The new project-level contribution is the quantitative
Gaussian local-measure interpolation plus proved meromorphic
replenishment and finite iteration. Its elementary interpolation,
complex analysis and lattice counting are not claimed as literature
inventions. No actual new arithmetic small-value estimate appears.

## 6. C04: the optimum one-path variance is exact and limited

For an absolutely summable finite or countable complex family,
remove zero weights and put Z=sum w_alpha, V=sum |w_alpha|.
A path sampled with p_alpha>0 returns W=w_alpha/p_alpha. Then

    E|W|^2=sum |w_alpha|^2/p_alpha >=V^2,
    E|W-Z|^2 >=V^2-|Z|^2.                               (R39.11)

Cauchy--Schwarz proves the inequality. Equality holds exactly for
p_alpha=|w_alpha|/V; the countable optimum is still a probability
law when V<infinity. Infinite second moments do not violate the
lower bound. For N independent paths, variances divide by N.

For the actual finite Euler expansion, w_S=(-1)^|S| product z_p,
z_p=chi(p)p^-s, so Z=product(1-z_p) and V=product(1+|z_p|).
The minimizing law happens to factor into Bernoulli choices of
probability |z_p|/(1+|z_p|), but R39.11 already minimizes over
all sampling laws. The one/two-prime formulas retain the empty
state, negative single-prime terms, positive pair term and every
mixed product in |Z|^2. They are correct for complex phases.

For the complete ordinary Gaussian, V(y) is the positive squarefree
count with the character's actual conductor zeros. The square-divisor
identity and periodic coprimality count give

    count_(n<=x)(mu(n)^2 1_(n,q)=1)=d_q*x+O_q(sqrt x),
    d_q=(1/zeta(2)) product_(p|q) p/(p+1)>0.

Stieltjes summation against the Gaussian gives exactly
V(y)=d_q e^(tau/2)e^y+O_(q,tau)(e^(y/2)). The derivative error is
integrable with its sqrt(x) majorant, as in W38's positive marginal
calculation. Thus, **conditional on** a mean of size O(e^(gamma y)),
gamma<1, the optimum independent sample mean requires order
e^(2(1-gamma)y) samples for RMS absolute error of that same order.
For nonzero mean the stated relative-variance formula is exact.

This is classical importance-sampling/Cauchy--Schwarz algebra applied
to the literal source, not a lower bound for every randomized or
deterministic algorithm. A known-sum control variate replaces the
weights by its residual weights; their own V_res^2-|Z_res|^2 is
the same variance price. Grouping, correlated procedures or a
proved small arithmetic residual remain outside this obstruction.
No small mean is inferred from the lower bound itself. The source
application is useful precision, with W38 normalization ancestry.

## 7. C01: exact rank and the paid analytic approximation

On disjoint finite prime sets U,V outside the conductor, the hard
product-cap matrix is

    T_de=mu(d)chi(d)mu(e)chi(e) 1_(de<=x).

Its sign/character factors are diagonal unitaries. They preserve
rank and singular values of the incidence matrix B, while its
signed scalar contraction still retains both boundary phases.
Sorted rows of B are prefix vectors; distinct nonzero prefix
lengths give independent vectors by successive subtraction.
Hence rank(B) is exactly the number of distinct nonzero prefix
lengths. The two-prime matrix has determinant -chi(p)chi(q) when
p<q<=x<pq and rank 1 after the cap disappears. This is a correct
test of the cutoff's rank cost, with the Sol wave01 A34 tensor
network seed explicitly credited.

For the Gaussian matrix K_de=g_tau(log d+log e-y), remove positive
row/column factors to leave exp(-u_i*v_j/tau). A nonzero real
combination of n distinct real exponentials has at most n-1
distinct real zeros: divide by one exponential, differentiate,
and apply Rolle inductively. A singular real n-by-n evaluation
matrix would give a real nullvector and n zeros, a contradiction.
Every square minor with distinct row/column logarithms is therefore
nonzero, proving full rectangular rank. The two-prime determinant
ratio exp(-log p log q/tau)-1 has the stated negative sign.

Full exact rank does not rule out approximation. With centered
logs u_d,v_e, |u_d|<=U, |v_e|<=V, w=a+b-y, the exact factorization
is C(w)A_d(w)B_e(w)exp(-u_d*v_e/tau), with the source's positive
C,A_d,B_e. The degree r-1 Taylor expansion gives rank <=r and
pointwise remainder <=e^Z Z^r/r!, Z=UV/tau. After the actual
signed contraction its absolute error is bounded by

    C(w)e^Z Z^r/r! (sum_d |mu(d)chi(d)| A_d)
                       (sum_e |mu(e)chi(e)| B_e).        (R39.12)

This includes the mass factors often omitted by an abstract
low-rank claim. The operator error is bounded using the analogous
l2 factors, since the Frobenius square is dominated by their
product. If the positive scalar prefactor is <=exp(C_1 L),
Z<=C_2 L and r=ceil(C_3 L), the factorial bound gives exponent
at most C_1+C_2+C_3 log(e C_2/C_3)+o(1), times L.
Choosing a sufficiently large fixed C_3 pays any fixed negative
power. Fixed-constant O(sqrt L) log-bin widths and center mismatch,
with finite coefficient masses exp(O(L)), meet those hypotheses.

This bounded-bin approximation is valid. It is neither a uniform
estimate on all unbinned prime states nor an algorithm that
computes the required signed moments cheaply. Each separated
factor is a signed moving-endpoint arithmetic sum of growing
degree. Reassembly needs all bins, tails, heights and cross-Gram
terms with their own error budgets. The actual cancellation
remains unproved. Existing W35 finite Gaussian/Fourier machinery
is related representation ancestry; no paid sector is added here.

## 8. Remaining selected tests and independent uniform audit C05

**F05.** The displayed divisor diamond Z and U multiply to identity
in both orders, including the +uv coefficient at pq. Z is the
tensor product of [[1,0],[u,1]] and [[1,0],[v,1]], in the stated
ordering. Each local normal operator has trace 2+|u|^2 and
determinant 1, so its smaller eigenvalue is exactly
(2+|u|^2-|u|sqrt(4+|u|^2))/2. Thus W39.30 and the inverse-norm
formula follow. Complex phases are unitarily removable. Passing
to Z*Z squares the condition number; it supplies no independent
gap. This is the natural normal-operator test, not a theorem about
every genuine cochain/Hodge construction. AM19--21 and G32 already
separate finite inverse bounds from the unbounded physical readout.
In particular, unconditional N^epsilon finite inverse bounds above
1/2 cannot themselves imply a new reciprocal half-plane.

**D02.** For a single exponential, translated fields are proportional
and their Gram has rank 1 regardless of its real growth exponent.
For two exponentials G=CJC*, so det G=|det C|^2 det J gives exactly
W39.32. The fourth-order coalescence statement needs nonzero mode
amplitudes, distinct shifts and a nondegenerate **weighted** measure.
To see the precise condition, let rho_2=rho+delta,
J0=integral e^(2Re(rho)t)w(t)dt>0, and let Var_mu(t)>0 under its
normalized weighted measure. Then

    det J=J0^2 Var_mu(t)|delta|^2+o(|delta|^2),
    |det C|^2=|AB|^2 e^(2Re(rho)(h1+h2))
                   (h2-h1)^2 |delta|^2+o(|delta|^2).

Expand e^(delta t) on the fixed finite interval to obtain the first
formula; its constant/linear pieces cancel in the Gram determinant,
leaving the centered second moment. Expand the two-shift determinant
for the second. Their product explains fourth order. A zero weight
or zero amplitude is degenerate and should not be called exact
fourth order. This is a precision qualification, not a repair of the
rank-one obstruction. No actual-Mobius lower bound or failure of
the different reciprocal Hankel D3 determinant follows.

**B05.** The full defect is 2Re<U,V>+||V||^2. An upper bound on
||U+V|| needs a **lower** bound on that defect before it can bound
||U||. The literal mu(1)=1,mu(2)=-1 Gaussian cell has overlap
g_(2tau)(log 2) and exact norm ratio
2[1-exp(-(log 2)^2/(4tau))]. This is <1 exactly when
tau>(log 2)/4, so the author's finite-cell test is correct. It is
the ordinary mu coefficient in W39.1, not a substitution of -1
for the original A(2)=-3 in G1. A two-label, full-line cell does
not estimate the whole uncut arithmetic field or a native masked
moment; it verifies the already known noninheritance mechanism.

**C05, frozen uniform parked audit.** Let F_tau be the normalized
fixed-coefficient Gaussian, V_tau(y)=e^(-gamma y)F_tau(y), and
E_tau=integral_a^b |V_tau|^2 dy on a finite interval. Termwise
differentiation is locally justified. The exact equations are

    partial_tau F=(1/2)partial_y^2 F,
    partial_tau V=(1/2)V_yy+gamma V_y+(gamma^2/2)V,
    dE_tau/dtau=[Re(conj(V)V_y)+gamma|V|^2]_a^b
                       -integral_a^b|V_y|^2+gamma^2 E_tau. (R39.13)

The bracket is equivalently Re[e^(-2gamma y)conj(F)F_y]_a^b.
This retains both endpoints. A whole-line identity without the
bracket requires separately proved integrability and vanishing
boundary flux. Those are not available for free at a target gamma.

For the **raw kernel in the seed**, Phi_tau=sqrt(2*pi*tau)F_tau,
the equation has the additional Phi_tau/(2tau) term. Its weighted
energy derivative has the additional E_raw/tau term. Thus its
zeroth-order energy term is (gamma^2+1/tau)E_raw, not gamma^2 E_raw.
The source report consistently switches to normalized kernels;
this distinction must survive if the parked card itself is used.

The normalized heat mode exp(tau*rho^2/2+rho y) has unchanged
log-scale real exponent Re rho. The raw mode has the additional
sqrt(2*pi*tau) amplitude only. For real beta>gamma, finite-interval
flux restores the exact derivative beta^2 E_tau (or
(beta^2+1/tau)E_raw), so suppressing that flux would give a false
monotonicity inference. This is the existing W38-06/R38.10 and
U-SCALE/F26.H failure, now checked with the seed normalization.
It does not refute a future source-specific coercive flux theorem.
It gives no new c, and no density or submask theorem by itself.

## 9. Every original card remains in the portfolio

The complete original 29-family/109-child library, late index and

read at final intake. This is portfolio coverage, not re-verification

|---|---|

## 10. Evidence limits and handoff

The independently written `review_checks.py` passed once at
22:02:37 UTC. It binds the eight immutable author artifacts and

the exact buffered recurrence against current c3; 256 literal

These checks protect arithmetic, conjugations, chronology and source

The next substantive mathematical work is to estimate the actual

## G216. Exact recovery, actual absolute cost and complete diagonal

Let E_m=P_m(D)E. The proved coarse bound E_m(Y)=O(Y), together with
Phi(X)=E_m(X)-2^(r+1)E_m(X/2), gives for every J>=1

    E_m(X)=2^(-J(r+1))E_m(2^J X)
           -sum_(j=1)^J 2^(-j(r+1))Phi(2^j X).

The first term is O(X2^(-Jr)), so the FULL future-scale inverse is

    E_m(X)=-sum_(j>=1)2^(-j(r+1))Phi(2^j X).        (11)

Every future scale remains. For gamma<r+1 and sufficiently small
epsilon, a complete exponent gamma+epsilon pays the series with
ratio2^(-(r+1-gamma-epsilon))<1. Changing variables in each dyadic
shell proves the same statement in L1. Conversely finite shifts of
E_m imply the Phi bound. Thus their complete every-epsilon exponent
classes are equivalent. The possible homogeneous mode X^(r+1) is
excluded by the actual O(X) bound, not discarded. Shorter support
alone is not a weaker arithmetic obligation.

The complete arithmetic absolute cost also stays linear. Elementary
square-divisor inversion, with all coprimality factors, gives

    Q_q(y)=sum_(n<=y,(n,q)=1)mu(n)^2
          =kappa_q y+O_q(sqrt y),
    kappa_q=zeta(2)^(-1) product_(p|q)(1+1/p)^(-1)>0.

For the original g, for P_m(T)g, and for K, the function absolute value
is absolutely continuous and its a.e. derivative is bounded by the
absolute derivative of the kernel. Both tails give finite
integral_0^infinity sqrt(t)|K'(t)|dt. Stieltjes summation therefore proves

    sum_n |mu(n)chi(n)K(n/X)|
      =kappa_q X integral_0^infinity|K(t)|dt+O(sqrt X). (12)

The integral is positive by the e^(-t) coefficient in (5). For g and
P_m(T)g, use their nonzero principal algebraic tail or nonprincipal
slowest exponential instead. This is a lower asymptotic for the
ACTUAL absolute price, not a lower bound on the signed field or M_chi.
Full triangle inequality cannot yield a fixed sublinear exponent.
Full Abel summation from any known |M_chi(y)|<<y^beta yields only
X^beta integral t^beta|K'(t)|dt; it preserves beta. The bounded
non-arithmetic sequence n^beta-(n-1)^beta tests that operator limitation,
without purporting to refute cancellation of mu chi.

There is an explicit principal normalization. At q=1,r=2,m=0,
v=e^(-t), f(t)=v(1+v)/(1-v)^3, and

    K_0(t)=f(t)-8f(2t)=v(1-v)/(1+v)^3
           =(1/4)tanh(t/2)sech^2(t/2)>0.           (13)

The numerator identity is
v(1+v)^4-8v^2(1+v^2)=v(1-v)^4.
Substitute u=tanh(t/2), dt=2du/(1-u^2), to obtain

    integral K_0(t)dt=integral_0^1 u/2 du=1/4,
    integral K_0(t)^2dt
        =integral_0^1 (u^2-u^4)/8 du=1/60.          (14)

Consequently the literal field
Phi_0(X)=F_(1,2)(X)-8F_(1,2)(X/2)=sum mu(n)K_0(n/X) has

    sum_n |mu(n)K_0(n/X)|=X/(4zeta(2))+O(sqrt X),
    sum_n mu(n)^2 K_0(n/X)^2=X/(60zeta(2))+O(sqrt X). (15)

The second is its POINTWISE squared diagonal. Integrating over a
complete shell dx/x gives X/(60zeta(2))+O(sqrt X).
The full energy retains both ordered off-diagonal orientations:
for this real principal kernel it is the diagonal plus twice the
signed sum over m<n. Absolute convergence on each shell justifies
expansion; no cross term is omitted. The diagonal is not a lower
bound for the full square. For gamma>1/2 its exponent1 is already
below2gamma; the complete cross estimate remains the substantive task.
An energy exponent below1.7497080728 would clear the current numerical
target; the displayed targets .8748,5/6,3/4 ask for1.7496,5/3,3/2.
None of these full signed estimates is proved here.

statement:
## 3. Complete signed fixed-grid obstruction and finite seeds

Let W_q be the H_sigma-closed complex span of all w_(q,n). For k!=0 set

    s_k=1+2pi i k/log q.

Zeta is holomorphic at these nonreal points, so every wavelet has E_(s_k)=0.
At the excluded real point s=1, however, (1-q^(1-s))zeta(s) has value log q.
The real pole cancellation does not erase the nonreal lattice.

For every W in W_q, continuity and (R2) imply

    ||1-W||_sigma^2 >= 2(1-sigma)/|s_k|^2,   k!=0.        (R5)

This lower bound is for the entire signed function in the infinite norm. It
already allows arbitrary complex coefficients, negative cross terms, complete
future repetitions, changing finite supports, and norm limits. It does not
come from replacing an arithmetic sum by its absolute majorant.

For q=2, log2>2/3 and pi<22/7 imply 2pi/log2<66/7. Thus

    ||1-W||_sigma^2 > (98/4405)(1-sigma).                 (R6)

The exact strict floors at c=1-sigma are respectively

| c benchmark | R6 floor |
|---|---|
| .125135=25027/200000 | 1226323/440500000 |
| .125136=7821/62500 | 383229/137656250 |
| 1/6 | 49/13215 |
| 1/4 | 49/8810 |

They are positive norm constants, not exponent losses that can be added to a
Gaussian or H budget. The frame fails even before asking for a first gain.

Now fix a finite E and S=sum_(n in E)c_n f_n. If 1-S were in W_q, evaluation at
every s_k would force

    zeta(s_k) P(s_k)=1,
    P(s)=sum_(n in E)c_n(n^(-1)-n^(-s)).                   (R7)

Remove n=1 terms. If r=|E|>0, set alpha_n=log n/log q. For every integer Q>=2,
the Q^r+1 orbit points j(alpha_n)_n modulo one occupy only Q^r coordinate boxes
of side 1/Q. Subtracting two points gives 1<=k<=Q^r and
max_n ||k alpha_n||<=1/Q. If these selected k have a bounded subsequence as
Q tends to infinity, a fixed nonzero k has all phases integral. Then P(s_k)=0,
contradicting R7. Otherwise pass to an unbounded subsequence. There

    |P(s_k)| <= (2pi/Q) sum_(n in E)|c_n|/n.               (R8)

The elementary estimate |zeta(1+it)|=O(log(2+|t|)) is sufficient. It follows
from, for integer N>=1 and Re(s)>0, s!=1,

    zeta(s)=sum_(n<=N)n^(-s)+N^(1-s)/(s-1)
                   -s integral_N^infinity {u}u^(-s-1)du.

This identity follows by integrating the floor counting function first in
Re(s)>1 and then continuing the absolutely convergent fractional-part tail.
Taking N=ceil|t| for |t|>=1 bounds the finite sum by O(log(2+|t|)) and both other
terms by O(1). Since log k<=r log Q and q is fixed, R8 gives
zeta(s_k)P(s_k)=O_(S,q)(log Q/Q), tending to zero. This contradicts R7.
The case E empty was already excluded by R5.

Finally W_q+span{f_n:n in E} is closed: it is the orthogonal sum of W_q and the
finite-dimensional image of that seed span under I-P_(W_q). Hence

    dist(1,W_q+span{f_n:n in E}) > 0.                     (R9)

This last step is essential. It converts failure for each fixed S into failure
for arbitrary sequences of refitted seed coefficients, including unbounded
ones. The proof does not give a useful numerical constant uniformly over all
finite sets E, and the candidate correctly does not claim one. For a specified
S, R2 and R7 give exactly the candidate's evaluable supremum B8.

Any fixed finite collection of q=3 wavelets is a finite collection of original
f_n combinations, so it cannot repair W_2. Conversely the theorem says nothing
against an unbounded supply of new directions. If ratios are powers b^j of one
integer base, the identity

    w_(b^j,n)=sum_(r=0)^(j-1) b^r w_(b,b^r n)

places the enlarged family inside W_b. Merely adding more such widths preserves
the obstruction.
title: 3. Complete signed fixed-grid obstruction and finite seeds

## 3. Direct large-prime extraction: the actual unpaid price

For fixed squarefree h the exact inverse divisibility component is

    M_(h|a)(R)=mu(h)phi_u(h)(Nh)^(-1/2) M^(h)(R/Nh). (5)

The moving mask is restored by ALL h-smooth powers, with absolute mass
product_(p|h)(1-(Np)^(-1/2))^(-1)<<_epsilon (Nh)^epsilon.
This uses the original inverse, rather than a new coefficient theorem.

Suppose an outer shell Nh~U^kappa is summed absolutely with divisor-bounded
coefficients, before putting a plain prime of norm U^lambda into MI.
The shell coefficient price furnished by ideal counting is U^(kappa/2+epsilon).
The squared price is U^kappa. The first new gate requires

    r-kappa+2v+2lambda<1,
    kappa>2lambda-g,       g=1-r-2v,                  (6)

and the second additionally requires
kappa>r+4v+4lambda-3/2. The shortened plain upper bound saves beta lambda
in the squared norm. Thus this method's paid squared saving is at most

    beta lambda-max(0,2lambda-g),                    (7)

even before its second gate, fine losses and a full divisor cover. It
ceases to give a power saving once lambda>=g/(2-beta). This is a bound
on what this stated absolute extraction proves, NOT a lower bound for the
actual signed source. A thinner or coherently summed extraction could behave
differently, but needs its own complete cover and arithmetic estimate.

Keeping an extracted inverse prime as another live prime slot is no repair:
its first-power term has r'=r-kappa and z=v+kappa+lambda, so the first
gate becomes r+2v+kappa+2lambda<1, worse than the original large-prime gate.
The full coprimality restoration does not remove this first-power term.

A complete inverse decomposition cannot simply assume a divisor in the
desired intermediate shell. A prime inverse ideal has no such divisor.
Together with a coprime large-prime plain ideal it has F=1, theta=0 and
survives the actual source. This is a coefficient example, not an actual
high-zero row or a norm lower bound. The full complement has not been paid.

The already accepted amplified marked estimate G90 also remains available:

    E_MI=1/6+(5/6)max(1,r+2(v+lambda),
                                      (2r+8(v+lambda))/3).

The prime extraction and(4) yield inverse exponent E_MI-beta lambda.
For example take physical/internal grade7/10, v=0, eta=1/1000, the
full-fit G137 crossing t=25/18-1/1000, r=2t/3, m=t/3, and lambda=m.
Even with margins omitted this available exponent is
1121789/810000>1. This only shows that this licensed estimate does not
settle the large-prime sector; it is not evidence that signed cancellation
is impossible. The next arithmetic action there is a coherent estimate
across the h-sum, or a native estimate for the full large-prime marked
divisor profile, with the inverse-prime complement included.

- **F14.T — O.** Start exact opposite-frequency torus tensor reproducing β; retain root-number couplings and all coprime cocycles through transformation. Direct Parseval cost C^(2−2σ) remains.
- **F14.M — O.** Matrix/twisted-convolution multiple series with actual cocycle(barK,1,K); one domain-enlarging relation beats a formal Weyl label. Standard A3/fixed twist/scalar Euler repair fail two/three-prime tests.
- **F14.A — O.** a⁴b⁸→a⁴b² on squarefree columns with radical retained. Nominal lengthA²BT⁵ requires full intertwining/reflected-energy proof; generic sieve only pays inverse wedge.

### F15. Matched cusps, collective tests and changed source spaces
- **F15.C — S.** Actual outgoing/incoming calibration and projected test, not another source-orthogonality argument. Two ordinary/inverse seed channels already centrally costQ(Q−1).
- **F15.I — O.** Two-prime CRT test for mixed/inverse-composite cusp; preserve nonunits, cube sharing and tails. Only promote if it covers new physical boxes. A18: simple diagonal oldforms r=0,1 vanish; r=2 still costs Q centrally before norm costs. General combinations and actual projected tests remain open.
- **F15.S — O.** One squarefree vector, finite R balance or independently specified current image can escape whole-span obstruction. No automatic continuity from Hilbert convergence.
- **F15.D — O.** Weight cubeB byq_B^−ν; norm/period ratios known, completion formally shifts. Fixed-factor extraction is now paid, so require conductor benefit in actual current/test product.
- **F15.G — O.** Current graph norm or squarefree reference tensor; cannot define norm by desired period. Diagonal shell Sobolev cure fails; finite-shell calibration gives necessary product-cost test but angular-product divergence must be proved, not assumed.

### F16. Asymmetric slots and Euler jets
- **F16.J — O.** Extra Euler jet, second channel or repeated prime with preserved principal map; compute all6 valuations, bad places, collisions and coefficient/profile growth, then rerun full physical/numerator minimax.
- **F16.D — O.** Derivative in slot length is a new detector only if its principal residue survives and error powers change. First compute residue, then mixed numerator; otherwise it annihilates signal.
- **F16.X — F.** Reoptimization, smoothing or regrouping inside unchanged inequalities cannot improve c0. Escape requires a new analytic bound or actual changed local factor with paid costs.

### F17. Coefficient-sensitive trace formulas and transformed kernels
- **F17.R — O.** Exact RTF/Kuznetsov for actual bilinear current or H-col, including cover/multiplier/level/cusp/angular type/residual spectrum. Match local coefficient first, then show diagonal/errors fit OM/FIN/H.
- **F17.T — O.** Derive genuine additive/rational trace kernel, classify degeneracy/diagonals, then prove local bound and moving-modulus transfer. Raw AB16 rank-one/sixth-valuation factors do not justify Deligne/N/K.
- **F17.S — O.** Keep actual p⁴ or e⁴R³P⁴ index projector before full Fourier norm; alternatively complete the μ(u)Ξ_R(u) sum at fixed sparse index with its collision masks. Ambient energy charges E⁴K³L⁴; fixed-cuspidal/cubic-Kubota literature does not match residual/moving source.

### F18. Short intervals, exceptional rows and amplitude-sensitive bounds
- **F18.A — O.** Exceptional countX^d and amplitudeX^B costX^(d+2B); one orderX row can ruin OM. Need a large-value tail/amplitude cap in physical weights or FIN's real incidence measure.
- **F18.I — O.** Short-interval theorem only after long-average mode, exceptional intervals and profile derivative sums are paid. Log-saving or power-saving exceptional cardinality is not automatically a power gain in MOB.
- **F18.X — F.** Arithmetic row labels are not zeta ordinates; good-row density does not imply all-height exclusion. Escape exact principal reconstruction or genuinely weaker density theorem with honest scope.

### F19. Higher integrability and stable future tails
- **F19.A — D.** First-shell inverse paid; require next-shell and infinite-tail capture, or actual residual Lp growth beating heavy-tail cost. Fixed constant-shell corrections cannot remove Mertens variance.
- **F19.D — O.** Optimal real damping gains(F+ReJ)²/(F+T) but leaves prior error. Revisit shells or recompute least squares; no infinite induction from one decrement.
- **F19.P — O.** Every fixed polynomial detrending degree retains detector; growing degree has new uniformity. Find an actual trend whose removal improves remaining signed Green form.

### F20. Function-field and finite arithmetic laboratory
- **F20.L — S.** Exact local rings or F_q[T], q≡1mod6, clone named Gauss/cocycle/mask/return identity and appropriate infinity analogue. Tests: small-gcd residual direction, two-/three-prime cocycle, reduced index, coherent embedding. Stop when named falsification question is answered.
- **F20.B — S.** 4/33 architecture as simpler calibration laboratory, not target milestone. A matching bad function-field main term can refute a proposed shape; success using function-field RH is not a number-field transfer.

### F21. Hardy residual discs and overlapping strips
- **F21.H — O.** a_H3/5,b_H−3/8, norm20/9, every-height residual32/15→strip3/4<σ<15/16→c1/4. Height-adapted approximants need certified derivatives/overlaps and worst-height analysis.
- **F21.N1 — O.** Target B E_t using known-critical-zero finite BlaschkeB; off-line evaluation gains penalty|B(ρ)|². Compare residual improvement to that cost before growing product; an infinite quotient needs separate arithmetic/inner-factor control.
- **F21.X — F.** Old a_H<1/2 strict uniform gain fails by critical-line clusters. Finite/sample-height discs are not full strips; deflation cannot discard its evaluation penalty. Escape repaired domain or a rigorously covered changed target.

### F22. Logarithmic potential and signed explicit formulas
- **F22.P — O.** Nonnegative band bump≥1 and Poincaré–Lelong pairing<1. Laplacian changes sign; derive arithmetic upper bound with boundaries and zero-quartet test.
- **F22.S — O.** Test negative on critical line could subtract known zeros, but loses positive-count implication unless all negative contributions are priced. Isolated off-line zeros survive density arguments.
- **F22.G — S.** Overlapping interior band, adjacent collar excluding line, prescribed-height rectangles, lens/curved regions and symmetric confinement require exact coverage and genuine improvement over inherited/reflected/density geometry. Endpoints are outputs, not numerology.
- **F22.L — D.** Density-subtracted prime kernel is explicit arithmetic version; no assumed norm comparison with generic potential.

### F23. Shifted Hermite–Biehler and canonical systems
- **F23.H — O.** Actual E_h=ξ(1/2+h−iz), K=(|E|²−|E#|²)/(4πImz); strict positivity→c1/2−h. Endpoint requires allh>0. First arithmetic kernel/sign representation plus common-zero control.
- **F23.C — O.** Controlled negative remainder or exact noncircular canonical/numerical-range model for same E_h. PSD alone hides common upper zeros, e.g.(z²+1)e^−iz. A system built from desired unknown zero locations is circular.

### F24. Left-first and two-sided spectral/Mellin methods
- **F24.T — O.** Keep two theta integrals x^(s/2),x^((1−s)/2), rotate/split together, retain all boundaries and exponential-height costs. Need a phase bound stronger than separate reflection.
- **F24.G — S.** Asymmetric analytic contours can be useful even when conclusion reflects; require actual lens/strip coverage. No repulsion from trivial zeros without a quantitative inequality.
- **F24.X — F.** Modular scattering denominatorΛ(2s) sees zeta zeroρ at parameterρ/2, outside asserted L² chamber. Functional equation alone adds no exclusion.

### F25. Triple-rotation theta products
- **F25.E — O.** Actual three-source double-torus convolution, compact r∈[1,2] scale energy. J_r noncommon zeros suffice; all fixed sectors and small-y dyads retained.
- **F25.S — O.** Trilinear spectral/horospherical restriction with residual/continuous/cusp terms before Hölder. Finite nuisance-profile quotient allowed only with noncommon multiplier calibration; quadrature needs derivative errors.
- **F25.C — O.** Finite cube-deleted trilinear functional may escape scalar whole-span obstruction; projection/level costs required. Absolute inverse cube sum stalls at a5/6; r variation leaves common angular numerator.
- **F25.K — O.** Controlled Bessel-profile representation in admissible fixed Möbius norms could share a saving; ideal/rational arithmetic and inverse analytic costs must be proved.
- **F25.X — F.** Degree-three Haar map is ordinary convolution, not mixing; Young givesO(1), absolute diagonalO(y), neither desired decay.

### F26. Direct shifted criteria and constrained operators
- **F26.O — O.** Prime diagonal det(I−T_s)=1/ζ onlyσ>1; det₂ extension omits e^−P(s), which retains unresolved poles. New non-diagonal operator needs exact prime-power determinant and controlled compensator/invertibility.
- **F26.R — D.** Actual residue source resolvent is a different arithmetic operator; positivity supplies no source-specific zero-atom bound.
- **F26.H — O.** Heat PDE∂tH=−∂z²H; seek arithmetic reverse stability/coercivity near original parameter. Positive even Fourier density and forward real-root flow do not imply original real roots.
- **F26.J — O.** Actual Jensen degree/shift-uniform root confinement, with full zero-strip transfer. Fixed-degree eventual hyperbolicity leaves unbounded region; finite matrices are diagnostics.
- **F26.L — D.** Shifted Li/Laguerre criteria become concrete prime kernels; keep principal pole/gamma terms and finite-height sensitivity.
- **F26.X — S.** Generic self-adjoint, topology, p-adic, quantum or random-graph proposal needs one noncircular zeta-sensitive identity and quantitative gate before further allocation. This is not an impossibility theorem.

### N27. Two-exponent finite-divisor incidence
- **N27.F — O.** Actual FIN-weight uses exactly-once divisors; g1 still requires OM at scaleK, while large prime rows pastK are absent forG≤K. Common-completed norm has identical exponent contract. (u,v)=(1/8,1/32) gives14/111.
- **N27.C — A.** Only corridor G≤C K^γ for fixed C, γ=(1−u)/(2+v), is necessary with full strip/profile family. Exponent γ=28/65 is now sufficient; exact whole-profile block enlargement prices tails. No cancellation estimate proved.
- **N27.P — O.** Complete a forced-prime-first dyad with full common core and actual row support; retain its principal term. Compare its exact energy to maximal KG only after writing the incidence measure.
- **N27.D — O.** Partition by the first admissible intermediate divisor, keeping signed selector weights and exceptional empty fibres. Test on rows with several repeated primes before invoking divisor density.
- **N27.X — O.** Bound exceptional FIN mass with both its amplitude and actual divisor incidence. Sparse exceptional cardinality alone is insufficient.
- **N27.N1 — O.** Keep completed h-by-divisor selector before Cauchy; derive sufficient signed energy and addbacks, then seek a saving. Alternating coefficients do not automatically remove g1.

### N28. Two-dilation and continuum-dilation Möbius energies
- **N28.D — O.** Δ_bM=M(bx)−b^αM(x), b2,3, fixedα∈(0,1). Noncommon multipliers retain every possible zeta pole. Common-scale6 compatibility is not contraction.
- **N28.C — O.** Average b continuously on [2,3]. G_α(s)=∫|b^s−b^α|²db has unique zero α, uniform positive high-height lower bound on compact real strips. Energy in dx/x≤X^(2a+ε) gives c=1−a and |1/ζ(s)|≲1+|t| on fixed compact strips strictly right of a.
- **N28.O — O.** f(t)=e^−αtM(e^t) turns continuum norm into weighted overlapping-log-interval difference energy. Prove finite-window comparison then signed cross-scale bound; Poincaré only converts a bound, not supplies arithmetic saving. Fixed-width dilation intervals are fallback.

### N29. Density-subtracted prime/Cayley/Laguerre criteria
- **N29.L — O.** Log[(s−1)ζ(s)] under Cayley vs s′ξ′/ξ Taylor coefficients are derivative-related by explicit nonvanishing gamma factor. Subexponential growth↔half-plane zero exclusion. Keep density subtraction and completed Laguerre weights; raw prime growth target is false at known pole1.
- **N29.P — O.** Actual signed log-scale/saddle prime-power kernel with complete complementary ranges and correlated gamma term. Changing fixed anchor cosmetically shrinks a root gap but proves no saving.
- **N29.N1 — O.** High-height anchorr≈sqrt(δ²+γ²) maximizes singlezero log|zρ|^−1≈δ/|γ|, subjectr>1−b. Degree for order-one amplification changes toT/δ, but no finite-degree detection follows. Require uniform degree/r estimate and band-to-allheight transfer with moving prime/gamma costs.

## 7. Exact residual form and the power budget

Define the remaining signed form

\[
Q_W^{\rm sf}:=
\mathscr Q_X\!\left[
\Omega_W\,\sigma_W(n)\sigma_W(n')
1_{|n-n'|>P_{\rm gap}}
\right].
\tag{PO42}
\]

First perform the two energy-level preparations (PO39), (PO41).
Then apply the cancellation (PO14), before any completed-product
gap is imposed. Finally remove the nearby completed-product band
by (PO28). The exact resulting estimate is

\[
\|B_X^{(W)}\|_2^2
=Q_W^{\rm sf}+O_\epsilon(X^{1.7489+\epsilon}),
\tag{PO43}
\]

uniformly for squarefree \(2\le W\le\sqrt{\log X}\). All
constants implicit in this statement come from fixed profiles,
the accepted exponent \(b\), and the arbitrary epsilon loss;
there is no unbounded moving-prime constant.

The exact exponents and gaps are:

| Step | Exponent | Gap below its target |
|---|---:|---:|
| Internal preparation, norm | \(6120551/7000000=.874364428571\ldots\) | \(879/7000000\) below \(a\) |
| Cross-gcd preparation, energy | \(6120551/3500000=1.748728857142\ldots\) | \(879/3500000\) below \(2a\) |
| One cofactor edge | \(b+1/2+.374=1.7489\) | \(1/12500\) below \(2a\) |
| Two cofactor edges | \(1+2(.374)=1.748\) | \(49/50000\) below \(2a\) |
| Nearby completed products | \(1+.7489=1.7489\) | \(1/12500\) below \(2a\) |
| Prime-square sector before the gap | Arbitrary negative power | From (PO27) |

As usual, the displayed strict gaps allow a sufficiently small
positive epsilon to be spent inside the proof. The arbitrary-epsilon
formulations follow by renaming that loss.

Combining (PO35) and (PO43), the full target is equivalent to

\[
|Q_W^{\rm sf}|\ll_\epsilon X^{1.74898+\epsilon}.
\tag{OPEN-PO}
\]

For the reverse direction, (PO43) controls the nonnegative energy;
for the forward direction it controls the modulus of the signed
remainder by that energy plus the absolute error. The norm
comparison (PO35) is applied separately in both directions.

The remainder still contains all original six gcd masks, the
original short-cofactor exclusions, the original finite
\(\ell,m\le J\), the original factor endpoints \(d_i>Y\), and
the broad far completed-product range. It has the additional
allocation-invariant restrictions and is squarefree at the selected
primes in both completed products. One may choose a growing
primorial subject to \(W\le\sqrt{\log X}\); no prime-distribution
asymptotic is needed for this choice or for the proof.

No estimate for (OPEN-PO) is proved here. In particular, local
prime-square cancellation does not estimate the remaining locally
squarefree coefficients, does not provide cancellation in the
fully pairwise-coprime stratum by itself, and does not supply a
new zero-free constant or a finite-height-to-infinite-height
inference. The imported T09 detector and its height and
calibration qualifications remain exactly as stated in the source.
