# Current coherent proof: the accepted local moment and a Gaussian route onward

[private research revision]. The accepted written analytic bound is **c3=125133/1000000=.125133**,
relative to the pinned PR9 framework and Gao's PR15 construction. Thus
zeta and every ordinary Dirichlet L-function are zero-free in
Re(s)>.874867, excluding the principal pole at1. The
[complete credited extension]([private research revision]/gao-window-integration.md)
uses thirty original-width amplifiers on the narrower useful slot window
[.034,.04], with fixed-family local capacity219/50=4.38. Both enlarged
old-moment complements, free shifts and every endpoint branch are paid.
It improves [private research revision] c2=.125128 by .000005 and Gao's
[accepted c_G=.1251134]([private research revision]/gao-local-moment-integration.md)
by .0000196. The old detector and weighted numerator remain in this proof.

The previous **c0=.125113352960035869...** has the
[independent three-kernel receipt]([private research revision]/formal-evidence-update.md).
The new endpoint's full formalization and independent kernel replay
remain pending. OpenAI, Hailey Collet and Akash Levy retain the separate
upstream contributions recorded in the assembly. Historical source and
review statements predating acceptance are preserved as such.

The forward architecture below aims to make a larger improvement easier
to prove. Its analytic reductions are proved; its final signed moment
is open. It replaces the detector upstream of that obstacle and does
not purport to derive Gao's result from an unproved Gaussian estimate.

The main sources are [W35](creative/round35-generation.md) and its
[independent review](creative/round35-review.md). The review proves the
arbitrary-power error extension separately from the author's initial
numerical specialization. The [controller reconstruction]([private research revision]/controller-review.md)
records the checks and the choice of architecture. The previous
[SP proof and signed renewal]([private research revision]/coherent-proof-snapshot.md) remain
available in their original source scope; no comparison of their signed
subfamilies with the new detector is assumed.

## 1. A fixed detector with a complete zero-exclusion return

Fix tau>0 once, independently of all large parameters, and set

    g_tau(v)=(2*pi*tau)^(-1/2) exp(-v^2/(2*tau)),
    A(n)=mu(n)-2*1_(2|n)*mu(n/2),
    G_tau(x)=sum_(n>=1) A(n)g_tau(log(n/x)).                 (G1)

The series and each fixed derivative converge locally uniformly. The
left tail x<=1 is O_tau(exp(-(log x)^2/(2tau))). Indeed log n>=0 and
(log n-log x)^2 >=(log n)^2+(log x)^2, while the remaining n-series is
absolutely convergent. Absolute Fubini on Re s>1 gives

    integral_0^infinity G_tau(x)x^(-s) dx/x
      =exp(tau*s^2/2)*(1-2^(1-s))/zeta(s).                 (G2)

Suppose, for a fixed 0<gamma<1 and every epsilon>0, that

    integral_X^(2X) |G_tau(x)|^2 dx/x
       <<_epsilon X^(2gamma+epsilon)                     (G3)

for all sufficiently large dyadic X. Cauchy–Schwarz on each shell,
followed by a dyadic sum, makes the left side of G2 holomorphic for
Re s>gamma, including all fixed s-derivatives. Choose epsilon smaller
than the distance to the desired boundary. The Gaussian left tail
pays x near zero. Multiplying by zeta continues the identity. The
exponential multiplier never vanishes, and 1-2^(1-s) has no zeros in
0<Re s<1. Thus G3 excludes zeta zeros in gamma<Re s<1; the known right
boundary completes the usual zero-free conclusion. The numerator's
zeros on Re s=1 are not discarded by assertion.

Consequently **any proved gamma<1-c3=.874867 gives a further improvement**. The
convenient target gamma=.87449 would give c=.12551, conditionally on G3.
Nearer targets, gamma=5/6 and gamma=3/4 remain worthwhile. Nothing below
claims G3 at any new exponent. The fixed kernel is essential: a detector
changed with X does not automatically inherit G2's single holomorphic
transform.

## 2. Exact completion and rapidly paid complementary fields

Write L=log X, Y=floor(X^.495), b(ell)=(-1)^(ell+1),
m_Y(n)=mu(n)1_(n<=Y), u_Y=mu-m_Y and q_2=delta_1-2delta_2.
Since mu*b=q_2, the exact convolution identity is

    u_Y*u_Y*b=A-2(m_Y*q_2)+m_Y*m_Y*b.                      (G4)

With S_tau(y)=sum_(ell>=1)b(ell)g_tau(log(ell/y)), it gives

    G_tau(x)=R_Y(x)+2L_Y(x)-I_Y(x),
    R_Y(x)=sum_(d,e>Y)mu(d)mu(e)S_tau(x/(de)),
    I_Y(x)=sum_(d,e<=Y)mu(d)mu(e)S_tau(x/(de)).            (G5)

L_Y is the short m_Y*q_2 term, supported at n<=2Y. Shared primes,
zero Möbius coefficients, both strict lower cuts and every alternating
restoration sign remain literal. The short Gaussian term is not zero.
On [X,2X] it is at most

    O_tau(Y exp(-(.505L-log2)^2/(2tau))),                  (G6)

and hence smaller than every fixed negative power of X. Absolute
convergence before cancellation follows from the d_3(n) majorant.

Here is the estimate that permits growing cutoffs without an unspecified
smoothness constant. Extend h(t)=g_tau(log t) by zero for t<=0. It is
Schwartz and flat at zero. Cauchy's formula on |z-t|=t/2 gives

    ||h^(m)||_1 <= K_tau 4^m m! exp(tau*(m-1)^2/2),
    K_tau=exp((pi^2/8+(log2)^2/2)/tau), m>=1.             (G7)

To check the constant, substitute t=e^v after Cauchy's formula and bound
exp((log2)|v|/tau) by the sum of its two signed exponentials. The two
Gaussian integrals give exactly the extra factor converting 2^m to4^m.
Alternating Poisson summation samples half-integers, so for m>=2,

    |S_tau(y)| <=2K_tau zeta(m)(4/pi)^m m!
       *exp(-(m-1)log y+tau*(m-1)^2/2).                  (G8)

Complete the ell sum before imposing an ell cutoff. With one common
order m=1+floor(.01L/tau), G8 pays I_Y by
exp(-(.01L)^2/(2tau)+O_tau(L log L)), including its Y^2 ordered labels.

For a fixed kappa>0, one common order
m=1+floor(kappa*sqrt L/tau) instead proves

    sum_(d,e>Y,de<=X exp(-kappa sqrt L))
       |mu(d)mu(e)S_tau(x/(de))|
       <= X^(1-kappa^2/(2tau)+o(1)).                     (G9)

The same estimate allows any bounded multiplier independent of ell.
It is not hereditary under arbitrary ell-dependent masks.

For fixed C>0 put B_X=2X exp(C sqrt L). Since
sum_(n<=t)d_3(n)<=t(1+log t)^2, Gaussian tail integration gives

    sum_(n>B_X)d_3(n)g_tau(log(n/x))
       <= X^(1-C^2/(2tau)+o(1))                         (G10)

uniformly on [X,2X]. This pays all omitted labels, including interacting
groups. No assumed cancellation occurs in this tail.

## 3. Four ordinary product-bin diagonals

Let H=kappa*sqrt L, Dmax=B_X/(Y+1), and define exact half-open bins

    i(d)=floor((log d-L/2)/H),
    I_i={d in N:Y<d<=Dmax, i(d)=i},
    J_X=floor((log B_X-L)/H).                            (G11)

Left bin edges are included and right edges excluded; Dmax is the
stated real cap. If i+j<-2 then de<X exp(-H), so G9 pays that entire
discarded source. If i+j>J_X, or d>Dmax or e>Dmax, then de>B_X;
G10 pays it. Therefore

    R_rect(x)=sum_(i+j=-2,...,J_X)
                 sum_(d in I_i,e in I_j)mu(d)mu(e)S_tau(x/(de))
    ||G_tau-R_rect||_(L2([X,2X],dx/x))
       <= X^(q_0+o(1)),
    q_0=max(1-kappa^2/(2tau),1-C^2/(2tau)).               (G12)

This argument bounds the actual discarded original labels. It does not
replace a coupled mask by independent rectangles without paying the
difference. Each retained bin factor is an ordinary Möbius interval;
there is no smooth-part state filter.

Take **C=kappa**. Then J_X=1 for all sufficiently large X. Precisely
the four permitted sums **i+j=-2,-1,0,1** remain, with at most
(.01/kappa)sqrt L+O_kappa(1) nonempty bins and O(sqrt L) ordered
components. This has different asymptotic count from SP's loglog X
times a very large fixed state count; it is not claimed to be uniformly
smaller in cardinality. Its arithmetic factors are simpler.

The ell sum in G12 is still complete. G10 then permits removing
de*ell>B_X at another paid cost. In the resulting finite coefficients

    c_rect,X(n)=sum_(de*ell=n; d in I_i,e in I_j;
                     i+j in {-2,-1,0,1})mu(d)mu(e)b(ell),
                  1<=n<=B_X,                            (G13)

one has |c_rect,X(n)|<=d_3(n) and
ell<=2 exp(3kappa sqrt L). Bin membership and both original lower
cuts are retained. The analogous literal de>X exp(-kappa sqrt L)
truncation has the smaller cap ell<2 exp(2kappa sqrt L); these two
coefficient families must not be interchanged.

## 4. Both height variables and the remaining signed scalar

Fix 0<a<1. For each retained ordered component set

    U_i(s)=sum_(d in I_i)mu(d)d^(-s),
    eta(s)=(1-2^(1-s))zeta(s),
    D_ij(t)=exp(tau*(a+it)^2/2)*eta(a+it)
               *U_i(a+it)U_j(a+it).                    (G14)

The Mellin transform of S_tau is exp(tau*s^2/2)eta(s). Prove this
first on Re s>1 by absolute Fubini, then use its two rapidly decaying
tails to continue before moving the line. An absolutely divergent
ell Dirichlet series is never interchanged on a<1. Mellin inversion
and Plancherel give

    G_ij(x)=(2*pi)^(-1)integral_R D_ij(t)x^(a+it)dt,
    integral_0^infinity |G_ij(x)|^2 x^(-2a)dx/x
       =(2*pi)^(-1)integral_R |D_ij(t)|^2dt.              (G15)

For T=D*sqrt L, define

    Z_X(x)=(2*pi)^(-1)integral_[-T,T]
                    [sum_(i+j=-2,...,1) D_ij(t)]x^(a+it)dt,
    Q_X=integral_X^(2X)|Z_X(x)|^2 dx/x.                 (G16)

Equivalently Q_X is (2pi)^(-2) times the double integral over
[-T,T]^2 of the complete product

    [sum D_ij(t)] conj([sum D_i'j'(t')])
       *((2X)^(2a+i(t-t'))-X^(2a+i(t-t')))/(2a+i(t-t')). (G17)

Every component interaction, complex phase and both independent height
variables remain. The diagonal t=t' has the continuous value of the
displayed kernel; no principal-value convention is needed.

The alternating partial sums imply |eta(a+it)|<=|a+it|/a.
Absolute interval sums and D_i^*D_j^*<=X exp(3kappa sqrt L) then pay
the entire omitted height field by

    X^(1-tau*D^2/2+o(1)).                               (G18)

This proof uses no moving-height Mertens or Hecke estimate.

The required arithmetic statement is now explicit:

**OPEN-GC:** for all sufficiently large dyadic X and every epsilon>0,
prove Q_X <<_epsilon X^(2gamma+epsilon), with these exact coefficients,
bins and fixed parameters. No current theorem supplies a new gamma.

The stronger sufficient **OPEN-GM** asks, for every retained ordered
component, integral_R |D_ij(t)|^2dt <<_epsilon
X^(2gamma-2a+epsilon), uniformly over its moving interval endpoints.
The O(sqrt L) count is subpower, so Cauchy–Schwarz makes it sufficient.
It is not necessary: a proof may use negative cross-component terms.

## 5. No prescribed power error floor

For **any fixed A_0>0**, choose once

    kappa=C=sqrt(2tau(1+A_0)),
    D=sqrt(2(1+A_0)/tau).                               (G19)

Then G9, G10 and G18 all have exponent -A_0. The remaining losses are
O_(A_0,tau)(sqrt L log L)=o(L); Type I and the genuine short term
are smaller still. In particular

    ||G_tau-Z_X||_(L2([X,2X],dx/x))
       <<_(epsilon,A_0,tau,a) X^(-A_0+epsilon).          (G20)

The same holds for the finite physical field using G13. The four
diagonals, subpower restoration, O(sqrt L) bins and O(sqrt L) height
window survive. Eventually T_X>Y^2 since .01L>kappa sqrt L.
Constants and thresholds depend on the fixed choices; A_0, tau and a
may not vary with X in this theorem. A literal O(X^(-A_0)) follows
by applying G20 with A_0+1.

A simple working choice is **tau=1, kappa=C=D=2, a=3/4**.
All discarded fields then have exponent -1. For every fixed gamma>0,
the norm triangle inequality makes OPEN-GC equivalent to G3 up to
the usual arbitrary epsilon. This removes the old positive analytic
error floor from this architecture. It does not estimate Q_X.

For a scalar comparison, the inherited calibration
M(t)=O(t^beta), beta=.8749, implies |G_tau(x)|<<x^beta by Abel
summation and an exponentially weighted Gaussian derivative integral.
If a field approximation error is X^(q+o(1)), q<beta, then

    | ||G_tau||_2^2-||R||_2^2 | <=X^(beta+q+o(1)).       (G21)

Both ordered mixed terms and the error square are included. With G19,
q=-A_0. For an especially low target, G20's norm equivalence avoids
an unnecessarily coarse scalar comparison.

## 6. A second exact target: signed near pairs

For the finite coefficient family G13 the physical Gram kernel is

    K_X(n,m)=g_(2tau)(log(n/m))
       *integral_0^(log2)g_(tau/2)(u-log(sqrt(nm)/X))du.  (G22)

The full energy equals sum c_rect,X(n)c_rect,X(m)K_X(n,m).
The kernel is entrywise positive; its coefficient products are signed.
The true n=m diagonal is X^(1+o(1)): use d_3(n)^2<=d_9(n) and the
divisor-sum bound. For fixed r>0 the complete absolute far-pair sum,
|log(n/m)|>r sqrt L, is at most

    X^(2-r^2/(4tau)+o(1)).                              (G23)

At tau=1, r=2 pays both the diagonal and the far pairs at exponent1.
Thus for gamma>1/2 it suffices to bound the **complete signed
off-diagonal near scalar** at exponent2gamma. This near scalar need
not be nonnegative. Dropping its negative terms or bounding unrelated
positive subblocks does not prove the required upper bound. G22–23
are for the new Gaussian field, not for an SP subfamily.

## 7. The complete problem reduces to one coprime cell

The [coprime reconstruction]([private research revision]/gaussian-coprime-reconstruction.md),
[independent derivation]([private research revision]/gaussian-coprime-independent-review.md)
and [frozen-source comparison]([private research revision]/gaussian-coprime-comparison.md)
give an alternative with every missing comparison paid. Put

    P_Y(x)=sum_(d,e>Y; (d,e)=1; (de,6)=1)
                    mu(d)mu(e)S_tau(x/(de)),
    f_3(n)=mu(rad(n/3^v_3(n))),
    F_6(x)=sum_(n>=1)f_3(n)g_tau(log(n/x)).               (G25)

Here f_3 is multiplicative, takes only the values +1 and -1, and is
not completely multiplicative. Every positive prime power other than
a power of3 contributes one minus sign. This explicitly chosen cell
is not justified by positivity or by an assumed hereditary moment.

Write n_(6)=n/(2^v_2(n)3^v_3(n)). The uncut pair coefficient is
b(n)mu(rad(n_(6)))=f_3(n). In the one-short sum the inner divisor
sum vanishes unless the short divisor is exactly rad(n_(6)). Thus

    P_Y=F_6-2J_Y+I_Y^prim,
    J_Y(x)=sum_n f_3(n)1_(rad(n_(6))<=Y)g_tau(log(n/x)). (G26)

The both-short term I_Y^prim has the same negative-power bound as G8:
the new pair mask is independent of ell. For every fixed delta>0,

    sum_n n^(-delta)/rad(n_(6))
      =prod_(p|6)(1-p^(-delta))^(-1)
       *prod_(p>=5)[1+p^(-1-delta)/(1-p^(-delta))]<infinity.

Together with 1_(rad<=Y)<=Y/rad and the bounded Gaussian exponential
weight, this proves |J_Y(x)|<<_(delta,tau)Y*x^delta. Therefore, on
every real shell X<=x<=2X with its own Y=floor(X^.495),

    |P_Y(x)-F_6(x)| <<_(delta,tau) X^(.495+delta).       (G27)

To recover the whole detector, let k,h be Dirichlet convolution
inverses with Euler factors (z=p^(-s))

    K_p=(1-z)^2,             H_p=(1-z)^(-2),  p=2,3;
    K_p=(1-z)^2/(1-2z),      H_p=(1-2z)/(1-z)^2, p>=5.

The nonconstant factors start at z^2 for p>=5. Since2/sqrt(5)<1,
both sums sum_r |k(r)|r^(-sigma) and sum_r |h(r)|r^(-sigma) converge
for each fixed sigma>1/2. The separate factors at2 and3 are essential.
Direct coefficient identities, including A's original prime-two
coefficients1,-3,2, give

    A=k*f_3,  f_3=h*A,
    G_tau(x)=sum_r k(r)F_6(x/r),
    F_6(x)=sum_r h(r)G_tau(x/r).                         (G28)

These are absolutely justified field identities. For
||V||_sigma=sup_(T>0) T^(-sigma)||V||_(L2([T,2T],dx/x)),
Minkowski gives ||sum c(r)V(./r)||_sigma
<=sum |c(r)|r^(-sigma)||V||_sigma. Both fixed fields have Gaussian
left tails; two neighboring dyadic shells cover every real shell.
Apply this norm theorem to G_tau and F_6, and only then apply G27
on each shell with its own frozen Y. It follows that, for gamma>1/2,

    ||G_tau||_[X,2X] << X^gamma on all large dyadic X
      iff ||F_6||_[X,2X] << X^gamma
      iff ||P_floor(X^.495)||_[X,2X] << X^gamma.          (G29)

The equivalence also holds with an arbitrary epsilon allowance at
gamma=1/2. No exact-power endpoint equivalence there is established.
Convolving a moving-cutoff family with its cutoff held wrong is not
part of this proof.

There is a finite quantitative reconstruction. Fix X_0>=2 and set

    R_X(x)=sum_(r<=X/X_0) k(r)
                      P_floor((X/r)^.495)(x/r).
    ||G_tau-R_X||_[X,2X] <<_epsilon X^(1/2+epsilon).     (G30)

For r<=X/X_0 use G27 and the weighted k norm. For the remaining r,
the fixed F_6 field has bounded t^(-sigma)F_6(t) on0<t<=2X_0;
this pays the whole small-scale tail. Four local product diagonals,
finite caps and height windows transfer by G9--G20 before the outer
r sum. Expanding the resulting scalar retains every r,r' interaction
and both heights, each with its own local window. Under the inherited
beta=.8749 calibration, the complete scalar error in G30 is
O_epsilon(X^(1.3749+epsilon)), including both mixed terms.

The cleanest remaining arithmetic target is therefore

**OPEN-F3:** for a fixed gamma<1-c3=.874867, every epsilon>0 and all large
dyadic X, prove

    sum_(m!=n) f_3(m)f_3(n)K_X(m,n)
           <= C_(epsilon,tau,gamma) X^(2gamma+epsilon). (G31)

K_X is exactly G22, now with the full uncut f_3 coefficient family.
Its true diagonal is O_tau(X). Absolute convergence justifies this
complete signed expansion. No absolute value inside the sum, deletion
of negative terms, favorable subfamily selection or random-sign
assumption is allowed. For gamma>=1/2, G31 is equivalent to the
complete moment target and hence supplies the zero-exclusion return.
An optional finite Gaussian window has paid tails, but its coefficient
list is not identical to the primitive pair list in G25.

The general finite-inverse shortcut is ruled out in a precise scope.
For the actual capped W35 coefficient c_X, weighted divisor matrices
L_sigma(c) and physical Gaussian readout W_X satisfy

    ||W_X[L_sigma(A)-L_sigma(c_X)]e_1||_2 << X^(-A_0+o(1)),
    ||W_X[L_sigma(A)-L_sigma(c_X)]||_(ell2->L2)
                      >>_(tau,sigma) X^(sigma+1/2),     (G32)

for fixed sigma>=0. The lower bound uses positive high-index columns
where the actual product cutoff makes c_X vanish. It does not lower
bound the true detector or contradict G29. A restricted arithmetic
operator argument would require its own readout estimate.

## 8. Paid sectors and literal f3 depth cancellation

The [actual f3 sector proof]([private research revision]/gaussian-signed/report.md) and
[independent reconstruction]([private research revision]/gaussian-controller-review.md)
now pay a common-factor sector of G31 directly. For each r define
f_r(n)=product_(p|n,p not dividing3r)(-1), retaining every prime power,
and let E_r(Y) be its whole Gaussian squared norm on [Y,2Y]. For any
fixed buffered Mertens exponent beta>1-c3 and every epsilon>0,

    T_>=D(X)=sum_(gcd(m,n)>=D)f3(m)f3(n)K_X(m,n)
      =sum_r [sum_(g|r,g>=D)mu(r/g)]E_r(X/r),
    |T_>=D(X)| << X^(2beta+epsilon)D^(1-2beta).          (G33)

This holds for all real D>=1, including D>X. Its diagonal is the
literal sum_(n>=D)K_X(n,n), paid separately. Hence G31 is equivalent
to its complete low-gcd off-diagonal estimate when
theta>(2beta-2gamma)/(2beta-1) and D=X^theta. The exact remainder is

    Q_<D=2 sum_(1<=g<D) sum_(h>=1) sum_((a,h)=1)
                       f_g(a(a+h))K_(X/g)(a,a+h).       (G34)

Both orders, every shift and all prime powers remain. The high-prime
switch comparison S17–S23 in that report also pays
X^(2beta)P^(1-3beta+epsilon), but the resulting signed energy sum
still contains E_1(X) itself. It supplies no bootstrap. Its low-radical
prime-two ray cancellation is real, but that region already has a
smaller positive cost than the current targets.

The [literal f3 renewal theorem]([private research revision]/f3-renewal/report.md), with
[controller reconstruction]([private research revision]/f3-renewal-controller-review.md),
directly handles a different signed partition. Set

    T_z(x)=sum_(#{p>z:p|n}<=1) f3(n)g_tau(log(n/x)),
    P(z)=product_(5<=p<=z)(p-2)/(p-1), t=log z, L=log X.

Uniformly on X<=x<=2X and 4<=t<=L/(1000log L),

    T_z(x)=3log2 P(z)e^(tau/2) x/(log x)^2
                                  *[1+O_tau(t/L)].    (G35)

The full proof gives its second term and prices all smooth cores,
prime powers, Gaussian tails, fixed-order PNT errors and growing
Taylor constants. Its leading reciprocal smooth mass vanishes at
prime2; the first derivative is positive. This is a direct proof on
the actual f3 coefficients, not an inherited masked convolution bound.
If t tends to infinity and both t,2t remain in range, the literal
added band T_(z^2)-T_z is (-1/2+o(1))T_z. All finite cross-Gram
entries are retained. The uncapped source has an infinite dominated
terminal telescoping identity, not an exact finite cutoff.

For the actual full field F and complement R_z=F-T_z, put
a=||T_z||, b=||R_z|| and rho=Re<T_z,R_z>/(ab). Then exactly

    ||F||^2=(a-b)^2+2ab(1+rho).                        (G36)

The accepted baseline already forces the large prefix and its entire
complement to nearly cancel. A proposed gamma improvement requires
BOTH |a-b|<<X^(gamma+epsilon) and
1+rho<<X^(2gamma-2+epsilon)t^2L^4. A leading asymptotic Gram does not
resolve either quantity at that precision. G35 and its negative bands
give no new full-field power estimate by themselves.

## 9. Fixed-power late flow and the square-root critical profile

The [[private research revision] threshold integration]([private research revision]/f3-threshold-integration.md)
and [independent proof]([private research revision]/f3-review/report.md) extend the literal
source in two separate ranges. Keep F, T_z and R_z=F-T_z as above and
L=log X. For fixed 1/3<rho_0<=rho<=rho_1<1/2 and a fixed buffered
mu-Mertens exponent 1/2<beta<1, set eta=(1-2rho_1)(1-beta)/4. Then

    R_(X^rho)(x)=C_f e^(tau/2) B(rho) x/L^3
                        +O(X/L^4+X^(1-eta)L),
    C_f=9log2 product_(p>=5)(1-1/(p-1)^2),
    B(rho)=2log((1-rho)/rho)-2/(1-rho)-1/(1-rho)^2.     (G37)

B is negative and strictly decreasing. Thus the actual band from
X^(3/8) to X^(2/5) is positive, with coefficient
C_f e^(tau/2)[79/225+2log(10/9)]. This sign differs from G35's
subpower bands. The complete tail above any fixed rho_plus>1/2 is
O_A(X^-A), so the band from a fixed rho<1/2 to rho_plus is negative.
No uniformity through rho=1/2 or moving transition has been proved.

The proof uses the actual f=h*mu convolution and the double zero of
its reciprocal series at1: signed reciprocal core moments are0,0,2C_f.
The two-rough-prime source identity is exact only below z^3; its
outside discrepancy, all repeated powers and the artificial p=q
diagonal are paid. Signed Abel summation removes large cores before
both sharp PNT substitutions. A signed Taylor remainder and its
derivative, not an unsigned harmonic estimate, pay O(X/L^4).

There is a separate theorem needing no Mertens or complete-F input.
For fixed tau>0 and kappa>=1, define the absolutely convergent profile

    J(v)=integral_v^infinity e^u(u-v)g_tau(u)du,
    Phi(q)=sum_(r>=1)f3(r)/r J(log(rq)).

Then uniformly on the full shell,

    R_(kappa sqrt(X))(x)=2x/L^2 Phi(kappa^2 X/x)
                                      +O(X/L^3).      (G38)

For kappa^2>=2e^(3tau), Phi(q)>=(3/4)J(log q)>0 throughout
q in [kappa^2/2,kappa^2]. Consequently, for fixed rho_plus>1/2,

    T_(X^rho_plus)-T_(kappa sqrt(X))
       =2x/L^2 Phi(kappa^2 X/x)+O(X/L^3)>0.            (G39)

All continuous-core extension tails and both Stieltjes errors are
absolute here. The global prime-density expansion, after scaling
p,q by sqrt(X), has integrable error O(L^-3); its unordered factor
1/2 times density4/L^2 gives2. The r=1 term dominates the entire
r>=2 profile by a factor at least4/3. This is fixed-kappa positivity,
not a uniform assertion for moving kappa or every threshold jump.

Both source theorems retain all Gram entries, the true original O(X)
diagonal and both independent heights. For the exact split in G36,
b=||R|| is comparable to X/L^d, with d=3 in G37 and d=2 for the
positive G38 profile. A full new 1/2<gamma<.874867 requires BOTH

    |a-b| << X^(gamma+epsilon),
    1+rho << X^(2gamma-2+epsilon)L^(2d).               (G40)

The baseline near cancellation normalized by actual b^2 is distinct
from the additional O(1/L) error introduced by a leading profile.
Neither a logarithmic asymptotic nor its rank-one leading Gram closes
G40 at new power precision. The fixed full-field convolution return
applies after reconstructing F; arbitrary moving masks inherit none.

## 10. Calibration, preserved tools and the next decisive estimate

Abel summation at both sharp interval endpoints using M(t)=O(t^beta)
gives, for a<beta,

    |U_i(a+it)| <<_(a,beta)(1+|t|)(D_i^*)^(beta-a),
    integral_R |D_ij(t)|^2dt <=X^(2beta-2a+o(1)).        (G24)

At a=.75, beta=.8749 this is **.2498**. Target gamma=.87449 needs
**.24898**; the .00082 benchmark gap is unproved. Using the accepted
endpoint with a fixed positive buffer improves the limiting baseline
to2(1-c3)-1.5=.249734, but still proves no further gain. The current
limiting target gap is .000754; a positive buffer is still required.
The exact first-gain condition is gamma<1-c3 for the complete norm,
or a sufficient complete moment exponent strictly below that limiting
baseline, with every transfer paid. No numerical search closes it.

The principal research task is to exploit the four signed diagonals,
the eta factor and the original Möbius coefficients before a positivity
step loses their interactions. OPEN-GC allows that cancellation;
OPEN-GM is an optional stronger route. The fixed Gaussian leaves ample
analytic room for higher targets; it supplies no arithmetic reason that
gamma=.75 is easy.

There is now a paid aggregate-overlap sector in this exact Gaussian
source. For the four original factors n=(d,e,d',e'), set
D(n)=product(n_i)/lcm(n_i), and restrict the complete signed scalar
of G12 to D>=T. The [W36 proof and direct Gaussian adapter](creative/round36-review.md)
give, under the inherited beta=.8749 calibration,

    |Q_(D>=T)| <<_epsilon X^(2beta+epsilon)T^(-(2beta-1)).

At T=X^.0011 the exponent is1.74897522, below the benchmark target
1.74898 by239/50000000. This pays a genuine original scalar sector;
the complete low-D signed scalar remains open. D uses original
incidences, not auxiliary gcd labels introduced in the proof. Neither
sector is assumed positive, and this is not a deletion of a field.
The theorem concerns the four-factor Gaussian source G12; it is not
silently substituted for the different f_3 correlation in G31.

Keep these valid tools available without unproved substitutions:

- [[private research revision] signed renewal]([private research revision]/rough-depth-renewal-review.md) proves
  actual negative prime-threshold bands for the exact SP source. Its
  late flow and any masked source transfer remain open. G35 separately
  proves the literal f3 result with a different leading order and band ratio.
- [W34](creative/round34-review.md) proves current-mask native support
  reductions and a scoped k'+k whole-field comparison. The Gaussian
  coefficients have not inherited those masks or component estimates.
- [H common-divisor review]([private research revision]/h-common-divisor-review.md) pays
  auxiliary composite covariance. All original prime pairs and the
  .004 pressure-cell deficit remain in the unpaid complement.
- [W22](creative/round22-review.md) already has the pole-normalized
  fractional source, semigroup and zero bridge for every fixed real
  alpha>0. W35 adds an explicit Gaussian renewal equation and the
  failure of a particular absolute-contraction argument, not a new
  fractional architecture or an arithmetic saving.

The [maintained attempt index](attempt-index.md) preserves the broader
portfolio, successful interfaces, useful discarded work and exact
reopening conditions. [private research revision] strengthens the complete local-moment
endpoint, proves fixed-power f3 sign reversal and its distinct critical
profile, building on [private research revision]'s paid scalar sector and literal subpower
asymptotics. The full signed moment remains open. No coverage
percentage or new formal-kernel certification follows from these results.


The [[private research revision] H and upstream disposition]([private research revision]/hard-upstream-controller-review.md)
also retains the exact simultaneous interval bound and the reciprocal
Hankel alternative. Its complete D20 moment would give c=.12551 for the
ordinary-character scope, but is open. The [W37 review](creative/round37-review.md)
gives an alternative exact largest-prime boundary organization of G13 and
a directly proved radical-without3 restriction of G33. Neither gives an
additional exponent gain or a hereditary signed-submask comparison.


The [[private research revision] Hankel recovery]([private research revision]/high-ceiling-integration.md) now
removes median and cofactor prerequisites for a distinct imaginary-shift
readout. Its finite face energy is equivalent to the original Gaussian
square moment for each fixed gamma>2/5; all finite leakage is paid. This
identifies the unchanged signed arithmetic rather than a new exponent.
The [W38 review](creative/round38-review.md) gives growing-coordinate
Gaussian marginals, an actual-law determinant obstruction and an exact
full-divisor SDP interface. None estimates the full unexposed parity or
the complete signed Gaussian energy.

statement:
## 4. Uniform discrete cancellation and the full small source

Let

    u=k-(k-1)r=2gamma-r>0,
    eta0=1/(100kpq).

The author's balanced choice is U=V=floor(sqrt(eta0) X^(u/2)). In fact
the proof establishes the following stronger form:

    U,V>=1 and UV<=eta0 X^u imply
    ||S_p,U,V||_1+||S_p,U,V||_2
                      <<_epsilon X^(gamma+epsilon). (R4)

The constants are uniform in such real U,V, even if their ratio grows.

To check (R4), first keep n=de*l<=M. Zero mean gives the literal finite
Fourier expansion b_p(l)=sum_(j=1)^(Q-1) beta_j e(jl/Q), with
sum|beta_j|<=pQ. For D=de<=UV, the phase is

    F_j(t)=jt/Q-(Dt/x)^k/(2pi).

For 1<=t<=M/D and every real x in [X,2X],

    0<=kD^k t^(k-1)/(2pi x^k)
        <= kUV M^(k-1)/(2pi X^k)
        <= k eta0/(2pi) < 1/(2Q).                   (R5)

The power identity u+(k-1)r=k is exact. Therefore F_j' decreases inside
[1/(2Q),1-1/(2Q)]. Integer increments Delta_t=F_j(t+1)-F_j(t), when
both endpoints lie inside the row, are monotone in the same interval.

For z_t=e(F_j(t)), put g(v)=1/(e(v)-1)=-1/2-(i/2)cot(pi v). Then
z_t=g(Delta_t)(z_(t+1)-z_t). Discrete summation by parts bounds any prefix
by two endpoint values of g plus its variation along the monotone
increment sequence, and a possible final atom. The cotangent is monotone
on this interval, so the total is O(Q). Empty and one-atom rows obey the
same bound. This supplies every real upper cutoff; it is not a sampled-x
or continuous-integral substitute for a discrete estimate.

Abel summation with exp(-Dl/x^b), whose derivative is negative, bounded
and actually included, gives O_(p,q)(1) per row. Consequently

    sup_(X<=x<=2X)|S_(n<=M)(x)| <<_(p,q) UV << X^u.

Since r>1 and u=2gamma-r<gamma, this is affordable. The n>M portion is
paid by (R3), including the frequencies where (R5) ceases to hold. The
proof does not treat that alias region as nonstationary or discard it.
For general U,V>=1, U+V<=UV+1, so the complete two short sources also
cost O(X^u+1). This proves the generalization (R4), not just the balanced
instance. It does not permit UV=X^gamma under the same row proof.

statement:
## 6. Complete CORE1 and CORE contracts

Fix0<c<=1/4, gamma=1-c and r=1+c/2. On each dyadic shell, freeze
L=X^gamma and M=X^r BEFORE varying x in[X,2X]. Write exactly

    W=A+T+B,
    A=sum_(n<=L)a_n exp(-n/x^(3/2)-i(n/x)^6),
    T=sum_(L<n<=M)a_n exp(-n/x^(3/2)-i(n/x)^6),
    B=sum_(n>M)a_n exp(-n/x^(3/2)-i(n/x)^6).

statement:
### 2.1 A neutral-prime realization works, but its harmonic price is linear

Choose a prime r with r not dividing q and chi(r)=1 for the particular character.
For all characters modulo q simultaneously, choose r=1 mod q. Such primes exist
by Dirichlet's theorem; see [NIST DLMF27.11](https://dlmf.nist.gov/27.11). Pair each
squarefree q-unit m<=X/r with r not dividing m to rm. The pairings are disjoint.
On each pair orient a differential d from the even-parity basis vector to the
odd-parity vector, with coefficient1; set d=0 on odd vectors and unpaired vectors.
Then d is odd, d^2=0, and it commutes with W_chi. The Laplacian
Delta=dd*+d*d is identity on every pair and zero on every unpaired vector. Its
positive spectral gap is exactly1 whenever X>=r. No estimate of the arithmetic source has been
used in obtaining that gap.

The unpaired basis is exactly

    r not dividing m, (m,q)=1, mu(m)^2=1, X/r<m<=X.

Consequently for every t>=0,

    M_chi(X)=Str(W_chi exp(-t Delta))
            =sum_(X/r<m<=X,(m,qr)=1) mu(m)chi(m).       (19.1)

Both endpoints and the empty-face atom have been accounted for: every m<=X/r
is paired and cancels because chi(r)=1. For chi(r)!=1 the exact extra term is
(1-chi(r)) sum_(m<=X/r,r not dividing m) mu(m)chi(m); it cannot be discarded.

Write d_q=zeta(2)^(-1) product_(p|q) p/(p+1), with empty product1. Elementary
square-divisor counting gives

    #{m<=y:mu(m)^2=1,(m,D)=1}=d_D y+O_D(sqrt(y)).

For completeness, expand mu(m)^2=sum_(d^2|m)mu(d); only (d,D)=1 contributes,
count k<=y/d^2 coprime to D as (phi(D)/D)y/d^2+O_D(1), sum d<=sqrt(y), and
bound the omitted d-tail by O_D(sqrt(y)). Its Euler product is d_D. Hence

    dim ker Delta=d_(qr)(1-1/r)X+O_(q,r)(sqrt(X))
                 =d_q (r-1)/(r+1) X+O_(q,r)(sqrt(X)). (19.2)

Thus phase-preserving cross-integer pairing does repair the chain-map defect,
but its unsigned harmonic price is still linear. This is not a lower bound on
M_chi. At q=1,r=2 its leading rank is2X/pi^2, agreeing with the known squarefree
complex. Björner's [Theorems3.1/3.4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1101.5704v1) give the
classical topology and a stronger error; no literature novelty is claimed for
that case. W27's fixed simplicial contraction and [private research revision] G74 already explain
related harmonic obstructions. Our next calculation allows a different
differential and therefore does not import their fixed-complex rank floor.

### D26.4 Sixth-power extraction and the stronger paid target

Keep the source's b(p) and R=b(p)Q^(3-6s) exactly, and define

    V6(s)=product_(p notin S)(1-R)^-1,
    h(s)=E(s) V6(s) Rhat(s),
    rhat_p=(1-R)(1-tD)h_p.

This is a defined Euler series, not an appeal to an unproved estimate for an angular character. Its coefficients are b(a)(Na)^3 supported at the sixth-power ideals a^6, where b is the completely multiplicative extension of the specified prime values. Thus the absolute coefficient mass of V6 at sigma is sum_a Na^(3-6sigma), finite for sigma>2/3. Its inverse is supported at a^6 with coefficients mu_K(a)b(a)(Na)^3 and has the same positive majorant. These constants are paid in the norm transfer.

The exact local identity is

    rhat_p-1 = [t(1-t)D^2-tR+t^2DR]/(1-D).               (3.8)

For sigma>1/2 its weighted coefficient norm is

    ||rhat_p-1||_sigma
      <= [t(1-t)d^2+t r+t^2 d r]/(1-d)
      = O_sigma(Q^(-1-2sigma)+Q^(2-6sigma)).             (3.9)

The inverse obeys the same large-Q order. Explicitly, writing N=1-(1-t)D-tR,

    rhat_p^-1=(1-D)/[(1-tD)N],
    ||rhat_p^-1-1||_sigma
      <= [t(1-t)d^2+t r+t^2 d r]
         /[(1-t d)(1-(1-t)d-t r)].                     (3.10)

Here r<1, and (1-t)d+t r<(1-t)Q^-1/2+t<1. All local inverses are legitimate. The sums of (3.9)--(3.10) converge for sigma>1/2. In particular Rhat and its inverse have finite coefficient norms there. This does **not** lower the full old/new comparison threshold below 2/3: the extracted V6 still has its sixth-power cost.

Let Rhat_<=P and Rhat_>P retain all local powers, as before. The complete omitted product satisfies

    ||rhat_>P-delta_1||_sigma
       <<_sigma P^(-2sigma)+P^(3-6sigma), sigma>1/2.    (3.11)

For beta>3/4 the first term dominates. Define the second approximant by

    Mellin(What_P)(s)=exp(s^2)E(s)V6(s)Rhat_<=P(s)/L_K^S(s,eta).

The full infinite-prime limit is the same W as in (3.5). Every large-prime interaction is still in Rhat_>P; E and V6 are included at every prime. The inherited M_eta,2 beta bound therefore gives, uniformly in P,

    ||W-What_P||_[X,2X] << X^beta P^(-2beta), beta>3/4. (3.12)

Taking P=max(2,X^theta) gives error exponent qhat=beta-2beta*theta. If the actual full signed norm of What_(max(2,X^theta)) is O_epsilon(X^(gamma+epsilon)) for every positive epsilon and every large dyadic X, and qhat<gamma, then (3.12), D02 and the exact cross-energy identity (3.7) give the common zero-exclusion boundary gamma, provided this hypothesis holds for each fixed target as specified after (2.9). This is **OPEN-W42-sixth**. Its converse follows from a complete M_eta,2 gamma bound because E V6 Rhat_<=P has uniformly bounded coefficient mass at every gamma+epsilon>2/3. Hence it is a concretely different arithmetic representation of the same target exponent, not an established easier theorem.

For the same beta=8749/10000, the stronger strict cutoff thresholds are:

| Desired conditional c | gamma | theta>(beta-gamma)/(2beta) |
|---|---:|---:|
| current c5, comparison | 54679/62500 | 9/437450 |
| near gain .1252 | 2187/2500 | 1/17498 |
| 1/6 | 5/6 | 1247/52494 |
| 1/4 | 3/4 | 1249/17498 |
| formal target 1/3 | 2/3 | 6247/52494, every-epsilon convention |

For example theta=1/16000 already suffices for the near target: qhat=69983251/80000000=.8747906375, and gamma-qhat=749/80000000=.0000093625. All inequalities are strict; equality at a displayed threshold is not claimed. No bound for OPEN-W42-sixth has been proved.

The first useful arithmetic task is to estimate this exact What_P coefficient family, or the distinct W_P family from (3.5), including its full signed energy. A successful source-specific bound would transfer with the stated cost. A better Euler tail by itself, an angular-family label for V6, or a kernel change importing PR15 without its source adapter would not establish a gain.

statement:
## G106. Isolated root of the complete cutoff polynomial

Fix an ordinary character chi, with its natural nonunit zeros, and define

    Z_N(z)=sum_(n<=N,mu(n)^2=1)chi(n)z^omega(n)
          =1+A_N z+R_N(z),
    A_N=sum_(p<=N)chi(p),
    B_N=#{n<=N:mu(n)^2=1,(n,q)=1,omega(n)>=2}.

Then sum_(k>=2)|C_k|<=B_N<=N, and Z_N(-1)=M_chi(N) exactly. This is
the entire hard-cutoff polynomial, not the Euler product over primes<=N.

For Z=1+Az+R, sum|c_k|<=B, |A|>=8 and lambda=B/|A|^2<=1/8,
Rouche on |z|=2/|A| gives exactly one root counted with multiplicity:
the linear term has modulus>=1 and |R|<=4lambda<=1/2. For B>0,
on the circle centered at -1/A with radius2lambda/|A|,
|R|<=lambda(1+2lambda)^2<=25lambda/16<2lambda. Thus this same root
alpha is simple, uniquely nearest to0, and

    |A alpha+1|<=2lambda,
    (1-2lambda)/|A|<=|alpha|<=(1+2lambda)/|A|.

B=0 gives alpha=-1/A directly. Every circle is within |z|<1, so the
quadratic remainder bound is valid. Exact polynomial division gives
Z(z)=(1-z/alpha)Q(z), Q(0)=1, and the complete endpoint comparison

    (|A|/2)|Q(-1)|<=|Z(-1)|<=2|A||Q(-1)|.

The lower bound uses |1/alpha|-1>=4|A|/5-1>=|A|/2; the upper uses
1+4|A|/3<=2|A|. No truncated reciprocal or approximate root is substituted.

For the principal character of fixed q, A_N=P_N is the unramified prime
count. The elementary bound
4^m/(2m+1)<=binom(2m,m)<=(2m)^pi(2m), with m=floor(N/2), yields
P_N>>_q N/log N. Therefore all large N satisfy the lemma, and

    alpha_N=-P_N^(-1)(1+O_q((log N)^2/N)).

Reality follows from conjugation and uniqueness; alpha_N<0. The local
Taylor series log Z_N at0 has radius exactly |alpha_N|. This rules out a
fixed zero-free disk and the straight real path to-1 for these polynomials.
It leaves complex paths, exact deflation and different smoothing eligible.
A fugacity zero is not an L-function zero or a lower bound for M(N).

For every-epsilon exponents, the principal endpoint comparison implies

    M_chi0(N)<<N^(gamma+epsilon)
      iff Q_N(-1)<<N^(gamma-1+epsilon).

A bounded deflated endpoint is insufficient. First gain beyond c10 needs
decay beyond N^(-.12514596), with strict every-epsilon buffering. Targets
1/6 and1/4 require the corresponding power decays.

For arbitrary fixed chi, select the root branch exactly when |A_N|>=8
and |A_N|^2>=8B_N. Otherwise |1-A_N|=O(sqrt N), and
M_chi(N)=1-A_N+R_N(-1). Hence for1/2<gamma<1 the COMPLETE criterion

    root branch: |A_N Q_N(-1)|<<_(chi,epsilon)N^(gamma+epsilon),
    non-root branch: |R_N(-1)|<<_(chi,epsilon)N^(gamma+epsilon)

is equivalent to the all-N Mertens exponent gamma. Arbitrary branch
switches are allowed; neither branch or any exceptional cutoff is omitted.
One common gamma for every fixed ordinary chi gives all-height zero
exclusion through s integral_1^infinity M_chi(x)x^(-s-1)dx=1/L(s,chi),
initially on Re(s)>1 and then by meromorphic identity on Re(s)>gamma.
The principal pole becomes a reciprocal zero. Constants/onsets may depend
on chi; no growing-conductor or Hecke transfer follows.

At gamma=.8748 the conditional c=.1252 exceeds c10 by.00005404;
the non-root prime sector costs exponent1/2. This is a complete conditional
budget, not an achieved bound. The equivalent signed inputs remain OPEN.

There is also a necessary second-root consequence. If an actual principal
Mertens bound of exponent1-c is supplied for every epsilon, then
Q_N(-1)<<N^(-c+epsilon). Since a squarefree integer with D primes is at
least(D+1)!, deg Z_N<=(1+o(1))log N/loglog N. Factoring all roots of Q,
one factor |1+1/zeta| is at most |Q(-1)|^(1/deg Q). For every eta>0,
some root distinct from alpha_N consequently satisfies

    |zeta_N+1|<=2(log N)^(-c+eta)

for all large N. If Q(-1)=0 the conclusion is immediate; degree0 is
eventually excluded by the assumed decay. The upper degree bound has the
right direction because log|Q(-1)| is negative. One root near-1 is not
sufficient: every other factor is still unpaid. No bare strip statement
is silently promoted to the required pointwise Mertens input.

The older fugacity/continued-power/cluster and small-face roots retain
ancestry. The useful increment is the full large-cutoff root with explicit
constants and a two-branch, fully paid deflated source contract.

## 12. Portfolio allocation, promotion and stop rules

**Immediate:** the six contracts in §2. Treat small-gcd physical covariance, H and full-probe/numerator improvements as related alternatives with separate kernels. Keep the completed mean and finite-incidence branch together, while reserving meaningful independent effort for rational scale energy and the triple product. Direct cubic work should now use T05 and target both principal and nonprincipal costs.

**Medium-term:** actual A-dependent calibration; a coefficient-correct restricted trace identity; a Jacobi reconstruction with genuinely independent variables; compatible residue capture/resolvent bounds; a controlled MOB–VAR or MOB–TRI comparison; mixed-cusp tensorization only as a bounded enabling lemma. Promote a lower-ranked branch promptly if it produces a real useful estimate.

**Protected high-upside work:** quadratic \(\theta\approx1\); quadratic-row trilinear sources; a finite cube-deleted trilinear functional; strict shifted-HB or actual arithmetic heat/Jensen control; repaired Hardy geometry and the deflated-target screen; principal-subtracted adaptive prime kernels; a non-diagonal exact arithmetic operator. Each gets a named identity/calibration test before a large analytic allocation. No route is rejected merely because its endpoint exceeds the present cubic transfer range.

**Laboratory F20:** clone an exact finite rule over local rings or \(\mathbb F_q[T]\), \(q\equiv1\pmod6\), including Gauss signs, shared primes, units/infinity analogue, masks and ordered returns. Good tests include the small-gcd kernel's residual direction, mixed \(p^4q^2\) indices, the three-prime cocycle and coherent embedded discrepancies. An analogous bad main term can falsify a matching number-field conjecture; a small function-field sum does not transfer an estimate, and use of function-field RH is not independent evidence for the required number-field argument.

**Promotion standard.** A complete c improvement needs the exact detector theorem, all heights/scales, complete finite sectors, true norms/conductors, main/zero/diagonal terms, derivative costs and strict budget slack. A partial result earns promotion if it pays a named dominant sector with a credible complementary summation, removes an actual prerequisite, or provides a counterexample changing the plan. A new identity with no favorable cost should be retained but not allowed to monopolize the next cycle.

**Stop standards.** Stop a tactic when it reproduces a compensating-coefficient counterexample, unchanged active exponent, forbidden source span, canceled principal signal, unpriced moving level, long dual column or hidden completion zero. Preserve its exact surviving identity and an explicit changed child. Do not reject an entire family from a failure limited to one norm, branch or vector. Conversely, a small improvement over an old upper bound is not useful unless its restored total budget reaches an actual transfer threshold.

## 3. The genuine sextic bank and its recovery factor

Use the [restricted research revision] global primary generators and exact zero-extended symbol
psi_k(a)=chi_a(k). Their multiplicativity eliminates an untracked unit
in the representative of f^2 e^6. On every good ideal, including common
prime factors,

    chi_a(f)^4 chi_a(f^2 e^6)=1_((a,fe)=1).              (R9)

On coprime pairs the exponent is divisible by6; otherwise at least one
positive exponent preserves the symbol's zero. Treating a cancelled
character as the everywhere-one character would be wrong.

For X=Z^N,F=Z^V,E=Z^R define the genuinely new column family

    T_fk(x)=X^-1/2 sum_a mu_K(a)eta(a)1_((a,S)=1)
                  chi_a(k)chi_a(f)^4 g_tau(log(q_a/x)).    (R10)

The non-character column coefficient is independent of live f,k. On
each Gaussian annulus it has the normalized bounded l2 mass required by
the generic sieves. It is NOT the canonical Gauss coefficient a0, the
old physical numerator, or G115's completed Mobius divisor sum. The
ordinary source has not thereby acquired a native sextic identity.

At k=f^2e^6, T_fk=X^-1/2 U_rad(fe). For each fixed f the map e to k
is injective by ideal valuations, and q_k<=4F^2E^6. The exact selected
pair count is N_F N_E; possible repetitions across different f remain
distinct entries of the joint bank. With M=2V+6R and

    B_FE(X)=(N_F N_E)^(-1) sum_(f,e) ||U_rad(fe)||_2^2,
    J(X)=F^-1 sum_f sum_(q_k<=4Z^M) ||T_fk||_2^2,

positive enlargement gives

    B_FE(X) <= C_S X E^-1 J(X).                          (R11)

This is the actual recovery factor. There is no Urow^-1 divisor, no
additional division by F after F^-1 already normalized the f count,
and no discarded inducing/principal rows. Jensen and shell Cauchy give
||P_FE||_1<=sqrt(log2) sqrt(B_FE), so a complete B bound of exponent
2gamma suffices for(R7).

The Gaussian is handled by a complete annular decomposition: the j-th
profile and each prescribed derivative have polynomial-in-j times
exp(-c j^2) norms, while sieve prices grow at most exponentially in|j|.
Minkowski sums all annuli. Alternatively a C sqrt(log Z) annular cutoff
has arbitrarily small power tails by the absolute source bound. No tail,
short source or extra height/profile dependence is left out.

Conditional on the two named sieve inputs, [restricted research revision] applies to this fixed
coefficient class, and gives J<<Z^(Emix+epsilon), where

    Emix(M,N,V)=sup_(0<=t<=M) [(M-t)/6+min(C(t,N),t+L)],
    C(t,N)=max(t,N,5t/6+N/3,t/3+5N/6),
    L=max(0,N-V,(2N-V)/3).                              (R12)

Both estimates inside the minimum see the SAME complete positive norm
and the same fixed hole on each repetition layer. The cubic average
does not permit f-dependent coefficients. In particular substituting
k=f^2 BEFORE applying a free f-average cancels the character phase;
it does not leave an independent cubic family. A source-specific bound
on that correlated diagonal would be new arithmetic, not [restricted research revision] again.

Since C(V,N)>=N and V+L>=N, the member t=V gives

    N+Emix(2V+6R,N,V)-R >= 2N+V/6.                     (R13)

This obstructs THIS certificate below gamma=1 even before(R8). The two
author examples convert correctly to gamma97/96 and169/168. These are
upper-bound prices, not lower bounds on the actual Mobius norm.

For S13, use exactly the augmented finite cutoff complex with basis all squarefree unramified prime sets of product<=X, including the empty set, parity |S| and oriented deletion d. ## 2. Exact source and statement of the refined return

Fix tau>0. Let a(n) be ANY complex sequence with |a(n)|<=1 for n>=1, extended by zero for n<=0. For x>0 put

    g(v)=(2 pi tau)^(-1/2) exp(-v^2/(2 tau)),
    f_x(t)=g(log(t/x)) for t>0, and f_x(t)=0 for t<=0,
    F_a(x)=sum_(n>=1) a(n) f_x(n).

All the series below converge absolutely. The exact existing G72 objects are

    B_H(k)=sum_(j=0)^(H-1) a(k-j),
    w_X(k)=exp(-log(k/X)^2/(4 tau)),
    E_a(X,H)=(1/H) sum_(k>=1) |B_H(k)|^2 w_X(k).             (1)

Here H is an integer >=1, and every k>=1 is retained. In particular the first partial block, the zero extension, all character zeros and both infinite tails are part of (1). Its exact signed correlation expansion is the G72 expansion; no triangular constant weight is substituted and no cross term is removed.

Let h_tau(t)=g(log t), extended by zero for t<=0, and define the finite constants

    J_j(tau)=integral_0^infinity |h_tau^(j)(t)| dt,
    ell=log 2,
    K_tau=sqrt(2 pi tau) exp(tau/2)+2,
    C_(tau,r)=(2^r-1) sqrt(K_tau/(2 pi tau))
                       exp(3 ell^2/(2 tau)).

The zero extension of h_tau is C-infinity and Schwartz: each derivative on t>0 is t^(-j) times a fixed polynomial in log t times the Gaussian. This also proves every J_j finite, without an unspecified scale-dependent smoothness constant.

**Theorem W48.1 (fixed-order corrected window return).** For each integer r>=1, X>=1 and integer H>=1 satisfying 2rH<=X,

    sup_(X<=x<=2X) |F_a(x)|
      <= C_(tau,r) sqrt((X/H) E_a(X,H))
       + ((H-1)/2)^r [J_r X^(1-r)+J_(r+1) X^(-r)]
       + rH (2^r-1) g(0)
            exp(-log(X/(2rH))^2/(2 tau)).                    (2)

All constants are independent of a,X,H. The integer r and tau are fixed parameters; this statement does not claim controlled constants for r growing with X. Unlike a formal inverse of a box kernel, the proof gives an exact finite identity and a separately bounded residual. The positive energy in (1) is unchanged.

statement:
### B3. Strongest objection: actual cumulative inputs have bounded increments

The independent-state norm permits unrealistic adjacent oscillations. A source-specific proof could exploit them being cumulative sums. The following free-exploration test shows that adding only bounded increments and natural zeros still does not repair this centered contraction certificate.

Fix1/2<beta<1 and

    0<alpha<(1-beta)/(2-beta).                              (B11)

For every sufficiently large integer N there exists a SYNTHETIC coefficient sequence b_N(n), depending on N, with

    |b_N(n)|<=mu(n)^2 1_((n,q)=1),
    F_m=sum_(n<=m)b_N(n), |F_m|<=m^beta,
    |J_N(F)| >= c_(q,beta,alpha) N^(beta+alpha(1-beta)).     (B12)

It is essential that b_N is not claimed to have the fixed Mobius signs or the Mobius convolution law. This is a kinematic counterexample to a particular enlarged norm certificate, not a counterexample to the desired arithmetic estimate.

Here is a complete construction. Let

    Q_q(x)=sum_(n<=x)mu(n)^2 1_((n,q)=1)
          =kappa_q x+O_q(sqrt x),
    kappa_q=zeta(2)^(-1)product_(p|q)p/(p+1)>0.              (B13)

This elementary count follows by inserting mu(n)^2=sum_(e^2|n)mu(e), counting q-unit multiples with error O_q(1), and paying the sum of at mostsqrt x errors and the convergent e^-2 tail. No prime distribution theorem is used.

For each unramified prime power2<=d<=floor(N^alpha), set m_d=floor(N/d), H_d=floor(m_d^beta/8), and

    B_d(n)=max(0,H_d-|Q_q(n)-Q_q(m_d)|).

Each B_d is a triangular bump in the actual squarefree q-unit count. Its integer increment has modulus at most mu(n)^2 1_((n,q)=1), exactly0 at every natural-zero site. Since beta>1/2, (B13) puts its support within m_d+O_q(H_d). Since beta<1, every supported n is comparable to m_d and B_d(n)<=n^beta for large N.

The nearest possible distinct centers are separated by a constant multiple of N/d^2. Their support-width-to-separation ratio is at most a constant times

    N^(beta-1)d^(2-beta)
      <=N^(beta-1+alpha(2-beta)) ->0                       (B14)

by(B11). Thus the supports, including their increment boundaries, are disjoint. Under u->floor(N/u), the support of each bump lies in an interval around the corresponding integer d of width O_q(N^(beta-1)d^(2-beta)+d^2/N)=o(1), uniformly in d. Hence its only integer contact is d itself. It does not couple to another prime power or hide an omitted integer atom.

Put

    F_n=sum_d conj(chi(d)) B_d(n), b_N(n)=F_n-F_(n-1), F_0=0.

The preceding disjointness proves every natural-zero, increment and growth condition in(B12), including extension by0 before and after the finite supports. Each discrete atom in(B2) contributes exactly Lambda(d)H_d, a positive real number. For nonprincipal chi the drift is absent. For principal chi all selected phases equal1; each continuous contribution is at most H_d times its o(1) u-width, hence at most Lambda(d)H_d/2 eventually. Therefore

    |J_N(F)|>= (1/2)sum_d Lambda(d)H_d
       >> N^beta sum_(d<=N^alpha,(d,q)=1)Lambda(d)d^(-beta)
       >> N^(beta+alpha(1-beta)).                          (B15)

The same elementary Chebyshev estimate proves the last step. All bumps lie at states at least a constant multiple of N^(1-alpha). Thus any prescribed zero-error prefix m<=N^theta with theta<1-alpha is also preserved. One may choose alpha smaller to accommodate any fixed theta<1.

After dividing by log N, this norm still grows by N^(alpha(1-beta))/log N. At a near-current beta the admissible alpha is small but positive. The construction explicitly answers the bounded-jump/natural-zero objection; fixed signs, multiplicativity, the exact convolution inverse, and correlations tied to the actual single arithmetic source are the indispensable remaining escapes. No conclusion is drawn against those escapes.
title: B3. Strongest objection: actual cumulative inputs have bounded increments

## 1. Literal primitive cell and its exact contraction

Fix tau>0 and theta=.495. Put Y=floor(X^theta), and retain the W35
g_tau, S_tau, b(ell)=(-1)^(ell+1), A(n)=mu(n)-2*1_(2|n)mu(n/2).
Write n_(6)=n/(2^{v_2(n)}3^{v_3(n)}), and set

    f_3(n)=mu(rad(n/3^{v_3(n)}))
          =b(n)*mu(rad(n_(6))).                         (GC1)

Thus f_3(n) is always +1 or -1. At 3^j it is +1; at every other
positive prime power it is -1. It is multiplicative but not completely
multiplicative. Prime powers have not been set to zero.

Consider the following literal mask of the original two Mobius factors:

    P_Y(x)=sum_{d,e>Y; (d,e)=1; (de,6)=1}
                      mu(d)mu(e) S_tau(x/(de)).          (GC2)

This is a changed, explicitly specified original-pair cell, not a
claimed hereditary bound for the full W35 field. In particular, it is
not the current-SP mask or RN source. All original coefficients inside
this cell, complete alternating restoration and strict lower endpoints
remain. All series below converge absolutely before the finite divisor
identities are used: the coefficient majorant is at most d_3(n),
which the Gaussian in log(n/x) dominates.

Define

    F_tau(x)=sum_{n>=1}f_3(n)g_tau(log(n/x)),
    J_Y(x)=sum_{n>=1}f_3(n)1_{rad(n_(6))<=Y}
                                  g_tau(log(n/x)),
    I_Y^prim(x)=sum_{d,e<=Y; (d,e)=1; (de,6)=1}
                            mu(d)mu(e)S_tau(x/(de)).

The exact identity is

    P_Y=F_tau-2J_Y+I_Y^prim.                             (GC3)

Proof of the uncut coefficient: d and e are odd, hence b(n/(de))=b(n)
whenever de divides n. At each prime p>=5 dividing n, the allowed local
allocations to the coprime squarefree pair (d,e) are neither, d alone,
or e alone. Their signed sum is 1-1-1=-1. Primes 2 and 3 cannot be
allocated. The coefficient is exactly b(n)mu(rad(n_(6)))=f_3(n).
This treats every original prime power and the ordered-pair convention.

For the one-short source d<=Y, fix an allowed d dividing n. The inner
sum over e cancels unless d contains every prime p>=5 dividing n:
each missing prime contributes 1-1=0. Since d is squarefree and
6-free, the surviving d is exactly rad(n_(6)); its coefficient is
mu(d)b(n). Thus the one-short source equals J_Y, with the exact <=Y
endpoint. Inclusion-exclusion of the two lower cuts proves GC3.
No infinite Dirichlet series was moved to a new line in this argument.

statement:
# [private research revision]: exact prediction criterion with paid source formation

Accept G128-G130 from the frozen [W54 author](wild54/report.md) and
[independent review](wild54-review/report.md). These give a literal
ordinary-character prediction problem, a faster complete source-tail
bound, and two scoped obstructions that redirect the search to signed
arithmetic correlations. They prove no larger c. The source-relative
c11=312864909/2500000000=.1251459636 and inherited F0/analytic,
positive-slot and external definition/import/admission obligations stay
unchanged. No formalization, kernel action or new proof packet occurred.

## G128. Source, prediction and an exact zero census

Fix an ordinary Dirichlet character chi modulo q with natural zero
extension. Write delta=1 for the principal character and0 otherwise,
r=delta*phi(q)/q, A(x)=sum_(n<=x)chi(n), b(t)=A(exp t)-r exp t.
Periodicity gives |b|<=q. Abel summation initially for Re s>1 gives

    H(s)=integral_0^infinity exp(-st)b(t)dt
        =L(s,chi)/s-r/(s-1).

The integral continues H to Re s>0. Use the literal normalized source

    F_chi(s)=((s-1)/(s+1))^delta L(s,chi)/s.       (1)

At the principal pole its removable value is r/2, nonzero. Nonprincipal
characters receive no spurious factor s-1. All natural L-zeros in Re>0
and their multiplicities survive. No Hecke or growing-conductor transfer
is asserted. The causal inverse Laplace source is

    f(t)=b(t)                                       nonprincipal,
    f(t)=r exp(-t)+b(t)-2 integral_0^t exp(-(t-u))b(u)du
                                                   principal. (2)

Thus |f|<=C_q=1+3q. For principal chi, direct substitution gives

    f(log x)=2/x sum_(n<=x)n chi(n)-A(x)
            =A(x)-2/x integral_1^x A(y)dy.            (3)

For q=1 this is m(m+1-x)/x, m=floor x, a bounded nonnegative source.
Positivity is insufficient: the bounded positive delayed exponential
exp(-bt)+C exp(-b(t-T))1_(t>=T), C>1, has Laplace transform
(1+C exp(-sT))/(s+b) and zeros with positive real part log(C)/T.
That is a counterexample to a positivity-only inference, not an
arithmetic lower bound for (3).

Fix0<gamma<1, a=2-gamma, s(z)=gamma+a(1+z)/(1-z). Put
F(z)=F_chi(s(z)), F0=F_chi(2)!=0, the latter by the convergent Euler
product. F belongs to H-infinity since |F_chi(s)|<=C_q/Re s. Define

    f_gamma(t)=exp(-gamma t)f(t),
    h(t)=sqrt(2a) integral_0^t exp(-a(t-u))f_gamma(u)du,
    Qv=v-2a exp(-a t)*v,      ell0(t)=sqrt(2a)exp(-at),

with causal convolution on[0,infinity). Q is an L2 isometry: its boundary
Laplace multiplier is (it-a)/(it+a). Also Q*ell0=0 and ||ell0||=1.
The Cayley Jacobian a/[pi(a^2+t^2)] and Plancherel give exactly

    ||p(Q)h||_2^2=||pF||_H2^2,
    ||p(Q)h-F0 ell0||_2^2=||pF-F0||_H2^2.           (4)

Every output tail and cross term is included. No equivalent positive
metric mI<=P<=MI can give Q*PQ<=kappa P with kappa<1: iterate and
use Q's isometry to contradict m<=kappa^n M. This does not prohibit
source-specific signed polynomial cancellation.

Define the constrained prediction problem

    d_N=min_(p(0)=1,deg p<=N)||pF||^2,
    Delta_N=d_N-|F0|^2=min ||pF-F0||^2.              (5)

The equality follows from the exact constant coefficient. The full
Toeplitz Gram has G_jk=integral conjugate(z^jF)z^kF dm, so its quadratic
form is p*Gp. G is positive definite and d_N=1/(G^-1)_00. Delta_N>=0
decreases, but positivity supplies no convergence to zero.

For a hypothetical zero rho=beta+iT with beta>gamma set
w=(rho-gamma-a)/(rho-gamma+a), nonzero since the anchor2 is safe.
The complete error e=pF-F0 has e(0)=0, e(w)=-F0. Cauchy-Schwarz in zH2
therefore gives

    Delta_N>=|F0|^2(1-|w|^2)/|w|^2
       =4a|F0|^2(beta-gamma)/[(beta-gamma-a)^2+T^2]. (6)

A qualitative Delta_N->0 for each fixed chi at one common gamma
excludes every finite-height zero in Re>gamma. No exchange with a height
supremum is needed. A fixed nonzero residual bound does not suffice,
because the floor decays like T^-2.

The independent review proves the converse for this actual source.
The classical input is canonical inner/outer factorization and outer
cyclicity in H2; see Garcia and Ross, [Theorems2.12,2.16,2.20 and
formula2.10](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1312.5018). For F=IO, the closure of
polynomial multiples is IH2. Any admissible limit Iu has
u(0)=F0/I(0)=O(0), hence norm at least |O(0)|. Outer cyclicity gives
polynomials q_k with Fq_k->IO(0); evaluation at0 shows q_k(0)->1.
Renormalizing by these constants yields admissible approximants. Thus

    Delta_infinity=|F0|^2(|I(0)|^-2-1).             (7)

Here the singular inner factor is absent, for a reason specific to(1).
F continues across every boundary point except1. A singular measure in
its inner factor can be supported only on boundary zeros and1. One
direct justification: on each closed zero-free continued arc, |F| is
bounded below in an inner neighborhood, while |F|<=||F||_infinity
exp(-P[nu]). The Poisson integral of nu is consequently bounded there.
Weak boundary convergence then makes nu absolutely continuous on each
smaller arc; its singular restriction is zero. The remaining boundary
zeros away from1 are isolated and countable, so nu is purely atomic.
An atom c at zeta forces |F(r zeta)|<=||F||_infinity
exp[-c(1+r)/(1-r)]. At zeta!=1 this contradicts a finite-order analytic
zero; at1 it contradicts F_chi(sigma)~1/sigma as sigma->infinity,
which follows from chi(1)=1 and the literal Dirichlet series. Hence
nu=0. This also explains why mere zero-freeness would be insufficient
for an arbitrary bounded analytic source.

The inner factor is therefore exactly the Blaschke product of the
zeros rho_j in Re>gamma. With w_j their Cayley images,

    Delta_infinity=|F0|^2[product_j |w_j|^-2-1].     (8)

The product is positive and convergent by the bounded-source Blaschke
condition and F0!=0; multiplicities are retained. Boundary zeros create
no singular atom. Equation(8) makes Delta_N->0 equivalent to the
desired zero exclusion for this character. It is a precise criterion,
not a claim that the arithmetic difficulty has disappeared.

### A complete and faster source-tail bound

Let H0=sqrt(2a)C_q/(a-gamma), K=1+2a/(a-gamma). Then
|Q^j h(t)|<=H0 K^j exp(-gamma t). The omitted Gram beyond T is PSD
and at most (N+1)H0^2 K^(2N)exp(-2gamma T)/(2gamma) times I. For an
explicit polynomial, its complete squared error is at most

    integral_0^T |p(Q)h-F0 ell0|^2 dt
      +H0^2(sum_j |p_j|K^j)^2 exp(-2gamma T)/gamma
      +2|F0|^2 exp(-2aT).                           (9)

The exponential degree cost can instead be paid by a coherent source
approximation. If ||h-h_tilde||<=tau, the isometry gives

    ||p(Q)(h-h_tilde)||<=tau sum_j |p_j|.           (10)

Every Gram-entry error is <=tau(||h||+||h_tilde||), and its operator
error is at most N+1 times that amount. This is an absolute error,
not a PSD ordering of the two Grams. Even a compactly supported
h_tilde has full filtered future responses, which must be included.

For1/2<gamma<1 put lambda=a-gamma=2-2gamma in(0,1). At q=1, with
u={x}, f(log x)=1/2+B(x)-V(x)/x, B=1/2-u, V=u(1-u). The bounded
primitive of B is V/2, of norm<=1/8. Integrating by parts with its
lower endpoint, then paying V/x absolutely, proves

    |integral_x^infinity y^(lambda-1)(f(log y)-1/2)dy|
        <=D_lambda x^(lambda-1),
    D_lambda=(2-lambda)/[4(1-lambda)].              (11)

Thus h(t)=A0 exp(-gamma t)+C exp(-at)+R(t),
A0=sqrt(2a)/(2lambda), |R(t)|<=sqrt(2a)D_lambda exp(-(gamma+1)t).
Keep h unchanged on[0,T] and continue explicitly by

    h_tilde(t)=A0 exp(-gamma t)
       +(h(T)-A0 exp(-gamma T))exp[-a(t-T)]  for t>T.

Subtracting the expansions at t and T and paying both L2 tails yields

    ||h-h_tilde||<=D_lambda[1+sqrt(a/(gamma+1))]
                            exp[-(gamma+1)T].     (12)

No unknown infinite constant C is needed for this continuation.

All ordinary characters have the same construction. For nonprincipal
chi, A is q-periodic; subtract its mean m_chi. The mean-zero remainder
has primitive bounded by2q^2. For principal chi let B0=A-rx, beta its
period mean, D(x)=integral_1^x(B0-beta). Directly from(3),

    f(log x)=-beta+(B0(x)-beta)+(r+2beta-2D(x))/x.  (13)

The bounds |D|<=2q^2 and |r+2beta-2D|<=1+2q+4q^2 give(11)-(12)
with A0=sqrt(2a)m_chi/lambda and D_chi=4q^2 for nonprincipal chi,
or D_chi=4q^2+(1+2q+4q^2)/(1-lambda) for principal chi. Natural zeros
and complex components are retained. Fixed-q constants are allowed.
The constants blow up at gamma=1/2; no endpoint claim is made.

This adapts [private research revision]'s bounded-periodic-primitive method to the exact
pole-normalized source. It pays source formation, with the coefficient
sum in(10), but leaves the full signed prediction residual OPEN.

### Finite optimization and interpolation do not pay that residual

Every finite constrained minimizer has all roots outside the closed
disk, for any nonzero F with F0!=0. If p=(z-z0)q, variation by zq
preserves p(0)=1. Orthogonality and strict Cauchy-Schwarz for qF,zqF
give |z0|>1. This is classical optimal-polynomial ancestry; see
[Beneteau et al., Theorem3.2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1509.04807), with the
present constrained version proved directly in the retained report.

For F=1-z/r the size-m Gram determinant is sum_(k=0)^m r^(-2k),
so d_N is the ratio of the size N+1 and N determinants. Its limit is
r^-2 for r<1 and1 for r>=1. Grams for r and1/r differ by a scalar,
and hence give identical constrained minimizers despite different
interior zero geometry. For the inner source (z-r)/(1-rz), the Gram is
I while Delta_N=1-r^2. Stable roots and conditioning are insufficient.

If the full error e vanishes at finitely many safe nodes, including0,
form their finite Blaschke product B, including multiplicity. Then
e/B is in H2 with exactly the same norm, and at a hypothetical source
zero w away from those nodes,

    ||e||^2>=|F0|^2(1-|w|^2)/|B(w)|^2.             (14)

There is no extra norm charge for dividing an error already in BH2.
For F=1-z/r, its finite Taylor inverse gives e=-(z/r)^(N+1), so exact
finite matching can coexist with growing full error. Fixed-anchor
amplification at height T costs degree of order T^2/(beta-gamma).
Other node geometries remain eligible only with a paid full residual.

## G129. Actual divisor Bellman identity and a scoped price

Set a(n)=mu(n)chi(n), c(n)=chi(n). Their Dirichlet convolution is delta
on every integer, with ramified zeros retained. Thus a(1)=1 and
a(n)=-sum_(d|n,d<n)a(d)chi(n/d). Let x_n=(a(1),...,a(n)) and T_n
append this exact signed divisor row. With ell_N=(1,...,1), a sufficient
Hermitian Bellman certificate is

    P_n>=0, P_N>=ell_N*ell_N,
    T_n*P_nT_n<=P_(n-1)+E_n.

The debts E_n may be signed. Evaluation on the actual source telescopes:

    |M_chi(N)|^2<=x_1*P_1x_1
          +sum_(n=2)^N x_(n-1)*E_n x_(n-1).        (15)

An O_(chi,epsilon)(N^(2gamma+epsilon)) bound on the entire right side
gives Mertens exponent gamma and ordinary zero exclusion by Abel
continuation. For a reachable-state version, inequalities need hold
only after evaluation on the actual x; global matrix inequalities are
a stronger sufficient condition, not an assumption forced on that route.

The exact backward row is

    w_(N,n)(d)=sum_(j<=n/d)chi(j)M_chi(floor(N/(dj))). (16)

For an arbitrary prefix, form b(k)=sum_(d|k)x_d chi(k/d) for k<=n,
and0 for k>n. Its unique recurrence continuation is b*(mu chi).
Sum through N and reorder to obtain(16). Hence w_(N,N)=ell_N,
w_(N,n-1)=w_(N,n)T_n and w_(N,1)=M_chi(N). The no-debt metric
P_n=w_(N,n)*w_(N,n) is exact but starts with the unknown |M(N)|^2.
It locates the missing signed response; it is not a noncircular estimate.

Even after deleting all forced-zero coordinates, a global diagonal
terminal majorant has exponent-two price. Let I={n<=N:a(n)!=0}, K=|I|.
For D=diag(d_i)>0, D>=ell_I*ell_I is equivalent to sum 1/d_i<=1.
The actual terminal energy is sum d_i>=K^2, with equality d_i=K.
Squarefree q-unit counting gives

    K=kappa_q N+O_q(sqrt N),
    kappa_q=zeta(2)^-1 product_(p|q)(1+1/p)^-1>0.

Expand squarefreeness as sum_(d^2|n)mu(d), count q-units, and pay the
sqrt N counting errors and d^-2 tail. The resulting Theta_q(N^2)
price applies to this specified global diagonal class only. It is not
a lower bound on Mertens sums or every source-specific reachable metric.
Signed off-diagonal geometry and a usable reachability description remain
open. This specializes the earlier magnitude-only obstruction to the
literal divisor cocycle and its complete adjoint.

## G130. Raw principal finite-polynomial global contraction fails

For principal chi,0<gamma<1, let P(s) be a finite Dirichlet polynomial.
If R=1-L(s,chi)P(s) is bounded and holomorphic on the whole half-plane
Re>gamma, its pole at1 forces P(1)=0. If P=0 the norm is1. Otherwise
finite-frequency torus recurrence supplies unbounded T_k with
P(s+iT_k)->P(s) locally uniformly. Choose a disk centered at1 inside
the half-plane, with no P-zero on its boundary. Rouche supplies a zero
of P(s+iT_k) inside the disk. Translating back produces P-zeros with
unbounded heights away from the unique L-pole; at each, R=1. Therefore

    sup_(Re s>gamma)|1-L(s,chi)P(s)|>=1.            (17)

If the pole is not removed the supremum is infinite. Thus no sequence
of finite members yields globally uniform strict contraction in this
raw principal formulation. This does not obstruct compact convergence,
an open strip gamma<Re<1, one line, infinite filters, or the normalized
source(1). In particular the older W37 open-strip proposal excludes the
pole and is not rejected by(17). The escape is explicit, not a universal
Bezout impossibility claim.

## Evidence, preserved candidates and next estimate

Author R11/X26/X28 form one coherent architecture, with three bounded
developments. R16's lawful-state compression, F04's true-prefix
commutation and X30's weighted chain-map failure are scoped duplicates
with their broader signed alternatives retained. The independent blind
audits are X23 and F06, after skipping the author's six by frozen rules.
All30 dispositions and the complete29-family/109-child portfolio remain.
Literal22/12/25 sampling pools include every eligible group; saved draws
replay R16/F04/X28. The prospective entropy-procedure correction is
retained, not retroactively erased.



The live inputs are a noncircular signed prediction bound forcing
Delta_N->0, or a signed Bellman budget at a common gamma<.8748540364.
Gamma5/6 and3/4 retain the1/6 and1/4 targets. The faster source
continuation removes a concrete formation burden; exact zero census
and the scoped obstructions prevent false progress from stable roots,
positive Grams, finite interpolation or global raw polynomial contraction.

statement:
## 4. A polynomial dual truncation, including its error

At `Re(1-z)=1-a<1`, the dual L-series is not expanded as an infinite
absolutely convergent series. Take
\[
V(x)=\frac1{2\pi i}\int_{(d)}\frac{e^{w^2}}w x^{-w}\,dw,
\qquad d>a,
\]
and choose uniformly on the fixed core dyad
\[
N=(CE)^2T^4.
\]
This smoothing is bounded at zero and decreases faster than every
power at infinity. For every fixed `J>=2`,
\[
\begin{aligned}
L(1-z,\bar\eta)
={}&\sum_{\mathfrak n}\bar\eta(\mathfrak n)
q_{\mathfrak n}^{z-1}V(q_{\mathfrak n}/N)\\
&+O_J\!\left((CE)^{J+a-1/2}N^{-J}
T^{2J+2a-1}\right).
\end{aligned}
\tag{BC9}
\]
To prove this, start with the Mellin integral of
`L(1-z+w,bar eta) N^w exp(w^2)/w` on `Re w=d`. Its series there
converges absolutely. Shift to `Re w=-J`; only `w=0` contributes a
residue, since the dual L-function is nonprincipal. The ordinary
functional equation bounds the new line by conductor power
`(CE)^(J+a-1/2)` and height power `T^(2J+2a-1)` after integrating
the Gaussian vertical damping.

Since `|A(a+it)|<<T^(1-2a)`, multiplication by the outside
`A(z)(q_cq_e)^(1/2-z)` makes the error
\[
O_J((CE)^{-J}T^{-2J}).
\tag{BC10}
\]
DC10 and absolute core counting make this error harmless, retaining
both original core tails. Here `q_cq_e` and `CE` differ by fixed
dyadic constants only.

For the main series, ideal counting gives the absolute dual mass with
a subpower conductor cost:
\[
\sum_{\mathfrak n}q_{\mathfrak n}^{-1+a+\delta}
|V(q_{\mathfrak n}/N)|
\ll_{a,\delta}N^{a+\delta}.
\tag{BC11}
\]
Thus the truncation contributes only `(CE)^(O(a+delta))` and a
polynomial in `T`. The constants may deteriorate as `a` or `delta`
tends to zero. They need not be uniform there: both parameters are
fixed in terms of the final loss before any scale varies.

statement:
## G191. Complete periodic cofactor estimate for fixed b,k

Fix b>1, an integer k>=4 and a bounded mean-zero Q-periodic h. For X>=2,
any finite real D>=1, and any complex bank |A_m|<=A fixed before real x varies,
put

    f_x(n)=exp(-n/x^b-i(n/x)^k),
    H_D(x)=sum_(m<=D) A_m sum_(l>=1)h(l)f_x(ml).

With both norms on the entire shell [X,2X], measure dx/x,

    ||H_D||_1+||H_D||_2 << A(D+X^(b/2))log^4(2X).          (191.1)

Constants depend only on the fixed data. No growing b,k,Q, live-x bank,
arbitrary joint mask, or infinite undamped row bank is asserted. Divisor losses
become X^epsilon only over ranges bounded by a fixed power of X.

Here are the complete changes to G188's proof. Use the exact smooth partition
phi(n/X)+sum_(N=2^jX)w(n/N)=1, with w supported in[1,4]. Low rows m<=delta X
have all nonzero periodic Fourier derivatives separated from integers, including
the last discrete increment, for fixed delta depending on Q,k. Larger active
low rows have at most2/delta terms. Discrete summation by parts and actual
damping pay the entire low source by A min(D,X).

On each high block remove exactly empty m>4N BEFORE Poisson. For the frozen
row interval [M,2M) intersect[1,D] intersect[1,4N], put T=(N/X)^k. The exact
transform is m^(-1)sum_h beta_h I_(h/m), with beta_(Qj)=0 and

    I_r=int w(n/N)e^(-n/x^b)exp(i[2pi r n/Q-(n/x)^k])dn.

Both alias signs and every Fourier residue remain. In a fixed positive ambient
near range r~T/N, chosen before x, the critical point and full leading term are

    n_r=(2pi r/(kQ))^(1/(k-1))x^(k/(k-1)),
    Phi_r=(k-1)(2pi r/(kQ))^(k/(k-1))x^(k/(k-1)),
    Z_r=sqrt(2pi/[k(k-1)])x^(k/2)n_r^(-(k-2)/2)
                                    w(n_r/N)e^(-n_r/x^b),
    I_r=Z_r exp(i Phi_r-i*pi/4)+O((N/T)e^(-cN/X^b)).

After n=Nt, x=Xz, the phases form a fixed compact nondegenerate family.
The review proves this uniform remainder by a Morse coordinate, including
smooth support crossings. Every differentiated damping polynomial is absorbed
by a weaker exponential. Summing every near remainder, negative alias,
small nonstationary alias and large alias tail costs O(e^(-cN/X^b)) per row;
the large tail uses the exact m/N<=4 condition. No remainder derivative is used.

Reduce r=h/m=u/v and group the ENTIRE leading term, not just its phase:

    C_(u/v)=sum_(vj in row) A_(vj)beta_(uj)/(vj), |C_(u/v)|<<A/v.

The mandatory lower denominator v>=N/(CT) gives
sum_r|C_r|^2<<A^2(T/N)log(2M). For the full sharp x shell, both endpoints
and the weight1/z are retained in the Gram kernel

    (N^2/T)e^(-cN/X^b)min(1,1/(N|r-s|)).

Reduced fractions are1/(4M^2)-separated. Their complete positive kernel row
sum is O(1+(M^2/N)log(2N)), since their number is polynomial in N for fixed k.
The entire block, including all alias remainders, therefore has squared norm

    << A^2 e^(-cN/X^b)(N+M^2)log^2(2N).

Summing WHOLE block norms keeps all interactions. For fixed N the M terms
sum to O(min(D,N)); the sqrt(N) terms cost an additional log(2N). The full
infinite damped N sum is bounded by

    A[X^(b/2)log^2(2X)+D log^2(2X)].

Together with the low source and finite-measure Cauchy this proves(191.1).
Arbitrarily large finite D creates no log D. This is a complete extension of
the earlier degree6 proof, with its changed terms reconstructed explicitly.

statement:
## 6. Actual diagonal and absolute price

Let a_n=mu(n)chi(n), with chi of fixed modulus q. From
mu(n)^2=sum_(d^2|n)mu(d), counting q-units in each progression gives

    sum_(n<=Y)|a_n|^2=d_q Y+O_q(sqrt Y),
    d_q=(1/zeta(2)) product_(p|q)(1+1/p)^(-1)>0.        (R12)

The factor is (phi(q)/q)sum_((d,q)=1)mu(d)/d^2, which simplifies to
the displayed expression. The d tail and the O_q(1) counting errors both
cost O_q(sqrt Y). Damping and partial summation then give
sum_n |a_n|^2 exp(-2n/x^b)=d_q x^b/2+O_q(x^(b/2)).

With the author's exact kernel

    K_X(n,m)=integral_1^2 exp(-(n+m)/(X^b u^b))
                         exp(-i(n-m)/(Xu))du/u,

absolute Fubini is valid on each fixed shell. The diagonal of the complete
energy is exactly

    d_q(2^b-1)X^b/(2b)+O_q(X^(b/2)).                    (R13)

This is not a lower bound for the whole signed energy.

For the absolute off-diagonal price put N=X^b and partition [N,2N]
into O(N/H+1) bins of length at most H=floor(X/4). There are
A=d_q N+O_q(sqrt N+1) squarefree units. If A_j counts them in the
bins, sum A_j^2>=A^2/(number of bins)>>_q NH. Removing A diagonal
pairs still leaves >>_q NH distinct ordered pairs. On each such pair
|n-m|<=X/4 and n+m<=4X^b; hence

    Re K_X(n,m)>=exp(-4)cos(1/4)log 2>0.

Their coefficient modulus is one. This proves the author's genuine
actual-coefficient lower price

    sum_(n!=m)|a_n conjugate(a_m)K_X(n,m)|>>_(q,b)X^(b+1). (R14)

No signed Mobius correlation, principal-character restriction or total
energy lower bound was inserted. The same conclusion holds for every
fixed ordinary character because d_q>0.

An independent upper estimate identifies the exponent of that price.
For h=|n-m|>=1, substitute v=1/u and integrate the phase once by parts.
The amplitude v^(-1)exp(-(n+m)v^b/N), its endpoint values and total
variation are bounded by C_b(1+(n+m)/N)exp(-c_b(n+m)/N). Absorb the
polynomial into a slightly weaker exponential to obtain

    |K_X(n,m)|<=C_b exp(-c'_b(n+m)/N)min(1,X/h).         (R15)

Summing first over min(n,m), and then h, costs
O_b(N[X+X log(2N/X)])=O_b(X^(b+1)log(2X)) for fixed b>1.
Together with (R14), the logarithmic power exponent of the actual
