statement:
## Protected independent audit30: which commutator survives evaluation?

The original rare card proposes isolating a noncommutative/free contribution and paying the commutative error. Its first missing contract is the choice of word space. Two natural choices have different answers. Neither is safely replaced by a generic assertion about commutators.

In the full finite free-word space, retain every ordering of distinct unramified primes of product n<=N. Abelianization E maps each word to e_n. Adjacent-transposition differences span exactly the zero-sum hyperplane in each k! fiber: the adjacent-transposition graph on permutations is connected, and differences along a spanning tree have rank k!-1. Hence ker E is precisely the full within-fiber commutator span. The hard product cutoff preserves entire fibers. Integer summation annihilates those commutators identically; reducing their norm cannot change M_chi. This is a scope-specific zero, not a claim that all noncommutative models have zero commutator readout.

For arbitrary positive word weights w_v, let beta_n=sum_(Ev=e_n)1/w_v. The minimum squared norm of a lift of actual a_n is sum_n|a_n|^2/beta_n, and the scalar evaluation's squared norm is sum_n beta_n. Their product is at least (#S)^2 because |a_n|=1 on the squarefree q-unit set S. This is G117's exact orthogonal-fiber price, with the original masks retained.

A different, already available sorted-prime Fock realization retains a nonzero commutator. Fix sigma>1/2 and use the orthonormal basis of increasing unramified prime words, identified with squarefree q-unit n. Define

    A_p e_n = chi(p)p^(-sigma)e_(np) if p>P+(n), else0,
    T=sum_(p∤q) A_p,                  P+(1)=1.

The outputs of T^r for different input words are disjoint. Therefore ||T^r||^2<=S_sigma^r/r!, where S_sigma=sum_(p∤q)p^(-2sigma)<infinity. The Neumann series for (I+T)^(-1) converges in operator norm even if ||T||>=1, and its vacuum vector is exactly

    v_sigma=(I+T)^(-1)e_1,
    (v_sigma)_n=mu(n)chi(n)n^(-sigma).                  (A30.1)

This operator construction and coefficient identity are the retained matched-Max B22, not a new family. For p<r, A_p A_r=0; A_r A_p can be nonzero. With commutator convention [A,B]=AB-BA, the complete ordered commutator is

    C = sum_(p<r)[A_r,A_p] = T^2.                     (A30.2)

This infinite sum is paid: for finite prime cutoffs C_P=T_P^2, while ||T-T_P||^2<=sum_(p>P)p^(-2sigma), so C_P converges in operator norm to T^2. No rearrangement of a merely conditionally convergent series is used. For a hard integer cutoff N, intermediate products never exceed the final product, so the identical two-step formula holds on the compressed finite space too.

Let Lambda_(N,sigma)(u)=sum_(n<=N)n^sigma u_n. From (I+T)v_sigma=e_1 follows T^2v_sigma=v_sigma-e_1+T e_1. Thus the literal source return is

    M_chi(N)=1-sum_(p<=N)chi(p)+Lambda_(N,sigma)(C v_sigma). (A30.3)

The final term is exactly the contribution of integers having at least two distinct prime factors, with every sign and character factor correct. It need not be small; it must cancel the prime term. An all-scale N^(gamma+epsilon) bound for the COMPLETE scalar in (A30.3), for each fixed ordinary chi and every epsilon, returns the M bound and the all-height zero exclusion already proved above. A small norm of C alone supplies no such estimate, because the evaluator's cost and the prime term remain. This preserves the card's potentially useful cross-integer correlation question while rejecting an unpriced transition between full-word and sorted-word commutators.
title: Protected independent audit30: which commutator survives evaluation?

## Density expansion and the full critical-window profile

Write s=x/X in[1,2], p=sqrt(X)v and q=sqrt(X)w. Since kappa>=1,
v,w>=kappa and logv,logw>=0. For a=L/2 and b,c>=0,

    |1/((a+b)(a+c)) - 1/a²| <= (b+c)/a³.

The density is therefore4/L²+O((logv+logw)/L³). Its absolute integrated
error is O(X/L³), because

    sum_r integral_(v,w>=kappa)
       (1+logv+logw)g(log(rvw/s)) dv dw

is bounded uniformly in s in[1,2]. For an explicit convergence argument,
set y=vw; the inner integral becomes
integral_(kappa²)^infinity (1+logy)log(y/kappa²)g(log(ry/s))dy.
Put u=log(ry/s). Its lower limit is log(rkappa²/s); the Gaussian then
bounds this by C_(tau,kappa,B) r^(-B) for every fixed B, uniformly in s.
This prices the complete core and all logarithmic density moments by
absolute convergence, rather than by an invalid unsigned reciprocal
moment completion.

The leading double integral, without the extra logarithmic weight, is

    integral_(v,w>=kappa) g(log(rvw/s))dv dw
      = integral_(kappa²)^infinity log(y/kappa²)g(log(ry/s))dy
      = (s/r) J_tau(log(rkappa²/s)).                            (CT6)

Combining factor1/2, Jacobian X and density4/L² gives exactly CT1.
All constants are uniform for x in[X,2X]. No uniformity in moving kappa
or in tau is asserted.
title: Density expansion and the full critical-window profile

At every conductor prime the forced valuation remains in \(k\), and the residual primitive character retains its zero extension. With \(r=kz\), put \(h=H/q_k\). The profile is still
\[
W_0\!\left(\frac{q_z}{hx_a}\right)

|\operatorname{row}(h)|\ll\min(\sqrt R,h)
\le R^{1/4}h^{1/2}. \tag{FR3}

|\operatorname{row}(h)-\operatorname{zero}(h)|
\ll\min(1,h)\le h^{1/2}. \tag{FR4}

statement:
### D1d. A second root scale is forced by any Mertens power saving

For a fixed principal character, suppose the Mertens bound at exponent 1-c holds for every positive epsilon, with fixed c>0. Then D1.5 forces a different zero of Z_N to approach the parity point -1. More precisely, for every eta>0, all sufficiently large N have a zero zeta_N other than alpha_N satisfying

    |zeta_N+1| <= 2(log N)^(-c+eta).                   (D1.8)

It is enough to consider 0<eta<c. Let d=deg Q_N. A squarefree integer with D distinct primes is at least (D+1)!, because its j-th prime is at least j+1. The elementary integral bound for log((D+1)!) therefore gives

    deg Z_N <= (1+o(1))log N/loglog N.

If Q_N(-1)=0, take zeta_N=-1. Otherwise factor the entire polynomial, including every zero and its multiplicity:

    |Q_N(-1)|=product_(j=1)^d |1+1/zeta_j|.

The case d=0 is excluded at every sufficiently large N by Q_N(-1)=O(N^(-c+epsilon)). At least one factor is no larger than |Q_N(-1)|^(1/d). The every-epsilon bound and the upper bound for d make this factor at most (log N)^(-c+eta) eventually; first choose the internal epsilon sufficiently small. If delta=|1+1/zeta_j|<1/2, then |zeta_j+1|<=delta/(1-delta)<=2delta. This proves D1.8. It is a necessary consequence, not a sufficient criterion for a power saving: the other factors in the product remain unpaid.

Thus a complete principal hard-cutoff polynomial has a root near 0 unconditionally, and under any supplied subunit Mertens calibration it also has a root approaching -1 at a quantified logarithmic rate. The latter is distinct from alpha_N for large N. A proposed new c improves a necessary localization rate, but localization of one zero alone cannot establish that c. The full logarithmic product of all deflated factors is the relevant signed-arithmetic obligation.

**Strongest objection and next action.** The normalized root factor may encode the same hard cancellation less transparently. That objection survives. A useful next calculation would control the full deflated logarithmic product using actual root motion and arithmetic coefficients. Merely avoiding alpha_N along a complex path, bounding Q_N, or locating one zero near -1 does not meet D1.5. The immediate identity Q_(N+1)(-1)=[M_chi(N)+mu(N+1)chi(N+1)]/[1+1/alpha_(N+1)] is circular as an estimate and receives no credit. The non-root branch's full composite sum also needs an independent estimate before the full character statement can improve.
title: D1d. A second root scale is forced by any Mertens power saving

* The published Green--Tao theorem supplies the fixed-degree, coefficient-

* CORE1 is a complete sufficient L1 input and is equivalent to this source's

The substantive gain in the research architecture is a new source whose
**entire long tail and all crosses have a proved summable price**, followed

an unknown full norm in different notation. It still leaves a genuine

Independent additions proved below are: a positive smooth shell majorant

statement:
# Paid linear readout and complete absolute Gram: independent review

Verdict: draft R1-R3 are valid. R1 has the SHARP stronger constant1/2
in place of4/pi^2, independently of the lift dimension or vector sizes.
The direct-integral consequence holds for the exact full Gaussian and
full/retained-middle Jordan sources under a common measurable bounded
linear readout. One interpretation needs correction: integral L_x^2
pays the averaged functional, not automatically the full shell L2 return.
For that return a uniform essential-supremum bound suffices. Without a
separate diagonal bound the conclusion concerns only the TOTAL price.

This is a bounded strengthening and scope correction of G221, not an
arithmetic estimate. The draft's six discovery alternatives remain in
its original file. No signed-energy lower bound, endpoint improvement,
PR15 repair, PR26 admission or new all-family estimate follows.

## 1. Sharp dimension-free lemma

Let H be any real Hilbert space, T:H->R^2 bounded real-linear, ||T||=L,
and v_a a finite family. Put y_a=T v_a, M=sum_a|y_a| and
B=sum_(a,b)|<v_a,v_b>|, retaining every ordered pair. Then

    L^2 B >= M^2/2.                                      (1)

If all y_a lie on one real line, the constant improves to1. Cases L=0
or M=0 are immediate. The constant1/2 is optimal for the general lemma:
take H=R^2,T=Id,v_1=(1,0),v_2=(0,1). Then L=1,B=2,M=2.

Proof. Set u_a=y_a/|y_a| when y_a!=0 and u_a=0 otherwise. Define the
finite-rank operator A:R^2->H by A z=sum_a <u_a,z>v_a. Exactly,

    ||A||_HS^2=sum_(a,b)<v_a,v_b><u_a,u_b> <= B,
    T A=sum_a |y_a|u_a u_a^T.

The last matrix is positive2x2 with trace M. Thus

    M^2/2 <= ||TA||_HS^2 <= L^2||A||_HS^2 <= L^2 B.

This uses a common readout on the WHOLE family. It does not use the
false termwise inequality |<Tv_a,Tv_b>|<=L^2|<v_a,v_b>|. For collinear
images the same proof in a one-dimensional target gives M^2. Equivalently
choose the common real direction and sum its recovery-aligned real signs.
For a target R^r the same argument gives M^2/r; it depends on output
dimension, not the dimension of H. The r orthonormal output example
shows that constant is sharp. Only r=2 (or1) is needed here.

The draft's circle-average proof also works exactly as written and
proves its weaker4/pi^2. Preserve it as the historical derivation;
the Hilbert-Schmidt argument above supplies the sharper replacement.

For a countable family, apply(1) to every finite subset. Its nonnegative
absolute Gram sums and sum|y_a| then give the extended inequality. No
assertion about the infinite vector sum is required for this lower bound.
If B is infinite, that particular positive certificate is already infinite.
If a proof uses finite B to reconstruct a full vector sum, the tail bound
||sum_(a in F)v_a||^2<=sum_(a,b in F)|<v_a,v_b>| makes the net of finite
partial sums unconditionally Cauchy. This is a separate consequence, not
an assumption hidden in the lower-bound argument.

The common-readout condition is essential. In H=R^n take v_i=e_i and
let T_i(h)=h_i in a real output line. Each separate map has norm1 and
y_i=1, while B=n and M=n. There is no dimension-free conclusion using
those separate unit costs. The common map h->sum_i h_i has norm sqrt(n)
and pays exactly the missing factor. A changing lift/readout rescaling
likewise cannot remove its actual operator norm.

## 2. Pointwise source and its paid cost

For each real x suppose ONE T_x, common across all indices, recovers

    T_x v_a(x)=c_a K(q_a/x), ||T_x||=L_x.

Here complex values are R^2 and all coefficients, phases, holes and
positive weights can be included in v_a. Formula(1) gives

    L_x^2 sum_(a,b)|<v_a(x),v_b(x)>|
       >=(1/2)(sum_a|c_a K(q_a/x)|)^2.                    (2)

For G221's quaternion lift w_a(x)(xi_a(x)+t_a(x)j), first-coordinate
projection has norm1. No bound on t_a is needed for(2). Arbitrary extra
Hilbert coordinates cannot improve the paid COMPLETE absolute price.
G216's actual full and retained-middle Jordan absolute mass is of order x;
therefore(2) has quadratic scale. This improves G221's dimension/C-bound
price, while preserving its warning that the actual signed energy may
be much smaller. A nonlinear or collective readout without coefficientwise
common linear recovery is not covered.

## 3. Direct integral, absolute order and the variable-cost correction

Let I=[X,2X] with measure dx/x. Use a measurable real Hilbert field H_x
and its direct-integral space Hcal=L2(I;H_x). Each v_a must be an admitted
measurable square-integrable section. The field T_x:H_x->R^2 must be
measurable on sections, common across all indices, with norm bounded
by a measurable L_x and C_I=int_I L_x^2 dx/x<infinity. Then

    Tcal(v)=int_I T_x v(x)dx/x, ||Tcal||<=sqrt(C_I).       (3)

Bochner integrability in the finite-dimensional target follows from
Cauchy-Schwarz. Recovery may hold almost everywhere; the countable
index set permits a common full-measure set. Apply(1) to these sections:

    C_I sum_(a,b)|int_I <v_a(x),v_b(x)>dx/x|
       >=(1/2)(sum_a|int_I c_a K(q_a/x)dx/x|)^2.          (4)

If L_x<=L essentially, C_I<=L^2 log2, proving draft R3 with constant1/2.
The inner product is the REAL Hilbert inner product. For complex or
quaternion lifts it is the real part of the conventional Hermitian
product; a complex-modulus absolute price is larger and also obeys the
floor. Absolute values in(4) are AFTER each complete shell integration.
No exchange with pointwise absolute values was used.

For countably many labels the same finite-subset limit proves(4), even
when its left side is infinite. For the concrete lower bounds below it
is enough to retain finitely many central labels. No convergence of an
unbounded-lift global sum is required. Failure of square integrability
is a failure to define this certificate, not permission to apply(4).

Important correction: C_I is the cost of Tcal, the AVERAGED functional.
It is not in general the norm squared of v(x)->T_x v(x) from shell L2
to shell L2. On a measurable E of shell measure epsilon, take H_x=R,
T_x=epsilon^-1/2 1_E and v=epsilon^-1/2 1_E. Then C_I=1 and ||v||_2=1,
but ||T_x v||_2^2=epsilon^-1. The averaged functional remains bounded
as(3) says. Thus an energy-return argument may use a uniform ess-sup L,
giving ||sum_a T_x v_a||_2^2<=L^2||sum_a v_a||_2^2, but must not replace
L^2 by C_I without another source-specific estimate.

A lawful variable-cost alternative is to use w_a(x)=L_x v_a(x) in Hcal
and T'_x=T_x/L_x (set0 where L_x=0), provided each w_a is square
integrable. It changes the after-integration Gram to
sum_(a,b)|int_I L_x^2<v_a,v_b>dx/x|. Its common readout has norm at most1
pointwise. This is a different PAID Gram, not C_I times the old Gram.

## 4. Exact Gaussian and positive-hole application

For G218, K(t)=g_tau(log t)>0. With no moving holes, the squarefree count
on q_a in[X,2X] coprime to S+ is a positive constant times X plus a
square-root/logarithmic error. On this interval and the entire shell,
K(q_a/x) is bounded below by a fixed positive constant. Thus

    sum_a |c_a J_X(q_a)| >> X,
    J_X(t)=int_X^(2X)K(t/x)dx/x.                          (5)

All presented natural-zero primes are in S+. This holds over integers
or Eisenstein ideals, with the original one-ideal/unit convention.
For polynomial holes q_Q<=X^A, the preceding positive-hole review proves
the uniform strengthened count >>X/log(2X), by D(Q*)^-1<=sum_(q_d<=q_Q*)
q_d^-1<<log(2q_Q*) and G218's uniform squarefree error. Therefore the
right side of(5) is >>X/log(2X), uniformly in Q. For a normalized positive
mixture, use its ACTUAL coefficient c_a p(a), with p(a)>=0. Its mass is
the positive average of the individual masses, so the same bound holds.

Apply(4). The PAID after-integration price L^2 log2 times its absolute
Gram is >>X^2 for the fixed field, and >>X^2/log(2X)^2 for these moving
holes/mixtures. For an average of individual hole-bank prices apply the
inequality separately with each actual readout cost, then average the
nonnegative inequalities. Do not equate the joint kernel p(rad(ab)) with
the product p(a)p(b). An arbitrary positive mixture still has no automatic
Euler multiplier or zero-exclusion return.

Unlike the preceding corollary, this conclusion does not require lifted
pair phases to be fixed in x. The common integral readout controls them.
It closes the after-integration escape for this precise class of lifts;
it does not rule out every oscillatory joint-label observation. If such
an observation also has this coefficientwise common bounded recovery,
it IS covered. Otherwise its different readout and full return need
their own proof.

## 5. Exact Jordan kernel and moving middle

G215 fixes the presented ordinary character chi modulo q, parity-matched
r>=2, fixed m>=0, and

    Phi(x)=sum_n mu(n)chi(n)K(n/x),
    K(t)=P_m(T)(I-2^(r+1)T)f(t), T f(t)=f(2t).

Its proved kernel is smooth, K(t)=O(t^(2m+1)) at zero and
K(t)=e^-t+O(e^-2t) at infinity. Thus K is not zero and tends to0 at
infinity. For a NONREAL chi, K can be complex; the draft's real-kernel
qualification should be removed. The following proof works over C.

Set J(t)=int_1^2 K(t/u)du/u=int_(t/2)^t K(v)dv/v. It is continuous
and t J'(t)=K(t)-K(t/2). If J were identically zero, K(t)=K(t/2), hence
K(2^j t)=K(t) for every j, contradicting its decay and nonzero value.
Therefore some fixed0<a<b and j0>0 satisfy |J(t)|>=j0 on[a,b].
The fixed squarefree q-unit count gives

    sum_n |mu(n)chi(n)J(n/X)|
       >=j0 #{aX<n<=bX:n squarefree,(n,q)=1} >>_chi,K X. (6)

No cancellation of different labels is invoked. The nonzero slowest
exponential coefficient1 in G215 independently verifies the necessary
nonzero hypothesis for every fixed character and filter.

The ACTUAL retained middle is pointwise moving:

    Cmid(x)=sum_(x^alpha<n<=2x log x)mu(n)chi(n)K(n/x),
    alpha=1-(1-gamma)/(2m+2)<1, gamma in(0,1).

For every sufficiently large X, every n in(aX,bX] satisfies
(2X)^alpha<n and n<=2X log X. It is therefore retained for EVERY
x in[X,2X]. For these finitely many central labels the integrated
middle contribution is exactly mu(n)chi(n)J(n/X). Formula(6) and the
finite-family version of(4) prove the SAME quadratic paid floor for
the complete middle after-integration Gram. Other labels only add to
its nonnegative absolute sum. No false fixed-mask formula is assigned
to labels that enter or leave the middle during the shell.

This directly verifies the proposed Jordan extension for all fixed
ordinary characters in G215. It uses its complex kernel, natural zeros,
actual moving endpoints and fixed m,r. It does not assert a Hecke or
growing-character/filter version. The same nonzero/decay reasoning can
also be applied to G216's complete E_m kernel H, whose principal
algebraic tail tends to0; no retained-middle assertion for a different
mask is inferred from that observation.

## 6. Diagonal, return, ancestry and exact limits

Without an additional estimate on sum_a||v_a||_Hcal^2, no off-diagonal
floor follows. Orthogonal vectors may put the entire price on the
diagonal. For the bounded lifts of G221, ||v_a(x)||<=C|c_a K(q_a/x)|,
the full diagonal is O(C^2 X) by G216/Gaussian square counting. If C and
the recovery cost are fixed, subtracting it preserves the quadratic
after-integration off-diagonal floor. With growing costs one must debit
the actual PAID diagonal before making that claim. No such bound is
assumed for arbitrary unbounded auxiliary coordinates.

When a complete energy estimate is pursued by an absolute Gram and a
common uniform-L readout, its paid sufficient price has exponent at least2
(up to logarithms for moving holes), whereas target gamma=1-c requires
2-2c. The unpaid exponent is2c: .24 at c=.12, .2502919272 at conditional
c11, .25030 at c=.12515,1/3 at c=1/6 and1/2 at c=1/4. These statements
do not lower-bound the actual source norm. G215's weakest L1 return and
its paid outside-middle terms remain available; no arithmetic hypothesis
for that return has been proved here.

Historical audit: G221 already contains the general real-dimension trace
obstruction with a bounded lift/readout. The new argument removes its
lift-dimension/size dependence by using the COMMON output map, and then
applies it in a shell direct integral. G80's native trace/exterior estimate
controls a different operator and still needs its actual fourth
contractions; G82 already obstructs unrestricted Gaussian operator
majorants at squared price X^2. Neither supplies this common-readout
lemma as stated. The positive-hole corollary supplies the current uniform
count, not a new phase argument here. W66's principal weighted
Holder/Cauchy deletion-channel floor remains distinct and is owned by
root's separate integration. The complete maintained index was read in
the immediately preceding same-history review and its relevant entries
were checked again narrowly. No new broad archive or literature claim
was made after the interruption.

This closes the previously apparent growing-dimension and delayed-pair-
absolute escape only when the stated coefficientwise common recovery
exists and its true norm is paid. It leaves full signed companion
comparisons, cancellations before the complete absolute pair sum,
nonlinear/collective readouts and genuinely different source-dependent
relations open. A quaternion identity or determinant name alone does
not supply those arithmetic estimates.

Operational scope: same owner/history after the recorded terminal502;
no completed prefix was overwritten, no replacement or provider-route
change, and the original10:50UTC13October2026 deadline remains. Only the assigned new ignored tree
was written; no diagnostics, children, providers, canonical/tracker/Git,
kernel/formalization or public work occurred. Root owns integration.

### 3.4 Coincident frequencies must be grouped before taking energy

For a reduced positive rational r=u/v write h=uj,m=vj. The WHOLE amplitude Z_r, including its support and damping, depends only on r,N,x. The exact coefficient is

    C_(u/v)=sum_(j: vj in I_M) A_(vj)beta_(uj)/(vj).          (R9)

Every natural zero and every nonconstant phase beta_(uj) remains. No averaging along j is assumed. The dyadic interval gives |C_(u/v)|<=C A||b||inf/v. Since u>=1 and r<=C_Q T/N, every active denominator obeys

    v>=N/(C_Q T).                                           (R10)

Counting numerators only in an upper bound yields

    sum_r |C_r|^2
      <<A^2||b||inf^2 sum_(max(1,N/(C_QT))<=v<=2M)
                                          [(T/N)v+1]/v^2
      <<A^2||b||inf^2 (T/N)log(2M).                         (R11)

Indeed sum v^-2 from the lower limit is O(min(1,T/N)), hence O(T/N). The empty range gives zero. This is the decisive calculation: deleting (R10) would leave a false N^2/T term after energy formation. Shared rational frequencies cannot be treated as orthogonal original aliases; (R9) pays their exact coherent sum first.

## 3. D2 and selected duplicates

For C(m,n)=chi(n/m)1_(m|n) and A(m,n)=mu(n/m)chi(n/m)1_(m|n), every intermediate divisor lies inside1..N, so CA=AC=I with natural zeros. For ANY retained R containing1, E its complement,

    S=C_RR-C_RE C_EE^-1 C_ER,
    v=1_R-C_RE C_EE^-1 1_E,
    S^-1=A_RR,    M_chi(N)=e_1^T S^-1 v.             (R8)

C_EE is unit upper triangular even for an interleaved set. Reordering into blocks does not remove the true injection. For a prefix, C_ER=0 but v still contains the deleted source. For N=6,chi=1,R={1,6}, S=[[1,-1],[0,1]], v=(-2,1), and the readout is-1. The two deleted paths1->2->6 and1->3->6 give return2. An acyclic graph can connect different retained vertices through deleted vertices; only a return to the SAME vertex is prohibited. This correctly limits G69's zero-feedback assertion to its chronologically separated causal split.

If an unramified prime p is retained, no strict intermediate divisor exists between1 and p. Thus S(1,p)=chi(p) and S^-1(1,p)=-chi(p). If p is deleted, the coefficient of its arbitrary endpoint input w_p still equals A(1,p)=-chi(p). Exact elimination cannot remove that source coefficient; it can still merge it with OTHER signed endpoint contributions. No lower bound on the whole signed functional follows.

Writing T=C-I gives C^-1=sum_k(-T)^k with T^k=0 for2^k>N. Its coefficients are chi(n/m) times ordered factorizations of n/m into k factors>=2. Counts at6,12,30 are(1,2),(1,4,3),(1,6,6), with signed totals1,0,-1. At a prime only the first layer survives. This is classical incidence inversion and restores individual mu coefficients, not cross-integer cancellation.

For b_U=a1_(n<=U), r_U=delta-b_U*chi, the exact convolution identities are

    a=b_U+a*r_U,
    a=sum_(j=0)^(k-1)b_U*r_U^(*j)+a*r_U^(*k).         (R9)

They include squareful intermediate terms and repeated factors. At principal U=5, r_U(12)=1 and (b_U*r_U)(12)=0; deleting the former because mu(12)=0 breaks the expansion. At prime p>U, r_U(p)=(b_U*r_U)(p)=-chi(p), while r_U^(*j)(p)=0 for j>=2. For k>=2 the first residual layer retains that endpoint.

**Required support correction:** r_U^(*k) vanishes below (floor(U)+1)^k for real U>=1. With U<=N^u, fixed u<1, the binomial lower bound and pi(U)<=U give a price>>N/log N. This obstructs that absolute certificate only. It is not a lower bound for M, for an arbitrarily merged Schur residual, or for weighted Gaussian/native-H observations.

S16's finite future telescope is exact:

    M(x)=b^-J M(b^J x)-sum_(j=1)^J b^-j F_b(b^j x),
    F_b(x)=M(x)-bM(x/b).

The boundary vanishes under its STATED subunit-growth anchor (or M=o(x)); a forcing bound x^gamma, gamma<1, costs1/(b^(1-gamma)-1). For every-epsilon inputs the denominator uses gamma+epsilon after choosing that exponent<1. The source anchor must actually be available; it is not deduced from a strip slogan.

For the principal character modulo1, S18's ordinary jump coefficients at n=1,2,3,6 are1,-3,-4,12; these differ from the dilation weights and from mu. The complete mixed field is M(x)-2M(x/2)-3M(x/3)+6M(x/6). Commutation holds for every function; two anchored future inversions give the product of their fixed costs and no arithmetic estimate. ## 7. A changed source with a weaker observation geometry

**Theorem C (quartic replacement).** Define the fixed real, even, SIGNED kernel

    K(x)=(2pi)^(-1) integral_R exp(-t^4+itx)dt,
    F4(u)=sum_n a_n K(log n-u).

Under A1 with b>gamma, Theorem A remains true for F4 with the weaker geometric requirement log(1/delta_k)=o(k^(3/4)). The arithmetic values in the hypothesis are those of F4, not F. For the three literal coefficient fields in Section4 its Mellin multiplier is exp(-s^4), so the same zero-exclusion return holds in their respective domains.

Here is a complete proof of the new costs. Contour translation t->t+iy, y having the sign of real x, gives

    -Re(t+iy)^4-y*x <= -t^4/2+17*y^4-y*x.

The vertical closing sides vanish as their real part tends to infinity. Choose |y|=(|x|/68)^(1/3). Thus

    |K(x)|<=C exp(-c*|x|^(4/3)), c=51/68^(4/3)>0.      (C1)

Fixed derivatives have the same contour bound with an additional polynomial factor. This justifies every exponentially weighted real integral. The bilateral Laplace transform of K is exp(-s^4): both sides are entire in s by C1 and agree on the imaginary axis by Fourier inversion. In particular K(0)>0. It cannot be nonnegative: its second moment is0, whereas K is continuous and positive near0. Weighted absolute Fubini gives h4(u)=e^(-bu)F4(u) in L1 intersect L-infinity and

    hat h4(t)=exp(-(b+it)^4) sum_n a_n n^(-b-it),
    |hat h4(t)|<=A_b*exp(17*b^4)*exp(-t^4/2).           (C2)

For localization take r=j^(1/8), W_j(u)=K((u-j)/r)/K(0) and the pointwise product H_j(u)=h4(u)W_j(u). Its Fourier convolution has a uniform quartic envelope: for r>=1,

    x^4/2+r^4*(t-x)^4 >= t^4/32+(r^4/2)*(t-x)^4.

The integral of the last exponential is O(1/r), canceling the window transform's factor r. Hence |hat H_j(t)|<=C_b A_b exp(-t^4/32). Cut at T_j=[32*(b-gamma+2)*j]^(1/4); the full omitted frequency tail is O(T_j^(-3)exp(-(b-gamma+2)j)).

Use exactly the augmented thick set I_j,S_j from Section2. Its LS cost is still (200/delta_j^*)^(132*T_j+1)=exp(o(j)), now under log(1/delta_k)=o(k^(3/4)). On the observed set, with d=b-gamma-eta>0, C1 bounds H_j by

    C exp(-d*u-c*|u-j|^(4/3)/r^(4/3))
      <= C exp(-d*j+[27*d^4/(256*c^3)]r^4)
       =exp(-d*j+O(sqrt(j))).                          (C3)

On the unobserved exterior its bound is O(exp(-c'*j^(7/6))); both it and the multiplied frequency tail are therefore paid. For u in[j,j+1], W_j(u)->1 uniformly, hence |W_j(u)|>=1/2 eventually. The norm triangle inequality used in A11 now proves the full exponent gamma for F4. This establishes the asserted transfer without positivity of K.

For u sufficiently negative, A1 and C1 give |F4(u)|<=C A_b exp(-c*|u|^(4/3)) by maximizing exp(bv-c(v+|u|)^(4/3)) over v>=0. Thus its entire left Mellin tail is paid, and absolute convergence on Re s>1 gives exp(-s^4) times the SAME Dirichlet series in A13/A14. The multiplier never vanishes. This proves the arithmetic return, including the original modulus zeros and f3 p2/p3 factors.

A concrete OPEN-C(gamma) input is |E_k|>=exp(-k^(3/4)/log(k+2)) and ess sup_Ek|F4|<<_epsilon exp((gamma+epsilon)k), in every large unit interval. Any gamma<.874865 improves the current c under this input; 5/6 and3/4 retain their conditional returns. Abel summation of the accepted buffered Mertens bound still only gives F4,F4'=O(exp(beta*u)), beta>gamma4: its guaranteed valley width exp(-(beta-gamma)j) fails even this weaker contract. The Gaussian small-value hypothesis, positive RR law and Theorem B are not automatically inherited by this changed kernel. OPEN-C requires a new actual-source arithmetic estimate.

# Independent [private research revision] review: larger Gao amplifier and endpoint return



## Disposition

**The proposed amplifier change is supported by the exact pinned source, provided the explicit repricing below replaces the numerical passages of Gao's proof.** The old amplifier size `M/2000` is a proof choice, not an upper bound imposed by the amplification or second-transform theorem. The candidate `a=M/160`, `sigma=3a`, `k0=7/10`, and local capacity `C=111/25` closes every branch of the same finite local proof. It uses only the old `9/2` and unrestricted zero-slot descendant moments. This conclusion is based on the actual PR9 amplifier, radius, Poisson, capacity, exceptional source interfaces and the accepted PR15 analytic assembly; it is not inferred merely from a positive numerical certificate.

The complete endpoint return also closes, relative to those same accepted analytic inputs, at

```
theta = 2734/3125 = .87488
c = 391/3125 = .12512
ell = 1567/9375
h = 3969737987/5000000000
x = 5597986039/15000000000
y = 6894813961/15000000000
kappa_* = 2343/3125.
```

This gives an open zero-free half-plane `Re(s)>.87488` for the same finite-order, trivial-infinite-type Eisenstein Hecke family and ordinary Dirichlet L-functions, with the principal pole excluded, **if the controller accepts the written extension and complete composition**. It is a further `0.0000066` increase in `c` over the current accepted written result `c_G=.1251134`. It is not a global arbitrary-coefficient `4.44` moment. No new Lean endpoint, clean dependency build, Comparator, or independent-kernel verification is established by this review.

The frozen author manuscript comparison is complete and favorable; Section 6 records the exact artifact. All independent derivations and exact checks below were completed before receiving that frozen artifact, without reading the author's evolving manuscript, private reasoning, or candidate arithmetic implementation. The controller supplied only the candidate parameters and claims. The original Gao proof and the pinned arithmetic source were inspected as source evidence.

## 1. Source scope and independent evidence

The accepted PR15 pin is `ca182b70ac2aee2d053d679b4ddf1233883f9eef`, original contribution by **Zhongpai Gao, with AI assistance**. The upstream PR9 pin is `58344dfdbe756cf2f743da1908ffe0582418cf5b`. The existing source architecture and prior contributions retain their existing attribution. This review does not claim independent discovery or literature priority.

I read the complete [private research revision] integration record and the relevant local/endpoint review sections, then checked the original PR15 `PhysicalLocalAssembly.tex` (PLA), `RestrictedCanonicalSource.tex` (RC), `PhysicalScaleShortening.tex` (SS), `EndpointAssembly.tex` (EA), `PlainUnmarkedDensity.tex`, `SignedReconstruction.tex`, `FixedDictionaryBridge.tex`, and `FourierMaskTransport.tex`. Those preserved originals are under `[restricted mathematical source]`. I used the retained PR9 manuscript `[restricted provenance path] mathematical source]`, especially B3.57--B3.81 and B0.27--B0.62.

Missing decisive PR9 Lean sources were fetched read-only from the exact pin, in `proofs/[private research revision]-quartic-20261010/formalization/OAI/NumberTheory/DirichletL/`. Exact returned Git blob identities:

| Source | Blob | Consequential interface |

| `Moments/AmplifiedRetainedRadius.lean` | `f6d0c98a4212c85ac9de0c0ce7de35f519383d89` | `main_energy_common`; `eventually_original_amplification_common`, lines 220--255 |
| `Moments/AmplificationOriginalErrors.lean` | `dd04b07d66310413b7351dc60098006eed3c0e96` | exact original error conversion |
| `Moments/SmoothedWindowEnergy.lean` | `30e83531f16da45fb13e886d1458bf97ccec855b` | smooth-ball positive energy |
| `Moments/GaussEnergy.lean` | `200d3d5c9fb828b7bd1eb4e5a7160b10c5fd65bd` | `gaussEnergy_poisson`, lines 105--122, every positive radial scale |
| `Moments/SecondActualWidth.lean` | `9920da7d0518d8d159114642bb38432be3101dc4` | `actual_width_bound`; nonempty support before clipping |
| `Moments/SecondExceptionalFixedQSource.lean` | `286754d49563f233397d28b24f5e5138ef1027f2` | `original_exceptional_energy`, lines 61--80, actual positive `Kphys` and polynomial caps |
| `Moments/FirstSecondCapacityShift.lean` | `bf734e1c27bfd7e0e318379fbe964571a2955732` | generic nominal capacity identities and sigma dependence |

The final endpoint interfaces were also read directly at the same pin, beneath `proofs/[private research revision]-quartic-20261010/formalization/`: `[private research revision]/Energy/Physical/OriginalFourth.lean`, blob `353d935b029b6e1cf9a973f10b62151dca21653a`; `[private research revision]/Energy/Physical/CertifiedZero.lean`, blob `119ff247e5698a5d80dbf203c2e7b9a38477372f`; and `[private research revision]/Assembly/Continuation.lean`, blob `134c145c067b22469025d1cfd284ee9069997666`. These are source inspections, not executed Lean builds.

For example, the amplifier source is [the exact pinned file](https://github.com/HaileyStorm/QuasiRiemannTracker/blob/58344dfdbe756cf2f743da1908ffe0582418cf5b/proofs/[private research revision]-quartic-20261010/formalization/OAI/NumberTheory/DirichletL/Moments/FirstAmplificationChoice.lean). The older local 4/33 tree was used only to discover source filenames, never as the evidence pin.

`independent_check.py` was written from the displayed source formulas, using only Python `Fraction`, a new bivariate polynomial representation, and the binomial power-to-Bernstein identity. It imports no upstream or author polynomial code. It produced `independent-check.json` with exact positive Bernstein coefficients on a disjoint covering of `[0,3/4] x [0,1/2]`; separate exact pairwise interior-disjointness and total-area checks passed. The leaf counts are independently `6,6,1`. Execution exited zero, with a retained harmless Python executable-location warning before the JSON result. The receipt is arithmetic evidence only.

## 2. Why the larger amplifier is actually admissible

### The actual prime pool and slot gap

PR9 B3.7, manuscript lines 2356--2393, puts `ell_*=sigma/3`, requires mesh below `sigma/6`, and uses good primes in `(Z^(ell_*)/2,Z^(ell_*)]`. The exact source does not assume `sigma` tends to zero with the requested local epsilon:

```
eventually_original_amplification:
  sigma > 0, loss > 0, Mmax >= 0, profile upper endpoint b >= 0,
  eta_mesh < sigma/6;
  bounded masks R,s; retained dyadic row logarithm <= Mmax.
```

It then supplies the actual nonempty prime pool, its cardinality saving, source character families with conductor bounds, and the main/error energy inequality. The constant `(Mmax+2 sigma)/(sigma/6)` is a fixed multiplicity constant, not a new exponent. Any fixed positive sigma works. Polynomial mask sizes and row bounds can be enclosed uniformly on the compact local geometry. For `a=M/160`, choosing mesh below `a/10` is stronger than the required mesh below `a/2=sigma/6`. The finitely many original slots are smaller than every amplifier prime eventually. Removing support, row, mask, and first-projector primes omits only `O(log Z)` choices. There is no prime-supply or fixed-small-prime-cutoff obstruction.

This does **not** substitute `sigma=3M/160` into the old proof of the global `9/2` moment. In that proof, B3.10 (lines 2631--2656) chooses a small internal sigma so terminal costs `3 sigma + 5 sigma/3` fit an arbitrary epsilon. The new local proof calls the completed old theorem with its own chosen small loss, and therefore its own internal induction parameters. Its separate, fixed outer amplifier cost is paid by the local strict reserves. Conflating these two sigma choices would invalidate the extension; keeping them separate is legitimate and is what PLA already does for `M/2000`.

The main amplified term retains the original columns and coefficients. The amplifier prime does not become a new varying parent in its density dictionary. The three extracted errors do retain the appropriate moving-prime characters and conductor contribution; they are bounded by the old moment and the original extraction ledger, never by the fixed-parent density theorem.

### Genuine radius, transform, and widths

Use the actual ball

```
K_main = K0 + (d-c)_+ + 6a + omega,
K0 = 2A-c-d+R+E-M,
omega = retained-frequency padding + positive support-doubling reserve.
```

`AmplifiedRetainedRadius.main_energy_common` constructs the domination, including eventual `2 <= Z^reserve`; its hypotheses do not constrain sigma above. Thus this is not an unproved relabeling of the old radius. `GaussEnergy.gaussEnergy_poisson` requires `Kphys>0`, with no fixed exponent ceiling. A power of positive Z meets that condition even when its logarithm is negative. Raw frequency tails still have fixed polynomial envelopes because every exponent in this local proof remains in a bounded range.

PLA LA.6--LA.8 / RC give exactly

```
M' = M-(c-d)_+-6a-omega-g2+t2,
(A'-M')-(A-M) <= 6a+omega,
Delta = b2-p2+B_c+a >= a.
```

These formulas are affine identities for the real parameter a. The additional support, frequency, and fixed-conductor paddings are chosen afterward, smaller than the strict reserve. Actual moving-support cancellation can make `d_*=M_actual-M'` negative; this is not repaired by replacing it with zero. Use the exact inequality

`d_* + r(F-d_*)_+ <= delta2 + r F_+`, for `d_*<=delta2` and `0<=r<=1`.

The actual source `SecondActualWidth.actual_width_bound` checks a nonempty retained row before removing the max; a nominally negative unsupported window is empty. Bounded nonempty end windows cost the declared support padding. No positivity premise for a nominal width has been silently dropped.

The low-bin restriction is imposed only after both transforms on a positive allocated child energy. The literal coefficient/mask/relative-character identities in RC are unchanged. Slot deletion retains original canonical slots; it does not create arbitrary coefficients. The low indicator is removed only after paying each removed slot's pointwise cost. Empty selected slots use the unrestricted old zero-slot theorem, with no invented residual affine plain-capacity condition.

### Character, density, and profile restrictions remain the same

The signed row remains `w=u0 e F G V h'`, with residues `1+t` and `1-t` modulo six. A zero residue is an Euler hole. The fixed ideal is the original `Q_*`; the moving child does not replace the anchor. Parent translates remain separate for eligibility and zero maxima. The natural source constructor gives `conductor <= K Nw` with fixed K. Extra polynomial Euler holes are paid separately and do not enter a supposedly fixed modulus or finite dictionary.

The first projector and genuine second common primes divide w. The second projector need not divide w and is still paid by its dyadic count and two extraction scalars. The joint density/reconstruction remains

```
rho(delta)=1-10delta/[3(5-2delta)],  .7<=delta<=.75,
W=M-R-(c-d)_++L_c-6a,
joint count <= Z^(rho W+p-R-E+R0+eta)*(1+T)^J.
```

Increasing a only reduces the supported row bound W. If W is near or below zero, use the already stated bounded-window/empty-window rule. `rho>=2/7>1/6` is unchanged, so the sixth-power lift remains summable. The actual density statement handles all heights with one threshold; its internal height exponent is chosen before the separate external truncation exponent. There is no new detector cutoff or conductor condition depending on a.

The same common Fourier majorant and diagonal contraction apply. Smooth cutoffs are placed on fixed normalized boxes; Euler derivatives of `K(A product y_i^e_i)` remain uniform for all positive A. Changing a changes the bounded power envelope but not the finite profile mechanism. The four derivative-profile pairs required for scale supremum are retained. Small losses can be chosen from a numerical reserve before target/dictionary/finite-slot count; finite orders, constants, and the eventual threshold may depend on the fixed family, but must precede all live scales, subsets, masks, heights, and normalized slot widths. None of this is weakened by the larger amplifier.

## 3. Complete local repricing

Normalize `M=1`. In the same `.41<=n_i<=.44`, `.03<=z<=.04` window with `n1+n2+(111/25)z<=1`,

```
.85 <= A=n1+n2+z <= 1-(111/25-1)*.03 =1121/1250=.8968,
g=(n1+n2+(9/2)z-1)_+ <= (9/2-111/25)*.04=3/1250=.0024.
```

All displayed reserves below are multiples of M, before the aggregate arbitrarily small losses:

| Branch | Exact reserve |
|---|---:|
| Comparison, `.25+.5+4.5*.04` | `7/100` |
| Main low bins, `a-(7/45)(g+6a)` | `13/300000` |
| Main high bins | `3149/1350000` |
| Error valuation one | `93/80000` |

| Main fixed-inducing part, `1-A-4a` | `391/5000` |
| Error fixed-inducing part, `1-A-3sigma` | `939/20000` |

The main high bound deserves more than endpoint substitution. PLA LA.13 reduces its first-line excess to

`rho-1 + delta*A + a*(5-6rho)`.

The other two lines remain nonpositive by the same joint-label argument: `4rho-1-delta<=-79/270`, `L_c<=5(R-R0)`, `min(c,d)>=p>=R`, `rho+delta>1`, `5rho>1`, and `g2-t2<=b2`. Define

`H(delta)=1-rho(delta)-(.8968)delta-a(5-6rho(delta))`.

Its derivative is `50(1-6a)/(3(5-2delta)^2)-.8968`, bounded below by `1657177/4860000>0` on `[.7,.75]`. Its minimum is therefore exactly `H(.7)=3149/1350000>.00233`. This replaces Gao's coarser `A<=113/125` and claimed `>.01` reserve, which must not be reused. Choose all high losses from the new budget; assigning a high loss `.001` remains harmless, though a single smaller budget tied to the low reserve is simpler.

For the three errors, retain lambda=`log_Z Np` and eventually `lambda>=sigma/4`, justified by `Np>Z^(sigma/3)/2`. Their defects are at most `g+sigma+w-w_o`; their allowances are at least w. With global removal rate `1/6`, the reserves at the worst lambda are

```

5sigma/4-(g+sigma)/6,
6sigma/4-(g+sigma)/6.
```

Those are the exact fractions in the table. The normalized prime average is still normalized. No additional prime count occurs.

The original zero Gauss row remains unamplified. For fixed-inducing second rows, use the actual radius in B3.75 (manuscript lines 2565--2570): the exact main `F1` contains `-4a`, not `-5a`, and the support padding contributes `-5omega/6`. Together with `F2>=2b2/3`, the equal-product rectangle cancellation is governed by

`max_{v>=0}[A-5M/6-2v/3-(M/4-v)_+]=A-M`.

It is attained at `v=M/4`. This gives the main `A-M+4a` and error `A-M+3sigma` excesses. The exact `original_exceptional_energy` theorem requires only positive physical radius, fixed profile supports, proper fixed Q, and polynomial source/frequency/conductor caps. Its `Kphys^(5/6)` dependence is explicitly charged here. Increasing a leaves those caps polynomial, so it does not hide a growing constant as a small loss.

The smallest fixed reserve is the low one, `13M/300000`. Choose the aggregate eta budget as a sufficiently small fraction of this and the requested epsilon, then the bin/slot meshes, support and radius paddings. Every numerical margin is uniform on the compact local geometry, including the four profile choices. This closes the same local analytic proof with `C=111/25`.

## 4. Full endpoint return

### Exact geometry and physical source

The controller initially forwarded `ell=12518/75000`, then corrected it to `1567/9375`. The initial value is incompatible with `theta=11/12-ell/4` at `.87488`; it is a communication error and was not used in the check. Deriving from theta directly gives exactly the parameter table above, `x+y=1-ell`, `0<ell<x<y<2x`, and `y<1/2<h<2y`.

The source numerator remains `fixedSourcePrincipal S`, with the original common conjugate slot profile, power `33/50`, individual reflected heights, and whole-product conjugation. The target affects fixed arithmetic data, not a growing parent. Positive-gain selection uses the original whole-slot theorem at target capacity, retaining original total supply and zero gains on error slots. It produces the denominator gain at target capacity even if the positive-gain supply is exhausted, shorter than capacity, or empty. No positive-main-supply premise is added.

On `h-.001 <= d <= h+10^-10`, `0<=t<=.001`, set

```

z_A(t)=(1-2n(d,t))/C.
```

The exact new extrema are

```
n_min=714200000/1699173423                 ~= .420322016771563
n_max=402104737237/952737117000           ~= .422052138057932
z_min=74263821263/2115076399740           ~= .0351116495234541
z_max=6769335575/188608249953             ~= .0358909834362329.
```

Thus the old bounds `.422` and `.0355` are false for this candidate; simply importing SS unchanged is invalid. The replacement upper bounds `.423` and `.036` have strict slacks approximately `.00094786` and `.000109017`. Reserve the small selection decrement and annular/box padding inside these slacks.

For the actual selected width z and actual clipped plain lengths `x_i<=n(d,t)`:

* If `z<=.03`, the old positive moment has budget at most `2*.423+4.5*.03=.981`, reserve `19/1000`; the empty case uses the unrestricted zero-slot theorem.
* If `.03<=z<=.036` but one `x_i<=.41`, the old budget is at most `.41+.423+4.5*.036=.995`, reserve `1/200`.
* Otherwise both plain lengths and slot width lie in the unchanged local window, and `x1+x2+Cz<=2n+C z_A<=1`, so the proved local extension applies.

The old two-variable scale supremum is applied on these three regions with all four derivative profiles. Bounded nonempty subunit scales are handled by bounded dilation. No local moment below `.41` is needed.

### Every free Euler shift

Keep B0.42--B0.44 literally: monomial shifts `h0 h_r`, the repeated-prime conductor allocation, the reflected scale at most a fixed multiple of `(U/Y)h0`, and the mass `sum |c_u(h0,h_r)| h0^(delta/2)`. The conductor deficit is used once. Restoring Euler factors only shortens scales. The original support `h0<<Y` keeps reflected individual lengths below `1+o(1)<2`, so the physical unrestricted zero-slot theorem remains valid when affine capacity vanishes.

Direct source check: `certified_original_numerator_fourth` still has the old nonempty capacity `2(m+xi)+6kappa sum width<=1`, or the explicit alternative `T=empty`, and requires `m+xi<=2`. Its fixed-character padding is absorbed into the chosen small loss. One cannot just call this old Lean theorem with the coefficient `111/25`. The new nonempty local branch is the written physical source/reflection composition using the proved local moment, as in Gao's accepted EA; only the old and empty branches directly use the existing wrapper. `certified_reflected_zero_fourier_moment` expressly retains both independent heights and permits individual scales up to `U^2` without a sum-of-plain-lengths gate.

For `b=2y/d-1` and `t>=t0=.001`, use

```
z_old(t)=max(0,(b-2t)/(9/2)),
S_b(t)=t/2-(b/C-z_old(t))/4.
```

The worst b is `b_max=1-2n_min`. Independently,

`S_bmax(t0)=304699205057/1131649499718000 ~= .000269252277435 > 1/4000`.

The old claim `>3/10000` is no longer true and must be replaced. Before clipping, `S'_b=7/18`; afterward, `S'_b=1/2`. Since `0<=q<=delta/2`, every larger shift is paid. For small shifts the direct difference is `t(delta/2-q/C)>=0`. The weighted coefficient mass is sufficient on the full support; no dyad is omitted.

Supply also has large slack: `ell-d_max z_max ~= .1386511>0`; detector supply `ell/d_max-4/21 ~= .02004988`; lower-row supply `2ell-1/3=3/3125>0`. All original slot widths can be fixed below `d0` times the common local/old mesh, with `d0=1/200`, before the target. Their minimum is positive and fixes the common principal-product reserve.

### Complete scalar numerator bound

I independently cleared the exact detector denominator. Put

```
D=3-p-2p/(3kappa_*),
P=2(1-p)(1-p/(3kappa_*)),
V=5/6-delta,

On the whole rectangle, `J>28895/168696>1/10`, by `V>=1/12`, `D>=D(.5)`, and `delta P>=0`. For a row d and physical coefficient c, EA.5 becomes

```
G(d,c)=(1+delta)/2+13h/75-y/2-ell/2+ell*q
       +d*(1/4+3R/4-17/50)-q*(2y-d)/(2c),
```

at the certified endpoints `d>=1/2>y`. The independent Bernstein certificates prove `theta-margin-G>=0` with strict polynomial coefficient positivity:

| Row | Physical coefficient | Certified saving | Rectangles |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `h` | `111/25` | `1/10000000` | 6 |
| `h-1/1000` | `6kappa_*` | `1/100000` | 6 |
| `1/2` | `6kappa_*` | `1/1000` | 1 |

The joint boundary is valid because `C<6kappa_*` and `2y-d>0`. Affinity covers the near-endpoint local interval and the upper old interval. The local slope is at most 2, so the tiny upper row extension leaves `499/5000000000=9.98e-8`. For lower d, retain the full `min(d,2y-d)` old expression; it is convex in d. The explicit old lower endpoint at `d0` has saving `82262161363/750000000000>.1`, so no unexamined row interval remains.

The floor saving is `224790013/15000000000>.01`. The small nonprincipal row relative saving is `21477387121/250000000000>.05`, including finite unit rows. Large rows use the original raw absolute bound and its freely chosen positive line parameter after fixing the row extension. Those arguments are independent of the local amplifier.

### Principal, contour, and continuation costs

The actual compensated-probe geometry has

```
y-2x+ell=-597986039/5000000000<0,
1+3ell-2(x+y)=-308/1875<0,
(5x+y)/12=theta-k,  k=5/6-x/3-ell/6.

The physical principal contour margins remain positive: w-margin `314081484089/15000000000000`, z-margin `219737987/3000000000000`. ## 7. What individual active-conductor sorting actually proves

For one original atom define
\[
\mathfrak h(a,A)=\prod_{v_p(A)-v_p(a)\not\equiv0\ (6)}p,
\qquad h_1=q_{\mathfrak h(a,A)},\quad
h_2=q_{\mathfrak h(b,A')}.
\tag{PH24}
\]
For every surviving pair \(\mathfrak r\mid[\mathfrak h(a,A),\mathfrak h(b,A')]\), in particular \(R\le h_1h_2\). The calibration \(\xi\) cancels in a covariance. Its nonprincipal linear completion cannot simply be applied to the paired row, and the XM linear functional is not a norm estimate.

There is nevertheless a rigorous way to factor positive pre-completion coefficient masses. Fix \(1/6<\beta\le1\), \(\gamma\ge0\), and a polynomial cap \(1\le B\le Z^C\). Let \(\mathscr A_D(\beta,\gamma;B)\) be the absolute sum of actual single-atom coefficients with \(h_{\rm act}\le B\), weighted by
\(h_{\rm act}^{\gamma}\sum_k|b_k|q_k^{-\beta}\), including its source normalization but not its physical branch normalization. Then the exact XM coefficient count gives
\[
\mathscr A_D(\beta,\gamma;B)
\ll Z^\epsilon Y_D^{-1/2}B^{\gamma+1/2}.
\tag{PH25}
\]
For clarity, this is a coefficient lemma derived from XM, not an inference from the value of its linear row sum. Write \(a=tu\), with \(t\) squarefree and \(u\) squareful, and let \(U=q_u\), \(R_u=q_{\prod_{p\mid u,\,6\nmid v_p(u)}p}\). Original zeros force \((u,A)=1\). On a core/cube dyad \(C N^3\asymp T\), its three positive factors are:

- the exact source-amplitude weight \(\sqrt{Y_D}U^{1/2-\beta}R_u^{\beta-1/2}\);
- the source/core count \(\sqrt{Y_D C B/(UR_u)}\), obtained from the actual gcd condition \(q_tq_cR_u/q_{(t,c)}^2\le B\);
- the total cube coefficient \(C^{-1/2}\), along with source normalization \(Y_D^{-3/2}\) and the bound \(h_{\rm act}^{\gamma}\le B^\gamma\).

Their product is
\[
Y_D^{-1/2}B^{\gamma+1/2}U^{-\beta}R_u^{\beta-1}.
\]
Its squareful-source Euler product converges for \(\beta>1/6\), with the exact principal weights \(q_p^{-6j\beta}\). The original completed envelopes sum the dyads and both tails as in XM27-XM30. This proves (PH25) for all actual source powers.

Now expand two single-atom kernels, retaining their exact divisors \(k_1,k_2\). After the common-row embeddings their divisors are
\(k_1'=k_1/(k_1,e^2)\), \(k_2'=k_2/(k_2,d^2)\).
Every surviving paired divisor is at least their lcm; coherent unit-mask expansion can add a prime but cannot lower it. Therefore
\[
q_{[k_1',k_2']}^{-\rho}
\le(q_{k_1'}q_{k_2'})^{-\rho/2}
\le(q_dq_e)^\rho(q_{k_1}q_{k_2})^{-\rho/2}.
\tag{PH26}
\]
If exact valuations conflict, the term is zero before this bound. At common active primes the additional unit-mask expansions cost only the usual divisor factor; all resulting phases retain modulus one. No independent row mask is inserted.

For \(R>1\), completion costs at most
\(R^{(1-\rho)/2}H^\rho\le(h_1h_2)^{(1-\rho)/2}H^\rho\).
Use (PH25) with \(\beta=\rho/2>1/6\) and \(\gamma=(1-\rho)/2\), then restore the exact physical factor. Since
\(H^\rho(q_dq_e)^\rho=Q^\rho/(q_Dq_E)^\rho\), the result for caps \(h_1\le B_D,h_2\le B_E\) is
\[
\boxed{
\sum_{\substack{R>1\\h_1\le B_D,\ h_2\le B_E}}|C_{\lambda\mu}|
\ll\frac{Z^\epsilon Q^{\rho-1}}Y
\sum_{D,E}\frac{|\omega_D\omega_E|}
{(q_Dq_E)^\rho}(B_DB_E)^{1-\rho/2},
\quad 1/3<\rho\le1.
}
\tag{PH27}
\]
The sum is understood with the corresponding polynomial cap in each branch. Constants may depend on the fixed polynomial range, \(\rho\), and epsilon, as in the original XM estimate. It permits extra bounded pair masks. It is an actual covariance-intersection estimate, not positivity of a localized form.

For uniform left/right caps \(B_1,B_2\), writing \(B=B_1B_2\), this becomes
\[
\sum_{R>1,\ h_i\le B_i}|C_{\lambda\mu}|
\ll\frac{Z^\epsilon}{Y}
Q^{\rho-1}L^{2-2\rho}B^{1-\rho/2}.
\tag{PH28}
\]
This particular factorization yields no new sector: \(R\le B\), and FR19 on that larger sector has the same \(Q,B\) powers but the smaller embedding factor \(L^{\max(2-4\rho,0)}\). Thus FR dominates (PH28) for every allowed \(\rho\).

Quantitatively, at the saved geometry the largest affordable product-cap exponent from (PH28) is its buffered \(\rho\downarrow1/3\) limit,
\[
\log_Z B\le
\frac45(M-2\ell)+\frac15(y-x)
=0.412469059106539142\ldots.
\tag{PH29}
\]
It is smaller than the FR exponent by \(0.163830503216995006\ldots\). The derivative of the affordable exponent has the sign of
\(-(M-2\ell)/2+(y-x)/12<0\), so another choice inside this family does not repair the loss. The limiting source series is not evaluated at \(\beta=1/6\); choose a positive buffer and absorb its polynomial cost as before.

A low/high cross term with no finite cap on the second side requires an additional bound on its actual coefficient mass or its actual Hilbert norm. T06 pays the sum of same-core norms, not the norm after summing all high-conductor cores. Substituting that unknown norm into Cauchy would restate part of the open covariance. A useful improvement would have to retain arithmetic coupling discarded in (PH26), or prove cancellation between the actual paired columns. The numerical loss above diagnoses this concrete factorization, not all possible active-conductor methods.

## PS3. Cubic twists occupy square-indexed sextic rows

Fix the original finite ray component and finite excluded set S. Away
from S write `theta_c=chi_c^2` for the cubic and sextic characters, both
extended by zero at nonunits. For the actual dual core twist,

\[
\psi_n(c)=\theta_c(\lambda)\overline{\theta_c(n)}
=\nu(c)\overline{\chi_c(n^2)},\qquad
\nu(c)=\theta_c(\lambda).
\tag{PS15}
\]

The fixed lambda phase is handled only in its prescribed fixed finite
family. A dual row with `q_n~H` becomes a sextic index `u=n^2` with
`q_u~H^2`. If n is cube-free then u is sixth-power-free. The primitive
good conductor may be `rad(n)`; this does not change the indexing norm
in a moment summed over `q_u~U`. The same distinction is recorded in
[private research revision] T01's conventions and the BC natural-zero argument.

On the balanced bare outside-cube piece, freeze each permitted external
incidence/deletion mask R and profile before applying a positive moment.
Define the centrally normalized polynomial

\[
M_n=D^{-1/2}\!
\sum_{q_c\asymp D,\ (c,R)=1}
\mu(c)\nu(c)\overline{\chi_c(n^2)}W(c).
\tag{PS16}
\]

Here W includes only the original annular/common norm and fixed-ray
profiles, independent of n; row-natural zeros remain in the character.
For unequal columns and common-core projector divisor g the same
argument uses the residual lengths and masks in BC, not arbitrary
pair-dependent coefficients. For `n=d kappa^3`, the exact identity has
the additional mask `(c,kappa)=1`; no condition `(d,kappa)=1` is imposed.

Let `mathcal M_u` denote the same sum with `bar chi_c(u)` in place of
`bar chi_c(n^2)`, so `M_n=mathcal M_(n^2)`. The whole sextic-row UM/MI
estimate, when its length and mask hypotheses hold, permits the
positive enlargement

\[
\sum_{q_n\asymp H}^{\mathrm{cube\text{-}free}}|M_n|^2
\le O(1)\sum_{q_u\asymp H^2}^{(6)}|\mathcal M_u|^2
\ll T^A H^{2+\epsilon}.
\tag{PS17}
\]

The fixed O(1) is the generator multiplicity, absent for ideal indexing.
At `H=D^2/K`, `K<=D^.87653`, one has `D<H`, so the unmarked short-length
condition `D<=U^(1/2)` with `U=H^2` is not the difficulty. The lost factor
is row density: the requested family has O(H) indices inside a family
of O(H^2) indices. Positivity alone cannot recover that factor.

The physical balanced covariance has normalization `D^2/H` after PS16.
Thus this import gives only `T^A D^(2+epsilon) H`, not `D^(2+epsilon)`.
Even this statement concerns its CC piece; it supplies no identification
of a dual class with the original signed whole II subtraction.

A sufficient genuinely new interface for this primitive band would be

\[
\sum_{q_n\asymp H}^{\mathrm{cube\text{-}free}}|M_n|^2
\ll T^A H(DH)^\epsilon,
\tag{PS18}
\]

with all the actual masks above, the two columns' common-core projector,
the BC weighted outer sums, and a common polynomial height bound.
Equivalently one may seek the corresponding exact bilinear estimate
before positive enlargement. PS18 is **not proved here** and is not a
consequence of an unweighted plain fourth moment or pointwise I-HECKE.
The remaining double-large-core CC minus whole II remains open.

# Accepted literal f3 threshold laws

Controller disposition, 11 October 2026: accept the frozen
[fixed-power source proof](f3-signed/report.md), the distinct
[critical-window candidate](critical-threshold-candidate.md), and the
[independent reconstruction](f3-review/report.md), with the exact scopes
below. The controller read all complete proofs and reconstructed the
source, signs, prime-density factors and return interfaces. The reviewer
supplies a useful explicit all-core continuous-integral tail bound for
the critical candidate's CT5. No new full-field power exponent or
zero-free constant follows from these source results.

Write f(n)=mu(rad(n/3^v_3(n))), with all valuations retained; g is the
fixed normalized variance-tau Gaussian. Set

    F(x)=sum_n f(n)g(log(n/x)),
    T_z(x)=sum_(omega_z(n)<=1)f(n)g(log(n/x)),
    R_z(x)=sum_(omega_z(n)>=2)f(n)g(log(n/x)),

where omega_z counts distinct prime divisors greater than z. Thus
F=T_z+R_z exactly on the uncapped integers. All estimates below are
uniform on the complete closed shell X<=x<=2X. Threshold masks inherit
no other source's cancellation estimate.

## Fixed powers below one half

Fix 1/3<rho_0<=rho<=rho_1<1/2, tau>0, and a buffered Mertens
exponent 1/2<beta<1 with sum_(n<=u)mu(n)=O_beta(u^beta). The retained
baseline permits beta=.8749; the new accepted endpoint permits any
fixed beta>.874872. Put L=log X, delta=(1-2rho_1)/4 and
eta=delta(1-beta)>0. Then

    R_(X^rho)(x)=C_f e^(tau/2) B(rho) x/L^3
                       +O(X/L^4+X^(1-eta)L),
    C_f=9log2 product_(p>=5)(1-1/(p-1)^2)>0,
    B(rho)=2log((1-rho)/rho)-2/(1-rho)-1/(1-rho)^2.

B is strictly negative and decreasing on (1/3,1/2). Hence the band
T_(X^b)-T_(X^a), for fixed 1/3<a<b<1/2, is positive with leading
coefficient C_f e^(tau/2)[B(a)-B(b)]. For a=3/8,b=2/5 this difference
is exactly 79/225+2log(10/9)>0. The complete terminal complement at
any fixed rho_plus>1/2 is O_A(X^-A), so the band from such a fixed a
to rho_plus is negative of order X/L^3. Signs of individual threshold
jumps have not been proved.

The mechanism is source-specific. Its Euler series is H(s)/zeta(s),
where H has absolutely summable coefficients for Re(s)>1/2 and a
simple zero from p=2 at s=1. Transferring the buffered mu-Mertens
bound through its actual convolution proves the f partial-sum bound.
The reciprocal series consequently has a double zero at1, giving
ordinary-order signed core moments 0,0,2C_f. It is not legitimate to
derive these partial sums merely by inverting a Gaussian norm bound.

Below a fixed power U<z^3 the original source has exactly n=rpq,
p<q both greater than z, each of valuation one, r<z, coefficient f(r).
Outside U the completed formula can fail; its full divisor-weighted
Gaussian tail is paid. Signed Abel summation removes r>X^delta before
prime-density substitution. The p=q correction and both sharp PNT
endpoints are paid. Two sequential fixed-order Stieltjes replacements
give the exact unordered density phi_t(A)=A^-1 log((A-t)/t), A>2t.
The Taylor remainder and its derivative are summed by signed Abel,
not an unsigned harmonic bound. The resulting C_f phi_t'' gives B.
The complete proofs price every source-completion and reciprocal-core
tail before reading off its sign.

The compact rho interval is fixed. No uniformity at rho=1/3, at
rho=1/2, or through a moving transition is asserted. In particular
[private research revision]'s negative subpower bands cannot be extrapolated into this
positive fixed-power band range.

## Fixed multiples of the square-root threshold

Fix tau>0 and kappa>=1. Define the absolutely convergent profile

    J(v)=integral_v^infinity e^u(u-v)g(u)du,
    Phi(q)=sum_(r>=1) f(r)/r J(log(rq)), q>0.

Then, with z=kappa sqrt(X),

    R_z(x)=2x/L^2 Phi(kappa^2 X/x)+O_(tau,kappa)(X/L^3).

This theorem uses ordinary fixed-order PNT and absolute core estimates;
it uses no Mertens input, conditional reciprocal moment or bound for F.
For kappa^2>=2e^(3tau), the entire shell has q>=e^(3tau) and

    Phi(q)>=(3/4)J(log q)>0.

Thus the actual complement is positive of order X/L^2. The full band
T_(X^rho_plus)-T_(kappa sqrt(X)), for any fixed rho_plus>1/2, has the
same positive leading profile and error, again without a bound for F.
A negative leading prefix T_z follows only after separately using the
accepted F(x)=O(X^beta). For other fixed kappa>=1 the profile formula
is proved, but this positivity criterion makes no sign assertion.

Here the core remains absolutely controlled because the threshold
forces a rapid Gaussian decay in log r. The central original source
has exactly two distinct rough primes as before. Cores above X^.01
and primes above X^.52 are complete Gaussian tails. Both finite
Stieltjes substitutions include both endpoints. The review proves the
continuous extension by the exact positive full-core expression

    x integral_(log a)^infinity e^u g(u)
       sum_(r<=e^u/a) (u-log(ar))/r du, a=kappa^2 X/x,

whose inner sum is O_kappa((1+u_+)^2). Every omitted set forces
u>=.01log X-O(1). This pays the extension before any cancellation.
After p=sqrt(X)v, q=sqrt(X)w, the global density error is bounded by
8(log v+log w)/L^3 and is absolutely integrable over all cores.
The unordered factor1/2 and leading density4/L^2 give exactly2.
Finally J(v+log r)<=r^-2 J(v) for v>=3tau; r=1 exceeds the total
r>=2 absolute contribution, at most J(v)/4. Neither kappa nor tau
moves with X in the admitted theorem.

## Complete energy and the remaining arithmetic problem

The reviewer retains all ordered Gram entries, the true original
n=m diagonal O(X), every cross interaction and both independent
Mellin heights. Auxiliary prime/core coincidences do not replace that
diagonal. The fixed finite threshold partition has a rank-one leading
Gram matrix, but logarithmic profile errors are too large for a new
power saving.

For the actual split F=T+R, set a=||T||, b=||R|| and
r_X=Re<T,R>/(ab). Exactly,

    ||F||^2=(a-b)^2+2ab(1+r_X).

For the fixed-power split b is comparable to X/L^3; for the positive
critical split it is comparable to X/L^2. At either split, a complete
new exponent 1/2<gamma<.874872 is equivalent, with epsilon allowance,
to BOTH |a-b|<<X^(gamma+epsilon) and
1+r_X<<X^(2gamma-2+epsilon)L^(2d), d=3 or2 respectively.
The baseline already gives near cancellation when normalized by the
actual b^2. Replacing b by its asymptotic profile introduces a separate
O(1/L) error; that error must not be mistaken for a power estimate.

The newly proved signs rule out a monotone late-band extrapolation and
expose an explicit critical profile. The next useful step is an actual
joint mismatch/cosine estimate, or a source-specific low-gcd correlation
bound, at power precision. More terms of a fixed logarithmic asymptotic
alone do not supply it. The exact whole-field convolution return is
available after reconstructing F; it gives no hereditary transfer to
arbitrary moving masks, SP/RN subfamilies or Hecke twists.

### 3.3 The full transformed-row error

Put H_m=mT/N. The number of positive near aliases is O(1+H_m). If any exists, its positive integer h forces H_m>=c_Q'>0. Consequently their remainders, INCLUDING1/m, sum to

    O(e^(-c rho)(N/(mT))(1+H_m))=O(e^(-c rho)).              (R8)

Outside the near window, nonzero |h|<=C H_m have scaled derivative separated from zero by cT. Two integrations by parts give (N/m)T^-2 e^(-c rho) per alias. Their count is O(H_m) whenever nonempty, so they cost O(T^-1 e^(-c rho)). This includes all negative aliases in that range.

For |h|>C H_m the derivative has size |h|N/m and dominates every higher phase derivative. Two integrations by parts give (m/N)|h|^-2 e^(-c rho). Summing BOTH signs costs O(T^-1 e^(-c rho)) if H_m is bounded below, and O((m/N)e^(-c rho)) otherwise. Here m<=X^alpha0<=N, so this is O(e^(-c rho)). The transition ranges have fixed constants and cause no loss. Thus every complete row equals its full stationary bank plus a uniform damped O(1). No infinite alias bill remains. Summing the block errors costs O(AMe^(-c rho)) pointwise and in both shell norms.

statement:
## 6. Protected S28: source-exact signed coupling audit

The seed proposes a joint signed coupling of additive and multiplicative filtrations, with a small total-variation defect. Its p=1/2000/high-ceiling status was protected before outcomes. A distinction between ordinary marginals and weighted divisor constraints is essential.

### 6.1 Conservation and the full finite dual

A usual finite signed or complex coupling has equal total row and column masses. If its additive marginal is a(n), 1<=n<=N, while its multiplicative marginal is (a*chi)(n)=delta_(n=1), the two totals are M_chi(N) and1. Such a coupling can exist only when M_chi(N)=1. At N=2, q=1 the totals are0 and1; for the quartic mod5 character they are1-i and1. A ghost/remainder repairing this particular mismatch must carry M_chi(N)-1. This refutes only that conservative interpretation, not a weighted, nonconservative divisor identity.

For a feasible version, partition {1,...,N} into additive cells I_i and another partition C_j. Let E contain precisely permitted nonempty intersections and let

    Z^0_ij=sum_(n in I_i intersect C_j)a(n),
    r_i=sum_j Z^0_ij, c_j=sum_i Z^0_ij.

Both marginal totals are now M. The exact minimum-TV problem has dual

    inf_(rows r, columns c, support E) sum_E |Z_ij|
      =sup_(|u_i+v_j|<=1 on E)
          Re[sum_i conj(u_i)r_i+sum_j conj(v_j)c_j].

Weak duality follows by substituting the two marginals and applying |u_i+v_j|<=1 to each entry. For equality, regard the marginal map B as a real linear map on a finite complex vector space. The minimum is the quotient norm inf_(BZ=b)||Z||_1 on range B; its unit ball is compact. A supporting functional at b has dual norm1, extends to the ambient marginal space in finite dimension, and gives B*phi with entries u_i+v_j. This proves the formula, including redundant marginal constraints. For real coefficients this is an LP after positive/negative splitting; for complex character coefficients it is a convex modulus/SOCP problem, not literally the same real LP. No arithmetic estimate is inferred from generic duality.

Taking all u_i to have the phase of M and v=0 gives minimum TV>=|M|. If every additive cell is a singleton, row marginals force

    sum_E |Z_ij|>=sum_(n<=N)|a(n)|,

and the actual intersection array attains equality. The squarefree unit count is kappa_q N+O_q(sqrt N), kappa_q>0, by the same square-divisor calculation as in B. Thus **full coupling TV** with singleton source rows is linear. This is not a lower bound for the TV of an intelligently chosen defect. Conversely, if two arrays have the exact same two marginals, their difference has both marginals zero: a small difference alone says nothing about the common M. Taking the arrays equal gives defect zero at any M. A useful defect argument must specify an independently controlled comparison readout and a full return, rather than infer cancellation merely from marginal invariance.

### 6.2 A paid weighted-divisor repair and its complete return

The actual multiplicative equations use a weighted triangular map, not a conservative coupling. On {1,...,N} define

    C_(n,d)=chi(n/d)1_(d divides n),
    A_(n,d)=mu(n/d)chi(n/d)1_(d divides n).

Both diagonals are1 and AC=CA=I, because a*chi=delta in Dirichlet convolution for a(n)=mu(n)chi(n). All prime powers and natural zeros occur. For any candidate vector v set e=Cv-e_1. Then v-a=Ae, exactly. For every integer interval (L,U] within [1,N],

    sum_(L<n<=U)v_n - [M(U)-M(L)]
      =sum_(k<=U)e_k [M(floor(U/k))-M(floor(L/k))].       (S28-R)

This follows by finite divisor summation, grouping n=kd before taking any norm. For L=0 it reads sum v-M(N)=sum e_k M(floor(N/k)). There is no independent-error assumption, missing k=1 source term, or endpoint smoothing. The checker validates complex and ramified examples with full intervals.

Consequently a proved O(N^(gamma+epsilon)) bound for BOTH the candidate readout sum v and the entire signed response on the right implies the same bound for M(N), with the usual all-scale/common-character quantifiers and the all-height Mellin return. This is a legitimate repair target, but its response is not automatically cheap. For unrestricted complex errors with weighted TV sum w_k|e_k|, the exact scalar operator norm is

    max_(k<=N) |M(floor(N/k))|/w_k.

Triangle gives the upper bound and an error supported at a maximizing k with aligning phase attains it. The k=1 term already contains M(N). The unconditional alternative is at most N sum |e_k|/k, with exponent1 in that generic price. Restrictions on actual compatible defects can escape this norm obstruction; they must be stated and proved. This is the established paid inverse/adjoint principle (G107 and W54-X23), now written for the seed's literal two-filtration ambition, not a new inverse family or a proof that all signed couplings fail.

**Disposition:** protect the genuinely global signed-coupling idea as promising but unbridged. Its naive conservative realization is impossible in general; a generic full-TV certificate is too expensive; the exact nonconservative repair above is available but requires a new source-specific signed estimate. G116's compatible actual defect and hard-region target illustrate why one must not turn an ambient norm bound into an arithmetic impossibility.
title: 6. Protected S28: source-exact signed coupling audit

### A4. Quantitative zero return and deliberately coarse allowance

For a(n)=mu(n)chi(n), absolute Mellin Fubini on Re s>1 gives exp(tau*s^2/2)/L(s,chi). A10 and dyadic Cauchy--Schwarz continue this transform holomorphically for Re s>eta+d/2. Multiplying by L continues the identity; the Gaussian multiplier is nonzero. Thus zeros there are excluded, with the usual principal pole at1 excepted. For actual a(n)=f3(n)chi(n) use its already paid nonvanishing-numerator/inverse-convolution return, in the fixed ordinary-character scope, and require eta+d/2>1/2. For the original ideal source a(mathfrak a)=mu_K(mathfrak a)eta(mathfrak a), the same direct Mellin proof applies with its own complete moment input; no transfer from an ordinary source to an ideal source is inferred.

The weakest sufficient condition in this construction for a first gain is

    eta+d/2 < .874864.                                  (A14)

Useful examples, all CONDITIONAL on the corresponding complete signed A13 bound:

| Arithmetic norm eta | Moving-order d | Returned boundary | Returned c |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
|.87449|.0007|.87484|.12516|
|5/6|.08|131/150=.873333...|19/150=.126666...|
|3/4|.24|.87|.13|
|5/6|0|5/6|1/6|
|3/4|0|3/4|1/4|

These are genuine complete analytic loss budgets, not ambitious endpoint names. For example eta=.75 allows d<.249728 to exceed c5. They do NOT show that the new scalar is easier to estimate. The continued arithmetic estimate is still wholly open. At fixed frequency, (1+t^2)^-r has only subpower decay in this range, so the old low-frequency coherent component is not automatically removed.

Strongest objection: an H^-r norm can hide high frequencies. A5/A7 pay precisely that obstruction for this actual Gaussian class. S45's raw atomic H^-r norm is a different, stronger hypothesis and cannot be substituted for A6. The claim is not a generic H^-r-to-L2 inequality, and no claim of optimality for d/2 on actual arithmetic sources is made.

## G3 — p<.10, multiplicative/noncommutative dual sector certificate

### W40-11 — Conditional expectation with a paid off-diagonal return; p=.08
O: Split a multiplicative operator into a conditional-expectation block and its complement, retaining the off-diagonal blocks rather than applying a triangle inequality.
B: A full block dual certificate or Schur complement might let a rigorously bounded structured sector pay for its entire complement.
T: For a 2 by 2 self-adjoint block matrix derive the exact minimum complement price as a function of the cross block.
X: The cross block can saturate the whole target norm; sector savings alone do not transfer.
R: Reusable exact criterion for when a restricted result can improve a full-form exponent.

### W40-12 — Multiplicative matrix martingale with signed increments; p=.06
O: Reveal prime valuations successively and encode coefficients as matrix martingale differences so that prime-local mean-zero identities survive noncommuting projections.
B: A variance bound plus explicit predictable drift could control the full signed moment more sharply than summing divisor patterns.
T: Two-prime model with noncommuting projectors; compute the drift created by revealing shifted arguments.
X: Arithmetic dependence and projector nonadaptedness may make drift as large as the original moment.
R: High upstream reach if drift has arithmetic cancellation; exact no-go if it cannot.

### W40-13 — Free-compression dimension diagnostic; p=.03
O: Compare a sector projector and arithmetic covariance projector through principal angles, using free-probability behavior only as a diagnostic, never as an assumption.
B: A deterministic principal-angle lower bound could make the restricted/complement interaction contractive.
T: Construct two rank-half projections with the same traces but arbitrary principal angles and test whether trace data give any uniform saving.
X: Dimension or equidistribution alone does not imply angle control; arithmetic projectors may align.
R: Precise obstruction to an attractive toy heuristic, redirecting work to an explicit angle statistic.

### W40-14 — Noncommutative sector capacity dual; p=.025
O: Define the smallest diagonal/block majorant of the actual signed full operator under a fixed sector budget, and write its semidefinite dual as a flow of test matrices.
B: A low-cost explicit dual witness or primal majorant could certify the exact complement price uniformly in size.
T: Solve an arrowhead block example with one structured sector and two interacting complements; compare separate versus joint complement payment.
X: Optimizing a finite matrix gives no arithmetic uniformity, and the full operator may be inaccessible.
R: Exact variational target capable of combining weak sector estimates without silently dropping cross terms.

### W40-15 — GNS positivity failure as a detector redesign; p=.012
O: Attempt to realize the signed arithmetic correlation functional as a positive state on a multiplicative algebra; use its negative Gram direction to construct a correction.
B: A bounded correction turning it into a positive state might unlock noncommutative moment bounds while preserving the zero implication.
T: Compute the smallest Gram minor on two prime generators with a signed coefficient and determine the exact positivity defect.
X: A positive correction may erase precisely the arithmetic cancellation; no bounded correction may exist.
R: A rigorous obstruction or a new corrected detector, not a license to assume positivity.
