statement:
### 3b. Strongest objection: stable optimal polynomials are automatic

Let p_N minimize (7). If p_N=(z-lambda)q has a root, variation by zq is admissible because it has zero constant term. Orthogonality gives

    ||qF||^2-lambda <qF,zqF>=0.

Multiplication by z is an isometry and equality in Cauchy--Schwarz is impossible for nonzero qF and zqF. Hence |lambda|>1. Every finite minimizer is therefore zero-free on the closed disk for EVERY nonzero F with F0!=0, including sources that have interior zeros. This proves that “the optimized polynomials are stable” is not an arithmetic result. It is a universal optimization property.

For the exact toy F(z)=1-z/r with real r>0, G_N is tridiagonal with diagonal 1+r^-2 and adjacent entries -r^-1. Its size-m determinant is D_m=sum_(k=0)^m r^(-2k), including D_0=1 for the empty determinant. Therefore

    d_N=D_(N+1)/D_N,
    lim d_N = r^-2 if 0<r<1, and 1 if r>=1.            (14)

At r=1, Delta_N=1/(N+1). At r=1/2, Delta_N tends to 3, although every optimizing polynomial is stable and the Gram spectrum is uniformly bounded between (1/r-1)^2 and (1/r+1)^2. More strongly, G_N(r)=r^(-2)G_N(1/r), so the entire sequence of constrained optimizing polynomials is IDENTICAL for an interior zero r and the exterior zero 1/r. Their coefficients or root locations alone cannot distinguish the two cases; the scalar residual normalization is essential. For the inner toy F=(z-r)/(1-rz), 0<r<1, the complete Gram is exactly the identity and d_N=1 for all N, while |F0|^2=r^2. Matrix positivity and good conditioning do not pay the prediction gap either. These are toy obstructions to the stated inference, not lower bounds on the actual character source.

This is classical optimal-polynomial approximation, not a literature novelty. The primary paper by Beneteau, Khavinson, Liaw, Seco and Sola, *Orthogonal polynomials, reproducing kernels, and zeros of optimal approximants*, arXiv:1509.04807v2 (17 September 2015), Theorem 3.2 and sections 5-6, establishes the related universal zero-free property and cyclicity/Gram framework: https://arxiv.org/pdf/1509.04807 . Our constrained p0=1 version is proved above. The contribution proposed for the QRH record is the literal ordinary-character source (2)-(5), complete tail (12)-(13), calibration and scoped failure; not a new general Hardy theorem.
title: 3b. Strongest objection: stable optimal polynomials are automatic

## 3. Primitive mixed-order Poisson, all holes, and both roots

Expand sixth-freeness with sum_(a0^6|u)mu(a0), retaining (a0,Hcol*x*y)=1, and expand the canceled-phase hole by sum_(d|E,d|u/a0^6)mu(d). Since d is prime to kxy, its character value is a unit; this does not divide out any zero. Put u=a0^6 d z. The row scale is U/(N(a0)^6 N(d)), and primitive Poisson applies to psi_k chi_x^e conjugate(chi_y^e), with conductor kxy. Nonprincipal summands have zero Fourier term at ell=0 and at primes shared by ell and that conductor.

Write q_d=N(d), q_a=N(a0). General CRT gives the normalized Gauss factor

    gamma(psi_k;k) gamma_e(x) gamma_-e(y)
       *psi_k(xy) chi_x(k*y)^e chi_y(k*x)^(-e).        (4)

The core cross ratio chi_x(y)^e chi_y(x)^(-e) is the fixed PR9 ray sign. Every remaining k interaction is a product of a function of x and a function of y. Its modulus is one on actual coprime supports. The mixed gamma(psi_k;k) also has modulus one; it is not replaced by a cuspidal coefficient or by gamma_1(k).

The actual inverse Mobius signs on residual x,y obey the same whole-slot sign identity as G185. Applying PR9 B1.10 leaves exactly the two G185 orientations: for e=-1, a0(x)conjugate(a0(y)) with chi_x(-1)conjugate(G(x))G(y); for e=+1, conjugate(a0(x))a0(y) with G(x)conjugate(G(y))chi_y(-1), together with the retained fixed ray sign. Multiply these by (4)'s separated k twists and all original collision coefficients. The factor psi_k(d)chi_x(d)^e chi_y(d)^(-e) from the hole expansion is also separated. Both orientations remain present.

Before extending coprimality or taking an absolute Fourier integral, pay the genuine far tail. On q_a~A, the original conductor is comparable to Kc N0^2/(L R). Fix tau=1/1000 and a fixed support constant C_* large enough. The retained cap is

    H_c=C_* U^tau A^6 q_d Kc N0^2/(U L R).          (5)

It is literal on each original collision/hole summand, fixed before the artificial f extension below. For ell beyond it the actual Schwartz argument is >c U^tau. PR9 B3.4 and the complete original tuple count pay the tail by

    O(H_J U^(149/30+epsilon-tau(B-1))).

Indeed the primitive prefactor of one original pair is U/(q_a^6 q_d N0 sqrt(Q)), Q=N(kxy)<=C N0^2. Its absolute frequency sum above that argument is bounded by this prefactor times (1+q_a^6 q_d Q/U)U^(-tau(B-1)). There are O(N0^2 U^epsilon) original paired tuples, O(U^(1/6)) a0 labels and only divisor-many d per tuple. The raw cost is at most U^(1/6)(U N0+N0^2)U^epsilon, bounded by U^(149/30+epsilon). This also covers H_c<1: then the entire nonzero lattice tail is treated by the same bound. Choose finite B after this raw count. No Poisson-frequency tail is discarded after algebraic extension.

For coprime squarefree x,y the pair coefficient and primitive root have prefactor

    U sqrt(LR)/(q_a^6 q_d N0^2 sqrt(Kc)),             (6)

with bounded original norm ratios kept in the smooth profile. Extend this displayed product expression formally to individually squarefree x,y prime to Hcol, and insert the COMPLETE identity sum_(f|x,f|y)mu(f). It kills every artificial noncoprime pair. The six gcd predicates remain their original collision-label predicates; they are not recomputed on the artificial f pairs. The frequency/collision/hole selectors are independent of f. Thus cancellation remains exact, with no imprimitive Poisson assertion on added pairs.

Write x=f m, y=f m', F=N(f). Independently allocate every f prime to its original inverse color or named surviving slot on each side. With all original shortenings, the two residual product scales are

    X_L=N0/(L F), X_R=N0/(R F).                      (7)

They need not agree. Both allocation multiplicities cost tau(f)^C. Each normalized column is an actual squarefree divisor/slot sum, with squared mass O(H_J U^epsilon), after dividing its coefficient squared mass by X_i. PR9 B1.11 and the fixed k,d,Hcol twists leave separated arbitrary sequences on that copy's two ORIGINAL inverse colors. The other copy is not a sieve variable. All punctures and natural zeros remain. Empty scales remain empty; nonempty subunit nominal scales have bounded clipping cost.

Restoring BOTH unnormalized roots is decisive:

    (6)*sqrt(X_L X_R)=U/(q_a^6 q_d N0 sqrt(Kc) F).   (8)

There is no additional L^-1, R^-1 or common-collision f^-1 factor. The real norm ratios remain once in the common profile. The complete Gauss extraction also leaves only unit f twists and the outer natural hole1_((f,ell)=1), never division by it.

Fix nominal dyads for a0,d,ell and all finitely many collision-norm coordinates before choosing live arithmetic labels. On their full ambient boxes the kernel is K(U q_ell L R/(q_a^6 q_d Kc q_n q_n')); its Euler derivatives are uniformly controlled for every nominal scaling constant. PR9 B3.3 therefore fixes one weighted Fourier measure first, including each original real root once. Only then substitute labels and allocations. No f-dependent profile or selector is introduced. All sharp masks remain outside the smooth separation. The number of such dyadic coordinates is bounded at fixed slot depth, hence costs a subpower.

The formal core extension may include the unit pair x=y=1 when k=1. Subtract this rank-one block explicitly; it is the already paid merged diagonal. Its FULL absolute Poisson-frequency sum, even after frequency selection, costs O(H_J U^(1+epsilon)): for one diagonal coefficient the a0,d sum is bounded by sum_(a0,d|E)(U/(q_a^6 q_d)+1)<<U^(1+epsilon), using q_a<<U^(1/6); then sum the complete c_abs(n)^2 mass. ## 3. Partial inverse marking and the conditioned envelope

Put h_delta=5-2delta, e_delta=5-6delta, and rho=1-10delta/(3h_delta). The accepted marked inverse amplification is

    E_MI(W,r,x)=W/6+(5/6)max(W,r+2x,(2r+8x)/3).

For r in [1/2,1], mark the highest-grade original slots up to x=min(v,(1-r)/2), after decreasing by the mesh/error margin. The other MI inequality has positive slack away from its harmless r=1/2 endpoint, where one decreases the capacity by the allocated tolerance. Greedy filling removes at least qbar*x of the total positive grade, where qbar is the actual mean. The complement's price is at most q(v-x). Divide the inverse witness and apply the original MI, not a bin-restricted Poisson identity. The weighted count is bounded by

    I(r)=1-delta r+q[v-(1-r)/2]_+  (r<=1),
    L(r)=1/6+(5/6-delta)r+qv       (r>=1).              (D3)

For r>=1, marking any positive additional width through the full amplified MI costs slope 5/3-q>0, so the unmarked amplified inverse is better. More generally, for r>=1/2 the third term of the MI maximum is no larger than r+2x. Minimizing the amplified MI plus the pointwise price over ALL partial x gives precisely (D3). Thus this partial-marking estimate is the optimum of that particular moment/pointwise operation. It does not assert optimality of the actual inverse norm.

I is continuous and strictly decreasing through r=1-2v, with slopes -delta and -(delta-q/2). The previous all-marked/unmarked minimum had an intermediate increasing/decreasing hump. That hump can be removed without a new moment theorem, although it was already below the binding short/long envelope in the accepted parameter range.

Using the original restricted MP with capacity 9/2 in the same way gives

    P(m)=1-2delta m+q[v-(1-2m)/(9/2)]_+.

Its slopes in m are negative, so m>=t-r can be weakened to m=t-r. Unrestricted zero-slot MP handles a bounded subunit length or the small m>1/2 tolerance. Full sixth-power amplification of MP beyond its capacity cannot help: its extra marked-width slope is 15/4-q>0. These calculations retain the exact natural masks and original coefficient family.

Define

    D=135delta-54delta^2-20q,
    v0=2e_delta/(135-54delta-24q),
    a=2delta q e_delta^2/[3h_delta D],
    b=3delta q(15+18delta-8q)/D.

Choose BEFORE witnesses

    v<=v0: t=(5-6qv)/h_delta,               r_b=2t/3;
    v>=v0: t=(135delta-20q-12delta q-108delta qv+24q^2v)/D,
             r_b=[(18delta-4q)t+2q-9qv]/(27delta-4q).

On the entire rectangle delta in [.68,.70], omega=delta-q in [0,.01], v in [0,.05], these choices have 1<t<3/2, 0<t-r_b<1/2 and r_b<1-2v. The helper proves the cleared continuous inequalities by 194 positive rational Bernstein coefficients for eleven polynomials over that whole three-dimensional box, with exact independent interior identities. It also checks the four defining polynomial identities. These are complete algebra certificates, not a sampled claim about the source.

For example t2-1=6(9delta-2q)(delta-2qv)/D is positive, and

    (3/2)D-N=e_delta(27delta/2-2q)+12qv(9delta-2q)>0,

where N is the second cutoff numerator. For the first crossing, the cleared gap before the inverse kink is e_delta-(30-12delta-12q)v>=11/100. The remaining rational gaps are in the receipt.

On r<=1, the better of the decreasing I and increasing P has its maximum at this short crossing. For r>=1, L increases and is bounded by L(t). The choice of t equates these two maxima. This proves the source-relative conditioned free-row theorem

    sum_(eligible high free rows satisfying D2) |Q_u|^2
      << Z^[E_delta,q(W,z)+epsilon] (1+T)^J,
    E_delta,q(W,z)=rho W+max(4delta q z/h_delta, -aW+bz).  (D4)

At q=delta this is exactly the accepted G envelope, not an extra gain counted on top of it. The switch identity, with v=z/W, is

 \quad\omega=\delta_1+\mathrm{reserve},\quad

# W67 two independent audits before author outcomes

Selection is fixed in audit-selection.json: author tested S02/S27/S15/S11/S24/S21; protected S28 and distinct uniform S09 follow the pre-outcome orders with no redraw. Only author selection metadata has been read. Both developments below precede author report, helper or outcome access. They are exact finite algebra and scoped research targets, not an arithmetic power estimate.

## Protected S28: an exact orthogonal coprimality realization

Let P be ANY finite set of K primes not dividing a fixed ordinary character modulus q. Index subsets A of P by n_A=product(p in A), including1. Retain a_A=mu(n_A)chi(n_A)=(-1)^|A|chi(n_A), and D=diag(a_A). Natural ramified zeros are handled by excluding those sites, not dividing by chi(p)=0. The local disjointness gate is

    G=[[1,1],[1,0]],  G_P=G tensor ... tensor G,
    (G_P)_(A,B)=1_(A intersect B empty).

With phi=(1+sqrt5)/2, set

    U=(phi^2+1)^(-1/2) [[phi,1],[1,-phi]].

Direct multiplication gives U^T U=I and U^T G U=diag(phi,-phi^(-1)). Consequently U_P=U^tensor K is orthogonal. Its own condition number is1: changing to this basis has no reconstruction loss in Euclidean norm. The gate eigenvalues are

    lambda_e=(-1)^j phi^(K-2j),  j=number of minus choices,

with multiplicity binomial(K,j). Thus rank(G_P)=2^K, ||G_P||_op=phi^K, ||G_P^(-1)||_op=phi^K, and ||G_P||_F^2=3^K. These are gate costs, not basis-change costs. Multiplying both sides by the unit-modulus diagonal D preserves singular values, even for complex chi; one must not confuse the bilinear D G_P D with a Hermitian conjugation.

Most importantly, take an arbitrary complex physical weight/mask W_(A,B), including its exact zero extensions. The full arithmetic contraction has the identity

    F(W)=sum_(A,B) a_A a_B 1_(A intersect B empty) W_(A,B)
        =sum_e lambda_e Z_(e,e),
    Z=U_P^T D W D U_P.                                  (A1)

Proof: the original sum is tr(G_P^T D W D); G_P is symmetric, then orthogonal conjugation and trace cyclicity give(A1). No mask is commuted through G_P or dropped. Frobenius norm is preserved: ||Z||_F=||W||_F. The generic absolute/Cauchy price is at most

    (sum_e |lambda_e|^2)^(1/2) (sum_e |Z_(e,e)|^2)^(1/2)
      <=3^(K/2)||W||_F.                                 (A2)

The signed diagonal sum in(A1) can be smaller, but that is an arithmetic estimate on the transformed complete boundary. Diagonalizing the local gate alone supplies no such estimate. Conversely the large generic price does not lower-bound F(W). This is a constructive realization, not a rejection of the proposed basis.

For the actual product cutoff W_(A,B)=1_(n_A n_B<=X)Phi(n_A n_B), grouping DISJOINT pairs yields exactly

    F(W)=sum_(n<=X, squarefree, p|n implies p in P)
                 mu(n)chi(n)2^omega(n)Phi(n).             (A3)

Every prime of n has two assignments to the ordered pair. Thus this simple masked network has coefficient2^omega(n)mu(n)chi(n), not mu(n)chi(n). An intended detector must preserve its own weight W, or prove a separate return for(A3). An appealing tensor picture does not license replacing the actual source coefficient.

There are two different size regimes. For a single divisor cube of an integer N with radical supported on P, product(P)<=N implies (K+1)!<=N, hence K=O(log N/loglog N). Then both2^K and the gate condition number phi^(2K) are N^o(1). Exact full rank on such a cube is not a fixed-power compression barrier. By contrast a complete n<=X source needs all its occurring primes, rather than the prime set of one integer; no single-divisor estimate bounds that global K by O(log X/loglog X). A cutoff projector P_X conjugates to U_P^T P_X U_P with the same rank and norm, but need not remain diagonal or sparse. The complete mask in(A1) is the safe formulation in both cases.

Next mathematical action: choose the LITERALLY intended source weight and establish a complete signed bound for sum_e lambda_e Z_(e,e), or a justified compression plus its entire signed error. Uniformity must include the actual changing P and cutoff. The orthogonal representation itself is paid; the arithmetic estimate remains OPEN. G121 already owns the threshold-mask obstruction and return, while the exact local gate is a prospective new coordinate calculation relative to the reviewed slices. Author overlap will be assessed only after this audit freezes.

## Uniform S09: exact source-specific linear dual and its hidden scalar

Use the actual finite set V={n<=N:mu(n)^2=1,(n,q)=1}. Put a(n)=mu(n)chi(n), including a(1)=1. Include every internal edge e=(n,pn) with p prime, p not dividing nq, pn<=N. Define

    (Bf)_e=f(pn)+chi(p)f(n).

Writing f(n)=a(n)g(n) gives (Bf)_e=a(pn)[g(pn)-g(n)]. The graph is connected by prime deletion, so ker B is exactly span(a). This is G165's native incidence fact, reused rather than claimed new. The exact constraints Bf=0, f(1)=1 determine the actual source uniquely. They are therefore legitimate, but uniqueness alone supplies no magnitude estimate for a target sum.

For arbitrary complex weights w_n let L_w(f)=sum_n w_n f(n). A complete exact dual identity

    L_w(f)=lambda f(1)+sum_e t_e(Bf)_e for EVERY f         (A4)

exists, and its unit coefficient is FORCED to be

    lambda=M_w:=sum_n w_n a(n).                           (A5)

Necessity follows by substituting f=a. Sufficiency follows since w-lambda e_1 annihilates ker B and hence belongs to range(B^T); all pairings here are bilinear, with the appropriate transpose, not a silently changed conjugate pairing. This range statement is finite-dimensional and applies to complex characters.

There is a constructive exact formula. Choose for each v>1 one parent v/p with p dividing v. These prime-deletion parents give a tree rooted at1, whose edges directed away from1 are original prime-adjoining edges. For a child v define F_v=sum_(u in subtree(v))w_u a(u). Since g(u)=g(1)+sum_(v on path1->u)(g(v)-g(parent(v))), exchanging these FINITE sums gives

    L_w(f)=M_w f(1)+sum_(v not1) [F_v/a(v)] (Bf)_(parent(v),v).
                                                               (A6)

All phases have modulus1 and all natural zero states were removed before inversion. For approximate constraints, the same identity retains the FULL residual bill sum_v |F_v| |(Bf)_e|. Changing the tree can change this bill but cannot change the coefficient M_w of the unit observation. Subtree sums are actual signed arithmetic sums, not a free positive constant.

A precise optimization formulation sharpens the issue. Allow any complex lambda,t and set r=w-lambda e_1-B^T t. Then

    M_w=lambda+sum_n r_n a(n),
    |M_w|<=|lambda|+||r||_1.

Moreover

    inf_(lambda,t) (|lambda|+||w-lambda e_1-B^T t||_1)=|M_w|. (A7)

The lower bound is the preceding triangle inequality. Equality is attained with lambda=M_w and an exact solution(A4), for which r=0. Thus the unrestricted dual optimization is exactly the actual signed target in another representation. This does not make a CONSTRUCTIVE certificate useless: explicit lambda,t whose full residual price is N^(gamma+epsilon) would prove the desired source bound. It does prevent claiming a saving merely from feasibility, compression, or the presence of multiplicative constraints.

Adding coprime multiplicativity identities does not add information to this already singleton feasible set. Enforcing false periodicity of mu(n)chi(n) is impermissible; chi is periodic, the twisted Mobius sequence is not generally periodic. A promising new restriction must supply a quantitatively controlled certificate or observation beyond the internal gradients, with all boundary terms paid. A positive norm of Bf alone cannot see a(n); adding outgoing zero-extension observations is precisely the already priced boundary route of G165.

This audit develops the complete tree dual and exact residual optimization, while preserving the possibility of an arithmetic certificate. It gives no Mertens lower bound, no fixed-character impossibility theorem, and no new c. The next useful test is an explicit structured t whose residual sum is proved small WITHOUT placing the desired sum in lambda. The one-way all-height return then needs the complete every-scale source bound, with the principal pole convention and natural zeros retained.

Both audited routes remain open for signed arithmetic development. Neither finite universal algebra nor a favorable review certifies a larger zero-free constant.

## A finite arithmetic target with every complementary term paid

The untruncated formal expression sum_n A(n)W_u(n) must not be obtained by
absolute Fubini over the full future v range: the absolute n sum grows
like exp(u+v), canceling the factor exp(-v), and the remaining Bessel
tail is not absolutely summable by the available bounds. B1 was defined
on the full signed field and justified by the accepted baseline. This
distinction matters.

The following finite reduction is valid. Fix tau=1 for concreteness and
a baseline exponent b=.8749>b0. Let V>0 be fixed. For u>=1, truncate v
at the literal endpoint Vu. By B1a the removed future is bounded by

    |Tail_v(u)| <<_b A*u*exp((b-(1-b)*V)*u)/(1-b).          (B13)

This uses the accepted full-field Mertens bound only at the fixed b=.8749.
It neither presupposes the desired saving nor discards positive cores.

Now define the sharp integer cap

    N(u)=floor(exp((1+V)*u+sqrt(u)))

and the exact finite kernel

    W_(A,V,u)(n)=g_1(log n-u)
       -integral_0^(Vu) exp(-v)*sqrt(Au/v)*J_1(2sqrt(Auv))
                                  *g_1(log n-u-v)dv,
    Q_(A,V)(u)=sum_(1<=n<=N(u)) A(n)W_(A,V,u)(n).          (B14)

Use the limiting value Au at v=0. The point v=Vu is retained; changing
that single integration endpoint has no effect. The integer cap includes
n=N(u). Both Mobius factors use their literal zero conventions. The first
checks are A(1)=1, A(2)=-3 and A(4)=2. Thus A(n) need not vanish at every
squareful n; its even correction is preserved literally.
There is no rough-prime mask, congruence projector or deleted diagonal.

All n-series interchanges on 0<=v<=Vu are now absolutely justified. For
n>N(u) and 0<=v<=Vu, log n-u-v>=sqrt(u)+o(1). Since |A(n)|<=3, the
Gaussian integral test and completion of the square yield

    sum_(n>N(u)) |A(n)|g_1(log n-u-v)
       << exp(u+v-u/2+O(sqrt(u))).

The factor exp(-v) in B14 cancels exp(v), and the Bessel factor is <=Au.
The integrated coefficient tail is consequently

    exp(u/2+O(sqrt(u)))*O_A(1+u^2).                       (B15)

The direct g_1 term satisfies the same bound. Floors change the threshold
by O(exp(-(1+V)u-sqrt(u))), absorbed in the displayed estimate. Thus

    D_A(u)=Q_(A,V)(u)
       +O_(A,b,V)(u*exp((b-(1-b)*V)*u))
       +exp(u/2+O(sqrt(u)))*O_A(1+u^2).                  (B16)

All constants are fixed before u. In general the future-tail condition is
V>(b-gamma)/(1-b). This pays both infinite complements for the choices below.
The finite initial range 0<=u<=1 contributes an entire transform and
does not enter an asymptotic shell estimate.

For the three target rows, simple rational choices are:

| gamma | V | Future-tail exponent b-(1-b)V | Largest arithmetic scale |
|---|---|---|---|
| .874484 | .004 | .8743996 | n<=x^1.004*exp(sqrt(log x)) |
| .83332 | .34 | .832366 | n<=x^1.34*exp(sqrt(log x)) |
| .74995 | 1.01 | .748549 | n<=x^2.01*exp(sqrt(log x)) |

Each future exponent and the coefficient-tail exponent 1/2 is strictly
below gamma. It therefore suffices to prove the finite, literal bound

    integral_(log X)^(log(2X)) |Q_(A,V)(u)|^2 du
                    <<_epsilon X^(2gamma+epsilon)         (B17)

with the same all-dyadic-X and every-epsilon quantifiers. B16 then gives
B6 by the triangle inequality in L2 without an exponent loss. This is the
exact unresolved arithmetic term in this architecture.

The weaker sufficient arithmetic target is likewise

    integral_(log X)^(log(2X)) |Q_(A,V)(u)|du
                      <<_epsilon X^(gamma+epsilon).       (B17-L1)

B16 pays its complements too. B17-L1 followed by B6-L1 is the weakest
complete first-gain chain developed here; B17/B18 are optional stronger
second-moment forms, with their exact cross terms displayed for audit.

For clarity, B17 is the FULL Gram. With N_max=N(log(2X)), it is exactly

    sum_(m,n<=N_max) A(m)A(n)
      *integral_(log X)^(log(2X)) 1_(m<=N(u))1_(n<=N(u))
                         *W_(A,V,u)(m)W_(A,V,u)(n)du.      (B18)

All cross terms and both moving caps stay inside this expression. No
individual positive block is substituted for it. Diagonal-only estimates,
generic bounded coefficients, or an independent bound on each future
window do not establish B18. The original full alternating convolution is
already encoded by the exact A=mu*(delta_1-2delta_2); if one re-expands
through G4, it must be restored in full. The four current Gaussian product
diagonals cannot be borrowed unchanged over the new range x to x^(1+V).
This is a replacement detector with its own finite source and return.

The longer arithmetic range is a substantial cost, especially at 1/4.
It is disclosed here rather than hidden as a logarithmic restoration.

    HS^2=4n2+n1=2(Q-p-r)=2(phi-1),  operator norm=2.

If only the p-component of t is nonzero, the multiplicities instead are n1=2(r-1), n2=(p-1)(r-1)/2, with correlation-(r-1); the other orientation is symmetric. The full mark carrier repeats each nonzero row singular value phi times and scales it by|b0|. Fourier conjugation changes none of these quantities.

For rank k<=n2 approximation, the squared HS error is at least4(n2-k)+n1; for k<n2 the operator error is at least2. This follows by removing at most k largest singular directions, or the min-max/kernel-dimension argument. The full carrier has the corresponding repeated multiplicities and b0 scaling. For k distinct integer shifts0<j<min(p,r), let P=sum c_j S_j. Their matrix diagonals are disjoint, so

    ||[M_m,P]||_op<=2||c||_1<=2 sqrt(k)||c||_2,
    rank[M_m,P]>=(phi-1)/(2k) if c!=0.

A8's prose needs normalization for moving coefficients: c_1=Q^(-10) is nonzero but produces a norm saving relative to|b0| alone. The valid no-saving conclusion is relative to|b0| ||c||_2, or for coefficients of nonvanishing normalized size. The displayed formulas and scale-invariant rank bound remain correct.

A useful explicit companion bound, without any cancellation assumption, is

    ||[M_m,P]||_op >= sqrt(2(phi-1)/Q) ||c||_2,

because rank<=Q and HS<=sqrt(Q) op. The full carrier multiplies this by|b0|. Thus an l2-normalized stencil has order-one operator cost even with parameter-dependent phases. Conversely a particular source can lie in a small-defect subspace; a large HS norm alone says nothing about its signed pairing. Simultaneously conjugating multiplier and shifts preserves the calculation. Gauging only the coefficient while retaining the old source/observer changes the problem. Multiplicative translation has an exact twisted relation m(uh)=m(u)m(h), which holds for every scalar multiple and gives no amplitude estimate.

The full H return remains the source contract: rooted marks u_i(P)/sqrt(q_P) once, masses Omega_i=sum|u_i(P)|^2/q_P, raw target

    Z^epsilon G0 K0 [N+L+(NL)^(2/3)] sqrt(Omega1 Omega2) P_orig.

Apply the outside N^(-1)G0^(-2) ONCE. All original masks, zeros, orientations, coefficients, both heights, tails and other branches remain due. The local multiplier obstruction pays none of the .004 full-H deficit. Its record increment is the native spectrum/stencil bill, not a full-source estimate.

## 3. Pole-centered and quotient-merged renewal norm

Fix any ordinary Dirichlet character chi modulo q with literal natural zeros, a(n)=mu(n)chi(n), a(1)=1. Let M(x)=sum_(n<=x)a(n), psi_chi(y)=sum_(d<=y)Lambda(d)chi(d), and delta=1 for principal chi,0 otherwise. The actual convolution identity (a log)=-a*(Lambda chi) gives

    R(x)=sum_(d<=x)Lambda(d)chi(d)M(x/d)=-sum_(n<=x)a(n)log n,
    M(x)log x=int_1^x M(t)dt/t-R(x).

These are [restricted research revision]/W55 prior credit. For any floor-invariant f and integer N>=2 define

    J_N(f)=sum_(d<=N)Lambda(d)chi(d)f_floor(N/d)
                  -delta int_1^N f_floor(N/u) du.

The continuous density is du, not du/u; its Mellin transform is1/(s-1). The exact original source is R(N)=J_N(M)+delta int_1^N M(N/u)du. The restored term equals N sum_(n<=N)a(n)/n-M(N) and is not discarded.

Equal quotient states coalesce to

    J_N(f)=sum_(1<=m<N)c_m f_m,
    c_m=psi_chi(N/m)-psi_chi(N/(m+1))-delta N/[m(m+1)].

The interval is (N/(m+1),N/m], with its lower atom excluded. At m=N the only discrete atom is d=1, of weight0, and the continuous interval clipped to[1,N] has length0. This explains why m=N is absent. For0<beta<1 and prescribed f_m=0 for m<=Y, the exact weighted independent-state norm is

    C_(beta,Y)(N)=N^(-beta) sum_(Y<m<N)|c_m|m^beta.

Equality follows by independently taking f_m=m^beta conj(c_m)/|c_m| at nonzero c_m.

Set D=floor(min(sqrt(N)/4,N/[4(Y+1)])). For each unramified prime power2<=d<=D, m=floor(N/d)>Y and m>=N/(2d). Its cell contains d and has length<=d^2/(N-d)<=1/8, hence no other integer. These cells are distinct. Consequently c_m=Lambda(d)chi(d)-delta L_m and |c_m|>=Lambda(d)/2. Therefore

    C_(beta,Y)(N)>=2^(-beta-1)
          sum_(2<=d<=D,(d,q)=1)Lambda(d)d^(-beta) >>_(q,beta) D^(1-beta).

The lower density used here is elementary. Each prime valuation of binomial(2n,n) is at most floor(log_p(2n)); hence psi(2n)>=log binomial(2n,n)>=2n log2-log(2n+1). Monotonicity gives psi(D)>>D, and deleting the finitely many q-prime-power rays costs O_q(log D). Multiplying by D^(-beta) suffices. Thus for Y=floor(N^theta),0<=theta<1, even C/log N grows at least as N^((1-beta)min(1/2,1-theta))/log N. This is a lower bound for this merged centered norm, not for J_N(M), R or M. A bounded smooth drift cannot cancel these isolated atoms after decreasing the constant in D.

## 4. Natural-zero increments and a fixed-source strengthening

The strongest immediate objection is that independent quotient states need not be cumulative inputs. The author's B3 successfully addresses that objection at the stated synthetic scope. Write

    Q_q(t)=sum_(n<=t)mu(n)^2 1_((n,q)=1)
          =kappa_q t+O_q(sqrt t),
    kappa_q=zeta(2)^(-1) product_(p|q) p/(p+1)>0.

This follows by mu^2(n)=sum_(e^2|n)mu(e), counting q-unit multiples, and paying all O_q(sqrt t) errors and the square-divisor tail. Fix1/2<beta<1 and0<alpha<(1-beta)/(2-beta). For each unramified prime power d<=N^alpha take m_d=floor(N/d), H_d=floor(m_d^beta/8) and

    B_d(n)=max(0,H_d-|Q_q(n)-Q_q(m_d)|).

The density formula first confines support to n comparable to m_d and then to |n-m_d|=O_q(H_d), uniformly, since sqrt(m_d)=o(H_d). Its increments have modulus at most mu(n)^2 1_((n,q)=1), with exact zero at every natural-zero site. The nearest-center spacing is at least N/[d(d+1)]-1. Relative support width is O_q(N^(beta-1)d^(2-beta))=o(1) uniformly; supports and their increment boundaries are disjoint and stay away from0,N.

Under u->floor(N/u), each support is within o(1) of d, including the floor error O(d^2/N). Thus d is its ONLY integer contact. Every supported n is comparable to m_d, and H_d<=n^beta eventually. Put F_n=sum_d conj(chi(d))B_d(n). Then |F_n|<=n^beta and |F_n-F_(n-1)|<=mu(n)^2 1_((n,q)=1). Every discrete contact contributes exactly Lambda(d)H_d. For nonprincipal chi there is no drift. For principal chi each bump is nonnegative and its entire continuous integral is at most H_d times its o(1) inverse-support width, at most Lambda(d)H_d/2 eventually. Hence

    J_N(F) >= c_(q,beta,alpha) N^(beta+alpha(1-beta)) >0.

Here J_N(F) is real with the chosen phases. All bumps lie above a constant times N^(1-alpha), so any prescribed growing zero-error prefix N^theta with theta<1-alpha survives. Taking alpha smaller handles each fixed theta<1. Additional zeros outside the supports are allowed; neither the actual Mobius signs nor multiplicativity is asserted. The finite helper uses smaller heights H about m^(7/8)/128 at one N; it checks conventions only, and is not evidence for the all-N asymptotic beyond the written proof.

INDEPENDENT STRENGTHENING. For each fixed chi,beta,alpha as above there is ONE infinite synthetic sequence b(n), independent of the evaluation cutoff, such that

    |b(n)|<=mu(n)^2 1_((n,q)=1),
    F(n)=sum_(j<=n)b(j), |F(n)|<=n^beta,
    |J_(N_j)(F)| >= c N_j^(beta+alpha(1-beta))

along an increasing sequence N_j->infinity. One may prescribe any finite initial zero prefix. For principal chi the construction can use real b(n) in{-1,0,1}. This removes the objection that ONLY cutoff-dependent inputs cause the failure, while still making no claim about actual Mobius coefficients.

Proof: use the preceding compact bump family G_j at a sufficiently large N_j, taking N_j so large that its entire support and both increment boundaries lie above the previous support and above N_(j-1). This is possible because its lowest center tends to infinity like N_j^(1-alpha), while its largest center is at most N_j/2+o(N_j). Each G_j vanishes before and after its block and has K_j=J_(N_j)(G_j)>0 with the preceding lower bound. Suppose F_old is the sum of earlier blocks. Choose z_j=J_(N_j)(F_old)/|J_(N_j)(F_old)| when that value is nonzero, and z_j=1 otherwise. Add z_j G_j. By linearity,

    |J_(N_j)(F_old+z_j G_j)|=|J_(N_j)(F_old)|+K_j>=K_j.

Every later support lies above N_j and hence changes no state sampled by J_(N_j). The locally finite sum F=sum_j z_j G_j is therefore a single well-defined cumulative input. Disjoint increment boundaries preserve its magnitude and natural-zero increment bounds. Put b(n)=F(n)-F(n-1); telescoping gives the required cumulative identity. In the principal case induction makes F_old and its J value real, so z_j is+1 or-1 and all increments remain0,+1,-1. This proves the claim without assuming cancellation in the earlier blocks or any prime-distribution estimate.

The fixed-sequence strengthening does NOT retain F(m)=0 for every m<=N_j^theta at infinitely many j with theta>0: that would force F identically zero. The author's cutoff-dependent version retains that separate property. Neither version imposes the actual inverse-convolution law or the prescribed mu(n)chi(n) signs. These qualifications are necessary.

## 5. Complete ordinary return and actual open estimate

The required arithmetic input remains, for every fixed ordinary chi and every epsilon>0, a COMPLETE all-real-x bound

including every prime power and the restored principal term. [restricted research revision]'s exact inverse is

                    -int_2^x R_chi(t)dt/[t(log t)^2], x>=2.

## 8. Separate continuous density envelope and raw lift

At a frozen plain witness dyad m, greedily retain width just below min(v,(1-2m)/(9/2)); the loss is at most one fine slot width. The subset depends on frozen lengths/dyads, not the live row. Use the exact MP bridge, pay the complementary actual slots first, then remove the bin restriction in the positive norm. Division by the fourth-power witness yields

    Pnew(m)=1-2delta m+delta[v-(1-2m)/(9/2)]_+.

Both slopes in m are negative. If the tolerance gives m>1/2, take no slots and use the old max(1,2m) plain bound, paying that tolerance once. Independent profiles cover every derivative pair. Combining this with the accepted inverse moments gives

    U(r)=max(1,(1+5r)/6)-delta r+delta v,
    A(r)=1/6+(5/6)max(1,r+2v,(2r+8v)/3)-delta r,
    P(r)=1-2delta(t-r)+delta[v-(1-2(t-r))/(9/2)]_+.    (R16)

    v<=v0: t=(5-6delta v)/(5-2delta), rb=2t/3;
    v>=v0: t=(115-12delta-84delta v)/(115-54delta),
             rb=[80-12delta-(45+30delta)v]/(115-54delta).

For r<=R, A decreases and P increases, crossing at rb. The full-fit capacity sign is proportional to v0-v in the first case and the partial leftover sign to v-v0 in the second. The twenty exact rational-function identities in the helper certify the algebra; these monotonicity and sign arguments supply the continuum proof.

      << Z^[rho(delta)W+(delta-eta_plus(delta))z+epsilon] H_J,
    0<=z<=W/20, delta in [.68,.70].                    (R18)

It uses the fixed canonical slot family and translate of Section 7. Dyads, fixed labels, conductor padding, greedy overshoot, inverse-amplifier slack and zero buffers use one preallocated loss. ## R42.6. D26's complete omitted-prime product

Set E(s)=L_K^S(s+1,eta). Its coefficients eta(a)/Na and the inverse Möbius coefficients have finite absolute sigma mass for every sigma>0. Removing this factor gives r_p=(1-tD)h_p and the independently checked identity

    r_p-1=(1-t)[tD^2+R(1-(1+t)D)]/((1-D)(1-R)).       (R42.10)

The prime coefficient is0 and the square coefficient is t(1-t)a^2. Every power and original phase remains. For sigma>2/3,

    ||r_p-1||_sigma=O_sigma(Q^-1-2sigma+Q^(3-6sigma)).

The inverse is paid by R42.4 and the E factor. Finite products and their inverses have uniformly bounded coefficient mass. Partial summation over prime ideals gives sum_(Q>P)||r_p-1||_sigma << P^-2sigma+P^(4-6sigma). Crucially, for the complete product use

    ||product_(Q>P)r_p-delta_1||_sigma
      <= product_(Q>P)(1+||r_p-1||_sigma)-1.           (R42.11)

For sufficiently large P this is O of the summed tail, by exp(u)-1=O(u); bounded P is absorbed by a fixed constant. This pays every interaction among omitted primes, not just the one-prime terms. For 2/3<sigma<1 it is O(P^(4-6sigma)).

Let W and W_P have Mellin transforms exp(s^2)h/L and exp(s^2)E(product_(Q<=P)r_p)/L respectively. All valuations at a retained prime are kept. Exactly P_eta(x)=C_S exp(25/36)W(exp(-5/3)x). Applying the full coefficient tail to U, with its inherited beta norm, gives uniformly for X>0, P>=2

    ||W-W_P||_[X,2X] << X^beta P^(4-6beta).            (R42.12)

There is no moving-mask substitution: this estimate holds for each P separately with one constant, so P=max(2,X^theta) can subsequently be chosen for the parent shell. If q=beta-theta(6beta-4)<gamma and the **complete signed** W_P norm is O_epsilon(X^(gamma+epsilon)) on every large dyad, then W, P_eta and U have that exponent and the full return R42.3 applies. Conversely a complete U gamma bound pays W_P uniformly through the coefficient norm at gamma+epsilon>2/3. The target is therefore equivalent in the stated range and remains open.

The scalar cross term is also paid. With R_X=W-W_P,

    ||W||^2=||W_P||^2+2Re<W_P,R_X>+||R_X||^2,
    | ||W||^2-||W_P||^2 |<=2||W_P||||R_X||+||R_X||^2. (R42.13)

Under the proposed moment, this costs X^(gamma+q+epsilon)+X^(2q), below X^(2gamma) after choosing the loss inside the positive margin. No negative cross term is dropped; using only beta to bound W_P would be unnecessarily coarser.

B is a fixed large number chosen after the raw scale/height powers, as in [restricted research revision]. At an actual nonprincipal zero rho of the SAME natural character, the accepted completed contour gives

    D_R(rho)=-1+O(U^(-A)).                              (C4)

It moves `Gamma(z)Y^z L^S(rho+z)C_R(rho+z)` from real part2 to -1/4; the Gamma residue vanishes at the zero and no nonprincipal L-pole occurs. There is no assertion about derivatives at rho. The finite terminal cutoff `Nn<=U^(B+1)` has arbitrarily small power error after every required fixed derivative. Its discarded exponential tail is estimated on the genuine expression, before splitting or extending any pair sum. Raw row and slot powers are fixed before selecting the error order. This repeats the already reviewed input solely to specify the source being reduced.

The new exact observation is

    A_R(n)=0 whenever n!=1 and N(rad n)<=R.             (C5)

Only squarefree divisors contribute to A_R, and they are exactly the divisors of rad n. Under the displayed condition every such divisor is inside the constant part of V. Their full Möbius sum is zero. Repeated prime powers do not evade this cancellation. This step requires the *complete signed divisor sum*: cutting its d-range into dyads before merging does not preserve (C5).

After merging all equal products `nP=l` WITH their signs,

    F_u(s):=D_R(s)Q_u=sum_l b_l(s) psi_u(l),
    b_l(s)=U^(-v/2) sum_(nP=l, Nn>R)
      A_R(n)nu(n)(Nn)^(-s) exp(-Nn/Y) alpha(P).         (C6)

Every extra frozen column hole is still present. Natural row zeros are in psi_u, including at shared n/P primes. P need not be coprime to n. The original pools are disjoint only from one another. The coefficient is independent of the live row.

For any required finite derivative, divisor counting gives, uniformly on a compact interval `sigma>1/2`,

    |partial b_l(s)| << H_J U^((sigma-1/2)v+epsilon)
                             (Nl)^(-sigma),
    b_l=0 unless Nl>=c0 U^(t+v) AND N(rad l)>R.        (C7)

The first support condition uses the original slot annuli. The second follows from (C5) and `rad n|rad l`. Coefficient multiplicities are divisor-many; no slot label count is paid twice. Norm-power derivatives in s contribute powers of log Nn, and fixed profile/slot-height derivatives have their prescribed seminorms. Since the terminal scale is fixed polynomial, divisor and logarithm losses can be chosen before the final U threshold to give the requested epsilon. For infinite majorants one first lowers sigma by an arbitrarily small fixed amount; `6sigma>1` and all subsequent series remain uniformly convergent.

## 4. Dilation, flux and observation costs

If A=alpha P U Q where U is unitary and P,Q contractions, alpha>=||A|| follows directly. For a contraction C the Halmos dilation

    U_C=[[C,(I-CC*)^{1/2}],[(I-C*C)^{1/2},-C*]]

is unitary, so alpha=||A|| is achievable for a single finite operator after normalization. This is standard, independently checked against [Robinson, Theorems 1-2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1803.09329). It removes no arithmetic norm. Repeated compression must retain the returning defect: for selfadjoint C, U_C^2=I while C^2=I-(I-C^2). Thus compression of the second power is not the square of the first compression. The author's scalar matrix residual bound and complete-mask Frobenius alternative are correct when all defect and boundary terms remain included.

For S11, diagonal sign gauge relates T to the unsigned disjointness gate [[1,1],[1,0]], so their singular values agree. This refutes an automatic local singular-radius improvement, not cancellation after arithmetic boundary contraction.

For S15 the exact indefinite metric J=[[-2,-1],[-1,2]] satisfies T^T J T=-J; hence T^2 preserves J. The eigenvector (phi,-1), phi=(1+sqrt(5))/2, has zero J-flux and expands by phi under T. Conserved indefinite flux alone cannot bound its positive coordinate observation. This is an actual local-gate counterexample to the stated inference, not a theorem that every indefinite arithmetic construction fails.

For S21 a finite selfadjoint K has unitary V=(K-iI)(K+iI)^{-1}, but

    (I-V)^{-1}=(I-iK)/2,
    ||(I-V)^{-1}||=sqrt(1+||K||^2)/2.

Thus the observation inverse retains growth. For the general complex A_chi above, the selfadjoint hypothesis is absent. No dissipativity theorem or continuation is licensed merely by writing a Cayley expression.

statement:
## A07. Source shell weights, cube damping, and diagonal calibration

**PROVED relative to the inherited shell identities; the full-span obstruction requires a nonzero comparison period.** Sources: BB R09; [restricted research revision] (AC5)–(AC9). The arbitrary-diagonal calibration in part 2 is new in this integration.

At a good prime \(p\) of norm \(Q\), the orthogonal cube shells satisfy
\[
 \|v_j\|^2=(1-Q^{-2})Q^{-2j}\|u\|^2,\qquad
 P_s(v_j)=x_p(s)^jP_s(v_0),\quad
 x_p(s)=\xi_{\rm ang}(p)Q^{1-3s}.
 \tag{A07.1}
\]
These are source probability norms, not norms of the actual bilinear currents.

### 1. Power weights do not repair whole-span continuity near the center

Give shell \(j\) the additional squared-norm weight \(Q^{2rj}\). The exact squared Riesz norm on its finite span is
\[
 \frac{|P_s(v_0)|^2}{(1-Q^{-2})\|u\|^2}
 \sum_{j=0}^JQ^{(4-6\sigma-2r)j},\qquad \sigma=\Re s.
 \tag{A07.2}
\]
This follows by summing squared functional values divided by squared orthogonal basis norms. At a nonzero base period, local boundedness requires \(r>2-3\sigma\). The original source has weighted norm ratio
\[
 \frac{\|u\|_r^2}{\|u\|^2}
 =\frac{1-Q^{-2}}{1-Q^{-2+2r}}.
 \tag{A07.3}
\]
Its all-prime product is finite and nonzero precisely for \(r<1/2\); for \(r\ge1\), even a single-prime norm diverges. For \(0\le r<1\), this follows by comparing the positive logarithm with \(Q^{-2+2r}\); for \(r<0\), both corrections are summable.

Where (A07.2) converges, its relative factor compared with the unweighted full-source period ratio is
\[
 \kappa_{p,r}(s)=
 \frac{|1-x_p(s)|^2}
 {(1-Q^{-2})(1-Q^{4-6\sigma-2r})}. \tag{A07.4}
\]
For \(\sigma>2/3\), the numerator product is absolutely convergent; the positive denominator requires \(r>5/2-3\sigma\).

For the near-central range \(\sigma=1/2+e\), \(0<e<1/6\), suppose \(r<1/2\) so the source remains present. Either the single-prime series already diverges, or
\[
 p_*=6\sigma+2r-4>0,\qquad p_*<6e<3\sigma-1,\qquad p_*<1.
\]
The logarithm of the positive denominator in (A07.4) contributes at least \(Q^{-p_*}\), while the numerator logarithm is \(O(Q^{-(3\sigma-1)})\). Hence, for every sufficiently large good prime,
\(\log\kappa_{p,r}\ge Q^{-p_*}/2\). Its all-prime sum diverges. Under the stipulated nonzero full-source comparison, no such power-weight norm both contains the original source and bounds the continued functional on its entire joint-shell span.

This does not obstruct a restricted estimate for one squarefree vector, a graph norm of the actual current map, or a different tensor reference with independently verified arithmetic.

### 2. Every positive diagonal renorm has an exact calibration cost

On a finite shell span assign arbitrary positive squared norms \(a_j\), and put \(u_J=\sum_{j=0}^Jv_j\). Cauchy–Schwarz gives
\[
 \|u_J\|_a^2\|P_s\|_{a,*}^2
 =\left(\sum_ja_j\right)\left(\sum_j\frac{|P_s(v_j)|^2}{a_j}\right)
 \ge\left(\sum_j|P_s(v_j)|\right)^2
 =|P_s(v_0)|^2\left(\sum_{j=0}^J|x_p|^j\right)^2.
 \tag{A07.5}
\]
Equality holds when \(a_j\) is proportional to \(|P_s(v_j)|\). If the source and a bounded compatible functional exist in the limiting norm, \(|x_p|<1\) and the known geometric period identity imply
\[
 \frac{\|u\|_a^2\|P_s\|_{a,*}^2}{|P_s(u)|^2}
 \ge\frac{|1-x_p|^2}{(1-|x_p|)^2}. \tag{A07.6}
\]
The factors multiply over finite tensor products of primes.

This is a proved necessary test for arbitrary positive diagonal weights, broader than part 1's power weights. It is not a general infinite-product obstruction: a positive real \(x_p\) gives factor one, and divergence of the infinite phase-sensitive product would need additional angular information. A non-diagonal current norm is outside this test.

### 3. Cube damping shifts the completion but proves no new norm bound

For \(\Re\nu\ge0\), let \(u_\nu=\sum_{j\ge0}Q^{-\nu j}v_j\). Orthogonality and the geometric period series give
\[
 \frac{\|u_\nu\|^2}{\|u\|^2}
 =\frac{1-Q^{-2}}{1-Q^{-2-2\Re\nu}},\qquad
 (1-Q^{-\nu}x_p)P_s(u_\nu)=(1-x_p)P_s(u).
 \tag{A07.7}
\]
The cross-multiplied identity includes zero base periods and is first justified in absolute convergence or on finite prime products with the inherited continuation. Formally weighting the entire cube label by \(q_B^{-\nu}\) changes the fixed completion to
\(L^S(3s-1+\nu,\xi_{\rm ang})D_h(s)\).
A nonzero convergent source-norm product does not continue the infinite period or current map. T01 already removes fixed-factor division; a useful damping argument must improve a calibrated current or restricted-test estimate.
title: A07. Source shell weights, cube damping, and diagonal calibration

## G131. Complementary divisors and the actual Poisson boundary

Use ideal norms and the literal cutoff V, equal to one on [0,1] and zero
on [2,infinity). Let `R=U^(4/3)` and

    A_R(n)=sum_(d|n) mu(d)V(Nd/R).

For every nonunit n, the complete divisor sum of mu is zero, so exactly

    A_R(n)=-sum_(dm=n) mu(d)[1-V(Nd/R)]
          =-sum_(m|n) mu(n/m)[1-V(Nn/(Nm R))].             (1)

The unit is excluded: its left side is one and complementary sum zero.
Nonzero summands have `Nd>R`; under `Nn<=C L`, therefore `Nm<C L/R`.
There is no coprimality restriction. Complete multiplicativity of the
natural character `phi_u` preserves (1), including shared primes and
all natural zeros. If every proper divisor has norm at most R, the
original sum gives `A_R(n)=mu(n)[V(Nn/R)-1]`.

On good squarefree n only, the source Gauss identities give

    gamma_1 gamma_2=mu alpha G,  a0=conj(alpha)gamma_2,
    |gamma_2|=1,
    A_R(n)gamma_1(n)=G(n)conj(a0(n))mu(n)A_R(n),
    mu(n)A_R(n)=-sum_(m|n)mu(m)[1-V(Nn/(Nm R))].         (2)

Here G is the fixed ray function. The last formula fails at prime squares:
the formal n=4,R=2 example has left side zero and right side minus one.
Equation (1) still holds. Even on squarefree n, the new amplitude can
equal two when n has three distinct prime factors individually at most R
and pair products at least 2R. Thus it is not the literal coefficient
allowed by B3.6, which permits no further arithmetic coefficient on n.
A divisor bound does not repair that source contract. This obstruction
does not prove a lower bound for the actual signed sum.

For coprime good squarefree nonunit l,l', without slots or a moving row
selector, the clean sixth-free row Poisson specialization is

    U/sqrt(Nl Nl') sum_b mu(b)/(Nb)^6 1_((b,ll')=1) R(l,l')
      *sum_h Gcal(l,h)conj(Gcal(l',-h))
        F(Phi)(U Nh/((Nb)^6 Nl Nl')).                    (3)

The b range is finite, `Nb<=(C_Phi U)^(1/6)`. The CRT factor is the actual
reciprocity sign R(l,l'). The conjugate Fourier factor explains `-h`;
the two Gauss normalizers explain `U/sqrt(Nl Nl')`. The identity
`u=b^6 k` retains all six units in k, without multiplying b by six.
The scalar from b is the displayed natural-zero indicator. Frequency
zero vanishes for these nonprincipal natural characters.

A fixed ray restriction still needs its finite character expansion; a
fixed hole mask needs every `d|rad(E)` with its coefficient, scalar and
rescaled kernel; omitted fixed-inducing rows need their actual subtraction.
Shared support, arbitrary valuations and original slots require the full
source reconstruction. A zero-bin selector cannot be inserted into (3).
At `Nl,Nl'~L=U^(4/3)`, the first dual length is `L^2/U=U^(5/3)`, so this
first transform alone does not produce a short dual sum.

## 5. Two transforms, joint labels, and low/high estimates

Compare the centered expression with the equal-product rectangle having plain lengths L=M/4 and n1+n2-L. Both original plains exceed L. Keep the whole-product character, profiles, slot coefficients and masks identical. Exact Euler deletion has Z^o(1) mass. Reflect only a comparison second plain longer than M/2; its retained natural scale is at most M/2+xi after combined-conductor accounting and restoration. Lower annuli have summable central weights and upper tails have rapid decay. Every comparison daughter has old budget at most

    M/4+M/2+(9/2)(M/25)+xi=.93M+xi<M.

Use only the old 9/2 moment or the old unrestricted nonprincipal zero-slot moment. This comparison never asks the new local theorem to hold at its .25 plain scale. No row indicator is inserted into the centered Poisson input.

For the first transform let c,d,p,R,E,s0 be the exact source widths and B_c=(3c-5d-R)_+/6, with B_d exchanged. Retain first common labels and the complete signed first projector inside the joint Hilbert direct sum. Required side estimates are

    sum_lambda N_C,lambda << Z^(p+A-c+R+E+B_c+small),
    sum_lambda N_D,lambda << Z^(p+A-d+R+E+B_d+small).

The outside factor is Z^(M-A-R/2-E). Joint Cauchy gives the exponent

    M+p-(c+d)/2+R/2+(B_c+B_d)/2 <= M.

For per-label branches the old -s0 allowance is retained and the count Z^(p+s0+small) is paid once. The high branch proves the joint side target directly; multiplying it by another label count would invalidate the proof.

The actual main logarithmic radius and main child width are

    Kmain=K0+(d-c)_++6a+omega,
    K0=2A-c-d+R+E-M,
    M'=M-(c-d)_+-6a-omega-g2+t2.

Thus

    (A-c-c2-M')-(A-M)
        =6a+omega-min(c,d)-(c2-g2)-t2 <=6a+omega.

The inner allowance is M'+Delta2 with Delta2=b2-p2+B_c+a>=a. The second projector and its priority allocation, natural coefficients, raw scalars, and clipping remain as in B3.65–B3.69. The error radii remain

    K0+max(d-c-2w+w_o,0)+3a+delta1+reserve.

For low bins, impose the extra keep predicate only on the positive allocated child energies after both transforms. RC identifies these with the literal natural child products. Use the original moving character and unchanged fixed anchor Q_*; do not absorb the former into the latter. Remove a greedy prefix of canonical slots with squared cost (.7+buffer) times removed width until the old 9/2 capacity holds or no slots remain. Only after this payment may the low indicator be dropped. Slot exhaustion uses unrestricted MP0 and adds no residual plain-sum defect. No improved moment is called on any descendant.

Actual minus nominal child width d_* satisfies only d_*<=delta2 and may be negative. For 0<=v<=1,

    d_*+v(F-d_*)_+ <= delta2+v F_+.

Indeed the left side is d_* if F<=d_*, and is (1-v)d_*+vF otherwise; split further according to F's sign. Applying v=7/45 to F<=g+6a+small yields low reserve a/15-7g/45. With (R2) this is at least alpha M/15=M/6000000. If the raw defect is nonpositive, the amplification still creates a 6a defect; its cost is 14a/15, leaving a/15. There is no zero-defect exemption from this cost.

For high bins delta in [.7,.75], put rho=1-10delta/[3(5-2delta)]. The actual signed row is w=u0 e F_c G_c V h', retaining the unit u0. Prime residues are 1+t_p on one orientation and 1-t_p on the other. A zero residue leaves its old puncture; it is not the constant-one coefficient. With canceled active radical width R0 and L_c=log_Z NF_c<=5(R-R0), actual frequency support gives

    log_Z Nw <= W+small,
    W=M-R-(c-d)_++L_c-6a.

Every genuine second common prime and the first projector divides w. The missing first radical has width at most p-R-E+R0. At fixed w and missing radical, the remaining labels are divisor-many for arbitrary valuations, by the Rankin product estimate in SignedReconstruction; a finite residue table would not prove this. The second residual projector need not divide w. Its dyadic count is paid by the two exact extraction scalars (B3.69). A possibly zero outside factor stays outside, without adding coprimality to the quotient plain variables.

FixedDictionaryBridge identifies the literal row on all ideals, including zeros, with a fixed ray factor times the complete sextic integer row and its holes. Natural representatives have primitive conductor O_fixed(Nw). The dictionary is a finite union of fixed parent translates; bins are formed within the actual translate, where all allowed presentations are nonprincipal. Whole-character conjugation reflects heights. The upper buffered maximum controls all factors, and a member of this fixed finite list supplies the lower zero witness. No live-label family is mistaken for a fixed dictionary. Sixth-power lifting converges because rho>=2/7>1/6.

The resulting joint count is Z^(rho W+p-R-E+R0+small)(1+T_h)^J. If nominal W is slightly negative, supported padding costs its allocated small loss; a negative supported range is empty. A nonempty bounded range is not assigned a count less than one. Exact pointwise/scalar normalization leaves excess

    M(rho-1)+delta A+a(5-6rho)
      +(1-rho)(c-d)_+-delta c-(1+rho)R-E-B_c+rho L_c+R0
      +g2-t2-(1+delta)b2+small.

The middle line is at most (4rho-1-delta)p-E-B_c<=-79p/270-E-B_c. Here min(c,d)>=p>=R, rho+delta>1 and 5rho>1 give the required signs. The last line is at most -delta b2-t2. Consequently only

    H_j(delta)=1-rho-delta A_j-(a_j/M)(5-6rho)

remains to be paid. Its derivative is 50(1-6a_j/M)/[3(5-2delta)^2]-A_j. The coarse simultaneous bound is 451778249/1562198400>0. At delta=.7 every interior cell has the same reserve

    H_j(.7)=1/27000-(91/41)e-(26/9)alpha

statement:
## 4. Completed restricted theorem: all large common factors, full norm

**Theorem LG.** Let X>=2 and G>=1 be real. Let |a_1(d)|,|a_2(e)|<=1 and |b(l)|<=B_0, with B_0 fixed. For EACH X and G choose any complex tuple weights theta_(X,G)(d,e,l), of modulus<=1, before real x varies. They may contain arbitrary strict or closed arithmetic cutoffs, natural zeros, independent coefficient phases and n-dependent support; they must be independent of live x. Define the literal ordered coefficient and full damped source

 v_G(n)=sum_(d e l=n, gcd(d,e)>G) a_1(d)a_2(e)b(l)theta_(X,G)(d,e,l),
 B_G(x)=sum_(n>=1)v_G(n)exp(-n/x^(3/2)-i(n/x)^6).

For every epsilon>0,

 ||B_G||_(L^2([X,2X],dx/x))
   <<_(epsilon,B_0) X^epsilon [X/G+X^(3/4)/sqrt(G)].             (LG1)

The same bound holds in L1. Constants are independent of G, all sequences and all frozen masks within these bounds. In particular there is no need for a polynomial upper cap on G. The physical applications below use G=X^(1-gamma). Absolute local convergence follows from the divisor bound and the damping. The theorem does not assert a pointwise bound at this strength.

### 4.1 Full collision and local multiplicity, with endpoints

Let r_G(n)=#{r>G:r^2|n}. Its first moment is <=2Y/G. The exact second-moment identity is

 sum_(n<=Y)r_G(n)^2
  =sum_(r,s>G)floor(Y/lcm(r,s)^2) <=16Y/G, Y>=1.               (LG2)

Every sum on the left and the nonzero part on the right is finite. In the inequality write r=g u,s=g v,(u,v)=1. The condition is g>G/min(u,v). For every t>0, sum_(g>t)g^(-2)<=2/t. Thus the right side is at most (2Y/G)sum_(u,v>=1)min(u,v)/(u^2v^2). The last series is <=2sum_u u^(-1)sum_(v>=u)v^(-2)<=4sum_u u^(-2)<8. This proves the stated constant16 without discarding collisions. Nonintegral Y/G, r=s and repeated/shared prime powers are included. Equality r=G, if integral, remains in the good source.

For fixed c,C>0, an interval I subset[cN,CN] of length h satisfies

 sum_(n in I)r_G(n) <<_(c,C) h/G+E_N,
 E_N=min(N^(1/3),N/G^2),                                (LG3)

whenever 1<=G<=sqrt(CN). If G>sqrt(CN) the sum is zero. To verify the inherited W24 count: if G<=N^(1/3), sum G<r<=N^(1/3) with count<=h/r^2+1. For larger r, reverse the summation to l=n/r^2<=CN^(1/3). The real root interval for each l has length O(h/(sqrt(N)sqrt(l))); length plus one gives O(h/N^(1/3)+N^(1/3)). If G>N^(1/3), reverse all roots and use l<=CN/G^2, giving O(h/G+N/G^2). This is a PAIR count (r,l), with multiplicities. Closed endpoints and h<1 are paid by the length-plus-one terms; if the block is nonempty N/G^2>=1/C, so no unpriced isolated endpoint remains. The global mass is O(N/G), by (LG2)'s first-moment version.

Writing d=r u,e=r v with r the EXACT gcd assigns every original ordered tuple once. At a given r^2|n, its remaining number of factorizations is at most d_3(n/r^2). Hence for every fixed eta>0

 |v_G(n)| <= B_0 d_3(n)r_G(n) <<_(eta,B_0) n^eta r_G(n),
 sum_(n<=Y)|v_G(n)| << Y^(1+eta)/G,
 sum_(n<=Y)|v_G(n)|^2 << Y^(1+2eta)/G.                    (LG4)

No coprimality was inserted between r,u,v,l beyond the defining (u,v)=1, and this last condition was only dropped in a POSITIVE upper bound. All tuple masks remain literal; the majorant counts every possible root, not only its largest or prime root. This is coefficient domination, not norm monotonicity under a signed subset.

### 4.2 Whole nonlinear kernel and the low/high split

Choose one nonnegative smooth w supported in[1/2,3], w>=1 on[1,2]. The weighted shell kernel K_X(n,m)=integral w(x/X)f_x(n)conj(f_x(m))dx/x obeys

 |K_X(n,m)| << exp(-c(n+m)/X^(3/2))
                    min(1,(X^6/|n^6-m^6|)^2),           (LG5)

with the minimum set to1 on the exact diagonal. Substitute x=Xu and integrate by parts twice in the nonstationary phase -(n^6-m^6)/(X^6u^6). Its derivative has no zero on the fixed support. Derivatives of the damping cost a fixed polynomial in (n+m)/X^(3/2), absorbed into a slightly weaker exponential. Compactly supported w removes boundary terms. This proves (LG5) on the full shell, not a sampled x grid.

Split B_G=B_lo+B_hi at the CLOSED cutoff n<=X. By (LG4), |B_lo(x)|<<X^(1+eta)/G throughout the support of w. All low/high interactions are paid by the norm triangle inequality, so no unconditional small scalar mixed term is asserted. It remains to bound the entire norm of B_hi, n>X. Expansion is justified first for finite truncations and then by local absolute convergence.

Partition every ordered upper pair into comparable pairs (ratio between1/2 and2) and far pairs. A bounded-overlap dyadic covering puts every comparable pair in [N/2,4N]^2 for some N>=cX. Let H=X^6/N^5. On this block |n^6-m^6| is bounded below by a fixed multiple of N^5|n-m|. The kernel is bounded by exp(-cN/X^(3/2))min(1,(H/|n-m|)^2), including its diagonal.

Using (LG3), the weighted r_G mass about ANY integer center n is O(H/G+E_N): divide distances into |m-n|<=H and successive doubling rings. For H>=1, local count gives a geometric sum H/G+E_N. For H<1, use |m-n|<=H for the possible diagonal and doubling rings beginning at H; empty subunit rings contribute nothing, and the same upper bound follows (or begin off-diagonal rings at1 with weight O(H^2)). Intersecting a ring interval with [N/2,4N] costs at most two intervals with the same fixed constants. Multiplying by the complete block mass O(N/G) gives the positive pair majorant

 P_N << exp(-cN/X^(3/2)) N^(2eta)
                      [X^6/(G^2 N^4)+(N/G)E_N].        (LG6)

Separately, the unweighted integer-kernel row sum is O(1+H): the off-diagonal sum over nonzero integer distances is O(H) for H>=1 and O(H^2)<=O(H) for H<1. Apply 2|v_G(n)v_G(m)|<=|v_G(n)|^2+|v_G(m)|^2 and (LG4) on [N/2,4N]. This bounds THE SAME positive pair majorant by

 P_N << exp(-cN/X^(3/2)) N^(2eta)(N/G)(1+H).             (LG7)

The global l2 density alone would leave the larger HN/G cost near N~X. It is (LG6), retaining the local square-divisor count, that closes this loss. Taking the minimum of the two valid bounds for the same complete block, and using min(A+B,C+D)<=A+C+min(B,D), gives

 P_N << exp(-cN/X^(3/2)) N^(2eta)
       [X^6/(G^2 N^4)+(N/G)(1+min(N^(1/3),H))].        (LG8)

Constants/exponentials are first made common. Both ordered orientations, exact coincidences, all distinct roots giving the same output, and all masks were included before taking this minimum.

Sum (LG8) over dyadic N>=cX. The first term is O(X^(2+2eta)/G^2). Actual damping pays the isolated1 term by O(X^(3/2+3eta)/G). The remaining sum is bounded without damping by

 (1/G)sum_(N dyadic>=cX)N^(1+2eta)min(N^(1/3),X^6/N^5)
       <<_eta X^(3/2+9eta/4)/G, 0<eta<1.               (LG9)

Indeed its increasing term N^(4/3+2eta) and decreasing term X^6N^(-4+2eta) meet at N=X^(9/8). Their geometric tails converge. This argument uses every high block, not only an average block or a low-frequency range. Blocks with G>sqrt(4N) are empty and may be kept as zero.

For far pairs take n~N, X<m<n/2, and include the reverse orientation. The gap is bounded below by a constant times N^6. The absolute coefficient shell and cumulative masses from (LG4) are each O(N^(1+eta)/G). Thus their complete total is

 <<sum_(N dyadic>=cX) X^12 N^(-12) N^(2+2eta)/G^2
 << X^(2+2eta)/G^2.                                    (LG10)

Damping can only improve this bound. There is no omitted large/small cross pair: both entries here belong to B_hi; B_lo/B_hi were paid earlier by triangle. Combining (LG8)-(LG10), the low bound and norm triangle gives

 ||B_G||_2^2 <<_(eta,B_0) X^(2+2eta)/G^2+X^(3/2+3eta)/G.

Choose eta>0 after the requested epsilon, for example eta=min(epsilon/4,1/4), to prove (LG1). L1 follows by Cauchy-Schwarz on logarithmic measure log2. This completes the theorem uniformly for every G>=1 and every stated frozen mask.

### 4.3 What the strongest uniform obstruction actually says

The first term X/G cannot be improved in this broad bounded-mask class by cancellation of the kernel alone. Choose a_1=a_2=b=1 and retain just d=e=r with G<r<=2G and r^2 l<=X/2. For 1<=G<=c sqrt(X), with a sufficiently small fixed c, there are >>X/G such ordered triples. Their phases for every x in[X,2X] lie between -1/64 and0; damping is bounded below. Therefore ||B_G||_1,||B_G||_2 >>X/G. This is an example in the explicitly quantified comparison class, not in the actual signed Liouville core. It establishes sharpness of this general method's first term and no impossibility theorem for the actual signs. In particular it does not rule out the endpoint exponent, an epsilon-loss bound, or any structured arithmetic improvement after restriction.
title: 4. Completed restricted theorem: all large common factors, full norm

statement:
### Exact row projection and mask coefficient

Restore the original `k=0` row, use one common **total-column** Poisson period, and retain nonzero physical frequencies whose good valuations are multiples of three. Denote this linear operation by `P_cub`. Its fixed unit/bad-prime cube-residual states are `sigma_*`. The original row and transformed zero frequency are different; transformed zero is excluded here.

For a column `cB³` with `c` squarefree, the original internal Type I coefficient is
\[
\mathcal J[I]_k(cB^3)=q_B\xi(B)\overline{\mathfrak G(c)}\vartheta_c(k)
\sum_{t\mid B}q_t^{-1/2}\overline{\xi(t)}I_Y(ct^3)1_{(t,k)=1}.
\]
Write
\[
\mathcal A_Y(c,B)=\sum_{t\mid B}q_t^{-1/2}\overline{\xi(t)}I_Y(ct^3)
\prod_{p\mid t,\,p\nmid c}(1-Q_p^{-1}).
\tag{T05.1}
\]
The density applies only outside the core. At a prime in `c`, the primitive row character already imposes its nonunit zero.

For coprime total columns `cB³,eE³`, retain precisely
\[
(c,e)=(c,E)=(e,B)=(B,E)=1.
\]
Let `M0=ce`, and `R0=rad(BE)` with the primes of `M0` removed. The reduced common period is `M0R0`. A frequency `h` on that period represents physical frequency
\[
u=(B^3E^3/R_0)h.
\]
At primes of `M0`, the transform is zero unless `h` is a unit. At primes of `R0`, the cube condition forces `v_p(h)=1 mod 3`. At other good primes it forces `v_p(h)=0 mod 3`. Consequently surviving reduced frequencies are exactly
\[
h=\sigma_*R_0z^3,\qquad(z,M_0)=1.
\]
For an outside-prime mask `r`, CP (23)'s Fourier factor is then
\[
\sum_{s\mid r}\mu(s)q_{R_0/s}1_{R_0/s\mid h}
=q_{R_0}\prod_{p\mid r}(1-Q_p^{-1}).
\]
The two masks are disjoint by total-column coprimality and split into (T05.1). The factor `q_R0` cancels the Poisson denominator, and the primitive phase becomes the fixed ray phase `chi_sigma_*(c) conjugate(chi_sigma_*(e))`, with the restriction `(ce,z)=1` retained. Thus the exact projected form is
\[
\begin{aligned}
P_{\rm cub}\mathfrak Q[I,I]
={K\over D^2}\sum_{\sigma_*}\sum_{(B,E)=1}
&\xi(B)\overline{\xi(E)}q_B^4q_E^4
\sum_{z\ne0}\Phi\!\left({Kq_B^3q_E^3q_{\sigma_*}q_z^3\over D^2}\right)\\
\times\sum_{\substack{c,e\ {\rm sf},\,(c,e)=1\\(c,EzS)=(e,BzS)=1}}
&\chi_{\sigma_*}(c)\overline{\chi_{\sigma_*}(e)}\sqrt{q_cq_e}
\mathcal A_Y(c,B)\overline{\mathcal A_Y(e,E)}
\overline{W_0(q_cq_B^3/D)}W_0(q_eq_E^3/D).
\end{aligned}
\tag{T05.2}
\]
For `M0=1`, the transform is only a periodic mask; the same Fourier identity holds directly and includes pure-cube columns.

The restored original row causes no remainder ambiguity: its completed coefficient is zero unless `c=1`, and then `C_0(B³)=q_B xi(B)` while `J[I]_0(B³)=-q_B xi(B)`. At `k=0` only internal `t=1` survives and `I_Y(1)=-1`. Hence C–C and I–I have identical original-zero terms.

statement:
### A compact sensor needs no positive-height numerator cover

The uniform critic audit S10 uses one fixed h>0 and M_chi(x)=0 for x<1:

    S_h(x)=int_0^h M_chi(x exp(-u))du
          =sum_(n<=x)mu(n)chi(n) min(h,log(x/n)).

The endpoints, unit and natural zeros remain. Absolute integration gives

    int_1^infinity S_h(x)x^(-s)dx/x
      =(1-exp(-hs))/(s^2 L(s,chi)), Re s>1.                (12)

If the COMPLETE S_h is O_(chi,epsilon)(x^(gamma+epsilon)) for every
epsilon>0 and all sufficiently large x, for one common0<gamma<1, the
left side is holomorphic on Re s>gamma. The factor(1-exp(-hs))/s^2 is
nonzero there: its nontrivial zeros have Re s=0, and s=0 is outside.
This gives the full ordinary-character all-height pole return, with the
principal-pole convention above. The arithmetic sensor estimate is open.

Stable reconstruction is a different requirement. On a weighted log L2
line sigma>0 the convolution multiplier K_h(s)=(1-exp(-hs))/s satisfies

    (1-exp(-h sigma))/|sigma+it| <= |K_h(sigma+it)|
      <=(1+exp(-h sigma))/|sigma+it|.

For S(y)=S_h(e^y), S'(y)=M_chi(e^y)-M_chi(e^(y-h)) almost everywhere.
The causal difference inverse costs at most(1-exp(-h sigma))^(-1) on
weighted L2, but its input is the derivative: if f=e^(-sigma y)S,
that input is f'+sigma f. Endpoints can be interpreted distributionally.
The derivative cost has not disappeared.

A finite bank of compact L1 kernels has multipliers tending to zero at
large heights on each such line, by step-function approximation and the
Fourier integral of an interval. Hence no fixed finite weighted sum of
squared multipliers has a positive global lower frame bound on unrestricted
weighted L2. This does not refute the one-way pole bridge, a bound on the
actual arithmetic source, atoms/derivatives, or a moving bank with paid
costs. W22/G109 retain the general smoothing/bank ancestry.
title: A compact sensor needs no positive-height numerator cover

statement:
## 3. D26: pay unrevealed correction primes after removing a known L-factor

### D26.1 Exact local repair

The naive tail of h_p-1 contains the prime coefficient tD and costs P^-sigma. Remove it by the exact, absolutely bounded factor

    E(s)=L_K^S(s+1,eta),
    H_eta(s)=C_S E(s) Rcal(s),
    r_p(s)=(1-tD) h_p(s).                               (3.1)

This E is not assumed small: its coefficient mass at sigma is sum_a Na^(-1-sigma), and its inverse has the same positive majorant. Both are finite for sigma>0. Every power and phase remains in

    r_p-1=(1-t)[tD^2+R(1-(1+t)D)]/[(1-D)(1-R)].          (3.2)

In particular the coefficient at p is zero, and that at p^2 is t(1-t)a^2. The original p^6 contribution remains; it is not converted to an arbitrary Gaussian kernel error.

For sigma>2/3,

    ||r_p-1||_sigma
       <= (1-t)[t d^2+r(1+(1+t)d)]/[(1-d)(1-r)]
       = O_sigma(Q^(-1-2sigma)+Q^(3-6sigma)).             (3.3)

The inverse r_p^-1=h_p^-1/(1-tD) has a corresponding summable local bound; hence finite products and their inverses have coefficient norms bounded uniformly in their prime cutoff. This follows either from the direct product or from (2.6) and the E factor. No randomness, conditional independence or martingale drift estimate is used.

Let Rcal_<=P and Rcal_>P be the literal products over Q<=P and Q>P, respectively. ALL valuations at retained primes are included. By ideal counting and partial summation,

    sum_(Q>P) ||r_p-1||_sigma
       <<_sigma P^(-2sigma)+P^(4-6sigma).

For 2/3<sigma<1 the second term dominates, and the product estimate yields

    ||r_>P-delta_1||_sigma <<_sigma P^(4-6sigma).          (3.4)

For bounded P enlarge the fixed constant. For large P use product(1+b_p)-1<=exp(sum b_p)-1. All omitted interactions among large primes are included in that product; (3.4) is not a sum retaining only one missing prime.

### D26.2 Complete field approximation and cross terms

Let W_P be the fixed field at a specified prime cutoff P whose Mellin transform is

    Mellin(W_P)(s)=exp(s^2) E(s) Rcal_<=P(s)/L_K^S(s,eta). (3.5)

The fully corrected field W has the same transform with Rcal in place of Rcal_<=P. By (2.8), P_eta is exactly C_S exp(25/36) times W at the fixed dilation exp(-5/3). Thus no physical scale normalizer is lost.

Assume the inherited complete M_eta,2 bound ||M_eta,2||_beta<infinity for one fixed 2/3<beta<1. This is the source-level calibrated bound furnished by the accepted fixed-family zero-free premise with a positive buffer; it is not a new exponent. The coefficient convolution norm, uniform finite-product mass and (3.4) give

    ||W-W_P||_[X,2X] << X^beta P^(4-6beta).               (3.6)

This holds for every X>0 and P>=2 with one constant for fixed eta,S,beta. It therefore remains valid at P_X=X^theta. Define q=beta-theta(6beta-4). Then the complete error is O(X^q).

If an actual source estimate proves

    ||W_(X^theta)||_[X,2X] <<_epsilon X^(gamma+epsilon)    (OPEN-W42)

for every large dyadic X, and q<gamma, (3.6) gives W, then P_eta and M_eta,2, the same gamma exponent. D02 supplies the fixed-family zero-exclusion return. Conversely a complete gamma bound for M gives OPEN-W42 because the weighted norms of E Rcal_<=P are uniformly bounded at each gamma+epsilon>2/3. In the stated range this remains an equivalent arithmetic target, not a weaker exponent theorem.

The full mixed energy is explicitly retained. For R_X=W-W_P,

    ||W||^2=||W_P||^2+2 Re<W_P,R_X>+||R_X||^2,
    | ||W||^2-||W_P||^2 |
       <=2 ||W_P|| ||R_X||+||R_X||^2.                  (3.7)

Under OPEN-W42 the right side is O(X^(gamma+q+epsilon)+X^(2q)); both terms are below the target 2gamma with a positive buffer. Using only the inherited beta bound would instead pay beta+q, which is coarser and is not needed for the norm implication. No negative cross term is dropped and no different detector savings are added.

### D26.3 Quantitative returns and first useful next estimate

Use beta=8749/10000=.8749, strictly above the accepted boundary .874864, so 6beta-4=6247/5000. Any strict theta larger than the displayed threshold pays the full tail below gamma:

| Desired conditional c | gamma=1-c | threshold theta>(beta-gamma)/(6beta-4) |
|---|---:|---:|
| current c5, as a comparison | 54679/62500 | 9/312350 |
| near gain .1252 | 2187/2500 | 1/12494 |
| 1/6 | 5/6 | 1247/37482 |
| 1/4 | 3/4 | 1249/12494 |
| formal absolute-boundary target 1/3 | 2/3 | 1/6, with every-epsilon norm convention |

The c5 row is not a proof of an additional gain; the other rows are conditional targets. Constants depend on the fixed positive gaps. A convenient **first-gain test** is theta=1/10000, gamma=2187/2500. Then q=43738753/50000000=.87477506 and gamma-q=1247/50000000=.00002494. Proving the full original-sign OPEN-W42 with this P_X would yield c=.1252. No such bound is proved here.

The reduced coefficient family is completely constructive: start with mu_K*eta, convolve with eta(a)/Na (the actual E factor), then multiply the finite set of exact r_p local series (3.2), retaining all valuations and original S zeros. A physical Gaussian truncation can subsequently be paid from any absolute coefficient line, but no finite cap is required for (3.5)--(3.7). It must not be confused with G13's two-Möbius/alternating-restoration list.

The next subsection gives a second, more accurate approximation by paying another explicit global factor. The two approximants have different coefficient lists; neither is substituted into the other's source estimate.

### D26.4 Sixth-power extraction and the stronger paid target

Keep the source's b(p) and R=b(p)Q^(3-6s) exactly, and define

    V6(s)=product_(p notin S)(1-R)^-1,
    h(s)=E(s) V6(s) Rhat(s),
    rhat_p=(1-R)(1-tD)h_p.

This is a defined Euler series, not an appeal to an unproved estimate for an angular character. Its coefficients are b(a)(Na)^3 supported at the sixth-power ideals a^6, where b is the completely multiplicative extension of the specified prime values. Thus the absolute coefficient mass of V6 at sigma is sum_a Na^(3-6sigma), finite for sigma>2/3. Its inverse is supported at a^6 with coefficients mu_K(a)b(a)(Na)^3 and has the same positive majorant. These constants are paid in the norm transfer.

The exact local identity is

    rhat_p-1 = [t(1-t)D^2-tR+t^2DR]/(1-D).               (3.8)

For sigma>1/2 its weighted coefficient norm is

    ||rhat_p-1||_sigma
      <= [t(1-t)d^2+t r+t^2 d r]/(1-d)
      = O_sigma(Q^(-1-2sigma)+Q^(2-6sigma)).             (3.9)

The inverse obeys the same large-Q order. Explicitly, writing N=1-(1-t)D-tR,

    rhat_p^-1=(1-D)/[(1-tD)N],
    ||rhat_p^-1-1||_sigma
      <= [t(1-t)d^2+t r+t^2 d r]
         /[(1-t d)(1-(1-t)d-t r)].                     (3.10)

Here r<1, and (1-t)d+t r<(1-t)Q^-1/2+t<1. All local inverses are legitimate. The sums of (3.9)--(3.10) converge for sigma>1/2. In particular Rhat and its inverse have finite coefficient norms there. This does **not** lower the full old/new comparison threshold below 2/3: the extracted V6 still has its sixth-power cost.

Let Rhat_<=P and Rhat_>P retain all local powers, as before. The complete omitted product satisfies

    ||rhat_>P-delta_1||_sigma
       <<_sigma P^(-2sigma)+P^(3-6sigma), sigma>1/2.    (3.11)

For beta>3/4 the first term dominates. Define the second approximant by

    Mellin(What_P)(s)=exp(s^2)E(s)V6(s)Rhat_<=P(s)/L_K^S(s,eta).

The full infinite-prime limit is the same W as in (3.5). Every large-prime interaction is still in Rhat_>P; E and V6 are included at every prime. The inherited M_eta,2 beta bound therefore gives, uniformly in P,

    ||W-What_P||_[X,2X] << X^beta P^(-2beta), beta>3/4. (3.12)

Taking P=max(2,X^theta) gives error exponent qhat=beta-2beta*theta. If the actual full signed norm of What_(max(2,X^theta)) is O_epsilon(X^(gamma+epsilon)) for every positive epsilon and every large dyadic X, and qhat<gamma, then (3.12), D02 and the exact cross-energy identity (3.7) give the common zero-exclusion boundary gamma, provided this hypothesis holds for each fixed target as specified after (2.9). This is **OPEN-W42-sixth**. Its converse follows from a complete M_eta,2 gamma bound because E V6 Rhat_<=P has uniformly bounded coefficient mass at every gamma+epsilon>2/3. Hence it is a concretely different arithmetic representation of the same target exponent, not an established easier theorem.

For the same beta=8749/10000, the stronger strict cutoff thresholds are:

| Desired conditional c | gamma | theta>(beta-gamma)/(2beta) |
|---|---:|---:|
| current c5, comparison | 54679/62500 | 9/437450 |
| near gain .1252 | 2187/2500 | 1/17498 |
| 1/6 | 5/6 | 1247/52494 |
| 1/4 | 3/4 | 1249/17498 |
| formal target 1/3 | 2/3 | 6247/52494, every-epsilon convention |

For example theta=1/16000 already suffices for the near target: qhat=69983251/80000000=.8747906375, and gamma-qhat=749/80000000=.0000093625. All inequalities are strict; equality at a displayed threshold is not claimed. No bound for OPEN-W42-sixth has been proved.

The first useful arithmetic task is to estimate this exact What_P coefficient family, or the distinct W_P family from (3.5), including its full signed energy. A successful source-specific bound would transfer with the stated cost. A better Euler tail by itself, an angular-family label for V6, or a kernel change importing PR15 without its source adapter would not establish a gain.
