statement:
## G155. Actual large-common-divisor saving

Set \(B=M(D_1)M(D_2)\). Cut its original ordered tuples by
\(N\gcd(d_1,d_2)\ge G\), **before** merging coefficients. This is not a
slot cut or a row selector. Define

\[
a_G(q)=\sum_{d\mid q,\,Nd\ge G}\mu(q/d).
\]

Divisor inversion gives \(\sum_{q\mid g}a_G(q)=1_{Ng\ge G}\),
\(a_G(q)=0\) for \(Nq<G\), and \(|a_G(q)|\le d(q)\).
Only squarefree q survive the two original Möbius factors. With
\(d_1=qx,d_2=qy\), their product is
\(\mu(x)\mu(y)1_{(x,q)=1}1_{(y,q)=1}\); no condition \((x,y)=1\) is
inserted. Thus the exact centrally normalized identity is

\[
B_{\ge G}(u)=\sum_{\substack{q\ \mathrm{squarefree}\\Nq\ge G}}
\frac{a_G(q)\phi_u(q)^2}{Nq}
M_u^{(q)}(D_1/Nq)M_u^{(q)}(D_2/Nq),                 \tag{G155.1}
\]

where superscript q means the literal coprimality mask. Fixed profile
support bounds \(Nq\ll D_1\). Natural zeros are kept, never divided out.

Restore each mask exactly:

\[
M_u^{(q)}(E;W)=
\sum_{h\ q\text{-smooth}}\frac{\phi_u(h)}{\sqrt{Nh}}
M_u(E/Nh;W).                                        \tag{G155.2}
\]

Primewise this is \(\mu*(1,1,\ldots)=(1,0,\ldots)\). It restores the
original Möbius coefficients, so the invoked moment is PR9 B0.9, not a
new moment for \(\mu*\mu\). All h shorten the scales. The finitely
supported sums may be dominated using
\(\prod_{\mathfrak p\mid q}(1-N\mathfrak p^{-1/2})^{-1}\ll(Nq)^\epsilon\).
A retained polynomially bounded puncture R0 is handled by qR0, within
the already frozen family. Nonempty subunit scales are bounded away
from zero by fixed profile support; smaller scales are empty.

Minkowski over q and both h, the trivial first-inverse bound and
\(\|M(E)\|_U^2\ll H_JU^\epsilon[U+U^{1/6}E^{5/6}]\) give

\[
\|B_{\ge G}Q\|_U^2\ll H_JU^{v+\epsilon}\frac{D_1}{G}
\left[U+U^{1/6}(D_2/G)^{5/6}\right].                 \tag{G155.3}
\]

The q-shell mass \(\sum|a_G(q)|/Nq\) is subpower; the shortened-scale
factors decrease geometrically. With \(G=U^{1/5}\), the second bracket
term dominates throughout the box and the exponent is
\(v+r+5s/6-1/5\). The target gap is at least

\[
\rho+(47/20)\delta-393/200\ge2809/273000>1/100.
\]

The derivative is \(47/20-50/[3(5-2\delta)^2]>0\). An independent exact
Bernstein certificate verifies this on the whole interval. Reserving
1/1000 for geometric pads and 1/500 for all auxiliary losses still
leaves a retained norm margin 1/200 and spare \(5/2184\).

On actual witnesses, where \(|B|^2\ge U^{\delta(r+s)-\eta}\), rows with
\(|B_{\ge G}|\ge|B|/2\) have the paid slot mass exponent
\(E_K-1/200+\epsilon\), after choosing the losses. Otherwise

The JN7 normalization1/Q and its PLUS sign on the second mark remain unchanged. The displayed finite character kernel is

    K(h,s,s')=chi_pi(h)^3 chi_pi'(h)^3
                        chi_pi(s)^2 chi_pi'(s')^4.

Natural zero support is T-invariant: h is a unit at both primes, s and s' are nonzero. Since chi(-1)=+-1 for a sextic character,

    K(Tz)=epsilon_(pi,pi') K(z),
    epsilon=chi_pi(-1)^5 chi_pi'(-1)^7
            =chi_pi(-1)chi_pi'(-1)
            =(-1)^[(q-1)/6+(q'-1)/6].               (AS2-8)

This is not uniformly -1. Norm pairs13/19 give -1;19/31 give+1, both admissible distinct split rational norms. An independent exact residue-exponent check exhausts61,009 and346,921 triples respectively, including every zero. These finite checks verify the kernel identity, not an asymptotic H bound or a choice of actual source arrays.

Let R_epsilon f(z)=(f(z)+epsilon f(Tz))/2. On the full finite group it is an orthogonal parity projection, and exact change of variables gives

    sum_z K(z) What(z)=sum_z K(z) R_epsilon What(z)
                     =sum_z K(z) Fourier(R_epsilon W)(z). (AS2-9)

The physical reflection acts simultaneously on(R,P,P'); the plus/minus signs in JN7 still give Fourier(TW)(z)=What(Tz). There is no additional Q, root or density factor. For epsilon=-1 only the odd part contributes, so even W suffices for exact cancellation. For epsilon=+1 only the even part contributes, so odd W suffices. Other signed cancellations are not excluded.     B_{>=G,u}=(D1D2)^(-1/2)

            phi_u(d1d2) W1(Nd1/D1)W2(Nd2/D2),         (3.1)

and `B_{<G}=B-B_{>=G}`. The prime slots are not part of this gcd cutoff; they remain fully original. Equation (3.1) is a column restriction before merging and before expansion against another row coefficient. It is not a selector of high rows.

Define the signed ideal-divisor coefficient

    a_G(q)=sum_(d|q, Nd>=G) mu(q/d).

Divisor convolution with 1 yields the exact finite identity

    1_(Ng>=G)=sum_(q|g) a_G(q).                       (3.2)

statement:
### 1. Power weights do not repair whole-span continuity near the center

Give shell \(j\) the additional squared-norm weight \(Q^{2rj}\). The exact squared Riesz norm on its finite span is
\[
 \frac{|P_s(v_0)|^2}{(1-Q^{-2})\|u\|^2}
 \sum_{j=0}^JQ^{(4-6\sigma-2r)j},\qquad \sigma=\Re s.
 \tag{A07.2}
\]
This follows by summing squared functional values divided by squared orthogonal basis norms. At a nonzero base period, local boundedness requires \(r>2-3\sigma\). The original source has weighted norm ratio
\[
 \frac{\|u\|_r^2}{\|u\|^2}
 =\frac{1-Q^{-2}}{1-Q^{-2+2r}}.
 \tag{A07.3}
\]
Its all-prime product is finite and nonzero precisely for \(r<1/2\); for \(r\ge1\), even a single-prime norm diverges. For \(0\le r<1\), this follows by comparing the positive logarithm with \(Q^{-2+2r}\); for \(r<0\), both corrections are summable.

Where (A07.2) converges, its relative factor compared with the unweighted full-source period ratio is
\[
 \kappa_{p,r}(s)=
 \frac{|1-x_p(s)|^2}
 {(1-Q^{-2})(1-Q^{4-6\sigma-2r})}. \tag{A07.4}
\]
For \(\sigma>2/3\), the numerator product is absolutely convergent; the positive denominator requires \(r>5/2-3\sigma\).

For the near-central range \(\sigma=1/2+e\), \(0<e<1/6\), suppose \(r<1/2\) so the source remains present. Either the single-prime series already diverges, or
\[
 p_*=6\sigma+2r-4>0,\qquad p_*<6e<3\sigma-1,\qquad p_*<1.
\]
The logarithm of the positive denominator in (A07.4) contributes at least \(Q^{-p_*}\), while the numerator logarithm is \(O(Q^{-(3\sigma-1)})\). Hence, for every sufficiently large good prime,
\(\log\kappa_{p,r}\ge Q^{-p_*}/2\). Its all-prime sum diverges. Under the stipulated nonzero full-source comparison, no such power-weight norm both contains the original source and bounds the continued functional on its entire joint-shell span.

This does not obstruct a restricted estimate for one squarefree vector, a graph norm of the actual current map, or a different tensor reference with independently verified arithmetic.
title: 1. Power weights do not repair whole-span continuity near the center

statement:
## 5. Independent derivation of the complete relative mass

For a pair l,l', use the actual valuation differences e_p in Z/6Z. Define pairwise coprime radicals q1,q2,q3 from e_p in {1,5}, {2,4}, {3}, and

    Q_i=Nq_i, Q=Q1 Q2 Q3, H=Q1 Q2^2 Q3^3.           (R11)

The complete residue vector, not merely the three norm values, specifies one relative character. At a good prime every nonzero local exponent has a nonprincipal character of conductor that prime. Fixed ray factors only modify fixed S-data and cannot cancel a good conductor prime. e=0 is the same ideal class modulo sixth powers, with all its natural holes retained.

Here is a derivation of [restricted research revision] that does not rely on a same-dyad estimate. For each choice of signs of the nonzero actual valuation differences, represent

    l=g a x^6, l'=g b y^6, (a,b)=1, Nab>=H.          (R12)

Take g as the actual ideal gcd. At a nonzero residue prime the remaining exponent in a or b is e_p or 6-e_p according to the sign; all multiples of six, including differences at zero-residue primes, go into x or y. This reconstructs every actual pair. Allowing arbitrary x,y afterward only overcounts. The number of sign choices is at most 2^omega(q1q2q3), a subpower on the polynomial terminal support. No coprimality between g and a,b is needed or imposed.

Put A=Na(Nx)^6 and B'=Nb(Ny)^6. The lower column support R3 requires

    Ng>=M=max(1,L0/A,L0/B').

The ideal count gives sum_(Ng>=M)(Ng)^(-2sigma)<<M^(1-2sigma), uniformly on the compact interval sigma>1/2. Since M>=L0/sqrt(A B') and 1-2sigma<0,

    (A B')^(-sigma) sum_(Ng>=M)(Ng)^(-2sigma)
       << L0^(1-2sigma) (A B')^(-1/2)
        = L0^(1-2sigma) (Nab)^(-1/2)
                              (Nx)^(-3)(Ny)^(-3).   (R13)

This remains true if L0/sqrt(A B')<1: M>=1 and the exponent has the required sign. The two root sums converge absolutely at exponent3. Multiplying by U^((2sigma-1)v+epsilon) from R3 and paying the finite sign choices gives

    sum_(l/l' in residue vector e)
          |partial b_l partial' b_l'|
      << H_J U^[-(2sigma-1)t+epsilon] H^(-1/2).       (R14)

The slot exponent cancels exactly because L0 is comparable to U^(t+v). R13 simultaneously prices all unequal scales and unequal roots. It also independently justifies the author's two convergent dyadic sums. There is no omitted g=1 branch, no arbitrary equality of column lengths, and no root diagonal restricted to l=l'. The projection to high cores only contracts this absolute mass.

In dyadic Q1,Q2,Q3 ranges, ideal counting and the finite residue choices give at most (Q1Q2Q3)^(1+epsilon) vectors. Multiplying their H^(-1/2) bounds yields

    total coefficient mass
      << H_J U^[-(2sigma-1)t+epsilon](Q1/Q3)^(1/2).  (R15)

This is the completed, original-slot version of external RM-A/RM7. The balanced-residue mechanism itself was already present in that source. Global character order six does not imply Q1>1: local exponents2 and3 at different primes give global order6 but Q1=1. The claimed ratio sector correctly includes those easier characters.

statement:
# [private research revision]: the whole one-unit-core C--C sector

9 October 2026. Derived by the cubic lane; UC1–UC17 were independently reviewed by the physical covariance lane, relative to the stated inherited inputs.
The accepted constant remains
`c0 = 0.125113352960035869...`; no larger constant follows from this result.

The theorem pays the actual whole C--C interaction with exactly one
squarefree core equal to one. It uses the established fixed angular
Hecke continuation and ordinary finite-order Hecke convexity. It does
not use I-HECKE's stronger buffered conductor bounds. It is neither a
transformed zero-frequency estimate nor the physical cube-row II
estimate of T05.

## 1. Statement and exact sector

Write M for [the merged manuscript](../../zeta_zero_free_validated_merged.md).
Use its original common column profile `W0`, smooth with all required
Euler derivatives rapidly decreasing at both endpoints, and its original
smooth radial Schwartz row profile `R = Phi_hat`, viewed as a function
of the norm variable. Indices for columns are good primary ideals, one
generator per ideal, and `q_a = Na`. Rows include all nonzero Eisenstein
elements, their six units, and all fixed-prime valuations. Fixed finite
ray/deletion refinements are discussed in section 5.

Let `Q_{1,*}` be the ordered part of M (2.15) with first squarefree core
one and second squarefree core `e > 1`; let `Q_{*,1}` be the reverse
orientation. For `D,K >= 1`, every fixed `0 < delta < 1`, and every
`epsilon > 0`, the theorem is
\[
\boxed{
|\mathfrak Q_{1,*}|+|\mathfrak Q_{*,1}|
\ll_{\delta,\epsilon}
K^\delta D^{11/6-\delta/2+\epsilon}.
}
\tag{UC1}
\]
Consequently, for any fixed `B0 > 0`,
\[
\boxed{
|\mathfrak Q_{1,*}|+|\mathfrak Q_{*,1}|
\ll_{\epsilon,B_0}D^{11/6+\epsilon},
\qquad 1\le K\le D^{B_0}.
}
\tag{UC2}
\]
Constants may depend on the original fixed profiles, the specified
finite number of Euler-derivative seminorms, fixed strip margins, and
the required fixed finite ray/deletion family. No uniformity for
arbitrary moving angular types or additional moving row masks is claimed.

M (2.14) gives
\[
\mathcal C_k(cB^3)=\beta(c)\vartheta_c(k)\xi(B)q_B,
\qquad \xi=\overline\alpha^{\,3},\qquad |\beta(c)|=1.
\]
M (2.8) establishes that there is no additional `1_{(B,k)=1}`.
Therefore the exact sector is
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathfrak Q_{1,*}
=\sum_{\substack{e>1\\e\ {\rm sf}}}\overline{\beta(e)}
\sum_{\substack{B,E\\(B,E)=1\\(B,e)=1}}
&\xi(B)\overline{\xi(E)}q_Bq_E
 \overline{W_0(q_B^3/D)}W_0(q_eq_E^3/D)\\
&\times\sum_{k\ne0}\overline{\vartheta_e(k)}
 R\!\left(\frac{q_k}
 {K(q_B^3/D)(q_eq_E^3/D)}\right).
\end{aligned}
\tag{UC3}
\]
The exact total-column coprimality is `(B,E)=(B,e)=1`.
The own-column overlap `(e,E)>1` remains allowed. Natural row zeros at
primes dividing `e` remain inside `vartheta_e`.

## 2. The fixed angular sums and the moving deletion

Put
\[
X_0=D^{1/3},\qquad Y_e=(D/q_e)^{1/3},
\]
and define
\[
\begin{aligned}
S_z^-(X)&=\sum_b\xi(b)q_b(q_b/X)^{3z}
                 \overline{W_0((q_b/X)^3)},\\
S_z^+(X)&=\sum_b\overline{\xi(b)}q_b(q_b/X)^{3z}
                 W_0((q_b/X)^3).
\end{aligned}
\tag{UC4}
\]
The established angular argument in
[CS8](../[private research revision]-continuation/cubic-sectors.md) gives,
uniformly for `Re z` in any fixed compact interval and for every fixed
`A > 0`,
\[
|S_z^\pm(X)|
\ll_A(1+|\Im z|)^{C_A}\min(X^A,X^{-A}).
\tag{UC5}
\]
For `X <= 1`, rapid upper-endpoint decay and ideal counting suffice.
For `X >= 1`, the auxiliary column Mellin integral contains the fixed
entire functions `L^S(w-1,xi)` or `L^S(w-1,bar xi)`, and its line moves
to `Re w=-A` without a residue. Their entire continuation and polynomial
growth on each fixed strip are supplied in
[[private research revision] T01](../[private research revision]/[restricted mathematical source]).
The Mellin transform of `u^(3z) W0(u^3)` has an imaginary translation
proportional to `Im z`; integration against the fixed angular function
therefore costs only a polynomial in `Im z`. This argument works on
every fixed compact interval of `Re z`, including the positive strip
used below.

Let `S_z^-(X;e)` be the first sum in (UC4) restricted to `(b,e)=1`.
Open this mask exactly:
\[
\boxed{
S_z^-(X;e)=
\sum_{r\mid e}\mu(r)\xi(r)q_r\,S_z^-(X/q_r).
}
\tag{UC6}
\]
The factor `q_r` is necessary. Formula (UC6), rather than a uniform
rapid-decay assertion for a moving-deleted angular function, prices
the moving deletion.

Insert the exact projector for `(B,E)=1` in (UC3), and write
`B=ell b`, `E=ell f`. The remaining first-column mask is
`(ell,e)=(b,e)=1`. The two angular factors at `ell` cancel. The column
expression after row Mellin inversion is exactly
\[
\begin{aligned}
T_e(z)
&=\sum_{(\ell,e)=1}\mu(\ell)q_\ell^2
 S_z^+(Y_e/q_\ell)S_z^-(X_0/q_\ell;e)\\
&=\sum_{(\ell,e)=1}\mu(\ell)q_\ell^2
 S_z^+(Y_e/q_\ell)
 \sum_{r\mid e}\mu(r)\xi(r)q_r
 S_z^-(X_0/(q_\ell q_r)).
\end{aligned}
\tag{UC7}
\]
The product is at the **same complex `z`**, not an absolute square.
In particular, with matching profiles,
`S_z^+(X)=conj(S_{bar z}^-(X))`. Both factors are bounded separately.

## 3. A complete column bound

From (UC5), with endpoint exponents greater than one,
\[
|S_z^-(u)|\ll (1+|\Im z|)^C u\qquad(u>0).
\]
Thus every divisor in (UC7) satisfies
\[
q_r\left|S_z^-\!\left(\frac{X_0}{q_\ell q_r}\right)\right|
\ll (1+|\Im z|)^C\frac{X_0}{q_\ell}.
\tag{UC8}
\]
Taking absolute values only after the exact openings gives
\[
|T_e(z)|
\ll (1+|\Im z|)^C\tau(e)X_0
       \sum_\ell q_\ell|S_z^+(Y_e/q_\ell)|.
\tag{UC9}
\]
For each fixed `A>2`, ideal counting and (UC5) give
\[
\sum_\ell q_\ell|S_z^+(Y/q_\ell)|
\ll_A(1+|\Im z|)^{C_A}
\begin{cases}
Y^2,&Y\ge1,\\
Y^A,&0<Y<1.
\end{cases}
\tag{UC10}
\]
For `Y>=1`, split at `q_ell=Y`: a norm dyad `q_ell ~ L` costs
`L^2 min((Y/L)^A,(Y/L)^(-A))`, and both geometric tails sum to `Y^2`.
For `Y<1`, the convergent upper bound is
`Y^A sum_ell q_ell^(1-A)`.

Consequently, for every prescribed `N>0`,
\[
\boxed{
|T_e(z)|
\ll_{N,\epsilon}
(1+|\Im z|)^C
Dq_e^{-2/3+\epsilon}E_N(q_e/D),
\quad E_N(u)=\min(1,u^{-N}).
}
\tag{UC11}
\]
For `q_e>D`, choose the endpoint exponent in (UC10) as `A=3N+2`.
This includes the complete unbounded profile tail. The bound is uniform
on the fixed positive strip used for the row contour shift.

## 4. The actual row character, contour, and complementary core sum

Initially take a single row Mellin line `Re z=rho>1`, with
\[
\widetilde R(z)=\int_0^\infty R(v)v^{z-1}\,dv.
\]
The six unit multiples annihilate the row sum unless
`vartheta_e|_{mu_6}=1`. For every surviving core,
\[
\sum_{k\ne0}\overline{\vartheta_e(k)}q_k^{-z}
=6L_{\mathbb K}(z,\overline{\vartheta_e}).
\tag{UC12}
\]
This is the **full** Hecke function, with the fixed-prime row Euler
factors retained. The unit-neutrality and primitive-conductor statement
is supplied by [review [private research revision], section 1](../review-cycle-9.md).
Because `e>1` is squarefree, its primitive good conductor `e` is
nontrivial. Hence there is no principal pole at one.

The exact row Mellin identity is
\[
\mathfrak Q_{1,*}
=\frac6{2\pi i}\int_{(\rho)}
\widetilde R(z)K^z
\sum_{\substack{e>1,\ {\rm sf}\\
                 \vartheta_e|_{\mu_6}=1}}
\overline{\beta(e)}
L_{\mathbb K}(z,\overline{\vartheta_e})T_e(z)\,dz.
\tag{UC13}
\]
The initial exchanges, including the coprimality expansion, are
absolute by the original profile tails and `rho>1`.

Fix `0<delta<1` and shift only this row line to `Re z=delta`.
No principal pole at one is crossed. The contour stays to the right
of zero, so it crosses no small-argument Mellin pole of `R` either.
The ordinary functional equation in review [private research revision], section 1, and
three-lines give
\[
|L_{\mathbb K}(\delta+it,\overline{\vartheta_e})|
\ll_{\delta,\epsilon}
q_e^{(1-\delta)/2+\epsilon}(1+|t|)^A.
\tag{UC14}
\]
One may derive this by absolute convergence on `Re z=1+nu`, the
functional equation on `Re z=-nu`, and interpolation. The resulting
`O(nu)` conductor loss is allocated inside `epsilon`. The gamma
quotient has polynomial fixed-strip height growth, with its order
independent of the moving conductor. This is ordinary convexity,
not an invocation of the stronger I-HECKE package.

Equation (UC11), with arbitrarily large `N`, makes the core series
normally convergent on the compact strip used in the shift and pays
every polynomial conductor bound there. The rapid vertical decay of
`R_tilde` on fixed positive lines absorbs all polynomial heights in
(UC11) and (UC14). Horizontal contour integrals vanish accordingly.

Using `|beta(e)|=1` and ideal counting gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
|\mathfrak Q_{1,*}|
&\ll K^\delta D
 \sum_e q_e^{-2/3+(1-\delta)/2+\epsilon}
                   E_N(q_e/D)\\
&\ll K^\delta D^{11/6-\delta/2+\epsilon}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{UC15}
\]
The reverse orientation has the same proof after exchanging the
profiles and angular factors. This proves (UC1). For fixed
`1<=K<=D^B0`, choose `delta>0` sufficiently small in terms of the final
loss and `B0`, allocate the preliminary losses, and obtain (UC2).

A concrete fixed-contour check is useful: at `delta=1/4` and
`K<=D^.87653`,
\[
|\mathfrak Q_{1,*}|+|\mathfrak Q_{*,1}|
\ll D^{1.927465833333\ldots+\epsilon}.
\tag{UC16}
\]
Thus affordability already follows with a fixed positive contour and
a strict power margin, without invoking an endpoint-looking notation.

## 5. Fixed components, remaining gate, and review scope

A fixed finite-ray refinement of a column expands into finitely many
finite-order character twists of `xi` or `bar xi`. Their infinity
types remain nonzero and their conductors remain fixed. Any resulting
`ell` or divisor phases have bounded magnitude. Hence (UC5)--(UC11)
hold componentwise. The argument does not move a deleted Euler
product with conductor depending on the core or row.

For fixed-place row refinements, retain the exact local factors and
finite component decomposition. Their Hecke characters still have
nontrivial good conductor `e`. Fixed-place factors are bounded on each
fixed strip `Re z>=delta>0`; fixed-prime valuation progressions have
their geometric factors there. None can principalize the nontrivial
good character. All fixed-prime row valuations and natural zeros are
therefore accounted for. This assertion covers the required fixed
refinements, not arbitrary additional moving masks.

No Mellin root of the original common profile has been moved or
discarded. The two auxiliary angular column shifts are residue-free;
the row shift has the nonprincipal justification above. The argument
uses no positivity of a coprimality-localized form.

Let `Q_{**}` denote the original C--C contribution with both squarefree
cores strictly greater than one. Combining this result with the accepted
whole pure-cube proposition in
[cubic-sectors.md](../[private research revision]-continuation/cubic-sectors.md)
gives the exact residual accounting
\[
\mathfrak Q_{\rm rem}
=\mathfrak Q_{**}-\mathfrak Q_{II}
 +O_\epsilon\!\left(DK^{1+\epsilon}+D^{11/6+\epsilon}\right)
\quad(1\le K\le D^{B_0}).
\tag{UC17}
\]
At `K<=D^.87653`, both displayed errors are below `D^2`.
The unpaid gate is the actual signed combination `Q_{**}-Q_{II}`.
[[private research revision] T05](../[private research revision]/[restricted mathematical source])
continues to pay only physical cube-row II; it is not promoted to an
estimate for whole C--C. No increase of `c0` is claimed.

Independent review checked the exact factor and rescaling in UC6, the permitted own-column overlap, the full unit-neutral row series, and normal convergence for the positive row-line shift. The moving-level issue is handled by the exact divisor opening UC6, without assuming uniformity of UC5 under moving deletions.

## G125. Exact curved return and actual coarse bound

For fixed b>1 define the literal infinite sources

    F_chi(z)=sum_(n>=1)mu(n)chi(n)exp(-nz), Re z>0,
    V_b,chi(x)=F_chi(x^(-b)+i/x).

For Re s>0 put I_n(s)=integral_0^infinity exp(-nt^b-int)t^(s-1)dt.
Substitute v=nt and rotate to arg v=-alpha, fixed0<alpha<pi/(2b).
The small arc vanishes; on the large arc exp(-n^(1-b)v^b) decays and
|exp(-iv)|<=1. On the new ray the Taylor remainder for exp(-z),Re z>=0,
is bounded by |z|^K/K!. Consequently

    I_n(s)=sum_(0<=k<K) A_k(s)n^(-s-(b-1)k)+R_n,K(s),
    A_k(s)=(-1)^k Gamma(s+bk)exp(-i*pi*(s+bk)/2)/k!,
    |R_n,K(s)|<=C_(b,K,C)n^(-Re s-(b-1)K),             (1)

uniformly on every compact C in Re s>0. The ray majorant is
exp(alpha Im s)Gamma(Re s+bK)/(K! sin(alpha)^(Re s+bK)). Thus the sum
of remainders is normally holomorphic for Re s>max(0,1-(b-1)K).
Absolute Fubini initially on Re s>b proves

    H_chi(s)=integral_0^infinity F_chi(t^b+it)t^(s-1)dt
      =sum_(k<K) A_k(s)/L(s+(b-1)k,chi)+R_chi,K(s).     (2)

Every L is the actual original ordinary character, with all Euler holes.
At b=3/2,K=1 the remainder is holomorphic for Re s>1/2, and the
multiplier Gamma(s)exp(-i*pi*s/2) has no zeros there. The sign of the
additive phase and that multiplier is fixed, not discarded.

A sufficient complete arithmetic input is, for everyepsilon>0 and every
large dyadic shell, with a common fixed gamma,

    integral_X^(2X)|V_b,chi(x)| dx/x <<_(chi,epsilon) X^(gamma+epsilon).
                                                               (OPEN-CURVE)

Constants and onset may depend on the fixed character. Shell L2 energy
bounded by X^(2gamma+epsilon) suffices by Cauchy–Schwarz. Dyadic summation
makes H holomorphic on Re s>gamma; the complementary t>=1 tail is paid by
exp(-t^b)/(1-exp(-t^b)). For b=3/2,gamma>1/2, (2) excludes every zero
there. The principal pole gives a zero of the reciprocal and is retained.
Imprimitive Euler factors were included from the start; their zeros lie
on Re s=0. No uniform bound over arbitrarily large imaginary parts is
asserted or needed: local holomorphy reaches each finite height.

For any fixed b>1,0<gamma<1 choose finite K with1-(b-1)K<gamma.
Starting from Re s>1, solve (2) successively on strips of width b-1:
all shifted reciprocals are already holomorphic on the next strip.
The same H and nonvanishing A_0 give the unshifted extension. Finitely
many steps reach Re s>gamma. Neither b nor K moves with x. No converse
equivalence to a Mertens bound has been proved.

At b=3/2, first gain needs gamma<theta11=.8748540364, or energy
exponent<1.7497080728. Conditional examples retain
gamma=.87485 (c=.12515), gamma=5/6 (c=1/6), gamma=3/4 (c=1/4).
They are open estimates, not accepted endpoints.

The pass proves the actual pointwise theorem

    V_(3/2),chi(x)<<_(chi,epsilon)x^(5/4+epsilon)        (3)

for every sufficiently large REAL x, including the whole infinite tail.
For its full proof use N=x^(3/2),T=N(log x)^2,U=V=floor(sqrt x), and
the all-integer convolution identity

    mu=mu_<=U+mu_<=V-mu_<=U*mu_<=V*1+mu_>U*mu_>V*1.

Both short sums cost O(sqrt x). Fixed-modulus additive Fourier inversion
preserves chi's zeros and reduces to beta=ell/q-1/(2*pi*x). For Y<=T,
the exact spacing estimates are

    sum_(d<=x)min(Y/d,1/(2||beta d||))<<_q x log(2x)+Y/x,
    sum_(h<=H)min(M,1/(2||beta h||))<<_q(H/x+1)(M+x log(2x)).

Split into q residue classes and blocks of length at most x. Phases in
each block move monotonically at spacing q/(2*pi*x); nearest points cost
the finite first argument, and the rest a harmonic sum. In the first
estimate a nontrivial zero crossing occurs only at d comparable to x,
so resonance costs Y/x. This includes noninteger real x and exact
resonance, not only generic phases.

The divisor-sized Type I coefficient, supported on d<=UV<=x, therefore
costs x^(1+epsilon). For Type II let b_d=sum_(c|d,c>V)mu(c).
In a box (M,2M]x(L,2L],md<=Y, Cauchy retains the COMPLETE Gram

    sum_(d,e)b_d conjugate(b_e)
       sum_(m in(M,2M],m<=Y/max(d,e))e(beta m(d-e)).

The inner set is one interval. Its diagonal and the second spacing bound
give squared cost

    T^epsilon [M^2 L+ML(L/x+1)(M+x log(2x))]
      <<T^epsilon(Y^2/U+Y^2/x+Yx)log(2x)<<x^(5/2+epsilon).

Summing the logarithmically many boxes proves the prefix bound uniformly
for Y<=T. Partial summation restores exp(-n/N), and the discarded tail
is O(N exp(-(log x)^2)), smaller than every fixed power. This proves (3).
The short terms and tail are paid for the target; BOTH Type I exponent1
and Type II exponent5/4 remain above theta11. A Type II improvement alone
would not complete a gain. Their full signed recombination is an eligible
weaker target. The pointwise saving is relative to damping length x^(3/2),
not the observation scale x.

The [Green–Tao primary source](https://aif.centre-mersenne.org/item/10.5802/aif.2401.pdf),
Lemma4.1, concerns a dyadic interval with UV<=N. Here the all-integer
identity restores both short terms and is separately derived from
mu*1=delta_1. The [BSZ theorem](https://publications.ias.edu/sites/default/files/disjointness%20b-s-z%20oct.pdf)
was discovery ancestry only; its fixed-parameter conclusion supplies no
uniform power saving under a shrinking parameter.

## R42.8. Other first tests: precise reach

T01 is correct: for positive definite Gamma, minimizing w*Gamma w subject to v*w=1 gives 1/(v*Gamma^-1v). If Gamma is semidefinite and v has a nonzero kernel component the minimum is0; otherwise use the range and pseudoinverse. v=0 is infeasible. This is one normalized linear signal constraint in two coordinates, not two independent zero constraints. It adds no arithmetic bound beyond the F09/F11 duality lineage.

T16 has the correct complex orientation for <U,V>=integral U conjugate(V): C=<U,V> and E1=||V||^2 give ||U-lambda V||^2=E0-|C|^2/E1+E1|lambda-C/E1|^2. For the actual normalized pair, Mellin(V)=h Mellin(U). At a simple zero rho, lambda=1/h(rho) removes the pole; at a multiple zero it may only lower the pole order, so the author's explicit simple-zero qualification matters. Shellwise optimization is not a fixed signal-preserving field. This does not rule out useful simultaneous arithmetic estimates, now made source-specific by D02 and D26.

T04 is valid for literal support deletion. For f3(p^k)=-1 at p!=3 and f3(3^k)=1, the prime-power field has leading term -exp(tau/2)x/log x. The fixed Gaussian prime number theorem gives the coefficient exp(tau/2); powers of degree>=2 and the prime3 exceptions are O_epsilon(X^(1/2+epsilon)) on the shell. The inherited complete f3 exponent below1 forces the complementary field to have the opposite leading term. Deleting primes is not a power-small error, and their cross term is essential. This does not invalidate a genuinely defined orthogonal projection or deletion of only higher powers.

T26 correctly reuses W40-12: p=2,q=5,x=sqrt10,tau=(log5)/2 give native four-label Gaussian weights proportional to(1,2,2,1), covariance -1/12 and correlation -1/3. This is a finite conditional example, not a claim about the unconditional infinite occupation law. D26's constructive replacement is a deterministic Euler-factor calculation, not a proof of stochastic prime independence.

T28 correctly retains W31 R31.30 ancestry. On the squarefree degree-j fiber, the j! ordered words have the same Möbius sign, and the commutative quotient has norm sqrt(j!). Repeated-letter fibers have smaller multiplicities; the stated operator norm is attained on distinct primes. The naive free transfer pays this factorial cost. No native H embedding or estimate for the actual symmetric lift is established.

### 5.2 Every retained p-valuation and a real projected price

Write n=p^a m with p not dividing m and m squarefree, j=omega(m). The exact filtered
tail coefficient is, with binomial coefficients outside0,...,J interpreted as0,

 (v_(p,J)*r_J)(p^a m)
  =chi(p)^a chi(m) [(-p)^a binom(J,a)W_J(j)
                    +(-p)^(a-1)binom(J,a-1)W_J(j+1)],      (27)

where the second term is absent at a=0. It vanishes for a>J+1, and for nonsquarefree
m or a ramified factor in m. Formula(27) retains the two possible squarefree
predecessors (p^a removed or p^(a-1) removed), including a=J+1. Replacing its two
terms by independent signs would change the source. Conversely, deleting positive
or negative valuations is not a signed upper bound.

For a principal chi, the unramified p-free sector of(27) has the fixed sign from
(21), with coefficient(J+1)! at omega(n)=J+1. Choose a fixed squarefree product A
of J distinct primes avoiding pq. On the literal projected family n=A*l with l a
prime not dividing Apq, n<=x, the coefficient is the nonzero constant
(-1)^(J+1)(J+1)!. Chebyshev's lower bound pi(y)>>y/log y consequently gives a
projected summatory price >>_(A,J) x/log x. Only finitely many primes are excluded.
This is an actual arithmetic family, not an arbitrary-sign countermodel.

This lower price rules out paying every such projected component separately with
the desired power after fixed-depth subtraction. It does NOT lower-bound the full
filtered tail, which includes essential p-divisible cross-valuations and other
prime counts. The terminal-prime projection strategy is inherited from the earlier
[restricted research revision]/[restricted research revision]/[restricted research revision] obstruction family; its new role here is diagnostic for the exact
Newton tail, not an independent claimed discovery of that general obstruction.

## A14. Grok's conditional geometry certificate and its scope corrections

### What the source actually certifies

Assume the **well-defined full-probe hypothesis**
\[
|I_\eta^{\rm comp}|\ll Z^{\theta-\sigma+\epsilon},
\quad \theta=x/2+(y-x)/12,\quad \sigma>0, \tag{A14.1}
\]
at the stated \(\tau=0\) geometry. To use the inherited \(\beta_*\) bootstrap, this must hold for every required fixed primitive finite-order target, its fixed deletion/ray data, and actual finite marked-prime configurations with the original weights and profiles. The real saving \(\sigma\) is common; constants and polynomial height costs may depend on fixed targets/data as permitted in M B0.7. A single chosen component, a single finite height, or an invented projection of the raw field is insufficient.

Relative to those hypotheses and the inherited B0.7 estimates, independent rerunning certifies:

| Conditional target \(c\) | Required \(\sigma\) | Safe lower bound for stationary slack \(b-F^*\) |
|---|---:|---:|
| \(313/2500=.1252\) | \(1/8000\) | \(0.0000432091\) |
| \(251/2000=.1255\) | \(3/5000\) | \(0.0003345304\) |
| \(12551/100000=.12551\) | \(7/10000\) | \(0.0006267350\) |
| \(63/500=.126\) | \(1/800\) | \(0.0003447368\) |
| \(16/125=.128\) | \(1/250\) | \(0.0008907891\) |

For each pair put \(b=1-c\), \(\kappa_t=2b-1\), \(\ell=4(11/12-b-\sigma)\), choose the smaller \(\delta\in(.46,.48)\) root of B0.48, and choose \(h\) by B0.45 with this \(\kappa_t,\ell,\delta\); let \(x=1+\ell-h,y=h-2\ell\). The certificate proves:

- All physical geometry, capacity and support inequalities, including \(\ell/h>4/21\), \(y<6\kappa_t\ell\), \(b>.87\), and the inactive positive part.
- The global amplitude rectangle inequality \(F_{\kappa_t}(\delta',p)\le b\), for \(0\le\delta'\le5/6,0\le p\le1/2\), by outward interval subdivision.
- The other dyadic endpoint, floor class, small rows and principal contour margins.
- With geometry fixed, \(\partial_\kappa F<1/20\) up to the accepted \(\kappa_0\).

If \(\beta_*>b\), write \(\mu=\beta_*-b\), and use \(\kappa=2\beta_*-1=\kappa_t+2\mu\). The derivative bound gives \(F_\kappa-\beta_*\le-.9\mu\). Convexity in the row exponent and the checked endpoint/floor margins complete the inherited numerator estimate. The physical saving gives \(J_\eta\ll Z^{b-k+\epsilon}\). M B0.7's original ordering of buffers, meshes, finite slots and small polynomial heights then gives the contradiction. No arithmetic estimate in (A14.1) is proved by the numerical certificate.

### Source-code inspection, execution, and corrected copy

The original script was inspected and independently executed. Every target passed all 23 checks; amplitude box counts were respectively 98017, 32449, 22269, 32265, 19093.

A corrected portable copy is included as checks/grok_transfer_certificate.py; its independent rerun is checks/grok_transfer_certificate_result.txt. It requires only Python's standard library. Corrections:

- Signed rational-to-Decimal rounding now uses the signed numerator directly. The original helper rounded negative nonterminating rationals in the wrong direction, although its only relevant negative test here was the exact terminating \(-1/50\), so the five original certifications were not affected.
- Printed slack/rate lower bounds use directed subtraction.
- Subdivision midpoints use directed addition and division; the original children still covered their parent in the actual run, but the revised arithmetic makes that coverage explicit.
- The geometry identity \(x+y+\ell=1\) is justified by its definitions and checked by an enclosure containing one, instead of a tolerance.
- An unused placeholder and the false comment that the quadratic's constant term was zero were removed.

The handoff's prose bound “uniform derivative \(<.043\)” is false. The maximum of its reported certified upper bounds is \(0.0440833871\ldots\), so use \(<.0441<1/20\). Several strict slack inequalities were rounded upward; the table above uses safe downward bounds. At \(c=.1255\),
\[
y-x=0.08753960844756839075\ldots,\qquad
\frac{y-x}{12}=0.00729496737063069923\ldots.
\]
Thus the supplied lower claim \(y-x>.08753960845\) is also an upward-rounding error. The ratio \(.0006/((y-x)/12)<.0823\) remains correct.

### Gram localization is not a vector projection

The three terms in B0.22's nonnegative majorant have square-root exponents
\[
\frac x2,\qquad \frac{y-x}{2},\qquad
\frac x2+\frac{y-x}{12}.
\]
The middle term is smaller than the first for \(y<2x\). This correctly identifies the \(P_a^{1/6}\) term as the sole excess in that majorant.

However the label \(k=r^6\) occurs after expanding pairs of outer columns, with profile argument \(\sqrt Q\,r^6/(ab)\). It is not a fixed additive spectral projection of \(A\). GS §2 states this caveat, but §7 then writes \(A^{(6)}\) without constructing it. Therefore the claimed “sixth-power portion of \(A\) paired with \(B\)” is **not presently a defined mathematical object**. Retain (A14.1), or construct an exact theta-paired bilinear identity/projector and prove its principal calibration before using that language. Positivity of a raw neutral-ray Gram does not refute a theta-specific cancellation estimate; it also does not define such a projection.

The claimed “full deletion permits only a detached window near \(.12937\)” is also too strong. That window is merely the diagnostic obtained by forcing equality \(\sigma=(y-x)/12\) and a particular stationary geometry. A stronger valid estimate may be deliberately weakened; for example the certified \(.1255\) geometry needs only \(\sigma=.0006\), much less than its full excess. The detached saturated-geometry window is not an obstruction to smaller improvements.

### New exact alternative to the fixed-point search

At fixed target \(\kappa\) and its chosen \(\delta\), put
\[
D_\kappa=3R'/4-1/(24\kappa),\quad
H_0=-1/(2D_\kappa),\quad
H_1=-(1/2+1/(6\kappa))/D_\kappa.
\]
Then \(h=H_0+H_1\ell\). Let
\[
A_\kappa=(2H_0-1)/12,\qquad
B_\kappa=(2H_1-3)/12,\qquad
\ell_b=4(c-1/12).
\]
The simultaneous equations \(\ell=\ell_b-4\sigma\), \(\sigma=\alpha(y-x)/12\) solve exactly as
\[
\sigma=
\frac{\alpha(A_\kappa+B_\kappa\ell_b)}
{1+4\alpha B_\kappa}, \tag{A14.2}
\]
whenever the denominator is nonzero. All capacity and rectangle constraints still require separate verification. This removes the need for a monotonicity-assuming binary search and is a new exact diagnostic simplification.

The resonant-coset, Pólya–Vinogradov-shaped, and generic \((Q+Z)\) comparisons in GS §5 are at most bookkeeping comparisons under their displayed models. The coset bound is not reconstructed there with full coefficients; do not promote it to a new uniform arithmetic lemma. The explicit algebraic comparisons at \(4/33\) are correct.

### 1.2 Exact two-prime source and all source-completion errors

Let nu=(3rho_0-1)/2>0 and U=X^(1+nu). Then U<z^3 for all rho in the
chosen interval and large X. If n<=U has at least two distinct primes
above z, it has exactly two, say p<q; each occurs to the first power.
Its unique factorization n=rpq has r<z, so (r,pq)=1 and f(n)=f(r).
Conversely every such factorization below U has the original source
coefficient. It follows that the two-prime completion is EXACT below U:

    f(n)1_(omega_z(n)>=2)
      =sum_(z<p<q, pq|n) f(n/(pq)),   n<=U.            (R1.4)

Above U the identity can fail, and we do not use it there. The number
of representations is at most d_3(n), so (R0.2) pays the whole
discrepancy. Thus

    R_z(x)=sum_(z<p<q) sum_(r>=1) f(r)g(log(rpq/x))
                  +O_A(X^-A).                        (R1.5)

This pays every term with three rough primes and every repeated rough
prime power. It preserves every valuation in the original source.
The frozen author's outside-range witnesses are correct: at z=5,
n=7^2*11 gives original +1 versus completion -1, and n=7*11*13 gives
original -1 versus completion -3. The equality is not global.
title: 1.2 Exact two-prime source and all source-completion errors

# [private research revision]: complete Gaussian compression and source-feedback obstructions

The controller accepts the following exact scopes after full reads of the
[W43 author](wild43/report.md) and [independent critic](wild43-review/report.md).
All30 seeds and immutable pools remain with the reports. These results do not
increase written c6=.125139 or pay the open complete arithmetic moment.
Historical .874864/.749728 targets in the frozen reports become
.874861/.749722 for the current endpoint. The original artifacts are unchanged.

## [restricted research revision]-W1. A summatory norm alone is not a convolution algebra

For 0<sigma<1, put ||a||_sigma=sup_x x^(-sigma)|sum_(n<=x)a(n)|.
There is no uniform convolution-algebra inequality for this norm, even when
both sequences have coefficients bounded by1. This is a finite-family
counterexample; it is not an actual Mobius or fixed-character counterexample.

Take A(d)=(-1)^(d+1)/2 for1<=d<=N and zero afterN, and a(d)=A(d)-A(d-1).
Choose H>=4(N+1)^2 and H^(1-sigma)>=16(N+1)^(2-sigma). At the distinct
knots floor(H/d), interpolate a function B with value sign(a(d))t^sigma,
using the endpoints specified in the source proof and extending by zero.
Its piecewise linear interpolation has slopes at most1 and
|B(t)|<=t^sigma; set b(n)=B(n)-B(n-1). The summatory norms remain bounded,
while the convolution atH aligns the signs and is at least a fixed multiple
of H^sigma sum_(2<=d<=N)d^(-sigma). This diverges relative to H^sigma.
Choosing H on the stated scale gives the diagnostic exponent1/(2-sigma).

A source-specific algebra using additional multiplicative or signed
structure is still eligible. What fails is the proposed inference from
the two summatory norm bounds alone.

## [restricted research revision]-W2. Exact Newton correction has a support/feedback dichotomy

Write m_Y(n)=mu(n)1_(n<=Y), d_Y=delta-1*m_Y, with Dirichlet convolution,
and q_(Y,k)=m_Y*(delta+d_Y+...+d_Y^(*(k-1))). Then exactly

    delta-1*q_(Y,k)=d_Y^(*k),
    d_Y(n)=0 for n<=Y,
    d_Y^(*k)(n)=0 for n<(Y+1)^k.

Thus q equals mu on that longer prefix. Truncating q to the prefix merely
produces a longer ordinary Mobius truncation. In Dirichlet-series notation,
with Q=Q_tr+T and D=1-zeta M,

    1-zeta Q_tr=D^k+zeta T.

The tail feedback cannot be dropped. At a zeta zero, D=1 and Q=kM: the
finite correction is regular there, so small support error alone has lost
the original reciprocal pole signal.

For a Y-rough integer, d_Y=-1. On a product with exactlyk prime factors
counted with multiplicity, d_Y^(*k)=(-1)^k k!/product e_p!. For fixedk
and Y=X^theta, theta<=1/k gives a rough-sector absolute Gaussian mass
at least a constant times X/(log X)^k, using distinct primes. This is not
a lower bound on the entire signed defect. For theta>1/k, the full defect
Gaussian is O_A(X^-A) for everyA by future support and the divisor bound;
its missing zero feedback is still unpaid. Growingk requires uniform
constants, all tails and a surviving zero signal. Fixed ordinary character
twists preserve their natural zeros; no Eisenstein extension is inferred.

## [restricted research revision]-W3. A concrete polynomial projection of the complete Gaussian field

Let |a(n)|<=1, tau>0 fixed and
F_a(x)=sum_n a(n)g_tau(log(n/x)), with the normalized log Gaussian.
Fix A>0, L=log X and C=sqrt(2tau(A+2)). Cover the entire log interval
[-C sqrt(L),log2+C sqrt(L)] by unit bins, rounding outward at the ends.
On each bin use counting-measure orthogonal projection onto polynomials
of degree<m in log(n/X), where

    m=ceil(2(A+2)L/log L).

If a bin has fewer thanm points, take its full value space. This defines
a fixed projection P_X for the entire shell. Both infinite tails and all
within-bin Taylor residuals are paid, and uniformly on x in[X,2X],

    F_a(x)=sum_n (P_X a)(n)g_tau(log(n/x))+O_A(X^-A).

The rank is O(L^(3/2)/log L). The proof uses the center-uniform error
2(2pi tau)^(-1/2)(e/(tau m))^(m/2); Gaussian tails supply the stated
truncation. This makes the projection source-exact, but its small rank
does not estimate the projected arithmetic coordinates.

The complete readout Gram c* K_X c is equivalent to the original shell
moment up to the paid errors. The positive coordinate energy
E_X=||P_X a||_2^2 is a stronger sufficient input:

    E_X << X^(2gamma-1+epsilon)  ==>  ||F_a||_(L2([X,2X],dx/x))
                                      << X^(gamma+epsilon).

This uses the full Gaussian Hilbert--Schmidt estimate X^(1+o(1)); it is
not a diagonal substitution for the signed readout Gram. A summatory bound
sum_(n<=x)a(n)=O(x^beta) already gives E_X<=X^(2beta-1+o(1)). The growing
degree is paid through the Lagrange derivative bound D_m=m(2e)^m,
discrete/continuous norm comparison and both Abel endpoint terms.
Consequently baseline recovery alone supplies no new arithmetic gain.
At current c6, a strict positive-energy improvement needs exponent below
.749722; exact Gram cancellation might be weaker and more useful.

Credit the earlier W39-C01 analytic compression mechanism. W43 adds this
concrete counting-measure source projection, full-tail return and baseline
comparison. All signed coefficients remain available, including actualf3.

## [restricted research revision]-W4. Native H graph transport must keep its harmonic residue

For the literal native coefficient vector b and kernel values phi, set
a=conjugate(b). Fix an incidence matrix B and positive edge weights W,
L=BWB*, h=projection_(ker L)a and j=WB*L^dagger a. Then

    H=<j,B*phi>+<h,phi>,
    ||j||_(W^-1)^2=a*L^dagger a.

This is the minimum-energy filling of the nonharmonic demand. Cauchy--Schwarz
pays the first term by the square roots of filling energy and edge-gradient
energy; the harmonic term remains. For relative boundaries, the residual
a_T-B_Tj likewise remains. A graph chosen adaptively gives a pointwise
identity but cannot inherit a sparse estimate proved only for a frozen graph.

The actual full-H target remains
GK[N+L+(NL)^(2/3)]sqrt(Omega1 Omega2)P_orig before the single outer
N^-1 G^-2 normalization. Every complementary H branch stays unpaid. This
extends the existing graph-transport library with the exact boundary and
harmonic contract; it supplies no .004-deficit reduction.

## Dispositions and the next useful mathematical work

The critic's protected audit21 supplies [restricted research revision]-W4. Its uniform audit18 rejects
the inference from overlapping domains or a nonzero vector state to scalar
nonvanishing: f(z)=1-z has a zero although (f,f') is never zero. A genuine
Rouche cover needs actual-source boundary enclosures, positive margins and
coverage at every height. A finite patch is insufficient.

Author tests19/20/30 preserve narrower failures: dependent completed
functional-equation columns have zero Wronskian; a positive block Gram
gives a lower bound, not the desired upper bound; small mutual information
alone does not control bias, and the actual f3 radical statistic determines
the sign. Shifted columns, an exact F=TH+E bridge and a complete signed
conditional law remain possible.

All30 cards are retained, with six author tests02/15/19/20/30/06, three
developments02/15/06, four explicit duplicates03/05/09/27, and two critic
audits21/18. The eighteen other nonduplicate cards remain untested, not
disproved. The critic's full all30 priority and permutation pools preceded
outcomes. Author numerical pools include every eligible unreserved card
across groups; immutable draws were not rerolled.

The useful next step is a genuine signed bound for the projected source or
graph filling, or a changed Newton feedback preserving the zero signal.
None follows from compression, a generic summatory estimate or support alone.
title: [private research revision]: complete Gaussian compression and source-feedback obstructions

## G205: small cube cores with paid sixth-power punctures

Write `(Delta ell)=kappa t^3 z^6`, with kappa cubefree and t squarefree;
overlaps among these factors are allowed. The character identity contains

    chi_m(kappa)^eta chi_m(t)^3 1_((m,z)=1), eta in {+1,-1},

in addition to the retained fixed unit factor. The hole at z is necessary:
a prime of valuation six still forces zero when it divides m.
Fix kappa and z before averaging the squarefree t variable. The puncture
is part of the arbitrary inner sequence; it is not dropped after taking
a sixth power.

Set `B=(H_A/N(kappa))^(1/3)` and `T0=B/N(z)^2`.
[Goldmakher-Louvel, arXiv1112.1642v2, Definition1 and Theorem1.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1112.1642v2)
gives price `T0+X`. The literal PR9 B2.24 family supplies primitivity,
trivial infinite type, the fixed finite reciprocity classes and the
equal-class coprime product-conductor condition. Its local convention is
retained in the complete reports; this is not permission for an arbitrary
quadratic family.

The alternative original-color pointwise price is `T0 S0`.
Split z at a threshold Z clipped to `[1,sqrt(B)]`. The complete cost is
bounded by

    B + X Z + B S0/Z,

with the endpoint interpretations paid separately. If the formal optimum
is inside the interval, balance the latter two terms. If it lies below one,
use the pointwise bound throughout; if above sqrt(B), use the sieve
throughout and `X<S0`. In all regimes the resulting bound is

    B + sqrt(B S0 X).

Summing cubefree cores through C gives

    H_A^(1/3) C^(2/3) + sqrt(S0 X) H_A^(1/6) C^(5/6).

The two complete normalized prices are therefore

    U^(2/3+tau/3) A^-3 N0^(-1/3) N(f)^-1 C^(2/3),
    sqrt(S0) U^(5/6+tau/6) A^-4 N0^(-1/6) N(f)^(-3/2) C^(5/6).

Both independent f allocations are divisor bounded. The f^-1 sum has a
paid small-power allowance; the f^-2 and f^(-3/2) sums converge after a
sufficiently small divisor loss. All fixed S-parts, slots, heights, ray
classes and both full orientations are retained.
title: G205: small cube cores with paid sixth-power punctures

## 4. Both source coefficients fix the identity-cell readout

Put alpha=pi/|pi|, epsilon=(nu0/pi)_2, h=(nu0/pi)_4 and
g=conjugate(gamma4(pi)). Then h^2=epsilon and g^2=-alpha^-1.
For the identity ray, normalize the selected nonzero seed coefficient to1.
Fourth-power periodicity and the square relation give

    r_j := selected residue at nu0 pi^(2j) / selected seed
         = 1                            if j=2r,
           Q^(-1/4) h g                 if j=2r+1.       (2)

Each actual source coefficient contributes Q^(j/4) r_j after the fixed
archimedean Bessel factor is removed. The nonconjugated product, multiplied
by the REQUIRED angular and quadratic correction alpha^j epsilon^j, is

    B_j = alpha^j epsilon^j Q^(j/2) r_j^2
        = A^r                 if j=2r,
          -A^r                if j=2r+1,
    A=alpha^2 Q=chi2(p)Q.                              (3)

The odd sign uses BOTH copies of h and g: epsilon*h^2=1 and
alpha*g^2=-1. Replacing the pairing by a Hermitian one would lose this
identity. For other good rays, applying the supplied ell_[m] and U_[m]
before squaring gives the same (3); treating the two ray entries as two
independent spherical sources is unnecessary and incorrect.

Define the normalized radial arithmetic functional, initially absolutely
convergent for Re(s)>1/2 on bounded radial f supported in O, by

    J_s(f)=sum_(j>=0) B_j Q^(-js) f(pi^j).              (4)

It has the multiplicative integral form
integral_(O minus0) B_(v(x)) |x|^s f(x) d^*x.
This is an exact coefficient readout derived from the coupled sources.
It is not yet the full relative scattering operator or an all-vector norm.

One can also specify a trilinear H-functional in an explicit compatible local
cover convention, which the actual adelic realization must match. Let W1,W2
be the source Whittaker functions
for psi(c x), and let gamma_q(x) be the Weil torus scalar in

    omega(a(b))f(x)=gamma_q(b)|b|^(1/2) f(bx).

Use compatible torus sections with sigma4(x,b)^2=sigma2(x,b) and
gamma_q(xb)=gamma_q(x)gamma_q(b)sigma2(x,b). For an unramified character chi
define, wherever convergent,

    Lambda_(s,chi)(W1,W2,f)
      = integral_(F^*) W1(a(x)) W2(a(x)) gamma_q(x)
                        chi(x) f(x) |x|^(s-2) d^*x.    (5)

This formula includes the Weil scalar; omitting it leaves a quadratic
cocycle in the torus change of variables. The two upper-unipotent source
characters cancel psi(-c(x1+x2)x^2) from the kernel. For simultaneous
a(b), the displayed cocycle identities and x->x/b give

    Lambda(T_delta(b) v)
       = |b|^(5/2-s) chi(b)^(-1) Lambda(v).            (6)

Thus (5) is a concrete H-equivariant distribution in its initial domain under
the stated compatible-section convention. This calculation proves covariance;
it does not independently verify that convention against every source lift.
Its torus degree matches the required 5/2 arithmetic normalization. Equality
with the actual global physical period still requires the named unfolding.
Covariance alone does not identify a normalized orbital integral in every
flag chart.

The source normalization required to identify (5) with (4) is explicit.
With W_i(1)=1, the clean identity-ray spherical values are

    W_i(a(pi^j))=Q^(-3j/4) r_j, j>=0,
    W_i(a(pi^j))=0, j<0.                              (7)

Here the actual slot is f_1, so ell_1(r(nu0))=1. No analogous normalization
is silently imposed on the other global ray at this same seed: its selected
coefficient can vanish. Outside the clean identity-ray calculation one must
retain the actual two-state ray transport before comparing local values.

The exponent -3j/4 follows directly by moving the rational diagonal to the
archimedean chart: height becomes v/Q^j, while N(nu0 pi^(2j))^(1/8)
contributes Q^(j/4); the Bessel argument is unchanged. The bad-place
stabilizer restriction above is needed for this move. Negative j vanishes
by unramified upper-unipotent invariance, since c pi^(2j) is nonintegral.
Equivalently W_p(g) can be defined by applying the fixed global seed
Whittaker functional after a right p-translate; this does not assume a
generic multiplicity-one theorem for quartic Whittaker models.
Here the diagonal lift is fixed by that rational-move convention. Transporting
to another chosen torus section rephases the Whittaker factors and the Weil
factor together; it cannot be omitted when matching (7) with (8).

At odd good places gamma_q is1 on units. Unit factors from W1 W2 cancel
those in gamma_q. Because -1 is a square, gamma_q(pi^j)=gamma_q(pi)^j.
These assertions follow from the unramified quadratic Gauss-sum formula:
the unit Weil index is1, the quadratic Hilbert symbol (pi,pi)_2 equals
(-1/pi)_2=1, and the displayed cocycle identity then handles all integer j.
Choose the local character line

    chi(pi)=alpha*epsilon/gamma_q(pi), chi|O^*=1.       (8)

Substitution of (7)–(8) into (5) gives exactly (3)–(4): the factor
|pi^j|^(s-2) supplies Q^(2j)Q^(-js). Formula (8), not a bare declaration
of odd parity, fixes the local angular/seed orientation.

At infinity the actual kernel has angular weight+1 and the two quartic
vectors have weight0. Under convention (6) the character must therefore
have angular weight-1. The fixed finite ray data must supply the compatible
global idele-class character and cover trivialization. The retained source
does not record that full adelic identification. Equations (5)–(8) give
the exact local convention it must meet, not a new certificate for arbitrary
bad places or a factorization of the global period.

## 4. W43-06: source projection, complete Gram and calibration

Fix tau>0 and |a(n)|<=1. Write g_tau(u)=(2pi tau)^(-1/2)exp(-u^2/(2tau)), F_a(x)=sum_(n>=1)a(n)g_tau(log(n/x)), L=log X. For a prescribed A>0 take

    C=sqrt(2tau(A+2)),
    j_-=-ceil(C sqrt L), j_+=ceil(log2+C sqrt L)-1,
    m=ceil(2(A+2)L/log L).

Use every complete unit logarithmic bin I_j={n: j<=log(n/X)<j+1}, j_-<=j<=j_+, with the stated half-open endpoints. On each counting-measure sample set let P_j be orthogonal projection onto values of polynomials of degree<m in t=log(n/X)-j; if there are fewer points than m this means the whole value space. Set P_X to their direct sum. It acts on the actual coefficient list, not a continuum surrogate or random signs.

**Gaussian error.** Outside the retained interval, |log(n/x)| is at least C sqrt L for x in[X,2X]. Counting/summation bounds both tails by X^(1-C^2/(2tau)+o(1))=X^(-A-1+o(1)). The lower tail uses at most X exp(-C sqrt L) integers and the upper tail includes the e^v counting density. Rounding adds only bounded logarithmic shifts and does not consume the fixed power buffer.

For any real center c and complex |z|=R,

    |g_tau(c+z)| <= (2pi tau)^(-1/2) exp(R^2/(2tau)).

Indeed the negative square of the real part can be discarded and |Im z|<=R. Cauchy's coefficient bound and summation of the Taylor tail on0<=t<=1, with R=sqrt(tau m)>=2, give

    eps_m <= 2(2pi tau)^(-1/2) (e/(tau m))^(m/2).    (R43-P1)

There is no unpriced center-dependent exponential. The sampled Gaussian vector on each bin lies within sqrt(#I_j)eps_m of the polynomial space. Self-adjointness and ||a||_2<=sqrt(#N_X) therefore bound the complete pairing error by #N_X eps_m. Since #N_X<=2eX exp(C sqrt L), log eps_m=-(A+2)L+o(L), this is O(X^(-A)) for sufficiently large X. Finite-X diagnostics that miss the asymptotic target are not a contradiction and do not certify an explicit threshold.

Thus uniformly for x in[X,2X],

    F_a(x)=sum_(n in N_X)(P_Xa)(n)g_tau(log(n/x))
              +O_(A,tau)(X^(-A)),
    rank P_X=O_(A,tau)(L^(3/2)/log L).               (R43-P2)

The coefficient bound is on a, not on P_Xa pointwise. No such latter bound is needed. All discarded coefficients and both physical tails have been paid before using the projection.

Choose a real orthonormal basis q_alpha for the finite polynomial value space, c_alpha=sum_n a(n)q_alpha(n), V_alpha(x)=sum_n q_alpha(n)g_tau(log(n/x)), and K_(alpha,beta)=integral_X^(2X)V_alpha(x)V_beta(x)dx/x. Then exactly

    ||F_X^proj||_2^2=c* K c.                        (R43-P3)

Complex source coefficients are allowed; the real symmetric Gram and conjugation in c* retain every cross term. For fixed gamma>0, the full all-dyadic every-epsilon Gaussian exponent gamma is equivalent to the same exponent for(R43-P3), by the arbitrary-power error and the norm triangle inequality. Replacing K by its diagonal is not justified. A projection independently recomputed at each dyadic X is permitted for this approximation; it does not define one fixed Dirichlet series in X.

The readout operator has squared Hilbert-Schmidt norm at most(log2)/(2pi tau)#N_X=X^(1+o(1)). Hence

    E_X=||P_Xa||_2^2=sum_alpha |c_alpha|^2
          <<_epsilon X^(2gamma-1+epsilon)           (R43-P4)

is a sufficient input. It can be strictly stronger than the complete Gram condition because it discards favorable interference. E_X<=#N_X is the available generic bound and only returns gamma=1. At the present limiting gamma=.874864 the proposed energy exponent is .749728; a first gain needs a strict buffered reduction. At5/6 and3/4 these exponents are2/3 and1/2. They do not denote H's physical pressure deficit.

**Growing degree is paid.** For a polynomial of degree<m, equispaced Lagrange interpolation yields ||p'||_infinity<=D_m||p||_infinity with D_m=m(2e)^m. For d=m-1, the sum of reciprocal node-product denominators is d^d2^d/d!, and differentiating contributes at most d; d!>=(d/e)^d gives the displayed bound. The constant-polynomial case has derivative0. This proof applies to complex coefficients too.

A one-sided interval of length1/(2D_m) near a maximum has modulus at least half the maximum, proving sup|p|^2<=8D_m integral_0^1|p|^2. On a COMPLETE bin R<=n<eR, integration against floor(t)-t gives

    sum |p(log(n/R))|^2
     =R integral_0^1|p(t)|^2 e^t dt
         +O(sup|p|^2+Var(|p|^2)).                   (R43-P5)

The error is O(D_m^2) times the continuous squared norm. All bins have R>=X exp(-C sqrt L-1), whereas D_m^2=exp(O(m))=X^o(1). Therefore the discrete norm dominates half the R-weighted continuous norm uniformly for large X. A discrete unit basis vector satisfies sup|q|+Var(q)<=R^(-1/2)exp(O(m)). No uniform orthogonal-polynomial estimate was assumed without proof.

If A_a(t)=sum_(n<=t)a(n)=O(t^beta), beta>1/2 fixed, Abel summation with A_a(R-) and A_a(eR-) explicitly retained gives

    |sum_(R<=n<eR)a(n)q(log(n/R))|
        << R^(beta-1/2) exp(O(m)).

Summing squares over polylogarithmically many basis vectors yields E_X<<X^(2beta-1+o(1)). Both the lowest and highest R equal X^(1+o(1)), so this is uniform across the growing range. Arbitrarily short terminal bins would need another argument; the author's full-bin alignment avoids them. This establishes W43.6, not a better beta.

For actual f3, the inherited buffered Mobius bound implies the same summatory exponent for the filtered coefficient A from G2; G28 then gives f3=h*A with the paid weighted absolute h norm. It is important to preserve the prime2 filter rather than claim that the full f3 Euler product has a reciprocal absolutely convergent beyond1/2 without qualifications. The accepted G28/G29/G31 return applies to the full Gaussian field: its Mellin numerator contains1-2^(1-s), which has no zeros in gamma<Re(s)<1. Its zeros on Re(s)=1 must not be erased. The known right half-plane boundary and all-height fixed-field Mellin argument complete the relevant zero exclusion. For gamma>1/2 the conditional projected complete moment supplies this same return and no new one. W43 does not prove a Hecke-family or moving-conductor adapter.

The broad analytic-rank mechanism, optimized Taylor reasoning and need for complete contractions are inherited from W39-C01 and the Gaussian observation work. The useful added interface is a concrete finite source statistic with a paid physical readout and a no-loss baseline for growing degree. The first unpaid input is(R43-P3), or stronger(R43-P4). Rank reduction alone estimates neither.

### A. Exact inverse and exact norm

The inverse is

    C_rho(d,n)=1_(d|n) rho^(-k(n))(-lambda)^(k(n)-k(d)).           (A2)
    ||B_rho||_(l1->l1)=1,
    ||C_rho||_(l1->l1)=R_rho^K_X.                               (A3)

For d|n every intermediate e with d|e|n is still in D_X. Expanding (CB)(d,n) factors over the primes of n/d and gives (lambda-lambda)^k(n/d), with coefficient1 for d=n; the other product is the same binomial cancellation. Thus the cutoff causes no missing intermediate state. The absolute column sum of C at n is rho^(-k(n))(1+lambda)^k(n)=R_rho^k(n); taking a maximal-degree column proves equality, not merely an upper estimate.

Every squarefree integer with k primes is at least (k+1)!. Consequently

    K_X <= (1+o(1)) log X/loglog X,
    fixed rho>0: R_rho^K_X=X^o(1).                             (A4)

The factorial lower bound and integral estimate for log(k!) prove the needed upper bound without a prime theorem. This corrects a possible full-cube objection: exp(const*pi(X)) is the wrong inverse price on D_X. The number of sites may be enormous, but a surviving column occupies at most K_X sites.

For moving retention, log R_(rho_X)=o(loglog X) still suffices for subpower loss. If rho_X=(log X)^(-b), fixed b>0, then the norm is X^(b+o(1)). Here equality uses K_X~log X/loglog X, obtained from the ordinary prime number theorem and primorial products, with only finitely many q-primes removed. This is a genuine debit: such increasingly severe deletion cannot be called exponent-neutral. The PNT input is [NIST DLMF27.12](https://dlmf.nist.gov/27.12); no growing-q uniformity is used.

## G95. An exact source with a positive signed global leading term

Fix chi modulo q with its original zeros, and an integer r>=2 satisfying
chi(-1)=(-1)^r; r=2 for even and r=3 for odd characters suffice. Put

    a(n)=mu(n)chi(n),
    Phi(x)=sum_(k in Z,k!=0)chi(k)e(kx)/k^r,
    R_N(x)=2cos(2pi x)-sum_(n<=N)a(n)n^-r Phi(nx).

Absolute convergence and sum_(d|n)mu(d)=1_(n=1) give the exact full tail
R_N=sum_(n>N)a(n)n^-r Phi(nx). Its Fourier coefficients vanish through
|k|<=N, while for N<|k|<=2N they are mu(|k|)chi(k)/k^r. Natural zeros
and negative frequencies are included.

Writing g=(n,m), the complete-period Gram is

    <Phi(nx),Phi(mx)>
      =2L(2r,chi0)chi(m/g)conj(chi(n/g))g^(2r)/(nm)^r.

The phases cancel against a(n)conj(a(m)) only in this COMPLETE-PERIOD
formula, and only q-units survive. Let

    d_q=1/zeta(2) product_(p|q)p/(p+1),
    d(D)=1/zeta(2) product_(p|D)p/(p+1).

The elementary squarefree count is d(D)t+O(2^omega(D)sqrt(t)). With
n=gu,m=gv,(u,v)=1, it yields

    ||R_N||_2^2=C_r(q)N^(1-2r)+O_(q,r)(N^(1/2-2r)),
    C_r(q)=2L(2r,chi0)/(2r-1)
      sum_((u,v)=1,(uv,q)=1)
      mu(u)mu(v)d(uvq)min(u,v)^(2r-1)/(uv)^(2r).

Both main and error sums converge absolutely for r>=2. The region
min(u,v)>N costs O(N^(2-4r)); it is not passed through an invalid
large-divisor density estimate. Parseval on the actual first band proves

    C_r(q)>=2d_q(1-2^(1-2r))/(2r-1)>0.

Thus even the complete signed global norm has order N^(1-2r), independent
of the choice of chi at fixed q,r. Its half-power remainder cannot be used
as an upper bound on a restricted arc: subtracting a scalar main term
removes the required positive-measure comparison.

For fixed distinct positive scales lambda_j and any coefficients with
sum|b_j|^2=1, including N-dependent coefficients,

    ||sum_j b_j R_floor(lambda_j N)||_2^2 >= C N^(1-2r)

eventually. The earliest nonzero source has a Fourier band untouched by
later scales; squarefree density gives its positive mass. Compactness
of the fixed finite coefficient sphere makes the lower constant uniform.
The independent review further derives the real symmetric positive
definite limiting Gram matrix

    M_jk=2L(2r,chi0)/(2r-1)
      sum_((u,v)=1,(uv,q)=1)
      mu(u)mu(v)d(uvq)/(uv)^(2r)
      max(lambda_j/u,lambda_k/v)^(1-2r),

with scaled Gram error O(N^-1/2), including floor errors. There is no
uniform claim when the number of scales grows or their gaps close.

# [private research revision] controller reconstruction

The accepted endpoint remains c0=.125113352960035869... . This record
distinguishes proved source reductions, actual signed cancellation,
and the remaining full arithmetic bound. The completed independent
renewal review and the controller reconstruction below justify
mathematical admission of [private research revision]; no documentation or pilot activity
is counted as mathematics.

## W34: native support inside the actual separated source

I read the frozen W34 review in full and reconstructed the payment and
return. The reviewer stopped at41285 bytes, SHA256
d5136bb64fa0739d401756e00aaf73de98b4de7b6dd6bba6ffc620060412c1ed;
same-context recovery returned these identical bytes without a rewrite.
The two author artifacts have hashes
8a90b3c33b3249e8bd9e9963c33f52d1e8993838f0e5b2dcee30ba5a2dd56f5f
and cc0ff73deba7dd2c46c415104f8e3ea57ed81aed788b3597baafa910ac18be58.

The exact new contract is compatible native-output pruning inside both
the55-coordinate smooth selector and the three-diagonal product mask.
For L=logX,H=L/logL, take selected odd primes p<=floor(H/(16logH)).
Their square product q has log(8q)<=H/4 eventually, and their allocation
and inclusion-exclusion counts are X^o(1). Native coefficients vanish
when one selected p^2 divides n. They also vanish at8|n, but do not
vanish at4|n: the original2-adic coefficients are1,-3,2,0.

The original positive master k pays the odd-square projector. The
alternative fixed profile kappa=k'+k additionally pays8-divisibility.
Integration by parts gives M_kappa(s)=(1-s)M(s), so its density moment
M_kappa(1) vanishes while its ordinary mass remains1. This distinction
is essential. The profile and its zero-exclusion bridge are W21 reuse;
the new result is the actual current-mask intersection and even output
support, not discovery of the derivative architecture.

For each periodic restoration sequence, normalized finite Fourier
expansion and Poisson summation give one coefficient per frequency r/Q,
not an extra factorQ. The mean vanishes either by odd antiperiodicity
or by the profile's zero density moment. Explicit derivative constants
then give a nonzero-frequency bound proportional to
Q^h y^(1-h) h! exp((log2)h^2/2+O(h)). This pays the complete small-small
native-null field with fixed large h. On excluded product bins y>exp(H-1)
and Q<=exp(H/4), choosing h~3H/(4log2) instead gives
log error <= L-9H^2/(32log2)+O(HlogH+logL), rapidly decreasing in X.
An unspecified fixed-order smoothness bound would not justify that step.

The smooth-code intersection is paid independently. Fixing each factor's
canonical w-smooth part, w=(logB)^7.5, fixes every selected prime in the
restoration restriction. Inclusion-exclusion leaves centered prefix
discrepancy <=2^(m+1)=X^o(1), even when the two fixed parts share primes.
For kappa the constant-density term of this potentially nonzero-mean
sequence vanishes exactly. The first two logarithmic derivatives are
therefore also controlled. Two-dimensional Abel summation uses the actual
rough Mobius prefix bound and keeps faces, corners and lower cuts. The
original code's Rankin payment then saves delta_p=.00083. No signed
subfamily heredity, coprimality between factors or arbitrary mask was used.

The Boolean identity
1=(1-K)+EK+(1-E)K(1-P)+(1-E)KP
pays the entire removed field. The resulting norm error is q=.87407,
and its complete scalar error is2beta-delta_p=1.74897. The restoration
cap is the current SP cap2e^3 exp(2H), not the shorter [private research revision] cap.

Separate odd-prime allocations are0,D,E. Their restoration Euler factor
is product_(p assigned)(1-p^-s) product_(p unassigned)(1-p^-2s).
For the even profile fix a=v2(d),b=v2(e) in{0,1}; restoration has
v2(ell)<=j=2-a-b. Its factor is
[1-2^(1-s)+2^(-(j+1)s)]zeta(s), with its pole at1 killed by1-s.
The four ordered even allocations must retain their original signs.
This gives X^o(1) actual product components, without pretending their
positive moments capture the full signed local moment.

The reverse profile transfer is also valid at its precise scope.
F_kappa=F-xF', and F=x integral_x^infinity F_kappa(t)t^-2 dt uses
the accepted beta<1 boundary. Conversely every fixed logarithmic
derivative of the actual F is O_m(X^beta). Finite differences on a fixed
enlarged shell, with h=X^(-(beta-gamma)/m), upgrade an assumed full
F norm X^(gamma+epsilon) to its derivative with loss (beta-gamma)/m.
Choosing m first for each final epsilon proves full-field exponent
equivalence. It does not differentiate a changing mask, compare separate
component moments, or license shrinking-width profiles.

Accept W34 A/B at this scope. Keep C's sign-conjugacy obstruction narrow:
conjugacy-invariant spectra omit the observation vector, but coefficient-
aware spectral analysis remains possible; decorated H is outside it.
The audited inverse-energy and PSD candidates remain open/repairable,
not disproved actual-arithmetic claims. The stronger all-odd-square W31
route remains separate; its all-prime current product intersection is
still unpaid. The unchanged moment gap .2498-.24898=.00082 is explicit.

## Current synthesis decision

Retain the unmodified SP source as the leading common object while the
new renewal theorem is reviewed. Its developing joint signed estimate
uses that exact source. Preserve the W34 odd and even versions as fully
priced alternatives with explicit local Euler factors. Do not silently
attach the renewal asymptotic to either changed source. Changing a source
may invalidate its old component asymptotic even when its full-field
exponent contract remains equivalent.

The benefit to assess is real source compatibility and a usable signed
band estimate, not a percentage of the still-open full moment gap.

## Renewal proof: controller's independent calculation

The author froze900 lines,38808 bytes at
50887c3cb513de5016f10e61a308aa7e47dda7359259a8b68216fca9d36776ea.
I read the full statement, core lemma, original-source application,
Gram return and source/novelty discussion. The following reconstruction
supports the original claimed range; independent Astra review is still
in flight and any reviewer extension is a separate result.

Let ell=logL,m=logell,t=logz, with ell^2<=t<=L/(ell*m^2), and
truncate each squarefree z-smooth core at U=exp(L/m). On |s-1|<=1/t,
the logarithmic derivatives of the finite products
P_z(s)=product_(p<=z)(1-p^-s), H_z(s)=product_(p<=z)(1+p^-s)
have integral O(1), uniformly in z. Cauchy's inequality thus bounds
P_z^(k)(1) by C*p_z*k!*t^k for every k, not an unspecified C_k.
The same bound holds for H_z with h_z in place of p_z. Also
h_z/p_z=O(t^2). A positive exponential tilt controls all moment tails
and max(D,E)>U by exp(-logU/(2t)) after paying the polynomial.

For an analytic two-core density F(A,B) on one fixed bidisc, expand
through total degree K-1 with K=floor(r0*L/(16t)). Completing those
moments to the full finite Euler product preserves their signed
P_z^(r)(1)P_z^(s)(1) factors. The nonconstant terms sum to
O(p_z^2*t/L). Only the Taylor remainder and truncation use absolute
moments, costing relative
O(t^4*exp(-cL/t)+t^4*exp(-L/(2mt))). Both are smaller than every
fixed inverse power of L in the advertised range. There is no moving
PNT exponent or moving derivative order of the restoration profile.

For the original source, first pay SP8 with the literal original-pair
prefix mask, then sum the full restoration as K(v)=A_k(1/v). Its
integral is log2*M(1)>0 although K can change sign. Zero-large-prime
factors and cores exceeding U cost only X times a rapidly decreasing
logarithmic tail. On the retained cores the original prime lower cuts
are far above z, and every smooth-code floor is exactly0 for all
sufficiently large X. This is an actual support calculation, not a
norm restriction to a signed subfamily.

Two Stieltjes integrations with the fixed-order PNT, keeping both
strict lower boundaries, give the ordered prime-pair density
h_(u,v)(T)=(logT)^-1*log[((logT-logu)(logT-logv))/(logu*logv)].
There is no factor1/2 or removal of the p=q diagonal. Its expression
in A=logD/L,B=logE/L is uniformly analytic on a fixed bidisc.
The condition Z*r>uv is x*r>Y^2, independent of the cores; the omitted
tiny-r region is paid by the fixed profile's flatness. Applying the
signed core lemma before taking absolute values gives

P_z(x)=C_theta*p_z^2*x/L*[1+O(t/L)],
C_theta=2log(101/99)*log2*M(1)>0,

uniformly on the entire physical shell. The signed bands arise by
subtracting actual nested original-label masks. When t doubles the
leading field becomes1/4 of its prior value, so the intervening band
has coefficient-3/4 and a genuinely negative physical cross term.
This is substantially stronger than simply writing a renewal identity.

It still leaves a prefix of norm asymptotic to a positive constant
times X*ell^2*m^4/L^3. At the literal terminal threshold
z_end=sqrt(B/Y), at most one prime>z_end can occur in either original
factor, so P_z_end=R_sep exactly. The late flow to that endpoint is
unpaid. The theorem does not lower-bound R_sep or transfer itself to
the changed W34 fields.

The complete-field target can be expressed using actual norms m_z,n_z
and cosine rho_z: both |m_z-n_z|<=X^(gamma+epsilon) and
1+rho_z<=X^(2gamma-2+epsilon)*L^2*t^4 are necessary and sufficient.
The linear one-sided normalized cross error has exponent-.1251,
whereas symmetric/cosine errors have-.2502 at the baseline. The
.87449 target needs-.25102 for the cosine as well as the smaller
norm mismatch. Using the leading asymptotic in place of an actual norm
would lose this precision. Every original coefficient, both Mellin
heights and all Fourier-Gram interactions remain in this return.

## A useful derived grouping statement from the accepted RN theorem

The accepted RN theorem gives a concrete multiscale block hierarchy.
Take t_j=2^j*t0 within its proved range and B0=P_exp(t0),
Bj=P_exp(tj)-P_exp(t_(j-1)) for j>=1. These are disjoint original-label
blocks; their sum is the exact final prefix. Their number is
1+floor(log2(tmax/t0)), asymptotic to loglogX/log2 when t0=(loglogX)^2.
This counts these specified renewal bands, not every block in the
research program and not a fraction of the full arithmetic difficulty.

For the prefix vector set a_j=C_theta*p_exp(tj)^2*X/L and h(x)=x/X.
Uniform RN gives P_j=a_j*h+e_j with ||e_j||2<=C*a_j*tj/L. Since
a_j is uniformly comparable to a0*4^-j, summing the squared errors
gives ||(e_j)||_(ell2(L2))<=C*(t0/L)*||(a_j)||ell2. Consequently the
whole prefix Gram differs from K_J*a*a^* in operator norm by at most
C*(t0/L)*||a||ell2^2. Passing to the disjoint bands uses a difference
matrix of operator norm at most2 and retains the corresponding bound.
This is a proof consequence of RN, not a separately counted discovery.

It quantifies the joint signed interactions across O(loglogX) levels.
For the actual sum of all bands, use exact telescoping and the last
prefix estimate; the approximate-rank bound alone can have too large
an error. The hierarchy supplies logarithmic cancellation, and its
stopped remainder still has exponent1. It does not make the full
moment gap partly solved or turn a matrix approximation into a power
saving.

## Final review and the separately derived range extension

The reviewer completed full readback and STOP at37644 bytes,872 lines,
SHA256283a2e10dd07ae1406da2a57bbb8e583dab05efe20f4d13f98675738ba646425.
RN1–48 are accepted without repair. Earlier in-flight wording above
records the order of reconstruction; the final disposition controls.
No source was rewritten to match the review.

I separately checked Appendix E. With delta=10^-6,tau=10^-8,
Q=delta*L,U=X^delta and ell^2<=t<=tau*L/ell, the largest actual code
argument is at most .3749*delta/h0<.028. Thus every floor remains0,
even though the normalized core domain no longer tends to0.
The fixed complex bidisc of radius .01 contains that domain and
the prime-density logs stay away from0. The positive large-core
field costs XL*t^2*exp(-Q/t)<=XL^-97; zero-large-prime factors have
a much stronger fixed logarithmic decay. The normalized polynomial
completion error is t^4 exp(-Q/(2t))<=L^-46. Since
K>=.01L/(32t), the Taylor remainder is <=CL^-31246.
The fixed PNT and profile errors are <=XL^-4, below the allowed
X/(L^2*t); only the signed nonconstant moments contribute the
displayed O(t/L) relative error. All constants are fixed before X.
This proves the reviewer extension at its own scope.

The largest admitted prefix now has size comparable to
tau^-2 X*(loglogX)^2/(logX)^3, without the author's extra
(logloglogX)^4 factor. The extension is eventually stronger, not a
practical finite-height estimate. It does not reach z=X^rho for any
fixed rho>0 and does not produce a power saving. The hierarchy and
Gram consequence above use this extended tmax as well.

## Cycle admission and next mathematical decision

Before this cycle the complete core/restoration asymptotic was known
at the older polylogarithmic roughness cutoff and the renewal bridge
was an exact unestimated identity. RN now estimates actual complete
signed bands of the current SP source uniformly for a growing
roughness range, including their negative main term and physical
cross interaction. The finite-Euler argument preserves signed
moments before pricing its remainder; an absolute first-order
Taylor estimate cannot prove this range. This is substantive
arithmetic progress on the joint grouping problem, not a renamed
target. W34 independently removes selected native-null output
classes inside both current masks and supplies an exact full-field
profile transfer.

The main proof keeps SP and its new RN hierarchy together. W34 is
a priced alternative, not a free transfer of RN. The [private research revision]
stronger error and shorter restoration remain available.
Potential for RN is assessed as moderate, with high confidence in
its scope and low confidence in extrapolating a power improvement.
The strongest objection is decisive: even the last proved prefix
has exponent1, and norm estimates of separate late blocks lose
the required cancellation. The next test is a global signed-core
or prime-renewal estimate across the late flow, retaining the
actual code boundary and shared-prime subtraction. A fixed-power
threshold needs genuinely new control, not substitution into RN.
W35 and the direct original-prime H attack remain independent
routes to new mechanisms while this is pursued.

The exact full moment gap remains .00082 and verified c gain0.
There is no defensible fraction of all arithmetic cases solved.
The proved block count and range are useful raw measurements;
they do not normalize into a percentage of endpoint progress.
