### 4.3 Paying the small-prime complement

Fix A>1 and let Y_N=(log(2N))^A. After removing the short singleton fibers, consider active fibers with p<=Y_N. Every associated d=pu is squarefree and has P^+(d)=p<=Y_N. Thus the absolute coefficient mass of their whole contribution is bounded by

    Psi_sf(N,Y_N)=#{d<=N:d squarefree,P^+(d)<=Y_N}.

For any0<sigma<1, the finite Euler product gives

    Psi_sf(N,Y) <= N^sigma product_(p<=Y)(1+p^-sigma)
       <= N^sigma exp(1+Y^(1-sigma)/(1-sigma)).                (W12)

This is just Rankin's inequality and comparison with the integer sum. Choose sigma>1-1/A. Since A(1-sigma)<1, the exponential in W12 is N^o(1). Hence, for every epsilon>0,

    Psi_sf(N,Y_N) <<_(A,epsilon) N^(1-1/A+epsilon).             (W13)

There is no assertion of a small finite-N constant, and no estimate of cancellation inside this sector. The logarithmic cutoff is frozen at the root N in every term of this partition. The exact finite price W12 remains available if the asymptotic threshold is too large.

## 2. Three different conductors and the actual linear field

Retain exactly
\[
Q=q_{b_*}XY,\quad P_a=Y^2/Q,\quad
Y_D=Y/q_D,\quad Q_D=Q/q_D^2,\quad
L=\prod_iP_i,\quad L_D=P_{\mathcal J^c},\quad N_D=ZL_D.
\tag{XM1}
\]
Here \(D\) is the original product in the embedded slot subset \(\mathcal J\); \(q_D\asymp P_{\mathcal J}\), with constants depending only on the fixed slot supports. The ideal \(J\) below is a cube label, not this slot subset. The fixed factor \(q_{b_*}\) is never set to one.

For a source \(s\) and one completed index \(A=IJ^3\), with \(I\) squarefree, define
\[
\mathfrak h(s,A)=
\prod_{\substack{p\notin S\\v_p(A)-v_p(s)\not\equiv0\ (6)}}p,
\qquad h_{\rm act}(s,A)=q_{\mathfrak h(s,A)}.
\tag{XM2}
\]
It is the active conductor of a single mixed row, on its surviving local support. It is not the hybrid norm hypothesis \(\mathcal H\). It is also not PC's relative conductor
\[
R=q_{\prod_{\ell_p\ne0}p},\qquad
\ell_p=v_p(A)-v_p(A')-v_p(a)+v_p(b)\pmod6,
\tag{XM3}
\]
which occurs after multiplying two completed fields and their two outer Gauss factors.

Let \(x_s=q_s/Y\). The exact additive coefficient in T06.2 obeys
\[
Y^{-1}x_s^{-1/2}q_s^{-1/2}
=Y^{-3/2}x_s^{-1}.
\tag{XM4}
\]
Mellin inversion of the original \(W_0(q_m/(Qx_s))\) therefore produces the source polynomial
\[
\mathcal A_{\sigma,v}(m;Y)
=Y^{-3/2}\sum_{s\in\sigma}
c_\sigma(s)W_1(x_s)x_s^{-1+iv}g_s(-m).
\tag{XM5}
\]
Here \(g_s\) is the unnormalized source Gauss sum and \(c_\sigma\) retains exactly \(\chi_s(b_*)/(\tau\xi(s))\) and the row-independent finite phases. In particular it is bounded uniformly in \(s\). Any further finite sector index, including the completed ray \(t\) in T06.2, is suppressed in this notation. Its source phase \(R(t,s)\) and the corresponding constraint on the completed labels are both retained. Splitting the source into its finitely many rays makes this a finite sum of the displayed products; the subsequent bounds discard a ray restriction only after taking a positive majorant.

Because \(W_0,W_1\) have fixed positive-annulus supports, choose one smooth compact cutoff \(\Omega\) in a positive annulus, equal to one on all their possible physical-row products. Then the row function is exactly
\[
f_v(z)=\Omega(|z|^2)|z|^{-2iv}.
\tag{XM6}
\]
It has fixed-order Schwartz seminorms bounded by a polynomial in \(1+|v|\). The cutoff does not alter the physical sum.

The completed coefficient in our original field is
\[
\frac{\lambda(I,J)}{\sqrt{q_I}\,q_J}K_D(IJ^3),
\qquad |\lambda(I,J)|\ll_S1.
\tag{XM7}
\]
There is no additional power of a complementary marked product in \(K_D\). In the external window convention, for \(x=q_A/T\),
\[
\frac{q_J^{1/2}}{T^{1/2}}W(x)
=\frac{x^{1/2}W(x)}{\sqrt{q_I}\,q_J}.
\tag{XM8}
\]
Thus our completed profile on a \(q_A\asymp T\) dyad corresponds to \(W(x)=x^{-1/2}\) times that original dyadic profile. Since \(x\) stays in a fixed annulus, this is an exact change of window with bounded seminorms, not a lost coefficient or a change of the detector.

Every branch of the compensated probe is consequently a finite sum over the original ray sectors of
\[
(-1)^{|\mathcal J|}\omega_Dq_D^{-3/2}Q_D^{-1/2}
\int_{\mathbb R}\widehat W_0(iv)\,
\mathcal M_D(v)\,\frac{dv}{2\pi},
\tag{XM9}
\]
where \(\mathcal M_D\) is the raw row sum of (XM5), the completed coefficients (XM7), and \(\xi(m)f_v(m/\sqrt{Q_D})\). The element embedding \(m'=D^2m\) is injective. It introduces no density or Jacobian in this discrete linear sum.

## G201. Exact native carrier spectrum, with normalized stencil cost

Use the literal Eisenstein [JN source](../[private research revision]/h-joint/report.md), not
an ordinary integer surrogate. Freeze the original long-prime pair of
distinct degree-one rational norms p,r, with Q=pr and phi=(p-1)(r-1).
The complete finite group has Q^2 elements and unitary Fourier factor 1/Q.
The row multiplier is m(h)=ell_p(h_p)ell_r(h_r), with quadratic characters
zero at zero. The mark factors vanish off exactly phi mark pairs and have
modulus one on them. The complete coefficient includes the original
b0=b(pi)conjugate(b(pi'))zeta_CRT, which may vanish.

For translation S_t f(h)=f(h+t), the row commutator is

    D_t=diag(m(h)-m(h+t)) S_t.

When t is nonzero in both residue fields, local autocorrelation is -1.
Indeed z^2=y(y+1) is equivalent, by an invertible change of variables over
an odd field, to (2y+1-2z)(2y+1+2z)=1. Counting its p-1 solutions proves
the local identity including the zero sites. CRT gives correlation 1.
There are B=(p-2)(r-2) positions where both row values are nonzero, two
where both vanish, and n1=2(p+r-3) where exactly one vanishes. Thus

    singular value 2: multiplicity n2=(B-1)/2;
    singular value 1: multiplicity n1;
    rank D_t=(Q+2p+2r-9)/2;
    ||D_t||_HS^2=2(phi-1),  ||D_t||_op=2.

For a shift nonzero only at p, replace these multiplicities by
n2=(p-1)(r-1)/2 and n1=2(r-1); the other case is symmetric. The full
carrier repeats each nonzero row singular value phi times and scales
it by |b0|. Unitary Fourier conjugation introduces no further saving.
For rank k<=n2 approximation the squared row Hilbert-Schmidt error is
at least 4(n2-k)+n1, and for k<n2 the operator error is at least 2.

Let P=sum c_j S_j for k distinct integer shifts 0<j<min(p,r). Distinct
matrix diagonals cannot cancel in Hilbert-Schmidt norm, so

    ||[M_m,P]||_HS^2=2(phi-1)||c||_2^2,
    sqrt(2(phi-1)/Q)||c||_2 <= ||[M_m,P]||_op
                             <=2 sqrt(k)||c||_2,
    rank[M_m,P] >= (phi-1)/(2k),  c!=0.

The lower operator bound uses rank<=Q. Moving coefficients require the
displayed normalization: c_1=Q^(-10) defeats the author's unnormalized
prose claim. The correct cost is relative to |b0| ||c||_2, or for stencils
whose normalized size does not vanish. The immutable author report is
retained with this explicit superseding correction.

These are ambient carrier facts. They do not identify the carrier with
the physical mark matrix, make the actual folded W an extremizer, or
bound its signed pairing below. All original projectors, ordered short
pairs including equality, complex gcd core, masks, roots, independent
heights and natural zeros remain. The raw H target is still

    Z^epsilon G K [N+L+(NL)^(2/3)] sqrt(Omega1 Omega2) P_orig,

followed by N^(-1)G^(-2) exactly once. None of the .004 full-H deficit is
paid. A source-specific recurrence and its complete observation/residual
estimate remain legitimate targets.

statement:
# W55: moving Riesz normalization, residue-class matching, and a signed renewal test

This batch proves quantitative representation statements and preserves precise failures. It proves no new bound for the complete arithmetic observable and no larger zero-free constant. The accepted written source-relative boundary remains theta11=.8748540364, c11=.1251459636; its inherited analytic/positive-slot/external-definition obligations remain open. No formalization, prover-kernel work or new proof packet was undertaken.

The most useful candidate increment is A: a complete second-order comparison of a finite signed combination of growing-order Riesz means with one fixed exponential detector. It includes a uniform constant, the infinite tail, all ordinary characters and the exact scale conversion. B records the converse as well as the forward direction of an ordinary-character rank-matching criterion; it is a refinement within known transport ancestry. C is the protected random rare development: the complete logarithmic renewal identity and its failed positive contraction estimate. Neither a representation nor a finite experiment supplies arithmetic cancellation.

## 1. Frozen generation and selection

Thirty seeds in six groups of five were saved, completely read back and hashed before reading creative-lane, current-proof, the index or detailed ancestry. `seeds.json` is 21,231 bytes, SHA256 `01d6ec8b37aa8b767e6c01689d015a742bbe73b5f2cfa1764650a84dad6f7eed`. Seed writes then stopped. All30 remained eligible: an incomplete bridge, known ancestor or inaccurate candidate identity was a question for testing, not an exclusion. The literal fractions are subjective generation typicalities, not truth or novelty probabilities.

Deliberate strongest bridges: S03 and S24. The all-group p<.10 pool had23 candidates; fresh OS byte12 selected zero-based12=S19. The remaining p<.01 pool had12 candidates; byte205 selected index1=S10. S14 was reserved as the most different remaining mechanism. The remaining wildcard pool had25 candidates; byte16 selected index16=S21. Every pool was frozen and fully read before its own entropy call. The saved rejection rule gives an exactly uniform index; no rejection or outcome reroll occurred. The six tests are therefore S03,S24,S19,S10,S14,S21. Three developments only: A/S03, B/S24, C/S10. C received a complete hard/upstream calculation; the wildcard's first decisive source calculation recovered a known barrier and is retained below.

## 2. A/S03: a fully paid moving-order Riesz return

### A1. Fixed detector and the seed's unnecessary desmoothing loss

For a fixed ordinary Dirichlet character chi modulo q, including q=1, put a(n)=mu(n)chi(n), with chi zero on nonunits. Define

    M_chi(t)=sum_(n<=t) a(n),
    E_chi(x)=sum_(n>=1) a(n) exp(-n/x),       x>0,
    R_r(N)=sum_(n<=N) a(n)(1-n/N)^r,         r>0.

The endpoint n=N has weight0. These are the full coefficients, without a favourable sector or hidden coprimality change. Absolute Fubini for Re(s)>1 gives

    int_0^infty E_chi(x)x^(-s) dx/x = Gamma(s)/L(s,chi),
    int_0^infty R_r(N)N^(-s) dN/N
        = Gamma(s)Gamma(r+1)/[Gamma(s+r+1)L(s,chi)].       (A1)

For fixed r the multiplier in the second line is nonzero when Re(s)>0. Thus an every-dyadic L2(dx/x) exponent gamma>0 for either fixed field directly excludes zeros in Re(s)>gamma. Sharp recovery of M_chi is unnecessary. This is standard Mellin/Riesz ancestry, including [restricted research revision]-C1 and Sol04-D12, not new detector credit. The Beta integral and nonvanishing of Gamma are recorded in [DLMF5.12](https://dlmf.nist.gov/5.12) and [DLMF5.2](https://dlmf.nist.gov/5.2); the coefficient identities above are derived here by n/x substitution.

For completeness, if ||E_chi||_[X,2X] <<_(chi,epsilon) X^(gamma+epsilon) on every sufficiently large dyadic X, Cauchy-Schwarz and dyadic summation make its Mellin integral holomorphic for Re(s)>gamma, with all logarithmic derivatives. Near0 the absolute geometric sum is O(exp(-1/x)). Identity continuation gives L(s,chi)H(s)=Gamma(s). At an L-zero in that half-plane the left side vanishes and the right side does not. The pole of a principal L at1 is treated meromorphically; it is not a zero. This proof treats every fixed character separately, with constants allowed to depend on q and chi, and makes no growing-conductor assertion.

The open issue becomes quantitative when r grows: (A1) is not the Mellin transform of a field whose r varies with the physical shell. The following comparison restores a single fixed field first.

### A2. Uniform first- and second-order comparison

Suppose, as an explicit input, |M_chi(t)|<=C_chi t^beta for all t>0, where beta>0. Taking beta=1,C_chi=1 is unconditional. A stronger buffered summatory bound may be substituted only if its own source contract is available; it is not inferred here merely from the number c11.

For real r>=2 define

    k_r(u)=(1-u/r)_+^r,
    B_r(x)=R_r(rx)=sum_n a(n) k_r(n/x),
    V_r(x)=2B_(2r)(x)-B_r(x),
    A(u)=u-u^2/2,
    K1(beta)=5*2^(beta+2)Gamma(beta+2)+2^(beta+3)Gamma(beta+3),
    K2(beta)=12*2^(beta+3)Gamma(beta+3)
             +4*2^(beta+4)Gamma(beta+4)+2^(beta+5)Gamma(beta+5).

Then, uniformly in all x>0 and r>=2,

    |B_r(x)-E_chi(x)| <= C_chi K1(beta) x^beta/r,
    |V_r(x)-E_chi(x)| <= (3/2)C_chi K2(beta) x^beta/r^2.  (A2)

No coefficient tail, moving-order constant, last integer or second branch has been suppressed. V_r includes the support out to2rx and both ordered cross terms in any squared norm. Its literal coefficient weight is2(1-n/(2rx))_+^(2r)-(1-n/(rx))_+^r.

Proof. For0<u<r, k_r'(u)=-(1-u/r)^(r-1); for u>r it is0. The function is continuous and absolutely continuous, and for r>=2 its derivative also matches0 at r. On0<=u<=r/2 let

    z_r(u)=(r-1)log(1-u/r)+u.

The log series gives z_r<=u/r,

    |z_r| <= (u+u^2)/r,
    |z_r-A(u)/r| <= (u^2/2+2u^3/3)/r^2.                (A3)

Indeed the terms of order>=3 have absolute sum at most
(r-1)(u/r)^3/[3(1-u/r)] <=2u^3/(3r^2). Using
|exp(z)-1-z|<=(z^2/2)exp(max(z,0)) proves

    |k_r'(u)+exp(-u)| <=(5u+u^2)exp(-u/2)/r,
    |k_r'(u)+exp(-u)[1+A(u)/r]|
                       <=P(u)exp(-u/2)/r^2,             (A4)
    P(u)=12u^2+4u^3+u^4.

Here the first inequality on the short range even holds with u+u^2. For u>=r/2 use |k_r'|<=exp(-u/2) on its support and0 outside, and r<=2u. After multiplying the proposed second inequality by r^2, the two constant terms cost at most8u^2, the u/r term at most2u^2 and the u^2/(2r) term at mostu^3. This is bounded by P(u). The first inequality follows there from2<=4u/r. Thus (A4) holds on the entire positive half-line, including the part beyond the finite support.

Abel/Stieltjes integration, with vanishing endpoint terms, gives

    sum_n a(n)h(n/x)=-int_0^infty M_chi(xu)h'(u)du.       (A5)

Apply (A4) to h=k_r-exp(-u), then integrate u^beta times its bound. For the second line write k_r'=-exp(-u)[1+A(u)/r]+e_r; the A/r terms cancel exactly in2k_(2r)'-k_r'+exp(-u). The complete remainder is at most(2/4+1)P exp(-u/2)/r^2. Its integral is(3/2)K2(beta)/r^2. This proves (A2), including the infinite exponential tail. Constants are deliberately coarse and explicit; their finiteness and uniformity matter more than their size.

### A3. Complete return and the actual scale budget

Fix delta>0. On each dyadic shell[X,2X], freeze one common

    r_X=max(2,ceil(X^delta)),   V_X(x)=V_(r_X)(x).

The complete approximation error is O_(chi,beta)(X^(beta-2delta)) pointwise and in shell L2. Consequently, for any gamma>0 with beta-2delta<=gamma, the every-epsilon shell bounds of exponent gamma for V_X and E_chi are equivalent. Use a strict inequality when a fixed power margin is desired. Only after this comparison is the fixed E Mellin transform used. With beta=1 this return needs no inherited cancellation at all.

| Prospective gamma | Prospective c | delta using only |a|<=1 | Complete error exponent |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| .87485 | .12515 | .063 | .874 |
| 5/6 | 1/6 | .084 | .832 |
| 3/4 | 1/4 | .126 | .748 |

These are conditional targets, not proved improvements. All signed V_X moments remain open. For an independently supplied beta=.874855, delta=.000003,.021,.063 would instead give error exponents .874849,.832855,.748855. That optional buffer is explicitly an extra input to this version of A2.

The largest raw cutoff on[X,2X] is4r_X X, of orderX^(1+delta). A raw-cutoff power bound R_r(N)=O(N^eta) corresponds to effective-scale exponent(1+delta)eta, not eta. In particular the unconditional positive bound

    |B_r(x)| <= sum_(n<=rx)(1-n/(rx))^r <=rx/(r+1)<=x

uses the decreasing integral test. It remains exponent1 at the effective scale. V_r costs at most3x by this method. The apparent saving from enlarging r is entirely a change of observed scale. This is a complete coarse estimate on the actual coefficients; it fails to beat the target and rules out the intended free smoothing gain.

The fixed signed extrapolation order2 is essential to the proved constant. No growing extrapolation order, asymptotic Gamma-ratio uniformity in moving height, Gaussian inverse or implicit convergence of changing Mellin transforms is claimed. The complete moment of V_X contains all interactions between both Riesz branches; bounding one favourable piece is insufficient. A is a source-exact refinement of smoothing/restoration ancestry, not literature priority or arithmetic-gap credit.

In particular no nonvanishing claim is made for the Mellin multiplier of a fixed V_r: a difference of two Gamma quotients need not inherit their separate nonvanishing. The moving V_X estimate reaches the fixed E by the explicit error before any zero argument. This resolves that numerator objection without assuming a new Euler identity.

## 3. B/S24: a complete residue-class rank-matching criterion

Fix q. For each reduced residue a mod q, list in increasing order

    u_(a,k): integers n==a mod q with mu(n)=+1,
    v_(a,k): integers n==a mod q with mu(n)=-1.

Zero Mobius values and nonunits are omitted from the lists, but their zero extensions are retained in every arithmetic sum. For fixed1/2<gamma<1 the following three statements are equivalent, with constants allowed to depend on q and gamma:

1. For every ordinary character chi mod q, M_chi(x)=O(x^gamma).
2. For every reduced residue a, M_(q,a)(x)=sum_(n<=x,n==a(q))mu(n)=O(x^gamma).
3. Both lists are infinite and their monotone rank matching satisfies |u_(a,k)-v_(a,k)|=O(k^gamma) for every a and all k.       (B1)

The equivalence also holds with the usual every-positive-epsilon loss. Thus a proof of the displacement bound with gamma<theta11 for every fixed q would imply the requested ordinary-character zero exclusion, while the q=1 case includes zeta. This is a direct summatory criterion; it makes no assertion that a short finite matching proves an asymptotic bound.

Proof of1<->2. The exact finite character Fourier identities are

    M_chi=sum_(a reduced)chi(a)M_(q,a),
    M_(q,a)=(1/phi(q))sum_(chi mod q)conj(chi(a))M_chi.

They retain principal, imprimitive and complex characters. This direction requires all characters of one fixed q, not one chosen nonreal character alone.

For2->3, the squarefree count in a reduced residue obeys the elementary formula

    Q_(q,a)(x)=d_q x+O_q(sqrt x),
    d_q=[q*zeta(2)]^(-1) product_(p|q)(1-p^-2)^(-1)>0.   (B2)

Indeed use mu(n)^2=sum_(d^2|n)mu(d). Since a is a unit, only(d,q)=1 contributes; each progression m==a*d^(-2) mod q has count x/(q d^2)+O(1). Summing at mostsqrt x errors and completing the absolutely convergent d^-2 tail proves (B2). Therefore the positive and negative counting functions equal d_q x/2+O_q(x^gamma). Inverting these monotone counting functions gives

    u_(a,k)=2k/d_q+O_q(k^gamma),
    v_(a,k)=2k/d_q+O_q(k^gamma),

and both sequences are infinite. This establishes3 with every endpoint accounted for.

For3->2, pair every u_(a,k) with v_(a,k). At cutoff x the difference of counts is exactly the signed number of pairs crossing x. A crossing pair has k<=x because its lower endpoint is an increasing positive-integer sequence. Its length is at mostC_q x^gamma, so its lower endpoint lies in(x-C_q x^gamma,x]. Distinct pairs have distinct lower endpoints. There are at mostC_q x^gamma+1 integers in this interval, proving2. No infinite series is rearranged: the two counts at each x are finite.

An exact check on the forward reasoning: if u_k<v_k within one residue, then

    Q(v_k)-Q(u_k)=M(v_k)+M(u_k),                         (B3)

because P(u_k)=k and N(v_k)=k. Both terms on the right are nonnegative. The reversed orientation has the corresponding negative signs. Thus the geometric gap is paid by the actual signed discrepancy plus the O(sqrt x) squarefree-density remainder. It is not controlled by density alone.

For a finite cutoff N, the algorithm pairs ranks only through min(P_a(N),N_a(N)); its unpaired count is exactly |M_(q,a)(N)|. Dropping those end ranks would delete precisely the arithmetic quantity needing control. Within two finite equal-sized ordered lists, monotone matching minimizes the largest edge length: uncrossing two reversed pairs cannot increase the larger distance. This elementary fact does not give a new bound on the resulting arithmetic distance.

Contact and novelty: G65 already derives monotone matching costs from an inherited summatory exponent for a Gaussian feature metric, with full ghost mass. W22 already prices ordinary-Mobius transport and its total-mass debt; G76/G94 explain why prime-toggle matchings leave a linear unsigned boundary. B supplies a clean two-sided l-infinity criterion simultaneously for all ordinary characters of a fixed q, with a self-contained squarefree-progression proof. It does not improve the previous cost or claim a new matching theorem in the literature. The next mathematical input is an actual uniform power saving for these rank displacements, or a different globally coherent pairing with a proved comparable crossing bound.

## 4. C/S10: protected rare signed renewal development

This test keeps the actual global prime law rather than an independent-jump model. Let Lambda be von Mangoldt and use Dirichlet convolution. Differentiating the absolutely convergent reciprocal Euler series in Re(s)>1 gives the coefficient identity

    (a log)(n)=-(a*(Lambda chi))(n).                     (C1)

It also follows directly from the prime-power divisor identity, so every prime power, natural zero and endpoint is present. Set

    R_chi(x)=sum_(d<=x)Lambda(d)chi(d)M_chi(x/d).

Finite summation and Abel integration give exactly

    M_chi(x)log x = int_1^x M_chi(t)dt/t - R_chi(x),
    M_chi(x)=1-R_chi(x)/log x
                  -int_2^x R_chi(t)dt/[t(log t)^2], x>=2. (C2)

The second formula uses R_chi(2-)=0 and a(1)=1. In particular a complete bound R_chi(x)=O(x^gamma log x), gamma>0, gives M_chi(x)=O(x^gamma). Conversely M_chi(x)=O(x^gamma) gives that R bound by the first formula. These statements remain equivalent with every-epsilon losses. Thus the exact signed renewal input is explicit and returns the same exponent, but it is not intrinsically weaker than the original problem.

The attempted positive contraction fails on the full source. On the weighted space |M(x)|<=x^gamma, the absolute discrete renewal kernel has mass

    sum_(d>=2)Lambda(d)|chi(d)|d^(-gamma),                (C3)

which is infinite for gamma<=1. At gamma=1 this follows elementarily from

    sum_(d<=X)Lambda(d)floor(X/d)=log(floor X!),
    sum_(d<=X)Lambda(d)/d >= log(floor X!)/X -> infinity.

Removing the finitely many prime-power rays dividing q changes the gamma=1 sum by a finite amount; for0<gamma<1 the weights are larger. No stochastic minorization exists after pretending this infinite signed measure is a probability distribution. Dividing the finite Volterra equation by log x does not supply a fixed subunit norm: the gamma=1 lower ratio approaches1, and the known positive prime-density asymptotic makes the gamma<1 ratio grow. The infinite-mass result alone suffices to reject a scale-independent absolute-kernel small-gain certificate.

A deliberately coarse complete estimate is |R_chi(x)|<=sum_(n<=x)log n<=x log x, using its exact value -sum a(n)log n. It returns only exponent1. Replacing M by an inherited exponent beta on the right of the first C2 does not bootstrap, because the signed correlation still needs new control. On the other hand the true signs in R can cancel; (C3) is not a lower bound for R or M. The viable residual is a complete signed prime-power/Mobius correlation estimate, including all d and every covariance if squared. This is renewal/Dirichlet-inverse ancestry (G78/G81/G92/G112), not a new arithmetic theorem or an impossibility result for signed renewal.

This is the promised hard/upstream/high-ceiling attempt before settling on the easier A and B refinements. It actually reaches the native arithmetic convolution and computes its full positive budget. It fails to supply the required cancellation, and that failure is retained without a replacement random draw.

## 5. The other three selected first tests

**S19: finite-memory inverse.** For a fixed finite prime cutoff Y the exact omitted-prime inverse defect has coefficients -chi(n) on n>1 with least prime factor>Y, and0 elsewhere. Its absolute Dirichlet norm diverges at every positive sigma<=1, already on the prime subsequence. This is the existing [restricted research revision]-W4/G78 boundary, not a new negative result. A small-gain proof cannot use the trivial infinite tail below1. G78 supplies the legitimate alternative: work at b>1, retain the exact growing inverse depth and pay its full physical tail before returning to the fixed field. That repair does not estimate the resulting signed arithmetic field. No fourth development or outcome-driven redraw was made.

**S14: phase-adapted Lyapunov metric.** The first test is deliberately a two-channel diagnostic, not a replacement for actual H. For

    A_rho=[[rho,1],[0,rho]], 0<rho<1, d=1-rho^2,
    P=[[1/d,rho/d^2],[rho/d^2,1/d+(1+rho^2)/d^3]],

direct summation of (A^k)*A^k gives P-A*PA=I. As rho tends to1,
lambda_max(P) is of order d^-3, lambda_min(P) of order d^-1, and the metric's Euclidean conversion costs sqrt(condition number) of order d^-1. Moreover the generic contraction certified by this equation is only sqrt(1-1/lambda_max(P)). At rho=1 an eigenvector with eigenvalue1 makes strict contraction in any positive metric impossible. This confirms the seed's strongest objection quantitatively: a near-resonant metric can absorb the entire prospective power gain through conditioning and a weak contraction rate. The actual source-dependent H transfer and a uniformly conditioned metric remain unbuilt. This diagnostic neither proves nor disproves a native H estimate; no phase, projector or mask is altered or claimed bounded.

**S21: squarefree-complex contraction, wildcard.** The product-cutoff prime-subset family really is a simplicial complex: every divisor is smaller. The seed's phrase suggesting failure to be a subcomplex was inaccurate and is corrected here; the failure is that the contracting homotopy and character weighting do not commute with the cutoff/readout.

For an unramified prime p define

    T_(p,chi)(x)=sum_(n<=x,p not dividing n)mu(n)chi(n).

The exact two-part decomposition is

    M_chi(x)=T_(p,chi)(x)-chi(p)T_(p,chi)(x/p)
      =sum_(x/p<n<=x,p not dividing n)mu(n)chi(n)
                          +(1-chi(p))T_(p,chi)(x/p).     (T21)

For q=1,p=2 only the boundary remains, precisely the classical squarefree-complex representation. For the quartic character mod5 with chi(2)=i and x=2, the whole value is1-i; the purported pure boundary is0 and the omitted bulk is1-i. The full character defect cannot be discarded. For chi(p)=1, a first-prime never-revisit matching leaves the familiar linear unsigned boundary; G94 already proves its asymptotic. For q=1,p=2, its size is(2/pi^2)x+O(sqrt x), while its signed sum is exactly M(x).

[Bjorner's primary paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/1101.5704), equations1.1-1.2 and Theorem3.1, identifies this complex's reduced Euler characteristic and its Betti basis. The source was checked directly. These are classical statements and already credited in W27/A-SIMPLICIAL; no new topology theorem is claimed. A refined matching that revisits vertices or mixes nearby products could still matter, but it needs the actual signed crossing estimate in B or a comparably complete alternative. The first test fails as a source of free rank savings; the viable general matching direction is retained, not rerolled into a new candidate.

A late closeout read also found the same character/chain-map correction in W54 critic audit X30, already frozen before this report. Its review SHA256 is `e5e6f8ccfec3150f3586233f2b499d18a15f8fd8c7130541551fe3f264efa1c0`. This reinforces the duplicate disposition; S21 receives no new mathematical credit. That review's own release receipt reports11:27:42Z and sentinel absence, independently confirmed by a read-only path check before the W55 handoff.

## 6. Actual arithmetic checks and what they establish

`check.py` built mu by a linear sieve through262144. Exact Gaussian-integer coefficient comparisons verified C1 through n=256 for the principal, mod4 real and mod5 quartic characters, with zero failures. The Lyapunov identity at rho=1/2 was checked in exact fractions. Untwisted T21 was checked at2,10,100,10000,100000; at the last cutoff the boundary count is20260 and both signed sums are-48. These are finite convention checks; the all-n statements rest on the proofs.

At x=4096,r=32, the principal B-to-E floating difference is about1.55e-7 whereas the two-branch difference is2.71e-7. Thus extrapolation does not promise a smaller error at every finite r and every source; it gives a uniform improved order. For the quartic mod5 character the respective floating differences are .06389885 and .00510686. E was summed through40x; its uncomputed absolute geometric tail is below1.75e-14 at this x. Roundoff is not included in that tail bound, so these are diagnostics, not interval certificates or proof of an exponent. A grid of the derivative majorants had maximum ratios below .200 and .084; again the inequalities are proved in A3-A4, not by this grid.

Completed rank pairs at N=262144 give:

| q | Largest completed displacement | Total unpaired end ranks | Largest residue partial-sum modulus through N |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
|1|495|24|154|
|3|1230|122|146|
|4|1156|53|126|
|5|2615|357|172|

Every unpaired end rank is retained in `checks.json`, with counts by residue and the worst pair. Pairs whose future endpoint exceeds N are not observed. No finite log-log fit, random-sign assumption, conductor-uniform claim or extrapolated power bound follows. The experiment shows that the criterion can be evaluated on the actual source and makes its censoring/debt explicit; it does not solve its all-scale estimate.

## E. Wildcard11: parity-preserving compression has a precise cost

In a finite cube Omega={0,1}^k let epsilon(x)=(-1)^(sum x_i). A syndrome map partitions Omega into fibres. If one fibre contains x,y of opposite parity, the coefficient vector c=delta_x-delta_y has zero fibre sums but sum epsilon*c=2. Hence no decoder of unsigned fibre sums can reconstruct the signed functional for arbitrary inputs. This is an exact kernel witness, not a heuristic entropy claim.

If parity is included in the syndrome, it is constant on every fibre. For normalized fibre-sum rows A_F=1_F/sqrt(|F|), the unique reconstruction coefficient is q_F=epsilon(F)sqrt(|F|), and

    ||q||_2^2=sum_F |F|=2^k=||epsilon||_2^2.             (E1)

The exact Euclidean readout norm is preserved, not reduced. A16-point check is in check.py. This uniform-cube diagnostic does not replace the actual arithmetic CRT law, whose occupation probabilities are1/p. W41's full-pattern covariance already identifies the corresponding arithmetic unpaid tail. No new coding mechanism survives this first test; an arithmetic restricted-input decoder with a genuinely smaller proved norm remains possible.

### The physical improvement

PH keeps the common forced ideal inside the divisor interpolation instead

The common ideal is

SC proves that sending the Möbius removal cutoff to infinity moves the

## DQ6--DQ8. A fixed-class polar asymptotic relative to I-HECKE

Define the original balanced polar form

\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathscr A_d(D)=
\sum_{\substack{c,e>1\ {\rm sf},\ (cB^3,eE^3)=1\\
                 \eta|_{\mu_6}=1}}
&\mu(c)\mu(e)\psi_d(c)\overline{\psi_d(e)}
\sqrt{q_cq_e}(q_Bq_E)^3\xi(B)\overline\xi(E)\,
W_D(c,e;B,E)\\
&\times\prod_{p\mid ce}(1-q_p^{-1}).
\end{aligned}
\tag{DQ6}
\]

Let `kappa_K=Res_(s=1) zeta_K(s)` and
`C_R=2 kappa_K A(2/3) R_tilde(2/3)`. This actual row-profile constant may
vanish; it is not replaced by a generic nonzero constant. For fixed
`b0<b<1` and `2/3<z1<(2+b)/3`, the candidate asymptotic is

\[
\boxed{
Q^{[d]}_{CC,\mathrm{bal}}
=C_R q_d^{-1/3}K^{2/3}D^{-4/3}\mathscr A_d(D)
 +O_\epsilon\!\left(
D^{2b+1+\epsilon}(K/D^2)^{z_1}q_d^{z_1-1+\epsilon}
\right).}
\tag{DQ7}
\]

This is a fixed-class statement; displayed conductor factors describe its
uniformity in `d`. It is not a normally convergent sum over all `d`.

Here is the density-weighted core continuation needed for the error. For a
finite-order core character `chi`, with all natural zeros and finite deletions
retained, write `s=3-3z`. Its Euler series factors as

\[
\prod_p\left(1-\chi(p)(1-q_p^{-s})q_p^{-w}\right)
=\frac1{L^S(w,\chi)}
\prod_p\left(1+
 \frac{\chi(p)q_p^{-w-s}}{1-\chi(p)q_p^{-w}}
\right).
\tag{DQ8}
\]

The second product is absolutely convergent when `Re w+Re s>1`, with
`Re w>0`. Fixed buffered core lines `Re w=b>b0` are therefore permitted
while `Re z<(2+b)/3`. I-HECKE bounds the reciprocal factor with subpower
actual finite conductor and height cost. The finite factors required by the
original column restrictions are retained before their subpower bounds; they
cannot be silently absorbed in fixed `S`. For good primes `q_p>=7`, their
local denominators stay uniformly away from zero on the fixed contours used
here. Fixed small-prime factors are kept separately.

Insert the complete `(c,e)=1` projector before separating the two core sums.
After `c=g c',e=g e'`, the Möbius/density weights and squarefree constraints
are exact; the positive majorant has a convergent `g^(-2b+epsilon)` sum.
For fixed `B,E`, the two masks `(c,E)=(e,B)=1` are finite core deletions.
Core Mellin inversion and (DQ8) give a bound
`D^(2b+1+epsilon) q_d^epsilon` with polynomial height. Because `q_c,q_e~D`,
the original rapid profile at `q_c q_B^3/D` and `q_e q_E^3/D` pays arbitrary
powers of `q_B,q_E`; all outside cube sums and their deletion costs converge.
Separable hard core endpoints follow from partial summation with the same
buffered bounds. Only finite-order core characters are asserted here.

In the fixed-class formula shift the row contour right from `a<2/3` to `z1`.
The only pole crossed is the zeta pole in `Z_ce(3-3z)`, whose residue is

`-(kappa_K/3) product_(p|ce)(1-q_p^(-1))`.

The right-shift identity is `I_a=I_z1 minus residues`, giving the positive
factor `6/3=2` in `C_R`. The gamma pole at `z=1` is not crossed, and the
original row transform is holomorphic throughout. The last-line bound is
exactly the error in (DQ7).

For `b=.8749`, `z1=.95`, and `K<=D^.87653`, the error for fixed `d` has
exponent `1.6825035`. The available estimate

# W58: character-preserving index, paid matching and an integrated Hankel gate

This batch proves no increase in c. The source-relative accepted value remains
c11=312864909/2500000000=.1251459636, theta11=.8748540364. Inherited analytic ancestry,
positive-slot uniformity and external definition/import/admission remain open.
The useful outputs below are precise source contracts and scoped failures. Their
remaining arithmetic estimates are explicit. No formalization or proof packet is
offered.

## 1. Immutable generation and six first tests

The frozen problem and sampler hashes were verified before generation. All30
original cards, their unnormalized subjective generation probabilities, and six
groups of five are in original-seeds.json, SHA256
55d8cbb0811f4874fbea51ba185d0a0d9c25ebff71b229477f43fbbe066997a1. The entire file was
read back before any detailed attempt-index/current-proof/creative-lane history.
One seedready message to root supplied that hash for separately coordinated blind
critic preparation. The author did not inspect critic choices or outcomes.

Every card remained eligible; no semantic-duplicate exclusion was made. The
deliberate choices were26 (strongest visible bridge),19 (protected high reach)
and25 (most different). Stage1 drew17 uniformly from all24 remaining literal
p<.10 cards; stage2 drew27 from all11 remaining literal p<.01 cards; stage3 drew11
from all25 remaining eligible cards, regardless of p. Each complete pool was
written, read and hashed in a tool call before its independent fresh entropy.
All three 256-bit words passed the exact uniform rejection map on the first draw.
No outcome was rerolled. The six tests below remain distinct even where their
mechanisms overlap earlier work.

| Card | First decisive test | Result and scope |
|---|---|---|
|26|Compute the exact two-delay multipliers and their common zero set.|All finite-height zeros are detected except a possible simple real zero at the shared cancellation line. An inherited safe line repairs this exception, but the arithmetic channel bound stays open. Existing G47/G109 ancestry is substantial.|
|19|Build a genuine character-preserving cross-integer differential and calculate its harmonic index.|A neutral-prime complex has gap1 and linear harmonic rank. Arbitrary residue-preserving matchings have an exact minimum rank equal to the l1 residue Mertens discrepancy. This is an index obstruction and a paid transport repair, developed in Section2.|
|25|Use a degree-zero phase loop with nonconstant positive crossing weights.|The weighted signed crossing sum need not vanish and can have arbitrary amplitude. Degree alone has no quantitative H return. This is a toy falsification of the proposed inference, not an estimate for the original H packet.|
|17|Hide a genuine exponential pole impulse beyond a finite observed source interval.|The pole can be arbitrarily small on a safe half-plane while unchanged finite data omit it. Adaptive quadrature needs an independently proved signed tail invariant. No arithmetic impossibility is claimed.|
|27|Compute a pole mode's Hankel norm, then use the complete integrated Mertens kernel.|A single pole is rank1 and produces exponential norm growth. Uniform boundedness of the complete weighted integrated Hankel operator has a rigorous zero-exclusion return. Operator norm can be much smaller than its Hilbert-Schmidt bound, but no actual arithmetic norm saving is proved. Section3 develops this protected rare choice.|
|11|Separate exact common zeros from high-frequency near-common zeros.|The all-height positive floor is zero on the critical line; a coarse explicit finite-height lower bound is nevertheless proved in Section4. The latter pays local division and does not provide a new arithmetic gain.|

## 2. Protected high-reach19: phase-preserving supersymmetry and the exact index bill

All constructions in this section use the complete actual squarefree source,
not f3 or the original H packet. Fix q>=1. Let V_X have the orthonormal basis e_n
for squarefree n<=X with (n,q)=1, including n=1. Its parity operator is
Gamma e_n=mu(n)e_n. For each character chi modulo q, retain natural zero extension
by having excluded only nonunits, and put W_chi e_n=chi(n)e_n. Thus

    Str(W_chi)=Tr(Gamma W_chi)=M_chi(X).

This is a replacement architecture with its own return. It does not inherit any
signed-submask estimate for a different detector.

### 2.1 A neutral-prime realization works, but its harmonic price is linear

Choose a prime r with r not dividing q and chi(r)=1 for the particular character.
For all characters modulo q simultaneously, choose r=1 mod q. Such primes exist
by Dirichlet's theorem; see [NIST DLMF27.11](https://dlmf.nist.gov/27.11). Pair each
squarefree q-unit m<=X/r with r not dividing m to rm. The pairings are disjoint.
On each pair orient a differential d from the even-parity basis vector to the
odd-parity vector, with coefficient1; set d=0 on odd vectors and unpaired vectors.
Then d is odd, d^2=0, and it commutes with W_chi. The Laplacian
Delta=dd*+d*d is identity on every pair and zero on every unpaired vector. Its
positive spectral gap is exactly1 whenever X>=r. No estimate of the arithmetic source has been
used in obtaining that gap.

The unpaired basis is exactly

    r not dividing m, (m,q)=1, mu(m)^2=1, X/r<m<=X.

Consequently for every t>=0,

    M_chi(X)=Str(W_chi exp(-t Delta))
            =sum_(X/r<m<=X,(m,qr)=1) mu(m)chi(m).       (19.1)

Both endpoints and the empty-face atom have been accounted for: every m<=X/r
is paired and cancels because chi(r)=1. For chi(r)!=1 the exact extra term is
(1-chi(r)) sum_(m<=X/r,r not dividing m) mu(m)chi(m); it cannot be discarded.

Write d_q=zeta(2)^(-1) product_(p|q) p/(p+1), with empty product1. Elementary
square-divisor counting gives

    #{m<=y:mu(m)^2=1,(m,D)=1}=d_D y+O_D(sqrt(y)).

For completeness, expand mu(m)^2=sum_(d^2|m)mu(d); only (d,D)=1 contributes,
count k<=y/d^2 coprime to D as (phi(D)/D)y/d^2+O_D(1), sum d<=sqrt(y), and
bound the omitted d-tail by O_D(sqrt(y)). Its Euler product is d_D. Hence

    dim ker Delta=d_(qr)(1-1/r)X+O_(q,r)(sqrt(X))
                 =d_q (r-1)/(r+1) X+O_(q,r)(sqrt(X)). (19.2)

Thus phase-preserving cross-integer pairing does repair the chain-map defect,
but its unsigned harmonic price is still linear. This is not a lower bound on
M_chi. At q=1,r=2 its leading rank is2X/pi^2, agreeing with the known squarefree
complex. Björner's [Theorems3.1/3.4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1101.5704v1) give the
classical topology and a stronger error; no literature novelty is claimed for
that case. W27's fixed simplicial contraction and [private research revision] G74 already explain
related harmonic obstructions. Our next calculation allows a different
differential and therefore does not import their fixed-complex rank floor.

### 2.2 Exact minimum over all character-preserving pairings

For each unit residue a modulo q define

    E_a(X)=#{n<=X:n squarefree,n=a mod q,mu(n)=1},
    O_a(X)=#{n<=X:n squarefree,n=a mod q,mu(n)=-1},
    I_a(X)=E_a(X)-O_a(X).

Consider ANY odd differential d on V_X satisfying d^2=0 and commuting with every
W_chi modulo q. Characters separate unit residue classes: if an n,m matrix entry
of d is nonzero then chi(n)=chi(m) for every chi, whence n=m mod q. Thus d splits
into the residue blocks. Since W_chi is unitary, d* also commutes with W_chi, and
the harmonic subspace of Delta=dd*+d*d splits in the same way.

For each residue block the even-minus-odd harmonic dimension is I_a(X). One
elementary proof decomposes the finite complex into im d, im d* and ker Delta:
the first two have equal dimensions with opposite parity, via d restricted to
im d*. Therefore

    dim ker Delta >= R_q(X):=sum_(a mod q,(a,q)=1)|I_a(X)|.       (19.3)

This lower bound is attained. In each residue class pair the first
min(E_a,O_a) even/odd basis vectors in increasing order and use the two-state
differential above. The remaining |I_a| vectors are harmonic and all positive
eigenvalues equal1. Thus the EXACT minimum harmonic dimension in this class of
differentials is R_q(X), with an attaining gap1 realization whenever any pairs exist.

Character orthogonality gives

    M_chi(X)=sum_a chi(a)I_a(X),
    I_a(X)=1/phi(q) sum_(chi mod q) conjugate(chi(a)) M_chi(X),
    max_chi |M_chi(X)| <= R_q(X)
       <= sum_chi |M_chi(X)| <= phi(q)max_chi |M_chi(X)|.         (19.4)

For each fixed q these are fixed constants. Therefore a power bound for the
optimal unsigned harmonic rank is equivalent to the same common power bound for
all characters modulo q. A gap theorem alone is vacuous here: gap1 was obtained
without bounding R_q. Optimizing the differential has not made an independent
arithmetic estimate. This conclusion is limited to this complete source and
character-preserving finite parity complexes; it does not prohibit a different
signed readout, a noncommuting differential with a paid commutator, or a new
analytic source.

Late source audit: the newly integrated [private research revision] G135 already proves the full
fixed-modulus character/residue discrepancy equivalence, its increasing-rank
matching version, and the exact unmatched-index price. The finite Hodge minimum
above is an operator formulation of that same index bill. It is not a new
arithmetic matching principle or an independent cancellation mechanism. This
overlap was found after the original seeds and random selections were frozen;
none of their eligibility or choices has been revised.

The exact diagnostic at X=80,q=5 gives indices (0,-3,-4,1) in residues1,2,3,4.
The minimum harmonic rank is8. The four character traces are -6,-1+i,8,-1-i,
exactly equal to the corresponding literal M_chi(80). A neutral-prime r=2
complex for the principal character has14 harmonic states instead. This checks
the finite indexing and shows why a14-state rank floor from one complex is not
valid for every changed differential. No asymptotic saving follows from80.

### 2.3 A paid transport repair with a complete Mellin return

The preceding optimal matching is finite and leaves an index. A different
mechanism uses one fixed GLOBAL pairing for each q, with every positive-Mobius
squarefree q-unit paired to a negative-Mobius squarefree q-unit of the same
residue class. Such pairings exist: each class has infinitely many negative
members given by primes in that class; fixing a prime r=1 mod q and multiplying
distinct primes in the class by r gives infinitely many positive members.
Increasing-rank matching is one definite construction. Existence alone bounds
no displacement.

Write an oriented pair as (u,v), mu(u)=1,mu(v)=-1, u=v mod q. Let
a=min(u,v), b=max(u,v), and define its total displacement in a dyadic minimum
shell by

    D_q(X)=sum_(pairs with X<=a<2X) (b-a), X=1,2,4,....          (19.5)

All partners, however far away, enter this sum. This is a finite sum in each
shell; it does not truncate or ignore a partner outside2X. Suppose that for one
common 0<gamma<1 and every epsilon>0,

    D_q(X) <<_(q,epsilon) X^(1+gamma+epsilon)
    for every sufficiently large dyadic X and every fixed q.               (T)

Then all ordinary Dirichlet L(s,chi) are zero-free in Re(s)>gamma. Here is the
complete return. On Re(s)>1, absolute convergence permits regrouping the full
reciprocal Dirichlet series into these pairs:

    1/L(s,chi)=sum_(pairs) chi(u)(u^(-s)-v^(-s)).              (19.6)

Natural zeros, squareful zeros and every n=1 contribution are already in the
source. For sigma=Re(s)>0,

    |u^(-s)-v^(-s)| <= |s|(b-a)a^(-sigma-1).                (19.7)

Thus(T), summed over dyadic minimum shells, gives normally convergent pair sums
on every compact subset of Re(s)>gamma: choose epsilon smaller than the compact
horizontal margin. Uniform convergence of holomorphic terms suffices; no
uncontrolled logarithm of the far endpoint is needed. The resulting holomorphic
F equals1/L on Re>1 and L F=1 meromorphically throughout the connected half-plane.
At an L-zero this identity is impossible. At a principal pole, F has a removable
zero; no pole is declared a zero. Original imprimitive L and its factors were
never replaced by a primitive function. Character-dependent constants and finite
height are unrestricted. This proves the claimed ordinary-character scope.

This route has an honest large loss allowance: ideal mean displacement of order
X^(1/2+epsilon), summed over O(X) actual pairs per shell, would meet gamma=1/2.
To reach the weaker c=1/4 it suffices to prove total displacement
X^(7/4+epsilon). For c=1/6 the budget is X^(11/6+epsilon). A nearby gamma=.87485
requires X^(1.87485+epsilon), giving c=.12515, a gain .0000040364 over c11.
These are conditional calibrations, not derived displacement estimates.

The strongest objection is concrete: same-residue arithmetic pairing may cost
precisely the unproved cancellation. For monotone pairing, the number of pair
intervals crossing a cutoff t is exactly |I_a(t)| in each residue class. Indeed
the kth positive and kth negative lists leave E_a(t)-O_a(t) unmatched indices
at that cut, all crossing in one orientation. Tonelli therefore gives

    sum_(pairs) length([a,b] intersect [A,B])
       =integral_A^B R_q(t)dt                              (19.8)

for this particular pairing. This is a proof of the cost identity, not an
independent bound. D_q in(19.5) charges the COMPLETE future interval of every
pair starting in a shell, so one cannot replace it by the left side of(19.8)
on that shell without paying intervals outside it. An arithmetic rule with a
proved complete D_q budget, or a new localized crossing estimate with its own
return, is the next action. The ancestry includes W01 signed transport,
[private research revision]'s priced coupling and [private research revision] G135's exact rank-displacement target.
Under G135's equivalent summatory/rank bounds at gamma>1/2, the kth endpoints
are comparable to k and have difference O(k^gamma); there are O(X) pairs in a
minimum shell. This immediately implies D_q(X)=O(X^(1+gamma)), also with
epsilon losses. Thus(T) is a separately priced sufficient total-displacement
contract, not an unconditionally achieved weaker arithmetic estimate. The
Hodge formulation and complete future-partner Mellin bill do not remove the
older matching target's open cancellation input.

There is also a complete ACTUAL arithmetic failure of the simplest global
construction. Fix r=1 mod q and pair every squarefree q-unit m with r not
dividing m to rm, with orientation determined by mu(m). This pairs the entire
source and preserves each residue class. Its minimum endpoint is m and its
length is(r-1)m, so

    D_q(X)=(r-1) sum_(X<=m<2X,(m,qr)=1) mu(m)^2 m
           =(3/2)(r-1)d_(qr)X^2+O_(q,r)(X^(3/2)).       (19.9)

The last identity follows by partial summation of the proved squarefree count;
half-open endpoints change at most O(X), already inside the error. The leading
coefficient is positive. This global neutral-prime rule therefore does not meet
any gamma<1 in(T), despite its exact phase cancellation and spectral gap1.
This rejects the named rule's positive displacement certificate, not every
same-residue matching or the signed Mertens target. To reach a subtrivial
exponent one needs genuinely closer cross-integer partners or a different
signed pricing rule with a proved complete return.

## 3. Protected rare27: integrated logarithmic Hankel operator

Fix one ordinary chi and 0<a<1. Put M=M_chi, with M(x)=0 for x<1, and

    h_a(v)=exp(-a v)M(exp v), v>=0.

For each L>0 let Gamma_(a,L) be the integral operator on L2(0,L) with kernel
h_a(t+u). All original arithmetic is inside the one complete M. Its associated
complex BILINEAR form is

    B_(a,L)(f,g)=integral_0^L integral_0^L h_a(t+u)f(t)g(u)dtdu.

The bilinear supremum equals the usual operator norm (complex conjugation in
the Hilbert pairing changes no norm). There is no unintended conjugation of
chi or of h. Kernels are bounded on every finite square, so all finite operators
are well-defined.

### 3.1 A uniform complete norm excludes all right-hand zeros

Assume

    K_(a,chi):=sup_(L>0)||Gamma_(a,L)|| < infinity.            (H)

The compatible forms extend from compactly supported functions to a bounded
bilinear form B_a on L2(R_+) by density. For Re(z)>0 put E_z(t)=exp(-zt). Its
squared norm is1/(2Re(z)). The map z->E_z is holomorphic into L2 on that
half-plane by exponential domination of every local derivative. Therefore
Q(z)=B_a(E_z,E_z) is holomorphic and

    |Q(z)| <= K_(a,chi)/(2Re(z)).                            (27.1)

Initially Re(a+z)>1, Fubini is absolute, and the line t+u=v has length v:

    Q(z)=integral_0^infinity v M(exp v)exp(-(a+z)v)dv
        =-d/ds [1/(s L(s,chi))] at s=a+z.                  (27.2)

The last identity follows directly from Abel summation, including the n=1
atom, since integral_0^infinity M(exp v)exp(-s v)dv=1/(sL(s,chi)) for Re(s)>1.
Both sides of(27.2) are meromorphic on Re(s)>a, while the left side is
holomorphic. The identity theorem forces the derivative of1/(sL) to have no
pole there. Every L-zero of order m>=1 would give1/(sL) a pole of order m and
its derivative a pole of order m+1, since s!=0. Hence no such zero exists.
The principal pole at1 is a zero of1/(sL), not an obstruction. No primitive
replacement, conductor growth, or height supremum has been introduced.

For a common gamma, it is enough to prove(H) for every fixed chi and every
a>gamma (one may restrict to a countable decreasing sequence tending to gamma).
The constants may depend on a and chi. Each individual zero with Re(rho)>gamma
then lies to the right of one such a. This is an all-finite-height conclusion.
There is no need to control one inverse norm uniformly as a approaches gamma.

This resembles the earlier W29 Sobolev-Hankel pole gate but changes the object:
W29 uses the atomic folded coefficient form and a Sobolev metric; here one
ordinary logarithmic primitive is built into the KERNEL and the input norm is
plain L2. The two contracts must not be identified without a proved operator
comparison. Neither supplies a bound for the other from terminology alone.

### 3.2 Pole, Hilbert-Schmidt and oscillation tests

For a literal one-mode kernel h(v)=R exp(lambda v), Gamma_L has rank1 and its
only nonzero singular value is

    |R| integral_0^L exp(2Re(lambda)t)dt
      =|R|(exp(2Re(lambda)L)-1)/(2Re(lambda)),

with value |R|L when Re(lambda)=0. Thus a low-rank approximation cannot throw
away the leading few singular modes without proving that a zero pole is not
among them. Finite computations at bounded L cannot settle the growing norm.
This calculation is a model calibration; it is not an unproved decomposition
of the full arithmetic source into independently bounded zero modes.

The exact Hilbert-Schmidt identity on a finite square is

    ||Gamma_(a,L)||_HS^2
      =integral_0^(2L) w_L(v) exp(-2av)|M(exp v)|^2 dv,
    w_L(v)=v for0<=v<=L, and2L-v forL<=v<=2L.             (27.3)

This follows by measuring each anti-diagonal. A finite full weighted moment
integral_0^infinity v exp(-2av)|M(exp v)|^2dv proves(H), but it essentially
reimports the old full signed energy and gives no new arithmetic saving.
The factor v is logarithmic in x and costs no fixed exponent.

Operator norm is nonetheless a strictly weaker functional target. For the
NONARITHMETIC example h(v)=exp(i v^2),

    Gamma f(t)=exp(i t^2) integral_0^infinity exp(2itu)exp(iu^2)f(u)du.

Extend exp(iu^2)f(u) by zero to the full real line. Plancherel for the Fourier
transform integral exp(i xi u) gives full-output squared norm pi||f||_2^2
after xi=2t; restricting t>=0 can only decrease it. Therefore every finite
compression has norm<=sqrt(pi), whereas its Hilbert-Schmidt norm equals L,
because the kernel has modulus1 on a square of area L^2. This is an exact
example of coherent oscillatory suppression missed by the positive HS price.
It is not a Mobius model and does not show that actual h has such oscillation.

### 3.3 Exact arithmetic target and coarse headroom

For compactly supported inputs, expanding the complete M gives

    B_a(f,g)=sum_(n>=1) mu(n)chi(n)
        integral_(t,u>=0,t+u>=log n) exp(-a(t+u))f(t)g(u)dtdu. (27.4)

Only finitely many n occur when both inputs are compactly supported. Every
coefficient, the threshold inequality and all q-unit zeros are literal. The
unproved estimate(H) is a uniform signed bound for this complete form. Taking
absolute values coefficient by coefficient would lose the proposed mechanism.

There is a complete finite-growth version that permits a much coarser bound
than(H) at the initial weight. Fix0<a<=gamma<1. It is sufficient that for every
epsilon>0 and all sufficiently large L,

    ||Gamma_(a,L)|| <<_(chi,epsilon)
          exp(2(gamma-a+epsilon)L).                       (H-growth)

Here is the full return, including every off-diagonal time rectangle. Write
I_j=[j,j+1), j>=0. The block of the a-weighted Hankel operator from I_j to I_i
is unitarily equivalent to its restriction with BOTH variables in
[(i+j)/2,(i+j)/2+1): translation balances the two coordinates while preserving
their sum. Thus its norm is at most K_a((i+j)/2+1), where
K_a(L)=||Gamma_(a,L)||. For sigma>a the sigma-weighted block is obtained by
multiplying the two slots by exp(-(sigma-a)t); its norm is consequently at most

    exp(-(sigma-a)(i+j)) K_a((i+j)/2+1).                   (27.5)

If K_a(L)<=C exp(2eta L), eta>=0, summing EVERY block gives the finite bound

    ||Gamma_sigma|| <= C exp(2eta)
          [1-exp(-(sigma-a-eta))]^(-2), sigma>a+eta.       (27.6)

The double geometric series converges in operator norm, agrees with the kernel
on compact inputs, and covers the whole quadrant. It does not discard mixed
blocks or assume that unequal side lengths behave like the longer side.
Choose eta=gamma-a+epsilon<sigma-a for any sigma>gamma. Then(H-growth) and the
already proved(H) bridge exclude all L-zeros to the right of gamma. Small L
are absorbed into C since finite kernels are bounded. At gamma=a the same
argument allows every subexponential K_a(L), not just a uniformly bounded one.

For the high-potential starting weight a=1/2, an ideal bounded operator would
have half-plane reach. A much weaker growth bound already suffices:

| Conditional target | Allowed L exponent in K_(1/2)(L), with every epsilon |
|---|---|
|First improvement over c11|strictly below .7497080728|
|gamma=.87485, c=.12515|.7497|
|gamma=5/6, c=1/6|2/3|
|gamma=3/4, c=1/4|1/2|

The elementary actual-source bound |M(exp v)|<=exp v gives only

    K_a(L)<=(exp(2(1-a)L)-1)/(2(1-a)), 0<a<1,             (27.7)

by dominating the kernel with the rank1 positive kernel
exp((1-a)t)exp((1-a)u). Thus at a=1/2 the proved elementary exponent is1,
while first gain needs below .7497080728. No part of that signed norm saving
is established here. More generally a PROVED pointwise envelope
|M(x)|<=C x^b would give the same rank1 upper bound with1-a replaced by b-a,
interpreted continuously at b=a. We do not infer such an envelope solely from
unquantified holomorphy or assign it to an unverified source contract.

These are coarse sufficient bounds: the constants can be arbitrarily large
and depend on chi and epsilon. No contraction or small norm is required.
The aspiration, quantitative loss allowance and missing arithmetic input are
therefore separate. Neither(H) at a new a nor(H-growth) at a new exponent has
been proved for the actual source.

The next mathematical action is to estimate the complete signed form(27.4)
using a specific oscillatory decomposition that preserves its cumulative
threshold, and to compare its cost to the inherited Sobolev gate. The HS route
does not reduce the arithmetic gap. Low-rank tail control alone misses a pole.

## 4. Wildcard11 and bridge26: finite-height division versus a global floor

Let U_chi be the fixed complete Gaussian Mobius field with Mellin transform
exp(tau s^2/2)/L(s,chi), and D_lambda U(x)=U(x)-lambda^beta U(x/lambda), for
fixed lambda>1 and fixed real beta. Its exact multiplier is

    m_lambda(s)=1-lambda^(beta-s).                        (26.1)

The Gaussian left tail and fixed dilation are paid as in the complete source
construction; a complete every-epsilon shell L2 exponent gamma for D_lambda U
makes its Mellin integral holomorphic on Re(s)>gamma. This is a conditional
arithmetic assumption, not a consequence of changing the multiplier.

For lambda2=2 and lambda3=3, the common zeros of m2,m3 are exactly s=beta.
Indeed their zeros are on Re(s)=beta; a nonzero common height would make
log2/log3 rational and hence2^k=3^l for nonzero integers, impossible. At the real
point beta both vanish simply. Accordingly two complete channel bounds exclude
all L-zeros in Re(s)>gamma except possibly a SIMPLE real zero at beta. Higher
multiplicity would survive in both quotients. If beta is in an independently
proved zero-free region, e.g. beta>theta11 under the accepted premise, the
exception is already excluded. Locally away from beta one nonzero multiplier
suffices; no global quantitative lower bound in height is needed for that
analytic argument. This is existing G47/G109-style detector-bank ancestry.

The stronger positive-floor hope fails. On the critical line, for any fixed
positive weights w2,w3,

    inf_(t>=T) [w2|1-exp(-it log2)|^2+w3|1-exp(-it log3)|^2]=0

for every finite T. Pigeonholing points nL(log2,log3)/(2pi) modulo1 supplies
arbitrarily high simultaneous near-returns. [private research revision] already proves this for
every fixed summable bank and pays its complete source formation. The failure
does not refute local analytic division or source-specific signed estimates.

There is an elementary explicit finite-height replacement. Let0<t0<=T and
kappa=(log2 log3)/(2pi). For t0<=|t|<=T,

    max(|m2(beta+it)|,|m3(beta+it)|)
      >= min(2t0 log3/pi,
             4 exp(-kappa T)/((log2+log3)sqrt(3))).      (11.1)

Proof: by symmetry take t>0 and choose nearest nonnegative integers k,l to
t log2/(2pi), t log3/(2pi), with errors e2,e3 in[-pi,pi]. If both integers are
zero, max|e_j|=t log3>=t0 log3. Otherwise3^k and2^l are distinct integers, so

    |k log3-l log2| >=1/max(3^k,2^l)
       >=exp(-kappa T)/sqrt(3).

On the other hand it is at most (log2+log3)max(|e2|,|e3|)/(2pi).
Finally |1-exp(-ie)|=2|sin(e/2)|>=2|e|/pi for |e|<=pi. Combining these two
cases proves(11.1). The estimate is deliberately coarse and deteriorates
exponentially with T. It gives a concrete finite-height inverse price on the
critical line away from beta; it does not improve the exponent of either
arithmetic channel. A common real blind point remains and must be paid above.

## 5. The other two precise failures

For25 take the smooth circle map exp(i sin t),0<=t<2pi. Its degree is zero.
The regular target1 has preimages t=0,pi with orientations+1,-1. For the positive
weight w(t)=A(1+epsilon cos t), A>0,0<epsilon<1, the oriented weighted crossing
sum is w(0)-w(pi)=2A epsilon. It can be arbitrarily large while the degree is
unchanged. Thus integer crossing cancellation does not imply quantitative
weighted cancellation. A repair must bound the actual paired weight difference
(for example by an actual variation integral) and restore all missing crossings.
We have not derived such a repair for the original H phase or its projectors.

For17 fix rho=beta+iT and A>0. The hidden causal tail
h_A(v)=exp(rho v)1_(v>=A) is identically zero on0<=v<A, yet its Laplace transform
is exp(-(s-rho)A)/(s-rho), with a genuine pole at rho. On Re(s)>=sigma0>beta its
modulus is at most exp(-(sigma0-beta)A)/(sigma0-beta), as small as prescribed by
choosing A. Hence finite source samples and an arbitrarily small safe-line tail
do not certify analytic continuation through rho. This nonarithmetic test does
not defeat a valid arithmetic tail inequality. It identifies exactly what the
adaptive quadrature proposal lacks: a signed tail invariant valid in the larger
domain, including every later continuation step. Prior W52 finite-prefix pole
completion and W54's full prediction residual have closely related scope.

## 6. Portfolio and next action

The high-reach19 repair was developed through actual phase preservation,
minimum-index algebra, an exact finite check and a complete matching return.
The rare27 survivor was developed through the full analytic gate, exact
singular/HS formulas and a strict functional separation example. Wildcard11
received an explicit finite-height calculation. These are substantive
developments, but none proves the open arithmetic estimates(T) or(H).

Cards01-10,12-16,18,20-24,28-30 that were not selected are retained as untested
in this batch, even where antecedents are known. More precisely the six tested
IDs are11,17,19,25,26,27; the other24 are author-untested. No low probability
is evidence of mathematical value or novelty. The reported refinements are
relative to the inspected QRH record, not claims of literature priority.

The sharpest immediate target is a genuinely arithmetic bound on complete
same-residue pairing displacement, or on the integrated Hankel form(27.4),
at gamma=.87485 before attempting5/6 or3/4. A proof that only changes basis,
establishes a spectral gap, removes exact common numerator zeros, or bounds
discarded singular values would not meet either target. The current endpoint
therefore remains c11, with its source-relative obligations unchanged.

# [private research revision]: weighted boundary spectrum and complete source transfers

Root accepts G164–G166 after the complete author and independent critic
reports, developments, exact helpers and receipts were read. The useful
increment is a uniform obstruction for arbitrary moving prime weights,
including weights that vanish at the smallest basis primes. It extends the
character-gauge/cone analysis in [G144–G145](../[private research revision]/wild57-integration.md).
The incidence and prime-removal tools retain every term needed to return
to the actual arithmetic source. No complete signed estimate or improved c
is proved. The highest accepted written value remains
312864909/2500000000 = 0.1251459636.

Frozen evidence: [author](wild59/report.md), [weighted development](wild59/fock-boundary.md),
[prime-removal development](wild59/renewal-overlap.md),
[independent review](wild59-review/report.md), and
[retention/source bindings](retention-manifest.json). These preserve all30
cards, six author first tests and two independent audits. Actual host-local
claim bytes are excluded. Source manifest timestamps pin captured bytes,
not an earlier whole-file reading of a concurrently maintained document.

## G164. Least-active-prime boundary multiplicity

Fix an ordinary Dirichlet character χ modulo q. The source is
a(n)=μ(n)χ(n), including a(1)=1 and all squareful/nonunit zeros. Let P be a
finite set of primes coprime to q containing all such primes at most N;
additional primes larger than N are allowed. Use the ordered exterior basis
indexed by squarefree products of P, with creation operators c_p and their
usual fermionic signs. Let Π project onto products at most N, Q=I−Π, and

\[
d=\sum_{p\in P}w_pc_p,\quad W=\sum_p|w_p|^2>0,\quad
D=\Pi d\Pi,\quad B=Qd\Pi,\quad E=B^*B.
\]

All weights may be complex, N-dependent, and zero. Divisor closure gives
Qd*Π=0 and ΠdQ=0. The canonical anticommutation relations therefore imply

\[
D^2=0,\qquad D^*D+DD^*=W\Pi-E,\qquad 0\le E\le W\Pi.       \tag{95.1}
\]

Let p* be the least **active** prime, meaning w_p*≠0. Define U to be the
span of p*-free basis states with N/p*<n≤N. Every active creation kills U
after truncation, so D|U=0. On V_N/U, the operator
(1/w_p*)c_p*^* is a contracting homotopy: the full anticommutator is the
identity, and every term that fails to cancel after truncation lies in U.
The long exact sequence of the quotient complex identifies H(D) with U
as graded vector spaces. Finite-dimensional Hodge theory and (95.1) give

\[
\dim\ker(E-WI)=\dim H(D)=C_{p_*}(N),\qquad
C_p(N)=\#\{N/p<n\le N:\mu(n)^2=1,(n,q)=1,p\nmid n\}.       \tag{95.2}
\]

This is an eigenspace **dimension**, not a statement that the critical
basis vectors themselves are harmonic. For example, at q=1,N=12 the
critical states7 and11 need not be killed by D*. The quotient contraction
need not have a uniform norm when w_p* tends to zero. If p*>N then D=0,
U=V_N, and the same formula still holds.

Set κ_q=ζ(2)^−1∏_{p|q}p/(p+1). Square-divisor inclusion-exclusion gives
Q_q(x)=κ_q x+O_q(√x). For fixed p∤q,

\[
C_p(N)=\kappa_q\frac{p-1}{p+1}N+O_{q,p}(\sqrt N).
\]

For a bound uniform in p, handle the finitely many p<4/κ_q with this
formula. For the other primes, count q-unit squarefree states in (N/2,N]
and subtract at most N/p multiples of p. Thus, for all N sufficiently
large depending only on q, every unramified p satisfies
C_p(N)≥κ_qN/8. The trace counts outgoing creation edges exactly, so

\[
\frac{\kappa_q}{8}WN\le\operatorname{Tr}E
=\sum_p|w_p|^2C_p(N)\le WN,
\quad \|E\|=W,\quad
\dim\ker(E-WI)\ge\frac{\kappa_q}{8}N.                    \tag{95.3}
\]

Consequently no choice of these moving weights produces an ambient
positive spectral gap or a power-saving positive trace certificate.
This does **not** give a lower bound for the complete signed arithmetic
source or for another detector. Signed cancellation within the large
boundary space is still an eligible mechanism.

Let Tχ be diagonal multiplication by χ(n), and Str the parity-weighted
trace. Supertrace of the full identity gives the exact source return

\[
W M_\chi(N)=\operatorname{Str}(T_\chi E)
 +\operatorname{Str}([T_\chi,D^*]D).                     \tag{95.4}
\]

For each p, its normalized contribution is

\[
\sum_{N/p<n\le N\atop p\nmid n}a(n)
 +(1-\chi(p))\sum_{n\le N/p\atop p\nmid n}a(n)=M_\chi(N).
\]

Both endpoints, the unit, and nonunit zeros are included. Dropping the
commutator bulk is invalid for general characters. Restricting active
primes to χ(p)=1 does kill that bulk, but retains (95.3). Moving χ phases
into the differential is a unitary gauge change: it preserves the
spectrum and moves the arithmetic dependence into the observer/bulk.

An estimate for the **complete** right side of (95.4), at most
C_{χ,ε} W N^{γ+ε} for every N and ε>0, with a common 0<γ<2187135091/2500000000
over the required fixed-character family, would give Mχ(N)≪N^{γ+ε}.
The actual reciprocal-L Dirichlet series then continues through Abel
summation to Re(s)>γ, and excludes zeros there, with the allowed principal
pole treated normally. No such estimate is supplied here; no uniformity
for growing conductors or native-H transfer is inferred.

The ordered product ∏_{p increasing}(I−χ(p)c_p), acting with its largest
factor first, generates the literal μχ source. Averaging over all orders
kills degrees at least2, hence changes the source. Restoring the missing
parity/signs restores the original source. This rejects that averaging
shortcut, not all fermionic representations.

Classical ancestry is [Björner2011, Theorems2.1/3.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1101.5704)
for the squarefree complex and [Bravyi–Kitaev2000v2, Eqs1–2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/quant-ph/0003137)
for creation signs. The weighted truncated identities and uniform bound
above are proved in the frozen development; no literature novelty claim
is made.

## G165. Incidence kernels and all acyclic face matchings

On the q-unit squarefree states at most N, define natural edge observations

\[
(\nabla_\chi f)(n,p)=f(pn)+\chi(p)f(n),\qquad pn\le N.
\]

Writing f(n)=a(n)g(n) gauges this to ordinary differences, up to a unit
phase per edge. The graph is connected by deleting primes down to1, hence

\[
\ker\nabla_\chi=\operatorname{span}\{a\}.                \tag{95.5}
\]

The source one wants to estimate is the exact unobserved direction.
Unitary Fourier conjugation transports this kernel rather than removing
it. In a length-N additive transform with the original zeros retained,
the zero-frequency component is Mχ(N)/√N. For the quartic character
modulo5 at N=7, the actual coefficients on1,2,3,6,7 are
1,−i,i,1,−i: every internal flux vanishes but Mχ(7)=2−i.
Adding outgoing zero-extension observations incurs the positive boundary
cost ∑|w_p|²C_p(N). This edge-observation cost is distinguished from the
coherent operator E; they are not interchangeable quadratic forms.

For any elementary face matching, pair a lower n with upper pn. The exact
source sum decomposes into

\[
M_\chi(N)=\sum_{n\text{ critical}}a(n)
 +\sum_{(n,pn)\text{ matched}}a(n)(1-\chi(p)).            \tag{95.6}
\]

In particular, the least unramified prime ℓ gives an acyclic matching
n↔ℓn for ℓ-free n≤N/ℓ. Reversing matched edges cannot create a cycle:
after an upward ℓ edge, any permitted downward non-ℓ edge still contains ℓ.
The surviving critical count is C_ℓ(N).

More generally every acyclic elementary face matching with m pairs
satisfies m≤rank D for the unit-weight exterior differential. Select
matched upper rows and lower columns of D. An off-diagonal incidence
u_i←l_j gives the oriented alternating path u_i→l_j→u_j. Acyclicity
orders these paths, making the selected minor triangular with nonzero
diagonal. Therefore

\[
\#\text{critical}=\dim V_N-2m
 \ge\dim V_N-2\operatorname{rank}D
 =\dim H(D)=C_\ell(N)\asymp_q N.                       \tag{95.7}
\]

No such matching gives a power-saving **unweighted absolute** critical
count. This does not lower-bound the signed critical sum, nor all weighted
homotopies. Any elimination using gradient paths must retain their full
coefficients and the norm of the scalar evaluation map. In the modulo5
example, pairs1↔2 and3↔6 leave critical contribution −i and matched bulk2;
discarding the latter changes the answer.

The independent S18 audit leaves broader absorbing-boundary/scattering
operators open; S12 leaves signed dual certificates open. They require
additional observations that see (95.5) and a paid return to μχ. The
positive-count obstruction is not a rejection of those broader proposals.

## G166. Prime removal with exact correction and all-shell return

For a fixed finite prime block B, let e_B be μχ on squarefree divisors of
P_B, r_B be χ on all B-smooth integers, including prime powers, and
a_B(n)=a(n)1_{(n,P_B)=1}. With Dirichlet convolution,

\[
e_B*r_B=\delta_1,\quad a=e_B*a_B,\quad a_B=r_B*a,
\quad A_B(s)=\frac1{L(s,\chi)E_B(s)},
\quad E_B(s)=\prod_{p\in B}(1-\chi(p)p^{-s}).            \tag{95.8}
\]

For overlapping blocks, A_A A_B=A_{A∪B}A_{A∩B}. This is an exact
overlap identity; a determinant invariant under a common meromorphic
multiplier cannot exclude that multiplier's poles by itself. It preserves
the earlier overlap/renewal ancestry in [G79–G81](../[private research revision]/wild47-integration.md),
G92, G108 and [G135](../[private research revision]/wild55-integration.md).

For the field norm sup_{T>0} T^−γ||F||_{L²([T,2T],dt/t)}, Minkowski gives
the absolute forward/reverse coefficient costs

\[
\prod_{p\in B}(1+p^{-\gamma}),\qquad
\prod_{p\in B}(1-p^{-\gamma})^{-1}.                    \tag{95.9}
\]

Every shifted shell and small tail is included. These are valid coarse
bounds, not claimed sharp operator norms on a restricted arithmetic
source. A same-shell bound alone does not supply (95.9).

For smoothing kernels exp(−n/x) and exp(−(n/x)^2), the Mellin factors are,
respectively, Γ(s)/(L(s,χ)E_B(s)) and Γ(s/2)/(2L(s,χ)E_B(s)). Their gamma
factors are nonzero on Re(s)>0. A complete large-shell bound of exponent
γ, for every ε>0 and the required fixed characters, yields the usual
all-height reciprocal-L continuation by Cauchy–Schwarz and Mellin
integration, retaining small x. The principal pole is allowed. Choosing
a different block at each x does not provide one fixed Mellin transform;
the transition costs cannot be dropped. This is a conditional return,
not an estimate for the smoothed arithmetic field.

There is also a sharp-cutoff identity with an explicit small-argument
correction. If min B>√N, then for every real1≤x≤N,

\[
M_\chi(x)=M_{B,\chi}(x)
 -\sum_{p\in B,\ p\le x}\chi(p)M_\chi(x/p).            \tag{95.10}
\]

The correction uses the **original** Mχ, and includes Mχ(1)=1 at x=p.
Two removed primes cannot occur in an integer at most N. For
B⊂(N^α,N^b], 1/2<α<b<1, and an available bound
|Mχ(t)|≤C t^β on t≤N^{1−α}, where0≤β<1, elementary summation gives

\[
\left|\sum_{p\in B,p\le x}\chi(p)M_\chi(x/p)\right|
 \le C\left(1+\frac1{1-\beta}\right)
 N^{\beta+b(1-\beta)}.                                \tag{95.11}
\]

No prime number theorem is required. As b decreases to1/2, this absolute
method approaches exponent (1+β)/2. Using the current β=0.8748540364
would leave exponent greater than0.9374270182, which is inadequate.
To beat the current γ, reach5/6, or reach3/4 by this limiting budget,
one would need respectively β<0.7497080728, β<2/3, or β<1/2, as well as
the independent estimate for M_B and a strict admissible b. These are
unpaid prerequisites. An inadequate upper bound is not a lower bound
for the signed correction.

When used as detectors, the full norm is ||U_B−C_B||², including its cross
term. Chaining prime removal with another detector, or controlling both
simultaneously, remains valid only after paying (95.8)–(95.11) or a
stronger proved signed transfer. Thus the user's mixed chained/simultaneous
strategy remains open in its full scope.

## Native matrix and other audited realizations

The original [native-H source convention](../[private research revision]/h-joint-integration.md)
retains coefficients, root marks once in v,w, masks, profiles, projectors,
all branches and the original normalization. A generic Julia dilation
requires a proved r≥||T|| and K=T/r. Its exact decomposition
||Kv||²+||(I−K*K)^{1/2}v||²=||v||² preserves the entire source cost.
A small observed channel does not pay its almost-complete loss channel,
and r is not free. No native-H adapter or arithmetic norm saving follows.

S17 commutator observations can miss a constant direction; the actual
principal source modulo3 at N=12 gives M=−2 with the tested commuting
residue/equal-bin observations. This is not a theorem about every
logarithmic partition. S11 transport retains ghost and prefix-imbalance
costs. S07's cutoff mask on primes2,3 at N=5 excludes their product6 and
is not a separable tensor mask. These precise failures and reopening
conditions are retained in the reports and first tests.

The author tested S04/S22/S17 and literal uniform draws S11/S23/S07
from group pools22/11/25. Full30-card threshold counts25/12 include cards
outside those groups; no eligible in-group card was excluded for suspected
duplication. Critic priorities and permutation were frozen before its
outcome intake; independent audits were protected S18 and uniform S12.
No stronger timestamp claim for the author's initial pool construction is
made. A preliminary critic UTF8 parser failure and its corrected exact
receipt remain recorded; entropy and selections were not rerolled.

The all-character signed estimate in (95.4), a source-observing scattering
construction, and a signed prime-removal correction are the useful next
targets. Near gains,1/6,1/4, all29 original families/109 children and later
ideas remain available. F0/analytic ancestry, inherited positive-slot
uniformity and external admission remain open. No formalization, new proof
packet or public record claim is part of this cycle.
