## 5. Earlier failures remain correct in their actual scopes

W01 card12/U-SCALE and W21-T28 are the prior observation-set
ancestors. W21 R21.27 takes a nonzero smooth compact bump theta,
repeats it with exponential weights e^(beta*j*tau), and obtains
Laplace transform integral(theta(v)e^-sv)/(1-e^((beta-s)tau)).
Its positive numerator leaves a genuine pole at beta, while a
fixed fraction of every interval has value zero. The example is
smooth with bounds for every fixed derivative, but is not an
entire function of the Gaussian growth used in R39.4. Its original
review explicitly left arithmetic/analytic observability open.
W39 answers that narrower open question rather than refuting the
earlier counterexample.

W38-18 uses bounded integer block coefficients at log positions
v_k and retains a larger exponent beta on O(sqrt J) exceptional
dyads. Throughout |u-v_k|<=2, each of its M_k positive block terms
has weight at least g_tau(3), because its log displacement inside
the block is <=log 2. That neighborhood contains a complete integer
unit interval. For gamma<beta, choose an input epsilon smaller
than beta-gamma; on infinitely many such intervals the whole
field exceeds any fixed C_epsilon e^((gamma+epsilon)j).
No positive-measure good subset exists there. It fails precisely
W39's every-interval hypothesis and remains a valid obstruction
to discarding a sparse collection of whole bad intervals.

The new project-level contribution is the quantitative
Gaussian local-measure interpolation plus proved meromorphic
replenishment and finite iteration. Its elementary interpolation,
complex analysis and lattice counting are not claimed as literature
inventions. No actual new arithmetic small-value estimate appears.

## R8. Blind uniform S15: arbitrary Witten weights retain the full twisted bulk

Use the same downward-closed squarefree q-unit complex as R6. Let S be any positive diagonal matrix, allowed to depend on N, commuting with parity; set

    d_S=S d S^(-1), Q_S=d_S+d_S*, Delta_S=Q_S^2.

Then d_S^2=0, Q_S is odd self-adjoint and Delta_S is the actual positive Laplacian. Delta_S is generally **not** S Delta S^(-1); using the latter would give the wrong adjoint and spectrum. Similarity of d preserves homology, while the positive spectrum can change.

For principal chi, every heat-supertrace equals the index:

    Str(exp(-T Delta_S))=Str Pi_0=Str I=M_chi0(N).

Positive eigenvalues cancel between parities. Any gap or Witten localization leaves the unknown signed principal source in the harmonic index. A small number of signed critical modes requires its own arithmetic estimate; positive spectral information alone does not give one.

For general chi, let D=D_chi be the diagonal character insertion, and Pi_0 the harmonic projection. Since D is even and Q_S is odd, graded cyclicity gives

    Str(D Delta_S exp(-t Delta_S))
        = (1/2) Str([D,Q_S]Q_S exp(-t Delta_S)).

Integrating the exact heat derivative yields, for every T>=0,

    M_chi(N)=Str(D exp(-T Delta_S))
        +(1/2) integral_0^T Str([D,Q_S]Q_S exp(-t Delta_S))dt.   (R8.1)

Every coefficient and conjugation is fixed by the actual adjoint. On an edge n to np, the deletion weight is its orientation times S_n/S_np; therefore

    Str(D Delta_S)
       =sum_edges |S_n/S_np|^2 mu(n)chi(n)(1-chi(p)).          (R8.2)

This is the full weighted first heat derivative, not a new independent signed estimate. Because S and D commute,

    [D,d_S]=S[D,d]S^(-1).

The deformation cannot make a previously nonzero character commutator vanish. A diagonal unitary character gauge has the same limitation. A genuinely different character-preserving complex or source insertion could be considered, but would need its own exact return.

If the positive spectral gap is lambda_*>0, finite-dimensional spectral calculus gives

    |Str(D(exp(-T Delta_S)-Pi_0))|
           <= dim(C) exp(-T lambda_*).                       (R8.3)

Here ||D||=1 on q-unit vertices. The bulk integral in (R8.1) also converges as T->infinity, since Q_S kills Pi_0. Consequently the exact limiting decomposition is a twisted harmonic trace **plus the entire integrated commutator**. A large gap pays only the heat remainder (R8.3). It does not erase either retained term.

An actual ordinary-character example exposes the missing bill. Take the nonprincipal character modulo 3, N=2, basis empty and {2}. Then D=diag(1,-1), Q_S=[[0,w],[w,0]] with w=S_1/S_2>0, Delta_S=w^2 I and Pi_0=0. The true source is M_chi(2)=2, whereas

    Str(D exp(-T Delta_S))=2 exp(-T w^2),
    (1/2) integral_0^T Str([D,Q_S]Q_S exp(-t Delta_S))dt
                                =2(1-exp(-T w^2)).            (R8.4)

Making the gap arbitrarily large drives the first term to zero while the complete bulk returns the full source. This is a counterexample to discarding that term, not an all-scale lower bound for M or a rejection of every Witten method.

The complete arithmetic target is a bound on the **sum** in (R8.1), or its harmonic-plus-integrated-bulk limit, by N^(gamma+epsilon) for every fixed chi. If supplied, it returns to zero exclusion by R9. It is currently equivalent bookkeeping for the unestimated signed source. The source-specific commutator formula extends the author's static S13 trace calculation, while G74 already supplies the general harmonic warning and W59 supplies the cutoff-Hodge ancestry. There is no new general index theorem or proved cancellation here.

at most(U/Y)h0 and weighted mass sum|c_u(h0,h_r)|h0^(delta/2)<<U^epsilon.
The critical h0=1 case already fails; increasing h0 cannot repair it.
Shortened cases do not pay their longer complements. Independent heights,
four clipped profile pairs, shortage and empty-selection alternatives,
zero capacity, fixed-inducing/principal branches, and the original

Nor does the imported density corollary fix the active density gate.
De Faveri Corollary1.5 at n=6, delta=2sigma-1 in[1/3,5/6], saves

    D6=3delta(6delta-1)/(60delta-36delta^2-10).

For delta in[17/25,7/10] its row exponent1-D6 exceeds the retained
rho=1-10delta/[3(5-2delta)] by

    delta(312delta-252delta^2-55) /
      [3(5-2delta)(60delta-36delta^2-10)] >17/100.    (14)

The concave numerator quadratic is at least998/25, delta>=17/25,
and the positive denominator is at most98007/625. The resulting

E_K<=rho+delta v, the new corollary is weaker even on the uncontested

Finally, the separated inverse source in [restricted research revision] has r+s>217/100,
delta in[17/25,7/10], v<=1/20 and target T=delta(r+s)+E_K.
Its merged length b=r+s+v exceeds2.17. Even the sixth-free sieve
cost b exceeds T by at least

    (1-delta)(r+s+v)-rho >=8077/27000.               (15)

The minimum is at v=0,r+s=217/100,delta=7/10: the delta derivative

This is a failure of the proposed sufficient price, not a norm lower

The current [restricted research revision] residual is R_U,hard+R_N,hard, replacing the older
[restricted research revision] R_nonunique+R_middle wording in these raw reports. Its one-sided

# [private research revision]: a conductor saving and the complete shared-zero detector

Accept G114 and G115 at the following written, source-relative scopes.
The [frozen author](joint-density/report.md) and
[independent review](joint-density-review/report.md) contain the complete
arguments; the [retention manifest](retention-manifest.json) binds their
original bytes and ten immutable source inputs. The author's historical
c10 and K=9/2 comparison are preserved. Current c11 remains
312864909/2500000000=.1251459636; no new endpoint follows.
F0/analytic ancestry, original positive-slot uniformity and exact external
root-LFunction definition/import/admission remain OPEN. No formalization
or public-record claim is made.

## 1. G114: primitive conductor on the actual witnessing character

Fix the original finite dictionary, translate, canonical ray quotient and
slots. Put U=Z^W, v=z/W, delta in[17/25,7/10]. The physical bin supplies
the squared price U^(delta v_I+small) for each actual slot subcollection.
Keep this upper price even if a later internal witness buffer rises.

Let one complete nonprincipal character phi have primitive conductor
Q<=U^lambda and a retained high zero. Select that finite label FIRST,
then form the internal buffered maximum for phi and its WHOLE conjugate.
Both have the same Q. An unrelated full-family maximizing label cannot
inherit the conductor bound. Partition the resulting internal bins before
the norm, and fix the cutoff from the original physical delta and lengths
before selecting row witnesses. This is the independent review's necessary
completion of the author's selection argument.

On the internal upper line a' and its reflected line, the primitive
functional equation and the original buffered logarithm estimate give

    |S_phi(U^m)|^2 << U^[delta' min(m,lambda-m)+small] H_J,
    delta'=2a'-1 >= delta-small,  H_J=(1+T)^J.

Redundant Euler holes of polynomial radical size cost only U^epsilon on
the fixed positive strip; their radical does not multiply Q in this
pointwise bound. This does not change the separate original reflected
scale contract. Fixed labels and moving factors all belong to phi;
whole conjugation preserves Q, an additional moving twist need not.

The original same-zero product lower bound, inverse upper bound, and
this plain upper bound imply

    m<=lambda/2+small, r<=t+small, r+m>=t-small,
    |M_phi(U^r)|^2 >= U^(delta r-small).

The comparison first uses delta', then weakens the inverse spike to delta.
It retains one actual character, real part and common height. No independent
witnesses or extra label measure is introduced. Principal inducing
characters keep their original separate branches.

Take lambda0=89/100, 0<=v<=1/20, and fix

    t=1+(3delta/5)(lambda0-2v), r0=t-lambda0/2,
    Ac=1-delta+lambda0 delta(1/2-3delta/5),
    Ec(W,z)=Ac W+(6delta^2/5)z.

The full rectangle has 1<t<3/2, r0>1/2 and
1-2v-r0>=33/2500. For r<1 mark an original slot subset of width just below
min(v,(1-r)/2). MI's gates r+2x<1 and 2r+8x<3 hold with the prescribed
small slack; greedy rounding loses one fine slot width, paid by epsilon.
Pay the actual complement pointwise and divide by the inverse spike:

    I(r)=1-delta r+delta[v-(1-r)/2]_+.

Both pieces decrease and I(r0)=1-delta r0. At r=1 use the original
unmarked scale supremum with an arbitrarily small adjacent-strip loss;
MI is not invoked with zero strict margin. For r>=1 the original free-row
sixth-power inverse amplification and full slot price give

    L(r)=1/6+(5/6-delta)r+delta v <= L(t).

Exact algebra yields 1-delta r0=L(t)=Ec(1,v), exhausting all lengths.
The source scale/Sobolev supremum pays separate rowwise real parts and
heights and the finite derivative profiles. MI permits the actual frozen
bounded prime masks; arbitrary-mask MP is not needed.

Define the historical K=9/2 envelope

    rho=1-10delta/[3(5-2delta)], k=rho+delta-1,
    a=2delta(5-6delta)^2/[3(5-2delta)(115-54delta)],
    b=14delta(5-6delta)/(115-54delta),
    Eold(W,z)=rho W+delta z-min(3kz,aW+bz).

Throughout the rectangle Ec(W,z)<=Eold(W,z)-W/5000. Indeed subtract
Ec+W/5000 from the second affine branch of Eold and multiply by
3(5-2delta)(115-54delta)>0. Its ten degree-(4,1) Bernstein coefficients
are positive, minimum5373459/97656250. This proves the continuum
comparison, including where the other Eold branch is larger. It does
not compare to every later strengthened envelope without another proof.

## 2. Complete raw subclass and complement

For raw rows of width W with z<=W/21, impose on an ACTUAL high character

    Q<=Z^((21/25)W).

Write w=u b^6, preserve the unit and freeze b. Set s=log_Z Nb, V=W-6s.
Use the conductor-bounded natural free core only for the witness; it has
the same positive-real zeros and primitive conductor. Retain every b-hole
on the actual slots as a fixed MI coefficient. Do not falsely assign a
V-scale modulus to the possibly larger raw radical.

When V>=20W/21, z<=V/20 and
(89/100)V-(21/25)W>=4W/525. Thus the free theorem applies with reserve.
Root counting costs Z^s, and

    s+Ec(V,z)=Ec(W,z)-(6Ac-1)s, 6Ac-1>=6869/6250>0.

When V<20W/21 the old unmarked density plus actual high-bin slot price
gives exponent rho W+delta z-(6rho-1)s, with s>W/126. Since G<=3kz,
the reserve after the requested W/5000 is

    (19/54-1/6-3k(.68))/21-1/5000
      =112003/257985000 >0.

Bounded/free fixed-inducing cores have actual raw population
O(Z^(W/6+small)); their high-bin pointwise slot bound fits that reserve.
Branches lacking that bin bound retain their original physical estimate.
Consequently the complete licensed raw subclass has weighted density
at most Z^[Eold(W,z)-W/5000+epsilon]H_J. The high rows with no such
low-conductor witnessing character retain Eold. Their union has no proved
uniform improvement. Repeated prime valuations allow conductor savings
even with empty common support, but neither construct a high zero nor
force every row into this subclass.

Use the restriction only on a positive child norm obtained after complete
signed reconstruction: retain both projectors, the missing radical, all
clipped rectangles and the original label measure counted once. Measure
Q on that complete character. Two restricted Cauchy factors average
their savings; one restricted factor earns only half its exponent gain.
No signed projector is presumed to preserve this row class. Where this
separation is unavailable, use the accepted full estimate.

All low/far-high bins, zero terms, FI populations with actual6a/9a radii,
K_phys^(5/6), shortages/no-slot complements, four independent profiles,
weighted Euler shifts including zero capacity, principal residue and
supremum feedback retain their paid bounds. The exceptional centered
M/24 reserve is unused. Fix losses/mesh before dictionary/profiles,
their finite orders before internal height powers, and raw powers before
tail orders and eventual thresholds. This result supplies no new c.

## 3. G115: complete cutoffs agree at the actual zero

For a fixed natural nonprincipal presentation phi with the original
S-omission, choose smooth V equal1 on[0,1], zero on[2,infinity), and set

    R=U^t, C_R(s)=sum_d mu(d)phi(d)V(Nd/R)(Nd)^(-s),
    A_R(n)=sum_(d|n) mu(d)V(Nd/R).

On the absolute half-plane L^S C_R has coefficient phi(n)A_R(n).
Complete multiplicativity includes natural zeros. The unit coefficient
is1 and A_R(n)=0 for1<Nn<=R; this cancellation is in the COMPLETE signed
divisor sum, not each dyadic inverse/plain piece.

Choose fixed B sufficiently large, Y=U^B, and define

    D_R(s)=sum_(Nn>R) phi(n)A_R(n)(Nn)^(-s)e^(-Nn/Y).

At a retained actual zero rho, Mellin inversion and a shift from2 to-1/4
give D_R(rho)=-1+O(U^-A) for any prescribed A. The Gamma residue is
L^S(rho)C_R(rho)=0; nonprincipality excludes an L-pole. B is chosen after
the finite strip/conductor/height/scale powers so Y^-1/4 pays them. The
unit is e^-1/Y. A smooth terminal cutoff at U^(B+1) costs every fixed
negative power after accounting for raw row/slot powers and derivatives.
The identity allows any fixed bounded t, including2 or3. It does not
invoke the old witness theorem beyond its t in[1,3/2] contract.

For finitely many cutoffs fixed before rows, use the SAME character and
zero. For nonnegative weights with total mass M,

    sum_u w_u D_j(rho_u) conjugate(D_k(rho_u))
      =M+O(U^-A M),
    sum_u w_u |sum_j c_j D_j(rho_u)|^2
      =|sum_j c_j|^2 M+O(U^-A ||c||_1^2 M).

The coefficients c_j are fixed and row independent. Normalized sums and
fixed finite products retain a constant signal; zero-sum combinations
kill it. This is a rank-one limit on actual zero rows. It supplies no
extra power in that signal and says nothing by itself about an ambient
mixed moment or whether selected dyadic witnesses agree. An ambient
signed estimate can still make simultaneous/chained combinations useful.

## 4. An exact positive norm and its fully paid diagonal

After the licensed anchor/orientation change, merge equal ideal products
WITH signs. With original slot product P and fixed slot coefficients alpha,

    D_R(s)Q_u=sum_l b_l(s)psi_u(l),
    b_l(s)=U^(-v/2) sum_(nP=l,Nn>R)
      A_R(n)nu(n)(Nn)^(-s)e^(-Nn/Y)alpha(P).

All independent slot heights, fixed phases, holes and natural zeros remain.
No arithmetic coefficient is hidden in a smooth seminorm. In particular
B3.6 forbids a further column coefficient; divisor boundedness alone does
not license UM/MI/MP or that canonical energy for b_l.

Use the review's explicit norm on I=[a,b],1/2<a<b<1,

    N_t(U)=sum_(u in R_U) w_u sum_(i,j in{0,1})
      integral_I integral_[-T-1,T+1]
        |partial_sigma^i partial_tau^j[D_R(s)Q_u]|^2 d tau d sigma.

R_U is the specified original natural/eligible nonzero row set with
Nu<=CU, fixed before the zero event; w_u is its original positive
radial/divisor weight or paid U^epsilon majorant. Required orientations
and derivative profiles have a fixed finite union cost. Tensor Sobolev
evaluation dominates each retained zero value; derivatives cost logarithms
on fixed polynomial terminal support. Thus a bound for this complete norm
implies the corresponding weighted density. The norm bound remains open.

For sigma in a fixed compact subinterval of(1/2,1), divisor counting gives

    |b_l(s)| << U^[(sigma-1/2)v+epsilon] * (Nl)^(-sigma),
    b_l=0 unless Nl>=c0 U^(t+v).

The same bound with arbitrarily small extra loss pays the finite derivative
list. Write l=c a^6, c sixth-power-free. The diagonal includes ALL pairs
ca^6,cb^6, unequal roots included, with fixed phases and zero masks.
For H>=2 the complete absolute class sum satisfies

    sum_(c sixth-free)[sum_(Nc Na^6>=H)(Nc Na^6)^(-sigma)]^2
      << H^(1-2sigma+epsilon).

For Nc>H, root convergence gives inner bound O((Nc)^-sigma), whose
squared tail is H^(1-2sigma). For Nc<=H, partial summation gives inner
bound H^(1/6-sigma)(Nc)^-1/6. Its square summed over c<=H costs
H^(1/3-2sigma)H^(2/3)=H^(1-2sigma). Enlarging sixth-free c to all ideals
only increases these bounds. Divisor losses, units and ray sectors are
paid; no squarefree density or cancellation is used.

There are O(U^(1+epsilon)) rows. The slots cancel in the exponent because
(2sigma-1)v+(1-2sigma)(t+v)=-(2sigma-1)t. Therefore the complete
within-class contribution D6_t is nonnegative and bounded by

    D6_t(U) << U^[1-(2sigma-1)t+epsilon] H_J.

For the integrated norm use the smallest sigma in I. This covers unequal
sixth roots, merged-product collisions and zero contractions. Define O6_t
as the FULL REAL signed ordered cross-class contribution, including row
kernel, masks, weights and every derivative inner product. Finite truncation
gives N_t=D6_t+O6_t, with tails already paid. Cross-class fixed-inducing
coincidences remain in O6; they are not declared oscillatory.

At t=4/3 and sigma>=(1+delta)/2, the diagonal exponent is at most7/75.
Since delta-3k=4delta^2/(5-2delta)>0, Eold(1,v)>=rho>=19/54.
The gap349/1350 leaves23/2700 after a density saving xi=1/4. Hence

    OPEN-C: O6_(4/3)(U) << U^[Eold(1,v)-xi+epsilon] H_J,
            any fixed0<xi<=1/4,

would imply that density saving with this exact norm. It is a ONE-SIDED
bound on the full signed sum, not an absolute bound on every pair. OPEN-C
is unproved. xi=1/4 here is a density saving, not the zero-free constant.

## 5. Conditional direct return, with the target row and principal pole

For z=0 enlarge the norm to ALL required natural target rows Nu<=U,
including fixed-inducing rows and the actual target unit row with w_1=1.
This is a NEW input, not the old eligible positive-slot theorem. Suppose
for every needed fixed target/rectangle, every epsilon and all large U,

    OPEN-H: O6_t(U)<=C_(epsilon,T) U^(-nu+epsilon), nu>0,
    (2a-1)t>1, sigma>=a>1/2.

Choose epsilon below both strict gaps. The complete positive norm tends
to zero; its unit-row detector value therefore tends to zero. At a
hypothetical nonprincipal zero its value tends to-1, a contradiction.
Constants/thresholds may depend on each fixed target and height rectangle.
Every required rectangle must be covered for the all-height conclusion.
There is no attained family supremum or growing-conductor constant.

For a first improvement c>c11 with c<1/4, t=2 gives exponent4c-1<0.
For c=1/6,t=2 it is-1/3; for c=1/4,t=3 it is-1/2. These are conditional
returns from OPEN-H, which remains unproved. They replace the detector
upstream rather than extrapolate the old physical geometry.

For a principal target the norm must include the principal unit row.
Insert(s+z-1) in the Mellin integral, cancelling the simple L-pole before
the contour shift. Gamma(z+1)=z Gamma(z) gives the exact tail kernel

    D_R^P(s)=sum_(Nn>R) phi(n)A_R(n)(Nn)^(-s)
                [s-1+Nn/Y]e^(-Nn/Y).

At a nontrivial zero rho its value is1-rho+O(U^-A), nonzero for fixed
rho!=1. The added kernel and derivatives obey the same bounds with
polynomial height costs. OPEN-H for this modified detector gives the
same contradiction while allowing the pole at1. For a nonprincipal
target at1 use the unmodified detector, whose signal is-1. Ordinary
right-boundary treatment and the original Hecke-to-ordinary Euler lift
remain their accepted source statements; deleted Euler factors have no
zeros in Re s>0. External definition/admission obligations are unchanged.

## 6. Evidence and next mathematical work

The independent helper uses rational value-to-Bernstein interpolation,
separate from the author's polynomial arithmetic:35 positive coefficients
on7complete boxes,3identities,7scalar reserves/exponents,12examples and
168natural-zero/sextic cases. The author also retains finite initial
Mobius-cancellation checks. These certify algebra only. Root fully read
both mathematical reports/helpers and the original witness/MI/energy
contracts. No unchanged helper was rerun, and no formal tool was used.

The remaining questions are concrete: improve the near-full-conductor
complement, or bound the actual signed O6 after complete coefficient
merging. Fixed-inducing correlations and full norm costs are essential.
Parallel transfer, simultaneous tests and alternation remain compatible;
their gain must come from a proved estimate in the receiving expression,
with every transfer/complement paid. Constant shared-zero signals alone
do not produce it. Preserve the full29-family/109-child portfolio, nearer
targets,1/6 and1/4, and all prior source/author credit.

## 5. Realizability, sharp endpoints, and the signed-profile calculation

The prescribed defects are realizable. On the finite states with 1<=m<=N and y=1 or a reachable prime, define by increasing m

    F_N(m,y)=1-sum_(y<ell<=m)chi0(ell)F_N(floor(m/ell),ell)
                  +Delta_N(m,y).

Every child has smaller m. If Delta vanishes on m<=y^r, that collar is descendant-closed and finite induction gives the exact rough-sum values there. For r>1 these values need not equal 1. Define Delta_N(N,1)=0 and the stated prime-profile residual elsewhere; every other residual is zero. The full root error is therefore the complete scalar in (V4), with no discarded complementary defect. No unknown Mertens value is used as input to the recurrence. Its computational economy or small root value is not asserted.

For the author's smooth profile, g(v)=(v-1)^3(2-v)^3 on [1,2], zero elsewhere, and h(v)=v^2g'(v). This extension is C1, h vanishes at both support endpoints, and

    m0=integral h(v)v^(-2)dv=0,
    m1=integral h(v)v^(-2)log v dv=-integral_1^2 g(v)/v dv<0.

The stated bound |h|<=3/4 follows from v^2<=4, [(v-1)(2-v)]^2<=1/16 and |3-2v|<=1. Direct integration gives m1=8log2-111/20; its sign follows from the positive integral, not a decimal approximation.

For one prime put L=log p, A=N/p^(r+1), u_p=log A/log p, v_m=m/p^r and S_m=W_q(N/(pm),p-). Exactly C_m=-(S_m-S_(m+1)), so zero extension of h gives

    sum_m C_m h(v_m)=-sum_m S_m[h(v_m)-h(v_(m-1))].      (V8)

The sign is minus. The last difference at the upper support boundary is included even when h itself vanishes at that grid endpoint. Omitting that term would break the formula.

For the smooth main approximation s(v) to S_m from (V3), write each increment as integral_(v_(m-1))^(v_m)h'(v)dv. Then

    |sum_m s(v_m)[h(v_m)-h(v_(m-1))]-integral s(v)h'(v)dv|
       <=p^(-r) sup|s'| integral|h'|.

Here sup|s'|=O(A/L^2) on the fixed compact support. This proves the claimed O(A/(p^r L^2)) error without assuming h' is Lipschitz or claiming an unjustified rectangle rule for a merely continuous h'. The uniform source remainder is multiplied by the total variation of h, not by the number of states.

With K=2 in (V3), Taylor expansion and

    integral h'(v)v^(-1)dv=m0,
    integral h'(v)v^(-1)log v dv=m1-m0

give the complete one-prime response

    sum_m C_m h(v_m)=b_(1,q)m1 omega''(u_p) A/L^3
                       +O(A/L^4+A/(p^rL^2)).            (V9)

The b2 term vanishes with m0, so neither its sign nor its numerical value is needed. Summation over the whole prime band adds exactly one logarithm in the denominator and the factor kappa_r:

    F_N(N,1)-M_chi0(N)
      ~ (q/phi(q))m1 omega''(u)kappa_r
                    N P^(-r)/(log P)^4.                (V10)

Choose fixed u>3 with omega''(u)!=0. If omega'' vanished eventually, omega would be affine on a tail, and the delay equation forces its slope to be zero; the constant-tail contradiction then applies. Thus such u exist arbitrarily far out. This confirms Theorem B as a fully induced signed defect, with its original collar and all complements.

## 4. A two-profile packet cancels one Mellin value, not its full component

Take nonzero nonnegative W0,W in C_c^infinity(1,2),
rho_0=1, rho_1=rho=3/2, and W_i(x)=W(x/rho_i).
Both probes use the same arithmetic phases, exclusions,
compensator and inner profile. A fixed dilation changes only
constants and annular endpoints.
The calculation below concerns the raw neutral-ray component.
It does not compute the mixed covariance of compensator branches;
using the same compensator is not a scalar operation on this Gram.

In B0.21--B0.24 notation, put Q=q_(b*)XY, P_a=Y^2/Q,
x_a=q_a/Y, and zeta(a)=chi_a(b*)/(tau_xi xi(a)).
The physical column fields, before separating the moving
radial profile, are

\[
A_i(m)=Y^{-3/2}\sum_{a\in\sigma}
\zeta(a)W_i(x_a)x_a^{-1}g_{\chi_a}(a,-m)
W_0(q_m/(Qx_a)).
\]

Row Poisson applied to A_i conjugate(A_j) gives exactly

\[
\frac Q{Y^3}\sum_{a,b\in\sigma}
\frac{\zeta(a)\overline{\zeta(b)}W_i(x_a)\overline{W_j(x_b)}}{x_ax_b}
\sum_k F(a,b;k)
\widehat{\mathcal W}_{x_a,x_b}(\sqrt Q k/(ab)),\quad
\mathcal W_{x,y}(z)=W_0(q_z/x)\overline{W_0(q_z/y)}. \tag{V16}
\]

Use the manuscript's complex Fourier convention and measure.
Choose the neutral ray a,b=1 modulo a fixed modulus m containing
36, the fixed conductors and supplements. Enlarge the fixed
excluded set S accordingly. On the common-core-one locus
(a,b)=1 and the pure-sixth sector k=r^6, B1.17 then makes
F(a,b;r^6) the indicator of ((ab),r)=1, with its natural zeros.
The resulting signed matrix component is

\[
\frac Q{Y^3|\tau_\xi|^2}
\sum_{\substack{a,b\equiv1\;(m)\\(a,b)=1}}
\frac{W_i(x_a)\overline{W_j(x_b)}}{x_ax_b}
\sum_{\substack{r\ {\rm primary}\\(r,S)=1}}
\mathbf1_{((ab),r)=1}
\widehat{\mathcal W}_{x_a,x_b}(\sqrt Q r^6/(ab)). \tag{V17}
\]

Here r is nonzero. Keep the FULL projector
1_(a,b)=1=sum_(d|a,b)mu(d). A nonzero Poisson sector is not
automatically a positive sub-Gram of the total physical energy.

For completeness, the restricted component has a controlled
continuum limit. Its column zero-mode density is

\[
\zeta_{\mathbb K}^{S}(2)^{-1}\beta(r),\qquad
\beta(r)=\prod_{\mathfrak p\mid r}\frac{Q_{\mathfrak p}-1}
 {Q_{\mathfrak p}+1}.
\]

At p|r the ratio of the two-unit density (1-Q_p^(-1))^2 to
the ordinary coprime-pair density 1-Q_p^(-2) gives this factor.
Writing beta=1*h with h(p)=-2/(Q_p+1) and h(p^j)=0 for j>=2,
fixed-S lattice counting gives, for a fixed smooth decaying profile,

\[
\sum_r\beta(r)\psi(q_r/T)
=\operatorname{Res}_{s=1}\zeta_{\mathbb K}^S(s)
 H_\beta(1)T\int\psi
+O_\psi(T^{1/2}),\quad
H_\beta(1)=\prod_{\mathfrak p\notin S}
 \left(1-\frac2{Q_{\mathfrak p}(Q_{\mathfrak p}+1)}\right)>0.
\]

The error follows since sum_d |h(d)|/sqrt(q_d) converges.
Centered column coefficients after each gcd projector are
periodic; B0.23 can be applied with the coarse period r^6.
Taking column zero modes BEFORE the short-root average, and
then the radial Fourier--Riesz identity, gives the leading matrix

\[
\frac QY P_a^{1/6}C_{\rm exc}\,\mathcal E,\quad
\mathcal E_{ij}=\int_0^\infty
 E_i(R)\overline{E_j(R)}R^{-1/6}\,dR,\quad
E_i(R)=\int W_i(x)x^{-5/6}W_0(R/x)\,dx. \tag{V18}
\]

Here C_exc is a fixed positive scalar. With the manuscript's
normalizations it is
rho_m^2 Res_(s=1)zeta_K^S(s) H_beta(1) C_R /
(6 |tau_xi|^2 zeta_K^S(2)), where
rho_m=2pi/(sqrt(3)q_m) and
C_R=(2pi/sqrt(3))^(2/3) Gamma(1/6)/Gamma(5/6).
The sixth-power substitution supplies the factor 1/6.
For the fixed two profiles the matrix error is

\[
O\left(\frac QY Z^\epsilon
\left[P_a^{1/12}+\frac{P_a^2}{Y}
                     +\frac{P_a^{1/6}}Y\right]\right). \tag{V19}
\]

The terms are respectively the root-lattice error, centered
column cost, and coprimality-density tail. This asymptotic is
useful, for example, for power scales P_a tending to infinity
with P_a^(11/6)=o(Y), taking epsilon smaller than the fixed
power gaps. It does not assert equidistribution of short roots
for each moving pair of columns separately.

The original row puncture |xi(m)|^2, the indicator of (m,b*)=1,
is also retained.
Expand it over d|rad(b*), and enlarge the neutral modulus so
chi_a(d)=1 for these finitely many d. The d-branch replaces
Q by Q/q_d and P_a by P_a q_d. Thus its leading matrix is
multiplied by the positive fixed product
product_(p|b*)(1-Q_p^(-5/6)); the same finite expansion preserves
the error bound. This is not removal of a character zero.

The profile part now has an exact spectral test. For
hat W(s)=int W(x)x^(s-1)dx,

\[
E_1(R)=\rho^{1/6}E_0(R/\rho),\quad
\widehat E_i(s)=\widehat W_0(s)\widehat W_i(s+1/6),\quad
p_i=C_R\widehat W_0(5/6)\widehat W_i(1)
    =C_R\int E_i(R)R^{-1/6}\,dR. \tag{V20}
\]

The other principal factors in B0.35 are common to the probes;
thus p=p0(1,rho). Mellin Plancherel gives

\[
\mathcal E_{ij}=\frac1{2\pi}\int_{\mathbb R}
\Lambda(t)\rho_i^{7/12+it}\rho_j^{7/12-it}\,dt,\quad
\Lambda(t)=|\widehat W_0(5/12+it)\widehat W(7/12+it)|^2. \tag{V21}
\]

Lambda is continuous and positive near zero. The phase
exp(it log rho) is not constant on that interval, so strict
triangle inequality shows
det(E)=rho^(7/6)[(int Lambda/(2pi))^2
-|int Lambda exp(it log rho)/(2pi)|^2]>0.
The leading component has rank two.

The vector c=(-rho^(7/12),1) cancels the evaluation at t=0
and retains p(c)=p0(rho-rho^(7/12))>0. But its exceptional
multiplier rho^(7/12)(exp(it log rho)-1) vanishes only on a
discrete set. It leaves positive full Gram cost. More generally,
Cauchy on the common support 1<R<4rho gives

\[
|p(c)|^2\le C_R^2\left(\int_1^{4\rho}R^{-1/6}\,dR\right)
c^*\mathcal E c. \tag{V22}
\]

This obstructs nulling the specified component separately in
the componentwise budget. It does NOT give a lower bound for
the total physical energy or a universal vector-probe
impossibility theorem. Cancellation against other ray or
common-core sectors requires their actual mixed covariance.

## 6. Fixed components and the exact remaining gate

Fixed column ray refinements twist the angular sums by finitely many
fixed finite-order characters; their infinity types remain nonzero.
Any resulting divisor or common-cube phases have bounded magnitude.
Fixed-place row refinements preserve the nontrivial good conductor
`ce`; their exact local factors are bounded on each fixed positive
strip. Natural zeros, fixed-prime valuations, original profiles,
Mellin roots, and all prescribed fixed components remain accounted for.

Combining with the previously paid unit-core sectors leaves
\[
\boxed{
\mathfrak Q_{\rm rem}
=\mathfrak Q_{\substack{q_c>C\\q_e>C}}
-\mathfrak Q_{II}
+O_\epsilon\!\left(
DK^{1+\epsilon}+D^{11/6+\epsilon}
+K^{1-b}D^{5/6+b+\epsilon}C^{1/6+b}
\right).
}
\tag{DC15}
\]
The original signed II subtraction remains whole. At `C=D^(1/6)`
and `b=7/8`, the complete displayed error is
`O(D^(1.991510694444...+epsilon))` in the requested row range.
T05 remains the physical cube-row II theorem; it is not a whole
C--C estimate.

The next unpaid object is the actual double-large-core C--C term
minus II. For comparison, continuing this pointwise method to
`C=D^(1/5)` costs `D^(2.02619625038...+epsilon)` under the limiting
I-HECKE budget. It would require additional averaging or signed
cancellation. No increase of `c0` is established.

Source anchors: M (1.6), (2.8), (2.14)--(2.15); review [private research revision],
section 1 (unit average, full row Hecke function, primitive good
conductor and ordinary functional equation); [private research revision] T01 (fixed
angular continuation and height growth), T07 (the explicitly stronger
I-HECKE strip); CS6--CS9 in the accepted pure-cube packet; and
UC4--UC15 in the one-unit-core draft.

### 2.2 Applying L1 to the COMPLETE Gaussian

For any coefficients with A_b=sum |a_n|n^-b<infinity at a fixed b>0, the completed square yields the entire bound

    |sum a_n g_tau(log n-z)|
      <= (2pi tau)^(-1/2) A_b
          exp(b Re z+tau b^2/2+(Im z)^2/(2tau)).       (L3)

For f3*chi take any b>1; all coefficients have modulus at most1. Let

    M_j=max_(u in[j,j+1]) |F_chi(u)|,
    J_j=integral_j^(j+1) log|F_chi(u)|du.              (L4)

The field is nonzero (its Mellin transform is nonzero on an absolute-convergence line), so M_j>0. Choose t0 at a maximizer and a radius R_j in[sqrt j,2sqrt j] containing no boundary zero. L3 bounds log B_j<=(b+2/tau)j+O_(b,tau,a)(sqrt j+1). With eta_j=8/log R_j=O(1/log j), L1 gives the exact inequality

    (1+eta_j) log M_j <= J_j+eta_j log B_j.            (L5)

Consequently, for every fixed gamma, the following EVERY-interval statements are equivalent:

    (i) J_j <= (gamma+epsilon)j+C_epsilon
        for every epsilon>0 and every sufficiently large integer j;
    (ii) M_j <<_epsilon exp((gamma+epsilon)j).          (L6)

The reverse implication is immediate. For the forward implication insert(i) into L5; its extra term is O(j/log j)=o(j), with every buffer fixed before j grows. Negative logarithms near real zeros are retained and cannot hide a larger exponential maximum. Missing intervals and finite numerical samples do not satisfy(i).

This supplies the nonconcentration condition absent from the earlier logarithmic-action card W21-T29, for this fixed Gaussian analytic class. It is stronger in input form than the positive logarithmic criterion: no log(1+|F|) or truncation of negative logarithms is required. It does not assert that a bound for a finite truncated field passes through log near its zeros.

## 4. A uniform strictly better density for a concrete class

Set lambda0=89/100. Consider the free high rows for which at least one actual buffered high zero has a witnessing primitive conductor Q<=U^lambda0. Define, before witnesses,

    t=1+(3delta/5)(lambda0-2v),
    r0=t-lambda0/2,
    Ac(delta)=1-delta+lambda0 delta(1/2-3delta/5),
    Ec(delta;W,z)=Ac(delta)W+(6delta^2/5)z.                (J4)

On the whole rectangle delta in [.68,.70], v in [0,.05],

    1<t<3/2, r0>1/2,
    1-2v-r0>=33/2500>1/100.                              (J5)

The supported inverse length obeys r>=r0 up to the small budget. For r<=1, choose an original slot subcollection of width just below
min(v,(1-r)/2). The choice depends on frozen lengths and witness dyads, not the live row. The existing fine mesh loses at most one slot width. The second MI inequality has a fixed reserve because r>=1/2 and v<=1/20. Dividing the inverse witness, applying MI to the marked subset and paying the remaining actual slots pointwise gives

    I(r)=1-delta r+delta[v-(1-r)/2]_+,   r<=1.            (J6)

Both pieces decrease with r. By J5, I(r0)=1-delta r0. This elementary use of MI is derived here; it does not import the preceding pending amplitude-conditioned theorem. It needs no conditioned amplitude grade and no marked-plain theorem.

For r>=1, the old unmarked sixth-power inverse amplification and the full slot pointwise price give

    L(r)=1/6+(5/6-delta)r+delta v.

This increases with r and is at most L(t). The cutoff J4 satisfies the exact balance

    1-delta r0=L(t)=Ec(delta;1,v).                        (J7)

Thus every inverse-length regime is covered. The witness dyad union, separate rowwise heights/real powers and all required derivative profiles are covered by the source scale/Sobolev supremum. No improved moment is called on a descendant. The resulting actual free-row estimate is

    sum_(high,eligible,free; low-conductor zero) |Q_u|^2
       << Z^[Ec(delta;W,z)+epsilon] (1+T)^J.              (J8)

It is a strict improvement on the accepted weighted density:

    Ec(delta;W,z) <= Eold(delta;W,z)-W/5000.              (J9)

For a transparent exact certificate, Eold is the maximum of
rho W+(delta-3k)z and (rho-a_delta)W+(delta-b_delta)z.
It suffices to subtract Ec+W/5000 from the SECOND expression. Clear the positive denominator 3(5-2delta)(115-54delta). `check.py` constructs that polynomial directly from J1 and J4 and gives all positive rational Bernstein coefficients on the entire two-dimensional box. It also certifies the cutoff/capacity/root-decay gates and the two exact J7 identities. There are seven positive polynomial certificates, 35 coefficients and twelve exact illustrative values. The examples are not the continuum proof.

The primitive conductor information is substantive. It can occur with c_s=d_s=b2=rbar=0: for example, a dual free row with a prime of valuation two has a primitive conductor contribution of one prime norm but row norm contribution of its square. This describes legal geometry, not the existence of a high zero. It is distinct from Hval's common-support gain. Conversely a squarefree natural row can have Q comparable to its full norm. Empty common support alone does not force J8.

## 6. A second exact target: signed near pairs

For the finite coefficient family G13 the physical Gram kernel is

    K_X(n,m)=g_(2tau)(log(n/m))
       *integral_0^(log2)g_(tau/2)(u-log(sqrt(nm)/X))du.  (G22)

The full energy equals sum c_rect,X(n)c_rect,X(m)K_X(n,m).
The kernel is entrywise positive; its coefficient products are signed.
The true n=m diagonal is X^(1+o(1)): use d_3(n)^2<=d_9(n) and the
divisor-sum bound. For fixed r>0 the complete absolute far-pair sum,
|log(n/m)|>r sqrt L, is at most

    X^(2-r^2/(4tau)+o(1)).                              (G23)

At tau=1, r=2 pays both the diagonal and the far pairs at exponent1.
Thus for gamma>1/2 it suffices to bound the **complete signed
off-diagonal near scalar** at exponent2gamma. This near scalar need
not be nonnegative. Dropping its negative terms or bounding unrelated
positive subblocks does not prove the required upper bound. G22â€“23
are for the new Gaussian field, not for an SP subfamily.

statement:
# Complete stationary cofactor payment and constant inverse cuts

[private research revision] controller acceptance after complete independent review and source
reconstruction. No new c, formalization or public-record claim.

The theorem improves the actual compensated ordinary-character source:
it pays the entire small-double source including every stationary alias.
This permits constant inverse cutoffs and halves the cofactor exponent
in the remaining signed core. All complementary sources are paid. The
arithmetic bound for that full core is still open.

Current source-relative c11=312864909/2500000000=.1251459636 and
gamma11=2187135091/2500000000=.8748540364 are unchanged. The preceding-c10
SAME-family license for K=28114053/6250000 is not bootstrapped from c11.
Analytic ancestry, original positive-slot uniformity and external
definition/import/admission remain open. The ordinary source below
does not automatically replace the native Hecke source.

Credit remains with [restricted research revision]/[restricted research revision]'s compensated periodic source, [restricted research revision]'s complete
Liouville square-short and tail results, and [restricted research revision]'s complete large-gcd
theorem. [restricted research revision]'s old UV cap does not include the new UV=X^gamma choice.
Earlier nonstationary Poisson removals do not pay this whole stationary
bank. The source-specific improvement is the complete estimate below.

## G188. A complete periodic-cofactor estimate

Fix bounded mean-zero Q-periodic b, X>=2 and any finite real D>=1. All A_m are fixed before x in [X,2X], with |A_m|<=A.
Write f_x(n)=exp(-n/x^(3/2)-i(n/x)^6) and use shell measure dx/x.
Then the theorem is

    H_D(x)=sum_(m<=D) A_m sum_(l>=1)b(l)f_x(ml),
    ||H_D||_1+||H_D||_2 << A(D+X^(3/4))log^4(2X).          (G188.1)

Constants retain only Q and ||b||inf (and the fixed cutoff). For D
bounded by a fixed power of X, divisor-bounded A_m replace the logarithm
by X^epsilon, for every epsilon after choosing the divisor loss. There is no growing-period, live-x coefficient or
arbitrary output/cofactor mask permission.

Take a fixed smooth nonincreasing phi equal1 on[0,1], zero on[2,infinity)
and w(t)=phi(t/2)-phi(t). The exact identity

    1=phi(n/X)+sum_(j>=0)w(n/(2^j X))                     (G188.2)

retains all transitions and the infinite damped tail. On the low part,
rows m<=delta_Q X have nonzero Fourier derivatives separated from
integers, including the last increment, for a sufficiently small fixed
delta_Q. Discrete first derivative and Abel summation give O_Q(1).
Larger active low rows have m<=2X and at most 2/delta_Q terms, so each
costs O_Q(1) trivially. All low rows cost O(A min(D,X))<=O(AD).

On a high block N=2^jX, rows m>4N are exactly empty. Remove these
before Poisson and use the frozen interval [M,2M) intersect[1,D]
intersect[1,4N]. In particular m/N<=4. Put T=(N/X)^6.
Poisson, with b expanded at period Q, gives EXACTLY

    sum_l b(l)w(ml/N)f_x(ml)=(1/m)sum_(h in Z)beta_h I_(h/m)(x),
    I_r=int_0^infinity w(n/N)e^(-n/x^(3/2))
                  exp(i[2pi r n/Q-(n/x)^6])dn.             (G188.3)

The periodic beta_h obey beta_(Qj)=0. Both signs and every alias remain.
For r>0, the critical point and its phase are

    n_r=(pi r/(3Q))^(1/5)x^(6/5),
    phase=5(pi/(3Q))^(6/5)r^(6/5)x^(6/5),
    second derivative=-30n_r^4/x^6.

Choose an ambient near range c_QT/N<=r<=C_QT/N before x or live labels,
wide enough to contain every stationary point meeting [N,4N]. The
rescaled phases form a compact nondegenerate family. Smooth stationary
phase, including smooth support crossings, yields

    I_r=Z_r exp(i*kappa_Q*r^(6/5)x^(6/5)-i*pi/4)
                      +O((N/T)e^(-cN/X^(3/2))),
    Z_r=sqrt(pi/15)x^3 n_r^(-2)w(n_r/N)e^(-n_r/x^(3/2)).   (G188.4)

Its uniformity follows from a compact Morse change and bounded damped
amplitude derivatives. Sharp stationary endpoints are not erased:
the argument completes the entire source before using smooth blocks.

Let H_m=mT/N. Near aliases number O(1+H_m), and any nonempty near bank
has H_m bounded below, so their total remainder after1/m is O(1)
with damping. Negative and small nonstationary aliases have rescaled
derivative comparable T; two integrations by parts give O(T^-1) after
summing them. The entire large-alias tail sums (m/N)h^-2, costing
O(T^-1) or O(m/N). Thus the whole transformed row has a damped O(1)
error, and the row-block error is O(AM e^(-cN/X^(3/2))).

Reduce r=h/m=u/v, so m=vj,h=uj. The ENTIRE Z_r and phase depend only
on r,N,x. The only remaining separate m factor is1/m. Consequently

    C_(u/v)=sum_(vj in original row block) A_(vj)beta_(uj)/(vj)

is x-independent and |C_(u/v)|<<A/v. All original truncations, Fourier
zeros and collisions are retained. Since u>=1 and r<=C_QT/N,
v>=N/(C_QT), while v<=2M. Therefore

    sum_r |C_r|^2 << A^2 sum_(max(1,N/(C_QT))<=v<=2M)
                         (vT/N+1)/v^2
                    << A^2(T/N)log(2M).                    (G188.5)

The lower denominator bound is essential; dropping it introduces an
unpaid N^2/T term.

For x=Xz, the first two needed amplitude bounds are
|Z_r|+|dZ_r/dz|<<(N/sqrt T)e^(-cN/X^(3/2)). Distinct r,s have phase
derivative comparable N|r-s|. One integration by parts retains both
shell endpoints and bounds their full inner product by

    (N^2/T)e^(-cN/X^(3/2))min(1,1/(N|r-s|)).               (G188.6)

The diagonal uses the same estimate with minimum1. Distinct reduced
fractions with denominators<=2M are separated by1/(4M^2). There are
J<<M+M^2T/N, and the full kernel row sum is
O(1+(M^2/N)log(2+J)). Applying2|C_r C_s|<=|C_r|^2+|C_s|^2 to the
entire pair sum and using(G188.5) proves

    ||whole (M,N) block||_2^2
         <<A^2 e^(-cN/X^(3/2))(N+M^2)log^2(2N).             (G188.7)

The already bounded row error is included by norm triangle. Summing
whole blocks in norm retains all cross terms. Since M<=4N, all
logarithms are O(log(2N)) without a log D. For fixed N, M sums to
O(min(D,N)), while the sqrt N part acquires at most log(2N). Thus the
whole high source is at most

    A sum_(N=2^jX)e^(-cN/X^(3/2))
        [sqrt N log^2(2N)+min(D,N)log(2N)].

The two sums are bounded by X^(3/4)log^2(2X) and D log^2(2X).
The infinite damped tail converges; finite-measure Cauchy gives L1.
This proves the arbitrary finite D extension, independently developed
by the reviewer and reconstructed by root. It does not assert an
infinite undamped coefficient bank or a different phase theorem.

## G189. Full constant-cut source transfer

For fixed ordinary chi modulo q and p not dividing q, let a=lambda chi,
h=chi and s(r^2)=chi(r)^2, zero off squares. Define

    q1=delta1-p chi(p)delta_p,
    q2=delta1-p chi(p)^2 delta_(p^2), v=q1*q2,
    b0=v*h, c=a*a*b0=v*a*s,
    b0(l)=chi(l)[1-p1_(p|l)-p1_(p^2|l)+p^2 1_(p^3|l)].     (G189.1)

The coefficient at p^2 in q2 is -p, not -p^2. The literal b0 has
fixed period p^3q, mean zero and bounded size. Natural character zeros,
shared factors and both physical compensations are preserved.

Fix3/4<=gamma<1 and a shell-frozen tau in the closed corridor
max(gamma tau,gamma(1-tau))<=(11gamma-3)/8. Set

    L=X^gamma, M=X^((6-2gamma)/4),
    U=X^(gamma tau), V=X^(gamma(1-tau)), G=X^(1-gamma).

The exact ordered identity is

    c=Q_U+Q_V-S+R,
    Q_U=a_(<=U)*(v*s), Q_V=a_(<=V)*(v*s),
    S=a_(<=U)*a_(<=V)*b0, R=a_(>U)*a_(>V)*b0.              (G189.2)

The whole S has frozen coefficients A_m=sum_(de=m,d<=U,e<=V)a(d)a(e),
supported m<=UV=L and bounded by d2(m). G188 pays its COMPLETE source
by X^(gamma+epsilon), including all stationary and infinite-tail terms.

[restricted research revision]'s square-short result permits frozen infinite root prefixes. For
D=X^alpha its four norm exponents are alpha,(3+8alpha)/11,
3/8+alpha/4, min(3/10+7alpha/10,15/32+alpha/4). All are<=gamma in
the stated corridor. Both physical labels1,p, weights1,-p chi(p), and
natural root zeros chi(r)^2(1-p1_(p|r)) remain in that complete result.

Every R tuple has de>UV=L, so the entire prefix n<=L is identically
empty. Its full infinite tail n>M has squared norm at most
X^(3/2+epsilon)+X^6 M^(-4+epsilon)<=X^(2gamma+epsilon).
[restricted research revision] G182 pays every remaining tuple with gcd(d,e)>G, under the
literal mask L<del<=M,d>U,e>V, by
X^epsilon[X/G+X^(3/4)/sqrtG]<=X^(gamma+epsilon).

Thus, defining the COMPLETE finite core

    T_rect=sum_(L<n<=M)f_x(n)
       sum_(del=n,d>U,e>V,gcd(d,e)<=G)a(d)a(e)b0(l),

the source transfer is

    ||C-T_rect||_(1,2)<<X^(gamma+epsilon), C=sum_n c(n)f_x(n). (G189.3)

All constants are uniform over allowed frozen tau, a compact corridor
for each fixed gamma. Endpoint gamma=3/4 and corridor equality remain
included with every-epsilon losses. No extra gcd involving l is imposed.

The old adaptive core T_ad has the same output window/gcd restriction
but smaller inverse cuts. Its removed signed wedge is paid by
||T_ad-T_rect||<=||T_ad-C||+||C-T_rect||. This uses TWO independently
proved complete transfers, never monotonicity under signed restriction.

Every retained cofactor has l<M/L=X^(3(1-gamma)/2), half the old
high-end adaptive exponent3(1-gamma). At gamma11 this is .1877189454;
at gamma=.8748 it is .1878; at5/6 it is1/4; at3/4 it is3/8.
Balanced inverse floors become X^(gamma/2). The exact merged source is
a(m)b0(l) times the ordered count of allowed de=m; Liouville complete
multiplicativity includes shared primes and natural zeros. It supplies
an identity, not arithmetic cancellation.

For one common gamma<gamma11 chosen before chi/zeros, OPEN-RECT asks
||T_rect||_1<<X^(gamma+epsilon) for every epsilon, all sufficiently
large dyadic shells, every fixed chi and both members of a fixed
covering prime pair. Tau may depend on fixed data, epsilon and shell,
but stays frozen before x. L2 suffices. A single cell, sampled x,
fixed loss or finite-height sample does not meet this hypothesis.

G189.3 makes that full norm hypothesis equivalent to the corresponding
complete C norm, and hence to the old core norm; it is not claimed
equivalent to zero exclusion. The fixed-source Mellin return retains

    D_c(z)=P_p(z)J_p(z)L(2z,chi^2)^2/L(z,chi),
    P_p=1-chi(p)p^(1-z), J_p=1-chi(p)^2p^(1-2z),
    H_p(z)=Gamma(z/6)e^(-i*pi*z/12)D_c(z)/6+E_p(z),
    E_p holomorphic on Re z>1/2.                           (G189.4)

The all-shell bound continues H_p above gamma with an epsilon buffer.
The numerator has no zeros there except P_p on Re z=1. Two distinct
unramified primes cover its nonzero-height zeros; for nonprincipal chi
one covering prime has chi(p)!=1 to cover height zero. The principal
pole at1 remains the allowed exception. This is the inherited complete
conditional ordinary-character all-height return, not a new theorem
for growing conductor or native Hecke coefficients. No variable b/k
or omitted shifted Mellin term is introduced here.

## G190. A paid diagonal and the actual remaining correlation

Take balanced cuts and gamma>6/7. First remove the gcd mask from the
WHOLE finite core with G182's paid cost. On each full original dyadic
cell n~N>=X,d~D,e~E,DE*l~N, orient D>=E; both exceed a constant times
X^(gamma/2). Cauchy in d retains the diagonal and the full e,e' Gram.
For e'=e+h the difference-phase derivative in d is comparable
T*h/(DE), T=(N/X)^6. Its maximum is O(T/D)=o(1), since
N<=M gives T<=X^(3(1-gamma)) and gamma>6/7.

The two exact product-cut intervals intersect in one interval or none.
First-derivative summation, with both endpoints and actual damping,
gives |K_(e,e+h)|<<min(D,DE/(T*h)). Summing ALL h and both orders,
including the diagonal, gives

    |sum_(d,e) a(d)a(e)f_x(del)|
        <<DE[E^(-1/2)+T^(-1/2)sqrt(log(2E))].              (G190.1)

After every cofactor and original dyadic label, the whole N block costs
X^epsilon[N X^(-gamma/4)+X^3/N^2]. The first term is paid by X^gamma
through N<=M when gamma>=6/7. The second is paid only at the top end.
The complete coarse calculation, including L<N<X, still gives X^(1+
epsilon). It proves no first gain, and no lower bound for the signed sum.

Before absolutes, the exact offdiagonal is

    B_(l,x)=2Re sum_(e<e') lambda(ee')chi(e)conj(chi(e'))
       sum_(d in I_e intersect I_e')
       exp(-i[(del/x)^6-(de'l/x)^6]) times both damping factors.

Natural zeros stay present; eliminating a(d) by Cauchy does not create
independent signs. A SUFFICIENT one-sided arithmetic input is

    B_(l,x)<=C_epsilon D E^2 X^epsilon (X^gamma/N)^2        (G190.2)

for EVERY finite-core cell, including N<X, each l and every real x.
This sufficient Gram condition and its diagonal budget also include
gamma=6/7. The coarse first-derivative test above requires strict
gamma>6/7; an O(1) derivative at equality need not avoid integer aliases.
The diagonal is already paid: E>~X^(gamma/2)>=(N/X^gamma)^2 up to
fixed cell factors when gamma>=6/7. Thus(G190.2) would give
DE X^(gamma+epsilon)/N, and the full cofactor sum costs only harmonic
factors. Negative B helps; an absolute correlation estimate is stronger
than needed.

For N>=X, the available coarse estimate misses(G190.2) by
X^(6-2gamma)/N^4=(M/N)^4. For L<N<X the gap is(N/L)^2.
At N~X the missing squared saving is X^(2(1-gamma)). Actual shifted
Liouville products lambda(e(e+h)) have been identified, not estimated.
This is the remaining arithmetic problem, together with possible
alternative complete norm arguments. No value of c is increased.

The nearer gamma=.8748 would give conditional c=.1252, exceeding c11
by135091/2500000000. The1/6 and1/4 targets keep the constant-cut transfer,
although the coarse small-derivative/diagonal argument above was only
claimed for gamma>6/7. Supporting finite checks verify transcription,
alias grouping and rational budgets; they are not the analytic proof.

## Evidence and scope

[Author](lcg-stationary/report.md) and [independent review](lcg-stationary-review/report.md) retain the full proofs; [review support](lcg-stationary-review/support.md) supplies the uniform Morse remainder. Sixteen frozen files and eighteen source bindings are preserved in the [retention manifest](retention-manifest.json). The author and reviewer each ran one distinct finite transcription check; neither was rerun by the controller. Both owners explicitly stopped and normally released their own claims. Standard stationary phase is credited to Tao’s 2007 lecture notes; novelty here is the complete source estimate and its paid application, with no literature-priority claim.

## G224. Exact chirp and paired-character audits, with reconstruction paid

The two independent unselected audits preserve useful alternatives and
their exact limits. For z=a-i kappa, a>0, the analytic square root gives

    sqrt(z/(2*pi)) exp(t^2/(2z))
       *int_R exp(-z u^2/2+i t u)du=1,
    P_z(t)=(|z|/a)^1/2 exp(a t^2/(2|z|^2)).                 (224.1)

The first identity follows by the Gaussian Fourier integral and normal
continuation on Re z>0. The second is its exact completely absolute
price. On |t|<=T set E=a T^2/(2|z|^2)>0,
C=|kappa|T^2/(2|z|^2). Then P_z(T)=(1+(C/E)^2)^1/4 e^E
>=sqrt(C)e^E/sqrt(E)>=sqrt(2e C). A power-sized exterior chirp C=X^delta
therefore costs at least X^(delta/2) under absolute payment. Finite
insertion is legitimate; infinite insertion must pay its exterior
exponential against the original full tail. Signed/L2 use remains open.

For odd prime Q, A nonzero mod Q, c=(4A)^-1 and
G_A=sum_v e_Q(A v^2), completing the square gives
sum_v e_Q(A v^2+t v)=G_A e_Q(-c t^2), |G_A|^2=Q.
For actual residue sums B_r and F_v=sum_r B_r e_Q(c r^2+v r),

    S=sum_r B_r=G_A^-1 sum_v e_Q(A v^2)F_v,
    sum_v |F_v|^2=Q sum_r |B_r|^2,
    |S|^2=Q^-1 sum_(v,w)e_Q(A(v^2-w^2))F_v conjugate(F_w).
                                                               (224.2)

All crosses and natural zeros remain. The Cauchy bound |S|^2<=sum_v|F_v|^2
is generically sharp: B_r=1 gives equality Q^2. That is an ambient
coherent example, not a claim about the actual arithmetic residue array.
The four-point curvature of one bilinear t=mn channel has phase
c(m^2-m'^2)(n^2-n'^2)+v(m-m')(n-n'); complete channel recombination
restores multiplier1. A selected curved channel is not a full estimate.

The other audit distinguishes conjugate heights and observation loss.
F_barchi(s)=conjugate(F_chi(conjugate(s))) for F=1/L. A pole at rho maps
to conjugate(rho), not necessarily rho. For a Laurent vector with leading
coefficient v and continuous observation A(s), the leading squared signal
is v* A(rho)* A(rho) v. Positive semidefiniteness alone can annihilate v;
one needs coverage of actual residue directions, or a uniform lower
singular-value bound. A complete bank must keep every associated source.

At real x, the actual pair satisfies
||(M_chi(x),M_barchi(x))||^2=2|M_chi(x)|^2. This also holds with common
REAL weights; complex weights and heights must be conjugated as well.
A full every-epsilon shell-L1 pair estimate has the ordinary all-height
Abel return in G222, but is exactly the scalar estimate up to sqrt2.
The difference observation for a real character is identically zero.
Degenerating coordinate changes must pay their inverse. These adapters
preserve existing detector/curvature ancestry and supply no exponent gain.

The author's other selected tests retain the complete asymmetric
hyperbola identity u_U*u_V*chi=a-m_U-m_V+m_U*m_V*chi. Its principal
absolute long-long tuple price is at least const X when U,V<=sqrt X/2,
by pairs of squarefree q-units in(sqrt X/2,sqrt X]. This is not a signed
corner lower bound. Exterior-boundary and least-prime matching tests
duplicate G164-G165: the outgoing boundary remains, critical coordinates
need not be harmonic, and the matched character bulk a(n)(1-chi(p))
cannot be discarded outside the principal case. Their failures and all
22 untested cards are retained without broad rejection of the mechanisms.

## 2. G117: two precisely scoped certificate obstructions

For squarefree q-units n<=N, put a_n=mu(n)chi(n). All k! orderings of its
k prime factors have the SAME arithmetic sign/phase. The map summing a
word fiber to n has norm sqrt(k!), while its minimum-norm right inverse
averages with1/k!. Its generic Cauchy price is

    sqrt(sum_n1/omega(n)!) sqrt(sum_n omega(n)!) >= #S.

More generally, for orthogonal integer fibers H_n with
<u_n,v_n>=1 (linear first slot), U=sum a_nu_n and V=sum v_n have
<U,V>=M_chi(N), but ||U||||V||>=sum||u_n||||v_n||>=#S.
The square-divisor identity gives

    #S=kappa_q N+O_q(sqrt N),
    kappa_q=(phi(q)/q) product_(p not dividing q)(1-p^-2)>0.

This is a floor on a PRODUCT-OF-NORMS certificate, not on M_chi. Arbitrary
geometry within fibers and exact diagonal rescaling cannot remove it;
correlations between different integers or a source-specific scalar estimate
remain outside the obstruction. Ordered-word/readout ancestry is retained.

For B_gamma, all f=0 below1 with norm sup_x x^-gamma|f(x)|, the dilation
T_c f(x)=sum_(n<=x)c(n)f(x/n) has extended norm
sum_n|c(n)|n^-gamma. Triangle gives the upper bound and alignment on
distinct x/n attains each finite prefix. This also holds on the all-scale
FLOOR-INVARIANT space: for fixed K take X>K(K+1), so each floor(X/n),n<=K,
is a singleton fiber among ALL n'<=X. Assign its aligning value and let
X tend to infinity. This does not identify one finite-X merged norm with
an unmerged price.

For any fixed finitely supported complex b, set r=delta-b*chi. If b(1)=0,
r(1)=1 implies ||T_r||>=1. Otherwise r(p)=-b(1)chi(p) for every
unramified prime beyond its support, and sum_p p^-gamma diverges for
0<gamma<=1. Divergence follows from the elementary Euler-product/harmonic
sum argument at gamma=1; finitely many ramified omissions do not matter.
Thus this full norm cannot certify a strict contraction.

Were ||T_r||<1 possible, the return would be legitimate:
T_chi M=1 gives M=T_b1+T_rM. The Banach solution is identified with actual
M by induction on integer intervals, since b(1)!=0 and all other x/n<x;
one need not assume M initially belongs to B_gamma. The premise fails,
not that identification. Infinite/moving preconditioners with fully paid
tails, arithmetic invariant spaces and signed norms remain eligible.

statement:
### 6.2 The full Gaussian observable is not a positive-real impedance

The initially proposed direct impedance would need a positive-real observable, in particular a nonnegative real part on its intended right half-plane. The standard finite-dimensional rational positive-real definition and its realization conditions were checked against Timothy H. Hughes, *A theory of passive linear systems with no assumptions*, arXiv1611.06140v3, Section2/Lemma1. This citation fixes the meaning of the proposal; no rational realization theorem is being imported for an infinite Dirichlet series. [Primary source](https://arxiv.org/html/1611.06140v3#S2).

The literal untwisted canonical prime2 factor (1-2*2^-s)/(1-2^-s) is negative at real0<s<1. That alone rejects a factorwise claim that each source factor is positive-real on the target strip; it is not a statement about the full product there.

A decisive COMPLETE-field test needs no unproved zero-free premise. At Re(s)>1 let D(s)=sum_n f3(n)chi(n)n^-s, so Mellin(F)(s)=exp(tau*s^2/2)D(s). Because the coefficient of1 is1 and all coefficients have modulus<=1,

    Re D(4+it)>=1-sum_(n>=2)n^-4>=2/3.                (31)

The last bound follows by integral comparison from1 to infinity. Set t=pi/(4tau). Then the Gaussian phase is exp(i*tau*4*t)=-1, and

    Re Mellin(F)(4+i*pi/(4tau))
       <=-(2/3)exp(8tau-pi^2/(32tau))<0.              (32)

This holds for every fixed tau>0 and every ordinary character including its zeros. The same certificate applies to B and U. Thus none of these full fixed Gaussian Mellin transforms is positive-real on a half-plane containing that point, including any proposed Re(s)>gamma with gamma<1. A Laplacian/dissipation certificate for this literal direct observable cannot be obtained merely from a passive-network interpretation.

Stripping the Gaussian, changing the readout, using a vector impedance, or a different supply rate changes the proposal and needs its own quantitative return. Those alternatives are not disproved. The test gives no lower bound for the physical field and no statement that all passive approaches to L-functions are impossible. The full-field sign certificate is self-contained; the unsuccessful oversized MIT PDF fetch is retained only as retrieval history, not supporting evidence.

## 2. Literal source contract and the same buffered grade

Use exactly PR9 B0.3--4 and B3.31: the Eisenstein ideal sum with primary/unit convention, fixed excluded set S, natural character zeros, one entire orientation

    phi_u(n)=nu(n) psi_u(n)^(+/-1),
    M_u(E)=E^(-1/2) sum_n mu(n)phi_u(n)W_I(Nn/E),
    S_u(E)=E^(-1/2) sum_n phi_u(n)W_P(Nn/E).

The fixed finite phase nu need not have order six. Let Q_u be the unchanged product of original disjoint prime slots, with total width v and all its individual fixed coefficients, canonical pools, holes and independent heights. In MI these coefficients may be arbitrary bounded row-independent coefficients; this is not a permission for arbitrary coefficients in MP or in the canonical column energy B3.6. The original re-anchoring to a witness label is the accepted [restricted research revision]/[restricted research revision] interface, not a new assumption that unrelated labels have the same zero.

Fix physical delta in[17/25,7/10], v in[0,1/20], 0<eta<=1/1000 and G137's cutoff t=t_*(delta,v)-eta BEFORE witnesses. Restrict to its crossing window |r-r_*(t)|<=2eta with the already allocated endpoint padding, r+m>=t-small and 0<=m<=1/2+small. Fix a witness label, internal bin and dyads R=U^r,D=U^m before their norm. The original finite unions and logarithmic dyad counts cost the already allocated small loss. Omega consists of the licensed nonprincipal supported-witness rows in this window; no all-length extension is claimed. Principal, artificial and fixed-inducing exceptional branches are not inserted into Omega. H_J denotes a fixed polynomial in the original height bounds; it is independent of the arithmetic thresholds G,H and T used below, and its degree may increase between inequalities.

PR9 B0.13 constructs a finite internal bin with a<=B_i<a+e and B_(i+1)<a+2e. The actual zero has a<=Re(rho)<a+e in the retained box. Write beta=2a-1. The internal grade can exceed the physical delta, but beta>=delta-small and beta lies in a fixed compact subset of(0,1); the preceding source-relative SAME-family bound supplies beta<=3/4 here. B0.19--20 first gives the SAME-character, SAME-real-power and SAME-height product spike with this beta. Dividing by its two B0.15 upper bounds gives B0.18 at this beta, before any weakening. In particular

    |S_u(D)|^2 >= D^beta U^(-epsilon_det).             (R3)

For every actual shortened E<=C D the direct, unreflected Mellin line Re(s)=a+6e in B0.15 gives

    |S_u(E)|^2 <= H_J U^(epsilon_det) E^beta.          (R4)

The fixed real powers and finite derivative profiles are carried in the same common smooth tests. Shortening E does not select another bin, height, zero or character. The direct line is sufficient even if a small endpoint tolerance leaves m just above 1/2. There is no need to claim an improved reflected-conductor estimate. Fixed positive-strip deleted Euler factors of polynomial radical size cost U^epsilon; they retain their natural zeros. For subunit E, a nonempty annulus forces E>=c>0, so R4 holds by a fixed constant; smaller E are empty.

Using D^delta as the only spike while retaining E^beta in R4 would lose D^(beta-delta). That would invalidate the claimed small saving. The author avoids this error. In the review below beta cancels at the D scale, and only then is beta weakened to delta in the saved exponent. No internal grade replaces the physical upper slot price.

# [private research revision]: moving finite detectors with a paid fixed-detector return

Root accepts the useful quantitative comparison below from the
[W55 author](wild55/report.md) and [independent review](wild55-review/report.md).
It includes the entire infinite comparison tail and both finite branches.
The remaining signed arithmetic estimate is OPEN. No larger c is proved:
`c11=312864909/2500000000=.1251459636`, `theta11=.8748540364` remain
source-relative, with inherited F0/analytic ancestry, positive-slot
uniformity and external definition/import/admission obligations OPEN.

The [retention manifest](retention-manifest.json) preserves twenty-eight
byte-identical artifacts and seventeen immutable source bindings, all
thirty candidate dispositions, three saved random draws and the two
independent audits. Actual claim snapshots remain local. This cycle
does not perform formalization or create another proof packet.

## G134. Uniform second-order moving Riesz comparison

For each fixed ordinary Dirichlet character chi, including principal,
imprimitive and complex characters with their presented-modulus zeros,
put `a(n)=mu(n)chi(n)`, `M(t)=sum_(n<=t)a(n)` and

    E(x)=sum_(n>=1)a(n)exp(-n/x),
    R_r(N)=sum_(n<=N)a(n)(1-n/N)^r,
    B_r(x)=R_r(rx), V_r(x)=2B_(2r)(x)-B_r(x).

Endpoint n=N has weight zero. For real r>=2 and an explicit summatory
input `|M(t)|<=C t^beta`, beta>0, the complete bounds are

    |B_r(x)-E(x)| <= C K1(beta)x^beta/r,
    |V_r(x)-E(x)| <= (3/2)C K2(beta)x^beta/r^2,           (1)
    K1=5*2^(beta+2)Gamma(beta+2)+2^(beta+3)Gamma(beta+3),
    K2=12*2^(beta+3)Gamma(beta+3)
       +4*2^(beta+4)Gamma(beta+4)+2^(beta+5)Gamma(beta+5).

These hold for every x>0 and real r>=2, uniformly in both. The unconditional
input beta=C=1 gives K1=176 and K2=11904, hence second-order constant17856.
A stronger summatory beta is an extra hypothesis, not a consequence of
writing down the accepted c alone.

Here is a global remainder proof. Set `k_r(u)=(1-u/r)_+^r` and
`A(u)=u-u^2/2`. On `0<=u<=r/2`, write
`z=(r-1)log(1-u/r)+u`. The complete logarithmic series gives

    z<=u/r, |z|<=(u+u^2)/r,
    |z-A(u)/r|<=(u^2/2+2u^3/3)/r^2.

Apply `|exp(z)-1-z|<=(z^2/2)exp(max(z,0))` and
`exp(-u+max(z,0))<=exp(-u/2)`. Then

    |k'_r+exp(-u)| <= (5u+u^2)exp(-u/2)/r,
    |k'_r+exp(-u)(1+A/r)| <= P(u)exp(-u/2)/r^2,
    P(u)=12u^2+4u^3+u^4.                                (2)

For `u>=r/2`, the derivative is zero beyond r and at most exp(-u/2)
in modulus on its support. Since `r<=2u`, multiplying the proposed
second inequality by r^2 costs at most `2r^2+r|A|<=10u^2+u^3<=P`.
The first inequality follows from `2<=4u/r`. Thus (2) covers the full
positive half-line, not just the expanding finite interval.

Abel integration with vanishing endpoints gives

    sum_n a(n)h(n/x)=-int_0^infty M(xu)h'(u)du.

Integrating (2) against C x^beta u^beta proves the first part of (1).
Writing `k'_r=-exp(-u)(1+A/r)+e_r`, the first-order term cancels
exactly in `2k'_(2r)-k'_r+exp(-u)`. The remaining multiplier is
`2/4+1=3/2`; integration proves the second part. This pays the branch
`rx<n<=2rx`, endpoint integers and the entire exponential tail. Any
squared V norm retains `4|B_(2r)|^2+|B_r|^2-4Re(B_(2r)conj(B_r))`.

On each shell [X,2X], freeze one `r_X=max(2,ceil(X^delta))`. Equation (1)
gives a uniform pointwise and L2(dx/x) comparison error
`O(X^(beta-2delta))`. Therefore the every-positive-epsilon shell exponent
gamma for the moving V is equivalent to that of the fixed E whenever
`beta-2delta<=gamma`. Strict inequality supplies a fixed margin.

Only after this comparison use the fixed Mellin transform. Absolute
Fubini for Re(s)>1 and substitution n/x give

    Mellin(E)(s)=Gamma(s)/L(s,chi),
    Mellin(R_r)(s)=Gamma(s)Gamma(r+1)/(Gamma(s+r+1)L(s,chi)).

The beta identity and nonvanishing Gamma are classical
[DLMF facts](https://dlmf.nist.gov/5.12.E1), with
[Gamma's analytic properties](https://dlmf.nist.gov/5.2).
A fixed-field dyadic exponent gamma>0 makes its Mellin integral
holomorphic on Re(s)>gamma: choose epsilon below the compact set's
distance to gamma and sum by Cauchy–Schwarz, including every logarithmic
derivative. E decays exponentially at zero; fixed R_r vanishes below1.
Multiply by L and continue the identity. Every hypothetical L-zero at
any fixed height contradicts the nonzero numerator. The principal pole
is treated meromorphically, not mistaken for a zero. Constants may depend
on each fixed character; no growing-conductor uniformity is asserted.

A moving-r field has no direct fixed-r Mellin formula. Nor is a difference
of two Gamma quotients automatically nonzero. The comparison to E avoids
both issues. With beta=1, the following are sufficient conditional targets:

|gamma|c|delta|Complete comparison error exponent|
|---|---|---|---|
|.87485|.12515|.063|.874|
|5/6|1/6|.084|.832|
|3/4|1/4|.126|.748|

The largest raw cutoff is `4r_X X`, of order `X^(1+delta)`. A raw-cutoff
bound with exponent eta yields `(1+delta)eta` only with constants uniform
in the moving order. The decreasing integral bound `|B_r(x)|<=x` gives
`|V_r(x)|<=3x`, still exponent one. Increasing r alone gains nothing.
The new useful component is the uniform actual-source comparison, not
a new Mellin principle or arithmetic saving. Only fixed extrapolation
order two is proved; growing extrapolation order has no paid bound here.

## G135. Exact rank and renewal targets, with their costs retained

For fixed q and each unit residue a, let u_(a,k) and v_(a,k) list the
mu=+1 and mu=-1 integers in order. For `1/2<gamma<1`, the following
conditions are equivalent, also with every-positive-epsilon losses:

1. Every character mod q has `M_chi(x)=O(x^gamma)`.
2. Every unit residue has `M_(q,a)(x)=O(x^gamma)`.
3. Both lists are infinite and `|u_(a,k)-v_(a,k)|=O(k^gamma)` for every k.

The first equivalence is the full finite character transform, including
principal and imprimitive characters. For the forward rank statement,
expand mu^2 by square divisors to obtain

    Q_(q,a)(x)=d_q x+O_q(sqrt x),
    d_q=(q*zeta(2))^(-1)product_(p|q)(1-p^(-2))^(-1)>0.

Each of at most sqrt(x) progression counts has error O(1); completing
the absolutely convergent d^(-2) tail costs O(sqrt(x)). Hence the two
signed counting functions are `d_q x/2+O(x^gamma)`, with infinite lists
and inverse ranks `2k/d_q+O(k^gamma)`. Conversely, each rank pair crossing
x has k<=x, length O(x^gamma), and a distinct lower endpoint in the last
O(x^gamma) integers before x. This bounds the discrepancy without an
infinite rearrangement. Finite lists have exactly |M_(q,a)(N)| unmatched
end ranks; dropping them would drop the target itself. This refines the
existing transport formulation, with no improved infinite displacement.

For the same actual a(n), the exact prime-power identity is
`a log=-a*(Lambda chi)`. Set
`R(x)=sum_(d<=x)Lambda(d)chi(d)M(x/d)=-sum_(n<=x)a(n)log n`.
Finite Abel summation gives

    M(x)log x=int_1^x M(t)dt/t-R(x),
    M(x)=1-R(x)/log x-int_2^x R(t)dt/[t(log t)^2].        (3)

The source constant1 and endpoint at2 are essential. For gamma>0,
`R=O(x^gamma log x)` and `M=O(x^gamma)` are equivalent, including
epsilon losses. This locates the full signed correlation, not a weaker
new hypothesis.

For `S_gamma(X)=sum_(d<=X)Lambda(d)|chi(d)|d^(-gamma)`,
`sum Lambda(d)floor(X/d)=log(floor X!)` implies
`S_1(X)>=log X-O_q(1)`. Removing finitely many ramified prime-power rays
costs a finite constant. Set `Y=exp(sqrt(log X))`. Since Lambda(d)<=log d,
`S_1(Y)<=(1/2)log X+O(sqrt(log X))`. Thus for every fixed0<gamma<1,

    S_gamma(X)/log X >=(1/2+o(1))exp((1-gamma)sqrt(log X)) -> infinity.

At gamma=1 the lower limiting ratio is at least one. This rules out
the proposed absolute normalized small-gain bound without using a prime
number theorem. It is never a lower bound for signed R or M. A complete
source-specific signed estimate remains eligible.

## G136. Paid coupling repair and complete resonant feedback

The independent protected audit separates ordinary coupling conservation
from the actual divisor map. A coupling with additive marginal a(n) and
multiplicative marginal `(a*chi)(n)=delta_(n=1)` would have total masses
M(N) and1, so ordinarily cannot exist. A repair must carry M(N)-1.

For feasible equal-mass marginals r,c and allowed finite edges E, the
minimum full total variation is exactly

    inf_(BZ=(r,c)) sum_E|Z_ij|
      =sup_(|u_i+v_j|<=1) Re[sum conj(u_i)r_i+sum conj(v_j)c_j].

This is finite-dimensional quotient-norm duality: the compact image of
the unit ball has a supporting functional giving the constraint above.
For real coefficients it is a linear program; for complex character
coefficients it is a modulus/SOCP problem. Singleton additive cells force
full TV `sum|a(n)|=kappa_q N+O_q(sqrt N)`. This is not a bound on every
possible defect. Two equal arrays have zero difference at any common M,
so a small marginal-preserving difference alone supplies no cancellation.

The literal repair instead uses triangular divisor matrices

    C_(n,d)=chi(n/d)1_(d|n),
    A_(n,d)=mu(n/d)chi(n/d)1_(d|n), AC=CA=I.

For a candidate vector v and `e=Cv-e_1`, exact inversion gives `v-a=Ae`.
Grouping n=kd, for every integer interval (L,U] one obtains

    sum_(L<n<=U)v_n-[M(U)-M(L)]
      =sum_(k<=U)e_k[M(floor(U/k))-M(floor(L/k))].        (4)

Thus small candidate readout AND a bound on the entire signed response
return the desired M bound. Unrestricted weighted error TV has scalar
operator norm `max_k |M(floor(N/k))|/w_k`, attained by a single aligned
error; k=1 already contains M(N). Actual compatible defects can evade
that ambient worst case only through a proved restriction. This is a
source-exact application of the existing inverse/adjoint principle.

The independent uniform audit preserves the original native H tensor,
both projectors, masks, signed short core, CRT phase, angular factors
and1/Q normalization from [[restricted research revision]](../[private research revision]/h-joint-integration.md) and
[G89](../[private research revision]/wild48-integration.md). Splitting its source into a unit
mode v and its orthogonal complement retains BOTH scalar readout and
innovation. A small innovation cannot discard the scalar.

If an exact compatible scale map is actually constructed with block
coefficients a_j,b_j,c_j,D_j, then

    alpha_(j+1)=a_j alpha_j+b_j eta_j,
    eta_(j+1)=c_j alpha_j+D_j eta_j,
    alpha_(j+1)=a_j alpha_j+b_j D_(j-1)...D_0 eta_0
       +sum_(k<j)b_j D_(j-1)...D_(k+1)c_k alpha_k.        (5)

Every empty product is the identity; actual forcing needs its complete
Duhamel terms. For the diagnostic `T=[[1,e],[e,0]]`, D=0 while
`alpha_(j+1)=alpha_j+e^2 alpha_(j-1)` has a root above1. Changing the
feedback sign changes the conclusion. This is a scoped objection to
innovation-only reasoning, not a native arithmetic lower bound. The
actual scale map, conditioning and complete signed feedback remain OPEN.

## Preserved tests and next action

The three other first tests retain the finite-prime inverse absolute-tail
failure, the near-resonant Lyapunov conditioning cost, and the full twisted
prime-removal bulk. The squarefree complex is a complex; its classical
Betti description is credited to [Bjorner, Theorem3.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1101.5704).
For a nonreal chi(p), the bulk `(1-chi(p))T_p(x/p)` cannot be deleted.
Neither this familiar topology nor its unsigned rank is a new signed
estimate. The inaccurate S09 seed equation remains frozen with its
explicit correction; all untested ideas retain their status.

Independent checks cover512 prime-log identities,640 twisted identities,
1152 complete matching readouts,18 two-branch Riesz cases,9 divisor
interval responses, both feedback signs and two exact metrics. They also
replay the saved23/12/25 author pools and protectedS28/uniformS15 audits
without new entropy. Floating experiments are diagnostics with no
roundoff enclosure or asymptotic credit. Infinite conclusions use proofs.

The decisive new use is a complete moving V shell bound at common
`gamma<.8748540364` for every fixed character; G134 then pays its return.
All branches, cross terms and moving-order constants remain mandatory.
Absent that input, retain the adapter in the library without creating a
duplicate active research lane. The full29-family/109-child portfolio
and nearer targets,1/6,1/4 remain preserved.
