# [private research revision] headroom pass: signed integer renewal and its friable mean

Working mathematical record, started 2026-10-12 08:26:56 UTC. This is a distinct pass,
not a continuation of the frozen arithmetic-dilation pass. Sole writer:
task [private operational identifier omitted] in this directory. No formalization.

Current comparison is the accepted, source-relative c8=.12514261,
gamma8=.87485739. Neither the .12514475 source candidate nor another valuation
candidate is assumed. All PR9/Gao import qualifications remain. No claim of
a new zero-free exponent is made in this saved prefix.

## Discovery and selection

The full current attempt index and recombination policy were read. The
29-family/109-child library is retained; this pass rotates away from periodic
dilations, the Gaussian growing-order core, and the live PR15 valuation lane.
The distinct mechanisms considered before selection were:

1. Integer-state least-prime renewal, using G92's exact coalescence before
   estimating residuals. Actual smooth-Mobius sums, rather than the unmerged
   real-state count, control its norm. Selected for development below.
2. Selberg's logarithmic convolution identity for mu, followed by a signed
   Volterra estimate. Direct absolute convolution with an x^gamma bound
   returns exponent1; a useful result would need signed prime-kernel control.
3. Close-ratio, odd-parity prime-product exchanges with revisits, as a repair
   of G93's increasing-prime greedy matching. Its full sharp boundary and
   character phases need a new matching theorem; the first-prime boundary
   theorem is not repeated here.
4. A higher-order simultaneous logarithmic-derivative detector. Prime
   positivity helps selected real characters but no uniform all-character
   bridge follows; fixed numerator zeros and full height scope must survive.
5. Type-I/II decomposition of the actual mu convolution, with short-interval
   multiplicative estimates as an outside input. The primary Matomaki--
   Radziwill theorem gives almost-all interval cancellation, not the uniform
   power-saving estimate needed for all renewal states.
6. A growing exact renewal collar, making the remaining smooth-prime state
   space small. This trades state count for exact high-depth collar values;
   no bound for those values is available for free. It is distinct from a
   fixed collar, but cannot be credited by counting remaining states alone.

The strongest source-specific issue in (1) is now being tested: friable mu
has a genuine Buchstab main term at fixed log(x)/log(y)>1. If it survives the
integer-state sums, G92's previously open independent-state norm cannot have
any fixed sublinear power. The possible constructive repair is to subtract
that deterministic mean and retain the structured, signed residual. This is
an arithmetic calculation, not a general countermodel or a declaration that
all renewal strategies are equivalent to Mertens.

## Exact inherited source, with no character or endpoint deletion

For ordinary chi, the least-prime recurrence for the rough sum R(t,y) is
R(t,y)=1-sum_(y<p<=t) chi(p)R(t/p,p). For a floor-invariant approximation F,
let Delta(t,y)=F(t,y)-1+sum_(y<p<=t)chi(p)F(t/p,p).
At integer root N, G92 proves the complete identity

    F(N,1)-M_chi(N) = Delta(N,1)
                    + sum_(p,m) C_(N,chi)(m,p) Delta(m,p),
    C_(N,chi)(m,p) = -chi(p) sum_(N/[p(m+1)]<u<=N/(pm),P+(u)<p)
                                     mu(u)chi(u).

Here P+(1)=1, all squareful and ramified zeros are literal, and no path-depth
tag is retained. For an exact integer collar m<=p^r, integer r>=1, the exact
independent-state sup-to-scalar norm is

    B_(r,chi)(N)=1+sum_(p,m>p^r)|C_(N,chi)(m,p)|.

The cross-depth cancellation at (N,p,m)=(20196,17,18) is inherited, not a new
finding. G92 deliberately did not infer a lower bound for B from its
unmerged real-state theorem. This pass addresses that missing issue using
the actual principal-character coefficients.

## External input, now checked from the original page images

Gerald Tenenbaum, *Sur un probleme d'Erdos et Alladi*, Seminaire de Theorie
des Nombres, Paris 1988--89, Birkhauser 1990, author-hosted original PDF:
https://tenenb.perso.math.cnrs.fr/PPP/Erdos-Alladi.pdf . Theorem2 and Theorem3
give a fixed-u expansion of the friable Mobius sum in terms of Buchstab
derivatives. The original PDF was downloaded and pages224--226 (PDF5--7)
were rendered and visually checked. The live-web text alone was insufficient:
it mangles both the derivative and the logarithm powers. The consequence
used below is a fixed-compact expansion, not a growing-order assertion.

Matomaki--Radziwill, *Multiplicative functions in short intervals*, Annals
183 (2016), https://annals.math.princeton.edu/wp-content/uploads/annals-v183-n3-p06-p.pdf,
was located as the outside short-interval mechanism. It is not being used
as a uniform power-saving assertion. Public source dates and live retrieval
are kept separate.

## 1. The fixed-compact arithmetic input

Write W(x,y)=sum_(n<=x,P+(n)<=y)mu(n), and let omega be the standard
Buchstab function: omega(u)=0 for u<1, omega(u)=1/u for 1<=u<=2,
and (u*omega(u))'=omega(u-1) for u>2. For every FIXED integer K>=1 and
compact interval I contained in (K+1,infinity), the cited Theorems2--3 imply

    W(x,y)=x sum_(j=1)^K a_j omega^(j)(u)/(log y)^(j+1)
               + O_(I,K)(x/(log y)^(K+2)),                 (1)
    u=log x/log y in I, y->infinity,
    sum_(j>=1) a_j z^j = 1/((1+z)*zeta(1+z)).

This is the entire external friable estimate used here. The coefficient
a1=1 follows from the simple pole of zeta at1. To check applicability:
choose fixed epsilon in (0,1/3) in the source's domain
exp((log x)^(2/3+epsilon))<=y<=x. Fixed u in I satisfies that domain for
large y. I lies above all the exceptional integers1,...,K+1, and hence
satisfies its D_K(log y) condition. The source's additional error is
O(Psi(x,y)/L_epsilon(y)); Psi<=x and L_epsilon grows faster than every
fixed power of log y. The constants are uniform on I, but NOT asserted
uniform when K or I grows with x. No zero-free strip stronger than the
classical input of this published theorem is being imported.

The strict prime cutoff in G92 is handled by y=p-1, exactly, not by
discarding multiples of p. Replacing log(p-1) by log p in a fixed-compact
expansion changes the expression by O_(I,K)(x/(p*(log p)^2)), absorbed in
the remainder in (1).

For any fixed modulus q, let W_q(x,p-)=sum_(n<=x,P+(n)<p,(n,q)=1)mu(n).
Once p exceeds every prime factor of q, the same expansion is

    W_q(x,p-)=x sum_(j=1)^K b_(j,q) omega^(j)(u)/(log p)^(j+1)
                  +O_(I,K,q)(x/(log p)^(K+2)),             (2)
    sum_(j>=1)b_(j,q)z^j = A_q(1+z)/((1+z)*zeta(1+z)),
    A_q(s)=product_(ell|q)(1-ell^(-s))^(-1),
    b_(1,q)=A_q(1)=q/phi(q), u=log x/log p.

Proof of this finite-modulus extension: exactly
W_q(x,p-)=sum_(d:q-smooth)W(x/d,p-), with W(t,p-)=0 for t<1.
The local factor at a prime dividing q cancels by convolution; repeated
powers in d are necessary. Truncate d at D=(log p)^B. For fixed q and
any 0<eta<1, sum_(q-smooth d>D)1/d <=D^(-eta) A_q(1-eta), so the discarded
part is O_q(x D^(-eta)). Choose B to absorb the desired fixed logarithmic
error. On d<=D, log d/log p tends uniformly to0; apply (1) on a slightly
larger fixed compact, and Taylor-expand each omega derivative. The convergent
moments sum_(q-smooth d)(log d)^l/d identify the coefficients with the
Taylor product in (2). The Taylor remainders are paid by the next convergent
fixed logarithmic moment; the required derivatives are bounded on the
chosen compact neighborhood. Thus (2) preserves natural zeros at all primes dividing q.
It is a PRINCIPAL-character statement. No corresponding main term for a
nonprincipal character is asserted.

## 2. The merged integer-state norm has exponent1 for every fixed collar

THEOREM A. Fix an integer r>=1 and a fixed principal ordinary character
chi0 modulo q. For G92's complete integer-state norm,

    lim_(N->infinity) log B_(r,chi0)(N)/log N =1.          (3)

More precisely, fix u>2 with omega'(u)!=0 and put

    P=N^(1/(u+r+1)),  kappa_r=(1-2^(-r))/r.

Then, as N runs through all sufficiently large positive integers,

    sum_(P<p<=2P) sum_(m>p^r) C_(N,chi0)(m,p)
       ~ -(q/phi(q))*omega'(u)*kappa_r
                    *N*P^(-r)/(log P)^3.                (4)

Consequently B_(r,chi0)(N) is at least a positive constant times
N^((u+1)/(u+r+1))/(log N)^3. This is a lower bound for the actual merged
coefficient norm; no unmerged count is substituted.

Proof. For fixed p, all integers m>p^r form a consecutive half-line. Its
disjoint intervals (N/[p(m+1)],N/(pm)] cover exactly

    (0,U_p],  U_p=N/(p*(p^r+1)).

Therefore their COMPLETE signed sum is

    sum_(m>p^r) C_(N,chi0)(m,p)=-W_q(U_p,p-).             (5)

For p in (P,2P], p is unramified for sufficiently large N,
U_p=(N/p^(r+1))*(1+O(p^(-r))), and

    log U_p/log p = u+O_(u,r)(1/log P).

The same small compact neighborhood of u works for EVERY prime in the
band. Formula(2), K=1, now gives uniformly

    W_q(U_p,p-)=(q/phi(q))*(omega'(u)+o(1))
                         *N/(p^(r+1)*(log P)^2).

All these block sums have one sign. Ordinary PNT and partial summation give

    sum_(P<p<=2P) p^(-r-1)
           ~ kappa_r P^(-r)/log P.

Together these prove (4). In particular the boundary m=p^r is not included;
using p^r instead of p^r+1 in (5) would be an incorrect exact identity.

For every arbitrarily large U there is u>U, away from integers, with
omega'(u)!=0. Otherwise omega would be constant on a tail. The equation
u*omega'(u)=omega(u-1)-omega(u) propagates that constant backwards one
unit at a time to (1,2), contradicting omega(u)=1/u. Continuity of omega'
at the selected u gives the required fixed-sign compact neighborhood.
Thus the exponents (u+1)/(u+r+1) in (4) approach1. The elementary upper
bound B<=N follows by expanding each merged coefficient, counting each
squarefree d exactly once, and using |chi0(d)|<=1. This proves (3).

This proves an issue explicitly left OPEN in G92 A5. The previously known
real-state exponent1 does not prove (3); equation(5) and the nonzero
friable main term do. The old example of complete cancellation in a single
integer fibre remains true and is compatible with (3).

An especially structured worst-case residual already witnesses (4): set
Delta(m,p) equal to one common sign for p in (P,2P] and m>p^r, and zero
elsewhere. It is bounded, constant across quotient states, and has no
path-depth tag. Finite triangular back substitution constructs a
floor-invariant F with precisely this residual and the exact collar.
This is NOT an assertion that a particular natural approximation has that
residual, and NOT a lower bound for M_chi.

## 3. Trying a signed repair that annihilates the leading mean

Taking absolute values was the proposed norm improvement; theoremA defeats
it even after exact integer coalescence. A more plausible repair gives the
residual a signed quotient profile chosen to cancel the leading mean.
Here that construction can be tested completely rather than guessed.

Let g(v)=(v-1)^3*(2-v)^3 on [1,2] and0 elsewhere, and set

    h(v)=v^2*g'(v),
    m0=integral_1^2 h(v)/v^2 dv=0,
    m1=integral_1^2 h(v)*log(v)/v^2 dv
         =-integral_1^2 g(v)/v dv <0.                    (6)

The extension g is C^2; h is C^1 with h(1)=h(2)=0 and |h|<=3/4.
This is an actual signed profile with its complete leading mean removed.
At each integer N prescribe the residual

    Delta_N(m,p)=1_(P<p<=2P)*h(m/p^r),
    Delta_N(N,1)=0,

and zero at all other states. It vanishes on the entire exact collar
m<=p^r. The finite recurrence

    F_N(m,y)=1-sum_(y<ell<=m,ell prime)
                    chi0(ell)F_N(floor(m/ell),ell)+Delta_N(m,y)          (7)

constructs the approximation and its defect, with all child states smaller
than m. Set Delta=0 unless y is a prime or the root as above. This defines
F_N without using an unknown value of M in its construction. Its exact
collar values are the genuine rough sums, not an imposed constant1.
The root error is the full G92 scalar, with no complementary residual.

THEOREM B. Fix u>3 with omega''(u)!=0, P=N^(1/(u+r+1)), and fixed q,r.
For (7), the exact signed root error satisfies

    F_N(N,1)-M_chi0(N)
      ~ (q/phi(q))*m1*omega''(u)*kappa_r
                         *N*P^(-r)/(log P)^4.            (8)

Thus the leading cancellation in (6) earns one logarithm but no fixed
power. For any gamma<1 choose a sufficiently large fixed u with omega''(u)
nonzero and (u+1)/(u+r+1)>gamma. Then this bounded, signed, exact-collar
residual has root error larger than N^gamma. This is a fully induced
defect calculation, not just a formal subtraction from a bound.

Proof. Put L=log p, A=N/p^(r+1), u_p=log A/log p, and v_m=m/p^r.
Let S_m=W_q(N/(pm),p-). Exactly C_m=-(S_m-S_(m+1)). Because h vanishes
at the endpoints and outside [1,2], discrete summation by parts gives

    sum_m C_m*h(v_m)=-sum_m S_m*(h(v_m)-h(v_(m-1))).     (9)

There are no omitted terms at either sharp support endpoint. Apply (2)
with K=2 uniformly on v in [1,2], using a fixed compact near u>3:

    S_m=A/v_m*[ b1*omega'(u_p-log(v_m)/L)/L^2
                +b2*omega''(u_p-log(v_m)/L)/L^3]
                          +O_(q,r,u)(A/L^4).

The total variation of the fixed h is bounded, so the remainder stays
O(A/L^4) in (9), rather than being multiplied by the number of m. Replacing
the main smooth sum by its integral has error O(A/(p^r*L^2)), which is
smaller. Taylor expansion and integration by parts give

    integral h'(v)/v dv=m0=0,
    integral h'(v)*log(v)/v dv=m1-m0=m1.

Hence the COMPLETE prime block is

    sum_m C_m*h(v_m)=b1*m1*omega''(u_p)*A/L^3
                 +O(A/L^4+A/(p^r*L^2)).                 (10)

The b2 term also vanishes by m0=0; no value or sign of b2 is needed.
Now u_p=u+O(1/log P), and PNT sums (10) over the entire prime band to
give (8). The principal natural zeros were already included in (2).

To justify arbitrarily large u with omega''(u)!=0, if omega'' vanished
on a tail then omega would be affine there. Substitution into
u*omega'=omega(u-1)-omega(u) forces its slope to vanish. The constant-tail
contradiction from theoremA applies. Thus the theorem is nonvacuous beyond
every prescribed target threshold, without a floating-point derivative
test or a conjecture about oscillations.

This construction is root-adapted through P and N, as the independent
error-norm question allows. It is an obstruction for a fixed-shape
annihilation certificate, not a claim that all source residuals are free
to vary this way. Its recurrence is finite but no economy of computing
the exact collar is asserted.

## 4. What more moment cancellation buys, and what it does not

The preceding repair has a complete generalization. Let h be a nonzero
fixed C^1 function compactly supported in (1,V), with possibly complex
values, and define m_j=integral h(v)*v^(-2)*(log v)^j dv. There is a finite
least J with m_J!=0: otherwise the continuous finite measure h(v)v^(-2)dv
annihilates every polynomial in log v, hence every continuous function on
its compact support, and is zero. This contradicts h!=0.

THEOREM C. For fixed u>J+2 with omega^(J+1)(u)!=0, the root residual
Delta_N(m,p)=1_(P<p<=2P)*h(m/p^r) has complete signed response

    sum_(p,m) C_(N,chi0)(m,p)*Delta_N(m,p)
       ~ [(q/phi(q))*(-1)^(J+1)*m_J/J!]
          *omega^(J+1)(u)*kappa_r
                   *N*P^(-r)/(log P)^(J+3).              (11)

Proof: in (9), use (2) through order J+1 and expand each derivative in
log v/log p. The exact identity

    integral h'(v)*v^(-1)*(log v)^l dv=m_l-l*m_(l-1)

(m_(-1)=0) makes every l<J term vanish. The first remaining contribution
has source index1 and Taylor index J, giving (11); all higher source
indices contribute only later logarithmic orders. Total variation pays
the complete uniform source remainder, and the Riemann error is
O(N*p^(-r-1)*p^(-r)/(log p)^2), negligible against every fixed logarithmic
order. The prime-band calculation is exactly the one already proved.

For every fixed k>=1, omega^(k) is nonzero at arbitrarily large points.
If it vanished on a tail, omega would be a polynomial there. A polynomial
of positive degree cannot satisfy u*omega'(u)=omega(u-1)-omega(u), by
comparison of the highest powers. The remaining constant case propagates
backwards and contradicts 1/u on (1,2). Thus suitable u exist beyond any
target threshold, avoiding the finitely many differentiability boundaries.

TheoremC gives an actual signed estimate with a logarithmic improvement
for every specified finite moment cancellation. It also says that NO
nonzero fixed compact quotient profile annihilates enough of the arithmetic
mean to force a fixed sublinear power uniformly in the root. Increasing a
fixed finite cancellation order changes a logarithm, not the exponent.
This does not cover N-dependent profiles of growing order, additional
cancellation across distinct prime bands, or residuals constrained by a
different arithmetic construction. Those are genuine reopening conditions.

A second version of the repair is to subtract the known Buchstab prefix
directly. For a fixed K, define a deterministic H_(K,p)(v) to agree with

    v sum_(j=1)^K b_(j,q)*omega^(j)(log v/log p)/(log p)^(j+1)

on the fixed compact u-range in question, and to vanish for sufficiently
small v. Retain any transition exactly. Write W_q=H_(K,p)+E_(K,p), and
replace each coefficient difference by the sum of its H and E differences.
For any finite quotient block [a,b], the E contribution is EXACTLY

    -E(N/(pa))*Delta_a+E(N/[p(b+1)])*Delta_b
    -sum_(m=a+1)^b E(N/(pm))*(Delta_m-Delta_(m-1)).        (12)

The identical H expression must still be added. Therefore subtraction
does not erase a deterministic boundary source or the variation cost.
With a fixed-variation residual, (2) only bounds (12) by a fixed logarithmic
improvement to its previous size. With an arbitrary bounded residual,
its variation can be the number of cells, so even that improvement is not
automatic. The explicit profile in (6) actually pays this variation and
boundary, and its surviving term is (8).

Letting K grow with N is NOT licensed by Tenenbaum's fixed-K theorem.
At a minimum, a growing-order version would need uniform constants,
uniform control near all derivative jumps, exact treatment of the growing
transition and collar, and a bound for the complete restored H contribution.
These are analytic prerequisites, not consequences of a finite certificate.

## 5. Complete return, the first-gain budget, and exact limitations

For a new floor-invariant approximation to prove an ordinary-character
improvement, it suffices, for each fixed q, each character chi modulo q,
and every epsilon>0, to construct F (possibly scale dependent) and prove
for ALL large integer N that

    |F(N,1)| <<_(q,chi,epsilon) N^(gamma+epsilon),
    |Delta(N,1)+sum_(p,m)C_(N,chi)(m,p)*Delta(m,p)|
                       <<_(q,chi,epsilon) N^(gamma+epsilon).           (13)

The exact identity then gives M_chi(N)<<N^(gamma+epsilon); nonintegral
x is covered by floor(x). A still weaker joint signed estimate is possible,
but merely rewriting that full expression as M_chi supplies no estimate.
Equation(13) states the two complete inputs that this attempted approximate
source would actually need. A fixed collar is a way to make some Delta
terms exactly zero, not permission to omit the rest.

For a concrete first target one can set

    c*=125143/1000000=.125143,
    gamma*=874857/1000000=.874857,

strictly improving the current accepted c8=.12514261. This is ONLY a
conditional target; (13) is not proved at gamma*. The near,1/6,1/4 targets
correspond to gamma*,5/6,3/4 respectively. In our actual prime-band tests,
the error exponent is

    theta(u,r)=(u+1)/(u+r+1)=1-r/(u+r+1).

It exceeds a target 1-c precisely when

    u>r/c-r-1.                                           (14)

For any proposed fixed gamma<1 choose such a fixed u with the appropriate
nonzero derivative, then choose epsilon<theta-gamma. Fixed logarithmic
factors cannot absorb the resulting positive power gap. This is an
inequality about the tested certificate, not an assertion that equality
in a separate strict-reserve argument is impossible for epsilon-loss moments.

The crude independent-state certificate is |error|<=B*||Delta||_infinity.
TheoremA shows its power cost is1 even with integer coalescence, so a
uniform bounded-defect premise alone cannot reach ANY of these targets.
The signed fixed-profile repair in theoremC has the same limiting power
cost despite arbitrary fixed-order vanishing moments. At a selected u
where theta>gamma, a scalar amplitude multiplying that profile would need
a power at least N^(gamma-theta), up to the displayed logarithms, to meet
the target. No such arithmetic amplitude estimate is supplied.

For completeness the zero return itself is elementary and all-height.
If M_chi(x)<<x^(gamma+epsilon) for each epsilon>0, then

    H_chi(s)=s*integral_1^infinity M_chi(t)t^(-s-1)dt

is holomorphic for Re s>gamma. On each compact subregion, choose epsilon
smaller than its distance to the boundary; all fixed derivatives are paid
by the convergent extra powers of log t. On Re s>1, absolute Euler
multiplication gives H_chi(s)L(s,chi)=1, using actual mu(n)chi(n) and its
ramified zeros. Analytic continuation preserves the identity, excluding
the usual principal pole at s=1. Thus no L-zero lies in Re s>gamma; for
an imprimitive fixed character the omitted Euler factors have zeros only
on Re s=0, outside this positive half-plane. No finite-height truncation
or uniform-in-conductor assertion is silently added. To obtain a theorem
for every ordinary character, (13) must hold for EACH fixed one, not only
the principal class tested here. No new Eisenstein/Hecke or external
root-L-function definition binding is proved.

TheoremsA--C are unconditional arithmetic statements relative only to the
published friable asymptotic and ordinary PNT. They do not use the PR15
source-relative endpoint as an input. Conversely they do not close any
PR9/Gao source/import/admission obligation. All original descendants,
valuations, joint labels, common-saving choices, Euler shifts, shortening
complements and exceptional returns remain with their accepted original
proofs. This pass replaces none of them and claims no saving from ignoring

unchanged; the current written c remains c8.

The useful next mathematical question is now sharper than G92's open B

## 6. Calibration and recovery amendment

    c9=500579/4000000=.12514475,
    gamma9=3499421/4000000=.87485525.

## G144. A regular-residue cover cannot repair the weighted Euler trace

The augmented squarefree q-unit cutoff complex has a basis e_S for
product n(S)<=X, including the empty face, graded by|S|. Oriented
deletion d and D_chi e_S=chi(n(S))e_S give Str(D_chi)=M_chi(X), but

    [D_chi,d]e_S=sum_(p in S)orientation(p,S)
                       chi(n(S)/p)(1-chi(p))e_(S minus p).

Distinct deletions have distinct target faces. A local deletion commuting
with D_chi must vanish whenever chi(p)!=1; assigning a phase does not
remove this defect. The proposed regular-register cover uses(S,g),
g in (Z/qZ)^*, and deletes p by(S,g)->(S minus p,gp). The conserved
coordinate h=g n(S) conjugates it exactly to d tensor I. Its character
Fourier sector is D_chi^-1 d D_chi with one basis vector per face.
Its Euler index is the principal M_chi0(X), independently of chi.
For q=3,X=5, the allowed faces1,2,5 have index-1, while actual M_chi=3.
The commuting insertion chi(h) has trace0 on the full regular register
for nonprincipal chi. Anchoring g=1 restores the signal but loses the
chain condition. This is an explicit counterexample to this cover/readout,
not to different chain groups or nonlocal signed interactions.

The existing cone/prime-toggle repair remains useful with its full defect.
Let ell be the least prime not dividing q. Faces without ell and product
<=X/ell, together with their ell cones, form a contractible subcomplex.
Every boundary face of a critical ell-free face in(X/ell,X] lies there.
Let h insert ell on the eligible faces and define P e_S=e_S-hd e_S on
critical faces, P=0 on the cone. Then P^2=P,dP=Pd=0,dh+hd=I-P, and

    Str(D_chi)=Str(D_chi P)+Str([D_chi,d]h)
      =B(X)+(1-chi(ell))A(X/ell),
    A(Y)=sum_(n<=Y,ell not dividing n)mu(n)chi(n),
    B(X)=A(X)-A(X/ell).

P is not just the diagonal critical-face indicator; its hd correction
is necessary. Full telescoping gives

    M_chi(X)=B(X)+(1-chi(ell))sum_(j>=1)B(X/ell^j).

At positive exponent alpha its cost is
1+|1-chi(ell)|/(ell^alpha-1), after a finite head. Conversely
A(X)=sum_(j>=0)chi(ell)^j M_chi(X/ell^j), so B has the same full
exponent as M. No character-weighted arithmetic gain is supplied.

The unsigned critical rank is
kappa_(q ell)(1-1/ell)X+O_q(sqrt X), equal to2X/pi^2+O(sqrt X)
for q=1. The long exact relative-homology sequence gives
b(K_X,K_Y)>=b(K_X)-b(K_Y) for total reduced Betti dimension. Along
any finite increasing filtration the sum of these unsigned relative
masses is at least final mass minus initial mass. An initial o(X) mass
therefore leaves a linear complete price, even for a changing filtration.
Signed interactions across annuli are outside that obstruction.

This section credits W27/G74/G76 and W53-W56 cone, character and
reconstruction ancestry. Its new test is the precise regular-cover
failure, with the full valid repair retained rather than relabeled new.

## 3. Independent reconstruction of the coupled local proof

Normalize M=1. Put

```
C=881/200,  r=9/2-C=19/200,  k=9/40,
h_s=1/5000,  b_j=3/100+j h_s,  j=0,...,50.
```

For `t=z/M` choose j=1 at t=b0 and otherwise `b_(j-1)<t<=b_j`. In case j choose the actual amplifier exponent `a_j=k b_j M`, sigma_j=3a_j. Then

```
1359/200000 <= a_j/M <= 9/1000,
A/M <= A_j=1-(C-1)b_(j-1),
g/M <= g_j=r b_j.
```

The ceiling intervals cover the entire closed slot range; their interiors are disjoint, and boundary conventions leave no gap. In particular the first interval uses its upper amplifier even at t=.03. The high reserve below pays that real rounding cost. The bound on A comes from the lower edge, and the bound on g from the upper edge of the **same** interval. No incompatible full-window extrema have been substituted.

### Actual amplifier and genuine radius

The original pool is `(U^(a_j/M)/2,U^(a_j/M)]`. The source requires sigma>0 and mesh<sigma/6, so a common mesh below `min_j(a_j/M)/10` is sufficient. Its eventual prime-cardinality estimate and omitted-prime bound work with common polynomial envelopes and the smallest positive a_j. The representation multiplicity `(Mmax+2sigma)/(sigma/6)` has a finite maximum over the atlas; it is a constant, not an exponent or an additional row count. The literal map is `h -> h p^6`. The main column coefficients and fixed density dictionary remain unchanged. Moving-prime characters in the extracted errors stay in their old canonical source.

Both equal-product rectangles use the same j. The actual main ball, before the second transform, is

```
K_main=K0+(d-c)_+ +6a_j+omega,
K0=2A-c-d+R+E-M,
omega=delta_1+reserve,  2<=Z^reserve.
```

The original error radius remains

`K0+max(d-c-2w+w_o,0)+3a_j+delta_1+reserve`.

It is not enlarged to the main ball. The common-radius theorem supplies actual domination, including support doubling, and the second Poisson theorem accepts every positive physical radial scale. An exponent may be negative while its positive power of Z remains a valid radius. Polynomial caps can be chosen once for all fifty cases. Also `7a_j/M<=63/1000<1/4`; further common-factor extractions continue to use the source's actual allocation and subunit-scale convention.

The original small internal sigma of the global old-moment induction is separate from these fixed outer sigma_j. This proof has two transforms, prices all terminal costs, and calls only the completed old `9/2` or unrestricted zero-slot theorem at descendants. No local induction on the claimed stronger moment occurs.

### Comparison, Cauchy and low bins

The equal-product comparison uses lengths M/4 and n1+n2-M/4. Exact mask deletion and reflection of its long factor give old capacity at most

`M/4+M/2+(9/2)(M/25)+xi=93M/100+xi`.

The old comparison therefore retains reserve `7M/100`, with identical product, whole character, independent heights and profiles. Empty slots use the old unrestricted theorem.

The first-transform outside exponent is `M-A-R/2-E`. Keep its labels inside Hilbert Cauchy. The C-side joint target is

`sum_lambda N_(C,lambda) << Z^(p+A-c+R+E+B_c+eta)`,

where `B_c=(3c-5d-R)_+/6`, and similarly with c,d exchanged. The primewise balance `B_c+B_d<=c+d-2p-R` makes the geometric mean, including the outside factor, at most `Z^(M+eta)`. There is no later first-label multiplicity.

At the actual radius the identities remain

```
M'=M-(c-d)_+-6a_j-omega-g2+t2,
(A-c-c2-M')-(A-M)
  =6a_j+omega-min(c,d)-(c2-g2)-t2 <= 6a_j+omega,
Delta=b2-p2+B_c+a_j >= a_j.
```

Low bins are imposed only on positive allocated child energy after both transforms. They are not differentiated or passed through Poisson. Delete original slots at squared price `.7+O(e)` per width, hence `7/45+O(e)` per old-capacity defect, then drop the paid indicator and apply the old canonical moment. Exhaustion invokes the unrestricted old zero-slot case; no plain-sum gate is invented.

The actual width discrepancy `d_*` may be negative. For `d_*<=delta2`, `0<=s<=1`, use

`d_*+s(F-d_*)_+ <= delta2+sF_+`.

Thus the combined actual-width and deletion cost is controlled by the same nominal defect, including support padding and one greedy mesh overshoot. The low reserve is

```
a_j/15-(7/45)g_j M
  = M b_j (k/15-7r/45)
  = M b_j/4500.
```

Its exact minimum is **151M/22500000**, exceeding the report's conservative **M/150000**. All small losses must be chosen from a strict fraction of this common budget and the requested epsilon. The frozen proof does so. The original per-label `-s0` allowance and `Z^(p+s0+eta)` label count still give the joint target, rather than an additional loss after Cauchy.

### High bins, signed reconstruction and every label

The literal signed row is `w=u0 e F_c G_c V h' != 0`; reflection gives -w and conjugates the entire character and height. Net first-common valuations give residues `1+t` and `1-t` modulo six. Residue zero stays an Euler hole. With canceled radical width R0 and `L_c=log_Z NF_c`, the source gives `L_c<=5(R-R0)` and

`log_Z Nw <= W+O(eta)`, where `W=M-R-(c-d)_+ +L_c-6a_j`.

The first projector divides the genuine row; the artificial second projector need not. The latter's dyadic count and two extraction scalars remain paid. Missing first common primes have radical width at most `p-R-E+R0`. Fixed-row valuations, projector choices and slot assignments are divisor-many using the source support bound, including arbitrary valuations. That missing radical is counted once.

The natural conductor remains at most `K Nw`, K fixed; polynomial Euler holes are separate. Literal eligibility and parent-translate separation use the original Q_* and dictionary. Sixth-power stripping retains holes, and the lift is summable because `rho>=2/7>1/6`. The common density threshold precedes height. For `.7<=delta<=.75`,

`rho(delta)=1-10delta/[3(5-2delta)]`

gives the joint population exponent `rho W+p-R-E+R0+eta`. Unsupported negative windows are empty; bounded supported end windows receive padding, so no nonempty population is bounded by a negative power without justification.

Relative to the joint target, the exact high excess is

```
M(rho-1)+delta A+a_j(5-6rho)
 +(1-rho)(c-d)_+-delta c-(1+rho)R-E-B_c
 +rho L_c+R0+g2-t2-(1+delta)b2+O(eta).
```

The middle terms are at most `(4rho-1-delta)p-E-B_c`, with coefficient at most `-79/270`, by `min(c,d)>=p>=R`, `rho+delta>1`, `5rho>1`, and the signed L_c bound. The last terms are nonpositive; the source gives the stronger bound `-delta b2-t2`. Every common label and missing factor is already included.

The remaining normalized saving is

`H_j(delta)=1-rho-delta A_j-k b_j(5-6rho)`.

Its derivative is `50(1-6k b_j)/(3(5-2delta)^2)-A_j`. The reported common lower bound is exactly `1548949/4860000>0`; the sharper independent minimum over actual cases is `3263273/9720000>0`. Thus the whole interval is minimized at .7, not merely sampled there. At that point

`H_j(.7)=35/54-7/10+(3467/2000)b_(j-1)-(13/20)h_s`.

This increases with j. Its exact minimum is **1/43200**, including the rounding charge **13/100000**. Bins crossing .7 are put in the buffered low branch; density is used only at or above .7. The smaller low reserve controls a common loss allocation.

### Extracted errors, zeros and fixed-inducing exceptions

The three original errors have `(w,w_o)=(lambda,lambda),(6lambda,0),(7lambda,lambda)`. From the actual pool, eventually `lambda>=3a_j/4`. Defect is at most `g+3a_j+w-w_o+eta`, allowance at least w. Old global removal rate `1/6` and the same signed-width correction give reserves

`a_j/4-g/6`, `13a_j/4-g/6`, `4a_j-g/6`.

The average over primes stays normalized. The moving characters, valuation-zero holes and extraction scalars stay literal. There is no new density assumption for those moving-prime errors.

The first zero frequency keeps its powerful-product argument and the added Gauss zero row is unamplified. The second zero excess is `A-M+5a_j+O(eta)`. For paired fixed-inducing rows, the exact original main F1 has `-4a_j-5omega/6`, not `-5a_j`, and satisfies `F1>=2c/3-4a_j-O(eta)`; `F2>=2b2/3`. With `v=c+min(c2,d2)`,

`max_(v>=0)[A-5M/6-2v/3-(M/4-v)_+]=A-M`,

attained at v=M/4. The main exception therefore costs `A-M+4a_j`; the error radius costs `A-M+9a_j`. The exceptional source's actual `Kphys^(5/6)` factor is included in these formulas. The paired leading terms cancel only because the products, masks, profiles, whole characters and independent-height norm powers agree; the atlas uses the same index on both rectangles.

Independent exact minima over all fifty interval envelopes are:

| Branch | Exact normalized minimum | Frozen conservative value, if weaker |
|---|---:|---:|
| Low | `151/22500000` | `1/150000` |
| High | `1/43200` | same |
| Error 1 | `14647/12000000` | `97/80000` |
| Error 6 | `259267/12000000` | `1717/80000` |
| Error 7 | `160211/6000000` | `1061/40000` |
| Second zero | `2727/40000` | same |
| Main fixed-inducing | `7497/100000` | same |
| Error fixed-inducing | `8199/200000` | same |

For the last three rows, `1-A_j-mk b_j=[(C-1)-mk]b_(j-1)-mk h_s`, with m=5,4,9. These are increasing in j. Every fixed amplifier cost is priced, rather than hidden in epsilon.

### Proof of the energy implication

For the whole completed column FD (68) gives
\[
S_h^{(g)}(w)=L^S(3w-1,\xi)
\sum_{d\mid g}x_{g/d}(w)
\prod_{p\mid d}(1-x_p(w))D_h^{(d)}(w),
\quad x_a(w)=\xi(a)q_a^{1-3w}.
\]
This selector includes primes shared by a squarefree core and its outside cube. At \(\Re w=1/2+e\),
\[
|x_a|^2=q_a^{-1-6e},\qquad
\prod_{p\mid d}(1+|x_p|)\ll q_d^\delta.
\]
Divisor Cauchy therefore reduces the finite whole-column trace to (T08.1) with cutoff \(G/q_a\le G\), followed by an absolutely convergent \(a\)-sum. The angular factor is incorporated into the original radial cube profile \(\Phi_V\) of FD (69), whose nonzero angular type makes its lower endpoint rapidly decreasing. It is not divided out. Finite Mellin shifts use inherited independent holomorphy and polynomial height bounds. Squaring costs \(D^{1+2e}\); choose \(e\) and preliminary losses sufficiently small in terms of final \(\rho\). This gives the first term of (T08.2).

FD (71)–(72) supplies the unchanged large-divisor energies. The three resulting weights are
\[
\frac{DK}{q_dq_aq_j},\quad
\frac{D^2K^{1/3}}{q_d^2q_a^4q_j^4},\quad
\frac{D^{5/3}K^{2/3}}{q_d^{5/3}q_a^3q_j^3}.
\]
Their sums over \(q_aq_d>G\), with the original finite supports, are the final three terms in (T08.2). The natural core-divisor and \(j\)-overlap conditions remain intact.

Finally, FD §19.3 separates the original common product kernel before applying positive Cauchy in the same divisor/row indices. This step preserves the signed coprime covariance, all original total-column profiles, radial norm twists and both separately paid zero terms. It does not apply a signed estimate to an arbitrarily partitioned profile.

Set \(G=\max(K^{1/3},KD^{-1/2})\). If \(K\le D^{3/4}\), the first term is at most
\[
D^{7/4+3u/4+v/4},
\]
which is strictly below \(D^2\) by \(3u+v<1\). If \(K=D^k\), \(k\ge3/4\), its exponent is
\[
1-v/2+k(1+u+v)<2
\]
for \(k<k_*\). Both tails are at most \(D^2\), and \(DK\le D^2\). Exact equality in a tail is harmless: M (2.18) asks for \(D^{2+\epsilon}\), with arbitrarily small loss. It does not require a power saving below \(D^2\) in every term. This proves the conditional current criterion and (T08.3).

statement:
## 1. Literal character source and causal realization

Fix one ordinary Dirichlet character chi modulo q with its natural zero extension. Let delta=1 for a principal character and 0 otherwise, r=delta*phi(q)/q, A(x)=sum_(n<=x)chi(n), and b(t)=A(exp t)-r exp t. Periodicity gives |b|<=q. For Re s>1,

    integral_0^infinity exp(-st)b(t)dt=L(s,chi)/s-r/(s-1).

The left side extends holomorphically to Re s>0. The report's source is exactly

    F_chi(s)=((s-1)/(s+1))^delta L(s,chi)/s.            (R1)

At a principal pole s=1 the removable value is r/2, nonzero. A nonprincipal character receives no artificial (s-1) factor. Thus all and only the natural L-zeros in Re s>0 survive, with multiplicity. Finite imprimitive factors and ramified zeros were not removed or filled in. The causal inverse Laplace source is

    f=b                                      nonprincipal,
    f(t)=r exp(-t)+b(t)-2 integral_0^t exp(-(t-u))b(u)du
                                             principal.      (R2)

It is bounded by C_q=1+3q. For principal chi, exact Abel summation gives

    f(log x)=2/x sum_(n<=x)n chi(n)-A(x)
            =A(x)-2/x integral_1^x A(y)dy.             (R3)

In particular q=1 gives m(m+1-x)/x for m=floor x, including the correct endpoint jumps. Positivity of that one source is not zero exclusion: a nonnegative delayed source exp(-bt)+C exp(-b(t-T))1_(t>=T) has transform (1+C exp(-sT))/(s+b), with zeros of positive real part when C>1. This is a toy counterexample to the inference, not an arithmetic lower bound.

For 0<gamma<1 set a=2-gamma and s(z)=gamma+a(1+z)/(1-z). The anchor is s(0)=2, where F0=F_chi(2) is nonzero by the absolutely convergent Euler product. Put f_gamma(t)=exp(-gamma t)f(t),

    h=sqrt(2a) exp(-a t)*f_gamma,
    Qv=v-2a exp(-a t)*v,
    ell0(t)=sqrt(2a)exp(-at).                          (R4)

The convolution is causal on [0,infinity). Q is an L2 isometry because its boundary Laplace multiplier is (it-a)/(it+a). Its full output tail is retained. The Cayley change of variables has measure a/[pi(a^2+t^2)]dt, exactly matching the sqrt(2a)/(w+a) Laplace factor. Hence, for every finite polynomial p,

    ||p(Q)h||_2^2=||p F||_H2^2,
    ||p(Q)h-F0 ell0||_2^2=||p F-F0||_H2^2,             (R5)

where F(z)=F_chi(s(z)). Also Q*ell0=0 and ||ell0||=1. These identities include all cross terms and complex phases. They are not comparisons of entrywise magnitudes. No uniformly equivalent positive metric P can have Q*PQ<=kappa P with kappa<1: iteration and Q's isometry contradict mI<=P<=MI. This is an unrestricted multiplier obstruction; it leaves source-specific output cancellation intact, as in W37 D03.
title: 1. Literal character source and causal realization

statement:
## G168. Exact harmonic and heat costs

The sorted-prime state from [G145](../[private research revision]/wild57-integration.md) is
retained: for σ>1/2, Tσ e_n=∑_{p>P⁺(n)}χ(p)p^−σ e_np on squarefree
q-units has ||Tσ^j||²≤Sσ^j/j!, Sσ=∑p^−2σ. Disjoint descendants follow
by deleting the j largest primes. Its convergent inverse gives
v(n)=μ(n)χ(n)n^−σ, but the physical output norm is asymptotic to a
constant times N^{σ+1/2}. This is reused source formation, not a new gap.
Diagonal congruence transports banded terminal metrics to G167 without
discarding a norm factor.

On all squarefree q-units at most N, take the connected graph n—np with
arbitrary positive edge weights. Let L be its real Laplacian, U=diag(a_n),
L_a=ULU*. Then x*L_a x=∑w_{n,p}|x_np+χ(p)x_n|² and L_a a=0. For
λ,η>0, H=λL_a+ηe_1e_1* is positive definite with a*Ha=η. Put
f=U*ℓ=conjugate(a), R=V_N\{1}, and E_N=f_R*(L_RR)^−1 f_R≥0. Exactly,

\[
\ell^*H^{-1}\ell=|M_\chi(N)|^2/\eta+E_N/\lambda,
\quad H\succeq\ell\ell^*\iff
|M_\chi(N)|^2/\eta+E_N/\lambda\le1.                    \tag{96.9}
\]

After conjugation, solve (λL+ηe_1e_1*)x=f. Summing yields
x_1=(∑f)/η; writing x=x_1ℓ+y,y_1=0 gives λL_RR y_R=f_R and (96.9).
If M≠0, require λ>E_N and η≥|M|²/(1−E_N/λ). If M=0, λ≥E_N suffices
for any η>0, including equality. N=1 has E_N=0. A graph gap may bound
the Green term; it cannot remove the actual harmonic amplitude.

There is an analogous exact bill for arbitrary positive diagonal Witten
weights on the downward-closed squarefree q-unit complex. Let d be
oriented deletion, S positive diagonal, d_S=SdS^−1,
Q_S=d_S+d_S*, Δ_S=Q_S², and Tχ the diagonal character insertion. The
adjoint matters: Δ_S is generally not SΔS^−1. Homology is unchanged,
while the positive spectrum may move. For principal χ the heat
supertrace equals the index Mχ(N) for every heat time.

For a general character, graded cyclicity and integration of the heat
derivative give, for every T≥0,

\[
M_\chi(N)=\operatorname{Str}(T_\chi e^{-T\Delta_S})
 +\frac12\int_0^T\operatorname{Str}
 ([T_\chi,Q_S]Q_Se^{-t\Delta_S})\,dt.                  \tag{96.10}
\]

In particular Str(TχΔ_S)=∑_{n,p}|S_n/S_np|² μ(n)χ(n)(1−χ(p)), with
every edge retained. Since S and Tχ commute,
[Tχ,d_S]=S[Tχ,d]S^−1; the deformation cannot make a nonzero commutator
vanish. For positive spectral gap λ*, the heat remainder beyond the
harmonic projection Π_0 is at most dim(V_N)e^−Tλ*. The integral also
converges because Q_SΠ_0=0, leaving the **twisted harmonic trace plus
the entire integrated bulk**.

For the actual nonprincipal character modulo3 at N=2, Tχ=diag(1,−1),
Q_S=[[0,w],[w,0]], w>0, and Π_0=0. The two terms in (96.10) are
2e^−Tw² and2(1−e^−Tw²), while the true source is2. Enlarging the gap
does not save the complete readout. This is a finite counterexample to
dropping the bulk, not an all-scale Mertens lower bound or a rejection
of all Witten constructions. The general harmonic warning is
[G74](../[private research revision]/wild46-integration.md); the cutoff ancestry and full
character bulk are [G164–G165](../[private research revision]/wild59-integration.md).

The author's specified superdeterminants are likewise exact:
sdet(I+zΔ)=1 and sdet(zI+Δ)=z^{Mχ₀(N)}, as meromorphic ratios after
cancellation. The unknown source remains in the zero-mode exponent.
Different regularizations or torsion definitions need their own return.

## Second coarse attempt: the actual positive price survives

The positive price of Core cannot be reduced to X^(eta+epsilon) just by discarding signs: actual Möbius coefficients themselves provide a large positive subcollection. This is a limitation of coefficientwise or separately positive estimates, not a lower bound for the full signed Q.

Put B=floor(X^(1/K)), so B<=Y for large X. For fixed q, squarefree integers coprime to q in[B/2,B] number at least c_q B for large B. An elementary proof expands mu^2(n)=sum_(d^2|n)mu(d), counts coprime multiples with error O_q(1), and obtains density (phi(q)/q)product_(p not dividing q)(1-p^-2)>0 with O_q(sqrt B) error. Their values mu(d)chi(d) lie in a fixed finite set of unit phases. Pigeonhole one phase zeta_X and a set D of at least c'_qB such integers with this phase.

Every ordered m-tuple from D contributes phase zeta_X^m and an output in[(B/2)^m,B^m]. By(N23), every other factorization of any one of these outputs has the identical phase. The total weighted mass of these outputs, with multiplicity, is therefore at least

  |D|^m B^(-m sigma) >=(c'_q)^m B^(m(1-sigma)).

Partition their logarithms into O(m+1) intervals of length at most1. One interval carries at least this mass divided by O(m+1). All ordered pairs of these outputs in that interval have positive phase product1 and Gaussian at least exp(-1/tau). Their contribution to the POSITIVE selected price is at least

  C_tau (c'_q)^(2m) B^(2m(1-sigma))/(m+1)^2
      =X^(1-sigma-o(1)).                                 (N29)

Removing the diagonal(N25) and the large-gcd positive price(N26) leaves the same exponent, since c+kappa>0. These pairs already obey the ratio condition in(N27). Moreover their total short-factor product nk lies between(B/2)^K and B^K, hence between Xexp(-Klog2-o(1)) and X. Since W/K tends to infinity, this entire positive subcollection lies INSIDE the balanced product window(N3), rather than solely in a product tail already discarded. This observation concerns the selected moment pairs; it does not identify Q with the physical norm of C^bal. Thus the coefficientwise absolute price of the actual small-gcd core is at least X^(1-sigma-o(1)). Since the needed eta=gamma-sigma is strictly below1-sigma, triangle inequalities cannot supply(N28).

This refines the location of the necessary cancellation: it must occur between different actual phases in the small-gcd, comparable-product sector. It does not preclude that cancellation, prove a zero, or exclude an epsilon-loss estimate at an equality boundary. The general positive-cone/prime-box obstruction has earlier ancestry; the added statement here is its uniform persistence for these actual growing-order squarefree-factor multiplicities, after a quantitatively paid large-gcd deletion. It is not advertised as a new general parity principle.

## 2. Development03: source identity and complete return

Fix one ordinary Dirichlet character chi of its presented modulus q and one tau>0. All natural zeros remain. Write c_p=chi(p), D_pV(x)=V(x/p), and
     
    F=sum f3(n)chi(n)g_tau(log(n/x)),

    f3(n)=product_(p|n,p!=3)(-1),
    b(n)=product_(p|n,p>=5)(-1).

These are COMPLETE fixed fields. f3 includes2, unlike b; every positive power of2 changes sign. No ideal, angular or growing-conductor extension follows.

For z_p=c_p p^-s the exact Euler factors are

    D_b=H/L,
    H_2=H_3=(1-z)^-2,

    K=H^-1, K_2=K_3=(1-z)^2,

At2,3 their masses are(1-r)^-2 and(1+r)^2. Ramified factors equal1. These same normally convergent products prove H and K nonzero on Re(s)>1/2.

For ||V||_sigma=sup_(X>0)X^-sigma||V||_(L2([X,2X],dx/x)), initial absolute Gaussian Fubini and then Minkowski give

    U=T_k B, B=T_h U,
    ||U||_sigma<=K_sigma||B||_sigma,

The left Gaussian tail pays every small scale; two neighboring dyads cover an arbitrary dilated shell. This is old G28 compensation with the corrected source. It does NOT say k*f3=mu: in fact

with prime-two coefficients1,-3c_2,2c_2^2. The old exceptional A source is distinct from ordinary mu.

For c=c_2!=0, finite substitution gives

                    -sum_(j=1..J)(2c)^-j F(2^j x). (R4)

Each fixed character's inherited ||U||_beta<infinity, theta6<beta<1, transfers to B by(R2), and bounds that boundary by ||B||_beta X^beta 2^-J(1-beta). It tends to0 on every fixed shell. The inherited baseline needs growth as well as zero-free holomorphy. For fixed q, periodic summation gives polynomial vertical growth of L on positive strips. Choose a zero-free line strictly between theta6 and beta. Analytic log L on buffered disks centered at Re(s)>1, normalized there by the absolutely convergent Euler logarithm, has real part O(log(2+|t|)). Borel--Caratheodory on smaller disks gives |log L|=O(log(2+|t|)); remove the principal pole first. Hence1/L has polynomial growth on the beta line/intervening strip. Gaussian Mellin shifting gives U=O_(chi,tau,beta)(x^beta) for x>=1, and the left tail gives the global norm. This uses the ACCEPTED buffered premise only. ### 2.1 Finite composition, both errors, and conditional targets

Let beta in(theta6,1), sigma0 in(1/2,beta), R=floor(X^b0), J=ceil(a log_2 X). The author's finite retained source is

For c=0 use sum_(r<=R)k(r)chi(r)F(x/r). Each summand is the SAME COMPLETE field, not an integer truncation. Exact substitution gives U-Q_X=E_2+E_K, where

         <=2||Q_X||||U-Q_X||+||U-Q_X||^2.           (R7)

No mixed term or signed-submask cost disappears. The sharp r<=R endpoint is literal; moving cutoffs are never held fixed at the wrong dilation.

## 3. Development16: the entire sign survives in harmonic degree

The local complex has one even vector e0, two odd vectors e+,e-, and d(e+)=d(e-)=e0. Its Laplacian has eigenvalues2 on e0 and the odd symmetric vector, and0 on the odd antisymmetric vector. The graded tensor product over DISTINCT p|n,p!=3 retains every repeated power without adding a coordinate;2 is included,3 is not. For n=1 and powers of3 there is one even factor. Koszul signs give d^2=0. The Laplacian is the sum of commuting local ones: one harmonic vector in degree omega(n/3^v3(n)), and all other eigenvalues positive multiples of2. Hence

On the complement, h=d*Delta^-1 has norm<=1/sqrt2, since d d*<=Delta and the gap is2. Its exact identity is dh+hd=I-P, never I; applying an I identity to the nonzero harmonic vector is a contradiction.

In the direct sum, W_(x,chi) is scalar chi(n)g_tau(log(n/x)) on C(n). Since3^omega(n/3^v3(n))<=n^2, Gaussian decay justifies trace class and all sums. The complete field is

The positive harmonic price is sum_(n,q)=1 g_tau(log(n/x)). Bounded-variation Riemann sums in fixed residue classes, with h(t)=g_tau(log t),h(0)=0, give

This is exponent1 for the ABSOLUTE price, not a lower bound on F or its moment. Heat time infinity leaves F unchanged. The author correctly rejects only cancellation inferred from the complement's gap.

## 6. Protected audit20: actual matching and its paid critical source

This card was author-untested. A matching between different integers is not refuted by the per-integer harmonic survivor. The following is a concrete construction on canonical f3.

Let P=(p1,...,pr) be any ordered finite set of distinct primes, none equal3 or dividing q; put Q=product P. For each n find the FIRST p_j with v_pj(n)<=1. If it exists, toggle valuations0 and1 by n<->p_j n or n<->n/p_j. All earlier valuations are>=2. The toggle preserves the first eligible index, so this is an involution with disjoint edges and no matching cycle. The critical vertices satisfy every v_pj>=2, exactly Q^2|n.

At a lower endpoint m, p_j does not divide m and earlier p_i^2 divide m. Consequently

    f3(p_j m)chi(p_j m)=-c_pj f3(m)chi(m).         (R15)

Every repeated power remains in another selected direction or the critical set. Natural character-zero vertices remain zero. A ramified prime is omitted from P because its upper vertex would be zero, not because chi(p) can be inverted. If2 is unramified it is eligible normally; if2 is ramified it is omitted for that explicit reason. Prime3 is excluded because it does not flip f3.

Define COMPLETE lower-endpoint fields

    A_j(x)=sum_(p_j not|m; p_i^2|m for i<j)
                         f3(m)chi(m)g_tau(log(m/x)),
    C_P(x)=sum_(Q^2|n)f3(n)chi(n)g_tau(log(n/x)),
    S_P(x)=sum_(j=1..r)[A_j(x)-c_pj A_j(x/p_j)].

    F(x)=S_P(x)+C_P(x).                             (R16)

Set

    R_(P,chi)(y)=sum_k product_(p|k,p!=3,p notin P)(-1)
                                   chi(k)g_tau(log(k/y)).

    C_P(x)=(-1)^r chi(Q)^2 R_(P,chi)(x/Q^2).         (R17)

    sum_(k>=1)g_tau(log(k/y))<=C_tau y.             (R18)

independently of P,q. This pays the complete Gaussian tail; it is not a fixed-period density asymptotic used outside its uniform range.

## 7. Uniform audit29: full contour gluing keeps the residue bill

This card was also author-untested. Use fixed U, whose source return to F is paid above, and M(s)=exp(tau s^2/2)/L(s,chi).     U(x)=V_(a,T)(x)+H_(a,b,T)(x)+Z_(a,b,T)(x)+R_(b,T)(x), (R22)

The COMPLETE right-line height tail is cheap without a new arithmetic premise. Absolute reciprocal coefficients on b give |1/L(b+it)|<=zeta(b). Gaussian tail integration yields

          <=C_(b,tau) X^b T^-1 exp(-tau T^2/2).    (R24)

    ||V||<=C X^a integral_(-T)^T e^(-tau t^2/2)|1/L(a+it)|dt,

            integral_a^b[|1/L(sigma+iT)|+|1/L(sigma-iT)|]d sigma. (R25)

Neither reciprocal integral is bounded here at a proposed new target. Boundary admissibility alone does not control a near-zero denominator. The complete residue sum, with multiplicities, remains. A FIXED nonempty finite residue packet with maximal real part sigma_*>gamma cannot itself be O(X^gamma) on all shells. Let d be the largest m-1 among its roots with real part sigma_*. The written source-relative c11=312864909/2500000000=.1251459636 and the

The [retention manifest](retention-manifest.json) binds18 immutable files
and21 reviewed inputs. Author and reviewer explicitly stopped and normally

## The literal source and inherited contract

Use [G179-G181](../[private research revision]/four-cross-gcd-integration.md) on the original
Eisenstein ideals, fixed excluded primes, primary/unit conventions and
finite dictionaries. With q_z=N(z), retain

    F_u=M_u(D1;W1,t1) M_u(D2;W2,t2) Q_u,

    M_u(D;W)=D^(-1/2) sum_d mu(d)nu(d)chi_d(u)^e W(q_d/D).

Here e=1 or -1 is a complete orientation. The two original inverse
heights are independent, with one common real parameter. Q retains its
ordered disjoint prime-slot pools, original coefficients, heights and
product profile, including intersections with inverse factors. The whole
right copy is conjugated. Every character keeps its natural zeros even
at powers0 or6. Rows are the original nonzero sixth-power-free free-row
enclosure with fixed smooth ball weight; original divisor row weights
are dominated before expansion. An arbitrary physical projector is not
inserted in this norm.

Retain the physical box

    17/25<=delta<=7/10, 17/20<r<47/50,
    33/25<s<141/100, s-r>3/8, 0<=v<=1/20.

With h=5-2delta, rho=1-10delta/(3h), k=rho+delta-1,
D_K=15K-10-6Kdelta, a_K=delta(5-6delta)^2/(3hD_K) and
b_K=2delta(5-6delta)(K-1)/D_K, use exactly

    E_K=rho+delta v-min(3kv,a_K+b_Kv),

Take R_unique to be exactly its pairs with n=d1 d2 P and n'=d1'd2'P'
both squarefree and coprime. Such pairs automatically meet all six

## G185. Primitive Poisson and the complete two-color sieve bound

On a squarefree merged column, the original coefficient is exactly

    F_sf,u=(-1)^j N0^(-1/2) sum_(n sf) mu(n)nu(n)chi_n(u)^e A(n),
    A(n)=sum_(original P|n) b(P)conjugate(nu(P))
                    sum_(d1 d2=n/P) W1(q_d1/D1;t1)W2(q_d2/D2;t2).

Slots retain their ordered labels. The sign is mu(d1)mu(d2)=(-1)^jmu(n);
the two inverse signs are not independent random variables. Since nu(P)
is a unit on the fixed good source, its conjugate is legitimate; no
natural row character value is divided out.

Expand the row indicator by sum_(a^6|u)mu(a), put u=a^6 z, and retain
(a,nn')=1. The row scale is U_a=U/q_a^6 with q_a<<U^(1/6). For actual
coprime squarefree n,n', psi=chi_n^e conjugate(chi_n'^e) is primitive
and nonprincipal at its full good conductor nn': its local exponents
are1 and5. Primitive Poisson therefore gives zero at ell=0 and at every
frequency sharing a good conductor prime. This does not remove a principal
original family. The normalized finite transform is

    sum_(x mod nn') psi(x)e(ell x/(nn'))
       =sqrt(q_n q_n') gamma(psi;nn') conjugate(psi(ell)).

The CRT factor chi_n(n')^e chi_n'(n)^(-e)=R(n,n') is the fixed ray sign
of PR9 B1.1-B1.5. It does not produce a variable cubic coupling across
copies. Set a0(n)=conjugate(alpha(n))gamma_2(n). PR9 B1.10 yields

    mu(n)gamma_1(n)=conjugate(a0(n))G(n),
    mu(n)gamma_-1(n)=a0(n)chi_n(-1)conjugate(G(n)).

Thus, apart from the retained nu(n)conjugate(nu(n')), the arithmetic
factors for e=-1 and e=1 respectively are

    R(n,n')chi_n(-1)conjugate(G(n))G(n')
         a0(n)conjugate(a0(n'))chi_n(ell)conjugate(chi_n'(ell));
    R(n,n')G(n)conjugate(G(n'))chi_n'(-1)
         conjugate(a0(n))a0(n')conjugate(chi_n(ell))chi_n'(ell).

Expand the fixed ray factors into the prescribed finite separated
dictionary. Fixed row restrictions modulo a disjoint S-supported modulus
retain primitive good-prime Fourier zeros by CRT. The dictionary may
depend on a's fixed residue class, with bounded cost. The first-dual cut
is on the actual fixed dual lattice; clearing a fixed denominator changes
its comparison constant and is not silently identified with the old cut.

The central pair coefficient and Poisson roots leave

    U/(q_a^6 N0^2),

with N0/sqrt(q_n q_n') retained in the smooth profile. Its radial kernel
keeps the exact argument U_a q_ell/(q_n q_n'), all original heights and
fixed factors. Before algebraic extension or an absolute Fourier integral,
pay the genuine far tail as proved in G186 below.

For fixed Y of at most a fixed polynomial size, define R_unique,<=Y by
the literal restriction0<q_ell<=Y in this exact expression. Pair
transposition with complete conjugation preserves that radial restriction;
the scalar can be kept real without assuming positivity.

Extend the displayed product expression and formal product conductor to
all individually squarefree n,n' in their original supports, then insert

    1_((n,n')=1)=sum_(f|n,f|n')mu(f).

The FULL identity kills every artificial noncoprime pair, including
inverse-slot and slot-slot intersections. No imprimitive Poisson theorem
is asserted on added pairs. Write n=fm,n'=fm'. Squarefreeness keeps
(f,m)=(f,m')=1 and

    a0(fm)=a0(f)a0(m)chi_m(f)^4,
    chi_f(ell)conjugate(chi_f(ell))=1_((f,ell)=1).

Each prime of f is allocated to its actual inverse color or original slot
on each side. The two allocations may differ. On one side f=f1 f2 fP,

    D1'=D1/q_f1, D2'=D2/q_f2, P'=P0/q_fP,
    X_f=D1'D2'P'=N0/q_f.

The other side has the same product X_f with independently shortened
color and slot lengths. Both allocation multiplicities together cost
tau(f)^C at fixed slot depth. Assigned slot coefficients and pool tests
remain present. Nonempty subunit nominal windows are clipped by bounded
original annular factors; truly empty windows stay empty.

Separate the full profile on the ambient original normalized norm box
BEFORE live labels, keeping its two real inverse roots once. On nominal
a- and ell-dyads A,H, the coupled kernel is

    K(C*y_ell/(y_a^6 product(y_original_columns))),
    C=UH/(A^6N0^2).

Its Euler derivatives are uniformly bounded for C>0 by fixed Schwartz
seminorms. PR9 B3.3 fixes the common Fourier measure first. Only then
substitute extracted factors; their imaginary powers have modulus one.
Sharp arithmetic masks and the dual cutoff stay outside the smooth
separation. Both original heights remain on their own profiles, with
the fixed finite-order H_J cost. This inherits, rather than resolves,
the open positive-slot uniformity ancestry.

For a fixed remaining slot tuple P, PR9 B1.11 gives

    a0(xyP)=a0(x)a0(y)a0(P)chi_y(x)^4 chi_x(P)^4 chi_y(P)^4.

All a,f,ell punctures, finite ray data and frequency twists separate
between x and y. Their coprimality is the natural cubic-symbol zero.
The two sieve variables are the original residual colors OF ONE COPY,
never a product mixing left and right columns.

The unconditional squarefree cubic large sieve, as stated in
[Dunn-Radziwill, equation1.11 and Theorem9.1](https://arxiv.org/html/2109.07463v3),
allows an arbitrary inner sequence independent of its outer variable,
with price D+E+(DE)^(2/3). Both variables are squarefree primary
Eisenstein elements. Cauchy and reciprocity/conjugation give

    |(DE)^(-1/2) sum_(x,y sf) alpha_x beta_y chi_y(x)^4|^2
       << H_J (DE)^epsilon [D+E+(DE)^(2/3)].

The two coefficient squared masses O(D),O(E) cancel the normalization.
Natural holes are zero coefficients or restrictions of the positive

method would require a genuinely stronger aggregate estimate, not a

This pass did try a deliberately coarse rigorous estimate; it did not

## 3. Literal second transform, projector and actual width

After an extracted amplifier alternative, put a0=A-c-w. Its unweighted Gauss allowance is

    Lambda_c = a0+qtilde+wo+w+Bc-s0,

where the extracted squared scalar is Z^(-wo). With row-ball length K+g and density Z^(-ell), additive orthogonality gives

    Z^(-ell-a0) sum_h Phi2(N(h)/Z^(K+g))
       |sum_u B(u) tau_1(u) N(u)^(it) G(u,h)|^2
    = Z^(K+g-ell-a0) sum_(u,v)
       B(u) conjugate(B(v)) tau_1(u) conjugate(tau_1(v))
       N(u)^(it) N(v)^(-it) / sqrt(N(u)N(v))
       sum_j F(u,v;j) K2(Z^(K+g)N(j)/[N(u)N(v)]).

Here F is the literal finite correlation in B1.14, with Fourier identity B1.15. In particular F(u,v;0)=1_(u=v) phi(u). The second zero is not part of the gain proposed here.

For nonzero j extract u=D2 a, v=E2 b, with complete common support and (a,b)=(ab,D2E2)=1. The exact identity is

    F(D2 a,E2 b;j) =
      F(D2,E2;j) R(a,E2) R(b,D2) R(a,b)
      chi_a(j) conjugate(chi_b(-j)).

Thus the two residual whole characters are tau_1(n) chi_n(j), up to fixed ray factors (including the -1 on the second side). There is no inversion of j on one child. Whole conjugation, when used to identify a family, must conjugate the entire character and its heights.

Use c2,d2,b2=(c2+d2)/2,p2,g2 from B3.62–B3.63. Put Gc=(D2,E2). At equal common multiplicity i not divisible by 6, split j/Gc into unit and nonunit cases, of radical widths t2,V, and write j=Gc V_id h'. The source scalar

    1_part F(D2,E2;Gc V_id h') / Z^(g2-t2)

has modulus at most one and is zero off the original partition. Every extracted prime punctures every remaining factor. A cancelled exponent remains a hole.

The nominal and actual widths are exactly

    m' = 2a0-K-g-g2-V,
    q' = qtilde+wo+t2+V,
    M' = M+J-g-g2+t2,  J=d-c+(K0-K)-2w+wo,
    m'_act=m'+delta2, M'_act=M'+delta2, 0<=delta2<xi.

The pulled-back weight and partition scalar are extended by zero on the rest of the actual enclosing ball. A negative supported upper length means an empty range; it is not replaced by a fictitious row of norm one. The source choices give M'<=M-sigma and actual decrease at least sigma/2 after the reserved padding.

The exponent ledger is

    -a0 + (K+g-a0) - ell + (p2-s0)
      + (g2-t2) + (a0-b2).

The p2-s0 uses the genuine first-projector divisor s in both second common parts. Subtracting this ledger from Lambda_c leaves the original allowance

    M'+Delta,  Delta=b2-p2+w+Bc+ell >= w+ell.

Before separating residual columns, retain every factor and insert the full residual projector sum_(t|a,b) mu(t). Extra primes in an individual artificial t term are not added to the genuine common parts. Use the source priority allocation, both extraction scalars and divisor count; selected plain quotients do not gain an invented puncture. The subsequent exceptional count below is valid even if a partition restriction is bounded by one, so artificial projector terms cause no extra congruence assumption.

## 4. Removing the new masks without an illegal moment input

For every q and every original common profile W,

    M_u^(q)(E;W)
      =sum_(h supported on primes of q)
          phi_u(h)/(Nh)^(1/2) M_u(E/Nh;W).            (4.1)

The h sum is finite on the actual annulus. At each p|q, the local convolution of mu with the all-nonnegative-exponent sequence 1 is `1,0,0,...`; at p not dividing q it is mu. Thus its coefficient is exactly `mu(n)1_(n,q)=1`. Complete multiplicativity carries phi through this identity even at zero values. The normalizations in (4.1) multiply to E^(-1/2), so there is no missing h power. Substituting qh into the fixed normalized arguments changes the scale, not the common W.

The absolute restoration mass is bounded by

    sum_(h q-smooth) (Nh)^(-1/2)
      =prod_(p|q)(1-(Np)^(-1/2))^(-1)
      <<_epsilon (Nq)^epsilon.                       (4.2)

To prove the last inequality, fix epsilon first; each sufficiently large prime's factor is at most `(Np)^epsilon`, and the finite small primes supply a fixed constant. This is uniform in polynomial q. Derivatives in log scale merely change the common profile. If an alternative convention puts a norm-height factor outside W, differentiating its q,h phase supplies powers of log(qh), bounded by a further subpower on the nonempty support. The two independent heights are never identified.

For an already frozen polynomial puncture R0, replace the prime set by that of qR0 in (4.1)--(4.2). This explicit outer expansion is the required justification; one must not invoke B0.9 directly on a moving q-mask. Similarly, applying B3.6 to the merged coefficient `mu*mu` would be illegal. statement:
### 3. The extra saving from the actual prime slots

For the original smooth/fixed-character prime weights, keep the assigned-to-\(g\) primes inside the transform. Set
\[
 \mathscr S_M(s)=\frac{L^S(s,\psi)}{L^S(2s,\psi^2)}
       \prod_{p\mid M,\,p\notin S}(1+\psi(p)q_p^{-s})^{-1},
 \qquad f_s(p)=\frac{\psi(p)q_p^{-s}}{1+\psi(p)q_p^{-s}}.
\]
For \((F,M\mathfrak f_\psi)=1\), the exact forced series equals
\(\mathscr S_M(s)\prod_{p\mid F}f_s(p)\). At \(\Re s=\sigma=b/2\),
\[
 f_s(p)=\psi(p)q_p^{-s}-\psi(p)^2q_p^{-2s}+O(q_p^{-3\sigma}).
 \tag{T07.8}
\]
Both leading good characters remain nonprincipal after every fixed-place factor. The inherited prime estimate therefore gives, for a fixed smooth annular \(w\), fixed real \(\Re a\), and a deleted radical \(B\),
\[
 \sum_{p\nmid B}\eta_0(p)w(q_p/P)q_p^a f_s(p)
 \ll P^{\Re a+b-\sigma+\epsilon}(Rq_B)^\epsilon T^A.
 \tag{T07.9}
\]
To see every term: the first two powers cost \(P^{\Re a+b-j\sigma+\epsilon}\), \(j=1,2\). The remaining powers cost \(P^{\Re a+1-3\sigma+\epsilon}\), which is smaller because \(1\le2b\). Removing specified primes costs their divisor count. Thus the first potentially principal third power is paid, not suppressed.

If both sides mark the same slot, independent prime sums count a common prime twice. The *exact* correction is the single-prime sum with multiplier
\[
 f_s(p)-f_s(p)^2
 =\psi(p)q_p^{-s}-2\psi(p)^2q_p^{-2s}+O(q_p^{-3\sigma}).
 \tag{T07.10}
\]
It obeys (T07.9) with the combined norm power; since \(b-\sigma>0\), its bound fits that of the product of the two slot sums. Different slots have disjoint supports.

Fix \(u,v,n,n',r,D,E\) and a priority pattern. Marks assigned outside \(g\) have divisor-many choices, because they divide those fixed cores or cube labels. Freeze them first. Their priority exclusions enter \(M\). Marks assigned to \(g\) avoid those choices and the embedded products, and are summed with (T07.9)–(T07.10). A common prime of \(D,E\) is excluded as a *mark*, but is not deleted from \(g\) unless an original character zero requires it. A prime assigned to \(g\) on one side and outside it on the other is correctly excluded. A prime in both \(g\) and a cube label remains allowed.

For completeness, the original coupled profiles survive this step as follows. Let \(a,a'\) be their independent Mellin variables and \(z\) the variable of \(w(q_g/G)\). Replace \(z\) by the squarefree-series variable \(s=1+a+a'+z\). The transformed factor is
\[
 \widehat w(s-1-a-a')G^{s-1-a-a'}\widehat V(a)\widehat{\bar V}(a')
 (Z/(q_uq_n^3))^a(Z/(q_vq_{n'}^3))^{a'}\mathscr S_M(s),
\]
times the finite prime expressions, with \(q_U^a,q_{U'}^{a'}\) still present. Fix the real parts of \(a,a'\) first and shift only \(s\) to \(\sigma\). The two Gaussian transforms and the annular transform control all three independent heights. Choosing either sign for the fixed real parts recovers rapid envelopes in both scale ratios. It follows that the complete marked \(g\)-sum is at most
\[
 Z^\epsilon G^{\sigma-1}R^{\sigma/2}(L_DL_E)^\sigma
 E\!\left(\frac{Gq_uq_n^3}{ZL_D}\right)
 E\!\left(\frac{Gq_vq_{n'}^3}{ZL_E}\right). \tag{T07.11}
\]
No arbitrary bounded prime coefficients are covered by this argument.

Put \(\nu_*=(1+\sigma)/2\). The outside coefficients are \(q_u^{-1/2}q_v^{-1/2}/(q_nq_{n'})\), and \(R^{\sigma/2}\ll(q_uq_vq_dq_e)^{\sigma/2}\). Counting \(u,v\) and summing the cube tails gives
\[
 \frac{Z^{1+\sigma}(L_DL_E)^{1/2+3\sigma/2}(q_dq_e)^{\sigma/2}}{G^2}Z^\epsilon.
 \tag{T07.12}
\]
The power of \(G\) is exactly \((\sigma-1)-2\nu_*=-2\).

statement:
## HCR11. Exact easy bound and its failed inequality

Choose FIXED b_*<beta<b<1. Partial summation gives

    1/zeta(b+it)=(b+it)*integral_1^infinity M(y)y^(-b-it-1)dy,
    |Phi(b+it)| <= C_(b,beta,tau)(1+|t|)exp(-tau*t^2/2).

The weighted f is integrable on the whole real line, and Phi is
integrable in t, so Fourier inversion is legitimate. Substituting it into
D_A is an absolute Fubini step: |B_(Au)(v)|<=Au and b<1 dominate the
future integral, uniformly in t before the integrable Phi factor. B0
then gives the actual all-height contour

    D_A f(u)=(2*pi)^(-1)*integral_R Phi(b+it)
                              *exp(u*phi_A(b+it))dt.      (HCR11.1)

Let delta=1-b>0 and 0<tau'<tau. For y=delta^2+t^2, the arithmetic-geometric
mean inequality gives

    tau'*t^2/2 + A*delta*u/(delta^2+t^2)
       =tau'*y/2+A*delta*u/y-tau'*delta^2/2
       >=sqrt(2*A*delta*tau'*u)-tau'*delta^2/2.

The remaining exp(-(tau-tau')t^2/2) absorbs (1+|t|). Hence

    |D_A f(u)| <= C exp(bu-sqrt(2*A*(1-b)*tau'*u)).         (HCR11.2)

This is B20. The contour uses all real t, not only |t|<=T or a fixed
window. For an absolute pointwise contour argument to force exponent
gamma<b, the missing uniform attenuation would be

    A*(1-b)/((1-b)^2+t^2) >= b-gamma   for every real t.

Its left side tends to zero. Optimizing it against the Gaussian puts
|t| at order u^(1/4), producing only the square-root-u loss in HCR11.2.
A Gaussian cutoff at order sqrt(u) leaves these smaller but growing
heights inside the contour. A fixed-height estimate does not cover them.

This failed inequality is a failure of the easy absolute method, not a
necessary condition for all possible estimates exploiting the phase and
the actual arithmetic coefficients. Nor may b decrease with u using an
uncontrolled C_b. The family of buffered estimates gives the usual
every-epsilon exponent b_* and none of the proposed improved exponents.
Combined with HCR8.4 it also pays the finite Q at exponent b_*, which is
strictly above the first-gain boundary.
title: HCR11. Exact easy bound and its failed inequality

### 2.5 Complete criterion and quantitative zero return

    H_R <= (1-delta_chi) I_R+B_chi.                    (OPEN-PF)

Then every L(s,chi) has no ordinary zero with Re s>gamma. Constants and onsets may depend on chi; the common gamma does not.

Proof: choose eta=delta_chi/4 separately in(4),(7); absorb the bounded initial R range. Insert (9) and OPEN-PF into(2). For every R>=0,

    (tau/2)|z(R)|^2+(delta_chi/2)I_R
       +tau*gamma*E_R<=B'_chi.                         (10)

Thus U(y)=O_chi(exp(gamma y)) for y>=0. The left Gaussian tail and this right bound make F(s)=int_(-infinity)^infinity U(y)exp(-sy)dy holomorphic on Re s>gamma, including all compact-uniform derivatives. Absolute Fubini on Re s>1 gives

    F(s)=exp(tau*s^2/2)/L(s,chi).

Continue L(s,chi)F(s)=exp(tau*s^2/2). Its right side is never zero. At every regular zero of L in the half-plane the left side would vanish. The principal pole at1 is allowed and forces F to vanish there; imprimitive Euler factors were already retained through chi's natural zeros. All complex heights and all zero multiplicities are covered. The ordinary continuation, pole and imprimitive-factor conventions were checked against [NIST DLMF25.15](https://dlmf.nist.gov/25.15), specifically25.15.1-4. This is a replacement source's complete return, with no borrowed native-H projectors, no unsmoothing and no fixed-height gap.

|Desired c|gamma|One allowed A|alpha=A(1-gamma)|Status|
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|

|1/6|5/6|5|5/6|Conditional|
|1/4|3/4|3|3/4|Conditional|
|.4999|.5001|1|.4999|Conditional high ceiling; gamma=1/2 is NOT covered|

The strongest objection is substantive: OPEN-PF is an unproved signed source-specific inequality. The full logarithmic equation lets its negative hard-prime correlation carry an entire hypothetical bad mode, so the identity alone cannot supply strict delta. A deliberately coarse trial does not close it. Even GRANTING an input |U(y)|<=C exp(beta y) for y>=0, gamma<beta<1, triangle and the full Gaussian left tail only give sum_p log p|U(y-log p)|<=C exp(y)(1+y). For p<=exp(y), sum over all integers p^-beta log p; for p>exp(y), use the Gaussian left tail and split into fixed log intervals. Thus the absolute flux budget has exponent1+beta-2gamma in R, whereas the available I_R budget has exponent2beta-2gamma up to logarithms. The unresolved exponent gap is1-beta. This is failure of that upper-bound trial, not a lower bound on the signed flux; the granted U input is not silently inferred from a bare zero-free assertion. The proposition is an explicit localization of that gap, with actual complete paid sectors, not a proof of a new exponent or a claim that the remaining estimate is easy. The binding source is [restricted research revision] h-joint/report.md, sections1-2, retaining the accepted JN4-JN9 transform. Freeze an original Eisenstein long-prime pair of distinct degree-one rational norms p,r (hence odd and at least7), Q=pr. Its group has Q^2 elements and UNITARY Fourier factor1/Q. The complete folded W contains both ordered short sources, equality, bounded complex gcd core, rational screen, both mark projectors, independent heights and original profiles. The kernel is

    K(h,s,s')=b0 chi_pi(h)^3 chi_pi'(h)^3
                    chi_pi(s)^2 chi_pi'(s')^4,

where b0=b(pi)conj(b(pi')) times the actual CRT root. It may vanish. All original nonunit zeros remain. The row multiplier is exactly m(h)=ell_p(h_p)ell_r(h_r), with quadratic characters zero at0; the mark factors have modulus1 at precisely phi=(p-1)(r-1) pairs and vanish elsewhere. This is the finite multiplier, not the physical mark matrix T or the scalar H.

For S_t f(h)=f(h+t),

    [M_m,S_t]=diag(m(h)-m(h+t)) S_t.

When t is nonzero in both local fields, quadratic autocorrelation is-1 in each. An elementary proof counts solutions z^2=y(y+1): the invertible change to (2y+1-2z)(2y+1+2z)=1 gives p-1 solutions. The CRT product correlation is therefore1. Both row values are nonzero at B=(p-2)(r-2) sites; exactly one vanishes at n1=2(p+r-3), and both vanish at2. The opposite-sign count is n2=(B-1)/2. Thus the nonzero singular values are2 with multiplicity n2 and1 with multiplicity n1. In particular

    rank=(Q+2p+2r-9)/2,
    HS^2=4n2+n1=2(Q-p-r)=2(phi-1),  operator norm=2.

If only the p-component of t is nonzero, the multiplicities instead are n1=2(r-1), n2=(p-1)(r-1)/2, with correlation-(r-1); the other orientation is symmetric. The full mark carrier repeats each nonzero row singular value phi times and scales it by|b0|. Fourier conjugation changes none of these quantities.

For rank k<=n2 approximation, the squared HS error is at least4(n2-k)+n1; for k<n2 the operator error is at least2. This follows by removing at most k largest singular directions, or the min-max/kernel-dimension argument. The full carrier has the corresponding repeated multiplicities and b0 scaling. This is an ambient defect statement, not a bound on W.

For k distinct integer shifts0<j<min(p,r), let P=sum c_j S_j. Their matrix diagonals are disjoint, so

    ||[M_m,P]||_HS^2=2(phi-1)||c||_2^2,

    rank[M_m,P]>=(phi-1)/(2k) if c!=0.

The valid no-saving conclusion is relative to|b0| ||c||_2, or for coefficients of nonvanishing normalized size. The displayed formulas and scale-invariant rank bound remain correct.

A useful explicit companion bound, without any cancellation assumption, is

    ||[M_m,P]||_op >= sqrt(2(phi-1)/Q) ||c||_2,

because rank<=Q and HS<=sqrt(Q) op. The full carrier multiplies this by|b0|. Thus an l2-normalized stencil has order-one operator cost even with parameter-dependent phases.
