## 4. The arithmetic pointwise bound survives the full prefix audit

For a given sufficiently large REAL x, put N=x^(3/2), T=N(log x)^2,
and U=V=floor(sqrt x). These integers are fixed throughout every
auxiliary prefix and the subsequent partial summation. The exact identity

    mu=mu_<=U+mu_<=V-mu_<=U*mu_<=V*1+mu_>U*mu_>V*1      (R5)

follows by expanding the last term and using mu*1=delta_1. It includes
n=1, squareful n, and BOTH short sums. The latter cost O(U+V).

Finite additive Fourier inversion of the original chi(n) reduces to
finitely many phases beta=ell/q-1/(2*pi*x), with total coefficient mass
bounded in terms of the fixed modulus q. This identity is applied before
the triangle inequality, so its exact natural zeros remain represented.

The following two elementary bounds are valid uniformly for real x large:

    sum_(d<=x)min(Y/d,1/(2||beta d||))
                      <<_q x log(2x)+Y/x,               (R6)
    sum_(h<=H)min(M,1/(2||beta h||))
                      <<_q (H/x+1)(M+x log(2x)).         (R7)

Here an exact resonance uses the finite first argument of min. To prove
(R7), split integers into intervals of length at most x and then into
their q residue classes. The fractional phase, with the rational part
frozen, advances monotonically by q/(2*pi*x); the total advance is less
than 1/(2*pi), up to harmless endpoint rounding. Remove at most two
nearest points to an integer, costing O(M). The other inverse distances
sum to O_q(x log(2x)) by their spacing. There are O(H/x+1) intervals
and only q classes. This proof also covers an integer lying just outside
the phase interval, and makes no Diophantine approximation assumption.

For (R6), the classes with ell d=0 mod q have exact distance d/(2*pi*x)
on d<=x and cost O(x log(2x)). On another class the initial fractional
part is j/q, 1<=j<q. A crossing of zero occurs at d*=2*pi*x*j/q.
Every nearest point in a fixed small neighborhood of that crossing has
d>=c_q x, so its finite cost is O_q(Y/x). The other points obey the same
harmonic-spacing bound. Distance to the integer 1 is at least 1/q on
these classes. If the crossing lies outside the interval, use its nearest
endpoint or the same spacing estimate. There is no discarded resonant d.
For example q=17, ell=1, d=103, x=1751/(2*pi) gives beta=6/103 and
beta d=6 EXACTLY, at a real x>d. It is handled by Y/d<<_q Y/x.

Type I has c_d=sum_(ab=d,a<=U,b<=V)mu(a)mu(b), supported on d<=UV<=x.
Using |c_d|<=tau(d)<<_eta d^eta and (R6), uniformly for Y<=T, gives
O_(q,epsilon)(x^(1+epsilon)). In particular Y/x<=x^(1/2)(log x)^2.
This is an upper bound, not a claim of an unavoidable actual Type I size.

For Type II write b_d=sum_(c|d,c>V)mu(c). The complete summation domain
is m>U, d>V, md<=Y. Dyadic boxes (M,2M]x(L,2L] which meet it have
ML<=Y and M,L<<Y/U; endpoint-truncated boxes are retained. Cauchy in m
gives an upper bound by M times the COMPLETE nonnegative Gram sum

    sum_(d,e)b_d conjugate(b_e)
       sum_(m in (M,2M], m<=Y/max(d,e)) e(beta m(d-e)).   (R8)

The inner set is one interval; its geometric sum is bounded by
min(CM,1/(2||beta(d-e)||)). Taking absolute values only at this stated
stage, and retaining the diagonal, gives

    |B|^2 << T^eta [M^2 L+ML(L/x+1)(M+x log(2x))]
          << T^eta (Y^2/U+Y^2/x+Yx)log(2x).              (R9)

Indeed M^2 L and ML^2 are <=C Y^2/U, (ML)^2/x<=Y^2/x,
and MLx<=Yx. The source's conjugation, difference sign and hyperbolic
intersection in (R8) are correct. No rectangular replacement of that
intersection is used. With Y<=T, (R9) is O(x^(5/2+epsilon)); the finite
Fourier expansion and O(log^2 x) boxes are absorbed. Thus

    sup_(Y<=T)|sum_(n<=Y)mu(n)chi(n)exp(-in/x)|
                        <<_(chi,epsilon)x^(5/4+epsilon). (R10)

Partial summation against exp(-n/N) costs at most a fixed multiple of
that supremum. The omitted infinite tail is bounded by
C N exp(-T/N)=O_A(x^(-A)) for every fixed A. This proves the literal
infinite-source estimate for every sufficiently large real x. No
character-free approximation, changing cutoff derivative, omitted short
term, integer-x restriction or unpriced tail remains.

small-row and principal complements retain their strict reserves. The
complete Fourier inversion precedes any reciprocal estimate; independent
height tails and both positive principal residues remain. A common
Delta is chosen before the target character. The numerator stays nonzero
on the required region above.87. The original Mellin contradiction and
finite-order norm lift give all ordinary Dirichlet characters modulo
every positive q, with their imprimitive factors. Classical right-edge
nonvanishing handles Re(s)>=1, including nonprincipal s=1; the principal
pole is excepted. The original fixed finite-order trivial-infinity
Eisenstein Hecke scope is retained. No growing-family or new infinity-type
uniformity is inferred.

A stronger combined support/slot saving and tilted plane are being
independently reviewed. Their proposed c=.12514261 is not accepted by

# [private research revision]: actual-source costs of positive certificates

Accept G167–G169 from the frozen [W61 author](wild61/report.md) and
[independent critic](wild61-review/report.md). The main new result supplies
actual squarefree coefficients that force an almost-linear root cost for
global positive certificates with short additive bandwidth or a small
union of permitted offsets. It extends [G129](../[private research revision]/wild54-integration.md),
with a different hypothesis and counting argument from
[G161](../[private research revision]/wild60-integration.md). Full graph, heat, occupation and
compact-source identities locate the remaining signed estimates. Reused
mechanisms retain their credit; none proves a higher c.

The accepted written c11=312864909/2500000000=.1251459636 and
γ11=2187135091/2500000000=.8748540364 remain unchanged. These are
source-relative research results, with inherited analytic/F0,
positive-slot and external admission obligations open. No formalization,
new proof packet or public record claim is part of this cycle.

## G167. Global positive majorants need sufficiently nonlocal interactions

Fix an ordinary character χ modulo fixed q and the literal vector
a_n=μ(n)χ(n),1≤n≤N, including natural zeros. Write ℓ=(1,…,1). A global
terminal certificate is a Hermitian matrix

\[
P\succeq\ell\ell^*,\qquad |M_\chi(N)|^2\le a^*Pa.       \tag{96.1}
\]

P may depend arbitrarily on χ,N and the actual source. The same results
hold after restricting to the nonzero source support, provided original
integer labels still determine matrix offsets. A certificate required
only on a separately proved reachable-state class is a different condition
and is not ruled out.

For a partition into blocks B_j, set b_j=∑_{n∈B_j}a_n. The exact optimum is

\[
\inf_{P\text{ block diagonal},\ P\succeq\ell\ell^*}a^*Pa
   =\left(\sum_j|b_j|\right)^2.                        \tag{96.2}
\]

Rotate one scalar phase on each block to align its sum. This leaves the
block-diagonal energy unchanged, while (96.1), which holds on all inputs,
forces the lower bound. Conversely use block weights
(∑|b_j|)/|b_j| times ℓ_jℓ_j*, with weighted Cauchy. Zero-sum blocks receive
an arbitrarily small reciprocal-weight share and a limit; if all sums
vanish the energy zero is attainable. This is an infimum statement, not a
claim of universal attainment or invertibility.

Suppose I consists of K squarefree q-units isolated from every other
nonzero source coordinate by P's permitted off-diagonal support. Then
P_II is diagonal, all actual I-to-complement cross terms vanish, and
P_II≽ℓ_Iℓ_I* implies ∑_{n∈I}P_nn≥K². Since |a_n|=1 on I and the
complementary principal block is positive semidefinite,

\[
a^*Pa\ge K^2.                                          \tag{96.3}
\]

This is a certificate cost, not |Mχ(N)|≥K. The dense admissible matrix
P=ℓℓ* has exactly the actual energy |Mχ(N)|² and retains distant signed
cross terms.

### Uniform arithmetic supply

For half-bandwidth h≥1, choose distinct primes p_r>h, p_r∤q, for each
0<|r|≤h. Impose

\[
n\equiv1\pmod q,\quad n\equiv-r\pmod{p_r^2},\quad
Q=q\prod_r p_r^2.
\]

The residue a_0 modulo Q is coprime to Q. Every shifted neighbor n+r is
squareful. For any coprime residue modulo any Q, square-divisor expansion
gives the explicit uniform estimate, N≥4,

\[
\#\{n\le N:n\equiv a_0\pmod Q,\ \mu(n)^2=1\}
=\frac NQ\prod_{p\nmid Q}(1-p^{-2})+R,\qquad
|R|\le3\sqrt N.                                       \tag{96.4}
\]

There are at most √N counting errors, each at most1, for d²|n with
(d,Q)=1. The omitted Euler tail contributes at most2√N/Q. The product is
at least1/ζ(2)>1/2. Deleting at most2h endpoint indices produces

\[
K\ge\max(0,N/(2Q)-3\sqrt N-2h).                        \tag{96.5}
\]

No prime theorem in progressions is used. The elementary central-binomial
bounds 4^m/(2m+1)≤binom(2m,m)≤(2m)^{π(2m)} supply π(x)≫x/log x:
each prime contributes at most2m to that factorization. Thus the required
2h primes can lie below C_q h log(2h), and

\[
\log Q\le\log q+4h\log(C_qh\log(2h)).                 \tag{96.6}
\]

For h=o(log N/loglog N), (96.3)–(96.6) force root cost N^{1−o(1)}.
For h=⌊κ log N/loglog N⌋ with fixed0<κ<1/8, they give
sqrt(a*Pa)≥N^{1−4κ−o(1)}. The upper restriction ensures the main term in
(96.5) dominates √N. Fixed h gives K≫_{q,h}N.

More generally let D_N be a symmetric set of permitted nonzero offsets,
all of absolute value at most N−1, and let k=|D_N|. Assign each r a
distinct prime not dividing qr. At any assignment at most
k−1+ω(q)+⌊log₂N⌋ primes are forbidden, so the first
J=k+ω(q)+⌊log₂N⌋+1 primes suffice. Their sizes are O(J log(2J)). The same
CRT construction gives

\[
\log Q\le\log q+2k\log(CJ\log(2J)),\qquad
K\ge\max(0,N/(2Q)-3\sqrt N).                           \tag{96.7}
\]

Neighbors outside the cutoff are irrelevant; no endpoint deletion is
needed. Hence k=o(log N/loglog N) also forces root cost N^{1−o(1)}, and
k∼κ log N/loglog N,0<κ<1/4, gives N^{1−2κ−o(1)}. Offsets may be large,
move with N, or be chosen after seeing the source. Crucially k counts
the **total union of offsets**, including both signs. Bounded row degree
with many distinct offsets is not covered; neither are general prime
dilation graphs merely because their rows are sparse.

For a target root exponent γ, the necessary thresholds are κ≥(1−γ)/4
for half-bandwidth and κ≥(1−γ)/2 for the offset union:

| Target | Half-bandwidth coefficient | Total-offset coefficient |
|---|---:|---:|
| Strict improvement over c11 | >.0312864909 | >.0625729818 |
| c=.1252 | ≥.0313 | ≥.0626 |
| c=1/6 | ≥1/24 | ≥1/12 |
| c=1/4 | ≥1/16 | ≥1/8 |

These are necessary widths, not sufficient savings or claims at an
unresolved equality threshold. q stays fixed.

### The complete nonlocal correction

Let P=D+E≽ℓℓ*, with D≽0 having the preceding support and E Hermitian,
||E||≤η in Euclidean operator norm. The exact same isolated set gives

\[
a^*Pa\ge K^2-\eta(K+N).                                \tag{96.8}
\]

The principal inequality costs ηK; the whole source error costs
η||a||²≤ηN. Positivity of D's complementary block is essential.
For K=N^{1−o(1)}, a fixed root exponent γ<1 therefore requires a
nonlocal correction with norm at least N^{1−o(1)} along this bound.
Small individual entries do not imply a small operator cost. Nonlocal
signed metrics, signed debts and proved source-only inequalities remain
eligible.

## G168. Exact harmonic and heat costs

The sorted-prime state from [G145](../[private research revision]/wild57-integration.md) is
retained: for σ>1/2, Tσ e_n=∑_{p>P⁺(n)}χ(p)p^−σ e_np on squarefree
q-units has ||Tσ^j||²≤Sσ^j/j!, Sσ=∑p^−2σ. Disjoint descendants follow
by deleting the j largest primes. Its convergent inverse gives
v(n)=μ(n)χ(n)n^−σ, but the physical output norm is asymptotic to a
constant times N^{σ+1/2}. This is reused source formation, not a new gap.
Diagonal congruence transports banded terminal metrics to G167 without
discarding a norm factor.

On all squarefree q-units at most N, take the connected graph n—np with
arbitrary positive edge weights. Let L be its real Laplacian, U=diag(a_n),
L_a=ULU*. Then x*L_a x=∑w_{n,p}|x_np+χ(p)x_n|² and L_a a=0. For
λ,η>0, H=λL_a+ηe_1e_1* is positive definite with a*Ha=η. Put
f=U*ℓ=conjugate(a), R=V_N\{1}, and E_N=f_R*(L_RR)^−1 f_R≥0. Exactly,

\[
\ell^*H^{-1}\ell=|M_\chi(N)|^2/\eta+E_N/\lambda,
\quad H\succeq\ell\ell^*\iff
|M_\chi(N)|^2/\eta+E_N/\lambda\le1.                    \tag{96.9}
\]

After conjugation, solve (λL+ηe_1e_1*)x=f. Summing yields
x_1=(∑f)/η; writing x=x_1ℓ+y,y_1=0 gives λL_RR y_R=f_R and (96.9).
If M≠0, require λ>E_N and η≥|M|²/(1−E_N/λ). If M=0, λ≥E_N suffices
for any η>0, including equality. N=1 has E_N=0. A graph gap may bound
the Green term; it cannot remove the actual harmonic amplitude.

There is an analogous exact bill for arbitrary positive diagonal Witten
weights on the downward-closed squarefree q-unit complex. Let d be
oriented deletion, S positive diagonal, d_S=SdS^−1,
Q_S=d_S+d_S*, Δ_S=Q_S², and Tχ the diagonal character insertion. The
adjoint matters: Δ_S is generally not SΔS^−1. Homology is unchanged,
while the positive spectrum may move. For principal χ the heat
supertrace equals the index Mχ(N) for every heat time.

For a general character, graded cyclicity and integration of the heat
derivative give, for every T≥0,

\[
M_\chi(N)=\operatorname{Str}(T_\chi e^{-T\Delta_S})
 +\frac12\int_0^T\operatorname{Str}
 ([T_\chi,Q_S]Q_Se^{-t\Delta_S})\,dt.                  \tag{96.10}
\]

In particular Str(TχΔ_S)=∑_{n,p}|S_n/S_np|² μ(n)χ(n)(1−χ(p)), with
every edge retained. Since S and Tχ commute,
[Tχ,d_S]=S[Tχ,d]S^−1; the deformation cannot make a nonzero commutator
vanish. For positive spectral gap λ*, the heat remainder beyond the
harmonic projection Π_0 is at most dim(V_N)e^−Tλ*. The integral also
converges because Q_SΠ_0=0, leaving the **twisted harmonic trace plus
the entire integrated bulk**.

For the actual nonprincipal character modulo3 at N=2, Tχ=diag(1,−1),
Q_S=[[0,w],[w,0]], w>0, and Π_0=0. The two terms in (96.10) are
2e^−Tw² and2(1−e^−Tw²), while the true source is2. Enlarging the gap
does not save the complete readout. This is a finite counterexample to
dropping the bulk, not an all-scale Mertens lower bound or a rejection
of all Witten constructions. The general harmonic warning is
[G74](../[private research revision]/wild46-integration.md); the cutoff ancestry and full
character bulk are [G164–G165](../[private research revision]/wild59-integration.md).

The author's specified superdeterminants are likewise exact:
sdet(I+zΔ)=1 and sdet(zI+Δ)=z^{Mχ₀(N)}, as meromorphic ratios after
cancellation. The unknown source remains in the zero-mode exponent.
Different regularizations or torsion definitions need their own return.

## G169. Complete occupation and compact-source interfaces

For uniform n∈{1,…,N}, every prime p≤N, including ramified primes, set

\[
U_p(n)=-(1+\chi(p))1_{p\mid n}+\chi(p)1_{p^2\mid n},
\quad Z_N(z)=\mathbb E\prod_p(1+z_pU_p).
\]

The factors equal1 at valuation zero,−χ(p) at valuation one and0 at
larger valuations. Thus Z_N(1)=Mχ(N)/N. First and distinct-prime moments
retain their literal floors:

\[
m_p=\frac{-(1+c_p)\lfloor N/p\rfloor+c_p\lfloor N/p^2\rfloor}{N},
\]
\[
m_{pr}=\frac{(1+c_p)(1+c_r)\lfloor N/(pr)\rfloor
 -(1+c_p)c_r\lfloor N/(pr^2)\rfloor
 -c_p(1+c_r)\lfloor N/(p^2r)\rfloor
 +c_pc_r\lfloor N/(p^2r^2)\rfloor}{N}.                  \tag{96.11}
\]

The formal log includes overlapping and repeated clusters; even though
Z_N is multiaffine, the z_p² coefficient of log Z_N is−m_p²/2.
Convergence at the physical activity requires a separate theorem.

For independent n,m define V_p=U_p(n)+conjugate(U_p(m))+
U_p(n)conjugate(U_p(m)). Then E∏(1+V_p)=|Mχ(N)/N|², including the
complete diagonal and off-diagonal. Its distinct two-prime connected
coefficient is |1+m_p+m_r+m_pr|²−|1+m_p|²|1+m_r|². A bound for a
selected cluster or a different Gaussian kernel is not a bound for this
complete contraction.

For q=1, keep only primes √N<p≤N and give them common activity t.
No integer up to N contains two of them, so

\[
Z_H(t)=1-B_Nt,\qquad
B_N=\frac2N\sum_{\sqrt N<p\le N}\lfloor N/p\rfloor
\longrightarrow2\log2>1.                              \tag{96.12}
\]

The limit follows from the [ordinary PNT](https://dlmf.nist.gov/27.2.E3),
partial summation and floor error at mostπ(N)/N=o(1). Thus this actual
partial marginal has a zero t_N=1/B_N inside(0,1) for all large N.
At N=100, B_N=27/25. Its logarithm at zero has radius less than1 and
the absolute series ∑B_N^j/j diverges at1. This blocks an absolutely
convergent log expansion on the full unit activity polydisc. It does
not turn a marginal zero into an L-zero or refute resummed, conditioned,
signed or differently parametrized replica expansions. The full
cross-sector return remains necessary. G145's high-prime clique, W51
fugacity and W38/[restricted research revision] occupation laws retain their ancestry.

The author also provides an explicit compact verification interface for
[G128's literal normalized source](../[private research revision]/wild54-integration.md).
Let δ indicate principal χ, r=δφ(q)/q, b(t)=∑_{n≤e^t}χ(n)−re^t, and

\[
F_\chi(s)=\left(\frac{s-1}{s+1}\right)^\delta\frac{L(s,\chi)}s
 =\int_0^\infty e^{-st}f(t)\,dt,\qquad |f(t)|\le C_q=1+3q.
\]

Here f=b for nonprincipal χ and
f(t)=re^−t+b(t)−2∫₀ᵗe^{−(t−u)}b(u)du for principal χ. F has exactly
the ordinary L-zeros on Re(s)>0; its value at the removed principal pole
is r/2, nonzero. If F_T truncates the integral at T, then on Re(s)≥σ₀>0,
|F−F_T|≤C_qe^−σ₀T/σ₀ and |F′|≤C_q/σ₀².

For a convex compact cell of radius d around z, a certified value v of
F_T(z) with error ε proves nonvanishing throughout that cell if

\[
|v|>\varepsilon+C_qe^{-\sigma_0T}/\sigma_0
                  +(C_q/\sigma_0^2)d.                 \tag{96.13}
\]

This pays truncation, evaluation and interpolation. If F is nonzero on
a given compact K, its positive minimum modulus lets all three errors
shrink below one eighth of that minimum, forcing eventual success.
Conversely soundness forbids success on a compact containing a zero.
Thus it is a semidecision procedure, with no efficiency claim and no
numerical execution in this cycle. Success on every
K_m={γ+1/m≤Re(s)≤m+2, |Im(s)|≤m} is equivalent to zero exclusion on
Re(s)>γ. The all-m premise remains unproved. Finite successes cannot
replace it, and G130's raw principal global-polynomial obstruction does
not reject this normalized compact construction.

## Return, evidence and next estimate

A complete bound for the actual Mχ(N), at one common γ and every fixed
ordinary χ, every ε>0 and all sufficiently large N, gives locally uniform
Abel continuation s∫₁∞Mχ(x)x^−s−1dx to Re(s)>γ. It equals1/L initially
on Re(s)>1 and retains principal poles, imprimitive factors and all finite
heights. Squared-energy bounds must retain every ε before taking square
roots. First gain needs γ<.8748540364; the illustrative γ=.8748,5/6,3/4
need complete squared exponents1.7496,5/3,3/2. No such saving is supplied.

S11's fixed-prime cone and S26's outgoing cutoff-flux readout are preserved
duplicates of G144 and Sol04 S38, with full reconstruction factors.
The latter observes the image in(X,pX]; projecting it back into[1,X]
would instead give zero. No general flux or torsion impossibility follows.

The [retention manifest](retention-manifest.json) binds32 frozen files,
13 reviewer sources and11 author sources, including historical navigation
bytes. Both full reports, helpers and receipts were read; existing exact
checks were not rerun. Finite checks validate algebra/indexing rather than
asymptotic cancellation. An actual host-local claim receipt is excluded.
All30 cards, author six S04/S29/S13/S11/S26/S23 and independent protected
S19/uniform S15 survive. Literal pools22/12/25, original entropy and
critic prep before outcome intake remain; no stronger chronology is
claimed. All29 families/109 children and later ideas are preserved.

The useful next work is a signed nonlocal or proved reachable-state
estimate escaping G167, control of the complete harmonic/heat readout,
a reorganized complete occupation contraction, or an all-compact
arithmetic margin. Chaining and simultaneous detector use remain eligible
when every transfer and complementary term is paid.

## 7. Exact all-branch linear-probe transfer

More generally let \(B_{\rm tar}>0\) be a fixed polynomial scale factor and suppose the cutoff in each nonempty branch satisfies
\[
1\le H_{0,D}\le Q_D^{10/11}B_{\rm tar}^{12/11}.
\tag{XM31}
\]
Then (XM26) gives a raw bound \(Q_DY_D^{-1/2}B_{\rm tar}Z^\epsilon\). The outside factor in (XM9) is
\[
|\omega_D|q_D^{-3/2}Q_D^{-1/2}
=\frac{|\omega_D|}{\sqrt Q\sqrt{q_D}}.
\]
Its product with the raw bound is exactly
\[
|\omega_D|q_D^{-2}\sqrt{Q/Y}\,B_{\rm tar}Z^\epsilon.
\tag{XM32}
\]
The source and row scales are those of this branch. There is no substitution of the common physical \(Q\) for \(Q_D\) inside its row estimate.

For each fixed slot subset, the original prime weights give
\[
\sum_D|\omega_D|q_D^{-2}
\ll_\epsilon Z^\epsilon
\prod_{i\in\mathcal J}\sum_{q_p\asymp P_i}q_p^{-2}
\ll_\epsilon Z^\epsilon\prod_{i\in\mathcal J}P_i^{-1}
\ll_\epsilon Z^\epsilon.
\tag{XM33}
\]
Bounded smooth weights and divisor-bounded variants are included by choosing smaller losses. There are finitely many subsets. Thus the original compensated linear probe restricted atomwise, in each branch, by (XM31) obeys
\[
\boxed{
|I^{\rm comp}_{\rm low\ act}|
\ll_\epsilon Z^\epsilon\sqrt{Q/Y}\,B_{\rm tar}.
}
\tag{XM34}
\]
This is an absolute bound after each arithmetic row sum, so an extra bounded row-independent label mask is permitted throughout.

Two useful choices are:

- \(B_{\rm tar}=P_a^{-\delta}\), \(\delta\ge0\): the all-source band
  \(h_{{\rm act},D}\le Q_D^{10/11}P_a^{-12\delta/11}\) costs
  \(Z^\epsilon\sqrt{Q/Y}P_a^{-\delta}\).
- \(B_{\rm tar}=P_a^{1/12}\): the band
  \(h_{{\rm act},D}\le Q_D^{10/11}P_a^{1/11}\) costs
  \(Z^\epsilon\sqrt{Q/Y}P_a^{1/12}\), the linear scale corresponding to the sufficient covariance target \(Y^{-1}P_a^{1/6}\).

If a displayed cutoff is below one, the corresponding good-conductor sector is empty. No nonempty branch with subunit conductor is introduced.

## 7. Complete zero-exclusion return, and the weaker sufficient observation

Fix ONE gamma with 1/2<gamma<gamma11 before choosing characters or hypothetical zeros. Fix J>=2 with beta_J=max(1/2,1-1/J)<=gamma. For every fixed chi choose a fixed pair of distinct unramified primes as described below. The author's OPEN-RHCHAIN condition is

    |T_(p,J)(x)| <<_(chi,p,J,epsilon)x^(gamma+epsilon)

for each prime, every epsilon>0, and all sufficiently large REAL x. By (6.5), it is equivalent to the same pointwise bound for S_(p,J) in this exponent range. This is an exact paid source comparison, not a claim that the new bound is arithmetically easier.

Initially for Re s>1, absolute Dirichlet convergence and ordinary partial summation give

    P_p(s)^J/L(s,chi)
       =s int_1^infinity S_(p,J)(x)x^(-s-1) dx.            (7.1)

The n=1 coefficient is correctly included; the formula holds for the right-continuous sharp summatory function. The finite initial interval contributes an entire function. The assumed bound and an epsilon buffer give normal convergence, including s derivatives, on every compact subset of Re s>gamma. Thus (7.1) is holomorphic there. Ordinary Dirichlet-L meromorphy identifies this continuation with the original quotient; no reciprocal power bound has been imported.

Zeros of P_p lie on Re s=1. At a common nonzero-height zero for two different primes, each t log p/(2pi) is a nonzero rational number because chi(p) has finite order. Their ratio would make log p1/log p2 rational, impossible for distinct primes. For nonprincipal chi choose one prime with chi(p)!=1: factor a unit integer with nontrivial character value to find such a prime. This covers height zero. For a principal character, the pole of L at s=1 is the allowed exception and gives a zero of 1/L. The power J changes orders but not the numerator zero locations.

Consequently every hypothetical ordinary zero in Re s>gamma is visible for at least one fixed prime. All natural imprimitive Euler factors remain, and every finite height is covered. Constants may depend on the fixed character and primes; no growing-conductor or uniform-in-height estimate is required.

### 7.1 Correction and independent shell-L1 extension

For clarity define ||F||_(j,X)=(int_X^(2X)|F(x)|^j dx/x)^(1/j). A pointwise bound at exponent gamma implies a shell-L2 bound at that exponent, and shell L2 implies shell L1 by finite-measure Cauchy. Therefore author line376's statement that an L2 condition would be stronger is not valid for these usual shell norms. An absolute-coefficient bound would indeed be stronger. The undefined L2 wording should be removed or qualified; it does not damage the actual proved pointwise implication.

In fact the following WEAKER complete sufficient input has its own paid return:

    int_X^(2X)|T_(p,J)(x)| dx/x
          <<_(chi,p,J,epsilon) X^(gamma+epsilon)           (OPEN-L1-CHAIN)

for both fixed covering primes, every epsilon>0 and every sufficiently large dyadic X. No subinterval or sample set is omitted; the underlying source remains the literal sharp summatory function. Equation (6.5) pays the entire comparison in shell L1 at the same exponent, including equality beta_J=gamma. On a compact set with Re s>=gamma+delta choose epsilon<delta/2. The absolute contribution of the dyadic shell to (7.1), and to each fixed s derivative, is bounded by

    C_K (log(2X))^m X^(-delta+epsilon).

The sum over dyadic X converges, proving normal holomorphy exactly as before. Hence OPEN-L1-CHAIN suffices for the SAME all-height ordinary-character zero exclusion, with the same principal exception and two-prime cover. Shell-L2 at the same exponent also suffices. No converse from zero exclusion, no pointwise recovery at exponent gamma, and no attained shell estimate are asserted.

This adjustment is an observation requirement, not an arithmetic gain. The complete new input remains open. It is consistent with earlier shell-observation returns but is proved here for this exact sharp source, with all finite filters and low-chain complements paid.

### 7.2 Calibration and full remaining price

The complete parameter rows remain:

| Prospective gamma | Fixed J | Paid low exponent | Conditional c |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 2187/2500=.8748 | 7 | 6/7 | .1252 |
| 5/6 | 6 | 5/6 | 1/6 |
| 3/4 | 4 | 3/4 | 1/4 |

The nearer prospective gain over c11 is 135091/2500000000=.0000540364. Equality at the latter two low-source endpoints is permitted; (5.4) even removes their low-source epsilon loss. The arithmetic input must still hold for every epsilon. These are not accepted endpoint increases or new source admissions.

For squarefree n, J^omega(n)=d_J(n). The complete residual obeys |r_J(n)|<=C_J d_J(n) on that support and zero elsewhere. Elementary repeated harmonic summation gives sum_(n<=x)d_J(n)<<_J x log^(J-1)(2x). Paying every filter term yields the entire bound

    |T_(p,J)(x)| <<_(p,J)x log^(J-1)(2x).                  (7.2)

Every p^a coefficient p^a meets its actual argument x/p^a; their powers cancel in this estimate. Terms with x/p^a<1 are empty. The bound proves only exponent one, including in shell L1 and L2. It misses each target by 1-gamma plus logarithms. Nothing in the new observation criterion, determinant dimension, positive permanent or fixed-color calculation supplies that power.

The next color t=8 has the available exponent 7/8, above gamma11 by .0001459636. A better bound for that one color would pay one extra sector; it would still leave every higher chain depth. This proximity does not calculate a new zero-free constant.

statement:
### 4.2 Whole nonlinear kernel and the low/high split

Choose one nonnegative smooth w supported in[1/2,3], w>=1 on[1,2]. The weighted shell kernel K_X(n,m)=integral w(x/X)f_x(n)conj(f_x(m))dx/x obeys

 |K_X(n,m)| << exp(-c(n+m)/X^(3/2))
                    min(1,(X^6/|n^6-m^6|)^2),           (LG5)

with the minimum set to1 on the exact diagonal. Substitute x=Xu and integrate by parts twice in the nonstationary phase -(n^6-m^6)/(X^6u^6). Its derivative has no zero on the fixed support. Derivatives of the damping cost a fixed polynomial in (n+m)/X^(3/2), absorbed into a slightly weaker exponential. Compactly supported w removes boundary terms. This proves (LG5) on the full shell, not a sampled x grid.

Split B_G=B_lo+B_hi at the CLOSED cutoff n<=X. By (LG4), |B_lo(x)|<<X^(1+eta)/G throughout the support of w. All low/high interactions are paid by the norm triangle inequality, so no unconditional small scalar mixed term is asserted. It remains to bound the entire norm of B_hi, n>X. Expansion is justified first for finite truncations and then by local absolute convergence.

Partition every ordered upper pair into comparable pairs (ratio between1/2 and2) and far pairs. A bounded-overlap dyadic covering puts every comparable pair in [N/2,4N]^2 for some N>=cX. Let H=X^6/N^5. On this block |n^6-m^6| is bounded below by a fixed multiple of N^5|n-m|. The kernel is bounded by exp(-cN/X^(3/2))min(1,(H/|n-m|)^2), including its diagonal.

Using (LG3), the weighted r_G mass about ANY integer center n is O(H/G+E_N): divide distances into |m-n|<=H and successive doubling rings. For H>=1, local count gives a geometric sum H/G+E_N. For H<1, use |m-n|<=H for the possible diagonal and doubling rings beginning at H; empty subunit rings contribute nothing, and the same upper bound follows (or begin off-diagonal rings at1 with weight O(H^2)). Intersecting a ring interval with [N/2,4N] costs at most two intervals with the same fixed constants. Multiplying by the complete block mass O(N/G) gives the positive pair majorant

 P_N << exp(-cN/X^(3/2)) N^(2eta)
                      [X^6/(G^2 N^4)+(N/G)E_N].        (LG6)

Separately, the unweighted integer-kernel row sum is O(1+H): the off-diagonal sum over nonzero integer distances is O(H) for H>=1 and O(H^2)<=O(H) for H<1. Apply 2|v_G(n)v_G(m)|<=|v_G(n)|^2+|v_G(m)|^2 and (LG4) on [N/2,4N]. This bounds THE SAME positive pair majorant by

 P_N << exp(-cN/X^(3/2)) N^(2eta)(N/G)(1+H).             (LG7)

The global l2 density alone would leave the larger HN/G cost near N~X. It is (LG6), retaining the local square-divisor count, that closes this loss. Taking the minimum of the two valid bounds for the same complete block, and using min(A+B,C+D)<=A+C+min(B,D), gives

 P_N << exp(-cN/X^(3/2)) N^(2eta)
       [X^6/(G^2 N^4)+(N/G)(1+min(N^(1/3),H))].        (LG8)

Constants/exponentials are first made common. Both ordered orientations, exact coincidences, all distinct roots giving the same output, and all masks were included before taking this minimum.

Sum (LG8) over dyadic N>=cX. The first term is O(X^(2+2eta)/G^2). Actual damping pays the isolated1 term by O(X^(3/2+3eta)/G). The remaining sum is bounded without damping by

 (1/G)sum_(N dyadic>=cX)N^(1+2eta)min(N^(1/3),X^6/N^5)
       <<_eta X^(3/2+9eta/4)/G, 0<eta<1.               (LG9)

Indeed its increasing term N^(4/3+2eta) and decreasing term X^6N^(-4+2eta) meet at N=X^(9/8). Their geometric tails converge. This argument uses every high block, not only an average block or a low-frequency range. Blocks with G>sqrt(4N) are empty and may be kept as zero.

For far pairs take n~N, X<m<n/2, and include the reverse orientation. The gap is bounded below by a constant times N^6. The absolute coefficient shell and cumulative masses from (LG4) are each O(N^(1+eta)/G). Thus their complete total is

 <<sum_(N dyadic>=cX) X^12 N^(-12) N^(2+2eta)/G^2
 << X^(2+2eta)/G^2.                                    (LG10)

Damping can only improve this bound. There is no omitted large/small cross pair: both entries here belong to B_hi; B_lo/B_hi were paid earlier by triangle. Combining (LG8)-(LG10), the low bound and norm triangle gives

 ||B_G||_2^2 <<_(eta,B_0) X^(2+2eta)/G^2+X^(3/2+3eta)/G.

Choose eta>0 after the requested epsilon, for example eta=min(epsilon/4,1/4), to prove (LG1). L1 follows by Cauchy-Schwarz on logarithmic measure log2. This completes the theorem uniformly for every G>=1 and every stated frozen mask.

### 3a(ii). A cheaper coherent source approximation, and a principal tail theorem

The K^N bound above is not intrinsic. If h_tilde is any fully specified L2 approximation with ||h-h_tilde||<=tau, the isometry of Q gives, for EVERY polynomial p,

    ||p(Q)h-p(Q)h_tilde||<=tau sum_j |p_j|.            (13a)

Consequently the exact residual is at most the fully computed residual of h_tilde plus this price. Each Gram-entry error is at most tau(||h||+||h_tilde||), independent of j,k. The matrix operator error is at most N+1 times that number. These are signed-source approximation bounds, not a positive-semidefinite comparison of the two source Grams. The simple choice h_tilde=h*1_[0,T] has tau<=H0 exp(-gamma T)/sqrt(2gamma). Its filtered output is NOT truncated: after T, Q^j h_tilde has its complete exponential-polynomial tail, which is explicitly computable from the finite convolution states at T. This retains the omitted future response and avoids K^N. The coefficient sum and the main residual remain payable.

For q=1, this can be improved unconditionally. Suppose 1/2<gamma<1, put lambda=a-gamma=2-2gamma in (0,1), and D_lambda=(2-lambda)/(4(1-lambda)). With u={x}, identity (3a) becomes

    f(log x)=1/2+B(x)-V(x)/x,
    B(x)=1/2-{x}, V(x)={x}(1-{x}).                    (13b)

The continuous periodic primitive of B starting at x=1 is P(x)=V(x)/2, with 0<=P<=1/8. Integration by parts gives, for x>=1,

    |integral_x^infinity y^(lambda-1)(f(log y)-1/2)dy|
       <=D_lambda x^(lambda-1).                      (13c)

Indeed the B term is at most x^(lambda-1)/4: one endpoint term at most x^(lambda-1)/8 and one integrated term of the same bound. The V/y term is at most x^(lambda-1)/[4(1-lambda)]. Thus, for a real constant C_lambda defined by the convergent subtracted integral,

    h(t)=sqrt(2a)/(2lambda) exp(-gamma t)
         +sqrt(2a) C_lambda exp(-a t)+R(t),
    |R(t)|<=sqrt(2a)D_lambda exp(-(gamma+1)t).          (13d)

No unknown L reciprocal enters this constant or proof. For a FINITE source approximation no infinite constant is needed: let A0=sqrt(2a)/(2lambda), keep h unchanged on [0,T], and for t>T use

    h_tilde_T(t)=A0 exp(-gamma t)
       +(h(T)-A0 exp(-gamma T))exp(-a(t-T)).           (13e)

The finite prefix and value h(T) completely determine this continuation. Comparing (13d) at t and at T, or using the tail integral in (13c), proves

    ||h-h_tilde_T||_2
       <=D_lambda[1+sqrt(a/(gamma+1))]
                        exp(-(gamma+1)T).            (13f)

For the second term, the error in the coefficient C_lambda estimated at T is at most D_lambda exp(-(1-lambda)T); its L2 tail contributes D_lambda exp(-(gamma+1)T), because a+1-lambda=gamma+1. The R tail contributes the other displayed term. Combining (13a) and (13f) pays the complete omitted principal source after any finite polynomial filter, with a coefficient-sum price and faster decay. The fixed-gamma constant blows up as gamma decreases to 1/2; no endpoint claim at 1/2 follows. All three calibration targets here lie strictly above 1/2.

The sharper D_lambda above is specific to q=1. A coarser extension covers EVERY fixed ordinary character. For nonprincipal chi, A(x) is q-periodic; write it as m_chi+B_chi(x), where m_chi is its period mean. Then B_chi has mean zero, |B_chi|<=2q, and its primitive starting at 1 has modulus at most 2q^2. There is no V term below.

For principal chi, put B0(x)=A(x)-r x, let beta be its period mean, and D(x)=integral_1^x(B0(y)-beta)dy. These are q-periodic and |D|<=2q^2. Formula (3a) gives EXACTLY

    f(log x)=m_chi+B_chi(x)+V_chi(x)/x,
    m_chi=-beta, B_chi=B0-beta,
    V_chi=r+2beta-2D(x).                              (13g)

Here |B_chi|<=2q, its primitive is D, and |V_chi|<=1+2q+4q^2. Thus (13c) holds with f-1/2 replaced by f-m_chi and the admissible coarse constant

    D_chi=4q^2                                  nonprincipal,
    D_chi=4q^2+(1+2q+4q^2)/(1-lambda)             principal.     (13h)

The first 4q^2 pays the endpoint and integral of the bounded primitive; the V/x term pays the second price. The same proof gives (13d)-(13f) for every fixed chi after replacing A0 by sqrt(2a)m_chi/lambda and D_lambda by D_chi. Complex character values and natural zeros are retained. For q=1 use the much sharper explicit D_lambda rather than (13h). For example gamma=3/4 gives a=5/4,lambda=1/2 and principal q=1 source error at cutoff X=exp(T) at most (3/4)(1+sqrt(5/7))X^(-7/4), before the explicit coefficient-sum price in (13a).

This is an actual source-tail theorem for the ordinary-character family, not a prediction or Mobius estimate. All fixed-q constants are allowed. The fixed-gamma constants blow up as gamma decreases to 1/2; no endpoint claim there follows. A family zero-free claim still requires the full prediction limit for each fixed ordinary chi. A fast source approximation does not imply that the limit in (8) is zero.
title: 3a(ii). A cheaper coherent source approximation, and a principal tail theorem

# [private research revision]: all four cross-gcd sectors paid in the original mixed source

Accept G179-G181 from the controller-pinned [author draft](signed-mixed-snapshot/report.md)
and the completed [independent review](signed-mixed-review/report.md). The
review reconstructs the stronger divisor-projection energy needed to retain
the within-column cuts, then pays all four large cross-copy gcd events and
all15 intersections. The actual remaining signed residual is smaller.
OPEN-R4 and the complete physical zero-exclusion return remain open.

The accepted source-relative c11=312864909/2500000000=.1251459636 and
K=28114053/6250000 from preceding c10 remain unchanged. Original F0/analytic
ancestry, positive-slot uniformity and external root-definition/import/admission
obligations remain open. No formalization, new packet or public record claim.

Root fully read both reports, helpers and receipts, reconstructed the
independent extension, and inspected the literal PR9 B0.3/B0.7-B0.9 and
B3.1-B3.7 contracts. The [retention manifest](retention-manifest.json) binds
14 unchanged files and18 input records. Two mutable-source hashes reproduce
the original CRLF working bytes from the exact preceding [restricted research revision] LF Git blobs;
both byte representations are identified. Hashes and finite checks do not
themselves prove an analytic estimate.

The snapshot was taken after repeated author stream failures. It is explicitly
a pinned draft, with no author STOP or release asserted. The independent
reviewer completed, stopped and normally released; the original author and
claim remain in same-context recovery, with its original missed deadlines
preserved. Root acceptance concerns the reviewed frozen mathematics. No
claim bytes were copied and no other owner's reservation was released.

## Fixed source and quantifiers

Use the original Eisenstein ideals, primary/unit convention, fixed excluded
set and finite dictionary. Put phi_u(n)=nu(n)psi_u(n)^(+1 or -1), including
all natural zeros, and

    M_u(D;W)=D^(-1/2)sum_n mu(n)phi_u(n)W(Nn/D),
    F_u=M_u(D1;W1)M_u(D2;W2)Q_u, D1=U^r,D2=U^s.

The original slot product Q retains disjoint slot pools, which may meet either
inverse, all coefficients and heights. The two inverse profiles have one
common real parameter and TWO independent heights. Aligning orientation, if
needed, conjugates the entire slot product at the positive norm. There is
no individual slot switch. Let P0=U^v,0<=v<=1/20 and
sup_u|Q_u|^2<<H_J U^(v+epsilon).

The positive row norm sums original nonzero sixth-power-free rows in a fixed
smooth enclosing ball. Dominate original divisor row weights before expansion.
An arbitrary signed physical projector or moving row selector is not admitted.
PR9 B0.7-B0.9 supplies only the canonical single-inverse estimate

    ||M(E;W)||_U^2 << H_J U^epsilon J(E),
    J(E)=U+U^(1/6)E^(5/6).                                (1)

Its UM slack and common-profile orders are fixed first. Moving polynomially
bounded punctures R are repaired before applying(1), by the exact identity

    M_u^(R)(E)=sum_(h R-smooth)phi_u(h)/sqrt(Nh) M_u(E/Nh),
    sum_(h R-smooth)(Nh)^(-1/2)<<_epsilon(NR)^epsilon.      (2)

The original annuli make each sum finite, and no zero character value is
divided out. Canonical coefficients cannot be replaced by an arbitrary
merged divisor-profile coefficient in B3.6.

Retain G147's physical box17/25<=delta<=7/10,
17/20<r<47/50,33/25<s<141/100,s-r>3/8. The internal buffered witness
may exceed delta=.70; extract its signal before weakening to physical
delta. With h=5-2delta define, exactly as G155,

    rho=1-10delta/(3h), k=rho+delta-1, D_K=15K-10-6Kdelta,
    a_K=delta(5-6delta)^2/(3h D_K),
    b_K=2delta(5-6delta)(K-1)/D_K,
    E_K=rho+delta v-min(3kv,a_K+b_Kv), T=delta(r+s)+E_K.

Then E_K>=rho>=19/54 and T>=123353/67500. The same-zero, common-annulus
and plain-complement restrictions of the actual witness are not erased
by using this larger box for an upper bound.

## G179. Full divisor-projection energy through the within-column cut

Keep original ordered inverse/slot tuples. Let G=U^(1/5), F_> retain
N gcd(d1,d2)>=G, and F_< retain its strict complement. For squarefree
q1,q2 let P_(q1,q2) insert q1|d1,q2|d2 in those tuples. This is a
coefficient operation, not an orthogonal row projection. For any fixed
integer A>=2 define

    D_A(X)=sum_(q1,q2 squarefree) tau(q1)^A tau(q2)^A
                                         ||P_(q1,q2)X||_U^2.

All label sums have a frozen global cap, with empty terms zero. The new
estimate needed for later cross-copy cuts is

    D_A(F_>) << H_J U^(v+epsilon)(D1/G)J(D2/G).            (3)

For real H>=1 write a_H(q)=sum_(d|q,Nd>=H)mu(q/d). Divisor inversion gives
sum_(q|g)a_H(q)=1_(Ng>=H), |a_H(q)|<=tau(q), and a_H(q)=0 if Nq<H.
The exact expansion is

    F_>=sum_f a_G(f)phi_u(f)^2/(Nf)
                       M_u^(f)(D1/Nf)M_u^(f)(D2/Nf)Q_u.

For fixed squarefree f split q_i=g_i h_i with g_i|f and(h_i,f)=1.
The condition q_i|f x_i is precisely h_i|x_i. Extracting h_i from its
canonical inverse gives the factor mu(h_i)phi_u(h_i)/sqrt(Nh_i) and
M_u^(f h_i)(E_i/Nh_i), E_i=D_i/Nf, with its original profile. Shared
primes between h1,h2 and slots remain allowed.

The first inverse's elementary bound, the second's repaired moment(1)-(2),
and all g_i divisor weights leave squared price

    H_J U^epsilon E1/(Nh1)^2
             [U/(Nh2)+U^(1/6)E2^(5/6)/(Nh2)^(11/6)].

The h1^-2 and h2^(-11/6) sums converge after small losses; the finite
h2^-1 sum costs subpower and gives NO reciprocal cutoff gain. Minkowski
in the full row x q1 x q2 Hilbert space, before summing f, proves(3).
Its worst exponent v+r+5s/6-1/5 lies below T by at least2809/273000.
Using only the unprojected G155 bound would not prove(3).

More generally, for i=1,2 put

    E_i^A(H;X)=sum_(q1,q2 sf,Nq_i>=H)tau(q1)^A tau(q2)^A
                                           ||P_(q1,q2)X||_U^2.

Extract and trivially bound inverse i, while repairing and applying(1)
to the other. The positive bounds are

    E_1^A(H;F)<<H_J U^(v+epsilon)(D1/H)J(D2),
    E_2^A(H;F)<<H_J U^(v+epsilon)(D2/H)J(D1),
    E_i^A(H;F_<)<=2E_i^A(H;F)+2D_A(F_>).                 (4)

The last line is a proved positive Hilbert-space inequality. It preserves
both within-column cuts in the paired form without asserting signed-subset
norm monotonicity. The author's same-index thresholds
H11=D1/U^(1/2),H22=D2/U^(3/4) and their signed intersection follow, with
raw gaps30607/1365000,1853/67500 and4682/16875. The intersection's U
term retains the harmonic cost mentioned above.

## G180. All four cross-copy events and every overlap

Use left indices(d1,d2), right indices(d1',d2'), and edges11,12,21,22.
Keep H11,H22 above and set H12=H21=U^(3/5). For a nonempty edge subset E,
let C_E(X) be the exact ordered-pair part of<X,X> with
N gcd(d_i,d_j')>=H_ij for every edge ij in E. Define left/right labels

    l_i=lcm(q_ij:ij in E), r_j=lcm(q_ij:ij in E),

where empty lcm=1. Repeated divisor inversion gives the literal identity

    C_E(X)=sum_(q_e sf) product_(e in E)a_H_e(q_e)
                              <P_(l1,l2)X,P_(r1,r2)X>.   (5)

The first entry has the original W1(t1),W2(t2) and full Q on its indices;
the entire second entry is conjugated, with those separately parameterized
profiles evaluated on the right indices. An opposite edge changes only
divisibility. It never exchanges the profiles, identifies heights or
conjugates a lone inverse. Individual terms can be complex; transposition
gives C_(E^t)=overline(C_E). The complete union is real, not necessarily positive.

For a fixed left lcm pair, each incident edge label divides the corresponding
l_i, with degree at most two. Since |a_H(q)|<=tau(q), all assignment weights
at that pair sum to at most tau(l1)^4 tau(l2)^4. The same holds on the
right, including shared primes between labels. Selecting any edge i0j0,
weighted Cauchy followed by this complete lcm count proves

    |C_E(X)| <= [E_i0^4(H_i0j0;X)E_j0^4(H_i0j0;X)]^(1/2). (6)

Apply(4) with X=F_<. For an opposite edge the two full-F exponents are
b1=v+r-3/5+e(s) and b2=v+s+2/5, e(t)=max(1,1/6+5t/6). The continuous
box bounds give

    T-b1>=12931/135000>1/20,
    T-b2>=rho+(113/50)delta-93/50>=9229/170625>1/20.

The second minimum occurs at delta=17/25: its derivative is bounded below
by5917/6075. Same-index-only edge subsets use the corresponding(4) bound.
Thus every one of the15 nonempty intersections is paid, including all12
that involve an opposite edge. The limiting gap is still(3).

Allocate at most1/1000 for fixed geometric pads and1/500 for ALL auxiliary
power losses combined, before distributing their individual epsilons. After
retaining margin1/200 the spare reserve is

    2809/273000-1/1000-1/500-1/200=5/2184>0.

Consequently

    sum_(nonempty E subset {11,12,21,22})|C_E(F_<)|
                              <<H_J U^(T-1/200+epsilon). (7)

The exact bad union is sum_E(-1)^(|E|+1)C_E. Equation(7) bounds absolute
values of15 complete scalar forms; it does not bound the sum of absolute
values of all underlying arithmetic pair terms.

## G181. A smaller signed residual, with the physical return still open

After(7), retain all six small-gcd conditions on the original tuples:
both within-column gcds<G, same-index cross gcds<H11,H22, and both
opposite-index cross gcds<U^(3/5). The old G156 diagonal and two conductor
sectors remain affordable after these extra restrictions, for a specific
reason: complete tuple absolute multiplicity obeys

    c_abs(n)<<H_J N0^(-1/2)U^epsilon,
    sum_n c_abs(n)^2<<H_J U^epsilon, N0=D1D2P0.

It majorizes every remaining ordered-pair subset before signs. It is not
|c_merged(n)|. Thus the old exponents1,109/60,9/5 survive with all natural
holes. Retain G157's original A^3B^2C support and conductor restrictions.

Let R4 be the exact ordered signed sum with the six gcd conditions,
n!=n', Q>U^(9/5), Q1/Q3>U^(8/5), all original slot labels, natural holes,
roots, phases, profiles and independent heights. It is real by pair
transposition and need not be positive. The full expansion gives

    ||F_<||_U^2=R4+O(H_J U^(T-1/200+epsilon)).             (8)

The new cuts remove a genuine previously retained factor pattern: with
r=.9,s=1.35 and no slots, take pairwise coprime squarefree factors of
exponents(.7,.2,1.35,.9,.65) for(q,a,e,b,f), and columns(qa,e,b,qf).
The two within and same-index gcds are1; edge12 has exponent.7. Its
relative Q1 exponent3.1 lies outside the old conductor sectors. This is
an admissible factor pattern, not a claimed zero configuration or norm
lower bound. Its transpose is handled by edge21.

The next arithmetic input is the one-sided OPEN-R4:

    R4<=H_J U^(T-xi+epsilon), some fixed xi>0,             (9)

uniformly over the licensed data and actual parameter suprema. An absolute
bound is stronger but unnecessary. Equations(3),(8) would imply free
OPEN-MIX with every strict margin below min(xi,1/200). Both actual G147
inverse-witness lower bounds and its counted prefix are still needed;
the resulting count would retain margin strictly below
min(xi,1/200,1/2000), after the stated losses. No possibly zero slot is
divided out.

This count is not a completed physical zero-exclusion proof. Both signed
physical projectors, family reconstruction, root/slot holes, exceptional
and inducing rows,6a/9a radii, K_phys and5/6 amplifier prices, clipped
rectangles, shortening, Euler shifts, errors, principal branches and the
common-mesh/actual-supremum return still require their full licensed payment.
The centered reserve is unspent. No numerical xi-to-c map is established,
and this box is not extrapolated to delta=2/3 or1/2.

The obstruction is now sharply located: fully coprime squarefree columns
can have all six gcds1 and Q1~N0^2, with Q2=Q3=1. They survive every cut,
while the available absolute envelope U N0 is too large. Their merged
two-divisor-profile coefficient is outside B3.6's canonical permission.
At equal heights a common-cofactor mu(g) sign squares away; distinct
heights retain nonpositive complex phases. Neither fact bounds the full norm.

Credit the earlier [[private research revision] MG21-MG30](../[private research revision]-continuation/mobius-gcd.md)
and its [independent review](../review-cycle-20.md) for the generic four-gcd
mechanism. That rational completed Mertens source uses four singleton Abel
summations and a fixed Mertens input; it is not imported into this unequal
Hecke mixed moment. The present useful addition is the literal original-source
projection-energy proof with independent heights, slots and all lcm labels.

For uniformity freeze the common mesh/buffer before the eventual family and
slot count, nominal cells/cuts before suprema, and one global label cap.
Do not differentiate thresholds. Tensor Sobolev keeps both inverse heights;
scale derivatives use -W/2-yW'. Fourier measures are fixed on the ambient
box before labels, derivative orders work backward through the bounded graph,
and raw label counts precede Fourier-decay choices. Genuine detector tails
remain G147's responsibility.

The independent run checked all15 graph identities in both orientations,
8192 extraction identities,3596 lcm-mass checks, natural zeros, conjugation,
weighted Cauchy and exact rational margins. One residual was negative,
confirming the importance of the one-sided contract. Those finite checks
do not prove the infinite estimate or an endpoint. The next substantive
target is signed cancellation in the actual unique relative-prime supports,
starting with the surviving fully coprime subclass and retaining both
divisor profiles and the full physical return.

## 5. Conditional direct return, with the target row and principal pole

For z=0 enlarge the norm to ALL required natural target rows Nu<=U,
including fixed-inducing rows and the actual target unit row with w_1=1.
This is a NEW input, not the old eligible positive-slot theorem. Suppose
for every needed fixed target/rectangle, every epsilon and all large U,

    OPEN-H: O6_t(U)<=C_(epsilon,T) U^(-nu+epsilon), nu>0,
    (2a-1)t>1, sigma>=a>1/2.

Choose epsilon below both strict gaps. The complete positive norm tends
to zero; its unit-row detector value therefore tends to zero. At a
hypothetical nonprincipal zero its value tends to-1, a contradiction.
Constants/thresholds may depend on each fixed target and height rectangle.
Every required rectangle must be covered for the all-height conclusion.
There is no attained family supremum or growing-conductor constant.

For a first improvement c>c11 with c<1/4, t=2 gives exponent4c-1<0.
For c=1/6,t=2 it is-1/3; for c=1/4,t=3 it is-1/2. These are conditional
returns from OPEN-H, which remains unproved. They replace the detector
upstream rather than extrapolate the old physical geometry.

For a principal target the norm must include the principal unit row.
Insert(s+z-1) in the Mellin integral, cancelling the simple L-pole before
the contour shift. Gamma(z+1)=z Gamma(z) gives the exact tail kernel

    D_R^P(s)=sum_(Nn>R) phi(n)A_R(n)(Nn)^(-s)
                [s-1+Nn/Y]e^(-Nn/Y).

At a nontrivial zero rho its value is1-rho+O(U^-A), nonzero for fixed
rho!=1. The added kernel and derivatives obey the same bounds with
polynomial height costs. OPEN-H for this modified detector gives the
same contradiction while allowing the pole at1. For a nonprincipal
target at1 use the unmodified detector, whose signal is-1. Ordinary
right-boundary treatment and the original Hecke-to-ordinary Euler lift
remain their accepted source statements; deleted Euler factors have no
zeros in Re s>0. External definition/admission obligations are unchanged.

## 15. Compact positivity and one-step improvement do not prove arithmetic approximation

**Valid operator, missing arithmetic convergence.** For \(K_w=\sum_nw_n|f_n\rangle\langle f_n|\), \(R_w(\lambda)=\langle1,\lambda(K_w+\lambda I)^{-1}1\rangle\) tends to the squared distance from \(1\) to the closed arithmetic span. Compact positivity does not prove the sufficient condition \(R_w=o(1)\). Spectral mass must include the zero atom; infinite rank prevents a positive uniform gap, and \(R_w=o(\lambda)\) is impossible by the norm lower bound. Finite truncations certify only their finite-height consequences. An optimal scalar shell step may also freeze an earlier error. Retain the resolvent and least-squares identities; pursue admissible arithmetic wavelets, revisited blocks or cumulative capture. [BB R10–R11; C9 R6–R10; A08–A09.]

## 2. The exact merged coefficient and what permission it needs

G185's complete mutual-gcd identity and finite ray expansion are retained. On each genuine primitive pair n,n', its two Gauss orientations, apart from nu(n)conjugate(nu(n')), are literally

    e=-1: R(n,n')chi_n(-1)conjugate(G(n))G(n')
           a0(n)conjugate(a0(n'))chi_n(ell)conjugate(chi_n'(ell)),
    e=+1: R(n,n')G(n)conjugate(G(n'))chi_n'(-1)
           conjugate(a0(n))a0(n')conjugate(chi_n(ell))chi_n'(ell).

Here a0(n)=conjugate(alpha(n))gamma_2(n). The CRT ratio R and the displayed G and chi(-1) factors have only the fixed ray dependence of PR9 B1.1-B1.11. They are expanded into the prescribed finite separated dictionary. No variable cubic coupling between copies is removed by assumption.

Extend the formal product expression to all individually squarefree columns, THEN insert the full sum_(f|n,f|n')mu(f). Artificial noncoprime pairs cancel pointwise in this COMPLETE sum, with the frequency selector still present. No imprimitive Poisson identity on added pairs is asserted. Put n=fm,n'=fm'. Each side independently allocates primes of f to its original two inverse colors or original slots:

    f=f1*f2*fP=g1*g2*gP,
    X=N0/Nf,
    (D1/Nf1)(D2/Nf2)(P0/NfP)=X,
    (D1/Ng1)(D2/Ng2)(P0/NgP)=X.

All assigned slot coefficients/pool tests remain. Both allocation multiplicities together are <=tau(f)^C at fixed original slot depth. Their normalization is EXACTLY

    U/[N(a)^6 N0 N(f)].                                  (2.1)

It follows from the old U/[N(a)^6 N0^2] and BOTH residual roots sqrt(X)*sqrt(X). The real factor X/sqrt(Nm Nm') stays in the common profile; it gives no extra Nf power. Imaginary norm powers extracted from either original height have modulus one. Natural frequency holes give

    chi_f(ell)conjugate(chi_f(ell))=1_((f,ell)=1).

No natural character value is divided out. The a-puncture and all remaining f-punctures stay in their own columns.

For one fixed allocation and one Fourier component, write the normalized residual column in its WHOLE merged index as

    B_f(ell)=X^(-1/2) sum_(m sf) c_f(m) chi_m(ell)^eta,
    eta=+1 or -1.                                       (2.2)

The actual c_f(m) contains a0(m) or its conjugate, fixed ray data, chi_m(f)^4 or its conjugate, the a/f punctures and the sum over ALL original residual ordered factorizations m=x*y*P. That sum keeps the shortened W1(t1), W2(t2), every remaining slot coefficient/profile and their pool tests. There is no replacement by independent signs or a model coefficient.

For a specified squarefree m, each prime can go to at most j+2 original places, at fixed j. Consequently the number of actual residual tuples is at most (j+2)^omega(m), and

    |c_f(m)| << H_J tau(m)^C,
    X^(-1) sum_(Nm~X) |c_f(m)|^2 << H_J U^epsilon.       (2.3)

This remains true with additional fixed punctures or a fixed multiplicative unit twist. It is uniform in the original f allocation, kappa, later z and all original heights at their fixed seminorm orders. Assigned slot choices were counted in tau(f)^C, not counted again here. Nonempty nominal subunit windows have bounded dilation; empty supports remain empty. Thus X may be clipped to1 at bounded cost. The factorizations have bounded original annular support, so ideal counting O(X) proves (2.3). No extra P0 squared mass is needed: the original slot labels are counted in each divisor-bounded merged coefficient.

The quadratic and cubic large sieves below explicitly permit an arbitrary inner sequence independent of the live OUTER frequency variable. They therefore permit (2.3). This is a different contract from PR9 B3.6, which still does NOT permit this coefficient. No extension of canonical terminal RE is asserted.

For a pointwise estimate used later, keep the unmerged original colors. On each side the two variables are x and y of lengths D1/Nf1,D2/Nf2, or x',y' of lengths D1/Ng1,D2/Ng2. They are never cross-copy products. G185 proves, uniformly under fixed additional holes,

    |B_f(ell)|^2 << H_J U^epsilon S0,
    S0=P0[D1+D2+(D1D2)^(2/3)].                         (2.4)

It follows from a0(xyP)=a0(x)a0(y)a0(P)chi_y(x)^4 chi_x(P)^4 chi_y(P)^4 and the squarefree cubic sieve on x,y, then triangle over ORIGINAL slots. A new z-puncture separates between x,y and those slots, so (2.4) also applies to the punctured coefficients used below.

statement:
# [private research revision]: one fixed balanced test and limits of the existing sextic budget

The accepted baseline remains c0=0.125113352960035869... and
b0=1-c0. No stronger zero-free constant is proved. This cycle
replaces the family of smooth Mobius tests by one explicit profile,
reduces its sum to two logarithmically balanced variables, and
identifies the remaining power saving. It also closes a geometry
loophole within the supplied sextic upper bounds and tests a
two-profile cancellation packet.

The controller derived the fixed-profile Mellin argument and the
geometry certificate. Separate agents checked the profile tails,
Mellin nonvanishing, geometry, and two-profile arithmetic calculation.
All assertions below retain the stated scopes; identities and
method obstructions are not improved estimates for zeta.

## 1. One fixed smooth test detects every zero in the right half-plane

For u>0 put

\[
V(u)=e^{-u-1/u},\qquad
\phi(u)=(uV(u))'=(1-u+u^{-1})e^{-u-1/u},\qquad
S_\phi(x)=\sum_{n\ge1}\mu(n)\phi(n/x). \tag{V1}
\]

Extend phi by zero to u<=0. It is a real Schwartz function, flat
at zero, with integral zero. Its entire Mellin transform is

\[
\Phi(s)=\int_0^\infty\phi(u)u^{s-1}\,du
       =2(1-s)K_s(2). \tag{V2}
\]

Integration by parts gives the factor 1-s. Substituting u=e^t
in the remaining integral gives the usual integral representation
of K_s; see [NIST DLMF 10.32.9](https://dlmf.nist.gov/10.32.E9).
This standard identity does not by itself assert nonvanishing.

**Nonvanishing in the order variable.** If K_s(2)=0, set
f(t)=K_s(2e^t), t>=0. The
[modified Bessel equation](https://dlmf.nist.gov/10.25.E1) gives

\[
-f''+4e^{2t}f=-s^2f,\qquad f(0)=0.
\]

For fixed complex s, the
[large-argument expansions](https://dlmf.nist.gov/10.40.E2)
and their derivative show
K_s(x)~sqrt(pi/(2x)) exp(-x). Thus f, f', and e^t f lie in L2,
the boundary term at infinity vanishes, and f is not identically
zero. Integration by parts gives

\[
0<
\int_0^\infty\left(|f'|^2+4e^{2t}|f|^2\right)\,dt
=-s^2\int_0^\infty|f|^2\,dt. \tag{V3}
\]

Consequently -s^2 is positive real and s is purely imaginary.
In particular K_s(2) is nonzero when Re s>0. Hence Phi is
nonzero in that half-plane except at s=1.

**Proved conditional criterion.** Let 0<a<1. If for every
epsilon>0, at every sufficiently large INTEGER N,

\[
|S_\phi(N)|\ll_\epsilon N^{a+\epsilon}, \tag{V4}
\]

then zeta has no zeros in Re s>a.

Indeed, absolute differentiation and a Schwartz envelope give
|S_phi'(x)|<=x^(-1) sum_n |(n/x)phi'(n/x)|<<1 for x>=1.
Integer bounds therefore give the same real-scale bound.
As x tends to zero, S_phi(x) is exponentially small.
For Re s>1, absolute integration and u=n/x give

\[
\int_0^\infty S_\phi(x)x^{-s-1}\,dx
       =\frac{\Phi(s)}{\zeta(s)}. \tag{V5}
\]

The left side continues holomorphically to Re s>a under (V4).
Multiplying by (s-1)zeta(s) and continuing the identity excludes
every zero there by (V2)--(V3). The point s=1 is zeta's pole,
not a possible zero. This argument does not require a uniform
lower bound for Phi on vertical lines, a zero-dependent profile,
simple zeta zeros, or a finite-height verification.

## 2. Complete Poisson cancellation before truncating the third factor

Let D=t d/dt. Cauchy estimates for z exp(-z-1/z), with radius
u/2 when 0<u<=1 and radius 1/2 when u>=1, give

\[
\|\phi^{(j)}\|_1\le CA^j(j!)^2.
\]

On the first range the integral of u^(-j) exp(-c/u) supplies a
second factorial; the exponential tail handles the second range.
The same conclusion holds for each fixed polynomial weight in u
and each fixed Euler derivative, with its own constants.
Optimizing integration by parts at j comparable to sqrt(|xi|)
therefore gives |hat phi(xi)|<<exp(-c sqrt(|xi|)).

With the Fourier convention exp(-2 pi i u xi), Poisson summation
and integral phi=0 yield the exact identity

\[
K(t):=\sum_{\ell\ge1}\phi(\ell t)
 =t^{-1}\sum_{m\ne0}\widehat\phi(m/t),\qquad
|D^rK(t)|\ll_r
\begin{cases}
e^{-c_r/\sqrt t},&0<t\le1,\\
e^{-t/2},&t\ge1.
\end{cases} \tag{V6}
\]

For the second estimate use the original sum; fixed polynomial
factors are absorbed by the exponential. The same argument with
weighted Fourier transforms proves the first estimate for every
fixed r.

For large N, write L=log N and set

\[
Y=\lfloor\sqrt N/L^2\rfloor,\quad
T_l=N/L^4,\quad T_u=NL^2,\quad J=\lceil2L^6\rceil.
\]

Choose fixed smooth 0<=rho,chi<=1 with rho=0 on (0,1], rho=1
on [2,infinity), chi=1 on (0,1], and chi=0 on [2,infinity).
The exact identity mu=2m-m*m*1+r*r*1, where
m=mu 1_(n<=Y) and r=mu-m, gives

\[
S_\phi(N)=
2\sum_{n\le Y}\mu(n)\phi(n/N)
-\sum_{d,e\le Y}\mu(d)\mu(e)K(de/N)
+\sum_{d,e>Y}\mu(d)\mu(e)K(de/N). \tag{V7}
\]

All rearrangements are absolute. For every fixed A>0:

- The first term is O(Y exp(-N/(2Y)))=O_A(N^(-A)).
- In the second term de/N<=L^(-4); (V6) bounds its absolute
  value by N exp(-c L^2)=O_A(N^(-A)).
- Removing Type II products de<=2T_l costs at most
  O(N log N exp(-c L^2/sqrt(2))) by summing the divisor count.
- The omitted upper-product tail is INFINITE. Its bound is
  sum_(q>=T_u) tau(q)|K(q/N)|
  <<exp(-L^2/4) sum_q tau(q)exp(-q/(4N))
  <<N log N exp(-L^2/4).
- Only after these steps truncate the ell sum. On the retained
  support t=de/N>L^(-4), so Jt>=2L^2. Every fixed Euler derivative
  of K-sum_(ell<=J)phi(ell t) is bounded by
  C_r(1+t^(-1))poly_r(Jt)exp(-Jt/4). There are
  O(N log^3 N) retained pairs, so the total tail is O_A(N^(-A)).

It follows that

\[
\boxed{S_\phi(N)=\mathcal B_\phi(N)+O_A(N^{-A}),}
\quad
\mathcal B_\phi(N)=
\sum_{d,e>Y}\mu(d)\mu(e)
\rho(de/T_l)\chi(de/T_u)
\sum_{\ell\le J}\phi(\ell de/N). \tag{V8}
\]

Every nonempty pair in this FINITE sum satisfies

\[
\frac{\sqrt N}{\log^2N}<d,e<2\sqrt N\log^4N,
\qquad \ell\le\lceil2\log^6N\rceil. \tag{V9}
\]

The original signs, shared primes, and Mobius zeros are unchanged.
No coprimality surrogate has been inserted.

The N-dependent cutoff profile

\[
F_N(t)=\rho(tL^4)\chi(t/L^2)\sum_{\ell\le J}\phi(\ell t)
\]

has uniformly bounded fixed Euler seminorms. Lower-cutoff
derivatives occur where (V6) and the ell-tail are exponentially
small in L^2; upper-cutoff derivatives occur at t comparable to
L^2. This uniformity need NOT hold for the truncated ell sum
alone near t comparable to 1/J. That range is excluded here.

Two-dimensional Stieltjes summation, retaining every edge and
corner and the cut at Y, bounds an actual dyadic pair rectangle
by O_delta((DE)^(b0+delta)) times its controlled profile seminorm.
Both variables have only O(log log N) possible dyadic sizes,
and DE<<N log^2 N. The accepted Mertens bound therefore gives

\[
\mathcal B_\phi(N)\ll_\epsilon N^{b_0+\epsilon}. \tag{V10}
\]

This recovers the baseline only. Improving this ONE fixed
kernel to N^(.87449+epsilon) at every integer scale would give
c=.12551 by (V4)--(V8). The missing amplitude saving is
b0-.87449=.000396647039964... . Neither Poisson cancellation
nor the logarithmic balance supplies that saving.

## 3. Geometry alone cannot improve the supplied upper-budget family

This is a certificate about the combination of S.5 and B0.41,
not an impossibility theorem for the actual arithmetic sums.
Use only geometries for which those estimates and their marked
row counts apply, including their supply and retention conditions.
In particular the endpoint d=h is retained, 0<h<2y, and the
physical restriction ell<=M/2 is satisfied. Losses from buffers
and meshes are nonnegative.

Let b in [.87,b0), kappa=2b-1, h=1+ell-x,
tau=x+y+ell-1, so y=h-2ell+tau. The physical exponent supplied
by S.5, after the square root in the physical bound, is

\[
b_{\rm phys}=\frac{11}{12}-\frac\ell4+\frac\tau{12}
+\max\{0,(1+3\ell-2x-2y)/8,\tau/2\}. \tag{V11}
\]

For kappa in [.74,.75], let delta be the smaller root of

\[
P(\kappa,\delta)=(324\kappa^2-3)\delta^2
+(-756\kappa^2+54\kappa+5)\delta
+300\kappa^2-40\kappa=0. \tag{V12}
\]

It lies in (.46,.48). The identity B0.48 gives
R_kappa(delta,1/2)=5/9+delta/(18kappa).
At this admissible amplitude class, the d=h numerator endpoint
from B0.46 is

\[
F=\frac{1+\delta}{2}-\frac\ell2+\frac{\ell\delta}{2}
+h\left(\frac12+\frac{\delta}{24\kappa}\right)-\frac y2
-\frac{\delta}{24\kappa}\min(h,2y-h).
\]

Since min(h,2y-h)<=2y-h, it follows exactly that

\[
F\ge f(\ell,\kappa)-A_\tau\tau,\quad
f(\ell,\kappa)=\frac{1+\ell}{2}+\frac\delta2
+\frac{\delta\ell}{2}\left(1+\frac1{3\kappa}\right),
\quad A_\tau=\frac12+\frac{\delta}{12\kappa}. \tag{V13}
\]

Equality holds when y<=h<2y. If h<=y, the extra term is
delta(y-h)/(12kappa)>=0. Thus h cannot avoid this necessary
budget. This uses a permitted upper-bound class, not a claim
that actual rows saturate its count.

Put ell_b=4((1-b)-1/12)=(5-6kappa)/3 and
A_ell=(1+delta(1+1/(3kappa)))/2. Dropping only the nonnegative
row branch in (V11), b_phys<=b forces

\[
\ell\ge
\begin{cases}
\ell_b+\tau/3,&\tau\le0,\\
\ell_b+7\tau/3,&\tau\ge0.
\end{cases} \tag{V14}
\]

The coefficients of tau after insertion in (V13) are

\[
\frac{A_\ell}{3}-A_\tau
=-\frac13+\delta\left(\frac16-\frac1{36\kappa}\right)<0,
\quad
\frac{7A_\ell}{3}-A_\tau
=\frac23+\delta\left(\frac76+\frac{11}{36\kappa}\right)>0.
\]

Both signs therefore give F-b>=f(ell_b,kappa)-b.
The best possible necessary budget occurs at tau=0.

Here is an exact rational certificate for the last inequality.
On the displayed kappa/delta rectangle, the functions
P(kappa,.46) and P(kappa,.48) increase with kappa, and

\[
P(.74,.46)=717189/390625>0,\quad
P(.75,.48)=-5577/2500<0.
\]

Elementary interval bounds give

\[
P_\delta\le-245507/1250,\quad
35297/15625\le P_\kappa\le21397/1250.
\]

Thus 0<delta'(kappa)<=21397/245507<1. Differentiating yields

\[
\frac{d}{d\kappa}\left[
f(\ell_b,\kappa)-\frac{1+\kappa}{2}\right]
=-2A_\ell-\frac12
+\frac{\delta'}2\left(1+\ell_b+\frac{\ell_b}{3\kappa}\right)
-\frac{\delta\ell_b}{6\kappa^2}
\le-\frac{25459}{16650}<0. \tag{V15}
\]

For this upper bound use delta>=23/50, kappa<=3/4,
ell_b<=14/75, kappa>=37/50, and delta'<=1.
The accepted baseline equations give f(ell_0,kappa_0)=b0
and ell_b=ell_0 at kappa_0=2b0-1. Hence F>b for every b<b0
in the stated interval. No choice of geometry in this supplied
budget family certifies an improvement, even before restoring
the omitted positive costs.

This closes the wider-geometry loophole left by [private research revision]'s
Gaussian test only when its linear comparator stays in the
domain just specified. It does not exclude new coefficient
estimates, signed cancellation, other detector families, or
geometries outside the available source bounds.

## 4. A two-profile packet cancels one Mellin value, not its full component

Take nonzero nonnegative W0,W in C_c^infinity(1,2),
rho_0=1, rho_1=rho=3/2, and W_i(x)=W(x/rho_i).
Both probes use the same arithmetic phases, exclusions,
compensator and inner profile. A fixed dilation changes only
constants and annular endpoints.
The calculation below concerns the raw neutral-ray component.
It does not compute the mixed covariance of compensator branches;
using the same compensator is not a scalar operation on this Gram.

In B0.21--B0.24 notation, put Q=q_(b*)XY, P_a=Y^2/Q,
x_a=q_a/Y, and zeta(a)=chi_a(b*)/(tau_xi xi(a)).
The physical column fields, before separating the moving
radial profile, are

\[
A_i(m)=Y^{-3/2}\sum_{a\in\sigma}
\zeta(a)W_i(x_a)x_a^{-1}g_{\chi_a}(a,-m)
W_0(q_m/(Qx_a)).
\]

Row Poisson applied to A_i conjugate(A_j) gives exactly

\[
\frac Q{Y^3}\sum_{a,b\in\sigma}
\frac{\zeta(a)\overline{\zeta(b)}W_i(x_a)\overline{W_j(x_b)}}{x_ax_b}
\sum_k F(a,b;k)
\widehat{\mathcal W}_{x_a,x_b}(\sqrt Q k/(ab)),\quad
\mathcal W_{x,y}(z)=W_0(q_z/x)\overline{W_0(q_z/y)}. \tag{V16}
\]

Use the manuscript's complex Fourier convention and measure.
Choose the neutral ray a,b=1 modulo a fixed modulus m containing
36, the fixed conductors and supplements. Enlarge the fixed
excluded set S accordingly. On the common-core-one locus
(a,b)=1 and the pure-sixth sector k=r^6, B1.17 then makes
F(a,b;r^6) the indicator of ((ab),r)=1, with its natural zeros.
The resulting signed matrix component is

\[
\frac Q{Y^3|\tau_\xi|^2}
\sum_{\substack{a,b\equiv1\;(m)\\(a,b)=1}}
\frac{W_i(x_a)\overline{W_j(x_b)}}{x_ax_b}
\sum_{\substack{r\ {\rm primary}\\(r,S)=1}}
\mathbf1_{((ab),r)=1}
\widehat{\mathcal W}_{x_a,x_b}(\sqrt Q r^6/(ab)). \tag{V17}
\]

Here r is nonzero. Keep the FULL projector
1_(a,b)=1=sum_(d|a,b)mu(d). A nonzero Poisson sector is not
automatically a positive sub-Gram of the total physical energy.

For completeness, the restricted component has a controlled
continuum limit. Its column zero-mode density is

\[
\zeta_{\mathbb K}^{S}(2)^{-1}\beta(r),\qquad
\beta(r)=\prod_{\mathfrak p\mid r}\frac{Q_{\mathfrak p}-1}
 {Q_{\mathfrak p}+1}.
\]

At p|r the ratio of the two-unit density (1-Q_p^(-1))^2 to
the ordinary coprime-pair density 1-Q_p^(-2) gives this factor.
Writing beta=1*h with h(p)=-2/(Q_p+1) and h(p^j)=0 for j>=2,
fixed-S lattice counting gives, for a fixed smooth decaying profile,

\[
\sum_r\beta(r)\psi(q_r/T)
=\operatorname{Res}_{s=1}\zeta_{\mathbb K}^S(s)
 H_\beta(1)T\int\psi
+O_\psi(T^{1/2}),\quad
H_\beta(1)=\prod_{\mathfrak p\notin S}
 \left(1-\frac2{Q_{\mathfrak p}(Q_{\mathfrak p}+1)}\right)>0.
\]

The error follows since sum_d |h(d)|/sqrt(q_d) converges.
Centered column coefficients after each gcd projector are
periodic; B0.23 can be applied with the coarse period r^6.
Taking column zero modes BEFORE the short-root average, and
then the radial Fourier--Riesz identity, gives the leading matrix

\[
\frac QY P_a^{1/6}C_{\rm exc}\,\mathcal E,\quad
\mathcal E_{ij}=\int_0^\infty
 E_i(R)\overline{E_j(R)}R^{-1/6}\,dR,\quad
E_i(R)=\int W_i(x)x^{-5/6}W_0(R/x)\,dx. \tag{V18}
\]

Here C_exc is a fixed positive scalar. With the manuscript's
normalizations it is
rho_m^2 Res_(s=1)zeta_K^S(s) H_beta(1) C_R /
(6 |tau_xi|^2 zeta_K^S(2)), where
rho_m=2pi/(sqrt(3)q_m) and
C_R=(2pi/sqrt(3))^(2/3) Gamma(1/6)/Gamma(5/6).
The sixth-power substitution supplies the factor 1/6.
For the fixed two profiles the matrix error is

\[
O\left(\frac QY Z^\epsilon
\left[P_a^{1/12}+\frac{P_a^2}{Y}
                     +\frac{P_a^{1/6}}Y\right]\right). \tag{V19}
\]

The terms are respectively the root-lattice error, centered
column cost, and coprimality-density tail. This asymptotic is
useful, for example, for power scales P_a tending to infinity
with P_a^(11/6)=o(Y), taking epsilon smaller than the fixed
power gaps. It does not assert equidistribution of short roots
for each moving pair of columns separately.

The original row puncture |xi(m)|^2, the indicator of (m,b*)=1,
is also retained.
Expand it over d|rad(b*), and enlarge the neutral modulus so
chi_a(d)=1 for these finitely many d. The d-branch replaces
Q by Q/q_d and P_a by P_a q_d. Thus its leading matrix is
multiplied by the positive fixed product
product_(p|b*)(1-Q_p^(-5/6)); the same finite expansion preserves
the error bound. This is not removal of a character zero.

The profile part now has an exact spectral test. For
hat W(s)=int W(x)x^(s-1)dx,

\[
E_1(R)=\rho^{1/6}E_0(R/\rho),\quad
\widehat E_i(s)=\widehat W_0(s)\widehat W_i(s+1/6),\quad
p_i=C_R\widehat W_0(5/6)\widehat W_i(1)
    =C_R\int E_i(R)R^{-1/6}\,dR. \tag{V20}
\]

The other principal factors in B0.35 are common to the probes;
thus p=p0(1,rho). Mellin Plancherel gives

\[
\mathcal E_{ij}=\frac1{2\pi}\int_{\mathbb R}
\Lambda(t)\rho_i^{7/12+it}\rho_j^{7/12-it}\,dt,\quad
\Lambda(t)=|\widehat W_0(5/12+it)\widehat W(7/12+it)|^2. \tag{V21}
\]

Lambda is continuous and positive near zero. The phase
exp(it log rho) is not constant on that interval, so strict
triangle inequality shows
det(E)=rho^(7/6)[(int Lambda/(2pi))^2
-|int Lambda exp(it log rho)/(2pi)|^2]>0.
The leading component has rank two.

The vector c=(-rho^(7/12),1) cancels the evaluation at t=0
and retains p(c)=p0(rho-rho^(7/12))>0. But its exceptional
multiplier rho^(7/12)(exp(it log rho)-1) vanishes only on a
discrete set. It leaves positive full Gram cost. More generally,
Cauchy on the common support 1<R<4rho gives

\[
|p(c)|^2\le C_R^2\left(\int_1^{4\rho}R^{-1/6}\,dR\right)
c^*\mathcal E c. \tag{V22}
\]

This obstructs nulling the specified component separately in
the componentwise budget. It does NOT give a lower bound for
the total physical energy or a universal vector-probe
impossibility theorem. Cancellation against other ray or
common-core sectors requires their actual mixed covariance.

## 5. Joint theta sampling still pays the wrong scale

For the infinity/b=1 component, retain the exact annular theta
polynomials G_P from [private research revision], including the raw angular factor,
squarefree projection and common profiles. For a good squarefree
row R with primitive quadratic character delta_R, put

\[
r_R(a)=\frac{\delta_R(\lambda)^{-1}}{q_R}
\sum_{x\bmod R}\delta_R(x)e_{\mathbb K}(ax/R),\qquad
X_R=\sum_P\frac{a_P}{\sqrt{q_P}}\mathbf1_{(R,P)=1}
\sum_{a\bmod R}r_R(a)G_P(-9a/R). \tag{V23}
\]

This is the original quadratic twist, with the existing Fourier
normalization; no new source coefficient has been substituted.
Finite Fourier inversion gives
r_R(a) conjugate(r_R(b))=delta_R(a)delta_R(b)/q_R, including
zeros on nonunits. Its rank-one block has norm phi(R)/q_R<=1.

Count each denominator once by its primary ideal representative.
Primitive fractions a/R with q_R comparable to K are distinct
on the complex lattice torus and separated by a constant times
K^(-1). Indeed a nonzero numerator after cross-multiplication
has norm at least one. Multiplication by 9 preserves distinctness
because every denominator avoids its fixed prime factors.

For one fixed polynomial G of frequency radius O(sqrt(N)),
a smooth reproducing kernel with decay
N(1+sqrt(N)|z|)^(-A) and packing of these points give

\[
\sum_{R,\;a\ {\rm unit}}|G(-9a/R)|^2
\ll (N+K^2)\sum_u|c_u|^2. \tag{V24}
\]

The two-dimensional sampling cost is K^2, not K. Row Cauchy,
the exact finite mask expansion, and the existing mark estimate
therefore give only (N+K^2){N+L+(NL)^(2/3)}, which is worse
than the existing (N+K){N+L+(NL)^(2/3)} certificate.
The preprojected H is the signed inclusion--exclusion
H_full-D_u-D_(Pu)+D_intersection; its terms cannot be removed
by positivity. This organization supplies no new saving.

## 6. The balanced kernel retains the zero it would need to exclude

This is a diagnostic for the new fixed profile, with an actual
Mellin identity as well as a continuous model. It is not an
explicit formula for Mobius.

The entire Mellin transform of K satisfies

\[
\mathcal J(s)=\int_0^\infty K(t)t^{s-1}\,dt
            =\zeta(s)\Phi(s). \tag{V25}
\]

The endpoint bounds (V6) prove entireness; absolute interchange
first proves the equality for Re s>1, then continuation proves
it everywhere. The zero of Phi at 1 cancels zeta's pole.

Put q=Y^2/N and J_q(s)=int_q^infinity K(t)t^(s-1)dt.
For fixed continuous coefficient modes A d^(rho-1) and
B e^(tau-1), exact change of variables p=de gives, when rho!=tau,

\[
I_{\rho,\tau}:=AB\int_Y^\infty\int_Y^\infty
d^{\rho-1}e^{\tau-1}K(de/N)\,dd\,de
=\frac{AB}{\rho-\tau}
\left[Y^{\tau-\rho}N^\rho J_q(\rho)
-Y^{\rho-\tau}N^\tau J_q(\tau)\right]. \tag{V26}
\]

The equal-label limit, with B=A, is
A^2 N^rho[log(N/Y^2)J_q(rho)+J_q'(rho)].
For Y=floor(sqrt(N)/log^2 N), replacing J_q and a fixed
number of its derivatives by J costs O_M(N^(-M)), including
the displayed polynomial factors. Constants depend on the
fixed labels and derivative orders.

Distinct zeta-zero labels cancel in this model since both
J-values vanish. Equal simple labels instead leave
A^2 N^rho zeta'(rho)Phi(rho). For A=1/zeta'(rho), this is
N^rho Phi(rho)/zeta'(rho), precisely the individual pole
contribution. Here equal means rho=tau, not conjugate pairing.

Multiple zeros do not avoid the resonance. Differentiating
(V26) produces logarithmic density modes. At distinct labels
of orders m,n, derivatives j<m, k<n still cancel. At an
equal label of order m, the first nonzero derivatives have
j+k=m-1 and coefficient
AB N^rho j!k! J^(m)(rho)/m!. This follows by expanding the
leading divided difference (u^m-v^m)/(u-v). Higher derivatives
have additional terms. No simplicity assumption is needed
for this model obstruction.

For the ACTUAL Mobius coefficients and each fixed finite Y,
M_Y(s)=sum_(n<=Y)mu(n)n^(-s), Mellin inversion on c>1 gives

\[
\sum_{d,e>Y}\mu(d)\mu(e)K(de/N)
=\frac1{2\pi i}\int_{(c)}
\Phi(s)N^s
\left[\frac1{\zeta(s)}-2M_Y(s)+\zeta(s)M_Y(s)^2\right]\,ds.
\tag{V27}
\]

The bracket follows exactly from J(s)(1/zeta-M_Y)^2.
The last two terms are analytic at every zeta zero. Thus the
full polar part of this integrand equals that of Phi(s)N^s/zeta(s).
No contour shift across those poles, uniformly convergent
zero expansion, or summation of fixed-mode errors is asserted.
The extra cancellation found in (V26) does not bound the
remaining diagonal resonances or improve (V10).

## Evidence and next estimates

The exact-rational certificate in
[check_cycle12.py](experiments/check_cycle12.py) checks the
interval and geometry algebra. These finite checks do not
prove (V4), a theta restriction estimate, or a new zero-free
constant. The analytic proofs and their independent reviews
are recorded above; the inherited manuscripts retain their
original bytes.

The immediate distinct targets remain: a power saving for
the actual fixed balanced sum (V8); a coefficient-specific
joint restriction estimate for the short projected divisors
in H; or central continuation/ordinary mean for the complete
sixth-order row series. Each requires new cancellation beyond
the tests in this record. Cancelling isolated Mellin values,
reoptimizing the supplied geometry, and using generic point
sampling have now been tested within their precise scopes.
