## G69. The global Euler norm fails; its mass escapes the physical scale

For P>=5 let f_P=f3 restricted to P-smooth integers and V_P its complete
Gaussian. Its exact finite Euler series, including all powers, is

    E_P(s)=(1-3^-s)^-1 product_(p<=P,p!=3)(1-2p^-s)/(1-p^-s).

For sigma>0 weighted Gaussian Fubini and Plancherel give

    ||e^(-sigma u)V_P||_2^2
      =e^(tau sigma^2)/(2pi) integral_R e^(-tau t^2)|E_P(sigma+it)|^2dt.

Choose P_X=ceil(2X exp(C sqrt(log X))). Missing coefficients lie entirely
in the Gaussian tail, so on the physical shell
|F-V_(P_X)|<=X^(1-C^2/(2tau)+o(1)). This exact choice also ensures
P_X=X^(1+o(1)); the author's lower bound on P_X alone did not ensure it.
A global norm O(P^kappa) would return exponent sigma+kappa, but is false
for every fixed1/2<sigma<1 and every finite kappa.

Indeed at t=a/log P, uniformly for a in[5pi/6,7pi/6], ordinary PNT yields

    sum_(p<=P)p^(-sigma-ia/log P)
      =P^(1-sigma)/log P [e^(-ia)/(1-sigma)+o(1)].

The Euler logarithm is the negative real part of this sum plus O_sigma(1).
Its small-prime factors are bounded and nonzero. Integration over this
height interval proves

    ||e^(-sigma u)V_P||_2 >= C_(sigma,tau)(log P)^(-1/2)
                exp(P^(1-sigma)/(2(1-sigma)log P)).

Only pi(x)~x/log x is imported, as supplied by
[Johnston-Yang, v2, Corollary1.3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2204.01980), PDF page2.
The source's sharper estimates and any stronger zero-free conclusion are
unnecessary. No effective onset is asserted; contrary finite diagnostics
remain in the author evidence.

Critic audit30 proves the decisive scope refinement. Uniformly in P,
|V_P(u)|<=C_tau e^u for u>=0 and <=C_tau exp(-u^2/(2tau)) for u<=0.
Hence for every fixed T>0,

    ||1_(u<=T log P)e^(-sigma u)V_P||_2=O(P^(T(1-sigma))),
    ||1_(u>T log P)e^(-sigma u)V_P||_2/||e^(-sigma u)V_P||_2 ->1.

The excess mass escapes every polynomial physical scale. It supplies no
lower bound for the original shell. The global certificate must be retired,
while the source-specific restricted estimate remains eligible.

There is an exact causal identity for that output. On weighted L2, set
A_P=product_(p<=P)(I-D_p), B_P=product_(p<=P,p!=3)(I-2D_p), b=B_P g_tau.
Then V_P=A_P^-1 b. Split at U=log X and V=log(2X) into past L, shell I,
and future R. Every delay is causal; every nonidentity delay is at leastlog2.
Thus A_II=I and the future-input blocks vanish, giving

    (V_P)_I=b_I-A_IL A_LL^-1 b_L.

The Schur feedback is exactly zero, but the past injection is not. The
generic norm of A_LL^-1 is product_p(1-p^-sigma)^-1, again superpolynomial
for sigma<1. Estimate the complete signed sum, not the two pieces separately.
Future excess mass does not feed back into this causal output. This exact
source identity and localization refine the old Schur/finite-incidence
objections without reversing their valid quadratic inequalities.
title: G69. The global Euler norm fails; its mass escapes the physical scale

## 4. A single fixed sparse mask with an explicit error

The uniform audit proves a probabilistic source approximation. Fix
0<kappa<1 and independent Bernoulli I_a with p_a=(Na)^(-kappa), once for all
ideals. Set Utilde(x)=sum_a I_a (Na)^kappa mu_K(a)eta(a)g_tau(log(Na/x)).
Every realization defines a complete field with polynomially bounded
coefficients. No new Euler product is assigned to this nonmultiplicative mask.
Exact variance and ideal counting give

    E ||Utilde-U||_[X,2X]^2 << X^(1+kappa).           ([restricted research revision]-P7)

Markov plus Borel--Cantelli on dyads yields, almost surely, error exponent
(1+kappa)/2+epsilon for every positive epsilon. A separate exponential
count bound gives retained support O(X^(1-kappa)) on every large norm dyad.
A countable intersection supplies one fixed mask for all prescribed fixed
characters, finite masks and widths, with no conductor-uniform constants.
The error Mellin transform is holomorphic to the right of(1+kappa)/2,
so it cannot cancel the original reciprocal poles there.

At kappa=.749 the support exponent is.251 and the limiting error exponent
is.8745. Choosing actual error exponent.8747 leaves room below target.8748.
The full signed sparse-field target would give c=.1252, but is equivalent
to the original target and remains open. Retained coefficients near X are
amplified by X^.749. The exact identity E||Utilde||^2=||U||^2+variance shows
why sparsity or unbiasedness alone yields no gain. This is a probability-one
existence theorem, not an explicit certified good mask, operational random
draw, finite computational proof or faster algorithm.

All [30 frozen cards](wild42/seeds.md), six first tests, both developments and
independent audits24/29 are preserved. Twenty-two cards remain untested.
Author pools were serialized before every literal all-group draw. The critic
knew the six selections before freezing its audits but read no outcomes;
that chronology is retained without reroll. Source identities, probabilistic
lemmas and exact finite checks are distinct from the still-open arithmetic
moment and from the full new-endpoint kernel evidence.

### 4.1 Signed I/II return through the interval tree

Let F_I and F_II denote the two exact normalized linear terms of
[private research revision] B1--2, with all their original n,R,P,g factors. Restriction to
any tree interval J is multiplication by 1_(q_n in J), hence commutes
with the pointwise identity:

    (F_I+F_II)_J = F_(all-prime),J.                  (SF15)

The strict far covariance is consequently the exact sum of its four
ordered (I,I),(I,II),(II,I),(II,II) tree expressions. On every eligible
semiprime above both cutoffs the interval coefficient is still 1,-1
on the two linear pieces, giving 1,-1,-1,1 in the ordered covariance
whenever the original pair is in that rectangle. Thus the two ordered
mixed terms remain necessary. They cancel BEFORE the prime projection,
not as a post hoc cancellation between positive bounds.

On an original prime n, the coefficient in F_I is one and that in
F_II is zero. It stays in the unit factor cell D=1,E~N at every tree
level. In this cell

    T(1,N;L)=min{S(N,L),S(1,NL)} comparable to N,

so SF11 gives K G^2 N^2, of target-relative size G N, with exponent
.839507578307735986.... This is weaker than the existing joint
quadratic/cubic bound and is not promoted. Combining all signed
allocations FIRST restores the original prime source at original
length N; applying the established joint sieve to it restores
G(K+NG)S(N,L), still with deficit .004. No shortened unit source is
created by SF15.

This is the decisive obstruction to this attempted route. The exact
product-interval adapter fixes an analytic masking loss, but the
first positive fixed-row estimate still discards the covariance that
the unit prime source needs. The signed small-gcd complement remains
the original-prime form minus the already paid common-core composite
counterterm. No new equality identifies that counterterm with primes.

The next useful target is therefore an estimate on SF15's JOINT
original-row interval vectors before the fixed-R cubic Cauchy step,
or a signed Type-I/Type-II estimate in that same joint norm. A theorem
with the square-function scope of SF2 would now return the full sharp
far mask by SF8 at logarithmic cost. Proving such a row estimate is
still the arithmetic work; SF2/SF11 do not assume it.

non-power-of-two original supports. All exact integer assertions

two-cutoff prime identity, the unit obstruction and the failed leading

## 6. The other three selected tests

**11, full critical Gram.** For a Hermitian 2x2 matrix,
M<=lambda I iff both diagonal gaps are nonnegative and their product
dominates the squared cross entry. This includes equality cases.
The accepted actual critical rough profile is uniformly positive and
of size X/log^2 X at fixed kappa^2>=2e^(3tau). In L2([X,2X],dx/x),
its squared norm is therefore comparable to X^2/log^4 X. The largest
eigenvalue of the actual two-vector Gram is at least that diagonal.
A full-matrix O(X^(2gamma)) bound, gamma<1, is impossible. The scalar
direction(1,1) can still cancel. The four signed Gram pieces cannot
be individually discarded. [private research revision] now separately accepts the stronger
rough low-gcd/mixed opposition theorem; the author's older unintegrated
description remains provenance, not the current status. This test uses
the earlier unmasked profile and does not need hereditary mask transfer.

**29, phase occupancy.** Equal masses at +/-pi/3 satisfy the proposed
fixed arc cap and still sum to half their total mass; scaling preserves
the exponent. The exact stronger return |integral e^(i theta)dmu|<=2Delta
is valid for the supremum discrepancy over all connected half-open arcs.
After subtracting uniform measure, the cumulative function has oscillation
at most Delta. Center its range, rotate the desired Fourier coefficient
to its real part and integrate against cos: integral|sin|=4 gives2Delta.
The zero total mass removes endpoint terms; cuts can avoid atoms.
An actual power-small weighted discrepancy remains open. A constant
occupancy hypothesis is not secretly a power estimate.

**28, collision differential.** Direct composition of the stated bar maps
gives d1d2[a|b]=epsilon(a)epsilon(b)-epsilon(ab), and d2d3[a|b|c]
is that same defect times[c]. For a=b=p, it is1 for mu and2 for f3
when p!=3. These are the actual squareful zero and repeated-prime sign,
not abstract incidence signs. Multiplicativity on coprime pairs does not
remove the original collision cells. Prime by prime,
f3(ab)=f3(a)f3(b)f3(gcd(a,b)), so the displayed cocycle identity follows.
It is a coboundary because all f3 values are +/-1. Twisting the algebra
can restore multiplicativity, but cannot retain an unchanged right
module or old differential without checking compatibility. The scoped
failure is sound; no general homological impossibility is proved.

## 4. The global reflection does not shorten the columns

Work in the ENTIRE fixed-level induced space, with compact-picture
bases f_j^+ and f_l^- and actual fixed-place intertwining matrix
M_S(w)f_j^+=sum_l m_lj(w)f_l^-. The four original norm selectors
need not form an invariant subspace. Define reflected arithmetic
coefficients by E^-_(r,l)(a_y;z)=J W^-(r,y,z) A^-_l(r,z).
This retains every fixed-place sector and row valuation; it does not
identify A^- with one of the four original Psi functions.

For r=h^4, kappa=2pi/sqrt(3), B=B_nu and xi=B^6, the established
Whittaker comparison and the
[KP global intertwiner and functional equation, II.1.2--II.1.3](https://pmihes.centre-mersenne.org/item/10.1007/BF02698770.pdf)
give the meromorphic operator identity

\[
\Psi_j^+(h,w)=
\kappa\bar\alpha(r)(\kappa|r|)^{1-2w}
\frac{\Gamma(w)}{\Gamma(2-w)}
\frac{L^S(6w-3,\xi)}{L^S(6w-2,\xi)}
\sum_l m_{lj}(w)\mathcal A^-_l(r,1-w). \tag{R5}
\]

The two archimedean minus signs and J cancel. Reflection inverts
the inducing ratio B and preserves the center by the common B(det)
twist, trivial on SL2. The genuine epsilon remains the calibrated
one; it is not silently conjugated.

Multiplying by Lambda(6w-2,xi)/Gamma(w+1) gives the completed
coefficient. Its gamma factor is

\[
\frac{\Gamma_{\mathbb C}(6w+1)}{\Gamma(w+1)}
=C A^w\prod_{j=1}^{5}\Gamma(w+j/6).
\]

Thus the FORMAL conductor and balanced length are
q_h^4 T^10 and q_h^2 T^5, respectively. In particular
|h^4|^(1-2w)=q_h^(2-4w). A usable arithmetic approximate functional
equation still needs the normalized bad-place matrix, cancellation
or clearing of its apparent poles, arithmetic reflected coefficients
and coefficient-energy bounds, and row-map collision bounds for
squarefree extraction. A pointwise extraction l1 bound alone does
not transfer an all-row mean.

Even granting those missing inputs ideally, a central column dyad
of length M has squared coefficient mass O(M^(-2epsilon)).
The all-element sieve costs
[X+X^(1/3)M+(XM)^(2/3)] M^(-2epsilon), hence
X^(7/3-4epsilon) at M=X^2. Ideal cube-free extraction would reduce
this only to X^(2-4epsilon).

Unbalancing M=X^a, N=X^(4-a) gives the two costs
F(X,M)M^(-2epsilon) and X^(-8epsilon)F(X,N)N^(2epsilon).
For 0<epsilon<1/6, the direct long-column term when a>=2, or
the dual one when a<=2, has at least the balanced certificate's
exponent. This is a limitation of THESE upper-bound estimates,
not a lower bound on the actual mean. It supplies neither eta=3/32
nor a new zero-free constant.

statement:
# [private research revision] independent review: actual f3 hard correlation

Disposition: **PASS, with the scope qualifications stated below.** The frozen
author packet proves its complete coprime rough-block obstruction A3--A5 and
its separate complete low-gcd hard-mask obstruction A29a--b. Its one-full-factor
estimate A18 has the claimed uniformity, including large divisors. I find no
required mathematical repair. Neither result proves a full-field energy lower
bound, a new cancellation estimate, or a new c.

## Current worklog and retained authority



The author's analytic input is deliberately historical: c2=.125128, with any
fixed buffered Mertens exponent .874872<beta<1. Its explicit budgets use
beta=.874873. The accepted c4=.125135 and commit
`38c33e67d13ac905a403046fc68a1dd6c7c6b3cc` are later controller state, not new
premises inserted into this frozen proof. In particular the historical target
c=.125129 is not a proposed improvement over the current incumbent.

## 1. Packet, source bindings, and interpretation of PASS

The complete frozen author files were verified against the supplied lengths
and SHA256 values:

| File under `[restricted provenance path] research revision]-drafts/f3-correlation/` | Bytes | SHA256 |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| report.md | 40584 | 0c78b87163e74c69011b371f201d5fdc2ed959416b349dc71855e1d2b75ce2ab |
| check_source.py | 6388 | 6f96a3226c9b84651f28bcb04b68e794bd545ab35425c8d1a10df5aac35bb75f |
| evidence.json | 4172 | c991464558a40788f5c332e2d1ce8f11be5d525e9ce8810b06d43d45deb3fe4f |

The author report was read in full. One combined display truncated a middle
slice; that exact slice was subsequently read without truncation. The helper
and JSON were also read in full. I did not run the author helper because it
writes the frozen author's evidence file.

All nine source bindings were checked. Seven retain exactly the author's
bytes and hash: [private research revision] threshold integration, [private research revision] independent review,
[private research revision] signed report, [private research revision] Gaussian-signed report, cycles01--32 attempt
archive, [private research revision] merged portfolio, and round38-review. The live
`[restricted mathematical source]` and `[restricted mathematical source]` have advanced to
the independently accepted c4 state. The retained evidence records both
author and observed hashes/lengths, marking those two comparisons false.
This is disclosed source drift, not a claim that nine historical snapshots
were recovered. The unchanged supporting source proofs and the controller's
explicitly retained c2 baseline supply the relevant earlier premises.

Applicable readback covered current-proof G31--G40 and the current index;
the [private research revision] critical-threshold and source-transfer arguments; [private research revision]
S1--S14 and S24--S29; the archived F01.R/M/N1/X and N28.D/C/O arguments;
the [private research revision] actual-source and dilation calibration; and the full applicable
R38.5 positive-law argument. These sources do not supply hereditary signed
submask bounds or an independence theorem for the actual remaining phase.

PASS means the stated fixed-tau, fixed-kappa asymptotic theorem and its
interfaces follow from the named already accepted analytic inputs. The
finite check is independent evidence for algebra and arithmetic only. The
asymptotic verdict comes from the arguments in the following sections.

## 2. Exact source and the complete critical two-prime estimate

Write

    g(u)=(2 pi tau)^(-1/2) exp(-u^2/(2 tau)),  tau>0 fixed,
    f(n)=mu(rad(n/3^v3(n))),
    K_X(m,n)=integral_X^(2X) g(log(m/x))g(log(n/x)) dx/x.

Throughout, ||W||^2 means integral_X^(2X)|W(x)|^2 dx/x; every
displayed shell norm uses this same logarithmic Gaussian normalization.

All powers of a prime other than 3 have local sign -1; all powers of 3
have sign +1. Fix kappa with kappa^2>=2 exp(3 tau), put z=kappa sqrt(X),
L=log X, and freeze this original threshold on the whole closed shell.
Let A_R(n)=1_(omega_z(n)>=2), A_T=1-A_R and let R,T,F be the Gaussian
fields with coefficients f A_R,f A_T,f. Thus F=T+R exactly. There is no
moving-tau or moving-kappa uniformity claim.

For bounded real coefficient sequences u,v define

    C_1(u,v)=sum_((m,n)=1) u(m)v(n)K_X(m,n).

The coprime mask is not positive semidefinite. Every use of positivity below
is an explicitly positive majorant, not a masked Cauchy--Schwarz step.
The only coprime diagonal is m=n=1. The rough coefficient vanishes there,
so RR,TR,RT and FR have no coprime diagonal.

Set

    V(x)=sum_(z<p<q) g(log(pq/x)),
    U(x)=sum_(r>=2) sum_(z<p<q) g(log(rpq/x)),
    J(v)=integral_v^infinity exp(u)(u-v)g(u)du.

I independently obtain the bounded-core-coefficient version of A6:

    S_c(x):=sum_(r>=1)c(r)sum_(z<p<q)g(log(rpq/x))
       = (2x/L^2) sum_(r>=1)c(r)/r J(log(rz^2/x)) + O(X/L^3),       (R1)

uniformly in x in [X,2X] and all |c(r)|<=1. Such coefficients may be
chosen anew with X and need not be multiplicative. This is a linear PNT
approximation with an absolute error, not a theorem giving cancellation
for an arbitrary arithmetic mask.

Here are the complete tail and density payments used to obtain R1.

First, the all-scale lattice estimate is

    sum_(n>=1) g(log(n/y)) <= C_tau y,                       all y>0. (R2)

For y>=1, compare on multiplicative intervals or use the integrable
Gaussian majorant and its variation. For 0<y<1, g(log(n/y))<=C(y/n)^2,
so the sum is O(y^2), which is O(y). More generally, splitting the
Gaussian into two factors gives, for fixed epsilon>=0,

    sum_(|log(n/y)|>=W) n^epsilon g(log(n/y))
       <= C_(tau,epsilon) y^(1+epsilon) exp(-W^2/(4 tau)). (R3)

The remaining Gaussian has variance 2 tau, and its weighted all-scale
lattice bound follows in the same way. This includes y<1; no small-scale
exception is hidden in a later divisor sum.

In the completed two-prime sum, multiplicity at a product n is at most
d_3(n). The parts r>X^.01 or max(p,q)>X^.52 force
log(rpq/x)>=.01 L-O(1). Applying R3 with d_3(n)<<_epsilon n^epsilon
therefore gives O_A(X^-A) for every fixed A. This pays all prime powers,
all core valuations and all overcounted representations in these tails.

On r<=X^.01 and z<p,q<=X^.52, replace p<q by half the ordered pair,
subtracting the actual p=q completion diagonal. Its full positive cost is

    sum_(p>z)sum_(r>=1)g(log(rp^2/x))
       <= C x sum_(p>z)p^-2 <= C sqrt(X).                       (R4)

This is a diagonal of the two-prime representation, not the true m=n
diagonal of an energy scalar.

Use fixed-order PNT pi(t)-li(t)=O_N(t/log^N t), with N=10 fixed before
X varies. If q,r are fixed, the two Stieltjes endpoint terms at z and
X^.52, and the derivative term, each have bound Cx/(rq L^N):

    sup_p p g(log(rpq/x)) <= C x/(rq),
    integral p |d[g(log(rpq/x))]| <=
                       (x/(rq)) integral exp(u)|g'(u)|du.

The lower endpoint is correctly excluded even if z itself is prime.
Summing the first error over r,q costs at most two harmonic factors.
Apply the second Stieltjes replacement inside the positive first-prime
integral, with both of its endpoints retained. Its derivative estimate
has the same form, and the sum/integral of reciprocals again costs at
most O(L^2). Total PNT error is O(X/L^8). There is no unaccounted
product of two PNT errors.

The extension of the continuous rectangle to all r,p,q is absolute.
For a=z^2/x in the compact interval [kappa^2/2,kappa^2], its unweighted
positive integral can be written

    x integral_(log a)^infinity exp(u)g(u) W_a(u)du,
    W_a(u)=sum_(r<=exp(u)/a) (u-log(ar))/r
           <<_(kappa) (1+u_+)^2.

Every omitted part has u>=.01 L-O(1), giving a superpower tail after
the entire core sum. The prime-density denominators are bounded on
p,q>=z and do not spoil this estimate.

For the leading density put p=sqrt(X)v, q=sqrt(X)w. Since kappa>=1,
v,w>=kappa, and the global inequality

    |1/[(L/2+log v)(L/2+log w)] - 4/L^2|
       <= 8(log v+log w)/L^3                                   (R5)

holds, rather than only a compact Taylor expansion. The integral of
(1+log v+log w)g(log(rvw/s)), s=x/X in [1,2], summed over all r,
is uniformly finite. Indeed h=log(vw/kappa^2)>=0 turns it into an
integral bounded by a constant times

    kappa^2 integral_0^infinity exp(h)(1+2log kappa+h)h
                     g(h+log(rkappa^2/s))dh,

which is O_B(r^-B) for any fixed B. Thus R5 costs O(X/L^3) globally.
The leading double integral is (s/r)J(log(rkappa^2/s)). Its prefactor
is (1/2)X(4/L^2), giving exactly 2x/(rL^2), with the positive sign
in R1. This verifies the factor 2, both PNT replacements, and the
completed-core extension independently.

The choice of kappa gives the uniform small-core-complement bound.
Completing the square gives

    J(v)=exp(tau/2) integral_0^infinity h g(h+v-tau)dh.

For v>=3 tau and r>=1,

    J(v+log r) <= r^-2 J(v),

because the Gaussian quotient is at most
exp(-(v-tau)log r/tau-(log r)^2/(2 tau)). Now
z^2/x>=kappa^2/2>=exp(3 tau), and

    sum_(r>=2)r^-3 <= 1/8 + integral_2^infinity t^-3 dt = 1/4.

Consequently, if V_0=(2x/L^2)J(log(z^2/x)), R1 yields

    V=V_0+O(X/L^3),   U<=V_0/4+O(X/L^3),
    V asymp X/L^2,    0<=U<=V/3                             (R6)

eventually, uniformly on the shell. The gap from 1/4 to 1/3 absorbs
the absolute errors. All constants can depend on the fixed tau,kappa;
J is strictly positive on their compact range. No Mertens estimate
has entered R1--R6.

## 3. Complete coprime RR, long shifts, and the four distinct primes

Below z^3, an integer with at least two distinct primes exceeding z
has exactly two, both at valuation one. Thus it has the unique form
n=rpq, z<p<q, r<z, and f(n)=f(r). A third rough prime or a repeated
rough prime together with the other one would force n>z^3. Above
z^3 the difference between the literal and completed fields is
bounded with d_3(n) and R3 by O_A(X^-A). Hence

    R=V+S_core+O_A(X^-A),    |S_core|<=U.                    (R7)

Also, at every n, the absolute literal rough coefficient is bounded
by the number of representations n=rpq with p<q>z. Therefore its
positive field is bounded exactly by V+U, with no tail exception.

The original integer window is

    W_X=log 2+sqrt(24 tau L),
    I_X=[X exp(-W_X),X exp(W_X)].

If x is in the shell and n is outside this window, then
|log(n/x)|>=sqrt(24 tau L). R2--R3 show that the entire positive
original-pair mass with either integer outside I_X is O(X^-4).
This calculation uses bounded original coefficients: one factor has
mass O(X exp(-6L)), the other O(X), and the shell has bounded
logarithmic measure. The divisor-weighted completed-source tails
have already been paid separately. Eventually max I_X<z^3, and all
cores in the central source satisfy r<=exp(W_X)/kappa^2<z.

To prove the coprime lower bound one must subtract the whole signed
noncoprime contribution, not discard an unfavorable part of it. On
the central window split noncoprime rough pairs as follows.

If a rough prime p>z divides both integers, the total absolute mass
is at most

    sum_(p>z) integral_X^(2X)
                   [sum_(a>=1)g(log(pa/x))]^2 dx/x
       <= C X^2 sum_(p>z)p^-2 << X^(3/2).                    (R8)

This upper bound includes coincident primes, repeated valuations and
diagonal pairs; any overcount is positive and hence harmless.

If there is no common rough prime, any common divisor greater than
one is in the two cores. Both cores then exceed one. Their entire
absolute pair contribution is at most ||U||^2. Enlarging to all
completed positive cores is allowed for this upper bound. Together
with the original window tail,

    |sum_((m,n)>1)f(m)A_R(m)f(n)A_R(n)K_X(m,n)|
       <= ||U||^2 + C X^(3/2)+O(X^-4).                      (R9)

By R6--R7 the lower pointwise bound V-U-O_A(X^-A) is eventually
positive, so its square may be used in the lower bound for ||R||^2.
Subtracting R9 then cancels the U^2 term and gives

    C_1(R,R) >= integral [V^2-2VU] dx/x - C X^(3/2)
               >= (1/3)||V||^2-C X^(3/2),
    |C_1(R,R)| <= ||V+U||^2 <= (16/9)||V||^2,
    ||V||^2 asymp_(tau,kappa) X^2/L^4.                       (R10)

This proves A3 for the complete signed coprime block. In particular,
the favorable r=1 family was only an ingredient of a bound that also
paid for every other core. The positive-subset fallacy does not occur.

For every integer h>=1 and every Y>0, R2 gives

    sum_(a>=1)K_Y(a,a+h) <= C_tau Y.                        (R11)

Use sup g on one factor and R2 on the other, then integrate over the
shell. This estimate is valid also for Y<1. Both integer orders in
|m-n|<=H therefore have total positive cost O(XH). For RR,FR,TR,RT
there is no coprime diagonal. If C_1^H also restricts m,n to I_X,
m!=n, and |m-n|>H, then

    C_1^H(R,R)=C_1(R,R)+O(XH+X^-4).                         (R12)

At H=X/L^6 the removed mass is o(X^2/L^4), proving A4. Every
retained integer has two rough primes of valuation one, and
gcd(m,n)=1 forces all four rough primes in the pair to be distinct.
All admissible cores and all long shifts are retained. A3 alone would
not control cancellation among other gcd values; Section 6 treats
that separate issue with its own complete complement estimate.

## 4. A18: one full factor, all original masks, all divisors

The accepted input here is the fixed buffered Mertens estimate
M(t)<<_beta t^beta, .874872<beta<1. It is the accepted zero-free
baseline, not an inference from a Gaussian norm bound. Define

    f_d(n)=product_(p|n, p not dividing 3d)(-1).

For every positive integer d,n, including repeated primes,

    f(dn)=f(d)f_d(n),    f_d=h_d*mu.                         (R13)

The local h_d generating factors, with w=p^-s, are

    (1-w)^(-2),                        p|3d,
    (1-2w)/(1-w)^2 = 1-sum_(j>=2)(j-1)w^j,   p not dividing 3d.

For fixed beta>1/2 the absolute coefficient sum satisfies

    B_d(beta):=sum_a |h_d(a)|a^-beta
       <= C_beta product_(p|d)(1-p^-beta)^(-2)
       <<_(beta,delta) d^delta,                            any delta>0. (R14)

The product over unexceptional primes converges because its first
nonconstant term is O(p^-2beta). The final bound absorbs finitely
many small primes in the constant and bounds each remaining factor
by p^delta. No reciprocal of the prime-two zero is taken.

Convolution with M gives

    sum_(n<=t)f_d(n) <<_beta B_d t^beta,    t>=1,

and this partial sum is zero below one. Abel summation over the whole
positive half-line, with vanishing Gaussian endpoint terms, yields

    F_d(y):=sum_n f_d(n)g(log(n/y))
       <<_(beta,tau) B_d y^beta,                            all y>0. (R15)

The controlling integral is
y^beta integral exp(beta v)|g'(v)|dv. Extending below t=1 only
enlarges this bound. Thus d>X, where y=x/d may be less than one,
is explicitly covered.

Now fix ANY original one-variable mask A_X(n) with 0<=A_X(n)<=1.
It may depend on X arbitrarily, have discontinuities, and fail to be
multiplicative. It remains frozen as a coefficient sequence while x
varies in the shell. Define its induced divisor field with the exact
argument

    G_(d,A)(y)=sum_n f_d(n)A_X(dn)g(log(n/y)).

Only the positive estimate |G_(d,A)(y)|<=C_tau y is used. Insert the
Möbius formula for coprimality before estimating either factor.
By R13, the two occurrences of f(d) multiply to one, giving exactly

    C_1(F,f A_X)=sum_(d>=1)mu(d) integral_X^(2X)
                     F_d(x/d)G_(d,A)(x/d) dx/x.            (R16)

Fubini is already justified before cancellation by the positive bound
sum_d [sum_n g(log(dn/x))]^2<=C x^2 sum_d d^-2. After applying
R14--R15, the absolute sum in R16 is at most

    C X^(1+beta) sum_d B_d/d^(1+beta) << X^(1+beta),         (R17)

choosing delta<beta. This proves A18 uniformly over the stated
original masks, with constants independent of their choice. Every
divisor, every valuation and the exact induced moving threshold
A_X(dn) remains in the restored scalar.

These quantifiers are necessary. The statement needs one unmasked
factor. It proves no cancellation estimate for two arbitrary masks,
for a general pair mask, or for a masked field by itself. Replacing
A_X(dn) by a mask defined at scale X/d changes the source. Similarly,
arbitrary independent d-dependent masks would no longer restore the
same original scalar, even if their individual absolute estimates
remained available. In the present rough application the correct
threshold is always the original z=kappa sqrt(X).

Taking A_X=1 and using R15 on BOTH full factors gives separately

    C_1(F,F)=sum_d mu(d) integral F_d(x/d)^2 dx/x
                  =O(X^(2beta)),                          (R18)

because sum_d B_d^2/d^(2beta) converges after choosing
2delta<2beta-1. Its only coprime diagonal K_X(1,1) is superpower
small. This is A19 at the accepted baseline only.

Apply R17 with A_X=A_R and pay the short-shift/window removal by
R11--R12. Exact F=T+R at the same pair mask gives

    C_1^H(F,R)=O(X^(1+beta)+XH+X^-4),
    C_1^H(T,R)=-C_1^H(R,R)+O(X^(1+beta)+XH+X^-4),
    C_1^H(R,T)=C_1^H(T,R).                                (R19)

For H=X/L^6 the error is o(X^2/L^4), since beta<1 is fixed.
This proves A5, including its opposite sign. The fourth ordered
piece is also fixed by the exact identity:

    C_1^H(F,F)=C_1^H(T,T)+C_1^H(T,R)+C_1^H(R,T)+C_1^H(R,R),
    C_1^H(T,T)=C_1^H(R,R)+O(X^(1+beta)+XH+X^-4).            (R20)

For R20 use R18, its removed negligible diagonal, and the positive
short-shift payment. Since 2beta<1+beta, that full-factor error is
absorbed. The algebra uses no PSD property of the coprime scalar.
All four ordered pieces remain; replacing the two mixed pieces by
one, or taking their absolute values, would destroy the full return.

The primitive coprime form is exactly

    C_1^H(R,R)=2 sum_(h>H)sum_((a,h)=1)
       f(a(a+h))A_R(a)A_R(a+h)1_(a,a+h in I_X)K_X(a,a+h).

Here gcd(a,a+h)=1 justifies f(a)f(a+h)=f(a(a+h)). The ordered TR
scalar instead uses the bracket
A_T(a)A_R(a+h)+A_T(a+h)A_R(a), without an extra factor two.
This is the full actual g=1 obstruction, not a prime-dilation ray.

## 5. The unpartitioned hard target and exact return costs

For the full, unpartitioned coefficient, the accepted G33/S10 signed
high-gcd estimate and its true diagonal subtraction give, for D>=1,

    Q_off=Q_<D+O_epsilon(X^(2beta+epsilon)D^(1-2beta)).       (R21)

This estimate is not transferred to rough or arbitrary signed
submasks. The true high-gcd diagonal fits its size: if D<=X, its
O(X) total is at most X^(2beta)D^(1-2beta); if D>X, a Gaussian
weighted tail bound supplies the same inequality. Thus the separately
paid diagonal in the cited source does not leave a large-D gap.

Write m=ga, n=g(a+h), where g=gcd(m,n), h>=1 and (a,h)=1.
Using R13 and coprimality, the exact full off-diagonal identity is

    Q_<D=2 sum_(1<=g<D)sum_(h>=1)sum_((a,h)=1)
                          f_g(a(a+h))K_(X/g)(a,a+h).       (R22)

The kernel rescales exactly, with no extra factor g. For any ordered
threshold piece (i,j), its summand has the bracket

    A_i(ga)A_j(g(a+h))+A_i(g(a+h))A_j(ga).                 (R23)

The masks and I_X are evaluated on the ORIGINAL integers. Their
threshold is kappa sqrt(X), not kappa sqrt(X/g). For i=j, R23 is
twice the product. The full partition sums all ordered (i,j), so
TR and RT both occur even though the symmetric scalars are equal.
Summing all four brackets gives the factor two in R22.

For every g, remove primitive h<=H using R11 at Y=X/g. This costs

    C XH sum_(g<D)1/g <= C XH log(2D).                     (R24)

The original window costs O(X^-4) once in the whole scalar: the
original pair has a unique gcd, so there is no duplicate tail cost
to sum over g. Define Q_hard by R22 with h>H and both original
integers in I_X. Then

    Q_off=Q_hard+O_epsilon(X^(2beta+epsilon)D^(1-2beta)
                            +XH log(2D)+X^-4).            (R25)

To return to ||F||^2 add the true full diagonal
Delta(X)=sum_n K_X(n,n)=O_tau(X) exactly once. Delta is unrelated
to the p=q completion diagonal R4.

For D=X^theta, H=X^alpha, gamma>1/2 and the strict inequalities

    theta>(2beta-2gamma)/(2beta-1),  theta>=0,
    0<=alpha<2gamma-1,                                    (R26)

the complementary errors lie below X^(2gamma), after taking
epsilon smaller than the fixed margins. In the author's improvement
targets gamma<beta, so R26 automatically forces theta>0. The
one-sided bound Q_hard<=C_epsilon X^(2gamma+epsilon), for every
epsilon>0 on all sufficiently large dyadic shells, is equivalent
to the unpaid full f3 Gaussian target with those parameters. It is
an upper bound on the complete signed scalar; no absolute or
separate-piece estimate is silently substituted.

For the three displayed targets, the accepted G30 reconciliation
cost O_epsilon(X^(1.3749+epsilon)) is below X^(2gamma). The full
G25--G31 interface already pays the outer prime-power convolution,
finite caps, local product diagonals and both independent heights.
The present obstruction supplies no improved estimate for that
interface. A successful new full scalar estimate would still have
to enter it with its exact signs and scale.

I checked the author's c2-only budgets as exact rational arithmetic:

| gamma | theta | alpha | high-gcd exponent | margin below 2gamma | short-shift margin |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| .874871 | .000006 | .749740 | 1.749741501524 | .000000498476 | .000002 |
| 5/6 | .111 | .66 | 1.666524194 | 213709/1500000000 | 1/150 |
| 3/4 | .334 | .49 | 1.499330836 | 167291/250000000 | 1/100 |

These are budgets for returning a hypothetical bound, not a proof of
the hard scalar bound. The first line remains a historical c2 target;
it cannot be promoted as a gain over c4. The other displayed targets
remain open. All uses of beta have a fixed buffer, never equality
at a zero-free boundary.

## 6. A29a--b: complete all-g hard masks, with independent positive costs

The g=1 lower bound alone would leave open signed cancellation among
other g. The author's separate complete complement estimate closes
that gap for its specific rough scalar. For every real D>=1,

    sum_((m,n)>=D) K_X(m,n)
       <= sum_(integer d>=D) integral [sum_a g(log(da/x))]^2 dx/x
       <= C X^2 sum_(d>=D)d^-2 <= C X^2/D.                 (R27)

Every original pair is counted at least at d=gcd(m,n). Positive
overcounting is permissible here, and R2 pays the entire infinite
divisor tail. R27 is a positive mass bound for ANY bounded
coefficients, distinct from the signed unpartitioned G33 estimate.

Let Q_hard(u,v) use exactly the mask in R25: m!=n, gcd(m,n)<D,
|m-n|/gcd(m,n)>H, and m,n in the original I_X. Its difference from
the uncut scalar has the absolute bound

    E=X^2/D+XH log(2D)+X+X^-4,                            (R28)

by R27, R24, the true diagonal, and the original window tail.
These masks are compatible and are the SAME for all four pieces.
Thus the whole rough scalar, not merely its g=1 subfamily, satisfies

    Q_hard(R,R)=||R||^2+O(E),
    Q_hard(F,R)=O(X^(1+beta)+E),
    Q_hard(T,R)=-Q_hard(R,R)+O(X^(1+beta)+E),
    Q_hard(R,T)=Q_hard(T,R),
    Q_hard(T,T)=Q_hard(R,R)+O(X^(1+beta)+E).                (R29)

For the FR line, use the actual accepted full field F(x)<<X^beta
and the elementary |R(x)|<=C X, then pay R28. For TT, combine
the exact four-piece identity with ||F||^2=O(X^(2beta)); this error
is absorbed in X^(1+beta). No hereditary estimate on an arithmetic
submask is used. R7--R6 give ||R||^2 asymp X^2/L^4, or one can
use the already accepted critical-source theorem at this fixed
kappa. Its leading function is uniformly positive here.

For any FIXED theta>0 and 0<=alpha<1, D=X^theta,H=X^alpha give
E=o(X^2/L^4). Since beta<1, all remaining errors in R29 are also
o(X^2/L^4). Therefore the COMPLETE all-g<D hard RR scalar is
positive and comparable to X^2/L^4; its complete mixed TR and RT
scalars have the opposite sign and comparable magnitude. This is
A29b, and it is not inferred from a positive g=1 subcollection.

When theta<1/2, eventually D<z. A shared rough prime would divide
the literal gcd and force it to be at least z, contradicting the
hard mask. Thus central retained RR pairs again have four distinct
rough primes. This extra assertion requires theta<1/2; it is not
claimed for all theta>0. The three displayed budgets satisfy it.

The cost X^2/D need not be small enough for a desired full power
budget X^(2gamma). Its role here is to be small compared with the
particular obstruction size X^2/L^4. Confusing these uses would
overclaim the result. Likewise, R29 is compatible with extensive
full-field cancellation: the leading RR,TR,RT,TT terms have signs
+,-,-,+ and cancel in their full sum. There is no full-energy lower
bound from R29.

## 7. Exact scalar, diagonal and two-height interface

For a frozen original pair mask B_X(m,n), let c_i(n)=f(n)A_i(n),
and, on Re(s_1)=Re(s_2)=sigma>1, define

    D_ij,B(s_1,s_2)=sum_(m,n>=1)
                  B_X(m,n)c_i(m)c_j(n)m^-s_1 n^-s_2.

For |B_X|<=1 it is absolutely bounded by zeta(sigma)^2. Gaussian
Mellin inversion gives the exact bilinear scalar

    (1/(2pi)^2) integral_(R^2)
      exp(tau(s_1^2+s_2^2)/2) D_ij,B(s_1,s_2)
      [integral_X^(2X) x^(s_1+s_2) dx/x] dt_1 dt_2,
    s_j=sigma+i t_j.                                     (R30)

This is a real-coefficient bilinear representation, so it correctly
uses s_1+s_2 without an inserted conjugate. Changing t_1 to -t_1
produces the equivalent conjugated first-height convention. It
does not factor D_ij,B when B_X couples the integers. Gaussian
decay exp(-tau(t_1^2+t_2^2)/2) pays both independent height tails
and justifies the initial exchanges. No equality t_1=t_2 is imposed.

The threshold, divisor condition, shift condition and window are
original-X masks. They are not altered during Mellin inversion,
reindexed to X/g masks, or differentiated as a contour parameter.
The original complete TT,TR,RT,RR sum, the true diagonal and the
outer accepted full-source convolution must all be restored before
an improvement can enter the mismatch estimate. R30 supplies no
primewise-independent or RN/pair02 substitute through the kernel.

The actual obstruction therefore narrows the unpaid route: an
estimate of separate absolute block sizes, or even a power upper
bound on this complete RR block alone, is false for any fixed
gamma<1 with epsilon chosen below 2-2gamma. What remains possible
and unpaid is a signed cancellation estimate for the complete hard
scalar, including all four pieces and all its dependent variables.

## 8. Prime-two alternative: exact conditional self-copy, no contraction

Let psi=f_6, so that primes 2 and 3 are ignored by its sign and
psi(2n)=psi(n). Let chi_2(n)=1-2*1_(2|n). Then f=chi_2 psi.
Define P,Z,D by the Gaussian fields with coefficients psi,1,chi_2.
The exact dilation relations are

    F(x)=P(x)-2P(x/2),
    D(x)=Z(x)-2Z(x/2).                                   (R31)

The function q(u)=g(log u) for u>0, extended by zero for u<=0,
is Schwartz and flat at zero. Poisson summation thus gives

    Z(x)=exp(tau/2)x+O_N(x^-N),
    D(x)=O_N(x^-N),                                      x>=1. (R32)

For D, apply the Z expansion at x and x/2; the bounded intermediate
range is absorbed in its constant. This is an actual positive
all-integer law, not the squarefree occupation law of R38.5.

Under nu_x(n)=g(log(n/x))/Z(x), the means of chi_2,psi and their
product are D/Z,P/Z,F/Z. Two binary signs satisfy the exact formula

    sum_(a,b in {+-1})
      |Pr(chi_2=a,psi=b)-Pr(chi_2=a)Pr(psi=b)|
         = |F/Z-DP/Z^2|.                                 (R33)

Each signed cell difference is ab times the covariance divided by
four. Thus this is total L1 distance; total variation has the extra
factor one half. Since |P|<=Z and D is superpower small, R33 shows
that independence at a new power would essentially reassert a new
bound for F/x. The very small marginal D/Z does not give that
independence. Its shell L2 interpretation has the same obstruction
because Z asymp X uniformly on the shell.

The exact even branch numerator is P(x/2), while the odd branch is
P(x)-P(x/2). Exposing prime 2 has left the same remaining sign
coefficient at half scale. This is the conditional self-copy that
prevents the marginal argument from supplying a new contraction.

The accepted h_d*mu bound at d=6 supplies P(x)<<x^beta. Iterating
R31 toward future scales gives for each integer J>=1

    P(x)=-sum_(j=1)^J 2^-j F(2^j x)+2^-J P(2^J x),
    |2^-J P(2^J x)|<<x^beta 2^(-(1-beta)J).               (R34)

The remainder tends to zero, and the infinite sum converges
absolutely at this fixed beta<1. If a full-shell norm bound
||F||_[Y,2Y]<=C Y^gamma holds on every sufficiently large dyadic
shell with gamma<1, the triangle inequality and exact shell
rescaling give

    ||P||_[X,2X] <= C X^gamma/(2^(1-gamma)-1).

Conversely R31 transfers a P bound to F with factor
1+2^(1-gamma). These are equivalences below exponent one, not an
improvement mechanism by themselves.

To make the available baseline remainder in R34 smaller than a
proposed X^gamma, it suffices to choose

    J > ((beta-gamma)/(1-beta)) log_2 X

with a fixed positive coefficient margin. Correspondingly the
largest future scale exceeds X^((1-gamma)/(1-beta)) by a fixed
power margin. This is a sufficient budget based on the known upper
bound, not a necessary lower bound on the true remainder. The exact
rational horizons in the saved evidence match the author. Repeating
the existing beta bound through R34 produces no exponent gain.

The archived N28 dilation calculations already identify this
calibration issue. R38.5 instead proves a positive squarefree
occupation law with Bernoulli marginals 1/(p+1), in its stated
finite-coordinate range. It does not prove the all-integer joint
law of chi_2 and this signed psi, much less the coupled coprime,
shift and two-height assertion needed here. Likewise the prime-ray
Katai-type average (1-2/p)(1-2/q) repeats [private research revision] S24. The author
correctly gives it no new cancellation credit.

## 9. Lean exact evidence and final qualifications

The retained independent helper used N=168 and the separable integer
kernel w(m)w(n), w(n)=n^2+1. It checked the Möbius restoration with
one full factor against direct coprime enumeration for a rough mask
and for the nonmultiplicative mask (n mod 4)/3. Their exact scaled
values were 9196130146 and -266115328142. Divisors d>N/4 contributed
nonzero values 1426123732 and 296849014 respectively; they were
retained, not silently dropped.

The same helper independently enumerated original pairs and the
g,a,b reindexing with original window [7,168], D=11/2 and primitive
shift cutoff H=3. The four ordered values agreed exactly:

    TT=-37323089430, TR=-912968635,
    RT=-912968635,  RR=2362956600.

This exercises original-scale masks, nonintegral D, primitive shift
division, both orders and all four pieces. These numbers are not
Gaussian data and do not prove the asymptotic signs or sizes.
The proof of those facts is R1--R29. Exact rational arithmetic also
verified the three historical budgets and future-scale horizons.
No parameter search, outcome-driven new sample, or broad test suite
was used; the retained successful check was not rerun after recovery.

The qualifications on admission are substantive but already
respected by the frozen report:

1. The source theorem fixes tau and kappa, freezes masks on the
   original X shell, and retains every core and valuation. The
   completed positive field is a bound or PNT source, not an
   automatically interchangeable signed arithmetic family.
2. A18 is uniform in one original mask with the other factor full.
   It neither bounds arbitrary two-mask scalars nor transfers the
   full Mertens/Gaussian estimate to a signed subfamily.
3. The complete coprime scalar is not PSD. The coprime RR lower
   bound pays the whole noncoprime error. The all-g hard-mask
   theorem has its own complete positive complement payment.
4. Four distinct rough primes follow in the g=1 theorem and, for
   the all-g hard mask, when theta<1/2. The larger-theta obstruction
   does not need that extra conclusion.
5. All scalar restorations keep the true diagonal, both ordered
   mixed pieces and both independent Mellin heights. The costs
   X^2/D and XH log(2D)+O(X) have their stated roles and cannot be
   replaced by a hereditary signed G33 estimate.
6. The prime-two calculation rules out the proposed marginal
   shortcut at its stated scope. It is not a theorem excluding
   every future approach using that prime.
7. The author uses an earlier valid buffered baseline. The two
   live-source hash changes and later c4 acceptance are disclosed;
   they do not retroactively change the packet's premises or make
   its historical first budget a current improvement.

**Admission recommendation:** accept A3--A5, A18--A22 and A29a--b as
proved source-specific restrictions/obstructions, together with the
exact A24--A30 return and the prime-two conditional-self-copy
calibration. Keep the full joint cancellation problem and every new
c claim open. No edit to the frozen author packet is required by
this independent review.

## 7. Physical and quartic decisions

P19/P18r is the first unpaid prime-row gate for the translated-profile route: one-sided real signed inverse–difference–modulus interaction. Using a local theorem after UM costs U times U^(.5-delta), hence delta>=1.5-J, or3/8 at the nominal point versus available1/40. Endpoint aggregation still has ||r_H*||₂~A^1.5 and the same fourth-moment price. A useful improvement must enter before that loss; this is a quantified gate, not an impossibility claim.

The unshifted-profile finite-difference stencil is separately useful: reindexing its character changes the common weight, so the translated-profile cancellation does not remove its endpoint structure. Its UM-weighted approximation is paid, but its complete mixed source remains to be bounded. Arbitrary endpoints/rays, nonunit and composite complements do not follow from the local theorem.

At a good odd quartic place the compact invariant space is Ce. Upper-unipotent invariance forces support in O; Weyl invariance then forces O-translation invariance. Projection reads integral_O f. The displayed exterior extension is self-Fourier, with f(0)=integral f=0, but projects to (1-Q^-2)e. Its residual g has squared norm2Q^-2(1-Q^-2), yet arithmetic readout/norm ratio Q^(2-2sigma). This is an explicit warning against pricing that readout by Hilbert smallness, not a claim about a bounded functional on all L2 vectors.

When the first two actual factors are K-fixed, simultaneous compact averaging factors through the same 1-dimensional projection. The moving family becomes A(t)e and retains the common numerator L_K^S(2s-1,chi2), where A(t)=zeta_K^S(2-it)/zeta_K^S(2) is bounded away from 0. A vector of projected t-values is rank1 and offers no complementary numerator zeros. This does not settle unprojected moving numerators, bad places, archimedean matching or the full relative boundary. Those costs remain open; no unreviewed claim from the other source review was used.

The unprojected family still has a real conditional covering advantage: on any fixed interval I of positive length, t maps to L_K^S(2s-1-it,chi2), which cannot vanish identically in L2(I) at a fixed s by the identity theorem. Thus its full vector norm can retain a zero hidden in an individual numerator. No uniform all-height lower constant is required for that fixed-pole contradiction. The actual OPEN-QFAM bound remains open. The direct smoothing hierarchy of section 4 also applies to this same Hilbert-valued coefficient family: its coefficient absolute mass grows polynomially, uniformly for t in fixed I, and Minkowski preserves L2(I). This transfers a paid norm between kernels; it does not compare the quartic coefficients with A(n), nor price a relative restriction. Projection removes the numerator variation that made this vector return useful.

# W50: exact energy return and the cost of a prime-phase trace

Status: bounded author result for independent review, not acceptance of a new zero-free constant. Seeds were frozen at c7=6257/50000=.125140 and theta7=43743/50000=.874860. The useful output is an exact ordinary-character energy target, an actual-character finite trace obstruction, and a sharp large-prime response diameter. The three other selected control/dilation ideas fail their first sufficient test or remain unembedded in arithmetic.



Current worklog: all 30 seeds and reservations were frozen before detailed history; the single recipe-seeded draw selected exactly04,07,23,26,30,27. Six first tests and three substantive developments are complete. Character quantifiers and natural zeros are retained. ## 1. Freeze, ancestry and six tests

The immutable seed file is `seeds.json`, SHA256 `5df86fb9fc27ceb478e1937c83b166a6befaf90ada550221185e2f7c1bfb764c`, 21,258 bytes. The immutable `draw-receipt.json`, SHA256 `ec05d2bc48cc7ed1f21c876af77ca1fa538d2e34fd253db4f109b411dfdee3c6`, records all pools, the recipe's integer entropy, every PRNG state, indices19,12,22 and the six selections. One stream, one draw per pool, no rerolls. Eligibility uses every card's literal p, independently of group. The first two groups are free invention. Four substantive recipe combinations inform groups3–6. Card29's incoherent raw indefinite-energy assertion is preserved before its proposed repair.

After the seed-only notification to root, I read current-proof, attempt-index and relevant source history. The headers still said c6; this lane uses the parent's explicitly frozen c7. In particular:

* W35/current-proof G1–G3 already has a Gaussian shell-energy continuation bridge; W27 and F01 have earlier weak/energy detector ancestry. The unsmoothed E1–E4 below are a direct derivation, not a new general detector principle.
* [private research revision] G68 keeps a full arithmetic response after exact Walsh truncation; G69 rejects a global Euler norm while proving a causal output identity. [private research revision] G71 is a much stronger fixed-sequence asymptotic countermodel than our finite-prefix example, but it is not mu times an actual Dirichlet character. These scopes must not be conflated.
* W27-08/13/19, the early prime-toggle/code family, and the retained random-phase warnings precede our trace proposal. The explicit Jacobi realization and exact tail diameter are the refinements supplied here. I did not locate those exact statements in the bounded history search; this is not a literature-novelty claim.
* JN4–JN9, [private research revision] FG1–FG8, and [private research revision] H retain the actual phase, natural zeros, two rooted marks, full projectors and moving pair kernel. Existing orbit projections can preserve a signed pairing while discarding norm. Our generic dilation test does not refute those legitimate projections.

| Selected card | First decisive test | Result and boundary |
|---|---|---|
|04, strongest bridge|Derive the full pair kernel and continuation directly.|E1–E7 below hold; no new arithmetic energy estimate. Substantive development1.|
|07, highest ceiling|Compute phase-evaluation norm and realize the bad phase with an actual character.|T1–T5 below show a uniform trace loss of at least X^(1/2); a fixed-modulus repair has an exact signed covariance cost. Substantive development2.|
|23, most different|Compute every cofactor in the one-large-prime complement.|P1–P4 give its exact response radius and actual-character realization, with the fixed-character limitation explicit. Substantive development3.|
|26, first strict p<.10 draw|Preserve the literal H pairing through a unitary dilation and compression.|H1–H3 identify the unpaid complement; unitary norm conservation alone provides no gain. No native H estimate.|
|30, strict p<.01 draw|Derive the causal multiplicative delay identity including its moving upper limit.|D1–D2 are exact; a Mellin mode cannot be inserted below absolute convergence without paying the boundary. No stability estimate.|
|27, uniform remaining draw|Construct an unstable but unobservable two-state mode.|The toy refutes output-stability alone; no such hidden arithmetic mode is asserted.|

Only the first three are substantive developments. The finite helper checks the advertised identities at small cutoffs; it proves neither asymptotic cancellation nor zero exclusion at a new exponent.

## 2. Development04: unsmoothed energy and a full character return

Fix an ordinary Dirichlet character chi modulo q, extended by zero exactly on nonunits, and put a(n)=mu(n)chi(n). Complete multiplicativity, including zero values, gives

    (a*chi)(n)=chi(n) sum_(d|n) mu(d)=delta_(n=1).        (E1)

Let M_chi(x)=sum_(n<=x)a(n), and for every real X>=1 define

    E_chi(X)=integral_1^X |M_chi(x)|^2 dx/x
      =sum_(m,n<=X) a(m) conjugate(a(n))
                            log(X/max(m,n)).            (E2)

Proof: the pair (m,n) is present exactly when x>=max(m,n). The finite integral of its indicator is the displayed logarithm. Integer upper endpoints have zero weight when max(m,n)=X; no half-weight convention occurs. The terminal log X contribution is part of E2. The pair kernel is a positive Gram kernel, but its signed off-diagonal summands need not be positive.

**Energy-to-zero-exclusion theorem.** Suppose 0<gamma<1 is common to all ordinary characters and, for each fixed chi and every epsilon>0,

    E_chi(X) <= C_(chi,epsilon) X^(2gamma+epsilon)       (E3)

for all sufficiently large real X (or merely all sufficiently large dyadic X, by positivity/monotonicity). Then L(s,chi) has no zeros in Re(s)>gamma. Principal poles retain their usual separate meaning. Constants and thresholds may depend on chi; no growing-conductor uniformity is assumed.

Proof: H_chi(s)=integral_1^infinity M_chi(x)x^(-s)dx/x. On a compact subset with Re(s)>=sigma0>gamma, choose 0<epsilon<2(sigma0-gamma). Cauchy–Schwarz on [2^j,2^(j+1)] bounds the absolute integral, including any fixed number k of s-derivatives, by

    O_(chi,epsilon,k)( (j+1)^k
                       2^(j(gamma+epsilon/2-sigma0)) ).

Its sum converges locally uniformly. Thus H_chi is holomorphic on Re(s)>gamma. Absolute summation first gives sH_chi(s)=1/L(s,chi) on Re(s)>1, since integral_n^infinity x^(-s)dx/x=n^(-s)/s. Meromorphic continuation of L and the identity theorem give

    L(s,chi) sH_chi(s)=1                               (E4)

throughout the connected half-plane, with the principal pole treated meromorphically. A zero of L there contradicts E4 because sH_chi is holomorphic and s!=0. Every finite height belongs to this open half-plane; no unproved uniform moving-height estimate is used. Natural imprimitive Euler factors were never stripped from a or L. This proves the theorem.

Extracting a pointwise bound from E3 using only |a|<=1 generally loses an exponent; this proof does not perform that extraction. It returns directly to a reciprocal L-function. Conversely a complete Mertens bound at gamma trivially supplies E3. I do not claim a new equivalence theorem beyond these two stated implications.

There is an exact fixed-modulus version of the high-ceiling trace idea. For all phi(q) characters modulo one FIXED q, orthogonality gives

    Ebar_q(X)=(1/phi(q)) sum_(chi mod q) E_chi(X)
      =sum_(m,n<=X; (mn,q)=1; m==n mod q)
                   mu(m)mu(n) log(X/max(m,n)).           (E5)

This retains all characters, including imprimitive ones and the principal character. It is an exact finite-family positive average, not an average over growing moduli or a statement about most characters. Each E_chi<=phi(q) Ebar_q. Consequently an E3-type bound for Ebar_q for EVERY FIXED q with one common gamma suffices for EVERY FIXED chi; the factor phi(q) is an allowed constant.

The literal diagonal is

    D_q(X)=sum_(n<=X;(n,q)=1)mu(n)^2 log(X/n)=O_q(X).    (E6)

One can sharpen this elementarily to D_q(X)=d_q X+O_q(sqrt(X)+1), with d_q=(phi(q)/q) product_(p not dividing q)(1-p^(-2))>0, by inserting mu(n)^2=sum_(d^2|n)mu(d), counting units, and integrating their O_q(sqrt X) summatory error. An additive constant can be absorbed into the error. This sharpening is not needed for the bridge.

Thus a precise remaining input, sufficient whenever gamma>1/2, is

    OFF_q(X):=sum_(m!=n<=X; (mn,q)=1; m==n mod q)
              mu(m)mu(n) log(X/max(m,n))
       <= C_(q,epsilon) X^(2gamma+epsilon)              (E7)

for every fixed q, every epsilon>0 and all large X. There is no absolute value inside the signed sum and no deletion of negative terms. E7 is OPEN. At q=1 it already contains the unsolved complete Möbius energy, so this finite-family repair creates no free cancellation.

Calibration: a first gain requires 2gamma<1.749720=43743/25000. Targets c=1/6 and 1/4 require gamma=5/6 and 3/4, hence squared-energy exponents 5/3 and 3/2. The elementary absolute bound E_chi(X)<= (X^2-1)/2 leaves a first-gain saving strictly greater than .250280 in the squared exponent. These are sufficient budgets, not achieved estimates. No numerical experiment is being counted as a reduction of that gap.

The finite check uses the genuinely complex order-four character modulo 5, including its zeros, at N=60. It compares exact integer coefficients of every log j in E2 with the integral of the step function: all 3,600 ordered pairs agree, including terminal log60 coefficient 13. This checks indexing only.

## 3. Development07: exact trace loss, realized by Dirichlet characters

Fix a positive integer q0. For squarefree n<=X coprime to q0, let z(n)=product_(p|n)z_p on the product unit torus over primes p<=X not dividing q0. Define

    P_X(z)=sum_(n<=X;(n,q0)=1)mu(n)z(n),
    Q_q0(X)=sum_(n<=X;(n,q0)=1)mu(n)^2.

Orthogonality of distinct prime monomials gives

    ||P_X||_(L2(torus))^2=Q_q0(X).                      (T1)

More generally, evaluation at any unit phase has norm sqrt(Q_q0(X)) on the Q_q0(X)-dimensional squarefree polynomial space: Cauchy gives the upper bound, and coefficients conjugate to that phase attain it. For the PARTICULAR coefficients mu(n), choose z_p=-1 at every unramified prime p<=X. Then mu(n)z(n)=mu(n)^2, so

    P_X(z)=Q_q0(X),
    |P_X(z)|/||P_X||_2=sqrt(Q_q0(X)).                   (T2)

The elementary squarefree count used after E6 gives Q_q0(X)=d_q0 X+O_q0(sqrt X), with positive d_q0. This is the maximal power loss X^(1/2), not X^o(1).

This bad phase can be realized by actual ordinary characters at every finite scale, not only by a nonperiodic multiplicative toy.

**Finite real-character realization lemma.** Given X>=2, a fixed q0, and arbitrary signs epsilon_p in {+1,-1} for primes p<=X not dividing q0, there is a real Dirichlet character chi modulo q0 D such that

    chi(p)=epsilon_p for p<=X, p not dividing q0,
    chi(n)=0 iff gcd(n,q0)>1 for every n<=X.             (T3)

Globally chi has its natural additional zeros at prime divisors of D; these are retained, not filled in.

Proof: choose an odd positive D congruent to 1 mod 4. At2, when unramified and prescribed, take D==1 mod 8 for epsilon_2=+1 and D==5 mod 8 for epsilon_2=-1. For each odd prime p<=X not dividing q0 choose a nonzero residue r_p with Legendre symbol (r_p/p)=epsilon_p and require D==r_p mod p. Require D==1 mod p for any other prime p dividing q0, and for ramified primes<=X. These CRT conditions are consistent and make D coprime to q0 and to every prime<=X. One may take any positive representative. Set chi(n)=1_(n,q0)=1 (n/D), where (n/D) is the Jacobi symbol. It is a real Dirichlet character modulo q0 D. Generalized quadratic reciprocity gives (p/D)=(D/p) because D==1 mod 4; the supplementary law handles 2. Thus T3 follows, and every prime divisor of D is>X. No prime-in-progression existence theorem, squarefree D assumption, primitive-character assertion or factorization of D is required. The Jacobi-character and reciprocity facts are explicitly recorded in [NIST DLMF §27.9](https://dlmf.nist.gov/27.9), verified2026-10-12.

Taking epsilon_p=-1 realizes T2 for a genuine chi, with a=mu chi and the GLOBAL exact identity a*chi=delta. Thus full finite convolution identities plus exact squarefree support do not supply a CHARACTER-UNIFORM bound

    |M_chi(X)| <= C X^eta ||P_X||_2,
    eta<1/2,                                          (T4)

with C independent of chi and X. In particular a universal eta<.374860=.874860-1/2 cannot be deduced merely by declaring the coherent phase trace to be random-like. The quarter-strip aspiration eta=1/4 encounters the same obstruction. The finite test at X=120 constructs

    D=10666004750947751128137555211484342435842576157,
    M_chi(120)=Q_1(120)=75,

checks all 120 convolution identities, and obtains trace-ratio-squared 75. This is an indexing witness, not the proof of the asymptotic norm statement.

**Essential quantifier limitation.** The requested result allows C_chi and X0_chi. Our character varies with X, and may have enormous modulus. T4 therefore does NOT rule out a fixed-character estimate with any eta<1/2, does NOT refute the accepted c7, and is weaker in asymptotic scope than G71. It rules out a particular conductor-independent transfer shortcut. A proof that uses the actual fixed modulus to link large primes is not refuted.

Indeed the corrected finite-group lift gives, for one fixed modulus q,

    (1/phi(q))sum_(chi mod q)|sum_(n<=X)mu(n)chi(n)|^2
      =sum_(r mod q;(r,q)=1)|sum_(n<=X;n==r mod q)mu(n)|^2,
    |M_chi(X)| <= sqrt(phi(q)) ||M_.(X)||_(average L2).  (T5)

The trace factor is now an acceptable fixed constant. Its ambient norm is no longer Q_q(X)^(1/2): the full same-residue Möbius correlations remain. Integrating T5 yields exactly E5–E7. This is the paid repair; it supplies no estimate for the new norm.

For completeness, constraints (b*chi)(n)=delta_(n=1) only for n<=Y force b(n)=mu(n)chi(n) only for n<=Y, by the unit-diagonal triangular recursion. Higher coordinates remain unconstrained by those LINEAR equations. In a squarefree coefficient Hilbert space the homogeneous free-coordinate evaluation norm is the square root of the number of allowed coordinates aboveY. Imposing full multiplicativity is an additional nonlinear restriction; the arbitrary-free-coordinate observation does not claim otherwise. T3 shows that even full arithmetic multiplicativity does not prevent bad finite traces when the character/modulus is free to change.

## 4. Development23: the exact large-prime response diameter

Let X>=4, sqrt(X)<=y<=X, and prescribe completely multiplicative unit values z_p for p<=y, with z_p=0 at p|q0. For p>y, p not dividing q0, initially allow independent unit phases. Extend completely multiplicatively, put a_z(n)=mu(n)z(n), and set

    S_y(X)=sum_(n<=X; Pplus(n)<=y)a_z(n),
    A(t)=sum_(m<=t)a_z(m),        1<=t<=X/y<=y.

Here Pplus(1)=1, and A depends only on the fixed low-prime data. Every squarefree n<=X with a prime factor>y has exactly one such factor p, occurring once, and n=pm with m<=X/p<p. Hence its coefficient is exactly -z_p a_z(m), including the ramified zeros. Therefore

    M_z(X)=S_y(X)-sum_(y<p<=X; p not dividing q0)
                                      z_p A(X/p).       (P1)

Both the whole smooth sector and the whole complementary prime sector are retained. Repeated-prime terms vanish by mu, rather than being assigned arbitrary signs. No coprimality factor is missing because m<p.

Define R_y(X)=sum_(y<p<=X;p not dividing q0)|A(X/p)|. Independent phase alignment yields

    max_z |M_z(X)-S_y(X)|=R_y(X),
    max_(z,z') |M_z(X)-M_z'(X)|=2R_y(X).               (P2)

The first upper bound is the triangle inequality. To attain it in direction e^(it), choose z_p=-e^(it) conjugate(A(X/p))/|A(X/p)| when A!=0, and choose an arbitrary unit value when A=0. Opposite directions attain the diameter. If the low values are real signs, S_y and every A are real, and the choices z_p=-sign(A) and z_p=sign(A), with any sign at 0, give exactly S_y+R_y and S_y-R_y. T3 realizes both by actual real Dirichlet characters having identical low-prime data and the same ramified zeros up toX. In particular at least one has |M_chi(X)|>=R_y(X).

There is an exact endpoint-sensitive cofactor formula. With pi_q0(t) counting primes<=t not dividing q0,

    R_y(X)=sum_(1<=m<=floor(X/y)) |A(m)|
      [pi_q0(X/m)-pi_q0(max(y,X/(m+1)))].               (P3)

The lower prime endpoint is strict and the upper endpoint inclusive, exactly as floor(X/p)=m requires. The possible terminal empty interval contributes 0. For y<=X/2 the m=1 term alone gives

    R_y(X)>=pi_q0(X)-pi_q0(X/2).                       (P4)

For fixed q0 and growing X, ordinary PNT makes this (1/2+o(1))X/log X. Only the ordinary PNT is used here, not a character prime theorem or any zero-free improvement; its asymptotic is documented in [NIST DLMF §27.12](https://dlmf.nist.gov/27.12), verified2026-10-12. P1–P3 and the exact inequality P4 do not need PNT.

The finite checks include nontrivial natural ramification. For (X,y,q0)=(120,11,1), S=2,R=17 and the two character sums are 19,-15. For (120,11,3), S=1,R=15 and sums 16,-14. For (255,16,5), S=-2,R=38 and sums 36,-40. Every full enumeration agrees with P1–P3; the receipt stores the realizing moduli.

This is a precise obstruction to a phase-blind small-prime certificate that attempts to pay the complement at any fixed exponent<1 uniformly over its compatible characters. It is NOT an asymptotic counterexample for one fixed character and not a lower bound for its actual Mertens energy. The two realizing moduli generally differ, and the extra natural zeros beyondX are different.

There is also a simple reason the fixed-modulus escape is real. Two characters modulo one fixed q that agree on all primes<=q not dividing q agree on every unit residue: factor its least positive representative r<=q into those primes. The zero classes agree by the modulus. Thus once y>=q, the low-prime values determine the whole character. At y=sqrt X this happens for X>=q^2. The adversarial independent tail is then unavailable. A useful next estimate must exploit that global linkage, rather than claim P2 is an obstruction for all sufficiently large X at one fixed q.

## 5. The three short control/dilation tests, with literal H scope

For card26 the actual source is JN9, not an invented positive H matrix. Fix the original ordered long-prime pair pi,pi' of distinct rational norms and the original short sources g=du,g'=dv. Write Q=q_pi q_pi'. The unitary finite transform has group size Q^2 and factor1/Q, with phase

    -Rh/(pi*pi') -Ps/pi +P's'/pi'.                      (H1)

Its kernel is chi_pi(h)^3 chi_pi'(h)^3 chi_pi(s)^2 chi_pi'(s')^4, including zeros whenever (h,pi*pi')!=1, s==0 mod pi or s'==0 mod pi'. The outer coefficient is

    b(pi) conjugate(b(pi')) zeta_(pi,pi')
                          C0(pi) conjugate(C0(pi')),
    b(pi)=alpha(pi)eta(pi)chi_pi(lambda)^(-2)gamma3(pi),
    zeta=chi_pi((pi')^(-1))^3 chi_pi'(-pi^(-1))^3.

The entire W_d retains h(d)A0(du)conjugate(A0(dv)), xi(u)conjugate(xi(v)), both original coefficients u1(P)/sqrt(q_P) and conjugate(u2(P'))/sqrt(q_P'), the row factor chi_R(uv)^3, profiles, independent heights, source windows and

    1_(R,d)=1 1_(P,Rdu)=1 1_(P',Rdv)=1.                (H2)

The full row/mark projectors may be expanded into all D,D' with mu(D)mu(D'); no signed child inherits the parent's estimate automatically. For the original far complement also retain q_pi!=q_pi' and |q_pi-q_pi'|>floor(Z^.05), along with all remaining front selectors. This is the exact historical packet, not the complete all-branch H theorem.

Use the inner product linear in its second argument, take W to be the actual transformed W_d, and take k to be the complex conjugate of the displayed native character kernel. Thus <k,W> is the original unconjugated kernel sum, with no phase changed. For any isometric lift V and orthogonal compression P, a single native pairing decomposes exactly as

    <k,W>=<PVk,PVW>+<(I-P)Vk,(I-P)VW>.                 (H3)

Apply H3 before summing every outer coefficient, d and height. Unitarity alone only conserves the full norm. The complement is zero if a proved projection preserves the kernel vector; this is a legitimate possibility, and the existing kernel-invariant orbit projection is not refuted. Otherwise the complete complement needs a signed bound. A 2x2 unitary with columns (3/5,4/5) and (4/5,-3/5) already shows that discarding the second coordinate can hide 16/25 of squared norm without lowering the complete norm. No general unitary-dilation theorem supplies the required arithmetic improvement.

Calibration of this historical H subpacket remains its original one: fixed-u,v raw target G K S sqrt(Omega1 Omega2), existing G(K+N)S bound, N/K=Z^.003, and outside factor N^(-1)G^(-2). The all-g estimate has its separate .004 deficit. The inherited pressure exponents are not recalculated as if c7 changed their analytic inputs. This lane pays neither deficit and claims no complete H-to-c7 return.

For card27, take the two-state system A=diag(7/8,-1), input B=(1,1)^T and observation C=(0,1). Then C(sI-A)^(-1)B=1/(s+1), although the reachable state has the pole 7/8. Thus stable output alone does not exclude an unobservable pole. A valid arithmetic realization must prove that every putative L-zero mode is observed, with its exact numerator and complements. No embedding of this toy pole into H or an L-function is asserted. This is a first-test rejection of the unqualified inference, not an arithmetic impossibility theorem.

For card30, define the locally finite causal measure K_chi=sum_(n>=1)chi(n)delta_(log n), and F_chi(u)=M_chi(e^u) for u>=0, zero for u<0. Finite convolution and E1 give exactly

    (K_chi*F_chi)(u)
      =sum_(n<=e^u)chi(n)M_chi(e^u/n)=1_(u>=0).        (D1)

For Re s>1 its Laplace transform is L(s,chi) and the inverse response is 1/[sL(s,chi)]. Below 1 the absolute delay-kernel norm

    sum_n |chi(n)| n^(-sigma)                          (D2)

diverges for sigma<=1, by summing over unit residue classes. A causal test mode e^(su) gives e^(su) sum_(n<=e^u)chi(n)n^(-s), with a moving upper cutoff; it is not automatically L(s,chi)e^(su). For the principal character and Re s<1 the raw partial sum even has a growing main term. A claimed exponential stability estimate below1 therefore needs actual signed arithmetic control and the causal boundary correction. E3 is one exact adequate control, still open at a new exponent. The helper verifies D1 at six cutoffs with the complex character modulo 5; this says nothing about the missing weighted stability theorem.

## 6. Every card's final disposition

Untested means not disproved. An ancestry overlap is not a mathematical refutation.

## 7. Appended current calibration: c8, without seed changes

After the seed freeze and initial developments, root reported an independently reviewed complete source/endpoint acceptance of written c8=12514261/100000000=.12514261, theta8=87485739/100000000=.87485739. Its mechanism is the marked inverse/weighted density with combined support k(delta)z and a tilted local plane. This report uses that value as supplied task calibration, not as a separately reproduced endpoint proof. The PR9/Gao upstream obligations remain; no formalization is claimed. The original seed SHA and all draw choices remain exactly unchanged.

For E3/E7 a current first gain now requires gamma<.87485739, hence 2gamma<1.74971478=87485739/50000000. For the T4 aspirational trace the threshold is eta<.37485739=37485739/100000000. The gap from the absolute squared-energy exponent2 is strictly greater than .25028522=12514261/50000000. The 1/6 and 1/4 target exponents 5/3 and 3/2 do not change. No estimate here pays any part of these strict gaps. Earlier numerical c7 lines in this report and the finite receipt are historical frozen calibration, not the current incumbent.

## 8. What is and is not established

Established in this report: the complete ordinary-character implication E3=>zero exclusion, exact kernels E2/E5 and fixed-modulus return; actual finite Jacobi-character realization with all natural zeros and the convolution identity; exact prime-tail diameter with its cofactor endpoints; and the restricted first-test identities for dilation/observability/causal delays. Independent review is still required for canonical admission.

Not established: E7 at any gamma below the current .87485739 boundary (nor the earlier .874860 boundary); a low-loss trace estimate for every fixed character at all large X; a useful actual H compression bound; any new c, near gain,1/6 or1/4 theorem; a literature-priority claim. The strongest objection is decisive: the finite hostile characters change their modulus with X, whereas the requested theorem fixes chi first. The report both states and proves the fixed-modulus escape, rather than silently substituting uniform conductor quantifiers.

The next mathematical action is to seek a signed estimate for E7 using the global periodic character linkage, or to retain the same exact natural coefficients while constructing a replacement with a demonstrably cheaper complete covariance. Any finite prime-prefix certificate must show how it uses the modulus after y>=q. A bound for only one interval, typical characters, independent phases, a positive subblock or a truncated causal system would not complete that action.

All30 dispositions are retained. No new tracker/Git/canonical state was written. The final freeze manifest binds this report and every owned artifact; the author stops writing before retirement and sends exactly one final evidence-bound reviewer followup after own-claim release.
