## 3. Development15: actual inverse Newton iteration and its complete rough sector

Throughout, g_tau(v)=(2pi tau)^(-1/2)exp(-v^2/(2tau)), with tau>0 fixed. Let bold1(n)=1, delta(n)=1_(n=1), and let * denote Dirichlet convolution. For integer Y>=1 put

    m_Y(n)=mu(n)1_(n<=Y),
    d_Y=delta-bold1*m_Y,
    M_Y(s)=sum_(n<=Y)mu(n)n^(-s),
    D_Y(s)=1-zeta(s)M_Y(s).

The finite convolution m_Y is literal, including every zero coefficient. For fixed integer k>=1 define

    q_(Y,k)=m_Y*(delta+d_Y+...+d_Y^(*(k-1))),
    Q_(Y,k)(s)=M_Y(s)sum_(j=0)^(k-1)D_Y(s)^j.

The k=2 step is precisely the proposed Newton inverse M(2-zeta M). Repeated Newton squaring corresponds to k a power of2. All identities are first coefficient identities or absolutely convergent series on Re(s)>1, then meromorphic identities away from the principal pole.

**W43.2 (exact support and length return).**

    delta-bold1*q_(Y,k)=d_Y^(*k),
    d_Y(n)=0 for n<=Y,
    d_Y^(*k)(n)=0 for n<(Y+1)^k,
    q_(Y,k)(n)=mu(n) for n<(Y+1)^k.

The first line is the finite geometric identity. The second is mu*bold1=delta with all divisors below the original cutoff. The third follows because every nonzero convolution factor is at least Y+1. Multiply the first line by mu to obtain q_(Y,k)=mu-mu*d_Y^(*k), which proves the last line. Thus truncating q below (Y+1)^k produces exactly the ordinary longer Mobius prefix. This is an identity, not a faster estimate for that prefix. No assertion is made that the endpoint (Y+1)^k is always the first nonzero defect; natural Mobius zeros may delay it.

Let Q^tr be the Dirichlet polynomial obtained by truncating q to n<(Y+1)^k, and T=Q-Q^tr. The entire truncation feedback is

    1-zeta Q^tr = D_Y^k + zeta T.                  (N1)

It is not legitimate to omit zeta T because Q^tr is exactly the longer Mobius prefix. At any zeta zero rho in the open critical strip,

    D_Y(rho)=1, Q_(Y,k)(rho)=k M_Y(rho),
    1-zeta(rho)Q^tr(rho)=1.                       (N2)

Q and T are holomorphic at rho: they are finite polynomials in zeta multiplied by finite Dirichlet polynomials. The apparent formula Q=(1-D_Y^k)/zeta has a removable singularity there. This distinguishes the proposed observable from the actual Gaussian reciprocal detector, whose Mellin transform has a nonvanishing numerator over zeta. A small local smoothed defect has not inherited that pole return.

**W43.3 (all rough coefficients and a fixed-order absolute barrier).** Say n is Y-rough if every prime factor exceeds Y. For every Y-rough n>1, d_Y(n)=-1, because the only divisor admitted by m_Y is1. Hence, for every Y-rough n,

    d_Y^(*k)(n)=(-1)^k F_k(n),

where F_k(n) is the nonnegative number of ordered k-tuples of integers>1 whose product is n. In particular it vanishes for Omega(n)<k, and if Omega(n)=k then

    F_k(n)=k! / product_(p^e||n)e! .               (N3)

This includes prime powers; no squarefree surrogate or changed mask is used. For a fixed k and0<theta<=1/k, take Y=floor(X^theta) and the complete rough Gaussian subfield

    V_(Y,k)(x)=sum_(P^-(n)>Y) d_Y^(*k)(n)
                              g_tau(log(n/x)).

Its terms all have the one sign (-1)^k. Restrict just for a lower bound to products of k distinct primes in (X^(1/k),2X^(1/k)]. These primes exceed Y, and their products lie in[X,2^k X]. The Gaussian has a positive lower bound depending only on fixed tau,k for every such product and x in[X,2X]. The prime number theorem gives >>_k X^(1/k)/log X primes in that interval. Unique factorization and (N3) yield, uniformly on the whole shell,

    |V_(Y,k)(x)| >>_(tau,k) X/(log X)^k.          (N4)

Thus its norm is also >>X/(log X)^k. The same lower bound holds for the absolute value majorant of the complete d_Y^(*k) field. No fixed finite order k permits an absolute coarse estimate with norm exponent gamma<1 in this range. The PNT input is the standard asymptotic checked at [NIST DLMF27.2.3](https://dlmf.nist.gov/27.2#E3); no moving modulus or short-interval theorem is used.

The full signed d_Y^(*k) field also contains nonrough terms. Their interaction can cancel (N4), so this is NOT a lower bound for that full field or for the actual f3/Gaussian detector. The complement is precisely what an improved signed argument must pay. The model resembles earlier semiprime obstructions at a conceptual level but the coefficients here are the exact Newton defect, not DP's E=-2 or the f3 critical rough field.

**W43.4 (opposite regime and missing bridge).** If theta>1/k is fixed, every d_Y^(*k) coefficient begins beyond (Y+1)^k=X^(k theta+o(1)), strictly to the right of the shell. Since |d_Y(n)|<=d_2(n), one has |d_Y^(*k)(n)|<=d_(2k)(n). The elementary divisor count sum_(n<=u)d_(2k)(n)<=u(1+log u)^(2k-1) and Gaussian tail integration give, for every fixed A>0,

    sum_n |d_Y^(*k)(n)| g_tau(log(n/x))
       <<_(A,tau,k,theta) X^(-A),  X<=x<=2X.      (N5)

Indeed the lower logarithmic distance is (k theta-1)log X-O(1); its negative quadratic Gaussian exponent dominates every linear exponent and fixed logarithmic factor. This is completely unconditional. It coexists with (N2) at any hypothetical zero because the defect is not a reciprocal pole detector and because its scale-dependent future tail is not discarded from a continued Mellin integral.

The dichotomy is consequential for the proposed high-ceiling mechanism: at fixed finite order with k theta<=1, absolute treatment fails at every gamma<1; with k theta>1, arbitrary local Gaussian smallness is automatic yet has no zero-exclusion implication. This rules out the particular advertised coarse-loss-budget route, not every nonlinear detector or growing-order scheme. Growing k changes divisor constants, prime counting, combinatorics and Mellin return; it is not covered by these fixed-k statements.

**Weakest honest return left.** A source-exact estimate |1-zeta(s)Q^tr(s)|<1 on the desired region directly excludes zeros there. N1 shows that it must retain zeta T. Alternatively, convergence of the longer actual inverse prefixes to an analytic reciprocal would suffice, but the usual hypothesis sum_(n<=x)mu(n)=O_epsilon(x^(gamma+epsilon)) is exactly a new arithmetic bound. A c=1/6 or1/4 endpoint would respectively need gamma=5/6 or3/4 (with appropriate open-strip buffers), and neither is supplied. Merely squaring D or proving (N5) does not weaken these complete obligations.

For a fixed ordinary character, complete multiplicativity gives d_(Y,chi)(n)=chi(n)d_Y(n) and the same exact truncation identity with L(s,chi). Natural zeros remain. The absolute rough-sector obstruction persists after excluding the finitely many conductor primes; no signed lower bound for a nonreal character is asserted. No Eisenstein-ideal analogue or growing-conductor uniformity is claimed from this rational-integer calculation.

Functional signature: literal truncated Mobius inverse; polynomial reciprocal iteration; formal defect-power cancellation followed by exact tail feedback; first unpaid estimate is the complete signed correction or an actual pointwise reciprocal bound; proved return is the support/rough-sector dichotomy and a failed zero-detection shortcut. This was the serious hard/upstream attempt. It achieved a useful negative result rather than a larger c.

# Explicit endpoint constants for the common fixed filter

This supplement proves the two low-color endpoints used in report.md Section5. It changes no source or cutoff and asserts no estimate for the signed tail. All sums have the closed real endpoint n<=x; x>=1. Fix an ordinary chi modulo q, an unramified prime p, and a fixed integer J>=2. Keep chi's natural zero extension.

Write Q=delta1-p chi(p)delta_p, v_j=Q^(*j), b=Q*chi, and f_t(n)=mu^2(n)t^omega(n)chi(n). Choose

    D>=max(1, sup_n|b(n)|, sup_(y>=1)|sum_(n<=y)b(n)|).

For instance D=p^2 q suffices because b has period pq, mean zero and modulus at most p. All constants below therefore exist for every fixed character, including principal characters.

## 1. Exact one-color endpoint

The coefficient identity f_1=chi*g_1 has

    g_1(r^2)=mu(r)chi(r)^2, and g_1(n)=0 off squares.

Consequently the complete summatory source for Q*f_1=b*g_1 has modulus at most D floor(sqrt x). For v_J*f_1, sum the remaining J-1 filter coefficients at their actual shifted arguments. A term with p^a>x is empty, and every retained term is bounded by

    binom(J-1,a) p^a D sqrt(x/p^a).

Thus, uniformly in every real x>=1,

    |sum_(n<=x)(v_J*f_1)(n)|
       <=D(1+sqrt p)^(J-1)sqrt x.                         (S1)

No endpoint Euler convergence is presumed.

## 2. Exact two-color endpoint

The periodic hyperbola decomposition is exact with Y=sqrt y:

    sum_(n<=y)b^(*2)(n)
      =2 sum_(a<=Y)b(a)sum_(c<=y/a)b(c)
          -(sum_(a<=Y)b(a))^2.

It gives a bound 2D^2 floor(sqrt y)+D^2<=3D^2 sqrt y for every y>=1. The correction f_2=chi^(*2)*g_2 has local polynomial

    1-3 chi(l)^2 l^(-2s)+2 chi(l)^3 l^(-3s).

Coefficientwise absolute values are dominated by the nonnegative local series (1-z^2)^(-3)(1-z^3)^(-2). Hence

    |g_2(n)|<=sum_(a^2 c^3=n)d_3(a)d_2(c),
    sum_(n<=x)|g_2(n)|/sqrt n
       <=zeta(3/2)^2 (1+log(sqrt x))^3.                   (S2)

Indeed the c series converges absolutely and the remaining sum of d_3(a)/a is bounded by the cube of the harmonic sum up to sqrt x. Natural zero factors only reduce the absolute majorant. Combining (S2) with v_J*f_2=b^(*2)*g_2*v_(J-2) yields

    |sum_(n<=x)(v_J*f_2)(n)|
       <=3D^2 zeta(3/2)^2 (1+sqrt p)^(J-2)
                       sqrt x (1+0.5 log x)^3.           (S3)

This accounts for every shifted argument. The logarithm at x/p^a is no larger than the displayed logarithm; shifted arguments below one contribute zero.

## 3. Complete low-chain combination

The exact J=2 combination is L_2=3delta1-3f_1+f_2. Therefore its COMPLETE filtered source satisfies

    |sum_(n<=x)(v_2*L_2)(n)|
      <=3(1+p)^2+3D(1+sqrt p)sqrt x
                +3D^2 zeta(3/2)^2 sqrt x(1+0.5 log x)^3.  (S4)

For every fixed J>=3, report.md equation(4.7) gives the t>=3 colors with sigma=1-1/t>1/2 exactly. Each costs O(x^(1-1/t)) and hence O(x^(1-1/J)). Bounds(S1),(S3) and the finite t=0 source are absorbed into that latter power: the gap above 1/2 is positive and fixed. The finite identity

    L_J=sum_(t=0)^J(-1)^t binom(J+1,t+1)f_t

then proves O_(p,q,J)(x^(1-1/J)) with no epsilon loss. All binomial coefficients and all common-filter shifts remain. This permits equality between gamma and the paid low exponent in the conditional return, but supplies no cancellation in T_(p,J).

The proof uses exact identities, a periodic partial-sum bound and convergent positive series. There is no new numerical helper or claimed empirical verification. It is not uniform in growing J,p or q.

statement:
## 3. Reconstructing the author's unconditional estimate

The actual positive counting object is

    r_G(n)=#{r>G:r^2 divides n}.

It counts every possible square divisor, including products of smaller primes and distinct roots producing the same output. It is not an indicator of one large repeated prime. The identity

    sum_(n<=Y) r_G(n)^2
       =sum_(r,s>G)floor(Y/lcm(r,s)^2) <=16Y/G            (R3)

is valid, uniformly for real G>=1. Setting r=gu,s=gv with (u,v)=1 gives g>G/min(u,v), not a maximum. The g tail contributes at most 2min(u,v)/G; the resulting absolutely convergent double series has bound below eight. Thus the author's constant sixteen is safe. The first moment is at most 2Y/G. Diagonal r=s, nonintegral cutoffs and the strict r>G convention are all included.

At each actual tuple, r is the unique exact gcd(d,e), with d=ru,e=rv and (u,v)=1. Dropping this last condition only in a positive upper bound leaves at most d3(n/r^2)<=d3(n) factorizations. Hence

    |v_G(n)| <<_(eta,B0) n^eta r_G(n),
    sum_(n<=Y)|v_G(n)| <<Y^(1+eta)/G,
    sum_(n<=Y)|v_G(n)|^2 <<Y^(1+2eta)/G.                 (R4)

This proof survives every admissible complex tuple mask. It does not require the actual signed merged coefficient to retain an unsigned number of factorizations. In particular it is not an invalid norm monotonicity assertion.

W24's count gives, for intervals I in [cN,CN] of length h,

    sum_(n in I)r_G(n) <<h/G+min(N^(1/3),N/G^2).         (R5)

The reciprocal count h/G+N/G^2 is valid for all G by reversing n=r^2 l; there are at most CN/G^2 cofactors l and each real root interval has length O(h/(sqrt(N)sqrt(l))). The +1 in each count pays closed endpoints and intervals shorter than one. If G>sqrt(CN), the sum is empty. The N^(1/3) alternative is the usual small-root split. No prime distribution or arithmetic cancellation is used in either estimate.

The smooth enclosing-shell kernel follows by two integrations by parts:

    |K_X(n,m)| <<exp(-c(n+m)/X^(3/2))
                   min(1,[X^6/|n^6-m^6|]^2),           (R6)

with diagonal factor one. After x=Xu, the phase derivative never vanishes on the fixed positive support. Derivatives of the true damping create only fixed polynomials in (n+m)/X^(3/2), absorbed into a weaker exponential. This is uniform over every real x in the shell at the norm level; an x grid is irrelevant.

Split exactly at n<=X. The whole low source costs O(X^(1+eta)/G). For every comparable ordered high pair use a bounded-overlap block n,m~N>=cX, and put H=X^6/N^5. Local annuli, (R5), and the full mass O(N/G) give the author's LG6. The integer row sum O(1+H), inequality 2|v_n v_m|<=|v_n|^2+|v_m|^2 and (R3) give LG7 for the SAME positive absolute pair sum. Thus taking their minimum is lawful. The diagonal at H<1 is paid by the local +1 contribution; off-diagonal distances begin at one, with weights O(H^2).

The author's resulting bound

    exp(-cN/X^(3/2))N^(2eta)
      [X^6/(G^2N^4)+(N/G)(1+min(N^(1/3),H))]

sums to O(X^(2+2eta)/G^2+X^(3/2+3eta)/G). In the last minimum, N^(4/3) and X^6 N^-4 meet at N=X^(9/8), with squared cost X^(3/2)/G. The isolated diagonal uses the actual infinite damping. No high block is discarded.

For far pairs, n~N and X<m<n/2, the gap has size N^6. The shell and cumulative masses from (R4) yield X^12 N^(-10+2eta)/G^2; summing from N~X gives X^(2+2eta)/G^2. The reverse ordered orientation contributes the same bound. The entire low/high interaction is paid by norm triangle, rather than an unjustified scalar cross-term error. Taking square roots and choosing eta after epsilon proves (R1), and finite-measure Cauchy-Schwarz gives L1.

These checks resolve the strongest cheap objections: collisions are counted, local density is not replaced by a support indicator, H<1 retains its diagonal, both far orientations survive, arbitrary frozen phases cause no change, and no polynomial upper bound on G was inserted.

### The actual close-point Gram and its normalization

For n in[X,2X], set s=log(n/X), epsilon=log(1+1/n),
v_s(u)=g_tau(s-u) on0<=u<=log2. The literal physical Gram G22 is
<v_s,v_t>; every coefficient is the actual f3(n), including all powers.
The Schur pivot of v_(s+epsilon) against v_s is

    p_s(epsilon)=||v_(s+epsilon)||^2
           -|<v_s,v_(s+epsilon)>|^2/||v_s||^2
      =epsilon^2 [||v_s'||^2
           -|<v_s,v_s'>|^2/||v_s||^2]+O_tau(epsilon^3).  (D48.1)

Taylor expansion is uniform on the compact s-range, and
v_s'/v_s=-(s-u)/tau is nonconstant on a positive-length interval.
The bracket is ||v_s||^2 Var_(v_s^2)(u)/tau^2>0,
continuous with a positive compact minimum. Hence p_s~n^-2
uniformly. The Gram's largest eigenvalue is bounded above/below,
so its condition number is comparable to n^2. This is a native
kernel statement, not a f3 energy lower bound. Whitening the Gram
can amplify a unit coefficient error by order n.

The source-adapted alternative keeps the cheap difference mode
explicit and never inverts the Gram. This changes S48's original
orthogonal-prime-word proposal after source intake; the seed remains
unaltered and the salvage is attributed to this development.

## 5. What is new here, what was reused, and the next live estimate

The main gain in this bounded attack is S10--S13: a direct estimate for
an ACTUAL f3 scalar sector that the existing W36 result explicitly did
not cover. It comes with a uniform modified-coefficient proof, all
prime powers, all common divisors, the diagonal, the entire tail,
both heights, and the full signed complement. It supplies no complete
moment exponent. Its numerical threshold resembles W36 because both
ultimately sum a common-factor weight of degree -2beta, but the
underlying arithmetic sources and masks are different.

S17--S21 add an exact prime-switch covariance and a quantitative
P^(1-3beta) source-change error, before making any positive estimate.
This provides a usable bound for such changes inside the actual
Möbius expansion, not a claim that its unsolved common component is
smaller. The exact shifted target S15 is preferable to treating the
r=1 self-copy in S22 as a solution.

The following components are reused or elementary adaptations:

- MG9--16 already provide the buffered Mertens/coprimality mechanism
  and Möbius extraction of an original-source gcd. S4 proves the
  different all-prime-power f_r multiplier required here; no new
  general Möbius-inversion principle is claimed.
- [private research revision] GC1--GC20 and its independent review already establish the
  fixed f3 detector, its original-cell comparison and complete
  zero-exclusion return. Their inverse kernels and all-dyad
  equivalence are imported, not rederived as a new result.
- W36/R36.4 pays an aggregate shared-prime overlap in FOUR ORIGINAL
  squarefree factors. S10 is not inferred by restricting that signed
  estimate. It is proved directly for the TWO full f3 integers.
- W35's fixed-order Gaussian Poisson mechanism supplies S28. The

- The attempt index and its [private research revision]--52/early/late subdivisions were

  priority in the external literature is asserted.

The first unpaid calculation is specific. For a chosen gamma and
theta satisfying S13, estimate the ENTIRE signed S15 on all large
dyadic X at exponent 2gamma. In the difficult part, g can be 1,
a and h are both comparable to X, and a(a+h) has a large radical.
Neither the periodic average in d, the high-gcd bound, nor the

weight, and the complete sum of shifts. Replacing the signs by a
character, independent random variables or a positive majorant would
change this arithmetic problem.

This is a real remaining arithmetic estimate, not a missing source-
comparison or analytic-tail condition. The near gamma=.87449 target
and the larger gamma=5/6 and 3/4 targets remain open.

Retain OpenAI's initial framework, Hailey Collet's PR9/QRH source architecture, Akash Levy's weighted-numerator contribution, and Zhongpai Gao's AI-assisted local construction/bridges; later QRH refinements remain separately attributed. Keep PR15 `LICENSE`, `NOTICE.md`, `UPSTREAM_NOTICE.md`. The pinned admission contract in the controller's brief is a separate external delivery condition, not a mathematical inference or an instruction to run formalization. The controller should assemble one immutable new written-proof snapshot only after the endpoint decision, with this selection map as evidence.

statement:
# [private research revision]: independent coprime-cell transfer review



## Verdict and current checkpoint

The proposed transfer is valid. The Euler identity, both Dirichlet
inverses, the exact one-short contraction, the full untruncated cutoff
error, and the required all-dyad norm equivalence are proved below.
The norm argument compares the two fixed fields before inserting any
dyad-dependent cutoff. It includes the entire region x/n < 1.

For fixed tau > 0 and each fixed gamma > 1/2, the following statements
are equivalent, with constants allowed to depend on tau, gamma and
epsilon:

1. For every epsilon > 0, on every sufficiently large dyadic X,

       integral_X^(2X) |G_tau(x)|^2 dx/x
           << X^(2 gamma + epsilon).

2. With Y_X = floor(X^.495), for every epsilon > 0, on every
   sufficiently large dyadic X,

       integral_X^(2X) |R_{6,Y_X}(x)|^2 dx/x
           << X^(2 gamma + epsilon).

This permits the single original masked coprime cell to
replace the collection of cross-gcd cells as the remaining arithmetic
target. It uses neither positivity of a signed subfamily nor a bound
deduced by deleting terms from a signed sum. It proves no estimate at
any new gamma. The accepted zero-free constant remains
c0 = 0.125113352960035869... .

Two independently proved extensions are separated in Section 7:
exact-power equivalence at gamma > 1/2, and the all-epsilon formulation
at gamma = 1/2. The boundary without epsilon is not proved.

Completed: independent proofs and exact finite coefficient checks.
Remaining: prove the signed correlation estimate in Section 8 at a
gamma < 1-c0; optionally compare this review with a frozen author
source through the controller. Next mathematical action: attack that
specific signed moment, retaining its full kernel and all dyads.

## 1. Definitions and absolute rearrangements

Fix tau > 0 throughout. For x > 0, put

    g_tau(v) = (2 pi tau)^(-1/2) exp(-v^2/(2 tau)),
    b(l) = (-1)^(l+1),
    S_tau(y) = sum_{l >= 1} b(l) g_tau(log(l/y)),
    A(n) = mu(n) - 2 1_{2|n} mu(n/2),
    G_tau(x) = sum_{n >= 1} A(n) g_tau(log(n/x)).

For every integer Y >= 1, the original cell under review is exactly

    R_{6,Y}(x) = sum_{d,e > Y; (d,e)=1; (de,6)=1}
                    mu(d) mu(e) S_tau(x/(de)).             (1.1)

The lower cuts are strict, the sum is over ordered pairs, and the
Möbius coefficients are not replaced by nonzero surrogates.

Write uniquely

    n = 2^a 3^b q,       (q,6)=1,
    r(n) = rad(q),
    beta(a) = 1 if a=0, and -1 if a>=1.

Use rad(1)=1 and mu(1)=1. The proposed fixed field is

    f_3(n) = mu(rad(n/3^{v_3(n)}))
           = beta(a) mu(rad(q)),
    F_6(x) = sum_{n >= 1} f_3(n) g_tau(log(n/x)).           (1.2)

In particular f_3(n) is always +1 or -1, including prime powers.
The exponent v_3(n) is the exact nonnegative 3-adic valuation.

All label rearrangements below are absolutely justified before
cancellation. The uncut (d,e,l) sum is dominated by

    sum_{n >= 1} d_3(n) g_tau(log(n/x)) < infinity.

For example, for every c > 1,

    g_tau(log(n/x)) <= C_{c,tau} x^c n^(-c),
    C_{c,tau} = (2 pi tau)^(-1/2) exp(tau c^2/2),

and sum d_3(n)n^(-c)=zeta(c)^3 is finite. This also proves local
uniform convergence. No product or height truncation is needed here.

## 2. The exact uncut field and the two inverse kernels

### 2.1 Uncut coprime identity

For Re(s)>1, the uncut field's coefficient Dirichlet series is

    eta(s) product_{p>=5}(1-2p^(-s)),
    eta(s) = sum_{l>=1} b(l)l^(-s)
           = (1-2^(1-s)) zeta(s).                         (2.1)

At each prime p>=5, coprimality allows exactly three squarefree
allocations to (d,e): neither, d only, or e only. Their local sum is
1-p^(-s)-p^(-s). Primes 2 and 3 are forbidden in both d and e.
This preserves the actual ordered-pair multiplicity 2.

The local Dirichlet factors of f_3 are

    p=2:    (1-2z)/(1-z),
    p=3:    1/(1-z),
    p>=5:   (1-2z)/(1-z),                  z=p^(-s).

These are exactly the local factors in (2.1). Therefore

    F_6(x) = sum_{d,e>=1; (d,e)=1; (de,6)=1}
                 mu(d)mu(e)S_tau(x/(de)).                 (2.2)

Equation (2.1) is an absolutely convergent identity on Re(s)>1.
It is not an assertion that its first-order Euler product converges
absolutely throughout Re(s)>1/2.

### 2.2 Kernel coefficients and convergence

Let K_6(s)=sum k_6(n)n^(-s), with local factors

    p=2,3:  (1-z)^2,
    p>=5:   (1-z)^2/(1-2z)
           = 1 + z^2/(1-2z)
           = 1 + sum_{j>=2} 2^(j-2) z^j.                 (2.3)

Its formal Dirichlet inverse J_6(s)=sum j_6(n)n^(-s) has

    p=2,3:  (1-z)^(-2) = sum_{j>=0}(j+1)z^j,
    p>=5:   (1-2z)/(1-z)^2
           = 1 - z^2/(1-z)^2
           = 1 - sum_{j>=2}(j-1)z^j.                    (2.4)

In particular the p>=5 inverse has zero coefficient at p, and all
its coefficients at p^j, j>=2, are negative; they are not alternating.

Fix sigma>1/2 and set r_p=p^(-sigma). Since

    2 r_p <= 2*5^(-sigma) < 2/sqrt(5) < 1,

all geometric sums in (2.3) converge absolutely. Their exact absolute
Dirichlet norms are

    sum_n |k_6(n)| n^(-sigma)
      = (1+r_2)^2 (1+r_3)^2
          product_{p>=5} (1 + r_p^2/(1-2r_p)) < infinity, (2.5)

    sum_n |j_6(n)| n^(-sigma)
      = (1-r_2)^(-2) (1-r_3)^(-2)
          product_{p>=5} (1 + r_p^2/(1-r_p)^2) < infinity.(2.6)

The denominators are bounded away from zero at this fixed sigma,
and sum_p p^(-2sigma)<infinity. These facts prove convergence of
the positive products, hence of the absolute coefficient sums.

The candidate local poles 1-2p^(-s)=0 have

    Re(s) = log(2)/log(p) <= log(2)/log(5)
          = 0.4306765580... < 1/2.                       (2.7)

The inverse's possible local zeros have exactly those real parts.
The factors 1-p^(-s) have no zeros at positive real part. Thus there
are no omitted local zeros or poles in Re(s)>1/2. Normal convergence
of the products, or the absolutely convergent identity K_6 J_6=1,
also rules out an infinite-product zero there. The factor at 2 has
no denominator 1-2*2^(-s): that factor was common to G and F and
has been cancelled as a coefficient identity on Re(s)>1.

The choice to exclude 3 matters for the advertised threshold. If
3 were allowed, its corresponding geometric factor would have a
pole at log(2)/log(3)=0.6309297535... . This objection does not
apply to the actual (de,6)=1 cell.

At sigma=1/2 the products (2.5)--(2.6) do not converge absolutely:
their logarithms have a divergent prime harmonic contribution.
No endpoint absolute-convergence claim is made.

### 2.3 Fixed-field convolution identities

The coefficient series for A is

    sum A(n)n^(-s) = (1-2^(1-s))/zeta(s),   Re(s)>1.

Multiplying the local factors in (2.1)--(2.4) gives the exact
Dirichlet convolution identities

    A = k_6 * f_3,                 f_3 = j_6 * A,
    k_6 * j_6 = delta_1.                                  (2.8)

Consequently, for every x>0,

    G_tau(x) = sum_{m>=1} k_6(m) F_6(x/m),
    F_6(x)   = sum_{m>=1} j_6(m) G_tau(x/m).               (2.9)

These are genuine field identities, not only formal Mellin ratios.
Indeed |f_3(n)|=1 and |A(n)|<=3. For c>1, either rearranged
double sum is bounded by a constant times

    x^c (sum_m |a(m)|m^(-c)) (sum_n n^(-c)) < infinity,

where a is k_6 or j_6. This proves pointwise and local uniform
absolute convergence of the rearrangement.

## 3. Exact long-cut completion, including endpoints

For integer Y>=1 define the one-short and both-short fields

    U_Y(x) = sum_{d<=Y,e>=1; (d,e)=1; (de,6)=1}
                   mu(d)mu(e) S_tau(x/(de)),
    B_Y(x) = sum_{d,e<=Y; (d,e)=1; (de,6)=1}
                   mu(d)mu(e) S_tau(x/(de)).              (3.1)

By inclusion-exclusion of the two short conditions and symmetry,

    F_6 - R_{6,Y} = 2 U_Y - B_Y.                         (3.2)

To compute U_Y's n-th coefficient, fix n=2^a3^bq, (q,6)=1.
A contributing d must be a squarefree divisor of q; otherwise its
Möbius coefficient is zero or it is prohibited by the 6-mask.
Every allowed e is odd. Thus

    b(n/(de)) = beta(a)

for every summand: the alternating sign does not depend on e, d,
the positive 2-adic exponent a, or the 3-adic exponent b.
For fixed squarefree d|q, the inner e-sum is

    sum_{e|q/d; (e,d)=1} mu(e)
      = product_{p|q; p does not divide d} (1-1)
      = 1_{rad(q)|d}.                                    (3.3)

The presence of powers p^j in q changes none of this. Möbius zeros
delete nonsquarefree e; each prime of q absent from d remains an
available squarefree e-prime, and each prime in d is forbidden in e.
Since d itself is squarefree and divides q, rad(q)|d forces
d=rad(q). Therefore

    U_Y(x) = sum_{n>=1} f_3(n) 1_{r(n)<=Y}
                                  g_tau(log(n/x)).       (3.4)

This is the claimed small-radical field, with coefficient exactly
f_3(n), not its square, absolute value or a different parity sign.

Endpoint checks:

- d=Y belongs to the short side; d>Y belongs to the original long
  side. Equation (3.4) uses r(n)<=Y with that same convention.
- d=e=1 is present in B_Y for every Y>=1 and is handled by
  inclusion-exclusion once, rather than removed or double counted.
- For q=1, r(n)=1. The only possible d,e are 1,1, so U_Y=B_Y=F_6
  at that coefficient and the long-pair coefficient is zero.
- For q a power of one prime p>Y, no two coprime long divisors
  can occur. In this case U_Y has zero coefficient, B_Y has
  coefficient beta(a), and f_3(n)=-beta(a), again giving zero.
- Positive powers of 3 do not affect f_3; positive powers of 2
  give the single minus sign beta(a)=-1, not (-1)^a.

## 4. The untruncated completion error

### 4.1 Small-radical bound

For every delta>0,

    C_delta := sum_{n>=1} n^(-delta)/r(n)
      = (1-2^(-delta))^(-1)(1-3^(-delta))^(-1)
          product_{p>=5}
             (1 + p^(-1-delta)/(1-p^(-delta)))
      < infinity.                                       (4.1)

For sufficiently large p the denominator is at least 1/2, so the
prime contribution is O_delta(p^(-1-delta)), a summable series.
The finitely many remaining factors are finite and positive.
This proves (4.1) without any uniformity as delta tends to zero.

Using 1_{r(n)<=Y}<=Y/r(n) and the exact Gaussian supremum,

    g_tau(log(n/x)) <= C_{delta,tau} x^delta n^(-delta),

gives, uniformly for every x>0 and every integer Y>=1,

    |U_Y(x)| <= C_{delta,tau} C_delta Y x^delta.           (4.2)

This includes all n, however large relative to x, and all powers
of 2 or 3. There is no finite-height replacement hidden in (4.2).

### 4.2 Both-short bound under the fixed pair mask

Extend h(t)=g_tau(log t) for t>0 by h(t)=0 for t<=0.
The Gaussian beats every power at both t=0 and t=infinity after
any fixed number of derivatives, so h is Schwartz and flat at zero.
For Fourier transform hhat(xi)=integral_R h(t)exp(-2 pi i t xi)dt,
Poisson summation with the alternating character gives

    S_tau(y) = -y sum_{k in Z} hhat(y(k+1/2)).             (4.3)

There is no zero frequency. For each fixed M>1, Schwartz decay
and summability of |k+1/2|^(-M) imply

    |S_tau(y)| <= C_{M,tau} y^(1-M),       y>=1.

Equivalently, for each fixed A>0,

    |S_tau(y)| <= C_{A,tau} y^(-A),        y>=1.           (4.4)

Now take X>=1, x in [X,2X], theta=.495 and
Y=Y_X=floor(X^theta). Then

    x/(de) >= X/Y^2 >= X^(.01) >= 1

for d,e<=Y. Taking absolute values only after completing each
alternating l-sum yields

    |B_Y(x)| <= C_{A,tau} Y^2 (X/Y^2)^(-A)
             <= C_{A,tau} X^(.99-.01 A).                 (4.5)

The pair mask (d,e)=1, (de,6)=1 and the Möbius signs are fixed
independently of l, so this argument is valid under that mask.
It does not assert inheritance under an arbitrary l-dependent mask.
For any prescribed N>0, choose A>=100(N+.99); then

    sup_{X<=x<=2X}|B_{Y_X}(x)| <<_{N,tau} X^(-N).        (4.6)

### 4.3 Error in the required norm

For delta>0 and N>0, equations (3.2), (4.2) and (4.6) give

    sup_{X<=x<=2X}|F_6(x)-R_{6,Y_X}(x)|
       <<_{delta,N,tau} X^(.495+delta) + X^(-N).         (4.7)

The same estimate holds for the L2(dx/x) norm on that shell, up
to the fixed factor sqrt(log 2). For every gamma>=1/2, choose
0<delta<gamma-.495. The error is then O(X^rho) for a fixed
rho=.495+delta<gamma. No estimate for R at a transported or
nonintegral cutoff is needed.

## 5. A general dyadic convolution lemma with its left-tail input

For a real alpha and a locally square-integrable function H on
(0,infinity), define

    D_H(T) = (integral_T^(2T)|H(x)|^2 dx/x)^(1/2),
    ||H||_{D_alpha} = sup_{T>0} T^(-alpha) D_H(T).         (5.1)

**Lemma.** Suppose ||H||_{D_alpha}<infinity and

    ||a||_{1,alpha} = sum_{m>=1}|a(m)|m^(-alpha)<infinity.

Then T_a H = sum_m a(m)H(./m) converges in L2 on every compact
subinterval of (0,infinity), and

    ||T_a H||_{D_alpha}
        <= ||a||_{1,alpha} ||H||_{D_alpha}.               (5.2)

If a*b=delta_1 and both weighted coefficient norms are finite,
T_a and T_b are mutually inverse bounded operators on this space.

*Proof.* The change of variable u=x/m gives exactly

    ||H(./m)||_{L2([T,2T],dx/x)} = D_H(T/m)
         <= ||H||_{D_alpha} T^alpha m^(-alpha).

Minkowski's inequality for finite partial sums gives (5.2).
The same estimate applied to tails proves convergence in shell L2,
hence locally in L2. For the inverse assertion, the double series
is absolutely summable in this norm because

    sum_{m,n}|a(m)b(n)|(mn)^(-alpha)
       = ||a||_{1,alpha}||b||_{1,alpha}<infinity.

Its reordering is therefore justified and gives T_b T_a=T_delta_1.
The proof includes every m>T and all of its arguments T/m<1. QED.

### 5.1 From large dyadic shells to all positive scales

Suppose alpha>0, H is locally square-integrable, and

    D_H(2^j) <= C 2^(j alpha)

for all sufficiently large integers j. This does not by itself
control the left tail. Assume additionally that for each fixed N>0,

    |H(x)| <= C_N x^N,                  0<x<=1.          (5.3)

Then ||H||_{D_alpha}<infinity. To see this, first absorb the finite
number of intermediate shells by local square integrability. If
2^j<=T<2^(j+1), the shell [T,2T] lies in the union of the two
dyadic shells starting at 2^j and 2^(j+1). Hence, for T>=1,

    D_H(T)^2 <= C^2(2^(2j alpha)+2^(2(j+1)alpha))
             <= C^2(1+2^(2alpha)) T^(2alpha).             (5.4)

For T<=1/2 choose N>=alpha in (5.3) and integrate x^(2N)
over [T,2T]. This gives D_H(T)<<T^N<<T^alpha. Compact scales
1/2<T<1 cause no problem. This proves the claim and accounts for
both non-dyadic shifts and the entire left tail.

### 5.2 The actual left tails of both fixed fields

Both fields satisfy the stronger uniform bound

    |F_6(x)| + |G_tau(x)|
      <= C_tau exp(-(log x)^2/(2 tau)),       0<x<=1.     (5.5)

Indeed log n>=0, -log x>=0, and

    (log n-log x)^2 >= (log n)^2+(log x)^2.

Use |f_3(n)|=1, |A(n)|<=3 and the finite sum
sum_n exp(-(log n)^2/(2 tau)). For every fixed N>0,

    exp(-(log x)^2/(2 tau))
       <= exp(tau N^2/2) x^N,              0<x<=1,

so (5.3) follows. This is an independently verified input for
each fixed field; no left-tail estimate for a dyad-varying R is
assumed or used.

## 6. Proof of the requested all-dyad equivalence

Fix gamma>1/2 and epsilon>0. Suppose the G estimate in the
checkpoint holds. Put alpha=gamma+epsilon/2. Taking its square
root gives D_G(2^j)<<2^(j alpha) for all sufficiently large j.
Equations (5.3)--(5.5) imply ||G||_{D_alpha}<infinity.
The inverse coefficient estimate (2.6), the identity (2.9), and
the lemma imply

    ||F_6||_{D_alpha}
       <= ||j_6||_{1,alpha}||G||_{D_alpha}<infinity.       (6.1)

Therefore D_F(X)<<X^(gamma+epsilon/2) on every dyadic X>=1.
Choose any fixed delta with 0<delta<gamma-.495 in (4.7).
The triangle inequality then gives

    D_{R_{6,Y_X}}(X)
       <= D_F(X)+O(X^(.495+delta))
       << X^(gamma+epsilon/2),                           (6.2)

which squares to the requested exponent 2gamma+epsilon.

Conversely assume the R estimate for every epsilon>0 at its
own frozen cutoff Y_X on each dyadic X. Equation (4.7) gives
the F estimate at the same exponent and the same dyadic X.
The fixed field F has the left tail (5.5), so it belongs to
D_alpha. Apply the lemma with k_6, whose norm is finite by
(2.5), and the other identity in (2.9). This proves the G
estimate at exponent 2gamma+epsilon.

Since epsilon>0 was arbitrary, the all-epsilon statements are
equivalent. No constant is asserted to be uniform as epsilon
tends to zero. Thresholds for sufficiently large dyads may depend
on epsilon; the finite initial range is absorbed exactly as in
Section 5.1.

This proof never applies K_6 or J_6 to the family
x -> R_{6,floor(X^.495)}(x). Such an application would transport
x while retaining the wrong short cutoff. Instead, the two uses
of (4.7) occur only on their original dyads; the convolution acts
solely on fixed F_6 and G_tau. The suspected cutoff mismatch is
therefore absent, rather than silently estimated away.

## 7. Independently proved extensions and precise endpoint limits

**Extension A: exact-power equivalence.** For every fixed gamma>1/2,

    D_G(X)<<X^gamma on all sufficiently large dyadic X

if and only if

    D_{R_{6,Y_X}}(X)<<X^gamma
          on all sufficiently large dyadic X.            (7.1)

Use alpha=gamma in the same proof, since both coefficient norms
are finite there; choose delta<gamma-.495. This does not require
an epsilon loss in the norm transfer itself.

**Extension B: the all-epsilon endpoint.** The checkpoint's
all-epsilon equivalence also holds for gamma=1/2. For each
epsilon>0 take alpha=1/2+epsilon/2>1/2, where both coefficient
norms converge, and choose a fixed 0<delta<.005 for the cutoff
error. The argument above is then unchanged.

**Limit.** Neither absolute coefficient norm converges at exactly
alpha=1/2, so this proof gives no exact O(X^(1/2)) equivalence.
It also gives no transfer at gamma<1/2 through these weighted
absolute sums. Those statements would require additional input;
their failure is not proved here.

The same completion proof would work for a fixed cutoff exponent
0<theta<1/2, replacing .495 by theta, because X/Y^2 grows as
X^(1-2theta) and delta can be chosen below gamma-theta.
This is a generalization of the proof, not a change to the actual
frozen cutoff used in the stated result.

## 8. Exact residual signed correlation and zero-exclusion return

There is now a particularly explicit equivalent arithmetic target.
For m,n>=1 and dyadic X>=1 put

    W_{tau,X}(m,n)
      = integral_X^(2X)
          g_tau(log(m/x))g_tau(log(n/x)) dx/x
      = (2 pi tau)^(-1) exp(-(log(m/n))^2/(4 tau))
          * integral_{log X}^{log(2X)}
               exp(-(t-(log m+log n)/2)^2/tau) dt.        (8.1)

This weight is real, strictly positive and retains the exact
finite shell endpoints. Absolute summability permits expansion:

    integral_X^(2X)|F_6(x)|^2 dx/x
      = sum_{m,n>=1} f_3(m)f_3(n) W_{tau,X}(m,n).         (8.2)

For clarity, that sign is

    f_3(m)f_3(n)
       = (-1)^[omega(m/3^{v_3(m)})+omega(n/3^{v_3(n)})],

where omega counts distinct prime factors and omega(1)=0.
Every positive prime power other than a power of 3 contributes
one minus sign, irrespective of its exponent. There is no
random-sign assumption and no averaging over tau.

The diagonal is O_tau(X). One direct proof uses unimodality to
bound, for x>=1,

    sum_n exp(-(log(n/x))^2/tau)
       <= 2 + integral_0^infinity exp(-(log(t/x))^2/tau)dt
       = 2 + x sqrt(pi tau) exp(tau/4).

Multiplying by (2 pi tau)^(-1) and integrating dx/x gives
sum_n W_{tau,X}(n,n)<<_tau X.

Consequently, for gamma>=1/2, the exact remaining demand can
equivalently be written as the one-sided signed estimate

    sum_{m != n} f_3(m)f_3(n) W_{tau,X}(m,n)
       <= C_{epsilon,tau,gamma} X^(2 gamma+epsilon)       (8.3)

on every sufficiently large dyadic X, for every epsilon>0.
The off-diagonal is real and bounded below by minus the diagonal,
since the complete moment is nonnegative. No absolute value
inside the sum, sign deletion, or restriction to a favorable
subfamily is permissible. The absolute double sum is in general
only O_tau(X^2), which does not supply a new exponent.

Combining a future proof of (8.3) at 1/2<=gamma<1 with the fixed
G_tau Mellin return in G1--G3 of `[restricted mathematical source]` would
exclude zeta zeros in gamma<Re(s)<1. A first improvement needs
gamma<1-c0. The present transfer supplies no such moment estimate,
so it does not increase the accepted constant or verify a theorem
whose main arithmetic input remains open.

The benefit proved here is structural: the full signed detector
is equivalent, above the stated threshold, to one original
coprime cell and then to the explicit bounded-coefficient field
f_3. The arithmetic difficulty is retained in (8.3). No novelty
relative to the external literature is claimed.

## 9. Verification record and limitations

An exact-integer calculation evaluated all allowed divisors d,e
for every 1<=n<=1200 and

    Y in {1,2,4,5,6,7,10,24,35}.

All 10,800 (n,Y) cases passed the following three equalities:

    uncut coefficient = f_3(n),
    one-short coefficient = f_3(n) 1_{r(n)<=Y},
    uncut minus long coefficient = 2*one-short - both-short.

The calculation used actual Möbius zeros, gcd(d,e)=1, gcd(de,6)=1,
d*e dividing n, and the original parity sign b(n/(de)). It included
prime powers, smooth numbers and cutoff equalities. It also
reported 2/sqrt(5)=0.8944271909999159 and the two pole abscissae
in Section 2. This finite check is diagnostic support for the
algebra; the proofs are the arbitrary-n arguments above.

The stronger objections have been resolved as follows:

- The smallest allowed prime is 5, so the geometric expansion
  converges at every sigma>1/2. Prime 3 is genuinely excluded.
- The inverse factors and their possible zeros were checked
  explicitly, rather than assuming formal invertibility supplies
  an absolutely summable inverse.
- The small-radical estimate includes the entire infinite field.
- The alternating sum is completed before bounding B_Y, and
  its fixed pair mask is independent of the alternating index.
- The norm proof includes non-dyadic arguments and x/m<1.
- Dyad-dependent cutoffs are never transported by convolution.
- The final arithmetic moment remains signed and unproved.

No repository integration, shared-state mutation, tracker change,
Git mutation, external-provider contact, or author-source comparison
was performed by this lane. Only this assigned artifact was written.

## 7. Paired q=2,3 conditioning: exact scope, all heights and two heights

Define the entire normalized factors

    B_q(s)=(1-q^(1-s))/(s-1),   B_q(1)=log q.

Their nonreal zero lattices have no common point: equality of the phases would
give a nontrivial equality between integer powers of 2 and 3. This observation
alone has N28 ancestry. The candidate additionally pays a coarse effective
conditioning bound sufficient for Gaussian height cutoffs.

Here is an independent verification of its constants. For t>=1 let
delta=max_(q=2,3)|1-e^(-it log q)| and choose nearest nonnegative integers m,n
to t log2/(2pi), t log3/(2pi). Let the two phase errors be e_2,e_3. The sine
chord bound on [-pi,pi] gives |e_q|<=pi delta/2. If delta<1/2, m,n cannot both
be zero: otherwise t log3<=pi/4<log3. Unique factorization gives 3^m!=2^n, and
the integral of 1/u between these distinct integers implies

    |m log3-n log2| >= 1/max(3^m,2^n)
       >=3^(-1/2)exp(-t log2 log3/(2pi)).

The phase-error identity gives the upper bound delta log6/4 for the same
quantity. Thus delta>=4 exp(-t log2 log3/(2pi))/(sqrt3 log6)>=e^(-t)/2.
If delta>=1/2 the last inequality is immediate. Dividing by t proves
max_q|B_q(1+it)|>=e^(-t)/(2t). Negative t follow by conjugation.
For |t|<=1, the chord bound instead gives
|B_q(1+it)|>=2 log q/pi; in particular B_2>1/4 and B_3>1/2 in modulus.
Consequently, for T>=1 and |t|<=T,

    S(t)=|B_2(1+it)|^2+|B_3(1+it)|^2
       >=e^(-2T)/[4(1+T)^2].                             (R15)

For a measurable common V(t), define W_q(t)=B_q(1+it)V(t). Pointwise,

    V(t)=sum_(q=2,3) m_q(t)W_q(t),
    m_q(t)=conjugate(B_q(1+it))/S(t),
    |V(t)|^2<=S(t)^(-1)sum_q|W_q(t)|^2.                  (R16)

On [-T,T] this recovery has L2 operator norm at most 2(1+T)e^T. On the whole
line R15's proof gives S(t)^(-1)<=4(1+|t|)^2e^(2|t|). For tau>tau'>0 put
Delta=tau-tau'. Then (1+u)^2<=e^(2u) and 4u-Delta u^2<=4/Delta imply
the explicit bound

    integral_R |e^(tau(1+it)^2/2)V(t)|^2 dt
      <=4 exp(Delta+4/Delta) sum_(q=2,3)
            integral_R |e^(tau'(1+it)^2/2)W_q(t)|^2 dt.  (R17)

This independently proves B17 with all heights paid. Extended integrals are
allowed; when the right side is finite it gives the asserted finite left side.
The constant depends on the positive Gaussian-width gap. It is not a bound
with tau'=tau. Indeed S(t)<=8/t^2 for nonzero t; choosing V supported in
[T,T+1] disproves an equal-width inequality with a fixed constant for arbitrary
V as T tends to infinity. This is a useful precise limit of the stated lemma.

At T=D sqrt(log X), fixed D, the recovery coefficient bound and the product of
two such bounds are X^o(1). This observation pays multiplier coefficients; it
does not prove an original physical Gaussian energy comparison.

To display the missing distinction, on a finite height interval let
P(x)=integral a(x,t)V(t)dt and K(t,t')=integral a(x,t)conjugate(a(x,t'))dnu(x),
under hypotheses allowing the indicated finite integrals. Substitution of R16
gives the exact expansion

    ||P||^2=sum_(q,r in {2,3}) integral integral
       K(t,t') m_q(t) conjugate(m_r(t'))
       W_q(t) conjugate(W_r(t')) dt dt'.                 (R18)

There are four ordered grid pairs and two independent heights. Neither R15 nor
R17 replaces K(t,t') by its diagonal. A local physical norm, arithmetic mask,
or limiting whole-height version of this local formula needs its own valid
comparison and tail theorem. The candidate expressly reserves these steps.

The exact actual-source common-signal interface is also worth recording. For
the SAME finite coefficient list c_n in the two grids, put A(s)=sum c_n n^(-s).
Then R4 gives

    Mellin(sum c_n w_(q,n))(s)=B_q(s)V(s),
    V(s)=((s-1)zeta(s)/s)A(s).                            (R19)

Thus the paired recovery really can apply to a common arithmetic source, not
just an arbitrary abstract vector. However independently fitted lists give
A_2 and A_3, hence generally different V_2 and V_3. R16 cannot be applied to
them as a common V without a new identity. Moreover the recovered expression
in R19 is not automatically in the required unweighted half-plane Hardy space
or the original physical source class: the multiplier contains s-1, and the
boundary inverse uses conjugation. B17 establishes only the stated weighted
line norm. These restrictions are necessary to interpret simultaneous
detectors accurately.

## 4. Protected audit S25: decimation with all induced interactions

The high-reach seed proposes integrating out a prime block in a signed squarefree gas while keeping the cutoff. The correct object can be constructed exactly; a positive or independent-product replacement cannot be imported.

Fix a finite block B of distinct primes and P_B=product_(p in B)p. Let a(n)=mu(n)chi(n), with its actual zeros. Define

    H_B(t)=sum_(d|P_B,d<=t)a(d),    H_B(t)=0 if t<1.

Every squarefree n factors uniquely as d m, where d|P_B and (m,P_B)=1. These factors are coprime, so a(dm)=a(d)a(m), including zero cases. Consequently for every real X>=1,

    M_chi(X)=sum_(m<=X,(m,P_B)=1)a(m)H_B(X/m).       (R10)

All d subsets and all remaining cofactors are present. This is an exact finite decimation, not an independence approximation. If B changes with X the identity still holds separately at each X; any quantitative constants and full return then have to be uniform in that changing block.

For two primes p<r, t>=1,

    H_{p,r}(t)=1-chi(p)1_(t>=p)-chi(r)1_(t>=r)
                   +chi(p)chi(r)1_(t>=pr).

Let h_p(t)=1-chi(p)1_(t>=p). The exact induced two-prime interaction is

    H_{p,r}(t)-h_p(t)h_r(t)
        =-chi(p)chi(r)1_(r<=t<pr).                  (R11)

The upper endpoint is STRICT: at t=pr the pair first becomes admissible and the defect vanishes. Substituting t=X/m gives the full error from the naive product:

    E_{p,r}(X)
      :=sum_(m<=X,(m,pr)=1)a(m)[H_{p,r}(X/m)-h_p(X/m)h_r(X/m)]
       =-chi(p)chi(r)
          sum_(X/(pr)<m<=X/r,(m,pr)=1)mu(m)chi(m).   (R12)

Natural q zeros remain in a and in the outer prime factors. A ramified p or r annihilates this interaction; a proof may not replace that zero by a unit phase. Equation(R12) retains its complex sign and every integer endpoint. In particular no independent averaging of the two prime occupations produces this expression automatically.

The actual principal p=2,r=3 example is decisive for one proposed norm:

    H_{2,3}(t)=1 on[1,2), 0 on[2,3),
               -1 on[3,6), 0 on[6,infinity).

Thus the signed marginal changes sign and vanishes on open intervals. There is no finite, everywhere-defined logarithmic effective potential -log H_{2,3} on this real cutoff domain, nor an everywhere-positive Gibbs interpretation. This does not forbid keeping the unnormalized polynomial, using complex fugacity on a chosen nonzero domain, or retaining exact zero states.

For this example the coefficientwise absolute price of the discarded interaction is

    sum_(X/6<m<=X/3,(m,6)=1)mu(m)^2
       = X/(2 pi^2)+O(sqrt X).                       (R13)

To derive the constant, insert mu(n)^2=sum_(d^2|n)mu(d) and count units modulo6. The q=6 squarefree density is

    d_6=(phi(6)/6)product_(p not dividing6)(1-p^-2)
       =3/pi^2.

The interval length is X/6. The O(sqrt X) error follows by summing O(1) counting errors for d<=sqrt X and the convergent d^-2 tail. This is the same elementary density mechanism as G93, not a new prime-distribution input.

Equation(R13) disproves a subunit bound for THAT absolute interaction price. It does NOT lower-bound the signed interval in(R12), M(X), or every possible decimation norm. Fixed primes are essential to this linear asymptotic; growing blocks/primes require their own uniform analysis. In fact retaining the signed interval is precisely the source of any potential improvement.

Every higher-order interaction can also be written without truncation. For auxiliary prime variables z_p, set

    H_B(t;z)=sum_(S subset B)(-1)^|S| chi(p_S) z_S 1_(p_S<=t),
    p_S=product_(p in S)p, z_S=product_(p in S)z_p.

At t>=1, compare with the product of its single-prime marginals:

    H_B(t;z)-product_(p in B)[1-chi(p)z_p1_(p<=t)]
     =sum_(S subset B,|S|>=2)(-1)^|S|chi(p_S)z_S
           [1_(p_S<=t)-1_(max S<=t)].                (R14)

For unramified primes this coefficient is nonzero throughout max S<=t<p_S, at EVERY order. No pairwise closure follows. The formula is simply coefficient comparison of two finite multilinear polynomials; squarefree signs are Boolean Mobius signs, not set-partition cumulant coefficients.

For a proposed approximation Htilde_(B,X), define the full signed approximated contraction Atilde_chi(X) using(R10), and define Delta_chi(X) by substituting H-Htilde into that same complete sum. Then

    M_chi(X)=Atilde_chi(X)+Delta_chi(X).               (R15)

Bounds for BOTH terms at X^(gamma+epsilon), for every fixed chi, every epsilon and all sufficiently large X with a common gamma, give the exact Mellin return in section2. A moving block does not change the target source because(R15) returns to M before continuation. If an energy is used instead, it must retain the full contraction and its cross terms; a count of induced interactions is not an energy estimate.

No such bound is proved here. The useful audit output is the explicit source and the sharp two-prime correction, which an actual contraction theorem would have to estimate. It protects the seed's signed-interaction approach while rejecting only naive product replacement, positive normalization through zeros, and their unsupported absolute price.

Ancestry includes U-FUGACITY, W09/W23 actual dependence, W31 T28's distinct cumulant coefficients, W34's cluster majorant, W38's occupation laws and W50 audit13's continuation-state interface. This is a concrete ordinary sharp-source calculation, not a new statistical-mechanics family or a transfer from those different Gaussian/native-H sources.

## 3. Literal valuations, both signs and the unbounded certificate

At a first common prime let i,j>=1 be its complete multiplicities in the two full columns. B3.50--52 includes both plain powers and every slot occurrence. With l_p=log_Z Np, the C orientation has t=(i-j) mod 6. The source's active radical r, exponent e in F, and active canceled indicator r0 are:

| t | r | e | r0 | f_t=(1+rho)r-rho e-r0 |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| 1 | 1 | 2 | 0 | 1-rho |
| 2 | 1 | 3 | 0 | 1-2rho |
| 3 | 1 | 4 | 0 | 1-3rho |
| 4 | 1 | 5 | 0 | 1-4rho |
| 5 | 1 | 0 | 1 | rho |

The inactive t=0 case is not assigned an exponent one. It is already in the common puncture and its optional divisor expansion contributes through E separately. The t=5 sixth power is exactly the coprimality mask; exponent zero in F does not erase that zero. For the other side exchange i and j, so its active exponent is 1-t rather than 1+t. The same table applied to its own ordered pair proves the same bound. Generator units remain in the finite unit dictionary. Whole-product conjugation preserves the row norm and reflects all heights; changing just one fixed factor is not permitted.

Consequently c=sum i l_p, d=sum j l_p, R=sum r l_p, L=sum e l_p and R0=sum r0 l_p are the actual source quantities. The first mask divisor has E>=0. The target is LA.4,

    sum_lambda N_C,lambda << Z^[p+A-c+R+E+Bc+small],
    Bc=(3c-5d-R)_+/6.

It is a joint target. First-label Cauchy and B3.56 retain

    M+p-(c+d)/2+R/2+(Bc+Bd)/2 <= M.

Retaining Bc in the relative excess improves a bound inside this same target and does not spend its outside balance twice. LA.13 gives

    E1=(1-rho)(c-d)_+-delta c-(1+rho)R-E-Bc+rho L+R0,
    rho=1-10delta/[3(5-2delta)], .68<=delta<=.70.       (V1)

The algebra of this line is literal; its use below .70 imports the accepted [restricted research revision]/[restricted research revision] density extension, not an unstated extension of PR15's printed theorem range.

If c<=d, the positive parts vanish. Since 1-4rho<0 on the interval, i>=1 and f_t>=1-4rho imply f_t>=(1-4rho)i. Summation yields

    -E1 >= (delta+1-4rho)c+E.                         (V2)

If c>=d, put

    Hplus=delta-(6+27rho)/37,
    lambda=(9-15rho)/37, u=(19rho-4)/37.

Here 0<=lambda<=1/6 and u>0, so Bc>=lambda(3c-5d-R), even when its argument is negative. Subtract Hplus c from -E1 and use that bound. The coefficients of c,d are respectively u,2u; the remaining prime terms are (28+52rho)r/37-rho e-r0. It remains to prove

    (19rho-4)(i+2j)+(28+52rho)r-37rho e-37r0 >=0.     (V3)

The minimum i+2j in residue t=0,...,5 is 3,4,5,6,7,5. Every positive pair reduces by multiples of six in each coordinate to a pair in [1,6]^2 with the same residue. Increasing i by six adds 6(19rho-4)>0 to (V3); increasing j by six adds 12(19rho-4)>0. This proves reduction to the least representatives for all unbounded multiplicities. At their minima, the six expressions are

    57rho-12, 12+54rho, 8+36rho, 4+18rho, 0, 147rho-29.

All are nonnegative for 19/54<=rho<=103/273. Thus

    E1<=-Hval(delta)c-E,
    Hval=min(delta+1-4rho, delta-(6+27rho)/37).        (V4)

Both constituents strictly increase with delta because rho'<0. They cross at rho=43/121, delta=585/839. Their minimum is increasing, with Hval(.68)=1166/6825. The helper verifies the entire affine dual identities using their two coefficients, as well as the least-residue table. It does not extrapolate a sampled finite valuation search.

The old relaxed equality R=min(c,d), c=2d, L=5R is impossible for nonempty actual support: R=d forces all common primes active with j=1, whereas L=5R forces t=4 and hence every i>=5. Thus c>=5d contradicts c=2d.

The replacement has exact local equality patterns. For V2 use C=P,D=P^3, giving t=4, c<=d, L=5c and E=0. For V3 use disjoint U,V with valuations (5,1) and (1,3), and support widths in ratio 13:9. Then c=74t,d=40t,R=22t,L=110t,R0=E=0 and 3c-5d-R=0; the dual lower bound is attained. These powers can be allocated in the source's unrestricted natural plain sums at sufficiently small fixed widths, with slots and residual factors avoiding the frozen support. proof audit of every historical entry. D35.1 and [private research revision] S24--S29 were

## 2. D04: exact reconstruction, complete quantifiers and zero return

Write f(n)=mu(rad(n/3^v3(n))). Fix tau>0 and one ordinary character chi
modulo q, with its actual zero extension on nonunits. Define

    F_chi(x)=sum_(n>=1) f(n)chi(n)g_tau(log(n/x)).

For finite P of unramified primes>=5, let V_P have the SAME coefficients
but vanish on integers divisible by any p in P. Define a_P(r)=f(r)chi(r)
on all P-smooth integers, zero otherwise. The unique decomposition of n
into its FULL smooth part r and rough part v gives the coefficient
identity a_P*f_P=(n -> f(n)chi(n)) and hence

    F_chi(x)=sum_(r P-smooth) a_P(r)V_P(x/r).       (A1)

At every deleted p, a_P(p^j)=-chi(p)^j for ALL j>=1. The local series
is (1-2chi(p)z)/(1-chi(p)z), not1-chi(p)z. The precise positive price is

    W_P(u)=sum |a_P(r)|r^-u=product_(p in P)(1-p^-u)^-1.

Prime2 and exceptional3 remain in V_P; natural zeros at q are retained.
For any fixed P and a weight u>1, the positive Gaussian integer field
is bounded by C_u t^u on all t>0: at infinity its size is O(t), and at
zero it has faster-than-power decay. Summing this bound with W_P(u)
proves absolute, locally uniform convergence of A1 before any open
moment hypothesis. Thus no rearrangement hides a source assumption.

Fix1/2<gamma<1,0<sigma<gamma,0<delta<1,A>0 with

    A(1-sigma)<1,
    q_head=sigma+delta(1-sigma)<gamma.              (A2)

For each large dyadic parent X, freeze
P_X={5<=p<=(log X)^A:p does not divide q}. OPEN-D04 asks for every
epsilon>0, with a constant uniform in X and EVERY REAL U,

    ||V_(P_X)||_[U,2U],dx/x <= C_epsilon U^(gamma+epsilon),
                   X^delta<=U<=X.                (A3)

The parent prime set stays fixed during every dilation. Replacing it by
P_U, or bounding only primes/one rough depth/a submask, changes A3.

Since sigma<1, summing p^-sigma over all integers up to(log X)^A gives
log W_(P_X)(sigma)=O((log X)^(A(1-sigma)))=o(log X). No PNT is needed.
Split A1 at r=X^(1-delta). For shorter r, the exact shell U=X/r is in
A3. Minkowski gives X^(gamma+epsilon')W_(P_X)(sigma), and a smaller
epsilon' absorbs the subpower price.

For larger r, t=x/r<=2X^delta. The positive Gaussian integer field is
O(t) when t>=1 and O_sigma(t^sigma) when0<t<1. Therefore uniformly on
this head it is O(X^(delta(1-sigma))t^sigma). Summing EVERY smooth r
in the head bounds its pointwise, hence shell-L2, contribution by

    X^q_head W_(P_X)(sigma)=X^(q_head+o(1)).        (A4)

The strict gap in A2 pays it. The norm triangle pays the head square
and both cross terms of a subsequent energy expansion. No inheritance
of a masked moment, projector commutation or deletion of positive energy
is used. This proves the conditional full F_chi gamma moment. The head
price is sufficient, not a universal optimum or impossibility boundary.

### 2.1 Independent Mellin check

For Re s>1, Fubini and the exact local factors give

    M(F_chi)(s)=exp(tau*s^2/2) H_chi(s)/L(s,chi),
    H_(chi,p)=(1-2chi(p)p^-s)/(1-chi(p)p^-s)^2, p!=3,
    H_(chi,3)=(1-chi(3)3^-s)^-2.                   (A5)

Factors at p|q are1. For unramified p>=5 the first-order term cancels;
the product converges absolutely locally in Re s>1/2. Its numerator
zero lines are Re s=log_p2<1/2, denominators' zero lines are Re s=0.
The exceptional p2 numerator has zero line Re s=1, and p3 has no
numerator. Thus H_chi is holomorphic and nonzero in1/2<Re s<1.
Complex character phases do not alter those real parts.

The full moment implies that the defining Mellin integral is holomorphic
in Re s>gamma: on each large dyadic shell use Cauchy--Schwarz with an
epsilon smaller than the distance to that line; all fixed derivatives
are summable there. The left Gaussian tail handles x tending to zero.
Multiplying A5 by L and analytically continuing, a zero rho with
gamma<Re rho<1 contradicts the nonzero right side. The independently
accepted right boundary covers Re s>=1; principal pole handling is
meromorphic. No claim that the p2 numerator is nonzero on Re s=1 is
needed. Every height is covered by analytic continuation, not a grid.

This is a conditional result for EACH fixed chi separately. Zeta-only
A3 is not a bound for all chi. No growing conductor, new angular scope,
Hecke family or SP/H addback is imported.

### 2.2 The reverse implication is valid and fixes the strength claim

The inverse local series is

    (1-chi(p)z)/(1-2chi(p)z)
       =1+sum_(j>=1)2^(j-1)chi(p)^j z^j.

For fixed u>log_5(2), the inverse coefficients b_P have mass

    B_P(u)=product_(p in P)(1-p^-u)/(1-2p^-u).      (A6)

The sign and every prime power matter. For fixed u<1, its logarithm
is O_u((log X)^(A(1-u))). The coefficient identity and absolutely
convergent field identity are V_P=sum_r b_P(r)F_chi(./r).

Assume the original fixed F_chi moment with exponent gamma and every
epsilon. Its real-shell bound follows from at most two dyadic shells;
its Gaussian left tail extends the bound to all positive shell scales.
Choose0<epsilon'<epsilon small enough that u=gamma+epsilon'<1.
Since gamma>1/2>log_5(2) and gamma>sigma, A6 is finite and subpower.
Minkowski gives

    ||V_(P_X)||_[U,2U] <= C U^(gamma+epsilon') B_(P_X)(u)
                       = U^(gamma+epsilon') X^o(1).

For U>=X^delta the last factor is absorbed into U^(epsilon-epsilon'),
uniformly in X,U. This is exactly A3. Together with A1--A4 it proves
the first critic's additional interpretation: **under A2, OPEN-D04 and
the original complete fixed-character gamma moment are equivalent at
the every-epsilon exponent level.** The idea pays a range obligation
and changes the organization; it does not weaken the required arithmetic
exponent. This equivalence is credited to the first Sol critic, not
retrospectively to the generator or to this final validation.

| gamma | Conditional c | (A,sigma,delta) | q_head | gamma-q_head | A(1-sigma) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
|2187/2500|313/2500|(6,17/20,1/10)|173/200|49/5000|9/10|
|5/6|1/6|(5,41/50,1/20)|829/1000|13/3000|9/10|
|3/4|1/4|(3,7/10,1/10)|73/100|1/50|9/10|

credit. The useful continuation here is the literal f3*chi all-power

## 3. D33: periodic cancellation is real; the full correction is unpaid

For finite P containing2 and excluding3, put Q=product P and
e_P(n)=product_(p in P)(-1)^(1_(p|n)). This is the actual all-valuation
local f3 sign at these primes, extended periodically. Completing one
entire residue period, including n=0, CRT gives

    mean e_P=product_(p in P)(1-2/p)=0,
    mean e_P(n)e_P(n+h)=product_(p in P)c_p(h),
    c_p(h)=1 if p|h, and1-4/p otherwise.             (A7)

For p not dividing h the two negative residues are0,-h; for p|h the
local product is1. This handles h=0, the p2 odd/even sign and every
prime power. It does not assert independence for the completed f3 pair.

Let h_tau(t)=g_tau(log t) for t>0 and0 otherwise. It is Schwartz and
flat at zero. The mean-zero DFT of e_P has no zero frequency and
coefficients of modulus<=1. Poisson and m>=2 integrations by parts give

    |W_P(x)| <= C_(tau,m) x^(1-m) Q^m,              (A8)
    W_P(x)=sum_(n>=1)e_P(n)g_tau(log(n/x)).

There is no extra factor Q: reindexing Qj-k runs bijectively over
nonzero integers not divisible by Q, whose m-power reciprocal sum is
at most2zeta(m). All derivative constants depend on fixed m,tau, not P.
For z_X=a log X/loglog X,0<a<1, elementary factorial comparison gives
Q<=X^(a+o(1)). On the whole closed parent shell, one fixed
m>(1+A0)/(1-a) makes W_(P_X)=O(X^-A0), for any prescribed A0.
This is a proved restricted model estimate, not a favorable finite
experiment or an application of an impermissible moving mask to G9.

The exact transform shows why it is not a zero detector:

    M(W_P)(s)=exp(tau*s^2/2)zeta(s)product_(p in P)(1-2p^-s).

Prime2 cancels the pole at1. The transform for fixed P is entire; zeta
zeros are numerator zeros, not singularities. The genuine source is

    f(n)=e_P(n)r_P(n),
    F=W_P+E_P,
    E_P(x)=sum_n e_P(n)(r_P(n)-1)g_tau(log(n/x)),     (A9)

with r_P the product of all remaining prime signs except3. Its only
given absolute estimate is O(x). For the moving sieve in A8, the
every-epsilon gamma shell bound for E_(P_X) is equivalent by two norm
triangles to the same bound for fixed full F. All energy cross terms
remain in that exact identity. When gamma>1/2, restoring the genuine
O(X) diagonal also recovers the usual complete signed correlation
contract. No correction or moment gain has been obtained.

The relaxed marginal obstruction is sound: preserving all small-prime
patterns but allowing arbitrary hidden signs permits r=e_P. The full
coefficient becomes1 and its positive Gaussian field has size
e^(tau/2)x+O(1), hence norm exponent1. That adversary is not the actual
rough arithmetic sign and need not satisfy its prime-deletion identities.
It disproves certification from those marginals alone.

The first critic's ancestry correction is necessary. [private research revision] S24--S29
already gives exact all-valuation periodic ray signs, prime2 cancellation

Together with S04/D04 and S33/D33 this covers exactly ten author tests.
Four are duplicate organizations/failures(S15,S31,S51,S54); two are

## 5. Protected audit S42: what a scale counterterm actually removes

This audit executes the proposed two-scale signal/error test and derives
an exact fixed-source return. It does not assume that a bound
F(x)=O(x^beta) is an actual leading asymptotic Bx^beta.

### 5.1 Two-mode recurrence and precision

Fix lambda>1. In the toy two-state evolution, the signal and nuisance
coordinates evolve by diag(lambda^rho,lambda^beta), with real beta and
complex rho. The scalar observation is

    y_j=A lambda^(rho*j)+B lambda^(beta*j).

Applying T-lambda^beta I gives eigenvalues lambda^rho-lambda^beta and0,
so the scalar counterterm is exactly

    y_(j+1)-lambda^beta y_j
       =A(lambda^rho-lambda^beta)lambda^(rho*j).     (A10)

It kills the nuisance, but preserves the signal's growth exponent when
the multiplier is nonzero. Signal is also killed when
rho=beta+2pi i k/log lambda. If Re rho>=beta+eta, the normalized
multiplier |1-lambda^(beta-rho)| is uniformly at least1-lambda^-eta;
on Re rho=beta it can vanish. There is no general exponent improvement
from the recurrence identity itself.

For a scale-dependent coefficient c_j=lambda^beta(1+epsilon_j), the
pure nuisance B lambda^(beta*j) leaves residual
-B epsilon_j lambda^(beta*(j+1)). To bound this by C lambda^(gamma*j)
with gamma<beta and fixed nonzero B requires

    |epsilon_j| <= C' lambda^(-(beta-gamma)*j).      (A11)

Merely epsilon_j tending to0 or having finite sum does not imply that
power-rate accuracy. This is an exact necessity for the stated toy;
it is not a universal obstruction to every nonlinear renormalization.

### 5.2 Exact actual-f3 filter and all-height return

For integer lambda>=2, use the actual fixed field from A5 and define

    G_lambda(x)=F_chi(x)-lambda^beta F_chi(x/lambda).

It is an exact Gaussian field with coefficients

    c_lambda(n)=f(n)chi(n)
       -lambda^beta 1_(lambda|n) f(n/lambda)chi(n/lambda). (A12)

Thus all original powers and character zeros are retained. No Gaussian
support or signed cross term is discarded. The fixed Mellin identity is

    M(G_lambda)(s)=(1-lambda^(beta-s))
                    exp(tau*s^2/2)H_chi(s)/L(s,chi).   (A13)

For fixed beta in(1/2,1), suppose EACH of G_2,G_3 satisfies
||G_lambda||_[X,2X],dx/x<=C_epsilon X^(gamma+epsilon), for every
epsilon>0 and all large dyadic X, where1/2<gamma<1. Their Mellin integrals
are holomorphic in Re s>gamma by the same left-tail/Cauchy--Schwarz
argument as A5. For a zero rho with gamma<Re rho<1, both symbols must
vanish unless a pole survives. Their common zero set is exactly{s=beta}:
vanishing forces Re rho=beta and t log2,t log3 in2pi Z; any nonzero t
would make log2/log3 rational, contrary to unique factorization.

Moreover each symbol has a SIMPLE zero at beta, since its derivative
there is log lambda. H_chi is nonzero there. Therefore these two moment
hypotheses exclude every zero in gamma<Re s<1 **except possibly one
simple real zero at s=beta**. A multiple zero at beta would leave a
pole in both transforms. If beta<=gamma, or if L(beta,chi)!=0 has
separate evidence, this is a complete conditional return, with the
accepted right boundary as before. No such moment bounds or real-zero
exclusion for every chi are proved by the audit.

For the zeta member, the possible real exception is independently absent
when0<beta<1. One elementary proof uses the alternating Dirichlet series:
its paired terms (2k-1)^-beta-(2k)^-beta are positive and summable,
so eta(beta)>0. The continuation identity
eta(s)=(1-2^(1-s))zeta(s), initially proved for Re s>1 and continued
to Re s>0 by the convergent alternating series, has a nonzero negative
factor at real beta in(0,1). Thus zeta(beta)!=0. Consequently the
PAIR of actual zeta f3 filter moments suffices for the complete gamma
zero return even though either individual symbol has an infinite
vertical grid of zeros. This is a proved conditional adapter, not a
proved improvement or a claim that the filters are easier to estimate.

For the character family a real exceptional zero cannot simply be
discarded. The exact restriction above is part of the theorem. Constants
may depend on the fixed chi, beta and tau; moving conductors and Hecke
transfer have not been added.

### 5.3 Uniform gain is a separate question from qualitative return

Even the two incommensurate filters have no positive uniform joint gain
on the vertical line Re s=beta. Put alpha=log3/log2, irrational. Among
Q+1 fractional parts0,alpha,...,Q alpha, two lie in the same one of Q
equal bins. For some1<=q<=Q, distance(q alpha,Z)<=1/Q. At
t=2pi q/log2 the symbol for2 vanishes and that for3 has magnitude
at most2pi/Q. Along Q tending to infinity a subsequence of q is
unbounded, because any finite nonzero q has strictly positive distance
from an integer. Hence both symbols can be arbitrarily small at
unbounded heights without a common nonreal zero.

This disproves a fixed positive all-height gain for this filter pair.
It does NOT invalidate A13's fixed-zero analytic return: a nonzero
residue, however small, still contradicts holomorphy. Conflating these
two quantifiers would repeat an avoidable signal mistake.

For general x-dependent counterterms there is no single fixed symbol
A13. If c(x)=lambda^beta+e(x), the exact additional source is
-e(x)F_chi(x/lambda). Under an available F_chi=O(x^beta) bound, a
supremum bound e=O(X^(-(beta-gamma))) on the parent shell is sufficient
to pay that residual at gamma. This only prices the extra error; it
does not supply the desired norm of the constant-counterterm G_lambda.
The inherited f3 beta bound is not a known pure beta mode to cancel.

Ancestry remains fixed-filter/translated-detector and W22/W36 pole-safe
counterterm work. This audit's contribution is the explicit actual-f3
two-scale symbol, complete common-zero/multiplicity return and precise
distinction between qualitative return and uniform gain. It is not a
new family or an unconditional stable arithmetic fixed point.

## 6. Uniform audit S22: exact indefinite metric and the positive readout

Take the specified three-state laboratory with
J=diag(1,1,-1), q(v)=v*Jv. The nonzero vectors v=(1,0,1) and
w=(1,0,-1) both have q=0. Projection of v onto the first coordinate
has q=1, and onto the third has q=-1. For the readout l(v)=v1-v3,
|l(w)|^2=4 despite q(w)=0. Scaling w makes this readout arbitrarily
large with unchanged zero signed energy. Thus an upper bound for an
indefinite quadratic form does not by itself bound a positive witness,
and an ordinary orthogonal projection need not preserve its sign.
This is a finite countertest, not a claim that the native H Gram is
indefinite.

An asterisk on a vector or matrix denotes conjugate transpose in the
formulas below.

The exact escape is a source-range condition. Write v=(u,Ku), with
u in C^2 and K:C^2->C. If ||K||=kappa<1, then

    q(v)=u*(I-K*K)u >=(1-kappa^2)||u||^2,
    ||v||^2 <=[(1+kappa^2)/(1-kappa^2)] q(v).       (A14)

The constant is sharp at a top singular vector of K. For K=(kappa,0),
u=(1,0) attains it exactly. At kappa=3/5 the ratio is17/8. It blows
up as the physical range approaches an isotropic direction; kappa=1
has a nonzero null vector and kappa>1 has a negative direction.

The readout may cost less than the whole vector norm. For
l(v)=a*u+b*Ku, define d=a+K*b as a column and D=I-K*K>0. Cauchy--Schwarz
in the D metric gives the EXACT best constant

    |l(v)|^2 <= C_l q(v),
    C_l=d*D^-1 d.                                 (A15)

Equality holds at u=D^-1 d, unless d=0, when the readout vanishes.
This follows by writing d*u=(D^-1/2 d)*(D^1/2 u). Thus a near-null
direction is not automatically fatal if the actual readout annihilates
it with a controlled coefficient. Such alignment needs proof from the
original source, not an abstract signature.

For K=(kappa,0), reading the first coordinate costs1/(1-kappa^2),
the second costs1, and the aligned readout v1-kappa*v3 costs
1-kappa^2. The laboratory therefore supplies both the generic
conditioning obstruction and a genuine readout-sensitive escape.

To identify the actual Gaussian source, any finite set of its original
integer labels has the POSITIVE Gram

    G_mn=integral_[X,2X] g_tau(log(m/x))g_tau(log(n/x)) dx/x,
    ||F_N||^2=c*G c, c_n=f(n)chi(n).                (A16)

Both independent labels, all chosen signs and the natural zeros remain.
G is positive because it is a Gram of the actual functions. Absorbing
the source coefficients into a diagonal D_c gives D_c*G D_c>=0.
A signed expansion or a Krein realization may represent this same
quantity, but cannot replace A16 by an unrelated difference of positive
sector norms and call it the physical energy. In particular, a mere
signature count or small signed trace is insufficient.

If a proposed exact realization maps the arithmetic coefficient vector
into a graph range as above, it must prove the uniform bound on K and
the actual readout A15, then restore all excluded source terms. The

conditioning can consume it. No such graph condition or alignment is
established for native H, the full f3 correlations or a completed

counterexample does not rule out a source-specific realization that
does prove them.

Ancestry is the indefinite storage/observer and U-VARIATIONAL readout
obstruction. The fresh bounded audit supplies an exact three-state

## 3. A complete constant-cut core

Fix3/4<=gamma<1 and choose tau before x in the CLOSED interval

 max(gamma tau,gamma(1-tau)) <= (11gamma-3)/8.

Set

 L=X^gamma, M=X^r, r=(6-2gamma)/4,
 U=X^(gamma tau), V=X^(gamma(1-tau)), G=X^(1-gamma).              (15)

These inverse cuts are CONSTANT throughout the shell, independent of n. In particular UV=L. Define full coefficient sequences

 Q_U=a_(<=U)*(v*s), Q_V=a_(<=V)*(v*s),
 S=a_(<=U)*a_(<=V)*b0,
 R=a_(>U)*a_(>V)*b0.

The exact identity is

 c=Q_U+Q_V-S+R.                                                (16)

All ordered terms and strict complements are retained. The small-double source has coefficients

 A_m=sum_(de=m,d<=U,e<=V)a(d)a(e), m<=UV=L, |A_m|<=d_2(m).

They are frozen, so H' with D=L gives ||sum_n S(n)f_x(n)||_(1,2)<<X^(gamma+epsilon), since gamma>=3/4. This pays its ENTIRE infinite cofactor tail and every stationary alias. No original mask is attached after this mean-zero estimate.

For Q_U and Q_V use the accepted [restricted research revision] complete square-short theorem with infinite root endpoints and the two literal physical labels1,p with weights1,-p chi(p). At D=X^alpha its norm exponents are

 alpha, (3+8alpha)/11, 3/8+alpha/4,
             min(3/10+7alpha/10,15/32+alpha/4).

Each is <=gamma under (15): alpha<=gamma, the second is the stated corridor, and the last two follow already from gamma>=3/4. Fixed p only changes constants. Natural root zeros beta(r)=chi(r)^2(1-p1_(p|r)), both physical multipliers and all cross-row collisions remain paid by the source theorem. Its hypotheses include arbitrary frozen prefixes, so infinity is allowed.

Every tuple in R has de>UV=L. Hence R(n)=0 for n<=L; there is NO missing low-output prefix. Also |R(n)|<=(p+1)^2 d_3(n). The accepted complete coefficientwise high-tail theorem gives

 ||sum_(n>M)R(n)f_x(n)||_2^2
      << X^(3/2+epsilon)+X^6 M^(-4+epsilon)
      << X^(2gamma+epsilon).                                 (17)

The whole infinite tail, its diagonal and both cross orientations are included. Next apply [restricted research revision] G182, b=3/2,k=6, to the exact mask

 1_(L<del<=M)1_(d>U)1_(e>V),

with actual colors a(d),a(e),b0(l), and strict gcd(d,e)>G. It pays that full removed source by X^epsilon[X/G+X^(3/4)/sqrt(G)]<<X^(gamma+epsilon). No condition involving gcd(d,l) or gcd(e,l) is inserted.

Define the new finite core

 T_rect(x)=sum_(L<n<=M) f_x(n)
       sum_(del=n,d>U,e>V,gcd(d,e)<=G)a(d)a(e)b0(l).             (18)

Combining (16), H', both complete short sources, (17) and G182 proves

 ||C-T_rect||_(1,2) <<_(chi,p,gamma,epsilon) X^(gamma+epsilon),  (19)

uniformly in allowed frozen tau. For fixed gamma the corridor is a compact subset of(0,1); its largest exponent (11gamma-3)/8 is <1. All thresholds/constants can consequently be chosen uniformly in tau. H' uses alpha0=gamma<1. The endpoints gamma=3/4 and corridor equality are INCLUDED with the usual every-epsilon losses. No equality-impossibility assertion is made.

The old [restricted research revision] core T_ad uses the same n window and gcd cutoff but U(n)=B(n)^tau,V(n)=B(n)^(1-tau), with B(n)<=L. Thus (18) is literally a further restriction of its tuple set. Its signed removed wedge is paid as

 ||T_ad-T_rect||_(1,2) <=||T_ad-C||_(1,2)+||C-T_rect||_(1,2)
                         <<X^(gamma+epsilon).                (20)

This is a comparison of two independently proved COMPLETE source transfers, not monotonicity under signed deletion. It does not reapply the periodic mean after a gcd mask.
