# Positive cofactor-hole absolute Gram: independent corollary check

Verdict: the proposed statement is correct for BOTH specified prices,
including their complete off-diagonals. The existing inputs give the
stronger uniform estimate

    X^2/log(2X)^2 << A_theta(X), B_theta(X) << X^2.       (1)

The same lower bound holds after removing the diagonal. Thus each price
is >>_epsilon X^(2-epsilon) for every epsilon>0. Constants/onsets depend
on the fixed ring, S, presented character eta, tau and polynomial-hole
exponent A, but NOT on the chosen probability weights or holes.

This is a scoped corollary of [restricted research revision] G218-G221, not a new general positive
certificate obstruction or a new high-ceiling result. The real-rank-two
argument is already contained in G221's general rank inequality. Its
application to arbitrary positive polynomial-hole mixtures on the actual
Gaussian mu*eta source, and the equality before/after pair integration,
should be recorded explicitly. The logarithmic lower bound in(1) is an
elementary quantitative refinement using the already available count.
No Mobius cancellation, signed-energy lower bound, new c or PR15 repair
follows. The numerical c11 remains conditional.

## Exact objects and scope

Use G218's integers or Eisenstein integral ideals, q_a=a or Na, fixed
tau>0, and positive logarithmic Gaussian g=g_tau. Eta is one fixed ordinary
Dirichlet character or finite-order trivial-infinity Hecke character.
Set c_a=mu_R(a)eta(a)1_((a,S)=1). Let S+ include S and ALL natural-zero
primes of the PRESENTED character, including imprimitive modulus primes.
Then |c_a|=1 precisely on squarefree S+-coprime indices, and is0 otherwise.

On each entire shell[X,2X], choose any nonnegative theta_Q summing to1,
on radical Q coprime to S with q_Q<=X^A, where A>0 is fixed. There are
only finitely many such distinct Q. Their weights may depend on X and
on the actual source, but are frozen in x on the shell. No independence
from arithmetic data is required. Define

    I_Q(a)=1_((a,Q)=1), p(a)=sum_Q theta_Q I_Q(a),
    K_X(a,b)=integral_X^(2X)g(log(q_a/x))g(log(q_b/x))dx/x,
    A_theta=sum_(a,b)|Re(c_a conjugate(c_b))|
                       K_X(a,b) p(rad(ab)),
    B_theta=sum_(a,b)|Re(c_a conjugate(c_b))|
                       K_X(a,b) p(a)p(b).                (2)

A_theta averages the termwise real-absolute Gram prices of the individual
U_Q fields. B_theta is that price for P=sum_Q theta_Q U_Q. Both include
the diagonal and both ordered off-diagonal orientations. The positive
kernel K_X does not depend on eta or theta. These are distinct prices;
neither is identified with the signed norm it majorizes.

No Euler multiplier or zero-exclusion return is asserted for an arbitrary
choice of theta. G218 proves returns only for its specific reconstructed
fixed sources under their complete arithmetic hypotheses.

## Uniform squarefree mass, with a logarithmic refinement

Write Q*=rad(S+ Q), and D(Q*)=prod_(p|Q*)(1+q_p^-1)^(-1).
The G218(218.3) count, subtracted at2X and X, gives

    N_sf(X,2X;Q*)=kappa_R X D(Q*)/zeta_R(2)
          +O(sqrt(X)log(2X) S_1/2(Q*))              [K],
    N_sf(X,2X;Q*)=X D(Q*)/zeta(2)
          +O(sqrt(X) d(Q*))                       [Z]. (3)

The ideal version counts ideals, not associates. This uniform estimate
does not require q_Q<=X. Repeated Q factors do not create new holes.

To improve the candidate's X^(1-delta) lower count, use the exact identity

    D(Q*)^-1=sum_(d|Q*) q_d^-1
       <=sum_(q_d<=q_Q*)q_d^-1 << log(2q_Q*).             (4)

The last bound follows by partial summation from the elementary count
A_R(T)<<T. It uses no prime number theorem or new external input.
Because q_Q*<=C_(S,eta)X^A, (4) gives D(Q*)>>1/log(2X).
For any fixed delta>0, the prime-product argument already used in G219
gives S_1/2(Q*)<<_delta q_Q*^delta. The same elementary small/large-prime
split gives d(Q*)<<_delta q_Q*^delta over Z: each large-prime factor2
is at most q_p^delta, while the finitely many small-prime factors have
a fixed product. Choose delta=1/(4A). The errors in(3) are then
O_(S,eta,A)(X^(3/4)log(2X)), below its positive main term for all large X.
Consequently, uniformly in the entire allowed Q family,

    N_sf(X,2X;Q*) >> X/log(2X).                           (5)

For q_a and x in[X,2X], log(q_a/x) lies in[-log2,log2], where g has a
fixed positive minimum. Therefore

    W_Q(x):=sum_a |c_a| I_Q(a)g(log(q_a/x))
             >> X/log(2X),  every x in[X,2X].            (6)

Also W_Q(x)<=W_1(x)<<x by the complete Gaussian majorant. Both bounds
are uniform in Q. The natural zeros enter S+ once; no character value
of zero is replaced by a unit phase. All large-parameter thresholds
remain allowed to depend on the fixed presented character.

## Rank two proves both actual-source prices

For each nonzero c_a, identify xi_a=c_a/|c_a| with a unit vector in R^2.
For fixed Q,x let w_a=|c_a|I_Q(a)g(log(q_a/x)) and

    M_Q(x)=sum_a w_a xi_a xi_a^T, trace(M_Q)=W_Q.

This positive real2x2 matrix satisfies

    sum_(a,b) w_a w_b |xi_a dot xi_b|
       >=sum_(a,b)w_a w_b (xi_a dot xi_b)^2
       =trace(M_Q^2) >= W_Q^2/2.                         (7)

The first inequality is |t|>=t^2 for |t|<=1; the last is the two
nonnegative eigenvalue inequality. The Mobius signs and character phases
in xi remain the ACTUAL ones. No replacement by positive coefficients
or equidistribution assumption is used. For a real-valued character all
nonzero xi are+1 or-1, so the pointwise single-Q price is W_Q^2 and the factor
1/2 improves to1. We do not claim a sharp constant for every other fixed
character or an arithmetic lower bound on its signed energy.

Averaging(7) over theta and using(6), then integrating over the shell,
proves the A_theta lower bound in(1). For B_theta use instead

    w_a=|c_a|p(a)g(log(q_a/x)),
    sum_a w_a=sum_Q theta_Q W_Q(x) >> X/log(2X).

The SAME rank-two argument proves the B_theta lower bound independently.
It never compares the two kernels. Probability normalization is essential:
there is no extra hole-count factor or free gain from many labels.
Adaptive selection of theta at a shell cannot evade a lower bound that
holds for each admissible Q with the same constant.

Infinite sums cause no gap. First truncate the nonnegative weights to
q_a<=T and apply(7). Their total mass increases to finite W_Q, bounded
by the full O(x) Gaussian majorant. Matrix entries converge absolutely;
the nonnegative double sums converge monotonically. Tonelli then permits
the finite Q average and shell integration. Each full price is at most
integral_X^(2X) W_1(x)^2 dx/x << X^2, proving the upper bound in(1).

## Diagonal, covariance and integration checks

The two exact diagonal prices are

    D_A=sum_a |c_a|^2 K_X(a,a)p(a),
    D_B=sum_a |c_a|^2 K_X(a,a)p(a)^2.

Since0<=p<=1, both are at most integral sum_a g(log(q_a/x))^2 dx/x=O(X).
This follows from the same lattice/integer count; the Gaussian squared
is a constant multiple of a narrower Gaussian. Thus removing D_A or
D_B from(1) leaves at least a fixed positive multiple of X^2/log(2X)^2
for sufficiently large X. Both orientations remain; no factor2 is lost.
This proves the requested off-diagonal claim for every epsilon>0 as well.

The kernels p(rad(ab)) and p(a)p(b) are neither generally equal nor
entrywise ordered. Choose two distinct fixed good primes l,m outside S+.
With theta_1=theta_lm=1/2, at a=l,b=m they are1/2 and1/4. With
theta_l=theta_m=1/2, they are0 and1/4. All these holes obey q_Q<=X^A
for sufficiently large X. These examples concern kernel entries; no
unstated ordering or reverse ordering of the complete prices is inferred.
G220 already retains the distinction between joint and product covariance.

For every pair, its phase Re(c_a conjugate(c_b)) is independent of x,
and its Gaussian product and each relevant probability factor are real
nonnegative. Hence, EXACTLY,

    integral |Re(c_a conjugate(c_b))| g_a(x)g_b(x)dx/x
       =|Re(c_a conjugate(c_b)) K_X(a,b)|.                 (8)

The same identity holds with either fixed nonnegative kernel in(2).
Thus taking the absolute real pair contribution after integration does
not reduce THESE Gaussian prices. This assertion does not apply to a
profile whose phase changes with x, or to a collective signed sum before
the absolute value. It does not revise G221's broader Jordan-lift escape:
that theorem allows x-dependent lifted directions and its different
kernel, so cancellation after integration still requires its own audit.

## Historical overlap and what remains open

The complete maintained index was read. The exact [restricted research revision] author/reviewer
support copies match the earlier frozen bytes already read in this
same reviewer's retained history. This check adds a corollary, not a
repeat source-repair pass or primary-input admission.

- G218(218.3) and G219 supply the uniform squarefree-hole count and
  positive mass. G219's earlier changed-coefficient counterexample is
  different from the actual-mu REAL absolute Gram here. The count is reused.
- G220(220.2)-(220.4) already distinguishes the finite joint-label Gram,
  squared averaged field, and their limit error. No new covariance
  identity is claimed by writing(2).
- G221(221.3) and its general real-dimension paragraph supply the rank
  argument. Taking dimension2 and unit lift/readout yields(7). This is
  existing mathematics, specialized to the new mask-uniform Gaussian scope.
- W66's retained independent review, Section3(7)-(9), already proves an
  exponent-one floor for all positive diagonal Holder/Cauchy certificates
  of its PRINCIPAL deletion-channel readout, including arbitrary moving
  retention/weights. Its positive output b_X and observer h satisfy
  sum|h|b=sum_(n in D_X)prod_(p|n)(3-2rho_p)>=#D_X. That is a different
  finite divisor channel and separable certificate, not this arbitrary
  polynomial-hole Gaussian pair kernel for complex eta. Preserve its
  priority for that claim; no wider W66 integration was undertaken here.
- G127/[private research revision] already records an actual-coefficient absolute off-diagonal
  obstruction for a different curved source and length/phase regime.
  The general lesson that absolute prices can destroy useful cancellation
  is not new. No exhaustive literature novelty is claimed.

The useful retention is the explicit actual-source corollary with all
positive hole distributions, its logarithmic quantitative version(1),
and its precise Gaussian after-integration scope. Every actual signed
energy can still be much smaller through its retained negative real
pairs. Signed theta weights are outside the proof. So are nonprincipal
f,k joint label kernels whose summed entries oscillate: nonnegative
outer weights do not make every expanded character kernel nonnegative.
Only the literal cofactor-hole masks and their positive averages are
covered. No arbitrary positive average automatically retains a zero
signal, Euler multiplier, original height uniformity or physical return.

statement:
# Conditional high-gain sharpening and a tilted affine plane

Status: conditional on the independently pending [private research revision] weighted-density and literal-projector argument, and on the same imported analytic base as written c6. The candidate obtained here is

    c = 12514261/100000000 = .12514261,
    theta = 87485739/100000000 = .87485739.

This is not an accepted increased constant. It exceeds c6=.125139 by .00000361, but no numerical certificate establishes the pending analytic lemma. This supplement changes neither the frozen [private research revision] candidate nor its review assignment. No formalization, proof assistant, kernel, provider or external model was used.

The controller supplied the stronger support/residual-slot split and the slope-tilt observation. This report checks their actual units, proves the resulting conditional all-configuration saving, and recomputes the full local atlas and endpoint return. Source credit and limitations remain those of [private research revision]: OpenAI; Hailey Collet; Akash Levy; Zhongpai Gao with AI assistance. No literature-priority claim is made.

## 1. Exact conditional inputs and source boundary

The frozen input is `[restricted provenance path] research revision]-drafts/binding-bin-development/report.md`, SHA-256 bbd8e388b9e7c068a9857a0f80dcb6b9e73722908563a15ce956c775614dfc4e, especially sections 2--5. The new arithmetic below requires its raw weighted estimate

    sum_rows |Q_w|^2 << Z^[rho(delta) W + gamma(delta) z + epsilon] H_J,
    rho(delta)=1-10delta/[3(5-2delta)],
    eta(delta)=delta-gamma(delta)=4delta(5/6-delta)/(5-2delta),

for delta in [17/25,7/10], z<=W/21, the actual eligible parent dictionary, both whole orientations, original slots and natural zeros, and the fixed missing-radical masks. It also requires the exact reduction of the second projector to fixed allocations and the frozen-slot inequality from that report. These are substantive conditions still undergoing independent review. This supplement does not re-prove them or weaken them to a theorem signature.

The literal joint ledger is PR15 PhysicalLocalAssembly LA.11--13, lines 295--379, at ca182b70ac2aee2d053d679b4ddf1233883f9eef. The complete second projector, arbitrary signed post-scales, scalar normalization and clipping are PR9 B3.65--69, lines 2464--2517, at 58344dfdbe756cf2f743da1908ffe0582418cf5b. These passages were read directly again. PR15 prints its high argument for [.70,.75]; its algebra below remains valid on [.68,.70], while the density extension and the new weighted input on that interval are explicitly those of the preceding [private research revision]/[private research revision] development. The PR15 narrower theorem is not silently widened.

The first-transform convention remains the corrected +xi_r(ab), with old D.10 C-side coefficient tau(a)chi_a(er)xi_r(a). Both signed active residues 1+t_p and 1-t_p remain separate. No equality between F_+ and F_- is used. The exceptional M/24 improvement remains restricted to a centered equal-product difference, L=M/4, and an independently justified JOINT opposite-side target. It supplies no reserve here. All original fixed-inducing branches retain their old 4a and 9a costs.

The whole rectangle, two transforms, natural zero extensions, relative characters, independent heights and both complete coprimality projectors remain exactly those of the frozen source. In particular, no transform is applied to a zero-bin indicator. The imported F0/analytic-ancestry, positive-slot uniformity and exact comparison-root-definition obligations remain unresolved. Source receipts retain dates as recorded; PR15's source header is 11 October 2026, while the forward map's 12 October 03:08:26 UTC timestamp is a receipt time, not a theorem date.

## 2. The stronger saving in the actual paired units

Write c_s,d_s for first genuine support widths, to distinguish them from the zero-free constant. The actual signed row has

    W=M-R-(c_s-d_s)_+ +L_c-6a,
    L_c<=5(R-R0), R<=min(c_s,d_s).

For the other first side exchange C,D and use its own signed residue. The original actual child width, including its separate omega, g2 and t2 terms, is unchanged; W here is the high-row enclosing width, not a replacement child-width formula.

LA.13 gives, in the final joint paired exponent,

    E1=(1-rho)(c_s-d_s)_+-delta c_s-(1+rho)R-E-Bc+rho L_c+R0,
    E2=g2-t2-(1+delta)b2.

Put k(delta)=rho(delta)+delta-1. On [.68,.70], 5rho>1, 4rho-1>0 and rho<=2/5. With m=min(c_s,d_s), T=(c_s-d_s)_+,

    E1 <= -(delta-4rho+1)m-k(delta)T-E-Bc
       <= -k(delta)c_s,
    E2 <= -delta b2-t2,

because (delta-4rho+1)-k(delta)=2-5rho>=0. Here c_s=m+T, so the saving has its full coefficient, with no extra averaging by two.

Let rbar=(r_clip,1+r_clip,2)/2 and zbar=(z_1+z_2)/2 for the two actual surviving slot lists after the full second-projector allocation. PR9 B3.69 pays the divisor dyad by the two exact scalars. Separately, the plain pointwise exponent contains -delta rbar. Keeping this term does not spend either scalar again. The weighted row estimate replaces the paired slot price delta zbar by gamma zbar, saving eta zbar. These are all terms in the SAME paired joint exponent as E1 and E2. Applying Cauchy to the two live slot products produces rho W+gamma zbar, so it introduces no omitted factor two.

Set s=c_s+b2+rbar. Since delta>=k(delta)>0, the already present support and projector terms save at least k(delta)s. There are two exhaustive cases.

* If s>=z, they alone save k(delta)z. No weighted estimate or positive row width is needed in this case.
* If s<z, the conditional frozen-slot transport gives zbar>=z-s-small. Also

      W>=M-c_s-6a>=M-z-6a.

  Require M-6a>22z. Then W>21z and each individual z_j<=z satisfies the raw weighted lemma's restriction. The combined saving is at least

      k(delta)s+eta(delta)(z-s)-small
        =k(delta)s+2k(delta)(z-s)-small
        >=k(delta)z-small.

The equality eta=2k is exact. The minimum k on this interval is k(.70)=7/135; at q=.68, k(q)=391/6825. Thus the controller's proposed 7z/135 follows, and retaining k(delta)z is stronger. All endpoint, bin, clipping and source losses are charged to one preallocated small power, not once per slot.

There is no conditional transfer from an exceptional summand and no cross-label reserve exchange. Empty-support nonexceptional rows receive the weighted saving directly. Rows losing all slots fall in the first case. The width test is needed only in the second case. These facts prevent the two principal possible double-spending errors.

## 3. Tilted plane and every local branch

Put q=17/25, Ka=34/21, rho_q=rho(q), k_q=k(q), and

    D=q+(5-6rho_q)Ka=81379/15925,
    B0=14200/14361,
    Lambda_old=19312/4787,
    Lambda=Lambda_old-k_q/D=57775/14361,
    B=B0-3/500000=7099956917/7180500000.

This is a new tilted local plane n1+n2+Lambda z<=BM. B is only 4/1000000 above the old c6 intercept; most of the gain is in the smaller slot slope. It must not be compared to the fixed-slope trials by intercept alone.

Keep the same 600 original-slot cells b_j=.034+j/100000, j=1,...,600; cell=1/100000 and alpha=1/400000. Fix the physical amplifier from the original cell, before profiles, children or live scales:

    g_j=B-1+(9/2-Lambda)b_j,
    a_j/M=Ka g_j+alpha,
    A_j=B-(Lambda-1)b_(j-1).

At q the new high reserve is

    H_j=1-rho_q-q A_j-(5-6rho_q)a_j/M+k_q b_(j-1).

Its cell slope vanishes exactly, by the chosen Lambda. Low reserve remains 7/30000000. Including cell rounding and alpha, the exact limiting intercept for this plane is

    Bcap=B0-[q(Lambda-1)cell+(5-6rho_q)alpha+k_q cell]/D
        =6163068817207/6232980368000.

Bcap is approximately .988783608055, and B lies strictly below it. The actual high reserve is 1230658453/457397850000000. The stronger width reserve at the worst cell is

    1-6a_max/M-22/25=1461650461/33509000000>0.

Thus the weighted estimate is eligible throughout the new branch. On [.68,.70], k'=1-50/[3(5-2delta)^2]>=-139/486. Since z/M<=1/25, the lower bound for the derivative of H(delta)+k(delta)z/M is the old high derivative minus 139/12150. It is positive, exactly 4456776045796133/16857397761750000. Therefore checking q suffices over this entire interval. For [.70,.75] discard the new gain and retain the old high branch: its reserve at .70 is 2901555283/753952500000, and its old monotonicity remains positive. Buffered bins use their original aggregate O(e) endpoint budget.

Every remaining atlas quantity is affine in b_j, so its two endpoint values certify all 600 cells. Exact positive minima include:

|---|---:|
| first extracted error | 575224213/482529600000 |

The original three squared Gauss extraction scalars, normalized prime average, 6a radius increment, omega padding, global error-slot price 3/4, deletion rate 1/6, first-zero powerful-product bound, artificial-zero allowance and physical comparison cost are all retained as in the frozen candidate. The three extracted errors are not amplified a second time. Nothing in the new gain changes these source operations.

Choose the eventual power-loss budget below the smallest positive margin, then the source/fine slot mesh, profile degrees, height exponents and tail orders in the same order as [private research revision]. The new raw-width margin is strict and numerical. The small endpoint saving below requires a correspondingly smaller fixed tolerance; it does not change the quantifier order.

The geometry is

    h=397683/500000=.795366,

Keep d0=1/200, t0=1/1000 and d_-=h-1/1000. Set d_+=h+10^-12. The new endpoint saving is v=10^-10. The selected plain upper cutoff remains N=264/625. statement:
## 3. Exact moving cuts and the small-source estimate

Fix an ordinary Dirichlet character chi modulo q with its natural zeros,
and a prime p not dividing q. Put a(n)=mu(n)chi(n), h(n)=chi(n),
q_p=delta_1-p chi(p)delta_p, c_p=q_p*a, and b_p=q_p*h. Then

    b_p(l) = chi(l)(1-p 1_{p|l}).

It has period Q=pq and zero mean. The sum over a period equals
p(1-chi(p)) times the character sum modulo q, which is zero for a
nonprincipal character and also zero for a principal character because
chi(p)=1. All squareful terms introduced by the compensator remain present.
The coefficients of c_p are bounded by p+1.

Fix 1/2<gamma<1, integer k>2, 1<b<=2gamma, and

    r=(k-2gamma)/(k-2), L=X^gamma, M=X^r,
    eta=1/(100kpq), B(n)=min(L,eta X^k/n^(k-1)).

For tau=tau_X in [0,1] fixed before the shell variable x is chosen, set
U(n)=B(n)^tau and V(n)=B(n)^(1-tau). Use B^0=1, including when B<1.
For each physical integer n, freeze these two numbers before applying the
ordinary convolution identity. This yields the exact coefficient identity

    c_p(n)=Q_U(n)+Q_V(n)-S_tau(n)+R_tau(n),

where Q_U(n)=sum_{de=n}q_p(e)a(d)1_{d<=U(n)}, Q_V is analogous, and

    S_tau(n)=sum_{de l=n; d<=U(n),e<=V(n)} a(d)a(e)b_p(l),
    R_tau(n)=sum_{de l=n; d>U(n),e>V(n)} a(d)a(e)b_p(l).

This is a coefficientwise identity, not one convolution with globally fixed
cutoffs. Ordered pairs, strict complements, and both endpoints tau=0,1
must be retained. It remains valid for B<1. At interior tau and B<1 the
small sums disappear and R is the complete coefficient; at endpoint tau the
cutoff equal to one must still be treated literally.

For f_x(n)=exp(-n/x^b-i(n/x)^k), x in the full real shell [X,2X], the two
short sums have total absolute bound
(p+1)(floor(L^tau)+floor(L^(1-tau))) <<_p L.

The moving small source has the stronger full pointwise bound

    |sum_n S_tau(n)f_x(n)| <<_{p,q,k} L,

uniformly in tau and real x. Here is the decisive row calculation. For
0<tau<1, a contributing ordered pair satisfies d<=L^tau, e<=L^(1-tau).
Write W=max(d^(1/tau),e^(1/(1-tau))). Then de<=W<=L, and its exact allowed
l-values form the single prefix

    l <= (eta X^k/W)^(1/(k-1))/(de).

For tau=0 one has d=1,W=e; for tau=1 one has e=1,W=d. These are genuine
endpoint formulas, not limiting conventions that discard a row.

Expand the zero-mean periodic b_p into its nonzero Fourier modes. In each
mode the real phase divided by 2pi is

    F(t)=jt/Q-(de t/x)^k/(2pi),  1<=j<=Q-1.

On the whole permitted row, de(de t)^(k-1)<=eta X^k. Consequently the
negative correction to F' has magnitude at most k eta/(2pi), and the
monotone discrete phase increments stay a fixed distance at least 1/(2Q)
from the integers. The elementary discrete first-derivative estimate gives
an O_Q(1) bound for every undamped prefix. Abel summation against the actual
decreasing damping exp(-de t/x^b) preserves O_Q(1). There are at most
floor(L^tau)floor(L^(1-tau))<=L rows. This proves the assertion. An alias
region has not been discarded: coefficients outside the permitted small
prefix belong to the exact R complement.

This is more than a relabeling of a norm: it pays the actual small source

## 8. All-height zero exclusion and broader fixed-parameter scope

The remaining sufficient input is exactly OPEN-LC: one common
gamma<gamma11 chosen before chi, and for each fixed ordinary chi a fixed
covering pair of unramified primes p1,p2, such that for every epsilon>0
and every sufficiently large dyadic X an allowed shell-fixed tau_X gives

    integral_X^(2X)|T_tau_X,p,chi,X(x)| dx/x
           <<_{chi,p,gamma,epsilon} X^(gamma+epsilon).         (OPEN)

The whole finite sum, every real shell point, strict/closed physical cuts,
natural zeros and ordered divisor count are part of this hypothesis.
Tau_X may depend on epsilon because (R11) is uniform and C itself is
fixed. A full squared norm O(X^(2gamma+epsilon)) is a stronger sufficient
input; no L1-to-L2 implication or projected-subset substitute is asserted.

(R11) transfers OPEN to the fixed C. Its Mellin transform is holomorphic
on Re z>gamma by dyadic shell summation, including every fixed derivative
and arbitrary finite height compact sets. Polynomially bounded coefficients
and exp(-n/x^(3/2)) pay x near zero. First perform absolute Fubini only on
Re z>3/2, choosing the coefficient divisor exponent smaller than the
available real-part buffer.

For I_n(z)=integral exp(-nt^(3/2)-i(nt)^6)t^(z-1)dt, put v=nt and
rotate clockwise by fixed 0<theta<min(pi/3,pi/12). Principal powers are
retained. For each n, positive damping real part kills the large sector
arc; Re z>0 kills the small arc. On the rotated ray exp(-iv^6) supplies
exp(-c|v|^6). A one-term Taylor remainder for exp(-n^(-1/2)v^(3/2))
therefore gives, locally uniformly in Re z>0,

    I_n(z)=A0(z)n^(-z)+R_n(z),
    A0(z)=Gamma(z/6)exp(-i pi z/12)/6,
    R_n(z)=O_K(n^(-Re z-1/2)).

Derivatives have the corresponding logarithmic factors and compact
majorants. Because |c(n)|<<_delta n^delta for every delta>0, the remainder
sum is normally holomorphic on Re z>1/2. This justifies

    H_p(z)=A0(z)P_p(z)J_p(z)L(2z,chi^2)^2/L(z,chi)+E_p(z).     (R14)

A0 is nonzero and holomorphic on Re z>0, and J_p L(2z,chi^2)^2 is finite
and nonzero on Re z>1/2. Possible masking by P_p is confined to Re z=1.
For two distinct primes, a common nonzero-height zero would make their
logarithm ratio rational because character values are roots of unity;
unique factorization forbids it. For nonprincipal chi choose p1 with
chi(p1)!=1 to cover height zero. Such a prime exists by factoring a unit
integer with nontrivial character value. At height zero in the principal
case the pole at1 is the stated exception. Thus every candidate ordinary
zero in Re z>gamma is covered, with no height-uniform constant required.
Natural imprimitive Euler factors are present from the outset.

The author's broader fixed b,k claim is also valid at its conditional
scope. Its single-square high price is
X^(b/2)A^(-1/2)+(X/A)^(k/(2k-1)); when b>=2k/(2k-1), the first term
dominates for A>=1. Minkowski then pays short rows when
alpha<=(4gamma-b)/3. For any fixed gamma>1/2 one can choose fixed
1<b<=2gamma and sufficiently large fixed k so this corridor is nonempty
and the generic complete tail is paid. This is not arithmetic progress
toward gamma=1/2.

For that broader return retain every j<K term
A_j(z)D_c(z+(b-1)j), with

    A_j(z)=(-1)^j Gamma((z+bj)/k)
                    exp(-i pi(z+bj)/(2k))/(k j!),

and choose fixed K with 1-(b-1)K<gamma. The remainder is normally
holomorphic above that line in Re z>0. Starting above1, descend finitely
many strips of width b-1: every positive-shift reciprocal is already
holomorphic before solving for the unshifted reciprocal with the same
two-prime cover. No shift, boundary pole or positive numerator factor is
discarded. Growing b,k,K,p or q are outside the proved statements.
title: 8. All-height zero exclusion and broader fixed-parameter scope

## 7. A fixed coefficient counterexample strengthens the diagnosis

There is a real obstruction to any coefficient-blind power improvement, beyond the particular form of(5.5). Replace mu_K(a) in(5.2) by the FIXED sequence
    b(a)=mu_K(a)² conjugate(eta(a))
on the S-coprime ideals, so b(a)eta(a)=mu_K(a)². It is still squarefree-supported, bounded, and independent of f,k,X. Along every principal channel, the sum is positive.

For any fixed A>0, uniformly over q_Q<=X^A,
    sum_(X<q_a<=2X,(a,SQ)=1) mu_K(a)²
          >>_(S,A,epsilon) X^(1-epsilon).              (7.1)
The proof in support.md uses elementary ideal counting, inclusion–exclusion and the positive density product product_(p|SQ)(1+q_p^-1)^-1. The errors are O_S(sqrt X logX S_(1/2)(Q)); divisor products are subpower when q_Q is polynomial inX.

The Gaussian has a positive lower bound on this annulus. Therefore every corresponding positive U_Q(x) is X^(1-o(1)) on the full shell, and its principal bank has energy X^(2-o(1)). In the full normalized joint bank the principal pairs alone contribute
    Z^(N+R-o(1)).                                     (7.2)
Thus a bound strong enough to force c>0 cannot hold uniformly for all such column coefficients. A useful improvement must use the actual Möbius signs (or a genuinely different signal-carrying observation). A new orthogonality argument that only improves the coefficient-blind operator envelope cannot remove this obstruction.
title: 7. A fixed coefficient counterexample strengthens the diagnosis

Let H=L2(I), where I is a fixed bounded interval of positive length. For the
unprojected Q(i) family, write each good ideal uniquely as m=c d² with c
squarefree, allowing c,d to overlap, and put

    B_m(t)=mu_K(c)chi2(d)Nd^(1+it),
    F_k(x)(t)=sum_m B_m(t)k(log(Nm/x)).

The coefficients are fixed before x. Elementary ideal counting gives
sum_(Nm<=Y)||B_m||_H=O_I(Y log(2Y)). This pays the infinite sums, compact
left tails and Gaussian tails. The already proved scalar smoothing maps
therefore act on the whole H-valued family:

    F_new=S_no F_old,       F_G=S_gn F_new.

For every fixed a>0, their norm costs are the finite quantities
C_h(a)=integral |h(v)|exp(av)dv. Smoothing changes the scale profile and acts
as the identity on the retained phase coordinate. The phase family's
complementary numerator information survives.

The exact square-dilation formation of F_t from F_K also commutes with
smoothing on the absolute convergence domain. That identity supplies no
bounded square-dilation map at the desired exponent: its unattenuated
absolute cost still loses the gain, as the preceding integration explains.

different sources; this theorem does not identify them.

statement:
# W57-14: a flat residue cover does not create a twisted Mobius index

This is the protected hard/upstream development, following the independently frozen seed. It is a self-contained finite construction and a scoped obstruction, not a bound for M_chi. The elementary squarefree-complex/cone and weighted-commutator ancestry is U-PRIME-CHAIN, W27, G74, W53 T16, W54 X30 and W55 S21. W56 further supplies the complete persistence splitting and paid fixed/moving-window return. The specific proposed residue-cover repair is tested explicitly here; the classical cone, character defect and return are not new claims, and no literature novelty is claimed.

## 1. The exact finite object

Fix an ordinary Dirichlet character chi modulo q. Include only primes not dividing q. For real X>=1 let K_X have the finite prime sets S with n(S)=product_{p in S}p<=X, including the empty set. Let C have orthonormal basis e_S, graded by |S|, and the augmented deletion differential

    d e_S = sum_{j=1}^{|S|} (-1)^(j-1) e_(S minus {p_j}),
    p_1<...<p_|S|.

The empty face has degree0, so this is the usual augmented complex with all degrees shifted by1. It has d^2=0. Put D_chi e_S=chi(n(S))e_S. Then, literally,

    Str(D_chi)=sum_S (-1)^|S| chi(n(S))=M_chi(X).       (T1)

All squareful and ramified integers have their actual zero coefficient. A homological Euler characteristic would require a chain map. Direct calculation gives

    [D_chi,d] e_S
      =sum_j (-1)^(j-1) chi(n(S)/p_j)(1-chi(p_j))
                         e_(S minus {p_j}).            (T2)

For a local deletion differential with coefficient c(S,p), commutation with D_chi forces c(S,p)=0 whenever chi(p)!=1. The target spaces for different deletions are distinct, so there is no within-column cancellation of this condition. This holds for every cutoff and every fixed character.

## 2. The proposed cover: a precise gauge obstruction

Let G=(Z/qZ)^* and put one regular G-register on every face. On basis e_(S,g), define

    d_cov e_(S,g)=sum_j (-1)^(j-1)e_(S minus {p_j},g p_j).

Residues commute, so d_cov^2=0. The bijective relabeling

    U e_(S,g)=e_(S,g n(S))

conjugates d_cov to d tensor I: deleting p and replacing g by gp leaves g n(S) unchanged. Thus the cover is a disjoint gauge copy of the original complex, not a new contracting complex. Equivalently, in the Fourier sector spanned on each face by sum_g chi(g)^(-1)e_(S,g), its differential is

    d_chi e_S=sum_j (-1)^(j-1)chi(p_j)e_(S minus {p_j}).

This is D_chi^(-1) d D_chi. Every character sector has exactly one chain basis vector per face. Its Euler index is therefore sum_S(-1)^|S|=M_chi0(X), where chi0 is principal modulo q, independently of chi. Changing this differential cannot change those chain dimensions. The same conclusion holds for any differential on these fixed finite Fourier chain groups.

A small actual-character counterexample is q=3, chi(1)=1, chi(2)=-1, X=5. The unit squarefree faces are empty,{2},{5}. Their untwisted index is 1-1-1=-1, whereas M_chi(5)=1+1+1=3. The Fourier complex has boundary row (-1,-1), but its index remains -1. Thus assigning prime phases to the differential does not supply the required return.

A conserved residue label h=g n(S) gives a chain-map insertion chi(h), but tracing over the full regular register gives zero for nonprincipal chi. Restricting to an anchored slice g=1 recovers the desired weights and loses commutation. This is an exact choice of readout, not a growing-conductor objection or a mere missing dimension factor.

## 3. Cone contraction and its complete character defect

Let ell be the least prime not dividing q, and take X>=ell. The cone C_ell consists of the faces T without ell with n(T)<=X/ell and those T union {ell}. Since ell is the least available prime, every proper subface of a critical face

    S without ell, X/ell<n(S)<=X

belongs to C_ell: each deleted prime is greater than ell. The cone contraction h inserts ell on a face T of product<=X/ell lacking ell, and is zero otherwise. Ell is the first ordered prime, so the insertion orientation is +1. On cone chains, dh+hd=I. On a critical face, define

    P e_S=e_S-h d e_S;

and set P=0 on the cone. Then dh+hd=I-P, P^2=P, dP=Pd=0. This is verified directly because each critical boundary lies in the cone. In particular the relative chain complex K_X/C_ell has zero differential. Its one critical face per basis element gives the full reduced homology (with the grading shift already stated).

Graded cyclicity gives the exact formula

    Str(D_chi)=Str(D_chi P)+Str((D_chi d-d D_chi)h).     (T3)

Put c=chi(ell),

    A(Y)=sum_{n<=Y, ell not dividing n}mu(n)chi(n),
    B(X)=sum_{X/ell<n<=X, ell not dividing n}mu(n)chi(n).

The two terms of T3 are exactly

    Str(D_chi P)=B(X),
    Str((D_chi d-d D_chi)h)=(1-c)A(X/ell).

Hence the proposed topological repair reduces to the fully signed prime-toggle identity

    M_chi(X)=B(X)+(1-c)A(X/ell).                       (T4)

No character phase or boundary face has disappeared. This identity also follows by pairing n and ell*n and agrees with the earlier prime-toggle ancestry. For q=3,ell=2,X=5, B=1 from n=5 and A(5/2)=1 from n=1; T4 gives 1+2=3, as required.

## 4. Why unsigned homology still costs exponent1

The rank of P is exactly

    H_q(X)=#{X/ell<n<=X: mu(n)^2=1, (n,q ell)=1}.

For every fixed integer r, the elementary square-divisor identity and coprime counting give

    #{n<=x:mu(n)^2=1,(n,r)=1}=kappa_r x+O_r(sqrt x),
    kappa_r=(phi(r)/r) product_(p not dividing r)(1-p^-2)>0.

Indeed expand mu(n)^2=sum_(d^2|n)mu(d), retain (d,r)=1, and use #{m<=t:(m,r)=1}=(phi(r)/r)t+O_r(1); the d>sqrt x tail costs O_r(sqrt x). Therefore

    H_q(X)=kappa_(q ell)(1-1/ell)X+O_q(sqrt X).         (T5)

This proves the linear unsigned bill without importing a topological theorem or a prime-counting asymptotic. It is a lower bound for the rank/absolute homology certificate, NOT for the signed B or M_chi. For q=1 the coefficient is 2/pi^2. This elementary cone account reconstructs an existing obstruction and is not counted as a new arithmetic estimate.

## 5. An exact, quantitative return that remains eligible

Extend A and B by zero below1. Since B(X)=A(X)-A(X/ell), finite telescoping gives

    M_chi(X)=B(X)+(1-c)sum_(j>=1)B(X/ell^j),            (T6)

where terms below1 vanish. If for every epsilon>0 and all sufficiently large X,

    |B(X)| <<_(chi,epsilon) X^(gamma+epsilon),

for a common gamma>0, then the full M bound follows, with scale price at exponent alpha=gamma+epsilon

    1+|1-c|/(ell^alpha-1).                             (T7)

The finitely many bounded-scale terms add a fixed constant. Conversely the same bound on M implies one on A through A(X)=sum_(j>=0)c^j M(X/ell^j), and hence on B. Thus the complete signed critical-face estimate is exponent-equivalent to the original problem; topology has not supplied it.

Near gain gamma=.8748, gamma=5/6 and gamma=3/4 are all permitted by this return. T5 gives only exponent1. The serious upstream attempt therefore fails at the intended repair: the flat cover is gauge trivial, while a true weighted readout restores the exact unpaid commutator/critical signed sum.

Further escape condition: alter the chain groups/readout or permit genuinely nonlocal, phase-changing interactions and prove their complete signed transfer. Merely changing deletion weights or taking Fourier sectors of this regular cover cannot do it. For a real quadratic chi, a squarefree product of primes with chi(p)=-1 has mu(n)chi(n)=+1; no chi-preserving odd deletion entirely within that prime set can reverse its sign. Cancellation must couple this sector to other arithmetic states. This is a coefficient-level observation, not a density or impossibility theorem for M_chi.

## 6. The sampled W57-13 annular test

For the principal character, the alternating relative chain count of (K_X,K_(X/Y)) is exactly M_chi0(X)-M_chi0(X/Y). A character-weighted relative count remains a formal trace with the T2 commutator; it is not automatically a relative Euler index. Let b(K) denote total reduced Betti dimension in the augmented convention. Exactness of the long homology sequence gives

    b(K_X,K_(X/Y)) >= b(K_X)-b(K_(X/Y)).                (T8)

Combining T5 with T8 gives, for every fixed Y>1,

    b(K_X,K_(X/Y)) >=
      kappa_(q ell)(1-1/ell)(1-1/Y)X-O_q(sqrt X).

More generally, for ANY finite increasing filtration ending at X, the sum of total relative Betti dimensions is at least b(K_X) minus the starting Betti dimension, by repeated T8. Refining into thinner annuli cannot lower that complete unsigned bill below its linear endpoint value when the starting Betti dimension is o(X). This includes changing finite filtrations at each X. The sampled proposal therefore fails for an unsigned-relative-homology estimate. A signed index pairing across annuli is not excluded; it would need a bound not obtained by summing those Betti dimensions. This is a first test and a consequence of the cone calculation, not a fourth independent development.

## 2. Exact source family and the positive norm

Work in `O=Z[omega]`, use ideal norm `N`, sum column ideals through primary generators, and retain the six possible units of element rows. Fix the original finite dictionary, one complete orientation, the fixed bad-prime set S, and one natural presentation

    phi_u(n)=nu(n) psi_u(n),  psi_u(n)=chi_n(u)^(+/-1).        (C1)

The columns avoid S. All zeroth and sixth powers retain their original zero extensions. The fixed character nu may have order not dividing six; it remains in the coefficient and is never relabeled as a sextic row phase. A whole conjugation is permitted. Conjugating only nu is not that operation.

Start with the exact free-row family of PR15 PlainUnmarkedDensity: nonzero u with every ideal valuation less than six, natural coefficient dictionary, `Nu<=C U`. Remove precisely the fixed-inducing exclusions of the original fixed dictionary. They form a fixed finite set: their prime support is fixed, their valuations are at most five, and there are six units per ideal. This is PR15's explicit exception argument, not a guess from nonprincipality. One may instead retain those rows; the bounds below for nontrivial *relative* characters remain valid with or without that finite set. This latter version is necessary when a direct target/unit-row norm is requested.

Use the genuine disjoint, row-independent canonical prime pools. The slot count is fixed before U grows; their common profile, fixed ray coefficients, bounded real powers, independent heights and frozen extra holes are retained. Write `v=sum z_i<=1/20` and

    Q_u=U^(-v/2) sum_P alpha(P) psi_u(P),                 (C2)

where P selects one prime from each ORIGINAL pool and all fixed factors have been re-anchored into alpha by the accepted dictionary identity. The empty product v=0 is allowed. No arbitrary prime mask is substituted into MP. The proofs here are new elementary coefficient/row estimates, not an application of MP to a new coefficient.

Choose a nonnegative smooth radial majorant Phi, equal to at least one on the requested row ball, with fixed compact support. **Choose it on the positive norm BEFORE expansion.** A requested original row subset and a positive divisor/radial weight bounded by `U^epsilon` are dominated by `U^epsilon` times this clean full natural-row norm. This does not allow Poisson on an amplitude-selected row set, nor comparison of two signed subsums after changing their weights. We use the majorant norm as the explicit sufficient OPEN-C contract.

For a real interval I containing the required zeros and an enlarged height interval, put

    ||F||_U^2 = sum_(u free, eligible) Phi(Nu/U)
      sum_(i,j in {0,1}) int_I int_[-T-1,T+1]
        |partial_sigma^i partial_tau^j F_u(s)|^2 d tau d sigma,
    s=sigma+i tau.                                      (C3)

Finitely many orientations, labels and additional required fixed derivatives cost their original finite sum. Fixed row ray conditions may be expanded in their finite ray group. The threshold precedes the height; powers in all independent heights are denoted H_J. A common fixed row coprimality hole may be retained by its full Möbius expansion below. All its norms and other raw scales are in fixed polynomial ranges.

This is an explicit version of [restricted research revision] review R9. For comparison with a bin `delta in[17/25,7/10]`, the nominal lower edge is `(1+delta)/2`. A small real buffer is priced in Section7. No high-zero indicator is inserted in the sum in (C3).

## HCR1. Disposition and actual input

I accept B0--B9a as an independently checked analytic construction and
conditional return, with exactly the all-dyad hypotheses stated below.
B9b's bounded partner correction is valid with a fixed positive baseline
buffer. B11--B12a are valid continuous-density calculations, including
the even correction, and establish no estimate for the actual Mobius
field. B13--B18 retain the literal coefficients and pay the two indicated
infinite complements. B19--B21 identify a genuine failure of the proposed
baseline-only proof, without proving that the arithmetic target is false.

To avoid confusing the filter parameter A with its coefficients, write

    a_n = mu(n) - 2*1_(2|n)*mu(n/2),
    g_tau(v) = (2*pi*tau)^(-1/2) exp(-v^2/(2*tau)),
    f(u) = sum_(n>=1) a_n g_tau(log n-u),   tau>0 fixed.

If n=2^j m, m odd and squarefree, the actual coefficient is mu(m) for j=0,
-3 mu(m) for j=1, 2 mu(m) for j=2, and 0 for j>=3. It is 0 if m is not
squarefree. In particular a_1=1, a_2=-3, a_4=2; replacing a_n by mu(n), or
deleting all squareful n, changes the field. The uniform bound |a_n|<=3
is used only for an absolute source tail, not for the main signed norm.

The ordinary buffered Mertens consequence of the accepted baseline is
used in its actual form: for EACH FIXED beta>b_* one has
M(y)=O_beta(y^beta). There is no estimate at beta=b_* or one uniform as
beta decreases to b_*. This is the ordinary interface already used by the
author; the external endpoint itself is a stipulated controller input,
not re-proved here. Every quantitative finite-source calculation uses the
old-safe exponent b=.8749, so the tiny baseline update changes none of its
tail estimates.

The summatory function of a_n is M(y)-2M(y/2). Partial summation against
g_tau therefore gives |f(u)|<=C_b exp(bu), u>=0, for each fixed b>b_*.
For u<=0, the direct absolutely convergent series gives

    |f(u)| <= C_tau exp(-u^2/(2*tau)).

Indeed (log n-u)^2 >= u^2+(log n)^2 there, and the remaining n-series
converges. Thus the left-tail transform

    E(s)=integral_(-infinity)^0 f(u) exp(-su) du

is entire. Initially by absolute Dirichlet convergence in Re s>1, and
then by continuation in Re s>b_*,

    Phi(s)=integral_R f(u) exp(-su) du
          =exp(tau*s^2/2)*(1-2^(1-s))/zeta(s),
    F(s)=integral_0^infinity f(u) exp(-su) du=Phi(s)-E(s).

The last identity continues F meromorphically to C. Every nontrivial
zeta zero in 0<Re s<1 gives a pole of F of the same order: the Gaussian
factor never vanishes, and the zeros of 1-2^(1-s) all have Re s=1.
Subtracting the entire E cannot remove a pole.

Fallback: a rigorously summed thin small-gcd band, or an actual two-slot cumulant identity with its principal addbacks. Stop if the argument merely re-proves the paid large-gcd estimate or assumes positivity of a gcd-localized zero form.

### 2. Coefficient-specific short-divisor H

Write the exact projected column and three source families in SG, beginning with the actual \(e=1,b=1\) kernel. Retain both removed diagonals, all powerful parts, moving periods, original profiles and fixed sectors. Prove the cheap restriction calculation before choosing a trace formula.

The target replaces \(K+NB\) by \(K\) in the narrow all-branch budget. A two-/three-prime transformed identity with conductor and diagonal terms is a useful first milestone; a local complete-sum estimate alone is not enough. Close the other branches explicitly before using the .12551 certificate.

### 3. Frozen-dyad Möbius energy

Use T09's fixed \(\phi\) and finite \(\mathcal B_X\), with cutoffs frozen over each dyad. Expand the whole signed weighted shift kernel. The \(O(X)\) diagonal is affordable for the intended \(a>.5\); shifts of order \(X\), shared primes and product coincidences remain.

Seek one signed off-diagonal aggregate whose full coefficient and endpoint accounting meets exponent 1.74898. A narrower result is useful only if the omitted regions can be summed at the same target. Equal Mellin resonances cannot be discarded, and log-scale averaging does not imply short-shift support.

Fallback: continuum-dilation cross-scale energy T10, or an exact controlled comparison with affine variance. First derive the overlap/weight/endpoints; a generic Poincaré inequality supplies no Möbius saving.

### 4. Completed cube-free mean and finite incidence

Start with the ordinary face \(b=1\) of \(ab^2\) after the actual current/test calibration. Average current covariance before separate pointwise estimates. T04's inverse edge is already paid and should not be the sole output.

Test a forced-prime-first dyad or first-admissible-divisor partition entirely inside \(G\le CK^{28/65}\). The \(g=1\) term still contains a substantial ordinary mean.

### 6. Whole signed cubic remainder

Use T05 to compare the physical principal-cube remainder to C–C with a strictly affordable Type I error. At \(k=.8765\), the inherited principal upper budget is \(D^{2.000773294079928262\ldots}\); improving that term alone still leaves the much larger nonprincipal loss.

## D48: the block sum mode remains the hard source

For v_s(u)=g_tau(s-u),0<=u<=log2, the pivot after eliminating v_s from v_(s+epsilon) is

    epsilon^2 [||v_s'||^2-|<v_s,v_s'>|^2/||v_s||^2]+O(epsilon^3).

The bracket equals ||v_s||^2 Var_(v_s^2)(u)/tau^2. It is positive and has a positive minimum on the compact physical s interval. With epsilon=log(1+1/n), n in[X,2X], the pivot is comparable to n^-2. The larger eigenvalue is comparable to1, so condition number is comparable to n^2. This is a genuine native Gaussian conditioning statement; it is not a lower bound for the actual f3 energy in that direction, or for H.

For any fixed |a(n)|<=1, define b_B(j)=sum_((j-1)B<n<=jB)a(n), and V_B(x)=sum_j b_B(j)g_tau(log(jB/x)). Put k_x(t)=g_tau(log(t/x)). Its variation on(0,infinity) is2g_tau(0). On a block, each segment[n,jB] is contained in it, and at most B such segments cover any point. Hence

    |F_a(x)-V_B(x)| <= B integral_0^infinity |k_x'(t)|dt
                     =2B g_tau(0).                  (AS2-2)

This includes the first block, both infinite tails, every valuation and every signed coefficient. At0 the Gaussian is flat with limit0. No coefficient deletion or positive-submask monotonicity is used. For B_X=floor(X^theta) frozen for the entire shell and0<=theta<gamma, the complete norm exponent gamma for V_(B_X) is equivalent to that for fixed F_a. All interblock cross terms remain. This coordinate reduction does not reduce amplitudes: |b_B| can equal B.

For literal f3, f3(2j)=(1-2*1_(2 not dividing j))f3(j), so the displayed b_2 is correct for all powers of2. Multiplication by fixed chi preserves all ramified zeros. The independent checks verify this identity through j=600 and exact signed block masses for a quartic mod5 character, including its zeros. These finite facts do not certify an infinite moment.

For FIXED B and e_B(n)=Bceil(n/B),

    E_B(s)=sum_n a(n)[n^-s-e_B(n)^-s]

is holomorphic on Re s>0. The derivative integral bounds the summand by |s|B n^(-Re s-1); compact-set s derivatives add only summable log powers. On Re s>1, D_B=D_a-E_B by absolute rearrangement. Thus subtracting E_B preserves every pole of D_a in Re s>0, including order and principal part.

For a=f3 chi the literal Euler numerator is

    W_chi(s)=(1-2chi(2)2^-s)

## 7. Exact norm, coefficients and the full sixth-power diagonal

Here is one precise implementation of the author's positive norm. Fix a finite dictionary label and one complete natural orientation, the original slot profiles/pools/real powers/independent heights, t and B, and a fixed real interval I=[a,b] with 1/2<a<b<1 containing the retained zeros. On a slightly enlarged height interval [-T-1,T+1], use the tensor Sobolev norm

    N_t(U)=sum_(u in R_U) w_u sum_(i,j in {0,1})
      integral_I integral_[-T-1,T+1]
       |partial_sigma^i partial_tau^j [D_R(s)Q_u]|^2 d tau d sigma,
    s=sigma+i tau.                                    (R9)

Here R_U is the exact original nonzero natural/eligible row set for the requested density, fixed before any zero event, with Nu<=C U; 0<=w_u<=U^epsilon is the original positive radial/divisor weight or its paid majorant. For the direct OPEN-H return replace this by all required natural rows Nu<=U, including the unit, and take w_1=1. The finite-dictionary union is its original fixed cost. No high-bin indicator is inserted into R9. A finite sum of such norms covers required derivative profiles and orientations.

Repeated one-dimensional Sobolev evaluation on these fixed-width rectangles dominates each row's value at a retained zero; constants are finite and independent of U. Slot heights stay independent of s. The derivatives introduce only logarithms of Nn and fixed polynomial height factors. R8 then bounds the weighted high-row mass by a constant times N_t, with a negligible error chosen after the raw row/slot power. This proves the sufficient density implication J18. The moment bound itself is not proved.

After merging all equal ideal products WITH signs, the literal coefficient is

    b_l(s)=U^(-v/2) sum_(nP=l, Nn>R)
       A_R(n)nu(n)(Nn)^(-s)e^(-Nn/Y) alpha(P).          (R10)

P selects one prime from each original disjoint pool. Every individual fixed character, smooth weight, bounded real norm power, independent height and frozen hole stays in alpha; nu retains the fixed factor on n. All row dependence is in the common sextic character psi_u(l), with natural zeros. The identity phi(nP)=phi(n)phi(P) is valid at shared primes as well. Fixed phases of order not dividing six stay in b_l. They are never declared sextic row phases.

This coefficient is outside UM, MI and MP's licensed column contract. In particular B3.6 forbids an arbitrary extra coefficient on its canonical column. Divisor boundedness of A_R is not a license to use that energy theorem. Splitting its divisor summands by triangle inequality discards the precise signs whose cross-class sum remains open.

For a fixed slot count, P has norm comparable to U^v, and its possible tuple factorizations for a given l are divisor-many. Since |A_R(n)| is divisor bounded and all fixed coefficients are contractions up to finite seminorms, for sigma in I,

    |b_l(s)| <= U^[(sigma-1/2)v+epsilon](Nl)^(-sigma),
    b_l=0 unless Nl>=c_0 U^(t+v).                      (R11)

The same estimate with an arbitrary small additional loss covers all derivatives in R9. A bound in l by a divisor power is paid by a small reduction of sigma; because the terminal support has fixed polynomial size, its residual U-power can be allocated to epsilon before choosing the bound. No cancellation is used here.

Write l=c a^6 with c sixth-power-free. The relevant diagonal includes every pair c a^6,c b^6, not just l=l'. For fixed row u, the row phases agree away from their natural zeros; those zeros are contractions. Therefore its entire within-class contribution is bounded by the squared sum of the absolute coefficients in that class. The actual within-class contribution of R9 is itself nonnegative, being a sum of class squares; using its absolute majorant is sufficient.

The required infinite ideal sum is elementary. Put H>=2 and sigma>1/2. For Nc>H, convergence of sum_a (Na)^(-6sigma) gives a bound C(Nc)^(-sigma) for the inner root sum. Its squared sum over c>H is O(H^(1-2sigma)) by ideal counting. For Nc<=H, set A=(H/Nc)^(1/6)>=1. Partial summation of the ideal count gives

    sum_(Na>=A)(Na)^(-6sigma) << A^(1-6sigma).

Hence the inner sum is at most H^(1/6-sigma)(Nc)^(-1/6). Squaring and summing c<=H costs H^(1/3-2sigma) times sum_(Nc<=H)(Nc)^(-1/3), which is O(H^(2/3)). Both ranges yield

    sum_(c sixth-free) [sum_(Nc Na^6>=H)(Nc Na^6)^(-sigma)]^2
      << H^(1-2sigma+epsilon).                         (R12)

Extending c from sixth-free ideals to all ideals only enlarges these bounds. There is no density assumption about squarefree ideals and no missing unequal-root term. Units, primary generators and fixed ray sectors change only a fixed factor. Divisor factors fit a small exponent loss uniformly on the compact sigma interval.

There are O(U^(1+epsilon)) actual rows. Combining R11--12 with H comparable to U^(t+v) gives the complete within-class bound

    D6_t(U) << U^[1-(2sigma-1)t+epsilon] H_J.            (R13)

For the integrated norm use the smallest sigma in I. The slot exponent cancels exactly: (2sigma-1)v+(1-2sigma)(t+v)=-(2sigma-1)t. Fixed phases, repeated ideals, unequal roots and natural zeros have all been priced. Additional cross-class coincidences on fixed-inducing rows are not assumed oscillatory; they remain in the signed target.

Let O6_t be the full REAL ordered cross-class contribution, including the row kernel, masks, weights and every derivative inner product in R9. Finite truncation justifies the exact split N_t=D6_t+O6_t before limits; the tails are already bounded. A one-sided upper bound on O6 is sufficient. No absolute value on each pair is required or proved.

At t=4/3 and sigma>=(1+delta)/2, R13 has exponent at most 7/75. Also delta-3k=4delta^2/(5-2delta)>0, so Eold(1,v)>=rho>=19/54. The full diagonal gap is 349/1350, leaving 23/2700 after a proposed density saving xi=1/4. Thus OPEN-C with any fixed 0<xi<=1/4, at the exact norm/family just specified, would imply J18. Small real buffers are absorbed in that retained positive gap. This is a density-input implication, not a zero-free constant 1/4 and not evidence that OPEN-C holds.

### 2.3 Explicit absolute extension to every core and prime integral

After the substitutions the main term is half of the ordered positive
prime-density integral, summed with f(r). For large X, log p,log q
are >1. To bound any omitted integral it therefore suffices to remove
those denominators and replace f by its absolute value 1.

There is a direct bound that does not appeal to a discrete divisor
count for continuous variables. With t=pq,

    integral_(p,q>=z) g(log(rpq/x))dpdq
       =integral_(z^2)^infinity log(t/z^2)g(log(rt/x))dt.

Write a=z^2/x=kappa^2/s in [kappa^2/2,kappa^2] and put u=log(rt/x).
Tonelli gives the exact positive full-core formula

    sum_r integral_(p,q>=z) g(log(rpq/x))dpdq
      =x integral_(log a)^infinity exp(u)g(u) W_a(u)du,
    W_a(u)=sum_(1<=r<=exp(u)/a) (u-log(ar))/r.          (R2.2)

Every summand of W_a is nonnegative. The harmonic bound and
0<=u-log(ar)<=u-log a show

    W_a(u)<=C_kappa(1+u_+)^2,  u>=log a.              (R2.3)

If r>X^d, then u>=dL+log a. If p>B_X or q>B_X while the other is
>=z, then u>=2dL+log(kappa/s), since r>=1. Thus every integral added
when extending cores and prime limits is bounded by the right side
of (R2.2) restricted to u>=dL-O_kappa(1). By (R2.3) its size is
O_A(X^-A) for any fixed A. This pays all continuous extension tails
uniformly on the closed x shell, including overlaps between removed
sets. No cancellation among cores is used.

Combining these bounds, the discrete source tails, both PNT errors,
and the diagonal gives the exact CT5 approximation

    R_z(x)=(1/2)sum_r f(r)
       integral_(p,q>z) g(log(rpq/x))dpdq/(log p log q)
                  +O_(tau,kappa)(X/L^4).              (R2.4)

The O(X/L^4) term comfortably includes the O(X/L^8) PNT errors and
the O(sqrt(X)) diagonal. It is valid before the density expansion.

## 6. Actual next obstruction and a deliberately coarse complete test

Two potentially attractive shortcuts were tested and fail at identifiable
source steps, not by an abstract nonexistence theorem.

First, applying the complete mu*1 cancellation to an individual selected
inverse/plain dyad is false. On the unmarked, fully coprime squarefree part of
(18), merge n=ab and extract the row factor psi_u(n)^(+/-1).
Then mu(a)=mu(n)mu(b), so the literal coefficient is

 c(n)=mu(n)nu(n)/(RD)^(1/2)
       sum_(b|n) mu(b)W_I(N(n/b)/R)W_P(Nb/D),           (21)

with the original tuple cuts and zeros. At a common height and real power,
the two norm twists DO combine into one function of Nn/(RD). This pays their
normalization exactly, but the divisor-profile sum in(21) remains arithmetic.
It is not a smooth profile of Nn, a fixed ray character or a coprimality mask.
An additional original prime-slot tuple contributes its own literal factors
and product coincidences; it does not change this conclusion.

For a transparent actual coefficient test, take two distinct unramified prime
ideals p,l with Np on the inverse annulus, Nl on the much shorter plain annulus,
and choose nonnegative smooth profiles nonzero at these two points with small
fixed relative supports. At n=pl, only a=p,b=l lies in those two annuli; a=l,
a=1 and a=pl do not. The coefficient is -nu(pl) times their nonzero normalized
weights, before any natural row zero. It lies in N(a,b)=1, s_2(b)=1 and hence
survives every G,H>1. This is a literal coefficient failure of dyadic divisor
cancellation, not an example of a high zero or saturation of a whole norm.
No density, positive lower bound for the complete moment or independence of
such rows is asserted. The completed cutoff identity G115 still holds only
after all its required divisor/dyadic pieces have been reconstructed.

Second, the original canonical energy B3.6 expressly permits NO further
coefficient on its squarefree column. The divisor-profile factor in(21) is
outside that contract. Divisor boundedness, the common height, empty support
and the tiny repeated-prime bound(20) do not license its removal. The usual
unmarked inverse theorem B3.39 also has actual mu(n) coefficients; it cannot
be applied to(21) just by writing a new symbol for this factor. Such an
extension would require a new proof using the displayed signed divisor law.

The complete coarse test makes the remaining deficit explicit. On Omega,
the SAME-bin bound(2), followed by marked MI, gives

    ||B Q||_Omega^2 << H_J U^(1+beta*m+epsilon).

Using B_c=B-B_g-B_s and the already proved estimates gives the same upper
power for ||B_c Q||_Omega^2, with every mixed term paid by Hilbert triangle.
On Omega_c the only available comparison back to the original inverse is

    |M_u(R)| <= 2|B_c(u)|/|S_u(D)|.

The plain lower bound therefore yields U^(1+epsilon), precisely the old
inverse moment. It supplies NO positive eta saving. Replacing this triangle
by an unsupported comparison with a signed subset would be the missing proof.

This pinpoints the next arithmetic repair without a scalar re-optimization:
estimate the signed divisor-profile source(18)/(21), with its near-coprime
inverse/plain factors and small repeated-prime part, on the same buffered
large-plain rows. An estimate only for a different canonical coefficient,
for averaged unrelated heights, or for selected q/k terms is insufficient.
The full core with its actual product signal(7) is now the only unpaid source
inside this crossing window. It is not known to be easier merely because it
has been renamed. The substantive new progress is(5)--(6) and the exact,
overlap-paid support reduction(18)--(20), not a claimed solution of that core.

Include the enlarged fixed MI system and its required orders in the initial source/height choices before selecting these witnesses. Work only in its original crossing window |r-r_*(t)|<=2eta, including the preallocated small endpoint padding. Let R=U^r and D=U^m. Here m is bounded away from zero, and the two witnesses have the SAME natural character, real power, height and retained zero. Fix the internal bin, label and dyads before each norm. Omega contains only the licensed nonprincipal supported-witness rows; principal, artificial and separate fixed-inducing branches retain their original treatment.

Write phi_u=nu psi_u^(+/-1), with one common orientation. Fixed finite phases need not have order dividing six. Retain the original S omission, primary/unit convention, all natural zeros and fixed holes. The actual normalized polynomials are

    M_u(E)=E^(-1/2) sum_a mu(a)phi_u(a)W_I(Na/E),
    S_u(E)=E^(-1/2) sum_b phi_u(b)W_P(Nb/E).

Q_u is the COMPLETE original product of disjoint prime slots of total width v. Its count is fixed before U, its individual heights remain independent, and its original coefficients, supports and holes stay literal. PR9 B0.3--4 and B3.31 permit arbitrary bounded row-independent prime coefficients in MI, with either common orientation and every subcollection. The additional band slot is in precisely that contract. Any licensed re-anchoring or whole conjugation is done to the whole system first; an unrelated moving character is not inserted into a prime coefficient.

Let beta=2a-1 be the selected INTERNAL buffered grade. It may exceed physical delta. The retained same-family upper bound keeps beta<=3/4, while beta>=delta-small. PR9 B0.13--20 and the already reviewed [restricted research revision]/[restricted research revision] interface give

    |S_u(D)|^2 >= D^beta U^(-epsilon_det),
    |S_u(E;V)|^2 <= H_J U^epsilon_det E^beta,
                    0<E<=C D.                         (R1)

The direct line a+6e suffices for the second inequality. V ranges over the stated common smooth family and finite derivative profiles, at retained heights. Nonempty subunit scales are bounded dilations; scales below a fixed positive constant are empty. H_J is a polynomial in the height bounds, independent of the arithmetic thresholds below. Its fixed degree may increase between inequalities.

Keep beta in BOTH inequalities until D^beta cancels. Weakening the spike to D^delta earlier would leave an uncontrolled D^(beta-delta). No larger internal grade is used as a physical slot price.

Put A=U^(2eta), Y=U^(4eta), and let P_band be the fixed band of good prime IDEALS with A<=Np<=Y. Define

    ell_B(b)=sum_(p in P_band) v_p(b) log Np,
    theta(b)=ell_B(b)/log Nb, Nb>1; theta(1)=0.

The additive function is ell_B, not theta: ell_B(bc)=ell_B(b)+ell_B(c), with shared valuations counted. For example theta(p)=theta(p^2)=1 when p is in the band, so theta itself cannot be expanded additively. The original plain annulus has Nb>1 for sufficiently large U.

For any complete tuple polynomial, superscript[theta] means multiplying each original tuple coefficient by theta of its PLAIN ideal before signed merging. It is not a norm projection. With

    V_D(x)=W_P(x) log D/log(Dx),

the exact identity is

    S^[theta](D)
      =1/log D sum_(p in P_band,j>=1) log Np phi_u(p^j)
                  (Np)^(-j/2) S(D/(Np)^j;V_D).        (R2)

For every p, its j=1,...,v_p(b) terms contribute exactly v_p(b)log Np. Complete multiplicativity includes natural zero values, so no nonzero-character division is needed. The normalizations in R2 are exact. The denominator is log Nb, not an approximation by log D: V_D retains the exact ratio. On the fixed annulus log(Dx) is comparable to log D, and its finitely many Euler, real and log-scale derivatives are uniformly bounded in the given positive m range.

### A full future-partner return

In each reduced residue class there are infinitely many negative squarefree
integers (primes) and positive ones (a fixed r=1 mod q times different
primes in that class). Only infinitude of primes in each reduced progression
is imported here; see [NIST DLMF 27.11.9](https://dlmf.nist.gov/27.11.E9).
No prime-distribution error estimate is used. Thus a fixed global
same-residue pairing of the two signs exists. Orient each pair (u,v) by
mu(u)=1, mu(v)=-1 and set a=min(u,v), b=max(u,v). Define

    D_q(X) = sum_(X<=a<2X) (b-a),       X=1,2,4,... .

Every future partner is included, even when b is much larger than 2X.
For a common 0<gamma<1, the full hypothesis

    D_q(X) <<_(q,epsilon) X^(1+gamma+epsilon)
    for every epsilon>0 and every fixed q                 (OPEN-D)

implies ordinary zero exclusion in Re(s)>gamma. Indeed, initially Re(s)>1,
absolute regrouping gives

    1/L(s,chi) = sum_pairs chi(u)(u^(-s)-v^(-s)).

For sigma=Re(s)>0 the difference is bounded by
|s|(b-a)a^(-sigma-1). Summing dyadic shells with epsilon below a compact
set's horizontal margin gives normal convergence on Re(s)>gamma. The
identity L F=1 continues meromorphically, excluding zeros and permitting
the reciprocal zero at a principal pole. All fixed finite heights and the
literal imprimitive factors are covered; no uniform growth assertion follows.

Monotone same-residue pairing has crossing count R_q(t). Tonelli identifies
the total *clipped* interval length in [A,B] with integral_A^B R_q(t)dt.
That is not the complete D_q(A): omitted future portions and intervals
entering from earlier shells matter. Under G135's existing summatory/rank
bound with gamma>1/2, endpoints grow proportionally to their rank k and
pair displacement is O(k^(gamma+epsilon)); the complete D bound follows.
This adapter has not evaded the original arithmetic difficulty.

The global neutral-prime rule has the unconditional full cost

    D_q(X) = (r-1) sum_(X<=m<2X,(m,qr)=1) mu(m)^2 m
           = (3/2)(r-1)d_(qr) X^2 + O_(q,r)(X^(3/2)).

Partial summation of the squarefree count proves it, with the positive main
coefficient intact. Thus this rule cannot meet the positive-cost target for
any gamma<1. Other matchings or signed displacement estimates remain open.
Near/1/6/1/4 cost exponents are respectively below1.8748540364,11/6,7/4.
The new useful bill is complete future-partner cost and this actual rule's
failure; G135, W01 signed transport and [private research revision] priced coupling retain credit.

\frac{aA'}{bA}\in I_{\rm good}^{\,6}. \tag{A01.1}
\]
For every selected pair subtract its complete additive zero covariance in the AA19 sense, retaining the full continuous product profile. Denote the signed sum of differences by \(\mathcal E_{\ne,\rm coh}^{\rm raw}\). Then
\[
|\mathcal E_{\ne,\rm coh}^{\rm raw}|\ll_\epsilon Z^\epsilon. \tag{A01.2}
\]
If both good outer indices \(a,b\) are squarefree, the bound improves to \(Z^\epsilon/Y\). Physical energy includes the additional factor \(Q^{-1}\).

### Local masks and exact coherent incidence

At \(p\mid AA'\), write \(\alpha_p=v_p(a)\), \(\beta_p=v_p(b)\), \(d_p=v_p(A)-v_p(A')\pmod6\). AA14 forces \(\alpha_p,\beta_p\le1\) because the column character requires a unit row. The local row character exponent is \(d_p-\alpha_p+\beta_p\). Under (A01.1) it is zero and the factor is a unit scalar times \(1_{p\nmid m}\).

Since \(A=cn^3,A'=c'n'^3\), the difference between the two squarefree incidence differences lies in \([-2,2]\). It cannot cancel an odd multiple of three. Therefore, at those primes,
\[
\alpha_p-\beta_p=v_p(c)-v_p(c'),\qquad
v_p(n)-v_p(n')\equiv0\pmod2.
\]
Outside \(AA'\), the coherent condition is \(\alpha_p-\beta_p\equiv0\pmod6\), with the additional support restrictions below.

Consequently all surviving pairs admit the exact good-ideal parametrization
\[
c=gu,\ c'=gv,\quad
a=d_0ur_1^6,\ b=d_0vr_2^6,\quad
n=hs^2,\ n'=ht^2.
\]
Here \(g,u,v\) are pairwise coprime squarefree; \(h\) is squarefree; \((r_1,r_2)=1\); \((r_1r_2,AA')=1\); \((d_0,uv)=1\); and \(v_p(d_0)\le1\) at \(p\mid AA'\). Core/cube overlaps among \(g,u,v,h,s,t\) otherwise remain. In particular, \(r_i\) may share primes with \(d_0\) outside \(AA'\).

At a good prime outside \(AA'\), let \(E_j=1_{p^j\mid m}\), \(E_0=1\). Lifting a normalized local Gauss sum gives, for \(j\ge1\),
\[
G_j(m)=q^{j/2-1}1_{p^{j-1}\mid m}
\sum_{x\bmod p}^{*}\chi_p(x)^j
\psi_p(-mx/p^{j-1}).
\]
If \(6\nmid j\),
\[
|G_j(m)|^2=q^{j-1}(E_{j-1}-E_j).
\]
If \(6\mid j\),
\[
G_j(m)=q^{j/2-1}(qE_j-E_{j-1}),\quad
|G_j(m)|^2=q^{j-2}\{(q^2-2q)E_j+E_{j-1}\}.
\]
These explicitly retain principal-on-units spikes.

For unequal coherent valuations \(\alpha>\beta\), positive \(\beta\not\equiv0\pmod6\) gives disjoint supports. If \(\beta=0\), the principal formula for \(G_\alpha\) applies; if \(6\mid\beta>0\), \(G_\beta\) is constant on \(G_\alpha\)'s support. Every surviving local product is a linear combination of divisibility masks with coefficient \(\ell^1\) norm at most \(2q^{(\alpha+\beta)/2}\). CRT therefore writes the full good kernel as
\[
K_S(m)\sum_e b_e1_{e\mid m},\qquad
\sum_e|b_e|
\ll_\epsilon(q_aq_b)^{1/2}
(q_aq_bq_Aq_{A'})^\epsilon. \tag{A01.3}
\]
Here \(K_S\) belongs to the original fixed finite periodic family; no moving prime is placed in \(S\). If \(a,b\) are squarefree, the factor \((q_aq_b)^{1/2}\) is unnecessary.

### Uniform discrepancy, including periods beyond the row range

For every bounded smooth annular profile family on the Eisenstein lattice,
\[
\sum_{e\mid m}\Psi(m/\sqrt Q)
-\frac{Q}{q_e}\int_{\mathbb C}\Psi
=O_\Psi(1), \tag{A01.4}
\]
with the fixed lattice covolume included and uniformly in \(Q,e\).

To prove it, rotate and scale the ideal lattice by a generator of \(e\), and put \(L=(Q/q_e)^{1/2}\). For \(L\ge1\), Poisson bounds the nonzero dual sum by
\[
O_N\!\left(L^2\sum_{\xi\ne0}(1+L|\xi|)^{-N}\right)=O(1)
\]
for fixed \(N>2\). For \(L<1\), the compact annulus meets only \(O(1)\) lattice points and its continuous mass is \(O(L^2)\). Fixed residue classes satisfy the same argument. This proves (A01.4) with \(K_S\) and its actual zero average.

Applying this to (A01.3), each pair's row sum minus its complete zero mode is \(O(YZ^\epsilon)\) times fixed profile seminorms.

### Sum of the original coefficients

The modulus of a paired completed coefficient is
\[
\frac1{q_g\sqrt{q_uq_v}\,q_h^2q_s^2q_t^2}.
\]
For fixed \(d_0,r_1,r_2\), the outer annuli imply
\[
\sum_{u,v}(q_uq_v)^{-1/2}
\ll \frac{Y}{q_{d_0}(q_{r_1}q_{r_2})^3}.
\]
The original log-Gaussian profiles satisfy
\[
\sum_gq_g^{-1}|V(T_1q_g)V(T_2q_g)|\ll1
\]
uniformly in \(T_1,T_2>0\), by dyadic ideal counting and Cauchy. The \(h,s,t\) sums converge at norm exponent two, the \(r_i\) sums at exponent three, and \(\sum_{q_{d_0}\ll Y}q_{d_0}^{-1}\ll\log(2Y)\). Thus total absolute coefficient/profile mass is \(O(Y\log(2Y))\). Small powers of completed column lengths are absorbed in the original two-sided log-Gaussian envelope.

Multiplying by the raw prefactor \(Y^{-2}\) and the \(O(Y)\) per-pair discrepancy proves (A01.2). In the squarefree outer subcase that discrepancy is \(O(1)\), proving the stronger bound.

For a fixed number of all-marked slots at **unembedded \(D=1\)**, replace \(V\) by the exact AA18 kernel. Permitted divisors of \(A\) are divisor-bounded, and AA20 supplies a common envelope at scale \(ZP\). No extra tuple count or \(q_U^{-1/2}\) is inserted. The same proof applies.

**Unpaid:** nonprincipal good-character pairs, including their values at sixth-power additive frequencies; mixed embedded arguments \(e^2r,d^2r\); arbitrary \(A\)-dependent weights; growing slot counts; the full physical saving.

**Precise follow-up:** derive the actual embedded coherent row kernel first, with \(\operatorname{lcm}(D^2,E^2)\) and all character zeros. Once such a kernel is a fixed-sector divisibility combination, dilation introduces no difficulty for (A01.4), because \(1_{p^j\mid\lambda r}=1_{p^{(j-v_p(\lambda))_+}\mid r}\) and cannot increase coefficient \(\ell^1\) mass. The remaining problem is the correct character/coefficient incidence and total marked mass, not a blanket “long period” obstruction.

**Sources:** BB R08; [restricted research revision] AA14–AA20; [restricted research revision] AB16.

## A02. Additional exact index and budget results

### Orientation-sensitive rectangular means

Suppose for the same physical family one has
\[
\mathcal M(A,B)\ll T^C(AB)^\delta
\min_j A^{r_j}B^{s_j},\qquad r_j,s_j\ge0.
\]
Summing over \(AB^2\le X\) gives exponent
\[
R=\max_{0\le z\le1/2}\min_j\{r_j(1-2z)+s_jz\}.
\]
Every bound is nondecreasing in \(A\), so the outer maximum is on \(AB^2=X\). Only endpoints and intersections of the finitely many affine lines need checking. Dyads cost logarithms.

A fixed-\(b\) estimate \(Y^{1+\eta+\delta}q_b^{\nu+\delta}\) yields an all-physical-row exponent \(1+\eta\) if \(\nu<1+2\eta\): a \(b\)-dyad \(B\) contributes \(X^{1+\eta+\delta}B^{\nu-1-2\eta+O(\delta)}\).

The hypothetical pointwise model \(|F_{ab^2}|\ll q_aq_b^{1/2}\) gives rectangular mean \(A^3B^2\), and hence \(X^{3-4z}\). It reaches \(X^{35/32}\) only for \(z\ge61/128\). Combining it with the weak fixed-\(b\) exponent \(\nu=3/2,\eta=3/32\) gives worst exponent \(85/69>35/32\). These are exact limitations of the supplied upper bounds, not lower bounds for actual means. [BA D4.]

### Reduced index and the conditional anisotropic calculation

On squarefree sixth-order Gauss columns, \(h=ab^2\) permits replacing \(h^4=a^4b^8\) by \(a^4b^2\). The quotient is \(b^6\); at column primes dividing \(ab\), both local nonprincipal Gauss sums are zero. This algebra gives reduced norm \(A^4B^2\). It supplies no arithmetic approximate functional equation.

If one separately grants the proposed AFE length \(C=A^2B\), dual control, coefficient mass, and the displayed anisotropic sieve bound in BB R04.a, substitution gives \(A^{7/3}B^{5/3}\) for \(A\ge B\) and \(A^{8/3}B^{4/3}\) for \(B\ge A\). In the latter region it fits the target \(A^{1+\eta}B^{2+2\eta}\) only if
\[
B\ge A^{(5-3\eta)/(2+6\eta)}.
\]
At \(\eta=3/32\), this is \(B\ge A^{151/82}\). At \(A=B\), its physical exponent is \(4/3\). The algebra is verified; exact applicability of the cited external sieve and the AFE remain separate obligations.


The full unequal-cutoff proof is A16. Fixed off-central incidence budgets are in T08.

## A04. Exact calibration of a family of adaptive probes

**PROVED finite-dimensional identity; the arithmetic saving is OPEN.** Source: BA D6. Let \(G>0\) be the Gram of actual *complete physical probes*, let \(Ev=0\) encode nuisance constraints, and let \(p^*v=1\) retain the principal signal. Set
\[
 A=EG^{-1/2},\quad b=G^{-1/2}p,\quad
 \Delta=b^*P_{\ker A}b.
\]
If \(\Delta>0\),
\[
 \inf_{Ev=0,\ p^*v=1}v^*Gv=\Delta^{-1},\qquad
 v=G^{-1/2}P_{\ker A}b/\Delta \tag{A04.1}
\]
attains equality. If \(\Delta=0\), the constraints are infeasible. Indeed \(w=G^{1/2}v\) lies in \(\ker A\) and \(b^*w=1\); Cauchy gives the lower bound and the displayed vector attains it.

For a semidefinite Gram, first check whether a null vector satisfying the nuisance conditions carries the signal; otherwise use a justified quotient/regularization. For multiple principal aliases the scalar calibration becomes a matrix range condition. The first missing theorem is a lower bound on projected principal separation with all coefficient, derivative, and height costs included. The indefinite coprime covariance and the incomplete outer A-field cannot replace \(G\).

## A05. Triple-convolution cube inversion and the \(5/6\) absolute barrier

**PROVED RELATIVE TO the inherited triple diagonal; signed improvement OPEN.** Source: BA D7, [restricted research revision] Z13–Z18. With fixed \(r>0\), absorb the common Bessel normalization into
\[
 H_r(t)=tK_{1/3}(\kappa t)^2K_{1/3}(\kappa rt),\qquad
 P_{{\rm sf},r}(y)=y^3\sum_{c\ {\rm sf,good}}\mu(c)H_r(\sqrt{q_c}y).
\]
The actual coefficient identity, allowing shared core/cube primes, gives
\[
 P_r(y)=\sum_B\xi_{\rm ang}(B)q_B^{-3}
                    P_{{\rm sf},r}(q_B^{3/2}y),\qquad
 P_{{\rm sf},r}(y)=\sum_B\mu(B)\xi_{\rm ang}(B)q_B^{-3}
                    P_r(q_B^{3/2}y). \tag{A05.1}
\]
This is ordinary convolution inversion of commuting dilations, justified absolutely at each fixed \(y>0\) by the Bessel tail.

If \(P_r(y)\ll y^{3-2a}\) at zero and decays rapidly at infinity, absolute inversion requires
\(\sum_Bq_B^{3/2-3a}<\infty\), exactly \(a>5/6\). Splitting at \(q_B=y^{-2/3}\) gives bounds \(y^{3-2a}\) for \(a>5/6\), \(y^{4/3}(1+|\log y|)\) at equality, and \(y^{4/3}\) below it. These are upper-budget limitations, not lower bounds on the signed inverse. An angular Möbius partial-sum bound \(O(U^\theta)\), with the needed derivative control, permits Abel summation when \(\theta<3a-3/2\). At \(a=3/4\) this asks for \(\theta<3/4\), a separate unpaid theorem. The numerical \(5/6\) shared with the source-shell obstruction does not identify their spaces.
