## A06. Fixed-degree polynomial detrending still detects zeros

**PROVED CONDITIONAL TRANSFER.** Source: BA D8. Let \(M(x)=\sum_{n\le x}\mu(n)\), fix \(r\ge0\), and suppose, for every \(\epsilon>0\),
\[
 \inf_{\deg P\le r}\int_N^{2N}|M(x)-P(x)|^2dx
       \ll_{\epsilon,r}N^{2a+1+\epsilon},\qquad 0<a<1. \tag{A06.1}
\]
Then \(\zeta(s)\ne0\) for \(\Re s>a\). To prove this, choose
\(\phi=\psi^{(r+1)}\), \(\psi\in C_c^\infty(1,2)\), and set
\(T_\psi(N)=\int_1^2M(Nu)\phi(u)\,du\).
Polynomial moments vanish, so Cauchy gives \(T_\psi(N)\ll N^{a+\epsilon}\). Initially for \(\Re s>1\),
\[
 \int_0^\infty T_\psi(N)N^{-s}\frac{dN}{N}
 =\frac{\int_1^2\phi(u)u^sdu}{s\zeta(s)}.
\]
The left side is holomorphic for \(\Re s>a\). Integration by parts makes the numerator
\((-1)^{r+1}s(s-1)\cdots(s-r)\int\psi(u)u^{s-r-1}du\).
At any possible nontrivial zero in that half-plane its polynomial factor is nonzero, and a localized \(\psi\) makes the integral nonzero. This contradicts holomorphy. Euler nonvanishing handles \(\Re s>1\); the line \(\Re s=1\) is covered by the accepted baseline.

The discrete version follows because a fixed-degree least-squares fit to \(|M(n)|\le2N\) has scaled coefficient norm \(O_r(N)\); it varies by \(O_r(1)\) on a unit interval. Interpolation costs \(O_r(N)\), affordable for \(a>0\). Growing degree is a different hypothesis: its calibration can increasingly approximate the very power \(x^\rho\) one must detect.

## A07. Source shell weights, cube damping, and diagonal calibration

**PROVED relative to the inherited shell identities; the full-span obstruction requires a nonzero comparison period.** Sources: BB R09; [restricted research revision] (AC5)–(AC9). The arbitrary-diagonal calibration in part 2 is new in this integration.

At a good prime \(p\) of norm \(Q\), the orthogonal cube shells satisfy
\[
 \|v_j\|^2=(1-Q^{-2})Q^{-2j}\|u\|^2,\qquad
 P_s(v_j)=x_p(s)^jP_s(v_0),\quad
 x_p(s)=\xi_{\rm ang}(p)Q^{1-3s}.
 \tag{A07.1}
\]
These are source probability norms, not norms of the actual bilinear currents.

### 1. Power weights do not repair whole-span continuity near the center

Give shell \(j\) the additional squared-norm weight \(Q^{2rj}\). The exact squared Riesz norm on its finite span is
\[
 \frac{|P_s(v_0)|^2}{(1-Q^{-2})\|u\|^2}
 \sum_{j=0}^JQ^{(4-6\sigma-2r)j},\qquad \sigma=\Re s.
 \tag{A07.2}
\]
This follows by summing squared functional values divided by squared orthogonal basis norms. At a nonzero base period, local boundedness requires \(r>2-3\sigma\). The original source has weighted norm ratio
\[
 \frac{\|u\|_r^2}{\|u\|^2}
 =\frac{1-Q^{-2}}{1-Q^{-2+2r}}.
 \tag{A07.3}
\]
Its all-prime product is finite and nonzero precisely for \(r<1/2\); for \(r\ge1\), even a single-prime norm diverges. For \(0\le r<1\), this follows by comparing the positive logarithm with \(Q^{-2+2r}\); for \(r<0\), both corrections are summable.

Where (A07.2) converges, its relative factor compared with the unweighted full-source period ratio is
\[
 \kappa_{p,r}(s)=
 \frac{|1-x_p(s)|^2}
 {(1-Q^{-2})(1-Q^{4-6\sigma-2r})}. \tag{A07.4}
\]
For \(\sigma>2/3\), the numerator product is absolutely convergent; the positive denominator requires \(r>5/2-3\sigma\).

For the near-central range \(\sigma=1/2+e\), \(0<e<1/6\), suppose \(r<1/2\) so the source remains present. Either the single-prime series already diverges, or
\[
 p_*=6\sigma+2r-4>0,\qquad p_*<6e<3\sigma-1,\qquad p_*<1.
\]
The logarithm of the positive denominator in (A07.4) contributes at least \(Q^{-p_*}\), while the numerator logarithm is \(O(Q^{-(3\sigma-1)})\). Hence, for every sufficiently large good prime,
\(\log\kappa_{p,r}\ge Q^{-p_*}/2\). Its all-prime sum diverges. Under the stipulated nonzero full-source comparison, no such power-weight norm both contains the original source and bounds the continued functional on its entire joint-shell span.

This does not obstruct a restricted estimate for one squarefree vector, a graph norm of the actual current map, or a different tensor reference with independently verified arithmetic.

### 2. Every positive diagonal renorm has an exact calibration cost

On a finite shell span assign arbitrary positive squared norms \(a_j\), and put \(u_J=\sum_{j=0}^Jv_j\). Cauchy–Schwarz gives
\[
 \|u_J\|_a^2\|P_s\|_{a,*}^2
 =\left(\sum_ja_j\right)\left(\sum_j\frac{|P_s(v_j)|^2}{a_j}\right)
 \ge\left(\sum_j|P_s(v_j)|\right)^2
 =|P_s(v_0)|^2\left(\sum_{j=0}^J|x_p|^j\right)^2.
 \tag{A07.5}
\]
Equality holds when \(a_j\) is proportional to \(|P_s(v_j)|\). If the source and a bounded compatible functional exist in the limiting norm, \(|x_p|<1\) and the known geometric period identity imply
\[
 \frac{\|u\|_a^2\|P_s\|_{a,*}^2}{|P_s(u)|^2}
 \ge\frac{|1-x_p|^2}{(1-|x_p|)^2}. \tag{A07.6}
\]
The factors multiply over finite tensor products of primes.

This is a proved necessary test for arbitrary positive diagonal weights, broader than part 1's power weights. It is not a general infinite-product obstruction: a positive real \(x_p\) gives factor one, and divergence of the infinite phase-sensitive product would need additional angular information. A non-diagonal current norm is outside this test.

### 3. Cube damping shifts the completion but proves no new norm bound

For \(\Re\nu\ge0\), let \(u_\nu=\sum_{j\ge0}Q^{-\nu j}v_j\). Orthogonality and the geometric period series give
\[
 \frac{\|u_\nu\|^2}{\|u\|^2}
 =\frac{1-Q^{-2}}{1-Q^{-2-2\Re\nu}},\qquad
 (1-Q^{-\nu}x_p)P_s(u_\nu)=(1-x_p)P_s(u).
 \tag{A07.7}
\]
The cross-multiplied identity includes zero base periods and is first justified in absolute convergence or on finite prime products with the inherited continuation. Formally weighting the entire cube label by \(q_B^{-\nu}\) changes the fixed completion to
\(L^S(3s-1+\nu,\xi_{\rm ang})D_h(s)\).
A nonzero convergent source-norm product does not continue the infinite period or current map. T01 already removes fixed-factor division; a useful damping argument must improve a calibrated current or restricted-test estimate.

## A08. An arithmetic source operator and the exact approximation cost

**PROVED operator reductions; every useful arithmetic rate remains OPEN.** Source: BB R10, inherited fractional-part detector. For \(\sigma>0\), put
\[
 H_\sigma=L^2((0,1),x^{2\sigma-1}dx),\qquad
 f_n(x)=\{1/(nx)\}-n^{-1}\{1/x\},\quad n\ge2.
\]
On \(1/(k+1)<x\le1/k\), \(f_n(x)=(k\bmod n)/n\); thus \(0\le f_n<1\). Its exact Mellin transform is
\[
 \mathcal Mf_n(s)=\frac{\zeta(s)}s(n^{-1}-n^{-s}),\qquad\Re s>0, \tag{A08.1}
\]
with the removable value at one. Let \(w_n>0\), \(\sum w_n<\infty\), and
\[
 K_w=\sum_{n\ge2}w_n(f_n\otimes f_n),\qquad
 R_w(\lambda)=\langle1,\lambda(K_w+\lambda I)^{-1}1\rangle.
\]
It is positive trace class, with trace at most \((2\sigma)^{-1}\sum w_n\).
Its quadratic form shows
\(\ker K_w=\overline{\operatorname{span}\{f_n\}}^\perp\).
The spectral theorem then proves
\[
 R_w(\lambda)\longrightarrow d_\infty^2,\quad
 R_w(\lambda)=\int\frac{\lambda}{t+\lambda}\,d\mu_1(t)
 =\inf_{c}\left\{\left\|1-\sum c_nf_n\right\|^2+
                   \lambda\sum|c_n|^2/w_n\right\}. \tag{A08.2}
\]
The infimum is over \(\sum |c_n|^2/w_n<\infty\), equivalently over finite sequences by density. It follows by completing the square with \(Ae_n=\sqrt{w_n}f_n\).
Any \(R_w(\lambda)=o(1)\) suffices for half-plane nonvanishing: a zero
\(\rho=\beta+i\gamma\), \(\beta>\sigma\), would force by (A08.1)
\[
 R_w(\lambda)\ge d_\infty^2\ge 2(\beta-\sigma)/|\rho|^2. \tag{A08.3}
\]
The evaluation functional used here has norm \([2(\beta-\sigma)]^{-1/2}\).

For \(0<\delta<1\), integration by parts gives
\(\mu_1([0,u])\ll u^\delta\Rightarrow R_w(\lambda)\ll\lambda^\delta\);
conversely \(\mu_1([0,\lambda])\le2R_w(\lambda)\). The interval must include zero. At \(\delta=1\) the general upper bound is \(\lambda\log(1/\lambda)\); a rate \(o(\lambda)\) is impossible since
\(R_w(\lambda)\ge\lambda\|1\|^2/(\|K_w\|+\lambda)\).

The columns are infinitely independent: a finite relation on the \(k=1\) interval gives \(\sum a_n/n=0\), and subtraction leaves \(\sum a_n\lfloor k/n\rfloor=0\); taking \(k\) equal to the smallest nonzero coefficient index contradicts it. Thus this compact operator has no positive uniform gap on its support.

For \(V_N=\operatorname{span}(f_2,\ldots,f_N)\), \(d_N=\operatorname{dist}(1,V_N)\), and \(\tau_N=(2\sigma)^{-1}\sum_{n>N}w_n\), Cauchy in the \(K_w+\lambda I\) metric applied to \(v=P_{V_N^\perp}1\) proves
\[
 R_w(\lambda)\ge\frac{\lambda}{\lambda+\tau_N}d_N^2. \tag{A08.4}
\]
Indeed \(\langle1,v\rangle=d_N^2\), the finite part annihilates \(v\), and the remaining quadratic form is at most \((\lambda+\tau_N)d_N^2\).
Weights \(2^{-n}\) make a power resolvent rate demand exponentially fast approximation in \(N\); weights \(n^{-1-\alpha}\) demand only \(d_N^2\ll N^{-\alpha\delta}\). Neither rate follows merely from changing weights.

For numerical certificates, \(K_{w,N}\le K_w\) implies
\[
 R_w(\lambda)\le
 \langle1,\lambda(K_{w,N}+\lambda I)^{-1}1\rangle. \tag{A08.5}
\]
A certified finite-rank value is already an upper bound; no extra operator-tail correction is needed in this direction. Gram integrals and linear solves still require certified errors. A value below \(2\delta/(1+T^2)\) excludes \(\beta\ge\sigma+\delta,\ |\gamma|\le T\); only a vanishing limit establishes a fixed all-height region.

## A09. Optimal shell correction and a genuine higher-moment escape

**PROVED identities; convergence OPEN.** Source: BB R11. For the inherited prefix interpolants set \(r_N=1-h_N\), \(c_N=h_{2N}-h_N\). On \(N\le k<2N\), \(c_N=r_N\); both vanish earlier. Let
\[
 F=\|r_N1_{[N,2N)}\|^2,\quad T=\|c_N1_{[2N,\infty)}\|^2,\quad
 J=\langle r_N1_{[2N,\infty)},c_N1_{[2N,\infty)}\rangle.
\]
Expansion gives
\[
 \|r_N\|^2-\|r_N-\lambda c_N\|^2
 =2\lambda(F+\Re J)-\lambda^2(F+T).
\]
For \(F+T>0\), the best real scalar is
\(\lambda_*=(F+\Re J)/(F+T)\), with gain \((F+\Re J)^2/(F+T)\).
Clamp \(\lambda_*\) to \([0,1]\) if underrelaxation is required. This can improve on full refitting, but leaves \((1-\lambda)r_N\) on the first shell; moving only forward freezes that error.

An arbitrary specified shell residual can still be matched by the actual arithmetic span. Put
\[
 b_n=nf_n-2Nf_{2N},\qquad
 a_n=-[r(n)-r(n-1)]/n,\quad r(N-1)=0,\quad N\le n<2N.
\]
On that shell \(b_n(k)=-n1_{k\ge n}\), so \(\sum a_nb_n(k)=r(k)\), and the correction is zero earlier. Future repetitions persist. The special formula \(h_{2N}-h_N\) must not be reused after arbitrary damping.

Under \(\Pr(K=k)=k^{-2\sigma}-(k+1)^{-2\sigma}\), Hölder for a residual supported on \(K\ge N\) gives
\[
 \mathbb E|r_N|^2\le
 N^{-2\sigma(1-1/p)}(\mathbb E|r_N|^{2p})^{1/p},\quad p>1.
\]
Hence the genuinely new target \(\mathbb E|r_N|^{2p}\ll N^\kappa\) with
\(\kappa<2\sigma(p-1)\) would force convergence. The inherited tail upper bound only decays for \(\sigma>1/(2-b_0)\approx.8887993351\), which is weaker than the premise. Its failure to decay is not proof of divergence.

## A10. Two exact countermodels for positivity-based geometric shortcuts

**PROVED counterexamples to generic implications; not counterexamples to an arithmetic theorem for \(\xi\).** Source: BB R12.

For \(h>0\), set \(E_h(z)=\xi(1/2+h-iz)\), where \(\xi\) now denotes the completed Riemann xi function. Real symmetry and the functional equation give \(E_h^\#(z)=\xi(1/2-h-iz)\). The correctly signed Hermite–Biehler kernel has diagonal
\[
 K_h(z,z)=\frac{|E_h(z)|^2-|E_h^\#(z)|^2}{4\pi\Im z}.
\]
Strict positivity for \(\Im z>0\) excludes zeros with \(\beta>1/2+h\), since \(\rho=\beta+i\gamma\) maps to
\(z=-\gamma+i(\beta-1/2-h)\). At \(h=0\) the two functions coincide, so strictness is impossible; the RH endpoint would require every \(h>0\).

Positive semidefiniteness alone does not exclude a common upper zero. The kernel of \(E_0(z)=e^{-iz}\) is
\[
 \frac{\sin(z-\bar w)}{\pi(z-\bar w)}
 =\frac1{2\pi}\int_{-1}^1e^{itz}\overline{e^{itw}}dt,
\]
hence positive. Multiplication by \(R(z)=z^2+1=R^\#(z)\) multiplies the kernel by \(R(z)\overline{R(w)}\), preserving positivity while introducing a zero at \(i\) in both functions. Strict diagonal positivity or a separately proved common-zero exclusion is essential.

A positive Fourier measure does not reverse the heat deformation. The measure
\(2\delta_0+(\delta_1+\delta_{-1})/2\) gives
\[
 H_t(z)=2+e^t\cos z,\qquad \partial_tH_t=-\partial_z^2H_t.
\]
Its measure and moment Hankel matrices are positive. Its zeros are nonreal for \(t<\log2\), double real at equality, and real simple for \(t>\log2\). For a smooth strictly positive density let
\[
 \rho_a(x)=2g_a(x)+[g_a(x-1)+g_a(x+1)]/2,\quad
 g_a(x)=(4\pi a)^{-1/2}e^{-x^2/(4a)}.
\]
Completing the square after multiplication by \(e^{tx^2}\), with \(d=1-4at>0\), gives
\[
 F_t(z)=d^{-1/2}e^{-az^2/d}
           \{2+e^{t/d}\cos(z/d)\}.
\]
Thus real zeros occur once \(t\ge\log2/(1+4a\log2)\), even though the initial zeros are nonreal. Scaling frequency makes the initial strip arbitrarily thin. An arithmetic reverse-stability theorem for xi remains a different open proposal.

## A11. One corrected coefficient criterion, with two arithmetic presentations

**PROVED exact criteria and their equivalence; the coefficient bounds are OPEN.** Sources: BA D12; BB R13. The explicit derivative merger below is new in this integration.

Put \(Z_0(s)=(s-1)\zeta(s)\), fix \(0<b<1\), and map the disk by
\[
 s_b(z)=b+(2-b)\frac{1+z}{1-z},\qquad
 \log\frac{Z_0(s_b(z))}{Z_0(2)}
       =\sum_{n\ge1}\ell_n(b)z^n
\]
near zero. Then
\[
 \limsup|\ell_n(b)|^{1/n}\le1
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \zeta(s)\ne0\quad(\Re s>b,\ s\ne1). \tag{A11.1}
\]
If the coefficients are subexponential, exponentiating their holomorphic disk series agrees with \(Z_0(s_b(z))/Z_0(2)\) by analytic continuation and cannot vanish. Conversely, a nonzero holomorphic function on the simply connected half-plane has a holomorphic logarithm. The canceled pole has \(Z_0(1)=1\).

Set \(\lambda=2(2-b)\), \(A=\lambda-1=3-2b\), and
\[
 P_n(x)=\sum_{k=1}^n\binom{n-1}{k-1}\frac{(-x)^k}{k!},\quad
 e^{-xz/(1-z)}=1+\sum_{n\ge1}P_n(x)z^n.
\]
The Euler expansion at \(s=2\) gives
\[
 \ell_n(b)=\frac{(-1)^{n+1}A^n+1}{n}
     +\sum_{p,m\ge1}\frac{p^{-2m}}m P_n(\lambda m\log p). \tag{A11.2}
\]
For each fixed \(n\) these sums converge absolutely. If
\(d\Pi=\sum_{p,m\ge1}m^{-1}\delta_{p^m}\), substitution \(t=\log x\) and integration of its finite polynomial show
\[
 \int_1^\infty x^{-2}P_n(\lambda\log x)\frac{dx}{\log x}
 =\sum_{k=1}^n\binom{n-1}{k-1}\frac{(-\lambda)^k}{k}
 =\frac{(-A)^n-1}{n}.
\]
The integrand is finite at the lower endpoint because \(P_n(\lambda\log x)=O(\log x)\). Hence the exponential principal term cancels *exactly*:
\[
 \boxed{\ell_n(b)=\int_1^\infty x^{-2}P_n(\lambda\log x)
              \left(d\Pi(x)-\frac{dx}{\log x}\right).} \tag{A11.3}
\]
The required bound is \(O_\delta(e^{\delta n})\) for every \(\delta>0\).
The accepted region gives only the radius
\[
 r_0=(2-b_0)/(2+b_0-2b),\qquad
 \limsup|\ell_n(b)|^{1/n}\le r_0^{-1}
\]
when \(b<b_0\); at \(b=.87449\) this is about \(1.00070508\), not one.

For a general anchor \(r>1-b\), let \(s(z)=b+r(1+z)/(1-z)\), and let \(a_n\) be the coefficients of \(s'(z)\xi'/\xi(s(z))\). Exactly the same analytic-continuation argument, now using the nonremovable logarithmic pole of a zero, proves
\[
 \limsup|a_n|^{1/n}\le1\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
                 \xi(s)\ne0\quad(\Re s>b). \tag{A11.4}
\]
The Laguerre generating function yields the prime part
\[
 a_n^{\rm prime}=-2r\sum_{m\ge2}\Lambda(m)m^{-b-r}
                  L_n^{(1)}(2r\log m). \tag{A11.5}
\]
It must be combined with the coefficients of
\[
 s'(z)\left\{\frac1{s(z)}+\frac1{s(z)-1}
       -\tfrac12\log\pi+\tfrac12\psi(s(z)/2)\right\}. \tag{A11.6}
\]
The zeta pole maps to \(z_1=(1-b-r)/(1-b+r)\in(-1,0)\). Its raw prime contribution is \(+z_1^{-n-1}\); \(s'/(s-1)\) contributes \(-z_1^{-n-1}\), plus its boundary term \(1/(1-z)\). The raw prime coefficients alone therefore cannot be the subexponential target, even under RH.

**New exact merger.** At \(r=2-b\), \(\xi(s)=\tfrac12s\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)Z_0(s)\). Therefore
\[
 a_n=(n+1)\ell_{n+1}(b)
 +[z^n]\,s_b'(z)\{1/s_b(z)-\tfrac12\log\pi+\tfrac12\psi(s_b(z)/2)\}.
 \tag{A11.7}
\]
The added function is holomorphic on the disk because \(\Re s_b>b>0\), so its coefficients are subexponential. Multiplication by \(n+1\) changes no exponential growth rate. The density-subtracted log criterion and the completed Laguerre criterion are thus equivalent arithmetic presentations at this anchor, not independent conjectural gains.

A zero \(\rho=\beta+i\gamma\) maps to
\[
 z_\rho=\frac{\rho-b-r}{\rho-b+r},\quad
 |z_\rho|^2=\frac{(\beta-b-r)^2+\gamma^2}{(\beta-b+r)^2+\gamma^2}.
\]
For fixed \(r\), its sensitivity exponent is
\(\log|z_\rho|^{-1}=2r(\beta-b)/\gamma^2+O_{b,r}(\gamma^{-4})\).
Degree of order \(\gamma^2/[r(\beta-b)]\) is needed even for order-one sensitivity, and individual coefficients can contain cancellation between zeros. A height-dependent anchor \(r\asymp|\gamma|\) changes this calibration but creates an additional uniform two-parameter coefficient problem; it is not supplied by the fixed-anchor criterion.

**New exact anchor optimization.** Put \(\delta=\beta-b>0\), and suppose \(\gamma\ne0\). The sensitivity at anchor \(r\) is
\[
 f(r)=\frac12\log\frac{(r+\delta)^2+\gamma^2}{(r-\delta)^2+\gamma^2},
\quad
 f'(r)=
 \frac{2\delta(\delta^2+\gamma^2-r^2)}
 {((r+\delta)^2+\gamma^2)((r-\delta)^2+\gamma^2)}.
 \tag{A11.8}
\]
The unique unconstrained maximum is \(r_*=\sqrt{\delta^2+\gamma^2}\), with
\[
 f(r_*)=\operatorname{artanh}(\delta/r_*)\sim\delta/|\gamma|.
\]
When \(r_*>1-b\), this is an admissible Euler anchor. Otherwise the admissible supremum occurs as \(r\downarrow1-b\). The displayed derivative proves both statements. At heights \(|\gamma|\asymp T\), the reciprocal sensitivity, which measures degree for order-one amplification of a *single zero's modulus*, changes from order \(T^2/(r\delta)\) for fixed \(r\) to \(T/\delta\). This does not prove finite-degree detection: contributions from different zeros can cancel, and a height-dependent anchor requires a bound uniform in both degree and \(r\), with the moving prime weights and gamma terms included. The case \(\gamma=0\) has a singularity at \(r=\delta\); a prospective zero with \(\beta\le1\) cannot make that point an admissible Euler anchor. The real interval \((0,1)\) is already zero-free. This is the proved calibration underlying portfolio N29.N1.

## A12. A prime Fredholm determinant and the regularization trap

**PROVED identity and method-specific obstruction.** Source: BA D9. On the Hilbert space indexed by rational primes let \(T_s=\operatorname{diag}(p^{-s})\).
For \(\Re s>1\),
\[
 \det(I-T_s)=\prod_p(1-p^{-s})=1/\zeta(s).
\]
For \(\Re s>1/2\), \(T_s\) is Hilbert–Schmidt and
\[
 D_2(s)=\det{}_2(I-T_s)
 =\exp\!\left(-\sum_{m\ge2}\frac1m\sum_pp^{-ms}\right)
\]
is holomorphic and nonzero, by locally absolute convergence. But initially
\[
 1/\zeta(s)=D_2(s)e^{-P(s)},\qquad P(s)=\sum_pp^{-s}.
\]
The compensating factor carries the unresolved continuation and possible poles. Regularization has removed the difficult arithmetic contribution from the determinant, not proved it harmless. A bounded similarity preserves trace-class membership, so it cannot repair the original divergent trace norm. A useful changed operator needs a new verified determinant identity with its compensator controlled.

## A13. Jacobi identities and the quadratic/triple construction

For odd squarefree \(n\), unit \(v\bmod n\), and every frequency \(t\), including nonunits, put
\[
J_n(t;v)=\sum_{x\bmod n}\chi_n(x(v-x))e_n(tx).
\]
Substitute \(x=vy\) and apply QD (1), then scale the unit Kloosterman variable:
\[
J_n(t;v)
=\chi_n(-1)e_n(tv/2)S(1,t^2v^2/16;n)
=\chi_n(-1)e_n(tv/2)S(v^2,t^2/16;n).
\]
Nonunit \(v\) is outside this rescaling identity. The two visible squared parameters do not form two unconstrained dense intervals, and generic squareful moduli are excluded.

For a nontrivial cubic character \(\theta\) over a good residue field of size \(Q\), extended by zero, define
\[
J_\theta(t)=\sum_x\theta(x)\overline{\theta(1-x)}\psi(tx).
\]
The map \(v=x/(1-x)\) is a bijection from \(x\ne1\) to \(v\ne-1\). Thus
\[
J_\theta(t)=\sum_{v\ne-1}\theta(v)
\psi\!\left(\frac{tv}{1+v}\right),\quad
J_\theta(0)=-1,\quad
\sum_t|J_\theta(t)|^2=Q(Q-2).
\]
The zero value follows from the complete character sum and \(\theta(-1)=1\); Parseval gives the energy since exactly \(Q-2\) original coefficients have modulus one. Products of the good squarefree zero modes encode Möbius, but replacing one mode by all Fourier modes incurs the displayed large positive energy.

The proposed quadratic-twisted triple identity is algebraically consistent:
\[
\psi_u(cB^3)=\psi_u(c)\psi_u(B)
\]
for a quadratic \(\psi_u\), including its zeros. If an actual triple source realizes that total-index twist with the correct normalizations, its absolute-chamber Mellin series would be
\[
J_r(s)\frac{L^S(3s-3/2,\xi_{\rm ang}\psi_u)}
{L^S(s,\psi_u)}.
\]
No complete twisted source/current construction or conductor-uniform restriction estimate is supplied. Cubic rows evaluated on squares do not create quadratic characters. [BB R14; QD; [restricted research revision] Z13–Z18.]

Gemini's claimed prime-square identity is false: its proposed right side simplifies to \(S(1,4p^2;n)\), not \(\chi_n(p^2)\). At \(n=5,p=2\), it equals \((3-\sqrt5)/2\), whereas \(\chi_5(4)=1\). To check the value exactly, the Kloosterman sum is \(2+e_5(2)+e_5(3)=2+2\cos(4\pi/5)=(3-\sqrt5)/2\).
title: A13. Jacobi identities and the quadratic/triple construction

## A14. Grok's conditional geometry certificate and its scope corrections

### What the source actually certifies

Assume the **well-defined full-probe hypothesis**
\[
|I_\eta^{\rm comp}|\ll Z^{\theta-\sigma+\epsilon},
\quad \theta=x/2+(y-x)/12,\quad \sigma>0, \tag{A14.1}
\]
at the stated \(\tau=0\) geometry. To use the inherited \(\beta_*\) bootstrap, this must hold for every required fixed primitive finite-order target, its fixed deletion/ray data, and actual finite marked-prime configurations with the original weights and profiles. The real saving \(\sigma\) is common; constants and polynomial height costs may depend on fixed targets/data as permitted in M B0.7. A single chosen component, a single finite height, or an invented projection of the raw field is insufficient.

Relative to those hypotheses and the inherited B0.7 estimates, independent rerunning certifies:

| Conditional target \(c\) | Required \(\sigma\) | Safe lower bound for stationary slack \(b-F^*\) |
|---|---:|---:|
| \(313/2500=.1252\) | \(1/8000\) | \(0.0000432091\) |
| \(251/2000=.1255\) | \(3/5000\) | \(0.0003345304\) |
| \(12551/100000=.12551\) | \(7/10000\) | \(0.0006267350\) |
| \(63/500=.126\) | \(1/800\) | \(0.0003447368\) |
| \(16/125=.128\) | \(1/250\) | \(0.0008907891\) |

For each pair put \(b=1-c\), \(\kappa_t=2b-1\), \(\ell=4(11/12-b-\sigma)\), choose the smaller \(\delta\in(.46,.48)\) root of B0.48, and choose \(h\) by B0.45 with this \(\kappa_t,\ell,\delta\); let \(x=1+\ell-h,y=h-2\ell\). The certificate proves:

- All physical geometry, capacity and support inequalities, including \(\ell/h>4/21\), \(y<6\kappa_t\ell\), \(b>.87\), and the inactive positive part.
- The global amplitude rectangle inequality \(F_{\kappa_t}(\delta',p)\le b\), for \(0\le\delta'\le5/6,0\le p\le1/2\), by outward interval subdivision.
- The other dyadic endpoint, floor class, small rows and principal contour margins.
- With geometry fixed, \(\partial_\kappa F<1/20\) up to the accepted \(\kappa_0\).

If \(\beta_*>b\), write \(\mu=\beta_*-b\), and use \(\kappa=2\beta_*-1=\kappa_t+2\mu\). The derivative bound gives \(F_\kappa-\beta_*\le-.9\mu\). Convexity in the row exponent and the checked endpoint/floor margins complete the inherited numerator estimate. The physical saving gives \(J_\eta\ll Z^{b-k+\epsilon}\). M B0.7's original ordering of buffers, meshes, finite slots and small polynomial heights then gives the contradiction. No arithmetic estimate in (A14.1) is proved by the numerical certificate.

### Source-code inspection, execution, and corrected copy

The original script was inspected and independently executed. Every target passed all 23 checks; amplitude box counts were respectively 98017, 32449, 22269, 32265, 19093.

A corrected portable copy is included as checks/grok_transfer_certificate.py; its independent rerun is checks/grok_transfer_certificate_result.txt. It requires only Python's standard library. Corrections:

- Signed rational-to-Decimal rounding now uses the signed numerator directly. The original helper rounded negative nonterminating rationals in the wrong direction, although its only relevant negative test here was the exact terminating \(-1/50\), so the five original certifications were not affected.
- Printed slack/rate lower bounds use directed subtraction.
- Subdivision midpoints use directed addition and division; the original children still covered their parent in the actual run, but the revised arithmetic makes that coverage explicit.
- The geometry identity \(x+y+\ell=1\) is justified by its definitions and checked by an enclosure containing one, instead of a tolerance.
- An unused placeholder and the false comment that the quadratic's constant term was zero were removed.

The handoff's prose bound “uniform derivative \(<.043\)” is false. The maximum of its reported certified upper bounds is \(0.0440833871\ldots\), so use \(<.0441<1/20\). Several strict slack inequalities were rounded upward; the table above uses safe downward bounds. At \(c=.1255\),
\[
y-x=0.08753960844756839075\ldots,\qquad
\frac{y-x}{12}=0.00729496737063069923\ldots.
\]
Thus the supplied lower claim \(y-x>.08753960845\) is also an upward-rounding error. The ratio \(.0006/((y-x)/12)<.0823\) remains correct.

### Gram localization is not a vector projection

The three terms in B0.22's nonnegative majorant have square-root exponents
\[
\frac x2,\qquad \frac{y-x}{2},\qquad
\frac x2+\frac{y-x}{12}.
\]
The middle term is smaller than the first for \(y<2x\). This correctly identifies the \(P_a^{1/6}\) term as the sole excess in that majorant.

However the label \(k=r^6\) occurs after expanding pairs of outer columns, with profile argument \(\sqrt Q\,r^6/(ab)\). It is not a fixed additive spectral projection of \(A\). GS §2 states this caveat, but §7 then writes \(A^{(6)}\) without constructing it. Therefore the claimed “sixth-power portion of \(A\) paired with \(B\)” is **not presently a defined mathematical object**. Retain (A14.1), or construct an exact theta-paired bilinear identity/projector and prove its principal calibration before using that language. Positivity of a raw neutral-ray Gram does not refute a theta-specific cancellation estimate; it also does not define such a projection.

The claimed “full deletion permits only a detached window near \(.12937\)” is also too strong. That window is merely the diagnostic obtained by forcing equality \(\sigma=(y-x)/12\) and a particular stationary geometry. A stronger valid estimate may be deliberately weakened; for example the certified \(.1255\) geometry needs only \(\sigma=.0006\), much less than its full excess. The detached saturated-geometry window is not an obstruction to smaller improvements.

### New exact alternative to the fixed-point search

At fixed target \(\kappa\) and its chosen \(\delta\), put
\[
D_\kappa=3R'/4-1/(24\kappa),\quad
H_0=-1/(2D_\kappa),\quad
H_1=-(1/2+1/(6\kappa))/D_\kappa.
\]
Then \(h=H_0+H_1\ell\). Let
\[
A_\kappa=(2H_0-1)/12,\qquad
B_\kappa=(2H_1-3)/12,\qquad
\ell_b=4(c-1/12).
\]
The simultaneous equations \(\ell=\ell_b-4\sigma\), \(\sigma=\alpha(y-x)/12\) solve exactly as
\[
\sigma=
\frac{\alpha(A_\kappa+B_\kappa\ell_b)}
{1+4\alpha B_\kappa}, \tag{A14.2}
\]
whenever the denominator is nonzero. All capacity and rectangle constraints still require separate verification. This removes the need for a monotonicity-assuming binary search and is a new exact diagnostic simplification.

The resonant-coset, Pólya–Vinogradov-shaped, and generic \((Q+Z)\) comparisons in GS §5 are at most bookkeeping comparisons under their displayed models. The coset bound is not reconstructed there with full coefficients; do not promote it to a new uniform arithmetic lemma. The explicit algebraic comparisons at \(4/33\) are correct.

## A15. Gcd localization need not preserve positivity

**PROVED counterexample, new explicit formulation in this merge.** Choose distinct coprime core labels \(c_1,c_2\) with \(q_{c_i}>G_0>1\), and two identical nonzero vectors normalized to have Gram
\[
 B=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&1\end{pmatrix}.
\]
The small-gcd mask \(\mathbf1_{q_{(c_i,c_j)}<G_0}\) is
\(\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}\). Its entrywise product with \(B\) has eigenvalues \(1,-1\). Smooth weights with the same support separation give the same counterexample. Thus a positive complete-zero Gram cannot generically be bounded after gcd truncation by treating that truncation as a positive projection. This explains why T07 leaves the full small-gcd covariance and removes the already paid zero form only globally. It does not prove a negative eigenvalue for the particular arithmetic field.

## A16. Unequal Type I cutoffs

**PROVED bounded extension of the inherited Type I theorem.** Sources: BB R04b; M (3.15), (M.4)–(M.7), (M.35).

Let \(m_i=\mu1_{q\le Y_i}\), \(u_i=\delta-m_i*\mathbf1\), and \(R=Y_1Y_2\). Convolution algebra gives
\[
 \mu=m_1+m_2-m_1*m_2*\mathbf1+\mu*u_1*u_2.
\]
For the completed product Type I array \(a=-m_1*m_2\), one has support \(q_r\le R\), divisor-bounded coefficients, and prime valuations at most two. The unchanged central estimate M (3.15) costs
\(DK\|a\|_2^2\ll(DKR)^\epsilon DKR\).
The mixed estimate M (M.35) has outer weight
\(q_{\operatorname{rad}(rs)}^{1/2+\epsilon}/q_r\); the two divisor-weighted sums have sizes \(R^{1/2+\epsilon}\) and \(R^{3/2+\epsilon}\). Their product is \(R^{2+\epsilon}\). The double-residue factors \(q_r^{-1},q_s^{-1}\) have only subpower summed cost, exactly as in M (M.4)–(M.7). Therefore
\[
 |\mathfrak Q[I,I]|\ll(DKR)^\epsilon
 \{D^{5/3}K^{1/3}+D^{4/3}K^{7/12}R^2+DKR\}. \tag{A16.1}
\]
Both original Mellin roots and whole profiles remain in force. At \(K=D^k\), the two cutoff-dependent terms are affordable when
\[
 \log_D R<\min\{1-k,(8-7k)/24\}. \tag{A16.2}
\]
This enlarges the choice of decomposition geometry; it proves no improved remainder estimate.

## A17. Exact completed-cutoff and rough-column obstructions

**PROVED counterexamples and quantitative restricted bounds.** Sources: SA ([restricted research revision])–([restricted research revision]); CP (27); BB R04b.

The all-ideal identity \(I_Y(n)=-\mu(n)\) for \(q_n\le Y\) cannot be applied only to the squarefree core after completion. Take \(c=1,B=p\), with \(Q=q_p>Y\). Then \(I_Y(1)=I_Y(p^3)=-1\), and T05's exact density gives
\[
 \mathcal A_Y(1,p)
 =-1-Q^{-1/2}\overline{\xi_{\rm ang}(p)}(1-Q^{-1})\ne-1.
 \tag{A17.1}
\]
The stronger condition \(q_cq_B^3\le Y\) does imply
\(\mathcal A_Y(c,B)=-\mu(c)\): every sampled \(ct^3\) lies below the cutoff, and for \(t\ne1\) its Möbius value is zero. Cancellation therefore concerns small whole columns and requires both corresponding completed coefficients. It is not a cancellation of every small-core packet.

There is also a finite-cutoff averaging obstruction. Let \(c=pq,e=r\) for distinct good primes exceeding every cutoff in a fixed collection. Then \(I_Y(c)=I_Y(e)=-1\), while \(\mu(c)\mu(e)=-1\). Any normalized average of those cutoffs leaves
\[
 \mu(c)\mu(e)-I_Y(c)I_Y(e)=-2. \tag{A17.2}
\]
This rules out coefficientwise annihilation, not cancellation after summing columns with their actual phases.

The larger cutoff is not forbidden by the inherited Type I theorem: at \(K=D^k\), \(Y=D^y\), it permits
\[
 y<\min\{(1-k)/2,(8-7k)/48\}.
\]
For \(k=.8765\), the endpoint is \(.03884375\), whereas T05's complete cube-row restriction has a strict saving only for
\(y<(1-k)/6=.020583333\ldots\). That latter threshold is a limitation of its upper bound.

The bare outside-cube sector has a sharper rigorous estimate:
\[
 |P_{\rm cub}\mathfrak Q[I,I]_{B=E=1}|
 \ll_\epsilon(DKY)^\epsilon D^{2/3}K^{2/3}Y^4. \tag{A17.3}
\]
To prove it, repeat T05 without the outer cube sums and use the fixed-ray squarefree estimate on \(\Re s=1/2+\delta\). The two columns contribute \(D^{2+2\delta}Y^4\); row counting contributes \(K^{2/3}D^{-4/3}\). Choose the preliminary divisor loss below \(2\delta\) so its coprime-projector sum converges, then choose \(\delta\) inside the final epsilon. This gives (A17.3).

At \(k=.8765\), even the supremum over the admitted cutoff interval gives exponent \(11251/8000=1.406375\). These bounds do not produce a critical-sized II term available to offset the still-unpaid principal C–C contribution in the bare sector. This is an upper-budget comparison, not a lower bound on that C–C contribution.

statement:
## A18. Broad-cusp diagonal oldforms: exact support and scaling screen

**PROVED support and scaling identities; no new changed-current norm is established.** Sources: SA Part I §11, (S16)–(S19); [restricted research revision] AA21–AA23; [restricted research revision] AB14–AB15.

Let \(Q=q_p\), \(\Phi_r=\operatorname{diag}(p^r,1)\), and let the broad cusp be
\(\gamma=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&0\\C_0&1\end{smallmatrix}\right)\).
For nonnegative integer \(r\), choose \(p^rd_r-C_0b_r=1\), compatibly with the fixed level. Direct multiplication gives
\[
 \Phi_r\gamma=
 \begin{pmatrix}p^r&b_r\\C_0&d_r\end{pmatrix}
 \begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&p^r\end{pmatrix}
 \begin{pmatrix}1&-b_r\\0&1\end{pmatrix}. \tag{A18.1}
\]
The first source has frequency \(\mu n/p^r\), height \(Y/Q^{r/2}\), and its exact translated phase. The ordinary twisted second source has frequency \(\mu m/p^2\), height \(Y/Q\), and its multiplier vanishes if \(p\mid m\). Opposite frequency matching forces
\[
 m=p^{2-r}n. \tag{A18.2}
\]
Thus \(r=0\) and \(r=1\) vanish identically. A single-prime dilation does not restore the ordinary orientation.

At the first favorable dilation \(r=2\), unit indices are allowed and both heights are \(Y/Q\). Even assuming the fixed phases match the desired arithmetic coefficient, the invariant radial pairing is
\[
 \int J(Y/Q)Y^{2s}\frac{dY}{Y^3}
 =Q^{2s-2}\int J(y)y^{2s}\frac{dy}{y^3}. \tag{A18.3}
\]
Probability averaging cancels the horizontal Jacobian. Extraction therefore costs \(Q^{2-2\sigma}\), namely \(Q\) at the central edge, before any cost of a new current norm.

The source supports valuations \(0,1\pmod3\). For \(r=2+3j\), matching gives \(n=p^{3j}m\); the coefficient relation
\(\tau(p^{3j}m)=Q^{j/2}\tau(m)\), together with the first source's height factor \(Q^{-3j/2}\), leaves \(Q^{-j}\). Its favorable period factor is \(Q^{2s-2-j}\), worsening extraction. For \(r=3+3j\), the new squarefree prime contributes the inverse cubic phase that cancels the ordinary row twist, producing a principal good core rather than the desired ordinary one. For \(r=4+3j\), the forbidden local valuation makes it vanish.

For a negative dilation \(r=-m\), \(m\ge1\), use the projective representative \(\operatorname{diag}(1,p^m)\). The exact identity
\[
 \begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&p^m\end{pmatrix}\gamma
 =\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\p^mC_0&1\end{pmatrix}
  \begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&p^m\end{pmatrix}
\]
again gives first-source scale \(z/p^m,Y/Q^{m/2}\). The first unit-compatible case \(m=2\) has the same favorable radial cost. The available common cover
\(\Gamma_0(p^2)\cap\Gamma^0(p^m)\) has good-prime index
\(Q^{m+2}(1+Q^{-1})\); imposing its two off-diagonal divisibilities in the determinant-one matrices proves this count. At the broad cusp the width is \(p^{\max(m,2)}\), because conjugating its unipotent requires the same parameter to satisfy both divisibilities. Its available probability-normalized seed norm therefore has an additional cost of order \(Q^{\min(m,2)/2}\).

These are costs and support restrictions for the specified diagonal-oldform construction, not minimal-norm theorems for every source or cusp. General oldform combinations, non-diagonal constructions, and a test projected onto the actual current span remain possible, but require a better calibrated period-to-norm ratio and an actual norm estimate.
title: A18. Broad-cusp diagonal oldforms: exact support and scaling screen

### W40-01 — Cumulant cancellation before absolute moments; p=.22
O: Replace a high absolute moment expansion by the logarithm of a signed Gaussian generating function; isolate connected arithmetic correlations as cumulants.
B: A full uniform cumulant majorant, including repeated indices and all masks, could lower the actual .24973 moment exponent below .24898 with buffer.
T: Compute the first four cumulants for a finite signed zero-extended multiplicative toy sequence and compare termwise absolute and connected bounds.
X: The desired positive majorant may itself discard the cancellation; formal log coefficients need not control the required moment.
R: Direct moment-bottleneck replacement, potentially upstream to larger c.

### W40-02 — Orthogonalize the two heights jointly; p=.12
O: Treat the two height parameters as coordinates of a Mellin wave packet and construct orthogonal polynomials against their exact common measure before applying Cauchy.
B: A two-height Bessel inequality that preserves the zero detector might remove a duplicated height-volume loss.
T: Derive the 2 by 2 Gram matrix for two coincident height windows and inspect whether tensor-product orthogonality falsely doubles dimension.
X: A fixed offending zero requires pointwise control, so averaging in its height may be inadmissible.
R: Modest direct exponent saving if the actual loss is a joint-volume artifact.

### W40-03 — Magnetic holonomy in the ordered H graph; p=.055
O: Encode each signed H interaction as a weighted directed edge with its exact complex phase; gauge along a forest and retain cycle holonomies.
B: Quantified nontrivial holonomy could force cancellation in the complete quadratic form without replacing arithmetic coefficients by arbitrary vectors.
T: Derive an exact triangle identity and compare its cancellation with a rank-one phase coboundary.
X: Arithmetic phases may be pure coboundaries; projectors or sparse incidence may destroy useful cycles.

O: Before norm estimates, average the original Gaussian arithmetic sum over its exact unit orbits and decompose the coefficient into unit representations.
B: Orthogonality might remove an unwanted angular or parity mode while preserving the fixed trivial-infinity family and its transfer.
T: Write the four-unit trace for an arbitrary signed coefficient and determine which original terms survive.
X: Existing coefficients may already be unit-invariant, giving no new cancellation.
R: Exact simplification or proof of redundancy; modest exponent gain only if a costly mode vanishes.

### W40-05 — Exterior-power exclusion witness; p=.035
O: Form a small matrix of shifted copies of the zero detector and study a determinant or exterior power instead of a single norm.
B: A hypothetical zero could create an approximate linear dependence whose determinant lower bound is arithmetic and cheaper than the scalar high moment.
T: Two-detector toy calculation: determine whether both detectors share the same zero factor and the determinant vanishes identically.
X: Common-factor degeneracy or determinant estimates can multiply every existing loss.

## G103. Complete unsmoothed energy and fixed-modulus covariance

For a fixed ordinary character chi, with its natural zeros, put
a(n)=mu(n)chi(n), M(x)=sum_(n<=x)a(n). Complete multiplicativity gives
a*chi=delta. Direct finite integration gives the exact positive energy

    E_chi(X)=integral_1^X |M(x)|^2 dx/x
      =sum_(m,n<=X)a(m)conj(a(n))log(X/max(m,n)).

The terminal weight is zero; all signed off-diagonals and both orientations
remain. If, for every fixed chi and epsilon>0, E_chi(X)<<X^(2gamma+epsilon)
at all large dyadic X with one common0<gamma<1, positivity extends it to all
large X. On each dyadic interval, Cauchy--Schwarz gives locally uniform
convergence of integral M(x)x^(-s)dx/x and all its s derivatives for
Re(s)>gamma. Initially s times that integral equals1/L(s,chi). The identity
continues meromorphically and excludes all L zeros in that half-plane;
the principal pole at1 becomes a reciprocal zero. This avoids lossy
pointwise extraction from the energy. Constants and thresholds depend on
the fixed character; no growing-conductor bound is claimed.

For ALL characters of one fixed modulus q, orthogonality gives

    Ebar_q=(1/phi(q))sum_(chi mod q)E_chi
      =sum_(m,n<=X,(mn,q)=1,m=n mod q)mu(m)mu(n)log(X/max(m,n)).

Since each energy is nonnegative, E_chi<=phi(q)Ebar_q. The literal diagonal
is d_q X+O_q(sqrt X+1), where
d_q=(phi(q)/q)product_(p not dividing q)(1-p^-2)>0. This follows by inserting
mu(n)^2=sum_(d^2|n)mu(d) and counting units, then integrating. For gamma>1/2
it is already below the target. The entire signed off-diagonal upper bound
OFF_q(X)<<X^(2gamma+epsilon), for every fixed q and all large X, is the
remaining arithmetic input. There is no absolute value inside this sum.
At q=1 it already includes the unsolved complete Mobius energy.

At current c10, first gain requires gamma<.87485404, squared exponent
2gamma<1.74970808 and saving>.25029192 from the elementary exponent2.
Targets1/6 and1/4 require squared exponents5/3 and3/2. No part of these
arithmetic gaps is paid here. The general weak/energy continuation principle
is existing F01/W27/W35 ancestry; the value is this complete source contract.

## G104. Actual finite character traces and their exact limitation

The squarefree prime polynomial P_X(z)=sum_(n<=X,(n,q0)=1)mu(n)z(n) has
torus norm squared Q_q0(X)=sum mu(n)^2 over the same support. Its evaluation
norm is sqrt(Q_q0(X)). The actual coefficients attain this loss at z_p=-1,
where P_X=Q_q0(X)=d_q0 X+O_q0(sqrt X).

Every prescribed finite set of real prime signs is realizable by an ordinary
character. CRT selects an odd D=1 mod4, coprime to q0 and every p<=X,
with the desired quadratic residues and D=1 or5 mod8 when2 is unramified.
Then chi(n)=1_((n,q0)=1)(n/D) has those signs and exactly the q0 zeros up toX;
the extra D zeros beyondX remain. Jacobi characters and composite reciprocity
license this construction without requiring D prime or squarefree.
[NIST DLMF27.9](https://dlmf.nist.gov/27.9) records those facts.

Thus a conductor-independent phase trace of loss X^eta with eta<1/2 fails,
even for actual arithmetic coefficients with the full inverse identity.
The realizing character changes with X. This does NOT refute fixed-character
estimates whose constant and onset depend on chi. For a fixed q, the exact
character-average trace factor is instead sqrt(phi(q)), an allowed constant;
its ambient norm contains the full same-residue signed covariance of G103.
The earlier G71 fixed-sequence asymptotic countermodel has different scope.

For sqrt X<=y<=X the complete one-large-prime complement is exactly

    M_z(X)=S_y(X)-sum_(y<p<=X,p not dividing q0) z_p A(X/p),
    R_y(X)=sum_p |A(X/p)|,

where S_y is the entire smooth part and A depends only on fixed low-prime
values. Its maximal distance from S_y is R_y and its diameter is2R_y;
this does not assert that every point in a disk is attainable. For real low
values, opposite prime signs attain S_y+/-R_y and are realized by the CRT
characters above. The exact endpoint-sensitive price is

    R_y=sum_(1<=m<=floor(X/y)) |A(m)|
       [pi_q0(X/m)-pi_q0(max(y,X/(m+1)))].

If y<=X/2 the m=1 term is at least pi_q0(X)-pi_q0(X/2), asymptotic to
X/(2log X) for fixed q0 by the ordinary prime number theorem.
[NIST DLMF27.12](https://dlmf.nist.gov/27.12) supplies that asymptotic;
the identities need no PNT. This prevents uniformly sublinear phase-blind
pricing, but fixed-q characters agreeing on all unramified primes<=q are
identical, by factoring each least unit representative. Once y>=q, the
independent tail is unavailable. Global character linkage remains a live
escape, not a disproof. All smooth terms, cofactors and later cross energies
must be retained.
title: G104. Actual finite character traces and their exact limitation

For Z=1+Az+R, sum|c_k|<=B, |A|>=8 and lambda=B/|A|^2<=1/8,
Rouche on |z|=2/|A| gives exactly one root counted with multiplicity:
the linear term has modulus>=1 and |R|<=4lambda<=1/2. For B>0,
on the circle centered at -1/A with radius2lambda/|A|,
|R|<=lambda(1+2lambda)^2<=25lambda/16<2lambda. Thus this same root
alpha is simple, uniquely nearest to0, and

    |A alpha+1|<=2lambda,
    (1-2lambda)/|A|<=|alpha|<=(1+2lambda)/|A|.

B=0 gives alpha=-1/A directly. Every circle is within |z|<1, so the
quadratic remainder bound is valid. Exact polynomial division gives
Z(z)=(1-z/alpha)Q(z), Q(0)=1, and the complete endpoint comparison

    (|A|/2)|Q(-1)|<=|Z(-1)|<=2|A||Q(-1)|.

The lower bound uses |1/alpha|-1>=4|A|/5-1>=|A|/2; the upper uses
1+4|A|/3<=2|A|. No truncated reciprocal or approximate root is substituted.

For the principal character of fixed q, A_N=P_N is the unramified prime
count. The elementary bound
4^m/(2m+1)<=binom(2m,m)<=(2m)^pi(2m), with m=floor(N/2), yields
P_N>>_q N/log N. Therefore all large N satisfy the lemma, and

    alpha_N=-P_N^(-1)(1+O_q((log N)^2/N)).

Reality follows from conjugation and uniqueness; alpha_N<0. The local
Taylor series log Z_N at0 has radius exactly |alpha_N|. This rules out a
fixed zero-free disk and the straight real path to-1 for these polynomials.
It leaves complex paths, exact deflation and different smoothing eligible.
A fugacity zero is not an L-function zero or a lower bound for M(N).

For every-epsilon exponents, the principal endpoint comparison implies

    M_chi0(N)<<N^(gamma+epsilon)
      iff Q_N(-1)<<N^(gamma-1+epsilon).

A bounded deflated endpoint is insufficient. First gain beyond c10 needs
decay beyond N^(-.12514596), with strict every-epsilon buffering. Targets
1/6 and1/4 require the corresponding power decays.

For arbitrary fixed chi, select the root branch exactly when |A_N|>=8
and |A_N|^2>=8B_N. Otherwise |1-A_N|=O(sqrt N), and
M_chi(N)=1-A_N+R_N(-1). Hence for1/2<gamma<1 the COMPLETE criterion

    root branch: |A_N Q_N(-1)|<<_(chi,epsilon)N^(gamma+epsilon),
    non-root branch: |R_N(-1)|<<_(chi,epsilon)N^(gamma+epsilon)

is equivalent to the all-N Mertens exponent gamma. Arbitrary branch
switches are allowed; neither branch or any exceptional cutoff is omitted.
One common gamma for every fixed ordinary chi gives all-height zero
exclusion through s integral_1^infinity M_chi(x)x^(-s-1)dx=1/L(s,chi),
initially on Re(s)>1 and then by meromorphic identity on Re(s)>gamma.
The principal pole becomes a reciprocal zero. Constants/onsets may depend
on chi; no growing-conductor or Hecke transfer follows.

At gamma=.8748 the conditional c=.1252 exceeds c10 by.00005404;
the non-root prime sector costs exponent1/2. This is a complete conditional
budget, not an achieved bound. The equivalent signed inputs remain OPEN.

There is also a necessary second-root consequence. If an actual principal
Mertens bound of exponent1-c is supplied for every epsilon, then
Q_N(-1)<<N^(-c+epsilon). Since a squarefree integer with D primes is at
least(D+1)!, deg Z_N<=(1+o(1))log N/loglog N. Factoring all roots of Q,
one factor |1+1/zeta| is at most |Q(-1)|^(1/deg Q). For every eta>0,
some root distinct from alpha_N consequently satisfies

    |zeta_N+1|<=2(log N)^(-c+eta)

for all large N. If Q(-1)=0 the conclusion is immediate; degree0 is
eventually excluded by the assumed decay. The upper degree bound has the
right direction because log|Q(-1)| is negative. One root near-1 is not
sufficient: every other factor is still unpaid. No bare strip statement
is silently promoted to the required pointwise Mertens input.

The older fugacity/continued-power/cluster and small-face roots retain
ancestry. The useful increment is the full large-cutoff root with explicit
constants and a two-branch, fully paid deflated source contract.

## G107. Exact divisor elimination and the real-cutoff repair

For indices1..N let C(m,n)=chi(n/m)1_(m|n) and
A(m,n)=mu(n/m)chi(n/m)1_(m|n). Exact convolution gives CA=AC=I.
For ANY retained set R containing1, with complement E, put

    S=C_RR-C_RE C_EE^-1 C_ER,
    v=1_R-C_RE C_EE^-1 1_E.

Then S^-1=A_RR and M_chi(N)=e1^T S^-1 v. A prefix has zero return
C_ER but still the full deleted source injection. An interleaved partition
need not: at N=6,chi=1,R={1,6}, S=[[1,-1],[0,1]],v=(-2,1),readout=-1.
Acyclicity forbids returning to the same vertex, not paths between two
different retained vertices. G69's chronological zero-feedback scope stays.

For a prime endpoint p, the coefficient of arbitrary source input w_p
in the root output remains -chi(p) under every exact partition. It may
still cancel against other signed endpoints. The finite chain inverse
sum_k(-[C-I])^k restores each individual mu coefficient, not cancellation
between integers.

For a=mu chi, b_U=a1_(n<=U), r_U=delta-b_U*chi, convolution gives

    a=sum_(j=0)^(k-1)b_U*r_U^(*j)+a*r_U^(*k).

**Use support at least(floor(U)+1)^k for real U>=1.** The author's
(U+1)^k requires integer U. At U=3/2,chi=1,r_U(2)=-1 and
r_U^(*2)(4)=1, although4<25/4. The frozen author text is preserved;
this correction governs reuse. Intermediate squareful terms remain:
at U=5, r_U(12)=1 while(b_U*r_U)(12)=0.

For p>U prime and k>=2, the entire endpoint lies in the first residual
layer, with coefficient -chi(p). A principal-character absolute certificate
itemizing these endpoints pays >>N/log N when U<=N^u, fixed u<1.
This obstructs that unmerged absolute price only, not a signed Schur norm,
the Mertens sum, weighted observations or cross-endpoint cancellation.

Anchored future telescoping and the full mixed filter
M(x)-2M(x/2)-3M(x/3)+6M(x/6) are retained as duplicate-level identities.
They require the stated subunit-growth boundary input. Commutation for
every function gives no new arithmetic magnitude estimate.

## G108. Complete prime-block interactions and descendant errors

The protected25 audit defines H_B(t)=sum_(d|P_B,d<=t)mu(d)chi(d), where
P_B is the product of a finite prime block. Unique coprime factorization
gives the complete contraction

    M_chi(X)=sum_(m<=X,(m,P_B)=1)mu(m)chi(m)H_B(X/m).

For p<r and h_p(t)=1-chi(p)1_(t>=p), the exact missing interaction is

    H_{p,r}(t)-h_p(t)h_r(t)=-chi(p)chi(r)1_(r<=t<pr).

Thus naive product replacement discards the signed cofactor interval
-chi(p)chi(r)sum_(X/(pr)<m<=X/r,(m,pr)=1)mu(m)chi(m).
The strict lower/inclusive upper endpoints and ramified zeros are essential.
For principal p=2,r=3, H takes values1,0,-1,0 on the four successive
cutoff intervals. An everywhere-positive Gibbs model or finite real
logarithmic potential cannot represent it. The absolute discarded price
is X/(2pi^2)+O(sqrt X), from squarefree-unit density3/pi^2 and interval
length X/6. This does not lower-bound the signed interval.

All higher interactions remain: the coefficient for S subset B,|S|>=2
is(-1)^|S|chi(p_S)z_S[1_(p_S<=t)-1_(max S<=t)]. No pairwise closure
or positivity follows. Any approximation must bound BOTH its entire
signed contraction and the entire signed error before the Mertens return.
Moving blocks also require uniform constants in their actual choice.

The uniform19 audit uses the exact largest-prime state
S_chi(x,y)=sum_(n<=x,P+(n)<=y)mu(n)chi(n), with n=1. It satisfies

    S_chi(x,y)=1-sum_(p<=min(x,y))chi(p)S_chi(x/p,p^-).

For any approximation F define
Delta_F=F-1+sum_p chi(p)F(x/p,p^-). Finite substitution gives

    F(x,y)-S_chi(x,y)=Delta_F(x,y)
      +sum_(2<=d<=x,mu(d)^2=1,P+(d)<=y)
          mu(d)chi(d)Delta_F(x/d,P-(d)^-).

All strict descendant states, signs and natural zeros survive. Merge equal
integer states with their signed coefficients before taking absolute values.
This is the smooth/largest-prime version of the existing renewal ancestry.
Inserting F=x^rho without its y state cannot test an arithmetic spectral
mode: already S(t,2^-)=1. Finite Euler polynomials have no zeros on
Re(s)>0, but their infinite continuation/identification below1 is not
licensed by that finite fact. The complete signed defect estimate remains.

## G109. Fixed countable banks, exact buffering and the complete source

Let lambda_j>1, w_j>0 and 0<W=sum_j w_j<infinity be fixed. Write
ell_j=log(lambda_j), r_j=exp(-delta ell_j), for delta>=0, and

    F_delta(t)=sum_j w_j |1-r_j exp(-it ell_j)|^2,
    A(delta)=sum_j w_j (1-r_j)^2.

Both sums converge uniformly in real t by domination with 4w_j. Exactly

    F_delta(t)-A(delta)
      =2 sum_j w_j r_j (1-cos(t ell_j)) >=0.             (75.1)

For any finite head of length r and integers H,L>=1, divide the unit
r-torus into H^r boxes. Two of the H^r+1 points nL(ell_1,...,ell_r)/(2pi)
modulo1 lie in the same box. Their difference gives t=Lq with
L<=t<=L H^r and distance(t ell_j/(2pi),Z)<=1/H for every j<=r.
Consequently, uniformly for delta>=0,

    0<=F_delta(t)-A(delta)
      <=4pi^2 W_head/H^2+4W_tail.                      (75.2)

Given any fixed T>=0, first take L>=max(1,ceil(T)), then a sufficiently
small full tail and sufficiently large H. Equations75.1-2 prove

    inf_(t>=T) F_delta(t)=A(delta).                    (75.3)

This uses no independence assumption on the logarithms. It keeps every
channel and never changes character to manufacture adverse phases. The
principal character modulo1 already defeats a shortcut required for all
ordinary characters. Arbitrarily prescribed complex target phases on
related scales are outside this identity-target recurrence proof. The
large bound L H^r gives no useful arithmetic power estimate in height.

At delta=0 the infimum is zero. At delta>0 it is positive and also equals
F_delta(0). Dominated convergence gives A(delta)->0 as delta decreases
to zero. Furthermore,

    A(delta)/delta^2 -> sum_j w_j (log lambda_j)^2,

where the limit may be +infinity. For a finite second log moment use
dominated convergence; otherwise arbitrarily large finite partial moments
force the liminf to infinity. Summability alone does not supply a finite
quadratic coefficient or a universal decay rate. For lambda_j=2^j,
w_j=2^-j, j>=1, the exact checks are A(1)=10/21 and second log moment
6(log2)^2.

On the global space L2(R_+,x^(-2sigma) dx/x), put sigma=beta+delta and
D_j V(x)=V(x)-lambda_j^beta V(x/lambda_j). The unitary logarithmic change
f(u)=exp(-sigma u)V(exp u), Tonelli and Plancherel give

    sum_j w_j ||D_j V||_global^2 >= A(delta)||V||_global^2.

Continuity of the uniformly convergent symbol and localized Fourier
packets show sharpness, also near arbitrarily high near-minimizers.
These are unrestricted test functions, not arithmetic sources. A single
point frequency is not a nonzero L2 extremizer. The theorem is not an
exact constant for a joint physical-shell norm, nor for a sum of separate
shell suprema. Those distinctions from G52/Sol03 remain essential.

### Formation is paid for the actual Gaussian source

Fix tau>0 and the normalized Gaussian g_tau(v)=(2pi tau)^(-1/2)
exp(-v^2/(2tau)). Let

    a(n)=mu(n)chi(n), U(y)=sum_n a(n)g_tau(log(n/y)).

For any A>max(1,beta), the elementary bound |a(n)|<=1 proves for all y>0

    |U(y)|<=C_A y^A,
    C_A=zeta(A)(2pi tau)^(-1/2) exp(tau A^2/2).

Indeed n^A g_tau(log(n/y)) is at most y^A times the supremum of
exp(Av)g_tau(v), and sum_n n^-A=zeta(A). Hence |D_j U(x)|<=2C_A x^A
uniformly in j, since lambda_j^(beta-A)<=1. In particular

    sum_(j>r) w_j |D_j U(x)|^2 <=4C_A^2 x^(2A) W_tail.

The entire bank is therefore well defined locally and on every finite
shell, with its complete tail paid. This closes the source-formation
qualification in the shared review. It supplies only an exponent A>1;
the desired subtrivial arithmetic moment remains OPEN.

### Endpoint correction: gamma=beta is admissible

Suppose the COMPLETE bank obeys, for every epsilon>0 and every sufficiently
large dyadic X,

    sum_j w_j integral_X^(2X) |D_j U(x)|^2 dx/x
      =O_(chi,epsilon)(X^(2gamma+epsilon)),
    0<gamma<1, beta<=gamma.                            (75.4)

Choose one fixed channel with positive weight. For every sigma>gamma,
choose epsilon<2(sigma-gamma). Dyadic covering, finite initial shells
and the preceding all-y bound give its finite N_sigma norm, where
N_sigma(V)=sup_(X>0) X^-sigma ||V||_[X,2X]. Since sigma>beta, its causal
inverse converges geometrically, with cost

    w_j^(-1/2)/(1-lambda_j^(beta-sigma)).

The K-th telescoping remainder is lambda_j^((K+1)beta)
U(x/lambda_j^(K+1)), bounded by C_A x^A
lambda_j^(-(K+1)(A-beta)); it tends to zero. Thus (75.4) returns the
same every-epsilon exponent gamma for U, INCLUDING gamma=beta.
The inverse constant may diverge as sigma approaches beta; that is
permitted in an every-epsilon conclusion. No inverse at sigma=beta is
asserted. This corrects the shared review's unnecessarily strict beta<gamma.

The direct Mellin check gives the same result: the numerator of this
channel is (1-lambda_j^(beta-s)) exp(tau s^2/2), which has no zero in
Re(s)>gamma when gamma>=beta. Its transform is holomorphic there under
the complete shell hypothesis and the paid left tail, so the reciprocal-L
identity excludes every zero in that half-plane. For gamma<beta one
channel leaves numerator zeros on Re(s)=beta. Two multiplicatively
independent scales leave a possible simple real zero at beta; the existing
G47 exception must still be addressed. No automatic stronger family
theorem follows.

The live alternatives outside the obstruction are height-dependent or
nonsummable banks, different critical lines, signed cross-channel forms,
and estimates restricted to the actual arithmetic source. Each owes its
own definition, complete costs and zero-exclusion return. Chaining or
simultaneous use remains eligible when it supplies actual new arithmetic
control; additional fixed positive channels alone supply no critical gap.

## G110. The canonical amplitude-conditioned theorem

Fix the original canonical ray-character family, genuine good-prime pool,
common slot profile, natural coefficient zeros, fixed polynomial puncture
and one physical high bin delta in[17/25,7/10]. The accepted [private research revision]
re-anchoring permits the witness presentation to differ from the original
slot parent, keeping its actual quotient/pool and exact zero extensions.
Fixed extra holes are removed by the signed B3.41 expansion before
Minkowski. Arbitrary MI coefficients or prime subsets are not thereby
admissible in MP. Both inverse and plain witnesses come from one actual
zero, at the same character, real part and height. Slot heights remain
independent. The physical bin supplies upper slot prices; a larger internal
height-box maximum is never substituted for that upper price.

Normalize the row width W to1 temporarily and write v=z/W<=1/20. Fix
positive squared-amplitude grades 0<=q_i<=delta with
sum_i q_i z_i<=qv, delta-.01<=q<=delta. This is a bound on positive
grades, not merely a product bound that lets tiny factors offset large
ones. Amplitude classes and one greedy original slot subset are fixed
before each class/dyad moment. One fractional-slot loss and all mesh,
height and profile losses are paid. No division by a possibly zero slot
is used. With witness cutoff t fixed before witnesses, the source gives
r<=t, r+m>=t, 0<=m<=1/2 and squared witnesses at least
Z^(delta r), Z^(delta m), up to preallocated small losses.

Partial inverse marking minimizes the actual amplified inverse moment
plus the full complementary slot price. Since 2x<=r for the permitted
marked width and r>=1/2, its third capacity term is dominated. The exact
piecewise bound is

    I(r)=1-delta r+q[v-(1-r)/2]_+    (r<=1),
    L(r)=1/6+(5/6-delta)r+qv        (r>=1),
    P(m)=1-2delta m+q[v-(1-2m)/(9/2)]_+.

The factor2 in the plain term is its fourth power. I and P decrease,
while L increases; I remains continuous through its kink. This removes
the previous nonbinding transition hump without adding a new moment
theorem. Bounded/zero plain witnesses use the old unrestricted no-slot
theorem; all finite dyads and derivative-profile pairs retain common
thresholds.

Put h_delta=5-2delta, e_delta=5-6delta and
D=135delta-54delta^2-20q. Balancing the short crossing against L(t)
gives the weighted-density exponent

    E_delta,q(W,z)=rho W+max(4delta q z/h_delta,-aW+bz),
    rho=1-10delta/(3h_delta),
    a=2delta q e_delta^2/(3h_delta D),
    b=3delta q(15+18delta-8q)/D.                         (76.1)

The switch is v0=2e_delta/(135-54delta-24q). The two cutoffs are
(5-6qv)/h_delta and
(135delta-20q-12delta q-108delta qv+24q^2v)/D.
Their short crossings are respectively2t/3 and
[(18delta-4q)t+2q-9qv]/(27delta-4q).
Eleven entire cleared polynomial inequalities, with194 positive rational
Bernstein coefficients, verify all denominators, cutoff/witness ranges,
inverse kink gates and a<1/500 on the FULL delta/omega/v box, where
omega=delta-q in[0,.01]. At q=delta this is exactly the previously
accepted nonlinear envelope, not an additional gain counted twice.

The first branch has partial_q E/W>=68v/91. On the second branch,
a'_q>0 and v>=v0 give partial_q E/(Wv)>=b'_q-a'_q/v0>=7/10;
its entire cleared numerator is among the positive certificates.
Continuity across the switch and integration prove

    E_delta,delta(W,z)-E_delta,delta-omega(W,z)
       >=(7/10)omega z,  0<=omega<=.01.                (76.2)

For raw w=u b^6 keep the actual root holes, freeze b and put
s=log_Z Nb, V=W-6s. The main range V>=20W/21 decays at rate
6(rho-a)-1>0. In the tail, the old unmarked density with the actual
conditioned slot price pays the entire gain<=3k(delta)z, where
k=rho+delta-1 and z<=W/21: rho-1/6-3k(.68)=818/61425>0.
Bounded free windows and fixed-inducing free cores retain their raw
population O(Z^(W/6+qz+small)); they are not declared finite raw sets.

The additional saving can be applied after the two transforms to their
positive child energies if each actual live list satisfies the condition.
For empty common support, trivial projectors and no clipping, both live
widths equal the original z; their Cauchy average gains7omega z/10.
An original deficit is NOT transported through arbitrary signed mask
removal or discarded slots. No theorem here forces any such deficit.

The retained scalar extremizer shows only that the stated one-witness
positive moments, marking/amplification choices and convex Hölder
combinations cannot force a uniform improvement at q=delta. It does not
construct an arithmetic high row, simultaneous witnesses at all cutoffs
or independence of the two events. A true mixed estimate remains eligible.
The concrete target OPEN-J is a positive power saving in the inverse
moment restricted to the actual large-plain-witness rows near the short
crossing, keeping the same zero, labels, heights, holes and full signed
reconstruction. The separate moments still provide only zero extra saving.

## G111. Accepted c10 licenses a smaller density capacity

This step uses the literal PR9 theorem, not its original choice of
parameter. At commit58344dfdbe756cf2f743da1908ffe0582418cf5b, paper
SHA2562b4c67c3e817d7854ee57e451cea1789c8a4a1d03a72ddb83b980421167096d8,
B3.40 assumes 7/10<=kappa<=3/4, beta_*>=51/100 and
2beta_*-1<=kappa. Its positive-slot capacity is
n1+n2+6kappa z<=M, with the original fixed-inducing exclusions,
canonical pools, individual ray characters and common profile. Its
common mesh precedes the arithmetic family, slot count, profiles and
height uniformly over that kappa interval. Equality in the supremum
condition is allowed; the prime contour has its own positive margin.

The accepted [[private research revision] return](../[private research revision]/valuation-integration.md) bounds
the SAME finite-order trivial-infinity Eisenstein Hecke-family supremum
beta_*<=theta10=.87485404. This is explicit in its independent review
Section7, not merely an ordinary-character conclusion. An ordinary-only
bound would be insufficient for this step. Therefore under a putative
beta_*>theta11 we may fix, BEFORE target or witness selection,

    kappa10=2theta10-1=9371351/12500000=.74970808,
    K=6kappa10=28114053/6250000=4.49824848.

All B3.40 hypotheses hold. The dependency is acyclic:

    original accepted contracts -> accepted c10 family theorem
      -> original B3.40 at fixed kappa10 -> new density -> c11.

Only the density proof uses the reduced K. The physical detector keeps
its actual kappa=2beta_*-1; descendant, low and fallback budgets retain
9/2. The numerical kappa_*=2theta11-1 is not a moment premise.

Replace the plain line in the unconditioned calculation by
P_K(m)=1-2delta m+delta[v-(1-2m)/K]_+. With

    D_K=15K-10-6Kdelta,
    a_K=delta(5-6delta)^2/[3(5-2delta)D_K],
    b_K=2delta(5-6delta)(K-1)/D_K,
    G_K(W,z)=min(3k(delta)z,a_K W+b_K z),              (76.3)

the complete high-row bound is Z^(rho W+delta z-G_K(W,z)+epsilon)
times its original polynomial height factor. Seven source gates with64
positive coefficients cover the ENTIRE delta in[.68,.70], K in[Knew,9/2],
v in[0,.05] box. The full-fit cutoff and crossing are
t=(5-6delta v)/(5-2delta), r=2t/3. Otherwise they are

    t=[15K-10-6delta-12delta(K-1)v]/D_K,
    r=[(2K-2)t+1-Kv]/(3K-2).

The exact switch is v=(5-6delta)/[3K(5-2delta)-12delta]. The same
root-tail proof applies because a_K<1/500 and G_K<=3kz. This theorem
is unconditioned on amplitudes. When both affine branches are active,

    G_K(W,z)-G_(9/2)(W,z)
      =delta(5-6delta)^2(9/2-K)(W-2z)/(D_K D_(9/2)).  (76.4)

This is a strict source gain for W>2z, including legal empty common
support. No strict gain is asserted when the min chooses3kz. All original
anchor, label, threshold, natural-hole and signed puncture arguments remain.

## G112. Coalescence does not lower the independent-defect power cost

For each fixed ordinary character chi preserve all natural zeros and put
R(t,y)=sum_(n<=t,P^-(n)>y)mu(n)chi(n), with P^-(1)=infinity.
Its least-prime recurrence is R=1-sum_(y<p<=t)chi(p)R(t/p,p).
For a floor-invariant approximation F let Delta be its full recurrence
defect. G92 gives the exact root identity

    F(N,1)-M_chi(N)=Delta(N,1)+sum_(p,m) C_(N,chi)(m,p)Delta(m,p),
    C_(N,chi)(m,p)=-chi(p)
      sum_(N/[p(m+1)]<v<=N/(pm),P^+(v)<p)mu(v)chi(v).    (77.1)

All coefficients are merged by the actual integer state BEFORE absolute
values. The strict lower/inclusive upper endpoints, v=1 and strict prime
ordering matter. For the exact integer collar m<=p^r, fixed integer r>=1,
the independent bounded-defect norm is

    B_(r,chi)(N)=1+sum_(p,m>p^r)|C_(N,chi)(m,p)|.        (77.2)

The earlier real-state exponent-one lower bound did not prove anything
comparable after signed coalescence. The actual cancellation at
(N,p,m)=(20196,17,18), v=65,66 remains valid. Here a new arithmetic
argument proves, for EVERY fixed principal character chi0 modulo q,

    lim_(N->infinity) log B_(r,chi0)(N)/log N=1.        (77.3)

The external input is Tenenbaum's fixed-order friable Mobius expansion,
combining Theorems2-3 in the [original source](headroom/Erdos-Alladi.pdf).
Write omega for the Buchstab function. For fixed K>=1 and a fixed compact
I contained in(K+1,infinity), uniformly for u=log x/log y in I,

    W(x,y)=sum_(n<=x,P^+(n)<=y)mu(n)
      =x sum_(j=1)^K a_j omega^(j)(u)/(log y)^(j+1)
        +O_(I,K)(x/(log y)^(K+2)),
    sum_(j>=1)a_j z^j=1/[(1+z)zeta(1+z)], a1=1.        (77.4)

The primary images confirm the sign, derivative index and logarithm power.
The source domain exp((log x)^(2/3+epsilon))<=y<=x holds for a fixed
epsilon in(0,1/3) and large y at each fixed compact u-range. That compact
is away from the first K+1 exceptional integers. Its extra error
Psi(x,y)/L_epsilon(y) is smaller than every needed fixed logarithmic
order. No uniform growing K or u estimate is imported. The published
theorem and ordinary PNT are mathematical premises, not consequences of
the local finite helper or a complete reproof of the twenty-page source.

The strict cutoff is exactly y=p-1. Its replacement by log p changes the
main expression by O(x/[p(log p)^2]), within the fixed-order remainder.
For principal q define A_q(s)=product_(ell|q)(1-ell^-s)^-1. Once p exceeds
every prime divisor of q, the complete convolution is

    W_q(x,p-)=sum_(d q-smooth) W(x/d,p-),
    sum_(j>=1)b_(j,q)z^j=A_q(1+z)/[(1+z)zeta(1+z)].    (77.5)

All powers of the primes dividing q occur. Truncating at D=(log p)^B
costs at most x D^-eta A_q(1-eta), for fixed0<eta<1. Fixed logarithmic
moments of d then justify the Taylor product on a slightly larger compact.
Thus (77.4) holds with b_(j,q) and b_(1,q)=q/phi(q). This retains the
principal character's natural zeros; it is not a nonprincipal extension.

For fixed p the intervals in(77.1), summed over m>p^r, cover exactly
(0,U_p], U_p=N/[p(p^r+1)]. Hence

    sum_(m>p^r) C_(N,chi0)(m,p)=-W_q(U_p,p-).          (77.6)

Choose a FIXED u>2 with omega'(u)!=0 and P=N^(1/(u+r+1)). Uniformly for
P<p<=2P, log U_p/log p=u+O(1/log P), and the K=1 expansion has a fixed
nonzero sign. PNT with partial summation gives

    sum_(P<p<=2P)sum_(m>p^r) C_(N,chi0)(m,p)
      ~ -(q/phi(q))omega'(u) kappa_r N P^-r/(log P)^3,
    kappa_r=(1-2^-r)/r>0.                              (77.7)

The plus one in U_p is exact; its later relative O(p^-r) replacement is
paid. Triangle inequality gives a lower bound for the actual merged norm,
with power theta(u,r)=(u+1)/(u+r+1). Expanding the merged coefficients
before the upper bound counts each squarefree q-unit d at most once,
so B<=N. There are admissible u arbitrarily large: an eventually zero
omega' would make omega constant on a tail, and
u omega'(u)=omega(u-1)-omega(u) propagates that constant backward to
(1,2), contradicting omega(u)=1/u. Taking successively larger FIXED u
in the liminf bound proves(77.3), without a growing-u asymptotic.

## G113. Actual signed profiles buy logarithms, with exact limits

An explicit attempted repair cancels the leading mean. Set
g(v)=(v-1)^3(2-v)^3 on[1,2], zero elsewhere, and h(v)=v^2 g'(v).
Then h is C1, vanishes at the two endpoints, |h|<=3/4, and

    m0=integral h(v)v^-2 dv=0,
    m1=integral h(v)v^-2 log v dv
      =-integral_1^2 g(v)/v dv=8log2-111/20<0.           (77.8)

Prescribe Delta_N(m,p)=1_(P<p<=2P)h(m/p^r), root defect zero, and all
other defects zero. Finite triangular back substitution constructs F_N
with exactly these defects; the collar is descendant-closed and receives
its exact rough-sum values, which need not be1 when r>1. No unknown
Mertens value is used in the construction. Its root value and computation
cost are not thereby bounded. The complete root error is the signed
scalar(77.1), with no discarded complementary residual.

Put L=log p, A=N/p^(r+1), u_p=log A/log p, v_m=m/p^r and
S_m=W_q(N/(pm),p-). Exact discrete summation gives

    sum_m C_m h(v_m)=-sum_m S_m[h(v_m)-h(v_(m-1))].     (77.9)

Zero extension pays both support boundaries, including the last
difference. The K=2 expansion yields the full response

    F_N(N,1)-M_chi0(N)
      ~ (q/phi(q))m1 omega''(u) kappa_r
                           N P^-r/(log P)^4,           (77.10)

for fixed u>3 with omega''(u)!=0. The second source coefficient cancels
with m0; its sign is not needed. There is a real logarithmic gain but
no uniform sublinear power over all admissible prime-band placements.

More generally take a fixed nonzero complex C1 profile compactly
supported inside(1,V), and let J be the first nonzero logarithmic moment
m_J=integral h(v)v^-2(log v)^J dv. Such a finite J exists by polynomial
density after the change of variable log v. Then for fixed u>J+2 with
omega^(J+1)(u)!=0 the full response is

    [(q/phi(q))(-1)^(J+1)m_J/J!] omega^(J+1)(u)
                       kappa_r N P^-r/(log P)^(J+3).   (77.11)

Here and above the ratio to the displayed nonzero main term tends to1.
The identity integral h'(v)v^-1(log v)^k dv=m_k-km_(k-1) shows that
only source index1 and Taylor index J survive at the first order.
Total variation, rather than the number of states, pays the uniform
source remainder. For the smooth main approximation s, writing profile
increments as exact integrals proves the quadrature bound

    |sum_m s(v_m)Delta h_m-integral s(v)h'(v)dv|
      <=p^-r sup|s'| integral|h'|=O(A/[p^r L^2]).       (77.12)

This completes the author's C1 argument without assuming h' is Lipschitz.
For each fixed derivative order, omega^(k) is nonzero arbitrarily far
out: otherwise a tail polynomial would satisfy the delay equation, whose
degrees force it to be constant, giving the preceding contradiction.

The independent review extends(77.11) to any fixed nonzero RIGHT-CONTINUOUS
complex profile of bounded variation, compactly supported inside(1,V).
With nu=dh, exact sampling assigns each increment to nu((v_(m-1),v_m]);
the bound(77.12) becomes p^-r sup|s'| |nu|(R). Stieltjes integration by
parts, with the zero extension retaining endpoint atoms, gives the same
moments. Right continuity rules out isolated values invisible to them.

For example h=(5/9)1_[5/4,7/4)-1_[7/4,9/4) has m0=0,m1<0, and the
complete one-prime response is

    -(5/9)S_ceil(5p^r/4)+(14/9)S_ceil(7p^r/4)
                                     -S_ceil(9p^r/4). (77.13)

The half-open endpoints and ceilings are mandatory. An independent exact
case(N,p,q,r)=(441,7,6,1) gives5/9 by three representations. Four earlier
zero cases remain in the receipt. These finite examples do not prove the
asymptotic; that uses(77.4),(77.12) and PNT.
