# [private research revision]: a conductor saving and the complete shared-zero detector

Accept G114 and G115 at the following written, source-relative scopes.
The [frozen author](joint-density/report.md) and
[independent review](joint-density-review/report.md) contain the complete
arguments; the [retention manifest](retention-manifest.json) binds their
original bytes and ten immutable source inputs. The author's historical
c10 and K=9/2 comparison are preserved. Current c11 remains
312864909/2500000000=.1251459636; no new endpoint follows.
F0/analytic ancestry, original positive-slot uniformity and exact external
root-LFunction definition/import/admission remain OPEN. No formalization
or public-record claim is made.

## 1. G114: primitive conductor on the actual witnessing character

Fix the original finite dictionary, translate, canonical ray quotient and
slots. Put U=Z^W, v=z/W, delta in[17/25,7/10]. The physical bin supplies
the squared price U^(delta v_I+small) for each actual slot subcollection.
Keep this upper price even if a later internal witness buffer rises.

Let one complete nonprincipal character phi have primitive conductor
Q<=U^lambda and a retained high zero. Select that finite label FIRST,
then form the internal buffered maximum for phi and its WHOLE conjugate.
Both have the same Q. An unrelated full-family maximizing label cannot
inherit the conductor bound. Partition the resulting internal bins before
the norm, and fix the cutoff from the original physical delta and lengths
before selecting row witnesses. This is the independent review's necessary
completion of the author's selection argument.

On the internal upper line a' and its reflected line, the primitive
functional equation and the original buffered logarithm estimate give

    |S_phi(U^m)|^2 << U^[delta' min(m,lambda-m)+small] H_J,
    delta'=2a'-1 >= delta-small,  H_J=(1+T)^J.

Redundant Euler holes of polynomial radical size cost only U^epsilon on
the fixed positive strip; their radical does not multiply Q in this
pointwise bound. This does not change the separate original reflected
scale contract. Fixed labels and moving factors all belong to phi;
whole conjugation preserves Q, an additional moving twist need not.

The original same-zero product lower bound, inverse upper bound, and
this plain upper bound imply

    m<=lambda/2+small, r<=t+small, r+m>=t-small,
    |M_phi(U^r)|^2 >= U^(delta r-small).

The comparison first uses delta', then weakens the inverse spike to delta.
It retains one actual character, real part and common height. No independent
witnesses or extra label measure is introduced. Principal inducing
characters keep their original separate branches.

Take lambda0=89/100, 0<=v<=1/20, and fix

    t=1+(3delta/5)(lambda0-2v), r0=t-lambda0/2,
    Ac=1-delta+lambda0 delta(1/2-3delta/5),
    Ec(W,z)=Ac W+(6delta^2/5)z.

The full rectangle has 1<t<3/2, r0>1/2 and
1-2v-r0>=33/2500. For r<1 mark an original slot subset of width just below
min(v,(1-r)/2). MI's gates r+2x<1 and 2r+8x<3 hold with the prescribed
small slack; greedy rounding loses one fine slot width, paid by epsilon.
Pay the actual complement pointwise and divide by the inverse spike:

    I(r)=1-delta r+delta[v-(1-r)/2]_+.

Both pieces decrease and I(r0)=1-delta r0. At r=1 use the original
unmarked scale supremum with an arbitrarily small adjacent-strip loss;
MI is not invoked with zero strict margin. For r>=1 the original free-row
sixth-power inverse amplification and full slot price give

    L(r)=1/6+(5/6-delta)r+delta v <= L(t).

Exact algebra yields 1-delta r0=L(t)=Ec(1,v), exhausting all lengths.
The source scale/Sobolev supremum pays separate rowwise real parts and
heights and the finite derivative profiles. MI permits the actual frozen
bounded prime masks; arbitrary-mask MP is not needed.

Define the historical K=9/2 envelope

    rho=1-10delta/[3(5-2delta)], k=rho+delta-1,
    a=2delta(5-6delta)^2/[3(5-2delta)(115-54delta)],
    b=14delta(5-6delta)/(115-54delta),
    Eold(W,z)=rho W+delta z-min(3kz,aW+bz).

Throughout the rectangle Ec(W,z)<=Eold(W,z)-W/5000. Indeed subtract
Ec+W/5000 from the second affine branch of Eold and multiply by
3(5-2delta)(115-54delta)>0. Its ten degree-(4,1) Bernstein coefficients
are positive, minimum5373459/97656250. This proves the continuum
comparison, including where the other Eold branch is larger. It does
not compare to every later strengthened envelope without another proof.

## 2. Complete raw subclass and complement

For raw rows of width W with z<=W/21, impose on an ACTUAL high character

    Q<=Z^((21/25)W).

Write w=u b^6, preserve the unit and freeze b. Set s=log_Z Nb, V=W-6s.
Use the conductor-bounded natural free core only for the witness; it has
the same positive-real zeros and primitive conductor. Retain every b-hole
on the actual slots as a fixed MI coefficient. Do not falsely assign a
V-scale modulus to the possibly larger raw radical.

When V>=20W/21, z<=V/20 and
(89/100)V-(21/25)W>=4W/525. Thus the free theorem applies with reserve.
Root counting costs Z^s, and

    s+Ec(V,z)=Ec(W,z)-(6Ac-1)s, 6Ac-1>=6869/6250>0.

When V<20W/21 the old unmarked density plus actual high-bin slot price
gives exponent rho W+delta z-(6rho-1)s, with s>W/126. Since G<=3kz,
the reserve after the requested W/5000 is

    (19/54-1/6-3k(.68))/21-1/5000
      =112003/257985000 >0.

Bounded/free fixed-inducing cores have actual raw population
O(Z^(W/6+small)); their high-bin pointwise slot bound fits that reserve.
Branches lacking that bin bound retain their original physical estimate.
Consequently the complete licensed raw subclass has weighted density
at most Z^[Eold(W,z)-W/5000+epsilon]H_J. The high rows with no such
low-conductor witnessing character retain Eold. Their union has no proved
uniform improvement. Repeated prime valuations allow conductor savings
even with empty common support, but neither construct a high zero nor
force every row into this subclass.

Use the restriction only on a positive child norm obtained after complete
signed reconstruction: retain both projectors, the missing radical, all
clipped rectangles and the original label measure counted once. Measure
Q on that complete character. Two restricted Cauchy factors average
their savings; one restricted factor earns only half its exponent gain.
No signed projector is presumed to preserve this row class. Where this
separation is unavailable, use the accepted full estimate.

All low/far-high bins, zero terms, FI populations with actual6a/9a radii,
K_phys^(5/6), shortages/no-slot complements, four independent profiles,
weighted Euler shifts including zero capacity, principal residue and
supremum feedback retain their paid bounds. The exceptional centered
M/24 reserve is unused. Fix losses/mesh before dictionary/profiles,
their finite orders before internal height powers, and raw powers before
tail orders and eventual thresholds. This result supplies no new c.

## 3. G115: complete cutoffs agree at the actual zero

For a fixed natural nonprincipal presentation phi with the original
S-omission, choose smooth V equal1 on[0,1], zero on[2,infinity), and set

    R=U^t, C_R(s)=sum_d mu(d)phi(d)V(Nd/R)(Nd)^(-s),
    A_R(n)=sum_(d|n) mu(d)V(Nd/R).

On the absolute half-plane L^S C_R has coefficient phi(n)A_R(n).
Complete multiplicativity includes natural zeros. The unit coefficient
is1 and A_R(n)=0 for1<Nn<=R; this cancellation is in the COMPLETE signed
divisor sum, not each dyadic inverse/plain piece.

Choose fixed B sufficiently large, Y=U^B, and define

    D_R(s)=sum_(Nn>R) phi(n)A_R(n)(Nn)^(-s)e^(-Nn/Y).

At a retained actual zero rho, Mellin inversion and a shift from2 to-1/4
give D_R(rho)=-1+O(U^-A) for any prescribed A. The Gamma residue is
L^S(rho)C_R(rho)=0; nonprincipality excludes an L-pole. B is chosen after
the finite strip/conductor/height/scale powers so Y^-1/4 pays them. The
unit is e^-1/Y. A smooth terminal cutoff at U^(B+1) costs every fixed
negative power after accounting for raw row/slot powers and derivatives.
The identity allows any fixed bounded t, including2 or3. It does not
invoke the old witness theorem beyond its t in[1,3/2] contract.

For finitely many cutoffs fixed before rows, use the SAME character and
zero. For nonnegative weights with total mass M,

    sum_u w_u D_j(rho_u) conjugate(D_k(rho_u))
      =M+O(U^-A M),
    sum_u w_u |sum_j c_j D_j(rho_u)|^2
      =|sum_j c_j|^2 M+O(U^-A ||c||_1^2 M).

The coefficients c_j are fixed and row independent. Normalized sums and
fixed finite products retain a constant signal; zero-sum combinations
kill it. This is a rank-one limit on actual zero rows. It supplies no
extra power in that signal and says nothing by itself about an ambient
mixed moment or whether selected dyadic witnesses agree. An ambient
signed estimate can still make simultaneous/chained combinations useful.

## 4. An exact positive norm and its fully paid diagonal

After the licensed anchor/orientation change, merge equal ideal products
WITH signs. With original slot product P and fixed slot coefficients alpha,

    D_R(s)Q_u=sum_l b_l(s)psi_u(l),
    b_l(s)=U^(-v/2) sum_(nP=l,Nn>R)
      A_R(n)nu(n)(Nn)^(-s)e^(-Nn/Y)alpha(P).

All independent slot heights, fixed phases, holes and natural zeros remain.
No arithmetic coefficient is hidden in a smooth seminorm. In particular
B3.6 forbids a further column coefficient; divisor boundedness alone does
not license UM/MI/MP or that canonical energy for b_l.

Use the review's explicit norm on I=[a,b],1/2<a<b<1,

    N_t(U)=sum_(u in R_U) w_u sum_(i,j in{0,1})
      integral_I integral_[-T-1,T+1]
        |partial_sigma^i partial_tau^j[D_R(s)Q_u]|^2 d tau d sigma.

R_U is the specified original natural/eligible nonzero row set with
Nu<=CU, fixed before the zero event; w_u is its original positive
radial/divisor weight or paid U^epsilon majorant. Required orientations
and derivative profiles have a fixed finite union cost. Tensor Sobolev
evaluation dominates each retained zero value; derivatives cost logarithms
on fixed polynomial terminal support. Thus a bound for this complete norm
implies the corresponding weighted density. The norm bound remains open.

For sigma in a fixed compact subinterval of(1/2,1), divisor counting gives

    |b_l(s)| << U^[(sigma-1/2)v+epsilon] * (Nl)^(-sigma),
    b_l=0 unless Nl>=c0 U^(t+v).

The same bound with arbitrarily small extra loss pays the finite derivative
list. Write l=c a^6, c sixth-power-free. The diagonal includes ALL pairs
ca^6,cb^6, unequal roots included, with fixed phases and zero masks.
For H>=2 the complete absolute class sum satisfies

    sum_(c sixth-free)[sum_(Nc Na^6>=H)(Nc Na^6)^(-sigma)]^2
      << H^(1-2sigma+epsilon).

For Nc>H, root convergence gives inner bound O((Nc)^-sigma), whose
squared tail is H^(1-2sigma). For Nc<=H, partial summation gives inner
bound H^(1/6-sigma)(Nc)^-1/6. Its square summed over c<=H costs
H^(1/3-2sigma)H^(2/3)=H^(1-2sigma). Enlarging sixth-free c to all ideals
only increases these bounds. Divisor losses, units and ray sectors are
paid; no squarefree density or cancellation is used.

There are O(U^(1+epsilon)) rows. The slots cancel in the exponent because
(2sigma-1)v+(1-2sigma)(t+v)=-(2sigma-1)t. Therefore the complete
within-class contribution D6_t is nonnegative and bounded by

    D6_t(U) << U^[1-(2sigma-1)t+epsilon] H_J.

For the integrated norm use the smallest sigma in I. This covers unequal
sixth roots, merged-product collisions and zero contractions. Define O6_t
as the FULL REAL signed ordered cross-class contribution, including row
kernel, masks, weights and every derivative inner product. Finite truncation
gives N_t=D6_t+O6_t, with tails already paid. Cross-class fixed-inducing
coincidences remain in O6; they are not declared oscillatory.

At t=4/3 and sigma>=(1+delta)/2, the diagonal exponent is at most7/75.
Since delta-3k=4delta^2/(5-2delta)>0, Eold(1,v)>=rho>=19/54.
The gap349/1350 leaves23/2700 after a density saving xi=1/4. Hence

    OPEN-C: O6_(4/3)(U) << U^[Eold(1,v)-xi+epsilon] H_J,
            any fixed0<xi<=1/4,

would imply that density saving with this exact norm. It is a ONE-SIDED
bound on the full signed sum, not an absolute bound on every pair. OPEN-C
is unproved. xi=1/4 here is a density saving, not the zero-free constant.

## 5. Conditional direct return, with the target row and principal pole

For z=0 enlarge the norm to ALL required natural target rows Nu<=U,
including fixed-inducing rows and the actual target unit row with w_1=1.
This is a NEW input, not the old eligible positive-slot theorem. Suppose
for every needed fixed target/rectangle, every epsilon and all large U,

    OPEN-H: O6_t(U)<=C_(epsilon,T) U^(-nu+epsilon), nu>0,
    (2a-1)t>1, sigma>=a>1/2.

Choose epsilon below both strict gaps. The complete positive norm tends
to zero; its unit-row detector value therefore tends to zero. At a
hypothetical nonprincipal zero its value tends to-1, a contradiction.
Constants/thresholds may depend on each fixed target and height rectangle.
Every required rectangle must be covered for the all-height conclusion.
There is no attained family supremum or growing-conductor constant.

For a first improvement c>c11 with c<1/4, t=2 gives exponent4c-1<0.
For c=1/6,t=2 it is-1/3; for c=1/4,t=3 it is-1/2. These are conditional
returns from OPEN-H, which remains unproved. They replace the detector
upstream rather than extrapolate the old physical geometry.

For a principal target the norm must include the principal unit row.
Insert(s+z-1) in the Mellin integral, cancelling the simple L-pole before
the contour shift. Gamma(z+1)=z Gamma(z) gives the exact tail kernel

    D_R^P(s)=sum_(Nn>R) phi(n)A_R(n)(Nn)^(-s)
                [s-1+Nn/Y]e^(-Nn/Y).

At a nontrivial zero rho its value is1-rho+O(U^-A), nonzero for fixed
rho!=1. The added kernel and derivatives obey the same bounds with
polynomial height costs. OPEN-H for this modified detector gives the
same contradiction while allowing the pole at1. For a nonprincipal
target at1 use the unmodified detector, whose signal is-1. Ordinary
right-boundary treatment and the original Hecke-to-ordinary Euler lift
remain their accepted source statements; deleted Euler factors have no
zeros in Re s>0. External definition/admission obligations are unchanged.

## 6. Evidence and next mathematical work

The independent helper uses rational value-to-Bernstein interpolation,
separate from the author's polynomial arithmetic:35 positive coefficients
on7complete boxes,3identities,7scalar reserves/exponents,12examples and
168natural-zero/sextic cases. The author also retains finite initial
Mobius-cancellation checks. These certify algebra only. Root fully read
both mathematical reports/helpers and the original witness/MI/energy
contracts. No unchanged helper was rerun, and no formal tool was used.

The remaining questions are concrete: improve the near-full-conductor
complement, or bound the actual signed O6 after complete coefficient
merging. Fixed-inducing correlations and full norm costs are essential.
Parallel transfer, simultaneous tests and alternation remain compatible;
their gain must come from a proved estimate in the receiving expression,
with every transfer/complement paid. Constant shared-zero signals alone
do not produce it. Preserve the full29-family/109-child portfolio, nearer
targets,1/6 and1/4, and all prior source/author credit.

## 1. G116: a complete paid complement for integer renewal

Fix an ordinary Dirichlet character chi modulo q, retaining natural zeros.
Let P^-(1)=infinity and P^+(1)=1. The inherited G92 source is

    R(m,p)=sum_(n<=m,P^-(n)>p)mu(n)chi(n)
          =1-sum_(p<ell<=m,ell prime)chi(ell)R(floor(m/ell),ell).

For a floor-invariant approximation F define its ACTUAL defect

    Delta(m,p)=F(m,p)-1
        +sum_(p<ell<=m)chi(ell)F(floor(m/ell),ell).

Assume F=R on the exact collar m<=p^r, fixed integer r>=1. The collar is
descendant-closed, so Delta=0 there; for r>1 its value is generally not1.
Finite triangular inversion, with floors composed before grouping, gives

    F(N,1)-M_chi(N)=Delta(N,1)+sum_(p,m>p^r)C_N(m,p)Delta(m,p),
    C_N(m,p)=-chi(p)
      sum_(N/[p(m+1)]<u<=N/(pm),P^+(u)<p)mu(u)chi(u).

Signs, nonunit zeros, root term and half-open endpoints are literal. This
identity and the N=20196 cancellation are inherited G92, not new credit.

If distinct integers u<v lie in the same interval, then
mv<=N/p<(m+1)u, whence m(v-u)<u and u>m. Thus a fiber containing a
cofactor u<=m is a SINGLETON, even before smoothness/squarefree/zero masks.
No fiber mixes short and long cofactors.

For each active short path d=pu, m=floor(N/d)>p^r and u<=m give
pu^2<=N and p^(r+1)u<N. Dropping restrictions only in the positive count,

    S_r(N)<=sum_(j>=2)min(sqrt(N/j),N/j^(r+1))
          <=(4+1/r)N^alpha_r, alpha_r=(r+1)/(2r+1).

Split at J=ceil(N^(1/(2r+1))). The initial part is at most2sqrt(NJ)
and the tail at most N/(rJ^r); the stated constant covers N>=1. On q-units
the singleton coefficient has absolute value1. If D_N bounds EVERY active
prime-state defect, the full short contribution costs at most D_N S_r(N).
This is an all-depth price, not a fixed-depth truncation.

Freeze Y_N=(log(2N))^A at the ROOT, A>1. Remove the short fibers first;
the remaining p<=Y_N paths are squarefree Y_N-smooth integers d<=N.
For0<sigma<1 their total absolute coefficient mass is at most

    Psi_sf(N,Y)<=N^sigma product_(p<=Y)(1+p^-sigma)
        <=N^sigma exp(1+Y^(1-sigma)/(1-sigma)).

Choose sigma just above1-1/A. Then A(1-sigma)<1, giving for every epsilon
Psi_sf(N,Y_N)<<N^(1-1/A+epsilon). The onset may be large; this is not a
small finite-N constant. The finite bound remains available.

All remaining fibers satisfy

    Y_N<p<N^(1/(2r+1)), p^r<m<sqrt(N/p), u>m,
    P^+(u)<p, omega(u)>=r+1.

Indeed N>=pum>pm^2>p^(2r+1), and a squarefree u with at most r primes
below p would be<p^r. In particular all larger primes have already been
paid. Let H_F be the ENTIRE signed C_N Delta sum over this hard region.
The exact disjoint partition is

    F(N,1)-M_chi(N)=Delta(N,1)+E_short+E_small+H_F,
    |E_short|+|E_small|
      <=D_N[(4+1/r)N^alpha_r+Psi_sf(N,Y_N)].

There is no absolute value inside H_F and no independence of defects.
The independent review supplies the useful weaker conditional contract:
for fixed d>=0, common gamma<1, every fixed chi/every epsilon/all large N,

    D_N<<N^(d+epsilon),
    d+max(alpha_r,1-1/A)<gamma,
    |F(N,1)|+|Delta(N,1)|+|H_F(N)|<<N^(gamma+epsilon).

Splitting epsilon among products proves M_chi(x)<<x^(gamma+epsilon) for
all large real x. Root-dependent F is allowed, provided each root uses
one F and its actual defects on the entire reachable system. No consistency
between different roots is required. No such F and hard-region estimate
has been constructed. F=R leaves the unknown Mertens sum at the root;
the terminal-only approximation does not have a free bounded defect.

For r=1,A=3, the paid exponent is2/3. At the CURRENT boundary a first gain
can allow

    d < theta11-2/3 =1561405273/7500000000,
    d+2/3 < gamma < theta11=.8748540364.

Using A=3 instead of A=7 makes a smaller paid small-prime sector and a
larger hard remainder; it is not a gain for an unchanged H_F. At gamma=5/6
with r=1,A=5 one may take d<1/30; at gamma=3/4 with r=1,A=3, d<1/12.
These conditional1/6 and1/4 returns do not establish their premises.

The zero-exclusion bridge is complete: s integral_1^infinity
M_chi(x)x^(-s-1)dx is holomorphic on Re s>gamma, including all compact-set
derivatives after choosing epsilon with room. It equals1/L(s,chi) on
Re s>1; continuation of L times this function=1 excludes every zero in
the half-plane. A principal pole at1 becomes a reciprocal zero, not an
excluded L-zero. Natural imprimitive factors and all heights remain.
Constants may depend on each fixed ordinary chi; no Hecke extension follows.

G112's principal full merged norm exponent1 is compatible with this result:
G116 pays restricted sectors, leaving the whole signed hard-region
correlation. It neither disproves the principal norm result nor obtains a
natural-residual lower bound from it.

## 2. G117: two precisely scoped certificate obstructions

For squarefree q-units n<=N, put a_n=mu(n)chi(n). All k! orderings of its
k prime factors have the SAME arithmetic sign/phase. The map summing a
word fiber to n has norm sqrt(k!), while its minimum-norm right inverse
averages with1/k!. Its generic Cauchy price is

    sqrt(sum_n1/omega(n)!) sqrt(sum_n omega(n)!) >= #S.

More generally, for orthogonal integer fibers H_n with
<u_n,v_n>=1 (linear first slot), U=sum a_nu_n and V=sum v_n have
<U,V>=M_chi(N), but ||U||||V||>=sum||u_n||||v_n||>=#S.
The square-divisor identity gives

    #S=kappa_q N+O_q(sqrt N),
    kappa_q=(phi(q)/q) product_(p not dividing q)(1-p^-2)>0.

This is a floor on a PRODUCT-OF-NORMS certificate, not on M_chi. Arbitrary
geometry within fibers and exact diagonal rescaling cannot remove it;
correlations between different integers or a source-specific scalar estimate
remain outside the obstruction. Ordered-word/readout ancestry is retained.

For B_gamma, all f=0 below1 with norm sup_x x^-gamma|f(x)|, the dilation
T_c f(x)=sum_(n<=x)c(n)f(x/n) has extended norm
sum_n|c(n)|n^-gamma. Triangle gives the upper bound and alignment on
distinct x/n attains each finite prefix. This also holds on the all-scale
FLOOR-INVARIANT space: for fixed K take X>K(K+1), so each floor(X/n),n<=K,
is a singleton fiber among ALL n'<=X. Assign its aligning value and let
X tend to infinity. This does not identify one finite-X merged norm with
an unmerged price.

For any fixed finitely supported complex b, set r=delta-b*chi. If b(1)=0,
r(1)=1 implies ||T_r||>=1. Otherwise r(p)=-b(1)chi(p) for every
unramified prime beyond its support, and sum_p p^-gamma diverges for
0<gamma<=1. Divergence follows from the elementary Euler-product/harmonic
sum argument at gamma=1; finitely many ramified omissions do not matter.
Thus this full norm cannot certify a strict contraction.

Were ||T_r||<1 possible, the return would be legitimate:
T_chi M=1 gives M=T_b1+T_rM. The Banach solution is identified with actual
M by induction on integer intervals, since b(1)!=0 and all other x/n<x;
one need not assume M initially belongs to B_gamma. The premise fails,
not that identification. Infinite/moving preconditioners with fully paid
tails, arithmetic invariant spaces and signed norms remain eligible.

## 3. G118: finite-prefix and all-layer audits

The protected audit25 names an exact finite relaxation. Fix principal
chi0 mod q, K, and w_q(n)=mu(n)^2 1_((n,q)=1). Impose the true first K
inverse coefficients, all squareful/ramified zeros, real |b(n)|<=1, and
a fixed consistent old summatory envelope Cx^beta. For
1/2<gamma<sigma<beta<1 choose T>=K with |M_chi0(K)|<=CT^beta/2,
nonzero real t, and0<lambda<=min(1,(C sigma/2)T^(beta-sigma)). Set

    b(n)=mu(n)chi0(n) for n<=K; b(n)=0 for K<n<=T;
    b(n)=lambda w_q(n)n^(sigma-1)cos(t log n) for n>T.

Every finite convolution equation up to K and every stated zero mask
holds. For x>=T, the absolute tail is at most(lambda/sigma)x^sigma,
so the fixed Cx^beta envelope survives; the known prefix and middle
interval do also. T and |t| can be arbitrarily large.

Yet D_q(z)=sum_n w_q(n)n^-z has continuation

    D_q(z)=kappa_q z/(z-1)
       +z integral_1^infinity[sum_(n<=x)w_q(n)-kappa_q x]x^(-z-1)dx

on Re z>1/2. The error is holomorphic and the pole at1 has residue kappa_q.
The constructed series B(s) is a finite entire correction plus
(lambda/2)[D_q(s+1-sigma-it)+D_q(s+1-sigma+it)]. It has genuine poles
sigma+it and sigma-it, each residue lambda kappa_q/2. These are synthetic
completion poles, NOT L-zeros. The sequence violates global convolution
and multiplicativity: at a prime beyond T the convolution residual is
1+b(p)!=0. The result rejects only sufficiency of the stated finite
relaxation; full arithmetic or proved all-height tail constraints may repair it.

The uniform audit09 retains every squarefree layer and p-free cofactor.
Let B_k(X)=sum_(n<=X,omega(n)=k)mu(n)chi(n). Inserting one prime gives

    k B_k(X)=-sum_(p<=X)chi(p) B_(k-1)^(p)(X/p).

Each k-factor squarefree n has exactly k parents. Summing all layers yields

    M_chi(X)=1-sum_(p<=X)chi(p)
       sum_(m<=X/p,p not dividing m)mu(m)chi(m)/(omega(m)+1)
      =1-sum_(p<=X)chi(p) integral_0^1 G_(p,X)(t)dt,
    G_(p,X)(t)=sum_(m<=X/p,p not dividing m)mu(m)chi(m)t^omega(m).

All degrees, product caps, endpoints and natural zeros remain. The COMPLETE
coefficientwise absolute edge price is exactly the number of squarefree
q-units2<=n<=X: each n has k edges of weight1/k. It is
kappa_q X+O_q(sqrt X)-1, not a bound below for the signed flux. Factorial
layer rescaling requires the inverse factorial readout and does not remove
that price. Signed correlations between cofactor responses remain open.

For any proposed Gtilde define Atilde by replacing G in that root formula
and E by the FULL signed difference. Then M=Atilde+E exactly. Bounding
BOTH complete contractions by X^(gamma+epsilon), with the usual every-
character/every-epsilon/all-large-X quantifiers, gives the same Mellin return.
Root-dependent approximations must return to this fixed source before
continuation. Selected primes, central degrees or separate variances do not
pay the full error.

The separate logarithmic identity also retains every prime power:

    M_chi(X)log X=integral_1^X M_chi(t)dt/t
       -sum_(p^j<=X,j>=1)chi(p)^j log p M_chi(X/p^j).

It follows coefficientwise from the full log-derivative convolution.
Prime powers restore squareful cancellations; deleting them would not be
the p-free insertion identity above. Neither identity supplies a contraction.

## G119. Anchored one-sided pressure has an exact zero-exclusion return

Fix an ordinary character chi modulo q with its natural ramified zeros.
Let delta be1 for principal chi and0 otherwise. For Re s>0 define

    J_y(s)=integral_2^y u^(-s)/log(u) du,
    H_y(s)=delta J_y(s)+sum_(p<=y)log(1-chi(p)p^(-s)),
    Q_y(s)=exp(H_y(s)).

Each logarithm means its fixed local power series, including every prime
power. No unknown prime sum is subtracted in J_y. On Re s>1 the complete
Euler expansion gives Q_y -> exp(delta J_infinity)/L(s,chi). The function

    B(s)=(s-1)exp(J_infinity(s))

extends to an entire nonvanishing function because
B'/B=(1-2^(1-s))/(s-1) is entire, including its removable value log2.
Fix the multiplicative constant at one real point>1. The optional series
in the source agrees with [NIST 6.6.2](https://dlmf.nist.gov/6.6.E2);
the derivative proof suffices without that formula. The identity to extend is

    (s-1)^delta L(s,chi) Q(s)=B(s)^delta.                 (80.1)

For principal chi the first factor at s=1 is product_(p|q)(1-1/p),
nonzero. Finite imprimitive Euler factors have zeros only at Re s=0.
Thus a holomorphic limit Q satisfying (80.1) excludes all L-zeros in its
domain, while treating the principal pole explicitly.

For0<a<1, suppose for every compact K in Re s>a and every epsilon>0,
eventually for every integer k,

    integral_K (Re H_(2^k)(s))_+ dA <= C_(K,chi,epsilon) 2^(k epsilon).
                                                               (LP_a)

This is an area estimate on the complete dyadic sequence. A countable
rectangle exhaustion suffices. The subharmonic area mean inequality
gives local upper bounds on Re H. At one real b>1, the actual logarithms
are uniformly bounded as complex numbers. Borel-Caratheodory in the safe form

    sup_(D(c,R/2))|h| <=3|h(c)|+2 max(0,sup_(D(c,R))Re h)

propagates this anchor through a fixed finite disk chain. Hence H_(2^k)
is locally O(2^(k epsilon)) for every epsilon. Its increments f_k are
O_b(2^(-k(b-1))) on Re s>=b>1 by the integer tail majorant.

Choose overlapping inner/middle/outer disks with radii r,2r,4r inside
Re s>a. Three-circle interpolation propagates a decay exponent d_j by
d_(j+1)=(d_j-epsilon)/2. For N fixed steps, epsilon<d_0/2^(N+1)
makes every resulting exponent positive. Centers at distance<=r let
the previous middle disk cover the next inner disk. Finite covers handle
any compact. Therefore sum_k f_k converges locally uniformly, H_(2^k)
has a holomorphic limit H and Q=exp(H) is nonzero. The identity theorem
extends (80.1). This is an all-height return: every alleged finite-height
zero lies in a suitable compact. Constants may depend on chi and K.

For this exact anchored sequence, LP_a is EQUIVALENT to local uniform
convergence of H_(2^k): the reverse follows from local boundedness. For
a>1/2 the higher-prime-power logarithm converges absolutely, so LP_a is
also equivalent to local convergence of the centered DYADIC prime sum
sum_(p<=2^k)chi(p)p^(-s)-delta J_(2^k)(s). This is not an equivalence
with bare zero exclusion or a claim about every intermediate cutoff.
It refines the one-sided sufficient input without providing cancellation.

A separate global-height hypothesis gives a numerical loss budget. Suppose
a>0,kappa>=0,a+kappa<1, and for every epsilon>0 there are fixed A,C with

    |H_y(a+it)| <= C(1+|t|)^A y^(kappa+epsilon)

for every dyadic y and real t. Apply three-lines to f_k(s)/(s+D)^m,
D>1,m>A, on a<=Re s<=b with b>1. Each finite source is bounded in height;
the denominator pays the horizontal boundary. The resulting exponent is

    E=[(kappa+epsilon)(b-sigma)+(1-b)(sigma-a)]/(b-a).

At epsilon=0 its zero is
r_b=a+kappa+kappa(1-a-kappa)/(kappa+b-1). For each compact to the right
of a+kappa choose finite b large enough, then epsilon small enough.
Geometric convergence and (80.1) return Re s>a+kappa. For kappa=0 the
same argument uses a positive epsilon buffer. A_y growing with cutoff,
or an estimate on finitely many heights, does not meet this contract.

At a=3/4 the current first-gain threshold is
kappa<312135091/2500000000=.1248540364. The conditional choice
kappa=78/625 returns c=.1252, gain135091/2500000000 over c11.
Choices (a,kappa)=(3/4,1/12) and (2/3,1/12) return1/6 and1/4.
All these inputs remain open. The actual direct bound is y^(1-a),
giving a+kappa=1. Synthetic h_k=sum_(j<=k)2^(j(a+kappa-s))/j shows
the strict abstract boundary cannot improve for free: its exponential
limit has a pole at a+kappa. This model is not an arithmetic L-source.

## G120. Complete phase blocks and thermal readout prices

For NONPRINCIPAL chi, partition every unramified prime into disjoint
finite blocks B and an unmatched set U. Suppose fixed m,C satisfy
|B|<=m, r_B=min B, diameter B<=C r_B^(1-eta), exact sum_B chi(p)=0,
eta>0, and U(x)<=C x^delta_U. Every exception belongs to U. For
sigma0>gamma_B=max(1/2,1-eta,delta_U),

    |sum_B chi(p)p^(-s)| <=m C |s| r_B^(-sigma0-eta).

This follows from the derivative of u^(-s) and exact phase balance.
Distinct blocks have distinct integer anchors. Their singleton sum,
all higher powers and the full unmatched logarithm converge normally.
Exponentiation and initial Euler agreement return zero exclusion
Re s>gamma_B. The omitted anchor-Y tails are respectively
O_K(Y^(1-sigma0-eta)), O_K(Y^(1-2sigma0)), O_K(Y^(delta_U-sigma0)).
No selected or unpaired prime is omitted.

For0<eta<=1 an incomplete block crossing x has anchor in
(x-Cx^(1-eta),x]. Counting these anchors gives the actual natural-cutoff
prime discrepancy O_chi(x^(1-eta)+x^delta_U+1). The difference between
anchor and natural Euler cutoffs is O_K(Y^(1-eta-sigma0)+Y^(-sigma0)).
Thus this is a structural sufficient condition for the classical prime
discrepancy route, not a separate obtained saving. Principal unramified
phases are all1, so no nonempty balanced block exists; the entire prime
set as unmatched has exponent1. A separate principal input is mandatory.
Current first gain requires eta>c11 and delta_U<theta11, with common
exponents across the covered characters. Approximate balance incurs an
additional complete block-residual sum. Its price is not zero.

The protected23 audit constructs the precise finite thermal object. On
two-state unramified sites let N_p=diag(0,1), K_y=sum_p(log p)N_p,
Z_y^+(sigma)=product_p(1+p^(-sigma)), rho_y=exp(-sigma K_y)/Z_y^+,
and U_(chi,t)=tensor_p diag(1,-chi(p)p^(-it)). Then

    P_y(s)=Z_y^+(sigma) Tr(rho_y U_(chi,t)),
    Q_y(s)=exp(delta J_y(s))Z_y^+(sigma) Tr(rho_y U_(chi,t)).

rho_y is positive with trace1, U is unitary and distinct-site correlations
factor exactly. Trace cyclicity proves the finite Gibbs/KMS identity.
These facts do not control the extensive parity readout. Positivity only
bounds its magnitude by1 and leaves the full Z_y^+ and principal vacuum.
The exact LP integrand is the positive part of
delta Re J_y+log Z_y^++log|Tr(rho_y U)|. A useful mixing theorem must
bound that complete expression. Analyticity comes from the exact source,
not a separate claim that rho_y depends holomorphically on s.

For the normalized signed functional on the finite supremum-norm algebra,

    ell_y(F)=P_y(s)^(-1) sum_(n|product P)mu(n)chi(n)n^(-s)F(n),
    ||ell_y||=Z_y^+(sigma)/|P_y(s)|.

At principal real0<sigma<=1, log||ell_y||>=2 sum_(p<=y,p not|q)p^(-sigma)
tends to infinity. The occupied one-site expectation is negative.
Compatible ell_y therefore cannot extend boundedly to the supremum-norm
completion of the infinite cylinder algebra. A scalar vacuum multiplier
does not change this normalized functional. This is a specified norm
obstruction; different norms, full parity estimates and signed arithmetic
projections remain eligible. It neither lower-bounds M_chi nor refutes LP.
title: G120. Complete phase blocks and thermal readout prices

## G121. Exact threshold rank and the complete signed rectangle return

At integer N partition ALL unramified primes<=N into disjoint L,R.
List squarefree L-products u_i<=N and R-products v_j<=N increasingly,
including1. Put T_ij=1_(u_i v_j<=N), alpha_i=mu(u_i)chi(u_i) and
beta_j=mu(v_j)chi(v_j). Unique factorization gives

    M_chi(N)=alpha^T T beta.                              (80.2)

Ramified sites are zero rows/columns, not inverted factors. All retained
phases have modulus1; diagonal multiplication preserves matrix rank and
singular values while the final scalar may still cancel.

Let t_i be the row's prefix length, and0<h_1<...<h_d its distinct positive
values, h_0=0. The exact decomposition is

    T=sum_(ell=1)^d 1_(t_i>=h_ell) 1_(h_(ell-1)<j<=h_ell).

Choosing one row of each length h_i and columns h_j gives the triangular
submatrix L_d=(1_(j<=i)), determinant1. Thus rank T=d. Each length is
a function of floor(N/u_i), giving d<=2 floor(sqrt N). This is an
O(sqrt N) representation, not a polylogarithmic rank or cancellation bound.

L_d^(-1)=I minus a truncated shift has operator norm<=2. Restrict any
rank-r approximation T_r, r<d, to this submatrix and use an orthonormal
basis of its kernel, dimension at least d-r. Every vector has error norm
at least1/2. Hence ||T-T_r||_F^2>=(d-r)/4 and ||T-T_r||_op>=1/2.
Restriction is a contraction for either norm; the same result holds for
the character-weighted tensor. No rank-growth assumption is needed.

If R_N,C_N are the row and column counts, the COMPLETE scalar error is
alpha^T(T-T_r)beta, bounded above by sqrt(R_N C_N)||T-T_r||_op, or
the same factor times the Frobenius norm. Leakage outside uv<=N is part
of this error. The matrix lower bounds are not lower bounds on its signed
scalar contraction. A norm budget tending to zero forces r>=d; no claim
that every prime partition has such a budget or large rank is made.

Contracting the exact decomposition gives

    M_chi(N)=sum_ell [sum_(i:t_i>=h_ell)alpha_i]
                       [sum_(h_(ell-1)<j<=h_ell)beta_j].

Every prime restriction and endpoint is explicit. A selection of rectangles
must bound both its full signed contribution and the entire omitted signed
sum by N^(gamma+epsilon), for all large N/every epsilon/every fixed chi
and common gamma<theta11. Moving partitions need uniform bounds in their
actual choice. Then s integral_1^infinity M_chi(x)x^(-s-1)dx continues
1/L to Re s>gamma, giving ordinary all-height zero exclusion. This uses
the full source, not analytic continuation of the moving tensors.

# [private research revision]: complete low-core and relative-conductor reduction

Accept G122–G124 below, from the frozen [author](completed-crossclass/report.md)
and [independent review](completed-crossclass-review/report.md). They reduce
the arithmetic input still needed for the completed detector. They do not
prove that input or raise the accepted written
c11=312864909/2500000000=.1251459636. The source-relative F0/analytic ancestry,
original positive-slot uniformity and exact external L-function
definition/import/admission obligations remain OPEN.

The balanced-residue and masked-Poisson mechanisms come from the expert
[merged note, Section2.5](../external/gpt6-pro-20261011/QRH_merged_research_and_extensions.md),
RM-A/RM10. The new work extends them to the actual completed merged
coefficients with all original slots, proves a stronger radical-support
projection, and pays complete sectors against the current density envelope.
This is source-specific progress, without a literature-priority claim.

## Exact source and norm

Fix the original finite natural dictionary, excluded primes S, complete
orientation and admissible slot system. For ideal columns and element rows,
write phi_u(n)=nu(n)psi_u(n), psi_u(n)=chi_n(u)^(+/-1), including all natural
zeros. A fixed nu of order other than six stays in the coefficient. Whole
conjugation acts on every factor. All six units remain in the row family.

For the original row-independent prime pools and profiles,

    Q_u=U^(-v/2) sum_P alpha(P)psi_u(P), 0<=v<=1/20,

with NP comparable to U^v. The no-slot term is P=1,v=0. Common primes
between n and P remain allowed with their zero extensions. No arbitrary
coefficient version of UM/MI/MP is asserted.

Let R=U^t,Y=U^B, and use the actual V, equal to1 on[0,1] and0 on[2,infinity).
Set

    A_R(n)=sum_(d|n) mu(d)V(Nd/R),
    D_R,u(s)=sum_(Nn>R) phi_u(n)A_R(n)(Nn)^(-s)e^(-Nn/Y).

The [accepted completion](../[private research revision]/joint-density-integration.md) gives
D_R,u(rho)=-1+O(U^(-A)) at a zero of the same natural nonprincipal character.
The primitive inducing character must be nonprincipal; adding Euler holes
to a principal character does not suffice. The identity is a value
identity, not a claim that derivatives vanish at a zero.

First pay the genuine exponential tail Nn>U^(B+1), with all needed fixed
derivatives and cross terms. A crude polynomial bound on the retained
expression and arbitrarily small absolute tail error suffice. Fix raw
row/slot/height powers before the tail order, B and final threshold. Pair
classification then concerns a finite polynomially supported expression;
it never assigns a uniform subpower loss to unbounded conductors.

Merge equal nP=l with signs:

    F_u=D_R,u Q_u=sum_l b_l(s)psi_u(l),
    b_l=U^(-v/2) sum_(nP=l,Nn>R)
        A_R(n)nu(n)(Nn)^(-s)e^(-Nn/Y)alpha(P).

The finite terminal cutoff is understood. For each required derivative,
on a fixed compact real interval sigma>1/2,

    |partial b_l| << H_J U^((sigma-1/2)v+epsilon)(Nl)^(-sigma),
    b_l!=0 implies Nl>=L0=c0 U^(t+v).                 (1)

H_J contains fixed seminorms and a fixed height polynomial, not a live
arithmetic coefficient. Divisor multiplicities, logarithms and fixed
derivatives are absorbed into the requested loss before the threshold.

Choose a smooth positive radial Phi>=1 on the required row ball BEFORE
expansion. Use every nonzero sixth-power-free row, with the original
fixed-dictionary exclusions (or retain that finite set). PR15 proves those
exclusions finite from fixed prime support and valuations at most5.
For a fixed positive-width interval I whose lower edge is at least
(1+delta)/2-h0, 0<=h0<=10^(-5), put

    N(F)=sum_(u free,eligible) Phi(Nu/U)
        sum_(i,j in {0,1}) integral_I integral_[-T-1,T+1]
        |partial_sigma^i partial_tau^j F_u|^2 d tau d sigma.       (2)

Finite extra derivatives and orientations mean their finite sum. An
original positive row weight bounded by U^epsilon and its selected subset
are dominated on the FULL norm before expansion. This does not dominate
individual signed sectors or license amplitude-selected Poisson kernels.

## G122. Radical support and all low/high crosses

If n!=1 and N(rad n)<=R, every squarefree divisor lies inside the plateau
of V. Thus exactly, including the endpoint,

    A_R(n)=sum_(d|rad n) mu(d)=0.                     (3)

Consequently b_l!=0 implies N(rad l)>R. Write l=c a^6 with c sixth-free.
Since rad l divides ca, Nc Na>R. This is stronger than the support
inequality Na>(R/Nc)^(1/6). It requires the merged convolution, not a
separated divisor dyad.

Project the actual merged columns onto Nc<=C0=U^lambda<R. For each row
and every required derivative, (1) gives

    |partial F_lo,u|
      << H_J U^((sigma-1/2)v+epsilon)
         sum_(Nc<=C0) (Nc)^(-sigma)
         sum_(Na>R/Nc) (Na)^(-6sigma)
      << H_J U^((sigma-1/2)v+epsilon) R^(1-6sigma) C0^(5sigma).

The source's linear ideal count proves the inner convergent tail by

shared slot primes and exceptional rows are included. Therefore

                                      +(2sigma-1)v+epsilon].    (4)

-4+2v<0. Its nominal lower-edge value is

A downward real buffer raises it by at most4h0. Every low/high cross term
is paid by the Hilbert triangle inequality

    sqrt(N(F))<=sqrt(N(F_hi))+sqrt(N(F_lo)).            (5)

Squaring costs only a fixed factor2. No slot-amplitude lower bound,
division by Q_u, or favorable sign of a cross term is used.

## G123. Complete relative mass and full-hole Poisson

For the actual valuation differences modulo6 of l,l', let q1,q2,q3 be
the radicals with residues {1,5},{2,4},{3}. Define

The complete residue vector e specifies the relative phase. Good-prime
nonzero residues have conductor that prime; fixed ray factors cannot
cancel a conductor outside S. The zero vector is the entire same
sixth-power class, including unequal roots.

For one choice of actual difference signs write

using the actual gcd g. Multiples of6, including differences with zero
residue, enter x,y. There are at most2^omega(q1q2q3) sign choices; no
coprimality between g and ab is imposed. Allowing all x,y only overcounts.
Put A=Na(Nx)^6,B'=Nb(Ny)^6. The lower supports imply
Ng>=M=max(1,L0/A,L0/B'). Since 1-2sigma<0,

    (AB')^(-sigma) sum_(Ng>=M)(Ng)^(-2sigma)
      << L0^(1-2sigma)(AB')^(-1/2)
       = L0^(1-2sigma)(Nab)^(-1/2)(Nx)^(-3)(Ny)^(-3).

factor U^((2sigma-1)v) in (1) cancels the v in L0 exactly, proving

individual cores only contracts the positive majorant in (6).

different primes already give order6. Those easier mixed cases are paid.

and6, and the fixed omissions. Its norm is polynomial after termination.

zero vanishes. Schwartz decay and lattice counting give
a sum_(h!=0)|F Phi(a Nh)|<<1, a=V/Q, so the primitive sum is

sum vanishes, which pays the small-V case. Fixed ray characters and finite

absorbed in (7). Retaining them is also allowed. All units are retained.

exclusion dictionaries. The optional raw-row analogue covers only a
fixed finite list of excluded sixth-power-core families; its O(U^(1/6))
deletion cost fits (7). It does not license all moving physical selectors.

      min(U(Q1/Q3)^(1/2),

the full class square, or (6) with H=1 and the trivial row bound:

## G124. Current margins and precise remaining signed input

Use the accepted [[private research revision] envelope](../[private research revision]/density-integration.md),
with K=28114053/6250000 inherited from c10 in the SAME family. Do not
bootstrap K from c11. Write

    h=5-2delta, rho=1-10delta/(3h), k=rho+delta-1,
    D_K=15K-10-6Kdelta,

the derivative of rho+4delta/3 is at least23/486>0. Their minima are at

at most7/75. Thus these are interval proofs, not sampled endpoint claims.

reserve is

reserve before the threshold. No physical projector or exceptional
centered reserve was spent. Independent rational Bernstein checks cover
the buffered interval inequalities as well.

then the ratio cut outside it. The exact remainder R_hi is the real
ordered cross-class sum with actual derivative inner products and actual
kernel, restricted to

real. Thus N(F_hi)=D_hi+P_hi+R_hi, with the entire same-class D_hi and

still UNPROVED one-sided estimate

for every required fixed family, Phi, original slot system, rectangle
and height list implies the same bound for N(F), by (5) and (9). Restore
the genuine tail with its full positive-norm error. Original absolute
bounds with an enlarged fixed height polynomial cover the outer height
range; B and the threshold are never chosen after a row or zero is seen.

row domination BEFORE expansion gives the corresponding improved
original slot-weighted high-row density. No amplitude lower bound or
division by Q_u occurs.

This conditional density implication does not complete its physical use.
Both coprimality projectors, clipped rectangles, moving phases/support,
reconstruction, raw roots/holes, shared label counts, fixed-inducing and
exceptional branches, actual6a/9a charges, K_phys^(5/6), weighted Euler
shifts including zero capacity, no-slot/shortening complements, principal
residue and common-Delta family-supremum step keep their existing
contracts. Numerical c credit requires every one of those terms.

## Surviving mechanism and direct-return boundary

The remainder contains actual coefficients: with no slots, distinct good
primes p,p'>2R have A_R(p)=A_R(p')=1, individual cores p,p',q1=pp',q2=q3=1.
At the unit row their sextic phases are1. Equal fixed nu-values produce
a positive real product at real s. This conditional named-prime/phase
example shows coherence that an estimate must handle. It is not a
uniform prime-population claim, a high zero, or a lower bound for the
whole signed norm. Other coefficients can cancel it. The generic coprime
squarefree absolute envelope costs exponent1+(1-delta)t, still much
larger than E_K; this limits that envelope, not the true signed sum.

For a direct OPEN-H target, keep the unit row with weight at least1 and
all required FI rows. With v=0 and sigma>=a, the low-core exponent is
1+2t(1-6a)+10a lambda; a relative Q<=U^w cut costs
1/6-(2a-1)t+11w/12; a ratio<=U^r cut costs1-(2a-1)t+r/2.
Those costs must be negative for that application. The density cutoffs
above do not supply OPEN-H. Near gains,1/6,1/4 remain conditional targets.

For a principal target retain the reviewed kernel
[s-1+Nn/Y]exp(-Nn/Y), its principal unit row and signal1-rho for rho!=1.
The radical cancellation and derivative/tail bounds still apply. For a
possible nonprincipal zero at1, use the unmodified signal-1. No new
external ordinary-L identification follows.

The next development attacks (10) with its actual merged A_R signs,
retaining two plain convolution variables through a legal full-modulus
Poisson/reciprocity transformation and testing unit coherence and holes.
An additional small-core payment alone cannot close this remainder.

## Evidence and acceptance

Root read both full reports and mathematical helpers, reconstructed the
analytic arguments, and inspected exact PR9 B3.5/B3.6, PR15 fixed-exception
and ideal-count source, and expert RM-A/RM10. Fourteen frozen artifacts
and seven immutable premise pins are retained in the
[manifest](retention-manifest.json). No claim snapshot is copied.

Independent checks cover six whole-interval certificates (18 Bernstein
coefficients), three identities, six scalar values,588 radical cases,
896 merged supports,4096 unequal-root representations,3920 natural-zero
cases and10 local character sums. They support the written reconstruction;
they do not prove OPEN-[restricted research revision] or a new c. No unchanged checks were rerun.
Both original owners stopped, froze and released before integration;
follow-up work uses new exclusive scopes. No formalization was performed.

# [private research revision]: curved additive source and complete signed Gauss bank

Accept G125–G127 from the frozen [author](curved-source/report.md) and
[independent review](curved-source-review/report.md). This recurring
headroom pass discovered a replacement detector, proved its quantitative
return, tried a coarse arithmetic estimate, and isolated the remaining
signed sum. No larger c is proved: c11=.1251459636 and all inherited
F0/analytic, positive-slot and external definition/import/admission
obligations remain unchanged. Scope is fixed ordinary Dirichlet characters,
including natural zeros, every finite height and the principal pole.

Five initial mechanisms were considered before selection: prime-dilation
disjointness, fugacity root deflation, weighted prime-block contraction,
rational Fourier observation, and separate additive wavelength/damping.
The selected last route extends W24's angular-contour seed with an actual
moving-source return. W21 supplied general peak-width ancestry. No
literature-priority claim or conductor-uniform theorem is made.

## G125. Exact curved return and actual coarse bound

For fixed b>1 define the literal infinite sources

    F_chi(z)=sum_(n>=1)mu(n)chi(n)exp(-nz), Re z>0,
    V_b,chi(x)=F_chi(x^(-b)+i/x).

For Re s>0 put I_n(s)=integral_0^infinity exp(-nt^b-int)t^(s-1)dt.
Substitute v=nt and rotate to arg v=-alpha, fixed0<alpha<pi/(2b).
The small arc vanishes; on the large arc exp(-n^(1-b)v^b) decays and
|exp(-iv)|<=1. On the new ray the Taylor remainder for exp(-z),Re z>=0,
is bounded by |z|^K/K!. Consequently

    I_n(s)=sum_(0<=k<K) A_k(s)n^(-s-(b-1)k)+R_n,K(s),
    A_k(s)=(-1)^k Gamma(s+bk)exp(-i*pi*(s+bk)/2)/k!,
    |R_n,K(s)|<=C_(b,K,C)n^(-Re s-(b-1)K),             (1)

uniformly on every compact C in Re s>0. The ray majorant is
exp(alpha Im s)Gamma(Re s+bK)/(K! sin(alpha)^(Re s+bK)). Thus the sum
of remainders is normally holomorphic for Re s>max(0,1-(b-1)K).
Absolute Fubini initially on Re s>b proves

    H_chi(s)=integral_0^infinity F_chi(t^b+it)t^(s-1)dt
      =sum_(k<K) A_k(s)/L(s+(b-1)k,chi)+R_chi,K(s).     (2)

Every L is the actual original ordinary character, with all Euler holes.
At b=3/2,K=1 the remainder is holomorphic for Re s>1/2, and the
multiplier Gamma(s)exp(-i*pi*s/2) has no zeros there. The sign of the
additive phase and that multiplier is fixed, not discarded.

A sufficient complete arithmetic input is, for everyepsilon>0 and every
large dyadic shell, with a common fixed gamma,

    integral_X^(2X)|V_b,chi(x)| dx/x <<_(chi,epsilon) X^(gamma+epsilon).
                                                               (OPEN-CURVE)

Constants and onset may depend on the fixed character. Shell L2 energy
bounded by X^(2gamma+epsilon) suffices by Cauchy–Schwarz. Dyadic summation
makes H holomorphic on Re s>gamma; the complementary t>=1 tail is paid by
exp(-t^b)/(1-exp(-t^b)). For b=3/2,gamma>1/2, (2) excludes every zero
there. The principal pole gives a zero of the reciprocal and is retained.
Imprimitive Euler factors were included from the start; their zeros lie
on Re s=0. No uniform bound over arbitrarily large imaginary parts is
asserted or needed: local holomorphy reaches each finite height.

For any fixed b>1,0<gamma<1 choose finite K with1-(b-1)K<gamma.
Starting from Re s>1, solve (2) successively on strips of width b-1:
all shifted reciprocals are already holomorphic on the next strip.
The same H and nonvanishing A_0 give the unshifted extension. Finitely
many steps reach Re s>gamma. Neither b nor K moves with x. No converse
equivalence to a Mertens bound has been proved.

At b=3/2, first gain needs gamma<theta11=.8748540364, or energy
exponent<1.7497080728. Conditional examples retain
gamma=.87485 (c=.12515), gamma=5/6 (c=1/6), gamma=3/4 (c=1/4).
They are open estimates, not accepted endpoints.

The pass proves the actual pointwise theorem

    V_(3/2),chi(x)<<_(chi,epsilon)x^(5/4+epsilon)        (3)

for every sufficiently large REAL x, including the whole infinite tail.
For its full proof use N=x^(3/2),T=N(log x)^2,U=V=floor(sqrt x), and
the all-integer convolution identity

    mu=mu_<=U+mu_<=V-mu_<=U*mu_<=V*1+mu_>U*mu_>V*1.

Both short sums cost O(sqrt x). Fixed-modulus additive Fourier inversion
preserves chi's zeros and reduces to beta=ell/q-1/(2*pi*x). For Y<=T,
the exact spacing estimates are

    sum_(d<=x)min(Y/d,1/(2||beta d||))<<_q x log(2x)+Y/x,
    sum_(h<=H)min(M,1/(2||beta h||))<<_q(H/x+1)(M+x log(2x)).

Split into q residue classes and blocks of length at most x. Phases in
each block move monotonically at spacing q/(2*pi*x); nearest points cost
the finite first argument, and the rest a harmonic sum. In the first
estimate a nontrivial zero crossing occurs only at d comparable to x,
so resonance costs Y/x. This includes noninteger real x and exact
resonance, not only generic phases.

The divisor-sized Type I coefficient, supported on d<=UV<=x, therefore
costs x^(1+epsilon). For Type II let b_d=sum_(c|d,c>V)mu(c).
In a box (M,2M]x(L,2L],md<=Y, Cauchy retains the COMPLETE Gram

    sum_(d,e)b_d conjugate(b_e)
       sum_(m in(M,2M],m<=Y/max(d,e))e(beta m(d-e)).

The inner set is one interval. Its diagonal and the second spacing bound
give squared cost

    T^epsilon [M^2 L+ML(L/x+1)(M+x log(2x))]
      <<T^epsilon(Y^2/U+Y^2/x+Yx)log(2x)<<x^(5/2+epsilon).

Summing the logarithmically many boxes proves the prefix bound uniformly
for Y<=T. Partial summation restores exp(-n/N), and the discarded tail
is O(N exp(-(log x)^2)), smaller than every fixed power. This proves (3).
The short terms and tail are paid for the target; BOTH Type I exponent1
and Type II exponent5/4 remain above theta11. A Type II improvement alone
would not complete a gain. Their full signed recombination is an eligible
weaker target. The pointwise saving is relative to damping length x^(3/2),
not the observation scale x.

The [Green–Tao primary source](https://aif.centre-mersenne.org/item/10.5802/aif.2401.pdf),
Lemma4.1, concerns a dyadic interval with UV<=N. Here the all-integer
identity restores both short terms and is separately derived from
mu*1=delta_1. The [BSZ theorem](https://publications.ias.edu/sites/default/files/disjointness%20b-s-z%20oct.pdf)
was discovery ancestry only; its fixed-parameter conclusion supplies no
uniform power saving under a shrinking parameter.

## G126. Exact whole-shell bank with two branches paid

For prime P not dividing q and (a,P)=1, finite multiplicative
orthogonality, including the ramified multiples n=Pm, gives on Re s>1

    sum_n mu(n)chi(n)e(an/P)n^(-s)
      =1/(P-1)sum_(psi modP)psi(a)tau(conjugate psi)/L(s,chi psi)
       -chi(P)P^(-s)/L(s,chi psi0).                    (4)

The sign psi(a) and negative correction are substantive. The latter uses
mu(Pm)=-mu(m)1_(P not dividing m), retaining all P^2 and character zeros.
Since tau(psi0)=-1, its reciprocal contains exactly
L(s,chi psi0)=(1-chi(P)P^(-s))L(s,chi). Fixed-character constants cannot
be silently summed uniformly over these growing moduli.

More usefully, freeze any unramified prime P comparable to X before
varying x over the ENTIRE shell [X,2X]. Let
w_P(x)=x^(-b)+i(1/x-2*pi/P). Absolute convergence and the same finite
orthogonality prove

    V_b,chi(x)=G_P,chi(x)+B_P,chi(x),
    G_P,chi(x)=1/(P-1)sum_(psi!=psi0)psi(-1)tau(conjugate psi)
                                      F_(chi psi)(w_P(x)),
    B_P,chi(x)=-F_(chi psi0)(w_P(x))/(P-1)
                               -chi(P)F_(chi psi0)(P w_P(x)).     (5)

The common profile and every shell point are retained, even where its
residual imaginary part vanishes. Because |F_eta(w)|<=1/Re w,

    |B_P,chi(x)|<=x^b/(P-1)+x^b/P<<X^(b-1).           (6)

Thus BOTH the principal Gauss branch and ramified branch are paid
without a growing-conductor estimate. For gamma>=b-1 the every-epsilon
whole-shell L1 target for V is equivalent to that for G; likewise for
the L2 energy via the triangle inequality of square-root norms. At b=3/2
all proposed targets exceed1/2. Choosing P separately for each shell
changes the representation, not the global Mellin source. All remaining
chi psi are nonprincipal when (P,q)=1.

The coherent bank G is still unbounded at the desired exponent. Taking
absolute values term by term can spend sqrt(P) in Gauss weights. That
is a certificate cost, not a lower bound on its true signed sum. The
complete common-profile bank is the precise new arithmetic target.

## G127. Energy, absolute price and point observation

For every bounded coefficient sequence, the same complete varying-damping
energy satisfies E_b(X)<<_b X^(b+1), without epsilon. Put
d=1/[2(2X)^b],G(z)=sum a_n exp(-dn)z^n,Delta=x^(-b)-d.
Then d<=Delta<=C_b d and the subharmonic Poisson inequality bounds
|G(exp(-Delta-i theta))|^2 by P_Delta*|G|^2,theta=1/x.
The kernels obey P_Delta<=C'_b P_d. Since dx/x<=2X|dtheta|,
enlarge the positive integral to a full period and use Parseval:

    E_b(X)<=C_b X sum_n |a_n|^2 exp(-2dn)<<X/d<<X^(b+1).

Variable damping was paid by Poisson domination, not replaced informally.
A scale-dependent diagnostic array a_n=exp(in/x0),n<=X^b,x0=3X/2,
has magnitude of order X^b on logarithmic width X^(1-b); it shows this
uniform bounded-array exponent is sharp. It is not a Möbius counterexample
or an assertion about one fixed infinite array. In particular exponent5/2
energy alone contains no arithmetic gain; the pointwise theorem (3) does.

For the ACTUAL a_n=mu(n)chi(n), square-divisor expansion gives
sum_(n<=Y)|a_n|^2=d_qY+O_q(sqrt Y), with
d_q=zeta(2)^(-1)product_(p|q)(1+1/p)^(-1)>0. In the exact energy kernel

    K_X(n,m)=integral_1^2 exp(-(n+m)/(X^b u^b))
                              exp(-i(n-m)/(Xu))du/u,

the diagonal is d_q(2^b-1)X^b/(2b)+O_q(X^(b/2)). It is not a lower
bound for total signed energy. Binning squarefree units in [X^b,2X^b]
into intervals of length X/4 produces order X^(b+1) distinct close pairs
by Cauchy. For them Re K>=exp(-4)cos(1/4)log2. Hence the ACTUAL
termwise-absolute off-diagonal price is at least a constant times
X^(b+1). One phase integration by parts also gives

    |K_X(n,m)|<=C_b exp(-c_b(n+m)/X^b)min(1,X/|n-m|),

so that price is at most O_b(X^(b+1)log(2X)). It obstructs that absolute
pricing method; aggregate signed cancellation remains eligible.

Finally |V_b'(x)|<<X^(2b-2) on an enlarged shell. A peak of height A
has width at least a constant times A/X^(2b-2). Its L2 and L1 masses
cost respectively A^3/X^(2b-1) and A^2/X^(2b-1). Thus whole-shell energy
exponent2gamma gives point exponent(2gamma+2b-1)/3; L1 exponent gamma
gives( gamma+2b-1)/2. At b=3/2 the quarter-energy target permits point
exponent7/6, not3/4. Isolated rational-frequency values therefore do not
inherit the same shell exponent and are not themselves an obstruction.

## Acceptance and next action

Root read complete author/reviewer reports and both helpers, reconstructed
all arguments, and checked primary scope and the named earlier ideas.
Ten frozen artifacts and five immutable source pins are in the
[manifest](retention-manifest.json). Exact finite checks cover the two
rational decompositions, full hyperbolic Gram, resonance and budgets.
No unchanged checks were rerun. These checks do not prove OPEN-CURVE.

Next seek a bound for the complete signed Type I/II combination, coherent
nonprincipal bank, or original shell L1 norm, below theta11. Preserve
the exact damping, every branch, natural zeros and all shell points.
The accepted pointwise gap is5/4-theta11=.3751459636; the generic energy
gap is5/2-2theta11=.7502919272. Neither is an available proof reserve.
Near gains,1/6 and1/4 remain explicit conditional targets. The next
recurring pass may replace this architecture; it must discover and develop
a promising mechanism before testing its weakest complete estimate.

statement:
## G128. Source, prediction and an exact zero census

Fix an ordinary Dirichlet character chi modulo q with natural zero
extension. Write delta=1 for the principal character and0 otherwise,
r=delta*phi(q)/q, A(x)=sum_(n<=x)chi(n), b(t)=A(exp t)-r exp t.
Periodicity gives |b|<=q. Abel summation initially for Re s>1 gives

    H(s)=integral_0^infinity exp(-st)b(t)dt
        =L(s,chi)/s-r/(s-1).

The integral continues H to Re s>0. Use the literal normalized source

    F_chi(s)=((s-1)/(s+1))^delta L(s,chi)/s.       (1)

At the principal pole its removable value is r/2, nonzero. Nonprincipal
characters receive no spurious factor s-1. All natural L-zeros in Re>0
and their multiplicities survive. No Hecke or growing-conductor transfer
is asserted. The causal inverse Laplace source is

    f(t)=b(t)                                       nonprincipal,
    f(t)=r exp(-t)+b(t)-2 integral_0^t exp(-(t-u))b(u)du
                                                   principal. (2)

Thus |f|<=C_q=1+3q. For principal chi, direct substitution gives

    f(log x)=2/x sum_(n<=x)n chi(n)-A(x)
            =A(x)-2/x integral_1^x A(y)dy.            (3)

For q=1 this is m(m+1-x)/x, m=floor x, a bounded nonnegative source.
Positivity is insufficient: the bounded positive delayed exponential
exp(-bt)+C exp(-b(t-T))1_(t>=T), C>1, has Laplace transform
(1+C exp(-sT))/(s+b) and zeros with positive real part log(C)/T.
That is a counterexample to a positivity-only inference, not an
arithmetic lower bound for (3).

Fix0<gamma<1, a=2-gamma, s(z)=gamma+a(1+z)/(1-z). Put
F(z)=F_chi(s(z)), F0=F_chi(2)!=0, the latter by the convergent Euler
product. F belongs to H-infinity since |F_chi(s)|<=C_q/Re s. Define

    f_gamma(t)=exp(-gamma t)f(t),
    h(t)=sqrt(2a) integral_0^t exp(-a(t-u))f_gamma(u)du,
    Qv=v-2a exp(-a t)*v,      ell0(t)=sqrt(2a)exp(-at),

with causal convolution on[0,infinity). Q is an L2 isometry: its boundary
Laplace multiplier is (it-a)/(it+a). Also Q*ell0=0 and ||ell0||=1.
The Cayley Jacobian a/[pi(a^2+t^2)] and Plancherel give exactly

    ||p(Q)h||_2^2=||pF||_H2^2,
    ||p(Q)h-F0 ell0||_2^2=||pF-F0||_H2^2.           (4)

Every output tail and cross term is included. No equivalent positive
metric mI<=P<=MI can give Q*PQ<=kappa P with kappa<1: iterate and
use Q's isometry to contradict m<=kappa^n M. This does not prohibit
source-specific signed polynomial cancellation.

Define the constrained prediction problem

    d_N=min_(p(0)=1,deg p<=N)||pF||^2,
    Delta_N=d_N-|F0|^2=min ||pF-F0||^2.              (5)

The equality follows from the exact constant coefficient. The full
Toeplitz Gram has G_jk=integral conjugate(z^jF)z^kF dm, so its quadratic
form is p*Gp. G is positive definite and d_N=1/(G^-1)_00. Delta_N>=0
decreases, but positivity supplies no convergence to zero.

For a hypothetical zero rho=beta+iT with beta>gamma set
w=(rho-gamma-a)/(rho-gamma+a), nonzero since the anchor2 is safe.
The complete error e=pF-F0 has e(0)=0, e(w)=-F0. Cauchy-Schwarz in zH2
therefore gives

    Delta_N>=|F0|^2(1-|w|^2)/|w|^2
       =4a|F0|^2(beta-gamma)/[(beta-gamma-a)^2+T^2]. (6)

A qualitative Delta_N->0 for each fixed chi at one common gamma
excludes every finite-height zero in Re>gamma. No exchange with a height
supremum is needed. A fixed nonzero residual bound does not suffice,
because the floor decays like T^-2.

The independent review proves the converse for this actual source.
The classical input is canonical inner/outer factorization and outer
cyclicity in H2; see Garcia and Ross, [Theorems2.12,2.16,2.20 and
formula2.10](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1312.5018). For F=IO, the closure of
polynomial multiples is IH2. Any admissible limit Iu has
u(0)=F0/I(0)=O(0), hence norm at least |O(0)|. Outer cyclicity gives
polynomials q_k with Fq_k->IO(0); evaluation at0 shows q_k(0)->1.
Renormalizing by these constants yields admissible approximants. Thus

    Delta_infinity=|F0|^2(|I(0)|^-2-1).             (7)

Here the singular inner factor is absent, for a reason specific to(1).
F continues across every boundary point except1. A singular measure in
its inner factor can be supported only on boundary zeros and1. One
direct justification: on each closed zero-free continued arc, |F| is
bounded below in an inner neighborhood, while |F|<=||F||_infinity
exp(-P[nu]). The Poisson integral of nu is consequently bounded there.
Weak boundary convergence then makes nu absolutely continuous on each
smaller arc; its singular restriction is zero. The remaining boundary
zeros away from1 are isolated and countable, so nu is purely atomic.
An atom c at zeta forces |F(r zeta)|<=||F||_infinity
exp[-c(1+r)/(1-r)]. At zeta!=1 this contradicts a finite-order analytic
zero; at1 it contradicts F_chi(sigma)~1/sigma as sigma->infinity,
which follows from chi(1)=1 and the literal Dirichlet series. Hence
nu=0. This also explains why mere zero-freeness would be insufficient
for an arbitrary bounded analytic source.

The inner factor is therefore exactly the Blaschke product of the
zeros rho_j in Re>gamma. With w_j their Cayley images,

    Delta_infinity=|F0|^2[product_j |w_j|^-2-1].     (8)

The product is positive and convergent by the bounded-source Blaschke
condition and F0!=0; multiplicities are retained. Boundary zeros create
no singular atom. Equation(8) makes Delta_N->0 equivalent to the
desired zero exclusion for this character. It is a precise criterion,
not a claim that the arithmetic difficulty has disappeared.

### A complete and faster source-tail bound

Let H0=sqrt(2a)C_q/(a-gamma), K=1+2a/(a-gamma). Then
|Q^j h(t)|<=H0 K^j exp(-gamma t). The omitted Gram beyond T is PSD
and at most (N+1)H0^2 K^(2N)exp(-2gamma T)/(2gamma) times I. For an
explicit polynomial, its complete squared error is at most

    integral_0^T |p(Q)h-F0 ell0|^2 dt
      +H0^2(sum_j |p_j|K^j)^2 exp(-2gamma T)/gamma
      +2|F0|^2 exp(-2aT).                           (9)

The exponential degree cost can instead be paid by a coherent source
approximation. If ||h-h_tilde||<=tau, the isometry gives

    ||p(Q)(h-h_tilde)||<=tau sum_j |p_j|.           (10)

Every Gram-entry error is <=tau(||h||+||h_tilde||), and its operator
error is at most N+1 times that amount. This is an absolute error,
not a PSD ordering of the two Grams. Even a compactly supported
h_tilde has full filtered future responses, which must be included.

For1/2<gamma<1 put lambda=a-gamma=2-2gamma in(0,1). At q=1, with
u={x}, f(log x)=1/2+B(x)-V(x)/x, B=1/2-u, V=u(1-u). The bounded
primitive of B is V/2, of norm<=1/8. Integrating by parts with its
lower endpoint, then paying V/x absolutely, proves

    |integral_x^infinity y^(lambda-1)(f(log y)-1/2)dy|
        <=D_lambda x^(lambda-1),
    D_lambda=(2-lambda)/[4(1-lambda)].              (11)

Thus h(t)=A0 exp(-gamma t)+C exp(-at)+R(t),
A0=sqrt(2a)/(2lambda), |R(t)|<=sqrt(2a)D_lambda exp(-(gamma+1)t).
Keep h unchanged on[0,T] and continue explicitly by

    h_tilde(t)=A0 exp(-gamma t)
       +(h(T)-A0 exp(-gamma T))exp[-a(t-T)]  for t>T.

Subtracting the expansions at t and T and paying both L2 tails yields

    ||h-h_tilde||<=D_lambda[1+sqrt(a/(gamma+1))]
                            exp[-(gamma+1)T].     (12)

No unknown infinite constant C is needed for this continuation.

All ordinary characters have the same construction. For nonprincipal
chi, A is q-periodic; subtract its mean m_chi. The mean-zero remainder
has primitive bounded by2q^2. For principal chi let B0=A-rx, beta its
period mean, D(x)=integral_1^x(B0-beta). Directly from(3),

    f(log x)=-beta+(B0(x)-beta)+(r+2beta-2D(x))/x.  (13)

The bounds |D|<=2q^2 and |r+2beta-2D|<=1+2q+4q^2 give(11)-(12)
with A0=sqrt(2a)m_chi/lambda and D_chi=4q^2 for nonprincipal chi,
or D_chi=4q^2+(1+2q+4q^2)/(1-lambda) for principal chi. Natural zeros
and complex components are retained. Fixed-q constants are allowed.
The constants blow up at gamma=1/2; no endpoint claim is made.

This adapts [private research revision]'s bounded-periodic-primitive method to the exact
pole-normalized source. It pays source formation, with the coefficient
sum in(10), but leaves the full signed prediction residual OPEN.

### Finite optimization and interpolation do not pay that residual

Every finite constrained minimizer has all roots outside the closed
disk, for any nonzero F with F0!=0. If p=(z-z0)q, variation by zq
preserves p(0)=1. Orthogonality and strict Cauchy-Schwarz for qF,zqF
give |z0|>1. This is classical optimal-polynomial ancestry; see
[Beneteau et al., Theorem3.2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1509.04807), with the
present constrained version proved directly in the retained report.

For F=1-z/r the size-m Gram determinant is sum_(k=0)^m r^(-2k),
so d_N is the ratio of the size N+1 and N determinants. Its limit is
r^-2 for r<1 and1 for r>=1. Grams for r and1/r differ by a scalar,
and hence give identical constrained minimizers despite different
interior zero geometry. For the inner source (z-r)/(1-rz), the Gram is
I while Delta_N=1-r^2. Stable roots and conditioning are insufficient.

If the full error e vanishes at finitely many safe nodes, including0,
form their finite Blaschke product B, including multiplicity. Then
e/B is in H2 with exactly the same norm, and at a hypothetical source
zero w away from those nodes,

    ||e||^2>=|F0|^2(1-|w|^2)/|B(w)|^2.             (14)

There is no extra norm charge for dividing an error already in BH2.
For F=1-z/r, its finite Taylor inverse gives e=-(z/r)^(N+1), so exact
finite matching can coexist with growing full error. Fixed-anchor
amplification at height T costs degree of order T^2/(beta-gamma).
Other node geometries remain eligible only with a paid full residual.

## G129. Actual divisor Bellman identity and a scoped price

Set a(n)=mu(n)chi(n), c(n)=chi(n). Their Dirichlet convolution is delta
on every integer, with ramified zeros retained. Thus a(1)=1 and
a(n)=-sum_(d|n,d<n)a(d)chi(n/d). Let x_n=(a(1),...,a(n)) and T_n
append this exact signed divisor row. With ell_N=(1,...,1), a sufficient
Hermitian Bellman certificate is

    P_n>=0, P_N>=ell_N*ell_N,
    T_n*P_nT_n<=P_(n-1)+E_n.

The debts E_n may be signed. Evaluation on the actual source telescopes:

    |M_chi(N)|^2<=x_1*P_1x_1
          +sum_(n=2)^N x_(n-1)*E_n x_(n-1).        (15)

An O_(chi,epsilon)(N^(2gamma+epsilon)) bound on the entire right side
gives Mertens exponent gamma and ordinary zero exclusion by Abel
continuation. For a reachable-state version, inequalities need hold
only after evaluation on the actual x; global matrix inequalities are
a stronger sufficient condition, not an assumption forced on that route.

The exact backward row is

    w_(N,n)(d)=sum_(j<=n/d)chi(j)M_chi(floor(N/(dj))). (16)

For an arbitrary prefix, form b(k)=sum_(d|k)x_d chi(k/d) for k<=n,
and0 for k>n. Its unique recurrence continuation is b*(mu chi).
Sum through N and reorder to obtain(16). Hence w_(N,N)=ell_N,
w_(N,n-1)=w_(N,n)T_n and w_(N,1)=M_chi(N). The no-debt metric
P_n=w_(N,n)*w_(N,n) is exact but starts with the unknown |M(N)|^2.
It locates the missing signed response; it is not a noncircular estimate.

Even after deleting all forced-zero coordinates, a global diagonal
terminal majorant has exponent-two price. Let I={n<=N:a(n)!=0}, K=|I|.
For D=diag(d_i)>0, D>=ell_I*ell_I is equivalent to sum 1/d_i<=1.
The actual terminal energy is sum d_i>=K^2, with equality d_i=K.
Squarefree q-unit counting gives

    K=kappa_q N+O_q(sqrt N),
    kappa_q=zeta(2)^-1 product_(p|q)(1+1/p)^-1>0.

Expand squarefreeness as sum_(d^2|n)mu(d), count q-units, and pay the
sqrt N counting errors and d^-2 tail. The resulting Theta_q(N^2)
price applies to this specified global diagonal class only. It is not
a lower bound on Mertens sums or every source-specific reachable metric.
Signed off-diagonal geometry and a usable reachability description remain
open. This specializes the earlier magnitude-only obstruction to the
literal divisor cocycle and its complete adjoint.

## G130. Raw principal finite-polynomial global contraction fails

For principal chi,0<gamma<1, let P(s) be a finite Dirichlet polynomial.
If R=1-L(s,chi)P(s) is bounded and holomorphic on the whole half-plane
Re>gamma, its pole at1 forces P(1)=0. If P=0 the norm is1. Otherwise
finite-frequency torus recurrence supplies unbounded T_k with
P(s+iT_k)->P(s) locally uniformly. Choose a disk centered at1 inside
the half-plane, with no P-zero on its boundary. Rouche supplies a zero
of P(s+iT_k) inside the disk. Translating back produces P-zeros with
unbounded heights away from the unique L-pole; at each, R=1. Therefore

    sup_(Re s>gamma)|1-L(s,chi)P(s)|>=1.            (17)

If the pole is not removed the supremum is infinite. Thus no sequence
of finite members yields globally uniform strict contraction in this
raw principal formulation. This does not obstruct compact convergence,
an open strip gamma<Re<1, one line, infinite filters, or the normalized
source(1). In particular the older W37 open-strip proposal excludes the
pole and is not rejected by(17). The escape is explicit, not a universal
Bezout impossibility claim.
title: G130. Raw principal finite-polynomial global contraction fails

statement:
## G131. Complementary divisors and the actual Poisson boundary

Use ideal norms and the literal cutoff V, equal to one on [0,1] and zero
on [2,infinity). Let `R=U^(4/3)` and

    A_R(n)=sum_(d|n) mu(d)V(Nd/R).

For every nonunit n, the complete divisor sum of mu is zero, so exactly

    A_R(n)=-sum_(dm=n) mu(d)[1-V(Nd/R)]
          =-sum_(m|n) mu(n/m)[1-V(Nn/(Nm R))].             (1)

The unit is excluded: its left side is one and complementary sum zero.
Nonzero summands have `Nd>R`; under `Nn<=C L`, therefore `Nm<C L/R`.
There is no coprimality restriction. Complete multiplicativity of the
natural character `phi_u` preserves (1), including shared primes and
all natural zeros. If every proper divisor has norm at most R, the
original sum gives `A_R(n)=mu(n)[V(Nn/R)-1]`.

On good squarefree n only, the source Gauss identities give

    gamma_1 gamma_2=mu alpha G,  a0=conj(alpha)gamma_2,
    |gamma_2|=1,
    A_R(n)gamma_1(n)=G(n)conj(a0(n))mu(n)A_R(n),
    mu(n)A_R(n)=-sum_(m|n)mu(m)[1-V(Nn/(Nm R))].         (2)

Here G is the fixed ray function. The last formula fails at prime squares:
the formal n=4,R=2 example has left side zero and right side minus one.
Equation (1) still holds. Even on squarefree n, the new amplitude can
equal two when n has three distinct prime factors individually at most R
and pair products at least 2R. Thus it is not the literal coefficient
allowed by B3.6, which permits no further arithmetic coefficient on n.
A divisor bound does not repair that source contract. This obstruction
does not prove a lower bound for the actual signed sum.

For coprime good squarefree nonunit l,l', without slots or a moving row
selector, the clean sixth-free row Poisson specialization is

    U/sqrt(Nl Nl') sum_b mu(b)/(Nb)^6 1_((b,ll')=1) R(l,l')
      *sum_h Gcal(l,h)conj(Gcal(l',-h))
        F(Phi)(U Nh/((Nb)^6 Nl Nl')).                    (3)

The b range is finite, `Nb<=(C_Phi U)^(1/6)`. The CRT factor is the actual
reciprocity sign R(l,l'). The conjugate Fourier factor explains `-h`;
the two Gauss normalizers explain `U/sqrt(Nl Nl')`. The identity
`u=b^6 k` retains all six units in k, without multiplying b by six.
The scalar from b is the displayed natural-zero indicator. Frequency
zero vanishes for these nonprincipal natural characters.

A fixed ray restriction still needs its finite character expansion; a
fixed hole mask needs every `d|rad(E)` with its coefficient, scalar and
rescaled kernel; omitted fixed-inducing rows need their actual subtraction.
Shared support, arbitrary valuations and original slots require the full
source reconstruction. A zero-bin selector cannot be inserted into (3).
At `Nl,Nl'~L=U^(4/3)`, the first dual length is `L^2/U=U^(5/3)`, so this
first transform alone does not produce a short dual sum.
title: G131. Complementary divisors and the actual Poisson boundary

## G132. A complete positive prefix estimate

Fix a finite natural dictionary and one whole orientation. Let H be smooth,
equal to one on [0,1], between zero and one, supported in [0,C] for fixed
C. For fixed `B`, bounded `lambda>=0`, and `t=4/3`, put

    L=U^(t+lambda), Y=U^B,
    P_u(s)=sum_(Nn>R) phi_u(n) A_R(n) (Nn)^(-s)
                         exp(-Nn/Y)H(Nn/L).             (4)

All nonunit terms below R vanish anyway. For
`17/25<=delta<=7/10`, set `a=(1+delta)/2`. Let N0(P) be the sum over
nonzero sixth-free element rows, with a nonnegative smooth ball majorant,
of squared tensor Sobolev norms on `[a,1] x [-T-1,T+1]`, using derivatives
`partial_sigma^i partial_tau^j`, `i,j in {0,1}`. The real interval has
width at least 3/20. For every epsilon>0,

    N0(P) << H_J U^(J(delta,lambda)+epsilon),
    J(delta,lambda)=1/6+(5/6-delta)t+(1-delta)lambda.     (5)

H_J retains finite smooth seminorms and polynomial height costs. Constants
may depend on the fixed dictionary and profiles; no moving conductor
uniformity is inferred.

To prove (5), insert (1) before expanding a square:

    P_u(s)=-sum_(Nm<C L/R) phi_u(m)(Nm)^(-s)
       *sum_d mu(d)phi_u(d)(Nd)^(-s)[1-V(Nd/R)]
                      H(Nd Nm/L)exp(-Nd Nm/Y).           (6)

On a d dyad of size D, `D` is at least a fixed multiple of R and
`D<<L/Nm`. The inner inverse coefficient remains exactly `mu(d)phi_u(d)`.
The coupled cutoffs are common smooth profiles: on fixed positive annuli,
all Euler derivatives are uniformly bounded in their positive dilation
parameters. Apply the full-box B3.3 common-profile representation before
choosing a live m or row. Freeze the entire profile during restoration;
in particular, do not reset R when the inverse scale is shortened.

The old centrally normalized inverse moment and its Sobolev consequence
give `H_J U^(1/6)D^(5/6+epsilon)` in this range, including the row ball's
smaller dyads and unit window. The weight `Nd^(-s)` changes its squared
bound by `D^(1-2a)=D^(-delta)`. All mixed derivatives pay logarithms and
the retained finite height factors. Hilbert triangle over D is dominated
by `D<<L/Nm`, since `5/6-delta>0`. The outside character is a contraction
even at shared primes and natural zeros. The resulting norm is at most

    H_J^(1/2) U^(1/12+epsilon)L^((5/6-delta)/2)
       *sum_(Nm<C L/R)(Nm)^(-a-(5/6-delta)/2).

The exponent on Nm is exactly `-11/12`. The ideal count O(X), with its
unit included, bounds this sum by `O((L/R)^(1/12))`. Squaring gives
`U^(1/6+epsilon)L^(5/6-delta)(L/R)^(1/6)`, exactly (5). No signed
cancellation between cofactors was assumed or hidden in a divisor loss.

For the actual original slot product Q_u of total width v, keep the
slots inside the same positive norm. The retained marked inverse estimate
has exponent

    E_MI(1,r,v)=1/6+(5/6)max(1,r+2v,(2r+8v)/3).

With active `r>=4/3+o(1)` and `v<=1/20`, its maximum is `r+2v`. Thus the
same proof yields

    Nv(P Q) << H_J U^(J(delta,lambda)+5v/3+epsilon).     (7)

This uses the [restricted research revision] fine slot mesh, chosen from the loss and bounded ranges
before the eventual dictionary, slots, profiles and heights. Original
independent heights and the complete orientation remain. Shared cofactor
and slot primes are handled by the natural contraction, not deleted.
Equation (7) bounds the complete positive norm, not a signed pair slice.
title: G132. A complete positive prefix estimate
