## G133. Two restricted returns with rational interval certificates

For actual nonprincipal buffered zero rows, the licensed completed detector
has `D_R,u(rho_u)=-1+O(U^(-A))`. Its original contour, smoothing and height
order must be retained. On the subset E_pre where `|P_u(rho_u)|>=1/4`,
positive Sobolev evaluation bounds the cardinality by (5). Only then use
the physical bin slot estimate `|Q_u|^2<<H_J U^(delta v+epsilon)`:

    sum_(u in E_pre)|Q_u|^2 << H_J U^(J+delta v+epsilon). (8)

This is a positive counting argument, with no E_pre selector in Poisson.
It is not a principal detector theorem or an arbitrary coefficient moment.

Keep the independently accepted preceding-family constant
`K=28114053/6250000`; do not feed c11 back into it. Write

    h=5-2delta, rho=1-10delta/(3h), k=rho+delta-1,
    D_K=15K-10-6Kdelta,
    a_K=delta(5-6delta)^2/(3h D_K),
    b_K=2delta(5-6delta)(K-1)/D_K,
    E_K=rho+delta v-min(3kv,a_K+b_K v).

All denominators, k and b_K are positive on the closed delta interval.
For `0<=lambda<=1/2500` and `0<=v<=1/25`,

    E_K-(J+delta v)>=1/5000.                             (9)

Indeed, set `J0=23/18-4delta/3`. A sufficient lower bound after subtracting
1/5000 is `rho-J0-a_K-b_K/25-(1-delta)/2500-1/5000`.
Multiply by `3h D_K` and substitute `delta=17/25+x/50`. Its cubic
Bernstein coefficients on `0<=x<=1` are

    17291065395149/1464843750000000,
    35476907047777/109863281250000,
    25900645202087/43945312500000,
    24797299722/30517578125,

all positive. This is a whole-interval certificate. For the full marked
norm, `0<=v<=1/200` suffices for

    E_K-(J+5v/3)>=1/5000.                                (10)

Use `min(3kv,a_K+b_K v)<=3kv`. Multiply the sufficient lower bound
`rho-J0-(1-delta)/2500-(5/3-delta+3k)/200-1/5000` by `3h`.
Its quadratic Bernstein coefficients after the same substitution are
`737/1171875,37031/3750000,1993/125000`, all positive.
After choosing all epsilon, buffer, endpoint, logarithm and height-power
shares to spend less than 1/10000, at least 1/10000 remains. The unspent
algebraic 1/5000 must not be advertised as the final paid margin.

The proposed whole range `v<=1/20` fails already for (8): at
`delta=17/25,v=1/20,lambda=0`, its exact comparison is
`-228190682/298987653375`. Larger lambda worsens that value. No global
optimality follows, but this failed extension must be retained.
title: G133. Two restricted returns with rational interval certificates

statement:
## G134. Uniform second-order moving Riesz comparison

For each fixed ordinary Dirichlet character chi, including principal,
imprimitive and complex characters with their presented-modulus zeros,
put `a(n)=mu(n)chi(n)`, `M(t)=sum_(n<=t)a(n)` and

    E(x)=sum_(n>=1)a(n)exp(-n/x),
    R_r(N)=sum_(n<=N)a(n)(1-n/N)^r,
    B_r(x)=R_r(rx), V_r(x)=2B_(2r)(x)-B_r(x).

Endpoint n=N has weight zero. For real r>=2 and an explicit summatory
input `|M(t)|<=C t^beta`, beta>0, the complete bounds are

    |B_r(x)-E(x)| <= C K1(beta)x^beta/r,
    |V_r(x)-E(x)| <= (3/2)C K2(beta)x^beta/r^2,           (1)
    K1=5*2^(beta+2)Gamma(beta+2)+2^(beta+3)Gamma(beta+3),
    K2=12*2^(beta+3)Gamma(beta+3)
       +4*2^(beta+4)Gamma(beta+4)+2^(beta+5)Gamma(beta+5).

These hold for every x>0 and real r>=2, uniformly in both. The unconditional
input beta=C=1 gives K1=176 and K2=11904, hence second-order constant17856.
A stronger summatory beta is an extra hypothesis, not a consequence of
writing down the accepted c alone.

Here is a global remainder proof. Set `k_r(u)=(1-u/r)_+^r` and
`A(u)=u-u^2/2`. On `0<=u<=r/2`, write
`z=(r-1)log(1-u/r)+u`. The complete logarithmic series gives

    z<=u/r, |z|<=(u+u^2)/r,
    |z-A(u)/r|<=(u^2/2+2u^3/3)/r^2.

Apply `|exp(z)-1-z|<=(z^2/2)exp(max(z,0))` and
`exp(-u+max(z,0))<=exp(-u/2)`. Then

    |k'_r+exp(-u)| <= (5u+u^2)exp(-u/2)/r,
    |k'_r+exp(-u)(1+A/r)| <= P(u)exp(-u/2)/r^2,
    P(u)=12u^2+4u^3+u^4.                                (2)

For `u>=r/2`, the derivative is zero beyond r and at most exp(-u/2)
in modulus on its support. Since `r<=2u`, multiplying the proposed
second inequality by r^2 costs at most `2r^2+r|A|<=10u^2+u^3<=P`.
The first inequality follows from `2<=4u/r`. Thus (2) covers the full
positive half-line, not just the expanding finite interval.

Abel integration with vanishing endpoints gives

    sum_n a(n)h(n/x)=-int_0^infty M(xu)h'(u)du.

Integrating (2) against C x^beta u^beta proves the first part of (1).
Writing `k'_r=-exp(-u)(1+A/r)+e_r`, the first-order term cancels
exactly in `2k'_(2r)-k'_r+exp(-u)`. The remaining multiplier is
`2/4+1=3/2`; integration proves the second part. This pays the branch
`rx<n<=2rx`, endpoint integers and the entire exponential tail. Any
squared V norm retains `4|B_(2r)|^2+|B_r|^2-4Re(B_(2r)conj(B_r))`.

On each shell [X,2X], freeze one `r_X=max(2,ceil(X^delta))`. Equation (1)
gives a uniform pointwise and L2(dx/x) comparison error
`O(X^(beta-2delta))`. Therefore the every-positive-epsilon shell exponent
gamma for the moving V is equivalent to that of the fixed E whenever
`beta-2delta<=gamma`. Strict inequality supplies a fixed margin.

Only after this comparison use the fixed Mellin transform. Absolute
Fubini for Re(s)>1 and substitution n/x give

    Mellin(E)(s)=Gamma(s)/L(s,chi),
    Mellin(R_r)(s)=Gamma(s)Gamma(r+1)/(Gamma(s+r+1)L(s,chi)).

The beta identity and nonvanishing Gamma are classical
[DLMF facts](https://dlmf.nist.gov/5.12.E1), with
[Gamma's analytic properties](https://dlmf.nist.gov/5.2).
A fixed-field dyadic exponent gamma>0 makes its Mellin integral
holomorphic on Re(s)>gamma: choose epsilon below the compact set's
distance to gamma and sum by Cauchy–Schwarz, including every logarithmic
derivative. E decays exponentially at zero; fixed R_r vanishes below1.
Multiply by L and continue the identity. Every hypothetical L-zero at
any fixed height contradicts the nonzero numerator. The principal pole
is treated meromorphically, not mistaken for a zero. Constants may depend
on each fixed character; no growing-conductor uniformity is asserted.

A moving-r field has no direct fixed-r Mellin formula. Nor is a difference
of two Gamma quotients automatically nonzero. The comparison to E avoids
both issues. With beta=1, the following are sufficient conditional targets:

|gamma|c|delta|Complete comparison error exponent|
|---|---|---|---|
|.87485|.12515|.063|.874|
|5/6|1/6|.084|.832|
|3/4|1/4|.126|.748|

The largest raw cutoff is `4r_X X`, of order `X^(1+delta)`. A raw-cutoff
bound with exponent eta yields `(1+delta)eta` only with constants uniform
in the moving order. The decreasing integral bound `|B_r(x)|<=x` gives
`|V_r(x)|<=3x`, still exponent one. Increasing r alone gains nothing.
The new useful component is the uniform actual-source comparison, not
a new Mellin principle or arithmetic saving. Only fixed extrapolation
order two is proved; growing extrapolation order has no paid bound here.
title: G134. Uniform second-order moving Riesz comparison

## G135. Exact rank and renewal targets, with their costs retained

For fixed q and each unit residue a, let u_(a,k) and v_(a,k) list the
mu=+1 and mu=-1 integers in order. For `1/2<gamma<1`, the following
conditions are equivalent, also with every-positive-epsilon losses:

1. Every character mod q has `M_chi(x)=O(x^gamma)`.
2. Every unit residue has `M_(q,a)(x)=O(x^gamma)`.
3. Both lists are infinite and `|u_(a,k)-v_(a,k)|=O(k^gamma)` for every k.

The first equivalence is the full finite character transform, including
principal and imprimitive characters. For the forward rank statement,
expand mu^2 by square divisors to obtain

    Q_(q,a)(x)=d_q x+O_q(sqrt x),
    d_q=(q*zeta(2))^(-1)product_(p|q)(1-p^(-2))^(-1)>0.

Each of at most sqrt(x) progression counts has error O(1); completing
the absolutely convergent d^(-2) tail costs O(sqrt(x)). Hence the two
signed counting functions are `d_q x/2+O(x^gamma)`, with infinite lists
and inverse ranks `2k/d_q+O(k^gamma)`. Conversely, each rank pair crossing
x has k<=x, length O(x^gamma), and a distinct lower endpoint in the last
O(x^gamma) integers before x. This bounds the discrepancy without an
infinite rearrangement. Finite lists have exactly |M_(q,a)(N)| unmatched
end ranks; dropping them would drop the target itself. This refines the
existing transport formulation, with no improved infinite displacement.

For the same actual a(n), the exact prime-power identity is
`a log=-a*(Lambda chi)`. Set
`R(x)=sum_(d<=x)Lambda(d)chi(d)M(x/d)=-sum_(n<=x)a(n)log n`.
Finite Abel summation gives

    M(x)log x=int_1^x M(t)dt/t-R(x),
    M(x)=1-R(x)/log x-int_2^x R(t)dt/[t(log t)^2].        (3)

The source constant1 and endpoint at2 are essential. For gamma>0,
`R=O(x^gamma log x)` and `M=O(x^gamma)` are equivalent, including
epsilon losses. This locates the full signed correlation, not a weaker
new hypothesis.

For `S_gamma(X)=sum_(d<=X)Lambda(d)|chi(d)|d^(-gamma)`,
`sum Lambda(d)floor(X/d)=log(floor X!)` implies
`S_1(X)>=log X-O_q(1)`. Removing finitely many ramified prime-power rays
costs a finite constant. Set `Y=exp(sqrt(log X))`. Since Lambda(d)<=log d,
`S_1(Y)<=(1/2)log X+O(sqrt(log X))`. Thus for every fixed0<gamma<1,

    S_gamma(X)/log X >=(1/2+o(1))exp((1-gamma)sqrt(log X)) -> infinity.

At gamma=1 the lower limiting ratio is at least one. This rules out
the proposed absolute normalized small-gain bound without using a prime
number theorem. It is never a lower bound for signed R or M. A complete
source-specific signed estimate remains eligible.
title: G135. Exact rank and renewal targets, with their costs retained

statement:
## G136. Paid coupling repair and complete resonant feedback

The independent protected audit separates ordinary coupling conservation
from the actual divisor map. A coupling with additive marginal a(n) and
multiplicative marginal `(a*chi)(n)=delta_(n=1)` would have total masses
M(N) and1, so ordinarily cannot exist. A repair must carry M(N)-1.

For feasible equal-mass marginals r,c and allowed finite edges E, the
minimum full total variation is exactly

    inf_(BZ=(r,c)) sum_E|Z_ij|
      =sup_(|u_i+v_j|<=1) Re[sum conj(u_i)r_i+sum conj(v_j)c_j].

This is finite-dimensional quotient-norm duality: the compact image of
the unit ball has a supporting functional giving the constraint above.
For real coefficients it is a linear program; for complex character
coefficients it is a modulus/SOCP problem. Singleton additive cells force
full TV `sum|a(n)|=kappa_q N+O_q(sqrt N)`. This is not a bound on every
possible defect. Two equal arrays have zero difference at any common M,
so a small marginal-preserving difference alone supplies no cancellation.

The literal repair instead uses triangular divisor matrices

    C_(n,d)=chi(n/d)1_(d|n),
    A_(n,d)=mu(n/d)chi(n/d)1_(d|n), AC=CA=I.

For a candidate vector v and `e=Cv-e_1`, exact inversion gives `v-a=Ae`.
Grouping n=kd, for every integer interval (L,U] one obtains

    sum_(L<n<=U)v_n-[M(U)-M(L)]
      =sum_(k<=U)e_k[M(floor(U/k))-M(floor(L/k))].        (4)

Thus small candidate readout AND a bound on the entire signed response
return the desired M bound. Unrestricted weighted error TV has scalar
operator norm `max_k |M(floor(N/k))|/w_k`, attained by a single aligned
error; k=1 already contains M(N). Actual compatible defects can evade
that ambient worst case only through a proved restriction. This is a
source-exact application of the existing inverse/adjoint principle.

The independent uniform audit preserves the original native H tensor,
both projectors, masks, signed short core, CRT phase, angular factors
and1/Q normalization from [[restricted research revision]](../[private research revision]/h-joint-integration.md) and
[G89](../[private research revision]/wild48-integration.md). Splitting its source into a unit
mode v and its orthogonal complement retains BOTH scalar readout and
innovation. A small innovation cannot discard the scalar.

If an exact compatible scale map is actually constructed with block
coefficients a_j,b_j,c_j,D_j, then

    alpha_(j+1)=a_j alpha_j+b_j eta_j,
    eta_(j+1)=c_j alpha_j+D_j eta_j,
    alpha_(j+1)=a_j alpha_j+b_j D_(j-1)...D_0 eta_0
       +sum_(k<j)b_j D_(j-1)...D_(k+1)c_k alpha_k.        (5)

Every empty product is the identity; actual forcing needs its complete
Duhamel terms. For the diagnostic `T=[[1,e],[e,0]]`, D=0 while
`alpha_(j+1)=alpha_j+e^2 alpha_(j-1)` has a root above1. Changing the
feedback sign changes the conclusion. This is a scoped objection to
innovation-only reasoning, not a native arithmetic lower bound. The
actual scale map, conditioning and complete signed feedback remain OPEN.
title: G136. Paid coupling repair and complete resonant feedback

# [private research revision]: a narrow simultaneous-witness target with its complete source return

Accept G137–G139 at the scopes below. The [author](wild56/REPORT.md),
[independent review](wild56-review/report.md) and
[retention manifest](retention-manifest.json) preserve 29 original files
and five immutable mathematical source bindings. Current written
c11=312864909/2500000000=.1251459636 is unchanged. The new arithmetic
hypotheses remain OPEN, as do inherited F0/analytic ancestry, original
positive-slot uniformity and external definition/import/admission.
No formalization, kernel work, new packet or public-record claim follows.

## G137. A restricted inverse moment can pay both witness branches

Use the exact [[private research revision]](../[private research revision]/density-integration.md) family and
[[private research revision]](../[private research revision]/joint-density-integration.md) same-character,
same-zero witness contract. Freeze K=28114053/6250000=4.49824848 from
the accepted c10 SAME-family input; it is not the physical kappa and
is not recalibrated from c11. Keep the original labels, natural holes
and coefficient zeros, independent slot heights, derivative profiles,
positive grades, finite dictionary and common thresholds. A signed
projector does not automatically preserve a joint-witness restriction.

Normalize the free width to 1, write d=delta in[.68,.70], v=z/W, and
retain r<=t, r+m>=t, m<=1/2 from the original witnesses. Their bounds are

    I(r)=1-d r+d[v-(1-r)/2]_+,
    P(m)=1-2d m+d[v-(1-2m)/K]_+,
    L(t)=1/6+(5/6-d)t+d v.

The long inverse branch is bounded by L(t). Put

    u=2d(K-1)/K, alpha=u/(d+u)=2(K-1)/(3K-2),
    D=15K-10-6Kd,
    t_A=(5-6dv)/(5-2d),
    t_B=[15K-10-6d-12d(K-1)v]/D,
    t_*=max(t_A,t_B),
    r_*(t)=min(2t/3,[u t+d(1/K-v)]/(d+u)).

These are the old complete separate-moment cutoff and short crossing.
The minimum of the crossing locations is required because P is the
maximum of its two affine pieces. Near the crossing I is in its
full-fit piece 1-dr. The old short maximum Q_*(t)=1-d r_*(t) is the
maximum of decreasing affine functions with slope magnitudes 2d/3
and d alpha. At t_* it agrees with the long bound E0(1,v).

Fix 0<eta<=.001 and the SAME cutoff t=t_*-eta BEFORE witnesses.
The new hypothesis J_eta^all is a saving eta in the ORIGINAL inverse
moment restricted to actual rows that also carry the large plain
witness of that SAME character and zero, only when

    |r-r_*(t)|<=2eta,   0<=v<=1/20.

After dividing by the inverse spike this gives I(r)-eta. Require it
uniformly in every original source parameter and every actual live
positive child list where it is used. It is not supplied by separate
moments, witness independence, a changed prime pool or the rank-one
shared-zero signal in G115. This hypothesis is OPEN.

Here is its paid implication. Across the plain kink the increasing
function P(t-r) has slopes between u and 2d. If the new crossing moves
left by h, then eta=(d+b_eff)h for b_eff in[u,2d]. Its value falls by
b_eff h>=alpha eta, and h<2eta. Outside the window, the old minimum
has already fallen by at least 2d eta>=alpha eta. This remains valid
beyond adjacent pieces by monotonicity. Thus the entire short maximum
is at most Q_*(t)-alpha eta. Moving t down by eta increases Q_* by at
most (2d/3)eta, while it decreases the long branch by (5/6-d)eta.
On the full d interval,

    alpha-2d/3>=2/15,   5/6-d>=2/15.

Therefore the COMPLETE free-row envelope improves by (2/15)eta W.
Keeping the old cutoff would leave the long branch unchanged and
would not prove this conclusion.

The independent 20-by-25 exact rational interval enclosure covers
d in[.68,.70], v in[0,.05], eta in[0,.001], including both sides of
the plain kink and zero slot width. It verifies the entire length
window has r>1/2, 0<m<1/2, 1<t<3/2 and r+2v<1. The last gate and
r>1/2 also imply 2r+8v<3. Its full-fit reserve exceeds .01017.
The original fine mesh and all finite losses are fixed below positive
reserves before witnesses. Since m>=t-r>t-1>0 in the short regime,
bounded/zero-length plain witnesses cannot create an omitted short
branch; long and unrestricted exceptional cases keep their source bounds.

For raw w=u_core b^6, freeze b, preserve its holes and set
s=log_Z Nb, V=W-6s. Define

    rho=1-10d/[3(5-2d)], k=rho+d-1,
    a_K=d(5-6d)^2/[3(5-2d)D],
    b_K=2d(5-6d)(K-1)/D,
    E0(W,z)=rho W+d z-min(3kz,a_K W+b_K z).

For V>=20W/21 and 0<=z/W<=1/21 the free ratio z/V<=1/20.
The two W-slopes of E0 are rho and rho-a_K, so

    E0(W-6s,z)<=E0(W,z)-6(rho-a_K)s.

Counting all roots costs Z^s. The conditional exponent is therefore

    E0(W,z)-(2/15)eta W
      -[6(rho-a_K-(2/15)eta)-1]s.

The bracket exceeds 1.10376 on the complete box. In the remaining
V<20W/21 range, s>W/126 and the OLD unmarked tail pays the gain with
reserve [(rho-1/6-3k)/21-(2/15)eta]W>.00109398W. Original bounded
free windows and fixed-inducing free cores retain their actual raw
populations and fit this reserve; they are not declared finite raw sets.
Consequently J_eta^all implies the complete source-relative bound

    Z^[E0(W,z)-(2/15)eta W+epsilon] H_J,
    0<=z/W<=1/21.

At eta=.001 the conditional saving is W/7500. A sharper version on
.034<=z/W<=.05 retunes t=t_B-12(K-1)eta/D and gives
C_J eta W, C_J=2(5-6d)(K-1)/D>=7/50. Its narrower hypothesis does
not imply J_eta^all. Both versions and their checks are preserved.

No numerical endpoint is assigned. Every child saving uses its actual
width. Support loss, signed reconstruction, extraction scalars,
amplifiers, local plane, complete physical rectangle, Euler shifts
including zero capacity, principal residues and actual-supremum
feedback still need integration. The unchanged architecture's c<2/15
barrier cannot reach 1/6 or 1/4 by this envelope alone. The decisive
next estimate is the actual inverse moment on this same-zero,
large-plain subset, not another optimization of the old separate bounds.

## G138. Full integral persistence and fixed versus moving readouts

Use the augmented squarefree complex with deg(e_n)=omega(n),
ordered prime-deletion differential and C(x)=0 for x<1. For each odd
squarefree m set b_m=e_(2m), z_m=d b_m=e_m-e_2 wedge d e_m.
Every correction has index 2m/p<m. This gives an integral
unitriangular basis at EVERY real cutoff, with d b_m=z_m and d z_m=0.
Thus the entire persistence module splits into intervals [m,2m) in
augmented degree omega(m), including [1,2) in degree 0 (reduced -1).
Inclusions are identity while an interval survives and zero at death.
This is a direct filtered-basis proof, not an imported barcode theorem.
Classical static topology retains its Björner/W27 attribution.

All logarithmic lifetimes equal log2. The map H(C(x))->H(C(2x)) is
zero, although M(3)=-1. A selection of longer-lived classes deletes
the signal. For fixed alpha in[1/2,1), write

    O_chi(x)=sum_(odd n<=x) mu(n)chi(n),
    R_alpha,chi(x)=O_chi(x)-O_chi(alpha x),
    M_chi(x)=O_chi(x)-chi(2)O_chi(x/2).

Character weighting is an arithmetic readout, not a commuting chain
map. Include chi(2)=0, every natural zero and the n=1 atom. On Re s>1,

    Mellin R=(1-alpha^s)/[s(1-chi(2)2^-s)L(s,chi)].

Both extra factors are nonzero on Re s>0. A COMPLETE every-epsilon
dyadic L2 bound at exponent 2gamma therefore excludes zeros Re s>gamma
for every fixed ordinary character at every height, with common gamma
and character-dependent constants. The left tail vanishes below 1;
dyadic Cauchy–Schwarz pays holomorphy and its derivatives. The principal
pole is a meromorphic point and actual imprimitive factors remain.
Pointwise reconstruction is the finite-for-each-x sum
O_chi(x)=sum_j R_alpha,chi(alpha^j x), costing (1-alpha^gamma)^-1.
Unsigned rank remains [4(1-alpha)/pi^2]x+O(sqrt x).

For T(x)=x-x^(1-eta), 0<eta<1, the arithmetic difference
R_eta(x)=O_chi(x)-O_chi(T(x)) is bounded trivially by x^(1-eta)+1.
Its persistence interpretation starts at x>=2^(1/eta); the initial
bounded interval is paid separately. Iteration until x<2 takes at
most 2+2^(k eta) steps in the dyadic band [2^k,2^(k+1)). Thus a
uniform pointwise R_eta=O(x^gamma), gamma>=0, only gives
O_chi=O(x^(gamma+eta)). The odd constant comparison source proves
this black-box loss can be sharp; it is not a Möbius lower bound.
At eta=1/4 a first gain needs gamma<.6248540364. The trivial .75
readout does not supply it. Keep the signed-window target OPEN.

## G139. A finite detector bank and actual-law audit targets

For the same Gaussian field U_chi, let S U(x)=U(x/2), a=15/8,
b=31/16, D_a=U-a S U and D_b=U-b S U. Retain the literal delayed
coefficient mu(n/2)chi(n/2), including ramification. Exactly

    U=31D_a-30D_b,
    |u-av|^2+|u-bv|^2
      =|u|^2/1861+(1861/256)|v-(976/1861)u|^2.

This sharp two-value algebraic cost is not claimed sharp in the
arithmetic family. The two individual multiplier zero lines differ;
31(1-a2^-s)-30(1-b2^-s)=1 removes their common-zero defect without
division near either zero. A complete positive bank energy at exponent
2gamma gives U energy and its nonvanishing Gaussian Mellin return.
Conversely U energy bounds both bank energies using the adjacent x/2
shell. The fixed bank is equivalent in exponent to U; its arithmetic
moment is OPEN. A moving separation comparable to X^-eta costs eta
in amplitude, 2eta in energy. The generic u=x,v=x/2 example pays this
bill and makes no arithmetic lower-bound claim.

The critic's protected card29 uses the ACTUAL uniform integers 1..N,
a(n)=mu(n)chi(n), K_N=sum|a(n)|^2 and exact prime-valuation cells.
With X_j=E[a|F_j], Delta_j=X_j-X_(j-1),

    K_N/N-|M_chi(N)/N|^2
      =sum_(j<=J) E|Delta_j|^2+E|a-X_J|^2.

The unrevealed residual is mandatory. Revealing all primes<=N makes
it zero. A lower variance bound within O(N^(2gamma-2+epsilon)) of
K_N/N is equivalent to the desired M bound, not an easier consequence
of concentration around an unknown mean. Hermitian 2-by-2 dilation
has the same identity under normalized trace. A useful actual-source
variance estimate remains eligible; Bernoulli independence is not assumed.

The independent uniform card13 gives the exact finite entropy price:
if a finite word space contains the actual word w*, pi(w*)>0 and t>0,
then E(w*)<=[log sum_w pi(w)e^(tE(w))+log(1/pi(w*))]/t.
On a relaxed K-sign source, t=1/(4K) gives partition function<=sqrt2,
but the actual-word mass 2^-K leaves O(K^2), not a subcritical energy.
Fixing every arithmetic constraint makes the class singleton and the
partition bound circular. An intermediate correlated class needs BOTH
its actual-word mass and full partition estimate. Complex characters
and coefficient zeros cannot be omitted.

The other author tests retain the precise relaxed parity/row-span
limitations and the initial, terminal and interior charges in a weighted
scale telescope. They do not refute actual integer-law information or
source-specific signed estimates.

## Evidence and disposition

All 30 original cards and six first tests survive. Author draws16/28/15
were uniform on the declared pools20/9/19, with no reroll. The whole
mechanism exclusions27/30 were too broad: their observability/gluing
variants remain untested. Do not claim exhaustive literal-threshold
coverage. The independent protected29 and uniform13 audits retain
their frozen pre-outcome priorities. Original missed deadlines and
subsequent recovery are preserved; authors and critic STOP/released.

Root read both reports, the developed arguments, three mathematical
helpers and exact [restricted research revision]/[restricted research revision] source contracts. Independent finite evidence
includes integral bases through120, 240 character identities, 625 complex
bank cases, 500 continuum interval boxes, actual-law martingale cases
and finite entropy checks. These support the written arguments; they
do not prove new arithmetic cancellation. No unchanged helper was rerun.
All29 families/109 children, later ideas, nearer gains,1/6 and1/4 remain.

# [private research revision]: a nonlinear detector with a completely paid far tail

Accept G140–G142 as written ordinary-character results at the scopes
below. The [author](nonlinear-source/report.md),
[independent review](nonlinear-source-review/report.md) and
[retention manifest](retention-manifest.json) retain eleven original
artifacts and two immutable local mathematical sources. No new c is
proved: c11=.1251459636, theta11=.8748540364 remain current. Inherited
F0/analytic ancestry, original positive-slot uniformity and external
definition/import/admission remain OPEN. This source has its own ordinary
Dirichlet-character return; no Hecke or conductor-uniform scope is inferred.
No formalization, kernel work, new packet or public-record claim is made.

The discovery pass compared a coherent Gauss bank, quadratic-family
moments, signed Vaughan recombination and this upstream phase replacement.
The first and third still need new signed estimates; the inspected
quadratic-family asymptotic assumes GRH and is not imported. W14's unused
nonlinear-phase idea motivated a new integer source, not a claim that its
native sextic covariance problem has been solved.

## G140. The actual source and its nonvanishing Mellin return

Fix an ordinary complex character chi modulo q, retain
a_n=mu(n)chi(n) with every squareful/nonunit zero, and choose fixed b>1
and integer k>2. Define for every real x>0

    W_(b,k),chi(x)=sum_(n>=1) a_n exp(-n/x^b-i(n/x)^k).

The sum converges absolutely and locally uniformly. The selected source
has b=3/2, k=6. The phase uses n^k but the damping uses n; neither may
be substituted for the other in the Mellin calculation.

For Re s>0 let I_n(s)=integral_0^infinity exp(-nt^b-i(nt)^k)t^(s-1)dt.
After v=nt, rotate clockwise by fixed
0<alpha<min(pi/(2b),pi/(2k)), with principal power branches. The large
arc is killed, for each n, by exp(-n^(1-b)R^b cos(b alpha)); the other
exponential has modulus at most1 throughout the sector. The small arc
vanishes for Re s>0. On the rotated ray exp(-iv^k) has modulus
exp(-|v|^k sin(k alpha)). Taylor's integral remainder for Re z>=0 gives
|exp(-z)-sum_(j<K)(-z)^j/j!|<=|z|^K/K!. Consequently

    I_n(s)=sum_(j<K) A_j(s)n^(-s-(b-1)j)+R_(n,K)(s),
    A_j(s)=(-1)^j Gamma((s+bj)/k)
                  exp(-i*pi*(s+bj)/(2k))/(k j!),
    |R_(n,K)(s)| <= n^(-sigma-(b-1)K) exp(alpha Im s)
       Gamma((sigma+bK)/k)
       /[k K! sin(k alpha)^((sigma+bK)/k)].

The coefficient follows by a decaying gamma-ray rotation. Local
domination, including each fixed logarithmic derivative, proves remainder
holomorphy. Its series with a_n is normally convergent on
sigma>max(0,1-(b-1)K). Initial Fubini is used only for sigma>b, where
the absolute sum of integrals equals Gamma(sigma/b)zeta(sigma/b)/b.
Thus, for H(s)=integral_0^infinity W(1/t)t^(s-1)dt,

    H(s)=sum_(j<K) A_j(s)/L(s+(b-1)j,chi)+R_chi,K(s).

For b=3/2,k=6,K=1 this is

    H(s)=Gamma(s/6)exp(-i*pi*s/12)/(6L(s,chi))+R_chi,1(s),

with R holomorphic on Re s>1/2 and nonzero leading multiplier on Re s>0.
The complete every-epsilon shell L1 bound

    integral_X^(2X)|W(x)|dx/x <<_(chi,epsilon) X^(gamma+epsilon)

for one fixed gamma>1/2 makes H holomorphic on Re s>gamma. Choose
epsilon below the compact real-part margin; shell summation also pays
all fixed derivatives. At x tending to zero the bound
1/(exp(x^(-b))-1) pays every Mellin power. Continuation of the displayed
identity excludes every zero of the actual L in that half-plane. The
principal pole produces a reciprocal zero and is retained; imprimitive
Euler factors remain in L. Arbitrary compact height ranges suffice for
all finite heights. For all characters, gamma is common, while constants
and onsets may depend on the fixed character. L2 at exponent2gamma is a
stronger sufficient premise; equivalence with zero exclusion is not claimed.

## G141. Every tail and cross term, including an actual arithmetic floor

For arbitrary |a_n|<=1, set N=X^b and write the complete energy kernel

    E(X)=sum_(n,m>=1) a_n conjugate(a_m) K_X(n,m),
    K_X(n,m)=integral_1^2 exp(-(n+m)/(N u^b))
                  exp(-i(n^k-m^k)/(X^k u^k))du/u.

Conjugate symmetry retains both ordered cross terms. With v=u^(-k),
the positive amplitude is exp(-A v^(b/k))/(kv), A=(n+m)/N. It decreases
on[2^-k,1]; endpoints plus total variation are at most2^(k+1)/k.
Integration by parts, with the damping differentiated, proves

    |K_X(n,m)| <<_(b,k) min(1,X^k/|n^k-m^k|), n!=m.

For n>m, n^k-m^k>=n^(k-1)(n-m). All pairs outside the core n,m<=M
have max(n,m)>M, so both orientations sum absolutely to
O(X^k M^(2-k)log(2M)), for every shell-fixed real M>=2. Hence exactly

    E(X)=E_<=M(X)+D_>M(X)+O_(b,k)(X^k M^(2-k)log(2M)),
    D_>M=sum_(n>M)|a_n|^2 K_X(n,n)>=0,  D_>M<<_b X^b.

This includes the full core/tail strip, distant tail, real-cutoff
endpoints and both ordered crosses. Damping and the summable majorant
justify limits from finite squares. The same formula without E_<=M
holds for the tail's own energy. Only after this identity can positivity
of the remaining core or diagonal be used in a lower or reverse bound.

For the actual coefficients, elementary squared-divisor counting gives

    sum_(n<=y)|a_n|^2=d_q y+O_q(sqrt y),
    d_q=zeta(2)^(-1) product_(p|q)p/(p+1)>0.

It counts the nonunit exclusions exactly and applies to every fixed
principal, nonprincipal or imprimitive character. With
C_(q,b)=d_q(2^b-1)/(2b), partial summation yields D_all=C_(q,b)X^b+O_q(X^(b/2)).
For b=3/2,k=6,M=X^(19/16), the complete identity becomes

    E(X)=E_<=M(X)+C_(q,3/2)X^(3/2)+O_q(X^(5/4)log X).

Thus E(X)>=(C_(q,3/2)+o(1))X^(3/2). An every-epsilon L2 exponent
2gamma<3/2 is impossible for THIS source. The gamma=3/4 boundary,
weaker L1 bounds and different b remain eligible.

The review improves the actual tail by keeping its cutoff correction:

    Q_(q,b)(X,M)=(d_q X^b/2) integral_1^2
                         u^(b-1)exp(-2M/(X^b u^b))du,
    D_>M=Q_(q,b)(X,M)+O_(q,b)(X^(b/2)).

Stieltjes integration on(M,infinity) includes the boundary error
sqrt(M)exp(-lambda M) and the integral of lambda sqrt(t)exp(-lambda t),
both O(lambda^-1/2), uniformly in M. Therefore at M=X^(4/3), b=3/2,k=6,

    E(X)=E_<=M(X)+Q_(q,3/2)(X,M)+O_q(X^(3/4)),
    E_>M(X)=Q_(q,3/2)(X,M)+O_q(X^(3/4)).

The cross exponent2/3 has room to absorb its logarithm. Replacing Q
prematurely by C X^(3/2) would lose a correction of order X^(4/3).

There is also a log-free UPPER norm bound on the original sharp shell.
Let h(t)=0 for t<=0, h(t)=10t^3-15t^4+6t^5 for0<t<1 and h(t)=1 for
t>=1. Then phi(u)=h(2u-1)h((4-u)/2) is nonnegative C^2, supported
on[1/2,4] and equal1 on[1,2]. Majorize the COMPLETE squared tail by
its phi-weighted integral. Its transformed amplitude and first derivative
vanish at endpoints, and its L1/second-derivative L1 norms are uniform
in A>=0, since A-polynomials are multiplied by exp(-cA). Two integrations
by parts give |K_phi(n,m)|<< (1+|n^k-m^k|/X^k)^-2. With
delta_n=X^k/n^(k-1), sum_(h>=1)min(1,(delta_n/h)^2)<<delta_n.
Thus, with all coefficients and the original sharp shell still present,

    ||W_>M||_2^2 <<_(b,k) X^b+X^k M^(2-k).

This proves E(X)<<X^2+X^b generically by taking M=X. It removes the
logarithm from an upper norm, not from the earlier sharp signed identity.
The bounded array a_n=1 for n<=floor(X/2), zero otherwise, gives E>>X^2
at b=3/2,k=6. This shell-dependent array is a generic obstruction,
not a lower bound for actual Möbius coefficients.

## G142. Actual logarithmic improvement and the remaining complete core

Use Green–Tao's [published Theorem1.1, pp.542–543](https://annals.math.princeton.edu/wp-content/uploads/annals-v175-n2-p03-p.pdf):
fixed-degree polynomial nilsequences have every fixed logarithmic Möbius
saving, uniform in the polynomial coefficients, with ineffective constants.
A fixed torus with the degree-k abelian filtration and fixed sine/cosine
functions gives sum_(n<=Y)mu(n)e(P(n))<<_A Y(log(2Y))^-A. A dummy torus
coordinate is available to satisfy the stated dimension convention.
The GRH power-decay remark is unused. The separately inspected
[Gao–Zhao v2 Theorem1.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2212.09241v2) assumes GRH
and is not an unconditional input.

Expand the actual periodic chi in its finite additive Fourier series,
retaining zeros and coefficient absolute sum<=q. Apply the polynomial
bound to ell n/q-n^k/(2*pi*x^k). Splitting prefix lengths at sqrt M
and Abel summing the decreasing damping proves
|W_<=M(x)|<<_(q,A) M(log M)^-A, uniformly in real x. For k=6,b=3/2,
take M=X(log X)^B, B=(D+2)/4, A=B+(D+2)/2. The core log exponent
is -D-2, the complete off-diagonal log exponent -D-1, so

    E(X)<<_(q,D) X^(3/2)+X^2(log X)^-D,
    ||W||_1<<_(q,D) X^(3/4)+X(log X)^-D

for every fixed D>0. This is actual arithmetic progress for this new
source. It still misses the first-gain energy threshold1.7497080728
by .2502919272 in power; logarithmic strength cannot grow with X.

For 0<c<=1/4 put gamma=1-c and r=1+c/2. Freeze L=X^gamma,M=X^r
before x varies over[X,2X]. The prefix n<=L costs O(X^gamma), while
G141 gives ||W_>M||_2^2<<X^(3/2)+X^(6-4r)<<X^(2gamma).
Both complementary L1 and L2 norms are therefore O(X^gamma). The
SINGLE complete core target is

    integral_X^(2X)|sum_(X^gamma<n<=X^r) mu(n)chi(n)
              exp(-n/x^(3/2)-i(n/x)^6)|dx/x
                   <<_(chi,c,epsilon) X^(gamma+epsilon).  (CORE1)

By the norm triangle inequality in both directions this is equivalent
to the full source L1 input. The same holds for L2, which is sufficient
but stronger. The complements also permit exact big-O equivalence.
No omitted cross is hidden: the full tail function was first bounded

## G141. Every tail and cross term, including an actual arithmetic floor

For arbitrary |a_n|<=1, set N=X^b and write the complete energy kernel

    E(X)=sum_(n,m>=1) a_n conjugate(a_m) K_X(n,m),
    K_X(n,m)=integral_1^2 exp(-(n+m)/(N u^b))
                  exp(-i(n^k-m^k)/(X^k u^k))du/u.

Conjugate symmetry retains both ordered cross terms. With v=u^(-k),
the positive amplitude is exp(-A v^(b/k))/(kv), A=(n+m)/N. It decreases
on[2^-k,1]; endpoints plus total variation are at most2^(k+1)/k.
Integration by parts, with the damping differentiated, proves

    |K_X(n,m)| <<_(b,k) min(1,X^k/|n^k-m^k|), n!=m.

For n>m, n^k-m^k>=n^(k-1)(n-m). All pairs outside the core n,m<=M
have max(n,m)>M, so both orientations sum absolutely to
O(X^k M^(2-k)log(2M)), for every shell-fixed real M>=2. Hence exactly

    E(X)=E_<=M(X)+D_>M(X)+O_(b,k)(X^k M^(2-k)log(2M)),
    D_>M=sum_(n>M)|a_n|^2 K_X(n,n)>=0,  D_>M<<_b X^b.

This includes the full core/tail strip, distant tail, real-cutoff
endpoints and both ordered crosses. Damping and the summable majorant
justify limits from finite squares. The same formula without E_<=M
holds for the tail's own energy. Only after this identity can positivity
of the remaining core or diagonal be used in a lower or reverse bound.

For the actual coefficients, elementary squared-divisor counting gives

    sum_(n<=y)|a_n|^2=d_q y+O_q(sqrt y),
    d_q=zeta(2)^(-1) product_(p|q)p/(p+1)>0.

It counts the nonunit exclusions exactly and applies to every fixed
principal, nonprincipal or imprimitive character. With
C_(q,b)=d_q(2^b-1)/(2b), partial summation yields D_all=C_(q,b)X^b+O_q(X^(b/2)).
For b=3/2,k=6,M=X^(19/16), the complete identity becomes

    E(X)=E_<=M(X)+C_(q,3/2)X^(3/2)+O_q(X^(5/4)log X).

Thus E(X)>=(C_(q,3/2)+o(1))X^(3/2). An every-epsilon L2 exponent
2gamma<3/2 is impossible for THIS source. The gamma=3/4 boundary,
weaker L1 bounds and different b remain eligible.

The review improves the actual tail by keeping its cutoff correction:

    Q_(q,b)(X,M)=(d_q X^b/2) integral_1^2
                         u^(b-1)exp(-2M/(X^b u^b))du,
    D_>M=Q_(q,b)(X,M)+O_(q,b)(X^(b/2)).

Stieltjes integration on(M,infinity) includes the boundary error
sqrt(M)exp(-lambda M) and the integral of lambda sqrt(t)exp(-lambda t),
both O(lambda^-1/2), uniformly in M. Therefore at M=X^(4/3), b=3/2,k=6,

    E(X)=E_<=M(X)+Q_(q,3/2)(X,M)+O_q(X^(3/4)),
    E_>M(X)=Q_(q,3/2)(X,M)+O_q(X^(3/4)).

The cross exponent2/3 has room to absorb its logarithm. Replacing Q
prematurely by C X^(3/2) would lose a correction of order X^(4/3).

There is also a log-free UPPER norm bound on the original sharp shell.
Let h(t)=0 for t<=0, h(t)=10t^3-15t^4+6t^5 for0<t<1 and h(t)=1 for
t>=1. Then phi(u)=h(2u-1)h((4-u)/2) is nonnegative C^2, supported
on[1/2,4] and equal1 on[1,2]. Majorize the COMPLETE squared tail by
its phi-weighted integral. Its transformed amplitude and first derivative
vanish at endpoints, and its L1/second-derivative L1 norms are uniform
in A>=0, since A-polynomials are multiplied by exp(-cA). Two integrations
by parts give |K_phi(n,m)|<< (1+|n^k-m^k|/X^k)^-2. With
delta_n=X^k/n^(k-1), sum_(h>=1)min(1,(delta_n/h)^2)<<delta_n.
Thus, with all coefficients and the original sharp shell still present,

    ||W_>M||_2^2 <<_(b,k) X^b+X^k M^(2-k).

This proves E(X)<<X^2+X^b generically by taking M=X. It removes the
logarithm from an upper norm, not from the earlier sharp signed identity.
The bounded array a_n=1 for n<=floor(X/2), zero otherwise, gives E>>X^2
at b=3/2,k=6. This shell-dependent array is a generic obstruction,
not a lower bound for actual Möbius coefficients.

## G143. Divisor-erasure recovery with literal coprimality and two prices

Fix an ordinary complex Dirichlet character chi modulo q. For integer N
and 1<=Y<=N/2 let S be the squarefree q-units through N, E={n in S:n<=Y},
H=S minus E, and a_n=mu(n)chi(n). The other integers retain their actual
squareful/nonunit zeros. The full convolution a*chi=delta_1 gives

    sum_(d in H,d|m) chi(m/d)a_d=b_m,
    b_m=-sum_(d in E,d|m)mu(d)chi(d)chi(m/d),  m in H.

H is convex inside every divisor interval between two of its elements.
Consequently the triangular matrix Z_(m,d)=chi(m/d)1_(d|m) has inverse
mu(m/d)chi(m/d)1_(d|m). Its matrix product reduces to
chi(m/d)sum_(e|m/d)mu(e); no general principal-submatrix inversion is used.
Summing the inverse columns gives the unique scalar dual

    lambda_m=sum_(k<=N/m,(k,m)=1)mu(k)chi(k),
    M_chi(N)=M_chi(Y)+sum_(m in H)lambda_m b_m.          (88.1)

This final contraction is bilinear, with no conjugate. The moving
coprimality is forced by squarefreeness of the multiple mk. At
Y=floor(sqrt N) every dual has short argument, but the entire m range
through N and every exposed divisor in b_m remain.

For independent row errors bounded by1, the exact scalar norm is
K_(N,Y)=sum_H|lambda_m|. Triangle gives the upper bound; errors
conj(lambda_m)/|lambda_m| attain it. Every m in S with m>N/2 has
lambda_m=1. The elementary square-divisor count

    Q_q(x)=#S_x=kappa_q x+O_q(sqrt x),
    kappa_q=(phi(q)/q) product_(p not dividing q)(1-p^-2)>0

therefore gives kappa_q N/2-O_q(sqrt N)<=K_(N,Y)<=N(1+log N).
Adding all convolution rows through N, including squareful rows and
known zeros, does not remove this terminal price: the column of an
unknown m>N/2 occurs only in its own row, with coefficient1. Every exact
linear certificate must assign1 to that row. Weighted independent errors
w_m have exact price sum_H|lambda_m|w_m, including all terminal weights.
This result concerns that linear error formulation, not multiplicative
perturbations of the source or nonlinear arithmetic constraints.

There is a separate actual-source result. Put P_N=sum_H|lambda_m b_m|
and permit any cutoff sequence1<=Y_N<=N/2. Each unramified prime
N/2<p<=N has lambda_p=1 and b_p=-chi(p). Thus P_N dominates the number
of those primes, while

    P_N<=N sum_(m<=N)tau(m)/m<=N(1+log N)^2.

If P_N=O(N^alpha) for some alpha<1 at all large N, dyadic intervals
N=2^j would make sum_p1/p converge. Euler's elementary finite-product
argument forbids that: bounded product_(p<=T)(1-1/p)^-1 would dominate
the divergent partial harmonic sums. Removing finitely many ramified
primes changes nothing. Hence

    limsup_(N->infinity) log P_N/log N=1                (88.2)

for every such cutoff sequence, with log0=-infinity. This is neither a
pointwise linear lower bound nor a lower bound on the signed sum(88.1).
It rules out the full absolute-payment strategy on the actual source.

The particular moving prime omissions can be paid without a fictitious
growing-conductor theorem. For any m and T,

    sum_(k<=T,(k,m)=1)mu(k)chi(k)
      =sum_(r<=T, p|r implies p|m)chi(r)M_chi(T/r).     (88.3)

Every power of a prime dividing m is included in r. If the fixed-character
bound |M_chi(t)|<=Ct^alpha is available,0<alpha<1, its price is

    CT^alpha product_(p|m)(1-p^-alpha)^-1
      <=CT^alpha exp(O_alpha((log(2N))^(1-alpha)))

uniformly for m<=N. Split at log(2N), bound the small primes by all
integers and the number of large prime divisors by log N/log2. This is
N^o(1), but summing absolute prices still cannot beat(88.2).

The surviving OPEN-E9 target is the complete signed sum in(88.1), with
Y=floor(sqrt N), bounded by N^(gamma+epsilon) for every epsilon>0, every
fixed ordinary chi and all large N, with one common1/2<gamma<theta11.
The exposed sector costs at most sqrt N. Thus this target is exponent-
equivalent to the full M bound; it is not claimed to be a weaker premise.
Targets gamma=.8748,5/6,3/4 all have room for that exposed sector.
Any model must bound its own complete contraction and the full signed
model residual, with terminal rows, coprimality and phases retained.

A proved full M bound defines
F_chi(s)=s integral_1^infinity M_chi(x)x^(-s-1)dx holomorphically on
Re s>gamma, locally uniformly with every fixed derivative. Initially
Re s>1 it is1/L(s,chi). Periodic partial sums continue nonprincipal L
to Re s>0; the elementary zeta integral gives the principal simple pole.
Continuation of LF=1 excludes all zeros at every height in Re s>gamma.
At the principal pole F has the appropriate zero; omitted imprimitive
Euler factors have zeros only on Re s=0. This return is conditional on
the complete all-scale fixed-character estimate, which is OPEN.

## G144. A regular-residue cover cannot repair the weighted Euler trace

The augmented squarefree q-unit cutoff complex has a basis e_S for
product n(S)<=X, including the empty face, graded by|S|. Oriented
deletion d and D_chi e_S=chi(n(S))e_S give Str(D_chi)=M_chi(X), but

    [D_chi,d]e_S=sum_(p in S)orientation(p,S)
                       chi(n(S)/p)(1-chi(p))e_(S minus p).

Distinct deletions have distinct target faces. A local deletion commuting
with D_chi must vanish whenever chi(p)!=1; assigning a phase does not
remove this defect. The proposed regular-register cover uses(S,g),
g in (Z/qZ)^*, and deletes p by(S,g)->(S minus p,gp). The conserved
coordinate h=g n(S) conjugates it exactly to d tensor I. Its character
Fourier sector is D_chi^-1 d D_chi with one basis vector per face.
Its Euler index is the principal M_chi0(X), independently of chi.
For q=3,X=5, the allowed faces1,2,5 have index-1, while actual M_chi=3.
The commuting insertion chi(h) has trace0 on the full regular register
for nonprincipal chi. Anchoring g=1 restores the signal but loses the
chain condition. This is an explicit counterexample to this cover/readout,
not to different chain groups or nonlocal signed interactions.

The existing cone/prime-toggle repair remains useful with its full defect.
Let ell be the least prime not dividing q. Faces without ell and product
<=X/ell, together with their ell cones, form a contractible subcomplex.
Every boundary face of a critical ell-free face in(X/ell,X] lies there.
Let h insert ell on the eligible faces and define P e_S=e_S-hd e_S on
critical faces, P=0 on the cone. Then P^2=P,dP=Pd=0,dh+hd=I-P, and

    Str(D_chi)=Str(D_chi P)+Str([D_chi,d]h)
      =B(X)+(1-chi(ell))A(X/ell),
    A(Y)=sum_(n<=Y,ell not dividing n)mu(n)chi(n),
    B(X)=A(X)-A(X/ell).

P is not just the diagonal critical-face indicator; its hd correction
is necessary. Full telescoping gives

    M_chi(X)=B(X)+(1-chi(ell))sum_(j>=1)B(X/ell^j).

At positive exponent alpha its cost is
1+|1-chi(ell)|/(ell^alpha-1), after a finite head. Conversely
A(X)=sum_(j>=0)chi(ell)^j M_chi(X/ell^j), so B has the same full
exponent as M. No character-weighted arithmetic gain is supplied.

The unsigned critical rank is
kappa_(q ell)(1-1/ell)X+O_q(sqrt X), equal to2X/pi^2+O(sqrt X)
for q=1. The long exact relative-homology sequence gives
b(K_X,K_Y)>=b(K_X)-b(K_Y) for total reduced Betti dimension. Along
any finite increasing filtration the sum of these unsigned relative
masses is at least final mass minus initial mass. An initial o(X) mass
therefore leaves a linear complete price, even for a changing filtration.
Signed interactions across annuli are outside that obstruction.

This section credits W27/G74/G76 and W53-W56 cone, character and
reconstruction ancestry. Its new test is the precise regular-cover
failure, with the full valid repair retained rather than relabeled new.

## G145. Full-word and sorted-creation commutators have different returns

In the full free-word lift, all k! orders of an integer's distinct primes
have the same phase. Abelianization maps each word to that integer.
Adjacent-transposition differences span its zero-sum kernel: the
permutation graph is connected, and a spanning tree has k!-1 independent
differences. The hard product cutoff retains entire fibers, so integer
evaluation annihilates every such within-fiber commutator. For positive
word weights w_v, beta_n=sum_(v in fiber n)1/w_v, the least squared lift
norm is sum_n|a_n|^2/beta_n and evaluator norm squared is sum_n beta_n.
Their product is at least(#S)^2. This is the existing G117 price;
cross-integer correlations remain eligible.

The existing B22 sorted-prime space has a different, nonzero commutator.
For fixed sigma>1/2 define on increasing unramified prime words

    A_p e_n=chi(p)p^-sigma e_(np) if p>P+(n), else0,
    T=sum_(p not dividing q)A_p,  P+(1)=1.

Different parents have disjoint r-step descendants, so
||T^r||^2<=S_sigma^r/r!, S_sigma=sum_(p not dividing q)p^-2sigma<infinity.
Hence the norm-convergent Neumann inverse gives
v_sigma=(I+T)^-1 e_1, with coordinate mu(n)chi(n)n^-sigma.
For p<r, A_p A_r=0. Thus, with[A,B]=AB-BA,

    C=sum_(p<r)[A_r,A_p]=T^2.

The infinite sum is defined through finite prime cutoffs: their C_P=T_P^2
converges in norm since ||T-T_P||^2<=sum_(p>P)p^-2sigma. Compression
to n<=N preserves the same identity because intermediate products never
exceed the final product. With Lambda_(N,sigma)u=sum_(n<=N)n^sigma u_n,

    M_chi(N)=1-sum_(p<=N)chi(p)+Lambda_(N,sigma)(C v_sigma). (88.4)

The final term is exactly the contribution with at least two prime
factors. It must cancel the prime term; a small norm of C alone does
not do so. Only an estimate for the complete scalar(88.4) gives the
all-scale M return. The source/operator construction is credited to B22;
the complete commutator/source accounting is the present adaptation.

Fixed fractional logarithmic regularity cannot pay the arithmetic gap.
For ||u||_s^2=sum_n(1+log n)^(2s)|u_n|^2 and fixed real s, v_sigma
belongs to every such space, while partial summation against Q_q gives

    ||Lambda_(N,sigma)||_(s,dual)^2
      ~kappa_q N^(2sigma+1)/((2sigma+1)(log N)^(2s)).

Its limiting power is still sigma+1/2>1. More generally every positive
diagonal weight w_(n,N), even chosen separately for each N, obeys

    sqrt(sum_(n in S)w_(n,N)|v_sigma(n)|^2)
      sqrt(sum_(n in S)n^(2sigma)/w_(n,N))>=#S.

This is a price for a product of norms, not a signed M lower bound.
Non-diagonal correlations and source-specific boundary estimates remain
open, with their complete return to be proved.
title: G145. Full-word and sorted-creation commutators have different returns

## G146. The complete prefix is paid over the original slot interval

Use the original sixth-power-free natural rows, all unit sectors, finite
dictionary, one complete orientation and original nonnegative row majorant.
The actual product Q_u of prime slots retains its canonical pools, relative
ray coefficients, smooth profiles, bounded real powers, independent heights,
fixed punctures and natural zeros. Shared primes are allowed. No new mask,
moving conductor or arbitrary inverse coefficient is licensed.

Set

    17/25 <= delta <= 7/10, a=(1+delta)/2, 0<=v<=1/20,
    K=28114053/6250000, t=33/25, lambda=1/2500,
    eta=1/1000, R=U^t, L=U^(t+lambda), Y=U^B.

K retains its preceding-family ancestry; it is not recomputed from c11.
The physical bin gives |Q_u|^2 << H_J U^(delta v+epsilon).
H_J denotes the retained finite seminorm and polynomial-height factors.
All numerical cutoffs precede live rows. Fixed inducing exceptions are
paid separately below.

For the original V, equal to one on [0,1] and zero on [2,infinity), put

    A_R(n)=sum_(d|n) mu(d)V(Nd/R),
    D_R,u(s)=sum_(Nn>R) phi_u(n)A_R(n)(Nn)^(-s)e^(-Nn/Y),
    P_R,u(s)=sum_(Nn>R) phi_u(n)A_R(n)(Nn)^(-s)
                                    e^(-Nn/Y)H(Nn/L),
    F_R,u=D_R,u-P_R,u,

where H is fixed, one on [0,1] and compactly supported. The character is
the actual attaining natural presentation. A principal inducing character
with extra zeros is not a nonprincipal presentation.

The completed identity from [restricted research revision] Section6 applies to every fixed bounded t:
at an actual nonprincipal zero, D_R,u(rho_u)=-1+O(U^(-A_tail)). Mellin
inversion of the exponential and a contour shift from 2 to -1/4 give this
identity. The Gamma residue at zero vanishes; no L-pole is crossed.
The finite inverse polynomial and ordinary Hecke strip bounds have fixed
polynomial costs, paid by choosing B afterward. The unit is e^(-1/Y)
before being isolated. The terminal cutoff at U^(B+1) and its finite
derivative tails are paid before raw row/slot amplification. This value
identity asserts no vanishing derivative at a zero.

For every nonunit ideal n, with no coprimality or squarefree assumption,

    A_R(n)=-sum_(dm=n) mu(d)[1-V(Nd/R)].                 (1)

The unit is excluded from (1). Thus P is an inverse sum with complementary
cofactor Nm << L/R. Define N0(P) as its complete positive tensor Sobolev
norm over the original free rows, real interval [a,1] and enlarged height
box, with derivatives partial_sigma^i partial_tau^j, i,j in {0,1}.
The fixed real width is bounded below. Then

    N0(P) << H_J U^(J_t+epsilon),
    J_t=1/6+(5/6-delta)t+(1-delta)lambda.               (2)

Here are the costs in (2). For a fixed cofactor m, inverse dyads have
R << D << L/Nm. Separate the coupled smooth profile on its full ambient
box before a live cofactor, row or height is chosen, as in PR9 B3.3.
Freeze the original R inside that profile during inverse-scale restoration.
The centrally normalized inverse moment is U^(1/6)D^(5/6+epsilon);
d^(-s) contributes D^(-delta) in its square. Since 5/6-delta>0,
Hilbert triangle over dyads is dominated by D~L/Nm. The outside character
is a contraction even at shared primes and natural zeros. The norm is at most

    H_J^(1/2) U^(1/12+epsilon)L^((5/6-delta)/2)
                 sum_(Nm<<L/R) (Nm)^(-11/12).

The exponent is exactly -a-(5/6-delta)/2=-11/12. Ideal counting including
the unit gives (L/R)^(1/12); squaring yields (2). Finite derivatives cost
logarithms and the same fixed height factors. No cofactor cancellation is
assumed. Positive evaluation bounds the rows with |P(rho_u)|>=1/4;
only afterward apply the physical slot bound. Their weighted count is
O(H_J U^(J_t+delta v+epsilon)). This is not a bound for the full marked
ambient norm with a cheaper coefficient than its licensed 5v/3.

Retain the [restricted research revision] density envelope

    h=5-2delta, rho=1-10delta/(3h), k=rho+delta-1,
    D_K=15K-10-6Kdelta,
    a_K=delta(5-6delta)^2/(3h D_K),
    b_K=2delta(5-6delta)(K-1)/D_K,
    G=min(3kv,a_K+b_K v), E_K=rho+delta v-G.

Throughout the closed delta/v rectangle,

    E_K-J_t-delta v > eta.                             (3)

It suffices to replace G by a_K+b_K/20. After subtracting eta and
multiplying by the positive 3h D_K, substitute delta=17/25+x/50.
The cubic Bernstein coefficients are

    31963522910683/488281250000000,
    51570739970441/146484375000000,
    2180434156111/3662109375000,
    97268801733/122070312500,

all positive. This is a continuous-interval argument, not a sampled grid.
The earlier t=4/3 failure at delta=17/25,v=1/20,lambda=0 remains
`-228190682/298987653375`. The replacement t pays this whole slot range
by changing the detector for the same counted problem. No ambient
comparison between the old and new far polynomials is asserted.

## G147. Two presentations confine the unpaid rows to a strict residual box

Outside the prefix exception, |F_R,u(rho_u)|>=1/2. A fixed product-annulus
partition therefore supplies X=U^ell with signal at least U^(-small).
On the same nonunit annulus and with the same common weight W_X,

    T_X,u=sum_(d,m) mu(d)phi_u(d)phi_u(m)(Ndm)^(-s)
                                      V(Nd/R)W_X(Ndm)
         =-sum_(d,m) mu(d)phi_u(d)phi_u(m)(Ndm)^(-s)
                                  [1-V(Nd/R)]W_X(Ndm). (4)

Complete multiplicativity includes zero values. The inverse arithmetic
coefficient in either presentation remains mu(d)phi_u(d). Split d,m into
fixed dyads. Common-profile separation yields one Fourier coordinate
within each inverse/plain pair; the two presentations may select different
coordinates and dyads. Both use the same actual character, zero and real
part, and their lengths obey r_-+m_-=r_++m_+=ell+o(1), with
r_-<=t+o(1) and r_+>=t-o(1).

The internal/physical-bin distinction is essential. Use [restricted research revision]'s internal
buffered construction and select its attaining zero before either
extraction. Its exponent delta_b can exceed .70 but is at least
delta-O(buffer). It is never substituted into the physical slot price
or E_K. The source product lower bound and actual-bin pointwise bounds are

    |M(U^r)S(U^m)|^2 >= U^(delta_b ell-small),
    |M(U^r)|^2 <= U^(delta_b r+small),
    |S(U^m)|^2 <= U^(delta_b min(m,1-m)+small).

They first force m<=1/2+small, including initially long product annuli.
Then divide by the other factor and weaken delta_b to delta to obtain

    |M_±|^2 >= U^(delta r_±-small),
    |S_±|^2 >= U^(delta m_±-small).                    (5)

The zero may differ from the initially selected physical-bin zero. Both
pairs still use the same internal attaining zero. Its real part is at
least a-O(buffer), so the prefix norm remains applicable with an arbitrarily
small loss. The incumbent zero-free bound keeps its real part in a compact
subset of (1/2,1). No upper assumption delta_b<=.70 is introduced.

Choose finite moment/profile/Sobolev degrees before the internal height
power. Inflate a small supplied witness height to the prescribed internal
power box, putting both Fourier coordinates within its buffered extension;
the fixed polynomial cost fits the allocated small loss. Completion B and
raw tail powers are fixed before the final small buffers and threshold.
Rapid Fourier decay pays the genuine tails under B3.3. Large heights use
the absolute row/slot count and a larger fixed H_J. Original slot heights
and their physical-bin bound are unchanged. These conventions preserve
the source's threshold before live height rather than claiming arbitrary
conductor/profile uniformity.

The licensed marginal count exponents from (5) are

    I(r)=max(1,(1+5r)/6)-delta r,
    P(m)=1-2delta m.

I uses the free inverse moment; P uses the zero-slot fourth plain moment,
not an unproved positive-slot variant. Fixed masks, relative characters
and whole orientations retain B3.40-41/[restricted research revision]/[restricted research revision]'s actual contracts.
After these positive counts, add the physical price delta v.

Put e=rho-G-eta, q=5/6-delta and

    A=(1-e)/delta, C=(e-1/6)/q.

Then I(r)<=e on [A,C], including its change at r=1, and P(m)<=e for
m>=A/2. Exact interval certificates give

    A<47/50<1<t<C, C-A>3/8, 3A/2-C<3/40,
    C-A/2>17/20.

Pay the union of every easy inverse/plain witness in both presentations.
Crucially, freeze BOTH the original product-profile family and the family
with its exponential replaced by one before making this union or any
rowwise selection. Fixed finite choices, dyads and continuous parameters
are paid by the retained partitions and Sobolev estimates. A padding
p=10^(-6) and the independent certificates with eight pads include the
boundaries; the remaining aggregate losses can be chosen below eta/2.

Every row outside this union has, up to the paid small endpoint losses,

    C<ell<3A/2,
    ell-A<m_-<A/2, 0<=m_+<ell-C,
    r_+-r_->C-A.

In particular the strict coarse box is

    .85<r_-<.94, .375<m_-<.47,
    1.32<r_+<1.41, 0<=m_+<.075,
    r_+-r_->.375,
    r_-+m_-=r_++m_++o(1).                             (6)

This follows continuously across the rectangle: replace e by
e_min=rho-a_K-b_K/20-eta. Increasing e decreases A and increases C.
Clearing the positive denominators gives polynomials of degree at most
four. The retained independent rational receipt supplies all Bernstein
coefficients, including the five direct/padded endpoint checks.

The prefix inequality also gives

    C-(t+lambda)>lambda/(6q)>=1/2300.                  (7)

Hence H is exactly zero on the selected residual annulus for large U.
V is one on the short inverse dyad, and 1-V is one on the long dyad.
Remove the exponential only AFTER locating ell<1.41. Per row, including
the finite derivatives, its difference from one costs
H_J U^((2-a)1.41-B+epsilon), by the divisor bound and ideal count.
Squaring and paying O(U) rows and absolute slot price U^v gives exponent
`10803/2500-2B`. Choose B>A_tail+10 and any larger contour requirement.
The error then has any required negative power after every raw cost.

Now re-extract both presentations with the exponential-free family on
the SAME product annulus. A new easy witness would already be in the
paid union; otherwise (6) applies again and the new inverse dyads have
the asserted constant cutoffs. Dyads and Fourier frequencies need not
match the first extraction. This proves ordinary annular inverse
profiles without a circular rowwise profile choice. Removing V from the
complete divisor sum would annihilate every nonunit coefficient and is
not a permissible simplification.

Let B_hi be the original physical high-row set. Let B_sep be the residual
subset admitting (5)-(6) with these exponential-free compatible profiles.
Then the proved counted reduction is

    sum_(u in B_hi)|Q_u|^2
      << H_J U^(E_K-1/2000+epsilon)
         +sum_(u in B_sep)|Q_u|^2.                    (8)

The first term pays the complete prefix, all easy witnesses in BOTH
families/presentations, too-long annuli, genuine terminal/Fourier tails,
finite dictionary/internal-bin labels, dyadic/supremum/derivative costs
and bounded nonempty subunit windows. The final paid margin is 1/2000;
the algebraic eta is not reported as an unspent final saving.

Fixed-bad-prime free cores have finitely many unit/valuation sectors,
with absolute slot mass O_fixed(H_J U^(v+epsilon)). A fixed finite list
of their raw sixth-power restorations costs at most U^(1/6+v+epsilon).
Both fit (8), since E_K>=rho>=19/54 and
delta-3k=4delta^2/(5-2delta)>0, with rho>1/6+1/20+eta.
This does not prove an arbitrary raw moving-support transfer. Actual
root holes, normalizations and positive-child width restrictions remain
obligations of any subsequent full density return.

The same result holds for EVERY fixed t in [11/10,33/25], selected before
rows. J_t increases with t, while A,C do not depend on it; A<.94<1.1<=t<C
and the gap (7) is worst at the upper endpoint. The inverse dyads remain
above exponent1 and completion permits each fixed t. Constants may
depend on the fixed choice; this is not live-row optimization.

## G148. The unresolved joint estimate and the exact dependence obstruction

OPEN-SEP would bound the actual B_sep mass in (8) by
H_J U^(E_K-xi+epsilon), uniformly in its source quantifiers for some xi>0.
It would give the smaller of xi and 1/2000 after allocating losses.
It is unproved; a c gain also needs the complete raw/positive-child and
physical endpoint return.

A stronger sufficient OPEN-MIX is

    sum_(clean natural free u)|M_-(U^r_-)|^2
                       |M_+(U^r_+)|^2 |Q_u|^2
      << H_J U^(delta(r_-+r_+)+E_K-xi+epsilon).        (9)

It must cover all compatible profiles in (6), the same actual natural
character, one common real parameter and TWO independent inverse heights.
The finite Sobolev derivatives must dominate rowwise suprema. Its positive
row majorant precedes any zero predicate; only the fixed inducing
exceptions already paid above may be omitted. The actual slots, their
relative phases and zero extensions remain. Divide (9) by both inverse
witness lower bounds, never by a possibly zero slot.

Old MI does not supply (9). The merged inverses have a two-divisor
coefficient, schematically mu*mu, with their profiles and shared primes.
It is not the canonical one-inverse column permitted by B3.6. Divisor
boundedness or separated lengths alone cannot grant that source theorem.

Nor do the marginal scalar bounds already force a gain. At v=0 choose

    ell=5/(5-2delta), r_-=2ell/3, m_-=ell/3,
    r_+=ell, m_+=0.

All three relevant marginal exponents equal rho:

    1-delta r_-=1-2delta m_-
               =1/6+(5/6-delta)r_+.

These lengths lie strictly in (6) and outside the easy set at e=rho-eta.
This is a feasible scalar exponent model, not an arithmetic realization
or a counterexample to (9).

Finally, the two full annular sums without the minus sign in (4) obey
T_<+T_>=0 coefficient by coefficient. Against a common nonnegative row
weight their covariance is exactly -||T_<||^2. Multiplying marginal
rarities as if the constructions were independent is therefore invalid.
This exact dependence itself supplies no cancellation saving: both
completed detectors still carry the same constant signal at a zero.
The useful next task is a source-specific joint estimate retaining that
dependence and all shared-prime terms.

No old signed R22 sector or prefix/far cross term has been removed.
Both physical projectors, clipped rectangles, actual label/missing-radical
counts, shortened scales/zero capacity, Euler shifts, extracted errors,
FI/zero/low/far-high branches, raw-root tails, 6a/9a radii,
K_phys^(5/6), principal residue and common-Delta feedback remain under
their existing contracts. The centered M/24 reserve is unspent.

The independent helper's thirteen interval certificates have 53 positive
Bernstein coefficients and three exact identities. Root read the complete
author/review/helpers, certificates and relevant source contracts without
rerunning unchanged helpers. Finite divisor/zero diagnostics are distinct
from the written infinite proof and establish no OPEN-MIX estimate.
Both original lanes stopped and released their own claims. The full
29-family/109-child portfolio, later ideas, near gains,1/6 and1/4 remain.

# [private research revision]: complete operator returns and an actual detector repair

Root accepts G149–G151 at the scopes below, after full author and independent
review reads. The written analytic endpoint remains
`c11=312864909/2500000000=.1251459636`, with boundary
`gamma11=.8748540364`. No arithmetic power saving is proved in this cycle.
The useful additions are a complete off-diagonal Hankel return, a fully
priced matching return and an actual two-variable detector whose principal
branch obstruction can be repaired exactly. These distinguish workable
interfaces from assumptions that would already solve the old problem.

The [author](wild58/report.md), [independent review](wild58-review/report.md)
and [retention manifest](retention-manifest.json) preserve all thirty seeds,
six author tests, three developments and two independent audits. Thirty-three
frozen files and thirteen mathematical source pins match their original
bytes. Actual host-local claims are excluded. The original 29-family/109-child
portfolio and later additions remain intact. F0/analytic ancestry,
positive-slot uniformity and external definition/import/admission remain open.
There is no formalization, kernel replay, new proof packet or public record claim.

## G149. The full logarithmic Hankel growth criterion

Fix an ordinary Dirichlet character chi, with squareful and ramified zeros
kept literally, and put

    M(x) = sum_(n<=x) mu(n) chi(n),       M(x)=0 for x<1,
    h_a(v) = exp(-a v) M(exp(v)),         v>=0, 0<a<1.

Let Gamma_(a,L) be the full Hankel operator on L2(0,L) with kernel h_a(t+u),
and K_a(L) its operator norm. For complex chi use the bounded bilinear form

    B_a(f,g) = integral integral h_a(t+u) f(t) g(u) dt du.

Conjugating one test input identifies its norm with the usual operator
norm. It does not conjugate chi or replace the arithmetic source by an
absolute value. Both variables and every off-diagonal rectangle are present.

If sup_L K_a(L)<infinity, density extends B_a to L2(0,infinity) twice.
For Re(z)>0 the vector E_z(t)=exp(-zt) is holomorphic with
norm squared 1/(2Re(z)). Consequently Q(z)=B_a(E_z,E_z) is holomorphic,
and initially for s=a+z, Re(s)>1, absolute convergence gives

    Q(z) = integral_0^infinity v M(exp(v)) exp(-s v) dv
         = -d/ds [1/(s L(s,chi))].                         (G149.1)

A zero rho of L with Re(rho)>a would give a pole of the derivative on the
right. Since a>0, rho is not zero; its pole cannot be removed by the factor
s or by differentiation. Meromorphic identity continuation contradicts
the holomorphy of Q. The principal-character pole instead gives a zero of
1/L and causes no false obstruction. The conclusion covers every fixed
finite height and the literal imprimitive L function. Constants may depend
on the fixed character; no growing-conductor or height-uniform growth
estimate has been inferred.

### Every rectangular block is paid

This is the substantive completion of the growth adapter. Write I_j=[j,j+1).
Opposite translations send the I_i by I_j rectangle to the square
[(i+j)/2,(i+j)/2+1) in both coordinates, preserving t+u. Therefore the
unweighted block norm is at most K_a((i+j)/2+1). Passing to a heavier
weight sigma>a multiplies it by at most exp(-(sigma-a)(i+j)). If

    K_a(L) <= C exp(2 eta L),       eta>=0, all L>0,

the sum of the norms of all blocks is bounded by

    C exp(2 eta) [1-exp(-(sigma-a-eta))]^(-2),
    provided sigma>a+eta.                                  (G149.2)

The sum is a deliberately coarse sufficient bound for the full bilinear
form: each block input norm is bounded by the norm of its complete input.
It includes arbitrarily unbalanced rectangles, not only a diagonal strip.
Apply (G149.1) at the heavier weight, taking sigma<1 when needed. Thus for
one fixed 0<a<=gamma<1 the complete hypothesis

    K_a(L) <<_(chi,epsilon) exp(2(gamma-a+epsilon)L)
    for every epsilon>0 and all L>0                         (OPEN-HK)

for every fixed ordinary character excludes all L zeros in Re(s)>gamma.
For any desired sigma>gamma choose epsilon<sigma-gamma first. Values
above one are already in the absolute Euler-product domain; arbitrarily
small positive margins cover the boundary. Alternatively uniformly bounded
Hankel forms for a sequence a decreasing to gamma give the same return.

At a=1/2, the current first-gain threshold for the exponential growth
coefficient is strictly less than .7497080728. The candidate gamma=.87485
would require coefficient .7497 and return c=.12515, a gain .0000040364.
The 1/6 and 1/4 targets require coefficients 2/3 and 1/2. These are
conditional targets. The elementary |M(x)|<=x gives coefficient
2(1-a), namely one at a=1/2, and supplies no gain.

### What can and cannot supply that estimate

The exact Hilbert–Schmidt square is

    integral_0^(2L) w_L(v) exp(-2av) |M(exp(v))|^2 dv,
    w_L(v)=v for v<=L, and 2L-v for L<=v<=2L.

Bounding this positive energy reimports the familiar complete energy
problem. Operator norm can in principle be smaller: the nonarithmetic
kernel exp(i(t+u)^2) has operator norm at most sqrt(pi), by extension and
Plancherel at frequency 2t, whereas its Hilbert–Schmidt norm is L. This
functional example supplies no estimate for mu(n)chi(n).

For the single model kernel R exp(lambda(t+u)), the singular value is
|R| integral_0^L exp(2Re(lambda)t)dt. Critical modes grow linearly and
unstable modes exponentially. This is not a license to decompose or truncate
an infinite arithmetic pole expansion without paying the complement.

The exact arithmetic form also reads

    B_a(f,g) = sum_n mu(n)chi(n)
               integral_(t+u>=log n) exp(-a(t+u))f(t)g(u)dtdu

for compactly supported inputs. Extending h_a by zero to the negative line,

    (partial_v+a) h_a = sum_n mu(n)chi(n)n^(-a) delta_(log n).

The atom at n=1 is retained. On compactly supported smooth inputs in the
positive half-line its pairing with f*g is a B_a(f,g)-B_a(f',g).
This gives an H1 by L2 bound from the Hankel bound, not a converse or a
native H estimate. Credit the broad operator/observability and reciprocal
return ancestry, including [W29](../creative/round29-review.md),
[W50 energy](../[private research revision]/wild50-integration.md) and
[W54 prediction](../[private research revision]/wild54-integration.md). The new credit is the
specific complete source interface and its balanced-block growth return.

## G150. Complete matching displacement, with the old rank equivalence retained

Let V have basis the squarefree q-units n<=X, parity mu(n), and all diagonal
character actions W_chi(n)=chi(n). An odd differential d with d squared
zero commuting with every character must preserve each reduced residue
class: the characters separate that finite group. Write E_a,O_a for the
two parity counts and I_a=E_a-O_a. Hodge decomposition then gives

    dim ker(dd*+d*d) >= R_q(X) := sum_a |I_a(X)|.

Matching min(E_a,O_a) opposite signs within each residue attains equality;
unit arrows give nonzero spectral gap one. The gap alone says nothing
about the residual rank. Orthogonality gives the exact comparisons

    max_chi |M_chi(X)| <= R_q(X) <= sum_chi |M_chi(X)|
                                      <= phi(q) max_chi |M_chi(X)|.

These are already [[private research revision] G135](../[private research revision]/wild55-integration.md).
Do not count this reformulation as a new weaker arithmetic prerequisite.
For example q=5,X=80 has residue indices (0,-3,-4,1), hence minimum rank
eight; a fourteen-state rank of a particular construction is not universal.

For one neutral prime r=1 mod q, the exact pairing m with rm, r not
dividing m, has residual rank

    d_q (r-1)/(r+1) X + O_(q,r)(sqrt(X)),
    d_q = zeta(2)^(-1) product_(p|q) p/(p+1).

The square-divisor expansion proves the squarefree q-unit count
d_q X+O_q(sqrt(X)). If only one chi is being preserved, chi(r)=1 suffices;
otherwise the multiplier 1-chi(r) must remain. This linear-rank obstruction
belongs to the named neutral-prime rule, not to every differential.

### A full future-partner return

In each reduced residue class there are infinitely many negative squarefree
integers (primes) and positive ones (a fixed r=1 mod q times different
primes in that class). Only infinitude of primes in each reduced progression
is imported here; see [NIST DLMF 27.11.9](https://dlmf.nist.gov/27.11.E9).
No prime-distribution error estimate is used. Thus a fixed global
same-residue pairing of the two signs exists. Orient each pair (u,v) by
mu(u)=1, mu(v)=-1 and set a=min(u,v), b=max(u,v). Define

    D_q(X) = sum_(X<=a<2X) (b-a),       X=1,2,4,... .

Every future partner is included, even when b is much larger than 2X.
For a common 0<gamma<1, the full hypothesis

    D_q(X) <<_(q,epsilon) X^(1+gamma+epsilon)
    for every epsilon>0 and every fixed q                 (OPEN-D)

implies ordinary zero exclusion in Re(s)>gamma. Indeed, initially Re(s)>1,
absolute regrouping gives

    1/L(s,chi) = sum_pairs chi(u)(u^(-s)-v^(-s)).

For sigma=Re(s)>0 the difference is bounded by
|s|(b-a)a^(-sigma-1). Summing dyadic shells with epsilon below a compact
set's horizontal margin gives normal convergence on Re(s)>gamma. The
identity L F=1 continues meromorphically, excluding zeros and permitting
the reciprocal zero at a principal pole. All fixed finite heights and the
literal imprimitive factors are covered; no uniform growth assertion follows.

Monotone same-residue pairing has crossing count R_q(t). Tonelli identifies
the total *clipped* interval length in [A,B] with integral_A^B R_q(t)dt.
That is not the complete D_q(A): omitted future portions and intervals
entering from earlier shells matter. Under G135's existing summatory/rank
bound with gamma>1/2, endpoints grow proportionally to their rank k and
pair displacement is O(k^(gamma+epsilon)); the complete D bound follows.
This adapter has not evaded the original arithmetic difficulty.

The global neutral-prime rule has the unconditional full cost

    D_q(X) = (r-1) sum_(X<=m<2X,(m,qr)=1) mu(m)^2 m
           = (3/2)(r-1)d_(qr) X^2 + O_(q,r)(X^(3/2)).

Partial summation of the squarefree count proves it, with the positive main
coefficient intact. Thus this rule cannot meet the positive-cost target for
any gamma<1. Other matchings or signed displacement estimates remain open.
Near/1/6/1/4 cost exponents are respectively below1.8748540364,11/6,7/4.
The new useful bill is complete future-partner cost and this actual rule's
failure; G135, W01 signed transport and [private research revision] priced coupling retain credit.

## G151. An actual two-variable repair and two fully priced detector interfaces

### The squarefree lift and its principal branch obstruction

Define, initially Re(s),Re(t)>1,

    F_chi(s,t) = sum_(m,n>=1) c(m,n)m^(-s)n^(-t),
    c(m,n) = mu(mn)chi(mn)2^(-omega(mn)),

with zero coefficient when mn is not squarefree. Natural ramified zeros,
the prime two when unramified, and c(1,1)=1 all remain. Unique allocation
of every prime to one of the two coordinates gives

    F_chi(s,t) = product_p [1-chi(p)(p^(-s)+p^(-t))/2],
    F_chi(s,s) = 1/L(s,chi).

On every finite hard product cutoff, the complete diagonal coefficient of
k is exactly mu(k)chi(k), since a squarefree k has 2^omega(k) allocations.
This is an actual source identity. Its absolute convergence cone is exactly
Re(s)>1 and Re(t)>1: the prime terms on either coordinate axis force the
two prime series, and their convergence suffices. Finite ramification
does not alter this cone.

For x=chi(p)p^(-s),y=chi(p)p^(-t), on both real parts greater than1/2 put

    log G(s,t) = sum_p [log(1-(x+y)/2)
                       - (1/2)log(1-x) - (1/2)log(1-y)].

Power-series logarithms are legitimate since |x|,|y|<1. The linear terms
cancel and the quadratic term is (x-y)^2/8; compactly uniform bounds by
a constant times |x| squared+|y| squared give normal convergence.
Thus G is holomorphic and nowhere zero there, G(s,s)=1, and initially

    F_chi(s,t)^2 L(s,chi)L(t,chi) = G(s,t)^2.                (G151.1)

For principal chi fix a safe real t0>1. Since L(s,chi) has a simple pole
at1, the right side of F(s,t0)^2=G(s,t0)^2/[L(s)L(t0)] has a zero of order
one at s=1. A square of a holomorphic function has even vanishing order.
Hence this particular F cannot be holomorphic near (1,t0), and cannot
extend to the whole product half-plane Re(s),Re(t)>gamma for
1/2<gamma<1, even if zero exclusion is already known. The diagonal itself
is consistent: both reciprocal factors there have the same zero.

This actual obstruction redirects the lift, rather than rejecting all
two-variable detectors. A sloping tube, different source or explicit pole
normalization remains possible. The exact simple repair B=F squared keeps
its genuine two-variable convolution coefficients

    b(m,n) = sum_(d|m,e|n) c(d,e)c(m/d,n/e),
    B(s,t) = G(s,t)^2/[L(s,chi)L(t,chi)],
    B(s,s) = 1/L(s,chi)^2.

These b are not the original c. For fixed1/2<gamma<1, holomorphy of B on
the whole product half-plane is equivalent to zero exclusion for L in
Re(s)>gamma. Fixing t0 and nonvanishing G proves the forward implication;
holomorphic1/L, including its principal-pole zero, proves the converse.
No growth estimate or coefficient cancellation follows from this equivalence.
This is a corrected exact return, not an independent gain or a claimed
literature priority.

### Fixed native H packets: commuting operations still have a mixed bill

Use the exact Eisenstein source in
[[private research revision] h-joint Sections1–2](../[private research revision]/h-joint/report.md), including long
prime ideals pi,pi' of distinct rational norms, original orientations and
bad-place data, complete ordered short g,g' including equality, the complex
core, rational gcd screen, both rooted mark weights, both projectors and
independent heights. The coefficient systems remain
a(n)=alpha(n)eta(n)chi_n(lambda)^(-2)gamma_2(n) and
xi(g)=alpha(g)^3 eta(g)^3. Nothing is replaced by an integer-norm or
positive-divisor surrogate.

For M=pi*pi',Q=q_M the finite group
(O/M) times(O/pi) times(O/pi') has size Q squared. Its unitary transform
F has factor1/Q and phases -Rh/M-Ps/pi+P's'/pi'. The literal dual kernel is
