## G150. Complete matching displacement, with the old rank equivalence retained

Let V have basis the squarefree q-units n<=X, parity mu(n), and all diagonal
character actions W_chi(n)=chi(n). An odd differential d with d squared
zero commuting with every character must preserve each reduced residue
class: the characters separate that finite group. Write E_a,O_a for the
two parity counts and I_a=E_a-O_a. Hodge decomposition then gives

    dim ker(dd*+d*d) >= R_q(X) := sum_a |I_a(X)|.

Matching min(E_a,O_a) opposite signs within each residue attains equality;
unit arrows give nonzero spectral gap one. The gap alone says nothing
about the residual rank. Orthogonality gives the exact comparisons

    max_chi |M_chi(X)| <= R_q(X) <= sum_chi |M_chi(X)|
                                      <= phi(q) max_chi |M_chi(X)|.

These are already [[private research revision] G135](../[private research revision]/wild55-integration.md).
Do not count this reformulation as a new weaker arithmetic prerequisite.
For example q=5,X=80 has residue indices (0,-3,-4,1), hence minimum rank
eight; a fourteen-state rank of a particular construction is not universal.

For one neutral prime r=1 mod q, the exact pairing m with rm, r not
dividing m, has residual rank

    d_q (r-1)/(r+1) X + O_(q,r)(sqrt(X)),
    d_q = zeta(2)^(-1) product_(p|q) p/(p+1).

The square-divisor expansion proves the squarefree q-unit count
d_q X+O_q(sqrt(X)). If only one chi is being preserved, chi(r)=1 suffices;
otherwise the multiplier 1-chi(r) must remain. This linear-rank obstruction
belongs to the named neutral-prime rule, not to every differential.

### A full future-partner return

In each reduced residue class there are infinitely many negative squarefree
integers (primes) and positive ones (a fixed r=1 mod q times different
primes in that class). Only infinitude of primes in each reduced progression
is imported here; see [NIST DLMF 27.11.9](https://dlmf.nist.gov/27.11.E9).
No prime-distribution error estimate is used. Thus a fixed global
same-residue pairing of the two signs exists. Orient each pair (u,v) by
mu(u)=1, mu(v)=-1 and set a=min(u,v), b=max(u,v). Define

    D_q(X) = sum_(X<=a<2X) (b-a),       X=1,2,4,... .

Every future partner is included, even when b is much larger than 2X.
For a common 0<gamma<1, the full hypothesis

    D_q(X) <<_(q,epsilon) X^(1+gamma+epsilon)
    for every epsilon>0 and every fixed q                 (OPEN-D)

implies ordinary zero exclusion in Re(s)>gamma. Indeed, initially Re(s)>1,
absolute regrouping gives

    1/L(s,chi) = sum_pairs chi(u)(u^(-s)-v^(-s)).

For sigma=Re(s)>0 the difference is bounded by
|s|(b-a)a^(-sigma-1). Summing dyadic shells with epsilon below a compact
set's horizontal margin gives normal convergence on Re(s)>gamma. The
identity L F=1 continues meromorphically, excluding zeros and permitting
the reciprocal zero at a principal pole. All fixed finite heights and the
literal imprimitive factors are covered; no uniform growth assertion follows.

Monotone same-residue pairing has crossing count R_q(t). Tonelli identifies
the total *clipped* interval length in [A,B] with integral_A^B R_q(t)dt.
That is not the complete D_q(A): omitted future portions and intervals
entering from earlier shells matter. Under G135's existing summatory/rank
bound with gamma>1/2, endpoints grow proportionally to their rank k and
pair displacement is O(k^(gamma+epsilon)); the complete D bound follows.
This adapter has not evaded the original arithmetic difficulty.

The global neutral-prime rule has the unconditional full cost

    D_q(X) = (r-1) sum_(X<=m<2X,(m,qr)=1) mu(m)^2 m
           = (3/2)(r-1)d_(qr) X^2 + O_(q,r)(X^(3/2)).

Partial summation of the squarefree count proves it, with the positive main
coefficient intact. Thus this rule cannot meet the positive-cost target for
any gamma<1. Other matchings or signed displacement estimates remain open.
Near/1/6/1/4 cost exponents are respectively below1.8748540364,11/6,7/4.

failure; G135, W01 signed transport and [private research revision] priced coupling retain credit.

# [private research revision]: compensated nonlinear source and paid cutoff coupling

The author develops the actual mean-zero compensated source; the independent
critic extends it to arbitrary product-bounded cutoffs and a one-Mobius core.
Root accepts G152–G154 after complete written review. These are useful
restricted estimates and an actual coupled cancellation. The complete
signed power estimate is OPEN. Written source-relative
c11=312864909/2500000000=.1251459636 is unchanged. F0/analytic ancestry,
inherited positive-slot uniformity and external admission remain OPEN.

Evidence: [author](compensated-source/report.md),
[independent review](compensated-source-review/report.md),
[retention manifest](retention-manifest.json), and the prior
[G140–G142 nonlinear source](../[private research revision]/nonlinear-source-integration.md).
Twelve original files are byte-preserved. Nine review-input pins include
five author files and four earlier mathematical sources. Original claims
are never copied. Both mathematical deadlines were met. A fourth reviewer
stream failure occurred after its normal own-claim release and full hash
readback; the frozen STOP/report and native release are the handoff evidence.
No missing final chat text is represented as received.

## G152. A complete compensated small-divisor estimate and zero return

Fix an ordinary Dirichlet character chi modulo q, with all natural zeros,
and choose a fixed prime p not dividing q. Put Q=pq and use Dirichlet
convolution, with delta_m denoting the coefficient at m:

    a(n)=mu(n)chi(n),  h(n)=chi(n),  a*h=delta_1,
    q_p=delta_1-p chi(p)delta_p,
    b_p=q_p*h=chi(n)(1-p 1_(p|n)),
    c_p=q_p*a=a(n)-p chi(p)1_(p|n)a(n/p).

The Q-periodic b_p has mean zero. Indeed its complete sum is
p(1-chi(p)) sum_(r mod q)chi(r), zero by orthogonality or, for a
principal character, chi(p)=1. The unramified-prime hypothesis matters.
The changed c_p can be nonzero on squareful integers; retain these terms.
It has |c_p|<=p+1, and still vanishes on nonunits modulo q.

For fixed b>1 and integer k>2 define

    f_x(n)=exp(-n/x^b-i(n/x)^k),
    C_p(x)=sum_(n>=1)c_p(n)f_x(n),
    ||F||_j=(integral_X^(2X)|F(x)|^j dx/x)^(1/j), j=1,2.

All cutoffs depend on X, chi and fixed parameters, and are frozen before
real x varies. Use literal closed n<=U and strict n>U for real U.
The tempting identity f_x(pn)=f_(x/p)(n) is false when b>1.

With m_U=a 1_(n<=U), u_U=a-m_U, set

    S_(U,V)=m_U*m_V*b_p,  R_(U,V)=u_U*u_V*b_p.
    c_p=q_p*m_U+q_p*m_V-S_(U,V)+R_(U,V).        (91.1)

Every ordered factor pair and every cofactor remains. Each S or R
coefficient has absolute value <=p d_3(n)<<_(p,eta)n^eta, uniformly
in U,V. The two short terms cost O_p(U+V) in both shell norms.

### Full divisor-bounded tail

If |v_n|<=A_eta n^eta and 2eta<k-2, the complete tail satisfies

    ||sum_(n>M)v_n f_x(n)||_2^2
      <<_(b,k,eta) A_eta^2
          [X^(b(1+2eta))+X^k M^(2-k+2eta)].    (91.2)

Use a nonnegative C2 majorant equal to one on the original shell,
supported in [1/2,4], with flat endpoints. After v=u^(-k), the
off-diagonal amplitude and two derivatives are uniformly bounded:
powers of A=(n+m)/X^b are absorbed by exp(-cA). Two integrations by
parts give the kernel

    min(1,(X^k/|n^k-m^k|)^2).

For m<n, n^k-m^k>=n^(k-1)(n-m). Writing delta=X^k/n^(k-1), the
full sum over gaps of min(1,(delta/gap)^2) is O(delta), including
delta<1. Sum n^(2eta)delta over n>M; the damped diagonal supplies
the first term in (91.2). Finite expansions followed by summable
domination justify the infinite calculation. Both orientations and
every cross are included; no off-diagonal part is dropped.

For 1/2<gamma<1, b<=2gamma and

    r=(k-2gamma)/(k-2), M=X^r,

(91.2) gives an O(X^(gamma+epsilon)) tail in L2 and L1 for every
epsilon>0, choosing eta after epsilon. This includes b=2gamma.
The tail proof needs no r<b restriction; damping helps when r>=b.

### Completed small-divisor source

Assume u=k-(k-1)r=2gamma-r>0 and put eta_0=1/(100kpq).
For ANY real U,V>=1 with UV<=eta_0 X^u,

    ||sum_n S_(U,V)(n)f_x(n)||_1
      +||sum_n S_(U,V)(n)f_x(n)||_2
               <<_(p,q,b,k,gamma,epsilon) X^(gamma+epsilon). (91.3)

On n<=M, expand b_p in its nonzero Fourier modes j/Q. For D=de,
the phase as a function of the cofactor is

    F_j(t)=jt/Q-(Dt/x)^k/(2pi).

Since D<=UV and Dt<=M, its derivative correction is at most
k UV M^(k-1)/(2pi X^k)<=k eta_0/(2pi)<1/(2Q).
Thus F_j' and each discrete phase increment lie monotonically between
1/(2Q) and 1-1/(2Q). Summation by parts with
1/(exp(2pi i v)-1)=-1/2-(i/2)cot(pi v) bounds every prefix by O(Q).
Abel summation preserves that bound under the actual decreasing damping.
This includes empty and one-term prefixes. Summing all ordered d,e costs
O_(p,q)(UV)=O(X^u); u<gamma. The complete n>M contribution is (91.2).
No Fourier gap is asserted beyond M. Also U+V<=UV+1 pays the short
terms, uniformly in the asymmetric choices.

This is an actual unrestricted small-product estimate, not an arbitrary
coefficient model. It does NOT allow UV=X^gamma without a new argument.

### Complete core and all-height return

For b=3/2,k=6 and gamma>=3/4, set L=X^gamma and freeze
U=V=floor(sqrt(eta_0) X^(u/2)). For sufficiently large X these exceed
one. Define the full balanced core

    T_(p,chi,X)(x)=sum_(d>U,e>V,L<del<=M)
       mu(d)mu(e)chi(del)(1-p 1_(p|l))f_x(del).

Its low prefix costs O(X^(gamma+epsilon)) by the divisor bound; its
full tail, S and short terms are already paid. Consequently

    ||C_p-T_(p,chi,X)||_j << X^(gamma+epsilon), j=1,2.       (91.4)

Every-epsilon whole-shell bounds for T and C_p are equivalent separately
in L1 and L2. L2 is sufficient for L1; the converse is not inferred.

The G140 Mellin calculation applies to the bounded changed coefficients.
After v=nt and rotation by a fixed admissible angle alpha, it gives

    integral_0^infinity C_p(1/t)t^(s-1)dt
       =A_0(s)P_p(s)/L(s,chi)+E_p(s),
    A_0(s)=Gamma(s/6) exp(-i pi s/12)/6,
    P_p(s)=1-chi(p)p^(1-s),                              (91.5)

where E_p is holomorphic for Re s>1/2 and A_0 has no zero for Re s>0.
Initially the identity holds in an absolutely convergent right half-plane.
The rotated remainder is locally uniform at EVERY fixed height; constants
can depend on height and chi. At x down to zero,
|C_p(x)|<=(p+1)/(exp(x^(-b))-1). The hypothesized every-epsilon L1 shell
bound therefore makes the left side holomorphic on Re s>gamma.

Choose two distinct fixed unramified primes p1,p2. For a nonprincipal
character choose p1 with chi(p1)!=1: a unit with nontrivial character
value has a prime factor with nontrivial value. Each P_p zero has Re s=1.
A common zero 1+it with t!=0 would make both t log(p_j)/(2pi) nonzero
rationals, contradicting irrationality of log(p1)/log(p2). At t=0 the
chosen nonprincipal p1 prevents a common zero. For a principal character
the possible common point is its allowed L pole, not an ordinary zero.
Thus bounds for both fixed compensated cores exclude ALL ordinary zeros
with Re s>gamma. No line-one nonvanishing theorem is hidden in the return.
Actual imprimitive Euler holes stay present; their zeros lie on Re s=0.

More generally, for each fixed gamma>1/2 choose k large enough that u>0,
1<b<=2gamma, and fixed K with 1-(b-1)K<gamma. Retain ALL shifts
A_j(s)P_p(s+(b-1)j)/L(s+(b-1)j) in G140's K-term expansion.
Starting above Re s=1, finite-strip descent of width b-1 gives the same
return. No growing k,K, uniform limit gamma down to 1/2, or endpoint
theorem is claimed. This extends the previous conditional architecture;
its required arithmetic power premise remains open.

## G153. Asymmetric completion and a one-Mobius core

The independent critic takes A=floor(eta_0 X^u), V=1. Since m_1=delta_1,

    (a-delta_1)*b_p=q_p-b_p=:h_p,
    R_(A,1)=u_A*h_p.

Explicitly h_p(1)=0, h_p(p)=-chi(p), and otherwise
h_p(j)=-chi(j)(1-p 1_(p|j)); |h_p(j)|<=p-1.
The two exceptional coefficients must remain. This h_p is not globally
periodic mean-zero after those corrections.

The actual asymmetric core is

    A_(p,chi,X)(x)=sum_(d>A,j>=2,L<dj<=M)
                    mu(d)chi(d)h_p(j)f_x(dj).            (91.6)

Its coefficients are bounded by (p-1)d_2(n); the literal cofactor cap is
j<=M/(A+1)<<_(p,q,k)X^(r-u), not a unit-constant cap. Applying (91.3)
with these cutoffs and retaining all complementary sources gives

    ||C_p-A_(p,chi,X)||_j<<X^(gamma+epsilon), j=1,2.       (91.7)

The same two-prime return applies. This is an exact simplification of the
remaining source, not a proof of its power bound.

When p does not divide n the merged residual coefficient is

    (u_A*h_p)(n)=-chi(n)sum_(d|n,A<d<n)mu(d).

It vanishes on primes. For distinct primes r,s not dividing pq it equals
chi(rs)(1_(r>A)+1_(s>A)); it vanishes when both primes are <=A.
This coefficient identity retains the original product cut and all signs.

| Conditional c | gamma | r | u | Balanced cut exponent | Asymmetric cut exponent | Cofactor exponent r-u |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| .1252 | 2187/2500 | 5313/5000 | 687/1000 | 687/2000 | 687/1000 | 939/2500 |
| 1/6 | 5/6 | 13/12 | 7/12 | 7/24 | 7/12 | 1/2 |
| 1/4 | 3/4 | 9/8 | 3/8 | 3/16 | 3/8 | 3/4 |

Every row is conditional. The first would improve c11 by
135091/2500000000. At the first two rows u>1/2 and 2u>r, so the
asymmetric core absorbs the balanced semiprime cell near n~X and
comparable semiprimes near the upper product cap. Neither holds for
the displayed 1/4 row. The old 2/5 architecture also remains conditional.

## G154. Actual coupled cancellation, and the surviving obstruction

For a principal character let B_X be the selected ordered source with
distinct primes d,e in (sqrt(X)/2,sqrt(X/2)] and cofactor l=1. For large
X these primes are unramified and satisfy every balanced-core cutoff.
If J is their number, the ordinary prime number theorem gives
J~2(1/sqrt(2)-1/2)sqrt(X)/log X. Uniformly on the full real shell,

    Re B_X(x)>=exp(-X^(1-b)/2)cos(2^(-k))J(J-1).

Thus ||B_X||_1 and ||B_X||_2 are comparable to X/log^2 X. The only
external input is ordinary PNT, e.g. [Selberg's original theorem (1.1),
printed p.305](https://www.math.lsu.edu/~mahlburg/teaching/handouts/2014-7230/Selberg-ElemPNT1949.pdf),
used here for fixed-proportion prime counts. This is a lower bound for
the selected arithmetic cell. It is NOT a lower bound for an unselected
dyadic factor box, T, R or C_p. It obstructs a triangle budget that pays
this cell separately at X^(gamma+epsilon), epsilon<1-gamma.

When u>1/2 the asymmetric core has zero coefficient on this cell, while
the balanced core has coefficient two per unordered pair. Put

    D_X=T_(p,chi,X)-A_(p,chi,X), K_X=D_X-B_X.

Equations (91.4) and (91.7) UNCONDITIONALLY give

    ||B_X+K_X||_j<<X^(gamma+epsilon)=o(||B_X||_j), j=1,2.

K_X contains every other exact term in the difference, with its signs
and cutoffs. In L2 this implies

    ||K_X||_2/||B_X||_2 -> 1,
    Re <B_X,K_X>=-||B_X||_2^2
                   +O(||B_X||_2 X^(gamma+epsilon)).

Their normalized real correlation tends to -1. By Markov's inequality,
outside logarithmic measure O_delta(X^(gamma-1+epsilon)log^2 X),
Re K_X<=-(1-delta)Re B_X. This is an actual paid cancellation across
representations; neither OPEN core estimate was used.

The asymmetric source still has an actual large positive cell. Take
j=p and primes d in (X/(4p),X/(2p)]. They satisfy d>A and L<pd<=M;
mu(d)h_p(p)=+1 for principal chi. The FULL merged coefficient at pd
is also +1: the other divisor labels contribute zero. This selected
source has both norms comparable to X/log X. Paying it alone therefore
still misses every fixed gamma<1. The balanced representation excludes
this fixed-small-prime factor, whereas the asymmetric representation
excludes the previous balanced semiprimes. These facts concern selected
cells, not lower bounds for either full signed core.

The next useful test must couple the terminal prime–cofactor cell with
its composite partners before taking absolute values, or replace the
upstream detector with a fully priced bridge. Repeating only the tail
bound or paying each positive cell separately cannot close this route.

## Comparison, source limits and verification

The generic full divisor bound is X^(1+epsilon), above every target.
G142's actual Green–Tao logarithmic estimate transfers to the bounded
compensated source with fixed p, yielding the previous X^(3/4) plus
X(log X)^(-D) scale. Fixed D cannot grow with X and supplies no power
gain. That earlier theorem is reused, not counted as new [private research revision] credit.

The published [Matomaki–Teravainen paper](https://ems.press/content/serial-article-files/32826?nt=1)
was inspected as outside-source motivation: Theorems1.1/1.5 give
logarithmic short-interval savings, and Lemma3.1 retains its restricted
prime range, small residual factor and explicit extraction error. None
is imported as the missing nonlinear, character-uniform power estimate.

The author helper checks four actual characters, three cutoff pairs
through n=480, natural zeros, the squareful correction, a ramified-prime
negative control and four rational target rows. The independent helper
checks four characters and three asymmetric cutoffs through n=720,
merged semiprime/terminal coefficients and the same budgets. Root read
both complete helpers and receipts; no unchanged helper was rerun.
Finite algebra is diagnostic evidence, not an analytic proof.

The accepted arguments retain all signs, shared primes, real shells,
strict endpoints, principal/imprimitive cases and every complementary
term. L1 and L2 premises remain distinct. No native positive-slot
improvement or full physical return is inferred. All29 families/109
children, later developments, nearer targets,1/6 and1/4 remain available.
No formalization, kernel work, new proof packet or public-record claim.

# [private research revision]: paid parts of the separated mixed moment

[private research revision] accepts G155–G157 relative to the same PR9 source contracts and
[private research revision] separated witnesses. It proves a large-common-divisor estimate,
pays three disjoint sectors of the remaining norm, and adds an intrinsic
restriction on its repeated-prime support. The signed high-conductor
remainder and its full physical return remain **OPEN**. The accepted
written value stays

\[
c_{11}=312864909/2500000000=.1251459636.
\]

The density input is still \(K=28114053/6250000\), licensed from the
preceding c10 same-family ancestry. No recalibration from c11, new
formalization, kernel result or external record admission is claimed.

The [author](separated-mixed/report.md) and
[independent development](separated-mixed-review/report.md) give the
complete calculations. [Retention](retention-manifest.json) binds fifteen
unchanged artifacts and fourteen review inputs: six author files, six
mathematical ancestry inputs and two assignment records. The original
review freeze is preserved alongside its corrected metadata receipt.

## Fixed object and quantifiers

Use the original Eisenstein field, primary/unit convention, fixed excluded
set and finite dictionary. Write
\(\phi_u(n)=\nu(n)\psi_u(n)^{\pm1}\), retaining natural zeros. The fixed
factor \(\nu\) need not have order six; it remains in column coefficients
when the row character is summed. For fixed smooth profiles put

\[
M_u(D;W)=D^{-1/2}\sum_n\mu(n)\phi_u(n)W(Nn/D).
\]

Let Q be the actual product of the original prime slots. Their pools are
pairwise disjoint, their coefficients and natural zeros are unchanged,
and \(P_0=\prod_iP_i=U^v\), \(0\le v\le1/20\).
The slot pools may intersect either inverse. The elementary bound is
\(\sup_u|Q_u|^2\ll H_JU^{v+\epsilon}\). If inverse orientation is reversed,
align the **entire** slot product at the positive norm, including its
coefficients, zeros and heights; individual slot switching is unavailable.

The norm sums nonzero sixth-power-free rows in a fixed nonnegative smooth
enclosing ball of scale U, with the licensed fixed ray/unit sectors. A
row divisor weight is dominated before expansion and Poisson. An
arbitrary row selector, zero predicate or signed physical projector is
not admitted into that free-row Poisson identity.

The physical box supplied by [G147–G148](../[private research revision]/far-complement-integration.md)
is

\[
17/25\le\delta\le7/10,\quad17/20<r<47/50,\quad
33/25<s<141/100,\quad s-r>3/8,\qquad D_1=U^r,D_2=U^s.
\]

Both inverse heights are independent. Their same-zero, same-annulus and
plain-complement restrictions remain those of the actual G147 witness;
enlarging its exponent set to this box is only for bounding the norm.
The internal buffer \(\delta_b\) may exceed .70; extract the signal there
before weakening to physical \(\delta\). Slot pricing uses physical
\(\delta\), not that internal buffer.

Use the existing common mesh and buffer **before** eventual arithmetic
family and slot choices. Then fix the allowed dictionary/slot data,
profiles, derivative orders, auxiliary losses and height choices before
the eventual large-U threshold. This is the reviewer's corrected order;
the author's abbreviated list is not permission to tune mesh after
seeing a family. Every implied constant has exactly this fixed-data
dependence. The UM slack is chosen before applying the original moment.

Tensor Sobolev covers the common bounded real parameter, both independent
inverse heights, the original slot heights and logarithmic scales. Scale
derivatives replace W by -W/2-yW'; other derivatives retain the original
twists and add fixed logarithmic factors. The tuple gcd threshold is
fixed at U and is not differentiated. Write q/h sums over a fixed global
support bound and use Hilbert Minkowski before the rowwise supremum.
For a common product profile, B3.3 fixes its Fourier measure on the whole
ambient box before any row or q label; keep both Fourier coordinates
distinct. Choose derivative orders backward through the bounded
dependency graph, and Fourier decay only after the raw polynomial label
count and all height orders are known. G147 already pays the genuine
detector tails and both frozen profile families; no completed divisor
identity is silently truncated here.

For reference, with \(h=5-2\delta\), put

\[
\rho=1-\frac{10\delta}{3h},\quad k=\rho+\delta-1,\quad
D_K=15K-10-6K\delta,
\]
\[
a_K=\frac{\delta(5-6\delta)^2}{3hD_K},\quad
b_K=\frac{2\delta(5-6\delta)(K-1)}{D_K},\quad
E_K=\rho+\delta v-\min(3kv,a_K+b_Kv),\quad
T=\delta(r+s)+E_K.
\]

Here \(E_K\ge\rho\ge19/54\), because
\(\delta-3k=4\delta^2/(5-2\delta)>0\). Consequently
\(T\ge123353/67500\). H_J denotes the fixed Sobolev/height envelope.

## G155. Actual large-common-divisor saving

Set \(B=M(D_1)M(D_2)\). Cut its original ordered tuples by
\(N\gcd(d_1,d_2)\ge G\), **before** merging coefficients. This is not a
slot cut or a row selector. Define

\[
a_G(q)=\sum_{d\mid q,\,Nd\ge G}\mu(q/d).
\]

Divisor inversion gives \(\sum_{q\mid g}a_G(q)=1_{Ng\ge G}\),
\(a_G(q)=0\) for \(Nq<G\), and \(|a_G(q)|\le d(q)\).
Only squarefree q survive the two original Möbius factors. With
\(d_1=qx,d_2=qy\), their product is
\(\mu(x)\mu(y)1_{(x,q)=1}1_{(y,q)=1}\); no condition \((x,y)=1\) is
inserted. Thus the exact centrally normalized identity is

\[
B_{\ge G}(u)=\sum_{\substack{q\ \mathrm{squarefree}\\Nq\ge G}}
\frac{a_G(q)\phi_u(q)^2}{Nq}
M_u^{(q)}(D_1/Nq)M_u^{(q)}(D_2/Nq),                 \tag{G155.1}
\]

where superscript q means the literal coprimality mask. Fixed profile
support bounds \(Nq\ll D_1\). Natural zeros are kept, never divided out.

Restore each mask exactly:

\[
M_u^{(q)}(E;W)=
\sum_{h\ q\text{-smooth}}\frac{\phi_u(h)}{\sqrt{Nh}}
M_u(E/Nh;W).                                        \tag{G155.2}
\]

Primewise this is \(\mu*(1,1,\ldots)=(1,0,\ldots)\). It restores the
original Möbius coefficients, so the invoked moment is PR9 B0.9, not a
new moment for \(\mu*\mu\). All h shorten the scales. The finitely
supported sums may be dominated using
\(\prod_{\mathfrak p\mid q}(1-N\mathfrak p^{-1/2})^{-1}\ll(Nq)^\epsilon\).
A retained polynomially bounded puncture R0 is handled by qR0, within
the already frozen family. Nonempty subunit scales are bounded away
from zero by fixed profile support; smaller scales are empty.

Minkowski over q and both h, the trivial first-inverse bound and
\(\|M(E)\|_U^2\ll H_JU^\epsilon[U+U^{1/6}E^{5/6}]\) give

\[
\|B_{\ge G}Q\|_U^2\ll H_JU^{v+\epsilon}\frac{D_1}{G}
\left[U+U^{1/6}(D_2/G)^{5/6}\right].                 \tag{G155.3}
\]

The q-shell mass \(\sum|a_G(q)|/Nq\) is subpower; the shortened-scale
factors decrease geometrically. With \(G=U^{1/5}\), the second bracket
term dominates throughout the box and the exponent is
\(v+r+5s/6-1/5\). The target gap is at least

\[
\rho+(47/20)\delta-393/200\ge2809/273000>1/100.
\]

The derivative is \(47/20-50/[3(5-2\delta)^2]>0\). An independent exact
Bernstein certificate verifies this on the whole interval. Reserving
1/1000 for geometric pads and 1/500 for all auxiliary losses still
leaves a retained norm margin 1/200 and spare \(5/2184\).

On actual witnesses, where \(|B|^2\ge U^{\delta(r+s)-\eta}\), rows with
\(|B_{\ge G}|\ge|B|/2\) have the paid slot mass exponent
\(E_K-1/200+\epsilon\), after choosing the losses. Otherwise
\(|B_{<G}|\ge|B|/2\). The full norm also satisfies
\(\|BQ\|^2\le2\|B_{<G}Q\|^2+2\|B_{\ge G}Q\|^2\), which pays every
large/small cross once the remaining norm is bounded. A cross-term
estimate alone is not that remaining norm bound.

## G156. Complete diagonal and two off-diagonal sectors

Merge only after the tuple cut:

\[
B_{<G}(u)Q_u=\sum_n c(n)\psi_u(n)^{\pm1},\qquad
n=d_1d_2\prod_ip_i,\quad N_0=D_1D_2P_0.
\]

The coefficient c contains every Möbius sign, fixed character, pool,
profile, independent height, normalization and original tuple gcd cut.
Each prime valuation of n is 0,1,2 or3, including all collisions. Hence
\(n/n'\) is a sixth power as an ideal only when \(n=n'\): the valuation
difference lies in [-3,3]. Finite unit/root phases remain in their fixed
sectors. This fact does not apply to older completions with unbounded
prime powers. Divisor bounds give
\(|c(n)|\ll H_JN_0^{-1/2}U^\epsilon\) and
\(\sum_n|c(n)|^2\ll H_JU^\epsilon\). The **complete** paired diagonal is
therefore \(O(H_JU^{1+\epsilon})\); this is not a lower bound for the full
norm.

For an off-diagonal pair let \(e_{\mathfrak p}=v_{\mathfrak p}(n)-
v_{\mathfrak p}(n')\), let q_j be the radical of primes with
\(|e_{\mathfrak p}|=j\), and write

\[
Q_j=Nq_j,\quad Q=Q_1Q_2Q_3,\quad V=Q_1Q_2^2Q_3^3.
\]

Retain the full oriented integer vector. Although signs +3 and -3 have
the same sextic phase, their integer ratios differ; the finite allocation
cost must not be discarded. Every nonzero exponent has nonprincipal
primitive local phase at a good prime. The fixed factor \(\nu\) stays
in c and is not falsely treated as order six.

Write \(n=ga,n'=gb,(a,b)=1\). Then \(NaNb=V\) and
\(Ng\ll N_0/\sqrt V\), so for one full relative vector

\[
\sum_{(n,n')\text{ inducing it}}|c(n)c(n')|
\ll H_JU^\epsilon V^{-1/2}.
\]

This includes all shared slot/inverse collisions. Counting vectors in
fixed dyadic Q1,Q2,Q3 boxes gives mass
\(\ll H_JU^\epsilon(Q_1/Q_3)^{1/2}\). Empty subunit gcd ranges remain
empty, with fixed endpoint constants retained.

The row kernel includes **all** natural-zero holes E from shared primes
whose character phases cancel, and all retained frozen punctures not
already in the primitive conductor. Cancellation of phase does not
remove a hole. Here NE is polynomial in U. Applying the existing masked
Poisson formula, whose primitive prefactor is X/\(\sqrt Q\) and dual
scale XNh/Q, gives \(\min(X,\sqrt Q)\), with zero dual term absent.
Expand sixth-power-freeness and full holes by
\(b^6\mid u\) and \(d\mid\operatorname{rad}E\), respectively, putting
\(X=U/((Nb)^6Nd)\). Splitting at
\(Nb=(U/(Nd\sqrt Q))^{1/6}\) yields

\[
|\mathcal K(n,n')|\ll H_JU^\epsilon
\min(U,U^{1/6}Q^{5/12}).                              \tag{G156.1}
\]

The hole Euler product with exponent -1/6 is subpower. Thresholds below
one use the complete tail; conductor-sharing natural zeros and fixed
excluded/ray sectors are retained. Finitely many inducing free-row
deletions cost O(1) per kernel, already absorbed. This is not a blanket
deletion license for the raw physical row set.

Separate the paired sum disjointly: full diagonal; then Q≤\(U^{9/5}\);
then the remaining pairs with \(Q_1/Q_3\le U^{8/5}\). The low-Q sum uses
V≥Q and the divisor count to sum \(Q^{-1/12+\epsilon}\); its total is
\(\ll H_JU^{109/60+\epsilon}\). The ratio sector uses the U branch of
(G156.1) and costs \(\ll H_JU^{9/5+\epsilon}\), with every Q2 and all
holes included. Polynomial conductor ranges cost only logarithmic boxes.

| Paid part | Exponent | Minimum gap below T | Spare after .001+.002+.005 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Complete diagonal | 1 | 55853/67500 | 55313/67500 |
| Total conductor Q≤U^(9/5) | 109/60 | 182/16875 | 47/16875 |
| Remaining ratio Q1/Q3≤U^(8/5) | 9/5 | 1853/67500 | 1313/67500 |

Each raw gap exceeds 1/100 and pays the retained 1/200 margin. These are
upper bounds for paid sectors, using absolute values there; no sign or
positivity is asserted for the residual. Masked Poisson and relative-mass
machinery are reused from the exact PR9/[private research revision] sources, rather than
counted as newly proved general theorems.

## G157. Repeated-prime support and the exact remaining estimate

The independent reviewer strengthens the actual small-gcd support.
For a surviving original tuple write \(d_1=gx,d_2=gy\), with g,x,y
pairwise coprime squarefree, and let \(p=\prod_ip_i\), squarefree by
disjoint original pools. Set

\[
A=(g,p),\quad b=(xy,p),\quad g=Ag_0,\quad xy=bz,
\quad p=Abp_0,\quad B=g_0b,\quad C=zp_0.
\]

Then A,B,C are pairwise coprime squarefree and

\[
n=A^3B^2C,\qquad n/\operatorname{rad}n=A^2B=gAb,
\qquad Ab\mid p.
\]

These radicals are intrinsic to the merged n, even when many tuples
contribute to c(n). Thus \(N(n/\operatorname{rad}n)<CGP_0\). Comparing
two such columns, the local valuation table gives
\(q_2q_3^2\mid(n/\operatorname{rad}n)(n'/\operatorname{rad}n')\) and
\(q_3\mid A(n)A(n')\). Consequently

\[
Q_2Q_3^2<CU^{2/5+2v},\qquad Q_3\le CU^{2v}.           \tag{G157.1}
\]

At maximal v the exponents are 1/2 and1/10. Fixed profile constants
require arbitrarily small geometric pads, rather than literal unpadded
finite-U cutoffs. Profile derivatives, independent heights and the
fixed positive common-profile integrals preserve this support. This is
an exact new support fact, not a signed norm saving by itself.

Let \(\mathcal R_{\rm mix}\) be the real ordered off-diagonal paired sum
remaining after G156, with the actual coefficients c(n)\(\overline{c(n')}\)
and full kernels. It has

\[
n\ne n',\quad Q>U^{9/5},\quad Q_1/Q_3>U^{8/5},\quad
Q_2Q_3^2<CU^{2/5+2v},\quad Q_3\le CU^{2v}.
\]

The same definition includes the fixed finite derivative sum and positive
common-profile measure needed for the Sobolev envelope. The necessary
open hypothesis is the **one-sided** estimate

\[
\mathcal R_{\rm mix}\le H_JU^{T-\xi+\epsilon}
\quad\text{for some fixed }\xi>0,                    \tag{OPEN-MIX-RES}
\]

uniformly over the licensed fixed data and both independent heights.
Absolute value would be a stronger optional target, not a proved or
necessary replacement. The residual need not be positive.

This estimate would complete G148 OPEN-MIX with a margin below
\(\min(\xi,1/200)\). Combining the actual separated witness and G147
counted prefix then requires a margin below
\(\min(\xi,1/200,1/2000)\), with every witness, height and buffer loss
chosen from that strict slack. It still does not pay the full raw or
positive-child physical return: both signed coprimality projectors,
family reconstruction, root/slot holes, fixed inducing and exceptional
rows, physical radii/amplifier, clipped rectangles, shifted/shortened
Euler families, principal terms and the actual supremum/common mesh
all retain their previous obligations. The centered reserve is unspent.

## Strongest surviving obstruction and the next attack

With zero slots and squarefree n, the actual coefficient already contains

\[
c(n)=(D_1D_2)^{-1/2}\mu(n)\nu(n)
\sum_{d\mid n}W_1(Nd/D_1)W_2(N(n/d)/D_2),
\]

with the two independent twists on their respective divisors. This
divisor-profile coefficient is outside the original canonical B3.6
Möbius moment. Squarefree coprime pairs can have \(Q_1\asymp N_0^2\),
Q2=Q3=1 and tuple gcd1; none of (G157.1) removes them. The available
absolute envelope UN0 is too large. That is an obstruction to this
upper-bound method, not an actual lower bound for the whole signed norm
or a realized high-zero configuration. Same-zero coupling supplies no
probabilistic independence.

The next useful step is an identity or correlation estimate for this
signed divisor-profile source, possibly after extracting the now-short
repeated-prime part. Further clean Poisson bounds or cutoff optimization
alone do not address this squarefree sector. A replacement source is
also admissible if it brings its own complete bridge and pays its terms.

Root read both complete reports, both helpers and receipts, checked exact
input hashes, and reviewed the literal moment/Poisson source slices.
Finite diagnostics retain independent nonconstant profiles and natural
zeros, plus all eight local valuation configurations and64 paired cases.
They check algebra and budgets; the written argument supplies the
analytic content. Inherited F0/analytic ancestry, positive-slot
uniformity and external admission remain open. The original29 families,

## G156. Complete diagonal and two off-diagonal sectors

Merge only after the tuple cut:

\[
B_{<G}(u)Q_u=\sum_n c(n)\psi_u(n)^{\pm1},\qquad
n=d_1d_2\prod_ip_i,\quad N_0=D_1D_2P_0.
\]

The coefficient c contains every Möbius sign, fixed character, pool,
profile, independent height, normalization and original tuple gcd cut.
Each prime valuation of n is 0,1,2 or3, including all collisions. Hence
\(n/n'\) is a sixth power as an ideal only when \(n=n'\): the valuation
difference lies in [-3,3]. Finite unit/root phases remain in their fixed
sectors. This fact does not apply to older completions with unbounded
prime powers. Divisor bounds give
\(|c(n)|\ll H_JN_0^{-1/2}U^\epsilon\) and
\(\sum_n|c(n)|^2\ll H_JU^\epsilon\). The **complete** paired diagonal is
therefore \(O(H_JU^{1+\epsilon})\); this is not a lower bound for the full
norm.

For an off-diagonal pair let \(e_{\mathfrak p}=v_{\mathfrak p}(n)-
v_{\mathfrak p}(n')\), let q_j be the radical of primes with
\(|e_{\mathfrak p}|=j\), and write

\[
Q_j=Nq_j,\quad Q=Q_1Q_2Q_3,\quad V=Q_1Q_2^2Q_3^3.
\]

Retain the full oriented integer vector. Although signs +3 and -3 have
the same sextic phase, their integer ratios differ; the finite allocation
cost must not be discarded. Every nonzero exponent has nonprincipal
primitive local phase at a good prime. The fixed factor \(\nu\) stays
in c and is not falsely treated as order six.

Write \(n=ga,n'=gb,(a,b)=1\). Then \(NaNb=V\) and
\(Ng\ll N_0/\sqrt V\), so for one full relative vector

\[
\sum_{(n,n')\text{ inducing it}}|c(n)c(n')|
\ll H_JU^\epsilon V^{-1/2}.
\]

This includes all shared slot/inverse collisions. Counting vectors in
fixed dyadic Q1,Q2,Q3 boxes gives mass
\(\ll H_JU^\epsilon(Q_1/Q_3)^{1/2}\). Empty subunit gcd ranges remain
empty, with fixed endpoint constants retained.

The row kernel includes **all** natural-zero holes E from shared primes
whose character phases cancel, and all retained frozen punctures not
already in the primitive conductor. Cancellation of phase does not
remove a hole. Here NE is polynomial in U. Applying the existing masked
Poisson formula, whose primitive prefactor is X/\(\sqrt Q\) and dual
scale XNh/Q, gives \(\min(X,\sqrt Q)\), with zero dual term absent.
Expand sixth-power-freeness and full holes by
\(b^6\mid u\) and \(d\mid\operatorname{rad}E\), respectively, putting
\(X=U/((Nb)^6Nd)\). Splitting at
\(Nb=(U/(Nd\sqrt Q))^{1/6}\) yields

\[
|\mathcal K(n,n')|\ll H_JU^\epsilon
\min(U,U^{1/6}Q^{5/12}).                              \tag{G156.1}
\]

The hole Euler product with exponent -1/6 is subpower. Thresholds below
one use the complete tail; conductor-sharing natural zeros and fixed
excluded/ray sectors are retained. Finitely many inducing free-row
deletions cost O(1) per kernel, already absorbed. This is not a blanket
deletion license for the raw physical row set.

Separate the paired sum disjointly: full diagonal; then Q≤\(U^{9/5}\);
then the remaining pairs with \(Q_1/Q_3\le U^{8/5}\). The low-Q sum uses
V≥Q and the divisor count to sum \(Q^{-1/12+\epsilon}\); its total is
\(\ll H_JU^{109/60+\epsilon}\). The ratio sector uses the U branch of
(G156.1) and costs \(\ll H_JU^{9/5+\epsilon}\), with every Q2 and all
holes included. Polynomial conductor ranges cost only logarithmic boxes.

| Paid part | Exponent | Minimum gap below T | Spare after .001+.002+.005 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Complete diagonal | 1 | 55853/67500 | 55313/67500 |
| Total conductor Q≤U^(9/5) | 109/60 | 182/16875 | 47/16875 |
| Remaining ratio Q1/Q3≤U^(8/5) | 9/5 | 1853/67500 | 1313/67500 |

Each raw gap exceeds 1/100 and pays the retained 1/200 margin. These are
upper bounds for paid sectors, using absolute values there; no sign or
positivity is asserted for the residual. Masked Poisson and relative-mass
machinery are reused from the exact PR9/[private research revision] sources, rather than
counted as newly proved general theorems.

# [private research revision]: plain-L2 Hankel source, complete complement and a signed obstruction

Root accepts G158–G160 after complete independent author/reviewer intake.
The accepted written constant remains
`c11=312864909/2500000000=.1251459636`. The new result removes a
derivative-norm prerequisite and identifies the exact remaining estimate;
it does not prove that estimate or increase c. The licensed density
`K=28114053/6250000` retains its preceding-c10 ancestry. Inherited analytic,
positive-slot-uniformity and external-admission obligations remain open.

Evidence: [author](hankel-source/report.md), [independent development and
review](hankel-source-review/report.md), [author exact receipt](hankel-source/exact-checks.json),
[reviewer exact receipt](hankel-source-review/receipt.json),
[input pins](hankel-source-review/input-receipt.json), and
[retention manifest](retention-manifest.json). Frozen source statements are
interpreted with the qualifications below. The changed arithmetic identity
already occurs in [DP21–24](../[private research revision]/dilation-pole-killing.md); the earlier
Sobolev formulation is [W29 R29E1–7](../creative/round29-review.md).
The full-rectangle exponential-test return is [G149](../[private research revision]/wild58-integration.md).
These are reused components, not newly claimed identities or priority.

## G158. Actual Type I removal on plain L2, including every character

Fix a Dirichlet character chi modulo q, extended by zero at nonunits;
principal, complex and imprimitive characters are included. Put
`alpha(n)=mu(n)chi(n)`, `alpha0=alpha 1_(n<=Y)`, `alpha1=alpha-alpha0`,
with integer Y>=1. Since `alpha*chi=delta_1`, literal Dirichlet convolution gives

    alpha = 2 alpha0 - alpha0*alpha0*chi + alpha1*alpha1*chi.

The pairs in these products are ordered and can share primes. Separate
pieces need not vanish on squareful integers; only their sum restores the
original coefficient. Neither squareful coefficients nor n=1 can be deleted.

For an arithmetic sequence z, write `Z(x)=sum_(n<=x) z(n)` and let
`Gamma[z]_(a,L)` be the operator on plain `L2(0,L)` with kernel
`exp(-a(t+u)) Z(exp(t+u))`, where `0<a<1`, `X=exp(2L)`.
Complex bilinear tests conjugate the test function, not the arithmetic
character. All operator norms below refer to this precise source.

Here is the prerequisite removal. If `B(y)=sum_(ell<=y)b(ell)` is zero
below 1 and bounded in modulus by Cb, then
`h(v)=exp(-av)B(exp(v))1_(v>=0)` has `L1` norm at most `Cb/a`. For each k,

    exp(-a(t+u)) B(exp(t+u)/k) = k^(-a) h(t+u-log k).

Zero extension, reflection, convolution, translation and restriction give
an operator norm at most `Cb k^(-a)/a`. This uses the complete partial sum
B before taking its modulus. No input derivatives or endpoint traces enter.
The same estimate holds for arbitrary rectangular restrictions.
An atom z(n) similarly costs at most `|z(n)| n^(-a)/a`.
With `A_Y=sum_(d<=Y)|alpha(d)|d^(-a) <<_a Y^(1-a)`, a nonprincipal
character has `Cb<=q`, and therefore

    | ||Gamma[alpha]|| - ||Gamma[alpha1*alpha1*chi]|| |
       <= (2 A_Y + q A_Y^2)/a <<_(a,q) Y^(2(1-a)).

This conclusion is not asserted for the principal character unchanged.
Indeed at Y=1 its removed piece is `2 delta_1-chi`; its partial sum is
`-(phi(q)/q)x+O_q(1)`. Its operator norm is
`(phi(q)/q)(exp(2(1-a)L)-1)/(2(1-a))+O_(a,q)(1)`.
This is the removed operator's size, not a lower bound for the full sum.

For a repair valid for every fixed character, choose a fixed prime r not
dividing q and set

    kappa = delta_1 - r chi(r) delta_r,
    c = kappa*alpha,                 b = kappa*chi.

Thus `c(n)=mu(n)chi(n)-r chi(r)1_(r|n)mu(n/r)chi(n/r)`; it is a
different coefficient sequence, including its possible squareful terms.
The sequence b is periodic of period qr with mean zero. Writing
`C_chi(y)=1_(chi principal)(phi(q)/q)y+E_chi(y)`, with `|E_chi(y)|<=q`,
shows `B(y)=C_chi(y)-r chi(r)C_chi(y/r)` is bounded by `q(1+r)`.
The linear terms cancel for the principal character, for which chi(r)=1.
Consequently the exact identity and norm comparison are

    c = 2 kappa*alpha0 - alpha0*alpha0*b + alpha1*alpha1*b,
    T_Y = Gamma[alpha1*alpha1*b],
    | ||Gamma[c]|| - ||T_Y|| |
      <= [2(1+r^(1-a)) A_Y + q(1+r) A_Y^2]/a.

The actual remaining partial sum is
`sum_(d,e>Y; de<=x) alpha(d)alpha(e) B(x/(de))`.
After expanding B it retains the joint cap `de ell<=x`, not merely
the individual bounds `d,e<=X/(Y+1)`, `ell<=X/(Y+1)^2`.

For completeness, the source return is literal. Initially in Re s>1,
`sum c(n)n^(-s)=m_r(s)/L(s,chi)`, where
`m_r(s)=1-chi(r)r^(1-s)`. G149's exponential test gives
`-d/ds[m_r(s)/(s L(s,chi))]`. A diagonal-box bound
`||Gamma[c]_(a,L)|| << exp(2 eta L)` controls every unit rectangle:
opposite translations preserve t+u and put rectangles i,j in a balanced
box of upper endpoint `(i+j)/2+1`. At a heavier weight sigma>a+eta,
their costs are bounded by a constant times
`exp(-(sigma-a-eta)(i+j))`, a summable double series.
Hence bounds `||Gamma[c]|| <<_(chi,epsilon) X^(gamma-a+epsilon)` for
every epsilon>0 and all L make that differentiated transform holomorphic
in Re s>gamma. Any zero rho of L with `gamma<Re rho<1` creates an
uncancelled pole: m_r has zeros only on Re s=1, rho is nonzero, and
differentiation raises the pole order. This single-repaired-source return
**retains the previously accepted safe-region premise Re s>=1**;
it does not silently prove that premise or rule out numerator cancellation
on that line. The principal pole at 1 is not an L-zero. Imprimitive factors
remain literal. No height-uniform lower bound on m_r is needed or claimed.
The unrepaired nonprincipal version uses G149 without this numerator.

## G159. All arithmetic and frequency complements are accounted for

Split the actual d,e sum disjointly into d=e, d!=e with gcd(d,e)>R,
and d!=e with gcd(d,e)<=R. The last class includes equality at R.
The first has partial sum at most `Cb sqrt(x)` in modulus, so its norm
is at most `Cb D_a(X)`, where

    D_a(X) = integral_0^L exp(2(1/2-a)t) dt.

It is O(X^(1/2-a)) for a<1/2, equals L for a=1/2, and is O(1) for
a>1/2. This estimate does not treat chi(d)^2 as positive.
For the second class, write d=gu,e=gv and discard coprimality only in
the positive counting bound. The count is at most
`x(1+log x) sum_(g>R)g^(-2) << x(1+log x)/R`.
Restoring the complete B before taking absolute values gives norm
`O_(a,q,r)(X^(1-a)(1+log X)/R)`.

For the third class define its exact coefficient

    C_Y,R(n) = sum_(de ell=n; d,e>Y; d!=e; gcd(d,e)<=R)
                   alpha(d)alpha(e)b(ell),
    S(x) = sum_(n<=x) C_Y,R(n).

The observed kernel is `k(v)=exp(-av)S(exp(v))1_(0<=v<=log X)`.
With Fourier convention `hat k(tau)=integral k(v)exp(-i tau v)dv`
and `s=a+i tau`, direct integration of each atom gives

    hat k(tau) = [F_Y,X(s) - X^(-s) S(X)]/s,
    F_Y,X(s) = sum_(n<=X) C_Y,R(n)n^(-s).

Both the complete hyperbolic cap and the sharp endpoint term are essential.
An atom at n=X cancels in this expression, consistent with a corner of
measure zero. Nonintegral X uses its literal summation cap.
The estimates
`sum_(n<=X)|C_Y,R(n)|n^(-a) << X^(1-a)(1+log X)^2` and
`|S(X)| << Cb X(1+log X)` yield
`|hat k(tau)| << X^(1-a)(1+log X)^2/(1+|tau|)`.

Split the entire full-line multiplier at `|tau|<=Omega` and its complement,
then reflect, extend and compress to L2(0,L). This defines Tlo and Thi,
with exact `Tlo+Thi` equal to the third arithmetic class and

    ||Thi|| <<_(a,q,r) X^(1-a)(1+log X)^2/Omega.

The low-pass kernel need not be causal; the full-line multiplier definition
makes the compression legitimate. A uniform full-symbol bound is sufficient
for the compressed norm, but is not necessary or equivalent to it.
A finite frequency sample or a rectangularized Dirichlet polynomial does
not supply the missing estimate.

Combining these disjoint contributions gives the complete comparison

    | ||Gamma[c]|| - ||Tlo_(Y,R,L,Omega)|| | <<_(a,q,r)
       Y^(2(1-a)) + D_a(X)
       + X^(1-a)(1+log X)/R + X^(1-a)(1+log X)^2/Omega.

The original nonprincipal source obeys the same formula with b=chi,c=alpha.
No comparison with a different detector's native norm is asserted.

Choose `0<a<gamma<1`, `gamma>1/2`, and
`0<nu<min(gamma-a,gamma-1/2)`. Put
`delta=(gamma-a-nu)/(2(1-a))`, `omega=1-gamma+2nu`,
`Y=floor(X^delta)`, `R=floor(X^omega)`, `Omega=X^omega`.
Then 0<delta<1/2. The Type I exponent is gamma-a-nu, the high-gcd and
high-frequency exponents are gamma-a-2nu before logarithms, and the
diagonal is strictly smaller. All these errors fit below the target.
What remains is exactly

    OPEN-LOW: ||Tlo_(Y,R,L,Omega)||
                 <<_(chi,epsilon) X^(gamma-a+epsilon)
              for every epsilon>0 and all L.

Parameters are fixed before X. The exponent gamma must be common to all
fixed characters; constants and onset may depend on chi and the fixed
repair prime. For these same cutoffs, the complete comparison makes
OPEN-LOW equivalent to the corresponding full-source growth bound up to
the displayed smaller error. Naming it does not create an arithmetic gain.

The following exact corridors use a=1/2:

| conditional c | gamma | nu | delta | omega | d,e exponent cap | ell exponent cap | paid exponent | open X exponent |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| .12515 | 17497/20000 | 1/20000 | 937/2500 | 501/4000 | 1563/2500 | 313/1250 | 937/2500 | 7497/20000 |
| 1/6 | 5/6 | 1/600 | 199/600 | 17/100 | 401/600 | 101/300 | 199/600 | 1/3 |
| 1/4 | 3/4 | 1/1000 | 249/1000 | 63/250 | 751/1000 | 251/500 | 249/1000 | 1/4 |

The first would improve current c11 by `10091/2500000000=.0000040364`
if OPEN-LOW and its complete return were supplied. Its required L-growth
exponent is .7497, below current .7497080728. All three remain conditional;
changing a alone does not save a power.

## G160. Every fixed character has a large isolated low-frequency sector

This independent extension identifies necessary cancellation. In either
source B(y)=1 for 1<=y<2. Let P_X be the unramified primes in
`sqrt(3X/5)<p<=sqrt(7X/10)`, set `c0=(1/2)log(5/4)`, and
`J=[L-c0,L]`. On J squared, `x=exp(t+u)` lies in `[4X/5,X]`,
whereas each product pp' lies in `(3X/5,7X/10]`. Thus
`8/7<=x/(pp')<5/3`, and B is exactly 1. Distinct ordered prime pairs
survive d,e>Y and gcd<=R for every corridor above.

The ordinary prime number theorem gives
`|P_X| ~ 2(sqrt(7/10)-sqrt(3/5))sqrt(X)/log X`;
removing finitely many ramified primes does not affect this asymptotic.
Only the ordinary PNT is used, not primes in progressions; see
[NIST DLMF 27.2.3](https://dlmf.nist.gov/27.2.E3).

Partition P_X into the finitely many values lambda of chi(p). At every
sufficiently large X some class has at least |P_X|/d primes, where d is
the size of the character's image on units. On pairs from that class,
`mu(p)mu(p')chi(p)chi(p')=lambda^2`, a constant of modulus 1.
The isolated sector's compression to J is therefore rank one with norm

    N_lambda(N_lambda-1) X^(-a)
         (exp(2a c0)-1)/(2a) >>_(chi,a) X^(1-a)/(log X)^2.

The large phase may vary with X. Finite pigeonhole gives one fixed phase
on an unbounded subsequence, not every phase for all X. No progression
equidistribution premise is hidden here.

This sector also survives the frequency cut: pp'>3X/5 forces ell=1 in
the entire observed cap, so its own endpoint/weighted coefficient mass
is O(X^(1-a)/(log X)^2). The same exact Fourier identity bounds its
high-frequency norm by `O(X^(1-a)/(Omega (log X)^2))`.
As Omega grows, its low-frequency part still has the displayed lower
bound. Hence isolated sectors cannot each obey the desired gamma<1 bound.

This is **not** a lower bound for the full signed Tlo, Gamma[c], Gamma[alpha]
or a native detector. Arithmetic selection is not an orthogonal operator
projection, and signed subset monotonicity is false. If OPEN-LOW holds,
the sum of the remaining low-frequency sectors must itself have norm at
least this order along that subsequence, by the reverse triangle inequality,
and must cancel the displayed sector. The next useful estimate must keep
this interaction rather than bound each sector separately.

## Verification and next estimate

Both complete reports, both exact helpers and both receipts were read.
The author checks fixed principal, complex and imprimitive characters,
literal convolution, squareful/nonunit behavior, endpoint arithmetic,
partitions and rational corridors. The independent helper uses different
characters and develops the all-character phase argument. Its finite
examples verify algebra, not the PNT, asymptotic norm estimates or OPEN-LOW.
No redundant helper rerun, formalization or kernel claim is substituted
for written mathematical review.

Twelve frozen artifacts and ten input pins are retained. Those ten include
seven mathematical sources, one historical index and two assignment records.
The index pin is bound to its exact [private research revision] Git blob, not overwritten to
match the advanced current index. Both authorship scopes are STOP/released.
No host-local claim is copied into canonical research.

The useful next target is a signed estimate for the full compressed
low-frequency operator, preserving the hyperbolic cap, endpoint and phase
interactions. G160 rules out sector-by-sector absolute payment. Compatible
mixed-detector or adaptive-cutoff components may be used only with a proved
transfer into this precise source. The 29-family/109-child portfolio and
all later mechanisms remain preserved; near gain, 1/6 and 1/4 remain live.

    F_Y,X(s) = sum_(n<=X) C_Y,R(n)n^(-s).

Both the complete hyperbolic cap and the sharp endpoint term are essential.
An atom at n=X cancels in this expression, consistent with a corner of
measure zero. Nonintegral X uses its literal summation cap.
The estimates
`sum_(n<=X)|C_Y,R(n)|n^(-a) << X^(1-a)(1+log X)^2` and
`|S(X)| << Cb X(1+log X)` yield
`|hat k(tau)| << X^(1-a)(1+log X)^2/(1+|tau|)`.

Split the entire full-line multiplier at `|tau|<=Omega` and its complement,
then reflect, extend and compress to L2(0,L). This defines Tlo and Thi,
with exact `Tlo+Thi` equal to the third arithmetic class and

    ||Thi|| <<_(a,q,r) X^(1-a)(1+log X)^2/Omega.

The low-pass kernel need not be causal; the full-line multiplier definition
makes the compression legitimate. A uniform full-symbol bound is sufficient
for the compressed norm, but is not necessary or equivalent to it.
A finite frequency sample or a rectangularized Dirichlet polynomial does
not supply the missing estimate.

Combining these disjoint contributions gives the complete comparison

    | ||Gamma[c]|| - ||Tlo_(Y,R,L,Omega)|| | <<_(a,q,r)
       Y^(2(1-a)) + D_a(X)
       + X^(1-a)(1+log X)/R + X^(1-a)(1+log X)^2/Omega.

The original nonprincipal source obeys the same formula with b=chi,c=alpha.

`0<nu<min(gamma-a,gamma-1/2)`. Put
`delta=(gamma-a-nu)/(2(1-a))`, `omega=1-gamma+2nu`,

high-frequency exponents are gamma-a-2nu before logarithms, and the
diagonal is strictly smaller. All these errors fit below the target.

    OPEN-LOW: ||Tlo_(Y,R,L,Omega)||
                 <<_(chi,epsilon) X^(gamma-a+epsilon)
              for every epsilon>0 and all L.

Parameters are fixed before X. The exponent gamma must be common to all
fixed characters; constants and onset may depend on chi and the fixed
repair prime. For these same cutoffs, the complete comparison makes
OPEN-LOW equivalent to the corresponding full-source growth bound up to
the displayed smaller error. Naming it does not create an arithmetic gain.

| conditional c | gamma | nu | delta | omega | d,e exponent cap | ell exponent cap | paid exponent | open X exponent |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| .12515 | 17497/20000 | 1/20000 | 937/2500 | 501/4000 | 1563/2500 | 313/1250 | 937/2500 | 7497/20000 |
| 1/6 | 5/6 | 1/600 | 199/600 | 17/100 | 401/600 | 101/300 | 199/600 | 1/3 |
| 1/4 | 3/4 | 1/1000 | 249/1000 | 63/250 | 751/1000 | 251/500 | 249/1000 | 1/4 |

if OPEN-LOW and its complete return were supplied. Its required L-growth

## G160. Every fixed character has a large isolated low-frequency sector

This independent extension identifies necessary cancellation. In either
source B(y)=1 for 1<=y<2. Let P_X be the unramified primes in
`sqrt(3X/5)<p<=sqrt(7X/10)`, set `c0=(1/2)log(5/4)`, and
`J=[L-c0,L]`. On J squared, `x=exp(t+u)` lies in `[4X/5,X]`,
whereas each product pp' lies in `(3X/5,7X/10]`. Thus
`8/7<=x/(pp')<5/3`, and B is exactly 1. Distinct ordered prime pairs
survive d,e>Y and gcd<=R for every corridor above.

The ordinary prime number theorem gives
`|P_X| ~ 2(sqrt(7/10)-sqrt(3/5))sqrt(X)/log X`;
removing finitely many ramified primes does not affect this asymptotic.
Only the ordinary PNT is used, not primes in progressions; see
[NIST DLMF 27.2.3](https://dlmf.nist.gov/27.2.E3).

Partition P_X into the finitely many values lambda of chi(p). At every
sufficiently large X some class has at least |P_X|/d primes, where d is
the size of the character's image on units. On pairs from that class,
`mu(p)mu(p')chi(p)chi(p')=lambda^2`, a constant of modulus 1.
The isolated sector's compression to J is therefore rank one with norm

    N_lambda(N_lambda-1) X^(-a)
         (exp(2a c0)-1)/(2a) >>_(chi,a) X^(1-a)/(log X)^2.

The large phase may vary with X. Finite pigeonhole gives one fixed phase
on an unbounded subsequence, not every phase for all X. No progression
equidistribution premise is hidden here.

This sector also survives the frequency cut: pp'>3X/5 forces ell=1 in
the entire observed cap, so its own endpoint/weighted coefficient mass
is O(X^(1-a)/(log X)^2). The same exact Fourier identity bounds its
high-frequency norm by `O(X^(1-a)/(Omega (log X)^2))`.
As Omega grows, its low-frequency part still has the displayed lower
bound. Hence isolated sectors cannot each obey the desired gamma<1 bound.

This is **not** a lower bound for the full signed Tlo, Gamma[c], Gamma[alpha]
or a native detector. Arithmetic selection is not an orthogonal operator
projection, and signed subset monotonicity is false. If OPEN-LOW holds,
the sum of the remaining low-frequency sectors must itself have norm at
least this order along that subsequence, by the reverse triangle inequality,
and must cancel the displayed sector. The next useful estimate must keep
this interaction rather than bound each sector separately.

# [private research revision]: short arithmetic moves and the complete signed remainder

Root accepts G161–G163 after complete mathematical intake of the
[W60 author](wild60/report.md) and [independent critic](wild60-review/report.md).
The main advance is a source-specific obstruction to fixed prime-factor
replacement budgets, even for complex flows. It redirects local matching
and coding constructions toward growing replacement counts or signed
estimates. It is not a lower bound for a full signed Möbius sum.

The accepted written value remains `c11=312864909/2500000000=.1251459636`,
with `gamma11=2187135091/2500000000=.8748540364`. The density constant
`K=28114053/6250000` retains preceding-c10 same-family ancestry.
Inherited analytic, positive-slot-uniformity and external-admission
obligations remain open. No formalization, new packet or public-record claim.

## G161. A fixed replacement budget leaves a large actual residual

Fix an ordinary character chi modulo a fixed q. The arithmetic source is
`a(n)=mu(n)chi(n)`, with squareful and nonunit zeros and n=1 retained.
It is distinct from the Eisenstein native-H coefficient system below.

Suppose every allowed edge {n,m}, n!=m, obeys
`|n-m|<=C min(n,m)^theta`, where `C>0`, `0<=theta<1`, and at each
squarefree endpoint at most a fixed d>=1 of its prime factors are deleted
when moving to the other endpoint. The restriction applies independently
at each squarefree endpoint, regardless of flow orientation. Auxiliary
squareful/nonunit integer vertices are permitted under this same rule.

Let g=gcd(n,m). Since g divides n-m,

    g<=|n-m|,       n/g >= C^(-1)n^(1-theta).

For squarefree n, the quotient n/g is exactly the product of its deleted
prime factors. If every prime of n is at most y, the budget implies
`n/g<=y^d`. Thus `n^(1-theta)>C y^d` makes n isolated in the entire graph,
including edges to integers outside the current shell or cutoff.

Choose a fixed integer `k>d/(1-theta)`. Products of k distinct primes in
`(X^(1/k),(2X)^(1/k)]` lie in `(X,2X]`, are squarefree, and eventually
avoid every prime dividing the fixed q. With `y=(2X)^(1/k)`,

    n^(1-theta)/(C y^d)
      >= C^(-1)2^(-d/k) X^(1-theta-d/k) -> infinity.

Every such product is therefore isolated for every sufficiently large X.
The ordinary prime number theorem gives, for this fixed k,
`t_X ~ k(2^(1/k)-1)X^(1/k)/log X` primes in the interval.
Unique factorization gives exactly binomial(t_X,k) products, hence

    |V_X| ~ A_k X/(log X)^k,
    A_k=[k(2^(1/k)-1)]^k/k! >0.

Only the ordinary PNT is used; see [NIST DLMF §27.12](https://dlmf.nist.gov/27.12).
There is no progression equidistribution, short-interval theorem, growing-k
substitution or uniformity in a modulus that can absorb those primes.
The constant may be tiny and the onset large, without changing the exponent.

For any complex flow F on this graph with defined divergence, an exact
source decomposition `a=div F+r` has `r(n)=a(n)` at every isolated n.
Therefore

    sum_(X<n<=2X)|r(n)| >= |V_X|.

No positivity, disjointness, bounded flow coefficients or acyclicity is
required. Repeated short steps cannot start at an isolated vertex.
This rules out `O_(epsilon)(X^(delta+epsilon))` absolute residual bounds
for delta<1: choose epsilon<(1-delta)/2. A bounded collection of budgets
is covered by its maximum; subpower inflation of C is absorbed by a
slightly larger fixed theta<1 before choosing k. No conclusion is claimed
for an unbounded d or k without a separate quantitative argument.

| displacement exponent theta | d | k | strict margin 1-theta-d/k |
|---|---|---|---|
| 17497/20000=.87485 | 3 | 24 | 3/20000 |
| current gamma11 | 3 | 24 | 364909/2500000000 |
| 5/6 | 3 | 19 | 1/114 |
| 3/4 | 3 | 13 | 1/52 |

For principal chi, the isolated k-prime layer has constant sign (-1)^k.
This does not control its cancellation with the other layers or the rest
of r. For complex chi, even that layer need not have constant phase.
There is no resulting lower bound for `|sum r|`, `|M_chi|`, a full detector
norm or a zero-free exponent. A viable local construction must instead
pay a growing number of deleted primes, at least
`((1-theta)log n-log C)/log y` at a y-smooth endpoint, or retain the full
signed interaction with other sectors. Long edges and different auxiliary
transfers also remain eligible. This is a record-relative refinement of
U-PRIME-CHAIN/U-TRANSPORT and the coding portfolio, not a literature claim.

### Character phase and the complete conditional return

For a finite set of unramified primes and `w(S)=(-1)^|S|chi(product S)`,
an exact toggle C has

    w(S xor C)/w(S) = (-1)^|C| product_(p in C)chi(p)
                                  product_(p in S intersect C)chi(p)^(-2).

It equals -1 for every state of the full Boolean cube exactly when
`chi(p)^2=1` for each p in C and `(-1)^|C|product_C chi(p)=-1`.
Necessity uses the empty state and each singleton; sufficiency is substitution.
No ramified character value is inverted. A cutoff-restricted state set can
have additional exchanges; this universal-cube test does not forbid them.
For the quartic character modulo 5 with chi(2)=i,chi(3)=-i,chi(11)=1,
the toggle {2,3,11} reverses 1 and 66 but gives the same coefficient -i
at 2 and 33. The state-specific exchange 6<->11 remains valid.

The global matching return is retained from transport ancestry. Suppose
one global disjoint pairing has opposite actual coefficients, the above
displacement exponent theta, and unmatched count
`O_(chi,epsilon)(x^(delta+epsilon))` for every epsilon>0. Pairs wholly
below x cancel exactly. Crossing pairs have distinct lower endpoints in
`[x-C x^theta,x]`, so

    |M_chi(x)| <= C x^theta+O_(chi,epsilon)(x^(delta+epsilon))+O_chi(1).

For a common `gamma=max(theta,delta)>0`, normal convergence of
`s integral_1^infinity M_chi(x)x^(-s-1)dx` and its derivatives on
Re s>gamma gives continuation of the actual reciprocal 1/L(s,chi).
Choose epsilon below each compact's horizontal margin. The meromorphic
identity L F=1 excludes regular zeros there; a principal pole forces
a reciprocal zero and is allowed. Imprimitive Euler factors and every
fixed height remain literal. Constants/onsets may depend on fixed chi.
Different finite-cutoff matchings do not automatically form this global
pairing. The bound is conditional, not supplied by the algebra.
Gamma=.87485,5/6,3/4 would return c=.12515,1/6,1/4; the near conditional
gain over current c11 is 10091/2500000000. G161 blocks the fixed-budget
construction's absolute unmatched premise, not all possible signed returns.

## G162. All finite comparable matchings have a terminal-prime cut

In the finite squarefree q-unit set n<=X, each unramified prime p in
`(X/2,X]` has exactly one distinct comparable vertex, namely 1.
It has no other divisor and no proper multiple inside the cutoff.
Every disjoint pairing along divisibility therefore leaves at least
`#{X/2<p<=X,p not dividing q}-1` terminal primes unmatched.
For a nonnegative fractional matching with vertex capacity 1, their total
incident weight is also at most the capacity of 1; the same bound applies
to unmatched mass. Character restrictions can only remove edges.

Ordinary PNT makes this asymptotic to X/(2 log X), for fixed q.
No acyclicity is used: the result covers adaptive pivots and comparable
pairs differing by several primes. It does not apply to arbitrary complex
shared-vertex homotopies, incomparable pairs or partners beyond the cutoff.
It is not a lower bound on G150's global future-partner displacement cost.

The exact decomposition `M_chi(X)=A_p(X)-chi(p)A_p(X/p)` with
`A_p(Y)=sum_(n<=Y,p not dividing n)mu(n)chi(n)` is already G144 ancestry.
Choosing chi(p)=1 does not bound the remaining boundary term.
The new cut has wider matching scope but a weaker numerical lower bound
than the linear count for G144's specified cone. W59's additional homology
argument remains separately frozen, root-pending evidence; this acceptance
does not promote it. Incomparable exchanges such as 6<->11 avoid this cut,
but bounded short replacements still face G161.

## G163. Exact native Schur and four-cycle bills

These independent audits clarify complete costs, rather than provide
an arithmetic saving. Freeze an actual finite native-H packet and its two
independent heights. Keep the Eisenstein primary/fixed-ray/six-unit/bad-place
data, distinct-rational-norm long primes, both orientations, every ordered
short pair including equality, bounded complex h, rational gcd screen,
both projectors, natural zeros, all profiles and CRT phases.
The source contract is [[restricted research revision] §1](../[private research revision]/h-joint/report.md), with the
corrected matrix convention in [G75 review R10–R11](../[private research revision]/wild46-review/report.md).

Specifically, `v_P=u1(P)/sqrt(q_P)`, `w_P'=u2(P')/sqrt(q_P')`,
and the scalar sum `sum v_P K_PP' conjugate(w_P')` is `H=w* T v`
with `T=K^T`. The rooted marks are in v,w **once**. Every other original
factor is in T. This explicit reviewer convention controls the author's
compressed Section5 wording that could double-count the roots.
The raw target is `B0 sqrt(Omega1 Omega2)`, where
`B0=G K0[N+L+(NL)^(2/3)]P_orig`, K0 is the original row parameter and
P_orig the actual profile/component costs. Apply `N^(-1)G^(-2)` once
afterward. Full heights, tails, components and other branches remain due.

For a partition `T=[T_R,T_E]`, `v=(u,z)`, let Pi be the output projection
onto ran T_E. Then, exactly,

    ||Tv||^2 = ||(I-Pi)T_R u||^2 + ||Pi T_R u+T_E z||^2,
    S=T_R*(I-Pi)T_R=A-B D^dagger B*,
    A=T_R*T_R, B=T_R*T_E, D=T_E*T_E.

The singular case follows from ker D=ker T_E, B annihilating this kernel,
and `T_E D^dagger T_E*=Pi`. Thus S>=0 and the fill-in is bounded by A.
For `D_lambda=D+lambda I`, lambda>0, there is also the exact completion

    v*(T*T)v = u*(A-B D_lambda^(-1)B*)u
      +(z+D_lambda^(-1)B*u)*D_lambda(z+D_lambda^(-1)B*u)
      -lambda ||z||^2.

A small Schur term alone does not bound the full source: z is fixed,
not freely minimized. The projection has norm 1, while an inverse
representation must pay its own spectral distance. For the synthetic
matrix `[[1,1,1],[0,e,-e]]`, e!=0, eliminating columns 2,3 makes S=0,
yet the source u=1,z=0 has energy 1 in the completion. This is an algebra
diagnostic, not an evaluated native packet. A sufficient OPEN-SC is the
sum of both displayed squared norms <=`B0^2(||u||^2+||z||^2)` with all
original uniformities. It is the full source bill after elimination.
Prior [G107](../[private research revision]/wild51-integration.md) and U-VARIATIONAL retain credit.

For two distinct input columns j,k, put
`b_i=conjugate(T_ij)T_ik`, `s_jk=sum_i|b_i|`,
`eta_i=b_i/|b_i|` only on nonzero entries, and
`psi_jk=sum_(i<l)|b_i||b_l||eta_i-eta_l|^2` over active pairs.
Expansion gives

    |(T*T)_jk|^2 = s_jk^2-psi_jk,
    ||T||^2 <= max_j [sum_i|T_ij|^2
                         +sum_(k!=j)sqrt(s_jk^2-psi_jk)],
    ||T||^4 <= sum_j (sum_i|T_ij|^2)^2
                         +sum_(j!=k)(s_jk^2-psi_jk).

The phase is the four-edge product
`conjugate(T_ij)T_ik T_lj conjugate(T_lk)` divided by its modulus.
Natural-zero entries contribute zero without division. The Hermitian
dilation is bipartite on two separate mark spaces, so it has no triangular
cycle even if the numerical labels coincide. Transported unitary gauges
preserve this four-cycle invariant; fixing source vectors while gauging
the matrix changes H. Short-core interference must remain inside each T entry.

An arithmetic bound on the complete Gram-row expression by B0 squared,
or on the complete fourth-moment expression by B0 to the fourth power,
would suffice. The diagonal and every significant coherent component
remain. A few frustrated cycles or a constant local deficit do not supply
a power saving. The 2-by-2 unit-entry formula `2+2|cos(Phi/2)|` is already
G75, and [W40's retained phase-length scope](../[private research revision]/reviewed-library-integration.md)
remains relevant. No native phase values were numerically evaluated here.

## Other tested cards, sampling and verification

- Card28: rational `a(pn)=-chi(p)a(n)` is not a licensed constraint on
  independent native-H mark arrays. An upstream transported relation remains open.
- Card26: a nonzero Hermitian bilinear dilation has positive and negative
  eigenvalues. A locally finite positive real linear MGF has positive
  semidefinite log Hessian at zero, so cannot represent that indefinite
  quadratic exponential. Complex Gaussian linearization is exact but
  taking modulus loses its imaginary-phase cancellation; nonlinear or
  complex alternatives are not excluded as families.
- Card25: the two-prime based complex with maps `(-b,a)^T` and `(a,b)`
  has torsion 1 up to sign, not ab. The finite determinant calculation uses
  the alternating convention in [Hutchings (2002), Appendix A](https://math.berkeley.edu/~hutching/pub/rt3/rt3.pdf).
  A direct sum stores the product but does not create cutoff cancellation;
  a truncated nonacyclic complex requires a different readout.
- Card30: the full Hermitian cyclic subspace is reducing, so its proposed
  Feshbach self-energy vanishes. Source-line projection has a nontrivial
  Schur resolvent, whose first/second moments still contain H or ||Tv|| squared.
  The spectral estimate remains unpaid. The full-cyclicity example is synthetic.

These failures retain their specified realizations and reopening conditions;
they do not retire whole detector, coding, spectral or complex-field families.
All 30 seed cards are retained, including the corrected-but-frozen Card10
notation: the left side should be a(pn), not bare mu(pn).
Six author tests are28/23/12/26/25/30. Literal all-group pools25/15/25
and indices21/11/24 produce26/25/30 with immutable entropy and no reroll.
Independent priorities and permutation froze before outcome intake;
mechanical exclusions force protected20 and uniform27. The persistence
receipt followed report intake, as disclosed, rather than claiming an
earlier receipt. Twenty-two remaining cards are untested in this round.

Thirty frozen artifacts, twelve reviewer source bindings and fifteen author
source bindings are retained in the [manifest](retention-manifest.json).
Historical mutable sources bind to exact Git blobs. The host-local claim
receipt is checked in place and excluded; its manifest hash entry remains
as provenance. Both STOPs and own releases were reconciled.
Both complete reports/helpers and exact receipts were read, together with
literal native source/ancestry slices and the primary external inputs.
No helper was rerun for reassurance. Finite matching, phase, endpoint,
Schur and cycle diagnostics support indexing/algebra, not the asymptotic
PNT-based proof, an actual native-H evaluation or a stronger c.

The next mathematical target is an exact growing-replacement interaction
or a signed bound on the complete smooth isolated complement coupled to
the larger-prime exchanges. Its displacement, phases and full return must
all be paid. Chained and simultaneous components remain usable through
proved transfers. Original 29 families/109 children and later work survive.
