# [private research revision]: weighted boundary spectrum and complete source transfers

Root accepts G164–G166 after the complete author and independent critic
reports, developments, exact helpers and receipts were read. The useful
increment is a uniform obstruction for arbitrary moving prime weights,
including weights that vanish at the smallest basis primes. It extends the
character-gauge/cone analysis in [G144–G145](../[private research revision]/wild57-integration.md).
The incidence and prime-removal tools retain every term needed to return
to the actual arithmetic source. No complete signed estimate or improved c
is proved. The highest accepted written value remains
312864909/2500000000 = 0.1251459636.

Frozen evidence: [author](wild59/report.md), [weighted development](wild59/fock-boundary.md),
[prime-removal development](wild59/renewal-overlap.md),
[independent review](wild59-review/report.md), and
[retention/source bindings](retention-manifest.json). These preserve all30
cards, six author first tests and two independent audits. Actual host-local
claim bytes are excluded. Source manifest timestamps pin captured bytes,
not an earlier whole-file reading of a concurrently maintained document.

## G164. Least-active-prime boundary multiplicity

Fix an ordinary Dirichlet character χ modulo q. The source is
a(n)=μ(n)χ(n), including a(1)=1 and all squareful/nonunit zeros. Let P be a
finite set of primes coprime to q containing all such primes at most N;
additional primes larger than N are allowed. Use the ordered exterior basis
indexed by squarefree products of P, with creation operators c_p and their
usual fermionic signs. Let Π project onto products at most N, Q=I−Π, and

\[
d=\sum_{p\in P}w_pc_p,\quad W=\sum_p|w_p|^2>0,\quad
D=\Pi d\Pi,\quad B=Qd\Pi,\quad E=B^*B.
\]

All weights may be complex, N-dependent, and zero. Divisor closure gives
Qd*Π=0 and ΠdQ=0. The canonical anticommutation relations therefore imply

\[
D^2=0,\qquad D^*D+DD^*=W\Pi-E,\qquad 0\le E\le W\Pi.       \tag{95.1}
\]

Let p* be the least **active** prime, meaning w_p*≠0. Define U to be the
span of p*-free basis states with N/p*<n≤N. Every active creation kills U
after truncation, so D|U=0. On V_N/U, the operator
(1/w_p*)c_p*^* is a contracting homotopy: the full anticommutator is the
identity, and every term that fails to cancel after truncation lies in U.
The long exact sequence of the quotient complex identifies H(D) with U
as graded vector spaces. Finite-dimensional Hodge theory and (95.1) give

\[
\dim\ker(E-WI)=\dim H(D)=C_{p_*}(N),\qquad
C_p(N)=\#\{N/p<n\le N:\mu(n)^2=1,(n,q)=1,p\nmid n\}.       \tag{95.2}
\]

This is an eigenspace **dimension**, not a statement that the critical
basis vectors themselves are harmonic. For example, at q=1,N=12 the
critical states7 and11 need not be killed by D*. The quotient contraction
need not have a uniform norm when w_p* tends to zero. If p*>N then D=0,
U=V_N, and the same formula still holds.

Set κ_q=ζ(2)^−1∏_{p|q}p/(p+1). Square-divisor inclusion-exclusion gives
Q_q(x)=κ_q x+O_q(√x). For fixed p∤q,

\[
C_p(N)=\kappa_q\frac{p-1}{p+1}N+O_{q,p}(\sqrt N).
\]

For a bound uniform in p, handle the finitely many p<4/κ_q with this
formula. For the other primes, count q-unit squarefree states in (N/2,N]
and subtract at most N/p multiples of p. Thus, for all N sufficiently
large depending only on q, every unramified p satisfies
C_p(N)≥κ_qN/8. The trace counts outgoing creation edges exactly, so

\[
\frac{\kappa_q}{8}WN\le\operatorname{Tr}E
=\sum_p|w_p|^2C_p(N)\le WN,
\quad \|E\|=W,\quad
\dim\ker(E-WI)\ge\frac{\kappa_q}{8}N.                    \tag{95.3}
\]

Consequently no choice of these moving weights produces an ambient
positive spectral gap or a power-saving positive trace certificate.
This does **not** give a lower bound for the complete signed arithmetic
source or for another detector. Signed cancellation within the large
boundary space is still an eligible mechanism.

Let Tχ be diagonal multiplication by χ(n), and Str the parity-weighted
trace. Supertrace of the full identity gives the exact source return

\[
W M_\chi(N)=\operatorname{Str}(T_\chi E)
 +\operatorname{Str}([T_\chi,D^*]D).                     \tag{95.4}
\]

For each p, its normalized contribution is

\[
\sum_{N/p<n\le N\atop p\nmid n}a(n)
 +(1-\chi(p))\sum_{n\le N/p\atop p\nmid n}a(n)=M_\chi(N).
\]

Both endpoints, the unit, and nonunit zeros are included. Dropping the
commutator bulk is invalid for general characters. Restricting active
primes to χ(p)=1 does kill that bulk, but retains (95.3). Moving χ phases
into the differential is a unitary gauge change: it preserves the
spectrum and moves the arithmetic dependence into the observer/bulk.

An estimate for the **complete** right side of (95.4), at most
C_{χ,ε} W N^{γ+ε} for every N and ε>0, with a common 0<γ<2187135091/2500000000
over the required fixed-character family, would give Mχ(N)≪N^{γ+ε}.
The actual reciprocal-L Dirichlet series then continues through Abel
summation to Re(s)>γ, and excludes zeros there, with the allowed principal
pole treated normally. No such estimate is supplied here; no uniformity
for growing conductors or native-H transfer is inferred.

The ordered product ∏_{p increasing}(I−χ(p)c_p), acting with its largest
factor first, generates the literal μχ source. Averaging over all orders
kills degrees at least2, hence changes the source. Restoring the missing
parity/signs restores the original source. This rejects that averaging
shortcut, not all fermionic representations.

Classical ancestry is [Björner2011, Theorems2.1/3.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1101.5704)
for the squarefree complex and [Bravyi–Kitaev2000v2, Eqs1–2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/quant-ph/0003137)
for creation signs. The weighted truncated identities and uniform bound
above are proved in the frozen development; no literature novelty claim
is made.

## G165. Incidence kernels and all acyclic face matchings

On the q-unit squarefree states at most N, define natural edge observations

\[
(\nabla_\chi f)(n,p)=f(pn)+\chi(p)f(n),\qquad pn\le N.
\]

Writing f(n)=a(n)g(n) gauges this to ordinary differences, up to a unit
phase per edge. The graph is connected by deleting primes down to1, hence

\[
\ker\nabla_\chi=\operatorname{span}\{a\}.                \tag{95.5}
\]

The source one wants to estimate is the exact unobserved direction.
Unitary Fourier conjugation transports this kernel rather than removing
it. In a length-N additive transform with the original zeros retained,
the zero-frequency component is Mχ(N)/√N. For the quartic character
modulo5 at N=7, the actual coefficients on1,2,3,6,7 are
1,−i,i,1,−i: every internal flux vanishes but Mχ(7)=2−i.
Adding outgoing zero-extension observations incurs the positive boundary
cost ∑|w_p|²C_p(N). This edge-observation cost is distinguished from the
coherent operator E; they are not interchangeable quadratic forms.

For any elementary face matching, pair a lower n with upper pn. The exact
source sum decomposes into

\[
M_\chi(N)=\sum_{n\text{ critical}}a(n)
 +\sum_{(n,pn)\text{ matched}}a(n)(1-\chi(p)).            \tag{95.6}
\]

In particular, the least unramified prime ℓ gives an acyclic matching
n↔ℓn for ℓ-free n≤N/ℓ. Reversing matched edges cannot create a cycle:
after an upward ℓ edge, any permitted downward non-ℓ edge still contains ℓ.
The surviving critical count is C_ℓ(N).

More generally every acyclic elementary face matching with m pairs
satisfies m≤rank D for the unit-weight exterior differential. Select
matched upper rows and lower columns of D. An off-diagonal incidence
u_i←l_j gives the oriented alternating path u_i→l_j→u_j. Acyclicity
orders these paths, making the selected minor triangular with nonzero
diagonal. Therefore

\[
\#\text{critical}=\dim V_N-2m
 \ge\dim V_N-2\operatorname{rank}D
 =\dim H(D)=C_\ell(N)\asymp_q N.                       \tag{95.7}
\]

No such matching gives a power-saving **unweighted absolute** critical
count. This does not lower-bound the signed critical sum, nor all weighted
homotopies. Any elimination using gradient paths must retain their full
coefficients and the norm of the scalar evaluation map. In the modulo5
example, pairs1↔2 and3↔6 leave critical contribution −i and matched bulk2;
discarding the latter changes the answer.

The independent S18 audit leaves broader absorbing-boundary/scattering
operators open; S12 leaves signed dual certificates open. They require
additional observations that see (95.5) and a paid return to μχ. The
positive-count obstruction is not a rejection of those broader proposals.

## G166. Prime removal with exact correction and all-shell return

For a fixed finite prime block B, let e_B be μχ on squarefree divisors of
P_B, r_B be χ on all B-smooth integers, including prime powers, and
a_B(n)=a(n)1_{(n,P_B)=1}. With Dirichlet convolution,

\[
e_B*r_B=\delta_1,\quad a=e_B*a_B,\quad a_B=r_B*a,
\quad A_B(s)=\frac1{L(s,\chi)E_B(s)},
\quad E_B(s)=\prod_{p\in B}(1-\chi(p)p^{-s}).            \tag{95.8}
\]

For overlapping blocks, A_A A_B=A_{A∪B}A_{A∩B}. This is an exact
overlap identity; a determinant invariant under a common meromorphic
multiplier cannot exclude that multiplier's poles by itself. It preserves
the earlier overlap/renewal ancestry in [G79–G81](../[private research revision]/wild47-integration.md),
G92, G108 and [G135](../[private research revision]/wild55-integration.md).

For the field norm sup_{T>0} T^−γ||F||_{L²([T,2T],dt/t)}, Minkowski gives
the absolute forward/reverse coefficient costs

\[
\prod_{p\in B}(1+p^{-\gamma}),\qquad
\prod_{p\in B}(1-p^{-\gamma})^{-1}.                    \tag{95.9}
\]

Every shifted shell and small tail is included. These are valid coarse
bounds, not claimed sharp operator norms on a restricted arithmetic
source. A same-shell bound alone does not supply (95.9).

For smoothing kernels exp(−n/x) and exp(−(n/x)^2), the Mellin factors are,
respectively, Γ(s)/(L(s,χ)E_B(s)) and Γ(s/2)/(2L(s,χ)E_B(s)). Their gamma
factors are nonzero on Re(s)>0. A complete large-shell bound of exponent
γ, for every ε>0 and the required fixed characters, yields the usual
all-height reciprocal-L continuation by Cauchy–Schwarz and Mellin
integration, retaining small x. The principal pole is allowed. Choosing
a different block at each x does not provide one fixed Mellin transform;
the transition costs cannot be dropped. This is a conditional return,
not an estimate for the smoothed arithmetic field.

There is also a sharp-cutoff identity with an explicit small-argument
correction. If min B>√N, then for every real1≤x≤N,

\[
M_\chi(x)=M_{B,\chi}(x)
 -\sum_{p\in B,\ p\le x}\chi(p)M_\chi(x/p).            \tag{95.10}
\]

The correction uses the **original** Mχ, and includes Mχ(1)=1 at x=p.
Two removed primes cannot occur in an integer at most N. For
B⊂(N^α,N^b], 1/2<α<b<1, and an available bound
|Mχ(t)|≤C t^β on t≤N^{1−α}, where0≤β<1, elementary summation gives

\[
\left|\sum_{p\in B,p\le x}\chi(p)M_\chi(x/p)\right|
 \le C\left(1+\frac1{1-\beta}\right)
 N^{\beta+b(1-\beta)}.                                \tag{95.11}
\]

No prime number theorem is required. As b decreases to1/2, this absolute
method approaches exponent (1+β)/2. Using the current β=0.8748540364
would leave exponent greater than0.9374270182, which is inadequate.
To beat the current γ, reach5/6, or reach3/4 by this limiting budget,
one would need respectively β<0.7497080728, β<2/3, or β<1/2, as well as
the independent estimate for M_B and a strict admissible b. These are
unpaid prerequisites. An inadequate upper bound is not a lower bound
for the signed correction.

When used as detectors, the full norm is ||U_B−C_B||², including its cross
term. Chaining prime removal with another detector, or controlling both
simultaneously, remains valid only after paying (95.8)–(95.11) or a
stronger proved signed transfer. Thus the user's mixed chained/simultaneous
strategy remains open in its full scope.

## Native matrix and other audited realizations

The original [native-H source convention](../[private research revision]/h-joint-integration.md)
retains coefficients, root marks once in v,w, masks, profiles, projectors,
all branches and the original normalization. A generic Julia dilation
requires a proved r≥||T|| and K=T/r. Its exact decomposition
||Kv||²+||(I−K*K)^{1/2}v||²=||v||² preserves the entire source cost.
A small observed channel does not pay its almost-complete loss channel,
and r is not free. No native-H adapter or arithmetic norm saving follows.

S17 commutator observations can miss a constant direction; the actual
principal source modulo3 at N=12 gives M=−2 with the tested commuting
residue/equal-bin observations. This is not a theorem about every
logarithmic partition. S11 transport retains ghost and prefix-imbalance
costs. S07's cutoff mask on primes2,3 at N=5 excludes their product6 and
is not a separable tensor mask. These precise failures and reopening
conditions are retained in the reports and first tests.

The author tested S04/S22/S17 and literal uniform draws S11/S23/S07
from group pools22/11/25. Full30-card threshold counts25/12 include cards
outside those groups; no eligible in-group card was excluded for suspected
duplication. Critic priorities and permutation were frozen before its
outcome intake; independent audits were protected S18 and uniform S12.
No stronger timestamp claim for the author's initial pool construction is
made. A preliminary critic UTF8 parser failure and its corrected exact
receipt remain recorded; entropy and selections were not rerolled.

The all-character signed estimate in (95.4), a source-observing scattering
construction, and a signed prime-removal correction are the useful next
targets. Near gains,1/6,1/4, all29 original families/109 children and later
ideas remain available. F0/analytic ancestry, inherited positive-slot
uniformity and external admission remain open. No formalization, new proof
packet or public record claim is part of this cycle.

statement:
# [private research revision]: actual-source costs of positive certificates

Accept G167–G169 from the frozen [W61 author](wild61/report.md) and
[independent critic](wild61-review/report.md). The main new result supplies
actual squarefree coefficients that force an almost-linear root cost for
global positive certificates with short additive bandwidth or a small
union of permitted offsets. It extends [G129](../[private research revision]/wild54-integration.md),
with a different hypothesis and counting argument from
[G161](../[private research revision]/wild60-integration.md). Full graph, heat, occupation and
compact-source identities locate the remaining signed estimates. Reused
mechanisms retain their credit; none proves a higher c.

The accepted written c11=312864909/2500000000=.1251459636 and
γ11=2187135091/2500000000=.8748540364 remain unchanged. These are
source-relative research results, with inherited analytic/F0,
positive-slot and external admission obligations open. No formalization,
new proof packet or public record claim is part of this cycle.

## G167. Global positive majorants need sufficiently nonlocal interactions

Fix an ordinary character χ modulo fixed q and the literal vector
a_n=μ(n)χ(n),1≤n≤N, including natural zeros. Write ℓ=(1,…,1). A global
terminal certificate is a Hermitian matrix

\[
P\succeq\ell\ell^*,\qquad |M_\chi(N)|^2\le a^*Pa.       \tag{96.1}
\]

P may depend arbitrarily on χ,N and the actual source. The same results
hold after restricting to the nonzero source support, provided original
integer labels still determine matrix offsets. A certificate required
only on a separately proved reachable-state class is a different condition
and is not ruled out.

For a partition into blocks B_j, set b_j=∑_{n∈B_j}a_n. The exact optimum is

\[
\inf_{P\text{ block diagonal},\ P\succeq\ell\ell^*}a^*Pa
   =\left(\sum_j|b_j|\right)^2.                        \tag{96.2}
\]

Rotate one scalar phase on each block to align its sum. This leaves the
block-diagonal energy unchanged, while (96.1), which holds on all inputs,
forces the lower bound. Conversely use block weights
(∑|b_j|)/|b_j| times ℓ_jℓ_j*, with weighted Cauchy. Zero-sum blocks receive
an arbitrarily small reciprocal-weight share and a limit; if all sums
vanish the energy zero is attainable. This is an infimum statement, not a
claim of universal attainment or invertibility.

Suppose I consists of K squarefree q-units isolated from every other
nonzero source coordinate by P's permitted off-diagonal support. Then
P_II is diagonal, all actual I-to-complement cross terms vanish, and
P_II≽ℓ_Iℓ_I* implies ∑_{n∈I}P_nn≥K². Since |a_n|=1 on I and the
complementary principal block is positive semidefinite,

\[
a^*Pa\ge K^2.                                          \tag{96.3}
\]

This is a certificate cost, not |Mχ(N)|≥K. The dense admissible matrix
P=ℓℓ* has exactly the actual energy |Mχ(N)|² and retains distant signed
cross terms.

### Uniform arithmetic supply

For half-bandwidth h≥1, choose distinct primes p_r>h, p_r∤q, for each
0<|r|≤h. Impose

\[
n\equiv1\pmod q,\quad n\equiv-r\pmod{p_r^2},\quad
Q=q\prod_r p_r^2.
\]

The residue a_0 modulo Q is coprime to Q. Every shifted neighbor n+r is
squareful. For any coprime residue modulo any Q, square-divisor expansion
gives the explicit uniform estimate, N≥4,

\[
\#\{n\le N:n\equiv a_0\pmod Q,\ \mu(n)^2=1\}
=\frac NQ\prod_{p\nmid Q}(1-p^{-2})+R,\qquad
|R|\le3\sqrt N.                                       \tag{96.4}
\]

There are at most √N counting errors, each at most1, for d²|n with
(d,Q)=1. The omitted Euler tail contributes at most2√N/Q. The product is
at least1/ζ(2)>1/2. Deleting at most2h endpoint indices produces

\[
K\ge\max(0,N/(2Q)-3\sqrt N-2h).                        \tag{96.5}
\]

No prime theorem in progressions is used. The elementary central-binomial
bounds 4^m/(2m+1)≤binom(2m,m)≤(2m)^{π(2m)} supply π(x)≫x/log x:
each prime contributes at most2m to that factorization. Thus the required
2h primes can lie below C_q h log(2h), and

\[
\log Q\le\log q+4h\log(C_qh\log(2h)).                 \tag{96.6}
\]

For h=o(log N/loglog N), (96.3)–(96.6) force root cost N^{1−o(1)}.
For h=⌊κ log N/loglog N⌋ with fixed0<κ<1/8, they give
sqrt(a*Pa)≥N^{1−4κ−o(1)}. The upper restriction ensures the main term in
(96.5) dominates √N. Fixed h gives K≫_{q,h}N.

More generally let D_N be a symmetric set of permitted nonzero offsets,
all of absolute value at most N−1, and let k=|D_N|. Assign each r a
distinct prime not dividing qr. At any assignment at most
k−1+ω(q)+⌊log₂N⌋ primes are forbidden, so the first
J=k+ω(q)+⌊log₂N⌋+1 primes suffice. Their sizes are O(J log(2J)). The same
CRT construction gives

\[
\log Q\le\log q+2k\log(CJ\log(2J)),\qquad
K\ge\max(0,N/(2Q)-3\sqrt N).                           \tag{96.7}
\]

Neighbors outside the cutoff are irrelevant; no endpoint deletion is
needed. Hence k=o(log N/loglog N) also forces root cost N^{1−o(1)}, and
k∼κ log N/loglog N,0<κ<1/4, gives N^{1−2κ−o(1)}. Offsets may be large,
move with N, or be chosen after seeing the source. Crucially k counts
the **total union of offsets**, including both signs. Bounded row degree
with many distinct offsets is not covered; neither are general prime
dilation graphs merely because their rows are sparse.

For a target root exponent γ, the necessary thresholds are κ≥(1−γ)/4
for half-bandwidth and κ≥(1−γ)/2 for the offset union:

| Target | Half-bandwidth coefficient | Total-offset coefficient |
|---|---:|---:|
| Strict improvement over c11 | >.0312864909 | >.0625729818 |
| c=.1252 | ≥.0313 | ≥.0626 |
| c=1/6 | ≥1/24 | ≥1/12 |
| c=1/4 | ≥1/16 | ≥1/8 |

These are necessary widths, not sufficient savings or claims at an
unresolved equality threshold. q stays fixed.

### The complete nonlocal correction

Let P=D+E≽ℓℓ*, with D≽0 having the preceding support and E Hermitian,
||E||≤η in Euclidean operator norm. The exact same isolated set gives

\[
a^*Pa\ge K^2-\eta(K+N).                                \tag{96.8}
\]

The principal inequality costs ηK; the whole source error costs
η||a||²≤ηN. Positivity of D's complementary block is essential.
For K=N^{1−o(1)}, a fixed root exponent γ<1 therefore requires a
nonlocal correction with norm at least N^{1−o(1)} along this bound.
Small individual entries do not imply a small operator cost. Nonlocal
signed metrics, signed debts and proved source-only inequalities remain
eligible.

## G168. Exact harmonic and heat costs

The sorted-prime state from [G145](../[private research revision]/wild57-integration.md) is
retained: for σ>1/2, Tσ e_n=∑_{p>P⁺(n)}χ(p)p^−σ e_np on squarefree
q-units has ||Tσ^j||²≤Sσ^j/j!, Sσ=∑p^−2σ. Disjoint descendants follow
by deleting the j largest primes. Its convergent inverse gives
v(n)=μ(n)χ(n)n^−σ, but the physical output norm is asymptotic to a
constant times N^{σ+1/2}. This is reused source formation, not a new gap.
Diagonal congruence transports banded terminal metrics to G167 without
discarding a norm factor.

On all squarefree q-units at most N, take the connected graph n—np with
arbitrary positive edge weights. Let L be its real Laplacian, U=diag(a_n),
L_a=ULU*. Then x*L_a x=∑w_{n,p}|x_np+χ(p)x_n|² and L_a a=0. For
λ,η>0, H=λL_a+ηe_1e_1* is positive definite with a*Ha=η. Put
f=U*ℓ=conjugate(a), R=V_N\{1}, and E_N=f_R*(L_RR)^−1 f_R≥0. Exactly,

\[
\ell^*H^{-1}\ell=|M_\chi(N)|^2/\eta+E_N/\lambda,
\quad H\succeq\ell\ell^*\iff
|M_\chi(N)|^2/\eta+E_N/\lambda\le1.                    \tag{96.9}
\]

After conjugation, solve (λL+ηe_1e_1*)x=f. Summing yields
x_1=(∑f)/η; writing x=x_1ℓ+y,y_1=0 gives λL_RR y_R=f_R and (96.9).
If M≠0, require λ>E_N and η≥|M|²/(1−E_N/λ). If M=0, λ≥E_N suffices
for any η>0, including equality. N=1 has E_N=0. A graph gap may bound
the Green term; it cannot remove the actual harmonic amplitude.

There is an analogous exact bill for arbitrary positive diagonal Witten
weights on the downward-closed squarefree q-unit complex. Let d be
oriented deletion, S positive diagonal, d_S=SdS^−1,
Q_S=d_S+d_S*, Δ_S=Q_S², and Tχ the diagonal character insertion. The
adjoint matters: Δ_S is generally not SΔS^−1. Homology is unchanged,
while the positive spectrum may move. For principal χ the heat
supertrace equals the index Mχ(N) for every heat time.

For a general character, graded cyclicity and integration of the heat
derivative give, for every T≥0,

\[
M_\chi(N)=\operatorname{Str}(T_\chi e^{-T\Delta_S})
 +\frac12\int_0^T\operatorname{Str}
 ([T_\chi,Q_S]Q_Se^{-t\Delta_S})\,dt.                  \tag{96.10}
\]

In particular Str(TχΔ_S)=∑_{n,p}|S_n/S_np|² μ(n)χ(n)(1−χ(p)), with
every edge retained. Since S and Tχ commute,
[Tχ,d_S]=S[Tχ,d]S^−1; the deformation cannot make a nonzero commutator
vanish. For positive spectral gap λ*, the heat remainder beyond the
harmonic projection Π_0 is at most dim(V_N)e^−Tλ*. The integral also
converges because Q_SΠ_0=0, leaving the **twisted harmonic trace plus
the entire integrated bulk**.

For the actual nonprincipal character modulo3 at N=2, Tχ=diag(1,−1),
Q_S=[[0,w],[w,0]], w>0, and Π_0=0. The two terms in (96.10) are
2e^−Tw² and2(1−e^−Tw²), while the true source is2. Enlarging the gap
does not save the complete readout. This is a finite counterexample to
dropping the bulk, not an all-scale Mertens lower bound or a rejection
of all Witten constructions. The general harmonic warning is
[G74](../[private research revision]/wild46-integration.md); the cutoff ancestry and full
character bulk are [G164–G165](../[private research revision]/wild59-integration.md).

The author's specified superdeterminants are likewise exact:
sdet(I+zΔ)=1 and sdet(zI+Δ)=z^{Mχ₀(N)}, as meromorphic ratios after
cancellation. The unknown source remains in the zero-mode exponent.
Different regularizations or torsion definitions need their own return.

## G169. Complete occupation and compact-source interfaces

For uniform n∈{1,…,N}, every prime p≤N, including ramified primes, set

\[
U_p(n)=-(1+\chi(p))1_{p\mid n}+\chi(p)1_{p^2\mid n},
\quad Z_N(z)=\mathbb E\prod_p(1+z_pU_p).
\]

The factors equal1 at valuation zero,−χ(p) at valuation one and0 at
larger valuations. Thus Z_N(1)=Mχ(N)/N. First and distinct-prime moments
retain their literal floors:

\[
m_p=\frac{-(1+c_p)\lfloor N/p\rfloor+c_p\lfloor N/p^2\rfloor}{N},
\]
\[
m_{pr}=\frac{(1+c_p)(1+c_r)\lfloor N/(pr)\rfloor
 -(1+c_p)c_r\lfloor N/(pr^2)\rfloor
 -c_p(1+c_r)\lfloor N/(p^2r)\rfloor
 +c_pc_r\lfloor N/(p^2r^2)\rfloor}{N}.                  \tag{96.11}
\]

The formal log includes overlapping and repeated clusters; even though
Z_N is multiaffine, the z_p² coefficient of log Z_N is−m_p²/2.
Convergence at the physical activity requires a separate theorem.

For independent n,m define V_p=U_p(n)+conjugate(U_p(m))+
U_p(n)conjugate(U_p(m)). Then E∏(1+V_p)=|Mχ(N)/N|², including the
complete diagonal and off-diagonal. Its distinct two-prime connected
coefficient is |1+m_p+m_r+m_pr|²−|1+m_p|²|1+m_r|². A bound for a
selected cluster or a different Gaussian kernel is not a bound for this
complete contraction.

For q=1, keep only primes √N<p≤N and give them common activity t.
No integer up to N contains two of them, so

\[
Z_H(t)=1-B_Nt,\qquad
B_N=\frac2N\sum_{\sqrt N<p\le N}\lfloor N/p\rfloor
\longrightarrow2\log2>1.                              \tag{96.12}
\]

The limit follows from the [ordinary PNT](https://dlmf.nist.gov/27.2.E3),
partial summation and floor error at mostπ(N)/N=o(1). Thus this actual
partial marginal has a zero t_N=1/B_N inside(0,1) for all large N.
At N=100, B_N=27/25. Its logarithm at zero has radius less than1 and
the absolute series ∑B_N^j/j diverges at1. This blocks an absolutely
convergent log expansion on the full unit activity polydisc. It does
not turn a marginal zero into an L-zero or refute resummed, conditioned,
signed or differently parametrized replica expansions. The full
cross-sector return remains necessary. G145's high-prime clique, W51
fugacity and W38/[restricted research revision] occupation laws retain their ancestry.

The author also provides an explicit compact verification interface for
[G128's literal normalized source](../[private research revision]/wild54-integration.md).
Let δ indicate principal χ, r=δφ(q)/q, b(t)=∑_{n≤e^t}χ(n)−re^t, and

\[
F_\chi(s)=\left(\frac{s-1}{s+1}\right)^\delta\frac{L(s,\chi)}s
 =\int_0^\infty e^{-st}f(t)\,dt,\qquad |f(t)|\le C_q=1+3q.
\]

Here f=b for nonprincipal χ and
f(t)=re^−t+b(t)−2∫₀ᵗe^{−(t−u)}b(u)du for principal χ. F has exactly
the ordinary L-zeros on Re(s)>0; its value at the removed principal pole
is r/2, nonzero. If F_T truncates the integral at T, then on Re(s)≥σ₀>0,
|F−F_T|≤C_qe^−σ₀T/σ₀ and |F′|≤C_q/σ₀².

For a convex compact cell of radius d around z, a certified value v of
F_T(z) with error ε proves nonvanishing throughout that cell if

\[
|v|>\varepsilon+C_qe^{-\sigma_0T}/\sigma_0
                  +(C_q/\sigma_0^2)d.                 \tag{96.13}
\]

This pays truncation, evaluation and interpolation. If F is nonzero on
a given compact K, its positive minimum modulus lets all three errors
shrink below one eighth of that minimum, forcing eventual success.
Conversely soundness forbids success on a compact containing a zero.
Thus it is a semidecision procedure, with no efficiency claim and no
numerical execution in this cycle. Success on every
K_m={γ+1/m≤Re(s)≤m+2, |Im(s)|≤m} is equivalent to zero exclusion on
Re(s)>γ. The all-m premise remains unproved. Finite successes cannot
replace it, and G130's raw principal global-polynomial obstruction does
not reject this normalized compact construction.

## Return, evidence and next estimate

A complete bound for the actual Mχ(N), at one common γ and every fixed
ordinary χ, every ε>0 and all sufficiently large N, gives locally uniform
Abel continuation s∫₁∞Mχ(x)x^−s−1dx to Re(s)>γ. It equals1/L initially
on Re(s)>1 and retains principal poles, imprimitive factors and all finite
heights. Squared-energy bounds must retain every ε before taking square
roots. First gain needs γ<.8748540364; the illustrative γ=.8748,5/6,3/4
need complete squared exponents1.7496,5/3,3/2. No such saving is supplied.

S11's fixed-prime cone and S26's outgoing cutoff-flux readout are preserved
duplicates of G144 and Sol04 S38, with full reconstruction factors.
The latter observes the image in(X,pX]; projecting it back into[1,X]
would instead give zero. No general flux or torsion impossibility follows.

The [retention manifest](retention-manifest.json) binds32 frozen files,
13 reviewer sources and11 author sources, including historical navigation
bytes. Both full reports, helpers and receipts were read; existing exact
checks were not rerun. Finite checks validate algebra/indexing rather than
asymptotic cancellation. An actual host-local claim receipt is excluded.
All30 cards, author six S04/S29/S13/S11/S26/S23 and independent protected
S19/uniform S15 survive. Literal pools22/12/25, original entropy and
critic prep before outcome intake remain; no stronger chronology is
claimed. All29 families/109 children and later ideas are preserved.

The useful next work is a signed nonlocal or proved reachable-state
estimate escaping G167, control of the complete harmonic/heat readout,
a reorganized complete occupation contraction, or an all-compact
arithmetic margin. Chaining and simultaneous detector use remain eligible
when every transfer and complementary term is paid.

# G170-G172: adaptive completion and the limits of cutoff mixing

The new paid region follows the nonlinear phase surface instead of a
single worst-case product cutoff. Its complete complement is still a
signed arithmetic problem. Root accepts the restricted results below;
the written constant remains

    c11=312864909/2500000000=.1251459636,
    gamma11=2187135091/2500000000=.8748540364.

Sources are the [author proof](adaptive-source/report.md), [partial
independent review](adaptive-source-review/report.md), and
[retention manifest](retention-manifest.json). The reviewer reconstructed
the consequential arguments and added the bounded-variation result in
G171. Its helper/receipt, newest full-index and outside ancestry checks
were unfinished. Root independently reconstructed the addition, inspected
the helper and every receipt case, reconciled all six source pins, checked
the current changed index and exact inherited tail/Mellin paragraphs, and
opened the cited primary ancestry. This does not rewrite the review as a
completed full audit. Original missed deadlines and both STOPs remain.

## G170. A moving small-product region with its complete return

Fix an ordinary character chi modulo q, a prime p not dividing q, and

    a(n)=mu(n)chi(n), h(n)=chi(n), q_p=delta_1-p chi(p)delta_p,
    c_p=q_p*a, b_p=q_p*h=chi(n)(1-p 1_(p|n)).

The periodic b_p has zero mean and period Q=pq; retain all natural and
squareful coefficients. Let 1/2<gamma<1, integer k>2, 1<b<=2gamma and

    f_x(n)=exp(-n/x^b-i(n/x)^k), x in[X,2X],
    r=(k-2gamma)/(k-2), L=X^gamma, M=X^r,
    eta=1/(100kpq), B(n)=min(L,eta X^k/n^(k-1)).

Choose tau=tau_X in[0,1] before the real shell variable x. For each n,
freeze U(n)=B(n)^tau,V(n)=B(n)^(1-tau), using B^0=1 even when B<1.
The exact coefficientwise completion is

    c_p(n)=Q_U(n)+Q_V(n)-S_tau(n)+R_tau(n),
    Q_U(n)=sum_(de=n,d<=U(n)) a(d)q_p(e),
    S_tau(n)=sum_(de*l=n,d<=U(n),e<=V(n)) a(d)a(e)b_p(l),
    R_tau(n)=sum_(de*l=n,d>U(n),e>V(n)) a(d)a(e)b_p(l).

This is not one convolution identity with globally fixed cuts. Ordered
pairs, strict complements and endpoint cuts are literal. The two short
sources cost at most (p+1)(floor(L^tau)+floor(L^(1-tau)))=O_p(L).

For 0<tau<1 put W=max(d^(1/tau),e^(1/(1-tau))). A contributing row has
de<=W<=L, and its entire allowed cofactor set is the single prefix

    l <= (eta X^k/W)^(1/(k-1))/(de).

At tau=0 use d=1,W=e; at tau=1 use e=1,W=d. Thus
de(de*l)^(k-1)<=eta X^k. Expand b_p in its nonzero Fourier modes.
For F_j(t)=jt/Q-(de*t/x)^k/(2pi), the decreasing phase derivative and
every applicable integer increment stay in[1/(2Q),1-1/(2Q)]. Discrete
summation by parts with 1/(exp(2pi*i*v)-1) gives O(Q) per undamped prefix.
Abel summation pays the actual decreasing damping. There are at most L
rows, so uniformly in tau and every real x,

    |sum_n S_tau(n)f_x(n)| <<_(p,q,k) X^gamma.

The omitted alias region belongs to R; it has not been called
nonstationary. With |R_tau(n)|<=p d_3(n), the prefix n<=L is affordable.
The complete divisor-bounded tail from [G152](../[private research revision]/compensated-source-integration.md)
is

    ||sum_(n>M) v_n f_x(n)||_2^2
      << A_delta^2 [X^(b(1+2delta))+X^k M^(2-k+2delta)],
    |v_n|<=A_delta n^delta, 2delta<k-2.

It majorizes the whole positive square, retaining the diagonal, both
orientations and actual damping. Since k+(2-k)r=2gamma, choose delta
after epsilon. On dx/x over[X,2X], the literal finite core

    T_tau(x)=sum_(L<n<=M) R_tau(n)f_x(n)

satisfies ||C_p-T_tau||_j<<_epsilon X^(gamma+epsilon), j=1,2,
where C_p=sum c_p(n)f_x(n). These are separate L1 and L2 comparisons;
L2 implies L1, and no converse or signed-subset monotonicity is asserted.

For tau=1 collapse before masking. With h_p=q_p-b_p,
h_p(1)=0,h_p(p)=-chi(p), the core becomes

    sum_(L<n=dj<=M,d>B(n),j>=2) mu(d)chi(d)h_p(j)f_x(n),
    j<n/B(n)=max(n/X^gamma,n^k/(eta X^k)).

Near n~X the cofactor cap is O(X^(1-gamma)); the far cap is retained.
The transition is n*=eta^(1/(k-1))X^((k-gamma)/(k-1)). For gamma=.8748,
k=6 the near exponent is .1252, while the far exponent remains .3756;
transition exponent1.02504. This pays a genuinely larger small-source
region than the constant cutoff's worst-case exponent. It does not
estimate the remaining cancellation.

OPEN-AD asks for the complete every-epsilon, every-large-shell L1 core
bound at one common gamma<gamma11, for every fixed character and a
fixed covering pair of unramified primes. The inherited all-height
Mellin return is exact: at b=3/2,k=6 its leading term is
Gamma(s/6)e^(-i*pi*s/12)P_p(s)/(6L(s,chi)), P_p=1-chi(p)p^(1-s),
with holomorphic remainder on Re(s)>1/2. Two fixed primes cover numerator
zeros; for nonprincipal chi choose one with chi(p)!=1, and preserve the
principal pole at1. General fixed b,k use every shifted reciprocal in
a finite expansion and strip descent, never delete those terms. No
growing-conductor, native H or old positive-slot estimate is inferred.
Targets .1252,1/6,1/4 remain conditional; even the elementary full-source
bound remains X^(1+epsilon).

## G171. Arbitrarily many cuts at bounded total variation

For each X choose any finite J_X, parameters tau_j,X and complex weights
lambda_j,X, all fixed before x, with sum lambda_j=1 and
sum|lambda_j|<=Lambda for a fixed Lambda. The complete bank
T_bank=sum lambda_j T_tau_j obeys the same paid comparison with an extra
factor Lambda, uniformly in J_X. For a PRINCIPAL character its selected
semiprime projection nevertheless has L1 and L2 norm >> X/log X.

Here is the reviewer extension independently checked by root. Write
c=1-gamma,t_j=gamma*tau_j and

    F(alpha)=sum_j lambda_j[
       1_(t_j<alpha<t_j+c)+1_(gamma-t_j<alpha<1-t_j)].

F is symmetric, |F|<=2Lambda and integral_0^1 F=2c. Set
delta=c/(4Lambda),m=c/(8Lambda). The set ReF>=c/2 in[delta,1/2]
has measure at least m. Define the endpoint measure nu with mass
|lambda_j| at each of t_j,t_j+c,gamma-t_j,1-t_j; its total is<=4Lambda.
Variation of F on an interval is bounded by the nu-mass there.
For n=rs, alpha=log r/log X and kappa=log(n/X)/log X, the actual merged
coefficient G shifts both upper endpoints by kappa; its error from F
is bounded by nu([alpha-|kappa|,alpha+|kappa|]).

Choose a fixed grid of width h=c^2/(4096Lambda^2). Discard the terminal
strip[1/2-m/4,1/2] and the at most two boundary cells. A cell is bad
when its h-enlargement has nu-mass>c/8. A point lies in at most four
such closed enlargements, so bad length is<=128Lambda*h/c=m/4.
The total discarded length is<=m/2+2h<m. Some full good cell I contains
a point with ReF>=c/2. Throughout I, variation and displacement each
cost<=c/8 whenever |kappa|<=h. Thus ReG>=c/4, |G|<=2Lambda,
without a bound on the number of breakpoints.

Choose a fixed a in(0,1/4] with(2a)^k<=c/(64Lambda), and select primes
X^(inf I)<r<=X^(sup I), aX/r<s<=2aX/r. For large X these give distinct
unramified semiprimes in the literal core, B(n)=L and |kappa|<h.
Their phase on every real shell point is small, so the real part of
G f_x(n) is bounded below by a fixed positive constant. Ordinary PNT
on polynomially large fixed-ratio intervals and partial summation of
sum1/r give >> X/log X selected products, uniformly in the grid cell.
This proves the projected norm bound.

No coefficient was replaced by its absolute value. The projection may
depend on X and the bank. This rules out paying all such selected pieces
separately at the desired power merely by adding more normalized cuts
at bounded variation. It does NOT lower-bound T_bank or C_p, exclude
cancellation against their complements, or treat unbounded Lambda as
free. The author proved the fixed-J version; the uniform finite-J_X
extension belongs to the reviewer, with independent root reconstruction.

## G172. Deflation changes the obstructing cell and preserves its cost

For fixed K>=1 use

    v_K=(p chi(p))^K delta_(p^K)*q_p,
    b_K=v_K*h, c_K=v_K*a, h_K=v_K-b_K.

This equals a difference of two compensators, with v_K(1)=0 and
b_K(j)=chi(j)[p^K 1_(p^K|j)-p^(K+1)1_(p^(K+1)|j)]. It has zero
mean, period Q_K=p^(K+1)q. The adaptive proof works for each FIXED K
with eta_K=1/(100kQ_K), paying all K-dependent constants. Since
h_K=(p chi(p))^K delta_(p^K)*h_p, its prime values vanish. At tau=1
the entire semiprime projection vanishes where B(n)>=1; otherwise the
long label d=1 must be retained. The whole-core statement follows when
u=2gamma-r>0 for large X, including the three displayed targets.

The Mellin numerator gains the nonvanishing factor
chi(p)^K p^(K(1-s)); the fixed two-prime return survives. This is a
fixed multiplicative dilation, not a new cancellation theorem. For
principal chi, the actual cell n=p^(K+1)d, d prime in
(X/(4p^(K+1)),X/(2p^(K+1))], has entire merged coefficient+p^K:
the d term contributes, the pd term has h_K(p^K)=0, and higher p powers
in the Mobius variable vanish. Its projected norm remains comparable
to X/(p log X).

If p^(K+1)<=X^(1-gamma-delta) for fixed0<delta<1-gamma, the same
selected-cell lower bound remains uniform. That diagnostic does not
import the full comparison uniformly in K. Existing short and row
upper budgets grow with K and must be reproved for a growing-depth
architecture. Their growth is not an impossibility theorem for a
better estimate of the complete signed source.

## Evidence, ancestry and next estimate

Nine frozen artifacts retain original proofs, partial review, helpers,
receipts and missed deadlines. The author's single exact run checked
16 adaptive cases through600 with four actual characters,1024 row-prefix
memberships, nine signed profiles, eight deflations and three rational
targets. Root read it without rerunning; these checks prove no asymptotic.
The inherited G140-G142 and G152-G154 tail/continuation/compensator
components retain credit. [Helfgott and Thompson](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s40993-022-00408-8)
provide primary ancestry for completion and product-dependent divisor
geometry, not a nonlinear cancellation estimate or imported running-time
exponent. Ordinary PNT is the only prime-counting input here.

The next target is the complete signed transition core, with correlations
between its cells, or a different architecture with a fully paid return.
Increasing cutoff-bank size alone at bounded variation is insufficient
for the separate-piece strategy. No increased c, formalization, native-H
adapter or external record admission follows. The original29-family/
109-child portfolio and nearer,1/6,1/4 targets remain intact.

# G173-G175: a paid prime-flux reduction and exact returned sources

The main new reduction pays every higher prime power, a growing small-prime
range and the exact same-output diagonal in the Gaussian logarithmic
equation. What remains is a strict signed off-diagonal estimate. It is
unproved. The written source-relative constant stays

    c11=312864909/2500000000=.1251459636,
    gamma11=2187135091/2500000000=.8748540364.

Root accepts the restricted statements below after reading the [author
proof](wild62/report.md), [independent review](wild62-review/report.md),
both helpers, receipts and relevant ancestry. The [retention
manifest](retention-manifest.json) binds 28 original artifacts and sixteen
source bindings from each side. Source hashes, semantic read extents and
historical versions remain distinct. Independent reviewer additions are
identified explicitly. No finite diagnostic proves an asymptotic bound.

## G173. The complete hard-prime off-diagonal criterion

Fix an ordinary Dirichlet character chi modulo fixed q, principal or
imprimitive allowed, tau>0 fixed, and 1/2<gamma<1. Put

    a(n)=mu(n)chi(n),
    g(v)=(2pi tau)^(-1/2)exp(-v^2/(2tau)),
    U(y)=sum_(n>=1)a(n)g(log n-y), z(y)=exp(-gamma y)U(y).

The unit, prime2, squareful zeros and character zeros are literal.
Gaussian majorants justify local absolute convergence and derivatives;
the entire left tail is bounded by a polynomial times a Gaussian.
Coefficientwise logarithmic differentiation of a*chi=delta gives

    a(n)log n=-sum_(d|n)a(n/d)chi(d)Lambda(d),
    tau U'+yU+K1 U+K2 U=0,
    K1 U=sum_p chi(p)log p U(y-log p),
    K2 U=sum_(p,j>=2)chi(p)^j log p U(y-j log p).

The last two surviving local terms cancel at squareful n. Deleting higher
prime powers would change the source. This identity has W35/G118 ancestry.
In z coordinates each delay d has coefficient chi(d)Lambda(d)d^(-gamma).
For every R>=0 define

    I_R=int_0^R y|z(y)|^2dy, E_R=int_0^R |z(y)|^2dy,
    Qj(R)=-Re int_0^R conjugate(z(y))(Kj,gamma z)(y)dy.

The exact energy equation, including the initial value, is

    (tau/2)(|z(R)|^2-|z(0)|^2)+I_R+tau gamma E_R=Q1+Q2. (1)

Three full payments leave a more precise arithmetic problem.

First, the sum of absolute higher-power coefficients is finite:

    C_gamma=sum_(p,j>=2)log p p^(-j gamma)
      <=(1-2^(-gamma))^(-1)sum_(n>=2)log n n^(-2gamma).

Truncate z only above R, retaining its whole past. Translation contraction,
Minkowski and Cauchy give |Q2|<=C_gamma int_(-infinity)^R |z|^2. The past
is unconditionally finite. Split the positive integral at a fixed large Y;
for every eta>0 this proves

    |Q2(R)|<=eta I_R+B_eta.                                  (2)

B_eta uses only a fixed bounded interval and the Gaussian left tail, not
an unknown future norm. This is a relative form bound, not prime-power
cancellation.

Second, the author pays p<=(2+y)^A whenever A(1-gamma)<1. The reviewer
enlarges that region to the exact monotone cutoff

    Y_gamma(y)=((2+y)/log(e^2+y))^(1/(1-gamma)), y>=0.        (3)

Equality belongs to the small sector. Elementary binomial prime counting
gives theta(t)<=4(log2)t. Partial summation yields

    sum_(p<=Y)log p p^(-gamma)
      <=[4log2/(1-gamma)]Y^(1-gamma).

Thus the row sum for (3) is O_gamma((2+y)/log(e^2+y))=o(y).
For large y, log p<=y/2 on this sector, so v=y-log p belongs to[y/2,y].
In the second half of 2|z(y)z(v)|<=|z(y)|^2+|z(v)|^2, change variables
separately for every p. Since y<=2v, the column is bounded using
p<=Y_gamma(2v) and is o(v). Also v<=R. The bounded initial region has
finitely many primes and a fixed bounded input interval. Therefore

    |Q_small(R)|<=eta I_R+B_eta                              (4)

for every eta>0. Both row and column are paid. Formula (3) is larger
asymptotically than every fixed subcritical power (2+y)^A. It does not
transfer an assumed residual estimate between different masks for free.

Third, expand the hard-prime contribution with p>Y_gamma(y) before taking
absolute values. Its literal summand is

    -Re[conjugate(a(n))chi(p)a(m)] log p exp(-2gamma y)
          *g(log n-y)g(log(pm)-y),

over all m,n>=1 and 0<=y<=R. For n=pm its coefficient is +1 exactly when
pm is a squarefree q-unit, otherwise zero. For fixed n the retained prime
log-weights sum to at most log n. The exact whole-line integral is

    int exp(-2gamma y)g(log n-y)^2dy
      =exp(tau gamma^2)n^(-2gamma)/(2sqrt(pi tau)).

Consequently the exact diagonal D_R is nonnegative and bounded by the
fixed finite constant obtained by summing log n n^(-2gamma). Define
H_R=Q_hard-D_R, precisely the complete n!=pm form. Every sign, phase,
infinite source sum and the complementary prime mask remains inside it.

**OPEN-PF.** For one common gamma in(1/2,1), suppose every fixed ordinary
chi admits delta_chi>0, B_chi and R0_chi such that

    H_R <= (1-delta_chi)I_R+B_chi, every R>=R0_chi.           (5)

Take eta=delta_chi/4 in (2) and (4) and absorb the finite initial range.
Then (1) gives, for all R>=0,

    (tau/2)|z(R)|^2+(delta_chi/2)I_R+tau gamma E_R<=B'_chi.  (6)

Thus U(y)=O_chi(exp(gamma y)) on every sufficiently large real y. The
bilateral transform F(s)=int U(y)exp(-sy)dy is holomorphic on Re s>gamma,
locally uniformly with all derivatives. On Re s>1 absolute Fubini gives

    F(s)=exp(tau s^2/2)/L(s,chi).

Continue L(s,chi)F(s)=exp(tau s^2/2). Its right side never vanishes, so
there is no ordinary L-zero in Re s>gamma at any finite height or
multiplicity. The principal pole at1 is allowed and forces a zero of F;
imprimitive factors and natural zeros were never removed. The standard
continuation and Euler-product conventions are those of [DLMF
25.15](https://dlmf.nist.gov/25.15). No height-uniform lower bound for the
Gaussian multiplier, unsmoothing theorem or native-H adapter is needed
for this one-way return.

The gamma is common to all fixed characters; margins, constants and
onsets may depend on chi. Neither gamma=1/2 nor growing-conductor
uniformity is supplied. Conditional c=.12515 would improve c11 by
.0000040364; 1/6,1/4 and values below1/2 remain conditional possibilities.
None has (5) proved. Even if a bound U(y)=O(exp(beta y)), gamma<beta<1,
is GRANTED, absolute prime summation gives the coarse flux exponent
1+beta-2gamma, against I's exponent2beta-2gamma. The gap1-beta remains.
This failed upper-budget trial is not a signed lower bound, and the
granted U bound is not inferred from a bare zero-free statement.

W35/G79/G118 retain credit for Gaussian renewal, energy drift and the full
logarithmic identity. The increment is the combined complete payments,
the enlarged moving cutoff and its exact residual criterion. No strict
coercivity follows from the equation alone.

## G174. Actual cutoff boundaries and the price of a positive observation

Let S_N be the squarefree q-units n<=N. On its orthonormal basis define
B_p e_n=chi(p)e_(pn) when p does not divide n and pn<=N, zero otherwise.
Distinct insertions commute: their product exists in both orders exactly
when prn fits. The divisor-closed cutoff does not create noncommutative
independence. Ordered fermionic boundaries are different operators.

For p!=r the mixed adjoint commutator is exactly

    C_pr=B_p^*B_r-B_rB_p^*,
    C_pr e_(pm)=-conjugate(chi(p))chi(r)e_(rm),
    m squarefree, (m,qpr)=1,
    N/(pr)<m<=min(N/p,N/r),                                (7)

and zero elsewhere. The lower endpoint is strict and upper endpoints
inclusive. It is a phased negative partial isometry, norm1 if its domain
is nonempty. For a_N=sum_(S_N)mu(n)chi(n)e_n, every character phase cancels:

    <a_N,C_pr a_N>=-#domain(7).

With profile f, the exact contraction is instead
-sum_m conjugate(f(rm))f(pm). Complex profiles cannot be replaced by
positive counts. For the k unramified primes in(N/2,N], the sum over
ordered p!=r is -D_chi(J_k-I_k)D_chi^*. The actual vector -D_chi1 has
eigenvalue-(k-1) and quadratic value-k(k-1). A transported gauge preserves
it. This rejects the specified unweighted independence shortcut.

The reviewer preserves a genuine escape: if external weights lambda_p
are allowed, the same terminal contraction becomes

    <a_N,sum_(p!=r)conjugate(lambda_p)lambda_r C_pr a_N>
      =sum_p|lambda_p|^2-|sum_p lambda_p|^2.                (8)

For two primes, weights(1,1),(1,-1),(1,i) give-2,+2,0. Thus the unweighted
obstruction does not exclude all signed compensation. G164's positive
ordered E=B^*B result has different hypotheses. The complete readout is
still a_N=product_p(I-B_p)e_1 and M_chi(N)=<1,a_N>; bounding commutators
alone does not estimate it.

A second result concerns a precise positive certificate. For the principal
character modulo fixed q, partition S_N by its complete set of prime
divisors<=sqrt N. The empty cell is

    C0={1} union {p:sqrt N<p<=N,p not dividing q}.

If L counts those primes and Q=#S_N, its signed sum is1-L. For any
partition P, Cauchy gives

    |M(N)|<=sqrt(Q E(P)),
    E(P)=sum_(C in P)|sum_(n in C)mu(n)|^2/|C|.

The displayed observation and every refinement satisfy

    E(P)>=(L-1)^2/(L+1)=L-3+4/(L+1).                       (9)

Refinement only increases conditional-square energy. Square-divisor
counting gives Q=kappa_q N+O_q(sqrt N),
kappa_q=(6/pi^2)product_(p|q)p/(p+1)>0. Elementary binomial counting gives
pi(N)>>N/log N: each prime's factor in binomial(2m,m) is at most2m,
while the binomial is at least4^m/(2m+1). Removing sqrt N and finitely
many ramified primes leaves L>>_q N/log N. Therefore the NUMERIC RIGHT
SIDE sqrt(Q E(P)) is at least a constant times N/sqrt(log N).

This positive certificate cannot prove a fixed power below1. Its proposed
every-epsilon energy target N^(2gamma-1+epsilon) is false for gamma<1;
the current first-gain threshold is2gamma11-1=.7497080728. This is no
lower bound for |M|. Signed cross-pattern interactions, coarsening,
unrelated syndromes and nonprincipal phase cancellation remain available.
A finite syndrome example with identical syndrome law and opposite parity
bias is only a model illustration, not a broader arithmetic impossibility.

G103/G117/G145/G162 and the precise [restricted research revision]-[restricted research revision] positive certificate results
retain their separate scopes. Cell-constant projections can connect widely
separated primes, so this argument is not merely G167's short-offset
global positivity hypothesis under a different name.

## G175. Two exact source returns with their inverse costs

### Native Cayley scattering

The protected critic audit S22 keeps the literal Eisenstein H source:
original primary/fixed-ray/six-unit/bad-place conventions, distinct rational
long-prime norms and both excluded equal-norm orientations, both ordered
good primitive short ideals including equality, the actual complex core
and rational gcd screen, both original mark projectors and independent
heights, original masks and profiles. Its coefficient is
a_H(n)=alpha(n)eta(n)chi_n(lambda)^(-2)gamma_2(n), xi(g)=alpha(g)^3eta(g)^3.
With v_P=u1(P)/sqrt(q_P), w_P'=u2(P')/sqrt(q_P'), the entire signed scalar
kernel gives T=K^transpose, H=w^*Tv and ||v||^2=Omega1, ||w||^2=Omega2.
The raw target is B0 sqrt(Omega1 Omega2),
B0=G K0[N+L+(NL)^(2/3)]P_orig; physical N^(-1)G^(-2) is applied once.
No extra opposite-coprimality screen, selected source, or Mobius substitute
is inserted. The original range and all other branches remain obligations.

For any r>0 the self-adjoint dilation A=[[0,T^*],[T,0]] has a unitary
Cayley transform (A-irI)(A+irI)^(-1), without knowing ||T||<=r. Write

    D=(T^*T+r^2 I)^(-1),
    R=(T^*T-r^2 I)D, J=-2ir TD,
    R=R^*, R^2+J^*J=I, I-R=2r^2 D.

The exact returned input x=(I-R)^(-1)v obeys

    Tv=ir Jx,
    ||Tv||^2=r^2(||x||^2-||Rx||^2)
            =r^2(2Re<x,v>-||v||^2).                       (10)

Thus ||T||<=r iff R<=0, and the source-specific ||Tv||<=r||v|| iff
Re<x,v><=||v||^2. At r=B0>0 the latter suffices for the raw bound against
every allowed w, and is stronger than controlling one scalar pairing.
B0=0 needs that zero pairing directly. No arithmetic estimate for x is
proved. On a singular mode sigma, transmission is2r sigma/(sigma^2+r^2)
while the inverse is(sigma^2+r^2)/(2r^2). Small transmission can coexist
with a very expensive returned input. A known ||T||<=B only gives
r/2+B^2/(2r)>=B after the crude reconstruction bound.

For an approximation xhat, retain d=v-(I-R)xhat. The complete scalar is

    H=ir w^*J xhat+w^*T d.                                (11)

The residual is an actual native-source obligation. Compared with [restricted research revision]'s
Julia realization, Cayley removes its known-contraction prerequisite but
exposes this inverse/error cost. It proves no H saving or new exponent.

### A compact sensor needs no positive-height numerator cover

The uniform critic audit S10 uses one fixed h>0 and M_chi(x)=0 for x<1:

    S_h(x)=int_0^h M_chi(x exp(-u))du
          =sum_(n<=x)mu(n)chi(n) min(h,log(x/n)).

The endpoints, unit and natural zeros remain. Absolute integration gives

    int_1^infinity S_h(x)x^(-s)dx/x
      =(1-exp(-hs))/(s^2 L(s,chi)), Re s>1.                (12)

If the COMPLETE S_h is O_(chi,epsilon)(x^(gamma+epsilon)) for every
epsilon>0 and all sufficiently large x, for one common0<gamma<1, the

## G174. Actual cutoff boundaries and the price of a positive observation

Let S_N be the squarefree q-units n<=N. On its orthonormal basis define
B_p e_n=chi(p)e_(pn) when p does not divide n and pn<=N, zero otherwise.
Distinct insertions commute: their product exists in both orders exactly
when prn fits. The divisor-closed cutoff does not create noncommutative
independence. Ordered fermionic boundaries are different operators.

For p!=r the mixed adjoint commutator is exactly

    C_pr=B_p^*B_r-B_rB_p^*,
    C_pr e_(pm)=-conjugate(chi(p))chi(r)e_(rm),
    m squarefree, (m,qpr)=1,
    N/(pr)<m<=min(N/p,N/r),                                (7)

and zero elsewhere. The lower endpoint is strict and upper endpoints
inclusive. It is a phased negative partial isometry, norm1 if its domain
is nonempty. For a_N=sum_(S_N)mu(n)chi(n)e_n, every character phase cancels:

    <a_N,C_pr a_N>=-#domain(7).

With profile f, the exact contraction is instead
-sum_m conjugate(f(rm))f(pm). Complex profiles cannot be replaced by
positive counts. For the k unramified primes in(N/2,N], the sum over
ordered p!=r is -D_chi(J_k-I_k)D_chi^*. The actual vector -D_chi1 has
eigenvalue-(k-1) and quadratic value-k(k-1). A transported gauge preserves
it. This rejects the specified unweighted independence shortcut.

The reviewer preserves a genuine escape: if external weights lambda_p
are allowed, the same terminal contraction becomes

    <a_N,sum_(p!=r)conjugate(lambda_p)lambda_r C_pr a_N>
      =sum_p|lambda_p|^2-|sum_p lambda_p|^2.                (8)

For two primes, weights(1,1),(1,-1),(1,i) give-2,+2,0. Thus the unweighted
obstruction does not exclude all signed compensation. G164's positive
ordered E=B^*B result has different hypotheses. The complete readout is
still a_N=product_p(I-B_p)e_1 and M_chi(N)=<1,a_N>; bounding commutators
alone does not estimate it.

A second result concerns a precise positive certificate. For the principal
character modulo fixed q, partition S_N by its complete set of prime
divisors<=sqrt N. The empty cell is

    C0={1} union {p:sqrt N<p<=N,p not dividing q}.

If L counts those primes and Q=#S_N, its signed sum is1-L. For any
partition P, Cauchy gives

    |M(N)|<=sqrt(Q E(P)),
    E(P)=sum_(C in P)|sum_(n in C)mu(n)|^2/|C|.

The displayed observation and every refinement satisfy

    E(P)>=(L-1)^2/(L+1)=L-3+4/(L+1).                       (9)

Refinement only increases conditional-square energy. Square-divisor
counting gives Q=kappa_q N+O_q(sqrt N),
kappa_q=(6/pi^2)product_(p|q)p/(p+1)>0. Elementary binomial counting gives
pi(N)>>N/log N: each prime's factor in binomial(2m,m) is at most2m,
while the binomial is at least4^m/(2m+1). Removing sqrt N and finitely
many ramified primes leaves L>>_q N/log N. Therefore the NUMERIC RIGHT
SIDE sqrt(Q E(P)) is at least a constant times N/sqrt(log N).

This positive certificate cannot prove a fixed power below1. Its proposed
every-epsilon energy target N^(2gamma-1+epsilon) is false for gamma<1;
the current first-gain threshold is2gamma11-1=.7497080728. This is no
lower bound for |M|. Signed cross-pattern interactions, coarsening,
unrelated syndromes and nonprincipal phase cancellation remain available.
A finite syndrome example with identical syndrome law and opposite parity
bias is only a model illustration, not a broader arithmetic impossibility.

G103/G117/G145/G162 and the precise [restricted research revision]-[restricted research revision] positive certificate results
retain their separate scopes. Cell-constant projections can connect widely
separated primes, so this argument is not merely G167's short-offset
global positivity hypothesis under a different name.

## G176. A compensated Liouville source with all square collisions paid

Fix an ordinary character chi modulo q, with natural zero extension, and a
fixed prime p not dividing q. All convolutions below are Dirichlet convolutions.
Let a(n)=lambda(n)chi(n), h(n)=chi(n), and s(r^2)=chi(r)^2, with s zero off
squares. The prime-power identity gives a*h=s. Set

    q1=delta_1-p chi(p)delta_p,
    q2=delta_1-p chi(p)^2 delta_(p^2), v=q1*q2,
    b=v*h, g=a*s, c=v*g=a*a*b.

Complete multiplicativity a(d)a(e)=a(de) includes shared primes and natural
zeros. There is no corresponding unrestricted identity for mu. The exact
Dirichlet series on Re z>1 is

    D_c(z)=P_p(z)J_p(z)L(2z,chi^2)^2/L(z,chi),
    P_p(z)=1-chi(p)p^(1-z), J_p(z)=1-chi(p)^2p^(1-2z).

In particular the p^2 coefficient of q2 is -p chi(p)^2, not -p^2 chi(p)^2.
The ordinary and root sequences

    b(n)=chi(n)[1-p1_(p|n)-p1_(p^2|n)+p^2 1_(p^3|n)],
    beta(r)=chi(r)^2(1-p1_(p|r))

have zero means and periods p^3q and pq. The source v*s retains the two
physical root rows d r^2 and p d r^2 with weights1 and -p chi(p).
This combines W49's exact square convolutions with [restricted research revision]/[restricted research revision] compensation;
the complete new cross-row estimate below is the substantive addition.

Use f_x(n)=exp(-n/x^(3/2)-i(n/x)^6), real x in[X,2X], and dx/x norms.
For fixed alpha0<1, every1<=A<=pX^alpha0 and every frozen root prefix R,
including infinity, satisfy

    ||sum_(r<=R) beta(r) f_x(A r^2)||_2
        <<_(p,q,alpha0) 1+X^(3/8)A^(-1/4).                 (1)

For completeness, choose R0=c0(X/A)^(6/11), with c0 small and fixed.
Each nonzero periodic Fourier frequency stays separated from integers
through this low prefix, including the last discrete increment. Discrete
first-derivative summation and Abel summation of the actual damping pay
every low prefix by O(1). Above R0 the complete positive shell kernel is

    exp(-cA(r^2+s^2)/X^(3/2))
          min(1,[(X/A)^6/|r^12-s^12|]^2).

Its diagonal costs X^(3/4)A^(-1/2). Summing both off-diagonal orientations
costs (X/A)^6 R0^(-10)=(X/A)^(6/11), no larger than that diagonal.
The norm triangle inequality pays the low/high interaction and all aliases.

Now take arbitrary frozen |u_d|<=1 and arbitrary frozen row-prefix endpoints
R_de. Retain both e labels and form the complete source

    Q_D(x)=sum_(d<=D) u_d sum_(e=1,p) q1(e)
                           sum_(r<=R_de) beta(r) f_x(e d r^2),
    1<=D<=X^alpha0.

The strengthened bound is

    ||Q_D||_2^2 << D^2+X^(6/11)D^(16/11)+X^(3/4)D^(1/2)
                    +min(X^(3/5)D^(7/5),X^(15/16)D^(1/2)).  (2)

All constants depend only on the stated fixed data. There is no hidden
logarithmic or divisor-epsilon loss in(2). It bounds the full merged source.

Here is the decisive collision argument. Write
W_D(n)=#{d<=D:n/d is an integer square}. The exact count is

    sum_(n<=Y)W_D(n)^2
      =sum_(a squarefree,a<=D) sum_(u,v<=sqrt(D/a))
                         floor(sqrt(Y/a)/lcm(u,v))
      << sqrt(YD).                                        (3)

Indeed d1=a u^2,d2=a v^2 can collide only when their squarefree kernels
agree. After floor(t)<=t, the remaining absolute series is bounded by
2sqrt(YD) sum_(u,v) gcd(u,v)/(uv max(u,v)). Substitution u=g h,v=g k
reduces convergence to sum_g g^(-2) sum_k H_k/k^2<infinity. Thus every
coincident square divisor and repeated multiplier is paid.

Remove the exact low prefix from each row. Its total norm is O(D). The
merged remaining coefficient z_X(n) obeys

    |z_X(n)|<=C_p W_(pD)(n),
    n>N0=c0^2 p^(-1/11)X^(12/11)D^(-1/11).

Positive coefficient domination survives every original prefix mask.
It is not domination of a signed norm by a selected signed subset.
On a comparable block n,m~N put H_N=X^6/N^5. W24's complete local
multiplicity count gives one positive kernel bound

    exp(-cN/X^(3/2))[H_N D+sqrt(ND)min(N^(1/3),D)].

The independent collision estimate(3), integer row sum O(1+H_N) and
2|z_n z_m|<=|z_n|^2+|z_m|^2 give another bound for that SAME block,
exp(-cN/X^(3/2))sqrt(ND)(1+H_N). Their minimum is at most a fixed
multiple of

    exp(-cN/X^(3/2))
      [H_N D+sqrt(ND)(1+min(N^(1/3),D,H_N))].              (4)

Summing H_N D from N0 yields X^(6/11)D^(16/11); actual infinite damping
pays the isolated diagonal by X^(3/4)D^(1/2). The remaining expression
grows then decreases geometrically. Its meeting scale is
N=X^(6/5)D^(-1/5) if D<=X^(3/8), otherwise N=X^(9/8), giving the two
alternatives in(2). For far pairs the full kernel and both cumulative
masses give X^12 D N^(-11); summing from N0 gives O(D^2). Both
orientations and low/high interactions remain included.

## G177. Complete adaptive core and conditional all-height return

Fix3/4<=gamma<1. Let

    L=X^gamma, M=X^((6-2gamma)/4), Q=p^3q,
    eta=1/(6000Q), B(n)=min(L,eta X^6/n^5),
    U(n)=B(n)^tau, V(n)=B(n)^(1-tau).

Choose tau before real x, in the closed corridor

    max(gamma tau,gamma(1-tau)) <= (11gamma-3)/8.          (5)

The identity c=a*a*b gives exactly c=Q_U+Q_V-S_tau+R_tau, where

    Q_U(n)=sum_(de=n,d<=U(n))a(d)(v*s)(e),
    S_tau(n)=sum_(de l=n,d<=U(n),e<=V(n))a(d)a(e)b(l),
    R_tau(n)=sum_(de l=n,d>U(n),e>V(n))a(d)a(e)b(l).

Define C_p,chi(x)=sum_n c(n)f_x(n) and the full finite core
T_tau,X(x)=sum_(L<n<=M)R_tau(n)f_x(n). Then

    ||C_p,chi-T_tau,X||_j <<_(fixed data,epsilon) X^(gamma+epsilon),
    j=1,2, for every epsilon>0, uniformly in(5).           (6)

To see the improvement, the norm exponents of(2) at D=X^alpha are
alpha,(3+8alpha)/11,3/8+alpha/4 and
min(3/10+7alpha/10,15/32+alpha/4). All are at most gamma under(5),
so both complete short sources cost O(X^gamma), including endpoint equality.
The root cuts remain prefixes because B(edr^2) decreases in r. The
small-double source is O(X^gamma) by the zero-mean period of b and the
original fixed derivative-gap cut. The coefficient bound
|R_tau(n)|<=(p+1)^2d_3(n) pays n<=L and the complete n>M tail, whose
squared bound is X^(3/2+epsilon)+X^6M^(-4+epsilon). Norm inequalities
pay all complementary interactions. No signed submask bound is imported.

The actual merged residual is

    R_tau(n)=sum_(m l=n) a(m)D_(U(n),V(n))(m)b(l),
    D_(U,V)(m)=#{ordered(d,e):de=m,d>U,e>V}.

Complete multiplicativity retains one sign times an ordered divisor count;
it does not prove cancellation. Near n~X the cofactor l<n/X^gamma is
short, but every cofactor and all of the interval through M remain in T.

The remaining hypothesis OPEN-LC is the full L1 bound

    integral_X^(2X)|T_tau_X,X(x)| dx/x << X^(gamma+epsilon) (7)

for every epsilon>0 and all sufficiently large dyadic X, for each fixed
ordinary character and each of a fixed covering pair of unramified primes,
at one common gamma chosen before the character and candidate zero.
Tau_X may vary with the shell and epsilon, before x;(6) is uniform.
The complete C and T norm hypotheses are equivalent by(6). Their
equivalence to zero exclusion is not asserted. A full L2 bound suffices
but does not follow from the L1 statement.

Under(7), H_p(z)=integral_0^infinity C_p,chi(1/t)t^(z-1)dt is holomorphic
on Re z>gamma, by shell summation and the damping at x near zero.
[restricted research revision]'s clockwise contour rotation, first on Re z>3/2, gives

    H_p(z)=A0(z)P_p(z)J_p(z)L(2z,chi^2)^2/L(z,chi)+E_p(z),
    A0(z)=Gamma(z/6)exp(-i pi z/12)/6,                    (8)

with E_p normally holomorphic on Re z>1/2: each coefficient integral
has remainder O_K(n^(-Re z-1/2)), locally with derivatives. A0 and
J_p L(2z,chi^2)^2 are nonzero in Re z>1/2. The zeros of P_p lie on
Re z=1. Two distinct primes have no common nonzero-height zero there,
since character values are roots of unity and log p1/log p2 is irrational.
For nonprincipal chi choose p1 with chi(p1)!=1 to cover height zero;
for principal chi the pole at1 is the permitted exception. This proves
the conditional exclusion of every finite-height zero in Re z>gamma.
Imprimitive factors, natural zeros and fixed-character dependencies stay.

| Conditional c | gamma | M exponent | alpha cap | allowed tau |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| .1252 | 2187/2500 | 5313/5000 | 16557/20000 | [313/5832,5519/5832] |
| 1/6 | 5/6 | 13/12 | 37/48 | [3/40,37/40] |
| 1/4 | 3/4 | 9/8 | 21/32 | [1/8,7/8] |

The reviewer's improvement is below gamma=17/21; it leaves the nearer
and1/6 rows unchanged. At1/4 the author's range[1/3,2/3] expands to
[1/8,7/8]. None of these rows proves(7). The near target would improve
c11 by135091/2500000000 if that missing full estimate were established.

## G178. Actual variance, complete logarithmic test and higher-ceiling scope

The actual coefficient g has the exact variance identity

    |g(n)|^2=1_((n,q)=1) sum_(d^2|n)d_2(d^2),
    sum_(n<=Y)|g(n)|^2=C_chi Y+O_q(sqrt(Y)log^2(2Y)),
    C_chi=(phi(q)/q)sum_((d,q)=1)d_2(d^2)/d^2>0.

At each prime power the identity is sum_(j<=floor(nu/2))(2j+1)
=(floor(nu/2)+1)^2. Counting coprime integers and d_2(d^2)<=d_3(d)
pays the errors and the convergent constant. The finite v convolution
retains all its cross terms under Cauchy-Schwarz and gives
sum_(n<=Y)|c(n)|^2<<_(p,q)Y. It does not assert an exact c asymptotic.

Consequently, for M>=X the full actual source tail satisfies

    ||sum_(n>M)c(n)f_x(n)||_2^2 << X^(3/2)+X^6 M^(-4).   (9)

The integer off-diagonal row sum is O(X^6/n^5). Both orientations,
the actual damped diagonal and all far pairs are included. At M=X,
the complete coarse bound is ||C||_2<<X, which fails the first-gain target.

The exact expansion g(n)=sum_(r^2m=n)d_2(r)chi(r)^2 mu(m)chi(m)
transfers the fixed-degree logarithmic input from
[Green-Tao, Theorem1.1, pp542-543](https://annals.math.princeton.edu/wp-content/uploads/annals-v175-n2-p03-p.pdf).
Use the fixed torus/filtration, finite character expansion and a fixed
logarithmic cutoff in r; pay the entire remaining square tail absolutely.
No GRH power remark or growing complexity is imported. Abel summation
of the actual damping and M=X(log X)^B in(9) then give, for each fixed D,

    ||C||_2^2 << X^(3/2)+X^2(log X)^(-D),
    ||C||_1 << X^(3/4)+X(log X)^(-D).                     (10)

The constants may be ineffective. Every fixed D still falls short of a
power X^(gamma+epsilon), gamma<1. Equation(6) transfers the logarithmic
bound to the complete core. This is a complete arithmetic test with a
recorded failure, not an inferred power improvement. Standard Liouville
Euler ancestry is also noted in
[Humphries, arXiv v2, pp1-2](https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/1569441/1/Humphries_the_distribution_of_weighted_sums_of_the_liouville.pdf);
his RH/LI/moment distribution hypotheses are not used.

For fixed k>2,b>1, the same single-square argument gives high cost
X^(b/2)A^(-1/2)+(X/A)^(k/(2k-1)). If b>=2k/(2k-1), the first term
dominates. Even the weaker Minkowski short-source corridor
alpha<=(4gamma-b)/3 is nonempty for every fixed gamma>1/2, by choosing
fixed1<b<=2gamma and sufficiently large fixed k. The complete return
retains all K shifts D_c(z+(b-1)j), with1-(b-1)K<gamma. Finite strip
descent makes every positive shift holomorphic before solving the
unshifted reciprocal with the covering primes. This is conditional
architectural reach only; no endpoint gamma=1/2 or variable-parameter
estimate is asserted.

The independent finite run checked56 exact collision identities, three
masked-row examples and five rational target rows; the author recorded
7680 frozen-cut identities. Those checks support algebra and bookkeeping.
The asymptotic proofs are(1)-(10) and the full retained arguments.
The next useful work is signed cancellation in the actual ordered-divisor
core, exploiting the enlarged asymmetric range, or a new upstream source
with a complete return. Merely improving an already affordable tail would
not close OPEN-LC.

    D_A(X)=sum_(q1,q2 squarefree) tau(q1)^A tau(q2)^A
                                         ||P_(q1,q2)X||_U^2.

All label sums have a frozen global cap, with empty terms zero. The new
estimate needed for later cross-copy cuts is

    D_A(F_>) << H_J U^(v+epsilon)(D1/G)J(D2/G).            (3)

For real H>=1 write a_H(q)=sum_(d|q,Nd>=H)mu(q/d). Divisor inversion gives
sum_(q|g)a_H(q)=1_(Ng>=H), |a_H(q)|<=tau(q), and a_H(q)=0 if Nq<H.
The exact expansion is

    F_>=sum_f a_G(f)phi_u(f)^2/(Nf)
                       M_u^(f)(D1/Nf)M_u^(f)(D2/Nf)Q_u.

For fixed squarefree f split q_i=g_i h_i with g_i|f and(h_i,f)=1.
The condition q_i|f x_i is precisely h_i|x_i. Extracting h_i from its
canonical inverse gives the factor mu(h_i)phi_u(h_i)/sqrt(Nh_i) and
M_u^(f h_i)(E_i/Nh_i), E_i=D_i/Nf, with its original profile. Shared
primes between h1,h2 and slots remain allowed.

The first inverse's elementary bound, the second's repaired moment(1)-(2),
and all g_i divisor weights leave squared price

    H_J U^epsilon E1/(Nh1)^2
             [U/(Nh2)+U^(1/6)E2^(5/6)/(Nh2)^(11/6)].

The h1^-2 and h2^(-11/6) sums converge after small losses; the finite
h2^-1 sum costs subpower and gives NO reciprocal cutoff gain. Minkowski
in the full row x q1 x q2 Hilbert space, before summing f, proves(3).
Its worst exponent v+r+5s/6-1/5 lies below T by at least2809/273000.
Using only the unprojected G155 bound would not prove(3).

More generally, for i=1,2 put

    E_i^A(H;X)=sum_(q1,q2 sf,Nq_i>=H)tau(q1)^A tau(q2)^A
                                           ||P_(q1,q2)X||_U^2.

Extract and trivially bound inverse i, while repairing and applying(1)
to the other. The positive bounds are

    E_1^A(H;F)<<H_J U^(v+epsilon)(D1/H)J(D2),
    E_2^A(H;F)<<H_J U^(v+epsilon)(D2/H)J(D1),
    E_i^A(H;F_<)<=2E_i^A(H;F)+2D_A(F_>).                 (4)

The last line is a proved positive Hilbert-space inequality. It preserves
both within-column cuts in the paired form without asserting signed-subset
norm monotonicity. The author's same-index thresholds
H11=D1/U^(1/2),H22=D2/U^(3/4) and their signed intersection follow, with
raw gaps30607/1365000,1853/67500 and4682/16875. The intersection's U
term retains the harmonic cost mentioned above.

## G180. All four cross-copy events and every overlap

Use left indices(d1,d2), right indices(d1',d2'), and edges11,12,21,22.
Keep H11,H22 above and set H12=H21=U^(3/5). For a nonempty edge subset E,
let C_E(X) be the exact ordered-pair part of<X,X> with
N gcd(d_i,d_j')>=H_ij for every edge ij in E. Define left/right labels

    l_i=lcm(q_ij:ij in E), r_j=lcm(q_ij:ij in E),

where empty lcm=1. Repeated divisor inversion gives the literal identity

    C_E(X)=sum_(q_e sf) product_(e in E)a_H_e(q_e)
                              <P_(l1,l2)X,P_(r1,r2)X>.   (5)

The first entry has the original W1(t1),W2(t2) and full Q on its indices;
the entire second entry is conjugated, with those separately parameterized
profiles evaluated on the right indices. An opposite edge changes only
divisibility. It never exchanges the profiles, identifies heights or
conjugates a lone inverse. Individual terms can be complex; transposition
gives C_(E^t)=overline(C_E). The complete union is real, not necessarily positive.

For a fixed left lcm pair, each incident edge label divides the corresponding
l_i, with degree at most two. Since |a_H(q)|<=tau(q), all assignment weights
at that pair sum to at most tau(l1)^4 tau(l2)^4. The same holds on the
right, including shared primes between labels. Selecting any edge i0j0,
weighted Cauchy followed by this complete lcm count proves

    |C_E(X)| <= [E_i0^4(H_i0j0;X)E_j0^4(H_i0j0;X)]^(1/2). (6)

Apply(4) with X=F_<. For an opposite edge the two full-F exponents are
b1=v+r-3/5+e(s) and b2=v+s+2/5, e(t)=max(1,1/6+5t/6). The continuous
box bounds give

    T-b1>=12931/135000>1/20,
    T-b2>=rho+(113/50)delta-93/50>=9229/170625>1/20.

The second minimum occurs at delta=17/25: its derivative is bounded below
by5917/6075. Same-index-only edge subsets use the corresponding(4) bound.
Thus every one of the15 nonempty intersections is paid, including all12
that involve an opposite edge. The limiting gap is still(3).

Allocate at most1/1000 for fixed geometric pads and1/500 for ALL auxiliary
power losses combined, before distributing their individual epsilons. After
retaining margin1/200 the spare reserve is

    2809/273000-1/1000-1/500-1/200=5/2184>0.

Consequently

    sum_(nonempty E subset {11,12,21,22})|C_E(F_<)|
                              <<H_J U^(T-1/200+epsilon). (7)

The exact bad union is sum_E(-1)^(|E|+1)C_E. Equation(7) bounds absolute
values of15 complete scalar forms; it does not bound the sum of absolute

## G181. A smaller signed residual, with the physical return still open

After(7), retain all six small-gcd conditions on the original tuples:
both within-column gcds<G, same-index cross gcds<H11,H22, and both
opposite-index cross gcds<U^(3/5). The old G156 diagonal and two conductor
sectors remain affordable after these extra restrictions, for a specific
reason: complete tuple absolute multiplicity obeys

    c_abs(n)<<H_J N0^(-1/2)U^epsilon,
    sum_n c_abs(n)^2<<H_J U^epsilon, N0=D1D2P0.

It majorizes every remaining ordered-pair subset before signs. It is not
|c_merged(n)|. Thus the old exponents1,109/60,9/5 survive with all natural
holes. Retain G157's original A^3B^2C support and conductor restrictions.

Let R4 be the exact ordered signed sum with the six gcd conditions,
n!=n', Q>U^(9/5), Q1/Q3>U^(8/5), all original slot labels, natural holes,
roots, phases, profiles and independent heights. It is real by pair
transposition and need not be positive. The full expansion gives

    ||F_<||_U^2=R4+O(H_J U^(T-1/200+epsilon)).             (8)

The new cuts remove a genuine previously retained factor pattern: with
r=.9,s=1.35 and no slots, take pairwise coprime squarefree factors of
exponents(.7,.2,1.35,.9,.65) for(q,a,e,b,f), and columns(qa,e,b,qf).
The two within and same-index gcds are1; edge12 has exponent.7. Its
relative Q1 exponent3.1 lies outside the old conductor sectors. This is
an admissible factor pattern, not a claimed zero configuration or norm
lower bound. Its transpose is handled by edge21.

The next arithmetic input is the one-sided OPEN-R4:

    R4<=H_J U^(T-xi+epsilon), some fixed xi>0,             (9)

uniformly over the licensed data and actual parameter suprema. An absolute
bound is stronger but unnecessary. Equations(3),(8) would imply free
OPEN-MIX with every strict margin below min(xi,1/200). Both actual G147
inverse-witness lower bounds and its counted prefix are still needed;
the resulting count would retain margin strictly below
min(xi,1/200,1/2000), after the stated losses. No possibly zero slot is
divided out.

This count is not a completed physical zero-exclusion proof. Both signed
physical projectors, family reconstruction, root/slot holes, exceptional
and inducing rows,6a/9a radii, K_phys and5/6 amplifier prices, clipped
rectangles, shortening, Euler shifts, errors, principal branches and the
common-mesh/actual-supremum return still require their full licensed payment.
The centered reserve is unspent. No numerical xi-to-c map is established,
and this box is not extrapolated to delta=2/3 or1/2.

The obstruction is now sharply located: fully coprime squarefree columns
can have all six gcds1 and Q1~N0^2, with Q2=Q3=1. They survive every cut,
while the available absolute envelope U N0 is too large. Their merged
two-divisor-profile coefficient is outside B3.6's canonical permission.
At equal heights a common-cofactor mu(g) sign squares away; distinct
heights retain nonpositive complex phases. Neither fact bounds the full norm.

Credit the earlier [[private research revision] MG21-MG30](../[private research revision]-continuation/mobius-gcd.md)
and its [independent review](../review-cycle-20.md) for the generic four-gcd
mechanism. That rational completed Mertens source uses four singleton Abel
summations and a fixed Mertens input; it is not imported into this unequal
Hecke mixed moment. The present useful addition is the literal original-source
projection-energy proof with independent heights, slots and all lcm labels.

For uniformity freeze the common mesh/buffer before the eventual family and
slot count, nominal cells/cuts before suprema, and one global label cap.
Do not differentiate thresholds. Tensor Sobolev keeps both inverse heights;
scale derivatives use -W/2-yW'. Fourier measures are fixed on the ambient
box before labels, derivative orders work backward through the bounded graph,
and raw label counts precede Fourier-decay choices. Genuine detector tails
remain G147's responsibility.

The independent run checked all15 graph identities in both orientations,
8192 extraction identities,3596 lcm-mass checks, natural zeros, conjugation,
weighted Cauchy and exact rational margins. One residual was negative,
confirming the importance of the one-sided contract. Those finite checks
do not prove the infinite estimate or an endpoint. The next substantive
target is signed cancellation in the actual unique relative-prime supports,
starting with the surviving fully coprime subclass and retaining both
divisor profiles and the full physical return.
