statement:
## G182. Complete masked large-gcd theorem

Fix b>1, an integer k>=4 and B0. For X>=2, real G>=1, bounded sequences
|a1(d)|,|a2(e)|<=1, |b0(l)|<=B0, and an arbitrary complex mask
|theta(d,e,l)|<=1 fixed before live x varies, put

    v_G(n)=sum_(d e l=n, gcd(d,e)>G) a1(d)a2(e)b0(l)theta(d,e,l),
    F_G(x)=sum_(n>=1) v_G(n) exp(-n/x^b-i(n/x)^k).

Then on the full real shell [X,2X], with measure dx/x,

    ||F_G||_1+||F_G||_2
      <<_(b,k,B0,epsilon) X^epsilon [X/G+X^(b/2)/sqrt(G)].     (G182.1)

The constant is uniform in every sequence, mask and real G, with no upper
polynomial cap on G. The mask may depend on X,G and all tuple labels;
it may not depend on live x. Natural zeros, shared primes, strict or
closed arithmetic cuts and output-dependent support all fit this scope.
This is a full source norm theorem, not a pointwise bound or monotonicity
claim for signed subsets.

Write r_G(n)=#{r>G:r^2 divides n}. Exact root collisions give

    sum_(n<=Y)r_G(n) <=2Y/G,
    sum_(n<=Y)r_G(n)^2
      =sum_(r,s>G)floor(Y/lcm(r,s)^2) <=16Y/G.                (G182.2)

For the second bound set r=gu,s=gv,(u,v)=1. The two lower bounds on
r,s give g>G/min(u,v). Summing g^-2 leaves
(2Y/G)sum min(u,v)/(u^2v^2)<16Y/G. Equal roots, multiple square
representations and the strict endpoint r>G are included.

Every ordered tuple has exact gcd r, so d=ru,e=rv,(u,v)=1. Dropping
coprimality only in an absolute upper bound leaves at most d3(n/r^2)
factorizations. Thus for each fixed eta>0,

    |v_G(n)| << n^eta r_G(n),
    sum_(n<=Y)|v_G(n)| <<Y^(1+eta)/G,
    sum_(n<=Y)|v_G(n)|^2 <<Y^(1+2eta)/G.                    (G182.3)

The needed local multiplicity estimate is, for an interval I of length h
inside [cN,CN],

    sum_(n in I)r_G(n) <<h/G+N/G^2.                         (G182.4)

Reverse n=r^2 l: at most CN/G^2 positive l occur, and each permissible
real r interval has length O(h/(sqrt(N)sqrt(l))). Sum length plus one.
This is valid for all G>=1, including h<1, singleton endpoints and empty
blocks. The stronger old alternative with error min(N^(1/3),N/G^2)
is valid but unnecessary for this refinement.

A smooth nonnegative majorant of the shell, followed by two integrations
by parts, bounds the complete kernel by

    exp(-c(n+m)/X^b) min(1,[X^k/|n^k-m^k|]^2),              (G182.5)

with the minimum set to one on the diagonal. The derivative of the phase
has no stationary point on the fixed positive support. Damping
derivatives are fixed polynomials absorbed by a weaker exponential.
Exponential convergence justifies the full infinite expansion.

Pay n<=X pointwise by X^(1+eta)/G. Norm triangle pays its entire
interaction with the remaining source. On each bounded-overlap
comparable high block n,m~N>=cX, put H=X^k/N^(k-1). The local count
and full coefficient mass give the positive absolute pair bound

    exp(-cN/X^b)N^(2eta)[HN/G^2+N^2/G^3].

The integer kernel row sum O(1+H), collision bound and
2|v_n v_m|<=|v_n|^2+|v_m|^2 give, on the SAME pair majorant,

    exp(-cN/X^b)N^(2eta)(N/G)(1+H).

Taking the minimum bounds that block by the common factor times

    X^k/(G^2 N^(k-2))+N/G
                   +min(N^2/G^3,X^k N^(2-k)/G).             (G182.6)

The local +1 term keeps the diagonal when H<1; off-diagonal integer
distances start at one. Alternatively, separate the exact diagonal
first, reserving N/G solely for it, and use the O(H) off-diagonal row
sum. Both arguments retain all multiplicities and ordered pairs.

Absorb the coefficient loss using actual damping:

    N^(2eta)e^(-cN/X^b) <<X^(2b eta)e^(-cN/(2X^b)).

This avoids any illicit G^eta<=X^epsilon assumption when G is enormous.
The last two branches in (G182.6) meet at N_*=X G^(2/k); their entire
dyadic sum is

    O_k(X^2 G^(4/k-3)) <=O_k(X^2/G^2), k>=4.                (G182.7)

Both geometric tails converge, including the closed degree endpoint
k=4. The first term also sums to X^2/G^2; damping pays the diagonal
sum by X^b/G. Far ordered pairs and their reverse orientation have
total cost

    sum_(N>=cX) X^(2k)N^(2-2k+2eta)/G^2
       <<X^(2+2eta)/G^2.

Choose eta after epsilon and below k-1, take square roots, and include
the low part by triangle. Finite-measure Cauchy proves L1. This completes
(G182.1) with every low, high, diagonal, comparable and far contribution.

At b=3/2,k=6 this is the author's X/G+X^(3/4)/sqrt(G) bound.
For general phases it removes the author's extra
X^(2k/(3k-2))/sqrt(G) term. The original proof remains valid and is
retained; the stronger complete estimate is the active version.

## G183. Literal smaller signed core and complete return

Import the [[private research revision] source and complements](../[private research revision]/square-source-integration.md)
exactly. Fix an ordinary chi modulo q and an unramified prime p. Put
a=lambda chi, h=chi, s(r^2)=chi(r)^2, zero off squares, and

    q1=delta1-p chi(p)delta_p,
    q2=delta1-p chi(p)^2 delta_(p^2), v=q1*q2,
    b0=v*h, g=a*s, c=v*g=a*a*b0.                           (G183.1)

Here a*h=s and a is completely multiplicative, including its natural
zeros. The p^2 coefficient is -p chi(p)^2. The two complete cofactors

    b0(n)=chi(n)[1-p1_(p|n)-p1_(p^2|n)+p^2 1_(p^3|n)],
    beta(r)=chi(r)^2(1-p1_(p|r))

are bounded periodic sequences of mean zero, with periods p^3q,pq.
The exact Euler series is

    D_c(z)=P_p(z)J_p(z)L(2z,chi^2)^2/L(z,chi),
    P_p(z)=1-chi(p)p^(1-z), J_p(z)=1-chi(p)^2p^(1-2z).

For 3/4<=gamma<1 retain the accepted choices

    L=X^gamma, M=X^((6-2gamma)/4),
    B(n)=min(L,X^6/(6000p^3q n^5)),
    U(n)=B(n)^tau, V(n)=B(n)^(1-tau),
    max(gamma tau,gamma(1-tau))<=(11gamma-3)/8.             (G183.2)

Tau and all cuts are fixed before live x. The exact ordered decomposition
c=Q_U+Q_V-S_tau+R_tau still holds, with both full short slots, the whole
small-double source and the long-long source. No cutoff is differentiated.

In the finite core L<n<=M impose the new condition gcd(d,e)<=G, where
G=X^(1-gamma), on the original long-long tuples. Denote the resulting
full signed shell source by T_small. Its discarded part has EXACT mask

    1_(L<del<=M)1_(d>U(del))1_(e>V(del))

in G182 with the strict gcd>G condition. For b=3/2,k=6 its norm costs
X^(gamma+epsilon), since the second exponent is
1/4+gamma/2<=gamma. All composite common factors, shared cofactors,
squareful outputs, original orders and natural zeros remain accounted for.

The difference C-T_small also includes both old short sources, minus the
full small-double source, the prefix n<=L and the ENTIRE damped high
tail n>M. Their accepted [private research revision] payments remain applicable BEFORE
the gcd restriction. In particular no periodic-mean argument is reapplied
after a new mask that might break it. Norm triangle gives

    ||C-T_small||_(1,2) <<X^(gamma+epsilon).                (G183.3)

The retained merged coefficient is exactly

    sum_(m l=n)a(m)b0(l)
       #{ordered(d,e):de=m,d>U(n),e>V(n),gcd(d,e)<=G}.

The merge a(d)a(e)=a(de) uses Liouville complete multiplicativity. It
does not license an unrestricted Mobius merge.

The prior absolute finite-core price required G>=X^((3/2)(1-gamma));
G182 permits G=X^(1-gamma). At the conditional quarter target the
threshold changes from X^(3/8) to X^(1/4), and at1/6 from X^(1/4)
to X^(1/6). At the current gamma11 the exponent is exactly c11.
These describe paid complementary regions, not attained new values of c.

OPEN-LCG is the remaining full signed L1 bound for T_small by
X^(gamma+epsilon), for every epsilon and all sufficiently large dyadic
X, for each fixed ordinary character and each of a fixed covering pair
of unramified primes. One gamma<gamma11 is chosen before characters
and candidate zeros. Tau may vary with epsilon,chi,p,X inside the
allowed corridor, but stays fixed on each real shell. Constants and
thresholds may depend on the fixed data. L2 at that exponent suffices.
A selected cell, sampled x, finite height range or fixed epsilon loss
does not meet this input.

By (G183.3), this hypothesis is equivalent to the corresponding full L1
bound for the FIXED complete source C. It is not claimed equivalent to
zero exclusion. The inherited complete Mellin identity is

    H_p(z)=A0(z)D_c(z)+E_p(z),
    A0(z)=Gamma(z/6)exp(-i pi z/12)/6,
    E_p holomorphic on Re z>1/2.                           (G183.4)

The all-shell bound gives holomorphy of H_p on Re z>gamma. The identity
uses C, not the shell-dependent core. A0 has no zero there, J_p vanishes
only on Re z=1/2, and L(2z,chi^2) is finite and nonzero on Re z>1/2.
P_p zeros are on Re z=1. Two distinct fixed primes cannot have a common
P zero at nonzero height; for nonprincipal chi choose one with chi(p)!=1
to cover height zero. The principal pole at1 is retained as the stated
exception. This gives the conditional ordinary-character zero-exclusion
return at every finite height, with no height-uniform or growing-q claim.

The actual coefficient variance still gives only ||C||_2<<X. The prior
fixed logarithmic bound has squared norm X^(3/2)+X^2(log X)^(-D)
for every fixed D. Transfer to T_small retains the extra complementary
cost. Neither result supplies any fixed power below1. The entire
gcd-one signed source remains present and unproved.

## G184. Ambient lower prices and fixed-phase compatibility

The two upper scales have scoped comparison examples. For the first,
take a1=a2=b0=1 and retain d=e=r, G<r<=2G, r^2 l<=X/2,
with G<=c sqrt(X). At least a constant times X/G tuples have phases
inside a fixed positive real sector throughout the shell. This gives
the X/G lower price.

For the diagonal take Y=floor(X^b), G<=c sqrt(Y), and retain d=e=r,
G<r<=2G,Y/2<r^2 l<=Y. Let A_n count these roots. Then
sum A_n^2>=sum A_n>>Y/G. Give all tuples of output n the same
independent Rademacher sign epsilon_n. With z_n=A_n f_x(n), the
second and fourth moments imply

    E|sum epsilon_n z_n| >=(sum |z_n|^2)^(1/2)/sqrt(3).

Since |f_x(n)|>=e^-1, finite Fubini over the full shell proves existence
of ONE fixed sign mask with L1, hence L2, norm at least
X^(b/2)/sqrt(G). This is a finite existence argument, not a numerical
random experiment or a statement about the actual Liouville signs.
At b=3/2 the two scales dominate in different nonempty ranges, so both
are required for the broad mask class. No claim of sharpness for every
b or every mask is made.

For G=X^(1-gamma), G182 pays the complement whenever gamma>=b-1,
for all k>=4. In the stated range gamma>1/2 the diagonal comparison
rules out dropping this condition for the broad bounded-mask class.
The former additional condition gamma>=(k+2)/(3k-2) is unnecessary
for this complement. Every older short-source and tail constraint
must still be satisfied; this does not by itself lower the phase
degree of a complete proof architecture.

The accepted general architecture remains compatible with every fixed
gamma>1/2: choose fixed 1<b<=2gamma and sufficiently large k>=6,
with b>=2k/(2k-1), r=(k-2gamma)/(k-2)<b and the original short-source
corridor. Keep EVERY finite shifted Mellin term

    sum_(j<K) A_j(z)D_c(z+(b-1)j),
    A_j(z)=(-1)^j Gamma((z+bj)/k)exp(-i pi(z+bj)/(2k))/(k j!),

and choose fixed K with1-(b-1)K<gamma. Finite strip descent, the same
two-prime cover and the principal exception give the conditional return.
Example gamma=3/5,b=11/10,k=12,K=5,r=27/25 is compatible. No parameter
grows with X, and no gamma=1/2 endpoint or limiting uniformity follows.

The investigated cyclotomic separated-layer replacement meets the
existing W22/W35 branch obstruction; its coupled identity is retained
without new credit. The proposed direct prime-dilation profile has
large correlations and fails that orthogonality criterion's input.
Those scoped failures and primary-source read extents remain in the
original reports. Neither outside theorem is used in G182-G184.

The next substantive task is arithmetic cancellation in the exact
retained signed source, or a different source with a complete paid
return. Further improvement of an already paid complement alone cannot
raise the accepted value of c.

## G185. Primitive Poisson and the complete two-color sieve bound

On a squarefree merged column, the original coefficient is exactly

    F_sf,u=(-1)^j N0^(-1/2) sum_(n sf) mu(n)nu(n)chi_n(u)^e A(n),
    A(n)=sum_(original P|n) b(P)conjugate(nu(P))
                    sum_(d1 d2=n/P) W1(q_d1/D1;t1)W2(q_d2/D2;t2).

Slots retain their ordered labels. The sign is mu(d1)mu(d2)=(-1)^jmu(n);
the two inverse signs are not independent random variables. Since nu(P)
is a unit on the fixed good source, its conjugate is legitimate; no
natural row character value is divided out.

Expand the row indicator by sum_(a^6|u)mu(a), put u=a^6 z, and retain
(a,nn')=1. The row scale is U_a=U/q_a^6 with q_a<<U^(1/6). For actual
coprime squarefree n,n', psi=chi_n^e conjugate(chi_n'^e) is primitive
and nonprincipal at its full good conductor nn': its local exponents
are1 and5. Primitive Poisson therefore gives zero at ell=0 and at every
frequency sharing a good conductor prime. This does not remove a principal
original family. The normalized finite transform is

    sum_(x mod nn') psi(x)e(ell x/(nn'))
       =sqrt(q_n q_n') gamma(psi;nn') conjugate(psi(ell)).

The CRT factor chi_n(n')^e chi_n'(n)^(-e)=R(n,n') is the fixed ray sign
of PR9 B1.1-B1.5. It does not produce a variable cubic coupling across
copies. Set a0(n)=conjugate(alpha(n))gamma_2(n). PR9 B1.10 yields

    mu(n)gamma_1(n)=conjugate(a0(n))G(n),
    mu(n)gamma_-1(n)=a0(n)chi_n(-1)conjugate(G(n)).

Thus, apart from the retained nu(n)conjugate(nu(n')), the arithmetic
factors for e=-1 and e=1 respectively are

    R(n,n')chi_n(-1)conjugate(G(n))G(n')
         a0(n)conjugate(a0(n'))chi_n(ell)conjugate(chi_n'(ell));
    R(n,n')G(n)conjugate(G(n'))chi_n'(-1)
         conjugate(a0(n))a0(n')conjugate(chi_n(ell))chi_n'(ell).

Expand the fixed ray factors into the prescribed finite separated
dictionary. Fixed row restrictions modulo a disjoint S-supported modulus
retain primitive good-prime Fourier zeros by CRT. The dictionary may
depend on a's fixed residue class, with bounded cost. The first-dual cut
is on the actual fixed dual lattice; clearing a fixed denominator changes
its comparison constant and is not silently identified with the old cut.

The central pair coefficient and Poisson roots leave

    U/(q_a^6 N0^2),

with N0/sqrt(q_n q_n') retained in the smooth profile. Its radial kernel
keeps the exact argument U_a q_ell/(q_n q_n'), all original heights and
fixed factors. Before algebraic extension or an absolute Fourier integral,
pay the genuine far tail as proved in G186 below.

For fixed Y of at most a fixed polynomial size, define R_unique,<=Y by
the literal restriction0<q_ell<=Y in this exact expression. Pair
transposition with complete conjugation preserves that radial restriction;
the scalar can be kept real without assuming positivity.

Extend the displayed product expression and formal product conductor to
all individually squarefree n,n' in their original supports, then insert

    1_((n,n')=1)=sum_(f|n,f|n')mu(f).

The FULL identity kills every artificial noncoprime pair, including
inverse-slot and slot-slot intersections. No imprimitive Poisson theorem
is asserted on added pairs. Write n=fm,n'=fm'. Squarefreeness keeps
(f,m)=(f,m')=1 and

    a0(fm)=a0(f)a0(m)chi_m(f)^4,
    chi_f(ell)conjugate(chi_f(ell))=1_((f,ell)=1).

Each prime of f is allocated to its actual inverse color or original slot
on each side. The two allocations may differ. On one side f=f1 f2 fP,

    D1'=D1/q_f1, D2'=D2/q_f2, P'=P0/q_fP,
    X_f=D1'D2'P'=N0/q_f.

The other side has the same product X_f with independently shortened
color and slot lengths. Both allocation multiplicities together cost
tau(f)^C at fixed slot depth. Assigned slot coefficients and pool tests
remain present. Nonempty subunit nominal windows are clipped by bounded
original annular factors; truly empty windows stay empty.

Separate the full profile on the ambient original normalized norm box
BEFORE live labels, keeping its two real inverse roots once. On nominal
a- and ell-dyads A,H, the coupled kernel is

    K(C*y_ell/(y_a^6 product(y_original_columns))),
    C=UH/(A^6N0^2).

Its Euler derivatives are uniformly bounded for C>0 by fixed Schwartz
seminorms. PR9 B3.3 fixes the common Fourier measure first. Only then
substitute extracted factors; their imaginary powers have modulus one.
Sharp arithmetic masks and the dual cutoff stay outside the smooth
separation. Both original heights remain on their own profiles, with
the fixed finite-order H_J cost. This inherits, rather than resolves,
the open positive-slot uniformity ancestry.

For a fixed remaining slot tuple P, PR9 B1.11 gives

    a0(xyP)=a0(x)a0(y)a0(P)chi_y(x)^4 chi_x(P)^4 chi_y(P)^4.

All a,f,ell punctures, finite ray data and frequency twists separate
between x and y. Their coprimality is the natural cubic-symbol zero.
The two sieve variables are the original residual colors OF ONE COPY,
never a product mixing left and right columns.

The unconditional squarefree cubic large sieve, as stated in
[Dunn-Radziwill, equation1.11 and Theorem9.1](https://arxiv.org/html/2109.07463v3),
allows an arbitrary inner sequence independent of its outer variable,
with price D+E+(DE)^(2/3). Both variables are squarefree primary
Eisenstein elements. Cauchy and reciprocity/conjugation give

    |(DE)^(-1/2) sum_(x,y sf) alpha_x beta_y chi_y(x)^4|^2
       << H_J (DE)^epsilon [D+E+(DE)^(2/3)].

The two coefficient squared masses O(D),O(E) cancel the normalization.
Natural holes are zero coefficients or restrictions of the positive
outer sum. Ell is a fixed parameter here and need not be squarefree.
No arbitrary joint coefficient matrix or conductor-dependent loss is
admitted. No GRH refinement, optimality lower bound or cuspidal theorem
is imported into this noncuspidal source.

Triangle over the original surviving slots costs P' after squaring:
the normalized complete residual column B_f satisfies

    |B_f(ell)|^2 << H_J U^epsilon P'[D1'+D2'+(D1'D2')^(2/3)]
                << H_J U^epsilon P0[D1+D2+(D1D2)^(2/3)].

The other column has its own profile and allocation; use their geometric
mean. Restoring BOTH unnormalized roots contributes X_f, exactly

    [U/(q_a^6 N0^2)]sqrt(X_f X_f)=U/(q_a^6 N0 q_f).

The real profile ratio is X_f/sqrt(q_m q_m'), bounded on its actual
evaluation points, and produces no extra q_f power. All allocation
counts are paid before summing

    sum_a q_a^(-6)<<1,
    sum_(q_f<<N0)tau(f)^C/q_f<<_epsilon U^epsilon,
    #{ell:0<q_ell<=Y}<<Y.

The f-sum is harmonic up to small powers, not uniformly convergent.
Choose its divisor loss after the fixed scale cap. Restoring the complete
Fourier integral proves

    |R_unique,<=Y| << H_J U^(1+epsilon)Y/(D1D2)
                            [D1+D2+(D1D2)^(2/3)].       (G185)

The slot factor P0 cancels its denominator in N0 because it was paid.
This is a bound on a complete signed scalar sector after exact identities,
not on the absolute mass of its original pair expansion.

## G186. Larger paid low band, genuine far tail and finite signed residual

On the physical box s<2r,r<2s, so the last term dominates the bracket.
For Y=U^kappa the exponent is1+kappa-(r+s)/3. At kappa=3/2, the coarse
floors alone leave857/16875>1/20 below T. A sharper uniform calculation
uses E_K>=rho:

    T-[1+kappa-(r+s)/3]
       >=(delta+1/3)(r+s)+rho-1-kappa.

The derivative in delta is at least217/100-625/486=21481/24300>0;
the expression increases in r+s. Its limiting lower endpoint gives
kappa_*=268943/170625. Thus kappa=39/25 leaves the exact raw margin
2768/170625>.0162. Choose all finite geometric, arithmetic, profile and
height losses sufficiently small to retain margin1/100.

The far tail must be bounded on the GENUINE coprime source before the
extension and absolute Fourier separation in G185. Fix a bounded-overlap
partition q_a~A first and L_A=A^6N0^2/U. Each original copy has
O(H_J N0 U^epsilon) inverse/slot tuples. The central pair normalization
and primitive Poisson factor are O(U/(q_a^6N0^2)), and normalized
primitive Gauss factors have modulus one. Therefore on q_ell~H,

    |R_(A,H)| <= sum|genuine source terms|
       << H_J U^(1+epsilon) A^(-5)H(1+H/L_A)^(-B).

This pays O(A) labels and O(H) lattice frequencies, keeps all masks,
and uses the actual Schwartz kernel. For fixed tau>0, its dyadic tail
H>U^tau L_A costs

    H_J U^epsilon A N0^2 U^(-tau(B-1)).

Since L_A>>1 throughout the box, no omitted small-lattice term occurs.
Summing A<<U^(1/6) gives the deliberately coarse full bound

    H_J U^(149/30+epsilon-tau(B-1)),
    1/6+2(r+s)+2v<=149/30.

For any desired M choose finite B>1+(149/30+M+1)/tau and epsilon<1.
This is O(H_J U^(-M)). All orders and raw powers are fixed before B;
fixed support factors are retained in the cutoff or a small geometric
pad. Only after this payment is the retained finite expression extended
and its ambient profile separated. This is an application of PR9's
genuine-source tail rule, not new cancellation in the main dual range.

Define R_middle on each original a-dyad by the exact range

    U^(39/25)<q_ell<=U^tau A^6N0^2/U.

Then R4=R_nonunique+R_middle+R_low+R_far exactly. The paid low and far
pieces, together with G181, give

    ||F_<||_U^2=R_nonunique+R_middle
                      +O(H_J U^(T-1/200+epsilon)).     (G186)

This statement keeps the entire complementary source. The lowest natural
dual scale N0^2/U has exponent2(r+s+v)-1>3.34, and the largest a-dyad
cap can approach U^(4.8+tau). The finite middle is still very large.

OPEN-R4-MIDDLE is a one-sided bound on the SUM R_nonunique+R_middle
with some fixed saving xi>0. If proved, it would supply free OPEN-MIX
with every strict margin below min(xi,1/200). The two actual inverse
signals and counted prefix would retain margin below
min(xi,1/200,1/2000). A possibly zero slot is never divided out.

The physical zero-exclusion return would still require both signed
projectors, family reconstruction, root/slot holes, exceptional and
inducing rows,6a/9a radii,K_phys,5/6 amplification, clipped rectangles,
shortenings, Euler shifts, principal branches, actual suprema, common
mesh and all genuine detector tails. Buffered internal witnesses may
exceed delta=.70: extract their signal before weakening the physical bin.
The centered reserve is unspent. No xi-to-c map or endpoint follows.

## G187. Exact merged structure and why its simpler proposed price fails

The actual two-color squarefree mark is

    eta_(z,w)(n)=product_(p|n)(q_p^(-z)+q_p^(-w)).

It retains independent Mellin/height variables. Forced-slot division can
use Re z=kappa,Re w=-kappa, where every factor has modulus at least
q_p^kappa(1-q_p^(-2kappa))>0. On equal real contours it can vanish.
The cost is divisor bounded times n^kappa at fixed depth; natural character
zeros are not divided out. Coprime extraction is multiplicative, and
algebraic cube inversion works for any whole-index mark, because the
sum over h|c cancels at fixed completed index nc^3.

Extending eta(p^a)=q_p^(-az)+q_p^(-aw) gives a unitary two-color split
of the completed theta index. Its cross coefficient remains

    chi_(A2)(A1)^4=chi_(n2)(n1)^4,
    A_i=n_i b_i^3, (A1,A2)=1.

The actual norm7/norm13 prime example gives the nontrivial phase omega.
Thus the completed system is a coupled coprime theta convolution. PR9's
terminal reflected-energy theorem does not authorize this arbitrary
eta-weighted source. Cube inversion is not the missing analytic gate.

Even granting the unchanged canonical single-inverse exponent
e(L)=(1+5L)/6 at L=r+s would not suffice. Since E_K<=rho+delta v,

    e(r+s)-T>=1/6+(5/6-delta)(r+s)-rho-delta v
             >=1867/27000>.0691.

The endpoint for this lower bound is delta=.7,r+s=2.17,v=.05;
at v=0 the gap is703/6750. This is failure of a proposed upper-bound
price, not a lower bound on R4. Extending only the coefficient contract
would leave the quantitative problem open.

For completeness, on absolute lines the original coprime signed product
has Euler factors1-X_p-Y_p, with X_p=phi_u(p)q_p^(-s1),Y_p=phi_u(p)q_p^(-s2).
It equals [L_u(s1)L_u(s2)]^(-1) times the correction with local factor
1-X_pY_p/[(1-X_p)(1-Y_p)]. Its coefficient at positive exponents a,b
is -phi_u(p)^(a+b), with zero at just one positive exponent. The
correction is absolutely convergent when both real parts remain positive
and their sum exceeds one. It supplies no fourth moment or zero crossing.

## G188. A complete periodic-cofactor estimate

Fix bounded mean-zero Q-periodic b, X>=2 and any finite real D>=1. All A_m are fixed before x in [X,2X], with |A_m|<=A.
Write f_x(n)=exp(-n/x^(3/2)-i(n/x)^6) and use shell measure dx/x.
Then the theorem is

    H_D(x)=sum_(m<=D) A_m sum_(l>=1)b(l)f_x(ml),
    ||H_D||_1+||H_D||_2 << A(D+X^(3/4))log^4(2X).          (G188.1)

Constants retain only Q and ||b||inf (and the fixed cutoff). For D
bounded by a fixed power of X, divisor-bounded A_m replace the logarithm
by X^epsilon, for every epsilon after choosing the divisor loss. There is no growing-period, live-x coefficient or
arbitrary output/cofactor mask permission.

Take a fixed smooth nonincreasing phi equal1 on[0,1], zero on[2,infinity)
and w(t)=phi(t/2)-phi(t). The exact identity

    1=phi(n/X)+sum_(j>=0)w(n/(2^j X))                     (G188.2)

retains all transitions and the infinite damped tail. On the low part,
rows m<=delta_Q X have nonzero Fourier derivatives separated from
integers, including the last increment, for a sufficiently small fixed
delta_Q. Discrete first derivative and Abel summation give O_Q(1).
Larger active low rows have m<=2X and at most 2/delta_Q terms, so each
costs O_Q(1) trivially. All low rows cost O(A min(D,X))<=O(AD).

On a high block N=2^jX, rows m>4N are exactly empty. Remove these
before Poisson and use the frozen interval [M,2M) intersect[1,D]
intersect[1,4N]. In particular m/N<=4. Put T=(N/X)^6.
Poisson, with b expanded at period Q, gives EXACTLY

    sum_l b(l)w(ml/N)f_x(ml)=(1/m)sum_(h in Z)beta_h I_(h/m)(x),
    I_r=int_0^infinity w(n/N)e^(-n/x^(3/2))
                  exp(i[2pi r n/Q-(n/x)^6])dn.             (G188.3)

The periodic beta_h obey beta_(Qj)=0. Both signs and every alias remain.
For r>0, the critical point and its phase are

    n_r=(pi r/(3Q))^(1/5)x^(6/5),
    phase=5(pi/(3Q))^(6/5)r^(6/5)x^(6/5),
    second derivative=-30n_r^4/x^6.

Choose an ambient near range c_QT/N<=r<=C_QT/N before x or live labels,
wide enough to contain every stationary point meeting [N,4N]. The
rescaled phases form a compact nondegenerate family. Smooth stationary
phase, including smooth support crossings, yields

    I_r=Z_r exp(i*kappa_Q*r^(6/5)x^(6/5)-i*pi/4)
                      +O((N/T)e^(-cN/X^(3/2))),
    Z_r=sqrt(pi/15)x^3 n_r^(-2)w(n_r/N)e^(-n_r/x^(3/2)).   (G188.4)

Its uniformity follows from a compact Morse change and bounded damped
amplitude derivatives. Sharp stationary endpoints are not erased:
the argument completes the entire source before using smooth blocks.

Let H_m=mT/N. Near aliases number O(1+H_m), and any nonempty near bank
has H_m bounded below, so their total remainder after1/m is O(1)
with damping. Negative and small nonstationary aliases have rescaled
derivative comparable T; two integrations by parts give O(T^-1) after
summing them. The entire large-alias tail sums (m/N)h^-2, costing
O(T^-1) or O(m/N). Thus the whole transformed row has a damped O(1)
error, and the row-block error is O(AM e^(-cN/X^(3/2))).

Reduce r=h/m=u/v, so m=vj,h=uj. The ENTIRE Z_r and phase depend only
on r,N,x. The only remaining separate m factor is1/m. Consequently

    C_(u/v)=sum_(vj in original row block) A_(vj)beta_(uj)/(vj)

is x-independent and |C_(u/v)|<<A/v. All original truncations, Fourier
zeros and collisions are retained. Since u>=1 and r<=C_QT/N,
v>=N/(C_QT), while v<=2M. Therefore

    sum_r |C_r|^2 << A^2 sum_(max(1,N/(C_QT))<=v<=2M)
                         (vT/N+1)/v^2
                    << A^2(T/N)log(2M).                    (G188.5)

The lower denominator bound is essential; dropping it introduces an
unpaid N^2/T term.

For x=Xz, the first two needed amplitude bounds are
|Z_r|+|dZ_r/dz|<<(N/sqrt T)e^(-cN/X^(3/2)). Distinct r,s have phase
derivative comparable N|r-s|. One integration by parts retains both
shell endpoints and bounds their full inner product by

    (N^2/T)e^(-cN/X^(3/2))min(1,1/(N|r-s|)).               (G188.6)

The diagonal uses the same estimate with minimum1. Distinct reduced
fractions with denominators<=2M are separated by1/(4M^2). There are
J<<M+M^2T/N, and the full kernel row sum is
O(1+(M^2/N)log(2+J)). Applying2|C_r C_s|<=|C_r|^2+|C_s|^2 to the
entire pair sum and using(G188.5) proves

    ||whole (M,N) block||_2^2
         <<A^2 e^(-cN/X^(3/2))(N+M^2)log^2(2N).             (G188.7)

The already bounded row error is included by norm triangle. Summing
whole blocks in norm retains all cross terms. Since M<=4N, all
logarithms are O(log(2N)) without a log D. For fixed N, M sums to
O(min(D,N)), while the sqrt N part acquires at most log(2N). Thus the
whole high source is at most

    A sum_(N=2^jX)e^(-cN/X^(3/2))
        [sqrt N log^2(2N)+min(D,N)log(2N)].

The two sums are bounded by X^(3/4)log^2(2X) and D log^2(2X).
The infinite damped tail converges; finite-measure Cauchy gives L1.
This proves the arbitrary finite D extension, independently developed
by the reviewer and reconstructed by root. It does not assert an
infinite undamped coefficient bank or a different phase theorem.

## G189. Full constant-cut source transfer

For fixed ordinary chi modulo q and p not dividing q, let a=lambda chi,
h=chi and s(r^2)=chi(r)^2, zero off squares. Define

    q1=delta1-p chi(p)delta_p,
    q2=delta1-p chi(p)^2 delta_(p^2), v=q1*q2,
    b0=v*h, c=a*a*b0=v*a*s,
    b0(l)=chi(l)[1-p1_(p|l)-p1_(p^2|l)+p^2 1_(p^3|l)].     (G189.1)

The coefficient at p^2 in q2 is -p, not -p^2. The literal b0 has
fixed period p^3q, mean zero and bounded size. Natural character zeros,
shared factors and both physical compensations are preserved.

Fix3/4<=gamma<1 and a shell-frozen tau in the closed corridor
max(gamma tau,gamma(1-tau))<=(11gamma-3)/8. Set

    L=X^gamma, M=X^((6-2gamma)/4),
    U=X^(gamma tau), V=X^(gamma(1-tau)), G=X^(1-gamma).

The exact ordered identity is

    c=Q_U+Q_V-S+R,
    Q_U=a_(<=U)*(v*s), Q_V=a_(<=V)*(v*s),
    S=a_(<=U)*a_(<=V)*b0, R=a_(>U)*a_(>V)*b0.              (G189.2)

The whole S has frozen coefficients A_m=sum_(de=m,d<=U,e<=V)a(d)a(e),
supported m<=UV=L and bounded by d2(m). G188 pays its COMPLETE source
by X^(gamma+epsilon), including all stationary and infinite-tail terms.

[restricted research revision]'s square-short result permits frozen infinite root prefixes. For
D=X^alpha its four norm exponents are alpha,(3+8alpha)/11,
3/8+alpha/4, min(3/10+7alpha/10,15/32+alpha/4). All are<=gamma in
the stated corridor. Both physical labels1,p, weights1,-p chi(p), and
natural root zeros chi(r)^2(1-p1_(p|r)) remain in that complete result.

Every R tuple has de>UV=L, so the entire prefix n<=L is identically
empty. Its full infinite tail n>M has squared norm at most
X^(3/2+epsilon)+X^6 M^(-4+epsilon)<=X^(2gamma+epsilon).
[restricted research revision] G182 pays every remaining tuple with gcd(d,e)>G, under the
literal mask L<del<=M,d>U,e>V, by
X^epsilon[X/G+X^(3/4)/sqrtG]<=X^(gamma+epsilon).

Thus, defining the COMPLETE finite core

    T_rect=sum_(L<n<=M)f_x(n)
       sum_(del=n,d>U,e>V,gcd(d,e)<=G)a(d)a(e)b0(l),

the source transfer is

    ||C-T_rect||_(1,2)<<X^(gamma+epsilon), C=sum_n c(n)f_x(n). (G189.3)

All constants are uniform over allowed frozen tau, a compact corridor
for each fixed gamma. Endpoint gamma=3/4 and corridor equality remain
included with every-epsilon losses. No extra gcd involving l is imposed.

The old adaptive core T_ad has the same output window/gcd restriction
but smaller inverse cuts. Its removed signed wedge is paid by
||T_ad-T_rect||<=||T_ad-C||+||C-T_rect||. This uses TWO independently
proved complete transfers, never monotonicity under signed restriction.

Every retained cofactor has l<M/L=X^(3(1-gamma)/2), half the old
high-end adaptive exponent3(1-gamma). At gamma11 this is .1877189454;
at gamma=.8748 it is .1878; at5/6 it is1/4; at3/4 it is3/8.
Balanced inverse floors become X^(gamma/2). The exact merged source is
a(m)b0(l) times the ordered count of allowed de=m; Liouville complete
multiplicativity includes shared primes and natural zeros. It supplies
an identity, not arithmetic cancellation.

For one common gamma<gamma11 chosen before chi/zeros, OPEN-RECT asks
||T_rect||_1<<X^(gamma+epsilon) for every epsilon, all sufficiently
large dyadic shells, every fixed chi and both members of a fixed
covering prime pair. Tau may depend on fixed data, epsilon and shell,
but stays frozen before x. L2 suffices. A single cell, sampled x,
fixed loss or finite-height sample does not meet this hypothesis.

G189.3 makes that full norm hypothesis equivalent to the corresponding
complete C norm, and hence to the old core norm; it is not claimed
equivalent to zero exclusion. The fixed-source Mellin return retains

    D_c(z)=P_p(z)J_p(z)L(2z,chi^2)^2/L(z,chi),
    P_p=1-chi(p)p^(1-z), J_p=1-chi(p)^2p^(1-2z),
    H_p(z)=Gamma(z/6)e^(-i*pi*z/12)D_c(z)/6+E_p(z),
    E_p holomorphic on Re z>1/2.                           (G189.4)

The all-shell bound continues H_p above gamma with an epsilon buffer.
The numerator has no zeros there except P_p on Re z=1. Two distinct
unramified primes cover its nonzero-height zeros; for nonprincipal chi
one covering prime has chi(p)!=1 to cover height zero. The principal
pole at1 remains the allowed exception. This is the inherited complete
conditional ordinary-character all-height return, not a new theorem
for growing conductor or native Hecke coefficients. No variable b/k
or omitted shifted Mellin term is introduced here.

## G190. A paid diagonal and the actual remaining correlation

Take balanced cuts and gamma>6/7. First remove the gcd mask from the
WHOLE finite core with G182's paid cost. On each full original dyadic
cell n~N>=X,d~D,e~E,DE*l~N, orient D>=E; both exceed a constant times
X^(gamma/2). Cauchy in d retains the diagonal and the full e,e' Gram.
For e'=e+h the difference-phase derivative in d is comparable
T*h/(DE), T=(N/X)^6. Its maximum is O(T/D)=o(1), since
N<=M gives T<=X^(3(1-gamma)) and gamma>6/7.

The two exact product-cut intervals intersect in one interval or none.
First-derivative summation, with both endpoints and actual damping,
gives |K_(e,e+h)|<<min(D,DE/(T*h)). Summing ALL h and both orders,
including the diagonal, gives

    |sum_(d,e) a(d)a(e)f_x(del)|
        <<DE[E^(-1/2)+T^(-1/2)sqrt(log(2E))].              (G190.1)

After every cofactor and original dyadic label, the whole N block costs
X^epsilon[N X^(-gamma/4)+X^3/N^2]. The first term is paid by X^gamma
through N<=M when gamma>=6/7. The second is paid only at the top end.
The complete coarse calculation, including L<N<X, still gives X^(1+
epsilon). It proves no first gain, and no lower bound for the signed sum.

Before absolutes, the exact offdiagonal is

    B_(l,x)=2Re sum_(e<e') lambda(ee')chi(e)conj(chi(e'))
       sum_(d in I_e intersect I_e')
       exp(-i[(del/x)^6-(de'l/x)^6]) times both damping factors.

Natural zeros stay present; eliminating a(d) by Cauchy does not create
independent signs. A SUFFICIENT one-sided arithmetic input is

    B_(l,x)<=C_epsilon D E^2 X^epsilon (X^gamma/N)^2        (G190.2)

for EVERY finite-core cell, including N<X, each l and every real x.
This sufficient Gram condition and its diagonal budget also include
gamma=6/7. The coarse first-derivative test above requires strict
gamma>6/7; an O(1) derivative at equality need not avoid integer aliases.
The diagonal is already paid: E>~X^(gamma/2)>=(N/X^gamma)^2 up to
fixed cell factors when gamma>=6/7. Thus(G190.2) would give
DE X^(gamma+epsilon)/N, and the full cofactor sum costs only harmonic
factors. Negative B helps; an absolute correlation estimate is stronger
than needed.

For N>=X, the available coarse estimate misses(G190.2) by
X^(6-2gamma)/N^4=(M/N)^4. For L<N<X the gap is(N/L)^2.
At N~X the missing squared saving is X^(2(1-gamma)). Actual shifted
Liouville products lambda(e(e+h)) have been identified, not estimated.
This is the remaining arithmetic problem, together with possible
alternative complete norm arguments. No value of c is increased.

The nearer gamma=.8748 would give conditional c=.1252, exceeding c11
by135091/2500000000. The1/6 and1/4 targets keep the constant-cut transfer,
although the coarse small-derivative/diagonal argument above was only

## G191. Complete periodic cofactor estimate for fixed b,k

Fix b>1, an integer k>=4 and a bounded mean-zero Q-periodic h. For X>=2,
any finite real D>=1, and any complex bank |A_m|<=A fixed before real x varies,
put

    f_x(n)=exp(-n/x^b-i(n/x)^k),
    H_D(x)=sum_(m<=D) A_m sum_(l>=1)h(l)f_x(ml).

With both norms on the entire shell [X,2X], measure dx/x,

    ||H_D||_1+||H_D||_2 << A(D+X^(b/2))log^4(2X).          (191.1)

Constants depend only on the fixed data. No growing b,k,Q, live-x bank,
arbitrary joint mask, or infinite undamped row bank is asserted. Divisor losses
become X^epsilon only over ranges bounded by a fixed power of X.

Here are the complete changes to G188's proof. Use the exact smooth partition
phi(n/X)+sum_(N=2^jX)w(n/N)=1, with w supported in[1,4]. Low rows m<=delta X
have all nonzero periodic Fourier derivatives separated from integers, including
the last discrete increment, for fixed delta depending on Q,k. Larger active
low rows have at most2/delta terms. Discrete summation by parts and actual
damping pay the entire low source by A min(D,X).

On each high block remove exactly empty m>4N BEFORE Poisson. For the frozen
row interval [M,2M) intersect[1,D] intersect[1,4N], put T=(N/X)^k. The exact
transform is m^(-1)sum_h beta_h I_(h/m), with beta_(Qj)=0 and

    I_r=int w(n/N)e^(-n/x^b)exp(i[2pi r n/Q-(n/x)^k])dn.

Both alias signs and every Fourier residue remain. In a fixed positive ambient
near range r~T/N, chosen before x, the critical point and full leading term are

    n_r=(2pi r/(kQ))^(1/(k-1))x^(k/(k-1)),
    Phi_r=(k-1)(2pi r/(kQ))^(k/(k-1))x^(k/(k-1)),
    Z_r=sqrt(2pi/[k(k-1)])x^(k/2)n_r^(-(k-2)/2)
                                    w(n_r/N)e^(-n_r/x^b),
    I_r=Z_r exp(i Phi_r-i*pi/4)+O((N/T)e^(-cN/X^b)).

After n=Nt, x=Xz, the phases form a fixed compact nondegenerate family.
The review proves this uniform remainder by a Morse coordinate, including
smooth support crossings. Every differentiated damping polynomial is absorbed
by a weaker exponential. Summing every near remainder, negative alias,
small nonstationary alias and large alias tail costs O(e^(-cN/X^b)) per row;
the large tail uses the exact m/N<=4 condition. No remainder derivative is used.

Reduce r=h/m=u/v and group the ENTIRE leading term, not just its phase:

    C_(u/v)=sum_(vj in row) A_(vj)beta_(uj)/(vj), |C_(u/v)|<<A/v.

The mandatory lower denominator v>=N/(CT) gives
sum_r|C_r|^2<<A^2(T/N)log(2M). For the full sharp x shell, both endpoints
and the weight1/z are retained in the Gram kernel

    (N^2/T)e^(-cN/X^b)min(1,1/(N|r-s|)).

Reduced fractions are1/(4M^2)-separated. Their complete positive kernel row
sum is O(1+(M^2/N)log(2N)), since their number is polynomial in N for fixed k.
The entire block, including all alias remainders, therefore has squared norm

    << A^2 e^(-cN/X^b)(N+M^2)log^2(2N).

Summing WHOLE block norms keeps all interactions. For fixed N the M terms
sum to O(min(D,N)); the sqrt(N) terms cost an additional log(2N). The full
infinite damped N sum is bounded by

    A[X^(b/2)log^2(2X)+D log^2(2X)].

Together with the low source and finite-measure Cauchy this proves(191.1).
Arbitrarily large finite D creates no log D. This is a complete extension of
the earlier degree6 proof, with its changed terms reconstructed explicitly.

## G192. Complete degree12 source transfer

Use the IDENTICAL ordinary-character coefficients from G189. For a fixed
Dirichlet character chi modulo q, naturally zero at nonunits, and fixed p not
dividing q, let a(n)=lambda(n)chi(n), h0=chi, and s(r^2)=chi(r)^2, zero off squares.
All products below are Dirichlet convolutions:

    q1=delta1-p chi(p)delta_p,
    q2=delta1-p chi(p)^2 delta_(p^2), v=q1*q2,
    b0=v*h0, c=a*a*b0=v*a*s,
    b0(l)=chi(l)[1-p1_(p|l)-p1_(p^2|l)+p^2 1_(p^3|l)].

The q2 coefficient is -p. The bounded b0 is mean-zero of period p^3q.
Shared primes, both compensators, ordered factors and all natural zeros remain.
Fix b=3/2,k=12,gamma=5/6 and shell-frozen

    L=X^(5/6), U=V=X^(5/12), G=X^(1/6), M=X^(31/30).

With a_U=a1_(n<=U), the exact identity is

    c=Q_U+Q_V-S+R,
    Q_U=a_U*(v*s), Q_V=a_V*(v*s),
    S=a_U*a_V*b0, R=(a-a_U)*(a-a_V)*b0.

G191 pays the WHOLE S: its row coefficients are bounded by d2(m), supported
m<=UV=L. No output or gcd mask is inserted into G191.

The complete general-phase square-short proof in [restricted research revision], reconstructed in the
review, gives for every frozen root prefix R0, including infinity,

    ||sum_(r<=R0) beta(r) f_x(A0 r^2)||_(1,2)
                           << 1+X^(b/4)A0^(-1/4)

when beta is fixed bounded mean-zero periodic, A0 lies in a fixed sublinear
power range, and b>=2k/(2k-1). Its low derivative cutoff is
c0(X/A0)^(k/(2k-1)); the full high squared norm costs
X^(b/2)A0^(-1/2)+(X/A0)^(k/(2k-1)). Both orientations, diagonal, every root
and cross terms are paid. The original physical rows A0=d and pd, with their
literal weights, give

    ||Q_D||_(1,2)<<D+X^(3/8)D^(3/4).

At D=X^(5/12) the exponents are5/12 and11/16, both below5/6. No false scaling
f_x(pn)=f_(x/p)(n) or signed-subset norm comparison is used.

Every R tuple has de>L, so n<=L is empty. Its coefficients obey a complete
divisor bound. [restricted research revision]'s full infinite high-tail theorem gives

    ||sum_(n>M)R(n)f_x(n)||_2^2
                   << X^(3/2+epsilon)+X^12 M^(-10+epsilon)
                   << X^(5/3+epsilon).

The original proof retains all integer gaps and damping; it needs no M<X^b
assumption. G182 allows the literal mask d>U,e>V,L<del<=M and pays gcd(d,e)>G
by X^epsilon[X/G+X^(3/4)/sqrt(G)]=X^epsilon[X^(5/6)+X^(2/3)]. There is no
additional coprimality restriction involving l.

For C_p(x)=sum_n c(n)f_x(n), define the complete finite core

    T_p(x)=sum_(L<del<=M,d>U,e>V,gcd(d,e)<=G)a(d)a(e)b0(l)f_x(del).

Norm triangle for these WHOLE sources proves, for every epsilon>0,

    ||C_p-T_p||_1+||C_p-T_p||_2 << X^(5/6+epsilon).          (192.1)

All cross terms and complements are paid. The remaining cofactor satisfies
l<M/L=X^(1/5), compared with1/4 for degree6 at the same target. These are
different justified detectors; their signed norms are not ordered by inclusion.

The fixed detector retains its complete Mellin return:

    D_c(z)=P_p(z)J_p(z)L(2z,chi^2)^2/L(z,chi),
    P_p=1-chi(p)p^(1-z), J_p=1-chi(p)^2p^(1-2z),
    H_p(z)=Gamma(z/12)e^(-i*pi*z/24)D_c(z)/12+E_p(z).

Rotate the individual integral to a fixed clockwise ray with angle less than
pi/24. The unchanged damping b=3/2 leaves an n^(-1/2) remainder after one
Taylor term, normally holomorphic for Re z>1/2 after the full coefficient sum.
All local derivatives are controlled. No finite shift is omitted here.
The multiplier and J_p L(2z,chi^2)^2 are nonzero above1/2. A fixed pair of
unramified primes covers every P_p zero except the stated principal pole
exception; for nonprincipal chi choose one p with chi(p)!=1 to cover height0.

Thus a COMPLETE core L1 bound X^(5/6+epsilon), for every epsilon and every
large dyadic shell, every fixed ordinary chi and its covering prime pair,
would exclude ordinary zeros above5/6. The fixed full C_p is recovered from
shell-dependent cuts by(192.1). This all-height conditional statement imports
no growing conductor, native Hecke family or uniform-in-height estimate.
The core bound, called OPEN12, remains unproved.

## G193. Paid diagonal and the exact remaining signed estimate

First remove the WHOLE gcd restriction by G182. Partition the original
ordered source into n~N, d~D,e~E cells and retained l, orienting D>=E with
bounded multiplicity. Both inverse scales exceed a fixed multiple of X^(5/12).
Their product-cut d ranges intersect in one interval or are empty. Cauchy in
d, using |a(d)|<=1, produces the exact offdiagonal

    B_(l,x)=2Re sum_(e<e')lambda(ee')chi(e)conj(chi(e'))
      sum_(d in I_e intersect I_e')e^(-d(e+e')l/x^(3/2))
                         exp(-i[(del/x)^12-(de'l/x)^12]).

The complete squared cell bound is O(D)[O(DE)+B_(l,x)]. Both damping factors,
natural e zeros, endpoints and orientations remain. For N>=X and T=(N/X)^12,
the phase derivative for e'=e+h has size Th/(DE). Its largest value is
O(T/D)<<X^(-1/60), so it avoids nonzero integer aliases for large X.
Discrete first derivative and Abel summation give min(D,DE/(Th)). Summing
every h and the diagonal yields the full cell bound

    DE[E^(-1/2)+T^(-1/2)sqrt(log(2E))].

The COMPLETE output block, including the harmonic cofactor sum, is therefore

    << X^epsilon[N X^(-5/24)+X^6/N^5].                    (193.1)

The diagonal reaches exponent33/40 at N=M, saving1/120 against5/6.
The second term reaches5/6 only at N=M; at N~X it still costs X. The low
interval L<N<X also has only the available trivial X bound. The complete
coarse calculation proves no first gain.

A sufficient one-sided arithmetic input is

    B_(l,x)<=C_epsilon D E^2 X^epsilon (X^(5/6)/N)^2       (OG12)

for EVERY original finite cell, each l and EVERY real x, including N<X and
N~X. The diagonal is already paid since E>>X^(5/12) and (N/L)^2<=X^(2/5).
OG12 would pay the whole cofactor sum and imply OPEN12. Negative B helps;
an absolute-value correlation estimate is stronger than required. Neither is
proved. The available high-block price misses by(M/N)^10; below X the gap
is(N/L)^2. The transition still requires a squared saving X^(1/3).

For general fixed k with balanced cuts and tail r=(k-2gamma)/(k-2), this
particular Cauchy diagonal is paid exactly when

    gamma>=4k/(5k-2).

Strict inequality is required for the coarse derivative non-aliasing test.
At gamma=5/6, degree11 is the smallest integer degree passing that strict
test; degree12 gives more reserve:

| k | Tail exponent r | Cofactor exponent r-gamma | Norm diagonal reserve |
|---|---|---|---|
| 11 | 28/27 | 11/54 | 1/216 |
| 12 | 31/30 | 1/5 | 1/120 |

The threshold tends to4/5, and cannot reach3/4 by this particular diagonal
majorant. This is not an obstruction to the actual signed source, another
norm argument or the1/4 target. Increasing k does not improve the transition
gap X^(2(1-gamma)). Constants are not uniform as k grows.

More generally the COMPLETE analytic core/source transfer holds for fixed
1/2<gamma<1,k>=4 and 2k/(2k-1)<=b<=2gamma. Its cofactor exponent is
k(1-gamma)/(k-2). For a Mellin return with b other than3/2 retain every
A_j(z)D_c(z+(b-1)j), j<K, with

    A_j=(-1)^j Gamma((z+bj)/k)e^(-i*pi*(z+bj)/(2k))/(k j!),
    1-(b-1)K<gamma,

and the accepted finite descending-strip argument. The analytic transfer
does not license omission of these terms or prove its arithmetic hypothesis.
At the current gamma11, degree12's cofactor exponent is .15017515632,
compared with .1877189454 at degree6, without a proved ordering of their norms.

## G194. The literal matrix and its complete positive price

Fix an ordinary character chi modulo q with its natural zero extension.
For every real x>=1 use the finite divisor downset

    D_x={n<=x: mu²(n)=1,(n,q)=1}, N=|D_x|.

Order its indices increasingly. Let e be the coordinate of1, v=1-e, and

    Z(d,n)=chi(n/d)1_(d|n),
    B(d,n)=chi(n/d)1_(n/d prime), P=Z-I, R=Z+v e^T.

Every prime-cover path stays in the original downset. Its product is
chi(n/d), and each ordering of the k distinct factors gives one path:

    B^k(d,n)=k!chi(n/d)1_(d|n,omega(n/d)=k),
    exp(B)=Z, exp(-B)(d,n)=mu(n/d)chi(n/d)1_(d|n).

These are finite polynomial exponentials. The determinant lemma, detZ=1,
gives exactly detR=sum_(n<=x)mu(n)chi(n). No zero character value is inverted.
If K=max_(n in D_x)omega(n)>=1, define

    A_k=e^T P^k v=sum_(n in D_x,n>1)chi(n)k!S(omega(n),k).

Strict chains correspond to ordered partitions into k nonempty blocks.
For y=lambda-1, the finite resolvent identity and polynomial continuation
through y=0 yield

    det(lambda I-R)
      =y^(N-K-1)[y^(K+1)-sum_(k=1)^K A_k y^(K-k)].

The multiplicity at1 can exceed N-K-1 when a twisted top coefficient
cancels. K=0 means R=(1). The product of j distinct primes is at least
(j+1)!, so K=O(log(2x)/loglog(3x)); this alone bounds no determinant.
The classical ancestry is [Wilf's finite-poset construction](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0408263v1)
and [Vaughan's characteristic calculation](https://personal.science.psu.edu/rcv4/personal/Publications/REDCONF.pdf).
No full-integer spectral conclusion is imported to this altered support.

Put F_0=1 and F_j=sum_(k=1)^j k!S(j,k). Ordering each block internally,
then concatenating with marked cuts, proves F_j<=2^(j-1)j! for j>=1.
For any sigma>1, split primes at a fixed Y with
R_sigma=sum_(p>Y)p^-sigma<1/4. The tail elementary symmetric function
of degree b is at most R_sigma^b/b!. If a is the number of chosen small
primes, its entire remaining contribution is bounded by a fixed multiple
of sum_b(2R_sigma)^b(a+b)!/b!, which converges. The finitely many small
prime choices therefore prove

    sum_(n squarefree)F_(omega(n)) n^-sigma<infinity,
    P_q(x):=sum_(n in D_x)F_(omega(n)) <<_(q,epsilon)x^(1+epsilon).

This pays ALL depths, including growing depths. For principal chi it is
the permanent of R: each nonidentity permutation cycle is a strict chain
through1. It is also1+sum_k|A_k| in that case. Moreover

    P_q(x)>=|D_x|=delta_q x+O_q(sqrt x),
    delta_q=(phi(q)/q)prod_(p not dividing q)(1-p^-2)>0.

The density follows directly from mu²(n)=sum_(d²|n)mu(d), paying floors
and the tail of sum d^-2. Hence the full positive price has exact exponent1.
This is not a lower bound for the signed determinant.

Two tempting operator shortcuts also fail in their stated norms.
The unitary diagonal diag(chi(n)) gauges B to the principal matrix, but
changes the closing vector v. Parity diag((-1)^omega(n)) conjugates B to
-B, so ||exp(-B_chi)||_2=||exp(B_1)||_2. The Hermitian part of -B_1 has
a two-dimensional compression with positive eigenvalue sqrt(pi_q(x))/2.
There is no contraction in this Euclidean norm. This says nothing about
a different signed observable or a lower bound for M_chi.

## G195. Every fixed low-chain sector under one common filter

Fix p not dividing q and integer J>=2, independent of x. Define

    Q=delta1-p chi(p)delta_p, v_J=Q^(*J),
    P_p(s)=1-chi(p)p^(1-s),
    b=Q*chi=chi(n)(1-p1_(p|n)),
    f_t(n)=mu²(n)t^omega(n)chi(n), f_0=delta1.

b has period pq and mean zero, including principal/imprimitive characters.
Choose D>=max(1,||b||_infinity,sup_y|sum_(n<=y)b(n)|); D=p²q suffices.

For any fixed bounded mean-zero periodic b, the full ordered hyperbola
identity proves

    |sum_(n<=x)b^(*t)(n)|<=C_t x^(1-1/t),
    C_t<=(2D)^t(t!)².

Indeed each t-tuple of product<=x has a coordinate<=Y=x^(1/t).
In inclusion-exclusion with j<t short coordinates and m=t-j, induction
costs C_m x^(1-1/m)[sum_(n<=Y)|b(n)|n^(-1+1/m)]^j,
at most C_m(Dm)^j x^(1-1/t). For j=t the product cutoff is automatic:
the term is the bounded quantity(sum_(n<=Y)b(n))^t. All overlaps and real
floors are retained. The recurrence and m!m^(t-m)<=t! prove the stated
constant bound.

The exact Euler correction is

    sum_n f_t(n)n^-s=L(s,chi)^t G_t(s),
    G_t(s)=prod_l(1+t z_l)(1-z_l)^t, z_l=chi(l)l^-s.

The local linear term vanishes. The absolute coefficient series
Gabs_t(sigma)=sum|g_t(n)|n^-sigma converges for every fixed t and sigma>1/2.
Consequently, for1<=t<=J,

    v_J*f_t=b^(*t)*v_(J-t)*g_t,
    |sum_(n<=x)(v_J*f_t)(n)|
      <=C_t Gabs_t(sigma)(1+p^(1-sigma))^(J-t)x^sigma,
          sigma>1/2, sigma>=1-1/t.

Each finite p^a coefficient is evaluated at x/p^a; arguments below1
contribute zero. All colors on the left use the SAME filter v_J.

The independent review sharpens the two low endpoints without assuming
Euler convergence at1/2. For t=1, g_1 is supported on r² with coefficient
mu(r)chi(r)². For t=2, the local polynomial1-3z²+2z³ has absolute
coefficients dominated by(1-z²)^-3(1-z³)^-2. Thus

    |sum_(n<=x)(v_J*f_1)(n)|<=D(1+sqrt p)^(J-1)sqrt x,
    sum_(n<=x)|g_2(n)|/sqrt n
      <=zeta(3/2)²(1+0.5log x)³,
    |sum_(n<=x)(v_J*f_2)(n)|
      <=3D²zeta(3/2)²(1+sqrt p)^(J-2)sqrt x(1+0.5log x)³.

The second inequality follows by writing the majorant as
sum_(a²c³=n)d_3(a)d_2(c): the c-series converges, and the a-series is
bounded by the cube of a harmonic sum. The periodic two-variable
hyperbola bound is3D²sqrt x. All p shifts remain in these bounds.

Set a_0=delta1 and a_k(n)=mu²(n)chi(n)k!S(omega(n),k). Finite differences
give the complete first-J chain combination

    L_J=sum_(k=0)^J(-1)^k a_k
       =sum_(t=0)^J(-1)^t binom(J+1,t+1)f_t.

Combining ALL colors and their common filter proves, for every real x>=1,

    |sum_(n<=x)(v_J*L_J)(n)| <<_(p,q,J) x^(1-1/J), J>=3;
    |sum_(n<=x)(v_2*L_2)(n)| <<_(p,q) sqrt x log³(2x).

The exponent for J>=3 has no epsilon loss. This is a complete arithmetic
estimate of the low source, including principal characters.

Growing depth is not free. Splitting primes at t^(1/sigma) proves
logGabs_t(sigma)<<_sigma t^(1/sigma)log(2t) for fixed1/2<sigma<1.
The factorial hyperbola constant, finite p-shift factors and binomial
combination must all be paid, and sigma>=1-1/t still applies. These upper
prices establish no impossibility theorem for a better growing-depth proof.

## G196. The complete linked remainder and its weaker sufficient norm

With0^0=1 define

    W_J(j)=(-1)^j-sum_(t=0)^J(-1)^t binom(J+1,t+1)t^j,
    r_J(n)=mu²(n)chi(n)W_J(omega(n)),
    mu chi=L_J+r_J.

The exact generating function is

    sum_(j>=0)W_J(j)z^j
      =(-1)^(J+1)(J+1)!z^(J+1)/[(1+z)prod_(t=1)^J(1-tz)].

In particular W_J(j)=0 for j<=J; for J>=2 its remaining coefficients
have fixed sign(-1)^(J+1), since the denominator reduces to
(1-z²)prod_(t=2)^J(1-tz). Nevertheless |W_J(j)|<=C_J J^j, hence
|r_J(n)|<<_(J,epsilon)n^epsilon. The full factorial representation cost
has disappeared, without removing any chain depth.

Let T_(p,J)(x)=sum_(n<=x)(v_J*r_J)(n) and
S_(p,J)(x)=sum_(n<=x)(v_J*mu chi)(n). Then

    |S_(p,J)(x)-T_(p,J)(x)| << x^(1-1/J), J>=3,
    |S_(p,2)(x)-T_(p,2)(x)| << sqrt x log³(2x).

For n=p^a m, p not dividing m, m squarefree, j=omega(m), the literal
coefficient is

    chi(p)^a chi(m)[(-p)^a binom(J,a)W_J(j)
                  +(-p)^(a-1)binom(J,a-1)W_J(j+1)].

At a=0 the second term is absent. a=J+1 is retained; only a>J+1
vanishes. Out-of-range binomial coefficients are zero; nonsquarefree m
or ramified factors give zero. These linked valuations cannot be bounded
as arbitrary independent signed subsets.

Fix ONE gamma with1/2<gamma<gamma11 and choose fixed J with
max(1/2,1-1/J)<=gamma. For every fixed chi and a fixed covering pair of
distinct unramified primes, the following complete hypothesis suffices:

    OPEN-L1-CHAIN:
    integral_X^(2X)|T_(p,J)(x)|dx/x
      <<_(chi,p,J,epsilon)X^(gamma+epsilon)
    for every epsilon>0 and all sufficiently large dyadic X.

G195 pays the entire difference from S in the same norm. Initially for
Re s>1, ordinary partial summation gives

    P_p(s)^J/L(s,chi)=s integral_1^infinity S_(p,J)(x)x^(-s-1)dx.

On a compact set Re s>=gamma+delta, choose epsilon<delta/2. Each dyadic
shell, including any fixed s derivative, costs
O((log(2X))^m X^(-delta+epsilon)); the sum converges normally. The finite
initial interval is entire. Therefore the quotient is holomorphic in
Re s>gamma, with every sharp endpoint and filter term retained.

P_p zeros lie on Re s=1. A common nonzero-height zero for two distinct
primes would make logp1/logp2 rational, since character values are roots
of unity. For a nonprincipal character choose one prime with chi(p)!=1
to cover height0. Such a prime exists by factoring a unit integer on
which chi is nontrivial. For principal chi, the pole of L at1 is the
allowed exception. This fixed pair exposes every hypothetical ordinary
zero in Re s>gamma. No growing conductor or uniform height bound is used.

A pointwise T bound implies shell L2, and shell L2 implies shell L1.
This corrects the reversed norm wording at author line376; its original
bytes are retained. No reverse implication or attained norm estimate is
claimed. Both pointwise and complete shell hypotheses remain OPEN.

| Prospective gamma | Fixed J | Paid low exponent | Conditional c |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| .8748 |7|6/7|.1252|
|5/6|6|5/6|1/6|
|3/4|4|3/4|1/4|

The nearer prospective gain is135091/2500000000=.0000540364. Equality
with the paid low exponent is allowed. The full coarse bound is still
|T_(p,J)(x)|<<x log^(J-1)(2x), since J^omega=d_J on squarefree integers
and every p^a coefficient meets x/p^a. It supplies no first power gain.
Color8's available exponent7/8 misses gamma11 by.0001459636; improving
only that color would leave all higher depths.

For principal chi, the p-free subfamily n=A*l, with A a fixed product of
J primes avoiding pq and l another prime, has nonzero constant residual
coefficient. Its absolute price is at least a constant times x/log x,
using the [ordinary prime bound](https://dlmf.nist.gov/27.12).
This obstructs separately paying that projection below exponent1. It
does not lower-bound the full filtered sum, whose linked p valuations
can cancel. Setting J>=K(x) kills the residual below x but changes the
filter with x and makes the paid exponent tend to1; it has no fixed-source
Mellin return under the present estimates.

## G197. Two paid classes with complete shared-prime cost

For an ideal q define A_G(q)=sum_(d|q,Nd>=G) mu(q/d). Then
sum_(q|g)A_G(q)=1_(Ng>=G), A_G(q)=0 below G and |A_G(q)|<=tau(q).
Since a is squarefree, the high-gcd piece is exactly

    B_g=sum_(q sf) A_G(q)mu(q)phi(q)^2/(Nq)
                      M^(q)(R/Nq) S(D/Nq).                (3)

The extra inverse mask is restored by the COMPLETE q-smooth series

    M^(q)(E)=sum_(h q-smooth) phi(h)/sqrt(Nh) M(E/Nh).

All powers and natural zeros remain. Its absolute mass is at most
product_(p|q)(1-(Np)^(-1/2))^(-1) <<_epsilon (Nq)^epsilon.
Polynomial fixed inverse punctures are handled in the same way. Extracted
row phases are contractions after taking a positive norm, never new MI
column coefficients. Minkowski, (1)-(2) and ideal counting give

    ||B_g Q||^2_Omega << H_J U^(1+beta*m+epsilon) G^(-beta). (4)

Let s2(b)=product_p p^floor(v_p(b)/2). The high-square plain part is
sum_(Nk>=H) A_H(k)phi(k^2)/(Nk) S(D/(Nk)^2), with k unrestricted.
Its pointwise absolute bound is H_J U^epsilon D^(beta/2)H^(-beta).
The intersection with the high-gcd part uses L=lcm(q,k^2)=q k^2/(q,k):

    B_gs=sum_(q sf,k) A_G(q)A_H(k)mu(q)phi(qL)/sqrt(Nq NL)
                         M^(q)(R/Nq) S(D/NL).             (5)

Norm notation suppresses N only in the following positive mass:

    w_beta(q,k)=q^(-1-beta/2) k^(-1-beta) (q,k)^((1+beta)/2).

At q=k=p the local weight is p^(-3/2-beta); falsely independent divisibility
would miss p^((1+beta)/2). Put d=(q,k),k=de. The complete k-tail satisfies

    sum_(Nk>=H) k^(-1-beta)(q,k)^((1+beta)/2)
      << H^(-beta) sum_(d|q) d^((beta-1)/2)
      <= H^(-beta) tau(q).                               (6)

For d<=H use the e-tail; for d>H use the complete e-sum and
d^(-(1+beta)/2)<=H^(-beta)d^((beta-1)/2). Thus every large common divisor
is paid. The q-tail supplies G^(-beta/2), including all divisor/restoration
losses on the polynomial support. Squaring yields

    ||B_gs Q||^2 << H_J U^(1+beta*m+epsilon) G^(-beta)H^(-2beta).

Define B_s=M S_bad-B_gs and B_c=B-B_g-B_s. Hilbert triangle proves
||B_sQ||^2<<H_J U^(1+beta*m+epsilon)H^(-2beta). No signed-subset
monotonicity is asserted. Partition actual rows by |B_g|>=|B|/4, then
|B_s|>=|B|/4 outside the first class, then the remainder. Dividing (4)
and its B_s counterpart by the SAME lower bound (1) gives original inverse
moment savings delta*log_U(G) and 2delta*log_U(H), after losses.

At G=U^(4eta),H=U^(2eta), each pre-loss saving is at least(68/25)eta.
The remaining B_c has magnitude>|B|/2 and unmarked repeat factor<GH^2.
Every original slot remains, so the full repeat factor is<GH^2 NP.

## G198. A coupled cutoff halves the residual repeat width

Fix T before witnesses. Split original tuples by
F(a,b)=N(a,b)*(Ns2(b))^2>=T, obtaining B=B_T+C_T. The two-variable inverse

    A_T(q,k)=sum_(d|q,e|k) mu(q/d)mu(k/e)1_(Nd*(Ne)^2>=T)

satisfies sum_(q|g,k|s)A_T(q,k)=1_(Ng*(Ns)^2>=T), is divisor bounded,
and vanishes unless Nq*(Nk)^2>=T. Thus (5) is the exact expansion of B_T
with A_G A_H replaced by A_T. It retains every collision and natural zero.

In each dyadic q,k box with Q0 K0^2>=T/8, the COMPLETE tail estimate (6)
and its q-tail give mass <<U^epsilon Q0^(-beta/2)K0^(-beta)
<<U^epsilon T^(-beta/2). There are only O(log^2 U) supported boxes.
Minkowski and (1)-(2) prove

    ||B_T Q||^2_Omega << H_J U^(1+beta*m+epsilon)T^(-beta). (7)

An independent root check splits q=dq',k=dk',d=(q,k): after extracting
(D0^3 Q0 K0^2)^(-beta/2), the common-divisor box mass leaves
D0^((beta-1)/2), summable since beta<1. This confirms why the shared-prime
correction is harmless here rather than silently absent.

Keep the two original paid row classes FIRST. Outside them, add the class
|B_T|>=|B|/2. Equation(7) and (1) save delta*log_U(T) in the ORIGINAL
inverse moment on this third, disjoint class. All remaining rows satisfy
|C_T|>|B|/2. For every surviving tuple, since a is squarefree,

    ab/rad(ab)=(a,b)*b/rad(b),  b/rad(b) divides s2(b)^2,
    N(abP/rad(abP)) < T NP.                               (8)

At T=U^(4eta), the pre-loss saving is again at least(68/25)eta, exceeding
eta by(43/25)eta. The unmarked repeat width decreases from8eta to4eta;
with slots it decreases from8eta+v to4eta+v. Positive union of three
disjoint paid classes costs only a constant. This is a proved support
improvement at the same calibration, not a new norm ordering between cores.

Equality belongs to the high side. F is a TUPLE cutoff: different factorizations
of the same merged n may have different F. The intrinsic repeat bound is
necessary support information only. Signed merging can cancel, so preserving
old classes before the new test is necessary; no new class containment is
inferred from tuple containment. No claim ||C_TQ||<=||B_cQ|| is made.

## G199. Complete prime-band product estimate

For first powers split the exact band into dyads P<=Np<2P. Set E=D/P.
Before choosing a row,prime or color, separate the common profile V_D(yz)
on a fixed ambient compact box by PR9 B3.3. The normalization is exact:
P^(-1/2)E^(-1/2)=D^(-1/2). A separated term is M(R)Q times one new
prime slot at P and a plain factor at E. Apply its same-bin plain bound
FIRST, then enlarge only the remaining positive MI norm. This gives

    ||M Q * first-power dyad||^2
      <<H_J U^(1+epsilon)D^beta P^(-beta).             (2)

The prime coefficient can be fixed as log Np/log U, extracting the bounded
scalar log U/log D. Scale derivatives therefore do not change arithmetic
coefficients. The new slot has the SAME orientation phi, not another
moving character absorbed into a coefficient. All original slots remain.

With lambda=log_U(P)<=4eta+small and G137's first reserve>.01017,

    1-r-2(v+lambda) >=217/100000-small,
    3-2r-8(v+lambda)>=39417/50000-small.               (3)

Both margins hold throughout the whole window, including v=0; shortening
the inverse improves them. The enlarged fixed slot system and finite orders
are chosen before witnesses.

All support collisions are paid. Split the new pool outside the union of
old pools and into its intersections with each old pool i. For p=q in
an intersection, remove the old slot and extract its prime. The old scale
P_i is comparable to P, and ideal counting gives coefficient mass
sum_p(P_i Np)^(-1/2)(D/Np)^(beta/2)<<D^(beta/2)P^(-beta/2).
The remaining slots satisfy MI. The phase phi(p)^2 is a contraction,
including its zero, and the inverse is not declared coprime to p.

For p!=q independently color the prime IDEALS of that finite old pool:

    1_(p!=q)=4 E_color[1_(p in E0)1_(q in E1)].        (4)

Each colored pair has disjoint row-independent supports, so MI applies.
Minkowski under the NORMALIZED probability measure costs4, not the number
of colorings. Distinct ideals of equal norm must receive distinct labels;
coloring only norms would be false. Original pools are disjoint, so this
exhausts all new/old coincidences at a fixed count of cases.

For j>=2, apply the shortened plain bound before taking the extracted-prime
absolute sum. Its dyadic mass is P^(1-j(1+beta)/2)<=P^(-beta). The complete
j sum is geometric and gives squared saving A^(-2beta), better than (2).
All natural zeros, higher powers and collisions remain inside that bound.
Summing dyads costs only the prescribed small loss. Therefore

    ||M S^[theta] Q||^2_Omega
      <<H_J U^(1+epsilon)D^beta A^(-beta).            (5)

This complete product estimate is independent of the previous removals.

## G2 — uncapped free invention

### W40-06 — Signed extremal frequency detector; p=.24
O: Optimize a compact trigonometric/Mellin detector over a finite-dimensional signed basis subject to exact positivity only at the zero implication step.
B: A dual certificate for the optimum may prove a new detector with a better quantitative zero-exclusion balance.
T: Solve the degree-two analytic extremum and compare it with coefficientwise positivity constraints.
X: Pointwise positivity on an unbounded strip is not captured by a finite grid or finite moments.
R: Direct small endpoint improvement, with potential architecture ceiling.

### W40-07 — Exact scale commutator; p=.13
O: Telescope adjacent dyadic decompositions and isolate the commutator between truncation and the original arithmetic projector.
B: If boundary commutators are summable with power saving, a logarithmic blocking loss might be removed before taking a moment.
T: Derive the exact telescoping identity with zero extension and inspect the boundary coefficient at both endpoints.
X: A logarithmic saving is not the missing fixed power; endpoint mass may equal the full form.
R: Useful exact boundary lemma, probably below the present required gain unless a power accumulation is real.

### W40-08 — Inverse-L dispersion sum rule; p=.07
O: View a mollified reciprocal L-function as a response function and derive a contour sum rule coupling its modulus and logarithmic derivative.
B: A zero in the forbidden half-plane would incur a positive integrated response cost contradicting an arithmetic energy bound.
T: Test the identity on a one-zero rational function and identify every pole, subtraction and contour boundary term.
X: The integrated cost may miss a narrow zero spike or depend on the very zero-free input being sought.
R: High-ceiling replacement detector, potentially avoids the existing moment architecture.

### W40-09 — Character-local tensor compression; p=.16
O: Decompose arithmetic coefficients into prime-local tensors but retain the fixed character globally; contract only exact local orthogonality relations.
B: A tensor norm bound could preserve multiplicative cancellation lost in a scalar divisor estimate.
T: Two-prime exact enumeration with repeated prime powers and common factors; compare the full contraction with coprime-only factorization.
X: Shifted arguments do not tensor by prime, and CRT phase/height coupling can recreate the full difficulty.
R: Restricted friable-sector result with explicit complementary return.

### W40-10 — Finite annihilator against the extremizing profile; p=.045
O: Find a short linear combination of multiplicative shifts that annihilates the leading bad profile while retaining the zero's amplified contribution.
B: A separated spectrum of profile modes could suppress the extremal moment contribution with only bounded detector cost.
T: Solve the two-mode annihilation constraints and test whether the target zero mode lies in the same span.
X: Annihilating the obstruction may annihilate the detector or introduce coefficients growing with height.
R: Modest to substantial improvement, conditional on exact separation of target and bad modes.
title: G2 — uncapped free invention

## G200. Complete weighted removal and the fourth paid class

For a fixed extracted ideal L,E=D/NL, the literal multiplier is theta(Lc).
Its exact plain expansion is

    S_(theta,L)(E)=ell_B(L)/log D S(E;V_D)
      +(1/log D)sum_(p,j>=1)log Np phi(p^j)(Np)^(-j/2)
                                      S(E/(Np)^j;V_D). (6)

When p|L the first term counts its existing valuations and the second counts
every additional valuation of c. Nonempty support gives NL<=CD. The complete
first-power absolute mass is Y^((1-beta)/2), and higher powers are smaller:

    |S_(theta,L)(D/NL)|
      <<H_J U^epsilon(D/NL)^(beta/2)Y^((1-beta)/2).     (7)

This uniform bound on actual plain blocks is not an arbitrary coefficient
multiplier theorem. Insert it before [restricted research revision]'s complete q,k,lcm convolution,
including every shared divisor and all inverse smooth-power restorations.
The old gcd/square pieces gain exactly one squared cost Y^(1-beta).
For G=Y=U^(4eta),H=U^(2eta), their weighted savings are(8beta-4)eta;
(5) saves2beta eta. Since beta>2/3 with reserved buffer, the latter is smaller.
The complete old weighted core therefore saves2beta eta, with its exact
signed intersection subtraction paid by triangle.

More sharply, [restricted research revision]'s coupled cut F(a,b)=N(gcd(a,b))Ns2(b)^2 has exact blocks
M^(q)(R/Nq)S(D/Nlcm(q,k^2)) and FULL positive mass T^(-beta/2)U^epsilon.
It satisfies the author's conditional interface exactly. Thus

    ||C_T^[theta]Q||^2
      <<H_J U^(1+epsilon)D^beta
                [A^(-beta)+T^(-beta)Y^(1-beta)]
      <<H_J U^(1+beta*m-2beta*eta+epsilon),            (8)

at T=Y=U^(4eta). This is the complete weighted core, not a signed subset.
Keep [restricted research revision]'s three paid classes FIRST. On their complement |C_T|>|MS|/2.
Define the new actual class there by |C_T^[theta]|>=|C_T|/2. Dividing (8)
by the original SAME-beta plain spike pays original inverse moment

    sum_newclass w_u |M(R)Q|^2
      <<H_J U^(1-2delta*eta+epsilon).                 (9)

The preloss saving is at least(34/25)eta, reserve(9/25)eta above eta.
Q is never divided out. Every remaining row retains the exact signal

    |C_T^[1-theta]|>|MS|/4,
    1-theta(b)=log N(b_outside_band)/log Nb,            (10)
    N(abP/rad(abP))<T NP=U^(4eta)NP.

Band prime squares are absent from this core since p^2|b,Np>=A implies
F>=A^2=T. They were nonetheless fully paid in the preceding expansions.
The large-prime plain sector with squarefree coprime inverse has F=1 and
theta=0, so it survives. This is a coefficient example, not an actual
high-zero row or a lower bound for a signed norm.

The complete coarse norm from C_T^[1-theta]=C_T-C_T^[theta] is still
H_J U^(1+beta*m+epsilon). After the original plain division it is U^(1+epsilon).
The full signed outside-band estimate and whole-row cover remain OPEN.
No norm/class monotonicity follows from0<=theta<=1 or tuple inclusion.

All physical roots, projectors, positive children, original slots, labels,
low/high and fixed-inducing branches, shortage/empty cases, Euler shifts,
residues and common-Delta return retain their old prices. A signed projector
need not preserve a dominance class; paired restricted gains average under
Cauchy. The M/24 reserve is unspent. Current c11 and preceding-c10 K stay
unchanged, with F0, positive-slot uniformity and external admission open.

The [manifest](retention-manifest.json) preserves12 original files,7 author
source bindings, independent receipts and the prior raw scorecard. Both
owners STOPped and normally released. Root read both full reports, the full
helper/receipt and literal primary contracts, and reconstructed the gates,
coloring, valuations, Fourier integral and coupled-core return. The author's

does not certify imported analytic premises. No formalization was done.

## G201. Exact native carrier spectrum, with normalized stencil cost

Use the literal Eisenstein [JN source](../[private research revision]/h-joint/report.md), not
an ordinary integer surrogate. Freeze the original long-prime pair of
distinct degree-one rational norms p,r, with Q=pr and phi=(p-1)(r-1).
The complete finite group has Q^2 elements and unitary Fourier factor 1/Q.
The row multiplier is m(h)=ell_p(h_p)ell_r(h_r), with quadratic characters
zero at zero. The mark factors vanish off exactly phi mark pairs and have
modulus one on them. The complete coefficient includes the original
b0=b(pi)conjugate(b(pi'))zeta_CRT, which may vanish.

For translation S_t f(h)=f(h+t), the row commutator is

    D_t=diag(m(h)-m(h+t)) S_t.

When t is nonzero in both residue fields, local autocorrelation is -1.
Indeed z^2=y(y+1) is equivalent, by an invertible change of variables over
an odd field, to (2y+1-2z)(2y+1+2z)=1. Counting its p-1 solutions proves
the local identity including the zero sites. CRT gives correlation 1.
There are B=(p-2)(r-2) positions where both row values are nonzero, two
where both vanish, and n1=2(p+r-3) where exactly one vanishes. Thus

    singular value 2: multiplicity n2=(B-1)/2;
    singular value 1: multiplicity n1;
    rank D_t=(Q+2p+2r-9)/2;
    ||D_t||_HS^2=2(phi-1),  ||D_t||_op=2.

For a shift nonzero only at p, replace these multiplicities by
n2=(p-1)(r-1)/2 and n1=2(r-1); the other case is symmetric. The full
carrier repeats each nonzero row singular value phi times and scales
it by |b0|. Unitary Fourier conjugation introduces no further saving.
For rank k<=n2 approximation the squared row Hilbert-Schmidt error is
at least 4(n2-k)+n1, and for k<n2 the operator error is at least 2.

Let P=sum c_j S_j for k distinct integer shifts 0<j<min(p,r). Distinct
matrix diagonals cannot cancel in Hilbert-Schmidt norm, so

    ||[M_m,P]||_HS^2=2(phi-1)||c||_2^2,
    sqrt(2(phi-1)/Q)||c||_2 <= ||[M_m,P]||_op
                             <=2 sqrt(k)||c||_2,
    rank[M_m,P] >= (phi-1)/(2k),  c!=0.

The lower operator bound uses rank<=Q. Moving coefficients require the
displayed normalization: c_1=Q^(-10) defeats the author's unnormalized
prose claim. The correct cost is relative to |b0| ||c||_2, or for stencils
whose normalized size does not vanish. The immutable author report is
retained with this explicit superseding correction.

These are ambient carrier facts. They do not identify the carrier with
the physical mark matrix, make the actual folded W an extremizer, or
bound its signed pairing below. All original projectors, ordered short
pairs including equality, complex gcd core, masks, roots, independent
heights and natural zeros remain. The raw H target is still

    Z^epsilon G K [N+L+(NL)^(2/3)] sqrt(Omega1 Omega2) P_orig,

followed by N^(-1)G^(-2) exactly once. None of the .004 full-H deficit is
paid. A source-specific recurrence and its complete observation/residual
estimate remain legitimate targets.
title: G201. Exact native carrier spectrum, with normalized stencil cost

## G202. Centered quotient norm and one fixed cumulative source

Now use a separate ordinary Dirichlet character chi modulo fixed q, with
a(n)=mu(n)chi(n), a(1)=1 and literal natural zeros. Write M(x)=sum_(n<=x)a(n),
psi_chi(y)=sum_(d<=y)Lambda(d)chi(d), and delta=1 for principal chi and
zero otherwise. The exact [[restricted research revision] renewal identity](../[private research revision]/wild55/report.md)
is prior credit:

    R(x)=sum_(d<=x)Lambda(d)chi(d)M(x/d)=-sum_(n<=x)a(n)log n,
    M(x)log x=int_1^x M(t)dt/t-R(x).

For integer N>=2 and floor-invariant f define the centered functional

    J_N(f)=sum_(d<=N)Lambda(d)chi(d)f_floor(N/d)
                     -delta int_1^N f_floor(N/u) du.

The pole-subtraction measure is du. The restored principal term is exactly
N sum_(n<=N)a(n)/n-M(N); it cannot be dropped. Merge equal quotient states
before taking absolute values:

    J_N(f)=sum_(1<=m<N)c_m f_m,
    c_m=psi_chi(N/m)-psi_chi(N/(m+1))-delta N/[m(m+1)].

The lower interval endpoint is strict. State m=N contributes neither a
nonzero discrete atom nor positive continuous length. The exact norm for
|f_m|<=m^beta and f_m=0 at m<=Y, with 0<beta<1, is

    C_(beta,Y)(N)=N^(-beta) sum_(Y<m<N)|c_m|m^beta.

Set D=floor(min(sqrt(N)/4,N/[4(Y+1)])). Each unramified prime power
2<=d<=D has a distinct cell m=floor(N/d)>Y of length
N/[m(m+1)]<=d^2/(N-d)<=1/8, containing d alone. Therefore

    C_(beta,Y)(N)>=2^(-beta-1)
                    sum_(d<=D,(d,q)=1)Lambda(d)d^(-beta)
                  >>_(q,beta) D^(1-beta).

The lower estimate needs only an elementary Chebyshev bound: prime
valuations of binomial(2n,n) give psi(2n)>=2n log 2-log(2n+1), and deleting
the finitely many q-prime-power rays costs O_q(log D). For Y=floor(N^theta),
0<=theta<1, even C/log N grows at least as
N^((1-beta)min(1/2,1-theta))/log N. This is a merged centered norm bound,
not a lower bound for J_N(M), R, or M.

The obstruction survives cumulative inputs with honest natural-zero
increments. For 1/2<beta<1 and 0<alpha<(1-beta)/(2-beta), let

    Q_q(t)=sum_(n<=t)mu(n)^2 1_((n,q)=1)
          =kappa_q t+O_q(sqrt t),
    kappa_q=zeta(2)^(-1) product_(p|q)p/(p+1)>0.

For each unramified prime power d<=N^alpha, put m_d=floor(N/d),
H_d=floor(m_d^beta/8) and
B_d(n)=max(0,H_d-|Q_q(n)-Q_q(m_d)|). The squarefree density formula follows
by inserting sum_(e^2|n)mu(e), counting q-units, and paying every square-divisor
error and tail. It places each bump within m_d+O_q(H_d). The support-width
to nearest-center spacing ratio is O_q(N^(beta-1)d^(2-beta))=o(1).
Supports and increment boundaries are disjoint. Their inverse images
under u->floor(N/u) have width o(1), so each has exactly the integer
contact d; the floor error O(d^2/N) also tends uniformly to zero.

The compact synthetic sum G_N(n)=sum_d conjugate(chi(d))B_d(n) satisfies
|G_N(n)|<=n^beta and |G_N(n)-G_N(n-1)|<=mu(n)^2 1_((n,q)=1).
Every discrete atom contributes Lambda(d)H_d. For principal chi the full
continuous subtraction costs at most half this for sufficiently large N;
for nonprincipal chi it is absent. Thus

    J_N(G_N) >= c N^(beta+alpha(1-beta)) >0.

Independent strengthening: choose N_j increasingly so that each whole
bump block G_j, including its increment boundary, lies above N_(j-1)
and above the preceding support. If F_old is the earlier sum, choose
z_j=J_(N_j)(F_old)/|J_(N_j)(F_old)| when nonzero and z_j=1 otherwise.
Then |J_(N_j)(F_old+z_jG_j)|=|J_(N_j)(F_old)|+J_(N_j)(G_j).
Later blocks change no state sampled at N_j. Hence ONE locally finite
F=sum_j z_jG_j and b(n)=F(n)-F(n-1) satisfy

    |b(n)|<=mu(n)^2 1_((n,q)=1),  |F(n)|<=n^beta,
    |J_(N_j)(F)|>=c N_j^(beta+alpha(1-beta)).

Any fixed finite zero prefix can be prescribed. For principal chi, the
phases may be +/-1 and b(n) belongs to {-1,0,1}. A growing zero prefix
at infinitely many N_j would force F identically zero and is NOT claimed.
Only the cutoff-dependent construction retains that separate property.
Neither construction has the prescribed Möbius signs, multiplicativity,
or the actual inverse-convolution law. Those are the remaining structures
that a successful arithmetic argument must use.
