## G203. A signed inner source does not rescue the outer positive budget

For fixed ordinary chi and y=x^eta, 0<eta<1, split each squarefree n uniquely
into its y-smooth part a and y-rough part b. With S_y the entire signed
smooth prefix, including its unit, exactly

    M_chi(x)=sum_(b<=x,Pminus(b)>y)mu(b)chi(b) S_y(x/b).

The proposed outer absolute budget retains all cancellation inside S_y.
Nevertheless each unramified prime p in (x/2,x] contributes exactly one
to that budget, because S_y(x/p)=1. It is therefore >>_q x/log x by the
ordinary [prime number theorem, DLMF27.12.4-5](https://dlmf.nist.gov/27.12).
No arithmetic-progression or conductor-uniform theorem is imported.
On shells [X,2X], primes p in (X,3X/2] have the same unit inner prefix
through the common interval [3X/2,2X]. The sum of complete polymer L1 or
L2 norms also costs >>_q X/log X. This does not bound the signed sum or
its full Gram form below. Cross-polymer cancellation remains open.

## G204: small square cores with unrestricted cubic rows

Write `(Delta ell)=kappa b^2`, with kappa squarefree; kappa and b may overlap.
Fix kappa and put `B=(H_A/N(kappa))^(1/2)`. The arbitrary squarefree inner
sequence has length X. [Dunn, arXiv2403.13151v3, Section4 Theorem4.1 and
Corollary4.2](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.13151v3) permits the unrestricted
outer cubic variable and supplies price `B^(1/3)(B+X)`, up to the stated
small powers. Use reciprocity/duality and fixed unit/ray classes as in the
full proof. No cuspidal coefficient theorem or arbitrary extension of
PR9 B3.6 is invoked.

Summing squarefree cores through C gives the energy bound

    H_A^(2/3) C^(1/3) + X H_A^(1/6) C^(5/6).

Each independent column has this bound. Cauchy combines the two positive
outer energies once; it does not square their price again. Summing the
O(A) original labels and restoring the exact prefactor gives

    U^(1/3+2tau/3) A^-1 N0^(1/3) N(f)^-1 C^(1/3),
    U^(5/6+tau/6) A^-4 N0^(1/3) N(f)^-2 C^(5/6),

times `H_J U^epsilon` and the paid divisor multiplicities. This is a bound

## G205: small cube cores with paid sixth-power punctures

Write `(Delta ell)=kappa t^3 z^6`, with kappa cubefree and t squarefree;
overlaps among these factors are allowed. The character identity contains

    chi_m(kappa)^eta chi_m(t)^3 1_((m,z)=1), eta in {+1,-1},

in addition to the retained fixed unit factor. The hole at z is necessary:
a prime of valuation six still forces zero when it divides m.
Fix kappa and z before averaging the squarefree t variable. The puncture
is part of the arbitrary inner sequence; it is not dropped after taking
a sixth power.

Set `B=(H_A/N(kappa))^(1/3)` and `T0=B/N(z)^2`.
[Goldmakher-Louvel, arXiv1112.1642v2, Definition1 and Theorem1.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1112.1642v2)
gives price `T0+X`. The literal PR9 B2.24 family supplies primitivity,
trivial infinite type, the fixed finite reciprocity classes and the
equal-class coprime product-conductor condition. Its local convention is
retained in the complete reports; this is not permission for an arbitrary
quadratic family.

The alternative original-color pointwise price is `T0 S0`.
Split z at a threshold Z clipped to `[1,sqrt(B)]`. The complete cost is
bounded by

    B + X Z + B S0/Z,

with the endpoint interpretations paid separately. If the formal optimum
is inside the interval, balance the latter two terms. If it lies below one,
use the pointwise bound throughout; if above sqrt(B), use the sieve
throughout and `X<S0`. In all regimes the resulting bound is

    B + sqrt(B S0 X).

Summing cubefree cores through C gives

    H_A^(1/3) C^(2/3) + sqrt(S0 X) H_A^(1/6) C^(5/6).

The two complete normalized prices are therefore

    U^(2/3+tau/3) A^-3 N0^(-1/3) N(f)^-1 C^(2/3),
    sqrt(S0) U^(5/6+tau/6) A^-4 N0^(-1/6) N(f)^(-3/2) C^(5/6).

Both independent f allocations are divisor bounded. The f^-1 sum has a
paid small-power allowance; the f^-2 and f^(-3/2) sums converge after a
sufficiently small divisor loss. All fixed S-parts, slots, heights, ray
classes and both full orientations are retained.

## G206: enlarged caps tied to the original a-dyad

The initial author caps are `C_sq=U^(13/40)` and `C_cu=U^(3/4)`.
The independent review proves the larger original-A caps

    C_sq(A)=U^(13/40) A^(24/5),
    C_cu(A)=U^(3/4) A^(24/5).

These are fixed before live a and artificial f. Give square-core selection
priority, then select cube cores outside it. Define `R_hard,adapt` by
failing both tests. This partition applies to the original signed source
and commutes with the complete mutual-gcd expansion.

After substitution, the first A powers in the square and cube bounds are
respectively `3/5` and `1/5`; both second A powers are zero. Summing
`A<<U^(1/6)` gives first-term exponents `4027/3000` and `477/1000`,
including tau. Against the lower bound for T, the limiting second terms
have raw margins `23813/2730000` and `2768/170625`. The exact box check
uses a positive derivative floor `21481/24300`. After tau/6, auxiliary
loss `1/500`, and retained saving `1/200`, the respective reserves remain

    177/113750 and 8241/910000.

All remaining divisor/profile small powers and eventual thresholds are
chosen in the order specified by the full source proof. Near the largest
A, the caps reach scales `U^(9/8)` and `U^(31/20)`; fixed constants and
nominal dyadic endpoints are retained.

An f-dependent selector is not licensed. For a common prime p, the
unrestricted gcd weights give `1-1=0`, whereas retaining only f=p gives
`-1`. This blocks a tempting enlargement that would change the source.
The adaptive original-A selector avoids that defect.

Combining low, square-core, cube-core and far-tail payments yields the
complete signed identity

    ||F_<||_U^2 = R_nonunique + R_hard,adapt
                   + O(H_J U^(T-1/200+epsilon)).

Generic large squarefree frequencies fail both caps and survive. The
entire nonunique companion also survives. A bound for one signed subset
cannot be subtracted monotonically from another. A useful next input is
a one-sided saving for the SUM of these two complete residuals.

Even such a saving would still need the original detector return: physical
projectors, ancestry, exceptional rows, radius/K_phys, amplification,
shortenings, mesh and tails. In the retained free-row return the prospective
margin is capped by `1/200`; the actual two-inverse witness plus prefix
also retains its `1/2000` cap. Neither margin is a proved increase in c.

## G207: full product, collisions and weighted removal

Let `V_D,2(x)=W_P(x)[log D/log(Dx)]^2`. Its finite derivatives are
uniformly controlled on the original positive-m annulus. The exact
convolution is

    S^[omega](D)=(log D)^-2 sum_(p,q in J)
       log N(p) log N(q) phi_u(pq)/sqrt(N(p)N(q))
                              S(D/[N(p)N(q)];V_D,2).

For distinct p,q in dyads P1,P2, separate the common three-coordinate
profile before live rows, primes or colors. With `E=D/(P1 P2)`,
`P1^-1/2 P2^-1/2 E^-1/2=D^-1/2` exactly. The fixed prime coefficients
are `log N(p)/log U`, extracting only the bounded scalar `(log U/log D)^2`.
Scale differentiation changes no arithmetic pool or coefficient.

Apply the same-bin shortened plain estimate first, then marked MI with
the two additional slots. Each new width is at most `2eta`; the first
gate adds at most `8eta`, the second at most `32eta`. G137 gives
`r+2v<=1-.01017`, so their remaining margins are at least

    217/100000 and 39417/50000

at the largest eta and v, before prescribed fine losses. The off-diagonal
dyad has squared price `H_J U^(1+epsilon)D^beta(P1 P2)^(-beta)`.

The collision payment is complete. Each distinct new prime can equal at
most one old slot prime; two such equalities remove different old slots
because the old supports are disjoint. For an equality, the actual old
and new scales are comparable, and its normalizers have absolute mass
`sum_p(P_i N(p))^-1/2 <<1`. Both shortened plain savings remain.
The extracted phase `phi_u(p)^2` is a positive-norm contraction with its
zero retained. The inverse is never declared coprime to that prime.
Remaining equality exclusions are fixed row-independent prime supports.

For the surviving h distinct prime variables, one normalized random
coloring on the UNION of their prime-IDEAL pools gives

    1_(p_1,...,p_h all distinct)
       =h^h E_color product_i 1_(color(p_i)=i).

The cost is the fixed h^h, not the number of colorings. Equal-norm
different ideals remain different labels. Empty and one-slot cases use
their literal products. This exhausts old/new support intersections.

For p=q, leave the COMPLETE old Q and inverse inside MI. After applying
the shortened plain bound, the dyadic absolute mass is
`sum_p (log N(p)/log D)^2 N(p)^(-1-beta) <<U^epsilon P^(-beta)`.
Its squared price saves `Z^(-2beta)`, including p=q equal to an old
slot or inverse prime. Hilbert triangle over all patterns and dyads proves

    ||M S^[omega] Q||^2_Omega
         <<H_J U^(1+epsilon)D^beta Z^(-2beta).        (1)

Now pay the entire removed source B_T. G198 keeps the exact
`L=lcm(q0,k^2)` and complete q0-smooth inverse restoration, with norm
coefficient mass `T^(-beta/2)U^epsilon`. The plain multiplier is
omega(Lc), rather than omega(c). For d=pq, set `h=d/gcd(d,L)`.
Primewise valuations give `d|Lc` if and only if `h|c`, so the exact
extracted plain block equals

    S_(omega,L)(E)=(log D)^-2 sum_(p,q in J)
       log N(p)log N(q) phi_u(h)N(h)^(-1/2)
                                      S(E/N(h);V_D,2), E=D/N(L).

For p=q, h is p^2,p,1 when the valuation in L is 0,1,at least2.
No character is divided out. The denominator is exact because
`log(N(L)N(c))=log(D(N(c)/E))`. All residual cofactor valuations remain.

After the same plain bound, ideal counting and `N(L)<=C D` give uniformly

    |S_(omega,L)(D/N(L))|
       <<H_J U^epsilon (D/N(L))^(beta/2) A^(1-beta).

The squared cost is `A^(2(1-beta))=Y^(1-beta)`, once. Insert this inside
the FULL G198 coefficient convolution before absolute values, keeping every
shared prime and inverse restoration. Then

    ||B_T^[omega]Q||^2
       <<H_J U^(1+epsilon)D^beta T^(-beta)Y^(1-beta).

The exact signed identity `C_T^[omega]=B^[omega]-B_T^[omega]` and triangle
now give the COMPLETE core estimate

    ||C_T^[omega]Q||^2
       <<H_J U^(1+epsilon)D^beta
                         [Z^(-2beta)+T^(-beta)Y^(1-beta)]
       <<H_J U^(1+beta*m-2beta*eta+epsilon).          (2)

At beta=17/25 the two savings are `34eta/25` and `36eta/25`.
Their difference is positive since beta>2/3 with a reserved buffer.
This pays a genuinely new pair-divisibility source below the old band.

## G208: exact pair mass and a fifth actual row class

The reviewer sharpens the uniform block calculation. Write

    s=(1+beta)/2, w_p=log N(p)/log D,
    I=sum_(p in J,p|L)w_p,
    V=sum_(p in J,p not|L)w_p N(p)^(-s).

Then the EXACT positive pair mass is

    A_L=sum_(p,q in J)w_p w_q N(pq/gcd(pq,L))^(-s)
       =(I+V)^2-sum_(p in J,v_p(L)=1)w_p^2[1-N(p)^(-s)]
       <=(I+V)^2.                                  (3)

Distinct pairs factor. On the diagonal, valuation0 contributes p^(-2s),
valuation1 contributes p^(-s), and valuation at least2 contributes1.
Only the middle case differs from the diagonal of `(I+V)^2`. This proves
(3), including all p=q and shared-prime cases, with no extra diagonal loss.
Since `I<=1+O(1/log D)` and `V<<U^epsilon A^((1-beta)/2)`, it also
reproves the uniform block bound above. It is a sharper label-specific
positive mass, not a new global power saving or signed contraction.

Keep all FOUR previously paid classes FIRST. Their remaining actual rows
have `|C_T^[1-theta]|>|M(R)S(D)|/4`. On that complement, define

    Omega_pair={u: |C_T^[omega](u)|>=|M_u(R)S_u(D)|/8}.

Divide (2) by the ORIGINAL same-beta plain spike. Its D^beta cancels
before beta is weakened to physical delta, giving

    sum_(Omega_pair)w_u |M_u(R)Q_u|^2
         <<H_J U^(1-2delta*eta+epsilon).             (4)

Q is never divided out. This fifth class is disjoint by construction;
its preloss reserve above the requested eta is `9eta/25`.
Every remaining row satisfies

    |C_T^[1-theta-omega]|>|M(R)S(D)|/8,
    N(n/rad n)<T NP,
    0<=1-theta(b)-omega(b)<=1-theta(b).               (5)

Band prime squares remain absent. Lower-band prime squares are retained
and were paid explicitly in (1)-(3). The repeat support is a necessary
tuple consequence, not an intrinsic signed merged-coefficient projection.

For an actual surviving tuple with every prime factor of b in J, put
`e_b=eta log U/log N(b)`. Its repeat bound gives
`ell_rad,J(b)>log N(b)-4eta log U`, while
`d_1,J(b)<=2eta log U log N(b)`. In the source's positive-m range,
this yields `0<=1-omega(b)<=10e_b`. This is useful coefficient damping
but only a constant factor at fixed eta; it gives no signed power saving.

The full coarse norm is paid by the complete difference

    C_T^[1-theta-omega]=C_T-C_T^[theta]-C_T^[omega].

It still gives only `H_J U^(1+epsilon)` for the inverse moment after
division. Good prime plain ideals above Y with coprime squarefree inverse
tuples have F=1 and theta=omega=0. They survive unchanged. This is a
coefficient example, with no claim that it supplies a high-zero row.

## G209. All thirteen collision types and the exact mixed-order source

At each good prime record its six original site incidences: two inverses
and at most one slot on each copy. Each occupancy is zero or one.
For the thirteen types (a,b) with 0<=a,b<=3 and a+b>=2, let h_ab be the
squarefree product of primes of that type. The h_ab are pairwise coprime;
all named-slot tests and original coefficients remain attached. Define

    Lc=product h_ab^a, Rc=product h_ab^b,
    L=N(Lc), R=N(Rc), D=LR,
    k=product_(a!=b) h_ab, Kc=N(k),
    E=product_(a=b>=1) h_ab, Hcol=product h_ab.

Every pair uniquely has n=Lc*x,n'=Rc*y, with x,y squarefree, mutually
coprime and prime to Hcol. All six gcd predicates now depend only on
collision labels and incidences. Nonunique means Hcol!=1.

For either complete orientation e=+1 or -1, including natural zeros,

    chi_n(u)^e conjugate(chi_n'(u)^e)
      = psi_k(u) chi_x(u)^e conjugate(chi_y(u)^e) 1_((u,E)=1),
    psi_k = product_(a!=b) chi_p^(e(a-b)).

The good primitive conductor is kxy; each nonzero local exponent has
order 6,3 or2. Equal valuations leave a unit-indicator hole, not one.
The principal class kxy=1 is the entire merged diagonal and is paid
before zero-frequency vanishing. Its full row cost is
O(H_J U^(1+epsilon)) by the c_abs squared-mass bound.

Expand sixth-freeness with a0^6|u, retaining (a0,Hcol*x*y)=1, then expand
the full canceled-phase hole with d|E. Put qa=N(a0),qd=N(d).
Primitive Poisson and CRT preserve the mixed Gauss factor at k,
both residual orientations, separated k,d twists and every zero.

Fix an ORIGINAL a0-dyad qa~A and tau=1/1000. The literal retained cap is

    Hc = C_* U^tau A^6 qd Kc N0^2/(U L R).

Before any artificial extension, the complete genuine far tail is
O(H_J U^(149/30+epsilon-tau(B-1))); choose finite B after the raw count.
On the fractional dual lattice, emptiness uses its fixed least positive
norm. Hc<1 alone does not mean empty. Clearing by the fixed S-supported
Delta changes comparison constants; the original selector is unchanged.

Only then insert the COMPLETE mutual-divisor identity on x,y. For
x=fm,y=fm',F=N(f), allocate f separately through the original colors and
slots on both copies. The unequal residual lengths are

    XL=N0/(L F), XR=N0/(R F).

Both unnormalized roots give precisely

    [U sqrt(LR)/(qa^6 qd N0^2 sqrt(Kc))] sqrt(XL XR)
       = U/(qa^6 qd N0 sqrt(Kc) F).

Actual collision labels are not artificial f labels. No extra reciprocal
L or R occurs. All masks and the cutoff are fixed before f; otherwise
the projector's complete cancellation can fail. Fix the common weighted
Fourier measure on ambient nominal boxes before live labels. Subtract
the formal rank-one unit core explicitly at the already paid diagonal cost.

## G210. Unequal energies and all collision-label sums

For square cores (Delta ell)=kappa2*b^2, allow overlap and unrestricted b.
For cube cores (Delta ell)=kappa3*t^3*z^6, retain cubefree kappa3,
squarefree t and the exact hole 1_((m,z)=1), including sixth-power zeros.

The arbitrary-sequence cubic energy is B^(1/3)(B+X), with unrestricted
outer variable, from [Dunn, v3, Section4](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.13151v3).
The squarefree quadratic energy B+X uses the exact PR9 B2.24 family and
[Goldmakher-Louvel, v2, Definition1/Theorem1.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1112.1642v2).
Fixed twists enter arbitrary inner sequences; no conductor-dependent
family constant or arbitrary joint-matrix sieve is licensed.

Let l_i1,l_i2,l_iP be the extracted collision norms on side i.
The original-color pointwise estimate, with all fixed punctures, is

    Si=(P0/l_iP)[D1/l_i1+D2/l_i2+(D1D2/(l_i1 l_i2))^(2/3)].

At core cap C, square-column energy is As+Xi Bs and cube-column energy
is Ac+Zi Bc, where

    As=Hc^(2/3)C^(1/3), Bs=Hc^(1/6)C^(5/6),
    Ac=Hc^(1/3)C^(2/3), Bc=Hc^(1/6)C^(5/6),
    Zi=sqrt(Si Xi).

The cube formula splits sixth repetitions at
Z=sqrt(B Si/Xi), clipped to[1,sqrt(B)]. Both clipped endpoint regimes
give B+sqrt(B Si Xi); no assumption Si<=Xi is made.

For unequal x,y retain every term in

    sqrt((A+xB)(A+yB))
       <= A+B sqrt(xy)+sqrt(AB)(sqrt(x)+sqrt(y)).

The exact eight restored monomials are in the unchanged reviewer table.
The two cross terms in each sector cannot be discarded. Their collision
weights are summed over all thirteen ideals and every site allocation.

The support prices follow from the ORIGINAL source:

    N(h20),N(h02) << G P0, N(h11) << N0,
    N(h11^(ij)) < Hij.

The column defect n/rad(n) equals the within-column inverse gcd times a
divisor of its slot product. This proves the first bounds.
The other two are divisibility statements, not stochastic independence.

SQ0 and SQ2 have summable local exponents at least7/6 and4/3.
The SQ cross has only the transposed type(0,2) deficit11/12, costing
(GP0)^(1/12). CU0 costs N0^(1/3)(GP0)^(1/3).
Each CU cross costs N0^(1/4)(GP0)^(1/4); its type(0,3) is harmonic.
Polynomial caps are fixed before assigning all divisor/dyadic losses.

The limiting CU2 term requires expanding the THREE positive components
of Si on EACH copy. Only four configurations remain deficient:
two linear components with the shared (1,1) prime in both omitted inverse
sites. Each has weight5/6 and is paid by its ORIGINAL Hij^(1/6).
Geometric components leave at worst a harmonic weight.

After N0^(-1/6) and complete collision summation, removing the common
P0^(1/3), the nine-component certificate is:

| Component | Remaining factor |
|---|---|
| D1,D1 | D1^(1/3) U^(-1/8) |
| D2,D2 | D2^(1/3) U^(-1/12) |
| D1,D2 or D2,D1 | (D1D2)^(1/12) U^(1/10) |
| D1,geometric or transpose | D1^(1/4) |
| D2,geometric or transpose | D2^(1/4) |
| geometric,geometric | (D1D2)^(1/6) |

Every entry except D2,D2 is dominated by (D1D2)^(1/6) on the full closed
r,s rectangle. Its exact extra ratio is U^((s-r-1/2)/6).
Thus the complete limiting scale is

    P0^(1/3)(D1D2)^(1/6) max(1,U^((s-r-1/2)/6)).

Replacing both Si by an unchanged global bound would lose this payment.
This estimate preserves the actual color structure; it is not a theorem
for an arbitrary merged coefficient matrix.

statement:
## G212. Fixed-family binding and complete row/column lifts

Let K=Q(omega), q_a=N(a), with the original primary convention, fixed
excluded set S containing the primes above6 and fixed conductors, and the
original finite ray dictionary. Every character power, including a
cancelled phase, retains its zero at a nonunit. Write
psi_u(b)=chi_b(u) and phi_u=nu psi_u^(+/-1), with nu fixed; nu need not
have order dividing6. All coefficients below are independent of the row
being summed. A moving but fixed puncture is a zero column coefficient,
not a new fixed character datum.

The external input is de Faveri, *Optimal large sieve for fixed order
characters*, [arXiv2610.04045v1, Theorem1.1 and Sections2.3–2.5](https://arxiv.org/html/2610.04045v1).
It is the operator bound for sixth-power-free S-coprime ideal rows AND
columns, with arbitrary column coefficients:

    sum_(q_a<=A)^(6) |sum_(q_b<=B)^(6) lambda_b chi_a(b)|^2
      << (AB)^epsilon T6(A,B) sum_b |lambda_b|^2,
    T6(A,B)=A+B+A^(5/6)B^(1/3)+A^(1/3)B^(5/6).       (1)

The constants depend on the fixed construction data. This manuscript
already cited that theorem in Appendix S.1; its reuse is not a new
discovery of the external result. Its analytic proof and external
definition/import/admission remain named inputs, not newly verified here.

Here is the actual family binding. In the class-number-one Eisenstein
field choose the source's representative generators m_E to be global
primary generators. In its decomposition a=(x)E g^6, x=1 modulo the fixed
ray modulus, take a primary generator g0 of the fractional ideal g.
Then x m_E g0^6 and the primary a0 generate the same ideal and are both1
modulo3. Their quotient is a unit congruent to1 modulo3 and hence equals1.
Thus the source's symbol equals (a0/b)_6 on coprime ideals; its prescribed
zero extension also agrees. Other permissible generator conventions split
into finitely many S-unit classes modulo sixth powers, giving fixed column
twists. Split element units and S-valuations modulo6, then count their
S-supported sixth powers with a logarithmic loss. Absorb nu into the
column coefficients. For the opposite orientation conjugate the WHOLE
inner sum. Reverse residue-symbol orientation, when used, retains the
original finite modulo36 reciprocity sectors. No row-column coefficient
array or moving-conductor character license is inferred.

For a product of J fixed normalized polynomials of lengths X_j, put
B=product X_j. Exact ordered convolution, including all collisions, has

    F_u=sum_b lambda_b psi_u(b),  q_b<<B,
    |lambda_b| << B^(-1/2) d_J(b).                    (2)

Signs, phases, independent heights, original slot coefficients and the
fixed nu remain in lambda. Disjoint slot pools do not imply a slot is
coprime to a plain factor. Write b=d h^6 uniquely with d sixth-power-free,
allowing (d,h)>1. Then

    psi_u(d h^6)=psi_u(d) 1_((u,h)=1),
    sum_d |lambda_(d h^6)|^2 << B^epsilon q_h^(-6).

For each fixed h apply (1) and remove the h restriction only from its
positive outer norm. Hilbert Minkowski sums q_h^(-3), a convergent ideal
series. This gives T6(U,B) on sixth-power-free rows. For ALL rows write
u=a e^6, with all units and S-parts as above. The extra factor
1_((b,e)=1) is a fixed column mask for each e. Applying (1) at U/q_e^6
and summing every e yields

    sum_(0<q_u<<U) |F_u|^2 << (UB)^epsilon Tall(U,B),
    Tall(U,B)=U+B U^(1/6)+U^(5/6)B^(1/3)
                         +U^(1/3)B^(5/6).           (3)

The term B U^(1/6) counts the sixth-power repetitions; they are not a
finite dictionary. No principal or fixed-inducing row is discarded.
The normalized short gate is B<=U^(1/2). In particular S(U^m)^2 Q has
B=U^(2m+v), and two independent plains have B=U^(n1+n2+v). The failed
proposal m+v<=1/2 for a fourth moment lost a factor of2. The correct
2m+v<=1/2 and inverse r+v<=1/2 were already in equation (S.4) of Appendix S.1.

Now take the literal PR9 B3.6 canonical energy, writing X=Z^N,
U=Z^M, F=Z^V:

    E=F^(-1) sum_(q_f~F)^(sf) w(f)
       sum_(0<q_k<<U)
       |X^(-1/2) sum_n^(sf) a0(n)nu(n)rho(n)
           chi_n(k)chi_n(f)^4 d_I(n) W(q_n/X)|^2.    (4)

Here a0=bar(alpha)gamma_2 has modulus1 on good squarefree indices;
w is nonnegative divisor-bounded; rho is the fixed puncture; d_I is
the original product-form mark from fixed disjoint slot pools. Pools,
coefficients and punctures are independent of the live f,k. A fixed
polynomial-size puncture can move between instances. The coefficient
mass for each fixed f is Z^epsilon, uniformly in its natural holes;
F^(-1) cancels the count of f. Thus (3) gives exponent

    Eall(M,N)=max(M,N+M/6,5M/6+N/3,M/3+5N/6)
       = M                    for 0<=N<=M/2,
         5M/6+N/3             for M/2<=N<=M,
         N+M/6                for N>=M.              (5)

This bound alone remains valid for column coefficients depending on the
fixed f, provided the coefficient mass is uniformly controlled. That
extra freedom is NOT available in the label-average argument below.

The full completed theta source has index A=c b^3, c squarefree, and
coefficient

    a0(c)nu(c) bar(alpha(b))^3 nu(b)^3
      chi_A(f)^4 rho(A)d_I(A)V(q_A/X)/(sqrt(q_c)q_b). (6)

Its character is psi_k(A), with all common c,b primes permitted. Each
A has at most one such representation. Writing A=d h^6 gives
d=c b0^3, b=b0 h^2, with c,b0 squarefree and possibly overlapping.
The exponents of d are0,1,3,4. At fixed h the squared coefficient mass
is at most

    X^epsilon q_h^(-4)
       sum_(b0 sf) q_b0^(-2) sum_(q_c<<X/q_h^6) q_c^(-1)
      << X^epsilon q_h^(-4).                        (7)

All whole-index marks, phases and f/puncture/row holes stay in (6).
Minkowski now sums q_h^(-2), again convergent. Both T6 and Tall therefore
apply to the COMPLETE theta source with X as column length. This is not
a restriction to its b=1 or coprime c,b part.

The profile contract is annular support or rapid decay at both endpoints,
with prescribed finite derivative orders. Original common product
profiles use the Fourier measure fixed on the whole ambient box before
the live labels, as in PR9 B3.3. Minkowski and dyadic decomposition sum
these tails; subunit scales are treated at the original profile. Tensor
Sobolev restores the independent heights and the bounded profile/scale
suprema at a fixed polynomial cost H_J. Derivative orders and Fourier
decay precede the final large-scale threshold. This argument does not
grant a new small-x decay bound for an arbitrary sharply reflected
profile. Genuine detector tails keep their own prior payment.

When f=1 and rho=1, the old unmarked completed bound B2.43 may be
combined with (5). The resulting exponent is M, then5M/6+N/3, then
2M-N, thenM on the consecutive intervals
[0,M/2],[M/2,7M/8],[7M/8,M],[M,infinity). Its maximum is9M/8.
For the old marked S.5 scope, z<=M/2, take the minimum with
M+max(0,(N+2z-2M)/4,M+2z-N); e.g. N=.7M,z=.04M improves
1.38M to16M/15. These old-theorem comparisons are not extended to
new labels or punctures without their own proof.

## G213. Average the true cubic label before counting repetitions

In (4) fix k and use the order-three character chi_n(f)^4 in the actual
squarefree f,n variables. The old squarefree cubic sieve B2.25 gives,
after dividing by F and counting all k,

    Elabel=M+L,  L=max(0,N-V,(2N-V)/3).              (8)

For (6), fix b first:
chi_(c b^3)(f)^4=chi_c(f)^4 1_((b,f)=1).
The b phase has modulus at most1. Remove its natural f-hole only after
taking the fixed-b positive norm. Its coefficient mass is bounded by
q_b^(-2) times logarithms, and its c-length is X/q_b^3.
Minkowski sums q_b^(-1) for the constant-in-length term (a logarithm);
the positive column-length terms converge. Thus (8) holds for the full
theta source as well. This requires the coefficients, marks, puncture
and common profile to be independent of f. Arbitrarily conditioning them
on the label would invalidate the cubic sieve.

The whole-norm minimum of (5),(8) does not enlarge the boundary for the
canonical target exponent N+V. The label-only gate is
V>=max(M-N,M/2,(3M-N)/4), which is at least the old all-row gate.
There is nevertheless a stronger estimate BEFORE counting repetitions.

For each exact e in k=a e^6, both estimates apply to the SAME complete
positive joint norm in f and sixth-power-free a. The column mask
1_((A,e)=1) is fixed through both averages. Put Arow=U/q_e^6. Its bound
is the minimum of T6(Arow,X) and Arow Z^L, up to the same small loss
and height cost. The two methods do not select incompatible sources.
Counting EVERY e dyad q_e~Z^y, including both endpoints, with t=M-6y
therefore proves

    E << H_J Z^(Emix+epsilon),
    Emix(M,N,V)=sup_(0<=t<=M)
        [(M-t)/6+min(C(t,N),t+L)],
    C(t,N)=max(t,N,5t/6+N/3,t/3+5N/6).              (9)

This is valid for (4) and the complete (6). The dyadic count Z^y is
essential. No signed subsource monotonicity, invented f-average or
discarded principal layer occurs.

For completeness, a continuous evaluation of (9) gives

    E0=min(C(M,N),M+L),  P=(M+5N+L)/6,
    Emix=E0, except that
    Emix=max(E0,P) if L>=N/2 and N-L<=M.             (10)

Indeed C(t,N) has successive affine pieces
N,t/3+5N/6,5t/6+N/3,t, with breakpoints N/2,N,2N.
On the first piece its contribution after subtracting t/6 decreases,
whereas the label contribution increases. Their sole crossing is
t=N-L. Because0<=L<=N, it lies in the first piece and in[0,M]
exactly under the condition in (10). The value there is P.
On each later piece both branches increase: their respective slopes
after counting are1/6,2/3,5/6 and5/6. Their minimum increases as well.
Thus the endpoint t=M and that one crossing give the entire maximum.
This also covers a truncated first interval; M=0 or N=0 is immediate.

For M>0, the precise boundary of THIS proved upper envelope is

    Emix<=N+V iff V>=g(M,N),
    g(M,N)= M-N                   (0<=N<=M/2),
             5M/6-2N/3            (M/2<=N<=M),
             (2M-N)/6             (M<=N<=8M/7),
             M/7                  (N>=8M/7).        (11)

Here is the proof of necessity as well as sufficiency for the envelope.
For N<=M, (9)<=Eall proves sufficiency at the first two thresholds.
At t=M, the sieve branch reaches the target only at that threshold,
while the label branch requires the stronger gate following (8).
For N>=M the proposed threshold is at most M/6. In0<=V<=M/6,
L=N-V and the crossing t=V is present. Its price is
N+(M-V)/6, so it is paid exactly when V>=M/7.
The t=M label price exceeds N+V throughout this interval; the sieve
branch requires V>=(2M-N)_+/6. Their maximum switches at N=8M/7.
These conditions suffice by (10). Larger V decreases Emix and increases
the target; a smaller V fails a displayed envelope branch.
Equality has the usual Z^epsilon loss. Applications needing a strict
reserve must choose a padded inequality. This is no lower bound on the
true arithmetic energy.

At (M,N,V)=(1,8/7,1/7), the new price9/7 equals N+V, while Eall=55/42
and Elabel=2. At (1,2,1/7), they are15/7,13/6,20/7.
The gain over Eall is1/42 in each example. Polynomial-size common
punctures remain uniform; the improvement need not satisfy PR9 B3.7's
older sufficient Q gate. Conversely at V=0, L=N and C(t,N)<=t+N.
Equation (9) becomes EXACTLY Eall. In particular Emix>N for every
M>0. The complete unlabelled canonical target remains unpaid.

## G214. Counted sectors and the full physical obstruction

Useful lower-order subfamilies remain available with their counts.
For sixth-power-free u=t a^2, t squarefree, a cube-free, permit shared
primes and retain q_t<=D. In the completed source,

    chi_(c b^3)(t a^2)
      =chi_(c b^3)(t) chi_c(a)^2 1_((a,b)=1).

Fix b before the positive a norm and use the CUBE-FREE cubic input,
not a silent enlargement of squarefree B2.25. This input is explicit
in the retained [restricted research revision] MQ1 (or de Faveri's n=3 theorem with its binding).
Counting each t at length(U/q_t)^(1/2) gives

    (UD)^(1/2)+XD+U^(1/3)X^(2/3)D^(2/3).            (12)

For u=t a^3, t cube-free, a squarefree, the squarefree quadratic sieve
and counts instead give U^(1/3)D^(2/3)+XD. All coefficients, zeros
and b sums are treated as in the fixed-b proof above. [restricted research revision]'s MQ4 already
contains the counted cubic mechanism for its own original source.
These are useful actual-sector extensions, not a new universal sieve.
A generic squarefree row has t=u in both decompositions, so a small D
does not cover it. Non-S sixth-power repetitions require their own
counted lift; [restricted research revision] MQ5 additionally uses a named all-character reciprocal
strip. Neither that assumption nor a missing complement is free.

The physical failure can be quantified over the entire relevant range.
At [restricted research revision]'s conditional geometry set
ell=313594727/1875000000, M=1-ell; then1/6<ell<1/5.
Every compensator subset of width d in[0,ell] has

    M'=M-2d, z'=ell-d, N'=1+ell-d,
    N'-M'=2ell+d>0, N'-(M'+2z')=3d>=0.

PR9 B0.26 costs Eold=M'+max(0,-1+5ell+d)/4. Equation (5) costs
N'+M'/6, whose excess is

    (1+11ell)/6+2d/3-max(0,-1+5ell+d)/4 >19/45.     (13)

The first term exceeds17/36 and the subtracted term is less than1/20.
This pays the comparison on the whole subset interval, including the
empty subset. The exact signs, outside coefficients and tuple counts
in B0.25, and the old -d saving in B0.27, are retained on both sides.
These sources have f=1,V=0, so (9) cannot alter (13).

The actual two-plain window .41M<=n_i<=.44M with .034M<=v<=.04M
has merged length at least .854M. Equation (5) then costs at least
1.118M, instead of the required M. Even v=0 leaves length at least
.82M and misses the short gate. The literal Euler restoration B0.41–44
has h=h0 h_r, repeated-row allocation q_u/q_rad(u), reflected scale
at most(U/Y)h0 and weighted mass sum|c_u(h0,h_r)|h0^(delta/2)<<U^epsilon.
The critical h0=1 case already fails; increasing h0 cannot repair it.
Shortened cases do not pay their longer complements. Independent heights,
four clipped profile pairs, shortage and empty-selection alternatives,
zero capacity, fixed-inducing/principal branches, and the original
Euler/detector tails retain their old proofs. No label signal is inserted.

Nor does the imported density corollary fix the active density gate.
De Faveri Corollary1.5 at n=6, delta=2sigma-1 in[1/3,5/6], saves

    D6=3delta(6delta-1)/(60delta-36delta^2-10).

For delta in[17/25,7/10] its row exponent1-D6 exceeds the retained
rho=1-10delta/[3(5-2delta)] by

    delta(312delta-252delta^2-55) /
      [3(5-2delta)(60delta-36delta^2-10)] >17/100.    (14)

The concave numerator quadratic is at least998/25, delta>=17/25,
and the positive denominator is at most98007/625. The resulting
16966/98007 is greater than17/100. Since delta v<=.035 and
E_K<=rho+delta v, the new corollary is weaker even on the uncontested
untwisted subfamily. It is a zero-count bound, not zero exclusion;
arbitrary fixed-nu extensions are not asserted.

Finally, the separated inverse source in [restricted research revision] has r+s>217/100,
delta in[17/25,7/10], v<=1/20 and target T=delta(r+s)+E_K.
Its merged length b=r+s+v exceeds2.17. Even the sixth-free sieve
cost b exceeds T by at least

    (1-delta)(r+s+v)-rho >=8077/27000.               (15)

The minimum is at v=0,r+s=217/100,delta=7/10: the delta derivative
is negative on the whole interval. The all-row cost is larger.
This is a failure of the proposed sufficient price, not a norm lower
bound or impossibility theorem for the signed arithmetic.
The current [restricted research revision] residual is R_U,hard+R_N,hard, replacing the older
[restricted research revision] R_nonunique+R_middle wording in these raw reports. Its one-sided
saving and physical return remain open.

The field-source targets gamma<.8748540364 (energy<1.7497080728),
gamma=.87485 at c=.12515, gamma=5/6 at c=1/6 and gamma=3/4 at c=1/4
remain target conversions with their actual transfers required.
The old ell<1/5 limit c<2/15 and ell<x<=y, x+y=1-ell limit c<1/6
are restrictions of that architecture, not universal barriers.

statement:
## G215. Exact source, complete localization and all-height return

Fix an ordinary Dirichlet character chi modulo its PRESENTED modulus q,
including every natural nonunit zero. Let chi(-1)=(-1)^a and fix r>=2
with r congruent to a modulo2. The choices r=2 for even chi and r=3 for
odd chi suffice. All q,chi,r and the filter order below are fixed before
the scale, target height and implied constants. There is no growing-q,
growing-r or Hecke-family assertion.

Define the Jordan coefficient and Laplace source by

    J_r(n)=sum_(d|n) mu(d)(n/d)^r
          =n^r product_(p|n)(1-p^(-r)),
    F(X)=sum_(n>=1) chi(n)J_r(n) exp(-n/X).          (1)

Inclusion-exclusion counts primitive r-tuples modulo n and proves the
coefficient formula. Squareful values are deliberate: this source does
not claim to retain squarefree Möbius support. Absolute convolution
gives L(s-r,chi)/L(s,chi) on Re s>r+1, with all inducing factors.

Put m_q=phi(q)/q for principal chi and0 otherwise,
A=m_q r!/L(r+1,chi), and E(X)=F(X)-A X^(r+1). The Euler product
defines the reciprocal at r+1 without an unproved strip assumption.
For t>0 set

    H(t)=sum_(n>=1)chi(n)e^(-nt)
        =[sum_(v=1)^q chi(v)e^(-vt)]/[1-e^(-qt)],
    f(t)=(-d/dt)^r H(t),
    g(t)=f(t)-m_q r! t^(-r-1).

Absolute convergence of the original double series and of the
subtracted reciprocal series at r+1 proves the COMPLETE identity

    E(X)=sum_(d>=1) mu(d)chi(d)g(d/X).               (2)

The principal main coefficient is for the presented modulus, not its
primitive conductor. No finite Euler correction is suppressed.

For q>1 residue reflection gives H(-t)=-chi(-1)H(t).
For q=1 the extra constant is -1, removed by r differentiations.
The parity choice makes the regular part of f odd; its possible
principal pole is odd too. Thus g(t)=O(t), g'(t)=O(1) at zero.
At infinity f,f'=O(e^(-t)); principal g retains exactly the algebraic
tail -m_q r!t^(-r-1). Consequently

    |g(t)| <= C min(t,t^(-r-1)),  E(X)=O(X), X>=1.   (3)

The actual complete low/high absolute prices, for alpha<1<beta, are
O(X^(2alpha-1)) and O(X^(r+1-r beta)) at d<=X^alpha and d>X^beta.
For gamma in(0,1), alpha=(1+gamma)/2 and beta=1+(1-gamma)/r
pay both at X^gamma. The middle is still signed and unpaid.

Now fix b=2 and m>=0, put T h(t)=h(2t), D G(X)=G(X/2), and

    P_m(T)=product_(j=0)^(m-1)(I-2^(-(2j+1))T),
    B_r(T)=I-2^(r+1)T,
    K(t)=P_m(T)B_r(T)g(t)=P_m(T)B_r(T)f(t),
    Phi(X)=P_m(D)B_r(D)E(X)=P_m(D)B_r(D)F(X).

The empty product is identity. The B_r factor kills the principal
algebraic tail and the main term exactly. P_m removes the first m
odd Taylor powers. Therefore

    Phi(X)=sum_(d>=1) mu(d)chi(d)K(d/X),             (4)
    K(t)=O(t^(2m+1)), K'(t)=O(t^(2m)) as t->0,
    K(t)=e^(-t)+O(e^(-2t)),
    K'(t)=-e^(-t)+O(e^(-2t)) as t->infinity.         (5)

The coefficient of the slowest exponential is chi(1)1^r=1, since
every other dilation has argument at least2t. This also proves K
is nonzero. Equation (4) keeps exactly the original outer mu(d)chi(d).
Even when2 divides q, these are literal scale dilations: no chi(2)
is factored out, and the expanded output coefficients are not falsely
assigned the old support. Phi can be evaluated from F without knowing A.
It is O(X) at infinity and O(e^(-1/X)) at zero.

For any fixed gamma in(0,1), set

    alpha=1-(1-gamma)/(2m+2),
    Cmid(x)=sum_(x^alpha<d<=2x log x)mu(d)chi(d)K(d/x).

For every sufficiently large real x, the three disjoint ranges
d<=x^alpha, x^alpha<d<=2x log x, d>2x log x cover all divisors.
The first absolute price is
x^(-(2m+1)) sum_(d<=x^alpha)d^(2m+1)=O(x^gamma).
The last is O(sum_(d>2x log x)e^(-d/x))=O(x^-1).
Rounding the real cut changes only a fixed constant. Thus

    Phi(x)=Cmid(x)+O(x^gamma).                       (6)

The cuts decompose ONE fixed source; they do not create a different
Mellin profile at each x. The weakest return used here is the complete
dyadic-shell L1 hypothesis

    integral_X^(2X)|Cmid(x)| dx/x
       <<_(chi,r,m,epsilon) X^(gamma+epsilon)       (7)

for every epsilon>0 and all sufficiently large dyadic X, at one common
gamma across every fixed ordinary chi. A full shell L2 bound implies
(7); no favorable signed subset is substituted for the whole norm.
For m=1 the paid lower exponents are .9687135091 at gamma11,
.9687 at gamma=.8748,23/24 at gamma=5/6, and15/16 at gamma=3/4.
The full upper cutoff is2x log x in every case. These are explicit
complement budgets, not estimates of Cmid.

To establish the all-height return, ordinary functional equations,
trivial-zero parity and exact inducing factors give

    L(s-r,chi) !=0 for 0<Re s<=1.                   (8)

Indeed -r<Re(s-r)<=1-r lies between consecutive parity trivial zeros,
and the extra finite factors have zeros only on Re(s-r)=0.
The q=1 zeta case is treated separately at its negative even zeros.
These standard inputs are recorded in [DLMF25.15](https://dlmf.nist.gov/25.15)
and [DLMF25.10](https://dlmf.nist.gov/25.10); the source reflection above
is derived directly.

On Re s>r+1, finite scaling in the absolutely convergent transform gives

    Mellin(Phi)(s)=Gamma(s)Q_mr(s)L(s-r,chi)/L(s,chi),
    Q_mr(s)=(1-2^(r+1-s))
             product_(j=0)^(m-1)(1-2^(-(s+2j+1))).  (9)

Here Mellin(Phi)=integral_0^infinity Phi(X)X^(-s)dX/X.
The first factor cancels the actual principal numerator pole at r+1;
its zeros lie on Re s=r+1. The other zeros lie on negative odd
real-part lines. Hence Q_mr is nonzero in the entire target strip,
including Re s=1. Gamma(s) has no pole or zero there.

The unconditional O(X) and small-X exponential bounds make the full
integral holomorphic for Re s>1. Under (7), equation (6) supplies the
same shell L1 bound for Phi. Sum dyadic integrals on each compact subset
of Re s>gamma, choosing epsilon below its distance to gamma. Derivatives
only insert logarithmic powers. The small-X contribution is entire.
Continuation therefore preserves

    L(s,chi) Mellin(Phi)(s)
        =Gamma(s)Q_mr(s)L(s-r,chi), Re s>gamma.      (10)

A hypothetical zero in gamma<Re s<=1 contradicts (8)–(10); the Euler
product covers Re s>1. The principal pole at1 is allowed and has the
compensating transform zero. Normal convergence on every compact
handles every finite height without assuming a uniform height bound
or that a bare zero-free strip implies a sharp Mertens estimate.

The arithmetic hypothesis (7) remains OPEN. A common gamma<gamma11
would beat the conditional numerical benchmark in the ordinary-family
scope. Targets c=.1252,1/6,1/4 mean gamma=.8748,5/6,3/4 respectively.
No ordinary-to-Hecke or original-Gaussian source transfer is inferred.

statement:
## G216. Exact recovery, actual absolute cost and complete diagonal

Let E_m=P_m(D)E. The proved coarse bound E_m(Y)=O(Y), together with
Phi(X)=E_m(X)-2^(r+1)E_m(X/2), gives for every J>=1

    E_m(X)=2^(-J(r+1))E_m(2^J X)
           -sum_(j=1)^J 2^(-j(r+1))Phi(2^j X).

The first term is O(X2^(-Jr)), so the FULL future-scale inverse is

    E_m(X)=-sum_(j>=1)2^(-j(r+1))Phi(2^j X).        (11)

Every future scale remains. For gamma<r+1 and sufficiently small
epsilon, a complete exponent gamma+epsilon pays the series with
ratio2^(-(r+1-gamma-epsilon))<1. Changing variables in each dyadic
shell proves the same statement in L1. Conversely finite shifts of
E_m imply the Phi bound. Thus their complete every-epsilon exponent
classes are equivalent. The possible homogeneous mode X^(r+1) is
excluded by the actual O(X) bound, not discarded. Shorter support
alone is not a weaker arithmetic obligation.

The complete arithmetic absolute cost also stays linear. Elementary
square-divisor inversion, with all coprimality factors, gives

    Q_q(y)=sum_(n<=y,(n,q)=1)mu(n)^2
          =kappa_q y+O_q(sqrt y),
    kappa_q=zeta(2)^(-1) product_(p|q)(1+1/p)^(-1)>0.

For the original g, for P_m(T)g, and for K, the function absolute value
is absolutely continuous and its a.e. derivative is bounded by the
absolute derivative of the kernel. Both tails give finite
integral_0^infinity sqrt(t)|K'(t)|dt. Stieltjes summation therefore proves

    sum_n |mu(n)chi(n)K(n/X)|
      =kappa_q X integral_0^infinity|K(t)|dt+O(sqrt X). (12)

The integral is positive by the e^(-t) coefficient in (5). For g and
P_m(T)g, use their nonzero principal algebraic tail or nonprincipal
slowest exponential instead. This is a lower asymptotic for the
ACTUAL absolute price, not a lower bound on the signed field or M_chi.
Full triangle inequality cannot yield a fixed sublinear exponent.
Full Abel summation from any known |M_chi(y)|<<y^beta yields only
X^beta integral t^beta|K'(t)|dt; it preserves beta. The bounded
non-arithmetic sequence n^beta-(n-1)^beta tests that operator limitation,
without purporting to refute cancellation of mu chi.

There is an explicit principal normalization. At q=1,r=2,m=0,
v=e^(-t), f(t)=v(1+v)/(1-v)^3, and

    K_0(t)=f(t)-8f(2t)=v(1-v)/(1+v)^3
           =(1/4)tanh(t/2)sech^2(t/2)>0.           (13)

The numerator identity is
v(1+v)^4-8v^2(1+v^2)=v(1-v)^4.
Substitute u=tanh(t/2), dt=2du/(1-u^2), to obtain

    integral K_0(t)dt=integral_0^1 u/2 du=1/4,
    integral K_0(t)^2dt
        =integral_0^1 (u^2-u^4)/8 du=1/60.          (14)

Consequently the literal field
Phi_0(X)=F_(1,2)(X)-8F_(1,2)(X/2)=sum mu(n)K_0(n/X) has

    sum_n |mu(n)K_0(n/X)|=X/(4zeta(2))+O(sqrt X),
    sum_n mu(n)^2 K_0(n/X)^2=X/(60zeta(2))+O(sqrt X). (15)

The second is its POINTWISE squared diagonal. Integrating over a
complete shell dx/x gives X/(60zeta(2))+O(sqrt X).
The full energy retains both ordered off-diagonal orientations:
for this real principal kernel it is the diagonal plus twice the
signed sum over m<n. Absolute convergence on each shell justifies
expansion; no cross term is omitted. The diagonal is not a lower
bound for the full square. For gamma>1/2 its exponent1 is already
below2gamma; the complete cross estimate remains the substantive task.
An energy exponent below1.7497080728 would clear the current numerical
target; the displayed targets .8748,5/6,3/4 ask for1.7496,5/3,3/2.
None of these full signed estimates is proved here.

## G217. Actual-source obstructions and their exact scopes

The companion developments are retained because they rule out specific
repairs without declaring broader approaches exhausted.

First, the higher-arity source is the already known W01/W35/W48-R6
construction. Write a=mu chi,h=chi,m=a1_(n<=U),u=a-m,
q_p=delta_1-p chi(p)delta_p and b_p=q_p*h, with fixed unramified p.
Dirichlet convolution gives, with every zero and repeated prime kept,

    q_p^(k-1)*a=u^k*b_p^(k-1)
      +sum_(j=1)^k(-1)^(j+1)binom(k,j)m^j*q_p^(k-j)*b_p^(j-1). (16)

For fixed k>=2,0<delta<=1,U=X^((1-delta)/k), all short products are
at most X^(1-delta), up to fixed p-shifts. The cofactor series
(1-chi(p)p^(1-s))L(s,chi) is entire. Its fixed Gaussian transform can
be moved to any fixed negative line; the Gaussian dominates vertical
polynomial growth and the finite coefficient counts. This pays all
restoration terms on complete real shells. The j=1 delta-cofactor
term has direct Gaussian decay. No growing-k assertion follows.

For principal chi, products of k distinct unramified primes in
[X^(1/k),2^(1/k)X^(1/k)], excluding p, have hard coefficient exactly
(-1)^k k!. Every long factor must contain one prime, so the cofactor
is1. Fixed-proportion prime counts give order X/log^k X such products,
all on one shell. Their selected same-sign Gaussian field therefore
has linear exponent, including its normalized shell L1/L2 norm.
This blocks paying that proper sector separately; other sectors may
cancel it. Fixed k prime counts follow by partial summation from
[Selberg's PNT, theorem1.1](https://www.math.lsu.edu/~mahlburg/teaching/handouts/2014-7230/Selberg-ElemPNT1949.pdf).
The restriction U>=1 is necessary for the k! coefficient and the
vanishing of lower-degree cells: if delta>1, U<1 and u=a, the hard
source collapses to q_p^(k-1)*a. The raw author's wider claim is
corrected here; the convolution identity itself remains valid.

Second, fixed nonnegative compact smoothing and deletion of finitely
many activity layers do not repair the shrinking zero disk. Fix
continuous compactly supported w>=0 with w(0)>0 and w>=c>0 on some
[a,b],0<a<b. For principal chi modulo fixed q, let

    C_j(X)=sum_(n squarefree,(n,q)=1,omega(n)=j)w(n/X),
    Z_X^[ell](z)=C_0+C_ell z^ell+sum_(j>ell)C_j z^j,

where ell>=1 is fixed; this DELETES layers1,...,ell-1.
We have C_0->w(0)>0, total mass O(X), and, by products of ell
distinct primes in the fixed scaled interval,
C_ell>>X/log^ell X. Unique factorization costs only fixed ell!.
At R=(2C_0/C_ell)^(1/ell), eventually R<1, and

    |C_0+C_ell z^ell|>=C_0 for |z|=R,
    |sum_(j>ell)C_j z^j|<=O(X)R^(ell+1)
       =O(X^(-1/ell)log^(ell+1)X)=o(1).             (17)

Rouche gives exactly ell roots of the COMPLETE polynomial inside R.
All higher degrees are paid together. A scale-independent positive
radius for the logarithm at0 is unavailable. A weight vanishing on
a neighborhood of0 has C_0=0 eventually and no such logarithm at all;
this last observation is not a statement about every w with w(0)=0.
Restoring the original signed endpoint requires the deleted signed
layers; their individual absolute prices have linear exponent, but
their signed sum has not been lower-bounded. Signed or moving weights,
growing ell, exact deflation and another normalized object remain
outside this obstruction. These are activity zeros, not L-function
zeros. G106's sharp-cutoff root and G120/G145's normalization costs
remain the earlier mechanisms, with this specified extension.

The two independent pre-outcome audits add further scope checks.
For A_chi(x)=sum_(n<=x)chi(n)phi(n), every unramified prime p produces
a jump of magnitude p-1. No continuous background can have uniform
error O(x^gamma), gamma<1, on every large real x: left limit and
value at p would give p-1<=2Cp^gamma. The coefficient at1 and the
principal count2A_1(x)-1 are retained. An r-fold Riesz smoothing has
the exact transform L(s-1,chi)/[L(s,chi)s(s+1)...(s+r)], with its
principal terms and numerator nonvanishing still required for a return.
The parity Jordan construction addresses that numerator issue for its
own different source; it does not erase the sharp jump.

For the complete replica audit, on K squarefree q-units let
a_n=mu(n)chi(n). Exactly

    sum_(m<n)|a_m-a_n|^2=K^2-|M_chi(x)|^2.           (18)

Thus the useful estimate is a one-sided LOWER bound near K^2, not
positivity alone. For a simple d-regular graph on these K vertices,
1<=d<=K/2, adjacency A_G, compare
Ltilde=(K/d)(dI-A_G) with Lcomplete=KI-11*. The constant eigenvalue
is d and tr(A_G^2)=Kd, so

    ||Ltilde-Lcomplete||
      >=K sqrt((K-d)/(d(K-1)))>=K/sqrt(2d).          (19)

The source-independent error certificate K times this operator norm
cannot prove error O(x^(2gamma+epsilon)) unless
d>=x^(4-4gamma-2epsilon) up to fixed constants, since K~kappa_q x.
Before small losses the degree exponents are .5005838544 at gamma11,
2/3 at5/6, and1 at3/4. The last excludes every fixed-power sublinear
degree under an every-epsilon target, but not x^(1-o(1)).
This is a limitation of the stated regular-graph uniform certificate,
not a lower bound for its error on the actual Möbius vector or a
claim about weighted/nonregular graphs. A source-specific signed
comparison and the complete one-sided deficit remain open.

## G218. A genuine cofactor average with a fixed zero detector

Let R mean positive integers or nonzero integral ideals of K=Q(omega).
Write q_a=a or N(a). Fix a finite prime set S, tau>0 and one ordinary
Dirichlet character eta or finite-order trivial-infinity Hecke character.
All natural zero primes of the PRESENTED character remain. For the sextic
application S contains the primes above6. Let Q be a finite radical
coprime to S and put

    g(v)=(2*pi*tau)^(-1/2) exp(-v^2/(2tau)),
    U_Q(x)=sum_a mu_R(a)eta(a)1_((a,SQ)=1)g(log(q_a/x)),
    U=U_1.                                                (218.1)

These are complete infinite sums. Norm-Euclidean division in the
triangular lattice makes every Eisenstein ideal principal. The covolume
sqrt(3)/2 and six units give A_K(T)=kappa T+O(sqrt T),
kappa=pi/(3sqrt3); A_Z(T)=T+O(1). The first count remains valid at0<T<1
because the count is zero and T<=sqrt T. In particular A_R(T)<<T for
T>=1, |U_Q(x)|<<x uniformly in Q, and the small-x Gaussian tail is smaller
than every fixed power. No Moebius cancellation is used in these bounds.

Take the exact finite sets

    Fset={f squarefree:F<q_f<=2F,(f,S)=1},
    Eset={e:q_e<=E,(e,S)=1},
    P_FE(x)=(N_F N_E)^(-1)sum_(f,e)U_rad(fe)(x).             (218.2)

Shared f,e primes and every e valuation are allowed. The counts N_F,N_E
are their actual cardinalities, comparable to F,E once the fixed-S
threshold is passed. Freeze F,E throughout each shell. For a radical Q,
write h(Q)=prod_(p|Q)(1-q_p^-1), D(Q)=prod_(p|Q)(1+q_p^-1)^-1 and
S_a(Q)=sum_(d|Q)q_d^-a. Inclusion-exclusion followed by
mu^2(n)=sum_(r^2|n)mu(r) gives, uniformly in Q and for T>=1,

    A_Q^sf(T)=kappa T D(Q)/zeta_K(2)
                  +O(sqrt T log(2T)S_1/2(Q))             [K],
    A_Q^sf(T)=T D(Q)/zeta(2)+O(sqrt T d(Q))               [Z]. (218.3)

Indeed the lattice errors sum to sqrt T S_1/2(Q)sum_(q_r<=sqrt T)q_r^-1;
the omitted main tail is O(sqrt T). The integer floor errors are at most
sqrt T d(Q). The main coefficient uses h(Q)prod_(p|Q)(1-q_p^-2)^-1=D(Q).
There is no Q<=T restriction. The T>=1 qualification corrects the raw
author's tiny-T log(2T) notation; its uses at F,E are unaffected.

The squarefree-f and unrestricted-e avoidance probabilities have main
terms A(a)=prod_(p|a,p notin S)q_p/(q_p+1) and
B(a)=prod_(p|a,p notin S)(q_p-1)/q_p. Division by the EXACT sample counts
retains the same error order. Their errors add when multiplying, since
all four probabilities/main terms lie in[0,1]. Define the ONE fixed field

    W_w(x)=sum_a mu_R(a)eta(a)1_((a,S)=1)w(a)g(log(q_a/x)),
    w_p=(q_p-1)/(q_p+1).                                  (218.4)

Then, uniformly for x>0 and sufficiently large F,E,

    |P_FE-W_w| << x log(2F)(F^-1/2+E^-1/2)                [K],
    |P_FE-W_w| << x(1+log(2+x))(F^-1/2+E^-1)              [Z]. (218.5)

Both source tails are included: sum_(q_a<=T)S_1/2(rad a)<<T follows by
divisor summation and sum_d q_d^-3/2<infinity; the integer analogue is
sum_(n<=T)d(rad n)<<T log(2T). Partial summation against the entire
Gaussian gives(218.5). For x<1, writing L=log(1/x) separates a factor
exp(-L^2/(2tau)), which dominates every required fixed power.

The boundary cases are DIFFERENT fixed sources, not substitutions into
the two-sided limiting density. With e=1, let P_F^sf=N_F^-1 sum_f U_f;
its weight is A_p=q_p/(q_p+1) and its sole error is the F term above.
With f=1 and an unrestricted e average the weight is1-q_p^-1 and its
sole error is the E term. This preserves the unit cofactor explicitly.

For any of these three weights w_p=1-delta_p, delta_p is respectively
2/(q_p+1),1/(q_p+1),1/q_p. On Re s>1, absolute Fubini gives

    Mellin W_w(s)=exp(tau*s^2/2)H_w(s)/L^S(s,eta),
    H_w=prod_(p notin S)(1-w_p z_p)/(1-z_p),
    z_p=eta(p)q_p^-s.                                     (218.6)

Both H_w and its inverse have coefficient series in every l1_sigma,
sigma>0. Their local expansions are

    H_p=1+delta_p sum_(j>=1)z_p^j,
    H_p^-1=1-delta_p sum_(j>=1)w_p^(j-1)z_p^j.

The nonconstant absolute mass is O_sigma(q_p^(-1-sigma)); all local
denominators/numerators are nonzero on that half-plane. The normally
convergent inverse proves global nonvanishing. Eta(p)=0 contributes1.
The full Gaussian convolution identities W_w=h*U and U=h_inv*W_w use
V(x/q_d), with cost sum_d|h(d)|q_d^-sigma in the norm

    ||V||_(sigma,p)=sup_(X>0)X^-sigma||V||_(Lp([X,2X],dx/x)), p=1,2.

Formation is justified at sigma=1 before an unproved smaller exponent is
used. The small shifted scales have already been paid. Thus these FIXED
fields have equal every-epsilon shell exponent classes for gamma>0.

For gamma=1-c in(0,1), an every-epsilon complete shell L1 bound
||P_FE||_1<<X^(gamma+epsilon), with F=X^v,E=X^r fixed across the shell,
returns to W_w when v>=2c and r>=2c over K, or v>=2c and r>=c over Z.
For f-only, v>=2c suffices in both rings. Equality allows the displayed
logarithms through the every-epsilon convention. First pass to the fixed
field, then Mellin transform. Large-shell dyadic summation and the left
Gaussian tail prove normal convergence of all fixed derivatives on
Re s>gamma. The continued identity L^S Mellin W_w=exp(tau*s^2/2)H_w
excludes every zero there; the possible principal pole at1 is preserved.
Finite omitted Euler factors only have zeros on Re s=0.

For an ordinary-family conclusion gamma must be common to every positive
modulus/character, while constants and onsets may depend on the fixed
member. The ideal-field version covers only the stated Hecke family and
does not prove the ordinary premise. No moving cutoff is assigned a fixed
Mellin transform. All these returns need the still-OPEN signed L1 bound.

## G219. Actual principal channels and the cheapest generic price

Use the fixed primary representatives and symbol of
[[restricted research revision] G212-G214](../[private research revision]/sieve-layer-integration.md). On all good ideals,
with original zero extension,

    chi_a(f)^4 chi_a(f^2 e^6)=1_((a,fe)=1).                (219.1)

At a shared prime the left side remains zero; on coprime inputs its total
symbol exponent is divisible by6. Global primary multiplicativity keeps
the unit. This is not an arbitrary insertion of labels into an old source.

For X=Z^N,F=Z^V,E=Z^R form the genuinely NEW coefficient family

    T_fk(x)=X^-1/2 sum_a mu_K(a)eta(a)1_((a,S)=1)
                  chi_a(k)chi_a(f)^4 g(log(q_a/x)).       (219.2)

The non-character coefficients/profile are independent of f,k. They are
not canonical Gauss coefficients, the old physical numerator, or a PR26
source. On k=f^2e^6, T_fk=X^-1/2 U_rad(fe). For fixed f the map e->k is
injective, q_k<=4F^2E^6, and the selected PAIR count is exactly N_F N_E.
Thus, with M=2V+6R,

    B_FE=(N_F N_E)^(-1)sum_(f,e)||U_rad(fe)||_2^2,
    J=F^-1 sum_f sum_(q_k<=4Z^M)||T_fk||_2^2,
    B_FE <= C_S X E^-1 J.                               (219.3)

There is no extra division by F or by the full row count. All row
repetitions remain. Gaussian annuli have polynomial derivative factors
times exp(-c j^2); all length prices grow at most exponentially in|j|.
Minkowski sums the complete profile, including unit/short-source annuli.

Conditional on [restricted research revision]'s NAMED sixth-order and squarefree cubic sieve inputs,
its arbitrary fixed-column proof applies here and gives J<<Z^(Emix+eps),

    Emix(M,N,V)=sup_(0<=t<=M){(M-t)/6+min(C(t,N),t+L)},
    C(t,N)=max(t,N,5t/6+N/3,t/3+5N/6),
    L=max(0,N-V,(2N-V)/3).                              (219.4)

No new external admission or Moebius-specific sieve estimate is asserted.
In particular k=f^2 cannot be substituted BEFORE using a free f-average.
The t=V member gives Emix>=N+(M-V)/6 and hence the recovered upper-bound
PRICE N+Emix-R>=2N+V/6. It cannot certify gamma<1.

For fixed N,V, subtracting R leaves exactly

    Emix(2V+6R,N,V)-R
      =sup_(0<=t<=2V+6R){(2V-t)/6+min(C(t,N),t+L)}.       (219.5)

Only the domain grows with R, so extra e repetitions cannot improve this
recovered certificate. The f-only detector legitimately uses e=1, M=2V,
weight A_p and B_F^sf<=C X J. At N=1 the FULL envelope is

    Emix(2v,1,v)=1+v/6           for0<=v<=1/3,
                 5/6+2v/3       for1/3<=v<=1/2,
                 1/3+5v/3       for1/2<=v<=1,
                 2v            forv>=1.                (219.6)

For v<=1/2, L=1-v: the only extra maximum is t=v with value1+v/6;
compare it with the endpoint C(2v,1). Their crossing is v=1/3. For
v>=1/2 the endpoint gives the remaining two pieces. All pieces increase,
so the least field-admissible choice is v=2c. Its energy price is2+c/3
for c<=1/6, or11/6+4c/3 for1/6<=c<=1/4.

| Target c | Required energy | f-only certificate | Unpaid difference |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
|.12|1.76|2.04|.28|
|conditional .1251459636|1.7497080728|2.0417153212|.2920072484|
|1/6|5/3|37/18|7/18|
|1/4|3/2|13/6|2/3|

The e-only detector has price1+max(5r,1,4r+1/3,r+5/6), r>=2c over K.
It is worse at the tabulated targets, but can be cheaper for sufficiently
small c. F-only is optimal within the squarefree-label branch, not among
all possible detector architectures. These are certificate prices, not
lower bounds on the actual signed source.

A FIXED positive counterexample rejects coefficient-uniform power gains:
replace mu_K(a) by mu_K(a)^2 conjugate(eta(a)). For the lower count use
S+=S union ALL natural-zero primes of the presented character. On this
subset the product with eta is mu_K(a)^2, with no discarded negative term.
For q_Q<=X^A, (218.3), S_1/2(Q)<<q_Q^delta and D(Q)>>q_Q^-delta show
uniformly that there are >>X^(1-eps) good squarefree a in(X,2X]. Choose
delta so the square-root error is below the positive main term. The
Gaussian is bounded below on q_a,x in[X,2X]; consequently the positive
source has B_FE>=X^(2-o(1)) and J>=Z^(N+R-o(1)). The signed average is
also positive. This array satisfies the generic column contract, but is
not actual mu or canonical Gauss data. It rules out only a gain asserted
uniformly for that coefficient class.

## G220. Complete finite covariance and the limiting-bank alternative

For a fixed finite Q coprime to S, coefficientwise Euler factors give

    U_Q(x)=sum_(d Q-smooth)eta(d)U(x/q_d),
    U(x)=sum_(d|Q)mu(d)eta(d)U_Q(x/q_d).                   (220.1)

Both are complete absolutely formed Gaussian identities. For every
sigma,delta>0, prod_(p|Q)(1-q_p^-sigma)^-1<<q_Q^delta: split off finitely
many small primes and bound each remaining factor by q_p^delta. Thus
an all-shell exponent gamma>0 for U implies the same exponent uniformly
for polynomial-size Q, with arbitrarily small extra loss and small
shifted scales retained. Conversely, Jensen, (218.5) and the fixed Euler
inverse recover U from a complete positive-bank L2 bound, when the FIELD
error gate is paid. Hence those bank and U shell-L2 exponent classes are
equivalent. This does not identify L1 with L2.

For f-only let p_F(d)=N_F^-1#{f in Fset:(f,d)=1},
K_X(a,b)=integral_X^(2X)g(log(q_a/x))g(log(q_b/x))dx/x and
c_a=mu_R(a)eta(a)1_((a,S)=1). The exact finite bank is

    B_F^sf=sum_(a,b)c_a conjugate(c_b)K_X(a,b)p_F(rad(ab)). (220.2)

The squared averaged FIELD instead has kernel p_F(a)p_F(b). These
kernels differ by the entire label covariance. No independent-prime
model is used at finite F. On the actual squarefree coefficient support,

    A(rad(ab))=A(a)A(b)sum_(d|gcd(a,b))q_d^-1.

Therefore the limiting bank has the exact positive feature expansion

    B_infty(X)=sum_(d squarefree,(d,S)=1)q_d^-1 ||V_d||_2^2,
    V_d(x)=sum_(d|a)c_a A(a)g(log(q_a/x)).                (220.3)

The d=1 term is ||W_A||_2^2, and all other terms are the full limiting
label variance. Absolute Gaussian majorants justify every rearrangement:
after the divisor expansion the absolute factor is A(rad(ab))<=1.

Replacing the FINITE kernel by this limit costs

    |B_F^sf-B_infty| << X^2 F^-1/2 log(2F)              [K],
    |B_F^sf-B_infty| << X^2 F^-1/2(1+log(2+X))^2        [Z]. (220.4)

Indeed the avoidance-probability error at rad(ab) is bounded by the
product of its separate divisor majorants, and each Gaussian sum is
O(x), or O(x log(2+x)) over Z. Thus this ENERGY replacement needs v>=4c
at exponent2-2c, whereas the FIELD comparison only needs v>=2c. Keeping
(220.2) exact avoids this extra approximation.

There is also a fully paid DIRECT limiting-bank return. If W_A has an
all-shell L2 exponent sigma>0, remove the primes of d from its weighted
Euler product. The inverse factors are(1-A_p eta(p)q_p^-s)^-1, whose
l1_sigma cost is at most C_(sigma,delta)q_d^delta. For squarefree d,

    V_d(x)=mu(d)eta(d)A(d)W_(A,d)(x/q_d).

Hence for any0<delta<sigma,

    B_infty(X) <= C ||W_A||_(sigma,2)^2 X^(2sigma)
                    sum_d q_d^(-1-2sigma+2delta).        (220.5)

The sum converges by A_R(T)<<T, and every d and small shifted scale is
included. Conversely B_infty>=||W_A||_2^2, followed by the fixed inverse
in G218. Thus B_infty and U have the same every-epsilon L2 exponent class
for gamma>0. Estimating B_infty directly would need no finite-F limit
error, but its ENTIRE infinite hole family must then be paid. This
corollary does not permit substituting a finite-bank bound without(220.4),
and supplies no arithmetic saving. It leaves the exact signed finite
field/Gram and the direct limiting bank as distinct lawful targets.

## G221. The user's quaternion identity on the actual Jordan source

Retain G215-G216's fixed ordinary chi, parity-matched r>=2, fixed m,
complete filtered error E_m and lambda=2^(r+1). Put A_X=E_m(X),
B_X=E_m(X/2). In the user's convention jz=conjugate(z)j,

    (A_X+B_X j)(1+lambda j)=Phi(X)+Psi(X)j,
    Phi=A_X-lambda B_X, Psi=lambda A_X+B_X,
    |Phi|^2+|Psi|^2=(1+lambda^2)(|A_X|^2+|B_X|^2).         (221.1)

The multiplier coefficients are real, so this applies to complex chi
without a conjugation or chi(2) error, including2|q. The companion source
is explicit: if E_m=sum mu(n)chi(n)H(n/X), then
Psi=sum mu(n)chi(n)[lambda H(n/X)+H(2n/X)]. Every principal algebraic
tail, coefficient zero and divisor remains.

A lower bound for the COMPLETE companion energy within
Ceps X^(2gamma+eps) of(1+lambda^2)(||E_m||_2^2+||D E_m||_2^2) is exactly
the desired upper bound for||Phi||_2^2. With alpha=||E_m||_2,
beta=lambda||D E_m||_2 and rho the normalized real inner product, its
deficit is(alpha-beta)^2+2alpha beta(1-rho); zero-norm cases use(221.1).
Both amplitude mismatch and full signed correlation must be estimated.
Positivity provides no upper saving for this deficit.

The complete future inverse is

    E_m(X)=-sum_(j>=1)lambda^-j Phi(2^j X),
    remainder O(X 2^(-Jr)).                              (221.2)

G216's actual O(X) bound pays the remainder and excludes the homogeneous
X^(r+1) solution. For shell Lp(dx/x), p=1,2 and exponent beta<r+1, the
recovery cost is1/(2^(r+1-beta)-1). Finite shifts give the converse, so
the complete two-channel bank preserves the Phi exponent class. Using
uncentered F instead introduces a principal squared scale X^(2r+2)
and requires correspondingly sharper relative deficit precision.

A stronger obstruction than constant-embedding isometry holds on the
ACTUAL full or retained-middle Jordan source. Let w_n=|mu(n)chi(n)K(n/X)|,
xi_n=mu(n)chi(n)K(n/X)/w_n when nonzero. Encode it as w_n v_n with
v_n=xi_n+t_n j and N(v_n)<=C^2, C fixed. The first channel is exactly
the original scalar source. Its pointwise absolute Gram price is

    B_+=sum_(d,e)w_d w_e |Re(v_d conjugate(v_e))|
          >=(sum_n w_n)^2/(4C^2).                       (221.3)

Proof: S=sum_n w_n v_n v_n^T is a positive real4x4 matrix, trace S>=W,
trace(S^2)>=(trace S)^2/4, and each |v_d dot v_e|<=C^2. Finite truncation
and monotone convergence cover the whole source. G216 gives
W=kappa_q X integral|K|+O(sqrt X), with positive leading constant.
The paid low/far absolute mass is O(X^gamma)+O(X^-1), so the SAME linear
mass remains in the exact middle. Therefore B_+ costs X^2 for both.
For q1/r2/m0 its lower constant is1/(64C^2 zeta(2)^2), while the
diagonal is at most C^2[X/(60zeta(2))+O(sqrt X)]. This also forces a
quadratic absolute off-diagonal price, not a signed-energy lower bound.

More generally, real dimension d, readout norm L and lift norm<=C give
L^2 B_+>=W^2/[d(CL)^2]. A bound of exponent2gamma would need
d(CL)^2 at least X^(2-2gamma-eps), up to constants. Reciprocal rescaling
does not change CL. This excludes only that POINTWISE absolute-Gram
certificate. Collective signed companion estimates, absolute values
after integration, or a fully paid changing dimension/readout remain open.
The full automorphic spinor function space is not four-dimensional.

The arithmetic/analytic escape conditions also stay explicit. Prime
images of a coprime-multiplicative quaternion lift commute and occupy
one complex slice, unless all are real; the commutator is twice the
cross product of imaginary parts. Ordered prime words need a new scalar
return. Even commuting quaternion coefficients need not commute with
n^-s in the chosen complex plane: (j2^-s)(j3^-s)=-2^-conjugate(s)3^-s,
generically different from-6^-s. A lawful holomorphic matrix series
uses CENTRAL complex n^-s and reflected coefficient functions, with
determinant Z(s)Z#(s)+W(s)W#(s), not a positive norm at generic height.
These distinctions do not obstruct pointwise real-scale energy identities.

The existing sixth-order SU(2) compact factor is exactly the user's
M(t conjugate(d)-t conjugate(c)j), with norm1. Its Iwasawa extraction is
not automatically an arithmetic group homomorphism. S44's earlier
phase-embedding seed remains an untested precursor, not a disproved idea.
The [[restricted research revision] intake](../[private research revision]/quaternion-norm-intake.md) records that prior
overlap and the elementary conventions. The new full calculation here
does not transfer a Jordan bound to a Gaussian/Hecke norm without a proof.

## G222. Exact prime-deletion inversion and the full signed readout

Fix an ordinary Dirichlet character chi modulo q and real X>=1. Let D_X
be the squarefree q-units n<=X, including1. It is a divisor downset.
For each unramified prime choose0<rho_p<=1, lambda_p=1-rho_p,
R_p=(2-rho_p)/rho_p. With row d and column n in D_X, define

    B(d,n)=1_(d|n) prod_(p|d)rho_p prod_(p|n/d)lambda_p,
    C(d,n)=1_(d|n) prod_(p|n)rho_p^-1 prod_(p|n/d)(-lambda_p).
                                                               (222.1)

Empty products and0^0 are1. Every intermediate divisor e between d,n
remains in D_X. Expanding BC or CB factors over primes of n/d, giving
the cancellation(lambda_p-lambda_p) at each missing prime and diagonal1.
Consequently both products equal the identity. Absolute column sums give

    ||B||_(1->1)=1,
    V(X):=||C||_(1->1)=max_(n in D_X) prod_(p|n)R_p.          (222.2)

For uniform fixed rho, V=R^K_X, K_X=max_D omega(n). The factorial bound
n>=(omega(n)+1)! implies K_X<=(1+o(1))log X/loglog X, so V=X^o(1).
The size downset is essential: a full prime cube would give the wrong
exponential price. Uniform moving rho_X=(log X)^-b instead costs
X^(b+o(1)); the matching lower factor count follows from primorials and
the ordinary [prime number theorem](https://dlmf.nist.gov/27.12).

For a FIXED prime-dependent sequence, the exact criterion is

    V(X)=X^o(1) iff log R_p/log p ->0.                       (222.3)

Necessity uses the column n=p at X=p. For sufficiency, given epsilon>0
choose P with R_p<=p^epsilon for p>P. Then the product is at most
[prod_(p<=P,p not|q)R_p]n^epsilon. The constant is independent of X.
Thus rho_p=min(1,(log p)^-b), b>0, may tend to0 while inversion remains
subpower. This is different from assigning the SAME rho_X to all primes.
For arbitrary X-dependent choices, the maximum in(222.2), not(222.3),
is the bill. No prime theorem is needed for the fixed-sequence criterion.

Apply B to nu(n)=chi(n) on D_X. The actual output and observer are

    b_X(d)=chi(d)prod_(p|d)rho_p
      *sum_(m<=X/d,(m,dq)=1)mu(m)^2 chi(m)prod_(p|m)lambda_p,
    h(d)=prod_(p|d)(-R_p),
    M_chi(X)=sum_(d in D_X)h(d)b_X(d).                       (222.4)

The cofactor phase chi(m), every natural zero, unit and cutoff remain.
Indeed summing over d|n gives prod_(p|n)(lambda_p-rho_p R_p)=mu(n).
The readout is bilinear, without a conjugation. For ANY full approximant
btilde_X, with e_X=b_X-btilde_X, one has

    |M_chi(X)|<=|sum_d h(d)btilde_X(d)|+V(X)||e_X||_1.       (222.5)

Under(222.3), complete every-epsilon bounds at exponent gamma for BOTH
right-hand quantities before the subpower loss give the same exponent
for M. Under a moving inverse cost X^b, the residual must pay b.
A selected label or omitted error does not have this return. No such
arithmetic approximation has been constructed here.

For one common gamma in(0,1) and every fixed ordinary character, this
Mertens estimate continues s int_1^infinity M_chi(x)x^(-s-1)dx=1/L(s,chi)
normally to Re s>gamma after an epsilon buffer. The continued identity
LF=1 excludes all regular zeros at every finite height. The principal
pole at1 becomes a reciprocal zero; imprimitive zeros and modulus
conventions remain those of [DLMF25.15](https://dlmf.nist.gov/25.15).
Constants and onsets may depend on the fixed character. No growing-q
uniformity or native Eisenstein-source transfer follows.

The inverse is affordable, but positive readout certificates fail in an
exact broader sense. For principal chi, b_X(d)>0, even when some rho_p=1,
because n=d contributes. For ANY moving retentions and positive diagonal
weights w_d,

    P_abs=sum_d |h(d)|b_X(d)
       =sum_(n in D_X)prod_(p|n)(3-2rho_p),
    #D_X<=P_abs<=3^K_X #D_X=X^(1+o(1)),
    ||w h||_2 ||b_X/w||_2>=P_abs.                          (222.6)

The minimum is attained by w_d^2=b_X(d)/|h(d)|. The same lower bound
holds for any conjugate Holder pair. The fixed-q squarefree count
#D_X=kappa_q X+O_q(sqrt X), kappa_q=(phi(q)/q)prod_(p not|q)(1-p^-2)>0,
follows by expanding mu^2 and counting q-units; it needs no PNT.
Thus arbitrary adaptive diagonal weights cannot make this principal
separable certificate power-small. This does not bound the signed readout
from below or exclude nonlocal signed norms or growing signed centering.

Uniform rho also gives the exact cutoff polynomial

    P_X(z)=sum_d b_X(d)z^omega(d)=Z_X(lambda+rho z),
    Z_X(z)=sum_(n in D_X)chi(n)z^omega(n), P_X(-R)=M_chi(X).
                                                               (222.7)

Its circle evaluation costs at most sqrt(sum_(j<=K_X)R^(2j)), subpower
for fixed rho. For principal chi all coefficients are nonnegative and
the prime layer has beta_0+beta_1>=pi_q(X), hence ||P_X||_circle>=pi_q(X)/sqrt2.
Deleting every original degree<=r, for fixed r, does not fix that norm:
products of r+1 distinct primes in((X/2)^(1/(r+1)),X^(1/(r+1))] supply
at least const X/log(X)^(r+1) mass in r+2 nonnegative coefficients.
Their l2 norm is at least mass/sqrt(r+2), uniformly in moving retention.
Other original layers only increase coefficients. This is a norm
obstruction, not an alternating-sum lower bound; signed quotient and
growing-layer methods survive. With varying rho_p there is generally no
single scalar z representing h: retain the labeled/multivariate readout.

## G223. Critical small-prime payment with its exact margin debit

Use the complete ordinary-character source of
[G173](../[private research revision]/wild62-integration.md): fixed tau>0,1/2<gamma<1,

    a(n)=mu(n)chi(n), g(v)=(2*pi*tau)^-1/2 exp(-v^2/(2tau)),
    U(y)=sum_(n>=1)a(n)g(log n-y), z(y)=e^(-gamma y)U(y),
    I_R=int_0^R y|z|^2, E_R=int_0^R |z|^2.

The coefficient identity a(n)log n=-sum_(d|n)chi(d)Lambda(d)a(n/d)
retains ALL prime powers, including cancellation at squareful n. It gives

    tau z'+(y+tau gamma)z+K1 z+K2 z=0,
    K1 z(y)=sum_p chi(p)log p p^-gamma z(y-log p),
    (tau/2)(|z(R)|^2-|z(0)|^2)+I_R+tau gamma E_R=Q1+Q2,
    Qj=-Re int_0^R conjugate(z)Kj z.                         (223.1)

G173 pays |Q2|<=eta I_R+B_eta for every eta>0 by its summable j>=2
coefficient norm, the complete Gaussian past and a fixed initial interval.
No unknown future bound is used. The same-output prime diagonal is
nonnegative and O(1): its coefficient is1 precisely at squarefree
q-units n=pm, the prime log-weights sum to at most log n, and

    int_R e^(-2gamma y)g(log n-y)^2dy
      =e^(tau gamma^2)n^(-2gamma)/(2sqrt(pi*tau)).

Here is a larger paid small-prime region. Fix a0>0 and set

    b=1/(1-gamma), Y(y)=a0(1+y)^b,
    kappa=a0^(1-gamma)/(1-gamma).

Assign equality to p<=Y(y). PNT and partial summation give
S_gamma(t)=sum_(p<=t)log p p^-gamma~t^(1-gamma)/(1-gamma).
The row sum is(kappa+o(1))y. Apply2|z(y)z(y-log p)|<=|z(y)|^2+|z(y-log p)|^2.
For the column put v=y-log p; the mask gives log p=O(log y), so for
any epsilon>0 and all large y, y<=v/(1-epsilon). Its column sum is at
most S_gamma(a0(1+v/(1-epsilon))^b)<=(kappa/(1-epsilon)+o(1))v.
Both half factors are present. The bounded initial region has finitely
many primes and a fixed bounded source interval. Therefore

    |Q_small(R)|<=(kappa+eta)I_R+B_eta, every R>=0.          (223.2)

The elementary theta(t)<=4(log2)t instead gives4(log2)kappa. This
critical mask is larger than G173's logarithmically reduced mask, but
its nonzero debit must be retained; it does not inherit the old zero
relative price or an unproved hard estimate for another mask.

Let H_a0,R be the ENTIRE p>Y(y), n!=pm expansion with literal summand

    -Re[conjugate(a(n))chi(p)a(m)] log p e^(-2gamma y)
                 *g(log n-y)g(log(pm)-y),                  (223.3)

integrated over0<=y<=R, all m,n>=1. Gaussian majorants justify the
compact-interval sums; diagonal and every complementary source remain.
If THIS jointly chosen mask has constants delta>kappa,B_chi,R0_chi with

    H_a0,R<=(1-delta)I_R+B_chi, every R>=R0_chi,             (223.4)

then pay eta=(delta-kappa)/4 in(223.2) and the higher powers to obtain

    (tau/2)|z(R)|^2+((delta-kappa)/2)I_R+tau gamma E_R<=B'.  (223.5)

Thus U(y)=O_chi(e^(gamma y)). Its complete bilateral transform equals
e^(tau s^2/2)/L(s,chi) initially on Re s>1 and continues normally to
Re s>gamma; the numerator never vanishes. This excludes every zero
at every finite height there, preserves the principal pole and all
natural zeros, and assumes no height-uniform numerator lower bound.
Gamma is common across the family; a0,delta and constants may depend
on a fixed character. This is a one-way ordinary-source return.

Choosing a0=[delta(1-gamma)/2]^(1/(1-gamma)) spends kappa=delta/2;
it does NOT manufacture the margin for the resulting mask. The targets
c=.12,.12515,1/6,1/4 require gamma=.88,.87485,5/6,3/4 and critical powers
25/3,20000/2503,6,4. The .12515 target exceeds conditional c11 by.0000040364.
None of the corresponding complete inequalities(223.4) is proved.

The generic leading coefficient is sharp even for a one-sided form.
For principal chi take arbitrary test input
f_T(y)=exp(i*pi*y/log Y_T)1_[T,T+sqrt T], Y_T=a0(1+T)^b.
Delays lose only O(log T/sqrt T) relative overlap, Y(y)/Y_T->1 uniformly,
and prime-weight mass below Y_T^(1-epsilon) is negligible. On the rest
the real phase tends to-1 as T then epsilon tend to their limits. Hence
-Re<f_T,K_small f_T>/int y|f_T|^2->kappa. A supercritical fixed power b'
instead gives asymptotic kappa T^(b'(1-gamma)-1), which diverges.
These are arbitrary inputs, not the actual z, and do not lower-bound its
signed form. Even granting |U(y)|<=C e^(beta y), gamma<beta<1, the
coarse absolute full-prime price has exponent1+beta-2gamma against
2beta-2gamma for I_R: the missing saving remains1-beta.
title: G223. Critical small-prime payment with its exact margin debit
