## G224. Exact chirp and paired-character audits, with reconstruction paid

The two independent unselected audits preserve useful alternatives and
their exact limits. For z=a-i kappa, a>0, the analytic square root gives

    sqrt(z/(2*pi)) exp(t^2/(2z))
       *int_R exp(-z u^2/2+i t u)du=1,
    P_z(t)=(|z|/a)^1/2 exp(a t^2/(2|z|^2)).                 (224.1)

The first identity follows by the Gaussian Fourier integral and normal
continuation on Re z>0. The second is its exact completely absolute
price. On |t|<=T set E=a T^2/(2|z|^2)>0,
C=|kappa|T^2/(2|z|^2). Then P_z(T)=(1+(C/E)^2)^1/4 e^E
>=sqrt(C)e^E/sqrt(E)>=sqrt(2e C). A power-sized exterior chirp C=X^delta
therefore costs at least X^(delta/2) under absolute payment. Finite
insertion is legitimate; infinite insertion must pay its exterior
exponential against the original full tail. Signed/L2 use remains open.

For odd prime Q, A nonzero mod Q, c=(4A)^-1 and
G_A=sum_v e_Q(A v^2), completing the square gives
sum_v e_Q(A v^2+t v)=G_A e_Q(-c t^2), |G_A|^2=Q.
For actual residue sums B_r and F_v=sum_r B_r e_Q(c r^2+v r),

    S=sum_r B_r=G_A^-1 sum_v e_Q(A v^2)F_v,
    sum_v |F_v|^2=Q sum_r |B_r|^2,
    |S|^2=Q^-1 sum_(v,w)e_Q(A(v^2-w^2))F_v conjugate(F_w).
                                                               (224.2)

All crosses and natural zeros remain. The Cauchy bound |S|^2<=sum_v|F_v|^2
is generically sharp: B_r=1 gives equality Q^2. That is an ambient
coherent example, not a claim about the actual arithmetic residue array.
The four-point curvature of one bilinear t=mn channel has phase
c(m^2-m'^2)(n^2-n'^2)+v(m-m')(n-n'); complete channel recombination
restores multiplier1. A selected curved channel is not a full estimate.

The other audit distinguishes conjugate heights and observation loss.
F_barchi(s)=conjugate(F_chi(conjugate(s))) for F=1/L. A pole at rho maps
to conjugate(rho), not necessarily rho. For a Laurent vector with leading
coefficient v and continuous observation A(s), the leading squared signal
is v* A(rho)* A(rho) v. Positive semidefiniteness alone can annihilate v;
one needs coverage of actual residue directions, or a uniform lower
singular-value bound. A complete bank must keep every associated source.

At real x, the actual pair satisfies
||(M_chi(x),M_barchi(x))||^2=2|M_chi(x)|^2. This also holds with common
REAL weights; complex weights and heights must be conjugated as well.
A full every-epsilon shell-L1 pair estimate has the ordinary all-height
Abel return in G222, but is exactly the scalar estimate up to sqrt2.
The difference observation for a real character is identically zero.
Degenerating coordinate changes must pay their inverse. These adapters
preserve existing detector/curvature ancestry and supply no exponent gain.

The author's other selected tests retain the complete asymmetric
hyperbola identity u_U*u_V*chi=a-m_U-m_V+m_U*m_V*chi. Its principal
absolute long-long tuple price is at least const X when U,V<=sqrt X/2,
by pairs of squarefree q-units in(sqrt X/2,sqrt X]. This is not a signed
corner lower bound. Exterior-boundary and least-prime matching tests
duplicate G164-G165: the outgoing boundary remains, critical coordinates
need not be harmonic, and the matched character bulk a(n)(1-chi(p))
cannot be discarded outside the principal case. Their failures and all
22 untested cards are retained without broad rejection of the mechanisms.
title: G224. Exact chirp and paired-character audits, with reconstruction paid

## G225. Actual positive cofactor-hole prices, including after integration

Use the full G218 Gaussian over integers or Eisenstein integral ideals,
q_a=a or Na, with fixed eta,tau,S. Put c_a=mu_R(a)eta(a)1_((a,S)=1).
Let S+ add ALL natural-zero primes of the PRESENTED character, including
imprimitive modulus primes. On each entire shell[X,2X], choose arbitrary
nonnegative theta_Q with sum1 on radicals coprime to S, q_Q<=X^A,
fixed A>0. The choices may depend on X and the actual arithmetic source,
but are frozen in x. Define

    p(a)=sum_Q theta_Q 1_((a,Q)=1),
    K_X(a,b)=int_X^(2X)g(log(q_a/x))g(log(q_b/x))dx/x,
    A_theta=sum_(a,b)|Re(c_a conjugate(c_b))|K_X(a,b)p(rad(ab)),
    B_theta=sum_(a,b)|Re(c_a conjugate(c_b))|K_X(a,b)p(a)p(b).
                                                               (225.1)

The first is the average absolute-real Gram price of each hole field;
the second is that price for their averaged field. Both include diagonal
and both off-diagonal orientations. They are not the signed energies.

Uniformly over this entire family,

    X^2/log(2X)^2 << A_theta, B_theta << X^2.                (225.2)

Constants/onsets depend on R,S,eta,tau,A, not theta or Q. The lower bound
survives diagonal removal. This is a corollary of the G218 count and
G221 real-rank bound with a useful logarithmic refinement.

For Q*=rad(S+ Q), D(Q*)=prod_(p|Q*)(1+q_p^-1)^-1 satisfies

    D(Q*)^-1=sum_(d|Q*)q_d^-1
       <=sum_(q_d<=q_Q*)q_d^-1 << log(2q_Q*) << log(2X).

Partial summation of the elementary A_R(T)<<T proves this without PNT.
Subtract the uniform G218 squarefree counts at2X and X. The errors
are O(sqrt X log(2X)S_1/2(Q*)) over ideals and O(sqrt X d(Q*)) over
integers. The elementary small/large-prime split gives each factor sum
<<_delta q_Q*^delta; take delta=1/(4A). Thus errors are
O(X^(3/4)log(2X)), smaller than the main X/log(2X). No Q<=X
restriction is needed. Since g has a positive minimum on[-log2,log2],

    W_Q(x)=sum_a |c_a|1_((a,Q)=1)g(log(q_a/x))
       >>X/log(2X), every x in[X,2X],                     (225.3)

while the complete Gaussian majorant gives W_Q(x)<<x. No character
zero is replaced by a unit phase.

Regard xi_a=c_a/|c_a| as a unit vector in R^2 on its nonzero support.
With positive weights w_a, let M=sum_a w_a xi_a xi_a^T and W=sum_a w_a.
Then

    sum_(a,b)w_a w_b |xi_a dot xi_b|
      >=trace(M^2)>=W^2/2.                               (225.4)

The first step uses |t|>=t^2 on[-1,1]; the second uses two nonnegative
eigenvalues. All ACTUAL Mobius signs and character phases remain.
Apply it first to w_a=|c_a|1_((a,Q)=1)g, average theta and integrate.
Apply it separately to w_a=|c_a|p(a)g, whose mass is sum theta_Q W_Q.
These prove both lower bounds without comparing their kernels. For real
eta the constant1/2 can be1. Truncation, nonnegative convergence and the
Gaussian O(x) majorant justify every infinite sum and the O(X^2) upper bound.

The diagonals are sum_a |c_a|^2 K_X(a,a)p(a) and the same with p(a)^2.
Both are O(X), since0<=p<=1 and the squared Gaussian is a constant times
a narrower Gaussian. Subtracting them preserves(225.2) for large X.
The covariance kernels are not ordered entrywise: theta_1=theta_lm=1/2
gives joint/product1/2,1/4 at a=l,b=m, whereas theta_l=theta_m=1/2
gives0,1/4, for two distinct good primes and sufficiently large X.

For each pair the phase is independent of x and K_X is positive, so
int |Re(c_a conjugate(c_b))|g_a g_b dx/x
=|Re(c_a conjugate(c_b))K_X(a,b)| exactly. Hence taking pairwise real
absolute values AFTER integration gives the same scalar Gaussian price.
This identity does not discard cancellation in a collective signed sum,
extend to oscillatory joint-label kernels, or certify an arbitrary theta
as a zero detector. The latter needs its own complete fixed-source return.
G222's principal deletion-channel Holder floor and G127's different
curved-source obstruction retain their distinct priority and scope.
title: G225. Actual positive cofactor-hole prices, including after integration

statement:
## G226. A dimension-free obstruction after paying a common linear readout

This develops the user's quaternion proposal beyond the G221 bounded
rank-four argument. Root's [discovery and initial proof](linear-readout/root-draft.md)
tested growing dimension and delayed absolute values as possible escapes.
The [independent review](linear-readout/review.md) sharpened the initial
constant4/pi^2 to the sharp1/2 and clarified the complex-kernel and
variable-readout scopes. The earlier argument remains historical evidence.

Let H be ANY real Hilbert space, T:H->R^2 a bounded real-linear map with
norm L, and(v_a) a finite family. Define y_a=T v_a,
M=sum_a|y_a| and B=sum_(a,b)|<v_a,v_b>|, with all ordered pairs. Then

    L^2 B >= M^2/2.                                      (226.1)

No dimension or upper bound on individual vectors appears. To prove it,
let u_a=y_a/|y_a| when y_a!=0 and u_a=0 otherwise. Define A:R^2->H by
A e_j=sum_a u_(a,j)v_a. Its Hilbert-Schmidt norm satisfies

    ||A||_HS^2=sum_(a,b)<v_a,v_b><u_a,u_b><=B,
    TA=sum_a |y_a|u_a u_a^T,
    M^2/2<=trace((TA)^2)=||TA||_HS^2<=L^2||A||_HS^2.

The positive2x2 operator has trace M and squared eigenvalue sum at least
M^2/2. This proves(226.1). Equality occurs for
T=identity on R^2, v_1=e_1,v_2=e_2. If all images lie on one real line,
the constant improves to1. More generally a target R^r gives the sharp
constant1/r, depending on OUTPUT dimension rather than lift dimension.
This is not the false termwise inequality
|<Tv_a,Tv_b>|<=L^2|<v_a,v_b>|.

Separate maps per index do not meet this hypothesis: v_i=e_i in R^n,
T_i(v)=v_i gives B=n, M=n and separate norms1. The COMMON recovery
v->sum_i v_i has norm sqrt(n), restoring the missing bill.

For an infinite family, apply(226.1) to every finite subset and take
nonnegative limits. No convergence of an infinite vector sum is needed
for this extended inequality. Each vector and readout must still exist.
The result includes arbitrary dimension, additional quaternion components,
and X-dependent choices of the common map, once its norm is paid.

Pointwise, if T_x v_a(x)=c_a K(q_a/x), then

    L_x^2 sum_(a,b)|<v_a(x),v_b(x)>|
       >=(1/2)[sum_a|c_a K(q_a/x)|]^2.                    (226.2)

For the G221 quaternion lift w_a(xi_a+t_a j), first-complex-coordinate
projection has L_x=1. Thus the actual full/middle source has quadratic
pointwise absolute price even WITHOUT a bound on t_a. The old necessary
dimension/readout tradeoff remains valid but is weaker: growing the
dimension does not reduce the price after a common linear recovery is paid.

There is a corresponding after-integration theorem. Put I=[X,2X],
measure dx/x and length ell=log2. Let v_a belong to its direct-integral
real Hilbert space, and let T_x be measurable common recovery maps with
essential supremum norm L_X<infinity on the shell. Assume

    T_x v_a(x)=c_a K(q_a/x),
    J(t)=int_1^2 K(t/u)du/u.

The common map Tcal(v)=int_I T_x v(x)dx/x has norm at most L_X sqrt(ell)
and sends v_a to c_a J(q_a/X). Apply(226.1) in the direct integral:

    L_X^2 ell sum_(a,b)|int_I <v_a(x),v_b(x)>dx/x|
       >=(1/2)[sum_a |c_a J(q_a/X)|]^2.                  (226.3)

All absolute values on the left are AFTER pair integration. A fixed
common ambient H is sufficient; measurable Hilbert bundles also work
when the stated direct integral and maps are well defined. It suffices
to apply the argument to finite central subsets; infinite absolute prices
then dominate those finite ones. Arbitrary x-dependent lifts are allowed.

The variable bound int_I ||T_x||^2 dx/x also bounds Tcal's squared norm,
but it does NOT automatically pay full shell-L2 reconstruction. For the
actual source-energy certificate the uniform L_X above is sufficient:
||sum_a T_x v_a||_(L2)^2<=L_X^2||sum_a v_a||_(L2(H))^2<=L_X^2 B_after
when the sums/convergence required for that upper estimate are justified.
If no such finite reconstruction bill is available, do not claim a
source upper bound from the averaged-functional inequality alone.

The right side has quadratic order for the exact Jordan source, including
its retained middle. Its fixed kernel is generally COMPLEX for nonreal
chi, and G215 gives K(t)=e^-t+O(e^-2t), so K is continuous, nonzero and
tends to0 at infinity. More generally these three properties imply J is
not identically zero: in logarithmic coordinates J'=K(t)-K(t/2); J=0
would force K(t)=K(2t), hence K=0 by repeated scaling to infinity.
Choose a fixed interval[a,b] in(0,infinity) on which |J|>=k>0. The
fixed-q squarefree count gives

    sum_(d>=1)|mu(d)chi(d)J(d/X)| >>_(q,K) X.              (226.4)

For G215's middle, d in[aX,bX] lies in x^alpha<d<=2x log x for EVERY
x in[X,2X] once X is large, because alpha<1. Thus these central vectors
have exactly the same integrated image c_d J(d/X); they alone prove the
same lower bound in(226.3). No omitted tail, principal main term or
varying-cutoff identity has been discarded. The actual compensated K,
not the uncentered Jordan source, is used.

For the G218 Gaussian, positivity directly gives |J(t)| bounded below
on[1,2]. Fixed holes give mass >>X; polynomial-sized holes, or their
positive normalized field averages, give >>X/log(2X) by G225, with all
presented character zeros retained. Applying(226.3) separately to each
hole also permits a positive average of its complete lifted price.
No arbitrary oscillatory joint-label kernel is identified with that
positive-mask construction.

These are TOTAL-price lower bounds. To conclude the same for the absolute
off-diagonal, also pay the diagonal. In G221's bounded lifts with fixed
C, sum_a int_I ||v_a||^2=O(C^2 X), so the quadratic lower bound survives
its removal. Without such a bound an unbounded lift may move the bill
onto its diagonal; no off-diagonal assertion is then made.

The complete returned shell-L2 target gamma=1-c requires energy exponent
2-2c. The paid source-index absolute-Gram price above has exponent at
least2, leaving deficit2c: .24 at c=.12, .2502919272 at conditional c11,
.25030 at c=.12515,1/3 at c=1/6 and1/2 at c=1/4. G215/G218 supply their
own L2-to-L1 and all-height returns; the price theorem proves none of
the necessary signed estimates and imports no cross-family transfer.

The scope matters: one vector per actual source coefficient, a common

Cancellation inside blocks before the absolute value, full signed
companion comparisons, nonlinear reconstruction, or genuinely different

not a lower bound on the actual signed source energy. It strengthens

## G227. An actual twisted inverse and its cofactor-resolved observation

Fix an ordinary Dirichlet character chi modulo a fixed positive integer q.
Let S_N={a<=N: a squarefree, (a,q)=1}, ordered increasingly, with N>=1 an
integer. Write E_ad=1_(d|a) and M=diag(mu(a)). Every divisor interval of S_N
is complete, so finite Mobius inversion gives E^-1=M E M. With

    A_chi=E diag(mu(d) conjugate(chi(d))) E^T,
    (A_chi)_ab=prod_(p|(a,b))(1-conjugate(chi(p))),

the diagonal is invertible because |chi(d)|=1 on the actual labels. Therefore

    (A_chi^-1)_ab=mu(a)mu(b)
                   sum_(d in S_N,[a,b]|d)mu(d)chi(d).       (227.1)

The pairing and transpose are bilinear. A_chi is generally complex symmetric,
not Hermitian. Its (1,1) inverse entry is exactly M_chi(N)=sum_(n<=N)mu(n)chi(n).
Simply phase-gauging the real coprimality matrix would leave that observed
inverse entry untwisted, so it does not establish (227.1).

Put g=(a,b), l=[a,b]. Writing d=lm in (227.1), squarefreeness forces (m,l)=1,
and mu(a)mu(b)mu(l)=mu(g). Hence

    (A_chi^-1)_ab=mu(g)chi(l) M_(chi,lq)(N/l),
    M_(chi,h)(y)=sum_(m<=y,(m,h)=1)mu(m)chi(m).             (227.2)

This is zero for l>N. In particular the first inverse row and complete
residual identity, for ANY proposed column z and r=e1-A_chi z, are

    R_N(a)=chi(a) M_(chi,aq)(N/a),  |R_N(a)|<=floor(N/a),
    M_chi(N)=z1+sum_(a in S_N) R_N(a)r(a),
    B_N(z):=sum_a |R_N(a)r(a)|
       <=W_N(z):=N sum_a |r(a)|/a.                         (227.3)

All coordinates remain. If r is supported on a>N/H, H>=1, this costs at most
H||r||1. A global inverse operator norm is therefore an unnecessarily large
default price for a residual known to live on large labels. The exact signed
sum in (227.3) remains available; its absolute bound is only a sufficient bill.

For fixed 0<gamma<1, a complete every-epsilon bound for |z1|+B_N(z), or the
stronger explicit |z1|+W_N(z), by N^(gamma+epsilon) gives the same Mertens
bound. The alternative every-epsilon integral_1^X |M_chi(t)|^2 dt/t bound
by X^(2gamma+epsilon) also suffices. On each dyadic shell Cauchy bounds
the Abel integral and all its fixed derivatives, with a positive exponent
buffer on any compact subset of Re(s)>gamma. The normally convergent function

    s integral_1^infinity M_chi(t)t^(-s-1)dt

equals 1/L(s,chi) on Re(s)>1. Continuing the identity with L excludes regular
zeros in Re(s)>gamma at every finite height. At the principal pole s=1 the
reciprocal has a zero. Natural character zeros stay in the coefficients.
Constants may depend on the fixed character and epsilon; no growing-conductor
or Hecke assertion follows. This is a complete return from an OPEN estimate.

Two concrete inverse cautions survive. In the principal N=2 case the signed
coprimality matrix [[1,-1],[-1,0]] is invertible but its nuisance block [0]
is singular and its inverse (1,1) entry is0. A Schur formula requiring that
block inverse fails. On m distinct prime labels the matrix is J-I, full rank
for m>=2, while rank-one J has operator residual1 and scalar residual at most
||u||2||v||2. Exact rank alone therefore does not rule out a paid approximation.
title: G227. An actual twisted inverse and its cofactor-resolved observation

## G228. The sharp depth of a low-omega-completed inverse column

Fix 0<beta<1. For 1<=T<=beta N and an integer k>=0 define

    F_(T,k)(d)=1_(d<=T OR omega(d)<=k),
    z=E^-T (chi(d) F_(T,k)(d))_d.

The first row of E^-T is mu(d), and multiplying by A_chi cancels chi against
its conjugate. Using sum_(d|a)mu(d)=1_(a=1) gives the exact identities

    z1=sum_(d in S_N)mu(d)chi(d) F_(T,k)(d),
    r(a)=sum_(d|a,d>T,omega(d)>k)mu(d).                     (228.1)

If omega(a)=k+1 and a>T, all proper divisors are included, so r(a)=mu(a).
For a>N/2 its cofactor observation is exactly R_N(a)=chi(a).
Let b_k be the product of the first k primes not dividing q, b_0=1, and put
alpha=max(beta,1/2). Every prime p in (alpha N/b_k,N/b_k] not dividing b_k q
gives a distinct actual coordinate a=b_k p with |R_N(a)r(a)|=1. Thus

    B_N(z)<=W_N(z),
    B_N(z)>=#{alpha N/b_k<p<=N/b_k : p prime, p not|b_k q}. (228.2)

The second line is an exact finite inequality, possibly zero for small N.
For fixed k, the ordinary prime number theorem gives the lower asymptotic
(1-alpha)N/(b_k log N). Correcting primes, semiprimes or any other fixed number
of omega layers has not made this absolute residual small at any exponent<1.

There is also a matching upper bound for growing depth. Set h=k+1,
H_N=sum_(m<=N)1/m and A_N=sum_(p<=N)1/p, including conductor primes if desired.
Taking the absolute value in (228.1) and exchanging the finite divisor sums,

    W_N(z)<=N H_N sum_(d<=N,d squarefree,omega(d)>=h)1/d
           <=N H_N sum_(j>=h) A_N^j/j!
           <=N H_N exp(A_N) A_N^h/h!.                     (228.3)

An unordered j-prime set occurs j! times in A_N^j. Admitting repeated primes
and products above N only enlarges the positive sum. The last inequality
uses (h+r)!>=h!r!. This pays EVERY residual coordinate and is uniform in T.

Ordinary PNT and partial summation give p_j~j log j and A_N=O(loglog N).
The [NIST reference](https://dlmf.nist.gov/27.12) records the prime asymptotics;
the consequences here are derived from them. Removing fixed q's finitely
many primes changes indices by a bounded amount, so log b_k~k log k as k grows.
If k~kappa log N/loglog N for fixed 0<kappa<1, then
b_k=N^(kappa+o(1)), while its largest prime is O(log N). The prime interval
in (228.2) lies above all these factors eventually; its endpoint is
N^(1-kappa+o(1)). PNT on a fixed-ratio interval, together with (228.3) and
log(h!)=h log h-h+O(log h), proves

    B_N(z)=N^(1-kappa+o(1)),  W_N(z)=N^(1-kappa+o(1)).      (228.4)

These are logarithmic exponents, uniform for 1<=T<=beta N, not fixed-k
logarithmic asymptotic formulas. If k=o(log N/loglog N), both exponents are1.

More generally fix ONE sequence k_N>=0 and ONE cutoff sequence
1<=T_N<=beta N for all sufficiently large N, independently of epsilon. For 0<gamma<1,

    B_N(z_N)<<_epsilon N^(gamma+epsilon) for EVERY epsilon>0
    iff W_N(z_N)<<_epsilon N^(gamma+epsilon) for EVERY epsilon>0
    iff liminf_N k_N loglog N/log N >= 1-gamma.             (228.5)

For sufficiency, bound the nonnegative tail in (228.3) at any smaller depth
a log N/loglog N with 0<a<1-gamma and then let a approach1-gamma according
to epsilon. For necessity, if the liminf is smaller, choose such an a above
it. Along infinitely many N the primorial is at most N^(a+o(1)), so (228.2)
has exponent at least1-a, contradicting a sufficiently small fixed epsilon.
No short-interval or growing-modulus prime theorem is used.

Equality in (228.5) is sufficient for the residual bill alone. It does not
pay z1. In fact, with D_N the number of omitted coefficients,

    z1=M_chi(N)-sum_(d in S_N,d>T,omega(d)>=h)mu(d)chi(d),
    D_N<=sum_(n<=N)binom(omega(n),h)
        =sum_(d<=N,d squarefree,omega(d)=h)floor(N/d)
        <=N A_N^h/h!.                                    (228.6)

Once (228.5) holds, the every-epsilon exponent-gamma estimate on z1 is
equivalent to that on M_chi(N). The retained coordinate still carries the
arithmetic problem. At the c11 benchmark the residual's threshold is
liminf k_N loglog N/log N >= .1251459636; the full certificate is still open.

The lower bounds concern COMPLETE ABSOLUTE bills of this SPECIFIC column
family. They do not lower-bound the complete signed residual, Mertens sum,
any arbitrary approximant or a Gaussian energy. Higher residual layers need
not have a common sign: for k=1,T=11,a=30, r(30)=mu(15)+mu(30)=0.

The ancestry is the first-unpaid-layer argument in W43/[restricted research revision] and [restricted research revision]'s
fixed-layer circle obstruction. W43's Newton defect includes prime powers
and factorial multiplicities; at T=1,k=1 its order-two defect at pq is2,
where (228.1) is1. G78/G83-G85 already paid their own growing-order Gaussian
restoration, so that older obligation is not reopened. The new scoped result
is the cofactor certificate's exact depth threshold and its remaining z1
obligation, rather than a new generic lesson about truncation.

## G229. A full Walsh source with its Gaussian and Euler returns paid

This section concerns the principal coprime Gaussian P_Y of G25-G30. Fix
tau>0, Y=floor(X^.495), B_X=2X exp(C sqrt(log X)), with fixed C>0. The Boolean
cube uses ALL primes5<=p<=B_X. For labels u,v put d(u)=prod_p p^u_p and

    K(u,v)=(-1)^(|u|+|v|)1_(u and v disjoint),
    W_x(u,v)=1_(d(u)>Y,d(v)>Y,d(u)d(v)<=B_X)
      *sum_(ell<=B_X/(d(u)d(v)))(-1)^(ell+1)
           g_tau(log(d(u)d(v)ell/x)).

Then Z_X(x)=sum K W_x is the literal output-truncated ordered source.
Shared-prime zeros, p=2,3 exclusions, both strict cuts and every ell sign
remain. With K_0 cube sites and an unnormalized Walsh transform in BOTH
variables, finite orthogonality proves

    Z_X(x)=2^(-2K_0) sum_(alpha,beta) Khat(alpha,beta) What_x(alpha,beta).
                                                               (229.1)

There is no complex conjugation in this bilinear identity. Locally,
H=[[1,1],[1,-1]], T=[[1,-1],[-1,0]], and H T H=[[-1,1],[1,3]]. All four
dual gate entries are nonzero. Sparsity of the complete transformed mask
would require its own theorem; the global prime cube is not one divisor cube.

The original d3 coefficient majorant bounds the discarded output field,
uniformly on x in[X,2X], by X^(1-C^2/(2tau)+o(1)). The counting Jacobian
is included in that exponent. Choose C with this exponent below the desired
gamma>1/2. G27 independently pays |P_Y-F6|<<X^(.495+delta), delta<gamma-.495.
G28 then uses fixed Euler convolutions and their inverses, with direct
factor (1-z)^2 at2,3 and (1-z)^2/(1-2z) at p>=5. Their weighted absolute
coefficient sums converge for every fixed sigma>1/2; the original exceptional
prime2 coefficients1,-3,2 remain. Apply this norm transfer to the FIXED F6
and G_tau fields, then apply each shell's own frozen Y comparison.

Thus a COMPLETE every-epsilon shell L2 bound for (229.1) at exponent gamma
would return the original fixed Gaussian G3 and its zeta zero exclusion.
The changing finite cube has no independently asserted Mellin transform.
Both copies, all dual modes, their cross terms and the complementary field
remain. An ordinary-character or Hecke extension is an additional theorem.
No arithmetic estimate for the whole right side has been proved.

## G230. Paid ambient realizations and two independent audits

If A=alpha P U Q with U unitary and P,Q contractions, alpha>=||A|| follows
by submultiplicativity. For C=A/alpha a contraction, the Halmos block
[[C,(I-CC*)^(1/2)],[(I-C*C)^(1/2),-C*]] is unitary; the defect intertwining
identity proves it directly. It realizes the optimum alpha=||A||. For
selfadjoint C its square is I, whereas C^2=I-(I-C^2); repeated use must
retain the returning defect or intermediate physical projections. A
source-specific approximation remains possible, with the full scalar
residual bounded by delta||u||2||v||2 when its operator error is delta.

The signed local gate T is a diagonal sign gauge of [[1,1],[1,0]], so their
singular values agree. The indefinite J=[[-2,-1],[-1,2]] satisfies T^TJT=-J,
yet v=(phi,-1), phi=(1+sqrt5)/2, is J-null and Tv=phi v. Conserved flux
does not bound that positive observation. For a selfadjoint K, the Cayley
unitary V=(K-iI)(K+iI)^-1 has (I-V)^-1=(I-iK)/2 and inverse norm
sqrt(1+||K||^2)/2. No selfadjoint claim is licensed for complex A_chi.

The protected S28 audit diagonalizes the disjointness gate orthogonally.
For K_0 sites its eigenvalues are (-1)^j phi^(K_0-2j), with binomial
multiplicity, and squared Frobenius norm3^K_0. Writing the FULL physical
boundary in that basis preserves its Frobenius norm; the generic contraction
bill is3^(K_0/2)||W||F. A product-only weight counts each ordered prime
allocation and produces mu(n)chi(n)2^omega(n), not the original Mertens
coefficient. A single n-divisor cube has omega(n)=O(log n/loglog n);
that does not bound the global prime set of every n<=X.

The uniform S09 audit uses the connected prime-adjoining graph on S_N.
For (Bf)_(n,pn)=f(pn)+chi(p)f(n), write f(n)=a(n)g(n), a(n)=mu(n)chi(n).
Then ker B=span(a). In ANY complete identity w=lambda e1+B^T t, pairing
with a forces lambda=sum_n w_n a(n). A rooted prime-deletion tree constructs
t from complete signed subtree sums. If r=w-lambda e1-B^Tt, then

    |sum_n w_n a(n)|<=|lambda|+||r||1,
    inf_(lambda,t)(|lambda|+||w-lambda e1-B^Tt||1)=|sum_n w_n a(n)|.
                                                               (230.1)

The upper equality chooses the exact signed target as lambda; the lower is
the triangle inequality. This leaves constructive arithmetic certificates
eligible, but feasibility alone hides the original target in a coordinate.

All these bills concern their named positive, absolute or generic ambient
arguments. They leave complete signed arithmetic cancellation open. The
review's S28/S09 audits froze before author outcomes, and all30 original
cards and dispositions remain in the retained source reports. Conditional
c11 and the separate PR15/F0/positive-slot/external-admission gaps are unchanged.
title: G230. Paid ambient realizations and two independent audits

Fix distinct unramified primes p,ell. Let m(n)=mu(n)chi(n), s(r^2)=chi(r)^2 and s(n)=0 off squares, Q_p=delta_1-p chi(p)delta_p, B_p=delta_1-p chi(p)^2 delta_(p^2), and h_p=Q_p*(B_p*s*s-delta_1)*m. Then the exact complete aggregate
v=B_ell*Q_ell*h_p-B_p*Q_p*h_ell=Q_p*Q_ell*(B_p-B_ell)*m
has eight actual shifts: v(n)=sum_(d|n)a_d m(n/d). In the order d=p^2,p^3,p^2 ell,p^3 ell,ell^2,p ell^2,ell^3,p ell^3, a_d/chi(d)=-p,p^2,p ell,-p^2 ell,ell,-p ell,-ell^2,p ell^2. Shared primes and character zeros remain literal. The finite readout cost is (p+ell)(1+p)(1+ell); this is not power sparsity.
For Re(z)>1,
D_v(z)=[(1-chi(p)p^(1-z))(1-chi(ell)ell^(1-z))(chi(ell)^2 ell^(1-2z)-chi(p)^2 p^(1-2z))]/L(z,chi).
The numerator never vanishes in 1/2<Re(z)<1. Cumulative coefficient-square mass is O_(p,ell)(Y).
Fix rho=(k-2gamma)/(k-2)<b, L=X^gamma, M=X^rho, and K_(v,X)(x)=sum_(L<n<=M)v(n)exp(-n/x^b-i(n/x)^k). Every shifted realization keeps exp(-d n/x^b), phase (d n/x)^k and the local cuts L/d<n<=M/d; it is not an unpriced scale-x/d observation. The complete prefix and tail give ||F_v-K_(v,X)||_(1,X)+||F_v-K_(v,X)||_(2,X) << X^gamma. The respective full/core growth hypotheses are equivalent in each norm separately; L2 is stronger than the least L1 premise, and no L1-to-L2 implication is claimed.
The least unpaid source premise is ||K_(v,X)||_(1,X) <<_epsilon X^(gamma+epsilon), for every epsilon and all sufficiently large dyadic shells. With a fixed Taylor order K satisfying 1-K(b-1)<gamma, the complete Mellin descent returns ordinary fixed-character zero exclusion above gamma. Existing higher-Taylor descent receives its original credit; this is not a new continuation theorem. The classical line-1 endpoint and permitted principal pole are paid independently; alternatively all three pairs of a fixed covering triple need their own aggregate hypotheses. No earlier conditional boundary is used.
A separately stronger L2 device keeps all damping moments: choose fixed J>=1 with (J+1)rho-Jb<=gamma; let Delta=X^k, t0=(1+2^(-k))/(2X^k), Psi_J(z)=sum_(0<=j<J)z^j/(j!)^2 and W_X(n,n')=(1-|n'^k-n^k|/Delta)_+.
Q_X=2 Re sum_(L<n<n'<=M) v(n)conj(v(n')) exp(i t0(n'^k-n^k)) W_X(n,n') Psi_J(nn'/X^(2b)); D_X=sum_(L<n<=M)|v(n)|^2 Psi_J(n^2/X^(2b)); E_X=D_X+Q_X>=0.
The exact remaining hypothesis for this L2 device is the one-sided Q_X<=C_epsilon X^(2gamma+epsilon), not an absolute bound on each correlation. Negative Q_X helps. D_X=O(M) is paid because rho<b<=2gamma, and ||K_(v,X)||_(2,X)^2 <<_(k,J) E_X+X^(2gamma). Thus this hypothesis implies the complete L1 premise. All 64 mixed dilation pairs, their coefficients, local cuts, character zeros, ordering and triangular/Taylor weights remain.

At gamma=0.8748 the required squared exponent is 1.7496, leaving a 0.2504 power gap. A fixed logarithmic saving does not close it. raw_source_record.statement:
Use the complete G231 field with m(a)=mu(a)chi(a), t_p(r)=chi(r)^2[tau(r)-p 1_(p|r)tau(r/p)], b1(v)=chi(v)(1-p 1_(p|v)), f_x(n)=exp(-n/x^b-i(n/x)^k), and T(x)=sum_(2<=r<=R)t_p(r) sum_(a,b'>U_r; v>=1; n=r^2ab'v<=M)m(a)m(b')b1(v)f_x(n). Define Tlo by multiplying every original summand by zeta(v/[X^eta(1+(n/X)^k)]), preserving the original upper mask. Then sup_[X,2X]|T-Tlo| <<_A X^(-A) for every fixed A>0, and the same bound holds separately in both complete shell norms j=1,2. Thus the respective every-epsilon X^(gamma+epsilon) hypotheses for T and Tlo are equivalent.
The exact frozen bank A_d has d=r^2ab'>X^gamma and |A_d|<=(p+1)tau_4(d), with shared primes retained. The cofactor b1 has fixed period pq and complete mean zero, including the principal and imprimitive ordinary cases. On a smooth n~N block put S=N/d,Tphase=(N/X)^k,V=X^eta(1+Tphase). The high weight is nonzero only for d<4N/V. Its Jth derivative is O_J(exp(-cN/X^b)(1+Tphase)^J), uniformly over all phase scales and cutoff transitions. Repeated mean-zero periodic primitives give the complete integer-row bound O_J(S^(1-J) exp(-cN/X^b)(1+Tphase)^J), without discarded endpoints. Summing all d and all dyadic N yields O(X^(b(1+xi)-J eta)); choose fixed J after A,eta,xi. The original upper cutoff costs exactly zero: for n>M and d>X^gamma the cutoff argument is <X^(-eta-k(1-gamma)/(k-2))<1, so the complementary weight vanishes.
For0<eta<1-gamma the whole long-cofactor transition sector is genuinely removed, including the smooth boundary. For n~X^nu,nu>=1 the new cap exponent eta+k(nu-1) improves nu-gamma only below nu_*=(k-gamma-eta)/(k-1), and rho-nu_*=[k(1-gamma)+eta(k-2)]/[(k-2)(k-1)]>0. For eta>=1-gamma the high weight vanishes everywhere, giving only a trivial reduction. The v=1 source and higher nonlinear/alias range remain; an isolated positive principal prime-pair cell prevents a triangle payment of every individual cell, not cancellation in the complete signed field.
This is a source-specific nonlinear adapter. Generic complete periodic cancellation, repeated primitives and earlier balanced finite forms are antecedents. Inspected Eisenstein-lattice Lean modules motivated exact contract checks only; their dimensions, seminorms and changing moduli are not transferred as applicable black-box theorems. The one-dimensional row argument is proved separately. No new zero-free constant or end-to-end formalization follows.

raw_source_record.statement:
For every bounded complex sequence |a(n)|<=1, fix R=4/3 and A_j=R^j,I_j={n>=1:A_j<=n<A_(j+1)}. Given a shell X>=e and fixed E>0, choose r=max(1,ceil((E+1)log X/log3)), N=floor(2(E+2)X log X), J=floor(log N/log R), before live x in[X,2X]. Retain the exact moments C_(j,m)=sum_(n in I_j,n<=N)a(n)((n-A_j)/A_j)^m and complete synthesis S_X(x)=sum_(j=0)^J exp(-A_j/x)sum_(m=0)^(r-1)(-A_j/x)^m C_(j,m)/m!. Then sup_[X,2X]|sum_(n>=1)a(n)exp(-n/x)-S_X(x)| <<_E X^(-E), with O_E(log^2 X) moments. Every within-cell order, last-cell cut, original sign/natural zero and cross-cell interaction remains. The degree-uniform finite error for any integer r>=1,N is <=(1/3)^r(Rx+2), obtained by the complete unimodal sum of t^r exp(-t), integral r! and at most two peak values. The omitted integer tail is <=(2X+1)exp(-N/(2X)).
For actual a(n)=mu(n)chi(n), fixed ordinary chi, a complete every-epsilon shell L1 bound ||S_X||_1 << X^(gamma+epsilon), with0<gamma<1 common to the asserted fixed-character family, transfers to the fixed Laplace source. Its full Mellin transform Gamma(s)/L(s,chi), paid left tail and nonvanishing Gamma then exclude all finite-height zeros of every multiplicity above gamma, with the principal pole and imprimitive factors retained. The signed synthesis bound is unproved; absolute separate moment payment only gives exponent1.
Coarse logarithmic cell balance is insufficient: assign +1 to the first floor(#I_j/2) integers, -1 to the last, and0 to any central leftover. Every cell sum vanishes, while the ordinary Dirichlet series has a simple pole at1 of residue log(49/48)/log(4/3). The one-cell Riemann error is O_K(R^(-j Re(s))) on compact subsets of Re(s)>0, giving a holomorphic remainder. This is a bounded integer countermodel, not a Mobius counterexample. For actual mu(n)chi(n), the absolute one-mode rounding bill is asymptotic in order to eta X uniformly for X^(-1/2+delta)<=eta<=eta0, with fixed q,delta>0 and sufficiently small fixed eta0. That absolute price does not lower-bound signed rounding error.
The mechanism refines earlier Gaussian compression and signed transport; the moment count is not an arithmetic algorithm or an improvement over the earlier Gaussian rank. No arithmetic power saving or c increase is established.

raw_source_record.statement:
Let a(n)=mu(n)chi(n) for a fixed ordinary character, M(t)=sum_(n<=t)a(n), and nu_N=sum_(n<=N)a(n)delta_log(n)-M(N)delta_log(N+1). The unique compact adjacent-gap current is J_N(u)=M(exp u) for0<=u<log(N+1), zero outside. For every absolutely continuous complex f, int f dnu_N=-int J_N f'. For nonnegative integrable w, sup_(f(log(N+1))=0,|f'|<=w)|int f dnu_N|=int|J_N|w. Equality uses f'=-w conjugate(J_N)/|J_N| where J_N is nonzero; hence nonreal phases are retained. Splitting longer line edges into adjacent gaps proves no routing can reduce this metric cost. The endpoint ghost is retained exactly and is not an estimate of M(N).
For w=1 the norm is int_1^(N+1)|M(t)|dt/t. If for a common0<gamma<1 every fixed character and every epsilon satisfy int_X^(2X)|M(t)|dt/t <<_(chi,epsilon)X^(gamma+epsilon) on all sufficiently large dyadic shells, then H(s)=s int_1^infinity M(t)t^(-s)dt/t is holomorphic for Re(s)>gamma, including every fixed derivative, and agrees initially with1/L(s,chi). The complete Abel identity excludes all finite-height zeros of every multiplicity there, treating the principal pole by its reciprocal zero. It does not require first deducing a pointwise Mertens bound of exponent gamma. The elementary coefficient-continuity argument only yields the weaker pointwise exponent(1+gamma)/2.
The exact norm identity supplies no independent arithmetic upper bound. Endpoint cell balance alone leaves linear current cost for the bounded countermodel of G237. This refines earlier endpoint-anchored shell current and signed-transport mechanisms; a different Hilbert-feature transport cost and its square-root mass factor do not transfer to this linear metric. No c gain is established.

raw_source_record.statement:
For a finite matrix K retaining the entire original labeled source, put A=[[0,K],[K*,0]]. Represent each nonzero contribution by a directed edge e, with computational reverse bar(e) of weight conjugate(w_e); parallel labels remain distinct. Define(Sf)_e=f_head(e),(Tg)_v=sum_(tail(e)=v)w_e g_e,(Rg)_e=w_bar(e)g_bar(e). Then A=TS and B=ST-R is the exact weighted nonbacktracking lift. Where all displayed inverses exist, F(z)=I-zT(I+zR)^(-1)S satisfies F(z)^(-1)=I+zT(I-zB)^(-1)S. Each reverse pair has R^2=|w_e|^2I, so the eliminated operator has diagonal1+sum_tail z^2|w_e|^2/(1-z^2|w_e|^2) and off-diagonal contributions-z w_e/(1-z^2|w_e|^2). Both backtrack diagonals and changed off-diagonal weights remain.
The original projected source y*Kx is the coefficient of z in y0*F(z)^(-1)x0, with x0=(0,x),y0=(y,0). A Cauchy return must pay its actual contour, projected resolvent, lift norms and exceptional parameters. The generic lift bounds are ||T||^2=max_v sum_tail|w_e|^2 and ||S||^2=max_v #{head(e)=v}, counting parallel labels. For a d-leaf unit-weight star, B^2=0 but ||B||=d-1 and ||A||=sqrt d. Thus spectral radius alone cannot bound the original source norm. This is a generic graph counterexample, not an arithmetic native-H lower bound or obstruction on its actual source range.
In the original native-H application retain the full coefficients, original additive character, both complete mark projectors, natural zeros, parallel labels, signed d and g,g' sums, true-core weights and source complement. The fixed-u,v raw K+N deficit at N=K Z^.003 differs from the full all-g K+NG deficit with G=Z^.001; neither the .003 nor .004 saving is proved by this identity. The outer squared scalar N^(-1)G^(-2) and original signed near-band restoration remain. An actual projected resolvent estimate with complete source return is still required; no ordinary-character identification, arithmetic power saving or c gain follows.

raw_source_record.statement:
Let e=1 for principal chi and0 otherwise, A(s)=(s-1)^e L(s,chi), and v_j=W(s_j)/L(s_j,chi), using the actual inverse Dirichlet series. If every matrix K_N(i,j)=(B^2-v_i conj(v_j))/(s_i+conj(s_j)-2gamma) is positive semidefinite, then bounded half-plane interpolants and normal-family compactness give F holomorphic on H_gamma with |F|<=B and A(s)F(s)=(s-1)^e W(s). Thus every finite-height zero of L in H_gamma is excluded; the principal point1 is its permitted pole, not a zero. Imprimitive Euler factors/natural zeros remain. This sufficient fixed-weight bounded-reciprocal criterion is not equivalent to qualitative zero exclusion.
Approximate global interpolants with the same B and errors epsilon_N->0 at each fixed sample suffice. For Re s_j>=1+delta, v_j^(J)=W(s_j)sum_(n<=J)mu(n)chi(n)n^(-s_j) has error <=|W(s_j)|J^(-delta)/delta. If Re s_j-gamma>=d>0, |v_j|<=V and sample errors<=r, the finite matrix error norm is <=N(2Vr+r^2)/(2d); a larger least-eigenvalue margin certifies that finite matrix only. Neither one finite PSD matrix, diagonal bounds, a nonzero limiting error nor samples escaping to infinity proves the all-N hypothesis. A finite hidden-pole countermodel is ambient analytic evidence, not an arithmetic counterexample.

For any sequence u with sum_(m<=Y)|u(m)|^2<=C Y, the COMPLETE mismatch E_(u,d)(x)=sum_m u(m)[f_x(dm)-f_(x/d)(m)] obeys ||E_(u,d)||_2 <<_(b,k) sqrt(C)[X^(b/2)d^(-1/2)+X^(2-b)d^(b-2)]exp(-c d/X^b), with fixed c>0. Low m<=X/d and the entire high Gram/tail are paid; both actual sources satisfy the square-coefficient hypothesis. Summing every w/z shift gives full errors O(X^theta log^3(2X)), theta=max(b/2,2-b), and bounded forward/inverse shell operators at every sigma>1/2. Hence for gamma>=theta, each j=1,2 separately has ||F_cM||_(j,X)<<_epsilon X^(gamma+epsilon) iff the corresponding full c_L bound holds. Minimum theta is2/3 at b=4/3. Phi_p is C_p times the density of sum_(j>=0)p^(-j)E_j for independent Exp(1) variables; it is positive, smooth, flat at0, <=exp(-t), and integral Phi_p=C_p. For0<t<=1, log Phi_p(t)<=-(log(1/t))^2/(2log p)+(log(1/t))/2. Signed dilation moments sum_j u_j p^(mj)=0 for every integer m>=0; positive kernel moments do not vanish. Its Mellin multiplier K_p(s)=Gamma(s)product_(j>=0)(1-p^(-(s+j))) is entire and nonzero for Re s>0. The full transform is K_p(s)L(2s,chi^2)/L(s,chi); a full L1 growth bound at gamma>1/2 gives all-height ordinary zero exclusion. Gamma inverse is not polynomial in height.
Exactly F=sum_j u_j F0(x/p^j) and F0=sum_j v_j F(x/p^j), v_j=1/C_j. Forward absolute gamma-sum is finite and inverse cost <=C_p^(-1)/(1-p^(-gamma)), gamma>0, including all shifted shells/small arguments. raw_source_record.statement: Let a=mu chi, h=chi, Q_p=delta_1-p chi(p)delta_p. Fix R>=2, J=R+1, delta in {0,1} with chi(-1)=(-1)^delta. Let w_J be the J-fold convolution of 1_[0,log2], Psi(y)=int w_J(t)exp(-i y^6 exp(-6t))dt, Phi(y)=y^delta Psi(y), K=6J-delta. Put Q*=Q_p*(delta_1-delta_p), b*=Q* convolved with h, c*=Q* convolved with a. The mean-zero periodic b* has period p^2 q independent of R and b*(0)=0. Its Laplace coefficients B_j and Phi derivatives obey B_j Phi^(j)(0)=0 for every j; hence |sum_l b*(l)Phi(Dl/X)|<< (D/X)^R. For u=(R+gamma)/(R+1), U=V=X^(u/2), M=X^((K-gamma)/(K-1)), the entire T*=sum_(d>U,e>V,del<=M)a(d)a(e)b*(l)Phi(del/X) differs from Z*=sum_n c*(n)Phi(n/X) by O_epsilon(X^(gamma+epsilon)); all short, small-double and infinite-tail terms are included. Its Mellin factor is Gamma((s+delta)/6)exp(-i*pi*(s+delta)/12)/6 times ((2^(s+delta)-1)/(s+delta))^J times (1-chi(p)p^(1-s))(1-p^(-s))/L(s,chi). New factors have no zeros in Re(s)>0. For q>1 the extra delta_1-delta_p factor may be omitted. A complete bound for T* and a fixed covering prime bank give the conditional return. Constants depend on fixed R; R cannot grow with X.

For the compensated Liouville-square source c=(lambda chi)*(lambda chi)*(q1*q2*chi), q1=delta_1-p chi(p)delta_p, q2=delta_1-p chi(p)^2 delta_(p^2), freeze tau in [0,1], U=X^(gamma tau), V=X^(gamma(1-tau)), L=X^gamma, G=X^(1-gamma), M=X^((k-gamma)/(k-1)). Retain sum_(d>U,e>V,L<del<=M,gcd(d,e)<=G)(lambda chi)(d)(lambda chi)(e)(q1*q2*chi)(l)f_x(del). Its complete complement costs O(X^gamma log^2(2X)) in P_X. At b=3/2 the conditional return extends to gamma=1/2; the Mellin integral is improper signed, not absolutely integrable. For any coefficient sequence with cumulative absolute mass O(Y), changing fixed damping constants has full primitive defect O(X^(2-b)) for k>2 and O(X^(2-b)log X) for k=2. The direct Mellin remainder is holomorphic on positive Re(s)>2-b. At b=2 the DISTINCT source c_mu=Q_p*(mu chi)=(mu chi)*(mu chi)*(Q_p*chi) has the same complete core reduction for 0<gamma<1, with mu(d)mu(e)chi(de), not mu(de). Its Mellin numerator has no square L factor and its remainder is holomorphic in Re(s)>0. Whole/r-free primitive classes are equivalent after paying the fixed-prime damping defect and actual exponential left tail.

Then ||T_r||=rho(u), where rho=u+u^2-u^3 for u<=sqrt(5)-2 and rho=(sqrt(5)/2)u(1+u^2) otherwise. Thus rho(3/5)^2=2601/3125 and for r>=3,sigma>=1/2, rho^2<=20/27<1. The sharp ambient inverse is ||E_r^(-1)||=[(1-u)(1-u^2)]^(-1); its coefficients are (-t)^j(floor(j/2)+1). Finite distinct-prime banks have the sharp product norm by rational independence of log primes. For the fixed Gaussian-smoothed compensated Liouville-square source, E_rF=F_r with the complete r-free forcing, and the Gaussian left tail justifies causal inversion before assuming H_sigma membership. Fixed banks preserve every-epsilon exponents. The conditional Mellin return may use gamma=1/2; no forcing estimate follows from contraction.

raw_source_record.statement: For fixed tau,sigma>0 and positive integer Q, the finite span of G_tau(log(n/x)), (n,Q)=1, is dense in H_sigma. Under logarithmic conjugation, an orthogonal vector would have an entire Gaussian convolution of order at most two vanishing at all log n-tau sigma with (n,Q)=1; exponential zero count contradicts the quadratic Jensen bound. Hence a finite-bank inverse from G252 remains norm-sharp on finite Gaussian polynomials. Coefficient caps do not change norm ratios after rescaling. Applying C_p=[(I-p chi(p)D_p)(I-p chi(p)^2D_p^2)]/[(I+chi(p)D_p)(I-chi(p)^2D_p^2)] to polynomials supported away from pq and the bank has dense range: numerator zeros are at most a null frequency set. This retains natural zeros and the exact compensating-prime ray law, and bank inversion restores its prime rays. The resulting free-coefficient class lacks the fixed global lambda law. Thus Gaussian regularity and these local recurrences alone cannot improve the uniform inverse norm; additional actual arithmetic structure remains eligible.

raw_source_record.statement: For the literal joint annular vector F(v,w), remove each label-dependent plain-scale phase diagonally and unitarily. Its Fourier support lies in one fixed log-ratio box. Choose a fixed Schwartz eta with Fourier transform 1 there, so F=eta*F. For rho_m(v,w)=c_m^2(1+v^2)^(-m)(1+w^2)^(-m), Cauchy gives ||F(v,w)||^2<=C_m(1+v^2)^m(1+w^2)^m int rho_m||F||^2, without a label-count loss. Conversely a pointwise bound with polynomial degree J gives a finite weighted average for m>J+1/2. Therefore existence of a finite-degree pointwise estimate and of a finite-m weighted-average estimate is equivalent on this fixed-bandwidth class. Weighted Hilbert transport and its exact signed Gram expansion remain valid, but the averaged condition is not an independently weaker arithmetic obligation. Retain all original arithmetic labels, radial weights, both ordered cross terms, masks and Fourier tails.

raw_source_record.statement: For a fixed Gaussian log kernel and its eta combination U(x)-2U(x/2), comparison coefficients can retain squareful zeros and agreement with mu on every z-smooth integer, z=log X, while their complete eta energy is large. In the complex multiplicative class, choose small-prime values -1 and large-prime values p^(it). The full x^(1+it) main term has eta factor 1-2^(-it): t=0 is annihilated, t=pi/log2 survives and yields energy at least c X^2/log^4 X with the full error retained. A real squarefree-supported multiplicative H_X assigns prime signs -1 below z and above Y=2exp(3tau)X, and +1 between. Then |H_X|^2=mu^2 and the complete one-large-prime expansion, eta-cancelled base and above-Y^2 Gaussian tail give G_(H_X)(x)<=-cX/log X on [X,2X], hence energy at least c^2 X^2/log^2 X. H_X depends on X; moving-band constants are not uniform fixed-Euler-correction constants. These classes omit the global mu convolution inverse law. The result obstructs uniform estimates for these enlarged classes, not actual mu or one fixed comparison sequence at every scale.

Merge A_delta=sum_(labels at delta)W_label and C(t)=sum_(delta>t)A_delta. Then dC=-sum A_delta delta_delta, and for ordered gaps d_j, sum h(d_j)A_dj=h(d_1)C(d_1-)+sum_(j>=2)(h(d_j)-h(d_(j-1)))C(d_j-). Equivalently for absolutely continuous h, sum_(delta>t0)h(delta)A_delta=h(t0)C(t0)+int_(t0)^D h_prime(t)C(t)dt. Equality atoms and the hard anchor remain. Varying only threshold does not move arithmetic projectors. If w,P,Q also jump, Delta(wPQ)=(w+-w-)P+Q+ +w-(P+-P-)Q+ +w-P-(Q+-Q-). For the original ordered graph a<Delta<=b both degrees are <=4(floor(b-a)+1); integer-gap weights cost B_h=4sum|h(j)|. raw_source_record.statement: For squarefree primorial P let V_t be the augmented oriented-deletion complex on subsets with product<=t, graded by subset cardinality. A window is the relative complex V_b/V_a, with parity trace sum_(a<d<=b,d|P)mu(d), not a divisor-closed interval complex. If P contains2 and3, the interval (P/3,2P/3] contains exactly P/2. Its deletion faces lie below P/3, so the relative complex has one generator, zero differential and nonzero homology. The generator is distance P/6 from each endpoint. Hence universal support in additive endpoint strips o(X) fails for this primorial-window model. The exact least-prime matching instead crosses a full multiplicative layer. The least-prime partner P is outside the interval; no internal elementary face matching can pair the surviving generator. This does not estimate the full signed Mobius source.

On its exact d-step staircase, orthonormal class embeddings give T=U B V*, B=diag(sqrt(m_i))L_d diag(sqrt(n_j)), with positive integer multiplicities and L_d the d-by-d lower triangular all-ones matrix. Its singular values are sigma_j(L_d)=[2sin((2j-1)pi/(4d+2))]^(-1). Thus for0<=k<d every rank-k approximation has operator error at least sigma_(k+1)(B)>=sigma_(k+1)(L_d)>=(2d+1)/(pi(2k+1)); the corresponding squared Frobenius error is at least the sum of the squared discarded singular values. Zero/repeated classes are handled before this compression; different partitions can have different d. This sharpens the older1/2 operator floor and preserves exact continuation classes. Averaging theta gives sup_z|M_z|>=(2/pi)R_Q(N)=delta_Q N/pi+O_Q(sqrt N), delta_Q=(phi(Q)/Q)product_(p not dividing Q)(1-p^(-2))>0. raw_source_record.statement:
For a_n=mu(n)chi(n), I_N={N+1,...,2N}, g_tau(u)=(2*pi*tau)^(-1/2)exp(-u^2/(2*tau)), f_N(t)=sum_(n in I_N)a_n g_tau(t-log n) and E_N=int_R|f_N|^2dt, set kappa=(4*pi*tau)^(-1/2). Exactly E_N=kappa D_N+2*kappa Re sum_(h=1)^(N-1) sum_(n=N+1)^(2N-h)mu(n)mu(n+h)chi(n)conj(chi(n+h))exp(-log(1+h/n)^2/(4*tau)), D_N=sum_(n in I_N)|a_n|^2<=N. This is the full covariance: both orientations, joint n,h weight, endpoints and all squareful/ramified zeros remain. The diagonal is not a lower bound for the signed energy. With all-one bounded coefficients E_N>=kappa exp(-log(2)^2/(4*tau))N^2, and shifts in[N/4,N/2] alone cost order N^2. This rejects absolute sublinear shift truncation for the generic kernel, not actual Mobius cancellation.
For A_N(xi)=sum_(n in I_N)a_n n^(-i xi), Fourier convention exp(-i xi t) gives E_N=(2*pi)^(-1)int_R exp(-tau*xi^2)|A_N(xi)|^2dxi. The ENTIRE |xi|>H complement is <=N^2 exp(-tau H^2)/(2*pi*tau*H), H>0. Fix delta>0 and H_N=sqrt((2-2gamma+delta)log N/tau), N>=2. The complement is O(N^(2gamma-delta)/sqrt(log N)). Thus E_N<<_epsilon N^(2gamma+epsilon) is equivalent to the same every-epsilon bound for int_(-H_N)^(H_N)exp(-tau*xi^2)|A_N(xi)|^2dxi. This is a continuous integral, not a finite sample test. For gamma>1/2 the arithmetic premise is precisely a one-sided upper bound of this order on the entire real signed off-diagonal; separate absolute shift bounds are stronger, not necessary.
For each h retain alpha_h(r)=chi(r)conj(chi(r+h)) and all q Fourier coefficients c_h(b)=q^(-1)sum_(r mod q)alpha_h(r)exp(-2*pi*i*b*r/q); alpha_h(n)=sum_(b mod q)c_h(b)exp(2*pi*i*b*n/q). This exact finite transform supplies no arithmetic estimate. For the quartic character modulo5 with chi(2)=i, alpha_1 on1,2,3,4 is(-i,-1,i,0). The unshifted divisor-Ramanujan span {c_d(n):d|5}, constant on units, cannot represent it. Shifted/richer or infinite expansions are not excluded and owe their own convergence/tails.
Under the stated every-epsilon energy premise, g_(2tau)=g_tau*g_tau and Cauchy-Schwarz bound each FULL width-2tau block source by ||g_tau||_2 sqrt(E_N). Sum all N<=x^(1+eta) geometrically, costing O(x^((1+eta)(gamma+epsilon/2))); sum every N>x^(1+eta) using C_tau N exp(-log(N/x)^2/(4*tau)), whose complete dyadic sum is O_A(x^(-A)) for every A>0 at sufficiently large x. Retain n=1 separately. Choosing eta and epsilon for each requested epsilon'>0 yields F_(2tau)(x)=sum_(n>=1)a_n g_(2tau)(log(n/x))<<x^(gamma+epsilon'). No backward heat inverse or omitted cross-block claim is used; the block premise is sufficient, not asserted necessary.
For x<=1 and any A>1, |F_(2tau)(x)|<=C_A zeta(A)x^A. Initially Re(s)>1, int_0^infinity F_(2tau)(x)x^(-s)dx/x=exp(tau*s^2)/L(s,chi). Both tails and logarithmic derivatives continue this integral holomorphically to Re(s)>gamma. The nonzero multiplier excludes all ordinary L zeros there at every finite height and multiplicity; the principal pole at1 is a reciprocal zero. No height-uniform inverse norm is required. Neither energy nor low-band arithmetic premise has been proved.

raw_source_record.statement:
For fixed real r>0, M(x)=sum_(n<=x)a_n (zero below0), R_r(x)=sum_(n<=x)a_n(x-n)^r/Gamma(r+1), S_r(x)=Gamma(r+1)x^(-r)R_r(x). Retain n=1 and the zero n=x endpoint. Define k_b(t)=t^(b-1)/Gamma(b) for t>0 and zero for t<=0. Causal beta integration gives R_r=k_r*M and k_b*k_c=k_(b+c). For nonnegative phi in C_c^infinity(0,1), integral phi=1, integer m>r and phi_h(t)=h^(-1)phi(t/h), put K_h=k_(m-r)*phi_h^(m). Then K_h*R_r=phi_h*M and ||K_h||_1=C_(r,phi)h^(-r). All endpoint terms vanish; cancellation of the first m moments of phi^(m) gives the complete K_1(u)=O(u^(-r-1)) far tail, including fractional r.
If |R_r(x)|<=C(1+x)^(r+theta),0<=theta<1, and |a_n|<=1, then for1<=h<=x, |M(x)|<<x^(r+theta)h^(-r)+h+1. The discrete variation cost is |M(x)-M(x-u)|<=u+1. Choosing h=x^beta gives M(x)<<x^beta, beta=(r+theta)/(r+1)=1-(1-theta)/(r+1). Every-positive-epsilon source bounds yield the corresponding every-epsilon conclusion. A NEW uniform variation law |M(x)-M(x-u)|<<X^kappa h^alpha for x~X,0<=u<=h,alpha>0,kappa>=0 would give exponent [alpha(r+theta)+r*kappa]/(r+alpha), only when the optimizer h=X^((r+theta-kappa)/(r+alpha)) lies in[1,X]. This extra short-interval hypothesis is not supplied.
The exponent beta is sharp in the class of arbitrary bounded coefficients. Fix integer m>r,B=max_(0<=l<=m)binom(m,l), sufficiently sparse integer T_j (a late tail of2^(2^j) suffices), H_j=floor(T_j^beta). On n=T_j+l H_j+k,0<=l<=m,1<=k<=H_j set b_n=(-1)^l binom(m,l)/B; elsewhere b_n=0. Disjoint complete blocks have mass0 and |b_n|<=1, while M_b(T_j+H_j)=H_j/B. For D(v)=sum_(l=0)^m(-1)^l binom(m,l)(v-l)_+^r, D is bounded everywhere and O(v^(r-m)) for v>m+1. Each block contributes H_j^r/[B Gamma(r+1)]sum_(k=1)^(H_j)D((x-T_j-k)/H_j) to R_r[b](x), hence O(H_j^(r+1)) at EVERY x, including its full fractional far tail. Sparse summation yields R_r[b](x)=O(x^(r+theta)), yet no M_b exponent beta-delta,delta>0, holds. This generic example is not a Mobius/character counterexample or optimality proof for actual arithmetic coefficients.
For the arithmetic specialization a_n=mu(n)chi(n), the previously recorded fixed-Riesz principle local:G134 avoids this loss for zero exclusion: a fixed-r S_r(x)<<_epsilon x^(theta+epsilon) gives int_1^infinity S_r(x)x^(-s)dx/x=Gamma(s)Gamma(r+1)/(Gamma(s+r+1)L(s,chi)), initially Re(s)>1. The majorant B(Re(s),r+1)sum_n n^(-Re(s)) pays Fubini; S_r vanishes below1. The multiplier is holomorphic and nonzero for Re(s)>0, so compact epsilon margins give all-finite-height, all-multiplicity zero exclusion in Re(s)>theta. Principal poles and imprimitive/natural zeros remain literal. Direct c=1-theta contrasts with c=(1-theta)/(r+1) through unsmoothed recovery. Moving r(x) has no such fixed Mellin identity without a separate paid comparison. This record's refinement is recovery and generic sharpness, not a new fixed-Riesz return or arithmetic source saving.

statement:
## G3 — p<.10, multiplicative/noncommutative dual sector certificate

### W40-11 — Conditional expectation with a paid off-diagonal return; p=.08
O: Split a multiplicative operator into a conditional-expectation block and its complement, retaining the off-diagonal blocks rather than applying a triangle inequality.
B: A full block dual certificate or Schur complement might let a rigorously bounded structured sector pay for its entire complement.
T: For a 2 by 2 self-adjoint block matrix derive the exact minimum complement price as a function of the cross block.
X: The cross block can saturate the whole target norm; sector savings alone do not transfer.
R: Reusable exact criterion for when a restricted result can improve a full-form exponent.

### W40-12 — Multiplicative matrix martingale with signed increments; p=.06
O: Reveal prime valuations successively and encode coefficients as matrix martingale differences so that prime-local mean-zero identities survive noncommuting projections.
B: A variance bound plus explicit predictable drift could control the full signed moment more sharply than summing divisor patterns.
T: Two-prime model with noncommuting projectors; compute the drift created by revealing shifted arguments.
X: Arithmetic dependence and projector nonadaptedness may make drift as large as the original moment.
R: High upstream reach if drift has arithmetic cancellation; exact no-go if it cannot.

### W40-13 — Free-compression dimension diagnostic; p=.03
O: Compare a sector projector and arithmetic covariance projector through principal angles, using free-probability behavior only as a diagnostic, never as an assumption.
B: A deterministic principal-angle lower bound could make the restricted/complement interaction contractive.
T: Construct two rank-half projections with the same traces but arbitrary principal angles and test whether trace data give any uniform saving.

## G67. Signed logarithmic bounds return the complete exponent

For f analytic near |z-t0|<=R, R>=16, f(t0)!=0, and any unit interval I
containing t0, let B>=sup_disk|f|. Avoid boundary zeros by varying R. Then

    integral_I log|f(t)|dt
      >=log|f(t0)|-(8/log R)log(B/|f(t0)|).

The proof uses the nonnegative superharmonic function
log(B/|f|), its positive harmonic part and the complete disk Green sum over
zeros with multiplicity. Near zeros have integrated Green excess at most4
and center Green value at least(log R)/2; far zeros and the harmonic part
obey the explicit Harnack bound. Real logarithmic singularities are integrable.
No zero separation, multiplicity cap or discarded negative logarithm is used.

For coefficients with sum|a_n|n^-b finite, the fixed Gaussian is entire and

    |F(z)| <= (2pi tau)^(-1/2)sum|a_n|n^-b
               exp(b Re z+tau b^2/2+(Im z)^2/(2tau)).

Choose t0 at a maximum on [j,j+1] and R in[sqrt j,2sqrt j]. Writing
M_j=max|F| and J_j=integral_j^(j+1)log|F| gives

    (1+eta_j)log M_j <= J_j+eta_j log B_j,
    eta_j=O(1/log j), log B_j=O(j).

Consequently J_j<=(gamma+epsilon)j+C_epsilon on EVERY sufficiently large
integer interval, for every epsilon>0, is equivalent in exponent to the
complete pointwise bound and the complete all-shell L2 bound. Jensen proves
the moment-to-log direction; the Green comparison returns the maximum with
only O(j/log j) loss. Sparse intervals or an average over j do not suffice.
This settles W21-T29's missing nonconcentration question for this complete
Gaussian class. It does not defeat the old smooth-signal or exceptional-dyad
counterexamples under their different hypotheses.

The actual Mellin numerator is

    N_chi=1-2chi(2)2^-s,

    a_P=sum_S A_S Z_S,

                      product_(p notin S)(1-2q_p)

has degree-energy polynomial

    sum_S A_S^2 z^|S|=product_p[(1-nu_p)+nu_p z],

## G69. The global Euler norm fails; its mass escapes the physical scale

For P>=5 let f_P=f3 restricted to P-smooth integers and V_P its complete
Gaussian. Its exact finite Euler series, including all powers, is

    E_P(s)=(1-3^-s)^-1 product_(p<=P,p!=3)(1-2p^-s)/(1-p^-s).

For sigma>0 weighted Gaussian Fubini and Plancherel give

    ||e^(-sigma u)V_P||_2^2
      =e^(tau sigma^2)/(2pi) integral_R e^(-tau t^2)|E_P(sigma+it)|^2dt.

Choose P_X=ceil(2X exp(C sqrt(log X))). Missing coefficients lie entirely
in the Gaussian tail, so on the physical shell
|F-V_(P_X)|<=X^(1-C^2/(2tau)+o(1)). This exact choice also ensures
P_X=X^(1+o(1)); the author's lower bound on P_X alone did not ensure it.
A global norm O(P^kappa) would return exponent sigma+kappa, but is false
for every fixed1/2<sigma<1 and every finite kappa.

Indeed at t=a/log P, uniformly for a in[5pi/6,7pi/6], ordinary PNT yields

    sum_(p<=P)p^(-sigma-ia/log P)
      =P^(1-sigma)/log P [e^(-ia)/(1-sigma)+o(1)].

The Euler logarithm is the negative real part of this sum plus O_sigma(1).
Its small-prime factors are bounded and nonzero. Integration over this
height interval proves

    ||e^(-sigma u)V_P||_2 >= C_(sigma,tau)(log P)^(-1/2)
                exp(P^(1-sigma)/(2(1-sigma)log P)).

Only pi(x)~x/log x is imported, as supplied by
[Johnston-Yang, v2, Corollary1.3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2204.01980), PDF page2.
The source's sharper estimates and any stronger zero-free conclusion are
unnecessary. No effective onset is asserted; contrary finite diagnostics
remain in the author evidence.

Critic audit30 proves the decisive scope refinement. Uniformly in P,
|V_P(u)|<=C_tau e^u for u>=0 and <=C_tau exp(-u^2/(2tau)) for u<=0.
Hence for every fixed T>0,

    ||1_(u<=T log P)e^(-sigma u)V_P||_2=O(P^(T(1-sigma))),
    ||1_(u>T log P)e^(-sigma u)V_P||_2/||e^(-sigma u)V_P||_2 ->1.

The excess mass escapes every polynomial physical scale. It supplies no
lower bound for the original shell. The global certificate must be retired,
while the source-specific restricted estimate remains eligible.

There is an exact causal identity for that output. On weighted L2, set
A_P=product_(p<=P)(I-D_p), B_P=product_(p<=P,p!=3)(I-2D_p), b=B_P g_tau.
Then V_P=A_P^-1 b. Split at U=log X and V=log(2X) into past L, shell I,
and future R. Every delay is causal; every nonidentity delay is at leastlog2.
Thus A_II=I and the future-input blocks vanish, giving

    (V_P)_I=b_I-A_IL A_LL^-1 b_L.

The Schur feedback is exactly zero, but the past injection is not. The
generic norm of A_LL^-1 is product_p(1-p^-sigma)^-1, again superpolynomial
for sigma<1. Estimate the complete signed sum, not the two pieces separately.
Future excess mass does not feed back into this causal output. This exact
source identity and localization refine the old Schur/finite-incidence
objections without reversing their valid quadratic inequalities.

       <=sqrt(K_tau (X/H+1) E_a(X,H))+2H g_tau(0).

statement:
## G74. A spectral gap can leave the entire arithmetic sign harmonic

For each distinct p|n,p!=3, take C0 with one even basis vector and C1
with two odd vectors, both mapped to the even vector. Its Laplacian has
eigenvalues 2,2,0, one odd harmonic state and supertrace -1. Tensoring
over distinct primes gives one harmonic state of parity omega_(p!=3)(n),
uniform positive gap 2 and a complement homotopy of norm <=1/sqrt(2).
Repeated powers add no cube; p=3 contributes a trivial factor.

With the actual chi(n)g(log(n/x)) weights, complete trace convergence
follows from 3^omega(n/3^v3(n))<=n^2. For every t>=0,

    F=Tr(Gamma W exp(-t Delta))=Tr(Gamma W P_harmonic).

The inverse/homotopy only acts on I-P, so the gap gives no bound on F.
Its absolute harmonic price is (phi(q)/q) exp(tau/2)x+O_(q,tau)(1),
an upper-certificate obstruction, not a lower bound on the signed field.
Different-integer matching requires a separate weighted readout estimate.

The direct complete Gaussian scalar is also not positive-real on its
proposed right half-plane: at s=4+it, Re D(s)>=2/3 for each of F,B,U,
since the coefficient of 1 is 1 and the remaining absolute mass is <=1/3.
At t=pi/(4 tau), exp(tau s^2/2) has negative real phase, so the real part
of the Mellin observable is strictly negative. This excludes this literal
scalar realization only; a different/vector readout must prove its return.

statement:
## G76. Exact first-eligible-prime matching, with a uniform critical bill

Choose any finite ordered list P=(p1,...,pr) of distinct primes excluding
3 and primes dividing q; 2 remains eligible. Put Q=product P. At the
first j with v_pj(n)<=1, toggle that valuation between 0 and 1. Earlier
pi^2 still divide both endpoints, so this is a disjoint involution. Its
unmatched set is exactly Q^2|n. Define the complete lower-endpoint field

    A_j(x)=sum_(p_j not dividing m, p_i^2|m for i<j)
                 f3(m)chi(m)g(log(m/x)).

The exact decomposition is

    F(x)=S_P(x)+C_P(x),
    S_P(x)=sum_j [A_j(x)-chi(p_j)A_j(x/p_j)],
    C_P(x)=sum_(Q^2|n) f3(n)chi(n)g(log(n/x)).

Every power and natural zero is present. On writing n=Q^2 m, the
coefficient equals (-1)^r chi(Q^2) times the character-weighted sign
which ignores P, and therefore has modulus <=1. Uniformly for every y>0,

    sum_(k>=1)g(log(k/y)) <= C_tau y,
    C_tau=max(exp(tau/2)+2g(0), 2g(0)exp(2tau)).

For y>=1 use bounded variation; for y<=1 complete the square and sum
k^(-2)<=2. Consequently

    ||C_P||_[X,2X] <= 2 C_tau sqrt(log 2) X/Q^2.

For moving P_X and Q_X^2>=X^(1-gamma+eta), eta>0, a complete signed
S_(P_X) bound with every-epsilon exponent gamma is equivalent to the
same fixed-F bound, in both directions. For gamma=.87486,5/6,3/4 the
required Q exponent is respectively .06257,1/12,1/8 plus eta/2.
All cross terms stay inside ||S_P||. Making Q huge alone does not simplify
this arithmetic target. No Mellin transform is taken of a moving source.

**The absolute edge certificate costs order X, uniformly in moving P.**
For a fixed first prime p, c=chi(p),

    J_p(c)=integral exp(v)|g(v)-c g(v+log p)|dv
            >= exp(tau/2)|1-c/p| >= exp(tau/2)(1-1/p).

For fixed P the jth edge price has leading constant
(phi(q)/q) Q_<j^(-2)(1-1/p_j)J_pj(chi(p_j))x.
To cover a changing first prime, let Z_q(y) be the positive coprime
Gaussian sum and B_p(y)=Z_q(y)-Z_q(y/p). The first edge price is at least
B_p(x)-B_p(x/p)>=Z_q(x)-2 C_tau x/p. For all sufficiently large p this
is uniformly a positive multiple of x; finitely many smaller p have a
positive minimum from the fixed-prime formula. Thus every nonempty
moving list has positive certificate cost Omega_(q,tau)(X). This is
not a lower bound on F or S_P. The signed cancellation is precisely
the remaining input. Derivative rewriting retains (1-c)g and the full
integral of g'; it cannot erase chi(p) or its price.

This develops U-PRIME-CHAIN/U-TRANSPORT and W43/W44 ancestry into an
all-power canonical matching with a uniform moving residual estimate.
It does not claim the basic prime-toggle idea as new.
title: G76. Exact first-eligible-prime matching, with a uniform critical bill

## G77. Full contour gluing includes the horizontal and residue terms

For fixed U, M(s)=exp(tau s^2/2)/L(s,chi). Start at b>1, choose a in
(1/2,1) avoiding zero real parts and a finite height T avoiding boundary
zeros. No zero-free interior is assumed. The rectangle identity is

    U=V_(a,T)+H_top-minus-bottom+Z_residues+R_(b,T).

A zero rho of multiplicity m contributes x^rho times a polynomial in
log x of degree m-1 with nonzero leading coefficient
m exp(tau rho^2/2)/L^(m)(rho). The principal pole at 1 instead gives a
zero of 1/L. The F numerator has no zeros in this open strip.
The complete right-tail shell norm is

    ||R_(b,T)|| <= C X^b T^(-1) exp(-tau T^2/2).

Choose a boundary-admissible T_X within one unit above
sqrt(2(b-gamma+delta)log X/tau). The error is
O(X^(gamma-delta)/sqrt(log X)); the truncated ORIGINAL b-line band
is thus exponent-equivalent to U. Moving to a requires the full prices

    C X^a integral_(-T)^T exp(-tau t^2/2)|1/L(a+it)|dt,
    C X^b exp(-tau T^2/2) integral_a^b
                      (|1/L(sigma+iT)|+|1/L(sigma-iT)|)d sigma,

and all residues. No proximity-to-zero bound is assumed away.
A fixed finite nonempty residue packet whose maximal real part is
sigma*>gamma has shell norm >=c X^sigma* (log X)^d for all large X,
by positive definiteness of the fixed distinct-frequency Gram matrix.
This is conditional on such zeros existing. Its constant is not uniform
in growing T, zero count or separation, and it supplies no lower bound
for the growing packet. Complete contour gluing remains an open
arithmetic estimate, not automatic flux cancellation.

statement:
## G78. Uniform depth and the full physical tail

Let a(n)=mu(n)chi(n), ell(n)=chi(n), m_Y(n)=a(n)1_(n<=Y),
and use Dirichlet convolution below.
Set d_Y=delta-ell*m_Y. For fixed b>1 choose a fixed integer Y>=2 with

    eta=zeta(b)Y^(1-b)/(b-1)<1.
    Q_k=m_Y*(delta+d_Y+...+d_Y^(*(k-1))).

The inverse identity a*ell=delta gives, for every k>=1,

    a-Q_k=a*d_Y^(*k),
    Q_k(n)=a(n) for n<(Y+1)^k,
    sup_k sum_n |Q_k(n)|n^(-b) <= zeta(b)/(1-eta),
    sup_k sum_n |a(n)-Q_k(n)|n^(-b)
        <= B_b=zeta(b)(1+1/(1-eta)).

These include complex and ramified characters. The support inequality is
strict. Q_k is a polynomial in infinite arithmetic series, generally not
a finite-support Dirichlet polynomial. Newton doubling reaches Q_(2^r)
in O(log log X) formal stages; this is not a computational complexity bound.

For g_tau(v)=(2 pi tau)^(-1/2)exp(-v^2/(2tau)), let

    U(x)=sum a(n)g_tau(log(n/x)),
    N_X=2X exp(C sqrt(log X)),
    k_X=floor(log N_X/log(Y+1))+1,
    V_X(x)=sum Q_(k_X)(n)g_tau(log(n/x)).

The full tail, with no hidden cutoff of Q_k, obeys

    sup_(X<=x<=2X)|U(x)-V_X(x)|
      <= B_b sup_(X<=x<=2X, n>=N_X) n^b g_tau(log(n/x))
      << X^(b-C^2/(2tau)+o(1)).

A power-of-two depth at least k_X has
the same bound. Concretely b=2,Y=4 give eta<1/2, Q norm<4 and B_b<6.
C=sqrt(3tau) pays the complete error at X^(1/2+o(1)), so for every
fixed gamma>1/2 the every-shell norm bound for V_X is equivalent to that
for U, allowing every positive epsilon loss. Return to fixed U before
using its Mellin transform exp(tau s^2/2)/L(s,chi).

The inverse algebra and prefix are AH20/W43 ancestry; uniform depth and
the complete tail are the new increment. No gamma<.874861 estimate of
V_X is proved. The old absolute-norm obstruction at b<=1 remains valid
at its own scope and does not contradict this b>1 tail argument.
title: G78. Uniform depth and the full physical tail

## G79. Exact drift and normalized Ward defects

For h>0, a_h=exp(gamma h), E_j=int_(jh)^((j+1)h)|U(e^y)|^2dy and
D(y)=U(e^(y+h))-a_h U(e^y),

    E_(j+1)-a_h^2 E_j=int (|D|^2+2a_h Re(D conjugate(U)))dy.

An every-j one-sided drift estimate at exponent2gamma is equivalent to
the energy bound. The actual squarefree diagonal has density
kappa_q=prod_(p|q)(1-1/p)prod_(p not|q)(1-1/p^2) and pointwise main term
kappa_q exp(tau/4)e^y/(2sqrt(pi tau)), with O_(q,tau)(e^(y/2)) error.
Its drift is negative for gamma>1/2; the signed off-diagonal is unbounded
by this calculation. This is an adaptation of the existing scale family.

For a finite prime exterior space, Q=sum w_p a_p^*, W=sum|w_p|^2>0,
and even diagonal Z, the CAR identity yields

    Str(Q^*[Q,Z])=W Str(Z).

For actual Gaussian entries, Str(Z)=U_P. Every individual prime term is
|w_p|^2 U_P, so no prime-count cancellation occurs. Primes through N_X
give full omitted error X^(1-C^2/(2tau)+o(1)). Exponent equivalence is
for the normalized defect divided by W, or W=1; arbitrary moving W is
charged. This corrects the unqualified raw-defect wording in the author.
title: G79. Exact drift and normalized Ward defects

## G80. Sharp exterior certificate, with the actual H contract

For A=T^*T, full dimension d>=2, t=tr A>0 and
e2=(t^2-tr A^2)/2=||wedge^2 T||_HS^2,

    lambda_max(A)<= [t+sqrt((d-1)((d-1)t^2-2d e2))]/d.

The inequality is sharp when the other eigenvalues are equal. For
t/d<=B^2<=t the sufficient threshold is

    e2 >= [t^2-B^4-(t-B^2)^2/(d-1)]/2.

d=1,t=0 and out-of-range B are handled separately. A fixed area fraction
does not provide a power gain. For original H, T must retain every core,
height, mark projector, ray phase, sharp window and equal-norm deletion;
with ||v_i||^2=Omega_i the raw target is
Z^epsilon G K[N+L+(NL)^(2/3)]P_orig. The original outside squared scalar
N^(-1)G^(-2) is charged once. Required native trace/fourth contractions
are still OPEN. A fixed core or height does not substitute for this form.

Far masking is an orthogonal coordinate projection in Hilbert-Schmidt
matrix space. It is not generally PSD-preserving. This is the precise
repair of the author's ambiguous “not a positive projector.”

The native unit syndrome retains phase variance1 and a full covariance
with the source. The JN frequency phase is affine only in its frequency
variables; its joint physical-frequency Hessian is not asserted zero.
A mark-independent J-frequency row set captures at most O(KJ/Q) of
the full norm. These scoped tests yield neither an H upper bound nor an
actual signed lower bound, and do not cover arbitrary adaptive mark sets.

statement:
## G83. Actual balanced completion at growing order

Fix an ordinary, possibly imprimitive complex Dirichlet character chi and
tau>0. Put a(n)=mu(n)chi(n), m_Y=a 1_(n<=Y), u_Y=a-m_Y, and
g_tau(v)=(2 pi tau)^(-1/2) exp(-v^2/(2tau)). All convolutions below are
Dirichlet convolutions. Since a*chi=delta, for every integer K>=2,

    u_Y^(*K)*chi^(*(K-1))
      =a+sum_(j=1)^K (-1)^j choose(K,j)m_Y^(*j)*chi^(*(j-1)).

Write L=log X. In band I take L^(1/3)/2<=K<=2L^(1/3); in band II take
(2/5)sqrt(L)/log L<=K<=2sqrt(L)/log L. Define

    Y=floor exp(L/(K-1/2)), V=L/(2K-1), W=V/2, r=K-1,
    F(x)=sum a(n)g_tau(log(n/x)),
    F_r=(1-x d/dx)^r F,
    phi_r(v)=(1+d/dv)^r g_tau(v).

Let C be (-1)^(K+1) times the sum of

    a(d1)...a(dK) chi(ell1)...chi(ell_(K-1))
      phi_r(log(d1...dK ell1...ell_(K-1)/x))

over every d_i<=Y and every ell_i>=1. Let C_bal impose only
Xe^(-W)<=d1...dK<=2Xe^W. Shared primes and squareful products remain.
Every d_i in that balanced sum lies between e^W and e^(2V). Uniformly
for X<=x<=2X and for all integers K in either band, for every A>0,

    |F_r(x)-C_bal(x)| <<_(A,chi,tau) X^(-A).

The proof separately pays C-F_r and C-C_bal. The derivative estimate is
|phi_r(v)|<=exp(O_tau((r+1)log(r+2))) exp(-v^2/(4tau)). For a completed
j-face its Mellin integrand contains
exp(tau s^2/2)(1-s)^(K-1)L(s,chi)^(j-1); the possible principal pole at
1 is canceled, including j=K. Functional equation, reflection and
duplication give on Re(s)=-B the uniform bound

    |L(-B+it,chi)| <= C_q^(B+1) Gamma(B+1) exp(pi|t|/2).

The resulting face cost is bounded by

    exp[-BZ+tau B^2/2
      +O(K(B+1)log(B+2)+K^2+Klog(K+2))],

with Z at least V or W as appropriate. Taking B=Z/tau gives a negative
term of order L^(4/3) in band I and L(log L)^2 in band II. It dominates
the full tuple and multiplicity costs. The all-large remainder starts at
(Y+1)^K>Xe^V and is paid with its d_(2K-1) coefficient envelope and a
Gaussian tail. Neither side of the product cutoff is dropped. A sufficient
general order regime is K growing with K^2 log L=o(L), with separately
compatible future-order bands; optimality is not claimed.

The dyadic balanced-source return keeps its exact premise. If
M_chi(z)=sum_(n<=z)a(n)<<z^b for fixed b<1, then the future-Gamma identity

    F(e^u)=1/Gamma(r) integral_0^infinity e^(-t)t^(r-1)F_r(e^(u+t))dt

holds. K is chosen at the base scale and held fixed throughout this
integral. The band margins keep it admissible through t<=4log X. An
every-dyadic C_bal norm bound at exponent gamma gives the desired main
term, while the future tail costs X^(5b-4+o(1)). Thus 5b-4<=gamma is
sufficient, with every positive epsilon retained. The source-relative
b=7/8 input gives 3/8. This route does not erase its growth premise.
title: G83. Actual balanced completion at growing order

statement:
## G84. Exact moment and genuine paid sectors

For 1/2<sigma<1 and even K=2m, put

    M_Y(s)=sum_(n<=Y)a(n)n^(-s),
    Q(X,K)=integral_R exp(-tau t^2/4)|M_Y(sigma+it)|^(2m)dt.

The full Mellin majorant H for C satisfies

    H=integral exp(-tau t^2/2)|1-sigma-it|^(K-1)
          |L(sigma+it,chi)|^(K-1)|M_Y(sigma+it)|^K dt,
    ||C||_(L2([X,2X],dx/x)) << X^sigma H,
    H <= exp(O_(chi,tau,sigma)(Klog(K+2))) Q.

Consequently Q<<X^(eta+epsilon) supplies gamma=sigma+eta, with no
square root of Q. The full |t|>3sqrt(L)/tau tail of H is O(X^(-3));
the central part remains an arithmetic problem.

The coefficient of M_Y^m is exactly lambda(n)chi(n)N_(m,Y)(n), where
N_(m,Y) counts ordered factorizations into m squarefree positive integers
at most Y. Unit factors, repeated primes across factors and squareful
outputs remain. With N=Y^m=X^(1/2+o(1)),

    Q=sqrt(4pi/tau) sum_(n,k<=N) lambda(n)lambda(k)chi(n)conj(chi(k))
        N_(m,Y)(n)N_(m,Y)(k)(nk)^(-sigma)
        exp(-(log(n/k))^2/tau).

This is the complete double sum. Its total is nonnegative, but its signed
sectors need not be. The independent proof bounds:

- Diagonal: at most a fixed Gaussian constant times zeta(2sigma)^(m^2)
  =X^o(1), by N_(m,Y)<=d_m and d_m(p^j)^2<=d_(m^2)(p^j).
- Large gcd: its coefficientwise absolute price, for 1<=G<=N, is
  <<_epsilon X^(1-sigma+epsilon)/G. Divisor submultiplicativity and
  Rankin summation retain the costs zeta(1+delta)^m and
  zeta(1+delta)^(m^2); both are X^o(1) in the stated bands.
- Large ratio: |log(n/k)|>=L^(2/3) has price O_A(X^(-A)) for every A.

Set gamma=sigma+eta<1, eta>=0, c=1-gamma, choose
0<kappa<gamma-1/2 and G=X^(c+kappa). Let Core be the same signed
double sum, including its Gaussian constant, with n!=k, gcd(n,k)<G
and |log(n/k)|<L^(2/3). Then

    Core <= X^(eta+epsilon)  for every epsilon>0

is equivalent at the exponent level to the Q bound: the discarded gcd
sector costs X^(eta-kappa+epsilon), the diagonal X^o(1), and the ratio
tail decays faster than any power. The inequality is one-sided.

Taking termwise absolute values cannot prove it. A positive-density
squarefree unit-phase class in [B/2,B], B=floor X^(1/K), yields a
positive subcollection with price X^(1-sigma-o(1)). Grouping products
in logarithmic windows of length1 pays the Gaussian. Removing the
diagonal and large gcd sector leaves this exponent unchanged. These
products lie inside the balanced product window because W/K tends to
infinity. This is an actual coefficientwise-price obstruction, not a
lower bound for signed Core, Q or the physical norm; cancellation between
different actual phases can still pay the desired estimate.
title: G84. Exact moment and genuine paid sectors
